norm: It's responsible to keep children safe.
situation: Kent was watching his kids playing in the backyard of his house and looking for saftey measures.
intention: Kent wants to add security to his back yard.
moral_action: Kent installs cameras around his yard to look for intruders.
moral_consequence: Kent's kids feel much safer with the camera's watching them.
immoral_action: Kent installs an electric fence around his yard to keep intruders out.
immoral_consequence: One of Kent's kids gets shocked by the fence when they accidentally run into it.

norm: It's wrong to become addicted to gambling.
situation: Kevin bet on the Kentucky Derby and won big, so now he wants to make horse races his new hobby.
intention: Kevin wants to place more wagers.
moral_action: Kevin decides to place a wager once every weekend.
moral_consequence: Kevin enjoys his new hobby and wins some cash once in a while.
immoral_action: Kevin places several bets a day and at an increasing rate.
immoral_consequence: Kevin ends up losing everything he won.

norm: It's admirable to remain loyal to one's romantic partner.
situation: Curtis, an engaged man, is at a friend's party when a beautiful woman tells him that she's recently single and starts flirting with him.
intention: Curtis wants to have a great time at the party.
moral_action: Curtis explains to the woman that he's engaged and spends some time introducing her to his good friend who, like her, is also newly single.
moral_consequence: Curtis leaves the party feeling happy that he was able to set up his friend with a beautiful woman.
immoral_action: Curtis chats with the woman and spends the evening flirting back and forth with her.
immoral_consequence: Curtis ends up questioning the quality of his relationship with his fiancee since he had such a great time with another woman.

norm: It's polite to go to a friend's wedding when invited.
situation: Anna gets an invitation to her friend Carol's wedding that will be held in another state.
intention: Anna needs to decide whether she will attend.
moral_action: Anna decides to attend the wedding even though it causes her some inconvenience.
moral_consequence: Carol is so grateful that Anna comes to her wedding, and she gives Anna a big hug.
immoral_action: Anna decides it is too much trouble to attend, and she declines the invitation.
immoral_consequence: Carol is upset that Anna doesn't attend, and it puts a strain on their friendship.

norm: You should not shirk household chores.
situation: Greg's mother has ordered him to clean his messy room but his friend James has invited him over to play video games.
intention: Greg needs to decide whether to accept James' invitation.
moral_action: Greg tells James that he can play tomorrow and spends the next couple of hours cleaning his room.
moral_consequence: Greg's mother is happy with him and rewards him with a cookie.
immoral_action: Greg accepts James' invitation to play video games and skips out on cleaning his room like he was supposed to.
immoral_consequence: Greg's mother gets upset and grounds him for one week when he gets home.

norm: It's wrong to use violence to solve your problems.
situation: Ben lives in a neighborhood with assigned parking and his neighbor's friend frequently uses his assigned spot.
intention: Ben wants to stop the neighbors friend from taking up his parking spot.
moral_action: Ben calls a tow truck and gets the car of the neighbor's friend's towed away.
moral_consequence: The neighbors see the tow truck and learn to be more mindful about the assigned parking.
immoral_action: Ben ends up getting into a physical altercation with the neighbors friend.
immoral_consequence: The neighbors are concerned for their safety because of his actions.

norm: You shouldn't lie about your gender online.
situation: Jess is an transgender female who is a popular influenster on Instagram.
intention: Jess wants to wait for the right moment to tell her audience her gender.
moral_action: Jess discloses her gender in an Instagram post that explains why she waited so long.
moral_consequence: Jess's audience understands why she waited so long to disclose her gender and are okay with it.
immoral_action: Jess's gender is leaked online before she is able to disclose it on her own.
immoral_consequence: Jess's community does not trust her as much, and they don't understand why she doesn't trust them.

norm: Family shouldn't bully other family members.
situation: Lydia is visiting her cousin Melody who just had a baby.
intention: Lydia wants to comment about Melody's health.
moral_action: Lydia tells Melody that she and her baby look healthy and happy.
moral_consequence: Melody is grateful for Lydia's visit and talks about her worries about being a new mom.
immoral_action: Lydia tells Melody that she looks as fat as she used to be back in middle school.
immoral_consequence: Melody is irritated at Lydia's behavior and asks her to leave and never to talk to her again.

norm: You shouldn't get too demanding with your friends.
situation: Jerry's car broke down and its repair won't be finished within a few days, and his friend Aaron lives near him.
intention: Jerry wants to get a ride to work.
moral_action: Jerry calls Uber to get to work everyday before his car gets fixed.
moral_consequence: Aaron offers to give Jerry a ride if he needs one.
immoral_action: Jerry asks Aaron to give him a ride to work everyday before his car gets fixed, even though their work places are not close by.
immoral_consequence: Aaron feels tired and exhausted for the long drive everyday.

norm: It's kind to wait for people.
situation: Josh drives Penelope to work every day and is hanging outside her house to pick her up, but there's no sign of her.
intention: Josh needs to get to work.
moral_action: Josh continues to sit outside Penelope's house until she walks out the door a few minutes later.
moral_consequence: Penelope appreciates Josh's patience and thanks him for waiting around.
immoral_action: Josh shrugs his shoulders and drives away to work after sitting around a moment.
immoral_consequence: Penelope comes running out of the house shouting to wait, but she's too late.

norm: It's rude to disrupt others with loud noises.
situation: Logan is playing video games when his sister Laura asks him to turn down the volume because she's studying.
intention: Logan wants to listen to the game's soundtrack.
moral_action: Logan plays the game sound track through his gaming headset.
moral_consequence: Logan has fun listening to music while playing games.
immoral_action: Logan continues playing the game at a loud volume.
immoral_consequence: Logan is banned from playing video games from the rest of the night when his sister talks to her mom about her brother.

norm: It is bad to take from family.
situation: Sandra is visiting her cousin's house when she sees a doll she really likes.
intention: Sandra wants to have a doll like her cousin has.
moral_action: Sandra asks her mother nicely if she can have a doll just like her cousin's and her mother buys her one.
moral_consequence: Sandra gets a brand new doll that she likes just for herself.
immoral_action: Sandra takes her cousins doll and hides it under her dress then takes it home.
immoral_consequence: Sandra's parents find out that she stole the doll and punish her.

norm: People are expected to keep their clothing clean.
situation: Dave has a job interview for an accounting position at a downtown office.
intention: Dave wants to commute to the interview without driving his car.
moral_action: Dave calls a taxi cab to take him to the office.
moral_consequence: Dave arrives at the interview looking professional, making a good first impression.
immoral_action: Dave walks through a muddy forest to reach the office.
immoral_consequence: Dave looks dirty and unprofessional when he arrives at the interview, making a bad first impression.

norm: It is wrong to break the law.
situation: Frank is alone at a bar and notices the bartender left the drawer open and unattended.
intention: Frank wants to pay his tab.
moral_action: Frank keeps an eye on the drawer and pulls money out of his wallet to give to the bartender when he returns.
moral_consequence: The bartender is thankful for Franks assistance and pays for his next drink.
immoral_action: Frank reaches over the bar and snatches some money from the register.
immoral_consequence: The owner of the bar fires the bartender after he looks at the security footage, and Frank is arrested.

norm: It's disgusting not to bathe
situation: Mark woke up late on his first day of work at a new company.
intention: Mark wants to get to work on time.
moral_action: Mark ordered an Uber rather than taking the bus so that he could take a shower and still get to work on time.
moral_consequence: Mark's new coworkers welcomed him warmly to the new team.
immoral_action: Mark skipped taking a shower so that he wouldn't be late for work.
immoral_consequence: Mark's coworkers noticed his body odor and made fun of him behind his back.

norm: Its wrong to be affronted when it's someone else's party.
situation: Ruth is at her friend Terri's birthday party when she notices that many of the guests did not bring gifts.
intention: Ruth wants to react to the other guests.
moral_action: Ruth focuses on making sure that Terri is enjoying her party.
moral_consequence: Ruth fosters a great party atmosphere for Terri.
immoral_action: Ruth approaches the guests that didn't bring gifts and informs them of how rude they appear.
immoral_consequence: Ruth creates tension at Terri's party.

norm: It is creepy to stand too close and stare.
situation: John looks out of the window and notices his neighbor is burning something in the backyard.
intention: John wants to find out what his neighbor is doing.
moral_action: John takes a picture of his neighbor with his cellphone and zooms in what they are doing.
moral_consequence: His neighbor is undisturbed by John and continues with the activity.
immoral_action: John immediately goes to his neighbor's open backyard so that he can see it more clearly.
immoral_consequence: His neighbor feels offended and asks John to leave his backyard.

norm: It's wrong not to talk to your in-laws.
situation: John is walking through a local park where he runs into in-laws.
intention: John wants to get home quickly to catch an upcoming football game on television.
moral_action: John says he to the in-laws and makes small talk for a few minutes.
moral_consequence: John is late but still catches most of the game and feels good that he talked with his in-laws.
immoral_action: John pretends he doesn't he his in-laws and quickly changes paths to avoid them.
immoral_consequence: John makes it home in time for the game but his in-laws call him on the phone, disrupting his viewing experience.

norm: It's wrong to reveal one's secrets just to spite them.
situation: Anthony had recently told Billy a deep dark secret about himself, and a few days later they are now in a large fight in front of their other friends.
intention: Billy wants to win the argument with Anthony.
moral_action: Billy uses something Anthony said prior in the argument to prove he is wrong.
moral_consequence: Anthony continues arguing for a while, but eventually concedes the argument.
immoral_action: Billy uses the secret Anthony told him against him, to try to get points with everyone else.
immoral_consequence: Anthony is devastated, and runs off, never to talk to Billy or the rest ever again.

norm: It's irresponsible to drink too much alcohol.
situation: Clay is at a business meeting and the client tells him to help himself to some scotch.
intention: Clay wants to have a drink.
moral_action: Clay pours himself a small shot of scotch and sips it throughout the meeting.
moral_consequence: Clay is able to make a deal with the client and leaves happy.
immoral_action: Clay pours himself an over-sized glass of straight scotch and gets really drunk.
immoral_consequence: Clay makes a fool of himself and loses the client.

norm: It's rude to make fun of your friend.
situation: Paula and her friend are shopping, and her friend tries on a dress that doesn't flatter her.
intention: Paula wants to prevent her friend from buying the unflattering dress.
moral_action: Paula tells her friend that the dress is not right for her and offers to help her find a more flattering one.
moral_consequence: Paula's friend takes the advice and ends up finding a dress that looks great on her instead.
immoral_action: Paula mocks her friend's appearance, calling her ugly and lumpy in the ill-fitting dress.
immoral_consequence: Paula's friend is hurt terribly and leaves the shop in tears without buying anything.

norm: It is inconsiderate cancel a reservation at the last minute.
situation: Darryl made a reservation at a restaurant, with an elaborate plan in place to propose to his girlfriend, but he and his girlfriend are now in a fight.
intention: Darryl has to decide whether to cancel the reservation or not.
moral_action: Darryl called the restaurant as soon as he suspected that he may not be able to execute his plan, and that the reservation may not be necessary.
moral_consequence: The restaurant was able to accommodate him by setting the plans on hold, so that even if he didn't make the reservation there would be no cost.
immoral_action: Darryl waits, but it doesn't work out, so he cancels the reservation and the plan on the day he was supposed to carry it out.
immoral_consequence: The restaurant had already ordered special supplies and had prepared their staff for the event, so they needed to charge a fee for the late cancellation.

norm: It's good to try to enjoy yourself.
situation: Lori has a whole week off from her very stressful job.
intention: Lori wants to care for her mental health and relax.
moral_action: Lori treats herself to a few days at the beach where she is able to relax, eat well, and get plenty of rest.
moral_consequence: Lori returns to work feeling refreshed and recharged.
immoral_action: Lori realizes that her home and yard are very messy and overextends herself cleaning and doing yard work for the whole week.
immoral_consequence: Lori has to go back to work, even more stressed, frazzled, and exhausted.

norm: It's considered scholarly to learn multiple languages.
situation: Ed loves to read the Bible and is considering pursuing a career in Biblical studies, but doesn't like language learning much.
intention: Ed wants to become a Bible scholar.
moral_action: Ed pursues a career as a Bible scholar and makes efforts to learn Greek and Hebrew in the process.
moral_consequence: Ed is able to help with a prestigious Bible translation project and helps people through it.
immoral_action: Ed takes courses on Bible scholarship and avoids any of the connected languages such as Greek and Hebrew.
immoral_consequence: Other scholars don't take Ed seriously because he cannot read the original Bible texts.

norm: It's immoral to steal from a company
situation: Tom has worked for the same company for the past thirty years.
intention: Tom needs more money to get a new car.
moral_action: Tom has a meeting with his boss to ask if he can get a raise.
moral_consequence: Tom's boss recognizes his hard work and bumps up his pay considerably.
immoral_action: Tom starts taking money from the safe everyday when everyone is out of the office.
immoral_consequence: Tom is caught on camera taking the money and is promptly arrested.

norm: You shouldn't give wild animals to your parents.
situation: Fred's parents lost their dog and are sad about it.
intention: Fred wants to get his parents a new pet.
moral_action: Fred gets his parents a kitten from a nearby neighbor.
moral_consequence: Fred's parents love the kitten and are grateful.
immoral_action: Fred gets his parents a baby raccoon that he found.
immoral_consequence: The raccoon turns feral and attacks his parents.

norm: It's rude to disallow a roommate from having guests over.
situation: Penny recently began renting a room in her house to Hope, but Penny gets upset when Hope has friends over and they make a mess in the living room.
intention: Penny wants to keep a tidy living space.
moral_action: Penny sits down and comes up with house rules regarding guests and cleanup with Hope.
moral_consequence: Penny is relieved that conflict with her roommate is avoided.
immoral_action: Penny bans Hope from having friends over.
immoral_consequence: Penny starts to feel uncomfortable because Hope gets hostile towards her.

norm: It's wrong to disturb someone who is sleeping.
situation: Peter is hanging out with his friends at summer camp, one late evening, while others are already asleep.
intention: Peter wants to make his friends laugh.
moral_action: Peter keeps on churning out funny stories.
moral_consequence: All those already asleep sleep on peacefully.
immoral_action: Peter devises a prank to startle one of the sleepers awake.
immoral_consequence: The person who was brutally awakened feels terrible.

norm: It's improper to modify someone's order at a restaurant.
situation: Jake is a waiter at a restaurant and a customer named John has just ordered his expensive steak extra well done to the point of being burnt.
intention: Jake wants to ensure that the steak is at best medium if not rawer.
moral_action: Jake spends a minute extolling the virtues of a steak done at medium or medium rare.
moral_consequence: John is convinced by Jake to switch his choice to medium rare and to his surprise enjoys the steak more.
immoral_action: Jake writes down John's order but changes the steak to be medium before relaying the order to the chef.
immoral_consequence: John is livid when he sees his steak is not burnt to a crisp and demands that Jake return the meal.

norm: It is irresponsible to leave the house without your wallet.
situation: Joey's daughter Maria just called from a friends and asked for a ride home.
intention: Joey wants to pick up Maria.
moral_action: Joey hops in his car, but realizes he forgot his wallet, so he goes back in to grab it and gets Maria.
moral_consequence: When Joey is pulled over for a broken tail light, Joey is able to hand the cop his driver’s license from his wallet.
immoral_action: Joey hops in his car, but realizes he forgot his wallet, and instead of going back to get it, he goes to pick up Maria.
immoral_consequence: When Joey is pulled over for a broken tail light, Joey receives a ticket since he is unable to hand the cop his driver’s license he carries in his wallet.

norm: It's rude to steal someone's seat.
situation: Tiffany booked a flight and was given an isle seat despite requesting a windowed seat.
intention: Tiffany wants to sit in a windowed seat.
moral_action: Tiffany sits in her assigned seat and when someone sits in the windowed seat she asks if they would be willing to trade.
moral_consequence: Tiffany's offer to trade is accepted, and she gets to sit in the windowed seat.
immoral_action: Tiffany boards the plane and sits in the windowed seat hoping nobody will confront her about it.
immoral_consequence: The person assigned the windowed seat lets the flight attendant know, and Tiffany is asked to leave the plane.

norm: It is rude to leave abruptly.
situation: Megan is at a dinner party at her friend Adrian's house and is starting to feel very tired.
intention: Megan wants to go home and go to bed.
moral_action: Megan finds Adrian and lets him know that she had fun but needs to leave because she is tired.
moral_consequence: Adrian thanks Megan for coming and sees her off on her way out.
immoral_action: Megan says she is going to the bathroom but actually slips out and goes home without saying goodbye to anyone.
immoral_consequence: Adrian and Megan's other friends are upset with Megan for being rude and do not invite her to the next party.

norm: It's good to love someone.
situation: Christine had her heart broken by her ex husband and has decided she is done with love.
intention: Christine wants to live a happy life.
moral_action: Christine opens her heart to loving others and starts dating a great guy.
moral_consequence: Christine's friends finds her warm and loving.
immoral_action: Christine chooses to be single and rejects all potential suitors, focusing on herself instead.
immoral_consequence: Christine's friends find her aloof and self-absorbed.

norm: You should always apologize to your parents.
situation: Ryan is coming home past his curfew and his parents are waiting for him.
intention: Ryan wants to talk to his parents about being late.
moral_action: Ryan explains why he is late and says he is sorry to his parents.
moral_consequence: Ryan's parents will think he is contrite.
immoral_action: Ryan makes an excuse and says the curfew is too early.
immoral_consequence: Ryan's parents will think he is not mature enough to stay out later.

norm: It's not okay to invade someone else's privacy.
situation: Monica was sitting at her desk at work when she noticed her coworkers phone on the floor.
intention: Monica wants to pick up the phone.
moral_action: Monica takes the phone to the person who it belonged to.
moral_consequence: Monica's coworker buys her a gift card for helping her find her phone.
immoral_action: Monica takes the phone and reads all the texts that were on it.
immoral_consequence: Monica is reported to HR and is reprimanded by her boss.

norm: It's polite to sneeze into a tissue or your elbow.
situation: Mark is on a plane, and he has a slight cold.
intention: Mark needs to sneeze.
moral_action: Mark gets out a tissue that he brought with him and proceeds to sneeze into it.
moral_consequence: The people on the plane feel fear hearing him sneeze but then feel relieved seeing that he sneezed into a tissue.
immoral_action: Mark sneezes without covering his mouth while on the plane.
immoral_consequence: The people on the plane start becoming fearful that they might get the coronavirus.

norm: It's good to be appreciative of your teacher's help.
situation: Jasmine, Mary's teacher, keeps mentioning being hungry while tutoring Mary.
intention: Mary wants Jasmine to stop talking about being hungry.
moral_action: Mary gives Jasmine a chocolate bar to Jasmine and thanks Jasmine for tutoring her.
moral_consequence: Jasmine offers to continue tutoring Mary.
immoral_action: Mary reminds Jasmine that she can eat in thirty minutes after her tutoring session is over.
immoral_consequence: Jasmine is shocked by Mary's rude statement, and she finishes the study session early.

norm: You shouldn't ditch someone you have plans with.
situation: James promised his friend that he'd attend his improv show, then won free tickets to a concert on the same evening.
intention: James wants to go to the concert.
moral_action: James scalps the concert tickets for enough money to buy tickets on a non-conflicting date.
moral_consequence: James goes to his friend's show and loudly applauds his performance.
immoral_action: James tells his friend that he got sick and can't come to his show, instead going to the concert.
immoral_consequence: James' friend sees his concert photos on Facebook and gets mad at him.

norm: It's bad when toddlers use offensive language.
situation: Gene is babysitting a toddler and is teaching him how to say single words.
intention: Gene wants to teach the toddler an unusual word.
moral_action: "Gene teaches the toddler to say the word, ""snarfdoodle""."
moral_consequence: "The toddler says ""snarfdoodle"" repeatedly, making his parents laugh uncontrollably."
immoral_action: Gene teaches the toddler how to say a swear word.
immoral_consequence: The toddler repeats the swear word over and over in front of his parents, horrifying them.

norm: It is wrong to commit a robbery.
situation: Lois sees a watch that she really wants in a jewelry store, but she can't afford it.
intention: Lois wants to get the watch.
moral_action: Lois takes some extra hours at work, so she can get more money to buy the watch.
moral_consequence: Lois is able to buy the watch with no issues.
immoral_action: Lois breaks into the jewelry store after hours and takes the watch.
immoral_consequence: Lois is caught and arrested by the police.

norm: It is rude to not attend a meeting.
situation: Harold has a meeting scheduled with his boss at eight o clock.
intention: Harold wants to go to work in the morning.
moral_action: Harold makes sure to get to work early enough to go to the meeting.
moral_consequence: Harold learns a lot of important information at the meeting that helps him move up in his job.
immoral_action: Harold gets to work at nine o clock in the morning and disregards the meeting even took place.
immoral_consequence: Harold's boss calls him into his office because he is mad that he missed the meeting.

norm: It's nice to visit other's.
situation: Charlie has been busy at work with no time to see anyone, but he finally has a day off.
intention: Charlie wants to do something during his day off.
moral_action: Charlie goes to see his friend and hangs out with them.
moral_consequence: Charlie gets to enjoy the company of his friend and build upon the relationship.
immoral_action: Charlie stays at home and plays video games all day.
immoral_consequence: Charlie does not see anyone and does not forge social bonds.

norm: It's good to go out and socialize
situation: Henry spends most of his time alone in his house with little social contact.
intention: Henry would like to talk to someone to ease the loneliness.
moral_action: Henry decides to go out and hang with his friend for some time.
moral_consequence: Henry feels recharged and much better after spending time with his friend.
immoral_action: Henry decides to call a friend up and talk on the phone.
immoral_consequence: Henry still feels a bit lonely after the phone call because it wasn't very personal.

norm: It's good to communicate with other people.
situation: Bill is upset that Jane didn't clean off the TV when she cleaned the rest of the living room.
intention: Bill wants the TV cleaned.
moral_action: Bill asks Jane why she didn't clean the TV off as well when cleaning the room.
moral_consequence: Jane didn't realize that you could clean a TV, Bill points out how it's done and the issue stops occuring.
immoral_action: Bill just cleans it off himself and decides not to say anything to Jane.
immoral_consequence: Bill continues to get upset every time Jane cleans the room but not the TV.

norm: It's bad to lose something that belongs to your family.
situation: Mark's family is moving to a new home and Mark is using his truck to help out.
intention: Mark wants to drive some belongings to the new home.
moral_action: Mark puts in extra effort to ensure all the family items are secured in his truck and makes the drive.
moral_consequence: Mark and his family are glad they manage to move all their stuff without any major problems.
immoral_action: Mark does not properly secure his family belongings in his truck and loses a valuable item during the drive.
immoral_consequence: Mark's family is upset at Mark about the lost item.

norm: It is not good to be rude to your family
situation: Dave's parents need to go to work to earn a living and Dave needs to do house work for his parents.
intention: Dave wants to cook a meal for his parents.
moral_action: Dave makes a very nutritional and delicious meal for his parents.
moral_consequence: His parents thanks Dave for making a wonderful meal and agrees to take him to Disneyland next year.
immoral_action: Dave is angry and just cooks plain noodle for his parents.
immoral_consequence: His parents feel bad and deducts allowance for Dave.

norm: It's rude to break your dad's xbox controller.
situation: Ulysses' is playing call of duty on his father's xbox when the input lag causes him to lose the match.
intention: Ulysses wants to express his frustrations.
moral_action: Ulysses rants about his experience in a Call of Duty forum.
moral_consequence: Ulysses receives advice on how to reduce input lag.
immoral_action: Blaming the controller for his mistakes aloud, Ulysses slams the controller onto the table breaking the controller.
immoral_consequence: Ulysses has to pay for a new controller.

norm: It's good to put safety first.
situation: Sam slept in and is in danger of being late to work.
intention: Sam wants to get to work on time.
moral_action: Sam puts his seat belt on and drives to work at the speed limit.
moral_consequence: Sam arrives to work just in time to avoid getting in trouble.
immoral_action: Sam rushes to work in his car speeding and doesn't take the time to put his seatbelt on.
immoral_consequence: Sam get's into a car accident.

norm: You shouldn't steal your roommate's things.
situation: Jill notices that her roommate has a really cute shirt in her closet.
intention: Jill wants to wear the shirt when she goes out.
moral_action: Jill compliments her roommate on the shirt and asks to borrow it for a night.
moral_consequence: Jill's roommate feels validated in her sense of style and agrees to let her borrow it.
immoral_action: Jill takes the shirt and fails to return it.
immoral_consequence: Jill's roommate notices one day and gets extremely upset.

norm: It is good to inform your parents of your whereabouts.
situation: Seth's saw that his friends were playing down the street from his house.
intention: Seth wanted to play with his friends.
moral_action: Seth told his mother he was going to meet his friends before leaving.
moral_consequence: Seth's mother called him back for dinner when it started to get late.
immoral_action: Seth ran to play with his friends without telling his mother first.
immoral_consequence: Seth's mother thought he was missing and called the police to help find him.

norm: You shouldn't hate a parent over something minor.
situation: Tim was upset because his mom made him go to bed half an hour earlier than his friends.
intention: Tim wants to explain how he feels.
moral_action: Tim decides to sit down and explain why the minor issue was a big deal to him.
moral_consequence: Tim's mother understands and apologizes to Tim for the minor issue.
immoral_action: Tim complains and rants and is upset about what his mother did.
immoral_consequence: Tim's mother and everyone else he tells ignores him because the issue is so small.

norm: It is rude to ignore guests.
situation: Tom has the day off of work and wants to have some friends over.
intention: Tom wants to invite some friends over for drinks.
moral_action: Tom hosts a small get together and catches up with his buddies.
moral_consequence: Everyone has a good time at Tom's house.
immoral_action: Tom has friends over but focuses more on playing his video game.
immoral_consequence: Tom's friends feel that he is rude and don't have a good time.

norm: You should always pay people back if you owe money.
situation: Jennifer borrowed some money from Tammy last week, said she'd pay her back in a week  and just got her paycheck today.
intention: Jennifer wants more money in her account.
moral_action: Jennifer pays Tammy back what she owes her and gets another job too.
moral_consequence: Tammy respects Jennifer and feels closer to her as a friend.
immoral_action: Jennifer tells Tammy her job didn't pay her yet and to wait another week.
immoral_consequence: Tammy doesn't trust Jennifer anymore and reconsiders their friendship.

norm: You shouldn't yell at people in class.
situation: Nick is teaching his 3rd grade class when Jimmy in the back keeps being disruptive and talking to his friends.
intention: Nick wants to get Jimmy to stop disrupting the class.
moral_action: Nick tells Jimmy that he needs to get up and go to the principal's office because he's not capable of behaving.
moral_consequence: Jimmy goes to the principal's office where his parents are called in, and he learns a valuable lesson about following rules.
immoral_action: Nick throws a piece of chalk hitting Jimmy in the face and then screams at him for being a loser and tells him to shut up.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy is traumatized as he gets screamed at by an angry Nick and embarrassed to be called a loser in front of everyone.

norm: It's good to help customers with their problems.
situation: June is nearing the end of a long shift at her retail job when a customer approaches her for help with a time consuming problem.
intention: June wants to clock out, so she can get off her feet.
moral_action: June helps the customer until the next shift arrives then hands the customer issue over.
moral_consequence: June gets a customer compliment that her boss uses in her annual review.
immoral_action: June tells the customer to wait for the next shift to come and help her, then leaves the customer to wait.
immoral_consequence: June gets written up when her boss discovers the customer waiting.

norm: It's frowned upon snoop in someone's phone.
situation: Barry notices his boyfriend has been staying late at work and has been distant lately.
intention: Barry wants to find out if his boyfriend is having an affair.
moral_action: Barry ask his boyfriend after he comes home late to be truthful.
moral_consequence: Barry's boyfriend admits that he has been spending time with a coworker.
immoral_action: Barry grabs his boyfriend's phone one night and scrolls through messages.
immoral_consequence: Barry's boyfriend catches him and gets angry that Barry doesn't trust him.

norm: You're expected to help people when they need it.
situation: Steven's house had a tree fall down on the roof, and he knows his friend Anthony is talented carpenter.
intention: Steven needs help fixing his house.
moral_action: Steven ask Anthony for help, and Anthony is willing to help his buddy.
moral_consequence: Steven feels very happy that his friend is so willing to help.
immoral_action: Steven calls Anthony up on the phone and asks for help with his roof, and Anthony gives him a price quote.
immoral_consequence: Steven feels betrayed that Anthony won't help him for free.

norm: It is good to discuss holiday plans early.
situation: Susan and her family spend a weekend together for every Christmas break.
intention: Susan wants to make plans for the holiday.
moral_action: Susan starts planning their get together in the middle of August.
moral_consequence: All of Susan's family is able to plan their holiday and attend the get together.
immoral_action: Susan waits until three weeks before Christmas to try to make plans with her family.
immoral_consequence: All of Susan's family already have plans, and they miss their get together.

norm: You should tell your ex the truth about your feelings.
situation: Jack's ex wife asks him what happened in their relationship.
intention: Jack wants to end the conversation.
moral_action: Jack honestly points out the flaws he had with his ex-wife.
moral_consequence: His ex-wife thanks him and tries to improve for her next relationship.
immoral_action: Jack tells his ex wife that it was all his own fault and that he's just a terrible husband.
immoral_consequence: His ex-wife has three more failed marriages because Jack didn't tell the truth.

norm: It's not okay to stuff yourself with food.
situation: Joshua, who hasn't eaten anything all day, just sat down at an all-you-can-eat buffet.
intention: Joshua wants to satisfy his hunger.
moral_action: Joshua grabs a plate of food and some dessert but stops eating as soon as he feels comfortably full.
moral_consequence: Joshua really enjoys his meal and leaves the restaurant feeling invigorated and energized.
immoral_action: Joshua finishes his plate of food and then keeps going back for more helpings until he cannot eat another bite.
immoral_consequence: Joshua starts to feel sick to his stomach.

norm: It's good to care about the environment.
situation: Bill is packing up after a beach party when he notices that people have thrown pizza boxes into the recycling bin, and plastic cups onto the ground.
intention: Bill wants to finish packing.
moral_action: Once he finishes packing, bill moves the pizza boxes from the recycling to the trash, and rinses off the plastic cups before recycling them.
moral_consequence: The environment is a little cleaner as a result of Bill's efforts.
immoral_action: Bill ignores the incorrectly disposed boxes and cups, and continues with his packing.
immoral_consequence: The pizza boxes mess things up at the recycling facility, and the plastic cups make their way to the ocean.

norm: It is wrong to sexualize minors.
situation: Josephine enters her pre-teen daughter into a lot of beauty pagents.
intention: Josephine wants her daughter to win.
moral_action: Josephine dresses her daughter neatly in age-appropriate cloth and styles her hair nicely.
moral_consequence: Josephine's daughter wins awards in several of the pagents.
immoral_action: Josephine puts a lot of makeup on her daughter and dress her in skimpy provocative clothing.
immoral_consequence: Josephine's daughter is stalked and kidnapped by pedophile.

norm: It's rude to honk at cyclists.
situation: Matt is driving when he sees a cyclist riding on the shoulder.
intention: Matt wants to warn the cyclist of his approach.
moral_action: Matt flashes his lights several times at the cyclist.
moral_consequence: The cyclist sees and waves Matt past him.
immoral_action: Matt honks his horn at the cyclist to warn him.
immoral_consequence: The cyclist misinterprets the horn and makes an offensive sign at Matt.

norm: You shouldn't block your neighbor's house.
situation: James invited dozens of people over for a family reunion at his house, which had limited parking available.
intention: James wants to find parking for all his family members.
moral_action: James asks his neighbor if he can pay him for parking.
moral_consequence: The neighbor moves his car and lets the relatives use his driveway for a moderate fee.
immoral_action: James tells some of his family members to park in his neighbor's driveway.
immoral_consequence: James' neighbor calls a local tow company to tow the family members' cars.

norm: You should compliment someone when they get a new look.
situation: Carrie gets a new haircut and asks her boyfriend, Jim, what he thinks.
intention: Jim wants to respond to Carrie's new hair.
moral_action: Jim tells Carrie that her new hair really shows off her cheekbones.
moral_consequence: Carrie smiles and feels more confident than ever.
immoral_action: Jim tells Carrie he hates her new hair.
immoral_consequence: Carrie feels self-conscious and starts to cry about her hair.

norm: It's rude to comment negatively on people's clothing.
situation: Jim's friend got a new pair of jeans, and they ask Jim how they look in them.
intention: Jim wants to tell his friend what he thinks of their jeans.
moral_action: Jim says his friend's jeans look fine and adds that it's hard to go wrong with a pair of jeans.
moral_consequence: Jim's friend stops worrying about how they look in the new jeans.
immoral_action: Jim tells his friend that the jeans are really dorky and that they have terrible fashion sense.
immoral_consequence: Jim's friend loses confidence in how they look in their new jeans.

norm: It's good to help out children who have been bullied.
situation: Michael was playing on the playground during recess and a group of kids at the top of slide were keeping a boy from getting on.
intention: Michael wants to make new friends.
moral_action: Michael goes to the slide and asks the boy if he would like to go play somewhere more fun.
moral_consequence: Michael and the boy have fun at recess and become longtime friends.
immoral_action: Michael ignores what is going on at the slide and goes over to the jungle gym where he meets a new friend.
immoral_consequence: The boy at the bottom of the slide feels sad that others treat him poorly.

norm: It's wrong to have a one-sided relationship.
situation: Bobby and Grace have been living together since quarantine started, working from home and interacting a lot.
intention: Bobby wants to show grace an interesting video.
moral_action: Bobby shows Grace an interesting video on his computer and then watches a video in return, and they laugh together at both videos.
moral_consequence: Grace and Bobby continue enjoying their time in quarantine together and their relationship grows.
immoral_action: Bobby shows Grace an interesting video on his computer and when she tries to show him one back Bobby ignores Grace's video and walks away.
immoral_consequence: Grace gets tired of the one-sided behavior and breaks up with Bobby.

norm: It is bad to sleep with a married person.
situation: Susan's boss Jeffrey just got back from his honeymoon and is being flirtatious in the office.
intention: Susan wants to approach her boss about his flirtation.
moral_action: Susan tells her boss that she's not interested in being involved with a newly married man and asks him to stop.
moral_consequence: Susan's boss gets the message and looks for his affair outside of the workplace.
immoral_action: Susan asks her boss if he'd like to go somewhere more private and sleeps with him in his office.
immoral_consequence: Jeffrey's wife finds out about the affair and exposes Susan and Jeffrey for their inappropriate workplace relationship.

norm: You should never settle for less than you're worth.
situation: Jane is interviewing for a job as a marketing manager.
intention: Jane wants to work for this company.
moral_action: Jane is offered the job but details reasons why she is worth more than the original offer.
moral_consequence: Jane is hired at a higher salary, and she is able to afford many more things the rest of her life.
immoral_action: Jane is offered the job but does not negotiate her salary and takes one lower than average.
immoral_consequence: Jane will always make less money the rest of her career because she started off making lower.

norm: It's good to be supportive of someone in college.
situation: Keith is at home watching TV when his son who is away at college calls to ask for money.
intention: Keith wants to respond to his son's request.
moral_action: Keith tells his son t hat he can wire him some money, and he can pick it up at the bank.
moral_consequence: Keith's son is relieved he doesn't have to worry about whether he's going to eat and can concentrate on studying.
immoral_action: Keith tells his son that if he wants money he needs to get himself a job then.
immoral_consequence: Keith's son is stressed out and alone at college and is scared about how he'll find a job.

norm: Yelling is frowned upon.
situation: Jeremy is walking past the doors of a testing area when he receives a text about winning a prize.
intention: Jeremy wants to express his excitement.
moral_action: Jeremy makes a post on Twitter about his big win.
moral_consequence: One of his friends offers to take Jeremy out to the bar to celebrate his win.
immoral_action: Jeremy declares that he's one in a loud tone that echos down the halls.
immoral_consequence: Jeremy is scolded by the person in charge of the testing area for being disruptive.

norm: It's inappropriate to yell at people.
situation: Tom is about to give a speech to a crowd and there is a mic stand about four feet in front of him.
intention: Tom wants to let everyone hear him while he gives his speech.
moral_action: Tom walks up to the mic stand and addresses the crowd in a moderate voice using the microphone.
moral_consequence: The crowd claps after Tom gives his speech and are appreciative the sound was good and that he used a mic.
immoral_action: Tom decides not to use the mic stand and yells at the crowd.
immoral_consequence: The crowd shouts back at Tom to use the mic as his speaking is obnoxious to them.

norm: You shouldn't talk about rape in class.
situation: Mark is in biology class, and his teacher started bringing up the#MeToo movement.
intention: Mark wants to give his opinion on the movement.
moral_action: Mark tells his class that the men who are responsible for these abuses of power should be held accountable.
moral_consequence: A girl in Mark's class supports what Mark said and is happy that a man supports such a thing.
immoral_action: Mark tells the class that he thinks that women secretly wish to be sexually assaulted.
immoral_consequence: A girl in Mark's class who was previously abused feels triggered and starts thinking about her nightmare.

norm: You shouldn't laugh when people die.
situation: Keith is walking across the street when he sees a man get hit by a car.
intention: Keith wants to show his feelings about the situation.
moral_action: Keith starts to cry as he tries to process what he has just seen happen.
moral_consequence: The people in the crowd try to comfort Keith as he sits and cries.
immoral_action: Keith starts to laugh as the rest of the crowd rushes to try to save the man's life.
immoral_consequence: The people in the crowd accuse Keith of being cruel and insensitive.

norm: It is rude to say mean and hurtful things.
situation: Jen brings home a new hat she just bought and models it for her husband Dave, asking him what he thinks about it.
intention: Dave wants to respond to the question.
moral_action: Dave tells Jen that she looks beautiful with her hat on and that he wishes she wore it all the time.
moral_consequence: Jen is delighted that Dave likes her choice of hat and happily prances around the house humming.
immoral_action: Dave tells Jen that she looks hideous and that she is so obese that a hat doesn't make any difference to her looks.
immoral_consequence: Jen is devastated and sobs uncontrollably feeling totally unsupported and hurt by her husband.

norm: Doxxing people is wrong.
situation: Jenelle has been getting harassed by someone named Claire on social media.
intention: Jenelle wants Claire to pay for what she's done.
moral_action: Jenelle reports Claire's account for bullying.
moral_consequence: Claire's account gets suspended.
immoral_action: Jenelle finds out where Claire lives and posts her address all over social media.
immoral_consequence: People begin going to Claire's home and throwing rocks at her window.

norm: It's wrong to drink too much alcohol.
situation: Ted goes to the bar with his friends for a night out with the boys.
intention: Ted wants to have an awesome time on his night out.
moral_action: Ted has a few shots and cracks jokes with his friends all evening.
moral_consequence: Ted and his friends have a great boys night.
immoral_action: Ted gets wasted and acts foolishly in front of his friends, laughing the whole time.
immoral_consequence: Ted is embarassed the next day when his friends rehash the night with him.

norm: You should be responsible with your pets.
situation: Kyle has a husky that requires a lot of exercise.
intention: Kyle wants to find an activity to do with the dog.
moral_action: Kyle goes long distance running with the dog regularly.
moral_consequence: The dog will get exercise and be well tempered.
immoral_action: Kyle throws a ball at the dog a couple times in doors at night.
immoral_consequence: The dog will not get enough exercise and become destructive.

norm: It's responsible to put something away after you use it.
situation: John is working on his car and using a lot of tools.
intention: John wants to finish the project.
moral_action: John finishes up fixing his car and takes the time to put all his tools back in garage where they belong.
moral_consequence: The next time John needed a tool for a project he knew exactly where to find them.
immoral_action: John finishes fixing his car and rushes inside to get cleaned up without putting his tools back in his garage.
immoral_consequence: A passerby with no morals notices the John's tools and steals them and now John has no tools.

norm: It is bad to leave pets unattended in a car
situation: Mateo has just picked up his dog Frizzy from the vet, and he needs to pick up an item from the grocery store.
intention: Mateo needs to get food.
moral_action: Mateo calls his roommate and asks them to pick up the items he needs.
moral_consequence: Mateo and Frizzy have a nice weekend at home.
immoral_action: Mateo leaves Frizzy in the backseat of the car while he goes shopping.
immoral_consequence: Mateo has to make another trip to the vet when he discovers Frizzy unconscious in the backseat.

norm: It's good to be responsible and work.
situation: Jay's job is offering extra shifts to employees because they're understaffed.
intention: Jay wants to pick up some extra hours at work.
moral_action: Jay volunteers for an extra shift and spends it working as hard as he can.
moral_consequence: Jay is allowed to pick up as many extra shifts as he wants when his boss finds out what a good job he did.
immoral_action: Jay volunteers for an extra shift but spends it playing on his cell phone.
immoral_consequence: Jay isn't allowed to work any more extra shifts when his boss finds out he was slacking off.

norm: It's wrong to lie to get a job.
situation: Nima is a physicist making his resume to get a tenure-track college physics professor position, something Nima didn't explicitly study.
intention: Nima wants to impress the person who reads the resume.
moral_action: Nima lists the degrees that he's earned and his work experience in the field of physics.
moral_consequence: The department hires Nima for a research position in the physics department instead of a professor.
immoral_action: Nima says that he has a Ph.D. in a field that he actually doesn't have.
immoral_consequence: Nima is hired based on the fictional Ph.D. and realizes that he's completely incompetent for the job.

norm: You shouldn't ask someone if they are a school shooter.
situation: James was assigned a new lab partner who died his hair jet black and wore a black trench coat.
intention: James wants to reassure himself his lab partner is friendly.
moral_action: James asks his lab partner what kind of hobbies he has as an ice breaker.
moral_consequence: It turns out that James and his lab partner like some of the same bands, and they come to enjoy working together.
immoral_action: James asks his lab partner if he would ever consider shooting up the school.
immoral_consequence: James' lab partner is offended and gives him the silent treatment, making lab work very difficult.

norm: It's not okay to give up on your child.
situation: Joan warned her son that he'd get in big trouble if he ever got arrested again, and he got arrested.
intention: Joan needs to either punish or help her son.
moral_action: Joan gets her son out of jail and talks to him about what problems he's been going through.
moral_consequence: Joan's son feels that he can depend on Joan and feels like he's taken care of.
immoral_action: Joan decides to not help her son and doesn't call him in jail.
immoral_consequence: Joan's son starts to become depressed and has no one to turn to.

norm: You shouldn't lie about being sick.
situation: Rick has stayed up all night watching a series on Netflix and is scheduled to work in the morning.
intention: Rick wants to take the day off.
moral_action: Rick uses some of his personal time off for a day off.
moral_consequence: Rick's employee gets to cover his shift and earn extra money that week.
immoral_action: Rick calls in and tells his boss that he is sick.
immoral_consequence: Rick's boss is concerned what kind of sickness he might have.

norm: You should be there for your friend at their wedding.
situation: Nina just found out that a college she is considering is have open house on the same day as her good friend's wedding.
intention: Nina wants to get a tour of the college.
moral_action: Nina calls the college to schedule a private tour so that she can attend her friend's wedding.
moral_consequence: Nina's friend is happy that Nina cared enough to show up.
immoral_action: Nina decides to skip the wedding and go to the open house instead.
immoral_consequence: Nina's friend feels Nina doesn't really care that much about her.

norm: It's rude to keep repeating someone's name over and over.
situation: Cai needs permission to sleep over at his friend's house, but his mother is working.
intention: Cai wants to get his mother's attention.
moral_action: Cai waits until his mother is at a good stopping point before asking his mother about the sleepover.
moral_consequence: Cai spends the entire weekend at his friend's house.
immoral_action: Cai pokes his mother while chanting his mother's name to get her attention.
immoral_consequence: Cai's mother punishes him by making him do all of the chores in the house.

norm: You should not inject a needle into your veins.
situation: Hank is training to be a nurse in school and is practicing how to give injections, with volunteers nearby.
intention: Hank wants to inject a person.
moral_action: Hank gets a volunteer and inserts a needle into him.
moral_consequence: The volunteer flinches, but Hank keeps his hands steady and succeeds.
immoral_action: Hank inserts the needle into his own vein, not wanting to bother a volunteer.
immoral_consequence: Hank flinches while inserting the needle and twists it, causing blood to spurt out of him.

norm: Its wrong to physically hit a relative.
situation: Jonah is at his brother Al's house in the summer and Al pulls a prank on Jonah by soaking him with a water balloon.
intention: Jonah wants to react to being soaked.
moral_action: Jonah tells Al that he got him this time but that he better watch out Jonah will get him back.
moral_consequence: Al laughs along with Jonah and tells him that he looks forward to seeing what Jonah will come up with in retaliation.
immoral_action: Jonah runs up to Al and swings his fist into Al's face, knocking Al to the ground.
immoral_consequence: Al is shocked that Jonah would resort to violence and cowers in fear of being hit again.

norm: Getting rid of important family items is disrespectful.
situation: Paula is helping her parents move to a different town and their house has many items such as albums.
intention: Paula wants to clean out her parent's house.
moral_action: Paula asks her parents about the picture albums she finds and what to do with them.
moral_consequence: Paula's parents will explain the pictures to Paula and teach her about the past.
immoral_action: Paula throws away picture albums she finds.
immoral_consequence: Paula's parents become upset at Paula and saddened the memories are lost.

norm: You shouldn't throw out things that can be recycled.
situation: Sonya is cleaning her apartment and going through old items.
intention: Sonya wants to get rid of any unnecessary clutter.
moral_action: Sonya sorts her paper products into recycling and donates her old books to local schools.
moral_consequence: Sonya has contributed to solving the issue of waste and pollution.
immoral_action: Sonya finds old books and notebooks and tosses them into the trash.
immoral_consequence: Sonya has contributed to the growing waste and pollution problem.

norm: You shouldn't be upset at your deceased family member's partner.
situation: Juliet's father passed recently, and she is at her step mother's house visiting.
intention: Juliet wants to ask about some heirlooms of her father's.
moral_action: Juliet inquires about the heirlooms of her father's and asks if her step mother still has them.
moral_consequence: Juliet's step mother is touched that Juliet would want to know about the heirlooms that also mean a lot to her.
immoral_action: Juliet asks her step mother about the heirlooms while implying that she has kept them away from Juliet on purpose.
immoral_consequence: Juliet's step mother does not like the insinuation Juliet is making.

norm: You shouldn't kick out your partner if they are depressed.
situation: Alfred's girlfriend is suffering from depression and has made their apartment very messy because she has no motivation to clean.
intention: Alfred wants to live in a clean apartment.
moral_action: Alfred encourages his girlfriend to go to therapy and cleans all of her messes in the meantime.
moral_consequence: Alfred and his girlfriend stay together and Alfred feels really tired all the time from doing all the cleaning.
immoral_action: Alfred tells his girlfriend she will have to move out if she can't clean up after herself.
immoral_consequence: Alfred and his girlfriend break up, and he gets a clean apartment all to himself.

norm: You shouldn't mess with other people's toothbrushes.
situation: Serena recently had a huge argument with her sister, Hayley, and is still very upset with her.
intention: Serena wants to vent out her frustrations with Hayley.
moral_action: Serena tells Hayley she wants to talk about their argument.
moral_consequence: The sisters are able to discuss their feelings and make up without toothbrushes involved.
immoral_action: Serena uses Hayley's toothbrush to scrub the toilet, then puts it back in its place.
immoral_consequence: Hayley gets a mouth infection and needs to visit the hospital.

norm: It's not okay to ruin your home.
situation: Jeff likes to party and use fireworks, which his landlord allows him to do as long as he is respectful of the home.
intention: Jeff wants to throw a big party tonight.
moral_action: Jeff's friends come over to party, and he makes sure everyone is in the backyard away from the house before setting off fireworks.
moral_consequence: Everyone enjoys the fireworks and the house remains unharmed.
immoral_action: Jeff's friends come over to party, and they all begin setting off fireworks from the front porch.
immoral_consequence: One of the fireworks hits a window and breaks the glass, prompting Jeff's landlord to evict him.

norm: People shouldn't have sex with other people's partners.
situation: Robert is single and often hangs out with a nice couple, whom he knows are going through a rough patch in their relationship.
intention: Robert wants to have sex with someone soon.
moral_action: Robert keeps on looking for a partner and meets a cool girl with whom he sleeps.
moral_consequence: Robert's relationship with the new girl is wonderful and Robert is over the moon.
immoral_action: Robert has a tryst with the wife of the nice couple.
immoral_consequence: The couple ends up divorcing because of that and Robert feels really guilty.

norm: You shouldn't talk back to teachers.
situation: Steve is in class, and gets an answer wrong, the teacher makes a snotty comment.
intention: Steve wants to address the comment.
moral_action: Steve waits until after class, and confronts the teacher saying his feelings were hurt.
moral_consequence: The teacher realizes she was wrong, and apologizes, and promises to not do it again.
immoral_action: Steve instantly fires back, calling the teacher a complete loser.
immoral_consequence: The teacher sends Steve to detention for openly disrespecting her.

norm: You should try to get along with your coworkers
situation: Bob's coworker always plays their radio very loudly at the office making it difficult for Bob to do his work.
intention: Bob wants to talk to his coworker about their radio use.
moral_action: Bob explains that the radio is making work difficult for Bob and asks his coworker to turn it down or wear headphones.
moral_consequence: Bob and his coworker come to a compromise about the radio and continue to have a respectful relationship.
immoral_action: Bob yells at his coworker to turn off their radio and threatens to make a complaint to the boss.
immoral_consequence: Bob and his coworker have a poor relationship form then on which creates an uncomfortable work environment.

norm: It's not okay to be overly focused on a career.
situation: Paul just started his own business in an area that he is passionate about, and he is setting up a new home office.
intention: Paul wants to double his business's revenue in the next three months.
moral_action: Paul develops a business strategy and brings in consultants to help implement it in a timely manner.
moral_consequence: Paul's business thrives while Paul gets to work normal hours, making his family happy.
immoral_action: Paul spends 14 hours each day in his new office trying to do everything himself to grow his business.
immoral_consequence: Paul burns himself out and his family feels left out and frustrated by the fact that they never see him.

norm: You shouldn't disobey others.
situation: Neal's parents have tried to teach him to have responsible sex.
intention: Neal wants to have lots of sex.
moral_action: Neal always wears a condom before he has sex.
moral_consequence: Neal gets to have lots of sex.
immoral_action: Neal has a lot of unprotected sex.
immoral_consequence: Neal increases his chances of getting an STD.

norm: It is kind to hose people in your home.
situation: Lorne's old friend from college just called him to ask him if him and his wife could stay at Lorne's place while they are visiting Lorne's city.
intention: Lorne wants his house to be tidy and impeccable at all times.
moral_action: Lorne accepts to house his friend and his wife and asks them to put all their stuff in one room while they're visiting.
moral_consequence: Lorne's friend is delighted to see Lorne again and enjoys his time with him.
immoral_action: Lorne turns down his old friend because he doesn't want to end up with a mess of suitcases and clothes in his house.
immoral_consequence: Lorne's friend is very disappointed and feels Lorne let him down.

norm: It's mean to reject people.
situation: Tony has had a crush on Tina for a long time.
intention: Tony wants to ask Tina out on a date for this weekend.
moral_action: Tony asks Tina if she would like to go on a date with him this weekend, and she tells him yes.
moral_consequence: Tony is very happy he finally asked her out after having a crush on her for so long.
immoral_action: Tony asks Tina if she will go out with him this weekend, and she tells him she doesn't want to date him.
immoral_consequence: Tony feels really bad and wishes that he'd never asked Tina out.

norm: It's bad to pay bills late.
situation: Anna is having technical problems with her old computer and has some major bills which are due.
intention: Anna wants to buy a new computer.
moral_action: Anna pays all her bills first then charges the new computer to one of her credit cards.
moral_consequence: Anna is up to date on her bills and enjoys her new computer.
immoral_action: Anna decides to avoid making a payment on her phone bill to buy the computer.
immoral_consequence: Anna's phone service gets cut off, and she is charged a late fee on top of that.

norm: It is best to separate friendship and money.
situation: Jack is reluctant to lend his friend Bob a large sum of money.
intention: Jack wants to maintain his friendship with Bob.
moral_action: Jack suggests various financial institutions that can give Bob a loan.
moral_consequence: Jack is glad to help his friend without jeopardizing their friendship.
immoral_action: Jack lends Bob the money and is surprised when Bob fails to pay him back promptly.
immoral_consequence: Jack gets angry and his friendship with Bob deteriorates.

norm: It's mean to make fun of someone with poor vision.
situation: Art is in the office break room with Karen, and Jill, who is blind.
intention: Art wants to say something amusing to Karen.
moral_action: Art Tells Karen the plot to the first Star Wars movie.
moral_consequence: Karen hears and interesting story and Art gets to participate in an innocuous social exchange.
immoral_action: Art Says to Karen that Jill has retard eyes.
immoral_consequence: karen feels that Art is a cruel person, and Jill feels embaressed and ashamed at being ridiculed.

norm: It's encouraged you compromise if you're disagreeing with someone
situation: Mary and her husband are about to paint their living room but don't really agree on the color they should choose: pale yellow or orange?
intention: Mary wants the living room to look warm and bright.
moral_action: Mary decides to make a bit of a change to her initial idea and agrees with her husband on a deep yellow.
moral_consequence: Mary's husband likes the new color they chose, which is closer to what he initially wanted.
immoral_action: Mary insists that they must paint the living room a pale yellow.
immoral_consequence: Mary's husband is frustrated by her lack of flexibility and doesn't like the pale yellow.

norm: It's not okay to spend your money gambling.
situation: Nathan, a former compulsive gambler, is invited to the casino by his coworkers after work.
intention: Nathan wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Nathan drops by his favorite bar for the night to order something to drink.
moral_consequence: Nathan befriends another former gambler at the bar.
immoral_action: Nathan gambles his entire paycheck on the slot machines at the casino.
immoral_consequence: Nathan is unable to pay his bills.

norm: It's rude to just leave somewhere.
situation: Henry is working in the middle of a shift at the office and things are really hectic.
intention: Henry wants make things a little less hectic.
moral_action: Henry focuses on the little steps he can take to complete the bigger tasks and tackles them one at a time.
moral_consequence: Henry is able to work efficiently and reduce his stress by staying focused on just one thing at a time.
immoral_action: Henry stops the work he is doing and makes his way to the door without letting anybody know.
immoral_consequence: Henry is able to relax for the day but is fired from his job for just leaving.

norm: It's rude to take advantage of a friend's generosity.
situation: James offers to buy Bob a dinner that evening and Bob is happy about it.
intention: Bob wants to enjoy the meal.
moral_action: Before the dinner, Bob warns James that he usually orders expensive meals.
moral_consequence: James is okay with that, and he works it out with Bob.
immoral_action: Bob orders a $300 dollar meal that evening.
immoral_consequence: James is upset because he wasn't planning on spending that much.

norm: It's bad when your friend convinces you to hate yourself.
situation: Faith's best friend Peggy often belittles her achievements and rarely offers encouragement.
intention: Faith wants to have a happier relationship with Peggy.
moral_action: Faith tells Peggy how much her criticism hurts.
moral_consequence: Faith is able to build a healthier relationship with Peggy when she adjusts her behavior.
immoral_action: Faith doesn't address Peggy's criticisms.
immoral_consequence: Faith is made to feel worse as Peggy's toxic friendship gains strength.

norm: It is risky to make a cat hiss.
situation: Clair tries to walk past a cat in a dark hallway with no lights on.
intention: Clair wants to get past the cat.
moral_action: Clair waits for the cat to walk past her before moving through the hall.
moral_consequence: The house stays quiet as Clair gets past the cat and into another room.
immoral_action: Clair steps on the cat's tail, it hisses loudly at her and makes noise.
immoral_consequence: The cat's hissing wakes up the whole house and the others are upset with Clair.

norm: It is bad to let children be the boss.
situation: Timmy hates going to school every day, but Greg doesn't want him staying at home all day.
intention: Greg wants Timmy to go to school.
moral_action: Greg doesn't listen to Timmy and makes him go to school every day.
moral_consequence: Timmy gets educated and starts to get used to going to school.
immoral_action: Greg agrees to let Timmy go to school every other day.
immoral_consequence: Timmy doesn't get the education that he needs, and he becomes lazy.

norm: You shouldn't hire someone that isn't eligible for a position.
situation: Kyle runs his own business, and he knows his friend's son is looking for a job.
intention: Kyle wants to hire someone to fill a position in the office.
moral_action: Kyle hires the most experienced applicant that he happened to interview.
moral_consequence: Kyle's new worker helps the business do better over time.
immoral_action: Kyle meets with his friend's son and hires him even though he has no work experience.
immoral_consequence: Kyle's business goes through production problems with the young man working for him.

norm: You shouldn't lie about stupid things.
situation: Chad is talking about TikTok with his friend, and his friend asked him how many followers he has.
intention: Chad wants to impress his friend.
moral_action: Chad says that he only has 150 followers, but he just started using the app one week ago.
moral_consequence: Chad's friend is impressed that he has as many followers as he does in such a short period of time.
immoral_action: Chad tells his friend that he has 300,000 followers on TikTok.
immoral_consequence: Chad's friend is able to find out that he's lying and doesn't understand why he would lie.

norm: It's rude to try to make others feel guilty.
situation: Chad's son was playing outside, but he left the door open, and their dog ran away.
intention: Chad wants to talk to his son.
moral_action: Chad tells his son that everyone makes mistakes and that he should remember to close the door next time.
moral_consequence: Chad's son feels a little bit better and doesn't feel as guilty.
immoral_action: Chad tells his son that he'll never get to see their dog again.
immoral_consequence: Chad's son feel really guilty and misses the dog even more.

norm: It's proper to give your full attention to a speaker.
situation: Andy is listening to a speech given at a graduation when his phone vibrates in his pocket.
intention: Andy wants to check his phone.
moral_action: Andy waits until the speaker is done and then pulls out his phone and looks at it.
moral_consequence: The speaker is happy that he had the crowd's attention.
immoral_action: Andy pulls his phone out of his pocket and looks at it.
immoral_consequence: The speaker notices a man looking at his phone and is disheartened.

norm: You shouldn't open someone else's mailbox.
situation: Todd was waiting for a new credit card in the mail, but he didn't receive it.
intention: Todd wants to check if his neighbors received his mail instead.
moral_action: Todd asks his neighbors if they happened to receive any mail that was for him.
moral_consequence: Todd's neighbors think that he is polite, and Todd is able to find out if they received his mail.
immoral_action: Todd looks in his neighbor's mailbox without asking and goes through their mail.
immoral_consequence: Todd is invading people's privacy and could be in trouble if they find out.

norm: It's bad to make your parents feel stressed.
situation: Jane is in trouble with the law because of her addictions and has been arrested unbeknownst to her parents.
intention: Jane wants to get out of jail.
moral_action: Jane waits to have her case heard by a judge and commits to going to rehab in lieu of further jail time.
moral_consequence: Jane's parents are relieved to hear their daughter is making a good life decision finally.
immoral_action: Jane calls her parents hoping they can bail her out sooner rather than later.
immoral_consequence: Jane's parents become worried about the situation with their daughter.

norm: It's wrong to rearrange someone's house without their permission.
situation: Jill has been going to her sister's house to catsit while her sister is away, and noticed that the house is in terrible shape.
intention: Jill wants her sister's house to be nicer.
moral_action: Once Jill's sister is back, Jill suggests helping her refresh her decor a bit.
moral_consequence: Jill's sister is happy with the suggestion and enjoys working on her house with Jill.
immoral_action: Jill decides to move furniture around and redecorate her sister's house, while her sister is gone.
immoral_consequence: Once she comes back, Jill's sister feels intruded upon and judged by Jill.

norm: It's good to be a team player.
situation: Larry is playing basketball with his friends and is guarded on the 3 point line.
intention: Larry wants to decide on his next move.
moral_action: Larry passes the ball to an unguarded teammate.
moral_consequence: Larry's teammate successfully scores.
immoral_action: Larry decides to get some glory and take a shot despite being guarded.
immoral_consequence: Larry misses and the opposing team takes the ball.

norm: It's expected that people will be quiet at the movies.
situation: Rick and his friends are going to the midnight showing of the new summer super hero movie.
intention: Rick wants to see the new movie.
moral_action: Rick cheers and applauds when appropriate.
moral_consequence: Rick and his friends love the movie and make plans to go see it again.
immoral_action: Rick cheers and yells though the movie.
immoral_consequence: Rick gets asked to leave the movie because he is ruining it for everyone else.

norm: It's rude to share with some people and not others.
situation: James' mother brought home several boxes of discontinued candy from the sweet shop where she works.
intention: James wants to share the candy with his school friends.
moral_action: James brings in a whole box of candy and asks the teacher if he can give a few pieces to everyone.
moral_consequence: James is extremely popular and several kids say they want to work where his mom works when they grow up.
immoral_action: James brings enough candy for himself and his friends and starts passing it out in class.
immoral_consequence: The teacher confiscates' James candy because he didn't bring enough for everyone to share.

norm: It's not okay to be careless with things.
situation: Brett, who has trouble keeping track of things, just got an expensive new phone and is outside at the park playing with it.
intention: Brett wants to take a quick walk.
moral_action: Brett puts the phone in his pocket and walks around the park, then sits back down.
moral_consequence: Brett keeps his phone while getting his exercise and enjoys the phone for a long time to come.
immoral_action: Brett puts his phone down on a bench and takes a quick lap around the park for exercise.
immoral_consequence: Someone else sees the phone and takes it, and Brett is dejected that he lost his phone.

norm: It's wrong to prevent someone from enjoying their life.
situation: Valarie is overseeing a project with tight deadlines, and one of her workers Emily wants to celebrate her birthday.
intention: Valarie wants to meet her goals.
moral_action: Valarie switches around Emily's shift with another one of her coworkers.
moral_consequence: Emily works harder on the project because she feels like her coworkers respect her.
immoral_action: Valarie forces Emily to work on her birthday.
immoral_consequence: Emily is sad because she can't celebrate her birthday.

norm: Leaving the dishes dirty is lazy behavior.
situation: Marc is living in an apartment by himself for the first time and is responsible taking care of himself and the apartment.
intention: Marc wants to devote himself to his passion towards video games.
moral_action: Marc creates a schedule that includes a large block of time for video games and smaller blocks for household chores.
moral_consequence: Marc is able to keep onto of cleaning while still being able to spend substantial time on his passion for video gaming.
immoral_action: Marc spends all of his waking hours on video games while neglecting the other areas of his life, like washing the dishes.
immoral_consequence: Dirty dishes pile up in Marc's sink and attract bugs, causing his apartment to smell and him to feel embarrassed and disgusted.

norm: It's  good to call the police on possible pedophiiles.
situation: Carl is in the park when he notices a little girl Jane being stalked by a pedophile, Phil.
intention: Carl wants to do something about the Pedophile.
moral_action: Carl calls the police and tells them there's a pedophile stalking children in the park.
moral_consequence: The police come arrest Phil and take him away preventing him from offending again.
immoral_action: Carl tells Phil to leave and if he catches him again he'll do something to him.
immoral_consequence: Phil leaves but later comes back and stalks a different child and abducts it.

norm: It is good to show your appreciation towards a veteran.
situation: During a Veteran's Day celebration, John's class is singing a song for an audience of Veterans.
intention: John wants to get the most attention in the show.
moral_action: John holds a military salute at the end of the song and keeps a serious face.
moral_consequence: The Veterans are impressed by John's respectful action and applaud him.
immoral_action: John makes a loud farting sound with his mouth during a quiet part of the song being sung.
immoral_consequence: John's teacher and class are embarrassed and the veterans are angry at John's interruption and disrespect.

norm: It is unhealthy to eat too much
situation: Garfield loved to eat pasta, in fact he couldn't stop eating pasta until it was all gone.
intention: Garfield wants to eat more pasta.
moral_action: Garfield decides not to make too much pasta since he knows he won't stop eating it.
moral_consequence: Garfield eats all the pasta he made, and he still feels alright.
immoral_action: Garfield made a lot of pasta, and he kept eating and eating until he was sick.
immoral_consequence: Garfield was sick for a while from eating too much because he couldn't stop eating pasta.

norm: You shouldn't be cheap when it comes to your health.
situation: Kelly noticed that her leg had been hurting her for a while.
intention: Kelly wants her leg to stop hurting.
moral_action: Kelly goes to the doctor to see what was wrong with her leg.
moral_consequence: Kelly is prescribed medication and exercises that make her leg better.
immoral_action: Kelly puts ice on her leg for a few minutes before going back to work.
immoral_consequence: Kelly has to eventually have surgery because she didn't see about her leg problem.

norm: You should plan group trips with everyone involved.
situation: Connor is taking his wife and three kids on a vacation, they're driving cross country to visit relatives.
intention: Connor wants to have an enjoyable trip.
moral_action: Connor plans out the route in advance, taking suggestions from his wife and kids for activity stops.
moral_consequence: Everyone in the car gets to do some activities that they like, and it's a very enjoyable trip for everyone.
immoral_action: Connor plans out the route in advance, including activity stops, without consulting his family.
immoral_consequence: Connor's route and activities are of interest to him and his wife, but the kids are bored and whine a lot.

norm: You shouldn't act so entitled.
situation: Tim is at a crowded restaurant for dinner.
intention: Tim wants to tell the waiter his order.
moral_action: Tim orders an item from the menu.
moral_consequence: The kitchen of the restaurant can fill all the orders for the night promptly.
immoral_action: Tim makes numerous adjustments to his order and states the order should be out at a specific time at a specific temperature.
immoral_consequence: The kitchen of the restaurant gets backed up fulfilling Tim's wishes and other diners get.

norm: You should be kind to your friends.
situation: Mary's friend is getting married.
intention: Mary wants to be in the wedding.
moral_action: Mary offers to help her friend contact vendors.
moral_consequence: Mary's grateful friend asks her to be her maid-of-honor.
immoral_action: Mary tells her friend to put her in the wedding party.
immoral_consequence: Mary's friend is angry at being put on the spot, and doesn't invite Mary to the wedding.

norm: It is expected that you do not bite people.
situation: Zoe grabs Chloe from the front with a tight hug.
intention: Chloe wants to get out of the hug.
moral_action: Chloe asks Zoe to let her go.
moral_consequence: Zoe lets go of the hug.
immoral_action: Chloe bites Zoe on the neck.
immoral_consequence: Zoe starts bleeding and crying.
