norm: You shouldn't be a slut.
situation: Mary has been having sexual urges while her boyfriend Dan has been away on military deployment.
intention: Mary wants to satisfy her sexual urges.
moral_action: Mary buys a vibrator to deal with her sexual urges.
moral_consequence: Dan is glad that Mary was able to stay faithful.
immoral_action: Mary has sex with a lot of Dan's friends while he's gone.
immoral_consequence: Dan eventually finds out and breaks up with Mary for being unfaithful.

norm: It's bad to judge a whole store based on gossip.
situation: Jon heard about a new pizza place in his area and wanted to check it out.
intention: Jon wanted to learn more about the pizza place.
moral_action: Jon visits the pizza place after work to see what the hubbub was all about.
moral_consequence: Jon becomes a loyal customer of the pizza place after seeing what it's like in there firsthand.
immoral_action: Jon read online that the pizza place was run by pedophiles, so he decided not to go.
immoral_consequence: Jon is never able to experience what the pizza place is like due to fake news.

norm: It's unscrupulous to mislead people who trust you with finances.
situation: Bill is gathering financial and market information to put into a prospectus.
intention: Bill wants to raise money from investors to expand his business.
moral_action: Bill accurately reflects his current financial position in his correspondence with his investors.
moral_consequence: Bill receives the required funding and expands his business.
immoral_action: Bill pads his current revenue numbers and omits some of his liabilities in the promotional materials.
immoral_consequence: Some of Bills investors lodge a complaint with the SEC.

norm: It's not okay to become a racist in life.
situation: Dan is an employer and has to choose from three very qualified black men and one talent-less white friend of his.
intention: Dan wants to decide who to hire.
moral_action: Dan decides to pick the most qualified person, which is one of the black men.
moral_consequence: The new employee does well and Dan feels proud of his choice.
immoral_action: Dan decides to pick his white friend for this job, ignoring the credentials of the black applicants.
immoral_consequence: Dan is sued in court for racial discrimination by a black applicant and Dan feels very sorry.

norm: It's bad to go back on a promise.
situation: Julie arranged to pick up a friend from the airport, but found out that her new boss is hosting a happy hour at the same time.
intention: Julie wants to make a good impression on her boss.
moral_action: Julie tells her boss that she has to pick up a friend from the airport and says that they should plan another happy hour soon.
moral_consequence: Julie's friend is grateful that she picked her up, and Julie's boss is happy to move the happy hour back a day.
immoral_action: Julie decides to go to the happy hour instead and texts her friend that they can find a cab after they land.
immoral_consequence: Julie's friend has to pay a lot of money for the cab ride and is too angry to meet with her later that night.

norm: It's rude to back out on plans with friends.
situation: Timmy had planned to go on a camping trip with friends, but learns that his cousin is coming to visit him that same weekend.
intention: Timmy wants to spend time with his cousin.
moral_action: Timmy invites his cousin to come camping with him and his friends.
moral_consequence: Timmy's friends enjoy their time with him and his cousin and have a great time on their camping trip.
immoral_action: Timmy cancels his plans with his friends.
immoral_consequence: Timmy's friends are very disappointed.

norm: It is wrong to start fires in a park.
situation: Marcy and her friends brought wood, a lighter, and s'mores ingredients to the picnic they are at.
intention: Marcy wants to eat the s'mores at the picnic soon.
moral_action: Marcy decides not to set up a fire and instead prepare the s'mores without roasting them, and then eats.
moral_consequence: Marcy's and her friends are able to enjoy the meal in peace and quiet.
immoral_action: Marcy sets up the wood and lights a bonfire at the park to eat the s'mores.
immoral_consequence: Marcy gets in trouble for lighting a bonfire at the park and her friends feel bad.

norm: It's rude to use your phone while having a conversation.
situation: Mark is talking and eating with his mom at a restaurant when his phone dings.
intention: Mark wants to check his email.
moral_action: Mark tells his mom he needs to use the bathroom and checks his phone email there.
moral_consequence: Mark's mom thinks Mark is polite and cares about her feelings.
immoral_action: Mark pulls out his phone as his mom is talking and checks his email.
immoral_consequence: Mark's mom gets upset and thinks Mark doesn't care about her.

norm: It's rude to dictate what your children's surnames will be.
situation: John and Andrea are expecting their first child, which they know will be a boy from the ultrasound.
intention: John wants to name his new son after his grandfather, Bob.
moral_action: John explains that he was very close to his grandfather and appeals to Andrea to allow him name their first son Bob.
moral_consequence: Andrea agrees that if they can pick a name that they both like, they will use Bob as a middle name, as a compromise.
immoral_action: John insists that the name of their first son will be Bob, and he will not entertain any other ideas.
immoral_consequence: Andrea gets angry and tells John that she will not approve the name Bob, no matter what, leaving both new parents upset.

norm: It's not normal to Hate Yourself
situation: Jane is a teenager and is struggling socially at school through no fault of her own.
intention: Jane wants to stop struggling.
moral_action: Jane seeks out help from her parents, counselors, and doctors in hopes of fixing her problems.
moral_consequence: Jane is able to work out the issues she is having with the professional help and begins to see things in a different light.
immoral_action: Jane begins to blame herself for her problems and grows to resent herself to the point she thinks harming herself is the only fix.
immoral_consequence: Jane suffers further and sadly never comes back out of the emotional hole she made for herself.

norm: It's good to eat a healthy breakfast.
situation: Matt is getting ready to go to work.
intention: Matt wants to get some food before work.
moral_action: Matt fixes himself an omelette with veggies and turkey sausage for breakfast.
moral_consequence: Matt has a fruitful and productive morning at work from the protein energy of his healthy breakfast.
immoral_action: Matt stops at a fast food place and loads up on junk food.
immoral_consequence: Matt has a mid-morning crash from his junk food breakfast and falls behind on his work.

norm: It's rude to crush children's imaginations.
situation: Maggie's son is often writing wild stories in his spare time and his grades have dropped because of his avid imagination.
intention: Maggie wants her son to get better grades.
moral_action: Maggie supports her sons writing but tells him it's important to do better at school, which helps him get his grades higher.
moral_consequence: Maggie's son continues writing lavish stories, which later leads to him having a career in literature.
immoral_action: Maggie demands that her son stop writing stories and get his grades higher, or he will be punished, which leads to her son getting better marks.
immoral_consequence: Maggie's son becomes despondent and spends way less time with his friends and family.

norm: It is nice to invite and include other people
situation: Billy is handing out invitations to his birthday party when he gets to a classmate he doesn't like much.
intention: Billy wants to decide whether or not to give the classmate an invitation to his birthday.
moral_action: Billy gives his classmate an invitation to his birthday party even though he doesn't really like them.
moral_consequence: Billy's classmate it happy that they are able to join in Billy's birthday celebration.
immoral_action: Billy doesn't give the classmate he doesn't like an invitation and just walks past them.
immoral_consequence: Billy's classmate feels sad to be left out of Billy's birthday party.

norm: It's wrong to let young children near unpredictable dogs.
situation: Gail is walking with her son on the sidewalk when she sees a large dog with no leash walking towards them.
intention: Gail wants to decide what to do concerning the dog.
moral_action: Gail crosses the street with her son to avoid the dog.
moral_consequence: The dog avoids interacting with her son.
immoral_action: Gail lets her son walk closely beside the dog.
immoral_consequence: The dog may bite her son.

norm: It is bad to have incest relations.
situation: Hank, a single man, goes to a family reunion and sees a lot of beautiful relatives.
intention: Hank wants to find a potential wife while at the reunion.
moral_action: Hank meets a fifth cousin by marriage, dates her, marries her, and has a child with her.
moral_consequence: The child is normal and has no genetic abnormalities that anyone can see.
immoral_action: Hank meets a second cousin, eventually marries her, and has a child with her.
immoral_consequence: The child has a recessive genetic disorder because Hank and his wife share a defective gene.

norm: It's nice to adopt animals.
situation: Harold has noticed a stray dog walking around his neighborhood for weeks.
intention: Harold wants to get the dog off the street.
moral_action: Harold takes the dog to the vet and files adoption paperwork.
moral_consequence: The dog has a new home in Harry's comfortable house.
immoral_action: Harold calls animal control to have the dog taken away.
immoral_consequence: The dog is placed in a crowded animal shelter with other strays.

norm: It's wrong to shame people for being fat.
situation: Teddy is at a party with a bunch of friends and is introduced to an overweight girl.
intention: Teddy wants to feel good about himself.
moral_action: Teddy starts talking about how much he loves cooking and exchanges healthy recipes with the overweight girl.
moral_consequence: The overweight girl loves talking with Teddy and feels excited about trying new recipes.
immoral_action: Teddy starts talking about how he stays fit and directly tells the girl how great it feels to have good self control.
immoral_consequence: The overweight girl is ashamed at being called out as having low self control.

norm: You shouldn't exclude people just because they don't drink.
situation: Peter is friends with a lot of people, including some who don't like alcohol.
intention: Peter wants to celebrate his birthday at a local bar with some friends.
moral_action: Peter invites as many people as possible to the celebration.
moral_consequence: Peter's non-drinking friends have fun alongside everyone else at the celebration.
immoral_action: Peter only invites his alcohol drinking buddies to the birthday celebration.
immoral_consequence: Peter's non-drinking friends become mad at him for not inviting them.

norm: YOu are expected to treat your friends' siblings with respect.
situation: Casey, a seven year old, glares at his sister Sabrina when she refuses to let him have one of her cookies.
intention: Casey wants to express his anger.
moral_action: Casey talks about his intense feelings and his desire with his mother.
moral_consequence: Sabrina overhears the conversation and bakes another batch of cookies for her family.
immoral_action: Casey sticks out his tongue at Sabrina calling her a toad before walking away.
immoral_consequence: Sabrina avoids Casey for the next three days.

norm: It is wrong to take money that is not yours.
situation: Tanya is working at the register at a diner that is in the center of town.
intention: Tanya wants to make extra money when she is working on her shift.
moral_action: Tanya asks her boss if she can work a little later that night.
moral_consequence: Tanya is able to wait on a dozen more customers and makes more tips.
immoral_action: Tanya takes some money out of the register and puts it in her pocket.
immoral_consequence: Tanya's boss sees her and fires her from her job that same night.

norm: You should never get so angry that you hit someone.
situation: Matt is with him roommate cooking dinner in the kitchen of their shared apartment.
intention: Matt wants his roommate to clean up after himself.
moral_action: Matt asks his roommate to clean up for himself or else he'll move out.
moral_consequence: Matt's roommate is afraid he wouldn't be able to pay the entire rent by himself and agrees to clean up after himself, making Matt feel happy.
immoral_action: Matt angrily confronts his roommate about the messy kitchen and hits him so hard that he falls backward.
immoral_consequence: Matt's roommate stumbles into the kitchen window and shatters it, causing Matt to spend hundreds of dollars on a new window.

norm: It's not okay to hurt others with your work.
situation: Lizelle just got a new job at a celebrity news magazine in the city.
intention: Lizelle wants her first project to succeed.
moral_action: Lizelle writes a story of how a local actress, Cleo, overcame adversity to succeed.
moral_consequence: Cleo includes the story in the CV and ends up getting better acting work because of it.
immoral_action: Lizelle writes a story about an embarrassing event in the life of Cleo, a local actress.
immoral_consequence: Cleo is embarrassed by the story and her career takes a big dive.

norm: You shouldn't humiliate teachers in front of the whole class.
situation: Charlie is a high school student.
intention: Charlie wants to have some fun.
moral_action: Charlie tells a good pun related to the lesson the teacher is going over.
moral_consequence: Everyone in the class laughs and the teacher appreciates Charlie's wit.
immoral_action: Charlie mocks their teacher's voice and posture and yells over them to get attention.
immoral_consequence: The students laugh, the teacher is humiliated, and the class is disrupted.

norm: It's bad to be too picky about your food order.
situation: Bill and Nancy are dining at a restaurant and have begun their meal when the waiter comes to ask how everything is.
intention: Bill wants to answer the waiter's question.
moral_action: Bill tells the waiter that everything is quite delicious and perfect.
moral_consequence: The waiter is delighted to hear that his customers are enjoying their meal.
immoral_action: Bill tells the waiter that the portion size is rather small and that the meal is unseasoned and needs more salt.
immoral_consequence: The waiter is annoyed by Bill's nitpicking and snobbish demeanor.

norm: Terrorism is cowardly and criminal.
situation: Jamie is angry to hear that her government is unwilling to address the climate change crisis.
intention: Jamie needs to do something to motivate her government officials to take climate change more seriously.
moral_action: Jamie writes a thoughtful letter to her congressional representative and copies several high profile news outlets on the content of the message.
moral_consequence: Her message is received and published for others to read, validating her argument and furthering her cause.
immoral_action: Jamie starts a fire in a government building to show her disapproval of government policy related to climate change.
immoral_consequence: Jamie's message is misrepresented and nobody even knows that she was protesting climate change policy and people are injured in the explosion.

norm: It's bad to blame others for your problems.
situation: Ariel is thinking about the failures she has made in life.
intention: Ariel wants to feel better about her failures.
moral_action: Ariel accepts the challenge of self-improvement and determines to do better.
moral_consequence: Ariel corrects her defects and stays on good terms with her parents.
immoral_action: Ariel blames her parents' poor child raising skills for her failures.
immoral_consequence: Ariel hates her parents and yells at them whenever she can.

norm: People shouldn't wear out their welcome.
situation: Molly plans to vacation upstate for a weekend in the same town that her friend Leslie lives in.
intention: Molly wants to save money on a hotel by staying with Leslie during her vacation.
moral_action: Molly completes her upstate vacation and thanks Leslie for her hospitality at the end of the weekend.
moral_consequence: Leslie is glad for the short reunion she had with Molly, and suggests they do it again next year.
immoral_action: Molly has had so much fun during her weekend away, that she decides to extend her vacation for another week.
immoral_consequence: Leslie is worn out by Molly's presence and doesn't call her ever again once she leaves.

norm: It's bad to expose others to your illness.
situation: Frank has been home sick with the flu and is still experiencing symptoms.
intention: Frank wants to get some soup to help the natural healing process.
moral_action: Frank stays at home and orders contact free delivery from a place with soup.
moral_consequence: Frank prevents the spread of the flu he has to others.
immoral_action: Frank goes to the grocery store to pick up some cans of soup.
immoral_consequence: Frank puts people at risk and contaminates any surfaces he touches.

norm: It is good to drink responsibly.
situation: Chase is at a party with some friends.
intention: Chase wants to drink some alcohol.
moral_action: Chase drinks one or two beers.
moral_consequence: Chase is tipsy, but maintains control.
immoral_action: Chase decides to drink a bottle of Everclear.
immoral_consequence: Chase gets sick, throws up everywhere, and passes out.

norm: It's good to rescue abandoned animals.
situation: Kate wants a new dog, but she doesn't know where she should buy one.
intention: Kate wants to buy a dog.
moral_action: Kate decides to buy a dog from a rescue shelter.
moral_consequence: Kate adopts an abandoned puppy and helps a rescue shelter stay in business.
immoral_action: Kate decides to buy a dog from a puppy mill.
immoral_consequence: Kate supports a puppy mill, and it is able to keep breeding dogs.

norm: You should have respect for other people's possessions.
situation: Garrett's car battery is dead.
intention: Garrett wants to drive to the store.
moral_action: Garrett borrow's his roommate's car, and makes sure to fill up the tank to show his appreciation.
moral_consequence: Garrett's roommate is grateful and happy he can save money on gas.
immoral_action: Garrett borrow's his roommate's car without permission, and leaves the gas tank almost empty.
immoral_consequence: Garrett's roommate is angry and has to pay the refill the tank.

norm: It's inconsiderate to make other people cover your work shift
situation: Erin was given tickets to see her favorite band live, but she has to work at the restaurant that night.
intention: Erin wants to see the concert.
moral_action: Erin talks with her coworker a few days before the concert to get her shift covered, so she can see the concert.
moral_consequence: Erin's coworker who needed the extra money can work the shift and no one has to change their plans at the last minute.
immoral_action: Erin calls in sick at the last moment before her shift to be able to go to the concert.
immoral_consequence: Erin's coworker has to stay to cover her shift and then her coworker has to cancel her dinner plans with friends who are moving out of town.

norm: It is not okay to ruin other people's friendships.
situation: Carl dislikes his friend Jane's other friend Mack.
intention: Carl wants to spend less time with Mack.
moral_action: Carl declines invitations to hang out with Jane when Mack is invited too.
moral_consequence: Carl stays friend with Jane but does not have to see Mack.
immoral_action: Carl tells Jane that Mack did horrible things to get her to stop being friends with Mack.
immoral_consequence: Jane finds out Carl lied and stops being friends with him.

norm: It's bad to play a joke that damages someone's property.
situation: Daniel and his brother Jake celebrate April Fool's Day every year.
intention: Daniel wants to play a memorable joke on Jake for the holiday.
moral_action: Daniel puts a bucket of water at the top of Jake's door.
moral_consequence: Jake opens the door, the water falls on him, and he laughs.
immoral_action: Daniel puts sugar in the gas tank of Jake's car.
immoral_consequence: Jake's car won't start, and he becomes furious.

norm: It is alright to not know how to act.
situation: Victoria is at a formal dinner and does not know all the customs, and it is making her anxious.
intention: Victoria wants to relieve her anxiety.
moral_action: Victoria asks the person next to her which fork she should be using.
moral_consequence: The person next to Victoria is happy to help her, and she ends up enjoying her dinner.
immoral_action: Victoria has a small meltdown over the stress and runs from the dinner.
immoral_consequence: Victoria feels embarrassed and vows never to go to a formal dinner again.

norm: You shouldn't rush your co-workers.
situation: Kevin works in an office, is working on a team project, and needs someone else to finish his part before continuing.
intention: Kevin wants to be productive.
moral_action: Kevin finds some side jobs that he hasn't completed yet to fill the time.
moral_consequence: The side jobs get done and Kevin's coworker finished his part.
immoral_action: Kevin insists that the person finish his part in the next hour, so he can keep working.
immoral_consequence: The person gets annoyed and intentionally slows down to vex Kevin.

norm: Using profanity against family members is rude.
situation: James' mother asked him to clean his room when he was in the middle of a video game.
intention: James wants to keep playing his video game.
moral_action: James tells his mom he'll start cleaning his room in ten minutes, betting she'll forget by then.
moral_consequence: James' mom forgets what she asked him to do, and he gets to keep playing his game.
immoral_action: James screams at his mom to leave his room and calls her a c-word.
immoral_consequence: James' mom leaves him alone for that afternoon, but ends up shipping him out to military school.

norm: It's good to do favors for close friends.
situation: Jenny is friends with Colleen and Colleen asks Jenny if she can pick her up at the airport.
intention: Jenny wants to respond to Colleen's request.
moral_action: Jenny tells Colleen that she can pick her up.
moral_consequence: Colleen will think Jenny is a good and reliable friend.
immoral_action: Jenny tells Colleen she should take a cab from the airport.
immoral_consequence: Colleen will think Jenny is not a good friend.

norm: It is expected that you act respectfully toward your coworkers
situation: Karen is listening to complaints of Jane, her coworker, about her spouse's financial problems.
intention: Karen wants to comment on Jane's situation.
moral_action: Karen gives some good advice to Jane and promises to keep the conversations between them.
moral_consequence: Jane feels appreciated and thanks Karen for being helpful.
immoral_action: Karen disclosed Jane's situation to another coworker, who later asks Jane about her problems.
immoral_consequence: Jane feels betrayed and not being respected.

norm: It's wrong to infringe on someone's copyright.
situation: Gabe is hired by an influential politician to create ads for his campaign.
intention: Gabe wants to create something memorable.
moral_action: Gabe combines footage of the politician during events to create a small narrative of their life and values.
moral_consequence: The politician receives a flood of donations after the ad goes online.
immoral_action: Gabe uses a popular song from a popular artist during the advertisement.
immoral_consequence: The politician is sued by the musical artist for using their song without permission.

norm: You should not make fun of people's mental difficulties.
situation: Rick is in class watching John who is developmentally challenged struggle to solve a math problem on the blackboard.
intention: Rick wants to make a comment to John.
moral_action: "Rick yells out loud towards John ""Hey Johnny, you can do it buddy just concentrate!""."
moral_consequence: John feels extra confidence from being cheered on to do better and concentrates harder on solving the problem.
immoral_action: "Rick yells to John ""Hey John are you a moron or something?"" and begins to laugh loudly pointing at him."
immoral_consequence: John is embarrassed and recoils in horror at Rick's comments, terrified what everyone is thinking.

norm: You shouldn't give handouts to people who don't deserve it.
situation: Cara's brother plays video games all day and asked her for some money to help him buy a new TV.
intention: Cara has to decide whether to give her brother money.
moral_action: Cara tells his brother to get a job in order to buy a new TV.
moral_consequence: Cara's brother has to feel motivated to work if he really wants a new TV.
immoral_action: Cara gives his brother the money that he wanted, so he can buy a TV.
immoral_consequence: Cara's brother, and he continues to be lazy and doesn't pay her sister back.

norm: It's disruptive to call someone out in a movie theater.
situation: Antoinette is watching a movie in a theater and sees a friend come into the theater five minutes into the movie.
intention: Antoinette wants to get her friend's attention so the friend can sit with her.
moral_action: Antoinette quietly waits for her friend to get closer to her before making nonverbal movements to usher her friend close.
moral_consequence: Antoinette is able to enjoy the rest of the movie with her friend.
immoral_action: Antoinette makes a loud call for attention to her friend that everybody in the theater can hear.
immoral_consequence: Antoinette gets popcorn thrown at her by other moviegoers for her rude outburst, and she feels embarrassed.

norm: It is wrong to hit women
situation: "James is shopping at a WalMart when he hears a security guard shout, ""Stop, thief!"" as a woman runs past him carrying ten iPhones."
intention: James wants to stop the woman from stealing from the WalMart.
moral_action: James steps into the woman's path, so she runs into him and knocks them both down.
moral_consequence: The woman is arrested for theft, and the security guard and manager thank James.
immoral_action: James punches the woman in the face as she runs by him.
immoral_consequence: The woman is arrested for theft, but James is also arrested for assault.

norm: You should only take ADHD medication if you have ADHD.
situation: Jake has had trouble paying attention in class so his friend offered him some Adderall.
intention: Jake wants to pay better attention in class.
moral_action: Jake tells his teacher that he's having trouble paying attention, and his teacher gives him advice.
moral_consequence: Jake learns how to better pay attention without having to resort to using drugs.
immoral_action: Jake takes some Adderall in order to better remember what his teacher was teaching.
immoral_consequence: Jake can become addicted to the drug when he realizes how it feels.

norm: It's nice to tell people to have a great day.
situation: Neil is at the office and about to walk past his coworker Jack in the hallway.
intention: Neil wants to greet Jack.
moral_action: Neil tells John hello and tells him that he hopes John has a wonderful day today.
moral_consequence: John is pleased to be greeted so pleasantly and it makes him smile.
immoral_action: Neil gives John a tiny smirk and waves at him with a quick and mumbled hello.
immoral_consequence: John thinks that Neil is awkward and wonders why he seems so nervous around him.

norm: It's wrong to hate fat people.
situation: Ken meets up with his friend John who also brought along a new person to the group, Lonny who is dangerously obese.
intention: Ken wants to say something to John about bringing a new friend unannounced.
moral_action: Ken tells John that it's a little weird that a 3rd person is with them but that he'll give Lonny a fair chance.
moral_consequence: Lonny is happy to hear that Ken isn't terribly upset that he's there and that he'll be nice to him.
immoral_action: Ken tells John that he hates fat people because they're sloths and can't believe John would just spring one on him like that.
immoral_consequence: Lonny is insulted that Ken hates fat people and is destroyed inside as his self conscious mind goes even deeper into self loathing.

norm: It's bad to do something that is your co-worker's responsibility.
situation: Jeff has a new colleague who doesn't have a lot of experience and works slowly.
intention: Jeff wants to help his coworker finish his work before the end of the day.
moral_action: Jeff has a meeting with his coworker during which he gives him helpful pointers about how to complete tasks quickly.
moral_consequence: Jeff's coworker completes all his tasks efficiently and is proud of himself.
immoral_action: Jeff decides to finalize one of his coworker's projects.
immoral_consequence: Jeff's coworker feels disenfranchised and underestimated.

norm: You shouldn't report your neighbors without a good reason.
situation: Rasheeda has a neighbor Mike who lives above them that is up late at night.
intention: Rasheeda needs it quieter at night because she works early.
moral_action: Rasheeda meets Mike and explains that she works early and that sometimes Mike makes too much noise.
moral_consequence: Mike is understanding and makes an effort to be quieter, Rasheeda hears Mike less often.
immoral_action: Rasheeda calls the apartment security nightly for noise complaints whenever she hears Mike moving after 10pm.
immoral_consequence: Rasheeda is warned for harassment and abuse of apartment resources once it is determined that Mike is not violating any rules.

norm: You should thank friends for inviting you to do things
situation: Brian is at a friend's party.
intention: Brian wants to go home and get ready for work tomorrow.
moral_action: Brian makes sure to tell his friends goodbye and shows his appreciation for being invited to the party.
moral_consequence: Brian's friends are glad he had a good time and are sure to invite him to their next party.
immoral_action: Brian slips out the back door without saying goodbye to anyone.
immoral_consequence: Brian's friends think he is rude and don't invite him next time.

norm: Slow and steady wins the race.
situation: Tyrone is starting a fitness routine and is looking for ways to build muscle in a short time.
intention: Tyrone wants to do all he can to build muscle.
moral_action: Tyrone follows a strict diet and has help from a personal trainer to meet his goals.
moral_consequence: Tyrone gains a steady 1-2 pounds of muscle a month, gradually becoming large and strong.
immoral_action: Tyrone starts taking anabolic steroids and eating a lot to promote lots of muscle growth.
immoral_consequence: The steroids' side effects hurt Tyrone, giving him heart trouble and other health problems.

norm: You should be polite to preachers.
situation: Mike, a gay atheist, sees a preacher come into his store.
intention: Mike wants to let the preacher know how he feels about religion.
moral_action: Mike asks if he can voice his feelings about religion to the preacher to hear his response.
moral_consequence: Mike and the preacher have a respectable conversation and become friends.
immoral_action: "Mike mocks the preacher for believing in a ""fake god""."
immoral_consequence: The preacher no longer shops at the store Mike works at and deprives them of business.

norm: It is important to teach children independence.
situation: Will is a parent of a child in an elementary school.
intention: Will wants their child to hand in a science project.
moral_action: Will gives tips to their child about the science project but lets the child do the work.
moral_consequence: Will's child learns how to prepare and execute projects.
immoral_action: Will does the entire science project for their child for the child to hand in.
immoral_consequence: Will's child does not learn how to do project for them self.

norm: You shouldn't fart around other people because it's gross.
situation: Kyle is working and is in an elevator with guests, but has a stomach ache and bad gas.
intention: Kyle needs to decide whether to sneak one out or hold it in.
moral_action: Kyle holds it in until he can get away.
moral_consequence: Kyle is relieved that he got through it.
immoral_action: Kyle carefully lets out what he can.
immoral_consequence: A guest tells the manager and Kyle is very embarassed.

norm: It's expected that you'll be kind toward your siblings.
situation: John and Chris are two ten year old brothers living with their parents.
intention: John wants his parents to love him more than his they do his brother.
moral_action: John treats his brother Chris very well especially in front of his parents.
moral_consequence: Chris is much happier and John's parents think John is a model child.
immoral_action: John beats Chris up whenever he can and also tells his parents that Chris does bad stuff.
immoral_consequence: Chris becomes very sad and John's parents find out the truth and punish John.

norm: It's wrong to be a glutton.
situation: Matthew comes home from work and feels hunger pangs in his stomach.
intention: Matthew wants to choose something to eat.
moral_action: Matthew makes a meal that consists of vegetables, protein, and carbohydrates.
moral_consequence: Matthew will gain good nutrients from his meal.
immoral_action: Matthew orders a bucket of fried chicken and a pizza and eats all of it.
immoral_consequence: Matthew will gain a lot of weight and decrease his heath.

norm: It's good to keep track of children.
situation: Claire takes her child Rod to the park for the afternoon.
intention: Claire wants to occupy herself while Rod plays.
moral_action: Claire follows Rod around the park and shows him how to use the playground equipment.
moral_consequence: Rod picks some wildflowers and gives them to Claire at the end of the day to thank her for taking him to the park.
immoral_action: Claire lies down and takes a nap on the grass.
immoral_consequence: Rod runs into the forest surrounding the park and gets lost.

norm: It's wrong to steal someone's vehicle.
situation: Wallace is walking home on a hot summer day and passes an empty running and unlocked car.
intention: Wallace wants to get home and out of the heat.
moral_action: Wallace calls out trying to the owner of the vehicle while remaining a distance from it and lets them know they left it unlocked and then continues walking home.
moral_consequence: The owner of the vehicle is thankful for Wallace's warning and secures their vehicle.
immoral_action: Wallace looks around before entering the vehicle and using it to get home quicker.
immoral_consequence: The person that owns the vehicle that Wallace stole is angered when they find out the vehicle is missing and their day is ruined.

norm: You shouldn't want to be friends with murderers.
situation: Phil is studying behavioral science with a focus on serial killers.
intention: Phil wants to pick the mind of a serial killer.
moral_action: Phil arranges to conduct monitored interviews with a convicted serial killer.
moral_consequence: Phil is able to get the killer to open up and share important data with him.
immoral_action: Phil starts a correspondence with a convicted serial killer and soon develops a friendship with him.
immoral_consequence: As Phil gets closer to the killer he begins to adopt some of his beliefs.

norm: You shouldn't leave people behind.
situation: Jess is a track coach, and one of the members of the team keeps stopping to get their breath as everyone else runs.
intention: Jess wants to decide how to handle the member.
moral_action: Jess goes back and stays by the member until they can run again.
moral_consequence: The member is appreciative of Jess and will work to make her proud.
immoral_action: Jess doesn't come back to help the member and continues to run.
immoral_consequence: The member feels bad and feels like they let Jess down.

norm: You shouldn't make someone who is positive cry.
situation: Bart's friend Kip is very excited about a video game that is coming out.
intention: Bart wants to comment on Kip liking the video game.
moral_action: Bart says he can't wait to play the game with Kip.
moral_consequence: Kip will feel happy that Bart wants to play the game with him.
immoral_action: Bart says that video games are for babies and dumb people.
immoral_consequence: Kip will become upset and cry.

norm: It's not okay to beg strangers for treats.
situation: Ben, who is five years old and hungry, is waiting for his mother to get out of an appointment, when he notices a woman eating crackers next to him.
intention: Ben wants to get food.
moral_action: After his mother gets out of her appointment, Bill tells his mother that he's hungry.
moral_consequence: Bill's mom buys him some food on the way home.
immoral_action: Ben asks the woman next to him to give him some of her crackers multiple times.
immoral_consequence: Ben's mother finds out about his behavior and scolds Ben.

norm: It’s wrong to yell racial slurs.
situation: James is walking in a park when he sees two black men named Mark and Phil coming toward him.
intention: James wants to start a conversation with the two men.
moral_action: "James motions over to Phil and Mark and says ""hey guys come here""."
moral_consequence: Phil and Mark look at each other, shrug and happily walk over to see what the stranger wants.
immoral_action: "James screams ""hey blackies"" at the two men in an attempt to call them over."
immoral_consequence: Mark and Phil are disgusted by James' racism and curse at him as they walk away.

norm: It's nice to celebrate anniversaries.
situation: James' wife Sandy mentions that their wedding anniversary is coming up and asks him if he's planned anything.
intention: James wants to respond to Sandy's question.
moral_action: James tells Sandy that he has planned something but that it's a surprise, and she'll have to wait.
moral_consequence: Sandy is bursting with excitement to find out what it is and is happy that her man planned something for them.
immoral_action: James tells Sandy that since it's just another day in their ordinary life he hasn't planned anything.
immoral_consequence: Sandy is sad and hurt that James isn't paying careful attention to their important relationship dates.

norm: Snooping on someone is wrong.
situation: Eric is feeling suspicious over one of his partner's friends who seems to be too friendly with her.
intention: Eric wants to put his mind at ease.
moral_action: Eric is open about his concerns and brings them up to his partner directly.
moral_consequence: Eric's partner feels bad that he was uncomfortable and reassures him.
immoral_action: Eric goes through his partners devices to check if anything is going on.
immoral_consequence: Eric's partner finds out what he's doing and feels her privacy has been violated.

norm: It's rude to tell someone to go away.
situation: Jason has had a guest at his apartment for a few hours and Jason would like them to leave already.
intention: Jason wants to indicate that it's time for his guest to leave.
moral_action: Jason yawns and mentions how busy he is tomorrow and how he should get some rest soon.
moral_consequence: Jason's guest understands Jason's polite hints that it's time for them to depart, and they soon do so.
immoral_action: Jason tells his guest to leave the apartment as they've been there for too long.
immoral_consequence: Jason's guest is really insulted and embarrassed by Jason telling them to go away so bluntly.

norm: You shouldn't badmouth someone's religion.
situation: Joe is invited to attend his best friend Zack's church.
intention: Joe wants to respond to the invitation.
moral_action: Joe thanks Zack for the invitation and says he will check it out.
moral_consequence: Zack feels supported by his best friend.
immoral_action: Joe tells Zack that his religion is stupid, and he has no interest in going to church.
immoral_consequence: Zack is upset and ends his friendship with Joe.

norm: It is mean to take advantage of other people.
situation: Jason's sister Georgia is a meek but very talented freelance designer who has trouble asserting herself.
intention: Jason wants Georgia to design a logo for him.
moral_action: Jason hires Georgia to design the logo for him.
moral_consequence: Georgia designs a logo Jason is happy with and is compensated for her time and work.
immoral_action: Jason asks Georgia to design the logo for him for free since he's family.
immoral_consequence: Georgia feels obligated to help Jason and loses out on paying work because she is busy with Jason's logo.

norm: You shouldn't put up with someone who makes racist jokes.
situation: Jack's buddy Tim keeps making racist jokes about every race, including his own.
intention: Jack wants to decide to tell Tim or not about the jokes.
moral_action: Jack tells Tim that he won't deal with the racist jokes anymore.
moral_consequence: Tim stops telling the racist jokes because of Jack.
immoral_action: Jack doesn't like the jokes but deals with them because Tim is a good friend otherwise.
immoral_consequence: Jack keeps looking the other way each time Tim tells a joke.

norm: You shouldn't bludgeon dead birds with bricks.
situation: Zach finds a dead bird near a run-down brick wall and is curious about it.
intention: Zach wants to experiment with the bird.
moral_action: Zach uses his sleeve to handle the dead bird and examine its features.
moral_consequence: Zach learns some things about bird anatomy.
immoral_action: Zach takes a nearby fallen brick and smashes the dead bird with it.
immoral_consequence: Gore and guts fly everywhere, including on to Zach's clothes.

norm: It's rude to tell your father what to do.
situation: Ron is at his parent's house, and sees that the lawn is massively overgrown.
intention: Ron wants the lawn to get cut.
moral_action: Ron goes into the garage, gets the mower and cuts the grass himself.
moral_consequence: Ron's father is very thankful that his son is taking care of him.
immoral_action: Ron tells his father that he needs to cut the lawn, that the neighbors will be upset.
immoral_consequence: Ron's father is embarrassed that his son called him out.

norm: It's good to buy things for your partner.
situation: It is  Billy and Shirly's 25th anniversary this year and Shirly had been thinking about it her whole life.
intention: Billy wants to celebrate his anniversary with his wife.
moral_action: Billy takes his wife out to a nice dinner and buys her a special ring for the important anniversary.
moral_consequence: Shirly is thrilled with the ring and has something special to remember the day the rest of her life.
immoral_action: Billy not knowing what to do decides they could watch the game and eat left overs.
immoral_consequence: Shirly feels unloved and like billy her husband doesn't care or think about her.

norm: Spending time with one's family is to be expected.
situation: Alexander lives in the same town as his immediate family and today is his mother's birthday.
intention: Alexander wants to enjoy his night.
moral_action: Alexander buys a gift for his mother and heads over to her place to spend the night with his family.
moral_consequence: Alexander's mom appreciates that her son came over for her birthday.
immoral_action: Alexander decides to head to the bar to have some drinks with friends despite it being his mother's birthday.
immoral_consequence: Alexander's mom misses him at her birthday party and wonders why he did not come.

norm: It's good to give others tips to help them out.
situation: Nick is the company computer guy and is helping a coworker with a common computer error.
intention: Nick wants to fix the problem.
moral_action: Nick takes the time to explain to his coworker how the error happened and shows how to do the quick fix.
moral_consequence: Nick's coworker appreciates the tips and tricks that Nick shows them and feels more confident using the computer.
immoral_action: Nick asks the coworker to move aside and quickly fixes the problem before leaving.
immoral_consequence: The coworker feels dumb that they couldn't fix it when it was such a quick fix Nick and then feels even worse when they repeat the error soon after.

norm: It's bad to act impolitely when you're in a store.
situation: Geraldine is grocery shopping, but she can't find some of the items she needs.
intention: Geraldine wants to find the missing items.
moral_action: Geraldine asks an employee if the missing item might be located elsewhere in the store.
moral_consequence: Geraldine finds what she needs.
immoral_action: Geraldine yells at the store workers, and demands that they get the items she needs.
immoral_consequence: Geraldine is kicked out of the store.

norm: It's wrong to body shame people.
situation: Tyler and Mykel took off their shirts to go for a swim in a public park, prompting Tyler to compare his body with Mykel’s.
intention: Tyler wants to feel more confident about his physique.
moral_action: Tyler laughs and tells Mykel that they're both in decent shape and have nothing to be ashamed of.
moral_consequence: Tyler feels better about himself and bonds with Mykel.
immoral_action: Tyler makes fun of how scrawny Mykel is compared with him.
immoral_consequence: Mykel is put off and doesn't like Tyler anymore, even though Tyler feels better about his body now.

norm: It is bad to purposely try to make people jealous
situation: Eddie, while standing near an alley where a homeless man is begging, realizes he has won the lottery when he checks the lotto numbers on his phone.
intention: Eddie wants to tell someone that he just won.
moral_action: Eddie calls the local hospital and tells them that he will donate some money once the lottery winnings are paid.
moral_consequence: The homeless man overhears Eddie and as the homeless man gets aid from the hospital, he's delighted.
immoral_action: Eddie turns to the homeless man in the alley and screams at him mockingly that he has just become a millionaire.
immoral_consequence: The homeless man feels ashamed of his lot in life and embarrassed for being mocked and angry for being made jealous.

norm: It's rude not to share with others.
situation: John is at a restaurant with his friends, their food has just arrived and John notices that his plate of fries is humongous.
intention: John wants to eat some fries.
moral_action: After putting some fries on his plate, John moves it into the middle of the table and invites his friends to help themselves.
moral_consequence: John is offered some food from his friends' plates in return.
immoral_action: John eats all the fries on his plate.
immoral_consequence: John feels really gross and has a stomach ache all evening.

norm: It's bad to to lie to get out of work.
situation: Jerry is a baseball fan that works evening shift at a lab.
intention: Jerry wants to go to the game for his favorite team.
moral_action: Jerry switches shifts with a co worker so that he can go to the game.
moral_consequence: Jerry enjoys the game and is able to make up the work hours the next day.
immoral_action: Jerry calls in sick and then goes to the game.
immoral_consequence: Jerry is tagged on facebook at the game by a friend and the boss fires him after finding out.

norm: It's good to vent to your friends.
situation: Harry was back at home after spending a hard day at work.
intention: Harry wants to let out his anger.
moral_action: Harry tells his roommate all about why his day was so bad.
moral_consequence: Harry's roommate gives him a beer from the fridge and offers to order a pizza.
immoral_action: Harry starts to yell at his roommate and throws a vase at him.
immoral_consequence: Harry's roommate moves out and Harry has to pay the lease himself.

norm: It's crazy to suggest testing weapons on random people.
situation: Wesley is a weapons researcher working in a group on a new type of rail gun.
intention: Wesley wants to test how the gun works.
moral_action: Wesley suggest testing the weapon by using it in a closed course with mannequins.
moral_consequence: The gun is tested without harming anyone, and Wesley is congratulated for his idea.
immoral_action: Wesley suggest testing the weapon by shooting it at people on the street.
immoral_consequence: Wesley is immediately fired and told he needs to seek professional help.

norm: It's frowned upon to go back on your word.
situation: Charles, a journalist, invites Martin, a criminal with a record, to an interview and promises him safety from prosecution.
intention: Charles wants to keep Martin from committing more crimes.
moral_action: Charles has the interview and tries to convince Martin to leave a life of crime.
moral_consequence: Martin sees the need for change and promises to leave crime.
immoral_action: Charles contacts the police and has them show up at the meeting and arrest Martin.

norm: You shouldn't steal money.

norm: It's impolite to overshare details about your bodily functions.

norm: It's wrong to hurt a kitten.

norm: It's bad to use your ex.

immoral_consequence: The psychiatric staff confines Jack to his room and the patients get scared.

norm: You shouldn't throw water on people.
situation: Dave and his wife Wendy are walking through the park, holding water bottles when a wasp lands on Wendy's head.
intention: Dave wants to chase the wasp away from Wendy.
moral_action: Dave waves in the direction of the wasp, near Wendy's head to get it to fly away.
moral_consequence: Wendy is happy that Dave noticed a danger and acted quickly to try to prevent harm to her.
immoral_action: Dave pops the top off his water bottle and pours it on Wendy's head to get the wasp to fly away.
immoral_consequence: Wendy screams as the cold water runs down her head and body and is angry with Dave for soaking her in public.

norm: It's rude not to help your coworkers.
situation: David is at work, and sees that a coworker is struggling to get his work done.
intention: David wants the coworker to stop struggling so much.
moral_action: David jumps in to assist his coworker, lightening his workload.
moral_consequence: David's coworker is very thrilled that his coworker cares so much.
immoral_action: David runs and tells his boss that his coworker can't keep up.
immoral_consequence: David's boss comes out and yells at his coworker, making him even more stressed.

norm: It's kind to be there for someone who is crying.
situation: Jack's friend's dog just passed away, and she can't stop crying about it.
intention: Jack wants to decide whether she should comfort his friend.
moral_action: Jack drives to his friend's place to see what he can do for her.
moral_consequence: Jack's friend feels supported and is glad that someone care about her.
immoral_action: Jack doesn't know what to say to her, so he decides to stay at home.
immoral_consequence: Jack's friend has no one to comfort her and continues to feel sad.

norm: It's good to do things with your kids.
situation: Max is the father of three and just got home from a long day at work.
intention: Max wants to get some sleep.
moral_action: Max takes the time to catch up with his kids after coming home, playing a game with them before going to sleep, to give them the required attention.
moral_consequence: Max's kid are excited to see their father and have a happy time playing the game with him.
immoral_action: Max sneaks in his house and sneaks past his children straight to bed, so he can get a good night's sleep without interruption.
immoral_consequence: Max's children don't realize their father is home and miss him through the night after having already missed him during the day.

norm: It's rude to inconvenience employees.
situation: Terry is at the store and needs help with a purchase when she sees an employee going on lunch.
intention: Terry wants to find someone to help her.
moral_action: Terry approaches the worker and asks if they can page someone else to help her.
moral_consequence: The worker gets to their lunch break on time and Terry gets assistance.
immoral_action: Terry approaches the worker and insists they help her.
immoral_consequence: The employee misses half of their lunch break and resents Terry.

norm: It's fair to exchange favors
situation: Terri has been busy, so her friend has been taking her kids to school for her.
intention: Terri wants her children to get a good education.
moral_action: Terri decides to take her children and her friend's children on a field trip.
moral_consequence: Terri's friend enjoys a day off from parenting.
immoral_action: Terri decides to take her kids on a field trip without inviting her friend's children.
immoral_consequence: Terri's friend feels unappreciated.

norm: It's bad to lie to family.
situation: Jack recently lost his job and his father asks him to pay the electricity bill.
intention: Jack wants to get financial help.
moral_action: Jack tells his father that he lost his job, so he is unable to pay the bill and needs financial help.
moral_consequence: His father is empathetic about Jack's situation and agrees to pay the bill on his behalf.
immoral_action: Jack makes up a story that he has lost money in his stock and and asks his father if he can pay the bill for him.
immoral_consequence: His father gets angry at his stupid financial management and refuses to help him.

norm: It's good to run because it's good for you.
situation: Gabe weighs 200 pounds and has heart trouble.
intention: Gabe wants to start an exercise program.
moral_action: Gabe starts running for half an hour each day.
moral_consequence: Gabe starts losing weight.
immoral_action: Gabe starts walking for five minutes a day.
immoral_consequence: Gabe's exercise isn't strenuous enough, so he keeps gaining weight.

norm: You shouldn't pig out on candy.
situation: Peter is a child who just got home after trick or treating for hours.
intention: Peter wants to eat some of the candy he got.
moral_action: Peters has a couple pieces of his favorite candy.
moral_consequence: Peter feels satisfied.
immoral_action: Peter eats as much candy as he can as quickly as he can.
immoral_consequence: Peter gets a stomachache and feels sick.

norm: It's rude to act like a scumbag.
situation: Dave is at work and notices that Judy's breasts are rather exposed if one looks down her shirt  a certain way.
intention: Dave wants to make a comment about Judy's cleavage showing.
moral_action: Dave quietly tells Judy that she needs to go to the bathroom and check her shirt because she's having a bit of an accident.
moral_consequence: Judy is embarrassed but thankful to Dave for pointing that out to her and goes to fix it.
immoral_action: Dave tells Judy that he can see her boobs and that they look fantastic, and he can't wait to grab a handful and motorboat them.
immoral_consequence: Judy is repulsed by Dave's rapey comments and runs away to the bathroom to regroup.

norm: It's wrong to avoid your partner.
situation: Joe is finished with workday and about to begin his drive home where his wife is.
intention: Joe wants to spend some time alone to reflect on his thoughts.
moral_action: Joe drives straight home to see his wife as soon as possible, but tells her that he wants to spend some time relaxing tonight.
moral_consequence: Joe's wife is happy to see him and lets him have some alone time to reflect on his thoughts.
immoral_action: Joe drives around aimless for an hour while listening to music instead of going home.
immoral_consequence: Joe's wife asks him why it took him so long to get home, and she makes Joe cook his own dinner.

norm: You should encourage someone who is suicidal to seek help.
situation: David's friend confides in him that he's been thinking about killing himself.
intention: David wants to respond to his friend.
moral_action: David gives his friend advice, and encourages him to see a therapist.
moral_consequence: David's friend feels less alone, and tries to find professional help.
immoral_action: David tells his friend to keep it a secret, and stop being such a baby.
immoral_consequence: David's friend feel even worse than before, and shuts down even more.

norm: It's wrong to drop out of school.
situation: Greg has been put on the spot by his teacher who asks him a basic question he cannot answer which earns him a reputation for being unintelligent.
intention: Greg wants to avoid struggling in class in front of others.
moral_action: Greg signs up for some one on one lessons to improve his understanding of the material.
moral_consequence: Greg's parents consider him to be responsible kid for making this decision.
immoral_action: Greg decides to drop out of school since he's so far behind.
immoral_consequence: Greg's parents think he will not make anything of himself.

norm: It is distasteful to have an affair.
situation: Hunter and his girlfriend haven't been having much sex lately.
intention: Hunter wants to have more sex.
moral_action: Hunter talks with his girlfriend and explains he would be happier with more sex.
moral_consequence: Hunter and his girlfriend start exploring more things in the bedroom and invigorate their sex life.
immoral_action: Hunter decides to start having sex with a girl from the neighborhood.
immoral_consequence: Hunter's girlfriend finds out and ends the relationship.

norm: You shouldn't punish an employee for voicing concerns.
situation: James, concerned by the difficulties people were having with the new software system, asked his employees what specifically was causing all the problems.
intention: James wants people to work all day without being distracted by computer problems.
moral_action: James makes a list of everyone having problems and hires a computer skills instructor to retrain them.
moral_consequence: The employees learn how to handle the new software and productivity goes way up.
immoral_action: James fires anyone who says the software is confusing, on the grounds that they must be technically illiterate.
immoral_consequence: While the remaining employees can solve all their own computer problems, there's half as many of them, so they get half as much work done.

norm: It's not right to throw food at people.
situation: Bill is at dinner with his wife Judy, and they're seated at opposite ends of a long table when Judy asks Bill to pass her a bread roll.
intention: Bill wants to move the bread roll from the basket to Judy's hand.
moral_action: Bill grabs the whole basket of bread rolls and walks it over towards Judy, so she can take one.
moral_consequence: Judy is delighted that Bill hand delivered the bread to her and smiles as she takes a roll and thanks him.
immoral_action: Bill picks up one of the bread rolls and launches a hard arcing throw so the roll lands in Judy's hand.
immoral_consequence: Judy is angry at Bill for disrespecting the food like that and for putting his germ laden hands on her bread roll.

norm: Parents shouldn't shower with their children.
situation: Paul and his two kids are at the beach and need to rinse off before leaving.
intention: Paul wants to be respectful of others at the beach.
moral_action: Paul puts his children in a separate stall, and showers himself in another stall.
moral_consequence: Beachgoers are spared the uncomfortable sight of watching a grown man shower with children.
immoral_action: Paul showers with his two children in view of other beachgoers.
immoral_consequence: Beachgoers disapprove but appreciate that the family does not take up three separate stalls.

norm: You shouldn't be defensive when you are doing something wrong.
situation: John is washing dishes when his wife Kathy points out that the ones in the rack that are drying actually still have food on them.
intention: John wants to respond to Kathy's statement.
moral_action: John apologizes for the mistake telling Kathy he accidentally overlooked it and offers to rewash them.
moral_consequence: Kathy is happy John can take credit for his mistakes and work to correct them right away, and she gains respect for him.
immoral_action: John tells Kathy that he's doing a good enough job and if she wants it done to her higher standards that she can do them herself.
immoral_consequence: Kathy is shocked John is being so childish about an obvious mistake and begins to think he's going to be difficult to live with.

norm: Children are expected to communicate with their parents regularly.
situation: Zach, who lives with his parents, is invited by some friends to a late-night party.
intention: Zach wants to go to the party.
moral_action: Zach calls his parents and asks to go to the party.
moral_consequence: Zach's parents are relieved and give him a reasonable time to be home.
immoral_action: "Zach goes to the party and doesn't call his parents, so they can't say ""no""."
immoral_consequence: Zach's parents get worried and go looking for him, getting him in trouble.

norm: It is rude not to show compassion.
situation: Peter won a competition that his friend Charlie also entered and Charlie is upset about losing.
intention: Peter wants to celebrate his achievement.
moral_action: Peter buys himself an expensive watch he had been eyeing as a reward for winning.
moral_consequence: Peter feels satisfied and Charlie isn't forced to relive his loss.
immoral_action: Peter throws a big party to celebrate his win and invites Charlie.
immoral_consequence: Charlie feels like Peter is rubbing the win in his face and their friend group see Peter as insensitive.

norm: It's wrong to steal something from a friend.
situation: John is extremely hungry.
intention: John needs to find some food to eat.
moral_action: John asks Reuben is he has any food to spare.
moral_consequence: Reuben offers to share his bag of chips and John eats and is satisfied.
immoral_action: John decides to take some of Reuben's lunch off his desk without asking, and he eats it.
immoral_consequence: Reuben sees John eating his lunch and doesn't want to be friends anymore.

norm: You shouldn't laugh at your friend when they hurt themselves.
situation: Billy is skateboarding with friends, when his friend Evan falls off his skateboard and skins his knee.
intention: Billy wants to do something about Evan.
moral_action: Billy asks if Evan needs help and tries to get him some medical attention.
moral_consequence: Billy is seen as considerate and helpful by his friends, especially Evan.
immoral_action: Billy laughs about Evan's injury and posts mean things about it on social media.
immoral_consequence: Billy is shunned by his friends for his inconsiderate behavior.

norm: It is disgusting to poop in a saucepan.
situation: Marcus is waiting for his date Susan to get out of the bathroom, but is having trouble holding it.
intention: Marcus wants to evacuate his bowels.
moral_action: Marcus feels he can't wait and goes across the hall to ask a neighbor to use their restroom.
moral_consequence: Marcus uses the neighbor's restroom and returns to explain where he'd been to Susan.
immoral_action: Marcus feels he can't wait any longer and grabs the nearest saucepan to void himself into.
immoral_consequence: Susan is disgusted by Marcus pooping in the saucepan and says she doesn't want to continue the date.

norm: Workers shouldn't act childishly.
situation: Arnold is working at a warehouse.
intention: He wants to have some fun at his job.
moral_action: Arnold tells his coworkers some funny jokes while they move boxes.
moral_consequence: Arnold has fun with his coworkers in a mature and productive way.
immoral_action: Arnold drives the forklift around the warehouse like a racecar.
immoral_consequence: Arnold loses control and runs into some shelving, causing a great amount of damage.

norm: It's wrong to be mean to a child.
situation: Ken is at the grocery store with his son Liam who asks Ken to buy ice cream.
intention: Ken wants to respond to Liam's request.
moral_action: Ken tells Liam that he can't be eating too much sugar, so they'll have to get it next time.
moral_consequence: The other customers are happy to see Ken being conscious of what Liam eats.
immoral_action: Ken tells Liam that he's a gluttonous little monster who sucks money out of him like a vacuum, and he should shut it.
immoral_consequence: The other customers are appalled at how Ken speaks to Liam and are worried for Liam's safety.

norm: It's bad to sleep with your friend's ex.
situation: Jerry has been abstinent for a long time and finds out his friend just broke up with his attractive girlfriend.
intention: Jerry wants to have a sexual encounter.
moral_action: Jerry goes onto a dating website and meets a nice girl online.
moral_consequence: Jerry's friend meets the girl, and they get along well adding another person to their circle of friends.
immoral_action: Jerry meets up with his friend's ex and ends up hooking up with her.
immoral_consequence: Jerry's friend finds out, and he loses a lot of trust in him.

norm: Animal neglect is morally wrong
situation: Dwight is at home watching TV when his dog Bruno starts whining and begging in the usual way when he wants food.
intention: Dwight wants to not hear the whining anymore.
moral_action: Dwight goes to Bruno's food bowl and fills it with dog food before calling him over.
moral_consequence: Bruno excitedly runs towards the food and happily eats it with reckless abandon.
immoral_action: Dwight takes Bruno by the collar and leads him down into the basement where he closes him in, so he can't hear him.
immoral_consequence: Bruno is stressed and hungry and is confused as to why he's suddenly confined in the basement.

norm: It is rude to exclude friends.
situation: Connor is planning a party for his upcoming birthday.
intention: Connor wants to invite a some guests.
moral_action: Connor sends out party invitations to all his family and close friends.
moral_consequence: Connor has a good time at his party with all his loved ones.
immoral_action: Connor invites all his family to his birthday party.
immoral_consequence: Connor is given the cold shoulder by his best friend for not being invited to the party.

norm: It's good to clean things and do your chores.
situation: Dawn is busy studying for a test tomorrow, but there are dirty dishes and crumbs on the floor from dinner.
intention: Dawn wants to make a decision.
moral_action: Dawn gets up to clean and returns to studying shortly after.
moral_consequence: Dawn avoids getting pests in her home and is still able to learn.
immoral_action: Dawn decides to ignore the mess and just focus on her studies.
immoral_consequence: Dawn gets cockroaches and has trouble getting rid of them.

norm: You should not argue in public
situation: Katie is at the grocery store with her partner who says something that really bothers her.
intention: Katie wants to confront her partner about what he said.
moral_action: Katie waits until they get back home to bring up the issue.
moral_consequence: Katie's and her partner are able to talk in private about the issue and resolve it.
immoral_action: Katie gets into it with her partner, and they argue while at the store.
immoral_consequence: Katie's partner brushes her off and focuses on how she made a scene in public.

norm: It is rude to give someone mean looks.
situation: Jason is on a basketball team and thinks his teammate Leon isn't showing effort.
intention: Jason wants to communicate with Leon about his effort.
moral_action: Jason talks to Leon and tell him he needs to play harder.
moral_consequence: Leon will try to perform with more effort.
immoral_action: Jason stares down Leon during basketball practice.
immoral_consequence: Leon will be confused and think Jason has a bad personality.

norm: It's wrong to abuse substances to get high.
situation: Mark was prescribed medical marijuana, and his friends are asking him for some.
intention: Mark wants to have fun with his friends.
moral_action: Mark suggests that they watch YouTube videos instead since he needs the marijuana.
moral_consequence: Mark's friends all understand Mark's reasoning and enjoy watching the videos.
immoral_action: Mark allows his friends to use his marijuana so that they can smoke as much as they want.
immoral_consequence: Mark's friends will want more and more marijuana to satisfy their craving.

norm: It's rude to turn down family members.
situation: Oscar lives in a different town than his family and his brother is calling him to let him know he is in Oscar's town while travelling.
intention: Oscar wants to hear what his brother wants.
moral_action: Oscar finds out his brother is in town and wants to see Oscar so Oscar says for him to come stop by.
moral_consequence: Oscar's brother is happy to see and catch up with his brother.
immoral_action: Oscar finds out his brother is in town and wants to see Oscar but Oscar tells him he is busy.
immoral_consequence: Oscar's brother is offended that Oscar wouldn't make time for him even though he is in town.

norm: You shouldn't park in the wrong spot.
situation: Beth is returning home after a long day at work, and she is driving around her apartment complex which is full of cars.
intention: Beth wants to find a place to park.
moral_action: Beth parks in the general parking area even though it is a little bit of a walk to her apartment.
moral_consequence: Beth has no issues with finding her car the following morning since she parked in a legitimate parking space.
immoral_action: Beth parks in a space reserved for another tenant because it is close to her door.
immoral_consequence: Beth is dismayed the following morning when she discovers that her car has been towed.

norm: It's bad to ditch your kids to go out drinking.
situation: Lauren is at home with her young daughter when her friends invite her to go drinking.
intention: Lauren wants to have a good time with her friends.
moral_action: Lauren hires a babysitter to watch her daughter while she goes out with her friends.
moral_consequence: Lauren's daughter is kept safe by the babysitter and is less likely to get hurt.
immoral_action: Lauren leaves her daughter alone to go out to the bar with her friends.
immoral_consequence: Lauren's daughter is unsupervised at the house and might get hurt.

norm: It's good to lend rides to people who need it.
situation: Sherry's friend needs a ride to the grocery store in town.
intention: Sherry wants to be a good friend.
moral_action: Sherry borrows her mother's car to take her friend to the store.
moral_consequence: Sherry's friend is grateful for the ride and buys Sherry lunch.
immoral_action: Sherry gives her friend well-meaning advice on which bus she could take to get to the grocery store.
immoral_consequence: Sherry’s friend is a bit disappointed that Sherry didn’t offer to drive her in her mother’s car.

norm: It's unacceptable to touch people without their permission.
situation: Daryl sees a woman who has a dryer sheet stuck to the back of her dress.
intention: Daryl wants to remove the dryer sheet from the woman's dress, so she won't look silly in public.
moral_action: Daryl tells the woman she has a dryer sheet on her and asks if he can remove it for her.
moral_consequence: The woman allows Daryl to remove the dryer sheet from her back and then thanks him for his consideration.
immoral_action: Daryl reaches out and pulls the dryer sheet off the woman's dress without telling her what he's doing.
immoral_consequence: The woman thinks Daryl is groping her and screams, then slaps him across the face.

norm: It's not acceptable to be violent towards others.
situation: Jakes sees a fight.
intention: Jake wants to help.
moral_action: Jake approaches the fighters and defuses the situation.
moral_consequence: No one gets hurt and Jake is praised for having a cool head.
immoral_action: Jake runs into the middle of the fight and starts punching.
immoral_consequence: Jake gets a black eye and arrested.

norm: It's bad to drive without a license.
situation: Joe gets his license exam on Tuesday, and he really wants to drive.
intention: Joe wants to drive right away.
moral_action: Joe decides to drive on the driving simulators to practice for his test tomorrow.
moral_consequence: Joe does very well on the test because of the practice he got.
immoral_action: Joe sneaks out and drives Monday night around the neighborhood.
immoral_consequence: Joe gets caught by the police and has to pay a huge fine.

norm: You shouldn't try to get back at people.
situation: Max was mad at Steve for breaking one of his toys.
intention: Max wants Steve to know how he feels.
moral_action: Max talks to Steve and tells him why he is so upset.
moral_consequence: Steve feels bad and goes out to buy Max a new toy.
immoral_action: Max breaks one of Steve's toys in retaliation for what Steve did.
immoral_consequence: Steve punches Max in the face when he sees what Max did to his toy.

norm: It's selfish to use other people
situation: Frank meets the Regional Manager of his company at a Christmas party.
intention: Frank wants to move up in the company.
moral_action: Frank is respectful of his Regional Manager and asks him genuine questions about his movement through the company.
moral_consequence: Frank's Regional Manager is impressed by Frank's thoughtfulness.
immoral_action: Frank tries to suck-up to his Regional Manager in hopes of getting a promotion.
immoral_consequence: Frank's Regional Manager is annoyed that Frank is being pushy and tries to avoid him.

norm: It's expected you meet and greet any new neighbors
situation: Barbara finds out that a couple from China have juat moved into the house across the street.
intention: Barbara wants to find out more about her new neighbors.
moral_action: Barbara drops in on her new neighbors with a house warming gift.
moral_consequence: Barbara gets to know her new neighbors with some one on one face time.
immoral_action: Barbara chats with some of her other neighbors about the new home owners.
immoral_consequence: Barbara learns nothing but gossip and innuendo from her other neighbors.

norm: It is wrong to hurt your significant other
situation: George's and his wife get into a heated argument, and she says some very mean things about his appearance.
intention: George wants to express his anger.
moral_action: George yells at her and storms out of the house.
moral_consequence: George and his wife take time to calm down they talk about their problems and resolve them.
immoral_action: George pushes his wife away from him and storms out of the house.
immoral_consequence: George's wife falls and hurts her arm, and has to go to the hospital.

norm: It's good to give someone information when they seek it.
situation: While driving Vanessa sees a person on the side of the road wave her down.
intention: Vanessa wants to get to the mall before it closes.
moral_action: Vanessa drives slowly and answers the person's question before speeding up to go to the mall.
moral_consequence: The person on the side of the road is grateful and happy to have the answer.
immoral_action: Vanessa pretends not to see the person and speeds off to the mall.
immoral_consequence: The person on the side of the road is sad and doesn't get the help they need.

norm: It's good to show your appreciation to people.
situation: It's Sandra's birthday, and she gets a new toy from her father.
intention: Sandra wants to play with her new toy.
moral_action: Sandra thanks her father for the present then enjoys playing with her new toy.
moral_consequence: Sandra's farther feels that his gift is appreciated and is happy.
immoral_action: Sandra runs of to her room to play with her new toy without thanking her father for the birthday gift.
immoral_consequence: Sandra's father is offended that she didn't show any gratitude for his thoughtful gift.

norm: It's nice to help people you like improve themselves.
situation: Chris loves to work out with free weights and has a friend who wants to get into exercising.
intention: Chris wants to encourage his friend to exercise.
moral_action: Chris brings his friend with him and shows him his exercise routine, then helps his friend make one.
moral_consequence: Chris' friend starts seeing results quickly and keeps working to meet his goals.
immoral_action: Chris tells his friend that exercise has done him a lot of good, showing off his muscles.
immoral_consequence: Chris' friend wants to exercise but has no idea how to get started or get good results.

norm: You should get help if you have a drinking problem.
situation: John has been an alcoholic for some time but is faced with the need to stop to take advantage of an opportunity.
intention: John wants to try to stop drinking.
moral_action: John seeks out help and expertise from a local detox and rehabilitation center.
moral_consequence: John is able to successfully sober up and completes a lengthy treatment and has even more opportunities than he started with.
immoral_action: John tries to stop drinking on his own even though it hasn't worked before.
immoral_consequence: John eventually relapses and misses out on the opportunity.

norm: It's evil to physically assault someone.
situation: Martha is walking home from class after dark and sees her friend Beth under a nearby awning.
intention: Beth wants to get some money from Martha.
moral_action: Beth tells Martha that she is really hungry and could really use some money to get food.
moral_consequence: Martha gives Beth some cash from her wallet and wishes her well, not wanting her friend to suffer.
immoral_action: Beth steps out in front of Martha and grabs her hair, telling her that she will get hurt if she doesn't give Beth some cash.
immoral_consequence: Beth is approached by University Police for her attack on Martha and is kicked off of campus.

norm: Partners should limit flirting with other people.
situation: Kate and Barry have been dating for a while, but Kate likes to flirt with other men, which Barry tells her he is uncomfortable with.
intention: Kate wants to reply to Barry's request not to flirt with other men.
moral_action: Kate apologizes to Barry and stops flirting all the time.
moral_consequence: Barry and Kate become closer partners and eventually marry each other.
immoral_action: Kate says the flirting is harmless and continues to do it.
immoral_consequence: Barry becomes very upset and breaks up with Kate.

norm: It's good to take responsibility for your messes.
situation: Jae bumps into his father's glass vase causing it to shatter onto the floor.
intention: Jae doesn't want to get in trouble.
moral_action: Jae uses his allowance to buy a new vase, and he offers it to his father.
moral_consequence: Impressed by his honestly, Jae's father repays Jae for the vase.
immoral_action: Jae sweeps the broken shards of glass underneath the table.
immoral_consequence: Jae is punished by his father when he discovers the truth.

norm: You should always be there for your employees.
situation: Jimmy, the manager of a company, has recently assigned a big project to his team members to finish without three days, and today is his wedding anniversary.
intention: Jimmy wants to celebrate the wedding anniversary with his wife.
moral_action: Jimmy postpones the celebration to next week after the project is finished, and works overtime with his team members.
moral_consequence: His team members feel supported and work overtime happily together.
immoral_action: Jimmy goes to a restaurant for dinner to celebrate the wedding anniversary with his wife tonight, despite the imminent project deadline.
immoral_consequence: His team members feel angry and refuse to work overtime for the project.

norm: You should help your neighbors.
