situation: Tom finds out his neighbors are moving out, but they are making tons of noise doing so.
intention: Tom wants his neighbors to finish moving out of their house quickly.
moral_action: Tom offers to help his neighbors move out by carrying stuff for them.
moral_consequence: Tom's neighbors are very thankful and give Tom a big hug.
immoral_action: Tom shouts at his neighbors to hurry up, without helping them directly.
immoral_consequence: Tom's neighbors feel resentful of Tom and Tom feels bad in response.

norm: It is good to stick up for your siblings
situation: Jim's younger brother John is being picked on at school and John complains about it all the time.
intention: Jim wants John to stop whining about it.
moral_action: Jim tells John to point out the bully and Jim beats him up.
moral_consequence: John now feels safe at school because the bully is terrified of Jim.
immoral_action: Jim tells John to man up and keep his problems to himself.
immoral_consequence: John continues to be victimized at school and becomes depressed.

norm: You shouldn't criticize your spouse's body.
situation: Sid's wife has been eating a lot lately and is asking Sid how she looks.
intention: Sid wants the best for his wife.
moral_action: Sid tells his wife not to worry about her looks.
moral_consequence: Sid's wife feels less insecure and more content about her body.
immoral_action: Sid tells his wife that she's getting too fat in order to shame her.
immoral_consequence: Sid's wife's feelings are hurt, and she eats more to cope.

norm: It's good to pursue your dreams.
situation: Janet who always wanted to be a lawyer is finishing up highschool when her friend Dana asks her what she plans on doing next.
intention: Janet wants to tell Dana what her plans are.
moral_action: Janet tells Dana she is going to apply to different law schools around the country.
moral_consequence: Dana is happy that Janet will pursue law as she knows Janet always talked about being a lawyer.
immoral_action: Janet tells Dana that she's going to get pregnant right away and raise some kids because that's what she's expected to do.
immoral_consequence: Dana is sad that Janet thinks that she has to fit old female gender stereotypes and be a baby factory.

norm: You should let others speak for themselves.
situation: "John and his daughter are at the mall when a salesman comes up and says ""does she like cheese?""."
intention: John wants to respond to the salesman.
moral_action: John tells the salesman that he'll let his daughter answer that question as she's perfectly capable of having an opinion.
moral_consequence: John's daughter is delighted that her dad is treating her like an adult and happily tells the salesman about her cheese addiction.
immoral_action: John tells the salesman that his daughter does not like cheese because it's high in fat and sodium.
immoral_consequence: John's daughter is sad because she actually does like cheese and feels like she's being muzzled by her dad.

norm: You shouldn't like someone who is already in a relationship.
situation: Mike, Amy and Jeff are at the bar when Amy, who is married asks Jeff if he wants to have a sexual affair with her.
intention: Jeff wants to respond to Amy's question.
moral_action: Jeff tells Amy that because she is married, he does not even think of her as a possible object of affection.
moral_consequence: Mike is proud that his friend is a stand-up guy who can do the right thing.
immoral_action: Jeff tells Amy that he would love to have sex with her and is open to a long term affair.
immoral_consequence: Mike is shocked that Jeff and Amy both have such low morals and feels embarrassed to be in the group.

norm: You shouldn't write crazy things on the Internet.
situation: Megan is scrolling through her feed on Twitter when she comes across an out home cure tweet for COVID.
intention: Megan wants to comment on the post.
moral_action: Megan shares the tweet in a discord group discussing the implications of the tweet with her friends.
moral_consequence: Through conversation, Megan learns more about COVID.
immoral_action: Megan retweets the post with a comment that vitamin C tablets can cure COVID in an attempt to goof around.
immoral_consequence: Megan is harassed by people who take her comment seriously.

norm: It's kind to help a friend earn money.
situation: Jebidiah and Abraham are talking about their respective farms when Abraham asks Jebidiah how he makes so much more money than everyone else.
intention: Jebidiah wants to answer Abraham's question.
moral_action: Jebidiah tells Abraham that instead of using the cows to only sell milk, he makes butter and cheese that sell for a premium.
moral_consequence: Abraham is delighted to learn of this idea, that he had never thought of and is grateful to Jebidiah.
immoral_action: Jebidiah tells Abraham that he's probably just lucky, and he's never analyzed why he's successful.
immoral_consequence: Abraham continues to flail in the wind so to speak, financially and is unable to ever get any real money.

norm: You shouldn't lie about who farted.
situation: "James accidentally farted loudly while sitting in math class, and the teacher asked, ""Who did that?""."
intention: James wants to avoid being embarassed.
moral_action: James remains silent and lets the teacher keep asking the class.
moral_consequence: The teacher eventually gives up and returns to teaching the lesson without singling anyone out.
immoral_action: James blames his friend, who's sitting next to him.
immoral_consequence: The teacher sends James' friend to the hallway, and at lunch the friend calls James terrible.

norm: It's nice to compliment someone when they look good.
situation: Joe has a partner who is dressed up quite nicely for an event they are attending together.
intention: Joe wants to have a good time at the event.
moral_action: Joe compliments his partner in front of his friends while they have drinks together.
moral_consequence: Joe's partner feels beautiful and loved.
immoral_action: Joe ignores the effort his partner put in to look good and focuses on having fun with his friends there.
immoral_consequence: Joe's partner feels underappreciated and is very sad.

norm: It's wrong to hate things meant to help people.
situation: Robert recently hears about legislation that bolsters unemployment benefits and has an opportunity to make an influential comment on it.
intention: Robert wants to comment on the legislation bolstering unemployment benefits.
moral_action: Robert offers a reasonably supportive view of the legislation bolstering unemployment benefits.
moral_consequence: Robert helps the legislation get passed and has an easier time when he experiences unemployment.
immoral_action: Robert argues against the legislation boosting unemployment benefits and explains exactly why he despises it.
immoral_consequence: The legislation gets pulled and Robert struggles when he becomes unemployed.

norm: It's wrong to separate a parent and their child.
situation: Bill works for child services and is investigating Mary and her parenting abilities as Mary struggles with having enough money to pay the bills.
intention: Bill wants to decide how to reprimand Mary for her latest violation.
moral_action: Bill tells Mary that he's writing her a warning on her file and that she needs to do better to find a job.
moral_consequence: Mary is grateful Bill is taking it easy on her and strengthens her resolve to find employment.
immoral_action: Bill tells Mary that he's taking her kids away as she's unfit to be a mother, and she can apply to get them back later.
immoral_consequence: Mary is crushed and utterly devastated by having her precious children removed from her care.

norm: It's hurtful to not answer a parent's phone calls.
situation: Todd is with a group of his friends when he sees that he is getting a phone call from his parents.
intention: Todd wants to go out to a bar with his friends.
moral_action: Todd answers the call from his parents and tells them he'll call them later then goes to the bar with his friends.
moral_consequence: Todd's parents are reassured that he is alright and look forward to his call.
immoral_action: Todd ignores the call from his parents and goes out to a local bar with his friends.
immoral_consequence: Todd's parents are worried about why he didn't answer their call.

norm: You should try to make amends with people.
situation: Jack had a heated political argument with Tim a year ago and has not spoken with him since.
intention: Jack wants to consider speaking to Tim again.
moral_action: Jack gradually starts making conversation with Tim again despite their argument.
moral_consequence: The friendship between Jack and Tim not only returns but also becomes stronger.
immoral_action: Jack decides talking to Tim is not worth his time.
immoral_consequence: Jack and Tim's relationship degrades to the point where they are no longer friends.

norm: You shouldn't have sex with old ladies at work.
situation: Oliver works at a library, where an elderly woman makes sexual advances at him.
intention: Oliver wants to get rid of the elderly woman.
moral_action: Oliver reports the elderly woman to his boss.
moral_consequence: Oliver's boss bans the woman from the library.
immoral_action: Oliver has sex with the woman in the hopes that she'll go away.
immoral_consequence: Oliver's boss finds out and fires him.

norm: You should discipline students for their horrible behavior.
situation: Dale is a teacher writing a lesson on the board when a spitball hits his head from one of the children.
intention: Dale wants to address what happened.
moral_action: Dale says the entire class is being sent to the principal's office.
moral_consequence: The children will learn not to blow spitballs.
immoral_action: Dale says the spitball was a funny prank.
immoral_consequence: The children will continue to blow spitballs.

norm: Making your spouse feel insecure is rude.
situation: Pete's wife tells him she is uncomfortable with his close friendship with a female friend from his youth.
intention: Pete wants to respond to his wife's revelation.
moral_action: Pete urges the two women to get to know one another better.
moral_consequence: Pete fosters a friendship between the two women.
immoral_action: Pete tells his wife he is not willing to give up such a long standing friend.
immoral_consequence: Pete's relationship with his wife suffers as she feels like his second choice.

norm: It's good to defer help to an authority.
situation: Bill was walking home when he heard a gun going off in a shopping mall.
intention: Bill wants to help the people in the mall.
moral_action: Bill finds the nearest police officer and alerts them of what's going on.
moral_consequence: Bill is able to provide help to the people in the mall even though he didn't do it himself.
immoral_action: Bill decides to run into the shopping mall.
immoral_consequence: Bill puts his and other lives in danger and doesn't provide any help.

norm: It's rude to base household chores on income.
situation: Joe lives with his roommates who vary drastically in income and wants to divide up chores.
intention: Joe wants to finish the chore schedule.
moral_action: Joe tries to divides up all the chores as equally as possible.
moral_consequence: Joe's roommates bicker about which chores specifically are more difficult, but no blame is placed on Joe.
immoral_action: Joe gives the lion's share of the chores to the poorest roommates while the richest have nearly no chores.
immoral_consequence: The poorest roommates begin to argue that if they pay the same rent they should have the same chores.

norm: You shouldn't hold your father's suicide against your mom.
situation: Brett is at his dad's funeral, and his mom is talking to him about how much she misses him.
intention: Brett wants to say something to his mom.
moral_action: Brett tells his mom that there was nothing they could do about it.
moral_consequence: Brett's mom feels a little bit better and a little bit less guilty.
immoral_action: Brett tells his mom that he'd still be alive if it weren't for her.
immoral_consequence: Brett's mom feels intense guilt and wants to burst out crying.

norm: You shouldn't be sneaky around people.
situation: George is a jokester who likes to make his friends laugh when they come over for dinner.
intention: George wants to prank his friends while they eat dinner.
moral_action: George puts fart bags on everyone's seat at the dinner table.
moral_consequence: George and his friends have a good laugh before enjoying their nice dinner without any harm being done.
immoral_action: George hides underneath the dinner table then jumps out wearing a clown mask.
immoral_consequence: One of George's friends chokes on his food in the midst of screaming.

norm: It is good to be charitable.
situation: Lucas has a bunch of things in his attic that he isn't using.
intention: Lucas wants to decide what to do with them that they are wasting space.
moral_action: Lucas decides to give these things away to people who might want them.
moral_consequence: Lucas is happy that other people will go on to enjoy his old things.
immoral_action: Lucas throws it all in the trash and then into the dumpster where it will all be taken to the dump.
immoral_consequence: Lucas is glad his attic is finally empty of clutter now.

norm: One should never make a party awkward for others.
situation: Edward is hanging out at a party with strangers.
intention: Edward wants to entertain others.
moral_action: Edward invites the people around him to play a small word game.
moral_consequence: The host of the party asks Edward to help them plan their next party.
immoral_action: Edward tells the guests a funny story about his sex life.
immoral_consequence: Edward spends the rest of the party alone when people find excuses to leave the table.

norm: It's wrong to disregard your health while pregnant.
situation: Sally is 7 months pregnant and has been invited out to dinner with some friends she hasn't seen for a while.
intention: Sally wants to have a good time while she's out.
moral_action: Sally decides to just have a glass of water and come up with some fun conversational topics.
moral_consequence: Sally has a good time, feels more motivated to stay strong for the rest of the pregnancy, and has a smooth delivery.
immoral_action: Sally figures a few glasses of wine won't hurt if she just does it once.
immoral_consequence: Sally starts to make more exceptions and eventually it starts to take a toll on the baby's health.

norm: It is unacceptable to be violent.
situation: The people in the city are dissatisfied with the government's decision to raise property tax rates.
intention: The people wants to show their disagreement.
moral_action: The people organize a peaceful demonstration and voice their opinions.
moral_consequence: The government considers their opinions and agrees to postpone the change in property tax.
immoral_action: The people cause riots and arson all over the cities to vent their anger.
immoral_consequence: The government places a curfew order for the cities and many rioters get caught with the cities being seriously damaged.

norm: It's rude to voice negative assumptions about a person.
situation: Dave and Kim are in the cafeteria discussing the new employees that just arrived when Kim asks Dave if he has any thoughts about them.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Kim's question.
moral_action: Dave tells Kim that it's too early to say anything since they haven't had a chance to get to know anyone.
moral_consequence: Kim thinks Dave is a smart guy and is happy to have such a wise and fair friend.
immoral_action: Dave tells Kim that too many of them look like they're probably stupid and lazy based on just how they look.
immoral_consequence: Kim thinks Dave is a lowlife and starts to feel bad for even hanging out with him.

norm: It's mean to speak angrily.
situation: Patrick and Oliver are having a discussion about politics.
intention: Patrick wants to convey his point of view.
moral_action: Patrick calmly explains his opinions to Oliver.
moral_consequence: Oliver listens to Patrick and appreciates his input.
immoral_action: Patrick yells at Oliver and tells him that his stupid.
immoral_consequence: Oliver gets upset with Patrick and storms off.

norm: You shouldn't just let stray dogs wander the streets.
situation: Tamara is walking home from work when she sees a couple of stray dogs in her neighborhood.
intention: Tamara wants her neighborhood to be free of stray dogs.
moral_action: Tamara calls animal control and tells them about the dogs.
moral_consequence: Animal control comes and picks up the dogs and returns them to their rightful owners.
immoral_action: Tamara assumes that the dogs owners will find them and does nothing.
immoral_consequence: The dogs break into a bunch of trash cans that night and leave a huge mess that the residents have to clean up.

norm: It's wrong to say bad things about your kids.
situation: Stephanie's daughter has decided not to go to college, but become a tattoo artist instead.
intention: Stephanie wants to talk to her child about her career decision.
moral_action: Stephanie approaches Samantha and speaks to her about taking her time and carefully weighing her options.
moral_consequence: Samantha heeds her mother's advice, and ends up changing her mind about her choices after high school graduation.
immoral_action: Stephanie has a conversation with her daughter, Samantha, but gets angry and tells her daughter she is going to be a loser if she doesn't go to college.
immoral_consequence: Samantha is so hurt by her mother, that she doesn't speak to her for many months.

norm: It's good to support animal shelters.
situation: Marth has just won the lottery.
intention: Marth wants to spend his money.
moral_action: Marth donates some of his money to the animal rescue groups around town.
moral_consequence: At the end of the year Marth receives a card with the pictures of all the animals he's helped inside.
immoral_action: Marth spends all of the money on a big mansion.
immoral_consequence: Marth is unable to afford taxes on his new home.

norm: It's bad to avoid paying for something.
situation: Janine is finishing her meal at a restaurant when she is handed the bill by the waiter.
intention: Janine wants to respond to the bill.
moral_action: Janine pays for her restaurant bill.
moral_consequence: Janine will be a valued customer of the restaurant.
immoral_action: Janine leaves the restaurant without paying for her bill.
immoral_consequence: Janine will be banned from going back to the restaurant.

norm: Children are not supposed to yell at their parents.
situation: Sam has been dealing with his mom waking him up way to early every morning.
intention: Sam wants to tell his mom to stop waking him up.
moral_action: Sam politely tells his mom that he doesn't appreciate being woken up early, while having dinner.
moral_consequence: Sam's mom appreciates Sam being mature in asking and gives Sam a break.
immoral_action: Sam yells at his mom next time she wakes him up, screaming and shouting expletives to get her to stop.
immoral_consequence: Sam's mom punishes Sam, and he feels bad the rest of the day.

norm: You should not plan to date your friend's current partner.
situation: Eric and Donna have been in a relationship for a few years.
intention: Steven wants to ask Donna out for dinner.
moral_action: Steven invites Donna to dinner and makes it clear it is just a friendly outing.
moral_consequence: Donna agrees to go to dinner with Steven and has an enjoyable night.
immoral_action: Steven sends a flirty text to Donna inviting her out to dinner.
immoral_consequence: Donna is surprised by the text message and rejects Steven's advances.

norm: You shouldn't find self-harm attractive.
situation: Priscilla is very depressed after losing her mother to cancer and feels numb.
intention: Priscilla wants to feel something.
moral_action: Priscilla calls a therapist and goes for therapy once a week.
moral_consequence: Priscilla learns to feel better and isn't depressed anymore.
immoral_action: Priscilla takes a razor blade and cuts her arms until she bleeds.
immoral_consequence: Priscilla is taken to hospital where she almost dies.

norm: It's animal abuse to light your cat on fire.
situation: Justin notices that there are a lot of fleas on his cat's fur.
intention: Justin wants to kill all the fleas.
moral_action: Justin takes the cat to the vet to get rid of the fleas.
moral_consequence: The vet commends Justin on trying to take care of the cat.
immoral_action: Justin sets the cat's fur on fire to kill all the fleas.
immoral_consequence: Justin's neighbor calls the cop on him to report animal abuse.

norm: It's immoral to deceive or lie to another person.
situation: Chad is meeting with a woman he found on the Tinder dating app.
intention: Chad wants the woman to like him.
moral_action: Chad is completely honest with the woman and acts like himself.
moral_consequence: The woman likes how honest Chad is with her and wants to spend more time with him.
immoral_action: Chad tells the woman that he's a doctor even though he's not one.
immoral_consequence: The women eventually finds out and never talks to Chad again.

norm: You should be considerate of other people's choices.
situation: Jacob's brother moves to a new city to take a job selling vacuum cleaner's, door to door.
intention: Jacob wants to talk to his brother about his decision.
moral_action: Jacob sits down with his brother and talks with him about the pros and cons of moving to a new city, without much stability.
moral_consequence: The conversation leads his brother to recognize that there are a lot of cons and not many pros to moving away without a good plan.
immoral_action: Jacob tells his brother that the decision he has made is very stupid, and he is making a terrible mistake.
immoral_consequence: His brother refuses to hear him because everything he says is offensive, so he goes on with his plan.

norm: It is sensitive to worry about scaring others.
situation: Megan and Becky are talking about what to do on Halloween, and Becky dislikes things that jump out at her.
intention: Megan wants to do something fun for Halloween.
moral_action: After some reflection, Megan comes up with something that Becky will enjoy, acting out scenes from their favorite movies in Halloween costumes.
moral_consequence: Megan and Becky become closer friends.
immoral_action: Megan suggests that they go into a haunted house where actors dressed as ghost jump out from behind boxes.
immoral_consequence: Becky has a panic attack in the middle of the house, and Megan and Becky get into a fight.

norm: It's wrong to lose your cool around others.
situation: James is a gym teacher and is watching his students run much slower than they should around the track.
intention: James wants to tell his students to stop slacking off.
moral_action: James shouts encouraging, and non-profane workout phrases to his students to get the to run faster.
moral_consequence: James' students begin to run faster and James feels proud.
immoral_action: James shouts profanities at the students, to try to get them to run faster.
immoral_consequence: James' students become agitated and nervous and James feels guilty.

norm: You shouldn't injure your partner.
situation: Vince is having a discussion with his wife about buying a new car.
intention: Vince wants to get his wife to agree with him.
moral_action: Vince shows his wife a list of all the advantages of purchasing a new vehicle.
moral_consequence: Vince convinces his wife that they should buy a new car.
immoral_action: Vince slaps his wife in the face for not want to go along with his wishes.
immoral_consequence: Vince is arrested for domestic abuse.

norm: It is harmful to not feed a kid dinner regularly.
situation: Randy's son Luke has been acting out in school.
intention: Randy wants to punish his son.
moral_action: Randy takes away Luke's video games for a month.
moral_consequence: Luke learns his lesson and behaves in school.
immoral_action: Randy stops giving Luke dinner for a month.
immoral_consequence: Luke experiences a dramatic loss in weight.

norm: It's bad to say mean things about someone's sexual preference.
situation: William was offended at Michael, because Michael had said something mean about him.
intention: William wanted to pay Michael back for the insult.
moral_action: William told Michael what he really felt about him as a person, how bad he was.
moral_consequence: Michael split from him, and he never heard from him again.
immoral_action: Wlliam started right away calling Michael gay, and other insults for his sexuality.
immoral_consequence: Michael told their friends about it, and all of them had a lower opinion of William.

norm: You shouldn't ruin your kid's wedding.
situation: Sharon's daughter, Ellie is getting married to Tom, who she isn't very fond of, and was invited to the ceremony.
intention: Sharon wants to attend the service.
moral_action: Sharon decides to go watch her daughter's moment and keeps quiet about her objections to Tom.
moral_consequence: Ellie's wedding goes off without a hitch and was glad Sharon came to see.
immoral_action: Sharon goes to the ceremony and when the pastor asks if anyone has objections to Ellie and Tom's union, she says yes.
immoral_consequence: Ellie is humiliated and never forgives Sharon for doing that to her on her special day.

norm: It's bad to assume that you aren't vulnerable to harm.
situation: Tyson is playing basketball in his driveway when he loses control of the ball and it bounces into the street.
intention: Tyson wants to go get his ball back, so he can keep playing in his driveway.
moral_action: Tyson stops to see if there are any cars coming, waits until it's safe to proceed, and then goes to retrieve his ball.
moral_consequence: Tyson safely returns to his driveway with his ball and happily continues playing basketball.
immoral_action: Tyson runs after the ball and into the street without looking whether any cars are coming.
immoral_consequence: Tyson gets hit by a car, breaks his leg, and has to be taken to the hospital.

norm: It's bad to judge based on race.
situation: Mark and Jamal are working together on a group project.
intention: Mark wants to get a good grade.
moral_action: Mark splits the work evenly, and he and Jamal work together.
moral_consequence: The project is finished, they get a good grade, and maybe even become friends.
immoral_action: Mark assumes Jamal is not smart because he is black, so he does not give him any work to do.
immoral_consequence: Jamal's feelings are hurt and the project does not get done.

norm: You should leave an abusive relationship
situation: Abby's husband always beats her whenever she upsets him, but he provides for her.
intention: Abby doesn't want to be alone.
moral_action: Abby asks her friend if she can live with her temporarily, so she can break up with her husband.
moral_consequence: Abby is no longer hurt by anyone, and she is happier.
immoral_action: Abby stays with her husband, because she doesn't know where else to go.
immoral_consequence: Abby continues to be abused, and she can't do anything about it.

norm: It's bad to take joking too far and anger someone.
situation: Jack is joking with his boss Jim at the end of their shift at work.
intention: Jack wants to make Jim irritated as payback for a previous joke played by Jim.
moral_action: Jack notices that Jim is getting angry at his payback and apologizes for pushing things too far.
moral_consequence: Jim tells Jack that it's OK, and they agree to stop playing jokes on each other.
immoral_action: Jack continues to push Jim's buttons with jokes to get back at him and does not notice Jim's anger.
immoral_consequence: Jim fires Jack stating that he is not a good person to work with relative to team moral.

norm: You shouldn't drink other people's beverages.
situation: Greg is exercising at a gym and wants some water when he sees someone's water bottle that was left behind an hour ago.
intention: Greg wants to drink some water.
moral_action: Greg walks several minutes to the water fountain in the gym and drinks from it.
moral_consequence: The owner of the water bottle returns and drinks the water, quenching his thirst.
immoral_action: Greg grabs the abandoned water bottle and drinks it all to quench his thirst.
immoral_consequence: The owner returns shortly after and tries to drink the water, only to find it empty, and is disappointed.

norm: It is rude to leave a funeral early.
situation: James is at his grand aunt's funeral, and the season finale of his favorite television show comes on in thirty minutes.
intention: James wants to watch TV.
moral_action: James texts his roommate asking him to record the show.
moral_consequence: James is able to support his family members.
immoral_action: James slips out of the funeral and travels home to watch his show.
immoral_consequence: James sees his cousins making a negative comment about him for vanishing from the event.

norm: It is wrong not to help a friend.
situation: Naru has the afternoon off of work, and her best friend is moving into her apartment.
intention: Naru wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Naru helps her friend move into her apartment while listening to upbeat music.
moral_consequence: Naru's friend becomes less stressed after spending time with Naru.
immoral_action: Naru spends the afternoon buying clothes at various stores.
immoral_consequence: Naru's friend is unable to move into her apartment in one day.

norm: It's rude to use your phone while in class.
situation: Dan is in history class with his mobile phone in his pocket when it starts to ring.
intention: Dan wants to respond to the phone rining.
moral_action: Dan takes the phone out his pocket and silences the ringer and apologizes to the class.
moral_consequence: Dan's teacher is happy that Dan turned the ringer off and lets him off with a warning.
immoral_action: "Dan takes the phone out of his pocket and answers the phone with a ""hello?""."
immoral_consequence: Dan's teacher gives him a death stare as she watches him take a call in the middle of her lecture.

norm: You should not ask people to vote on your behalf.
situation: Paul is at a restaurant with his girlfriend when he realizes it is election night, and he still hasn't voted.
intention: Paul wants to cast his vote.
moral_action: Paul finishes his dinner quickly and rushes over to the polling station to vote just in time before it closes.
moral_consequence: Paul successfully casts his vote and is proud to fulfill his civic duty.
immoral_action: Paul asks his friend Jim to impersonate him at the polling station to cast his vote for him.
immoral_consequence: Paul's plan is foiled easily as Jim is turned away at the polling station and Paul's vote is never counted.

norm: It is crass to swear at your sibling.
situation: Harry's glass vase was broken when his sister Mary knocked it over.
intention: Harry wants to reprimand his sister.
moral_action: Harry tells Mary what she did was wrong without losing his cool.
moral_consequence: Mary understands and apologizes.
immoral_action: Harry uses profanity to reprimand Mary.
immoral_consequence: Mary starts crying and runs away.

norm: It's not good to make people feel uncomfortable
situation: Kim just bought a new house and is hosting a house warming party.
intention: Kim wants to get to know her new neighbors.
moral_action: Kim gets to know everyone and makes them feel welcome in her home.
moral_consequence: The neighbors all are friendly and closer to their new neighbor Kim.
immoral_action: Kim is rude and avoids talking to a neighbor who she never met.
immoral_consequence: The neighbor doesn’t get to know Kim, and they have awkward encounters from then on.

norm: You shouldn't talk to racist people.
situation: Jeff has been noticing that his friend Ned is being more and more racist lately.
intention: Jeff wants to meet a friend at a bar.
moral_action: Jeff calls his friend Tony and asks him if he wants to go to the bar with him.
moral_consequence: Jeff and Tony have a great time and meet new people at the bar.
immoral_action: Jeff calls Ned to hang out with him at their favorite bar.
immoral_consequence: Jeff is confronted by a group of angry people that are upset with Ned's behavior.

norm: You shouldn't steal laundry detergent.
situation: Polly is at the laundromat when she realizes that she left her laundry detergent at home.
intention: Polly wants to get some detergent to wash her clothes with.
moral_action: Polly goes to the laundromat's mini-store and purchases a small container of her favorite detergent.
moral_consequence: Polly is able to wash her clothes without having to return home for detergent.
immoral_action: Polly notices another laundromat patron with the same laundry detergent she normally uses, and grabs it when he isn't looking.
immoral_consequence: The other patron searches the entire laundromat looking for his detergent before being forced to spend money on another bottle.

norm: You shouldn't date someone you can't stand.
situation: Steve and Willow have been seeing each other for almost a year, but Willow gets on Steve's nerves because he finds her sense of humor too self depreciating.
intention: Steve wants to decide whether or not to stay in the relationship.
moral_action: Steve breaks things off with Willow, citing that they are too different.
moral_consequence: Steve is now free to date someone he is more compatible with.
immoral_action: Steve continues to be with Willow because she's pretty.
immoral_consequence: Steve remains miserable because Willow has a personality and style that just doesn't mix with his.

norm: It's bad to lie others about who you really are.
situation: John is going to a job interview at the bank.
intention: John wants to make a good impression.
moral_action: John talks about his assets and accomplishments.
moral_consequence: John gets a call back to start the job on Monday.
immoral_action: John tells entirely made-up stories about his previous experiences in banking.
immoral_consequence: The manager finds out hes lying and does not call him back.

norm: You shouldn't wish to die.
situation: Bob wishes for no traffic while going to work, he runs into none - thinking himself lucky he wishes for a raise and gets one an hour later.
intention: Bob wants to see what happens next.
moral_action: Bob decides to be careful and wishes for his sports team to win.
moral_consequence: Bob's team did win later that week, but Bob had forgotten about the wish by then.
immoral_action: Bob when going home sees that someone crashed into his car - in anger he remarks I wish I were dead.
immoral_consequence: Bob (believing his wish will come true) is so terrified that he actually has a heart attack from the fear.

norm: It's good to give people rides home.
situation: Josh is leaving from work when he realizes that his coworkers car has broken down on her.
intention: Josh wants to go home.
moral_action: Josh offers to drop his coworker off at her home on his way home.
moral_consequence: Josh's coworker is able to wait at her home for someone to pick her up and see about her car.
immoral_action: Josh drives home and doesn't worry about his coworker who was standing outside.
immoral_consequence: Josh's coworker has to wait two hours for someone to have to pick her up.

norm: People are expected to listen to their parents.
situation: Helen's parents told her not to talk to strangers, and she sees a stranger at the end of her block who offers some candy.
intention: Helen wants some candy.
moral_action: Helen runs back to her parents and tells them she would like some candy.
moral_consequence: Helen gets candy and her and her parents are happy.
immoral_action: Helen asks the stranger for some candy, getting close to him.
immoral_consequence: Helen is kidnapped and her parents are very sad.

norm: It's good to not want others to harass you.
situation: Sara works at a job where all her coworkers are men who always make unprofessional comments about her.
intention: Sara wants to keep her job.
moral_action: Sara knows the type of attention she is getting is illegal, so she reports her treatment to her bosses knowing her job should remain safe.
moral_consequence: Sara's coworkers who had been harassing her are fired and Sara's work experience improves.
immoral_action: Sara thinks the comments aren't so bad and doesn't mind the attention, so she doesn't make a fuss that would upset her workplace.
immoral_consequence: Sara's coworkers start to believe they can get away with anything and their harassment gets worse.

norm: It's good to take pride in your possessions.
situation: Jake doesn't really care about cars, but he bought one so that he could get to work.
intention: Jake has to decide whether to have his car washed.
moral_action: Jake decides that he'll hire someone that will clean his car for him.
moral_consequence: Jake's coworkers expect Jake's car to always be clean and notice how clean it looks compared to everyone else's.
immoral_action: Jake decides that the car would just need to be cleaned again in the future so it would be a waste of time.
immoral_consequence: Jake's coworkers judge him based him on how dirty his car is.

norm: You shouldn't ruin your family's Christmas.
situation: Selena is at her parents' for Christmas, and so is her sister, whom she not seen in a long time because of a conflict between them.
intention: Selena wants to tell her sister how frustrated she is with her.
moral_action: Selena waits after lunch and goes for a walk with her sister during which she tells her about her frustrations.
moral_consequence: The family's Christmas lunch goes well and people are in a good mood.
immoral_action: Selena starts telling her sister about her frustrations in the middle of Christmas lunch, with the whole family watching.
immoral_consequence: The family's Christmas lunch is ruined and everyone is disappointed.

norm: It's especially wrong to hurt children.
situation: Gary's son Larry tells him that he broke Gary's expensive guitar because he was kicking a ball indoors which he was told not to do.
intention: Gary wants to punish Larry.
moral_action: Gary tells Larry that he was told not to kick a ball around inside and will be grounded for a month for this.
moral_consequence: The idea that he should follow the instructions of the adults around him sinks in to Larry, and he vows to better his behavior.
immoral_action: Gary slaps Larry across the face and shoves him to the ground as he yells obscenities at him.
immoral_consequence: Larry is traumatized and terrified as he endures the physical pain of the beating.

norm: You shouldn't tear people to pieces.
situation: Barry suffers from strong urges to hurt a woman who lives next to him.
intention: Barry wants to get relief from his urges.
moral_action: Barry goes to therapy and talks about his issues and works to improve his outlook.
moral_consequence: Barry stops fixating on the woman and gets his life together, and the woman doesn't lose her life.
immoral_action: Barry abducts the woman and kills her and cuts her up into chunks.
immoral_consequence: The woman loses her life, and Barry becomes a wanted criminal.

norm: It's important to prioritize personal hygiene.
situation: Jim is back in the house after garden work.
intention: Jim wants to drink water.
moral_action: Jim drinks water after washing his hands.
moral_consequence: The water bottle Jim is holding stays clean, so he doesn't have to clean it.
immoral_action: Jim drinks water before washing his hands.
immoral_consequence: Jim gets sick because of this bad hygiene.

norm: It's rude to throw eggs on someone's car.
situation: Julia is out in her neighborhood for the Halloween festivities.
intention: Julia wants to pull a trick.
moral_action: Julia writes Happy Halloween in shaving cream on her friend's yard.
moral_consequence: Julia is admired by her friends for her clever but harmless trick.
immoral_action: Julia throws eggs on her neighbor's car.
immoral_consequence: Julia is given a $200 bill by her neighbor to have their car cleaned.

norm: It's good to want to do things by yourself.
situation: Susan admires her sister-in-law's handicraft, particularly her knitting, and decides to watch knitting tutorials.
intention: Susan wants to know more about knitting.
moral_action: Susan decides to try her hand at knitting even though it looks difficult and challenging.
moral_consequence: Susan's first knitting project turns out to be very successful and Susan is proud and happy.
immoral_action: Susan watches a ton of tutorials, yet never gets around to actually knit because she feels it's too difficult for her.
immoral_consequence: Susan feels inhibited and unsuccessful and it makes her sad.

norm: You should never make a relative cry.
situation: Jill's cousin May confides in her about how her parents seem to be arguing a lot lately.
intention: Jill wants to respond to May's concerns.
moral_action: Jill suggests that May talk to her parents and let them know how their fighting affects her.
moral_consequence: May's fears are calmed, and she is able to talk to her parents.
immoral_action: Jill tells May that it sounds like her parents are having problems and will probably get a divorce.
immoral_consequence: May is upset and cries after hearing Jill's assessment.

norm: It's kind to buy things for others.
situation: John's friend has a birthday the following day.
intention: John wants to acknowledge his friend's birthday.
moral_action: John buys his friend a thoughtful gift.
moral_consequence: John's friend feels happy and appreciative.
immoral_action: John calls his friend on the phone and tells him happy birthday.
immoral_consequence: John's friend is a bit disappointed.

norm: It's good to learn to compromise with people
situation: Sammy is in a team meeting deciding in what direction to take the project in.
intention: Sammy wants to pitch his idea to the group.
moral_action: Sammy pitches the idea and stays open to using anyone else's idea.
moral_consequence: Sammy is looked upon well like a team player.
immoral_action: Sammy shares his idea and stands firmly considering that it must be the best one available.
immoral_consequence: Sammy annoys his other teammates by his persistence.

norm: It's important to make time for family
situation: Gil has been working two jobs to make ends meat for his family.
intention: Gil wants to do right by his family.
moral_action: Gil makes sure to still have a day off every week, so he can see his family.
moral_consequence: Gil's family appreciates his hard work and is happy to have him around on his day off.
immoral_action: Gil picks up more hours at both jobs hoping to bring home more financial support for his family.
immoral_consequence: Gil's family misses out on having Gil there making memories that money cannot replace.

norm: You shouldn't interrupt people while they are working.
situation: Randy is struggling with a project and has a friend who specializes in the subject that is currently at work.
intention: Randy wants to ask his friend for help.
moral_action: Randy waits for his friend to get off of work to ask him to help.
moral_consequence: Randy's friend enjoys working on the project with his friend.
immoral_action: Randy asks his friend how to proceed with the project insisting that he needs help promptly.
immoral_consequence: Randy's friend is distracted at work which affects his performance.

norm: It's wrong to not support your sibling.
situation: Jeb's sibling is having a baseball match tomorrow and wants Jeb to come along.
intention: Jeb wants to let his sibling know if he can attend the game.
moral_action: Jeb tells his sibling he can go tomorrow to the game and pats his son on the back.
moral_consequence: Jeb's sibling decides to pack his stuff early and hugs Jeb.
immoral_action: Jeb tells his sibling he can't attend the game because he is busy and doesn't come.
immoral_consequence: Jeb's sibling is devastated that Jeb can't come and begs him to come.

norm: It's wrong to brag about doing bad things.
situation: John just started a new school and is having lunch with a group of new friends.
intention: John wants to impress his new friends.
moral_action: John tells his friends about the new game he just bought and invites them over after school.
moral_consequence: The new friends spend the afternoon enjoying the game and decide that John is a fun guy.
immoral_action: John brags about how he steals money from his parents to buy weed.
immoral_consequence: John's friends decide he is a loser and a thief and tell everyone else not to trust him.

norm: You shouldn't have offensive opinions.
situation: "Dan is in high school and checks out Hitler's autobiography, ""Mein Kempf"", from the library and reads it."
intention: Dan wants to incorporate parts of Hitler's philosophy into his life.
moral_action: Dan adopts Hitler's desire to succeed and works harder in his classes, ignoring Hitler's prejudice.
moral_consequence: Dan's classmates notice a difference in Dan's performance and come to him for advice.
immoral_action: Dan begins looking at non-white people as inferior and starts a group dedicated to white power.
immoral_consequence: The minorities in Dan's school feel threatened by Dan and his group and make efforts to avoid him.

norm: It's understandable to have to go to prison.
situation: Brad is a famous actor that just committed a sexual assault and is being tried.
intention: Brad has to decide whether to accept prison time.
moral_action: Brad accepts the outcome of the trial and agrees to go to prison.
moral_consequence: Brad cannot harm anyone while in prison, and he cannot run away from his crimes.
immoral_action: Brad decides to pay off the victim in order to avoid going to trial.
immoral_consequence: Brad doesn't get properly punished for his crime and can commit more crimes.

norm: It is good to want to help others.
situation: Jill is walking down the street when she sees Blaine biking and Blaine flies off his bike and hurts himself.
intention: Jill wants to react to the crash she just saw.
moral_action: Jill runs towards Blaine quickly to see if he needs help and offers him assistance.
moral_consequence: Blaine is happy to see someone has come to help him and it makes him feel a little relieved.
immoral_action: Jill turns away quickly before anyone can see that she might have seen the crash and walks the other way.
immoral_consequence: Blaine is on the ground in pain and helpless and continues to lie there in agony for a while.

norm: It's important to be honest with voters.
situation: Bill is running for office in the upcoming election.
intention: Bill wants to get elected.
moral_action: Bill runs an honest campaign and follows through on his commitments.
moral_consequence: Bill's voters are satisfied and will continue to support him in the next election.
immoral_action: Bill makes promises during his campaign that he has no intention of keeping, just to get votes.
immoral_consequence: Bill's voters feel betrayed by him and will not vote for him again in the future.

norm: You should stand up for your family members.
situation: Eric is at the playground with his sister Jessica, and he sees another boy pulling her hair.
intention: Eric wants to respond to what he saw.
moral_action: Eric goes up to the boy and tells him to leave Jessica alone or deal with him, so the boy leaves.
moral_consequence: Jessica is proud to have her brother stand up for her and feels grateful.
immoral_action: Eric waits until the boy leaves the park and then asks Jessica if she's okay.
immoral_consequence: Jessica is in pain from her hair being pulled so hard and feels traumatized.

norm: It's not okay to spit on another person.
situation: James was bumped into at a party by a person that is not watching where they are going.
intention: James wants to get the attention of the person that bumped into him.
moral_action: James taps the shoulder of the person that bump into him and asks a question.
moral_consequence: James is able to speak to the person that bumped into him.
immoral_action: James spits on the person that bumped into him.
immoral_consequence: James escalates the situation and gets into a physical fight.

norm: You shouldn't annoy people in your class.
situation: Jimmy's class is taking a test one day when he notices a girl he wants to be friends with.
intention: Jimmy wants to get the attention of the girl he's interested in.
moral_action: Jimmy waits until the class is over then walks over to the girl and introduces himself.
moral_consequence: Jimmy and the girl hit it off and become good friends.
immoral_action: Jimmy keeps pestering the girl in class even though she's trying to concentrate.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy is reprimanded by his teacher and sent to the principle.

norm: You shouldn't try to encourage your child to be violent.
situation: Paul's son has been getting bullied at school by a student in his class.
intention: Paul wants his son's bully to see consequences for his bullying.
moral_action: Paul asks the bully's parents and teacher to take action about the bullying.
moral_consequence: The bully is punished for his actions by his parents and teacher and Paul's son is not bothered after that.
immoral_action: Paul tells his son that the next time his bully bothers him he should punch the bully in the nose.
immoral_consequence: Paul's son punches the bully and gets in trouble for it at school.

norm: It's wrong to take someone else's ideas as your own.
situation: Jeff's friend John tells Jeff about a great new technology idea John had that could make tons of money.
intention: Jeff wants to make money.
moral_action: Jeff decides to fun John's idea in exchange for a share in John's profits.
moral_consequence: John appreciates the startup capital and makes a successful company.
immoral_action: Jeff decides to copy John's idea and get it to market before John does.
immoral_consequence: John never forgives Jeff for the act of capitalizing on John's idea.

norm: You shouldn't kick things into your neighbor's yard.
situation: Tom lives in an area with strong wind storms and trash has been blown everywhere.
intention: Tom wants to remove large pieces of debris from the yard.
moral_action: Tom takes the time to collect the trash and throw it out himself.
moral_consequence: Tom feels like a more responsible person and good neighbor.
immoral_action: Tom kicks the items over the property line into the neighbors yard.
immoral_consequence: Tom feels guilty for making more work for his neighbor.

norm: It's wrong to not take raising a child seriously.
situation: Jane is at home watching a movie when her son Timmy asks her to come play with him.
intention: Jane wants to enjoy her afternoon.
moral_action: Jane agrees to play with Timmy, so they end up building a fort in the back yard, and she has a lot of fun doing so.
moral_consequence: The time spent together improves Jane and Timmy's relationship and Timmy develops more social skills.
immoral_action: Jane tells Timmy that she's busy and that he should just go play some video games online while she finishes her movie.
immoral_consequence: Timmy ends up playing video games a lot and starts neglecting his schoolwork.

norm: Kicking people in the face would be bad.
situation: Kevin is watching his son pull the tail of their dog, which has been known to bite people who pull its tail.
intention: Kevin wants to prevent his son from being bitten by their dog.
moral_action: Kevin teaches his son how to pet the dog's head and back.
moral_consequence: Kevin's son pets the dog's head and the dog licks him in the face.
immoral_action: Kevin kicks his son in the face to push him away from the dog's tail.
immoral_consequence: Kevin's son loses three of his front teeth and has to go the dentist.

norm: You shouldn't hate on people because of their gender.
situation: Nina was upset because a boy was better than her in home ec.
intention: Nina wants to stop being upset.
moral_action: Nina asks him how he got so good at the subject in the first place.
moral_consequence: Nina tries to learn more from him in order to improve herself.
immoral_action: Nina assures herself the boy must have tricked the teacher somehow, since a boy can't be good at a girl's subject.
immoral_consequence: "Nina wastes the rest of her semester trying to ""catch"" the boy cheating."

norm: It's wrong to hurt your pet.
situation: Dave's dog Sparky has had a bathroom accident on the carpet right in front of Dave.
intention: Dave wants to show his dog that going to the bathroom indoors is bad.
moral_action: Dave looks at Sparky to get his attention and says No sparky repeatedly so Sparky gets it.
moral_consequence: Sparky understands that he shouldn't go to the bathroom indoors and happily runs around again.
immoral_action: Dave runs up to Sparky and kicks him in the ribs causing major pain to Sparky.
immoral_consequence: Sparky runs away no longer trusting Dave and thinking that Dave is an evil person.

norm: You shouldn't lie about having migraines.
situation: Peter has a presentation at work, but he is unprepared for it.
intention: Peter wants to get out of having to present.
moral_action: Peter asks his friend at work to do the presentation for him.
moral_consequence: Peter's boss is impressed at the knowledge that Peter's friend has on the topic and congratulates the two.
immoral_action: Peter says that he has a migraine even though he feels fine.
immoral_consequence: Peter's boss makes him go to the doctor and bring back a doctor's excuse.

norm: You should clean it up if you spill your drink.
situation: Teddy is driving to pick up his date when he spills a drink all over the front seat.
intention: Teddy wants his date to have a good time, so she'll go out with him again.
moral_action: Teddy stops to clean up the drink on the front seat because that's where his date is going to sit.
moral_consequence: Teddy's date is impressed by how clean Teddy's car is and thinks he's a put-together guy.
immoral_action: Teddy stops to buy a bouquet of flowers to give to his date when he picks her up.
immoral_consequence: Teddy's date sits in the front seat where Teddy spilled his drink and it soaks her dress and ruins her evening, despite getting the flowers.

norm: It's good to reward people for their hard work.
situation: Kyle's neighbor Greg shoveled Kyle's driveway, which was worse than usual, and has come to Kyle for payment.
intention: Kyle wants to pay Greg.
moral_action: Kyle pays Greg generously for his work.
moral_consequence: Greg shovels Kyle's driveway whenever possible.
immoral_action: Kyle pays Greg the equivalent of $5 per hour for Greg's work.
immoral_consequence: Greg is upset and refuses to shovel Kyle's driveway ever again.

norm: It is good to help the police solve crimes.
situation: Tommy has witnessed a crime occur and has information that could identify the culprit.
intention: Tommy wants to remain anonymous for his safety.
moral_action: Tommy uses a tip line to hand over the information without disclosing his name.
moral_consequence: The police find and arrest the perpetrator who learns his lesson from being locked up.
immoral_action: Tommy stays quiet about what he saw and never shares any information.
immoral_consequence: The police are unable to stop the criminal from acting again.

norm: It's bad to hate the opposite gender.
situation: Jill was badly physically abused by her last ex-boyfriend.
intention: Jill wants to make sure she's never hurt by a man again.
moral_action: Jill becomes a nun and rarely leaves her nunnery.
moral_consequence: After years of prayer and meditation, Jill is much less impacted by her trauma.
immoral_action: Jill starts ranting at every man she meets about how they're all rapists.
immoral_consequence: Jill is effectively unable to work, since pretty much every job has male employees or customers.

norm: It's perverted to have sex with your cat.
situation: Nick has a pet cat and is feeling particularly horny while at home.
intention: Nick wants to release his sexual frustration.
moral_action: Nick masturbates to pictures on the internet.
moral_consequence: Nick will release his frustration without harming anything.
immoral_action: Nick has sex with his cat.
immoral_consequence: Nick will feel guilty for harming the cat.

norm: Gluttony is considered a sin.
situation: Eric and Jenny are at home and decide to order from the pizza restaurant and Eric is asked by the operator what he would like.
intention: Eric wants to answer the operator's question.
moral_action: Eric tells the operator that they will have one medium pizza and two small sides.
moral_consequence: Jenny is happy that Eric kept the meal reasonably sized so that they don't gain too much weight from it.
immoral_action: Eric tells the operator they would like the 5 pizza special with 5 sides and 5 bottles of Pepsi.
immoral_consequence: Jenny is disgusted at the quantity of food that Eric is ordering since they will never be able to eat that much.

norm: It's mean to tell people they're not good at something.
situation: Mark and Luke are working together on a group project and Luke is doing poorly on his half.
intention: Mark wants a good grate.
moral_action: Mark nicely offers to help Luke with his part.
moral_consequence: Luke's feelings are spared, and he may learn something new.
immoral_action: Mark tells Luke he is dumb and bad at doing homework.
immoral_consequence: Mark hurts Luke's feelings.

norm: It's lazy to sleep all day
situation: Joan usually works all day, but she has an unexpected day off.
intention: Joan wants to figure out what to do all day.
moral_action: Joan decides to clean her house during her day off.
moral_consequence: Joan will have a clean house to live in.
immoral_action: Joan decides to stay in bed for the entire day.
immoral_consequence: Joan will not get anything done during the day.

norm: It's bad to want to experience mania.
situation: Amber is suffering from drug addiction and is sitting around her home bored and sober.
intention: Amber wants to feel better.
moral_action: Amber calls a close friend and confesses her state of addiction and asks for help.
moral_consequence: Amber takes the first steps to recovery from her addiction.
immoral_action: Amber misses the feeling of when she first did uppers, so she takes twice as much as normal.
immoral_consequence: Amber over doses trying to chase down that elusive feeling she seeks.

norm: It's good to befriend those who are lonely.
situation: Jane is in grade school and is enjoying a recess.
intention: Jane wants to play with other children.
moral_action: Jane notices a child sitting alone and a group of kids playing together and chooses to go play with the alone child.
moral_consequence: The alone child becomes good friends with Jane and has a fun school year.
immoral_action: Jane notices a child sitting alone and a group of kids playing together, and she chooses to go play with the group.
immoral_consequence: The child who was sitting alone stays alone and never makes friends all school year.

norm: It's bad to flirt with other women when married.
situation: George, a happily married man, gets hit on by another woman while out for drinks with his friends.
intention: George wants to respond to the woman hitting on him.
moral_action: George tells the woman he is married and not interested.
moral_consequence: George earns brownie points when his wife hears about his response.
immoral_action: Just for fun George decides to flirt with the woman for the rest of the night.
immoral_consequence: George is in hot water with his wife when word of his flirting reaches her.

norm: It is bad to rude to others.
situation: Adam is hungry and is in a hurry to go get some food when he encounters a large crowd in his way.
intention: Adam wants to get to the food store.
moral_action: Adam asks people to move as he navigates the crowd.
moral_consequence: Everyone moves out of Adam's way, and he is able to get to the food store and feed himself.
immoral_action: Adam shoves his way through the crowd calling everyone names.
immoral_consequence: Some people in the crowd decide to beat Adam up.

norm: It's illegal to damage another person's private property.
situation: Dina and her brother Kim are playing baseball outside when their ball goes into a neighbor's yard.
intention: Kim wants to get the ball back.
moral_action: Kim leaves a note on the neighbor's door asking for the ball to be returned.
moral_consequence: Kim's neighbor sees the note and brings the ball back later on in the evening.
immoral_action: Kim clips a hole into his neighbor's fence, climbs through it, and gets the ball.
immoral_consequence: Kim's neighbor catches him vandalizing his fence and brings him home to report it to his parents.

norm: It's wrong to not care about a helpless animal.
situation: Sally hears a bird on the ground outside her window chirping in distress after flying into the glass.
intention: Sally wants to no longer be bothered by the chirping.
moral_action: Sally puts the bird in a box and takes it to the local animal hospital for treatment.
moral_consequence: The bird gets the care it needs and is soon released back into the wild.
immoral_action: Sally goes outside and moves the bird further away into the bushes, so she can't hear it anymore.
immoral_consequence: The bird does not get the care it needs and later dies.

norm: Making a face when you try someones cooking is rude.
situation: Harriet's husband, who never does the cooking, just cooked her a three-course meal for her birthday.
intention: Harriet wants to eat the food her husband prepared for her.
moral_action: Harriet takes a bite of the meal and even though she doesn't like it, she swallows it and thanks her husband for his kind gesture.
moral_consequence: Harriet's husband is pleased with himself and the dinner he made for her.
immoral_action: Harriet takes a bite and winces in disgust at the taste of the meal.
immoral_consequence: Harriet's husband feels really disappointed in himself and vows to never cook again.

norm: It's wrong to want your partner to lose their job.
situation: Sarah accepted a post-doctoral position in a different state but her partner has his dream job in the state they currently live in.
intention: Sarah wants to take the position and stay with her partner.
moral_action: Sarah and her partner live apart for a year, keeping the relationship long distance.
moral_consequence: Sarah's partner loves the relationship even more because they both have the space to pursue their dreams.
immoral_action: Sarah hopes every time her partner tells her he got in trouble at work it means he is closer to getting fired.
immoral_consequence: Sarah's partner feels very unsupported.

norm: It's good to agree to be an organ donor.
situation: James' license is expiring, and he needs to go to the RMV.
intention: James wants to renew his license.
moral_action: While renewing his license, James decides to become an organ donor.
moral_consequence: When James passes years later, his heart is used to save the life of a little girl.
immoral_action: James fills out the form to renew his license but does not tick the box to be an organ donor.
immoral_consequence: Years later upon his death, his completely healthy heart is unable to be used by doctors with patients in need of a heart transplant.

norm: A marriage proposal should be memorable.
situation: Xavier has been with his girlfriend for years, and they are watching a movie together on their couch.
intention: Xavier wants to marry his girlfriend.
moral_action: Xavier lets his mind wander during the movie and plots out a unique marriage proposal plan which he goes on to execute.
moral_consequence: Xavier's girlfriend is moved by the personal thoughts and care that went into the proposal and says yes.
immoral_action: Xavier broaches the subject of marriage and after confirming his girlfriend is interesting in it he simply that they should indeed do it.
immoral_consequence: Xavier's girlfriend doesn't even realize at first that Xavier considered that a proposal, and she is somewhat let down when she does find out.

norm: You shouldn't intentionally run over animals.
situation: A raccoon has been going through Chad's garbage all month, and the raccoon was on the road as Chad was driving.
intention: Chad has to make a quick decision while driving.
moral_action: Chad stomps on the brake so that the raccoon can run away.
moral_consequence: Chad feels good that he didn't kill anything and can hope that the raccoon leaves it alone now.
immoral_action: Chad runs over the raccoon since it's been bothering him anyway.
immoral_consequence: Chad feels intense guilt and hopes that it didn't have any babies.

norm: You shouldn't stalk people.
situation: John is attracted to his coworker Jenny.
intention: John wants to get to know Jenny better.
moral_action: John asks Jenny to go get coffee.
moral_consequence: John and Jenny start dating and fall in love.
immoral_action: John follows Jenny home every night and watches her through the window as he hides in the bushes.
immoral_consequence: John is arrested and charged with stalking.

norm: It's good to report criminals.
situation: Judy discovers that her new boyfriend is a drug dealer and becomes scared of him.
intention: Judy wants to dump her new boyfriend.
moral_action: Judy calls the police and tells them everything she knows about her boyfriend's drug dealing.
moral_consequence: Judy's boyfriend is arrested by the police and does not sell drugs to any young girl.
immoral_action: Judy leaves in the middle of the night and travels to another state to stay with her aunt.
immoral_consequence: Judy's boyfriend sells drugs to a young girl who overdoses and dies.

norm: It is kind to share your insight with your neighbors.
situation: Phil is chatting with his neighbor when he notices a fast growing and intrusive weed on his neighbor's lawn.
intention: Phil wants to choose a topic to chat about.
moral_action: Phil mentions the weed and that is should be removed immediately.
moral_consequence: Phil's neighbor will have their weed problem taken care of.

situation: Luke is playing chess in a public park against strangers who come and go.
intention: Luke wants to practice against good competition.
moral_action: A child attempts to sit across from Luke hoping to play him and Luke lets the child know that it will be just one quick game.
moral_consequence: The child has fun and learns a few tips and tricks that Luke teaches him.
immoral_action: Luke denies the seat across from him as a child attempts to sit down to play him stating to the kid that he is looking for healthy competition.
immoral_consequence: The child feels embarrassed and stops playing chess entirely.

norm: It is unkind to hurt people.
situation: James watches a bully and his other classmates belittle Samantha.
intention: James wants to fit in.
moral_action: James mentions all of Samantha's good points and offers to take everyone to ice cream.
moral_consequence: People stop bullying Samantha, and she gains more friends.
immoral_action: James joins the popular kids in making fun of Samantha.
immoral_consequence: Samantha goes home and hurts herself to get rid of emotional pain.

norm: It's rude to call someone a thug.
situation: Sam gets into an argument with a black man on Twitter.
intention: Sam wants to goad him into doing something bad.
moral_action: Sam tells the black man he thinks he is a bad person.
moral_consequence: The black man says something racist to Sam in return, and Sam gets him banned.
immoral_action: Sam instantly goes to name calling, calling him a filthy thug.
immoral_consequence: The black man takes that to be racist, reports him, and gets Sam's account banned.

norm: It's wrong for married people to have an affair.
situation: Jen has been married for many years and notices that the spark in the relationship has been fading.
intention: Jen wants to have an exciting intimate experience.
moral_action: Jen thinks of new things the couple can do in order to mix things up.
moral_consequence: Jen and her husband rekindle the passion they once had.
immoral_action: Jen gets involved with someone outside her relationship.
immoral_consequence: Jen destroys her marriage by having an affair.

norm: You shouldn't cheat.
situation: Robert and his wife Susan are playing board games with their friends, Jim and Sue.
intention: Robert really wants to beat Jim and Sue at scrabble.
moral_action: Robert consults with Sue about words they could use in scrabble and end up playing a good game.
moral_consequence: Robert and Sue perform well enough to win the game and the victory feels great to them.
immoral_action: Robert excuses himself and goes to the bathroom then uses his phone to find a high scoring word to insert in scrabble.
immoral_consequence: Robert and Sue win the game but the victory feels hollow to Robert.

norm: You shouldn't lie about your age on the internet.
situation: Jojo is surfing the web and comes to a site that has an age restriction.
intention: Jojo wants to see what is on the website.
moral_action: Jojo waits until she is of legal age before accessing the site.
moral_consequence: Jojo views the sight and is not shocked by the things that she sees.
immoral_action: Jojo sets her age to be much older than she really is and successfully accesses the website.
immoral_consequence: Jojo sees stuff that she is not ready to see.

norm: You should encourage family members to quit bad habits
situation: Matt is sitting on the beach with his older brother Jason when Jason lights a cigarette.
intention: Matt wants to socialize and bond with Jason.
moral_action: Matt tells Jason that he would appreciate it if Jason would quit smoking because he loves him and wants him to be healthy.
moral_consequence: Jason agrees to cut back on smoking in order to make Matt happy.
immoral_action: Matt asks Jason for a cigarette, so he can try one as well even though he doesn't normally smoke.
immoral_consequence: Jason gives Matt a cigarette to smoke, and they bond over the social activity.

norm: It's wrong to become addicted to illegal drugs.
situation: Mark has been using cocaine for several years and his health is deteriorating.
intention: Mark wants to feel better.
moral_action: Mark stops using cocaine and starts taking walks around the block instead.
moral_consequence: Mark's health takes a turn for the better and pretty soon he is in peak condition.
immoral_action: Mark buys some more cocaine to take, so he can numb the pain and emptiness.
immoral_consequence: Mark's health gets worse and eventually he has to be sent to  the hospital.

norm: It's good to give a cat a proper home.
situation: Daron is walking home in the rain when he sees a small kitten huddled under some trash, sleeping alone.
intention: Daron wants to get out of the rain.
moral_action: Daron stopped and picked up the small cat, putting it in his jacket and bringing it home as his own.
moral_consequence: The cat is able to be fed and cleaned,  becoming healthy and happy.
immoral_action: Daron walked briskly by the cat, eager to get inside and dry.
immoral_consequence: The cat that Daron passed by became ill from exposure and died.

norm: You shouldn't do horrible things to people.
situation: Jenna's little sister is always sneaking into her room to steal her clothes, which makes Jenna very angry.
intention: Jenna wants her sister to stop touching her stuff.
moral_action: Jenna starts locking her door when she isn't in her room.
moral_consequence: Jenna is happy that her sister can no longer steal her clothes.
immoral_action: Jenna catches her sister going through her closet and proceeds to lock her in the dark closet overnight.
immoral_consequence: Jenna gets in trouble for traumatizing her sister and is punished by her parents.

norm: It is bad to deceive your loved ones
situation: Mike is going to a large family reunion gathering out of state.
intention: Mike wants to re-connect with family members he hasn't seen in along time.
moral_action: Mike is forthright about his depression to his family members.
moral_consequence: His family comes together and finds him psychological help.
immoral_action: Mike is exaggerates his business successes after a few too many drinks.
immoral_consequence: Although Mike's family members were glad to see him, he is reduced in their opinion.

norm: It's best not to disturb wildlife.
situation: George sees a moose on the outskirts of a forest and is tempted to prod the moose with a stick.
intention: George wants to consider poking the moose.
moral_action: George slowly backs away from the moose and leaves the moose alone.
moral_consequence: Both George and the moose enjoy the rest of their day in peace.
immoral_action: George decides to go ahead and poke the moose with a stick.
immoral_consequence: The moose immediately becomes annoyed and causes severe injuries to George.

norm: You're expected to apologize to someone for yelling at them.
situation: John's wife Mindy is asking John to apologize for yelling at her for nothing.
intention: John wants to keep his pride.
moral_action: John takes a breath, puts his hand on Mindy's shoulder and says he's sorry.
moral_consequence: Mindy smiles and loves John more and is happier to be with him.
immoral_action: John says he will not apologize and in fact Mindy should apologize to him.
immoral_consequence: Mindy becomes exasperated and cries profusely and leaves John.

norm: It is wrong to be negative about grown children's choices
situation: Barry finds out that his oldest son has chosen to be a Democrat.
intention: Barry wants to respond to his son's political choices.
moral_action: Barry tells his son that he'd like to have a conversation to understand his views.
moral_consequence: Barry's son feels respected and opens up to him about his opinions.
immoral_action: Barry tells his son he's been watching too much MSM and has become brainwashed.
immoral_consequence: Barry's son gets upset at the criticism and pulls away from Barry.

norm: You shouldn't try to touch a stranger's hair.
situation: Eva is standing in line behind a stranger with beautiful hair.
intention: Eva wants the stranger to know how beautiful their hair was.
moral_action: Eva tells the woman how beautiful she thinks her hair is.
moral_consequence: The woman lets Eva know what kind of products she uses on her hair.
immoral_action: Eva runs her hands through the woman's hair and lets her know how lovely it is.
immoral_consequence: The woman slaps Eve across the face and tells her to keep her hands to herself.

norm: It's nice to give coupons to your friends.
situation: Mark is clipping coupons and finds some he won't be able to use but his friends may want.
intention: Mark wants to decide what to do with the coupons.
moral_action: Mark gives the coupons to his friends.
moral_consequence: Mark's friends can get discounts on items.
immoral_action: Mark throws the coupons away.
immoral_consequence: Mark's friends won't get discounts.

norm: It's good to care for your dog's needs.
situation: Frank is at the vet with his dog when the vet offers to give Frank's dog an expensive rabies shot.
intention: Frank wants to decide about the rabies shot.
moral_action: Frank accepts the rabies shot, even though its expensive.
moral_consequence: Frank doesn't worry about his dog when it gets into minor dog fights.
immoral_action: Frank declines the rabies shot, as it is too pricey for him right now.
immoral_consequence: Frank's dog gets into a minor fight with another dog and gets rabies from it.

norm: It's wrong to do something your partner doesn't want.
situation: Hallam wants to spend the evening at a swingers club, but his wife Daphne doesn't like the idea.
intention: Hallam wants to go somewhere on a date.
moral_action: Hallam takes Daphne to her favorite cafe for desert.
moral_consequence: Daphne and Hallam enjoy a nice meal together.
immoral_action: Hallam takes his wife to the swingers club without telling her.
immoral_consequence: Daphne leaves Hallam alone in the club for the evening.

norm: It's wrong to bite a child.
situation: Jon's 3 year old son is biting him on the hand.
intention: Jon wants the child to stop biting him.
moral_action: Jon puts his 3 year old son in timeout for biting.
moral_consequence: The child learns to no longer bite.
immoral_action: Jon bites his 3 year old son back to teach him a lesson.
immoral_consequence: The child's hand bleeds.

norm: It's wrong to hate women.
situation: Gary just found out that he lost out on a promotion to one of his female coworkers.
intention: Gary wants his coworkers to think that he is competent.
moral_action: Gary accepts that he didn't get the promotion and tells his coworkers that we will work even harder in the coming months.
moral_consequence: Gary's coworkers respect how humble he is and speak positively about him to his boss.
immoral_action: Gary tells his colleagues that he only lost out on the promotion because of diversity hiring and that women can't do as good a job without special help.
immoral_consequence: One of Gary's male colleagues shares this message with his boss and Gary gets reprimanded.

norm: It's polite to give notice when you move out.
situation: Madeline is Cynthia's only tenant, and Cynthia relies on Madeline's rent money to pay her bills.
intention: Madeline wants to move out of Cynthia's apartment.
moral_action: Madeline gives Cynthia a two-month notice before moving out of her apartment.
moral_consequence: Cynthia is able to line up a new tenant who will move in once Madeline is gone, assuring that all of her bills continue to be paid on time.
immoral_action: Having already paid this month's rent, Madeline packs her things and moves without saying goodbye or giving warning to Cynthia.
immoral_consequence: Expecting Madeline's rent money to pay next month's bills, Cynthia ends up late on many of them and struggles to catch up for a while.

norm: It's helpful when people advertise their services on social media.
situation: Rachel has started a new business geared towards young people and it figuring out how to get the word out to the community.
intention: Rachel wants people to know about her business.
moral_action: Knowing she is trying to target a younger crowd, Rachel buys ads on social media and targets them to local users.
moral_consequence: Rachel is pleased when many customers at her business mention seeing the ad on social media.
immoral_action: Rachel decides to spend her advertising budget on ads in local print newspapers.
immoral_consequence: Rachel's target audience never sees the ads and Rachel is disappointed by the performance of her business.

norm: It's bad to not be honest about your grades.
situation: Lenny gets his report card which is all B's and comes home when his mom asks him how he did in school this semester.
intention: Lenny wants to answer his mom's question.
moral_action: Lenny tells his mom that he got all B's as it said on the report card.
moral_consequence: Lenny's mom tells him it's not that bad but that he could work harder to improve which he agrees with.
immoral_action: Lenny tells his mom that he got one B but otherwise he got straight A's.
immoral_consequence: Lenny's mom falsely believes that Lenny is doing OK and doesn't check up on him leading Lenny to fall behind at school.

norm: It's wrong to pick on a fellow kid.
situation: Tommy is playing in the school yard and notices another child, Tim, struggling to climb up the jungle gym.
intention: Tommy wants to say something to Tim about his struggle.
