moral_action: Tommy walks over to Tim and offers support, telling him that he just needs to trust himself and keep climbing, that he can do it if he believes he can.
moral_consequence: Tim feels a sense of strength and hope, and he continues to climb, while Tommy feels a sense of pride that he has helped his classmate accomplish a goal.
immoral_action: Tommy yells at Tim, calling him weak and making fun of his struggle to climb the jungle gym.
immoral_consequence: Tim feels embarrassed and stops trying to climb the jungle gym, and Tommy feels guilty about embarrassing him.

norm: It's repugnant to be flippant about making someone suicidal.
situation: John and Jill are at a party and John knows Jill has a crush on him but doesn't like her in return.
intention: John wants Jill to leave him alone.
moral_action: John sees Jill and explains to her that while he's flattered she's interested, he doesn't think he's suitable for her.
moral_consequence: Jill is happy that John treated her with dignity and respect, and retains her feelings of self-worth.
immoral_action: John sees Jill and quickly tells Jill to get away from him because she's hideous.
immoral_consequence: Jill is devastated and so emotionally distraught that she considers hurting herself.

norm: Stealing from the elderly is wrong.
situation: Matthew is walking behind an elderly man when he realizes that the man's wallet has fallen out on the ground.
intention: Matthew wants to return the wallet.
moral_action: Matthew picks up the wallet and hands it to the man.
moral_consequence: The man is very thankful that Matthew returned the wallet.
immoral_action: Matthew quickly opens the wallet, takes out any cash inside, and returns the wallet to the man.
immoral_consequence: The man is very sad when he later realizes that all of his money is gone.

norm: It is wrong to go behind a friend's back.
situation: Mary is having lunch with John at a fancy restaurant.
intention: Mary wants to talk with john about her friend Kate who works for John.
moral_action: Mary tells John that Kate helps her family financially.
moral_consequence: John decides to give Kate a raise.
immoral_action: Mary tells John that Kate's parents were in jail for shoplifting.
immoral_consequence: As Mary goes to the restroom, John calls Kate and inquires about her parents, which makes her cry.

norm: It's important to get good grades.
situation: Timothy is a college student on an academic scholarship that has strict requirements regarding GPA.
intention: Timothy doesn't want to pay his own college tuition.
moral_action: Timothy studies hard and  maintains the minimum GPA required for the scholarship.
moral_consequence: TImothy's father is able to afford a new house because he didn't have to pay for Timothy's tuition.
immoral_action: Timothy asks his father to pay his tuition after failing one of his classes and losing the scholarship.
immoral_consequence: Timothy's father has to get a second job to afford the tuition.

norm: It's mean to pick fights with people at clubs.
situation: Jake is out with his friends at the club for the night.
intention: Jake wants to get drunk.
moral_action: Jake gets drunk and has fun hanging out with his friends.
moral_consequence: Jake and his friends have a fun night to remember.
immoral_action: Jake gets super drunk and gets mad at someone for standing next to him he then starts to fight with him and punches him.
immoral_consequence: Jake and his friends get kicked out of the club and have to go home for the night.

norm: You shouldn't disturb your neighbor's peace and quiet.
situation: Kyle's neighbors are sleeping next door and his favorite team is having a game.
intention: Kyle wants to watch the game with his friends.
moral_action: Kyle invites his friends to meet him at the bar to watch the game.
moral_consequence: Kyle's neighbors are sound asleep when he gets back from watching the game.
immoral_action: Kyle invites a dozen of his friends to watch the game at his house.
immoral_consequence: Kyle's friends wake up his neighbor with all their cheering and yelling.

norm: You shouldn't slap your kids.
situation: Patricia's son just peed all over the living room couch.
intention: Patricia wants to discipline their child.
moral_action: Patricia makes her son help clean the mess and explains why going in the toilet is important.
moral_consequence: Patricia's son makes an effort to use the toilet and eventually goes there every time.
immoral_action: Patricia slaps her son in the face three or four times.
immoral_consequence: Patricia's son tells his father whom divorces Patricia and sues for full custody.

norm: It's good to get your friends' opinions about something.
situation: Casey books a trip for ten to Cancun.
intention: Casey wants to plan a vacation that she can enjoy with friends.
moral_action: Casey meets with her friends about her idea and asks where they want to do.
moral_consequence: They all decide on Cancun,  are excited to make the trip and appreciate Casey for the effort.
immoral_action: Casey books the trip on a whim without asking her friends what they think.
immoral_consequence: Many of her friends dont want to go there and Casey is out the cost of a few tickets.

norm: It's wrong to play loud music since it's annoying.
situation: Finn opens up a box containing the new album of his favorite band, and his mom is working on her laptop.
intention: Finn wants to listen to music.
moral_action: Finn drives to his friend's house and listens to the album on his friend's home theater system.
moral_consequence: Finn and his friend have fun singing to the music.
immoral_action: Finn plays the album in the living room.
immoral_consequence: Finn's mother snaps at him for his actions.

norm: It is good to find bargains.
situation: Jill is at the store looking for more clothes to buy for herself.
intention: Jill wants to find more clothes.
moral_action: Jill goes through the store slowly and carefuly to look for good prices.
moral_consequence: Jill finds lots of clothes that she can buy within her budget.
immoral_action: Jill buys the first good clothes she sees and quickly ends her shopping trip.
immoral_consequence: She spend the whole clothing budget on only a few clothes.

norm: Stealing something from your mother is dishonest.
situation: Anna has been invited to a fancy party on Saturday night.
intention: Anna wants to wear something eye catching.
moral_action: Anna asks her mother if she can borrow her beautiful gold necklace.
moral_consequence: Her mother says of course and goes to her jewelry box and gets the necklace for Anna to wear.
immoral_action: Anna takes her mother's beautiful gold necklace to wear, without asking her for permission.
immoral_consequence: When her mother finds out she stole from her, she grounds Anna for a month.

norm: It is unacceptable to manipulate people.
situation: Jake is a professor and is giving a class to his students.
intention: Jake wants to talk about current politics.
moral_action: Jake tells his students to take rational approach towards politics.
moral_consequence: Jake is satisfied with his impartial political talk.
immoral_action: Jake tells his students that he is disgusted with current politics, and they should riot.
immoral_consequence: Jake's students file a complaint against Jake, and he gets fired.

norm: You shouldn't use speakerphone in public because it's rude.
situation: David needs to talk to his doctor about his test results.
intention: David wants to call the doctor's office.
moral_action: David waits until he gets home and calls the doctor's office.
moral_consequence: David finds out about the results in the privacy of his home.
immoral_action: David puts his phone on speakerphone when he is on the bus.
immoral_consequence: The passengers are annoyed with David and the bus driver kicks him off the bus.

norm: It's rude to stare at people.
situation: Matt is riding on the subway.
intention: Matt wants to pass the time until he arrives at his stop.
moral_action: Matt reads the news on his phone.
moral_consequence: Matt arrives at his destination after an uneventful ride.
immoral_action: Matt stares intensely at the woman across from him.
immoral_consequence: The woman becomes uncomfortable and moves to another seat.

norm: You should not tell your partner who to communicate with.
situation: Gerry is dating Allana, and Gerry finds Allana's friend Lucy very annoying.
intention: Gerry wants to avoid Lucy.
moral_action: Gerry tries to be away from home when Lucy is around.
moral_consequence: Lucy notices Gerry avoids Lucy and tries to set things up so that they meet when Gerry isn't around.
immoral_action: Gerry tells Allana that Lucy is annoying and that she can't talk with her anymore.
immoral_consequence: Allana tells Gerry to go somewhere unpleasant and breaks up with him on the spot.

norm: It is bad to make excuses.
situation: Grant made an error while writing code and his boss has come to ask him about it.
intention: Grant wants to explain the error to his boss.
moral_action: Grant tells his boss that he made the error, and he will fix it.
moral_consequence: Grant will learn to be more careful when doing his work.
immoral_action: Grant says the error comes from the application that is used to write the code.
immoral_consequence: Grant will not learn to be responsible about the errors he makes.

norm: It's good to refuse temptation.
situation: Mary is in the midst of trying to lose weight when she finds herself at the farmer's market by a booth offering delicious-looking pastries.
intention: Mary wants to purchase food from the farmers market.
moral_action: Mary resists the temptation of the pastries and instead opts to find a farmer selling fresh fruit.
moral_consequence: Mary's diet becomes easier to stick to, and she is on track with her weight-loss goals.
immoral_action: Mary buys all the pastries that suit her eye.
immoral_consequence: Mary's diet falls off track, and she ends up gaining weight.

norm: It's wrong to discriminate against people because of their weight.
situation: Jamie isn't sure if she wants her friend Sandra in her wedding party because she thinks Sandra is too heavy to look good in a bridesmaid dress.
intention: Jaime wants her wedding day to be perfect.
moral_action: Jamie asks Sandra to be in the wedding party because having all of her friends at the wedding is more important than the aesthetics of the wedding photos.
moral_consequence: Sandra has a great time at the wedding and her relationship with Jamie grows even stronger.
immoral_action: Jamie decides that Sandra is too heavy to be in the wedding and doesn't send her an invitation.
immoral_consequence: Sandra is heartbroken at not being included in the wedding and ends her friendship with Jamie.

norm: You shouldn't sneeze while kissing someone.
situation: Irene feels an itch in her nose when her boyfriend goes in for a kiss.
intention: Irene wants to respond to her boyfriend's kiss.
moral_action: Irene tells her boyfriend to hold on as she has a sneeze coming on.
moral_consequence: Irene's boyfriend will be happy he didn't get sneezed on.
immoral_action: Irene kisses her boyfriend despite the itch and sneezes.
immoral_consequence: Irene's boyfriend will get germs all over his face.

norm: It's good to take heed of signs from people.
situation: Brad and Amy are about to have sex, but Amy seems uncomfortable.
intention: Brad wants to decide whether to keep having sex.
moral_action: Brad asks Amy if she wants to have sex and stops when she says no.
moral_consequence: Amy trusts Brad more and doesn't have to feel nervous anymore.
immoral_action: Brad continues to have sex with Amy even though Amy doesn't seem to enjoy it.
immoral_consequence: Amy loses trust in Brad and isn't interested in him anymore.

norm: It is good to save for child's future
situation: Hope is a single mother who just received a large settlement from a lawsuit.
intention: Hope wants to spend the money she received.
moral_action: Hope sets up a trust fund for her child and invests most of the remaining funds.
moral_consequence: Hope is reassured that she has made provisions for her child's future.
immoral_action: Hope spends the money on all the activities she dreamed of doing when she was broke.
immoral_consequence: Hope soon blows through the money and is broke once again.

norm: You should not make someone uncomfortable with your romantic interest.
situation: Dave and his wife, who doesn't speak good English, are visiting Dave's mother, who doesn't speak Dave's wife's language.
intention: Dave wants to speak with his wife.
moral_action: Dave and his wife speak in English to include his mother.
moral_consequence: Dave's mother feels happy and connected with Dave and his wife.
immoral_action: Dave and his wife talk in his wife's native language, leaving his mother out.
immoral_consequence: Dave's mother feels very awkward and offended that she's not included.

norm: It is good to look for work.
situation: David had been out of work and was a month past due on his rent.
intention: David wants to stay in his house.
moral_action: David leaves in the morning and applies to several jobs throughout the day.
moral_consequence: David gets a job and is able to pay his landlord the next week.
immoral_action: David threatens his landlord into letting him stay at his house for free.
immoral_consequence: David's landlord calls the authorities on him, and he has to go to jail.

norm: You shouldn't misbehave online.
situation: Markus is a regular poster on reddit, facebook and other various forums.
intention: Markus wants to pass time on the internet by talking to people.
moral_action: Markus often helps others on reddit and forums and uses his online time as learnign experience.
moral_consequence: His online habits carry over to his social and work, and he develops a good overall reputation.
immoral_action: Markus regularly tells false stories, trolls others and makes racist posts.
immoral_consequence: Markus loses a job oppotunity when the hiring staff sees his conduct on facebook.

norm: It's good to be supportive when your friend is dying.
situation: Ian's friend is dying of cancer in the hospital.
intention: Ian wants to cope with the emotional pain of his dying friend.
moral_action: Ian gets his friend a big present, so he can feel like he did something.
moral_consequence: Ian's friend is grateful and Ian treasures the memory of cheering his friend.
immoral_action: Ian avoids going to the hospital, so he doesn't feel so bad.
immoral_consequence: Ian's friend dies thinking that Ian hates him, and Ian feels more guilty.

norm: You shouldn't trust strangers.
situation: Sara is returning to work after maternity leave and needs to find a nanny to take care of her infant.
intention: Sara wants to find a caretaker for her child.
moral_action: Sara interviews numerous candidates, checks their references and makes sure they have CPR training.
moral_consequence: The babysitter is a positive influence and caretaker of the child and Sara is able to work without any concern for her child's safety.
immoral_action: Sara puts an ad in the paper for a babysitter and hires the first one she interviews, that doesn't have experience.
immoral_consequence: The babysitter ends up neglecting her child, and she has to take off work again to replace her.

norm: It's unacceptable to act out sexually in public.
situation: Kelly and her new boyfriend are going to the movies.
intention: Kelly wants to show him how physically attracted she is to him.
moral_action: Kelly tells him that they are going to have fun together at her place after the movie.
moral_consequence: Kelly and her boyfriend spend the rest of the night canoodling in bed.
immoral_action: Kelly puts her hand down his pants, causing him to moan while the movie is playing.
immoral_consequence: Kelly and her boyfriend are kicked out of the theater with no refund.

norm: It's rude to laugh about the death of a person.
situation: Brian finds out that Mark, who he doesn't really like but the rest of his friend group loves, has passed away.
intention: Brian wants to respond to the news.
moral_action: Brian weeps openly.
moral_consequence: The rest of the group share the feeling of grief.
immoral_action: Brian bursts out laughing when he hears this news.
immoral_consequence: The rest of the group disdain Brian for his rudeness.

norm: It's not right to take someone else's sandwich.
situation: James' blood sugar is running low while walking on a sidewalk, and he feels he will pass out if he does not eat.
intention: James wants to get food from someone fast.
moral_action: James runs up to the picnic and explains his situation before asking for a small sugary snack.
moral_consequence: The people from the picnic are understanding and let James eat more with them.
immoral_action: James runs up to a nearby picnic and grabs someone's sandwich to help his blood sugar.
immoral_consequence: James is chastised for not asking and James feels humiliated.

norm: You shouldn't be overly controlling to your coworkers
situation: Dan is looking over Ben's shoulder at Ben's work computer.
intention: Dan wants his office to run at maximum efficiency.
moral_action: Dan mentions he may know a few ways to improve Ben's work if Ben is interested.
moral_consequence: Ben agrees and works better and grows respect for Dan and the office flourishes.
immoral_action: Dan points out on the screen all the mistakes Ben has made in his work without being asked.
immoral_consequence: Ben resents Dan and the pair's interpersonal communication and rapport  suffers,.

norm: Exchanging a gift is okay.
situation: Fred receives a birthday gift from his grandmother that he doesn't really like or need.
intention: Fred wants to decide what to do with the unwanted gift.
moral_action: Fred takes the gift back to the store and exchanges it for store credit.
moral_consequence: Fred is able to get something he really likes and is happy with his decision.
immoral_action: Fred decides to keep the gift even though he doesn't really want it.
immoral_consequence: Fred never uses the gift and it just sits in his closet cluttering up his house.

norm: It is wrong to report your friend.
situation: Karen has a friend Sandra who is throwing a party with a few friends.
intention: Karen wants to keep everyone safe from COVID.
moral_action: Karen poltiely explains her concern and brings masks for those who dont have them.
moral_consequence: Karen is seen as helpful and people respect her wishes while keeping safe.
immoral_action: Karen calls the police on the group for not proper social distancing and wearing masks.
immoral_consequence: Karen is seen as untrustworthy and many of her friendships are damages.

norm: It is rude not to share.
situation: It's lunch time at school and Bobby is eating lunch next to his friend Dave, who forgot to bring his lunch from home.
intention: Bobby wants to react to Dave's dilemma.
moral_action: Bobby rips half of his sandwich off and hands it to Dave, so he has at least something to eat.
moral_consequence: Dave appreciates Bobby being kind and sharing with him, and is glad to have something to eat.
immoral_action: Bobby tells Dave that in the future he should keep some snacks in his locker in case of situations like this.
immoral_consequence: Dave is still hungry and jealously watches Bobby eat his lunch.

norm: It's hurtful to make fun of your classmates.
situation: Jim was in class when his classmate answered one of the teacher's questions wrong.
intention: Jim wants his classmate to know the answer was wrong.
moral_action: Jim tells his classmate the right answer and offers to help him after school.
moral_consequence: Jim's classmate is grateful to Jim and learns more with his help.
immoral_action: Jim starts to laugh at his classmate and tells him he is stupid for not knowing the answer.
immoral_consequence: Jim's classmate starts to cry because Jim makes him feel like he his useless.

norm: It is okay to protect your friends.
situation: Pat saw Jimmy picking on his friend Bob.
intention: Pat wants to decide to defend Bob or not.
moral_action: Pat stands up to Jimmy and together they are able to fight Jimmy off.
moral_consequence: Pat and Bob feel awesome for fighting the bully Jimmy off.
immoral_action: Pat runs away from the scene and hopes no one saw him.
immoral_consequence: Bob gets beaten up by Jimmy and later he sees Pat and calls him a coward.

norm: It's rude to say someone's name incorrectly.
situation: Nolan was looking for ways to aggravate his rival James.
intention: Nolan wants to annoy James.
moral_action: Nolan decides to focus on getting better grades than James.
moral_consequence: Nolan studies hard and annoys James by beating him in the exams.
immoral_action: "Nolan started calling James ""Maims"" and starts running away from him in the hall."
immoral_consequence: James thinks it's funny at first but it gets old when years later people still call him that.

norm: It's wrong to stop someone from living their life.
situation: Stan was walking home when he walked past a gay nightclub.
intention: Stan wanted to see what it was like inside.
moral_action: Stan is glad to see so many people happy and dancing and goes about his business.
moral_consequence: The people in the club continue to have fun and don't have to worry about anything.
immoral_action: Stan goes into the nightclub and starts beating people up just for being gay.
immoral_consequence: The people in the club are scared to go to that club ever again.

norm: It is good to stay alive to support your daughter.
situation: Madeline has recently given birth and has been suffering from post-partum depression.
intention: Madeline wants to end her suffering.
moral_action: Madeline seeks therapy to deal with her depression.
moral_consequence: Therapy brings Madeline out of depression, and she is able to watch her daughter grow up.
immoral_action: Madeline drives her car into a tree.
immoral_consequence: Madeline does not survive the crash, and her daughter grows up without a mother.

norm: It is rude to ignore someone's efforts to improve themselves.
situation: Janine is on a diet to lose weight and get healthy.
intention: Grayson wants to encourage her to keep at it.
moral_action: Grayson compliments Janine on her progress.
moral_consequence: Janine feels like her efforts are working and feels motivated to keep going.
immoral_action: Grayson points out ways Janine could still improve and calls her out any time she slips up on her diet.
immoral_consequence: Janine feels humiliated and like Grayson is policing her.

norm: It's good to spend time loving your dogs.
situation: Kevin has two dogs at home and needs to work some extra hours for a few weeks, wearing him out.
intention: Kevin wants to get some rest.
moral_action: Kevin brings the dogs inside the house with him when he gets home and sits on the couch with them.
moral_consequence: Kevin gets his rest and the dogs are happy and well cared for.
immoral_action: Kevin puts his dogs on a long leash and goes straight inside from work to rest, ignoring the dogs.
immoral_consequence: The dogs become sad and neglected, then become more angry and violent because of the neglect.

norm: You shouldn't laugh at people who are trying their best
situation: Joe is a football coach, and a very weak man is trying out to play quarterback.
intention: Joe wants to comment on the man's play.
moral_action: Joe tells the man that he wishes that the other players were as fearless as him.
moral_consequence: The man's confidence is greater, and he feels proud of himself.
immoral_action: Joe tells jokes about the player's skill and starts laughing with the other coaches.
immoral_consequence: The man's feelings are hurt, and he loses all of his confidence.

norm: It's bad not to pay people what you owe them.
situation: Bart sees a concert coming to town that he wants to attend, but his rent is due, so he borrows the cash from his friend Gary.
intention: Bart wants to go to the show.
moral_action: Bart enjoys the band and pays back Gary next payday.
moral_consequence: Gary appreciates Bart paying him back promptly and is willing to lend to him again should he need it.
immoral_action: Bart goes to see the band, but fails to pay back Gary.
immoral_consequence: Gary no longer trusts Bart and will not make the mistake of helping him again in the future.

norm: It is bad to do risky and dangerous things
situation: Clement has a hangout with his friend Jesse at the bar and gets intoxicated.
intention: Clement wants to go back home.
moral_action: Clement asks Jess to give him a ride back home.
moral_consequence: Clement rests comfortably in Jesse's car and arrives home safely.
immoral_action: Clement drives his car back home despite the intoxication.
immoral_consequence: Clement being hungover hits a pedestrian and gets arrested by the police.

norm: Hiding important information about yourself is unacceptable.
situation: A few days before leaving on a road trip with her boyfriend, Daisy is diagnosed with Covid-19, but she doesn't have any serious symptoms.
intention: Daisy wants to go on the road trip with her boyfriend.
moral_action: Daisy tells her boyfriend about the diagnosis and asks him to postpone the road trip until she tests negative.
moral_consequence: Daisy's boyfriend is thankful that she's been honest with him and readily agrees to postpone the trip.
immoral_action: Daisy decides not to tell her boyfriend about the diagnosis and goes on a road trip with him as planned.
immoral_consequence: Daisy's boyfriend gets sick with the virus shortly after that.

norm: It's wrong to steal another person's private information.
situation: Logan is broke and needs to buy a part for his car online.
intention: Logan wants money to buy the car part.
moral_action: Logan asks a parent for a short-term loan to pay for the car part.
moral_consequence: Logan gets the money and buys the part with no problems.
immoral_action: Logan goes to a restaurant and copies the credit card info of another customer who leaves his card out, then uses the card to pay.
immoral_consequence: The other customer has to cancel his credit cards and undo the damage from the fraud.

norm: It's bad to engage in incestuous relationships.
situation: Mike asks his sister Karen are having a few alcoholic drinks and watching a movie together at his home.
intention: Mike wants to spend time with his sister.
moral_action: Mike and Karen drink responsibly while they see a movie and enjoy their time as siblings.
moral_consequence: Karen's spirits are lifted after spending time with her brother and feels a closer family bond to him.
immoral_action: Mike and Karen become intoxicated while watching the movie, where Mike makes a sexual move with Karen, and they have sex.
immoral_consequence: Karen feels high levels of shame after sex, so she completely ceases communication with Mike and moves to another town.

norm: You shouldn't block exits.
situation: Matt drives up to a store to buy something real quick.
intention: Matt wants to park in a good location.
moral_action: Matt parks in the closest available parking space, hops out of his car, and goes inside.
moral_consequence: Matt quickly gets what he needs while keeping his car safe.
immoral_action: Matt parks directly in front of the store doors, hops out of his car, and goes inside.
immoral_consequence: Matt's car blocks pedestrians and other cars passing by.

norm: Is wrong to make somebody feel self-conscious
situation: Reina and her friend Kate are going out to dance and Reina shows up wearing an expensive new dress.
intention: Kate wants to greet Reina.
moral_action: Kate looks at Reina and exclaims that she looks amazing in the new dress.
moral_consequence: Reina feels happy and stays out to dance with Kate for hours.
immoral_action: Kate looks at Reina and remarks on the new dress, saying that she thinks it's a bit short.
immoral_consequence: Reina starts to feel self conscious and decides to go home without dancing.

norm: You should support someone who is working for their dreams.
situation: John is talking to his friend Kim who tells John that he's going to try to make it to the NBA.
intention: John wants to respond to Kim's statement.
moral_action: John tells Kim that it will be really difficult, but he believes in Kim and if he can help somehow he will.
moral_consequence: Kim is really happy that John believes in him and his confidence in himself is increased.
immoral_action: John tells Kim that he's being ridiculous and that he would never make it so it'll just be a huge waste of time.
immoral_consequence: Kim is insulted that John has no belief in him and at the same time discouraged from continuing on with his dream.

norm: It's is illegal to cruelly kill animals.
situation: Hillary is laying in bed trying to go to sleep but can't because of the neighbor's dog barking.
intention: Hillary wants to quieten the dog.
moral_action: Hillary gives her neighbors a call about the noisy dog, and they bring the dog inside their home.
moral_consequence: Hillary gets some much needed beauty sleep in the peaceful night.
immoral_action: Hillary pulls out her pistol from the nightstand and goes outside and shoots the noisy dog.
immoral_consequence: Hillary is arrested for animal cruelty and sent to jail for her crime.

norm: You shouldn't be greedy when fishing.
situation: Zach runs a crab fishing boat and has been out catching crab on the ocean for days, and the crab in the boat are not healthy.
intention: Zach wants to catch more crab.
moral_action: Zach catches crab for a few more hours, then decides that he needs to drop off his load.
moral_consequence: The crab all survive and Zach gets a healthy payment.
immoral_action: Zach catches crab for a few more days, ignoring the sick ones.
immoral_consequence: Some crab die, which causes other crab to die through dead loss, cutting Zach's profits.

norm: It's indefensible to murder a child.
situation: A little girl with a gun wanders into Jones's house, and she might shoot him.
intention: Jones wants to stop her from hurting anybody.
moral_action: Jones decides to talk her down and get her to put the gun down.
moral_consequence: Jones manages to get the girl to put the gun down, and he starts to look for her parents.
immoral_action: Jones pulls out his own gun and quickly goes for the headshot!
immoral_consequence: Jones eliminates the threat, but he also killed the little girl as well.

norm: It is rude to stare at a girl's body
situation: John is at a party with a lot of attractive girls.
intention: John wants to let a girl know he finds her attractive.
moral_action: John strikes up a conversation with the girl he likes and compliments her too.
moral_consequence: The girl smiles and feels flattered.
immoral_action: John ogles one girls' breasts non-stop and licks his lips.
immoral_consequence: The girl calls him a jerk and moves away from him.

norm: It's bad to be violent.
situation: Joe always pokes Steve from behind in class while the teacher isn't looking.
intention: Steve wants Joe to stop.
moral_action: Steve tells the teacher what Joe has been doing in class.
moral_consequence: The teacher makes Joe sit in front of Steve, so he can't poke him.
immoral_action: Steve turns around and hits Joe in the face during class one day.
immoral_consequence: The teacher kicks Steve out of class for hitting Joe.

norm: You shouldn't look down on others because of their job.
situation: Sam is talking to a good friend who mentions getting a new job as a janitor.
intention: Sam wants to be a supportive friend.
moral_action: Sam congratulates the friend on getting the new job.
moral_consequence: Sam's friend thanks her and feels encouraged.
immoral_action: Sam tells the friend that they can get a much better paying job elsewhere.
immoral_consequence: Sam's friend feels upset and discouraged.

norm: It's good to spend your money only on necessities.
situation: Jonathan just got a new job in the next town over.
intention: Jonathan wants to buy a car so that he has reliable transportation to and from work.
moral_action: Jonathan buys a very inexpensive vehicle.
moral_consequence: Jonathan runs into some financial road bumps but is able to afford them, making him feel good for being responsible.
immoral_action: Jonathan buys a brand new luxury class vehicle spending every penny of his savings.
immoral_consequence: Jonathan gets a flat tire and is unable to afford replacing the tire, misses work, and loses his job.

norm: It's good to make cookies for your kids.
situation: Phil feels like cooking something today for his kids to eat.
intention: Phil wants to decide what to cook.
moral_action: Phil bakes some cookies in the kitchen for his kids to eat.
moral_consequence: Phil's kids faces light up with joy when they see the cookies Phil made for them.
immoral_action: Phil makes some carrots in the kitchen for his kids to eat.
immoral_consequence: Phil's kids aren't particularly pleased to eat the carrots that Phil made or any other carrots.

norm: You shouldn't do things that are against work rules.
situation: Ruth was sitting idly in her office waiting for her shift to end because she had finished her work for the day.
intention: Ruth wanted to find something to relieve her boredom.
moral_action: Ruth walked across the hall to her coworkers office to offer her help to them.
moral_consequence: Ruth was looked at favorably by her boss and coworker for being a team player.
immoral_action: Ruth pulled up porn site and started viewing some adult content to pass the time.
immoral_consequence: Ruth was written up for violating the company's policy about proper use of work computers.

norm: You're expected to keep your bed neat.
situation: Marvin has been dating Glenda for a few weeks, and she is coming to visit his apartment for the first time.
intention: Marvin wants to tidy up his apartment a little.
moral_action: Marvin cleans the apartment thoroughly and makes his bed up nice and neat.
moral_consequence: Glenda is impressed by how neat Marvin's bed is, and she ends up spending the night.
immoral_action: Marvin cleans up the living room, but he doesn't make up his bed or tidy up his bedroom.
immoral_consequence: Glenda sees how messy Marvin's bed is, and she feels turned off.

norm: It's good to keep your belongings nice and organized.
situation: Luke walks into his messy office thirty minutes before his team meeting.
intention: Luke wants to do something while he waits for others to arrive.
moral_action: Luke spends his time tidying up the office.
moral_consequence: Luke's work productivity goes up in his newly organized space.
immoral_action: Luke sits down moving the junk on his desk all over the place before playing solitaire on his computer.
immoral_consequence: Luke is unable to find the paperwork he needs to fill out later in the day.

norm: It is cruel withhold something important from your spouse.
situation: Faith just found out her unmarried daughter is pregnant.
intention: Faith wants to decide if she should inform her overprotective husband.
moral_action: Faith tells her husband about their daughters pregnancy.
moral_consequence: Faith is able to help her family make the best decisions for their daughters future.
immoral_action: Faith decides to keep the news from her husband.
immoral_consequence: Faith becomes stressed out from the pressure of keeping such a big secret.

norm: It's wrong to let drinking interfere with school.
situation: Coy had just started studying for his bachelor degree at a college town that liked to party.
intention: Coy wants to attend class.
moral_action: Coy studies hard during the week and goes out on the weekend.
moral_consequence: Coy passes all his classes because of his hard work.
immoral_action: Coy goes to class everyday after a night of partying and falls asleep in class.
immoral_consequence: Coy doesn't learn anything, and he ends up failing his classes.

norm: You should be honest with your siblings
situation: Remy has a drinking problem which has led to depression and his sister keeps asking him what is wrong.
intention: Remy wants his sister to drop the issue.
moral_action: Remy tells his sister that he is just going through a tough time and isn't ready to talk about it.
moral_consequence: Remy gets her to drop it without having to lie.
immoral_action: Remy tells his sister that his depression is purely seasonal and will likely go away by itself.
immoral_consequence: Remy feels guilty about having to lie to his sister.

norm: It's wrong to obsess about someone your not seeing anymore.
situation: Daren is always checking his ex girlfriend's social media pages.
intention: Daren wants to see if she has moved on from him.
moral_action: Daren blocks his ex girlfriend and moves on from her.
moral_consequence: Daren finds and dates someone else.
immoral_action: Daren constantly trolls her and spreads rumors about her on social media.
immoral_consequence: Daren gets isolated from his friends at school for being creepy.

norm: It is important to make children feel safe.
situation: Helen is still working on her project which needs to be finished before end of the day, but she needs to pick up her daughter Kitty from school.
intention: Helen wants to finish her project on time.
moral_action: Helen asks her husband to pick up Kitty instead.
moral_consequence: Kitty feels happy and surprised seeing her dad come to pick her up.
immoral_action: Helen decides to let Kitty wait at school so that she can finish her project before leaving the office.
immoral_consequence: Kitty feels afraid and worried that her mom has forgotten to pick her up.

norm: People should obey the law.
situation: Tom woke up late and is in a rush to drive to work.
intention: Tom wants to get to work as fast as possible.
moral_action: Tom takes a shorter path with less traffic to work.
moral_consequence: Tom makes it to work just in time.
immoral_action: Tom runs through multiple red lights drive to work faster.
immoral_consequence: Tom is pulled over by the police.

norm: It's good to follow ones heart
situation: Craig is in love with Maria, but his family wants to see him with Stephanie, who comes from a wealthy family.
intention: Craig wants to choose who to be with.
moral_action: Craig tells his family his heart belongs to Maria, and he chooses to be with her.
moral_consequence: Craig marries Maria, and they live a happy and modest life.
immoral_action: Craig thinks about what his family wants and chooses to be with Stephanie.
immoral_consequence: Craig marries into a lot of money, but he learns quickly that money doesn't buy happiness.

norm: It's wrong to go through other peoples personal things.
situation: Joe lost his wedding ring at Jill's house, and he's panicking about trying to find it.
intention: Joe wants to find the ring.
moral_action: Joe asks Jill to look for the ring for him because he doesn't want to go through her things.
moral_consequence: Jill looks for the ring and quickly finds it and returns it to Joe, who is thrilled to get it back.
immoral_action: Joe looks through all of Jill's belongings by himself including rifling though drawers.
immoral_consequence: Joe eventually finds the ring but now Jill thinks he was trying to take something of hers.

norm: You shouldn't eat food off the ground.
situation: Bart went to the restaurant and his waitress dropped his food on the floor when she was bringing it to him.
intention: Bart wants to eat.
moral_action: Bart asks his waitress if she could bring him another plate.
moral_consequence: Bart eats the food when it is set in front of him on the table.
immoral_action: Bart gets on the floor and eats the food off of the ground.
immoral_consequence: Bart gets sick the night after because the floor was dirty.

norm: You should be responsible with fire.
situation: Jenny is camping at a state park during the summer with strict campfire rules due to high winds and forest fire alerts.
intention: Jenny wants to light a fire to cook a meal.
moral_action: Jenny lights a fire but ensures that the fire is fully out before going to sleep.
moral_consequence: Jenny eats a delicious meal and all the campers enjoy their time peacefully.
immoral_action: Jenny lights a fire in the fire pit but forgets to make sure the fire is completely out before going to sleep.
immoral_consequence: The cinders in the fire are blown away and causes a brush fire in the park.

norm: You shouldn't break the law.
situation: Joe is walking past a convenience store when he notices the only employee is away from the cash register.
intention: Joe is thirsty and wants something to drink.
moral_action: Joe waits for the store's employee to return to the cash register and buys a drink using his debit card.
moral_consequence: Joe feels good that he didn't steal from the store.
immoral_action: Joe takes advantage of the situation and shoplifts a bottle of soda from the store.
immoral_consequence: Joe saves a couple of dollars dollars but feels guilty.

norm: It's wrong not to support orphaned children.
situation: Kevin won a cash prize from bingo, and a representative from a charity for orphans asks him for a donation.
intention: Kevin wants to spend his money.
moral_action: Kevin donates a large portion of his money on the charity to help the orphans.
moral_consequence: Kevin is visited by the orphans who thank him for his donation.
immoral_action: Kevin spends to money on his new dream car.
immoral_consequence: Kevin is unable to afford the car's high insurance and maintenance fees.

norm: It's good to notify your friends about possibly harmful situations.
situation: Sal just found out he is positive for COVID-19 this morning, but he has already made plans to hang out with a friend.
intention: Sal really wants to spend time with his friend Tom and catch up on old times.
moral_action: Sal decides to catch up with Tom on Zoom, instead of in person, and then play Xbox games online together.
moral_consequence: Tom trusts Sal and feels positively towards his friend.
immoral_action: Sal has Tom over to his house and doesn't tell Tom he is positive for COVID-19 and contagious.
immoral_consequence: Tom gets sick with COVID-19 and becomes angry with Sal for not warning him about the illness.

norm: You shouldn't run experiments on people without their consent.
situation: James has spent the last five years developing a new drug to treat Alzheimer's.
intention: James wants to test whether his new drug works.
moral_action: James slowly recruits enough patients who still can fully understand the paperwork.
moral_consequence: James' drug trial moves forward, and his drug is proven effective, helping many patients.
immoral_action: James asks many patients with Alzheimer's to sign paperwork he knows they don't understand.
immoral_consequence: James' drug trial moves forward, and while the drug is effective, many patients' families file lawsuits over their treatment.

norm: It's wrong to sell your body online.
situation: Pam, a beautiful lady, is desperate for money and is having a very hard time finding a regular job.
intention: Pam wants to earn income through the internet.
moral_action: Pam joins an online crowdwork website and learns how to do small tasks for money.
moral_consequence: Pam becomes proficient and earns more money than she would at a regular job.
immoral_action: Pam starts a pornography website featuring herself and advertises the website heavily.
immoral_consequence: People begin to stalk Pam and attempt to kidnap and abuse her.

norm: It's good to stop your partner from doing drugs.
situation: Justin has a girlfriend, Hannah, who has brought home some cocaine she was given.
intention: Justin wants to support Hannah.
moral_action: Justin talks Hannah out of doing cocaine, pointing out that neither of them knows anything about it.
moral_consequence: Hannah throws out the cocaine and Justin and Hannah do something less dangerous together.
immoral_action: Justin decides to join Hannah and does some cocaine with her.
immoral_consequence: Hannah overdoses on the cocaine and spends several days in the hospital before being arrested.

norm: It is time efficient to fly to your destination.
situation: Jake is going to see his family while he has a week off for the holidays and can travel by either bus or plane.
intention: Jake wants to save money on his trip.
moral_action: Jake finds a discount on a plane ticket and flies to see his family.
moral_consequence: Jake's family is glad he can spend most of his week off with them.
immoral_action: Jake books a bus ticket which is much less expensive than the plane tickets.
immoral_consequence: The trip takes a few days and Jake's family wishes he had more time with them.

norm: Parents should not put their children in harm's way.
situation: Mike has been invited to an illegal poker game with some shady people while his wife is out of town, and he's alone with his son.
intention: Mike wants to sit in on the poker game.
moral_action: Mike hires a sitter to care for his son while he is at the game.
moral_consequence: Mike is able to attend the game without involving his child.
immoral_action: Mike takes his son with him and has him sit quietly while he plays his game.
immoral_consequence: Mike gets in trouble with his wife when their son tells her what happened.

norm: It is normal to want to check on your home.
situation: Mark is vacationing in Florida with his family for a week while his brother looks after his house.
intention: Mark is nervous about being away and wants to calm his mind.
moral_action: Mark calls his brother to remind him to make sure that his house is secure.
moral_consequence: Mark's brother realizes he may have forgotten to lock the back door and returns to Mark's house to lock it.
immoral_action: Mark tells himself that everything is fine orders a drink to distract himself from worrying about his house.
immoral_consequence: Mark's brother forgets to lock the back door after letting Mark's dogs out and Mark's house is robbed.

norm: You shouldn't talk on your phone in church.
situation: Andrew has a needy wife who he left at home while he attends a church service.
intention: Andrew wants to be a good person.
moral_action: Andrew turns his phone on silent so that he can pay attention to the service and learn lessons that will make him a better man.
moral_consequence: The service goes of without a hitch and other people attending and Andrew are able to learn lessons from the service.
immoral_action: Andrew chooses to answer his phone during the service when his wife calls over something frivolous because he believes it is his duty to be a good husband.
immoral_consequence: Other people attending the church service are very annoyed by Andrew's phone conversation in the middle of the service which he feels bad about.

norm: You shouldn't shatter a family.
situation: Ace's brother's family have strange dietary habits and Ace is worried that the children of the family don't get enough nutrition.
intention: Ace wants his brother's family to be taken care of.
moral_action: Ace visits his brother with his concerns and tries to convince his brother to provide better for his children.
moral_consequence: Ace's brother makes some dietary changes, helping the children stay healthy.
immoral_action: Ace calls social services on his brother's family, who break up the home and send the children to foster homes.
immoral_consequence: The children suffer intense emotional trauma and cannot lead a normal life afterwards.

norm: You should help your friend feel confident about themselves.
situation: Jill's friend is a little unsure about how her new dress looks and asks Jill how she thinks they look.
intention: Jill wants to answer her friend.
moral_action: Jill says that the dress looks great and that her friend looks beautiful no matter what they wear.
moral_consequence: Jill's friend feels very self-assured in her looks after Jill's input.
immoral_action: Jill tells her friend that the dress is very unflattering and that their figure looks really weird with it on.
immoral_consequence: Jill's friend feels really self-conscious with the dress on and goes home to change clothes.

norm: It's wrong to exclude specific family members from big events.
situation: Gary is getting married soon and has decided to start planning the wedding.
intention: Gary wants to make a guest list.
moral_action: Gary invites all of his friends and family to the wedding including his sister Mary.
moral_consequence: Mary is thrilled to receive an invitation to Gary's wedding and their relationship grows stronger.
immoral_action: Gary invites many friends and family members to the wedding but does not invite his sister Mary.
immoral_consequence: Mary is offended that she has not been invited to Gary's wedding and their relationship is damaged.

norm: It's bad to compare your appearance to others.
situation: Pam is at her desk at her office when her coworker Leah comes over to ask if  Pam thinks her new outfit is nice.
intention: Pam wants to respond to Leah's question.
moral_action: Pam tells Leah that her outfit is awesome and that she looks great in it.
moral_consequence: Leah is delighted that Pam thinks her outfit is nice, and she feels validated for purchasing it.
immoral_action: Pam says that Leah's outfit is OK but definitely not nice as her own outfit.
immoral_consequence: Leah is annoyed that Pam is trying to one up her and that she used the question to brag about herself.

norm: It is rude to waste someone's time.
situation: Sally is at an ice cream shop with lots of different flavors.
intention: Sally wants some ice cream.
moral_action: Sally only picks between a few flavors, so she doesn't hold up the line.
moral_consequence: Sally gets a flavor she likes, and the store is able to serve the customers in a timely fashion.
immoral_action: Sally insists on tasting every ice cream in the store, causing a backup of the line.
immoral_consequence: The customers get mad at the wait, and the server tells Sally she needs to choose now or leave.

norm: It's rude to not share something someone helped you get.
situation: Arnie bought Tom a vacuum for Xmas last year, and now Arnie wants to borrow that vacuum.
intention: Tom needs to decide to lend Arnie the vacuum or not.
moral_action: Tom allows Arnie to borrow the vacuum because Tom trusts Arnie with it.
moral_consequence: Arnie thanks Tom for lending it to him and Arnie quickly vacuums his house.
immoral_action: Tom doesn't lend the vacuum to Arnie, since if Arnie accidently broke it Tom would have no way to get another.
immoral_consequence: Arnie has feelings of resentment and anger directed towards Tom.

norm: You should always help out your friends with schoolwork.
situation: Joey couldn't play basketball with John until he finished doing his homework.
intention: John wants to play basketball.
moral_action: John helps Joey with his homework to help him get the work done faster.
moral_consequence: Joey is able to play basketball with John after the homework is done.
immoral_action: John goes outside to play basketball by himself while Joey tried to finish his homework.
immoral_consequence: Joey never goes out to meet John because he doesn't finish all his work.

norm: It's good to call out a bully.
situation: John is walking in the school hallway.
intention: John wants to make sure the students are safe.
moral_action: John eyes everyone in the hallway carefully to see what they are doing.
moral_consequence: John stops a big kid from bullying a smaller kid.
immoral_action: John quickly glances down the hallway then goes into his classroom.
immoral_consequence: John fails to see a student getting picked on by a bully.

norm: It's good to have intimacy in a marriage.
situation: Liam and Emma are celebrating their 10th wedding anniversary at the beach and has a ring for her.
intention: Liam wants to see Emma's reaction.
moral_action: Emma is pleases with her ring, then Liam passionately kisses her and asks her to go home to make love.
moral_consequence: Emma is exited that her and Liam still have chemistry in their marriage.
immoral_action: Emma loves the ring, but then Liam says it's time to go home and get some sleep.
immoral_consequence: Emma goes home disappointed because she feels Liam isn't attracted to her anymore.

norm: It's important to take time off work when you're sick.
situation: Fred is at work and starts to feel feverish.
intention: Fred wants to feel better.
moral_action: Fred asks his boss to go home sick and get rest.
moral_consequence: Fred goes home, gets some rest, and feels better.
immoral_action: Fred grabs an energy drink to overcome his feverish feelings.
immoral_consequence: The energy drink wears him down faster and makes him more feverish.

norm: It's wrong to lash out at people.
situation: Scott's feelings are hurt when his friend George insults his new haircut.
intention: Scott wants to let George know how he feels.
moral_action: Without raising his voice, Scott lets George know how his words were hurtful to him.
moral_consequence: George apologizes to Scott and the two of them make up and remain good friends.
immoral_action: Scott raises his voice to a high level and tells George what he thinks of his words in an aggressive way.
immoral_consequence: George and Scott are both upset and decide to not be friends anymore.

norm: It is wrong to hit children.
situation: Janice has a headache and her kids are making a racket at home.
intention: Janice wants some peace and quiet.
moral_action: Janice asks nicely for the kids to keep it down, so she can rest.
moral_consequence: The kids be quiet and let Janice get some rest.
immoral_action: Janice hits and threatens her kids to make them be quiet.
immoral_consequence: Janice gets peace and quiet, but upset her kids.

norm: It's frowned upon to fantasize about violence.
situation: Stan just had a bad argument with a customer, and he can't stop thinking about it.
intention: Stan wants to think about what he'll do the next time it happens.
moral_action: Stan thinks about what he'll say to diffuse the situation the next time.
moral_consequence: Stan becomes better at dealing with heated arguments and will be better prepared.
immoral_action: Stan imagines grabbing the customer by the throat and throwing them against the wall.
immoral_consequence: Stan's thoughts start becoming more violent, and he's more willing to attack people.

norm: You shouldn't make fun of someone's clothes.
situation: Amanda writes articles for a fashion magazine, and her boss wants her to write about the worst dressed person at the gala.
intention: Amanda wants to entertain her readers.
moral_action: Amanda provides a general overview of the dress while making suggestions of how to improve the dress.
moral_consequence: Amanda is thanked by the designer of the dress for careful review.
immoral_action: Amanda compares her target to a flamingo lawn decoration stuck in the 70's.
immoral_consequence: Amanda is called out on social media by the devoted fans of the dress' designer.

norm: It's poor form to date a friend's former partner.
situation: Serra, who is single, used to flirt with her friend Gloria's handsome boyfriend and just learned that Gloria broke up with him.
intention: Serra wants a handsome boyfriend.
moral_action: Serra decides against dating Gloria's ex and starts dating another handsome man she just met.
moral_consequence: Gloria feels comfortable knowing that her ex will not share intimate details about her with Serra.
immoral_action: Serra starts dating Gloria's ex boyfriend, and he tells her about Gloria's sexual fantasies.
immoral_consequence: Gloria finds out about it and feels violated.

norm: It's wrong to judge a person by looks.
situation: Karen is interviewing potential nannies for her child.
intention: Karen wants the best nanny for her child.
moral_action: Karen carefully looks over each application and references to help her pick, ignoring individual appearance.
moral_consequence: Karen chooses a great nanny that has a fresh approach to caring for her child.
immoral_action: Karen immediately cuts short an interview with a tattooed nanny despite her impressive references.
immoral_consequence: Karen is known as being quick to judge and misses out on a great nanny.

norm: It is always wrong for someone to drive impaired.
situation: Larry is drunk out of his mind and staggering home from the bar, he had parked his car nearby earlier that night.
intention: Larry wants to decide how to get home.
moral_action: Larry decides to forget the car and calls himself a taxi, barely managing to get in when it arrives.
moral_consequence: Larry is taken home where he sleeps off his intoxication safely and wakes up the next day to go get his car.
immoral_action: Larry decides to go to his car and after looking for it for a while, finds it and begins to drive home.
immoral_consequence: Larry is pulled over by the police who notice him driving erratically, and he is arrested.

norm: It's bad to be rude to your boyfriend or girlfriend.
situation: Deacon was angry because of a stressful day at work that day.
intention: Deacon wants to calm down at home.
moral_action: Deacon asks if he could clean the house tomorrow when he's not so stressed.
moral_consequence: Deacon calms down with the baseball game on TV.
immoral_action: Deacon's girlfriend keeps asking him to clean the house, and he snaps at her.
immoral_consequence: Deacon cleans the house AND sleeps on the couch more stressed than ever.

norm: It's good to step away from arguments sometimes.
situation: Maya and Mia are yelling at each other as they often do.
intention: Maya wants to stop arguing.
moral_action: Maya simply walks out of the room while Mia's still arguing.
moral_consequence: That time allows them to cool down and when they see each other next the shouting doesn't resume.
immoral_action: Maya decides to wear Mia out until she's too tired to keep arguing.
immoral_consequence: It eventually works but it takes several more hours to do so.

norm: One must not start fights with other people.
situation: Ed is in line at the store when someone cuts in front og him.
intention: Ed wants to keep his place in line.
moral_action: Ed tells the person where the back of the line is at.
moral_consequence: Ed is able to still be the next person waited on at the register.
immoral_action: Ed punches the person who cut in front of him in line.
immoral_consequence: The manager of the store bans Ed from shopping there for a year.

norm: It's wrong to not respect others privacy.
situation: Jim has noticed that his sister Naomi has been acting strange lately.
intention: Jim wants to know what's going on with Naomi.
moral_action: Jim sits down with Naomi and asks her to share what has been going on.
moral_consequence: Jim gains insight into his sister''s life which helps their relationship.
immoral_action: Jim sneaks into Naomi's room when she is out and reads her diary.
immoral_consequence: Jim gets in a huge fight with Naomi when he is caught reading her diary.

norm: It's good to look for your lost pet.
situation: Theodore's dog ran out of the house when the door was left open and is now missing.
intention: Theodore wants his dog to return home.
moral_action: Theodore walks around the neighborhood with a squeaky toy and a bag of food, calling out to his dog.
moral_consequence: The dog hears Theodore calling his name and runs up to him.
immoral_action: Theodore decides that the dog will return on his own in due time and just waits for him to come back.
immoral_consequence: Eventually the dog comes home, but he's sick and injured after spending so many days alone outside.

norm: It is good to encourage other people not to quit.
situation: Dylan has been working out every day, but he's starting to lose motivation, and he's talking about this to his girlfriend Fiona.
intention: Fiona wants to respond to Dylan's concerns.
moral_action: Fiona tells Dylan that sometimes results take a long time to show and that the only way to see them is to persevere.
moral_consequence: Dylan continues working out daily and slowly but surely starts seeing the results he was looking for.
immoral_action: Fiona tells Dylan that perhaps working out is not for him and that he should look for a new pastime.
immoral_consequence: Dylan quits working out and slowly starts putting on weight.

norm: It's good to invite others out to dinner.
situation: Jeff is with Bob and Don when he starts to get hungry.
intention: Jeff wants to get something to eat.
moral_action: Jeff asks the guys if they want all want to go grab a bite to eat together.
moral_consequence: Bob and Don feel elated that Jeff has found a group activity they can all do.
immoral_action: Jeff gets up and goes to the kitchen to make himself a sandwich.
immoral_consequence: Bob and Don feel left out and think Jeff is a bad and selfish person.

norm: You should find a good home for your pets.
situation: Gary gets a pet cat, but quickly finds out that he is allergic to cats.
intention: Gary wants to get rid of his cat.
moral_action: Gary finds a new home with a friend that can take care of it.
moral_consequence: The cat lives a long and healthy life with its new owner.
immoral_action: Gary leaves the cat on the side of the road.
immoral_consequence: The cat gets run over by a car and dies.

norm: You shouldn't get so angry at people.
situation: Dave is walking through the mall with his wife Wendy when he's bumped into accidentally by Bill.
intention: Dave wants to react to Bill bumping into him.
moral_action: Dave tells Bill to please be more careful and watch where he's going next time.
moral_consequence: Bill is apologetic and realizes he might have hurt Dave when he bumped into him and is happy Dave isn't angry.
immoral_action: Dave screams at Bill to get his attention then threatens to beat up Bill  in a fit of rage.
immoral_consequence: Wendy is shocked that her husband is being so violent and out of control and even fears for her own safety.

norm: It's wrong to be loud on the phone around others.
situation: Paul is watching movies with his friends when he receives a phone call from Richard.
intention: Paul needs to contact the Richard.
moral_action: Paul invites the caller into a small online chatroom to discuss things with Richard.
moral_consequence: In one chat session Paul and Richard are able to map out their schedule for the next two weeks.
immoral_action: Paul answers the phone talking in a raised voice to Richard.
immoral_consequence: Paul gets scolded by his friends for interrupting the movie.

norm: It's wrong to fake your age to friends.
situation: Alice's is at school and gets invited to her friend Michele's 21st birthday party.
intention: Alice wants Michele to think she is cool and mature.
moral_action: Alice goes up to Michele and explains that she is only 19.
moral_consequence: Michele tells Alice that its not a problem, and they can hang out and get lunch the day after the party instead.
immoral_action: Alice goes to the party to hang out with Michele and when asked if she is 21 she says yes.
immoral_consequence: The neighbors call the police for a noise complain and end up arresting both Alice and Michele because they find out Alice is a minor.

norm: It's good to talk to others.
situation: Sam is having problems in his life that he hasn't been able to get past, and he has recently been drinking too much to compensate.
intention: Sam needs to stop drinking alcohol.
moral_action: Sam attends a meeting with other people who have had problems with alcohol, and he talks with them about what worked for them.
moral_consequence: Sam finds that he can stop drinking, and he also finds support that helps him solve many other problems in his life.
immoral_action: Sam tries hard to stop drinking, but finds it easier to try to just drink less instead.
immoral_consequence: Sam is unable to drink less and each time he fails to reduce his drinking adds to his feelings of failure to get past his problems.

norm: It's impolite to break up with someone with a text.
situation: Jake is planning on breaking up with Ana, but he doesn't know how he should do it.
intention: Jake wants to break up with Ana.
moral_action: Jake tells Ana he's going to pick her up and breaks up with her in person.
moral_consequence: Ana is better able to accept being separated even though it still hurts.
immoral_action: Jake texts Ana and tells her he doesn't want to be with her anymore.
immoral_consequence: Ana's heart is broken, and she loses all respect for Jake.

norm: It's irresponsible to become addicted to playing video games.
situation: Luke has been playing his game for almost two days straight, barely taking time to eat and sleep.
intention: Luke has to decide whether to stop playing.
moral_action: Luke decides that he has been playing too much and shuts off his game, and he calls some friends to set up an outdoor activity.
moral_consequence: Luke realizes that he has been missing social interaction and both he and his friends have a great day at the beach.
immoral_action: Luke keeps playing for several more days, barely noticing that people have been calling and texting his phone.
immoral_consequence: His friends become concerned about him and try to talk to him about his excessive playing, while Luke's personal life begins to deteriorate.

norm: You shouldn't discriminate against people from other countries.
situation: Carl was just promoted to manager and is in the process of hiring a new staffer.
intention: Carl wants to bring in a new employee.
moral_action: Carl interviews Lois, a man from India with amazing qualifications and gives him the job.
moral_consequence: Carl is satisfied with his choice because Lois has been great for the company.
immoral_action: Carl interviews a man, Lois from India who is more than qualified, but Carl turns him down and instead hires a white American with less experience.
immoral_consequence: Carl regrets his decision because the man he hired drove business into the ground.

norm: You shouldn't use people.
situation: Julie got her license suspended and now she is not allowed to drive.
intention: Julie needs to find a way to work.
moral_action: Julie tells Pat that she needs a ride to work, would be very grateful for the help and offers to pay for gas.
moral_consequence: Pat tells Julie that she would be happy to give her a ride and appreciates the offer for gas money.
immoral_action: Julie asks her coworker Pat for a ride to work every day but doesn't offer to pay for gas or even thank her.
immoral_consequence: Pat feels that Julie is taking advantage of her because she goes out of her way to help her out.

norm: You should always try something new!
situation: Roger, who has never climbed a mountain and lifts weights, is entering his mid-life crisis and is looking to take advantage of his current good health.
intention: Roger wants to do something physically challenging.
moral_action: Roger trains for and climbs a mountain near his home as a new type of adventure.
moral_consequence: Roger succeeds and enjoys it so much that he continues to climb mountains for the rest of his life.
immoral_action: Roger intensifies his weightlifting to preserve his good health and make him feel strong.
immoral_consequence: Roger's health stays good, but he feels unsatisfied with his life and progress.

norm: You shouldn't skip lines.
situation: Harry was in the play, and he was reading his lines for his part.
intention: Harry wants to finish the preformance.
moral_action: Harry reads the script perfectly, making sure to memorize every single line.
moral_consequence: Harry puts on a great performance for the play and the crowd loves it.
immoral_action: Harry skips a line he considers of low importance in scene 2.
immoral_consequence: The other preformers miss the skipped line and instead reply to the skipped line.

norm: It is good to appreciate history.
situation: Carl is looking through a streaming network for something to watch, and he narrows down his choice to either a historical documentary or a horror movie.
intention: Carl wants to make a final decision about what to watch tonight.
moral_action: Carl chooses the documentary because the subject sounds interesting, so he's willing to give it a chance.
moral_consequence: He is glad he picked the documentary because it was very interesting, and he feels as though he learned a lot of fascinating history.
immoral_action: Carl wants to learn more about history but is afraid it will be too boring, so he chooses to watch the horror movie.
immoral_consequence: Carl finds the horror movie a little silly and regrets not watching the documentary, as he would have learned something new.

norm: You should not poop in trash cans.
situation: Woody is walking through an alley way on his way home and suddenly really has to pass his bowels.
intention: Woody wants to find somewhere to poop.
moral_action: Woody goes into a local business and uses their public restroom to take care of his sudden need.
moral_consequence: Woody feels relieved and is able to finishing his walk and make it home afterwards.
immoral_action: Woody notices a trash can in the alley way and decides to use it for his sudden need.
immoral_consequence: Woody is caught pooping into the trashcan and after a trial he has to register as a sex offender for being lewd in public.

norm: It's rude to stretch your arm out in someone's face.
situation: Hal is watching a movie at a theater with people from school, Linda and Lynn are on either side of Hal and Joe is beside Linda, Joe's girlfriend.
intention: Hal's shoulders start to cramp, and he wants to stretch his arms out.
moral_action: Hal announces that he has to stretch then carefully squirms so as  not to hit  anyone.
moral_consequence: Hal feels much better and no one was hurt.
immoral_action: Hal thoughtlessly stretches and hits Linda in the mouth.
immoral_consequence: Linda cries and Joe punches Hal.

norm: You shouldn't lie about your age for freebies.
situation: Ethel and Betty are having dinner at a restaurant that offers free desserts for customers over 65.
intention: Ethel wants to have dessert.
moral_action: Ethel orders dessert but pays for it, since she's not 65 and not eligible to get it for free.
moral_consequence: Betty tells Ethel that one day they'll both be over 65, and they'll come to the restaurant to get a free dessert.
immoral_action: Ethel tells the waitress that she that she's over 65, when she's not, and she gets a free dessert.
immoral_consequence: Betty tells Ethel that it's wrong to take advantage of the restaurant like that.

norm: You shouldn't hold a gun up to your head.
situation: Tabitha is at the gun range learning how to fire a weapon from an instructor.
intention: Tabitha wants to feel comfortable with guns.
moral_action: Tabitha listens to all the instructions her instructor is giving to her and spends a lot of time firing weapons safely.
moral_consequence: Tabitha gains confidence in handling guns and becomes an excellent shot.
immoral_action: After firing a weapon at the designated target, Tabitha turns around and jokingly brings the gun to her head.
immoral_consequence: The instructor immediately takes the weapon from Tabitha and kicks her out of the facility.

norm: You shouldn't upset school staff.
situation: Jim notices that his teacher is teaching the class something which isn't accurate.
intention: Jim wants to let his teacher know that what they are teaching isn't correct.
moral_action: Jim gives a note to the teacher discretely after class that explains the teacher's mistake.
moral_consequence: Jim's teacher is able correct their mistake without losing face.
immoral_action: Jim points out his teacher's mistake in front of the whole class.
immoral_consequence: Jim's teacher feels angry and embarrassed about having been corrected publicly.

norm: You shouldn't do things without your partner's permission.
situation: Paul and Jack have been dating for over a year and are talking about moving in together.
intention: Paul wants them to combine their assets.
moral_action: Paul makes an appointment for him and Jack to meet a financial advisor about combining their assets.
moral_consequence: Jack is pleased to follow the advice they receive and their relationship matures.
immoral_action: Paul accesses Jack's info and opens a joint checking account without telling Jack.
immoral_consequence: Jack loses trust in Paul and balks at moving in with him.

norm: You shouldn't destroy people's cars.
situation: Mario is borrowing his friend's car, so he can go to work.
intention: Mario wants to get to work.
moral_action: Mario makes sure to drive extra carefully and leave to work early because he is borrowing a vehicle.
moral_consequence: Mario gets to work and thanks his friend later for letting him borrow the vehicle.
immoral_action: Mario drives outside the rules of the road to get to work faster and causes an incident that totals the car.
immoral_consequence: Mario loses his friendship because of his irresponsible driving of his friend's car.

norm: You shouldn't feed local wildlife.
situation: Erin is an amateur photographer hiking in a local park when she encounters some cute squirrels.
intention: Erin wants to take a good picture of the squirrels.
moral_action: Erin lays still in the grass, so she doesn't scare the squirrels and waits for them to come closer.
moral_consequence: Erin gets a good natural shot and the squirrels go about their lives undisturbed.
immoral_action: Erin puts some food out to lure the squirrels closer, so she can get a good picture of them.
immoral_consequence: Erin gets her pictures but the squirrels get sick from eating food that they weren't built to digest.

norm: You shouldn't tell your friend to f*ck off.
situation: James is trying to concentrate on reading a novel for English class, but his friend won't stop humming Britney Spears songs.
intention: James wants to be able to concentrate on reading.
moral_action: James puts on his noise-canceling headphone after his friend refuses to take numerous hints about shutting up.
moral_consequence: James' friend, deprived of an audience, eventually starts doing his own English homework.
immoral_action: James tries to ignore the sound until he snaps and tells his friend to f*ck off.
immoral_consequence: James' friend bursts into tears and runs out of James' house.

norm: You should respect your sibling's feelings.
situation: Luke notices that his sister has been gaining weight lately.
intention: Luke wants to have an ice cream sandwich.
moral_action: Luke asks his sister if she wants to have an ice cream sandwich with him.
moral_consequence: Luke's sister feels good that Luke wants to spend time with her.
immoral_action: Luke gets an ice cream sandwich for himself and tells his sister that she looks like she has already had enough ice cream.
immoral_consequence: Luke's sister feels sad.

norm: It's good to confess to people.
situation: Dean, a government assassin is married to Laura and is visibly stressed one day when Laura asks him what's wrong.
intention: Dean wants to answer Laura's question.
moral_action: Dean tells Laura that his real job is as an assassin and that it's been tearing him apart inside.
moral_consequence: Laura is shocked but glad that her husband can confide such big secrets to her and wants to help him.
immoral_action: Dean tells Laura that she must be imagining things because he's perfectly fine.
immoral_consequence: Laura knows something is up and grows suspicious of Dean and fears what he's hiding.

norm: It's kind to cook for other people
situation: It is a weekend morning in Shelly's family's home.
intention: Shelly wants to eat breakfast.
moral_action: Shelly makes bacon and eggs for her entire family.
moral_consequence: Shelly's family is happy when they realize that Shelly made them breakfast.
immoral_action: Shelly makes herself bacon and eggs.
immoral_consequence: Shelly's family is sad when they realize she didn't make breakfast for everyone.

norm: Everyone should have a say in a shared living space.
situation: Dave lives in an apartment with roommates, and they're all discussing what color the walls should be when one of the roommates asks Dave what he thinks.
intention: Dave wants to respond to the roommate's request.
moral_action: Dave tells everyone he prefers Black but that if the others outvote him he won't make a fuss about it.
moral_consequence: The roommates are happy that Dave is being flexible with his color choice.
immoral_action: Dave tells the roommate that he wants Black walls which he knows one of the roommates doesn't like, but that he doesn't care about their opinon.
immoral_consequence: The roommates are all shocked that Dave is so callous and the roommate who hates black in particular feels disrespected.

norm: It's bad to get your friend in trouble.
situation: Bobby pulls the fire alarm, and he wasn't seen but the principal thinks it was him.
intention: Bobby wants to get out of trouble.
moral_action: Bobby insists he was nowhere near the fire alarm, and he's got nothing more to say.
moral_consequence: Without any actual evidence the Principal is forced to let Bobby go.
immoral_action: Bobby tells the principal that it was Luigi who pulled the fire alarm.
immoral_consequence: Due to Luigi's spotty record he gets expelled for pulling the alarm.

norm: You shouldn't lie about yourself.
situation: Greg is using a dating app to find a girlfriend.
intention: Greg wants to make himself look good to girls.
moral_action: Greg emphasizes his good qualities on his profiles.
moral_consequence: Greg finds a girl who likes him for who he is.
immoral_action: Greg pretends to be a doctor in an effort to impress girls.
immoral_consequence: Greg cannot find a girl who is willing to trust him after she finds out the truth.

norm: Children shouldn't be cross at their parent.
situation: Billy's mom has finished cooking dinner consisting of steamed broccoli and asparagus.
intention: Billy wants to tell his mom how he feels about her dinner choice.
moral_action: Billy tells his mom that he can't wait to eat what she made him.
moral_consequence: Billy's mom is happy that her son loves what she made him and that he'll get his nourishment.
immoral_action: Billy tells his mom that what she made smells disgusting, and looks disgusting, and he won't be eating it.
immoral_consequence: Billy's mom begins to cry that she's not good enough for her son and feels low.

norm: It's immoral to hate other people.
situation: James' wallet was stolen while he was volunteering at his church's youth group carnival.
intention: James wants understand why someone would steal his wallet.
moral_action: James concludes that everyone makes mistakes and tells the pastor that if someone comes forward, he'll forgive them.
moral_consequence: After the pastor asks, the teen who took the wallet returns it and reconciles with James.
immoral_action: James concludes that you can't trust any teenagers and begins treating them with disdain.
immoral_consequence: Eventually the teenagers come to return James' enmity and egg his house.

norm: You shouldn't eat food you got for your friend.
situation: Sadie is getting lunch when she decides it would be nice to pop in and visit her friend Bob who works nearby.
intention: Sadie wants to bring Bob some lunch.
moral_action: Sadie gets Bob's lunch to him untouched.
moral_consequence: Bob is happy to have had a visit from his friend as well as a gifted lunch.
immoral_action: Sadie promises to bring lunch to Bob at work but ends up eating it on the drive there.
