immoral_consequence: Bob's lunchbreak is coming to an end and with no time to get more food, he starves for the rest of the workday.

norm: It's wrong to objectify women.
situation: Thomas is a manager at a consulting firm and has a subordinate named Beth who he enjoys working with.
intention: Thomas wants to compliment Beth.
moral_action: Thomas tells Beth that she's been doing a very good job on her assignments recently.
moral_consequence: Beth is proud of herself and feels more loyal and motivated to work for Thomas.
immoral_action: Thomas tells Beth that she looks very sexy in the tight tight blouse and skirt she's wearing.
immoral_consequence: Beth complains to HR about Thomas' comment, and he loses his job.

norm: It's wrong to spy on people in the bathroom.
situation: Robert's sister has been in the shower for a while and Robert has been waiting.
intention: Robert wants to know how long his sister will be.
moral_action: Robert calls out to his sister and asks if she will be long.
moral_consequence: Robert's sister yells that she won't be much longer in the shower.
immoral_action: Robert pops the door open a crack to see if his sister is almost finished with her shower.
immoral_consequence: Robert's parents send him to counseling because he is looking at his sister naked.

norm: it is inconsiderate to do a poor parking job
situation: Bill drives to a meeting and sees two parking spaces near where he's going.
intention: Bill wants to park his car.
moral_action: Bill parks his car taking care to use only one parking space.
moral_consequence: The next person who wants to park in that area is able to fit into the spot next to Bill's car.
immoral_action: Bill parks his car quickly and carelessly taking up both spaces with his car.
immoral_consequence: The next person that wants to park in that area isn't able to because Bill took all the parking spots.

norm: People should never feel obligated to have sex.
situation: Jean's husband Pete's birthday is today, and he' asked her if she wants to make love, but she is tired.
intention: Jean wants to answer Pete's question.
moral_action: Jeans let's Pete know she is exhausted but would like to have a rain-check, and he is understanding.
moral_consequence: Jean is happy Pete respected her enough not to press the issue and sees him as a good man.
immoral_action: Jean tell's Pete to just hurry and get it over with, so she has sex with him, but isn't into it.
immoral_consequence: Jean feels used after Pete is finished and see's him as selfish.

norm: It's not okay to do things to demean children.
situation: Mike is at a kid's softball game just watching them play when Casey, a kid, comes up to bat.
intention: Mike wants to say something to Casey.
moral_action: Mike tells Casey that he's doing great, and he can get a hit, that Mike believes in him.
moral_consequence: Casey's confidence is boosted as this random stranger is acting like a fan and Casey feels like he's in the majors.
immoral_action: Mike tells Casey that he stinks, and he'll never get a hit because he's a tiny little loser.
immoral_consequence: Casey is embarrassed and starts crying as he has no idea why the mean stranger is insulting him.

norm: It is good to pay people back.
situation: Sally sees a ring she likes while shopping with a friend but cannot afford it.
intention: Sally wants a loan for the ring.
moral_action: Sally gets a loan from her friend and pays her back on time, even offering to pay interest.
moral_consequence: Sally's friend tells everyone how reliable she is and Sally has no trouble getting help from her friends in the future.
immoral_action: Sally gets a loan from her friend but ghosts her after to avoid paying her back.
immoral_consequence: Sally is known as a scammer and no one trusts her anymore.

norm: It is wrong not to feed animals.
situation: Jen, who lives with a partner, is in bed after a long day of work and watching shows on Netflix but remembers her cat's food bowl is empty.
intention: Jen wants to stay in bed and relax without having to do anything.
moral_action: Jen texts her partner while shes laying there and asks him to feed the cat.
moral_consequence: Jen's cat is excited to finally get his dinner and goes to bed with a full stomach.
immoral_action: Jen puts it out of her mind and continues to watch her shows.
immoral_consequence: Jen's cat ends up going without dinner and has to feel hungry all night.

norm: It's rude to call people disgusting.
situation: Becker watches his student perform a scene poorly for an acting assignment.
intention: Becker wants to critique his student.
moral_action: After grading his student, Becker sends them an email with tips on how to improve their performance.
moral_consequence: Becker's student applies the advice landing a leading role in the school play.
immoral_action: Becker notes that his performance made him ill and reminded him of moldy bread.
immoral_consequence: His student breaks down  crying.

norm: You should share duties with your roommates.
situation: John and his roommate agreed they would clean the apartment together and today is cleaning day.
intention: John wants  to go to a friend's house.
moral_action: John spends a couple of hours cleaning the apartment with his roommate before going to his friend's house.
moral_consequence: John's roommate happy that John took his share of the responsibility for cleaning their apartment.
immoral_action: John goes over to his friend's house without doing any cleaning at all.
immoral_consequence: John's roommate thinks that John is lazy and selfish for leaving them with all the cleaning.

norm: You should apologize when you hurt someone or something.
situation: Carol and Marty have an argument and Carol says some very harsh words to Marty.
intention: Carol wants to feel better about what she did.
moral_action: Carol expresses that though still angry, that there was no justification for how she spoke and apologizes.
moral_consequence: Marty accepts and they settle the dispute peacefully shortly after.
immoral_action: Carol justifies her reason behind what she said and does not apologize to Marty.
immoral_consequence: They do not talk for weeks and the marriage is strained for months.

norm: It's wrong to waste your savings.
situation: Tony has money saved up from his summer job in his bank account, and wants to reward himself.
intention: Tony wants to buy himself a gift.
moral_action: Tony buys himself a video game and keeps the rest in savings.
moral_consequence: Tony is happy playing his game and feels responsible saving for the future.
immoral_action: Tony spends everything he's got on liquor and party supplies to share with friends.
immoral_consequence: Tony quickly regrets his decision because he has nothing to show for his hard work.

norm: It's wrong to hurt defenseless animals
situation: Byron has a new dog, and he is getting annoyed by the dog barking at night.
intention: Byron wants to get his dog to stop barking, so he can sleep.
moral_action: Byron gets lessons and tips from a professional dog trainer about getting the dog to bark less.
moral_consequence: Byron is able to get his dog to calm down and sleep during the night, so he is also able to sleep well.
immoral_action: Byron starts to hit his dog every time the dog barks and wakes him up.
immoral_consequence: The dog becomes very fearful of Byron, and they are never able to establish a good relationship.

norm: You shouldn't be biased against Christian people.
situation: Dan feels unsure about going to his friend's wedding, believing that the Christian family will have strong feelings against Dan bringing his husband as his guest.
intention: Dan wants to support his friend by going to the wedding.

moral_consequence: Dan meets a lot of new people, has a great time, and realizes that Christian people are actually very nice and accepting.
immoral_action: Dan decides to go to the wedding with his husband but tries not to talk to anyone and leaves immediately after dinner.
immoral_consequence: Dan leaves feeling sad that he had a bad time at the wedding.

norm: It's rude to clean the toilet with someone's toothbrush.
situation: The bathroom in Emily's house is very dirty.
intention: Emily wants to clean the bathroom.
moral_action: Emily uses the appropriate brushes and supplies to clean the bathroom.
moral_consequence: The bathroom is clean and everyone is healthy.

immoral_consequence: Her brother gets very ill from the germs.

norm: It's mean to get someone fired from their job.
situation: Dean was a customer waiting in a long line at the grocery store.

moral_action: Dean told the manager that the clerk was working very hard at their job.
moral_consequence: The manager gave the clerk a raise and more time off after talking to Dean.
immoral_action: Dean told the manager that the clerk was way too slow and that he was never going to shop there again.
immoral_consequence: The manager fired the clerk right after he talked to Dean.

norm: You shouldn't use a bat to destroy someone's car.
situation: Someone is parked in Alison's assigned parking spot, and she is very upset about it.
intention: Alison wants to get back at the car's owner.

moral_consequence: The inappropriately parked car is towed away and Alison gets her parking spot back.
immoral_action: Alison gets a bat and hits the car, breaking the windows and windshield.
immoral_consequence: Alison is arrested for destruction of property.

norm: You shouldn't refuse to do things with your parents.
situation: Dan is thinking of going to the movies, but his dad Jack wants to go with im.

immoral_consequence: Jack's feelings are hurt, and he starts to feel worthless.

norm: It's wrong to expect money out of people.

norm: It's wrong to insult the people who care about you.
situation: Mike's wife Jen walks up to him in the living room and asks Mike what he thinks of her new hairstye.
intention: Mike wants to respond to Jen.
moral_action: Mike tells Jen that her hair looks as gorgeous as it ever has and that she should come kiss him.
moral_consequence: Jen is delighted that the person whose opinion matters the most to her likes her hair choice.
immoral_action: Mike tells Jen that her hair is awful and that it makes her look like a weird boy.
immoral_consequence: Jen's confidence is shattered, and she begins to cry as she feels her hair choice was a huge mistake.

norm: It's bad to bully others just because they bullied you.
situation: Jake has been bullied in the past by Ray but has been working out and sees Ray.

norm: You shouldn't be friends with people that ridicule you.

norm: You should always take responsibility for anything you do.

immoral_action: Jill says she has no idea who was behind that project.
immoral_consequence: Jill's boss exits the room looking for someone else.

norm: It's good to want what is best for your country.

norm: Ignoring your friends when other people are around is hurtful

norm: It's wrong to push a product to your family.

norm: You shouldn't chat about personal things during a meeting.

norm: You shouldn't seek revenge on your family.
situation: John's father has forbidden him from driving the family car because John hasn't done well in school.

immoral_action: John goes outside and slashes his father's tires and comes back inside to tell him that now they're even since he can't drive either.
immoral_consequence: John's father is incensed that John would do something so wild and rude and is afraid his son is not all there.

norm: It's wrong to resort to violence

norm: You shouldn't date someone who isn't reasonable.

norm: It's good to compromise with your significant other.

situation: Jim is looking through all the resumes he has for a job opening at his company.
intention: Jim wants to pick someone to hire for the job.
moral_action: Jim carefully maps out all the applicants qualifications and hires the person with the best relevant work history for the position.
moral_consequence: Jim is complemented by his department head for choosing the perfect candidate for the job.
immoral_action: Jim ignores all the applicants qualifications and chooses his nephew for the job.
immoral_consequence: Jim is fired for displaying nepotism in his hiring practices.

norm: It's wrong to not sympathize with a creatures death.
situation: Jenny's dog has just recently died and Jenny tells her friend Dave about the sad news.
intention: Dave wants to react to Jenny telling him her dog died.
moral_action: Dave tells Jenny that the news is terrible and that he feels really bad for the poor dog.
moral_consequence: Jenny is a little uplifted by Dave's sympathetic and kind words and feels slightly better about the situation.
immoral_action: Dave tells Jenny that it's fine since it's just a dog, not someone important like a human so not to worry about it so much.
immoral_consequence: Jenny is unhappy that Dave is trivializing the loss of a loved pet and starts to get scared that Dave is a sociopath.

norm: You shouldn't post inappropriate things.
situation: Carla is angry at the Republican party for supporting a bill she opposes and wants to complain about it on social media.
intention: Carla wants to vent her frustrations.
moral_action: Carla tweets to the Republican party's Twitter account that she isn't happy with the party's vote.
moral_consequence: Carla feels better because she expressed herself and let the Republican party know of her discontent.
immoral_action: In the heat of the moment, Carla goes on Twitter to call all Republican's fascists.
immoral_consequence: Carla later feels guilty because some of her friends that follow her are Republican voters.

norm: People shouldn't protest giving schools more funding.
situation: Kent, an elderly resident of a town, hears about a tax hike for school funding and gets upset.
intention: Kent doesn't want to pay more taxes.
moral_action: Kent goes to a public meeting about the taxes, acknowledges that education is important, and asks if they can reduce taxes elsewhere.
moral_consequence: The city reduces taxes in another area to pay for the educational tax increase, helping the school.
immoral_action: Kent goes to a public meeting about the taxes and vigorously protests them.
immoral_consequence: Kent's influence stirs up other people, the taxes are defeated, and the school can't give a quality education.

norm: It is wrong to be with multiple partners.
situation: John is on a dating website when he receives date requests from five women.
intention: John doesn't want to hurt anyone.
moral_action: John chooses one of the women to date, and he sets the other women up with his attractive single friends.
moral_consequence: John gains friends and a wonderful new girlfriend.
immoral_action: John dates all of the women at the same time.
immoral_consequence: John is discovered by the women, and his reputation on the dating site is tarnished.

norm: It's wrong to take advantage of one's partner.
situation: Alex is sleeping in his bed with his wife Jen, and he is sexually aroused.
intention: Alex wants to get rid of his sexual arousal.
moral_action: Alex asks Jen to have sex and decides to just masturbate after she says now.
moral_consequence: Jen trusts Alex to not force her to have sex when she doesn't want to.
immoral_action: Alex has sex with his wife while she is sleeping and without her consent.
immoral_consequence: Jen feels violated and doesn't feel safe sleeping in the same bed with Alex anymore.

norm: It's good to lend your support in an election.
situation: Riley lives in a country with a democracy and it is election day.
intention: Riley wants to spend her day wisely.
moral_action: Riley knows many positions and issues on the ballot can affect her day to day life, so she makes the time to cast her votes in the election.
moral_consequence: Riley makes sure her voice is heard along with others and the country's citizens keep their government in check.
immoral_action: Riley spends all day at work earning a living and misses out on a chance to vote.
immoral_consequence: Riley and people like her grow apathetic about their government since they don't participate and the government abuses their apathy more and more over time.

norm: It's good to realize when you're bothering others.
situation: Bob is talking with a coworker but it seems like they are trying to get work done and that Bob might be annoying them.
intention: Bob wants to decide whether to keep talking to his coworker.
moral_action: Bob decides it's best to leave the coworker alone to do their work and see if they instigate further conversation.
moral_consequence: Bob's coworker is relieved that Bob realized that he was annoying them and feels that now they can get back to work.
immoral_action: Bob keeps talking to the coworker figuring that they would tell him to stop if they wanted him to.
immoral_consequence: Bob's coworker is very annoyed by Bob, and they don't know why he won't get the hint to leave them alone.

norm: It's bad to stay with someone who abuses you.
situation: Christine is hiding in her room after her boyfriend punches her in the face.
intention: Christine wants to be loved.
moral_action: Christine reaches out to her friends for affection, and with their support she breaks up with her boyfriend.
moral_consequence: Christine's relationship with her friends deepens.
immoral_action: Christine stays in the relationship thinking that her boyfriend's behavior will improve.
immoral_consequence: Christine has to go to the doctor after her boyfriend breaks her arm.

norm: It's good to help others find internships and work.
situation: James' parents keeping nagging him to help his younger brother find his first job out of college.
intention: James wants his parents to stop nagging him.
moral_action: James talks to the HR department at his company and recommends his brother as an internship candidate.
moral_consequence: James' brother does well in the interview and often hangs out with James on their lunch breaks.
immoral_action: James tells his parents that his brother might as well enlist in the military since he doesn't know of any job leads.
immoral_consequence: James' parents stop asking about jobs, but complain that he doesn't help the family enough.

norm: It's not nice to shoot animals.
situation: John and Nancy are in their backyard when a couple of annoying seagulls won't stop flying by and disturbing them.
intention: John wants to get the seagulls to stop.
moral_action: John uses a rolled up newspaper to slap against the palm of his hand as loud as he can to scare the birds.
moral_consequence: Nancy is happy to see John find an animal friendly way to get rid of the birds without causing them harm.
immoral_action: John gets out his double barreled shotgun and proceeds to shoot ten rounds into each bird.
immoral_consequence: Nancy is appalled at John's animal abuse and the carnage happening before her and is terrified of John's temper.

norm: It's wrong to not tip someone.
situation: Tom is eating out at a restaurant and the kitchen has overcooked his food.
intention: Tom wants to show that he is unhappy with his meal.
moral_action: Tom points out the problem with his food but tips the server on his way out and later leaves a negative yelp review.
moral_consequence: The server is relieved that they got a tip even though the order was messed up.
immoral_action: Tom complains about the meal and proceeds to leave no gratuity.
immoral_consequence: The server is punished for the mistake of the kitchen staff.

norm: It's bad to cause inconvenience for others.
situation: Joe is at home without a car and his roommates are running late to the game.
intention: Joe wants to go to the mall.
moral_action: Joe hires a taxi and goes to the mall that way.
moral_consequence: Joe's roommates rush to the game not too late and enjoy it and are happy.
immoral_action: Joe begs his roommates to drive him to the mall and says it's an emergency.
immoral_consequence: Joe's roommates will be late to the game and upset with Joe.

norm: Parents should not give up on their children
situation: Lily's daughter is a great artist but is not good at math and English and might have to redo 6th grade again because of that.
intention: Lily wants to stop worrying about her daughter's grades.
moral_action: Lily decides to focus on the things her daughter does well and starts praising her for her art.
moral_consequence: Lily's daughter feels supported and starts thriving at school.
immoral_action: Lily decides it's useless to believe her daughter will ever amount to anything and starts ignoring her.
immoral_consequence: Lily's daughter feels abandoned by her mother and her grades get even worse.

norm: Work shouldn't be treated like a social event.
situation: Brad's is at work and sees his colleague and friend Josh in the office for the first time since he got back from vacation.
intention: Brad wants to know how Josh's vacation was.
moral_action: Brad waits until their lunch break and then asks Josh about his vacation.
moral_consequence: Brad is excited to hear about Josh's vacation and enjoys his lunch.
immoral_action: Brad asks Josh about his recent vacation and spends 20 minutes chatting with him about it in the middle of the office.
immoral_consequence: Brad's boss reprimands him for being disruptive and spending work time chatting about personal matters.

norm: It's bad to attack someone.
situation: Amy saw a man physically fighting with a woman on the sidewalk in front of a jewelry store.
intention: Amy wanted to save the woman from being hurt by the man.
moral_action: Amy called the police when she saw the scuffle on the sidewalk.
moral_consequence: The man got his watch back from the police who arrested the woman for trying to steal his watch.
immoral_action: Amy jumped on the man's back and started choking him while the woman ran away.
immoral_consequence: The man was badly hurt by Amy even though he was the real victim and the woman was trying to steal his watch.

norm: It's considerate to help to help friends
situation: Harry has a friend who has asked him for a ride into work, but he is scheduled to go in early.
intention: Harry wants to get to work on time.
moral_action: Harry makes sure they leave extra early in order to take his friend and get to work on time himself.
moral_consequence: Harry's friend arrives to work early which gives a good impression on his boss.
immoral_action: Harry tells his friend he is unable to take him because he works early.
immoral_consequence: Harry's friend can't find a ride and gets fired for missing another day.

norm: It is good to see a doctor after fainting.
situation: Tom is out walking in the park on a hot summer day when he begins to get dizzy and briefly faints.
intention: Tom wants to feel better.
moral_action: Tom goes to the doctor and receives treatment for dehydration and minor heat exhaustion.
moral_consequence: Tom feels much better and is happy to have gone to the doctor.
immoral_action: Tom drives home and takes an advil.
immoral_consequence: Tom continues to be dehydrated and feels slightly unwell with a minor headache.

norm: It is bad to lie as a cop.
situation: One night James, a cop, arrested a drunk driver but was too tired to fill the paperwork out properly.
intention: James wants the drunk driver convicted.
moral_action: James admits that he forgot to fill out the paperwork and advises the DA to make a deal.
moral_consequence: The drunk driver takes the deal, which involves pleading guilty and a short jail sentence.
immoral_action: James fills out the paperwork two weeks later and testifies that he did it the night of the arrest.
immoral_consequence: The drunk driver's attorney picks James' story apart during questioning, resulting in perjury charges.

norm: You should distinguish your pot brownies from regular brownies.
situation: Phil makes a pan of pot brownies for a party with friends and a pan of regular brownies for a work event.
intention: Phil wants to make sure he takes the right brownies to the right event.
moral_action: Phil bakes the pot brownies in a metal pan and the regular ones in a glass pan.
moral_consequence: Phil is easily able to identify the right brownies for each occasion.
immoral_action: Phil samples brownies from both pans to identify the non-pot pan before work.
immoral_consequence: Phil goes to work high from the brownie he sampled.

norm: You shouldn't pace because it makes other people nervous.
situation: James is trying to concentrate on a difficult programming problem in his open-plan office.
intention: James wants to pace because it helps him concentrate.
moral_action: James takes his laptop outside and paces along the back of the building where no one can see him.
moral_consequence: Both James and his coworkers are fully able to concentrate on their work.
immoral_action: James starts walking back and forth in the open walkspace in the middle of the office.
immoral_consequence: Several of James' colleagues say that he's distracting them, but James ignores them.

norm: It's bad to have affairs.
situation: Chuck and his wife are going through a difficult time in their relationship and Chuck feels unloved.
intention: Chuck wants to feel loved.
moral_action: Chuck makes efforts to treat his wife kindly and to love her.
moral_consequence: Chuck's relationship with his wife improves, and she returns the affection.
immoral_action: Chuck finds another woman and has an affair with her.
immoral_consequence: Chuck's marriage gets even worse as he's no longer emotionally involved in it.

norm: It gross to use someone else's tooth brush.
situation: Jack is getting ready for bed.
intention: Jack needs to brush his teeth but can't find his toothbrush.
moral_action: Jack gets a new toothbrush out of the closet and brushes his teeth.
moral_consequence: His teeth are clean and no one is mad at him.
immoral_action: Jack uses his brother's toothbrush.
immoral_consequence: When he brother finds out, he punches Jack for being so gross.

norm: It is wrong to be disrespectful to soldiers.
situation: Peter was attending a Fourth of July parade and sees soldiers walking in the street.
intention: Peter wants to let the soldiers know how he feels about their service.
moral_action: Peter approaches the soldiers and thanks them for their service to the country.
moral_consequence: Peter feels proud for letting the soldiers know their actions are meaningful.
immoral_action: Peter yells at the soldiers and calls them names such as killers.
immoral_consequence: The organizers of the parade make Peter leave the area for the day.

norm: It is bad to just kick people out.
situation: Jacob notices drunk best friend getting into trouble with the other guests at his party.
intention: Jacob wants people to have fun at his party.
moral_action: Jacob escorts his friend to his room until he sobers up, and plays a game with the other guests.
moral_consequence: Jacob joins the game when he's sober making new friends.
immoral_action: Jacob demands that his friend go home removing him from the party.
immoral_consequence: His best friend gets into a wreck when he attempts to drive home.

norm: You shouldn't refuse your coworker's requests.
situation: Oliver asks his coworker Sam to help him print some copies of the report because Oliver has too much on his hands.
intention: Sam wants to respond to Oliver.
moral_action: Sam asks Oliver how many copies he needs printed and if he could help with anything else.
moral_consequence: Oliver is grateful for Sam's help and treats him to lunch.
immoral_action: Sam tells Oliver that he can do it himself because Sam was about to go on break in 30 minutes.
immoral_consequence: Oliver looks irritated with Sam and two have a strained working relationship.

norm: You shouldn't bother someone while they are trying to sleep.
situation: Jenny needs to study for an important exam and her roommate Jill knows the material but just got home from work and went to bed.
intention: Jenny wants help with her studies.
moral_action: Jenny decides to look for help online, asking around on various forums until she gets the answers she seeks.
moral_consequence: Jill gets a full night's sleep and wakes up happy and refreshed.
immoral_action: Jenny bugs Jill to help her until Jill finally gets out of bed and works on studying with her.
immoral_consequence: Jill doesn't sleep well and misses an important class in the morning.

norm: It's good to inspire people with a good speech.
situation: Nelson leads a squad of soldiers in the army and is preparing to lead them into a tough battle.
intention: Nelson wants to get the squad moving towards the enemy.
moral_action: Nelson stands tall and delivers a speech about fighting for King and Country before leading the charge.
moral_consequence: Nelson's squad members give a loud cheer and advance on the foe with fire in their bellies.
immoral_action: Nelson gestures vaguely towards the enemy positions and tells the squad to get moving already.
immoral_consequence: Nelson's squad members grumble among themselves and move forwards halfheartedly.

norm: You shouldn't let people tell you how to eat.
situation: John's friend tells John not to eat the french fries, as they are fattening.
intention: John doesn't want to offend his friend.
moral_action: John tells his friend that it's his cheat day for his diet and it's a one-time treat.
moral_consequence: John's friend agrees and leaves John alone.
immoral_action: John agrees with his friend and doesn't eat the french fries.
immoral_consequence: John wastes his money that he spent on the fries and goes hungry.

norm: It's nice to make food for your parents.
situation: Jill lives at home with her mom and has woken up starving since she skipped dinner.
intention: Jill wants to make breakfast at home.
moral_action: Jill makes enough food for breakfast to feed both her and her mother.
moral_consequence: Jill's mother is touched that she prepared breakfast for her, and they eat together.
immoral_action: Jill makes only enough breakfast for one plate which she eats alone.
immoral_consequence: Jill's mom has to spend time and energy to make her own breakfast.

norm: It is wrong to get your friend in trouble.
situation: Larry is interrogated by his teacher after witnessing his friend Greg put a frog in her water bottle as a prank.
intention: Larry wants to answer the teacher's questions.
moral_action: Larry tells his teacher that he didn't see who was responsible for the prank.
moral_consequence: Greg doesn't get in trouble and is thankful to Larry for his loyalty.
immoral_action: Larry tells his teacher that Greg was responsible for the frog in her water bottle.
immoral_consequence: Greg gets detention for the prank and is mad at Larry for tattling on him.

norm: Not hitting on your best friend's significant other is expected.
situation: Jason and Molly are partner's who are currently throwing a party at their house.
intention: Mark wants to comment on Molly's appearance.
moral_action: Mark tells Molly that he likes her dress and shoes.
moral_consequence: Molly thanks Mark for the comments and returns the favor to him.
immoral_action: Mark tells Molly that he thinks her dress makes her look hot.
immoral_consequence: Molly tells Jason and has Mark kicked out of the party.

norm: It is rude to argue with someone about their religion.
situation: Jeff's new roommate is a Muslim and when the roommate gets up very early to pray, he wakes up Jeff.
intention: Jeff wants to sleep later in the mornings.
moral_action: Jeff sits down with his roommate and asks him if can do his morning prayer in the living room, far from the bedrooms.
moral_consequence: Jeff's roommate agrees to pray in the living room in the morning, and Jeff can sleep in.
immoral_action: Jeff yells at his roommate when he gets home, saying his stupid chants for his stupid religion are waking him up every morning.
immoral_consequence: Jeff's roommate gets angry at Jeff and decides to move out, leaving Jeff to find another roommate.

norm: It is bad to make unwanted advances on others
situation: Joe is passing out awards to the winners at a big press conference.
intention: Joe wants to have his picture taken with the winners.
moral_action: Joe stands beside each winner with his hands behind his back and smile for the camera.
moral_consequence: Joe is respected for his admirable treatment and enthusiasm for taking photos with the award winners.
immoral_action: Joe puts his around around a young girl while they pose for a picture, and he gropes her breast.
immoral_consequence: Joe is looked at as a creep by everyone who sees the picture of him groping the young girl.

norm: It's expected that people tip a waiter for their service.
situation: Rin, who is at a restaurant,has waited a long time for her steak meal to come out and when it does it's overcooked.
intention: Rin wants to show how unhappy she is with the meal.
moral_action: Rin points out the problem with the steak and leaves an average tip for the service.
moral_consequence: The server is relieved to get a tip even though there was a problem with the food.
immoral_action: Rin tells the server about the temperature of the meat and leaves no tip.
immoral_consequence: The server makes less money for the day because of the chef's mistake.

norm: You shouldn't tell people to lose weight since it's rude.
situation: John is at work when he sees Tim, an old teammate that was in another division for the past year who has gained significant weight.
intention: John wants to comment on Tim's changed appearance.
moral_action: John tells Tim that it's been so long since they've seen each other he hardly recognized Tim.
moral_consequence: Tim happily replies that it's been a long time, indeed and that he's happy to see John.
immoral_action: John tells Tim that he looks way bigger than the last time he saw him and that he needs to slim back down.
immoral_consequence: Tim is insulted by the comment and now feels self conscious about his appearance.

norm: It's unhealthy to accept abuse from somebody else
situation: Tom has been in a long term emotionally abusive relationship with someone.
intention: Tom wants to avoid confrontation.
moral_action: Tom stands his ground and dumps his partner giving them no room to even confront him by cutting them off completely.
moral_consequence: Tom is liberated from a terrible relationship and is happier from it.
immoral_action: Tom pretends everything is okay in order to avoid fighting.
immoral_consequence: Tom suffers staying in the abusive relationship.

norm: It's good to speak out against people who harmed you.
situation: Karen, who was abused by a man, sees that the man is charged with abusing another woman.
intention: Karen wants to help the abused woman.
moral_action: Karen comes out publicly with her story of abuse from the man and joins in the charges.
moral_consequence: The man loses the case and is put in prison, away from potential victims.
immoral_action: Karen sends an encouraging, anonymous letter to the other abused woman.
immoral_consequence: The woman feels encouraged, but she loses the case due to lack of evidence.

norm: You shouldn't say something hurtful to your spouse.
situation: Millie thinks her husband is not involved enough in house chores and finds it frustrating.
intention: Millie wants to vent out her frustration.
moral_action: Millie tells her husband that she is tired of doing almost everything around the house and asks if he could help her with it.
moral_consequence: Millie's husband understands how much she has been doing and feels glad she told him.
immoral_action: Millie tells her husband how frustrated she is and tells him she thinks he is selfish and unhelpful.
immoral_consequence: Millie's husband is shocked by Millie's accusations.

norm: It's good to give cats a good home.
situation: Terry has noticed a stray cat wandering outside his house in the street.
intention: Terry wants to help the stray cat.
moral_action: Terry lures the cat into his house with food and water.
moral_consequence: The cat is adopted into a good home.
immoral_action: Terry leaves out some food and water for the cat.
immoral_consequence: The cat eats and drinks but remains homeless.

norm: It's marvelous to make someone's day with a simple call.
situation: Anthony's grandmother has been staying at home due to the quarantine order, with only her caregiver to check on her.
intention: Anthony wants to check on his grandmother.
moral_action: Anthony calls his grandmother to see how she is doing.
moral_consequence: Anthony and his grandmother have a long conversation, and she feels less lonely.
immoral_action: Anthony texts his grandmother's caregiver to check his grandmother's condition.
immoral_consequence: The caregiver replies that Anthony's grandmother has been feeling lonely.

norm: You shouldn't stay with someone who wants a divorce.
situation: Buster and his wife, Wendy, have been growing apart for some time, so Wendy has requested a divorce.
intention: Buster wants to keep Wendy in his life.
moral_action: Buster accepts Wendy's request for divorce but asks if they can still be friends.
moral_consequence: Wendy agrees to Buster's proposal, and they both move on to live better lives.
immoral_action: Buster refuses to sign the divorce papers.
immoral_consequence: Buster and Wendy are both deprived of moving on and finding happiness again.

norm: It's bad to involve your friends in your drama.
situation: Jack decides to break up with Jill after finding out she cheated on him.
intention: Jack wants the support of their circle of friends.
moral_action: Jack leans on his friends for emotional support but doesn't begrudge them for remaining friendly with Jill.
moral_consequence: Jack manages not to pressure his friends into picking sides.
immoral_action: Jack badmouths Jill to all of their mutual friends and asks them to turn away from her.
immoral_consequence: Jack loses the friends who disapprove of his actions.

norm: It's rude to be late for an appointment
situation: Mandy has set up an appointment to discuss extra credit work with her professor, who has told her that he has a doctors appointment right after their meeting time.
intention: Mandy wants to make the meeting with her professor.
moral_action: Mandy sets an alarm, so she can get to her appointment on time.
moral_consequence: Mandy and her professor work out a suitable extra credit arrangement, and he makes it to the doctors office on time.
immoral_action: Mandy neglects to set an alarm and therefore arrives late to her meeting with the professor.
immoral_consequence: Mandy's professor waits for her to arrive and ends up missing his doctors appointment.

norm: People are expected to make sure their pets are safe.
situation: Peter has just adopted a tiny gerbil whom he's very fond of.
intention: Peter wants his gerbil to enjoy the outdoors.
moral_action: Peter builds a protective enclosure outside for the gerbil and puts him there.
moral_consequence: The gerbil enjoys the warm outdoors and Peter is happy too.
immoral_action: Peter puts his gerbil on the back yard grass and watches him.
immoral_consequence: A bird quickly comes and snatches the gerbil and Peter is sad.

norm: You should always pay someone for their services.
situation: Jackie has some computer trouble and asks her nephew Bobby to fix her computer for her, so she can finish her work project.
intention: Jackie needs to have her computer fixed enough for her to finish a work project.
moral_action: Jackie asks Bobby to fix her computer and pays him the small fee that he asks for.
moral_consequence: Jackie's computer is fixed, and she is able to continue using it for her work projects.
immoral_action: Jackie asks Bobby to help fix her computer but says no when he asks for payment, causing Bobby to rush through the repairs.
immoral_consequence: Jackie's computer works long enough to finish her project but breaks after, and she has to spend $200 to have her problem fixed.

norm: It's wrong to start fights with coworkers.
situation: Spencer and Kendall are going to door to door handing out pamphlets for a new business.
intention: Spencer wants to split the pamphlets evenly.
moral_action: Spencer suggests that they split the pamphlets evenly so that they each do the same amount of work.
moral_consequence: Kendall agrees and they finish the job fairly.
immoral_action: Spencer takes half of the pamphlets and throws the other half at Kendall.
immoral_consequence: Kendall is offended and calls their boss to complain about Spencer's behavior.

norm: You shouldn't let someone underage drive a car.
situation: Ben, who has a large piece of property, has a teenage son who wants to start driving but isn't old enough yet.
intention: Ben wants his son to get experience driving now.
moral_action: Ben helps his son get his own used dirtbike and has him practice on it.
moral_consequence: Ben's son crashes the dirtbike several times but quickly learns to handle it.
immoral_action: Ben allows his son to drive his car on the property for practice.
immoral_consequence: Ben's son goes too fast, loses control of the car, and hits a tree.

norm: It's deceitful to cheat on your spouse
situation: Max isn't happy with his marriage to his wife and has a crush on a coworker.
intention: Max doesn't want to get divorced from his wife.
moral_action: Max tells his wife that they should go to counseling to work on improving their marriage.
moral_consequence: Max's wife is encouraged by Max's willingness to work on strengthening their marriage.
immoral_action: Max has a secret affair with his coworker and goes to great lengths to hide it from his wife.
immoral_consequence: Max's wife wonders why Max is so distant from her and becomes unhappy.

norm: It's kind to give someone a ride who needs it.
situation: Ryan is getting ready for work when his coworker and friend Henry calls and asks if Ryan can pick him on his way because his car died.
intention: Ryan wants to get to work on time.
moral_action: Ryan only has time to pick up Henry or get breakfast on his way to work, he decides Henry is more important and stops to grab him.
moral_consequence: Henry is so happy that he got to work on time and thanks Ryan by buying him lunch later that day.
immoral_action: Ryan is running a little late and really wants to grab breakfast on his way to work, so he doesn't pick up Henry and gets breakfast instead.
immoral_consequence: When Henry gets to work an hour late he gets mad at Ryan for not picking him up and ends their friendship for his selfishness.

norm: You shouldn't judge someone who is abstinent.
situation: John has been dating Jane for a few months when she tells him that she won't have sex before marriage.
intention: John wants to tell Jane how he feels about her admission.
moral_action: John respects Jane's position on having a sexual relationship.
moral_consequence: John is free to decide if he wants to pursue a long term relationship with Jane.
immoral_action: John calls Jane a tease and tries pressuring her to have sex with him.
immoral_consequence: John loses any chance he had of being with Jane again.

norm: It's polite to ask people how they're doing.
situation: Doug heads over to his friend Deacon's house.
intention: Doug wants to talk to Deacon.
moral_action: Doug asks Deacon how he is when he first sees him.
moral_consequence: Deacon mentions himself for a little while before they talk about other stuff.
immoral_action: Doug gets right into talking about football and food.
immoral_consequence: They talk for a while but Deacon is mildly annoyed Doug didn't ask how he was.

norm: It's wrong to destroy someone's items.
situation: Tony is a movie star who is on a date with Jenny, when Frank the paparazzi appears out of nowhere and takes Ton'ys picture.
intention: Tony wants to express to Frank his displeasure at Frank taking a picture.
moral_action: Tony tells Frank that he is just trying to have a quiet evening with his girlfriend and would appriciate some privacy.
moral_consequence: Jenny is impressed that Tony can handle pressure with such grace and is even more attracted to him.
immoral_action: Tony walks up to Frank aggressively and grabs the camera out of his hand before smashing it to pieces on the ground.
immoral_consequence: Jenny is horrified that Tony is so violent and immediately is full of regret about dating him.

norm: It's not safe to drive fast
situation: Keith was running late when he was driving to work in his car.
intention: Keith wants to work eight hours.
moral_action: Keith arrives to work late, so he stays at work a half hour later than normal.
moral_consequence: Keith doesn't lose any hours on his paycheck when he gets paid.
immoral_action: Keith drives as fast as he can in order to get to work on time.
immoral_consequence: Keith is stopped by a police officer and gets a speeding ticket.

norm: You shouldn't gossip about your friends.
situation: Darcy has just learned that her friend Romy is pregnant, and then Darcy's boyfriend calls.
intention: Darcy wants to talk to her boyfriend.
moral_action: Darcy tells her boyfriend about how she and Romy met and became friends.
moral_consequence: Romy's trust in Darcy remains intact, and she makes her the Godmother of her baby.
immoral_action: Darcy tells her boyfriend that Romy is pregnant and criticizes her for being irresponsible.
immoral_consequence: Romy finds out that Darcy thinks she's irresponsible for getting pregnant and doesn't invite her to her baby shower.

norm: You shouldn't aggressively sell to people.
situation: Tim works as a sales person for a home delivery company.
intention: Tim wants to be a top seller.
moral_action: Tim maintains a client list that he uses to track what his customers like to buy.
moral_consequence: Tim is able to keep track of his best clients and contact them only when what they like is available.
immoral_action: Tim targets elderly clients and calls them repeatedly to pressure them to buy.
immoral_consequence: Tim gets numerous complaints about his tactics.

norm: You shouldn't uninvite your friends from your party.
situation: Hank invites people to a party when he realizes that the location won't hold all of his friends.
intention: Hank wants to avoid overfilling the party location.
moral_action: Hank finds a larger place to have the party so everyone can come.
moral_consequence: Everyone comes and enjoys the party.
immoral_action: Hank contacts some friends and tells them that there's not enough room for them to come.
immoral_consequence: The friends Hank calls think that Hank doesn't like them as much as others and get jealous.

norm: Parents should take charge of their children's health.
situation: Nancy's son skinned his knee while biking outside and is treating the wound.
intention: Nancy wants the wound to heal.
moral_action: Nancy has her son report to her twice a day to clean and re-bandage the wound.
moral_consequence: The wound heals quickly under Nancy's care.
immoral_action: Nancy instructs her son on how to care for the wound, including cleaning and re-bandaging it.
immoral_consequence: Nancy's son prefers to play instead of care for a wound, so it gets infected.

norm: It's good to support artists and their work.
situation: Jill goes to the museum and sees a sign that says suggested donation.
intention: Jill wants to enter the museum.
moral_action: Jill puts some money into the donation box that is displayed.
moral_consequence: Jill sees the exhibits and feels good about herself for supporting the art in them.
immoral_action: Jill just walks on into the museum without paying anything at all.
immoral_consequence: Jill sees the exhibits for free and without having to pay for them.

norm: It's wrong to take advantage of people's insecurities.
situation: James is on a date with a woman who has body image issues related to obesity and low self-esteem.
intention: James wants to try to seduce his date.
moral_action: James tries to compliment his date instead of insulting her to win her over.
moral_consequence: James' date begins to feel a connection, and they both laugh and talk for hours.
immoral_action: James tries to 'neg' his date by insulting her weight in an effort to seduce her.
immoral_consequence: James' date just feels insulted and the date goes horribly.

norm: It's great to have a close relationship with older relatives.
situation: Jack's grandma lives on her own and sometimes feels lonely.
intention: Jack wants to respond to his grandma's situation.
moral_action: Jack is empathetic to his grandma and visits her once every week.
moral_consequence: His grandma feels very happy and makes a delicious meal for Jack every time he comes to her home.
immoral_action: Jack thinks that old people are annoying and troublesome, so he never contacts his grandma.
immoral_consequence: His grandma feels very lonely and develops into a depression.

norm: It is bad to hurt your friend's feelings
situation: Bill's friend Tom just got a new haircut that isn't so great, and he asks Bill how it looks.
intention: Bill wants to respond to Tom's question.
moral_action: Bill tells Tom that the haircut looks great and that he is very handsome.
moral_consequence: Tom feels happy and confident about how he looks.
immoral_action: Bill tells Tom that his new haircut is ugly and it makes him look funny.
immoral_consequence: Tom feels bad and becomes more self conscious about how he looks.

norm: It's wrong to hate everybody
situation: Jeff hates everybody, because no one seems to like him.
intention: Jeff wants to cheer himself up.
moral_action: Jeff decides maybe if he likes some people they will like him back.
moral_consequence: Jeff stops hating some people and turns out some of those people start liking him.
immoral_action: Jeff keeps on hating everyone as he watches TV and hates the characters on the show.
immoral_consequence: No one likes Jeff because he in turn likes no one else, and he continues to be stuck in hate.

norm: It's rude to ignore the rules in the library.
situation: Charles is in the library with a friend, working on an assignment together, when Charles sees a mistake in his friend's paper.
intention: Charles wants to notify his friend about his mistake.
moral_action: Charles points at his friend's mistake, then shows him his paper with the correct work.
moral_consequence: Charles' friend corrects his work and no one is disturbed.
immoral_action: Charles tells his friend that he messed up and describes the problem to him.
immoral_consequence: The librarian gets annoyed and tells Charles to be quiet.

norm: It's polite to make plans with friends in advance.
situation: Bob bought a pair of season tickets for the local college's football season, planning to treat one of his friends to a game.
intention: Bob wants to take his friend Bill to a football game.
moral_action: Bob contacts Bill a few weeks in advance with an offer to go to a football game.
moral_consequence: Bill has time to catch up on his chores and is free to accompany Bob to the game while ensuring domestic bliss.
immoral_action: Bob shows up at Bill's house one Saturday morning and insists that Bill come to the game with him.
immoral_consequence: Bob and Bill go to the game but Bill's wife is upset that he is leaving his weekend chores undone.

norm: Not wanting to infect your coworkers is common decency.
situation: Joe has a bit of cough and fever and isn't feeling that great on Monday morning.
intention: Joe wants to avoid losing money for the day.
moral_action: Joe calls his boss and asks if he can work from home since he isn't feeling well.
moral_consequence: Joe gets all his work done at home while being sick with no loss of pay.
immoral_action: Joe ignores his symptoms and goes to work anyway, so he doesn't miss out on his pay.
immoral_consequence: Joe infects his coworkers and everyone has to self-isolate for 2 weeks.

norm: It's rude to be antisocial at work.
situation: John has been suffering in his personal life but still has to work with others.
intention: John just wants to get through his work day and have it over with.
moral_action: John keeps his personal life out of the workplace and tries to stay busy at work so the day goes by faster.
moral_consequence: John's co-workers are undisturbed by John's problems which are not theirs, and they work flow goes smoothly for the day.
immoral_action: John avoids people all day at work because of his sour mood about his personal life hoping it'll make the day easier for him.
immoral_consequence: John's co-workers find him difficult to work with and John becomes a bottleneck for everybody's work flow.

norm: It's good to try and meet new friends in life.
situation: John is at a corporate event and sees co-workers as well as visitors attending the event.
intention: John wants to talk to someone.
moral_action: John finds a new person to talk with and gets to know him better.
moral_consequence: The person John meets is able to help him with his career.
immoral_action: John finds a co-worker to talk with and chats with him the whole time.
immoral_consequence: John's social circle stays small, and he gets into a social rut.

norm: It's good to teach children responsibility with good pet choices.
situation: Jaime has a son, Mark, and Mark has caught a mouse that was in the house to keep as a pet.
intention: Jaime wants Mark to have a pet.
moral_action: Jaime tells Mark he can't keep a wild animal, but they go and get a fish.
moral_consequence: Mark has fun watching the fish swim around and feeding it.
immoral_action: Jaime lets Mark keep the mouse and Mark keeps it in a box.
immoral_consequence: The mouse escapes and chews up one of Mark's stuffed animals.

norm: It's wrong to say mean things to homeless people.
situation: Tom exits a convenient store upon which a homeless person approaches and asks for money.
intention: Tom wants to make it clear he won't be giving out any money.
moral_action: Tom apologizes to the homeless person and tells him he cannot spare any money.
moral_consequence: The homeless person thanks him anyway for acknowledging him.
immoral_action: Tom tells the homeless person to get a job and brushes him off.
immoral_consequence: The homeless person is sad and discouraged by this treatment.

norm: It's good to protect the vulnerable and defenseless.
situation: Jess sees an hooded man hit an elderly woman while trying to pull her purse from her.
intention: Jess wants to remain safe.
moral_action: Jess uses her taser on the robber.
moral_consequence: The robber falls to the ground and Jess gets the elderly woman home.
immoral_action: Jess runs away while the elderly woman gets beaten and robbed.
immoral_consequence: Jess escapes to safety, but feels guilty for leaving the old woman.

norm: You should be understanding of other people's issues.
situation: Hilda's friend Rosa is crying because she mistakenly broke a fingernail.
intention: Hilda wants to reply to Rosa.
moral_action: Hilda explains that lots of people have other problems a lot worse than a broken nail.
moral_consequence: Rosa is glad she doesn't have any of those problems and feels much better.
immoral_action: "Hilda gets upset and points out that she has several ""real"" problems she isn't crying over."
immoral_consequence: Rosa gets upset and cries even more because her friend is shouting at her.

norm: You shouldn't let people drink that are underage.
situation: Keith is drinking a beer on his porch after completing yard work with his 15 year old son John.
intention: Keith wants to commend John for a job well done.
moral_action: Keith offers John an ice cream from a local shop as a reward for working hard in the yard.
moral_consequence: John and Keith get a ride to the ice cream shop and enjoy sundaes together.
immoral_action: Keith offers John a beer as a 'thank you' for helping out with the yard work.
immoral_consequence: John enjoys the beer and begins seeking it out through other people on a more regular basis, forming a harmful habit.

norm: You shouldn't ignore your girlfriend.
situation: Bob and Sue have been dating on and off for a couple of months.
intention: Bob wants to reach max level on his World of Warcraft golblin shaman.
moral_action: Bob contacts Sue frequently and shares his excitement about reaching a milestone for his online character.
moral_consequence: Bob maxes out his WoW character and Sue thinks Bob is a silly boy but a good boyfriend.
immoral_action: Bob pretty much ignores Sue and spends most of his free time gaming.
immoral_consequence: Bob maxes out his WoW character but Sue dumps him for someone more attentive.

norm: It's nice to comfort someone when they're upset.
situation: John's at home with his buddies when his wife Mindy walks in crying.
intention: John wants to go with his buddies to the game.
moral_action: John tells his buddies he'll meet them at the game later and comforts his wife.
moral_consequence: Mindy feels happier and loves John more.
immoral_action: John rushes out with his buddies to the game.
immoral_consequence: Mindy gets more upset and resents John.

norm: It's rude to very loud in an office setting.
situation: Jack is sitting at his desk at work, and he is listening to a very funny podcast.
intention: Jack wants to laugh out loud.
moral_action: Jack goes into the hallway to laugh about the podcast he was listening too.
moral_consequence: Jack avoids disturbing his office environment, and he also gets to laugh the way he wanted.
immoral_action: Jack laughs manically at his desk, disrupting the quiet office and annoying his coworkers.
immoral_consequence: Jack's coworkers are frustrated with him making all this noise, and he is reported.

norm: It is important to not offend others.
situation: John is upset that Eric is on his computer longer than anticipated.
intention: John wants to vent his anger.
moral_action: John asks Eric how long he will be on the computer and says he needs it soon and takes a deep breath.
moral_consequence: Eric is grateful for John letting him use the computer and tries to finish up quickly.
immoral_action: John confronts Eric and calls him a bunch of bad names in a raised voice.
immoral_consequence: Eric resents John and doesn't feel badly at all for using his computer.

norm: It's bad to blow up with anger at a parent.
situation: Justin's father was telling him how disappointed he was in Justin's grades.
intention: Justin wants his father to know why his grades are falling.
moral_action: Justin explains to his father that he needs more help on his school work.
moral_consequence: Justin's father calls his teacher, and they find a tutor for Justin.
immoral_action: Justin starts to yell at his father and tell him that the bad grades were his father's fault.
immoral_consequence: Justin's father is shocked and upset at the outburst and grounds Justin for a week.

norm: You shouldn't stop talking to your friends.
situation: Mary's grade school best friend Kelly is considered a dork now that they are in high school.
intention: Mary wants to be popular in high school.
moral_action: Mary and Kelly make new friends together.
moral_consequence: Mary forms a network of friends she can be close to.
immoral_action: Mary starts to ignore Kelly as she tries to gain popularity.
immoral_consequence: Mary trades a true friend for some superficial friendships.

norm: It is wrong to use volence against a partner.
situation: Jonesy is with his partner and the are having a disagreement.
intention: Jonesy wants to settle the disagreement once and for all.
moral_action: Jonesy concedes to his partner in the disagreement and does what they want to do.
moral_consequence: Jonesy is annoyed he isn't heard but knew the disagreement wasn't worth the trouble.
immoral_action: Jonesy lays his hands on his partner to bring an abrupt end to their disagreement.
immoral_consequence: Jonesy's partner doesn't like the abuse and calls the police leading to Jonesy's arrest.

norm: It's good to share charities with others.
situation: Monica asks April how she should spend her prize money.
intention: April wants to help her friend spend money.
moral_action: April encourages Monica to give her money to a charity from a list she provides.
moral_consequence: Monica receives a thank you gift from the community for her donations.
immoral_action: April takes Monica shopping, and encourages Monica to buy everything she wants at the stores.
immoral_consequence: Monica can't fit all of the things she buys into her apartment.

norm: It is bad to get sent to detention
situation: Alan is a 4th grader who is excited about a Christmas party that he will be going to tonight.
intention: Alan wants school to be over with so the night can begin.
moral_action: Alan quietly counts down the hours to the day but stays focused on his work.
moral_consequence: Alan gets home from school without incident and enjoys the party that evening.
immoral_action: Alan acts up and is disruptive in class resulting in him getting detention.
immoral_consequence: Alan is punished by his parents by not being allowed to go to the Christmas party.

norm: It's unreasonable to avoid a woman when she's menstruating.
situation: John and his currently menstruating wife are both home for the evening.
intention: John wants to watch TV.
moral_action: John makes his wife a treat and invites her to join him in the living room for their favorite TV show.
moral_consequence: John's wife feels comforted and cared for by her husband which strengthens their relationship further.
immoral_action: John sees that his wife is already watching TV in the living room, so he goes to the watch the basement TV instead.
immoral_consequence: John's wife notices John's choice and their relationship grows more distant.

norm: It is bad to intentionally say things to offend people
situation: David is talking with a group of friends when Joe is walking nearby and drops a stack of books.
intention: David wants to impress his group of friends.
moral_action: David rushes over to help Joe pick up his books for him.
moral_consequence: Joe is thankful for the help and continues on his way.
immoral_action: David loudly laughs and points at Joe and calls him clumsy.
immoral_consequence: Joe's feeling are hurt, and he picks up his books.

norm: It's good to have an intimate relationship with your partner.
situation: Jennifer and Brad are in bed when Jennifer starts to touch Brad and asks him if he wants to make love.
intention: Brad wants to answer the proposal for lovemaking.
moral_action: Brad tells Jennifer that she doesn't have to ask him twice and jumps on her.
moral_consequence: Jennifer is delighted that Brad is still attracted to her and that he wants to make love to her.
immoral_action: Brad tells Jennifer that he's exhausted and that it's not a good time right now.
immoral_consequence: Jennifer feels lonely and unsatisfied and a little bit self conscious wondering why Brad isn't into it.

norm: It's wrong to downvote posts just because they are new.
situation: Stacy posted an awesome selfie on a subreddit but people are ignoring it in favor of newer posts.
intention: Stacy wants people to see her post on the subreddit.
moral_action: Stacy start linking her Reddit post outside of Reddit so more people see it.
moral_consequence: Stacy's post gets more views and Stacy feels satisfied.
immoral_action: Stacy starts downvoting newer posts so that her post is seen.
immoral_consequence: Reddit suspends Stacy for vote manipulation and Stacy feels ashamed.

norm: It's bad to make a mess.
situation: Mark is cooking dinner at his friend's house and dishes are piling up.
intention: Mark wants to get dinner done on time.
moral_action: Mark cleans as he goes so when he is done, there are no dishes to do.
moral_consequence: Everyone has a good night and enjoys Mark's cooking.
immoral_action: Mark does not do any dishes, and leaves them laying around.
immoral_consequence: Mark will never be invited to his friend's house again to cook.

norm: It's wrong to be rude to a friends girlfriend.
situation: Scott's friend Joe is dating a girl that he just met named Brooke who is not seen as very attractive by most.
intention: Scott wants to meet Brooke.
moral_action: Scott gives Brooke a chance and makes an effort to get to know her.
moral_consequence: Scott and Brooke have  alot in common, and he thinks that Brooke and Joe are a great match.
immoral_action: Scott mocks Brooke for her looks and makes rude comments to Joe saying that he could do better.
immoral_consequence: Joe continues to date Brooke and stops hanging around Scott because of his rudeness to her.

norm: It's wrong to disobey your boss.
situation: Emmy's boss wants her to spy on a rival business to find out what they're doing differently.
intention: Emmy has to respond to her boss.
moral_action: Emmy agrees to spy on the company and learns a lot of big secrets.
moral_consequence: Emmy's boss is proud of her and thinks about giving her a pay raise.
immoral_action: Emmy refuses to spy on anyone because she says it goes against her values.
immoral_consequence: Emmy's boss doesn't think Emmy is dedicated enough and thinks about firing her.

norm: It's wrong to sneak into places.
situation: Once he got home after attending a party at the house of one of his coworkers, Bob realizes he had forgotten his favorite cap there.
intention: Bob wants to get his favorite cap back.
moral_action: Bob waits until the next day and calls his coworker in advance before stopping by her place to get his cap.
moral_consequence: Bob's coworker gets a good night sleep and is not bothered by Bob's behavior.
immoral_action: Bob returns to his coworker's place and since the lights are off decides to enter the house through the back door and find his cap.
immoral_consequence: Bob's coworker wakes up from the noise, thinks there's an intruder in the house and gets extremely scared.

norm: It's bad to serve guests with dirty dishes.
situation: Peter is having his friends over for a dinner party tonight.
intention: Peter wants to serve dinner to his friends.
moral_action: Peter thoroughly cleans his dishes before serving food on them to his guests.
moral_consequence: Peter's guests love his food and go to his dinner parties regularly.
immoral_action: Peter serves dinner on dishes that have little bits of food stuck to them.
immoral_consequence: Peter's guests are disgusted and do not go to Peter's dinner parties anymore.

norm: It's wrong to cheat on your partner.
situation: Jeff, a married man, has been working with a very attractive coworker.
intention: Jeff wants to get to know his coworker better.
moral_action: Jeff learns more about his coworker and maintains a professional relationship.
moral_consequence: Jeff leads a happy life with his wife and is also successful at his work.
immoral_action: Jeff decides to start an intimate relationship with his coworker.
immoral_consequence: Jeff's wife finds out and demands a divorce.

norm: You shouldn't take someone else's medication without permission
situation: Christina is feeling a lot of pain in her head.
intention: Christina wants the pain to stop.
moral_action: Christina goes to a doctor and gets a prescription.
moral_consequence: Christina's headache feels much better.
immoral_action: Christina sneaks into her mom's room and takes her Valium.
immoral_consequence: Christina gets yelled at by her mom.

norm: It's bad to make a creepy move on someone.
situation: Benjamin is at a party and meets Tina who is exactly his type.
intention: Benjamin wants to show Tina he is interested.
moral_action: Benjamin engages with Tina about her interests and compliments her on her personality.
moral_consequence: Tina appreciates Benjamin's attention and becomes interested in Benjamin.
immoral_action: Benjamin makes some suggestive comments towards Tina and drapes his arm around her.
immoral_consequence: Other partygoers notice that Benjamin is making Tina uncomfortable and call him out for being a creep.

norm: It's bad to try to get someone fired.
situation: Eric is a worker at an office, and his coworker, Terry, annoys him with his non-stop phone talking.
intention: Eric wants Terry to stop annoying him.
moral_action: Eric aks Terry if he could do his phone conversations somewhere else.
moral_consequence: Terry obliges, and Eric is able to work in peace and quiet.
immoral_action: Eric goes to his boss claiming Terry is always late to work.
immoral_consequence: Eric's boss investigates, finds out Eric is not telling the truth, and fires him.

norm: You shouldn't be passive-aggressive.
situation: Finn has left the dishes in the sink again which annoys his wife Greta.
intention: Greta wants Finn to do the dishes.
moral_action: Greta tells Finn that it bothers her when he leaves dishes in the sink and asks him to wash them as soon as possible.
moral_consequence: Finn understands and begins correcting his bad habit.
immoral_action: Greta takes the dirty dishes from the sink and puts them in Finn's car.
immoral_consequence: Finn gets upset and he and Greta start fighting.

norm: It's good to be employed in a full time job.
situation: Carla is offered a stable full time job, but her best friend wants to employ her at her temporary agency.
intention: Carla doesn't want to offend her best friend.
moral_action: Carla works at her full time job, but she works for her friend one day a week.
moral_consequence: Carla takes a nice vacation over the holidays with the extra money she gets from working two jobs.
immoral_action: Carla works at her friends temporary agency.
immoral_consequence: Carla is unable to pay her bills later in the year after her job ends.

norm: You shouldn't lie about being sober.
situation: Tom is proud of his wife, Lisa, because she has stopped drinking and is attending meetings to help her, but Lisa has started to drink again.
intention: Lisa doesn't want Tom to know that she started drinking again.
moral_action: Lisa comes clean at a meeting and tells her support group that she needs help to stop drinking again, and that she doesn't want it to hurt her marriage.
moral_consequence: She gets the help that she needs and stops drinking again through her support structure, and Tom continues to be proud of her efforts.
immoral_action: Lisa keeps attending the meetings, but she drinks both before and after each one of them.
immoral_consequence: Tom and everyone at the meetings quickly become aware that Lisa is drinking and Lisa feels shame and embarrassment that they found out.

norm: It's good to talk to your parents about sex.
situation: Randy and Diana's daughter Brittany is planning to lose her virginity to her boyfriend, but isn't well educated on intercourse and protection.
intention: Brittney wants to try to avoid getting pregnant.
moral_action: Brittney tells Randy and Diana she plans to sleep with her boyfriend, so they take her to get birth control and tell her about protection.
moral_consequence: Brittney avoids becoming pregnant because she took proper precautions.
immoral_action: Brittney makes love to her boyfriend without a condom, but tells him to pull out before he's finished.
immoral_consequence: Brittney takes a pregnancy test a few days later and it comes back positive.

norm: It's rude to move snow onto someone else's car.
situation: Hector is shoveling snow from around his car after a heavy winter storm.
intention: Hector wants to get the snow off of his shovel.
moral_action: Hector carefully throws the snow onto the side of the road where it is out of everyone's way.
moral_consequence: The car owner sees Hector shoveling the snow responsibly and thanks him for being courteous.
immoral_action: Hector throws the snow onto another car behind him, blocking the windshield.
immoral_consequence: The car owner sees Hector throwing snow on his car and challenges him to a fight.

norm: You shouldn't use prescriptions that aren't meant for you.
situation: Megan, who is having a headache, is hanging out with Gina when she notices Gina's pain medicine on a table.
intention: Megan wants to get rid of her headache.
moral_action: Megan asks Gina if she knows anything that would help lessen her pain.
moral_consequence: Megan receives some relaxing tea that eliminates her headache.
immoral_action: Megan takes some of Gina's pain medications.
immoral_consequence: Megan ends up consuming a high dose by accident and is sent to the hospital.

norm: It is rude to return things in an unusable condition.
situation: Danny promised to return Jim's bike after a week, but both of its tires blew while riding it.
intention: Danny wants to return the bike to Jim.
moral_action: Danny gets the tires replaced before giving the bike back to Jim.
moral_consequence: Jim thanks Danny for returning his bike in working order.
immoral_action: Danny gives the bike back to Jim as it is.
immoral_consequence: Jim gets mad at Danny for ruining the tires on his bike.

norm: It's wrong to judge people based on factors like age.
situation: James needed to hire a new receptionist and the most qualified candidate was 55 years old.
intention: James wants to hire a personable, hard-working receptionist.
moral_action: James hires the older candidate on the basis of their extensive experience.
moral_consequence: James is pleased by how little training his new receptionist needs.
immoral_action: James hires a fresh college grad with a much shorter resume rather than the older candidate.
immoral_consequence: James is frustrated by his receptionist's compulsive use of social media during working hours.

norm: You shouldn't decieve others on social media.
situation: Kim just added her crush from school on a new facebook account.
intention: Kim wants her crush to like her.
moral_action: Kim sends a message to her crush asking him how he is doing.
moral_consequence: Kim's crush is flattered that she is interested in him and wants to meet up.
immoral_action: Kim posts fake pictures and invents another personality in order for her crush to like her.
immoral_consequence: Kim's crush finds out that she is not real and hates her for tricking him.

norm: You shouldn't put yourself down.
situation: Ted has a girlfriend and is going through a rough time in life.
intention: Ted wants to cope with his suffering.
moral_action: Ted starts telling himself that he can overcome these difficulties to encourage him to put out effort.
moral_consequence: Ted's girlfriend admires Ted more for pushing through difficulties proactively.
immoral_action: Ted keeps telling himself that he is a worthless person and can't do anything right as a way of explaining his suffering.
immoral_consequence: Ted's girlfriend gets fed up with Ted's lack of self-esteem and leaves him.

norm: Friends should support each other in difficult times.
situation: Kim is at home relaxing when she gets a call from her friend Pete who asks her to babysit for him because he's in a pinch.
intention: Kim wants to respond to Pete's request.
moral_action: Kim tells Pete that she can watch his kids for him if he needs her to and asks him when to come over.
moral_consequence: Pete is delighted that Kim is going to help him out and relieved he found a babysitter.
immoral_action: Kim tells Pete that she's not really good with kids, in fact, she doesn't like them, so he should hire a professional.
immoral_consequence: Pete is stressed out that he still doesn't have a babysitter and is annoyed at Kim for not wanting to help him.

norm: It is rude to exclude someone from a game.
situation: Jose was picking a team to play a pick-up basketball game, and one guy was left out of the teams.
intention: Jose has to decide what to tell the last guy.
moral_action: Jose tells the guy that he can be a substitute for his team.
moral_consequence: The guy feels relieved that he gets to play and doesn't feel as embarrassed.
immoral_action: Jose tells the guy to get lost, because he's not good enough.
immoral_consequence: The guy's feelings are hurt, and they feel disrespected.

norm: It's bad to lose your friend's property.
situation: Sue has a date with Aaron and borrowed her friend June's bracelet for the night.
intention: Sue wants to meet with June afterwards.
moral_action: After Sue's date she is washing her hands in a public restroom, but leaves the bracelet on, so she can avoid getting it lost, then goes to June's.
moral_consequence: Sue is able to give June back her bracelet and feels grateful for her letting her borrow it.

norm: It's good to refrain from being angry with others.
situation: Gary is on the subway when the subway has to brake hard and Kyle who wasn't holding a hand rail comes flying into Gary hurting him.
intention: Gary wants to show his displeasure to Kyle for causing him pain.
moral_action: Gary tells Kyle that he really needs to hold the hand rail because of situations like this and that he really hurt him.
moral_consequence: Kyle is remorseful and apologizes to Gary and asks him if there's anything he can do to make him feel better.
immoral_action: Gary starts to foam at the  mouth and silently grabs Kyle by the neck and stares into his eyes while squeezing his throat.
immoral_consequence: Kyle is utterly terrified as Gary looks like a maniac and Kyle is finding it hard to breathe.

norm: It's wrong to try to deceive other people.
situation: Jack is the owner of a used car with many problems and tries to sell the car.
intention: Jack wants to sell his used car.
moral_action: Jack fully discloses all the issues with the used car before making the sale.
moral_consequence: The person who buys the car is aware of the problems and has no issues paying Jack for the car.
immoral_action: Jack avoids mentioning any problems with the used car throughout the sales process.
immoral_consequence: The buyer of the used car files a lawsuit against Jack for selling him a bad car.

norm: You should apologize for spilling drinks on people.
situation: Jamie is out have dinner with some co workers.
intention: Jamie wants to order some dessert.
moral_action: Jamie spills her water glass on her boss and then apologizes and cleans it up then she orders dessert.
moral_consequence: Jamie's boss respects her and decides to promote her the next week.
immoral_action: Jamie knocks her elbow into her water glass and the water spill on her boss she doesn't apologize and just orders some dessert.
immoral_consequence: Jamie's boss feels disrespected and decides not to give Jamie a promotion.

norm: You shouldn't wear other people's underwear.
situation: Jenny is sleeping over her friend Kalani's house when she realizes she has forgotten her underwear at home.
intention: Jenny wants to find a pair of undies to wear.
moral_action: Jenny tells Kalani that she forgot to pack underwear.
moral_consequence: Kalani gives Jenny a brand new, unworn pair that she recently purchased.
immoral_action: Jenny goes through Kalani's clothes and puts on a pair of her undies.
immoral_consequence: Kalani sees Jenny wearing her underwear and is so creeped out she tells her to leave.

norm: It's wrong to kick people in the testicles.
situation: Ben and Harry were arguing with each other after school was out.
intention: Ben wants it to be quiet.
moral_action: Ben walks away from Harry for a few minutes to be alone.
moral_consequence: When Ben returns, Harry apologizes to him for arguing with him.
