immoral_action: Jane goes to her child and tells the child how hard of a day she had.
immoral_consequence: The child is confused and doesn't know how to react.

norm: It is rude not to get food for your partner.
situation: Brenda's husband was at home with a broken leg while she was in town getting something to eat.
intention: Brenda wants to order her food.
moral_action: Brenda drives up to her favorite fast food place and orders food for her and her husband.
moral_consequence: Brenda's husband is grateful that she took the time to think about him.
immoral_action: Brenda drives up to her favorite fast food place and orders a burger and fries for herself.
immoral_consequence: Brenda's husband has nothing to eat that night and is jealous when he sees Brenda's food.

norm: It's wrong to like hearing kids cry.
situation: Sammy is working tonight at a haunted house as a zombie, and his job involves chasing certain targets to scare them.
intention: Sammy wants to do his job well.
moral_action: Sammy observes groups from afar before attacking the person most nervous in the group.
moral_consequence: Sammy is invited to work at the haunted house next year.
immoral_action: Sammy only targets children because he enjoys scaring them.
immoral_consequence: Sammy's pay is docked when customers complain about his performance.

norm: It's acceptable to rescue an animal that's being mistreated.
situation: Doug's neighbor hasn't fed or let their dog inside in over a 3 weeks.
intention: Doug wants to check on the dog.
moral_action: Doug goes towards the dog and sees that he is extremely thin, then unchains him and puts him in his vehicle to get him help.
moral_consequence: The dog gets medical treatment and begins to thrive.
immoral_action: Doug approaches the dog and notices clear signs of abuse and neglect, but walks away afraid of confrontation.
immoral_consequence: The dog becomes very ill and passes away without getting help or treatment.

norm: It's bad to abandon your significant other.
situation: Tom just found out that his girlfriend Edna is pregnant with his baby, and he expects that raising it will cost him a lot of money.
intention: Tom wants to maintain his lifestyle.
moral_action: Tom decides to ask for a promotion at work and begins investing some of his money, so he can increase his income and help Edna raise the baby.
moral_consequence: Edna and Tom grow closer and their relationship improves as they raise their child together without having to make financial sacrifices.
immoral_action: Tom packs up and moves to another town, leaving Edna to raise the baby on her own.
immoral_consequence: Tom is able to live as he was before and Edna has to shoulder all the costs of raising the child.

norm: You shouldn't disrespect others in front of children.
situation: Joni and her kids are at a drive through buying food the employee taking their order is rude.
intention: Joni wants to respond to the worker.
moral_action: Joni asks to speak to the manager to explain the way she was treated.
moral_consequence: Joni's kids learned how to properly deal with rude employee's.
immoral_action: Joni begins to berate the employee for the way they look because she is upset.
immoral_consequence: Joni's kids begin to treat other kids at school poorly because now that they've seen their mom do it, they think it's fine.

norm: It's rude to leave clean-up activities to other camp goers.
situation: Tony has been camping for a couple of nights at a campsite in the mountains, and today he is going back home.
intention: Tony wants to deal with his campsite before he goes.
moral_action: Tony thoroughly cleans up the campsite and leaves it in the same state as he found it.
moral_consequence: The next campers at the site don't need to clean anything and are able to start enjoying themselves right away.
immoral_action: Tony puts out the fire he made but leaves a bunch of trash lying around.
immoral_consequence: The next campers at the site have to clean up Tony's mess, which spoils their fun.

norm: It's good to try to not be a horrible person.
situation: James arrives at work and hears one of his co-workers has recently lost her mother.
intention: James wants to say something to the grieving person.
moral_action: James approaches his co-worker and tells her that he is available if she ever wants to talk.
moral_consequence: The co-worker hugs him and thanks him for his generosity.
immoral_action: James approaches his co-worker and tells her a Yo Mama joke.
immoral_consequence: The co-worker breaks down into tears and berates James for his insensitivity.

norm: It's bad to aggravate an animal.
situation: Jeff's cat is growling and hissing at Jeff's friend Murray who has come to visit.
intention: Murray wants the cat to stop hissing.
moral_action: Murray gets down on the ground and puts a hand out for the cat to sniff.
moral_consequence: The cat slowly approaches to smell Murray and stops hissing as he does so.
immoral_action: Murray hisses back at the cat and pretends to try and swipe at him.
immoral_consequence: The cat's hissing stops but only because he is now lunging at Murray's face.

norm: You shouldn't push homeless people.
situation: Vernon is walking to work and a homeless person is in his way.
intention: Vernon wants to get to work.
moral_action: Vernon simply walks around the person, stepping onto the street to pass them.
moral_consequence: Vernon continues his walk to work uninterrupted.
immoral_action: Vernon pushes them over, so he can keep walking on the sidewalk to work.
immoral_consequence: People boo Vernon for pushing someone over like that, but he ignores it.

norm: It's good to listen when someone needs to talk.
situation: Paul's colleague begins talking about a personal matter that is bothering him.
intention: Paul needs to decide if he should redirect the conversation back to work topics, or if he should listen.
moral_action: Paul listens to his colleague and responds with moral support and hopes that things get better soon.
moral_consequence: Paul is glad that he gave his colleague some personal support and both of them feel happier at work for the rest of the day.
immoral_action: Paul ignores his colleagues comments about his personal life and continues working, only speaking about work related issues.
immoral_consequence: His colleague is let down and has the feeling that Paul is a cold person, while Paul feels guilty about not listening to a person in need.

norm: IT is not good to steal from anyone.
situation: Holly is having problems paying rent, and she notices her grandmother's diamond ring lying on the table.
intention: Holly needs money.
moral_action: Holly makes custom masks and puts them onto her online store.
moral_consequence: She gets enough money from her masks to pay for her rent.
immoral_action: Holly takes her mothers ring and sells it to a thrift shop for cash.
immoral_consequence: Holly loses her relationship with her grandmother when someone sends her grandmother a picture of Holly selling the ring.

norm: Asking a professional driver for a free ride is disrespectful.
situation: Bella is an instragram influencer who needs an Uber ride.
intention: Bella wants to make good business connections for her Instagram account.
moral_action: Bella pays for the fare plus tip and shares a pic with the driver on instagram.
moral_consequence: Bella is seen as generous and gains more popularity.
immoral_action: Bella asks to ride for free in exchange for exposure and is rude when the driver says no.
immoral_consequence: The driver shares the recorded conversation on social media and her influencer reputation is ruined.

norm: It's good to be generous to people.
situation: Jim gets an unexpected windfall from a smart stock investment.
intention: Jim wants to do something with his extra money.
moral_action: Jim sets up a charity to send underprivileged youth to college.
moral_consequence: Jim is given a humanitarian award by the city in which he lives.
immoral_action: Jim buys some cocaine.
immoral_consequence: Jim gets busted and sent to jail.

norm: It's bad to strike something in anger.
situation: Luigi was upset because he thought his brother Mario got the better Xmas gift.
intention: Luigi wants to point out he's upset.
moral_action: Luigi tries to explain that Mario got a much better present than he did.
moral_consequence: Luigi's parents are upset but as Luigi has broken no rules he is not punished.
immoral_action: Luigi tries to make a running punch on the punching bag, but he misses and hits the wall.
immoral_consequence: Luigi ends up paying for a broken wall out of his allowance.

norm: It's bad to break your marriage vows.
situation: When Harry married Minnie, he vowed to never lose his cool, but recently they've been arguing a lot.
intention: Harry wants Minnie to know how upset he's been.
moral_action: Harry tells Minnie things have been hard for him, and suggests that they seek marriage counseling.
moral_consequence: Harry and Minnie are able to work through their problems and return to their best selves.
immoral_action: Harry throws a lamp against the wall, narrowly missing Minnie's head.
immoral_consequence: Fearing for her safety, Minnie divorces Harry.

norm: It is greedy to horde all the cookies for yourself.
situation: Charlie and his friends often get treats after playtime at his day care.
intention: Charlie wants to enjoy some cookies.
moral_action: Charlie takes two cookies after playing and eats them slowly.
moral_consequence: Charlie enjoys the snack which makes the rest of the day easier for him.
immoral_action: Charlie stops playing a little early sneaks away and eats all of the cookies.
immoral_consequence: Charlie gets sick from eating too much and is not allowed to have cookies for a week as a punishement.

norm: You shouldn't let your partner comment on your eating habits.
situation: John's eating a snack of potato chips when his wife Sally tells him that he's being unhealthy by eating the chips.
intention: John wants to respond to Sally's statement.
moral_action: John tells Sally that he's eating a small portion, and she should mind her own business.
moral_consequence: Sally is taken aback but eventually realizes she has gained respect for John for his ability to tell her his real feelings.
immoral_action: John tells Sally that he's sorry for eating food that she has deemed unnaceptable and puts the chips away.
immoral_consequence: While initially happy, Sally begins to think less of John for being such a pushover.

norm: It's wrong to cheat off other people's work.
situation: Marilyn has to take an important exam in her biology class tomorrow, and she is not sure she will do well.
intention: Marilyn wants to get a passing grade on the exam.
moral_action: Marilyn stays up late studying for the exam and does her best work on it in class.
moral_consequence: Marilyn is sure that she will get a passing grade since she worked hard.
immoral_action: Marilyn looks over at her classmates paper and copies some of her answers.
immoral_consequence: The teacher sees Marilyn looking at her classmates work and doesn't allow her to finish the exam.

norm: It's inappropriate to judge people's character based on their appearance.
situation: Margret is interviewing a man in used clothes named Josh for a position in her company.
intention: Margret needs to decide if she wants to hire Josh.
moral_action: Margret asks John more questions about his work experience attempting to learn more about John.
moral_consequence: Margret learns new things about the industry through her conversation with John.
immoral_action: Margret dismisses Josh citing his attire does not fit her personal standards.
immoral_consequence: Margret receives hateful direct messages on Twitter after Josh calls her out online.

norm: You shouldn't date a convicted sex offender.
situation: Carrie is at home on her computer and discovers the man she has been dating is on the sex offender registry.
intention: Carrie wants to decide what to do about the relationship.
moral_action: Carrie immediately calls off the relationship after finding out the news.
moral_consequence: Carrie goes on to live a safe and healthy life by keeping a sex offender out of her life.
immoral_action: Carrie decides to continue seeing the man despite her recent discovery.
immoral_consequence: Carrie is eventually abused by the man she is dating when his dark side comes out.

norm: You shouldn't laugh at someone's food.
situation: Joe's girlfriend May has invited him over for dinner.
intention: Joe wants to react to the vegetarian menu.
moral_action: Joe thanks May for the meal.
moral_consequence: May feels her effort is appreciated.
immoral_action: Joe laughingly refers to the meal as rabbit food.
immoral_consequence: May gets offended and never invites him over again.

norm: It's a little gross to eat to excess.
situation: Tim took a girl he met on Tinder to an expensive Italian restaurant.
intention: Tim wants to eat pasta.
moral_action: Tim orders one plate of pasta and talks to the girl for the rest of the date.
moral_consequence: Tim's date is able to enjoy the date, and Tim doesn't eat too much food.
immoral_action: Tim orders four different plates of pasta and eats everything off of them.
immoral_consequence: Tim looks like a slob in front of his date, and she is less attracted to him.

norm: You should not let down people that depend on you.
situation: Jim promised his brother to come pick him up from soccer practice in his car.
intention: Jim wants to drive to a girl's house.
moral_action: Jim takes his brother home from soccer practice quickly before driving to the girl's house.
moral_consequence: Jim's brother is glad that he can rely on Jim to keep his promises.
immoral_action: Jim forgets about his brother and goes to the girl's house.
immoral_consequence: Jim's brother has to walk home from soccer practice which takes two hours.

norm: One should keep their belongings neatly organized.
situation: John is writing a research paper and needs to bring his research notes to school.
intention: John wants to pack his research notes.
moral_action: John spends 15 minutes putting paper clips on his note sections, then puts them all in his backpack.
moral_consequence: John has no trouble finding the proper sections and locating the papers that he needs.
immoral_action: John puts his research notes into a big pile and places them into his backpack.
immoral_consequence: When John pulls out his notes, he can't figure out where he placed anything.

norm: It's wrong to troll innocent people on the internet
situation: Fred is often bored and lonely, so he spends time online looking at his schoolmates social media accounts.
intention: Fred wants to connect with his schoolmates.
moral_action: Frank learns about his schoolmates likes and dislikes and uses that information to get to know them better.
moral_consequence: Frank is able to establish a circle of friends with common interests.
immoral_action: Frank decides to make anonymous hurtful comments on his schoolmates social media pages then discuss them at school the next day.
immoral_consequence: Frank is discovered to be the source of the rumors and is ostracized by his schoolmates.

norm: You shouldn't serve people food that is horrible.
situation: Martha cooks dinner for her children but it gets burned and is in terrible condition.
intention: Martha wants to do something with the food she cooked.
moral_action: Martha throws the burnt food away and orders delivery for her children to eat instead.
moral_consequence: Martha's children enjoy the special treat of eating delivery and thank Martha for getting it.
immoral_action: Martha serves the burnt food to her children even though it's not appetizing at all.
immoral_consequence: Martha's children don't enjoy the meal at all and complain that it's burnt.

norm: It's expected that you be supportive of your pregnant spouse.
situation: Leo's wife is pregnant and asks Leo to cook her a certain type of food.
intention: Leo wants to respond to his wife's request.
moral_action: Leo tells his wife that he will cook her the food.
moral_consequence: Leo's wife will be happy with Leo and consider him a good husband.
immoral_action: Leo tells his wife that she can cook the food herself.
immoral_consequence: Leo's wife will be angry with Leo and consider him a poor husband.

norm: You shouldn't spread diseases through sex.
situation: Charles and Jill are about to have sex, but Charles has an STD, though he is not yet aware.
intention: Charles wants to have sex with Jill.
moral_action: Charles puts on a condom before having sex with Jill.
moral_consequence: Charles needs medication for his STD, but does not pass the disease to Jill.
immoral_action: Charles has sex with Jill without using any kind of protection.
immoral_consequence: Charles passes his STD to Jill, and they both need medical treatment.

norm: It's bad to try to seek revenge on people.
situation: Jorge and Mark got into an argument when Jorge accidentally rear ended Mark.
intention: Mark wanted to make Jorge know how mad he was.
moral_action: Mark sends a badly worded letter to Jorge to vent his frustrations.
moral_consequence: No one is physically harmed this way.
immoral_action: Mark crashes his car into Jorge's on purpose to show him what its like.
immoral_consequence: Mark get charged with a crime and further damages his car.

norm: You should always release butterflies after you catch them.
situation: Nelly caught a butterfly while playing outside in the yard.
intention: Nelly wants to decide what to do with the butterfly.
moral_action: Nelly lets the butterfly go after looking at it.
moral_consequence: Nelly will be happy the butterfly gets to live freely.
immoral_action: Nelly keeps the butterfly in a sealed jar.
immoral_consequence: Nelly is sad because the butterfly dies in the jar.

norm: You shouldn't use someone else's social media account.
situation: Jenny is sitting next to her friend's computer and sees that their social media site account is signed in.
intention: Jenny wants to send someone a message on the social media site.
moral_action: Jenny signs into her own account to send something over on the social media site.
moral_consequence: Jenny's friend is glad Jenny didn't use their account on the social media site which would have been weird.
immoral_action: Jenny uses her friend's social media account to send a message to someone.
immoral_consequence: Jenny's friend is angry at Jenny for using their account which they see as a violation of privacy.

norm: It's good to obey company policies.
situation: Eric is having a really rough morning at his job and is really exasperated with it.
intention: Eric wants to head out early from work.
moral_action: Eric goes to his boss and asks if he can take some personal time and leave right away.
moral_consequence: Eric gets to go home early and relax after his stressful time at the office.
immoral_action: Eric slides out a side door after lunch without telling anyone he is leaving.
immoral_consequence: Eric is written up by his supervisor for not finishing his shift.

norm: You shouldn't invade your friend's personal space.
situation: Dave and John are hanging out together at John's house.
intention: Dave wants to find out if John has a secret crush he hasn't told anyone about.
moral_action: Dave simply asks John if there are any girls that John is crushing on.
moral_consequence: John is happy that Dave is taking an interest in his love life and tells him that there are none, but he’ll keep Dave updated.
immoral_action: Dave sneaks off into John's room and rummages through his things in an attempt to find John's diary.
immoral_consequence: John catches Dave and feels horrified that his privacy has been invaded and feels embarrassed about what Dave might have seen.

norm: It's good to look nice for your important events.
situation: Kelly has to attend her husbands work function right after having a huge argument with him.
intention: Kelly wants to teach her husband a lesson.
moral_action: Kelly makes her husband sleep on the couch after the event.
moral_consequence: Kelly calms down after spending time away from her husband.
immoral_action: Kelly decides to embarrass her husband by dressing sloppily for the event.
immoral_consequence: Kelly winds up feeling more embarrassed than her husband when people keep staring at her.

norm: It's rude to give a girlfriend grief over minor problems.
situation: Jason's girlfriend Kelly is very friendly and tends to strike up conversations with strangers wherever they go.
intention: Jason wants to address Kelly's friendliness.
moral_action: Jason asks Kelly if they could focus more in each other than other people when they are together.
moral_consequence: Jason convinces Kelly to adjust her behavior.
immoral_action: Jason accuses Kelly of being a flirt and insists that she stop being chatty.
immoral_consequence: Jason's words spark a furious argument with Kelly.

norm: You shouldn't mess up your house.
situation: James was feeling very stressed and short on time as a major deadline approached at work.
intention: James wants to cut out unnecessary wastes of time.
moral_action: James stops playing video games and starts ordering takeout for every meal.
moral_consequence: James' friends and family are impressed by how hard he's been working.
immoral_action: James stops cleaning his house and lets trash and dirty dishes pile up.
immoral_consequence: James' friends and family refuse to visit him until he cleans his house up.

norm: You're discouraged from bragging about your possessions.
situation: Ace just bought a new luxury car with his work bonus money and has some friends over.
intention: Ace wants to tell his friends about his new car.
moral_action: Ace mentions that he got a nice new car and asks his friends what cars they like.
moral_consequence: Ace's friends all share about their cars, starting a nice conversation.
immoral_action: Ace tells his friends about his car and goes over every detail of its luxury features.
immoral_consequence: Ace's friends get annoyed because they really don't care much about the car.

norm: It's wrong to make someone suffer.
situation: On an especially hot Summer day, Frank asks Rob if he could borrow his cast iron skillet for supper.
intention: Rob wants to get the cooking tools.
moral_action: Rob invites Frank inside the house while he searches for the skillet.
moral_consequence: Frank's opinion of Rob improves.
immoral_action: Rob forces Frank to wait outside in the heat while he searches for the skillet in his kitchen.
immoral_consequence: Frank gets sunburn and dehydrated from waiting outside in the hot sun.

norm: You shouldn't have sex with your partner's family members.
situation: Matt talks to his husband's cousin, Gregory, and finds him really interesting.
intention: Matt wants to spend more time with Gregory.
moral_action: Matt meets Gregory at the coffee shop to chat over breakfast.
moral_consequence: Matt and Gregory develop a friendship which brings Gregory and his cousin closer together.
immoral_action: Matt invites Gregory over while his husband is at work and the two end up in bed together.
immoral_consequence: Gregory feels incredibly guilty, and skips family gatherings for years to avoid running into his cousin.

norm: It's bad to practice polygamy.
situation: Dave who is already married is hanging out with Susan who suddenly asks him to marry her.
intention: Dave wants to respond to the marriage proposal.
moral_action: Dave tells Susan that he cannot marry her since that's both immoral and illegal.
moral_consequence: Dave's wife is happy to know her husband is a loyal and faithful man.
immoral_action: Dave tells Susan that he would be honored to be her loving husband the rest of her life.
immoral_consequence: Dave's wife is devastated to learn Dave has married someone else.

norm: It's wrong to emulate someone who is a murderer.
situation: Ron has been transfixed by reading about Jeffrey Dahmer so much, and is at his friend's house.
intention: Ron wants to do something about his obsession.
moral_action: Ron tells his friend about how he's been feeling, and what to do.
moral_consequence: Ron's friend convinces him to see a psychiatrist and get some help.
immoral_action: Ron pulls out a knife, and stabs his friend to death.
immoral_consequence: The cops come and Ron gets arrested on the spot.

norm: It's immoral to restrict another person's freedom.
situation: Brian is a jealous husband who is married to Sherry.
intention: Brian wants to go out with his friends.
moral_action: Brian tells Sherry that she should enjoy herself while he goes out with his friends.
moral_consequence: Sherry is happy that Brian is trying to work on his jealousy.
immoral_action: Brian tells Sherry that she cannot leave the house while he goes out with his friends.
immoral_consequence: Sherry feels trapped and decides to divorce Brian.

norm: It's noble to want to help other people.
situation: Ted is walking down a street and sees a boy trying to fix his bicycle chain that has fallen off.
intention: Ted wants to encourage the boy.
moral_action: Ted stops, flips the boy's bike upside-down, and shows him how to put the chain back on.
moral_consequence: The boy is very happy and has learned a valuable skill which he uses next time his bike chain falls off.
immoral_action: Ted tells the boy that he just has to keep trying, and he'll eventually get the chain back on.
immoral_consequence: The boy isn't successful and cries out of frustration, especially because Ted didn't help him.

norm: It's bad to spy on your significant other.
situation: Susan and Jake have been married for more than five years, and Jake comes back home late recently due to heavy workload.
intention: Susan wants to know what causes Jack to come home late.
moral_action: Susan patiently waits for Jack to come back home and asks if he has worked overtime and feels tired.
moral_consequence: Jack thanks Susan for her care and feels warm.
immoral_action: Susan pretends to be a customer and goes to the shop where Jake works, checking out if Jake is still working at late evening.
immoral_consequence: Jake sees Susan and feels offended and angry.

norm: Bailing on a friend's birthday trip is rude.
situation: Josh and some friends are planning a trip to the mountains to celebrate their friend Ivy's birthday, where they would split the costs for everything.
intention: Josh wants to save money on the cost of the trip.
moral_action: Josh researches travel deals.
moral_consequence: Josh finds a discount on hotels that saves the group a large chunk of money.
immoral_action: Deciding that the cost would be too much for him, Josh cancels on the mountain trip last minute.
immoral_consequence: Ivy is let down by Josh's absence, and the cost of the trip goes up for everyone else without Josh's contribution.

norm: It's good to try hard at your school work.
situation: Sam is assigned a book report that is due next Friday.
intention: Sam wants to finish the book report.
moral_action: Sam reads the book thoroughly and gives his best effort on writing the report.
moral_consequence: Sam receives an A on the report and easily passes the class.
immoral_action: Sam gives little effort on the book report and finishes it as quickly as possible without actually reading the whole book.
immoral_consequence: Sam receives a D on his book report and fails the class.

norm: It's unhealthy to eat too much candy
situation: Greg goes trick-or-treating and gets a large bag of candy.
intention: Greg wants to enjoy his candy.
moral_action: Greg eats two or three pieces of candy after lunch daily.
moral_consequence: Greg enjoys his candy for several months.
immoral_action: Greg eats half of the bag of candy in two hours time.
immoral_consequence: Greg can't sleep all night and feels sick.

norm: It is insensitive to have preference toward biological children.
situation: Tina and her partner have reached the stage where they are ready to settle down.
intention: Tina wants to raise children.
moral_action: Tina convinces herself that there are many children who need to be adopted into good homes.
moral_consequence: The kids are adopted into a better home with dedicated parents.
immoral_action: Tina considers some kids in foster care but prefers to give birth to her own.
immoral_consequence: The kids remain in foster care and live a harder life.

norm: It is nice to have family over to visit.
situation: Jacob has the evening off of work, and he feels somewhat lonely.
intention: Jacob wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Jacob invites his brother over to play video games.
moral_consequence: Jacob has a fun time bonding with his brother.
immoral_action: Jacob spends the evening reading his favorite book.
immoral_consequence: Jacob goes to bed feeling somewhat lonely after spending time alone.

norm: It's wrong to kidnap and torture a child.
situation: Jeremy is driving home when he sees a young child walking down the road by himself.
intention: Jeremy wants to pick the child up.
moral_action: Jeremy picks the child up and brings him to the local authorities to help get him home safe.
moral_consequence: Jeremy is late getting home but is glad to have helped a child in danger.
immoral_action: Jeremy picks the child up under the guise of giving him a ride, then rapes and slowly kills him.
immoral_consequence: Jeremy is discovered as a child killer and is sentenced to a life in prison.

norm: It is normal to go home when you are sick.
situation: Jacob has been sneezing and coughing all morning at work.
intention: Jacob wants to avoid losing pay for not working.
moral_action: Jacob asks his boss could he be excused with pay due to illness.
moral_consequence: Jacob's boss grants him an excused absence with pay.
immoral_action: Jacob stays at work all day while he is sick.
immoral_consequence: Jacob's boss is annoyed by his lack of consideration and makes note to demote him.

norm: It's good to mentor students.
situation: Anna had been working as a teacher for a while, and she wanted to be promoted soon.
intention: Anna wants to do something that will impress her boss.
moral_action: Anna starts mentoring students by spending time with them after school to impress the boss.
moral_consequence: Anna's students all do very well and benefit from the extra time with Anna.
immoral_action: Anna enrolls in classes, so she can further her education to impress the boss, so she must leave right after class each day.
immoral_consequence: Anna cannot spend time mentoring students after class and a few of her students really fall behind.

norm: It's wrong to get too drunk to fulfill your obligations.
situation: Halen is entertaining his boss' daughter Trisha for the night, and Trisha wants him to enter a drinking contest.
intention: Halen wants to make Trisha happen.
moral_action: Halen suggests that they return home for a glass of wine and a fun movie on Netflix.
moral_consequence: Halen and Trisha become good friends.
immoral_action: Halen drinks eight shots in a row to win the contest.
immoral_consequence: Halen has to be sent to the hospital for alcohol poisoning.

norm: It's good to give advance notice.
situation: Janelle is invited to a wedding for her niece.
intention: Janelle wants to go on a float trip with her friends the same day.
moral_action: Janelle promptly tells her niece that she can't make it to the wedding, sends a nice gift, and goes on the float trip.
moral_consequence: Janelle's niece is thankful for the gift.
immoral_action: Janelle goes on the float trip and sends her niece a text message saying that she won't be able to make the wedding that day.
immoral_consequence: Janelle's niece is offended that she hadn't told her earlier.

norm: It's good to let dogs outside for exercise.
situation: Kyle is busy cleaning his house and his dogs are distracting him.
intention: Kyle wants the ogs to not bother him while he's cleaning.
moral_action: Kyle lets the dogs into the yard to play while he cleans the house.
moral_consequence: The dogs have a blast in the yard while Kyle cleans the house.
immoral_action: Kyle locks the dogs in the game room while he cleans the rest of the house.
immoral_consequence: Kyle finds the game room trashed at the end of the day giving him more work than before.

norm: It is hurtful to not treat everyone kindly.
situation: Will just showed up to a party and doesn't recognize a guy there.
intention: Will has to decide whether to acknowledge the stranger.
moral_action: Will introduces himself to the guy he didn't recognize at the party.
moral_consequence: The guy is relieved that Will didn't ignore him and feels better.
immoral_action: Will walks right past the guy that he didn't recognize.
immoral_consequence: The guy's feelings are hurt, and he starts to feel like he doesn't belong.

norm: It's rude to make people beg.
situation: Mark is walking down a sidewalk and comes across a homeless man asking for money.
intention: Mark wants to give the homeless man money.
moral_action: Mark hands the man some money without making him do anything for it.
moral_consequence: The man feels grateful for Mark, and he didn't have to demean himself for the money.
immoral_action: Mark makes the homeless man get on his knees before he gives him money.
immoral_consequence: The man feels embarrassed and thinks that Mark is a jerk.

norm: You shouldn't be mean to your step-sibling.
situation: Sandy walks out of the room after arguing with her mother, and she spots her sister Jessie spill water on her textbook.
intention: Sandy wants to vent her frustrations.
moral_action: Sandy rants about her feelings in a group chatroom.
moral_consequence: Sandy gains comfort for being around people who support her.
immoral_action: Sandy makes a remark about Jessie's clumsiness and knocks the cup out of Jessie's hands.
immoral_consequence: Sandy gets in trouble with her mother after Jessie starts crying.

norm: You shouldn't bully your partner.
situation: Lucille and Edward are eating at a restaurant, and they ordered different things.
intention: Lucille wants to eat some of what Edward ordered.
moral_action: Lucille shares her food with Edward and asks him if she could try some of his meal.
moral_consequence: Lucille and Edward have a wonderful date and enjoyed their meal together.
immoral_action: Lucille makes fun of what Edward ordered, criticizing him for not ordering something more manly, and she should eat it instead.
immoral_consequence: Edward feels uncomfortable and breaks up with Lucille for her constant critiques.

norm: It is supportive to participate in an adoptathon for pets.
situation: Alexander has the weekend off of work, and he notices the adoption event in the park.
intention: Alexander wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Alexander decides to spend the entire weekend volunteering for the adoption event.
moral_consequence: Alexander comes home with a new dog.
immoral_action: Alexander spends  the weekend running around the park for exercise.
immoral_consequence: At the end of the weekend Alexander wishes he did something better with his time.

norm: You shouldn't drink if you have drinking problems.
situation: Greg is an alcoholic who wants to cut back, and he just arrived home after a very hectic day.
intention: Greg wants to do something to help him relax.
moral_action: Greg puts on a lighthearted comedy movie and relaxes in bed watching it.
moral_consequence: Greg is able to get into the movie and improve his mood in a healthy way.
immoral_action: Greg pours himself a drink and uses it to take the edge off.
immoral_consequence: Greg ends up becoming even more dependent on drinking alcohol.

norm: Asking someone what they like is considerate.
situation: Alex sits with a group of friends after an evening meeting of their book club.
intention: Alex wants to go out and get something to eat.
moral_action: Alex expresses to his friends that he is getting hungry and asks if anyone has any suggestions on where they could go to enjoy a meal together.
moral_consequence: Alex's friends discuss where they should go and decide as a group on a restaurant, everyone enjoys the evening.
immoral_action: Alex informs his friends that he is going out to get some tacos and tells them that they can come along if they want.
immoral_consequence: Alex's friends find it rude that he decided on a type of food, without asking anyone's opinion, and invited everyone else to join him for his choice of cuisine.

norm: You should not marry someone for the wrong reasons.
situation: Maria finds herself falling madly in love with a coworker although she currently has a rich boyfriend.
intention: Maria wants to find a future husband.
moral_action: Maria breaks up with her boyfriend and pursues a romantic relationship with her coworker.
moral_consequence: Maria finds true love with her coworker, and they are soon happily married.
immoral_action: Maria decides to marry her current boyfriend because of his wealth and material possessions.
immoral_consequence: Maria later regrets her decision and finds that money is not as important as true love.

norm: It's bad to date within your own family.
situation: Ted's friends are laughing at him for never having gone on a date before.
intention: Ted wants to ask a girl out.
moral_action: Ted asks the girl that lives next door to go to the movies with him.
moral_consequence: Ted and the girl have a good time and start dating.
immoral_action: Ted asks his sister to go with him to the movies.
immoral_consequence: All of his friends laugh and him and call him names.

norm: It is rude to disturb someone who is studying.
situation: Dave's brother Kyle is in his bedroom studying when Dave finds out a band he likes is coming to town.
intention: Dave wants to tell someone about his excitement for the upcoming concert.
moral_action: Dave calls up one of his friends on the phone and tells him all about his excitement for the show.
moral_consequence: Kyle continues to study uninterrupted in his room and does very well in his classes.
immoral_action: Dave runs into Kyle's room and tells him all about the concert and how he can't wait to go.
immoral_consequence: Kyle is annoyed that Dave has broken his concentration and is wasting his time for something so trivial.

norm: It is wrong to steal the property of others.
situation: Donald s running for public office and schedules a series of public rallies.
intention: Donald wants to attract the attention of voters.
moral_action: Donald claims to be a big fan of the entertainer and invites him to perform at a rally.
moral_consequence: The entertainer refuses, but the voters notice and approve of Donald's taste in music.
immoral_action: Donald uses the music of a popular entertainer at the rallies without the entertainer's permission.
immoral_consequence: Voters form an unfavorable impression of Donald when the entertainer sues him for copyright infringement.

norm: It's bad to take medication that you don't need.
situation: Micheal is struggling with his essay when he notices his younger brother's bottle of adderall beside him.
intention: Micheal wants to focus on his schoolwork.
moral_action: Micheal exercises for outside for thirty minutes.
moral_consequence: Exercising gives Micheal enough energy to power through is essay.
immoral_action: Micheal takes a pill of his brother's Adderall.
immoral_consequence: Micheal is grounded when his mother discovers his actions.

norm: You shouldn't demand apologies from people.
situation: Ron is walking into the local grocery store and accidentally bumps into another man as he approaches the door.
intention: Ron wants to say something to the man he bumped into.
moral_action: Ron smiles and gives a brief apology to the man for bumping into him.
moral_consequence: The man accepts Ron's apology and tells him to have a nice day.
immoral_action: Ron gets angry and loudly shouts at the man, demanding an apology.
immoral_consequence: The other man yells back at Ron and tells him to watch where he's going.

norm: It's good to tip people who give you good service
situation: Hilary eats a nice dinner at a fancy restaurant and is ready for her waiter to bring out the check.
intention: Hilary wants to pay for her meal.
moral_action: Hilary pays for the meal and leaves a big tip for the waiter.
moral_consequence: The waiter thanks Hilary for leaving such a generous tip.
immoral_action: Hilary leaves just enough money to pay for the meal without tipping.
immoral_consequence: The waiter calls Hilary a cheapskate after she leaves the restaurant.

norm: It's good to go on vacation with your friends.
situation: Peter has some time off of work, and feels he wants to get out of his house a bit.
intention: Peter wants to go away on vacation.
moral_action: Peter asks his buddies to come along with him to the beach, and they do.
moral_consequence: Peter and his friends get closer, and have a lot of fun together.
immoral_action: Peter decides to go away on vacation alone, going to the beach.
immoral_consequence: Peter enjoys it for a few hours, but then gets bored and lonely.

norm: It's bad for parents not to watch over their babies.
situation: Christina is playing with her baby on her bed when the doorbell rings.
intention: Christina wants to answer the door.
moral_action: Christina picks up the baby and answers the door with her baby in her arms.
moral_consequence: Christina is able to supervise her baby while tending to other things.
immoral_action: Christina runs out of the room to answer the door, leaving her baby on the bed.
immoral_consequence: Christina's baby falls off of the bed and bruises her face.

norm: It's wrong to laugh at less intelligent people.
situation: Al is in class listening to the history lesson and his classmate Gina is called on to answer a question, and she doesn't know it.
intention: Al wants to react to Gina's inability to respond.
moral_action: Al see's Gina struggling, so he chimes in to help her understand.
moral_consequence: Gina feels good to have a classmate help her out, and she learned something new.
immoral_action: Al thinks it's funny that Gina didn't know how to answer such an easy question, so he bursts out into laughter.
immoral_consequence: Gina feels embarrassed and leaves class feeling depressed.

norm: It's irresponsible to renege on one's responsibilities.
situation: John promised to pick the kids up from school.
intention: John wants to catch the football game at his buddy's house.
moral_action: John picks up his kids and drops them off at home and leaves to his friend's house.
moral_consequence: John's wife expresses her love and gratitude which makes John feel very good about himself, and is able to watch the game in a great mood with no outside worries.
immoral_action: John decides to go straight to his friend's house for the game, making up an excuse about being caught up at work.
immoral_consequence: His wife discovers he was lying after she picks the kids up herself and this puts a temporary strain in their marriage.

norm: You shouldn't make out with your friend's crush.
situation: Sara's best friend Julie has a crush on one of their classmates, but is too shy to talk to him.
intention: Sara wants to speak to the classmate about Julie.
moral_action: Sara stops the classmate in the parking lot to tell him about Julie's crush, but he tries to kiss her instead, where Sara push him away.
moral_consequence: Julie finds out from Sara about the classmate's inappropriate behavior, and thanks her for stopping him and being honest.
immoral_action: Sara meets the classmate at the park to talk to him about Julie, but she begins to like him and soon is kissing him on the bench.
immoral_consequence: Julie hears rumors that Sara and the classmate were seen in an embrace at the park, so she stops being friends with Sara.

norm: It's wrong to bully someone just because they bullied you.
situation: John plays baseball at school and the team captain has been really mean to him lately when the coach is not around.
intention: John wants the team captain to learn that he cannot push John around.
moral_action: John speaks to the coach about his problems with the team captain to ask the coach to intervene.
moral_consequence: The team captain is addressed by the coach and starts working on improving his behavior and the team.
immoral_action: John starts making fun of the team captain and getting other teammates to do the same.
immoral_consequence: The team captain grows very upset and does a bad job managing the team.

norm: You shouldn't get into trouble.
situation: Katy is a huge fan of a rock group that will be coming to town for a show over the next weekend.
intention: Katy wants to meet the guitarist for the band and get his autograph.
moral_action: Katy contacts the band's media representative and finds out they will be signing autographs and meeting fans before the concert.
moral_consequence: Katie gets to talk to the entire band and the guitarist signs a picture just for her.
immoral_action: Katy stakes out the hotel where the band is playing and breaks into the guitarist's room while he's out, to wait for him.
immoral_consequence: Katy never gets to meet him, and he never signs anything for her because he calls the police to complain about her behavior.

norm: You shouldn't treat cashiers like they are trash.
situation: Sandy is not feeling well, but she has to stop by the pharmacy after going to the doctor.
intention: Sandy wants to pick up her prescription.
moral_action: Sandy picks up her prescription and hands the cashier the money.
moral_consequence: The cashier tells Sandy thank you and that she hopes she feels better.
immoral_action: Sandy tells the cashier to go get her prescription immediately and then throws her wadded up money at the cashier.
immoral_consequence: The cashier is offended because of Sandy's very rude behavior.

norm: Not tipping a delivery person is rude.
situation: Steve is home alone.
intention: Steve wants to order some food.
moral_action: Steve thanks the driver and tips him generously.
moral_consequence: The driver remembers Steve the next time and prioritizes his order.
immoral_action: Steve gets his food and slams the door on the delivery driver without tipping.
immoral_consequence: The driver makes a note in his computer and Steve is given horrible service from then on.

norm: It's wrong to harm others with a car.
situation: Jeff, who suspects that his girlfriend is cheating on him, follows her and sees her being affectionate with another man.
intention: Jeff wants to get even.
moral_action: Jeff finds some condoms that his girlfriend keeps and soaks them in hot sauce for the other man.
moral_consequence: Both the girlfriend and the other man suffer without getting seriously injured.
immoral_action: Jeff waits until they are in an open area at night, then takes his car and runs them both down, injuring them.
immoral_consequence: Both his girlfriend and the other man are seriously wounded and spend lots of money on recovery.

norm: It's wrong to cyber-stalk an ex-partner.
situation: Rhonda finds her ex-boyfriends Facebook left open and logged into her computer.
intention: Rhonda wants to browse the web right now on the only computer in the room.
moral_action: Rhonda exits out of Facebook to browse Google alone.
moral_consequence: Rhonda's ex-boyfriend thanks Rhonda for exiting out of his Facebook account.
immoral_action: Rhonda goes onto Facebook and browses her ex-boyfriends activities.
immoral_consequence: Rhonda's ex-boyfriend notices someone is browsing his account, and he reprimands Rhonda.

norm: It is expected to stick up for your family.
situation: Ruth's mom is being berated in a supermarket by another customer for using an electric scooter, as her disability is invisible.
intention: Ruth wants to stop hearing the woman yelling.
moral_action: Ruth gets between the customer and her mother, telling the woman to speak with management if she has a problem.
moral_consequence: Ruth and her mother can finish shopping and go home without further issues.
immoral_action: Ruth walks away from the confrontation, checking out her phone to distract herself.
immoral_consequence: Ruth's mother feels threatened by the other woman and walks back to her car, injuring herself in the process.

norm: It's good to stand up for yourself at work.
situation: Michelle has been sexually harassed by one of her co-workers and it is affecting her work performance.
intention: Michelle needs to talk to her boss.
moral_action: Michelle reports her co-worker to her boss, citing his actions as a cause of her performance issues.
moral_consequence: Michelle's co-worker is fired and charges are brought against him for harassment.
immoral_action: Michelle apologizes for her performance but does not tell her boss about her co-worker's behavior.
immoral_consequence: Michelle's co-worker continues to harass her as well as harassing other women in the office,.

norm: It's not okay to violate someone's personal privacy.
situation: Cameron has a crush on his sister's friend and just noticed that his sister left her laptop open when she left the house.
intention: Cameron wants to know what his sister's friend thinks about him.
moral_action: Cameron waits until his sister gets back and tells her he likes her friend and asks what she thinks about him.
moral_consequence: Cameron's sister tells him tells him that her friend likes him as a friend but not really romantically.
immoral_action: Cameron goes on his sister's computer while she's away and reads her chat logs with her friend.
immoral_consequence: Cameron's sister finds the chat logs open when she gets back and angrily confronts her brother.

norm: You shouldn't try to take advantage of people.
situation: Sean is at a trading event for a popular card game and sees a person who has just started playing the game.
intention: Sean wants to trade cards with the new player.
moral_action: Sean looks at what the person has, makes some suggestions, and offers to trade some of his cards that would help the new player.
moral_consequence: The new person accepts the trade and builds a powerful deck that helps him succeed in future matches.
immoral_action: Sean picks out the person's best cards, says that they're not very good, and offers him a trade for some less-valuable cards.
immoral_consequence: The new person accepts the trade, finds out that he gave up great cards, and becomes bitter towards other players.

norm: You shouldn't talk while others are enjoying a movie.
situation: Britney is watching a movie with her friends in a movie theater.
intention: Britney wants her friends to know how she feels about what is happening in the movie.
moral_action: Britney communicates with her friends by making silent faces, i.e. sad, amused etc. during the movie.
moral_consequence: The people seated near Britney can enjoy the movie in peace.
immoral_action: Britney talks to her friends during the movie to let them know how she feels about it.
immoral_consequence: People seating near Britney can't hear the movie because of her incessant talking.

norm: You should not be unwilling to go to Jury Duty.
situation: Lyle receives a piece of mail and upon opening it sees it's a jury summons for next week.
intention: Kyle wants to decide what to do with the letter.
moral_action: Kyle takes the jury summons and puts it on his office desk at home to take with him when he reports for jury duty.
moral_consequence: Kyle serves his citizen duty as a member of the jury and the justice system continues to function the way it was intended.
immoral_action: Kyle takes the jury summons and tosses it in the garbage since he has no intention of responding to it.
immoral_consequence: Kyle is found to have been neglecting his duties as a citizen and is later fined by the court.

norm: Dating a friend's ex is frowned upon.
situation: Jenna's friend Samantha just broke up with the guy she'd been dating for three years.
intention: Jenna wants to find a new boyfriend.
moral_action: Jenna creates an account on OkCupid to find a boyfriend who doesn't know any of her friends.
moral_consequence: Jenna eventually hits it off with someone and goes on a double date with Samantha and her new boyfriend.
immoral_action: Jenna immediately asks Samantha's ex out on a dinner date.
immoral_consequence: Samantha confronts Jenna crying and says she can't be friends anymore.

norm: You should be happy if your friend gets engaged.
situation: Tim's best friend Dave announces that he is now engaged to his girlfriend.
intention: Tim wants to congratulate Dave.
moral_action: Tim is honestly happy for Dave and is excited for his friend's wedding.
moral_consequence: Tim has lots of fun with Dave's announcement and asks him 100 questions.
immoral_action: Tim congratulates Dave but on the inside he's worried that Dave will spend less time with him.
immoral_consequence: Tim is upset the entire time and doesn't have any fun.

norm: It's good to give encouragement to someone close to you.
situation: Evan asked Jerry for some words of advice about his upcoming project.
intention: Jerry wants to give his honest opinion to Evan.
moral_action: Jerry sits down and gives Evan constructive critisism.
moral_consequence: Evan gets the encouragement that he needs.
immoral_action: Jerry yells at Evan to get his own ideas and tells him he sucks.
immoral_consequence: Evan is hurt by the way the Jerry acted.

norm: It's embarrassing to storm out of somewhere.
situation: Alexandra is at a lecture and the speaker is saying things that she does not agree with and make her uncomfortable.
intention: Alexandra wants to get away from the lecture hall.
moral_action: Alexandra slips out as quietly as possible during a pause in the lecture.
moral_consequence: The others in the audience are able to continue to listen to the lecture.
immoral_action: Alexandra abruptly stands up, loudly exits the room and lets the door slam behind her.
immoral_consequence: The others in the lecture hall are disrupted and think Alexandra is rude.

norm: It's good to help family members.
situation: Mike's brother, Jim, calls Mike and asks him if he can lend him some money for his monthly rent payment that is due soon.
intention: Mike wants to respond to Jim's request.
moral_action: Mike agrees to lend some money to Jim and tells him not to worry about repaying him until he is able to.
moral_consequence: Jim feels grateful toward Mike and has a positive mood for the rest of the day.
immoral_action: Mike chastises Jim for not being financially responsible and angrily hangs up the phone.
immoral_consequence: Jim feels betrayed and decides to never speak to Mike again.

norm: It's frowned upon to tell people what to do.
situation: Wyatt is relaxing at home when his wife Jody tells him she's going out shopping.
intention: Wyatt wants to react to Jody's statement.
moral_action: Wyatt tells Jody to drive safely and to have a great time out and about.
moral_consequence: Jody is delighted that Wyatt has wished her well and is concerned about her safety.
immoral_action: Wyatt tells Jody she can't go because he doesn't want her spending their money and forbids her from leaving.
immoral_consequence: Jody is terrified that Wyatt is acting abusive and is stressed that she's being confined.

norm: You should talk to your friends if you're struggling.
situation: Irma just broke up with her boyfriend and is very upset.
intention: Irma wants to make herself feel better.
moral_action: Irma confides in her friends about her relationship problems and asks them for advice.
moral_consequence: Irma receives some very good advice and is able to look at her situation from a different perspective.
immoral_action: Irma ignores all of her friends and isolates herself, so she can work through her feelings on her own.
immoral_consequence: It takes Irma a long time to get over the breakup.

norm: You shouldn't accept trades from customers for items.
situation: Jimmy is talking to a customer who wants to buy a microwave but doesn't have enough money.
intention: Jimmy wants to clsoe the sale.
moral_action: Jimmy offers the customers a payment plan that works for them, and they agree to buy the microwave.
moral_consequence: Jimmy is able to meet his sales goal for the month and receives a bonus.
immoral_action: Jimmy offers to let the customer have the microwave if they give him a video game he has been wanting.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy gets reprimanded once his boss finds out he's been trading products for things.

norm: It's bad to expect others to pay for your vacations.
situation: Isaac was invited by his friend Amy to go on a trip to Berlin.
intention: Isaac wants to attend the trip.
moral_action: Isaac accepts Amy's invitation and takes his savings with him to help pay for his way and some gifts.
moral_consequence: Amy and Isaac are both able to afford to do everything they wanted.
immoral_action: Isaac accepts Amy's invitation but doesn't take any funds with him.
immoral_consequence: Amy is left to cover the cost of everything and it causes tension between her and Isaac.

norm: You shouldn't drive your car on the sidewalk.
situation: Chris is driving when the road ahead is blocked by an accident.
intention: Chris wants to continue to his destination.
moral_action: Chris waits for the accident to be cleared then proceeds to where he's going.
moral_consequence: Chris gets to his destination in a safe and legal way and without incident.
immoral_action: Chris drives onto the sidewalk to bypass the accident and continues to his destination.
immoral_consequence: A traffic camera catches Chris driving on the sidewalk, and he is later issued a fine.

norm: It's bad to drink on the job.
situation: Robert previously suffered from alcoholism and works as a security guard in a mall.
intention: Robert wants to consider getting a drink.
moral_action: Robert resists the temptation of getting an alcoholic drink and simplies goes for a non-alcoholic drink.
moral_consequence: Robert manages to do his job well as a security guard and receives some recognition for it.
immoral_action: Robert gets his favorite alcoholic beverage and drinks its during his shift.
immoral_consequence: Robert becomes too drunk to perform his duties and gets fired.

norm: It's rude to hack people.
situation: Dan works for an anti-extremism organization that is tracking an extremist site.
intention: Dan wants to shut down the site.
moral_action: Dan decides to report the extremist site to the domain registrar and the site gets taken down.
moral_consequence: Dan gets a raise for his work and feels proud.
immoral_action: Dan decides to take down the site through illegal denial of service attacks.
immoral_consequence: Dan get charged with criminal hacking and goes to jail and feels bad.

norm: It's bad to owe money.
situation: Katie had her work hours reduced and is now struggling with money.
intention: Katie wants to find money to pay for expenses.
moral_action: Katie gets part time work that supplements her income to pay for expenses.
moral_consequence: Katie pays her expenses with the extra income.
immoral_action: Katie gets a pay day loan to pay her expenses.
immoral_consequence: Katie has to pay a high amount of interest on the loan.

norm: You shouldn't intentionally annoy a friend.
situation: Meo is a bit bored while hanging out with Mea in the house.
intention: Meo wants to get out some energy.
moral_action: Meo turns on music and starts dancing.
moral_consequence: He gets out energy and Mea dances with him.
immoral_action: Meo starts kicking around a foam soccer ball.
immoral_consequence: The ball hits Mea a couple of times, and she leaves, leaving Meo depressed.

norm: It's wrong to sexually harass people.
situation: John sees his co-worker Jill standing at the water cooler.
intention: John wants to give Jill a compliment.
moral_action: John walks over to Jill and tells her he likes the color of her shirt.
moral_consequence: Jill is flattered and compliments John on his clothing as well.
immoral_action: John walks over to Jill and says the shirt she is wearing make her breasts look good.
immoral_consequence: Jill is offended and files a complaint against John with human resources.

norm: It's rude to slam doors.
situation: Timmy's mom works odd hours and is often sleeping when he leaves for school.
intention: Timmy wants to make sure the front door is secured when he leaves for school.
moral_action: Timmy gently closes the door before locking it.
moral_consequence: Timmy's mother is able to get a restful night's sleep and has enough energy to get through her work day.
immoral_action: Timmy slams the door shut on his way out of the house in the morning.
immoral_consequence: Timmy's mom is awakened by the loud noise and arrives to work grouchy and unrested.

norm: It's rude to hold people up because you are reading.
situation: Jim is reading a book when he is called to go out for dinner by his mom.
intention: Jim wants to respond to his mom.
moral_action: Jim tells his mom he's ready to go and puts his book down.
moral_consequence: Jim's mom will get to eat dinner on time.
immoral_action: Jim says he needs to finish reading to his mom.
immoral_consequence: Jim's mom will be annoyed with him for delaying dinner.

norm: You should be nice to new people you meet.
situation: Joe meets a new person for the the first time who introduces himself to Joe.
intention: Joe wants to say something to the person.
moral_action: Joe compliments the person he just met and tells them to let Joe know if they ever need help with anything.
moral_consequence: The person Joe met is happy to have met such a nice and helpful person as Joe.
immoral_action: Joe tells the person that he just met that they're kind of ugly and don't look to bright either.
immoral_consequence: The person Joe met is really offended and never likes Joe after that.

norm: You shouldn't ruin your partner's important events.
situation: Jack's fiancee is graduating form university and a ceremony is being held the honor the graduates.
intention: Jack wants to attend his fiancee's graduation.
moral_action: Jack goes to his fiancee's graduation and stays on his best behavior.
moral_consequence: Jack's fiancee feels the graduation is a proud moment she will always remember fondly.
immoral_action: Jack gets tremendously drunk at the graduation, yelling at people and starting a fight.
immoral_consequence: Jack's fiancee feels her graduation was an embarrassment and a black mark on her reputation.

norm: It's good to prevent your friend from driving drunk.
situation: Tom and Tim are hanging out at Tom's apartment when a drunken Tim wants to drive home.
intention: Tom wants to avoid a conflict with Tim.
moral_action: Tom hides the keys and Tim gives up looking, deciding to stay the night.
moral_consequence: Tim feels sick the next morning but thanks Tom for keeping him safe.
immoral_action: "Tom gives and and gives Tim the keys saying ""please just be careful""."
immoral_consequence: Tim crashes his car resulting in the death of the other driver leave Tom and Tim feeling guilty for life.

norm: You shouldn't be with a partner that puts you down.
situation: Ash is unhappy in a relationship with a partner who has a really short fuse.
intention: Ash wants to tell her partner how she feels.
moral_action: Ash talks with her partner and proceeds to break up with him right then and there.
moral_consequence: Ash feels liberated from the bad relationship.
immoral_action: Ash talks with her partner who gets angry in response and stays with him afterward.
immoral_consequence: Ash continues to be unhappy in her relationship.

norm: It's wrong for schools not to teach kid right.
situation: Emery is teaching her students how to convert fractions into decimals, but she is having a hard time because she has never understood this well.
intention: Emery wants to finish the lesson today.
moral_action: Emery meets with another teacher during lunch, learns how to do the conversion, and is able to teach the students correctly.
moral_consequence: The students understand how to do the math and get good grades on their homework.
immoral_action: Emery comes up with a way of converting the fractions that she thinks might be right and explains it to the class for their daily lesson.
immoral_consequence: The students believe this is the right way to do the math and get all of the answers on their homework wrong.

norm: It's wrong to say bad things about gay people.
situation: Phil's best friend Chuck comes out of the closet to him.

norm: You shouldn't be rude and petty to people.
situation: Dan is getting groceries at the store.

moral_consequence: Dan is thanked for his resourceful thinking by other people waiting in line.
immoral_action: Dan refuses to let a person with only a couple of items go in front of him in line.
immoral_consequence: Dan is given dirty looks by all the people around him.

norm: You shouldn't poke around in your family's private life.
situation: Joe hears that his little sister is dating a boy in his class, and he wants to find out more about it.

moral_action: Joe has a frank conversation with his sister to ensure she is well informed and able to make good decisions.
moral_consequence: Joe's sister is grateful for his guidance.

immoral_consequence: Joe's sis is embarrassed by her brothers behavior.

norm: It's wrong to abandon a friend that needs help.
situation: Sam is hanging out with his friend Amanda and notices she has new cut scars on her arms.

norm: It's wrong to break one's word.
situation: Karen promised his son that she would take him to a Cubs game if he did his homework.

moral_action: Karen surprises her son with multiple tickets to a Cubs game so that he can bring his friends.
moral_consequence: Karen's son trusts that his mom will never break a promise that she makes.
immoral_action: Karen brings her son to a minor league baseball game.
immoral_consequence: Karen's son is disappointed and doesn't trust her mom anymore.

norm: You should keep your kids safe during Halloween.
situation: Carry is driving her children around town on Halloween night to trick or treat.
intention: Carry wants to take her children trick or treating.
moral_action: Carry walks with her kids to and from houses trick or treating on Halloween night.
moral_consequence: Carry's kids stay safe and have a good time with their mom.
immoral_action: Carry takes her kids trick or treating but stays in the car and doesn't pay attention to where her kids are going.
immoral_consequence: Carry's kids get lost in an unknown neighborhood, and they feel scared.

norm: It's kind to adopt a stray animal.
situation: Tom has a stray cat the is always hanging out in his backyard.

moral_action: Tom adopts the stray cat and takes it into his home.
moral_consequence: The stray get a nice home life and Tom gets a new pet he loves.

immoral_consequence: The stray cat is left homeless and alone.

norm: It's bad to take liberties with someone else's money.
situation: Sally was shopping for her mother-in-law to stock up on household supplies.

moral_consequence: Sally's mother-in-law has enough money to pay her other bills and pay Sally later for the extra items.
immoral_action: Sally fills the cart with extra items that are in addition to the things her mother-in-law authorized her to buy with her credit card.
immoral_consequence: Sally's mother-in-law does not have enough money left to pay her other bills.

norm: It's wrong to contact your ex's partner.
situation: Valerie is dating Will and is considering moving in with him.

moral_consequence: Valerie will get a fair perspective because Will's roommate has no grudge against Will.
immoral_action: Valerie messages Will's ex-girlfriend to ask how he is as a roommate.

norm: It's wrong to not explain yourself.
situation: Bill is very moody at work and short with everyone including his boss.

moral_action: Bill meets with the boos before work explaining that he suddenly lost a pet last night.

immoral_action: Bill shouts and everyone to leave alone and says that things are none of their business.
immoral_consequence: Bill is written up by his boss for misconduct towards other employees.

norm: You shouldn't be rude to your significant others.
situation: Jack is taking Sally out on a date for their anniversary.

norm: It's good to ask customers what they want.
situation: Tonya is working as a waitress at a restaurant and is assigned a table to serve.

moral_action: Tonya goes through he normal routine of asking the customers if they want appetizers or are ready to order.

immoral_action: Tonya walks up to the table with her pad and pen and stands next to the customer's silently in a pose showing she is ready to write.
immoral_consequence: The customers find it rude that Tonya didn't address them and go on to leave her no tip.

norm: You shouldn't get pregnant if you're too young.
situation: Meg and Tom are high school sweethearts and plan to get married after college.

norm: It's good to care about your community.
situation: Galvin has time off after returning from his business trip, and his hometown has been damaged by floods.

norm: It's nice to offer advice when someone is confused.

norm: It's rude to take advantage of people.
situation: Maria met Phil and found out that he had a lot of money.

norm: It's not okay to do things to disturb your neighbors.

norm: It's bad to copy off of someone else's schoolwork.

norm: You shouldn't lie to someone about hitting their car.

norm: It's wrong to text during class.

norm: It's good to care about the planet.

norm: You shouldn't beat up your friends.

norm: It's bad to not enjoy a vacation.
situation: Carol goes on a beach vacation with her family.

norm: It is rude to wipe your nose on your clothes.

norm: It's wrong to disturb your roommates.

norm: It's bad to be unemployed.
