moral_action: Paul wrestles the knife away and pins the woman to the ground, then shouts for help.
moral_consequence: The bystanders call for help and the police arrest the woman.
immoral_action: Paul deflects the knife and punches the woman in the face repeatedly.
immoral_consequence: Some bystanders see Paul assaulting the woman misinterpret what is happening.

norm: It's good to keep your family in the know.
situation: Harold is getting tired of living with his parents, even though his parents like having him there, and his friend offers to let him move in with them.
intention: Harold wants to accept his friend's offer.
moral_action: Harold explains to his parents that he wants to start living on his own before making his decision.
moral_consequence: Harold's parents are sad at first, but they understand and support his decision.
immoral_action: Harold moves out without saying anything to his parents and moves in with his friend.
immoral_consequence: Harold's parents are shocked to find him gone and are furious with him when they find out.

norm: It is rude to laugh at a stuttering kid.
situation: Ms. Jane is teaching  a class of middle school students about public speaking.
intention: Ms. Jane wants to give the students feedback.
moral_action: Ms. Jane listens to a child that is stuttering through his presentation and makes sure to compliment him on his structure and topic choices.
moral_consequence: The student feels empowered by the feedback Ms. Jane gives him and is less afraid of presenting in the future.
immoral_action: Ms. Jane listens to the speech a child with a stutter is giving, then criticizes him for his speech being poor and difficult to understand.
immoral_consequence: The child is embarrassed and his parents report Ms. Jane's bullying to the school board, and she is put on unpaid leave while the issue resolves.

norm: It's rude to wipe your boogers on things.
situation: Tim is feeling congested during math class but doesn't have any tissues handy.
intention: Tim wants to clear out his nasal passages.
moral_action: Tim excuses himself to the bathroom where he uses a tissue to blow his nose.
moral_consequence: Tim feels relieved and can breathe more easily.
immoral_action: Tim picks his nose and wipes his snot and boogers on the desk.
immoral_consequence: Tim feels embarrassed when other students see him and make fun of him for picking his nose.

norm: You shouldn't shoplift from department stores.
situation: Jonny is shopping at a local department store and sees a pair of shoes he really wants but can't afford.
intention: Jonny needs to get the shoes.
moral_action: Jonny leaves the store and gets to work saving up for the shoes, and later returns and buys them.
moral_consequence: Jonny really enjoys showing off his new shoes which are the product of all his hard work.
immoral_action: Jonny switches the shoe's he's wearing out for the ones he wants, and then walks out of the store.
immoral_consequence: Jonny is identified on camera stealing the shoes and is later arrested.

norm: It's bad to think you're better than other people.
situation: Sandra loves singing and takes part in a singing contest.
intention: Sandra wants to win the singing contest.
moral_action: Sandra took a singing course before the contest to improve her singing skills.
moral_consequence: Sandra is applauded by the judges and the audience for her excellent performance and wins the contest.
immoral_action: Sandra does not practice her song hard enough before the contest because she thinks that nobody can beat her sweet voice.
immoral_consequence: Sandra does not win the contest because the judges think her singing skills are not good enough.

norm: It's bad to want a job where you hurt others.
situation: Bill is looking through a careers page online as he's in need of a new job.
intention: Bill wants to decide which job to apply to.
moral_action: Bill decides to apply for a job in a government office where he would process paperwork.
moral_consequence: Bill finds that the job requires him to do little for a lot of money, and he spends his days happy at work.
immoral_action: Bill decides to apply for the job of a bodyguard for a rich man and his family.
immoral_consequence: Bill finds that the job requires him to kill those who attempt to harm his clients and it eventually wears on his conscience.

norm: It is kind to say goodbye when you are leaving.
situation: Joe is ready to leave the Christmas party.
intention: Joe wants to make sure that everyone knows he is leaving.
moral_action: Joe excuses himself and thanks the host for having him.
moral_consequence: Joe leaves the party still respected by his peers.
immoral_action: Joe knocks over the Christmas tree on the way out the door.
immoral_consequence: Everyone at the party is startled and glares angrily at Joe.

norm: It's wrong to laugh at threats about animals.
situation: Paul lets his dog defecate on his neighbor's lawn, and now his neighbor threatens that if it happens again, he'll shoot the dog.
intention: Paul wants to respond to his neighbor's threat.
moral_action: Paul tells his neighbor that he'll keep his dog on his own property from now on.
moral_consequence: Paul's dog defecates in Paul's yard and then chases and barks at some birds.
immoral_action: Paul laughs at his neighbor and tells him that he doesn't have the guts to do anything about Paul's dog.
immoral_consequence: Paul's dog defecates on the neighbor's lawn the next day and is shot by the neighbor.

norm: You should be supportive of people with mental illnesses.
situation: Nick is hanging out with his best friend.
intention: Nick wants to talk with his friend.
moral_action: Nick hears the pain in his friend's voice and offers to take him to a therapist.
moral_consequence: Nick is praised by the therapist for getting his friend the help he needs.
immoral_action: Nick doesn't pick up on his friend's clues about their depression during their conversation.
immoral_consequence: Nick loses his friend to suicide.

norm: You shouldn't lie about your age.
situation: Becky just turned 18 and when an older guy asked her out to a 21 and over club.
intention: Becky wants to go to a club.
moral_action: Becky gives her date an alternate venue that she can legally attend.
moral_consequence: Becky has a great time on her date and a romance begins to bloom.
immoral_action: Becky gets a fake id and goes to the club with her date.
immoral_consequence: Becky's fake id fails to fool the bouncers, and she is embarrassed when she is denied entrance.

norm: It's bad to murder people for money.
situation: Matt, who used to be in the armed special forces, receives an email requesting a contract killing.
intention: Matt wants to reply to the offer.
moral_action: Matt declines the offer and tells the man that he's not for sale.
moral_consequence: Matt lives a peaceful life and receives no more offers for killings.
immoral_action: Matt accepts the offer and goes to meet with his client.
immoral_consequence: The client turns out to be a police officer who arrests Matt and charges him.

norm: It's good to accept your children.
situation: June has been questioning her sexual identity and after determining she is gay, she tells her mother, Mary.
intention: Mary wants to let June know how she feels.
moral_action: Mary hugs June and tells her that she loves her no matter what.
moral_consequence: June feels accepted and tells Mary she loves her too.
immoral_action: Mary tells June that being homosexual is a sin and to stop being gay.
immoral_consequence: June argues with Mary until Mary throws her out of their home.

norm: It's good to feed the unfortunate.
situation: Benji is walking down the street when he's asked by Fred, a homeless man to spare some change.
intention: Benji wants to help the homeless man.
moral_action: Benji tells Fred he has no cash but that he'll buy him a coffee and a sandwich from the local deli using debit.
moral_consequence: Fred is delighted that he'll get to eat and grateful for Benji for helping him out.
immoral_action: Benji tells Fred  that there's a homeless shelter nearby, and he can show him where it is.
immoral_consequence: Fred is annoyed because he knows about the shelter, which provides nothing for him except a place for his things to get stolen.

norm: It's rude to enjoy the misfortune of a classmate.
situation: Ken was in class when he saw Sally being fussed at by the teacher.
intention: Ken wants to do his work.
moral_action: Ken ignores what is going on with Sally and does his classwork.
moral_consequence: Ken makes an A in the class because he stays focused on his own work.
immoral_action: Ken laughs at Sally while he continues doing his classwork.
immoral_consequence: Ken's teacher fusses at him for not minding his own business.

norm: It is bad to hit others.
situation: Carl is playing at the park when another little boy takes his toy from him.
intention: Carl wants to get the toy back.
moral_action: Carl tells his mother that the boy took his toy from him.
moral_consequence: Carl's mother is able to get the toy back from the little boy.
immoral_action: Carl hits the boy and takes the toy back from him.
immoral_consequence: Carl's mother fusses at him when the other boy starts to scream.

norm: It's courteous to wear clean clothing
situation: Harry was going to be attending the wedding reception of one of his friends.
intention: Harry wants to get dressed for the wedding.
moral_action: Harry put on a nice suit and tie to attend his friend's wedding reception.
moral_consequence: Harry had a great time with his friends at the wedding reception.
immoral_action: Harry puts on a stained tee shirt and blue jeans to attend the reception.
immoral_consequence: The ushers at the reception refuse to allow Harry into the party because of his clothing.

norm: It's wrong to spoil your grandchildren.
situation: Barry's grandma was taking care of Barry for the weekend.
intention: Barry's grandma wants to make sure he gets something to eat.
moral_action: Barry's grandma fixes Barry healthy meals with a few treats during his stay.
moral_consequence: Barry is full of energy and him and his grandma have lots of fun over their weekend.
immoral_action: For dinner Barry says he wants ice cream and chips, and she lets him have it.
immoral_consequence: Barry ends up getting sick and doesn't feel good the rest of the weekend.

norm: You shouldn't let your kids go places without your permission.
situation: Sally's 13 year old is asking her to sign a permission slip for school.
intention: Sally wants to get her nails done today.
moral_action: Sally signs the slip right away then heads out to get  her nails done.
moral_consequence: Sally's child has permission to go on the trip and has a fun day.
immoral_action: Sally ignores her child and goes out to get her nails done.
immoral_consequence: Sally's child forges her moms signature her teacher finds out and bans her from the trip.

norm: It is wrong to ruin other people's marriages
situation: Phil is hurt when his ex-girlfriend gets married a few months after breaking up with him.
intention: Phil wants relief from the pain he feels.
moral_action: Phil gets emotional support from his friends and family in order to get over his ex.
moral_consequence: Phil is able to move on to a happier relationship with another woman.
immoral_action: Phil sends his ex flirty texts and e-mails which causes her husband to begin distrusting her.
immoral_consequence: Phil is shamed when their mutual friends find out what he has done and get mad at him.

norm: You shouldn't eat too many snacks because it's unhealthy.
situation: Lisa, an overweight girl, sits down on the couch stressed after work.
intention: Lisa wants to relax.
moral_action: Lisa exercises with her favorite music playing in the background.
moral_consequence: Lisa is full of energy for the rest of the night.
immoral_action: Lisa eats an entire bag of potato chips and some cookies.
immoral_consequence: Lisa gains weight.

norm: It's bad to hate people because of their sexuality.
situation: Mike sees one of his neighbors putting up a rainbow LGBT flag on her house.
intention: Mike wants to comment on the flag.
moral_action: Mike tells the neighbor that he likes the flag and thinks it adds to the neighborhood.
moral_consequence: The neighbor has a good impression of Mike and invites him in for a drink.
immoral_action: Mike screams obscenities at the neighbor for supporting gay rights and threatens to burn her house down.
immoral_consequence: The neighbor calls the police on Mike, and he is arrested for making threats.

norm: It is unsafe to drive too fast.
situation: Kenny stayed up too late last night and didn't hear his alarm go off, so he overslept.
intention: Kenny wants to be able get to work on time.
moral_action: Kenny knows if skips breakfast to make up for oversleeping he can get to work just in time.
moral_consequence: Kenny safely arrives at work ready to start the day.
immoral_action: Kenny knows he if drives fast he can get to work on time, so he drives over the speed limit the whole way.
immoral_consequence: Kenny has to hit his breaks hard because he nearly hits a pedestrian crossing the street.

norm: It's good to smile at babies.
situation: Ed is sitting on a bench at the park and sees a baby in a stroller close to him.
intention: Ed wants to play with the baby.
moral_action: Ed looks at the baby and starts making really goofy faces.
moral_consequence: The baby starts laughing and attempting to imitate Ed's faces.
immoral_action: Ed looks over the stroller and makes a monstrous face at the baby.
immoral_consequence: The baby starts crying loudly, attracting the mother and making her angry at Ed.

norm: You should try to make your parents proud.
situation: Chris just got done with college and moved back in with his parents.
intention: Chris wanted to find a job, so he could move out of his parents' house.
moral_action: Chris starts a tech company that helps people learn how to code.
moral_consequence: Chris's parents are happy that they get to brag about Chris's new business to their friends.
immoral_action: Chris became a freelance pornstar in order to make money.
immoral_consequence: Chris's parents become ashamed of him and don't want him living in their house anymroe.

norm: It's bad to buy expensive things you can't afford
situation: Jessie's car has stopped running, and she needs a car to get to her minimum wage job.
intention: Jessie wants to buy a car.
moral_action: Jessie goes to a used car dealership and looks at cars in her price range.
moral_consequence: Jessie finds a car that she can pay with cash and doesn't have a car note.
immoral_action: Jessie goes to the car dealership and buys a luxury car that she can't afford.
immoral_consequence: Jessie misses a few car payments and the car is taken away from her.

norm: It's good to end a relationship on good terms.
situation: Vicky is in a relationship with Tom, but is interested in someone else.
intention: Vicky wants to break up with Tom.
moral_action: Vicky gently tells Tom that she doesn't see the relationship going anywhere, but wants to stay friends.
moral_consequence: Tom is hurt, but over time they remain friends.
immoral_action: Vicky tells Tom that he's a loser and that he should get lost.
immoral_consequence: Tom holds a grudge against Vicky and makes her life difficult.

norm: It is wrong to want to die.
situation: Scott went through a traumatic experience and is now depressed.
intention: Scott wants to deal with the emotional pain.
moral_action: Scott sees a therapist to help him deal with the traumatic experience.
moral_consequence: Scott becomes a more pleasant person, cheering up everyone around him.
immoral_action: Scott becomes obsessed with dying and tells people about his intentions to commit suicide.
immoral_consequence: Scott's friends and family worry greatly about Scott's well-being.

norm: It's noble to apologize and make up for past misdeeds.
situation: John just started a new job and on his first day he runs into Paul a guy he bullied in high school.
intention: John wants a fresh start with Paul.
moral_action: John apologizes for his past behavior and asks for Paul's forgiveness.
moral_consequence: Paul is able to let go of his lingering hostility allowing an adult friendship to form.
immoral_action: John pretends he doesn't remember Paul and introduces himself as a stranger.
immoral_consequence: Paul is resentful that his childhood tormentor doesn't remember him.

norm: It's usually wrong to destroy things.
situation: Greg needs to tear down houses in order to build a new luxury hotel, but the current residents haven't agreed to it.
intention: Greg has to come up with a solution.
moral_action: Greg decides to build the hotel elsewhere after he can't get the consent of the owners.
moral_consequence: The owners get to keep their homes, and Greg still gets to build his hotel.
immoral_action: Greg tears down the houses without the consent of the owners.
immoral_consequence: Greg makes a bunch of people homeless and gives a potential hotel a bad reputation.

norm: It's bad to date an old love interest's sibling.
situation: Delia was dating Kevin for a long time, and they broke up but Delia sees Kevin's brother Dale at the bar and is asked out by him.
intention: Delia wants to respond to Dale.
moral_action: Delia tells Dale that she won't date him as she dated Kevin.
moral_consequence: Kevin will be able to live peacefully without his brother dating his ex.
immoral_action: Delia tells Dale that she will date him.
immoral_consequence: Kevin will feel awkward whenever Delia is around with Dale.

norm: It's good to treat your kids sometimes.
situation: Manny is returning home with his son who wants McDonald's for dinner.
intention: Manny wants to avoid cooking dinner.
moral_action: Manny buy's his son McDonald's as he wanted.
moral_consequence: Manny's son is thrilled that he gets a treat.
immoral_action: Manny makes his son eat elsewhere instead.
immoral_consequence: Manny's son is disappointed that he didn't get his favorite food.

norm: It is rude to mess up areas.
situation: Kelly has just finished cleaning in the living room when her son Jim walks into the room.
intention: Jim wants to play with his toys.
moral_action: Jim plays with his toys and then picks them up after himself.
moral_consequence: Jim's toys stay in the toy box until the next time that he plays with them.
immoral_action: Jim plays with his toys and leaves them on the floor that Kelly just cleaned.
immoral_consequence: Kelly is annoyed and picks up and throws all Jim's toys in the trash.

norm: You shouldn't put your spouse down
situation: Jane's husband played a football game and his team lost.
intention: Jane wants to comment about the game to her husband.
moral_action: Jane tells her husband that even though the team lost he played well.
moral_consequence: Jane's husband feels better about the outcome of the game after Jane's comment.
immoral_action: Jane tells her husband that the team lost because of his incompetence.
immoral_consequence: Jane's husband's self esteem is deflated by her comment on his performance.

norm: You shouldn't mow the lawn while going commando.
situation: Henry is standing nude before his mirror in his bedroom getting ready to do some yard work.
intention: Henry wants to decide what to wear while mowing the lawn.
moral_action: Henry decides to put on a tracksuit, a hat, safety goggles and safety boots.
moral_consequence: Henry doesn't feel any effect from the bugs or the mower shrapnel as he finishes mowing the lawn unscathed.
immoral_action: Henry decides to put on just a pair of shorts and socks and shoes and nothing else.
immoral_consequence: Henry's thighs and midsection are besieged by bugs while little twigs and other shrapnel from the mower carve his skin up.

norm: It is wrong to be an abusive father.
situation: David has two stepchildren from his wife, Missy, who are often rowdy and test his patience.
intention: David wants the kids to stop misbehaving.
moral_action: David sees the kids acting up and explains to them why their behavior is unacceptable.
moral_consequence: The kids listen to David and change their behavior.
immoral_action: David sees the kids acting up and lashes at them both with a belt.
immoral_consequence: Missy's kids become afraid of David and grow up not trusting people.

norm: You should apologize when you betray your friends.
situation: Jon kissed his friend's girlfriend wile drunk and his friend confronts him about it.
intention: Jon wants to react to his friend's confrontation.
moral_action: Jon says he's really sorry for what he did saying that he was drunk at the time and asking for forgiveness.
moral_consequence: Although Jon's friend is upset he's happy Jon apologized and forgives him over time.
immoral_action: Jon tells his friend that since their girlfriend was willing to kiss Jon they should blame their girlfriend for what happened.
immoral_consequence: John's friend thinks Jon is scummy for betraying them and doesn't consider Jon a close friend any longer.

norm: It's abusive to smack your children.
situation: Kim has a child who has been acting up all day and causing trouble.
intention: Kim wants to discipline her child.
moral_action: Kim takes away her child's favorite game.
moral_consequence: Kim's child learns there will be consequences to acting out.
immoral_action: Kim becomes fed up and slaps her child.
immoral_consequence: Kim's child starts to cry and becomes afraid of her.

norm: You shouldn't discriminate against people with mental problems.
situation: John is a landlord reviewing the rental application of a man named Bill who has disclosed having prior mental health issues.
intention: John wants to find a new tenant for his property.
moral_action: John judges Bill to be a good potential tenant and approves him to rent the property.
moral_consequence: Bill is happy with his new housing and proves to be a great tenant.
immoral_action: John denies Bill's application due to his history of mental health problems and signs a lease with someone else.
immoral_consequence: Bill has trouble finding adequate housing and has to move in with his parents for the time being.

norm: It is good to voice your concerns with others.
situation: Lindsey notices that her manager is taking supplies from the office.
intention: Lindsey wants to react to her manager taking supplies.
moral_action: Lindsey tells the company owner that her manager is taking supplies.
moral_consequence: Lindsey's boss will be reprimanded or fired and the supply loss will stop.
immoral_action: Lindsey keeps quiet about what her manager is doing.
immoral_consequence: Lindsey's boss continue to take supplies and cost the company money.

norm: It's rude to swear at others.
situation: Stephanie is ordering food at a fast food store and the employee is having a hard time getting her order correct.
intention: Stephanie wants to get her meal.
moral_action: Stephanie takes her time explaining her order to the employee until they get it right.
moral_consequence: The employee thanks Stephanie for their patience and Stephanie is able to enjoy her meal.
immoral_action: Stephanie begins to raise her voice while talking trying to get the employee to get the order right and eventually begins using profanity due to her impatience.
immoral_consequence: The employee has enough and walks away leaving Stephanie without a meal.

norm: It's bad to drink alcohol to excess.
situation: Jerry is attending his company Christmas party.
intention: Jerry wants to loosen up.
moral_action: Jerry has two shots of tequila and feels nice and relaxed.
moral_consequence: Jerry has fun mingling with the other party goers.
immoral_action: Jerry drinks one shot after another of tequila.
immoral_consequence: Jerry gets drunk to the point he can't walk and embarrasses himself in front of his boss and coworkers.

norm: It's wrong to yell at people who have different opinions
situation: Brian was talking to his coworkers during their break when they get into a heated discussion about politics.
intention: Brian wants to get his point across.
moral_action: Brian explains to his coworkers why he thinks the way that he does.
moral_consequence: Brian and his coworkers decide that they will agree to disagree.
immoral_action: Brian begins to yell at his coworkers and belittle them because of their opinions.
immoral_consequence: Brian's boss brings him into the office and tells him that he is fired.

norm: You shouldn't try to impress people by acting tough.
situation: Jim is out with his girlfriend Janet at the Fair when another guy calls Janet a bad name.
intention: Jim wants to impress and stand up for his girlfriend.
moral_action: Jim tells the guy he shouldn't talk to women like that and Janet is a wonderful girl, and he takes Janet to a safer part of the Fair.
moral_consequence: Janet respects Jim for his wisdom and peacefulness and loves him more.
immoral_action: Jim immediately punches the guy and the guy falls down bleeding and hurt.
immoral_consequence: Janet is petrified and thinks Jim is a jerk and leaves him.

norm: It's discouraged to drink alcohol when you're a minor.
situation: Josh has plans to go to his friend's party, which is for teenagers, on the weekend where some people are planning on bringing alcohol.
intention: Josh wants to have fun at his friend's Saturday celebration.
moral_action: Josh attends his friend's bash, where he stays sober and participates in team online games.
moral_consequence: His friend appreciates that he didn't drink, and they become best friends.
immoral_action: Josh goes to his friends party, drinks whiskey and goes swimming at their pool.
immoral_consequence: His friend's parents find out the following week and ban Josh from coming back to their home.

norm: Mocking people is rude.
situation: Anthony sees his friend do something silly.
intention: Anthony wants to stop his friend from doing it again.
moral_action: Anthony quietly asks his friend to be better.
moral_consequence: Anthony's friend realized what he did was wrong.
immoral_action: Anthony loudly makes fun of his friend, drawing a crowd.
immoral_consequence: Anthony's friend is humiliated and hurt.

norm: It's bad to steal someone's identity.
situation: Gwen gets laid off from her job because the company moved to Mexico for cheaper labor.
intention: Gwen wants to get money to pay her bills.
moral_action: Gwen put her resume on several job sites.
moral_consequence: Gwen gets a new job and is able to pay her bills.
immoral_action: Gwen goes on the dark web and buys someone's personal information and uses it to get a credit card.
immoral_consequence: Gwen gets arrested for identity theft when her crime is discovered.

norm: It's frowned on to have a squalid home.
situation: Francis is a woman who doesn't enjoy cleaning her home, and is fine with the piles of trash and mess everywhere.
intention: Francis wants to live her life the way she pleases.
moral_action: Francis decides that she'd be more comfortable with room to breathe and starts to clean up.
moral_consequence: Francis realizes how poorly she's been living and starts cleaning her home on a regular basis.
immoral_action: Francis continues to let trash and other items pile up in her home.
immoral_consequence: Francis' home is condemned by the city when a neighbor reports it as unsafe for human dwelling.

norm: It is polite to offer friends a place to stay.
situation: Ross' house is messy, but he has some friends flying in from out of town to visit him.
intention: Ross wants to avoid being inconvenienced by his friends.
moral_action: Ross hires a cleaning service to come clean up the mess in his house before his friends visit.
moral_consequence: Ross' friends appreciate being given a clean place to stay and make an effort to stay more in touch after the trip.
immoral_action: Ross tells his friends that his house has water damage, and they need to stay somewhere else, even though it's not true.
immoral_consequence: Ross' friends find out that his house did not have water damage and it made the rest of the trip awkward.

norm: It's wrong to control your child's life.
situation: Maggie's son Trevor wants to go over to Micah, his new friend's, house.
intention: Maggie wants to make sure her son is safe.
moral_action: Maggie gives Trevor her phone number and reminds him to call her if Trevor ever feels unsafe.
moral_consequence: Trevor feels like his mother loves and support him, and he has a fun night with his friends.
immoral_action: Maggie refuses to let Trevor visit his friend demanding that Micah comes over to her house first.
immoral_consequence: Trevor is embarrassed and upset at his mother.

norm: It's inconsiderate to steal someone else's lunch.
situation: Jenny is taking her lunch break in the break room at work and forgot her lunch, but see's her co-worker Alex has a big salad in the fridge.
intention: Jenny wants to eat.
moral_action: Jenny asks Alex if he would mind giving her some of his salad.
moral_consequence: Alex is happy to help Jenny and shares it with her.
immoral_action: Jenny takes Alex's salad and begins eating it, then Alex walks in and catches her.
immoral_consequence: Alex is angry because now he has nothing to eat, and he knows Jenny stole from him.

norm: It's rude to be offensive to kids.
situation: Paul was sitting in the park when some kids start playing near him.
intention: Paul wants to be alone in the park.
moral_action: Paul gets up and finds a more secluded part of the park.
moral_consequence: Paul enjoys the rest of his day relaxing at the park alone.
immoral_action: Paul yells at the kids and tells them to beat it.
immoral_consequence: The parents of the children go over to Paul and beat him up.

norm: Showing excitement over a gift is considerate.
situation: Chris's grandma gives him a hideous knitted sweater for christmas.
intention: Chris wants to respond to his Grandma's gift.
moral_action: Chris smiles as his grandmother gives him the sweater and jumps to his feet to try it on immediately.
moral_consequence: Chris's grandmother appreciates that her hard work is being valued.
immoral_action: Chris accepts his grandma's gift impassively, before turning and tossing it in a trashcan.
immoral_consequence: Chris's grandmother is devastated that her heard work was not appreciated.

norm: It's wrong to lie to your friends.
situation: Eddie has been invited to his friend's birthday party, but he doesn't want to go.
intention: Eddie wants to go to the park.
moral_action: Eddie tells his friend that he had planned on going to the park instead.
moral_consequence: Eddie's friend is disappointed, but they plan to get together another time.
immoral_action: Eddie tells his friend he is too sick and goes to the park instead of the birthday party.
immoral_consequence: Eddie is seen at the park and his friend is mad that he lied.

norm: It's good to celebrate someone's life when they die.
situation: Kim's mother has passed away and Kim's father Larry has come to ask Kim whether she is coming to her mother's wake.
intention: Kim wants to respond to her father.
moral_action: Kim tells her father that of course she will be at the wake as her mother is the most important thing to her.
moral_consequence: Larry is in mourning but feels a sense of strength from his family and is happy that Kim will be there.
immoral_action: Kim tells her father that she will not be going to the wake as she is too tired and it'll be too boring for her to be there.
immoral_consequence: Larry is devastated and begins to question whether Kim is capable of loving anyone.

norm: It is wrong to be addicted to a substance.
situation: Steve has been using drugs every day for several months and is having a hard time stopping.
intention: Steve has to decide what he should do about his drug use.
moral_action: Steve finds a group, with an internet search, that provides help and support for people who want to stop using drugs.
moral_consequence: Steve is able to stop using drugs and develops new social relationships, as his health and outlook on life steadily improves over time.
immoral_action: Steve continues using drugs, because he finds it too difficult to stop.
immoral_consequence: Steve's health and all of his social relationships deteriorate, as he isolates himself and prioritizes his use of drugs.

norm: It is good to be proud of others.
situation: Ben is at home when his son Mike comes home and gives him his report card full of straight A's.
intention: Ben wants to put the report card somewhere.
moral_action: Ben looks at the grades and tells Jim he did an amazing job before sticking the report card on the fridge with a magnet.
moral_consequence: Jim is delighted that his dad is so proud of him that he put the report card on the fridge to be displayed.
immoral_action: Ben thanks Jim for giving him the report card and puts it away with his other paperwork.
immoral_consequence: Jim is disappointed Ben didn't even look to see what grades Jim got and thought his dad would be more excited.

norm: You should not expect others to pay for your things.
situation: Darryl is unemployed and dating a girl with a good job.
intention: Darryl wants to enjoy life's pleasures.
moral_action: Darryl applies and get a good job and saves up for his ferrari car.
moral_consequence: Darryl's girlfriend will be impressed with him and respect and love him more.
immoral_action: Darryl asks his girlfriend to buy him a ferrari car on her credit.
immoral_consequence: Darryl's girlfriend will resent Darryl and respect him less and probably dump him.

norm: It is wrong to disregard your education.
situation: Brad is talking about college with his cousin Josh and his mother Connie who paid for Brad's education.
intention: Brad wants to give Josh advise.
moral_action: Brad tells Josh about how he uses what he learned in his degree in his job.
moral_consequence: Connie feels proud of Brad.
immoral_action: Brad tells Josh that his degree in English was a waste of money.
immoral_consequence: Connie's feelings are hurt by Brad's words.

norm: It's advisable to hire a professional for important jobs.
situation: Rob needs to do some home repairs for safety and has been quoted too high of a price.
intention: Rob wants to save money on the repairs.
moral_action: Rob finds a coupon code for a licensed professional whom he hires.
moral_consequence: The repairs are done safely and the house is now safer for those living there.
immoral_action: Rob hires an unlicensed laborer to perform the repairs for much less.
immoral_consequence: The laborer does not complete the repairs according to code making it a hazard for the occupants.

norm: You should support your loved ones through the hard times.
situation: William has just told his wife Linda that he has lost his job.
intention: Linda wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Linda takes William with her out on a walk near the lake.
moral_consequence: William's head is cleared, and he is more at peace in the tranquil setting.
immoral_action: Linda goes out with her friends to eat and watch a movie.
immoral_consequence: William is left alone with his thoughts and drinks himself drunk.

norm: It's not okay to use something bad to get attention.
situation: John is a teenager in high school going through changes and feeling left out.
intention: John wants to feel cared about.
moral_action: John visits the school's counselor and explains all of the problems he has a been feeling.
moral_consequence: The counselor speaks to John's parents who then choose to make more time for John.
immoral_action: John begins to act out at school by getting in fights and talking back to teachers in front of his classmates.
immoral_consequence: John is suspended from school and punished by his parents making him more withdrawn.

norm: Having stains on your clothes makes you look dirty.
situation: Frank is about to leave for an important work meeting one morning when he notices a stain on his shirt.
intention: Frank wants to get to the work meeting on time.
moral_action: Frank quickly uses a Tide pen to remove the stain before rushing to work.
moral_consequence: Frank looks clean and professional and his colleagues value his contributions at the meeting.
immoral_action: Frank ignores the stain and hops in his car to drive to work.
immoral_consequence: Frank's colleagues notice the stain on his shirt and snicker at his slovenly and unprofessional appearance.

norm: You shouldn't take lost animals and just leave them somewhere.
situation: Mark finds a lost dog wandering around his neighborhood with no collar or ID and takes it in for the night.
intention: Mark needs to find something to do with the dog he found.
moral_action: Mark takes the dog in his truck to the local animal shelter, in hopes that the original owner will come to claim it.
moral_consequence: The dog is thrilled when its owner arrives to pick it up.
immoral_action: Mark puts the dog in his truck and drives to an empty field before letting it loose.
immoral_consequence: The dog wanders around the unfamiliar terrain, and is stressed out and scared.

norm: You should never be cruel to an animal
situation: Tom's dog continually bites him and visitors, and it's becoming a problem.
intention: Tom wants to let his dog know not to bite.
moral_action: Tom decides to reward his dog with treats for not biting.
moral_consequence: Tom's dog appreciated the treats and Tom is happy to see changed behavior from his dog.
immoral_action: Tom decides to kick his dog whenever his dog bites.
immoral_consequence: Tom's dog does not approve of Tom's actions and both never resolve the conflict.

norm: It's rude to act out against your babysitter.
situation: Ken hired a new babysitter to help him with his kids but the babysitter did not put the kids to bed at 8 pm.
intention: Ken wants to respond to the babysitter's failure.
moral_action: Ken tells the babysitter that the kids were not in bed by 8 pm and that he would like this to be resolved next time.
moral_consequence: The babysitter continues to work for Ken and gets the kids in bed by 8 pm next time.
immoral_action: Ken raises his voice against the babysitter over her failure to get the kids in bed by 8 pm.
immoral_consequence: The babysitter never works for Ken again and Ken struggles to find another babysitter.

norm: It's wrong to lie about the quality of your food.
situation: Jamie is out having dinner at a nice restaurant.
intention: Jamie wants a discount on her dinner bill.
moral_action: Jamie asks the waiter if the restaurant offers any discounts.
moral_consequence: The waiter signs Jamie up for their email list which allows a discount on your first meal.
immoral_action: After finishing dinner, Jamie tells the waiter that the food was terrible and refuses to pay her bill.
immoral_consequence: The restaurant involves the police, who make Jamie pay her bill.

norm: You should have fun while cooking
situation: Ryan is in the middle of a diet plan and is preparing meals for the week.
intention: Ryan wants to stick to his diet.
moral_action: Ryan makes sure to keep things interesting while preparing the meals and is always willing to try or learn something new in the kitchen.
moral_consequence: Ryan's dedication and interest in the preparing of the meals ends up the most crucial influence on him sticking to his diet.
immoral_action: Ryan slops together his meals as quickly as possible using any cooking short cut he can think of as to be done with the task.
immoral_consequence: Ryan's meal quality suffers from the lack of care while preparing them and this eventually leads to him faltering from the diet.

norm: You shouldn't pretend to have a girlfriend when you don't.
situation: Jack's friends and their dates are all going to the homecoming dance.
intention: Jack wants to go to the dance with his friends.
moral_action: Jack tells his friends he wants to go to the homecoming dance, but he doesn't have a girlfriend to go with.
moral_consequence: Jack's friends get him a date to take to the dance and Jack and his date dance and have fun.
immoral_action: Jack tells his friends he has a girlfriend, even though he doesn't, and that she can't come to the dance since she’s in Canada.
immoral_consequence: Jack ends up being a fifth wheel at the dance and stands alone while his friends have fun and dance.

norm: Refusing to pay for a first date is cheap.
situation: John and Wilma are on their first date at a restaurant when John realizes that he doesn't have money to pay.
intention: John wants to get the meal paid for.
moral_action: John asks the restaurant to put the bill on his tab and gives something personal as collateral.
moral_consequence: John pays for the bill later and keeps Wilma as his girlfriend.
immoral_action: John asks Wilma to cover the food bill.
immoral_consequence: Wilma is disgusted, pays for the food, and never sees John again.

norm: It's nice to help out others who live with you.
situation: Bobby is home where he lives with a roommate who is currently trying to fix a part of their house.
intention: Bobby wants to ask what his roommate is doing.
moral_action: Bobby inquires as to what his roommate is working on while offering to lend a hand in any way possible.
moral_consequence: Bobby's roommate is appreciative and explains the project as well as the ways Bobby can help.
immoral_action: Bobby asks his roommate what he is working on with no intention of sticking around.
immoral_consequence: Bobby's roommate explains the project and is disappointed when Bobby doesn't offer a helping hand since they both live there.

norm: You shouldn't yank at your clothes.
situation: Mary is feeling uncomfortable in her new dress.
intention: Mary wants to fix her dress so that she is comfortable.
moral_action: Mary goes to a seamstress and explains her issues with the new dress.
moral_consequence: Mary's dress fits well, and she doesn't have to constantly adjust it.
immoral_action: Mary constantly pulls at her new dress to get it to sit the way she likes.
immoral_consequence: Mary ends up pulling too hard and her dress rips.

norm: Snooping is rude.
situation: June is concerned because her boyfriend Steve has been acting secretive lately.
intention: June wants to find out if Steve has been hiding anything from her.
moral_action: June confronts Steve with her concerns and asks for an explanation of his behavior.
moral_consequence: June is able to establish an open and honest line of communication with Steve.
immoral_action: June goes through Steve's phone and computer to find out what he has been up to.
immoral_consequence: June loses Steve's trust when he finds out about her intrusive behavior.

norm: It's kind to give money to those in need.
situation: Ted is walking through the city and sees a homeless man asking for change.
intention: Ted wants to motivate the homeless man.
moral_action: Ted gives the man a $100 dollar bill and tells him to take care of himself.
moral_consequence: The man is able to buy a new outfit and haircut to apply to a new job.
immoral_action: Ted gives the man a motivational speech that involves his own life.
immoral_consequence: The man is unaffected by the speech and continues to suffer.

norm: It's good to take your child to a fun place.
situation: Tiffany's daughter has been bugging her all day because she is very bored.
intention: Tiffany wants to find a way to keep her daughter busy.
moral_action: Tiffany takes her daughter to the amusement park.
moral_consequence: Tiffany and her daughter have a lot of fun together and their relationship becomes closer.
immoral_action: Tiffany tells her daughter to go watch television.
immoral_consequence: Tiffany's daughter becomes addicted to television and never goes outside.

norm: It's mean to finish the last of someone's ice cream.
situation: Jessie and Kevin are roommates and Kevin has been saving some ice cream for a special treat.
intention: Jessie wants a sweet snack.
moral_action: Jessie goes to the store and buys his own ice cream to eat.
moral_consequence: Jessie and Kevin both get to enjoy their desserts.
immoral_action: Jessie eats Kevin's ice cream that he has been saving.
immoral_consequence: Kevin gets upset with Jessie and is disappointed.

norm: It's nice to help people's self esteem.
situation: Hal is talking to his friend Don who's wife just left him for another man and is feeling down.
intention: Hal wants to talk to Don.
moral_action: Hal tells Don that he knows it hurts but to remember that he's a great looking and funny guy.
moral_consequence: Don cheers up right away because he was reminded that he has good qualities and will find someone else because of it.
immoral_action: Hal tells Don that there's not much he can do about it, so to just try to get over the fact his wife loves someone else.
immoral_consequence: Don feels even more depressed because what Hal said was not uplifting.

norm: It's bad to put a snake in someone's bed.
situation: Jessica attends a boarding school where she is bullied by one of the girls named Annabelle, who is in her dorm.
intention: Jessica wants Annabelle to stop bullying her.
moral_action: Jessica tells the headmistress about the bullying, and asks to be assigned to a different dorm.
moral_consequence: Annabelle and Jessica no longer share a dorm or any classes, and Jessica is no longer bullied.
immoral_action: Jessica catches a garter snake and puts it in Annabelle's bed one day, scaring Annabelle very badly.
immoral_consequence: Jessica is expelled from the school and never sees Annabelle again.

norm: It's bad to have low work ethic.
situation: Jerry has a number of homework assignments due the next day.
intention: Jerry wants to consider doing his homework.
moral_action: Jerry focuses up and motivates himself to work on his homework immediately.
moral_consequence: Jerry receives praise for his good work and manage to pass his classes with straight 'A's.
immoral_action: Jerry decides to go do something fun instead of doing his homework.
immoral_consequence: Jerry receives a failing grade for multiple classes and is held back a grade.

norm: It's wrong to spoil your kids.
situation: Ursula is walking through the mall with her young daughter Bella when Bella sees an expensive fur coat for kids and asks her mom to buy it.
intention: Ursula wants to respond to Bella's request.
moral_action: Ursula tells Bella that her request is beyond absurd and that if she wants a coat like that she can go to college and then get a job.
moral_consequence: Bella begins to understand that money is not something that's just available for everyone and it serves her better later in life.
immoral_action: Ursula tells Bella that if she wants the expensive coat she can have it and goes to buy it.
immoral_consequence: Bella never learns the value of a dollar or what it takes to make money and fails later in life.

norm: You shouldn't cut off people who are trying to speak.
situation: Jonas is listening to Allie tell an exciting story about her backpacking trip.
intention: Jonas wants to respond to Allie's story.
moral_action: Jonas waits for Allie to finish her story and then says what he wants to.
moral_consequence: Allie will be able to tell her full story without being interrupted.
immoral_action: Jonas starts talking in the middle of Allie telling her story.
immoral_consequence: Allie will think Jonas is rude for interrupting.

norm: Death is difficult and you shouldn't try to suppress grief.
situation: Shane just received a phone call that his best friend Jodi died in a car crash.
intention: Shane wants to react to the news.
moral_action: Shane tries to remember all the good times he had with Jodi and takes the news one day at a time.
moral_consequence: Shane is still sad but every day gets easier for him to cope.
immoral_action: Shane thinks he can avoid feeling the pain of loss if he just tries to put it out of his mind.
immoral_consequence: Shane's bottled emotions get the best of him within a few weeks, and he falls into a deep depression.

norm: It's rude to catcall girls.
situation: John is driving home from work when he notices a beautiful woman walking along the street.
intention: John wants to get the woman's attention.
moral_action: John gives the woman a friendly wave as he drives by.
moral_consequence: The waves back and continues her walk undisturbed.
immoral_action: John calls the woman beautiful and tells her to smile more as he drives by.
immoral_consequence: The woman is very offended and flips John off.

norm: It is rude to be racist towards others.
situation: Clark is a cashier at a convenience store who works in a diverse area.
intention: Clark wants to keep his store safe and crime free.
moral_action: Clarks gives his customers the benefit of the doubt and only reacts if security camera show sometihng obvious.
moral_consequence: The store gains a lot of repeat customers and Clark makes a lot of money.
immoral_action: Clark follows around the black customers and often wrongfully accuses them of taking things without paying.
immoral_consequence: Clark's shop has a bad reputation on yelp, and he eventually has to close down.

norm: It's wrong to encourage people to target others.
situation: Laura is giving a speech about the importance of protecting the environment.
intention: Laura wants to inspire her listeners to take action.
moral_action: Laura tells her listeners ways they can make changes in their life that can help the environment.
moral_consequence: To Laura's delight, her listeners practice some of her techniques and reduce their environmental footprint.
immoral_action: Laura tells her listeners that peaceful action is no longer viable and to take arms against those who would harm the planet.
immoral_consequence: Laura is arrested for inciting violence and radical listeners take Laura's words as reason to incite violence.

norm: It's rude to sneak somewhere.
situation: John is walking by a movie theater and sees a new film he is interested in that costs $10 a ticket.
intention: John wants to get in and watch the new movie.
moral_action: John pays $10 for a ticket and finds a good seat for the movie.
moral_consequence: John has a great time and really enjoys the movie.
immoral_action: John attempts to sneak in the back exit door to see the movie without paying for a ticket.
immoral_consequence: John is caught by security staff and thrown out of the theater, so he doesn't get to see the movie.

norm: You are expected to help out friends in need
situation: Sarah is watching TV when she gets a text from her friend Keisha asking to come pick her up as she's run out of gas on the highway.
intention: Sarah wants to respond to Keisha's request for help.
moral_action: Sarah texts Keisha to stay put and drives to her with a gas canister of fuel.
moral_consequence: Keisha fills up her car and drives home within a half hour of running out of gas.
immoral_action: Sarah texts Keisha back and tells her to walk to the nearest gas station to buy some fuel.
immoral_consequence: Keisha has to walk miles to a gas station and back to refuel her car, and it's hours before she's back on the road.

norm: It's rude to make pot brownies and not tell people.
situation: Taylor is going to a potluck work Christmas party and needs to bring a dish to pass.
intention: Taylor wants to bring a dessert.
moral_action: Taylor bakes a batch of chocolate brownies from a recipe she found online.
moral_consequence: Taylor gets many compliments from her coworkers for the delicious chocolate brownies she brought.
immoral_action: "Taylor makes pot brownies and takes them to the party with a sign reading, ""Double Chocolate Brownies""."
immoral_consequence: Taylor is fired when multiple coworkers realize they've consumed pot and identify the source as Taylor's brownies.

norm: Parents should not cut ties with their child.
situation: Brian's young adult son Frank identifies himself as a homosexual at dinner with the family one night, of which Brian disapproves.
intention: Brian wants to respond to Frank's revelation.
moral_action: Brian tells Frank he's free to continue living their in spite of their different opinions on appropriate sexuality.
moral_consequence: Frank is thankful to have such a supportive father, even if he doesn't approve of Frank's lifestyle.
immoral_action: Brian tells Frank he won't have anyone with that label living in his household and tells him to pack his things and leave.
immoral_consequence: Frank harbors deep resentment towards Brian and never speaks to him again.

norm: It is rude to interrupt someone's conversation.
situation: Sean needs help with his assignment, but his teacher is talking with someone else.
intention: Sean wants to ask his teacher for help.
moral_action: Sean waits for his teacher's conversation to end before asking for help.
moral_consequence: Sean's teacher thinks that he is polite and is more willing to help him.
immoral_action: Sean barges into the conversation and asks her teacher for help.
immoral_consequence: Sean's teacher thinks that Sean is rude and obnoxious and asks him to wait.

norm: You shouldn't play with your food.
situation: Cameron is at a fancy restaurant eating dinner with his parents.
intention: Cameron wants a bite of mashed potatoes.
moral_action: Cameron takes a bite of mashed potatoes and uses his napkin to clean up his face.
moral_consequence: Cameron's mother tells him that she is proud of his table manners.
immoral_action: Cameron takes a bite of mashed potatoes and has it erupt out of his mouth like a volcano.
immoral_consequence: Cameron's mother drags him out of the dining area and gives him a lecture in the lobby.

norm: It's bad to let kids rule the house.
situation: Jane has just a single child whom she adores.
intention: Jane wants her child to be happy.
moral_action: Jane makes time for her child whenever possible to teach it all that is right and wrong as well as explore its interests.
moral_consequence: The child grows up well loved, well adjusted and properly motivated.
immoral_action: Jane breaks and bends to satisfy her child's every whim without every considering saying no to it.
immoral_consequence: The child becomes a spoiled brat who is in no way prepared for life and struggles to make any friends.

norm: People shouldn't constantly look to trade up on relationships.
situation: Emily has always been impressed by people with money, and it's a factor in how she chooses her partners.
intention: Emily wants to feel good about herself.
moral_action: Emily decides that making money herself is better than dating a rich guy, and she lands a well-paying job.
moral_consequence: Emily's friends are impressed by her career and admire her.
immoral_action: Emily just ditched her boyfriend for someone richer, after doing the same thing last year.
immoral_consequence: Emily's friends are secretly starting to feel that she is superficial.

norm: It's good to support your child's college decision.
situation: Melissa, Jared's daughter, tells Jarred that she is not sure she should apply for her dream university.
intention: Jared wants to encourage Melissa.
moral_action: Jared offers to help Melissa with her application to her chosen university.
moral_consequence: Melissa gets an acceptance letter for her ideal university.
immoral_action: Jared tells Melissa that there's other universities more suited for her skill level, and that she can probably get accepted into those.
immoral_consequence: Melissa passes over her ideal school for second best, and she doesn't fully enjoy her college life.

norm: It is reckless to drive while drunk.
situation: Barney is out of beer and the evening is young.
intention: Barney wants more beer to drink.
moral_action: Barney plays it safe and finds an alcohol delivery service.
moral_consequence: Barney remains safe at home while still being able to enjoy more drinks.
immoral_action: Barney drives to the store despite feeling quite buzzed thinking that he is okay.
immoral_consequence: Barney is pulled over when seen swerving and charged with a DUI.

norm: It's bad to use racial slurs.
situation: Elena is driving home and a car driven by a person a different race than her cuts her off.
intention: Elena wants to react to being cut off.
moral_action: Elena slows down as to let the bad driver get some distance away from her to make her feel safer.
moral_consequence: Elena is able to drive home safely without further incident.
immoral_action: Elena mutters to herself comments about the other driver that are connected to their race that others might find offensive.
immoral_consequence: Elena becomes used to using those racial slurs and eventually repeats them in public offending others.

norm: It's rude to bring up someone's past mistakes.
situation: Tony's wife cheated on his many years ago, and is asking him if she can go out with her girlfriends for some drinks.
intention: Tony wants his girlfriend to stay in tonight.
moral_action: Tony tells her that he would really prefer her to stay home with him tonight and watch some movies.
moral_consequence: Tony and his wife have a great time watching movies together and their relationship grows stronger.
immoral_action: Tony asks her if it's so she can spend the night with some other guy again, and tells her not to go out.
immoral_consequence: Tony's wife grows resentful because she knows she has been faithful for years, and eventually seeks a divorce.

norm: It's good to hang out with people.
situation: Zach just finished up with his classes for the week and is relaxing at home playing video games, when his friends invite him to go out.
intention: Zach wants to have a good time.
moral_action: Zach agrees to meet up with his friends.
moral_consequence: Zach's friends have a lot of fun hanging out with him, and they invite him out next time as well.
immoral_action: Zach declines his friends' invitation and stays home playing video games all weekend.
immoral_consequence: Zach's friends eventually stop inviting him out.

norm: It's wrong to lock your pet up in closed quarters.
situation: Don has a dog that has just torn his couch apart when left alone at home.
intention: Don wants to teach the dog not to damage the furniture.
moral_action: Don uses a scented product which is offensive to dog noses on the furniture.
moral_consequence: The dog loses interest in getting anywhere near the furniture.
immoral_action: Don closes the dog in a room as a form of discipline.
immoral_consequence: The dog doesn't understand why he is being shut in the room because the damage was done hours ago.

norm: It's hurtful to wish your child wasn't born.
situation: Bob's child wrote on the wall with a marker.
intention: Bob wants to punish his child.
moral_action: Bob tells his child to clean the wall and that they will have no play time for a week.
moral_consequence: Bob's child will learn they have to fix the bad things they do.
immoral_action: Bob tells his child that life was better when they were not around.
immoral_consequence: Bob's child will feel unwanted and sad.

norm: You should discuss issues in a calm manner.
situation: Don and Sam are having a debate over healthcare policy in the US.
intention: Don wants to voice his views.
moral_action: Don listens to Sam and voices his disagreements when it's his turn to speak.
moral_consequence: Don is able to see where he and Sam agree and disagree and come to a mutual understanding.
immoral_action: Don begins yelling over Sam because he disagrees with his position.
immoral_consequence: Don looks childish for not having a civilized conversation and fails to truly understand Sams point.

norm: It's illegal to jaywalk.
situation: Tyler is walking to the store and is approaching an intersection to cross the street.
intention: Tyler wants to cross the street to reach the store.
moral_action: Tyler is approaching the intersection crosswalk and continues until he reaches the light to cross the street.
moral_consequence: Tyler crosses the street legally and makes it to the store without issue.
immoral_action: Tyler is approaching the intersection crosswalk and decides to cross the street before it to save walking time.
immoral_consequence: A cop sees Tyler illegally jaywalk and stops him to give a ticket for the crime and Tyler continues to the store.

norm: It's good to get your kids involved in fun activities.
situation: Bryan has two children, and they have just begun their summer vacation from school.
intention: Bryan wants to make a summer plan for them.
moral_action: Bryan enrolls his children in summer camps and sports activities to keep them occupied.
moral_consequence: The children have a fantastic summer where they learn a lot and make new friends.
immoral_action: Bryan makes a list of chores and house projects for them to work on all summer.
immoral_consequence: The children dislike doing all the housework, and they are bored and miserable all summer.

norm: It's good to help friends when they need it
situation: John lives with Eric, his friend, and Eric needs a ride to the store.
intention: John wants to watch a movie at home tonight.
moral_action: John drives Eric to the store and tells him he will pick him up later when the movie is over.
moral_consequence: Eric likes John more and will help him in the future too.
immoral_action: John ignores Eric and puts the volume up loud on his movie as he watches from the couch.
immoral_consequence: Eric will resent John and not help him when he needs help in the future.

norm: You should not be wasteful.
situation: Michelle is cleaning out her garage.
intention: Michelle wants to get rid of some things.
moral_action: Michelle put her items on the curb and makes an ad on Craigslist under the Free section so people can come and take the items to use.
moral_consequence: Michelle gets praise and thanks from the people who pick up her unwanted items.
immoral_action: Michelle sets her unwanted items out for the garbage truck to pick up.
immoral_consequence: Michelle is scolded by her neighbor for putting perfectly fine items in the landfill.

norm: It's bad to get too drunk.
situation: Garrett was invited to go to his best friend's wedding reception.
intention: Garrett wants to have a drink.
moral_action: Garrett goes to the bar and orders a glass of wine.
moral_consequence: Garrett enjoys himself talking with the other guests over his wine.
immoral_action: Garrett goes to the bar and drinks several shots of tequila in succession.
immoral_consequence: Garrett can't walk straight and is kicked out of the reception party.

norm: You shouldn't get mad at someone who is helping you.
situation: Danny is helping John paint his apartment and John notices that Danny is painting the wrong part of the wall.
intention: John wants to tell Danny to stop painting.
moral_action: John doesn't tell Danny he's doing anything wrong, he just simply tells Danny to take a break while he finishes the wall.
moral_consequence: Danny is happy to take a break and thinks his friend is giving him a break because he appreciates his hard work so far.
immoral_action: John yells at Danny to stop, calls him an idiot and exasperatedly tells him he's doing it all wrong.
immoral_consequence: Danny is stunned that his friend is so mad and is offended that his help is being criticized.

norm: You shouldn't attend events that you weren't invited to.
situation: Charla lives in Hollywood and found out that her favorite fashion icon, Mia, is attending a party by her house tonight.
intention: Charla wants to see what Mia wears to the party.
moral_action: Charla goes on social media to check Mia's account.
moral_consequence: Charla sees that Mia has posted tonight's outfit to her account.
immoral_action: Charla crashes the party to see Mia.
immoral_consequence: People begin to realize that Charla shouldn't be there, and she is kicked out.

norm: It's rude to mistreat people in the service industry.
situation: Carlita just received her order from the food counter and it does not match what she ordered.
intention: Carlita wants to get the order corrected.
moral_action: Carlita lets the worker know that the order is wrong and explains clearly what her order was.
moral_consequence: The worker apologizes for the mistake and quickly fixes Carlita's order, and she also receives a full refund.
immoral_action: Carlita draws attention to herself with volume and tosses the food she received back over the counter all over the worker that gave it to her.
immoral_consequence: Carlita is perceived as crazy and rude and promptly removed and barred from the premises.

norm: You shouldn't do things that you can't afford.
situation: Ben is thinking of having a kid but him and his wife are both unemployed.
intention: Ben has to make a decision on whether to have a kid.
moral_action: Ben decides to wait on having a kid until he can find a job.
moral_consequence: Ben doesn't have to worry about taking care of anyone and can focus on himself.
immoral_action: Ben and his wife decide to have the kid while they still don't have jobs.
immoral_consequence: Ben's child suffers, and Ben is overwhelmed with everything he has to do.

norm: It's good to do the right thing.
situation: Ian is walking down the street and sees some money fall out of a woman's pocket.
intention: Ian wants to do something about the money.
moral_action: Ian calls out to the woman and returns the money to her.
moral_consequence: Ian feels proud of himself for making the right choice.
immoral_action: Ian puts the money in his pocket and doesn't tell the woman.
immoral_consequence: Ian later feels guilty about not returning the money.

norm: It's wrong to do things to hurt your spouse
situation: Joe has been invited to go out with his friends to play pool after work but his wife is making dinner for him.
intention: Joe wants to play pool with his friends.
moral_action: Joe goes home, has dinner with his wife, and then goes to the pool hall.
moral_consequence: Joe's wife enjoys having dinner with her husband.
immoral_action: Joe goes to the pool hall and decides he'll deal with his wife later.
immoral_consequence: Joe's wife is very upset when he doesn't come home for dinner.

norm: You shouldn't spy on people.
situation: Brandy just got into an argument with her boyfriend.
intention: Brandy wants to know if her boyfriend is being faithful to her.
moral_action: Brandy asks her boyfriend for proof of his loyalty.
moral_consequence: Brandy's boyfriend shows her texts and images from his recent days, showing her that he was with family.
immoral_action: Brandy waits until her boyfriend isn't looking and spies on him through his texts and messages.
immoral_consequence: Brandy's boyfriend discovers her spying and breaks up with her for her lack of trust.

norm: It's important to return the things you borrow on time.
situation: Ted borrows his classmate's textbook and promises to give it back the very next day.
intention: Ted wants to return his classmate's textbook.
moral_action: Ted gives the textbook back to his classmate early the next day as promised.
moral_consequence: Ted's classmate is able to used the textbook the next day to do their homework.
immoral_action: Ted brings the textbook back to his classmate two days after taking it.
immoral_consequence: Ted's classmate isn't able to do their homework without the textbook and fails the assignment.

norm: You should not call people names.
situation: Sam is in a fight on twitter with another person, and that person gets personal.
intention: Sam wants to react to the other person.
moral_action: Sam decides to block the other person, deciding it isn't worth it.
moral_consequence: Sam is able to carry on with his day, not bothered by anything.
immoral_action: Sam calls the other person a racist name on twitter.
immoral_consequence: Other people find the tweet, and Sam gets fired when it gets sent to his boss.

norm: It's bad to make crude jokes.
situation: Daryl is at a party and there are a lot of pretty ladies attending it.
intention: Daryl wants to impress the girls.
moral_action: Daryl dances uninhibited on the dance floor and motions for some of the ladies to join him.
moral_consequence: Some of the ladies enjoy Daryl's carefree dancing and join him which makes Daryl quite happy.
immoral_action: Daryl repeats a bad taste joke that his friends enjoyed earlier to some of the ladies at the party.
immoral_consequence: The ladies are turned off by the vulgar joke and Daryl is unable to talk to any of them for the rest of the night.

norm: It's not okay to be so lazy it effects others.
situation: Nick was recently laid off from his job, and his girlfriend is currently the sole provider for their household.
intention: Nick wants to live a good life.
moral_action: Nick takes this time to submit applications to jobs he takes interest in, while doing the housework when his girlfriend is at work.
moral_consequence: Nick's girlfriend is extremely grateful and Nick eventually lands his dream job.
immoral_action: Nick enjoys himself by eating junk food and playing video games all day, and doesn't cook, clean, or look for a job while his girlfriend is at work.
immoral_consequence: Nick's girlfriend gets sick of having to do everything around the house and leaves him.

norm: It is good to be polite when saying no.
situation: A homeless man walked up to Jake and asked him if he had any spare change.
intention: Jake wants to respond the the man.
moral_action: Jake tells the man that he doesn't but that he would if he had some on him.
moral_consequence: The man's a little disappointed, but he's glad that Jake was nice about it.
immoral_action: Jake tells the man that he wouldn't give him any change even if he had some.
immoral_consequence: The man's feelings are hurt, and he starts to become depressed.

norm: You should not make light of a tragic event.
situation: Lola's friend's grandmother had just died after she got into a car crash.
intention: Lola wants to send her friend a message on social media.
moral_action: Lola sends her friend a message with a heart saying that she is sorry.
moral_consequence: Lola's friend thanks her for her thoughts and calls her the next day.
immoral_action: Lola sends her friend a meme of a car going up in flames.
immoral_consequence: Lola's friend breaks down into tears and blocks her from social media.

norm: You shouldn't treat someone differently because of their looks.
situation: Kathy is working as a waitress.
intention: Kathy wants to earn a lot of tips.
moral_action: Kathy seats a table of men in tattered clothes, but treats them the same as her other tables.
moral_consequence: The men enjoy a good meal with great service from Kathy.
immoral_action: Kathy seats a table of men in tattered clothes, so she is less attentive to them than her other tables.
immoral_consequence: The men notice that Kathy is not serving them properly and leave to find another restaurant.

norm: You shouldn't do drugs when you're underage.
situation: James feels stressed by the pressures of maintaining his grades and participation in four different extracurricular activities.
intention: James wants to feel less stressed.
moral_action: James tells his parents that he wants to drop two extracurriculars, so he can have a more reasonable schedule.
moral_consequence: James is able to sleep more and occasionally spend time with his friends.
immoral_action: James starts smoking pot, so he'll feel less anxious about all his obligations.
immoral_consequence: James' grades begin to suffer, causing his parents to confront him at least once a week.

norm: You should never pretend you're pregnant.
situation: Jenna is afraid that her boyfriend is going to break up with her even though she's still in love with him.
intention: Jenna wants to avoid breaking up with her boyfriend.
moral_action: Jenna asks her boyfriend what they could do to make their relationship better.
moral_consequence: Jenna's boyfriend says he wishes she listened to him more, and Jenna agrees to try.
immoral_action: Jenna buys a fake pregnancy test off the Internet and tells her boyfriend she's pregnant.
immoral_consequence: Jenna's boyfriend insists on accompanying her to the doctor and finds out she's faking.

norm: You should be professional at work.
situation: Art is in the office, when Bill, the company's CEO walks by.
intention: Art wants to exchange social chit chat with the CEO.
moral_action: Art mentions last night's sports game to Bill.
moral_consequence: Bill recognizes that Art is a steady and capable man with respectful hobbies and considers him for a promotion.
immoral_action: Art tells Bill about his favorite type of pornography in great detail.
immoral_consequence: Bill feels ill at ease with how personal the talk is and fires Art, thinking he may speak this way in front of clients.

norm: It's good to help out your kids with their problems.
situation: Nick is sitting in his living room when his son Alex tells him he can't figure out a math problem in his homework.
intention: Nick wants to respond to Alex's statement.
moral_action: Nick tells Alex to bring his workbook over, so he can take a look and help him figure it out.
moral_consequence: Alex is delighted that his dad will help him and runs off to get his workbook.
immoral_action: Nick tells Alex that he should go online and see if he can find out the answer to the problem.
immoral_consequence: Alex feels abandoned to go off on his own and figure it out and is sad that his father is of no use.

norm: You shouldn't fight others on the street.
situation: Rick is walking home from school down the street when a bully comes up and starts an argument with him.
intention: Rick wants to fight the bully.
moral_action: Rick tells the bully that he'll fight him at a boxing ring in a nearby gym.
moral_consequence: Rick and the bully settle their argument wearing safe gloves and in a private location.
immoral_action: Rick moves in on the bully and begins to fight him before he can make a move.
immoral_consequence: A police car drives by and arrests both Rick and the bully for fighting in public.

norm: It's bad to tell jokes that go too far.
situation: Jim is at a get together with people he doesn't know very well.
intention: Jim wants to make people laugh and show that he has a sense of humor.
moral_action: "Jim tells very lighthearted ""dad"" jokes."
moral_consequence: Everyone laughs at the wholesome jokes.
immoral_action: Jim tells some very offensive jokes to the group.
immoral_consequence: Although some are entertained, others are quite offended and taken back.

norm: It's wrong to lick your dog's eyeball because it's gross.
situation: Stan is playing truth or dare with a group of friends at his house while watching his dog.
intention: Stan wants to impress his friends.
moral_action: Stan picks truth instead of dare and tells a very personal story.
moral_consequence: Stan's friends respect his bravery and courage to speak out in such a personal manner.
immoral_action: Stan's friend laughs out loud and dares him to lick his dog's eyeball.
immoral_consequence: Stan agrees and in the middle of it, his mother walks in sees and yells at him.

norm: It is rude to embarrass a class mate.
situation: Tim is at school and notices that his classmate Bill has a piece of toilet paper stuck to his shoe.
intention: Tim wants to inform Bill about the toilet paper on his shoe.
moral_action: Tim waits until class is over and discretely informs Bill about the toilet paper on his shoe.
moral_consequence: Bill is thankful to Tim and removes the toilet paper without anyone else noticing.
immoral_action: Tim tells Bill that there is toilet paper stuck to his shoe in front of the whole class.
immoral_consequence: Many of the students laugh at Bill, and he feels embarrassed.

norm: It's creepy to catfish a family member.
situation: David is overprotective of his teenage daughter, and he fears that she is too naive.
intention: David wants to make sure his daughter won't let someone take advantage of her.
moral_action: David has a serious conversation with his daughter, explaining to her that she needs to be very careful when dealing with guys.
moral_consequence: David's daughter is thankful for the advice and promises her father to be cautious.
immoral_action: David makes a fake online profile, using the pictures of an attractive guy and starts messaging his daughter to see how she'll react.
immoral_consequence: David's daughter finds out what her father has done and is creeped out by his actions and disappointed in him.

norm: It's good to wait your turn patiently.
situation: Sara is excited for the newest Harry Potter book and makes plans to wait in line for the release.
intention: Sara wants to read the newest Harry Potter book as early as possible.
moral_action: Sara waits her turn and buys the new book that nigiht.
moral_consequence: Sara gets to go home and read until she is done with the new book.
immoral_action: Sara gets impatient in line and offers someone money to let her go in front of them.

norm: it's important to treat family members with respect
situation: Kris is talking with his mom Dana who tells him he needs to get a job.
intention: Kris wants to agree with his mom.
moral_action: Kris tells his mom that he agrees with her and that he's going to double his efforts.
moral_consequence: Dana is happy that her son agrees and is proud of him for saying he's willing to put in extra effort to find a job.
immoral_action: Kris tells his mom that she's stating the obvious and that he's not an idiot, and she should shut up and let him do his thing.
immoral_consequence: Dana is shocked that her son is so callous and angry with him for speaking to her that way.

norm: It's rude to get someone's car towed.
situation: Jane has borrowed her mom's car to go shopping, and she notices an empty spot right in front of the store, next to a fire hydrant.

norm: It's rude to masturbate in the presence of others.
situation: Louis is in a position of power and is meeting a person working under him he finds attractive.

norm: It's immoral to show up for work when you're intoxicated.
situation: Sara has stayed up all night drinking and is still intoxicated when it's time to come into work.

moral_consequence: Sara stays home to recover and still gets paid for the day.

norm: It's not okay to use violence to solve your problems.
situation: Nicole is high school freshman who has been dealing kids blocking her locker every day just to chat.

norm: It is inappropriate to snoop on other people.
situation: Alexa is home alone because her best friend and roommate is out on a date.
intention: Alexa wants to avoid being bored.
moral_action: Alexa decides to find a TV show to watch and relaxes on the couch until her friend comes back from her date.
moral_consequence: Alexa's best friend gets the thrill of telling Alexa all the details of her date.
immoral_action: Alexa decides to go to the same bar she knows her best friend went on a date to and watches the date from across the room.
immoral_consequence: Alexa's friend eventually notices Alexa and feels that Alexa has lost some of her trust.

norm: It's wrong to force someone to talk to you
situation: Brad is at a bar and talking to a woman who says she has to get home as it's late.
intention: Brad wants to continue talking to the woman.
moral_action: Brad asks the woman for her number, so he can call her.
