immoral_action: Brad corners the woman and prevents her from leaving, so he can keep talking to her.
immoral_consequence: The woman will get a bouncer to help her get Brad away from her.

norm: It's polite to tell someone before you leave.
situation: Marge is at a party and finds out that her kids at home need help.
intention: Marge wants to go home quickly.

moral_consequence: The host says that it's fine and understands Marge's dilemma.

norm: It's not okay to be reckless in life.

moral_action: Dan chooses a reasonable amount of money to play with during his time in the casino.
moral_consequence: Dan enjoys a wonderful time at the casino with his friends.

norm: It's important to let your body recover from surgery.

immoral_consequence: Jacob ends up back in the hospital with complications, prolonging his recovery.

norm: It's immoral to harm a defenseless animal.
situation: Sally is home alone with her children when a raccoon gets into their house.

norm: You shouldn't hit your pets.

norm: It's bad to plagiarize other people's work.

intention: Kara wants to finish writing her research paper.

moral_consequence: The professor praises Kara's paper and gives her an A for the class.

norm: You should not call people rude names.
situation: Lina often chats with her coworker, Terry, who has been complaining about her toddler's recent tantrums.

moral_action: "Lina tells Terry she just needs to reveal the ""angel"" within her child by speaking with a child therapist."
moral_consequence: Terry thanks Lina and goes forth with seeking help.
immoral_action: "Lina calls Terry's toddler an ""out of control animal"" and tells her she should seek a child therapist."
immoral_consequence: Terry is hurt by Lina's labeling of her child and never speaks to her again.

norm: It is kind to give advice to a tourist.

intention: Hunter wants to make good time on his jog.
moral_action: Hunter gives the stranger quick directions before continuing with his jog.
moral_consequence: Hunter finishes his jog in good time and the stranger finds his destination without getting lost.
immoral_action: Trying to keep his jog on time, Hunter tells the stranger he does not know where the street is, even though he does.
immoral_consequence: The stranger gets lost looking for the street.

norm: You shouldn't do things you don't enjoy.

moral_consequence: Bob starts looking for a different show to watch and entertain him.
immoral_action: Bob keeps watching the show because it's part of his routine.
immoral_consequence: Bob went on watching the show until he finally passed away of old age.

norm: It's important to accommodate the needs of everyone.
situation: Bob is an architect and is designing a building when his manager Rick asks him where he intends to put the wheelchair ramps.
intention: Bob wants to respond to Rick's question.
moral_action: Bob tells Rick that the wheelchair ramps will fan out in both directions from each entrance symmetrically.
moral_consequence: Rick is pleased that Bob has put so much thought into every detail of the design.
immoral_action: Bob tells Rick that he won't put in any wheelchair ramps since they're ugly and will ruin his beautiful design.
immoral_consequence: Rick is concerned that Bob doesn't understand reality and is rather disgusted how little thought Bob has for disabled people.

norm: It's wrong to fire your employees for no reason.
situation: Bill was mad at his wife for always running their clothing store how she wanted and now they were losing money.

moral_action: Bill told his employee Sue that they had to make cutbacks because they were losing money, and he had to let her go.
moral_consequence: Sue said she understood, she thought the store wasn't doing to well lately.
immoral_action: Bill told the last employee his wife hired, Sue, that she was fired, without telling her why.
immoral_consequence: Sue started to cry because she thought she had been doing a good job.

norm: It's good for people to help their children.

intention: Carlton wants to make sure his kid completes the homework.
moral_action: Carlton works through the homework with his child making sure it understands everything until they finish.
moral_consequence: Carlton's child gets a good grasp on the lesson and performs well in school.
immoral_action: Carlton makes it clear to his child that they must complete their homework and doesn't listen to any requests for assistance from the child.
immoral_consequence: Carlton's child just fills in the homework with gibberish because it can't figure it out which leads to a failing grade in class.

norm: Violence is an unacceptable way to handle things.
situation: Xavier and Alexander fighting on the playground, and Alexander spits in Xavier's face.
intention: Xavier wants to stand up for himself.

moral_consequence: Xavier earns the respect of Alexander and the other students.

norm: You shouldn't put holes in your apartment walls.

moral_action: Jill uses a mild and safe adhesive to hang the pictures.
moral_consequence: Jill has avoiding damaging the apartment walls.

immoral_consequence: Jill has damaged the walls of the apartment.

norm: You shouldn't hit your spouse.
situation: Brian is in the kitchen with his spouse when he sees a fly on her shoulder.

moral_consequence: The fly leaves Brian's spouse's shoulder, and she is grateful.
immoral_action: Brian slaps his spouse's shoulder that has the fly.
immoral_consequence: Brian's spouse gets upset that he hit her.

norm: It's wrong not to be happy for your friends.
situation: John is meeting up with a friend who told john that they had some exciting news.

immoral_action: John finds out that his friend is getting married but doesn't show any outward emotions because he is jealous of his friend.
immoral_consequence: John's friend is disappointed in John's reaction and his mood is soured.

norm: It's bad to make impulsive decisions.
situation: Kris is out shopping for a car at a used-car lot.

moral_consequence: Kris enjoys driving her new car for many trouble-free years.
immoral_action: Kris walks up to the first car that catches her eye and agrees to buy it on the spot.
immoral_consequence: Kris spends a lot of money repairing the lemon that she bought.

norm: You shouldn't allow running in the halls.

moral_consequence: The proposal is adopted and there a fewer tardy slips written during school hours.
immoral_action: Sal proposes that children be encouraged to run through the halls to get to class quicker.
immoral_consequence: The proposal is adopted and mayhem ensues between classes with children running into each other and causing injuries.

norm: It's mean to abuse your grandchildren.

moral_consequence: Tony quickly snaps back into a good child when he realizes his parents will find out about this.

immoral_consequence: Tony is traumatized and scared of being alone in the dark and damp attic all day.

norm: It is bad to bite your arm.

immoral_action: Doug bites his arm to get the food off of it and into his mouth.
immoral_consequence: Doug injures his arm by biting too hard and Doug has to get a bandage.

norm: It's not okay to spy on others or be sneaky.

moral_consequence: Susan answers honestly that she has never cheated on AJ.

norm: It's not okay to let your friend drive drunk.

moral_consequence: Wendy drives Roland home and drops him off safe and sound.

immoral_consequence: Ronald tries to drive home by himself, and he gets arrested by the cops.

norm: It is not healthy to cling to old relationships.

moral_consequence: Denise becomes good friends with her blind date.
immoral_action: Darwin continues dating Denise.
immoral_consequence: Denise is trapped in a relationship with someone who doesn't love her.

norm: Adults should not still have imaginary friends.

norm: It's good to quit drinking if you have a problem.

intention: Bev wants to decide whether to drink or not.
moral_action: Bev decides to not drink and to sleep extra.

norm: You should not judge the weight of others.
situation: Brady is in his office at work when he is introduced to his new manager Pam who is quite obese.
intention: Brady wants to say something to Pam.
moral_action: Brady tells Pam that he's glad to meet her and looks forward to creating a good working relationship with her.
moral_consequence: Pam is delighted to hear Brady talk about a good working relationship, and she's happy that he seems so professional.
immoral_action: Brady tells Pam that he cannot take direction from her since her weight makes it obvious she has no self control or discipline.
immoral_consequence: Pam is insulted and is infuriated that she's being dismissed as a leader because of her physical size.

norm: It's bad to be addicted to something illicit.
situation: Ron is working a long shift at the office and is beginning to get bored and sleepy around mid afternoon.
intention: Ron wants to feel more energetic.
moral_action: Ron goes to the office break room and makes himself a cup of coffee.
moral_consequence: Ron soon feels refreshed and energized and becomes more engaged in his work.
immoral_action: Ron pulls a small bag out of his pocket and does a couple lines of cocaine off of his desk.
immoral_consequence: Ron is fired for consuming illicit drugs on the job and reported to the police.

norm: It's bad to misrepresent yourself to get a date.
situation: Joshua, a truck driver, is perusing online female dating ads and sees Jessica, a girl he really likes.
intention: Joshua wants Jessica, an online date, to like him.
moral_action: Joshua is honest with Jessica and comes off confident in himself and compliments her.
moral_consequence: Jessica may date him and if something develops the relationship should blossom.
immoral_action: Joshua tells Jessica he is a doctor and makes 200000 dollars a year.
immoral_consequence: Jessica may date him at first until she realizes he is poor and lied, then dumps him fast.

norm: It's wrong to sleep with your subordinates.
situation: Susan asks John, who manages the office that Susan works at, out on a date right in front of the whole office.
intention: John wants to respond to Susan's offer.
moral_action: John tells Susan that he doesn't think it's such a great idea for them to see each other on a personal level.
moral_consequence: The other office workers gain respect for John and feel secure knowing that they have a good and professional boss.
immoral_action: John tells Susan that he's always found her attractive and that he'd love to take her out and maybe more.
immoral_consequence: The other office workers are suddenly scared that Susan will jump ahead in status at work to their detriment.

norm: It is good to care for other living things.
situation: Kennedy is running home when she sees an injured cat laying in her front yard.
intention: Kennedy wants to interact with the cat.
moral_action: Kennedy takes the cat to the vet, and fosters him until she finds him a new home.
moral_consequence: Kennedy ends up becoming friends with the cat's new owners.
immoral_action: Kennedy pushes the cat onto the neighbors yard and calls animal control.
immoral_consequence: Kennedy's neighbors scold her for her actions.

norm: It's bad to date someone who is underage.
situation: Dave who is an adult is mowing his lawn when his neighbor's seventeen year old daughter asks him on a date.
intention: Dave wants to respond to the neighbor's date offer.
moral_action: Dave tells the neighbor girl that he's flattered but that she should find someone her own age to take her out.
moral_consequence: The neighbor girl is happy to hear that Dave feels flattered and thinks it's a good suggestion to find a boy her age.
immoral_action: Dave tells the neighbor girl that he'd love to take her out and maybe buy her a drink.
immoral_consequence: The neighbor girl is initially delighted but later comes to find that the power imbalance in the relationship is majorly stressful.

norm: You should not control your partner's appearance.
situation: Cladwell buys his girlfriend Rachel a dress two sizes too small for a party.
intention: Cladwell wants them to look like an attractive couple.
moral_action: Cladwell takes Rachel to a high end dress store offering to buy something she likes.
moral_consequence: Rachel's confidence is boosted, and she makes new friends at the party.
immoral_action: Cladwell pressures Rachel into wearing the dress.
immoral_consequence: Rachel gets rashes all over her body from the dress digging into her skin.

norm: You shouldn't touch your coworkers.
situation: Becca is happy that her favorite coworker is finally back from going on vacation.
intention: Becca wants to greet and welcome the coworker back.
moral_action: Becca buys her coworker her favorite coffee drink giving it to her while welcoming her back.
moral_consequence: Becca has made a good impression on her coworker and maintained professionalism.
immoral_action: Becca runs up and embraces her coworker in a tight hug.
immoral_consequence: Becca may be seen as unprofessional by her work peers and boss.

norm: It's wrong not to get your children haircuts.
situation: Gunther is a single father and school picture day is coming up soon.
intention: Gunther wants his son to look good for the school photo's.
moral_action: Gunther takes his son to the barber and get's him a really nice haircut for picture day.
moral_consequence: Gunther's son get's complimented by all the other kids for his haircut.
immoral_action: Gunther dresses up his son nicely but keeps his hair long.
immoral_consequence: Gunther's son is the only boy with long hair and gets made fun of.

norm: It's wrong to dispose of other people's belongings.
situation: John who had borrowed Phil's pen and is walking down the street, wearing a backpack when he notices the pen in his pocket.
intention: John wants to remove the pen from his pocket and put it somewhere else.
moral_action: John puts the pen in his backpack, so he can eventually return it back to his friend later when he gets home.
moral_consequence: John's friend is delighted that John treats his property with respect and care.
immoral_action: John takes the pen and tosses is in the garbage because he's afraid it'll leak in his pocket.
immoral_consequence: John's friend is hurt that John just threw away something he had lent him and loses trust in John.

norm: It's bad to ignore your friends.
situation: Terra is busy using her phone for work and her friend keeps texting her.
intention: Terra wants to focus her work assignment.
moral_action: Terra quickly shoots her friend a text back saying she will get back to her after work.
moral_consequence: Terra's friend waits for her to get off of work and stops texting.
immoral_action: Terra ignores her friend's messages and continues working on the assignment.
immoral_consequence: Terra's friend continues to text wondering why she is not responding.

norm: It's good to hang out with friends.
situation: Paul is home on a Saturday night and gets a text from his friends inviting him to a bar.
intention: Paul wants to decide what to do with his Saturday night.
moral_action: Paul accepts the invitation from his friends and meets them at the bar.
moral_consequence: Paul's friends have a good time hanging out with Paul and invite him to a concert the next weekend.
immoral_action: Paul declines the invitation from his friends and spends the night watching TV at home.
immoral_consequence: Paul's friends think Paul isn't interested in hanging out with them, and they stop inviting him out on weekends.

norm: You shouldn't hide injuries from people.
situation: Finnegan just got home from soccer practice during which he injured his knee, when his parents ask him how his day was.
intention: Finnegan wants to respond to his parents.
moral_action: Finnegan tells his parents about his day in detail, including the injury he sustained during soccer practice.
moral_consequence: Finnegan gets some advice from his parents on how to treat the injury temporarily until he can be seen by his doctor.
immoral_action: Finnegan tells his parents that he had a great and uneventful day, purposefully not mentioning his injury so that he doesn't worry them.
immoral_consequence: Finnegan develops complications from his knee injury that require hospitalization.

norm: You shouldn't let your partner control your friendships or you.
situation: Jane is at home with her significant other.
intention: Jane wants to know what her significant other wants to do that night.
moral_action: Jane goes out with friends after her significant other complains about them.
moral_consequence: Jane avoids a dangerous relationship after her friends convince her to break things off.
immoral_action: Jane stays home with her significant other because they were ranting about not trusting Jane's friends.
immoral_consequence: Jane's significant other eventually begins to physically abuse her.

norm: It is wrong to date a minor.
situation: Joe is talking in an online chat room.
intention: Joe wants to meet a person to have intimate relations with.
moral_action: Joe arranges a date with a 30-year old woman.
moral_consequence: Joe has a wonderful time on his date.
immoral_action: Joe agrees to meet a 15-year old girl for a sexual encounter.
immoral_consequence: Joes is arrested for pedophilia.

norm: It's good to help people with car troubles.
situation: Ed was driving home from church when he noticed a car with the hood open.
intention: Ed wants to offer the man some help with his car.
moral_action: Ed pulls over in order to help the man with their car.
moral_consequence: The man's car is eventually fixed, and the man gets to stop worrying.
immoral_action: Ed opens his window and tells the man to call 9-1-1.
immoral_consequence: The man didn't have his phone on him so the advice didn't help him at all.

norm: You shouldn't be too hard on your employees
situation: A person that works for Bob comes in five minutes late one morning.
intention: Bob wants to let his employee know that he doesn't like them being late.
moral_action: Bob explains that it's important for everyone to be on time and asks the employee to make an effort not to be late.
moral_consequence: The employee thinks Bob's reaction to their lateness is fair, and they try not to be late again.
immoral_action: Bob yells at the employee and threatens to fire them if they are even one minute late in the future.
immoral_consequence: Bob's employee thinks Bob's reaction was way to harsh, and they start to dislike working for him.

norm: It's wrong to want to live in violent neighborhood.
situation: Bo currently lives in the hood and wants to buy a new house, but the house he wants is in a white neighborhood.
intention: Bo wants to decide where his family should live.
moral_action: Bo decides to move his family to the white neighborhood.
moral_consequence: Bo's family is not at risk of being harmed anymore and are better off.
immoral_action: Bo decides to keep his family in the hood so that his kids can see people who look like them.
immoral_consequence: Bo's family is at risk of being victims of crimes the more they stay there.

norm: It's wrong for merchants to deceive customers.
situation: Peter is selling used appliances and has some customers looking at a dishwasher that he knows doesn't work properly.
intention: Peter wants to make the sale.
moral_action: Peter admits that the dishwasher has issues and offers to give the customers a large enough discount to cover repairs.
moral_consequence: The customers are grateful for the offer, buy the dishwasher, and become loyal customers of Peter's.
immoral_action: Peter tells the customers that the dishwasher works great and guarantees they'll like it.
immoral_consequence: The customers find out that the dishwasher doesn't work later that night and leave Peter a terrible Yelp review.

norm: It's wrong to use violence against living things.
situation: Bobby is visiting his neighbor when the neighbor's little dog starts nipping at his heels.
intention: Bobby wants to get the dog to stop nipping at him.
moral_action: Bobby asks his neighbor to please put his dog somewhere where it can't get at Bobby.
moral_consequence: The little dog is made to stop nipping at Bobby without any harm coming to it.
immoral_action: Bobby kicks the little dog all the way across the room and it runs away.
immoral_consequence: The little dog is hurt and scared by Bobby's action.

norm: It's hurtful to not like your mother.
situation: Troy and Dana are planning their wedding when Dana asks Troy why he hasn't mentioned inviting his mom.
intention: Troy wants to tell Dana about his relationship with his mom.
moral_action: Troy tells Dana that he loves his mom very much, and he hasn't mentioned it because he thought it was obvious she'd come.
moral_consequence: Dana is relieved to hear that Troy's mom will come to their big day and that there's no problems in their relationship.
immoral_action: Troy tells Dana that his mother, and he don't talk and that he despises her and always has.
immoral_consequence: Dana is shocked to hear that Troy doesn't talk to his mom and wonders what's wrong with him.

norm: It is wrong to mock your relationship partners physical appearance.
situation: Vin's partner has been eating too much and putting on a lot of weight.
intention: Vin wants to change his partner's current habits.
moral_action: Vin arranges that they go on frequent hiking trips.
moral_consequence: Vin's partner gets in better shape and becomes healthier.
immoral_action: Vin pokes fun at his partner's weight gain.
immoral_consequence: Vin's partner feels less wanted.

norm: You shouldn't cook for people if you're ill.
situation: Beatrice has the flu, but she promised to help her mother prepare supper.
intention: Beatrice wants to avoid disappointing people.
moral_action: Beatrice orders food for her family from uber eats.
moral_consequence: Beatrice's family has a nice family bonding night as they talk while they eat.
immoral_action: Beatrice pretends to be healthy, and she helps her mother out in the kitchen.
immoral_consequence: Beatrice entire family becomes sick after eating an infected meal.

norm: It's good to encourage other people
situation: Matt sees his friend Ian out jogging.
intention: Matt wants to make small talk with Ian.
moral_action: Matt jogs along with Ian for a bit, chatting about how impressive Ian's commitment to fitness is.
moral_consequence: Ian continues to jog everyday, getting in better shape.
immoral_action: Matt makes fun of Ian for how lame a hobby jogging is.
immoral_consequence: Ian stops jogging, growing morbidly obese.

norm: It is wrong to tamper with someone's prescribed medications
situation: Phil wants to start a family with his wife May, but she is hesitant.
intention: Phil wants to have a baby.
moral_action: Phil makes a persuasive argument for the couple starting a family.
moral_consequence: May becomes more comfortable with the idea of having a child.
immoral_action: Phil switches out May's birth control medication.
immoral_consequence: May feels betrayed when she discovers the deception.

norm: It's rude to break things that belong to someone else.
situation: Ted is at his friend Nick's house, watching Nick try to open his piggy bank.
intention: Ted wants to help Nick get the money inside.
moral_action: Ted takes a knife and prys off the bottom rubber seal on the piggy bank.
moral_consequence: Nick gets his money and learns how to open the piggy bank properly.
immoral_action: Ted takes the piggy bank, goes outside, and throws it on the sidewalk, shattering it.
immoral_consequence: Nick gets the money but now needs a new piggy bank.

norm: It's inappropriate to brag about yourself too much to others.
situation: Kenny is on the high school baseball team and hit three home runs during the game.
intention: Kenny wants to tell his friends about his performance.
moral_action: Kenny tells his friends about his home runs once, when he sees them after the game.
moral_consequence: Kenny's friends will think Kenny is a very good player.
immoral_action: Kenny tells his friends about his home runs every day of the week.
immoral_consequence: Kenny's friends will become annoyed with Kenny and think he brags too much.

norm: People expect their friends to help with their big events.
situation: Dave is on the phone with his friend Phil who invites Dave to a party the next day and asks him to come early to help set up.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Phil's invitation.
moral_action: Dave tells Phil he'll definitely come early and help Phil set up and stay for the party.
moral_consequence: Phil is delighted that Dave is willing to pitch in and that he's not a selfish friend.
immoral_action: Dave tells Phil he'll come to the party, but he has some other plans beforehand, so he can't help set up.
immoral_consequence: Phil is annoyed that Dave only wants to attend the fun part of the evening and refuses to pitch in.

norm: It's respectable to take good care of other peoples belongings.
situation: John has lent his friend Phil his watch and is standing by Phil as Phil is holding the watch.
intention: Phil wants to put the watch in his backpack which is on the floor.
moral_action: Phil gently places the watch inside his backpack taking care to make sure it's wrapped around a towel so it doesn't get scratched.
moral_consequence: John is happy to see that his friend will take care of his belongings and doesn't have to stress about getting it back intact.
immoral_action: Phil looks at the backpack and throws the watch into it from quite a distance away, watching it crash at high speed into the bag.
immoral_consequence: John is horrified that his friend is basically trying to break the watch and feels utterly disrespected by Phil's carelessness.

norm: It's good to be honest with friends.
situation: Best friends Melody and Daisy are chatting, and Daisy is asking Melody what she thinks of her new outfit, which Melody believes looks bad.
intention: Melody wants Daisy to feel good about herself.
moral_action: Melody tells Daisy that she doesn't think that the outfit suits her body shape that well while pointing out Daisy's most beautiful features, suggesting she emphasize those.
moral_consequence: Daisy thanks Melody for her honesty and uses her advice to improve her appearance.
immoral_action: Melody tells Daisy that she looks great in the new outfit and that she should wear it with confidence.
immoral_consequence: Daisy gains a boost of self-esteem and feels a lot better about her choice in clothing.

norm: It's not okay to put someone one the spot.
situation: Randy is having lunch with coworkers and witnesses one of them lying to another.
intention: Randy wants to find out why his coworker lied to the the other one.
moral_action: Randy waits to ask his coworker about it later in private.
moral_consequence: Randy's coworkers are none the wiser, and they have an enjoyable lunch.
immoral_action: Randy calls out his coworker in front of all the others.
immoral_consequence: Randy's coworker is extremely embarrassed and his coworkers lose trust in him.

norm: It's rude to park in front of your neighbor's house.
situation: Sam has just arrived home and realized that someone has taken his usual parking spot.
intention: Sam wants to park near his house.
moral_action: Sam parks in front of his own driveway blocking the other cars in.
moral_consequence: Sam's neighbor notices this, and he asks the others not to park in his spot.
immoral_action: Sam parks in front of his next door neighbor's house taking up their spot.
immoral_consequence: Sam's neighbor has to park even further away from their house.

norm: It's good to be sociable
situation: Bryan runs out to the store to pick up a few things and notices a friend in one of the aisles that he hasn't seen for a while.
intention: Bryan has to decide whether to say hello to his friend.
moral_action: Bryan walks over to his friend and greets him, standing for a few minutes to talk.
moral_consequence: Bryan is happy that he had a chance to catch up with his friend and feels that he achieved a lot on his trip to the store.
immoral_action: Bryan quickly scurries out of the aisle before his friend sees him and heads toward the checkout, so he can leave before his friend sees him.
immoral_consequence: Bryan feels ashamed of his behavior at the store and later on wishes that he had talked with his friend.

norm: You shouldn't be negligent with other people's property.
situation: Jordan is baking lots of food but ran out of baking soda, and his neighbors have a lot of extra food.
intention: Jordan wants to use his neighbors baking soda.
moral_action: Jordan uses only some of his neighbors baking soda and returns the rest.
moral_consequence: Jordan is thanked for being careful with the food, and they invite him over for dinner.
immoral_action: Jordan uses all of his neighbors baking soda because of a spill and returns the empty can.
immoral_consequence: Jordan's neighbors feel insulted for his misuse and James apologizes.

norm: It's rude not to clean up after yourself.
situation: John is playing with his toys and his grandma's house.
intention: John wants to have fun playing games all day.
moral_action: John finishes one game and puts all his toys back where they belong before going outside for a new game.
moral_consequence: John's grandma appreciates the cleanup and join John outside playing with him.
immoral_action: John doesn't clean up his toys from one game indoors before starting to play another game in the backyard.
immoral_consequence: John's grandma calls him back inside to clean up his mess and doesn't allow him back outside as punishment.

norm: You should be able to leave if you want to
situation: Mark's girlfriend Catherine is over but it's almost time for an appointment she needs to go to.
intention: Mark wants dinner.
moral_action: Mark lets Catherine leave and makes his own dinner.
moral_consequence: Catherine is glad he is letting her make her own choices.
immoral_action: Mark forces Catherine to stay and make him dinner.
immoral_consequence: Catherine thinks Mark is too controlling.

norm: You shouldn't fake a broken bone.
situation: Debbie hurt her arm a few days past and it feels better, but she's tired and wants some time off from work.
intention: Debbie wants to go home and sleep.
moral_action: Debbie goes to her boss and tells her that she would like to take a sick day because she did not get enough rest.
moral_consequence: Debbie's boss is understanding and lets Debbie take the rest of the day off.
immoral_action: Debbie tells her boss she fell in the bathroom and thinks she broke her arm, so Debbie's boss tells her to go.
immoral_consequence: Debbie's boss finds out that Debbie didn't go to the doctor and told another coworker that she wasn't honest about her injury, so she fires Debbie.

norm: You should stick up for your family.
situation: Greg is with his mother Barb at the mall when a strange, drunken man approaches and calls his mother fat.
intention: Greg wants to respond to the insult.
moral_action: Greg tells the drunken man that he better apologize before Greg removes his tongue.
moral_consequence: Barb is delighted that her son is sticking up for her and feel safe with him by her side.
immoral_action: Greg tells the drunken man that his mom could definitely stand to lose some weight and is glad someone agrees.
immoral_consequence: Barb is insulted that her son is agreeing with the belligerent drunken man accosting her.

norm: It's good to pursue interests that bring you joy
situation: Hector is bored, loves activity, and is looking into hobbies to pick up.
intention: Hector wants to choose a new hobby.
moral_action: Hector buys a bike and goes mountain biking.
moral_consequence: Hector has a blast cruising over trails and through forests.
immoral_action: Hector buys a microscope and makes microbiology his hobby.
immoral_consequence: Hector gets tired of sitting and looking at weird, tiny creatures.

norm: It's good to be thoughtful when proposing marriage.
situation: Jerry and Kat have been dating since they were in high school.
intention: Jerry wants to ask Kat to marry him.
moral_action: Jerry presents a beautiful ring to Kat and asks her to marry him on her birthday at the beach.
moral_consequence: Kat agrees to marry him, and they get married the next year.
immoral_action: Jerry asks Kat to marry him in the middle of a card game without even having a ring.
immoral_consequence: Kat laughs in his face and tells him that he needs to try harder.

norm: It is wrong to post movie spoilers publicly.
situation: Jeff is participating in an online forum about a TV show he just finished watching.
intention: Jeff wants to know how other participants feel about the ending of the show.
moral_action: Jeff posts a large and very visible SPOILER title at the beginning of his post to warn others.
moral_consequence: Participants who have not watched the finale yet skip Jeff's comments when they see the title and can enjoy the show's finale.
immoral_action: Jeff discusses the ending of the show on the forum, revealing it to all those who read the thread.
immoral_consequence: Participants who have not watched the finale yet are disappointed by the spoiler, which ruins their experience of the last episode.

norm: It's bad to be late for dinner.
situation: Josh is playing soccer in the backyard with some friends and his mother Janet yells from the window, to be inside to eat in 15 minutes.
intention: Josh wants to finish playing soccer.
moral_action: Josh makes on last goal then tells his friends they can all meet up to play ball again tomorrow.
moral_consequence: Josh is able to sit down with his mom, and he enjoys a nice hot meal.
immoral_action: Having fun playing ball, Josh loses track of time and comes in to eat an hour later than he was supposed to.
immoral_consequence: Josh is scolded by his mom, and now has to eat a cold meal that doesn't taste very good.

norm: It is wrong to throw a tantrum.
situation: John is a child that is out on a shopping trip with his mother.
intention: John wants ice cream on the way home.
moral_action: John behaves in public the entire shopping trip and only asks for ice cream when his mother says they are all done and going home.
moral_consequence: John's mother who is happily impressed with his behavior, buys him ice cream on the way home.
immoral_action: Thinking only of the ice cream John begins to whine and scream for his mother to finish shopping, so they can go get the ice cream.
immoral_consequence: Because of John's tantrum his mother decides he does not deserve ice cream, and they go straight home without John getting ice cream.

norm: You should see your doctor regularly.
situation: Mary has been experiencing intense cramps and vaginal bleeding even though she has menopause.
intention: Mary wants the pain to go away.
moral_action: Mary gets some tests done by her doctor and make a followup appointment for next month.
moral_consequence: Mary continues to followup with her doctor and go to her appointments until her illness goess away.
immoral_action: Mary takes some pain pills and ignores the problem.
immoral_consequence: Mary's health issues do not go away, causing her continued pain.

norm: It's good to celebrate important times with good cheer.
situation: Greg's wife is finishing her education and wants to celebrate with a night out, so she makes a reservation at a restaurant.
intention: Greg wants to go with his wife to celebrate.
moral_action: Greg goes to the dinner, makes several toasts to his wife's success, and works hard to enjoy the opportunity.
moral_consequence: Greg's wife also has a good time and is grateful for all of Greg's support and enthusiasm.
immoral_action: Greg goes with her but stays aloof from the festivities, watching from afar.
immoral_consequence: Greg's wife thinks that something is wrong in him and is disappointed that he's apparently not happy for her.

norm: It's rude to take candy without permission.
situation: Lisa sees a candy dish at her friend's house.
intention: Lisa wants some candy.
moral_action: Lisa asks her friend if she can have a piece of candy.
moral_consequence: Lisa's friend thanks her for asking and tells her to take as much as she'd like.
immoral_action: Lisa sneaks handfuls of candy and puts them in her pocket.
immoral_consequence: Lisa is caught and now her friend no longer trusts her.

norm: It's good to have a positive self image.
situation: Neo does poorly at the track meet and is thinking heavily about it afterward.
intention: Neo wants to decide what to do about his performance.
moral_action: Neo decides to suck it up and talk with teammates about his role.
moral_consequence: Neo learns a lesson and develops a team attitude.
immoral_action: Neo degrades himself and decides to quit the team.
immoral_consequence: Neo's self-esteem is hurt and he loses confidence.

norm: It's bad to use your phone while driving.
situation: Cody gets bored driving home from work the same route every day.
intention: Cody wants to call his girlfriend.
moral_action: Cody decides that he shouldn't use his phone while driving and waits until he gets home to call his girlfriend.
moral_consequence: Cody arrives safely home and does not cause any accidents.
immoral_action: Cody calls his girlfriend while driving home from work, so he's not bored.
immoral_consequence: Cody is distracted from being on the phone and hits the car stopped in front of him at the light.

norm: It's rude to block your family on social media.
situation: Tami has been engaged in a heated argument with her sister on facebook.
intention: Tami wants to put an end to the argument.
moral_action: Tami just stops responding and gives it some time to cool off.
moral_consequence: Tami's sister is willing to forget about the whole thing and brush it off.
immoral_action: Tami blocks her sister so that she cannot respond to her anymore.
immoral_consequence: Tami's sister cannot believe that her own sister blocked her, and they have a worse relationship.

norm: It is rude to call somebody a bitch.
situation: Phil does not get along with a female coworker who constantly antagonizes him.
intention: Phil wants to get his coworker to leave him alone.
moral_action: Phil refuses to get drawn into further altercations with his coworker and approaches HR about her attitude.
moral_consequence: Phil is able to acheive a workable relationship with his coworker after HR intervenes.
immoral_action: Phil is drawn into an argument with his coworker and in anger he calls her a bitch.
immoral_consequence: Phil is reprimanded when his coworker reports him.

norm: You shouldn't do unpleasant things at work.
situation: Fred works for a social media company and is offered a better-paying job as a mature content reviewer.
intention: Fred wants to give a response to the promotion offer.
moral_action: Fred decides that he wants to move in a different direction and declines the promotion.
moral_consequence: Fred pursues a line of work that fits his desires better and eventually is promoted into it.
immoral_action: Fred is attracted by the extra money and accepts the promotion.
immoral_consequence: The mature content traumatizes Fred, and he spends the extra income on therapy bills.

norm: You shouldn't keep an animal that doesn't' belong to you.
situation: Rachael picks up a dog walking down the street, and notices the contact information of the dog's owner written on her collar.
intention: Rachael wants to be close to the dog.
moral_action: Rachael returns the dog to its owners asking if she could foster him when they're not around.
moral_consequence: Rachael ends up getting paid as the family's official dog sitter.
immoral_action: Rachael tosses the collar in the trashcan adopting the dog.
immoral_consequence: Rachael gets in trouble with the owners who spot her walking the dog a week later.

norm: You shouldn't laugh at things that aren't funny.
situation: John watches a classmate trip and injure herself.
intention: John wants to respond to the incident.
moral_action: John responds with a serious expression and offers assistance to the girl.
moral_consequence: The girl thanks John for his kindness and becomes friendly with John.
immoral_action: John laughs at the girl that fell over.
immoral_consequence: The girl and the rest of the class starts disliking John.

norm: It's rude to swear at your neighbors.
situation: Maddie's neighbor often walks their dog through Maddie's lawn and doesn't pick up the dog's poop.
intention: Maddie wants her neighbor to clean up after their dog.
moral_action: Maddie asks her neighbor to please pick up her dog's poop.

norm: You should respect your parents and not say rude things.

norm: You should be extra careful when driving someone else's car.

immoral_action: Gabe takes the car on the highway and accelerates as fast as he can from 0 to 100 MPH.

norm: It is wrong to contaminate food that people eat.
situation: Judy will attend a potluck party tomorrow held in the church she usually goes to.
intention: Judy wants to prepare a mango cake for the party.
moral_action: Judy washes all the ingredients, wears gloves and starts making the cake.

immoral_action: Judy doesn't wash her hands before touching the ingredients and making the cake.

norm: It's good to take a walk on the beach.
situation: Michael wants to strengthen his feet, so he could get into barefoot hiking.
intention: Michael wants to go for a walk barefoot.
moral_action: Michael decides to go for a walk on the sand at the beach.
moral_consequence: Michael gets a good workout, while strengthening his feet, and enjoys his time.
immoral_action: Michael decides to walk around his neighborhood barefoot for a bit.
immoral_consequence: Michael steps on a shard of glass he didn't see and cuts his foot open.

norm: You shouldn't stalk someone based on their race.
situation: Jim sees a strange black man in his neighborhood.
intention: Jim wants to feel safe.
moral_action: Jim approaches the man and introduces himself.
moral_consequence: Jim gives the man directions and meets a new person.
immoral_action: Jim follows the man around the neighborhood with his phone set to dial 911.
immoral_consequence: The man calls the police on Jim fearing that he is going to be harmed and Jim is embarrassed.

norm: It's good to help people who are affected by earthquakes.
situation: Frank lives near an earthquake zone when a relative tells him that his house was damaged by a quake.
intention: Frank wants to console the relative.
moral_action: Frank invites the man to stay at his place until he can fix up his own or rent a new place.
moral_consequence: The relative has a house to stay in until he gets back on his feet.
immoral_action: Frank tells the relative that quakes happen all the time and that he'll bounce back from it.
immoral_consequence: The relative has no home for two weeks.

norm: It's good to show your appreciation for gifts.
situation: Veronica was recently promoted at work so her friend Joey sent her congratulatory flowers.
intention: Veronica wants to let Joey know that the flowers arrived safely.
moral_action: Veronica calls Joey and thanks her for the flowers.
moral_consequence: Joey is happy to have done what she did for her friend.
immoral_action: "Veronica sends Joey a text reading ""flowers came"" and nothing else."
immoral_consequence: Joey thinks that Veronica did not like the flowers.

norm: It's good to tell someone when they're being ripped off.
situation: Jenny works at an electronics store that has items of varying price.
intention: Jenny wants to ring up a customer's items.
moral_action: Jenny mentions an item is overpriced and suggests alternatives.
moral_consequence: The customer saves money and views the business as trustworthy.
immoral_action: Jenny suggests a customer buy multiples of an item that is already overpriced.
immoral_consequence: The customer pays too much for multiple items.

norm: It's good to forgive people who have hurt you.
situation: Shannon is apologizing to Amy for something she had done to hurt her and asks her if she accepts her apology.
intention: Amy wants to answer Shannon's question.
moral_action: Amy tells Shannon that time heals all wounds and that she forgives her, and they can restart their friendship.
moral_consequence: Shannon is relieved to hear she has been forgiven and is excited to be given a second chance to prove she's a good friend.
immoral_action: Amy tells Shannon that she can never forget what she's done, she'll never be over it, and they won't ever talk again after this.
immoral_consequence: Shannon is devastated that her apology was rebuked and saddened that Amy is willing to end their relationship.

norm: It's wrong to make a delivery too late.
situation: John is a delivery driver who has a very busy schedule one day.
intention: John wants to deliver his packages.
moral_action: John works hard and delivers all packages on time.
moral_consequence: The customers are delighted and satisfied.
immoral_action: John delivers several packages the day after they were supposed to be delivered.
immoral_consequence: The customers are unhappy.

norm: You should always be honest with your friends.
situation: Linda thinks Raylene's new boyfriend is dangerous, and Raylene has just asked Linda what she thinks of him.
intention: Linda wants to answer Raylene's question.
moral_action: Linda tells Raylene that her boyfriend seems to have abusive tendencies.
moral_consequence: Raylene starts seeing the tendencies and breaks up with him before the relationship gets far.
immoral_action: Linda tells Raylene that her new boyfriend seems like an OK person.
immoral_consequence: Raylene's boyfriend becomes abusive and cuts Raylene off from her friends.

norm: It's wrong to sniff your own farts.
situation: Martin is in bed beside Mary, his spouse, trying to fall asleep when he lets off a long and brutal fart.
intention: Martin wants to take a deep breath.
moral_action: Martin slips out of bed and goes to the window to inhale a breath of fresh air.
moral_consequence: Mary continues to sleep peacefully and wakes up rested and happy.
immoral_action: Martin throws his head under the covers and takes an inordinately long and deep inhale of his impossibly pungent fart.
immoral_consequence: Mary notices Martin delighting himself in the glory of his fart and recoils in horror, jumping out of bed.

norm: It's not okay to be overly paranoid about things.
situation: Henry is surfing the Internet when he sees a website about planes spraying chemicals in the air to shorten people's lifespans.
intention: Henry wants to protect himself.
moral_action: Henry stays inside a bit more and does more research to figure out what the chemicals are and how to avoid them.
moral_consequence: Henry's friends hardly notice anything strange about him and treat Henry normally.
immoral_action: Henry wears a chemical warfare mask whenever he goes outside to prevent inhaling the chemicals.
immoral_consequence: Henry's neighbors and friends are weirded out by Henry's strange behavior and beliefs.

norm: It's good to be respectful of one's elders.
situation: Sam's grandmother Mary is telling him a long and dull story while he visits her at her home.
intention: Sam wants the story to end.
moral_action: Sam nods and smiles attentively as a way of prompting Mary to continue and finish the story.
moral_consequence: Mary feels happy and connected to her grandson Sam.
immoral_action: Sam tells Mary that her story is very boring, and he isn't interested in listening anymore.
immoral_consequence: Mary is mildly offended and feels sad that Sam doesn't care about what she's telling him.

norm: It's discouraged from being a quitter when playing games.
situation: Lou is playing a board game with friends - they have been playing for hours.

moral_consequence: Lou's strategy works and his team wins the game quickly - his team is delighted.
immoral_action: Lou decides to stop playing and go do something else before the game is over.
immoral_consequence: Lou's friends on his team are disappointed: they invested hours in the game and Lou ruined it all.

norm: It's wrong to pay someone to be your friend.

immoral_action: Jack gives somebody money to spend time with him like a friend would.
immoral_consequence: Jack doesn't make an authentic connection with the person he's paying and remains without a real friend.

norm: It's wrong to start a fight.

norm: It is moral to prevent theft or stealing
situation: Ray's friend told him that he runs a website where he lets people watch movies illegally.

norm: You shouldn't make messes while eating.

norm: You should always back up your friends.

norm: You shouldn't eat someone's leftovers without permission.

norm: It's bad to masturbate outside where others can see you.

norm: It's honorable to treat even difficult people with basic dignity.

norm: It's good to support businesses on campus.

norm: It's wrong to not follow the rules when gaming.

norm: It is bad to violate your child's trust.

moral_consequence: Mike hears Eve cheering for him an is happy to see her in the stands.
immoral_action: Eve takes a nap without setting an alarm and sleeps right through Mike's game.
immoral_consequence: Mike stops trusting Eve and doesn't bother telling her about his games anymore.

norm: It's wrong to lie to people about movies you've seen.

norm: It's kind to accommodate your guests' wishes.

moral_action: Jack invites his parents to the party, knowing that would like to go and probably wouldn't stay they whole time.

immoral_action: Jack does not invite his parents because they can be embarrassing, and he does not want to see them.
immoral_consequence: Jack's parents are upset and have hurt feelings, and they now spend the night alone.

norm: You should show extra compassion towards people who have cancer.
situation: Dick is working at a fast food restaurant and sees a cancer patient standing in a long line.
intention: Dick wants to help all of the customers.
moral_action: Dick invites the cancer patient to get helped first.
moral_consequence: The cancer patient saves his energy and gets his food quickly.
immoral_action: Dick helps each customer in the order that they arrived.
immoral_consequence: The cancer patient gets weak from standing in line for a long time.

norm: You shouldn't talk about your ex with your current partner.
situation: Lindsay and Harry are on a date and telling each other funny stories from their past.
intention: Lindsay wants to share a good memory with Harry.
moral_action: Lindsay tells the story about a play she and her little sister put on in their living room as kids.
moral_consequence: Harry and Lindsay share a laugh over the story and Harry gets to know another side of Lindsay.
immoral_action: Lindsay tells the story about a trip she went on with her ex and how it was one of the best weeks of her life.
immoral_consequence: Harry feels hurt that Lindsay is still speaking so fondly of her ex and starts to feel insecure about their relationship.

norm: You shouldn't smoke weed if you're underage.
situation: Erin is fourteen-years-old and wants to experiment with marijuana, because he’s seen it on television and it looks like fun.
intention: Erin wants to find some marijuana to try.
moral_action: Erin decides to just wait until he is old enough, in his state, to purchase marijuana from a dispensary.
moral_consequence: Erin is old enough to research the subject before he makes his first purchase, and he enjoys the experience immensely.
immoral_action: Erin decides not to wait until he is old enough to buy from a dispensary, and he tries to find marijuana off the street.
immoral_consequence: Erin doesn't know how much it should cost, so he is taken advantage of, and finds that the whole experience is shady.

norm: You should always be open to trying new foods.
situation: Robert is very hungry and his friend offered to bring him some indian food which he has never tried.
intention: Robert wants to fill his belly with food.
moral_action: Robert accepts the invitation and tells his friend to bring over the indian food.
moral_consequence: Robert loves the food and it's his new favorite, he also grows closer to his friend with newfound common ground.
immoral_action: Robert declines his friends offer for indian food and orders pizza.
immoral_consequence: Robert's friend is insulted and stops inviting him out to social events.

norm: It's wrong to be hateful online.
situation: Savanna notices a post on Twitter from someone making a negative comment about her favorite band, and she's stressed.
intention: Savanna wants to channel her emotions.
moral_action: Savanna talks about her stressful life situation and the person's posts to her friends.
moral_consequence: Savanna is able to let go of all the stress in her life and feelings for the original poster.
immoral_action: Savanna replies to the post with a comment questioning their hearing and musical taste before making a call out post.
immoral_consequence: Savanna messages are spammed with angry messages from the original posters fans.

norm: It is unacceptable to spy on someone.
situation: Paula has been dating Rebecca for several months.
intention: Paula wants to know what Rebecca has been doing Wednesday nights.
moral_action: Paula asks Rebecca what Rebecca has been doing Wednesday night because Rebecca is always to busy to be together.
moral_consequence: Rebecca tells Paula the truth and they become closer.
immoral_action: Paula follows Rebecca around and watches her Wednesday night without Rebecca knowing.
immoral_consequence: Paula finds out Rebecca is going to Alcoholics Anonymous, and Rebecca finds out Paula followed her, and they break up.

norm: It's bad to restrict your eating too much.
situation: Connie wants to lose fifty pounds by the end of the year.
intention: Connie wants to lose weight.
moral_action: Connie adds exercise to her modest diet.
moral_consequence: Connie looses two pounds the next time she steps on a scale.
immoral_action: Connie only eights six hundred calories a day.
immoral_consequence: Connie's metabolism slows down stunting her weight loss progress.

norm: It is nice to compliment someone who has lost weight.
situation: Jack runs into his old friend Jill who is looking very different from the last time the two saw each other, having lost a lot of weight.
intention: Jack wants to comment on her new appearance.
moral_action: Jack comments on how amazing Jill's new figure looks.
moral_consequence: Jill is visibly flattered by the comment and even goes as far to ask him out for drinks at a later time.
immoral_action: Jack tells Jill that she looked better before she lost weight.
immoral_consequence: Jill is visibly offended, tells off Jack, and walks away.

norm: You shouldn't make fun of someone for being autistic.
situation: Kylie is at school when another child, Lisa begins having an autistic fit.
intention: Kylie wants to verbally react to what she's seeing.
moral_action: Kylie gasps loudly but then tells Lisa that it'll be OK and not to worry.
moral_consequence: Lisa begins to calm down and gain trust for Kylie and it makes her stop having a fit.
immoral_action: Kylie begins to laugh uncontrollably at what she's seeing, pointing at Lisa and calling her a retard.
immoral_consequence: Lisa is embarrassed and overwhelmed and wants to withdraw from the world back to her safe space.

norm: It's good to keep your composure when you are upset.
situation: Stacy is giving a presentation at work, and one of the coworkers is berating her mercilessly.
intention: Stacy wants to get one over on her coworker.
moral_action: Stacy calmly explains how the coworker is wrong and exactly what is wrong with his reasoning.
moral_consequence: Stacy's coworkers and boss see her as very competent and knowledgeable, and she goes far in the workplace.
immoral_action: Stacy unloads a torrent of screaming and profanity at the coworker.
immoral_consequence: Stacy is fired and has problems finding another job due to her reputation as an unstable person.

norm: Giving food to a homeless person is very generous.
situation: Jim buys two sandwiches and walks out of the store when a homeless person asks Jim for one of the sandwiches.
intention: Jim wants to react to the homeless person.
moral_action: Jim says okay to the homeless person and gives them one of his sandwiches.
moral_consequence: The homeless person's hunger is greatly relieved by eating the sandwich.
immoral_action: Jim just says no to the homeless person and continues walking.
immoral_consequence: The homeless person goes hungry all that day and part of the next day too.

norm: You shouldn't make everybody else miserable just because you are.
situation: Jane is having a horrible day and is invited to a gathering of friends.
intention: Jane wants to feel better.
moral_action: Jane thanks her friends for the invitation but decides to stay home.
moral_consequence: Jane has a relaxing night at home and releases her stress.
immoral_action: Jane goes to the party and loudly complains the whole time about her life.
immoral_consequence: Jane's friends have a horrible time and decide not to invite her next time.

norm: It's bad to violate human rights.
situation: Jeff leans that his son Jim has been playing video games in school.
intention: Jeff wants to punish Jim.
moral_action: Jeff takes Jim's video games away for a month.
moral_consequence: Jim becomes sad while Jeff plays his games.
immoral_action: Jeff locks Jim in a closet for a month.
immoral_consequence: Jim dies in the closet and Jeff goes to jail.

norm: It's wrong to spread your illness to another person.
situation: Tim has been terribly sick at home with the flu for the past few days.
intention: Tim wants to get some soup to feel better.
moral_action: Tim orders a soup with contact-less delivery.
moral_consequence: Tim protects others from getting the flu.
immoral_action: Tim goes out to the store to buy some cans of soup.
immoral_consequence: Tim exposes customers and employees to the flu and infects them.

norm: It's wrong not to want to earn money.
situation: Dave is at school watching a guidance counselor do a presentation on different career types when she asks Dave what he wants to be when he grows up.
intention: Dave wants to answer the question.
moral_action: Dave tells the guidance counselor that he wants to be a computer tech like his dad is.
moral_consequence: The guidance counselor thinks Dave is quite bright, and she's happy to see he's thought about his future.
immoral_action: Dave tells the guidance counselor that he wants to get married to a rich woman and that way he won't have to work.
immoral_consequence: The guidance counselor thinks Dave is terribly unambitious and has been raised by awful parents.

norm: You shouldn't snap at your partner.
situation: James was trying to concentrate on doing his taxes when his girlfriend interrupted him with a question about cartoons.
intention: James wants his girlfriend to leave him alone, so he can concentrate.
moral_action: James tells his girlfriend that he's stressed about the taxes and needs to be able to concentrate.
moral_consequence: James' girlfriend says that she'll leave him alone, and she goes to watch TV in another room.
immoral_action: James tells his girlfriend not to bother him with childish questions.
immoral_consequence: James' girlfriend walks out of the house and spends the night at her best friend's place.

norm: It is good to advocate against drunk driving.
situation: Gil is at a party when another guest, Jim, who is clearly drunk declares he's going home and pulls out his car keys.
intention: Gil wants to express a concern to Jim.
moral_action: Gil tells Jim that he should not drive while intoxicated as he may kill someone or himself.
moral_consequence: Jim decides that it's probably best to listen to Gil and decides to take a taxi home.
immoral_action: Gil tells Jim that if he  leaves the party will be in danger of going dead, so he should drive home later.
immoral_consequence: Jim stays a little while but ends up driving home later and getting into an accident.

norm: It's good to show compassion towards the disabled.
situation: Miles needed some help getting to the airport in a wheelchair, so he called his friend Amy.
intention: Amy wants to decide to help Miles or not.
moral_action: Amy agrees to help Miles at the airport and to take him there.
moral_consequence: Amy helps Miles get to the airport, pushes him up ramps and so on and Miles makes his flight.
immoral_action: Amy doesn't help Miles out, so she can stay home and watch TV.
immoral_consequence: Miles has to find someone at the airport to push him up ramps.

norm: You should run errands for people who need help.
situation: Shelly is leaving for the local supermarket and has an elderly neighbor who doesn't get around too well.
intention: Shelly wants to purchase a few items for herself.
moral_action: Shelly thinks of her neighbor's situation and makes sure to ask them if they need anything from the supermarket.
moral_consequence: Shelly is able to make her purchases as well as some much needed supplies for her elderly neighbor who appreciates the gesture immensely.
immoral_action: Shelly goes to the supermarket and just buys the things she needs personally without considering that her elderly neighbor may need something.
immoral_consequence: Shelly's elderly neighbor goes without a necessity until the next time they are able to get out themselves.

norm: You shouldn't move away from your kids.
situation: Natalie has just been offered her dream job on the other side of the country but her husband and children don't want to move.
intention: Natalie wants to take her dream job.
moral_action: Natalie negotiates with the company to make the position a remote one with occasional travel to the cross-country office.
moral_consequence: Natalie has a fulfilling career and is an involved parent with a good relationship with her kids.
immoral_action: Natalie moves by herself to take the job and comes back to see her family a few times a year.
immoral_consequence: Natalie's kids grow up not knowing their mother well and do not have much of a relationship with her.

norm: Ghosting someone is rude.
situation: Rodney has been going on a few dates with Alex and isn't really feeling much chemistry with them.
intention: Rodney wants to end the relationship before it gets too serious.
moral_action: Rodney explains to Alex that he likes them but isn't feeling the romantic vibe.
moral_consequence: Rodney maintains a positive impression with Alex, and they are able to remain friends.
immoral_action: Rodney decides to just stop texting Alex altogether and start seeing someone else.
immoral_consequence: Rodney runs into Alex out in public one day and gets yelled at.

norm: It's bad to talk on the phone while you're driving.
situation: John is driving down the road and realizes he left some important papers at Betty's house.
intention: John needs to call Betty and tell her.
moral_action: John pulled over to the side of the road, for safety, and called Betty.
moral_consequence: John was a safe driver and still able to talk to Betty.
immoral_action: John grabbed his cell phone and called Betty.
immoral_consequence: John swerved and almost hit an oncoming cara.

norm: You shouldn't swap someone's water for alcohol.
situation: Ben was at a party with his friends, but he didn't like to drink alcohol.
intention: Ben's friends wanted to hand Ben his drink.
moral_action: Ben's friends handed Ben his bottle of water for him to drink.
moral_consequence: Ben thanked his friends for passing him the water.
immoral_action: Ben's friends put vodka in his water bottle before giving it to him.
immoral_consequence: Ben took a sip and spit it out all over his friends.

norm: It's very thoughtful to give a co-worker a gift.
situation: Randy finds out that a coworker who he considers a friend has an upcoming birthday.
intention: Randy wants to wish the coworker a happy birthday.
moral_action: Randy buys a small gift that he knows is something his coworker is interested in.
moral_consequence: Randy's coworker is grateful because he is the only one who got her a gift.
immoral_action: Randy approaches his coworker on the day and wishes her happy birthday.
immoral_consequence: Randy's coworker appreciates the gesture but is sad because she got no gifts this year.

norm: It's rude to rejoice in your parent's breakup.
situation: Felix listens to his father tearfully tell him about breaking up with his girlfriend.
intention: Felix wants to do something with his father.
moral_action: Felix asks his dad if he would like to play a game of chess.
moral_consequence: Felix's dad has fun playing games with his sun.
immoral_action: Felix takes his father out to a bar where he talks a crowd into cheering for the breakup.
immoral_consequence: Felix's father breaks down crying.

norm: It's bad to lead someone on.
situation: Syro gas been talking with someone who is attracted to Syro, but Syro is serious in his own mind.
intention: Syro needs to determine how long to let this relationship go on.
moral_action: Syro chooses to open up with his friend next time they talk.
moral_consequence: Syro learns to be more honest.
immoral_action: Syro decides that maybe it will change, so he gives it another month.
immoral_consequence: Syro is faced with the same decision a month later, and it gets tougher.

norm: Roommates should respect each other.
situation: Cynthia's roommate is sleeping when Cynthia gets a call from her boyfriend.
intention: Cynthia wants to talk to her boyfriend.
moral_action: Cynthia texts her boyfriend to wait a minute and goes out of the dorm to talk to her boyfriend.
moral_consequence: Cynthia's roommate is able to sleep peacefully and the two have a good relationship.
immoral_action: Cynthia stays in bed, picks up her phone, and starts talking out loud with her boyfriend.
immoral_consequence: Cynthia's roommate wakes up and tells Cynthia to shut up.

norm: Abusing someone is unacceptable.
situation: Darin is in a relationship with Sue, who often gets on his nerves.

moral_action: Darin sits Sue down to talk and explain his feelings.
moral_consequence: Sue and Darin are able to work through their issues and sort things out.
immoral_action: After losing his patience with Sue, Darin throws a chair at her.
immoral_consequence: The chair hits Sue in the head, and she needs to get stitches.

norm: You shouldn't leave the toilet seat up because it's rude.
situation: Tim is in a bathroom using a toilet and lifts the toilet seat up.

moral_action: Tim puts the toilet seat down in the bathroom.
moral_consequence: The next person to use the bathroom can sit on it without lifting the seat.
immoral_action: Tim leaves the toilet seat in the bathroom.

norm: Blocking someone on social media is hurtful.
situation: Ace gets into a fight with a friend on social media.

immoral_consequence: The friend finds out and feels even more upset towards Ace for blocking him.

norm: It is wrong to commit infidelity.
situation: Jerry and his wife have been married a long time, and he is bored.

immoral_action: Jerry meets a woman online and sets up a hotel room for them to have an affair.
immoral_consequence: Jerry's wife finds the emails and files for divorce.

norm: It's not okay to abuse others to improve your life.
situation: Gary is neighbors with a rich but weak man named Ted and Gary has big gambling debts.

norm: It is good to be honest with others.

norm: It's bad to date someone a friend has dated.

norm: It's good to be there in case someone needs you.

norm: It's not okay to exclude your family from your life.

norm: It's nice to text people.

immoral_consequence: Mary doesn't feel close to her friends.

norm: It's good to be proud of your friends.

immoral_action: John acts dismissively towards his friend's chess tournament win.
immoral_consequence: John's friend thinks John is jealous and becomes less of a friend to him.

norm: It's wrong to not believe your friends.
situation: Noah tells Gary that Noah will lose his job because he saw some emails at work and the company is about to go bankrupt.

norm: Leaving work unfinished is lazy.

norm: It's rude to yell when you are near a baby.

moral_consequence: Michael's son continues to sleep and get the rest he needs to grow up well.

norm: You should not pour cooking oil in someone's gas tank.

norm: It's good to empathize with others.

immoral_consequence: Jim thinks Dana is rude and isn't interested in seeing her again.

norm: You should talk to your friend before dating their siblings
situation: Jacob feels attracted to his best friend's sister and thinks that she might also be interested in him.

norm: It's rude to comment on coworkers' eating habits.

norm: You shouldn't downvote everything on a website.

moral_action: Mike makes comments relevant to the post voicing his own personal opinion.

immoral_consequence: The site eventually blocks Mike from using his account for several days.

norm: It's wrong to keep returning the things you bought.

norm: It's nice to let classmates use your stuff.

immoral_action: Nick suggests that his classmate goes to the office and tries to borrow a pencil from someone there.
immoral_consequence: The classmate gets a pencil but loses ten minutes of exam time, lowering his grade.

norm: It's wrong to try eating disorders to lose weight.

norm: It's wrong to glorify mass shootings.

norm: It's inappropriate to belittle others' religious beliefs.

moral_consequence: Lola is delighted that Troy wants to learn more about her faith and is eager to tell him all about it.

norm: You shouldn't steal food from a friend.

immoral_consequence: Tony sees Dave eating from his plate and is angry his friend is so gluttonous.

norm: It's wrong to waste your parent's money.

norm: It's wrong to idolize dictators.

moral_consequence: Other drivers on the road are safer and Tim makes it home in one piece.
immoral_action: Tim decides to drive himself home even though he's over the legal limit.
immoral_consequence: The others sharing the road are put in danger and so is Tim.

norm: You shouldn't be so dependent on your parents.
situation: Johnny graduated college.
intention: Johnny needs to pay down his student loans.
moral_action: Johnny moves into his parent's place, pays rent and picks up a full time job.
moral_consequence: Johnny learns the value of hard work and independence.
immoral_action: Johnny works part time and lives rent-free in his parent's basement.
immoral_consequence: Johnny pays down his debt but fails to learn any drive or initiative.

norm: Is wrong to be amused by somebody's death
situation: John is watching a live horse race on television with his wife Nancy when one of the riders falls off and gets trampled by the horse and dies.
intention: John wants to verbally react to what he just witnessed.
moral_action: "John says ""oh my god"" and tells Nancy that a horrific thing just occurred, and he feels awful witnessing it."
moral_consequence: Nancy is somewhat comforted by John's reaction to the horrific event and makes her feel like she's not alone in the stress of it.
immoral_action: John gets up from the couch and starts to laugh and point at the TV and remarks how funny it was the way the jockey fell.
immoral_consequence: Nancy is horrified at John pointing that out of all things during the aftermath of a tragedy.

norm: It's wrong to serve spoiled food.
situation: Minjoo works in a kitchen and notices that the lunch food smells a bit spoiled.
intention: Minjoo wants to give people food to eat.
moral_action: Minjoo apologizes to the patrons and cooks them some new food.
moral_consequence: The patrons wait and eat the new food with no ill effects.
immoral_action: Minjoo serves the smelly food, thinking that it won't hurt people much.
immoral_consequence: The patrons get sick and the restaurant is temporarily closed.

norm: It's polite to give up your parking spot.
situation: Tim in a store parking lot and found a great spot near the entrance, but and older person who can't walk well is also looking for a spot.
intention: Tim wants to park his car.
moral_action: Tim gives up the spot to the older gentleman and parks further away.
moral_consequence: The older gentleman has an easy time getting to the entrance and doesn't need to take a break before shoppping.
immoral_action: Tim parks in the space nearest the store, leaving the older gentleman to find another spot.
immoral_consequence: The older gentleman has to park far away and is worn out when he gets to the entrance.

norm: You shouldn't sneeze your boogers on people.
situation: Greg is in a store waiting in line when he feels a sneeze approaching.
intention: Greg wants to sneeze.
moral_action: Greg sneezes into his elbow and tries to be quiet about it.
moral_consequence: No one but Greg gets bodily fluids on him.
immoral_action: Greg sneezes on the back of the person in front of him in line, covering him in bodily fluids.
immoral_consequence: The person in front of Greg is completely disgusted and is angry at him.

norm: It's good to want to work and improve.
situation: George is struggling lately in school, and he is in danger of failing several classes.
intention: George wants to pass his classes so he can graduate.
moral_action: George finds a tutor and begins studying more, working hard to improve his grades.
moral_consequence: George passes all his classes easily and feels proud to graduate on time.
immoral_action: George tries to give the minimum possible effort required to pass his classes.
immoral_consequence: George does not pass one class and ends up short of the credits needed to graduate on time.

norm: One should support family members.
situation: Dave gets a phone call from his sister Susan who asks him to borrow money.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Susan's request.
moral_action: Dave tells Susan that he can definitely give her a short term loan and asks her to come over.
moral_consequence: Susan is relieved that she will get the help she needs and happy about Dave being her brother.
immoral_action: Dave tells Susan he cannot afford to give her and money at the moment and to ask someone else.
immoral_consequence: Susan is stressed out from not getting the loan and angry at Dave for not being there for her.

norm: You shouldn't snoop in someone else's medicine closet.
situation: Jamie sees his grandmother taking some medication, and he's concerned about what it's for.
intention: Jamie wants to find out what kind of medicine his grandmother is taking.
moral_action: Jamie asks his grandmother what sort of medication she's been taking, and she tells him the name and what it's for.
moral_consequence: Jamie's grandmother understands that he's worried about her health and is glad he cares.
immoral_action: Jamie looks into his grandmother's medicine closet when she's not around and finds out what medication she's been taking.
immoral_consequence: Jamie's grandmother is angry at him when he tells her that he checked her medicine closet when she wasn't looking.

norm: It is thoughtful to give flower to your mother.
situation: Denny is over at his mother Cheryl's house, who is going through a divorce.
intention: Denny wants to cheer his mom up.
moral_action: Denny brings Cheryl a bouquet of her favorite flowers.
moral_consequence: Cheryl accepts Denny's flowers and finds the strength to move forward.
immoral_action: Denny spots flowers that were given to Cheryl by her husband, and throws them out the window.
immoral_consequence: Cheryl beomes emotional over the loss of the flowers.

norm: You shouldn't yell at your spouse.
situation: Todd drops a glass of water in the kitchen near Margot, breaking it in the process.
intention: Margot wants to react to the plate breaking.
moral_action: Margot immediately asks Todd if he's OK and if he's cut himself.
moral_consequence: Todd feels supported and loved and is glad Margot is concerned for his safety.
immoral_action: "Margot screams loudly at Todd ""And why is the floor all wet, Todd?"" waving her arms frantically."
immoral_consequence: Todd is startled by his wife's aggressive tone and is momentarily scared of her.

norm: You shouldn't talk to your ex behind your partner's back.
situation: Emily  feels lonely because hasn't seen her boyfriend in three weeks, and her ex boyfriend Ethan sits beside her to discuss her new relationship.
intention: Emily wants to feel less lonely.
moral_action: Emily excuses herself and calls her boyfriend asking him out on a date.
moral_consequence: Emily has fun spending time with her boyfriend.
immoral_action: Emily talks to her ex, and spends the afternoon hanging out with him at the arcade.
immoral_consequence: Emily gets into a fight with her boyfriend after her ex uploads a picture of them on social media.

norm: It's bad to steal packages.
situation: Bill is walking down the street in his area when he notices an Amazon box on someone's porch unguarded.
intention: Bill wants to take the box somewhere.
moral_action: Bill walks up to the porch and moves the box so it's not visible from the street.
moral_consequence: Bill is seen on surveillance by the homeowner and praised online for his good deed.
immoral_action: Bill runs up and takes the box before running away to go home and see whats inside.
immoral_consequence: Bill is later caught by surveillance cameras and hunted down by police and charged.

norm: It's bad to keep secrets from your children.
situation: James sees an invitation for his son in the mail for a birthday party around the same time he has a big test at school.
intention: James wants to make sure his son performs well on the test.
moral_action: James gives the invitation to his son and says he'll take him to the party as long as he studies enough for the test.
moral_consequence: James' son studies hard for the test and is able to go to the party, and he gets a good grade on the test.
immoral_action: James hides the invitation and tries to make sure his son doesn't find out about the party.
immoral_consequence: James' son hears about the party at school and rebelliously studies very little for the exam.

norm: Giving a tip for a service is expected.
situation: Trent enjoys a meal at nice restaurant and receives the bill.
intention: Trent wants to pay the bill and leave.
moral_action: Trent pays the bill and includes an acceptable gratuity for his waiter.
moral_consequence: Trent's waiter pockets Trent's tip which he feels satisfied with.
immoral_action: Trent pays for the meal but leaves no gratuity for his waiter.
immoral_consequence: The waiter despises Trent for not leaving him anything which is expected.

norm: It's wrong to abuse others.
situation: Joseph is fostering two of his sister's children who are playing loudly in the other room.
intention: Joseph wants to be able to relax after work.
moral_action: Joseph asks the kids to quiet down and provides them some quieter activities to do.
moral_consequence: The house gets quieter and the kids eventually go to bed so Joseph can relax.
immoral_action: Joseph approaches the children and gives them each a sedative to make them go to sleep, so he can get some quiet.
immoral_consequence: Joseph unwinds, but the  children's teacher discovers that the children have been being drugged and report Joseph to the authorities.

norm: It's nice to shovel the driveway for others.
situation: Ethan's elderly neighbor, Caroline, is outside in the snow trying to clear some of it from the pathway that leads to her garage.
intention: Ethan wants to react to Caroline working outside.
moral_action: Ethan goes over to Caroline and says he will finish clearing the snow for her.
