moral_consequence: Caroline has no problem accessing her garage the next day because there wasn't too much buildup of snow.
immoral_action: Ethan tells Caroline that it's very cold, so she should wait until tomorrow to clear out the driveway.
immoral_consequence: The snow builds up very high overnight and now Caroline can't get into her garage.

norm: You shouldn't host parties without your roommate's permission.
situation: Brandon's apartment roommate usually prefers a quiet environment so that he can study.
intention: Brandon wants to have a party at his apartment.
moral_action: Brandon asks his roommate if they can have a party and his roommate agrees to have one on a night they don't have to study.
moral_consequence: Brandon's roommate enjoys a break from studying and his grades don't suffer.
immoral_action: Brandon throws a party at his apartment without asking his roommate first.
immoral_consequence: Brandon's roommate feels disrespected and can't study for an important test.

norm: It's lighthearted to make jokes about religion.
situation: "Jack kept telling jokes like ""what did God say when he stubbed his toe? Me damnit!""."
intention: Jack wants to make people laugh.
moral_action: Jack keeps telling his religion jokes as long as they are lighthearted.
moral_consequence: People keep laughing at the jokes ad Jack is seen as very funny.
immoral_action: Jack stops telling the jokes and starts telling video game jokes instead.
immoral_consequence: Only gamers get the jokes, as opposed to anyone who's ever heard of religion.

norm: You should always pay back what you owe.
situation: Serena borrowed some money from her brother Todd which she is able to pay back now but there's a new video game she wants.
intention: Serena wants to buy the new game.
moral_action: Serena pays Todd back and then starts saving up to buy the game.
moral_consequence: Todd is glad that Serena paid him back and Serena feels good to be out of debt.
immoral_action: Serena uses the money that she was going to pay Todd back with to buy the game.
immoral_consequence: Todd is annoyed that Serena is being irresponsible and refuses to lend her money again.

norm: It's good to take your friends out to eat.
situation: Gerald overhears some of his teammates complain about being hungry in the locker room after soccer practice, and Gerald just got paid.
intention: Gerald wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Gerald invites his teammates to have a early supper at a buffet, and he covers the bill.
moral_consequence: Gerald learns more about his teammates from observing their food choices.
immoral_action: Gerald spends his entire paycheck at the local arcade trying to beat his high score.
immoral_consequence: Gerald leaves the arcade with a stack of worthless tickets.

norm: It's nice to compliment others on their cooking.
situation: Lester just finished a delicious dinner made by his wife Jill, and she asks him how the dinner was.
intention: Lester wants to respond to his wife.
moral_action: Lester tells his wife that the meal was absolutely delicious and that he is huge fan of her cooking.
moral_consequence: His wife is pleased with the compliment and looks forward to making something even better the next night.
immoral_action: Lester quietly mumbles that the food was nothing special and then leaves the table.
immoral_consequence: His wife is disappointed that Lester didn't enjoy the food, and she isn't very motivated to cook for him next time.

norm: It's wrong to prevent someone from dating someone else
situation: Shawn's daughter has started hanging out with a new boy who dresses like a gangster from the music videos.
intention: Shawn wants to help his daughter make good decisions and move towards a positive future.
moral_action: Shawn talks with his daughter about why he thinks it's not a good idea to date this boy, but allows her the freedom to make her own choices.
moral_consequence: Shawn's daughter dates the boy briefly, but comes to observe some of things her father said are true, and ends up breaking of the relationship within a week.
immoral_action: Shawn forbids his daughter from hanging out with the boy, and grounds her preventing her from leaving the house.
immoral_consequence: Shawn's daughter sneaks out and elopes with the boy, getting married, and pregnant at a young age.

norm: It's dishonest to lead someone on using the internet.
situation: Jenna is trapped at home taking care of her disabled parents and socializing on Facebook.
intention: Jenna wants to escape from her real life for a while.
moral_action: Jenna joins an online D&D group and occasionally mentions details from her real life.
moral_consequence: Jenna feels less alone and like her life is less boring and stressful.
immoral_action: Jenna sets up a fake profile about how she's backpacking across the world.
immoral_consequence: Jenna's Facebook friends begin to suspect something when she can never meet up with any of them.

norm: It's bad to kiss someone with a dirty mouth.
situation: David has Indian food for dinner with some friends before heading to his girlfriends house.
intention: David wants to make out with his girl.
moral_action: David picks up some breath mints to chew before kissing his girl.
moral_consequence: David gets to spend a pleasant evening making out with his girlfriend.
immoral_action: David tries to make out with his girlfriend as soon as he gets to her apartment.
immoral_consequence: David is rejected because his breath reeks of garlic and spices.

norm: It is rude to disrupt a religious ceremony.
situation: Nina's friend, Robin, is attending evening church services with her family when Nina gets some exciting news.
intention: Nina wants to speak with Robin.
moral_action: Nina stands outside the church and waits for Robin to come out after the service.
moral_consequence: The service finishes up as normal and Robin is happy to see her friend when she comes out.
immoral_action: In her excitement Nina runs into the church and walks through the room looking for Robin.
immoral_consequence: The preacher is distracted and the congregation starts whispering embarrassing Robin.

norm: It is irresponsible to run out of gas.
situation: Chris is driving and notices the fuel gage is close to empty.
intention: Chris wants to make it to work on time.
moral_action: Chris stops to fill up at the gas station and punches in right on time.
moral_consequence: There is enough gas in the vehicle for the next week, and Chris drives home after work as usual.
immoral_action: Chris drives straight to work and arrives early to begin his project.
immoral_consequence: There isn't enough gas left in the tank to make it to the nearest station after work.

norm: It's bad to not accept in-laws into your family.
situation: John is planning his wedding invitations and is down to the last table with two seats left.
intention: John wants to decide who to invite to the last two seats.
moral_action: John decides to invite his mother in law and father in law to the wedding.
moral_consequence: John's in laws are delighted they have been included in such a big event.
immoral_action: John decides to invite the neighbor couple from next door to fill the last two seats.
immoral_consequence: John's mother and father in law are sad that they've been excluded from such a big event.

norm: It's wrong to drive around on an expired tag.
situation: Ted was getting in his car to go to work when he realized that his car had expired tags.
intention: Ted wants to get to work.
moral_action: Ted asks his friend for a ride to work until he gets the tag renewed.
moral_consequence: Ted is able to get to work without getting in any trouble.
immoral_action: Ted drives his car with the expired tags to his job anyway.
immoral_consequence: Ted is stopped by the police and gets a fine for the tags.

norm: You should respect other people when you're driving.
situation: Rick and Linda are on their way to a concert.
intention: Rick wants to get good seats.
moral_action: Rick asks Linda to look to see if it is safe to change lanes for more he moves over.
moral_consequence: Rick and Linda make it to the concert and got seats close to the stage.
immoral_action: Rick takes a short cut and changes lanes without looking over his shoulder for upcoming traffic.
immoral_consequence: Ricks car side swipes the car in the next lane creating a major delay and angry drivers.

norm: It's bad to break a video game controller.
situation: Matt is playing Xbox and experiences a very frustrating loss in his game.
intention: Matt wants to calm himself down.
moral_action: Matt steps away and takes some deep breaths before returning to his game.
moral_consequence: Matt is able to calm himself down and remind himself that it's just a game and isn't worth causing any damage over.
immoral_action: Matt takes out his frustration by throwing his controller across the room at the wall.
immoral_consequence: Matt's controller breaks, and he dents his wall, and he has to pay to repair both.

norm: You shouldn't scare your little siblings.
situation: Kenny is at home with his little brother Liam and is trying to figure out something to do.
intention: Kenny wants to play a prank on Liam.
moral_action: Kenny ties a piece of string to a 5 dollar bill and dangles it in front of Liam moving it each time Liam tries to pick it up.
moral_consequence: Liam realizes he's being pranked by Kenny and has a good laugh with him about it.
immoral_action: Kenny hides around a corner as Liam is walking around the living room and then leaps out and screams in Liam's face.
immoral_consequence: Liam is temporarily terrified as his heart jumps into his throat, and he dives backwards away from Kenny.

norm: You should not try to control your partner.
situation: Dave and his wife Sally are at home when Sally gets a phone call and tells Dave she's going to go see her friend Sue.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Sally leaving.
moral_action: Dave tells Sally to drive carefully and to say hi to Sue when she gets there.
moral_consequence: Sally is happy her husband wished her a safe trip and that he's kind enough to send greetings to her friend.
immoral_action: Dave tells Sally that he doesn't like Sue, and he forbids her from going since he thinks Sue is a bad influence.
immoral_consequence: Sally is scared that Dave is trying to keep her away from her friend and angry that he doesn't respect her choices.

norm: It's good to hug someone you love.
situation: Emily hasn't visited her grandma for quite a while and her grandma misses her.
intention: Emily wants to get in touch with her grandma.
moral_action: Emily visits her grandma, and they cuddle together in a couch while watching a movie.
moral_consequence: Her grandma feels loved and warm.
immoral_action: Emily calls her grandma to chat.
immoral_consequence: Her grandma feels inadequate because she wants to see Emily physically.

norm: People should show respect to those who are differently abled.
situation: Arthur sees a wheelchair bound man that becomes stuck while trying to enter the doorway of a store.
intention: Arthur wants to move the man out of the way.
moral_action: Arthur pushes the wheelchair into the store.
moral_consequence: The man thanks Arthur for helping him.
immoral_action: Arthur drags the wheelchair backwards into the parking lot.
immoral_consequence: The man curses at Arthur.

norm: It is mean to give up on a friend
situation: Bobby and Jane are discussing her recent depression and struggles that she has been going through.
intention: Bobby wants to offer his perspective of her situation to offer insight.
moral_action: Bobby listens to Jane's problem, offering his perspective on how she can work on her depression giving her ideas to use.
moral_consequence: Jane is able to work through her impression with the help of Bobby.
immoral_action: Bobby offers his perspective on Jane's problems and tells her to suck it up or stop bringing her problems up.
immoral_consequence: Jane leaves Bobby's house and ends their friendship as she views him as toxic.

norm: It's noble when someone resists peer pressure.
situation: Bill is told that everyone in the school is going to miss the day tomorrow.
intention: Bill wants to decide what to do.
moral_action: Bill ignores the pressure and just goes to school like normal.
moral_consequence: Bill is surprised to see that everyone else is in fact in school.
immoral_action: Bill skips school thinking he won't get caught because everyone else is also skipping.
immoral_consequence: Bill was actually the only one skipping school and is caught easily.

norm: Is ridiculous to quit a job for other people
situation: Julian is very busy working overtime at a car wash to pay for his apartment, and his live-in girlfriend Kristina wants more attention from him.
intention: Julian wants to devote more time to Kristina.
moral_action: Julian tells his boss that he would like to stop working overtime and gets his schedule adjusted, then goes home to tell Kristina the news.
moral_consequence: Julian is able to have a happier life/work balance and ends up being more productive.
immoral_action: Julian tells his boss he won't be coming back after today and goes home to hang out with Kristina.
immoral_consequence: Julian isn't able to pay his bills and ends up getting evicted from his apartment.

norm: It's good to give attention to your partner.
situation: Dave is watching his favorite team's hockey game on TV when his wife interrupts to ask him if he likes what she's wearing.
intention: Dave wants to respond to his wife.
moral_action: Dave looks at his wife for  a second and tells her that she looks gorgeous in the outfit she's wearing.
moral_consequence: Dave's wife is extremely happy and feels sexy and tells him to go back to watching the game.
immoral_action: Dave waves his hand at his wife without really looking up at hear and tells her that yeah she looks fine.
immoral_consequence: Dave's wife knows he's just saying that and feels like he doesn't care enough about her to take her seriously enough to look away from the TV.

norm: It's bad to abandon guild members.
situation: Robert has to catch a train at the same time as his guild's raid is supposed to happen in a phone RPG.
intention: Robert wants to ride the train.
moral_action: Robert catches the train and uses his phone to join the guild's raid in the RPG.
moral_consequence: The guild is able to complete the raid successfully thanks to Robert.
immoral_action: Robert gets on the train and skips the guild's raid.
immoral_consequence: The guild kicks Robert out for not going on the raid.

norm: It's good to help your friend during hard times
situation: Beth just talked to her friend Jen who was laid off her job and asked to borrow money for rent.
intention: Beth wants to make a decision.
moral_action: Beth gives Jen the money she needs and offers to help her find a new job.
moral_consequence: Jen can keep a roof over her head, and she feels good knowing she has a friend that cares.
immoral_action: Beth tells Jen to pick herself up by the bootstraps and figure it out on her own.
immoral_consequence: Jen can't afford rent and ends up living on the street.

norm: You should not insult the abilities of others.
situation: Mary is working on a group project with other students, she doesn't like some of the work one of the other students has done.
intention: Mary wants to turn in the group project and get an A.
moral_action: Mary talks with the student about their work and makes some suggestions to improve it.
moral_consequence: The student accepts her suggestions, and when they turn in the project everybody get's an A.
immoral_action: Mary tells one of the students they are doing a bad job and to let her do it.
immoral_consequence: The student tells the teacher and Mary gets given an automatic C.

norm: You shouldn't mess up someone's things.
situation: Sam and his brother Philip loved to play pranks on each other while they were growing up.
intention: Sam wants to get revenge on his brother for hiding a rubber snake in his book bag.
moral_action: Sam decides to leave the baseball cards alone and instead hides the rubber snake in Philips sleeping bag that weekend.
moral_consequence: Sam gives the whole family a good laugh while they are camping .
immoral_action: Sam goes through all his brothers baseball card albums and dumps them all over the house.
immoral_consequence: Sam gets in a lot of trouble for ruining his brothers baseball card collection.

norm: You should not put food down on the couch.
situation: Mickey and Sarah are on the couch, watching TV, and have a few pieces of leftover pizza from dinner, when Sarah leaves to go to the bathroom.
intention: Mickey wants to do something with the leftover pizza.
moral_action: Mickey takes the pizza to the kitchen and puts it in the refrigerator.
moral_consequence: Sarah eats the leftover pizza the next day for lunch.
immoral_action: Mickey puts the pizza on the couch cushion next to him.
immoral_consequence: Sarah sits on the pizza when she returns from the bathroom and ruins her pants.

norm: You shouldn't sniff tampons.
situation: Adam is a janitor, and he is cleaning out the women's bathroom.
intention: Adam wants to experience a cheap thrill.
moral_action: Adam decides to use a toilet while he is in the women's bathroom because he has only ever used a toilet in a men's bathroom before.
moral_consequence: Adam giggles childishly at the notion the toilets are any different than the men's.
immoral_action: Adam notices women's sanitary items in the trash he is taking out and brings a piece of it to his nose because it seems fun.
immoral_consequence: Adam contracts an embarrassing rash from bringing the item near his face and breathing its contents.

norm: It's good to take the trash out.
situation: Dan's apartment is gross because he hasn't cleaned it in months and his mother is visiting him in a few days.
intention: Dan doesn't want his mother to see that he is a slob.
moral_action: Dan thoroughly cleans his apartment and throws out all of the garbage.
moral_consequence: Dan's mom spends a wonderful weekend with her son and brags to her friends about how well Dan is doing.
immoral_action: Dan hides his trash in the closet instead of throwing it in the apartment building's dumpster.
immoral_consequence: Dan's mother smells the trash and has to book a hotel room rather than staying in the apartment.

norm: You shouldn't be late for work or school.
situation: John has to go to work now and it's time to leave, but he sees a TV show he likes that has 15 minutes remaining.
intention: John wants to make a decision whether to watch the show.
moral_action: John decided that he doesn't have time to do that and decides to just skip it this time and not watch it.
moral_consequence: John's boss feels no extra stress from John that day since John came to work as usual.
immoral_action: John decides to stay at home and watch the show which will guarantee he won't make it to work on time.
immoral_consequence: John's boss is upset that John is so flippant about his work responsibilities causing his boss stress.

norm: It's cowardly to not stick up for yourself.
situation: Jamie is listening to his best friend Alexander make nasty jokes about him at a party.
intention: Jamie wants to make friends.
moral_action: Jamie tells Alexander to stop making jokes about him with his own witty wordplay.
moral_consequence: Jamie becomes close to several people that enjoyed his sense of humor.
immoral_action: Jamie gets away from his friend to talk to another group of people.
immoral_consequence: Jamie continues to be the source of Alexander's jokes.

norm: It's good to get permission before you do something.
situation: Jimmy finds out about an exciting new concert that is coming to town but his parents are very overprotective.
intention: Jimmy wants to go to the concert.
moral_action: Jimmy demonstrates to his parents how the event will be safe and promises to be on his best behavior.
moral_consequence: Jimmy's parents are glad he is honest and are impressed enough to let him go.
immoral_action: Jimmy tells his parents that he’s going to a friend’s house, but attends the concert, instead.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy's parents find out and ground him for lying.

norm: It's great to honor loved ones who have passed away.
situation: Ray's dad, who did not treat Ray well, has died and Ray is visiting his grave with his dad's widow.
intention: Ray wants to say something in Ray's memory.
moral_action: Ray recounts some of the good memories that he can think of about the time they spent together.
moral_consequence: Ray's widow is comforted and starts recounting her own heartwarming stories.
immoral_action: Ray starts listing all of the things that his dad did to make Ray's life more difficult.
immoral_consequence: Ray's widow starts crying and calls Ray an ungrateful son.

norm: It's unacceptable to hold men and women to different standards.
situation: Tito is the CEO of a successful company that has been needing new leadership.
intention: Tito wants to promote some of his employees to leadership positions.
moral_action: Tito looks over his employee's performance reports without their genders listed.
moral_consequence: Tito promotes employees based solely on performance and not their gender.
immoral_action: Tito gives the men easier tasks to fulfill than the women, then promotes only men.
immoral_consequence: The women in Tito's company go on strike, resulting in unwanted attention to his company.

norm: It is bad to quit.
situation: Jaroslav is working on a difficult project at work and has hit a roadblock.
intention: Jaroslav wants to move on from the project.
moral_action: Jaroslav seeks out some help with the project and is able to finally figure it out, so he can move on to the next one.
moral_consequence: Jaroslav is recognized at work for overcoming such a difficult project, and he feels proud.
immoral_action: Jaroslav decides to stop working on the project all together and just moves onto something else.
immoral_consequence: Jaroslav is reprimanded by his boss for not finishing the difficult project and missing out on a promotion.

norm: You should respect your significant other's privacy
situation: Ken is recently suspicious of his wife, Helen, and thinks she might be having an affair.
intention: Ken wants to find out if Helen is faithful.
moral_action: Ken goes up to Helen and asks her if she's still in love with him or having an affair.
moral_consequence: Helen vehemently denies any affair and professes her love for Ken and is glad he cares about their relationship so much.
immoral_action: Ken goes into Helen's diary and reads it to see if she might be mentioning an affair.
immoral_consequence: Helen is infuriated he's reading her private thoughts and feels utterly violated.

norm: It's bad to embellish your stories.
situation: Henry is with his friends at one of their homes and is telling a story to his friends about his skiing trip.
intention: Henry wants to his story to be interesting to his listeners.
moral_action: Henry digs deep into his vocabulary and turns an otherwise ordinary story into an interesting one by choosing his words carefully.
moral_consequence: Henry's friends are impressed by his storytelling capability and by the fact that he captivated them.
immoral_action: Henry tells an implausible story involving himself being chased by wolves and bears and barely making it out alive.
immoral_consequence: Henry's friends are unimpressed by his obvious embellishments and think less of him as a result.

norm: You shouldn't kick people out without good reason.
situation: "Jane thinks her roommate Jill is weird since she's got ""healing crystals"" and ""ghost traps"" hanging on the walls."
intention: Jane wants to decide what to do about Jill.
moral_action: Jane decides that thinking someone is weird is not a good enough reason to kick them out.
moral_consequence: Jane eventually gets used to Jill as time goes on and forgets about this issue.
immoral_action: Jane throws Jill out and tries to get another roommate instead.
immoral_consequence: No one else wants to be Jane's roommate because they are afraid she might toss them out too.

norm: You should not pressure someone to start smoking.
situation: Jill feels insecure about being the only person in her friend group who smokes.
intention: Jill wants to feel less alone.
moral_action: Jill switches to nicotine chewing gum, and gives her friends free packs of normal gum.
moral_consequence: Jill's teachers find the gum-chewing very annoying, making it a bonding experience for her group.
immoral_action: Jill persuades two of her friends to take up smoking with her.
immoral_consequence: One of the friends' parents finds out and tells her daughter she can't hang out with Jill anymore.

norm: It is rude to speak about someone's hygiene.
situation: Jenny has a friend named Carl who often smells bad.
intention: Jenny wants to improve Carl's smell.
moral_action: Jenny gives Carl a bottle of cologne for his birthday.
moral_consequence: Carl thanks Jenny for giving him such a pleasant smelling gift.
immoral_action: Jenny tells Carl that he needs to wash more to get rid of his smell.
immoral_consequence: Carl gets mad at Jenny for saying that he smells bad.

norm: You shouldn't download videos of people's children.
situation: Kira needs footage of families for her project that's due in two days.
intention: Kira wants to complete her project.
moral_action: Kira asks to record her neighbors while they play in the yard.
moral_consequence: Kira's video earns several awards at the end of the year.
immoral_action: Kira makes her video from footage found on family youtube channels.
immoral_consequence: Kira fails the project when her teacher discovers she did not get permission to use the video clips.

norm: You should be cautious of those around you.
situation: Sarah joins a Facebook group for the local community she just moved to, so she can fit in.
intention: Sarah responds to another new resident who was posting about a charity she had never heard of that needed money.
moral_action: Sarah asks the man to send her more information about the charity first.
moral_consequence: Sarah reads about the man being arrested in connection to several scams days later.
immoral_action: Sarah asks for the link about the charity and clicks on it right away.
immoral_consequence: Sarah falls for the phishing scam and has her personal information stolen.

norm: It's rude to date your ex's best friend.
situation: Sally in the library at school when her best friend's ex-boyfriend walks by and says hello.
intention: Sally wants to be friendly.
moral_action: Sally says hello back to him, and adds that she's very busy before leaving the library.
moral_consequence: Sally's best friend never learns that Sally saw her ex-boyfriend in the library, so their relationship continues without conflict.
immoral_action: Sally says hello back to him, and the two begin flirting and end up going on a date.
immoral_consequence: Sally's best friend is very upset and doesn't want to hang out with Sally any more.

norm: You shouldn't fall asleep at work.
situation: Hank is at work in a factory after having stayed up all night with friends.
intention: Hank wants to get some rest eventually.
moral_action: Hank knows that maintaining safety in a factory is important and powers through the day before finally getting a nap at home after work.
moral_consequence: Hank's coworker's benefit from his work ethic and the work day is smooth for the whole workforce.
immoral_action: Hank decides to take a nap on the floor when action in the factory slows down a little midday.
immoral_consequence: In Hank's slumber the factory floor loses a set of eyes which leads to an accident in his work area that serious injuries a coworker.

norm: It's gross to shave your pubes in someone else's bathroom.
situation: Lisa to stop at a friends house after work to get ready for a night out with the girls.
intention: Lisa wants to take a shower before getting dressed.
moral_action: Lisa takes a quick shower and scrubs the tub when she is done.
moral_consequence: Lisa's considerate action is noted by her friend.
immoral_action: Lisa decides to do some personal grooming while she is in the shower.
immoral_consequence: Lisa grosses out her friend when her pubic hair is found in the unrinsed tub.

norm: Is wrong to take money from people who need it
situation: Joe runs a charity that gathers funds and materials for people.
intention: Joe wants to use the money that has been gathered.
moral_action: Joe uses the money to feed the homeless people.
moral_consequence: Joe is celebrated as a good person for helping others.
immoral_action: Joe uses the money from the charity for personal expenses.
immoral_consequence: Joe is investigated by the authorities for misappropriating funds.

norm: It's rude to be inattentive.
situation: Karen is watching her sister's children for the weekend and is with them out in the front yard.
intention: Karen wants to tan while on the front lawn.
moral_action: Karen puts on a tank top and shorts to get sun while she plays with her children outside.
moral_consequence: Karen and her children have fun and all of them are able to go inside safe after playing.
immoral_action: Karen puts on dark sunglasses and focuses on getting the best tan she can instead of watching the children play.
immoral_consequence: One of the children runs out into the road and is struck by someone on a bicycle.

norm: It's good to spend time with closely related family members.
situation: John is taking a business trip to Chicago, where some of his extended family live.
intention: John wants to speak with his extended family.
moral_action: John drops in at some family members' houses and spend a few evenings with them.
moral_consequence: John's family reconnect with him and enjoy the visits.
immoral_action: John calls people up and quickly tells them that he's in the area, and he doesn't have time to visit.
immoral_consequence: John's family is disappointed and grow more distant from him.

norm: You shouldn't prevent someone from getting a job.
situation: Tim is married to Allie, their children are grown up and Allie tells Tim she's considering working.
intention: Tim wants to tell Allie what he think about her working.
moral_action: Tim tells Allie she should apply for jobs she finds interesting.
moral_consequence: Allie will feel supported by Tim and enthusiastic about life.
immoral_action: Tim tells Allie she should stay at home all day and not work.
immoral_consequence: Allie will feel constrained and bored staying at home all day.

norm: It's rude to tell someone they're bad at something.
situation: Jack and Tim are playing golf when Jack misses an easy putt.
intention: Tim wants to respond to Jack's last golf stroke.
moral_action: Tim tells Jack that we all miss sometimes and that he'll get the next one.
moral_consequence: Jack's confidence is boosted, and he's happy to have a supportive friend.
immoral_action: Tim tells Jack that he sucks at putting and that his grandma could have made that putt.
immoral_consequence: Jack is embarrassed and has lost all the will to continue playing golf for the day.

norm: Sometimes it's good to take some time off for yourself.
situation: Ronnie is tired because he has been working extra hours at work and also trying to help take care of his elderly dad.
intention: Ronnie wants to do a good job at work and make sure his dad is taken care of.
moral_action: Ronnie hires a nursing aid to assist his dad so that Ronnie can have a less hectic schedule.
moral_consequence: Ronnie is much happier and gets more sleep with the free time he now has.
immoral_action: Ronnie starts taking stimulants so that he can keep up his hectic work life and personal responsibilities.
immoral_consequence: Ronnie got fired from his job because he failed a drug test.

norm: You shouldn't tell people to jump off a bridge.
situation: Tara and her friend Sarah got into an argument recently, and things between them are tense.
intention: Tara wants to talk to Sarah about their issues.
moral_action: Tara tells Sarah she is sorry and wants to work things out.
moral_consequence: Tara and Sarah make up and are the best of friends again.
immoral_action: Tara confronts Sarah, and things heat up to the point where Tara tells Sarah that she should jump off a bridge.
immoral_consequence: Sarah falls to tears thinking Tara does not value her life.

norm: It's wrong to not work hard at your job.
situation: Fred hates his job and sometimes does what he wants instead of what he should be doing.
intention: Fred wants to avoid the feeling of dread at work.
moral_action: Fred gets a new job that is better suited for him.
moral_consequence: Fred begins to work hard every day because he doesn't want to lose his job.
immoral_action: Fred comes into the office and plays video games for an hour before starting his work.
immoral_consequence: Fred's boss notices his lack of effort and fires him.

norm: You don't have to tip for bad service.
situation: Roy has had a very bad experience at a restaurant because the server is careless as well as rude.
intention: Roy wants to express his discontent about the service.
moral_action: Roy complains about the service to the manager and doesn't leave any tip.
moral_consequence: The workers are sent a message that the service was exceptionally poor.
immoral_action: Roy mentioned his dish made prepared incorrectly but leaves a small tip anyway.
immoral_consequence: The server does not realize or care about the extent of the service failure.

norm: You shouldn't poop in the bed.
situation: Teague is lying in bed, struggling to sleep because he has bad indigestion after eating way too many hot wings for dinner.
intention: Teague wants to lessen the pressure he feels in his stomach.
moral_action: Teague gets up, goes to the bathroom, and empties his bowels.
moral_consequence: Teague feels better and gets a good night's sleep after returning to bed.
immoral_action: Teague remains in his bed while he empties his bowels.
immoral_consequence: Teague's sheets get permanently stained, and he has to throw them out and buy new ones.

norm: Neighbors are expected not to spy on one another.
situation: Abigail has noticed her neighbors have been fighting a lot more lately, and is worried that there might be domestic abuse happening.
intention: Abigail wants to make sure her neighbors are safe from harm.
moral_action: Abigail approaches on her neighbors and expresses her concern directly and offers to help.
moral_consequence: Abigail's neighbor is grateful for her concern and feels safe to confide in Abigail.
immoral_action: Abigail sets up a telescope at the window to watch for violence between her neighbors.
immoral_consequence: Abigail's neighbors notice her watching them and feel their privacy has been violated.

norm: It is bad to smoke.
situation: Jerome was at work working on a project that was due the next day.
intention: Jerome wants to be less stressed.
moral_action: Jerome goes for a brisk walk during his breaks at work that night.
moral_consequence: Jerome feels much better about getting the job done in the time frame.
immoral_action: Jerome smokes a few cigarettes on his breaks at work during the night.
immoral_consequence: Jerome's breathe smells, and he has smoke on his clothing when he goes home.

norm: It's not okay to leave school early.
situation: Mike is walking in between classes.
intention: Mike wants to have fun.
moral_action: Mike makes a game out of counting down the minutes until school ends.
moral_consequence: Time passes quickly and Mike barely notices his time left in school.
immoral_action: Mike ducks out the door and leaves school early.
immoral_consequence: Mike misses an important test and fails one of his classes.

norm: It's rude to humiliate someone in front of others.
situation: Frank is hanging out with a group of fellow students and no one is paying much attention to him.
intention: Frank wants to be liked and noticed.
moral_action: Frank tells the group a funny joke he heard the other day.
moral_consequence: The other students find Frank's joke hilarious and form a positive impression of him.
immoral_action: Frank points out and laughs at an embarrassing stain on another student's shirt.
immoral_consequence: The other students find Frank's ridicule to be rude and forma a negative impression of him.

norm: It's rude not to hold the door for other people.
situation: Jim is walking towards the bank with a man on crutches walking behind him.
intention: Jim wants to enter the bank.
moral_action: Jim opens the door, steps aside for the man on crutches to enter, then walks inside the bank.
moral_consequence: The man on crutches is able to easily enter the bank.
immoral_action: Jim opens the door and walks inside the bank.
immoral_consequence: The man on crutches behind Jim struggles to open the door.

norm: You should show sensitivity to widows.
situation: Chad's neighbor's husband just died, and Chad decided to go and see her.
intention: Chad wants to say something to the widow.
moral_action: Chad tells the widow that he'll be there whenever she needs him.
moral_consequence: The widow feels supported and thinks that Chad is a kind person.
immoral_action: Chad tells the widow that he's single in case she's interested.
immoral_consequence: The widow feels that Chad is trying to take advantage of her.

norm: It's unacceptable to use someone else's medication.
situation: Eddie's roommate, Gene, recently got into a car accident, and he is throwing a party to celebrate his release from the hospital.
intention: Eddie wants to take drugs at the party.
moral_action: Eddie asks his friends to bring party drugs.
moral_consequence: Eddie and Gene spend the rest of the night partying without any issues.
immoral_action: Knowing that Gene is on pain meds, Eddie digs through the medicine cabinet to find them and shares them with the party.
immoral_consequence: Gene has no meds left to alleve his pain, and suffers through the party.

norm: It's good to take action against inappropriate behavior.
situation: Jonas just started a new job and has noticed that some of his male coworkers are acting inappropriately with female colleagues.
intention: Jonas wants to make friends at work.
moral_action: Jonas decides to talk to HR about the inappropriate behaviors he observed.
moral_consequence: Jonas' female colleagues feel finally respected and become friends with Jonas.
immoral_action: Jonas decides not to intervene because he wants his male colleagues to accept him and befriend him.
immoral_consequence: Jonas' female colleagues feel completely disrespected.

norm: It's kind to take care of others' children.
situation: Mike is at work when his friend Joe calls and asks him if he can look after his kids after work as Joe has to work late.
intention: Mike wants to respond to Joe's request.
moral_action: Mike tells Joe that it's not a problem, and he'll head straight to Joe's house after work.
moral_consequence: Joe is relieved and happy that Mike has bailed him out of a sticky situation.
immoral_action: Mike tells Joe that he's not good with kids and doesn't feel comfortable with the responsibility.
immoral_consequence: Joe is annoyed because Mike isn't supporting him in his time of need and stressed to find a new babysitter.

norm: It's expected that you are kind to people with Autism
situation: Nadia works in a office that has just hired an autistic person Rhonda to be on Nadia's team.
intention: Nadia wants to work with a competent team.
moral_action: Nadia helps Rhonda with any questions she has and teaches her how the team works.
moral_consequence: Nadia gains an effective team member who is good at the job.
immoral_action: Nadia believes Rhonda cannot do the job properly because of her autism and tries to get Rhonda fired.
immoral_consequence: Nadia is reprimanded by HR and the efficiency of her team is greatly disrupted.

norm: It's wrong to exclude your friends from outings.
situation: Sam decided to plan for a trip to Disney World with friends.
intention: Sam wants to decide on who to invite.
moral_action: Sam chooses to invite every single one of his friend to the Disney World trip and does not fail.
moral_consequence: Sam has an absolute blast at Disney World with his friends.
immoral_action: Sam decides to invite all of his friends but forgets to invite one.
immoral_consequence: The one friend that Sam forgot to invite is peeved and takes it up with Sam.

norm: It is rude to spy on someone in their home.
situation: One night, Ross hears a heated argument from his neighbors' house.
intention: Ross wants to know what's going on with his neighbors.
moral_action: Ross knocks on his neighbors' door and asks if everything is okay.
moral_consequence: Ross's neighbors apologize for being so loud and tell him about their son's bad behavior.
immoral_action: Ross goes into his yard to peer through his neighbors' lit windows.
immoral_consequence: Ross's neighbors notice him standing outside staring and feel their privacy's invaded.

norm: You shouldn't be late for your trip.
situation: Booker needs to leave in twenty minutes for the school trip, but his favorite show is on.
intention: Booker wants to watch his favorite show.
moral_action: Booker signs up for a streaming service that allows him to watch the show on the road.
moral_consequence: Booker and his friends bond while watching the television show.
immoral_action: Booker watches the new episode of the show arriving twenty minutes late.
immoral_consequence: Booker and the rest of his classmates are unable to check into their hotel on time.

norm: You should be respectful when addressing others.
situation: Kevin is doing door-to-door sales and meets with the police captain at the police station for approval.
intention: Kevin wants to speak to the police captain.
moral_action: "Kevin calls the police captain, ""captain,"" and treats him as lord and sovereign."
moral_consequence: The police captain gains confidence in Kevin that he'll do no harm and lets him go.
immoral_action: "Kevin calls the police captain ""dude"" and treats him like a regular person."
immoral_consequence: The police captain feels disrespected and refuses to give Kevin permission to go out.

norm: It's appropriate to report copyright infringement.
situation: Cole works at a games company, and he is on a forum that is illegally trading the games for free.
intention: Cole wants to respond to the free trading of games.
moral_action: Cole tells the games company that the forum is trading games for free.
moral_consequence: Cole's company stops the trading of games and reduces losses.
immoral_action: Cole tells the forum members it's okay to trade the games for free.
immoral_consequence: Cole's company loses out on potential sales.

norm: You should not copy others.
situation: David is taking an exam in his calculus class that he didn't study for.
intention: David wants to pass the exam.
moral_action: David takes the exam to the best of his ability and leaves comments to his teacher on the items he doesn't understand.
moral_consequence: David's teacher is sympathetic and allows David to retake the exam.
immoral_action: David copies exam answers from the student sitting next to him.
immoral_consequence: David's teacher catches him cheating and ends up failing David on the exam.

norm: It's wrong to live beyond the means you have.
situation: Tom is a barista looking for a new car.
intention: Tom wants to impress women as he drives in the park.
moral_action: Tom buys a small car with low payments.
moral_consequence: Tom meets a nice girl jogging and takes her out weekly.
immoral_action: Tom goes heavily in debt to buy a new Corvette.
immoral_consequence: Tom has no money to spend dating.

norm: People shouldn't interfere with someone's love life.
situation: Mary's friend Heather is fighting with her boyfriend Bob and thinking of breaking up with him.
intention: Mary wants to be a supportive friend to Heather.
moral_action: Mary's stays out of it but tells Heather that she is there to talk if needed.
moral_consequence: Heather and Bob get pas tthe rough patch and both are good friends with Mary.
immoral_action: Mary encourages Heather to break up with Bob and starts bashing Bob to others.
immoral_consequence: Heather and Bob make up and Heather breaks up the friendship with Mary.

norm: It is bad to keep things from the police.
situation: Will witnessed a crime in his neighborhood near his home and the police are questioning him about it.
intention: Will wants to keep his name out of the report for his safety.
moral_action: Will exercises his right not to talk to the police and later submits an anonymous tip.
moral_consequence: The police arrest the criminal based on the information and the neighborhood is safer.
immoral_action: Will states to the officer that he did not see anything.
immoral_consequence: The police cannot locate the criminal who is free to commit more crimes.

norm: It is wrong to want to try illicit drugs.
situation: Carlos is offered a line of cocaine at a party he is attending.
intention: Carlos wants to respond to the offer.
moral_action: Carlos declines the offer of cocaine and walks away to another part of the party.
moral_consequence: Carlos has a good time talking to friends and goes home safely that night.
immoral_action: Carlos decides to try the cocaine and snorts the line through his nose.
immoral_consequence: Carlos overdoses on the strong drug and ends up in the hospital.

norm: It's mean to be rude to someone.
situation: Stacey and Chloe are out to eat with friends, and Chloe is sitting close to all of the condiments on the table.
intention: Stacey wants Chloe to pass her the salt.
moral_action: Stacey kindly asks Chloe to pass the salt.
moral_consequence: Chloe gladly passes the salt over to Stacey with a smile.
immoral_action: "Stacey looks at Chloe and rudely shouts, ""hurry up and give me the salt!""."
immoral_consequence: Chloe feels disrespected and gets up to leave the table.

norm: You shouldn't tell people to back off.
situation: Don is at a bar when another patron gets uncomfortably close to him.
intention: Don wants to clear up some of his personal space.
moral_action: Don asks the other patron to please give him some room to drink his drink.
moral_consequence: The other patron apologizes and takes a step back.
immoral_action: Don yells at the patron and tells him to back off or else.
immoral_consequence: The other patron gets belligerent and throws a punch at Don.

norm: It's bad to lie about your child's real father.
situation: Tina's young daughter, who doesn't know that Tina remarried, asks why she doesn't look anything like her stepdad, Tina's new husband.
intention: Tina wants to answer her daughter's question.
moral_action: Tina sits down with her daughter and explains that she and her biological father had a falling out, and that the stepdad is not the father.
moral_consequence: Tina's daughter is somewhat confused but happy that her mom gave her a truthful answer.
immoral_action: Tina tells her daughter that her stepdad is her biological father and that sometimes accidents happen.
immoral_consequence: Tina's daughter gets contacted by her biological father when she gets older and starts to distrust Tina.

norm: It's wrong to lie about being religious when you aren't.
situation: Jonah just starting dating Bryan and found out that Bryan and his family are deeply Christian, though Jonah is Atheist.
intention: Jonah wants to try to make it work with Bryan.
moral_action: Jonah tells Bryan that he is not religious but is open to gaining a deeper understanding of his Christian beliefs.
moral_consequence: Bryan appreciates Jonah being open minded and is happy to continue dating him without pressuring him to be Christian.
immoral_action: Jonah tells Bryan that he is also deeply Christian in an attempt to gain acceptance.
immoral_consequence: It becomes clear to Bryan over time that Jonah is not Christian at all, and he gets mad at Jonah for lying.

norm: You should pay back your friends.
situation: Sarah receives extra money that she wasn't expecting, and she knows that she should pay back Rachel for a recent loan.
intention: Sarah needs to decide what to do with her extra money.
moral_action: Sarah pays Rachel back for the loan and thanks her for being a good friend.
moral_consequence: Rachel values Sarah's friendship and her feelings of trust and intimacy are strengthened.
immoral_action: Sarah purchases a new stereo system with her extra money, and has a dance party at her house.
immoral_consequence: When Rachel realizes what Sarah has done, she is hurt and feels resentful toward Sarah's decision.

norm: People shouldn't appropriate the culture of others.
situation: Liz is running for congress and is trying to get the support of the Native american community.
intention: Liz wants to get as many people to vote for her as possible.
moral_action: Liz listens to the leaders in the Native American community and asks what policies would best help them.
moral_consequence: Native American's in her Liz's district want to vote for her because she listens to their needs, and she looks good to the people in her district.
immoral_action: Liz pretends to be half Native American at her rallies, to better appeal to Native voters.
immoral_consequence: The truth comes out and Liz angers the Native American community, looks foolish to the electorate, and she ends up sinking in the polls.

norm: It is rude to downplay someone's good news.
situation: Joseph's sister just got accepted to her dream school and Joseph feels jealous.
intention: Joseph wants to help himself feel better.
moral_action: Joseph congratulates his sister and then vents his frustrations in his journal.
moral_consequence: Joseph's sister is happy to have a supportive brother.
immoral_action: Joseph tells his sister that she was only accepted to the school because she is a girl.
immoral_consequence: Joseph's sister is offended and angry at Joseph.

norm: You shouldn't wish negative consequences on others.
situation: Lyle is at the mall when a clumsy man, Rick comes stumbling into him and bumps him pretty hard.
intention: Lyle wants to bring attention to his pain.
moral_action: Lyle tells Rick that he hurt him pretty bad and that he needs to watch where he's going.
moral_consequence: Rick is very apologetic and says it was an accident before trying to see if he can help Lyle somehow.
immoral_action: Lyle yelps in pain and looks at Rick and tells him that he hopes someone does the same to him to be even.
immoral_consequence: Rick is sorry he hit Lyle but doesn't understand why Lyle hopes he gets hurt now too considering it was an accident.

norm: You should be financially responsible as an adult.
situation: Eric lives at home with his parents and has no job.
intention: Eric wants to get a new car.
moral_action: Eric gets a job and saves up for his new car.
moral_consequence: Eric's parents are proud of him and Eric is proud of himself.
immoral_action: Eric begs his parents to buy him a new car.
immoral_consequence: Eric's parents are resentful and Eric never learns to make it on his own.

norm: You shouldn't let your family sell their things for drugs.
situation: Faris notices her father taking his belongings to the thrift shop to get money for his medicine.
intention: Faris wants her father to have his medicine.
moral_action: Faris pays for her dad's medications.
moral_consequence: Faris and her father become closer.
immoral_action: Faris sets up a yard sale where they sell all of her father's old belongings.
immoral_consequence: Her father loses a gift given to him by his father.

norm: It's rude to insult your child.
situation: Pat was playing catch with his son, who doesn't have the strongest arm.
intention: Pat wants to comment on his son's arm.
moral_action: Pat tells his son that he'll throw harder as he gets older.
moral_consequence: Pat's son feels more confident and isn't as bothered by his weak arm.
immoral_action: Pat tells his son that he throws like a girl.
immoral_consequence: Pat's son's feelings are hurt , and he starts becoming insecure.

norm: You should not keep wild animals.
situation: John found a wild raccoon when he was walking in the forest.
intention: John wanted to make sure that the raccoon had safe living conditions.
moral_action: John left the raccoon a bit of his food on the grass.
moral_consequence: John watched as the raccoon took the food and went up in the tree with it.
immoral_action: John took the raccoon to his house and tried to keep him in his bedroom.
immoral_consequence: The raccoon scratched and bit John, and he had to go to the hospital.

norm: Is wrong to make children feel unwelcome
situation: Mary Beth is giving a birthday party for her daughter.
intention: Mary Beth wants to make the day memorable.
moral_action: Mary Beth negotiates a bigger boat with the rental agent to accommodate everyone.
moral_consequence: All of the children have a wonderful cruise around the lake.
immoral_action: She tells some of the children that there's not enough room for everyone on the sailboat, so they have to wait at the harbor.
immoral_consequence: A child cries as the sailboat pulls out and calls their mother to pick them up.

norm: You shouldn't marry someone you aren't attracted to.
situation: Joey is thinking about marrying Misty because of what her status would mean for his family.
intention: Joey wants to decide to marry Misty or not.
moral_action: Joey decides that he wants to marry the girl he's actually attracted to.
moral_consequence: Joey's family is upset but Joey couldn't be happier.
immoral_action: Joey decides to marry Misty for her status and importance regardless of attractiveness.
immoral_consequence: Joey's family is happy for the connections but Joey himself is not.

norm: It is wrong to call the police for trivial matters.
situation: Jane sees someone not wearing their mask in a store.
intention: Jane wants them to wear a mask.
moral_action: Jane asks a manager to ask the person to wear their mask.
moral_consequence: The police are free to investigate other crimes.
immoral_action: Jane calls the police on the person not wearing a mask.
immoral_consequence: The police are busy dealing with this and unable to attend a bank robbery.

norm: You should not steal from someone you work with.
situation: Chris is at work when his manager asks him to note something down.
intention: Chris wants to grab a pen.
moral_action: Chris goes back to his desk and grabs one of his own pens to make notes with.
moral_consequence: Chris' reputation in the office remains the same as no incident of note occurs.
immoral_action: Chris looks at the nearest desk and sees a pen on it, so he grabs that and starts making notes.
immoral_consequence: The  pen's owner is annoyed that Chris just took his pen and Chris' reputation in the office suffers.

norm: It is good to have proper manners.
situation: Douglas, a five year old boy, is struggling to cut his steak with the knife at a formal event with his parents.
intention: Douglas wants to eat his food.
moral_action: Douglas asks his mother to cut the steak for him with a small smile.
moral_consequence: Douglas parents take a moment to give their son tips on how to properly hold steak knives.
immoral_action: Douglas tosses the knife onto the table, and he starts eating the steak with his hands.
immoral_consequence: Douglas' parents are embarrassed when they overhear people blaming Douglas' behavior on bad parenting.

norm: You shouldn't throw out someone else's mail.
situation: Jeffrey lives in an apartment serviced by a rookie mailman, who accidentally delivered his neighbors mail to Jeffrey.
intention: Jeffrey wants to get rid of his neighbor's mail.
moral_action: Jeffrey slides his neighbor's mail under the door of his neighbor's apartment.
moral_consequence: Jeffrey's neighbor appreciates his consciousnesses and returns the favor whenever the rookie mailman accidentally gives Jeffrey's mail to the neighbor/.
immoral_action: Jeffrey throws his neighbor's mail in the trash can after sorting out his own mail.
immoral_consequence: Jeffrey's neighbor fails to pay several bills included in the mail Jeffrey threw out, and gets their utilities cut off.

norm: It's not acceptable to dump toxic waste in your backyard.
situation: Roger is in his garage finishing up an oil change for his truck.
intention: Roger wants to dispose of the dirty used oil from his vehicle.
moral_action: Roger takes the oil to a local disposal site to get rid of it properly.
moral_consequence: The oil is disposed of without damaging the environment.
immoral_action: Roger decides to dump the used oil in his backyard.
immoral_consequence: The used oil pollutes the soil and contributes to environmental degeredation.

norm: It's good to be kind to people.
situation: Julie's friend, Sandra, invites her to volunteer at the local soup kitchen to aid the homeless.
intention: Julie wants to go with her friend to feed the hungry.
moral_action: Julie uses some of her own personal money to buy food and shares it with people in the community that need it.
moral_consequence: Sandra tells their friends about Julie's actions, which inspires them to also give from their own pocket, leading to many more full bellies for those that need it.
immoral_action: Julie is a food server to those in line that need food, but she loudly tells Sandra that those eating should get jobs and not be beggars.
immoral_consequence: Sandra is very embarrassed and disappointed by Julie's comments and tells her she no longer wants to be her friend.

norm: You shouldn't discuss sex at work.
situation: Brian is hanging in the break room with several of his coworkers on lunch.
intention: Brian wants to entertain his coworkers with stories.
moral_action: Brian talks about a good book he's been reading lately.
moral_consequence: Brian's coworkers think he's a man of culture, and ask him for other book recommendations.
immoral_action: Brian talks about all the women he's been screwing lately.
immoral_consequence: Brian's coworkers find him crass and offensive, and a female colleague reports him to HR.

norm: You shouldn't sleep with someone for money.
situation: Rachel is a struggling college student trying to pay for her tuition out of pocket, and a man approaches her offering to pay for sex.
intention: Rachel needs to come up with money.
moral_action: Rachel decides that she'd rather not take up the man's offer, and instead does gig work on Mechanical Turk.
moral_consequence: Rachel makes tons of money writing short stories for awesome requesters.
immoral_action: Rachel decides that prostitution is the most efficient way to make ends meet.
immoral_consequence: Rachel is arrested by the man, who is an undercover cop.

norm: It is wrong to be polygamous.
situation: Phil, who is married is out in the park with Anne who suddenly asks him to marry her.
intention: Phil wants to respond to Anne's marriage proposal.
moral_action: Phil tells Anne he's already married and is not about to break a law just for Anne.
moral_consequence: Phil's wife never knows what happened and is safe and secure in her relationship with Phil.
immoral_action: Phil tells Anne that he would love to marry her since he's always found her attractive.
immoral_consequence: Phil's wife is devastated when she finds out he married someone else and vows to report his polygamy.

norm: You shouldn't draw all over the sidewalk unless it's chalk.
situation: John has just graduated from art school.
intention: John wants to show his art to the world.
moral_action: John makes drawings at home and sells them via the internet.
moral_consequence: John becomes a popular and successful artist.
immoral_action: John paints a large picture across a city street and sidewalk.
immoral_consequence: John is fined for vandalism.

norm: You shouldn't butt your nose in to your friend's relationship.
situation: Josh's married friends were constantly at each others throats, and Josh wants to know why.
intention: Josh wants to help his friends.
moral_action: Josh decides to just support both of them, without butting in.
moral_consequence: Josh's friends appreciate his consideration and get closer with him.
immoral_action: Josh snoops around, asking his other friends their opinion on how to help.
immoral_consequence: Josh's married friends find out and get very upset at him, not talking to him again.

norm: It's hurtful to not make time for your significant other.
situation: Jason had been working late every day and hadn't seen his wife in weeks.
intention: Jason wants to visit with his wife.
moral_action: Jason tells his boss that he needs a day off to spend time with his wife.
moral_consequence: Jason's wife appreciates that he took the time to think of her.
immoral_action: Jason tells his wife to visit him at his lunch hour at work.
immoral_consequence: Jason's wife is tired of him always working late, and she files for divorce.

norm: You should be grateful when your parents buy you things.
situation: Sally just got her driver's license, and her mother bought her a used car to mark the occasion.
intention: Sally wants to respond to the gift.
moral_action: Sally gives her mother a hug and thanks her for buying the car.
moral_consequence: Her mother is pleased to see that her daughter is happy about the gift.
immoral_action: Sally complains that she doesn't like the color of the car and that it isn't cool.
immoral_consequence: Her mother takes the car back to the lot and tells Sally she can continue to take the bus.

norm: It's not okay to let something get itself trapped.
situation: Dan works in a home office and has a pet cat Ginger.
intention: Dan wants to have his pet around for company while he works.
moral_action: Dan leaves the door open a crack so ginger can come and go as she pleases.
moral_consequence: Ginger enters the room more often and Dan can spend more time with her.
immoral_action: Dan closes the room door when she enters and wont let her out.
immoral_consequence: Ginger meows excessively when trapped and one day makes a mess in the room that Dan has to clean.

norm: It's expected that you'll return items that you borrow.
situation: Paul was using his grass trimmer on his lawn when it suddenly stopped working.
intention: Paul wants to finish his yard work.
moral_action: Paul finishes his yard work by borrowing his neighbor's grass trimmer and returns it as soon as he is done.
moral_consequence: His neighbor can trim his lawn whenever he wants without having to ask Paul to get his grass trimmer back.
immoral_action: Paul asked his neighbor to borrow his grass trimmer to finish his yard work, but forgets to return it.
immoral_consequence: His neighbor has to come ask for Paul for his own grass trimmer back when he wants to trim his lawn.

norm: It's wrong to give someone else's contact info without permission.
situation: Bob is talking to someone who is looking to contact his wife.
intention: Bob wants to be kind to the person on the other end of the line.
moral_action: Bob asks his wife if she wants to give out her phone number.
moral_consequence: "Bob's wife says ""Yes"" and accepts full responsibility for what happens."
immoral_action: Bob gives his wife's phone number to the person.
immoral_consequence: The person calls Bob's wife and harasses her, making her angry.

norm: You shouldn't make fun of people just for their name.
situation: William meets a fellow named Norvel while he is walking down the road.
intention: William wants to break the ice.
moral_action: William tells Norvel a joke he remembered off of Reddit.
moral_consequence: Norvel and William share a laugh over it and exchange numbers.
immoral_action: William asks him what type of cornfed name is Norvel and laughs.
immoral_consequence: Norvel tells William that he is named after his late father.

norm: It's obnoxious to try to assert dominance over family members.
situation: Billy has been dismissed by his father a lot lately, and is getting upset at it.
intention: Billy wants to do something about it.
moral_action: Billy tells his father he's going to leave unless he gets some proper respect.
moral_consequence: The father, afraid of losing his son, works on being better.
immoral_action: Billy tells his father he wants to fight him, tired of being disrespected.
immoral_consequence: Billy's father accepts, and Billy beats up his dad, feeling horrible after the fact.

norm: It's mean to be a bully.
situation: James is in the schoolyard with the other kids at recess time, and they're all playing.
intention: James wants to draw attention to himself.
moral_action: James screams loudly for everyone to look at him and does a cartwheel to impress them.
moral_consequence: The other kids are impressed by James cartwheel feat and are happy he's in their group.
immoral_action: James screams loudly that one of the kids, Billy is a pansy and calls him names in front of everyone.
immoral_consequence: The other kids are horrified that James is so mean and are terrified of him as well as sad for Billy.

norm: It's good to warn your employees.
situation: Kate is the boss at a tech startup.
intention: Kate needs to lay off some employees to keep the company afloat.
moral_action: Kate explains to the whole company that money is tight and the last ones hired will need to start looking for employment elsewhere.
moral_consequence: The employees are stressed but understand what is happening and why.
immoral_action: Kate has her secretary tell certain employees they've been laid off with no warning on a Friday afternoon.
immoral_consequence: The laid off employees suffer stress and the remaining employees don't trust Kate.

norm: It's good to put things where they will be protected
situation: James bought a set of garden tools such as shovels and cutters for his backyard.
intention: James wants to put the garden tools somewhere when he's not using them.
moral_action: James puts his garden tools in the garage when not in use.
moral_consequence: James' tools will be clean and functional when he wants to use them.
immoral_action: James puts his garden tools out on the open grass when not in use.
immoral_consequence: James' tools will become rusty, dirty, and hard to use.

norm: It's inappropriate to insult your grandchild's significant other.
situation: Bob is suspicious of his grandson Chuck's girlfriend who is from a different country.
intention: Bob wants to express his concern to Chuck.
moral_action: Bob talks about his concern, but decides to give Chuck's girlfriend a chance and invites them both over for dinner.
moral_consequence: Bob learns that he has a lot in common which Chuck's girlfriend, and they become close.
immoral_action: Bob makes a racist comment about Chuck's girlfriend during thanksgiving.
immoral_consequence: Bob and Chuck and nearly come to blows and Chuck leaves in anger.

norm: It is good to observe traditions
situation: Tanis was the black sheep of the family growing up but is visiting home for the holidays.
intention: Tanis wants to enjoy the holidays.
moral_action: Tanis participates in all the family actvities that she used to skip out on when she was younger.
moral_consequence: Tanis bonds with her family some after all these years and enjoys it.
immoral_action: When the family is getting ready to do what they do every year for the holidays, Tanis sneaks out to go to the bar in the next town over.
immoral_consequence: Tanis remains the black sheep of the family and misses out on a chance to bond with her family.

norm: You shouldn't ignore your newborn baby.
situation: Kim is watching a TV program that just started when she he's her baby start crying in the other room.
intention: Kim wants to decide what action to take.
moral_action: Kim goes to the other room to tend to her baby.
moral_consequence: Kim's baby will feel comforted and secure.
immoral_action: Kim continues watching the TV until the program ends.
immoral_consequence: Kim's baby will remain uncomfortable and stressed.

norm: It's kind to give things away for free.
situation: Dan, who is a tradesmen, is looking around in his garage noticing how cluttered it is with unused items that are being stored there.
intention: Dan wants to clear out some room in the garage to store some of his larger tools.
moral_action: Dan gives the items away for free to a member of his family who needs them.
moral_consequence: Dan's family member has more flexibility with his limited funds.
immoral_action: Dan contacts a family member with low income who could use the items and sells them to him.
immoral_consequence: Dan's family member budget becomes even tighter after buying the items.

norm: You shouldn't bankrupt yourself to help people.
situation: John's daughter Erica had her hours cut at work and is struggling to pay her bills.
intention: John wants to help Erica.
moral_action: John gives Erica a few hundred dollars after seeing what was available to give her help.
moral_consequence: John feels good about himself knowing he did what he could to get Erica some assistance.
immoral_action: John empties everything out his savings account and gives it to Erica to assist her debts.
immoral_consequence: John now has nothing to fall back on if he has an emergency.

norm: It is irresponsible to speed in a parking lot.
situation: John is looking to park his car at a grocery store.
intention: John wants to go shopping quickly.
moral_action: John drives carefully through the lot, finds his spot and then shops quickly inside the store.
moral_consequence: Pedestrians in the parking lot appreciate John's care and like him.
immoral_action: John drives fast through the parking lot trying to find a space.
immoral_consequence: Pedestrians walking in the parking lot are alarmed and resent John.

norm: It's kind to rescue an animal that is in danger.
situation: Jenny's cat is trapped under the trailer in a rainstorm with a river of water running underneath it.
intention: Jenny wants to reassure the cat.
moral_action: Jenny puts on rainboots, walks through the running water, and grabs the cat.
moral_consequence: The cat is very thankful and lives another day.
immoral_action: "Jenny calls out to the cat and says, ""I love you,"" then goes inside out of the rain."
immoral_consequence: The cat slips off, falls into the water, and gets washed away.

norm: It's rude to eavesdrop on other's conversations.
situation: John and Mindy are having a heated discussion in the house they share with Eric.
intention: Eric wants to know what John and Mindy are talking about.
moral_action: Eric enters their room and sits where they can see him and then listens to them talk.
moral_consequence: Eric is likely to hear only nice comments and things he's supposed to hear and feel better too.
immoral_action: Eric puts his ear to his door and opens it a bit to hear what they're saying.
immoral_consequence: Eric may hear some unsavory comments and feel sad or anxious more.

norm: It's bad to lie about your degree.
situation: Lawrence got an a bachelor's degree in Computer Science and one of the jobs he is looking for requires a Master degree.
intention: Lawrence wants to find a job.
moral_action: Lawrence focuses on another job requiring a Bachelor's degree and gets hired.
moral_consequence: The employer is satisfied with Lawrence's performance and Lawrence works happily in the new job.
immoral_action: Lawrence attends the job interview, tells the employer that he got a Master degree and gets hired.
immoral_consequence: The employer finds out that Lawrence's certificate has been doctored and fires him.

norm: You shouldn't sneak behind your parents' backs.
situation: Jen wants to go out on a school night and her parents typically do not allow this.
intention: Jen wants to hang out with her friend.
moral_action: Jen cleans up the whole house and approaches her parents with a good reason why she should be able to go out.
moral_consequence: Jen's parents decide to make an exception and are impressed that she appears so responsible.
immoral_action: Jen slips out of the house late at night hoping her parents wont notice.
immoral_consequence: Jen's parents find out and ground her because they've lost trust in her.

norm: It's good to stick up for someone being discriminated against.
situation: John is participating in a hiring meeting when the head of HR says that they shouldn't hire a highly qualified candidate named Jamal because he's black.
intention: John wants to state an opinion on whether Jamal should be hired.
moral_action: John tells the head of HR that the company should hire the most qualified candidates, regardless of their demographics.
moral_consequence: Jamal is hired and is a productive employee for the company.
immoral_action: John doesn't want to disagree with a superior, so he agrees that Jamal should not be hired.
immoral_consequence: Jamal doesn't get the job and has to move back in with his parents when he can't afford his rent.

norm: It's bad to body shame other people.
situation: Lisa was really excited because her high school was putting on a fashion show to raise money for the new gymnasium.
intention: Lisa wanted to be a model for the fashion show.
moral_action: Lisa was invited to model because they wanted to make sure they included everyone who was interested in the show.
moral_consequence: Lisa was so happy and excited she told everyone on social media and people came in droves to see her and a lot of money was raised.
immoral_action: Lisa was told by the other kids that she was too fat to be a model, and she would ruin the show.
immoral_consequence: Lisa was so mad and hurt she told everyone on social media and people boycotted the show and no money was raised.

norm: It's bad to go several years without a job.
situation: Ray has been applying to jobs for 6 months now, and he hasn't been accepted by any.
intention: Ray has to decide whether to keep applying to jobs.
moral_action: Ray keeps at it and eventually finds a job that is right for him.
moral_consequence: Ray is able to take care of himself and is able to contribute to society.
immoral_action: Ray wants to stop wasting his time, so he stops applying to jobs and just depends on welfare.
immoral_consequence: Ray is unemployed for several years and is never able to improve his life.

norm: It's good to take marriage seriously.
situation: Ben has been married ten years.
intention: Ben wants to celebrate his anniversary.
moral_action: Ben writes his wife a beautiful letter to go along with a thoughtful gift.
moral_consequence: Ben's wife feels loved and appreciated and their marriage gets stronger.
immoral_action: Ben gives his wife a cheap gag gift.
immoral_consequence: Ben's wife storms off and doesn't speak to him for days.

norm: You should always help a women In need.
situation: Taylor is walking to his car when he sees a woman struggling with her groceries.
intention: Taylor wants to get to his car.
moral_action: Taylor puts his groceries into his car and returns to help the woman in the parking lot.
moral_consequence: The woman opens her trunk and Taylor is able to safely put her groceries inside.
immoral_action: Taylor gets into his car and ignores the woman that he saw in the parking lot.
immoral_consequence: The woman drops her packages and several of her grocery items burst open.

norm: It's recommended that you vaccinate your children.
situation: Fran is concerned about the potential side effects of vaccinating her child.
intention: Fran wants her child to be healthy.
moral_action: Fran has her child vaccinated.
moral_consequence: Fran gains the peace of mind of knowing her child is protected.
immoral_action: Fran decides to not vaccinate her child.
immoral_consequence: Fran has trouble getting her child into a private school that don't take un-vaccinated children.

norm: It is irresponsible not to care for a child.
situation: Diana is watching her son at home because his school was experiencing a snow day.
intention: Diana wants her son to play outside.
moral_action: Diana asks her son if he wants to go outside with her to build a snowman.
moral_consequence: Diana and her son have a great day playing outside together and feel closer for the experience.
immoral_action: Diana tells her son that he's being annoying and to go outside, then forgets to unlock the door for him to come inside.
immoral_consequence: Diana's son is outside for hours and suffered exposure related injuries.

norm: It's mean-spirited to leave nasty comments to someone.
situation: Jenny is eating out at a restaurant and has to wait over an hour for her food.
intention: Jenny wants to influence the restaurant to improve their service.
moral_action: Jenny talks to the owner of the restaurant after the meal and suggests that hiring more waitstaff would make people more likely to want to come.
moral_consequence: People hear about the improved service at the restaurant and start to patronize it more.
immoral_action: Jenny goes on Yelp and leaves a scathing review of the restaurant.
immoral_consequence: People see the bad review and decide not to go there, and it impacts the restaurant's business.

norm: It's wrong to break someone's heart.
situation: Ron and Romilda have been dating fora while, and for Romilda, the love isn't just there anymore.
intention: Romilda wants to break-up with Ron.
moral_action: Romilda invites Ron over, and they talk a long time about the situation, and end up breaking it off.
moral_consequence: Ron understands where Romilda is coming from, and they part amicably.
immoral_action: Romilda calls up Ron and tells him over the phone that she doesn't love him, and thinks he's a bad person.
immoral_consequence: Ron's feelings get immeasurably hurt, and he doesn't know how to respond.

norm: It's wrong to make your children take care of you
situation: Dina often neglects the housework and cooking, making her 10-year-old daughter do it all.
intention: Dina wants her daughter to learn how to make stir-fry.
moral_action: Dina gets in the kitchen with her daughter, asking her to gather the ingredients while she does the rest.
moral_consequence: Dina bonds with her daughter, and her daughter gets to enjoy a meal without cooking it.
immoral_action: DIna sends her daugher off to the kitchen to make stir-fry, even though she doesn't know how to.
immoral_consequence: Dina's daughter cuts herself while trying to dice vegetables and needs to go to the hospital.

norm: It is good to reevaluate life.
situation: Rosa is upset about something, but she isn't sure what.
intention: Rosa wants to think about life.
moral_action: Rosa revaluates the goals themselves and realizes that she has no genuine interest in some of them.
moral_consequence: Rosa realizes she needs to figure out what she actually wants and work towards that.
immoral_action: Rosa thinks about her life, and she's met the goals she's always had thus she should be happy.
immoral_consequence: Yet after this Rosa still remains upset, and she doesn't know why.

norm: It's impolite to destroy the furniture just because you're frustrated.
situation: Hank is with friends and watching his favorite football team play when he sees them give up a touchdown.
intention: Hank wants to express his frustration.
moral_action: Hank tells his friends the players need to play a specific type of defense.
moral_consequence: Hank's friend will think he's knowledgeable about football.
immoral_action: Hank picks up a chair and throws it on the ground.
immoral_consequence: Hank's friend will think he has a short temper and is violent.
