norm: It's good to return people's wallets to them.
situation: Dennis is walking his dog, and he finds a wallet laying by the curb.
intention: Dennis wants to get home in a hurry because it has started to rain.
moral_action: Dennis hurries home and calls the person that owns the wallet to tell them he found it and can return it.
moral_consequence: The person that owns the wallet tells Dennis how grateful they are for getting their wallet back and offers him a reward.
immoral_action: Dennis hurries home with his dog and the wallet and decides he will keep the wallet because he needs the money.
immoral_consequence: Then Dennis feels guilty for keeping the wallet because he knows he didn't do the right thing.

norm: Is wrong to steal clients from your employer
situation: John is an accountant leaving his employer of several years to start his own business.
intention: John wants to start his new business off with lots of clients.
moral_action: John advertises heavily prior to opening his business, and gets many new clients when he opens.
moral_consequence: John's business thrives while earning reasonable rates from his new customers.
immoral_action: John copies the e-mails of several top clients at his old job and reaches out to them with lower rates than his old employer which they accept.
immoral_consequence: John's old employer finds out about this, and responds in kind with an insuing pricing war.

norm: You shouldn't ask your child to buy you booze.
situation: May is having friends over for dinner.
intention: May wants her guests to enjoy themselves.
moral_action: May asks one of her friends to pick up some wine on the way to her place.
moral_consequence: May hosts a successful dinner party.
immoral_action: May is running behind, and so she sends her underage son to the bodega for some wine.
immoral_consequence: May gets in trouble with the police when the bodega owner calls them on her son.

norm: It's good to learn about sex when you're old enough.
situation: Leah is a teenager raised in a conservative Christian family who only taught her about abstinence, but she has started dating a boy from her school who she really likes.
intention: Leah wants to become more intimate with her boyfriend.
moral_action: Leah does her own research online and calls her doctor to ask her for advice on how to have safe sex.
moral_consequence: Leah has healthy, safe, and consensual sex with her boyfriend.
immoral_action: Leah just follows her boyfriend's lead, and they secretly have sex without using protection.
immoral_consequence: Leah finds out that she is pregnant a few months later.

norm: It is wrong to lie to your employeer.
situation: Joe has stayed up all night binge watching a series and is scheduled to work early in the morning.
intention: Joe wants to take the day off.
moral_action: Joe uses a day of his paid vacation and takes a personal day.
moral_consequence: Joe is reinforcing responsible habits.
immoral_action: Joe tells his boss that he is sick and can't come in.
immoral_consequence: Joe feels bad and irresponsible about lying.

norm: It's rude to single someone out in class.
situation: Roy has a class full of students who are bad at math.
intention: Roy wants to point out their errors.
moral_action: Roy points out a common error made by the class as a whole.
moral_consequence: The class pays attention to the error and makes an effort to correct it.
immoral_action: Roy points out a specific error made by only one student.
immoral_consequence: The class laughs at that one student for their error in class.

norm: It's irresponsible to make a mess at home.
situation: Wayne and Iris are just finishing up dinner at their kitchen table and Wayne has finished his meal.
intention: Wayne wants to put his empty plate somewhere.
moral_action: Wayne takes his empty plate and rinses it quickly before putting it in the dishwasher.
moral_consequence: Iris is happy that she's with a guy who knows to put things where they belong, and she doesn't have to chase after him.
immoral_action: Wayne takes his empty plate and puts it on the kitchen counter and leaves to go watch TV.
immoral_consequence: Iris is annoyed that Wayne put the empty plate on the counter where it doesn't belong.

norm: Siblings should be kind to each other.
situation: Declan notices Olivia studying for her math test.
intention: Delcan wants to have fun with his sister.
moral_action: Delcan creates a math based game for himself and Maria.
moral_consequence: Maria bonds with her brother through the game.
immoral_action: Delcan takes Olivia's study materials hiding them for a game of hide and seek.
immoral_consequence: Maria is unable to study for her test.

norm: It's immoral to sell yourself to someone.
situation: Jamal is a poor person from a West African country, and a man from France offered to buy him to work for him.
intention: Jamal has to respond to the offer.
moral_action: Jamal refuses to sell himself to the man and tells him to leave his country.
moral_consequence: Jamal feels more pride in himself and is happy that he doesn't belong to anyone.
immoral_action: Jamal agrees to sell himself to the man because he needs the money.
immoral_consequence: jamal suffers while working under the man and rethinks his decision.

norm: It's wrong to be ungrateful for a gift.
situation: Billy's mom buys him a new bike for his birthday that isn't the color he wanted, and she asks how he likes it.
intention: Billy wants to answer his mother's question.
moral_action: Billy tells his mother that he loves the bike and can't wait to ride it.
moral_consequence: Billy's mother feels loved and appreciated and is thrilled to hear that Billy likes it.
immoral_action: Billy tells his mother he doesn't like it all that much and it isn't the color he wanted.
immoral_consequence: Billy's mother is sad that her gift wasn't liked and appreciated.

norm: It is rude to be disruptive when people are eating.
situation: Kyle who is a waiter is watching over his customers Pam and Sam who are eating their meal.
intention: Kyle wants to make sure Pam and Sam's meal is OK so far.
moral_action: Kyle walks into the field of view of Pam and Sam and does a thumbs up gesture while raising his eyebrows.
moral_consequence: Both Pam and Sam return the gesture to let him know they're good and appreciate that he didn't make them speak.
immoral_action: Kyle walks up to Pam and Sam's table and asks them while they're chewing if everything is good.
immoral_consequence: Both Pam and Sam are annoyed as they feel rushed to chew through their current bite to answer Kyle's question.

norm: It is inconsiderate to force your views on others.
situation: Terri is a person with very strong political views, and is at a Super Bowl party with a bunch of people.
intention: Terri wants to express her political views.
moral_action: Terri mentions something about kneeling players, but otherwise keeps the conversation about football.
moral_consequence: People find Terri nice to be around and invite her to parties.
immoral_action: Terri won't stop talking politics and ultimately gets into an argument with someone of a different political view.
immoral_consequence: Terri stops getting invited to parties and people try to avoid her.

norm: It's good to wake up early.
situation: Phil is a gig worker on AMT and there's a particularly contested batch of HITs he wants to participate on that always go pretty fast in the morning.
intention: Phil needs to make some money.
moral_action: Phil sets his alarm early the following morning and wakes up to see the batch is still available to be worked on.
moral_consequence: Phil happily gets to work on the HITs and manages to make enough money for the day in only a couple hours.
immoral_action: Phil decides to sleep in and try and catch these HITs at a normal hour, but they're all gone, and he does penny transcription HITs instead.
immoral_consequence: Phil has to spend twenty hours transcribing customer receipts in order to make decent money.

norm: Is important to compromise with your significant other
situation: Roland and Mandy are a couple that are arguing over whether to go to a movie or stay in and watch Netflix.
intention: Roland wants to go to a movie.
moral_action: Roland agrees to watch something on Netflix tonight if they go to a movie tomorrow.
moral_consequence: Mandy and Roland have a good time and enjoy each other's company.
immoral_action: Roland stands firm and insists that they go to the movie.
immoral_consequence: Mandy resents Roland for his stubbornness and the couple grow apart.

norm: You should share food with your family.
situation: Pierce keeps a special stash of cookies for himself but his daughter is asking to have one since the family supply has run out.
intention: Pierce wants to have enough cookies for himself.
moral_action: Pierce gives his daughter one of his cookies and goes out to buy more to replenish his stash and the family supply.
moral_consequence: Pierce's daughter is happy and has a steady supply of further cookies.
immoral_action: Pierce tells his daughter she cannot have a cookie because they are for him only.
immoral_consequence: Pierce's daughter doesn't understand why her father won't share with her and cries.

norm: It's bad to tease someone because of how they act.
situation: Homer was attending a summer block party with all the people from his neighborhood.
intention: Homer wanted to interact with people at the party.
moral_action: Homer complimented a woman on the attractive summer dress that she was wearing.
moral_consequence: Homer made a new friend and enjoyed spending time with her.
immoral_action: Homer started talking to a man with a stutter, then started making fun of his speech problem.
immoral_consequence: Homer was not invited to any more neighborhood events due to his rude action.

norm: It's wrong to get into relationships with students.
situation: Tyler, who is a professor, has been single for a year and has an attractive student show romantic interest in him.
intention: Tyler wants to start dating again.
moral_action: Tyler turns down his student and instead decides to download a dating app.
moral_consequence: The student is able to properly focus and have a more appropriate relationship with her professor.
immoral_action: Tyler decides to get romantically involved with the student from his class.
immoral_consequence: The student performs poorly in the class due to their relationship.

norm: It's good to remind your partner of important things.
situation: Jeremy and Luke have been married for four years and their wedding anniversary is coming up.
intention: Jeremy wants Luke to make reservations for their anniversary dinner.
moral_action: Jeremy consistenly asks Luke if he has made reservations at the restaurant.
moral_consequence: Luke eventually makes a reservation at the restaurant, and they go on to have a lovely anniversary dinner date.
immoral_action: Jeremy assumes Luke has made reservations and doesn't bring up their upcoming dinner until the night of.
immoral_consequence: Jeremy finds out Luke forgot to make reservations, and they spend the night bickering.

norm: You shouldn't break someone's window.
situation: Jude spent the night housesitting for his parents, and left for work leaving both the housekey and his wallet on the kitchen table.
intention: Jude needs to get to his wallet.
moral_action: Jude calls his parents and asks where the spare key is hidden, retrieving it and getting inside to grab his wallet.
moral_consequence: Jude's parents appreciate his quick problem solving abilities and are impressed.
immoral_action: Jude breaks a window and climbs inside to grab his wallet.
immoral_consequence: Jude's parents are angry with him when they get home.

norm: It is mean to criticize people
situation: Chris is working with two new hires at his job teaching them the routine at work.
intention: Chris wants to give the new hires performance feedback.
moral_action: Chris gives the new hires feedback based on very low standards set to accommodate for the learning process.
moral_consequence: The new hires are eager to improve and work hard towards becoming fully trained at work.
immoral_action: Chris tells the new hires that he thinks they are both terribly incompetent and that he dreads working together.
immoral_consequence: The new hires both find Chris's behavior to be unacceptable and unfitting of a manager and go to HR together to report him.

norm: Grown people are not expected to need a nightlight.
situation: Kayla, who lives with her partner, watches a lot of scary movies and it makes her scared of having all the lights off at night.
intention: Kayla wants to fall asleep comfortably.
moral_action: Kayla convinces herself that there is nothing supernatural lurking in the dark and turns all the lights off.
moral_consequence: Kayla's partner is able to fall asleep readily with the lights off.
immoral_action: Kayla keeps a small light on at night to put her mind at ease.
immoral_consequence: Kayla's partner has trouble getting to sleep because of the nightlight.

norm: It's fine to give someone a treat.
situation: While out on a walk, Jane's daughter saw that the local bakery was having a sale on brownies.
intention: Jane wants to teach her daughter to eat healthily.
moral_action: Jane tells her daughter that brownies are a sometimes food.
moral_consequence: Jane's daughter learns to eat sugar in moderation and maintains an optimal weight.
immoral_action: Jane tells her daughter she should never eat brownies, or she'll get fat.
immoral_consequence: Jane's daughter becomes very worried about getting fat and develops an eating disorder.

norm: It's wrong to talk during a movie at the theater.
situation: Darnell is watching a movie in a theater.
intention: Darnell sees his friend Marcus sitting in a row ahead and wants to get his attention.
moral_action: Darnell waits until the movie is finished and finds Marcus as the patrons exit the theater.
moral_consequence: Everyone in the audience enjoys a film with no disruption.
immoral_action: Darnell loudly calls out to Marcus while the feature is playing.
immoral_consequence: The theater is distracted from the movie the crowd paid to watch.

norm: It's wrong to comment negatively on a partner's attributes.
situation: Jonah's partner Amy has started eating more junk food and stopped exercising which has caused her to gain a lot of weight.
intention: Jonah wants to encourage Amy to lose weight.
moral_action: Jonah invites Amy to join him at the gym and suggests cooking healthy meals together.
moral_consequence: Amy does not feel attacked and is able to build good habits with Jonah.
immoral_action: Jonah tells Amy that she is getting too big for him to find attractive and that she needs to lose weight if they are going to stay together.
immoral_consequence: Amy is hurt and goes to stay with her sister for a few days while she rethinks their relationship.

norm: It's frustrating when people trivialize health conditions.
situation: Trevor's friend forgot their asthma inhaler and wants Trevor to wait for them to go get it.
intention: Trevor wants to reply to his friend.
moral_action: Trevor says that his friend should go get their asthma inhaler just in case.
moral_consequence: Trevor's friend is happy that Trevor is considerate about their health issues.
immoral_action: Trevor tells their friend that asthma is no big deal, so they should just leave without the asthma inhaler.
immoral_consequence: Trevor's friend feels like Trevor doesn't care about their well-being at all.

norm: It is wrong to abandon your pets.
situation: Jake has a dog named Woofie and is moving to a new apartment that does not allow pets.
intention: Jake needs to decide what to do with Woofie.
moral_action: Jake asks a friends of his to adopt Woofie when Jake moves.
moral_consequence: Woofie is happy whenever Jake visits Jake's friend and loves the new home.
immoral_action: Jake drives Woofie out to a field and lets him loose before running back to his car and driving away.
immoral_consequence: Woofie is left to eke out a miserable existence in the wild.

norm: It's good to provide empathy to people who are struggling.
situation: John is talking with Susan when Susan tells John that she is feeling depressed.
intention: John wants to respond to Susan's statement about depression.
moral_action: John tells Susan that he's sure it's tough and that he's there for her if she needs him.
moral_consequence: Susan feels supported and is glad John is understanding, so she feels a tiny bit better as hard as it is.
immoral_action: John tells Susan to just suck it up and cheer up already, that it can't really be that bad.
immoral_consequence: Susan feels isolated and lonely because John doesn't understand what she's going through.

norm: You shouldn't aspire to do well just to gloat.
situation: Lisa has always stood in her older sister Naomi's shadow.
intention: Lisa wants to be successful.
moral_action: Lisa strives to reach her goals in areas that please and interest her.
moral_consequence: Lisa is able to reach a level of success that brings her happiness.
immoral_action: Lisa works hard in her studies and work so that she may one day rub her sisters face in her success.
immoral_consequence: Lisa's success feels hollow as she has been working to prove herself to someone else.

norm: It's not okay to put poison into the environment.
situation: The CEO of the paint company was working in her office.
intention: The CEO of the paint company wanted to increase the value of her company's stock.
moral_action: The CEO decides on proper disposal of waste and is written up for her decision in Forbes magazine which raises the value of  the company's stock.
moral_consequence: Because of the proper disposal of waste, most people that live near the paint company remain healthy.
immoral_action: The CEO decides to save money by disposing of the company's waste improperly which increases the value of the company's stock.
immoral_consequence: Because of the improper disposal of waste, many people that live near the paint company develop cancer.

norm: You should not come between your partner and their family.
situation: Paul's wife Stacy spends a lot of time with her family, making Paul lonely.
intention: Paul wants more time with Stacy.
moral_action: Paul joins Stacy on her outings with her family to be with her more.
moral_consequence: Paul and Stacy enjoy time with Stacy's family and improve their relationship.
immoral_action: Paul tells Stacy to stop vising her family and spend more time with him.
immoral_consequence: Stacy gets offended and argues with Paul.

norm: It's wrong to watch naked people.
situation: Phil is uncomfortable when he notices that his neighbor sometimes forgets to draw the curtains when she undresses.
intention: Phil wants to be comfortable with his neighbor.
moral_action: Phil goes over to his neighbors house and explains the situation to her.
moral_consequence: Phil is relieved when his neighbor installs screens that make it impossible to see into her room.
immoral_action: Phil starts to purposely look for opportunities to watch his neighbor undress and becomes familiar with her body.
immoral_consequence: Phil gets charged as a peeping tom when his neighbor catches him and calls the police.

norm: It's good to make sure your pets have food.
situation: Gina plans to go to the beach for a weekend without her cats.
intention: Gina wants to avoid hiring a cat sitter.
moral_action: Gina purchases an automatic cat feeder and makes sure that both the food and water tanks are filled to the brim.
moral_consequence: Gina's cats remain healthy while she enjoys herself at the beach.
immoral_action: Gina purchases an automatic cat feeder but only fills the water portion.
immoral_consequence: Gina's cats go two days without food and are lethargic when she returns from her trip.

norm: It's bad to get married too soon.
situation: Kara has been dating someone for two months and feels convinced that he is the one.
intention: Kara wants to get married.
moral_action: Kara waits to get married after at least a year of dating the guy.
moral_consequence: The couple are more sure about each other and have a better chance at a successful marriage.
immoral_action: Kara decides to get married and arranges a wedding very early on in their relationship.
immoral_consequence: Getting married so soon takes the excitement out of their relationship.

norm: You shouldn't cause family drama.
situation: Joe was at his mother's house visiting when his brother says something rude to him.
intention: Joe wants to let his brother know that he is being rude.
moral_action: Joe pulls his brother aside and asks him if he can tone it down.
moral_consequence: Joe's brother apologizes and promises to act better in the future.
immoral_action: Joe punches his brother in the jaw because of the things he said.
immoral_consequence: Joe's mother tells Joe he has to leave the house.

norm: It's wrong to want your pet to die.
situation: Dwayne got a new puppy a few weeks ago, but the puppy hasn't stopped peeing on all of his things.
intention: Dwayne wants to stop needing to clean puppy pee.
moral_action: Dwayne enrolls the puppy in classes and studies about how to potty train a puppy.
moral_consequence: Dwayne is able to train his puppy to start peeing outside and the two become great friends.
immoral_action: Dwayne takes the dog outside, puts it in a pillow case, and tosses it into a nearby river.
immoral_consequence: Dwayne is caught on surveillance cameras and is arrested for felony animal abuse.

norm: It's rude to scold a couple for having multiple children.
situation: Linda is chatting with Tina, who has seven kids.
intention: Linda wants to express concern for he planet and the limited amount of resources we must share.
moral_action: Linda mentions ways to conserve energy and recycle.
moral_consequence: Tina starts recycling her garbage and lessons the planet's burdo.
immoral_action: Linda tells Tina that Tina is hogging resources by having too many kids.
immoral_consequence: Tina feels scolded and that Linda is trying to control Tina's freedom.

norm: It's rude to exclude people.
situation: Stephen is bored one day thinking about his friends Billy and Rose, and he's much closer with Billy.
intention: Stephen wants to invite someone over.
moral_action: Stephen invites both Billy and Rose over to his house.
moral_consequence: Rose is very happy to be included and gets closer with Stephen.
immoral_action: Stephen decides to invite Billy over, telling him specifically not to mention it to Rose.
immoral_consequence: Billy accidentally tells Rose, and Rose gets very hurt.

norm: You shouldn't judge others simply because they are strange.
situation: Frances has new neighbors who are quite eccentric.
intention: Frances wants to feel safe.
moral_action: Frances decides to be open-minded and get to know her new neighbors better.
moral_consequence: Frances's new neighbors feel welcomed and become friends with Frances.
immoral_action: Frances thinks there is something wrong with her neighbors because they are a bit weird and decides to ignore them.
immoral_consequence: Frances' neighbors are sad to be rejected in their new neighborhood.

norm: It's good to be protective of your children.
situation: Jon's son, Luke, is having trouble in school with being picked on.
intention: Jon wants Luke to enjoy school.
moral_action: Jon gets involved with the teachers and explains the issue.
moral_consequence: Luke is helped at school and enjoys it.
immoral_action: Jon doesn't get involved and asks Luke to stick up for himself.
immoral_consequence: The bullying continues and Luke hates school.

norm: It's unhealthy to sneeze on others.
situation: Alex has a cold, but had to work today and while on lunch break with his co-worker Mary, he feels a tickle in his nose.
intention: Alex wants to feel relief.
moral_action: Alex knows he's about to sneeze so excuses himself and does so in the bathroom with a tissue.
moral_consequence: Mary is able to remain safe from getting sick.
immoral_action: Alex knows he's about to sneeze but remains seated and gets mucus on Mary.
immoral_consequence: Mary catches Alex's cold and is grossed out.

norm: You shouldn't blame Youtube for ruining your relationship.
situation: Jessica broke up with her boyfriend and was telling this to her friend.
intention: Jessica wants to talk about it to her friend.
moral_action: Jessica talks about how they didn't spend enough time together.
moral_consequence: Her friend calmly listens and agrees with what Jessica is saying.
immoral_action: Jessica blames Youtube for how her boyfriend acted and not spending time with her.
immoral_consequence: Her friend replies that he never spend time with her before he got YouTube either.

norm: It's wrong to lie about sickness.
situation: Brendan is scheduled to work during opening day of the baseball season.
intention: Brendan wants to go to the baseball game.
moral_action: Brendan asks his boos if there are options to get the time off.
moral_consequence: Brendan is given permission to take a half day if he works four hours on saturday and gets to attend the game.
immoral_action: Brendan calls out of work stating that he is sick with a stomach bug.
immoral_consequence: Brendan is on TV when he catches a foul ball and gets written up by his boss the next day.

norm: It's good to be concerned about someone's drug habits.
situation: Gordon's brother has been on the streets buying and using drugs for the past few months.
intention: Gordon wants his brother to stop using drugs.
moral_action: Gordon stages to have an intervention to end his brother's drug habit.
moral_consequence: Gordon's brother overcomes his addiction and Gordon finally has his brother back to normal.
immoral_action: Gordon approaches the local drug dealer and tells them to stop selling to his brother.
immoral_consequence: The drug dealer beats up Gordon and puts him in the hospital.

norm: It's rude to take something meant for someone else.
situation: Allen is looking for his headphones in a lost and found bin that is full of clothing that belongs to other people.
intention: Allen wants to add some new button up shirts to his closet.
moral_action: Allen leaves everything in the bin and stops by the discount store later to grab some new shirts.
moral_consequence: The person who the shirt belongs to stops by and finds their shirt and is glad they don't need to buy a new one.
immoral_action: Allen takes a nice shirt from the lost and found bin that belongs to someone else.
immoral_consequence: The person who the shirt belongs to comes by later and is sad that they can't find their shirt.

norm: It is rude to throw things at someone.
situation: George is sitting across the room from Jared and asks him for a beer.
intention: Jared wants to give George a drink.
moral_action: Jared takes a cold drink from the cooler and walks over to hand it to George.
moral_consequence: George is able to have his beverage while Jared feels good knowing he did his friend a favor.
immoral_action: Jared takes a cold drink from the cooler and tosses it at George who misses it.
immoral_consequence: The can sprays all over the room making a big mess that George and Jared have to clean.

norm: It's good to celebrate birthdays with family.
situation: After staying up for forty-eight hours for work, Stanley collapses onto the bed staring at the wall, and it's his birthday.
intention: Stanley wants to relax.
moral_action: Stanley invites his family over to his house to watch movies and drink herbal tea with him.
moral_consequence: Stanley enjoys bonding with his family.
immoral_action: Stanley decides to take a nice long nap to refresh his tired mind.
immoral_consequence: Stanley wakes up in the evening sad that he missed doing something fun on his birthday.

norm: It's good to call the police if you were harassed.
situation: Casey has already told Doug no a few times, but he continues to follow her down the street demanding she give him a kiss.
intention: Casey wants to stop Doug from following and harassing her.
moral_action: Casey grabs her cell phone and calls the police loud enough so Doug can hear her doing so.
moral_consequence: Doug freaks out because he knows he's being creepy and decides to run away in the other direction.
immoral_action: Casey starts to run away, running as fast as she can into a pretty empty nearby park.
immoral_consequence: Doug begins to chase her and seizes the chance to grab her when no one can see and tries to force himself on her.

norm: It's good to spend time with your child.
situation: Ruby's daughter was studying for a test that she was going to have in school the next day.
intention: Ruby wanted her daughter to pass the test.
moral_action: Ruby sat with her daughter to help her study for the test.
moral_consequence: Ruby's daughter was able to pass the test the next day with flying colors.
immoral_action: Ruby sent her daughter to her room to study while she watched her soap operas.
immoral_consequence: Ruby'd daughter didn't understand the material, and she wasn't able to pass the test.

norm: It's encouraged to practice good grooming as often as possible.
situation: Greg works late nights as a security guard and doesn't have a lot of free time.
intention: Greg wants to get ready for work efficiently.
moral_action: Greg buys an electric razor and takes 5-minute showers, puts on clothes, and goes to work daily.
moral_consequence: Greg's clients look favorably at his appearance and give him more work.
immoral_action: Greg showers and shaves once a week to give himself extra time, puts on some clothes, and goes to work.
immoral_consequence: Greg's clients are disgusted by his unkempt appearance and do not treat him well.

norm: It's kind to share your food with others
situation: John is with his friend Will - who doesn't have a lot of money - at his school's cafeteria.
intention: John wants to eat quickly because he has a class starting soon.
moral_action: John doesn't have time to eat all his meal and leaves the leftovers to Will.
moral_consequence: Will ends up eating a satisfying lunch without spending too much.
immoral_action: John doesn't have time to eat all his lunch, so he throws what he did not eat in the trash although Will was still hungry after his meal.
immoral_consequence: Will will have to buy more food even though he is pretty poor.

norm: It's wrong to sabotage someone's work.
situation: Mia wanted to win the painting contest and Maya was the only real opposition.
intention: Mia wants to win the contest.
moral_action: Mia adds some extra details to her own painting to improve it.
moral_consequence: Mia ends up winning the contest because of the improvements to her painting.
immoral_action: Mia adds a tree to Maya's painting because she knows the judge hates trees.
immoral_consequence: Mia ends up winning the contest because of the painting's added tree.

norm: It's wrong not to do your chores.
situation: Jackie has been busy all week and has laundry lying all over her room.
intention: Jackie wants to consider doing her laundry.
moral_action: Jackie pushes herself to collect and finally do her laundry.
moral_consequence: Jackie ends up with fresh clothes to change into for the next week.
immoral_action: Jackie decides to forget about her laundry and go do something more enjoyable.
immoral_consequence: Jackie doesn't have any clean clothes to wear the next day.

norm: It is compassionate to give gifts to the homeless.
situation: Barry sees a homeless man sitting on the steps in front of a building in the middle of a rain storm.
intention: Barry wants to keep the rain from falling on the homeless man.
moral_action: Barry gives the homeless man his own umbrella to use.
moral_consequence: The homeless man thanks Barry and uses the umbrella to stay dry.
immoral_action: Barry calls the police to have the homeless man moved to a dry area.
immoral_consequence: The homeless man is put inside of a police car and taken away.

norm: It's bad to withhold things from your partner.
situation: Ken's tooth is hurting, and he is visibly in pain so his wife Martha asks him if everything is OK?
intention: Ken wants to respond to Martha's question.
moral_action: Ken tells Martha that he is in excruciating tooth pain and that he's just trying to get through it right now.
moral_consequence: Martha feels bad for Ken but is happy he's being honest with her, so she can help him get some relief.
immoral_action: Ken tells Martha that everything is fine, and she has nothing to worry about, and she should stop asking.
immoral_consequence: Martha is hurt that Ken is lying as something is obviously wrong, and she feels like he's shutting her out or doesn't think she can provide comfort.

norm: It's wrong to talk badly about someone's wedding.
situation: Bob is attending a friend's wedding and is chatting about it with the other attendees.
intention: Bob wants to comment on the wedding.
moral_action: Bob highlights all the good parts of the wedding and does not say anything about the less positive parts.
moral_consequence: Bob enjoys a decent chat with the other attendees and is thanked for his attendance at the wedding.
immoral_action: Bob mentions how bad the food is and severely critiques several other aspects of the wedding.
immoral_consequence: Bob annoys other people attending the wedding and is asked to leave the wedding.

norm: It's rude to repeatedly borrow money from others.
situation: Bill is behind in his rent, for the seventh time this year, and has already asked his friends for help a lot.
intention: Bill needs to pay his rent.
moral_action: Bill asks the landlord to give him a few days of clemency.
moral_consequence: The landlord obliges, since he respects Bill for asking directly.
immoral_action: Bill asks his best friend for another loan to help pay his rent.
immoral_consequence: Bill's friend gives him the money, but gets annoyed and scolds him for asking so much.

norm: Leaving someone stranded in an ice storm can cause hypothermia.
situation: John drives a long-haul semi truck and is going through an ice storm when he sees a stranded motorist waving him down.
intention: John wants to react to the motorist waving.
moral_action: John pulls his truck over just ahead and yells for the motorist to hurry up and get in quickly.
moral_consequence: The motorist is thankful that John just saved his life and can't stop telling him how much he appreciates it.
immoral_action: John blows his horn a few times, smiles, and waves back at the motorist as he drives by.
immoral_consequence: The motorist can't believe John thought he was saying hello and is left to ponder the inevitability of certain death.

norm: Sometime's it's good to keep your mouth shut.
situation: Justin is in an important business meeting at work and thinks he has noticed an error in a fellow employee's report that could cost the company.
intention: Justin wants to make sure the error is addressed.
moral_action: Justin waits and then takes his fellow employee aside after the meeting to let them know privately that he thinks he may have seen an error.
moral_consequence: Justin's coworker explains things from his point of view and Justin learns there is in fact no error but the coworker thanks him for his concerns nonetheless.
immoral_action: Justin interrupts the meeting and draws attention to the error in his coworker's report that he believes he sees.
immoral_consequence: Justin is immediately proven to be incorrect in his perception and his reputation at work takes a hit.

norm: It is not okay to allow pets to suffer.
situation: Theodore has two dogs and a cat.
intention: He wants to go out of town for the weekend.
moral_action: Theodore hires his neighbor as a pet sitter so his animals are taken care of.
moral_consequence: When Theodore returns home his animals are happy and healthy and the neighbor volunteers to help any time.
immoral_action: Theodore goes out of town and only leaves a small amount of food out for his animals.
immoral_consequence: When Theodore returns home he finds his animals are injured from fighting and sickly thin.

norm: It is wrong to feel entitled to someone else's time.
situation: Claire is a manager and has an important project for her and the team at work to finish before a soon-coming deadline.
intention: Claire wants to finish the project.
moral_action: Claire talks with other departments if they can spare some extra team members to meet the coming deadline.
moral_consequence: Claire's employees are grateful for the extra help and put their best efforts in to finishing the project.
immoral_action: "Claire declares ""mandatory overtime"" for all of her employees and says that they must report for work."
immoral_consequence: Claire's employees have no personal time and get burnt out, further hurting their productivity.

norm: It is unhealthy to keep toxic people for long.
situation: Austin hangs out with Perry who constantly puts down Austin which causes Austin to lose self esteem.
intention: Austin wants to talk to Perry about the put downs.
moral_action: Austin tells Perry they can't hang out anymore because of Perry's behavior.
moral_consequence: Austin removes a negative influence from his life.
immoral_action: Austin tells Perry that the put downs are okay.
immoral_consequence: Austin continues to be put down by Perry and his self esteem continues to suffer.

norm: It's good to admit when you have a problem.
situation: Gin is a closet alcoholic who really needs to get her drinking under control with the help of her family.
intention: Gin wants to get the help that she needs to recover.
moral_action: Gin asks her family if they would be willing to help her pay for rehab.
moral_consequence: Gin goes into rehab and hopes to make a full recovery from her addiction.
immoral_action: Gin drinks until she is admitted to the hospital and required to go to inpatient rehab.
immoral_consequence: Gin is forced into getting sober, but it still changes her life for the better.

norm: It is bad to be a monster.
situation: Cliff has been reading a lot of horror books and feels inspired by the evil characters he reads about.
intention: Cliff wants to feel like the characters he reads about.
moral_action: Cliff gets prop weapons and costumes to use as an employee at a Halloween attraction.
moral_consequence: Cliff loves being able to pretend to be  monster while being a good person at heart.
immoral_action: Cliff obtains tools and attempts to go on a murder spree.
immoral_consequence: Cliff murders someone and feels like his heroes, but is apprehended and is sent to prison.

norm: It is kind to adopt someone.
situation: Robert's student Tammy has no living relatives after her parents died.
intention: Robert wants Tammy to have a family.
moral_action: Robert volunteers to take Tammy in.
moral_consequence: Tammy moves in with Robert and is grateful.
immoral_action: Robert calls Child Protective Services to find a foster home for Tammy.
immoral_consequence: Tammy waits for someone to adopt her, but never gets a guardian.

norm: It's irresponsible to drive too fast on roads.
situation: Carl is a speed demon who likes racing people in cars.
intention: Carl wants to race someone.
moral_action: Carl goes to the local speedway.
moral_consequence: Carl is able to drive as fast as he wants without harming himself or anyone else.
immoral_action: Carl sees a car similar to his and challenges the person driving it to a race.
immoral_consequence: Carl and the other driver are going so fast that they both crash into a barrier.

norm: You shouldn't go on a playdate if you're sick
situation: Minnie isn't feeling well and is invited to the park.
intention: Minnie wants to have fun.
moral_action: Minnie declines and watches movies at home instead.
moral_consequence: Minnie keeps her friends safe and has a good time by herself.
immoral_action: Minnie goes to the park with her friends.
immoral_consequence: Minnie gets all of her friends sick, and they are angry with her.

norm: It's expected to set rules for you child.
situation: Jenna is trying to work from home while her son keeps begging to play video games instead of doing his math homework.
intention: Jenna wants her son to leave her alone, so she can work.
moral_action: Jenna puts her son in an empty room out of earshot with only his textbooks, a pencil, and a desk.
moral_consequence: Jenna can no longer hear her son complaining, and they both are able to concentrate on work.
immoral_action: Jenna gives in and lets her son play games without doing his homework.
immoral_consequence: Jenna gets her work done, but her son fails that weekend's assignments, causing his grades to drop and Jenna to yell at him.

norm: It's good to want a child to get some rest.
situation: Casey's daughter has an important exam tomorrow and wants to stay up until midnight to study.
intention: Casey wants her daughter to do well on the exam.
moral_action: Casey tells her daughter to get sleep and study in the morning.
moral_consequence: Casey's daughter feels refreshed and alert while taking the exam.
immoral_action: Casey lets her daughter stay up and cram for the exam.
immoral_consequence: Casey's daughter is exhausted and can hardly think straight while taking the exam.

norm: It's ok to try to train your pets.
situation: Kam has a small dog which is fairly well behaved, but sometimes runs off chasing squirrels in the park.
intention: Kam wants the dog to stop running away when they're in the park.
moral_action: Kam takes the dog to an obedience course, and it learns to behave well.
moral_consequence: The dog sees a squirrel, and acts as if it wants to run, then obey's Kam's command to heel.
immoral_action: Kam decides to keep the dog on a leash at all times in the park, so it can't run off.
immoral_consequence: The dog tries to run after a squirrel, jerking the leash so hard that Kam gets a sprained wrist.

norm: It is important to try in school.
situation: John is in first year of college.
intention: John wants to make the most of his college experience.
moral_action: John studies hard for the classes in which he is struggling while also finding the time to meet new friends.
moral_consequence: John maintains a healthy grade point average and makes lasting connections.
immoral_action: John spends time socializing and partying with all the new friends he has made.
immoral_consequence: John fails too many classes to remain in college and has to go back home.

norm: It's good to pace yourself when it comes to drinking.
situation: John who's had five alcoholic drinks already is at the bar when the bartender asks him what else he wants.
intention: John wants to respond to the bartender's question.
moral_action: John tells the bartender that he just wants water now as he needs to get some hydration back.
moral_consequence: The bartender thinks John is a smart man who's a good customer and feel safe about having him in the bar.
immoral_action: John tells the bartender to make him another whiskey sour and to make it a double.
immoral_consequence: The bartender thinks John is a lush who has no self control and is scared of how this night will turn out.

norm: It's not healthy to be a shut-in
situation: Gordon is an avid video-gamer and homebody whose friends have invited him to a party.
intention: Gordon wants to have fun.
moral_action: Gordon decides to take a chance on the party.
moral_consequence: Gordon ends up having a great time and bonds with his friends at the party.
immoral_action: Gordon chooses to stay in and play video games in lieu of going out with friends.
immoral_consequence: Gordon's friends give up on inviting him to future events.

norm: It's good to motivate others.
situation: Tom is the Sales lead for a team of Sales reps, he gets a small commission on every representative's sales, he notices some employees aren't making many sales.
intention: Tom wants to maximize his commission payments.
moral_action: Tom calls a sales meeting with all the agents and gives them a speech to help motivate them.
moral_consequence: All the employees are motivated and get more sales, allowing Tom to make more money from commissions.
immoral_action: Tom fires the under performing employee's so that he can hire better sales representatives.
immoral_consequence: The remaining employee's upset at how Tom treated them all decide to quit, leaving top without any sales agents for weeks hurting his commissions greatly.

norm: Getting rid of your own child is selfish.
situation: Walter's son Jimmy has been struggling at school and also fighting other kids and generally misbehaving.
intention: Walter wants to do something drastic to alter the course of Jimmy's life.
moral_action: Walter takes Jimmy to a military academy for young boys to learn discipline and order.
moral_consequence: Jimmy is given direction and purpose in life as well as having discipline instilled in him.
immoral_action: Walter takes Jimmy to the adoption agency and puts him up for adoption.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy is traumatized from being abandoned by his father and scared of his future.

norm: It's good to encourage your siblings.
situation: Dave is in his bedroom when his brother Tim tells him that he just signed up for the hockey team.
intention: Dave wants to respond to the news he just heard.
moral_action: Dave tells Tim that it's a great idea and that if he tries hard he can be one of the best hockey players around.
moral_consequence: Tim's confidence increases, and he's delighted to hear that his brother thinks he has what it takes to succeed.
immoral_action: Dave tells Tim that he thinks Tim will be terrible at hockey since he's not a good skater.
immoral_consequence: Tim is discouraged and feels sad that his brother doesn't believe in him.

norm: It is bad to be too clingy in a relationship.
situation: Rachel has been ignoring her girlfriend Tanya's calls and texts because Rachel is at work.
intention: Tanya wants to know what Rachel is up to.
moral_action: Tanya waits for Rachel to respond before texting or calling her again.
moral_consequence: Rachel feels like Tanya is being better at respecting Rachel's personal space.
immoral_action: Tanya keeps calling Rachel's phone and leaving messages asking why Rachel won't answer.
immoral_consequence: Rachel is annoyed at how needy Tanya is being, and has second thoughts about the relationship.

norm: It's bad to date a bunch of people at once.
situation: John is dating Susan but sees other attractive girls at a party he likes.
intention: John wants more sexual excitement in his life.
moral_action: John asks Susan back to his place where he tries new romantic stuff with her in bed they've never done before.
moral_consequence: No other girls are hurt at all and Susan loves John even more.
immoral_action: John asks three other girls at the party to date him, and they say yes.
immoral_consequence: Eventually all the girls are jealous of each other, and they all dump him, including Susan.

norm: It's frowned upon to refuse food that someone offers.
situation: Brad is on a diet, but he's over at a house party and his friend Ted offers him a homemade cookie.
intention: Brad wants to lose weight.
moral_action: Brad accepts a cookie and goes for a run later to make up for it.
moral_consequence: Ted feels happy that Brad enjoyed one of his homemade cookies.
immoral_action: Brad pushes the cookie away and refuses to eat it.
immoral_consequence: Ted is a little offended and hurt thinking that Brad doesn't find the cookie appetizing.

norm: You shouldn't laugh at how people look
situation: Henry saw a homeless man with raggedy clothing on the side of the street one day.
intention: Henry wants to stop and talk to the man.
moral_action: Henry stops and talks to the man and offers to buy him some new clothing.
moral_consequence: The mans starts to cry because he is grateful at Henry's kindness.
immoral_action: Henry stops and tells the man that he looks disgusting and starts to laugh at him.
immoral_consequence: The man begins to cry because he has no money to buy any other clothing.

norm: It's nice to wrap presents for people.
situation: It's Jerry's sister's birthday soon and Jerry just bought a nice present for her.
intention: Jerry wants her sister to think he is generous.
moral_action: Jerry decides to make an extra effort and takes the time to wrap up the gift nicely.
moral_consequence: Jerry's sister feels the beautiful wrapping is an other proof of Jerry's affection for her.
immoral_action: Jerry feels it's not necessary to wrap up the present and just puts it in a plastic bag before giving it to his sister.
immoral_consequence: Jerry's sister appreciates the nice gift but feels Jerry is a bit sloppy in his gift-giving.

norm: It's polite to thank people for their military service.
situation: Lisa is at the airport arrival gate when she sees a soldier walking towards her.
intention: Lisa wants to react to the soldier.
moral_action: Lisa asks to shake the soldiers hand and thanks him for fighting for her.
moral_consequence: Lisa helps the soldier feel welcomed home.
immoral_action: Lisa calls the soldier a murderer and turns her back on him.
immoral_consequence: Lisa is condemned by the nearby people who witnessed her attack on the soldier.

norm: It's bad to fall for a scam.
situation: Ulmer needs a thousand dollars to pay for his knee surgery, and he receives a suspicious message claiming that he inherited twenty thousand dollars.
intention: Ulmer wants money.
moral_action: Ulmer creates a post on social media asking for donations for his surgery.
moral_consequence: Ulmer's post goes viral, and he receives enough money to cover his surgery.
immoral_action: Ulmer responds to the email, and he follows the instructions by making a down payment for his inheritance.
immoral_consequence: Ulmer loses five hundred dollars that he can't get back.

norm: It's good to get an A on your assignments.
situation: Dean is working on a take home project for his Algebra 2 class.
intention: Dean wants to pass the class.
moral_action: Dean checks over his work on the project several times to make sure that he has done the best job possible.
moral_consequence: Dean maintains his A average in the class which helps boost his GPA.
immoral_action: Dean spends about fifteen minutes making sure he completed all the minimum requirements for the project.
immoral_consequence: Dean gets a D on the project which drops his overall class grade to a C ruining his GPA.

norm: It's frowned upon to be a dictator.
situation: John's boss has put him in charge of an important project with several of his other coworkers.
intention: John wants to lead his team.
moral_action: John moves everyone into the same office dividing the tasks evenly among everyone, and he asks anyone who has problems to come to him directly.
moral_consequence: John and his team work together quickly finishing the job early, and they continue working together in the future.
immoral_action: John insists that his teammates follow tight guidelines and frequently checks on his coworkers three times an hour.
immoral_consequence: His teammates reports John to human resources about his behavior, and John is taken off the project.

norm: It's good to give compliments to your friends.
situation: Irene has bought a new pair of shoes and is showing it off to her friend Shane, and she asks him what he thinks.
intention: Shane wants to respond to Irene's question.
moral_action: Shane tells Irene that the shoes are great but what's really great is her because she's so pretty.
moral_consequence: Irene blushes and smiles and is happy that Shane is such a wonderful friend and makes her feel good inside.
immoral_action: Shane tells Irene that the shoes are OK and just leaves it at that.
immoral_consequence: Irene is confused whether Shane actually likes the shoes and begins to feel self conscious.

norm: It's good to be proud of your work.
situation: Zach is in his office when his manager Todd comes in to tell him his last project won an industry prize, and he is invited to the award show.
intention: Zach wants to respond to the news.
moral_action: Zach tells Todd that he's delighted to hear the news, and he can't wait to attend and make a speech.
moral_consequence: Todd is happy that Zach is keen on going and that he's such a great representative for the company.
immoral_action: Zach tells Todd that it's nice and all but industry awards are dumb, and he's not going to attend.
immoral_consequence: Todd is sad that Zach doesn't care that he's being recognized and is not into representing the company at the awards.

norm: It is disgusting to shove food down your throat.
situation: Luke, a five year old boy, is eating super with his little sister Anne.
intention: Luke wants to tell Ann a joke.
moral_action: Luke tells Ann the joke after he's finished eating all of the food on his plate.
moral_consequence: Ann laughs at the joke becoming closer with her brother.
immoral_action: Luke tells his Ann the job while he's chewing his food.
immoral_consequence: Ann is uncomfortable with Luke's actions.

norm: It's good to stay faithful to your partner.
situation: Newly engaged Rob runs in to an old boyfriend and makes plans to meet him for drinks.
intention: Rob wants to reconnect with his former paramour.
moral_action: Rob invites his partner to join him and his ex for drinks.
moral_consequence: Rob's fiancee spends the whole night bragging about how wonderful Rob is.
immoral_action: Rob drinks beyond moderation and ends up sleeping with his old flame.
immoral_consequence: Rob's fiancee pawns the ring Rob gave him and moves to another state.

norm: Kids are expected to obey their parents.
situation: Mary gets in trouble by her mom and is told to go to her room by her mom.
intention: Marcy wants to leave the room.
moral_action: Marcy decides to follow directions and go to her own room.
moral_consequence: Marcy's mom visits Marcy, and they have a heart to heart chat that is ultimately productive.
immoral_action: Marcy decides to leave the room by exiting the house.
immoral_consequence: Mary's mom gets Marcy in even more trouble for not following directions.

norm: It is wrong to give other people drugs.
situation: Jonah is at a party where he does not know anyone, and he is feeling anxious.
intention: Alison wants to help Jonah feel more comfortable.
moral_action: Alison makes conversation with Jonah and introduces him to her friends.
moral_consequence: Jonah meets new people feels more comfortable talking to them.
immoral_action: Alison gives Jonah a hit of acid and tells him it will loosen him up.
immoral_consequence: Jonah reacts badly to the acid and has to go to the hospital.

norm: It is wrong to not support people with mental illnesses.
situation: Susan's friend Mary has got into a depression due to loss of her mom recently and Mary needs help from Susan.
intention: Susan wants to react to Mary's situation.
moral_action: Susan suggests Mary to get help from a mental health doctor and spends time with her when necessary.
moral_consequence: Mary thanks Susan for her advice and gets a proper mental healthcare.
immoral_action: Susan finds Mary to be increasingly annoying and dependent on her, so she stays away from Mary.
immoral_consequence: Mary feels unsupported and wants to commit suicide.

norm: It is disrespectful to swear at your parents.
situation: Jim comes home past his curfew and his waiting parents tell him he's grounded for a month.
intention: Jim wants to show his displeasure about being grounded.
moral_action: Jim explain to his parents that he was late because their was a wreck on the highway.
moral_consequence: Jim has his grounding lifted when his parents check the news and see the accident report.
immoral_action: Jim curses out both his parents for being so strict and for grounding him.
immoral_consequence: Jim gets grounded for 6 months instead of 1 month.

norm: It's hurtful to ditch a friend.
situation: Theresa was at the mall shopping with her friend Debbie.
intention: Theresa wants to go home.
moral_action: Theresa tells Debbie that it is about time to go home.
moral_consequence: Debbie is happy that she got to spend time with her friend during the day.
immoral_action: Theresa leaves the mall without telling Debbie she was leaving.
immoral_consequence: Debbie gets scared and starts crying because she thinks she is lost.

norm: It's wrong to kick your siblings.
situation: Cindy is a child at a table eating chicken nuggets with her family when her little brother takes one from her.
intention: Cindy wants to respond to her brother taking her food.
moral_action: Cindy tells her parents that her brother took the food.
moral_consequence: Cindy will get to eat in peace.
immoral_action: Cindy kicks her brother under the table for taking her food.
immoral_consequence: Cindy will get in trouble with her parents for kicking her brother.

norm: It's good to give free things to people.
situation: Frank found a bunch of golf balls that had been lost from the nearby course.
intention: Frank wants to decide what to do with the balls.
moral_action: Frank decides to give the balls away to the golfers he sees.
moral_consequence: Frank makes some friends at the golf course by giving out balls.
immoral_action: Frank decides to sell the golf balls at exorbitant prices.
immoral_consequence: Frank makes some bank off the golf balls he found.

norm: It's good to figure out ways to help a friend.
situation: Kathy is visiting with her friend who is going through a divorce.
intention: Kathy wants to find her friend a new place to live.
moral_action: Kathy offers to let her friend stay with her for a while until they can find her an affordable apartment.
moral_consequence: Kathy's friend feels cared for and happy to have a safe place to stay.
immoral_action: Kathy insists that her friend moves out immediately, and suggests she live in her car.
immoral_consequence: Kathy's friend feels forced into an unsafe living situation.

norm: It's morally wrong to abuse an animal.
situation: Sandy notices her dog fuzzy chewing on the couch.
intention: Sandy wants fuzzy to stop damaging things.
moral_action: Sandy sprays the couch with a smell that wards off dogs.
moral_consequence: Fuzzy stops chewing on the couch.
immoral_action: Sandy hits Fuzzy with the newspaper multiple times and locks him in the kennel.
immoral_consequence: Fuzzy breaks out of the kennel and makes a mess in the room.

norm: It's good to apologize to people.
situation: Frank mistakenly dresses down an employee before realizing he has the wrong person.
intention: Frank wants to address the error.
moral_action: Frank apologizes for the error and tries to make amends for his error.
moral_consequence: Franks is able to avert any bad feelings that might have developed.
immoral_action: Frank berates the employee for not speaking up about the error in the first place.
immoral_consequence: Frank comes across as being unfair to his employees.

norm: It's best have medical issues looked at by a doctor.
situation: Jack is a smoker who has been coughing a lot lately, but doesn't have a car to get to the hospital.
intention: Jack wants to avoid having to find a ride to see a doctor.
moral_action: Jack sets up a video conference with his doctor.
moral_consequence: Jack's doctor is able to diagnose and prescribe him medicine from their video chat.
immoral_action: Jack ignores his cough as it worsens.
immoral_consequence: Jack gets lung cancer that could have been prevented if he had seen the doctor earlier.

norm: It's bad to disrespect your parents.
situation: Jenny's parents just denied her request to go on a ski trip with some of her high school friends.
intention: Jenny wants to respond to her parents decision.
moral_action: Jenny gets some of her friends to come over and help her beg her parents to let her go.
moral_consequence: Jenny and her friends combined effort persuades her parents.
immoral_action: Jenny hurls insults at her parents out of frustration.
immoral_consequence: Jenny is punished for her behavior.

norm: Dating someone for purely physical appearances is rude.
situation: Martha is in the second semester of her senior year of high school.
intention: Martha wants to have a date to the prom.
moral_action: Martha invites the handsome Ernest to the prom, and finds they have many common interests and sense of humor.
moral_consequence: Ernest feels appreciated by Martha and it boosts his confidence.
immoral_action: Martha asks Ernest to the prom because he is handsome, but tells her friends he is stupid.
immoral_consequence: Ernest hears that Martha is mocking him, and leaves heartbroken and disillusioned.

norm: It's good to be nice to elderly people.
situation: An elderly charity worker asks John for a donation outside of a grocery store.
intention: John wants to respond to the man.
moral_action: John thanks the man for his work and donates five dollars to the charity.
moral_consequence: The elderly man is happy.
immoral_action: John tells the man to go to hell.
immoral_consequence: The elderly man is hurt and offended.

norm: You shouldn't be rude toward employees.
situation: Dave who is a manager of an office sees that Phil, an employee is doing a bad job.
intention: Dave wants to say something to Phil about his work habits.
moral_action: Dave tells Phil that he notices Phil is having a hard time at work and offers to give Phil a coaching session.
moral_consequence: Phil is delighted that someone is going to help him acquire the skills needed to the job properly.
immoral_action: Dave tells Phil that he is a moron and that his work habits are awful and that if he doesn't pick it up he's gone.
immoral_consequence: Phil is angry at Dave for being so harsh and at the same time insecure and worried about his job security.

norm: It's good to do activities together with your spouse.
situation: Jenny's husband asks her to go hiking with him like they used to do.
intention: Jenny wants to tell her husband if she'll go hiking with him.
moral_action: Jenny agrees to go hiking with her husband and seems excited for the activity.
moral_consequence: Jenny's husband is happy that they still share activities together and thinks the hike will be a chance to reconnect.
immoral_action: Jenny says she doesn't feel like going hiking with her husband and will just stay home.
immoral_consequence: Jenny's husband feels like they don't do things together any more and that they are growing apart.

norm: You shouldn't serve people food that they are allergic to.
situation: Evelyn is having her family over for dinner, and she knows her sister is allergic to peanuts.
intention: Evelyn wants to serve a delicious dinner.
moral_action: Evelyn makes sure that all of the food she is serving is safe for her sister to eat.
moral_consequence: Evelyn's sister eats everything that is served and enjoys the party.
immoral_action: Evelyn makes her favorite barbecue sauce that contains peanut oil thinking that her sister's peanut allergy is overblown.
immoral_consequence: Evelyn's sister has a severe reaction and almost dies.

norm: You should never kick a friend out of your home.
situation: Chad's drunk best friend Mark is causing problems with his rowdy behavior.
intention: Chad wants to remove Mark from the party.
moral_action: Chad leads Mark upstairs into his room telling him to rest in bed until he feels better.
moral_consequence: Mark comes back down when he's sober, and he becomes friends with the last remaining guests at the party.
immoral_action: Chad tells Mark that he's no longer welcome at the party, and pushes him out of the door.
immoral_consequence: Mark gets into a traffic accident while attempting to drive home.

norm: It's expected that you'll make schooling a priority.
situation: Ben is in college and feels fried the night before final exams when he's invited out by his friends.
intention: Ben wants to relieve his weary mind.
moral_action: Ben says that he has to study and goes for a half-hour walk to relieve his brain.
moral_consequence: Ben pushes through the study session and does well on his exam.
immoral_action: Ben goes out to the party with his friends and blows off steam.
immoral_consequence: Ben parties too hard, arrives late to his final, and fails it.

norm: It's impolite to pick your nose in front of people.
situation: Corey is at lunch with his friends when he feels an uncomfortable blockage in his nose.
intention: Corey wants to clear his nose.
moral_action: Corey excuses himself and goes to the bathroom and blows his nose.
moral_consequence: Corey clears his nose and doesn't give his friends any ammo against him.
immoral_action: Corey picks his nose to get the blockage out while his friends are talking.
immoral_consequence: Corey's friends notice and are grossed out and start teasing Corey relentlessly.

norm: It is good to provide a home for your family
situation: Matt is divorcing his wife who quit school to stay at home and raise their two kids.
intention: Matt wants the divorce to go fairly.
moral_action: Matt agrees to give the house to his ex-wife since she sacrificed to take care of the house and kids.
moral_consequence: Matt's ex-wife is able to go back to school and finish her degree.
immoral_action: Matt thinks since he paid for the house it is rightfully his.
immoral_consequence: Matt's ex-wife works a dead-end job to afford a shabby apartment.

norm: You should do things that make you happy
situation: Mario has the whole day off of work and has no plans.
intention: Mario wants to find something to do.
moral_action: Mario goes to the movies and grabs some food from his favorite fast food spot.
moral_consequence: Mario is happy and more relaxed when he goes back to work the next day.
immoral_action: Mario decides to take the time to do more work on an assignment for his job.
immoral_consequence: Mario is annoyed with himself for not doing something for himself on his day off.

norm: People are expected to support their relatives' performances.
situation: James' sister asked him to come to her community theater troupe's performance of Hamilton.
intention: James wants to avoid listening to three hours of historical rap.
moral_action: James goes to his sister's play but wears headphones under his jacket and covertly listens to Taylor Swift during the whole performance.
moral_consequence: James' sister is none the wiser and thanks him for being a supportive brother.
immoral_action: James tells his sister to her face that she can't sing, and he's not coming.
immoral_consequence: James' sister tells him she's never coming to anything to which he invites her ever again.

norm: You shouldn't have to spread sickness to people around you.
situation: Al was at work, but he hadn't been feeling very well.
intention: Al wants to finish the project he was working on.
moral_action: Al leaves and goes home to complete the work remotely while he healed.
moral_consequence: Al is able to finish the work on the project without getting anyone else sick.
immoral_action: Al stays at work in order to finish the project he was working on.
immoral_consequence: Al gets other people on his team sick with the illness that he had.

norm: You shouldn't make people who sacrificed for you mad.
situation: Tad's mother was working extra hours so that he could take guitar lessons.
intention: Tad wants to go to his friend's house.
moral_action: Tad takes his bicycle to get to his friend's house down the street.
moral_consequence: Tad's mother picks him up later to bring him to his lessons.
immoral_action: Tad takes his mother's car to his friend's house without asking.
immoral_consequence: Tad's mother stops paying for his lessons and grounds him for a month.

norm: You shouldn't judge people based on their race.
situation: Mike is a sports announcer, and he is calling a professional game.
intention: Mike wants to talk about the players.
moral_action: Mike calls the game as he sees it and compliments the players who are doing well.
moral_consequence: Viewers enjoy Mike's no nonsense approach to commentating and enjoy the game.
immoral_action: Mike makes a comment about a black player and how he must be naturally gifted athletically, so he didn't have to work hard to go pro.
immoral_consequence: Viewers are offended by the insinuations Mike's comment makes and dislike him as a commentator.

norm: It's wrong to wish evil on anybody
situation: Steven is driving to his mothers house for dinner.
intention: Steven wants to pass a car that is too slow.
moral_action: Steven passes the slow car in front of him and sees it is a older woman and smiles at her.
moral_consequence: Steven has a good feeling and has a rest of his night.
immoral_action: Steven is mad at the slow car in front of him and wishes something bad would happen to it then he speeds up and passes the car.
immoral_consequence: After Steven passes the car it crashes into a tree Steven feels guilty all night and does not feel good.

norm: It's good to accept others' differences.
situation: Toby is having a discussion with his cousin and finds out that they disagree politically.
intention: Toby wants to react to his cousin's different political beliefs.
moral_action: Toby tells his cousins that he accepts that they have a different set of political beliefs than him and then tries to change the subject.
moral_consequence: Toby's cousin is glad that Toby can accept their politics even though they differ from Toby's.
immoral_action: Toby says that he doesn't even want to talk to a person who holds those kinds of political beliefs, like his cousin does.
immoral_consequence: Toby's cousin is hurt that their own family member would be so rude to them based on a political disagreement.

norm: It's rude to flaunt wealth.
situation: John notices that his niece and nephew are wearing old, worn out clothes.
intention: John wants to get some new clothes for the kids.
moral_action: John asks his sister if it would be alright to take the kids out, because he wants to spend time with them and buy them a few gifts.
moral_consequence: His sister and brother in law are not offended by his desire to spend time with the kids and are happy to see them get some gifts.
immoral_action: John goes to his sister and brother in law to let them know that he has plenty of money and wants to help the kids to dress better.
immoral_consequence: His sister and brother in law are offended that he is insinuating that the kids are not being taken care of and decline to accept his help.

norm: You shouldn't spend your whole day satisfying yourself sexually.
situation: Justin has the day off work and a list of chores to do and is feeling horny.
intention: Justin wants to deal with his desire.
moral_action: Justin allows himself to masturbate once, only after all the chores are finished.
moral_consequence: Justin is able to be productive by channeling his desire into action.
immoral_action: Justin masturbates over and over again throughout the day, laying on the couch watching TV in between sessions.
immoral_consequence: Justin doesn't get any chores done, and is behind on housework when he goes back to work.

norm: It is rude to not pay your obligations.
situation: Jack was down on his luck and John loaned him 100 bucks to pay his rent, and now Jack has recovered financially and John is asking for his money back.
intention: Jack needs to decide how to respond to John.
moral_action: Jack pays John back the 100 dollars he owed him.
moral_consequence: John appreciates Jack's timely repayment and tells him if he ever needs help again in the future he can feel free to ask him.
immoral_action: Jack tells John he's going to have to wait because Jack's enjoying having money again.
immoral_consequence: John stops being friends with Jack because Jack is unreliable.

norm: It's not okay to lie to your children.
situation: Troy's father was killed in an auto accident, but his mother Susan doesn't know how to tell him.
intention: Susan wants to talk to Troy.
moral_action: Susan tells Troy that his father is dead, and helps him process the grief.
moral_consequence: Troy is deeply saddened but learns to accept that people die, and bonds with his mother through their grief.
immoral_action: Susan tells Troy that his father abandoned them, feeling unable to tell him the truth.
immoral_consequence: Troy grows up with abandonment issues, always wondering why his father left him.

norm: It's not right to lie to family members.
situation: Chad's parents ask Chad how he did on his math test, which he failed.
intention: Chad wants to not get grounded before his friend's birthday party this weekend.
moral_action: Chad is honest with his parents, knowing that he may get grounded.
moral_consequence: Chad's parents may appreciate the honesty and cut him some slack.
immoral_action: Chad tells his parents that he did really well on the test.
immoral_consequence: Chad is caught in a lie and gets grounded even worse.

norm: It's wrong to get a teacher suspended.
situation: John fails a history test and is in danger of having to repeat the grade.
intention: John wants to be given a chance to pass the course.
moral_action: John expresses concern to the teacher and asks what he can do to pass.
moral_consequence: John gets extra help from the teacher and does well enough for the rest of the  year to get a passing grade.
immoral_action: John makes a false harassment accusation on the teacher to the principal.
immoral_consequence: The teacher is suspended while the investigation occurs, but when found innocent John's reputation is tainted for the rest of his time in the town.

norm: It is good to visit your sick grandmother.
situation: Ash receives a phone call from his grandmother inviting him to visit her on Saturday.
intention: Ash wants to enjoy his weekend.
moral_action: Ash talks to his grandmother about how she's doing and play games with her.
moral_consequence: Ash learns more about his grandmother and apperciates her more.
immoral_action: Ash spends his weekend skateboarding at a nearby park.
immoral_consequence: Ash skates all day while his grandmother spends her day alone not doing much.

norm: It's good to make money doing something.
situation: Bob has just graduated from college.
intention: Bob wants to do something meaningful and fulfilling.
moral_action: Bob pursues a career in his field of study.
moral_consequence: Bob becomes happy and successful.
immoral_action: Bob decides to travel the world.
immoral_consequence: Bob runs out of money and becomes homeless.

norm: It's good to go to a new place to eat.
situation: Earl and Penny are planning where to eat tonight after eating at Subway twenty days in a row.
intention: Earl wants to suggest a place to eat.
moral_action: Earl tells Penny that they should go to the new pizza joint that opened up recently.
moral_consequence: Penny is delighted to explore a new place with Earl and starts craving a pizza.
immoral_action: Earl tells Penny they should eat at Subway because it's probably going to be good like always.
immoral_consequence: Penny wants to gag at the idea of eating subway again and is sad that she might have to eat the same thing three weeks in a row.

norm: You shouldn't make false accusations about someone.
situation: Robert is a high school student who isn't too fond of his math teacher, Mrs. Greene.
intention: Robert wants to go to school without having to see Mrs. Greene.
moral_action: Robert speaks with his guidance counselor, telling him that he won't succeed if he has to continue on in Mrs.Greene's class.
moral_consequence: Robert's guidance counselor switches him to a different math class taught by someone else.
immoral_action: Robert files an anonymous report to the school saying that Mrs.Greene hits her students, although she never has.
immoral_consequence: Mrs. Greene is temporarily suspended pending the investigation of the claim.

norm: You shouldn't judge other people on the way they look
situation: Dell and his friends were hanging out at the mall getting something to eat in the food court.
intention: Dell wanted to chat with his friends.
moral_action: Dell asked his friends if they were excited about the new superhero moving coming out next week.
moral_consequence: Dell had a spirited discussion about movies with his friends.
immoral_action: Dell said a man walking by was so ugly it made him not want to finish his food.
immoral_consequence: Dell's friend admonished him for making a rude comment about the man's appearance.

norm: It is despicable to steel from the disabled.
situation: Carson sees that a man in a wheelchair dropped his bag on the sidewalk.
intention: Carson wants to pick up the bag.
moral_action: Carson picks put the bag and brings it back to the man.
moral_consequence: Carson feels happy to have helped out the man when he lost his bag.
immoral_action: Carson picks up the bag and takes it home with him.
immoral_consequence: Carson feels guilty for days about stealing the man's bag.

norm: It's rude to make fun of someone for saying no.
situation: Alexa is smoking weed and offers a hit to her friend, Maggie, who refuses.
intention: Alexa wants to tell people about Maggie's distaste for weed.
moral_action: Alexa asks their friend group to be respectful by not offering Maggie any weed because she doesn't smoke.
moral_consequence: Maggie is able to hang out with her friends without feeling pressure.
immoral_action: "Alexa posts photos of Maggie's face with the word ""prude"" all over social media."
immoral_consequence: Maggie is publicly humiliated and withdraws from being social.

norm: It is unacceptable to neglect or abuse children.
situation: Peter has a young son named Kyle who is misbehaving.
intention: Peter wants to correct the behavior.
moral_action: Peter calmly reiterates the house rules with Kyle and puts him in a time out.
moral_consequence: Kyle learns his lesson from the punishment and says he will not misbehave again.
immoral_action: Peter beats Kyle very severely causing his face and body to be covered in bruises.
immoral_consequence: Kyle has to go to the hospital for his injuries and nearly dies.

norm: It's rude to hate veteran appreciation.
situation: Varius, an anti-war activist, is sitting next to Madonna  create care packages for people in the military.
intention: Varius wants to interact with Madonna.
moral_action: Varius asks Madonna if she needs anything to complete her work.
moral_consequence: Varius and Madonna learns more about the military through working with Madonna.
immoral_action: Varius tells Madonna that she shouldn't be supporting an organization that promotes violence.
immoral_consequence: Varius is shunned by Madonna  when she move to another room.

norm: It's frowned upon to fail to return a high-five.
situation: Reese is walking up to the podium during high HS graduation ceremony, where his principal is standing with an arm raised for a high-five.
intention: Reese wants to accept his diploma.
moral_action: Reese high-fives his principal, does a little dance, and goes off stage with his diploma in hand.
moral_consequence: The crowd laughs and cheers Reese on for his stage presence and silly behavior.
immoral_action: Reese takes the diploma from his principal's hand and walks off the stage wordlessly.
immoral_consequence: Reese's principal looks disappointed and the crowd thinks of Reese as impolite.

norm: It's bad to steal from your parents.
situation: James has a signature on his mom's bank account and needs some extra money for a night ot.
intention: James wants to get some money.
moral_action: James asks one of his friends to float him a loan for the night, to be repaid when he gets his paycheck.
