moral_consequence: James and his friends have a good time out that night and James pays the money back.
immoral_action: James withdraws some money from his mom's bank account and goes out for the night.
immoral_consequence: James's mom notices the theft and is distraught that her son would take her money without asking.

norm: You should never put drugs in someone's drink
situation: Mark goes out clubbing and meets a girl that he is interested in named Rose.
intention: Mark wants Rose to come home with him.
moral_action: Mark invites Rose to a nightcap at his place.
moral_consequence: Rose agrees to go with Mark, and they leave the club together.
immoral_action: Mark spikes Rose's drink so that she is more likely to go home with him.
immoral_consequence: A bouncer witnesses Mark's action and kicks him out of the club.

norm: It's good to give food to homeless people.
situation: While Fred is walking to work a homeless man asks him for any food or change he might have.
intention: Fred wants to respond to the homeless man's request.
moral_action: Fred tells the man to have a nice day and gives him a bagel.
moral_consequence: The homeless man feels happy and well fed.
immoral_action: Fred tells the man to get a job and ignores his request.
immoral_consequence: The homeless man goes hungry and feels bad.

norm: It's rude to insult someone's fashion choices.
situation: Pam's friend Joyce just bought her an unflattering outfit for her birthday.
intention: Pam wants to respond to the gift.
moral_action: Pam keeps her opinions to herself and thanks Joyce for the gift.
moral_consequence: Joyce is pleased that she was able tp make her friend happy.
immoral_action: Pam tells Joyce that the outfit is awful and questions her taste.
immoral_consequence: Joyce is offended and their friednship suffers.

norm: It is important to be prepared for school.
situation: Todd was sitting on the couch watching tv after he came home from school.
intention: Todd wanted to get ready for the next school day.
moral_action: Todd went over the practice test his teacher gave out to be ready for a test.
moral_consequence: Todd had no trouble with his test and the teacher gave him a good grade.
immoral_action: Todd took his sneakers out and made sure they were fresh and clean looking.
immoral_consequence: Todd scored poorly on a test the next day because he didn't study.

norm: You shouldn't abuse Adderall.
situation: Douglas is having trouble studying before his biology test when he sees his roommates Adderall bottle laying on the table.
intention: Douglas wants to do well on his test.
moral_action: Douglas drinks some coffee and does jumping jacks to wake himself up before studying.
moral_consequence: Douglas studies and goes to the test full of energy.
immoral_action: Douglas uses some of his roommates Adderall to study and take the test.
immoral_consequence: Douglas has a panic attack because the Adderall raises his levels of anxiety.

norm: It's rude to exclude others in social interactions.
situation: John is talking to his friend at a party when Billy, an acquaintance walks up to him.
intention: John wants to continue his conversation with his friend.
moral_action: John steps back to invite Billy to listen in on what he and his friend are discussing while he continues talking.
moral_consequence: Billy stands there and politely waits his turn to engage in the conversation, but he is happy to be part of the interaction.
immoral_action: John turns his body to ignore Billy and keeps talking to friend as if nothing happened.
immoral_consequence: Billy stands there awkwardly before leaving in a bad mood.

norm: It is rude to ask friends for free things.
situation: Delilah's friend is a graphic designer.
intention: Delilah wants their friend to design a logo for them.
moral_action: Delilah aks to hire her friend to design a logo.
moral_consequence: Delilah and her friend start a good business relationship.
immoral_action: Delilah asks her friend to design a free logo for her as a favor.
immoral_consequence: Delilah's friend gets upset that Delilah is trying to take advantage of them.

norm: You should be nice to people.
situation: Gerald just started working at a factory, and he's having trouble lifting a large box, so another worker, Bill, takes notice.
intention: Bill wants to talk to Gerald.
moral_action: Bill tells Gerald that company policy says to ask another worker for help with boxes over 50 pounds, and proceeds to help.
moral_consequence: Gerald feels good knowing that someone was looking out for him, and feels at home in his new job.
immoral_action: Bill snidely tells Gerald to that whoever trained him didn't do a very good job, and then walks away.
immoral_consequence: Gerald doesn't feel welcome at his new place of work and decides to quit.

norm: It is wrong for kids underage to be drinking.
situation: Heather attends her first high school party with her friends.
intention: Heather wants to look cool in front of her friends.
moral_action: When Heather is offered an alcoholic beverage, she thanks her friend for the thought but declines to take the drink.
moral_consequence: Heather establishes herself as a strong, independent person and enjoys the rest of the party.
immoral_action: When Heather is offered an alcoholic beverage, she takes a big drink to impress her friends.
immoral_consequence: Heather gets very sick from the drink and ends up having to go home early from the party.

norm: It is rude to yell at an elder.
situation: John is driving and is in front of a traffic light that has just turned green, but an old lady is still slowly crossing the street.
intention: John wants to drive through the intersection before the light turns red again.
moral_action: John avoids saying anything and cautiously drives around the old lady.
moral_consequence: The old lady makes it across the street safely and John is also able to make it through the light in time.
immoral_action: John yells at the old lady to move faster.
immoral_consequence: The old lady hurries up, but she trips and falls at the end of the crosswalk.

norm: You shouldn't disrespect service members.
situation: Karen is ordering a fast food meal at a drive through and notices that the order has no ketchup and mustard packets.
intention: Karen wants to get condiments with her order.
moral_action: Karen parks her car, goes inside and quietly grabs a few packets before going back home.
moral_consequence: She goes home and enjoys her dinner without any incident.
immoral_action: Karen storms in to the building and riases her voice at the service workers while demanding a free meal and asking for a manager.
immoral_consequence: Karen is confronted by the manager who makes her leave and says that she is no longer allowed at the restaurant.

norm: You shouldn't hate your partner's pets.
situation: Rita is planning a day trip with Peter when Peter asks if he should bring his dog.
intention: Rita wants to convince Peter not to bring the dog.
moral_action: Rita tells Peter that she just wants it to be the two of them and the dog might be a distraction.
moral_consequence: Peter agrees that it's best if they are distraction free and agrees to leave the dog at home.
immoral_action: Rita tells Peter that she hates his dog, that it's a filthy animal, and she doesn't want to look at it all day.
immoral_consequence: Peter is insulted as he loves his dog and wonders why anyone would hate a dog like that.

norm: It's wrong not to help out your boss at work.
situation: Pat's boss Erica is managing the front counter all by herself during a rush while Pat is texting on his phone.
intention: Pat wants to finish his conversation.
moral_action: Pat sets his phone down to help the customers, then returns to his text conversation.
moral_consequence: Erica is appreciative of Pat helping her and doesn't mention him using his phone while working.
immoral_action: Pat ignores the growing line of customers and continues texting with his friend.
immoral_consequence: Erica makes note of Pat slacking off and writes him up for his behavior on the job.

norm: You shouldn't be violent toward a significant other.
situation: Returning home, Chloe just walked in on her fiance Richard sleeping with another woman and is furious.
intention: Chloe wants to express her anger.
moral_action: Chloe raises her voice at Richard and tells him that she never wants to see him again.
moral_consequence: Realizing his mistake, Richard runs after Chloe and begs her to take him back.
immoral_action: Chloe walks up to Richard and slaps him across the face.
immoral_consequence: Richard decides to take Chloe to court and presses assault charges against her.

norm: It is bad to support people's addictions
situation: Michael's best friend disappeared years ago, but recently showed up at his door asking for money to get heroin.
intention: Michael wants to help his friend.
moral_action: Michael refuses to give him the money but instead forces his friend to stay with him and detox.
moral_consequence: The road was hard but by taking care of his friend and refusing to feed his addiction his friend is able to get clean.
immoral_action: Michael gives his friend $300 to help him get more heroin.
immoral_consequence: Michael's friend takes the money to buy drugs and later that week he ends up in the hospital in a coma.

norm: It's not okay to spoil a child.
situation: Gina's son Mark is having a temper tantrum because he wants candy, and Gina is not allowing it.
intention: Gina wants Mark to stop his tantrum.
moral_action: Gina stands firm and tells Mark to go to his room.
moral_consequence: Mark's tantrum peters out, and he ends up falling asleep, and Gina gets some peace.
immoral_action: Gina relents and allows Mark to have all the candy he wants.
immoral_consequence: Mark learns that he can get whatever he wants by having a tantrum and does it all the time, including in public.

norm: It's wrong to want a family member dead.
situation: Amy has gotten into a serious fight with her cousin.
intention: Amy wants to ruminate over the fight.
moral_action: Amy thinks that her cousin needs to get her act together.
moral_consequence: Amy is able to stand firm on her stance about her cousin.
immoral_action: Amy wishes that something would happen that would result in her cousins life ending.
immoral_consequence: Amy feels guilty for wishing that her cousin would die out of anger.

norm: You should support your family when they need your help.
situation: Lana works mornings and lives with her elderly mom, who needs to take out several bags of trash to the curb.
intention: Lana wants to go to work.
moral_action: Lana grabs the trash bags, puts them in the car, and drops them off by the curb as she leaves for work.
moral_consequence: Lana's mom doesn't have to do any heavy lifting and stays safe.
immoral_action: Lana grabs her work papers and runs off to her car, letting her mom take care of the trash.
immoral_consequence: Lana's mom can't handle all of the bags and falls, hurting herself.

norm: It's good to have a strong relationship with your siblings.
situation: Tony, living with his parents and three brothers, is considering two job offers and one of them is paying better but very far away from his home.
intention: Tony wants to respond to the job offers.
moral_action: Tony chooses the job which is closer to his home so that he doesn't need to move but and can stay with his brothers.
moral_consequence: Tony feels supported by his brothers every time he is frustrated by his work problems.
immoral_action: Tony chooses the higher paying job and moves to an apartment closer to the work place.
immoral_consequence: Tony feels lonely and distanced from his brothers.

norm: It is good to feed your family
situation: Bailey gets her weekly paycheck one Friday and cashes it in at the grocery store.
intention: She wants to spend the money.
moral_action: Bailey spends the money on fruits, vegetables and other delicious food.
moral_consequence: Her children are able to eat balanced and nutritious meals because of the variety of food they have in the house.
immoral_action: Bailey spends all the money on lottery tickets and ends up with nothing.
immoral_consequence: Her children go to bed hungry because there isn't any food in the house.

norm: It is bad to have debts.
situation: Hank needs a car, has $10,000 of cash on hand, and is at a car lot deciding on what kind of car he should buy.
intention: Hank wants to pick and buy a car.
moral_action: Hank chooses a gently used car that costs less than $10,000 and pays cash for it.
moral_consequence: Hank owns the car and doesn't pay interest on any loans for it.
immoral_action: Hank picks a new car, puts the $10,000 as a down payment, and takes a loan out for the rest.
immoral_consequence: The loan accrues interest, making Hank pay more for the car than it's actually worth.

norm: You shouldn't copy your friend's paper.
situation: Jane and Mary are working on their homework together after school, and Jane is very tired.
intention: Jane wants to finish her paper.
moral_action: Jane drinks a huge cup of coffee and focuses all her energy on writing the paper based on her class notes.
moral_consequence: Jane gets outstanding marks on her paper and gets it published on the school website.
immoral_action: Jane gets Mary's permission to copy her paper so that she can go to bed early.
immoral_consequence: Jane gets detention because the teacher notices the similarities in Jane and Mary's papers.

norm: It's wrong to pull pranks.
situation: Tate was sitting in his desk in the classroom of his least favorite teacher.
intention: Tate wants to get switched to another class.
moral_action: Tate talks to the counselor at school about taking another class.
moral_consequence: Tate is able to substitute another class for the one that he is currently taking.
immoral_action: Tate puts a thumb tack on the seat at his teacher's desk.
immoral_consequence: Tate injures the teacher and gets kicked out of the school for the rest of the year.

norm: You should call people out for cheating.
situation: Anne is taking a test and notices a fellow student looking at their notes secretly while taking the test.
intention: Anne wants the results of the test to be fair.
moral_action: Anne goes up and talks to the teacher, pointing out that the other student is looking at their notes.
moral_consequence: The other student receives a 0 on their exam and everyone else in the class gets a fair curve.
immoral_action: Anne doesn't say anything and hopes the other student does poorly despite looking at their notes.
immoral_consequence: The other student gets a good grade and throws off the curve for the rest of the class.

norm: It's illegal to claim the copyrighted material of others.
situation: Jack is a bedroom music producer who wants to grow in popularity.
intention: Jack wants to be paid for a great song.
moral_action: Jack practices hard at production, creates his masterpiece, and sells it on his website.
moral_consequence: Jack is proud of himself for creating a brilliant original work.
immoral_action: Jack finds an obscure song from a popular artist and sells it as his own.
immoral_consequence: The original artist decides to sue Jack from the use of the music to make a profit.

norm: You should fire someone who breaks the rules.
situation: Bela is a manager at a company.
intention: Bela wants to review employee performance.
moral_action: Bela tells an employee that has numerous violations that they're being released.
moral_consequence: Bela is able to train a replacement employee properly and have increased efficiency.
immoral_action: Bela notices numerous violations on an employee's record but decides to keep them.
immoral_consequence: Bela has to deal with the employee's poor behavior which takes away from other work.

norm: You shouldn't drink too much in public.
situation: Oscar is out at a bar, drinking with his friends.
intention: Oscar wants to have fun with his friends.
moral_action: Oscar drinks one beer, then takes a cab home.
moral_consequence: Oscar is in bed by 11 PM.
immoral_action: Oscar drinks so much that he starts yelling at people.
immoral_consequence: Oscar gets arrested for being drunk and disorderly.

norm: You shouldn't fall in love with your step-sister.
situation: Phil's mother just remarried, and he now has a step-sister that is his age.
intention: Phil wants to be close to his new step-sister.
moral_action: Phil makes an effort to get to know his step-sister and be a true brother to her.
moral_consequence: Phil is able to develop a strong familial bond with his step-sister.
immoral_action: Phil takes his step-sister out on romantic dates and soon starts to feel attracted to her.
immoral_consequence: Phil is separated from his step-sister when their parents become aware of his feelings.

norm: It is important to pay off your debt.
situation: Gavin is a newlywed who has been racking up credit card debt for years.
intention: Gavin wants to apply for a home loan, so he and his wife can start a new life together.
moral_action: Gavin saves up enough to pay off his past debts before applying for a home loan.
moral_consequence: Gavin's credit is in good standing, and he is approved for the loan.
immoral_action: Without paying off any of his debts, Gavin goes to the bank to apply for a home loan.
immoral_consequence: The bank sees that Gavin's credit is not in good standing and denies him the loan.

norm: You shouldn't give people drugs.
situation: Jared is hanging out with his friend John, and John is having bad cramps.
intention: Jared wants to help his friend feel better.
moral_action: Jared makes John some green tea and a glass of water.
moral_consequence: The tea helps John relax which cures his cramps.
immoral_action: Jared gives John some of his father's prescription pain medication.
immoral_consequence: John is sent to the hospital due to the medication's side effects.

norm: It is good to plan valentines day with your girlfriend.
situation: It was Valentine's day and Jim had been with his girlfriend for a month.
intention: Jim wanted to eat on Valentine's day.
moral_action: Jim took his girlfriend out to eat at the nicest place in town.
moral_consequence: Jim's girlfriend was happy and told all of her friends how great her boyfriend was.
immoral_action: Jim ordered a pizza and ate alone in his apartment on Valentine's day.
immoral_consequence: Jim's girlfriend was disappointed that he hadn't done anything for her on Valentine's Day and stopped seeing him.

norm: It's good to support people in following their dreams
situation: Steve's son comes to him asking for advice after failing to make the varsity basketball team for the second year in a row.
intention: Steve wants to make his son feel better.
moral_action: Steve tells his son to never give up doing what he loves and to follow his dreams no matter how hard it may seem.
moral_consequence: Steve's son is inspired and after redoubling his efforts the next year he makes the team and eventually becomes a professional basketball player.
immoral_action: Steve tells his son to forget about basketball and takes him out for ice cream.
immoral_consequence: Steve's son initially feels better but later regrets giving up his pursuit of basketball.

norm: It's nice to get people a surprise.
situation: Trent is happy because he won some money in the lottery, but his wife is sad because she's struggling at work.
intention: Trent wants to spend his lottery winnings.
moral_action: Trent blindfolds his wife and takes her to a spa resort for the weekend and pays to have her pampered for two days.
moral_consequence: Trent's wife feels loved and understood and goes back to work feeling like things will eventually get better.
immoral_action: Trent books himself a trip to Las Vegas for the weekend.
immoral_consequence: Trent's wife feels very lonely while Trent is away and wallows in her unhappiness about work.

norm: You shouldn't expect family members to give you money.
situation: Amanda is taking a new college course over the summer.
intention: Amanda wants to get the textbooks she needs for the class.
moral_action: Amanda uses her savings to buy the textbooks.
moral_consequence: Amanda's parents are proud of her for being self sufficient.
immoral_action: Amanda asks her parents to buy her the textbooks.
immoral_consequence: Amanda's parents believe she is irresponsible and immature.

norm: You shouldn't chase someone's pet.
situation: Al is a child with a neighbor that has a dog.
intention: Al wants to get a dog as a companion.
moral_action: Al like looking at his neighbor's dog and chooses the same breed as a pet.
moral_consequence: Al has a dog that he owns completely.
immoral_action: Al chases his neighbor's dog and takes it to his own home to keep.
immoral_consequence: Al is accused of kidnapping his neighbor's pet and is punished.

norm: It's wrong to always use your parent's money for things.
situation: Ray is in high school and is set on getting a nice car to impress his friends and have freedom.
intention: Ray wants to buy the car.
moral_action: Ray finds a job and works to save money for the car, not accepting help from anyone.
moral_consequence: Ray saves the money and creates a lifelong saving and working habit that helps him greatly.
immoral_action: Ray begs his parents for money to get the car, asking about it at every opportunity.
immoral_consequence: Ray's parents continue to feed Ray's desires and have less money for themselves and real needs.

norm: It's selfish to expect special treatment.
situation: Barry is hanging out at Tom's house and feels thirsty.
intention: Barry wants to drink something.
moral_action: Barry asks Tom if he can have a cool glass of water.
moral_consequence: Tom gets Barry a glass of water with some ice in it.
immoral_action: Barry tells Tom to make him an elaborate cocktail with his finest liquor.
immoral_consequence: Tom tells Barry to get out of his house and never come back.

norm: It is immoral to commit acts of violence
situation: Jim is being bullied by Sandy who is insulting him and getting in his face.
intention: Jim wants to defend himself.
moral_action: Jim brings up all of the times he had to rescue Sally at work.
moral_consequence: Jim earns the respect of everyone including Sally.
immoral_action: Jim pushes Sally away from him hard enough for Sandy to fall onto the floor.
immoral_consequence: Jim gets written up at work by human resources for potentially hurting Sandy.

norm: It's wrong to steal from your parents.
situation: Amy is looking for some money to go shopping with friends and notices her father's wallet on the table.
intention: Amy wants to consider taking money from her father's wallet.
moral_action: Amy decides against taking money out of her father's wallet and simply waits to ask him for money.
moral_consequence: The father of Amy obliges and gives Amy some spending money.
immoral_action: Amy quickly takes money from her father's wallet and goes shopping with her friends.
immoral_consequence: Amy's father finds out Amy stole money out of his wallet and severely punishes her.

norm: It's rude to flip someone off.
situation: Birch and his wife Agatha are stuck in traffic when another car almost runs into them.
intention: Birch wants to express his emotions.
moral_action: Birch laughs at the other drive and plays the song Highway to Hell.
moral_consequence: Agatha has a fun time singing along to one of her favorite songs.
immoral_action: Birch honks his horn at the other driver and makes and obscene gesture at them.
immoral_consequence: Agatha is embarrassed by her husband's behavior.

norm: You shouldn't argue with people during class time.
situation: Heather is a student in Mr. Stephenson's Biology class.
intention: Heather wants class to be less boring.
moral_action: Heather gives the class a chance despite initially being bored.
moral_consequence: She learns that she is interested in plants and animals and becomes a biology major in college.
immoral_action: Heather argues with Mr. Stephenson every day about how pointless the class is.
immoral_consequence: The time taken in daily arguing results in the class not learning every unit results in low final exam grades including her failing the course.

norm: You shouldn't judge someone who doesn't like using the internet.

norm: It's bad to hit on your friend's girlfriend.

norm: It's polite to apologize to someone you have wronged.

norm: You shouldn't intentionally spill things on people.

norm: You shouldn't refuse to pay what you owe.

norm: You should be respectful of your neighbors and their property.

norm: "You shouldn't call women ""total babes"" because it's rude."

norm: It's bad to be careless with your possessions.

norm: You shouldn't overstay your welcome at someone's home.
situation: Jimmy invited his brother Kyle over for dinner and is heading out for drinks and a movie with his girlfriend Sarah afterwards.

norm: People should not ruin other people's belongings.

norm: It is important to watch for other people while driving.

norm: You shouldn't be over-critical of your partner.

norm: It's wrong to talk in class and disrupt the class.

norm: It's understandable to look for your father when he's missing.

norm: It's rude to insult one's partner.
situation: David and his wife, Maria, who has gained some weight after having a baby, are getting dressed to go out for dinner.

norm: You shouldn't ask for refunds on works of art.
situation: Tracy visits an art exhibit featuring paintings by a friend of hers, and she buys a painting, that she can’t really afford, on a whim.

norm: You shouldn't secretly add things to your partner's drinks.
situation: Jenna and her boyfriend have a couple days off of work at the same time and decide to have some drinks.

norm: It's wrong to give into peer pressure.

norm: It's impolite to pick at you nails in public.

norm: You should ask before you take photos of someone.

moral_consequence: The beach remains clean for other visitors to enjoy.
immoral_action: Andrea throws the crumpled chip bag on the sand before heading to her car.
immoral_consequence: Another visitor sees the litter and is disgusted by the lack of respect people have for the beach.

norm: It's good to only smoke where it doesn't bother others.
situation: Nina is roommates with Jessie and is a pretty heavy smoker.
intention: Nina wants to smoke a cigarette.
moral_action: Nina goes outside far from the apartment door to smoke her cigarettes.
moral_consequence: Nina and Jessie have a nice-smelling apartment and are roommates for a while.
immoral_action: Nina lights up her cigarettes right in the apartment living room.
immoral_consequence: Jessie complains bitterly and tells Nina she needs to find a new apartment.

norm: It's wrong to take advantage of your employer's mistakes.
situation: Blake sees his boss Amy leave the safe unlocked as they're getting ready to leave work.
intention: Blake wants to close the safe door.
moral_action: Blake asks Amy if he can close the safe door, and she watches as he does it.
moral_consequence: The safe is secure and Amy is grateful to Blake for pointing out such an important mistake.
immoral_action: Blake approaches the safe while Amy isn't looking, takes a stack of money, and closes the door quietly.
immoral_consequence: Security footage reveals Blake's theft, and he must appear in court and lose his job.

norm: It's important to protect underage girls from predators.
situation: Don's young niece Julie asks him to take her to the mall to do some shopping.
intention: Don wants to take Julie to the mall.
moral_action: Don takes Julie to the mall and walks around and shops with her.
moral_consequence: Julie will have an adult around if someone tries to kidnap her.
immoral_action: Don drops Julie off at the mall and lets her shop alone.
immoral_consequence: Julie will not have an adult around if someone tries to kidnap her.

norm: You shouldn't flake out on someone's birthday party.
situation: John's friend Mark is having a birthday party.
intention: John wants to have a fun night.
moral_action: John goes to Mark's party and brings him a gift.
moral_consequence: Mark feels closer to John and knows he is a good friend.
immoral_action: John goes to the club to dance.
immoral_consequence: Mark sees a picture of John at the club on social media and is hurt.

norm: It's not okay to cause people undo stress.
situation: Marnie is shopping for fancy new clothes at a classy boutique.
intention: Marnie wants to look really fabulous at a friends wedding.
moral_action: Marnie asks the staff for assistance and also follows their instruction for putting away clothes she doesn't want.
moral_consequence: The staff appreciate Marnie as a customer and offer her a discount.
immoral_action: Marnie tries on multiple outfits and tosses them all over the floor before deciding what to buy.
immoral_consequence: The staff have to spend hours cleaning up after Marnie and lose sales.

norm: It is rude to ditch friends
situation: Amy is at the bar with her friend who has become quite drunk and is behaving badly.
intention: Amy wants to leave the bar.
moral_action: Amy coaxes her friend into calling it a night and guides her out of the bar.
moral_consequence: Amy gets her friend home safely and her friend is able to sleep off the night.
immoral_action: Amy pays her tab and leaves the bar without telling her friend because she doesn't think her friend would leave with her.
immoral_consequence: Amy's friend gets more drunk and is taken advantage of without Amy around to look out for her.

norm: You shouldn't be ignorant of things.
situation: John is at home and hungry on a Friday night alone and is about to cook but doesn't know how or have any recipes.
intention: John wants to make lasagna.
moral_action: John calls his mom for her lasagna recipe and writes down the instructions.
moral_consequence: John's lasagna comes out very tasty, and he is happy.
immoral_action: John guesses what pasta to use and sauce and puts it all together on the fly.
immoral_consequence: The lasagna comes out awful and John is very upset.

norm: It's wrong to try to upset people on purpose.
situation: Dave learned that his friend Jimmy did poorly on a science test they took.
intention: Dave wants to talk to Jimmy about the test.
moral_action: Dave tells Jimmy they can study together for the next test.
moral_consequence: Jimmy will think Dave is a good friend and motivated to do better.
immoral_action: Dave taunts Jimmy and tells him he has a small brain and won't imrpove.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy will get angry at Dave and tell him he doesn't want to be friends anymore.

norm: It's wrong to take death lightly.
situation: Liam is sitting at home with his wife Pam when Liam gets a call that his mom died.
intention: Liam wants to tell his wife that his mother is dead.
moral_action: Liam tells his wife that his mother died and begins to cry uncontrollably in front of her.
moral_consequence: Pam is understanding as to why  Liam is reacting this way and goes over to comfort him.
immoral_action: Liam tells his wife that his mom just died but that's OK because everyone dies so no big deal.
immoral_consequence: Pam is shocked that Liam is not expressing any grief and worries if he's in the right mental state.

norm: You should be patient when waiting for somebody
situation: Kate's husband Eric asked her to give him a ride to work because his car broke down.
intention: Eric wants to go to his job.
moral_action: Eric waits 10 minutes and gets nervous Kate isn't coming, so he calls her, and she says she is almost there.
moral_consequence: Kate is happy Eric called because she would have been angry for coming all the way for nothing.
immoral_action: Eric waits for 10 minutes and gets nervous that Kate isn't coming, so he walks to work.
immoral_consequence: Kate arrives minutes later and is now mad at Eric for making her waste her time.

norm: It's wrong not to pay something you owe.
situation: Charles receives a call from his cousin Pat, who asks Charles to pay back some money that Pat loaned him.
intention: Charles wants to respond to Pat.
moral_action: Charles tells Pat he will transfer the money to him immediately.
moral_consequence: Pat is pleased to get his money back and remains willing to help Charles in the future.
immoral_action: Charles tells Pat to get over it and stop bothering him about the money.
immoral_consequence: Pat no longer trusts Charles and refuses to help him ever again.

norm: It's rude to ignore an old friend.
situation: Missy is walking to an appointment when she sees an old friend.
intention: Missy wants to get to her appointment on time.
moral_action: Missy waves to her friend and calls out that she is in a hurry but will call them later.
moral_consequence: Missy gets to her appointment on time without hurting her friend's feelings.
immoral_action: Missy ducks her head and ignores her friend when they call her name.
immoral_consequence: Missy's friend is angry with her and tells everyone that she is stuck up.

norm: You shouldn't try to sabotage someone's life.
situation: Rev and Rae broke up a month ago and Rev is still very angry about it.
intention: Rev wants to find a release for his anger.
moral_action: Rev starts to work out more and see a psych.
moral_consequence: Rev learns much about himself and gets fit.
immoral_action: Rev posts something embarassing on Rae's social media account, getting revenge.
immoral_consequence: Rae gets fired from her job and Rev feels guilt now.

norm: It's good to participate in events in your community.
situation: Brian hears about a community picnic being organized in his apartment complex next weekend.
intention: Brian wants to decide how to spend his weekend.
moral_action: Brian decides to pac a lunch and hang out at the community picnic.
moral_consequence: Brian meets several interesting people from his apartment complex, and they start hanging out frequently.
immoral_action: Brian decides to ignore the event and stay at home playing video games.
immoral_consequence: Brian doesn't get to meet anybody new or have an exciting day out of the house.

norm: It's wrong to enjoy spreading germs.
situation: Mary knows that she has the flu and has been diagnosed at the doctor's office.
intention: Mary wants to get groceries to make herself a soup.
moral_action: Mary orders groceries from a delivery service she finds on the internet.
moral_consequence: The manager of the store is happy that Mary is staying home when she is sick.
immoral_action: Mary goes to the grocery store and coughs and sneezes all over the cashier.
immoral_consequence: The manager of the store bans Mary from going to the store for the rest of the year.

norm: It's inexcusable to sexualize young children.
situation: Bob is a photographic artist preparing for an upcoming show.
intention: Bob wants to meaningfully juxtapose the innocence of childhood with the sensuality of the adult.
moral_action: Bob phototographs adult models engaged in childlike play.
moral_consequence: Bob's work receives critical praise for his achieving his thematic goals.
immoral_action: Bob photographs underage models in adult social interactions.
immoral_consequence: Bob's work receives critical praise while also drawing great interest from pedophiles, which puts his models at risk.

norm: It's not okay to bribe your kids.
situation: Ashley's son Gary gives her his report card which has terrible grades on it this semester.
intention: Ashley wants to motivate Gary to do better in school next semester.
moral_action: Ashley tells Gary that he better get his act together and get good grades next semester, or she'll send him to boarding school.
moral_consequence: Gary is instantly motivated to do better and gains respect for his mother's firm guiding hand.
immoral_action: Ashley tells Gary that if he gets good grades next semester Ashley will give him $2500.
immoral_consequence: Gary becomes a spoiled brat over time who only does even the most basic of tasks if there's something in it for him.

norm: It's wrong to have an affair with a married person.
situation: Jane who is known to be married approaches Bill and offers a one night stand.
intention: Bill wants to respond to Jane's offer.
moral_action: Bill tells Jane that it's known that she's taken and that he doesn't feel comfortable being with her.
moral_consequence: Bill feels relieved that he resisted temptation and is happy to have inner peace.
immoral_action: Bill tells Jane that she is very attractive and proceeds to indulge in having a torrid one night stand with her.
immoral_consequence: Bill later feels guilt eating at him because he knows Jane has a heartbroken husband back home.

norm: It's good to let your friends borrow things.
situation: Mark's friend asked to borrow Mark's car in order to get to a job interview.
intention: Mark wants to help his friend.
moral_action: Mark lets his friend borrow his car for the day.
moral_consequence: Mark's friend is able to get to his job interview on time.
immoral_action: Mark tells his friend to order an Uber instead of taking his car.
immoral_consequence: Mark's friend's Uber comes by 15 minutes late, and his friend arrives late to his job interview.

norm: It's good to try to talk through disagreements.
situation: Zelda is having an argument with her friend over how they should solve a puzzle.
intention: Zelda wants to show her way is the right solution.
moral_action: Zelda demonstrates to her friend how the solution she has in mind would actually indeed work.
moral_consequence: Zelda's friend comes to understand things from Zelda's perspective, and they move on.
immoral_action: Zelda tells her friend to leave her alone and that she will just do the puzzle herself.
immoral_consequence: Zelda's friend feels left out and spurned so their tiff continues later on.

norm: It's wrong to judge a person by their significant other.
situation: It is John's first day of work at his new job.
intention: John wants to get to know his co-workers.
moral_action: John introduces himself to another co-worker after already having an unpleasant run in with their spouse.
moral_consequence: John finds out that the co-worker shares many of his interests.
immoral_action: John dismisses a co-worker after they explain that their spouse likes a sports team John loathes.
immoral_consequence: John gets off on the wrong foot with his new co-worker and will have to spend months building up a relationship.

norm: It's inappropriate to steal things.
situation: A new racing game just came out, and Chad really wants to play it.
intention: Chad wants to obtain the game.
moral_action: Chad decided to buy the game to support the creators.
moral_consequence: The creators are compensated for the time they put into the game.
immoral_action: Chad downloads a crack to the game online and obtains the game that way.
immoral_consequence: The creators of the game are not compensated even though Chad enjoys the game.

norm: You shouldn't smoke just to prove a point.
situation: Chris and Amy are eating lunch at school near the fieldhouse, Amy is flirting with Chris.
intention: Amy wants to impress Chris.
moral_action: Amy declines Chris's offer, saying she's never done it before and doesn't think now is the right time.
moral_consequence: Chris respects Amy's choice and is impressed by her honesty, asking if she wants to hang out later.
immoral_action: Chris offers Amy a puff on his joint, Amy smokes it even though she hasn't ever smoked weed before.
immoral_consequence: Chris is impressed by Amy's casual attitude, but she goes on to be more forthright about her feelings than she meant to be and feels awkward.

norm: You should not encourage mass shootings.
situation: James is an up-and-coming political blogger in a state that just had a major mass shooting.
intention: James wants to increase his audience.
moral_action: James posts an emotional video interview with one of the victims' families.
moral_consequence: James' blog acquires many new followers who praise him for his compassion.
immoral_action: James posts a video arguing that the shooter might have been a very fine person.
immoral_consequence: James' blog is flooded with new readers all trying to argue with him.

norm: It is rude to be hypocritical in your actions.
situation: Scott tells his son Nathaniel not to eat ice cream for breakfast, but Scott always craves ice cream.
intention: Scott wants to eat ice cream.
moral_action: Scott waits until the evening to eat a bowl of ice cream.
moral_consequence: Nathaniel join his father in eating ice cream in the evening.
immoral_action: Scott devours an ice cream cone early in the morning.
immoral_consequence: Nathaniel becomes mad that he can't eat ice cream in the morning, while his dad can.

norm: It's rude to not clean up your dog's poop.
situation: James likes to walk his dog around his apartment building's ground every morning.
intention: James wants to avoid touching dog poop.
moral_action: James uses a small shovel to carry his dog's poop to the garbage can.
moral_consequence: People think James is a bit odd, but appreciate that he cleans up after his dog.
immoral_action: James leaves his dog's poop lying around on the grass around the apartment building.
immoral_consequence: James' neighbors start leaving irritated notes on his door ordering him to clean up after his dog.

norm: You shouldn't say things that offended people
situation: Blake is at the grocery store looking for apples, but they're all spoiled.
intention: Blake wants to vent his anger.
moral_action: Blake takes a breath and asks a worker if he has any fresh apples.
moral_consequence: The worker is glad to find Blake some fresh apples.
immoral_action: Blake says in a raised voice that the workers in the store can't do their jobs in front of a worker.
immoral_consequence: The worker won't help Blake find fresh apples and resents him.

norm: It's frowned upon to say unkind things about people.
situation: Kent does not like his country's leader at all, so he complains about him.
intention: Kent wants to discuss with his friends.
moral_action: Kent decides that he should save his rants on the leader for when it's appropriate to do so.
moral_consequence: Kent's friends appreciate that he's not ranting about the politician right now.
immoral_action: Kent rants about the leader and how stupid and such he must be.
immoral_consequence: Kent's rant bores is friends who don't care about politics and don't like the rudeness.

norm: You shouldn't use dating sites when you aren't single.
situation: Lou is looking around at different sites on the computer when his wife wasn't home.
intention: Lou wanted to find someone to chat with.
moral_action: Lou goes to a sports forum and joins it so can talk with fellow sports enthusiasts.
moral_consequence: Lou makes a new friend who is as passionate about sports as him.
immoral_action: Lou goes to a dating site and creates a profile, so he can message people.
immoral_consequence: Lou gets into a fight with his wife when she sees the dating site on the computer.

norm: It's good to care about the well-being of your neighbors.
situation: Sue caught the Coronavirus and becomes mildly sick.
intention: Sue wants to recover from the disease.
moral_action: Sue decides to self quarantine herself for 14 days in order not to spread the disease.
moral_consequence: Her neighbors thank Sue for self quarantining and send her family masks and disinfecting sprays to help containment of the disease in her home.
immoral_action: Sue thinks that fresh air is important in treating the disease, so she goes outside everyday for a walk without wearing a mask.
immoral_consequence: Her neighbors get infected by Sue and some of them need to be hospitalized.

norm: It is good to learn from others.
situation: Sarah recently struggles with her Math study and Ann is good at Math.
intention: Sarah wants to improve her grade in Math.
moral_action: Sarah asks Ann for advice on getting a better grade in Math test and follows it through.
moral_consequence: Sarah gets a good grade in the test without using extreme and harsh measures.
immoral_action: Sarah stayed up and did not sleep the night before the Math test in order to study more.
immoral_consequence: Sarah gets sick after the test even though she gets a good grade in the test.

norm: It's not okay to make people suffer through your art.
situation: Jane is a model who is posing for photographer Francis in his photography studio.
intention: Francis wants to direct Jane to make it look like she's suffering.
moral_action: Francis tells Jane to stare out of the window and look melancholy, so he can make a photo about a suffering metaphor.
moral_consequence: Jane does what she's told, and she's happy when Francis tells her they got a good photo.
immoral_action: Francis tells Jane to claw her nails into her skin until it bleeds, so he can make a photo about a suffering metaphor.
immoral_consequence: Jane does what she's told and puts herself through a lot of pain, so she doesn't care much when Francis tells her it's a good photo.

norm: You should always help out around the house.
situation: Nicholas' friend has invited him over to watch the football game, but there are chores to do and Nicholas' wife doesn't have time to do them all.
intention: Nicholas wants to watch the football game.
moral_action: Nicholas lets his friend know he won't be joining him and puts the game on the television at home, watching it as he cleans up around the house.
moral_consequence: Nicholas' wife thanks him for his help and cooks him a nice dinner to show her appreciation.
immoral_action: Nicholas goes over to his friend's house to watch the game, leaving his wife to finish up the chores.
immoral_consequence: Nicholas' wife is furious at his behavior and yells at him when he gets back.

norm: It's invasive behavior to Google someone's address.
situation: Daryl found out his classmate Lisa was having a house party, and is interested in attending.
intention: Daryl wants to attend Lisa's house party.
moral_action: Daryl goes up to Lisa and mentions that he has heard talk of her party.
moral_consequence: Lisa invites Daryl to her house party, and they have a great time.
immoral_action: Daryl doesn't talk to Lisa about her party, and instead decides to just show up after googling her address.
immoral_consequence: Creeped out, Lisa kicks Daryl out of her party, embarassing him in front of everyone.

norm: It's wrong to try to change people.
situation: Kelly has a new boyfriend, Greg, who is an amateur stand-up comic, and she is coming to see his act tonight.
intention: Kelly wants to react to Greg's comedy.
moral_action: Kelly sees that Greg uses real life experiences and understands that people relate better to him because of it.
moral_consequence: Greg appreciates that Kelly understands his work, which inspires him to get even more personal in his act which makes his career take off.
immoral_action: Kelly hears a lot of personal stories in Greg's act, and she tells him that he shouldn't use real life experiences.
immoral_consequence: Greg takes Kelly's advice and the next time he performs he gets booed off the stage.

norm: You should let elderly people ahead of you in line.
situation: Ty was in line at the grocery store when he sees an old man with a cane standing right behind him.
intention: Ty wants to check out.
moral_action: Ty lets the man check out ahead of him in line.
moral_consequence: The old man is able to get back to his car and off of his feet sooner.
immoral_action: Ty ignores the man with the cane and checks out ahead of him.
immoral_consequence: The old man's legs and feet hurt by the time that he is able to check out.

norm: You shouldn't make fun of the way someone talks.
situation: Kara meets a new girl at her school named Sandy, who is from Australia.
intention: Kara wants to speak to Sandy.
moral_action: Kara tells Sandy she is excited to meet someone from another country and wants to learn more about her.
moral_consequence: Sandy is happy to make a new friend, and she feels more comfortable in her new setting.
immoral_action: Kara laughs at Sandy and tells her that her accent is really weird.
immoral_consequence: Sandy feels self-conscious about her accent and becomes unhappy and withdrawn.

norm: It's good to teach people to swim.
situation: Charles takes his son Jack to the beach to swim but Jack does not know how to swim.
intention: Charles wants to react to Jack's inability to swim.
moral_action: Charles demonstrates to Jack how to do free-style swim and asks him to try to do it.
moral_consequence: Jack feels interested and is able to swim several strokes after practicing for an hour.
immoral_action: Charles asks Jack to wear a life jacket to keep him safe.
immoral_consequence: Jack does not have fun being stuck inside a life jacket.

norm: You shouldn't have an affair if you're a stripper.
situation: Caroline is a stripper, and she has been having doubts about her marriage lately.
intention: Caroline wants to try something new.
moral_action: Caroline asks her husband to try some new things to spice up their sex life.
moral_consequence: Caroline finds sex with her husband fun again, and falls in love with him all over again.
immoral_action: Caroline asks a client if they want to have sex, and they agree.
immoral_consequence: Caroline's husband finds out, and throws her out of the house.

norm: It's rude to try and bully people.
situation: Phil is a teenager at the busy basketball court and realizes he did not bring his ball with him.
intention: Phil wants to get a basketball.
moral_action: Phil goes back home to get his ball to play with.
moral_consequence: Phil is able to play basketball at the court with his ball.
immoral_action: Phil takes a ball from kids he sees at the court.
immoral_consequence: Phil will get in trouble for taking a ball from kids.

norm: It's good to adopt a new animal.
situation: Casey spots a small dog laying on the ground outside of his house.
intention: Casey wants to do something with the dog.
moral_action: Casey fosters the dog for a couple of weeks before deciding to keep the dog.
moral_consequence: the dog is happy being near Casey.
immoral_action: Casey takes the dog to an animal shelter.
immoral_consequence: The crowded shelter puts the dog to sleep after no one adopts it.

norm: It is nice to tip generously at restaurants
situation: Karen is out at a restaurant in a state that allows tipped workers to be paid far below minimum wage.
intention: Karen wants to thank the waitress for their good service.
moral_action: Karen knows the best way to thank the waitress is to leave a health fifty percent on top of the moderate bill for the meal.
moral_consequence: Karen's waitress is very happy to see such a healthy tip and continues to serve with a smile the rest of the day.
immoral_action: Karen compliments the waitress for the service and pays her bill without filling in a gratuity.
immoral_consequence: The waitress is insulted that not only did Karen not leave a tip, but complimented her beforehand which seems especially cruel.

norm: It's bad to follow someone while they are jogging.
situation: Kevin is running down the sidewalk behind a person jogging late at night.
intention: Kevin wants to get home in a hurry.
moral_action: Kevin crosses the street to have the sidewalk all to himself.
moral_consequence: Kevin doesn't scare the jogger, and they both go on their way.
immoral_action: Kevin follows very closely behind the jogger.
immoral_consequence: The jogger gets scared that Kevin is a mugger and maces them.

norm: It is wrong to frighten animals.
situation: Clara is showing Jake her new kitten that is inside a pet carrier.
intention: Jake wants to get the kitten to do something other than sit.
moral_action: Jake offers the kitten a tiny piece of tuna.
moral_consequence: The kitten rolls playfully forward to get the tuna and Clara finds it endearing.
immoral_action: Jake picks up the pet carrier and shouts 'BOO' into it.
immoral_consequence: The kitten is very frightened and refuses to eat for several days after the incident and Clara is furious.

norm: It's wrong to lose your temper.
situation: Mr. Nelson is an English teacher who has trouble being patient and is teaching a rowdy group of students.
intention: Mr. Nelson wants the students to behave.
moral_action: Mr. Nelson switches to an activity-based teaching style to channel his students' energy and engage them.
moral_consequence: The students love Mr. Nelson's class because they get to do lots of interesting activities.
immoral_action: Mr. Nelson loses his temper and loudly tells the students to be quiet, lamenting how undisciplined they are.
immoral_consequence: The students feel hurt and resentful and lose respect for Mr. Nelson, talking about him behind his back.

norm: It's good to want to express your emotions.
situation: Jenni is going thru a rough patch in her life because she lost her job and boyfriend.
intention: Jenni wants to feel better.
moral_action: Jenni calls a therapy hot-line and discusses her life with a trained counselor.
moral_consequence: Jenni begins to feel better by talking thru her problems with another person.
immoral_action: Jenni turns to shooting heroin to get her mind off her situation.
immoral_consequence: Jenni overdoses on some heroin cut with fentanyl and dies.

norm: Cell phone use is rude during events.
situation: Danny is seeing a movie and realizes he has a missed call as the movie begins.
intention: Danny wants to respond to the call.
moral_action: Danny waits till the movie is over before returning the call.
moral_consequence: Danny gets to enjoy the movie without upsetting anybody else.
immoral_action: Danny calls back the number of the missed call and has a conversation while the movie plays.
immoral_consequence: Danny gets pelted by popcorn from angry fellow movie watchers.

norm: It's rude to hate on women.
situation: John is at home with his wife Mindy who cooks his dinner way too salty for him.
intention: John wants to vent his anger.
moral_action: John takes a breath and tells Mindy it can be hard to get the salt amount just right in cooking and the rest of it tastes good.
moral_consequence: Mindy feels respected and loved by John and loves him.
immoral_action: John raises his voice and says in front of Mindy that women just can't cook.
immoral_consequence: Mindy resents John more and respects him less as a person.

norm: You shouldn't be rude to kids.
situation: Rick is a famous movie star who's sitting in a restaurant when he's approached by a kid asking for him for an autograph.
intention: Rick needs to decide whether to give an autograph.
moral_action: Rick smiles and nods to the kid, signing his name on a restaurant napkin and giving it to him.
moral_consequence: A reporter sees the event and posts about it on social media, making Rick look like a nice guy.
immoral_action: Rick tells the kid to beat it and let him eat in peace.
immoral_consequence: A reporter sees the incident and posts about it on social media, tarnishing Rick's reputation.

norm: It's wrong to cause accidents while driving.
situation: Adam is going home from work.
intention: Adam wants to get home as fast as possible.
moral_action: Adam takes the toll road home to avoid heavy traffic.
moral_consequence: Adam gets home much earlier than he normally does.
immoral_action: Adam cuts off a car while speeding and weaving in heavy traffic on the highway and the car crashes.
immoral_consequence: Adam is arrested for reckless driving.

norm: It's good to invite your friends over to play.
situation: Jared is lonely and has been talking with his friends they all have a free schedule.
intention: Jared wants to hang out with his friends today.
moral_action: Jared invites his friends over to his house, and they all hang out together.
moral_consequence: Jared's friends are happy they get to go to Jared's house and don't have to clean their house.
immoral_action: Jared insists that he go to his friends house instead of inviting them over to his house, and they hang out.
immoral_consequence: Jared's friends think Jared is being pushy, and they feel manipulated while hanging out.

norm: You shouldn't steal things from stores.
situation: Chris is shopping at Walmart by himself in the sporting section.
intention: Chris wants to get new lures to fish with.
moral_action: Chris walks over to the sporting section, picks out his lures and then pays at the register.
moral_consequence: Chris takes his lures fishing and has a great time.
immoral_action: Chris walks over to the sporting section and sticks a few expensive lures in his pocket.
immoral_consequence: The next time Chris enters the store the manager tells him that he is banned for life as they saw him on camera stealing.

norm: Sexual harassment is wrong.
situation: Calypso is in the break room with his crush Amber.
intention: Calypso wants to express his attraction to Amber.
moral_action: Calypso compliments Amber's appearance and personality.
moral_consequence: Calypso and Amber go on a date after work.
immoral_action: Calypso touches Amber's chest.
immoral_consequence: Amber reports Calypso to HR.

norm: You should be respectful when you are questioning your superiors.
situation: Mary is angry because her work team was given the wrong information and now they are behind schedule on their assignment, because of it.
intention: Mary wants to find out why she doesn't have the right information.
moral_action: Mary lets her boss know that an error has been made, and she needs to understand how it was made before proceeding with her work group's current instructions.
moral_consequence: Her boss explains her perception of what happened and how the error occurred, and she reassures Mary that her current instructions are correct.
immoral_action: Mary asks her boss why she was given incorrect information and suggests that management is incompetent.

norm: It's good to take action to protect the vulnerable.

norm: You shouldn't say mean things to people.
situation: A girl in Janet's class has lost a little weight and asks Janet how she looks.

norm: It's good to be confident.

norm: You shouldn't use your roommate's things without their permission.

norm: It is rude to block the view of others.

norm: You shouldn't lie about your qualifications.
situation: Kyle is interviewing to be a high school teacher but has never worked with high schoolers before.

immoral_consequence: The interviewer calls the neighboring high school to confirm, and learns that Kyle has never worked there.

norm: You should be grateful to people that treat you well.

norm: It's encouraged you be nice to your neighbors

norm: It's not okay to not spend time with your kids.
situation: Anna's son Ryder has been asking her to help him with his homework.

norm: It's selfish to not care about those closest to you.
situation: Paul is sitting on the couch at home watching a football game when his wife comes home crying.

moral_action: Paul says hi but then looks at his wife and sees she's crying, so he immediately asks her what's wrong.

immoral_consequence: Paul's wife is annoyed that Paul is not noticing that she's crying and feels like he doesn't care about her.

norm: It's not good to lie.
situation: Frasier who is 31 is interviewing for a contest with contest director Roz when she asks him how old he is.
intention: Frasier wants to state his age.
moral_action: Frasier tells Ros that he just recently turned thirty one years old.

norm: "It's wrong to call grown men ""boys."""

norm: It's kind to buy tickets for your friends.

norm: You shouldn't break up with someone you've gotten pregnant.

immoral_action: Chris leaves his girlfriend and focuses on protecting himself.

norm: It's smart to talk about one's grief with others.
situation: Frank is going through some inner turmoil which is beginning to show on his face so his friend Andy asks him what's wrong.

immoral_consequence: Andy disbelieves Frank since it's pretty obvious something is wrong and is sad Frank won't tell him what it is.

norm: It is bad to be disruptive on public transportation
situation: Annie was taking the bus home from her local library.
intention: Annie wants to get the bus driver's attention because her stop is coming up.

norm: You should not sabotage your own career.
situation: John has a promising career as a scientists, and is at a party where people are doing cocaine.

norm: It's wrong to lie about a desease.

norm: You shouldn't verbally abuse people.
situation: Evan is frustrated at his coworker Abby for not understanding how to operate equipment properly.

norm: You shouldn't disturb other people by being loud and annoying.
situation: Tommy's dad works from home, where Tommy often hangs out with his friends.

norm: It is rude to pester people with personal questions.

norm: It's bad to put all housework on your partner.
situation: Dan and his fiance recently moved in together and are figuring out how to split up duties around the house.
intention: Dan wants to come to an agreement that he likes.
moral_action: Dan agrees to do the chores that finds more satisfying to do, and they come to a fairly even split of duties.

immoral_action: Dan argues that his fiance should do nearly all of the housework since he makes more money.

moral_consequence: John's parents think he is responsible and self sufficient.
immoral_action: John asks his parents for money, saying that he’s raising funds for a charity.
immoral_consequence: John's parents find out that he lied and trust him less going forward.

norm: You're encouraged to make friends instead of enemies.
situation: Andrew walks into a room filled with people.
intention: Andrew wants to interact with the people.
moral_action: Andrew goes up to a group of people talking and joins their conversation.
moral_consequence: Andrew and the people become friends.
immoral_action: Andrew goes up to a group of people talking and tells them they're all stupid.
immoral_consequence: The people think that Andrew is mean and tell everyone he's a bad person.

norm: It's not polite to eavesdrop on people.
situation: Jenny has finished her work and has to wait for her coworker, Ellen, to get off the phone, so they can leave together.
intention: Jenny wants to find something to do.
moral_action: Jenny sits in her office and plans the next day's work while she waits for Ellen.
moral_consequence: Jenny is able to keep busy and Ellen can have privacy during her phone call.
immoral_action: Jenny stands next to her Ellen's office door and listens in on her phone call.
immoral_consequence: Ellen notices that Jenny is listening to her conversation and asks Jenny to give her some privacy.

norm: It's wrong for a person to steal.
situation: Jake is broke and wants to take his girlfriend out to dinner and a movie.
intention: Jake wants to get some cash.
moral_action: Jake goes to his brother and asks him for a loan until he gets paid next week.
moral_consequence: Jake's brother loans Jake his requested amount and Jake is able to take his girlfriend out.
immoral_action: Jake finds some cash on his brother's bedroom dresser while his brother is gone and takes the cash.
immoral_consequence: Jake's brother realizes that Jake has taken his money and confronts him, which leads to the brothers fighting.

norm: It's good to compliment people on their looks.
situation: Lois and her husband are both getting dressed up at their home before going out on a date.
intention: Lois wants to have a good feeling night.
moral_action: Lois compliments her husband's attire and admires their fashionable outfits once they’re ready to leave the house.
moral_consequence: Lois's husband appreciates the compliments and feels good about himself.
immoral_action: Lois spends all of her time concentrating on how she looks because it makes her feel good and doesn't mention her husband's looks at all.
immoral_consequence: Lois's husband feels a little down about Lois not complimenting his looks when he put in the time to get ready too.

norm: It is responsible to report criminals to law enforcement.
situation: Jenny sees the face of a man who shoots a store owner.
intention: Jenny wants to keep her identity hidden.
moral_action: Jenny sends an anonymous tip to the police.
moral_consequence: The shooter is arrested.
immoral_action: Jenny stays silent about the crime.
immoral_consequence: The shooter strikes again.

norm: It's wrong not to take care of your teeth.
situation: John woke up late this morning, just rolled out of bed and needs to rush to get to work on time.
intention: John needs to cut something off his morning routine to make up for lost time.
moral_action: John skips the morning coffee in an attempt to get out the door quicker.
moral_consequence: John's teeth aren't stained brown by the coffee he normally drinks.
immoral_action: John skips brushing his teeth in an attempt to get out the door quicker.
immoral_consequence: John later develops a cavity due to his lack of dental hygiene.

norm: It's harmful to give people caffeine they didn't ask for.
situation: Max was waiting in a diner, and a customer wanted some decaf coffee, but there wasn't any brewed.
intention: Max wanted to finish the table.
moral_action: Max brews a fresh pot of decaf for the customer, pouring some into a mug for her.
moral_consequence: The customer is satisfied, and gives Max a reasonable tip for her effort.
immoral_action: Max grabs the pot of regular coffee, and fills up the mug of the customer without telling her.
immoral_consequence: The customer is allergic to it and has a bad reaction, struggling on the floor.

norm: You should not desecrate graves.
situation: Tommy is walking through a graveyard with friends and is bored.
intention: Tommy wants to have a good time, even in the graveyard.
moral_action: Tommy starts looking for strange quotes among the headstones and reads them to his friends.
moral_consequence: Tommy and his friends laugh at some of the things people want written after they die.
immoral_action: Tommy starts kicking over flowers and wreaths and draws silly faces on the headstones.
immoral_consequence: The families of the people's graves are horrified and very upset.

norm: You shouldn't look weird and creepy for your school photos.
situation: Dean is at home getting dressed and will have school pictures taken today.
intention: Dean wants to wear something to impress his friends.
moral_action: Dean brushes his hair, puts on a collared shirt, and gets his school picture taken.
moral_consequence: Dean's friends like it and his parents send the photo to family and friends.
immoral_action: Dean dresses up in all black, does his hair like a goth, and gets his school picture taken.
immoral_consequence: Dean's friends love it, but his parents are horrified.

norm: It's nice to pick an activity that everyone will enjoy.
situation: John is spending the day at the park with friends.
intention: John wants to decide what activity the group will participate in.
moral_action: John decides that the group will play basketball because he knows all his friends love it.
moral_consequence: John's friends all enjoy playing basketball in the park with him.
immoral_action: John decides that the group will play rugby because it is his favorite sport.
immoral_consequence: John's friends don't have a great time because they aren't very familiar with rugby and don't know how to play.

norm: You should always ask before going through someones phone.
situation: Tammy and her friend are trying to decide where to go out to dinner, and her friend leaves briefly to use the bathroom and leaves her phone behind.
intention: Tammy wants to choose a good restaurant.
moral_action: Tammy waits until her friend returns from the bathroom and asks if they can use her phone to look up restaurants on Yelp.
moral_consequence: Tammy's friend is happy to look at reviews and choose a restaurant together.
immoral_action: Tammy grabs her friends phone to look up restaurants on Yelp, and accidentally sees sensitive pictures her friend has sent to her boyfriend.
immoral_consequence: Tammy's friend is embarrassed and angry that she used her phone without asking.

norm: You should share with your friends.
situation: Harry was at the bar with his friends when he realized he was hungry and decided to order a large appetizer.
intention: Harry wants to eat.
moral_action: When the waiter delivers the appetizer, Harry leaves it in the center of the table and encourages his friends to have some.
moral_consequence: Harry's friends are appreciative of his generosity and enjoy the food.
immoral_action: When the waiter delivers the appetizer, Harry pulls it toward himself and eats it all without offering his friends any.
immoral_consequence: Harry's friends feel annoyed and have to order their own food.

norm: It's expected that family should openly communicate.
situation: Mindy comes home from work crying and wants to talk to her husband John about what happened.
intention: John wants to watch the ballgame.
moral_action: John puts the game on record and comforts Mindy and talks with her.
moral_consequence: Mindy feels loved and much closer to John than ever.
immoral_action: John pretends he doesn't see Mindy and puts the volume up on the tv.
immoral_consequence: Mindy feels even more upset and resents John and thinks of leaving him.

norm: People will think you're a bully if you harass others.
situation: Roberto is at a house party with a lot of pretty girls, and a couple of other men.
intention: Roberto wants to impress the girls.
moral_action: Roberto befriends one of the other guys, and they take turns telling jokes to the girls.
moral_consequence: The girls like the jokes and eventually two of them invite Roberto and the other guy out on a double date.
immoral_action: Roberto starts calling out of the other guys shortcomings in front of the girls.
immoral_consequence: The girls band together, call Roberto a bully, and force him to leave the party.

norm: It is good to take care of your property.
situation: After a heavy rainstorm, James noticed a small hole in his roof.
intention: James doesn't want to have to learn how to fix a roof.
moral_action: James finds a roofing company on Craigslist and contracts them to fix the roof.
moral_consequence: James is much more comfortable once his roof is repaired and all his stuff is dry.
immoral_action: James puts a pot under the hole in the roof and tries to ignore the leak.
immoral_consequence: The hole in the roof slowly gets bigger and many of James' possessions become water-logged.

norm: It's bad to not use birth control when having sex.
situation: Mikah is a college senior who has been getting serious with her longtime boyfriend, Jeff.
intention: Mikah wants to take her relationship with Jeff to the next level.
moral_action: Mikah purchases condoms online and uses one with Jeff once they come in.
moral_consequence: Mikah and Jeff have a healthy sex life and are able to complete their final year of college.
immoral_action: Too embarrassed to go out and purchase condoms, Mikah has sex with Jeff without one.
immoral_consequence: Mikah ends up pregnant and is forced to drop out of college.

norm: You shouldn't watch adult shows with minors.
situation: Patrick is sitting on the couch with his young son Mitch flipping trough the channels on the TV.
intention: Patrick wants to pick a show to watch.
moral_action: Patrick picks a nature documentary about animals of the Serengeti plains.
moral_consequence: Mitch is engrossed with watching the animals and loves learning new facts about them.
immoral_action: Patrick picks a crime show on a specialty channel that contains lots of graphic violence.
immoral_consequence: Mitch is traumatized and confused by the images he sees and has nightmares for weeks.

norm: It's cruel to make someone cry.
situation: Julie's friend, Clarissa, is from a poor family and arrives to school every day in the same outfit.
intention: Julie wants to talk to Clarissa about clothes.
moral_action: Julie compliments Clarissa's outfit and tells her she can borrow her clothes anytime she wants.
moral_consequence: Clarissa takes Julie up on her offer, and they bond over fashion.
immoral_action: "Julie asks Clarissa why she wears the same ""dirty old rags"" every day."
immoral_consequence: Clarissa looks down at her outfit and begins to cry.

norm: It is uncouth to fart in the presence of others.
situation: Richard watches his little sister start crying when his mom doesn't order desert at a restaurant.
intention: Richard wants to make his little sister smile.
moral_action: Richard folds a napkin into a small bird to get his sister's attention.
moral_consequence: His sister learns how to make things out of paper from her brother.
immoral_action: Richard stands up, puffs out his chest, and makes loud farting noises.
immoral_consequence: Richard's actions embarrasses his sister, and she hides behind her mother.

norm: You shouldn't use the internet to ruin a business's reputation.
situation: Kate recently visited Colby's restaurant and the waitress forgot her ketchup.
intention: Kate wants Colby to know about the service she got.
moral_action: Kate talks to Colby the next time she sees him in town.
moral_consequence: Colby makes sure that the staff at his restaurant are being properly trained and listen to the customers.
immoral_action: Kate goes on every site she can find to leave Colby a bad review.
immoral_consequence: Colby's restaurant suffers as people see the one star reviews online.

norm: It is weird to be attracted to kids.
situation: Leonard and his work friends are talking about the types of girls they like.
intention: Leonard wants to talk about the girls he thinks are attractive.
moral_action: Leonard says he thinks girls with slim bodies are attractive.
moral_consequence: Leonard's work friends will agree and continue the conversation.
immoral_action: Leonard says he thinks really young girls in middle school are attractive.
immoral_consequence: Leonard's work friends will think he's a creep and avoid him.

norm: It is okay to set rules for your own house
situation: Gigi has a group of friends and acquaintances over at her house for a party.
intention: Gigi wants her guests to feel at home in her house.
moral_action: Gigi explains to people that she always takes her shoes off before entering the house, and asks them to do the same.
moral_consequence: The house is mostly clean after the party and Gigi is happy not to have too much cleanup to do.
immoral_action: Gigi is too shy to ask people to take their shoes off before entering her house.
immoral_consequence: All the floors are filthy after the party and Gigi is pretty discouraged by the extent of the cleanup she's stuck with.

norm: It is wrong to flirt with women who are taken.
situation: John sees a beautiful woman walking with her boyfriend in the park and a woman walking alone.
intention: John wants to talk to women.
moral_action: John talks to the woman walking alone.
moral_consequence: John doesn't get hurt or embarrassed.
immoral_action: John walks up to the couple and starts talking to the woman.
immoral_consequence: John gets punched in the face.

norm: It's rude to make your child's life annoying.
situation: Ben hates taking karate class, so he asks his father if he can quit.
intention: Ben's father wants him in an extracurricular activity.
moral_action: Ben's father takes him out of the karate class and enrolls him in an art class instead.
moral_consequence: Ben's is grateful that he doesn't have to do something he doesn't want to anymore.
immoral_action: Ben's father tells him to suck it up and makes him go to karate class.
immoral_consequence: Ben starts to act out and skips the class when his father isn't there.

norm: You can't expect all your classes to be easy.
situation: Cade has the night free, but he has a test for his entry level math class tomorrow.
intention: Cade wants to have fun.
moral_action: Cade studies by playing an educational game he downloaded onto his computer.
moral_consequence: The game teaches him valuable study skills that he uses throughout the semester.
immoral_action: Cade goes out with his friends for the evening.
immoral_consequence: Cade fails the difficult math test.

norm: You shouldn't download things illegally.
situation: Marvin is excited about the release of a new game he wants to play.
intention: Marvin wants to get the game.
moral_action: Marvin purchases the game from a games website.
moral_consequence: Marvin plays and enjoys his new game he purchased.
immoral_action: Marvin downloads a cracked version of the game from a website for free.
immoral_consequence: Marvin gets sued by the publisher of the game.

norm: It's good to say nice things about other people.
situation: John had a tough day at work and comes home to see his wife Mindy cooking dinner.
intention: John wants to feel good about himself.
moral_action: John confides in Mindy that he had a rough day and then tells her the food looks amazing.
moral_consequence: Mindy comforts John and feels closer to him and happy too.
immoral_action: John tells Mindy she shouldn't be cooking because she can't make anything tasty.
immoral_consequence: Mindy feels sad and resents John and wonders if she'll cook again for him.

norm: People should not physically assault each other.
situation: Scott is on the playground at recess when a classmate Jimmy approaches him and forcefully takes the ball he's playing with from him.
intention: Scott wants to get the ball back.
moral_action: Scott tells Jimmy that he was using the ball and asks if he will give it back to him.
moral_consequence: Jimmy apologizes to Scott and gives him back the ball.
immoral_action: Scott strikes Jimmy with his fists and pushes him to the ground before taking the ball back.
immoral_consequence: Scott is sent to the principal's office and later suspended from school for using violence against another student.

norm: It's nice to share your birthday.
situation: Jill has a twin sister and her mom is planning their birthday party.
intention: Jill wants to feel special at her birthday party.
moral_action: Jill suggests that they make two birthday cakes so their friends can sing to each of them individually.
moral_consequence: Jill and her sister have a lot of fun at their birthday party and enjoy their special birthday song.
immoral_action: Jill tells her mom she doesn't want to have to share a birthday party with her sister.
immoral_consequence: Jill doesn't have a party at all because Jill's mom decided if the girls couldn't agree on one party, then they would have no party at all.

norm: You shouldn't worry your parents.
situation: Karen had a date planned with her boyfriend, but she hadn't told her parents yet.
intention: Karen has to decide whether to tell her parents where she's going.
moral_action: Karen tells her parents about her date and gives them his phone number.
moral_consequence: Karen's parents are glad that she was willing to tell them where she's going.
immoral_action: Karen sneaks out of her house and doesn't tell her parents what she's doing.
immoral_consequence: Karen's parents find out that she's gone and start to worry.

norm: It's bad to scare someone you know is vulnerable.
situation: Dean's older brother Graham has returned home from the military after being diagnosed with PTSD.
intention: Dean wants to play a prank on Graham for April Fool's Day.
moral_action: Dean switches around the contents of his and Graham's cereal boxes.
moral_consequence: Graham is surprised to pour the wrong cereal and shares a laugh with Dean when he realizes what happened.
