immoral_action: Dean buys a fake gun and pretends to be a robber breaking into Graham's room.
immoral_consequence: Graham's PTSD is triggered, and he reflexively hurts Dean because he thinks his life is in danger.

norm: It's nice to ask people they eat.
situation: Jane wants to throw a big party for her friends.
intention: Jane wants to throw the party.
moral_action: Jane asked her friends what they ate, so she could have food for everyone.
moral_consequence: Jane worked around lots of allergies and eating disorders.
immoral_action: Jane orginized the party without asking any of her friends anything except when they could come.
immoral_consequence: The food she had made was inedible to half of her guests.

norm: It is mean to prevent someone from using the bathroom.
situation: Jeff is holding a meeting when one of his subordinates indicates a desire to go to the restroom.
intention: Jeff wants to respond to his subordinates request.
moral_action: Jeff allows for the bathroom break and works around the subordinates absence.
moral_consequence: Jeff's subordinate returns refreshed and ready to rejoin the meeting.
immoral_action: Jeff doesn't want to disrupt the flow of the meeting, so he denies the request for a bathroom break.
immoral_consequence: Jeff's subordinate has a hard time focusing on the meeting as his discomfort grows.

norm: You should help your friends.
situation: Mary's friend John is moving to a new house and has asked for help.
intention: Mary wants to go to a party on John's moving date.
moral_action: Mary offers to come over and help John pack prior to the move so that she can attend the party later.
moral_consequence: John is appreciative of Mary's help, and they become closer as friends.
immoral_action: Mary goes to the party and ignores John's calls during the week of the move.
immoral_consequence: John gradually stops calling Mary and the friendship ends.

norm: You shouldn't kick someone just because they asked you out.
situation: James was asked out by his least favorite coworker, who attends some kind of local board meeting at least twice a week to complain.
intention: James wants his coworker to leave him alone.
moral_action: James goes to HR and tells them that one of his coworkers is making unwanted advances.
moral_consequence: The HR department talks to James' coworker and tells her to leave him alone.
immoral_action: "James kicks his coworker's ankle and says, ""I told you to leave me alone!""."
immoral_consequence: James' coworker complains to HR and has him fired for touching her.

norm: You shouldn't shoot people in the face.
situation: Bella is getting ready to play paintball with a group of friends.
intention: Bella wants to shoot her friends with paintballs.
moral_action: Bella waits for the game to begin and takes cover while carefully aiming her shots at her friends.
moral_consequence: Bella's friends are impressed with her accuracy in hitting them and have tons of fun playing the game.
immoral_action: Bella opens fire on her friends hitting them all over with paintballs before the game begins and before people have their protective face masks on.
immoral_consequence: Bella's friend suffer physical pain from being hit in the face without facemasks on and get incredibly angry at Bella.

norm: You shouldn't do things that would put you in jail.
situation: Vince is an accountant with a company.
intention: Vince wants to get some extra money.
moral_action: Vince helps his friends with their taxes for a fee.
moral_consequence: Vince makes some extra money.
immoral_action: Vince takes some money and works the accounting so that no one can see the loss.
immoral_consequence: The records are audited and Vince's theft is discovered, so he is fired and arrested.

norm: It is inconsiderate to make other people sick.
situation: Igor has the flu but can't afford to miss a day of work.
intention: Igor wants to work despite his illness.
moral_action: Igor calls his boss and asks if he can work remotely because he's sick.
moral_consequence: The people at Igor's work don't catch Igor's illness.
immoral_action: Igor goes to work as if he is healthy and works hard.
immoral_consequence: Igor gets other people sick, who then miss work and hurt the business.

norm: It's arrogant to judge others inferior to yourself.
situation: Larry is a successful lawyer who just won a case against another lawyer, who's nowhere near as successful as Larry.
intention: Larry wants to say something to his opponent - the lawyer who lost the case.
moral_action: Larry encourages the other lawyer, tells him not to give up and even gives him some good advice.
moral_consequence: The other lawyer feels a little better despite loosing the case, and he is very grateful to Larry for the kind words and the advice.
immoral_action: Larry tells the other lawyer that he is a joke, and he'd better change careers, because he has no future as a lawyer.
immoral_consequence: The other lawyer is humiliated by Larry's words, his confidence is crushed, and he feels useless.

norm: People should teach children kindness and gentleness.
situation: Allison is taking her child to a playgroup for the first time.
intention: Allison wants her child to be around other children.
moral_action: Allison sees that her child has a problem taking other children's toys and tells her she must share them.
moral_consequence: Her child learns manners and makes many friends in the play group.
immoral_action: Allison sees her child take a toy from another child and says nothing.
immoral_consequence: Her child becomes ostracized and no one will play with her.

norm: Is wrong to cheat on your significant other
situation: Jeff is at the bar with some friends while his wife Holly is at home when a strange woman asks to take Jeff home.
intention: Jeff wants to respond to the offer.
moral_action: Jeff tells the woman that while she's hot, he will not go home with her.
moral_consequence: Holly is delighted that Jeff is a man who can be trusted and who is faithful to him, and she's happy she married him.
immoral_action: Jeff tells the woman that he will definitely go home with her as she's really hot.
immoral_consequence: Holly is devastated when she finds out her relationship with Jeff has been broken beyond repair.

norm: It's illegal to kill another human being.
situation: Mason was arguing with Jenson at a bar one night.
intention: Mason wants Jenson to leave him alone.
moral_action: Mason leaves the bar and goes over to one of his friend's house.
moral_consequence: Mason is able to enjoy his night without having to worry about Jenson.
immoral_action: Mason hits Jenson in the head several times with a glass bottle.
immoral_consequence: Mason is arrested when Jenson dies from his head injuries.

norm: It's rude to attack people with a knife.
situation: John is in the kitchen making dinner with his wife.
intention: John wants to make a salad.
moral_action: John is making a salad his wife says hes doing it wrong, so he ask her to help him.
moral_consequence: John and his wife have a nice dinner and later watch a movie.
immoral_action: While John is making a salad his wife starts yelling at him that hes doing it wrong so John shoves the knife in her face attacking her.
immoral_consequence: Johns wife gets so angry and leaves she divorces him a week later.

norm: It's wrong to disapprove of someone's choice of boyfriend.
situation: Gabby's friend Hannah just started dating a new boy, and Hannah asks Gabby what she thinks of him.
intention: Gabby wants to respond to Hannah's question.
moral_action: Gabby says she doesn't know Hannah's boyfriend well enough to judge him.
moral_consequence: Hannah invites Gabby to hang out with her and her boyfriend, so they can get to know each other better.
immoral_action: Gabby says she thinks Hannah's new boyfriend is a jerk.
immoral_consequence: Hannah gets upset at Gabby and stops talking to her.

norm: Keeping information from a partner is not considered good behavior.
situation: Jim is married and his father passed away and left him an inheritance.
intention: Jim wants to buy a second home.
moral_action: Jim and his wife buy a vacation home together.
moral_consequence: Jim's wife will be happy and feel appreciated by Jim.
immoral_action: Jim buys a second home as a bachelor pad to bring dates back to and doesn't tell his wife.
immoral_consequence: Jim's wife will divorce him when she finds out he's cheating on her.

norm: You shouldn't binge drink because it's bad for you.
situation: Peter is at a party where he doesn't know too many people.
intention: Peter wants to make new friends.
moral_action: Peter decides to drink moderately  and entertains everyone with fun stories.
moral_consequence: Peter feels great the next day.
immoral_action: Peter starts drinking with a few guys he just met, and they bond while drinking all night.
immoral_consequence: Peter is terribly sick the next day.

norm: You should not pressure your partner to marry you.
situation: John and Mary are on a weekend trip to a bed and breakfast in the country.
intention: John wants to get married to Mary.
moral_action: John proposes to Mary, and when she says no, he respects her decision.
moral_consequence: John and Mary have a nice weekend at the bed and breakfast and return to the city.
immoral_action: John proposes to Mary, and when she says no, he demands she accept his proposal.
immoral_consequence: Mary leaves, and later decides to end her relationship with John.

norm: It's nice to compliment others.
situation: Gene's wife Angela just got back from the hair salon with a new hairstyle, but he doesn't really like it.
intention: Gene wants to react to Angela's hair.
moral_action: Gene tells Angela that he thinks she looks as pretty as ever, but likes her hair the other way too.
moral_consequence: Angela feel beautiful and is glad Gene thinks she looks good no matter what.
immoral_action: Gene tells Angela that the style she got doesn't compliment her bone structure.
immoral_consequence: Angela now feels self-conscious and is embarrassed to go out in public.

norm: It's rude to expect others to fix things for free.
situation: Ken's best friend Jacob is a mechanic and Ken's car has a problem with its transmission.
intention: Ken wants to ask Jacob to fix his car.
moral_action: Ken asks Jacob if he'll fix his car for him if Ken pays him his normal rate.
moral_consequence: Jacob agrees to fix Ken's car and gets it up and running within a day.
immoral_action: Ken asks Jacob to fix his car for him for free because they're best friends.
immoral_consequence: Jacob refuses to fix the car for free and then stops talking to Ken because he thinks he'll be asked for more favors.

norm: It's rude to think you are better than others.
situation: Mia is comparing test scores with friends and clearly has the best scores so is being praised.
intention: Mia wants to decide how to handle all the praise.
moral_action: MIa remains humble and gracious, with humor.
moral_consequence: Her friends respect her more.
immoral_action: Mia emphasizes her strengths and tells the others why they didn't do as we;;.
immoral_consequence: Her friends are alienated by Mia.

norm: It's bad to use someone's property without permission.
situation: Caleb was at his friend's house for a sleep over when he realized that he forgot his toothbrush.
intention: Caleb wants to brush his teeth.
moral_action: Caleb calls his mother and asks her to bring his toothbrush to his friend's house.
moral_consequence: Caleb gets his toothbrush from his mother a half hour later and is able to brush his teeth.
immoral_action: Caleb goes to the bathroom and uses his friend's toothbrush to brush his teeth.
immoral_consequence: Caleb catches strep throat from his friend and has to go to the doctor.

norm: It's rude to stop talking to someone.
situation: Jill and Yolanda are in a long-distance relationship.
intention: Jill wants to break up with Yolanda.
moral_action: Jill explains her reasons for wanting to break up to Yolanda over the phone.
moral_consequence: Yolanda is sad but understands.
immoral_action: Jill suddenly cuts off all contact with Yolanda and disappears.
immoral_consequence: Yolanda feels worried about Jill and devastated that she's been abruptly dumped.

norm: It's fun to go out with your buddies.
situation: Timothy is playing a video game by himself when a buddy calls and tells him and invites him to hang out with them.
intention: Timothy wants to play his video game.
moral_action: Timothy agrees to hang out with them for a while, and then goes back to his video game when he gets home.
moral_consequence: Timothy and his friends have a good time and hang out again later.
immoral_action: Timothy turns his buddy down and goes back to his video game.
immoral_consequence: Timothy's buddy doesn't bother to call him the next time they hang out.

norm: It is wrong to impregnate somebody without consent.
situation: Grant is married to his wife Joan, and they use condoms for birth control.
intention: Grant wants to have a baby.
moral_action: Grant explains to Joan his desire to have a baby.
moral_consequence: Joan will be open to Grant's desires.
immoral_action: Grant pokes holes in the condoms, so he can get Joan pregnant.
immoral_consequence: Joan will feel betrayed and upset with Grant.

norm: It's wrong to leave trash or belongings in nature
situation: Josh is out camping with his friends, and he just finished drinking a beer.
intention: Josh wants to get rid of the beer can.
moral_action: Josh walks to the other side of the camp ground to throw his trash away in the trashcan.
moral_consequence: Josh meets some cool people hanging around the trash area.
immoral_action: Josh places the beer can in the woods outside of the campground.
immoral_consequence: A park ranger spots Josh and fines him for littering.

norm: It is wrong to poison people
situation: Tim's mother is sick and isn't feeling very well today.
intention: Tim doesn't want his mother to be in pain.
moral_action: Tim calls a doctor to pay his mother a house visit.
moral_consequence: The doctor prescribes medications for Tim's mother to take.
immoral_action: Tim gives his mother a high dose of poison to drink.
immoral_consequence: Tim's mother dies from the poison, and he is arrested.

norm: It's good to accept help from people.
situation: Jon is looking to start a new business and comes from a very supportive, financially stable family.
intention: Jon wants to find funding for his new business.
moral_action: Jon gets the start up capital that he needs from his family.
moral_consequence: Jon's family is happy to help him on his way and be part of his plans.
immoral_action: Jon decides to slowly save up the money himself which is a long and difficult process.
immoral_consequence: Jon's family feels regret when they see him struggling to get his business going.

norm: You should help people out when their car breaks down.
situation: Joel is on his way to work when he sees a man named Jack with his car broken down on the side of the highway.
intention: Joel wants to make it to work on time.
moral_action: Joel tells Jack that he doesn't have time to stick around, but can call and pay for a mechanic.
moral_consequence: Jack is thankful for Joel's help and is able to get his car fixed to drive home safely.
immoral_action: Hoping to get to work on time, Joel drives right by the broken down car without stopping.
immoral_consequence: Because no one stopped to help Jack, he is forced to walk home and leave his car on the side of the road.

norm: You shouldn't sabotage people's goals.
situation: Dale wants to build a 50 foot guard tower in his neighborhood and that annoys Bill.
intention: Bill wants to do something about the tower.
moral_action: Bill tells Dale how he feels about the tower directly.
moral_consequence: Dale decides to build a huge swimming pool instead and Bill helps him out.
immoral_action: Bill tells the city that Dale shouldn't be allowed to build the guard tower.
immoral_consequence: The city rejects Dale's variance and Dale settles for building a 39 foot guard tower.

norm: It's okay to focus on your family.
situation: Chris has a busy work-life and is equally busy at home, since he wants to help his wife with taking care of their newborn baby as much as he can.
intention: Chris is tired of multitasking and wants to be able to focus his efforts.
moral_action: Chris chooses to spend more time with his family and to focus less on work.
moral_consequence: Chris' wife feels supported and enjoys the way their home life unfolds.
immoral_action: Chris decides to focus on his work and devotes less time to his family.
immoral_consequence: Chris' wife feels overwhelmed and tired taking care of everything at home.

norm: You should not yell at your pet.
situation: Jan's pet dog, Spot, chewed up her favorite dress shoes.
intention: Jan wants Spot not to destroy her things.
moral_action: Jan locks away the rest of her shoes and mildly admonishes Spot.
moral_consequence: Spot does not chew up any more of her shoes.
immoral_action: Jan yells at Spot, who is so scared he pees on the floor.
immoral_consequence: Jan has to clean up dog pee, as well as her shoes.

norm: It's good to say a well-meaning remark to someone struggling.
situation: Claire sees that her friend Ashley is down in the dumps about a breakup.
intention: Claire wants to give Ashley her advice.
moral_action: Claire tells Ashley that she is a strong person, and she will be fine.
moral_consequence: Ashley gets strength from Claire's support and feels better about herself everyday.
immoral_action: Claire tells Ashley that it's her fault for the breakup because she has bad taste in men.
immoral_consequence: Ashley cries and feels like everything in her life is hopeless.

norm: You shouldn't expect others to cover for you at work.
situation: Jon is currently at work and is about to go on his lunch break.
intention: Jon wants to take an extended lunch to take care of a personal matter.
moral_action: Jon doesn't mention anything to his coworker, so he can say he doesn't know.
moral_consequence: Jon's friend is able to finish his work shift comfortably.
immoral_action: Jon instructs his friend and coworker on a story to tell his boss if asked.
immoral_consequence: Jon's friend feels pressured into having to lie to the boss.

norm: Using violence to get back at someone is immature.
situation: Tim insults Al's mother and it hurts Al's feelings alot.
intention: Al wants to get back at Tim.
moral_action: Al decides to make a clever remark about Tim himself.
moral_consequence: Everyone laughs at Al's joke and Al is satisfied at the results.
immoral_action: Al punches Tim and starts a fight because of the insult.
immoral_consequence: Al and Tim end up fighting and injuring each other over a petty squabble.

norm: Parents are expected to have faith in their children.
situation: Todd's daughter wants to be an actress.
intention: Todd wants to help his daughter financially.
moral_action: Todd tells his daughter he will support her financially for a year, after which he knows she will be able to support herself through her acting.
moral_consequence: Todd's daughter is buoyed by her father's trust in her abilities.
immoral_action: Todd tells his daughter he will support her financially because he does not think she can support herself with her acting.
immoral_consequence: Todd's daughter is sad that her father does not have faith in her abilities.

norm: It's not okay to use addictive drugs.
situation: Jamie had previously been prescribed a strong narcotic after getting into a bad car accident.
intention: Jamie wants the narcotic out of his house for good.
moral_action: Jamie brings his pills to an appropriate location to be dropped off and disposed of.
moral_consequence: Jamie, and others, are safe from the dangers of the narcotic.
immoral_action: Jamie decides to take the remainder of his pills even though he does not need them.
immoral_consequence: Jamie becomes addicted and his life goes into a downward spiral.

norm: It is wrong to purposely embarrass someone else.
situation: Jimmy was at the talent show as his competition Billy got on the stage.
intention: Jimmy wants to win the talent show.
moral_action: Jimmy uses the time to practice his own talents during Billy's show.
moral_consequence: Jimmy does his best, and he is able to outperform Billy and win the competition.
immoral_action: Jimmy heckles Billy during the show to try and throw him off his game.
immoral_consequence: Billy screws up because of the taunts and Jimmy wins the show, however people no longer like Jimmy.

norm: It's wrong to demean a gender.
situation: Wally is the debate team manager and is in charge of picking the team lineup.
intention: Wally wants to choose students for the debate team.
moral_action: Wally chooses the debate team lineup based on performance regardless of gender.
moral_consequence: The debate team will have a higher chance of winning.
immoral_action: Wally only chooses boys for the debate team lineup because he thinks boys are smarter.
immoral_consequence: The debate team will miss out on potentially intelligent members by only choosing boys.

norm: You shouldn't make old people do things.
situation: Sam's elderly father William is living with Sam since he had a bad injury, and he has difficulty walking long distances.
intention: Sam wants to go camping.
moral_action: Sam decides to go camping alone for a couple of days and gives his father his cell phone number in case of an emergency.
moral_consequence: William is able to spend a quiet weekend relaxing at home without aggravating his injury.
immoral_action: Sam decides that they should go on a family excursion and takes William camping along with him.
immoral_consequence: William gets very tired throughout the camping trip and is uncomfortable walking through the woods.

norm: It's not okay to handle things that aren't yours.
situation: Octavian notices that his brother's car is blocking the entrance to the driveway.
intention: Octavian wants to move his brother's car.
moral_action: Octavian knocks on his brother's door informing him about his car.
moral_consequence: Octavian is thanked by his stressed brother.
immoral_action: Octavian attempts to back his brother's car out of the driveway.
immoral_consequence: Octavian runs into a mailbox damaging the back of the car.

norm: It is rude to be bossy.
situation: Jenna was working with her classmates to make a poster for history class.
intention: Jenna wants to make sure they get an A.
moral_action: Jenna concentrates on doing her part of the poster well and gives her classmates occasional advice.
moral_consequence: Jenna's group gets an A and thanks her for her help.
immoral_action: Jenna tells her classmates exactly how to do every part of the poster.
immoral_consequence: Jenna's group gets an A, but all of her group mates are angry at her by the end.

norm: You shouldn't be bitter and jealous toward your friends.
situation: Edward's friend just landed an amazing job while Edward has been struggling for a while.
intention: Edward wants to help himself feel better.
moral_action: Edward congratulates his friend and takes some time to do activites that relax and center him.
moral_consequence: Edward's friend is happy to have Edward's support.
immoral_action: Edward puts down his friend's achievement and makes snide comments.
immoral_consequence: Edward's friend is hurt and ends their friendship.

norm: It is gross to be excessively dirty.
situation: Jan lives alone with two dogs and never cleans up after them or her house.
intention: Jan wants to have some company over.
moral_action: Jan sweeps, cleans, and airs out her house before inviting a friend over.
moral_consequence: Jan and her friend spend the day catching up on her couch.
immoral_action: Jan invites a friend over without picking up first.
immoral_consequence: Jan's friend starts coughing and has to leave due to all of the dirt and pet odor in Jan's home.

norm: It's mean to abandon your dog to fend for itself.
situation: George is camping with his Golden Retriever, Sparky when a raccoon attacks the dog.
intention: George wants to react to the situation.
moral_action: George grabs a stick and swats it at the raccoon which makes it flee from Sparky.
moral_consequence: Sparky is able to avoid any serious injury.
immoral_action: George is afraid and lets Sparky handle the raccoon on his own.
immoral_consequence: Sparky ends up blind in one eye because the raccoon scratched it really hard.

norm: You shouldn't call someone's parent fat.
situation: Jake and Paula are driving home after having just met Paula's parents for the first time.
intention: Jake wants to give Paula his impression of her parents.
moral_action: Jake tells Paula how much he enjoyed her parents company.
moral_consequence: Paula is pleased that Jake liked her parents.
immoral_action: Jake comments on how rotund Paula's father is.
immoral_consequence: Paula takes offense to Jake's observation.

norm: It's good to be there for your partner.
situation: John and his girlfriend have a school test coming up in a subject that John is much better at than his girlfriend.
intention: John wants to be prepared for the test.
moral_action: John spends part of his time studying for the test but also spends some time tutoring his girlfriend.
moral_consequence: John's girlfriend get's a good grade on the test and passes the class.
immoral_action: John spends his time studying for the test and leaves his girlfriend to fend for herself.
immoral_consequence: John's girlfriend fails the test and receives a low grade for the class.

norm: It's wrong to swear at your family.
situation: Roger is at a family dinner when the discussion gets ugly and his parents start saying hurtful things to each other.
intention: Roger wants his parents to listen to what he has to say.
moral_action: Roger starts speaking forcefully and eloquently about family values and respect.
moral_consequence: Roger's parents are inspired by what he's saying.
immoral_action: Rogers acts angry and curses at his parents to carry his point across.
immoral_consequence: Roger's parents listen to him but are shocked by his disrespectful tone.

norm: It is wrong to spit into the food of others.
situation: Christina is working at Subway and is taking the order of a woman who once bullied her.
intention: Christina wants to feel better about her former bully being in the store with her.
moral_action: Christina asks her manager if she can go into the back for a moment to get away from her aggressor.
moral_consequence: Christina's boss understands and takes Christina's former bully's order.
immoral_action: Christina waits until the customer's back is turned and lets some of her saliva fall into the sandwich.
immoral_consequence: Christina's boss sees her unhygienic action and terminates her from her job.

norm: It is not okay to disrespect someone's home.
situation: John just started his own interior design firm and is meeting with a new client.
intention: John wants to prove he is good at his job.
moral_action: John comments on the lived-in charm of the living room.
moral_consequence: The client feels respected by John and hires him.
immoral_action: John laughs at the decor in the client's living room, pointing out all the things he will change.
immoral_consequence: The client decides to hire a different designer.

norm: It's rude to tease someone about their hair.
situation: Jenna's sister was trying to save money for a new car, so she went to a hair salon and got a disastrous haircut.
intention: Jenna wants to avoid lying about her opinion of the haircut.
moral_action: Jenna tells her sister that she has some beautiful head scarves she can borrow.
moral_consequence: Jenna's sister thanks her and says she wants to sue the incompetent hairdresser.
immoral_action: Jenna tells her sister that her hair's so short she looks ready to enlist in the military.
immoral_consequence: Jenna's sister responds that Jenna's hair looks like a rat's nest.

norm: You shouldn't drink if you're a teen because it's illegal.
situation: Steve is 16 and is at his older brother's college campus when someone offers him a drink.
intention: Steve wants to make a decision.
moral_action: Steve turns down the drink stating he isn't old enough yet.
moral_consequence: A police officer pulls up and ID's everyone with a beer in their hand, so Steve's brother and friends feel lucky that he turned down their offer.
immoral_action: Steve takes a bottle of beer and drinks it down.
immoral_consequence: A  police officer pulls up and sees Steve drinking, then Steve's brother and his friends are brought up on charges of contributing to a minor.

norm: It's wrong to bully someone.
situation: Terrence is in the school cafeteria and doesn't have money to buy lunch, but see's that his classmate Jeremy has a whole tray.
intention: Terrence wants to eat Jeremy's food.
moral_action: Terrence asks Jeremy if he would mind sharing some food with him, so he gives him half.
moral_consequence: Jeremy feels good about himself for helping his fellow classmate.
immoral_action: Terrence walks up to Jeremy and says he will beat him up unless he gives up his food, so Jeremy hands it over.
immoral_consequence: Jeremy feels sad and angry, and now has nothing to eat.

norm: You shouldn't hire the wrong people for the job.
situation: Angela is the owner of a small business.
intention: She wants to hire a new manager.
moral_action: Angela hires a qualified candidate through a professional interview process.
moral_consequence: Angela gains a lot of new business and makes a lot of money.
immoral_action: Angela hires her cousin even though he is unqualified.
immoral_consequence: Angela loses a lot of business and has to declare bankruptcy.

norm: It's bad to not watch where you're going.
situation: Ben is walking through a busy lot back to the car before meeting up with a friend.
intention: Ben wants to text his friend to let them know he's on the way.
moral_action: Ben waits to get in his car before texting.
moral_consequence: Ben pays attention to where he is going and doesn't get in anyone's way.
immoral_action: Ben starts texting while walking through a crowd of people.
immoral_consequence: Ben runs into someone causing them to think he is rude and aloof.

norm: You shouldn't take time off work unless you are sick.
situation: Jerry is getting ready to go to work.
intention: Jerry wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Jerry buys doughnuts on the way to work and invites everyone to enjoy them on their morning break.
moral_consequence: Jerry gains favor with his boss for creating a fun work environment.
immoral_action: Jerry calls in sick to work and goes to a baseball game.
immoral_consequence: Jerry gets fired when his bosses see him at the game when watching it on tv.

norm: It's inexcusable to throw someone's children into bodies of water.
situation: Boris is watching his friend's children scared to jump into the pool.
intention: Boris wants the kids to have fun.
moral_action: Boris tosses a bunch of floats and water toys into the water for the kids to enjoy.
moral_consequence: Boris is thanked by the kids who have fun paddling around the pool on the floats.
immoral_action: Boris pushes the kids into the pool while making silly monster sounds.
immoral_consequence: Boris is scolded by the kid's parents who are unhappy with his actions.

norm: It's good to decorate for Halloween.
situation: Heather recently moved into a new neighborhood and Halloween is coming up in a few days.
intention: She wants to prepare for trick-or-treaters.
moral_action: Heather decorates her yard and house to really get into the Halloween spirit.
moral_consequence: The neighborhood kids all stop by her house to trick-or-treat for some candy.
immoral_action: Heather prepares a bowl of candy at her front door but doesn't do any decorating.
immoral_consequence: The neighborhood kids mostly walk by her house and assume she is not participating in Halloween.

norm: It is rude to refuse to tip.
situation: Sally found a hair in her salad which she ordered at a restaurant.
intention: Sally wants to show how disgusted she is.
moral_action: Sally gets her meal comped but proceeds to leave a tip for the server because it wasn't her fault.
moral_consequence: Sally's server is happy to get a tip despite the bad customer experience.
immoral_action: Sally refuses to pay for her meal and tips nothing because of the incident.
immoral_consequence: Sally's server doesn't make enough money during her shift because of the kitchen staff's mistake.

norm: It's good to take your kids fun places.
situation: Mary and her kids have some free time during the weekend.
intention: Mary wants to go out with her kids.
moral_action: Mary takes her kids to an amusement park.
moral_consequence: Mary and her kids have an exciting afternoon.
immoral_action: Mary takes her kids to the library.
immoral_consequence: Mary reads while her kids fall asleep from boredom.

norm: It's bad to flake out on your group.
situation: Pat is part of a basketball team that has a game coming up and Pat is still in bed.
intention: Pat wants to decide what to do with his day.
moral_action: Pat gets out of bed and goes to the game.
moral_consequence: Pat's team will be able to play with a full roster.
immoral_action: Pat stays in bed and decides not to go to the game.
immoral_consequence: Pat's team will be down 1 player and be at a disadvantage.

norm: It is wrong to tell on a friend.
situation: Gina has just found out that her friend Tim has been having unprotected sex with strangers, and she feels worried.
intention: Gina wants to keep Tim safe.
moral_action: Gina has a heart-to-heart with Tim and explains how she is scared for him and asks him if there is anything wrong.
moral_consequence: Tim opens up to Gina and agrees to stop his risky behavior.
immoral_action: Gina tells Tim's parents what he has been doing.
immoral_consequence: Tim is punished and no longer trusts Tina.

norm: It's good to nurture your friendships.
situation: Stephanie has a new job and has to move away from her hometown.
intention: Stephanie wants to earn a lot of money and live independently.
moral_action: Stephanie works hard at her job but continues to stay in contact with her friends and go out with them in her free time.
moral_consequence: Stephanie has a great work-life balance and talking with her friends helps her manage the stress from work.
immoral_action: Stephanie works hard at her job but ignores her friends when they invite her out.
immoral_consequence: Stephanie drifts apart from her friends, and they stop inviting her, making Stephanie feel lonely.

norm: It's nice to throw a party for your friend's birthday.
situation: Gina's best friend's birthday is coming up soon and people have suggested Gina organize a birthday party at her own house for her friend.
intention: Gina wants her house to be a private place, a refuge to get away from it all.
moral_action: Gina decides to throw a big party at a fancy restaurant for her best friend's birthday.
moral_consequence: Gina's best friend is delighted about the party.
immoral_action: Gina decides not to organize a party for her friend because she doesn't want people in her house.
immoral_consequence: Gina's best friend is disappointed Gina did not organize anything for her.

norm: You shouldn't be sassy toward your parents.
situation: Isabelle, who was recently grounded, watches her mother struggle to remove viruses from her computer.
intention: Isabelle wants to comment on her mother's situation.
moral_action: Isabelle spends time explaining and teaching her mother about computer viruses.
moral_consequence: Isabelle's mother orders chocolate cake to thank Isabelle for helping her.
immoral_action: Isabelle crosses her arms and tells her mom that most normal people would have eliminated the virus by now.
immoral_consequence: Isabelle is grounded an extra day for her attitude.

norm: It's rude to ignore people's complaints.
situation: Eric asks John if he can open his windows a bit in his room to make it smell better.
intention: John wants to keep his utility bills low.
moral_action: John compromises with Eric and installs insulating windows that can be opened a bit while being energy efficient.
moral_consequence: Eric appreciates John's concern for him and likes him more.
immoral_action: John pretends he doesn't hear Eric and says windows have to remain shut.
immoral_consequence: Eric resents John and considers moving out.

norm: You should not call someone you care about insulting names.
situation: Henry was having a conversation with his mother when they got into a disagreement.
intention: Henry wants to tell his mother goodbye.
moral_action: Henry tells his mother that he loves her and tells her goodbye.
moral_consequence: Henry's mother gives him a hug and tells him to be home in time for dinner.
immoral_action: Henry calls his mother an old hag and walks away from her.
immoral_consequence: Henry's mother kicks him out of the house and tells him that she doesn't want to see him anymore.

norm: Partners are expected to recall their wedding anniversary.
situation: Frank remembers that his wedding anniversary is coming up in a few weeks and buys his wife something special.
intention: Frank wants to hide the gift for his wife.
moral_action: Frank  hides the gift and sets a calendar reminder to retrieve the gift the day before the anniversary.
moral_consequence: Frank's wife is surprised and delighted by the wedding fit.
immoral_action: Frank puts the gift in a secret place at work and forgets about it.
immoral_consequence: The wedding anniversary comes and goes without notice and Frank's wife becomes distraught.

norm: It is good to take responisibility.
situation: Josh has broken his mother's vase on accident and knows she will be upset.
intention: Josh wants to tell his mother about the vase.
moral_action: Josh tells his mother that he will work to pay for the vase that he broke.
moral_consequence: Josh's mother is upset, but she is proud of him for telling the truth.
immoral_action: Josh tells his mother that his brother was the one who broke the vase.
immoral_consequence: Josh gets in trouble when his mother finds out that Josh was not telling the truth.

norm: Abandoning animals makes you look cold.
situation: Randy's cat is pregnant, and he doesn't have enough time at home to care for kittens.
intention: Randy wants to get rid of his cat.
moral_action: Randy brings the cat to the SPCA and surrenders her to them.
moral_consequence: Randy is sad, but the people at the SPCA make him feel like they understand his situation.
immoral_action: Randy drives to a nearby neighborhood and puts his cat outside of his car on the side of the road before driving off.
immoral_consequence: One of the neighborhood locals sees Randy's action, takes his photo, and shames him on social media.

norm: It is good to share needed information with other people
situation: Elliot learned facts about a singer he'd never heard of, later on Johnny asks him about the same singer.
intention: Elliot wants to continue the conversation with Johnny.
moral_action: Elliot realizes that while that singer is unimportant to Elliot, it's important to Johnny and thus tells him about it.
moral_consequence: Johnny is excited to hear new information about his favorite artist.
immoral_action: Elliot doesn't tell Johnny about the singer because Elliot doesn't care about the singer.
immoral_consequence: Johnny misses out on some important information on his favorite artist.

norm: You should always help out others.
situation: Jerry is walking down the street and sees a stranded couple having car trouble.
intention: Jerry wants to feel better about the sight of the stranded couple.
moral_action: Jerry stops to help the stranded couple fix their car.
moral_consequence: The couple is happy to have received help and goes on their way.
immoral_action: Jerry ignores the stranded couple and soon forgets about them.
immoral_consequence: The stranded couple continues to be in a bad situation.

norm: It's foolish to turn down a well-paying job.
situation: Ron has been looking for work when he suddenly gets a call for an interview to be a nursing assistant.
intention: Ron wants to talk to the interviewer.
moral_action: Ron finishes his interview and is offered the job at a rate of $30.00 an hour which he accepts.
moral_consequence: Ron ends up very well off from a financial standpoint.
immoral_action: Ron finishes his interview and is offered the job at a rate of $30.00 an hour, but turns it down because they only offer 2 weeks in vacation a year .
immoral_consequence: Ron doesn't get another offer that comes remotely close, so he has to accept something worse.

norm: It's good to have respect for teachers.
situation: Billy is a middle school student and his math teacher asks him to demonstrate a problem on the blackboard.
intention: Billy wants to respond to his teacher's request.
moral_action: Billy complies with the request and demonstrates how to solve the math problem on the blackboard.
moral_consequence: Billy is praised for his effort and pariticpation and feels proud of himself.
immoral_action: Billy tells the teacher to buzz off and proceeds to ignore her.
immoral_consequence: Billy is sent to the principal's office for talking back to the teacher in a disrespectful manner.

norm: It is bad to use alcohol to cope.
situation: Chelsea is going through a difficult divorce from her husband Max.
intention: Chelsea wants to calm her nerves.
moral_action: Chelsea starts to practice meditation and learns to use deep breathing exercises to cope.
moral_consequence: Chelsea learns a healthy way to deal with her stress and feels good about her progress.
immoral_action: Chelsea begins drinking large quantities of whiskey on a daily basis.
immoral_consequence: Chelsea develops an alcohol addiction and has to check into rehab.

norm: It's wrong to hate others.
situation: Josh is not accepted by a group of students at his school because he dresses different, and they often tease him for his style.
intention: Josh wants to be left alone by the teenagers.
moral_action: Josh talks to a counselor about the student's negative remarks and the counselor talks to the students, where they start being nice to Josh.
moral_consequence: The students decide to treat Josh with kindness and Josh later becomes great friends with them.
immoral_action: Josh starts having extremely negative emotions towards the students and threatens them, where they are scared and stay away from him.
immoral_consequence: The students report Josh to the principal for the threat, which leads to Josh being expelled for school.

norm: You shouldn't take advantage of someone with down syndrome.
situation: One of James' classmates, Alan, has Down Syndrome and gets $10 from his parents every day to buy lunch.
intention: James wants enough money to buy a candy bar at lunch.
moral_action: James offers to help Alan with his homework in exchange for $2.
moral_consequence: James is able to afford his candy bar and Alan has a slightly easier time in school.
immoral_action: James sells white gravel to Alan, telling him that the pebbles are diamonds.
immoral_consequence: James is eventually caught and given a week's worth of lunch detentions.

norm: It is wrong to steal another person's child.
situation: Kelly is barren and is researching her options.
intention: Kelly wants a child to raise and love.
moral_action: Kelly goes through all the requirements to be able to adopt an orphan child and provide it love and a home.
moral_consequence: Kelly raises a young child who was orphaned and the child grows up happy and loved.
immoral_action: Kelly decides the cheapest and fastest option is to find an unattended child in public to grab and take home.
immoral_consequence: Kelly traumatizes a young child when she grabs it away from its parents.

norm: It's not okay to make racist comments or jokes
situation: James is trying to come up with a dark comedy routine for a party.
intention: James wants to make people laugh.
moral_action: James calls his friends and spends the evening coming up with fresh material.
moral_consequence: James is proud when his friend laughs at his jokes.
immoral_action: James makes his jokes based on racial stereotypes.
immoral_consequence: James is called out for being a racist later by the angry crowd.

norm: It's good to bake people a cake for their birthday.
situation: James, who worked in HR, knew that one of his colleagues had a birthday coming up.
intention: James wants to help his coworker celebrate his birthday.
moral_action: James bakes a funfetti cake and tops it with buttercream frosting and candles.
moral_consequence: Everyone compliments James on the delicious treat he made for them.
immoral_action: James brings in a veggie platter in an effort to encourage healthy lifestyles.
immoral_consequence: No one touches the veggie platter, which ends up in the garbage.

norm: You shouldn't get involved in a relationship with an ex.
situation: Katie, who is single, is feeling particularly lonely and has been talking to her ex who cheated on her.
intention: Katie wants to be with someone romantically.
moral_action: Katie keeps her ex at a distance and finds someone new on a dating website.
moral_consequence: The ex regrets what he did when he sees her with a new partner.
immoral_action: Katie rekindles her feelings with her ex and dates him again.
immoral_consequence: The ex gets the impression that his previous actions are forgiven.

norm: It's rude to hog the bathroom.
situation: Joanne is getting ready for school in the bathroom she has to share with her two sisters.
intention: Joanne wants to look good for school.
moral_action: Joanne uses the bathroom to take a shower and then finishes getting ready in her room.
moral_consequence: Joanne's sisters are happy that they are able to use the bathroom before going to school.
immoral_action: Joanne stays in the bathroom getting ready until a few minutes before the bus comes to pick them up.
immoral_consequence: Joanne's sisters are mad that they have to go to school without being able to use the bathroom at all.

norm: It's seen as being an alcoholic if you drink alone.
situation: Sam works as a salesperson in a high stress environment and today was especially troublesome.
intention: Sam wants to have some drinks after work to help him relax.
moral_action: Sam purchases some drinks and invites his friends over to share them with.
moral_consequence: Sam's friends think he is generous for buying them the drinks.
immoral_action: Sam decides to pick up some alcohol and drink alone at his place.
immoral_consequence: Sam's friends find out what he's doing and think he is becoming an alcoholic.

norm: You should never scam anyone out of their money
situation: Bobby finds himself running out of money after losing his job with his rent coming due.
intention: Bobby wants to attain some money in order to pay his bills.
moral_action: Bobby sells his laptop on Craigslist and puts away the money in his bank account.
moral_consequence: Bobby is able to pay his rent with the proceeds from selling his laptop.
immoral_action: Bobby decides to sell items on craigslist and and as he is meeting somebody to sell his laptop he snatches the money and drives off.
immoral_consequence: The buyer reports Bobby's license plate to the police, and he is arrested.

norm: It's polite to flush after using the restroom.
situation: Randy is using the restroom at the gym and notices the flush handle appears to be quite dirty.
intention: Randy wants to avoid touching the handle.
moral_action: Randy uses his foot on the flush handle to press it down.
moral_consequence: The next person to use the bathroom has more a sanitary facility to use.
immoral_action: Randy leaves after using the restroom and does not flush it.
immoral_consequence: The person that uses the restroom after Randy is grossed out that someone didn't flush.

norm: It's good to show interest in other people's interests.
situation: Joe has a crush on his classmate, Lisa, and is about to approach her to strike up a converstation.
intention: Joe wants to ask Lisa out on a date.
moral_action: Joe asks Lisa about the things she likes to do before asking her out.
moral_consequence: Lisa agrees to go out with Joe because he seems to be interested in the same things she is.
immoral_action: Joe ignores what Lisa is doing and talks about himself, then asks her out.
immoral_consequence: Lisa turns him down because he seems self-centered and boring.

norm: You're encouraged to tell people the truth.
situation: Mindy is asking John at home who ate the last piece of cake that she wanted.
intention: John doesn't want Mindy to be upset that he ate the last piece of cake.
moral_action: John admits he ate it but tells Mindy he also bought her a brand new one as well.
moral_consequence: Mindy trusts John and is happy to have a whole new cake too.
immoral_action: John tells Mindy he thinks the kids ate it.
immoral_consequence: Mindy gets upset with the kids and later finds the truth and doesn't trust John anymore.

norm: You shouldn't skip out on your friend's birthday.
situation: John has had a friend since childhood and their birthday is today.
intention: John wants to have a good time.
moral_action: John plans an elaborate birthday evening for his friend.
moral_consequence: John's friend appreciates the efforts and has a very memorable birthday.
immoral_action: John receives a call from a new lady friend who wants him to come out to the bar which he does.
immoral_consequence: John's friend since childhood feels betrayed that John chose somebody else over them on their birthday.

norm: You shouldn't play music that could annoy others.
situation: Janine is riding the bus to work.
intention: Janine wants to listen to some music.
moral_action: Janine takes out her phone and listens to her favorite song with her earbuds.
moral_consequence: Janine is able to enjoy some tunes and the other passengers are undisturbed.
immoral_action: Janine pulls out her phone and listens to her favorite song through the speaker.
immoral_consequence: The other passengers are disturbed because they can hear and give Janine dirty looks.

norm: Showing off is frowned upon.
situation: Benny is at a local fair where a man named Ken is breathing fire and wowing the crowd.
intention: Benny wants to react to the fire breather.
moral_action: Benny says to the crowd that Ken is really impressive and that he's never seen anything like it.
moral_consequence: Ken is delighted that Benny appreciates his skill and art and that he's pumping up the crowd for him.
immoral_action: Benny says to the crowd that the fire breather isn't all that impressive, and he can do better, then proceeds to dance for them.
immoral_consequence: Ken is completely disgusted by Benny's attempts to steal the spotlight from himself.

norm: It's good to tell others how you feel about them.
situation: Bill really likes a girl in his class but isn't sure how she feels about him.
intention: Billy wants to decide whether or not confess his feelings for the girl.
moral_action: Billy decides to be brave and tell the girl that he feels strongly for her.
moral_consequence: As a consequence of Billy admitting his feelings he ends up in a relationship with the girl and is very happy.
immoral_action: Billy decides not to let the girl know about his feelings for her in case she doesn't feel the same way about him.
immoral_consequence: Billy always regrets not taking a chance and sharing his feelings for the girl and wonders what might have been if he did.

norm: It's good to see a movie with your kids.
situation: Jordan got some free tickets to the local theater and can't decide if he wants to take his friend Billy or take his kids.
intention: Jordan wants to have a good time out.
moral_action: Jordan prioritizes his kids and takes them to see a cartoon they've been wanting to see.
moral_consequence: Jordan's kids have a great time and are thankful to hang out with their dadddy.
immoral_action: Jordan takes Billy to see an action flick.
immoral_consequence: Jordan's kids are sad and disappointed they couldn't spend time with their Dad.

norm: You shouldn't expect people to wait for you.
situation: Jonny is late meeting up with his friends who are at the movie theater.
intention: Jonny wants to watch a new movie with friends.
moral_action: Jonny tells his friends to start the movie without him and save him a seat.
moral_consequence: Jonny's friends enjoy good seats and are able to save one for him as well.
immoral_action: Jonny tells his friends to wait even though he is significantly late.
immoral_consequence: Jonny's friends are disappointed that they miss the beginning of the movie.

norm: You should behave professionally at work.
situation: After a tense team meeting, Wally notices his coworkers standing by the coffee machine looking tense.
intention: Wally wants to create a positive atmosphere.
moral_action: Wally offers to buy everyone snacks from the vending machine after shaking everyone's hand.
moral_consequence: Wally is thanked by his friends for his actions.
immoral_action: Wally impersonates his boss in a loud tone as he grabs a cup of coffee.
immoral_consequence: Wally is written up for his strange behavior.

norm: You shouldn't skip work.
situation: It's Saturday morning, Ken is listening to his voicemail and hears a message from his boss asking him to report to work on Saturday.
intention: Ken wants to react to the voicemail.
moral_action: Ken deletes the voicemail and starts getting ready to go into work right away.
moral_consequence: Ken's boss is delighted when Ken arrives and apologizes for the short notice but tells Ken he'll get a bonus for this.
immoral_action: Ken hangs up the phone and doesn't delete the voicemail or mark it heard, so he can pretend he never got the message yet.
immoral_consequence: Ken's boss is livid with Ken the next week asking him why he never showed up on Saturday and threatening to fire him.

norm: It's good to share food with people.
situation: Timmy is really hungry and ordered an especially large lunch at school and notices his friend didn't get anything.
intention: Timmy wants to talk with his friend.
moral_action: Timmy sits down and offers part of his meal to his friend without food and asks him why he is without food.
moral_consequence: Timmy's friend explains the unfortunate reason he didn't have any food but feels grateful that Timmy shared with him.
immoral_action: Timmy starts a long conversation with his friend that has no food and eats his entire meal in front of his friend during the conversation.
immoral_consequence: Timmy's friend is saddened that Timmy didn't inquire as to why he didn't have any food and goes hungry.

norm: You shouldn't let people eat out of your garbage cans.
situation: Callie notices a homeless person digging a hamburger tossed out of her trashcan.
intention: Callie wants the homeless person to have food.
moral_action: Callie cooks dinner for herself and the homeless person.
moral_consequence: The homeless person talks Callie into hiring her for doing odd jobs for her in exchange for food.
immoral_action: Callie enters her apartment allowing the homeless person to continue digging through her trash.
immoral_consequence: The homeless person gets sick from the germs in Callie's trash can.

norm: It's wrong to keep matters of physical health from children.
situation: Betty is a mother of three who has just been diagnosed with an aggressive cancer.
intention: Betty wants to avoid making her children sad.
moral_action: Betty tells the kids right after her diagonsis and asks for their support.
moral_consequence: The kids are sad at the news but their support is enough to help Betty battle and survive the cancer.
immoral_action: Betty withholds the fact that she has cancer until just before her death.
immoral_consequence: The kids feel both shocked at the seemingly sudden death and resentful that she hid it from them.

norm: You should not let your pet get overweight.
situation: Amber has a dog named Twinkie who loves to beg for scraps.
intention: Amber wants Twinkie to be happy.
moral_action: Amber teaches Twinkie not to beg and only feeds her portioned meals with occasional treats.
moral_consequence: Twinkie stops begging and remains healthy enough to run around.
immoral_action: Amber gives Twinkie scraps every time she begs.
immoral_consequence: Twinkie begs more and more and becomes overweight.

norm: It's wrong to brag.
situation: Todd purchased a lottery ticket while getting gas and won a large sum of money.
intention: Todd wants to let others know of his good fortune.
moral_action: Todd is celebrating at a bar with his friends and decides to by drink for all of the bar crowd.
moral_consequence: The bar crowd congratulate him on his good luck and thank him for the free drinks.
immoral_action: Todd is at a bar with friends and is overheard by some of the bar crowd boasting about his large gambling winnings.
immoral_consequence: Some of the bar crowd follow Todd to his car after closing hours and robbed him at gunpoint.

norm: You shouldn't play favorites with your kids.
situation: Tara has two children and one of them is a lot less of a hassle than the other.
intention: Tara wants to buy presents for her kids.
moral_action: Tara makes sure to give both of her children gifts that they want because she cares for them both.
moral_consequence: Tara's children both grow up knowing their mother loves them and it increases their odds of being well adjusted.
immoral_action: Tara always buys nicer presents for the kid that gives her less trouble.
immoral_consequence: Tara's children recognize she has a favorite and it affects both of their attitudes negatively as they grow up.

norm: It's wrong to lie to the people you sleep with.
situation: Hannah met Bob last night, who is married, and drunkenly slept with him and the next morning she asks him if he's married.
intention: Bob wants to answer Hannah's question.
moral_action: Bob tells Hannah that he is indeed married and that he has been for a while.
moral_consequence: Hannah is glad to know that this was only a one time thing, and she doesn't have to get attached to Bob.
immoral_action: Bob tells Hannah that he is not married and that he actually never has been.
immoral_consequence: Hannah falsely believes that maybe there could be more to their relationship before she's later heartbroken when she finds out Bob is married.

norm: It's wrong to marry within your family.
situation: Iris is tired of being single and lonely while all of her friends are getting married.
intention: Iris wants to get married and have kids.
moral_action: Iris ventures out of her circle of friends and family and finds a nice man to marry.
moral_consequence: Iris's friends are happy for her and always include the couple in their plans.
immoral_action: Iris doesn't know any single men except her cousin, so she decides that they should get married.
immoral_consequence: Iris's friends think the marriage is creepy and don't want to hang out with the couple.

norm: It's wrong to betray the trust of family members.
situation: Tom is mowing the grass like he promised his mother he would do when his friend Dan asks him to go to a movie.
intention: Tom wants to go to the movie.
moral_action: Tom tells Dan he can see the movie with him tomorrow and finishes mowing the grass.
moral_consequence: Tom's mother his happy that he successfully mowed the lawn.
immoral_action: Tom abandons mowing the grass and goes with Dan.
immoral_consequence: Tom's mother is offended that Tom broke his promise to mow the grass.

norm: It's not okay to take advantage of tourists.
situation: Hector drives a taxi in Costa Rica and sees a foreign family come into the bus station.
intention: Hector wants to make some money off of the foreign family.
moral_action: Hector offers to drive the tourists and gives them a group rate.
moral_consequence: The tourists accept the group rate and thank Hector for his openness.
immoral_action: Hector offers to drive the tourists for a price, neglecting to tell them that the price is only per person and not for the group.
immoral_consequence: The tourists have to pay several times more than what they thought and are very angry at Hector.

norm: It's wrong to deceive people out of loneliness.
situation: Jake is lonely and hasn't had a girlfriend in over eight years.
intention: Jack wants to get a date off Tinder.
moral_action: Jack decides to use his real photo and wait, after which a woman decides to go on a date with him.
moral_consequence: Jack and his date enjoy getting to know each other's real selves and fall in love.
immoral_action: Jack decides to catfish and put a fake photo of a male model and gets a date quickly.
immoral_consequence: Jack's date is horrified at Jack's dishonesty and Jack continues feeling alone.

norm: You should always replace your friend's things that you ruined.
situation: Chelsea spills coffee all over a sweater that was borrowed from her friend Megan.
intention: Chelsea wants to bring Megan a sweater.
moral_action: Chelsea goes to the store to buy Megan a brand new sweater.
moral_consequence: Megan is impressed with Chelsea's honesty, and they continue to borrow each other's clothes.
immoral_action: Chelsea returns the stained sweater to Megan.
immoral_consequence: Megan loses her trust in Chelsea and stops lending her clothes.

norm: It is wrong to hit animals.
situation: Brittany's dog went to the bathroom on the living room carpet.
intention: Brittany wants to discipline her dog.
moral_action: Brittany rubs her dogs nose in the excrement and puts it outside.
moral_consequence: Brittany's dog understands that he should go to the bathroom outside and doesn't go inside again.
immoral_action: Brittany slaps her dog across the nose three or four times.
immoral_consequence: Brittany's dog becomes afraid of her and won't come to her when she calls.

norm: You shouldn't delete things on your friend's phone.
situation: Shawna has her friend Lacy's phone and is feeling mischievous.
intention: Shawna wants to play a prank on Lacy.
moral_action: Shawna takes pictures to put into Lacy's phone.
moral_consequence: Lacy will be amused because she can delete the pictures Shawna added.
immoral_action: Shawna erases pictures that she finds on Lacy's phone.
immoral_consequence: Lacy will become upset because the pictures will be lost forever.

norm: It's good to take a break from work sometimes.
situation: Felipe is working late at the office, trying to wrap up an important project, when he starts feeling very worn down and unmotivated.
intention: Felipe wants to feel more energized.
moral_action: Felipe decides to stretch his legs and grab a quick bite to eat at the restaurant next door before returning to finish the project.
moral_consequence: Felipe feels rejuvenated and motivated when he returns from his break and finishes the project quickly and efficiently.
immoral_action: Felipe grabs an energy drink out of the fridge and decides to power through the rest of the project immediately.
immoral_consequence: Felipe makes a bunch of errors and the quality of the project suffers.

norm: It is bad to cheat on someone in a relationship.
situation: William and his wife are going through a rough patch in their relationship and William is feeling unloved and underappreciated.
intention: William wants to be in a loving relationship.
moral_action: William talks to his wife about going to counseling to try to repair their relationship.
moral_consequence: William and his wife work through their problems and their marriage becomes stronger.
immoral_action: William begins an affair with a coworker that he has always gotten along well with.
immoral_consequence: William's wife finds out and begins a nasty divorce process.

norm: It's not okay to hurt others for your own enjoyment.
situation: Josh is spending the night at a party with friends having some drinks.
intention: Josh wants to entertain the others.
moral_action: Josh tells some dad jokes that he knows of.
moral_consequence: People are entertained by the silly but humorous jokes.
immoral_action: Josh makes jokes directed at a friend of his.
immoral_consequence: People laugh but Josh's friend takes the jokes too personally.

norm: It's good to let children express themselves.
situation: Bobby is standing on the train tracks at a carnival with his kids who keep talking while he's trying to hear a clown.
intention: Bobby wants his kids to be quiet, so he can hear.
moral_action: Bobby lets his kids talk as long as they promise to be quiet after.
moral_consequence: They warn him to step off the train tracks - Bobby does so and the kids are quiet for the rest of the day.
immoral_action: Bobby yells at his kids to be quiet no matter what it is.
immoral_consequence: The kids are quiet until Bobby is run over by a passing train.

norm: It's wrong to steal from others.
situation: Billy is eating cookies with Suzy, and Billy has finished eating the last cookie on his plate.
intention: Billy wants to continue eating cookies.
moral_action: Billy asks Suzy if there's more cookies in the kitchen.
moral_consequence: Suzy and Billy's relationship remains intact.
immoral_action: Billy eats the cookies off of Suzy's plate.
immoral_consequence: Suzy doesn't get to have her share of the cookies.

norm: It's worrying to have nothing in your fridge.
situation: Once again Phil's fridge has nothing in it, just cold air.
intention: Phil wants to get some food.
moral_action: Phil goes to the grocery store and gets enough food to fill the fridge.
moral_consequence: Now Phil's fridge is filled with nice food to eat.
immoral_action: Phil orders some take out since there's nothing in the cold box.
immoral_consequence: The next day the fridge is still empty, and this happens again.

norm: You shouldn't drink and drive with kids in the car.
situation: Samantha is having some wine with a friend and feeling tipsy, and her daughter Helena is getting out of school soon.
intention: Samantha wants Helena to get picked up.
moral_action: Samantha decides to ride a cab to pick up Helena from school.
moral_consequence: Samantha and Helena are able to remain safe and Helena is pleased she made a sound decision.
immoral_action: Samantha decides to get in the car and picks up Helena from the school.
immoral_consequence: Samantha gets into a car accident because she was inebriated, and he and Helena end up in the hospital.

norm: It's rude to skip in line.
situation: It's lunchtime and Kelly is near a popular cafe but she's running late for class too.
intention: Kelly wants to grab lunch and get to class.
moral_action: Kelly places an online order with the cafe through her phone, so she doesn't have to wait in line.
moral_consequence: Kelly gets her food quickly and makes it to her class on time.
immoral_action: Kelly goes straight to the front of the ordering line because she wants to get her food as quickly as possible.
immoral_consequence: Kelly is called out by the other patrons for being rude and shamed into leaving the cafe.

norm: You should help other people besides your son.
situation: Kevin has a son that is on a little league team and Kevin is a coach on the team.
intention: Kevin wants to give hitting tips.
moral_action: Kevin gives hitting tips to all the players on the team.
moral_consequence: The other kids will think that Kevin is a good coach.
immoral_action: Kevin gives hitting tips only to his son.
immoral_consequence: The other kids on the team will become jealous of Kevin's son.

norm: It's rude to cheat when playing a game.
situation: Billy sets up a game night with friends.
intention: Billy wants to win at scrabble.
moral_action: Billy studies a dictionary before playing scrabble and wins.
moral_consequence: Billy's friends have fun and are amazed as his knowledge.
immoral_action: Billy has hidden extra letters up his sleeve during scrabble and wins.
immoral_consequence: Billy's friends notice the extra letters after and tell Billy they won't play games with him anymore.

norm: It's rude to call someone when they're sleeping.
situation: James was watching cartoons at 2 AM and heard a really funny joke.
intention: James wants to share the joke with his best friend.
moral_action: James waits until the next day at school to tell his friend the joke.
moral_consequence: James' friend laughs and tells James that's the funniest thing he's heard all year.
immoral_action: James calls his friend at 2 AM to recite the joke.
immoral_consequence: James' friend swears at him and throws the phone across the room.

norm: It's rude to not accept a gift from someone.
situation: Sasha is celebrating her birthday and somebody brought her a gift she didn't ask for.
intention: Sasha wants to enjoy her birthday.
moral_action: Sasha appreciates the thought that went into the gift and thanks the guest for it.
moral_consequence: The guest feels good about themselves and enjoys the party.
immoral_action: Since Sasha didn't ask for the gift she tells the person to just keep it.
immoral_consequence: The guest is offended that Sasha didn't accept the gift and leaves the party.

norm: It is kind to make food for your wife.
situation: Jorah and Maryanne are sitting at home, and both are fairly hungry, but Maryanne isn't feeling up to cooking.
intention: Jorah wants to get some food for Maryanne.
moral_action: Jorah goes into the kitchen and cooks him and Maryanne a pasta dinner.
moral_consequence: Jorah and Maryanne enjoy the meal together, and Maryanne really appreciates it.
immoral_action: Jorah orders some food from grubhub and has to tip the driver.
immoral_consequence: Jorah pays a lot more for food than if he made it himself, Maryanne is a bit annoyed.

norm: It is bad to throw out unfounded accusations
situation: Doug thinks his girlfriend Denise has been acting a bit differently lately and spending a lot of time at work.
intention: Doug wants to figure out what is going on with Denise.
moral_action: Doug asks Denise if everything is okay at work and if she needs anything from him.
moral_consequence: Denise appreciates Doug's concern and lets him know about what she has been dealing with.
immoral_action: Doug confronts Denise and accuses her of having an affair with her coworker.
immoral_consequence: Denise is upset that Doug does not trust her and asks for some space between them for a while.

norm: It is good to not give up.
situation: Terry failed a class in college which is disheartening to him.
intention: Terry wants to consider what to do next.
moral_action: Terry continues taking classes and studies more.
moral_consequence: Terry gets a degree.
immoral_action: Terry drops out of college.
immoral_consequence: Terry does not get a degree.

norm: It is good to care for people you like.
situation: James is relaxing at home when his wife Mary runs in with a bleeding finger from cutting herself while making dinner.
intention: James wants to help Mary.
moral_action: James tells Mary to hang on and runs to go get some band aids and gauze from the bathroom cabinet.
moral_consequence: Mary is relieved that James is going to tend to her injury and calms down a little.
immoral_action: James tells Mary that the band aids are in the bathroom cabinet, and she should go get one.
immoral_consequence: Mary is annoyed that James is only telling her where to look instead of helping.

norm: It's fun to play video games to relax and unwind.
situation: Kimmy just finished a long day of work and is at home playing video games.
intention: Kimmy wants to have fun.
moral_action: Kimmy chooses a relaxing game to play and just mellows out and enjoys the game.
moral_consequence: Kimmy feels relieved and rested from the video game after her long day of work.
immoral_action: Kimmy gets really into the video game she is playing and gets worked up and competitive about how well she does.
immoral_consequence: Kimmy gets stressed out from the game considering she already had a busy day beforehand.

norm: It is rude to expose others to illness.
situation: Fran had been feeling sick and felt like she was going to throw up.
intention: Fran needed some medicine for her stomach.
moral_action: Fran asks her husband to run to the store for her to pick up her medicine.
moral_consequence: Fran keeps her germs to herself and doesn't spread it to anyone outside of her house.
immoral_action: Fran goes to the store herself to pick up the medicine that she needs.
immoral_consequence: Fran spreads her germs to other people she gets in contact with at the store.

norm: It's wrong to trick one's friends.
situation: Brad and Andy are hanging out with a bunch of strangers at a party.
intention: Brad wants to entertain the new people.
moral_action: Brad tells everyone silly jokes.
moral_consequence: Brad gains new friends.
immoral_action: Brad plays a silly prank on Andy to make people laugh.
immoral_consequence: Brad is lectured by Andy's girlfriend when she finds out about the event.

norm: It's rude to pick your teeth at the table.
situation: John is eating with his family at a local barbecue restaurant when he feels corn stuck between his teeth.
intention: John wants to remove the food from his teeth.
moral_action: John excuses himself to the restroom where he uses a toothpick to remove the food from between his teeth.
moral_consequence: John is relieved and enjoys the rest of the evening at the restaurant.
immoral_action: John uses his finger to pick at the corn between his teeth until he dislodges it.
immoral_consequence: John feels embarrassed after receiving disapproving glares from his family and other diners for his rude table manners.

norm: You should call people by their correct or preferred name.
situation: Debbie's coworker has recently come out as trans and has asked to be called by a name that matches their true gender.
intention: Debbie wants to call her coworker.
moral_action: Debbie calls her coworker and uses their correct new name.
moral_consequence: Debbie's coworker feels respected and validated by the use of their correct name.
immoral_action: Debbie calls her coworker but uses their dead name instead of their new correct name.
immoral_consequence: Debbie's coworker feels disrespected and invalidated by the use of their dead name.

norm: It is immoral to rob someone
situation: Sean sees that a kid has a new pair of shoes that he likes a lot.
intention: Sean wants the shoes.
moral_action: Sean asks the kid where he bought the pair of shoes.
moral_consequence: Sean will be able to go to the store to buy the shoes.
immoral_action: Sean tells the kid to give him the shoes, or he will be hurt.
immoral_consequence: Sean will be accused of robbery and wanted by the law.

norm: It's good to want to share you feelings.
situation: Tory just lost a big basketball game and comes home to her dad named Dan.
intention: Tory wants to explain her sports loss to Dan.
moral_action: Tory lets her Dad know about the loss and lets her Dad know she is very upset.
moral_consequence: Tory and her Dad hug and decide to plan something special to make her feel better.
immoral_action: Tory describes the basketball game loss but does not share how upset she is.
immoral_consequence: Tory and Dan aren't able to connect emotionally and the conversation abruptly ends.

norm: It's always good to be honest with your friends.
situation: Maddie's friend Jonas is dating a woman who is cheating on him.
intention: Maddie wants Jonas to know about it.
moral_action: Maddie tells Jonas that the woman is actively cheating on him.
moral_consequence: Jonas breaks off the relationship and starts seeing another, more faithful woman.
immoral_action: Maddie tells Jonas that she heard about the cheating but doesn't believe it's true.
immoral_consequence: Jonas continues to date the woman, who eventually leaves him for the man she was cheating on him with.

norm: It's bad to wish your ex would overdose.
situation: Tom recently ended his relationship with Kerry after finding out about her drug use, but she's been calling him wanting to get back together.
intention: Tom wants Kerry to stop calling.
moral_action: Tom tells Kerry their time is over and changes his number.
moral_consequence: Kerry is unable to call Tom, and they both move on with their lives.
immoral_action: Tom tells Kerry to pop a bunch of pills and forget his number.
immoral_consequence: Tom's statement sends Kerry into such a spiral that she does just that and ends up in the hospital.

norm: You should be grateful for the gifts you receive
situation: On his birthday Juan receives a gift card to a store he considers low quality from his secretary.
intention: Juan wants to acknowledge the gift.
moral_action: Juan thanks his secretary for thinking of him on his bithday.
moral_consequence: Juan is able to show his coworkers he can be gracious.
immoral_action: Juan tells his secretary the store is too low brow for him and asks her if she can return the gift card.
immoral_consequence: Juan gains a reputation for being a snob around the office.

norm: You shouldn't fight with your mother.
situation: Andrea and her mother were discussing what to watch on television.
intention: Andrea wants to watch cartoons.
moral_action: Andrea asks her mother if she can watch cartoons after she does her homework.
moral_consequence: Andrea's mother finishes watching her television show and then gives Andrea the remote control.
immoral_action: Andrea yells at her mother until she changes the channel to her cartoons.
immoral_consequence: Andrea's mother puts her in a juvenile boot camp for her behavior problems.

norm: It's rude to neglect your romantic partner.
situation: John and Mindy are at home and Mindy gets a call that her dad died and starts crying.
intention: John wants to watch the game tonight.
moral_action: John puts the tv on record and comforts Mindy for a bit before resuming the game.
moral_consequence: Mindy feels closer to John and loves him more than before.
immoral_action: John puts the volume on the tv louder to drown out Mindy's cries.
immoral_consequence: Mindy feels resentful towards John and considers leaving the relationship.

norm: It is rude to downplay someone's hopes.
situation: Amy has a friend who has called her up to ask for some advice about her dream of becoming a singer.
intention: Amy wants to point her friend in the right direction.
moral_action: Amy tells her friend hard work and persistence are important but also tells her to have a back up plan.
moral_consequence: Amy's friend is grateful for the support and advice.
immoral_action: Amy scoffs at idea, says it will never happen, and tells her friend to be more realistic.
immoral_consequence: Amy's friend feels upset and discouraged by the feedback.

norm: It's fun to go on a vacation with your partner.
situation: John is a homebody and his wife likes to go out a lot and is ready to travel.
intention: John wants to improve his relationship with his wife.
moral_action: John asks his wife where she'd like to go and packs his bags and challenges his limitations.
moral_consequence: John's wife is very happy and feels closer to John and their marriage improves.
immoral_action: John refuses to leave the house but instead reads therapy books with his wife all day in the house.
immoral_consequence: John's wife becomes restless and resents John not going anywhere with her.

norm: It's encouraged for authority figures to use their power wisely.
situation: Jim is the CEO of a company and has to make a choice on who to promote.
