intention: Jim wants to promote an employee.
moral_action: Jim promotes strictly based on performance.
moral_consequence: Jim's company gains a motivated high performance employee.
immoral_action: Jim plays favorites and promotes his friend.
immoral_consequence: The other candidates become demotivated and eventually leaves the company.

norm: You shouldn't intrude on people.
situation: Helen lives in a shared apartment with a roommate who is currently in their bedroom with the door closed.
intention: Helen has a question she wants to ask her roommate.
moral_action: Helen sends her question to her roommate in a text message.
moral_consequence: Helen's roommate has time to put on clothes before leaving her room to tell Helen the answer to her question.
immoral_action: Helen opens her roommates door without knocking to ask her question.
immoral_consequence: Helen's roommate is naked and screams when she hears the door open.

norm: You should be nice to your neighbors.
situation: Randy is outside and sees his neighbors having a party in their back yard.
intention: Randy wants to get his lawn cut.
moral_action: Randy waits until the next day to cut his grass and doesn't disturb the party.
moral_consequence: Randy gets invited over to the party and has a drink with his neighbors.
immoral_action: Randy cuts his grass while the party is going on and is loud and annoying to his neighbors.
immoral_consequence: Randy's neighbors are upset that he choose this time to do it and don't like him as much anymore.

norm: You shouldn't scream in public.
situation: Tim sees his friend across a busy street with many people around.
intention: Tim wants to get his friend's attention.
moral_action: Tim waves his arm until his friend notices the movement and recognizes Tim.
moral_consequence: The people on the street aren't bothered by Tim, most don't even notice him.
immoral_action: Tim yells loudly so that his friend notices him across the street.
immoral_consequence: The people on the street are annoyed by Tim's loud yelling.

norm: You should never steal someone else's possessions.
situation: Heath is playing with his friend Tom.
intention: He sees a toy he likes and wants to take it home.
moral_action: Heath asks Tom if he can borrow the toy for a few days.
moral_consequence: Tom gladly lends the toy to Heath and their friendship remains strong.
immoral_action: Heath puts the toy in his pocket without telling Tom.
immoral_consequence: Tom finds out that Heath stole his toy, so Tom doesn't want to be his friend anymore.

norm: It is rude to make unwanted advances on others
situation: A pretty woman at the bar tells John she isn't interested in dancing with him.
intention: John wants to respond to the woman.
moral_action: John tells the woman he is sorry to bother her and goes on with his evening.
moral_consequence: John enjoys drinking and socializing at the bar.
immoral_action: John grabs the woman by the arm to drag her to the dance floor.
immoral_consequence: John is thrown out of the bar by the bouncer.

norm: It's not okay to think of yourself as dumb.
situation: James and his wife Linda are putting together a backyard furniture set and James hits his thumb with a hammer.
intention: James wants to react to the accident he just had.
moral_action: James yelps in pain then says that he's gotta be more careful and goes to get ice.
moral_consequence: Linda chuckles to herself but is glad to see James went to take care of the injury right away.
immoral_action: James yelps in pain then goes on muttering about how stupid he is and how he always does this.
immoral_consequence: Linda doesn't like how James thinks of himself, and she's starting to lose faith in him because of his low confidence.

norm: It's good to offer to tutor people.
situation: Trent is listening to his friend Jake complain about his difficult math class.
intention: Trent wants Jake to get some help.
moral_action: Trent offers to help Jake understand the topic.
moral_consequence: Jake understands Trent's explanation and does well in class.
immoral_action: Trent directs Jake to a math tutoring website.
immoral_consequence: Jake gets some help, but has trouble understanding the website and still needs more.

norm: It is wrong to treat any animal poorly.
situation: Kal buys a puppy and when he gets it home it won't stop barking.
intention: Kal wants not to hear the dog barking any more.
moral_action: Kal looks up ways to train a puppy online and uses the information to teach the dog not to bark.
moral_consequence: Kal has a fun time playing with his new puppy.
immoral_action: Kal puts tape around the dog's mouth and ties it to a tree in the furtherest part of his yard.
immoral_consequence: Kal is arrested for animal cruelty when a neighbor sees his actions and calls the cops.

norm: It is wrong to harm children
situation: Travis is having pizza with his nephew Brutus and notices Brutus reaching for the last piece.
intention: Travis wants more food.
moral_action: Travis asks Brutus if he minds splitting the pizza and cuts it in half with a knife.
moral_consequence: Brutus learns that it's good to share and act respectfully.
immoral_action: Travis lunges for the slice knocking Brutus off his chair in the process.
immoral_consequence: Brutus hits his head as he falls and needs to get stitches.

norm: It's good to take what someone says seriously.
situation: Andrew is talking with his friend Brian when Brian says he's had thoughts of hurting himself.
intention: Andrew wants to make Brian feel better.
moral_action: Andrew asks Brian if he has talked to a counselor or therapist about this, and offers to go with him to therapy if he wants that.
moral_consequence: Brian feels cared for and gets the help he needs.
immoral_action: Andrew laughs and says that Brian should just not do that.
immoral_consequence: Brian no longer feels comfortable opening up to Andrew.

norm: You should keep your house clean
situation: Tina's boyfriend Frank is knocking on her door, so they can cook dinner together as planned.
intention: Tina wants to invite Frank inside.
moral_action: Tina tells Frabk to come inside, and he sees what an immaculate place she keeps.
moral_consequence: Frank is impressed with Tina's home and looks forward to cooking.
immoral_action: Tina tells Frank to come in, and when he does, he sees what a mess it is.
immoral_consequence: Frank quickly loses his appetite and decides to leave.

norm: You shouldn't ditch people.
situation: Fred was driving to work, and he was supposed to pick pup Susan on the way there.
intention: Fred wants to arrive at work.
moral_action: Fred stops to pick up Susan like he's supposed to on the way to work.
moral_consequence: Susan thanks Fred for arriving on time and with his car clean.
immoral_action: Fred decides to go right to work and leave Susan there.
immoral_consequence: Fred gets an angry call from Susan about not picking her up for work.

norm: You should not expect something for helping someone.
situation: Kyle has spent the day helping his friend move to a new house.
intention: Kyle wants to make some extra money.
moral_action: Kyle helps for free not expecting payment and schedules some extra work shifts.
moral_consequence: Kyle's friend gives pays him and remembers to owe him a favor.
immoral_action: Kyle asks how much his friend will give him for the labor.
immoral_consequence: Kyle's friend is offended because they never mentioned payment.

norm: It's polite to be considerate of others in a conversation.
situation: Sam is talking to Taylor about what he did that day and what he's planning on doing later.
intention: Sam wants to tell Taylor about where he's going for dinner.
moral_action: Sam tells Taylor about the restaurant he's going to and asks if she's ever been.
moral_consequence: Taylor says that she has and tells him about a special dish the restaurant serves that's not listed on the menu.
immoral_action: Sam tells Taylor about the restaurant he's going to for dinner, talking over her every time she tries to interject something.
immoral_consequence: Taylor doesn't feel like she's part of the conversation and begins scrolling through her social media accounts on her phone.

norm: It is mean to taunt your sibling
situation: Brad and his sister Lucy are playing in the backyard when she falls and bangs her knee.
intention: Brad wants to react to Lucy's fall.
moral_action: Brad kneels down beside Lucy and tells her she's going to be okay before helping her up.
moral_consequence: Lucy feels comforted and appreciates her brother's care and support.
immoral_action: Brad points at his sister on the ground and begins laughing at her.
immoral_consequence: Lucy feels pain and embarrassment and calls for her mother.

norm: It's frowned upon to discuss the value of gifts.
situation: Susan receives a high tech and fancy looking bread maker as a wedding gift from her friend Samantha.
intention: Susan wants to find out more about the gift.
moral_action: Susan asks Samantha where she got the gift.
moral_consequence: Samantha is happy to tell her more about the bread maker and how she found it at Bed Bath and Beyond.
immoral_action: Susan asks Samantha how much the gift cost.
immoral_consequence: Samantha is mildly irritated and finds it inappropriate for Susan to inquire about the gift's cost.

norm: It is nice to be helpful to elders
situation: Jim arrives at a crosswalk and sees that an elderly person is having a difficult time crossing the street.
intention: Jim wants to cross the street.
moral_action: Jim holds the elderly person's hand and helps them get across the the street with him.
moral_consequence: The elderly person is relieved to get some help crossing the street.
immoral_action: Jim crosses the street passing the elderly person who is having difficulties doing so.
immoral_consequence: The elderly person has a hard time crossing and becomes anxious as cars wait for them to cross.

norm: It is good to get your work done.
situation: Jim has work left to do that his boss wanted done that day even though it's already the time he usually goes home.
intention: Jim wants to go home.
moral_action: Jim stays at work an extra hour and finishes all his work before going home.
moral_consequence: Jim is commended by his boss for staying late and getting all his work done.
immoral_action: Jim goes straight home leaving his work unfinished because he feels tired already.
immoral_consequence: Jim is reprimanded by his boss the next day for not finishing his work on time.

norm: It's wrong for parents not to support their children.
situation: Dee is a teacher who lives with her son Frank, who dreams of being a musician.
intention: Dee wants to feel better about herself.
moral_action: Dee tells Frank he can do anything he puts his mind to, and she supports him.
moral_consequence: Frank feels closer to Dee and loves her more.
immoral_action: Dee tells Frank to forget his dreams and do something practical, like become a teacher.
immoral_consequence: Frank doesn't feel supported and resents Dee.

norm: It's expected that most police officers will be good people.
situation: Maurice is a cop who is investigating a shooting that resulted in woman named Shauna getting severely injured.
intention: Maurice wants to make an arrest.
moral_action: Maurice thoroughly investigates the case and is able to track down the shooter and make an arrest.
moral_consequence: Maurice is proud of himself for taking a violent man off the streets.
immoral_action: Maurice can't find the shooter, so he plants a gun on an innocent man and arrests him for the crime.
immoral_consequence: Maurice now has to live with the guilt of wrongfully ruining a man's life.

norm: It's rude to expose non-smokers to secondhand smoke.
situation: Janice is a smoker who has four young children living with her.
intention: Janice wants to have a cigarette.
moral_action: Janice goes outside to smoke, making sure her kids are in the house when she does so.
moral_consequence: Janice's children are never exposed to the cigarette smoke and grow up without respiratory issues.
immoral_action: Janice smokes in the living room while her kids are watching TV.
immoral_consequence: Janice's kids inhale the smoke and grow up to have asthma and other respiratory issues.

norm: You shouldn't buy tacky gifts for people.
situation: It's fathers day and Kelly is shopping to buy her dad a present.
intention: Kelly wants to get her dad something interesting.
moral_action: Kelly buys her dad a functional dress shirt.
moral_consequence: Kelly's dad is pleased because he wears the shirt on a weekly basis for work.
immoral_action: Kelly buys her father a tie with loud pink and green colors.
immoral_consequence: Kelly's dad is disappointed with the gift and never ends up wearing it.

norm: It's not okay to hurt other people's animals.
situation: Frank has a neighbor whose dog uses the bathroom on his lawn.
intention: Frank wants to make the dog go away.
moral_action: Frank shoos the dog away with a strong tone and hand motions.
moral_consequence: The neighbor sees what is happening and tries to keep his dog from doing it again.
immoral_action: Frank takes the dog and physically removes him from his yard using force roughly.
immoral_consequence: The neighbor witnesses frank being rough with his dog and gets into an altercation with him.

norm: It's bad to be a buzzkill on vacation.
situation: Randy gets a text message with bad news about a sick family member while on vacation with friends.
intention: Randy wants to confide in someone about the bad news.
moral_action: Randy does his best to put the bad news out of his mind while he's on vacation and waits to talk to someone about it later.
moral_consequence: Randy's friends have a good time on vacation.
immoral_action: Randy brings up the bad news to his friends who are having fun on vacation.
immoral_consequence: Randy's friends feel sad upon hearing the news and aren't sure what to say making the trip awkward.

norm: You shouldn't ruin the fun of other people.
situation: Milton is studying at a coffee shop when a loud group of people sit beside him.
intention: Milton wants to focus on his book.
moral_action: Milton puts in headphones and listens to relaxing music.
moral_consequence: The music gets him in the right mindset, and he retains more information.
immoral_action: Milton asks the group to leave because they're distracting him.
immoral_consequence: Milton's request is overheard by an employee who scolds him in front of everyone.

norm: It is good to cook dinner for yourself.
situation: Austin is living on his own for the first time and is getting in the swing of things.
intention: Austin wants to have something to eat.
moral_action: Austin makes himself a nice evening meal from scratch and eats it.
moral_consequence: Austin benefits from the healthier and cheaper option of cooking dinner for himself.
immoral_action: Austin orders out for dinner because he has never cooked for himself before and this quickly becomes a regular habit of his.
immoral_consequence: Austin loses a lot of money buying overpriced prepared meals and his health also suffers.

norm: It is misleading to lie about your gender.
situation: Bob is a old, single man who likes to hang out in chat rooms online to kill time.
intention: Bob wants to meet young men.
moral_action: Bob tells people in the chat room his true age and gender while trying to meet them.
moral_consequence: Bob ends up meeting people from the chat rooms who actually appreciate him as he truly is.
immoral_action: Bob pretends to be an 18-year old woman from California while trying to arrange meetings with people online.
immoral_consequence: Bob ends up meeting with several people from the chat rooms, who are unpleasantly surprised by Bob's actual identity.

norm: It's not okay to be obsessed with someone's race.
situation: Megan is a big fan of Japanese media, and Haru a Japanese exchange student sits her.
intention: Megan wants to become friends with Haru.
moral_action: Megan offers Haru some of her cookies and shows him around the school.
moral_consequence: Haru learns to trust Megan.
immoral_action: Megan begins asking Haru questions based on stereotypes in Japanese media and stresses amazing Japanese people look.
immoral_consequence: Haru feels uncomfortable around Megan.

norm: It’s wrong to feel like you cheated.
situation: Louise is playing a card game with her brother.
intention: Louise wants to win.
moral_action: Louise plays the game fairly and wins the game.
moral_consequence: Louise feels happy that she was able to beat her brother.
immoral_action: Louise hides some of her cards under the table while her brother isn't looking and wins the game.
immoral_consequence: Louise feels bad because she knows she didn't win fairly.

norm: It is bad to have too many pets.
situation: Tyler's finances are not in a good spot as an owner of two dogs, and he recently came across a third dog up for adoption.
intention: Tyler wants to address the third dog.
moral_action: Tyler resists taking in the third dog and simply moves on.
moral_consequence: Tyler proceeds to live within his means while working to improve his finances.
immoral_action: Tyler decides to just take in the third dog regardless of his financial situation.
immoral_consequence: Tyler fails to make ends meet financially and experiences the stressful problems that comes with it.

norm: It is unacceptable to bring a weapon to school.
situation: Stan, whose parents have a gun at home, gets threatened by a bully at school and is afraid for his safety.
intention: Stan wants to get some protection.
moral_action: Stan finds some friends to hang around with, so he's never alone at school.
moral_consequence: The bully never gets an opportunity to corner Stan and leaves him alone.
immoral_action: Stan takes his parents' gun and brings it to school in his backpack.
immoral_consequence: Security finds the gun and arrests Stan on suspicion of planning a school shooting.

norm: It's rude to judge other's diets.
situation: Jeff is perusing the aisles of the local grocery store on his weekly shopping trip.
intention: Jeff wants to see what other shoppers are buying to see if he might like it.
moral_action: Jeff asks a person with a lot of organic fruits and vegetables in their cart about the benefits of eating organic.
moral_consequence: Jeff learns a good deal about healthy food and clean eating from the wise shopper.
immoral_action: Jeff tells a woman with a cart full of chips, soda and frozen pizza that all that food will make her fat.
immoral_consequence: Jeff is seen as a mean bully by all the shoppers who overhear his hurtful comment.

norm: It's bad to be too busy for your family.
situation: Fred has a heavy work load and his kids ask him to watch a movie with them.
intention: Fred wants to respond to his kids.
moral_action: Fred tells his kids he can watch a movie with them.
moral_consequence: Fred's kids will enjoy a movie with their father.
immoral_action: Fred tells his kids that he has too much work, and they can watch a movie another time.
immoral_consequence: Fred's kills will be disappointed.

norm: You should not starve yourself.
situation: Donna was looking in the mirror and started to think that she was fat.
intention: Donna wanted to lose weight.
moral_action: Donna starts to eat more fruit and vegetables for her snacks.
moral_consequence: Donna loses ten pounds the first month on her diet.
immoral_action: Donna starts to skip meals and only drinks water all day.
immoral_consequence: Donna starts to suffer from malnutrition and has to be hospitalized.

norm: It's rude to sell shoddy products to people.
situation: Chris wants to sell a universal TV remote that only works with half the TVs it says it does.
intention: Chris wants to sell the remote.
moral_action: Chris decides to disassemble the remote and try to find the issue.
moral_consequence: "Chris is able to fix the remote and lists it as ""seller refurbished""."
immoral_action: Chris puts the remote for sale but leaves all the problems with it out.
immoral_consequence: By chance the buyer has one of the TVs it works with, so they don't notice.

norm: You should always pay back your friends.
situation: Lisa is out shopping with friends but has run out of money.
intention: Lisa wants a shirt that is on sale.
moral_action: Lisa asks her friend for a loan and pays her back that friday when she is paid.
moral_consequence: Lisa's friend appreciates her honesty and Lisa enjoys her new shirt guilt free.
immoral_action: Lisa asks her friend for a loan but stops taking her calls after to avoid paying the loan back.
immoral_consequence: Lisa is kicked out of her friend group for being a con.

norm: It's good to have guests over and enjoy good company.
situation: Olivia sinks down onto her couch worn out after a long day of work, and she craves companionship.
intention: Olivia wants to do something relaxing.
moral_action: Olivia invites her close friends over for some tea and bread.
moral_consequence: Olivia learns how to make a tea that gives her energy from her friends.
immoral_action: Olivia lays down in bed reading chapters of her favorite book before taking a nap.
immoral_consequence: Olivia feels lonely.

norm: You shouldn't make fun of someone's tastes.
situation: Larry is listening to music that Tim thought he would like, through earphones.
intention: Larry wants to tell Tim that he doesn't like his music.
moral_action: Larry tells Tim he does not like the music, but respects his taste.
moral_consequence: Larry and Tim move onto other music to explore together.
immoral_action: Larry calls the band Tim is listening to a swear word, and proceeds to make fun of it.
immoral_consequence: Larry find Tim very upset at him and refuses to talk to him.

norm: You shouldn't be gluttonous.
situation: Len takes his date to the Chinese buffet for dinner.
intention: Len wants to experience as many different dishes as possible.
moral_action: Len takes a couple of small bites of many different dishes from the buffet.
moral_consequence: Len and his date have a nice meal discussing all the different flavors they have enjoyed that night.
immoral_action: Len heaps large amounts of every dish on the buffet on multiple plates and makes many trips back to get more food.
immoral_consequence: Len is thought of poorly by his date for his overeating, and she doesn't go out with him again.

norm: It's good to support your community parks.
situation: Vivian wins the lottery, and the park beside her house is having a charity drive.
intention: Vivian wants to spend money.
moral_action: Vivian gives the money to the park's charity drive.
moral_consequence: Vivian's name is written in the donations statue in the center of the park.
immoral_action: Vivian spends her money luxury items.
immoral_consequence: Vivian does not have room in her apartment for all of her new stuff.

norm: You shouldn't try to run over people.
situation: James is driving when Keith who was riding a bike cuts him off.
intention: James wants to react angrily to Keith's cut off.
moral_action: James speeds up his car to catch up to Keith and then flips him the finger before driving off.
moral_consequence: James feels satisfaction from his gesture and is satisfied that he got his anger out of his system.
immoral_action: James speeds up his car and slams into the back of Keith's' bike knocking him down and running him over.
immoral_consequence: Keith is hunted down by police and eventually caught and charged with attempted murder.

norm: It is usually wrong to lie about your identity.
situation: Simon receives a message from Anna on Facebook confusing him with someone with a similar name.
intention: Simon wants to get to know Anna.
moral_action: Simon posts a link to the guy Anna wants  while asking her questions about the interests on her profile.
moral_consequence: Anna asks Simon to hang out with her next weekend.
immoral_action: Simon pretends to be the guy as he talks to Anna through the night.
immoral_consequence: Simon is blocked by the Anna once she discovers the truth.

norm: It's good to be supportive of others during arguments.
situation: Chris was having a political argument with Jen.
intention: Chris wanted to end the argument.
moral_action: Chris acknowledges that Jen has made a lot of good points.
moral_consequence: Jen is feeling less argumentative and feels good that Chris understands her point of view.
immoral_action: Chris tells Jen that she should read more if she wants to continue the argument.
immoral_consequence: Jen feels disrespected and feels that Chris is a jerk.

norm: It's bad to think mass killers are good.
situation: Jed thoroughly researched a recent mass shooter at LSU on Reddit.
intention: Jed wants people to learn more about mass killers.
moral_action: Jed lists the warning signs that the mass shooter showed in a Reddit post.
moral_consequence: Jed makes someone aware of the warning signs that another potential shooter was showing.
immoral_action: Jed creates a subreddit in order to honor the LSU mass shooter.
immoral_consequence: Jed's subreddit inspires future mass shoooters.

norm: You shouldn't be a controlling significant other.
situation: Matthew's wife, Michelle, often attracts the attention of men.
intention: Matthew wants to prevent Michelle from leaving him for someone else.
moral_action: Matthew talks to Michelle about his concerns.
moral_consequence: Michelle assures Matthew that she has no interest for anyone else.
immoral_action: Matthew forbids Michelle from leaving the house without him.
immoral_consequence: Michelle divorces Matthew in order to salvage her freedom.

norm: You shouldn't estrange yourself from your family.
situation: Justin's family life has been difficult because of how controlling his parents are, although he gets along well with his siblings.
intention: Justin wants his parents to stop meddling in his life.
moral_action: Justin tells his parents he will stop seeing them if they don't mind their own business and keeps hanging out with his siblings.
moral_consequence: Justin's siblings enjoy his company and are happy to still be a part of his life.
immoral_action: Justin decides to completely break off contacts with his family.
immoral_consequence: Justin's siblings miss him and feel he abandoned them.

norm: You shouldn't try to play with other peoples' heads.
situation: Mindy goes to see her friend Homer and his family.
intention: Mindy wants to see them all.
moral_action: Homer introduces his family and Mindy says hello to each of them in turn.
moral_consequence: Homer's family are happy to meet his friend Mindy as she was nice to them.
immoral_action: Homer introduces his family and Mindy pets them all on the head as they are introduced.
immoral_consequence: Homer's family get irritated at how Mindy plays with their heads.

norm: It's good to teach your kids new skills.
situation: "Fred is driving with his wife and child when he hears a ""pop"", then realizes that his tire has gone flat."
intention: Fred wants to change his car tire.
moral_action: Fred brings his child out with him and has him help change the tire.
moral_consequence: Fred's child learns to change a tire and is ready for the next time it happens.
immoral_action: Fred tells the wife and child to stay in the car and changes the tire himself.
immoral_consequence: When Fred's child has a flat tire, he has no idea what to do and needs to call for help.

norm: Listening while someone speaks is respectful
situation: Jessica is in the living room while her mother is talking to her.
intention: Jessica wants to watch her favorite television show which is playing.
moral_action: Jessica pauses the show on the television while her mother speaks.
moral_consequence: Jessica is able to finish watching her favorite show after her mother leaves the room.
immoral_action: Jessica turns the volume on the television louder, so she can hear it.
immoral_consequence: Jessica's mother turns the television off and sends Jessica straight to her room.

norm: It is good to have manners in a restaurant.
situation: Roger is having dinner at a steak house with his fiancee, Erica for her birthday, but feels gassy halfway through the meal.
intention: Roger wants to relieve himself.
moral_action: Roger, not wanting to embarrass Erica, goes to the restroom where he can belch in private.
moral_consequence: Roger feels better and Erica is able to enjoy her birthday dinner.
immoral_action: Roger decides that in order to feel better he needs to burp, so he let's one out at the table.
immoral_consequence: Now Roger feels bad because Erica is embarrassed by his actions and tells him she wants to leave.

norm: You shouldn't not hire someone just because they smell.
situation: Harry is conducting interviews for an open position at his company and the best candidate is a brilliant but unkempt and smelly young man.
intention: Harry wants all his employees to be well groomed and look professional.
moral_action: Harry convinces the young man to change his grooming practices and clean up his act, then hires him.
moral_consequence: Harry just hired and excellent candidate who will greatly benefit the company.
immoral_action: Harry chooses not to hire the unkempt young man because he smells.
immoral_consequence: Harry deprives his company of the best candidate for the position.

norm: It's good to invite someone to something.
situation: John and Mary are at the park when John gets a text from his other friends to come play soccer.
intention: John wants to go play soccer.
moral_action: John asks Mary if she'd like to come play soccer with him and some of his friends.
moral_consequence: Mary feels delighted to be invited to meet new people and agrees to go play.
immoral_action: John tells Mary that he's been summoned to play soccer and that he has to go now.
immoral_consequence: Mary feels left out and lonely.

norm: It's wrong to spy on other people.
situation: Ash has a partner who she suspects is going behind her back with another girl.
intention: Ash wants to try to find out if her partner is cheating.
moral_action: Ash approaches her partner directly and asks him if something is going on.
moral_consequence: Ash's partner is happy to reassure her that nothing is happening and proves it to her.
immoral_action: Ash starts digging around for information and monitoring her partners internet activity.
immoral_consequence: Ash's partner finds out what she is doing and thinks she is out of her mind.

norm: You shouldn't break promises.
situation: Joey tells Timmy that she'll go to the prom with him but then the star quarterback at the school asks her to go with him instead.
intention: Joey wants to have a great time at the prom.
moral_action: Joey tells the quarterback that she already accepted Timmy's invitation to go to the prom and that she always has fun with Timmy.
moral_consequence: Timmy has the night of his life at the prom with Joey.
immoral_action: Joey tells Timmy that she can't go to the prom with him and that she'd rather go with the quarterback.
immoral_consequence: Timmy is crushed and instead of going to the prom, he stays home with his grandmother.

norm: You shouldn't rummage through your dad's things.
situation: Joe is writing an essay for an assignment.
intention: Joe needs paper to print his essay.
moral_action: Joe asks his father for the paper.
moral_consequence: Joe prints his essay.
immoral_action: Joe searches his father's desk for paper instead of asking where the paper is.
immoral_consequence: Joe finds the paperwork for a family secret that he wished he didn't know about.

norm: It's good to have expectations for your spouse.
situation: Britt's husband is now unemployed, and he doesn't have many responsibilities around the house.
intention: Britt has to decide whether to make her husband do anything.
moral_action: Britt makes her husband wash the dishes after everyone is done eating.
moral_consequence: Britt's husband allows Britt to get some rest, and he provides value to the household.
immoral_action: Britt decides that she is fine with her husband not doing anything.
immoral_consequence: Britt's husband becomes dependent on her, and he becomes lazy.

norm: You should help out your child when they need you.
situation: Lizzy is in the shower, and she has been hearing her son yelling for about ten minutes.
intention: Lizzy wants to finish finish her shower up.
moral_action: Lizzy wraps herself in a towel and rushes to her son's room, deciding to rinse off after she finds out what is wrong.
moral_consequence: Lizzy sees that her son and the dog are fighting too aggressively and separates them before they can escalate their behavior.
immoral_action: Lizzy continues her shower for another ten minutes before checking on her son.
immoral_consequence: Lizzy realized too late that her son had been being attacked by the family dog, and he is seriously injured.

norm: It's wrong to be a sore loser.
situation: Tad is running for president, but lost his parties primary.
intention: Tad wants to keep working on a campaign.
moral_action: Tad decides to campaign for the primary winner, instead of continuing to run.
moral_consequence: Tad feels like he has a purpose and gets along with the campaign team.
immoral_action: Tad decides to run as a third party, against the primary winner, out of spite.
immoral_consequence: Tad is banished from his party and Tad feels alone.

norm: You shouldn't be unkind to people.
situation: Mack is driving through heavy traffic on the highway when he sees a fast-moving car quickly approaching behind him.
intention: Mack wants to maintain his place in traffic.
moral_action: Mack pulls over quickly, lets the car by, and jumps right back into his lane.
moral_consequence: The other car continues weaving through traffic and Mack is able to continue safely.
immoral_action: Mack refuses to pull over for the car and boxes him in so the car must follow him.
immoral_consequence: The car driver gets upset, drives erratically, and starts shouting at Mack.

norm: It's wrong to encourage cheating
situation: Henry is on a racing team and is in a meeting with the driver.
intention: Henry wants the team to win.
moral_action: Henry offers to improve his pit crew time to help get the car out faster.
moral_consequence: The team appreciates Henry's initiative.
immoral_action: Henry advises putting some illegal fuel additive to make the car go faster.
immoral_consequence: The team fires Henry for breach of conduct.

norm: It's unprofessional to have a relationship with your boss
situation: Jane's boss wants to know if she will go out with him for steak.
intention: Jane needs to have dinner.
moral_action: Jane declines and goes home for dinner.
moral_consequence: Their coworkers are glad because if Jane and the boss were dating they are concerned they would not be treated fairly.
immoral_action: Jane goes out to dinner with her boss.
immoral_consequence: Their coworkers do not trust that their boss will be fair with them compared to Jane.

norm: It's good to share your baked desserts with others.
situation: Timmy is sitting at lunch with classmates and has a big chocolate brownie remaining.
intention: Timmy wants to consider sharing the brownie with his classmates.
moral_action: Timmy decides to split the big chocolate brownie with his classmates.
moral_consequence: Timmy is seen as generous and makes some new friends.
immoral_action: Timmy decides to eat the entire chocolate brownie by himself.
immoral_consequence: Timmy is seen as a bit gluttonous and selfish by everyone around him.

norm: It's rude to judge someone that loves chick flicks.
situation: Levi is at home watching a copy of Dirty Dancing when his wife Angie walks in the room.
intention: Angie wants to react to Levi watching the movie.
moral_action: Angie tells Levi that she grew up watching that movie and says it's a really good story with decent actors.
moral_consequence: Levi is glad that Angie also enjoys this film and invites her to watch with him.
immoral_action: Angie sarcastically asks Levi if he thinks Dirty Dancing might be too girly for him.
immoral_consequence: Levi feels embarrassed that his wife would ask him something like that.

norm: It is good to eat fresh fruit.
situation: Linda, who has underlying health conditions, has finished her dinner and is still a little hungry.
intention: Linda wants to eat something sweet as a dessert.
moral_action: Linda cuts up some fresh fruit to quell her sweet craving.
moral_consequence: Linda benefits from the vitamins and nutrients found in fruits.
immoral_action: Linda has a large piece of decadent chocolate cake as her dessert.
immoral_consequence: Linda's health problems are aggravated by the junk food she eats.

norm: It's not okay to neglect your responsibilities.
situation: John has to work in an hour, but has just gotten a new video game.
intention: John wants to play his new game.
moral_action: John goes to work on time, then plays the game afterward.
moral_consequence: John gets paid for his time at work, and gets to play his video game.
immoral_action: John stays home and plays his video game all night long.
immoral_consequence: John gets fired from his job and must find a new one.

norm: People shouldn't buy more stuff than they can feasibly use.
situation: Katherine is about to go on a weekend trip to the beach and is shopping at the mall.
intention: Katherine wants to buy a bathing suit.
moral_action: Katherine picks out one bathing suit that was her favorite and purchases it.
moral_consequence: Katherine wears her bathing suit multiple times over the weekend and is thrilled with her purchase.
immoral_action: Katherine notices five bathing suits she really likes and decides to buy them all.
immoral_consequence: Katherine doesn't get to wear all her new bathing suits at the beach, and she also has significantly less money to enjoy her vacation.

norm: It's good to pick up your partner.
situation: Matt has the car at his work when his wife calls him, asking him for a ride home as she doesn't have a car.
intention: Matt wants his wife to get home.
moral_action: Matt gets permission to temporarily leave work and picks up his wife to bring her home.
moral_consequence: Matt's wife gets home in good time and can continue her business.
immoral_action: Matt contacts a family friend and asks her to pick up his wife so that he can continue working.
immoral_consequence: The family friend gets lost on the way to Matt's wife's work, wasting an hour of time.

norm: You should be grateful when strangers are kind.
situation: Francine is checking out at the market when she realizes she forgot her wallet, and the person behind her, Lany, pays for her groceries.
intention: Francine wants to keep her dignity.
moral_action: Francine thanks Lany and tells her she will pay her back.
moral_consequence: Francine goes home with her groceries after exchanging numbers with Lany, intending to pay her back in the future.
immoral_action: Francine tells Lany to mind her own business and walks out of the store without her groceries.
immoral_consequence: Lany never helps another stranger in need again.

norm: You shouldn't back out on an agreement with your partner.
situation: Tom promised his wife, Susan, that he will mow the lawn today but remembered that he is supposed to meet some friends at the bar in less than an hour.
intention: Tom wants to enjoy his evening.
moral_action: Tom quickly mows the lawn as promised before heading out to the bar to meet his friends.
moral_consequence: Susan sees that the yard looks great and is pleased with the job Tom has done.
immoral_action: Tom forgoes mowing the lawn in order to go out to the bar with his friends.
immoral_consequence: Susan is upset and disappointed that Tom broke his promise.

norm: It's wrong to eat too many sweets and become fat.
situation: Bart, who has a sweet tooth, has been warned by his doctor that his blood pressure is too high, and he needs to lose weight.
intention: Bart wants to eat some candy.
moral_action: Bart portions out a small amount of candy to eat.
moral_consequence: Bart begins to lose weight, and his blood pressure becomes more normal.
immoral_action: Bart eats the entire bag of candy in one sitting.
immoral_consequence: Bart gains even more weight, and his blood pressure continues to rise.

norm: You should not disrupt others with your bodily functions.
situation: Alan is having dinner with his family, and he's seated next to his younger brother Harrison who seems a bit sad.
intention: Alan wants to make Harrison laugh.
moral_action: Alan does a humorous impression of Harrison's favorite cartoon character.
moral_consequence: Alan's parents notice his efforts to cheer up his brother and praise him for it later on.
immoral_action: Alan takes a big swig of his soda and makes a very loud and exaggerated burp.
immoral_consequence: Alan's parents are appalled at his poor table manners and scold him.

norm: It's accepted that it's everyone's responsibility to copulate responsibly.
situation: Polly is at a party where she has been flirting with a guy named Chip all night.
intention: Polly wants to sleep with Chip.
moral_action: Polly makes sure to use a condom with Chip.
moral_consequence: Polly is able to have safe sex without getting pregnant.
immoral_action: Polly tells Chip not to use a condom.
immoral_consequence: Polly gets pregnant from her one-night stand.

norm: It's rude to talk while at a live performance.
situation: Nick is at an orchestral performance with a friend who has never been to the orchestra before.
intention: Nick wants to inform his friend about what will happen in the performance.
moral_action: Nick pulls out his phone, looks up the performance, and hands it to his friend to read.
moral_consequence: The performance continues uninterrupted and everyone enjoys the live program.
immoral_action: Nick leans over to his friend and starts telling him about the performance and the composer.
immoral_consequence: The conductor stops the orchestra, turns around, points his baton at Nick, and tells him to be silent.

norm: It is foolish to ignore the advice of your doctor.
situation: Reggie is ordering a dessert at a restaurant, though his doctor has warned him he needs to lose weight, or he may have a heart attack.
intention: Reggie wants to eat dessert.
moral_action: Reggie orders a small cookie and eats only that for dessert.
moral_consequence: Reggie starts losing weight and becomes more healthy and fit.
immoral_action: Reggie orders a large ice cream sundae and eats the whole thing.
immoral_consequence: Reggie gains more weight and eventually has a heart attack.

norm: You shouldn't scribble on someone's personal item.
situation: Cindy is at her boss's desk talking with someone from technical support.
intention: Cindy wants to write down a phone number.
moral_action: Cindy writes the number down on her hand, so she will remember it.
moral_consequence: Cindy is able to call the number when she looks at it on her hand.
immoral_action: Cindy writes the number down in her boss's date book.
immoral_consequence: Cindy's boss yells at her because he can't see the information in his date book.

norm: It's improper for a spouse to cheat on their partner.
situation: Mann and Olga are coworkers who are attracted to one another, but are married to different partners.
intention: Mann wants to bring up the obvious attraction they have for each other.
moral_action: Mann talks reasonably with Olga, focusing on his marriage.
moral_consequence: They come to an agreement and their marriages remain strong.
immoral_action: Mann asks Olga if she wants to have a weekend getaway with him.
immoral_consequence: Mann becomes emotionally torn between his partner and Olga, painfully.

norm: It's wrong to judge people for things they can't control.
situation: Dan is in a classroom with Bill who has tourettes which results in involuntary verbal tics.
intention: Dan wants to react to Bill's verbal tics.
moral_action: Dan reads aboit tourettes and asks Bill questions about what it is like to have it.
moral_consequence: Dan understand Bill's condition, and they soon become friends.
immoral_action: Dan mocks Bill for the tics and shames him for it in front of others in order to impress them.
immoral_consequence: The class sees Dan as a bully and does not associate with him.

norm: It's rude to masturbate on someone else's property.
situation: After a heavy petting session, Lacy's boyfriend disappears to visit his other friends leaving Lacy wound up at the party.
intention: Lacy wants her urges to go away.
moral_action: Lacy gets something to drink and steps outside to distract herself from her current state of mind.
moral_consequence: Lacy meets other people with common interests outside.
immoral_action: Lacy walks into the bathroom and touches herself until she's satisfied.
immoral_consequence: Someone hears Lacy and reports her to the host who removes her from the party.

norm: It's good to find harmless ways to express your anger.
situation: Samuel opens the break room fridge at work to find that someone has eaten his food.
intention: Samuel wants justice from whoever took his food.
moral_action: Samuel leaves a note asking whoever ate his lunch to replace it, no questions asked.
moral_consequence: Samuel comes into work the next day to find his lunch replaced with an apology note attached.
immoral_action: Samuel empties the entire fridge, tossing its contents into the trash.
immoral_consequence: Everyone at work goes hungry after having their lunches tossed.

norm: You shouldn't wear inappropriate clothes.
situation: Rosa loves the bikini she got from her boyfriend, so she now wants to wear it everywhere.
intention: Rosa wants to wear clothes she likes.
moral_action: Rosa realizes that the same clothes at a beach and at a store might mean different things to many people.
moral_consequence: Rosa decides to wear her second favorite clothes to the store and work instead.
immoral_action: Rosa wears her new bikini everywhere she goes such as the grocery store and work.
immoral_consequence: Rosa is embarrassed when she inevitably finds out about clothing norms.

norm: It's expected that people with bathe most every day.
situation: Josiah is on a two week camping trip with friends and realizes that he doesn't have a lot of soap.
intention: Josiah wants to make his soap last.
moral_action: Josiah asks to borrow some soap from a friend and takes baths as normal.
moral_consequence: Josiah's friends are pleased with how Josiah smells.
immoral_action: Josiah limits his baths to one every five days to conserve soap.
immoral_consequence: Josiah's friends are repulsed by the smell and avoid him whenever possible.

norm: You should feed your pets high-quality food.
situation: Dana calls for her dog to come inside of the house and into the kitchen.
intention: Dana wants to feed her dog.
moral_action: Dana feeds her dog the food that was recommended to her by the vet.
moral_consequence: Dana's dog stays fit and healthy for a long time.
immoral_action: Dana gives her dog the scraps left over from her meal.
immoral_consequence: Dana's dog gets really fat and develops canine diabetes.

norm: It's wrong to give someone something that might hurt them
situation: Dave is shopping for a birthday present for his son max at the mall.
intention: Dave wants to buy an item.
moral_action: Dave decides to purchase a toy gun replica for Max as Max really likes police movies.
moral_consequence: Max plays with his new present happily making gun sounds and using his imagination.
immoral_action: Dave decides to purchase a handgun for Max as Max really likes police movies.
immoral_consequence: Max plays with his new present until it accidentally goes off and maims him for life.

norm: You should not interrupt other people.
situation: Winston is listening to Hillary tell a story about her day when he gets a text saying he has won a prestigious competition.
intention: Winston wants to share his good news.
moral_action: Winston waits for Hillary to finish her story before sharing his exciting news.
moral_consequence: Hillary is happy for Winston and the two celebrate together.
immoral_action: Winston cuts Hillary off in the middle of her sentence to share his win.
immoral_consequence: Hillary is annoyed about being interrupted and doesn't sincerely congratulate Winston.

norm: It's frowned upon to wake neighbors with loud noises.
situation: Jake is a drummer in a local band, and they have a big show coming up.
intention: Jake needs to practice for the show.
moral_action: Jake practices during the day while the neighbors are at work.
moral_consequence: Jake's neighbors go to see his show when the big day arrives.
immoral_action: Jake practices late into the night, playing wildly on his drum set.
immoral_consequence: Jake's neighbors are upset at all the racket and file a police report.

norm: You should try to be supportive of your friends.
situation: Ken's friend wants to be an actor even though he is terrible at acting.
intention: Ken wants what is best for his friend.
moral_action: Ken encourages his friend to go to a theater class and helps him run lines.
moral_consequence: Ken's friend feel motivated to improve.
immoral_action: Ken insult's his friend's acting and tells him to give up on his unrealistic dreams.
immoral_consequence: Ken's friend is hurt and ends their friendship.

norm: It's rude to break someone's seashells.
situation: James and his sister went looking for seashells, and she found a lot more than he did.
intention: James wants the seashells to be distributed more evenly.
moral_action: James asks his sister if she'll give him some of the shells she found.
moral_consequence: James' sister lets him pick out a few shells, so they have about the same number.
immoral_action: James crushes some of his sister's shells between heavy rocks.
immoral_consequence: James' sister tries to retaliate by crushing his shells and James has to run away with them.

norm: It's wrong to keep old food because it's probably expired.
situation: Sally is making dinner for herself, but the only thing in her refrigerator is some funny-smelling Chinese takeout from a few weeks ago.
intention: Sally wants to eat something.
moral_action: Sally goes to the grocery store and buys some food to eat.
moral_consequence: Sally has a nice meal and is no longer hungry.
immoral_action: Sally eats the weeks-old Chinese food even though it smells funny.
immoral_consequence: Sally gets horrible food poisoning and misses two days of work.

norm: You shouldn't pretend to be suicidal just to get attention.
situation: Marla has several siblings and her parents work a lot so she if feeling neglected.
intention: Marla wants her parents to pay more attention to her.
moral_action: Marla tells her parents about how she is feeling neglected.
moral_consequence: Marla's parents will understand her and try to help remedy the situation.
immoral_action: Marla pretends to consume an entire bottle of pills and lays on the ground for her parents to find her.
immoral_consequence: Marla's parents will be very worried then very angry at her deception.

norm: Regifting is rude.
situation: Josh's best friend Tyler's birthday was coming up soon.
intention: Josh needed to give him a gift.
moral_action: Josh looks up on Pinterest how to make a fancy home made gift and makes one.
moral_consequence: Tyler is really appreciative that Josh did something entirely creative for him.
immoral_action: Josh gives Tyler a gift card that he previously received on his last birthday, but couldn't remember who gave it to him.
immoral_consequence: Tyler remembers giving Josh that same gift card, and is offended Josh gave him back his present.

norm: It is rude to ruin someone else's birthday celebration.
situation: Toms best friend lied to him about something small, and then invited him to his birthday celebration.
intention: Tom wants to confront his friend about the lie.
moral_action: Tom asks his friend for a private word at the party and asks why he lied.
moral_consequence: Tom’s friend apologizes to Tom, and explains that he lied in order to keep a promise to a mutual friend of theirs.
immoral_action: Tom clings his glass at the birthday celebration and tells the entire party about his friend’s lie.
immoral_consequence: Everyone picks a side and is either upset with Tom or his friend, nobody has a good time, and his friend cancels the celebration kicking everyone out.

norm: It's inappropriate for an adult to be dating a teenager.
situation: Amber has been texting a man named Chuck she met at a carnival a few weeks ago and is really into his personality.
intention: Chuck wants to meet up with Amber.
moral_action: Chuck asks to meet with Amber and her parents to discuss her joining a circus act.
moral_consequence: Amber's parents aren't thrilled with the idea but make plans to hear Chuck out at another date.
immoral_action: Chuck asks Amber if the two of them can meet alone to go on a date together.
immoral_consequence: Chuck's age and job put him in a position of power that creates an abusive and unhealthy dynamic in their relationship.

norm: It's good to remove abusive people from an environment.
situation: Emanuel is teaching a classroom of at risk teens and one particular student keeps starting physical altercations.
intention: Emanuel wants to keep the class under control.
moral_action: Emanuel removes the particular student from the classroom and tells him that he cannot come back until he is ready to settle down.
moral_consequence: The rest of Emanuel's class is able to focus and learn with the abusive student removed.
immoral_action: Emanuel clears out an area in the classroom and tells the one particular student and another to have it out hoping that they will settle down afterwards.
immoral_consequence: The fight between the Emanuel's students starts more fights and the class gets worse.

norm: It's bad to try to cheat at cards.
situation: James is playing poker with some friends after work.
intention: James wants to win enough money to buy a new pair of shoes.
moral_action: James plays a fair game of poke.
moral_consequence: He wins more than enough money to buy his new shoes and gets invited to play again next week.
immoral_action: James hides an Ace in his sleeve and switches it with a card in his hand, giving him 4 of a kind.
immoral_consequence: One of the other players thinks he saw James cheating and bans him from any future poker games.

norm: It is rude to disrespect your brother
situation: James, an avid reader and chess player, couldn't understand why his brother liked sports so much.
intention: James wants to feel closer to his brother.
moral_action: James goes to watch some of his brother's football games to better understand the allure.
moral_consequence: James is pleased to see how excited the games make his brother and compliments his dedication.
immoral_action: "James tries to teach his brother to play chess despite his lack of interest, so he'll have ""something better to do that hit people all day”."
immoral_consequence: James' brother says that James obviously doesn't understand who he is.

norm: It's good to care about your performance at work.
situation: Sally is working on a team project that is due tomorrow.
intention: Sally wants to get home in time for her child's soccer game.
moral_action: Sally works hard all day and skips lunch to make sure her work is done well before she leaves the office.
moral_consequence: Sally's coworkers use her work in the project and everyone goes home on time.
immoral_action: Sally rushes through her tasks and leaves a draft of her work which her coworkers have to stay late to finish.
immoral_consequence: Sally's coworkers have to stay late to finish her part of the project.

norm: You should help out your partner if they get injured.
situation: Stan and Jen were hiking in California when they came across a mountain lion that attacked Jen.
intention: Stan wanted to get away from the mountain lion.
moral_action: Stan threw some food near the mountain lion, so he could distract the mountain lion and escape with Jen.
moral_consequence: Jen feels like she trusts Stan more and is glad that they're both still alive.
immoral_action: Stan runs away from the mountain lion while leaving Jen behind.
immoral_consequence: Jen suffers permanent damage to her body and doesn't trust Stan as much.

norm: It's rude to go on a political tirade in public.
situation: Violet is in the grocery store and thinks the prices are outrageous.
intention: Violet wants to complain about the prices.
moral_action: Violet complains about the prices to her friends quietly.
moral_consequence: Violet's friends advise her to shop at a cheaper store.
immoral_action: Violet starts ranting about late stage capitalism and how the store is exploiting them all.
immoral_consequence: Violet only accomplishes holding up the line for everyone else.

norm: It is bad to be irresponsible about your work schedule
situation: Tim heading out after work on Friday night after his last server shift of the week.
intention: Tim wants to get his work shift schedule for the following week.
moral_action: Tim takes a photo of the schedule sheet with the camera on his phone.
moral_consequence: Tim shows up for all his scheduled shifts for the week.
immoral_action: Tim looks at the schedule for a few seconds to memorize his shifts.
immoral_consequence: Tim misses one of his shifts because he forgets part of his schedule.

norm: It's impolite to use a roommate's things.
situation: Tom is getting ready for work and cannot find his deodorant.
intention: Tom wants to stay fresh at work.
moral_action: Tom stops by the store before work to buy some deodorant.
moral_consequence: Tom feels more comfortable and better knowing he is wearing deodorant.
immoral_action: Tom uses his roommates deodorant while getting ready.
immoral_consequence: Tom feels gross about sharing such a product with someone else.

norm: It's encouraged you listen to your parents and behave
situation: Gary's parents told him to stay home because he has been running a fever.
intention: Gary wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Gary turns on the television and watches cartoons while he lays in bed.
moral_consequence: Gary starts to feel better the next day because he has been resting.
immoral_action: Gary goes to the park with his friends when his parents leave the house.
immoral_consequence: Gary starts feeling worse and his parents have to take him to the hospital.

norm: It's wrong to cheat on your SO
situation: Billy works long hours and hardly ever sees his wife anymore.
intention: Billy wants to fulfill his sexual and romantic desires.
moral_action: Billy realizes that change is needed, gets marital counseling and changes his job, so he can work from home more.
moral_consequence: Billy and his wife and doing well and have rekindled their relationship.
immoral_action: Billy grows close with a female co worker, and they have an ongoing affair.
immoral_consequence: Billy's wife finds out and files for divorce.

norm: It is good to not let someone die alone.
situation: Cory is working on a project for his boss, and his mom is in the hospital in critical condition.
intention: Cory wants to please his boss.
moral_action: Cory gives his boss a breakdown of the project before spending time with his mother.
moral_consequence: Being with Cory gives his mother a sense of peace and courage for the remainder of her life.
immoral_action: Cory continues working on his project.
immoral_consequence: His mother dies alone.

norm: It is wrong to waste the money of others.
situation: Stacy collects money from a gofundme to pay for her surgery.
intention: Stacy wants to spend the money.
moral_action: Stacy gets the surgery, and she donates the rest to charity.
moral_consequence: Stacy receives a box of chocolates at the end of the year from the charity thanking her for the donation.
immoral_action: Stacy goes on a vacation to a resort hotel.
immoral_consequence: Stacy's reputation is destroyed online when people discover her vacation.

norm: People are expected to do their best to get along.
situation: Alphonse got assigned to a group of people he didn't like for a school project.
intention: Alphonse wants to get an A on the project.
moral_action: Alphonse tries his best to work with his group and helps to submit the project.
moral_consequence: Everyone in his group get's an A, and they actually end up finding stuff in common and becoming friends.
immoral_action: Alphonse tells the other group members that he doesn't like them, and that he will do the project on his own.
immoral_consequence: The teacher gives Alphonse an F for not working with the group.

norm: You shouldn't cope with your emotions by drinking.
situation: Jason was getting over a bad breakup with his girlfriend and was feeling depressed.
intention: He wanted to do something to make himself feel better.
moral_action: Jason went to a nearby arboretum and walked around for hours enjoying the nature scenes.
moral_consequence: Jason felt much better after his walk and gained a more optimistic perspective on life.
immoral_action: Jason went to a nearby bar and drank his sorrows away for several hours.
immoral_consequence: Jason drove home drunk and crashed into a tree, seriously injuring himself.

norm: It's encouraged you remain professional when dealing with clients
situation: Hector works in a bank and helps clients with financial services.
intention: Hector wants to come across as friendly with his clients.
moral_action: Hector greets his clients pleasantly and demonstrates interest for them in a professional manner.
moral_consequence: Hector's boss praises Hector's professionalism.
immoral_action: Hector playfully teases clients and jokes with them in a very informal way.
immoral_consequence: Hector's boss reprimands Hector for being too informal with clients.

norm: It's good to tell people about harmful work environments.
situation: Jim works for a shipping company that has a lot of workplace accidents.
intention: Jim wants to stop getting yelled at by his boss for injuries to workers.
moral_action: Jim decides to start informing his workers every day about potential safety risks.
moral_consequence: Jim is happy that his employees are no longer getting hurt as frequently.
immoral_action: Jim decides to just stop reporting injuries that occur.
immoral_consequence: Jim is fired for unethical reporting practices and is now broke.

norm: You shouldn't hum things that are suggestive.
situation: Charles is sitting with his girlfriend on a crowded bus.
intention: Charles wants to entertain his girlfriend.
moral_action: Charles tells his girlfriend a funny story about his day.
moral_consequence: Charles and his girlfriend become closer.
immoral_action: Charles quietly sings his girlfriend's favorite song about bedroom activities.
immoral_consequence: Charles is called out by some of the other people on the bus.

norm: It's morally unacceptable to support a terrorist organization.
situation: Ben has money to spare to donate to an organization pushing for world change.
intention: Ben wants to pick an organization to donate to that will change the world.
moral_action: Ben chooses to donate his money to Doctors Without Borders.
moral_consequence: The money is used to help people in disadvantaged countries and helps save lives.
immoral_action: Ben chooses to donate to ISIS and sends his money to them.
immoral_consequence: ISIS uses the money to recruit more fighters, who then kill and oppress people in the Middle East.

norm: It's good to confront a bad pet owner.
situation: To his astonishment, Ben saw his neighbor beating a small dog.
intention: Ben wanted to bring the dog to safety.
moral_action: Ben immediately went up to his neighbor and accused the neighbor of animal abuse.
moral_consequence: Embarrassed, Ben’s neighbor apologized, promised to never do it again, and Ben felt good knowing he did something good for the dog.
immoral_action: When it became dark outside, Ben snuck into his neighbor’s yard in an attempt to quietly carry the dog away.
immoral_consequence: Ben’s neighbor called the police and Ben was arrested for trespassing.

norm: It's wrong to steal your relative's purse.
situation: Jane is hanging out with her grandma and Susan and Susan has to step away and go to the garage for something.
intention: Jane wants to get some money to buy a new shirt.
moral_action: Jane asks her grandma for a bit of money when she gets back in the room and Susan gives Jane a ride to the store to buy a shirt.
moral_consequence: Jane and Susan's relationship remains strong and Susan is glad that Jane feels comfortable asking her for help.
immoral_action: Jane takes her grandma's purse while she is in the garage and drives to the store and purchases a shirt.
immoral_consequence: Jane's grandma knows that Jane is the person who took her purse and informs Jane that she will no longer be allowed to her house.

norm: It is irresponsible to leave children around an alcoholic alone.
situation: Mary has two young children at home with her alcoholic husband and considers getting a babysitter before she leaves for work.
intention: Mary wants to find someone to watch over her children.
moral_action: Mary finds a babysitter to help take care of her children.
moral_consequence: Mary's children gets proper care from the babysitter until Mary comes home.
immoral_action: Mary simply decides to leave her children in care of her alcoholic husband.
immoral_consequence: One of Mary's children suffers an injury and Mary's alcoholic husband fails to act.

norm: One should not disturb neighbors with loud partying.
situation: Carlos moved into his new apartment, and he invites people over to celebrate moving in.
intention: Carlos wants to have fun.
moral_action: Carlos starts a table top roleplaying game, and sets up an adventure for his guests.
moral_consequence: Carlos becomes more popular with the community for his unique party idea.
immoral_action: Carlos plays music at a high volume while dancing with his friends.
immoral_consequence: The apartment security issues Carlos a citation for being too loud.

norm: It's good to use a reusable water bottle.
situation: Diana is getting ready to go out for her morning jog.
intention: Diana wants to bring some water with her.
moral_action: Diana fills up a reusable water bottle and takes it with her on the jog.
moral_consequence: Diana is protecting the environment and keeping relevant taxes lower.
immoral_action: Diana brings a single use plastic water bottle with her and disposes of it afterward.
immoral_consequence: Diana is causing needless plastic waste which hurts the environment and costs taxpayer money.

norm: It is good to call people out for doing wrong
situation: Andrew is a very honest person, and he is at the store with his friend when he notices him stealing.
intention: Andrew wants to maintain his integrity.
moral_action: Andrew confronts his friend and explains why stealing is wrong.
moral_consequence: Andrews friend decides to listen to him and stops stealing, and they remain great friends for many years.
immoral_action: Andrew decides to stop being friends with the person.
immoral_consequence: Andrew feels lonely and his friend continues towards a life of crime.

norm: It is unacceptable to rape someone.
situation: John has a crush on Susan but is too coward to express his love.
intention: John wants to have a closer relationship with Susan.
moral_action: John plucks up his courage, sending Sally a bouquet of red roses and asks her to be his girlfriend.
moral_consequence: Sally is delighted and agrees to be John's girlfriend.
immoral_action: John invited Susan to his home and has sex with her despite her unwillingness.
immoral_consequence: Susan calls the police and John gets caught for forcing her to have sex without her agreement.

norm: It's wrong to tell a partner flat out no.
situation: Fred is watching a football game on TV when his wife Sue asks him to wash the dishes.
intention: Fred wants to answer Sue's request to wash the dishes.
moral_action: Fred agrees to wash the dishes and cleans them all at halftime of the game.
moral_consequence: Sue is pleased with Fred and glad to see him contributing around the house.
immoral_action: Fred tells his wife that he doesn't want to do it and that she can wash the dishes if she wants them clean.
immoral_consequence: Sue is upset with Fred and feels irritated that he doesn't do his part around the house.

norm: It's good to help out your family with the laundry.
situation: Vince notices that the laundry hamper is full of dirty clothing.
intention: Vince wants the clothing to be cleaned.
moral_action: Vince takes the laundry basket and does the laundry himself.
moral_consequence: Vince's mother is relieved that she has one less chore to do.
immoral_action: Vince tells his mother that it is time to do the laundry.
immoral_consequence: Vince's mother does the laundry, and she has no time to rest.

norm: You shouldn't try to get out of going to school.
situation: Barbara told her mom about a mild stomach ache and Barbara's mom asks her if she wants to go to school.
intention: Barbara wants to tell her mom what she will do.
moral_action: Barbara tells her mom she can go to school because the stomach ache isn't bad.
moral_consequence: Barbara will be able to learn the lessons of the day.
immoral_action: Barbara tells her mom she won't be going to school because of the stomach ache.
immoral_consequence: Barbara will miss out on the lessons for the day and fall behind.

norm: You shouldn't send naked photos of yourself to others.
situation: Chris is sending messages to Francine to convey his desire to hook up with her.
intention: Chris wants to send Francine a message to get her in the mood.
moral_action: Chris sends a short romantic poem that he wrote to Francine.
moral_consequence: Francine loves the poem and makes plans to hook up with Chris.
immoral_action: Chris sends Francine a picture of himself without any clothes on his body.
immoral_consequence: Francine deletes Chris' number and never talks to him again.

norm: It's good to read books that you enjoy.
situation: On her lunch break Addison walks into the break room with a book in her hands.
intention: Addison wants to do something fun on her lunch break.
moral_action: Addison reads a couple of chapters in her favorite book.
moral_consequence: Addison befriends another one of her coworkers after they make a comment on her book.
immoral_action: Addison plays some games on her favorite games on her mobile phone.
immoral_consequence: Addison goes to work lacking intellectual stimulation.

norm: It's wrong to cut off your kids from your life.
situation: Cindy and her adult daughter get into an argument and stop speaking to each other for a while, which hurts Cindy.
intention: Cindy wants to deal with the pain.
moral_action: Cindy tries to make up and start a positive relationship with her daughter to avoid fighting.
moral_consequence: Cindy and her daughter reconnect over time and no longer fight.
immoral_action: Cindy refuses to talk to her daughter any longer, so she doesn't have another fight.
immoral_consequence: Cindy never gets to see her grandchildren and is never satisfied with the situation.

norm: It's good to help feed those dealing with food scarcity.
situation: Michael buys lots of extra canned goods from the grocery store, because he is afraid food will be harder to get in the coming days.
intention: Michael needs to find a place to put all the extra food he has been buying.
moral_action: Michael takes a portion of the extra canned goods that he has purchased to a local food bank and donates the food to help families in need.
moral_consequence: Michael feels good that his extra purchases will help people in need and the people who receive the food are grateful to him for his charitable action.
immoral_action: Michael continues to cram food into his cupboards, pantry and even in the closets, until he has more than he could eat in a year's time.
immoral_consequence: Michael regrets packing so much more food than he needs into his house and begins to feel guilty about all the people who don't have enough to eat.

norm: You shouldn't try to steal from work.
situation: Ross's band is playing their first show soon.
intention: Ross wants to print out some flyers to advertise the show.
moral_action: Ross goes to a print shop and prints the flyers theres.
moral_consequence: Ross keeps his job and successfully advertises the show.
immoral_action: Ross takes paper and printer ink from the supply closet at work, without asking for permission, to print the flyers.
immoral_consequence: Ross is caught by the security cameras and fired.

norm: It's wrong to make your parents do things by themselves
situation: Kelsey is a senior in high school who has outgrown her bedroom decor.
intention: Kelsey wants to ask her mom for a room makeover.
moral_action: After asking her mom to redo her room, Kelsey and her mom go shopping for new furniture.
moral_consequence: Kelsey is able to bond with her mom before leaving to college in a year.
immoral_action: After asking her mom to redo her room, Kelsey leaves her with a wishlist then goes off to have fun with her friends everyday.
immoral_consequence: Kelsey's mom is left to do everything herself, and Kelsey ends up not liking her room.

norm: It is kind to give gifts to family.
situation: Jane's sister just finished college and is having a graduation party but hasn't been able to find a job.
intention: Jane wants to make her sister happy.
moral_action: Jane saves up money and gives her sister a book on how to improve her interview skills.
moral_consequence: Jane's sister reads the book and lands a good job shortly after.
immoral_action: Jane tells her sister that she loves her, but she can't afford to give her anything.
immoral_consequence: Jane's sister is happy her sister came to the party and doesn't care that she didn't receive a gift.

norm: It's good to donate your organs to help out others.
situation: Zigmund is at the department of motor vehicles applying for a new driver's license.
intention: Zigmund wants to fill out the paperwork.
moral_action: Zigmund decides to check off the organ donation box on the form because it doesn't slow him down and knows it is supposed to be a thing to do.
moral_consequence: When Zigmund passes, multiple people benefit from his organs being donated.
immoral_action: As he finishes the form, Zigmund selects to not donate his organs because he finds thinking about his own mortality hard.
immoral_consequence: Others who could've benefited from Zigmund's organs don't when he passes.

norm: It is undesirable to be an alcoholic.
situation: Ken just lost his job and has had a greater urge to drink more alcohol.
intention: Ken has to decide whether to give in to temptation.
moral_action: Ken realizes that he has a problem, so he talks to someone about it.
moral_consequence: Ken is able to get the help he needs before anything wrong happens.
immoral_action: Ken buys multiple packs of beer and starts drinking them constantly.
immoral_consequence: Ken's health suffers, and he's not able to get another job.

norm: You shouldn't eat your boogers because it's gross.
situation: Bobby is sitting on the couch by Sue with a booger stuck to his finger.
intention: Bobby wants to get rid of the booger.
moral_action: Bobby goes to the restroom and wipes the booger off with a tissue.
moral_consequence: Sue never knew the booger existed and still has a good opinion of Bobby.
immoral_action: Bobby decides the easiest thing to do would be to just lick his finger clean.
immoral_consequence: Sue notices the booger going into Bobby's mouth and starts feeling nauseous.

norm: It's rude to curse another people
situation: Gary is shopping in the store when the cashier gives him back the wrong change.
intention: Gary wants to get the right change back.
moral_action: Gary tells the cashier that she gave him back the wrong change.
moral_consequence: The manager comes to the register and gives Gary back the correct change.
immoral_action: Gary curses at the cashier and calls her a bunch of names.
immoral_consequence: The manager of the store kicks Gary out of the store and bans him for life.

norm: It's mean to abandon someone who needs guidance.
situation: Jack's student, Jenny, has told Jack that her parents who are alcoholics and neglect her.
intention: Jack wants to be the best teacher possible.
moral_action: Jack calls CPS and reports Jenny's parents of abuse.
moral_consequence: Jenny ends up being taken away from her parents.
immoral_action: Jack decides to ignore Jenny's problem because he doesn't want to break up the family or become legally liable.
immoral_consequence: Jenny's grades fall as she sinks into depression.

norm: It is bad to fight constantly with others.
situation: Tom is up for a promotion at work.
intention: Tom wants to appear assertive.
moral_action: Tom takes extra care to make sure all his work related decisions are well researched and on-point.
moral_consequence: Tom makes a favorable impression on his superiors.
immoral_action: Tom takes to arguing his point of view with various staff members.
immoral_consequence: Tom gains a reputation for being quarrelsome.

norm: It's not okay to do things you know are illegal.
situation: Han was shipping cargo from a city where it's cheap to another where it's expensive.
intention: Han wants to make money.
moral_action: Han keeps shipping the legal cargo that earns the biggest profits.
moral_consequence: Han makes a lotta money off of his shipments between cities.
immoral_action: Han realizes that he can make way more money by shipping illegal cargo.
immoral_consequence: Han gets caught by the police who were randomly checking cargo trucks.

norm: You shouldn't hate nerds.
situation: Matt is walking down a hallway of his school and sees his brother's best friend Nate who loves coding.
intention: Matt wants have a quick chat with Nate about his brother.
moral_action: Matt tells Nate to help his brother with technical stuff.
moral_consequence: Matt's brother is glad to receive extra support from Nate.
immoral_action: Matt tells Nate to stop influencing his brother as he can't stand people obsessed with computers.
immoral_consequence: Matt's brother gets upset as Nate stops talking to him.

norm: You shouldn't break someone's heart over and over again.
situation: James isn't especially happy in his current relationship, but doubts his ability to find another partner.
intention: James wants a more satisfying relationship.
moral_action: James breaks up with his girlfriend permanently and endures some loneliness while trying to find a new one.
moral_consequence: James eventually hits it off with someone at work and ends up much more satisfied.
immoral_action: James constantly breaks up with his girlfriend then makes up a few weeks later.
immoral_consequence: Eventually James' girlfriend gets fed up and moves across the country to get away from him.

norm: It's frowned upon to be rude.
situation: Zach who isn't wearing  a watch is asked by a stranger, Nick if he knows what time it is.
intention: Zach wants to tell Nick he doesn't know the time.
moral_action: Zach tells Nick that unfortunately he doesn't own a watch, so he has no idea.
moral_consequence: Nick tells Zach thanks anyways and continues to walk down the street.
immoral_action: Zach tells Nick that he's a moron for not seeing that he's not wearing a watch so Nick should realize that he doesn't know.
