immoral_consequence: Nick is angry that Zach responded so aggressively to such a simple question and wonders if Zach isn't mentally ill.

norm: You shouldn't make fun of someone's parents.
situation: Jack comes over to William's house for the first time where he is greeted by William's dad who is in a wheelchair.
intention: Jack wants to tell William what he thinks of William's dad.
moral_action: Jack tells William that he is delighted to meet his father and hopes to get to know him more.
moral_consequence: William is happy to have introduced the two of them and is all smiles.
immoral_action: "Jack turns to William and laughingly says ""wow your father is a cripple? I never knew""."
immoral_consequence: Both William and his father are hurt, embarrassed and horrified at Jack's callousness.

norm: It's good to support your child's hobbies.
situation: Khloe's son Bobby has recently taken up painting as a new hobby, but he's very bad at it.
intention: Khloe wants to see Bobby succeed.
moral_action: Khloe signs Bobby up for an after school painting program so that he can hone his skills and become a better painter.
moral_consequence: Bobby gradually improves his painting skills and through his dedicated efforts becomes a decent artist.
immoral_action: Khloe convinces Bobby to abandon painting and try and find a new activity that he's actually good at.
immoral_consequence: Bobby is able to find a hobby that he excels in, but he doesn't enjoy it and feels like it's a chore.

norm: It's hurtful to compete with friends for guys.
situation: Emma's best friend Renee is telling her about her new crush, Tom, which also happens to be Emma's secret crush.
intention: Emma wants to respond to Renee's revelation.
moral_action: Emma hides her feelings about Tom from Renee and wishes her good luck, deciding it's not worth ruining their friendship over a man.
moral_consequence: Renee and Emma's relationship improves since Renee felt like she was able to confide in Emma.
immoral_action: Emma tells Renee that Tom is also her crush and that she's not going to back down.
immoral_consequence: Renee and Emma's relationship deteriorates since they find themselves in constant competition for Tom's attention.

norm: It's juvenile to take joy in the humiliation of others.
situation: Steve was Kent's bully when they were kids but now Steve is broke and lost his house.
intention: Kent wants to decide how to react to Steve's misfortune.
moral_action: Kent is shocked that even Steve's family money couldn't protect him from this.
moral_consequence: Kent decides to start looking into economic collapse and what causes it.
immoral_action: Kent laughs at Steve thinking no one deserves it more than Steve.
immoral_consequence: Kent feels good for a while knowing that karma caught up with the bully.

norm: It is rude to make classmates do your work.
situation: Noah has been assigned to work on a group project with the best students in his class.
intention: Noah wants to get a good grade.
moral_action: Noah works hard on his part of the project and asks his group members for help when he needs it.
moral_consequence: Noah does a good job on his part and learns a lot from the experience.
immoral_action: Noah lets his group members do the whole project because they are better at it than he is.
immoral_consequence: Noah doesn't learn anything from the project and his classmates resent him for not doing his part.

norm: It's good to help out homeless people.
situation: Chris is approaching the entrance to his job when he approaches a man with a cardboard sign begging for help.
intention: Chris wants to get to work.
moral_action: Chris puts his pocket change into the man's jar and wishes him well.
moral_consequence: The homeless man is able to find something he can afford to eat and comes back to thank Chris later in the day.
immoral_action: Chris tells the homeless person to get a job, and is overheard by one of his coworkers approaching the workplace.
immoral_consequence: Chris arrives to work, but the people who work with Chris judge him as being cruel and uncaring because of his actions .

norm: You should ask first before you eat someone's food.
situation: Jake has to work through lunch and doesn't have time to go buy take out.
intention: Jake wants something to eat.
moral_action: Jake asks a coworker to get him some takeout when they go out for lunch.
moral_consequence: Jake is able to fulfill his work commitments and get something to eat.
immoral_action: Jake grabs someone else's boxed lunch from the employee break room fridge.
immoral_consequence: Jake is embarrassed when the owner of the food confronts him.

norm: It's good to go places with your date.
situation: Kevin is on a date with Lisa, and he's thinking about what to do.
intention: Kevin wants Lisa to have a good time.
moral_action: Kevin takes Lisa to several places around the city after they eat.
moral_consequence: Lisa as a lot of fun going all these places with Kevin.
immoral_action: Kevin decides to go to one expensive restaurant and spend the whole night there.
immoral_consequence: Lisa likes the food but the restaurant got old after a while.

norm: It's bad to lose someone's pet.
situation: Leah is pet sitting her neighbor Chris's dog, Sparky, and is taking him for a walk when a cat runs past, and he takes off chasing it.
intention: Leah wants to react to Sparky breaking away from her.
moral_action: "Leah yells at Sparky to ""heel"" and he stops right on his tracks."
moral_consequence: Chris is happy that Leigh took great care of Sparky while he was gone.
immoral_action: Leah panics and lets Sparky get too far away before she begins to look for him, and now it's too late.
immoral_consequence: When Chris returns he is angry because Leah failed to keep Sparky safe.

norm: It is bad to make your partner worry.
situation: Jack went out to play video games with his friends and told Ann he would be back by midnight.
intention: Jack wants to hang out with friends all night.
moral_action: Jack calls Ann and lets her know he is having fun and wants to stay but didn't want her to worry.
moral_consequence: Ann was happy that Jack respects her and loves her enough to not let her worry.
immoral_action: Jack decides he's going to stay at his friends place and not call Ann to tell her.
immoral_consequence: Ann gets worried and thinks Jack is cheating on her and breaks up with him.

norm: It's wrong to badmouth people behind their back.
situation: Jared sits down in the break room after a tense exchange with his coworker Morgan.
intention: Jared wants to vent his frustrations.
moral_action: Jared writes down his feelings in his mood journal on his phone.
moral_consequence: Jared feels better after getting rid of all his negative feelings.
immoral_action: Jared discusses Morgan's flaws in great detail with another coworker.
immoral_consequence: Jared is criticized by HR for his actions.

norm: It's rude to ignore someone on a business call.
situation: Cameron is on a conference call with an important client when his favorite coworker, Dan, walks into his office with donuts.
intention: Cameron wants to enjoy a donut.
moral_action: Cameron quietly thanks Dan while grabbing a donut, then enjoys it silently as he continues his conversation with the client.
moral_consequence: Cameron and his client reach a good deal, and Cameron is able to enjoy his donut.
immoral_action: Cameron asks the client to hold, and spends the next twenty minutes joking around with Dan over donuts.
immoral_consequence: Frustrated with waiting, Cameron's client hangs up and Cameron loses the account.

norm: It is wrong to abandon family members.
situation: Joe took his 5 year old son to the ball game.
intention: John wants to grab a hot dog.
moral_action: John holds his son's hand to lead him to the hot dog stand.
moral_consequence: John and his son have a great time at the game with hot dogs.
immoral_action: John turns away from his son for a second to get a hot dog.
immoral_consequence: John's son wanders away and gets lost for a few hours.

norm: It's bad to push a small kid.
situation: Dave is at the mall window shopping when he feels a small child, Gary  leaning on him while he's staring at the shop window.
intention: Dave wants to get Gary off him.
moral_action: Dave taps Gary on the shoulder to get his attention then asks him to please get off his leg.
moral_consequence: Gary realizes that he's leaning on Dave and says a sheepish sorry before running back behind his mom.
immoral_action: Dave shoves Gary quite hard and Gary goes flying away from Dave, landing on his butt and hurting himself.
immoral_consequence: Gary starts to cry loud and hard right away as the whole mall looks at Dave with bewilderment and anger.

norm: It's nice to compliment people.
situation: Joe is taking his break and notices a coworker in the break room who has a new hairstyle.
intention: Joe wants to make small talk with the coworker.
moral_action: Joe tells the coworker that he likes the way she did her hair.
moral_consequence: The coworker is excited that someone finally noticed her new hairstyle.
immoral_action: Joe asks the coworker about her day and about work topics.
immoral_consequence: The coworker feels sad thinking that he hasn't noticed her hair.

norm: Partners are expected to be together during a medical emergency.
situation: Bill receives a frantic call telling him the his wife Patty's appendix burst, and she has been rushed to the hospital.
intention: Bill wants to finish making a presentation to his boss.
moral_action: Bill asks a coworker to make the presentation for him and rushes to Patty's side.
moral_consequence: Patty gets her paperwork done promptly and has her surgery on time.
immoral_action: Bill stays at work to make his presentation before going to the hospital.
immoral_consequence: Patty's surgery is delayed while they wait for him to arrive and sign consent forms.

norm: It's wrong to leave a small child unsupervised.
situation: Billy is cooking and just now realized that he doesn't have any flour that he needs for dinner, he is currently watching his two year old son.
intention: Billy needs to go to the supermarket.
moral_action: Billy knocks on his neighbor's door and asks him to watch his kid for five minutes while he runs to the supermarket.
moral_consequence: The neighbor agrees, and Billy's son is feeling calm and safe.
immoral_action: Billy tells his son he'll be right back and runs out to the supermarket.
immoral_consequence: Billy's son is afraid of staying alone and terrified the entire time.

norm: It's unhygienic not to wash your hands
situation: Andrea has a cold and when coughing covers up her mouth with her palm to keep the germs away from her husband.
intention: Andrea wants to wipe her palm off.
moral_action: Andrea goes to the sink and washes her palms with soap and water.
moral_consequence: Andrea is able to keep her husband from catching her cold.
immoral_action: Andrea grabs a paper towel and gets the mucus off her palm.
immoral_consequence: When touching other objects around the house, Andrea spreads germs and infects her husband.

norm: It's wrong to neglect the needs of someone you love.
situation: Sam's family is struggling after he got laid off from his job.
intention: Sam wants to determine what he should spend less money on.
moral_action: Sam spends less money on entertainment such as cable TV.
moral_consequence: Sam's children are bored more often, but their needs are met.
immoral_action: Sam decided to spend less money on food for his children.
immoral_consequence: Sam's children starve and have trouble paying attention in school.

norm: You shouldn't think your kids are nuts.
situation: Aron's son is so hyper that he thinks something is wrong with him.
intention: Aron wants to decide whether he should get his son help.
moral_action: Aron accepts that all kids are hyper and decides to just leave his son alone.
moral_consequence: Aron's son becomes less hyper with age and is happy.
immoral_action: Aron takes his son to go see a child psychologist.
immoral_consequence: Aron's son starts to become self-conscious and feels that he did something wrong.

norm: It's important to be honest and communicative in a relationship.
situation: John spent the whole day partying with some friends.
intention: John wants to have fun with his friends.
moral_action: John tells his girlfriend about going to the party with his friends.
moral_consequence: John's girlfriend is happy for John and asks to join John next time.
immoral_action: John does not tell his girlfriend about the party.
immoral_consequence: John's girlfriend thinks John is cheating on her and breaks up with John.

norm: You shouldn't hide things from your partner.
situation: Dylan and Lucy are a married couple with a joint bank account, and Dylan's been struggling with a secret gambling addiction.
intention: Dylan wants to go to the casino.
moral_action: Dylan confesses to Lucy about his problem and goes to the casino to suspend his account.
moral_consequence: Lucy forgives Dylan and helps him navigate his way out of his addiction.
immoral_action: Dylan goes to the casino behind Lucy's back and drains their bank account.
immoral_consequence: Lucy's card is declined while she is at the grocery store, and she leaves the store embarrassed and without food.

norm: One should always cheer those close to them on.
situation: Jeff is supposed to go to his son’s baseball game tonight, but he doesn’t feel like going.
intention: Jeff wants to decide what he should do tonight.
moral_action: Although he doesn’t feel like it, Jeff decides to go to his son’s game to be supportive.
moral_consequence: Jeff’s son hits a home run, and he is super excited his dad got to see it.
immoral_action: Jeff decides to tell his son he can’t come to the game because he has a work meeting even though he really doesn’t have a meeting.
immoral_consequence: Jeff’s son hits a home run, but he is very upset because his dad did not get to see it.

norm: It's wrong to bully your classmates.
situation: Riley is the most popular girl in her school and there has been another student who she has been finding annoying lately.
intention: Riley wants to address her issues with the annoying student.
moral_action: Riley has a private conversation with the student, and they talk out their issues.
moral_consequence: Riley is able to become friends with the student and continues to enjoy her popularity thanks to this type of behavior.
immoral_action: Riley uses her popularity to start rumors about the other student and make them feel small in front of others.
immoral_consequence: Riley soon gets in trouble for her bullying behavior and is expelled from school.

norm: You shouldn't expect to be perfect because nobody is.
situation: Janalin has a young toddler, who makes a mess of everything and refuses to obey her.
intention: Janalin wants to improve her parenting skills.
moral_action: Janalin gets a parenting book and implements a little bit of it at a time.
moral_consequence: Janalin slowly improves her parenting skills over time and doesn't stress about it.
immoral_action: Janalin gets a parenting book and tries to follow everything in it to the very letter.
immoral_consequence: "Janalin can't learn everything immediately and criticizes herself for being ""stupid""."

norm: You should help your parents out whenever you can.
situation: Tim's parents are busy cleaning up after a birthday party they had at their house.
intention: Tim wants to go outside and play.
moral_action: Tim helps his parents clean up for an hour before going outside to play.
moral_consequence: Tim's parents clean up the house a quickly with Tim's help.
immoral_action: Tim goes straight out and plays without helping his parents at all.
immoral_consequence: Tim's parents have to do a lot of work to clean up the messy house.

norm: It's important to keep debate civil
situation: Dan and Bob are co-workers that support different ideologies, having a discussion on healthcare policy.
intention: Dan wants to get his point across.
moral_action: Bob listens closely to Dan's view, and calmly explains where the flaws in his logic is.
moral_consequence: Dan understands Bob's solid points, and comes around to changing his mind.
immoral_action: After Bob gives his views, Dan objects so strongly that he screams about why Bob is wrong.
immoral_consequence: Dan is unwilling to look at things from another perspective because Bob was scolding him.

norm: It is good to help out others at work.
situation: Adam's coworker is overloaded with work and goes around the office looking for assistance.
intention: Adam wants to consider his coworker's request.
moral_action: Adam tells his coworker that he will help and sets aside time to provide assistance.
moral_consequence: Adam and his coworker develop a strong professional relationship that involves mutual assistance.
immoral_action: Adam looks away and ignores his coworker when he asks for assistance.
immoral_consequence: Adam's coworker starts viewing Adam as an uncaring person and does not help Adam out when he needs help.

norm: It is bad to be a creep
situation: Malcom has a crush on his new neighbor Jessie, and he wants to become Jessie's friend.
intention: Malcom wants to know more about Jessie.
moral_action: When Jessie is in her yard, Malcom talks to her asking about her interests.
moral_consequence: Jessie and Malcom become friends.
immoral_action: Malcom watches Jessie browsing her favorite sites on the internet from outside her window.
immoral_consequence: Jessie's parents spot Malcom and ban him from seeing their daughter.

norm: It's bad to try to get pregnant too early.
situation: Megan is a teenager who loves  children.
intention: Megan wants to be around and take care of babies.
moral_action: Megan gets some babysitting jobs and volunteers at a day care.
moral_consequence: Megan learns to take care of children and becomes a great mother a few years later.
immoral_action: Megan gets pregnant on purpose and has a baby at the age of 16.
immoral_consequence: Megan must drop out of school and is now a single mother with no education.

norm: It's bad to be in a loveless marriage.
situation: Celia's idea to Adam is they could get married so Adam becomes a citizen and Celia could afford a better lifestyle.
intention: Celia wants to decide if she should continue with her plan.
moral_action: Celia realizes she would end up trapped in a loveless marriage.
moral_consequence: Celia and Adam decide not to get married after all.
immoral_action: Celia and Adam get married just like her original plans.
immoral_consequence: Since they aren't actually in love their marriage isn't the greatest or the funnest.

norm: People will think you're cruel if you abandon a puppy.
situation: Chris is feeling cramped up in his small apartment because he has so many belongings.
intention: Chris wants to move into a bigger place.
moral_action: Chris looks for a new place which allows him to have pets.
moral_consequence: Chris' friends enjoy hanging out with him at his new apartment.
immoral_action: Chris finds an upgrade which doesn't allow pets, so he gives the dog away to someone.
immoral_consequence: Chris' friends realize what he did and think less of him.

norm: You shouldn't take wild animals.
situation: Carrie sees a squirrel on her porch eating from her bird feeder.
intention: Carrie wants the squirrel to leave the bird feeder alone.
moral_action: Carrie installs a squirrel-proof guard on her bird feeder to keep squirrels out and sets a separate feeding station up for squirrels.
moral_consequence: Carrie's bird feeder is safe from squirrels and the birds can eat from it freely.
immoral_action: Carrie traps the squirrel and tries to keep it inside as a pet.
immoral_consequence: The squirrel becomes depressed and agitated and attacks Carrie due to the stress of living indoors.

norm: It's good to lend your friends money.
situation: Thomas knows his friend Greg really wants a new bike but can't afford it at the moment.
intention: Thomas wants his friend to obtain the bike.
moral_action: Thomas lends money to Greg so that he can buy the bike.
moral_consequence: Greg is ecstatic about getting the bike and pays Thomas back as soon as he can.
immoral_action: Thomas advises his friend Greg to work more hours and save up more money for the bike.
immoral_consequence: Greg can't get extra hours at work and fails to save up the money he needs to afford the bike.

norm: It's compassionate to foster cats from a shelter.
situation: Katie has just visited the shelter, and she feels bad for the cats there.
intention: Katie wants to encourage people to adopt.
moral_action: Katie adopts a cat from the shelter and shows it off to her friend.
moral_consequence: Katie's friend is inspired to adopt a cat from the shelter as well and multiple cats get good homes.
immoral_action: Katie suggests to her friend that she should adopt a shelter cat.
immoral_consequence: Katie's friend is skeptical and doesn't end up adopting so the cats don't have a proper home.

norm: It's nice to love your husband.
situation: Laurie comes home after work when she notices her husband Jarvis laying on the couch stressed.
intention: Laurie wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Laurie talks Jarvis into playing a game of Mario Party.
moral_consequence: Jarvis feels relaxed enough to discuss his problems with Laurie.
immoral_action: Laurie goes to the bar to hang out with her friends.
immoral_consequence: Jarvis is depressed.

norm: You should not spend money you know is not real.
situation: Carla loves clothes and accessories but doesn't have too much money.
intention: Carla really wants a new Gucci purse.
moral_action: Carla waits for a few weeks until she has the money, then buys the purse.
moral_consequence: Carla's debt is under control.
immoral_action: Carla decides to buy the purse on credit even though she knows it's money she doesn't have.
immoral_consequence: Carla's debt becomes hard to manage.

norm: It's good to try out new foods.
situation: Cleo is ordering food at a restaurant she has never been to before.
intention: Cleo wants to pick something to eat.
moral_action: Cleo decides to pick something she hasn't had before that the waiter recommends.
moral_consequence: Cleo enjoys the meal and discovers that the restaurant serves food she really can enjoy.
immoral_action: Cleo picks a dish she gets at other restaurants just to be certain she gets something familiar.
immoral_consequence: Cleo's meal experience isn't memorable, and she doesn't recommend the restaurant to anybody.

norm: It's mean to judge someone for being easy.
situation: Jerry had a one-night-stand, without much effort on Jerry's part, and Jerry sees his friends the next day.
intention: Jerry wants to talk to his friends about his date.
moral_action: Jerry tells his friends that he had an enjoyable date and doesn't judge the woman involved.
moral_consequence: Jerry's friends find Jerry respectable and Jerry stays with them for a while.
immoral_action: "Jerry tells his friends that his date was a slut and probably had a bad childhood, because she was, ""easy""."
immoral_consequence: Jerry's friends think Jerry is rude and avoid Jerry while Jerry reconsiders what he said.

norm: You shouldn't leave a job if your boss needs you.
situation: Carol has been working as an executive assistant for her current employer for five years, and he is very dependent upon her.
intention: Carol wants to make a higher salary.
moral_action: Carol speaks directly with her boss about some financial issues she's been having.
moral_consequence: Carol's boss gives her a raise and some extra vacation days.
immoral_action: Carol quits suddenly with no prior notice.
immoral_consequence: Carol is unable to find higher paying work and winds up making less money at a job she doesn't enjoy.

norm: You shouldn't do drugs on the job.
situation: Lisa has been taking her opiate painkillers at an increasing rate and today she has work.
intention: Lisa wants to do her job.
moral_action: Lisa is in pain, but decides to wait until she gets home to take her pain medicine because it makes her foggy.
moral_consequence: Lisa is able to perform her work tasks and keep up a professional appearance.
immoral_action: Lisa is in pain so takes some more opiate painkillers.
immoral_consequence: Lisa is obviously inebriated and her boss notices and fires her for being high on the job.

norm: You shouldn't purposely ignore people.
situation: Sam's mother asks him to clean his room because it is messy.
intention: Sam wants to not have to clean his room right now.
moral_action: Sam asks his mother if it is okay for him to clean his room later.
moral_consequence: Sam's mother agrees and Sam enjoys playing video games before going to clean his room later.
immoral_action: Sam pretends that he doesn't hear his mother and plays video games instead.
immoral_consequence: Sam's mother gets angry and sends him to his room.

norm: It is wrong to mislead others to fit in.
situation: Nancy has just joined a new reading club in her area.
intention: Nancy wants to impress her new club friends.
moral_action: Nancy comes to the book club with some articles about the author to give them some context.
moral_consequence: Nancy's book club friends are delighted that she adds an extra level of interest to their book club.
immoral_action: Nancy tells her friends that she is friends with the author of the book they are reading, even though she isn't.
immoral_consequence: Nancy's book club friends ask her questions about the author, and realize she is not telling the truth.

norm: It's hurtful to not invite family to big events.
situation: Jeff and Jen are planning their wedding and trying to decide what kind of ceremony they'd prefer.
intention: Jeff wants to settle the matter.
moral_action: Jeff convinces Jen to have a big wedding with as many invitees as possible.
moral_consequence: Jeff's family, among others, has a wonderful time at the wedding.
immoral_action: Jeff convinces Jen to elope with him to Vegas for a private ceremony.
immoral_consequence: Jeff's family is insulted that they weren't invited to the wedding.

norm: Pick up litter is a good thing to do.
situation: Jacob is taking a walk with his little sister Kate in the park eating a candy bar when he drops the wrapper.
intention: Jacob wants to get rid of the candy wrapper.
moral_action: Jacob stops to pick up the candy wrapper and disposes of it in a trash can.
moral_consequence: Kate sees this behavior and learns it is bad to leave trash around.
immoral_action: Jacob simply ignores the wrapper and continues on his walk.
immoral_consequence: Kate sees this behavior as okay and begins to litter herself.

norm: You shouldn't destroy things that belong to other people
situation: Chris is trying to put staples into a stapler he borrowed from a coworker but it is jammed shut.
intention: Chris wants to open the stapler.
moral_action: Chris asks his coworker about opening the stapler, and they manage to get it open properly.
moral_consequence: Chris is able to use the stapler without any further issues.
immoral_action: Chris uses all his strength and breaks open the stapler.
immoral_consequence: Chris' coworker becomes angry with Chris for breaking his stapler and refuses to let Chris borrow items from him in the future.

norm: Being hateful to someone over their sexual orientation is wrong.
situation: Sam has just found out that a co-worker named Bobbie is gay.
intention: Sam doesn't want Bobbie on his work group.
moral_action: Sam goes to Human Resources, and requests a transfer to another team, because of 'personality differences'.
moral_consequence: Sam gets the transfer without any negative consequences.
immoral_action: Sam starts making hateful comments about Bobbie being gay where everyone can hear.
immoral_consequence: Sam is called into the Human Resources office and given a written warning, then transferred to another shift.

norm: Siblings shouldn't intentionally hurt each other.
situation: Jeff was playing outside in the backyard with his little brother Jack.
intention: Jeff wanted Jack to leave him alone.
moral_action: Jeff told his brother he was going play at a friend's house.
moral_consequence: Jeff was able to play without having to worry about his brother.
immoral_action: Jeff punched Jack and told him to stay away from him.
immoral_consequence: Jeff's mother scolded him, and he ended up being punished for a week.

norm: It's wrong to be late for your classes.
situation: Shay is currently in nursing school, but she also has another job that she has to spend time at.
intention: Shay wants to focus on becoming a nurse.
moral_action: Shay moves her schedule around so that she can get to class early each day.
moral_consequence: Shay's instructor respects that Shay is dedicated and is more willing to help her.
immoral_action: Shay makes sure she gets to every class, but she's often late.
immoral_consequence: The instructor doesn't believe that Shay is that dedicated, and Shay disrespects the instructor.

norm: It's bad to be prejudiced against a religious group.
situation: Francis is a self professed atheist and has just found out a classmate is Mormon during a class discussion about religion.
intention: Francis wants to explain that he is a Atheist.
moral_action: Francis explains why he is an atheist to his Mormon classmate while emphasizing how it is great that people are all different.
moral_consequence: Francis comes off as understanding and kind to his classmates.
immoral_action: Francis makes broad brush stroke comments about Mormon's while explaining how he thinks atheism is superior to it in every way.
immoral_consequence: Francis is seen as a cruel and rude person for the way he demeaned somebody's religion.

norm: It's wrong to lick animals.
situation: Harold visits the home of his friend Pam when her dog runs through the front door excitedly and licks Harold's hand.
intention: Harold wants to respond to the dog's kind gesture.
moral_action: Harold playfully pets the dog's head and begins to talk to the dog in a cute voice.
moral_consequence: Pam is happy to see her friend making her dog happy and it puts a big smile on her face.
immoral_action: Harold quickly gets on his knees and licks the dogs head as a reciprocal gesture to show the dog gratitude.
immoral_consequence: Pam is grossed out at Harold's bizarre behavior and starts to feel nervous and uncomfortable wishing Harold would leave.

norm: You shouldn't lie when texting someone.
situation: James' friend invited him out to dinner, but James felt very tired.
intention: James wants to stay in tonight.
moral_action: James texts his friend that he's really tired and not up for going out.
moral_consequence: James' friend argues a bit but eventually agrees to leave James alone.
immoral_action: James texts his friend he'll come, then texts twenty minutes later to say he's stuck in traffic and can't make it.
immoral_consequence: James' friend becomes annoyed at his flaky behavior and confronts James the next time they meet.

norm: It's wrong to divorce people without a good reason.
situation: Paul has been married for a decade.
intention: Paul wants to talk about the marriage with his wife.
moral_action: Paul tells his wife that he loves her, and they should be able to work out problems.
moral_consequence: Paul's wife will feel loved and committed to the marriage.
immoral_action: Paul tells his wife that he wants a divorce and says that's just the way he feels.
immoral_consequence: Paul's wife will feel confused and betrayed.

norm: It's wrong to throw things at others.
situation: Josh is holding onto a textbook in his hands during an intense argument with his boyfriend.
intention: Josh wants to defend himself.
moral_action: Josh asserts his opinions to his angry boyfriend by talking about his feelings, and asks Josh to let him in.
moral_consequence: Josh learns more information about his boyfriend.
immoral_action: Josh tosses his textbook at his boyfriend as he slowly backs away.
immoral_consequence: Josh has to pay for his boyfriend's medical bills after the book knocks out one of his boyfriend's teeth.

norm: You shouldn't tell your friend they look fat.
situation: Sally is at the mall with her larger friend, Sara, who asks her how she looks after trying on something.
intention: Sally wants to be honest with her friend.
moral_action: Sally replies that she thinks the outfit itself is cute and refrains on commenting on Sara's figure.
moral_consequence: Sara feels a sense of validation like she has a good sense of style.
immoral_action: Sally replies that the outfit is nice but makes her look overweight.
immoral_consequence: Sara starts to feel very self conscious about her weight and appearance.

norm: It's not okay to waste time because your so selective.
situation: Jones is trying to decide what he should write his book about.
intention: Jones wants to write a good book.
moral_action: "Jones decides to let an RNG just ""pick"" certain things and stick with them."
moral_consequence: Jones quickly writes a sold book and his publisher is thrilled.
immoral_action: Jones keeps changing his mind and wastes lots of time on the title, the font, and what genre the book should be.
immoral_consequence: Jones eventually finishes the book after enough reedits and drafts to fill an entire series.

norm: You should not remove a wild animal from his habitat.
situation: Phil is out on a big game hunt and wounds a tiger with a tranquilizer dart.
intention: Phil needs to decide what to do with the tiger.
moral_action: Phil leaves the tranquilized tiger to later wake up and return to the wild.
moral_consequence: The neighbors hear all about Phil's exciting hunt when he gets back and are impressed.
immoral_action: Phil captures the tiger and brings it home as a pet.
immoral_consequence: The neighbors are terrified of Phil's new pet and call the authorities to report it.

norm: You should always remember people's names at your wedding.
situation: Emma is standing in the receiving line at her wedding when an older lady walks up who Emma doesn't immediately recognize.
intention: Emma wants to greet the woman.
moral_action: Emma thinks back to who she invited, realizes that the lady is her mom's friend, Joan, and greets her by name.
moral_consequence: Joan is happy to speak with Emma and has a good time at the wedding.
immoral_action: Emma asks the lady what her name is and then thanks her for coming to the wedding.
immoral_consequence: The lady is upset that she came to the wedding and Emma doesn't even remember who she is.

norm: You should confide in your friends.
situation: Hina is going through a rough patch with her partner and her friend asks her how the couple is doing.
intention: Hina wants to talk about her relationship issues.
moral_action: Hina tells her friend what is going on and asks for advice.
moral_consequence: Hina's friend feels like they have a good deal of trust in them.
immoral_action: Hina says everything is going well and talks with her family about the issues later.
immoral_consequence: Hina's friend knows she isn't being upfront, so they feel a lack of trust.

norm: It's good to be a hard worker.
situation: Josh just got a job at a local business and showed up for his first day of work.
intention: Josh wants to make an impression on his boss.
moral_action: Josh does his best to complete his tasks quickly and efficiently.
moral_consequence: Josh's boss notes that Josh might be future management material.
immoral_action: Josh works at a leisurely pace throughout the day, taking frequent breaks and checking his phone constantly.
immoral_consequence: Josh's boss notes that Josh is probably not going to make it very far in the company.

norm: You shouldn't play video games all day long.
situation: James is an avid video game player and just bought a new game.
intention: James wants to get all the achievement awards in a video game.
moral_action: James plans an hour a day to play the game to get the achievements over time.
moral_consequence: James leads a well balanced life where he experiences many things.
immoral_action: James does nothing but play the game without going out to get the achievements.
immoral_consequence: James's physical health deteriorates from sitting all day.

norm: You shouldn't flirt with people when you're in a relationship.
situation: Luna, who is married, is at work where she is friends with many coworkers.
intention: Luna wants to enjoy work.
moral_action: Luna makes wise cracks with her coworkers and keeps things light throughout the work day.
moral_consequence: Luna has fun at work and her coworkers enjoy working with her.
immoral_action: Luna gets physically close and leads on a coworker who doesn't know she is married.
immoral_consequence: Luna is looked down upon by those that do know she is married.

norm: You shouldn't pee in someone's food because that's unsanitary.
situation: Anthony, a chef in a rather prestigious restaurant overhears a customer, who recently ordered pasta with tomato sauce insult his looks to someone else.
intention: Anthony wants to pay back the customer.
moral_action: Anthony excuses himself from the kitchen and walks up to the customer and confronts him.
moral_consequence: The customer apologizes and admits it was little of him, and he shouldn't have done it.
immoral_action: In the late stages of the tomato sauce, Anthony decides to pee a small amount into it.
immoral_consequence: The customer gets ill from it, and ends up vomiting, and then suing the restaurant.

norm: It's wrong to date two men at the same time.
situation: Shelia is looking for someone to date.
intention: Sheila wants to find a husband.
moral_action: Sheila goes to a speed-dating event.
moral_consequence: Sheila finds the perfect man for her to be in a relationship with.
immoral_action: Sheila starts see two different gentlemen suitors.
immoral_consequence: Sheila gets dumped by both men when they find out about each other dating the same woman.

norm: It's hurtful to leave a parent.
situation: Thomas has been living with his handicapped mother Sandra and just got a new job.
intention: Thomas wants to live on his own.
moral_action: Thomas moves to a house close by Sandra and continues looking after her needs too.
moral_consequence: Sandra feels loved by Thomas and is happy and healthy too.
immoral_action: Thomas moves across the country from Sandra and doesn't talk to her anymore.
immoral_consequence: Sandra becomes very depressed and gets sick.

norm: It's good to prepare meals for people.
situation: Ryan has a sister who is sick and stuck in bed with the flu.
intention: Ryan wants to get his sister some soup.
moral_action: Ryan makes a homemade soup for his sister from scratch.
moral_consequence: Ryan's sister feels much better after eating the carefully made food.
immoral_action: Ryan orders some soup and has it delivered to his sister.
immoral_consequence: The food isn't made well and doesn't really help the situation.

norm: It's kind to help out a friend when possible.
situation: Hank is at home relaxing when he gets a phone call from his friend John who asks Hank to help him move.
intention: Hank wants to respond to John's request.
moral_action: Hank tells John that he'll come by and complete the move with him and that he'll be right over.
moral_consequence: John is relieved that he'll get the help he needs and is really appreciative of having Hank as a friend.
immoral_action: Hank tells John that moving is hard, and he shouldn't be asking him to help him do such physically demanding chores.
immoral_consequence: John is surprised that Hank is so lazy and unsupportive and stressed out to find someone else to help him.

norm: Locking a living being in a closet is cruel.
situation: Amber's son Billy has been misbehaving a lot in school lately and Amber is growing frustrated with him.
intention: Amber wants to discipline Billy.
moral_action: Amber takes away Billy's game console and talks to him about his behavior.
moral_consequence: Billy is frustrated but learns that he must start to behave well at home and in school to get his game back.
immoral_action: Amber tells Billy to get into his bedroom closet and padlocks the door from the outside.
immoral_consequence: Billy is traumatized and tells his teacher about the treatment he got from his mom resulting in a CPS visit for the family.

norm: People are expected to be hospitable to guests.
situation: Aaron and his fiancee Delia are planning their wedding but don't have much money.
intention: Aaron wants to save money where he can in the wedding budget.
moral_action: Aaron chooses to invite fewer people, so he and Delia can afford to provide a good experience.
moral_consequence: The invited guests have a good time at Aaron and Delia's wedding and are happy to celebrate with them.
immoral_action: Aaron chooses to cut the caterin budget and does not serve to the guests at the wedding.
immoral_consequence: The wedding guests are unhappy and many leave early because they are grumpy and hungry.

norm: It's rude to tell someone you hate them.
situation: Timmy and Suzy are school friends and are playing together, but are fighting over who gets to play with a toy.
intention: Timmy wants to play with the toy.
moral_action: Timmy compromises with Suzy by letting her play with the toy for a few minutes.
moral_consequence: Suzy plays with the toy, then Timmy gets to play with it.
immoral_action: Timmy grabs the toy and tells Suzy he hates her for trying to take it.
immoral_consequence: Suzy cries and leaves, and they never play together again.

norm: You are not obligated to lend your possessions to others.
situation: Chase is at home where he owns many tools and his brother is on the phone talking about the house project he is working on.
intention: Chase wants to be a good brother.
moral_action: Chase's brother mentions many tools he needs for the house project that Chase owns, so Chase explains to his brother the value of owning your own tools for projects.
moral_consequence: Chase's brother invests in some tools of his own and Chase is able to have his own tools at his disposal.
immoral_action: Chase's brother mentions many tools he needs for the house project that Chase owns, so Chase thinks it is his brotherly duty to offer the tools.
immoral_consequence: Chase's brother begins to expect that Chase's tools are at his disposal any time, even when it is inconvenient for Chase.

norm: You shouldn't get involved with your friend's ex.
situation: Robert's friend recently broke up with his girlfriend, and Robert is finding himself attracted to her.
intention: Robert doesn't want to make things uncomfortable with his friend.
moral_action: Robert talks to his friend and asks if he would be ok with Robert asking his ex out.
moral_consequence: Robert's friend is hesitant, but he eventually agrees to let Robert ask his ex out without any hard feelings.
immoral_action: Robert asks his friend's ex out and keeps it secret from his friend.
immoral_consequence: Robert's friend finds out that Robert asked out his ex and feels betrayed.

norm: You should do things with your kids.
situation: John is at home with his wife and kids on a Friday night and his kids want to go bowling with him.
intention: John wants to hang out at the bar with his friends.
moral_action: John calls his friends and tells them he'll be late to the bar and takes his kids first to bowling.
moral_consequence: John's kids respect and love John and feel very loved by him.
immoral_action: John pretends he doesn't see his kids and rushes out to the bar with his friends.
immoral_consequence: John's kids resent John and wonder if he loves them.

norm: It's not okay to do things that embarrass other people.
situation: Billy and his coworkers go to a bar to drink heavily after finishing crunch time on an important project.
intention: Billy wants to let loose after a stressful work week.
moral_action: Billy sublimates his stress into singing karaoke.
moral_consequence: Billy's coworkers laugh at his performance and continue enjoying the night.
immoral_action: Billy decides to take his dress shirt off in the middle of the bar since it feels too stuffy.
immoral_consequence: Billy's coworkers look mortified and shun him the rest of the night.

norm: It's good to take time to improve your math skills.
situation: David has some time off of work, and he has an algebra test next week.
intention: David wants to do something fun.
moral_action: David creates a mathematical game as a way of studying for his test.
moral_consequence: David discovers a new method of studying the enhances his academic experience.
immoral_action: David watches his favorite television while talking with his friends on the phone.
immoral_consequence: David has less time to study for his math test.

norm: Excluding one member of your family from something is hurtful.
situation: Brooke doesn't get along with her brother, and she is celebrating her birthday.
intention: Brooke wants to have a great birthday.
moral_action: Brooke celebrates her birthday with her boyfriend at home binge watching her favorite show.
moral_consequence: Brooke has a great time with the person that matters most to her.
immoral_action: Brooke invites everyone but her brother to her birthday dinner celebration.
immoral_consequence: Brooke's brother gets mad and keys her car the next time they are visiting.

norm: It's good to keep your animals safe.
situation: Sheryl has a dog that likes to play outside while she is at work.
intention: Sheryl wants to let her dog play outside while she is at work.
moral_action: Sheryl installs a doggy door so the dog can go between her house and outside.
moral_consequence: Sheryl's dog can go inside if it is in danger outside.
immoral_action: Sheryl locks her dog outside while she is at work.
immoral_consequence: Sheryl's dog can't get inside the house if it encounter danger outside.

norm: Staying silent about your problems isn't healthy
situation: John who recently lost a lot of money is visibly stressed so his friend Marty asks him if everything is OK?
intention: John wants to respond to Marty's question.
moral_action: John tells Marty that he is having financial problems and that they've been bothering him quite a lot.
moral_consequence: John is relieved to get a stressful secret off his chest and feels better just by telling someone.
immoral_action: John tells Marty that everything is fine and that Mary is probably just imagining things.
immoral_consequence: John's stress continues to eat at him inside as he suffers away.

norm: It's rude to make fun of your friend's dancing.
situation: Paul has a large group of friends who enjoy planning activities together.
intention: Paul wants to go clubbing with his friends.
moral_action: Paul notices that one of his friends is not very good at dancing and gives some pointers to help his friend get into the rhythm.
moral_consequence: Paul's friend has a lot more fun dancing and goes clubbing with Paul often.
immoral_action: Paul notices one of his friends dancing awkwardly at the club and takes a video with his phone to post online.
immoral_consequence: Paul's friend is embarrassed by the video and stops hanging out with Paul.

norm: You should be there to support your family.
situation: Mike, who has plans to watch a nature documentary, is asked by his cousin Haley to come see her choir sing.
intention: Mike wants to watch the documentary.
moral_action: Mike goes to see Haley in the choir and watches a repeat of the documentary later.
moral_consequence: Haley is overjoyed to see Mike sitting in the audience while she sings.
immoral_action: Mike blows off Haley and stays home to watch the documentary.
immoral_consequence: Haley has tears in her eyes while she's singing with the choir.

norm: You shouldn't tell jokes that others may be offended over.
situation: Gary is on a date with a Jewish girl named Lisa and needs to say something funny to win her over.
intention: Gary wants to make Lisa laugh.
moral_action: Gary tells Lisa a funny joke about a famous celebrity.
moral_consequence: Lisa laughs at the joke and gets closer to Gary.
immoral_action: Gary tells Lisa a series of derogatory jokes about Jewish people.
immoral_consequence: Lisa is horrified by the jokes and walks away from the date.

norm: It's bad to think there's a way all feminists look.
situation: Harry was told by his dad that all feminists look the same.
intention: Harry wants to think about what his dad said.
moral_action: Harry considers his dad's words and realizes that unless feminists have a dress code they all don't dress the same.
moral_consequence: Harry starts wondering if his father was wrong about other races too.
immoral_action: Harry just assumes that anything daddy says is true.
immoral_consequence: Harry assumes that anyone wearing the clothes his dad pointed out is a feminist.

norm: It's nice to make people smile.
situation: Kayla is at the grocery stores shopping and there are many other customers in the aisle.
intention: Kayla wants to get everything on her list.
moral_action: Kayla takes the time to smile at some of the other customers in the store as she goes down aisles getting things on her list.
moral_consequence: Some customers smile back at Kayla and sometimes that's all somebody needs, so Kayla and the customers feel better that day.
immoral_action: Kayla rushes through the aisles ignoring other customers and grabbing everything she needs.
immoral_consequence: Kayla and the customers pass by one another like robots.

norm: It's wrong to play with someone else's mental health.
situation: Amber and Colt share an apartment where they each keep their prescriptions on the kitchen table.
intention: Amber wants to prank Colt.
moral_action: Amber hides Colt's TV remote in the morning before he wakes up.
moral_consequence: Colt is annoyed but finds the remote easily and isn't annoyed about the silly prank.
immoral_action: Amber takes Colt's psychiatric medication and empties the bottle to all but one.
immoral_consequence: Colt has a panic attack upon being fooled into thinking he was out of his medication and is angry when he finds that it was a joke.

norm: You shouldn't get back together with your ex.
situation: After a breakup, Chuck feels lonely one evening.
intention: Chuck wants some companionship.
moral_action: Chuck goes out and meets some new people.
moral_consequence: Chuck finds another woman to be his girlfriend, and it works out better than before.
immoral_action: Chuck calls up his ex and gets back together with her.
immoral_consequence: Chuck and his ex have the same problems as they had before, making them both miserable.

norm: It's impolite to smoke around a nonsmoking roommate.
situation: John is sitting on the back patio with his roommate.
intention: John wants to smoke a cigar.
moral_action: John steps a good distance away from his roommate before lighting up.
moral_consequence: Smoke goes nowhere near John's roommate and the two have a nice conversation.
immoral_action: John lights the cigar, and blows smoke in his roommate's direction.
immoral_consequence: John's roommate coughs and glares at him.

norm: It's great to propose to your partner.
situation: Jimmy has been with his partner for years, and they are having a special evening together.
intention: Jimmy wants the relationship to continue.
moral_action: Jimmy uses the special evening to get down on one knee and ask his partner to spend the rest of their life with him.
moral_consequence: Jimmy's partner is deeply touched by the gesture and says yes to the proposal.
immoral_action: Jimmy enjoys the special evening with his partner and takes things a day at a time with the relationship.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy's partner eventually grows tired of Jimmy not making a long term commitment to the relationship.

norm: You shouldn't call people idiots
situation: Louis and his friend Mick are studying math problems and Mick gets a problem wrong.
intention: Louis wants to respond to Mick getting the problem wrong.
moral_action: Louis tells Mick how to solve the problem correctly.
moral_consequence: Mick will learn the correct way to solve the problem.
immoral_action: Louis calls Mick an idiot for getting the problem wrong.
immoral_consequence: Mick will feel that he's bad at math.

norm: It's bad to misrepresent yourself online.
situation: Henry is filling out his online dating profile.
intention: Henry wants to go on a date.
moral_action: Henry uses a candid everyday photo of himself.
moral_consequence: Henry's date is glad that he is who he appeared to be in his profile and wants to get to know Henry better.
immoral_action: Henry uses a picture of a male model instead of his own.
immoral_consequence: Henry's date is upset that he doesn't look like he did online and leaves early.

norm: You shouldn't throw tantrums.
situation: Stan is shopping in the toy store with his mother for his birthday present.
intention: Stan wants to get a good toy.
moral_action: Stan requests a new game for his Playstation.
moral_consequence: Stan goes home with a new video game for his birthday present.
immoral_action: Stan pitches a fit when his mother won't buy him a really expensive new video game system.
immoral_consequence: Stan is taken home by his mother without getting to chose a toy.

norm: It's wrong to raise your voice to a coworker.
situation: Sam's new coworker has no previous experience and is having trouble keeping up.
intention: Sam wants his new coworker to work more efficiently.
moral_action: Sam teaches his new coworker how to get more work done.
moral_consequence: Sam's coworker learns something and doesn't feel as discouraged.
immoral_action: Sam screams at his coworker to work faster than he has been working.
immoral_consequence: Sam's coworker loses confidence and has trouble concentrating at work.

norm: Telling lies to your friends is deceitful.
situation: Brad, who is still unemployed and James are friends who are talking when James asks Brad if he's found a job yet?
intention: Brad wants to answer James' question.
moral_action: Brad tells James that he has been looking, but he has not been able to find a job just yet.
moral_consequence: James feels for his friend's struggle and tells Brad that he'll see what he can do through his contacts.
immoral_action: Brad tells James that he has found a Job as a salesman and that he's making good money already.
immoral_consequence: James later finds out Brad actually didn't get hired and mistrusts Brad and wonders what else had lied about.

norm: You shouldn't change the difficulty setting on someone else's game.
situation: Jimmy tells Joe that Joe can play games on Jimmy's computer while Jimmy gets chores done.
intention: Joe wants to play challenging games.
moral_action: Joe makes sure he undoes any changes to game settings before closing the game.
moral_consequence: Jimmy feels respected and tells everyone that Joe can be trusted.
immoral_action: Joe opens the settings to several games and changes the difficulties until he finds one that is challenging enough.
immoral_consequence: When Jimmy tries to play games he discovers the tampering and loses respect for Joe.

norm: Expecting a child to behave unsupervised is foolish.
situation: Gina paints a wall and listens for an expected delivery while her young son, Tim, plays nearby.
intention: Gina wants to get her package.
moral_action: Gina hears the delivery man and returns with her package, she sees spilt paint everywhere and starts to clean up the mess while reassuring Tim.
moral_consequence: Tim is a good father to his children when he grows up.
immoral_action: Gina hears the delivery man and returns with her package, she sees spilt paint everywhere and beats Tim.
immoral_consequence: Tim's emotional and psychological development is impacted, and he starts having issues in school.

norm: It's wrong to steal someone else's intellectual property.
situation: Ella is starting a new brand to sell her creations.
intention: Ella wants an attractive logo that she can use to market.
moral_action: Ella hires a designer to make a logo for her.
moral_consequence: Ella gets a nice logo that she likes.
immoral_action: Ella copies an artist's drawing from their website and edits it slightly to use as a logo.
immoral_consequence: Ella gets caught and her business reputation is ruined.

norm: You should accept others as they are.
situation: Lenny is a coach for a baseball team.
intention: Lenny wants to look at recruits.
moral_action: Lenny bases his recruiting on player's skills.
moral_consequence: Lenny develops a team that can win games.
immoral_action: Lenny says a recruit won't be brought on because of their hair style.
immoral_consequence: Lenny misses out on a good hitter.

norm: It's normal to sell baked goods for charity.
situation: Molly is going to a charity for cancer.
intention: Molly wants to sell something at the charity.
moral_action: Molly brings cupcakes to sell at the charity.
moral_consequence: Molly raises a bunch of money at the charity and sells all the cupcakes.
immoral_action: Molly brings hot Cheetos to sell at the charity.
immoral_consequence: Molly does not raise very much money at the charity.

norm: You're expected to greet people politely.
situation: Paul is a cashier at a liquor store, and a customer walked up to him .
intention: Paul wants to greet the customer.
moral_action: "Paul smiles at the customer and asks them, ""What would you like?""."
moral_consequence: The customer thinks Paul is polite and is more willing to ask them for help.
immoral_action: "Paul looks at the customer and asks them, ""What the heck do you want?""."
immoral_consequence: The customer thinks that Paul is rude and is put in a bad mood.

norm: It's bad to yell at someone.
situation: Joy is walking down a crowded sidewalk on her way home from work.
intention: Joy wants to get to her place quickly.
moral_action: Joy jumps on an electric scooter for rent and rides it to her apartment building.
moral_consequence: Joy gets home much quicker than walking along the crowded sidewalk.
immoral_action: Joy screams at a slow-walking elderly person in front of her to hurry the hell up.
immoral_consequence: Joy is chastised by other people walking nearby for her rudeness to the person.

norm: You shouldn't make noise when someone is trying to sleep.
situation: Sam who lives with family, just arrived home late after a long day at work and wants to do something fun.
intention: Sam wants to play a new video game he got.
moral_action: Sam puts on his gaming headphones to play.
moral_consequence: Sam's family gets a restful sleep because the house remains quiet.
immoral_action: Sam plays the game keeping the audio on the speakers.
immoral_consequence: Sam wakes up his family with the volume from the game.

norm: It is wrong to take away someone's income without notice.
situation: Harold owns a store that has been losing money for a long time.
intention: Harold wants to shut down the store.
moral_action: Harold gives his employees a month's notice that he is shutting down.
moral_consequence: Harold's employees are able to find new jobs and keep getting paid.
immoral_action: Harold shuts down the store without telling his employees, leaving a note on the door.
immoral_consequence: Harold's former employees are out of work and can't pay their bills.

norm: It's wrong to take advantage of your parent's kindness.
situation: Tommy moved away from home to attend college in another state and, though his parents pay for his education, he struggles with finances as a young student.
intention: Tommy wants to get the money together to go on a weekend trip.
moral_action: Tommy finds a job cleaning out an abandoned house, off campus, that pays enough for him to go away for the weekend.
moral_consequence: His parents are proud of him because he found a way to make some money for himself, and he enjoys his weekend more because he worked to get there.
immoral_action: Tommy calls his parents and claims that he needs some money to pay for an extracurricular, school related activity, instead of telling them it’s for a personal trip.
immoral_consequence: Tommy's parents are duped into sending money under false pretenses and Tommy feels guilty about going on his trip because he lied to get there.

norm: It is never acceptable to swear at someone serving food.
situation: Karen is dining out with her family when her order is not done accurately.
intention: Karen wants to get the correct order.
moral_action: Karen points out the mistake in the order and asks if anything can be done.
moral_consequence: Karen is given the correct order and comped a free dessert because of the mistake.
immoral_action: Karen uses expletives in a voice that is audible to customers around them while questionsing the competence of the waiter.
immoral_consequence: Karen is approached by the manager and asked to leave after other customers complain about her behavior.

norm: Punctuality is considered to be polite.
situation: Bill is on his way to a regional sales meeting, which will be attended by his colleagues and some of his company's customers.
intention: Bill wants a cup of coffee to take with him into the meeting.
moral_action: Bill rushes to the meeting, arriving with time to spare to brew himself a mug of coffee at the office kitchen.
moral_consequence: Everyone at the meeting is appreciative of Bill's prompt arrival to the meeting place.
immoral_action: Bill stops off at a coffee shop to pick up a coffee to take with him to the meeting.
immoral_consequence: The stop at the coffee shop takes a few minutes and Bill arrives late to the meeting, which causes tension among his colleagues and their clients.

norm: You shouldn't fight with people.
situation: Sam accidently bumped in to the person in front of her, and they swore at her.
intention: Sam wants to respond to the person.
moral_action: Sam tells the person sorry for bumpng into you.
moral_consequence: The person doesn't respond and Sam ignores them from there.
immoral_action: Sam gets into a fight with the person in front of her.
immoral_consequence: Sam wins the fight sure, but that's the third place she's been banned from this year.

norm: You should always return someone's things.
situation: Linda's laptop charger got frayed over time, and she had to borrow one from a friend, so she could use her computer.
intention: Linda wants to have a laptop charger to use long term.
moral_action: Linda returns her friends charger and orders a new one for herself off of the internet.
moral_consequence: Linda's friend appreciates getting the charger back and tells Linda she can use it anytime she needs.
immoral_action: Linda keeps her friend's charger, hoping that her friend will forget and won't ask her to return it.
immoral_consequence: Linda's friend gets annoyed that it's taking so long to get her charger back, and she doesn't lend Linda anything else after that.

norm: Children should respect their elders.
situation: John sees his mother's new car sitting in the driveway.
intention: John wants to drive over  to a friends house to visit.
moral_action: John asks his mother if he can borrow the car.
moral_consequence: John's mother agrees to let him borrow it, and he gets to visit his friend.
immoral_action: John takes the car without asking his mother if he can borrow it.
immoral_consequence: John's mother calls the car in as stolen to the police, and he is arrested.

norm: You shouldn't cancel on your family members.
situation: Arna is a loner and is invited to her sister's anniversary and is at home deliberating on whether to attend.
intention: Arna wants to call her sister with an answer.
moral_action: Arna says she'll go but admits her desire to be alone.
moral_consequence: Arna bonds with her sister and they compromise.
immoral_action: Arna tells her sister that she doesn't feel comfortable attending.
immoral_consequence: Arna hears less often from her sister and misses the social contact.

norm: You shouldn't tell children that they are small and weak.
situation: Mike and his young son are moving bricks into the house to make a wall.
intention: Mike wants to talk to his son about his brick carrying.
moral_action: Mike tells his son that he's proud of his effort in carrying the bricks.
moral_consequence: Mike's son will have confidence and enjoy helping his father.
immoral_action: Mike tells his son that he's not strong and big enough to carry the bricks properly.
immoral_consequence: Mike's son will feel depressed and not like being around his father.

norm: It's bad to leave without telling anyone.
situation: Jenna has been at a party for three hours and is getting tired, but knows her friends will try to convince her to stay.
intention: Jenna wants to go home and sleep.
moral_action: As Jenna walks out the door, she tells her friends she had a great time, but she feels really tired.
moral_consequence: Jenna's friends only have time to wave goodbye before she's on the sidewalk walking home.
immoral_action: Jenna sneaks out the back door without talking to her friends.
immoral_consequence: Jenna goes home and sleeps while her friends panic about her going missing.

norm: It's good to take your partner out to dinner.
situation: James and his girlfriend have an anniversary coming up.
intention: James wants his girlfriend to know he loves her.
moral_action: James makes reservations at his girlfriends favorite restaurant to celebrate their anniversary.
moral_consequence: James' girlfriend is surprised by the dinner, and they have a great night celebrating their love.
immoral_action: James doesn't plan for his anniversary at all and simply tells his girlfriend he loves her, then proceeds with his day.
immoral_consequence: James girlfriend feels that he doesn't find their anniversary to be special, and spends the day crying.

norm: You should tell someone if they offend you.
situation: Greta, a Christian, is hanging out with Stacy when Stacy makes a joke about Christians.
intention: Greta wants to respond to Stacy.
moral_action: Greta tells Stacy that the joke is in bad taste.
moral_consequence: Stacy will not make jokes about Christians anymore.
immoral_action: Greta changes the subject but does not tell Stacy she doesn't like the joke.
immoral_consequence: Stacy will continue to think it's okay to make jokes about Christians.

norm: It's wrong to be lazy when you have a kid.
situation: Shana has a son, and she is feeling particularly unmotivated today.
intention: Shana wants to relax on the couch and watch TV.
moral_action: Shana has a coffee for energy and gets in a good workout before kicking back on the couch.
moral_consequence: Shana's son learns that hard work can come with a reward.
immoral_action: Shana plops down on the couch and watches TV all day.
immoral_consequence: Shana's son learns from his mom that it's okay to be lazy.

norm: It is destructive to be argumentative in a relationship.
situation: Nick and Kelly are a couple who occasionally criticize one another, but love each other very much.
intention: Nick wants to respond to Kelly's criticisms.
moral_action: Faced with her criticism, Nick gently asks Kelly why she feels the way she does, and apologizes for his actions.
moral_consequence: Nick and Kelly's relationship grows from being able to communicate, and they argue less.
immoral_action: Faced with her criticism, Nick screams at Kelly and denies everything she says.
immoral_consequence: Feeling unheard, Kelly decides to leave the relationship.

norm: It's bad to be overconfident in your abilities.
situation: Sam's friend Bill invites him to go rock climbing even though he has never done it before.
intention: Sam wants to respond to Bill's invitation.
moral_action: Sam tells Bill he doesn't know how to rock climb and declines the invitation, thanking Bill for the offer.
moral_consequence: Sam stays home and remains uninjured.
immoral_action: Sam agrees to go rock climbing with Bill.
immoral_consequence: Sam slips and falls due to his inexperience and is injured.

norm: It's expected that you help children.
situation: Wanda, a grade school teacher, is walking through the school hallway when she notices a little girl looking slightly lost.
intention: Wanda wants to get to her classroom to begin the class.
moral_action: Wanda gives the girl directions to her classroom and then continues walking down the hallway.
moral_consequence: The girl is able to get to her class on time.
immoral_action: Wanda continues walking down the hallway to her classroom, ignoring the girl.
immoral_consequence: The girl starts crying because she doesn't know where to go.

norm: You shouldn't ignore bad smells in your house.
situation: Danny recently moved into a new apartment and noticed a foul odor in his home, but does not know where it is coming from.
intention: Danny wants to do something about the odor.
moral_action: Danny thoroughly searches the apartment to find a dead squirrel in the attic.
moral_consequence: The squirrel is removed from the attic, and Danny can live odor-free.
immoral_action: Danny does not look for the odor, instead opting to light candles to cover it up instead.
immoral_consequence: The odor does not go away, and Danny's friends and family refuse to visit.

norm: It's rude to make someone feel insecure about their weight.
situation: Bella is spending time with her friend who has been depressed lately.
intention: Bella wants to get her friend out of her funk.
moral_action: Bella has a nice long discussion with her friend and encourages her to talk through her current problems while listening.
moral_consequence: Bella's friend is able to vent a little by actually describing her problems aloud and makes the first small step to feeling better.
immoral_action: Bella tries to motivate her friend by pointing out that she has put on weight from being so depressed and doesn’t look especially good.
immoral_consequence: Bella's friend is in no condition to hear the blunt truth and becomes even more depressed and self concious.

norm: It is bad to keep a family recipe for others.
situation: Micah is in a cooking contest against his sister Emily who asks him the recipe for his mother's pie.
intention: Micah wants to win the cooking contest.
moral_action: Micah tells Emily that they should join the cooking contest as a team.
moral_consequence: Emily learns how to become a better cook by baking with Micah.
immoral_action: Micah tells Emily the wrong ingredients for the pie.
immoral_consequence: Emily feels hurt when she discovers Micah's deception.

norm: It's wrong to be late to an appointment.
situation: Mike driving to a dentist appointment and is on track to make it on time when he notices his car's gas tank is nearly empty.
intention: Mike wants his car to last as long as possible.
moral_action: Mike parks his car at a nearby store and quickly jogs to the appointment in only a few minutes time.
moral_consequence: Mike makes it to the appointment on time but is sweaty and uncomfortable during the appointment.
immoral_action: Mike stops to put gas in his tank to avoid causing damage by running out of fuel on the road, but this takes several minutes.
immoral_consequence: Mike is late to the appointment, but the dentist is behind schedule and it doesn't matter.

norm: It is good to smoke outside instead of inside.
situation: Greg is an occasional smoker who is hanging out at a friend's house and having a few beers.
intention: Greg wants to have a cigarette.
moral_action: Greg steps outside onto the back porch to have a smoke.
moral_consequence: Greg enjoys his brief cigarette break before returning inside to his friends.
immoral_action: Greg lights up and begins to smoke a cigarette in the living room.
immoral_consequence: Greg's smoking causes an unpleasant smell and his friends yell at him for smoking inside.

norm: It's bad to play the blame game with people.
situation: Linda works in a lab with others and often is careless with tests.
intention: Linda wants to avoid getting in trouble for bad job performance.
moral_action: Linda owns her mistakes and works on improving them.
moral_consequence: After time Linda becomes good at her job and is respected by her team.
immoral_action: Linda accuses others of making the mistakes and tries to other depaartments.
immoral_consequence: Linda is not likes by others in the job and treated coldly by others.

norm: It's good to talk about the fun times you had.
situation: Ash is talking to his friend Bill about the movies they saw together.
intention: Ash wants to keep talking to Bill.
moral_action: Ash brings up the best times they had watching movies together.
moral_consequence: They have fun talking about their best times in the movie theater.
immoral_action: Ash mentions the worst movies they ever saw together.
immoral_consequence: They spend an hour talking about terrible, terrible films.

norm: It's good to give people credit where credit is due.
situation: Martha is preparing a presentation for a major marketing meeting.
intention: Martha wants to get input from multiple people with expertise.
moral_action: Martha talks to various experts and asks them if she can include their ideas in her presentation.
moral_consequence: Martha's presentation goes beautifully, and she is praised for the in depth research she has done.
immoral_action: Martha gets information from other employees private files and uses them without permission.
immoral_consequence: Martha's presentation is interrupted by the audience when they see other people's work that they recognize.

norm: It's good to use birth control.
situation: Before making love to Ellen for the first time, George asks her if she is on birth control.
intention: Ellen wants to have sex with George.
moral_action: Ellen tells George he has to use a condom as she is not on the pill.
moral_consequence: Ellen spends an enjoyable night with George.
immoral_action: Ellen says that she is on birth control, knowing that this isn’t true.
immoral_consequence: Ellen gets pregnant and has to face a furious George when she has to confess to her lie.

norm: You shouldn't spend all day masturbating.
situation: James felt overwhelmed, so he decided to take a mental health day off from work.
intention: James wants to relax.
moral_action: James decides to try a new restaurant and then go out to a play.
moral_consequence: James enjoys himself and has a very memorable day out.
immoral_action: James spends most of the day watching porn and masturbating.
immoral_consequence: James feels relaxed, but a little bored that he always does the same thing.

norm: You shouldn't foil your grandchildren's healthy diet.
situation: Patsy is babysitting for her two grandchilden.
intention: She wants to give them something to eat.
moral_action: Patsy gives her grandchildren a plate of healthy fruits and vegetables.
moral_consequence: The two children eat everything on the plate, making them happy and energetic.
immoral_action: Patsy feeds her grandchildren candy and ice cream against the express wishes of their mother.
immoral_consequence: The two children aren't used to all the sugar, and they both get a stomachache.

norm: You shouldn't let other people pay for your things.
situation: Daruka is on a date with a recently jobless traditional man Jeremy, and Jeremy wants to pay the bill.
intention: Daruka doesn't want to hurt Jeremy's feelings.
moral_action: Daruka suggests that she pay for the meal while Jeremy can pay for the deserts.
moral_consequence: Jeremy trust in Daruka deepens.
immoral_action: Daruka lets Jeremy take care of the entire bill.
immoral_consequence: Jeremy is hit with overdraft fees on his credit card.

norm: It's good to do schoolwork.
situation: George is a student in the 6th grade who struggles with math.
intention: George wants to make doing math less time consuming.
moral_action: George stays once a week for extra help when the teacher offers.
moral_consequence: George learns the math quicker and his homework is less time consuming as a result.
immoral_action: George does not do the homework and plays with friends instead.
immoral_consequence: George fails math and must take summer school to avoid repeating a grade.

norm: It's bad to be unfaithful.
situation: Bonnie and her husband are taking a vacation together at a resort in Cancun.
intention: Bonnie is feeling amorous and wants to have sex.
moral_action: Bonnie asks her husband to have sex with her on the beach under the moonlight.
moral_consequence: Bonnie shares a wonderful sexual time with her husband.
immoral_action: Bonnie brings a stranger back to their hotel room and has sex with him.
immoral_consequence: Bonnie is divorced by her husband after he walks in the room and sees her infidelity.

norm: It's bad to lie to your spouse.
situation: Ted has been working hard all day and feels he should have some fun.
intention: Ted wants to go to have drinks with his coworkers after work.
moral_action: Ted tells his wife had some drinks with his coworkers.
moral_consequence: Ted's wife is unhappy that he got home later than usual but glad that he had a nice time with his coworkers.
immoral_action: Ted tells his wife he had to work late and doesn't tell her he went out for drinks.
immoral_consequence: Ted feels guilty about lying to his wife and has to tell more lies about working late.

norm: It's wrong to neglect children.
situation: Luigi tries to think of what he needs to do today after work.
intention: Luigi wants to plan his day.
moral_action: Luigi remembers he needs to pick up his kids from school.
moral_consequence: Luigi goes to the school and picks them up on time.
immoral_action: Luigi forgets that it's his day to pick up the kids, and he goes straight home.
immoral_consequence: Luigi goes home and realizes the kids aren't there before he goes to pick them up.

norm: It's rude to insult your significant other.
situation: Sophie is getting dressed for a night out with her partner Marie, who is sitting beside her.
intention: Marie wants to give Sophie outfit feedback.
moral_action: Marie tells Sophie that the color of the dress is really lovely on her.
moral_consequence: Sophie feels happy and confident, and the two of them enjoy their evening.
immoral_action: Marie tells Sophie that the dress she is wearing makes her body look really bad.
immoral_consequence: Sophie feels self conscious and doesn't want to go anywhere anymore, so they stay home.

norm: You shouldn't call someone the wrong name.
situation: James, who comes from a very conservative family, has a class with a transgender student who changed their name from Joe to Joanna.
intention: James wants to share his conservative political views.
moral_action: James uses Joanna's name while talking about his beliefs about the importance of a traditional family .
moral_consequence: Joanna tells James that he's wrong, but appreciates that he uses the correct name.
immoral_action: James insists all calling Joanna by her old name, which clearly bothers her.
immoral_consequence: James' classmates start ostracizing him because they sympathize with Joanna.

norm: You should not talk about another person's children.
situation: Wilson talks to his wife about those no good Smith kids and their son (who is friends with those kids) overhears.
intention: Wilson wants to explain to his son.
moral_action: Wilson realizes what he was doing was wrong and apologizes to his son.
moral_consequence: Their son thanks him for the apology and heads back to his room.
immoral_action: Wilson fabricates a story about a different Smith from work who is not one of his son's friends.
