immoral_consequence: Their son points out that talking behind people's backs about people is wrong no matter who it is.

norm: People should be kind.
situation: Tim is hanging out with a group of friends who are cruelly mocking someone.
intention: Tim wants to keep having a good time with everyone.
moral_action: Tim changes the subject to something he is sure everyone is interested in.
moral_consequence: Tim feels good for protecting someone's feelings.
immoral_action: Tim joins in on the mocking and eggs everyone on.
immoral_consequence: Tim feels guilty for having fun at someone's expense.

norm: It's wrong to be unfaithful to someone you love
situation: Brad and Jennifer are married, and one of Brad's old girlfriends calls him up.
intention: Brad wants to communicate with his old girlfriend.
moral_action: Brad talks to his old girlfriend on the phone and tells Jennifer about it later.
moral_consequence: Jennifer is happy Brad told her about the conversation.
immoral_action: Brad meets up with his old girlfriend, and they sleep together.
immoral_consequence: Jennifer finds out and files for a divorce.

norm: You shouldn't call out your customers on social media.
situation: Fiona sits in her car after getting into a fight with a rude customer.
intention: Fiona wants to vent her frustrations.
moral_action: Fiona rants to another one of her coworkers on the phone.
moral_consequence: With all of the anger out of her system, Fiona is able to enjoy the rest of her night.
immoral_action: Fiona makes a posts about the incident on her Twitter.
immoral_consequence: Fiona is written up after the customer discovers the tweet and reports it to her boss.

norm: You shouldn't approve of your grandchildren's irresponsible behavior.
situation: Neji watches his grandson do dangerous stunts on their bicycles.
intention: Neji wants to make his grandson happy.
moral_action: Neji says that he's cooking his grandson's favorite food, and Neji gives safety tips during supper.
moral_consequence: Neji's grandson passes on the information to his friends who treat him as an expert.
immoral_action: Neji cheers on his grandson for the edge of the sidewalk.
immoral_consequence: His grandson falls off his bike injuring his leg.

norm: It's wrong to sleep around because that's slutty.
situation: Mary is devastated when her boyfriend dumps her after telling her he finds her sexually boring.
intention: Mary wants to feel better about her sexuality.
moral_action: Mary devotes herself to rebuilding her self esteem.
moral_consequence: Mary is able to get past her ex's cruel words and find a better suited partner.
immoral_action: Mary decides to gain experience by sleeping with multiple partners in a short period of time.
immoral_consequence: Mary's reputation suffers, and she has a hard time finding a permanent partner.

norm: It's good to treat yourself every now and then.
situation: Kevin has been working seven days per week for a month but now has his Saturday off at home with his wife.
intention: Kevin wants to do something on his day off.
moral_action: Kevin goes to a spa and gets himself an hour-long massage.
moral_consequence: Kevin feels relaxed and takes his wife out for a romantic dinner that night.
immoral_action: Kevin spends his Saturday doing chores for his wife around the house.
immoral_consequence: Kevin ends up yelling at his wife because he's stressed and thinks she's too demanding.

norm: You shouldn't give your roommate a curfew.
situation: Jason is about to leave to go out with his friends and tells his roommate Alan goodbye.
intention: Alan wants to respond to Jason.
moral_action: Alan tells Jason to have a great time and that he'll see him later.
moral_consequence: Jason is happy that Alan wished him a good time and is excited to get going.
immoral_action: Alan tells Jason to make sure he's back home before eleven pm or Alan will be very angry.
immoral_consequence: Jason is confused why Alan would think he can say that to him and is angry for suggesting that Alan has control over Jason.

norm: It's not okay to be to obsessive about people.
situation: Leila met a cute guy at a party a few weeks ago and has been on dates a few times with him since then.
intention: Leila wants the cute guy to think she is someone special.
moral_action: Leila sends a few interesting links to the cute guy along with original and thoughtful texts.
moral_consequence: The cute guy becomes more and more interested by Leila.
immoral_action: Leila can't stop thinking of the cute guy and starts texting him dozens of times a day.
immoral_consequence: The cute guy becomes weary of Leila and tries to avoid her.

norm: It's noble to prioritize making money over leisure.
situation: Don's school is on summer break.
intention: Don wants to get a tan.
moral_action: Don gets a job as a  lifeguard for the summer.
moral_consequence: Don's parents are happy that Don has money to help them with the bills.
immoral_action: Don goes to the pool all day and lays around.
immoral_consequence: Don's parents are annoyed that he isn't doing anything useful.

norm: It's wrong to leave someone because of their infertility.
situation: Carlow wants to start a family, but his wife Santana developed a condition making having kids impossible.
intention: Carlow wants kids.
moral_action: Carlow and Santana decide to adopt three children.
moral_consequence: Santana has fun spending time with her children.
immoral_action: Carlow divorces his wife to start a family with a younger woman.
immoral_consequence: Santana is heartbroken.

norm: You should treat restaurant workers with respect.
situation: Joey is one a first date a nice restaurant with a man he just met.
intention: Joey wants to order more wine from their server.
moral_action: Joey signals to their server to get her attention and place his wine order.
moral_consequence: Joey gets another date with the man who thinks Joey is quite a nice, refined gentleman.
immoral_action: Joey calls their server fat and slow when she finally comes by to take their order.
immoral_consequence: Joey doesn't get a second date because the man thought he was disrespectful to the server.

norm: It's unusual to climb through your bathroom window.
situation: Sam is locked out of his house and doesn't have the key, but some windows are partly open.
intention: Sam wants to get inside the house.
moral_action: Sam tries to climb in through a living room window.
moral_consequence: After a struggle, Sam safely makes it inside.
immoral_action: Sam tries to climb through the bathroom window.
immoral_consequence: Sam missteps and puts his foot into the toilet, soaking it.

norm: It's wrong to mess with a boyfriend's career.
situation: Jane gets a call from her boyfriend saying he forgot his lunch at work and needs her to deliver.
intention: Jane wants to deliver lunch to her boyfriend.
moral_action: Jane delivers the food to her boyfriend without interrupting the workplace.
moral_consequence: The people in the office don't see Jane coming in and Jane is happy to help her boyfriend.
immoral_action: Jane talks with her boyfriends coworkers while delivering the lunch, interrupting their work.
immoral_consequence: The people in the office are insulted and Jane feels guilty.

norm: You should ask before taking something.
situation: Cooper is working on his car and needs a specific tool that his dad has.
intention: Cooper wants to acquire the tool for his car.
moral_action: Cooper asks his dad to use the tool.
moral_consequence: Cooper's dad lets Cooper use the tool and knows where the tool is.
immoral_action: Cooper uses the tool without informing his dad.
immoral_consequence: Cooper's dad will think someone stole the tool and will become anxious.

norm: It's good to be concerned about your roommate's pets.
situation: Chrissy was asked to pet-sit her roommate Jack's dog.
intention: Chrissy wants to do a favor for Jack.
moral_action: Chrissy takes Jacks dog out and cleans up after him.
moral_consequence: When Jack comes home he is very happy he was able to trust Chrissy.
immoral_action: Chrissy watches Jacks dog but doesn't take him out.
immoral_consequence: The dog pees all over the carpet and Jack is angry when he comes home.

norm: It's wrong to get into fights with your partner.
situation: Ian and Holly disagree on where they should go for vacation.
intention: Ian wants to go to his chosen destination.
moral_action: Ian attempts to negotiate with Holly to go to his place, but do things she wants to do.
moral_consequence: Ian and Holly reach a compromise, and both get what they want.
immoral_action: Ian shouts at Holly and attempts to bully her into accepting his idea.
immoral_consequence: Holly gets angry and storms out of the house.

norm: It's not very nice to snap at a friend.
situation: Walter's friend tells him that he has been secretly talking with Walter's girlfriend.
intention: Walter wants his friend to stop talking to his girlfriend in secret.
moral_action: Walter tells his friend that it is very hurtful to hear that he has been talking to Walter's girlfriend in secret, and he asks his friend to stop doing that.
moral_consequence: Walter and his friend have a conversation about what has been going on and come to a resolution that they can both live with.
immoral_action: "Walter points at his friend and yells loudly, ""you better stop talking to her behind my back!""."
immoral_consequence: Walter and his friend are both upset and the conversation ends without any resolution.

norm: An engagement should be about more than a material thing.
situation: Samuel and his wealthy significant other have become very close lately.
intention: Samuel wants to propose to his significant other.
moral_action: Samuel proposes because he and his significant other are deeply in love.
moral_consequence: Samuel and his significant other get married and live happily.
immoral_action: Samuel proposes because he wants a chunk of his significant other's wealth.
immoral_consequence: Samuel is seen as a gold-digger and his significant other leaves him.

norm: You shouldn't waste a policemen's time.
situation: Jill was out walking her dog when she saw a strange man waking through her neighborhood.
intention: Jill wants to make sure no one in her neighborhood is the victim of a crime.
moral_action: Jill approaches the man and asked if he moved into the neighborhood recently.
moral_consequence: The man says he just moved in from Colorado, and Jill realizes he's quite a charming, trustworthy neighbor.
immoral_action: Jill calls the police and claims that the man is acting suspiciously.
immoral_consequence: The police come question the man, realize he lives in the neighborhood, and scold Jill for wasting their time.

norm: Manager should not be mean to their employees
situation: Jason, a manager at a fast food restaurant, just noticed that his employee Jill made a huge mess.
intention: Jason wants to get Jill to clean up the mess.
moral_action: Jason asks Jill to clean up the mess and gives her tips to avoid getting into this situation in the future.
moral_consequence: Jill learns how to follow proper work procedures and decides to be more diligent.
immoral_action: Jason yells at Jill and tells her that she's fired if she doesn't clean up the mess immediately.
immoral_consequence: Jill's feelings are hurt, and she decides to start looking for another job.

norm: It's good to want what is best for your kids.
situation: Mary found out her daughter is going to college and her daughter needs help finding a college.
intention: Mary wants to help pick a college for her daughter.
moral_action: Mary picks the best school she can afford, which is a nice out-of-state, private school.
moral_consequence: Mary's daughter learns a lot from her college, and her mom feels proud of Mary.
immoral_action: Mary picks the cheapest school for her daughter even though it is the worst school in the state.
immoral_consequence: Mary's daughter has a horrible time at the school and Mary feels negative energy from her daughter.

norm: It is unacceptable to sexually harrass co workers.
situation: Cindy went to work at the office with lots of coworkers.
intention: Cindy wants to decide how to act at the office.
moral_action: Cindy acted more professional at the office to suit the enviorment.
moral_consequence: Cindy gets praise from the bosses for getting lots of work finished.
immoral_action: Cindy would slap her male coworker's butts as they walked away or past her.
immoral_consequence: Cindy eventually got complaints for sexual harassment of coworkers.

norm: It's good to be loyal to old friends.
situation: Mark's childhood best friend Justin has fallen on some hard times and asks Mark if he can crash at Mar's place for a few weeks.
intention: Mark wants to continue living alone.
moral_action: Mark tells Justin he can't let him stay at Mark's place, but offers to put in up in a hotel for a few weeks.
moral_consequence: Justin really appreciates the help, and uses the time effectively to get his life back together.
immoral_action: Mark tells Justin he can't let him stay at Mark's place right now but wishes him good luck.
immoral_consequence: Justin remains homeless and suffers living on the streets in desperation.

norm: It's wrong to verbally abuse your mother.
situation: Steve is not happy with his mother asking him to do so many chores.
intention: Steve wants to express anger at his mother.
moral_action: Steve asks his mom to talk and explains how he feels that the amount of work is unfair.
moral_consequence: Steves mother listens, understands and gives him the option of less chores or a raised allowance.
immoral_action: Steve swears at his mother and calls her stupid.
immoral_consequence: Steve is further punished by his mother and grounded for a week.

norm: It's bad to work for a company that's hated.
situation: Anna gets a well paying job offer from Facebook, a company all of her friends hate for its manipulative policies.
intention: Anna wants to have a prestigious job and make a lot of money.
moral_action: Anna rejects the job offer and keeps applying to other prestigious jobs.
moral_consequence: Anna is stressed out with job seeking for a while, but eventually finds a good job at a company she likes.
immoral_action: Anna accepts the job offer and works for Facebook.
immoral_consequence: Anna makes a lot of money and her friends are mad at her.

norm: Open relationships can be hurtful to your partner.
situation: Natasha, who is in an open relationship with her partner that was entirely her decision, is out on a date with somebody else.
intention: Natasha wants to indulge herself.
moral_action: Natasha calls to check in on her partner while on her date and her partner confesses that he does not like the idea of an open relationship.
moral_consequence: Natasha goes home and has a long discussion with her partner, and they agree to separate amicably.
immoral_action: Natasha stays out all night with her date and doesn't call home to let her partner know because of her imposed open relationship.
immoral_consequence: Natasha's partner feels neglected and the couple go through a complicated break up.

norm: It's wrong to throw away someone else's property.
situation: Cal was cleaning the house, and he stumbled over his friend's shoes.
intention: Cal wants the shoes out of the way.
moral_action: Cal takes the shoes and puts them at the door for his friend.
moral_consequence: Cal's friend tells him thank you for putting the shoes aside for him.
immoral_action: Cal takes the shoes and throws them in the garbage bin outside.
immoral_consequence: Cal's friend makes him pay for the shoes that he threw away.

norm: You're expected to respect other people's comfort.
situation: Carlos is flying in economy class on a cross-country plane trip and is sitting in front of a tall man.
intention: Carlos wants to have a more comfortable plane ride.
moral_action: Carlos brings a special neck pillow and eye mask to use during the flight.
moral_consequence: Carlos and his neighbors all complete their flight with minimal discomfort caused by others.
immoral_action: Carlos reclines his seat back, so he can lay backwards comfortably.
immoral_consequence: Carlos gets in the space of the man behind him and causes him to have a cramped and uncomfortable flight.

norm: You shouldn't offend people.
situation: It is amateur comedy night at a local night club.
intention: Jo wants to win the audience members over with her jokes.
moral_action: Jo made a joke mocking ableist attitudes towards those with disabilities.
moral_consequence: More than a few audience members bought her comedy CD on the way out.
immoral_action: Jo told a joke mocking disabled people's struggles.
immoral_consequence: Some of the audience members got up and left the show.

norm: It's good to be tolerant of animals.
situation: Noah's kids have been asking for a new pet.
intention: Noah wants to purchase a new pet for his children.
moral_action: Noah allows the cat to roam the house on the condition that his kids bathe it weekly.
moral_consequence: Noah, his kids, and the cat live in harmony.
immoral_action: Noah gets a new cat for his kids, but keeps it in the basement because he doesn't like the way it smells.
immoral_consequence: The cat becomes depressed and isn't receptive to the kids.

norm: It is wrong to lie to your kids.
situation: Mark was at a friend's BBQ instead of going to his daughter's recital and was confronted by his daughter.
intention: Mark wants to respond to his daughter.
moral_action: Mark states how he was catching up with a friend at a BBQ and apologizes.
moral_consequence: Mark's daughter is initially disappointed with Mark but eventually forgives him.
immoral_action: Mark tells his daughter that he was busy at work and could not come to her recital.
immoral_consequence: Mark's daughter finds out that Mark was lying and starts caring less about Mark.

norm: It's good to speak to your neighbors about problems.
situation: Sonya's downstairs neighbor watches TV late into the night at a loud volume.
intention: Sonya wants a quieter residence at night.
moral_action: Sonya knocks on Rudy's door and lets him know that his TV is too loud late at night.
moral_consequence: Rudy apologizes and offers to wear headphones after 10PM resolving the situation.
immoral_action: Sonya complains to the apartment for three nights in a row without ever expressing concern to Rudy.
immoral_consequence: The apartment threatens to evict Rudy, leading to a tense relationship between Sonya and Rudy.

norm: People should be friendly with their neighbors.
situation: Nick has a lawn mower and his neighbor wants to borrow the mower for a price.
intention: Nick wants to let him borrow the mower.
moral_action: Nick lets his neighbor use the mower for free.
moral_consequence: Nick's neighbor lets Nick borrow things for free in return.
immoral_action: Nick agrees and charges his neighbor $15/hr to use the mower.
immoral_consequence: Nick's neighbor feels ripped-off and never invites Nick for events.

norm: It's not okay to want someone else's death.
situation: Sarah’s boyfriend just broke up with her after dating for three years.
intention: Sarah wants to get revenge on her ex boyfriend.
moral_action: Sarah decides to call her ex boyfriend and cuss him out.
moral_consequence: Sarah feels much better after getting all of the built up anger out.
immoral_action: Sarah buys a book of magic spells and recites a spell that is supposed to kill whoever she is thinking about.
immoral_consequence: Sarah’s ex boyfriend coincidentally gets in a bad car wreck that night and Sarah feels absolutely terrible for doing what she did.

norm: Buying a small gift for someone you love it thoughtful.
situation: Janice is returning home from a vacation in Hawaii, and her kids, Cathy and James, are waiting for her arrival and hoping for a present.
intention: Janice wants to show Cathy and James she missed them.
moral_action: Janice brings the kids each a Hawaiian Lei, so they could get a small taste of the island.
moral_consequence: The kids feel like Janice truly missed them while she was away and are happy with the present.
immoral_action: Janice come in empty handed, gives the kids a big hug and tells them she's glad to see them.
immoral_consequence: The kids are disappointed Janice didn't bring back a souvenir, and feel like she didn't really think of them much.

norm: It's bad to end a relationship for an irrational reason.
situation: Brandon notices his girlfriend Carla talking to another boy and having a good time.
intention: Brandon wants to address this with Carla.
moral_action: Brandon nonchalantly asks Carla about the boy she was talking to.
moral_consequence: Brandon finds out that the boy is Carla's cousin and is happy he didn't overreact.
immoral_action: Brandon accuses Carla of not being faithful to him and breaks up with her.
immoral_consequence: Brandon later feels regret when he discovers the other boy is Carla's cousin.

norm: It's wrong steal something from a store.
situation: Christine is at the mall when she remembers she has a work dinner coming up.
intention: Christine wants to find a nice dress to wear to her work dinner.
moral_action: Christine shops around until she finds a dress that is within her budget.
moral_consequence: Christine doesn't spend too much on the dress and is prepared for her work dinner.
immoral_action: Christine spots a dress she likes that is out of her budget, so she tosses it into her purse when shop employees aren't looking.
immoral_consequence: The security tag on the dress sounds the alarm as Christine tries to leave the store, and she is arrested.

norm: It's wrong to pick on other people
situation: Kyle, who is paralyzed in a wheelchair is at his first day of high school, and Jason see's him wheeling up.
intention: Jason wants to say something to Kyle.
moral_action: Jason introduces himself to Kyle and offers to show him around the campus.
moral_consequence: Kyle hits it off with Jason and feels good having made a new friend on his first day.
immoral_action: Jason approaches Kyle and sarcastically says, you can hide, but you can't run.
immoral_consequence: Kyle's feelings are hurt because he wanted to make friends on his first day, but was made fun of instead.

norm: You shouldn't give away your partner's dog.
situation: Winnie's boyfriend has gotten a new puppy that stays in the house.
intention: Winnie wants to keep the house free of puppy pee.
moral_action: Winnie starts to house train her boyfriend's new puppy for him.
moral_consequence: The puppy learns to not pee or poop in the house on Winnie's floor.
immoral_action: Winnie gives the dog away when her boyfriend is out at work.
immoral_consequence: Winnie's boyfriend gets in an argument with her and breaks up with her.

norm: People shouldn't abuse their positions of power.
situation: Jim is an auditor with the IRS and his friend John gets a tax bill that has him worried.
intention: Jim wants to soothe John.
moral_action: Jim tells John not to worry that he can get all his answers from the IRS guides available to the public and to just breathe.
moral_consequence: John feels a little better knowing there's some literature he can read on the matter and educate himself.
immoral_action: Jim tells John not to worry about it, he'll go into work Monday and erase the problem from Jim's file.
immoral_consequence: John thinks that Jim is unscrupulous and doesn't want to get involved in a corruption scheme with Jim.

norm: It's wrong to expect kids to pay for things.
situation: Rick is driving back home with his son who wants to stop to get fast food as a treat.
intention: Rick wants to teach his son responsibility.
moral_action: Rick gets his son the fast food under the condition that he gets an A on an upcoming test.
moral_consequence: The son is encouraged to keep his grades up in school to get rewards.
immoral_action: Rick stops to get fast food but makes his son use his allowance to buy his own food.
immoral_consequence: The son will feel like his father is not being fair.

norm: You shouldn't disobey your partner's parents.
situation: Mark and Natalie have been dating for a while but Natalie's parents don't allow her to stay at his house.
intention: Mark wants to take Natalie on a weekend trip.
moral_action: Mark talks to Natalie's parents and asks for their permission to take Natalie, and they agree with a few stipulations.
moral_consequence: Natalie's parents are happy that their daughter is dating such a respectable person.
immoral_action: Mark tells Natalie not to tell her parents about the trip, and that they will deal with them when they get back.
immoral_consequence: Natalie's parents are very upset when they don't know where Natalie is.

norm: It's wrong to give your parents ultimatums.
situation: Charlie has siblings and is arguing with his parents about cleaning his room, which he does not want to do.
intention: Charlie wants to avoid cleaning his room.
moral_action: Charlie bribes one of his siblings to clean his room for him, in exchange for a nice toy.
moral_consequence: The sibling is happy with the toy, the parents are happy for a clean room, and Charlie is happy to avoid cleaning it.
immoral_action: Charlie tells his parents to let him go without cleaning or else he will trash the house.
immoral_consequence: Charlie's parents exert their authority and ground Charlie for a month.

norm: You shouldn't snoop around your child's things.
situation: Jack is suspicious that his son is hiding some porn magazines in his room.
intention: Jack wants to figure out what his son is hiding.
moral_action: Jack confronts his son calmly and asks him if he is hiding the magzines.
moral_consequence: Jack's son is honest with him and their relationship improves as a result.
immoral_action: Jack snoops around his son's room when he is at school.
immoral_consequence: Jack violates in son's trust and privacy, and his son is mad at him.

norm: You shouldn't call the cops on a friend.
situation: John and Jim are leaving a party and Jim is very drunk and wants to drive himself home.
intention: John wants to keep Jim from hurting himself.
moral_action: John convinces Jim to ride home in John's car instead, saying it isn't safe for Jim to drive.
moral_consequence: Jim appreciates John looking out for Jim's best interest and vows to return the favor sometime.
immoral_action: John calls the cops as Jim is getting in the car and tells them there's a drunk driver in the area.
immoral_consequence: The cops stop Jim and take him into custody, and Jim is furious at John when he finds out it was him who called them.

norm: Telling someone to mind their own business can be rude.
situation: Steve is sitting down at the cafeteria lunch table and a fellow student Fred asks him what he brought for lunch.
intention: Steve wants to respond to Fred's inquiry.
moral_action: Steve tells Fred that his mother packed him a sandwich, carrots, grapes and a cookie.
moral_consequence: Fred is happy to hear the answer and continues to chat with Steve while enjoying his lunch.
immoral_action: Steve tells Fred to buzz off and mind his own business.
immoral_consequence: Fred's feelings are hurt, and he goes to sit at another lunch table.

norm: It's expected that you spend the holidays with family.
situation: Henry's mother calls him up on the telephone and asks him if he's coming over to her place for Christmas.
intention: Henry wants to answer his mother's question.
moral_action: Henry tells his mother that he'll be there and that he can't wait to see everyone.
moral_consequence: Henry's mother is warmed at the thought of the whole family being together for Christmas.
immoral_action: Henry tells his mother that he's not coming because he wants to find a woman to spend the night with.
immoral_consequence: Henry's mother is shocked and insulted that Henry would prioritize sex over his family.

norm: It's expected that you will keep your yard looking nice.
situation: Zachery has a lawn that has become overgrown because he is too occupied with work, and he has the weekend off of work.
intention: Zachery wants to rest on his days off.
moral_action: Zachery hires a landscaping company to maintain his yard.
moral_consequence: Zachery's neighbors are relieved that he's finally maintained his outside space.
immoral_action: Zachery ignores his lawn situation and relaxes during his weekend break.
immoral_consequence: Zachery's lawn grows out more and his neighbors think he is lazy because he has not taken care of his lawn.

norm: It's rude to spray someone with a hose.
situation: Lily is cleaning off her sidewalk in the summer time.
intention: Lily wants to get all the dirt off her sidewalk to make it look nice.
moral_action: Lily stops spraying when she sees a stranger walk by.
moral_consequence: Lily and the stranger exchange pleasantries and both smile and get along with their day.
immoral_action: When a stranger walks by lily doesn’t stop using the hose and sprays the stranger with water.
immoral_consequence: The stranger gets upset and wants to get into a fight.

norm: It's rude to leave your dirty laundry laying around.
situation: Max walks home from the gym, and he has to be at work in thirty minutes.
intention: Max wants to be at work on time.
moral_action: Max goes into work and changes into the spare work uniform in his office.
moral_consequence: Max is able to make good progress on his work before everyone arrives.
immoral_action: Max leaves his dirty gym clothes on the floor after he changes.
immoral_consequence: Max is scolded by his roommate for leaving his belongings on the floor.

norm: One should not be rude to their parents.
situation: Carla's mother had asked her to do the dishes before she went out on her date.
intention: Carla wants to go on her date.
moral_action: Carla does all the dishes and tells her mother goodbye before leaving on her date.
moral_consequence: Carla's mother tells her goodbye and gives her twenty dollars to spend when she goes out.
immoral_action: Carla rolls her eyes and runs out the house to meet her date.
immoral_consequence: Carla's mother meets her at the door when she returns and grounds her for a week.

norm: You shouldn't hurt animals if you love them.
situation: Erin's cat is scratching up a couch that has sentimental value to her.
intention: Erin wants to stop the cat's behavior.
moral_action: Erin squirts her cat with a water gun.
moral_consequence: Erin's cat is temporarily startled and learns not to scratch the furniture.
immoral_action: Erin hits her cat in order to strongly deter this behavior.
immoral_consequence: Erin's cat loses trust in her and feels unsafe.

norm: You shouldn't exclude your fiance's family from important events.
situation: Riley and Janet are about to get married so Janet is planning the wedding and asks Riley where they should seat Janet's parents.
intention: Riley wants to respond to Janet's question.
moral_action: Riley tells Janet that the parents should be seated with his parents, so they can mingle together.
moral_consequence: Janet thinks that Riley's idea is brilliant and looks forward to the parents getting to know each other.
immoral_action: Riley tells Janet that he'd rather that her parents don't come at all since he doesn't like them.
immoral_consequence: Janet is shocked that Riley would try to exclude her parents from their wedding and starts to have doubts about marrying him.

norm: It's good to fill in for coworkers that need help.
situation: Percy has a co-worker in his company that is sick and is missing work.
intention: Percy wants to respond to his co-worker's absence.
moral_action: Percy tells his co-worker he will do their work for them since they are sick.
moral_consequence: The company will be able to maintain pace as work is done.
immoral_action: Percy tells his co-worker that they will need to catch up with their work when they are better.
immoral_consequence: The company will be off schedule because of the missed work.

norm: It is nice to give gifts to friends.
situation: Thomas' best friend Richard invited him to his birthday party.
intention: Thomas wants to save his money.
moral_action: Thomas spends a little within his budget on a gift for Richard and saves the rest.
moral_consequence: Richard is happy to get a gift and feels closer to Thomas.
immoral_action: Thomas goes to the birthday party empty-handed and then leaves.
immoral_consequence: Richard is sad and wonders if Thomas really likes him.

norm: It's wrong to steal things from other people.
situation: Nathan is visiting a friend, and his friend shows him a really cool video game that he got recently.
intention: Nathan wants to get a copy of the game for himself.
moral_action: Nathan goes to the store on the way home and picks up a copy of the game.
moral_consequence: Nathan's friend is excited that he got the game and wants to play it with him online.
immoral_action: Nathan tucks the video game into his jacket right before he leaves his friend's house and takes it home without asking.
immoral_consequence: Nathan's friend finds out and gets angry at him for taking the game.

norm: People might think you're cruel for abandoning a puppy.
situation: Theo realizes that his new puppy is too much for him to handle.
intention: Theo wants to get rid of the puppy.
moral_action: Theo puts an ad online and finds someone that takes the puppy.
moral_consequence: Theo is seen as admirable for finding the puppy a good home.
immoral_action: Theo takes the puppy to a busy street corner and leaves it on the curb.
immoral_consequence: Theo is seen as an awful person for leaving the puppy on the side of the road.

norm: It is unhealthy to stay in stressful situations.
situation: Bo is at a big party and see's his ex-girlfriend flirting with all his friends.
intention: Bo wants to stay at the party.
moral_action: Bo ignores his ex, and asks another woman to dance with him.
moral_consequence: Bo enjoys himself and is no longer concerned with what his ex is doing.
immoral_action: Bo approaches his ex and starts yelling that what she's doing is wrong.
immoral_consequence: Bo makes a spectacle of himself and feels embarrassed.

norm: It's rude to overstay your welcome.
situation: Josh is a guest at Jimmy's house.
intention: Josh wants to be entertained.
moral_action: Josh decides to go home when night falls and play some videogames.
moral_consequence: Jimmy appreciates being able to get a full night's sleep.
immoral_action: Josh lies down on Jimmy's couch and starts watching TV late into the night.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy stays up late to keep his guest company, and is late for work the following day.

norm: It's discouraged to always be silly.
situation: Mike is a comedian who likes to make people smile, and he's about to make a speech at his uncle's funeral.
intention: Mike wants his speech to be memorable.
moral_action: Mike tells a story about his uncle's life and accomplishments accompanied by a note about how much his uncle enriched his life.
moral_consequence: Mike is complimented after the funeral by his aunt for his speech.
immoral_action: Mike strings together a series of jokes about his uncle's personality as a tribute of sorts.
immoral_consequence: Mike asked to leave the stage when the crowd becomes tired of his antics.

norm: It's wrong to relieve yourself in public.
situation: Alex had been drinking cans of soda all throughout the day.
intention: Alex wanted to urinate.
moral_action: Alex went to the port o potty in the middle of the public park.
moral_consequence: Alex felt much better after he had finished relieving himself.
immoral_action: Alex pulled his pants down and urinated in the bushes at the public park.
immoral_consequence: Alex was arrested for indecent exposure in the town park.

norm: It's wrong to call people out over petty things.
situation: Tom and Dan run an unprofitable store and are having a meeting about what needs to change.
intention: Tom wants to tell Dan something he wants Dan to do differently at the store.
moral_action: Tom tells Dan that Dan needs to analyze sales data to determine which products are making money and which aren't.
moral_consequence: Dan looks at the sales data and discovers that they can eliminate some items they stock that are losing them money.
immoral_action: Tom tells Dan that he should press the buttons on the cash register less firmly to make less noise.
immoral_consequence: Dan doesn't think Tom is taking the meeting seriously and walks out of the store.

norm: It's not okay to make a mess for others.
situation: Jill makes a mess all over the room while she's playing with her toys.
intention: Jill wants to decide what to do next.
moral_action: Jill cleans up the mess herself before going to do another acctivity.
moral_consequence: The room is clean once she's finished and everyone is satisfied with the clean room.
immoral_action: Jill puts her toys away but leaves the mess; without her toys it appears as though one of her siblings was responsible.
immoral_consequence: Jill's siblings have to clean up the mess, and they are upset about it.

norm: It is wrong to kick someone out of a group.
situation: Harry is the leader of a gaming clan and one of the older members is causing problems with many of the others.
intention: Harry wants to keep the peace in his clan.
moral_action: Harry gives the member a warning and instructs him to change his behavior.
moral_consequence: The member is given another chance and chooses differently next time.
immoral_action: Harry kicks out the member who seems to be causing all the trouble.
immoral_consequence: The member suffers because the membership meant a lot to him.

norm: You should not comment on someone's weight.
situation: Teri and Susan are talking at work when Susan asks Teri what she thinks of her office neighbor Leah.
intention: Teri wants to answer Susan's question.
moral_action: Teri tells Susan that Leah seems alright, but she wishes Leah would talk to her more.
moral_consequence: Susan is happy that Teri agrees Leah is decent and hopes Teri gets to know her more.
immoral_action: Teri tells Susan that Leah is really chubby so Teri is having a hard time taking her seriously.
immoral_consequence: Susan thinks that Teri is extremely shallow and starts to wonder why she's friends with Teri.

norm: It's encouraged to resolve conflicts amicably.
situation: Basil is about to park at the mall when Austin drives into his parking spot.
intention: Basil wants to react to having his spot snatched.
moral_action: Basil gets out of his car and tells Austin that he was there first and Austin should really let him park there.
moral_consequence: Austin apologizes and says he didn't see Basil and agrees to give up the spot for him.
immoral_action: Basil gets out of his car and tells Austin that he should probably wipe the floor with him for being so rude.
immoral_consequence: Austin is terrified that Basil will get violent with him and locks himself in his car.

norm: It's good to comfort people who have lost someone.
situation: Chris and Bobby were playing in Chris's tree house when Bobby suddenly bursts into tears, saying how his grandmother died last night.
intention: Chris wants to get Bobby to stop crying.
moral_action: Chris tells Bobby that it’s ok to be sad and cry, and that he can always come over to play in the tree house when he feels sad.
moral_consequence: Bobby feels better about missing his grandma, and he thanks Chris for being nice.
immoral_action: Chris tells Bobby only girls cry when they are sad and to not be sad because she was old and sick anyway.
immoral_consequence: Bobby develops issues with being sad and crying that he later in life through therapy traces back to his childhood friend Chris.

norm: You should be able to adapt to change.
situation: Jeff is the CEO of a struggling company, and others are urging him to modernize the company.
intention: Jeff wants to make a decision on what to do with the company.
moral_action: Jeff decides to make sure that everything with the company is up-to-date.
moral_consequence: Jeff's company begins to grow again, and they're able to hire even more employees.
immoral_action: Jeff decides to stick to what he knows, so he doesn't want to modernize.
immoral_consequence: Jeff's company suffers, and many people have to lose their jobs to make up for it.

norm: You shouldn't disrespect someone's wife.
situation: Anthony is upset at Shawn's wife because she has been rude to him lately.
intention: Anthony wants to do something about it.
moral_action: Anthony tells Shawn's wife that he doesn't want to fight with her, and that he wants to get along.
moral_consequence: Shawn overhears this and pressures his wife to dial it back.
immoral_action: The next time Shawn's wife slights him, Anthony calls her a slur.
immoral_consequence: Shawn gets very upset with Anthony, and their friendship ends over it.

norm: You shouldn't tell a child that you don't want them.
situation: Star is having a rough day with her son being out of control.
intention: Star wants to punish her child.
moral_action: Star puts her son in time out while she cools her temper.
moral_consequence: Star's son calms down and apologizes for misbehaving.
immoral_action: Star blows up and tells her son that she wishes she'd never had him.
immoral_consequence: Star's son runs to his room sobbing and refuses to talk to her for days.

norm: It is wrong to cause people to become homeless
situation: Ron's rent is due in a few days and his roommate Tim has yet to pay his share of the rent because he is experiencing financial hardship.
intention: Ron wants to pay the rent on time.
moral_action: Ron uses some spare money to pay Tim's share of the rent for the upcoming month.
moral_consequence: Tim is grateful to Ron and pays him back a couple months later.
immoral_action: Ron kicks Tim out of their apartment to find a new roommate who has plenty of money for rent.
immoral_consequence: Tim has nowhere to stay and becomes homeless.

norm: It's good to keep one's property looking presentable.
situation: Hank is a propane salesman who is preparing to host a barbecue at his house for all of the employees at his workplace this weekend.
intention: Hank wants to impress his supervisor at the barbecue.
moral_action: Hank carefully mows his yard and tends to his landscaping before the barbecue since he knows that everyone will be looking at.
moral_consequence: Hank's boss is impressed by his yard, but thinks the food is just okay.
immoral_action: Hank buys a new propane grill and an impression selection of meat, but forgets to mow his lawn.
immoral_consequence: Hank's boss likes the food, but views Hank negatively due to his unkempt yard.

norm: You should help out people that are sick.
situation: John's roommate, Hope, is stuck in bed with the flu and hasn't been able to get out of the house.
intention: John wants to react to react to Hope.
moral_action: John goes to the store to pick up some food for Hope, to get her through until she feels better.
moral_consequence: Hope sees John as a thoughtful roommate, and is glad to have him around.
immoral_action: John tells Hope that he prays she gets better soon, so she can get herself to the store.
immoral_consequence: Hope now see's John as selfish with his time, and regrets having him as a roommate.

norm: You shouldn't fake your depression just to get sympathy.
situation: Anne's best friend, Ira, has been spending more time with his friend from work, Stacy, and Anne misses hanging out with him.
intention: Anne wants to get Ira's attention.
moral_action: Anne tells Ira she misses doing things with him, so he makes plans with her later that evening.
moral_consequence: Ira came to realize while spending time with Anne how much he missed her company as well.
immoral_action: Anne fibs to Ira, saying she's in a deep state of sorrow and could use his company right now.
immoral_consequence: Ira comes over, but soon sees that Anne isn't really sad, and now looks at her in a negative light for lying.

norm: You shouldn't sell someone's belongings without asking first.
situation: Hiroki plays a game with a friend, who trusts Hiroki with his account password and who has some extra items lying around.
intention: Hiroki wants to get some in-game money.
moral_action: Hiroki asks if his friend could lend him some in-game money.
moral_consequence: Hiroki's friend lends him the money he wants to buy a nice item.
immoral_action: Hiroki logs on to the friend's gaming account and sells some little-used items, then transfers the money to himself.
immoral_consequence: Hiroki's friend get upset as he had been saving those items to trade with others.

norm: It's rude to play music over people talking.
situation: Charlie is playing a game on his phone while his parents are chatting on the couch.
intention: Charlie wants to listen to some music.
moral_action: Charlie grabs his earbuds, connects them to the phone, and plays music he can only hear.
moral_consequence: Charlie’s parents continue talking without being interrupted.
immoral_action: Charlie walks over to the stereo and plays a rock song on full blast.
immoral_consequence: Charlie’s parents make him turn it off, and they lecture him on how disrespectful he was.

norm: It is sanitary to wash your hands before eating food.
situation: Jared works at a hospital.
intention: Jared wants to go on his lunch break.
moral_action: Jared washes his hands thoroughly before eating his lunch.
moral_consequence: Jared doesn't get sick and is able to care for more patients.
immoral_action: Jared doesn't wash his hands before eating his lunch.
immoral_consequence: Jared gets the coronavirus and unknowingly passes it to his patients.

norm: It's bad to pollute.
situation: Roger has a lot of empty bottles that he needs to get out of his car to make free space.
intention: Roger wants to get rid of the empty bottles.
moral_action: Roger drives to the nearest recycling bin and puts the bottles in it.
moral_consequence: Roger's car is free of the bottles and now he has free space.
immoral_action: Roger throws the empty bottles out of his window while he is driving.
immoral_consequence: Roger gets a ticket from a police officer who sees him.

norm: It's accepting to treat unconventional couplings with grace.
situation: Frank's best-friend Peter just came out of the closet to him and wants him to meet his boyfriend.
intention: Frank wants to respond to Peter's request.
moral_action: Frank puts aside any discomfort and agrees to meet Frank's boyfriend.
moral_consequence: Frank is able to be there for his friend by being open and accepting.
immoral_action: Frank is uncomfortable and so refuses to meet Peter's boyfriend.
immoral_consequence: Frank's inability to adjust to Peter's revelation causes a rift between them.

norm: You shouldn't let your friend copy your paper.
situation: Kim is taking a test and notices that her friend is having a hard time.
intention: Kim wants to help her friend do well in the class.
moral_action: After the test, Kim offers to help her friend study for the next exam.
moral_consequence: Kim's friend works hard studying with Kim and is able to raise her grade in the class.
immoral_action: Kim scoots her paper to the edge of her desk so her friend can copy it.
immoral_consequence: Both Kim and her friend get caught and receive a 0 on the test.

norm: It's bad to be overly reactive to things.
situation: Maria is stressed at work when she spills a gallon of milk before she can put it in the refrigerator.
intention: Mary wants to express her emotions.
moral_action: Mary closes her eyes taking a moment to collect herself before asking a friend to help her, and she vents her problems to her friend.
moral_consequence: Mary becomes better friends with her coworker.
immoral_action: Mary shouts loudly and walks away leaving the janitor to clean up after her.
immoral_consequence: Mary gets written up at work for disorderly behavior.

norm: It's bad to want someone to help you get drugs.
situation: Gary is hanging out with one of his friends after school in his parents' basement.
intention: Gary wants to try marijuana.
moral_action: Gary talks with his friend about marijuana for the rest of the afternoon before deciding to seek out a source himself.
moral_consequence: Gary's friend isn't aware that Gary bought marijuana and is happy with their friendship.
immoral_action: Gary asks his friend if he can help get him some marijuana.
immoral_consequence: Gary's friend feels nervous, but he helps find a drug dealer and buys marijuana for the two of them.

norm: Littering is a bad thing
situation: Mike parked his car in the park where he ate his fast food lunch.
intention: Mike wants to get rid of his trash.
moral_action: Mike gathers his trash and walks to the trash can to throw it away.
moral_consequence: Visitors to the park are pleased with how well maintained the park looks.
immoral_action: Mike rolls down his window and throws his wrappers on the ground as he drives away.
immoral_consequence: Visitors that arrive to the park after Mike think the park looks unkempt.

norm: It's rude to cheat in video games.
situation: Billy is off from work and wants to unwind playing some of his favorite video games.
intention: Billy wants to have fun competing against other players.
moral_action: Billy plays fair and square, winning with only his skills.
moral_consequence: His opponents lose but despite that enjoyed such a competitive match.
immoral_action: Billy uses hacking tools to unfairly defeat his opponents.
immoral_consequence: His opponents are upset because Billy is obviously cheating.

norm: It's good to be grateful for things.
situation: Kevin is at John's wedding and gives him an envelope full of cash as a gift.
intention: John wants to respond to Kevin's gift.
moral_action: John thanks Kevin and tells him he didn't have to give him such a generous gift.
moral_consequence: Kevin feels good that John is happy and is delighted to see his friend full of joy.
immoral_action: John tells Kevin that he thought Kevin would give him more than that and throws the envelope into a pile of gifts.
immoral_consequence: Kevin is saddened that John is unappreciative and is embarrassed that his gift wans't good enough.

norm: It's good to maintain your property.
situation: John's grass has been neglected and is growing very tall looking entirely unkempt.
intention: John wants to rest after a long day of work.
moral_action: John pays a neighbor's son to mow his lawn for him.
moral_consequence: John gets to rest and his yard looks much better.
immoral_action: John ignores the lawn care duties and puts it off for another day.
immoral_consequence: John has more work to complete on another day and his yard looks terrible.

norm: It's embarrassing to throw up in public.
situation: Phil ate some bad oysters and feels a rumbling in his stomach that makes him feel sick.
intention: Phil wants to relieve his upset stomach somewhere.
moral_action: Phil goes to a bathroom to throw up his stomach contents in a toilet.
moral_consequence: People will not find Phil disgusting.
immoral_action: Phil goes to a park to throw up his stomach contents on the ground.
immoral_consequence: People at the park will be disgusted by Phil.

norm: It's wrong to be noisy around your roommates.
situation: Patrick has a few friends over at the apartment he shares with Phil.
intention: Patrick wants to entertain his guests.
moral_action: Patrick and his friends go into his bedroom to hang out and listen to music quietly.
moral_consequence: Patrick has a great time with his friends and Phil is happy to have them back in the future.
immoral_action: Patrick puts on a movie in the living room at full volume for his friends.
immoral_consequence: Patrick and his friends enjoy the movie, but Phil is angry with him afterwards for being inconsiderate about the nosie.

norm: It's important to support LGBT friends.
situation: Hank is at home watching TV when his gay friend Lou calls him and asks him to come to a pride event.
intention: Hank wants to answer Lou's request.
moral_action: Hank tells Lou that he would be glad to come and asks where they should meet.
moral_consequence: Lou is delighted that his friend is supportive and will come to the event.
immoral_action: Hank tells Lou that he doesn't really want to be seen in that crowd, and he won't come.
immoral_consequence: "Lou is insulted that ""the crowd"" is not good enough for Lou and that he's insinuating they're a lesser people."

norm: It's bad to let a pet run loose without supervision.
situation: Joe just adopted a rabbit and loves it very much.
intention: Joe wants his rabbit to have fun in the yard.
moral_action: Joe puts nets up above his yard and watches his rabbit play in the yard.
moral_consequence: Joe's rabbit lives a happy life and Joe enjoys watching him.
immoral_action: Joe leaves his rabbit outside in his yard with free reign and leaves to go shopoping.
immoral_consequence: A bird sees the rabbit and kills it and Joe is saddened.

norm: Behaviour that causes other people discomfort is considered wrong.
situation: Sandra, who speaks Spanish, is out with some friends at a restaurant, including some others that speak Spanish.
intention: Sandra wants to talk with her friends.
moral_action: Sandra talks in a language that everyone understands and involves them in conversation.
moral_consequence: All of her friends join in and have a great and memorable conversation during their meal.
immoral_action: Sandra talks in Spanish with the friends that speak Spanish, enjoying a lively conversation.
immoral_consequence: The other friends feel left out and become both suspicious and jealous of Sandra.

norm: You shouldn't have to listen to everyone's problems.
situation: Randy has had an exhausting day at work when his friend Rick calls to whine, as Rick does almost daily.
intention: Randy wants to respond to Rick's incessant whining.
moral_action: Randy tells Rick that he needs to seek professional help and to stop calling him to whine about nonsense so frequently.
moral_consequence: Rick learns that it's taxing to your friends to hear you complain constantly and vows to improve his attitude.
immoral_action: Randy tells Rick to go on and tell him all about what is causing him an issue that day.
immoral_consequence: Rick continues to bother Randy almost daily with phone calls that are just long, depressing mopes about nothing.

norm: You shouldn't insult your friends.
situation: John notices that his friend Bill is gaining a lot of weight lately.
intention: John wants to tell Bill to lose weight.
moral_action: John tells Bill that he's concerned about Bill's health and wants to see him lose weight and offers to help Bill in doing so.
moral_consequence: Bill is momentarily self conscious but is overall really happy to see his friend take an interest in his health and offer support.
immoral_action: John tells Bill that he has to stop eating like a pig and take care of his bloated body.
immoral_consequence: Bill withers away in shame and embarrassment and begins to cry.

norm: You shouldn't pretend you like someone.
situation: Ray is jealous when his ex girlfriend goes to prom with one of his football teammates.
intention: Ray wants to have a good time at prom.
moral_action: Ray goes to prom with his single friends and ignores his ex.
moral_consequence: Ray enjoys prom night with his friends.
immoral_action: Ray asks Beth, a girl his ex doesn't like, to prom with the intention of getting under her skin.
immoral_consequence: Beth sees Ray is distracted by his ex and feels as though she's been used.

norm: It' rude to hide people's property from them.
situation: Sam's sister Tammy asks him where her Gameboy is.
intention: Sam wants to respond to Tammy's question.
moral_action: Sam retrieves the Gameboy from his room and hands it to her.
moral_consequence: Tammy is happy to have her Gameboy back.
immoral_action: Sam tells Tammy he doesn't know where the Gameboy is, while he hides it in his room, so he can play it.
immoral_consequence: Tammy is upset thinking that she has lost her Gameboy.

norm: It's rude to judge someone who hasn't seen Blade Runner.
situation: Chris is talking with a group of his friends about different movies the they've seen.
intention: Chris wants to find out who has seen Blade Runner.
moral_action: When Chris finds out one of his friends hasn't seen Blade Runner, he invites her over to his house for a movie night.
moral_consequence: Chris and his friend share a fun evening together watching films.
immoral_action: When his friend says he's never seen Blade Runner, Chris makes fun of him.
immoral_consequence: Chris is admonished by his friends for his rude behavior.

norm: You should help people out when they feel ill.
situation: Becky gets sick unexpectedly and needs Bill's help to finish the work assignment.
intention: Bill wants to help Becky with her work assignment so that she is able to keep her job.
moral_action: Bill finishes the project promptly and returns it to Becky before the next morning.
moral_consequence: Bill helps Becky so that she does not get in trouble with her boss.
immoral_action: Bill finishes up the project and tells his boss how much he had to help Becky.
immoral_consequence: Bill makes Becky appear as if she has not helped much on the work assignment.

norm: It's important to think about how your actions affect others
situation: Stan and his brother, Joe, are moving a heavy couch into Joe's apartment.
intention: Stan wants to finish moving the couch.
moral_action: Stan coordinates with Joe to lower the couch gently.
moral_consequence: The couch is in place, and Joe thanks Stan with a beer.
immoral_action: Stan lets go of the couch without warning Joe first.
immoral_consequence: The leg on the couch breaks, and Joe is very angry with Stan and makes him pay for the repair.

norm: It's rude to point out someone's lack of friendships.
situation: Phil notices that he has way more friends than Jane does.
intention: Phil wants to decide if he should say something to Jane.
moral_action: Phil is curious why Jane has fewer friends but decide it would be rude to pont it out.
moral_consequence: When Phil pays more attention he notices that some people seem to have 100 friends and others nearly none.
immoral_action: Phil makes fun of Jane for having less friends than him.
immoral_consequence: Phil's friends point out that that was hurtful of Phil to say.

norm: There is no need to be mean with your siblings.
situation: Janet goes to her brother Joe's room to ask him if he thinks her shoes go with her dress.
intention: Joe wants to answer Janet's question.
moral_action: Joe tells Janet that they do go together and that she looks great.
moral_consequence: Janet is delighted that her brother helped her choose her outfit and that he's so complimentary toward her.
immoral_action: Joe tells Janet that everything on her looks hideous and that she shouldn't bother trying.
immoral_consequence: Janet is hurt and embarrassed and feels self conscious so she begins to cry.

norm: It's good to practice sports with others.
situation: Bobby has just made it onto the high school basketball team.
intention: Bobby wants to sharpen his basketball skills.
moral_action: Bobby practices with a group of his friends who shoot the ball around together.
moral_consequence: Bobby's friends are amazed when they see him make the long distance shots.
immoral_action: Bobby practices by himself on the basketball court and makes a few baskets from half court.
immoral_consequence: Bobby tells his friends, and they just think that he's making it up.

norm: You should mind your own business sometimes.
situation: Mitt is walking down the street when he sees a group of people, who are doing a drug deal, quietly talking on a side street.
intention: Mitt wants to know what's going on.
moral_action: Mitt walks by the group and glances out of the corner of his eye while making efforts not to be noticed.
moral_consequence: Mitt sees the drugs without catching the group's attention and quickly leaves.
immoral_action: Mitt walks up to the group and asks them if there's a problem that he can help with.
immoral_consequence: The group turns on Mitt, sees him as a threat to their deal, and assault him.

norm: It's good to help out your former employees.
situation: A person who used to work for Jake asks him if he can write them a letter of recommendation for a job they want.
intention: Jake wants to give the person who used to work for him an answer.
moral_action: Jake agrees to help his ex employee and writes a glowing letter of recommendation for them.
moral_consequence: Jake's ex employee gets the job they wanted due to Jake's help.
immoral_action: Jake says he doesn't want to be responsible for recommending anybody for work and refuses to help his ex employee.
immoral_consequence: The person who used to work for Jake doesn't get the job that he really wanted.

norm: You shouldn't talk back to authority figures.
situation: George has been struggling with school lately and is pulled aside by his teacher to talk about a recent test.
intention: George wants to get out of the situation.
moral_action: George listens to what his teacher has to say and is cooperative.
moral_consequence: George's teacher shows him some studying tips to help on his next test and lets him go home.
immoral_action: George snaps at his teacher, telling them stop bothering him and that it's their fault for not teaching the class well enough.
immoral_consequence: George's teacher calls his parents to let them know about his behavior, and he gets grounded for 2 weeks.

norm: It's good to be faithful to your wife.
situation: Cal is married, but he meets a beautiful women at a store when getting groceries.
intention: Cal wants to have drinks.
moral_action: Cal goes home and asks his wife if she wants to go out for a drink.
moral_consequence: Cal and his wife have a great time out drinking at the bar.
immoral_action: Cal asks the woman if she wants to have a drink with him.
immoral_consequence: Cal's wife divorces him, and he loses half of what he owns in the divorce.

norm: You shouldn't turn down someone offering you a generous tip.
situation: Adam is a waiter at a high-end steakhouse, and a new customer just offered him a big tip.
intention: Adam wants to say something to the customer.
moral_action: Adam accepts the tip, and lets the customer know how grateful he is.
moral_consequence: The customer feels happy that they made Adam's day, and Adam feels motivated to work harder.
immoral_action: Adam rejects the tip, telling the customer that they should donate the money.
immoral_consequence: The customer doesn't donate the money, and Adam continues to struggle as a waiter.

norm: You shouldn't ignore your neighbors.
situation: Juliet is checking her mail when a neighbor waves at her.
intention: Juliet wants to get her mail inside.
moral_action: Juliet waves and smiles at her neighbor before grabbing her mail and going back inside.
moral_consequence: Juliet is seen as a friendly neighbor and her neighbor.
immoral_action: Juliet pretends she does not notice her neighbor's wave and just grabs her mail and goes back inside.
immoral_consequence: Juliet develops a reputation of being a rude person among the neighbors.

norm: It's wrong to get into fights.
situation: Bill is very proud of his roots despite coming from a poor family, which other students take as a reason to pick on him.
intention: Bill wants to stand up for himself.
moral_action: Bill laughs off his bullies' taunts and ignores their calls to fight.
moral_consequence: Bill's bullies get bored and stop picking on him, and his humor makes him some friends.
immoral_action: Bill gets into a fistfight with one of his bullies.
immoral_consequence: Bill gets a black eye, is suspended, and his parents punish him.

norm: It's wrong to feel superior to others.
situation: Jim is a black belt in karate and recently won a gold trophy at a martial arts tournament.
intention: Jim wants to let his friends know what happened.
moral_action: Jim brings up the tournament while hanging out with his friends, and mentions offhand that he won a trophy but still has much to learn.
moral_consequence: Jim's friends appreciate his modesty and ask him several follow-up questions about the tournament.
immoral_action: Jim carries the trophy around all day, waving it in his friend's faces and talking about how good at karate he is.
immoral_consequence: Jim's friends can't stand the way he's acting and avoid him.

norm: It is good to share news with your family.
situation: Joe found out that a politician  owes several million to the mob.
intention: Joe wants to tell the right people.
moral_action: Joe tells his family and to keep it quiet until the media runs the story.
moral_consequence: Joe's family is shocked to hear the news but is glad to know.
immoral_action: Joe tells the story to the mediaand no one else until the news is public.
immoral_consequence: Joe's family is upset that he didn't tell them about the news.

norm: It's bad to put a person out on the street.
situation: Terrance attempts to collect the past due rent from a family to whom he is renting an apartment.
intention: Terrance needs to get the money owed to him, for his rental unit.
moral_action: Terrance explains to the family that he understands financial trouble, but that he expects a payment arrangement to be made so that their account will be brought up to date.
moral_consequence: The family is grateful for his flexibility, and they work hard to bring the account current, they keep renting and Terrance keeps making money.
immoral_action: Terrance informs the family that they have one week to either pay the back rent in full, or vacate the apartment.
immoral_consequence: The family has to quickly find somewhere to live and Terrance doesn't get any of the money that he is owed.

norm: It's good to help a friend with an addiction problem.
situation: Julian is talking with his friend Rick who tells him that he's been struggling with Heroin addiction.
intention: Julian wants to respond to Rick's statement.
moral_action: Julian tells Rick that he can call him anytime he needs a distraction and that if he wants to go to rehab he'll drive him there.
moral_consequence: Rick is relieved that Julian is willing to be there for him and takes him up on the offer of going to rehab.
immoral_action: Julian tells Rick that it's OK and that we all have problems and that he'll get over it eventually.
immoral_consequence: Rick is surprised and sad that Julian doesn't seem to take his drug addiction seriously and thinks it'll just go away.

norm: It is cruel to make a baby cry on purpose
situation: Janet asks Josh to entertain her baby while she steps out to take a phone call.
intention: Josh needs to interact with the baby.
moral_action: Josh plays peek-a-boo with the baby.
moral_consequence: Everyone thinks Josh is so sweet with little kids.
immoral_action: Josh pokes the baby to see how much it will take to make her cry.
immoral_consequence: Everyone thinks Josh is a terrible person.

norm: It's good to applaud someone's great performance.
situation: Sally's mom, Stacy, is watching Sally play at her flute recital.
intention: Stacy wants to see Sally play well.
moral_action: Stacy gives Sally a standing ovation at the end of her recital.
moral_consequence: Sally feels very accomplished and practices her flute playing even more.
immoral_action: Stacy thinks Sally played well, but didn't clap for her at the end of the performance.
immoral_consequence: Sally thinks she didn't do so well and begins to lose interest in the flute.

norm: It's rude to tell someone they are ugly.
situation: Simon is hanging out with some of his friends when his rival shows up in a tacky outfit and asks how he looks.
intention: Simon wants to comment on his rival's outfit.
moral_action: Simon tells his rival that his outfit is interesting along with giving him tips on how to look better.
moral_consequence: Simon's rival accepts Simon's advice and changes the way he dresses.
immoral_action: Simon tells his rival that his outfit makes him look like moldy cheese.
immoral_consequence: Simon's rival starts getting teary eyed after hearing Simon's word.

norm: It's fun to do things with your friends.
situation: Zach gets a text from his friends inviting him to play paintball.
intention: Zach wants to release his stress.
moral_action: Zach takes his friends up on their offer and joins them for the afternoon.
moral_consequence: Zach has fun playing with his friends.
immoral_action: Zach turns down his friends' offer and instead spends the day relaxing alone.
immoral_consequence: Zach feel regenerated, but his friends are now a little bit more distant from him.

norm: You should not try to pursue and office romance.
situation: John is being hit on by his subordinate Jeff at the office they both work at.
intention: John needs to decide how to respond to Jeff's advances.
moral_action: John declines Jeff's advances, stating he's flattered but won't mix work and pleasure.
moral_consequence: John and Jeff remain on good terms and have a healthy workplace relationship.
immoral_action: John decides to give a relationship with Jeff a shot, and they start dating.
immoral_consequence: John and Jeff's romantic relationship is discovered and John gets fired for employee fraternization.

norm: It's bad to enter a marriage if you aren't committed.
situation: Ben and Jane have just got married and are on honeymoon.
intention: Ben wants to go to the bar.
moral_action: Ben ask Jane if she wants to go to the bar to drink.
moral_consequence: Jane feel happy and has fun.
immoral_action: Ben tells Jane that he needs a break from her to go drink, and he goes to the bar.
immoral_consequence: Jane is unhappy and feels left out.

norm: It's hurtful to disown someone.
situation: Jenna is mad at her sister for wearing a white dress to Jenna's wedding.
intention: Jenna wants to stop dealing with her sister's attention-seeking behavior.
moral_action: Jenna convinces all her sister's friends to tell her sister to apologize.
moral_consequence: Jenna's sister succumbs to peer pressure and apologizes to Jenna.
immoral_action: Jenna refuses to speak to her sister ever again and moves a thousand miles away.
immoral_consequence: Jenna often misses her sister but is too stubborn to recontact her.

norm: It's not okay to lie to someone in a relationship.
situation: George does not have to work this weekend.
intention: George wants to go to the football game but knows that his girlfriend wants to go to the Oktoberfest.
moral_action: George tells his girlfriend how much it means for him to go to the football game with his buddies.
moral_consequence: George's girlfriend understands and agrees that they can do something together the next time George has off for the weekend.
immoral_action: George tells his girlfriend that he has to work and instead goes to the football game with his buddies.
immoral_consequence: George's girlfriend ends the relationship when she learns that George did not have to work and actually went to a game.

norm: You shouldn't take away your child's college funds.
situation: Harold's wife Jennifer points out to Harold that if they dip into their son's college savings they can afford a new car.
intention: Harold wants to respond to his wife's idea.
moral_action: Harold tells his wife that while a new car would be great, their son's college education is way more important.
moral_consequence: Harold and Jennifer's son has enough money when college time comes and isn't forced to take loans.
immoral_action: Harold tells his wife that's a great idea and that he can't wait to drive it when they get it.
immoral_consequence: Harold and Jennifer's son doesn't save enough money to pay for college and is forced into debt.

norm: It's rude to lie to people about your name.
situation: Fabian is standing at the counter of the fast food restaurant when the cashier asks him his name.
intention: Fabian wants to give a name to the cashier that he will recognize when it is called.
moral_action: Fabian tells the cashier his name is Fabian.
moral_consequence: The cashier feels content when she call's Fabian to pick up his food.
immoral_action: Fabian tells the cashier that his name is Mike Rotch.
immoral_consequence: The cashier is embarrassed when the customers start laughing, and she realizes what she has said.

norm: It's good to get along with your siblings.
situation: Hannah has a younger sister Alice, and they live together with their parents.
intention: Hannah wants to manage her relationship with Alice.
moral_action: Hannah takes care of many things for Alice when their mom is busy, and they are not just siblings but also best friends.
moral_consequence: Alice makes a delicious dessert for Hannah whenever she feels stressed with her college homework.
immoral_action: Hannah doesn't talk or show love to Alice much because she spends more time with her friends.
immoral_consequence: Alice feels unloved and lonely.

norm: It's good to talk to dietitians about your diet.
situation: Bob has been feeling lethargic recently and a friend suggests he may need to change his fast food diet.
intention: Bob wants to respond to his friends suggestion.
moral_action: Bob takes the suggestion seriously and consults a dietitian.
moral_consequence: Bob's improved eating habits give him more energy and improves his health.
immoral_action: Bob laughs his friends comment off and continues his current eating habits,.
immoral_consequence: Bob's health steadily declines.

norm: It's good to invite people to fun events.
situation: Luke spoke to Han because he wanted to invite Han over to a BBQ with his friends.
intention: Luke wants to talk to Han.
moral_action: Luke invites Han to the BBQ with his other friends.
moral_consequence: Han is excited to go to the BBQ with Luke and friends.
immoral_action: Luke talks to Han about sports and games and such and forgets to invite him.
immoral_consequence: Luke is upset because it would be more fun with Han there.

norm: You shouldn't date someone that does drugs.
situation: Sadie is dating Mark, but just found out that he does drugs.
intention: Sadie wants to talk to Mark about his drug habit.
moral_action: Sadie tells Mark that she loves him, but she can't be with a man that does drugs.
moral_consequence: Sadie later meets another man who doesn't do drugs, and she is much happier with him.
immoral_action: Sadie tells Mark that she loves him no matter what and will be with him through thick and thin.
immoral_consequence: Mark convinces Sadie to start doing drugs with him and Sadie becomes homeless.

norm: It's wrong to influence someone to do something dishonest.
situation: Jenna's friend Anna really wanted to go on the class trip to see Harry Potter: The Cursed Child, but her ultra-religious parents thought fantasy books led to Satanism.
intention: Jenna wants her friend to come with her to see the play.
moral_action: Jenna asks Anna if any of her grandparents are saner than her parents and will sign the permission slip.
moral_consequence: Anna gets her grandmother to sign her permission slip and goes to the play with Jenna.
immoral_action: Jenna encourages her friend to let Jenna sign the permission slip instead of her parents.
immoral_consequence: Jenna's teacher recognizes Jenna's handwriting and makes Anna stay behind.

norm: You should be courteous to customers
situation: Jen is working a busy line and notices a customer appearing lost nearby.
intention: Jen wants to clear the queue as fast as possible.
moral_action: Jen asks the customer if they need help finding something and multitasks while telling them what aisle to look in.
moral_consequence: The customer is grateful and buys the item from the store.
immoral_action: Jen ignores the customer and focuses solely on the people waiting in line.
immoral_consequence: The customer doesn't find what they need, and they shop elsewhere.

norm: It's harmful to spread fake news as truth.
situation: Anton is a manager for a large firm and his employee's productivity has started to suffer.
intention: Anton wants his employee's to be productive.
moral_action: Anton sets up additional paid training for his employee's.
moral_consequence: Anton's employee's benefit greatly from the training and the firms overall productivity skyrockets.
immoral_action: Anton spreads a fake story that his company will be firing unproductive employee's.
immoral_consequence: Anton's boss finds out that he spread a fake news story and fires him.

norm: It is rude to exclude people from events.
situation: Uzuri is sending out invites for her birthday party, and she's worried that her gossiping coworker Samantha will cause drama.
intention: Uzuri wants to create a fun atmosphere.
moral_action: Uzuri calls Samantha expressing her concerns and makes Samantha promise not to cause trouble at the party.
moral_consequence: Samantha learns that her actions hurt others, and she stops gossiping about her coworkers.
immoral_action: Uzuri invites all of her coworkers except Samantha to the part.
immoral_consequence: Samantha is hurt when she sees pictures of the party on social media.

norm: You shouldn't leave your spouse for someone you barely know.
situation: Jess was in a relationship with Joe, but had recently taken a liking to Bill.
intention: Jess wants see what her future holds with Bill.
moral_action: Jess stays friends with Bill and does not peruse anything romantic.
moral_consequence: Jess stays with Joe and does not end up leaving him.
immoral_action: Jess decides to break things off with Bill to see what will happen.
immoral_consequence: Joe is heartbroken by break up.

norm: It is kind to invite your friends to swim.
situation: Oliver just got his new pool filled up when his friends stop by.
intention: Oliver wants to cool off.
moral_action: Oliver tells his friends he's about to go for a swim, and asks if they want to join him.
moral_consequence: Oliver's friends get to cool off and have fun with Oliver.
immoral_action: Oliver jumps in the pool and asks his friends to wait for him on the porch.
immoral_consequence: Oliver's friends remain hot as they sit on the porch feeling left out.

norm: It is disgusting to try and hit on a child.
situation: Jimmy sees his friend Paul's underage daughter Kate come into the room.
intention: Jimmy wants to get Kate's attention,.
moral_action: Jimmy asks Kate how Kate s doing in school.
moral_consequence: A routine social exchange occurs and no one is upset.
immoral_action: Jimmy makes sexually suggestive remarks about Kate's physical development.
immoral_consequence: Kate feels violated and Jimmy begins to question whether Jimmy might have issues with sexual deviance.

norm: You shouldn't expect to get your way every time.
situation: Brad wanted to become a professional baseball pitcher.
intention: Brad wants to get as many strikeouts as possible.
moral_action: Brad doesn't get too upset when someone gets a hit off of him.
moral_consequence: Brad is better able to forget his mistakes.
immoral_action: Brad gets mad whenever someone gets a hit off of me.
immoral_consequence: Brad's anger affects his performance.

norm: It's wrong to create a jealous household.
situation: Pam's kids come home from school with their grade cards to show her.
intention: Pam wants to talk to the kids about their grades.
moral_action: Pam takes John and Jake aside individually and looks over their cards pointing out something good on each one.
moral_consequence: John and Jake both feel great about themselves and spend the evening playing together.
