immoral_action: Pam looks at both cards together and points out how much better John's is than Jake's.
immoral_consequence: John feels spiteful toward Jake and the two start having problems getting along.

norm: It's wrong to date your sibling's ex.
situation: Charlie needs a date for the upcoming dance and learns that his big brother Alex just got dumped by his ex-girlfriend Stacy.
intention: Charlie wants to ask a girl to the dance.
moral_action: Charlie asks a girl named Eve to the dance when he overhears someone saying she needs a date.
moral_consequence: Alex lets Charlie borrow some of his cologne, so he smells good for his date with Eve.
immoral_action: Charlie asks Stacy if she'll go to the dance with him now that she's single.
immoral_consequence: Alex learns that Charlie asked out Stacy and punches him for the act of disloyalty.

norm: You should prioritize important pursuits above hobbies.
situation: Dallas' best friend invites her to a concert on a night that she is scheduled to work.
intention: Dallas wants to have a fun, well-rounded life.
moral_action: Dallas tells her friend that she can't make the concert, but can hangout the next night.
moral_consequence: Dallas keeps her job and is still able to have fun with her friend.
immoral_action: Dallas skips her work shift to go to the concert.
immoral_consequence: Dallas is fired from her job.

norm: You shouldn't fake medical disorders.
situation: Brianna has to give a big presentation in her English class but is nervous that she will embarrass herself in front of the class.
intention: Brianna wants to avoid giving the presentation.
moral_action: Brianna tells her teacher that she is nervous about talking to such a large group and that she cannot do it.
moral_consequence: The teacher compromises and lets Brianna record her presentation and play the recording to the class.
immoral_action: Brianna tells her teacher that she has a condition that causes her to faint when she is nervous in front of a large crowd, so she cannot do the presentation.
immoral_consequence: The teacher allows Brianna to present privately instead, but Brianna feels bad that she lied.

norm: It is rude to intentionally misgender someone.
situation: Harry's friend Tina has recently transitioned and used to be known as Tony.
intention: Harry wants to express his disapproval of Tina's transgenderism.
moral_action: Harry says he is not comfortable with Tina's choice, but refers to her by her new name and gender.
moral_consequence: Harry grows more comfortable with Tina, and the two remain friends.
immoral_action: "Harry continues to call Tina Tony and refer to Tina as ""he""."
immoral_consequence: Tina stops hanging out with Harry, and the two stop being friends.

norm: It is kind to help people with directions.
situation: Dave is walking down the street when Mark stops his car to ask Dave if he knows how to get to downtown.

moral_action: Dave tells Mark that if he just continues on the road he's on, he'll eventually reach downtown.
moral_consequence: Mark is grateful for the help and happy that Dave explained where downtown is.
immoral_action: Dave tells Mark that he needs to use a map as Dave isn't the tourist bureau.
immoral_consequence: Mark feels offended by Dave's comment and his suggestion to use a map.

norm: It's rude to insult someone based on their size.
situation: Tom is very skinny, and his friend, Devin, is very big compared to him.
intention: Tom wants to talk to Devin about their weight.
moral_action: Tom tells Devin that he wishes he were as big as Devin.
moral_consequence: Devin feels better about his own weight and likes that Tom doesn't judge him.
immoral_action: Tom tells Devin that he has to lose weight if he wants to keep hanging out with him.
immoral_consequence: Devin's feelings are hurt, and he doesn't think Tom likes him that much.

norm: You shouldn't lie and tell people you have a cold.
situation: Tanya has just come home after a long work week when her friends call to invite her out to the club.
intention: Tanya wants to stay home and relax.

moral_consequence: Tanya's friends are understanding of her situation and plan to catch up some other time.
immoral_action: Tanya tells her friends she can't make it because she's feeling ill.
immoral_consequence: Tanya's friends stop by to drop off soup and medicine before they head out, only to find that she is perfectly healthy.

norm: It's inappropriate to gossip about your wife.
situation: Tim is talking to some of his buddies, and they are all talking about thier wives.
intention: Tim wants to add something to the conversation.
moral_action: Tim turns the conversation to sports and talks about his favorite teams.
moral_consequence: Tim and his friends spend a few hours discussing games they've been to.
immoral_action: Tim talks about embarrassing things about his wife to all his friends.
immoral_consequence: Tim's wife is very upset with him when he arrives back home.

norm: It’s bad to not go to work.
situation: Tyler wakes up with a headache and has to go to work.

moral_action: Tyler take some medicine for the headache and goes to work.
moral_consequence: The headache goes away and Tyler is able to work.
immoral_action: Tyler skips work and sleeps all day until the headache goes away.
immoral_consequence: Tyler gets fired for not going into work or calling out sick.

norm: It's wrong to hope that something bad happens to you.

immoral_consequence: May is reminded of how her getting injured would affect her family.

norm: It's bad to be verbally abusive.
situation: John just lost his job and comes home to his wife Mindy.

moral_action: John calmly shares with Mindy the news, and they talk it over.
moral_consequence: Mindy is happy he is sharing with her, and they get closer.
immoral_action: John calls Mindy all sorts of bad names and yells at her.
immoral_consequence: Mindy feels badly and cries and resents John.

norm: It's wrong to cheat on an exam.
situation: Roman is sitting in class taking a big final exam in his math class.
intention: Roman wants to score well on the exam.
moral_action: Roman blocks out everything and concentrates extra hard to remember everything he studied for the test.
moral_consequence: Roman get a really good score on his exam when he gets it back from the teacher.

immoral_consequence: Roman gets busted cheating by the teacher and fails the exam.

norm: It's wrong to have a taste for human flesh.
situation: Jeffrey is at home thinking about dinner with a friend he just met next to him.

moral_action: Jeffrey does a google search for exotic foods and picks a recipe to try.
moral_consequence: Jeffrey tries a new dish, and he and his friend are happy.
immoral_action: Jeffrey drugs his friend, dismembers him and cooks him to taste.
immoral_consequence: Jeffrey gets arrested and goes to jail and his friend dies.

norm: It's bad to not pay someone back.
situation: Christian's crush, Lila, has asked him out on a date, but he is broke and can't afford dinner.
intention: Christian wants to have dinner with Lila.
moral_action: Christian borrows his uncle's rent money and pays it back when he says he will.
moral_consequence: Christian and Lila were able to go on their date, and Christian's uncle is able to pay his rent on time.
immoral_action: Christian borrows money from his uncle with the promise to pay him back before rent is due, but doesn't.
immoral_consequence: Christian's uncle is late on rent and forced to pay a late fee.

norm: Driving under the influence is bad.
situation: Alice has been drinking with friends at a bar and feels drunk.
intention: Alice wants to go home.
moral_action: Alice calls a taxi cab to take her home.
moral_consequence: Alice makes it home safely without injuring anyone on the road.
immoral_action: Alice drives her car home from the bar.
immoral_consequence: Alice hits another vehicle because she is impared and injures them.

norm: It's irresponsible to play so raucously that it causes damage.
situation: Hank and his friends are playing flag football outside in the field.

moral_action: Hank runs behind the player and tears off the player's flags.
moral_consequence: The player stops running, and so the teams start another play.
immoral_action: Hank charges the player with the ball and tackles him full-force.
immoral_consequence: The player gets angry at the unnecessary roughness and starts punching Hank.

norm: You should not be a toxic person.
situation: Don got stressed at his work after being promoted to a senior level.
intention: Don wants to deal with his stress.
moral_action: Don goes to the doctor to treat his mental problem due to the stress.
moral_consequence: His family members support his decision and care and love him more.
immoral_action: Don vents his stress and becomes abusive towards his family members.
immoral_consequence: His family members feel sad and intimidated.

norm: It's mean to stop talking to your friends.

immoral_action: Megan gives Nancy the cold shoulder and ignores her at every possible opportunity.
immoral_consequence: Nancy refuses to break off her relationship with Megan's ex-boyfriend and instead begins to hate Megan for her ill treatment of her.

norm: You should invite people over for the holidays.
situation: Every year, Janet hosts a Christmas party for her big family.

moral_consequence: Janet has a great time with her friends that night.

immoral_consequence: Janet enjoys the alone time, but feels lonely without anyone there.

norm: You should always go to the dentist every six months.

intention: John wants to clear up his schedule a bit.
moral_action: John decides to cancel his night out at the movies.
moral_consequence: John gets a thorough cleaning at the dentist and his teeth remain healthy and strong.
immoral_action: John decides to cancel his dentist appointment and go some other time.
immoral_consequence: John ends up with several cavities when he finally reschedules his appointment.

norm: It is good to teach people financial responsibility.
situation: Lucia, a wealthy woman, has a teenage daughter, who very much wants to go on an expensive trip with friends.
intention: Lucia wants her daughter to be happy.

immoral_action: Lucia pays for the trip without any comment.
immoral_consequence: Lucia's daughter feels entitled to everything, without any effort.

norm: You shouldn't discourage your child when they're applying to college.

moral_consequence: Ronald works harder and improves his grades.
immoral_action: Dave tells Ronald that he would never make it to that university.
immoral_consequence: Ronald's self esteem is lowered, and he goes straight into the workforce instead of attending college.

norm: It's not okay to steal things from your workplace.

moral_consequence: John gets a deal on paper and his daughter is happy, while his department colleagues aren't affected.
immoral_action: John brings home a large ream of paper that he takes from his office copy machine so that he doesn't need to buy paper for his daughter to draw on.
immoral_consequence: The copy machine runs out of paper the next day, negatively impacting John's work activities.

norm: One should not hurt their friends.

immoral_action: Tony shoves Joanne in the back as she tries to make a basket.
immoral_consequence: Joanne falls and cuts her knee on the driveway pavement.

norm: People should be able to govern themselves as they choose.
situation: George is the leader of a country and at a government meeting.

moral_consequence: The people of George's country prosper, and he is held in high regard.
immoral_action: George decides that his people just comply with his every whim.
immoral_consequence: George's people grow to resent him and eventually rebel.

norm: It's good to be eager about controlling your life.
situation: Billy has just graduated high school and is asked about what he will do.

moral_action: Billy says he wants to be an attorney and will be attending college.
moral_consequence: Billy will be able to achieve the goals he has.
immoral_action: Billy says that he will go with the flow and doesn't have plans.
immoral_consequence: Billy will not be able to have control over his life and will be directionless.

norm: It's bad to lie about your health.
situation: Larry feels better after being sick from COVID for a week, and Aubrey invites him to a baseball game.
intention: Larry wants to see the game.
moral_action: Larry asks Aubrey to live stream the game through her video recorder.
moral_consequence: Larry enjoys the football game at home, Ashley respects him more in the future.
immoral_action: Larry does not tell Aubrey about his COVID symptoms, and she takes him to the baseball game.
immoral_consequence: Larry infects Aubrey with COVID, and his condition gets slightly worse from being outside.

norm: It is nice to thank someone who praises you.
situation: Jack and his boss are in a meeting and Jack's boss thanks Jack for a job well done.
intention: Jack wants to not appear awkward in front of his boss.
moral_action: Jack thanks his boss for the praise before continuing on with the meeting.
moral_consequence: Jack's boss is pleased.
immoral_action: Jack says nothing about the praise and continues with the meeting.
immoral_consequence: Jack's boss may think Jack is being rude or did not appreciate the praise.

norm: It's bad to make threats about shooting people.
situation: Oliver and Danny get into a nasty argument when Oliver sees Danny kissing his girlfriend.
intention: Oliver wants Danny to stay away from his girlfriend.
moral_action: Oliver asks his girlfriend to stay away from Danny if she respects their relationship.
moral_consequence: Oliver grows closer to his girlfriend during the conversation.
immoral_action: Oliver tells Danny to get away from his girlfriend, or he'll shoot Danny's leg with the gun in his car.
immoral_consequence: Oliver is arrested by the police after Danny reports him.

norm: It's wrong to use your illness to your advantage.
situation: Kati has cancer, it's a slow moving cancer but a scary one all the same, and she's in an argument with her friend.
intention: Kati wants to win the argument.
moral_action: Kati uses some logic to outwit her friend in this argument.
moral_consequence: Kati's friend admits that Kati was right, and they go back to normal.
immoral_action: Kati asks her friend how she can be happy fighting with a person who has cancer.
immoral_consequence: Kati's friend feels very guilty and apologizes, but doesn't really seem to be wrong in the argument.

norm: It's wrong to value money over one's friends.
situation: Lexie has a chance to work an extra shift at work tonight, but she had already promised her friend Dana to go to the night club.
intention: Lexie wants to talk with Dana.
moral_action: Lexie tells her employer that she already made plans, and calls Dana to tell her to get ready to go out.
moral_consequence: Dana has a fun night out with her friend and appreciates Lexie for sticking to their plans.
immoral_action: Lexie calls Dana to tell her she's going to get in some extra hours instead of going to the club.
immoral_consequence: Dana is disappointed because she got all ready to go out for nothing.

norm: It is mean to make people cry on purpose.
situation: Roger is in a relationship with his girlfriend but is not happy.
intention: Roger wants to break up with his girlfriend.
moral_action: Roger tells his girlfriend that he wants to break up but is nice to her and doesn't make her cry.
moral_consequence: Roger is happy and remains friends with his ex.
immoral_action: Roger starts yelling at his girlfriend that he wants to breakup he calls her names and makes her cry on purpose.
immoral_consequence: Roger feels guilty about how he handled the breakup.

norm: It's unusual to drink beer for lunch and nothing else.
situation: Tom does not have much money but agrees to go out with his coworkers to a local pub during lunch.
intention: Tom wants to have fun with his friends.
moral_action: Tom uses his money to buy one beer and some cheap food.
moral_consequence: Tom is able to join his coworkers for a drink while not impairing or depriving himself.
immoral_action: Tom uses all his money to buy two beers in order to keep up with his coworkers.
immoral_consequence: Tom doesn't perform well at work later because he didn't eat anything and the alcohol had no buffer.

norm: You shouldn't bring up old relationships with your current partner.
situation: Holden is taking his girlfriend to a park in the town he grew up in.
intention: Holden wants to convey how great the park is to his girlfriend.
moral_action: Holden recalls a fond memory he had in the park with an ex-girlfriend, but explains it in a way that doesn't reference her at all.
moral_consequence: Holden's girlfriend appreciates the story and grows more excited about the visit.
immoral_action: Holden mentions a fond memory he had a the park with an ex-girlfriend of his.
immoral_consequence: Holden's girlfriend gets angry at him for talking about his ex and it ruins the entire visit.

norm: It's bad to lose control of your emotions too frequently.
situation: Sam was just dumped and tends to vent out his frustrations on a regular basis using social media.
intention: Sam wants to confide in someone about what happened.
moral_action: Sam calls a family member to discuss what happened.
moral_consequence: Sam is able to express his feelings in private in a controlled manner.
immoral_action: Sam writes out a long social media post after feeling self pity.
immoral_consequence: Sam leave a bad impression on those who read the post.

norm: It is unacceptable to force someone to drink alcohol.
situation: Paul is celebrating a work promotion at a bar with his friends, including Wayne, who's acting as the designated driver.
intention: Paul wants to buy rounds of shots for his friends.
moral_action: Paul buys shots for all of his friends except Wayne, because he needs to be sober to drive them home.
moral_consequence: Wayne drives Paul and his friends home safely and then drinks a beer and watches Netflix on his couch.
immoral_action: Paul insists that everyone, including Wayne, drink five shots before they go home.
immoral_consequence: Wayne gets pulled over driving Paul and his friends home and gets charged with a DUI.

norm: It's good to help save your company.
situation: Lou works for a company that is in danger of losing a main client, and his manager asks him to work this weekend as an emergency measure.
intention: Lou wants to decide what to do this weekend.
moral_action: Lou agrees to work this weekend and helps the company overcome the emergency.
moral_consequence: The company retains its main client, and Lou gets a raise for his effort.
immoral_action: Lou declines to work this weekend and goes to play golf instead.
immoral_consequence: The company loses its main client and goes bankrupt, costing Lou his job.

norm: You shouldn't buy a house for your kids.
situation: Lisa has two sons named Gary and Wyatt that live in the same room, and they always argue.
intention: Lisa wants her sons to stop arguing.
moral_action: Lisa puts Gary and Wyatt in separate rooms in the same house.
moral_consequence: Lisa no longer has to deal with Gary and Wyatt arguing.
immoral_action: Lisa buys two separate houses for both Gary and Wyatt to live in.
immoral_consequence: Lisa becomes bankrupt and can't afford to buy anything else.

norm: People appreciate having their things returned to them.
situation: John has finished a home project with which he used a friend's tools to complete.
intention: John wants to start a new project.
moral_action: John contacts his friend to return his tools before preparing for his next project.
moral_consequence: John's friend appreciates the gesture and offers John tools to use for the next project.
immoral_action: John begins a new project and continues to use his friend's tools for the new project.
immoral_consequence: John's friend becomes annoyed that John has had his tools for so long and grows resentful of him.

norm: It is good to plan your future.
situation: Anastasia just started her first job and has just moved into her first apartment.
intention: Anastasia wants enjoy her newfound freedom.
moral_action: Anastasia knows owning a home one day will lead to even more freedom, so she enjoys herself in moderation and begins to invest and save her extra income.
moral_consequence: Over time Anastasia's saving and net worth grow until she has more and more financial freedom and buys a house.
immoral_action: Anastasia spends a lot of time and money on day to day activities like eating out and going concerts with friends.
immoral_consequence: Anastasia is soon living a lifestyle that out paces her earnings and bills which leads her to having to move back home.

norm: It's rude to take all the credit from your partner.
situation: Zelda and her husband worked hard to get rid of the roaches in the old house.
intention: Zelda wants to talk about the acomplishment.
moral_action: Zelda talked about the ideas she came up with and the ones her husband did.
moral_consequence: They both get credit for the termination of the roach infestation.
immoral_action: Zelda tells people how she came up with the ideas and took the roaches down herself.
immoral_consequence: Her husband gets upset because she's not giving him any credit.

norm: You shouldn't push your way into someone else's home.
situation: Hal is working as a landscaper for a wealthy landowner.
intention: Hal wants to see what the inside of the home looks like.
moral_action: Hal asks the owner if he could give him a tour of the house.
moral_consequence: The owner obliges and takes Hal on a short tour around the property.
immoral_action: Hal creeps into the house uninvited to look around and see what's there.
immoral_consequence: The owner of the house sees Hal, and he is fired on the spot.

norm: It is rude to snoop through other people's private messages.
situation: Dave is dating a partner who has a friend who he is feeling jealous over.
intention: Dave wants to see if there's anything going on between them.
moral_action: Dave finds a way to casually ask his partner about the nature of their relationship.
moral_consequence: Dave's partner feels bad for the misunderstanding and reassures him that it's just a friend.
immoral_action: Dave takes his partner's phone and starts looking through her messages.
immoral_consequence: Dave's partner catches him snooping and is upset about his lack of trust.

norm: It's wrong to be a lazy bum.
situation: Kevin has been laying around the house and doing nothing for weeks, when he suddenly sees that he has a missed call from a prospective employer.
intention: Kevin has to decide whether to call the prospect back.
moral_action: Kevin calls the prospective employer back as soon as he sees the missed call and sets up an interview time.
moral_consequence: Kevin gets the job and feels good about himself, and he enjoys his new job.
immoral_action: Kevin needs to work but has been enjoying the time off, so he decides not to call the prospective employer back right away.
immoral_consequence: By the time Kevin calls the employer back, they have already filled the position that was available, leaving Kevin with no money and no job.

norm: It's wrong to skip studying to go out and party.
situation: Sam was invited to a party the day before a big math test.
intention: Sam wants to do well on the test.
moral_action: Sam rejects the party invitatin.
moral_consequence: Sam has enough time to study to do well on the test.
immoral_action: Sam goes to the party thinking that she can study once she comes back home.
immoral_consequence: Sam will not have enough time to study.

norm: It is good to help others in need.
situation: Francis and his friends are driving through the downtown city streets when they see a homeless man on the corner.
intention: Francis wants to get to the game with his friends.
moral_action: Francis stops, hands the homeless guy some change, then drives to the game.
moral_consequence: The homeless guy is happier and Francis' friends respect Francis more.
immoral_action: Francis ignores the homeless guy at the light and speeds off to the game.
immoral_consequence: Francis' friends don't respect him as much and the homeless guy is sad.

norm: It's wrong to lose things that are important to people.
situation: Nancy is helping her Aunt Sally clean out her home office because it has become quite a mess of papers.
intention: Nancy wants to get all of the papers cleared out in her Aunt's home office.
moral_action: Nancy is careful to have her Aunt Sally look through the oldest papers to be sure nothing important is thrown out.
moral_consequence: Nancy's Aunt Sally is able to save some old poems from her boyfriend that are very important to her.
immoral_action: Nancy places all papers that are over five years old into the trash without paying attention to things that may be sentimental to her Aunt.
immoral_consequence: Nancy's Aunt Sally is very upset that some poems from her old boyfriend were thrown in the trash.

norm: It's bad to slash someone's tires.
situation: Sue's boyfriend breaks up with her.
intention: Sue wants to get back at him.
moral_action: Sue gets a makeover and starts going out and having fun.
moral_consequence: Sue meets many new people and feels better about herself.
immoral_action: Sue hides outside his work and slashes his tires.
immoral_consequence: Sue is caught on security camera and arrested.

norm: It is wrong to punch children.
situation: Bobby's son John knocks over their big screen TV and breaks it.
intention: Bobby wants to punish his kid and teach a lesson.
moral_action: Bobby holds his anger in and sends his son to his room telling him to be more careful around electronics.
moral_consequence: John makes sure to be careful around the house and his relationship remains strong with Bobby.
immoral_action: Bobby allows his anger to take hold of him, and he punches his son in the arm as punishment.
immoral_consequence: John stops liking his dad Bobby and their relationship deteriorates to nothing.

norm: You shouldn't lie to your friends about being ill.
situation: Sawyer receives a text message from his friends inviting him to hang out with them today.
intention: Sawyer wants to spend his Saturday lounging at home.
moral_action: Sawyer tells his friends that he doesn't feel like going out today.
moral_consequence: Sawyer's friends accept his explanation after sharing their concerns, and Sawyer spends the day relaxing by himself.
immoral_action: Sawyer tells his friends that he is sick with the flu.
immoral_consequence: Sawyer's friends come over to give him soup, but discover he's well and end up trusting him less.

norm: You shouldn't talk to your partner's ex.
situation: Jack's girlfriend is attending an event while Jack watches a football game on tv.
intention: Jack wants to call someone to discuss the football game.
moral_action: Jack calls his friend Bo and discusses the game.
moral_consequence: Jack and Bo have a good conversation.
immoral_action: Jack calls his girlfriend's ex and discusses the game.
immoral_consequence: Jack's girlfriend is furious.

norm: It's good to try hard at school.
situation: Billy has a big test tomorrow, but an awesome new video game was released today that he's been waiting months to play.
intention: Billy wants to play the new video game.
moral_action: Billy studies for the test and waits until the next day to start playing the new game.
moral_consequence: Billy passes the test and is able to play the new game all night the next night.
immoral_action: Billy blows off studying and plays the new video game all night.
immoral_consequence: Billy fails his test and his parents forbid him to play the game again.

norm: It's bad to judge people based on sexual preference.
situation: Tammy and her friends are talking about the new gay couple that moved into their neighborhood.
intention: Tammy wants to keep her religious beliefs intact.
moral_action: Tammy tells her friends that God says all humans are equal, and they should love that couple.
moral_consequence: Tammy's friends respect Tammy more and think she is kind.
immoral_action: Tammy tells her friends that the couple is going to hell, and she won't talk to them.
immoral_consequence: Tammy's friends respect Tammy less and distance themselves from her.

norm: It's wrong to boast about one's possessions.
situation: Ellie just got a PS5 and some awesome games for it.
intention: Ellie wants to talk to her friends about it.
moral_action: Ellie talks about the PS5 including everything she hates about it.
moral_consequence: Ellie's friends all discuss the pros and cons of the PS5 with her.
immoral_action: Ellie brags to all her friends about how awesome her PS5 is.
immoral_consequence: Ellie quickly finds her friends list emptied of people who want to play with her.

norm: It's rude to brag about getting the last of something
situation: Julia has finally made it to a ticket booth after waiting in a long line for tickets and discovers she got the last ticket.
intention: Julia wants to celebrate that she got a ticket.
moral_action: Julia makes her way to her car quickly and quietly and once inside lets her emotions out.
moral_consequence: Julia is able to celebrate and kick and scream in joy without insulting those who missed out.
immoral_action: Julia waves the ticket in front of people that were still waiting in line with giddiness and lets them know it was the last one.
immoral_consequence: Julia is targeted by the crowd with name calling and physical object being thrown at her which cause her fear.

norm: You shouldn't get pregnant before you get married.
situation: Lisa has a boyfriend with Ben and is in love with him.
intention: Lisa wants to have a baby with Ben.
moral_action: Lisa develops her relationship with Ben which leads to marriage and then a baby.
moral_consequence: Ben is committed to Lisa and Lisa feels supported while they raise their baby.
immoral_action: Lisa has a baby with Ben while they are still dating.
immoral_consequence: Ben does not feel committed to Lisa and leaves Lisa alone to take care of the baby.

norm: You shouldn't take more food then you can finish.
situation: Matt is very hungry as he visits an all-you-can-eat buffet and is overwhelmed by all the food choices.
intention: Matt wants to decide what foods to select for his meal.
moral_action: Matt takes one plate worth of his favorite foods from the buffet.
moral_consequence: Matt satisfies his hunger and enjoys his meal immensely.
immoral_action: Matt takes several large plates worth of food from the buffet before sitting down to eat.
immoral_consequence: Matt overats, feels sick and can't finish all the food, so he ends up having to throw it away.

norm: It's rude to hi-jack your friend's joke entirely.
situation: Steve starts telling a joke at a party that his friend, Chris, already knows.
intention: Chris wants to contribute to the joke.
moral_action: Chris lets Steve finish telling the joke and joins in the raucous laughter even though he'd heard it already.
moral_consequence: Steve feels glad that Chris found the joke funny even though he'd heard it before.
immoral_action: Chris starts talking over Steve to tell the rest of the joke.
immoral_consequence: Steve feels annoyed that Chris wouldn't let him tell his own joke.

norm: It's good to be sensitive to someone's depression and anxiety.
situation: Bob has noticed a negative change in his wife's mood lately.
intention: Bob wants to address his wife's nervous and down-spirited behavior.
moral_action: Bob is supportive and urges his wife to seek professional help.
moral_consequence: Bob helps his wife get the help she needs.
immoral_action: Bob tells his wife to get over whatever her problem is or their marriage is over.
immoral_consequence: Bob's response sends his wife into a downward spiral.

norm: It's bad to cut someone off who is young.
situation: Midge is driving down the highway and there are several aggressive teen drivers around.
intention: Midge wants to get away from the young drivers.
moral_action: Midge slows down in the right lane.
moral_consequence: The teens speed away.
immoral_action: Midge speeds up to create separation.
immoral_consequence: Midge rear ends another driver.

norm: It's wrong to make comments about people's appearance.
situation: Todd meets a man with a large mole on his face.
intention: Todd wants to say something to the man.
moral_action: Todd makes normal small talk with the man and asks about his interests.
moral_consequence: The man feels comfortable around Todd and is happy with their interaction.
immoral_action: Todd tells the man that he looks hideous and that he should have the mole removed.
immoral_consequence: The man is deeply shamed and angered by Todd's callous comments.

norm: You shouldn't associate with mean people.
situation: Maggie is alone at a large party, and she feels somewhat lonely.
intention: Maggie wants to form new friendships.
moral_action: Maggie goes outside and asks to dance with people she recognizes from work.
moral_consequence: Maggie makes some new friends.
immoral_action: Maggie starts up a conversation with an ambitious woman known for bullying others.
immoral_consequence: Maggie is seen by others at the party as another bully.

norm: It's kind to help an older person with a chore.
situation: Ron's grandpa has trouble bathing himself and asks Ron if he can help.
intention: Ron has to decide whether to help his grandpa bathe.
moral_action: Ron decides to stay in the same room as his grandpa as he bathes.
moral_consequence: Ron's grandpa is able to get help in case he needs it.
immoral_action: Ron chooses not to help his grandpa and starts to ignore him.
immoral_consequence: Ron's grandpa is at risk of slipping in the tub.

norm: It's rude not to tell somebody your name
situation: Betsy is greeting her stressed out coworker for the first time.
intention: Betsy wants to make her coworker feel better.
moral_action: Betsy shows coworker around the office and gives them her contact information.
moral_consequence: Betsy's coworker makes it to the office without help the next day due to Betsy's directions.
immoral_action: Betsy tells her coworker a joke about her name.
immoral_consequence: Her coworker feels foolish in front of others when they ask questions using the fake name.

norm: Spoiling movies for people could make them angry at you.
situation: Mark invites his friend over to watch his favorite movie.
intention: Mark wants to share the movie with his friend.
moral_action: Mark enjoys watching his friend's reactions to the plot twists in the movie.
moral_consequence: Mark's friend loves the movie, and they now have something else in common.
immoral_action: Mark announces the ending halfway through the movie in his excitement.
immoral_consequence: Mark's friend leaves after saying there is no point watching a spoiled movie.

norm: You shouldn't track your child's phone.
situation: Penny's teenage son Adam is going out with his friends for the evening.
intention: Penny wants to know where Adam will be.
moral_action: Penny asks Adam to text her and let her know where he's going to be.
moral_consequence: Adam agrees and texts Penny from his destination.
immoral_action: Penny uses a phone tracking app and monitors Adam's whereabouts all evening.
immoral_consequence: Adam notices the app on his phone and is upset that his mother doesn't trust him.

norm: It's wrong to lose your virginity to a one-night stand.
situation: Ron is single and his friends tease him for being a virgin.
intention: Ron wants to have sex.
moral_action: Ron finds a long-term girlfriend and sleeps with her.
moral_consequence: Ron feels happy that he's so closely connected with someone he cares about.
immoral_action: Ron goes to a club and sleeps with a random woman.
immoral_consequence: Ron feels unsatisfied by the one-night stand.

norm: You should not talk freely about sensitive subjects.
situation: Jackie is at a work party.
intention: Jackie wants to converse with her coworkers.
moral_action: Jackie talks to the coworkers about a vacation she took.
moral_consequence: Jackie's boss tells her that sounds like a good place to visit and shares his own experiences.
immoral_action: Jackie tells the coworkers all about her and her husband's sex life.
immoral_consequence: Jackie's boss calls her into his office the next day and reprimands her for being inappropriate.

norm: It's good to finally come clean about one's transgressions.
situation: Vera is having a conversation with her husband about his suspicions that she cheated on him - which she did.
intention: Vera wants her husband to keep on loving her.
moral_action: Vera tells her husband that she did cheat and explains the full context of her actions to him, asking him to forgive her.
moral_consequence: Vera is relieved that her secret is out and that she came out clean.
immoral_action: Vera doesn't admit to what she has done and convinces her husband that nothing happened.
immoral_consequence: Vera feels dirty and dishonest.

norm: People should not sever relationships with family without good reason.
situation: Biff lives with his parents who are strictly religious.
intention: Biff wants freedom to explore other worldviews and lifestyles.
moral_action: Biff calmly explains his feelings to his parents and continues his personal exploration.
moral_consequence: Biff is free to explore and though his parents disapprove he is still a loving family member.
immoral_action: In frustration, Biff moves out on his own and cuts ties with his parents.
immoral_consequence: Biff is free to explore but misses out on the emotional support of a family.

norm: You should not overwhelm others with your problems.
situation: Olivia is meeting up with her friends and has had some problems in her home life lately.
intention: Olivia wants to tell her friends about her problems.
moral_action: Olivia briefly mentions her problems at home, but asks others how they are doing.
moral_consequence: Olivia's friends let her know they feel for her and try to help her.
immoral_action: Olivia goes on and on about all her problems at home and won't let anyone else talk.
immoral_consequence: Olivia's friends find her exhausting and stop hanging out with her.

norm: It's good to stop unwanted romantic gestures.
situation: Judy works at an office with Jonas, who constantly blows her kisses throughout the day in spite of her best attempts to ignore him.
intention: Judy needs to decide how to respond to Jonas.
moral_action: Judy decides it's best to tell Jonas that she doesn't appreciate his behavior.
moral_consequence: Jonas apologizes to Judy, saying he was just kidding and stops doing it, which makes Judy happy.
immoral_action: Judy decides it's best to just continue ignoring Jonas's behavior.
immoral_consequence: Jonas gets progressively more and more brazen in his advances, making Judy even more uncomfortable.

norm: It's okay to want to keep your baby.
situation: At only 18 years old Chastity recently found out that she is pregnant but the father Biff is encouraging her to terminate the pregnancy.
intention: Chastity wants to decide whether to comply with Biff's suggestion to end the pregnancy.
moral_action: Chastity goes against Biff's wishes and carries the pregnancy to term.
moral_consequence: Chastity loves her new born baby and motherhood provides her a happy and fulfilling life.
immoral_action: Chastity agrees with Biff and goes to a clinic to have an abortion.
immoral_consequence: Chastity later regrets her decision and wishes she had had the child.

norm: You should not expect someone to do more than you.
situation: Vince and some workers are shoveling coal in a boxcar and is very tired.
intention: Vince wants to take a break.
moral_action: Vince asks everyone if they can take a break together.
moral_consequence: Everyone gets a break and is refreshed for work.
immoral_action: Vince tells the others to keep working and takes a ten minute break.
immoral_consequence: The other workers get upset with Vince and refuse to work, causing trouble.

norm: It's wrong to call people losers.
situation: Benny is at work when his manager Glenn fires another employee, Jordan.
intention: Benny wants to say something to Jordan.
moral_action: Benny tells Jordan to hang in there and that he'll find another job soon.
moral_consequence: Jordan is a little happy that Benny is being supportive in his rough moment.
immoral_action: Benny tells Jordan that only losers get fired, and he is therefore a total loser.
immoral_consequence: Jordan is angry and sad and Benny is now just making everything even worse.

norm: You should respect people that are fat.
situation: Mark and his sister Jane are having a conversation about a party Mark is planning.
intention: Mark needs to decide who to invite.
moral_action: Mark invites Jane even though he is concerned of what his friends will think about Jane being overweight.
moral_consequence: Jane is happy she gets to go to the party.
immoral_action: Mark tells Jane she can't come because she is too heavy.
immoral_consequence: Jane feels disrespected.

norm: It's not okay to be dependent on your phone.
situation: Carol hasn't seen her friend Jimmy in a long time, and is visiting to catch up and reconnect.
intention: Carol wants to be connected to friends.
moral_action: Carol turns her phone on silent and keeps it in her purse to focus fully on the conversation with Jimmy.
moral_consequence: Jimmy feels appreciated and grateful for Carol's undivided attention.
immoral_action: Carol is constantly interrupting the conversation with Jimmy to respond to non-urgent text messages and check her social media pages.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy feels ignored and hurt by Carol's constant focus on her phone.

norm: You shouldn't put up with self-centered kids.
situation: Larry is at the mall with his son Max who demanded ice cream, which Larry refused and now Max is throwing a tantrum.
intention: Larry wants to respond to Max's tantrum.
moral_action: Larry tells Max that he's going to stuff him in a box and mail him to Rwanda if he doesn't quiet down.
moral_consequence: Max learns to respect his father and do as he says which serves him well later in life.
immoral_action: Larry tells Max fine, he'll get him ice cream if he just stops screaming.
immoral_consequence: Max learns that he can get anything he wants as long as he annoys his father enough which destroys him later in life.

norm: It's good to discuss your activities with others.
situation: James was getting coffee in the break room when one of his coworkers asked what he did that weekend.
intention: James wants to get to work without wasting time on small talk.
moral_action: "James says, ""I went wind-surfing, check out the pictures on my Facebook!""."
moral_consequence: James is able to substitute social media for time-consuming in-person interaction.
immoral_action: "James says ""None of your business,"" and walks to his desk to start working."
immoral_consequence: James' coworkers talk behind his back about how abrasive he is.

norm: It's good to want someone to be healthy.
situation: Heike is a nurse working at an institution when an outbreak of a virus comes to the institution.
intention: Heike wants the virus to go away.
moral_action: Heike takes steps to keep people separated and make sure that everyone practices good hygiene.
moral_consequence: Only a few people get sick and the rest stay healthy and productive.
immoral_action: Heike lets people get infected, so they will get immunity and the virus will disappear.
immoral_consequence: The people who get infected get very sick, with some going to the hospital.

norm: It's rude to negatively comment on someone's look.
situation: Ron is sitting and having dinner with Sammy, when they see a relatively ugly woman walk by.
intention: Ron wants to make Sammy laugh.
moral_action: Ron tells a funny joke he heard on Reddit the other day.
moral_consequence: Sammy laughs, and as the woman hears the end of the joke, knows he's laughing at the joke.
immoral_action: Ron comes up with a pretty witty comment on the girl's looks.
immoral_consequence: Sammy laughs and the woman knows they're laughing at her, and gets hurt.

norm: You shouldn't sleep with someone who is already married.
situation: Justin runs into his friend Shana from high school who had a crush on him, and finds out she's married.
intention: Justin wants to take some time to reconnect with Shana.
moral_action: Justin has a short chat with Shana at the store, learning about her kids and current job, then hugs her and says goodbye.
moral_consequence: Shana goes home to her husband, mentions meeting an old friend, and continues her life.
immoral_action: Justin invites Shana out for drinks, and has sex with her in a motel after they get drunk.
immoral_consequence: Shana commits infidelity and feels guilty, and her marriage suffers moving forward.

norm: You shouldn't let your friends ask out your crush.
situation: Aaron is attracted to a girl, but his friend Steve is asking Aaron if he can ask her out.
intention: Aaron doesn't want to disappoint his friend.
moral_action: Aaron tells Steve that he doesn't want to fight over her and suggests another lady that they both know.
moral_consequence: Aaron and Steve don't have conflicting interests in the same girl and both end up happy.
immoral_action: Aaron allows Steve to ask out the girl, who accepts Steve's request.
immoral_consequence: Aaron feels very jealous towards Steve, dividing them and ending their friendship.

norm: It's not okay to hurt an animal.
situation: Sara has a cat that will not stop scratching the very expensive furniture.
intention: Sara wants to discourage the cat's behavior.
moral_action: Sara finds natural scents that discourage the cat from being interested in the furniture.
moral_consequence: Sara feels like a loving pet owner.
immoral_action: Sara hits her cat whenever he scratches the furniture.
immoral_consequence: Sara feels guilty for hitting her cat.

norm: You should always clean up after your pets.
situation: Meagan is walking her dog on a beautiful day and a man is also walking in their direction.
intention: Megan wants her dog to poop.
moral_action: Megan's dog defecates on the grass next to the sidewalk, and she picks it up with a paper and puts it in the trash.
moral_consequence: The man approaching walks over the spot where the dog pooped, but because Megan cleaned up, his shoes stay clean, and she feels like a responsible dog owner.
immoral_action: Megan's dog defecates on the grass next to the sidewalk, but she doesn't pick it up.
immoral_consequence: The man approaching steps in dog poop and Megan feels foolish.

norm: Stealing is bad.
situation: Matt is at the grocery store and realizes he forgot his wallet.
intention: Matt needs food.
moral_action: Matt decides to head home, get his wallet and return to shopping.
moral_consequence: Matt enjoys a tasty meal when he arrives home.
immoral_action: Matt decides to walk out of the store with a full cart without paying.
immoral_consequence: Matt is identified by security cam as a thief and is arrested.

norm: It's rude to tell someone you don't like a gift.
situation: Dave's wife comes home after work and surprises Dave with a gift of a new shirt.
intention: Dave wants to react to the offer of the gift.
moral_action: Dave tells his wife that it's so nice of her to bring him an unexpected gift like that.
moral_consequence: Dave's wife is really delighted that Dave loves the surprise and it warms her to see him happy.
immoral_action: Dave tells his wife that the shirt is a color that he hates and that he probably won't wear it.
immoral_consequence: Dave's wife is really sad that he hates his gift and is embarrassed about the choice she made.

norm: You shouldn't be greedy when it comes to booze.
situation: Baldwin and his friends are enjoying a twelve pack of beer while tailgating.
intention: Baldwin wants something relaxing to drink.
moral_action: Baldwin orders a cooling fruit smoothie from the pop up food cart for himself and his friends.
moral_consequence: Baldwin's friends are able to enjoy the night completely sober.
immoral_action: Baldwin drinks eight cans of beer.
immoral_consequence: Baldwin's friends are unable to have a drink.

norm: It's wrong to trade people counterfeit items.
situation: Steve needs some extra money to pay some bills.
intention: Steve wants to sell some things to a pawn shop.
moral_action: Steve sells some of his personal items that he doesn't use much anymore.
moral_consequence: Steve gets the money to pay for the bills.
immoral_action: Steve sells a counterfeit watch, trying to make some more money.
immoral_consequence: The pawn shop finds out and calls the police on Steve.

norm: It's bad to not feed your children.
situation: Melanie is unemployed and at home with her three kids who are hungry and malnourished.
intention: Melanie wants to save money.
moral_action: Melanie applies for food stamps and makes her kids healthy, simple meals.
moral_consequence: Melanie's kids start to feel better and healthier, and she keeps them.
immoral_action: Melanie eats only a small amount herself and doesn't give her kids any food.
immoral_consequence: Melanie's kids get sicker and sicker and may get taken away from her.

norm: It's bad to not think about the environment.
situation: Stuart is finishing his coffee as he walks to work one morning.
intention: Stuart wants to dispose of the empty coffee cup.
moral_action: Stuart carries the empty cup along with him until he encounters a recycling bin which he uses to dispose of the cup properly.
moral_consequence: Stuart is happy to recycle the cup and continues on his way to work.
immoral_action: Stuart carelessly drops the empty coffee cup on the sidewalk.
immoral_consequence: A police officer happens to be across the street and cites Stuart for littering.

norm: You shouldn't make fun of someone for mental health issues.
situation: Robert's seat in the classroom is next to a classmate who is severely depressed.
intention: Robert wants to speak to his depressed classmate.
moral_action: Robert shares some kind words with his classmate and tries to cheer him up.
moral_consequence: Robert's classmate appreciates Robert's effort and Robert develops a positive reputation.
immoral_action: Robert calls his classmate weak-willed and proceeds to laugh at him.
immoral_consequence: Robert gets ignored by his classmate as he starts getting viewed as a mean callous person.

norm: It's wrong for men to sexually harass women.
situation: Ashton has a coworker Ashley at the cubicle next to him who he's very attracted to.
intention: Ashton wants to let Ashely know he's interested.
moral_action: Ashton asks Ashley if she'd like to have a coffee sometime, and when she says no he respects it.
moral_consequence: Ashley considers Ashton a gentleman, and their workplace relationship remains professional.
immoral_action: Ashton wolf whistles every day as Ashley walks by his cubicle.
immoral_consequence: Ashley thinks Ashton is a disgusting pig and reports him to HR.

norm: You shouldn't break up with someone via text message.
situation: Ian is in a romantic relationship that has been toxic lately.
intention: Ian wants to split up with his partner.
moral_action: Ian informs is partner that they need to have a talk, and they both know that they will be discussing splitting up.
moral_consequence: Ian's partner is relieved that Ian is ready to move on because they were too, and they break up amicably.
immoral_action: Ian lacks the courage to communicate which caused the problems to begin with, so he sends a text about to his partner informing them the relationship is over.
immoral_consequence: Ian's partner is profoundly irritated by the idea that Ian would break up with them via a text and vows revenge.

norm: Siblings are expected to stand up for each other.
situation: Even though both Gary and his brother both drew on the walls, their mom only yelled at Gary's brother.
intention: Gary wants to decide what to do.
moral_action: Gary steps in and tells his mom that he was involved as well.
moral_consequence: Gary's brother is glad that Gary took some of the heat away from him.
immoral_action: Gary doesn't get involved and ignores his brother for the rest of the day.
immoral_consequence: Gary's brother feels betrayed and loses his trust in Gary.

norm: You shouldn't brag about your IQ.
situation: Rory and his friends took an IQ test, and Rory scored the highest of the group.
intention: Rory wants to comment on the IQ test result.
moral_action: Rory tells them that IQ test aren't everything and that any of them could have scored better on a different day.
moral_consequence: Rory's friends appreciate Rory's humbleness and continue to hang out with him.
immoral_action: Rory brags to all of them about how much smarter he is than the rest of them.
immoral_consequence: Rory's friends get tired of his bragging and stop hanging out with him.

norm: It's good to help out people in the military.
situation: Jon runs into a military veteran at the store who mentions being down on his luck financially.
intention: Jon wants to do something positive towards the veteran.
moral_action: Jon decides to give the veteran a bit of cash to hold him over.
moral_consequence: The veteran is able to use the cash to cover short term expenses.
immoral_action: Jon thanks the veteran for his service and shakes his hand.
immoral_consequence: The veteran is unable to find anyone to help his situation.

norm: It's bad to cheat on your wife.
situation: John feels that he and his wife are in a rut, when one of his female coworkers invites him to join her at a romantic restaurant.
intention: John wants to do something different for a change.
moral_action: John declines the invitation from his coworker and instead takes his wife for the romantic dinner.
moral_consequence: John's wife is pleased with the change in their routine and reciprocates which leads to a revitalization of their marriage.
immoral_action: John tells his wife that he’s going to visit his parents, but instead joins his coworker for a romantic meal and a night together.
immoral_consequence: John's wife finds out he cheated and leaves him.

norm: It's rude to tell someone their baby is ugly.
situation: Gina is visiting her friends for the first time since their baby was born, and is surprised to see that the baby is very ugly.
intention: Gina wants to avoid lying to her friends.
moral_action: Gina compliments the cute baby clothes without commenting on the baby's appearance.
moral_consequence: Gina's friends are glad that Gina liked the cute baby clothes.
immoral_action: Gina makes a face and bluntly says to her friends that their new baby is ugly.
immoral_consequence: Gina's friends and offended and ask her to leave their house.

norm: You should discuss issues calmly with others.
situation: Faris and Emile disagree on how to do a group project.
intention: Faris wants to convince Emile his way is better.
moral_action: Faris calmly lays out all the reasons he believes his approach is best.
moral_consequence: Emile listens to Faris and takes his views into serious consideration.
immoral_action: Faris berates Emile and shouts down his ideas for being inferior.
immoral_consequence: Emile is unwilling to cooperate with Faris and becomes contentious as well.

norm: You shouldn't give your employee discount to strangers.
situation: Jane is working retail at a big box store and has to deal with lots of customers of varying degrees of politeness all day.
intention: Jane wants customers she interacts with to be satisfied.
moral_action: Jane is dealing with a particularly rude customer and follows protocol by deferring them to her manager.
moral_consequence: Jane's manager handles the situation and then apologizes to Jane that she had to deal with the customer which calms Jane down.
immoral_action: Jane is dealing with an irate customer who is making unfounded complaints so Jane appeases them by offering her employee discount to their purchase.
immoral_consequence: Jane is reprimanded for this behavior by her boss as it violates the rules of her employment.

norm: You shouldn't let your friends harass your little siblings.
situation: Jeff's little brother is getting talked down to by Jeff's friends as Jeff is walking in.
intention: Jeff wants to make a comment about the situation.
moral_action: Jeff adamantly tells his friends to stop treating his little brother like this and takes control of the situation.
moral_consequence: Jeff's friends respect his decision and the little brother starts admiring Jeff more.
immoral_action: Jeff joins his friends in talking down to his little brother.
immoral_consequence: Jeff's little brother eventually grows up to despise Jeff and his friends.

norm: It's good to help people out and enjoy it.
situation: Josh committed a crime and has been ordered by the judge to perform community service, and decides to work at a homeless shelter's soup kitchen.
intention: Josh needs to serve people food.
moral_action: Josh serves out Soup with energy and enthusiasm, and gives a kind word to every recipient.
moral_consequence: The people at the shelter really appreciate Josh's efforts.
immoral_action: Josh does the bare minimum and hates every minute of it.
immoral_consequence: The people at the shelter aren't happy with the way Josh treats them.

norm: It's not socially acceptable to use discriminatory slurs.
situation: John is at home with wife and kids listening to the news about the black lives matter movement.
intention: John wants to feel good about himself.
moral_action: John states out loud that black people matter just as much as white people do.
moral_consequence: John's kids and wife respect him more and grow up healthy.
immoral_action: John says out loud that these 'n-words' oughtta go back to Africa.
immoral_consequence: John's kids and wife respect him less and may grow up to be racists too.

norm: You shouldn't wear inappropriate clothes to a funeral.
situation: Chuck has to go to a funeral and needs to get a new suit because his old one is too small.
intention: Chuck wants to wear a suit that fits to the funeral.
moral_action: Chuck buys a plan black suit and a matching tie to wear.
moral_consequence: Chuck gets compliments on how well he looks at the funeral.
immoral_action: Chuck buys a lime green suit with purple stripes and wears it at the funeral.
immoral_consequence: Chuck gets a lot of weird looks from people at the funeral.

norm: It's lazy to not clean up after yourself.
situation: James just finished cooking a big meal and the kitchen is a mess.
intention: James wants to eat his food while it's hot.
moral_action: James eats his food and then washes all the dishes and wipes down the counters.
moral_consequence: James comes out to a ready kitchen when he needs to make breakfast the next morning.
immoral_action: James eats his food and leaves the dishes to sit for several days.
immoral_consequence: James' roommate eventually puts the dirty dishes on James' bed.

norm: It's okay to be wrong and learn from your mistakes
situation: Janice is in math class, about to receive back a homework assignment that she is confident she did poorly on.
intention: Janice wants to find out her homework grade.
moral_action: Janice looks at the grade on her paper and then goes through each question to understand what she did wrong.
moral_consequence: Janice better understands the material and improves her grade on the next exam.
immoral_action: Janice looks at the grade at the top of the returned homework assignment then tears up the assignment.
immoral_consequence: Janice doesn't learn what she did wrong on the homework assignment and ends up doing poorly on her next exam.

norm: It's rude to leave class before it's finished.
situation: Kenny is in his last class of the day when he starts to feel a bit nauseous and feverish.
intention: Kenny wants to feel better.
moral_action: Kenny sips some water and sticks it out until the end of the class to avoid causing a disruption.
moral_consequence: Kenny's professor finishes the rest of the lecture smoothly.
immoral_action: Kenny quietly gets up and leaves class to visit the bathroom.
immoral_consequence: Kenny's professor sees him leave, loses his concentration, and is flustered for the rest of the lecture.

norm: It is polite to include others when ordering food.
situation: Joe is out with his friend Julia at a local restaurant, and they're both very hungry, however Julia is broke.
intention: Joe needs to order food.
moral_action: Joe orders an appetizer platter and offers Julia a share.
moral_consequence: Julia ends up having something to eat and appreciates Joe's kindness.
immoral_action: Joe orders an entree for himself and does not share.
immoral_consequence: Julia ends up having nothing to eat and remains hungry.

norm: It's wrong to use your roommate's things without their permission.
situation: Jeff has been stuck inside all day, and he thinks he should get some fresh air.
intention: Jeff wants to go for a bike ride.
moral_action: Jeff's bike has a flat, so he decides to wait until his roommate Ben comes home to ask if he can borrow his bike to go ride.
moral_consequence: When Jeff asks Ben if he can borrow his bike he says yes and tells him to have fun.
immoral_action: When Jeff sees that his bike has a flat he decides to take the other bike that belongs to his roommate Ben.
immoral_consequence: When Ben gets home and sees that his bike is missing he thinks that someone stole it.

norm: It's not polite to treat a partner with disrespect.
situation: Steve and his girlfriend are having dinner with friends at a nice retaurant.
intention: Steve wants to talk all about his new job promotion.
moral_action: Steve tells his friends about his promotion and includes his girlfriend in the conversation.
moral_consequence: Steve's girlfriend enjoys talking to everyone and has a nice time at dinner.
immoral_action: When his girlfriend talks Steve tells her nobody wants to hear what she has to say and continues talk about his promotion.
immoral_consequence: His girlfriend gets very upset and immediately starts to cry.

norm: It is good to uphold laws and regulations
situation: Jim is driving towards the airport.
intention: Jim wants to make it to his flight on time.
moral_action: Jim drives within the speed limit and reaches the airport quickly.
moral_consequence: Jim arrives on time to board his flight.
immoral_action: Jim drives above the speed limit in an attempt to get to the airport faster.
immoral_consequence: Jim is pulled over by a police officer for speeding, is ticketed, and misses his flight.

norm: It's nice to feed dogs.
situation: Jon walks home from work everyday and passes by a vacant lot with stray dogs.
intention: Jon wants to do something to help the dogs.
moral_action: Jon buys a bag of dog food and puts a little out in a bowl for the dogs every day when he walks past.
moral_consequence: Jon helps the dogs keep from going hungry and starving to death.
immoral_action: Jon calls animal control about the stray dogs.
immoral_consequence: Jon is responsible for the dogs being euthanized because the animal shelter is overcrowded.

norm: It's good to speak up when someone is being unsafe.
situation: Larry is at a party when his friend is about to leave drunk.
intention: Larry wants to be a good friend.
moral_action: Larry asks his friend not to drive and offers to call him an uber.
moral_consequence: Larry's friend gets home safe and thanks Larry for being a good friend.
immoral_action: Larry lets his friend leave because he doesn't want to offend him.
immoral_consequence: Larry's friend gets a DWI and Larry feels guilty.

norm: It is nice to give company to sick children.
situation: Sam's son hasn't been feeling well because his stomach is bothering him.
intention: Sam wants his son to stay home.
moral_action: Sam calls into work and stays home with his sick son.
moral_consequence: Sam is able to help his son into the bathroom when he feels the need to vomit.
immoral_action: Sam goes to work while his son stays home in bed alone.
immoral_consequence: When Sam gets back from work, he has to change the sheets on the bed because his son couldn't get out of bed.

norm: It is not okay to call people names.
situation: Charlie is getting into an argument with the manager of a grocery store who he feels is ripping him off.
intention: Charlie wants to tell the manager off.
moral_action: Charlie tells the manager why he is very unhappy in the store.
moral_consequence: The manager listens, and tells Charlie he'll look into fixing things.
immoral_action: Charlie raises his voice and starts cursing at the manager and calling him names.
immoral_consequence: The manager turns away from Charlie and tells him to leave, not bothering with him anymore.

norm: You should never try to be someone you're not.
situation: Fred is a pretty nerdy kid with few friends at school.
intention: Fred wants to make some friends.
moral_action: Fred is his normal self and doesn't try to fit in with any particular group.
moral_consequence: A small group of people who are nerdy like Fred take him in, and they become friends.
immoral_action: Fred pretends he loves sports so that he fits in with some kids at school.
immoral_consequence: Fred is miserable because he can't do the things he likes, and he has to follow something he's not interested in.

norm: It's wrong to ignore your parents.
situation: James always laughed at his parents when they told him he had to wear a helmet when biking.
intention: James wanted to avoid looking dorky in front of his friends.
moral_action: James insisted that his parents buy him a helmet with the logo of his favorite heavy metal band.
moral_consequence: "When James' friends saw his helmet, the only thing they said was, ""Metal""."
immoral_action: James refused to take his parents' advice and rode his bike without a helmet.
immoral_consequence: James hit a rock while biking without a helmet, flew ten feet away and cracked his skull open.

norm: It's hurtful to disparage a persons sexual prowess.
situation: Mary is having a tryst with her lover.
intention: Mary wants to tell her lover what she thinks.
moral_action: Mary tells her sex partner that he is a great performer in the bedroom.
moral_consequence: Mary's lover gain self-confidence and becomes a great parter to Mary and all his future lovers.
immoral_action: Mary tells her lover that he is lousy at making love.
immoral_consequence: Mary's lover develops a complex toward women and has trouble with all his future relationships.

norm: Calling a person crippled is considered rude.
situation: Alex is in an argument with a guy in a wheelchair over a parking spot he pulled into.
intention: Alex wants to express his frustration.
moral_action: Alex tells the man just because he isn't in a wheelchair, doesn't mean he doesn't deserve the spot.
moral_consequence: Alex gets the spot, the wheelchair guy wheels off irritated, but understanding.
immoral_action: Alex laughs at the wheelchair guy and calls him a cripple to his face.
immoral_consequence: Someone overhears and records it, and it goes viral on twitter and Alex gets fired.

norm: Ending a friendship can be hurtful.
situation: James' friend started posting disturbing QAnon conspiracy theories all over Facebook.
intention: James wants to avoid being spammed with conspiracy theories.
moral_action: James convinces his friend to talk to a therapist and changes the subject whenever politics or QAnon comes up.
moral_consequence: James' friend eventually begins to question the conspiracy theories he's been reading.
immoral_action: James ends his friendship with the QAnon conspiracy theorist and blocks him on social media.
immoral_consequence: James' friend spirals further down the rabbit hole, since the only people who will hang out with him are other conspiracy theorists.

norm: It's rude to delete people's numbers.
situation: Jane likes to clear out clutter on her phone from time to time.
intention: Jane wants to get rid of stuff on her phone.
moral_action: Jane isn't sure if the numbers are important, so she keeps them just in case.
moral_consequence: She gets an important call from one of the numbers and Jane answers the call.
immoral_action: Jane deletes a bunch of phone numbers that she doesn't recognize.
immoral_consequence: Some of her friends cannot call Jane since their number no longer shows up in her phone.

norm: It's rude to make jokes that offend others.
situation: Billy is with a group of coworkers at happy hour when the group starts taking turns telling jokes.
intention: Billy wants to fit in with his coworkers.
moral_action: Billy tells a joke about their boss that everyone thinks is hilarious.
moral_consequence: Billy's coworkers think he is very funny and start talking to him more at work.
immoral_action: Billy tells a joke about Mexicans that offends one of his coworkers who is dating a Mexican woman.
immoral_consequence: Billy's coworker gets angry Billy and leaves, making Billy feel bad.

norm: It's bad to mistreat your family.
situation: Dave beats up Kyle and takes his things because he's the big brother, so he's in charge.
intention: Dave wants to continue to be in charge.
moral_action: Dave learns that you shouldn't mistreat your family, so he starts treating Kyle better.
moral_consequence: Kyle forgives Dave, and they start having fun together rather than fighting.
immoral_action: Dave keeps taking Kyle's stuff because he's the boss and such.
immoral_consequence: Kyle decides to go to the gym until he's strong enough to fight back against Dave.

norm: It's wrong to vandalize someone's property
situation: James, an ardent Democrat, lives next door to someone who put up a MAGA sign with a giant portrait of Trump.
intention: James wants to express his disapproval of Trump.
moral_action: James puts up his own sign supporting Joe Biden and calling Trump a criminal.
moral_consequence: James' neighbors scowl at his sign every time they walk their dog past it.
immoral_action: James spray-paints a diaper and a Nazi flag on his neighbor's portrait of Trump.
immoral_consequence: James' neighbors call the cops, but they can't prove James was responsible.

norm: It's wrong to marry someone for their money.
situation: Jake, who comes from a poor family, is dating Eve, who makes a six-figure salary.
intention: Jake wants to be rich.
moral_action: Jake gets to know Eve as a person and realizes they are not compatible.
moral_consequence: Jake breaks up with Eve, even though she is wealthy.
immoral_action: Jake marries Eve and then spends all her money.
immoral_consequence: Eve realizes Jake only married her for her money and files for a divorce.

norm: You shouldn't cancel on someone's wedding at the last minute.
situation: Christine is a photographer who has agreed to photograph her best friend Judy's wedding on Valentine's day.
intention: Christine wants to celebrate Valentine's day with her boyfriend.
moral_action: Christine invites her boyfriend to Judy's wedding where they can dance and have dinner for Valentine's day.
moral_consequence: Christine is able to work and enjoy being a guest at Judy's wedding at the same time.
immoral_action: Christine decides to have a romantic night out with her boyfriend, skipping Judy's wedding entirely.
immoral_consequence: Judy has no photographs to remember her wedding day by.

norm: It feels bad to be alone on your birthday.
situation: Jon has a birthday tomorrow and doesn't have any plans yet.
intention: Jon wants to do something different for his birthday.
moral_action: Jon invites a group of friends to try a fine dining restaurant.
moral_consequence: Jon has a memorable birthday and cherishes the memory for a long time.
immoral_action: Jon eats at a fine dining restaurant which is normally out of his budget.
immoral_consequence: Jon feels lonely eating such a nice dinner at the restaurant alone.

norm: It's wrong to grope people without their permission.
situation: Jake is dancing at a club with an attractive woman, and they are having good time.
intention: Jake wants to make a move on the girl.
moral_action: Jake gets the girl's number and asks her out on dates before making any moves.
moral_consequence: The girl becomes comfortable enough with Jake to be intimate with him.
immoral_action: Jake, while dancing close to the girl, runs his hang against her leg.
immoral_consequence: The girl is offended by his actions and runs away from him.

norm: Going to a stripclub is seedy.
situation: A group of friends including Al are deciding how to spend the evening.
intention: Al wants the group to have a fun night.
moral_action: Al suggests the group sing Karaoke.
moral_consequence: Everyone in the group agrees that it is an activity that could suit all.
immoral_action: Al suggests going to a strip club.
immoral_consequence: Some of the group members are offended by the aggressive display of sexuality and feel uncomfortable.

norm: It's good to delegate duty to subordinates.
situation: Mike is the managing team leader of a group and has just been given an extremely important assignment to complete.
intention: Mike wants to make sure the assignment is completed to exacting standards.
moral_action: Mike divides the assignment among the team members and monitors their work closely.
moral_consequence: Mike's team is productive and learn some new skills on the assignment.
immoral_action: Mike does the work on his own because he doesn't want his subordinates messing it up.
immoral_consequence: Mike's team have free time at work that is now being wasted.

norm: It's good to seek professional help when you've been abused.
situation: Mary just got out of an abusive relationship.
intention: Mary wants to try and get over all the horrible things that happened to her in her relationship.
moral_action: Mary goes to a therapist who gives her some advice for coping with problems like the ones she's faced.
moral_consequence: Mary is able to process all the negative things that happened to her and move on with her life.
immoral_action: Mary starts drinking heavily on a regular basis, making it easier for her forget about her problems.
immoral_consequence: Mary becomes an alcoholic and loses her job.

norm: You shouldn't throw away food that your parents give you.
situation: James' father always packs him a nutritious lunch to take to school.
intention: James wants to eat cookies with his lunch.
moral_action: James asks his father if he can have cookies as a snack instead of crackers.
moral_consequence: James' father agrees to pack cookies if James eats an extra piece of fruit.
immoral_action: James throws his packed lunch away and begs his friends for money to buy cookies.
immoral_consequence: James' teacher sees him throwing the food away and tells his father, who scolds James.

norm: It's wrong to intentionally disrupt someone when they're working.
situation: Wendel and Nancy are plumbers who like to prank each other, and Nancy is working on a pipe with a blowtorch.
intention: Wendel wants to scare Nancy with a prank.
moral_action: Wendel waits until Nancy is done with the blowtorch to prank Nancy.
moral_consequence: Nancy is startled, then laughs and says she'll get Wendel next time.
immoral_action: Wendel decides to prank Nancy while she is soldering the pipe.
immoral_consequence: Nancy jumps in fear and burns her hand with the blowtorch.

norm: It's rude to sabotage someone's life and smile about it.
situation: Jack does not like Ben and has the opportunity to ruin a major project that Ben is working on.
intention: Jack wants to make a decision on the opportunity.
moral_action: Jack resists the temptation to ruin Ben's major project and simply observes Ben.
moral_consequence: Jack watches Ben become successful and they eventually become friends.
immoral_action: Jack ruins Ben's major project and smiles about it in front of Ben.
immoral_consequence: Ben figures out Jack was responsible and retaliates against Jack for ruining his project.

norm: It's wrong to tell other people what to eat
situation: Jen is dating a partner who has an unhealthy diet and has been gaining a lot of weight.
intention: Jen wants to help her partner lose weight.
moral_action: Jen makes going to the gym a couple's activity for them.
moral_consequence: Jen's partner has fun working out with her at the gym and becomes healthier.
immoral_action: Jen tells her partner to stop eating fast food and gives him a hard time if he doesn't listen.
immoral_consequence: Jen's partner feels self conscious about their body and weight.

norm: It's mean to embarrass people in public.
situation: Andrea is out to lunch with her friends when she notices Jenna has a period stain on her skirt.
intention: Andrea wants to let Jenna know about the stain.
moral_action: Andrea pulls Jenna aside and offers her a jacket to cover up the stain.
moral_consequence: Jenna is grateful to Andrea and thinks she is a good friend.
immoral_action: Andrea tells Jenna that she has a period stain on her skirt in front of the rest of the table.
immoral_consequence: Jenna is embarassed and the rest of the group thinks Andrea is rude.

norm: You should always brush your hair before work or school.
situation: Janice has an important business meeting today that will determine if she gets a promotion.
intention: Janice wants to get to her meeting on time.
moral_action: Janice sets her alarm 15 minutes early and takes some time to style her hair before leaving for work.
moral_consequence: Janice makes a good impression with her professional look.
immoral_action: Janice hurries out the door in the morning without doing her hair or makeup.
immoral_consequence: Janice makes a bad impression at the meeting due to her disheveled appearance.

norm: You should be honest with someone you have feelings for.
situation: Max is approached by a classmate named Emily, asking him to the prom, but he doesn't like Emily.
intention: Max wants to answer Emily's request.
moral_action: Max declines Emily's request, stating he doesn't think they get along well.
moral_consequence: Emily understands and Max feels happy for being honest.
immoral_action: Max tells Emily he loves her, and he would love to go to the prom with her.
immoral_consequence: Max hates his time at the prom and Emily senses it.

norm: People should give content a chance before deciding it's inferior.
situation: Hank is surfing on a video website when he sees an excellent video with very few reviews.
intention: Hank wants to decide whether to view the video or not.
moral_action: Hank decides to watch the video and promotes it once he realizes that it's good.
moral_consequence: The video gets more views and goes viral, helping many people who watch it.
immoral_action: Hank decides that the video doesn't have reviews because it's not as good as it seems and ignores it.
immoral_consequence: The video doesn't get the views that it deserves and people are not benefited by it.

norm: It is bad to steal from your job.
situation: Belinda works at a retail store, but has fallen behind on her bills lately.
intention: Belinda wants to get more money to pay her bills.
moral_action: Belinda does some side jobs online for extra money when she is not at work.
moral_consequence: Belinda soon has enough money to pay all her bills .
immoral_action: Belinda skims from the register to get the money for her bills.
immoral_consequence: The manager finds out Belinda is stealing when her drawer is short and fires her on the spot.

norm: It's inconsiderate to ignore social norms when in public.
