situation: Pola is in a crowded line at the airport and feels a bit bubbly.
intention: Pola wants to somehow get out a burp or two.
moral_action: Pola covers her mouth and lets them out slowly.
moral_consequence: Pola feels better and hasn't attracted attention.
immoral_action: Pola lets them come naturally.
immoral_consequence: Others make comments and Pola feels uncomfortable and gross.

norm: It's unwise to jump off tall cliffs.
situation: Andrew and his friends are daredevils who enjoy partaking in extreme activities.
intention: Andrew wants to find his next adrenaline rush.
moral_action: Andrew and his friends go to a go-cart racing track.
moral_consequence: Andrew gets an adrenaline rush in a safe and controlled environment.
immoral_action: Andrew and his friends go to the quarry and dare each other to jump from the highest cliff into the water.
immoral_consequence: Andrew takes the dare and breaks a leg on the way down.

norm: It's good to want to keep people safe at night.
situation: Melinda is a single mother at home with three two year olds on a Friday night and is bored.
intention: Melinda wants to go dancing at the danceclub.
moral_action: Melinda hires a babysitter for her kids and then goes dancing.
moral_consequence: Melinda's kids are happy and safe and stay in the house.
immoral_action: Melinda leaves her kids on the floor and drives off to the danceclub.
immoral_consequence: Melinda's kids become anxious and cry out and child services is called and takes them away.

norm: It's rude to tell someone they are a bad singer.
situation: Mary attends a singing contest in which her friend, Sue, is one of the contestants.
intention: Mary wants to respond to Sue's singing.
moral_action: Mary suggests Sue to listen more to rhythmic beats so that she can improve her skills.
moral_consequence: Sue thanks Mary for her good advice and feels supported.
immoral_action: Mary criticizes that Sue did not follow the rhythm correctly.
immoral_consequence: Sue feels hurt and immediately starts to cry.

norm: It's bad to be too controlling of your teenager.
situation: Melanie has a sixteen year old daughter Kelly who asks her mother if she can go to a friend's house that evening.
intention: Melanie wants to answer her daughter.
moral_action: Melanie allows her daughter to go to her friend's house but first talks to her about making responsible decisions.
moral_consequence: Kelly listens to her mother's advice on being responsible and is determined not to lose her mother's trust.
immoral_action: Melanie tells her daughter that she cannot go anywhere without an adult chaperone and does not let her leave the house.
immoral_consequence: Kelly resents her mother for not trusting her, and she looks for ways to sneak around instead.

norm: It's wrong to keep secrets from your future spouse.
situation: Mindy has a daughter from her prior marriage and has agreed to marry Sam soon.
intention: Mindy wants to decide where to accommodate her daughter.
moral_action: Mindy tells Sam that she has a daughter when Sam proposes to her, and that her daughter will live them after marriage.
moral_consequence: Sam thanks Mindy for her honesty and happily accepts her daughter as his stepdaughter.
immoral_action: Mindy asks her parents to take care of her daughter and doesn't tell Sam the she has a daughter.
immoral_consequence: Sam feels betrayed and offended after knowing Mindy has a daughter, and decides to break up with her.

norm: It's rude to pull a girl's hair
situation: Frank notices his crush playing on the swings with his classmates.
intention: Frank wants to get his crush's attention.
moral_action: Frank stands behind his crush's swing offering to push her.
moral_consequence: Frank and his crush have a fun conversation as he pushes her.
immoral_action: Frank tugs on his crush's hair while calling her name.
immoral_consequence: Frank is smacked in the face by his crush.

norm: You shouldn't surprise people if they don't like it.
situation: Julie's father, who's turning 90 soon, has a heart condition and is scared of loud noises.
intention: Julie wants to celebrate her father's 90th birthday.
moral_action: Julie takes her father to a very fancy restaurant on his birthday.
moral_consequence: Julie's father has a delicious meal and thinks Julie is thoughtful and kind.
immoral_action: "Julie throws a surprise party for her father and everyone yells ""Surprise!"" when he comes home."
immoral_consequence: Julie's father is startled and has a heart attack and dies.

norm: One should try to work out their differences with classmates.
situation: John is just starting his first year of college and had a disagreement with a classmate.
intention: John wants to put the disagreement in the past.
moral_action: John approaches the classmate the following day and openly listens to their point view until they reach a mutual apology.
moral_consequence: John and the classmate become great friends over the course of John's college years and John makes lifelong memories.
immoral_action: John just ignores the issue and the classmate he had the issue with going forward.
immoral_consequence: John develops a reputation that causes people to avoid him and makes his college experience lonely and unpleasant.

norm: It's rude to accuse someone of something without proof.
situation: Doug is at a performance pickpocket show when he realizes that his wallet is missing and has no idea when he lost it.
intention: Doug wants to find the reason for his missing wallet.
moral_action: Doug retraces his steps and checks in the hotel room, the last place that he had it, and finds it there.
moral_consequence: The performer's reputation stays intact and Doug has his wallet back without problems.
immoral_action: Doug stands up and accuses the performer of taking his wallet and demands that he be arrested.
immoral_consequence: The performer feels somewhat offended at the baseless accusation and allows himself to be searched, proving his innocence.

norm: You shouldn't use emergency exit doors unless there's an emergency.
situation: William just finished his shopping at the mall and is at the very back of the building, far from the main exit.
intention: William wants to exit the shopping mall.
moral_action: William walks back through the entire length of the shopping mall and exits through the front doors.
moral_consequence: William finishes his shopping trip successfully and without incident.
immoral_action: William decides to take a shortcut and leaves through the emergency exit at the back of the building.
immoral_consequence: William is reprimanded by a security guard  who was standing outside in the parking lot and saw him use the exit.

norm: You shouldn't be mean to people with lower intellectual capacity.
situation: Naime is getting frustrated training her new mentally disabled coworker.
intention: Naime wants to vent her frustrations.
moral_action: Naime posts about her frustrations online seeking advice for her current situation.
moral_consequence: Naime gains knowledge on how to properly communicate with her coworker.
immoral_action: Naime compares her coworkers intelligence to a earthworm before walking off.
immoral_consequence: Naime is written up after her boss discovers her behavior.

norm: It is good to be considerate to your neighbors.
situation: Kevin who lives next door to Neil is planning a party for the weekend.
intention: Kevin wants to decide the number of attendees.
moral_action: Kevin decides to invite only four key couples for a total of eight people.
moral_consequence: Neil sleeps soundly as he cannot hear a thing from the small gathering next door.
immoral_action: Kevin decides to invite everyone he knows which is about two hundred people.
immoral_consequence: Neil is annoyed when over two hundred people show up and make a lot of noise and ruckus all night.

norm: It's bad to ditch your significant other on a holiday.
situation: Paul is invited to go on a camping trip with his friends, but it is on the same day as Valentine's day, which he normally spends with his girlfriend Laura.
intention: Paul wants to respond to the invitiation.
moral_action: Paul turns down the camping invitation and spends Valentine's day with his girlfriend instead.
moral_consequence: Laura is glad to spend Valentine's day with Paul, and she gets him a nice gift.
immoral_action: Paul decides to go on the camping trip and leaves his girlfriend alone on Valentine's day.
immoral_consequence: Laura is angry and upset, and she breaks up with Paul a week later.

norm: You shouldn't ditch people when you're out shopping with them.
situation: Mary is out shopping with friends.
intention: Mary feels tired and wants to go home.
moral_action: Mary asks her friends to wrap up their trip, explaining her fatigue.
moral_consequence: Mary's friend's offer to find another way home and allow Mary to leave guilt free.
immoral_action: Mary waits until her friends are trying on clothes and leave.
immoral_consequence: Mary's friends are angry and vow to not speak to her for weeks.

norm: It's rude to disregard or refuse compliments.
situation: Dave is at the bar ordering a drink when the bartender tells him he's really good looking.
intention: Dave wants to respond to the compliment.
moral_action: Dave tells the bartender that she's really being nice and that he's flattered by her nice words.
moral_consequence: The bartender is happy that Dave received her compliment well and that he seems happy about it.
immoral_action: Dave tells the bartender that she's just flattering him and that he knows for a fact he's not especially attractive.
immoral_consequence: The bartender is shocked and insulted at the insinuation that she's lying and feels Dave is pathetic.

norm: It's good to offer to help someone moving heavy boxes.
situation: Jon's friend called him to help him move heavy boxes to his new apartment.
intention: Jon wants to order a pizza.
moral_action: Jon says he will help his friend if they can get pizza to eat after.
moral_consequence: Jon's friend pays for the pizza to show he was thankful.
immoral_action: Jon tells his friend he is too busy and goes out to eat pizza.
immoral_consequence: Jon's friend doesn't talk to him for three weeks because he didn't help.

norm: It's wrong not to care when someone is being abused.
situation: Jerry has been seeing his mom abuse his dad, and is not happy about it.
intention: Jerry wants to talk to his dad about the abuse he witnesses.
moral_action: Jerry tells his dad he cares a lot about what is happening, and he wants to help stop it.
moral_consequence: Jerry's dad agrees and Jerry feels relieved.
immoral_action: Jerry tells his dad he doesn't care his dad is being abused but that it needs to stop regardless.
immoral_consequence: Jerry's dad gets angry at Jerry, and they have an argument.

norm: It's bad to be attracted to someone else's husband.
situation: Mary is at a barbecue at a friend's house.
intention: Mary wants to socialize with the other party goers.
moral_action: Mary avoids having one-on-one conversations with married men at the gathering and joins in on the conversation a group of women are having.
moral_consequence: Mary has a nice evening at the social gathering and makes some new friends.
immoral_action: Mary flirts with her friend's husband.
immoral_consequence: Mary's friend notices Mary's behavior and asks her to leave immediately.

norm: You shouldn't destroy someone else's property.
situation: Ash is watching tv at Jacob's house, and the TV remote is having problems working which annoys Ash.
intention: Ash wants to express his anger.
moral_action: Ash releases his emotions by writing a critical review of the product on Amazon.
moral_consequence: Ash feels better because he warned people about the horrible remote.
immoral_action: Ash tosses raises his voice and tosses the remote against the coffee table breaking it.
immoral_consequence: Ash has to buy a new remote to Jacob.

norm: It's okay to go home when you're sick.
situation: Sam has an important math test at school during the last period of the day but is feeling increasingly sick.
intention: Sam wants to pass his math class.
moral_action: Sam informs his math teacher that he is feeling sick and goes home to rest.
moral_consequence: Sam's teacher is understanding and allows him to make up the test at a later date.
immoral_action: Sam tries to tough it out and remains at school to take the test.
immoral_consequence: Sam feels very ill and has trouble concentrating on the test which results in a bad grade.

norm: You shouldn't steal your coworkers food.
situation: Ivan is at the work cafeteria with both their food on the table while his coworker Liam is getting a drink.
intention: Ivan wants to take a bite of the food.
moral_action: Ivan reaches for his own plate and grabs a little bite of food from it.
moral_consequence: Liam sees Ivan eating his own food and rushes back to join him.
immoral_action: Ivan reaches over into Ivan's plate and grabs a bite of a piece of his food.
immoral_consequence: Liam sees Ivan eating food from his plate and is livid that Ivan is spreading his germs on his plate.

norm: It's bad to let an addiction take over your life.
situation: Joey is a recovering addict who used to use heroine and alcohol.
intention: Joey wants to have a good time.
moral_action: Joey goes to a baseball game with a few of his friends.
moral_consequence: Joey has a great time spending time doing something other than drugs.
immoral_action: Joey calls his dealer and gets him to deliver some heroin to him.
immoral_consequence: Joey passes out and doesn't wake up until the next day.

norm: It is not okay to lie about things.
situation: Chad had broken the vase in his mother's house playing catch with his brother.
intention: Chad wants to tell his mother that the vase is broken.
moral_action: Chad tells his mother that the vase is broken and that it's partially his fault.
moral_consequence: Chad's mother is somewhat upset, but she tells Chad she is proud of him for telling the truth.
immoral_action: Chad tells his mother that the vase was knocked down by the dog running through the room.
immoral_consequence: Chad's mother finds out what really happened, and she grounds him for a week.

norm: It's expected that you report illegal activity to the police.
situation: Roger is going to his bank to deposit money.
intention: Rodger wants to get in and out quickly.
moral_action: Roger notices an acquaintance stealing money but alerts the security guard right away.
moral_consequence: Rodger is praises for his action and is given a reward.
immoral_action: Roger sees an acquaintance grab money from behind the counter when the teller isn’t looking.
immoral_consequence: Rodger pretends his didn’t see it and later gets brought in for abetting a crime.

norm: It's kind to visit the terminally ill.
situation: Hailey is about to go to work when she finds out her aunt is in hospice and won't likely survive the night.
intention: Hailey wants to go to work.
moral_action: Hailey lets her work know she will be late and visits her aunt for a few minutes.
moral_consequence: Hailey gets to say goodbye to her aunt, and her aunt is comforted a little before she dies.
immoral_action: Hailey goes to work right away and her aunt passes away while she is there.
immoral_consequence: Hailey never gets to say goodbye to her aunt and feels great regret.

norm: Always leave injured animals to the professionals.
situation: Sue is in her yard one morning when she sees an injured raccoon.
intention: Sue wants to save the animals life.
moral_action: Sue stays inside and calls animal control about the situation.
moral_consequence: The animal is safely rescued and sent to an animal rehabilitation center.
immoral_action: Sue gets a blanket and first aid kit and decided to take the raccoon in.
immoral_consequence: Sue is bitten by the raccoon who is rabid and ends up needing a series of rabies shots.

norm: It's rude to spread rumors about other people's health care.
situation: James hears a rumor about a girl Jane in his school about having herpes.
intention: James wants to have fun with his friends.
moral_action: James and his friends scold people for spreading that rumor and end up taking Jane to a movie and have a lot of fun.
moral_consequence: Jane makes a new friend group and thanks James and his friends for being good people.
immoral_action: James and his friends spread the rumor that Jane has herpes and finds it fun in the moment.
immoral_consequence: Jane has a mental breakdown in school and ends up dropping out and ruining her education.

norm: It's unacceptable to steal your neighbour's pet.
situation: George lives next to a neighbor that has a dog that barks all night.
intention: George wants to be able to sleep in peace and quiet.
moral_action: George calls his neighbor and asks if they can keep the dog quiet.
moral_consequence: George's neighbor goes out and buys a muzzle to put on the dog at night.
immoral_action: George takes his neighbors dog and drops it off outside of town.
immoral_consequence: George is eventually arrested for the theft of his neighbor's dog.

norm: It's good to call your kids.
situation: Jane's kids are all adults and have moved out of the home.
intention: Jane wants to maintain a relationship with her kids.
moral_action: Jane makes a point to schedule a day of the week for calling each of her kids.
moral_consequence: Jane is always abreast on the goings-on in all of her kid's lives.
immoral_action: Jane just waits until her kids come to visit for the holidays to catch up with what is going on in their lives.
immoral_consequence: Jane's kids grow distant from her over the years as once a year isn't enough time to fill their mother in about their lives.

norm: You should be able to control your emotions.
situation: Xavier asks for a toy in a store, but his parents tell him no.
intention: Xavier wants to get the toy.
moral_action: Xavier asks his parents if he can work for the toy.
moral_consequence: Xavier's parents agree and make him do chores for them in exchange for the toy.
immoral_action: Xavier cries and fusses about the toy, ignoring his parents pleas to be quiet.
immoral_consequence: Xavier's parents haul Xavier out of the store to avoid more embarrassment, denying him the toy.

norm: It's bad to do anything that affects your child's health.
situation: Ron is a cigarette smoker and sometimes uses cigarettes while indoors.
intention: Ron wants to avoid smoking in the cold.
moral_action: Ron goes out to smoke in his car.
moral_consequence: The kids are healthier without second hand smoke in the house.
immoral_action: Ron smokes in a closed room in the house.
immoral_consequence: The kids are affected by second hand smoke permeating the house.

norm: It's inappropriate to sleep with coworkers.
situation: Joe has been single for a long time and finds a specific coworker to be very attractive.
intention: Joe wants to find a partner to be physically intimate with.
moral_action: Joe downloads a dating app and makes a profile.
moral_consequence: Joe meets a nice woman off the dating site.
immoral_action: Joe hooks up with the coworker.
immoral_consequence: Joe is worried a manager will find out and it will affect his job.

norm: People shouldn't say negative things about customers while at work.
situation: Clara places an item on the counter of guest services after a tense encounter with a customer.
intention: Clara wants to vent her frustrations.
moral_action: Clara closes her eyes ranting to herself in her own head for a moment before getting back to work.
moral_consequence: Clara learns how to become more in tune with her emotions.
immoral_action: Clara tells her coworker about the event mimicking the customer's voice.
immoral_consequence: Clara is written up by her boss after the customer overhears her words.

norm: Nudity in front of children is wrong.
situation: Sandy is babysitting when the young girl vomits on her, with the fluid seeping through her shirt and onto her bra.
intention: Sandy needs to change her shirt quickly.
moral_action: Sandy went into the bathroom to wash off her shirt and bra.
moral_consequence: The girl's parents gave her extra money the next time she babysat to pay for a new shirt.
immoral_action: Sandy takes her shirt and bra off in front of the girl.
immoral_consequence: The girl's parents informed Sandy she would not be babysitting for them anymore.

norm: It's bad to steal someone's gold when they find it.
situation: Ron and Jamie are panning for gold on vacation.
intention: Ron wants to find some gold and take it home.
moral_action: Ron keeps panning for gold and finds a nice bit to take home.
moral_consequence: Ron is happy he and Jamie had a good time on vacation.
immoral_action: When Jamie back is turned Ron takes some of her gold.
immoral_consequence: Jamie finds out Ron takes her gold and the trip is ruined.

norm: It's wrong to harass other people because of their ethnicity.
situation: Mario meets a man named Tom at the bus stop who is black.
intention: Mario wants to start a conversation with Tom.
moral_action: Mario talks about the sports game that was on television last night.
moral_consequence: Tom mentions all of the plays that were going on in the game.
immoral_action: Mario makes fun of Tom because of his hair texture and his skin.
immoral_consequence: Tom walks away from Mario and never talks to him again.

norm: It's immoral to abandon your children.
situation: Mary, a single mother, has recently gotten into a serious relationship with a wealthy man.
intention: Mary wants to get married.
moral_action: Mary makes sure her boyfriend and her kids get to know each other in comfortable setting.
moral_consequence: Mary's kids are able to form a relationship with their mum's boyfriend.
immoral_action: Mary leaves her kids with her parents in order to be free to pursue her relationship.
immoral_consequence: Mary's kids grow distant as time passes.

norm: It's good to make coffee for yourself.
situation: Ted is working long hours on an important project at the office and begins to get tired and unfocused.
intention: Ted wants to feel more energized.
moral_action: Ted makes himself a cup of coffee in the office break room before returning to his desk.
moral_consequence: The coffee makes Ted feel alert and energetic and his productivity soars.
immoral_action: Ted does a few jumping jacks and splashes cold water on his face.
immoral_consequence: Ted feels refreshed momentarily but quickly gets tired again and his productivity suffers.

norm: You shouldn't try to pet someone's dog without their permission.
situation: Max is walking down the street and another person's dog approaches him wagging it's tail.
intention: Max wants to welcome the dog he sees.
moral_action: Max verbally greets the dog and smiles at it.
moral_consequence: The dog continues wagging it's tail and Max waves the dog goodbye.
immoral_action: Max decides to pet the dog without the owner's permission.
immoral_consequence: The dog bites Max on the hand and Max cries out in pain.

norm: It's rude to crowd in line.
situation: Jimmy wants goes to the opening night of a movie and see the line for tickets is long.
intention: Jimmy wants to get on the line for tickets.
moral_action: Jimmy gets on the line and stays an arms length from the people in front of him.
moral_consequence: Jimmy and the people in front of him stand in the line undisturbed.
immoral_action: Jimmy gets on the line and walks into the people in front of him.
immoral_consequence: The people in front of Jimmy start a fight with him for invading their personal space.

norm: You should tell someone if their partner is manipulating them.
situation: Lisa's friend Stephanie has a manipulative boyfriend whom she loves dearly and thinks that such behavior is normal.
intention: Lisa wants Stephanie to be safe.
moral_action: Lisa tells Stephanie that her boyfriend fits the profile of an manipulative man and that she is in danger.
moral_consequence: Stephanie realizes that she's in trouble and begins to work to change the situation.
immoral_action: Lisa tells Stephanie that if she ever needs help with anything, she'll be there to support her, hoping that she'll call.
immoral_consequence: Stephanie doesn't see the problem and the manipulation continues, wearing Stephanie down.

norm: It is wrong to ditch a friend.
situation: Kasey is waiting for his friend to return from the bathroom when his friends invite him to play a carnival game.
intention: Kasey wants to have fun.
moral_action: Kasey plays games on his cell phone until his friend comes out of the bathroom.
moral_consequence: Kasey's friend feels happy that his friend is by his side.
immoral_action: Kasey goes with other friends to play the carnival games.
immoral_consequence: 's friend wanders around depressed as he searches for Kasey.

norm: You should not overextend yourself financially.
situation: Peter and Carol who have $1000 in their budget are shopping for necessities at the mall, when a salesman asks Peter if he'd like to buy a $1300 watch.
intention: Peter wants to respond to the salesman.
moral_action: Peter tells the salesman that although the watch is beautiful and finely crafted, he cannot aford such luxuries.
moral_consequence: Carol is delighted that she has a prudent partner who helps to guard their finances.
immoral_action: Peter tells the salesman that the watch is one of a kind and that he must have it, and agrees to pay buy it.
immoral_consequence: Carol is stressed beyond belief as all the money for their necessities is now gone.

norm: It's mean to make a middle schooler cry.
situation: Karen shows her father Bob a painting she made in middle school last week.
intention: Bob wants to tell Karen his thoughts on the painting.
moral_action: Bob tells Karen that the painting looks great.
moral_consequence: Karen is overjoyed and hugs Bob.
immoral_action: Bob tells Karen that he doesn't like the painting.
immoral_consequence: Karen runs to her room crying.

norm: It's good to do something nice for someone else.
situation: Tanya is doing some organizing of her apartment.
intention: Tanya wants to get rid of items that she has no need for any longer.
moral_action: Tanya donates her unwanted items to the local Goodwill store.
moral_consequence: Tanya is given a receipt to write her donation to charity off of her taxes and saves some money.
immoral_action: Tanya puts all her unwanted items in the apartment complex trash compactor.
immoral_consequence: Tanya is called out and shamed by her neighbor for not donating perfectly good items to charity.

norm: It's hurtful to cut off family members.
situation: Jen and her cousin have never gotten along well and recently got into a huge argument over politics.
intention: Jen wants to avoid dealing with her cousin.
moral_action: Jen takes a break from her cousin and keeps her at a distance.
moral_consequence: Jen's cousin eventually approaches her and apologizes for her behavior.
immoral_action: Jen stops communicating with her cousin altogether and then blocks her.
immoral_consequence: Jen's cousin is hurt that her own family member would block her.

norm: It's wrong to disturb other's with noise.
situation: Andy is at the library studying and it is quiet around him.
intention: Andy wants to listen to music.
moral_action: Andy plays a song through his earbuds on his phone.
moral_consequence: The other people in the library do not notice Andy's music and are undisturbed.
immoral_action: Andy plays a song through the speakers on his phone.
immoral_consequence: The other people in the library are distracted by Andy's music.

norm: You should be respectful of people at memorial services.
situation: Eric is at a former friend's wake with some other friends and is standing in a very long line to see the coffin.
intention: Eric wants to talk with his friends.
moral_action: Eric talks with his friends about the person who died and all the fun experiences they had together.
moral_consequence: The family hears about the experiences and gives Eric an opportunity to share them up-front.
immoral_action: Eric starts joking about how the people around them look as dead as the person in the coffin.
immoral_consequence: The family gets very offended and kicks Eric out of the funeral home.

norm: It's rude to accuse people.
situation: Walter walks into a room to see Jody looking at his books and soon realizes one of them, which is on the coffee table, is missing from the shelf.
intention: Walter wants to find his missing book.
moral_action: Walter describes the missing book and asks Jody if she's seen it laying somewhere.
moral_consequence: Jody points to the book on the coffee table, and Walter thanks her.
immoral_action: Walter instantly accuses Jody of taking the book without asking.
immoral_consequence: Jody gives him a dirty look and points to the book on the coffee table, then leaves and never speaks to Walter again.

norm: It's wrong to want something bad to happen to someone.
situation: Max gets into a fight with his friend.
intention: Max wants to feel better.
moral_action: Max tells his friend how he is hurt by him.
moral_consequence: Max has a conversation with his friend and the whole situation resolves peacefully.
immoral_action: Max wishes his friend would get hurt in an accident.
immoral_consequence: Max's friend dies in an accident and Max never recovers from the guilt.

norm: It's nosy to get involved with other people's relationships.
situation: Carmen is talking to her friend Stella about an argument she had with her boyfriend earlier that day.
intention: Stella wants to help Carmen.
moral_action: Stella listens to Carmen vent about the argument and asks if there's anything she can do to help.
moral_consequence: Carmen feels supported by her friend.
immoral_action: Stella contacts Carmen's boyfriend and tells him he should apologize.
immoral_consequence: Carmen's boyfriend thinks Carmen asked Stella to intervene, and breaks up with her.

norm: You shouldn't be a burglar.
situation: Mike hangs out with a group of friends who decide one night to rob a rich man's house that lives near them.
intention: Mike wants to keep his friends.
moral_action: Mike declines to go with his friends and stays clear of the entire situation in case it goes badly.
moral_consequence: Mike's friends stay friends with him and Mike continues to live an honest and productive life.
immoral_action: Mike joins his friends, helps to break into the rich man's house, and takes a lot of stuff from him.
immoral_consequence: The rich man is furious that his house was broken into and Mike turns to a life of crime.

norm: It's good to intern for things and gain experience.
situation: Courtney is in college and it is time for summer break.
intention: Courtney wants to do something during the summer.
moral_action: Courtney applies for an internship and interns during the summer.
moral_consequence: Courtney learns how to operate in a working environment.
immoral_action: Courtney spends her time shopping at the mall during the summer.
immoral_consequence: Courtney spends money and does not learn anything.

norm: It is hurtful to destroy someone's work.
situation: Mya has entered the science fair, but she knows that Kim is working on a better project than hers.
intention: Mya wants to win the science fair.
moral_action: Mya changes her topic to a more interesting one and works extra hard.
moral_consequence: Mya comes out first in the science fair and beats Kim fair and square.
immoral_action: Mya goes to Kim's house and rips apart Kim's science project to shreds.
immoral_consequence: Kim's parents catch Mya and Mya is disqualified from the science fair.

norm: It's good to give cute names to your pets.
situation: Jane is at the crowded dog park with her pet dog.
intention: Jane wants to teach her dog to socialize with other dogs.
moral_action: "Jane begins to introduce herself and her dog to other park visitors and calls her dog over with the nickname ""Pumpkin""."
moral_consequence: The other dog owners find the name cute and compliment it and introduce their dogs to hers.
immoral_action: Jane begins to introduce herself and her dog to other park visitors and calls her pet over with cruel vulgar names.
immoral_consequence: The other dog owners are taken aback and slowly dismiss themselves one by one until Jane finds herself alone.

norm: It's wrong not to show strong support for a partner.
situation: Jeffrey's wife Karen has just told him that she wants to start a small craft business, so she needs them to take out a joint loan.
intention: Jeffrey wants to avoid losing a lot of money.
moral_action: Jeffrey tells Karen that he will happily support her and her decision as long as she takes a class on business management to try and ensure some success.
moral_consequence: Karen is thrilled that Jeffrey is so supportive, and she puts a lot of energy and effort into the business in order to make sure she doesn't disappoint him.
immoral_action: Jeffrey tells Karen that this is a very bad idea and that the business will likely not succeed, so he won't sign for the loan.
immoral_consequence: Karen is offended that Jeffrey doesn't believe in her and her skills.

norm: You shouldn't play in the street.
situation: James is holding a ball on a street with moving cars when he spots a friend waving to him.
intention: James wants to consider tossing the ball to his friend.
moral_action: James decides to hold onto the ball and greets his friend.
moral_consequence: James' friend suggests going somewhere safer to play ball and has a good time with James.
immoral_action: James decides to play around by throwing the ball to his friend.
immoral_consequence: James' friend fails to catch the ball and gets injured trying to retrieve it from the road with moving cars.

norm: It is wrong to allow abuse in a relationship.
situation: Shay and Juan are in a relationship, and Juan recently hit Shay after an argument.
intention: Shay has to decide how to respond to getting hit.
moral_action: Shay threatens to leave Juan if he ever hits her again.
moral_consequence: Juan never thinks about hitting Shay again, and Shay is seen as assertive.
immoral_action: Shay decides to stay with Juan thinking that Juan just made a mistake.
immoral_consequence: Juan continues to become more and more abusive as time goes on.

norm: You should be careful to not bump into others.
situation: Jack was taking part in a marathon and was in the starting line with a large crowd of runners.
intention: Jack wants to get ahead of the crowd of runners.
moral_action: Jack waits until the crowd disperses and weaves his way through the other runners.
moral_consequence: Jack is able to get ahead of the crowd and set a good running pace.
immoral_action: Jack pushes his way through the crowd of runners, jostling other runners as he tried to get ahead.
immoral_consequence: The other runners get angry at Jack's behavior and pushes him back.

norm: It's good to help prevent theft in your neighborhood.
situation: Wayne's neighborhood has had a crime spree recently.
intention: Wayne wants to protect his valuables.
moral_action: Wayne starts a neighborhood watch program and sets up some cameras.
moral_consequence: The thief is caught on camera and identified by witnesses, ending the crime spree.
immoral_action: Wayne gets an alarm system and locks up his valuables.
immoral_consequence: Other houses without alarms are broken into and stolen from, hurting the owners.

norm: It's rude to move others' belongings without their permission.
situation: Chris is cleaning his dorm and comes across baggages belonging to his roommate.
intention: Chris wants to consider moving the baggages.
moral_action: Chris chooses to leave his roommate's baggages alone and focuses on cleaning around it.
moral_consequence: Chris' dorm is fairly well cleaned and Chris' roommate is satisfied with the results.
immoral_action: Chris decides to move his roommate's baggages into the corner of the room.
immoral_consequence: Chris' roommate is furious at Chris for moving his stuff and loudly expresses his frustration.

norm: It's bad to cheat on exams.
situation: Joan has to take an important test that makes up half of her grade.
intention: Joan wants to get an A on the test.
moral_action: Joan dedicates an entire week to study for the test.
moral_consequence: Joan gets an A on the test and a congratulatory message from her teacher.
immoral_action: Joan hides notes in her sleeve to use on the test.
immoral_consequence: Joan is caught using the notes by her teacher and kicked out of class.

norm: People shouldn't get drunk before class.
situation: Charlene sitting around her dorm room and is bored before class.
intention: Charlene wants to find something to do to kill time before until class.
moral_action: Charlene decides to read a chapter of a novel that she is reading to pass the time before going to class.
moral_consequence: Charlene is attentive in class and learns the subjects presented with ease.
immoral_action: Charlene decides to drink some leftover liquor from the weekend and then heads to class.
immoral_consequence: Charlene throws up in the middle of class and is very embarrassed.

norm: It's good to help people having difficulty in their marriages.
situation: Jane's coworker is crying in the next cubicle after finding out her husband has been unfaithful.
intention: Jane wants to talk to her colleague.
moral_action: Jane recommends a marriage counselor to her colleague and offers her a tissue.
moral_consequence: Jane's coworker is grateful and calls the recommended marriage counselor.
immoral_action: Jane tells her colleague to quiet down because she can't concentrate on her work.
immoral_consequence: Jane's colleague is embarrassed and retreats to the bathroom.

norm: It is bad to harbor hate and resentment toward others
situation: John was tricked into making a fool of himself by Mark and is embarrased.
intention: John wants to get even with Mark.
moral_action: John plays a prank on Mark the following day, making Mark look foolish.
moral_consequence: John feels satisfied that he got even with his Mark and moves on.
immoral_action: John plots a disproportionate revenge towards Mark over the course of many years before finally getting even.
immoral_consequence: John wastes a ton of time on plotting that could be better spent doing something more productive.

norm: You shouldn't break the rules of an establishment.
situation: Valerie, a smoker, is in a restaurant with a no-smoking policy and suddenly has the urge to smoke.
intention: Valerie wants to smoke a cigarette.
moral_action: Valerie goes outside to smoke at a designated smoking area.
moral_consequence: Valerie smokes her cigarette and is able to finish her meal.
immoral_action: Valerie lights up a cigarette at the table and smokes.
immoral_consequence: Valerie is kicked out of the restaurant and banned from returning.

norm: It's wrong to get involved with married people.
situation: Bob, who is married, and Steve, who is single, have both showed interest in wanting to start a romantic relationship with April.
intention: April is single and wants very badly to be in a romantic relationship.
moral_action: April chooses to go out on a date with Steve.
moral_consequence: April and Steve develop a satisfying romantic relationship.
immoral_action: April begins to have an affair with Bob.
immoral_consequence: Bob's wife finds out and publicly humiliates April over the affair.

norm: It's wrong to invade other peoples personal space.
situation: Becca is sitting quietly in her room with the door shut, reading a book.
intention: Becca's roommate Jen wants to talk to Becca about something.
moral_action: Jen knocks on Becca's door and asks if Becca has a moment to talk.
moral_consequence: Jen respects Becca's privacy, and Becca can decide whether or not to engage.
immoral_action: Jen opens the door and walks into Becca's room without knocking first.
immoral_consequence: Jen invades Becca's privacy, and Becca is annoyed with Jen.

norm: It's rude to keep other people waiting for you
situation: Utari is playing a match in Overwatch when his alarm notifies him of his meeting with a client in twenty minutes.
intention: Utari wants to have fun.
moral_action: Utari drives to the meeting place, and reads his favorite book while he waits for his client.
moral_consequence: Utari and his client bond over talking about the book.
immoral_action: Utari continues playing Overwatch until he reaches a stopping point.
immoral_consequence: Utari is thirty minutes late for the meeting, and he's unable to make a deal with his client.

norm: It's not okay to support a evil leader.
situation: A politician in Don's country wants to deport all Mexicans from his country.
intention: Don has to decide whether to vote for the politician.
moral_action: Don realizes that Mexicans have never bothered him and votes for someone else.
moral_consequence: The man has one less vote, and Don doesn't have to feel guilty.
immoral_action: Don realizes that he doesn't have any Mexican friends, so he votes for him.
immoral_consequence: The man ends up following through on his promise, and Don feels bad.

norm: You shouldn't eat your child's food.
situation: Henry hadn't eaten all day and has just finished eating a light dinner with his son.
intention: Henry wants to eat until he is full.
moral_action: Henry whips up a quick sandwich.
moral_consequence: Henry's son feels enthusiastic when he remembers his leftover food.
immoral_action: Henry eats his son's leftover food.
immoral_consequence: Henry's son is disappointed when he looks to eat the food later.

norm: You shouldn't abuse your privileges.
situation: Jim is a business executive who is looking to hire a new secretary.
intention: Jim wants to hire a loyal secretary.
moral_action: Jim looks for applicants that have been with their last job for multiple years.
moral_consequence: Jim's new secretary gets a new job without having to be exploited for it.
immoral_action: Jim promises his applicants that they'll get the job if they're willing to have a relationship with him.
immoral_consequence: Jim's new secretary feels pressured have a relationship in order to get a job.

norm: It's good to not be racist.
situation: Karen is organizing a group project to meet after work and knows that Michelle, a women of color, has kids.
intention: Karen wants to schedule meetings in a way that fits everyone's schedule.
moral_action: Karen asks the entire group if any of them have family obligations after work.
moral_consequence: Karen's coworkers are grateful to have their needs accommodated.
immoral_action: Karen asks Michelle if she needs to find a babysitter since she must be a single mom.
immoral_consequence: Karen's coworkers are appalled at her assumption.

norm: You shouldn't put your life on hold for somebody else
situation: Jenna had just been accepted to college, but her boyfriend told her his band had a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to tour.
intention: Jenna wants to support her boyfriend.
moral_action: Jenna and her boyfriend decide to date long distance while Jenna goes to college.
moral_consequence: While dating long-distance is challenging, Jenna feels relieved that she's still making progress towards her goals.
immoral_action: Jenna decides to take a gap year and tour with her boyfriend's band.
immoral_consequence: Jenna and her boyfriend break up halfway through the year, leaving her sad and aimless.

norm: It's fun to have a good dessert after dinner.
situation: Beth is hosting a dinner, and everyone has finished the main course.
intention: Beth wants to give everyone a dessert.
moral_action: Beth gives everyone a piece of cherry pie with whipped cream.
moral_consequence: The guests rave about the delicious dessert.
immoral_action: Beth gives everyone a mint Lifesaver candy.
immoral_consequence: The guests are satisfied, but no one comments on the dessert.

norm: It's bad to remain silent about an assault.
situation: Brad was assaulted and robbed in the alley near his home.
intention: Brad wants to move on after the assault.
moral_action: Brad calls the police to make a report about the incident.
moral_consequence: The police catch the person who assaulted Brad, and he is unable to attack anyone else.
immoral_action: Brad goes home after the attack too embarrassed to tell anyone about the incident.
immoral_consequence: The person who attacked Brad continues to attack and rob other people in the neighborhood.

norm: It's good to admit you were rude to someone.
situation: Cal pushes past a woman when trying to order a drink at the bar.
intention: Cal wants to address the woman.
moral_action: Cal tells the woman that he's sorry and didn't see her.
moral_consequence: The woman will accept Cal's apology and not think ill of him.
immoral_action: Cal tells the woman she should not stand around in front of the bar.
immoral_consequence: The woman will think Cal is push and a jerk.

norm: It's good to greet family members when you see them.
situation: Timmy goes to visit his grandparents' house for the day, and they say hello to him.
intention: Timmy wants to watch TV.
moral_action: Timmy says hello to his grandparents and asks if he can watch their TV.
moral_consequence: Timmy's grandparents are proud of little Timmy's manners and give him a treat.
immoral_action: Timmy runs to his grandparents' TV without saying a word to them and watches a show.
immoral_consequence: Timmy's grandparents think Timmy is a very impolite little boy for not even saying hello to them.

norm: You shouldn't force-kiss people.
situation: Steve is sitting around the campfire having a few beers with a mixed group of friends.
intention: Steve wants to find an outlet for his amorous feelings.
moral_action: Steve chats up an attractive girl and gets consent to give her a kiss.
moral_consequence: Steve has a lovely time making out with his new found female friend.
immoral_action: Steve leans over and grabs the face of the girl next to him and lays a kiss on her unexpectedly.
immoral_consequence: Steve gets beaten up by the girl's boyfriend and his friends for his crude action.

norm: It's good to go to the library to study.
situation: Fabio has a biology test tomorrow, but he's sick of being at home.
intention: Fabio wants to go somewhere.
moral_action: Fabio goes to the library to read his textbook.
moral_consequence: He runs into some of his classmates, and they have fun studying together.
immoral_action: Fabio spends the evening hanging out at the arcade.
immoral_consequence: Fabio fails his biology test.

norm: Fantasizing constantly is excessive.
situation: Norm is a published writer and his agent expects him to deliver another novel soon.
intention: Norm wants his next novel to be a great and original idea.
moral_action: Norm spends some time musing about some ideas then starts putting together an outline he is satisfied with.
moral_consequence: Norm is able to compile a novel he is proud of and it becomes his bestseller.
immoral_action: Norm spends his weeks day dreaming about different scemarios for his next novel without writing anything down.
immoral_consequence: Norm never gets his next novel written because he spends all his time just imagining it and his agent drops him.

norm: You should ask before borrowing others' items.
situation: Jim and Gabe are both at home for the holidays and jim's car breaks down.
intention: Jim wants to buy some last-minute gifts at the store.
moral_action: Jim asks Gabe if he could drive Gabe's car to buy some things at the mall.
moral_consequence: Gabe goes with Jim to the mall because Gabe also needed to buy gifts.
immoral_action: Jim takes Gabe's car keys while Gabe is still asleep and drives to the mall.
immoral_consequence: Gabe and Jim get into an argument because Gabe also needed to use the car.

norm: You shouldn't have crushes on people at work.
situation: James just started a new job as an accountant and one of his coworkers is very attractive.
intention: James wants to feel less bored at work.
moral_action: James chats with his attractive coworker about their favorite films while they fill out spreadsheets.
moral_consequence: The conversation makes accounting less mind-numbing for James and his attractive colleague.
immoral_action: James spends lots of time at work fantasizing about dating and having sex with his attractive coworker.
immoral_consequence: James' productivity declines and the attractive coworker complains to her friends about how James looks at her.

norm: It's wrong not to pay your ex child support.
situation: Jay has a child with his ex, and he's in a tough financial situation after losing his job.
intention: Jay wants to cut his costs, so he can improve his finances.
moral_action: Jay arranges to make lower payments for couple months then pay more the following months.
moral_consequence: Jay's ex is relieved that he is still going to pay the child support.
immoral_action: Jay skips out on paying child support for a few months.
immoral_consequence: Jay's ex thinks that he is being an uncaring father.

norm: You shouldn't be near people when you're sick.
situation: Jack was invited to a party, but he has the flu.
intention: Jack wants to attend the party and have fun.
moral_action: Jack stays home, but Skypes in to the party to socialize.
moral_consequence: Jack stays home but has fun and keeps everyone else healthy.
immoral_action: Jack goes to the party even though he is sick.
immoral_consequence: Jack infects all of his friends, and they all get sick.

norm: It's rude to stand someone up.
situation: David had scheduled a date with Lisa, but his friends had tickets to the ball game.
intention: David wants to go to the ball game.
moral_action: David calls Lisa to reschedule their date to go to the ball game.
moral_consequence: Lisa meets David the next day to get together for their date.
immoral_action: David goes to the ball game without telling Lisa that he isn't going to meet her.
immoral_consequence: Lisa ignores David the next day when he calls to try to apologize.

norm: Cheating on a college paper is unacceptable.
situation: Deedee sits behind Dexter (the smartest student) during the exam.
intention: Deedee wants to preform well on the exam.
moral_action: DeeDee pays attention to her own paper and tries her best.
moral_consequence: DeeDee manages a 92% on the exam and is proud of her hard work.
immoral_action: DeeDee copies the answers off of Dexter's paper when the teacher isn't looking.
immoral_consequence: DeeDee gets a perfect score on the exam and attracts her instructor's suspicion.

norm: It's rude to talk non-stop to people.
situation: Sharon is a greeter for a hotel and sees a customer coming inside to stay a few nights.
intention: Sharon wants to make the customer feel welcome.
moral_action: Sharon says hello to the customer and exchanges a few questions and answers with him.
moral_consequence: The customer feels welcome at the hotel and continues to the front desk to check in.
immoral_action: Sharon engages the customer in conversation and begins to tell her about every detail of the past week.
immoral_consequence: The customer gets uncomfortable and annoyed, then finally leaves the hotel to stay somewhere else.

norm: It's rude to only think about yourself when talking.
situation: Sharon is sitting at lunch with some other girls who are having a conversation about visiting foreign countries.
intention: Sharon wants to share her experiences in Taiwan.
moral_action: Sharon asks the girls questions about the countries that they have visited in the past, creating a dynamic conversation.
moral_consequence: The girls have a great time talking with Sharon and connect with her and her experiences in a foreign land.
immoral_action: Sharon starts talking about Taiwan and hardly pauses for breath between each story.
immoral_consequence: The other girls are silent and slowly become resentful that Sharon is dominating the conversation, eventually leaving the table.

norm: It's impolite to criticize your friend's dating choices.
situation: Dave and Mark are talking when Mark tells Dave that he asked out Krista, and she said yes.
intention: Dave wants to react to Mark's story.
moral_action: Dave tells Mark that he's happy for him, and he wishes the two of them a happy time together.
moral_consequence: Mark feels supported by his friend and is glad to have someone to share his joy with.
immoral_action: Dave tells Mark that Krista slept around before and that he doesn't think Krista is really the right kind of girl for him.
immoral_consequence: Mark feels disturbed that Dave knows Krista's sexual past and feels angry that Dave is judging her without knowing her.

norm: You shouldn't abandon your family after a divorce.
situation: Burton just lawfully ended his marriage with his wife, and they have two children together.
intention: Burton wants to enjoy being single.
moral_action: Burton joins a dating group specifically for single parents so that any future partners know he has kids right off the bat.
moral_consequence: Burton's kids have Burton in their lives and are more likely to grow up well adjusted.
immoral_action: Burton makes sure his ex-wife gets full custody of their children, so he can concentrate on himself.
immoral_consequence: Burton's children grow up without their father and suffer emotionally.

norm: It is wrong to ruin someone else's dreams.
situation: Brad is talking to his son, Jay, who wants to be a writer.
intention: Brad wants to impart practical knowledge that will help Jay later in life.
moral_action: Brad suggests finding a balance between developing art skills, and preforming practical work.
moral_consequence: Jay listens and learns a valuable lesson in feasibility.
immoral_action: Brad says that Jay isn't clever or interesting enough to be a writer, and if Jay was, would not make any money, and Jay should work in a factory.
immoral_consequence: Jay loses self confidence and doesn't develop his passion, and submits to working in a factory while all joy within him dies.

norm: It's good to take people nice places.
situation: Tom is on vacation, in Paris, with his spouse, and they have not yet visited unique places.
intention: Tom wants to take his spouse someone special on vacation.
moral_action: Tom takes his spouse to the Eiffel Tower, to see the nice building.
moral_consequence: Tom's wife is thrilled and gives Tom a big kiss.
immoral_action: Tom takes his spouse to the sewers of Paris, to see the underground of the city.
immoral_consequence: Tom's spouse is mortified and offended, and Tom regrets his choice.

norm: It's wrong to incite bad emotions in people.
situation: Dave is a theater director who is coaching an actress, Tanya, who is a single mom, through a death scene.
intention: Dave wants to explain to Tanya how to act more sad.
moral_action: Dave tells Tonya that she needs to use facial expressions more to really sell the fact that she's sad.
moral_consequence: Tonya appreciates the constructive criticism and gets a better understanding of what she needs to do.
immoral_action: Dave tells Tonya that to truly act out the part she needs to image her child is dead, so she feels properly sad.
immoral_consequence: Tonya is disturbed by the suggestion and reflexively visualizes her child's death upsetting her greatly.

norm: It is good to accommodate peoples allergies if you can.
situation: Tom is hosting his friends for a dinner party and one his friends is allergic to peanuts.
intention: Tom wants everyone to have a good time.
moral_action: Tom accommodates his friend and cooks peanut-allergy-friendly dishes.
moral_consequence: Everyone has a good and safe time.
immoral_action: Tom ignores his friends allergy and makes the main course include peanuts or peanut oil.
immoral_consequence: His friend cannot eat and feels left out, or worse, has a reaction.

norm: It's wrong to leave your friends behind.
situation: Dave drove his friend Jack to a bar downtown, but Dave is not having a good time, while Jack is.
intention: Dave wants to go home.
moral_action: Dave tells Jack that he's going to leave after Jack has one more drink.
moral_consequence: Jack goes home with Dave after one more drink and then buys him gas as thanks for taking him out.
immoral_action: Dave leaves the bar while Jack is in the bathroom and drives home.
immoral_consequence: Jack has no ride home and has to spend $40 on a cab.

norm: You should be careful around aggressive dogs.
situation: Lucas sees Sarah's new dog barking loudly and growling.
intention: Lucas wants to meet the dog.
moral_action: Lucas asks Sarah if he can meet and pet the dog.
moral_consequence: Sarah explains that he is a rescue dog who is skittish around people but allows lucas to throw him some treats from a safe distance.
immoral_action: Lucas runs over to the fence and grabs at the dog to pet them.
immoral_consequence: The dog bites lucas's arm and lucas needs to get stitches.

norm: It is bad to sleep in a public bathroom.
situation: James drank enough at the bar to be too tired to walk home.
intention: James wants to fall asleep immediately.
moral_action: James calls a cab and tells the driver to wake him up when he gets to his house.
moral_consequence: James takes a nap in the back of the cab and feels a little more alert when he gets home.
immoral_action: James falls asleep on the floor of the disabled stall of the men's bathroom.
immoral_consequence: The bouncer finds James after a few hours and throws him out into the alleyway.

norm: It's good to get out and exercise your civic duty.
situation: Al wakes up and realizes that it's election day.
intention: Al wants to decide whether to vote today.
moral_action: Al gets out and votes for the policies he believes in at the voting booth.
moral_consequence: The politician Al supports wins the election thanks to voters like Al.
immoral_action: Al doesn't vote because there is no way [unpopular politician] can possibly win.
immoral_consequence: The unpopular politician barely wins because so much of his opposition didn't show up and vote.

norm: You shouldn't let your friends pressure you into trying drugs.
situation: Meredith recently moved to a new school and made some new friends who just invited her to smoke weed with them after school.
intention: Meredith wants to find a crowd to fit in with quickly.
moral_action: Meredith declines their invitation and starts looking around at different clubs that she can join.
moral_consequence: Meredith joins a couple clubs that catch her attention, and she makes new friends through those.
immoral_action: Meredith decides to hang out with her new friends and smoke weed with them after school every day.
immoral_consequence: Meredith and her friends get caught one day by a school police officer and get in trouble for using drugs.

norm: Parents shouldn't leave their children.
situation: Sally Mae is driving around town, running earrands on a hot day with her daughter in the backseat of the car.
intention: Sally Mae wants to get a new dress for a wedding she's going to next month.
moral_action: Sally Mae parks and takes her daughter into a women's clothing store with her.
moral_consequence: Sally Mae's daughter has fun looking at all the bright dresses her mother tries on in the store.
immoral_action: Sally Mae leaves her daughter in the car as she parks and goes into a women's clothing store.
immoral_consequence: Sally Mae's daughter overheats in the back of the car waiting for her mother and has to be rushed to the hospital.

norm: You shouldn't leave poop around on the ground.
situation: Molly walks her dog around the neighborhood every day.
intention: Molly wants to get the dog enough exercise.
moral_action: Molly takes the time to clean up after her dog when the dog poops.
moral_consequence: Molly's dog walk takes a little longer, but she is seen as a good neighbor by others.
immoral_action: Molly keeps moving when the dog poops in a yard, thinking that it is no big deal.
immoral_consequence: Molly picture is posted by a neighbor on the next door site, and she is eventually caught and fined by the police.

norm: You can't expect your parents to always keep their promises.
situation: Roy has been promised a new video game console for Christmas but his parents are not able to afford it.
intention: Roy wants to play a game with a friend.
moral_action: Roy decides to wait until a better time in order to ask for the gift.
moral_consequence: Roy's parents are able to focus more on paying for the essentials.
immoral_action: Roy brings up the promise when he finds out his parents weren't able to buy the console.
immoral_consequence: Roy's parents feel even worse about their current financial situation which adds stress.

norm: It's rude to wear someone else's hat.
situation: Sarah is hanging out in the park with some friends when she spots a fancy hat on the bench.
intention: Sarah wants to decide on what to do with the hat.
moral_action: Sarah decides to leave the hat alone and simply continue hanging out with her friends.
moral_consequence: Sarah enjoys a good time with friends in the park without any issues.
immoral_action: Sarah puts on the fancy hat and asks her friends how it looks on her.
immoral_consequence: The owner of the hat sees what Sarah is doing and expresses her annoyance to Sarah.

norm: It's wrong not to feel empathy toward people.
situation: Chuck's girlfriend got into a fight with her mom and is crying about it over the phone.
intention: Chuck wants her girlfriend to stop crying.
moral_action: Chuck tells his girlfriend that he knows how she feels and is sorry that she's hurting.
moral_consequence: Chuck's girlfriend feels comforted that someone else understands what she is going through.
immoral_action: Chuck tells his girlfriend to get over it and not worry about her feelings so much.
immoral_consequence: Chuck's girlfriend is offended and thinks that he is an insensitive jerk.

norm: It's polite to clap for others' performances.
situation: Jill's classmate is performing a dance for the class that ends with a flourish.
intention: Jill wants to react to her classmate's performance.
moral_action: Jill joins the class in a round of applause for the dancer.
moral_consequence: Jill's classmate is happy that the whole class showed their support for her performance.
immoral_action: Jill just stares at her classmate blankly as the rest of the class claps in appreciation.
immoral_consequence: Jill's classmate thinks Jill is mean for not showing any appreciation for their dancing.

norm: Sometimes it is better to mind your own business.
situation: Lauren hears people shouting and sounding increasingly violent outside.
intention: Lauren wants to feel safe about what's happening.
moral_action: Lauren calls the non emergency police line to report the talking outside and gives a description from her window.
moral_consequence: The people outside are told to disperse by local police and leave the area quickly, letting Lauren relax.
immoral_action: Lauren goes outside to get in the middle of the argument and gets slapped by one of the people.
immoral_consequence: Lauren calls the police and the person who struck her is apprehended, but her face hurts quite badly.

norm: You shouldn't feel entitled to use people's stuff.
situation: Marie's sister told Marie to never touch her laptop because she needs it for school.
intention: Marie wants to watch YouTube.
moral_action: Marie begs her mom to borrow her tablet, so she can watch videos.
moral_consequence: Marie's mom agrees that Marie can have an extra hour of screen time if she washes the dishes after dinner.
immoral_action: Marie borrows her sister's laptop and accidentally clicks on a popup that downloads a virus.
immoral_consequence: Marie's sister sees the virus and immediately guesses it's Marie's fault, so all of Marie's family members yell at her.

norm: It is rude to cancel a date on short notice.
situation: Tim scheduled a date with Tina a week from now, but later figured out he is busy that day.
intention: Tim wants to formally cancel his date with Tina.
moral_action: Tim lets his date know a week ahead of time that he cannot attend the date.
moral_consequence: Tina is happy with Tim for letting her know, and they have a conversation about other things.
immoral_action: Tim waits until three hours before the date to inform Tina he can't come.
immoral_consequence: Tina feels betrayed by Tim and decides to break up with Tim.

norm: It's good to serve food to your friends and family.
situation: Emily has invited some friends over to hang out at her place.
intention: Emily wants to encourage her friends to have some snacks.
moral_action: Emily prepares a snack platter and brings it to her friends.
moral_consequence: Emily's friends enjoy the snacks as they arrived quite hungry already.
immoral_action: Emily tells her friends that there are snacks in the pantry and to help themselves.
immoral_consequence: Emily's friends are hungry but too shy to get the snacks themselves, so they don't eat.

norm: You shouldn't cheat on your wife with a mistress.
situation: Earl is in a relationship which has lost a lot of it's initial passion.
intention: Earl wants an exciting and intimate experience.
moral_action: Earl thinks of something new he can try with his wife in the bedroom.
moral_consequence: Earl's wife enjoys the new experience and her passion is also renewed.
immoral_action: Earl begins to engage with a new woman physically outside his marriage.
immoral_consequence: Earl's wife finds out about the other woman and wants a divorce.

norm: It's rude to show up late for dinner.
situation: Gordon has plans to meet with his parents for dinner at 7:00, but he is playing World of Warcraft with his friends at 6:00.
intention: Gordon wants to meet his parents for dinner.
moral_action: Gordon ends the game and gets dressed so that he can leave the house by 6:30 to meet with his parents.
moral_consequence: Gordon's parents are happy to see him and the entire family has an enjoyable meal together.
immoral_action: Gordon decides to play one more raid with his friends before meeting his parents at the restaurant, and he ends up not leaving until 7:00.
immoral_consequence: Gordon's parents assume he is not coming, and they get a table for two, so there is nowhere for Gordon to sit when he arrives.

norm: You shouldn't care about how much someone eats.
situation: Oscar has a large friend named Tom, whom he thinks is too heavy, and is eating at a restaurant with him.
intention: Oscar wants to help Tom lose weight.
moral_action: Oscar offers to start an exercise routine with Tom to get in better shape.
moral_consequence: Tom exercises more and loses weight despite his bad diet.
immoral_action: Oscar tells Tom that he needs to cut down on how much food he eats, so he doesn't die.
immoral_consequence: Tom refuses to give up the food he loves and suffers a heart attack.

norm: You shouldn't hug someone without their permission.
situation: Bill is walking down the street when he sees his cousin who, unbeknownst to Bill, was recently diagnosed with Covid.
intention: Bill wants to show his cousin how happy he is to see him.
moral_action: Bill runs to his cousin but stops 6 feet away from him and tells him how great it is to see him.
moral_consequence: Bill stays healthy.
immoral_action: Bill happily runs to his cousin and without asking, hugs him.
immoral_consequence: Bill is contaminated with Covid.

norm: Asking a boss for feedback is good.
situation: Kyle is about to submit a report to his boss and is unsure if he has covered all the bases.
intention: Kyle wants to get a second opinion of his report.
moral_action: Kyle goes to his boss with the report and asks what he thinks.
moral_consequence: Kyle's boss is glad he approached him and uses it as a teachable moment.
immoral_action: Kyle asks around to his peers to get feedback on the report.
immoral_consequence: Kyle's boss catches wind of this and questions his ability to make decisions independently.

norm: You should not try to control your parents' actions.
situation: Nick's parents are going through a rough patch and his mother has started a new job his father disapproves of.
intention: Nick wants his father to be happy.
moral_action: Nick convinces his father that the job is a perfect opportunity for his mother and makes him feel good about it.
moral_consequence: Nick's mother feels supported by her family and thrives in her new job.
immoral_action: Nick tells his mother that the job is not for her because she is too old and not competent enough.
immoral_consequence: Nick's mother doubts herself so much after that that she ends up quitting her new job.

norm: It's bad to boss people around.
situation: Henrik is a young child at school playing a game with all of his classmates during recess.
intention: Henrik wants to have fun.
moral_action: Henrik runs around playing with the kids reacting and adjusting with them as the game they're playing evolves.
moral_consequence: All the kids are having fun so Henrik is able to enjoy himself among the group.
immoral_action: Henrik takes control of the game deciding what each of his classmates should be doing and correcting them if they stray from his instructions.
immoral_consequence: Henrik's classmates get fed up from not being able to play how they would like and Henrik is left with nobody to play with.

norm: It's annoying when people gloat about themselves.
situation: Robert is on the playground at recess and his two of his classmates are picking teams for a kickball match.
intention: Robert wants the other kids to know how talented and athletic he is.
moral_action: Robert remains silent and displays his athletic prowess by trying hard during the kickball game.
moral_consequence: The other children are impressed with Robert's skills and form a positive impression of him.
immoral_action: Robert loudly brags to the other kids about how he's the best athlete in the whole school.
immoral_consequence: The other kids find Robert's gloating to be arrogant and off-putting, and he is picked last.

norm: It's mean to burn your sibling's toys.
situation: Matt is walking across the room when he steps on his brother Greg's toys, injuring his foot.
intention: Matt wants to get the toys out of the way.
moral_action: Matt goes to Greg, shows Greg his foot, and asks Greg to pick up the toys.
moral_consequence: Greg apologizes and puts the toys away, grateful that Matt told him.
immoral_action: Matt takes Greg's toys that were on the floor outside and burns them in a pile with gasoline.
immoral_consequence: Greg cries when he finds out that his favorite toys are gone.

norm: You shouldn't hurt or traumatize your family members.
situation: John is married with two kids.
intention: John wants to have fun on a family vacation.
moral_action: John goes swimming at the beach with his family.
moral_consequence: His kids learn to swim, and they all have a nice time.
immoral_action: John pressures his family into bungee jumping off a bridge even though they are afraid of heights.
immoral_consequence: John's family are terrified and then anxious the rest of the trip and don't trust him.

norm: It's rude to tell someone their condition isn't real.
situation: Sally is talking with Frank and Sally tells Frank that she has a severe fear of flying.
intention: Frank wants to talk to Sally about her condition.
moral_action: Frank listens to Sally and asks questions about where her fear comes from.
moral_consequence: Sally feels respected and is grateful for Frank's openness.
immoral_action: Frank tells Sally that fears aren't real, and she should just get over it.
immoral_consequence: Sally is hurt that Frank doesn't believe her feelings.

norm: It's rude to insinuate that people will get fat.
situation: Steven is having a conversation with his girlfriend as she eats a cheese cake.
intention: Steven wants to make a remark about the food his girlfriend is eating.
moral_action: Steven states that the cheese cake looks good and that he will go get some for himself.
moral_consequence: Steven enjoys a nice cheese cake with his girlfriend as they chat.
immoral_action: Steven tells his girlfriend that she will put on some pounds if she keeps eating so much cheese cake.
immoral_consequence: Steven's girlfriend quickly becomes annoyed with Steven and starts giving him the cold shoulder.

norm: It's inappropriate for adults to engage in relationships with children.
situation: Rika is grading papers after class when her student Daisuke starts flirting with her.
intention: Rika doesn't want to hurt Daisuke.
moral_action: Rika sets Daisuke up with her younger sister.
moral_consequence: Daisuke thanks Rika later for introducing him to his new girlfriend.
immoral_action: Rika dates Daisuke.
immoral_consequence: Rika gets fired form her job after someone discovers her relationship.

norm: It's expected that you be gracious towards your in-laws.
situation: John is a newly wed and visiting his wife's family for the first time.
intention: John wants to stay close to his wife.
moral_action: John spends lots of time with all the different members of his wife's family during the visit.
moral_consequence: John and his wife bond over their, now shared, family experience.
immoral_action: John tries to spend as much time alone with his wife as possible during the visit while ignoring her family.
immoral_consequence: John's wife's family grow to not trust John and their comments about it to John's wife eventually sour the marriage.

norm: You should practice self control while eating.
situation: Grant meets some Girl Scouts at the door and buys 10 boxes of cookies from them.
intention: Grant wants to enjoy some Girl Scout cookies.
moral_action: Grant has 2-3 cookies with his lunch and savors every single one.
moral_consequence: Grant controls his weight and blood sugar effectively and makes the cookies last.
immoral_action: Grant eats a box of cookies every day until they are gone, then orders more.
immoral_consequence: Grant gains a lot of weight and begins to have blood sugar issues.

norm: It's wrong to dismiss someone's abilities based on their gender.
situation: Dev and Deva are practicing soccer together in a flirty way and Deva makes a great save.
intention: Dev wants to comment on the save.
moral_action: Dev high fives her and shares the moment.
moral_consequence: Dev is happy with their budding relationship.
immoral_action: Dev tells her he's never seen a girl make such a  save.
immoral_consequence: Deva is offended and Dev loses his chance with her.

norm: You should thank someone who gives you good advice.
situation: James was struggling to change a flat tire when a passerby pointed out that he was using the wrong size of wrench.
intention: James wants to avoid feeling incompetent.
moral_action: James thanks the passerby and swaps his wrench for the correct size from his toolset.
moral_consequence: James is quickly able to replace the tire and continue on his trip.
immoral_action: James insists that the passerby must be blind, and he's using the right wrench.
immoral_consequence: The passerby shrugs and laughs as James goes back to struggling with the tire.

norm: It's wrong to assault people.
situation: Mary is walking down the street when a man whistles at her.
intention: Mary wants to show her displeasure with the man's behavior.
moral_action: Mary berates the man for acting in a rude and demeaning manner.
moral_consequence: Mary feels good about putting the man in his place by pointing out his misbehavior.
immoral_action: Mary slaps the man across the face with all her strength.
immoral_consequence: Mary gets in trouble with the authorities for hitting the man.

norm: It's good to balance one's work life and home life.
situation: Joan works at a bakery.
intention: Joan wants to make her business profitable.
moral_action: Joan asks her husband to help her run the bakery, so they can be around each other more and be invested in the bakery.
moral_consequence: Joan's husband feels needed and cares more about Joan's bakery being successful, and Joan is less tired and appreciates her husband more.
immoral_action: Joan works such long hours she doesn't see her husband and has no patience for him.
immoral_consequence: Joan's husband feels neglected and Joan is stressed all the time about the bakery.

norm: You should always tell your friends the truth.
situation: Tim's friends want him to come to the park with them to play baseball, but Tim has plans with a girl.
intention: Tim doesn't want to hurt his friends.
moral_action: Tim tells his friends that he has feelings for the girl he's about to go on a date with.
moral_consequence: Tim's friend respect him more for being honest and open with them.
immoral_action: Tim tells his friends that he has a doctor's appointment to go to.
immoral_consequence: If Tim's friends find out he was lying, they won't trust him anymore.

norm: It's hurtful to strike a family member.
situation: Denise found out her child decided to go play outside instead of finishing her homework.
intention: Denise wants to punish her child for breaking the rules.
moral_action: Denise talks to her child and tells her to go to her room as punishement.
moral_consequence: Denise's child feels the punishment is fair and talks to Denise about how she can be better.
immoral_action: Denise calls her child to her and spanks her for breaking the rules.
immoral_consequence: Denise's child cries and feels violated throughout the process.

norm: You must commit to caring for any pet you get.
situation: Jenny is visiting her local pet store after work.
intention: Jenny wants to get a pet.
moral_action: Jenny decides to start with a small aquarium given her work hours.
moral_consequence: Jenny finds that she really enjoys relaxing after work with a glass of wine watching the fish and plans a bigger setup.
immoral_action: Jenny gets a puppy even though she is rarely home.
immoral_consequence: Jenny's puppy destroys the house, and she eventually takes it to the shelter.

norm: You should clean your dirty dishes.
situation: Penny is cleaning the house today.
intention: Penny wants to relax and watch t.v.
moral_action: Penny cleans up the house then does the dishes after that she sits down to relax and watch t.v.
moral_consequence: Penny's house is clean and no bugs come in her kitchen.
immoral_action: Penny cleans up a bit but then decides to skip doing the dishes and sits down to relax and watch t.v.
immoral_consequence: The dirty dishes sit there and bugs start crawling all over them and her kitchen.

norm: It's wrong to get upset with someone over a tattoo.
situation: Sasha is hanging out with her boyfriend Shaun when she notices his ex's name tattoed on his arm.
intention: Sasha wants to comment on Shaun's tattoo.
moral_action: Sasha asks Shaun the story behind the tattoo and tells him about her insecurities.
moral_consequence: Sasha and Shaun become closer as they learn more about each other.
immoral_action: Sasha reminds Shaun that his girlfriend is gone from his life, and she questions his loyalty multiple times.
immoral_consequence: Shaun leaves the house disgusted at Sasha's behavior.

norm: You shouldn't make jokes about hurricane devastation.
situation: Dan is in a barber shop and hurricane Irene is ravaging the East Coast of the United States that day.
intention: Dan wants to talk about hurricane Irene.
moral_action: Dan expresses verbal grief over the loss of lives in hurricane Irene.
moral_consequence: The barber patrons agree, and they engage in further serious conversation.
