immoral_action: Dan jokes about the number of deaths in hurricane Irene to the patrons.
immoral_consequence: Dan is given a cold stare and Dan feels confused.

norm: Yelling at people is disrespectful and should be avoided.
situation: Laine, who sometimes has anger issues, is having a dinner date with Kit at a local diner and Laine's chicken is under-cooked.
intention: Laine wants to let the server know something's wrong with the food.
moral_action: Laine calls the server over and calmly tells her that the chicken is still pink in the middle.
moral_consequence: Kit is proud of Laine for handling the problem so well, and because of that, Laine is proud of herself.
immoral_action: Laine calls the server over and begins to aggressively berate her for the horrible meal.
immoral_consequence: Kit is embarrassed by Laine's behavior and walks out, so now Laine feels foolish.

norm: You shouldn't get angry with your mother.
situation: John's mother keeps listening in on his phone conversations with a girl.
intention: John wants to let his mother know he doesn't like her invading his privacy.
moral_action: John calmly tells his mother that it's not okay for her to be eavesdropping on his conversations.
moral_consequence: John's mother agrees to stop listening in on his phone calls.
immoral_action: John loses his temper and yells at his mother to get of the phone line when he's on it.
immoral_consequence: John's mother is hurt by his violent outburst which she sees as unnecessary.

norm: You shouldn't film other people in the shower.
situation: Henry notices a small hole in the ceiling of his hotel room bathroom.
intention: Henry wants to see if there is camera hidden in the hole.
moral_action: After looking into the hole and seeing a camera, Henry calls the police.
moral_consequence: Henry is praised for bringing the source of child pornography to the attention of the police.
immoral_action: After looking into the hole and seeing a camera, Henry asks the hotel owner if he can have some video footage of young girls in the shower.
immoral_consequence: Henry is eventually caught and is arrested for child pornography.

norm: It's impolite to dominate a conversation.
situation: Sam is the boss in an office.
intention: Sam wants to interact with subordinates more.
moral_action: Sam invites subordinates into his office to get to know them better.
moral_consequence: Sam's subordinates feel more appreciated and invite him to lunch.
immoral_action: Sam budges into conversations subordinates are having and talks over them.
immoral_consequence: Sam's subordinates go out of their way to avoid him.

norm: It's rude to insult or put down others.
situation: Kevin is in an audience at a stand up comic event where the comedian is on stage doing his act.
intention: Kevin wants to yell something at the comedian.
moral_action: "Kevin raises his fist and screams out ""All right, yeah!"" and begins to clap his hands loudly at the comedian."
moral_consequence: The comedian is amused by Kevin's cheerleading and relaxes on stage, delivering an even better performance.
immoral_action: Kevin screams out that the comedian is horrible and tells him he sucks, turning to the crowd and laughing.
immoral_consequence: The comedian is horrified, annoyed and distracted by Kevin and begins to hate him.

norm: It's always good to apologize.
situation: James was trying to find a seat on a crowded subway when he accidentally knocked over someone's bag of groceries.
intention: James wants to sit down because he's tired.
moral_action: James apologizes to the person with the groceries and sits on the floor while he gathers them up.
moral_consequence: The person with the groceries thanks James and lets him have her seat when she gets off at the next stop.
immoral_action: James keeps walking forward to look for a seat without acknowledging the spilled groceries.
immoral_consequence: Several people on the subway insult James for being clumsy and not apologizing.

norm: It's okay to worry about your spouse's health.
situation: Jack's wife has been gaining a lot of weight over the past few months, and he believes it is affecting her health.
intention: Jack wants to have a long-lasting marriage.
moral_action: Jack tactfully broaches the subject with his wife, and suggests they start exercising together.
moral_consequence: Jack's wife loses weight and her health improves.
immoral_action: Jack ignores his wife's health issues to avoid conflict in the marriage.
immoral_consequence: Jack's wife continues to gain weight and her health suffers.

norm: It's rude to leave your fiancee at the altar.
situation: Mark has second thoughts about marrying his fiance Tiffany.
intention: Mark wants to break off the wedding.
moral_action: Before the wedding, Mark tells Tiffany that he's not ready to get married.
moral_consequence: Tiffany is sad, but appreciates that Mark told her before the wedding.
immoral_action: Mark doesn't show up to the wedding and leaves Tiffany a break up letter.
immoral_consequence: Tiffany becomes angry and frustrated at Mark for being so cruel.

norm: You should let others pray for you if they offer.
situation: Amy just got away from a mass shooting and her friend offered to pray for her.
intention: Amy wants to respond to her friend.
moral_action: Amy thanks her friend for being so considerate.
moral_consequence: Amy feels closer to her friend.
immoral_action: Amy tells her friend that praying is stupid.
immoral_consequence: Amy is seen as rude and unkind.

norm: It's kind to share your extra belongings with others.
situation: Lloyd, who is barehanded, and Harry, who is wearing two pairs of gloves are around a fire in the freezing cold winter when Lloyd remarks how cold his hands are.
intention: Harry wants to respond to Lloyd's statement.
moral_action: Harry tells Lloyd that he is actually wearing two pairs of gloves and asks Lloyd if he would like to wear his extra pair.
moral_consequence: Lloyd is delighted that his friend is willing to share with him and is relieved that he will finally get some warmth.
immoral_action: Harry tells Lloyd that he should have brought gloves with him since he knew he was going to be in the cold mountaints.
immoral_consequence: Lloyd feels miffed that his friend is dismissing his.

norm: It's good to get vaccinated.
situation: Flu season is coming up and there's free vaccinations at the local pharmacy that Ryan lives near, and he hasn't gotten one yet.
intention: Ryan needs to decide whether to get vaccinated.
moral_action: Ryan decides he should get vaccinated at the local pharmacy.
moral_consequence: Ryan's vaccination prevents him from catching the flu that year.
immoral_action: Ryan decides not to get vaccinated and instead rely on herd immunity.
immoral_consequence: Ryan gets the flu and is bed-ridden for several days.

norm: It is wrong to interfere with wild animals.
situation: Amy, an animal lover, is at the park and notices wild geese at the pond pecking at some trash.
intention: Amy wants to help the wild geese.
moral_action: Amy decides to clean up some of the trash from the park.
moral_consequence: The wild geese are safer around the park without all the litter in their habitat.
immoral_action: Amy feeds the geese some snacks from her bag.
immoral_consequence: The wild geese learn the wrong behavior to approach people for food.

norm: It is ungrateful to waste a gift.
situation: Ian gets a nice pair of headphones from a fellow friend who doesn't need them any more.
intention: Ian wants to use the headphones.
moral_action: Ian puts the headphones in a protective case and uses them while sitting.
moral_consequence: Ian's friend is impressed with how Ian cares for things and gives him more expensive gifts.
immoral_action: Ian puts the headphones in his backpack and uses them everywhere, quickly breaking them.
immoral_consequence: Ian's friend complains that the headphones cost a lot of money and that he's a fool for breaking them.

norm: It's wrong to be prejudiced against disabled people.
situation: Mike asks his friend that are a couple, John and Teresa, to an exclusive restaurant that doesn't have handicap accessibility, but Teresa is in a wheelchair.
intention: Mike wants to eat at a particular restaurant, known for their fine cuisine.
moral_action: Mike decides to eat at the restaurant the next weekend and takes John and Teresa out to a restaurant that has handicap accessible entrances.
moral_consequence: John appreciates that Mike is sensitive to his wife's needs and posts on social media what a great guy he is to have as a friend.
immoral_action: Mike tells John to just go without Teresa, since she has no adequate way to enter, because he wants eat at the exclusive restaurant.
immoral_consequence: John is highly offended by Mike's attitude and ends up posting his negative behavior on social media sites where they share mutual connections.

norm: You should share things with your partner.
situation: Mark is eating in the cafeteria and his friend forgot his lunch and is upset.
intention: Mark wants to help his friend eat lunch.
moral_action: Mark decides to share his food with his friend, by splitting his meal.
moral_consequence: Mark is happy he gets food, and they both enjoy a good conversation.
immoral_action: Mark asks other if they have food they can give his friend to eat.
immoral_consequence: Mark's friend feels weirded out that Mark doesn't share and Mark feels selfish.

norm: It's bad to try to get away from your children.
situation: The parents have been cooped up with their children for months without a break.
intention: The parents want to live harmoniously.
moral_action: The parents resolve to do more fun things together with the children.
moral_consequence: The children enjoy time spent with their parents and the mood in the house improves.
immoral_action: The parents drop the children off with their aunt the first chance they get.
immoral_consequence: The children have a great time and return to the family house in a good mood.

norm: It is irresponsible to get somebody else's property stolen
situation: Tony borrows his friend Jim's shovel to dig a hole in his front yard.
intention: Tony wants to put the shovel somewhere after digging the hole.
moral_action: Tony puts the shovel in his locked garage.
moral_consequence: Tony is able to return the shovel to Jim.
immoral_action: Tony leaves the shovel in the front yard where it is visible.
immoral_consequence: The shovel is stolen and Tony has to buy a new shovel for Jim.

norm: It's bad to buy more unnecessary junk you don't need.
situation: Randy is at the thrift store with his wife Sue, and they're looking for trinkets for their home.
intention: Randy wants to purchase some items.
moral_action: Randy picks out a trinket or two that he likes and puts them in his shopping cart.
moral_consequence: Sue likes the trinkets Randy found and is OK With the amount of money they cost.
immoral_action: Randy packs their shopping cart with a bunch of trinkets plus a bunch of garden gnomes and some outdoor shelves.
immoral_consequence: Sue is stressed out because this will cost so much money, and they don't really have a place for some of these things.

norm: It's bad to tell others' secrets.
situation: Sandra knows an interesting secret about her brother, and she sees her friend.
intention: Sandra wants to tell her friend something interesting.
moral_action: Sandra tells her friend about something interesting that happened to her over the weekend instead of the secret she knows.
moral_consequence: Sandra's brother is happy that his secret is safe and that he can trust his sister.
immoral_action: Sandra tells her friend the secret about her brother although he asked her not to tell anybody.
immoral_consequence: Sandra's brother is very embarrassed when he finds out that someone knows his secret.

norm: You should show sympathy to people in hard times.
situation: Ann's neighbor is undergoing hard times and Ann is acutely aware of this.
intention: Ann wants to avoid loaning money to her neighbor.
moral_action: Ann visits her neighbor and finds ways to help other than financially.
moral_consequence: Ann and her neighbor become good friends.
immoral_action: Ann avoids her neighbor.
immoral_consequence: Ann becomes disliked in the neighborhood.

norm: You should not fail academically.
situation: Jordan plays senior high school football but because of a grueling practice schedule, he falls behind in math class which he needs to pass in order to graduate.
intention: Jordan wants to prioritize what's important to him.
moral_action: Jordan cuts back on his practice schedule to work on his math.
moral_consequence: Jordan passes his class and goes on to graduate and play college football.
immoral_action: Jordan ignores his studies because he feels football is his calling in life.
immoral_consequence: Jordan fails math class and has to repeat the school year, and now can't play college football.

norm: It's wrong to commit crimes.
situation: Molly recently lost her job and is worried about her ability to meet her financial obligations.
intention: Molly wants to acquire more money to pay her monthly bills.
moral_action: Molly works hard to find a new job as quickly as possible.
moral_consequence: Molly gets a job at an accounting firm and is able to get the money needed to pay her bills.
immoral_action: Molly uses a firearm to hold up a convenience store and demands cash from the register.
immoral_consequence: Molly is tracked down by police and arrested for armed robbery.

norm: It's rude to interrupt people while they're talking.
situation: Alex is in a team meeting where one member is presenting something when he comes up with a great idea.
intention: Alex wants to get his idea out before he forgets.
moral_action: Alex writes his idea down in his notes and waits for the presenting member to finish before sharing it.
moral_consequence: The other team member has a meaningful presentation and receives Alex's idea well.
immoral_action: Alex cuts off the team member who is talking to pitch the idea.
immoral_consequence: The other team member was about to make a good point which wont have the same emphasis now.

norm: It's considered inappropriate to use explicit language in work communications.
situation: Francine is composing an email to her work group after they lost a big account.
intention: Francine wants to express her disappointment through the email.
moral_action: Francine uses phrasing that is professional but emotive.
moral_consequence: Francine's work group will be able to relate to her disappointment.
immoral_action: Francine uses many explicit words in the email to express herself.
immoral_consequence: Francine's work group will think she is unhinged.

norm: It's good to be tolerant toward someone else's beliefs.
situation: Amanda is talking to a friend at work who details her religious beliefs, and they sound very strange to Amanda.
intention: Amanda needs to respond to her friend.
moral_action: Amanda listens to her friend and indicates that her belief system is different but that she respects everyone's beliefs.
moral_consequence: Her friend doesn't talk about religion anymore because Amanda doesn't believe the same things, but no one feels disrespected or attacked.
immoral_action: Amanda tells her friend that her religion is just weird, and she doesn't want to hear any more about it, because it's crazy.
immoral_consequence: Amanda and her friend end up in an argument over religion, that only results in hurt feelings and doesn't change anyone's mind about their beliefs.

norm: It's not okay to call people names or be insulting.
situation: Maria is in a crowded mall parking lot, and someone just parked into the spot she was trying to park in.
intention: Maria wants to vent out her anger.
moral_action: Maria loudly comments about the other driver, but keeps her windows closed so the other woman doesn't hear.
moral_consequence: Maria feels better, yet the other woman has not been insulted.
immoral_action: Maria yells rude things at the woman in the other car.
immoral_consequence: The woman yells back at her, and they both feel terrible.

norm: You shouldn't start fights with your family.
situation: Paul's sister Mary is talking loudly while he is trying to read a book.
intention: Paul wants his sister Mary to be quiet.
moral_action: Paul asks Mary to please be quieter while he is reading.
moral_consequence: Mary apologizes and quiets down while Paul enjoys reading his book.
immoral_action: Paul shoves Mary and tells her to shut up and stop bothering him.
immoral_consequence: Paul and Mary get into a fight, and they are both put in timeout by their mother.

norm: It's inappropriate to be pervy as an old man.
situation: James, a seventy year old man, is eating lunch at a restaurant when an attractive waitress places food on the table.
intention: James wants to compliment the waitress.
moral_action: James tells the girl that this was the best service he's had in a while.
moral_consequence: James receives a discount on his meal from the thankful waitress.
immoral_action: James tells the waitress that she has a nice body while staring at her chest.
immoral_consequence: James is asked to leave early by the manager for making the waitress uncomfortable.

norm: It's wrong to be happy that someone died.
situation: Tanya just heard from her husband that her husband died, while sitting in her room.
intention: Tanya wanted to talk to her husband about her brother dying.
moral_action: Tanya expresses concern for the fact that her sibling died while talking.
moral_consequence: Tanya and her husband hug and try to forget about the event.
immoral_action: Tanya verbalizes her glee about her sibling dying, and jumps up and down in celebration.
immoral_consequence: Tanya's husband calls Tanya a monster and Tanya sulks by herself.

norm: It's wrong to encourage your partner to skip their classes.
situation: Bobby wakes up to his alarm and notices that Jill is still in bed during her class time.
intention: Bobby wants to wake Jill up.
moral_action: Bobby wakes Jill up and encourages her to go to class even if she is late.
moral_consequence: Jill attends the class and is able to complete an important project.
immoral_action: Bobby wakes up Jill and tells her that it is OK if she sleeps through class.
immoral_consequence: Jill misses an important project assignment and fails her course.

norm: It is bad to care about only money in life.
situation: Harriet is a well-off businesswoman and single mother to a teen daughter, Molly.
intention: Harriet wants to be able to provide for her daughter.
moral_action: Harriet sets a regular work schedule so that she has time to spend with her daughter every day.
moral_consequence: Harriet and Molly spend their days together without any worry about finances.
immoral_action: Although she can afford not to, Harriet spends the majority of her time at the office, only coming home to sleep.
immoral_consequence: Molly grows up without any memories involving her mother.

norm: It's bad for bosses to date their subordinates
situation: Sharon is a manager at a company and has fallen for Kelsey, one of the employees she supervises.
intention: Sharon wants to date Kelsey.
moral_action: Sharon asks Kelsey out after she transfers to a different department.
moral_consequence: Sharon and Kelsey have a romantic relationship that does not interfere with their work.
immoral_action: Sharon and Kelsey begin dating each other while keeping their positions in the office.
immoral_consequence: Sharon and Kelsey's work suffers as their personal relationship begins to effect their working relationship.

norm: You shouldn't act like an animal.
situation: Steve's buddy is clearly bored at his house at the moment.
intention: Steve wants to entertain his buddy.
moral_action: Steve pulls out the Xbox and him and his buddy play it.
moral_consequence: Steve's buddy is amused and having fun with Steve.
immoral_action: Steve decides to act like a monkey, to get a laugh out of his buddy.
immoral_consequence: Steve's buddy is a bit creeped out by it, and loses some respect for him.

norm: A parent should not date their child's ex.
situation: Kelly is a lonely single mom, and her daughter, Nina has just broken up with her boyfriend, Todd.
intention: Kelly wants to date someone.
moral_action: Kelly starts dating a man about her age that she met on a dating site.
moral_consequence: Kelly is able to console Nina over her breakup, and the two remain close.
immoral_action: Kelly starts dating Todd right after Nina breaks up with him.
immoral_consequence: Nina resents Kelly, and hides her dates from her mother in the future.

norm: You shouldn't abuse dogs.
situation: Steve's dog has been barking a lot recently and it is beginning to get on his nerves.
intention: Steve wants the dog to be quiet.
moral_action: Steve starts taking the dog to training so that it will follow his commands and bark less often.
moral_consequence: After a few months of training the dog is more well behaved and Steve is very happy.
immoral_action: Steve hits the dog, and chains it outside in his backyard where he won't hear it as much.
immoral_consequence: Steve's neglect and abuse is eventually reported by neighbors, and he is charged after his dog is taken away.

norm: It is bad to mix alcohol and prescription medications
situation: Jen is taking a new mediciation for her depression and anxiety.
intention: Jen wants to go out the bar with some friends.
moral_action: Jen plays it safe and stick to coffee and water when at the bar with her friends.
moral_consequence: Jen has no medical issues that night and enjoys the entire evening.
immoral_action: Jen drinks three glasses of wine and a long island iced tea at the bar.
immoral_consequence: The drinks react badly with the medication causing her to pass out and be hospitalized.

norm: You shouldn't have affairs with people.
situation: Tammy is married, but meets a very physically attractive person at a golf course who she befriends.
intention: Tammy wants to spend the day with her new friend.
moral_action: Tammy spends the day going out to eat with her new friend in a non-romantic way, and they don't get intimate.
moral_consequence: Tammy has a good time and is never accused of any wrongdoing for her activities.
immoral_action: Tammy offers her friend sexual intercourse at the end of the day.
immoral_consequence: Rumor goes around about Tammy's affair, and she loses social status.

norm: You should not borrow something you cannot return.
situation: Nico is currently an unemployed gamer who has stumbled across a new gaming accessory online.
intention: Nico wants to obtain the gaming accessory.
moral_action: Nico takes on odd jobs and saves up money to buy the game with his own money.
moral_consequence: Nico's friend is able to buy the game by then, and they have fun playing together.
immoral_action: Nico borrows money from his friend to pay for the accessory.
immoral_consequence: Nico's friend is not returned the money which he really needs back.

norm: You shouldn't date your friend's ex.
situation: Henry  is going to a party.
intention: Henry wants to bring a fun date.
moral_action: Henry invites Maria, who he met at the coffee shop.
moral_consequence: Maria fits in great with all of Henry's friends, and becomes part of their social circle.
immoral_action: Henry decides to invite his best friend's ex, Lulu.
immoral_consequence: Henry's best friend is upset when he sees Henry and Lulu together, and never speaks to either of them again.

norm: You should not let your pets roam around outside.
situation: James just moved to the suburbs and is trying to decide if his cat should be an indoor cat.
intention: James wants to make his cat happy.
moral_action: James keeps his cat indoors and trains him to go on walks on a leash.
moral_consequence: The cat lives a long and very safe life and sleeps on top of James every night.
immoral_action: James installs a cat door so his cat can wander freely around the neighborhood .
immoral_consequence: One day the cat is run over by a car, leaving James grieving and lonely.

norm: It's good to give your mother flowers for her birthday.
situation: Mary's mother has a birthday which is coming up this month.
intention: Mary wants to wish her mom a happy birthday.
moral_action: Mary buys her mother a bouquet of her favorite flowers.
moral_consequence: Mary's mother is very happy and notes that Mary got her favorites.
immoral_action: Mary sends her mother an e-card for her birthday.
immoral_consequence: Mary's mother feels sad because the gift is not very thoughtful.

norm: It's rude to make jokes about Greta Thunberg.
situation: Gerald is a middle aged man.
intention: Gerald wants to point out Greta Thunberg to his teenaged daughter.
moral_action: Gerald says he hopes his daughter is as confident and outspoke as Greta Thunberg on things that are important to her.
moral_consequence: Gerald is a good father and his daughter is confident and feels heard by him.
immoral_action: Gerald tells his teen daughter he hopes she won't be as loud and obnoxious as Greta Thunberg.
immoral_consequence: Gerald looks like a jerk bullying a kid and his daughter feels insecure.

norm: It is responsible to keep your room tidy.
situation: John's family was going to the amusement park, and he wanted to bring his camera with him.
intention: John wants to go to the amusement park.
moral_action: John's room was organized so finding his camera was a snap.
moral_consequence: John was the first one in the car waiting for his less organized parents and siblings to get ready.
immoral_action: Because his room is so messy, John couldn't find the cameras before they left.
immoral_consequence: John went to the part but without his camera with him.

norm: It's good to worry about your friends.
situation: Fran is wondering why her friend Jean stood her up for dinner.
intention: Fran wants to be a good friend.
moral_action: Fran is concerned about Jean, so she goes over to Jean's house.
moral_consequence: Jean is relieved to see her friend show up and has Fran take her to the hospital.
immoral_action: Fran thinks that Jean must be busy and doesn't want to bother her.
immoral_consequence: Jean is sick at home and nobody checks on her.

norm: It is bad to mishandle sensitive documents
situation: John was given top sercet documents by the government.
intention: John wants to deliver the documents.
moral_action: John hides the documents and deilvers them unread as he should.
moral_consequence: Nobody ever finds out what was in those secret documents.
immoral_action: John lets his friends read the documents before he delivers them.
immoral_consequence: John's friends get offered bribes by an enemy government for information.

norm: It's bad to deceive your coworkers.
situation: Marie is invited to a work party.
intention: Mary wants to bring cookies.
moral_action: Mary buys cookies and mentions the store she bought them from.
moral_consequence: Mary's co workers think she has great taste and the store gains more customers as they go there to shop also.
immoral_action: Mary buys cookies but says she made them when they are complimented.
immoral_consequence: Mary is found out and her co workers now know her as a liar.

norm: It's good to tip delivery people.
situation: Maria has a pizza delivered to her house for dinner.
intention: Maria wants to show appreciation to the delivery driver.
moral_action: Maria thanks the driver and gives them an extra five dollars on top of the bill.
moral_consequence: The driver is grateful to receive additional compensation for delivering the pizza.
immoral_action: Maria verbally expresses her gratitude but does not give the driver a tip.
immoral_consequence: The driver is annoyed that they didn't make any money off of the delivery.

norm: You shouldn't send disgusting pictures to your ex.
situation: Phil got dumped by his girlfriend Jan, and he is still upset about the breakup.
intention: Phil doesn't want Jan to forget him.
moral_action: Phil asks Jan to stay friends on social media so that they don't lose touch with each other.
moral_consequence: Phil is able to stay in touch with Jan and develop a friendship with her.
immoral_action: Phil starts sending Jan disturbing pictures meant to scare her.
immoral_consequence: Phil gets served with a restraining order for his harassment which goes on his record.

norm: You shouldn't eat junk food and be lazy.
situation: Candace has recently lost her job and is quite depressed about it.
intention: Candace wants to be less depressed.
moral_action: Candace immediately starts looking for a new job and updates her skills.
moral_consequence: Candace finds a new job quickly and is back to her old self.
immoral_action: Candace responds to her job loss by sleeping all day and eating candy.
immoral_consequence: Candace loses all her money and gains a lot of weight.

norm: It's wrong to use bullying tactics to get things done.
situation: Amber is a busy lunch room at school and finds that she has forgotten her lunch money.
intention: Amber wants to buy herself lunch.
moral_action: Amber asks the person next to her in the lunch room if they have an extra dollar or two.
moral_consequence: The other student pays for Amber's lunch, and they enjoy the meal together.
immoral_action: Amber finds a younger student nearby and puts her hand on his chest, pushing him towards the wall to get his money out of his pocket.
immoral_consequence: After lunch, the student reports Amber to the student advisor.

norm: Not being honest with a housemate is selfish and wrong.
situation: Alexandria put the meat away in the fruit drawer, when shortly after her roommates asked her if she was the one who put it there.
intention: Alexandria wants to maintain a good relationship with her roommates.
moral_action: Alexandria tells them she did put them in the wrong place, and offers to come put them away correctly.
moral_consequence: Alexandria's roommates understood that everyone makes mistakes and ends up respecting her more for owning up to her mistake.
immoral_action: Alexandria wanting to avoid her roommates thinking less of her, tells them she put the meat away in the right place.
immoral_consequence: Alexandria's roommates call her a liar and start to trust her less.

norm: It's good to appreciate gifts.
situation: Bob's wife gives him a gift for Christmas.
intention: Bob wants to respond to his wife's present.
moral_action: Bob thanks her for the gift and gives her a hug.
moral_consequence: Bob's wife feels happy, loved, and appreciated.
immoral_action: Bob tells her it isn't what he wanted.
immoral_consequence: Bob's wife is sad.

norm: It's important to be direct with someone you're dating.
situation: Jill's boyfriend wants her to join him camping, which she doesn't enjoy.
intention: Jill wants to tell her boyfriend whether she'll go camping with him.
moral_action: Jill tells her boyfriend in a straightforward manner that she doesn't like camping and doesn't want to go.
moral_consequence: Jill stays home when her boyfriend goes camping and stays happy and comfortable.
immoral_action: Jill doesn't tell her boyfriend how she really feels about camping and ends up going with him.
immoral_consequence: Jill has a terrible time camping and is unhappy the whole time.

norm: It's good to have a spending limit on gift exchanges
situation: Pat wants to buy his friends at the office great gifts.
intention: Pat wants to please the people in the office.
moral_action: Phil buys everyone a dollar store item.
moral_consequence: Phil explains he was scared of breaking the limit, so he 'cheaped' out.
immoral_action: Phil buys everyone at the office a computer for their homes.
immoral_consequence: Phil makes everyone else's gifts look like garbage because he broke the limit.

norm: It's not okay to judge people on size.
situation: Paul is friends with Erica who is thin but feels insecure about how she looks.
intention: Paul wants to boost Erica's self-esteem.
moral_action: Paul tells Erica that she is a great person and a great friend who many people love.
moral_consequence: Erica feels better about herself and appreciates Paul's kindness.
immoral_action: Paul tells Erica that she looks great and that compared to their larger friend Hannah she is much more attractive and seems healtheir.
immoral_consequence: Erica is angry that Paul would insult Hannah like that and tells Hannah about what Paul said.

norm: It is wrong to judge who others can date.
situation: Emma is talking to her friend Deb about a new guy that Emma started dating.
intention: Deb wants to tell Emma what she thinks about the guy she's been seeing.
moral_action: Deb listens to Emma and tells her that she's excited for her new relationship.
moral_consequence: Emma is happy that Deb is a supportive friend.
immoral_action: Deb tells Emma that the guy she's dating isn't worth her time.
immoral_consequence: Emma is offended and gets mad at Deb.

norm: It's bad to sympathize with nazis.
situation: Robert has moved to a new high school in a big city, and he doesn't know anyone there.
intention: Robert wants to find a group to join.
moral_action: Robert joins up with some students that have formed a science and technology club.
moral_consequence: Robert learns a lot about science and makes some great friends in the process.
immoral_action: Robert meets a group of neo-Nazis and is convinced to join their movement.
immoral_consequence: Robert is later shot and killed in a violent protest orchestrated by his Nazi group.

norm: It's good to show someone you think they did well.
situation: Jack goes to see his brother perform in a play and his brother comes over to him when it's over.
intention: Jack wants to talk to his brother.
moral_action: Jack expresses to his brother how good their performance in the play was.
moral_consequence: Jack's brother is reassured by Jack's praise of their performance in the play.
immoral_action: Jack talks to his brother about sports but avoids talking about the play even though he liked his brother's performance.
immoral_consequence: Jack's brother thinks Jack must think they gave a poor performance in the play because he doesn't bring up the topic.

norm: It's good to honor the promises you made to someone.
situation: Andrew is busy at work but promised his daughter Rachel that he would take her out to dinner if she graduated, and she has graduated.
intention: Andrew wants to talk to his daughter about what he said.
moral_action: Andrew tells Rachel to pick a restaurant to go to since she has graduated.
moral_consequence: Rachel will feel happy that Andrew is honoring his promise to take her out for graduating.
immoral_action: Andrew says that he's too busy at work to take Rachel out for her graduation dinner.
immoral_consequence: Rachel will feel betrayed by Andrew and feel he is unreliable.

norm: It's rude to tailgate another car.
situation: Hasan is on his way to work in the heavy traffic of the highway.
intention: Hasan wants to get to work.
moral_action: Hasan follows the rules of the of the road and accepts the traffic situation.
moral_consequence: Hasan eventually makes it to work just like he does every commute.
immoral_action: Hasan tries to drive faster than the traffic is going and keeps ending up very close to the car ahead of him.
immoral_consequence: Due to being too close to the car ahead, Hasan accidentally runs into it when traffic stops suddenly.

norm: You should discuss your sex life with your partner.
situation: Isabella is in a relationship and hasn't been satisfied with their intimate life.
intention: Isabella wants to improve her sex life.
moral_action: Isabella has a talk with her partner about how she feels about their bedroom life.
moral_consequence: Isabella's partner learns about things from Isabella's perspective and puts in an earnest effort to change things which helps the relationship.
immoral_action: Isabella begins to explore other outlets for her desires outside of her relationship.
immoral_consequence: Isabella's partner is hurt by her seeking things elsewhere and their relationship suffers.

norm: It's not okay to be unhygeinic.
situation: Juan works in a crowded office and has a long lunch break every day.
intention: Juan wants to go jogging during his lunch breaks.
moral_action: Juan runs during his lunch break, goes to the bathroom to freshen up, and puts on clean clothes.
moral_consequence: Juan's coworkers enjoy having him as a coworker and admire his commitment.
immoral_action: Juan runs during his lunch break and returns to his desk sweaty and stinky.
immoral_consequence: Juan's coworkers are offended by his smell and try to stay away from him.

norm: It's wrong to not make your intentions clear when dating.
situation: Jimmy has been seeing a girl recently but met a new girl that he likes more.
intention: Jimmy wants to date the new girl.
moral_action: Jimmy explains to his current girlfriend that he thinks they should break up before he asks the new girl out.
moral_consequence: Jimmy's current girlfriend is upset at first but is able to move on and eventually stay friends with Jimmy.
immoral_action: Jimmy starts dating both girls at the same time without telling either of them about the other.
immoral_consequence: Both girls find out that Jimmy is cheating on them, and they both break up with him and never speak to him again.

norm: It's rude to lie to your girlfriend.
situation: Mary bought a poorly fitting outfit from the store to wear for work and wants to know what her boyfriend Tom thinks of it.
intention: Tom wants to give feedback on the outfit.
moral_action: Tom tells Mary that the outfit doesn't fit her body.
moral_consequence: Mary takes the outfit back to the store and gets one that fits.
immoral_action: Tom tells Mary that the outfit looks great on her.
immoral_consequence: Mary wears the outfit to work and gets laughed at by her co-workers.

norm: It's wrong to break up with someone over something silly.
situation: Jenny's boyfriend got her a chocolate cake for her birthday, but she doesn't like chocolate cake, she prefers vanilla cake.
intention: Jenny wants to react to the cake her boyfriend got her.
moral_action: Jenny shows appreciation for the cake her boyfriend got for her birthday, feeling that it's the thought that counts.
moral_consequence: Jenny's boyfriend is happy that him buying the cake was appreciated by Jenny.
immoral_action: Jenny tells her boyfriend that she's parting ways with him because he doesn't even know what she likes.
immoral_consequence: Jenny's boyfriend is really upset about the breakup especially since it was caused by something so irrational.

norm: It is bad to throw away a good jacket.
situation: Janice just bought a new winter jacket but then decides she doesn't like how it looks.
intention: Janice wants to get rid of her new jacket.
moral_action: Janice returns the new jacket to the store she bought it from and exchanges it for a different style.
moral_consequence: Janice wears her newest winter jacket once it gets cold and her friends compliment her on it.
immoral_action: Janice puts her new jacket in the garbage and leaves it on the curb to be collected.
immoral_consequence: Janice has to spend more money on another jacket once it gets cold.

norm: You shouldn't have people over when you're house sitting.
situation: Dick is watching his friend's home while they are on vacation.
intention: Dick doesn't want to be lonely while he's house sitting.
moral_action: Dick video-calls an old friend, and they have a long chat to catch up with each other's lives.
moral_consequence: Dick has an enjoyable time house sitting for his friend.
immoral_action: Dick invites a group of friends to the home that he's house sitting and has a wild party that trashes the house.
immoral_consequence: Dick has to pay for repairs to his friend's home.

norm: It's proper that rules are applied to everyone the same.
situation: Brian is the coach of his son's pee wee soccer game but his son isn't a good player.
intention: Brian wants his son to be able to play more.
moral_action: Brian gives his son extra coaching at home, so he can improve his skills and play more.
moral_consequence: Brian's son gets better at soccer and shares a bonding experience with his dad.
immoral_action: Brian puts his son in games more often than the other kids so his son has a chance to play more.
immoral_consequence: The other kids notice Brian's son is getting special treatment and are mean to him because they are upset.

norm: It's not okay to insult someone for what they do.
situation: Samantha almost slips on the floor that the janitor mopped but didn't put a sign down.
intention: Samantha wants to tell the janitor off.
moral_action: Samantha tells the Janitor he could have killed her, and to be more careful.
moral_consequence: The janitor notices that and apologizes, saying it's all his fault.
immoral_action: Samantha yells at the janitor and calls him a loser for being a janitor.
immoral_consequence: The janitor is offended, and feels lower than he ever has before.

norm: You shouldn't sleep with different people every week.
situation: Bryan goes to the bar by himself and starts to feel like he needs some company.
intention: Bryan wants to find someone to spend the evening with.
moral_action: Bryan meets someone at the bar and starts a conversation, finding that they have lots of things in common, and they begin a dating relationship.
moral_consequence: Bryan feels less lonely and more like part of a real relationship, the girl he is dating is happy to have someone in her life who cares for her.
immoral_action: Bryan finds a lonely-looking girl and asks her back to his house for the night, only to blow her off in the morning to find someone else next weekend.
immoral_consequence: Bryan feels empty and alone for the rest of the week and the girl he brought home feels as though she has been treated very poorly.

norm: It's bad to run up a high phone bill.
situation: Carrie wants to have long conversations with her long distance boyfriend, but her boyfriend is on another network.
intention: Carrie wants to talk to her boyfriend.
moral_action: Carrie asks her boyfriend if they could communicate on video chat on her computer.
moral_consequence: Carrie enjoys seeing her boyfriend's face when they talk.
immoral_action: Carrie uses up all of her minutes, and talks to her boyfriend for long hours whenever she misses him.
immoral_consequence: Carries phone bill is over one hundred and twenty dollars.

norm: Its' good to be grateful to others.
situation: Marlowe just got out of jail early thanks to a friend's letter to the judge.
intention: Marlowe wants to hang out with her friend.
moral_action: Marlowe treats her friend to a nice home cooked meal to thank the friend for the letter to the judge.
moral_consequence: Marlowe's friend feels good for having helped out Marlowe and feels closer to her.
immoral_action: Marlowe goes on and on to her friend about how good it is to be free without acknowledging that it was due to the friend.
immoral_consequence: Marlowe's friend is a little annoyed and find Marlowe to be a bit selfish.

norm: It's wrong to ask things that make people uncomfortable
situation: Larry has taken an interest in a new friend of his and thinks the feeling might be mutual.
intention: Larry wants to make a move on the girl.
moral_action: Larry spends time getting to know her better before he flirts with her.
moral_consequence: Larry's friend feels comfortable enough with him to flirt back with him.
immoral_action: Larry starts to ask his friend questions that are very personal in nature.
immoral_consequence: Larry's friend is put off by the way he is talking so soon.

norm: You should be proud of your accomplishments.
situation: Don works in sales and has received a salesman of the year plaque.
intention: Don wants to put the plaque somewhere in his office.
moral_action: Don puts the plaque where it can be seen from outside the office.
moral_consequence: Potential clients will see how accomplished a salesman Don is.
immoral_action: Don puts the plaque in a desk drawer.
immoral_consequence: Potential clients will not be drawn to Don.

norm: It's good to care about your dog's well-being.
situation: Jim's dog Rover sleeps outside at night and has been barking for several hours.
intention: Jim wants Rover to quiet down.
moral_action: Jim goes outside with a couple dog treats and soothes Rover.
moral_consequence: Rover curls up in his doghouse and sleeps contentedly now that he's full.
immoral_action: Jim goes outside and yells at Rover, smacking him with a rolled up newspaper.
immoral_consequence: Rover whines and hides in his doghouse, staring accusingly at Jim.

norm: It's bad to sneak out as a child.
situation: Cindy's mother had just fussed at her for misbehaving at home.
intention: Cindy wants her mother to leave her alone.
moral_action: Cindy goes into her room and closes the door behind her.
moral_consequence: Cindy feels much better when she is in the calm environment of her room.
immoral_action: Cindy sneaks out of the house and runs away from home.
immoral_consequence: At night, Cindy is cold and scared because she doesn't know where she is.

norm: You should help out your classmates.
situation: Jill's classmate asks Jill to help them with their math homework since Jill is so good at math.
intention: Jill wants to respond to her classmate.
moral_action: Jill says she will spend some time explaining the questions in the math homework to her classmate.
