intention: Joe wants to lessen the punishment for the inmate.
moral_action: Joe completely pardons the man in prison so that he can get to go home early.
moral_consequence: The person gets to live a free life and doesn't have to be punished for his mistakes anymore.
immoral_action: Joe decreases the inmate's prison term by 3 months.
immoral_consequence: The inmate still has to spend a lot of time in prison, and the 3 months won't make a big difference.

norm: It's not okay to not have friends.
situation: Sam had to move to a new country for his job, and he doesn't know anyone there.
intention: Sam has to decide whether he wants to make friends.
moral_action: Sam goes to a bar and watches sports with others in the country.
moral_consequence: The people in the country start to trust Sam more and aren't wary of him.
immoral_action: Sam decides to spend more time by himself and doesn't try to make friends.
immoral_consequence: The people in the country think that Sam is weird and dislike him.

norm: It's wrong to ditch your partner during their important event.
situation: Dennis accompanies his girlfriend Bea to a friend's wedding and reception, where he spots a very attractive bridesmaid.
intention: Dennis wants to have fun dancing at the reception.
moral_action: Dennis dances with Bea and has a good time; the bridesmaid asks him to dance at one point.
moral_consequence: Bea is glad for a rest, Dennis gets to dance with both women, and everyone is happy.
immoral_action: Dennis tells Bea he needs to use the restroom, then dances with the bridesmaid.
immoral_consequence: Bea finds out that Dennis ditched her for the bridesmaid and gets angry.

norm: It's bad to lie about your feelings to your partner.
situation: Peter is jealous that his wife Pam is spending time with a new guy friend, when Pam asks him if she can go away with the guy for the weekend.
intention: Peter wants to respond to his wife's request.
moral_action: Peter tells Pam that he isn't comfortable with his wife going away alone with another guy.
moral_consequence: Pam cancels her plans with her new guy friend and instead goes for a weekend getaway with Peter.
immoral_action: Peter doesn't want to admit his insecurity, so he tells his wife that he's fine with her going on the trip with the new friend.
immoral_consequence: Pam spends the weekend with the new friend and begins to develop romantic feelings for him.

norm: It's bad to freeload off your friends.
situation: Jack is a college student.
intention: Jack wants to go out with friends.
moral_action: Jack goes to a concert with friends and brings everyone a beer.
moral_consequence: Jack's friends appreciate it and pay him back, and they all have friend at the concert and agree to see that band again.
immoral_action: Jack goes to a bar with friends, drinks a lot, and says he forgot his wallet again.
immoral_consequence: Jack's friends stop inviting him along knowing he won't pay for himself, and he's left alone.

norm: You should alleviate the concerns that your partner might have.
situation: Jake doesn't often compliment his girlfriend Alyssa on her appearance, and she often asks whether he finds her attractive or not.
intention: Jake wants Alyssa to stop asking about his attraction to her.
moral_action: Jake tells Alyssa he is very much attracted to her and starts to compliment her more often.
moral_consequence: Alyssa finally feels secure enough in herself and her relationship to stop asking Jake about his attraction to her.
immoral_action: Jake responds to Alyssa's questions by telling her she is being ridiculous.
immoral_consequence: With her question unanswered, Alyssa's insecurities grow even larger.

norm: It's mean to call someone a braggart.
situation: Jocelyn hears that from her brother Phil that he got a really good SAT score.
intention: Jocelyn wants to respond to Phil.
moral_action: Jocelyn tells Phil that she knew he could get a high score.
moral_consequence: Phil will feel that his sister believes in him.
immoral_action: Jocelyn tells Phil that he is too proud of his score and a braggart.
immoral_consequence: Phil won't want to share his achievements anymore.

norm: You shouldn't keep a dog that isn't yours.
situation: "Fern has recently taken in a stray dog and is now seeing ""lost dog"" posters containing photos that look like him."
intention: Fern wants the dog to be safe.
moral_action: Fern calls the number on the posters and meets with the owners of the lost dog.
moral_consequence: Fern realizes that the owners care deeply about their dog and return him to them.
immoral_action: Not knowing what his owners are like, Fern keeps the dog safe in her posession.
immoral_consequence: The dog and his owners spend the rest of their lives missing each other.

norm: it's a good habit to save money when possible.
situation: Sally has a new job at a law firm where she needs to dress conservatively.
intention: Sally wants to get a new wardrobe.
moral_action: Sally visits some local second hand stores that have nice suits for work, and she gets a lot for her money.
moral_consequence: Sally pays all of her bills on time and does not have to worry about her bank balance too much.
immoral_action: Sally goes online and buys five new suits from a designer website.
immoral_consequence: Sally struggles to pay her bills the next month because she spent her whole paycheck on clothes.

norm: You shouldn't be a creep toward women.
situation: Gary is walking to attend his class and sees a group of young women on the way.
intention: Gary wants to walk past the group of the women.
moral_action: Gary says hi and simply walks past the women.
moral_consequence: The women also say hi and Gary feels a sense of glee.
immoral_action: As Gary is passing the group he teases the women.
immoral_consequence: Gary gets suspended from college for his mistreatment of the women.

norm: People love to take vacations to go gambling.
situation: Connor is a teacher who has his Christmas break coming up.
intention: Connor wants to go on a vacation.
moral_action: Connor books a vacation at a hotel and casino in Las Vegas.
moral_consequence: Connor wins $200 playing blackjack and uses his winning to see a performance by Cirque du Soleil.
immoral_action: Connor randomly chooses a city he's never been to and plans a trip to Bismarck, North Dakota.
immoral_consequence: Connor is extremely bored in Bismarck and can't find anything he wants to do.

norm: It's good to go on a tour.
situation: Jake goes on vacation to New York for the first time and is overwhelmed.
intention: Jake wants to explore the city.
moral_action: Jake decides to take an official bus tour of New York and goes on it.
moral_consequence: Jake learns a lot about the city and feels smart afterward.
immoral_action: Jake decides to explore the city without a map or a guide.
immoral_consequence: Jake gets lost and feels stressed out.

norm: It's bad to be abusive in a relationship.
situation: Hank is dating Gina and Gina didn't put enough salt in the food she made.
intention: Hank wants to respond to the lack of salt.
moral_action: Hank tells Gina that the food is good but can use a little more salt.
moral_consequence: Gina will take Hanks suggestions and improve her seasoning.
immoral_action: Hank takes the food and tosses it against the wall.
immoral_consequence: Gina will become afraid of Hank and plan to leave him.

norm: It's wrong to hit others.
situation: Bob's son Biff punched a classmate in the nose at recess.
intention: Bob wants to impress on Biff that hitting his classmates is unacceptable.
moral_action: Biff calmly explains that violence is unacceptable and that he is disappointed in Biff's behavior.
moral_consequence: Biff is embarrased by his behavior and sincerely promises to never hit anyone again.
immoral_action: Bob spanks Biff and threatens to do so again if Biff ever raises a hand to a classmate.
immoral_consequence: Biff never again hits a classmate but when he grows up Biff uses spanking to control his children's behavior.

norm: It's wrong to invade someone's personal space.
situation: Jeff has a new coworker named Jenny who just started at the office today.
intention: Jeff wants to welcome Jenny to the office.
moral_action: Jeff walks up smiling and extends his hand for a handshake.
moral_consequence: Jenny accepts Jeff's handshake and feels like she's already starting to belong.
immoral_action: Jeff sneaks up behind Jenny and gives her a great big bearhug.
immoral_consequence: Jenny is creeped out by Jeff acting so familiar when they just met.

norm: It's nice to cook others their favorite foods.
situation: Sally is having a dinner for her roommate to celebrate a promotion.
intention: Sally wants to have a really good meal.
moral_action: Sally asks her roommate what her favorite meals are then chooses one of them to make for dinner.
moral_consequence: Sally's roommate enjoys the dinner Sally prepared and even has seconds.
immoral_action: Sally makes her own favorite regional dish, a crawfish boil.
immoral_consequence: Sally's roommate does not care for crawfish boil and does not eat dinner at the party.

norm: You should follow through on your promises.
situation: Jeff had promised to spend the weekend with his father who he hadn't seen in a month.
intention: Jeff wants to see a movie with his friends.
moral_action: Jeff invites his father to join him and his friends on their trip to the movies.
moral_consequence: Jeff and his father have a great night spending time with each other.
immoral_action: Jeff cancels his plans with his father and watches a movie with his friends instead.
immoral_consequence: Jeff's father is upset and doesn't answer Jeff's calls for a week.

norm: It's wrong to not be honest with a roommate.
situation: Mack ate his roommate's sandwich in the fridge and is now confronted by his roommate about it.
intention: Mack wants to respond to his roommate.
moral_action: Mack admits he ate his roommate's sandwich and offers to replace his sandwich.
moral_consequence: Mack's roommate forgives Mack, and they enjoy a nice meal together.
immoral_action: Mack repeatedly denies eating his roommate's sandwich and even states he never saw a sandwich in the fridge.
immoral_consequence: This incident created a rift between Mack and his roommate that was never resolved.

norm: It is weak to give in to your addictions.
situation: Cindy is a recovering alcoholic, and is at a party where alcohol is being served.
intention: Cindy wants to have fun at the party.
moral_action: Cindy sticks to non-alcoholic drinks and dances with people a lot.
moral_consequence: Cindy has fun at the party and is bright and alert the next day.
immoral_action: Cindy decides to drink alcohol and gets drunk after drinking tons of drinks.
immoral_consequence: Cindy falls back into her addiction and loses her job.

norm: It is unusual to prefer obesity in a mate.
situation: Sebastian watches his overweight girlfriend Melissa get sick after exercising.
intention: Sebastian wants Melissa to feel better.
moral_action: Sebastian shows Melissa some lower intensity exercises that are good for her fitness level.
moral_consequence: Melissa slowly starts to lose weight.
immoral_action: Sebastian discourages Melissa  from working out telling her he finds her weight attractive.
immoral_consequence: Melissa develops diabetes.

norm: It's mean to frequently leave your spouse alone at night.
situation: Damien is married, and his mother just had surgery and requires constant care.
intention: Damien wants to help his mother.
moral_action: Damien works a few extra hours to help pay for a nurse to go and check on his mother every night.
moral_consequence: His mother is very appreciative and recovers quickly.
immoral_action: Damien goes and spends the night at his mother's house every night for over a month.
immoral_consequence: Damien's wife is very upset, lonely, and tells him she is considering leaving him.

norm: It's good to look for help dating.
situation: Natalie is single and her friends keep on trying to introduce her to single men they know.
intention: Natalie wants to have a boyfriend.
moral_action: Natalie accepts to meet her best friend's cousin, who is single.
moral_consequence: Natalie starts dating her friend's cousin and finds out he is a lovely man.
immoral_action: Natalie rejects her friends' offers and meets someone through Tinder.
immoral_consequence: Natalie's new boyfriend is unpleasant and quickly starts cheating on her.

norm: It's not okay to do things that hurt another person.
situation: Jimmy and Jeffrey are kids playing on a school playground, and Jimmy steals Jeffrey's lollipop.
intention: Jeffrey wants his lollipop back.
moral_action: Jeffrey knows he can just take the lollipop back, but goes to a nearby teacher and asks them to get his lollipop back from Jimmy instead.
moral_consequence: Jimmy is sent to detention and Jeffrey smiles and continues eating his lollipop.
immoral_action: Jeffrey takes a swing at Jimmy, who drops the lollipop and backs off.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy runs crying to the teacher, and Jeffrey gets sent home from school.

norm: It's wrong to fake an injury for attention.
situation: Jon is playing in a soccer match and his team is about to lose when the opponent scores a goal.
intention: Jon wants his team to win.
moral_action: Jon tries his best to block the shot.
moral_consequence: If he does not block the shot, at least he maintains his dignity.
immoral_action: Jon throws himself into his opponent and fakes an injury to stop the game and the goal.
immoral_consequence: Jon is looked at as a wuss and faker and not well respected.

norm: You shouldn't gamble your money.
situation: Fred's wants to bet on his favorite team in a big game, but he has already lost a lot of money gambling.
intention: Fred has to decide whether to place a bet.
moral_action: Fred decides that betting on sports is stupid and just watches the game.
moral_consequence: Fred doesn't have to lose any money, and he's able to resist the temptation.
immoral_action: Fred put $5,000 on his favorite team to win the game.
immoral_consequence: Fred has a large chance of losing the money and wouldn't be able to get the money back.

norm: It's wrong to brag about your looks.
situation: Sal is in the office at his desk when Carmine comes by and asks Sal what he thinks of his look today.
intention: Sal wants to respond to Carmine's question.
moral_action: Sal tells Carmine that he looks great today and that he should come to the office with that look more often.
moral_consequence: Carmine is delighted that Sal loves his new look and grows in self confidence.
immoral_action: Sal tells Carmine that he looks OK but definitely will never look good as Sal as he's the best looking person ever.
immoral_consequence: Carmine thinks Sal is disgustingly conceited and is insulted that his backhanded compliment was only meant to set up a brag.

norm: You should take action to keep yourself safe.
situation: Erica has been drinking, and she wants to go home.
intention: Erica needs to find a way home.
moral_action: Erica asks her friend at the party to take her home.
moral_consequence: Erica and her friend have a great time talking in the car on the way home.
immoral_action: Erica decides to risk driving home.
immoral_consequence: Erica gets into a traffic accident.

norm: It is bad to neglect relationships.
situation: Arnie was driving home to his family after work and was thinking about what to do.
intention: Arnie wants to plan the rest of his day.
moral_action: Arnie decides to take his whole family out to see a movie they all like to watch together.
moral_consequence: Arnie's family has a blast with the film and likes spending time with each other.
immoral_action: Arnie decides to watch TV and read some books before going to bed.
immoral_consequence: Arnie's family feels neglected since Arnie doesn't spend time with them.

norm: You shouldn't strip if you have a partner.
situation: Jane has a new boyfriend who has a birthday coming up, and she wants to make some money to buy him a nice present.
intention: Jane wants get a job.
moral_action: Jane works as a cashier and saves up fer her boyfriend's present.
moral_consequence: Jane's boyfriend is pleased with her new Job and loves the present she gets him.
immoral_action: Jane gets a job stripping at a local strip club.
immoral_consequence: Jane's boyfriend is unhappy about Jane's new occupation when he finds out about it.

norm: It's frowned upon to back out of an agreement.
situation: Robert just agreed with his regular plumber about a big repair job at his house when he discovers that another plumber would charge him less.
intention: Robert wants to save money.
moral_action: Robert discusses the situation with his regular plumber, and they agree on a lower price.
moral_consequence: Robert's regular plumber's schedule goes as planned and his employees work their regular hours.
immoral_action: Robert cancels the job with his regular plumber without explanation and hires the less expensive one instead.
immoral_consequence: Robert's regular plumber has to reorganize his schedule and decrease some of his employees' hours.

norm: You shouldn't leave dirty dishes in a shared sink.
situation: Tod's Mom asked Tod to load the dishwasher, but the dishwasher cannot fit all of the dishes.
intention: Tod wants to load the dishwasher to the brim and turn it on.
moral_action: Tod fills the entire dishwasher, and then handwashes the rest of the dishes in the sink.
moral_consequence: Tod's mom is impressed by Tod and tells him he did a good job.
immoral_action: Tod fills the entire dishwasher but leaves dishes in the sink.
immoral_consequence: Tod's Mom expresses disgust at Tod for leaving dishes in the sink.

norm: It is rude to make others uncomfortable on purpose.
situation: Rob and Karen are on a double date with their friend Josie who brings a guy, Eric she met online who gets on Rob's nerves.
intention: Rob wants to react to the situation.
moral_action: Despite Rob not liking Eric, he decides to be on his best behavior for Josie's sake.
moral_consequence: Josie and Eric enjoy their date and leave feeling like it was a successful first night out together.
immoral_action: Rob ignores Eric throughout the evening.
immoral_consequence: Josie and Eric both feel awkward and leave early with hurt feelings.

norm: It's good to be honest with your ex.
situation: Tim still has feeling for his ex-girlfriend Mia, but keeps it a secret.
intention: Tim wants to talk to Mia.
moral_action: Tim tells Mia that he still loves her.
moral_consequence: Mia gets back together with Tim and Tim is overjoyed.
immoral_action: Tim tells Mia that he has no feeling for her anymore.
immoral_consequence: Mia finds a new boyfriend and Tim becomes sad.

norm: You shouldn't be noisy in public.
situation: Dave is sunbathing in a beach.
intention: Dave wants to listen to music.
moral_action: Dave uses headphones to listen to the music.
moral_consequence: The people around him is undisturbed and enjoy their activities happily.
immoral_action: Dave turns on his cellphone very loud to play his music.
immoral_consequence: The people around him feel disturbed and irritated.

norm: You should support your spouse.
situation: Robert and Cecilia are couple and Robert's business has failed, and he needs financial help.
intention: Cecilia wants to respond to Robert's situation.
moral_action: Cecilia agrees to sell her house to get the money to help Robert go through his difficult time.
moral_consequence: Robert feels grateful and decides to maintain and reconstruct his business.
immoral_action: Cecilia divorces from Robert to pursue a better life.
immoral_consequence: Robert feels downhearted being impacted by both business failure and divorce.

norm: Taking drugs is frowned upon.
situation: Kevin has been assigned a difficult project by his manager and gets stressed by his work.
intention: Kevin wants to manage his stress.
moral_action: Kevin regularly practices meditation in order to achieve a mentally clear mind.
moral_consequence: Kevin feels emotionally calm and stable and becomes more efficient in his work.
immoral_action: Kevin takes Cannabis in order to reduce his stress.
immoral_consequence: Kevin feels panic and tired due to the side effects, so he can't concentrate well on his work.

norm: It's encouraged to report dishonest behavior to the affected parties.
situation: James sees his friend Bob, who he knows is married to Jane, kissing another woman at the bar.
intention: James wants to report the affair to someone to get it off his chest.
moral_action: James leaves the bar and telephones Jane to tell her her husband is being unfaithful.
moral_consequence: Bob is confronted by Jane when he comes home and is forced to change his ways after learning a lesson about breaking trust.
immoral_action: James leaves the bar and goes to his local church where he enters a confessional booth and tells the priest what happened.
immoral_consequence: Bob continues his cheating ways, taking advantage of his unsuspecting spouse and leading a double life.

norm: It's bad to see benefits to slavery.
situation: Charles is discussing slavery with a diverse group of friends, who are divided on the topic.
intention: Charles wants to come across as open-minded.
moral_action: Charles displays open-mindedness by listening to all his friends' opinions and ends up demonstrating how there were no objective benefits to slavery.
moral_consequence: Charles' Black friend feels supported by Charles' clear analysis.
immoral_action: Charles listens to his friends and ends up saying that he can see how slavery had some benefits.
immoral_consequence: One of Charles' friends, who is Black, is shocked and saddened by Charles' opinion.

norm: It's good to build close relationships with others.
situation: Tanya just started as a new freshman at her local college but hasn't made any friends yet.
intention: Tanya wants to do well in her classes.
moral_action: Tanya makes friends with some people in her class, and they form a study group for the upcoming semester.
moral_consequence: Tanya is able to work with the others in her study group on assignments, and they all get good grades.
immoral_action: Tanya spends almost all of her time studying at the library by herself or just watching tv in her dorm.
immoral_consequence: Tanya has difficulty with some of the homework assignments and gets lower grades since she doesn't have anyone to ask for help.

norm: You shouldn't plagiarize other people's work.
situation: Candy has been assigned a paper in her English class at school.
intention: Candy wants to finish writing the paper.
moral_action: Candy researches the topic and writes the paper in her own words.
moral_consequence: Candy's teacher gives her an A for her hard work on the paper.
immoral_action: Candy copies her work almost word for word from something that she find online.
immoral_consequence: Candy's teacher gives her a zero on the paper that she turns in.

norm: It's mean to disregard people's grief.
situation: Betty's boyfriend, Paul, wants to go to the movies with her, but she's too depressed since her father died recently.
intention: Paul wants to see a movie with Betty.
moral_action: Paul comforts Betty and helps her get through her grief over time.
moral_consequence: Betty eventually is ready to have fun times again, and she and Paul go see a great movie.
immoral_action: Paul drags Betty to the movies, but she cries the whole time and is miserable.
immoral_consequence: Betty resents Paul for not caring about her feelings and breaks up with him.

norm: It's good to warn parents of dangers to their children.
situation: Joe is looking out of Joe's window at the children playing on his lawn.
intention: Joe wants to avoid children being injured by falling into a dry well on his property.
moral_action: Joe explains to the parents of the children that there is an old dry well on Joe's property which might be fallen into.
moral_consequence: Parents in the neighborhood appreciate Joe and make sure to keep children safe following Joe's advice and no one is injured or upset.
immoral_action: Joe emerges from his house with a pistol aimed at the children and screams at them to go without explaining why.
immoral_consequence: The children are frightened and many parents in the neighborhood are mistrustful of Joe and do not like Joe.

norm: It's hurtful to turn your back on a loved one.
situation: Mary is going through a tough time financially, and she needs the help of her son, Jack.
intention: Jack wants to help his mom.
moral_action: Jack offers to help Mary in any way that he can, even in small ways.
moral_consequence: Mary gets the help she needs and her relationship with her son is impoved.
immoral_action: Jack does not perosnally help Mary, but he apologizes and wishes her well.
immoral_consequence: Mary is left alone and does not get any help she needs and her relationship with Jack is harmed.

norm: You shouldn't lie about having insomnia.
situation: Josie is a freshman in college and gets the worst dorm.
intention: Josie wants to upgrade her living siutation.
moral_action: Josie asks her RA to get a better room because she wants a good freshman year.
moral_consequence: The RA tells her someone pulled out of their living situation so there is a suite available.
immoral_action: Josie tells her RA she has insomnia to get a suite with a bathroom.
immoral_consequence: Josie gets paired with an awful roommate who actually has insomnia and causes her to not be able to sleep due to stress.

norm: It's good to provide a loving home for your pet.
situation: Janet has just adopted a puppy for her home who's barking loudly.
intention: Janet wants to go shopping all day.
moral_action: Janet pets the puppy and takes him for a walk and feeds him before leaving for the mall.
moral_consequence: The puppy will love Janet more and be happy all day.
immoral_action: Janet pretends she doesn't hear the barks and heads over to the mall.
immoral_consequence: The puppy will become depressed and mess up the entire house.

norm: It's bad to end your life.
situation: James feels extremely depressed since his mother died, and he lost his job.
intention: James wants his pain to end.
moral_action: James goes to a psychiatrist and asks for medication to help with his depression.
moral_consequence: James feels somewhat better and keeps working with the psychiatrist to fine-tune his medication.
immoral_action: James buys some rope, makes a noose, and hangs himself in his garage.
immoral_consequence: James' surviving family is wracked with grief at a second loss in so short a time.

norm: Being upfront with someone about your intentions is honorable.
situation: Bill is on a date with Sally when Sally flat out asks Bill if he was planning on them sleeping together that night.
intention: Bill wants to respond to Sally's question.
moral_action: Bill tells Sally that as embarrassing as it is to admit it that he definitely was hoping they'd end up in bed.
moral_consequence: Sally is happy Bill finds her attractive and is attracted to his bluntness and honesty and vows to make his wish come true.
immoral_action: Bill tells Sally that of course not, he only wants to show her a good time and take her home like a gentleman.
immoral_consequence: Sally thinks less of Bill because she knows he's lying, and she doesn't appreciate being toyed with and patronized.

norm: It's rude to make a charity event about yourself.
situation: Tom is invited as a speaker for a charity event and steps up to the podium.
intention: Tom wants to make a speech.
moral_action: Tom makes a moving speech highlighting the goals of the charity.
moral_consequence: Tom gains recognition as a talented speaker and feels good about helping the charity event become successful.
immoral_action: Tom brags about himself during his speech and attempts to promote his own brand.
immoral_consequence: Tom is removed from the podium and blacklisted from any future events.

norm: Parents should not favor certain children over the others.
situation: Gary who has two sons, is making out his will and last testament and is writing up the inheritance portion.
intention: Gary wants to decide who to leave his assets to.
moral_action: Gary decides to split the inheritance and give his sons an equal share to each of the two sons.
moral_consequence: Gary's sons both are delighted that their father has left them with assets and that they have no reason to be jealous of each other.
immoral_action: Gary decides to give all the money to one son as he believes the other son is going to waste it eventualy.
immoral_consequence: Gary's son that didn't receive any money is insulted and feels betrayed and sad as well as angry and bitter about being cut off.

norm: It's wrong to pick fights with others.
situation: Johnny has a growing and heated rivalry with another member of his middle school basketball team.
intention: Johnny wants to show up his rival.
moral_action: Johnny challenges his rival to a one-on-one game of basketball.
moral_consequence: Johnny beats his rival in the game and the other kids are all impressed by him.
immoral_action: Johnny starts a fight with his rival to prove that he is superior.
immoral_consequence: Johnny suffers minor injuries in the fight and is suspended from school for several days.

norm: It's bad to marry someone who hurts animals.
situation: John is a known animal abuser who takes Jenny out on a date and proposes to her.
intention: Jenny wants to answer John's marriage proposal.
moral_action: Jenny tells John that animal abuse is how serial killers get their start and tells him no.
moral_consequence: Jenny lives a safe any happy life and eventually meets a more reasonable man.
immoral_action: Jenny tells John that she would be honored to be his wife because she loves him.
immoral_consequence: John eventually abuses Jenny as well and hurts her physically many different times.

norm: It's bad to be prejudiced against others.
situation: John is the owner of a local paper company who is considering two job applicants for an open position, one of whom is white and the other black.
intention: John wants to decide which job applicant to hire.
moral_action: John hires the black job applicant because they are the most qualified for the position.
moral_consequence: The new hire thrives in the position and helps John's company increase its profits.
immoral_action: John hires the white job applicant despite being less qualified because he is prejudiced against minorities.
immoral_consequence: The new hire is a poor worker and John's company suffers financially.

norm: Is wrong to hurt yourself
situation: Mindy is at home being abused by John yet again.
intention: Mindy wants to feel less depressed.
moral_action: Mindy separates from her abuser John and only hangs around positive people.
moral_consequence: Mindy feels much happier and has a better life.
immoral_action: Mindy takes a kitchen knife and stabs herself in the chest out of depression.
immoral_consequence: Mindy dies and is therefore no longer able to feel anything ever again.

norm: It's wrong to be disrespectful to your parents.
situation: Gabby is in her room because her mother said she couldn't go out even though she really wants to.
intention: Gabby wants to show her mother how much she wants to go out.
moral_action: Gabby asks to have a conversation with her mother and tries to explain her motivations for going out.
moral_consequence: Gabby's mother appreciates her daughter's mature approach to the situation and feels good about the way she raised Gabby.
immoral_action: Gabby uses language she shouldn't in reference to her mother at a level her mother can clearly hear.
immoral_consequence: Gabby's mother is hurt by the vulgar insults and feels disrespected.

norm: It's not right to blame others for your own shortcomings.
situation: Frank is talking to Tom when Tom tells him that he's been struggling financially recently.
intention: Frank wants to respond to Tom's statement.
moral_action: Frank tells Tom that it's unfortunate and if he needs some help Frank can help him sort it out.
moral_consequence: Tom is delighted that Frank is offering support and feels he has a great friend in Frank.
immoral_action: Frank tells Tom that it's his own fault for not being prudent with his money, and he ought to learn how to do so.
immoral_consequence: Tom is insulted that Frank thinks he just squanders money and that everyone has equal access to money.

norm: It is good to tell friends about an opportunity.
situation: Billy has an idea on how to make a lot of money.
intention: Billy wants to capitalize on his idea.
moral_action: Billy tells a few of his friends about the idea he has on how to invest.
moral_consequence: Billy's friends join in, and they all reap the rewards of it.
immoral_action: Billy goes in on the investment completely alone, telling no one about it and succeeding.
immoral_consequence: Billy's friends get jealous about it, and stop talking to him.

norm: It's wrong to be intimate with your cousin.
situation: Brad's female cousin keeps hitting on him, and he thinks she is attractive.
intention: Brad has to decide whether to have sex with his cousin.
moral_action: Brad doesn't want inbred kids, so he decides not to have sex with his cousin.
moral_consequence: Brad feels good about himself and knows he can resist temptation.
immoral_action: Brad can't resist his cousin and decides to have sex with her.
immoral_consequence: Brad ends up feeling ashamed and has trouble getting rid of the memory.

norm: You shouldn't tell your friend's secrets to others.
situation: Dan is with his friend Mark who tells Dan that he has a crush on a girl in school.
intention: Dan wants to get the girl together with Mark.
moral_action: Dan makes sure to talk about Mark's good qualities with the girl at every possible opportunity.
moral_consequence: The girl becomes attracted to Mark and starts dating him.
immoral_action: Dan walks up to the girl and tells her that Mark is interested in her.
immoral_consequence: The girl tells her friends, the whole school finds out, and Mark is very embarrassed.

norm: It's wrong to shame people in public.
situation: Nancy notices her friend has toilet paper on her shoe.
intention: Nancy wants to tell her friend.
moral_action: Nancy pulls her friend aside and quietly tells her about the problem.
moral_consequence: Nancy's friend thanks her for her discretion.
immoral_action: Nancy loudly points out the toilet paper and laughs.
immoral_consequence: Nancy's friend becomes embarrassed and refuses to speak to her after.

norm: It's wrong to do drugs when you're underage.
situation: Jane is at a party when she is offered drugs.
intention: Jane wants to fit in.
moral_action: Jane declines and says that she feels too young to experiment with drugs.
moral_consequence: The person congratulates her on thinking for herself and Jane makes a new friend.
immoral_action: Jane takes the drugs even though she has never done drugs before.
immoral_consequence: Jane gets very sick and has to be taken to the hospital.

norm: It is good for families to talk through issues.
situation: Nick's dad is a harcore Trump supporter, but Nick has never talked to him about it.
intention: Nick has to decide whether to talk to his dad about his support for Trump.
moral_action: Nick talks to his dad about why his support for Trump bothers him.
moral_consequence: Nick is able to get things off his chest and let his dad know how he feels.
immoral_action: Nick never talks to his dad and just chooses to stay away from him.
immoral_consequence: Nick is never able to get along with his dad again.

norm: It's wrong to not respect people close to you.
situation: Andy's dad works at UPS, and he is giving Andy some career advice.
intention: Andy wants to respond to his dad's advice.
moral_action: Andy tells his dad that he'll keep his advice in mind.
moral_consequence: Andy's dad feel like he's helping Andy, and this makes him feel good.
immoral_action: Andy tells his dad not to give him any advice since he works at UPS.
immoral_consequence: Andy's dad feels disrespected and feels that Andy looks down on him.

norm: It's expected that you tip the server at a restaurant.
situation: Phil takes Jenny to a fancy restaurant he can barely afford on their first date.
intention: Phil wants to save money.
moral_action: Phil tips the waiter for his service.
moral_consequence: Jenny is impressed with her dates generosity.
immoral_action: Phil decides to skip the tip.
immoral_consequence: Jenny takes note of Phil's lack of generosity and declines a second date.

norm: You should respect events of others.
situation: Travis and Maria are celebrating their anniversary, and Chris, Travis coworker, is confused about their work project.
intention: Chris wants to contact Travis.
moral_action: Chris sends Travis an email, and Chris asks for help online from other professionals.
moral_consequence: Travis and Maria are able to have a wonderful evening.
immoral_action: Chris calls Travis multiple times with questions about their work project.
immoral_consequence: Travis is unable to enjoy time with Maria.

norm: It's rude to let someone struggle when they seem lost.
situation: Ben sees a little boy walking around in the store by himself.
intention: Ben wants to check out.
moral_action: Ben tells the boy to follow him and stops by the manager's office on the way to the register.
moral_consequence: The manager is able to reunite the lost boy with his mother in the store.
immoral_action: Ben goes to the registers with his items and lets the boy deal with his own problems.
immoral_consequence: The boy gets scared and begins to cry and even wets himself because he is scared.

norm: Friends don't steal things from other friends.
situation: Maria and her friend Jessica are at a makeup store, and Jessica grabs the last shade of Maria's favorite lipstick.
intention: Maria wants to obtain the lipstick.
moral_action: Maria asks one of the employees to check the backroom for the lipstick.
moral_consequence: Maria and Jessica come up with fun twin makeup looks after they return home with the lipsticks.
immoral_action: Maria takes the lipstick out of Jessica's shopping cart as they continue looking through the store.
immoral_consequence: Maria loses Jessica's trust after Jessica discovers the lipstick in Maria's shopping bag.

norm: It is rude to ghost people you are related to.
situation: Mary's cousin, Ann, always bombards her with tons of messages and Mary feels annoyed.
intention: Mary wants to react to the annoyance.
moral_action: Mary explains to Ann that she is too busy to read messages while working during the day.
moral_consequence: Ann feels sorry about her behavior and stops sending random messages to Mary but calls her instead for any important events.
immoral_action: Mary blocks Ann's messages and stays away from her.
immoral_consequence: Ann feels puzzled and sad not knowing what has happened to Mary.

norm: It's wrong to peep on people in bathrooms.
situation: Jake is a young man going through puberty and is feeling overwhelming sexual urges while his friend Janice is showering.
intention: Jake wants to see a naked woman.
moral_action: Jake logs onto the internet and does a google search for naked women, finding them in seconds.
moral_consequence: Janice has no idea what Jake is doing in the other room and continues to shower.
immoral_action: Jake goes to the bathroom where Janice is showering and slowly opens the door and stares at her naked body.
immoral_consequence: Janice is livid that Jake is spying on her and feels embarrassed and violated that her privacy was taken.

norm: It's bad to have body odor.
situation: Jason has spent most of his week home alone and hasn't taken a shower in 4 days.
intention: Jason wants to hang out with his friends today.
moral_action: Jason takes a shower and puts some effort into his appearance and goes out to meet his friends.
moral_consequence: Jason meets a girl while with his friends who tells him how nice he smells and asks him to hang out.
immoral_action: Jason decides not to shower after 4 days and goes to hang out with his friends anyway.
immoral_consequence: Jason's friends don't want to be around him because he smells, so they leave and stop inviting him places.

norm: You should forgive someone when they apologize to you earnestly.
situation: Carl accidentally forgot the handouts for a work meeting with his partner George and says that he is really sorry.
intention: George wants to talk to Carl about his mistake.
moral_action: George tells Carl that they really can't make mistakes like that again.
moral_consequence: Carl is understanding and promises to be more dedicated to the project going forward.
immoral_action: George tells Carl that his forgetfulness is indicative of a lack of dedication to the project and asks to do the presentation alone.
immoral_consequence: Carl feels angry and left out, so he speaks to the manager that he and George share about what he feels is unfair treatment.

norm: It is rude to expect others will cover for you.
situation: Terry works with Fred as a waiter and is scheduled to work but just learned his sister was in a car accident and is in the hospital.
intention: Terry wants to visit his sister in the hospital.
moral_action: Terry completes his shift and then visits his sister in the hospital on the way home.
moral_consequence: Terry is able to buy his sister flowers for her hospital room using the tips he made at work.
immoral_action: Terry writes an email to Fred and tells him to cover his shift, then goes to the hospital.
immoral_consequence: Terry is fired when neither he nor Fred show up for his shift that day.

norm: It's rude to excessively brag about your success.
situation: An affluent businessman, Kevin, has a blind date with a woman Susan tonight, and he would like to impress her.
intention: Kevin wants to let Susan know more about him.
moral_action: Kevin tells Susan about his life and business, but asks more questions about her.
moral_consequence: Susan sees Kevin as attentive and is intrigued by him, so accepts to go on a second date.
immoral_action: During the date, Kevin talks all about his accomplishments in the business world and never asks to hear more about Susan.
immoral_consequence: Susan thinks Kevin is self absorbed and declines to go out with him again.

norm: You should stand up for your partner.
situation: Ben and Rachel are out on a date when a few guys harass Rachel.
intention: Ben wants to prevent himself from getting hurt.
moral_action: Ben stands up to them in a non violent way stating that they will not tolerate their harassment.
moral_consequence: The group backs off, Rachel gains more respect for Ben and the relationship strengthens.
immoral_action: Ben ignores it and does not confront the guys harassing Rachel.
immoral_consequence: Rachel questions Ben character and loyalty and breaks up with him shortly after.

norm: It is not okay to drive while drunk.
situation: John is having many drinks at the bar after work.
intention: John wants to make it home in an hour to sleep in time for work.
moral_action: John uses the Uber app to hail a ride home.
moral_consequence: John makes it home safely without endangering himself or anyone else.
immoral_action: John drives himself home despite being heavily intoxicated.
immoral_consequence: John puts his life and that of others at risk.

norm: You shouldn't make fun of someone's fear of blood.
situation: Arjun is at a clinic waiting for a phlebotomist to draw blood samples, but Arjun is nervous because of his fear of blood.
intention: The phlebotomist needs to draw blood from Arjun.
moral_action: The phlebotomist notices Arjun's nervousness and explains the procedures calmly.
moral_consequence: Arjun feels better and manages to cope with his fear of blood.
immoral_action: The phlebotomist giggles at Arjun's anxiety and tells him he's acting like a little kid, and he should tough it out.
immoral_consequence: Arjun feels bad about himself and decides never to go back to that clinic for checkups.

norm: It's bad to make promises you'll regret.
situation: Joey's friends are planning on throwing a party the same day as his grandmother's birthday.
intention: Joey wants to throw a party.
moral_action: Joey tells his friends he'll join them next time around, and throws a birthday party for his grandmother instead.
moral_consequence: Joey's grandmother is elated by his thoughtfulness and has a wonderful birthday.
immoral_action: Joey and his friends throw the party, and he misses his grandmother's birthday.
immoral_consequence: Joey's grandmother is sad that he didn't come to visit her on her birthday.

norm: It's wrong to yell at a co-worker over an issue.
situation: Carla was working at a bar when her coworker spilt a drink on the floor.
intention: Carla wanted to make sure that the floor was clean where the drink had spilled.
moral_action: Carla asked her coworker nicely to take care of the spill for her.
moral_consequence: Carla's coworker cleaned up the spill and no one ended up slipping in the drink.
immoral_action: Carla yelled and belittled her coworker and told her she needed to clean up the spill.
immoral_consequence: Carla's coworker walked out on the job and Carla had to clean the mess herself.

norm: It's rude to test others.
situation: Sasha and her boyfriend have been seeing each other for 6 months.
intention: Sasha wants to know if she can trust her boyfriend.
moral_action: Sasha takes her time to really get to know him and lets trust develop.
moral_consequence: Sasha’s and her boyfriend’s feelings develop more and they end up getting married.
immoral_action: Sasha has one of her friends hit on her boyfriend to see what he does.
immoral_consequence: Sasha's boyfriend is shocked and when he finds out the truth he is devastated at the lack of trust.

norm: It is good to not smoke around kids.
situation: Jackson takes his kids to the playground and sits on a bench.
intention: Jackson wants to pass the time.
moral_action: Jackson jogs around the playground to regain energy.
moral_consequence: His kids feel that he is healthy and is a good dad.
immoral_action: Jackson takes out his vape pen and starts enjoying it.
immoral_consequence: His kids feel irritated and go to an area far away from him.

norm: You shouldn't lie about your name.
situation: Brent is pulled over by police officer Tony who tells Brent he matches a suspect description and asks Brent to tell him his name.
intention: Brent wants to answer officer Tony's question.
moral_action: Brent tells officer Tony that his name is Brent and hands him his ID.
moral_consequence: Officer Tony is appreciative that Brent seems to be cooperating right off the bat.
immoral_action: Brent tells officer Tony that his name is Phil Donahue, and he's visiting from out of state.
immoral_consequence: Officer Tony eventually asks Brent for ID and when he notices Brent was lying gets a little scared of what might happen next.

norm: It's nice to buy presents for your grandchildren.
situation: Mary's granddaughter Michelle is celebrating her 14th birthday and Mary is trying to decide what to give her.
intention: Mary wants to give Michelle something that will be useful her entire life.
moral_action: Mary opens a brokerage account for Michelle and gives her a book about investing.
moral_consequence: Michelle learns that she loves finance and decides to make that her career.
immoral_action: Mary decides the most useful thing she can do is to give Michelle nothing for her birthday so that Michelle will learn how to deal with disappointment.
immoral_consequence: Michelle doesn't appreciate Mary's lesson and wishes her grandmother was more normal.

norm: It's irresponsible to disrespect the environment.
situation: Mary is walking down the beach with her dog.
intention: Mary wants to keep the beach clean for visitors.
moral_action: Mary scoops up the dog poop into a bag and continues walking with her dog.
moral_consequence: Other people are able to walk along the beach and not worry about stepping in dog poop.
immoral_action: Mary lets her dog go to the bathroom in the sand.
immoral_consequence: A family walking down the beach steps in the dog poop.

norm: It is good to think before you act.
situation: Henry wants to change his job because he does not like his supervisor, but the job market is bad.
intention: Henry wants to make a decision regarding his job.
moral_action: Henry admits his mistake and agrees to improve while at the same time searching for a new job for a change.
moral_consequence: Henry feels secure and does not need to worry about financial instability.
immoral_action: Henry resigns from his job immediately after being blamed for a work mistake by his supervisor.
immoral_consequence: Henry is stuck at not being able to find a new job for a long time.

norm: It's wrong to hate someone because they're praised.
situation: Carl sees his co-worker get a promotion for the work they did and feels conflicted because he was not promoted.
intention: Carl wants to make sense of his feelings.
moral_action: Carl decides that he should use his co-worker as an example of how to achieve goals.
moral_consequence: Carl becomes a better worker with goals he wants to achieve.
immoral_action: Carl decides that he should dislike his co-worker as they have achieved something he has not.
immoral_consequence: Carl becomes bitter towards his co-worker and that interferes with his work.

norm: You shouldn't use your friend's phone without their permission.
situation: Lisa's phone is out of battery, and she really needs to make a phone call, Bart's phone is right there.
intention: Lisa wants to call someone right now.
moral_action: Lisa plugs her phone into the charger and calls while the phone is plugged in.
moral_consequence: Lisa finishes the call and she sighs in relief afterwards.
immoral_action: Lisa takes Bart's phone without premission and calls with it.
immoral_consequence: Bart finds out when they call back - on HIS phone - later on.

norm: It's wrong to stalk people online.
situation: Erika was talking to her friend Noelle about how she was stalking someone online and Noelle tells her not to do that.
intention: Erika wants to tell her story.
moral_action: Erika never realized that before, and she thanks her friend for warning her about it.
moral_consequence: Erika quits stalking people online and decides to do something more productive, like Mturk HITs.
immoral_action: "Erika insists that ""it's just the internet"" and that meatspace morality doesn't apply there."
immoral_consequence: Erika starts to notice that the people she's stalked are all starting to block her.

norm: It's wrong to not do what your employer asks.
situation: Dennis is stocking cereal at the grocery store and his manager tells him he has to finish stocking it before he goes on lunch break.
intention: Dennis wants to eat his lunch.
moral_action: Dennis finishes stocking the cereal and then goes to the lunch room to eat.
moral_consequence: Dennis' manager finds Dennis in the lunch room, thanks him for stocking the cereal, and joins him for lunch.
immoral_action: Dennis goes to the lunch room as soon as his manager is out of sight, without finishing stocking the cereal.
immoral_consequence: Dennis' manager finds Dennis in the lunch room and yells at him for not doing his job.

norm: It is unprofessional to forget when you have an appointment.
situation: Marnie is very busy with work and has an appointment with a vendor this afternoon.
intention: Marnie wants to do well and get her work done.
moral_action: Marnie sets a reminder on her phone for the meeting.
moral_consequence: Marnie maintains a good relationship with the vendor and gets her work done.
immoral_action: Marnie gets so wrapped up in her work that she forgets to go to the vendor meeting.
immoral_consequence: The vendor is upset and their business relationship with Marnie sours.

norm: It's bad to get addicted to heroin.
situation: Connie is extremely unhappy because she's failing out of school and her boyfriend dumped her.
intention: Connie wants to start feeling better.
moral_action: Connie begins regularly seeing a counselor to talk about her problems.
moral_consequence: Connie begins to feel more confident and happier, and her grades start to improve.
immoral_action: Connie starts using heroin regularly to get high and mask her emotional pain.
immoral_consequence: Connie overdoses and has to be rushed to the emergency room to save her life.

norm: It's bad to drink in high school.
situation: Chris goes to high school and sees a bunch of the other teens drinking.
intention: Chris wants to decide whether to drink or not.
moral_action: Chris decides that he shouldn't drink but instead study.
moral_consequence: Chris goes on to make the honor roll for his class.
immoral_action: "Chris decides to drink to be more ""cool"" to the others."
immoral_consequence: Chris ends up taken away by the cops with the others.

norm: It's wrong to judge people by their race.
situation: Roger is a loan officer at a bank, and an ambitious, millennial, African American couple, Shaun and Tamra, come in asking for a small business loan.
intention: Roger wants to perform his job.
moral_action: Roger takes note of their ambition and sees potential and goes ahead and approves their loan.
moral_consequence: Shaun and Tamra are able to start up a successful business and appreciate Roger.
immoral_action: Roger assumes because Shaun and Tamra are young and black, that they would default on the loan and doesn't approve them.
immoral_consequence: Shaun and Tamra aren't able to start their business venture and think Roger is a racist.

norm: It is good to put your phone down when driving.

intention: Ed wants to go to a new restaurant for dinner.
moral_action: Ed pulls into a gas station and asks a person for directions to the restaurant.
moral_consequence: Ed finds the restaurant and has a delicious dinner.
immoral_action: Ed looks at his phone to use his GPS app to get directions to the restaurant.
immoral_consequence: Ed smashes into the car in front of him and totals his car.

norm: You should always tell someone that you love them.
situation: Biff's father, whom he loves dearly, is dying of cancer, and Biff realizes that this is the last time he'll ever see him.
intention: Biff wants to say his last words to his father.
moral_action: Biff tells his father that he loves him and was glad to have him for a father.
moral_consequence: Biff is confident that his father knew that Biff loved him, and he feels glad knowing his father rests in peace.
immoral_action: Biff tells his father about the weather and what the stock market did that day.
immoral_consequence: Biff wonders whether his father knew that Biff loved him, and Biff feels regret every time he thinks of his dad.

norm: You shouldn't ruin someone's nap.
situation: Marlon and his brother Liam are hanging out at home while their father is taking a nap on the couch in the living room.
intention: Marlon wants to play with Liam.
moral_action: Marlon tells Liam to join him outside where they can play some Frisbee and run around.
moral_consequence: Marlon and Liam's father is able to nap without being disturbed.
immoral_action: Marlon invites Liam to play in the living room, where they run around making a lot of noise.
immoral_consequence: Marlon and Liam's father wakes up from his nap due to the noise and is very cranky.

norm: You shouldn't require someone else to pay for your things.
situation: Jerry is a broke guitar player who makes money playing at shows and is stressed out that his guitar is in bad condition.
intention: Jerry wants to obtain a new guitar.
moral_action: Jerry buys the guitar buy charging it on his credit card.
moral_consequence: Jerry's spouse is pleased because Jerry is no longer stressed over the guitar.
immoral_action: Jerry makes his spouse pay for his guitar citing that he needs it for work.
immoral_consequence: Jerry's spouse doesn't have enough money to buy something for herself now.

norm: You shouldn't expect your family to resolve your transportation difficulties.
situation: Sean has football practice.
intention: Sean wants a ride to practice.
moral_action: Sean realizes his dad is at work, so he calls a teammate to ask for ride to practice.
moral_consequence: Sean's dad is thankful that Sean took care of getting a ride on his own and didn't bother him at work.
immoral_action: Sean calls his dad at work and tells him he needs to come home to give him a ride to practice.
immoral_consequence: Sean's dad is mad and gets in trouble for leaving work to take Sean to practice.

norm: It's wrong to invade another person's space.
situation: Jack and Todd are gossiping about coworkers when Todd asks Jack if he has any secret crushes.
intention: Jack wants to answer Todd's question so only Todd can hear the answer.
moral_action: Jack whispers to Todd very quietly the answer to Todd's question.
moral_consequence: Todd smiles when he hears Jack's answer and agrees that it's a worthwhile crush to have.
immoral_action: Jack leans in so close to Todd that the tips of their noses are practically touching before he answers the question.
immoral_consequence: Todd is completely uncomfortable by Jack getting so incredibly close to him and is creeped out.

norm: It's wrong to wish harm on another person.
situation: Marcy sees Al stealing from the local grocery store.
intention: Marcy wants to alert Al that she saw him do a misdeed.
moral_action: Marcy tells Al that she saw him steal, and she hopes he puts the food back.
moral_consequence: Al tells Marcy that he's hungry but that theft is indeed below him and feels good about returning the stolen food.
immoral_action: Marcy tells Al that she saw him steal and that she hopes he dies.
immoral_consequence: Al, who is stealing because he's hungry is appalled that someone would wish death upon him for a relatively minor crime.

norm: It's expected that you love your children.
situation: Tristan, Marsha's daughter, is having a temper tantrum in the middle of a store screaming and crying.
intention: Marsha wants her daughter to stop crying.
moral_action: Marsha hugs Tristan and comforts her with kind words.
moral_consequence: Tristan stops crying and smiles.
immoral_action: Marsha wacks Tristan on the arm demanding her to stop crying in a stern tone.
immoral_consequence: Tristan's feelings are hurt.

norm: It's sad to see a student being bullied by another.
situation: Case is walking down the school hallway when he sees a bully threatening another student.
intention: Case wants to react to the confrontation.
moral_action: Case gets upset, walks up to the bully, and tells him to stop picking on the other student or else.
moral_consequence: The bully gets worried and lets the other student go, then leaves.
immoral_action: Case laughs at the bullied kid and cheers the bully on.
immoral_consequence: The bully is encouraged and begins to beat up the student.

norm: It's wrong to flirt with your parent's friends.
situation: Sandra's dad is having his friend over for dinner.
intention: Sandra wants to see the man because he is very handsome.
moral_action: Sandra joins her dad and his friend at the dinner table, admires the man's good features, and enjoys a nice dinner.
moral_consequence: Sandra's dad's friend has a good time and hopes to be invited back in the future.
immoral_action: Sandra joins her dad and his friend at the dinner table and rubs his leg with her foot under the table.
immoral_consequence: Sandra's dad's friend is shocked and leaves the house immediately.

norm: It's fine to go to a bar.
situation: Matilda works hard in school and rarely takes time for leisurely activities.

moral_action: Matilda takes the time to go to a bar with a few friends one evening after studying hard all week.
moral_consequence: Matilda has a great time.
immoral_action: Matilda never goes out to bars with her friends.
immoral_consequence: Matilda feels like she never has fun.

norm: It's wrong to hurt a child for what ever reason.
situation: Benjamin is at a children's party when a child pushes his daughter to the ground.
intention: Benjamin wants to let the kid know not to do that.
moral_action: Benjamin runs over and tells the child not to do that, and has a talk with the kid's parents.
moral_consequence: The kid apologizes to Benjamin's daughter and is then punished.
immoral_action: Benjamin runs over and slaps the kid across the face.
immoral_consequence: The kid's parents freak out and get into a shouting match with Benjamin.

norm: You shouldn't expect people to like your kids.
situation: Paul is taking care of his child and is talking to his friend on the phone who doesn't have any kids.
intention: Paul wants to catch up with his friend.
moral_action: Paul lets his friend know he is watching his child right now, so they just catch up over the phone.
moral_consequence: Paul's friend enjoys his conversation with Paul, and they catch up on a few things.
immoral_action: Paul invites his friend over to his house without telling his friend that he is watching his kid.
immoral_consequence: Paul's friend is let down to see the child when he arrives at Paul's house and doesn't have much fun.

norm: It's wrong to pirate software and not pay for it.
situation: Tom is reading video game reviews in his magazine.
intention: Tom wants to have the latest games.
moral_action: Tom saves up from his job and buys the games he wants from a store.
moral_consequence: Tom hurts no one and doesn't go to jail either and is happy.
immoral_action: Tom hops online and downloads pirated games from the internet.
immoral_consequence: Tom hurts the video game industry and may go to jail too.

norm: You shouldn't flake out on your friends.
situation: Mia is supposed to visit a haunted house with her friends, but she hates doing scary things.
intention: Mia wants to avoid being scared.
moral_action: Before entering the haunted house, Mia does some mental exercises to strengthen her mind against scary things.
moral_consequence: Mia's friends treat her to ice cream for pushing past her comfort zone.
immoral_action: Mia tells her friends that she has a bad cold at the last minute.
immoral_consequence: Mia regrets her decision after seeing pictures of her friends on Facebook.

norm: It is good to help others learn.
situation: Kara is doing her homework at the park after school, and she see's a girl, Molly, she knows from school looking confused at her notebook.
intention: Kara wants to see what Molly is so flustered about.
moral_action: Kara asks Molly what the problem is, so Molly shows her a difficult math problem, and Kara shows her how to do it properly.
moral_consequence: Molly feels relieved and is appreciative that Kara took the time to help her out.
immoral_action: Kara asks Molly what the problem is, so Molly shows her a difficult math problem, but Kara says she doesn't really have time to help.
immoral_consequence: Molly gets so frustrated that she gives up on the problem and learns nothing.

norm: You should get therapy if you want to kill yourself.
situation: Mark is really depressed because of the pandemic.
intention: Mark needs to relieve his depression without resorting to suicide.
moral_action: Mark looks online for a therapist and has an online session.
moral_consequence: Mark feels much better just by talking about his depression.
immoral_action: Mark tries to deal with the suicidal thoughts by drinking alcohol.
immoral_consequence: Mark's depression gets worse and is not relieved by the alcohol.

norm: You should always research before you buy new things.
situation: Justine recently broke her microwave and sees an ad for one at a very low price.
intention: Justine wants to purchase a new microwave .
moral_action: Justine looks up the details and specifications of a number of low-priced microwaves.
moral_consequence: Justine finds a microwave that is both low in price and compatible with her kitchen.
immoral_action: Justine buys the low-priced microwave without looking up its specifications.
immoral_consequence: The microwave turned out to only be compatible with outlets from a different country.

norm: You should always smile at people.
situation: Lisa meets Jennifer in the hallway after finishing a class.
intention: Lisa wants to respond to Jennifer.
moral_action: Lisa is happy seeing Jennifer and approaches her with a smile.
moral_consequence: Jennifer feels warm and talks to Lisa enthusiastically for a while in the hallway.
immoral_action: Lisa is tired after the class and pretends as if she doesn't see Jennifer.
immoral_consequence: Jennifer feels neglected and ignored.

norm: It is ok to encourage people to be healthy.
situation: Zach needs to give a beneficial talk at work and is thinking of topics to speak about.
intention: Zach wants to choose a topic.
moral_action: Zach chooses to talk about healthy eating and how it improves work.
moral_consequence: A few people decide to eat better, leading to an increase in productivity.
immoral_action: Zach chooses to talk about finding your true self.
immoral_consequence: Zach's audience are adults and already have a good sense of who they are, so they are bored.

norm: It is greedy to eat all the food
situation: Jasmine walks into the kitchen after a ten mile marathon, and she notices a pizza sitting on the table with her roommate Kathy absent.
intention: Jasmine wants to eat.
moral_action: Jasmine grabs a protein bar and reheats the rest of her frozen pasta before eating in the living room.
moral_consequence: Kathy shares a slice of pizza with Jasmine before placing it in her lunch box for tomorrow.
immoral_action: After waiting a minute for Kathy, Jasmine eats the entire pizza.
immoral_consequence: Kathy is unable to eat the pizza.

norm: You shouldn't ask for sex for your birthday.
situation: Tina is celebrating her birthday with some long time friends and it has been awhile since she had sex.
intention: Tina wants to enjoy her birthday.
moral_action: Tina thanks all her friends for their company on her birthday.
moral_consequence: Tina and her friends have a jolly time celebrating Tina's birthday.
immoral_action: Tina flat out asks one of her friends if they want to do the horizontal shuffle as a birthday present to her.
immoral_consequence: Tina's friend is shocked by the request and Tina feels heavy embarrassment.

norm: It is good to thank someone for making your food.
situation: Jared has been feeling sick and has spent the whole day in bed.
intention: Jared wants his wife Sandra to make him some soup.
moral_action: When Sandra brings Jared the soup she made, he thanks her for making it.
moral_consequence: Sandra feels appreciated for making the soup and asks Jared if she can get anything else for him.
immoral_action: Jared asks Sandra to make him soup and when she brings it to him he tells her to put it on the nightstand.
immoral_consequence: Sandra feels unappreciated because Jared didn't even thank her for making the soup.

norm: You shouldn't walk out on your family.
situation: Joe is stressed out raising a family of 4 with his wife Penelope, and heads out to the corner store to shop.
intention: Joe needs to find a way to cope with his stress.
moral_action: Joe buys a book on self-help book while at the convenience store.
moral_consequence: Joe's kids appreciate Joe putting effort into becoming a better person.
immoral_action: Joe finishes his shopping and decides never go back home.
immoral_consequence: Joe's kids are devastated that they have to grow up without a father.

norm: You shouldn't change the settings on your partner's games.
situation: Lana is playing her boyfriends game and notices the controls aren't intuitive for her.
intention: Lana wants to use different key settings for the game.
moral_action: Lana creates a new profile and chooses her own key settings for the controls.
moral_consequence: Lana's partner is happy that she has taken such an interest in the game.
immoral_action: Lana changes the key bindings so that it makes more sense to her.
immoral_consequence: Lana's partner is upset because it took so long for him to find suitable settings.

norm: You shouldn't steal things.
situation: Randy is at work at the office and sees some office supplies which remind him of what he needs for his home office.
intention: Randy wants to have a stapler to use at home.
moral_action: Randy stops buy an office supply store on his way home from work.
moral_consequence: Randy's office is more furnished with the supplies that he needs at home.
immoral_action: Randy takes home one of the staplers from his work office.
immoral_consequence: Randy gets caught stealing from work and is then fired from his job.

norm: It is wrong to vandalize other peoples property.
situation: Richard and his neighbor don't get along very well.
intention: Richard wants the neighbor to move his ugly RV from in front of his house.
moral_action: Richard calmly talks with his neighbor about moving the RV and offers to help him.
moral_consequence: Richard won't have to see the RV anymore because the neighbor parked it at a friend's house.
immoral_action: Richard takes a knife to the RV's tires in anger.
immoral_consequence: Richard will continue to have to look at the RV for longer since now it can't be driven.

norm: It's bad to sneak into your neighbor's house.
situation: Carlos just knocked on his good friend and neighbor Victor's door, but no one seems to be home.
intention: Carlos wants to borrow a screwdriver.
moral_action: Carlos decides to call Victor and ask him for his permission to go into his house and grab a screwdriver.
moral_consequence: Carlos gets permission and Victor tells him exactly where the screwdriver is stored.
immoral_action: Carlos decides to sneak into the house through the garage to grab the screwdriver.
immoral_consequence: Carlos finds the screwdriver and then has to come clean to Victor when it's time to return it.

norm: It's rude to seek revenge on a neighbor.
situation: Doug has a neighbor named Zane whose dog left droppings on Doug's yard.
intention: Doug wants to respond to the dog droppings.
moral_action: Doug talks to Zane about the dog leaving droppings.
moral_consequence: Zane will be more careful about where the dog goes.
immoral_action: Doug takes the dog droppings and smears them on Zane's door.
immoral_consequence: Zane will seek to destroy Doug's property in return.

norm: It's rude to miss a meeting.
situation: Zack has to meet with an important client, but he's been feeling sleepy all day.
intention: Zack wants to get some rest.
moral_action: Zack takes a short nap and then heads to the client meeting.
moral_consequence: The client is impressed with Zack and continues to give him business.
immoral_action: Zack sleeps for the rest of the day and misses the meeting.
immoral_consequence: The client decides not to do business with Zack any longer.

norm: It is irresponsible to shirk your duties.
situation: Doug has just cooked dinner for himself, dishes are everywhere, and his roommates come home.
intention: Doug wants to have a relaxing night in front of the tv.
moral_action: Doug washes his dishes quickly and jumps on the couch to watch tv.
moral_consequence: Doug's roommates are happy and can eat dinner too.
immoral_action: Doug ignores the dirty dishes and watches tv all night long.
immoral_consequence: Doug's roommates get angry they have no clean dishes to eat from.

norm: It's good to go home when you're not feeling well.
situation: Mark is at work when he realizes he has a fever.
intention: Mark needs to get his work done.
moral_action: Mark goes home and finishes his work online so that everyone is protected.
moral_consequence: No one else gets sick.
immoral_action: Mark stays at work because he has so much to get done.
immoral_consequence: Mark infects several people in his office.

norm: It's inexcusable to keep someone confined to a house.
situation: Barry is in his kitchen when his son Billy comes home and shows Barry his awful report card from this semester.
intention: Barry wants to punish Billy for the bad grades.
moral_action: Barry tells Billy that he's not going to get an allowance for a month to simulate how people with bad grades eventually fare in life.
moral_consequence: Billy learns that he should take his schooling more seriously as it might affect his finances his whole lifetime.
immoral_action: Barry tells Billy he's not allowed to leave the house for any reason for the whole entire summer.
immoral_consequence: Billy is nervous and stressed to spend all the good weather days indoors and begins to cry.

norm: It is bad to not listen while others speak.
situation: Steve is in math class and is bored.
intention: Steve wants to relieve his boredom.
moral_action: Steve starts taking notes on the lesson and asks questions to keep himself awake.
moral_consequence: Steve learns the lesson and aces the assignment.
immoral_action: Steve doodles on his notebook paper while the teacher is talking.
immoral_consequence: Steve misses the lesson and fails the homework assignment.

norm: It's good to be supportive when someone loses their child.
situation: Anna's employee Jan's son died suddenly yesterday.
intention: Anna wants a large report compiled for a business meeting.
moral_action: Anna assigns Beverly to write the report and gives Jan the week off of work.
moral_consequence: Jan has time to mourn the loss of her son.
immoral_action: Anna assigns Jan to write the report.
immoral_consequence: Jan does not have time to properly grieve for her son.

norm: It is rude to date someone while dating another person.
situation: Dave who has a girlfriend is out with friends at a mall when he's asked on a date for that night by another woman.
intention: Dave wants to answer the woman's proposal.
moral_action: Dave tells the woman that he's taken, and he cannot go out with her even if she's pretty.
moral_consequence: Dave's friends tell Dave's girlfriend who is happy to find out Dave is capable of being faithful.
immoral_action: Dave tells the woman that he'd be glad to take her out that night and gives her his phone number.
immoral_consequence: Dave's friends tell Dave's girlfriend who is shocked that he hurt her so much and cheated on her.

norm: It's wrong to abandon your close friends.
situation: Joe's best friend, Brian, is moving and asked Joe for help, but Joe feels tired.
intention: Joe wants to take a nap.
moral_action: Joe helps Brian, and they get the move done quickly.
moral_consequence: Joe can take his nap after they are done moving.
immoral_action: Joe blows off Brian and takes a long nap, ignoring Brian's calls and texts.
immoral_consequence: Brian gets very angry at Joe and tells him never to contact him again.

norm: You shouldn't take your parent's lifestyle decisions personally
situation: Brad's parents decided to divorce, because his mom fell in love with another woman.
intention: Brad wanted to say something to his mom.
moral_action: Brad tells his mom that he's proud that she's found someone that she truly loves.
moral_consequence: Brad's mom is elated that Brad supports her and feels that she made the right decision.
immoral_action: Brad tells his mom that he feels betrayed by her.
immoral_consequence: Brad's mom's feelings are hurt, and she begins to feel guilty.

norm: You shouldn't mock people.
situation: Abby said something annoying.
intention: John wants to respond to her to show how he feels.
moral_action: John takes Abby aside and tells her how what she has said is bothering him.
moral_consequence: John and Abby remain friends and Abby realizes she was being annoying.
immoral_action: John looked at Abby and starting repeating what she said in a high pitched voice.
immoral_consequence: Abby and the other friends watching are annoyed with John for being rude.

norm: Helping a person cheat on school work is wrong.
situation: Beth is hanging out with her friend Matt who asks her for help on a math test review assignment they have to complete for homework.
intention: Beth wants to help Matt with the homework.
moral_action: Beth spends time going over each test review question and letting Matt work out the answers himself.
moral_consequence: Matt gets a good grade on the math test because Beth prepared him well and didn't do the work for him.
immoral_action: Beth fills in the homework for Matt without teaching him what any of it means.
immoral_consequence: Matt does poorly on the test the next day because he doesn't understand the underlying principles from the review.

norm: It's disgusting to betray your partner's trust.
situation: Cory has a girlfriend who he is losing interest in and is developing an interest in another woman.
intention: Cory wants to hang out with the other woman.
moral_action: Cory is open to his partner about how he has been feeling.
moral_consequence: Cory's partner is given proper notice and does not expect their relationship to endure.
immoral_action: Cory tells his partner that he is with a male friend of his.
immoral_consequence: Cory's partner finds out about the other girl and feels betrayed.

norm: You should buy auto-insurance before you drive on the highway.
situation: Jared is living paycheck to paycheck, and he cannot afford his current insurance premium.
intention: Jared wants to cut back his insurance costs.
moral_action: Jared finds an insurance company that charges much lower premiums.
moral_consequence: Jared is more at ease while driving knowing that he is insured.
immoral_action: Jared decides to go without insurance in order to skirt the costs.
immoral_consequence: Jared gets pulled over and gets a fine for not having insurance.

norm: It's good to be supportive of your classmates.
situation: James, who isn't particularly interested in sports, just found out that his school's football team qualified for the state championships.
intention: James wants to avoid annoying his classmates.
moral_action: James congratulates all his classmates who are on the football team.
moral_consequence: James is invited to a party before the game, which he enjoys even though the game is rather boring.
immoral_action: James plays with his phone while everyone else is congratulating the football team.
immoral_consequence: James isn't invited to the big party before the state championship game.

norm: You shouldn't joke about people.
situation: Micheal wants to create a trending hashtag on twitter, and he notices that his favorite celebrity Jackson has not posted in weeks.
intention: Micheal wants to gain more followers.
moral_action: Micheal decides to share a story about his first kiss.
moral_consequence: Micheal's tweet starts a trend, and it nets him more followers.
immoral_action: Micheal creates the hashtag #JacksonIsDeadParty with a goofy picture.
immoral_consequence: Micheal is sent hateful direct messages when people take his hashtag seriously.

norm: It's good to not want to pester your spouse.
situation: Samuel has the day off work and wants to have cocktails with his wife Vivian, but he see's she's busy writing a paper for work.
intention: Samuel wants to ask Vivian to join him.
moral_action: Samuel asks Vivian if when she is finished, if she would like to have some drinks with him.
moral_consequence: Vivian is able to finish her work in a timely fashion, and she is able to join Samuel for drinks.
immoral_action: Samuel persistently asks Vivian to have drinks with him every hour on the hour.
immoral_consequence: Vivian's concentration is interrupted repeatedly, so she ends up having to work longer.
