norm: It's good to contribute ideas to a group project
situation: Pat is sitting with his work group who are brainstorming ideas for their project.
intention: Pat wants to avoid thinking too hard for the sake of the project.
moral_action: Pat recycles some ideas from a project he did in the past.
moral_consequence: Pat's team believes he is contributing as much as they are.
immoral_action: Pat sits back and lets the others come up with the ideas.
immoral_consequence: Pat's team notices this and hold it against him for not participating.

norm: You should not make a scene in public places.
situation: Vernon is walking through the store to buy soap when Jeannine grabs the last bar off the shelf right in front of him.
intention: Vernon wants to make a comment to Jeannine.
moral_action: Vernon chuckles and tells Jeannine that she got one over him this time and that he needs to be faster.
moral_consequence: Jeannine laughs and the two of them exchange a few pleasantries before she leaves.
immoral_action: Vernon throws his bags on the ground and stomps his foot while exclaiming that Jeannine took what is rightfully his.
immoral_consequence: Jeannine is embarrassed as everyone starts to look at her and angry at Vernon for accusing her of theft.

norm: You shouldn't search for your ex on Instagram.
situation: Veronica recently broke up with her boyfriend Archer and hasn't spoken to him since.
intention: Veronica wants to find out what Archer has been up to since their breakup.
moral_action: Veronica asks a common friend about what Archer's been up to since their breakup.
moral_consequence: Veronica finds out about Archer's recent activities through her friend, who knows how to tell her without making her upset.
immoral_action: Veronica decides to go on Instagram and search for Archer's account, so she can check up on him.
immoral_consequence: Veronica gets upset when she sees all the pictures that Archer has been posting, and she misses him.

norm: It is rude to abandon your friends.
situation: Ben was at a party, and he had brought some of his friends with him.
intention: Ben wants to go home.
moral_action: Ben tells his friends that he is leaving and offers them a ride home.
moral_consequence: Ben's friends are able to get home from the party safely.
immoral_action: Ben leaves from the party without telling his friends and goes to his house.
immoral_consequence: Ben's friends are stranded, and they don't have a ride home.

norm: You should tell people about the life you've lived.
situation: Tom, who was arrested for a crime in the past, is filling out a job application and needs to answer about any past crimes.
intention: Tom wants to get the job.
moral_action: Tom says that he did commit a crime, but has been rehabilitated.
moral_consequence: Tom is hired with a probationary period to prove his worth.
immoral_action: Tom says that he has never committed a crime and hands the application in.
immoral_consequence: The background check shows that Tom lied about not committing a crime, and he is denied the job.

norm: You shouldn't ignore homeless people.
situation: Amy had to walk by a small group of homeless people begging for money on her way to work every morning.
intention: Amy  doesn't want to give the homeless people any money.
moral_action: Amy explains to the homeless people that she sadly doesn't have any extra money, and they warn her that the subway isn't working that morning.
moral_consequence: Amy is able to catch a bus and get to work on time thanks to the homeless people telling her about the subway shutdown.
immoral_action: Amy turns up the volume on her music, so she can't hear what the homeless people are saying to her.
immoral_consequence: Amy doesn't hear the homeless people warn her about the broken fire hydrant, and she gets soaked by water from the hydrant.

norm: It's rude to hang up on a friend.
situation: David is talking to his friend Adam on the phone and it is getting close to bed time.
intention: David needs to get off the phone to get ready for bed.
moral_action: David waits for a break in the conversation and tells Adam he needs to go.
moral_consequence: Adam and David amicably end the conversation.
immoral_action: David hangs up on Adam while Adam is in the middle of talking.
immoral_consequence: Adam is offended by the sudden end to the phone call.

norm: Kicking someone you love out of their house is dramatic.
situation: Karen is in a long term relationship and it is very often contentious.
intention: Karen wants to get her point across during an argument.
moral_action: Karen sits down with her partner and talks about the issue without so much as raising her voice.
moral_consequence: Karen's partner responds with the same calmness, and they resolve the issue.
immoral_action: Karen kicks her partner out of his own home to show how serious she is about the matter.
immoral_consequence: Karen's partner grows increasingly weary about their relationship and wants to break up with her.

norm: It is wrong to manipulate people to get sympathy.
situation: Henry had lost his job and didn't have much money in his account.
intention: Henry wanted to get money to pay his car and house notes.
moral_action: Henry started looking for jobs as soon as he was fired.
moral_consequence: Henry got steady paychecks and was able to pay all his bills.
immoral_action: Henry told everyone that he was dying and needed money for medical bills.
immoral_consequence: Henry went to jail for fraud when everyone found out he wasn't sick.

norm: It's hurtful not to speak to someone.
situation: Sam's wife Karen accidentally bumps into a shelf and  breaks his favorite porcelain figurine.
intention: Sam wants to react to the accident.
moral_action: Sam tells his wife that it's just a figurine which he can buy again anytime he wants and that it's OK.
moral_consequence: Karen is relieved that Sam isn't mad and tells him that she'll replace it for him.
immoral_action: Sam tells his wife that the figurine was one of his prized possessions, and he doesn't want to speak to her anymore.
immoral_consequence: Karen is shocked that Sam is reacting so harshly and is sad he is going to give her the silent treatment.

norm: You should treat someone's injuries if they are badly hurt.
situation: Henry is walking with his friend, Paul, falls forward, busting open his head.
intention: Henry wants to help Paul.
moral_action: Henry uses his shirt to bandage Paul's wound and then gets Paul an ambulance.
moral_consequence: Paul gets some stitches and feels better a couple days later.
immoral_action: Henry tells Paul to man up and walk it off until they get to the hospital.
immoral_consequence: Paul falls unconscious while walking to the hospital and suffer brain damage.

norm: It's encouraged to be generous with others.
situation: Elizabeth is a small business owner on a tight budget and is taking a prospective financial backer out to lunch to try to convince him to invest in her business.
intention: Elizabeth wants to make a good impression to the investor.
moral_action: Elizabeth uses her limited to funds to buy an average cost lunch for them, but that enables her to leave a large tip for the waitress.
moral_consequence: The investor sees how well Elizabeth rewarded the waitress and decides that Elizabeth is the kind of person he wants to invest his money in.
immoral_action: Elizabeth uses her limited funds to buy an expensive lunch for them, but this requires her to leave a very small tip for the waitress.
immoral_consequence: The investor sees how poorly she rewarded the waitress and decides Elizabeth is not the kind of person he wants to invest in.

norm: It's good to handle your business in an expedient manner.
situation: Ben ordered a computer from an online store, but it doesn't work properly.
intention: Ben wants to return the computer.
moral_action: Ben repackages the computer and sends it back the next day.
moral_consequence: Ben gets a full refund on the computer.
immoral_action: Ben gets caught up in other things and returns the computer a month after he received it.
immoral_consequence: The return is rejected and Ben is stuck with a bad computer.

norm: It's wrong to spy on your partner.
situation: Drew and his girlfriend Diana have been together for a while, and Drew suspects she's bored witht he relationship.
intention: Drew wants to find out if Diana might leave him.
moral_action: Drew asks Diana if she's happy with the state of their relationship.
moral_consequence: Diana appreciates Drew's concern over the health of the relationship, and they stay together.
immoral_action: Drew starts hacking into Diana's e-mails and social media, trying to see if she's talking to any guys.
immoral_consequence: Diana finds out Drew's been violating her privacy and dumps him.

norm: You shouldn't be living with your ex.
situation: Shane is living in a shared apartment with a girl that he used to date who doesn't have much respect for him.
intention: Shane wants to save money on rent.
moral_action: Shane evicts his ex and finds a new roommate to share the place with.
moral_consequence: Shane's ex learns that not everyone will tolerate this sort of treatment.
immoral_action: Shane continues to stay with his ex because he only has to pay half the rent.
immoral_consequence: Shane's ex thinks that he is a pushover and treats him poorly.

norm: You shouldn't decline someone's invite.
situation: James was invited to a baseball game by Mike, but he didn't feel like going.
intention: James wants to decide what to do.
moral_action: James decides to go anyway and have fun with Mike.
moral_consequence: Between innings the announcer states that a ticket number has won $100,000 and it turns out to be Jame's ticket.
immoral_action: James declines the ticket and Mike takes one of their other friends instead.
immoral_consequence: At the stadium the other friend has the right ticket and wins $100,000 in a promotion.

norm: It's not nice to take credit for someone's hard work.
situation: Sally's partner for a school project stayed up late and did most of the work for the project.
intention: Sally wants to get a good grade on the project.
moral_action: Sally talks to her partner and asks if there's anything she can do to help out with the project.
moral_consequence: Sally's partner thinks of something for Sally to do, so she can earn the credit for the project.
immoral_action: Sally goes to the teacher and tells the teacher that she did the work that her partner actually did.
immoral_consequence: Sally's partner finds out and proves to the teacher that they did all the work.

norm: You shouldn't watch TV if your parent says no.
situation: Mark's parents have said no TV today.
intention: Mark needs to do something relaxing.
moral_action: Mark reads a book.
moral_consequence: His parents are glad he is obedient.
immoral_action: Mark decides to watch TV anyway.
immoral_consequence: His parents find out and ground him.

norm: You're expected to drive carefully.
situation: Kevin just realized he is late for his date with Jean, so he gets into his car to meet her.
intention: Kevin wants to get to Jean.
moral_action: Kevin decides to call Jean to let her know he's on his way, but running late.
moral_consequence: Kevin makes it to Jean safely, and she is glad he was careful driving to meet her.
immoral_action: Kevin, being in a rush, drives over the speed limit and swerves which causes him to get pulled over, making him more late for his date with Jean.
immoral_consequence: Kevin gets a ticket and Jean is angry at him for not taking his time to be careful.

norm: It's bad to waste electricity on needless activities.
situation: Rick has a workshop in his house and has just created a miniature tesla coil for fun.
intention: Rick wants to show off the tesla coil.
moral_action: Rick shoots a short video of the tesla coil and posts it online on his social media network.
moral_consequence: Other people see the tesla coil and are impressed, while Rick doesn't waste money.
immoral_action: Rick mounts the tesla coil on top of his house and runs it for a week straight.
immoral_consequence: The electricity bill goes up by several hundred dollars and Rick has a hard time paying it.

norm: It's wrong to bring weapons into your school.
situation: John is parking his car in the school parking lot when he remembers that he forgot to take his handgun out of his school bag.
intention: John wants to find a place to store the handgun.
moral_action: John decides to put the handgun in his car's trunk since that would be locked all day.
moral_consequence: John gets through the school day as normal and takes the gun back home at the end of the day with no consequence.
immoral_action: John decides to bring the handgun into the school and store it in his locker until the day is done.
immoral_consequence: The school's metal detector goes off and John is caught and expelled from school.

norm: It's wrong to park somewhere you are not allowed.
situation: John drives to the mall for some last minute Christmas shopping when he realizes that the parking lot is very full.
intention: John wants to find a place to park.
moral_action: John drives slowly around the parking lot until a spot opens up and takes it.
moral_consequence: John has a successful shopping trip at the mall.
immoral_action: John parks his car on the sidewalk in front of the mall.
immoral_consequence: John's car gets towed for illegally parking.

norm: It's wrong to be cold to people.
situation: There is a family reunion coming up and Fred hates those things.
intention: Fred wants to get through it as easily as possible.
moral_action: Fred decided to go to the reunion and act nice to everyone even though he didn’t want to go.
moral_consequence: Fred ended up actually having a great time, and he even met a few family members he didn’t know he had.
immoral_action: At the reunion, a family member tried talking to Fred, but Fred just acted aloof and mumbled one word answers.
immoral_consequence: The family member thought Fred was rude, so he took Fred out of his will.

norm: It's bad to hate a good friend.
situation: Doris wears a pair of new shoes and plays with her friend Eva, who accidentally steps on her shoe making it dirty.
intention: Doris wants to react to her dirty shoes.
moral_action: Doris tells Eva that her shoes are new and feels sad about the accident making them dirty.
moral_consequence: Eva cleans the shoes for Doris and decorates her shoes with her favorite pins, and Doris feels happy.
immoral_action: Doris acts in an antagonistic way toward Eva whenever they meet.
immoral_consequence: Eva feels puzzled and depressed.

norm: It's good to see your country's national parks.
situation: Greg has time off from work for a couple of weeks.
intention: Greg wants to take a road trip.
moral_action: Greg drives to various national parks and brings camping supplies.
moral_consequence: Greg experiences nature and new sights.
immoral_action: Greg drives to the college he went to to hang out with his old frat buddies.
immoral_consequence: Greg experiences the same things he's done in the past.

norm: You shouldn't desire to be an unhealthy weight.
situation: Though Jessica is at a normal weight, she feels like she looks fat when she looks in the mirror.
intention: Jessica wants to feel pretty.
moral_action: Jessica realizes she already looks pretty and doesn't change anything.
moral_consequence: Jessica becomes more confident and is able to handle any problems in her life.
immoral_action: Jessica stops eating and starves herself to lose some weight.
immoral_consequence: Jessica starts having serious health problems and has to go to the hospital.

norm: It is bad to abuse pain killers.
situation: Jake is recovering from having his wisdom teeth removed and is on Vicodin for the pain.
intention: Jake wants to numb the pain.
moral_action: Jake takes the recommended dosage for the pain.
moral_consequence: Jake's pain is relieved and it gets him through the worst part of the healing process.
immoral_action: Jake takes double the recommended dosage because the pain is so bad.
immoral_consequence: Jake falls into a coma and nearly dies.

norm: It's good to tell the truth instead of keeping secrets.
situation: James knew that his boss at McDonald's sometimes served hamburgers well past their expiration date.
intention: James wants to avoid unemployment.
moral_action: James applies for new jobs until he finds a better position, then calls the local food safety inspector.
moral_consequence: The McDonald's is shut down temporarily and the manger is fired, but James is content at his new position.
immoral_action: James doesn't mention the expired meat to anyone, so he can keep his job.
immoral_consequence: Eventually some customers get sick and sue the McDonald's where James works.

norm: It's rude to destroy other people's property.
situation: Jason is taking a shortcut home though an alley when his way is blocked by a locked gated fence.
intention: Jason wants to get home.
moral_action: Jason decides to just change his path and take the long way home.
moral_consequence: Jason gets home a little later than he wanted to but without incident.
immoral_action: Jason kicks open the gate breaking the lock in the process and continues to his house.
immoral_consequence: Jason is seen breaking the lock and is later fined for the damages.

norm: It's impolite to overstay one's welcome.
situation: Mack has not seen his brother in several years and wants to visit him at his home in another state.
intention: Mack wants to spend time with his brother.
moral_action: Mack goes to his brother's house for a week visit, where they visit places together and have a great time.
moral_consequence: His brother thanks him for the visit and invites him back next summer to stay.
immoral_action: Mack surprises his brother with a visit and stays for a month.
immoral_consequence: His brother ends up becoming tired of Mack being there so long and tells Mack he has to leave immediately.

norm: It's wrong to treat a sibling's friend badly.
situation: John is at home while he is day off and his sister, Mary, is playing with her friend in their home.
intention: John wants to watch his favorite movie.
moral_action: John goes to his bedroom and watches the movie in a laptop.
moral_consequence: Mary thanks John for being considerate and agrees to stay quiet as far as possible.
immoral_action: John asks Mary's friend to leave their home so that he can enjoy his movie quietly.
immoral_consequence: Mary feels disrespected and started arguing with John.

norm: It's rude to insult someone's intelligence.
situation: Shyla is watching her husband having trouble putting together a piece of furniture.
intention: Shyla wants to vocalize her observations to her husband.
moral_action: Shyla makes a tongue in cheek crack at her husband's efforts to assemble the piece of furniture.
moral_consequence: Shyla's husband laughs at her observation and invites her to try her hands at it in playful manner which they both laugh at.
immoral_action: Shyla comments on the instructions seeming very straight forward which implies things about her husbands abilities.
immoral_consequence: Shyla's husband is miffed by the insinuating observation and the couple get into a squabble.

norm: It's nice to help others by sharing.
situation: Hugo had just ordered a pizza pie when his friend, Ben, comes over.
intention: Hugo wants to eat pizza.
moral_action: Hugo offers Ben some slices of his pizza.
moral_consequence: Ben takes two slices and promises to pay Hugo back.
immoral_action: Hugo doesn't offer Ben any pizza even though he suspects Ben may want some.
immoral_consequence: Hugo eats a slice of pizza and puts the rest away while Ben sneaks awkward glances at the pizza.

norm: You shouldn't invite yourself to events.
situation: Jack and Jill are planning on attending a party this upcoming weekend, while John eavesdrops on their conversation, unbeknownst to them.
intention: John wants to find plans to fill his empty weekend.
moral_action: John waits until a conversation is being had between all three of them, and asks them if they have any plans for the weekend.
moral_consequence: Jill tells John about the party and both tell John he is more than welcome to come if he has no plans.
immoral_action: John buts in and asks where his invite is.
immoral_consequence: The atmosphere becomes tense and awkward as Jack and Jill try to think of excuses for why they may not end up going.

norm: You shouldn't spoil movies.
situation: Sean just saw a great film and is exited to tell his brother Mike he needs to see it.
intention: Sean wants to recommend the film.
moral_action: Sean calls up Mike and tells him how good this movie was while being careful not to reveal too much about the plot.
moral_consequence: Mike is intrigued and buys himself some tickets to see the film.
immoral_action: Sean calls up Mike and in his excitement reveals the ending to him.
immoral_consequence: Mike doesn't want to watch this film because he knows what will happen already.

norm: It's bad to repeat a grade multiple times.
situation: Luna is struggling in school and has already repeated her junior year because of bad grades.
intention: Luna wants to catch up in school.
moral_action: Luna decides to sign up for summer school during her summer break.
moral_consequence: Luna's peers think she has made a responsible decision and is becoming mature.
immoral_action: Luna decides to repeat the grade another time in order to learn the material.
immoral_consequence: Luna's peers develop a bad opinion of her due to her being stuck in 11th grade.

norm: People shouldn't take more than they need.
situation: Fernando is a hungry student at school and is in the cafeteria to eat lunch.
intention: Fernando wants to get food.
moral_action: Fernando gets one plate and returns for seconds according to his hunger level.
moral_consequence: The cafeteria makes good use of its food and doesn't waste much of anything.
immoral_action: Fernando takes an extra plate of food in case he doesn't get enough, then fills up before he can eat it all.
immoral_consequence: The food is thrown out and the cafeteria has to pay extra money for the waste.

norm: It's rude to keep someone else's USB drive.
situation: Katie would just take usb drives out of computers and keep them.
intention: Katie wants to own more USB drives.
moral_action: Katie decides to stop taking random USB drives and buy her own.
moral_consequence: Katie's computer appreciates not having strange usb drives plugged into it.
immoral_action: Katie keeps taking usb drives that she finds and uses them herself.
immoral_consequence: Eventually she mistakenly takes a USB killer and fries her computer.

norm: It's good to give money to people for their trouble.
situation: Ben's car broke down in the middle of a highway, and a stranger stopped to help.
intention: Ben wants to thank the stranger.
moral_action: Ben gives the stranger a $50 bill as he gets ready to leave.
moral_consequence: The stranger thinks that it was worth it to stop and help.
immoral_action: Ben offers the stranger a hug and thanks him for what he did.
immoral_consequence: The stranger isn't compensated for helping Ben when he didn't have to.

norm: It's immoral to bully or harass another person.
situation: Paul and Greg go to Junior high together.
intention: Paul wants to appear tough in front of others.
moral_action: Paul and Greg become friends and try out for football together.
moral_consequence: Paul becomes a starting linebacker and is respected by his peers at school.
immoral_action: Paul teases Greg every day.
immoral_consequence: Greg stands up to Paul beating him in a fight and causing humiliation.

norm: You should not ignore your responsibilities.
situation: Douglas is at his busy job on a Monday morning.
intention: Douglas wants to reduce his work stress.
moral_action: Douglas signs up for a time management class after work.
moral_consequence: Douglas feels calmer and more competent at his job.
immoral_action: Douglas ignores some job tasks and rests with his feet up at his desk.
immoral_consequence: Douglas' boss sees him and fires him on the spot.

norm: You shouldn't try to have a baby with someone noncommittal.
situation: Jake has recently told his girlfriend Megan that he isn't interested in having a baby with her.
intention: Megan wants to have kids.
moral_action: Megan tells Jake that the relationship isn't going to work.
moral_consequence: Megan is able to find another man that is willing to have children.
immoral_action: Megan tries to trick Jake into having a baby with her.
immoral_consequence: Jake finds out that Megan is pregnant, and he leaves her right away.

norm: It's rude to destroy things that were a gift.
situation: Katya's grandmother knitted her a sweater and a beanie as Christmas gifts.
intention: Katya wants to use her grandmother's gifts.
moral_action: Katya wears the sweater and beanie when she visited her grandmother.
moral_consequence: Katya's grandmother feels happy that Katya is using her gifts.
immoral_action: Katya pulls apart the sweater and beanie to make a scarf for herself.
immoral_consequence: Katya's grandmother is saddened that Katya didn't appreciate her handmade clothes.

norm: Being dishonest is wrong.
situation: Ed is a used care salesman at at local dealership.
intention: Ed wants to best his monthly quota by selling one more vehicle.
moral_action: Ed points out that the car is not a very good option and shows the buyer a more reliable vehicle that meets his requirements.
moral_consequence: The buyer is happy with his choice and decides to rely on Ed for his future car shopping.
immoral_action: Ed misrepresents a car's maintenance history  in order to make a sale.
immoral_consequence: The buyer faces a big repair bill when the car breaks down during his first week of ownership.

norm: It's bad to fall asleep at your desk at work.
situation: John is at work finishing up some accounts.
intention: John isn't feeling well and needs to rest.
moral_action: John tells his boss he's not feeling well and goes home to sleep.
moral_consequence: John's boss is caring and lets him leave.
immoral_action: John falls asleep right in his cubicle.
immoral_consequence: His boss notices him sleeping and fires him.

norm: It's wrong to interfere in a sibling's relationship.
situation: Jenny is worried that her sister's boyfriend won't be able to provide financially for her.
intention: Jenny wants to make sure her sister is happy.
moral_action: Jenny talks to her sister about her concerns, and offers to help find a better paying job.
moral_consequence: Jenny's sister is grateful for the help and feels more financially secure.
immoral_action: Jenny confronts her sister's boyfriend and demands he get a better job to earn more money.
immoral_consequence: Jenny's sister is angry at the intrustion and stops speaking to Jenny.

norm: You should not wander away from your parents.
situation: Wendy is a young child at the mall with her parents and see a store that interests her.
intention: Wendy wants to go into the store.
moral_action: Wendy takes her parents to the store with her.
moral_consequence: Wendy's parents will be able to know where she is.
immoral_action: Wendy leaves her parents to go into the store.
immoral_consequence: Wendy's parents will become worried about where she is.

norm: It is rude to tattle on people.
situation: Dave's older brother Mike often has friends over.
intention: Dave wants to be noticed by his older brother and his friends.
moral_action: Dave asks to join their activities and talks about their common interests.
moral_consequence: Mike and Dave have the same group of friends for their childhood and beyond.
immoral_action: Dave tattles on Mike and his friends every time they are over.
immoral_consequence: Mike does not trust Dave, so he ignores him and will not let him hang out with his group of friends.

norm: People who are liars should not be given your understanding.
situation: Dominick's employee Shana tells Dominick she did project work that Dominick actually did.
intention: Dominick wants to respond to Shana's assertion.
moral_action: Dominick tells Shana that she is being let go for not telling the truth.
moral_consequence: Shana will learn that she should not lie about her work.
immoral_action: Dominick tells Shana that she is a competent employee.
immoral_consequence: Shana will learn that she can take credit for others' work.

norm: It's good to be punctual.
situation: Ryan has an interview with Cassandra at noon and is getting ready in his house.
intention: Ryan wants to look his best for the interview.
moral_action: Ryan leaves the house promptly, making sure that he gets to the venue a few minutes early to freshen up before he meets Cassandra.
moral_consequence: Cassandra is impressed by Ryan's appearance and timeliness and strongly considers him for the position.
immoral_action: Ryan takes too long fixing his hair to make sure that it looks perfect before heading to his interview and is 15 minutes late.
immoral_consequence: Ryan looks great but has not made a good impression on Cassandra at all, she feels less interested in him for the position.

norm: It's illegal to break the age of consent law.
situation: Pat meets a bunch of teenaged girls at the mall that he is working at.
intention: Pat wants to talk to the girls.
moral_action: Pat asks the girls if there is anything that he can do to help them.
moral_consequence: Pat is recognized as his boss as the employee of the month for his customer service.
immoral_action: Pat asks the girls if they want to go out on a date with him.
immoral_consequence: Pat is later arrested for dating the girl who is under the age of consent.

norm: It's rude to judge someone just because of their age.
situation: Gail meets a woman named Jill at the gym who mentions that she is in her 60s.
intention: Gail wants to respond respond to Jill.
moral_action: Gail tells Jill she's an inspiration to her.
moral_consequence: Jill will feel proud about working out.
immoral_action: Gail tells Jill that she shouldn't bother with working out as she is elderly.
immoral_consequence: Jill will feel self conscious about going to the gym.

norm: It's good to compliment the beauty of others.
situation: Russel is at home with his wife who just had a long day.
intention: Russel wants to make his wife feel better.
moral_action: During a quiet moment Russel earnestly compliments his wife's physical looks.
moral_consequence: Russel's wife knows he is speaking from the heart and is warmed by his compliment.
immoral_action: Russel suggests that his wife may enjoy a bath because she looks worn out.
immoral_consequence: Russel's wife misinterprets the intention of Russel's suggestion and assumes he is pointing out how bad she looks.

norm: People are expected to be grateful for gifts.
situation: It is Christmas morning and ten year old Allison is opening her presents.
intention: Allison wants a new Xbox for Christmas.
moral_action: Allison thanks her parents for all the gifts they got her and asks if they will get her an Xbox in the future.
moral_consequence: Allison's parents get her an Xbox for her birthday a few months later.
immoral_action: Allison throws a tantrum, screaming and crying at her parents when an XBox is not one of her gifts.
immoral_consequence: Allison is grounded by her parents and is not allowed to go to her friend's house to play video games.

norm: It isn't okay to be overly dependent on other people.
situation: Jake lives at his parents house rent free and is playing video games when his mom Jenny bursts in and asks him when he's going to get a job.
intention: Jake wants to answer his mom's question.
moral_action: Jake tells his mom that he'll get his act together and get a job as soon as there's an opening.
moral_consequence: Jenny is delighted that her son is taking his future seriously and is planning on unburdening her and her husband of his presence.
immoral_action: Jake tells his mom he's not really planning on getting a job since he can live with her and dad for free.
immoral_consequence: Jenny is infuriated that her son thinks it's OK to continue to mooch off her and her husband forever.

norm: You should be able to get your own ride places.
situation: Vince doesn't have a car but has been invited to a party 45 minutes away from his house.
intention: Vince wants to go to the party.
moral_action: Vince takes an Uber to the party and back.
moral_consequence: Vince's friends are all happy to see Vince at the party and aren't inconvenienced by him.
immoral_action: Vince asks his friend Hannah who gives him a lot of rides to drive him to the party and back.
immoral_consequence: Hannah drives Vince but begins to resent him for always using her for rides.

norm: It's dishonest to take credit for work you didn't do.
situation: Harry is working on a project for his boss at work.
intention: Harry wants to get his work done on time.
moral_action: Harry works a lot of overtime hours to complete the project.
moral_consequence: Harry is praised by his boss for doing a good job.
immoral_action: Harry copies some work that a coworker completed and uses it in his project to save time.
immoral_consequence: Harry gets fired when his boss discovers his plagiarism of his coworker.

norm: You should help someone who is struggling with suicidal thoughts.
situation: Paul is hanging out with his friend Zach, who has been making subtle remarks about death and suicide.
intention: Paul wants to hang out with Zach.
moral_action: Paul tells Zach that he is here to help if Zach is serious about his suicide talk.
moral_consequence: Zach confides that he is depressed, and Paul gets him to call a professional to help him.
immoral_action: Paul ignores Zach's comments and acts like nothing is wrong with him.
immoral_consequence: Zach goes home after hanging out with Paul and commits suicide.

norm: It's not okay to be hateful to others.
situation: While out with work friends Jane runs across her ex Paul who dumped her without warning a few months ago.
intention: Jane wants closure to their relationship.
moral_action: Jane pulls Paul aside to have a private talk about her lingering feelings.
moral_consequence: Jane is able to get everything off her chest and can now move past their relationship.
immoral_action: Jane slaps Paul and yells out that he has a tiny penis.
immoral_consequence: Jane has to deal with rumors at her work about her temper.

norm: You shouldn't buy more than your budget can take.
situation: Roger's rent is due, but he really wants to buy a new pair of boots.
intention: Roger wants to make a decision.
moral_action: Roger puts off purchasing the boots until after his bills are paid.
moral_consequence: Roger is able to not end up in additional debt by budgeting correctly.
immoral_action: Roger decides to buy the new boots and worry later.
immoral_consequence: When Roger writes his rent check it bounces, and he owes the bank additional fees.

norm: It's frowned upon to cheat on a loved one.
situation: Jack, who is married, is at the bar with some friends when he's asked by an attractive stranger, Janet to go home with her.
intention: Jack wants to respond to Janet's proposal.
moral_action: Jack tells Janet that there's absolutely no chance she'll ever have a piece of him.
moral_consequence: Jack's friends are delighted to see Jack upholding his vows and staying faithful to his wife.
immoral_action: Jack tells Janet that she won't have to ask him twice since she's so good looking.
immoral_consequence: Jack's friends are disgusted how cheap and loose Jack is and how he's betraying his wife.

norm: It is expected that you repay your debts
situation: Mark has racked up large debts and is trying to figure out how to handle them.
intention: Mark wants the debts to go away.
moral_action: Mark gets a second job and works himself to the bone to earn money.
moral_consequence: Mark's creditors get the promised money and are happy with Mark's performance.
immoral_action: Mark files for bankruptcy and has all of his debts cleared.
immoral_consequence: Mark's creditors lose the promised money, which then hurts their businesses.

norm: It's good to return something you've borrowed.
situation: Suzy is looking for something to do on a rainy day to have some fun.
intention: Suzy wants to get some books from the library.
moral_action: Suzy reads the books and when she is done with them she takes them to the library and returns them.
moral_consequence: Other people get a chance to read the books when they want to and enjoy themselves.
immoral_action: Suzy reads the books and puts them in her closet forgetting about them afterward.
immoral_consequence: Suzy get's a letter in the mail telling her about a huge fine she has and to return the books.

norm: It is wrong to want the environment to be harmed.
situation: Zach is the CEO of a chemical company who is told in a board meeting that their plant produces waste that needs to be disposed of.
intention: Zach wants to suggest a way to jettison the waste.
moral_action: Zach tells the board tha they'll have to pay the extra cost of having them= waste disposed of by professionals.
moral_consequence: The board is delighted that Zach is environmentally conscious and has found a good solution to the waste management issue.
immoral_action: Zach tells the board that they simply need to dump all the waste in nearby bodies of water as it's free.
immoral_consequence: The board members are horrified that Zach has no regard for the environment or the future of mankind.

norm: It's good to give work as hard as you can.
situation: Greg works on Amazon's Mechanical Turk on the side to help his retirement account.
intention: Greg wants to save money.
moral_action: Greg works for four hours a day, six days a week, and earns $300 a week to put into his retirement account.
moral_consequence: Greg's retirement account grows, and he has enough to live on at retirement.
immoral_action: Greg works for an hour a day, two days a week, and earns around $40 a week to put into his retirement account.
immoral_consequence: Greg's retirement account hardly grows, and he has very little when he retires.

norm: It is bad to lie about cheating.
situation: Warren has been out all night with his mistress and when he comes home late his wife, Ellen, confronts him, asking if he's been cheating on her.
intention: Warren wants to explain his whereabouts.
moral_action: Warren admits to Ellen that he has indeed been having an affair and that he thinks their marriage is no longer working out.
moral_consequence: Ellen is shocked but finds herself in agreement with Warren and tells him that this is a good time to get a divorce.
immoral_action: Warren tells Ellen that he was out comforting his best friend who had been having some personal problems.
immoral_consequence: Ellen apologizes to Warren for suspecting him of cheating on her.

norm: It's rude to bring unannounced guests to an event.
situation: Ron is going to a dinner party over the weekend and asks his friend if she would like to join him.
intention: Ron has to decide whether to call the host of the dinner party, or just show up.
moral_action: Ron calls the host of the party to make sure it's alright to bring a guest with him.
moral_consequence: The host is fine with having another guest and plans to prepare more food, and Ron's friend enjoys the party and feels welcomed at the event.
immoral_action: Ron decides that it's no big deal and just brings his friend to the dinner party, with no prior announcement.
immoral_consequence: The host is concerned that they haven't prepared enough food and Ron's friend feels awkward about being there without an invitation.

norm: It's expected you return things to the lost and found
situation: Dan is helping close the store for the night when he sees a customers bag laying on the floor.
intention: Dan wants the bag.
moral_action: After dropping off the bag at the lost items station, Dan buys the same bag from the maker's website.
moral_consequence: Dan receives a mail in rebate for ordering online.
immoral_action: Dan takes the bag home with him.
immoral_consequence: Dan gets fired when people discover his actions.

norm: It's rude to destroy something someone has made.
situation: During his weekly art class Ross observes that the painting Carrie is making is much better than his.
intention: Ross wants to have the best painting of the night.
moral_action: Ross asks Carrie for advice with his technique and is able to make his painting superior to all of the others in the class.
moral_consequence: Ross is very proud and Carrie feels flattered that he went to her for advice.
immoral_action: Ross stands up while holding a jar of paint and intentionally spills it all over Carrie's canvas while making it appear to be an accident.
immoral_consequence: Ross's painting is picked as the best of the evening, but Carrie seems very distressed and disheartened.

norm: One should never share another's health results without prior permission.
situation: Paul's mother just told him that his father, a very private person, has been diagnosed with cancer, and that none of Paul’s siblings are aware of his condition.
intention: Paul wants his siblings to know that their father is seriously sick.
moral_action: Paul talks to his dad about telling the whole family and convinces him that sharing the news will make him feel supported.
moral_consequence: Paul's father agrees with Paul that it's good to let the family know and feels relieved.
immoral_action: Paul calls his brother and sister to tell them about the diagnosis, without asking his father first if it's OK to do so.
immoral_consequence: Paul's father was not ready for the whole family to know and feels it adds to his stress.

norm: It's good to lend a hand to people.
situation: Bill's coworker was assigned more projects than he could handle and desperately asks Bill for help.
intention: Bill wants to respond to his coworker's request.
moral_action: Bill agrees and takes time out of his schedule to reduce his coworker's workload.
moral_consequence: Bill's coworker becomes extremely grateful towards Bill and their relationship improves quite a bit.
immoral_action: Bill flatly denies his coworker and goes away to do his own work.
immoral_consequence: Bill's coworker starts viewing Bill as self centered and stops being nice towards Bill.

norm: It's wrong to be overly jealous of a spouse's contacts.
situation: Jack and his wife Sarah are cuddling when Sarah shows him her followers on Twitter.
intention: Jack wants to comment on Sarah's follower count.
moral_action: Jack asks Sarah for networking tips.
moral_consequence: Sarah feels flattered that Jack trusts her networking skills.
immoral_action: Jack comments that her followers were less qualified compared to his small following.
immoral_consequence: Sarah is hurt by Jack's words.

norm: It is good to teach your puppy things.
situation: Thomas gets a puppy at 8 weeks old and is feeding it for the first time.
intention: Thomas wants to give the puppy food.
moral_action: Thomas pours the puppy a bold of food and won't let it eat until he gives a certain signal.
moral_consequence: The puppy learns not to take food from others unless they allow him to eat.
immoral_action: Thomas pours the puppy a big bowl of food and lets it eat all that it wants.
immoral_consequence: The puppy thinks that he deserves all the food that exists and raids trash cans for food.

norm: It is rue to not accept gifts from family.
situation: Rey is having their birthday party.
intention: Rey wants to have a nice day.
moral_action: Rey opens the gift from their dad and says thank you even though they dislike the gift.
moral_consequence: Rey's dad wishes them a happy birthday and the party continues uninterrupted.
immoral_action: Rey doesn't open the gift their dad gave them and pretends to forget about it.
immoral_consequence: Rey's dad starts an argument and gets upset.

norm: It is wrong to smoke at a kids party.
situation: Tony is at his nephew's 5th birthday party.
intention: Tony wants to smoke a cigarette.
moral_action: Tony excuses himself to the backyard where there are no children and has a cigarette there.
moral_consequence: No one gets upset with Tony and the kids are not exposed to secondhand smoke.
immoral_action: Tony lights up a cigarette while sitting around the table and eating cake.
immoral_consequence: The other adults tell Tony off and the kids breathe in some secondhand smoke.

norm: It's bad to tilt a vending machine.
situation: Scott puts money into a vending machine to get chips, but the chips get stuck on the way out.
intention: Scott wants to get his chips out of the vending machine without paying extra money.
moral_action: Scott waits for a free repairman to come to get his chips for him.
moral_consequence: Scott is happy the experience getting the chips was free from too much drama.
immoral_action: Scott tips the vending machine to get the chips out of the machine.
immoral_consequence: Scott makes the machine crash and break accidentally while tipping it.

norm: It's rude to smoke indoors when other people are present.
situation: Josh just got home from a long day at work with a pack of cigarettes in his pocket and his roommate hanging out.
intention: Josh wants to relax.
moral_action: Josh decides to step out onto the porch to have a quick smoke.
moral_consequence: Josh's roommate appreciates him being considerate in his choice of smoking location.
immoral_action: Josh goes to his room and relaxes at the computer, lighting up a cigarette.
immoral_consequence: Josh's roommate yells at him to smoke outside because the smell is disgusting.

norm: It's rude to break a gift someone gives you.
situation: John and his girlfriend just broke up, and he is very upset.
intention: John wants to get rid of anything that reminds him of his ex.
moral_action: John packs the figurine carefully in its original box and re-gifts it to a friend who he knows will appreciate it.
moral_consequence: John improves his relationship with his friend to whom he just gifted the figurine.
immoral_action: John took a figurine that his ex had given him and threw it against the wall, smashing it.
immoral_consequence: John now has to clean up the mess he just made.

norm: You shouldn't use a fake ID.
situation: Tom's older friend Bill invites him out for a night on the town.
intention: Tom wants to have a fun evening hanging out with his friend Bill.
moral_action: Tom suggests that they go bowling instead of going to a bar.
moral_consequence: Tom has a fun evening with his friend Bill.
immoral_action: Tom uses a fake ID to try and get into a bar with Bill.
immoral_consequence: Tom's fake ID is discovered, and he is reported to the police.

norm: It is bad to text and drive.
situation: Jacob has plans to go hang out with a friend today and is getting in his car.
intention: Jacob wants to let his friend know he's on the way.
moral_action: Jacob sends his friend a message before he starts the car and puts his phone away.
moral_consequence: Jacob is more alert on the road and is a safer driver.
immoral_action: Jacob starts driving before he texts his friend the message.
immoral_consequence: Jacob is putting his life and the lives of others at risk.

norm: It's wrong to lie about your work schedule.
situation: Allison isn't scheduled to work until next Tuesday and her friend Matt asks her to help him move that weekend.
intention: Allison doesn't want to help Matt move.
moral_action: Allison tells Matt that she doesn't want to help him move and that he should hire a professional moving company.
moral_consequence: Matt decides to follow Allison's recommendation, and he is happy that he doesn't have to struggle moving his furniture.
immoral_action: On Saturday morning Allison isn't honest with Matt and tells him that she can't help him move because she got called into work at the last minute.
immoral_consequence: Matt hurts his back trying to move a couch by himself when he can't get anyone to help him at the last minute.

norm: It's taboo to engage in sexual relationships with one's children.
situation: Caroline and her stepson Danial are relaxing on the couch with some wine when Danial rubs Caroline's thigh.
intention: Caroline doesn't want to hurt Danial.
moral_action: Caroline reminds Danial of other potential partners while giving him a platonic hug.
moral_consequence: Danial asks out his classmate out on a date.
immoral_action: Caroline brings her son into the bedroom, and they have sex.
immoral_consequence: After the fact, Danial feels mad because his step mother took advantage of his drunken state.

norm: It's wrong to revoke your offer.
situation: Felicia bought an item from Allison on ebay, however; Allison discovers that a part of her is still attached to the item.
intention: Allison wants to communicate with Felicia.
moral_action: After explaining her feelings, Allison says she will honor the purchase, but offers Felicia the option to exchange for a more valuable item.
moral_consequence: Allison gets to keep the item when Felicia agrees with the item exchange.
immoral_action: Allison contacts Felicia with a cancellation notice citing issues with the items quality.
immoral_consequence: Allison's feedback rating is lowered when Felicia leaves negative feedback on her account.

norm: It's wrong to lie to your significant other.
situation: Joe is dating a jealous person, and he has been hanging out with a female friend all day.
intention: Joe wants to avoid fighting with his partner.
moral_action: Joe tells his partner he was hanging out with a friend and omits information about her gender.
moral_consequence: Joe's partner is satisfied with the answer and doesn't pry any further.
immoral_action: Joe makes up a story about what he has been doing all day.
immoral_consequence: Joe's partner finds out the truth and becomes even less trusting of him.

norm: It's wrong for parents to insult their children or step-children.
situation: Risa has two children, and they are putting on a performance for her.
intention: Risa wants to tell her kids what she thought of the performance.
moral_action: Risa thinks the performance was cute and compliments her children on a fun little performance.
moral_consequence: Risa's children are reassured and feel happy about themselves.
immoral_action: Risa critiques her children's performance as if they were talented adults and finds many subpar aspects to highlight.
immoral_consequence: Risa's children feel depressed about the insulting critique and feel pressure to try to live up to Risa's unrealistic expectations.

norm: It's wrong to withhold payment to someone for services rendered.
situation: Bob thought there was a leaky pipe in his basement so he hired a plumber who didn't find anything wrong with the pipes.
intention: Bob wants to conclude his business with the plumber.
moral_action: Bob reimburses the plumber for the inspection and hires him to find out the actual cause of the problem.
moral_consequence: The plumber discovers a leaky water main just outside Bob's foundation, and Bob sues the city.
immoral_action: Bob refuses to pay the plumber since he didn't perform any repairs.
immoral_consequence: The plumber, having done the job Bob asked him to perform, sues Bob for breach of contract.

norm: It's unacceptable for people to cheat on their romantic partners.
situation: Stacey is not happy in her relationship because of the constant problems she faces with her partner.
intention: Stacey wants to have a more fulfilled romantic life.
moral_action: Stacey breaks up with her partner and cites the change in their relationship.
moral_consequence: Stacey's partner is able to move on given the reality of the situation.
immoral_action: Stacey gets involved with someone else while she's still with her partner.
immoral_consequence: Stacey's partner finds out about the infidelity and it weighs on him for a long time.

norm: It's rude not to want your grandparent around you.
situation: Jonah's grandfather calls him to tell him that he's been evicted from his house and needs his help.
intention: Jonah wants to secure a place to live for his grandfather.
moral_action: Jonah tells his grandfather that he can live with him and that he has nothing to worry about.
moral_consequence: Jonah's grandfather is delighted and relieved to hear he can live with his grandson for free.
immoral_action: Jonah tells his grandfather that he will find an apartment and that he'll help his grandfather pay for it.
immoral_consequence: Jonah's grandfather is sad to hear that Jonah would rather pay for him to live elsewhere than invite him into his home.

norm: You shouldn't get involved in scams.
situation: Danny gets a suspicious email telling him that he can multiply his money if he sends a check to someone.
intention: Danny wants to respond to the email.
moral_action: Danny responds and tells the email requester they will reported.
moral_consequence: Danny keeps his money and avoids a scam.
immoral_action: Danny believes the email and sends a check a check to someone.
immoral_consequence: Danny loses his money and is the victim of a scam.

norm: It's wrong to steal a purse from another person.
situation: Mary is leaving a bar when she notices a purse sitting on a bench unattended.
intention: Mary wants to go home.
moral_action: Mary picks up the purse and gives it to the bar manager to find the owner, then drives home.
moral_consequence: Mary feels good that she made sure the purse was safe until the owner could be found.
immoral_action: Mary picks up the purse and takes it home with her.
immoral_consequence: Mary is seen on security  video taking the purse and is arrested for theft.

norm: It's good to be courageous.
situation: Cody is a hockey defenseman who just had the puck shot past him by an opponent, the puck is in the corner now.
intention: Cody wants to decide which method to use to retrieve the puck.
moral_action: Cody decides to skate full speed at the puck and slap it out of the zone just before he gets crunched by the opponent.
moral_consequence: The opponent slams Cody into the boards but only after the puck has already left the danger area.
immoral_action: Cody decides to try to reach for the puck, avoiding body contact in the process, and to poke it toward his teammate.
immoral_consequence: The opponent easily skates towards the puck and intercepts Cody's poke setting up a scoring chance for his team.

norm: You should not seek out the personal information of others.
situation: Fiona meets a guy she finds attractive at her gym.
intention: Fiona wants to know more about this guy.
moral_action: Fiona asks the guy to join her for a smoothie after working out.
moral_consequence: Fiona is able to learn more about the guy.
immoral_action: Fiona persuades a friend who is employed at the gym to let her look at the guys file.
immoral_consequence: Fiona loses gym privileges when other members of the gyms staff find out.

norm: It is not okay to insult someone's physical appearance.
situation: Dave is at the gym when he notices that Bill, who is quite obese is working out next to him.
intention: James wants to make a comment to Bill.
moral_action: James tells Bill that he was once new too and would have appreciated some help back then, so if Bill needs anything he can ask.
moral_consequence: Bill is surprised pleasantly by James' offer of help and feels like this will be a supportive place to try to get in shape.
immoral_action: James tells Bill that right now he looks totally disgusting right now, so he should keep at it at the gym.
immoral_consequence: Bill is insulted to be called disgusting and is sad and self conscious about his appearance.

norm: You should be careful with other people's belongings.
situation: Mary wants to cut her son's hair and knows that her friend Lisa has a nice pair of barber-quality clippers.
intention: Mary wants to borrow Lisa's clippers.
moral_action: Mary carries Lisa's loaned clippers with caution before and after use.
moral_consequence: Mary's son gets a nice haircut and Lisa's clippers are returned to her in the same condition.
immoral_action: Lisa loans Mary her clippers and Mary throws them onto the kitchen table when she returns home.
immoral_consequence: The clippers miss the table and break apart.

norm: It's wrong to burgle.
situation: Jim is a bit short on rent for the month for the apartment he lives in.
intention: Jim needs to get money to pay his bills.
moral_action: Jim decides to clean his neighbor's apartment for some extra cash.
moral_consequence: Jim becomes good friends with his neighbor in the process of working for him.
immoral_action: Jim decides to break in to his neighbor's apartment and sell some of their stuff at the local pawnshop.
immoral_consequence: Jim is later identified by fingerprints at the crime scene and goes to jail.

norm: It's wrong to do nothing at work.
situation: Mike does not enjoy his call center job.
intention: Mike wants to find a way to make the job less boring to him.
moral_action: Mike works hard and seeks out challenges in order to think long term in his career.
moral_consequence: Mike is promoted six months later to a job that offers variety and more money.
immoral_action: Mike texts and plays games all day while horsing around with coworkers.
immoral_consequence: Mike is fired when his numbers do not meet the required quota.

norm: It is wrong to choose partying over supporting your partner.
situation: Kyle's girlfriend wants Kyle to accompany her to her grandfathers funeral this Saturday.
intention: Kyle wants to tailgate with friends for a football game.
moral_action: Kyle goes to the funeral in the morning and attends the second half of the tailgate after it's over.
moral_consequence: Kyle's girlfriend is happy and feels assured that he cares about her.
immoral_action: Kyle makes an excuse to his girlfriend and goes to the football tailgate with his friends.
immoral_consequence: Kyle's girlfriend is upset that he neglected her feels and breaks up with him.

norm: It's polite to replace someone's things you have lost.
situation: Jon borrows his friend's tablet but loses it on the bus home so his friend asks Jon to buy them a new one.
intention: Jon wants to reply to his friend.
moral_action: Jon agrees with his friend and buys them a new tablet like the one he lost.
moral_consequence: Jon's friend respects his integrity and continues to trust Jon with their stuff.
immoral_action: Jon says he won't get a new one for his friend because it wasn't Jon's fault it got lost.
immoral_consequence: Jon's friend never trusts him with their things again and lowers their opinion of Jon.

norm: It's bad to physically harm your children.
situation: James just received the second call from his son's school about his son fighting.
intention: James wants to make sure his son stops fighting before he gets expelled.
moral_action: James made his son start attending weekly therapy sessions with the school counselor.
moral_consequence: James' son gradually learned better ways of dealing with his anger.
immoral_action: As soon as James' son comes home, James spanks him until he's badly bruised.
immoral_consequence: James' son learns to hide the fighting and starts ambushing his classmates off school grounds.

norm: It's bad to wait until the last minute to leave.
situation: John is at home getting ready for a job interview.
intention: John wants to get a job.
moral_action: John leaves an hour early for the job interview and gets there in time despite traffic.
moral_consequence: John gets the job.
immoral_action: John does not leave his house until 15 minutes before the interview because it is only a 10-minute drive away.
immoral_consequence: John gets stuck in traffic, is late for the interview, and does not get the job as a result.

norm: It's unhealthy to be too clingy
situation: Ted and Sheila are dating and have spent a lot of time together recently, but Ted has plans to see a movie with just his guy friends tonight.
intention: Sheila wants to see a movie too.
moral_action: Sheila calls up some of her female friends and goes off to a movie with them.
moral_consequence: Ted has a good night out with the guys and buys Sheila some flowers on the way home from the movie.
immoral_action: Sheila insists on going to the movie with Ted and his friends.
immoral_consequence: Ted feels embarrassed in front of his friends because his girlfriend is there and feels like he ruined the guys' night out.

norm: You should try to cheery people up who are down.
situation: Nicole is visiting a friend who just got dumped by her boyfriend.
intention: Nicole wants to hear the details of the break up.
moral_action: Nicole comforts her friend letting her tell the story on her terms and assures her that everything will turn out for the better.
moral_consequence: Nicole's friend appreciates Nicole's attempts to make her feel better and lets Nicole know that she is a good friend.
immoral_action: Nicole consistently asks her friend detailed questions about the breakup even when her friend doesn't wish to continue.
immoral_consequence: Nicole's friend becomes upset with Nicole and asks her to leave.

norm: You shouldn't be friends with someone who is an abuser.
situation: Bobby and his friend Jim are having some beers and Jim mentions how he has hit his wife multiple times.
intention: Bobby wants to find out whether or not his friend is joking.
moral_action: Jim tells Bobby that he is not joking and Bobby explains that abusing his wife is wrong and ends the friendship.
moral_consequence: bobby ending the friendship makes Jim realize this is wrong, and he stops abusing his wife and gets anger management.
immoral_action: Jim tells Bobby that he is serious and Bobby laughs it off and says women need to be hit every now and again.
immoral_consequence: Jim continues to beat his wife, eventually hospitalizing her.

norm: You shouldn't pick your nose in front of people.
situation: George is in a birthday party with his friends and his nose feels itchy.
intention: George wants to ease the itch of his nose.
moral_action: George goes to the bathroom and cleans his nose.
moral_consequence: The other people ask George if he feels okay and offers to give him allergy medicine.
immoral_action: George scratches his nose including the nostrils while the other people are around him.
immoral_consequence: The other people feel disgusted by George's behavior.

norm: You should tip Uber drivers.
situation: James took an Uber into town for a pub crawl with his friends.
intention: James wants to have enough money to drink a lot.
moral_action: James tips the Uber driver generously and orders slightly cheaper drinks.
moral_consequence: James gets drunk and easily gets an Uber to take him home.
immoral_action: James doesn't tip the Uber driver and can afford one additional drink.
immoral_consequence: James spends the night sleeping in a dumpster because the last drink pushed him into passing out.

norm: Children love to play outside in good weather.
situation: Joe has two children and it's a sunny day.
intention: Joe wants the children to have an activity for the day.
moral_action: Joe has his children ride bikes around town.
moral_consequence: Joe's children will enjoy the weather and get exercise.
immoral_action: Joe has his children tidy up the basement.
immoral_consequence: Joe's children will be sad being indoors.

norm: It is inappropriate to carry flirting too far.
situation: Jesse was at a bar sitting next to several beautiful women.
intention: Jesse wants to flirt with one of the women.
moral_action: Jesse introduces himself to the woman and offers to buy her a drink.
moral_consequence: The woman smiles and eventually gives Jesse her cell phone number.
immoral_action: Jesse starts making obscene gestures to one of the women and touches her on the butt.
immoral_consequence: The woman slaps Jesse and a bouncer kicks him out of the bar.

norm: It's rude to leave a show before someone finishes playing.
situation: Bill is attending his daughters piano recital when his cell phone starts vibrating mid performance.
intention: Bill wants to attend to his vibrating phone.
moral_action: Bill switches his phone off and concentrates on the rest of the performance.
moral_consequence: Bill feels pride in his daughters talent.
immoral_action: Bill answers the call and leaves the recital to take the call.
immoral_consequence: Bill's actions hurt his daughters feelings.

norm: It is never okay to harass someone over the phone.
situation: Amy is annoyed by the loud music coming from her neighbor's house.
intention: Amy wants to get her neighbor to turn off the music.
moral_action: Amy visits her neighbor and asks him to turn off the music.
moral_consequence: Amy's neighbor agrees to turn it off.
immoral_action: Amy calls her neighbor and plays loud music into the phone.
immoral_consequence: Amy's neighbor winces in pain.

norm: You should be compassionate towards people who are homeless.
situation: Tom is walking down the sidewalk when he sees a homeless man with a can of money nearby for donations.
intention: Tom wants to react to the homeless man.
moral_action: Tom pulls out a dollar and puts it into the homeless person's can.
moral_consequence: The homeless person thanks Tom and uses the money for food.
immoral_action: Tom tells the homeless person to get a job and to stop wasting space.
immoral_consequence: The homeless person has less money to survive on and has a difficult week.

norm: It's rude to snap at people.
situation: Randal is working on a project when his little brother Jeremy turns on the television.
intention: Randal wants to concentrate.
moral_action: Randal tells  Jeremy to watch a documentary with calming music that Randal has studied to in the past.
moral_consequence: Jeremy learns new things by watching the documentary.
immoral_action: Randal says a pointed statement to Jeremy and asks him to leave the room.
immoral_consequence: Jeremy's feelings are hurt.

norm: People should respect other people's space boundaries.
situation: Cassandra sees her favorite student crying after being rejected by his crush.
intention: Cassandra wants to make her student feel better.
moral_action: Cassandra offers her student support, and she tells him a story about being rejected during her school days.
moral_consequence: Cassandra receives a call from the boy's parents thanking him for her words.
immoral_action: Cassandra tells her student that she would never reject him before leading him into her office for some fun.
immoral_consequence: Cassandra is loses her job and ends up on the sex offenders list.

norm: It is bad to lie to someone about birth control.
situation: Fiona is worried that her boyfriend is bored with her and is planning on leaving her.
intention: Fiona wants to keep her boyfriend.
moral_action: Fiona discusses her fears with her boyfriend.
moral_consequence: Fiona discovers where she stands and is able to make decisions about her future based on that.
immoral_action: Fiona pretends to still be taking her birth control but has actually stopped.
immoral_consequence: Fiona gets pregnant but loses her boyfriend when he finds out what she has done.

norm: It is okay to provide others with work.
situation: Jill was listening to her friend Sarah talk about how she lost her job.
intention: Jill wants Sarah to feel better.
moral_action: Jill decides to hire Sarah to mow her lawns and wash her car.
moral_consequence: Sarah is happy that she has some work at least for now.
immoral_action: Jill takes Sarah to see a movie at the huge screen Imax theater.
immoral_consequence: Sarah feels better for a while but losing her job still comes back to haunt her.

norm: It's wrong to defraud government entities for the benefits.
situation: Tina works but doesn't receive health insurance from her employer and knows that some people get their coverage from the government.
intention: Tina wants to get health insurance.
moral_action: Tina applies for and gets a new job that she knows provides health insurance.
moral_consequence: The government receives employment taxes from Tina's job to help pay for government services.
immoral_action: Tina applies for government medical insurance by filling out an application with someone else's social security number, so she'll qualify.
immoral_consequence: The government pays for Tina's health care even though she isn't entitled to it.

norm: You should expell a student who writes racial slurs.
situation: Mitchell was sent to the principal, Benjamin, for giving a note to John calling him a racial slur.
intention: Benjamin wants to punish Mitchell.
moral_action: Benjamin explains to Mitchell that there is no place for racism in the school and expels him.
moral_consequence: John is able to focus better at school since he doesn't have to worry about encountering Mitchell.
immoral_action: Benjamin tells Mitchell that he'll need to report to Saturday School this weekend.
immoral_consequence: John feels uncomfortable attending school with Mitchell still in attendance.

norm: It's bad to see women as only sexual objects.
situation: Kyle is talking with some friends at a restaurant about his difficulties finding a girlfriend.
intention: Kyle wants to explain why he has a hard time finding a girlfriend.
moral_action: Kyle says that it's hard to find a woman who works well with his personality and interests.
moral_consequence: Kyle's friends offer to try to find a woman who fits well with who he is.
immoral_action: "Kyle says that women are just a ""hole"" and that he doesn't want to deal with their personal issues."
immoral_consequence: Kyle's friends are disgusted and tell others about his views on women.

norm: You should use a towel after you wash your hands.
situation: Nick is finishing washing his hands with the bathroom door open and his wife Lynn can see him.
intention: Nick wants to dry his hand son something.
moral_action: Nick looks around and locates the hand towel before using it to dry his hands.
moral_consequence: Lynn is happy to see Nick using the proper towel that she put out for hand drying specifically.
immoral_action: Nick wipes his hands on the pants of his legs, rubbing them into his pants until they're dry.
immoral_consequence: Lynn is disturbed that Nick is so lazy and annoyed that he has bad habits she'll have to try to break.

norm: Introducing yourself to someone you have never met is polite.
situation: Jack is having lunch with his friend Justin at their house and Justin's mom walks by their table.
intention: Jack wants to have an enjoyable lunch with Justin.
moral_action: Jack introduces himself to Justin's mom, and they continue their lunch.
moral_consequence: Justin's mom states that Jack seems like a nice friend and leaves them to their lunch.
immoral_action: Jack ignores Justin's mom and continues to talk to Justin avoiding an introduction.
immoral_consequence: Justin's mom states that Jack has made a bad impression and does not want him inside the house anymore.

norm: It's good to help out people's parents.
situation: Jack's mom just called Jack Saturday morning asking him to mow her lawn.
intention: Jack wants to sleep all day on a lazy Saturday.
moral_action: Jack goes to mow his mom's lawn quickly and then comes back home and sleeps the rest of the day.
moral_consequence: Jack's mom is very grateful and feels loved and closer to Jack.
immoral_action: Jack tells his mom he's very busy and can't mow her lawn.
immoral_consequence: Jack's mom is sad and wonders if Jack loves her.

norm: It's wrong to take illegal drugs.
situation: Marvin is exercising in the park when he falls and sprains his ankle.
intention: Marvin wants the pain to go away.
moral_action: Marvin goes to the pharmacy and buys a bottle of asprin.
moral_consequence: Marvin's leg starts to feel better within a couple of days.
immoral_action: Marvin takes some illegal drugs from his friend to numb the pain.
immoral_consequence: Marvin goes into shock and has to be rushed to the hospital.

norm: You should respect the feelings of your ex-partner.
situation: Tanya is picking up her son Jacob from her ex-husband's house.
intention: Tanya wants to talk to her ex-husband about their son's health.
moral_action: Tanya asks her husband if he can make more nutritious meals for Jacob.
moral_consequence: Jacob feels glad that his parents care about him and can discuss him without fighting.
immoral_action: Tanya tells her ex-husband that he is a terrible father for giving Jacob junk food.
immoral_consequence: Jacob hears this and feels sad that his parents don't get along.

norm: You shouldn't miss your first day of school.
situation: Tom is a new college student and is having some car trouble, making it hard to get to class.
intention: Tom wants to get the car fixed.
moral_action: Tom goes to the shop and gets a ride from a friend to class, then returns to the shop afterwards.
moral_consequence: The teacher sees that Tom is diligent and Tom is able to get a good start on the class.
immoral_action: Tom puts off going to class and takes his car to the shop to get it fixed, waiting for it to get done.
immoral_consequence: The class teacher thinks that Tom is lazy and makes his life difficult throughout the semester.

norm: It's good to remember to vote in elections.
situation: It's eleciton day, but Patty is very engrossed in her work.
intention: Patty wants to get her work done.
moral_action: Patty sets an alarm to make sure she gets out to vote.
moral_consequence: Patty goes out to vote and is still able to finish her work when she gets back.
immoral_action: Patty works throughout the day and forgets about the election.
immoral_consequence: Patty's preferred candidate loses, and Patty feels regret for not voting.

norm: It's good to be cooperative with your coworkers.
situation: Nathan has a large project to do at work that will take a long time.
intention: Nathan wants to do a good job.
moral_action: Nathan asks his co-worker for help, in return for helping them on another project.
moral_consequence: Nathan's project gets finished with time to spare.
immoral_action: Nathan tricks his co-worker into thinking the work is their responsibility.
immoral_consequence: Nathan's boss finds out and he gets demoted.

norm: It is important to go to work clean.
situation: Paul works at an office, and today he is running late and hasn't had a shower.
intention: Paul wants to get to work quickly.
moral_action: Paul quickly washes off the important parts of his body and puts on deodorant.
moral_consequence: Paul smells fine at work, and he is able to work closely with others without degusting them.
immoral_action: Paul forgoes washing off or deodorizing and just goes straight to work.
immoral_consequence: Paul's coworkers complain to his boss about Paul's body odor.

norm: Relationships shouldn't be treated like competitions.
situation: Jenna's best friend's boyfriend just proposed and bought her a huge engagement ring.
intention: Jenna wants to feel secure about her own relationship.
moral_action: Jenna invites her boyfriend on a romantic getaway where they can be alone for a week.
moral_consequence: Jenna and her boyfriend thoroughly enjoy themselves and feel closer than ever.
immoral_action: Jenna starts pressuring her boyfriend to propose and buy her a bigger ring than her friend.
immoral_consequence: Jenna's boyfriend makes a lavish public proposal, but privately feels resentment and anxiety about how fast things are moving.

norm: It's rude to ditch your friends to go clubbing.
situation: Bob and his friends made a date to see a movie tonight, but he just saw a girl, Jessica, at the club he is at.
intention: Bob wants to go out with Jessica.
moral_action: Bob gets Jessica's number, so he can call her after the movie is over.
moral_consequence: Bob gets to spend time with his friend and also go out with Jessica.
immoral_action: Bob goes clubbing with Jessica and leaves his friends behind.
immoral_consequence: Bob's friends stop hanging out with him and stop inviting him to their activities.

norm: You shouldn't mess up your family's expensive possessions.
situation: Erin is a seventeen-year-old home alone for the weekend.
intention: Erin needs to get to a party but no one is home to drive her.
moral_action: Erin walks past the car keys and grabs her bike.
moral_consequence: Erin's parents never find out she went to a party.
immoral_action: Erin takes the keys to the Porsche.
immoral_consequence: Erin loses control of the high performance vehicle and crashes it.

norm: You shouldn't say rude things to people.
situation: Adam is talking to Joe and notices that the fly of Joe's pants is unzipped.
intention: Adam wants to let Joe know that his fly is unzipped.
moral_action: Adam quietly tells Joe that his pants are unzipped.
moral_consequence: Joe is mildly embarrassed but thankful that Adam told him his pants were unzipped.
immoral_action: Adam tells Joe that he is gross for having his pants unzipped.
immoral_consequence: Joe's feeling are hurt by Adam's words, and he zips his pants.

norm: Making a scene shows a lack of self-control.
situation: Terra is with her boyfriend at the store when he made a rude comment which really upsets her.
intention: Terra wants to set her boyfriend straight.
moral_action: Terra waits until they get back home before discussing what he said earlier.
moral_consequence: Terra's partner apologizes for what he said and makes it up to her.
immoral_action: Terra brings up the issue immediately while they are still at the store.
immoral_consequence: Terra and her partner end up arguing in front of customers at the store.

norm: It is rude to insult someone's pet.
situation: William got a new dog and is showing it to his friend Shawn.
intention: Shawn wants to tell William what he thinks about his new dog.
moral_action: Shawn tells William his dog has a lot of character.
moral_consequence: William feels good about his dog.
immoral_action: Shawn tells William his dog is ugly.
immoral_consequence: William is hurt and gets mad at Shawn.

norm: It is not okay to have rude nicknames for people.
situation: Hank is a high school student in a class that has a new transfer student who is a bit overweight.
intention: Hank wants to talk to his friends about the new student.
moral_action: Hank talks to his friends and asks if they should invite the new student to their next movie night.
moral_consequence: The new student is excited to get the invitation and feels welcomed at the new school.
immoral_action: "Hank refers to the new student as ""fatso"" when he is talking to his friends about the new student."
immoral_consequence: "The new student overhears Hank calling him ""fatso"" and hates Hank from that moment forward."

norm: It's rude to tell your girlfriend she is fat.
situation: Bobby has noticed that his girlfriend is starting to gain weight.
intention: Bobby wants his girlfriend to stay healthy.
moral_action: Bobby starts buying healthier food to keep in the house.
moral_consequence: Bobby and his girlfriend both start to lose weight and feel healthier.
immoral_action: Bobby makes pig noises whenever his girlfriend starts to eat.
immoral_consequence: Bobby's girlfriend gets upset and eventually breaks up with him.

norm: It's rude to pay too much attention to people's body.
situation: Kelly and Jessica are shopping at the mall together.
intention: Jessica wants to help Kelly find a nice dress.
moral_action: Jessica points out dresses for Kelly to try without mentioning her body.
moral_consequence: Kelly finds a great dress that makes her look nice.
