situation: Sarah has a group of friends coming to her house for dinner and movies.
intention: Sarah wants to prepare for the visit.
moral_action: Sarah throws all the trash away, dusts and vacuums and wipes down the counters.
moral_consequence: Sarah's friends compliment her on the clean house, and they relax into a nice evening.
immoral_action: Sarah kicks some empty food boxes and soda cans under the table and calls it a day.
immoral_consequence: Sarah's friends see how dirty and unkempt the house is, and feel uncomfortable and gross while there.

norm: It's rude to judge someone's talent when they sing karaoke.
situation: Zoe has been successfully pressured by her friends, including Alazzo, to sing karaoke during their weekly night-out, despite being a famously bad singer.
intention: Allazzo wants to comment on Zoe's karaoke trial.
moral_action: Allazzo tells her that she really wasn't bad and that she's bold to go up there.
moral_consequence: Zoe and Allazzo laugh it off and get along.
immoral_action: Allazzo can't stop laughing while he tells Zoe that she was hilarious.
immoral_consequence: Zoe is offended and avoids Allazzo from then on.

norm: You should go to your friend's baby shower.
situation: Martha's best friend, Stella, recently announced she is expecting a baby.
intention: Martha wants to give Stella a gift.
moral_action: Martha wraps the gift and presents it to Stella's at her baby shower.
moral_consequence: Stella has a good time at the shower since her best friend is there to provide support.
immoral_action: Martha doesn't like parties, so she skips Stella's baby shower deciding to drop off the gift on her way home from work.
immoral_consequence: Stella misses having her friend at the shower and wonders if she's done something to cause the absence.

norm: It is good to spend time outside
situation: Jordan is at is house, has been slacking off lately, and is very out of shape.
intention: Jordan wants to get exercise every day this week.
moral_action: Jordan plays basketball outside everyday as part of his workout routine.
moral_consequence: Jordan finds he is more functional by going outside a lot.
immoral_action: Jordan runs on the treadmill everyday this week instead of going outside.
immoral_consequence: Jordan feels like he is divorced from nature and becomes depressed.

norm: You should not post other people's private information online.
situation: Lori is with her best friend Jenny when Jenny receives an acceptance letter to Harvard.
intention: Lori wants to congratulate Jenny on social media.
moral_action: Lori writes a congratulatory post on social media to Jenny, without including any personal photos or information.
moral_consequence: Lori and Jenny's social media friends send Jenny well wishes.
immoral_action: Lori posts a picture of Jenny's acceptance letter, address and all, to social media.
immoral_consequence: With Jenny's address plastered all over social media, she receives an influx of prank mail.

norm: It is bad to spy on others.
situation: Jack thinks that his girlfriend Kate is having an affair with his best friend Mike.
intention: Jack wants to check what Kate is doing.
moral_action: Jack goes to Kate's room and sees that Kate is studying for her exam.
moral_consequence: Jack feels good about Kate and goes back to his place to study.
immoral_action: Jack climbs up to the window of Kate's room and peeks inside.
immoral_consequence: Jack notices that Kate is studying, but he slips and falls down hard on the ground.

norm: It's frowned upon to take more than you need.
situation: Bob is at a buffet restaurant and heads over to the buffet area.
intention: Bob wants to get bring food back to his table.
moral_action: Bob takes only as much food as he will eat to his table.
moral_consequence: The employees are glad that they don't have to throw away a bunch of food since Bob didn't waste any.
immoral_action: Bob piles up a huge amount of food and takes it all back to his table but only eats a small portion of what he took.
immoral_consequence: The workers at the buffet have to clean up after Bob, throwing away all the food he wasted.

norm: It is wrong to tamper with people's possessions
situation: Omar was playing video games when his game controller broke.
intention: Omar wants to get a new game controller.
moral_action: Omar asks his roommate if he can borrow the money to get a new controller.
moral_consequence: Omar's roommate gives him the money, and he pays him back in a week.
immoral_action: Omar opens his roommates safe to get the money to buy the controller.
immoral_consequence: Omar's roommate kicks him out and tells everyone that he is a thief.

norm: It's good to eat neatly.
situation: Jake is at Wendy's birthday celebration when the cake is served.
intention: Jake wants to take a bite of cake.
moral_action: Jake uses the provided plastic fork to break off a piece of the cake and bring it to his mouth slowly.
moral_consequence: Everyone eats their cake in peace enjoying the nice birthday moment together.
immoral_action: Jake picks up the piece of cake with his bare hand and literally punches himself in the face with it causing most of it to splatter everywhere.
immoral_consequence: The guests are horrified and disgusted as cake shrapnel and chocolate syrup land all over them, staining their outfits.

norm: It's bad to let friends drive drunk.
situation: Jane is at a party and her drunk friend wants to leave.
intention: Jane wants her friend to get home.
moral_action: Jane drives her friend home in her own car.
moral_consequence: They both arrive safely at home.
immoral_action: Jane lets her friend drive her car home.
immoral_consequence: Her friend is pulled over by the police and is arrested.

norm: Helping the police catch criminals is always a good thing.
situation: Enrique is robbed while walking home at night by a mugger who threatens him not to call the cops.
intention: Enrique wants to decide whether to report the crime to the police.
moral_action: Enrique decides to call the police and report the crime.
moral_consequence: The criminal is captured and many would-be victims are saved.
immoral_action: Enrique decides to keep his mouth shut and declines to call the cops to report the crime.
immoral_consequence: The criminal is not caught and victimizes several more people.

norm: It's rude to disturb others with loud music.
situation: Josh is doing his weekly apartment cleaning.
intention: Josh wants music to play while he works.
moral_action: Josh plays his music at a considerate volume.
moral_consequence: Josh's neighbors are not disturbed by his music.
immoral_action: Josh blasts his music and opens the windows to air out the apartment.
immoral_consequence: Josh's neighbors complain about the loud music.

norm: It is good to have activities.
situation: Sean has a day off and the weather is beautiful.
intention: Sean wants to decide if he should plan something.
moral_action: Sean decides to get some exercise.
moral_consequence: He feels great the rest of the day.
immoral_action: Sean doesn't plan anything and relaxes all day.
immoral_consequence: He feels restless and lazy later on, but it's too late.

norm: It's wrong to break things that don't belong to you.
situation: Jane is at a house party being hosted by a co-worker she doesn't like too much.
intention: Jane wants to enjoy herself.
moral_action: Jane spends the evening mingling with the co-workers she does like and eventually finds a group that wants to leave the party and socialize elsewhere.
moral_consequence: Jane is able to enjoy her evening without ruining anybody else's.
immoral_action: Jane is in a room of the house all by herself and thinks it will feel good to break a vase belonging to the host, so she does.
immoral_consequence: Jane is spotted by another party goer and becomes wrought with guilt and fear.

norm: You shouldn't drink too much around your partner.
situation: Brad is at a bar with his girlfriend and a bunch of their friends.
intention: Brad wants to drink beer.
moral_action: Brad has two beers and is generally well behaved at the bar.
moral_consequence: Brad's girlfriend is happy that Brad doesn't drink excessively and has a good time with him.
immoral_action: Brad drinks nine beers at the bar and completely loses control of himself as a result.
immoral_consequence: Brad's girlfriend is humiliated by his drunken behavior and starts questioning the relationship.

norm: It's unhealthy to want to kill yourself
situation: Jenny is at work when she receives an email from corporate telling her that she's being laid off.
intention: Jenny wants to emotionally react to the terrible news.
moral_action: Jenny turns off her computer and begins to sob loudly and telling everyone how unfair it is.
moral_consequence: Jenny's coworkers take sympathy on her and try to be supportive to her through her tough moment.
immoral_action: Jenny turns off her computer and tells her coworkers she's going to kill herself before leaving the office.
immoral_consequence: Jenny's coworkers are terrified and worried about her intentions and scramble to try to alert someone.

norm: It's nice to help pay for things.
situation: Dustin has been dating Katie for a while, and they are eating at a diner.
intention: Dustin wants to leave after he is finished eating.
moral_action: Dustin takes out his wallet and pays for the bill when the waiter brings it to the table.
moral_consequence: Katie is grateful that Dustin is so generous with his money.
immoral_action: Dustin tells Katie to pay for the bill when the waiter brings the bill to the table.
immoral_consequence: Katie gets tired of paying for their meals all the time and breaks up with him.

norm: It is wrong to force your daughter to marry.
situation: Steve's daughter is 25 and still at home, he is worried she'll never find a suitor.
intention: Steve wants his daughter to marry.
moral_action: Steve tells his daughter how important seeing her married is to him.
moral_consequence: Steve's daughter puts everything into finding a good man to marry, and does.
immoral_action: Steve pressures his daughter into marrying her abusive boyfriend.
immoral_consequence: Steve's daughter lives in a miserable marriage for a few years until getting a divorce.

norm: It is wrong to sell drugs
situation: Moe is trying to make ends meet and doesn't want to lose his home, but he has very little cash.
intention: Moe wants to make some money fast.
moral_action: Moe gets himself a job and tries to rise up the ladder.
moral_consequence: Moe makes money while staying out of jail.
immoral_action: Moe decides to sell drugs with his friend to get some money.
immoral_consequence: Moe is caught by the police, and he gets jail time.

norm: It's good to help out your neighbors.
situation: Mark has just moved to a new neighborhood.
intention: Mark wants to make friends with the neighbors.
moral_action: Mark offers to help some neighbors with their lawn and gets to know them.
moral_consequence: His neighbors like him and help him out later when he needs help.
immoral_action: Mark invites himself over to a neighbors house and makes a mess and doesn't clean up after himself.
immoral_consequence: His neighbors stop talking to him.

norm: It's not okay to be overly prideful of things.
situation: Jane helped her soccer team win big an hour ago, and runs into her mom.
intention: Jane wanted to explain her victory to her Mom.
moral_action: Jane simply tells her Mom that she helped win a soccer game.
moral_consequence: Jane's Mom congratulates Jane, and they both have a nice conversation.
immoral_action: Jane tells her Mom that she is the best soccer player in the world and deserves presents for it.
immoral_consequence: Jane's Mom tells Jane she is spoiled and narcissistic, and Jane feels bad.

norm: It's wrong to use your children against your partner.
situation: Kenneth and his wife Brooke are getting divorced, and he's currently meeting with a lawyer.
intention: Kenneth wants to make the best possible case for himself during the divorce proceedings.
moral_action: Kenneth presents all the evidence he personally has about Brooke's inappropriate behavior declining any third party testimonies.
moral_consequence: The lawyer listens to Kenneth's side of the story and decides that his side of the story should be enough to proceed without involving others.
immoral_action: Kenneth asks his young children to testify about Brooke's inappropriate behavior during their marriage.
immoral_consequence: The lawyer forms a negative opinion of Kenneth and reconsiders how he can approach the case.

norm: It's good to give someone a gift as a reward.
situation: Bill returns from a week long vacation during which time his friend Greg was dog sitting for him.
intention: Bill wants to thank Greg for helping him out.
moral_action: Bill thanks Greg in person and gives him a substantial gift certificate as a reward for dog sitting.
moral_consequence: Greg is happy, appreciative and eager to help dog sit again in the future.
immoral_action: Bill leaves Greg a short voicemail telling him thank you for dog sitting.
immoral_consequence: Greg feels underwhelmed and a bit unappreciated by Bill's response and declines to dog sit for him in the future.

norm: It's good to help other people
situation: Steve notices a charity appeal on the touchscreen payment system at the grocery store while he is at the checkout.
intention: Steve wants to pay for his groceries.
moral_action: Steve donates a few dollars to the charity as he pays for his groceries.
moral_consequence: The charity receives more money and has increased resources to help those in need.
immoral_action: Steve pays for his groceries without making any charity donation.
immoral_consequence: The charity receives less money and has fewer resources to help those in need.

norm: It's mean to call your girlfriend a disgusting person.
situation: Josh notices that his girlfriend Nancy has gained a few pounds since he last saw her.
intention: Josh wants to comment on Nancy's weight gain.
moral_action: Josh tells Nancy that he loves how voluptuous she has gotten.
moral_consequence: Nancy is flattered that Josh loves the way her body looks.
immoral_action: Josh tells Nancy that she has turned into a disgusting pig.
immoral_consequence: Nancy is hurt my Josh's words and breaks up with him.

norm: You should be courteous of disabled people.
situation: Matt is driving down a two-lane highway when he sees a slow car with a handicap license plate.
intention: Matt wants to get around the car.
moral_action: Matt looks for a long straight road, then passes the slow vehicle while doing the speed limit.
moral_consequence: The handicapped driver waves at Matt and is grateful that there are kind drivers on the road.
immoral_action: Matt speeds up and quickly passes the car with the handicap plates while going 10 mph over the speed limit.
immoral_consequence: The handicapped driver is startled by Matt's quick pass and swerves on the road.

norm: You shouldn't burden others with your responsibilities.
situation: Rodger is at work and has a lot of projects piling up.
intention: Rodger wants to make sure the projects get done.
moral_action: Rodger works overtime to make sure he finishes all the projects that have piled up.
moral_consequence: Rodgers coworkers benefit from the projects being completed because it means everybody is pulling their weight.
immoral_action: Rodger calls in some favors with other coworkers and requests that they do the projects for him.
immoral_consequence: While the coworkers do the favors, they also have resentment towards Rodger for heaping the projects on to them like this.

norm: It is rude to meddle in someone else's relationship.
situation: Lynn notices that her friend is making passive aggressive comments about her relationship online.
intention: Lynn wants to point her friend in the right direction.
moral_action: Lynn waits for her friend to ask her for advice and tells her to do what is beneficial for her situation.
moral_consequence: Lynn's friend decides to work things out with her partner.
immoral_action: Lynn approaches her friend about the relationship and tells her to break up with the partner.
immoral_consequence: Lynn's friend breaks up with her partner prematurely when they could have worked things out.

norm: It's rude to be disrespectful towards people who are dead.
situation: Carla is at a funeral for her friend's mother one day.
intention: Carla wants to say something about her friend's mother.
moral_action: Carla tells everyone at the funeral home what a wonderful woman her friend's mother was.
moral_consequence: The family expresses their gratitude to Carla for her kind words.
immoral_action: Carla tells everyone at the funeral home about what a wretched witch the woman was.
immoral_consequence: Carla is asked by her friend's family to leave the funeral home immediately.

norm: Lying is wrong.
situation: Gal is applying for a job as an accountant even though they don't have any experience.
intention: Gal wants to become an accountant.
moral_action: Gal tells the interviewer she is willing to start off as an intern.
moral_consequence: Gal gets a job and is able to learn how to be an accountant.
immoral_action: Gal tells the interviewer that she's currently a full-time accountant.
immoral_consequence: Gal gets the job, but she is not able to successfully complete tasks.

norm: It is disgusting to defecate in public.
situation: Mike was out on his daily run when he urgently felt the need to defecate.
intention: Mike wants to relieve himself.
moral_action: Mike runs to the gas station around the corner and uses the restroom there.
moral_consequence: Mike feels better.
immoral_action: Mike runs up to a neighbor's porch, hides behind a plant, and defacates on their porch.
immoral_consequence: Mike is worried that the neighbor might have caught him on video camera.

norm: You shouldn't cheat in a class.
situation: Ben is in class taking a test on material that he hadn't studied for.
intention: Ben wants to make a good grade.
moral_action: Ben thinks logically about all the questions and does the best that he can.
moral_consequence: Ben is happy when the teacher gives the tests back, and he gets a grade of a B.
immoral_action: Ben copies the answers off the test of the classmate sitting right next to him.
immoral_consequence: Ben's teacher takes the test away from him and marks it with an F.

norm: You shouldn't karate chop people.
situation: Kent is confronting an angry man who is threatening someone else.
intention: Kent wants to end the bad situation.
moral_action: Kent apologizes and tries to verbally diffuse the situation.
moral_consequence: The angry man calms down and leaves.
immoral_action: Kent repeatedly karate chops the angry man in the face.
immoral_consequence: The angry man begins swinging and punches Kent.

norm: It's hurtful to have someone fired.
situation: Karen and her family are eating dinner at a restaurant and their waiter screws up one of their food orders.
intention: Karen wants the waiter to know she's unhappy with the service.
moral_action: Karen leaves a below-average tip, writing on the bill please pay better attention next time!
moral_consequence: The waiter takes this recommendation to heart and carefully studies customer orders in the future.
immoral_action: Karen talks to management and demands the waiter get fired, getting her way after an hour of yelling.
immoral_consequence: The waiter has to beg for money on the street to feed their family.

norm: You don't always have to comment about things.
situation: Ace is on a news program in an interview when he is asked about a very sensitive political issue.
intention: Ace wants to respond to the interviewer.
moral_action: Ace tells the interviewer that he has nothing to say on the issue.
moral_consequence: Ace maintains neutrality and no one feels alienated.
immoral_action: Ace takes a side on the political issue and tells interviewer his answer.
immoral_consequence: People feel alienated from Ace because he disagreed with them.

norm: It's good to give food to the poor.
situation: Dan is walking down the street when he is approached by a poor, drug-addicted man asking for money.
intention: Dan wants to give the man something helpful.
moral_action: Dan takes the man to a grocery store and buys some food for him.
moral_consequence: The man eats well for several days and feels better.
immoral_action: Dan reaches into his pocket and gives the man twenty dollars.
immoral_consequence: The man uses the money to buy drugs and feed his addiction.

norm: It's good to listen to your conscience.
situation: James is walking to dinner with his wife Lisa when he sees a strange man accosting an innocent person across the street.
intention: James wants to decide whether to intervene.
moral_action: James listens to his conscience and intervenes to defend the innocent person from the strange man.
moral_consequence: The strange man leaves and the innocent person is thankful and remains unharmed.
immoral_action: James decides not to get involved and continues walking to dinner as if he didn't notice anything.
immoral_consequence: The innocent person suffers minor injuries and feels rattled and upset.

norm: It is bad to pollute the environment with carbon emissions
situation: Greg has had a busy morning around the house and is running late a bit late to work.
intention: Greg wants to get to work on time.
moral_action: Greg hops on his bicycle and pedals to work as quickly as he can.
moral_consequence: Greg's biking is environmentally friendly and does not release any carbon into the atmosphere.
immoral_action: Greg gets dressed and drives himself to work in his large SUV.
immoral_consequence: Greg's vehicle emits a significant amount of carbon as he drives which pollutes the environment and contributes to global warming.

norm: It is good to avoid conflict with friends
situation: Jill is taken back by a comment that her friend has made to her at work.
intention: Jill wants to set her friend straight.
moral_action: Jill waits for a better time to bring up the issue and explains how it made her feel.
moral_consequence: Jill's friend apologizes for what she said.
immoral_action: Jill immediately raises the issue with her friend at work which leads to an argument.
immoral_consequence: Jill's friend becomes upset with her.

norm: It's bad to steal from your roommates.
situation: Joe has a date coming up and knows that his roommate, Tim, just bought a new blazer that he intended to return.
intention: Joe wants to wear a nice outfit on his date.
moral_action: Joe asks Tim if he has anything nice to wear that he can borrow for his date.
moral_consequence: Tim lends Joe an old blazer that fit perfectly, and was able to return the new one for a full refund.
immoral_action: Joe takes Tim's blazer without asking and spills wine on it during his date.
immoral_consequence: Tim's blazer is ruined and can't be returned.

norm: It is good to discuss issues with your friends.
situation: Sarah has been dealing with a breakup, but hasn't yet told anyone.
intention: Sarah wants to feel better.
moral_action: Sarah tells her friends about the breakup.
moral_consequence: Sarah's friends are able to guide her through the breakup in a healthy manner.
immoral_action: Sarah keeps the breakup a secret from her friends, and instead goes to the bar every night to deal with it alone.
immoral_consequence: Sarah develops a drinking problem that could have easily been prevented by talking to her friends.

norm: You should not favor some friends over others.
situation: Linda, Greeta, and Gertude are out at the mall having lunch together.
intention: Linda wants to share her cheesecake.
moral_action: Linda gives both Greeta and Gertude a taste of a cheesecake.
moral_consequence: Greeta and Gertude love the cheesecake so much they order slices for themselves.
immoral_action: Linda lets Greeta taste her cheesecake, but when Gertude asks to taste, Linda tells her that she wants to eat the rest.
immoral_consequence: Gertude feels left out and wonders if Linda is actually her friend.

norm: You should do favors for others when they need it.
situation: Jason sees his friend Paul moving his furniture into his car.
intention: Jason wants to say something to Paul.
moral_action: Jason tells Paul he can help him lift the furniture.
moral_consequence: Paul will think Jason is helpful and kind.
immoral_action: Jason tells Paul the furniture looks heavy and walks on.
immoral_consequence: Paul will think Jason makes unhelpful comments.

norm: You should always accept someone's apology.
situation: Mary is walking in the park and meets Jack who recently dumped her.
intention: Mary wants to know why Jack dumped her.
moral_action: Mary is satisfied with Jack's explanation and accepts his apology.
moral_consequence: Jack feels relieved and thanks Mary for being a good sports and wishes her the best.
immoral_action: Mary hears out Jack’s explanation for his behaviour but chooses to ignore his apology and walk away.
immoral_consequence: Jack feels guilty and begins to cry.

norm: You shouldn't ruin your school's events.
situation: Jeff is in charge of the school's homecoming dance this year.
intention: Jeff wants to decorate the gym for the dance.
moral_action: Jeff decorates the gym with streamers and balloons in all sorts of colors.
moral_consequence: The principal is pleased with Jeff's decorations and gives him a gift card for his work.
immoral_action: Jeff hangs obscene posters all around the gym for the dance.
immoral_consequence: The principal cancels the dance and suspends Jeff for a week.

norm: It's fine to wear whatever clothing you find appealing.
situation: Sara was invited by her friend to attend a party.
intention: Sara wants to choose a dress for the party.
moral_action: Sara bought a beautiful dress specially for the party and wears it on that day.
moral_consequence: Sara's friend is surprised by her charming look and thinks that she is gorgeous.
immoral_action: Sara chose a darker color dress over her favorite one in order not to catch too much attention.
immoral_consequence: Sara's friend is disappointed at her dress which makes her look older.

norm: It is expected that you pay people for their work
situation: Greg plans to sell his home, and is good friends with a professional painter named Nick.
intention: Greg wants to hire Nick to paint his home, so he can sell it.
moral_action: Greg pays Nick a fair price for each day that he works.
moral_consequence: Nick is happy to have been able to help Greg, and their friendship remains in tact.
immoral_action: Greg has Nick painting for an entire week but never compensates him for his time.
immoral_consequence: Nick feels that he was used by Greg and never speaks to him again.

norm: It's wrong to tell your roommate what to do.
situation: Jill has moved to a new city and is living with a roommate.
intention: Jill wants to schedule cleaning the apartment.
moral_action: Jill asks her roommate to help her pick dates to clean the apartment.
moral_consequence: Jill's roommate thinks Jill is considerate and wants to cooperate more with Jill.
immoral_action: Jill tells her roommate the apartment cleaning is during her roommate's birthday.
immoral_consequence: Jill's roommate moves out and Jill has to pay all the rent.

norm: It's good to celebrate your grandparent's birthday.
situation: Heather has a grandmother who lives in a nursing home with a birthday coming up soon.
intention: Heather wants to wish her grandmother a happy birthday.
moral_action: Heather plans a visit to her grandmother and hand delivers a gift to her.
moral_consequence: Heather's grandmother is excited to have company and appreciates the gift.
immoral_action: Heather sends her grandmother a card and a gift in the mail.
immoral_consequence: Heather's grandmother likes the gift but ends up spending her birthday alone.

norm: It's bad to be competitive over buying gifts.
situation: Elle is divorced and shares a daughter with her ex-husband who is financially better off than her.
intention: Elle wants to give her daughter a special birthday.
moral_action: Elle considers her daughter's interests and handmakes a gift for her with them in mind.
moral_consequence: Elle is able to bond with her daughter over the heartfelt gift.
immoral_action: Elle finds out what her ex-husband is getting their daughter and makes sure to buy more expensive gifts for her.
immoral_consequence: Elle spends too much and falls behind on her bills.

norm: You must always be kind to animals
situation: Paula is leaving home to do some shopping and notices that the dog's water bowl is empty.
intention: Paula wants to leave the dog at home.
moral_action: Paula fills the bowl with water before leaving dog alone in the house.
moral_consequence: The dog is able to get a drink when it gets thirsty.
immoral_action: Paula decides to fill the bowl when she gets home and leaves the dog with no water.
immoral_consequence: The dog gets thirsty while Paula is gone and has no way to quench it's thirst.

norm: It's wrong to kiss someone other than your spouse.
situation: Mark who is married is out with his friend Jenny, and they're about to part ways and go home.
intention: Mark wants to say goodbye to Jenny.
moral_action: Mark tells Jenny goodbye and waves his hand as he turns to walk towards home.
moral_consequence: Jenny waves back to mark and smiles as she turns to go back to her home.
immoral_action: "Mark pulls Jenny in close and gives her a long, passionate kiss on the lips before saying ""I'll miss you, goodbye""."
immoral_consequence: Jenny is shocked because she knows Mark is married and is extremely uncomfortable about the situation.

norm: You shouldn't have to feel pressured to talk to people.
situation: Lucas' sister is very shy and sometimes has a hard time with small talk when she meets new people.
intention: Lucas wants his sister to chat with one of his friends.
moral_action: Lucas suggests his sister play a board game with him and his friend.
moral_consequence: Lucas' sister has a great time playing the game with them and effortlessly strikes a fun conversation with Lucas' friend.
immoral_action: Lucas insists that his sister chat with his friend.
immoral_consequence: Lucas' sister has a short conversation with Lucas' friend but feels very ill-at-ease.

norm: It's rude to laugh during a serious movie.
situation: Keith is at the movies watching a movie where a man just died.
intention: Keith wants to express himself at the scene in the movie.
moral_action: Keith starts to cry silently from his seat in the theater.
moral_consequence: Another person in the theater gives Keith a tissue to wipe his eyes.
immoral_action: Keith starts to laugh loudly at the scene in the movie.
immoral_consequence: The other people in the theater are annoyed and tell Keith to shut up.

norm: It's wrong to fail your class.
situation: Kate has a big final exam to take, but she doesn't feel like going to school.
intention: Kate has to decide whether to go to school.
moral_action: Kate gets up and forces herself to go to school.
moral_consequence: Kate gives herself a chance of passing the class and feels proud of herself.
immoral_action: Kate decides to skip school and watch a movie at home instead.
immoral_consequence: Kate ends up failing the class and has to take it again.

norm: Never shove a sister because it can cause harm.
situation: Barb suspects that her sister Jackie stole her favorite denim jacket.
intention: Barb wants to confront Jackie about the missing jacket.
moral_action: After Jackie denies taking the jacket Barb goes to their mother and asks her to intervene.
moral_consequence: Barb is able to get her jacket back with her mum's help.
immoral_action: Barb asks Jackie about her jacket and when Jackie denies taking it Barb shoves her in anger.
immoral_consequence: Barb gets in trouble when Jackie ends up needing stitches after Barb's shove causes her to hit her head.

norm: You shouldn't park in someone else's spot without permission.
situation: Oliver pulls into his apartment complex parking lot after a long, arduous day at work.
intention: Oliver wants to get into his apartment for a stiff drink as quickly as he can.
moral_action: Oliver finds his parking spot and sprints all the way to his door.
moral_consequence: Oliver gets home quickly and cracks open a beer.
immoral_action: Oliver pulls into the first open spot near his door even though it's not his assigned spot.
immoral_consequence: Oliver has to pay a hefty fee to get his car back because it had been towed.

norm: It's wrong to make excuses for bad behavior.
situation: Ernie cleans out his garage and piles trash in his backyard, which he sets on fire causing a terrible smell throughout his neighborhood, and his neighbors come to his door.
intention: Eric needs to talk to his neighbors about the smelly trash fire.
moral_action: Eric admits to creating an environmental nuisance and apologizes to his neighbors, promising to never do that again.
moral_consequence: Eric's neighbors accept his apology and some of them help him put out the terrible smelling fire that he started.
immoral_action: Eric explains that he only meant to burn the wood, and that the tires, plastic and carpets were burned by mistake.
immoral_consequence: Eric's neighbors don't believe him because it is all in one big pile and Eric loses some of his standing as a good member of the community.

norm: It's wrong to try to interfere with a wedding.
situation: Elise is getting married in two days, and she tells her friend Miranda that she's stressed about a light figure not working right.
intention: Miranda wants support Elise.
moral_action: Miranda hugs her friend and offers her words of encouragement.
moral_consequence: Miranda receives a thank you card from Elise for her support through the wedding.
immoral_action: Miranda, to relieve Elise's stress, makes modifications to the light fixture after Elise leaves the room.
immoral_consequence: Miranda's modifications end up breaking some lights which delays the wedding for a week.

norm: It's good to take the trash out for others.
situation: Jerry is headed out the door to work one morning when he remembers it's garbage day.
intention: Jerry wants to get to work quickly.
moral_action: Jerry quickly runs and grabs the trash and jogs it to the curb before getting in his car and heading to work.
moral_consequence: Jerry and his wife are able to live normally without any added stressors.
immoral_action: Jerry leaves the garbage behind as he rushes to his car, assuming that his wife will take care of it.
immoral_consequence: Jerry's wife doesn't take the garbage out in time and it starts attracting flies as they wait for the next garbage day.

norm: You don't have to help everyone that asks for it
situation: Grant is running late for work when his neighbor asks him if he can help him get the mail.
intention: Grant wants to respond to his neighbor.
moral_action: Grant tells his neighbor he needs to go to work as he is late.
moral_consequence: Grant will get to work on time and not get in trouble.
immoral_action: Grant gets the mail for his neighbor.
immoral_consequence: Grant will be late for work and reprimanded.

norm: You shouldn't just blow off your old workplace.
situation: Jake just got a more prestigious job and hasn't told his old coworkers yet.
intention: Jake wants to tell his coworkers that this is his last day on the job.
moral_action: Jake lets his coworkers know how much he's going to miss working with them.
moral_consequence: Jake's coworkers feel appreciated and will miss having Jared around.
immoral_action: Jake tells his coworkers that he's not going to miss working the place at all.
immoral_consequence: Jake's coworkers feel small and feel as if they were disrespected by Jake.

norm: You shouldn't just bail on others.
situation: Caren and Kelly are best friends in a nightclub where Caren doesn't quite like the music.
intention: Caren wants to go to a nightclub that plays different music.
moral_action: Caren tells Kelly she would prefer different music and asks if she wants to check out another club.
moral_consequence: Kelly agrees and the two end up having fun elsewhere.
immoral_action: While Kelly is at the bar, Caren decides to go to a different club.
immoral_consequence: Kelly feels abandoned, and never speaks to Caren again.

norm: It is good to apologize to someone you stole from.
situation: Shawn stole some money from a friend's car one day, and his friend doesn't know Shawn took it.
intention: Shawn would like to repay his friend.
moral_action: Shawn walks up and hands the envelope to his friend, admits what he did, and apologizes.
moral_consequence: Shawn's friend graciously accepts it and tells him it's no problem and that if he needs money, just ask.
immoral_action: Shawn puts the money on the hood of the car where his friend won't miss it but doesn't tell him.
immoral_consequence: The money gets blown off by the wind and disappears, the friend is still out the money.

norm: It's rude to lie to someone about your backstory.
situation: Bill is preparing his resume for his ongoing job search.
intention: Bill wants to get a good job.
moral_action: Bill is forthright about his work experience and impresses an interviewer with his honesty at a respected company.
moral_consequence: Bill is hired and is given an interesting position with excellent advancement prospects.
immoral_action: Bill purposefully writes his resume in a way that makes it seem as if he has more supervisory experience than he really has.
immoral_consequence: Bill gets a good position, but is in constant fear that his lies will be found out.

norm: It's rude to only think about yourself in relationships.
situation: Jill's car is old and her husband really wants to travel for their next vacation instead of staying home, but their budget is relatively limited.
intention: Jill wants to buy a new car.
moral_action: Jill decides to buy a less expensive car so that her husband and herself can afford a great trip for their vacation.
moral_consequence: Jill's husband is very excited knowing that he will finally get his dream vacation.
immoral_action: Jill insists to buy an expensive car that she's coveted for a long time.
immoral_consequence: Jill's husband decides to give up on his dream vacation in order for Jill to have her expensive car, but he is very disappointed.

norm: It's good to be married when you have a baby.
situation: When May tells John she is pregnant he proposes marriage to her.
intention: May wants to give John an answer.
moral_action: May accepts John's proposal.
moral_consequence: May shares the nurden and joy of raising a child with it's father.
immoral_action: May refuses to Marry John and decides to have the baby alone.
immoral_consequence: May struggles under the pressure of being a single parent.

norm: It's wrong to want to do yourself harm.
situation: Tammy has a difficult home life and is awkward at school with not a lot of friends.
intention: Tammy wants to express her frustration about her life.
moral_action: Tammy talks to a school guidance counselor about her feelings.
moral_consequence: Tammy will be able to release her frustration through words.
immoral_action: Tammy takes a knife and cuts her arms to express her frustration.
immoral_consequence: Tammy will have scars from the cutting of her arms.

norm: It's wrong to domineer your children.
situation: John's kids have made a huge mess in the playroom.
intention: John wants to get his kids to clean up their playroom.
moral_action: John explains to the kids why it's a good idea to clean up.
moral_consequence: They clean up and love their dad.
immoral_action: John tells the kids to clean up, or he will beat them.
immoral_consequence: The kids clean up but are scared of their dad.

norm: Friends shouldn't get angry with each other.
situation: Bill and Matt are talking on the phone when Matt tells Bill that he won't be able to make it to Bill's concert tomorrow.
intention: Bill wants to respond to Matt's statement.
moral_action: Bill tells Matt that it's OK if he doesn't come as he's sure there's a good reason, and that there'll be other concerts.
moral_consequence: Matt feels relieved that he's not being pressured to go and promises to come next time.
immoral_action: Bill tells Matt that the fact he even contemplated not coming is enough to end their friendship and angrily slams down the phone.
immoral_consequence: Matt is taken aback at his friend's violent reaction and feels awful yet confused about what just happened.

norm: It's good to be creative with the gifts you give.
situation: Tommy stops at the local mall after work one afternoon.
intention: Tommy wants to find a birthday gift for his father.
moral_action: Tommy goes to a specialty store to shop for something that he really thinks his father will enjoy receiving.
moral_consequence: Tommy feels a sense of excitement to give his father his birthday gift and Tommy's father is touched by the effort his son put into making his birthday feel special.
immoral_action: Tommy goes to the same store he does every year and buys a neck tie for his father, as he does every year for his father's birthday.
immoral_consequence: Tommy feels as though he is letting his father down and his father feels hurt that Tommy didn't put any real thought into doing something special for his birthday.

norm: You should apologize to someone who you have hurt.
situation: Leah is on the phone with her ex husband Tom, and he tells her she had hurt him deeply in their relationship.
intention: Leah wants to end the conversation.
moral_action: Leah tells Tom that she's truly sorry for all the hurt she caused but that it's best if they never talk again.
moral_consequence: Tom is happy Leah apologized and agrees not to contact her again in the future.
immoral_action: Leah tells Tom she doesn't want to hear it and has to go and hangs up.
immoral_consequence: Tom is angry that Leah won't give him closure and an apology and agonizes further about how their relationship was.

norm: It's bad to eat too much bacon
situation: Jimmy is quite a large man and is at an all you can eat breakfast buffer.
intention: Jimmy wants to get his money's worth out of the meal.
moral_action: Jimmy makes sure to try all the variety of foods available in the buffets, so he can say he tried everything .
moral_consequence: Jimmy feels satisfied with his decision to get the buffet and his consumption doesn't interfere with the availability of items for others.
immoral_action: Jimmy decides to eat as much bacon as he can as he knows it is the likely the most expensive food stuff in the buffet.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy doesn't leave bacon for other customers that may have wanted some and likely did not do any favors to his own health.

norm: You shouldn't call others quitters.
situation: Lucas was upset with his staff for giving up on a project.
intention: Lucas wants to reprimand his staff.
moral_action: Lucas asks his staff what went wrong with the project and waits for responses.
moral_consequence: His staff replies about the contrasting demands and the conflict between the workers.
immoral_action: Lucas calls all of his staff a bunch of quitters and tells them to get back to the project.
immoral_consequence: The project is haphazardly finished and overall just not what the company should create.

norm: It is normal to have a celebration on your birthday
situation: Mike is socializing with friends and it is Mike's birthday.
intention: Mike wants not make a big deal of his birthday.
moral_action: Mike asks his friends to keep things quiet but suggests they buy a round of drinks since it is his birthday.
moral_consequence: Mike's friends have fun celebrating their friend's birthday.
immoral_action: Mike excuses himself from the group and goes home without telling them.
immoral_consequence: Mike's friends are left wondering what is wrong with their friend.

norm: You should thank your employee when you pay them.
situation: James was recently promoted to manager, and he was handing out paychecks for the first time.
intention: James wants to finish handing out the checks.
moral_action: James thanks all his employees as he hands them thier checks.
moral_consequence: The employees are pleased to have such a friendly manager.
immoral_action: James just hands out the checks quickly because people want their money.
immoral_consequence: James's employees wonder why James didn't thank them or say anything.

norm: You should not abuse your spouse
situation: Jim and his wife Jane have been cooped up together during the Corona quarantine so Jim suggests that they join a MMORPG together to pass time.
intention: Jim wants to share a fun activity with Jane.
moral_action: Jim is proud when Jane does a good job playing the game and compliments her when she beats him.
moral_consequence: Jane is happy with Jim and their relationship is strengthened by their new share interest in gaming.
immoral_action: Jim gets frustrated when Jane beats him at the game, so he rage quits the game and throws his controller at her.
immoral_consequence: Jane is hurt and makes Jim sleep on the couch.

norm: It's bad to cancel on friends at the last minute.
situation: Kenny has been invited to go on vacation with a friend in a few days but just found out he has an important meeting he must attend instead.
intention: Kenny wants to let his friend know he cannot make it.
moral_action: Kenny immediately tells his friend about the meeting to give his friend as much notice as he had.
moral_consequence: Kenny's friend appreciates the notice and is able to find another friend to go on the trip with.
immoral_action: Kenny spends the next few days planning for the meeting before letting his friend know about it on the day it is happening.
immoral_consequence: Kenny's friend is annoyed by the last moment notification and cannot find anybody else to go with them.

norm: You shouldn't say mean things to family.
situation: Lucas was vising his family, and he saw they were treating his siblings much better than him.
intention: Lucas wants to point this out to his family.
moral_action: Lucas explains they do things for his siblings that they don't do for him.
moral_consequence: Faced with logic Lucas's family apologizes and tries to explain themselves.
immoral_action: Lucas speaks loudly to his family about how much better his siblings are treated than him.
immoral_consequence: They loudly deny it and get into an argument with Lucas.

norm: It's wrong to tell your friends what to do.
situation: Danny forgot his lunch money at home.
intention: Danny wants to eat lunch.
moral_action: Danny asks his friend if he can help him buy lunch for today.
moral_consequence: Danny's friend buys him lunch and tells him not to worry about paying him back.
immoral_action: Danny tells his friend to buy him lunch.
immoral_consequence: Danny's friend tells him not to tell him what to do and doesn't hang out with him again.

norm: It's wrong to assume words don't hurt others.
situation: Billy and his friends have a playful relationship, and talk some trash on each other some time, Josh and Billy in particular.
intention: Billy wants to entertain his friends.
moral_action: Billy pokes a little fun at himself, mostly all at his expense.
moral_consequence: Billy's friends laugh, especially Josh cracks up a lot.
immoral_action: Billy makes a few jokes at Josh's expense, making fun of his sickly aunt.
immoral_consequence: Josh takes a lot of offense to it, thinking Billy went far too far.

norm: It's frowned upon to want to harm yourself.
situation: Chris is feeling overwhelmed by his school work and employment and is talking to his friend Mary.
intention: Chris wants to feel relief from his stress.
moral_action: Chris tells Mary that he needs some support and help in managing his life.
moral_consequence: Mary is compassionate and helps Chris figure out better stress management skills.
immoral_action: Chris tells Mary that the only thing that helps him feel better is burning himself and that he wants to immediately.
immoral_consequence: Mary is concerned for Chris and calls an emergency crisis team to intervene.

norm: Making up lies about someone cheating is immature.
situation: Mary is mad at her sister who took Mary's favorite dress without asking and got it stained with red wine.
intention: Mary wants to react to what her sister has done.
moral_action: Mary has a serious conversation with her sister, explaining how angry she is with her for ruining her favorite dress.
moral_consequence: Mary's sister takes responsibility for her actions, apologizes to Mary and buys her a new dress.
immoral_action: Mary tells her sister's boyfriend a made-up story about her sister having an affair with her best male friend.
immoral_consequence: Mary's sister has a huge fight with her boyfriend which puts a strain on their relationship.

norm: It's kind to give a treat.
situation: Jessie had gone through a hard day at school and was returning home with her mother.
intention: Jessie's mother wants her to feel better.
moral_action: Jessie's mother takes her out to get an ice cream cone down the street.
moral_consequence: Jessie feels better and forgets about the horrible day that she had at school.
immoral_action: Jessie's mother gives her a glass of water for a snack.
immoral_consequence: Jessie drinks the water but it doesn't stop her hunger or make her feel better about her day.

norm: You shouldn't ignore your partner.
situation: Brad is in the middle of playing a video game when his wife Christie asks him a question.
intention: Brad wants to finish playing his video game.
moral_action: Brad pauses his video game and answers Christie's question before returning to finish playing.
moral_consequence: Christie is relieved to know the answer to the question and happy that Brad is responsive.
immoral_action: Brad ignores his wife and pretends like he doesn't hear her so that he can keep playing his game.
immoral_consequence: Christie gets upset that Brad is ignoring her and storms out of the room.

norm: It's good not to string people along in a relationship.
situation: Lila is dating Ken who she doesn't think is long term material but enjoys short term benefits with.
intention: Lila wants to talk to Ken about their relationship.
moral_action: Lila tells Ken they should find other people.
moral_consequence: Ken will be able to find someone who is long term material for him.
immoral_action: Lila tells Ken she wants to keep dating him, and they have a future together.
immoral_consequence: Ken will think Lila really likes him when she is only using him.

norm: It's good to be an attentive parent.
situation: Tom's kids were playing in the backyard pool while he was on the deck.
intention: Tom wanted to get an ice cold beer from his fridge inside.
moral_action: Tom asks his oldest to run inside and grab a soda for himself and get Tom a beer.
moral_consequence: Tom gets a cold beer and his kids get refreshments without dying.
immoral_action: Tom gets up and leaves the children in the pool to get his beer.
immoral_consequence: Tom comes back outside to find his children drowned in the pool.

norm: You shouldn't use other's things what their permission.
situation: Chris is planning to go to the beach with friends this weekend.
intention: Chris wants to make sure he can get there.
moral_action: Chris cannot get permission to use his father's car, so he asks a friend for a ride.
moral_consequence: A couple of weeks after, his dad trusts him enough to let him use the car on the weekends.
immoral_action: Chris takes his father car without asking.
immoral_consequence: Chris crashes the car and his father makes him pay the damages while banning him from driving until college.

norm: It's rude to bring your animals to the grocery store.
situation: Daniel needs to make a trip to the store, but he doesn't want to leave his dog home by itself.
intention: Daniel wants to make sure his dog isn't alone.
moral_action: Daniel asks his neighbor to come over and watch his dog while he makes a trip to the store.
moral_consequence: Daniel is able to get his grocery shopping done worry-free and comes home to a happy dog.
immoral_action: Daniel decides to bring his dog with him to the store and plans to tell people that it's a service dog.
immoral_consequence: Daniel is asked to leave the store since the employees can clearly tell it isn't a service dog.

norm: It is bad to throw temper tantrums
situation: Mary is with her mom at the grocery store and sees a very sugary food at a discount price.
intention: Mary wants to tell her mom she wants the candy from the store.
moral_action: Mary asks for the candy and doesn't make an ultimatum.
moral_consequence: Mary's mom gives Mary the candy, and she feels happy.
immoral_action: "Mary starts screaming at her mom that she must have her candy, ""or else""."
immoral_consequence: Mary's mom grounds Mary and Mary feels sorry.

norm: It's expected that you'll help family members.
situation: Tom notices his family is doing Spring cleaning in another room, while he is lying on the couch.
intention: Tom wants to see the house get cleaned in person.
moral_action: Tom decides to watch the cleaning by helping out his family in the room.
moral_consequence: Tom's family thanks Tom and Tom feels generous.
immoral_action: Tom decides to enter the room and watch his family clean without helping them.
immoral_consequence: Tom's family insults Tom and Tom feels selfish for not helping.

norm: It is mean to keep grandparents from seeing their grandchildren.
situation: Matt stills holds a grudge against his parents, but they want to see Matt's kids.
intention: Matt has to decide whether to let his parents see his kids.
moral_action: Matt lets his parents see his kids since his kids wanted to see them.
moral_consequence: Matt feels good that his kids are happy, and his parents are relieved.
immoral_action: Matt makes up stories for why his parents can't see his kids.
immoral_consequence: Matt's parents know he's lying, and Matt continues to hold a grudge.

norm: It's good to shower and keep yourself clean.
situation: Marry has just finished an intense workout, and Mary has a date in an hour.
intention: Mary wants to prepare for her date.
moral_action: Mary freshens up with a nice shower before picking out a cute outfit for her date.
moral_consequence: Mary receives multiple compliments through the night about her clean appearance and attire.
immoral_action: Mary spends the entire hour doing her makeup and hair.
immoral_consequence: Mary's date goes poorly because her date thinks she smells bad.

norm: You should not reward behavior you do not enjoy.
situation: Lance's dog has started begging at the table during dinner which Lance finds very annoying.
intention: Lance wants his dog to leave him alone when he's eating.
moral_action: Lance ignores his dog's begging and gives him food whenever he stops.
moral_consequence: Lance's dog learns to not to beg at the table if he wants food and becomes better behaved.
immoral_action: Lance gives his dog some food whenever it starts begging so it will stop for a bit.
immoral_consequence: Lance's dog learns that begging will get him a reward, so he continues to beg.

norm: You shouldn't leave events early without notifying people.
situation: Jill is at a social event with friends and something urgent has just come up.
intention: Jill wants to leave in a hurry.
moral_action: Jill texts her friends about the situation before she leaves giving them a heads up.
moral_consequence: Jill's friends understand and are glad she was able to be there for a bit.
immoral_action: Jill leaves without bother saying anything to her friends that are there.
immoral_consequence: Jill's friends thinks they have been ghosted and are taken aback.

norm: You shouldn't ignore your partner while you play video games.
situation: Phil is playing video games on the PC while Sypha is talking.
intention: Phil wants to keep playing the game.
moral_action: Phil makes sure to listen to what Sypha is saying while he's playing.
moral_consequence: Sypha continues to talk and doesn't get upset with Phil.
immoral_action: Phil ignores what Sypha says altogether and keeps playing the game.
immoral_consequence: Sypha gets annoyed at Phil because he's not listening to her.

norm: It is good to care for something that is helpless.
situation: Diana is at a new years party at her friend's house when she notices her friend's dog trembling under the table.
intention: Diana wants to interact with the dog.
moral_action: Diana holds the dog close to her and gives the dog a treat.
moral_consequence: The dog learns to trust Diana.
immoral_action: Diana pushes the dog outside.
immoral_consequence: The scared dog digs holes all over the backyard.

norm: It is accommodating to learn the local language.
situation: Greg visited a country in Africa that would be considered a developing country.
intention: Greg wants to talk to the locals in the country.
moral_action: Greg learns the basics of their language in order to help him talk to people.
moral_consequence: The locals understand that Greg is trying his best and are willing to help him out.
immoral_action: Greg talks to the locals using simple English words even though they can't understand it.
immoral_consequence: The locals feel disrespected by Greg and won't want to help him.

norm: You should always pay a veterinarian for their work.
situation: Joe took his dog to the veterinarian and is handed a bill after the procedure.
intention: Joe wants to respond to the bill he has been handed.
moral_action: Joe pays the bill for the veterinarian visit.
moral_consequence: The veterinarian will be happy with having Joe as a client.
immoral_action: Joe tells the veterinarian that he won't pay for the bill.
immoral_consequence: The veterinarian will not want to service Joe's dog again.

norm: You should be kind to your coworkers.
situation: George's coworker is going through a rough time in their relationship and cries at work often.
intention: George wants to respond to his coworker's feelings.
moral_action: George asks his colleague if there is anything he can do for them.
moral_consequence: George's colleague is grateful to George for his kindness.
immoral_action: George tells his coworker to grow-up and get over it.
immoral_consequence: George's coworker feels worse and cries even more.

norm: It's good to let people know racism is wrong.
situation: Pat was on a train, and a white man started harassing a Muslim family on it.
intention: Pat has to decide whether to do something.
moral_action: Pat raises his voice and tells the guy to shut his mouth.
moral_consequence: The family feels relieved that someone came to their defense.
immoral_action: Pat minds his business and doesn't say anything to the man.
immoral_consequence: The Muslim family continues to be harassed and is sad that no one comes to their support.

norm: It's wrong to hide relationships from your spouse.
situation: In order to save money, Ben will be sharing a room with his female coworker Annie.
intention: Ben needs to tell his wife Maggie about the trip.
moral_action: Ben tells Maggie that he will be sharing a room with Annie, assuring Maggie that their relationship is strictly platonic.
moral_consequence: Maggie's trust in Ben increases.
immoral_action: Ben tells Maggie that he's traveling alone.
immoral_consequence: Maggie finds out about Annie, and she begins believing that Ben is cheating on her with Annie.

norm: It's wrong to protect someone who did something illegal.
situation: Stan and James are at an internet cafe when James lies to the cashier about his playing time.
intention: Stan wants to interject in the conversation.
moral_action: Stan tells James to fess up and pay the man what he deserves.
moral_consequence: James pays what he actually owes and leaves the cafe safely.
immoral_action: Stan says that he's confident that James is telling the truth and supports Jame’s story.
immoral_consequence: The man checks the camera footage and verifies that both Stan and James are lying, then calls the police.

norm: It's important to make time for your marriage.
situation: Alyssa's husband asks Alyssa to spend more evenings at home because Alyssa has been working late at the office every night.
intention: Alyssa wants to succeed in her job.
moral_action: Alyssa decides to leave earlier for work in the morning so that she is home in the evening.
moral_consequence: Alyssa's husband is happy to spend more time with her in the evening.
immoral_action: Alyssa turns down her husband's request and keeps on staying late at the office.
immoral_consequence: Alyssa's husband feels neglected and sad.

norm: It is rude to knock over a jigsaw puzzle.
situation: Ben is sitting at the table working on a jigsaw puzzle when Jessica walks in.
intention: Jessica wants to pick up a piece of the puzzle.
moral_action: Jessica takes a piece of the puzzle and puts it in the place where it belongs.
moral_consequence: Ben tells Jessica thank you for helping him with the puzzle.
immoral_action: Jessica takes a few pieces of the puzzle and throws them on the floor.
immoral_consequence: Ben starts to yell at Jessica and tells her to leave him alone.

norm: It's good to listen to your in-law's stories.
situation: Bill is having some drinks with the family while his in-law is telling the group a story from the past.
intention: Bill wants to go get more drinks.
moral_action: Bill asks his in-law to wait a moment because he wants to hear the rest of the story and offers to get them another drink.
moral_consequence: Bill's in law appreciates that he wants to hear the rest of the story.
immoral_action: Bill gets up in the middle of the story to go get more beer.
immoral_consequence: Bill's in-law is annoyed and thinks he is being rude.

norm: It's wrong to give other people herpes knowingly.
situation: Ian got herpes from unprotected sex and feels very angry about it.
intention: Ian wants to take action on his anger.
moral_action: Ian finds some treatments for herpes and spends his anger trying to stamp the disease out.
moral_consequence: Ian goes into remission and doesn't infect other people.
immoral_action: Ian sleeps with various people without informing them of his STD, so he won't suffer alone.
immoral_consequence: Other people get herpes and suffer from the disease like Ian does.

norm: It's wrong to kill someone else's pets.
situation: Jenny is losing sleep every night because her neighbor's dogs won't ever stop barking.
intention: Jenny wants to deal with the barking dogs.
moral_action: Jenny files a compliant with the county and the neighbors are fined and told they'll lose the dogs if they don't keep them quiet.
moral_consequence: The neighbors realize they'll get in trouble if they don't control their dogs, so they keep the dogs quiet.
immoral_action: Jenny puts rat poison in hamburger and feeds it to the neighbors dogs.
immoral_consequence: The neighbors cry about their dead dogs, and then get more barking dogs anyway.

norm: It's bad to ignore people because you're on your phone.
situation: Debbie is on a call with her boyfriend Jim and her daughter Sally really wants dinner.
intention: Debbie wants to have a discussion with her lover.
moral_action: Debbie tells Jim to hang on a minute and while she listens to Sally ask for dinner, then continues her call on speaker phone while cooking.
moral_consequence: Sally gets to satisfy her appetite and appreciates Debbie taking the time to listen.
immoral_action: Debbie is talking to Jim about their plans later that evening and when Sally asks when dinner is, Debbie pretends she doesn't hear.
immoral_consequence: Sally feels unimportant to Debbie and goes to sulk in her room still feeling hungry.

norm: It's wrong to flirt with your friend's partner.
situation: Ted was hanging out with his friend and his friend's girlfriend.
intention: Ted wants to make a joke with his friends.
moral_action: Ted tells a clean knock knock joke to his friend and his friend's girlfriend.
moral_consequence: Ted's friend and his friend's girlfriend both laugh at the joke Ted tells.
immoral_action: Ted makes a flirty joke to the girlfriend of his friend while his friend is standing there.
immoral_consequence: Ted's friend punches him in the face and doesn't talk to him in a month.

norm: It's bad to wear unprofessional clothing in some settings.

moral_action: Jeff decides that just because disabled people are restricted in one way doesn't mean they're restricted period and vows to help them.
moral_consequence: Mary is delighted that Jeff is so open minded and willing to help fellow humans.
immoral_action: Jeff decides that since disabled people are restricted in some ways, that he thinks they should all die and doesn't want them around.
immoral_consequence: Mary is disgusted by Jeff's sociopathy and decides to leave right away.

norm: You shouldn't talk back to your boss.
situation: Greg is in a work meeting with his boss where he disagrees with what is said.
intention: Greg wants to express his opinion.
moral_action: Greg approaches his boss after the meeting and expresses his concerns.
moral_consequence: Greg's boss praises him for handling the situation well and promises to look into his concerns.
immoral_action: Greg loudly berates his boss and calls her stupid.
immoral_consequence: Greg is fired.

norm: You should be supportive when your partner loses weight.
situation: Dylan is married to Hailey and Hailey is on a workout regime where she is losing a lot of weight.
intention: Dylan wants to talk to Hailey about her weight los.
moral_action: Dylan tells Hailey she is doing a great job, and he'll cook her healthy meals to help with the weight loss.
moral_consequence: Hailey will appreciate that Dylan wants to help her in her weight loss journey.
immoral_action: Dylan tells Hailey that Hailey is losing too much weight and should stop working out.
immoral_consequence: Hailey will think that Dylan is trying to detract from what she is accomplishing.

norm: It's hurtful to cancel your child's visit with her parent.
situation: Kitty lives with her mother who divorced with Kitty's father and one day Kitty doesn't do her Math homework properly.
intention: Kitty's mother wants to punish her.
moral_action: Kitty's mother asks her to do two more pages of practice in the Math book.
moral_consequence: Kitty feels obliged, carefully works through the practice and gets a better understanding of the Math concepts.
immoral_action: Kitty's mother does not let her see her father on the weekend.
immoral_consequence: Kitty feels sad and misses her father so much.

norm: It's not expected that you'll hit someone with a baguette.
situation: Kara is at the diner eating breakfast with her sister who says something offensive.
intention: Kara wants her sister to be quiet.
moral_action: Kara asks her sister if she could lower her voice a bit.
moral_consequence: The manager thanks Kara for stopping her sister from being a nuisance.
immoral_action: Kara throws a hot baguette across the table at her sister.
immoral_consequence: The manager of the diner kicks Kara out for disrupting the other patrons.

norm: It is rude to leave others out of a celebration.
situation: John has just been promoted at work and invited a group of friends over to celebrate.
intention: John wants to have a good time.
moral_action: John sees that his roommate is home and invites him to join in the celebration.
moral_consequence: John's roommate is happy to join the fun and meet John's other friends.
immoral_action: John does not invite his roommate to join the celebration, even though he is home.
immoral_consequence: John's roommate feels left out and annoyed with John for hosting a party without him.

norm: You shouldn't access someone else's online accounts without permission.
situation: John hears that Dave's girlfriend broke up with him by sending Dave an email.
intention: John wants to find out if the rumour is true.
moral_action: John calls Dave and just asks him if it's true that he had been broken up with through email.
moral_consequence: Dave is happy John is taking an interest in his personal life and is happy to share the breakup details with John.
immoral_action: John hacks into Dave's email by figuring out his birthday is his email password, so he can read the breakup email.
immoral_consequence: Dave finds out John violated his privacy and is infuriated and feels violated and distrustful towards internet security.

norm: It's good to report bad behavior in school.
situation: Norbert saw Dirk destroying textbooks in the library the other day and now a teacher has asked him if he knows anything about it.
intention: Norbert wants to answer the teacher's question.
moral_action: Norbert tells the teacher that he knows that Dirk did it because he saw him.
moral_consequence: The teacher is delighted and relieved to know who did the deed, so she can have them dealt with.
immoral_action: Norbert tells the teacher that he didn't see anything and has no idea what happened.
immoral_consequence: The teacher is stressed out because she can't figure out who did the bad deed.

norm: You should get a job if you can't afford something.
situation: Greg wants to buy some new sneakers, but he doesn't have enough money.
intention: Greg wants to get more money.
moral_action: Greg will get a job at his local supermarket and work his way up.
moral_consequence: Greg gets more than enough money and can buy his own sneakers.
immoral_action: Greg waits outside at night and waits for someone to walk by to take money from them.
immoral_consequence: It is not a sustainable way of making money so Greg will have to keep doing it.

norm: It's wrong to treat a partner rudely.
situation: Mark is talking to an important group of people with his girlfriend Jane.
intention: Mark wants to entertain everyone.
moral_action: Mark tells the people stories of some of the unique experiences he's had with Jane.
moral_consequence: Jane hugs Mark thanking him for never forgetting the important things in life.
immoral_action: Mark makes a funny joke about his wife's appearance.
immoral_consequence: Jane's feelings are hurt by Mark's actions, and she leaves the party.

norm: You should not fry everything you eat.
situation: Mickey doesn't have an oven, only a hot plate, so he fries all of his food, but lately he has been feeling lethargic and weakened.
intention: Mickey has to decide whether he needs to change his diet to feel better.
moral_action: Mickey starts eating more raw vegetables and fruits, and only cooks his food a few times a week until he gets an oven.
moral_consequence: His health begins to improve, and he has more energy, and as a result his life is more enjoyable and comfortable.
immoral_action: Mickey decides that his lethargy has nothing to do with his food, so he doesn't make any changes to his diet.
immoral_consequence: Mickey's health suffers as he continues to eat only fried foods, and he eventually needs medical attention.

norm: It is rude to edit encyclopedia entries with fake information.
situation: Paul is bored at home and decides to start browsing some Wikipedia entries.
intention: Paul wants to edit one of the entries.
moral_action: Paul edits the entry to mention some recent things a celebrity was working on, complete with sources.
moral_consequence: Other readers feel informed and thankful to Paul for adding the information.
immoral_action: Paul edits the entry to say that someone famous had died recently, when they hadn't.
immoral_consequence: Other readers spread the false information on social media and Paul gets in trouble.

norm: It's wrong to not give your best effort in school.
situation: Bella and her friends are all currently in high school.
intention: Bella wants to graduate.
moral_action: Bella joins clubs, takes AP classes, and gets an A in all her classes.
moral_consequence: Bella is able to get into her dream college and gets a scholarship.
immoral_action: Bella does the bare minimum so that she can pass her classes with a C.
immoral_consequence: Bella is not accepted into any of her colleges of choice.

norm: It's good to take responsibility for bad behaviors you've done.
situation: Walt's daughter is engaged and Walt has been using drugs.
intention: Walt wants to attend his daughter's wedding.
moral_action: Walt goes to a treatment program before attending the wedding.
moral_consequence: Walt's daughter is proud of him and enjoys her wedding peacefully.
immoral_action: Walt denies he has a problem and attends the wedding high.
immoral_consequence: Walt's daughter is embarrassed after Walt causes a scene while high.

norm: You should apologize if you hurt someone and they cry.
situation: Brad and Janet are arguing and Janet begins to cry after Brad tells her she's wrong.
intention: Brad wants to react to Janet crying.
moral_action: Brad tells Janet that he's really sorry, and he didn't mean it to come out the way it did.
moral_consequence: Janet is a bit relieved Brad didn't mean to be so callous earlier and is happy he's apologizing to her.
immoral_action: Brad tells Janet that she needs to get over it because he's right and crying doesn't change that.
immoral_consequence: Janet is even more upset because not only did Brad hurt her but now he's doubling down and insulting her further.

norm: It's wrong to neglect a pet without a reason.
situation: Sherri is caring for her sisters dog while she is away but her job keeps her away from home til late.
intention: Sherri wants to keep the dog occupied while she is away.
moral_action: Sherri arranges for a dog sitter to come during the day and adjusts her schedule to be home earlier.
moral_consequence: The dog thrives under the care it is being given.
immoral_action: Sherri leaves the TV on to keep the dog entertained.
immoral_consequence: The dog grows more withdrawn and lethargic due to the lack of attention.

norm: You should share your things with your little brother.
situation: Jimmy and Wilson are brothers, and they are staying at home on a Saturday.
intention: Jimmy wants to pass the time.
moral_action: Jimmy plays his new video game with Wilson.
moral_consequence: Jimmy feels excited and satisfied having a companion to play with.
immoral_action: Jimmy watches a movie on his own in his bedroom.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy feels bored with no one to share the happiness.

norm: It's inappropriate to raid the food from someone else's house.
situation: Jen has spent the night at her friends house who has to leave for work before she gets up.
intention: Jen wants to have something to eat.
moral_action: Jen calls and orders a pizza to her friends place.
moral_consequence: Jen's friend is pleasantly surprised she leaves her the rest of the pizza for when she gets home.
immoral_action: Jen rummages through her friends fridge and puts together something.
immoral_consequence: Jen's friend has to go back to the grocery store later because she was going to use those items for dinner.

norm: You shouldn't judge people based on their socio-economic situation.
situation: Laura is on enjoying her first date with Liam when he explains that he is currently homeless due to job loss.
intention: Laura wants to express her concern for Liam.
moral_action: Laura tells Liam that she wants to help him get in touch with people who can help improve his situation.
moral_consequence: Liam is grateful and accepting of Laura's help, and they enjoy the rest of their date together.
immoral_action: Laura tells Liam that his situation sounds horrible and that she's so sorry for him but that she thinks he shouldn't be focused on dating right now.
immoral_consequence: Liam is insulted by Laura giving him life advice on a date and leaves the date early, upset.

norm: It is unacceptable to tell someone what to wear.
situation: Donald hears that his daughter will be attending her first prom today.
intention: Donald wants to prepare his daughter for prom.
moral_action: Donald asks his daughter what she wants help with, which turns out to be driving to the prom.
moral_consequence: Donald's daughter gets to the prom on time, and both Donald and his daughter are excited.
immoral_action: Donald tells her daughter exactly what to wear, including colors involved.
immoral_consequence: Donald's daughter tells Donald he is overbearing, and they argue for hours.

norm: being unfaithful to a partner is morally wrong.
situation: Matt and Natalie are dating and Natalie is going to be away on a work trip for a week.
intention: Matt wants to avoid feeling lonely.
moral_action: Matt calls a friend and invites him over to play video games.
moral_consequence: Natalie is glad Matt had fun with his friend.
immoral_action: Matt calls his ex-girlfriend and invites her over to his house for an intimate evening.
immoral_consequence: Natalie finds out and breaks up with Matt.

norm: Children shouldn't be put in the middle of parental conflicts.
situation: Joe and Sarah are going through a custody battle and can't settle on a visitation schedule for when Joe gets to see his kids.
intention: Joe wants to spend more time with his kids.
moral_action: Joe is always early for his scheduled visits and focuses on the time the they do have instead of complaining.
moral_consequence: Joe's son appreciates the effort his dad puts forth when hanging out with him.
immoral_action: Joe coaches his son to tell the judge handling the custody case that his mom neglects him.
immoral_consequence: Joe's son breaks down in front of the judge, unable to handle the stress of lying.

norm: You should call your family member when they ask.
situation: Sam's dad texts him while he's in class, asking him to call when he's able to.
intention: Sam wants to find out what his dad wants.
moral_action: Sam finds a quiet place to call his dad after class is over.
moral_consequence: Sam's father is relieved to hear from his son and tells him what's going on.
immoral_action: Sam texts his dad rather than calling him.
immoral_consequence: Sam's dad is frustrated that his son texts rather than calls.

norm: It's wrong to con someone.
situation: Ashley, who quit an MLM, wants to sell her remaining stock of essential oils, and she notices Sandy complaining about hair loss.
intention: Ashley wants to get rid of her products.
moral_action: Ashley uses the oils to create custom soap bars, and gives samples to her friends and family.
moral_consequence: Ashley's soap becomes a hit, and she sells her remaining stock.
immoral_action: Ashley tells her friend that her product cures hair loss, and sells him the product at a marked up price.
immoral_consequence: Ashley's reputation is ruined among her friend group when her friend's hair does not grow back.

norm: It's good to support local restaurants.
situation: Ann just finished working at her officed located in her small home town and is feeling hungry.
intention: Ann wants to eat dinner.
moral_action: Ann drives to a local family owned restaurant to eat dinner.
moral_consequence: The money Ann spends supports the local economy.
immoral_action: Ann drives 30 minutes into the city to eat dinner at a chain restaurant.
immoral_consequence: The money Ann spends goes to a large chain restaurant in a different city, depriving her local economy of money.

norm: It's bad to like underage girls.
situation: Joe goes to a summer picnic that is organized annually by his neighborhood.
intention: Joe wants to meet some woman and potentially date them.
moral_action: Joe sees a new neighbor who appears to be around his age and strikes up a conversation with her.
