moral_consequence: They chat for a bit and hit it off well enough to agree to a date next Friday.
immoral_action: Joe hangs around the teenage daughters of some of the neighbors and tries to flirt with them.
immoral_consequence: The girls are creeped out and one of the fathers punches Joe out.

norm: It's hurtful to destroy your partners property.
situation: Amanda had a big fight with her boyfriend and comes across her boyfriend's favorite shirt on the floor.
intention: Amanda wants to decide what to do with the shirt.
moral_action: Amanda resists the temptation to damage the shirt and simply puts it away.
moral_consequence: Amanda's boyfriend makes up with her and treats her to a nice dinner.
immoral_action: Amanda decides to use scissors on the shirt and destroys it completely.
immoral_consequence: Amanda's boyfriend starts thinking about how petty Amanda is and breaks up with her.

norm: People should give clothing to those without.
situation: Jenny has ordered new garments to update most of her wardrobe.
intention: Jenny wants to clear out some space in the closet.
moral_action: Jenny takes the unneeded clothes to goodwill.
moral_consequence: People get clothes that they would not have otherwise.
immoral_action: Jenny puts the clothes in a bag and stores them in the garage.
immoral_consequence: People experiencing hard times don't get much needed clothing.

norm: You should give extra assistance to those with disabilities.
situation: Jake is entering a convenience store to buy some smokes and sees a man in a wheelchair coming up behind him to enter the store as well.
intention: Jake wants to decide whether to hold the door open for the disabled man.
moral_action: Jake holds the door open for the disabled man, allowing him easy access to the store.
moral_consequence: The disabled man appreciates the show of courtesy and thanks Jake.
immoral_action: Jake briskly enters the convenience store without holding the door open for the disabled man.
immoral_consequence: The door slams shut in the disabled man's face, and he feels disrespected.

norm: You shouldn't ride your bike in your house.
situation: Bob is stuck indoors while it is raining.
intention: Bob wants to do some exercise.
moral_action: Bob runs in place.
moral_consequence: Bob gets exercise without breaking things.
immoral_action: Bob rides his bike in the house.
immoral_consequence: Bob crashes into the shelves breaking them.

norm: It's good to order people food as gifts.
situation: Cory is in a long distance relationship with a girl, whose birthday is coming up, and they are both very antisocial people.
intention: Cory wants to send his girl something for her birthday.
moral_action: Cory orders take out from her favorite restaurant and sends it by courier to her.
moral_consequence: Cory's girlfriend is impressed that he remembered her favorite restaurant.
immoral_action: Cory decides to send her some new clothes as a gift.
immoral_consequence: Cory's girlfriend likes the clothing but has to cook for herself on her birthday.

norm: It's wrong not to help your classmates.
situation: Cassandra and Richard, who is struggling in math, are studying for an exam the rest of their class.
intention: Cassandra wants to adequately prepare of the exam.
moral_action: Cassandra invites Richard and their other classmates to go over the material as a group.
moral_consequence: Cassandra and Richard become friends, and they both do well on their test.
immoral_action: Cassandra ignores Richard studying alone.
immoral_consequence: While Cassandra does well on the test, Richard fails the math test.

norm: You shouldn't slap people.
situation: Betty runs into her sister at a party, when her sister had already said she was ill.
intention: Betty wants them to know that she is upset.
moral_action: Betty sits her sister down and talk out their problems.
moral_consequence: They come to a resolve and hang out for the rest of the night.
immoral_action: Betty smacks her sister and tells her that she is betrayed .
immoral_consequence: Betty and her sister get into a fight at the party.

norm: It is rude to upset someone on a special day.
situation: Claire is attending the wedding of her friend Martha, and the guests are all sitting around eating.
intention: Claire wants to make an impromptu speech.
moral_action: Claire stands up and tells a sweet story about a time Martha really came through for her.
moral_consequence: Martha feels really touched by the story, and she cries some tears of joy.
immoral_action: Claire stands up and tells an inappropriate story involving Martha and a previous boyfriend.
immoral_consequence: Martha feels humiliated on her wedding day and leaves the dinner in tears.

norm: It's wrong to reject people based on their weight.
situation: Paul has dinner with his friend Angie, and she expresses romantic feelings for him, and he feels the same way but finds her weight to be a problem.
intention: Paul needs to decide if he wants to reciprocate and tell Angie that he has romantic feelings for her too.
moral_action: Paul tells Angie that spending time with her is one of his favorite things, and he isn't sure about romance, but would be willing to explore the idea with her.
moral_consequence: Angie ultimately decides that she deserves better than an exploration of romance and doesn't date Paul, but he does not regret being honest with her.
immoral_action: Paul tells Angie that he doesn’t have time right now to pursue a new, romantic relationship with her, but the truth is that he finds her extra weight unattractive.
immoral_consequence: Paul regrets not being more honest and open with his friend and Angie suspects that he is being disingenuous in his response to her, which causes tension in their relationship.

norm: You shouldn't fantasize about torture.
situation: Sam is looking for a movie to watch and sees that a torture horror film has been released, so he goes and watches it.
intention: Sam wants to reflect on the movie.
moral_action: Sam considers how disgusting and unreasonable the movie was and refuses to think about it.
moral_consequence: Sam maintains a healthy view of the sanctity of life and works to make people happy.
immoral_action: Sam thinks about the movie and imagines himself torturing other people for fun.
immoral_consequence: Sam eventually acts out his fantasies and traumatizes an innocent person.

norm: It is gluttonous to eat too much.
situation: Larry is going to an all you can eat lunch buffet at a new restaurant with some of his friends.
intention: Larry wants to try everything on the menu.
moral_action: Larry tries a few bites of eat of the different food options before getting a regular portion of the one he liked best.
moral_consequence: Larry loves the restaurant and is excited to visit it again soon.
immoral_action: Larry grabs several plates worth of different foods and ends up eating large portions of all of the different options.
immoral_consequence: Larry feels sick to his stomach and ends up vomiting after he gets home.

norm: Parents shouldn't abandon their children.
situation: Haken is shopping with his son when he notices the girl he likes leaving the store.
intention: Haken wants to talk to his crush.
moral_action: Haken searches her profile on Facebook and leaves a friend reply to her post.
moral_consequence: Haken and his crush become friends.
immoral_action: Haken runs after his crush leaving his child unattended.
immoral_consequence: Haken is scolded by his crush for leaving his child.

norm: It's wrong to fake how you feel.
situation: Joe is having serious doubts about the girl he is currently seeing and the topic of their relationship comes up while they drive home together.
intention: Joe wants to avoid arguing on the way home.
moral_action: Joe insists that they will talk about things when later after arriving home.
moral_consequence: Joe's girlfriend does not bring the subject up again on the ride home.
immoral_action: Joe acts like there is nothing wrong with their relationship.
immoral_consequence: Joe's girlfriend is misled into believing that they are on good terms.

norm: You should always consult with someone before discarding their things.
situation: Jane's roommate moved out but left several items behind in the apartment.
intention: Jane wants to get rid of her ex roommates things.
moral_action: Jane contacts her ex roommate and tells them that they left things at the apartment.
moral_consequence: Jane's ex roommate is glad to have the items they forgot to take back.
immoral_action: Jane throws out her ex roommate's things into the garbage dumpster.
immoral_consequence: Jane's roommate is upset that her forgotten things were just thrown away.

norm: It's inconsiderate not to tip for good service
situation: Ken is footing the bill at an expensive restaurant and is worried about the cost.
intention: Ken wants to save some money on the food bill.
moral_action: Ken eats only an appetizer and doesn't order dessert to save money.
moral_consequence: Ken's server is relieved after service because the tip was much needed.
immoral_action: Ken ends up leaving no tip in order to save on the pricey bill.
immoral_consequence: Ken's server ends up not making enough money for the day.

norm: It's wrong to bribe your kids.
situation: Josh has a migraine, and he has a long drive with his kids ahead of him.
intention: Josh wants his kids to be quiet on the way back home.
moral_action: Josh asserts his authority as the father and warns his kids that there will be consequences if they do not keep quiet.
moral_consequence: Josh's kids learn not to push the boundaries with their parents too far.
immoral_action: Josh promises to buy his kids a new video game if they are quiet on the way home.
immoral_consequence: Josh's kids are encouraged to behave badly in order to rewarded to stop.

norm: It's morally unacceptable to have relations with a child.
situation: Steve has raised his step daughter for 5 years now and is starting to fall in love with her.
intention: Steve wants to show his step daughter how much he loves him.
moral_action: Steve makes sure to buy his step daughter whatever she wants.
moral_consequence: Steve's step daughter feels loved by Steve and is happier.
immoral_action: Steve asks his step daughter if she wants to be his girlfriend.
immoral_consequence: Steve's step daughter feels pressured to say yes and doesn't feel comfortable.

norm: It is wrong to neglect your pregnant wife.
situation: John is at home with his pregnant wife who is nearing labor.
intention: John wants to have a fun time on the town.
moral_action: John tends to his wife's needs, takes her to the hospital and waits for her to give birth before going out with friends.
moral_consequence: John's wife is happier and less anxious and loves him more.
immoral_action: John ignores her and goes bar-hopping.
immoral_consequence: John's wife feels stressed about giving birth and resents John.

norm: You shouldn't miss the birth of your baby.
situation: Peter's wife is about to give birth, which coincides with the last day of an important presentation Peter has to do for work.
intention: Peter absolutely wants to give the presentation himself.
moral_action: Peter asks for the presentation to be delayed by a few days, so he can be with his wife for the birth of their baby.
moral_consequence: Peter's wife feels comforted by his presence while she is giving birth.
immoral_action: Peter goes to work to give the presentation while his wife gives birth to their child.
immoral_consequence: Peter's wife feels abandoned and disappointed by his actions.

norm: You shouldn't smoke around pregnant people.
situation: All of Cindy's friends are pregnant, but she wants to smoke.
intention: Cindy wants to smoke.
moral_action: Cindy goes outside on a patio and smokes her cigarette there.
moral_consequence: Cindy's friends are all safe inside from the smoke, so they keep on talking.
immoral_action: Cindy gets out her cigarette from her purse and smokes it.
immoral_consequence: Her friends are all upset and bothered by the smoke and the harm it might cause to their kids.

norm: It's wrong to use things without the owner's permission.
situation: Tim's razor broke while he was getting ready to go to work.
intention: Tim wants to finish shaving.
moral_action: Tim asks Mark if he can uses his razor because his broke, and he needs to finish shaving.
moral_consequence: Mark tells Tim that's fine, as long as he cleans it afterwards, he's happy to loan him his razor.
immoral_action: Tim grabs his roommate Mark's razor without asking him and uses it to finish shaving.
immoral_consequence: Mark notices that someone has used his razor and confronts Tim, and they get into an argument.

norm: It's rude to smell bad.
situation: Penny is at the gym working out she is going on a blind date later tonight.
intention: Penny wants to be on time for her date.
moral_action: Penny leaves the gym early, so she can go shower and get ready for her date, and she makes it to her date on time.
moral_consequence: Penny smells good and her date calls her back the next day.
immoral_action: After the gym Penny goes home to get ready for her date she decides to skip the shower, and she makes it to her date on time.
immoral_consequence: Penny smells bad on her date and her date never calls her back.

norm: You shouldn't back out of a friend's plans.
situation: Larry got invited to dinner with Ken, and he said yes, but later in the day he was feeling lazy.
intention: Larry wants to enjoy his day.
moral_action: Larry goes out to dinner with his friend.
moral_consequence: Larry has a great time with his friend, and they get closer.
immoral_action: Larry cancels on his friend and stays home.
immoral_consequence: Larry hurts his friend's feelings.

norm: It's good to be patient with others.
situation: It's late on a Friday night and Eric asks John how to use the new microwave.
intention: John wants to go to sleep.
moral_action: John devotes a few minutes writing down how to use it and then goes to bed.
moral_consequence: Eric thinks John is gracious and is able to use the microwave.
immoral_action: John tells Eric it's late, and he should figure it out on his own.
immoral_consequence: Eric feels insulted and resents John and won't help John next time and can't use the microwave.

norm: It's good to give dogs a good home.
situation: Bill gets a puppy for his birthday even though he works long hours.
intention: Bill wants to give the puppy a good home.
moral_action: Bill realizes he cannot care for a puppy and reaches out to a no kill rescue.
moral_consequence: The rescue screens many people and finds the puppy a loving home that sends Bill update pictures.
immoral_action: Bill gets frustrated with the puppy soiling in the house while he is gone and sells it online.
immoral_consequence: The puppy is purchased by someone for dog fighting bait.

norm: You shouldn't make trash mountains.
situation: Holly is outside cleaning the yard and has picked up a lot of trash.
intention: Holly wants to get rid of the trash.
moral_action: Holly takes the trash and brings it to the recycling center.
moral_consequence: Holly receives a deposit from the recycling center for recycling all the trash.
immoral_action: Holly uses the trash to make a huge mountain in her yard.
immoral_consequence: Holly's home owner's association sends her a letter in the mail fining her for the eyesore.

norm: It's rewarding to make a good decision.
situation: Harry has to decide if he should go to the dance or if he should watch the football game.
intention: Harry wants to made a decision.
moral_action: Harry makes up his mind by himself and decides what he'd have more fun doing.
moral_consequence: Harry has lots of fun at his chosen event and glad he made this decision.
immoral_action: Harry doesn't decide at all, but instead asks his wife to choose for him.
immoral_consequence: Harry goes on the choice she choose for him, and he doesn't have much fun.

norm: It's bad to push other people's buttons.
situation: Chris, who has a slightly older sister, is in the house one day and is bored.
intention: Chris wants to add some excitement to his life.
moral_action: Chris goes outside and attempts to climb up some fences and walls for fun.
moral_consequence: Chris improves his climbing skills and has a fun time climbing over things.
immoral_action: Chris gets a metal pot and begins banging it outside of his sister's door, just to get a reaction out of her.
immoral_consequence: Chris' sister gets very upset and throws things at Chris, hitting him in the head.

norm: It's romantic to buy someone flowers.
situation: Jane scheduled a date over a dating app and is currently shopping.
intention: Jane wants to buy something for her date.
moral_action: Jane decides to buy some roses for the date and gives them to her date.
moral_consequence: Jane and her date laugh about the flowers, but Jane's date is very impressed.
immoral_action: Jane decides to buy something boring, a box of cheap cookies, for her date.
immoral_consequence: Jane's date is surprised about the gift but not that impressed with Jane.

norm: It's not okay to not be productive in life.
situation: Helga receives an unexpected inheritance and finds herself extraordinarily wealthy.
intention: Helga wants to decide whether or not she should quit her job.
moral_action: Helga decides to cut her hours and pursue an education.
moral_consequence: Helga’s diligence rewards her with a fulfilling life and respect in the community.
immoral_action: Helga quits to enjoy a life of leisure and luxury.
immoral_consequence: Helga drifts into ennui and becomes socially shunned for her laziness.

norm: It's frowned upon to be lazy.
situation: Baxter arrives home from work tired, but he needs to do his taxes.
intention: Baxter wants to do something relaxing.
moral_action: Baxter turns on an episode of his favorite television show while he does his taxes.
moral_consequence: In his new relaxed state of mind Baxter makes several discoveries that save him some money.
immoral_action: Baxter takes a long nap followed by several rounds of his favorite video game.
immoral_consequence: Baxter is unable to finish his taxes in time.

norm: It's good for parents to give their children work.
situation: Mike's son Tony is complaining to Mike that he's bored out of his mind.
intention: Mike wants to suggest an activity for Tony.
moral_action: Mike tells Tony that he needs to go outside and mow the lawn and do other yard work.
moral_consequence: Tony learns the value of a good day of work and also gets a bunch of productive chores done.
immoral_action: Mike tells Tony that he should go find a movie to watch on Netflix.
immoral_consequence: Tony wastes his time watching films and does nothing productive with his day.

norm: It's wrong to judge another person based on their heritage.
situation: Rob's classmate, Greg, grew up in a wealthy family, and Rob doesn't know how to feel about this.
intention: Rob wants to say something to Greg.
moral_action: Rob tells Greg that he understands that it's hard for him to live up to his parents' expectations.
moral_consequence: Greg feels closer to Rob since he's willing to put himself in Greg's shoes.
immoral_action: Rob tells Greg that he doesn't have the work ethic needed to succeed.
immoral_consequence: Greg feels disrespected and feels bad that people are judging him because of his parents.

norm: It's wrong to steal something that isn't yours.
situation: Sun's favorite musician has just put out a new album that Sun has been dying to listen to.
intention: Sun wants to download the album.
moral_action: Sun decides to purchase the album from a digital store.
moral_consequence: Sun supports his favorite artist and gets to listen to their music on his smart phone.
immoral_action: Sun downloads the album for free via online torrenting.
immoral_consequence: Sun now has the entire album on his smartphone without having to pay for it.

norm: It's fun to go on a trip with your parent.
situation: Nadine, who has a brand new boyfriend wins a trip for two from a local game show she was on.
intention: Nadine wants to pick who to take with her.
moral_action: Nadine decides to take her mother with her as her guest for the trip.
moral_consequence: Nadine and her mother have a wonderful time and do a lot of great bonding.
immoral_action: Nadine decides to take her boyfriend with her as her guest for the trip.
immoral_consequence: Nadine does not have fun with the boyfriend as they barely know each other and the isolated vacation backfires.

norm: You should help out your coworkers if they need help.
situation: Hilda is a manager working on a work project with Tina when Tina tells her she does not know how to use the printer.
intention: Hilda wants to respond to Tina not knowing how to use the printer.
moral_action: Hilda tells Tina how to use the printer.
moral_consequence: Hilda and Tina's work project will go on uninterrupted.
immoral_action: Hilda tells Tina that she should search online if she wants to know how to use the printer.
immoral_consequence: Hilda and Tina's work project will be delayed because Hilda did not help with the printer.

norm: It's important to get the proper nutrition in your diet.
situation: Jacob has just finished eating dinner.
intention: Jacob wants to eat dessert.
moral_action: Jacob eats a fruit salad.
moral_consequence: Jacob feels comfortable about his body fat when he goes to the beach next week.
immoral_action: Jacob eats a piece of cake.
immoral_consequence: Jacob gains weight and has to exercise in his free time.

norm: You should apologize for being untruthful to others.
situation: Jim's girlfriend finds out that he lied to her and confronts him about it.
intention: Jim wants to react to his girlfriend about his lying.
moral_action: Jim say's he's sorry for lying to his girlfriend and admits that it was wrong.
moral_consequence: Jim's girlfriend has hope that Jim learned a lesson and that he will be more honest in the future.
immoral_action: Jim tells his girlfriend that him lying is not a big deal and that she should get over it.
immoral_consequence: Jim's girlfriend sees Jim as dishonest and loses a lot of trust in him.

norm: You should help people out that are down.
situation: On his drive over to the gym, Eric sees a homeless guy on the side of the road begging.
intention: Eric wants to go work out at the gym.
moral_action: Eric stops and buys the homeless man some food, then goes to work out.
moral_consequence: The homeless man feels grateful and satiated.
immoral_action: Eric ignores the man and drives quickly to the gym.
immoral_consequence: The homeless man feels sad and hungry.

norm: It's good to give an animal a home.
situation: Jamie lives alone and thinks a dog would be nice to have for companionship.
intention: Jamie wants to get a new dog.
moral_action: Jamie goes to the shelter to adopt a dog.
moral_consequence: The dog is rescued from being put down, and Jamie has a new friend.
immoral_action: Jamie abducts her neighbors’ dog from their home.
immoral_consequence: The dog is scared and upset, and Jamie ends up going to jail when her neighbors find out.

norm: Continuing to work when sick might make you sicker.
situation: Theresa is a workaholic, but has woken up with a sore throat and a runny nose and feels run down.
intention: Theresa wants to get over her illness.
moral_action: Theresa takes a few days off until her symptoms subside.
moral_consequence: Theresa gets over her illness in a few days and is able to get back to work at full strength.
immoral_action: Theresa goes to work despite her symptoms and works like nothing is wrong.
immoral_consequence: Theresa feels very run down and takes weeks to get over her illness.

norm: It's nice to host guests.
situation: Thanksgiving is coming and Sue's family is requesting to celebrate the festival at Sue's house.
intention: Sue wants to respond to the decision.
moral_action: Sue learns to cook a variety of food for the party and decorates her house.
moral_consequence: Sue's family thanks her for being nice and gives her a big gift to show their appreciation.
immoral_action: Sue tells her family that her house is not comfortable enough to accommodate the guests.
immoral_consequence: Sue's family feels bad and decides to cancel the celebration.

norm: It's wrong to threaten to hurt someone for any reason.
situation: Alex is in his car at a red light when Quincy, coming up from behind, rear ends his car, hard.
intention: Alex wants to show Quincy his displeasure.
moral_action: Alex gets out of the car and calmly tells Quincy that his driving was awful and his insurance will have to pay for everything.
moral_consequence: Quincy is remorseful and knows he's about to get a huge increase in insurance because of his mistake.
immoral_action: Alex gets out of the car and screams at Quincy telling him he's going to kill him.
immoral_consequence: Quincy is terrified and locks himself in his car before clumsily attempting to back up and drive away, almost killing a bystander.

norm: It's rude to fly drones at your neighbor's house.
situation: Ted enjoys taking videos and recently bought a new drone for filming.
intention: Ted wants to film his surroundings with his drone.
moral_action: Ted flies his drone around his own backyard for filming.
moral_consequence: Ted's neighbor will think that Ted knows his boundaries and limits.
immoral_action: Ted flies and films his drone around his neighbor's house.
immoral_consequence: Ted's neighbor will become with annoyed with him and think he is a creep.

norm: It's not okay to miss out on your weekly obligations
situation: Andy gets a telephone call from his soccer teammate that he has a weekly practice with who tells him to prepare for this week by working on his free kicks.
intention: Andy wants to respond to the request to work on his backhand.
moral_action: Andy tells his teammate that he'll make sure he comes to practice with some free kicks already under his belt.
moral_consequence: Andy's teammate is delighted with Andy's dedication and holds optimism for their season.
immoral_action: Andy tells his teammate he's not feeling great, and he probably won't make it to practice this week.
immoral_consequence: Andy's teammate is annoyed that Andy will miss practice and the team will fall behind and so will Andy making their season worse.

norm: Violence is not an acceptable way to handle issues.
situation: Robbie and his friend are competing in a game and Robbie's friend is winning.
intention: Robbie wants to prove he is a good competitor.
moral_action: Robbie continues to try his best despite the losing effort and is humble in defeat when he congratulates his friend.
moral_consequence: Robbie and his friend bond over the experience and enjoy themselves immensely.
immoral_action: Frustrated with the way the competition is going Robbie begins to get physical with his friend as a way to show he is still better despite losing.
immoral_consequence: Robbie's friend becomes annoyed by Robbie's poor sportsmanship, and they don't finish their competition.

norm: It's good to be supportive of people with depression.
situation: James' friend has cancelled most of their plans to hang out lately, and recently revealed it's because clinical depression leaves him with no energy.
intention: James wants to spend more time with his friend.
moral_action: James starts dropping by his friend's with a pizza to watch Netflix or just talk.
moral_consequence: James' friend starts to feel a little better and has a good time during their quiet nights in.
immoral_action: James keeps pressuring his friend to go to concerts and loud parties.
immoral_consequence: James' friend stops responding to James entirely because he feels overwhelmed.

norm: It's good to complete things that you started.
situation: Romeo is working on a final paper the night before it is due and needs to finish the concluding paragraph.
intention: Romeo wants to be done with the paper.
moral_action: Romeo presses forward, writes a conclusion, and sends the paper in before the deadline.
moral_consequence: The teacher reads the paper thoroughly and gives Romeo a good grade for the paper's completeness.
immoral_action: Romeo decides that he's done enough work, leaves out the concluding paragraph, and turns it in as-is.
immoral_consequence: The teacher notices that it is unfinished and gives Romeo a low grade.

norm: It is always nice to smile at people.
situation: Mike and Pam are at the beach separately until they notice each other.
intention: Mike wants to acknowledge Pam's presence.
moral_action: As the two look at each other, Mike flashes a grin and nods his head in acknowledgement.
moral_consequence: Pam smiles back and approaches Mike to catch up with each other.
immoral_action: As the two look each other, Mike turns his face to a scowl.
immoral_consequence: Pam feels some anxiety as she wonders what caused Mike to react that way.

norm: You should be respectful of your roommates.
situation: Hal’s new roommate, Ed, has turned out to be somewhat of a slob, prompting Hal to demand that Ed either cleans up his mess or moves out.
intention: Ed wants to react to Hal’s ultimatum.
moral_action: Ed apologizes to Hal, saying that he will do better, which he does.
moral_consequence: Ed continues to have a roof over his head and Hal keeps living with a friend.
immoral_action: Ed disregards Hal’s request and keeps being messy in common areas.
immoral_consequence: Ed gets kicked out and is now homeless with nowhere to put his belongings, which makes Hal feel guilty.

norm: It's good to pick up trash.
situation: Tate is at the beach with his family, and they have a lot of trash with them.
intention: Tate has to figure out what to do with their trash.
moral_action: Tate holds onto the trash until he finds a trash can to put it in.
moral_consequence: The animals in the ocean don't get anywhere near the trash, and they get to thrive.
immoral_action: Tate throws the trash in the ocean while the lifeguard isn't watching.
immoral_consequence: Animals in the ocean suffer, and it affects the entire marine ecosystem.

norm: You shouldn't spread rumors about others.
situation: Sarah hears a rumor that her friend is secretly gay and afraid to come out.
intention: Sarah wants to know her friend's sexuality.
moral_action: Sarah approaches her friend and tells him directly that she is an ally and open to talking without judgment.
moral_consequence: Sarah's friend feels validated and safe to come out to Sarah.
immoral_action: Sarah approaches her friend's sister and tells her about the rumor and asks if it might be true.
immoral_consequence: Sarah's friend overhears the conversation and feels betrayed by Sarah.

norm: You shouldn't get involved in criminal activities.
situation: Jamie is out with her group of friends on a hot day when they suggest breaking into a rooftop pool to cool off.
intention: Jamie wants to cool off with her friends.
moral_action: Jamie tells her friends that isn't a good idea, and suggests going to the lake instead.
moral_consequence: Jamie and her friends have a great time cooling off at the lake, and everyone stays out of trouble.
immoral_action: Jamie agrees and goes off with her friends to break into the pool.
immoral_consequence: They are all caught and fined for breaking and entering.

norm: It's bad to not honor your end of an agreement.
situation: Brian promised his friend Ted to help him with his math homework tonight but just got invited to a party.
intention: Brian wants to attend the party.
moral_action: Brian spends an hour helping Ted and then heads over to the party.
moral_consequence: Ted is grateful to Brian, understands the math much better and is able to finish his homework.
immoral_action: Brian skips out on his agreement to help Ted in favor of attending the party.
immoral_consequence: Ted is disappointed and upset that his friend let him down and is unable to finish his homework on time.

norm: It's bad to ask people to lie for you.
situation: Becca has been seeing someone outside of the relationship with her romantic partner.
intention: Becca wants to have an excuse if he starts asking around.
moral_action: Becca makes up her own excuse and simply asks her friends not to say anything at all.
moral_consequence: Becca's friends are relieved that they can stay out of it.
immoral_action: Becca asks her friends to tell her partner a made up story.
immoral_consequence: Becca's friends feel obligated to tell the partner a story that isn't true.

norm: It is good to help the environment by carpooling
situation: Lorna just purchased a brand new vehicle which she can't wait to drive.
intention: Lorna wants to test out the car and see how it drives during her commute.
moral_action: Lorna offers to drive the carpool this week and her week, so she can try out her car with her coworkers.
moral_consequence: Lorna drives two weeks consecutively and her coworkers are grateful, allowing Lorna to keep the group's favor and test out her new car.
immoral_action: Lorna tells her carpool group she won't be joining as its not her driving week, and she wants to drive her new car.
immoral_consequence: Lorna messes up the carpool schedule with her coworkers and drives her car to work instead, all on her own.

norm: You shouldn't comment on how messy someone's car is.
situation: Joe is getting a ride from his friend, who's car is messy.
intention: Joe wants to ride in a clean car.
moral_action: Joe offers to help his friend clean his car quickly before they leave.
moral_consequence: Joe's friend gratefully accepts, and they head out in a clean car.
immoral_action: Joe calls his friend a pig and demands he clean his car before he will get in.
immoral_consequence: Joe's friend leaves and refuses to give him a ride.

norm: You shouldn't expect someone to share their money with you.
situation: Jill asks Jim for some money for the down payment on a car, but Jim refuses.
intention: Jill wants to buy a car.
moral_action: Jill accepts Jim's refusal and takes a side job to save up for the car.
moral_consequence: Jill is able to buy her car with her own money.
immoral_action: Jill hounds Jim for the money and gets very angry and yells at him.
immoral_consequence: Jim cuts Jill out of her life, and Jill never gets her car.

norm: Celebrating with family is encouraged to keep familial bonds strong.
situation: Bradley wrote a book and received a prestigious award for it.
intention: Bradley wants to celebrate his award.
moral_action: Bradley goes out to dinner at a restaurant with family members.
moral_consequence: Bradley will be able to talk about his award with his family members.
immoral_action: Bradley goes out to dinner at a restaurant by himself.
immoral_consequence: Bradley will have no one to talk to about his award.

norm: You shouldn't get into arguments in public.
situation: Peter is lining up at a driver's license office to renew his license and a man cuts the line.
intention: Peter wants to react to the man cutting the line.
moral_action: Peter stays calm and reports the situation to the office staff .
moral_consequence: The office staff politely asks the man to go to the end of the line in order to be fair to the other people.
immoral_action: Peter confronts the man for cutting the line, and they start yelling at each other.
immoral_consequence: The office staff asks them to behave, or they will be expelled from the office.

norm: You shouldn't destroy someone's property.
situation: Fred hears shouting over at the neighbor's place and suspects that they are fighting.
intention: Fred wants to stop the fight.
moral_action: Fred shouts through the door if his neighbors need any helpl.
moral_consequence: The neighbors open the door and explain the situation, thanking Fred for caring.
immoral_action: Fred kicks down his neighbor's door, ready to help with any trouble.
immoral_consequence: His neighbors get angry at Fred for destroying their door.

norm: It's considered inappropriate to have two different valentine's day vaentines.
situation: Paul's best friend May asks him if he will still get her a Valentine's gift now that he has a girlfriend.
intention: Paul wants to answer May's question.
moral_action: Paul lets May know that it would be inappropriate for him to give her a gift as well.
moral_consequence: Paul avoids unnecessary strife in his relationship with his girlfriend.
immoral_action: Paul decides to go ahead and buy May a Valentines day gift.
immoral_consequence: Paul has a fight with his girlfriend when she finds out he gave May a gift too.

norm: You are expected to congratulate the winner of a competition.
situation: Dave's teammate wins a swimming competition and walks up to Dave afterwards.
intention: Dave wants to talk to his teammate who won the swimming competition.
moral_action: Dave congratulates his teammate for winning the swimming competition and tells them they deserve the win.
moral_consequence: Dave's teammate thinks Dave is being supportive of them by congratulating them for winning the swimming competition.
immoral_action: Dave talks to his teammate about school and doesn't even mention the swimming competition.
immoral_consequence: Dave's teammate thinks Dave must be jealous of them because he didn't congratulate them for winning the competition.

norm: It is bad to be greedy.
situation: Joe loves seafood and is excited to go to an all you can eat seafood buffet with his friends.
intention: Joe wants to eat as much as he can.
moral_action: Joe eats heartily but stops when he is filled.
moral_consequence: Joe is able to enjoy his meal fully and enjoy time with his friends.
immoral_action: Joe eats multiple servings of seafood, continuing to eat even when he is full.
immoral_consequence: Joe gets sick from overeating and has to go home to rest rather than hang out with his friends.

norm: It's wrong to cheat with your friends' partners.
situation: Carmen has just met her boyfriend's best friend Danny at a party.
intention: Carmen wants to have dinner with Danny.
moral_action: Carmen invites Danny over to have dinner with her and her boyfriend.
moral_consequence: Carmen's boyfriend enjoys spending time with his girlfriend and his best friend.
immoral_action: Carmen invites Danny on a dinner date when her boyfriend goes out of town.
immoral_consequence: When Carmen's boyfriend gets back into town he beats up his friend and breaks up with Carmen.

norm: You should not embarrass others in a group.
situation: Ann and Mary are attending a party and Ann is wearing a dress that Mary doesn't like.
intention: Mary wants to comment on Ann's dress.
moral_action: Mary tells Ann that a brighter dress suits her skin color more while they are in the bathroom.
moral_consequence: Ann thanks Mary for her good advice and feels confident in choosing her clothes in the future.
immoral_action: Mary says that Ann's dress makes her look older while they are chatting with other girls in the party.
immoral_consequence: Ann feels belittled and frustrated, so she decides to leave the party earlier.

norm: You shouldn't blame your kids for your divorce.
situation: Tim is in court because he has sued his wife for a divorce.
intention: Tim wants to get out of his marriage.
moral_action: Tim tells the judge that the reason for the divorce is that he and his wife have grown apart.
moral_consequence: The judge grants equal visitation rights to both Tim and  his wife, and they divorce amicably.
immoral_action: Tim tells the judge that his children have turned his wife against him and that's why he wants a divorce.
immoral_consequence: The judge grants the divorce but Tim's children never speak to him again.

norm: It's wrong to ignore people.
situation: Bob hears a knock at the door while trying to cook lunch.
intention: Bob wants to finish cooking lunch.
moral_action: Bob lets the person in and asks him to wait while he finishes cooking.
moral_consequence: The person at Bob's door patiently waits for Bob.
immoral_action: Bob ignores the knock and continues to cook.
immoral_consequence: The person at Bob's door gets upset, as it's obvious that Bob is home.

norm: It is wrong to cheat on your romantic partner.
situation: Sandra is in an unhappy relationship with Jeff who is emotionally abusive and uncaring.
intention: Sandra wants to experience a loving relationship.
moral_action: Sandra ends her relationship with Jeff with the help of her best friend and begins looking for a better partner.
moral_consequence: Sandra begins leading a healthier and more fulfilling life without Jeff.
immoral_action: Sandra begins an affair with Marnie who she meets online and makes her feel special.
immoral_consequence: Jeff lashes out violently against Sandra when he finds out about the affair.

norm: It's wrong to discriminate against trans people.
situation: Tara is a manager at a store and one of her employees has just quit.
intention: Tara wants to find a replacement.
moral_action: Tara interviews a trans and hires them based on their experience.
moral_consequence: The trans person feels accepted and does well at their job.
immoral_action: Tara interviews a trans person and denies them based on their sexuality.
immoral_consequence: The trans person feels discriminated against and seeks litigation.

norm: It's wrong to hurt small animals.
situation: Paul's neighbor's chiwawa dog barks all night while he tries to sleep.
intention: Paul wants to get the dog to be quite.
moral_action: Paul calls his neighbor about the noise.
moral_consequence: Paul's neighbor decides to keep the dog in a room in the back of the house where neighbors can no longer hear the barking.
immoral_action: Paul decides to shoot the dog dead.
immoral_consequence: Paul's neighbor calls the police and Paul is arrested.

norm: It's bad to be involved with someone who is married.
situation: Matt, who is single, meets two attractive women, one of them is married.
intention: Matt wants to be in a relationship.
moral_action: Matt asks the unmarried woman on a date, and they start seeing each other.
moral_consequence: The married woman goes back home to her husband.
immoral_action: Matt starts an affair with the married woman.
immoral_consequence: Matt's mistress' husband finds out about the affair and is devastated.

norm: It's wise to check a hotel bed for bed bugs.
situation: After a long late check in, Charles has just wheeled his suitcase into his hotel room in Las Vegas.
intention: Charles wants to go to sleep.
moral_action: Charles takes the sheets off the bed and inspects the mattress before getting into bed.
moral_consequence: Charles has a good nights sleep and wakes up refreshed.
immoral_action: Charles get into his pajamas, pulls back the cover and crawls into bed.
immoral_consequence: Charles wakes up in the morning with bug bites all over his legs.

norm: It's unacceptable to commit a crime.
situation: Jim is in dire need of money to pay off a bookie who is threatening to kill him.
intention: Jim needs to locate cash money as soon as possible.
moral_action: Jim calls up his mother and reluctantly begs her for a loan to get him out of trouble.
moral_consequence: Jim's mom agrees to help him out if he agrees not to deal with the bookie again and Jim is eternally grateful.
immoral_action: Jim runs into the gas station, punches the clerk, and takes money out of the cash register.
immoral_consequence: Jim is chased down by police a short while later and taken into custody and charged with assault and robbery.

norm: It's polite to excuse yourself after you burp.
situation: Megan is on a date with a cute boy named Darren when she burps, making her feel embarrassed.
intention: Megan wants to feel less embarrassed.
moral_action: Megan apologizes to Darren for burping and says it was an accident.
moral_consequence: Darren laughs at Megan's faux pas and sees her as down-to-earth and likable.
immoral_action: Megan doesn't acknowledge her burp and distracts herself and Darren by talking about her hobbies.
immoral_consequence: Darren thinks Megan is crude and has bad manners and decides he doesn't want to date her anymore.

norm: It's good to teach small children new things.
situation: James is in a zoom meeting and his son is asking for help to login to his computer.
intention: James needs to address his son's problem.
moral_action: James takes a moment to teach his son how to login to the computer and then goes back to his meeting.
moral_consequence: His son has learned a new skill.
immoral_action: James tells his son to be quiet and figure it out himself and goes back to his meeting.
immoral_consequence: His son cries because he can't fix it.

norm: It's wrong to do all the work in a relationship.
situation: Pam and Oscar live together in an apartment.
intention: Oscar wants the apartment to be maintained.
moral_action: Oscar and Pam divide up the daily tasks that they need to do.
moral_consequence: Oscar and Pam feel like they both contribute and are both happy.
immoral_action: Oscar does all of the household chores while Pam does nothing.
immoral_consequence: Oscar gets upset with Pam at the unfair arrangement.

norm: It's good to practice when you want to win something.
situation: David has a race coming up in a few weeks that he wants to win.
intention: He wants to prepare for the race.
moral_action: David trains hard every day for several weeks before the rade.
moral_consequence: David is well prepared from the training and wins the race.
immoral_action: David only trains one day before the race.
immoral_consequence: David is not in shape for the race and performs very poorly.

norm: Riding a skateboard recklessly in the public area is dangerous.
situation: Jeff likes to skateboard through the town square in front of everyone.
intention: Jeff wants to perform a trick to impress the towns people.
moral_action: Jeff jumps in place a couple of times while his skateboard is moving slowly.
moral_consequence: Jeff lands on his feet and is able to impress the crowd.
immoral_action: Jeff tries to skate down the tall steps of the town square.
immoral_consequence: Jeff falls down the steps and breaks both of his legs.

norm: It is rude to sneak around someone else's property.
situation: Lucy has just moved into a new neighborhood.
intention: Lucy wants to get to know her next door neighbor.
moral_action: Lucy rings the neighbor's doorbell and introduces herself.
moral_consequence: Lucy starts developing a friendly relationship with the neighbor.
immoral_action: Lucy tries to sneak around the neighbor's house and peek into their windows to see what they're like.
immoral_consequence: Lucy gets caught and her neighbor wants nothing to do with her because she violated their boundaries.

norm: You shouldn't just let people steal things.
situation: Diane is shopping at a department store and sees a woman putting a bracelet into her bag.
intention: Diane wants to react to the woman's behavior.
moral_action: Diane reports the case to an associate who then asks to check the woman's bag for the bracelet.
moral_consequence: The woman gets caught and arrested by the police.
immoral_action: Diane leaves the scene immediately because she doesn't want to get involved as a witness.
immoral_consequence: The woman takes the bracelet home and feels validated for her action.

norm: It's kind to return someone's lost wallet to them.
situation: Gretchen is walking down the street when she finds a wallet lying on the ground that belongs to a man named Jake.
intention: She wants to decide what to do with the wallet.
moral_action: Gretchen finds a phone number for Jake in the wallet and gives him a call, so she can return it.
moral_consequence: Jake is very grateful to Gretchen, and he gives her a twenty dollar reward.
immoral_action: Gretchen removes the cash from the wallet and discards the rest in a trash can.
immoral_consequence: Jake has to go through a lot of trouble cancelling his bank cards and getting new identification cards.

norm: It's not right to lie.
situation: Mario broke the bathroom mirror, and he was worried about what would happen to him.
intention: Mario wants to minimize the trouble he gets in.
moral_action: Mario is asked if he broke the mirror, and he admits he did.
moral_consequence: Mario's parents decide to go easy on him for telling the truth.
immoral_action: Mario is asked if he broke the mirror, and he claims that he didn't.
immoral_consequence: Mario manage to lie his way out of trouble but now he has to deal with guilt.

norm: It's important to not lose your purse.
situation: Liz was riding the bus to work, and she got into a video game, she lost track of her possessions on the bus.
intention: Liz has to make sure she gets all of her stuff before she gets off the bus.
moral_action: Liz shuts down her game before she gets to her bus stop and double checks that she has all of her things.
moral_consequence: Liz keeps all of her stuff together, and she still has her purse at the end of the day.
immoral_action: Liz keeps playing her game, oblivious to her surroundings, as she departs the bus.
immoral_consequence: Liz forgets to grab her purse and someone takes it before the bus gets back to the depot.

norm: It's good to give others work advice.
situation: Craig is working on a team with a new employee who is having difficulty working through an assignment that Craig knows how to do.
intention: Craig wants to make sure he doesn't get distracted from his own work.
moral_action: Craig offers to give the new employee some pointers during his break and after he finishes his work for the day.
moral_consequence: The new employee picks up their work pace thanks to Craig's advice, and they are able to complete their work in time.
immoral_action: Craig does not offer to help the new employee and spends his time focusing on his own assignments.
immoral_consequence: The new employee is unable to finish their assignment by the deadline, and they get reprimanded.

norm: It is wrong to make someone late.
situation: Mary's friend is driving them to work when she realizes that she needs to use the restroom.
intention: Mary wants to go to the bathroom.
moral_action: Mary waits until they get to work to use the bathroom that is there.
moral_consequence: Mary's friend is happy that she got to the job site on time.
immoral_action: Mary makes her friend pull over to the restroom, so she can go to the bathroom.
immoral_consequence: Mary's friend gets annoyed with her because she made her late to work.

norm: You shouldn't spend hours playing.
situation: Carole got a new game console at her birthday party and is excited to use it.
intention: Carole wants to start one of her new games.
moral_action: Carole offers her friends to take turns playing on her new console.
moral_consequence: Everyone at the party has a great time and nobody feels left out.
immoral_action: Carole retreats from her party guests and spends the rest of the time in her room playing with her new system.
immoral_consequence: Carole's friends feel left out and confused because she left her own birthday party.

norm: You should be honest and straight forward with people.
situation: Kit and Leo were planning a camping trip, but Kit would rather spend the weekend with his girlfriend.
intention: Kit doesn't want to disappoint Leo, who was looking forward to camping.
moral_action: Kit tells Leo that his girlfriend is in town, and he wants to spend time with her that weekend.
moral_consequence: Leo suggests they both bring their girlfriends on the camping trip, and everyone has a good time.
immoral_action: Kit goes on the trip with Leo, but ends up spending a lot of time on the phone with his girlfriend.
immoral_consequence: Kit's girlfriend is mad at him, and Leo feels that Kit was being distracted from their activity.

norm: Communication is important in a relationship.
situation: Ned and Kati have been fighting a lot lately, and Ned is worried about the relationship.
intention: Ned wants to figure out what's going on.
moral_action: Ned asks Kati what's been happening, why they can't seem to be happy anymore.
moral_consequence: Kati says she doesn't know, but she wants to work on it and loves Ned.
immoral_action: Ned screams at Kati one day asking her what's wrong with her.
immoral_consequence: Kati retaliates and screams back at him, and they get no further.

norm: It's unlawful to take a pet from its rightful owner.
situation: John finds a dog in his yard, and the dog has tags with the address and phone number of its owners.
intention: John wants to find a home for the dog.
moral_action: John returns the dog to its owners.
moral_consequence: The dog's owners allow John to visit the dog about once a week.
immoral_action: John decides to adopt the dog into his own home keeping the dog in the backyard.
immoral_consequence: The neighbors spot the dog and alert its owner who threaten legal action against John.

norm: It's good to encourage your partner's art.
situation: Kevin's girlfriend Lara just finished a poor quality watercolor painting, and he's responding to her question about what he thinks of it.
intention: Kevin wants to be honest about his dislike of the painting.
moral_action: Kevin encourages Lara to keep trying because there are multiple parts of the painting that could be improved with further effort.
moral_consequence: Lara takes Kevin's advice into consideration and manages to substantially improve the painting.
immoral_action: Kevin tells Lara that he's not really a fan of the painting and that she should perhaps try and pursue a different hobby.
immoral_consequence: Lara feels very discouraged, her feelings are hurt, and she starts crying.

norm: It's bad to mock someone online.
situation: Kairi reads an ignorant post by someone on Twitter.
intention: Kairi wants to interact with the post.
moral_action: Kairi shows the post to her friend, and she likes her friend's post.
moral_consequence: Kairi is thanked by her friend group for sharing the tweet with them.
immoral_action: Kairi retweets the tweet with a comment about the poster's intelligence in a sarcastic tone.
immoral_consequence: Kairi is attacked by the original poster's followers for her words.

norm: It's nice when we can work and help people too.
situation: Pete wants to become a teacher, but he knows he'll get paid more to become a banker.
intention: Pete wants to decide what career he should pick.
moral_action: Pete decides to become a teacher at his old high school.
moral_consequence: Pete gets to work and help people at the same time and feels fulfilled.
immoral_action: Pete decides to become a banker, because he doesn't want to struggle.
immoral_consequence: Pete doesn't help anyone and is just focused on making money.

norm: It's rude to judge people who watch anime.
situation: John meets Bill for the firs time and in introducing himself Bill mentions that he enjoys watching Anime.
intention: John wants to respond to Bill's statement.
moral_action: John tells Bill that he doesn't really enjoy watching Anime himself but that it's nice that Bill has something he loves, which is important in life.
moral_consequence: Bill is happy that John seems like an understanding fellow and is eager to get to know him better.
immoral_action: John tells Bill that Anime is basically a cartoon and cartoons are for children and adult idiots.
immoral_consequence: Bill feels incredibly disrespected and also begins to feel sad and insecure about his hobby.

norm: It's mean to make jokes about disabled people.
situation: Jim is hanging out with a group of friends having a good time.
intention: Jim wants to tell a joke.
moral_action: Jim makes a funny joke about a sports team and their fans.
moral_consequence: His friend's explode with laughter making Jim feel very good about himself.
immoral_action: Jim makes a very insensitive joke about people with Autism.
immoral_consequence: Jim is called an ableist jerk by his friend's, and he immediately feels regret and shame.

norm: You shouldn't lay guilt trips on people.
situation: Maxwell's wife is a homemaker and Maxwell thinks she should always clean up after him when he gets home from his construction job.
intention: Maxwell wants to avoid doing chores when he gets home from work.
moral_action: Maxwell makes a deal with his wife that he won't do evening housekeeping during the work week but will do whatever she asks on the weekend.
moral_consequence: Maxwell's wife is happy with their arrangement and gets Maxwell to do important tasks when he's off.
immoral_action: Maxwell tells his wife that his job is much more difficult than hers, so he doesn't help her when he arrives home after working.
immoral_consequence: Maxwell's wife feel she is insignificant and withdraws from Maxwell in their marriage.

norm: It is wrong to defraud somebody about your appearance.
situation: Alvin is chatting with Beth, a woman he met on a virtual dating site.
intention: Alvin wants to send Beth a picture.
moral_action: Alvin sends Beth a picture of himself even though he is worried she won't like his appearance.
moral_consequence: Beth thinks Alvin looks nice in his picture, and she is happy when they eventually meet in person.
immoral_action: Alvin sends Beth a picture of his younger, athletic cousin and claims it is a picture of himself.
immoral_consequence: Beth is angry later on when they meet in person, and she realizes Alvin deceived her.

norm: It's mean to wish death upon someone.
situation: Becky gets into fights with her mother about Becky's unconventional clothing style.
intention: Becky wants her mother to understand how stifled she feels.
moral_action: Becky resolves to calmly discuss what her choice of clothing means with her mother.
moral_consequence: Becky is better able to get her feelings across to her mother, and they are able to reach a compromise.
immoral_action: During a fight Becky angrily tells her mother to drop dead if she can't accept her self-expression.
immoral_consequence: Becky is remorseful because her words make her mother cry.

norm: You should eat dinner with your family.
situation: Tom and his family ran into some of his coworkers at a restaurant when out for dinner.
intention: Tom wanted to talk about problems he'd been having at work.
moral_action: Tom invited his coworkers to join him and his family for dinner.
moral_consequence: Tom's family learned about the stress he and his coworkers were under.
immoral_action: Tom sat at a table with this coworkers leaving his family alone at another table.
immoral_consequence: Tom's family gave him the cold shoulder on the way home.

norm: It's rude to wake up someone who is sleeping.
situation: Simon returns home from work and sees that his wife is asleep after a 12-hour shift at the hospital.
intention: Simon wants to eat dinner.
moral_action: Simon looks up a recipe online and cooks some pasta for dinner.
moral_consequence: Simon eats his dinner and saves some for his wife when she wakes up.
immoral_action: Simon wakes up his wife and asks her to make dinner.
immoral_consequence: Simon's wife gets mad at him for waking her up, and she just goes back to bed.

norm: People shouldn't need to qualify their gender to others.
situation: Mary sees Jake approaching multiple single stall bathrooms and needs to go at the same time Jake is.
intention: Mary wants to know which bathroom Jake is going into.
moral_action: Mary asks which bathroom Jake is going into directly instead of asking about gender, and Jake tells her.
moral_consequence: Jake appreciates Mary's courtesy and doesn't make Mary wait long.
immoral_action: Mary asks Jake what his gender is to determine which bathroom they will enter, and Jake says which one.
immoral_consequence: Jake becomes mad at Mary for asking about their gender.

norm: It's wrong to give up on your children.
situation: Darrell has son named Gerald who is doing poorly in school.
intention: Darrell wants to give advice to Gerald about school.
moral_action: Darrell tells Gerald he needs to study more and work harder to achieve.
moral_consequence: Gerald will apply himself more and try to reach his full potential.
immoral_action: Darrell tells Gerald that school is a dead end for him, and he won't get better at it.
immoral_consequence: Gerald will not be able to reach his full potential.

norm: It's rude to try and control everything your partner does.
situation: Anna is at home with her partner who has informed them of an invitation to go to a friend's house.
intention: Anna wants to stay in tonight.
moral_action: Anna expresses to her partner that she doesn't want to leave the house and leaves her partner's decision up to them.
moral_consequence: Anna's partner spends some time at home with Anna before heading out to the friend's house and the couple is happy.
immoral_action: Anna informs her partner that she doesn't want to go out tonight and makes it clear that that means them too.
immoral_consequence: Anna's partner reluctantly stays home and grows to resent Anna which doesn't bode well for the relationship.

norm: It’s bad to deceive people.
situation: Jill has a lot of homework to do.
intention: Jill wants to be done with her homework.
moral_action: Jill buckles down and finishes her homework herself.
moral_consequence: Jill turns in her homework and does better in class.
immoral_action: Jill calls her friend and copies her friend's homework.
immoral_consequence: The teacher sees that they have identical homework and punishes Jill.

norm: It is wrong to perform a medical procedure without consent.
situation: Dr. Doom recommended a few surgeries be preformed on the patient, but they declined some of them.
intention: Dr. Doom wants the patient to live.
moral_action: Dr. Doom recommends other treatments for the issues if the patient doesn't want surgery.
moral_consequence: The patient is willing to try some of the other treatments recommended by the doctor.
immoral_action: Dr. Doom preforms all the surgeries he reccomends anyway.
immoral_consequence: Dr. Doom ends up defending against a malpractice lawsuit.

norm: You shouldn't leave someone who needs your support.
situation: Bill is a wealthy banker who just got into a big argument with his wife.
intention: Bill doesn't want to argue anymore.
moral_action: Bill admits that his wife was right in the argument in order to get along with her.
moral_consequence: Bill's wife no longer has to worry about Bill leaving her and feels content.
immoral_action: Bill divorces his wife and fights to make his divorce settlement as low as possible.
immoral_consequence: Bill's wife struggles since she relied on Bill's income to support her lifestyle.

norm: It's wrong to envy what others have.
situation: Chris has just got a brand new sports car and brings it to his friend John's house to show him.
intention: John wants to make his feelings on the car known.
moral_action: John tells Chris that the car is incredible and that everyone should be proud to own a car like that.
moral_consequence: Chris is delighted that John loves his new car and agrees with John that he should take pride in it.
immoral_action: John tells Chris that the car is nothing special and John's 1988 Hyundai Excel is just as good of a car if not better.
immoral_consequence: Chris thinks that John is being absurd and that he's jealous of his car and lashing out at him.

norm: It's good to eat with other people.
situation: Matt is away at a professional conference that is required for his job and it's now his lunch break.
intention: Matt wants to relax and take his mind off of work.
moral_action: Matt takes a seat at table with some friendly looking strangers and starts eating the lunch he packed.
moral_consequence: Matt engages in conversation with the people at the table and ends up enjoying himself.
immoral_action: Matt finds a private spot in a nearby parking lot and eats his lunch alone while listening to music.
immoral_consequence: Matt feels momentarily refreshed, but he doesn't make any new professional connections at the conference.

norm: It is rude to demand free services from others.
situation: Karen is a customer who has multiple lines for a telecommunications company.
intention: Karen wants to make sure that she is getting the best deal.
moral_action: Karen checks for the best deals online and only calls if she needs help.
moral_consequence: Karen has a good phoen and service and does not pay a high bill.
immoral_action: Karen calls in dozens of time a week escalting to manager while demanding free service and credits.
immoral_consequence: Karen is given a cease and desist letter and must now only speak to executive relations.

norm: You shouldn't forbid your children from talking to you.
situation: Art establishes a rule  with children.
intention: Art wants to raise and be the leader of his family.
moral_action: Art sets an open door policy with his kids telling him that he is always there to talk even if he will be disappointed in what they do.
moral_consequence: Art develops a strong bond with all of his kids and now spends his days with his grandchildren.
immoral_action: "Art set a ""do not speak unless spoken to"" policy with his kids and punishes them strictly when they violate it."
immoral_consequence: The kidsrefuse to stay in touch with him as soon as they move out, and he is lonely when he gets old.

norm: It's good to get upset when someone wrongs you.
situation: Fred gets picked on by Luke every day after school.
intention: Fred wants Luke to stop.
moral_action: Fred yells and angrily demands that Fred stop.
moral_consequence: Luke leaves Fred alone for the yest of the school year.
immoral_action: Fred kindly asks Luke to stop picking on him.
immoral_consequence: Luke laughs and continues to pick on Fred.

norm: It is wrong to judge someone for their relationship preferences.
situation: Aaron is holding a party and found out that his neighbor is in an open relationship.
intention: Aaron wants to ask his neighbor a question.
moral_action: Aaron asks his neighbor whether being in an open relationship has made him closer to his wife.
moral_consequence: Aaron's neighbor respects that Aaron cares about his life so much and is willing to answer the question.
immoral_action: Aaron asks his neighbor whether he or not he's scared of commitment.
immoral_consequence: Aaron's neighbor feels disrespected and doesn't like that Aaron is asking personal questions.

norm: It is wrong not to pay for a service.
situation: Joe was going to the barber shop when he realized he forgot his wallet.
intention: Joe wanted to get his hair cut.
moral_action: Joe turned around and got his wallet before going back to the barber shop.
moral_consequence: Joe got a nice hair cut and got his hair cut there every month.
immoral_action: When it came time to pay, Joe dashed out the door.
immoral_consequence: Joe was banned from the barber shop for life and arrested.

norm: It's good to sleep when you are tired.
situation: Eric has an exam in a few days and hasn't studied at all.
intention: Eric wants to study hard the night before the exam.
moral_action: Eric studies intensely the night before and then gets some sleep too.
moral_consequence: Eric stays awake during the exam and does better.
immoral_action: Eric pops caffeine pills all night long studying.
immoral_consequence: Eric falls asleep during the exam.

norm: It's not okay to embarrass your friends.
situation: Erin is hanging out with a group of friends, and they are sharing stories.
intention: Erin wants to bring up a private story about her friend.
moral_action: Erin waits until she's alone with the friend and brings up the story in private with her.
moral_consequence: Erin's friend remembers the story and has a good laugh about it.
immoral_action: Erin brings up the story to the group to make them laugh.
immoral_consequence: Erin's friend becomes very embarrassed that the group finds out about the incident.

norm: It's wrong to ask someone about their sexual fetishes.
situation: Rob notices his cashier at the grocery store is very attractive.
intention: Rob wants to flirt with his cashier.
moral_action: Rob asks his cashier if she's like to get dinner sometime.
moral_consequence: The cashier is flattered and gives Rob her number.
immoral_action: Rob asks his cashier if she's into BDSM.
immoral_consequence: The cashier is extremely uncomfortable with Rob's question.

norm: It's cruel to intentionally scare others.
situation: Evelyn, who has a heart condition, has her prankster grandson, Evan over at her house.
intention: Evan wants to play a joke on Evelyn.
moral_action: Evan decides to put fake poop on Evelyn's bed, and later on she finds it.
moral_consequence: Evelyn says it's gross, but her and Evan both laugh together.
immoral_action: Evan hides in Evelyn's closet and when she opens it, he jumps out.
immoral_consequence: Evelyn is so startled that she has a heart attack and now Evan feels awful.

norm: It is rude to not tip in certain situations.
situation: Sarah is eating dinner at a local Italian restaurant before going to a movie.
intention: Sarah wants to pay the bill so she can leave.
moral_action: Sarah leaves an extra ten dollars with her payment.
moral_consequence: Sarah's server is happy to receive a generous tip.
immoral_action: Sarah pays the bill with exact change and leaves no tip.
immoral_consequence: Sarah's server loses money from waiting on Sarah.

norm: People shouldn't give others food they've fouled without telling them.
situation: Bobby and his friend James are eating lunch at their favorite restaurant.
intention: Bobby wants to have lunch with his friend James.
moral_action: Bobby offers to pick up his and  James' food from the counter and brings it back to their table for both of them to finish.
moral_consequence: Bobby and James have a nice lunch and head back to their houses after.
immoral_action: Bobby offers to pick up his and James' food from the counter and adds a ghost pepper on James burger without his knowledge while finishing his own.
immoral_consequence: Bobby finishes all his food and notices that James is having an allergic reaction to the pepper, sending him to the hospital and ruining their friendship.

norm: It's not okay to unnecessarily inconvenience people.
situation: Becky has always called her brother whenever she needs help, but now that he is married he has less time for her.
intention: Becky wants her brother to cater to her needs.
moral_action: Becky hires a handyman to help her fix things around the house in order to give her brother a break.
moral_consequence: Becky is proud to find that she can manage without her brothers constant support.
immoral_action: Becky nags her brother into coming over to replace a fuse in the middle of the night.
immoral_consequence: Becky feels guilty when she later finds out that her brother and his wife got into an argument over the incident.

norm: It is wrong to touch people inappropriately
situation: Daniel is sitting next to Rita and notices a bee on her chest that Rita doesn't see.
intention: Daniel doesn't want Rita to be stung.
moral_action: Daniel tells Rita that she has a bee on her chest.
moral_consequence: Rita brushes away the bee and thanks Daniel for letting her know.
immoral_action: Daniel reaches out to brush the bug away but also touches Rita's breast.
immoral_consequence: Rita feels violated, slaps Daniel and runs away.

norm: It's polite to be thankful for the kindness of strangers.
situation: Fred, a stranger, helps Tina load some very heavy bags of dog food into the back of her car.
intention: Tina wants to tell Fred that she doesn't need anymore help from him.
moral_action: Tina thanks Fred for his help and tells him that if he hadn't been there for her, she couldn't have done it herself.
moral_consequence: Fred feels valued and useful and stops to help a person with a flat tire on the way home.
immoral_action: Tina tells Fred that she wishes he'd loaded the dog food into her car faster, but that he can go now.
immoral_consequence: Fred feels unappreciated and vows not to help anymore strangers because they don't deserve it.

norm: It's normal to have opinions.
situation: David attends a parent conference of his son's school and an after-conference survey is handed to him for completion.
intention: David wants to complete the after-conference survey.
moral_action: David answers every question carefully and honestly describes his viewpoints.
moral_consequence: The school acts on his feedback and works on improving the next parent conference.
immoral_action: David does not want to upset the speaker and answers every question favorably in a biased way.
immoral_consequence: The school finds that his answers are biased and his survey does not provide valuable feedback.

norm: It is bad not to help out around the house
situation: Danny is playing video games on his computer while his mother cleans their home and does his chores.
intention: Danny wants to feel accomplished.
moral_action: Danny does all of his chores by the end of the day.
moral_consequence: Danny feels proud of the hard work he's done.
immoral_action: Danny goes on a winning streak against his online opponents.
immoral_consequence: His mother gets frustrated at Danny and grounds him for ignoring his chores.

norm: It's nice for children to help their parents out
situation: Hank is at home just relaxing when his dad Tony calls him and asks him to come over and help him do some garden work.
intention: Hank wants to respond to his dad's request for help.
moral_action: Hank tells his dad that he needs to change into something less fancy, and he'll be right over.
moral_consequence: Tony is delighted that Hank will help him and relieved he won't have to do all the work himself.
immoral_action: Hank tells his dad that gardening is hard, and he's relaxing, so he can't really help him now.
immoral_consequence: Tony is annoyed that he can't get his son to come help him when he needs it and hangs up.

norm: It's wrong to skip school.
situation: A new phone that Erica wants is being released on Thursday and people have already started camping outside the store to buy it.
intention: Erica wants to buy the phone as soon as possible.
moral_action: Erica pre-orders the phone online and pays extra so it will be delivered to her when it's available.
moral_consequence: Erica stays on track with her studies and is able to conveniently obtain the phone.
immoral_action: Erica doesn't go to school on Wednesday or Thursday, so she can wait outside the store.
immoral_consequence: Erica falls behind in her classes and has to work extra hard to catch up with her classmates.

norm: You shouldn't let your dog bite your family members.
situation: Patty has a dog, Spot, that is known to be a bit rowdy with the family.
intention: Patty wants the dog to play with people.
moral_action: Patty trains the dog to be less aggressive, while still being playful.
moral_consequence: Patty's dog and the family get along well and have many happy years together.
immoral_action: Patty ignores the dog's increasing aggression, and tells them that the biting is just play.
immoral_consequence: The dog bites one of the kids hard enough to require medical attention, and Spot must be put down.

norm: It's not okay to steal things that aren't yours.
situation: Mark wants to take up bike riding to get some exercise.
intention: Mark wants to get a new bike.
moral_action: Mike saves up his money and buys a new bike.
moral_consequence: Mike enjoys riding the bike every day.
immoral_action: Mike takes his neighbor's new bike and keeps it as his own.
immoral_consequence: Mike is arrested for theft after his neighbor calls the police.

norm: You shouldn't let others change a contract.
situation: Fred has a contract with his brother George about who does what chores that is being discussed.
intention: Fred wants to finish the discussion.
moral_action: Fred doesn't allow George to change the contract, insisting they need to stick by it.
moral_consequence: Fred and George abide by the original contract and get used to silently following it.
immoral_action: Fred lets George change the contract as long as they both agree to the changes.
immoral_consequence: Effectively this leads to a new contract discussion every time one of them doesn't feel like doing a chore.

norm: It's wrong to be jealous of other people.
situation: Phil was jealous that one of the jocks was trying to take his girlfriend.
intention: Phil wants to decide what to do about his jealously.
moral_action: Phil ignores these feelings and continues on with his life.
moral_consequence: Phil still has his girlfriend a few years later when the jocks graduate.
immoral_action: Phil acts rudely to all the jocks whenever they are around.
immoral_consequence: Phil's girlfriend dumps him for his rude behavior.

norm: You are expected to be polite to service workers.
situation: Larry is having dinner at a restaurant when he notices that the meal he received is not what he ordered.
intention: Larry wants to get the correct meal.
moral_action: Larry calls over the waitress and asks her to please switch out his meal for what he originally ordered.
moral_consequence: The restaurant manager comes over to the table after the meal and apologizes profusely, giving Larry a coupon for his next visit.
immoral_action: Larry calls over the waitress and yells at her loudly while demanding she bring him what he ordered.
immoral_consequence: The restaurant manager notices Larry's behavior and asks him to leave the restaurant because he's bothering the other patrons.

norm: It is nice to send letters to your friend.
situation: Travis is at home missing his friend who is deployed overseas.
intention: Travis wants miss his friend less.
moral_action: Travis decides to start writing his friend every week to keep him updated on everything going on at home.
moral_consequence: Travis's friend looks forward to the letters every week, and they help him get through his deployment.
immoral_action: Travis decides to go out with other friends to distract himself from his friend who is overseas.
immoral_consequence: Since Travis doesn't catch up with his friend, his friend feels lonely overseas.

norm: It is wrong to disrespect people you live with.
situation: Henry's roommate Jill comes home in a new dress and asks Henry what he thinks of it?
intention: Henry wants to answer Jill's question.
moral_action: Henry ells Jill that the dress looks nice and that it compliments her eyes.
moral_consequence: Jill is delighted that Henry has complimented her and that he said nice things about her eyes and dress.
immoral_action: Henry tells Jill that the dress looks horrible on her as do most things since she's so fat.
immoral_consequence: Jill feels incredibly insulted and begins to fear living with Henry any longer.

norm: It's bad parenting to raise your children to be violent.
situation: Johnny's son Jimmy has been getting picked on at school and Johnny is concerned about him.
intention: Johnny wants to give Jimmy some advice.
moral_action: Johnny tells Jimmy if someone says something mean to him, try and find some common ground to start a positive relationship.
moral_consequence: Jimmy grows up being a kind, understanding and gentle soul who everybody loves to be around.
immoral_action: Johnny tells Jimmy if someone says something mean to him, he should stick up for himself and start a fight.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy grows up starting fights with everyone who gets on his bad side, and people are afraid of him.

norm: It's kind to feed your friends.
situation: Liam and John are hanging out at Liam's house when Liam starts to feel hungry.
intention: Liam wants to get some food.
