situation: John copied a story that he found online for an overdue creative writing assignment, and was asked by his teacher how he came up with such unique plot.
intention: John wants to answer the teacher's question.
moral_action: John reluctantly admits to the teacher that he ran out of time, so he copied and pasted that whole story and none of it is his work.
moral_consequence: The teacher tells John what he did is terrible but that since he was honest she will give him an extension to come up with something original.
immoral_action: John tells the teacher he leaned on some past memories and experiences to come up with the plot.
immoral_consequence: The teacher finds out John lied and gives him a failing grade for plagiarism.

norm: It's mean to hit a bear with a guitar.
situation: Joe was camping in Montana with his band when he came across a black bear.
intention: Joe wanted to scare away the black bear.
moral_action: Joe and his band mates make a lot of noise to shoo the bear away.
moral_consequence: The bear doesn't want to mess with them, so he decides to leave.
immoral_action: Joe grabbed his guitarist's guitar and hit the bear with it.
immoral_consequence: The bear suffers a concussion and doesn't understand why he was hit.

norm: It's bad to exercise to the point of injury.
situation: Anthony is very overweight, and is told by a doctor he needs to get healthier.
intention: Anthony wants to shed a lot of weight.
moral_action: Anthony consults a nutritionist on some lifestyle changes he can make over time.
moral_consequence: Anthony starts losing weight in a healthy manner, changing his entire life around.
immoral_action: Anthony starts off doing extreme workouts with no experience whatsoever.
immoral_consequence: Anthony triggers a heart attack, and passes away from it.

norm: It's expected that you stand up for your significant other.
situation: Charlie is at a party with his wife Karen, when one of the guests, Frank says Karen is fat.
intention: Charlie wants to respond to Frank's statement.
moral_action: Charlie tells Frank that he can't talk about his wife that way unless he want's to rumble.
moral_consequence: Karen is delighted that Charlie is defending her honor against the insulting stranger.
immoral_action: Charlie tells Frank that it's true, Karen is fat and could stand to lose some weight.
immoral_consequence: Karen is not only insulted by her weight being discussed  but is also angry with Charlie for agreeing with Frank.

norm: You shouldn't refuse to help a friend in need.
situation: Mario is listening to a hockey game on the radio when he gets a call from Luigi to pick him up from the airport.
intention: Mario wants to listen to the game.
moral_action: Mario listens to the game in the car while driving to the airport.
moral_consequence: Luigi thanks Mario, and they listen to the hockey game together.
immoral_action: Mario tells Luigi to take a taxi and continues listening to the game.
immoral_consequence: Luigi calls Mario selfish for choosing a hockey game over him.

norm: You shouldn't date your teachers.
situation: Joe has a close relationship with an attractive professor who is expressing a romantic interest in him.
intention: Joe wants to find someone to date.
moral_action: Joe turns down his teacher and finds someone off of a dating app.
moral_consequence: The professor is able to maintain a more professional relationship with Joe.
immoral_action: Joe decides to ask his professor to be his girlfriend.
immoral_consequence: Word gets out and the professor gets in trouble with the school that she works for.

norm: You shouldn't make fun of someone's likes.
situation: Susan loves painting ceramic frogs, but her husband David finds it to be a very boring hobby.
intention: David wants Susan to pick a hobby that he would enjoy doing with her.
moral_action: David asks Susan if she would be willing to try something new, with him, that they could do in their spare time together.
moral_consequence: Susan thinks of some things that they might like to do together and David likes some of them very much, and they spend more time together.
immoral_action: David tells Susan directly that he finds her choice of hobbies to be beneath her and ridiculous, that it's boring, and he wants her to find something else to do.
immoral_consequence: Susan is offended by David's remarks, and she is unwilling to switch to a new hobby that they can do together.

norm: It is okay to speak up when something is wrong.
situation: Tobias just started a new job when he hears his boss give a coworker very bad advice.
intention: Tobias wants to make a good impression.
moral_action: Tobias walks over and suggests an alternative to his boss and the coworker.
moral_consequence: Tobias' boss praises him for the great idea and offers him a promotion the following month.
immoral_action: Tobias doesn't say anything because he is afraid challenging his bosses advice will leave a bad impression.
immoral_consequence: Tobias' coworker follows the advice and ends up losing a valuable client.

norm: It's wrong to break up somebody's marriage
situation: Katie is having an affair with Dan who is married to Jill.
intention: Katie wants to be in a relationship.
moral_action: Katie realizes that there are children involved, breaks up with Dan and starts dating a single man.
moral_consequence: Katie's relationship with her new boyfriend hurts no one, and they become engaged.
immoral_action: Katie tells Dan to leave his wife for her.
immoral_consequence: Dan divorces his wife and his children grow up in a broken home.

norm: It is wrong to yell at children.
situation: Fran teaches kindergarten to a rowdy group of kids.
intention: Fran wants her students to settle down for class.
moral_action: Fran comes up with engaging activities that get her students full attention.
moral_consequence: Fran is able to control her class effectively.
immoral_action: Fran yells at her students until they take their seats and quiet down.
immoral_consequence: Fran is cautioned by the principle for scaring her students.

norm: It's wrong to refuse to pay rent.
situation: Will rents an apartment during the COVID-19 pandemic and hears about a pause in rent payments for those who can't pay.
intention: Will wants to decide when he should pay rent.
moral_action: Will tells his landlord that he'll keep paying rent on time, even though he doesn't have to.
moral_consequence: Will's landlord is thankful and keeps Will as a tenant for as long as possible.
immoral_action: Will tells his landlord that he won't pay rent until the pause in rent payments is over.
immoral_consequence: Will's landlord stops trusting Will and evicts him at the first possible opportunity.

norm: You should dress professionally at work
situation: Keith is getting ready for work in his bedroom and is looking at his closet of clothes.
intention: Keith wants to decide what to wear to work.
moral_action: Keith decides to put on his gray suit with a white shirt and blue tie before going to work.
moral_consequence: Keith's boss sees Keith and thinks that he looks quite sharp that morning.
immoral_action: Keith decides to put on short biker spandex shorts and a sleeveless tanktop before going to work.
immoral_consequence: Keith's boss is angry that Keith came to work looking like he's going to the gym and sends him home to change.

norm: It's inconsiderate to make someone homeless.
situation: Betty is very unhappy in her marriage.
intention: Betty wants to leave her husband.
moral_action: Betty sits down and talks with her husband and lets him know she is considering leaving him.
moral_consequence: Her husband feels the same way, and they make plans to separate once he can locate other living arrangements.
immoral_action: Betty moves all her husbands stuff out of the house while he is at work and changes the locks.
immoral_consequence: Betty's husband calls the police, and she is charged with an illegal eviction.

norm: It's good to take your kids places.
situation: Mike tells his dad Earl that he has a day off from school on Monday and asks his dad if he wants to do something together.
intention: Earl wants to suggest something for the two of them to do.
moral_action: Earl tells Mike he is going to take him to the zoo that day to see the fun animals.
moral_consequence: Mike has fun looking at the animals and learns a lot of facts about nature.
immoral_action: Earl tells Mike that there's a movie marathon on TV that day, and they can spend the whole day watching.
immoral_consequence: Mike has fun watching TV but gains no experiences from the day and learns to be lazy.

norm: You should always finish your homework.
situation: Don has just finished eating his dinner and goes up to his room.
intention: Don wants to get ready for school the next day.
moral_action: Don opens his textbooks and studies them, then completes his homework assignments for the week.
moral_consequence: Don gets a good grade in all his classes.
immoral_action: Don starts going thru is his clothing to pick out the perfect matching outfit to wear to school.
immoral_consequence: Don forgets to do his homework and gets a low mark from his teacher.

norm: It's not okay to throw things sometimes things get broke.
situation: Kit is sitting on the couch and his girlfriend Lilly asks him if she can use the remote to see what's on TV for them to watch.
intention: Kit wants to give Lilly the remote.
moral_action: Kit gets up off the couch and hands the remote to Lilly.
moral_consequence: Kit and Lilly are able to flip through the channels to find a show to watch.
immoral_action: Kit throws the remote across the room in hopes Lilly will catch it, but she misses and it breaks.
immoral_consequence: Kit and Lilly no longer have a working remote and can't watch what they want.

norm: You shouldn't be with a spouse that cheats on you.
situation: Macy caught her husband cheating months ago and is having trouble moving past it.
intention: Macy wants to talk to her husband about the incident.
moral_action: Macy and her husband talk about the cheating, and she tells him she wants a divorce.
moral_consequence: Macy gets divorced and finally doesn't have to worry whether or not her husband is being faithful.
immoral_action: Macy and her husband talk about the infidelity, and he reassures her it was a mistake that will never happen again.
immoral_consequence: Macy stays with her husband but suffers because she never fully trusts him again.

norm: You should not disturb someone when they are at work.
situation: James often has friends over for beers while his wife Samantha works from home.
intention: James wants to include Samantha in the fun.
moral_action: James makes sure to wait until Samantha is finished with work to tell her about all the fun he had.
moral_consequence: Samantha is able to do her work in peace and without disruptions.
immoral_action: James runs into Samantha's office anytime something funny happens to tell her about it.
immoral_consequence: James walks in drunk and belligerent during one of Samantha's video conferences, leaving her thoroughly embarrassed in front of her colleagues.

norm: Families should stay together.
situation: John has an argument with his dad regarding equal sharing of the rent among the family members.
intention: John wants to react to the rent sharing.
moral_action: John explains he can only afford half the requested amount but still wants to live with his family.
moral_consequence: His family agrees to pay the remaining share and is happy that they can still live together.
immoral_action: John moves away from his family to his girlfriend's tiny apartment because he thinks it is unfair for him to share the rent equally out of his minuscule income.
immoral_consequence: His family feels sad and frustrated.

norm: It's wrong to drive while on painkillers.
situation: Cathy is at home and took a large dose of Oxycontin to deal with pain and is feeling dizzy, but she is also hungry.
intention: Cathy wants to get food to eat.
moral_action: Cathy places a call for food delivery to her home.
moral_consequence: Cathy gets her food without incident.
immoral_action: Cathy drives to a fast food restaurant to get food.
immoral_consequence: Cathy drives erratically and increases her chances for an accident as she is dizzy.

norm: It's bad to annoy someone by following them around everywhere.
situation: Yvonne brings her son Mark to a work party where other people also bring their kids.
intention: Mark wants to spend time with his mom.
moral_action: Mark plays with the other kids for a little while, and then goes to find his mom.
moral_consequence: Yvonne is glad that Mark made friends and lets him stand with her.
immoral_action: Mark follows his mom around all night.
immoral_consequence: Yvonne gets annoyed with Mark and tells him to go play with the other children.

norm: It's kind to welcome people.
situation: Melanie is moving soon and will be selling her current house.
intention: Melanie wants to host an open house party.
moral_action: Melanie sets up her open house event and greets every guest with a plate of sweets.
moral_consequence: Melanie's welcome sets the tone, and she receives many offers on the house.
immoral_action: Melanie sets up her open house event, but does not acknowledge or greet any of her guests at the door.
immoral_consequence: The open house guests lose interest in Melanie's home and look elsewhere.

norm: Parents shouldn't interfere in their children's romantic relationships.
situation: Kim's daughter Roxanne has been dating a working class man, Thomas, for 2 years and Kim doesn't like him because he is doesn't have a good job in her view.
intention: Kim wants Roxanne to know she doesn't approve of Thomas.
moral_action: Kim tells Roxanne that she is worried about her financial future with Thomas.
moral_consequence: Roxanne reassures Kim that Thomas works hard, and they will be just fine which puts her mind at ease.
immoral_action: Kim tells Roxanne that she saw Thomas kissing another woman the night before, and that she should break up with him.
immoral_consequence: Roxanne knows this is false because she was with Thomas that night, and now refuses to talk to Kim.

norm: You shouldn't be nosy in your relationship.
situation: Tamara heard her boyfriend Charlie's phone ring when he was in the bathroom.
intention: Tamara wants the phone to stop ringing.
moral_action: Tamara hits the silence button on Charlie's phone and tells him that it rang.
moral_consequence: Charlie calls the person that called back as soon as he comes from the bathroom.
immoral_action: Tamara answers Charlies phone and asks the caller who they are and why they are calling.
immoral_consequence: Charlie gets upset and breaks up with Tamara that night.

norm: It's expected that you are respectful to your in-laws
situation: David and his wife were visiting his wife's parents home for dinner.
intention: David wants to let his mother in law what he thought about the food.
moral_action: David tells his mother-in-law that the food that she prepared was delicious.
moral_consequence: David's mother in law thanked him for the compliment and gave him the recipe.
immoral_action: David tells his mother-in-law that the food tasted like garbage, and he couldn't stand it.
immoral_consequence: David's in-laws were appalled and told David he needed to leave the house immediately.

norm: It is never acceptable to be a terrorist.
situation: Umar's dad was killed by a United States Marine, and he doesn't know why.
intention: Umar wants to avenge his father's death.
moral_action: Umar becomes a politician and orders the U.S. to remove its base from his country.
moral_consequence: Umar is making a difference, and his father's killers has to leave his country.
immoral_action: Umar joins a militant group that is trying to form its own state.
immoral_consequence: Umar ends up killing a lot of innocent people, and his father's killers are still free.

norm: You shouldn't be happy about your friend failing at something.
situation: Sandy was in a class with her best friend, Amy, and they studied together every night.
intention: Sandy wanted to be at the top in her class.
moral_action: Sandy offered to help Amy study harder for the test so Amy wouldn’t fail, for which Amy was very grateful.
moral_consequence: Sandy was happy for Amy when she got a B on the test so Amy hugged Sandy for her help and congratulated her on being #1.
immoral_action: When Amy almost failed her final text, Sandy was happy because Amy would not be a threat to her being the top student.
immoral_consequence: Sandy couldn’t hide her giddiness and Amy was hurt by her joyfulness.

norm: it's important to take care of animals that you've adopted.
situation: Ferris lives alone with his recently adopted great dane Donkey.
intention: Ferris wants to finish watching his movie marathon.
moral_action: Ferris pauses the movie, walks Donkey, feeds him and resumes his movie marathon.
moral_consequence: Donkey is happy and calm.
immoral_action: Ferris, unwilling to tear away from the tv, ignores Donkey the whole day.
immoral_consequence: Donkey becomes agitated, is hungry and messes up in the house and cries.

norm: You shouldn't end a friendship over petty reasons.
situation: Bill and his friend had agreed to meet at the movie theater but Bill's friend arrives half an hour late, so they miss the movie.
intention: Bill wants to show his friend that he's unhappy with them being late for the movie.
moral_action: Bill tells their friend that he's angry that they're late and that they are to blame for Bill missing the movie .
moral_consequence: Bill's friend apologizes to Bill for being late and promises to be on time for things from then on.
immoral_action: Bill says that he doesn't want to be friends with the person who was late anymore because he can't even count on them to be on time.
immoral_consequence: The person who was late can't believe that Bill would end their friendship over such a little thing like being late.

norm: It's bad to make homemade poison.
situation: Lisa walks into the kitchen finding it infested with ants.
intention: Lisa wants to get rid of the ants.
moral_action: Lisa hire an exterminator to get rid of the ants.
moral_consequence: Lisa learns more about pest control as the exterminator tells her what he will do to her house.

norm: It's unacceptable to hide something from your significant other.

norm: It's good to go to a concert with your friends.

norm: You shouldn't stop going somewhere just because you get older.

norm: It's wrong to cheat on your school assignments.

norm: You should include your friends.
situation: Julie is organizing a birthday party for herself, and she has had a clash with her friend Jane recently.

norm: Being honest is considered good.

norm: It's wrong to take advantage of your grandparents.

norm: You should get a bed if you don't have one.

norm: You shouldn't write people notes when you're in study hall.
situation: Curtis is doing schoolwork in a quiet classroom when his friend Joey passes him a piece of paper.

norm: It is good to be friendly to dogs.

norm: It's wrong to beat up people.

norm: It's bad to be controlling when in a relationship.

norm: It's disgusting to dip your johnson in the school's condiments.

norm: You should appreciate veterans.

norm: It's discouraged from farting in front of others.
