moral_consequence: Adrian finds the courage to tell Caden about his triggers.
immoral_action: Caden tells Adrian that he needs to take deep breaths because he's embarrassing both of them.
immoral_consequence: Adrian is hurt by Caden's rude behavior.

norm: It's good to plan for unseen power outages.
situation: Amy is doing some work her vacation condo in Florida.
intention: Amy wants to make sure the condo is ready for summer.
moral_action: Amy buys a backup generator and has it installed in the condo.
moral_consequence: Amy is able keep her food cold and charge her phone when a hurricane knocks out her power.
immoral_action: Amy buys some new curtains to block the sun.
immoral_consequence: Amy has to pay for new windows when a storm breaks them.

norm: Social media is expected to be misleading.
situation: Matt heard something about a bombing in Pakistan and wanted to learn more about it.
intention: Matt wanted to know who or what caused the bomb.
moral_action: Matt opens the New York Times website and looks for an article on it.
moral_consequence: Matt is informed of everything that is there to be known about the bombing.
immoral_action: Matt goes on Facebook and sees his family posting links about the bombing from weird websites.
immoral_consequence: Matt still doesn't know what happened and doesn't know what's true and what's not.

norm: It's negligent to shoot fireworks near someone else's property.
situation: Shawn is hosting a 4th of July party at his beach house, and he wants to light fireworks as part of the celebration.
intention: Shawn wants to pick a spot to setup the fireworks.
moral_action: Shawn sets up the fireworks well away from his neighbors.
moral_consequence: Shawn is able to launch a fireworks display that is least likely to bother his neighbors.
immoral_action: Shawn sets up the fireworks at the property line between him and his neighbor.
immoral_consequence: Shawn gets a citation when his neighbor complains about the noise and smoke.

norm: It's wrong to hurt people you're stronger than.
situation: Bill is talking to his son Lee in the kitchen.
intention: Bill wants Lee to know that he is unhappy with his performance at school.
moral_action: Bill explains that Lee will be deprived of various freedoms until Lee's grades improve.
moral_consequence: lee is physically and emotionally unharmed and learns that there are consequences for poor performance and behavior.
immoral_action: Bill grabs Lee and holds Lee while slapping Lee across the face.
immoral_consequence: Lee feels physical pain and psychological abuse that has lingering effects on Lee's personality.

norm: It's wrong to be violent in a relationship
situation: Ava was asked by her boyfriend Mason to hold his debit card, but she accidentally lost it.
intention: Mason wants Ava to know he's upset.
moral_action: Mason tells Ava that he really needs to find his card, so asks her to retrace her steps.
moral_consequence: Ava finds Mason's card at the bottom of her purse, and he's happy to have it back.
immoral_action: Mason begins to scream at Ava that she better find it, then slaps her across the face.
immoral_consequence: Ava leaves Mason and never returns because he was abusive.

norm: You should report people for this misconduct on the job.
situation: Jeff is at work when his boss make a sexist remark about a coworker.
intention: Jeff wants to be promoted.
moral_action: Jeff reports the comment his boss made to the human resources department.
moral_consequence: The human resources department thanks Jeff and offers a supervisor position.
immoral_action: Jeff ignores the comment and laughs about it with his boss.
immoral_consequence: The boss takes a liking to Jeff and recommends Jeff for a promotion.

norm: It's unusual to involve your ex in a new wedding
situation: Larry is getting married to his fiancee soon and is planning the wedding with her.
intention: Larry wants to send out wedding invitations.
moral_action: Larry invites only certain friends and family who can they both agree on.
moral_consequence: Larry's fiancee gets to have her dream wedding without a hitch.
immoral_action: Larry invites his ex girlfriend who is also a friend to the wedding.
immoral_consequence: Larry's soon to be wife does not approve of this and wonders why he would invite her.

norm: It's wrong to urinate in public.
situation: Fred really has to use the bathroom while at the outdoor concert, but the line at the porta-potty is extremely long.
intention: Fred needs to go to the bathroom right away.
moral_action: Fred walks to a concession stand and tells the person working there that he has an emergency need to use a restroom.
moral_consequence: The management of the venue allow Fred to use an employee restroom, one time, due to the emergency.
immoral_action: Fred can't wait to go to the bathroom, and he walks a short distance from the crowd and relieves himself on a chain-link fence.
immoral_consequence: Security watches Fred use the fence as a bathroom and ejects him from the concert.

norm: You shouldn't lie about being pregnant.
situation: Delaney doesn't like to clean, so her boyfriend Ron has grown to resent her laziness and plans to leave her over it.
intention: Delaney wants Ron to stay with her.
moral_action: Delaney starts a habit of cleaning, hoping it will change Ron's mind.
moral_consequence: Ron notices Delaney's changed behavior and decides to stay with her.
immoral_action: Delaney tells Ron she is pregnant even though she isn't, hoping he will stay.
immoral_consequence: Ron begins to prepare for a baby, but is ultimately devastated when he finds out that there never was one, and leaves Delaney anyway.

norm: It's not okay to abandon someone when you need them.
situation: Pete and Frank are delivering a refrigerator to a customer's home, which is a two-man job, and Frank is telling dirty jokes that upset Pete.
intention: Pete doesn't want to hear Frank's dirty jokes anymore.
moral_action: Pete asks Frank if he can refrain from telling jokes while they're on a delivery job.
moral_consequence: Frank stops telling jokes, and he and Pete successful deliver and install the refrigerator to a grateful customer.
immoral_action: Pete drops his end of the refrigerator and walks back to the delivery truck.
immoral_consequence: Frank is unable to lift the refrigerator by himself, so he drags it, scratching the customer's kitchen floor.

norm: You should always pay people the money you owe them
situation: Will owes his friend a grand total of 1,700 dollars.
intention: Will wants to decide if he should bring it up to his friend.
moral_action: Will decides to bring it up himself so that he can bring it up at a time in his life when paying it back would not hurt him.
moral_consequence: Will pays his friend back all the money he owes him.
immoral_action: Will stays quiet and hopes that either his friend won't bring it up or will get the amount wrong.
immoral_consequence: Unfortunately his friend brings it up at a time when Will has very little money to get by.

norm: You should not date the spouse of a client
situation: Craig has met the wife of one of his biggest clients at his work.
intention: Craig wants to see the woman again.
moral_action: Craig invites his client and his wife to his home to meet his own family.
moral_consequence: The client is impressed that Craig is a family man and sends more business to Craig.
immoral_action: Craig invites his client's wife back to his house for drinks.
immoral_consequence: The client stops doing business with Craig and Craig's business goes bankrupt.

norm: It's good to be faithful to your spouse.
situation: Kyle is married with two kids.
intention: Kyle wants to have more fun in middle age.
moral_action: Kyle plans a road trip he's wanted to go on since college and goes with his family.
moral_consequence: The whole family has fun and becomes closer.
immoral_action: Kyle has an affair with a woman half his age and his wife finds out.
immoral_consequence: His wife is humiliated and initiates a divorce.

norm: It's good to pay for what you want to buy.
situation: James was about to go on his first real date and knew that he needed condoms, but he felt embarrassed about buying them.
intention: James wants to obtain condoms.
moral_action: James asks his friend to buy the condoms for him.
moral_consequence: James has safe sex and doesn't have to been seen buying condoms.
immoral_action: James waits until the cashier is distracted and shoplifts the condoms from the drugstore.
immoral_consequence: "The next time James goes to the drugstore with his family, the same clerk loudly says, ""Hey, that's the kid who stole the condoms!""."

norm: It's horrible to drop kick someone.
situation: John is often frustrated with his sharp tongued coworker Paul.
intention: John wants to shut Paul up.
moral_action: John files a complaint with his company's HR and Paul is cautioned to be more accomodating.
moral_consequence: John is satisfied when Paul backs off and leaves him in peace.
immoral_action: John gets particularly annoyed with Paul and drop kicks him in anger.
immoral_consequence: John is promptly fired and faces assault charges.

norm: It is wrong to abuse your power over other people.
situation: Kerry owns a company and has an employee named Joe that works at the company as an office assistant.
intention: Kerry wants to give Joe work tasks.
moral_action: Kerry tells Joe to refill the printers with paper and ink.
moral_consequence: Joe works hard so that he can get promoted in the company.
immoral_action: Kerry tells Joe to go to Kerry's house and clean the bathrooms.
immoral_consequence: Joe quits the company because cleaning Kerry's home bathrooms is not part of his job.

norm: It is bad to get rid of something by littering.
situation: Jordan is eating a burger as he drives his car down the highway.
intention: Jordan wants to get rid of his burger wrapper.
moral_action: Jordan puts the wrapper on his seat until he can find a trash can.
moral_consequence: Jordan takes the wrapper down with him when he gets to his house and throws it.
immoral_action: Jordan throws the burger wrapper out of the car's window as he continues to drive.
immoral_consequence: A cop sees Jordan littering and stops him and writes him a ticket.

norm: It's nice to be hospitable to other people.
situation: Ben made a room of his available on Airbnb, and the person staying it in thinks it's too cold.
intention: Ben wants to say something to the person.
moral_action: Ben tells the person that he'll change the A/C to make it hotter.
moral_consequence: The person is more willing to leave a positive review on Airbnb for Ben.
immoral_action: Ben tells the person to put more clothes on and tells them to suck it up.
immoral_consequence: The person leaves a bad review on Ben's Airbnb profile.

norm: It's wrong to enjoy anothers pain.
situation: Luke's rival James got struck by a car and ended up in the hospital.
intention: Luke wants to decide how to react to James's accident.
moral_action: Luke sends James a get well card in the hospital because it's the right thing to do.
moral_consequence: James is surprised than even his rival is sending him a get well card.
immoral_action: Luke buys everyone around him a drink when he hears what happened to James.
immoral_consequence: People are upset with Luke for the rudeness of his actions.

norm: It is bad to talk to strangers.
situation: Ash has gone the wrong way and become quite lost in a new area of town.
intention: Ash wants to get directions to the original destination.
moral_action: Ash uses google maps to look up the correct directions before proceeding.
moral_consequence: Ash stays safe and sound in their car.
immoral_action: Ash walks up to a complete stranger to ask them where to go.
immoral_consequence: Ash risks getting themselves into a bad situation.

norm: You shouldn't disturb your partner's sleep.
situation: Penny woke up before her wife, Amy, to go to work and is looking for her keys.
intention: Penny wants to find her keys.
moral_action: Penny searches everywhere in her home until she finds the keys.
moral_consequence: Penny arrives to work a few minutes late.
immoral_action: Penny shakes Amy and asks if she knows where's the keys.
immoral_consequence: Amy is annoyed and cranky for the rest of the day.

norm: It is bad to put others' lives at risk
situation: Jim loves taking illicit drugs and his dealer just sold him a new, experimental drug.
intention: Jim wants to have a thrilling experience.
moral_action: Jim has friends over but decides to try the drug first before offering it to them.
moral_consequence: Jim's friends have a pleasant and safe evening.
immoral_action: Jim invites a few friends over and convinces them to try the new drug with him.
immoral_consequence: One of Jim's friends is seriously ill from the drug.

norm: It's not right to abandon your children.
situation: Renee is the mother to two toddlers, Caleb and Roger and finds out a new action movie is opening today.
intention: Renee wants to see an adult-oriented movie without the kids.
moral_action: Renee gets someone to babysit while she goes to the movie.
moral_consequence: The kids are entertained and kept safe until she returns.
immoral_action: Renee leaves the toddlers at home and goes to a movie.
immoral_consequence: The toddlers fall down the steps and are badly hurt.

norm: You should always admit when you need help with something.
situation: Jim thinks that math class is hard because of multiplication.
intention: Jim wants to pass the math class.
moral_action: Jim tells the teacher he can't memorize all the times tables there's just too much.
moral_consequence: The teacher explains math is about solving, not memorizing, and Jim learns how to study math and earns an A.
immoral_action: Jim insists on doing everything himself and studies on his own.
immoral_consequence: Jim after tons of studying manages a C for the class.

norm: You shouldn't discriminate against people based on their weight.
situation: Stacy, the new kid in class, was chosen to choose all her teammates for the basketball game.
intention: Stacy wants to choose her team.
moral_action: Stacy picks one kid at random, then asks them who in class is good at basketball.
moral_consequence: Stacy puts together a decent team and her team wins 56-52.
immoral_action: Stacy avoids picking all the fat kids assuming they will be bad.
immoral_consequence: Stacy's team loses the game 74 - 13.

norm: It's creepy to stalk people
situation: Sally is curious about her neighbor and stalks him to learn more.
intention: Sally wants to get to know her neighbor.
moral_action: Sally approaches her neighbor to find out more about him.
moral_consequence: Sally's neighbor feels safe outside his home.
immoral_action: Sally hangs around her neighbor and listens to his conversations.
immoral_consequence: Sally makes her neighbor feel paranoid and uncomfortable.

norm: It's good for people to visit elderly family members.
situation: The holidays are coming up and Ashley has a grandmother who lives in a nursing home who she's very close with.
intention: Ashley wants to wish her grandmother happy holidays.
moral_action: Ashley goes to see her grandmother and brings her a gift.
moral_consequence: Ashley's grandmother is pleasantly surprised to see her and is happy she came.
immoral_action: Ashley sends her grandmother a card and a gift in the mail.
immoral_consequence: Ashley's grandmother likes the gift but doesn't have any visitors for the holidays.

norm: You should not trespass on someone else's property.
situation: Calvin is looking for mushrooms outside with friends and sees some on nearby property.
intention: Calvin wants to find chanterelle mushrooms for dinner.
moral_action: Calvin approaches the property owner and asks if he can harvest the mushrooms.
moral_consequence: The property owner is glad to allow Calvin to take the mushrooms, as he has no use for them.
immoral_action: Calvin harvests the chanterelles even though there is a 'No Trespassing' sign on the land.
immoral_consequence: Calvin is arrested for theft of property and trespassing when the property owner discovers him there.

norm: You shouldn't give people your STDs.
situation: Sam is HIV positive, and they haven't had sexual intercourse in a long time.
intention: Sam wants to have sex with someone.
moral_action: Sam finds a partner that is HIV positive.
moral_consequence: Sam is satisfied and doesn't have to worry about spreading their disease.
immoral_action: Sam tells his sexual partners that he is clean and that they don't need to use protection.
immoral_consequence: Sam feels bad for putting them at risk.

norm: It's good to make yourself look nice for people.
situation: Kyle has a job interview at a local clothing store.
intention: Kyle wants to prepare for the job interview.
moral_action: Kyle combs his hair, trims his beard, and puts on washed and ironed clothes.
moral_consequence: The interviewer is impressed by Kyle's meticulous appearance and hires him for the job.
immoral_action: Kyle practices answering questions he thinks the interviewer might ask but doesn't comb his hair or trim his beard.
immoral_consequence: The interviewer doesn't think Kyle's sloppy look will represent the store well and doesn't hire him.

norm: It is good to tip at places you eat.
situation: Becky took her children to a dine in restaurant for lunch on the first day of vacation.
intention: Becky wants to pay the bill.
moral_action: Becky puts a nice sized tip on the table before ushering the kids to the car.
moral_consequence: The waitress thinks Becky must have noticed the extra effort she put into her service.
immoral_action: Becky hands the waitress just enough cash to cover the bill with no tip and thanks her.
immoral_consequence: The waitress is upset that Becky didn't think her service was good enough for a tip.

norm: You should care about dying relatives.
situation: Richard's grandpa has a heart condition and doctor's say he only has weeks to live.
intention: Richard wants to visit someone after work.
moral_action: Richard swings by his grandpa's house thinking he see him while he can.
moral_consequence: Richard's grandfather has a great evening chatting with Richard.
immoral_action: Richard decides it will be boring to visit his grandfather and goes to see his girlfriend.
immoral_consequence: Richard's grandfather is lonely and feels that Richard doesn't really love him.

norm: It's wrong to smoke around people.
situation: Sarah has been feeling stressed from work and goes inside a cafe.
intention: Sarah wants to relieve some stress.
moral_action: Sarah gets her coffee and goes out to smoke an empty park.
moral_consequence: Sarah gets to smoke and drink her coffee in peace.
immoral_action: Sarah lights a cigarette inside the cafe during the morning rush.
immoral_consequence: The cafe owner asks Sarah to put out her cigarette or leave the premises.

norm: It's rude to judge people based on their size
situation: Lola, who is single, has met two nice guys recently, one is an athlete, the other one a slightly plump nerd.
intention: Lola wants a nice, loving boyfriend.
moral_action: Lola decides to look past appearances, spends more time with the plump nerd and eventually starts dating him.
moral_consequence: The plump nerd is happy and in love.
immoral_action: Lola decides there is something wrong with the plump nerd, based on his appearance and starts dating the athlete.
immoral_consequence: The plump nerd feels rejected.

norm: It's wrong to point out another person's flaws.
situation: Suzy was having an argument over money borrowed by Lisa, who is known to have blown money in the past.
intention: Suzy wants to end the argument.
moral_action: Suzy doesn't mention Lisa's past, but points out that Suzy really needs the money back.
moral_consequence: Lisa pays back the money as soon as she can, and the two patch things together.
immoral_action: Suzy points out Lisa's irresponsible past and says Lisa will never repay because of it.
immoral_consequence: Lisa becomes resentful of Suzy and never speaks to her again.

norm: It's always good to repay others what you owe them.
situation: Zach is low on money and still owes his friend Tim $100 but his rent is due in a few days.
intention: Zach wants to pay his rent on time.
moral_action: Zach paints his parents' fence in order to earn some extra cash and is able to pay his rent and repay Tim.
moral_consequence: Tim is happy that Zach followed through with his commitment to repay him, and they remain good friends.
immoral_action: Zach fails to pay Tim back the money he owes in order to afford his monthly rent.
immoral_consequence: Tim gets upset that Zach won't pay him back and stops hanging out with him.

norm: It is rude to be ungrateful for a gift.
situation: Zem is celebrating Christmas at home and receives a weird gift from his cousin, who is present.
intention: Zem wants to react to the gift.
moral_action: Zem expresses curiosity and interest in the gift.
moral_consequence: Zem learns about it and bonds with his cousin.
immoral_action: Zem expresses indifference and confusion.
immoral_consequence: Zem feels guilt later and it takes a long time to make it up to his cousin.

norm: It's bad to slack off at work.
situation: Erika keeps falling asleep at work and hurting her buisness.
intention: Erika wants to stay awake at work.
moral_action: Erika decides to start going to bed sooner, so she'd be less tired.
moral_consequence: Erika starts staying awake at work and getting more work done.
immoral_action: Erika decides to keep watching videos on her computer to stay awake.
immoral_consequence: Erika stops falling asleep but still doesn't get any work done.

norm: It's bad to think your boyfriend is cheating.
situation: Melissa has been dating Chris for 6 months, and Chris is planning to have a guys night out with some friends.
intention: Melissa wants to respond to Chris's outing.
moral_action: Melissa tells Chris to have a good time, but to please not stay out too late.
moral_consequence: Chris promises he won't be gone long and appreciates Melissa trusting him.
immoral_action: Melissa tells Chris she doesn't want him to go because she thinks he will be unfaithful.
immoral_consequence: Chris gets angry because he feels Melissa doesn't trust him.

norm: It's good to let someone know your availability or lack.
situation: Kane has been working long hours and needs a break from work.
intention: Kane wants to take a vacation.
moral_action: Kane asks his boss for time off for a vacation.
moral_consequence: Kane's boss accepts his request and lets him go on vacation.
immoral_action: Kane plans the vacation and leaves without telling his boss.
immoral_consequence: Kane gets fired once he returns for being unreliable.

norm: It is wrong to abuse your children.
situation: Mary's kids are being really loud, and she has a headache.
intention: Mary wants peace and quiet.
moral_action: Mary takes some Tylenol and asks nicely that the kids be quiet.
moral_consequence: The kids are quiet and Mary's headache goes away.
immoral_action: Mary hits her kids to get them to be quiet and threatens them.
immoral_consequence: The kids are scared, hurt, and Mary may get in trouble.

norm: You should never go off on a girlfriend.
situation: Amy comes home and tells Jeff that she just got in an accident with their car.
intention: Jeff wants to react to the news he just heard.
moral_action: Jeff tells Amy that he doesn't care about the car and wants to know if she's OK.
moral_consequence: Amy is relived that he's not mad and really happy that he cares more about her than a material object.
immoral_action: Jeff screams at Amy for being a bad driver and tells her it's probably all her fault.
immoral_consequence: Amy is terrified at Jeff's threatening behavior and feels alone in her stress about the accident.

norm: It's good to appreciate someone else's appearance.
situation: Jane and her best friend who has recently lost weight are meeting each other for brunch.
intention: Jane wants to catch up with her best friend.
moral_action: Jane compliments her best friend's healthier appearance and inquires about the journey she has been on.
moral_consequence: Jane's best friend feels confident and proud after having her hard work noticed by Jane.
immoral_action: Despite her best friend looking healthier, Jane never broaches the subject and instead sticks to topics about herself during their brunch.
immoral_consequence: Jane's best friend loses confidence in her weight loss efforts and plateaus.

norm: It's wrong to lie to first responers.
situation: Bob had passed out and the paramedics were examining him.
intention: Bob wants to answer the paramedics.
moral_action: Bob tells the paramedics everything that is wrong with him.
moral_consequence: The paramedics are able to save Bob's life, and he makes a recovery.
immoral_action: Bob acts like he doesn't know what his health issues are out of concern for his privacy.
immoral_consequence: The paramedics aren't able to help Bob without the information, and he dies.

norm: It's wrong to take joy in the suffering of others.
situation: Jen has a huge rivalry with Alice and sees that Alice has fallen in a mud puddle.
intention: Jen wants to respond to Alice's fall.
moral_action: Jen reaches out to help Alice up and asks if she is alright.
moral_consequence: Everyone sees Jen as the better person, and she makes more friends.
immoral_action: Jen points and laughs and claps at seeing Alice fall in the mud.
immoral_consequence: Jen's friends find her needlessly cruel and petty and stop hanging out with her.

norm: It's not okay to stalk people.
situation: Frank's girlfriend recently broke up with him, but he still has strong feelings for her.
intention: Frank wants to feel better about the breakup.
moral_action: Frank joins some clubs and meets a lot of new people to help him forget about his ex.
moral_consequence: Frank's new friends help him get over his ex, and he soon finds a new girlfriend.
immoral_action: Frank follows his ex girlfriend around and tries to sabotage her attempts to find a new boyfriend.
immoral_consequence: Frank's girlfriend finds out, and he gets reported to the police for stalking.

norm: It's good to stick up for your family.
situation: Dave and his wife Emily and son Jake are at a baseball game wearing Yankees hats when a belligerent Orioles fan starts to berate Jake.
intention: Dave wants to offer his opinion on the situation.
moral_action: Dave tells the Orioles fan to leave his son alone, or he'll come up there and deal with him personally.
moral_consequence: Jake is happy to see his dad being protective of him and feel safe in his father's love and protection.
immoral_action: Dave tells his son to take his Yankee cap off so that the crazy Orioles fan hopefully calms down and the situation is tamed.
immoral_consequence: Jake is sad that his dad is making him take his hat of and doesn't feel like his dad is a hard, strong man.

norm: It's good to share food with people who are hungry
situation: Sara is about to order a pizza and her friend, who hasn't eaten all day, shows up to her house.
intention: Sara wants to have enough pizza leftover for tomorrow.
moral_action: Sara orders enough pizza to have some for later and to feed her friend.
moral_consequence: Sara's friend eats for the first time in awhile and is satiated.
immoral_action: Sara figures her friend will get her own food and orders only enough for herself.
immoral_consequence: Sara's friend is now starving, wishing she could have some of the pizza.

norm: You shouldn't lie to your significant other.
situation: Tom has done something wrong and has a partner that would be quite upset by it.
intention: Tom wants to avoid fighting.
moral_action: Tom calmly explains the truth and mentions that he wanted to be honest.
moral_consequence: Tom's partner is happy with his honesty and is very understanding about it.
immoral_action: Tom acts as though he is innocent and denies any wrongdoing.
immoral_consequence: Tom gets caught in the lie and his partner feels betrayed.

norm: It's frowned upon to be invasive into someone's life.
situation: Sasha watches Hannah leave the room for some water leaving her computer open.
intention: Sasha wants to learn more about Hannah.
moral_action: Sasha asks Hannah questions about her life.
moral_consequence: Hannah is impressed with Sasha's kindness, and she asks Sasha to hang out next week.
immoral_action: Sasha looks through Hannah's computer reading her files.
immoral_consequence: Hannah ends her friendship with Sasha when she returns.

norm: You should be polite to family members.
situation: Artie is at a thanksgiving dinner with his extended family when his aunt begins expressing a lot of controversial opinions.
intention: Artie wants to respond to his aunt.
moral_action: Artie tells his aunt that while he doesn't agree with her opinions, they can disagree with each other in a respectful manner.
moral_consequence: His aunt tones down her rhetoric a little bit and becomes more susceptible to hearing Artie's counter-arguments.
immoral_action: Artie tells his aunt that her ideas are ignorant and that only a stupid person would believe them.
immoral_consequence: His aunt feels extremely insulted, and she storms out to her car and goes home, making the rest of the dinner awkward.

norm: It's wrong not to take photos with your partner.
situation: Bart and his wife Lessie are on a trip to Thailand, and Lessie asks if they can take a picture together in front of some monkeys.
intention: Bart wants to respond to his wife.
moral_action: Bart agrees to get in the picture together with his wife.
moral_consequence: Lessie is happy that Bart is in the picture with her, and the picture comes out really well.
immoral_action: Bart says he doesn't want to be in any pictures and refuses to join her.
immoral_consequence: Lessie is upset and feels that they missed a good opportunity to get an interesting photo of their trip.

norm: Parents are expected to help children learn good habits.
situation: Amber and her son Billy  are at the playground together near a family playing ball.
intention: Amber wants Billy to learn to play ball as well.
moral_action: When Billy signals that he wants to play with the ball, Amber encourages him to ask.
moral_consequence: Billy asks if he can play ball as well and makes a new friend, learning the lesson of sharing and how to play ball.
immoral_action: Amber doesn't say anything when Billy runs and takes the other family's ball.
immoral_consequence: Billy believes that he can play with anything he wants, including things that are not his own.

norm: It's nice to share food.
situation: John is eating his lunch next to a classmate who forgot his lunch.
intention: John wants to eat his lunch.
moral_action: John offers a portion of his lunch to his classmate.
moral_consequence: John's classmate thanks John and becomes great friends with him.
immoral_action: John ignores his classmate and finishes his lunch.
immoral_consequence: John's classmate thinks John is a selfish person and avoids him later on.

norm: Attacking someone's sexual preferences is considered petty.
situation: John has just met Bill and as they are talking with each other Bill mentions that he is gay.
intention: John wants to respond to Bills declaration of his sexuality.
moral_action: John tells Bill that he appreciates that Bill is brave enough to tell him such a thing and tells Bill that who he loves is his business.
moral_consequence: Bill is happy that John is supportive and non judgmental about his homosexuality and feels safe around John.

immoral_consequence: Larry is upset by Steve's brash response and Steve regrets ending a friendship just because he was annoyed by a request.

norm: It's callous to be dismissive of other people's suffering.
situation: Jane suffers from a disease and talks about it at the doctor's office.
intention: Jane wants to talk to the other patients.
moral_action: Jane waits and listens to the other patients' problems as well.
moral_consequence: Jane learns a lot of things about the other patients in the waiting room.
immoral_action: Jane talks about her suffering, but she can't be bothered to listen to OTHERS suffering.
immoral_consequence: People in the office quickly learn not to like Jane much.

norm: It's wrong to tell a joke that hurts someone.
situation: James felt jealous of Don because Don got the lead role in the community play while James was just an extra.
intention: James wants to feel better about not getting a speaking role.
moral_action: James complains to anyone who will listen that he deserves a speaking roles.
moral_consequence: Several other actors in the play sympathize with James because the group is fairly tight-knit.
immoral_action: James begins making jokes about Don's height, weight, and vocal mannerisms.
immoral_consequence: Don eventually gets tired of the jokes and asks the director to make James stop or kick him out of the play.

norm: It's not okay to spend your time loitering in public.
situation: Hilda was wandering around a park all day long and someone asks her why.
intention: Hilda needs to decide what to say when someone walks up to her.
moral_action: Hilda tells them she's been lost all day and asks how to get out of the park.
moral_consequence: Hilda finally escapes the park thanks to the other person's help.
immoral_action: Hilda tells them she's just wasting time until she needs to go to work.
immoral_consequence: The other person walks away wondering why she chose to do this.

norm: You shouldn't cheat on your husband.
situation: Nicole is on a business trip away from her husband.
intention: Nicole wants to enjoy a night out and have fun.
moral_action: Nicole goes to a concert and enjoys the music.
moral_consequence: Nicole has a good story to tell her husband when she returns.
immoral_action: Nicole finds a local man and sleeps with him that night.
immoral_consequence: Nicole gets pregnant from the man.

norm: It's expected that you celebrate your friend's birthday.
situation: Liz is talking with her best friend.
intention: Liz wants to do something for her friend.
moral_action: Liz throws a big birthday party for her friend.
moral_consequence: Liz is thanked by her friend and they become closer.
immoral_action: Liz sends her friend some of her used clothes.
immoral_consequence: Liz loses some respect from her friend for the thoughtless gift.

norm: You shouldn't be angry at your grandchildren
situation: Carol hasn't seen her grandchildren in 3 months because her daughter-in-law won't allow her to see them often.
intention: Carol wants to have a relationship with her grandchildren.
moral_action: Carol realized that it is not the children's fault, and she tries to make the most of the times she does have with her grandchildren.
moral_consequence: Carol's grandchildren love seeing their grandma and ask their mom if they can go see her more often.
immoral_action: When Carol is allowed to see her grandchildren, she takes her anger out on the kids.
immoral_consequence: Carol's grandchildren are afraid of their grandma and don't talk to her much when they go around her.

norm: It is wrong to get angry at animals.
situation: Josh's dog Mittens had an accident in the kitchen after drinking too much water.
intention: Josh needs to clean up the floor.
moral_action: Josh takes Mittens outside before wiping the floor with some bleach and paper towels.
moral_consequence: Mittens plays with her toys outside, and she spends the evening snuggling with Josh.
immoral_action: Josh screams at Mittens as he slams the mop down hard onto the floor.
immoral_consequence: Mittens runs away hiding from Josh and avoids him for the rest of the night.

norm: You shouldn't ignore real people in favor of using technology
situation: Jamie has a date with his girlfriend on the same night his guild has a big event planned online.
intention: Jamie wants to make a decision about how to spend his evening.
moral_action: Jamie bows out of the online event and goes out with his girlfriend.
moral_consequence: Jamie has an enjoyable night in real life.
immoral_action: Jamie makes up an excuse and cancels on his girlfriend.
immoral_consequence: Jamie gets into a fight with his girlfriend when she finds out he bailed on her for a game.

norm: It's unwise to start a relationship in the workplace.
situation: Jackie, a new coworker of Robert's asks him out for a drinks and dinner.
intention: Robert wants to have drinks with Jackie.
moral_action: Robert has drinks with Jackie but makes it clear that no relationship will come of this.
moral_consequence: Jackie and Robert remain good friends and work really well together in the office.
immoral_action: Robert accepts the drinks, asks her to be his girlfriend and the relationship ends within a week of it's start.
immoral_consequence: Jackie lies to her boss and says that Robert pressured her into a relationship, causing him to lose his job.

norm: People should tell the truth.
situation: Dave is a car salesman and is showing cars to a customer.
intention: Dave wants to sell a car to the customer.
moral_action: Dave tells the customer the good and the bad about the car and details how much the bad would cost to fix.
moral_consequence: The customer finds a car that only needs a few repairs, buys it, and is very happy for Dave's honesty.
immoral_action: Dave tells the customer the good things about a particular car and downplays or avoids the bad things about it.
immoral_consequence: The customer buys the car, is dissatisfied, and hates car salesmen from that day on.

norm: You should follow any instruction that your teacher gives.
situation: Lexi is in class but is thinking about all the things she can do when she gets home.
intention: Lexi wants to get her work done before going home.
moral_action: Lexi listens intently and realizes the teacher didn't want some of the problems done.
moral_consequence: Lexi's teacher gives her an A for following directions.
immoral_action: Lexi rushes through the chapter and was the first to submit the homework.
immoral_consequence: Lexi's teacher sees that she didn't pay attention to the assignment and fails her.

norm: It's encouraged you call the police for indecent exposure
situation: Ann sees her neighbor sitting in their backyard just putting on an underwear.
intention: Ann wants to react to her neighbor's behavior.
moral_action: Ann threatens her neighbor that she will report to the police if they continue the disgusting behavior.
moral_consequence: The neighbor feels sorry and agrees to put on pants while outside.
immoral_action: Ann closes her blind in order not to see the neighbor.
immoral_consequence: The neighbor feels validated and continues to wear just an underwear while staying in their backyard.

norm: You shouldn't invade other's privacy.
situation: Samantha is borrowing her friend's computer and sees her financial software has been left open.
intention: Samantha wants to do some research on the internet.
moral_action: Samantha minimizes the financial software window and continues with her research.
moral_consequence: Samantha feels good that she didn't look at her friend's private information.
immoral_action: Samantha looks to see how much money her friend has in the bank before she continues with her research.
immoral_consequence: Samantha feels like she is a bad person for looking at her friend's private information.

norm: It's good to have something you feel proud of.
situation: Bobby has a week before he graduates high school and is waiting to take his final exams.
intention: Bobby wants to finish his final exams.
moral_action: Bobby studies hard and does well on his exams allowing him to graduate.
moral_consequence: Bobby is proud of graduating and continues on to college to earn a degree.
immoral_action: Bobby does not study for his final exams causing him to fail a class and not graduate.
immoral_consequence: Bobby into a depression and his life falls off track after he has to wait a year to go to college.

norm: It's wrong to have a crush on family members.
situation: It's valentines day for Jake, and his family are all giving each other gifts.
intention: Jake wants to write a valentine's day letter to his sister.
moral_action: Jake writes a platonic letter to his sister simply wishing her a good day.
moral_consequence: Jake and his sister have a good Valentine's day and are relaxed around each other.
immoral_action: Jake writes in the letter that he has a crush on his sister and loves her.
immoral_consequence: Jack's sister feels nauseous and the two have an argument.

norm: Its considered reckless to have too much alcohol to drink.
situation: Robert is out with some friends at a bar.
intention: Robert wants to have a good time.
moral_action: Robert has just a couple of drinks during the course of the evening.
moral_consequence: Robert has a good evening with friends and afterwards he arrives safely at home.
immoral_action: Robert keeps ordering drinks all night long and overdoes it.
immoral_consequence: Robert drives home afterwards and crashes into another car.

norm: You shouldn't steal things that don't belong to you.
situation: Ash notices that her sister has a really cute top when looking through the closet.
intention: Ash wants to wear the top when she goes out.
moral_action: Ash offers to trade a top that her sister likes for this one.
moral_consequence: Ash's sister is happy to trade the top as she likes the other one better.
immoral_action: Ash takes the top without asking and keeps it in her closet.
immoral_consequence: Ash's sister finds out and is furious with her as she was looking for it.

norm: It's okay to refuse to bow to peer pressure.
situation: Kenny is at the bus stop waiting for the bus when his friend Tony lights up a cigarette and offer one to him.
intention: Kenny wants to respond to Tony.
moral_action: Kenny is tempted, but says that he doesn't need a new habit.
moral_consequence: Kenny remains healthy and sets a good example.
immoral_action: Kenny, wanting to be seen as cool, accepts the cigarette and smokes it.
immoral_consequence: Kenny develops an addiction that he can't seem to break.

norm: It is good for parents to do things with children.
situation: Harry sees that his son enjoys playing video games a lot.
intention: Harry wants to address his son playing video games.
moral_action: Harry says that he'd like to play the game with his son.
moral_consequence: Harry's son will feel closer to his father through playing games.
immoral_action: Harry says video games are not useful for a person.
immoral_consequence: Harry's son will feel distant from his father.

norm: It's good to help the hungry.
situation: John gets his paycheck today after a month's of hard work, and he notices that some of his coworkers donate money to help fight hunger.
intention: John wants to decide how to use his money.
moral_action: John agrees to donate some of his money to the charity for stopping hunger in children and also signs up as a volunteer for the charity organization.
moral_consequence: The children in hunger get lots of support from the charity organization and grow healthily.
immoral_action: John spends most of the money buying his favorite ski equipment and has no money left for donation.
immoral_consequence: The children living in poverty level receive less donation money from the charity, and they suffer from hunger.

norm: You shouldn't force people to do things.
situation: Devon's house has created a mess in the kitchen.
intention: Devon wants the dishes cleaned.
moral_action: Devon has a house meeting on how everyone can clean the dishes.
moral_consequence: The dishes get done by everyone with no hurt feelings.
immoral_action: Devon berates his roomate Steve into doing the dishes alone.
immoral_consequence: Steve resents Devon and moves out.

norm: It is wrong to live outside your means.
situation: Sam gets a new job in the big city.
intention: Sam wants to reward himself for his achievment.
moral_action: Sam buys himself a nice steak dinner to celebrate.
moral_consequence: Sam lives happily and is able to save money for the future.
immoral_action: Sam spends his money lavishly on cars and an expensive apartment.
immoral_consequence: Sam runs out of money and has to move in with his parents.

norm: It's bad to look in your significant other's private things.
situation: Linda tends to be jealous and thinks she has seen her husband furtively texting behind her back.
intention: Linda wants to know what kind of texts his husband is sending.
moral_action: Linda directly asks her husband what he was texting about.
moral_consequence: Linda's husband likes how straightforward she is and tells her what the texts were about.
immoral_action: Linda looks at her husband's phone at night while he is sleeping.
immoral_consequence: Linda's husband wakes up to see Linda snooping in his phone and is very disappointed.

norm: It is wrong to take birds out of the wild.
situation: Cal is vacationing in Hawaii.
intention: Cal wants a souvenir from his vacation.
moral_action: Cal buys trinkets from the gift shop.
moral_consequence: Cal remembers his vacation fondly when looking at his trinkets.
immoral_action: Cal takes a bird he found in a tree with him home on the plane.
immoral_consequence: Cal is stopped for illegally transporting wild animals and gets in trouble.

norm: Gambling more than one can afford is not wise.
situation: Joe goes to Las Vegas and visits a casino.
intention: Joe wants to play some games.
moral_action: Joe sets a limit of $300 and gambles with it.
moral_consequence: Joe loses the money, but enjoys himself in the process.
immoral_action: Joe maxes out his credit card to get chips for gambling.
immoral_consequence: Joe loses the money and has to pay back the debt for five years.

norm: It's okay to sacrifice your happiness for your children.
situation: Casey is a mother that has been offered the career of her dreams but it would take her away from her children.
intention: Casey wants to do what is best for her.
moral_action: Casey knows she made the decision to have children and knows they must come first, so she turns down the job opportunity.
moral_consequence: Casey is able to devote herself to raising her children to the best of her abilities, and they grow up well adjusted thanks to it.
immoral_action: Casey decides that the career is not worth passing up and takes on the job.
immoral_consequence: Casey is absent from her children's lives as they grow up, and they never grow close to her.

norm: You shouldn't give handouts to your kids.
situation: Jenny's child Jude wants a brand next bike he saw for sale and asks Jenny to get it for him.
intention: Jenny needs to decide whether to buy the bike.
moral_action: Jenny tells Jude he needs to save up half the cost, and she'll pay the rest.
moral_consequence: Jude grows up appreciating the value of hard work and financial responsibility.
immoral_action: Jenny buys the bike for Jude the next day and gives it to him.
immoral_consequence: Jude grows up to be a spoiled adult who is obnoxious to be around.

norm: You shouldn't be around people that drink if you're underage.
situation: Ross, a sixteen year old, is at a crowded party alone.
intention: Josh wants to make friends.
moral_action: Josh walks into the pool area and talks to some people he knows from school.
moral_consequence: Josh gets his classmates phone number, and they decide to hang out every weekend.
immoral_action: Josh joins a group of twenty five year olds who are doing body shots.
immoral_consequence: Josh feels lonely because he can't drink with everyone.

norm: It's good to act more responsibly.
situation: Milton has had one too many drinks with his friends and is ready to call it a night.
intention: Milton wants to go home.
moral_action: Milton uses a ride share service to get a ride home.
moral_consequence: Milton makes it back to his house without any trouble.
immoral_action: Milton gets in his car and attempts to drive home.
immoral_consequence: Milton is pulled over and arrested for driving under the influence.

norm: It's reasonable to be happy when classes are cancelled.
situation: Kyle is on his way to class when his friend calls him to let him know that classes have been cancelled for the day.
intention: Kyle wants to stay busy.
moral_action: Kyle asks his friend if they would like to hang out since there are no classes.
moral_consequence: Kyle enjoys a fun filled afternoon with his friend.
immoral_action: Kyle is upset about the cancellation because he was hoping to do a lot of class work, so he immediately starts studying on his own.
immoral_consequence: Kyle misses out on some free time that could have been spent with friends.

norm: Taking out your anger on animals is not okay.
situation: Bob is having a bad day.
intention: Bob wants to feel better.
moral_action: Bob goes home and plays fetch with his dog.
moral_consequence: Bob feels better after a few moments of laughing at his dog.
immoral_action: Bob sees a stray dog and kicks it.
immoral_consequence: Bob is arrested for animal abuse.

norm: You shouldn't be late to work.
situation: Bruce hates getting up in the morning to go to his job working on an assembly line.
intention: Bruce wants to sleep as long as possible.
moral_action: Bruce calculates the exact amount of time he needs to get ready and travel and sets his alarm clock accordingly.
moral_consequence: Bruce makes it to work right on time replacing someone who is happy to go home.
immoral_action: Bruce goes back to sleep after his alarm goes off and wakes up at the time his shift should start.
immoral_consequence: The person Bruce is taking over for is angry when Bruce arrives because he's getting off late.

norm: It's rude to show off
situation: Thomas is at a homeless shelter when he just discovers he won the lottery.
intention: Thomas wants to share his good news.
moral_action: Thomas whispers to a good friend that he won and shares some of the winnings with his homeless friends.
moral_consequence: The homeless people are happy for him and themselves.
immoral_action: Thomas jumps up and down with glee and yells about all the things he's going to buy.
immoral_consequence: The homeless people around him feel jealous of him and resentful.

norm: It's good to take a break once in a while.
situation: Steve has a big essay due for school the next day and after several hours working on it he is beginning to get very tired.
intention: Steve wants to get a good grade on the paper.
moral_action: Steve takes a break to go for a walk and refocus his mind before returning to finish his paper.
moral_consequence: Steve gets an A- on his essay and is very happy with the grade.
immoral_action: Steve keeps working despite feeling tired and finishes writing the paper just before midnight.
immoral_consequence: Steve get a C- on his essay and is pretty disappointed.

norm: It's wrong to let little things get between a relationship.
situation: Victor is telling Jane that he wants the walls of their home painted yellow and Jane is absolutely refusing that color.
intention: Victor wants to express his disappointment to Jane.
moral_action: Victor tells Jane that he just wishes he could have  a yellow room and that it sucks she doesn't like it.
moral_consequence: Jane is sad to Victor pouting, but she tells him he'll be fine when he picks a different color.
immoral_action: Victor tells Jane that she's just too inflexible and hardheaded about the color and that he's done with her entirely.
immoral_consequence: Jane is flabbergasted that Victor just escalated a discussion about paint into the end of their relationship.

norm: It is not okay to laugh at others.
situation: Samantha spilled her drink all over her new dress at the cafeteria beside her friend Tina.
intention: Tina wants to try to make Samantha feel better.
moral_action: Tina offers to help Samantha clean the dress up and to borrow her extra change of clothes.
moral_consequence: Samantha is thankful to Tina for her offers and takes her up on them.
immoral_action: Tina tries to tell Samantha a joke to cheer her up about how it looks like she rolled in the mud, and laughs heartily at it.
immoral_consequence: Samantha feels even more embarrassed and runs out of the room.

norm: You shouldn't disturb someone's sleep.
situation: Ted finds out that his wife is pregnant and wants to tell someone, but his best friend Wayne is asleep.
intention: Ted wants to tell someone about the pregnancy.
moral_action: Ted sends Wayne twenty text messages about the pregnancy because he's so excited.
moral_consequence: Wayne keeps sleeping and sees the text messages in the morning.
immoral_action: Ted calls Wayne and tells him excitedly that his wife is pregnant.
immoral_consequence: Wayne drowsily tells Ted to call in the morning and hangs up on him.

norm: Housemates are expected to show respect to one another.
situation: Dan is living with his roommate John and has just cooked a meal.
intention: Dan wants to put the used pots and pans somewhere.
moral_action: Dan cleans the pots and pans and then puts them away.
moral_consequence: John will think Dan is considerate and cares that other people can use the pots and pans.
immoral_action: Dan leaves the pots and pans on the dinner table without cleaning them.
immoral_consequence: John will think Dan doesn't care about if other people can use the pots and pans.

norm: You should not claim someone else's work as your own.
situation: Jim has an important project coming up for an English class and has decided to write a paper for his.
intention: Jim wants to complete his essay.
moral_action: Jim writes his essay and includes information from multiple sources, making sure to reference them.
moral_consequence: Jim submits his essay with no issues and receives the highest mark.
immoral_action: Jim writes his essay and adds information directly copied and pasted from multiple sources and leaves it at that.
immoral_consequence: Jim's essay is flagged for multiple counts of plagiarism, and he is suspended by the school.

norm: You shouldn't refuse to pay someone back.
situation: Craig runs a rental car business that has installed kill switches in the cars and owes a large debt on the kill switches.
intention: Craig wants to save money.
moral_action: Craig pays the company what they are owed and pays it on time.
moral_consequence: Craig's business prospers and the threat of the kill switches means fewer delinquent payees.
immoral_action: Craig calls up the kill switch company and says that he is not going to pay the bill.
immoral_consequence: The company activates all of the kill switches on his cars, temporarily shutting down his business.

norm: You should call 911 when a house is on fire.
situation: On his way to work, Jack spots a house burning.
intention: Jack wants to get to his job meeting on time.
moral_action: Jack stops for a second, calls 911 about the house fire, then takes a short cut to his job meeting.
moral_consequence: The house and people inside survive the fire.
immoral_action: Jack stares for a second but then ignores the fire and drives fast to his job.
immoral_consequence: The house and people inside don't get the help they need and perish.

norm: You shouldn't take other people's belongings.
situation: Jane has stumbled across a cute looking skirt in her roommates room.
intention: Jane wants to wear the skirt.
moral_action: Jane approaches her roommate and asks her if she can borrow the skirt.
moral_consequence: Jane's roommate doesn't really like the skirt, so she just gives it to her.
immoral_action: Jane simply takes the skirt and keeping it as if it belongs to her.
immoral_consequence: Jane's roommate sees her wearing the skirt and considers her a thief.

norm: It's good to cooperate with the police.
situation: Henry is pulled over for speeding.
intention: Henry doesn't want to go to jail.
moral_action: Henry has a talk with the cops and apologizes for speeding.
moral_consequence: The cops issue him a mere citation and let him go.
immoral_action: As the cop gets out of his car, Henry slams the gas and speeds off.
immoral_consequence: Police chase Henry and up his charges substantially.

norm: It's wrong not to share with your neighbors.
situation: Mary ran out of salt while cooking and sees her neighbor Jim outside grilling steaks.
intention: Mary wants to ask Jim for some salt,.
moral_action: Jim amiles and offers her his salt shaker.
moral_consequence: Mary feels gratitude and goes out of her way to do something noce for Jim.
immoral_action: When Mary asks Jim for some salt, he hides the shaker and says he has none.
immoral_consequence: Mary will not share things with Jim the next time she sees him.

norm: It's good to give a spouse a special holiday gift.
situation: Robert and his spouse Sally recently moved in with one another and their first Christmas together is coming up.
intention: Robert wants to give Sally something nice for Christmas.
moral_action: Robert buys Sally a silver necklace that she had been wanting for a long time.
moral_consequence: Sally is thrilled to receive the necklace and very thankful for the thoughtful gift.
immoral_action: Robert gives his spouse Sally a big hug and tells her he loves her.
immoral_consequence: Sally is a bit disappointed and feels that Robert should have bought her a nice gift for Christmas.

norm: It's good to express confidence in someone.
situation: Andy is listening to his son Evan tell him what he wants to be when he grows up.
intention: Andy wants to be a good parent.
moral_action: Andy tells Evan he can accomplish anything he sets his mind to if he works hard.
moral_consequence: Evan pursues his dreams and increases his self-esteem.
immoral_action: Andy tells his son Evan to give up his dreams and do something more practical.
immoral_consequence: Evan loses confidence in himself and his dreams and never fulfills his potential.

norm: It's not okay to not appreciate living.
situation: Helena is very depressed, hates her life, and feels very lonely in her misery.
intention: Helena wants to open up to others about how unhappy she is.
moral_action: Helena tells her sister about her sadness and depression and asks her sister to help her seeing the good side of life.
moral_consequence: Helena's sister is happy to help Helena get better.
immoral_action: Helena starts complaining regularly to her sister about how horrible life is and how no one loves her.
immoral_consequence: Helena's sister starts being depressed herself because of Helena's grim view s about life.

norm: You can't expect everyone to like popular songs.
situation: Mary is creating a playlist for the school dance.
intention: Mary wants everyone to like the music.
moral_action: Marry creates a survey for song suggestion, and she uses the survey results to create the playlist.
moral_consequence: Impressed by her skills, the principal asks Marry to be in charge of the school's graduation party.
immoral_action: Mary fills the entire playlist from the songs in the Billboard top 40.
immoral_consequence: Marry's reputation suffers when some of the students complain about the music online.

norm: It is rude to verbally assault your friend.
situation: While playing in a large grass field after school, Jacob's friend Scott hits him with a  water balloon as a prank.
intention: Jacob wants to respond to being soaked by the water balloon.
moral_action: Jacob laughs it off and gets Scott back with a water balloon of his own.
moral_consequence: Jacob has a fun afternoon playing with Scott.
immoral_action: Jacob becomes enraged and berates Scott, accusing him of being stupid and inconsiderate.
immoral_consequence: Jacob remains upset all afternoon and goes home to dry off.

norm: It''s good to do things you enjoy with others.
situation: Kelly is going to a concert alone like she usually does but her friends are also interested in going to the show.
intention: Kelly wants to enjoy the concert to its fullest.
moral_action: Kelly invites her friends to go with her to share the experience.
moral_consequence: Kelly's friends declare it was the best show they've ever gone to.
immoral_action: Kelly tells her friends that she isn't going to the show and avoids them, so she can watch the concert alone.
immoral_consequence: Kelly's friends see her and are hurt that she lied.

norm: It's rude to spew body fluids on other people intentionally.
situation: Marcus is on his way home from work, driving a bit faster than he should and gets pulled over for speeding.
intention: Marcus wants to get home quick enough to catch the end of the Celtics game.
moral_action: Marcus, annoyed at getting pulled over, complies with the officers instructions.
moral_consequence: The officer lets Marcus off with a warning after a few minutes and Marcus is able to get home in time for the second half of the game.
immoral_action: Mark annoyed at the cop for pulling him over spits at him.
immoral_consequence: The cop gets furious and arrests Marcus for assaulting a police officer.

norm: It's hurtful to call people unflattering names.
situation: Jim often gets into arguments with Fiona who is his rival for the top spot in their school year .
intention: Jim wants to win an argument with Fiona.
moral_action: Jim relies on his intellect to try and win his arguments with Fiona.
moral_consequence: Jim is satisfied when he is able to hold his own against Fiona.
immoral_action: Jim resorts to making up a nickname that makes fun of Fiona's weight.
immoral_consequence: Jim is ashamed when others start bullying Fiona with that nickname.

norm: It is good to only do it with one person.
situation: Nate is invited to an orgy by Jane.
intention: Nate wants to have sex.
moral_action: Nate only has sex with Jane at the orgy.
moral_consequence: Nate has a fun time.
immoral_action: Nate has sex with multiple people at the orgy.
immoral_consequence: Nate gets an infection.

norm: It's bad to go to juvie.
situation: Damon is in court because he vandalized some buildings.
intention: Damon wants to tell the judge how he feels.
moral_action: Damon tells the judge that he will never vandalize again and asks for leniency in his case.
moral_consequence: Damon is free and not locked up with some bad kids.
immoral_action: Damon tells the judge to put him in jail because all his friends are there anyway.
immoral_consequence: Damon gets locked up and his parents are disappointed in him.

norm: It is rude to tell others what to do.
situation: Jenna and her brother James were playing in their family's backyard.
intention: Jenna wants to play jump rope with someone.
moral_action: Jenna asks her brother to play jump rope, and when he says no, she goes next door to ask her friend.
moral_consequence: Jenna and her friend have a great time playing games with the jump rope while her brother plays with the dog.
immoral_action: Jenna tells her brother that he has to stop what he's doing and play jump rope with her.
immoral_consequence: Jenna's brother holds the jump rope but complains the whole time.

norm: It is bad to cheat the system.
situation: Will has been on food stamps but has just been hired for a job which has enough income to disqualify him from those benefits.
intention: Will wants to keep his food costs low.
moral_action: Will cancels his food stamps benefits and starts following a strict weekly budget for food.
moral_consequence: There will be more money to help those who need welfare benefits.
immoral_action: Will avoids reporting his new job to the welfare office in order to continue collecting benefits.
immoral_consequence: Will uses money that should be allocated to the other people in need.

norm: It's bad to misuse email to harm someone else.
situation: Betty is reviewing her department's Q2 sales performance numbers spreadsheet.
intention: Betty wants to improve her department's apparent performance relative to her rival, Sara's, section.
moral_action: Betty sends a personal email to each of her people give personalized suggestions and encouragement.
moral_consequence: Betty's department works harder and improves their job performance in the next quarter.
immoral_action: Betty crafts a fake series of emails that make it appear that Sara is sabotaging Betty's team's sales numbers and shows it to her supervisor.
immoral_consequence: The supervisor adjusts Betty's numbers and fires Sara, Sara appeals, but there is no proof the emails were fake.

norm: It is acceptable to buy someone a nice gift.
situation: John has a good friend who loves to cook and whose birthday is coming up in a few days.
intention: John wants to get something for his friend.
moral_action: John gets his friend an expensive blender that he has been wanting for a long time.
moral_consequence: John's friend is very thankful and cooks for John whenever he comes over.
immoral_action: John gets his friend a funny card with his signature inside.
immoral_consequence: John's friend likes the card but doesn't even remember it the next day.

norm: Children are expected to ask for permission from their parents.
situation: Jimmy hears that a carnival is coming to town this weekend.
intention: Jimmy wants to go to the carnival.
moral_action: Jimmy asks his mother and dad if they would take him to the carnival.
moral_consequence: Jimmy's parents tell him that if his behavior is good for the rest of the week, they see no reason not to go to the carnival together.
immoral_action: Jimmy, knowing that his parents might say no if he asks to go to the carnival, sneaks out the day the event starts and enters without his parents permission.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy feels alone and frightened at the carnival, he knows once he is inside that he should have gotten permission from his parents.

norm: It's not okay to show up to events halfway through.
situation: Karla has a friend who is hosting an important event and insists that she needs her to come.
intention: Karla wants to make an appearance at the event.
moral_action: Karla shows up on time and ends up attending the entire event.
moral_consequence: Karla's friend is happy to see her there and have her support.
immoral_action: Karla shows up to the event fairly late after half of it has passed already.
immoral_consequence: Karla's friend is disappointed that she missed the beginning of the event.

norm: It is bad to seek for underage girls.
situation: Victor sits at his computer putting the finishing touches on the script for a teenage romance film with erotic scenes.
intention: Victor wants to hire actors.
moral_action: Victor creates a young adults open audition call on an acting network website.
moral_consequence: Twenty people show up for the audition giving Victor the opportunity to create a diverse cast.
immoral_action: Victor searches for teenage actresses and actors on Facebook to audition for him.
immoral_consequence: Victor is called out on his behavior when one of the teens leaks the erotic script online.

norm: It is bad to judge races.
situation: Claire is white and her daughter has made a new friend who is black.
intention: Claire wants to keep her daughter safe.
moral_action: Claire asks to meet her daughter's new friend's parents, so they can all feel more comfortable with each other.
moral_consequence: Claire feels reassured and her daughter can keep seeing her new friend.
immoral_action: Claire tells her daughter she is not allowed to play with her new friend anymore because of her skin color.
immoral_consequence: Claire's daughter is upset and is influenced by her mother's bigotry.

norm: It's not okay to disrespect someone's art.
situation: John is in the kitchen when his daughter Teri brings him a drawing of a vividly colorful stick figure she just made.
intention: John wants to comment on the drawing.
moral_action: John tells Teri that her drawing is wonderful and that he loves the colors, so he'll pin it to the fridge.
moral_consequence: Teri is delighted that her dad loves the drawing and that he wants to display it for everyone to see.
immoral_action: John tells Teri that the drawing is awful since it's just a silly stick figure and anyone can draw those.
immoral_consequence: Teri begins to cry and is discouraged from further attempts to create art.

norm: It's wrong to be a compulsive liar.
situation: Adam is with friends, and they are all sharing wild stories from their pasts.
intention: Adam wants to impress with his stories.
moral_action: Adam thinks of some times in his life that odd things have happened and shares those stories with his friends.
moral_consequence: Adam and his friends all have a good laugh looking back on their stories.
immoral_action: Adam pulls many a story out of thin air that are clearly to good to be true.
immoral_consequence: Adam's friends don't appreciate that he cannot be truthful with them and his constant lies eventually crumble atop one another which is quite embarrassing for him.

norm: It's rude to fall asleep in public.
situation: Liz is on the bus getting a ride home, and she is very drowsy from working all day.
intention: Liz wants to get some sleep soon.
moral_action: Liz makes herself stay up until she gets back home and sleeps right away.
moral_consequence: The other people riding the bus have a peaceful ride home.
immoral_action: Liz allows herself to fall asleep while still riding on the bus.
immoral_consequence: The other passengers are disturbed by Liz snoring and leaning over her spot.

norm: It is rude to make unwanted romantic advances.
situation: John wants to ask Daisy, his coworker out to dinner.
intention: John wants to pursue a romantic relationship with Daisy.
moral_action: John asks Daisy for her number and tells her he would like to take her out to dinner.
moral_consequence: Daisy tells John she will think about it and let him know later on.
immoral_action: John gets Daisy's number from a friend and keeps texting Daisy even though she has said no.
immoral_consequence: Daisy gets annoyed and reports John to HR.

norm: It is wrong to discriminate others because of race.
situation: John and Mindy are at home watching the news about Black Lives Matter.
intention: John wants to feel good about himself.
moral_action: John says that all lives matter and blacks are equal to whites and should be treated better.
moral_consequence: Mindy respects John and feels closer to him.
immoral_action: John raises his voice and says that blacks are inferior to whites, proven by science.
immoral_consequence: Mindy respects John less and feels more distant from him.

norm: It is rude to ignore friends for a relationship.
situation: Jacob has a new girlfriend Marlene, and they are madly in love with each other.
intention: Jacob wants to spend as much time with Marlene as possible.
moral_action: Jacob brings Marlene with him to his weekly Dungeons & Dragons sessions, so she can learn to play and join in.
moral_consequence: Jacobs friends are happy to meet Marlene and have another player join them.
immoral_action: Jacob skips his weekly Dungeons & Dragons sessions with his friends, so he can be with Marlene.
immoral_consequence: Jacob's friends are unhappy with Jacob for bailing so often and begin to exclude him from the group.

norm: You should listen to your employees about problem employees.
situation: Bill owns a store that's losing money when Tim, an employee, tells him that another employee, Scott, is stealing merchandise.
intention: Bill wants to reduce expenses at his store by firing someone.
moral_action: Bill considers what Tim told him about Scott and fires Scott.
moral_consequence: Bill starts making money at his store because he has fewer payroll expenses and also less losses due to theft.
immoral_action: Bill fires Tim because Tim has less seniority at the store than Scott.
immoral_consequence: Bill has fewer payroll expenses but his store keeps losing money because Scott keeps stealing merchandise.

norm: It's rude to interrupt others.
situation: John is at home with his wife Mindy having an argument.
intention: John wants his wife to listen to him.
moral_action: John listens to everything Mindy has to say and responds respectfully.
moral_consequence: Mindy feels happier and is more likely to listen to John and respect him.
immoral_action: John talks over Mindy, yelling at her and makes her listen to him.
immoral_consequence: Mindy feels resentful toward John and hurt.

norm: You should't kick out your in-laws.
situation: Meg's mother and father-in-law had been staying with her and her husband for a month because they were out of work.
intention: Meg wants to be alone with her husband.
moral_action: Meg tells her mother and father in-law that she and her husband will be going out to dinner.
moral_consequence: Meg and her husband are able to enjoy a pleasant night out.
immoral_action: Meg tells her mother and father in-law that they have to leave by the afternoon.
immoral_consequence: Meg's husband is extremely upset when he finds out how she was treating his family.

norm: It's wrong not to want to see your grandparents.
situation: Billy's grandpa has been recently put into a nursing home, and it is visiting day today.
intention: Billy wants to do something fun today.
moral_action: Billy brings a board game over to the nursing home to play with his Grandpa.
moral_consequence: Billy and his Grandpa bond over the game and get closer as a result.
immoral_action: Billy goes out with his friends to go see a new movie that just came out.
immoral_consequence: Billy's grandpa feels lonely, that his grandson didn't come visit him.

norm: You shouldn't hide that you're a transsexual from your partner.
situation: Jane is a transgender woman who is dating a man she met on a dating app.
intention: Jane doesn't want to lose her man.
moral_action: Jane tells the man that she's transgender on their next date.
moral_consequence: Jane's man empathizes with her, and she gains his trust.
immoral_action: Jane's man only finds out that she is transgender during intercourse.
immoral_consequence: Jane's man leaves her after feeling betrayed.

norm: It's wrong to damage another person's property.
situation: Neighborhood kids on skateboards have been throwing rocks at Jack's car.
intention: Jack wants to stop the skateboarding kids.
moral_action: Jack tells the kids' parents about their actions.
moral_consequence: The parents reprimand the kids.
immoral_action: Jack breaks the kids' skateboards.
immoral_consequence: The parents report Jack to the police.

norm: It's not okay to wallow in self pity.
situation: Ergo is depressed and hanging with a friend.
intention: Ergo wants to talk about what depresses him.
moral_action: Ergo tells his friend and asks for advice.
moral_consequence: Ergo cheers up a bit and begins to heal.
immoral_action: Ergo points out the reasons for his depression and does most of the talking about his life.
immoral_consequence: Ergo gets nowhere and has a disconnected time with his friend.

norm: You should follow someones rules when in their home.
situation: Alice is babysitting her neighbor's children and has been told by their parents that they are not allowed to have sugary treats on weekdays.
intention: Alice wants to have a snack.
moral_action: Alice cuts up some carrot sticks and fruit from the refrigerator for herself and the kids.
moral_consequence: Alice and the kids have a healthy snack and their parents continue to employ Alice.
immoral_action: Alice takes the kids out and buys some cupcakes for all of them to share.
immoral_consequence: Alice gets in trouble with the parents and is not hired to babysit again.

norm: You shouldn't overwork yourself to death.
situation: Jasper and Kait are lying in bed together on their mobile devices.
intention: Jasper wants to spend their time productively.
moral_action: Jasper decides to listen to foreign language study podcasts while they fall asleep.
moral_consequence: Jasper learns a few new words before getting restorative sleep.
immoral_action: Jasper continues doing tasks for work on their phone while in be, staying up for several hours.
immoral_consequence: Jasper is extremely exhausted after getting lots of work done, leading to their immune system being weakened and them getting sick.

norm: You shouldn't leave your children alone.
situation: Jeff was excited to take his family to the Great Adventure theme park.
intention: Jeff wants to ride the big roller coasters at the park.
moral_action: Jeff forgoes the big coasters to rides the rides his kids are tall enough for.
moral_consequence: Jeff gets to experience his kids first time on little coasters, bonding over them and passing on his love of park rides.
immoral_action: Jeff leaves his kids sitting near the roller coaster and gets in line for the coaster.
immoral_consequence: Jeff is yanked off the line by security when his children are found unattended, and they are escorted out of the park.

norm: It is good for parents to set rules.
situation: Jack's kids are always begging to be allowed to walk to the corner store a mile away, even though there are no sidewalks to safely walk on.
intention: Jack wants his kids to stop nagging him about walking to the store.
moral_action: Jack shows his kids a gruesome video about what happens to pedestrians who get hit by cars.
moral_consequence: Jack's kids, terrified, finally give up on walking to the store and start spending their allowances on Amazon.
immoral_action: Jack gives in and lets his kids start walking to the store on the main road.
immoral_consequence: A car comes around a corner too quickly and hits one of Jack's kids, breaking multiple bones.

norm: It is rude to ask someone to be quiet.
situation: Luke is reading in the living room next to his roommate and his friends who are laughing and joking loudly.
intention: Luke wants to read in peace.
moral_action: Luke decides to go read in his bedroom instead, and closes the door behind him.
moral_consequence: Luke's roommate enjoys his fun and boisterous evening with his friends.
immoral_action: Luke tells his roommate and friends he would like them to be respectful and less noisy.
immoral_consequence: Luke's roommate feels like he's not allowed to have fun in his own home.

norm: It's good to donate old furniture to a thrift store.
situation: Mark is moving, and he has a lot of old furniture that he doesn't want to bring with him to his new place.
intention: Mark wants to get rid of his extra furniture.
moral_action: Mark brings his old furniture to a thrift store.
moral_consequence: Other people buy Mark's old furniture, saving resources and money.
immoral_action: Mark brings his old furniture to the dump.
immoral_consequence: Mark's furniture rots in the dump and no one uses it anymore.

norm: It's good to practice good hygiene.
situation: Bill has only been brushing his teeth for a short moment when his arm begins to get tired.
intention: Bill wants to relieve his arm pain.
moral_action: Bill switches hands and brushes his teeth with the other hand as his painful one rests.
moral_consequence: Bill kills all the bacteria in his mouth and his teeth remain healthy.
immoral_action: Bill stops brushing his teeth and puts his arms down, goes to rest and forgets about brushing.
immoral_consequence: Bacteria build in Bill's mouth overnight beginning the process of forming a cavity.

norm: Not helping an old person could make you look uncaring.
situation: Dan's neighbor is an elderly woman who has a hard time getting around and one day he notices that she is having a hard time watering her outside plants.
intention: Dan needs to decide if he will help his neighbor.
