moral_action: Dan walks over to his neighbor's house to offer assistance with watering the plants.
moral_consequence: She is grateful to him for the help, and he feels great about helping someone in need of a hand.
immoral_action: Dan decides not to help and just watches the neighbor through his kitchen window.
immoral_consequence: His neighbor notices him just looking at her out of the window and feels that he must be kind of cold and uncaring to not offer help.

norm: It's considerate to watch someone's back for them.
situation: Nathan and Adam are friends who occasionally spot each other at the gym while using heavy equipment.
intention: Nathan wants to invite Adam to work out with him.
moral_action: Agreeing to spot Adam during his workout, Nathan notices the barbell's slipping and catches them.
moral_consequence: Adam is saved from being hurt and thanks Nathan for being there.
immoral_action: After agreeing to spot Adam during his workout, Nathan ends up walking away while Adam uses heavy barbells.
immoral_consequence: Adam hurts himself after his barbells fall on top of him.

norm: You shouldn't disobey your stepparents.
situation: John who has been forbidden from drinking by his stepfather is offered a beer by a friend.
intention: John wants to respond to the offer of a beer.
moral_action: John declines the offer of a beer and lets his friend know he's not allowed to drink.
moral_consequence: John's stepfather is delighted when he finds out his stepson can follow the rules and feels optimistic about his future.
immoral_action: John accepts the offer of a beer and happily drinks it with his friend.
immoral_consequence: John's stepfather is sad and disappointed when he finds out he was disobeyed and stresses out about his stepson's future.

norm: It's okay to stay true to your morals and values
situation: Steve is broke and down on his luck when his friend Bob asks him to help rob a liquor store for cash.
intention: Steve wants to decide whether to agree to Bob's request.
moral_action: Steve refuses to participate in the activity suggested by Bob because it is against his morals and values.
moral_consequence: Steve feels good about his decision and soon finds a good job which helps him turn his life around.
immoral_action: Steve participates in helping Bob hold up the liquor store for cash.
immoral_consequence: Steve is later arrested and sentenced to prison for his crime.

norm: It's not okay to make someone feel uncomfortable.
situation: Maggie is making dinner and invited her children to come over and eat.
intention: Maggie wants to have a family meal.
moral_action: Maggie's son shows up with his girlfriend and Maggie adds a plate to the table for her to enjoy the meal.
moral_consequence: Maggie's son thanks his mother for her hospitality and tells her he can't wait for her next invite.
immoral_action: Maggie's son also brought his girlfriend to eat, which Maggie doesn't like, so Maggie acts in a rude manner to her.
immoral_consequence: Maggie's son is angry towards Maggie, and he stops coming to her house for a long time.

norm: It is wrong to lie to get out of work.
situation: Lane is watching ESPN ands sees that his favorite baseball team is playing a double-header the next day.
intention: Lane wants to watch both games of his favorite team.
moral_action: Lane takes personal day from work to attend the double-header.
moral_consequence: Lane has a great day at the ballpark cheering for his team.
immoral_action: Lane calls in to work sick, so he can make the day game of the double-header.
immoral_consequence: Lane is spotted in the crowd by his boss watching the game and put on suspension for lying to him.

norm: You shouldn't believe in fortune telling and palm reading.
situation: Shelly is walking along the boardwalk and sees a psychic's store, so she checks it out.
intention: Shelly wants to get her palm read.
moral_action: Shelly does not allow herself to be convinced by the result of the palm reading.
moral_consequence: Shelly makes better decisions her own judgement and logical thought processes.
immoral_action: Shelly is convinced by what the psychic tells her, and she acts on it.
immoral_consequence: Shelly makes the wrong decision after relying on the palm reading.

norm: It's wrong to use someone else's pictures without their consent.
situation: Mark wants to advertise the new wigs from his store.
intention: Mark wants to capture people's attention.
moral_action: Mark asks his graphic designer friend to create a creative graphics for his store's twitter and website.
moral_consequence: The pictures Mark uploads goes viral, and Mark sells out of his new wigs.
immoral_action: Mark places a picture of an instagram influencer with hair similar to his wig in an advertisement.
immoral_consequence: Mark is sued by the instagram model for using her picture.

norm: it's rude to ignore your friends
situation: Tony is very sleepy and gets a phone call from Rick.
intention: Tony wants to get some sleep.
moral_action: Tony answers the phone for a quick conversation before going to sleep.
moral_consequence: Rick talks to Tony for a few minutes and lets him go to bed.
immoral_action: Tony covers his ears and pretends that he doesn't hear the phone, so he can sleep.
immoral_consequence: Rick gets mad that Tony isn't picking up the phone.

norm: It's rude to expect people to pay for your food.
situation: Jenny is out on a dinner date with James.
intention: Jenny needs to pay her half of the bill.
moral_action: Jenny gets out her wallet and pays for her food.
moral_consequence: Jenny and James have a fun night.
immoral_action: Jenny asks James to pay for her food since he asked her out.
immoral_consequence: He agrees to pay but is so annoyed that he doesn't ask her out again.

norm: It's bad to ignore a customer.
situation: Noah is at work and the phone is ringing while he is waiting on a customer.
intention: Noah wants to wait on the customer.
moral_action: Noah answers the phone and asks them to hold a second while they wait on their customer.
moral_consequence: Noah gets a raise when his boss sees how well he works with customers.
immoral_action: Noah picks up the phone and sets it back on the cradle, so he can focus on the person at the counter.
immoral_consequence: Noah gets talked to by his boss about customer service after finding out.

norm: You shouldn't live a life that is a lie.
situation: Vanessa wants more people to follow her on Instagram, but she thinks that people would be not interested in her boring life.
intention: Vanessa wants more followers.
moral_action: Vanessa follows people interacting with their posts while uploading pictures of herself taken from different angles.
moral_consequence: Vanessa slowly gains a modest following who interact with her content.
immoral_action: Vanessa edits her pictures creating a fake life for herself on the platform.
immoral_consequence: Vanessa is exposed when one of her friends calls out her lies.

norm: It's wrong to litter a neighbor's property.
situation: Heysel is walking down the sidewalk in a residential area and has just finished a bottle of water on a hot day.
intention: Heysel wants to discard his water bottle.
moral_action: Heysel smashes the water bottle and puts it in his pocket until he passes by a trash can.
moral_consequence: The water bottle goes into the trash and is easy to pick up.
immoral_action: Heysel casually throws his bottle to the side and onto someone's lawn, then continues walking.
immoral_consequence: The person whose lawn the water bottle is on has a bad back and has a hard time picking it up.

norm: You shouldn't steal hotel breakfasts.
situation: Ian has quite some time before an interview at a hotel which offers a complimentary breakfast for guests in the lobby.
intention: Ian wants to grab a bite to eat.
moral_action: Ian pays a fee to eat the breakfast as a non-guest.
moral_consequence: Ian enjoys his breakfast, guilt-free.
immoral_action: Ian pretends he is a hotel guest and helps himself to the breakfast buffet.
immoral_consequence: Ian feels bad for stealing and being dishonest.

norm: It's bad to commit crimes.
situation: Warren is a powerful CEO and is in the process of acquiring a large company.
intention: Warren wants to let others know about the big news.
moral_action: Warren tells his friends that he has big news coming, but he doesn't tell them what the news is.
moral_consequence: Warren is following SEC regulations and will not find himself in any trouble.
immoral_action: Warren tells his friends every detail so that they invest in Warren's company before the big news is announced.
immoral_consequence: Warren is not following insider trading laws and is putting his company at risk.

norm: You shouldn't call people weird.
situation: Claire asks Donald what he thinks about her making art with macaroni.
intention: Donald wants to give his opinion to Claire.
moral_action: Donald says that Claire is a good macaroni artist with talent.
moral_consequence: Claire thanks Donald and gives him a picture made of macaroni.
immoral_action: Donald says he thinks it's weird to make art with macaroni.
immoral_consequence: Claire get upset with Donald for talking negatively about her art.

norm: You shouldn't copy homework.
situation: Jerry was sent home with schoolwork that is due by tomorrow.
intention: Jerry wants to go out to play with his friends.
moral_action: Jerry asks a friend if he can use his schoolwork as a reference and writes his own original paper within the hour, so he ugoes outside to play.
moral_consequence: Jerry gets a good grade on his classwork and his mom is proud.
immoral_action: Jerry asks a friend if he can use his schoolwork as a reference and ends up plagiarizing the whole paper, then goes outside to play.
immoral_consequence: Jerry gets caught by his teacher and gets a note sent home to his mom, who grounds him.

norm: It's wrong to judge someone based on their name.
situation: Kyle is in class, and he just met a guy that's named Usama.
intention: Kyle wants to remark on Usama's name.
moral_action: Kyle tells Usama that it sucks that people probably make fun of his because of his name.
moral_consequence: Usama appreciates that Kyle is able to understand what it's like in his shoes.
immoral_action: Kyle asks Usama if he's a member of ISIS as a joke.
immoral_consequence: Usama feels insulted and doesn't want to talk to Kyle anymore.

norm: Letting your dog run around off a leash is irresponsible.
situation: Janet thinks it's a beautiful day outside to get some sunshine with her dog, Mr Beefy.
intention: Janet wants to spend time with Mr Beefy.
moral_action: Janet decides to go for a jog with Mr Beefy, so she keeps up pace with him on the leash.
moral_consequence: Mr Beefy loves running with Janet and the two of them have a nice time.
immoral_action: Janet decides to throw a stick for Mr Beefy and lets him off his leash to go after it.
immoral_consequence: Mr Beefy keeps running past the stick and gets lost, and now Janet can't find him.

norm: Children should not disrupt important events
situation: Charlie is home alone bored while his mom is in a remote meeting for her job.
intention: Charlie wants to play to ease his boredom.
moral_action: Charlie goes to his toy box and plays with his action figures.
moral_consequence: Charlie's mother is left unprovoked and is able to continue on with her meeting.
immoral_action: Charlie repeatedly asks his mom to come play with him while she is still meeting.
immoral_consequence: Charlie's mother is annoyed and scolds Charlie for interrupting her.

norm: It is rude not to pay back a debt.
situation: Jill and James are at the bank cashing their paychecks together, because James owes Jill money.
intention: James wants to go on a shopping spree after the bank trip.
moral_action: James pays Jill back and asks if she would like to go shopping with him.
moral_consequence: James and Jill go to the mall together and shop for the best deals and clearance items.
immoral_action: James tells Jill that his check is worth far less money than it is in reality, and asks to pay her back next month.
immoral_consequence: James goes to the mall to go shopping but bumps into Jill there, making her trust him less.

norm: It's rude to upskirt women.
situation: Pierre is at the crowded mall which is two stories with lots of escalators.
intention: Pierre wants to entertain himself.
moral_action: Pierre checks out his favorite shop in the mall and does a little shopping for himself.
moral_consequence: Pierre enjoys the experience and feels good about his purchases.
immoral_action: Pierre walks around on the first floor of the mall looking upwards to the second floor to try to find views of women who are wearing skirts.
immoral_consequence: Pierre is reported by somebody to mall security for being a pervert, and he is publicly reprimanded which is deeply embarrassing for him.

norm: You should make time for others.
situation: Sara was offered overtime at the hospital where she works.
intention: Sara wants to please her family.
moral_action: Sara accepts a limited amount of overtime and focuses more on her family in her time off.
moral_consequence: Sara feels satisfied with her balance between work and family.
immoral_action: Sara decides to lie to her family about the offer and spends more time with them.
immoral_consequence: Sara feels guilty and is scrutinized for her decision at work.

norm: It's good to look very nice for a person's wedding.
situation: Nicole is invited to a friend's wedding.
intention: Nicole doesn't want to spend a lot of money on her outfit.
moral_action: Nicole buys a beautiful new dress on sale to wear to the wedding.
moral_consequence: Many people at the wedding tell Nicole how nice she looks, and she feels proud.
immoral_action: Nicole wears an old ill-fitting dress to the wedding.
immoral_consequence: When Nicole sees pictures from the wedding, she feels embarrassed about her appearance.

norm: It's not okay to be creepy to others.
situation: Theo just met a girl in one of his college classes.
intention: Theo wants to know more about the girl he just met.
moral_action: Theo has easygoing, nice conversations with the girl, and they naturally become friends.
moral_consequence: The girl likes Theo and feels wonderful when he is around.
immoral_action: Theo starts asking questions about the girl to other students, and follows her home to know where she lives.
immoral_consequence: The girl thinks Theo is weird and scary and avoids him.

norm: It's good to be informed about current events.
situation: Kelly lives in a city with a lot of road construction.
intention: She has to drive her friend Carol to the airport next week.
moral_action: Kelly prepares to drive her friend by reading the local paper for updates on closures.
moral_consequence: Kelly finds a fast route with low traffic and is able to get Karol to the airport early.
immoral_action: Kelly knows about the construction so doesn't look into closures but just leaves a few minutes early.
immoral_consequence: Kelly encounters a detour that causes Karol to miss her flight.

norm: It's good to try to stick to your diet
situation: Floyd has an acid reflux problem and is planning on going on a trip to Texas with some friends.
intention: Floyd wants to enjoy himself on the trip.
moral_action: Floyd continues to follow his recommended diet during the trip and focuses on visiting a lot of tourist locations.
moral_consequence: Floyd feels good during the trip and has fun while doing a lot of sightseeing.
immoral_action: Floyd decides to ignore his diet during the trip and eats a lot of the local barbeque.
immoral_consequence: Floyd starts to have a bad acid reflux reaction and has to go see a doctor during the trip.

norm: You should show compassion to those you love.
situation: George's sister Michelle has fallen from her bicycle and starts crying loudly.
intention: George wants Michelle to stop crying.
moral_action: George hugs and comforts Michelle.
moral_consequence: Michelle slowly stops crying and wipes her tears away.
immoral_action: George yells at Michelle to stop crying.
immoral_consequence: Michelle cries even harder.

norm: It is wrong to assume guilt by association.
situation: Tim gets a call informing him that his son's group of friends have been arrested for vandalism.
intention: Tim wants to discuss the situation with his son.
moral_action: Tim talks to his son about choosing his friends more wisely.
moral_consequence: Tim's son starts to make better choices thanks to his dad's guidance.
immoral_action: Tim accuses his son of having some kind of involvement in the vandalism.
immoral_consequence: Tim's son grows resentful of his dad's lack of faith in him.

norm: It's wrong to be sad about another's good fortune.
situation: Chuck and Midge are at bingo night together and Midge wins a big prize.
intention: Chuck wants to talk about his evening.
moral_action: Chuck announces that Midge is a real winner and that he had a great night spending time with her.
moral_consequence: Midge feels happy and is excited to spend more time with Chuck.
immoral_action: Chuck complains loudly that Midge wins too often and the he doesn't find bingo enjoyable anymore.
immoral_consequence: Midge feels bad about her win and withdraws from her relationship with Chuck for some time.

norm: It's helpful to give your child food before they leave.
situation: John's son has his first day of school today.
intention: John wants to take him to school.
moral_action: John gives his son a lunch before dropping him off at school.
moral_consequence: John's son is satisfied and focused at school.
immoral_action: John drops his son off at school without a lunch.
immoral_consequence: John's son is hungry and lacks focus at school.

norm: It's wrong to leave your pet in a locked car.
situation: Missy needs to go to the mall on a hot Summer day but doesn’t want to leave her dog home alone, since he starts barking when lonely.
intention: Missy doesn't want her dog to bother the neighbors with his barking.
moral_action: Missy brings her dog and leaves it in the car but leaves a door unlocked in case something happens.
moral_consequence: Missy's dog gets very hot in the car but some passersby see him having a hard time and get him out of the car and in the shade.
immoral_action: Missy brings her dog and leaves it in the locked car while she runs her errand.
immoral_consequence: Missy's dog dies in the locked car which has become too hot, because passersby cannot open the car to save the dog.

norm: It is rude to not invite people to an event.
situation: Jo is throwing a Christmas party at the office for her employees.
intention: Jo wants to send out invitations.
moral_action: Jo invites everyone who works with her thinking the more the merrier.
moral_consequence: All the employees have a really good time at the party.
immoral_action: Jo only invites to her favorite workers thinking they deserve a reward.
immoral_consequence: The employees who didn't receive an invitation feel left out.

norm: It is mean to ignore your parents.
situation: Stan is in the middle of a boss battle in his favorite video game when his mother asks him to put his dirty clothes in the laundry.
intention: Stan wants to finish his video game.
moral_action: Stan pauses his video game to put his clothes in the laundry before returning to finish it.
moral_consequence: Stan is able to beat the video game and feels happy.
immoral_action: Stan pretends not to hear his mother and continues to ignore her while he keeps playing his video game.
immoral_consequence: Stan's mother takes his video games away for ignoring her and not doing as she says.

norm: It's wrong not to apologize to people.
situation: Edward accidentally breaks a neighbor's window while playing baseball with his little brother, and the neighbor starts shouting at them.
intention: Edward wants to explain what happened to their neighbor.
moral_action: Edward says sorry to the neighbor for breaking his window, and he tells the neighbor that it was an accident.
moral_consequence: The neighbor tells Edward and his little brother they can pay back the window by helping with some chores.
immoral_action: Edward tells the neighbor that it was all his little brother's fault.
immoral_consequence: Edward's little brother calls him a liar and the two get in a fight, while the neighbor calls their parents.

norm: It's rude to call someone a dick.
situation: Omar's father has just punished him, and they are still having a heated discussion.
intention: Omar wants to talk to his father.
moral_action: Omar calmly speaks to his father and offers his side of the story.
moral_consequence: Omar's father decides that he won't punish him after all.
immoral_action: Omar calls his father a dick and then storms off.
immoral_consequence: Omar's father punishes him for twice as long as he originally planned to.

norm: It's wrong to lie about what happened.
situation: Jim hits a neighbor's car with a hockey stick.
intention: Jim wants to avoid getting in trouble.
moral_action: Jim tells his neighbor the truth and offers to pay for the damage.
moral_consequence: Jim works off of the debt and has a clean conscience.
immoral_action: Jim tells his neighbor that he saw a stranger hit his car with a hockey stick and run away.
immoral_consequence: The neighbor needs to fix the car with his own money, and Jim feels guilty.

norm: It is good to encourage people to make positive choices
situation: Colby's friend was getting bullied and picked on in school.
intention: Colby wanted to help his friend solve the problem.
moral_action: Colby tells his friend that he needed to talk to the principal.
moral_consequence: Colby's friend learns how to deal with the bully and has more self esteem.
immoral_action: Colby gave a knife to his friend and told him he needed to fight the bully.
immoral_consequence: Colby's friend ended up in the hospital and then got arrested.

norm: It's wrong not to give advance notice of plans.
situation: John is sitting at home when he realizes he hasn't seen his friend Tony for a while.
intention: John wants to schedule a time to see Tony.
moral_action: John calls Tony and asks when a good time would be then after they agree writes it down in his planner.
moral_consequence: Tony is happy that John is planning an outing for the two of them and is excited to see him.
immoral_action: John decides that 10 minutes from now is a good time and goes straight over to Tony's house.
immoral_consequence: Tony is shocked to see John unannounced and is angry that John has interrupted his family time.

norm: You should not judge others eating habits.
situation: Bill and Peter are at the restaurant and are ordering food when Peter orders french fries soaked in gravy.
intention: Bill wants to comment on Peter's order.
moral_action: Bill tells Peter that his choice sounds delicious and tempting and that he'll order that next time.
moral_consequence: Peter is happy that his friend has validated his choice in what to eat that day.
immoral_action: Bill tells Peter his choice of appetizer was gross and unhealthy and that he'll die eating stuff like that.
immoral_consequence: Peter is annoyed that Bill is judging him and now feels self conscious about what he's going to eat.

norm: Parents should not put their children in dangerous situations.
situation: Lee wants to take his kid hiking up one of the largest mountains in the world with him.
intention: Lee wants his kid to have a good time.
moral_action: Lee brings his kid with him to the peak, and has a picnic with him.
moral_consequence: Lee's kid starts having a true love for nature, being in the moment.
immoral_action: Lee holds his kid over the ide of the mountain, to let him see how high they are.
immoral_consequence: Lee's kid slips out of his hands, and falls to his death.

norm: It's good to help someone with a project.
situation: Ray is sitting in his office at work.
intention: Ray wants to do something with his spare time.
moral_action: Ray joins a coworker that needs assistance on a project they're working on.
moral_consequence: Ray gets a good review from his boss for being a team player.
immoral_action: Ray looks at gambling websites on his work computer.
immoral_consequence: Ray is written up for using work computers for personal reasons.

norm: It is unacceptable to date your cousin.
situation: Dave is hanging out with his cousin Lucy when she offers to be his secret girlfriend.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Lucy's offer.
moral_action: Dave tells Lucy that she's a pretty girl but that she's family and that sort of thing is forbidden so no.
moral_consequence: Dave feels good for expressing a boundary for Lucy to follow and sticking to it.
immoral_action: Dave tells Lucy that he's always found her attractive and that he'd love to be with her.
immoral_consequence: Dave starts to feel regrets about his decision since they can't have children together, and he gets depressed.

norm: It is wrong to be anti-semetic.
situation: Ray lives in a multicultural town, needs to do repairs to his home, and wants to hire a professional.
intention: Ray wants to choose a contractor from those available.
moral_action: Ray hires the best contractor in town who happens to be Jewish.
moral_consequence: Ray gets the best work done on his home.
immoral_action: Ray learns the best contractor in town is Jewish and chooses a lesser skilled contractor.
immoral_consequence: Ray does not get the best work done on his home.

norm: It's wrong to judge others based on their sexual orientation.
situation: Paul is at the local bar enjoying a night out by socializing with friends and strangers alike.
intention: Paul wants to get to know a stranger he is talking to.
moral_action: Paul finds out that the stranger he has been talking to is of a different sexual orientation than him and continues the conversation.
moral_consequence: The stranger appreciates that Paul did not judge him for their differences and enjoys their evening.
immoral_action: Paul finds out that the stranger he has been talking to is of a different sexual orientation than him, so he ends the conversation.
immoral_consequence: The stranger is hurt by Paul's sudden end to the conversation after the topic of sexual orientation and their night is no fun.

norm: It's never acceptable to use racial epithets.
situation: Sanchez is playing basketball with his friend when some African American bullies kick them out of the basketball court.
intention: Sanchez wants to express his anger and frustration.
moral_action: Sanchez goes home and practices with his punching bag.
moral_consequence: Sanchez gets a good workout and no longer feels angry.
immoral_action: As Sanchez and his friend are leaving Sanchez yells a bunch of racial slurs at the bullies.
immoral_consequence: Sanchez's friend tells him that's not cool, and stops hanging out with him.

norm: You shouldn't fake mental illness.
situation: Joe, who forgot to bring his wallet to the store, sees a mentally ill man pan handling on the sidewalk.
intention: Joe wants to earn some money for the store.
moral_action: Joe does some back flips and break dances on the sidewalk.
moral_consequence: Joe gets money from strangers who are amazed by his dancing skills.
immoral_action: Joe panhandles while prentending that the has a personality disorder.
immoral_consequence: Joe gets called out and booed by strangers who notice that he's faking.

norm: It is rude to be concerned with someone else's weight.
situation: Jillian and her friend Cassidy have been invited to a pool party, but Jillian is worried that people will judge them based on Cassidy's weight.
intention: Jillian wants to avoid being embarrassed by Cassidy's weight.
moral_action: Jillian lets go of her worries about Cassidy's weight.
moral_consequence: Jillian and Cassidy attend the pool party together without incident.
immoral_action: Jillian tells Cassidy not to attend the pool party, so she doesn't have to be seen with her.
immoral_consequence: Cassidy goes anyway and calls off her friendship with Jillian.

norm: It's good to report illegal acts.
situation: Jack witnesses someone rob a jewelry store late at night and run away.
intention: Jack wants to tell someone what he saw.
moral_action: Jack tells the police what he saw and reports the crime.
moral_consequence: The thief is apprehended and another crime is solved.
immoral_action: Jack tells his friend what happened and tells them not to report it.
immoral_consequence: The thief gets away with his crime.

norm: It's bad to gloat about trivial achievements.
situation: Cranston is a 30-year-old adult who just figured out a faster way to tie his shoes.
intention: Cranston wants to tell others about his shoe-tying technique.
moral_action: While he happens to be tying his shoes, Cranston shows how he figured out a faster way to do it.
moral_consequence: Some people are interested in his technique and ask him to show them how to do it.
immoral_action: Every time Cranston sees someone tying a shoe, he brags that he can do it faster.
immoral_consequence: People get annoyed with Cranston and try to stay away from him.

norm: It's bad to be divorced.
situation: Jane no longer likes her husband Dan after months of fights.
intention: Jane wants to stop living around Dan.
moral_action: Jane takes a vacation away from Dan and hires a couples therapist.
moral_consequence: Jane is able to repair her relationship with Dan.
immoral_action: Jane divorces Dan and stops living with him.
immoral_consequence: Dan is angry at Jane for overreacting, and Jane regrets her decision.

norm: It's wrong to stand people up.
situation: Lance has agreed to have dinner with his friend, Liz, but is having second thoughts about it.
intention: Lance wants to skip dinner with Liz.
moral_action: Lance tells Liz that he can't make their scheduled dinner.
moral_consequence: Liz accepts Lance's cancellation and makes new plans with someone else.
immoral_action: On the night of their dinner, Lance stays home without informing Liz of his plans.
immoral_consequence: Liz waits at the restaurant for hours, wondering where Lance is.

norm: It's disrespectful to treat others poorly.
situation: Fernando just woke up, needs to go to work, and his wife made him breakfast.
intention: Fernando wants to get to work on time.
moral_action: Fernando rushes through breakfast but stops to thank his wife and give her a kiss before rushing out the door.
moral_consequence: Fernando's wife is flattered and brings him lunch to his work.
immoral_action: Fernando rushes through breakfast and doesn't thank his wife before rushing out the door.
immoral_consequence: Fernando's wife is offended and stops making him breakfast.

norm: You shouldn't approve of parents that beat their kids.
situation: Stan is a teacher and sees a child at school who has bruises on his arm and confesses to being beaten by his parents.
intention: Stan wants to help the child be strong.
moral_action: Stan tells the child that he needs to report his parents to the police, then goes with him to do so.
moral_consequence: The parents are prosecuted for their abuse of the child and the child is freed from his bad situation.
immoral_action: Stan tells the child that the beatings are good for his character and will make him into a man.
immoral_consequence: The child becomes more and more traumatized by the beatings and is mentally tortured by the thought that his feelings are wrong.

norm: It's wrong to hide someone from justice.
situation: After weeks of escalating physical fights, Jenna's brother killed his girlfriend and confessed his crime to her.
intention: Jenna wants her brother to be safe.
moral_action: Jenna tells her brother to confess, and she'll support his story that his girlfriend was abusing him.
moral_consequence: After a close trial, Jenna's brother is found innocent thanks to her testimony.
immoral_action: Jenna lets her brother hide in her crawlspace when the police search her house.
immoral_consequence: The police use thermal imagery to find Jenna's brother, and now they're both facing criminal charges.

norm: It's wrong to dictate how people should organize their wedding.
situation: Miranda is helping her daughter Natasha plan her wedding.
intention: Miranda wants Natasha's wedding to be special.
moral_action: Miranda acts as Natasha's assistant giving her tips along the way.
moral_consequence: Natasha shares a tearful thank you hug with Miranda before the wedding.
immoral_action: Miranda micromanages the entire process and invites a musical act Natasha hates to perform at the reception.
immoral_consequence: While Natasha's wedding is spectacular, Natasha is unhappy with the results.

norm: You should not spend more than you make.
situation: Tom really wants a car that is quite expensive because it's a luxury vehicle.
intention: Tom wants to enjoy the hard earned fruits of labor.
moral_action: Tom finds a certified used model of the car he wanted and purchases that.
moral_consequence: Tom saves a huge amount of money, and he remains financially stable.
immoral_action: Tom buys a new car that is way out of his budget.
immoral_consequence: Tom gets into financial trouble because of the car.

norm: You should reply to someone when they text you.
situation: Travis has car trouble and sends his wife Amanda a text asking her for help while she is chatting with friends in a cafe.
intention: Amanda wants to stay at the cafe.
moral_action: Amanda tells Travis where she is, and offers to call him a tow truck.
moral_consequence: Travis is understanding with Amanda and thanks her for helping.
immoral_action: Amanda glances at the text, and then puts her phone in her pocket without responding.
immoral_consequence: Travis gets suspicious of what Amanda could be doing and loses trust in her.

norm: You shouldn't wear clothes that are too revealing.
situation: Jen is currently shopping at the mall and trying on a bunch of clothes.
intention: Jen wants to buy new outfits for work.
moral_action: Jen decides to wear a modest and formal business outfit to work.
moral_consequence: Jen's coworker's are impressed with how well put together she appears to be.
immoral_action: Jen shows up to work wearing an outfit that is fairly revealing.
immoral_consequence: Jen's coworkers get the impression that she is not very professional.

norm: You should respect the boundaries of your roommates.
situation: Mary is having a friend over to the apartment where she and her roommate share.
intention: Mary wants to hang out with her friend.
moral_action: Mary and her friend spend the night watching television in the living room.
moral_consequence: Mary's roommate enjoys the privacy of her room when she gets home.
immoral_action: Mary and her friend hang out in her friend's bedroom watching her television.
immoral_consequence: Mary's roommate moves out because of the invasion of privacy and Mary has to pay rent herself.

norm: It's rude to steal someone's recipe for their special sauce.
situation: Maria is having her fiance's parents for dinner for the first time and wants to impress them with her cooking skills.
intention: Maria wants to cook her sister's special sauce.
moral_action: Maria tells her sister how important this dinner is for her and asks her sister if she would be okay with Maria cooking her special sauce.
moral_consequence: Maria's sister gladly accepts to give Maria the recipe and even offers her help with preparing the sauce.
immoral_action: Maria sneaks into her sister's room and takes her sister's recipe book without asking.
immoral_consequence: Maria's sister finds out and gets mad at Mary for taking her recipe book and cooking her special sauce without permission.

norm: It's good not to cancel plans.
situation: Ally had plans with Mike to go to the movies, but she has to work late.
intention: Ally wants to stay late at work.
moral_action: Ally calls Mike to see if he can reschedule his plans with her.
moral_consequence: Mike and Ally are able to go to the movies the next day.
immoral_action: Ally cancels her plans with Mike and stays late at her job.
immoral_consequence: Mike doesn't want to reschedule or do anything with Ally again.

norm: You're expected to put extra effort into long distance relationships.
situation: Mike, who has a girlfriend, is going to Honduras for a year but intends to stay with his girlfriend.
intention: Mike wants to call his girlfriend.
moral_action: Mike calls his girlfriend every night and talks with her about deep, personal issues.
moral_consequence: Mike's girlfriend feels like a part of Mike's life and maintains a connection with him while he's away.
immoral_action: Mike calls his girlfriend once a week and talks with her for an hour to catch up on the week's events.
immoral_consequence: Mike's girlfriend feels unsatisfied and grows more and more distant from Mike, eventually separating from him.

norm: It's bad to shower only once every 2 weeks.
situation: Ace is camping for a month and it's only 40 degrees Fahrenheit outside.
intention: Ace doesn't want to get cold.
moral_action: Ace warms up some water every day to take a hot sponge bath.
moral_consequence: Ace comes back smelling like a normal person, as well as his equipment.
immoral_action: Ace stays bundled up at all times and doesn't shower in the cold water.
immoral_consequence: Ace's clothing and camping equipment stink terribly when he returns.

norm: It's good to be polite when using your cell phone.
situation: Mary is taking a crowded bus home from work one day.
intention: Mary wants to answer her phone that's ringing.
moral_action: Mary sees she has a call, but decides to text the caller instead.
moral_consequence: The other passengers have a pleasant trip and aren't annoyed by Mary.
immoral_action: Mary picks up her phone and is talking well above normal levels.
immoral_consequence: The other passengers are mad at Mary for being selfish.

norm: Ignoring someone that is trying to contact you is rude.
situation: Oscar is working when he gets a text from Mike, an old friend, asking him to talk on the phone.
intention: Oscar wants to keep working.
moral_action: Oscar sends Mike a quick text, saying that he's busy and to call at a set time that night.
moral_consequence: Oscar and Mike connect at the scheduled time and have a good conversation.
immoral_action: Oscar doesn't answer the text and keeps working on his project.
immoral_consequence: Oscar forgets about the text and never contacts Mike, who thinks Oscar no longer cares about him.

norm: You shoud apologize when you interrupt someone.
situation: Lisa has just received some news her friends might find mildly important, and she sees her friend across the park in the middle of a game.
intention: Lisa wants to tell her friends the news.
moral_action: Lisa calls out to her friends apologizing for distracting from the game but says they'll want to hear the news she has.
moral_consequence: Lisa's friends are enthralled by the notion and eagerly await the news.
immoral_action: Lisa runs over into the middle of her friend's game forcing them to stop and tells them the news.
immoral_consequence: The friends are annoyed that Lisa interrupted the game they were playing to tell them the news.

norm: You shouldn't blame people for things they didn't do.
situation: Rosa tries to use the household computer and finds that it's broken.
intention: Rosa wants to make sure she isn't blamed.
moral_action: Rosa tells the truth that she has no idea what happened, and she just found the computer this way.
moral_consequence: Her parents fix the computer, and they all move on with thier lives.
immoral_action: Rosa quickly blames Drew for breaking the computer before anyone can blame her.
immoral_consequence: Drew of course has no idea what Rosa's talking about and gets into an arguement.

norm: It's good to want to keep a co-worker safe.
situation: Beth works in a laboratory.
intention: Beth has to clean up the lab.
moral_action: Beth sweeps up broken glass and mops after and lets her coworker to walk carefully on the wet floor.
moral_consequence: Beth's coworker appreciates the warning and cleans up herself after using the lab.
immoral_action: Beth cleans up quickly by brushing broken glassware into a corner and not mopping up all of a spill to leave work sooner.
immoral_consequence: Beth's coworker slips on the spill she can't see and cuts herself on the glass.

norm: You should not partake in illegal activities.
situation: Adam is at a gas station and sees an aisle full of candy.
intention: Adam wants candy.
moral_action: Adam chooses a candy bar and pays for it at the cash register.
moral_consequence: The store owner is happy to be doing business.
immoral_action: Adam hides a candy bar under his shirt when the cashier is not looking and leaves.
immoral_consequence: The store owner loses out money they could have made.

norm: "It's polite to type ""thank you"" on work messages."
situation: Ted is a manager and needs to send out a lot of instructional emails to his team about a new project.
intention: Ted wants to get the emails sent.
moral_action: Ted sends his team instructions and thanks each of them for their hard work in this trying time.
moral_consequence: The team feels busy but grateful and believe that Ted appreciates them.
immoral_action: Ted goes through the list of his employees and writes a quick email about what they need to do, with no signature.
immoral_consequence: Ted's employees see nothing but orders and think that Ted is insensitive and ungrateful.

norm: It's wrong to judge people on their entertainment choices.
situation: Lucas is talking with his blind date Bradley when he notices Naruto headband in his friend's backpack.
intention: Lucas wants to continue talking to Bradley.
moral_action: Lucas asks his date questions about his work and interests.
moral_consequence: Lucas learns more about various subcultures.
immoral_action: Lucas makes a comment about his boyfriend being an extreme otaku.
immoral_consequence: Lucas is left alone for the rest of the evening when his date excuses himself.

norm: Is wrong to abuse another person
situation: Sandy enters the office a fight with her husband when she spots her subordinate placing files in the wrong place.
intention: Sandy wants to vent her frustrations .
moral_action: Sandy vents to her employee about her problems with her husband.
moral_consequence: Sandy and her employee become closer friends.
immoral_action: Sandy pushes the files out of her employee's hands demanding that she pink up the papers on the floor.
immoral_consequence: Sandy is called out on social media after her employee posts about the incident.

norm: It's petty behavior to take revenge on other people.
situation: Jim is beaten up by a guy in his neighborhood.
intention: Jim wants the guy who beat  him up to pay for hurting him.
moral_action: Jim reports the beating to the police and files a report against the guy who beat him.
moral_consequence: Jim sees the guy who beat him go to jail for assaulting Jim.
immoral_action: Jim attacks the guy who beat him up with a baseball bat.
immoral_consequence: Jim is arrested for assault with a weapon and faces serious jail time.

norm: It is wrong to give an ultimatum in a relationship.
situation: Katie has been dating her boyfriend , Mike, for 2 years and thinks that it's time they got married.
intention: Katie wants to talk to Mike about the situation.
moral_action: Katie asks Mike where he thinks their relationship is heading, and if he can see them getting married anytime soon.
moral_consequence: Mike tells Katie that he is happy with their relationship and would like to get married some day.
immoral_action: Katie tells Mike that they've been going out a long time, and he should either propose or end the relationship.
immoral_consequence: Mike breaks up with Katie, and she regrets giving him an ultimatum.

norm: You should not treat others like they are disposable.
situation: John is shopping at the local supermarket.
intention: John has a particularly heavy bag he needs an employee to help with getting into his car.
moral_action: John tips the employee a dollar for the help.
moral_consequence: The employee feels appreciated and thanks John.
immoral_action: The employee helps John, who then tells him to get lost.
immoral_consequence: The employee is extremely annoyed by John's behavior.

norm: It's not okay to lie to get out of work.
situation: Tina is a call center worker who is burned out on her job which she has had for years.
intention: Tina wants to have a break from her work.
moral_action: Tina meets with an HR rep and works within the system to get a combination of paid vacation and unpaid family leave.
moral_consequence: Tina is refreshed and ready to work again after being able to take a break for a month.
immoral_action: Tina feigns an injury in order to file disability.
immoral_consequence: Tina is investigated when people get suspicious and is fined for disability fraud.

norm: It's rude to expect someone to give into your wants.
situation: Jimmy is at home with his mother.
intention: Jimmy wants to play a game.
moral_action: Jimmy sets up his toys in his room because he sees his mom is working in the living room.
moral_consequence: Jimmy's mother eventually comes to his room and joins in with the fun.
immoral_action: Jimmy demands that his mother stop what she is doing to play a game with him.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy's mother scolds him for interrupting her without asking politely.

norm: It is reasonable to enforce your company’s policy.
situation: Vance owns a video game company that is experiencing piracy, which it does not allow.
intention: Vance wants to address the pirating of the games.
moral_action: Vance says the people that pirate games will be sued by the company.
moral_consequence: The pirates will avoid pirating games by  the company and the company will have legal sales.
immoral_action: Vance says that some people may take the games for free.
immoral_consequence: The pirates will not be stopped and the company will lose money.

norm: It's bad to disrespect your mother.
situation: Derek's mother Sloane has been staying at his house since her home caught fire a year ago.
intention: Derek wants to ask his mother to find an apartment.
moral_action: Derek offers to put a deposit down on an apartment for his mother and to go look at them with her.
moral_consequence: Derek's mother is touched by his offer and goes to find an apartment with his help.
immoral_action: Derek leaves a formal eviction notice on his mother's bedroom door before leaving for work.
immoral_consequence: Derek's mother feels that his actions were cold and hurtful and no longer speaks with him.

norm: It's hurtful to not trust your husband with your baby.
situation: Lola is at home with her husband and baby where they are all trying to enjoy some family time together.
intention: Lola wants to make sure her baby is safe.
moral_action: Lola and her husband take turns giving their baby attention both in awe of the thing they have created together.
moral_consequence: Lola's husband is able to bond with baby and the family unit grows stronger.
immoral_action: The entire time they are having family time, Lola doesn't let her husband hold the baby for fear he may drop it.
immoral_consequence: Lola's husband is hurt that he cannot hold his own child and becomes withdrawn from the relationship and family.

norm: You shouldn't call Asians Nazi's.
situation: While attending a Pearl harbor memorial in honor of her grandfather Marie comes across some Japanese WW2 vets who are paying their respects.
intention: Marie wants to uphold her grandfathers memory.
moral_action: Marie talks to the Japanese vets about her grandfathers experience at Pearl Harbor.
moral_consequence: Marie is able to gain greater insight into the tragic events of the war.
immoral_action: Marie loses her temper and calls the old men nazi's.
immoral_consequence: Marie is humiliated when the crowd around them condemns her actions.

norm: It is rude to call people incessantly
situation: Sara is really excited about a new promotion which was just offered.
intention: Sara wants to share the news with her best friend.
moral_action: Sara calls her friend once and leaves a text to call her back.
moral_consequence: Sara's friend calls back and is proud of her upon hearing the news.
immoral_action: Sara calls her friend who is unavailable over and over.
immoral_consequence: Sara's friend is annoyed by her behavior.

norm: It's wrong to fake an illness.
situation: Jerry has to work tonight.
intention: Jerry wants to go a concert tonight.
moral_action: Jerry asks his boss if he can take some extra time off to go to the concert and his boss agrees.
moral_consequence: Jerry enjoys the concert and still has a job.
immoral_action: Jerry pretends to be sick, so he can get out of work and go to the concert.
immoral_consequence: Jerry's boss sees him at the concert and fires him.

norm: It's wrong to bully other people.
situation: Alan is a student in a high school.
intention: Alan wants to raise money for a charity.
moral_action: Alan organizes a fundraiser with other students for money.
moral_consequence: Alan learns to work with others and adds to his extracurricular activities.
immoral_action: Alan intimidates other students for money through force.
immoral_consequence: Alan gets in trouble and is suspended from school.

norm: It's wrong to cause someone undo inconvenience.
situation: Elliot was looking for someone to take him to the airport.
intention: Elliot wants a ride to the airport.
moral_action: Elliot asks Bob to take him and Bob lives right by the airport.
moral_consequence: Bob takes Elliot the short distance to the airport before going home.
immoral_action: Elliot asks Jack to take him, even though Jack lives the farthest away from the airport.
immoral_consequence: Jack takes Elliot there but is grumpy about how long it all takes because of the distance.

norm: It's bad for partners to flirt with other people.
situation: John and his girlfriend Sarah are having a drink at the bar when John goes to the bathroom.
intention: Sarah wants to make conversation with someone while she waits for John to get back.
moral_action: Sarah strikes up a friendly, casual conversation with the bartender.
moral_consequence: John will feel secure in his relationship with Sarah, knowing she isn't flirting behind his back.
immoral_action: Sarah begins saying sexually suggestive things to another patron seated at the bar.
immoral_consequence: John will become jealous and angry because he thinks Sarah would rather be with someone else.

norm: It's rude to laugh at someone for their singing voice.
situation: Simon is trying out for a singing competition, with Tim as a judge, and it is not going well.
intention: Tim wants to reject Simon.
moral_action: Tim rejects Simon, but recognizes that he only has some small things to fix and recommends a voice coach.
moral_consequence: Simon is able to fix his singing problems and wins the competition the next year.
immoral_action: Tim laughs at Simon's singing and makes fun of his voice.
immoral_consequence: Simon stops singing and no longer has confidence in the things he does.

norm: It's good to try to have a relationship with in-laws.
situation: Joe is married to Jane and is having her in-laws over.
intention: Joe wants to be entertained for the night.
moral_action: Joe decides to start up a lively conversation with Jane's parents.
moral_consequence: Jane's parents appreciate and approve of Joe's conversational skills.
immoral_action: Joe sits on the couch and watches TV while Jane's parents are over.
immoral_consequence: Jane's parents are annoyed that Joe doesn't seem to want to engage with them.

norm: It's rude to spread your germs to others.
situation: Adam is in a crowded park and has been sneezing.
intention: Adam wants to sneeze.
moral_action: Adam sneezes into his elbow.
moral_consequence: "A stranger says ""bless you"" before returning to his activity."
immoral_action: Adam sneezes in the direction of stranger.
immoral_consequence: The stranger yells at Adam and makes a scene.

norm: You shouldn't swear at women.
situation: John comes home to his wife Mindy after being stuck in a traffic jam for three hours on the way home from work.
intention: John wants to let off some steam after a hard day.
moral_action: John tells Mindy he had a tough day, hugs her and asks her if she wants to go out to eat.
moral_consequence: Mindy feels closer to John and loves him more.
immoral_action: John raises his voice at Mindy and uses bad language directed at her.
immoral_consequence: Mindy resents John and gets away from him in the house and cries.

norm: It's frowned upon to skip school.
situation: James dreads going to school every day because a bigger kid is bullying him.
intention: James wants to avoid getting beaten up.
moral_action: James asked his adult brother to escort him to school to protect him.
moral_consequence: When the bully tries to punch James, his brother grabs the bully's arm and drags him to the principal's office.
immoral_action: James walks past the school bus stop and spends the day in a local park.
immoral_consequence: James' school calls his parents to report his absence and James gets yelled at.

norm: It's wrong to steal a kid's toy.
situation: Kyle is at the park and is looking at a friend's baby playing with a toy.
intention: Kyle wants to play around with the baby.
moral_action: Kyle makes funny faces at the baby.
moral_consequence: The baby smiles and laughs at Kyle.
immoral_action: Kyle takes the baby's toy as a joke.
immoral_consequence: The baby gets upset and starts screaming.

norm: It's rude to take pleasure in punishing your children.
situation: Frank's son broke a lamp in the house.
intention: Frank wants to punish his son.
moral_action: Frank explains that his son has to do chores to replace the lamp.
moral_consequence: Frank's son will learn that they are responsible for things they break.
immoral_action: Frank laughs while repeatedly spanking his child.
immoral_consequence: Frank's son will become traumatized from the violence and laughter.

norm: It's wrong to get back at others.
situation: Carla is at a restaurant when she sees her boyfriend at dinner with another woman.
intention: Carla wants to express her anger.
moral_action: Carla confronts her boyfriend and the woman and breaks up with him.
moral_consequence: Carla feels better not having to worry about her boyfriend cheating anymore.
immoral_action: Carla goes outside and finds her boyfriend's car and keys the door.
immoral_consequence: Carla is forced to pay for the damage she did to the car.

norm: It is kind to teach someone who is ignorant.
situation: Cindy sees Jack's (who was just hired) car parked in a customer spot when he is an employee.
intention: Cindy wants to continue her day.
moral_action: Cindy finds Jack and warns him about the customer parking.
moral_consequence: Jack moves his car before anyone else notices he's in the wrong space.
immoral_action: Cindy ignores it all and just walks inside the work building.
immoral_consequence: Jack's car gets towed for parking in the wrong space.

norm: It's not good to ignore school responsibilities.
situation: Henry's friend Corin invited him to go to the park, but he has to catch up on his schoolwork.
intention: Henry wants to respond to Corin's invite.
moral_action: Henry tells Corin, thank you, but he has to put his schoolwork first.
moral_consequence: Henry is able to catch up in school and passes for the year.
immoral_action: Henry wants to have fun, so decides to blow off his classwork.
immoral_consequence: Henry falls too far behind in school and ends up failing for the year.

norm: You shouldn't watch videos loudly because it's disturbing to people.
situation: Steven is surfing the Internet late at night and comes across an interesting looking video.
intention: Steven wants to watch the video.
moral_action: Steven turns down the volume to a quiet level before pressing play.
moral_consequence: His mother never hears the video and is able to sleep soundly through the night.
immoral_action: Steven plays the video at a very high volume.
immoral_consequence: His mother wakes up from the noise and becomes very angry with Steven.

norm: You shouldn't lie to your romantic partner
situation: Barbara has been laid off by her company, and she lives with her boyfriend Daniel who works a night shift.
intention: Barbara wants to explain her recent situation to Daniel.
moral_action: Barbara tells Daniel that she has been laid off due to reconstruction of her company.
moral_consequence: Daniel takes a week off and goes on a vacation with Barbara to make her happy.
immoral_action: Barbara still goes out every morning and stays at a coffee shop surfing on the internet without telling Daniel about her layoff.
immoral_consequence: Daniel feels disrespected after knowing that Barbara has actually been laid off.

norm: It is important to have a job.
situation: Ryan comes from a privileged family, and he finds a new expensive gaming computer online.
intention: Ryan wants to obtain the gaming computer.
moral_action: Ryan decides to get a job and earn his own money to spend.
moral_consequence: Ryan's family takes note of him and are pleased that he can provide for himself.
immoral_action: Ryan gets the money from his rich family in order to buy the computer.
immoral_consequence: Ryan's family thinks he is taking what he has for granted.

norm: It's rude to arrive late to your engagements.
situation: Jane was invited to her best friend's wedding, and she is running late because she is waiting to finish downloading a movie.
intention: Jane wants to make it to the wedding.
moral_action: Jane stops the movie download and just leaves, arriving on time.
moral_consequence: No one notices anything wrong and everyone is happy.
immoral_action: Jane waits to download the movie and then leaves, making her late.
immoral_consequence: Her friend notices and is disappointed in Jane.

norm: It's wrong to cheat on your taxes.
situation: Peter realizes that Tax Day is coming up, and he hasn't filed yet.
intention: Peter wants to complete his tax return.
moral_action: Peter fills out his tax return, reporting all of his income and only taking credit for deductions he has receipts for.
moral_consequence: Peter receives a refund from the IRS and deposits it in his savings account.
immoral_action: Peter fills out his tax return but doesn't include all of his income and takes credit for numerous deductions he hasn't earned.
immoral_consequence: Peter gets audited by the IRS and has to pay interest and penalties when his taxes are recalculated.

norm: It's good to admit one's mistakes.
situation: Vince is willingly speeding down the freeway when he gets pulled over by officer Don who is about to write him a ticket.
intention: Vince wants to convince Don he should let him go.
moral_action: Vince tells Don he was an idiot for speeding and that he knows he shouldn't have done that, and he's sorry.
moral_consequence: Don sees that Vince is genuinely remorseful and reduces the infraction on the ticket to only the most minor fine.
immoral_action: Vince tells Don his foot had a spasm and got stuck on the accelerator, and he couldn't get it off in time.
immoral_consequence: Don knows Vince is probably making up nonsense and gives him the maximum fine possible for being dishonest.

norm: People should follow the rules of the establishments they're in.
situation: Lindsey lives in an apartment by herself that doesn't allow pets.
intention: Lindsey wants to adopt a pet dog to keep her company.
moral_action: Lindsey talks to her apartment manager and works out an arrangement where she might be able to have a dog.
moral_consequence: Lindsey and the manager come to an agreement where she pays a small fee and gets to adopt a dog.
immoral_action: Lindsey adopts a dog but doesn't tell the apartment manager, hoping they won't find out.
immoral_consequence: The apartment manager sees Lindsey taking the dog out to use the bathroom, and Lindsey has to pay a hefty fine and is not allowed to renew her lease.

norm: You shouldn't scare kids.
situation: Janet is babysitting her three little brothers.
intention: Janet wants to have a more entertaining night.
moral_action: Janet asks the kids if they want to go for a walk to get ice cream.
moral_consequence: Janet has fun walking to the ice cream shop with the kids and sees some of her friends there.
immoral_action: Janet pretends that the lights have gone out and that there is a killer outside of the house.
immoral_consequence: Janet has a good laugh at the children's fear, but gets grounded for two weeks when her parents find out.

norm: It is good to look out for loose pets.
situation: Jack met Lucy, who bred Italian greyhounds, and Jack was stoked when she accepted a ride home from him in his hopped up Camero.
intention: Jack wanted to make sure Lucy would never forget him.
moral_action: Jack parks his car on the street and walks Lucy to her door with a flashlight and petting each of her prize dogs.
moral_consequence: Lucy is impressed with his kindness and vows to always remember that night.
immoral_action: Jack whips around Lucy's house and yard doing several donuts in the dark.
immoral_consequence: Liucy screams as Jack runs over several of her prize dogs killing and injuring them.

norm: You shouldn't yell at your friends over trivial things.
situation: Billy walks home after being bullied at work, and he notices his friend Phillip moving his things to another table.
intention: Billy wants to express his feelings.
moral_action: Billy shuts himself into his room and vents his feelings to one of his coworkers.
moral_consequence: Billy feels better after getting the support of his friend.
immoral_action: Billy grabs his things off the table making remarks about Phillips lack of intelligence.
immoral_consequence: Billy is roasted by his other friends after Phillip makes a bad post about him on social media.

norm: You should be happy for other people's good news.
situation: Gene just proposed marriage to Missy, and she is telling her single friend, Cathy at work.
intention: Cathy wants to respond to the news.
moral_action: Cathy hugs Missy and tells her that she is very happy for her, while thinking she will find love for herself one day.
moral_consequence: Missy is glad to be able to share her happiness with her friend.
immoral_action: Cathy is jealous of Missy getting engaged, so she tells her that sounds nice, and changes the subject to work related topics.
immoral_consequence: Missy feels foolish because she expected Cathy to have a little more exitement.

norm: You shouldn't do things that get you banned.
situation: Fred, who has a concealed carry permit and a gun, goes to a nightclub, where a drunk person picks a fight with Fred.
intention: Fred wants to deal with the drunk person.
moral_action: Fred goes to the bartender and asks for help dealing with the drunk person.
moral_consequence: The bartender calls security, who throws the drunk person out and bans him.
immoral_action: Fred pulls his gun on the drunk person and tells him to back off immediately.
immoral_consequence: Security sees Fred with the gun, throws him out of the nightclub, and bans him from ever returning.

norm: People shouldn't go back on their word.
situation: A major sale at the mall is happening on the same day that Charlie promised to take Alex to the museum.
intention: Charlie wants to go to the sale.
moral_action: Charlie takes Alex to the museum and goes to the mall after they leave.
moral_consequence: Alex has a good time and buys something at the sale with Charlie.
immoral_action: Charlie goes to the mall and makes Alex go to the museum by himself.
immoral_consequence: Alex gets mad at Charlie and feels lonely at the museum.

norm: It's rude not to save food for everyone
situation: Kate, who lives at home with her parents, has been too busy with school assignments to fix up dinner.
intention: Kate wants to order a pizza.
moral_action: Kate orders an extra large pizza, enough to feed three and saves some for her parents.
moral_consequence: Kate's parents get to rest when they get home because dinner is provided.
immoral_action: Kate gets a medium pizza which is small enough for her to eat by herself.
immoral_consequence: Kate's parents have to cook for themselves when they get home from work.

norm: It's bad to drug someone so you can rape them.
situation: Ronald hasn't had sex in a while, and is very attracted to his new co-worker.
intention: Ronald wants to have sex with her.
moral_action: Ronald speaks his interest in his coworker to her, and asks if she'd be down for a one night stand.
moral_consequence: The coworker happily agrees, being attracted to Ronald as well.
immoral_action: Ronald invites the co-worker to his place and drugs her, so he can rape her.
immoral_consequence: The co-worker comes to after, and files charges, getting Ronald arrested.

norm: It's bad to impose rigid rules on how to live.
situation: Jim is concerned that his daughter is spending too much time playing video games.
intention: Jim wants to reduce his daughter's gaming habit.
moral_action: Jim discusses his daughter's gaming habits and together they create reasonable limits on her gaming.
moral_consequence: Jim's daughter feels respected by her father.
immoral_action: Jim tells his daughter video games are bad for her and forbids her from ever playing another game.
immoral_consequence: Jim's daughter is angry and runs away from home.

norm: You should support your partner.
situation: Aldo notices Julian, his partner, has been using drugs to the point that it interferes with Julian's moods.
intention: Aldo wants to let Julian know his feelings about the drug use.
moral_action: Aldo asks Julian if they can talk about the drug use, and maintains an open mind while discussing it.
moral_consequence: Aldo learns a lot about Julian, drug use, and becomes a better partner.
immoral_action: Aldo addresses the issue in a forceful manner, expressing his outlook on drugs.
immoral_consequence: Julian is alienated, uses more drugs and the relationship deteriorates.

norm: It's rude to make a mess of someone else's desk.
situation: June notices her employee's desk is a disorganized mess.
intention: June wants to discipline her employee for a messy desk.
moral_action: June offers to help her employee clean up her desk and learn organizational skills.
moral_consequence: June's employee feels relieved and June is happy to see a clean desk.
immoral_action: June messes her employee's desk up even more to prove to her employee she must clean it up.
immoral_consequence: June's employee gets upset and calls June abusive, while June feels guilty.

norm: It's hurtful to bring up painful things from someone's past.
situation: Jane is chatting with Jill in a coffee shop.
intention: Jane wants to comment on Jill's life experiences.
moral_action: Jane admires Jill's talent in dancing and asks her how to master dancing.
moral_consequence: Jill feels proud and tells Jane some good advice for improving her dancing skills.
immoral_action: Jane is nosy and asks Jill why she broke up with her ex-boyfriend.
immoral_consequence: Jill feels sad and starts to cry immediately.

norm: It's rude to startle others.
situation: While John's sister Mary watches TV in the living room, John is in the kitchen struggling to make enchiladas.
intention: John wants his sister's help making dinner.
moral_action: John calmly gets Mary's attention and kindly asks for her help in the kitchen.
moral_consequence: Mary agrees to help John and the enchiladas turn out great.
immoral_action: John sneaks up behind his sister and grabs her shoulder to get her attention and ask her for help.
immoral_consequence: Mary is startled and irritated that John scared her, so she declines to help him cook.

norm: It's rude to hate people.
situation: Jack walks around in his shirt that says **** [politician] and **** you if you vote for them.
intention: Jack wants to decide if he should keep wearing the shirt.
moral_action: Jack decides not to wear this shirt everywhere since broadcasting his hate everywhere is rude.
moral_consequence: People don't see Jack as anywhere near as annoying.
immoral_action: Jack keeps wearing his shirt everywhere and always talks about how much he hates [Politician].
immoral_consequence: Jack is seen as quite rude and annoying, epically to those uninterested in politics.

norm: You shouldn't be too loud for your neighbors.
situation: Samuel's birthday is coming up, and he is planning on having a house party.
intention: Samuel wants to invite lots of people over.
moral_action: Samuel invites a large amount of his closest friends, and asks them to be respectful with noise.
moral_consequence: Samuel's guests attend the party while keeping the noise level at an appropriate level.
immoral_action: Samuel tells his guests to invite anyone and everyone, and the party gets out of hand.
immoral_consequence: Samuel's neighbors are awakened by the noise of his many guests and call the cops.

norm: It's wrong to hit people if it's not in defense.
situation: Jeff is at the bar, and another guy bumps into him, spilling his drink.
intention: Jeff wants to respond to the spilled drink.
moral_action: Jeff realizes it was an accident, lets it go, and orders a new drink.
moral_consequence: The night moves on without being interrupted by drama, and Jeff is seen as nice and understanding.
immoral_action: Jeff spins the guy around and punches him in the face.
immoral_consequence: The guy is hurt, a fight breaks out, and Jeff ends up spending the night in jail and getting a fine.

norm: It's bad to sleep with your friend's significant other.
situation: Charles, who has a friend that is dating a mutual friend, broke up with his girlfriend and feels lonely.
intention: Charles wants to feel less loney.
moral_action: Charles calls his friend and asks to hang out with both him and his girlfriend to cheer him up.
moral_consequence: Charles' friend is happy for the chance to help Charles feel better and the three of them have fun together.
immoral_action: Charles calls his friend's girlfriend, persuades her to spend a night with him, and does so.
immoral_consequence: Both Charles and his friend's girlfriend regret it afterwards and it makes things very awkward and tense between them.

norm: It's kind to give what you have to others.
situation: Marvin caught and cooked more crab than he could eat.
intention: Marvin wants to get rid of the extra crab.
moral_action: Marvin knows his neighbor has nothing to eat, so he gives his neighbor the crab.
moral_consequence: Marvin's neighbor does not go hungry.
immoral_action: Marvin knows his neighbor has nothing to eat but throws away the crab in the garbage.
immoral_consequence: The food is wasted and Marvin/s neighbor goes hungry.

norm: It is common to worry about older family members
situation: Social distancing measures are recommended due to a pandemic, which John is unknowingly carrying, and he sees his parents for the first time in months while wearing a face mask.
intention: John wants to greet his parents.
moral_action: John waves hello, but keeps his distance and keeps his mask on out of concern for his parents' health.
moral_consequence: John prevents his parents from catching any virus he's carrying.
immoral_action: John runs up and gives his parents a big hug, stripping his mask off to give them each a kiss on the cheek.
immoral_consequence: John unknowingly gives both his parents a virus due to his lack of concern for their health.

norm: It's nice to call your relatives.
situation: Chad's aunt is in the hospital suffering from COVID-19.
intention: Chad wants to know how his aunt is doing.
moral_action: Chad calls his aunt directly in order to find out how she's doing.
moral_consequence: His aunt feels better knowing that Chad is thinking about her.
immoral_action: Chad asks his mom to tell him how his aunt is doing.
immoral_consequence: His aunt didn't know that he asked about her and feels bad knowing that he didn't contact her.

norm: You shouldn't stay with someone who abuses you
situation: Kelly is being abused by her boyfriend, Ronnie, which causes her to be sad very often.
intention: Kelly wants to talk to Ronnie about his behavior.
moral_action: Kelly tells Ronnie that his behavior is unacceptable and that she'll be leaving him over it.
moral_consequence: Kelly rediscovers herself in being single and finally experiences happiness.
immoral_action: Kelly asks Ronnie to change his behavior, and waits for him to do so.
immoral_consequence: Ronnie never changes and Kelly keeps getting abused.

norm: It's good to go out with people.
situation: Jared and his work team completed a big project and his team asks him if he wants to go out after work.
intention: Jared wants to respond to his team.
moral_action: Jared tells his team that he'll go out with them.
moral_consequence: Jared will be able to build better bonds with his work team.
immoral_action: Jared tells his team that he'll be going home after work.
immoral_consequence: Jared will not be able to build camaraderie with his work team.

norm: It's wrong to hate an entire country.
situation: Wanda is browsing the internet and reading comments about a negative news story from France about a bad person.
intention: Wanda wants to form an opinion on the news story.
moral_action: Wanda reads all the comments from different perspectives and realizes this was an individual behavior described in the article.
moral_consequence: Wanda feels well informed but makes sure to continuing reading more about the situation.
immoral_action: Wanda takes note of the more unique comments on the situation and begins making assumptions about everybody in France behaving the same as the story.
immoral_consequence: Wanda narrows her world view and continues down a slippery slope of ignorance.

norm: You shouldn't have kids you can't take proper care of.
situation: Shana, who is poor and unemployed, is pregnant with a child and the father has run off.
intention: Shana wants to bring the pregnancy to term.
moral_action: Shana gives birth and proceeds to put the child up for adoption.
moral_consequence: The child is given the chance to have a much better and healthy life.
immoral_action: Shana gives birth to the child and attempts to raise him with no resources.
immoral_consequence: Shana's child is not given the proper care that he needs.

norm: It's wrong to avoid doing chores.
situation: Jim knows his mother wants his help doing chores around the house today.
intention: Jim wants to go to his friend's house.
moral_action: Jim spends a few hours doing house chores before gong to his friend's house.
moral_consequence: Jim's mother is greatly helped by him doing  some of the house chores.
immoral_action: Jim goes to his friend's house leaving his mother to do all the chores without him.
immoral_consequence: Jim's mother has to spend much longer than she planned getting all the chores done.

norm: People should respect each other.
situation: John has just arrived home from football practice.
intention: John wants to eat dinner.
moral_action: John eats dinner in his room so that his stench doesn't bother the rest of the family.
moral_consequence: The rest of the family is glad he didn't stink up the kitchen.
immoral_action: John sits down at the kitchen table to eat a sandwich, smelling up the whole room with his body odor.
immoral_consequence: The rest of the family is disgusted by the smell and has to leave the room.

norm: It is rude to eat too quickly.
situation: Aaron is having a romantic dinner with his girlfriend.
intention: Aaron wants to feel full and satisfied.
moral_action: Aaron savors each bite of his meal with great enjoyment.
moral_consequence: The chef sees how much Aaron is enjoying the food and feels proud.
immoral_action: Aaron scarfed all of his food down within minutes of receiving his plate.
immoral_consequence: Aaron's girlfriend feels awkward as the only one eating for the rest of the meal.

norm: It's rude to stare at overweight people.
situation: Jackie is standing behind an obese man in the line at a fast food restaurant.
intention: Jackie wants to appear to be a kind person.
moral_action: Jackie pays no attention to the man and looks at the menu while he orders.
moral_consequence: Jackie feels good for treating the man respectfully.
immoral_action: Jackie pretends to not be looking but secretly stares at the man as he orders.
immoral_consequence: Jackie worries that someone might have noticed her staring.

norm: It's wrong to wish for destruction on people.
situation: After losing a loved one in the 9/11 attacks Peter is asked to write an article on his feelings towards Muslim's.
intention: Peter wants to express his feelings in the article.
moral_action: Peter writes about the importance of separating the actions of a few from the intent of the entire Muslim faith.
moral_consequence: Peter is lauded for his open minded viewpoint.
immoral_action: Peter writes an article calling for the annihilation of all Muslims in order to curtail further terrorist attacks.
immoral_consequence: Peter is viewed as an extremist by people who read his article.

norm: It is polite to thank others.
situation: John and his Wife Andi are dining when John is given a watch by his wife for their fifteenth wedding anniversary.
intention: John wants to respond to the gift.
moral_action: John tells Andi that it's wonderful and thanks her for going through the trouble of getting the gift.
moral_consequence: Andi is happy John is appreciative and is glad hat he likes what she has chosen for him.
immoral_action: John tells Andi that the watch isn't quite the type he likes and that he'll probably end up returning or exchanging it.
immoral_consequence: Andi feels sad that John doesn't like her gift and feels like she must have done something wrong.

norm: You shouldn't do illegal activities in your neighborhood.
situation: Daniel has been furloughed from his job and is having trouble making ends meet.
intention: Daniel wants to make some extra money, so he can pay his bills.
moral_action: Daniel decides to get a side hustle driving for Uber to make some extra money.
moral_consequence: Daniel is able to make enough money to pay his bills.
immoral_action: Daniel decides to make and sell crystal meth in order to make some money.
immoral_consequence: Daniel is reported to the police and arrested for doing drugs.

norm: You shouldn't purposely annoy people.
situation: Hugh is a huge Trump fan but knows his neighbor Sally hates Trump and what Trump stands for.
intention: Hugh wants to show his support for Trump at his house.
moral_action: Hugh puts one small Trump supporter sign in his yard and let's his neighbor Sally know beforehand he has nothing against her.
moral_consequence: Sally respects Hugh for his courtesy and views Hugh as the one Trump supporter she likes.
immoral_action: Hugh purchases 40 Trump supporter signs and puts them in his yard facing Sally's house.
immoral_consequence: Sally is outraged and calls the housing association on Hugh.

norm: It's expected that significant others kiss each other.
situation: John woke up late to work.
intention: John wants to get to work as soon as he can.
moral_action: John kisses his wife and leaves for work.
moral_consequence: John's wife gets him the video game he's been wanting.
immoral_action: In his hurry, John ignores his wife's request for a kiss goodbye.
