immoral_consequence: John's wife becomes angry with him and will not speak to him.

norm: It's good to give people space to process a tragedy.
situation: Noor has just lost his father in a tragic accident and is currently sitting in a tutoring session with Jade.
intention: Jade wants to help Noor feel better.
moral_action: Jade asks Noor if he'd rather sit alone for some time, and lets him decide what feels best.
moral_consequence: Noor takes Jade up on the offer and spends the rest of his tutoring time reminiscing about his dad, feeling a little better.
immoral_action: Jade offers to take Noor out on the town to party and forget his sadness.
immoral_consequence: Noor has a great night out but suffers from alcohol poisoning, as he drank too much in an attempt to forget losing his dad.

norm: It is rude to ignore your mother.
situation: Zach is talking with a friend when his mother comes up and starts asking him something.
intention: Zach wants to choose someone to listen to.

norm: It's hurtful to go behind someone's back.
situation: Terry is married and has an old car that is breaking down.
intention: Terry wants to buy a new vehicle.

moral_consequence: Terry's wife will feel appreciated in the marriage.

norm: You shouldn't take laxatives to lose weight.

intention: Barbara wants to do well in the interview.

moral_consequence: Barbara really impresses the casting agent at the interview and gets the part.
immoral_action: Barbara takes a lot of laxatives to lose weight and look thinner on camera.
immoral_consequence: Barbara smells terrible and has to excuse herself to go to the bathroom several times during the interview, and doesn't get called back.

norm: It is bad to abandon a cat after a move.
situation: Henry has a cat but is moving in with his fiance who is allergic.
intention: Henry wants to get rid of his cat for his fiance's sake.

moral_consequence: The cat gets a new home where it is taken care of.
immoral_action: Henry leaves the cat in the street when he moves out.
immoral_consequence: The cat struggles and dies because it is not accustomed to living outside on it's own.

norm: It's bad to pretend you aren't married.
situation: Roberta is having drinks at the bar when an attractive man sits down beside her.
intention: Roberta wants to talk to the man.
moral_action: Roberta says hello to the man and sparks up a conversation about her husband.
moral_consequence: The man has a good time chatting with Roberta and the two become friends.
immoral_action: Roberta quickly slides her wedding ring into her pocket and says hello to the man.
immoral_consequence: The man flirts with Roberta for the rest of the night and becomes angry with her upon learning the truth.

norm: It's good to help babysit your family members.
situation: Sandra's mom asks her to look after her little sister while her mom goes out.
intention: Sandra wants to answer her mother about babysitting her little sister.
moral_action: Sandra agrees to look after her little sister while her mother is out.
moral_consequence: Sandra's mom is proud of Sandra for being responsible and helping look after her little sister.
immoral_action: Sandra says she can't look after her sister because she has a date that night.
immoral_consequence: Sandra's mom has to pay for a babysitter and is disappointed that Sandra won't help in looking after her little sister.

norm: It's ok to raise money for good causes.
situation: Pamela is unable to visit her family for Christmas leaving her free for a week.
intention: Pamela wants to distract herself from missing her family.
moral_action: Pamela volunteers at a charity collecting money for people in front of a store dressed as an elf.
moral_consequence: Pamela befriends several people working at the charity.
immoral_action: Pamela spends her time spending money at bars.
immoral_consequence: Pamela is unable to pay for her bills at the end of the month.

norm: It's wrong to mess with food that isn't yours.
situation: Betsy is in the school cafeteria for lunch, but she forgot her lunch money at home.
intention: Betsy wants to get food to eat.
moral_action: Betsy explains the situation to the lunch lady and requests a free lunch.
moral_consequence: Betsy is given a tray of food at no cost to her.
immoral_action: Without permission Betsy takes food from another student's lunch tray and eats it.
immoral_consequence: Betsy gets in trouble for taking another student's food.

norm: You shouldn't take someone's tip money because that's stealing.
situation: Marty is a busboy, and he and the waitress Ann are the last ones in the cafe when it's time to close.
intention: Marty needs to clear the last table before they leave.
moral_action: Marty sees Ann's tip money is still on the table when he's clearing it, and he brings it to her.
moral_consequence: Ann thanks Marty and tells him she forgot all about her tip.
immoral_action: When Marty goes to clear the table he sees a customer left Ann a tip, and he pockets the money for himself.
immoral_consequence: Ann sees Marty put the tip money in his pocket and asks him what he's doing taking her tip money.

norm: You shouldn't spread rumors about your friends.
situation: Elaine's friend Susie just told her she heard her other friend Karen was cheating on her boyfriend, but isn't sure it's true.
intention: Elaine wants to decide whether or not to tell the rest of her classmates at school tomorrow.
moral_action: Elaine calls Karen to ask if it's true she cheated on her boyfriend.
moral_consequence: Karen tells Elaine that's it's not true, so Elaine sets the record straight with Susie and Karen's boyfriend never hears the false information.
immoral_action: When Elaine is in class the next day she tells the other people in her class.
immoral_consequence: The news comes back to Karen's boyfriend, and they break up over it.

norm: It's good to adopt children with no home.
situation: Mark and his wife are ready to start a family.
intention: Mark wants to parent a child.
moral_action: Mark's wife suggest adoption and Marks thinks that is a great idea they adopt a young girl.
moral_consequence: Mark and his wife have a great life and adopt more children soon after.
immoral_action: Marks wife suggest adoption but mark says that is so stupid they end up getting pregnant and having a baby instead.
immoral_consequence: Marks thoughts about adoption bother his wife so much that she leaves him a few years later.

norm: It's rude to perform sexual acts in public
situation: Christopher is in a park with his girlfriend when he starts to feel affectionate towards her.
intention: Christopher wants to act on his affection.
moral_action: Christopher brings his girlfriend home and then starts touching her sexually.
moral_consequence: Christopher's girlfriend will think he's considerate of her privacy.
immoral_action: Christopher starts to touch his girlfriend sexually in the park.
immoral_consequence: Christopher's girlfriend will think he's being inconsiderate of her privacy.

norm: You should always respect other people's parents.
situation: Tony and Mark are hanging out when Tony asks Mark to sleep over and Mark tells him that his parents wouldn't allow that.
intention: Tony wants to respond to Mark's statement.

moral_consequence: Mark feels happy that his friend understands his circumstances and respects his parents wishes.

norm: You shouldn't demand freebies.
situation: James is in his regular coffee shop and is planning on ordering a latte.
intention: James wants to get a cup of coffee.
moral_action: James orders and pays for a latte.
moral_consequence: James drinks his latte.

immoral_consequence: The barista gets the manager and the manager tells James he has to pay.

norm: You shouldn't put curses on people.
situation: Ed, a believer in voodoo practices, wants to get back at his friend Andrew for pulling a prank on him.
intention: Ed wants to get revenge on Andrew.
moral_action: Ed pulls a harmless prank on Andrew with a bucket of cold water.
moral_consequence: Andrew laughs and apologizes for pulling the prank on Ed earlier.
immoral_action: Ed gives Andrew a curse by using a voodoo doll.
immoral_consequence: Andrew feels pain whenever Ed uses the doll on him.

norm: It is mean to call someone out publicly.
situation: Greg is a teacher and sees a student copying off of another student's paper, preparing to turn it in.
intention: Greg wants to tell the student that cheating is wrong.
moral_action: Greg meets with the student after class and explains that he can't accept homework that was copied from another student.
moral_consequence: The student is disappointed but accepts the punishment.
immoral_action: Greg tells the student from the front of class that copying answers is not allowed and that his homework will get a zero.
immoral_consequence: The student gets very angry, defensive, and embarrassed in front of his peers.

norm: It's bad to come to class unprepared.
situation: Hank wakes up 10 minutes before class and realizes that he has to go.
intention: Hank wants to go to class.
moral_action: Hank takes some extra time to pack his bag and arrives to class a bit late.
moral_consequence: Hank is tardy, but hands in his homework on time.
immoral_action: Hank leaves quickly and shows up to class as fast as possible.
immoral_consequence: Hank leaves his homework at home and the homework is late.

norm: You shouldn't leave moldy pizza under your bed.
situation: Alan finds old pizza while cleaning his apartment.
intention: Alan wants to put the old pizza away.
moral_action: Alan puts the pizza in a garbage bin.
moral_consequence: Alan's apartment becomes free of debris.
immoral_action: Alan puts the pizza under his mattress frame in his room.
immoral_consequence: Alan's room smells bad and attracts rodents.

norm: You shouldn't cheat on people.
situation: Karina and Roland have been a serious couple for years, but recently Karina was asked out on a date by her coworker.
intention: Karina wants to respond to her coworker's invitation.
moral_action: Karina tells her coworker she is flattered, but is very much in love with Roland and must decline.
moral_consequence: Karina's coworker respects her honesty and leaves her alone.
immoral_action: Karina agrees to the date with her coworker.
immoral_consequence: Roland is heartbroken to find out about Karina's date and ends their years-long relationship.

norm: You should always try to remain friendly with coworkers.
situation: Stephanie works with a team of colleagues on a very demanding project which could bring great rewards.
intention: Stephanie wants the project to be successful.
moral_action: Stephanie is very dynamic and inspires her coworkers by working hard and praising their good work.
moral_consequence: Stephanie's coworkers think she's a great leader and love her.
immoral_action: Stephanie gets very pushy and bossy with her coworkers so that they keep up and work hard.
immoral_consequence: Stephanie's coworkers end up disliking her greatly.

norm: You should not get involved with your family's love life.
situation: Phil's sister has started dating a man that Phil does not trust.
intention: Phil wants his sister to know he cares about her.
moral_action: Phil tells his sister he cares for her deeply and that he is there for her if she needs advice.
moral_consequence: Phil's sister feels supported and safe.
immoral_action: Phil tells his sister he thinks her new boyfriend is not good for her.
immoral_consequence: Phil's sister stops seeing her boyfriend and is very sad about it.

norm: It is never okay to drug another person.
situation: Laura and Samantha are enjoying wine at a restaurant and while they wait for their meal Samantha uses the restroom.
intention: Laura wants Samantha to sleep with her.
moral_action: Laura flirts heavily with Samantha and hints to going home together throughout dinner.
moral_consequence: Samantha brings Laura to her apartment and the two have sex.
immoral_action: Laura puts a date rape drug in Samantha's drink while she is away from the table.

norm: You should not demand things from others.
situation: Paul is unable to drive and depends on his friends.
intention: Paul wants to get rides to where he needs to go.
moral_action: Paul offers gas money and always remembers not to take his friends help for granted.
moral_consequence: Paul finds it easier to get rides and is able to make for functions as a result.
immoral_action: Paul calls his friends daily and requests the rides in a demanding tone.
immoral_consequence: Some of his friends stop responding and Paul has a hard time getting rides.

norm: You shouldn't make fun of your siblings.
situation: Karl is playing chess with his younger sister Kristen.
intention: Karl wants to win the game.
moral_action: Karl concentrates on the positions and makes the better moves while playing against his sister.
moral_consequence: Karl wins the game by outplaying his little sister.
immoral_action: Karl calls his little sister names, trying to distract her from the game.
immoral_consequence: Karl wins the game because Kristen starts crying and can't concentrate on the game.

norm: It's good to help out the hard of hearing.
situation: Sally is on vacation in the Bahamas taking a guided tour of the island, but her husband Dan is hard of hearing.
intention: Sally wants to react to Dan.
moral_action: Sally understands what the guide is saying, so she tells Dan what's being said.
moral_consequence: Dan learns all about the island and is appreciative of Sally.
immoral_action: Sally understands what the guide is saying, but doesn't bother to tell Dan what she hears because she doesn't want to take away from her enjoyment.
immoral_consequence: Dan learns nothing on the guided tour and sees Sally as selfish for not sharing information.

norm: It is bad to go against the law.
situation: Nicole is going for a scenic drive through some country roads.
intention: Nicole wants to get some nice pictures of the scenery.
moral_action: Nicole stops the car and gets out to take pictures when there is nice scenery.
moral_consequence: Nicole finishes her drive with a nice photo album of the countryside scenes.
immoral_action: Nicole tries to use her cell phone camera while she is driving on curving road.
immoral_consequence: Nicole crashes into a tree and is seriously injured.

norm: You should not bully others with religion.
situation: Tate's cousin hasn't been going to church lately, and they're in a devoutly Christian family.
intention: Tate wants to tell his cousin something.
moral_action: Tate tells his cousin that he's allowed to support whatever religion he wants.
moral_consequence: Tate's cousin feels relieved and feels less pressure to have to go to church.
immoral_action: Tate tells his cousin that he;ll never come to heaven if he never comes to church.
immoral_consequence: Tate's cousin feels guilty and feels like Tate is judging him.

norm: It's annoying when people buy into conspiracy theories.
situation: George's best friend Frank has been trying to get him to believe the conspiracy theories that have captured his attention.
intention: George wants to respond to Frank's urging.
moral_action: George firmly tells Frank that he doesn't agree with him.
moral_consequence: George stays true to his beliefs.
immoral_action: George embraces Frank's beliefs.
immoral_consequence: George alienates his other friends and acquaintances as he starts spouting his newfound beliefs.

norm: You shouldn't drive if you had some alcohol earlier.
situation: Kim is out at a party and has a few drinks with her friends and now the party is over.

immoral_action: Kim drives home even though she's still buzzed.

norm: You shouldn't call someone nanny if they don't like it.

immoral_action: "Joan kept calling her ""nanny"" rather than learning her name."

norm: It's wrong to lie to your doctor.
situation: Carl is getting a checkup at his doctor's office, but he is embarrassed about how many sexual partners he has had.
intention: Carl wants to get through with the checkup.
moral_action: Carl tells the doctor that he has had sex with many different women of the last year.
moral_consequence: Carl's doctor screens him for STDs and finds out he is in the early stages of one, but he is easily cured of it.
immoral_action: Carl tells the doctor he is not sexually active, even though he's had sex with multiple women over the last year.
immoral_consequence: The doctor doesn't screen for STDs and misses that Carl has contracted one.

norm: It's bad to spread germs in stores.

norm: It is wrong to pressure someone for nude images.

norm: You should not single people out for their physical features.

immoral_action: Noticing about the same number of boys and girls, Tom tells them to split into two teams with boys on one team and girls on the other.
immoral_consequence: Several players tell Tom that it is not nice to pit boys against girls in what should be a fun game and Tom feels guilty, realizing that they’re right.

norm: It's polite to use somebody's name when talking to them

moral_consequence: Frank stops what he was currently working on and does what Ian asks him to do.
immoral_action: Ian shouts hey you to get Frank's attention, and repeats the phrase until Frank looks up at him.
immoral_consequence: Frank thinks Ian's pretty rude for not calling him by name, and mentions so to Ian's supervisor.

norm: It's good to appreciate someone's food.

immoral_consequence: Mindy resents John and feels sad and lonely.

norm: It is good to know your limits when drinking.

norm: It's wrong to blow hundreds of dollars on an app.

norm: You shouldn't do drugs around your neighbors.

norm: It's wrong to not prioritize a friend's special event.

moral_consequence: Daniel thanks Paul for coming to the recital.

norm: It's good to bring a snack to someone else's party.

moral_consequence: The guests are pleased because they can eat the pretzels to take away some of the acidity of the champagne.

norm: You shouldn't learn other people's passwords.

immoral_action: Macy demands to know the password from her grandpa, so she can remember it herself.

norm: You shouldn't kick someone in the nuts.

norm: It is wrong to deceive your loved ones

moral_consequence: The kids are excited that they get to eat a scoop of ice cream.
immoral_action: Mary takes the kids straight home after visiting the doctor's office.

norm: It is rude to yell at others.

norm: You shouldn't treat adults like kids.

norm: You should not watch tv  too much.

moral_consequence: Robert feels well-rested and is happy with how he spent his vacation.
immoral_action: Robert spends the whole vacation watching TV.
immoral_consequence: Robert's eyes hurt, and he feels like he wasted his vacation.

norm: It's good to support your family.
situation: Lisa's brother Joe lost his cat.
intention: Lisa wants to cheer her brother up.
moral_action: Lisa helps her brother look for his cat and posts missing flyers throughout the neighborhood.
moral_consequence: Someone calls Joe after seeing one of Lisa's flyers and says they have found his cat.
immoral_action: "Lisa tells her brother ""it's just a cat"" and gives him $1,000, hoping it will cheer him up."
immoral_consequence: Joe gets even more upset and begins to cry over his cat.

norm: It is responsible to turn in a lost item.
situation: Jake was at an airport, and he found a diamond ring on the ground.
intention: Jake wants to decide what to do with the ring.
moral_action: Jake walks up to an airport attendant and tells them that he found the ring.
moral_consequence: Jake is happy that he did the right thing regardless of if the owner is found.
immoral_action: Jake decides to keep the ring and sell it to a jeweler.
immoral_consequence: Jake feels guilty and hopes the owner doesn't need the ring.

norm: People are expected to look out for their relatives.
situation: Mary's mother is sick with the flu.
intention: Mary wants to go out on a date with her boyfriend.
moral_action: Mary calls her sister to sit with her mother while Mary goes out.
moral_consequence: Mary's sister takes care of her and her mother gets better.
immoral_action: Mary goes out with her boyfriend leaving her mother at home.
immoral_consequence: Mary's mother gets very sick and has to go to the hospital.

norm: It's wrong to insult someone on social media.
situation: Sarah is browsing social media when she notices the profile of a stranger named Hannah, a girl from her hometown.
intention: Sarah wants to message Hannah.
moral_action: Sarah messages Hannah and asks her how long she's been living in her town.
moral_consequence: Sarah and Hannah hit it off and plan to meet each other for lunch sometime.
immoral_action: Sarah messages Hannah telling her that her profile photo is not attractive.
immoral_consequence: Hannah feels hurt and her confidence sinks.

norm: It's important to be careful when moving heavy objects.
situation: Rudy is moving to a new house in the city and is unpacking the moving truck.
intention: Rudy wants to move the bulky boxes inside his new home.
moral_action: Rudy moves the boxes one by one using a back brace and a dolly to get them inside.
moral_consequence: Rudy finishes unpacking the moving truck in less than an hour and feels proud of his work.
immoral_action: Rudy stacks two boxes on top of one another and lifts using his back.
immoral_consequence: Rudy pulls his back and can't lift any longer.

norm: It's not okay to defend pedophiles.
situation: Frank is talking with Jimmy when Jimmy confides in Frank that he's a pedophile, and he abuses some children.
intention: Frank wants to respond to Jimmy's statement.
moral_action: Frank tells Jimmy that it's abhorrent that he's doing these things and that he needs to get help right away.
moral_consequence: Jimmy agrees that it's wrong and that he is losing the fight with his demons and vows to get help.
immoral_action: Frank tells Jimmy that we all have desires and that Jimmy's desires are normal like anyone elses.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy feels emboldened to continue abducting and abusing children, destroying many lives in the process.

norm: You shouldn't skip out on your chores.
situation: Malcolm is at home and his mother told him to do some chores for her before going out.
intention: Malcolm wants to get out of the house.
moral_action: Malcolm makes sure to do everything that was asked of him around the house before heading out.
moral_consequence: Malcolm has a fun time out and enjoys the earned trust he has with his mother.
immoral_action: Malcolm sneaks out right away without finishing any tasks that were asked of him.
immoral_consequence: When Malcolm gets home he is punished by his mother for not doing his chores before leaving.

norm: You shouldn't back out of an agreement.
situation: Tony finds a car he likes for sell in the paper and agrees to purchase it from the seller when he gets paid that Friday.
intention: Tony wants to get a reliable car at an affordable price.
moral_action: Tony gets paid Friday and is able to get the seller to take off another $200 dollars when he pays for the car.
moral_consequence: The seller uses the funds from the sell of his car to catch up on some overdue bills.
immoral_action: Tony buys a cheaper car the next day and never tells the previous seller he doesn't want his car.
immoral_consequence: The seller sees Tony at a store in the other vehicle and keys his car because he's angry at him for his behavior.

norm: It is good to support family when they are struggling.
situation: John's mother McKenzie is senile and needs to go to a nursing home.
intention: John wants to save his money.
moral_action: John looks for a decent nursing home and asks around for discounts and support from the community.
moral_consequence: McKenzie is well looked after and happy and thrives.
immoral_action: John finds McKenzie the cheapest nursing home around and puts her there.
immoral_consequence: McKenzie is not well looked after and unhappy and gets sick.

norm: It is good to get your kids vaccinated.
situation: Bea has never taken her infant son to get his vaccination shots.
intention: Bea wants to keep her son safe during the flu season.
moral_action: Bea takes her son to the doctor in order to get his flu shot.
moral_consequence: Bea's son stays safe and healthy all through the flu season.
immoral_action: Bea gives her son Vitamin C every day to keep the flu away.
immoral_consequence: Bea's son gets the flu and has to be admitted into the hospital.

norm: It's wrong to refuse to report child abuse.
situation: Sam is a teacher and a student comes to him, telling Sam that he is being abused and that he doesn't know what to do.
intention: Sam wants to avoid making the situation worse.
moral_action: Sam contacts his supervisor and reports the abuse that the student told him about.
moral_consequence: Sam's supervisor goes to the authorities who intervene and stop the abuse.
immoral_action: Sam gives the student some general advice about what to do and lets the issue drop.
immoral_consequence: The abuse continues and the student is emotionally scarred for life.

norm: It's cruel to hurt an animal.
situation: Lisa comes home and finds that her new puppy has peed on her rug.
intention: Lisa wants to teach the puppy not to pee on the rug.
moral_action: Lisa follows house breaking guidelines for a puppy.
moral_consequence: Lisa is able to train the pup and their bond grows.
immoral_action: Lisa drags the puppy to the rug and beats it repeatedly with her fist.
immoral_consequence: Lisa loses the puppy's trust and is unable to train it.

norm: It is hurtful to exclude a friend from a game.
situation: Dave is a team captain of a baseball game when Will, who can hardly play at all, wants to join his team.
intention: Dave wants to win the game.
moral_action: Dave takes Will onto his team and assigns him to be the catcher.
moral_consequence: Will learns to catch a ball and feels involved in the game without posing a big risk to his team.
immoral_action: Dave decides not to take Will because he's not very good, and he wants to win.
immoral_consequence: Will feels rejected and loses self-esteem, drifting away from his friends.

norm: It's bad to steal apples from the orchard.
situation: Dan lives near an orchard and see delicious apples on the trees.
intention: Dan wants to eat apples.
moral_action: Dan asks the owner of the orchard if he can have some apples.
moral_consequence: The owner of the orchard gives Dan a few apples.
immoral_action: Dan takes apples without asking the owner of the orchard.
immoral_consequence: The owner of the orchard accuses Dan of theft.

norm: It's wrong to lie about your parents being dead.
situation: Paulie has just moved to a new school where he does not know anyone and is having trouble meeting people.
intention: Paulie wants to make friends at school.
moral_action: Paulie joins some after school clubs that he is interested in.
moral_consequence: Paulie meets other students with the same interests as him and befriends them.
immoral_action: Paulie tells everyone he is an orphan because he thinks it will make him memorable and sympathetic.
immoral_consequence: Paulie's lie is quickly discovered and his classmates ostracize him for being a liar.

norm: You should take good care of your teeth.
situation: James always felt rushed in the morning when he was getting ready for school.
intention: James wants to save time in the morning.
moral_action: James starts brushing his teeth in the school bathroom after he eats breakfast and lunch in the cafeteria.
moral_consequence: James is able to sleep a little longer in the mornings while still keeping his teeth clean.
immoral_action: James stops brushing his teeth, so he can get a few extra minutes of sleep.
immoral_consequence: James' classmates start complaining about the eye-watering smell of his breath.

norm: It is rude to disturb the people around you.
situation: John is at the school library trying to study for finals surrounded by other students.
intention: John wants to ask a fellow student who's not present a question about study materials.
moral_action: John steps outside the library to make his phone call to the other student.
moral_consequence: Other students in the library appreciate John being so considerate.
immoral_action: John calls his fellow student from the library and has a long animated discussion with him.
immoral_consequence: Other students are aggravated with John because he's disturbing their studies.

norm: It's good to use social media.
situation: Jeff has started his own company and even has a Facebook page for it.
intention: Jeff wants to spread the word of his company.
moral_action: Jeff interacts with his customers every day on his Facebook page.
moral_consequence: Jeff gains more and more customers through his social media page.
immoral_action: Jeff tells a few of his neighbors that he has started a new company.
immoral_consequence: Business for Jeff doesn't grow as much as he expected, and he has to shut down.

norm: It's good to score points when playing games.
situation: David is playing a game with his younger brother, and his younger brother is horrible at video games.
intention: David wants his little brother to win the game.
moral_action: David gives his little brother some tips on how to score points before playing the game.
moral_consequence: David's little brother uses David's advice to overtake Danial on  the last turn winning the game.
immoral_action: David loses the game on purpose trying his best to not score a single point.
immoral_consequence: David's younger brother figures out David's plan, and he's sad that David thinks so little of his abilities.

norm: Safety is important
situation: Jill just bought a new motorcycle.
intention: Jill wants to take it out for a drive.
moral_action: Jill reviews the handbook on safe motorcycle handling she got from her riding classes.
moral_consequence: Jill enjoys the new bike and takes it out every weekend.
immoral_action: Jill doesn't like the way the helmet fits, so she leaves it behind.
immoral_consequence: Jill crashes and suffers a skull fracture.

norm: It's expected to keep your pets on a leech.
situation: James took his border collie on long walks because she was very high-energy.
intention: James wants to wear his border collie out, so she's not hyper at home.
moral_action: James keeps his border collie on her leash and walks her for a full hour.
moral_consequence: When James gets home, his border collie flops on the floor, exhausted.
immoral_action: James lets his border collie off her leash, so she can run around as he walks.
immoral_consequence: James' border collie jumps on another pedestrian, and they threaten to call animal control.

norm: You should always keep your eye on the weather conditions.
situation: Lou wakes up one day in March and notices that it is very warm outside.
intention: Lou wants to enjoy the unseasonably nice weather.
moral_action: Lou checks the weather and sees that winter like conditions will arrive in the next few hours.
moral_consequence: Lou goes for a short walk in a park near his hom and is back home before the storm comes in.
immoral_action: Lou decides on a whim to drive a couple of hours out to a state park in order to hike and have a picnic.
immoral_consequence: A sudden temperature drop followed by a snow comes in by early afternoon leaving Lou stranded in a rural area during a blizzard.

norm: It is wrong to not look for your dog.
situation: Tony is having a very bad week and realizes that his dog is missing.
intention: Tom wants to find his dog.
moral_action: Tom goes out and looks for his dog.
moral_consequence: Tom finds his dog and his dog is so happy that the joy of hugging him completely overwhelms his exhaustion and makes him feel great.
immoral_action: Tom tells his neighbor he is tired and asks if the neighbor will look for his dog while he rests.
immoral_consequence: His neighbor finds the dog but brings it to the shelter because they don't feel Tom is a fit owner.

norm: It's wrong to hate someone based on skin color
situation: Ronald doesn't like his coworker Steve very much at all, Steve asks why.
intention: Ronald wants to answer Steve.
moral_action: Ronald answers that Steve borrowed his pen on the first day and never gave it back.
moral_consequence: Steve apologizes to Ronald and gives him the pen back at once.
immoral_action: Ronald answers that he doesn't like Steve because of the amount of melanin in his skin.
immoral_consequence: Now no one at work likes Ronald at all because of this.

norm: It's bad to expect others to clean up after you.
situation: Luke, a child who hates cleaning up, leaves his room a mess.
intention: Luke wants his room to be clean.
moral_action: Luke takes all of the stuff on the floor in his room and dumps it into a large box.
moral_consequence: Luke's parents are proud of Luke's initiative and reward him.
immoral_action: Luke tells his parents that they should clean his room because he's their responsibility.
immoral_consequence: Luke's parents refuse to clean Luke's room and are offended at his rudeness.

norm: Expecting an expensive gift from your friend is selfish
situation: Robin's best friend gives her a handmade gift for her 40th birthday.
intention: Robin wants to acknowledge the gift.
moral_action: Robin appreciates the thoughtfulness behind the gift.
moral_consequence: Robin's best friend is thrilled that her gift was so well received.
immoral_action: Robin expresses her disappointment in the cheap gift.
immoral_consequence: Robin's best friend is hurt by her reaction.

norm: It's bad to not be true to yourself.
situation: Mik is hanging out with friends from school, and they're trying cigarettes which he finds gross.
intention: Mik wants to get along with his friends.
moral_action: Mik turns down the cigarettes but says he's cool with them smoking.
moral_consequence: They don't harrass Mik and he develops independence.
immoral_action: Mik smokes and says he likes it, even though he doesn't.
immoral_consequence: His friends keep asking him to smoke with them, building pressure.

norm: It's bad to end a relationship by just disappearing.
situation: Beatrice is dating Matt and thinks the relationship isn't working out.
intention: Beatrice wants to stop dating Matt.
moral_action: Beatrice tells Matt that the relationship is not working out.
moral_consequence: Matt will know that Beatrice does not want to date him, and he'll move on.
immoral_action: Beatrice stops answering Matt's calls and avoids him.
immoral_consequence: Matt will be confused by the way Beatrice is acting and not know the relationship is over.

norm: It's not okay to disrespect people and their traditions.
situation: Kate is lost in the city, and while walking past a mosque she see's a woman coming out wearing a burka.
intention: Kate wants to talk to the woman.
moral_action: Kate goes up to the woman and asks if she can point her in the right direction.
moral_consequence: The woman is happy to help and tells Kate how to reach her destination.
immoral_action: Kate, trying to break the ice before asking for directions, asks the woman if she's a ninja.
immoral_consequence: The woman is deeply offended and says that wearing it is a part  of her culture, so Kate ends up feeling foolish and doesn't get directions.

norm: It's not okay to have a double standard about things.
situation: Philip runs a small stock trading company that has an even number of male and female traders.
intention: Philip wants his company to succeed.
moral_action: Philip assess his traders individually and sends his strongest traders the best accounts regardless of sex.
moral_consequence: Philip builds a dynamic team that help grow his business.
immoral_action: Philip believes that men are more aggressive than women, so he sends male employees the larger accounts.
immoral_consequence: Philip looses many talented  female traders when they are poached by other companies.

norm: You should never physically attack another person
situation: Jasper wants to play Animal Crossing, but his brother refuses to share the Nintendo Switch.
intention: Jasper wants to play games.
moral_action: Jasper decides to play a game like Animal Crossing on the computer.
moral_consequence: Jasper meets new friends playing the game.
immoral_action: Jasper pushes his brother onto the ground and yanks the Nintendo Switch away from him.
immoral_consequence: Jasper is grounded after his brother tells his mom what happened.

norm: It's inconsiderate to blare your base in a residential neighborhood.
situation: Scott listens to rap music in the garage while working on his car.
intention: Scott wants to enjoy music as he works.
moral_action: Scott grabs his headphones and works on his car.
moral_consequence: Scott is realxed as he works and get the job done quickly.
immoral_action: Scott blares the music at full volume through his sound system.
immoral_consequence: Scott has the police called on him and is fined for violating an ordinance.

norm: It's wrong to make fun of people with disabilities
situation: Don is walking down the street when he encounters a man with one leg hobbling along.
intention: Don wants to feel good about himself.
moral_action: Don offers the man assistance and ask him how he is.
moral_consequence: The one legged man thanks Don and is happy.
immoral_action: Don breaks out laughing at the guy and impersonates him.
immoral_consequence: The one-legged man becomes angry and insults Don.

norm: It's wrong to make assumptions without evidence.
situation: Jane discovered that someone has eaten the sandwich she left on the kitchen counter for herself, with suspects including her dog and her roommate.
intention: Jane wants to eat a sandwich.
moral_action: Jane sees mustard surrounding the outer parts of her dog's mouth, realizes he was the culprit, and makes a replacement sandwich for herself.
moral_consequence: Jane is more aware and does not leave her food unattended in the future.
immoral_action: Jane accuses her roommate of taking her food, as he has done once before, and eats a sandwich he was keeping in his fridge.
immoral_consequence: Jane's relationship with her roommate continues to become strained and awkward.

norm: It is mean to make fun of people.
situation: Oliver is asked by his teacher to solve a math problem on the chalkboard for the rest of the class, but he is having difficulty.
intention: The class wants to react to Oliver.
moral_action: The class is patient while Oliver tries to solve it, and when he fails they quietly listen to the teachers explanation.
moral_consequence: Oliver is relieved no one insulted him and will have no issues going before the class in the future.
immoral_action: The class begins to make jokes and laugh at Oliver's inability to get the equation right.
immoral_consequence: Oliver is embarrassed and no longer has confidence to stand before the class again.

norm: Expecting someone to work without properly paying them is wrong.
situation: Bill is a project manager whose team is falling behind on a project with an important deadline coming up.
intention: Bill wants to get the project done over the weekend.
moral_action: Bill offers overtime for team members to work on the weekend.
moral_consequence: The team is happy to make some extra money.
immoral_action: Bill convinces his team to do volunteer work to finish the project.
immoral_consequence: The team resents having to work for free.

norm: You shouldn't expect your friends to do certain things.
situation: Greg, who loves extreme sports, is on a trip with some friends when he sees a bungee jumping place nearby.
intention: Greg wants to go bungee jumping.
moral_action: Greg asks his friends to drop him off at the bungee jumping place and to pick him up in a few hours.
moral_consequence: Greg's friends work to please Greg and are grateful that they don't have to do it with him.
immoral_action: Greg tells his friends that they need to go bungee jumping and keeps telling them until they give in.
immoral_consequence: Greg's friends have a bad experience bungee jumping and resent Greg for his selfishness.

norm: You shouldn't bite into an onion.
situation: Ivan buys a large, yellow onion at a local vegetable market.
intention: Ivan wants to eat the onion.
moral_action: Ivan chops up the onion and sautes it with a little oil.
moral_consequence: Ivan thinks the sauteed onion tastes delicious and uses it to enhance a spaghetti sauce.
immoral_action: Ivan bites directly into the onion without prepping or cooking it.
immoral_consequence: Ivan thinks it tastes too strange and ends up wasting the onion by throwing it away.

norm: It's rude to destroy someone's glasses.
situation: John is going to the movies with his mom.
intention: John wants to get a good seat in the theater.
moral_action: John sees that the couple in front of him has better seats, so he asks if he can pay to trade seats and they agree.
moral_consequence: John has a great time at the theater with his mom.
immoral_action: The couple in front of John gets better seats than him, so he breaks the mans glasses they are upset and leave, John takes there seats.
immoral_consequence: Johns mother is very mad at him, and she goes home.

norm: It's rude to make obnoxious noises in the workplace.
situation: Haru notices that his coworkers seem stressed after a tense meeting.
intention: Haru wants to make his coworkers smile.
moral_action: Haru offers to pick up something from Starbucks for his coworkers on his break.
moral_consequence: Haru wins the most thoughtful coworker of the month award at the end of the month.
immoral_action: Haru acts like a chicken making chicken noises while moving around the room.
immoral_consequence: Haru's reputation at work suffers.

norm: You shouldn't cause pain and discomfort to other people.
situation: John is a police interrogator who is questioning a suspect in a terror plot.
intention: John wants to receive information from the suspect.
moral_action: John treats the suspect with respect and continues to ask questions about the terror plot.
moral_consequence: The suspect refuses to speak to John.
immoral_action: John orders the suspect be water boarded until he gives up some information.
immoral_consequence: The suspect cracks and agrees to tell John anything he wants to hear, but John can't tell if the information is reliable.

norm: It's hurtful to doubt people.
situation: Kate is gym teacher, and one of her students wants to be a pro baseball player.
intention: Kate wants to say something to the kid.
moral_action: Kate tells the kid that if they keep working then it might happen.
moral_consequence: The kid feels motivated to work even harder to be a baseball player.
immoral_action: Kate tells the kid that there's no chance that they make it to the majors.
immoral_consequence: The kid's feelings are hurt, and they're embarrassed in front of the class.

norm: You shouldn't text people when you're drunk.
situation: Max has had a few drink and is thinking about a conversation he had with his boss earlier.
intention: Max wants to remember to follow up with his boss about the conversation.
moral_action: Max makes a note to himself on his mobile phone and sets an alarm for the next day to remind him to follow up with his boss about the conversation.
moral_consequence: Max wakes up to his alarm the next day and is reminded about the conversation which he follows up on.
immoral_action: Max decides to send some messages to his boss with his mobile phone about the conversation.
immoral_consequence: Max's messages don't make any sense because he had been drinking and it leads to embarrassment at work.

norm: It's good to show compassion to those with illness.
situation: Irvine is shopping when he receives a selfie from his bald sister after another round of chemotherapy.
intention: Irvine wants to buy something.
moral_action: Irvine borrows more money and buys his sister a wig.
moral_consequence: Irvine and his sister have fun taking selfies with his sister's new hair.
immoral_action: Irvine buys himself a new video game, and spends the evening playing at home.
immoral_consequence: Irvine feels bad for not doing more for his sister.

norm: You shouldn't take advantage of people while they are sleeping.
situation: Maria wakes up next to a strange man who she does not remember meeting the night before, while he is still asleep.
intention: Maria wants to get home.
moral_action: Maria wakes the man up to talk with him, so that she can find out more about the situation and the information she needs to get home.
moral_consequence: Both Maria and the strange man become more fully aware of their behaviors, and they part ways with more of a mutual sense of respect and self-awareness.
immoral_action: Maria finds the strange man's wallet and goes through it to find his address and any other information that she can.
immoral_consequence: The man will feel violated and have resentment and distrust for Maria, and Maria will feel a sense of shame for invading a stranger's privacy.

norm: It's wrong to make assumptions based on race and gender.
situation: When James showed up for the technical meeting, the only other person there was an African-American woman.
intention: James wants to greet the other person in the meeting room.
moral_action: "James says, ""Hi, I don't think we've met - I'm the product designer""."
moral_consequence: "The woman responds, ""Pleased to meet you, I'm the CTO,"" and continues making small talk."
immoral_action: "James says, ""Hi, are you the secretary for the engineering department?""."
immoral_consequence: "The woman raises her eyebrows and says, ""No, I'm the CTO,"" making the rest of the meeting very awkward."

norm: It's bad to throw rocks when people are around.
situation: Brad is walking and comes across a large puddle of water.
intention: He wants to skip a rock across it.
moral_action: Brad waits until no one is around before skipping the rock.
moral_consequence: Brad laughs with delight as the rock skips safely along the puddle.
immoral_action: Brad skips the rock while lots of other people are walking in the area.
immoral_consequence: Brad accidentally hits a small girl in the head with the rock and it knocks her out.

norm: You shouldn't charge people too much money.
situation: Sam is a plumber who is going to repair a leaking pipe at a home.
intention: Sam wants to earn extra money for Christmas gifts.
moral_action: Sam charges a high but fair rate for the service.
moral_consequence: Sam gains a loyal customer in the process.
immoral_action: Sam overcharges the customer because they have no way of knowing how much it should cost.
immoral_consequence: Sam feels guilty for charging too much.

norm: It's wrong to smoke pot when you're a kid.
situation: Jimmy found a joint on the sidewalk when he was walking to school in the morning.
intention: Jimmy wants to know what it's like to smoke pot.
moral_action: Jimmy doesn't pick up the joint but that night he asks his mom what it feels like to smoke pot.
moral_consequence: Jimmy's mom is happy that Jimmy didn't smoke the pot, and they have fun watching the movie Pineapple Express together that evening.
immoral_action: Jimmy lights up the joint and gets super high before going to class.
immoral_consequence: The school calls Jimmy's mom, and she has to leave an important meeting at work to go to the school after Jimmy is suspended.

norm: You shouldn't try to be controlling of your loved ones.
situation: Bill is married to Evelyn, but Bill thinks Evelyn is saying bad things about him to her friends.
intention: Bill wants to deal with his suspicions about Evelyn.
moral_action: Bill realizes he can't control Evelyn's every move, and trusts her to respect him.
moral_consequence: Evelyn respects and loves Bill and the two have a happy marriage.
immoral_action: Bill insists that Evelyn no longer hang out with her friends.
immoral_consequence: Evelyn resents Bill for trying to control her, and separates from him.

norm: It's good to spend time with your significant other.
situation: Dan has an extra ticket to a romance movie and his friends and family are all available to come.
intention: Dan wants to go to the movies with someone.
moral_action: Dan decided to pick his wife to go with him to the movie, and they go.
moral_consequence: Dan's wife enjoys the type of movie that is playing and Dan feels proud he picked the right movie.
immoral_action: Dan goes with a non-family friend to the movies, who he is not otherwise intimate with Dan.
immoral_consequence: Dan's friend is weirded out at the movie choice and Dan feel humiliated during the movie.

norm: It's nice to help keep a communal living space tidy.
situation: Lenny is cooking in the kitchen that he shares with George.
intention: Lenny wants to get back to his video games.
moral_action: Lenny finishes cooking and loads all of his dirty dishes into the dish washer before playing.
moral_consequence: George is relaxed and asks if he can play games with Lenny.
immoral_action: Lenny finishes cooking but leaves his pots and pans all over the stove and counter to play games.
immoral_consequence: George is very annoyed with Lenny and turns his game off in the middle of a match.

norm: People should advocate for ways of increasing public safety.
situation: Dale lives on a dangerous street that has a lot of car racing.
intention: Dale wants to figure out a way to avoid the danger.
moral_action: Dale writes letters to the government asking for more police patrolling on the street.
moral_consequence: The car racing is stopped by the police.
immoral_action: Dale moves to a different area of town.
immoral_consequence: The car racing is still prevalent on the street Dave used to live on.

norm: It's wrong to make obscene gestures at people.
situation: Jim is at a party with his friends when he sees a beautiful woman across the room.
intention: Jim wants to get the attention of the woman.
moral_action: Jim goes near the woman and introduces himself to her and her friends.
moral_consequence: The woman is charmed by Jim and agrees to go with him on a date.
immoral_action: Jim goes near the woman and starts to make sexually charged gestures.
immoral_consequence: The woman is upset and gets her friends to throw Jim out of the party.

norm: Talking during a concert is considered rude.
situation: Tammy is sitting in the audience at the symphony when she remembers something she forgot to tell her mom.
intention: Tammy wants to call her mom.
moral_action: Tammy waits for intermission and call her mom in the lobby.

norm: It's unusual to surround yourself with hate.

norm: It's rude to make faces at someone else's appearance.

norm: Cutting people off on the street is considered rude.

norm: It's ok to leave a job you don't like.

norm: It's wrong to break up with someone over something small.

norm: It's irresponsible to shirk work in favor of camping.

norm: It's rude to try to make customers leave.

norm: It's bad to yell at anyone.
