moral_action: Carl puts his video game controller on the floor and walks out of the room.
moral_consequence: Carl leaves his friend's house and plays the game with him another time.
immoral_action: Carl takes the video game console and throws it on the floor.
immoral_consequence: Carl has to pay to replace his friend's broken video game console.

norm: You can't expect everyone to be good at things.
situation: James, and avid and experienced rock climber, is planning a trip for himself and some friends to a canyon.
intention: James wants to decide whether to include a rock climbing session in the trip.
moral_action: James decides to omit the activity as he remembers at least a couple of his friends are older and probably wouldn't like rock climbing.
moral_consequence: James friends have a great trip together and no one is embarrassed about their inadequacies.
immoral_action: James decides that since he loves rock climbing he will go ahead and include the activity in the trip planning.
immoral_consequence: Once James' friends find out about the rock climbing they're disappointed as they're physically unable to take part and thus feel left out.

norm: It's not okay to hover over other people's children.
situation: Jenna took her toddler to the playground and saw a five year old swinging on the swings by herself.
intention: Jenna wants to make sure the five year old doesn't fall off the swings.
moral_action: Jenna watches the five year old from a park bench until she notices her call out to her mother ten feet away.
moral_consequence: Jenna is satisfied that the five year old is being adequately watched.
immoral_action: Jenna keeps asking the five year old if she wants Jenna to push her.
immoral_consequence: After the third time the five year old says no, her mother comes to tell Jenna to leave her alone.

norm: You shouldn't forget someone's name.
situation: Bill is starting his second day at work after meeting his co-workers for the first time yesterday.
intention: Bill wants to greet the office receptionist.
moral_action: Bill greets the receptionist using her first name.
moral_consequence: The receptionist appreciations that Bill remembers her name and feels friendly toward Bill.
immoral_action: "Bill says ""Hi Jennifer"" although the receptionists name is Jan."
immoral_consequence: The receptionist feels insulated that Bill didn't remember her name and is unfriendly to Bill.

norm: You should not take advantage of others.
situation: Ed was been out of work and his friend Brian has offered to let him stay at his place for a while.
intention: Ed wants to stay with Brian.
moral_action: Ed tries hard to get a job so that he can split the rent with Brian and pay his share of everything.
moral_consequence: Brian tells Ed that he likes having him stay with him.
immoral_action: Ed spends his days playing computer games and doesn't try to find a job or offer Brian any money for food or rent.
immoral_consequence: Brian gets upset with Ed and tells him that he'll have to leave soon if he doesn't go find a job.

norm: You shouldn't use road flares to destroy property.
situation: Roger is arguing with another driver on the side of the road after a minor car accident.
intention: Roger wants to end the argument.
moral_action: Roger calmly responds to the person and provides them with his insurance information.
moral_consequence: Roger is able to have his insurance cover the damage.
immoral_action: Roger picks up a road flare and throws it into the person's car, setting it on fire.
immoral_consequence: Roger is arrested and put in jail.

norm: It's wrong to laugh at someone.
situation: Jane's history class has been preparing presentations, and they are ready to start delivering them.
intention: Jane wants to listen to Martin's presentation and comment on it.
moral_action: "After Martin presents, Jane asks, ""How did you select such an interesting topic?""."
moral_consequence: Martin explains his thought process.
immoral_action: "After Martin presents, Jane asks, ""Why did you pick such a silly topic?"" and laughs."
immoral_consequence: Martin is embarrassed and the class scowls at Jane for being rude.

norm: It's wrong to use your neighbor's stuff without their permission.
situation: Mitchell's getting ready to go to the garage to get his mower when he notices his neighbors mower is already outside on the lawn.
intention: Mitchell wants to decide which mower to use.
moral_action: Mitchell decides to walk an extra ten feet and get his own mower from his garage.
moral_consequence: The neighbor comes outside and sees Mitchell mowing, so he says hi and gives him a wave.
immoral_action: Mitchell decides to use the neighbor's mower since it's right there, and he won't be long.
immoral_consequence: The neighbor comes out to see Mitchell using his mower and is upset that Mitchell would just assume he can borrow  it.

norm: You should always help people out at work.
situation: Gary is in his office at work when Glen, a coworker, comes over and asks for help on an Excel macro.
intention: Gary wants to respond to Glen's request.
moral_action: Gary tells Glen that he'll come over to his desk and show him how to do it.
moral_consequence: Glen is delighted that Gary will help him and relieved he'll figure out how to create a macro.
immoral_action: Gary tells Glen that they probably have a manual somewhere around here, and he should look there.
immoral_consequence: Glen is annoyed because he's aware that there are manuals, and he was requesting human help.

norm: It is disgusting to vomit on others.
situation: Peter just drank some milk from his friend Brian's fridge that was expired and now he feels queasy while Brian looks on beside him.
intention: Peter wants to puke.
moral_action: Peter leaves Brian to run to the toilet where he throws up.
moral_consequence: Brian appreciates Peter respecting his house by running to the bathroom.
immoral_action: Peter remains standing near Brian and throws up all over his shirt.
immoral_consequence: Brian is grossed out and begins to feel nauseous himself.

norm: It's rude to unset your partner's alarms.
situation: James lives with his girlfriend and has the day off while his girlfriend has work.
intention: James wants to sleep in late.
moral_action: James sleeps on the couch, so he won't be bothered by his girlfriend getting ready early.
moral_consequence: James' girlfriend can get to work on time without disturbing him.
immoral_action: James turns off his girlfriend's alarm so it won't bother him.
immoral_consequence: James' girlfriend is late for work and gets in trouble.

norm: You shouldn't disturb your roommates at night.
situation: Paul and Dane are in their dorm room at night, as Dane tries to get a good night's sleep because he has a test tomorrow.
intention: Paul wants to listen to music.
moral_action: Paul puts on a set of headphones and listens to his music in the dark.
moral_consequence: Dane gets a good night's sleep and so is well-rested for his test, which he does well on.
immoral_action: Paul turns his stereo all the way up and rocks out for hours.
immoral_consequence: Dane can't get to sleep and ends up doing poorly on his test because he's so tired.

norm: You should maintain your relationships with your friends.
situation: Maggie has just created a profile on Facebook.
intention: Maggie wants to do something with her profile.
moral_action: Maggie adds her friends and old contacts from her college days.
moral_consequence: Maggie is able to keep up with her friends daily activities.
immoral_action: Maggie fills out her profile and uploads pictures before logging out for months.
immoral_consequence: Maggie wastes her day filling out a profile she'll never use.

norm: It is reckless to leave your wallet at a bar.
situation: Steve is drunk and tired, he left the bar, forgetting his coat, and in it, his wallet, not realizing until he's in an uber on his way home.
intention: Steve wants to get home.
moral_action: Steve asks the Uber driver to turn around, so he can get his stuff.
moral_consequence: Steve ends up getting his stuff, and hopping back in the uber to go home.
immoral_action: Steve doesn't say anything to the uber driver, and just goes home, figuring he'll get the wallet the next day.
immoral_consequence: The jacket and wallet are stolen before the bartender notices them sitting there.

norm: It's weird to have a sugar baby.
situation: Steve is an single older man who is feels lonely most of the time.
intention: Steve wants female companionship.
moral_action: Steve gets to know a woman at a social event that he then starts dating.
moral_consequence: Steve's relationship is based on common interests.
immoral_action: Steve pays a younger woman to provide him with companionship.
immoral_consequence: Steve's relationship is dependent on him having money.

norm: It's rude to eat all of something.
situation: John's mother makes a batch of cookies for her children.
intention: John wants to satisfy his craving for a cookie.
moral_action: John eats one cookie and leaves the rest to share with his siblings.
moral_consequence: John's siblings are happy and excited to eat some of the cookies.
immoral_action: John eats all the cookies and leaves none for his siblings to eat.
immoral_consequence: John's siblings are sad and upset with him for being selfish.

norm: You shouldn't steal from someone's house.
situation: Matt's savings were running low.
intention: Matt wants to make more money.
moral_action: Matt obtains a new job with a higher salary than his old job.
moral_consequence: Matt's income increases, and he is able to save more money at the end of each month.
immoral_action: Matt breaks into his neighbor's house and takes their jewelry and electronics.
immoral_consequence: Matt is caught in the act and is arrested and convicted.

norm: It is unusual for affairs to go on indefinitely.
situation: James started sleeping with one of his coworkers when he and his wife were going through a trial separation.
intention: James wants to avoid an expensive divorce.
moral_action: James breaks up with his coworker and starts going to couples' therapy with his wife.
moral_consequence: James and his wife eventually reconcile most of their differences.
immoral_action: James continues to see his coworker while still living with his wife.
immoral_consequence: James' wife discovers the affair after a decade and throws all his stuff on the lawn.

norm: It's good to keep track of your pets.
situation: Owen was walking his dog in the park one afternoon.
intention: Owen wants to let his dog run in the grass.
moral_action: Owen jogs alongside his dog when he is running through the grass.
moral_consequence: Owen and his dog are both able to get exercise in the park.
immoral_action: Owen takes the leash off of his dog and lets it run around by itself.
immoral_consequence: Owen's dog runs far from him and gets lost and Owen never finds it again.

norm: You should not make accusations against friends
situation: Will's leather jacket has gone missing at school, and he thinks that Mike might have it.
intention: Will wants to see if Mike has the jacket.
moral_action: Will asks Mike if he has seen the jacket anywhere.
moral_consequence: Mike tells Will that he saw the jacket in the principal's office.
immoral_action: Will accuses Mike of taking the jacket and goes through his belongings to find it.
immoral_consequence: Mike gets mad at will for assuming that he would steal from him.

norm: You shouldn't break things on purpose.
situation: James' wife bought a lamp in the shape of a fishnet-covered leg that he found very offensive.
intention: James doesn't want to have to look at the lamp.
moral_action: James asks his wife if she can move the lamp from their living room to her home office.
moral_consequence: James' wife puts the lamp next to her desk where James doesn't have to look at it.
immoral_action: James knocks the lamp over and tells his husband that he accidentally smashed it.
immoral_consequence: James' wife is so upset that she doesn't talk to James for two days.

norm: It's good to invite people over to your house.
situation: Mary and her classmates want to hold a sleepover party and are deciding where to hold it.
intention: Mary wants to respond to the decision.
moral_action: Mary volunteers to hold the sleepover party in her house.
moral_consequence: Mary feels relaxed and happy as she doesn't need to worry about packing things.
immoral_action: Mary emphasizes that her house is too small to accommodate her friends and opines that it should be held in somebody's house.
immoral_consequence: Mary ends up having to pack many belongings and needs her mom to drive her to the sleepover party.

norm: It's good to recognize an employees long tenure.
situation: Steve is the CEO of a company that has been around for a long time.
intention: Steve wants to hold a conference where he talks about the emloyees.
moral_action: Steve says the older employees are the foundation of the company and gives them awards.
moral_consequence: The older employees will want to work hard for the company and set a good example.
immoral_action: Steve says the young employees are the future and the older employees are the past.
immoral_consequence: The older employees will feel disgruntled and not want to work as hard.

norm: It's not okay to pressure people into things.
situation: Tom and Jan went over to Tom's place after watching a movie, and Tom wants to convince her to have sex.
intention: Tom wants to have sex with Jan.
moral_action: Tom tells Jan that he wants to have sex only if she's okay with it.
moral_consequence: Jan feels comfortable with Tom and is more willing to have sex with him.
immoral_action: Tom asks Jan why she would come to his place if she didn't want to have sex.
immoral_consequence: Jan feels guilty and decides to have sex to make Tom feel better.

norm: It's good to want to show someone you appreciate them.
situation: Ann finally got a good paying job, and she knows her mom is responsible for her being in this position.
intention: Ann wants to decide whether to buy her mom something.
moral_action: Ann buys her mom a new electric car so that it lasts a long time.
moral_consequence: Ann's mom figures out how grateful Ann is for her.
immoral_action: Ann wants to save her money, so she decides not to buy any gifts.
immoral_consequence: Ann's mom is not made aware of how grateful Ann is for her.

norm: It's not polite to refuse an invitation from your partner.
situation: Jim's girlfriend invites him to come have dinner with her and her family.
intention: Jim wants to let his girlfriend know if he's coming for dinner with her family.
moral_action: Jim accepts his girlfriend's invitation to have dinner with her family.
moral_consequence: Jim's girlfriend feels closer to him because he's willing to spend time visiting with her family.
immoral_action: Jim says he won't go to dinner with her and her family because he would be uncomfortable.
immoral_consequence: Jim's girlfriend is insulted that he won't come and spend some time with her family.

norm: It's not okay to want to show off or brag.
situation: Courtney is a wealthy girl who attends a school with kids from varying socioeconomic backgrounds, and her dad recently bought her a designer backpack.
intention: Courtney wants to wear her new backpack to school.
moral_action: Courtney takes her backpack to school without mentioning it to anyone.
moral_consequence: Courtney is able to wear her bag without hurting anyone's feelings.
immoral_action: Courtney points out her new backpack to all of her classmates, being sure to mention the designer and price tag.
immoral_consequence: The lesser well-off kids in Courtney's class feel that what they have is inadequate.

norm: It's wrong to not take care of your health.
situation: Devin hadn't been feeling well and had started to miss days at work.
intention: Devin wants to feel better.
moral_action: Devin goes to the doctor to see what is wrong with him.
moral_consequence: The doctor gives Devin some medicine, and he is good enough to go back to work later that day.
immoral_action: Devin takes a nap the first thing in the morning when he gets to work.
immoral_consequence: Devin's boss sends him home, and he misses another day of work.

norm: You're expected to help your spouse with household chores.
situation: Fred is coming home exhausted from a stressful day at work and his wife was too busy with the kids to do the dishes.
intention: Fred wants to rest when he gets home.
moral_action: Fred takes a short nap when he gets home then does the dishes after.
moral_consequence: Fred's wife has more energy and time to take care of the kids the following day.
immoral_action: Fred turns in early for the night when he gets home.
immoral_consequence: The chores pile up and Fred's wife has even more to do the next day.

norm: It's bad to have no food.
situation: John is at the store shopping for tonight's date with Nancy which will be over at his house, and he's doing so because he has 0 consumables at home.
intention: John wants to buy something for them to consume.
moral_action: John decides to buy wine and a chacuterie board with cheese and meats because he thinks those pair well together.
moral_consequence: Nancy is delighted that John has served her both food and drink and thinks much more highly of him as a potential suitor.
immoral_action: John decides to buy wine and beer as he figures that Nancy will enjoy drinking with him.
immoral_consequence: Nancy is shocked when she sees that there is nothing to eat and refuses to drink on an empty stomach ruining her evening.

norm: It is wrong to eat food without permission.
situation: Tania's mom just baked a batch of delicious cupcakes for a party tomorrow.
intention: Tania wants to eat the cupcakes.
moral_action: Tania asks her mom if she can try a cupcake.
moral_consequence: Tania's mom gives her one cupcake and keeps the rest for the party.
immoral_action: Tania waits until her mom is out of the room, and then she takes eats several cupcakes.
immoral_consequence: Tania's mom does not have enough cupcakes to serve to her guests.

norm: You shouldn't fail all your classes.
situation: Rita had just started college and had bills to pay for her books.
intention: Rita wants to get a job.
moral_action: Rita gets a part time job in the book store on campus.
moral_consequence: Rita studies for her classes on her days off of her job.
immoral_action: Rita gets a full time job at the local grocery store in town.
immoral_consequence: Rita doesn't have time to study, and she fails all her classes.

norm: It's not okay to throw away things you can use.
situation: Jonah's wardrobe is stuffed after he purchased a lot of new clothes.
intention: Jonah wants to declutter his wardrobe.
moral_action: Jonah donates his old clothes to a charity.
moral_consequence: Jonah's old clothes are used by those who want and need them.
immoral_action: Jonah puts all his old in the garbage.
immoral_consequence: Jonah's old clothes get taken to the dump.

norm: People shouldn't be mean.
situation: Alice saw John break a vase unintentionally while playing in the family room.
intention: Alice wants to respond to the event.
moral_action: Alice asks John to cover the cost of the vase.
moral_consequence: John agrees to pay for the cost so that Alice can buy a new vase.
immoral_action: Alice blames John for being clumsy and careless.
immoral_consequence: John fights back and says that he will never come to Alice's home again.

norm: It's wrong to be proud of not tipping.
situation: Grant rides in a cab, makes it to his home and leaves without tipping.
intention: Grant wants to talk to his family about the cab.
moral_action: Grant talks to his family, and he was ashamed that he had no money for a tip.
moral_consequence: Grant's family conforts him and tells him that he should be happy to have made it home at all.
immoral_action: Grant brags to his family that he didn't tip and paid only the fair.
immoral_consequence: His family is upset but Grant kept talking about bringing the tipping system down.

norm: It's rude to use your housemate's things without permission.
situation: Jim, who lives with his roommate Sam, has work the next day but his car is in the shop.
intention: Jim wants to get to work.
moral_action: Jim gets up early the next morning and rides the bus to work.
moral_consequence: Jim arrives at work on time and has a productive day.
immoral_action: Jim takes Sam's car keys and borrows his car to go to work without asking first.
immoral_consequence: Jim gets yelled at later that day by Sam, who is furious that he took his car without permission.

norm: You shouldn't make messes.
situation: Eric has just cooked dinner for himself, dishes everywhere and his roommate John just got home.
intention: Eric wants to go to sleep early.
moral_action: Eric quickly washes his dishes and heads upstairs to eat and sleep.
moral_consequence: John has clean dishes to cook with and thinks Eric cares about him.
immoral_action: Eric goes upstairs to his room with his food without washing anything and eats and goes to bed.
immoral_consequence: John doesn't have any clean dishes to cook with and is very angry at Eric.

norm: You are expected to let others have their privacy.
situation: Tom overhears his roommate talking on the phone about some juicy gossip.
intention: Tom wants to know more about what they are talking about.
moral_action: Tom brings up a similar topic later with his roommate.
moral_consequence: Tom's roommate ends up sharing the gossip freely which Tom finds very entertaining.
immoral_action: Tom sits close to the wall, so he can continue to eavesdrop on the conversation.
immoral_consequence: Tom feels bad for listening in on the conversation.

norm: You shouldn't date multiple people without them knowing.
situation: Wally owns a company and enjoys spending his free time with women without becoming overly committed.
intention: Wally wants to have someone to be with.
moral_action: Wally finds one girl and dates her, going out with her on special weekends or during important events.
moral_consequence: The girl that Wally chose sees him frequently and doesn't feel neglected without being too close to him.
immoral_action: Wally meets and starts dating several girls in different locations, flying out to see each one on different weekends.
immoral_consequence: None of the girls are satisfied as Wally is rarely around for any one of them, and they all eventually leave him.

norm: You should accept and follow the rules
situation: Kelly just joined the swim team at school.
intention: Kelly wants to impress her new teammates.
moral_action: Kelly wants to dive, but instead chooses to show off her breast stroke.
moral_consequence: The other teammates think Kelly is very talented and ask her to help them with their breast strokes.
immoral_action: Kelly sees a sign that says, no diving, but does so anyway to much applause from the rest of the class.
immoral_consequence: The coach sees Kelly dive and cuts her from the team.

norm: You should report worrisome behavior to the authorities.
situation: Stephen has been noticing a suspicious car repeatedly driving by his neighbor's home for the past week.
intention: Stephen wants to stay within his boundaries.
moral_action: Stephen reports the suspicious activity to his neighbor, who reported it to police right away.
moral_consequence: The police presence in the neighborhood deterred the suspicious car from ever returning to the neighborhood.
immoral_action: Trying not to interfere, Stephen never mentions the suspicious activity to anyone.
immoral_consequence: Stephen's neighbor is robbed by the person who had been staking out his home.

norm: It's frowned upon to be addicted to drugs.
situation: Jennifer is an accountant, and has heard cocaine can keep you awake.
intention: Jennifer wants to stay awake.
moral_action: Jennifer decides to get to bed earlier to get more sleep at night.
moral_consequence: Jennifer is not as tired most days, and her work gets done more efficiently.
immoral_action: Jennifer starts taking cocaine and becomes addicted.
immoral_consequence: Jennifer loses her job after failing a drug test.

norm: It's rude to express that another culture's gatherings look ridiculous.
situation: Kyle is invited to a Diwali festival parade by his Indian friend Geet.
intention: Kyle wants to say something to Geet about the festival parade.
moral_action: Kyle tells Geet that the festival participants look very exotic and unlike anything he's ever seen.
moral_consequence: Geet proceeds to explain to Kyle the meaning and significance behind the costumes and dances in the parade.
immoral_action: Kyle tells Geet that the appearance, dress, and dance of the people in the parade seems primative and backwards.
immoral_consequence: Geet is insulted and gives Kyle the silent treatment for the rest of the day.

norm: It is phony to pretend to be something you aren't.
situation: Louis is a child who has been in commercials and has moved to a new town and school and is getting to know the other students.
intention: Louis wants to impress the other students.
moral_action: Louis tells the other children he is a child actor that has been in commercials.
moral_consequence: Louis will be able to relay his unique experiences and get attention.
immoral_action: Louis tells the other children he is a child actor that has been in big movies, which is false.
immoral_consequence: Louis will become stressed having to maintain the lie.

norm: It's irresponsible to not be vaccinated.
situation: Ann's doctor recommends her to get a flu shot so that she can be well protected from the coming flu season.
intention: Ann wants to react to the flu season.
moral_action: Ann gets the flu shot before the flu season comes.
moral_consequence: Ann does not get infected during the flu season and her coworker admires her smart decision.
immoral_action: Ann takes vitamin C every day thinking that her immune system will be strong enough to fight the flu.
immoral_consequence: Ann caught the flu and infected her coworker too.

norm: It's good to protect your own children.
situation: Lacey is in a relationship with Carter who supports her financially but has started treated Lacey's children poorly.
intention: Lacey wants to preserve the relationships that are most important to her.
moral_action: Lacey breaks up with Carter and takes her children with her to her parents home.
moral_consequence: Lacey and her children are safe and have a chance to get back on their feet.
immoral_action: Lacey looks the other way when Carter is mean to her kids and does whatever she can to keep Carter around because she has no money of her own.
immoral_consequence: Carter eventually starts abusing Lacey as well and makes it difficult for her to leave the relationship safely.

norm: It is good to treat your teachers respectfully
situation: Chris is feeling bored while his teacher is giving a lecture and thinks about just chatting with his friend.
intention: Chris wants to consider chatting with his friend.
moral_action: Chris resists the temptation of chatting with his friend and pushes himself to focus on the lecture.
moral_consequence: Chris manages to follow along with the lecture and the teacher experiences no problems giving the lecture.
immoral_action: Chris decides to just chat with his friend instead of listening to the lecture.
immoral_consequence: The teacher finds Chris' chatter disruptive and disrespectful, so he tells Chris to leave the classroom.

norm: You shouldn't lie to people about having a disease.
situation: Jarold needs money and is thinking about claiming he has cancer in order to solicit donations.
intention: Jarold wants to consider saying he has cancer.
moral_action: Jarold resists claiming how he has cancer and looks for a more proper way to make money.
moral_consequence: Jarold manages to make some money without resorting to lies.
immoral_action: Jarold tells everyone he has cancer in order to get some donations.
immoral_consequence: Eventually Jarold's lie gets discovered, and he runs into legal problems.

norm: You should not copy someone else's work.
situation: Claire and Colt are taking an exam in a classroom together and are within eyesight of each other's desks.
intention: Colt wants to do well on his exam.
moral_action: Colt uses study strategies he has learned to recall the information he needs most on his test.
moral_consequence: Colt feels accomplished when he gets his test grade back, and Claire congratulates him on doing well.
immoral_action: Colt looks over at Claire's exam paper a few times during the test to get the correct answers.
immoral_consequence: Claire notices Colt cheating during the test and calls him out at lunch time for it, embarrassing him.

norm: It's good to be married for a long time.
situation: Mary has a spouse of only a few months and the relationship has become very strained by many issues.
intention: Mary wants to be in a more fulfilling relationship.
moral_action: Mary asks her spouse to go to marriage counseling.
moral_consequence: Mary and her partner work things out with the help of a professional.
immoral_action: Mary decides to get a divorce after only a few months.
immoral_consequence: Mary loses her best friend and spouse.

norm: It is good to get away from abusive people.
situation: Jane is in the middle of being beaten up by her drunken husband Bill which is a common occurrence.
intention: Jane wants to lash out at Bill.
moral_action: Jane backs off Bill to get out of his clutches and tells him she's leaving him forever as she runs out the door.
moral_consequence: Bill stops when he realizes what he's been doing but it's too late and Jane is finally free of her abuser.
immoral_action: Jane backs off Bill to get out of his clutches and then spits in his face and calls him a coward.
immoral_consequence: Bill gets further enraged and punches Jane even harder knocking her unconscious.

norm: You should use a professional ringtone at work
situation: Bob just switched to a new cell phone provider and is setting up his new smartphone.
intention: Bob has to choose a ringtone for his new phone.
moral_action: Bob decides to use a simple instrumental piece as his ringtone and keeps the volume low at work.
moral_consequence: Bob's phone rings during a meeting and it is barely noticed.
immoral_action: Bob chooses his favorite obscenity-laden hard rock song as his ringtone and has the volume way up at work.
immoral_consequence: Bob's ringtone goes off during an important business meeting, and he is disciplined for it.

norm: It's disgusting to masturbate in public.
situation: James was sitting in math class when he spontaneously started to feel horny.
intention: James wants to masturbate and feel less horny.
moral_action: James asks for a bathroom pass and masturbates in the boys' bathroom.
moral_consequence: James feels calmer and more able to focus when he returns to class.
immoral_action: James begins masturbating at his desk in front of all his classmates.
immoral_consequence: The teacher sends James to the principal, who sends him to the school psychiatrist.

norm: It's wrong to do hurtful things towards others.
situation: Holly gets in an argument with her classmate, Allison.
intention: Holly wants to win the argument.
moral_action: Holly counters Allison's argument with a valid point and evidence to back it up.
moral_consequence: Allison considers Holly's argument and admits that it makes her see things differently.
immoral_action: Holly personally attacks Allison when she can't think of a counterpoint in the argument to shut her down.
immoral_consequence: Allison feels vulnerable and sad that she's been personally attacked.

norm: It's good to support your child's education.
situation: Mike just got a big bonus for meeting a sales quota.
intention: Mike wants to spend his bonus money.
moral_action: Mike spends his bonus paying for a semester of his son's college.
moral_consequence: Mike's son can focus more on his studies and appreciates his dad more.

moral_action: Alyssa asks Caroline to set some ground rules for their roommate arrangement including picking up after oneself in common areas.
moral_consequence: Alyssa and Caroline are able to make a mutual agreement to keep common spaces tidy.
immoral_action: Alyssa gathers up all of Caroline's trash from around the apartment and dumps it in Caroline's room on her bed.
immoral_consequence: Caroline gets mad at Alyssa for being passive aggressive and their living environment becomes tense.

norm: It's rude to make fun of someone for their heritage
situation: Martin is at a party with his Jewish friend Luke.
intention: Martin wants to entertain his people.
moral_action: Martin tells everyone a funny story about his dog.
moral_consequence: Martin ends up discussing dogs with another animal lover who gives him her phone number.
immoral_action: Martin points at Luke and makes a joke about Jewish history.
immoral_consequence: Martin is publicly shamed by his guests for his behavior.

norm: It's rude to get together with your ex's best friend.
situation: Ulmer listens to Trisha, his ex's best friend, confess her feelings for him.
intention: Ulmer doesn't want to hurt Trisha.
moral_action: Ulmer compliments the good aspects of Trisha's personality while stressing the importance of not hurting her best friend.
moral_consequence: Trisha walks away with a new appreciation of her best friend.
immoral_action: Ulmer responds to Trisha's request by gently hugging and kissing her.
immoral_consequence: Trisha loses her relationship with her best friend who spots the kiss.

norm: It's rude to leave an event without saying good-bye.
situation: It is late on a Saturday night and Nick is at a family gathering with his girlfriend Jenna.
intention: Nick wants to go home.
moral_action: Nick takes his girlfriend and the two make their way to each person to tell them they are leaving.
moral_consequence: Nick's family express their gratitude for showing up and wish them a safe drive.
immoral_action: Nick takes his girlfriend and the two sneak out  and drive home.
immoral_consequence: Nick's family is upset that he left the party without letting anyone know.

norm: It's not acceptable to break the law.
situation: Jason is driving to the bank on Friday after work before they close.
intention: Jason wants to cash his check.
moral_action: Jason stops at a red light and waits for the light to turn green.
moral_consequence: Jason arrives just in time and is able to cash his check.
immoral_action: Jason is in a hurry and runs a red light.
immoral_consequence: Jason gets pulled over by a cop, gets a ticket and doesn't make it to the bank in time.

norm: It's wrong to blow someone up.
situation: Spencer is an explosive expert working at the local mine where local teenagers have been trespassing at lately.
intention: Spencer wants to stop the trespassing.
moral_action: Spencer calls the local authorities to crack down on the trespassers since he is conducting blasts soon.
moral_consequence: Spencer is able to do his job effectively after the trespasser are thwarted by the local authorities.
immoral_action: Spencer knows there are proper warning signs, so he initiates a mining blast despite knowing a trespasser is in the area.
immoral_consequence: Spencer is arrested and found guilty for his role in blowing up a trespasser.

norm: It's wrong to steal things from a business.
situation: Douglas is at the game store browsing their products.
intention: Douglas wants to try out a new video games that just came out.
moral_action: Douglas picks up the new game and purchased it at the front counter.
moral_consequence: Douglas takes the game home and plays it four hours having a great time.
immoral_action: Douglas quickly slips a game into his pocket and runs out of the store.
immoral_consequence: Right outside the door a security guard stops Douglas and arrests him.

norm: You should call the police if someone is injured.
situation: Kim sees someone in the street get hit by a car which drives away.
intention: Kim wants to decide if she should call 911.
moral_action: Kim calls 911 on her phone right away to help the injured man.
moral_consequence: An ambulance arrives to help the injured man 3 minutes later.
immoral_action: Kim walks away assuming someone else will call the 911.
immoral_consequence: Everyone else does the same thing as Kim and the injured man gets no help.

norm: You shouldn't get into questionable friendships when you're married.
situation: Dave and his wife are in Las Vegas when a prostitute approaches them and asks Dave if they wanna hang out.
intention: Dave wants to respond to the prostitute's request.
moral_action: Dave tells the prostitute that she should find someone else to hang out with as she's not their type of friend.
moral_consequence: Dave's wife is happy that Dave understands the standards she holds their relationship up to.
immoral_action: Dave tells the prostitute that it's a great idea, and they should all go hang out a while and get to know each other.
immoral_consequence: Dave's wife is angry that Dave doesn't see the problems that could arise out of that friendship and doesn't trust Dave's judgement.

norm: You shouldn't abandon people.
situation: Madison is shopping with her friend Jill, when a good looking guy, Ken asks her if she wants to grab a bite to eat.
intention: Madison wants to go eat with Ken.
moral_action: Madison tells Ken she would love to grab a bite to eat as long as Jill can come too.
moral_consequence: Jill thinks Madison is a good friend and the three of them have fun together.
immoral_action: Madison just walks away with Ken to get food, leaving Jill behind.
immoral_consequence: Jill feels betrayed and alone by Madison's actions.

norm: It is rude to abandon your family.
situation: Ian watches his little brother get onto the teacup ride when his friends ask him invite him to the roller coaster.
intention: Ian wants to have fun.
moral_action: Ian plays a multiplayer game on his cell phone while he waits for his younger brother.
moral_consequence: His younger brother is able to ride more rides with his brother.
immoral_action: Ian gets onto the roller coaster with his friends.
immoral_consequence: His little brother wanders around alone after getting off of the teacup ride.

norm: It is bad to expose other people to germs
situation: Bob wakes up sick in the morning, he knows he has a cold today.
intention: Bob wants to earn some money today.
moral_action: Bob calls to tell his boss that he'll be working remotely today.
moral_consequence: Bob gets out his laptop and works from home while sick to avoid getting his coworkers sick.
immoral_action: Bob goes to work sick and keeps working all day like any other day.
immoral_consequence: Bob gets all his coworkers sick and drops the company productivity to a crawl.

norm: It's wrong to look for love in the wrong places.
situation: Alex has to go to AA meetings for her alcoholism, but he is single.
intention: Alex wants to feel closer to the people at the meetings.
moral_action: Alex talks with the people at the meetings and talks about his own issues.
moral_consequence: The people at the meeting trust Alex more and are more willing to have him as a friend.
immoral_action: Alex flirts with the women at the meetings and invites them to come to his place.
immoral_consequence: The people at the meetings feel that Alex is trying to take advantage of women in a bad mental state.

norm: It's good to be sensitive to other cultures.
situation: Hank is over at his Jewish friend's house for dinner and is told there won't be pork chops.
intention: Hank wants to comment about the lack of pork chops.
moral_action: Hank asks his friend why they don't eat pork chops.
moral_consequence: Hank's friend will explain to Hank about their dietary restrictions.
immoral_action: Hank tells his friend that their religion is lousy if they can't eat pork chops.
immoral_consequence: Hank's friend will not want Hank around at their house.

norm: It's good to pay off your debts.
situation: Laura had bought a new set of furniture for the living room in her apartment.
intention: Laura wants to make a payment on the furniture that she bought.
moral_action: Laura pays as much as she can on the furniture every week when she gets her check.
moral_consequence: Laura manages to pay off the furniture in just a few months and minimizes her interest charges.
immoral_action: Laura makes a five dollar payment on the furniture every week.
immoral_consequence: Laura is hit in the end of the year by massive interest charges that she can't afford.

norm: It's good to carpool.
situation: Nate and Ian are planning to go camping with three friends over the weekend.
intention: Nate wants to arrive to the campsite.
moral_action: Nate suggests they all ride together, and they drive to the campsite in Ian's car.
moral_consequence: The group is able to make it to the campsite and each person saves money by contributing the fill one tank.
immoral_action: Nate suggests the group travel separately and everyone goes in the own car.
immoral_consequence: Each person must get gas and the group spends $60 each to fill their tanks.

norm: It's polite to hold the door open for people.
situation: It's raining heavily as Paul pulls up to a convenience store, and as he gets out of his car and runs for the door he sees someone else running up.
intention: Paul wants to get inside.
moral_action: Paul opens the door and holds it open behind him for the stranger.
moral_consequence: The stranger thanks Paul for being so considerate and flashes him a smile.
immoral_action: Paul quickly opens the door to get out of the elements and steps inside.
immoral_consequence: The stranger is annoyed at Paul for not holding the door open for them and calls him a jerk.

norm: It's rude to say a friend doesn't look good.
situation: Nancy is helping her friend Cindy get ready for a night out.
intention: Nancy wants Cindy to look good.
moral_action: Nancy helps Cindy pick out a dress that looks amazing on her.
moral_consequence: Cindy has a blast that night and feels great.
immoral_action: Nancy tells Cindy she looks fat in the dress she's wearing and people will laugh at her.
immoral_consequence: Cindy is so upset she refuses to go out.

norm: It's tacky to lord what you have over others.
situation: Gary asks Bryan for some of his corn because Bryan is a farmer with a full field and Gary is out of work and needs to feed his family.
intention: Bryan wants to give Gary some corn.
moral_action: Bryan shares some corn with Gary and tells him that they have plenty of food on the farm and to please come back when he needs more.
moral_consequence: Gary is grateful for the help getting through a rough time and Bryan feels good that he has helped another human being.
immoral_action: "Bryan tells Gary that, ""you're lucky to know me, because your family would starve without me""."
immoral_consequence: Gary feels demoralized and hurt, while Bryan feels guilty for saying something so harsh to a person who came to him for help.

norm: You shouldn't tolerate a student having a crush on you.
situation: Amanda is a teacher at a high school and one of her students has been showing her affection.
intention: Amanda wants to be a good teacher.
moral_action: Amanda knows that this is unhealthy behavior for the student, so she has the student transferred to another class.
moral_consequence: The student eventually gets over their crush on Amanda and concentrates on school work in the other class they were transferred to.
immoral_action: Amanda allows the affection to continue thinking that the student will perform well in class if they like her like that.
immoral_consequence: The student that was showing Amanda affection gets more and more clingy and obsessed with Amanda.

norm: It's wrong to lie at job interviews.
situation: Mark has a job interview after a long period of unemployment.
intention: Mark really wants to get this job.
moral_action: Mark explains that he has been unemployed recently but really wants a job.
moral_consequence: Mark does not get the job because the interviewer wants to hire someone who has worked recently.
immoral_action: Mark tells the interviewer that he has been working a retail job for the past few years.
immoral_consequence: Mark gets the job because the interviewer thinks he is a good candidate.

norm: It is wrong to kick a dog.
situation: Tori is doing her morning jog when she's approached by a dog acting aggressively.
intention: Tori wants to keep distance between her and the dog.
moral_action: Tori picks up the pace and sprints away from the dog.
moral_consequence: Tori is relieved when she manages to get away unscatched.
immoral_action: Tori ends up kicking the dog to get it away from her in self defense.
immoral_consequence: The dog yelps in pain and Tori feels guilty for hurting it.

norm: It's wrong to say something just to irritate other people
situation: John and Mindy are at home together and Mindy has on a new hat she likes.
intention: John wants to laugh and have a good time.
moral_action: John tells Mindy her hat looks great and makes her look like a supermodel and laughs.
moral_consequence: Mindy is happy and laughs too and feels very good about herself and adores her hat even more.
immoral_action: John tells Mindy her hat makes her look like a ugly man and laughs.
immoral_consequence: Mindy feels sad and upset hearing this and thinks about returning the hat.

norm: It's rude to choose a friend over your significant other.
situation: Roger is getting ready for his date with Susan when his friend Antonio invites him to a football game.
intention: Roger wants to watch football.
moral_action: Roger takes Susan to a wings bar where they watch the football game while eating wings.
moral_consequence: Susan learns more about football.
immoral_action: Roger goes to the football game after telling Susan he's sick.
immoral_consequence: Susan is hurt when she finds out the truth.

norm: You should help family members in need.
situation: Eric gets a calls from his brother Bryan, who needs a temporary place to stay after losing his job and apartment.
intention: Eric wants to respond to Bryan.
moral_action: Eric tells Bryan that he can sleep in the guest room until he gets back on his feet.
moral_consequence: Bryan stays with Eric for a few weeks until he eventually finds a new job and gets his own place.
immoral_action: Eric tells Bryan that he doesn't have enough room to accommodate him.
immoral_consequence: Bryan has no one else that he can turn to and becomes homeless.

norm: It's wrong to get involved in your friend's sex life.
situation: Jane is hanging out with Susan, and they're talking about their boyfriends.
intention: Jane wants to ask Susan a question.
moral_action: Jane asks Susan if her boyfriend ever gets her flowers or other surprise gifts.
moral_consequence: Susan is happy to answer the question and it actually recalls fond memories for her of receiving flowers.
immoral_action: Jane asks Susan if her boyfriend ever performs oral sex on her or if he avoids it.
immoral_consequence: Susan is embarrassed to even discuss the topic and is shocked her friend would get so personal.

norm: It is rude to deceive someone you have relations with.
situation: Lori has been dating Ben and Tom at the same time, without either Tom or Ben being aware of each other.
intention: Lori wants to take the next step with Ben.
moral_action: Lori lets Tom down gently before asking Ben to be official.
moral_consequence: Ben agrees, and Lori is happy to have found the one.
immoral_action: Lori asks Ben to be official while continuing to text Tom in secret.
immoral_consequence: Ben sees Lori's texts with Tom and breaks up with her.

norm: You shouldn't be cruel to people.
situation: Rob walks into the kitchen and sees his sister Susie approaching the counter to get a cookie.
intention: Rob wants a cookie to eat for himself.
moral_action: Sam allows his sister to get a cookie and then grabs another for himself and eats it.
moral_consequence: Susie feels happy and enjoys eating the cookie.
immoral_action: Rob knocks the cookie out of Susie's hand and eats it.
immoral_consequence: Susie feels sad and upset and begins to cry.

norm: It's wrong to push through crowds of people.
situation: Olivia is at the grocery store with her items when she realizes the lines are really long at the registers.
intention: Olivia wants to check out.
moral_action: Olivia waits for twenty minutes to get to the beginning of the line.
moral_consequence: The manager of the store gives Olivia a ten dollar discount for the long wait.
immoral_action: Olivia pushes past all the people in the lines with her shopping cart  in order to get ahead in the line.
immoral_consequence: The manager of the store asks Olivia to leave the store right away.

norm: It's not nice to cheat.
situation: Marcus has an important math test today.
intention: Marcus wants to make an A.
moral_action: Marcus takes the test to the best of his abilities and makes an A.
moral_consequence: Marcus finishes with an A for the class.
immoral_action: Marcus decides to look at other students’ answers when he thinks that nobody is paying attention to him.
immoral_consequence: Marcus gets caught and is given a 0 for a grade.

norm: It's kind to help people when you're able to.
situation: Jeff's brother is moving this weekend and asked him if he could help, knowing that Jeff doesn’t have anything else planned.
intention: Jeff wants to be careful not to hurt his back.
moral_action: Jeff accepts to help his brother, but tells him he won't be able to move heavy objects.
moral_consequence: Jeff's brother is happy Jeff came and feels grateful.
immoral_action: Jeff turns his brother down and has a very restful weekend.
immoral_consequence: Jeff's brother is quite disappointed in Jeff and feels his brother is letting him down.

norm: You shouldn't inappropriately touch someone during a sleepover.
situation: Jessica and Maria are big slumber party, and Jessica has a crush on Maria.
intention: Jessica wants to express her attraction to Maria.
moral_action: Jessica compliments Maria's appearance throughout the night.
moral_consequence: Jessica deepens her relationship with Maria.
immoral_action: Jessica hugs Maria from behind and gently touches Maria's breasts.
immoral_consequence: Jessica is thrown out of the party by the host.

norm: You shouldn't exclude your family members.
situation: Jane is trying to decide whether to invite her socially awkward sister to her Emmy viewing party.
intention: Jane wants everyone at the party to have a good time.
moral_action: Jane invites her sister and coaches her on some possible small talk topics.
moral_consequence: Everyone at the party is engrossed in watching the Emmys, and Jane and her sister both enjoy themselves.
immoral_action: Jane tells her sister that she can't come to the party because she's too weird.
immoral_consequence: Jane's sister locks herself in her room and blasts black metal while Jane and her friends try to watch the TV downstairs.

norm: It's rude to joke about someone who is dead.
situation: Rudy is hanging out with his friend Sam who has been down in the dumps recently due to the passing of his grandfather.
intention: Rudy wants to lighten the mood and cheer Sam up.
moral_action: Rudy tells Sam a funny knock-knock joke that he heard the other day.
moral_consequence: Sam finds the joke hilarious and it cheers him up considerably.
immoral_action: Rudy makes a joke that involves Sam's recently deceased granfather.
immoral_consequence: Sam is offended and further saddened at the mention of his grandfather.

norm: It's good to make use of public resources.
situation: Bob is poor and is having trouble paying bills.
intention: Bob wants to buy food.
moral_action: Bob uses his food stamps to buy good quality food.
moral_consequence: Bob eats well and stays healthy.
immoral_action: Bob buys nothing but ramen noodles because they're cheap, ignoring his food stamps.
immoral_consequence: Bob's body reacts poorly to the bad food and gives him health issues.

norm: It's good to spend time with lonely people.
situation: Jimmy's cousin doesn't have a lot of friends and has frequent struggles with depression.
intention: Jimmy wants his cousin to be happier.
moral_action: Jimmy offers to take his cousin to get some drinks at a bar.
moral_consequence: Jimmy's cousin is able to get out of the house and spend time with people.
immoral_action: Jimmy texts his cousin every week to show him he's thinking about him.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy's cousin still has to spend all of his time in his house and is just as lonely.

norm: It's profane to abuse a sibling.
situation: Anna, Marie's five year old sister, is crying loudly in the middle of the store.
intention: Marie wants to make Anna stop crying.
moral_action: Marie hugs Anna and tries cheering her up with her favorite song.
moral_consequence: Marie forms a better relationship with Anna.
immoral_action: Marie wacks Anna's arm and covers her mouth telling her that she will wack her again if she keeps crying.
immoral_consequence: Anna tells her mother about Marie's actions which results in Marie getting grounded.

norm: It's rude to make fun of a sibling.
situation: Maria asks her brother Ray how she looks in her large blue hat.
intention: Ray wants to respond.
moral_action: Ray tells Maria that the hat looks good on her.
moral_consequence: Maria is happy that Ray likes how she looks.
immoral_action: Ray tells Maria that she looks funny in the hat.
immoral_consequence: Maria throws the hat down and runs away while crying.

norm: It is illegal to lie to the government.
situation: John is filing his taxes and is filling out a form.
intention: John wants to respond to the line item asking for his total income.
moral_action: John states his actual working income as shown on his W2.
moral_consequence: John feels good about helping the country grow and pay for all services.
immoral_action: John understates his income significantly, to avoid paying more taxes.
immoral_consequence: The government audits John, causing him to have to pay a lot more in the end due to fines and penalties.

norm: It's good to be physical in a relationship.
situation: John's girlfriend is going on a trip, and he's driving her to the airport.
intention: John wants to say goodbye to his girlfriend.
moral_action: John hugs his girlfriend tightly while saying goodbye.
moral_consequence: John's girlfriend will feel that John will miss her a lot when she is gone.
immoral_action: John says and waves goodbye as his girlfriend goes into the airport.
immoral_consequence: John's girlfriend will feel that John won't miss her when she is gone.

norm: It is bad to pester people
situation: Anna reads a poster about an upcoming concert by a band she likes.
intention: Anna wants to go to the concert.
moral_action: Anna sends one text to Mae, inviting her to join her.
moral_consequence: Mae accepts the invitation, and accompanies Anna to the concert.
immoral_action: Anna sends 15 texts to her friend Mae, in one hour, asking Mae to join her.
immoral_consequence: Mae is annoyed with Anna and refuses to go; so Anna has to go alone.

norm: It is bad to be an abusive father.
situation: Calvin's son is drawing pictures all over the wall.
intention: Calvin wants to stop his son's misbehavior.
moral_action: Calvin takes the marker away from his son and teaches him that the house is not for drawing.
moral_consequence: Calvin's son learns his lesson and emotionally bonds with him.
immoral_action: Calvin beats his son until he stops drawing.
immoral_consequence: CPS takes Calvin's son away from him.

norm: You should be honest with people about your feelings.
situation: Lee is in a relationship that hasn't really been working out due to all the fighting involved.
intention: Lee wants to avoid fighting and confrontation.
moral_action: Lee confronts his partner one last time and breaks it off for good.
moral_consequence: Lee avoids all the fighting after they finally break up.
immoral_action: Lee pretends everything is okay and successfully avoids fighting.
immoral_consequence: Lee is stuck in a bad relationship.

norm: Abusing your spouse is wrong.
situation: After a hard day at work Tom eats a terrible meatloaf prepared by his wife Betty.
intention: Tom wants to express his displeasure to his wife.
moral_action: Tom explains to Betty that he did not enjoy the meatloaf and feels he deserves better after working all day to provide for her.
moral_consequence: Betty buys a well-rated cookbook and begins preparing better meals for Tom.
immoral_action: Tom throws the meatloaf against the wall and then wraps his hands around Betty's neck and shakes her.
immoral_consequence: Betty calls the police and Tom is arrested for domestic violence.

norm: It's good to go bowling with friends.
situation: Ace's friends invite Ace, a pro bowler practicing for a tournament, to join them in a trip to the bowling alley.
intention: Ace wants to practice his bowling game.
moral_action: Ace accepts and works his bowling practice into his game with his friends.
moral_consequence: Ace helps his friends improve their own game and relaxes before the tournament.
immoral_action: Ace declines and goes to practice by himself at a different bowling alley, wanting peace and quiet.
immoral_consequence: Ace gets all stressed out from the pressure of practice and competition.

norm: It's rude to disrupt other's watching a play / movie.
situation: Edeline needs help on her project with Richard, and Richard is seeing a movie in theaters.
intention: Edeline wants to eliminate issues.
moral_action: Edeline asks for help on an online message board.
moral_consequence: Edeline receives different views from various individuals which deepens her understanding of the problem.
immoral_action: Edeline calls Richard multiple times over the next couple of hours.
immoral_consequence: Edeline is scolded by Richard for messing up his movie experience.

norm: You shouldn't punch teenagers.
situation: Mrs. Jones is teaching a class, and Chris keeps interrupting her.
intention: Mrs. Jones wants Chris to quiet down and let her teach.
moral_action: Mrs. Jones threatens Chris with a detention if he doesn't quiet down.
moral_consequence: Chris stops acting up in class because he doesn't want to get in trouble at home for his behavior.
immoral_action: Mrs. Jones approaches Chris's desk and punches him hard in the arm.
immoral_consequence: Chris doesn't speak for the rest of the class, but reports Mrs. Jones for abuse and gets her fired.

norm: It is wrong to purposely hit an animal.
situation: Jake comes home to find that his dog has chewed his couch.
intention: Jake wants to punish his dog.
moral_action: Jake leaves the room until he calms down and decides to crate the dog in the future.
moral_consequence: Jake's dog gets used to the crate and Jake's furniture stays safe.
immoral_action: Jake screams at the dog and begins hitting the dog.
immoral_consequence: The neighbors hear and call the police and Jake is arrested for animal cruelty.

norm: It's kind to give another person a present.
situation: Maya notices Sarah is upset and doesn't know what to do.
intention: Maya wants to make Sarah feel better.
moral_action: Maya brings a present for Sarah.
moral_consequence: Sarah loves the present and is much happier.
immoral_action: Maya tells Sarah a bunch of jokes to avoid having to buy a present.
immoral_consequence: Sarah is cheered up for a while but becomes sad again.

norm: It's bad to make up a death in the family.
situation: Zack has stayed up all night playing video games and has to work early in the morning.
intention: Zack wants to take the day off.
moral_action: Zack tells his boss that he has food poisoning.
moral_consequence: Zack gets to take the day off without lying about something serious.
immoral_action: Zack tells his boss that he has to attend a funeral of a family member.
immoral_consequence: Zack feels bad about lying about such a grim topic.

norm: It's wrong not to help out your coworkers.
situation: Nicole is getting ready to leave work when her new coworker, Ted, asks if she can help him finish up, so he can leave too.
intention: Nicole wants to respond to Ted.
moral_action: Nicole says of course and immediately chips in and helps Ted.
moral_consequence: Ted thanks Nicole for her help and tells her that she's been a great coworker.
immoral_action: Nicole tells Ted that she managed to finish her work by herself, so he should do the same, and then leaves.
immoral_consequence: Ted ends up having to work overtime to finish his work.

norm: It's bad to have a dirty sloppy appearance
situation: Jordan was wearing jeans and a dirty tee shirt when he work up.
intention: Jordan wants to get a job.
moral_action: Jordan changed his clothes and shaved before going job hunting.
moral_consequence: Jordan was hired and had a new job by the end of the day.
immoral_action: Jordan went into a nice office and tried booking an interview with the boss.
immoral_consequence: Jordan was escourted off the premises by the security in the building.

norm: It's rude to get revenge on your ex roommate.
situation: Jerry's old roommate, Justin, has just moved out after an acrimonious relationship with each other, with Justin leaving sand in Jerry's washer.
intention: Jerry wants to respond to the sand in the washer.
moral_action: Jerry refuses to give Justin the satisfaction of responding to Justin's prank, and simply cleans out the washer.
moral_consequence: Jerry moves on with his life and quickly forgets about his ex-roommate.
immoral_action: Jerry stalks Justin to his new place and slashes his tires.
immoral_consequence: Justin calls the cops, and Jerry is arrested and fined.

norm: You should punish a child that calls others names.
situation: Kelly's daughter, Stacey, has been increasingly disrespectful to her friends and family, and she's been name calling.
intention: Kelly needs to stop Stacey from calling people names.
moral_action: Kelly implements a new household policy that every time Stacey calls someone a name, she will lose her access to the internet, and her phone, for one full day.
moral_consequence: Stacey learns quickly, after only a couple of punishment periods, to be more respectful of other people.
immoral_action: Kelly sets up a system where Stacey has to put a quarter in a jar, every time she calls someone a disrespectful name.
immoral_consequence: Stacey treats the jar as a joke and actually asks her mother for change when she wants to start calling people names.

norm: It's wrong to terminate a relationship over someone's hobbies.
situation: Jim and his girlfriend are going to New York for vacation, Jim like museums, his girlfriend likes plays.
intention: Jim wants to talk about what to do in New York.
moral_action: Jim and his girlfriend make a plan where they will go to some museums and some plays.
moral_consequence: Jim's girlfriend is happy and values compromise and Jim.
immoral_action: Jim tells his girlfriend that they can't be together if she goes to a play.
immoral_consequence: Jim's girlfriend dumps him as he is too controlling.

norm: It's bad to be obsessive over someone.
situation: Jenna's boyfriend asked her to break up because she was too clingy.
intention: Jenna wants to try her best to convince her boyfriend to reunite with her.
moral_action: Jenna started dating a handsome coworker to make her boyfriend jealous.
moral_consequence: Jenna's boyfriend starting hanging out with her and eventually they hooked up again.
immoral_action: Jenna bombarded her boyfriend with calls, texts, and visits to his house and work.
immoral_consequence: Jenna's boyfriend got back together for a few weeks just to get some peace and quiet, before finally filing for a restraining order.

norm: It's rude to sleep with friends of a friend.
situation: Carolyn who is Dave's friend asks Dave's other friend Jim to hang out and maybe have sex tonight.
intention: Jim wants to respond to Carolyn's proposal.
moral_action: Jim tells Carolyn that out of respect for Dave they shouldn't really get involved with each other that way.
moral_consequence: Dave is delighted that Jim is doing what he can to maintain the trio as a good friendship.
immoral_action: Jim tells Carolyn that he thinks that's a great idea since he finds her very attractive.
immoral_consequence: Dave is sad that he seems to be left out of the trio now as two of his friends are hooking up.

norm: It's wrong to not accept others as they are.
situation: Mina's son is very introverted, so he's not very popular in school.
intention: Mina wants to say something to her son.
moral_action: Mina tells his son that he should do whatever that makes him comfortable.
moral_consequence: Mina's son feels good that his mom accepts him for who he is.
immoral_action: Mina tells her son that he needs to start talking more.
immoral_consequence: Mina's son feels uncomfortable talking a lot so he doesn't appreciate the advice.

norm: You shouldn't pull pranks that could harm someone.
situation: Dwight's coworker is always messing with people at work and recently finds that a line has been crossed.
intention: Dwight wants to teach his coworker a lesson.
moral_action: Dwight tapes his coworker's desk making it impossible to open without investing time removing all the tape.
moral_consequence: His coworker learns that people will get him back.
immoral_action: Dwight spikes his coworker's lunch with an incredibly spicy hot sauce.
immoral_consequence: His coworker has a really bad reaction to the hot sauce.

norm: It is good to appreciate the food you eat.
situation: Jenna's father spent an hour making a healthy dinner with lots of vegetables.
intention: Jenna wants to get out of eating her vegetables.
moral_action: Jenna compliments her father on the meal and sneaks her vegetables to the dog while her parents aren't looking.
moral_consequence: Later that night, the dog throws up the vegetables out on the lawn.
immoral_action: Jenna tells her father that the meal looks like a puddle of green puke.
immoral_consequence: Jenna's dad tells her she can't have dessert if she can't be polite.

norm: It's good to cook for other people
situation: Johnny is throwing a party and having all his friends over, but they will need food!
intention: Johnny wants to get food for his friends.
moral_action: Johnny decides to cook for them all himself and make things they all like.
moral_consequence: Johnny's friends all love the food Johnny made for them.
immoral_action: Johnny places a big order to the local McDonalds to feed all his friends.
immoral_consequence: Turns out several of his friends don't like McDonalds or any other fast food.

norm: You shouldn't act salty toward others.
situation: While playing an online game Jake gets thoroughly beaten by another player in a PVP battle.
intention: Jake wants to communicate with the other player.
moral_action: Jake congratulates the other player and asks for any tips they might have.
moral_consequence: Jake gains experience and guidance from a better player.
immoral_action: Jake sends messages to the other player saying that they can’t have possibly won by playing fair.
immoral_consequence: Jake gets a reputation as a poor loser in the game.

norm: It's rude to assume a cashier short-changed you on purpose.
situation: Biff bought something at the store, and he realized he was 78 cents short.
intention: Biff wants his money back.
moral_action: Biff asks the cashier about the missing money.
moral_consequence: The cashier notices the mistake and gives Biff the missing money.
immoral_action: "Biff runs up to the cashier and says ""way to short change me, butthead!""."
immoral_consequence: Biff does get his money back but not before arguing with the cashier and many other employees.

norm: You should not be rude to co workers.
situation: Alice was working on a project with her coworkers.
intention: Alice wanted to give her opinion on the project.
moral_action: Alice congratulates her coworkers for their contributions.
moral_consequence: Alice's coworkers thank her and smile.
immoral_action: Alice tells her coworkers that their contributions are terrible.
immoral_consequence: Alice's coworkers get upset and try to defend themselves.

norm: You shouldn't pour beverages on the floor
situation: Mario is cleaning the kitchen when he finds cans half full of soda.
intention: Mario wants to empty the soda from the cans on the counter.
moral_action: Mario pours the soda out into the drain in the sink.
moral_consequence: Mario is happy that he has less things to clean in the kitchen.
immoral_action: Mario pours the soda out of the cans onto the floor.
immoral_consequence: The floor ends up getting sticky and Mario has more to clean.

norm: It is rude to favor one kid over another.
situation: Stanley has 2 children who are interested in getting better at tennis, but one is clearly more talented than the other.
intention: Stanley wants to maximize his kids' ability.
moral_action: Stanley makes sure to split his time between both kids and pay for lessons when needed, so they get as much practice as possible.
moral_consequence: One kid improves quicker than the other, but they both practice hard and enjoy improving their abilities.
immoral_action: Stanley spends a lot more time with the more talented child and pays more more lessons for them.
immoral_consequence: The more talented child improves quickly and makes their school team, but the other feels neglected and starts to feel depressed.

norm: It's rude to talk about other's medical conditions.
situation: Mark works in an office with his friend, who has bipolar disorder.
intention: Mark wants to be better friends with the boss.
moral_action: Mark invites his boss to lunch since they seem a bit depresssed.
moral_consequence: Mark talks with his boss, and they both feel better, as the boss needed a break and Mark feels he knows and trusts his boss better.
immoral_action: Mark talks about his friend's manic episodes and how out of control he gets, to make his boss feel closer to him.
immoral_consequence: Mark's boss ends up letting the friend go because they're not seen as stable and reliable in the workplace.

norm: It's kind to loan things to a person in need.
situation: Dave is at home when he gets a phone call from his neighbor who wants to borrow his shrub snippers.
intention: Dave wants to respond to his neighbor's request.
moral_action: Dave tells the neighbor that of course he can borrow them and to come over and pick them up.
moral_consequence: The neighbor is delighted that Dave is willing to help him and that he'll get his job done.
immoral_action: Dave tells his neighbor that he thinks he'll need them soon, so he can't lend them to him.
immoral_consequence: The neighbor is miffed that Dave won't share his things and is sad that he can't do the job he needs to.

norm: It is wrong to always want your husband gone.
situation: Maude's husband Jim recently retired, and she's annoyed at how often he's at home now.
intention: Maude wants to be annoyed less.
moral_action: Maude tries to learn more about Jim since they aren't used to him being home.
moral_consequence: They talk and learn a lot more about each other and what bothers them.
immoral_action: Maude finds several ways to get Jim out of the house like golf and random trips with his buddies.
immoral_consequence: She's still annoyed any time he is home, the issues never get resolved.

norm: You shouldn't deny others and their medical diagnosis's.
situation: Erin has been diagnosed with a shellfish allergy.
intention: Grant wants to throw a nice dinner party which Erin is invited to.
moral_action: Grant serves nice steaks.
moral_consequence: Erin and all the other guests have a nice time at the dinner party.
immoral_action: Grant serves lobsters even though he knows about Erin's allergy.
immoral_consequence: Erin is unable to eat anything at the party and feels left out.

norm: It's bad to get so drunk you cause problems.
situation: Roger was in the bar hanging out with some of his friends.
intention: Roger wants to have a drink.
moral_action: Roger has a single beer with his friends while they watch a ball game.
moral_consequence: Roger can function well enough after his drink to be able to walk home.
immoral_action: Roger has a few beers and several shots of whiskey with his friends.
immoral_consequence: Roger gets so drunk that he has to be carried out of the bar after getting into a fight.

norm: It's good to invite people over for dinner.
situation: Jill is making dinner at home and is talking to an old good friend on the phone who is in town.
intention: Jill wants to catch up with her old friend.
moral_action: Jill invites her friend over for dinner explaining she is already cooking and it would be a great way to talk.
moral_consequence: Jill and her friend catch up over dinner and have a great time together.
immoral_action: Jill makes dinner for herself and continues to talk with her friend all night learning what they have been up to.
immoral_consequence: Jill and her friend catch up but never get around to hanging out together before the friend leaves town.

norm: You shouldn't ignore people that are ill.
situation: Jane's husband has been complaining about a pain in his abdomen for some time.
intention: Jane wants to stop hearing about her husband's abdomen.
moral_action: Jane makes an appointment with the family doctor, so they can get to the bottom of her husband's issue.
moral_consequence: The doctor is able to treat Jane's husband, and he recovers.
immoral_action: Jane calls up some friends and arranges a night out with them, so she can get out of the house.
immoral_consequence: Jane's husband's condition worsens, and he collapses while home alone.

norm: You shouldn't leave your kids without telling them.
situation: Betty's father had a heart attack while Betty's kids are playing in the back of the house.
intention: Betty needs to get to the hospital immediately.
moral_action: Betty pops her head out to tell her kids that everything is OK, she just needs to go out for a bit.
moral_consequence: Betty's kids know where their mom went, and are able to keep playing unconcerned.
immoral_action: Betty just picks up her keys and leaves the house without another word.
immoral_consequence: Betty's kids are confused, and scared that they don't know where their mother went.

norm: It's rude to call your roommate creepy.
situation: Ryan's roommate Todd is in a very strange relationship with a younger woman.
intention: Ryan wants to tell Todd he's concerned about his relationship.
moral_action: Ryan asks Todd what he sees in the younger woman, and why he is so transfixed by her.
moral_consequence: Todd explains why he loves his girlfriend so much, and assuages Ryan's concern.
immoral_action: Ryan calls Todd a pedophile, and tells him how inappropriate it is to date someone so much younger.
immoral_consequence: Todd gets very offended, and decides to move out on Ryan with no notice.

norm: It's good to give compliments to your significant other.
situation: Joe and his girlfriend Sarah are eating lunch in silence.
intention: Joe wants to break up the silence with friendly conversation.
moral_action: Joe tells Sarah all of the things he loves about her, and Joe asks Sarah about her day.
moral_consequence: Sarah feels like Joe cares about her, and she asks Joe to cuddle with her after supper.
immoral_action: Joe talks about himself and his favorite subjects that disinterest Sarah.
immoral_consequence: Sarah is bored, and she leaves the table early.

norm: It's irresponsible to overindulge in snacks.
situation: Vince broke up with his girlfriend, is very depressed, and could use some comfort in his life.
intention: Vince wants to eat.
moral_action: Vince allows himself a few cookies during lunch time to cheer himself up.
moral_consequence: Vince maintains control of his weight and feels better for it, improving his emotional recovery.
immoral_action: Vince buys some boxes of chocolates and cookies and snacks on them for a few hours.
immoral_consequence: Vince begins to gain weight and his health declines.

norm: It is harmful to spread germs in food.
situation: Jeremy is eating a food a party when he bites into something he dislikes.
intention: Jeremy wants to get rid of the food.
moral_action: Jeremy tosses the uneaten food into the trashcan.
moral_consequence: John ends up befriending another person standing near the trashcan.
immoral_action: Jeremy slips the half eaten food back onto one of the random food trays.
immoral_consequence: Jeremy is roasted on Facebook when someone shares a picture of his actions.

norm: It's good to make people feel better.
situation: Colt is a baseball coach for a youth team, and a disabled boy is on the team.
intention: Colt wants to give the boy some advice.
moral_action: Colt tells the boy that he's just been unlucky and that he should keep trying.
moral_consequence: The boy feels motivated to play even though they're not playing well.
immoral_action: Colt tells the boy to go to school so that they don't have to play baseball anymore.
immoral_consequence: The boy's feelings are hurt, and he might want to quit the team.

norm: It's rude to exclude your friend from your party.
situation: Alice is throwing a big Friday night party at her house and recently had a big fight with her best friend, Maggie.
intention: Alice wants to have a nice party.
moral_action: Alice decides to bury the hatchet and allow Maggie to her party.
moral_consequence: Alice and Maggie make up and become even closer friends.
immoral_action: Alice tells Maggie she's not invited to the party on Friday.
immoral_consequence: Maggie gets even madder at Alice, and the two stop speaking to each other.

norm: People shouldn't be violent towards one another.
situation: Jake and John are having a heated argument at the bar about whose sports team is better.
intention: Jake wants to end the argument.
moral_action: Jake provides a detailed statistical breakdown about why his team is superior to John's.
moral_consequence: Jake ends up winning the argument and is happy he proved his point.
immoral_action: Jake gets so mad at John not agreeing with him that he knocks John out.
immoral_consequence: Jake is thrown out of the bar for his actions and is later arrested.

norm: It's good to watch TV shows when you're lonely.
situation: Adrian is having a tough time and is home alone feeling very lonely.
intention: Adrian wants to get his mind off his loneliness.
moral_action: Adrian decides to watch his favorite TV show.
moral_consequence: After a few minute's Adrian is laughing and has forgotten all about his loneliness.
immoral_action: Adrian decides to buy some drugs and do them.
immoral_consequence: Adrian ends up becoming addicted to the drugs and his depression and loneliness get worse.

norm: You should not damage other peoples things for a prank.
situation: Vince is part of a fraternity and his frat brother Ben has a birthday coming up.
intention: Vince wants to pull a prank on Ben's car.
moral_action: Vince gets some window chalk and writes a lot of funny messages on Ben's car windows.
moral_consequence: Ben takes pictures of the messages, reads them, has a good laugh, and feels appreciated by his friends.
immoral_action: Vince jacks up the car, puts a hole in the tires, and fills each tire with cement, then lowers the car.
immoral_consequence: Ben tries to drive the car and can hardly get it to move, costing him hundreds of dollars in repairs.
