norm: You shouldn't sabotage your ex's new relationship.
situation: Steve and Mary divorced two years ago and Steve is now cleaning out the house.
intention: Steve wants to return Marys favorite little black dress.
moral_action: Steve packs up the dress along with her other belongings and mails it to Mary's house.
moral_consequence: Mary is happy to get her things back and sends Steve a thank you text.
immoral_action: Steve puts the dress in a gift box along with the poem he wrote the night they first met.
immoral_consequence: Mary opens the box in front of her new boyfriend, he gets angry and thinks she is cheating on him.

norm: It's wrong to be in a park after closing time.
situation: Dan is playing baseball at the park with his friend.
intention: Dan wants to get in practice before his next game.
moral_action: Dan and his friend finish practicing when the park is set to close and go home.
moral_consequence: Dan gets practice in and gets home with enough time to rest and come back when the park opens tomorrow.
immoral_action: Dan knows the park closes at 7 but stays late on purpose.
immoral_consequence: Dan and his friend get in trouble with the cops for being at the park too late.

norm: It's wrong to spend all your money on your kids.
situation: Tony is at the toy store and has 100 dollars to get a toy for his son and some dinner for tonight.
intention: Tony wants to pick a toy to buy.
moral_action: Tony buys a small Lego set that costs about twenty dollars.
moral_consequence: Tony's wife and child are delighted that he managed to get both a toy and some food for them.
immoral_action: Tony buys an elaborate one hundred dollar Lego train set with accessories.
immoral_consequence: Tony's wife and child are both unhappy that they are not going to eat tonight and spend the night with hunger pains.

norm: It's good to give up an unhealthy habit.
situation: An overweight man Fabio has avoided stress eating for months, but he was just fired from work.
intention: Fabio wants to get rid of his anxiety.
moral_action: Fabio meditates for an hour before redoing his resume.
moral_consequence: Fabio's new resume helps him get a new job.
immoral_action: Fabio orders five meals from McDonalds.
immoral_consequence: Fabio gains weight.

norm: It is wrong to stifle children's freedom of expression
situation: Mrs. Jones is teaching a pre-school art class how to paint trees with fingerpaint.
intention: Mrs. Jones wants the children to be proud of their drawings.
moral_action: Mrs. Jones demonstrates how to make a tree and lets the children pick colors that they love.
moral_consequence: The children all have beautiful and unique paintings that are easy to tell apart and reflect their identities.
immoral_action: Mrs. Jones gives each child one color of paint at a time and makes them follow her step by step.
immoral_consequence: The children like their paintings, but they all look almost entirely identical and are easily mixed up by the students.

norm: Stealing something from someone is wrong.
situation: Jim is going fishing on a hot afternoon.
intention: Jim wants to keep his drinks cold.
moral_action: Jim goes to the store and buys a cooler.
moral_consequence: Jim stays hydrated and refreshed with cold drinks on his fishing trip.
immoral_action: Jim takes a cooler he sees sitting in his neighbor's yard.
immoral_consequence: Jim's neighbor sees Jim take the cooler on video surveillance, calls the police and Jim receives a citation.

norm: It's good to massage your fiancee.
situation: John's fiancee Vanessa works in heels all day and often comes home with sore feet, while he works construction and comes home with a sore back.
intention: John wants to relax after work.
moral_action: John tells Vanessa he'll massage her feet if she massages his back afterwards.
moral_consequence: John and Vanessa benefit from a win-win situation and are able to relax after their massages.
immoral_action: Vanessa asks John for a foot massage, and he denies her so that he can take a nap.
immoral_consequence: Vanessa is left with no relief and resents John for denying her.

norm: It's wrong to be emotionally unavailable in the bedroom.
situation: Chris and Danielle just finished making love in their bed, and Danielle wants to talk to Chris about their relationship.
intention: Chris wants to decide whether or not to have a conversation.
moral_action: Chris talks with Danielle, and they discuss how they want their lives to be in the future together.
moral_consequence: Danielle feels loved and is pleased to have an attentive partner in Chris.
immoral_action: Chris tells Danielle he's tired and rolls over to go to sleep.
immoral_consequence: Danielle is sad because she feels that Chris doesn't really love her and is using her for sex.

norm: It's bad to be rude to someone on a plane.
situation: Jim is on an airplane flight home and the passenger next to him is snoring which really bothers Jim.
intention: Jim wants to stop hearing the passenger snoring.
moral_action: Jim asks the flight attendant for earplugs which block out the passenger's snoring.
moral_consequence: The snoring passenger continues sleeping and arrives at their destination refreshed.
immoral_action: Jim yells at the snoring passenger waking them up and tells them to shut up in a harsh tone.
immoral_consequence: The passenger is offended to have been woken up and yelled at for something they can't control.

norm: It's rude to ignore your neighbors.
situation: John, who is late to work, is pulling out of his driveway to go to work and see's his neighbor quickly approaching his car.
intention: John wants to avoid talking to his neighbor.
moral_action: John smiles and waves to his neighbor while quickly driving away.
moral_consequence: John's neighbor stops to smile and waves back, happy to be acknowledged.
immoral_action: John pretends that he doesn't see his neighbor and drives off.
immoral_consequence: John's neighbor knows that he saw him and just thinks he is rude.

norm: It's not good to go looking for trouble
situation: Peter has just gotten off of work, but he doesn't want to go home yet.
intention: Peter wants to find something fun to do.
moral_action: Peter goes to the bowling alley and meets some of his friends.
moral_consequence: Peter has a great time and gets a little bit of exercise.
immoral_action: Peter parks in an alley and buys drugs from a local drug dealer.
immoral_consequence: Peter is arrested and ends up in jail after buying the drugs.

norm: It's rude to steal from your family.
situation: Bob sees the expensive jewelry lying around in his sister's room.
intention: Bob wants to exit the room.
moral_action: Bob turns around and exits the room and advises his sister to keep those in a safe.
moral_consequence: Bob's sister thanks Bob for the advice and talks about the heirlooms.
immoral_action: Bob takes all of those watches and quickly heads to the pawn shop.
immoral_consequence: Bob's sister is heartbroken because all her heirloom watches were stolen.

norm: You shouldn't let someone eat your food.
situation: James often bought frozen dinners, but someone kept eating them before he could get to them.
intention: James wants to always have frozen dinners available.
moral_action: James secretly installs a camera in the kitchen to catch the person taking his food.
moral_consequence: James identifies which of his roommates is the culprit and confronts them, after which his dinners are safe.
immoral_action: James starts buying twice as many frozen dinners at the grocery store each week.
immoral_consequence: James always has food but has less money available to spend on recreation.

norm: It's rude to walk your dog off its leash.
situation: Dusty's enjoying his day off and his dog starts begging at the door to go outside.
intention: Dusty wants to respond to his dog.
moral_action: Dusty puts a leash on his dog, and they go outside.
moral_consequence: Dusty's dog sees a neighbors cat and tries to chase it, but Dusty pulls back on the leash, so the cat has nothing to fear.
immoral_action: Dusty opens the door, and he and his dog take off walking down the street.
immoral_consequence: Dusty's dog sees a neighbors cat and chases it up a tree.

norm: It's polite to say hello.
situation: Cindy's family is hosting a cookout, and her son Josh has a new girlfriend, Ana, who has never met them.
intention: Cindy wants Josh to bring Ana to the cookout.
moral_action: Ana arrives and says hello, and Cindy responds with a big warm hug.
moral_consequence: Ana feels welcomed at the family cookout and is able to relax and enjoy herself.
immoral_action: Ana arrives and says hello to Cindy, who then walks away.
immoral_consequence: Ana thinks that Cindy has snubbed her and feels unwelcomed.

norm: It's rude to miss your friend's graduation ceremony.
situation: Julie receives an invitation to attend a friends college graduation, but she has plans to watch a movie premiere on the same day.
intention: Julie wants to respond to the invitation.
moral_action: Julie cancels her movie plans and attends the graduation ceremony.
moral_consequence: Julie helps her friend celebrate her accomplishment.
immoral_action: Julie declines the invitation and goes to the movie premiere instead.
immoral_consequence: Julie disappoints her friend on her big day.

norm: You shouldn't misbehave or you'll be punished by your teacher.
situation: Fred is sitting with friends at a school assembly and is bored by the presentation.
intention: Fred wants to talk with his friends.
moral_action: Fred takes out some paper and a pencil and passes notes to his friends.
moral_consequence: Fred and his friends carry on a silent conversation unnoticed.
immoral_action: Fred starts talking with his friend, laughing and joking.
immoral_consequence: The supervising teacher sees Fred and his friends and gives them all after-school detention.

norm: It is rude to call people names.
situation: Jane and Jeff are having an argument over something they disagree on.
intention: Jeff wants to convey his frustration with Jane's reasoning.
moral_action: Jeff points out the flaws in Jane's logic and asks her to reconsider her position.
moral_consequence: Jane give's Jeff's line of thinking new consideration before forming her final judgment.
immoral_action: Jeff calls Jane a complete moron for disagreeing with what Jeff is claiming.
immoral_consequence: Jane is hurt by Jeff's personal attack and refuses to listen to his explanations.

norm: You should be happy when your classmates help you out.
situation: Gillian is trying to lift a box full of books at school, and finally some classmates help her lift it onto a shelf.
intention: Gillian wants to respond to her classmates helping her.
moral_action: Gillian thanks her classmates and offers to help them when they need it.
moral_consequence: Gillian's classmates come to like her, and she makes a few new friends.
immoral_action: Gillian gets annoyed and says she could have done it herself.
immoral_consequence: Gillian's classmates are put off by her attitude and avoid her.

norm: It's good to pray for people who are in trouble
situation: Stan's mom meets a woman named Cindy at the door who is going through a lot of personal problems.
intention: Stan wants to encourage Cindy.
moral_action: Stan asks Cindy if he can pray with her so that God will help her with her problems.
moral_consequence: Cindy cries out of gratitude, prays with Stan, and goes back into the conflict with renewed confidence.
immoral_action: Stan gives Cindy some encouraging advice on her situation and tells her to cheer up.
immoral_consequence: Cindy doesn't connect well with the advice and continues to make the same mistakes as before.

norm: It's wrong not to show up for an appointment.
situation: Jane and Lisa are working on a project at work that they must present soon.
intention: Jane wants to find the perfect outfit for the presentation.
moral_action: Jane picks out an outfit the day before the presentation and gets there early enough to prepare.
moral_consequence: Jane and Lisa look great presenting and are awarded bonuses for their performances.
immoral_action: Jane spends so much time picking out an outfit, she misses the presentation entirely.
immoral_consequence: Both Jane and Lisa are reprimanded at work and demoted.

norm: It's rude to call someone an insulting name.
situation: Clara is at the pool with her friend Sandy, who has just exited the changing room in her swimsuit.
intention: Clara wants to greet Sandy.
moral_action: "Clara flags Sandy down when she sees her, saying ""Hey girl!"" to get her attention."
moral_consequence: Clara and Sandy enjoy the pool together and have a good afternoon.
immoral_action: "Clara waves when she sees Sandy and says ""Hey Shamu!"" to get her attention."
immoral_consequence: Sandy feels mortified and very embarrassed, goes back to change, and no longer wants to hang out with Clara.

norm: It's wrong to be bitter and jealous toward others.
situation: George's friend got an A in a Math test, but he failed the test.
intention: George wants to comment on his friend's grade.
moral_action: George congratulates his friend for getting a good grade in the test.
moral_consequence: His friend thanks George and gives valuable advice to him on how to get a better grade in the test.
immoral_action: George criticizes that his friend got a good grade because of good luck.
immoral_consequence: His friend feels offended and turns away from him.

norm: You shouldn't steal a cat.
situation: Luke finds Cindy's cat on his roof when he's putting up lights.
intention: Luke wants the cat off his roof.
moral_action: Luke takes the cat off the roof and walks across the street to Cindy's house.
moral_consequence: Cindy is glad Luke found her cat before anything bad happened to it.
immoral_action: Luke takes the cat off the roof and puts it inside his house.
immoral_consequence: Eventually reward posters are seen around the neighborhood for a missing cat.

norm: It's good to want to do your best at academics.
situation: Ginger has a final exam coming up in a week for her freshman physics class, which covered 20 chapters of material.
intention: Ginger wants to prepare for the exam.
moral_action: Ginger studies roughly three chapters each night of the week before the test so that she understands all the material covered that year.
moral_consequence: Ginger gets a high grade on the exam and passes the course.
immoral_action: Ginger studies two chapters out of 20 the night before the exam, so she can answer at least some of the questions.
immoral_consequence: Ginger only gets correct answers on the material she studied, fails the exam, and has to redo the class next semester.

norm: It's wrong to steal people's wifi.
situation: Jeffrey hasn't paid his internet bill in months and knows that his neighbor, Holly, works from home with fast wifi.
intention: Jeffrey wants to get online.
moral_action: Jeffrey goes to the library to use their free wifi.
moral_consequence: Jeffrey is able to get online without paying for anything.
immoral_action: Jeffrey hacks into Holly's wifi account so that he can use her internet.
immoral_consequence: Holly experiences slow internet speeds and misses her work deadlines.

norm: It's not okay to have violent tenancies in life.
situation: Jon is working on a very frustrating project.
intention: He wants to relieve his stress.
moral_action: Jon recognizes h is frustration and walks away from his work for a moment to collect his thoughts.
moral_consequence: As Jon calms down he finds the solution to what has been frustrating him.
immoral_action: Jon is worked up from the project and hits his laptop out of anger.
immoral_consequence: Jon feels better from his outburst but finds he has broken his computer.

norm: It's mean to scare people for fun.
situation: John is spending time with his children and family.
intention: John wants to have fun with his son.
moral_action: John sets up a game for his son to play with him that is fun for both.
moral_consequence: John's son has a great time and grows a stronger bond with his father.
immoral_action: John hides from his son only to burst out and take him by suprise.
immoral_consequence: His son gets frightened and begins to sob uncontrollably ruining the day's fun.

norm: It’s polite to applaud.
situation: Bill is at a stand up comedy event and it's the moment when the performer finishes his bit.
intention: Bill wants to react to the end of the performance.
moral_action: Bill stands up and begins to clap loudly and cheer and whoop it up for the comedian.
moral_consequence: The comedian notices Bill and is delighted that Bill seems to have enjoyed the performance.
immoral_action: Bill stands up and begins to walk out towards the exit to go back home.
immoral_consequence: The comedian notices Bill walking out and is sad because he assumes that Bill hated the pefrormance.

norm: It is good to use a calendar.
situation: Carrie has been sent an invitation to join her friend Gia for a birthday brunch on the 27th of the month.
intention: Carrie wants to RSVP to the brunch.
moral_action: Carrie RSVP's to the brunch and marks it on her calendar.
moral_consequence: Carrie makes the brunch on time to celebrate Gia's birthday.
immoral_action: Carrie RSVP's to the brunch without noting the date on a calendar.
immoral_consequence: When the 27th comes around, Carrie completely forgets about the brunch and misses Gia's birthday celebration.

norm: It is good to work together to accomplish something hard.
situation: Sharon is building a house.
intention: She wants to begin roofing.
moral_action: Sharon calls her friends and schedules a day where she can have the most help.
moral_consequence: The roof is completed in one day and Sharon buys all her friends dinner and drinks for their help.
immoral_action: Sharon asks friends for help but no one is available for a few days, she impatiently decides to work on the roof herself.
immoral_consequence: Sharon gets a lot of the roof done, but she wakes up the next day with a pulled back and cannot build more for a few weeks.

norm: It's rude to use headphones when you're with other people.
situation: Randy hangs out with his friends every week and sometimes brings his music player to listen to.
intention: Randy wants to listen to music at his friend's house.
moral_action: Randy plays music over the stereo while him and his friends hang out.
moral_consequence: Randy and his friends are able to bond while listening to music.
immoral_action: Randy puts on a pair of headphones to listen to music while hanging out with his friends.
immoral_consequence: Randy's friends feel that he doesn't like their company enough and stop inviting him over.

norm: It's bad to text while driving a car.
situation: Jane is driving when she remembers that she has to tell her husband about something urgent.
intention: Jane wants to text her husband.
moral_action: Jane finds a place to briefly pull over and sends her husband the text message.
moral_consequence: Jane is able to get the urgent information to her husband safely and legally.
immoral_action: Jane continues to drive as she sends the text to her husband.
immoral_consequence: A police officer sees Jane texting and driving and gives her a ticket.

norm: You shouldn't use things that aren't yours.
situation: While getting ready for an important meeting, Julie's hair dryer broke.
intention: Julie wants to get her hair dry quickly.
moral_action: Julie uses a towel and vigorously rubs it all over her hair.
moral_consequence: Julie is relieved over the fact that she will still be to work on time.
immoral_action: Julie uses her sister's hair dryer and it breaks as well.
immoral_consequence: Julie is distraught over her sister's reaction when she finds out.

norm: You should share with your family.
situation: Gaby, who lives with her family, is at home watching Netflix, and she has the munchies.
intention: Gaby wants to order a pizza.
moral_action: Gaby orders a couple larger pizzas, so she can leave some for her family.
moral_consequence: Gaby's family is happy to have pizza and not have to make dinner.
immoral_action: Gaby orders only enough pizza for her to finish off by herself.
immoral_consequence: Gaby's family notices she got pizza and are disappointed there's not enough to go around.

norm: You shouldn't stand up for someone's bad behavior.
situation: Jeffrey is at the mall when he sees kids from school bullying another kid.
intention: Jeffrey wants to get involved.
moral_action: Jeffrey walks over to the bullies and stands up for the bullied kid by calling them out.
moral_consequence: The bullies run away with their tails between their legs and the bullied kid has a smile on his face.
immoral_action: Jeffrey joins in on the bullying.
immoral_consequence: The kid being bullied is hurt and ends up dropping out of school.

norm: You shouldn't take advantage of people.
situation: Sean plays a card game and is trading with James, who knows very little about the game.
intention: Sean wants one of James' valuable cards.
moral_action: Sean helps James realize the value and offers a rare card for the one he wants.
moral_consequence: James accepts the trade and is happy with it.
immoral_action: Sean offers James a trade using several common cards for the rare card.
immoral_consequence: James accepts the trade, realizes later that he was cheated, and loses respect for Sean.

norm: It's deplorable to intentionally give someone a sexually transmitted disease.
situation: Louis is having some drinks at his favorite martini lounge.
intention: Louis wants to have sex with someone.
moral_action: Louis picks up a handsome fellow and goes home with him and has sex using a condom.
moral_consequence: Louis has an exciting sexual encounter.
immoral_action: Louis takes a man home and has unprotected sex with him without telling him he is HIV+.
immoral_consequence: Louis is arrested for criminal transmission when the man discovers that Louis is positive.

norm: It's wrong for people to defraud others.
situation: Tim promised his roommate he'd have enough money to pay the rent that month, so he decides to sell his old, broken motorcycle.
intention: Tim wants to earn enough money to pay his rent.
moral_action: Tim asks his roommate to help him fix the motorcycle, so he can sell it.
moral_consequence: They get the motorcycle working and Tim sells it for more than enough money to pay the rent.
immoral_action: Tim places an ad on craigslist, listing his bike as being in top condition.
immoral_consequence: Tim can't pay the rent when no one buys the motorcycle because they find out it doesn't run.

norm: You shouldn't try to make people sick.
situation: Louisa has been coughing and sneezing for the past few days, and she thinks she might have Covid-19.
intention: Louisa needs to go shopping at the grocery store.
moral_action: Louisa decides to quarantine herself and stays at home until she feels better.
moral_consequence: Louisa feels better after a few days and doesn't contribute to the rising cases.
immoral_action: Louisa doesn't wear a mask and coughs while inside the grocery store.
immoral_consequence: People glare at Louisa, and Louisa is asked to leave the grocery store and fined.

norm: It's wrong to sleep with your partner's best friend.
situation: Josh is at a party when his girlfriend's best friend Marie starts flirting with him.
intention: Josh doesn't want to hurt Marie's feelings.
moral_action: Josh compliments Marie, and invites Marie to hang out with his attractive single friends later that night.
moral_consequence: Josh forms a close platonic friendship with Marie.
immoral_action: Josh returns Marie's advances leading into an intense erotic experience.
immoral_consequence: Josh is blasted on social media when people find out about his behavior.

norm: It's nice to share your art with others.
situation: Jamie is decorating his new apartment, and he his good friends with an artist, Tom.
intention: Jamie wants to decorate his new place with some of Tom's art.
moral_action: Tom agrees to help Jamie and even gives him a few art pieces free of charge.
moral_consequence: Jamie is overjoyed and decorates his place with the new artwork.
immoral_action: Tom refuses to help Jamie with decorating, and provides him with no artwork or advice.
immoral_consequence: Jamie is upset with Tom and his apartment continues to be bare.

norm: It's rude to make your sibling late for school.
situation: Angela's brother Bobby was supposed to wash the dishes but forgot to and now it is time to go to school.
intention: Bobby wants to get the dishes clean.
moral_action: Bobby decides that he will wash the dishes first thing when he gets home from school.
moral_consequence: Both Bobby and Angela arrive at school on time and the dishes get washed.
immoral_action: Bobby begs his sister to help him finish the dishes before heading to school.
immoral_consequence: Angela agrees to help wash the dishes but both of them are late for school and get in trouble.

norm: You should not make your partner feel unimportant.
situation: John's girlfriend achieved an important accomplishment that she has been working towards today.
intention: John wants to go to the bar.
moral_action: John suggests that he and his girlfriend go to celebrate her accomplishment at the bar.
moral_consequence: John's girlfriend feels that John cares about her life and accomplishments.
immoral_action: John doesn't celebrate his girlfriend's accomplishment and goes to the bar instead.
immoral_consequence: John's girlfriend feels like John doesn't value her at all.

norm: It's good to help friends find jobs.
situation: Natasha has been unemployed for several months and heard that her buddy Alex's job is looking for entry-level employees, so she asks if she can use him as a reference.
intention: Alex wants to respond to Natasha's question.
moral_action: Alex tells Natasha he will go a step further and write her a recommendation letter.
moral_consequence: Natasha appreciates what Alex is doing for her and it strengthens their friendship status.
immoral_action: Alex tells Natasha that he would prefer she didn't use him because if she gets hired and doesn't do well, it will reflect poorly on him.
immoral_consequence: Natasha takes offense to what Alex said because it shows he doesn't think she would do well, so she cuts off the friendship.

norm: It's good to have friends in your life.
situation: Vivian feels stressed due to heavy workload recently and her friend Maisy invites her for a hangout tonight.
intention: Vivian wants to respond to Maisy's invitation.
moral_action: Vivian agrees to go to dinner with Maisy.
moral_consequence: Vivian vents her frustration in her work to Maisy and feels much better.
immoral_action: Vivian decides to work overtime and turns down Maisy's invitation.
immoral_consequence: Vivian feels exhausted and sad for her increased stress.

norm: It's unacceptable to judge the way someone grieves.
situation: Patty's mother recently passed away and her brother did not want to attend the funeral.
intention: Patty wants to talk to her brother about not attending the funeral.
moral_action: Patty tells her brother it's okay for him to process their mother's death in his own way.
moral_consequence: Patty's brother will feel that Patty is trying to understand him and cares.
immoral_action: Patty tells her brother it was rude to not attend the funeral.
immoral_consequence: Patty's brother will feel misunderstood by Patty and attacked by her.

norm: It's good to report things to security.
situation: Amy is at the airport and sees somebody leave a backpack unattended.
intention: Amy wants to do something about the backpack.
moral_action: Amy knows that unattended packages are a danger in airports so immediately tells someone with a uniform.
moral_consequence: Security is able to respond to the backpack to take care of it safely and Amy feels good about reporting it.
immoral_action: Amy walks up to the backpack and takes it and then checks what is inside.
immoral_consequence: Amy is later arrested for stealing when the person who lost the backpack reports it stolen and police review CCTV footage.

norm: You should tip for good services.
situation: Jack just finished his favorite meal at a restaurant where he liked the waiter and is about to pay.
intention: Jack wants to save his money.
moral_action: Jack leaves a tip he can afford for the waiter.
moral_consequence: The waiter is grateful and likes Jack and will serve him well next time.
immoral_action: Jack doesn't give the waiter any tip and leaves.
immoral_consequence: The waiter doesn't like Jack and will give him bad service next time.

norm: Getting drunk is frowned upon.
situation: James' parents tried to make him come with them to a long, boring Christmas sermon.
intention: James wants to get out of going to the sermon.
moral_action: James pretends that he threw up and is afraid of infecting the other church members.
moral_consequence: James' parents let him stay home and read his favorite book instead of listening to endless preaching.
immoral_action: James chugs half a bottle of vodka and starting talking about utter nonsense.
immoral_consequence: James' parents let him stay home but lecture him extensively on Christmas morning.

norm: It is unobservant to lose track of your family members.
situation: Kerry was babysitting her younger brother and brings him to the park.
intention: Kerry wants to talk to her friend on her phone.
moral_action: Kerry waits until they get home to call her friend on the phone.
moral_consequence: Kerry is able to keep her brother in her sight the whole time they are on the phone.
immoral_action: Kerry lets her brother run off alone and talks to her friend the whole time they are at the park.
immoral_consequence: Kerry can't find her brother and has to call the police to file a missing persons report.

norm: It is rude to take something away from someone.
situation: Ash sees that Frank has a much nicer TV remote even though they have the same TV.
intention: Ash wants the better TV remote.
moral_action: Ash goes to an electronics store and buys the same remote Frank has.
moral_consequence: Ash enjoys the new remote for his TV and has a fun time using it and talks to Frank about it.
immoral_action: Ash takes Frank's TV remote without premission.
immoral_consequence: Frank assumes he lost the remote and just buys a new one.

norm: It's wrong to leave a pet out in bad weather.
situation: Penny's dog keeping pooping inside the house, but there's a tornado warning in her area.
intention: Penny wants to punish her dog.
moral_action: Penny makes her dog stay in their kennel for the night and potty trains them later on.
moral_consequence: Penny's dog is able to learn why they angered Penny in the first place.
immoral_action: Penny makes her dog stay outside during the tornado warning.
immoral_consequence: Penny's dog becomes scared and doesn't understand why they're being punished.

norm: It's mean to hurt people.
situation: Alex and Richie are in the playroom, and Richie is playing with the dinosaur toy.
intention: Alex wants to play with the dinosaur.
moral_action: Alex asks Richie if he could play with the toy, and when Richie says no Alex plays with something else.
moral_consequence: Alex and Richie end up playing with each other and having fun.
immoral_action: Alex pulls the dinosaur toy from Richie and pushes Richie down.
immoral_consequence: Richie starts crying and Alex's dad scolds Alex for hurting Richie.

norm: It's wrong to trick someone into going out with you.
situation: Gary is at a party and sees Lucy, who he finds very attractive.
intention: Gary wants to ask Lucy out.
moral_action: Gary tells Lucy his real occupation and asks Lucy about her life and interests.
moral_consequence: Lucy finds Gary charming, and they date for a long time.
immoral_action: Gary claims he is a doctor and very rich, though he is neither of those.
immoral_consequence: Lucy quickly realizes on their first date that Gary was lying and dumps him.

norm: It's not okay to burden someone staying in their home.
situation: Zen is staying at a friend's house because he lost his apartment and Zen has questions but his friend is working in his home office.
intention: Zen wants to decide if he should knock and ask the questions or not.
moral_action: Zen waits for his friend to finish work before asking questions.
moral_consequence: The relationship stays respectful and secure.
immoral_action: Zen knocks and is told to hold on, then mentions it'll take just a minute.
immoral_consequence: Zen realizes he's wearing out his welcome when his friend gets annoyed with him.

norm: You shouldn't be intolerant of people.
situation: Gwen is attending a Seder at her Jewish friend's home.
intention: Gwen wants to participate during the religious ceremony.
moral_action: Gwen asks appropriate questions as to why the host opened the back door.
moral_consequence: The host gives Gwen an interesting answer and is impressed by her curiosity; Gwen's friend is happy she invited Gwen to the dinner.
immoral_action: Gwen makes inappropriate comments when the host opens the back door.
immoral_consequence: The host of the dinner is offended and Gwen's friend is embarrassed that she invited Gwen to the dinner.

norm: It's good to reconcile your differences with your significant other.
situation: Mandy and her partner are not on good terms because of a recent and nasty argument.
intention: Mandy wants to avoid fighting over this issue again.
moral_action: Mandy extends an olive branch to her partner, and they talk it out.
moral_consequence: Mandy's partner is happy to move past the fight that they had and fix things with her.
immoral_action: Mandy decides to hold it against her partner and ends up leaving him.
immoral_consequence: Mandy's partner is heartbroken that she left him over the fight they had.

norm: It's good to get tested for things.
situation: Casey is working next to someone in his office with covid, and he lives older people.
intention: Casey wants to show concern about his own health.
moral_action: Casey gets tested at Walmart for Covid, and he warns his roommates about his sickness.
moral_consequence: Casey's elderly roommates take a vacation to the beach while Casey lives in isolation.
immoral_action: Casey takes herbal supplements that claim to keep the virus from entering the body.
immoral_consequence: Casey's elderly roommates are infected with Covid.

norm: You shouldn't play with the emotions of women.
situation: Cory meets Jessica at a bar and realizes that Jessica likes him.
intention: Cory wants to see and date women other than Jessica.
moral_action: Cory tells Jessica that he isn't interested, but they can still be friends.
moral_consequence: Cory and Jessica spend time together and become best friends.
immoral_action: Cory calls Jessica every night before he goes out on dates with other women.
immoral_consequence: Jessica falls in love with Cory and starts to stalk him at his work.

norm: It is good when couples help each other out.
situation: Olive has just gotten home from work while her wife Amy has been taking care of their infant son all day.
intention: Olive wants to relax.
moral_action: Olive tells Amy that she'll take a bath with their son and take a nap with him.
moral_consequence: Amy is glad to have some time for herself after a long day, and Olive gets to play with their baby in the bath.
immoral_action: Olive asks Amy if she can cook dinner while Olive takes a long bath on her own.
immoral_consequence: Amy glares at Olive and tells her she needs to help out with taking care of their baby, and the two get into a fight.

norm: You should be polite about weight comments with your partner.
situation: Lacey has noticed that her partner has been putting on a lot of unhealthy weight recently.
intention: Lacey wants to discourage her partner from being unhealthy.
moral_action: Lacey suggests that they both start going to the gym more often.
moral_consequence: Lacey's partner feels encouraged to be healthier.
immoral_action: Lacey points out that her partner is getting fat.
immoral_consequence: Lacey's partner is hurt by the way she mentioned his weight.

norm: It's unhealthy to stay in the bed relationship
situation: Laura had been dating Danny for two years, but he treated her poorly.
intention: Laura wants to get married.
moral_action: Laura leaves Danny and gets married to a new man that she meets.
moral_consequence: Laura is much happier without having Danny in her life.
immoral_action: Laura eventually gets married to Danny even though she doesn't like how he treats her.
immoral_consequence: Laura gets sadder and more depressed because of the way Danny treats her.

norm: It's inappropriate to makeout with your teacher.
situation: Erica is in college and having difficulty with a course.
intention: Erica wants to do well in the course.
moral_action: Erica hires a tutor to help her understand the course materials.
moral_consequence: Erica learns the materials and does well in the course.
immoral_action: Erica visits her professor's office and seduces him for a good grade.
immoral_consequence: They are caught by another student and the professor is fired and Amanda is disciplined.

norm: It's wrong to be overly protective of your things.
situation: Bryan owns an extremely rare and expensive trading card.
intention: Bryan wants to keep that trading card safe.
moral_action: Bryan simply locks the card in a safe with a solid combination.
moral_consequence: The safe keeps Bryan's card, well, safe from theft.
immoral_action: Bryan has a super security system installed that goes off every time a speck of dust enters the room the card is in.
immoral_consequence: The system has so many false positives that no one takes it seriously.

norm: Refusing to forgive is not cool in a relationship.
situation: Bella loaned a favorite book to her friend that came back tattered, however, her friend has apologized.
intention: Bella wants to talk to her friend about the apology.
moral_action: Bella tells her friend she accepts her apology and explains the significance of the book.
moral_consequence: Bella's friend will want to make it up to Bella for what she has done.
immoral_action: Bella tells her friend she can't accept the condition of the book no matter what her friend says as an apology.
immoral_consequence: Bella's friend will think Bella doesn't want to be friends anymore.

norm: It's wrong to violate human rights.
situation: King Bob needs to attract more tourists to his country.
intention: King Bob wants to built a world wonder.
moral_action: King Bob uses an army of paid laborers to get the wonder built quickly.
moral_consequence: Tourists the world over arrive to see the amazing construction and drastically ups the GDP of Bob's country.
immoral_action: King Bob uses an army of slaves to get the wonder built quickly.
immoral_consequence: The wonder attracts some tourists but many nations aren't keen on how it was built.

norm: It's rude to waste time.
situation: Bill has to give a speech to an audience of scientists on global warming that must last five minutes.
intention: Bill wants to give a long enough speech.
moral_action: Bill gives a compelling speech that gets right to the point.
moral_consequence: Bill is given a round of applause by the scientists.
immoral_action: Bill spends most of the five minutes of his speech talking slowly about irrelevant topics.
immoral_consequence: Bill is booed by the scientists for trying to pad his speech time.

norm: Friendship check on each other
situation: James hasn't seen his friend for a week, and the last time they met the friend was coughing.
intention: James wants to avoid getting COVID-19.
moral_action: James calls his friend ten times, and when his friend doesn't answer James sends emergency services for a welfare check.
moral_consequence: The EMTs find James' friend passed out and rush him to the hospital.
immoral_action: James tries to forget about his friend because even thinking about COVID-19 stresses him out.
immoral_consequence: The next thing James hears about his friend is that he died alone of COVID-19.

norm: It's good to become friendly with your significant other's family.
situation: Johnny is staying over at his husband's, James, family for the holidays.
intention: Johnny wants to be able to tolerate James' family weird eccentricities.
moral_action: Johnny laughs and nods at all of James' family stories and jokes.
moral_consequence: James' family grow to like and approve of Johnny.
immoral_action: Johnny spends most of the holiday hiding from James' family.
immoral_consequence: James gets upsets, and he and Johnny get into an argument.

norm: It is good to stand up for your pets.
situation: Jacky is petting her dog while her roommate Arnold insists that the dog chewed on shoes.
intention: Jacky wants to make Arnold happy.
moral_action: Jacky makes a joke about her dog being unable to chew on things left in Andrew's room.
moral_consequence: Andrew realizes that Jacky is right, and he offers to start taking the dog out on walks.
immoral_action: Jacky scolds her dog and agrees to keep her dog in a kennel while she's not in the room.
immoral_consequence: Andrew continues to blame Jacky's dog for everything wrong in the house.

norm: It's good to tell your children your feelings.
situation: Brandon has had a tough day at work and after work his son asks him to play catch.
intention: Brandon wants to respond to his son.
moral_action: Brandon tells his son he'd like to play catch, but he's exhausted from working all day.
moral_consequence: Brandon's son will understand that Brandon is tired.
immoral_action: Brandon tells his son he doesn't want to play catch.
immoral_consequence: Brandon's son will think Brandon is mean.

norm: It's wrong to judge others based on their life choices.
situation: Jason had just read something about trans people, and his next client is trans.
intention: Jason wants to comment on their gender.
moral_action: Jason asks the client what their pronouns are.
moral_consequence: Jason gets the trust of his new client.
immoral_action: Jason tells the client that trans identity is a form of mental illness.
immoral_consequence: Jason loses his new client.

norm: You should always get your school work done.
situation: Bastian is going on a camping trip with his Dad, but has a test coming up at school.
intention: Bastian wants to enjoy his trip.
moral_action: Bastian enjoys being out in nature and does his school work before bed each night.
moral_consequence: When the day of the test comes Bastian is well prepared and passes his test.
immoral_action: Bastian enjoys being out in nature and forgets all about his big test.
immoral_consequence: When the day of the test comes Bastian is unprepared and fails.

norm: You shouldn't out people before they are ready.
situation: Mark knew his friend, Joe, and Joe's partner, Neil, want to come out to their family.
intention: Mark wants to send out invitations for a celebration party for Joe and Neil.
moral_action: Mark send out invitations for a mystery party to Joe's and Neil's families.
moral_consequence: All families RSVP positively and Joe and Neil have a chance to talk to their families first.
immoral_action: Mark sends out invitations to Joe's and Neil's coming out party to their families.
immoral_consequence: Both families find out about their relationship from the invitations and RSVP saying they won't be coming.

norm: It's good to defend yourself as necessary.
situation: Bonnie is at school and a classmate keeps physically bullying her.
intention: Bonnie wants the abuse to stop.
moral_action: Bonnie decides to take a stand against the classmate and gets into an altercation making promises to do it again.
moral_consequence: Bonnie scares off the bullying for good and feels more confident in herself.
immoral_action: Bonnie decides that if she ignores it that it could stop, so she just hangs her head down when she is bullied.
immoral_consequence: The classmate bullying Bonnie sees it as a sign of weakness and teases Bonnie even more.

norm: You shouldn't refuse to help people.
situation: Tim receives an e-mail from his estranged brother asking him for help with a family matter.
intention: Tim wants to send a reply to his brother.
moral_action: Tim decides to be the bigger person and help his brother out.
moral_consequence: Tim reestablishes a relationship with his brother.
immoral_action: Tim reminds his brother that they are not on good terms and refuses to aid him.
immoral_consequence: Tim is later wracked with guilt when he finds out his brothers problems had a sad result.

norm: You shouldn't go behind your family's back.
situation: Jonah and his family are in financial ruin and are at home discussing their options.
intention: Jonah wants find a solution to the problem.
moral_action: Jonah coordinates with the entire family, and they set out a detailed plan to cover how they can recover.
moral_consequence: Jonah and his family work hard together and overcome their financial woes.
immoral_action: Jonah ignores the discussion because he figures he can solve the problem on his own and sets out to do so without telling anybody about his intentions.
immoral_consequence: Jonah doesn't solve the problem and fails miserably which only exacerbates the family's financial situation.

norm: It's bad to be late for an engagement.
situation: Maria has a very important business meeting with a client.
intention: Maria wants to attend the meeting.
moral_action: Maria thinks showing up earlier than scheduled will make her seem prepared.
moral_consequence: Maria's client thinks Maria is responsible and enjoys working with her.
immoral_action: Maria thinks showing up past the scheduled time will make her seem more important.
immoral_consequence: Maria's client thinks Maria is irresponsible and chooses a new person to work with.

norm: You shouldn't abuse the kids you babysit.
situation: Jill is babysitting her neighbor's kids, and they are acting up.
intention: Jill wants the kids to quiet down.
moral_action: Jill decides to distract the kids with a movie.
moral_consequence: The kids enjoy the movie Jill put on and the parents continue to hire her in the future.
immoral_action: Jill takes the kids upstairs and locks them in their rooms for the rest of the night.
immoral_consequence: The kids cry to their parents about being mistreated and Jill is never hired by them again.

norm: It's not okay to do things that hurt your kids.
situation: Ben's son was caught stealing candy from the neighborhood store.
intention: Ben wants to punish his son.
moral_action: Ben takes away his son's electronics for a month.
moral_consequence: Ben's son regrets stealing the candy bar.
immoral_action: Ben hits his son with a belt leaving welts and bruises.
immoral_consequence: Ben's son becomes afraid of his father.

norm: It is  good to reassure others
situation: Mike's younger sister told him that no one liked her.
intention: Mike wants to respond to his sister.
moral_action: Mike tells his sister that she is an interesting person and there are many people who like her.
moral_consequence: His sister feels more confident and is grateful for her brother.
immoral_action: Mike tells his sister that he is not surprised no one likes her because she is boring.
immoral_consequence: His sister gets upset and feels terrible the rest of the week.

norm: You should stay home from school when you are sick.
situation: Marty has to take a test at school but has flu symptoms.
intention: Marty wants to take the test.
moral_action: Marty calls his teacher and explains he is sick and arranges to take the test at a later time.
moral_consequence: Marty is able to get over the flu and not risk the other students getting sick.
immoral_action: Marty goes to school and takes the test.
immoral_consequence: Marty gets the rest of his class sick with the flu.

norm: You have no right to strike another person's child.
situation: Cindy's neighbor's kid runs into her yard and up to Cindy and slaps her.
intention: Cindy wants to respond to the slap.
moral_action: Cindy decides to take the kid back to the neighbor's house and tell the parents what the kid did.
moral_consequence: The parents start shouting at the kid who gets grounded for a month.
immoral_action: Cindy decides to slap the kid back for slapping her first.
immoral_consequence: The kid's parents come running and shout at Cindy for slapping the kid.

norm: It's rude to turn someone who's suffering away.
situation: James had just enough money to buy a supersized Big Mac meal when he was approached by a hungry homeless person.
intention: James wants to have a satisfying dinner.
moral_action: James gave the homeless man half of his dinner money.
moral_consequence: James got a cheaper cheeseburger meal, and felt happy that he'd saved someone from going hungry.
immoral_action: James refused to give the homeless man any money, rationalizing that he'd probably use it to buy drugs.
immoral_consequence: James bought a supersized Big Mac meal, but couldn't stop thinking about the hungry man as he ate.

norm: It is good to help others with your experience.
situation: Fiona is a senior executive at a company and is meeting a group of new employees.
intention: Fiona wants to tell the new employees something.
moral_action: Fiona tells the new employees tips on how she got to her position.
moral_consequence: The new employees will have a path to success.
immoral_action: Fiona tells the new employees that some of them won't last a year.
immoral_consequence: The new employees will not be comfortable at the company.

norm: Is wrong to expect your guests pay for your wedding
situation: Lily was planning a large wedding, and she realized the total bill was going to be pretty high.
intention: Lily wants to find a way to help pay the bill.
moral_action: Lily decides to get a part time job waiting tables for a few months to help with costs.
moral_consequence: Lily has a great wedding and is able to pay it off after a few months.
immoral_action: Lily decides to charge all of her guests a $50 door charge to attend her wedding.
immoral_consequence: Lily is disappointed when the majority of her guests cancel and do not attend.

norm: It's bad to throw away items that could be recycled.
situation: Ian just finished throwing a big party and his guests left the house full of empty beer bottles and cans.
intention: Ian wants to tidy up his house.
moral_action: Ian separates the can and bottles from the garbage and puts the recyclable items in separate bags.
moral_consequence: It takes a long time for Ian to clean up around the house, but he's able to return the recyclables to the redemption center and make some extra money.
immoral_action: Ian dumps all of the bottles and cans into a bag with the rest of the trash and takes it to the garbage bin.
immoral_consequence: Ian finishes cleaning around his house really quickly and his trash can is full to the brim.

norm: It's important to eliminate suffering.
situation: Tamara's grandfather is on life support, and she is the sole decision maker for his care.
intention: Tamara wants whats best for her grandfather.
moral_action: Tamara approves a compassionate termination of his life.
moral_consequence: Tamara and her grandfather spend one last wonderful day together and the plug is pulled on his life before his suffering becomes too harsh.
immoral_action: Tamara asks her grandfather to hang on and fight to stay alive.
immoral_consequence: Tamara's grandfather stays alive for months and is in intense pain the entire time.

norm: It's wroong to use racist language.
situation: James gets into an argument on twitter with a black person who calls him racist slurs.
intention: James wants to tell off the person he's fighting with.
moral_action: James tells the person he's classless and that the argument got heated but no excuse for that language.
moral_consequence: James's opponent agrees and apologizes for it, and they go back to debating maturely.
immoral_action: James responds to the racism with racism of his own directed at the black man.
immoral_consequence: Twitter finds the post and finds out where James works and gets him fired for racism.

norm: It's wrong to drink excessively.
situation: Sean is upset and depressed because he recently broke up with his girlfriend .
intention: Sean wants to manage his depression.
moral_action: Sean joins a health club and goes to do workout regularly.
moral_consequence: Sean feels energized and hopeful, and his health improves too.
immoral_action: Sean goes to the bar and orders a dozen of beer to drink hoping that he can forget the breakup, and then he drives back home despite the hangover.
immoral_consequence: Sean strikes a lamp pole and gets injured seriously.

norm: It's wrong to shovel snow onto your neighbor's driveway.
situation: Barry's driveway is packed with snow and Tom's driveway barely has any on it.
intention: Barry wants to get rid of the snow in his driveway.
moral_action: Barry shovels up the snow and uses it to make a snowman in his yard.
moral_consequence: Tom compliments Barry for making a great looking snowman with snow from the driveway.
immoral_action: Barry uses a shovel to transfer the snow from his driveway to Tom's.
immoral_consequence: Tom sees Barry and comes outside to yell at him.

norm: It's wrong to take your frustration out on other people.
situation: Josh walks out of the room after fighting with his wife, and he sees his son accidentally spill something onto the floor.
intention: Josh wants to vent his frusterations.
moral_action: Josh cleans up his son's mess, and he then talks about his angry feelings with his friend.
moral_consequence: His friend gives him a fresh perspective on the argument.
immoral_action: Josh yells at his son and forces him to clean up the mess.
immoral_consequence: Josh and his wife get into another argument later that night over his actions.

norm: You shouldn't forget to pick up your kids.
situation: John has a bunch of errands to run, including picking up the kids from soccer practice and buying groceries for dinner.
intention: John wants to make sure he what he needs to cook dinner.
moral_action: John goes to pick up the kids from soccer practice and buys groceries on the way back.
moral_consequence: John's kids enjoy a delicious dinner and thank him for taking care of them.
immoral_action: John goes to the grocery store and picks up what he needs, and then heads home.
immoral_consequence: John's kids feel neglected and have to ask someone else for a ride.

norm: It's nice to be gracious about receiving money.
situation: Doug is a homeless man on the street late at night panhandling.
intention: Doug wants other people's money.
moral_action: When Doug receives a donation he thanks the people and says god bless you.
moral_consequence: More people are likely to give Doug money.
immoral_action: When Doug receives money from passers-by he just takes it and looks down and doesn't say a word.
immoral_consequence: Other people who see Doug act like this are less likely to give him anything.

norm: It's harmful to recruit cult members.
situation: Jack, while high on many different drugs, believed that he saw God, who took the form of a talking walrus.
intention: Jack wants to share his spiritual experience with others.
moral_action: Jack begins attending substance use support groups, so he doesn't end up having crazy hallucinations again.
moral_consequence: Jack kicks his drug habit and becomes a very successful chef.
immoral_action: Jack begins attending grief support groups, so he can find people who are vulnerable to his message about the afterlife.
immoral_consequence: Jack builds a thriving cult before eventually being taken down by the BATF.

norm: It is rude to ditch your significant
situation: Bryce and Amber are on a date at a carnival together.
intention: Bryce wants to go home because he's tired.
moral_action: Bryce tells Amber that he's exhausted and asks if she wants to leave with him.
moral_consequence: Bryce and Amber both go home to relax and enjoy their evening together.
immoral_action: Bryce tells Amber he's going to the bathroom but goes to his car and leaves instead.
immoral_consequence: Amber freaks out with worry over where Bryce went and breaks up with him when she realizes he left her alone.

norm: It's not okay to stalk people over the internet.
situation: James recently broke up with his ex, who blocked him on all her social media accounts.
intention: James wants to be in a relationship again.
moral_action: James creates an account on a dating site and tries to meet someone new.
moral_consequence: James eventually finds a new girlfriend who makes him forget all about his ex.
immoral_action: James creates numerous fake accounts to follow his ex on social media.
immoral_consequence: The ex eventually recognizes James' writing, blocks him again, and complains about him to all their mutual friends.

norm: It's not okay to be dependent on your parents.
situation: Adam moved out of his parents house last year and has recently lost his job.
intention: Adam wants to make sure he can pay his bills on time.
moral_action: Adam goes to a temp agency to see if he kind find short term work to pay his bills.
moral_consequence: Adam ends up getting hired the local electric company and makes more than enough money to pay his bills.
immoral_action: Adam calls his mom and begs for a loan.
immoral_consequence: She reluctantly agrees but decides to charge him a large amount of interest.

norm: It's wrong to act rudely toward mentally challenged folks.
situation: Danny was watching his kids play at the park, when a bigger kid came along and took a toy away from one of his children.
intention: Danny has to get the toy back for his child.
moral_action: Danny walks over to the bigger kid, and it becomes apparent that the child is developmentally challenged, Danny decides to let him keep the toy.
moral_consequence: The child is happy and befriends Danny's children, while Danny is thankful that he controlled his temper and didn't say anything inappropriate.
immoral_action: Danny yells at the bigger kid and tells him to give the toy back, he also refers to the older, bigger child as stupid.
immoral_consequence: The bigger kid gets upset and tells his parents, who come to let Danny know that he is developmentally challenged and not stupid, and Danny feels awful.

norm: It is wrong to commit voter fraud.
situation: Tyrell is at the local polling place for the election.
intention: Tyrell wants his candidate to win.
moral_action: Tyrell hands out pamphlets at the polling place to explain his candidate's platform.
moral_consequence: Tyrell convinces several people to vote for his favored candidate.
immoral_action: Tyrell casts his vote and then goes to anther polling place and votes again.
immoral_consequence: Tyrell is arrested for voter fraud.

norm: It's good to help out lost or abandoned animals.
situation: While walking home from the train station Paul spots an injured cat by the side of the road.
intention: Paul wants to help the cat.
moral_action: Paul takes the cat to a local vet and stays to make sure the cat is ok.
moral_consequence: Paul is gratified when the cats owner later contacts him and offers a reward as a thank you.
immoral_action: Paul wants to relax at home, so he ignores the cat and heads straight home.
immoral_consequence: Paul feels remorseful when he finds out that the cat died.

norm: You shouldn't ignore your manners.
situation: Tom is in a rush to get to a social dinner after having to work late, so he has to go to the dinner with no time to stop anywhere.
intention: Tom wants to arrive at the dinner on time after working late.
moral_action: Tom orders a bottle of wine on Amazon that is delivered to the hostess chilled just before dinner.
moral_consequence: The hostess is touched by Tom's thoughtfulness and enjoys the wine he sent.
immoral_action: Tom arrives to the dinner with no gift for the hostess because he did not have time to stop.
immoral_consequence: The hostess is a bit offended that Tom did not take the time to make a gesture for her.

norm: It's wrong to hold onto other people's pets.
situation: Katie is petsitting her friend Peter's cat while he is on vacation and has realized she loves cats.
intention: Katie wants to have a pet cat.
moral_action: After returning Peter's cat, Katie goes to the animal shelter and adopts her own pet cat.
moral_consequence: Katie and Peter both have pets they love and a cat is rescued.
immoral_action: Katie tells Peter that she is keeping his cat because she is attached to it now and loves it.
immoral_consequence: Peter gets very angry with Katie and calls the police on her to get his cat back.

norm: It is bad to fight at the dinner table.
situation: Samantha is irritated at her husband for insulting her cooking, while sitting at the table with their kids.
intention: Samantha wants to argue with her husband.
moral_action: Samantha waits for the meal to be over, then pulls her husband aside.
moral_consequence: The kids don't hear the argument, and Samantha gets her release.
immoral_action: Samantha starts yelling at her husband during the meal, right in front of the kids.
immoral_consequence: The kids get very upset, and are unable to eat while their parents fight.

norm: It's unfair to bully people
situation: Chad is eating lunch in the school cafeteria and sees that his classmate Billy has several delicious looking cookies on his plate.
intention: Chad wants to taste the cookies.
moral_action: Chad asks Billy if he can try one of the cookies.
moral_consequence: Billy is happy to share and gives Chad a cookie which he enjoys very much.
immoral_action: Chad pins Billy against the table until he gives him all the cookies.
immoral_consequence: Chad is sent to the principal's office and later suspended for bullying.

norm: It's bad to do poor work for one's employer.
situation: Gabi works as a data entry technician, and often finds the task boring and repetitive.
intention: Gabi just wants to finish for the day, so she can enjoy the weekend.
moral_action: Gabi pays attention to her work, doing it correctly and carefully.
moral_consequence: Gabi finishes 10 minutes early, and her boss tells her she can go home.
immoral_action: Gabi speeds through her work, not bothering to check for accuracy and making several mistakes.
immoral_consequence: Gabi has to go back and make corrections, taking longer to finish for the day.

norm: It's bad to drink before you legally can.
situation: Mackenzie is a high school freshman at a house party with college kids.
intention: Mackenzie wants to play beer pong.
moral_action: Mackenzie plays beer pong using water instead of beer.
moral_consequence: Mackenzie is able to participate in party activities without drinking.
immoral_action: Mackenzie plays beer pong and downs a lot of beer by the end of the night.
immoral_consequence: The cops show up to bust the party, and Mackenzie is booked for underage drinking.

norm: It's good to give people gifts.
situation: Jane was invited to Eddie's birthday party, and she decided to go.
intention: Jane wants to respond to Eddie's birthday.
moral_action: Jane brings a birthday gift to the birthday party to give to Eddie.
moral_consequence: Eddie feels grateful and thanks Jane for coming.
immoral_action: Jane brings some leftover food to the birthday party for sharing with Eddie.
immoral_consequence: Eddie feels disgusted and offended.

norm: It's good to find your child's lost things.
situation: Kent's kid ran in and told Kent that they had lost their toy.
intention: Kent wants to end the conversation.
moral_action: Kent agrees to help their kid find the missing toy.
moral_consequence: Kent moves some of the furniture and it's soon found behind a dresser.
immoral_action: Kent ignores his kid, so he can finish more work on his laptop.
immoral_consequence: The kid continues to look for the toy alone but it's in vain.

norm: It's expected that people learn to clean up after themselves.
situation: Alexa is at a Taco Bell with her friends, and they ordered a lot of food.
intention: Alexa is done eating and wants to leave.
moral_action: Alexa and her friend throw all of their trash out before leaving.
moral_consequence: A minimum wage workers feel grateful for them and gets to relax for a bit.
immoral_action: Alexa and her friends leave all of their trash on the tables.
immoral_consequence: A minimum wage worker who already has plenty of work to do will have to clean up after them.

norm: It is wrong to hate someone based on their gender.
situation: Josh just found out that one of his friends is a transgender male.
intention: Josh wants to let his friend know what he thinks about this.
moral_action: Josh tells his friend that he doesn't care about gender and that they should've just told him.
moral_consequence: Josh's friend feels closer to him and is more willing to trust him with their secrets.
immoral_action: Josh tells his friend that he doesn't want to be seen around anyone who's transgender.
immoral_consequence: Josh's friend's feelings are hurt, and they feel ashamed for transitioning.

norm: It's rude to hate people's excitement.
situation: Clair is trying to study while her roommate Sarah is talking loudly to her friend about an upcoming concert.
intention: Clair wants to focus on her work.
moral_action: Clair movies into her room to study.
moral_consequence: The new environment allows Clair to focus on her work.
immoral_action: Clair tells Sarah to leave the room because her energy is annoying.
immoral_consequence: Clair is harassed for the reminder of the evening by Sarah's friend.

norm: It's wrong not to return a lost item.
situation: Greg is walking down the street when he finds a wallet on the ground that belongs to Jim.
intention: Greg wants to get the wallet off the street.
moral_action: Greg takes the wallet and looks to find Jim's name before looking his phone number up, so he can notify Jim he found it.
moral_consequence: Jim is delighted and relieved his wallet has been found, and he won't have to go through the hassle of canceling cards.
immoral_action: Greg picks up the wallet and throws it in the garbage to get it off the road and prevent someone from taking it.
immoral_consequence: Jim is stressed out about his lost wallet and is forced to call and cancel all his cards in fear of identity theft.

norm: You shouldn't take money from people that isn't yours.
situation: Sally has a date this weekend that she is anticipating eagerly.
intention: Sally wants to buy a new dress for the date.
moral_action: Sally spends all the money she had saved and buys the most attractive dress she can afford.
moral_consequence: The date goes great and Sally is happy.
immoral_action: At the store, Sally sneaks some money from an unattended purse and buys a much nicer dress than planned.
immoral_consequence: Sally theft is recorded on the store's security video, and she is later arrested.

norm: It's rude to heat fish up in the office microwave.
situation: It is early in the morning on a work day and Jack is deciding what to bring to work for lunch.
intention: Jack wants to eat fish for lunch.
moral_action: Jack stops at the grocery store and picks up a pack of sushi to take for lunch.
moral_consequence: Jack's coworkers stop by his desk to see what he is eating, and they agree that it looks delicious.
immoral_action: Jack grabs a Tupperware with leftover fried fish to heat up in the office microwave.
immoral_consequence: Jack's office stinks after he heats the fish and it causes his coworkers to be angry with him.

norm: It is wrong to antagonize your sibling.
situation: Sam and her sister are watching a movie when her sister falls asleep snoring.
intention: Sam wants to watch the movie in peace.
moral_action: Sam gently wakes up her sister and tells her to go to bed.
moral_consequence: Sam's sister hugs her and bids goodnight, leaving Sam to watch TV in peace.
immoral_action: Sam throws cold water on her sister to wake her up.
immoral_consequence: Sam gets grounded and her sister won't speak to her for weeks.

norm: It is wrong to use your child support on yourself.
situation: Katie has kids and is going to receive her child support check this week.
intention: Katie has to figure out what to buy with her check.
moral_action: Katie buys a lot of snacks and meals for her kids with the money.
moral_consequence: Katie's kids feel taken care of even though their father isn't present.
immoral_action: Katie buys herself Starbucks coffee every day with the child support money.
immoral_consequence: Katie's kids suffer and complain about not getting enough stuff.

norm: Taking your family member's things without their permission is wrong.
situation: Steve, who lives with his mom that has an appointment that day, is planning to shop in town, but his car refuses to start.
intention: Steve wants to go to town.
moral_action: Steve asks his mom if he can take her car to town.
moral_consequence: Steve's mom drops Steve off in town, then goes to her appointment.
immoral_action: Steve takes his mom's car without asking and goes on a shopping trip.
immoral_consequence: Steve's mom can't get to her appointment, as her car is gone.

norm: It's rude to push your religious beliefs on others.
situation: John, who is a passionate atheist, is at dinner with a large group of his friends.
intention: John wants to make conversation.
moral_action: John has an open discussion with his friends about the meaning of faith and it's purpose in people's lives.
moral_consequence: John's friends appreciate the interesting conversation topic, and they all have a good time.
immoral_action: John goes on and on about how religious people are nutjobs and atheists are much smarter than them.
immoral_consequence: John's friends find his line of conversation insulting and bigoted.

norm: It's smart to end relationships that are not healthy.
situation: Jane gets physical abuse from her partner, and she relies on her partner's financial support.
intention: Jane wants to react to her situation.
moral_action: Jane finds a job and leaves her abusive partner.
moral_consequence: Jane lives happily and meets a good man in a social gathering, who starts to date her.
immoral_action: Jane needs the financial support from her partner and stays with him.
immoral_consequence: Jane gets seriously injured by her partner one day and is sent to the hospital for treatment.

norm: It's good to show concern for your immediate family.
situation: Peter is at home when his mom calls him and is crying so hard when he picks up the phone that she can't get a word out.
intention: Peter wants to get his mom to say something.
moral_action: Peter tells his mom to take it slow and just breathe and then tell him what's wrong.
moral_consequence: Peter's mom begins to feel a little better as she takes a deep breath to gather herself before telling him her issue.
immoral_action: Peter tells his mom that she needs to get on with it, he can't just sit there waiting for her to speak.
immoral_consequence: Peter's mom is already devastated and now even more so because he's being curt and impatient with her.

norm: It's not okay to make someone dependent on you.
situation: Brad has been dating his girlfriend Marla for the past two months.
intention: Brad wants to help Marla pay her bills.
moral_action: Brad offers to help Marla pay for part of her car note.
moral_consequence: Marla is able to get back on her feet with Brad's help.
immoral_action: Brad makes Marla quit her job and pays her bills himself, making her dependent on him.
immoral_consequence: When Brad and Marla break up, she has no way to pay for her bills.

norm: It's good to help your girlfriend put out a fire.
situation: Jim's girlfriend is cooking in the kitchen when a fire breaks out.
intention: Jim wants to respond to the fire.
moral_action: Jim gets water and towels to snuff the fire out.
moral_consequence: The fire is contained and Jim's girlfriend thinks he is heroic.
immoral_action: Jim runs out of the house leaving his girlfriend.
immoral_consequence: The house burns down and Jim's girlfriend thinks he is useless.

norm: You shouldn't disturb someone's meal.
situation: James was eating a sandwich in a cafe when he heard the two women behind him express opposing political beliefs.
intention: James wants to refute the women's political talking points.
moral_action: James grinds his teeth and makes a political post on Facebook.
moral_consequence: The women behind James quickly finish their meal and leave, allowing James to continue eating in peace.
immoral_action: James turns around and begins arguing about politics with the women behind him.
immoral_consequence: The women call James crazy, he raises his voice in retaliation, and the restaurant manager eventually comes over to kick him out.

norm: It is important to stick with commitments.
situation: Jack promised to go to the fair with his daughter but then his buddy Bill gives him football tickets.
intention: Jack wants to decide what to do.
moral_action: Jack goes to the fair with his daughter just like he promised.
moral_consequence: Jack's daughter loved going to the fair with her father.
immoral_action: Jack takes the tickets and goes to the football game.
immoral_consequence: Jack's daughter cries because she didn't get to go to the fair.

norm: You shouldn't overcharge for your services.
situation: Corey runs a landscaping business and is in competition with a fellow local landscaper, Chris.
intention: Corey wants to make more money than Chris.
moral_action: Corey sets up a buy one get one half off promotion.
moral_consequence: Corey earns repeat customers this way and his business grows beyond state borders.
immoral_action: Corey charges his clients twice  what Chris charges for his services, hoping this will earn him more money.
immoral_consequence: Corey's clients find his prices to be a ripoff and take their business over to Chris.

norm: It is wrong to ditch obligations.
situation: Juan was sitting at home relaxing when he remembered that he was supposed to take his friend Lonnie to the airport.
intention: Juan wants to decide what to do next.
moral_action: Juan goes and picks up Lonnie like he promised he would.
moral_consequence: Lonnie is very grateful to Juan and promises to return the favor one day.
immoral_action: Juan isn't in the mood to leave home, so he texts Lonnie that he won't be able to drive him.
immoral_consequence: Lonnie is stuck with no ride and ends up missing his flight.

norm: It is wrong to date someone out of spite.
situation: Jane has been being pestered by a co-worker for years to date him.
intention: Jane wants the pestering to end.
moral_action: Jane contacts he workplace's human resources department and files a complaint against the pestering co-worker.
moral_consequence: The co-worker is reprimanded for their behavior and asked to transfer to another office far away from Jane.
immoral_action: While angry one day, Jane relents and offers to go on a single date with the co-worker.
immoral_consequence: The co-worker does not get the hint that it is a one off thing and begins to stalk Jane outside of work.

norm: It's bad to gossip about others at work.
situation: Dan is at work have a talk with one of his many coworkers.
intention: Dan wants to tell his coworker something interesting.
moral_action: Dan tells his coworker about an adventure of his from his past that most people usually find interesting.
moral_consequence: Dan's coworker enjoys the story and Dan feels good about their conversation.
immoral_action: Dan shares some private information he knows about their boss with his coworker.
immoral_consequence: Dan's coworker tells other coworkers about the information and soon everybody at work knows which could land Dan in trouble with his boss.

norm: It's rude to spit in white people's food.
situation: Brooklyn is at her job where she is a waitress and is serving a particularly rude customer.
intention: Brooklyn wants to vent her fustrations.
moral_action: Brooklyn tells her boss that she needs a break, so she can get some air.
moral_consequence: Brooklyn's boss takes care of the customer for her and Brooklyn is able to calm down outside.
immoral_action: Brooklyn decides to spit in the customer's food as revenge when she brings it out to them.
immoral_consequence: Another customer sees what Brooklyn does and gets her fired from her job.

norm: You shouldn't bring a sick child out in public.
situation: Harry's daughter has a bad cold and is crying because she feels so awful and bored.
intention: Harry wants to help his daughter feel better.
moral_action: Harry reads his daughter her favorite books and makes her favorite food for her.
moral_consequence: Harry's daughter is able to rest and start to feel better.
immoral_action: Harry takes his daughter to the park because he thinks playing might help her feel better.
immoral_consequence: Harry's daughter gets her germs all over the playground and recovers more slowly because she used up all her energy.

norm: It's wrong to fight with your family.
situation: Mary is having dinner with her family.
intention: Mary wants to tell her sister shes mad at her.
moral_action: Mary waits until after dinner then talks to her sister calmly.
moral_consequence: Mary and her sister solve the problems and have a fun night.
immoral_action: Mary starts yelling at her sister at the dinner table.
immoral_consequence: Mary and her whole family get into a fight.

norm: It is bad to run over an animal.
situation: Gina is on her way to work when she sees a cat crossing the road.
intention: Gina wants to make it to work on time.
moral_action: Gina turns onto a different street, so she doesn't have to wait for the cat to cross.
moral_consequence: Gina makes it to work on time and someone else ended up stopping for the cat.
immoral_action: Not wanting to wait for the cat to cross, Gina keeps driving and runs over the cat.
immoral_consequence: The cat does not survive the hit from Gina's car.

norm: It's immoral for old people to sleep with teenagers.
situation: Roger is hanging out at the pool when Samantha, a teenage girl, sits down on his lap and starts flirting with him.
intention: Roger doesn't want to hurt Samantha.
moral_action: Roger makes a funny joke about his age before offering to set Samantha up with one of his employees.
moral_consequence: Roger is thanked by his employee who enjoys spending time with Samantha.
immoral_action: Roger returns the kiss, and they end up having sex in the back yard.
immoral_consequence: Roger is arrested when a police officer catches them fooling around in the car.

norm: You're discouraged from trying to buy a girlfriend online.
situation: Ralph is a single man, and his friend invited him to a party that requires a date.
intention: Ralph wants to find a temporary partner for the night.
moral_action: Ralph asks his friend if they know any single girls looking for a date.
moral_consequence: His friend sets him up with a girl Ralph eventually marries.
immoral_action: Ralph orders a date from a shady escort service.
immoral_consequence: Someone at the party recognizes Ralph's date and embarrasses him in front of everyone.

norm: It's good to use a bike for short commutes.
situation: James lived four blocks away from the office building where he worked, but biking to work made him sweaty.
intention: James wants to look professional at work.
moral_action: James biked to work every day and took a sponge bath in the office bathroom before going into work.
