moral_consequence: James' coworkers praised him for his environmentally conscious behavior and good grooming.
immoral_action: James drove to work every day in an air-conditioned car.
immoral_consequence: James' coworkers constantly scolded him about not being environmentally responsible, as was the professional standard in their office.

norm: It is expected that you save food for other people

moral_consequence: Dan is happy at John's polite statement and is happy to see a familiar face in the crowd.
immoral_action: John quickly looks down at the ground pretending not to notice Dan's wave and scurries off in a different direction.
immoral_consequence: Dan is hurt that John is seemingly trying to ditch him and wonders what is wrong with him that John would not want to talk to him.

norm: It's rude to not show up to a date.
situation: Linda is supposed to go on a date tonight, but she stayed out too late the night before and is extremely tired.
intention: Linda wants to stay home and sleep.
moral_action: Linda calls her date to say that she won't be able to make it that night, reschedules for the following weekend, and goes to sleep.
moral_consequence: Linda's date is understanding and looks forward to the date the next weekend.
immoral_action: Linda doesn't tell her date that she won't be there, lays on the couch, and sleeps until the morning.
immoral_consequence: Linda's date arrives at the meeting place, waits for an hour, and is very upset that he has been stood up.

norm: It's bad to abuse children.
situation: John comes home to his house exasperated after being berated by his boss in front of his colleagues and sees his kids in the kitchen.
intention: John wants to let off steam after a tough day at work.
moral_action: John takes a deep breath, scoops his kids up in his arms and takes them to the movies.
moral_consequence: John's kids love him more and feel good and happy.
immoral_action: John raises his voice and uses bad language towards his kids.
immoral_consequence: John's kids become afraid of him and resent him and feel sad.

norm: You shouldn't dictate other people's diets.
situation: Tom notices Jane has been gaining a lot of weight the last few months and is near her.
intention: Tom wants to let Jane know she is not eating healthy.
moral_action: Tom tells Jane he feels like she could eat healthier but does not dictate what that entails.
moral_consequence: Jane thanks Tom for the feedback, and they are able to get along the rest of the day without drama.
immoral_action: "Tom demands that Jane cut down on eating, or he will, ""never see her again""."
immoral_consequence: Jane feels like Tom is overbearing, and they get into a shouting match.

norm: It is polite to maintain good personal hygiene
situation: James has a heavy course load and is very stressed studying for finals.
intention: James wants to use all his available time studying.
moral_action: James listens to his professors' recorded lectures while he showers.
moral_consequence: James is both well prepared for his finals and hygienic enough to be socially acceptable.
immoral_action: James stops showering, so he'll have more time available to study.
immoral_consequence: James' roommate eventually drag him into the shower to eliminate the stench.

norm: It is unhealthy to shoot up drugs.
situation: Charles has a busy fast paced life and must balance work and family.
intention: Charles wants to reduce stress and find activities that give him pleasure.
moral_action: Charles eats healthy and takes up exercise both on his own and with his family.
moral_consequence: Charles has more energy and less stress making his work life balance easier to manage.
immoral_action: Charles takes up drugs to fill the void including heroin and crystal meth.
immoral_consequence: Charles loses his job and family and must go to rehabilitation.

norm: It's good to rescue an animal.
situation: Jan is talking with the members of her family about getting a new pet.
intention: Jan wants get a dog.
moral_action: Jan goes to the county animal shelter and adopts a dog from them.
moral_consequence: Jan saves the life of a dog that would have euthanized.
immoral_action: Jan goes to a puppy mill and buys a dog from them.
immoral_consequence: Jan furthers the mistreatment of animals by purchasing a puppy.

norm: It is good to be different.
situation: Jake is going to a restaurant with friends, and is notorious for never picking a unique meal.
intention: Jake wants to order food at the restaurant.
moral_action: Jake orders what he likes instead of ordering what other people order.
moral_consequence: Jake's friends congratulate Jake on his personality growth and Jake enjoys his meal more than usual.
immoral_action: Jake orders what everyone else is ordering like usual.
immoral_consequence: Jake's friends verbally question if Jake has a personality, and Jake feels less confident.

norm: it's wrong to blame your faults on other people.
situation: Tom recently lost his job and worries that his stressed out family will blame him for it.
intention: Tom wants to explain why he lost his job to his family.
moral_action: Tom tells his family that, despite the mental health of his family, his job loss was his own fault.
moral_consequence: Tom feels relieved he had the courage to admit this, and his family thanks him for it.
immoral_action: Tom tells his family that the emotional problems of other family members caused him to lose his job.
immoral_consequence: Tom's family begins to think less of him for not taking responsibility and Tom feels guilty.

norm: You shouldn't leave an employer in a bad situation.
situation: Nyssa is the manager at a mom and pop owned grocery store, and has been offered a job at a bigger retailer.
intention: Nyssa wants to take the job with the bigger retailer.
moral_action: Nyssa gives a two-month notice to her employer before moving on in her career.
moral_consequence: Nyssa's employer is able to find her replacement, and she moves up with her career.
immoral_action: Nyssa leaves her job for the bigger retailer without informing her employer.
immoral_consequence: Nyssa's employer is left scrambling for months trying to find her replacement.

norm: It's frowned upon to produce and share naked photos.
situation: Carol is in high school and is a good student but does not have a very active social life.
intention: Carol wants to be popular with boys.
moral_action: Carol applies to become a cheerleader and is accepted on the cheerleading team.
moral_consequence: Carol's parents are very proud of her.
immoral_action: Carol decides to take naked pictures of herself and share them with a few boys.
immoral_consequence: Carol's parents find out what she has been doing and are ashamed of their daughter.

norm: It can be rude to point out someone's breathe stinks.
situation: Julie and her friend Laura are on a blind double date, and Julie notices that Laura's breath smells odd.
intention: Julie wants to help Laura with her breath.
moral_action: Julie asks if Laura wants to grab a couple drinks at the bar real quick and tells her to run use some mouthwash when they're alone.
moral_consequence: Laura appreciates Julie helping her out and feels more confident after fixing her breath.
immoral_action: Julie blurts out in the middle of the date that Laura's breath smells and that she should do something about it.
immoral_consequence: Laura goes to the bathroom to use some mouthwash, but feels self conscious and less sociable for the rest of the date.

norm: Pretending to have things you don't is not okay.
situation: As a member of the PTA at her son's exclusive private school Joan is expected to help plan a fundraiser.
intention: Joan wants to impress her peers.
moral_action: Joan contributes a great deal of her time and energy to make sure the event goes off without a hitch.
moral_consequence: Joan is able to be a driving force behind the event.
immoral_action: Joan says she can arrange a celebrity appearance, without having the means to do so.
immoral_consequence: Joan is humiliated when she is unable to arrange an adequate celebrity appearance.

norm: It's disgusting when people don't respect proper hygiene.
situation: James, a chef, leaves the kitchen for a quick bathroom break during a busy lunch shift.
intention: James wants to get back to the kitchen quickly.
moral_action: James rushes using the bathroom but stops to wash his hands.
moral_consequence: James satisfies the restaurants cleanliness standards.
immoral_action: James takes his time using the bathroom but skips washing his hands to save time.
immoral_consequence: James is spotted by a customer who then complains to the manager.

norm: You shouldn't ignore your friends and slip away from them.
situation: Randy just recently started dating Theresa, a young woman that he finds very attractive and interesting.
intention: Randy wants to spend more time getting to know Theresa.
moral_action: Randy invites Theresa to join him when he's hanging out with his group of friends.
moral_consequence: Randy's friends get to know Theresa as well, and they grow really fond of her.
immoral_action: Randy slowly spends more and more time with Theresa instead of with his friends who rarely ever get to see him anymore.
immoral_consequence: Randy's friends stop inviting him to hang out, and they eventually grow distant.

norm: It's wrong to judge people by how much they weigh.
situation: Andrea has a best friend, Christina, who is self-conscious about her weight.
intention: Andrea wants to go swimming with Christina.
moral_action: Andrea tells Christina that she looks great no matter what she wears.
moral_consequence: Christina feels free to be herself and has a great time swimming with Andrea.
immoral_action: Andrea tells Christina that two-piece bikinis don't suit her body type.
immoral_consequence: Christina feels embarrassed and refuses to swim with Andrea.

norm: It is good to treat everyone as equals.
situation: Anne talks to the various people around her in the pub.
intention: Anne wants to talk to lots of people.
moral_action: Anne talks to everyone she sees pretty much equally.
moral_consequence: Lots of people on the pub have fun talking to Anne.
immoral_action: Anne keeps talking to the richer people first and the poor people last.
immoral_consequence: Lots of people start assuming Anne's a gold-digger or otherwise after money.

norm: It is wrong to insult someone else's skills.
situation: Joe is an art director at a games company watching an employee draw.
intention: Joe wants to comment on the drawing.
moral_action: Joe says the drawing can have some improvements and points out where to do them.
moral_consequence: The employee will try to get better and improve.
immoral_action: Joe says the drawing is not up to level and the artist is not talented.
immoral_consequence: The employee will feel depressed about the comments.

norm: It's wrong to give animals food for people.
situation: Jill knows there are wild deer in the forest near her house.
intention: Jill wants to see the deer up close.
moral_action: Jill quietly waits for the deer to wander closer.
moral_consequence: The deer stick to their natural, healthy grazing spots.
immoral_action: Jill puts a bucket of grain out for the deer to eat.
immoral_consequence: The deer become dependent on the food Jill puts out and get sick when she stops.

norm: It's wrong to go through someone else's phone.
situation: Anna heard her boyfriend Kevin talking to someone quietly on the phone.
intention: Anna wants to find out was on the phone.
moral_action: Anna asks Kevin who he was talking to instead of going through his phone to find out.
moral_consequence: Kevin tells Anna that he was talking to a old friend.
immoral_action: When Anna sees Kevin's phone on the table she looks through his phone calls to see who he was talking to.
immoral_consequence: Kevin catches Anna with his phone and asks her what she's doing going through it.

norm: It's wrong to intentionally hurt someone
situation: Gloria deeply resents a colleague she knows very well and who made her look bad in front of their boss.
intention: Gloria wants to feel better after having been treated poorly.
moral_action: Gloria decides to tell her colleague how she feels and realizes her colleague did not act on purpose, which calms her down.
moral_consequence: Gloria is seen as a cool and mature individual who reacts wisely to perceived slights.
immoral_action: Gloria uses some private information she has on her colleague to hurt her feelings.
immoral_consequence: Gloria comes across as vengeful and bitter at work.

norm: It's good to appreciate others.
situation: Dave is told by Marsha that Dave's boss Tony, who Dave hasn't liked in the past, went out of his way to make Dave look good to upper management.
intention: Dave wants to respond to the news he just heard.
moral_action: Dave tells Marsha that he's amazed by Tony's generosity and hopes that he can find a way to thank Tony and repay him.
moral_consequence: Marsha gains respect for Dave and is happy to see someone willing to give praise to a person they didn't get along in the past.
immoral_action: Dave tells Marsha that it's about time that Tony did something useful as Tony is generally useless.
immoral_consequence: Marsha is taken aback at the fact that Dave is seeking to point out negatives and doesn't seem to care about Tony's compliments.

norm: People will think you're a creep if you stalk people.
situation: Jimmy has a big crush on his friend's sister who is in high school, but he's too shy to talk to her.
intention: Jimmy wants to know more about the girl before talking to her.
moral_action: Jimmy talks to his friend about his sister and tells him that he likes her.
moral_consequence: Jimmy is able to learn more about the girl and is more confident in talking to her.
immoral_action: Every time Jimmy sees the girl talking, he stands near her to hear what she's saying.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy is seen as a weirdo by the girl, and Jimmy ruins any chance he ever had with her.

norm: It's fun to go clubbing with your buddies.
situation: John is finishing up work on a Friday when his friend Tom calls him and invites him to go out clubbing that evening.
intention: John wants to respond to Tom's invitation.
moral_action: John accepts Tom's invitation and goes out clubbing with him that night.
moral_consequence: John has a great night out on the town and enjoys spending time with his friends.
immoral_action: John declines the invitation and stays home by himself on Friday night.
immoral_consequence: John feels bored and lonely at home and wishes he had gone out with his friends.

norm: It's wrong to mistreat people who have a disability.
situation: Enzo is walking to the local basketball court.
intention: Enzo wants to get to the court as soon as possible.
moral_action: Enzo takes a shortcut down an alley to get to the basketball court.
moral_consequence: Enzo arrives at the court quickly and joins the people playing ball.
immoral_action: Enzo pushes a man in a wheelchair out of his way and the man falls out of his wheelchair.
immoral_consequence: Enzo is arrested for injuring the man in wheelchair.

norm: It is bad to be disruptive during church.
situation: John is attending church with his family when his phone starts to vibrate.
intention: John wants to respond to the call.
moral_action: John declines the call and texts the caller that he will call back after the service.
moral_consequence: John is able to enjoy the rest of the service.
immoral_action: John answers the call and holds a hushed conversation with the caller.
immoral_consequence: John is asked to leave by an usher for disturbing fellow worshipers.

norm: It's good to tell someone they are doing something inappropriate.
situation: Louisa takes her daughter to the grocery store, and her daughter starts to throw a tantrum when Louisa wouldn't buy her candy.
intention: Louisa wants to finish shopping.
moral_action: Louisa quickly purchases her groceries, quietly takes her daughter to the side, tells her to calm down, and encourages her to talk rather than throwing a tantrum.
moral_consequence: Louisa's daughter learns what she did was wrong and learns how to communicate better.
immoral_action: Louisa gives in to her daughter's tantrums and buys her the candy, so she can shop in peace.
immoral_consequence: Louisa daughter gets a habit of throwing tantrums to get what she wants.

norm: It is bad to deceive your significant other
situation: Jane and her boyfriend Bob are chatting on the phone on a Friday night, and she asks him what his plans are for the evening.
intention: Bob wants to respond to Jane's question.
moral_action: Bob tells Jane that he's made plans to go out to the bar with his friends.
moral_consequence: Jane tells Bob to have a nice time and to give her a call if he needs a ride home.
immoral_action: Bob tells Jane that he's just staying home and taking it easy, despite his plans to go out later.
immoral_consequence: Jane pops over to Bob's apartment to surprise him, only to find out that he lied to her.

norm: It's rude to cancel your wedding venue on short notice.
situation: Beatrice scheduled a wedding at her chosen venue a year ago, and recently a pandemic started and a lot of people are cancelling their weddings.
intention: Beatrice wants to get married without contributing to the spread of the pandemic.
moral_action: Beatrice gets married at the venue after ensuring that everyone will wear masks and social distance.
moral_consequence: Beatrice enjoys her large wedding, but two of her friends who attend get very sick due to the pandemic.
immoral_action: Beatrice cancels her wedding venue weeks before the wedding and chooses to have a very small wedding instead.
immoral_consequence: Beatrice loses her deposit with the venue and does not get to have the wedding of her dreams, but does get married without anyone getting sick.

norm: It's terrible to destroy books.
situation: Kyle is at his house reading a book that he checked out from the library.
intention: Kyle wants to show his friend a page in the book.
moral_action: Kyle puts a bookmark in the book and brings it over to his friend's house.
moral_consequence: Kyle is happy to show his friend the page in the book.
immoral_action: Kyle tears the page out of the book, so he can show his friend.
immoral_consequence: Kyle has to pay a fee to the librarian for damaging the book.

norm: It is rude to judge people negatively for their appearance
situation: Bill is conducting open interviews for internships, for his company, and he is picking people out of a waiting room to talk with.
intention: Bill wants to pick the best candidate out of the people in the lobby.
moral_action: Bill requests applicants to interview based on time of arrival, and talks to as many people as he has time for.
moral_consequence: Bill finds the candidate he wants to work with early in the process, because the most eager people are the ones who showed up as early as they could.
immoral_action: Bill disregards people in the lobby if they are not physically attractive, because he feels that it is a sign of good breeding to look good.
immoral_consequence: Bill misses the opportunity to talk with the best candidate to work with, and Bill has since regretted the hiring decision that he made.

norm: You shouldn't always rely on luck for things.
situation: Brandy is barely able to pay her bills.
intention: Brandy needs to earn more money.
moral_action: Brandy uses her qualifications and experience to get a better job.
moral_consequence: Brandy is able to pay all her bills on time.
immoral_action: Brandy spends money on lottery tickets hoping she is lucky enough to win.
immoral_consequence: Brandy doesn't win and cannot pay bills.

norm: It's wrong to wear dirty undergarments.
situation: Charlie is getting dressed before he goes to work in the morning.
intention: Charlie wants to put on underwear.
moral_action: Charlie puts on a clean pair of underwear from the drawer in his dresser.
moral_consequence: Charlie feels fresh and clean throughout the whole work day.
immoral_action: Charlie puts on the same underwear that he wore for two nights in a row.
immoral_consequence: Charlie is called into human resources after people start to complain about Charlie's personal hygiene.

norm: It is not okay to be lazy in life.
situation: Evan loses his job and lives with his parents.
intention: Evan wants to enjoy life and be happy.
moral_action: Evan goes back to school and applies for a good job.
moral_consequence: Evan will move up in life and his parents will be proud of him.
immoral_action: Evan gets on unemployment and plays video games all day and asks his parents for stuff.
immoral_consequence: Evan will always be poor and his parents will resent him.

norm: It is bad to ambush or corner people
situation: Fred has a crush on his coworker Thelma.
intention: Fred wants to ask Thelma out.
moral_action: Fred asks Thelma to join him for lunch and while they are eating he asks her out on a date.
moral_consequence: Fred gets to go out on a properdate with his crush.
immoral_action: Fred waits by Thelma's car after work and won't let her leave until she agrees to go out with him.
immoral_consequence: Fred is fired after Thelma reports him for sexual harassment.

norm: It's good to apologize when you hurt your best friends.
situation: Leon got into a heated exchange over politics with his best friend and used some hurtful words.
intention: Leon wants to get past the argument.
moral_action: Leon approaches his friend and acknowledges the error of his ways.
moral_consequence: Leon's best friend is able to accept his apology and it doesn't linger in her mind.
immoral_action: Leon casually contacts his best friend and acts like nothing happened.
immoral_consequence: Leon's best friend goes along with it but his words stick to her deep down.

norm: It's immoral to cheat on your partner.
situation: Devin met a new female coworker at work who reminds him of his fiance.
intention: Devin wants to learn more about his coworker.
moral_action: Devin invites his coworker over to his house to spend time with him and his fiance.
moral_consequence: Devin and his fiance become friends with the new girl at work.
immoral_action: Devin asks his new coworker out to have dinner on a date.
immoral_consequence: Devin's fiance finds out about his dinner date and breaks off his engagement.

norm: You shouldn't give up on your goals.
situation: Ali is in university for undergraduate studies and dreams of becoming a top flight attorney.
intention: Ali wants to apply to law school.
moral_action: Ali applies to top tier law schools.
moral_consequence: Ali's job prospects are broad and give her many prestigious options.
immoral_action: Ali applies to low tier law schools.
immoral_consequence: Ali's job prospects narrow down and the chance of her becoming top flight diminish.

norm: You should do chores right away.
situation: Len is having people over to his home for a movie night.
intention: Len wants to straighten up his home.
moral_action: Len pulls out the vacuum and tidies up his home.
moral_consequence: Len is complemented by his friends on his tidy home.
immoral_action: Len decides to go for walk before cleaning the house.
immoral_consequence: Len is embarrassed at the state of his home when his friends show up earlier than he expected.

norm: It is unethical to accept sexual favors for rent.
situation: One of Carl's tenants offers to sleep with him in exchange for a free month of rent, since she is short on funds.
intention: Carl wants to help his tenant.
moral_action: Carl turns down the proposition, but still reassures his tenant that she can pay the rent late.
moral_consequence: Carl's tenant feels relieved that she doesn't have to worry about rent or compromise her morals.
immoral_action: Carl accepts the sexual proposition and sleeps with his tenant.
immoral_consequence: Carl's tenant feels like she has violated her moral code.

norm: It's nice to support your siblings decisions in life.
situation: John's brother decides to take a risk to start his own business.
intention: John wants to talk to his brother about the decision.
moral_action: John praises his brother for starting a business and offers to help.
moral_consequence: John and his brother becomes successful, wealthy and closer to each other.
immoral_action: John berates his brother for taking the risk to start a business.
immoral_consequence: His brother becomes successful and cuts off contact with John.

norm: You shouldn't train your neighbor's dog to shut up.
situation: Matt moves into a new house and his neighbor has a very loud dog.
intention: Matt wants his neighbor's dog to be quiet, so he can sleep.
moral_action: Matt rings his neighbor's doorbell and asks for the dog to be quiet, so he can sleep.
moral_consequence: Matt's neighbor gives the dog food so the dog stops barking, and Matt gets to sleep peacefully.
immoral_action: Matt goes outside and yells at his neighbor's dog to be quiet.
immoral_consequence: Matt's neighbor gets mad at him for yelling at the dog and it is very awkward when they see each other.

norm: It's wrong to misuse charitable donations.
situation: Dahlia, the owner of a charity, can't afford to pay her rent.
intention: Dahlia wants to settle her debts.
moral_action: Dahlia works out a payment plan with her manager that she can afford.
moral_consequence: This arrangement allows Dahlia to easily pay her bills for the rest of the year.
immoral_action: Dahlia pays her rent from the extra money in her charity.
immoral_consequence: Dahlia loses her position when the other workers discover her actions.

norm: It's wrong to leave your job without notifying anyone.
situation: Karen and Trish own a bakery together where Karen fulfills online orders, but she needs to pick up her daughter from school.
intention: Karen wants to leave to pick up her child.
moral_action: Karen tells Trish that she's leaving to pick up her child and will be back in a few hours.
moral_consequence: Trish monitors the online orders while Karen is away and prepares a very large order for an important client.
immoral_action: Karen gets her things together and leaves the bakery without telling Trish that she's going.
immoral_consequence: Trish doesn't check the online orders and an important customer shows up for a very large online order that isn't prepared.

norm: You shouldn't upset someone's pet.
situation: Suzie is visiting her aunt, who owns a cat.
intention: Suzie wants to pet the cat.
moral_action: Suzie waits for the cat to come over to her before petting it.
moral_consequence: The cat is calm and purrs at her.
immoral_action: Suzie immediately runs over to the cat to grab and pet it.
immoral_consequence: The cat is startled and scratches her after being let go.

norm: It is mean to get children suspended and expelled.
situation: Niles pulls the fire alarm one day while walking to class in school.
intention: Niles wants to get out of trouble.
moral_action: Niles says nothing and no one else saw him pull the alarm.
moral_consequence: With no evidence, the school cannot lay blame on a student.
immoral_action: Niles claims the school bully was the one who pulled the alarm.
immoral_consequence: Due to his already spotty record, the bully is expelled from the school.

norm: It's rude to show someone your middle finger.
situation: A driver cuts Jon off while he's on the road and almost hits him.
intention: Jon wants to show the driver he's annoyed.
moral_action: Jon honks the horn loud behind the person who cut him off.
moral_consequence: Jon feels satisfied when the other driver speeds up to avoid him.
immoral_action: Jon gives the other driver the middle finger as he's passing him.
immoral_consequence: Jon isn't paying attention and slams into a car in front of him.

norm: You should accept responsibility for breaking something.
situation: Carol and her friend Sharon like to do things together on the weekend.
intention: Carol wants Sharon to go shopping with her.
moral_action: While they are shopping Carol breaks a glass ornament, so she takes it to the sales clerk and offers to pay for it.
moral_consequence: Sharon tells Carol that she did the right thing, that's what she would do herself.
immoral_action: Carol breaks a glass ornament while they are shopping, but sets it back on the shelf without telling a sales clerk.
immoral_consequence: Sharon insists Carol let someone know what happened,  and says she's being irresponsible,.

norm: It's good to purchase things that you enjoy
situation: Allison has been bored lately and is interested in learning an instrument.
intention: Allison wants to buy music equipment.
moral_action: Allison decides on a guitar, which is her favorite instrument, and places the order.
moral_consequence: Allison is in love with the sound and has motivation to practice daily.
immoral_action: Allison see's a deal on a banjo, which isn't her favorite instrument, but she buys it regardless.
immoral_consequence: Allison hates the way it sounds and isn't motivated to learn.

norm: It's bad to leave your spouse alone in a disaster.
situation: Billy and Lia are preparing for a possible tsunami.
intention: Billy wants to stay as safe as possible.
moral_action: Billy helps Lia pack quickly, and they both exit the area in their car.
moral_consequence: Billy and Lia evacuate the area and are safe from harm.
immoral_action: Billy feels like Lia is going too slowly and drives away in the car without her.
immoral_consequence: Lia is trapped in the house during the tsunami and suffers terrible injuries, blaming Billy and considering him a coward.

norm: It's rude to point out embarrassing things about someone.
situation: Henry is at work when Jane walks and says hello with chocolate stains on her teeth.
intention: Henry wants to tell Jane she has a stain on her teeth.
moral_action: Henry motions for Jane to come close and whispers that she might want to check her teeth in the bathroom.
moral_consequence: Jane is thankful that Henry saved her from embarrassing herself in front of the other coworkers.
immoral_action: Henry loudly points at Jane and while laughing, tells her she looks ridiculous with her teeth all stained.
immoral_consequence: Jane is embarrassed and begins to cry and runs to the bathroom.

norm: It's wrong to be too dependent on your partner.
situation: Brianna is eating dinner with her parents, and her girlfriend Sarah is feeling sad over the loss of her job.
intention: Sarah wants comfort to lessen her depression.
moral_action: Sarah decides to hang out with some of her other friends for the evening.
moral_consequence: Brianna enjoys time with her family while Sarah gets some form of emotional support.
immoral_action: Sarah calls and texts Brianna multiple times through the night demanding attention.
immoral_consequence: Brianna is unable to enjoy time with her parents, and Sarah doesn't get the full attention she craves.

norm: It's rude to only think about yourself in a community.
situation: Scott is asymptomatic and has covid-19 but does not know it.
intention: Scott wants to go to the store.
moral_action: Scott wears a mask because he cares about people in his community.
moral_consequence: No one else gets sick.
immoral_action: Scott refuses to wear a mask because it's uncomfortable.
immoral_consequence: Scott infects several people at the store.

norm: It's bad to grope someone.
situation: Ray sees a woman that he is attracted to on the bus.
intention: Ray wants to get the woman's attention.
moral_action: Ray introduces himself to the woman and strikes up a conversation.
moral_consequence: The woman has a friendly conversation with Ray and gives him her number.
immoral_action: Ray grabs the woman on her butt and introduces himself to her.
immoral_consequence: The woman slaps Ray in the face and reports him to the authorities.

norm: It's good to inform your neighbor's of bad behavior.
situation: Jeff's neighbors kept throwing their trash in the yard instead of in the garbage bin.
intention: Jeff doesn't want the trash in the yard.
moral_action: Jeff talks to his neighbor about putting away his trash properly.
moral_consequence: Jeff's neighbor begins to throw all his garbage in the trash bin.
immoral_action: Jeff takes all the garbage and leaves it on his neighbor's front step.
immoral_consequence: Jeff's neighbor gets mad and gets in a fight with him.

norm: You shouldn't urinate outside of a toilet.
situation: Joe was visiting a friend's house and had been drinking a few beers.
intention: Joe wanted to use the restroom.

intention: Pam wants to make sure there is something for the vegetarian to eat.
moral_action: Pam takes the time to put together a few dishes that are specifically for the vegetarian.
moral_consequence: Pam is relieved to be able to cater to all her guests.
immoral_action: Pam decides to tell the vegetarian that the vegetable dishes are vegetarian, when they were made with meat sauces.
immoral_consequence: Pam is mortified when a piece of meat is discovered in the supposedly vegetarian dish.

norm: It's good to support your country.
situation: Jen is American and attending a live hockey game between Americans and Germans.
intention: Jen wants to cheer on the game.
moral_action: Jen cheers for her American team whenever they  perform well.
moral_consequence: Jen finds friends amongst the audience and has a good time.
immoral_action: Jen cheers for the German team every time they score a goal.
immoral_consequence: The audience around Jen scold Jen, and Jen feels upset.

norm: It is rude to disrupt someone's belongings without permission.
situation: Sally asks John to watch her bag while she runs to the bathroom.
intention: John wants to use some lip balm on his chapped lips.
moral_action: John waits for Sally to get back from the bathroom and asks if she has lip balm.
moral_consequence: John and Sally maintain a good, mutually-respectful relationship.
immoral_action: John goes through Sally's bag to look for lip balm.
immoral_consequence: John damages his relationship with Sally because she feels violated.

norm: It is hurtful to distance yourself from your family.
situation: Mary had an argument with her parents after telling them about her intention to drop out of college.
intention: Mary wants to be independent and make her own decisions.

moral_consequence: Mary's parents understand Mary's reasons and intentions and are proud that their daughter wants to take her life into her own hands.
immoral_action: Mary cuts off all ties with her parents and shuts off their attempts to contact her.
immoral_consequence: Mary's parents are extremely hurt and very worried about their daughter.

norm: It's wrong to spend so much time online.
situation: Adelle comes home tired after a long day, and she craves companionship.
intention: Adelle wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Adelle invites some of her friends over to watch movies.

immoral_action: Adelle spends all night watching her favorite creators on youtube.

norm: It's indefensible to mess with someone's beverage.

norm: It's good to show pride in your Alma Mater.
situation: Dominick is opening his mail and one item is a solicitation for donations from his Alma Mater.

moral_consequence: Thanks to donations Dominick's Alma Mater is able to provide quality education to more students which makes Dominick feel satisfaction.

norm: It's bad to not care about yourself.

norm: It's good to get a higher education.

moral_consequence: Bob and Judy are busy that day, but they will meet up in one week when Paul passes through town again.

immoral_consequence: Bob and Judy are upset at the awkward situation and ask Bon to leave.

norm: It's rude to be snooping on other people's personal lives.
situation: Callie is sitting in a diner when she overhears a couple having a heated discussion.
intention: Callie wants to eat her lunch.
moral_action: Callie takes her food and moves to another table to give the couple privacy.
moral_consequence: The couple is able to continue their conversation without anyone hearing them.
immoral_action: Callie stays at her table, so she can hear what the couple is talking about.
immoral_consequence: The couple notices that Callie is eavesdropping and starts to glare at her.

norm: It's bad to make people feel unsafe.
situation: Jason is bored and decides to prank one of his friends.
intention: Jason wants to have fun.
moral_action: Jason waits in a bush for his friend on a hot day, squirting him with a water gun.
moral_consequence: Jason's friend laughs and grabs another water gun as they proceed to have a water gun fight.
immoral_action: Jason tells his friend as they are driving that the car has no brakes, and they will crash.
immoral_consequence: Jason's friend freaks out and is angry with Jason for giving him a panic attack.

norm: It's wrong to leave someone with out a home.
situation: Kurt's family gets a request from Kurt for a place to stay after he is evicted from his apartment after not being able to pay rent.
intention: Kurt wants to find a place to live.
moral_action: An uncle of kurt's has a garage house that he lets Kurt use until he is on his feet.
moral_consequence: Kurt is able to find a job and pays his uncle back rent as a gesture of thanks.
immoral_action: Kurt's family ignores the request telling him that it is hsi responsibility to find his own place.
immoral_consequence: Kurt becomes homeless and finds himself still on the streets years later.

norm: You should help someone that is having trouble lifting something.
situation: Ben and June are in the process of moving to a new apartment and Ben is struggling with his guitar amp while June is carrying some folders.
intention: June wants to make a decision.
moral_action: June tells Ben to wait until she puts the folders away and grabs a dolly.
moral_consequence: Ben gets his amplifier in safely and avoids any discomfort.
immoral_action: June let's Ben handle the amplifier because she wants to get her folders put away.
immoral_consequence: Ben ends up throwing his back out and has to go to the hospital.

norm: It is wrong to drug someone's drink.
situation: Peter told Carl he had not yet had sex with his new girlfriend, Tammy, so Carl gave Peter a powder to put in her drink to make her “willing”.
intention: Peter wants Tammy to say yes to sex.
moral_action: Peter throws away the powder and talks to Tammy about sex, she says yes after they talk through a few things.
moral_consequence: Peter and Tammy are able to have a satisfying sex life.
immoral_action: Peter makes Tammy a drink with powder in it , she becomes  affectionate and tell's Peter she wants him.
immoral_consequence: Tammy has a bad and lasting reaction to the drugand Peter blames himself.

norm: It's horrible to tell your parents that you hate them.
situation: Patty is getting married to her girlfriend in a week.
intention: Patty wants to have her parents at her wedding.
moral_action: Patty knows her parents don't approve of her marriage but thanks them for coming to the wedding.
moral_consequence: Patty's parents see that Patty is happy and enjoy the rest of the day together.
immoral_action: Patty know her parents don't approve of her marriage so at her wedding she tells her parents that she hates them in anger.
immoral_consequence: Patty's parents leave the wedding and go home they don't speak to Patty for a year.

norm: You shouldn't pry into your partner's things.
situation: Ivy notices that her husband seems more stressed than normal after work, and she stumbles across his unlocked laptop.
intention: Ivy wants to know more about her husband.
moral_action: Ivy gives her husband a hug and asks him what's been bothering him.
moral_consequence: Ivy's gesture of affection makes her husband feel safe enough to open up about his problems.
immoral_action: Ivy reads her husbands emails and Facebook messages from his coworkers.
immoral_consequence: Ivy's husband yells at her when he discovers her reading his things.

norm: It's not good to disrupt people with loud music.
situation: Andrew plays music nightly in his apartment when his neighbor james is sleeping.
intention: Andrew wants to enjoy music and unwind after work.
moral_action: Andrew gets a request from James to turn it down and buys headphones to listen.
moral_consequence: Andrew and James have no issues and get along as neighbors.
immoral_action: Andrew blasts the music well past midnight and ignores James request to turn it down.
immoral_consequence: Andrews apartment gives him multiple warnings and eventually evicts him.

norm: It is rude to be ungrateful of someone's kind gesture
situation: Pauline's friend Kathy just gifted her some cookies she made and Pauline takes a bite.
intention: Pauline wants to give her opinion on the cookies.
moral_action: Pauline doesn't like the cookies, but she tells Kathy they taste great and thanks her.
moral_consequence: Kathy feels good about herself and continues to improve at baking.
immoral_action: Pauline tells Kathy that they taste terrible and spits out the bite she took.
immoral_consequence: Kathy's feelings are hurt and now she thinks she's a terrible baker.

norm: Being careful shows initiative for the environment around you.
situation: John is driving down the road and just finished drinking a soda.
intention: John wants to get rid of the empty soda can.
moral_action: John pulls over on the side of the road and carefully throws the soda in the recycling bin.
moral_consequence: John keeps his neighborhood nice and clean and contributes to a healthy environment.
immoral_action: John thoughtlessly throws the soda can out the window as he continues driving.
immoral_consequence: The soda can adds to the litter on the street and makes John's neighborhood more trashy and ugly.

norm: You should not express your rage on the road.
situation: Jason is driving on the highway and a car cuts him off.
intention: Jason wants to let out frustration.
moral_action: Jason mutters under his breath.
moral_consequence: Jason lets off steam without endangering others.
immoral_action: Jason pulls up next to the car and flips it off.
immoral_consequence: Both Jason and the driver of the car are angry and act in dangerous ways.

norm: You shouldn't pull pranks on people.
situation: Tony is visiting a friend and feels bored one afternoon while his friend is out buying something to eat.
intention: Tony wants to put some excitement in his life.
moral_action: Tony turns on one of his friend's movies really loud and acts it out while in the living room.
moral_consequence: Tony's friend comes home, sees what Tony is doing, and joins Tony in acting out the film.
immoral_action: Tony gets some wires and hooks up the front door knob to the house's 110V AC current.
immoral_consequence: Tony's friend comes home, grabs the doorknob, and shakes uncontrollably, dropping the food and injuring him.

norm: It's not okay to invade someone's personal space.
situation: Ricky's friend Hal has a new phone.
intention: Ricky wants to see the phone.
moral_action: Ricky asks Hal if he can get a closer look at the phone.
moral_consequence: Hal gives the phone to Ricky.
immoral_action: Ricky gets really close Hal while he's holding the phone.
immoral_consequence: Hal tells Ricky to go away.

norm: Children should not lie to their parents.
situation: Emma broke her mother's vase while playing near the new puppy.
intention: Emma wants to tell her mother about the vase.
moral_action: Emma tells her mother that she broke the vase and is very sorry.
moral_consequence: Emma's mother accepts her apology and asks her to help with chores to make up for it.
immoral_action: Emma tells her mother that the puppy broke the vase, not her.
immoral_consequence: Emma's mother puts the puppy on time out for breaking something and the puppy becomes confused about the house rules.

norm: You should always go to important family events.
situation: Cathy has tickets to see a movie at the same time as her brother Mike's 10th birthday party.
intention: Cathy wants to see the movie.
moral_action: Cathy exchanges her tickets for a different showtime and goes to the party.
moral_consequence: Mike is glad that he can spend time with Cathy on his birthday.
immoral_action: Cathy goes to the movie instead of going to the party.
immoral_consequence: Mike is devastated that his older sister couldn't be at his party.

norm: You shouldn't sleep over at a significant other's friend's house.
situation: Sarah's husband Jay is away on a business trip, and she needs someone to help her study her flashcards for an upcoming nurses exam.
intention: Sarah wants Jay's friend, Tom, to help her study.
moral_action: Sarah asks Tom if he can come over the next morning to help her study.
moral_consequence: Sarah and Tom study over breakfast before Tom has to leave for work.
immoral_action: Sarah goes over to Tom's late in the evening to study, when he suggests that she stay over.
immoral_consequence: One thing leads to another and Sarah and Tom end up sleeping together.

norm: Partners are not expected to have secrets from one another.
situation: Kelly has a shopping addiction and one of her friends just invited her to go to the mall.
intention: Kelly wants a new pair of shoes.
moral_action: Kelly calls her husband to ask if she can buy a pair of new shoes at the mall, and he agrees if they're under 100 dollars.
moral_consequence: Kelly buys the shoes and her husband is okay with the purchase.
immoral_action: Kelly purchases an expensive pair of new shoes using a credit card that she keeps hidden from her husband.
immoral_consequence: Kelly racks up debt and ends up ruining her credit score and preventing her family from buying a house.

norm: It's intolerant to harsh another's buzz by being a killjoy.
situation: John has just been accepted for his dream job, but John's older friend Ryan knows that getting the job is only the beginning.
intention: Ryan wants John to know that there is still more work ahead.
moral_action: Ryan tells John he did great, and lets John celebrate for the day before reminding him about the work he needs to do.
moral_consequence: John sees Ryan as a level-headed friend who gives good advice.
immoral_action: Ryan doesn't offer any congratulations, only telling John that he still has a lot of work to do to keep the job.
immoral_consequence: John doesn't celebrate with Ryan anymore, and stops telling Ryan about his life.

norm: It's bad to take advantage of your parents' generosity.
situation: Laurel's parents agreed to let her use their credit card to shop for some new school supplies.
intention: Laurel wants to buy a new cell phone in addition to her basic school supplies.
moral_action: Laurel buys the school supplies with the credit card and puts the cell phone on her own debit card instead.
moral_consequence: Laurel's parents trust her more in the future.
immoral_action: Laurel uses her parents' credit card to purchase the new cell phone she wanted in addition to the school supplies.
immoral_consequence: Laurel gets scolded by her parents for buying the cell phone without asking first.

norm: You shouldn't tell lies to get ahead in life.
situation: Jim is preparing to submit his application to a high paying position which is expected to get hundreds of applications.
intention: Jim wants to stand out from the rest of the applicants.
moral_action: Jim is honest on his resume but spends extra time preparing for the interview.
moral_consequence: Jim gets the job because of how well the interview went.
immoral_action: Jim adds fictitious experience to his resume, to make it seem like he is the perfect fit.
immoral_consequence: During the interview it's clear that Jim doesn't have as much experience as he claimed, and he doesn't get the job.

norm: It's good to make food for your kids.
situation: Colby just got home from school feeling hungry and tired, and his mom Stephanie is working on her laptop.
intention: Stephanie wants Colby to eat something.
moral_action: Stephanie closes her laptop and makes Colby a steak, with salad, and potatoes.
moral_consequence: Colby feels great after eating a balanced meal and goes out to play.
immoral_action: Stephanie tells Colby to stick a frozen meal in the microwave, and she continues working.
immoral_consequence: Colby doesn't get the proper nutrition he needs and feels sluggish after eating.

norm: It's good to ask others for support.
situation: John is working on an essay for his English class and struggling to complete it.
intention: John wants to finish writing the essay.
moral_action: John asks his mother for help with writing his essay.
moral_consequence: John's mother helps him, and he ends up getting an A on his essay.
immoral_action: John perseveres in writing the essay himself without any help despite his struggles with it.
immoral_consequence: John's essay doesn't turn out very well, and he gets a D on it.

norm: You shouldn't give money to people for gifts.
situation: Clara will be attending her friend Taylor's birthday party but has been struggling to find her a gift.
intention: Clara wants to find a gift quickly.
moral_action: Clara calls up her friend group and asks what they intend to gift Taylor.
moral_consequence: Clara gets ideas from her friend group and is able to gift Taylor something that is thoughful.
immoral_action: Overwhelmed by gift shopping, Clara decides to gift Taylor with cash.
immoral_consequence: Taylor feels that Clara put little thought into her gift.

norm: It's rude to be too noisy early in the morning.
situation: Billy lives in an apartment with three roommates.
intention: Billy wants to become a more productive person.
moral_action: Billy gets up early and goes to a local coffee shop with his laptop to start working early.
moral_consequence: Billy is a top performer at his job and his roommates envy him.
immoral_action: Billy wakes up early, makes himself coffee, and listens to music while planning for the day.
immoral_consequence: Billy's roommates are woken up by the music, and they are angry at Billy.

norm: You should always be there for your child's birthday party.
situation: Dennis' wife is throwing a birthday party for their son, Brayden, on the same day as an important work meeting.
intention: Dennis wants to tend to his work meeting.
moral_action: Dennis schedules the meeting for earlier in the day so that he can attend Brayden's party.
moral_consequence: Dennis' meeting concludes early enough that he is even able to help with Brayden's party setup.
immoral_action: Dennis attends his meeting, missing nearly all of Brayden's party.
immoral_consequence: Brayden feels let down by his dad and is unable to enjoy the party.

norm: It's good to be caring and protective of animals.
situation: Ben's saw his cat limping around.
intention: Ben wants to see what is wrong with his cat.
moral_action: Ben sees his cat's injured leg and takes his cat to a vet.
moral_consequence: Ben's cat heals up and shows Ben some affection later on.
immoral_action: Ben realizes his cat injured his leg but decides to not care about it.
immoral_consequence: Ben's cat develops an infection and dies leaving Ben alone.

norm: It's wrong to destroy a family.
situation: Bill works in an office with a lot of hot young interns and his wife.
intention: Bill wants to be sexually satisfied.
moral_action: Bill has sex with his wife when they get home from work.
moral_consequence: Bill and his wife spend many years together as husband and wife.
immoral_action: Bill invites an intern into his office and has sex with her.
immoral_consequence: Bill is divorced by his wife when she hears about his affair with the intern.

norm: It's bad to hide transmittable diseases from your significant other.
situation: Jose started an account on a gay dating app to meet somebody even though he is HIV positive.
intention: Jose wanted to have sex.
moral_action: Jose puts that he is HIV positive in his profile so that other men will know.
moral_consequence: A man who is interested in Jose sees that he has an STD, so he makes sure that he's protected before having sex.
immoral_action: Jose finds a man that is wiling to have sex with him, but Jose doesn't tell him that he has HIV.
immoral_consequence: The man ends up getting HIV, and it ends up turning into AIDS.

norm: It is good to stay in school
situation: Josh is a senior in high school who has been enjoying senior activities.
intention: Josh wants to have a fun senior year.
moral_action: Josh continues to do his schoolwork and go to school every day.
moral_consequence: Josh makes lots of lasting high school memories in his final year.
immoral_action: Josh decides to take a week off from school to rent a beach house with friends.
immoral_consequence: Josh and his friends are suspended for missing so much school and aren't able to graduate.

norm: It is wrong to shirk your work duties.
situation: Tim has been given the responsibility of doing some paperwork at his job before he leaves.
intention: Tim wants to go to the bar.
moral_action: Tim finishes all his assigned paperwork although he has to stay at work late then he heads to the bar for a bit.
moral_consequence: Tim's boss is pleased with Tim's performance and gives Tim a promotion.
immoral_action: Tim leaves work early without finishing his paperwork and goes straight to the bar.
immoral_consequence: Tim's boss is angry that Tim for not getting the paperwork done and issues Tim a formal employee warning.

norm: It is wrong not to have morals.
situation: Ken has a lot of plastic bottles in his house that are taking up space.
intention: Ken wants to dispose of the plastic bottles.
moral_action: Ken takes the plastic bottles to a recycling center.
moral_consequence: Ken helps out the environment by recycling.
immoral_action: Ken dumps the plastic bottles in a river in town.
immoral_consequence: Ken pollutes the river with his bottles.

norm: Its unpleasant to disapprove of another friends relationship.
situation: Jenna was raised in a very conservative home and taught that all LGBT people deserved to burn in hell, and she just found out her best friend is gay.
intention: Jenna wants to reconcile her upbringing with the fact she knows her friend is a good person.
moral_action: Jenna decides that her parents were wrong and gay people aren't very different from anyone else.
moral_consequence: Jenna and her friend become even closer and Jenna is eventually the friend's maid of honor.
immoral_action: Jenna decides that her friend is just going through a rebellious phase and isn't really gay.
immoral_consequence: Jenna constantly says offensive things about LGBT people in front of her friend, eventually ending the friendship.

norm: It is good to trust someone in a relationship.
situation: Mary's boyfriend John is part of a big project at work and has taken to sometimes pulling all-nighters.
intention: Mary wants to feel secure in her relationship.
moral_action: Mary is honest with John about her insecurities.
moral_consequence: Mary is better able to handle the temporary distance after John adjusts his schedule to give her more attention.
immoral_action: Mary follows John and confronts him when he goes for a meal with coworkers after work.
immoral_consequence: After embarrassing John in front of his coworkers Mary and John grow further apart.

norm: It's wrong to put your hand under a stranger's clothes.
situation: Mary is sitting next to a sleeping stranger on the subway.
intention: Mary wants to see the stranger's tattoo that's hidden by clothing.
moral_action: Mary asks to see the tattoo when the stranger awakes.
moral_consequence: The stranger feels respected and allows Mary to see more of her work.
immoral_action: Mary lifts the stranger's skirt to see the tattoo.
immoral_consequence: Mary is caught and the stranger becomes upset with her.

norm: It is bad not to help others in need
situation: Charles, who is a wealthy man, passes by a homeless man on the street asking for money.
intention: Charles wants to respond to the homeless man.
moral_action: Charles buys the man dinner and takes him to a homeless shelter.
moral_consequence: The homeless man is fed and has somewhere to sleep.
immoral_action: Charles tells the man to quit being lazy and get a job.
immoral_consequence: The homeless man remains hungry and homeless.

norm: It's good to visit new places.
situation: Igor is on vacation from work which he has been looking forward to for a long time.
intention: Igor wants to enjoy his vacation time.
moral_action: Igor decides to travel during his vacation to see parts of his country he had only read about.
moral_consequence: Igor gets new perspectives and makes good memories during his travels.
immoral_action: Igor decides to stay inside watching movies and eating badly all vacation to relax.
immoral_consequence: Igor's vacation is over before he knows it, and he is left feeling like he didn't do anything worthwhile.

norm: It's wrong to defecate in bed.
situation: Tim goes out to the local bar and gets completely hammered.
intention: Tim wants to sleep off his drunkeness.
moral_action: Tim goes into his bathroom to rest in case he feels sick for drinking too much.
moral_consequence: Tim is able to use the bathroom when he needs to and get some rest.
immoral_action: Tim passes out in his bed and loses control of his bowels from being too drunk.
immoral_consequence: Tim has to buy a new mattress and sheets because they are ruined.

norm: it is good to be faithful
situation: Tommy has been working at his current job for twelve years.
intention: Tommy wants to work more hours.
moral_action: Tommy asks his boss if he can pick up more hours at work.
moral_consequence: Tommy gets a raise when his boss sees how much initiative he is taking.
immoral_action: Tommy leaves his job and works more hours at a new job.
immoral_consequence: The new job pays less and Tommy ends up making less money than before.

norm: It's good to be humble when you win a competition.
situation: Rory just won a marathon, and his friends are asking how he did.
intention: Rory wants to tell his friends that he won the marathon.
moral_action: Rory tells his friends that he won the race, but it was a close one.
moral_consequence: Rory's friends think that he is tough and are proud of him.
immoral_action: Rory tells his friends that he was so much better than the other runners.
immoral_consequence: Rory's friends think that he's arrogant and like him less.

norm: Is wrong to think negatively about yourself
situation: Lily is at that age where she is seeing every flaw in the mirror.
intention: Lily wants to change what she thinks is wrong with her.
moral_action: Lily goes on a diet to lose weight responsibly.
moral_consequence: Lily loses weight and feels more confident in herself.
immoral_action: Lily starves herself to make herself look thinner.
immoral_consequence: Lily becomes an anorexic and loses a lot of nutrition from lack of eating.

norm: It's wrong to make other people feel bad.
situation: Kevin is at a party with friends.
intention: Kevin wants to entertain his friends.
moral_action: Kevin tells a story about one of his own embarrassing moments.
moral_consequence: Kevin's friends share a good laugh and the party continues smoothly.
immoral_action: Kevin tells a story about a friend's most embarrassing moment without their consent.
immoral_consequence: Kevin's friend leaves the party and refuses to speak with him.

norm: It's bad form to go through your parent's drawers.
situation: Ted asked his parents for money to go on a trip, but they didn't help him.
intention: Ted wanted money to go on his trip.
moral_action: Ted goes to a rich neighborhood and offers to cut their lawn for money.
moral_consequence: Ted's parents are proud that Ted worked for his money instead of begging.
immoral_action: Ted opens his dad's money drawer and takes out the amount of money he needs.
immoral_consequence: Ted's parents finds out and have to come up with a harsh punishment for Ted.

norm: It is dangerous to drive while you're drowsy
situation: Amy didn't get enough sleep last night, and she is very tired, but her work shift has now ended.
intention: Amy wants to drive home from work.
moral_action: Amy finds a quiet spot and takes a nap for a few minutes.
moral_consequence: Amy drives home alert and makes it home safely.
immoral_action: Amy gets in her car and drives home right after work.
immoral_consequence: Amy falls asleep at the wheel and rear-ends a car.

norm: It is good to responsibly take care of fish.
situation: James won a goldfish as a prize in a carnival game.
intention: James wants his pet to be low maintenance.
moral_action: James finds a cheap tank on Craiglists, sets it up with a filter and plants and feeds his fish regularly.
moral_consequence: James often watches the fish when he gets home from work and wants to relax.
immoral_action: James leaves his goldfish in the small round bowl it came in.
immoral_consequence: James' goldfish rapidly dies from lack of space and clean water.

norm: You shouldn't pick out girly clothes for your son.
situation: Tina is spending some time at the mall and shopping with her son.
intention: Tina wants to buy her son new clothes.
moral_action: Tina gets her son new clothes that are marketed to young boys.
moral_consequence: Tina's son makes some new friends in school who like his clothes.
immoral_action: Tina buys her son a bunch of cute clothes that are clearly meant more for girls.
immoral_consequence: Tina's son is made fun of in school for the clothes his mom got him.

norm: Researching information for others can give you new insight yourself.
situation: Maxwell notices his classmate looking at some academic journals for her paper, and he is free for the afternoon/.
intention: Maxwell wants to do something productive.
moral_action: Maxwell searches through some academic journals to cut down on his classmate's research time.
moral_consequence: Maxwell learns information that helps him complete papers in the future.
immoral_action: Maxwell leaves his friend going home to organize all the books in his room.
immoral_consequence: Maxwell feels guilty when he finds out that his classmate couldn't turn in her paper on time.

norm: It's good to make other people laugh.
situation: Joe sees that his friend Harry is sulking in the corner.
intention: Joe wants to get his friend out of the corner.
moral_action: Joe tells Harry a knock knock joke.
moral_consequence: Harry laughs at the joke and stands up.
immoral_action: Joe tells Harry that it's time to stand up like an adult.
immoral_consequence: Harry sulks even more.

norm: It's wrong to make a friend cry.
situation: Tracy has been listening to her friend Fiona complain about her deadbeat boyfriend.
intention: Tracy wants to tell Fiona what she thinks about the relationship.
moral_action: Tracy tells Fiona that she can do better and that she deserves to be with a wonderful partner.
moral_consequence: Fiona fells empowered to break off her problematic relationship.
immoral_action: Tracy tells Fiona she is a loser because she keeps dating losers.
immoral_consequence: Fiona bursts into tears and refuses to confide in Tracy any more.

norm: It's bad to use other's things without their permission.
situation: Sarah needs a ride to her friend Julie's house, but the only car there is her boyfriend John's, and he's at work.
intention: Sarah wants to visit Julie.
moral_action: Sarah calls John at work to ask if she can borrow his vehicle.
moral_consequence: John appreciates that Sarah asked, and he tells her she can use it.
immoral_action: Sarah just takes John's car and drives to Julie's without asking.
immoral_consequence: John gets home from work and no longer trusts Sarah because his car is gone.

norm: You shouldn't brag about drinking a lot of beer.
situation: Micah, the winner of several drinking contests, is talking with his crush Lisa at a party, and Lisa is warming up to him.
intention: Micah wants to impress Lisa.
moral_action: Micah demonstrates his knowledge on several topics with a cheerful smile.
moral_consequence: Lisa invites Micah to dinner the next week because she wants to learn more about him.
immoral_action: Micah talks about winning several drinking contests in a loud tone while gesturing to the wine bottle on the table.
immoral_consequence: Lisa is embarrassed, and she excuses herself from the table.

norm: It's good to spend time alone and enjoy yourself.
situation: Greg just finished a big project at work and feels very stressed when his friends invite him out to celebrate.
intention: Greg wants to feel better.
moral_action: Greg declines and spends the evening at home alone.
moral_consequence: Greg gets some more sleep and works out some of the stress.
immoral_action: Greg goes out with friends but is too fried to interact with them much.
immoral_consequence: Greg's friends think Greg is stuck-up and ignore him.

norm: It's bad to date convicts.
situation: Trevor is at his computer looking for prospective romantic dates on various website.
intention: Trevor wants to go on a date.
moral_action: Trevor joins a reputable dating website and eventually has his first date with a retail worker he meets through the website.
moral_consequence: Trevor enjoys the first date and is hopeful that more dates will follow.
immoral_action: Trevor finds a website that teaches people how to contact prison inmates and decides to try to find a date that way.
immoral_consequence: Trevor is naive expectations are taken advantage of by the convict that he contacts for a date.

norm: It's bad to break dishes.
situation: Tom is going to be in the talent show at school and has to show off a talent.
intention: Tom wants to practice juggling.
moral_action: Tom practices his juggling outside with a group of oranges.
moral_consequence: Tom learns to juggle and does well in the talent show.
immoral_action: Tom uses his mother's good dishes to practice his juggling skills.
immoral_consequence: Tom drops some of the dishes and breaks them when they land on the floor.

norm: You shouldn't pirate software.
situation: Josh wants the new Sims game, and he can't afford it.
intention: Josh wants to play the game.
moral_action: Josh sells some of his things to get money to buy the game.
moral_consequence: Josh room is less cluttered because he got rid of things he didn't need.
immoral_action: Josh downloads the game off of a torrent website.
immoral_consequence: Josh's computer becomes infected with computer viruses.

norm: People are expected to be punctual.
situation: Al is almost running late for work, in his car in traffic.
intention: Al wants a quick pick-me-up to get him ready for the workday.
moral_action: Al arrives on time and gets coffee from the machine at work.
moral_consequence: All at the office are productive and proceed normally without interruption and efficiently.
immoral_action: Al stops for a specialty coffee drink at a restaurant.
immoral_consequence: Al is late for work, team members who depend on Al do not get work done, upsetting the team members' progress.

norm: You should be considerate of other people's problems.
situation: James needed his coworker to fill out some paperwork for him, but she recently had a miscarriage.
intention: James wants his paperwork filled out quickly.
moral_action: James asks his boss if he can reassign the paperwork to another coworker.
moral_consequence: James' boss agrees and the other coworker is able to finish the work in little time.
immoral_action: James tells his coworker that there's no excuse for idleness and it's not even like she lost a child.
immoral_consequence: James' boss tells his that if he ever says anything like that again, he'll be fired.

norm: It is rude to point out their weight problem constantly.
situation: Randy watches his overweight friend Marshall eats a big tub of ice cream.
intention: Randy wants Marshall to lose weight.
moral_action: Randy suggests that they go jogging after Marshall eats his ice cream.
moral_consequence: Marshall discovers that he enjoys jogging, and he starts jogging every morning.
immoral_action: Randy reminds Marshall about his appearance multiple times.
immoral_consequence: Marshall feels stressed and eats the entire tub of ice cream.

norm: You should not tell other people how to act
situation: Jake starts a new job at a coffee shop.
intention: Jake wants to be a good employee at his new job.
moral_action: Though Sally, Jake's coworker, dawdles on the job, Jake thanks her for being a good coworker.
moral_consequence: Sally enjoys working with Jake and tells her boss that Jake is a good coworker.
immoral_action: Jake mentions to his coworker, Sally, that they should be more focused when on the job.
immoral_consequence: Sally becomes annoyed with Jake and lodges a complaint with their boss.

norm: It's wrong to poop in public.
situation: Nancy is a homeless drunk wandering the streets of San Franciso.

moral_consequence: Nancy is able to relieve her bodily functions in a clear and appropriate place.
immoral_action: Nancy squats on the sidewalk and defecates on it, in front of several passers-by.

norm: It is wrong to drive over the speed limit.
situation: Ron is running late for work because he slept through his alarm.
intention: Ron wants to get to the office.
moral_action: Ron calls his boss and explains that he accidenatlly overslept and will be there soon.
moral_consequence: Ron's boss is displeased, but understands and Ron arrives at work safely.
immoral_action: Ron gets on the highway and goes 10 miles an hour above the speed limit to get to work on time.
immoral_consequence: Ron gets pulled over by the police and gets a ticket which makes him even more late.

norm: It's nice to win something for your sibling.
situation: April is playing a carnival game, and her young brother Steve is helping her out.
intention: April wants to win the game.
moral_action: April wins and lets Steve pick out the prize for himself.
moral_consequence: Steve feels grateful and helps his sister out in return.
immoral_action: April wins the game and selects a prize only for herself.
immoral_consequence: Steve is depressed because he can't get a prize like April.

norm: You should keep your hands to yourself.
situation: James has a long, boring commute on the subway every weekday.
intention: James wants to entertain himself during his commute.

norm: You should not eat raw meat.
situation: Bill is cooking dinner and puts some refrigerated ground beef on a pan.
intention: Bill wants to decide at what temperature to cook the meat at.
moral_action: Bill turns the range on to 400 degrees Fahrenheit and puts the meat in the pan.
moral_consequence: Bill happily enjoys a delicious meal of well cooked and tasty ground beef.
immoral_action: Bill turns the range on to 100 degrees Fahrenheit and puts the meat in the pan.
immoral_consequence: Bill eats the hardly cooked meat and later that night has to be rushed to hospital with food poisoning.

norm: A man traditionally asks for a woman's hand in marriage.
situation: Sara and Mark have been dating for five years, live together and in a serious dating relationship.
intention: Sara wants to get married within the next 6 months.

moral_consequence: Mark treasures Sara as his wife, and they have a wonderful marriage together.
immoral_action: Sara proposes to Mark, and he agrees to marry her on their dating anniversary, a month later.
immoral_consequence: Mark soon starts feeling emasculated after their wedding because of the nontraditional proposal and starts having an affair.

norm: It's wrong to masturbate in class.
situation: Donny is sitting in a college class when he starts thinking about how attractive his classmates are and becomes horny.
intention: Donny wants to relieve himself of how horny he is.
moral_action: Donny waits to get back to his dorm before he touches his nether regions.
moral_consequence: Donny's classmates will think he is a normal person at the school.
immoral_action: Donny starts to touch his nether regions while sitting in class.
immoral_consequence: Donny's classmates will view him as a disgusting pervert and avoid him.

norm: It's good to avoid hurting someone's feelings.
situation: Nancy walks into the house where her children are cleaning up as a surprise for her.
intention: Nancy wants to react to the children's efforts.
moral_action: Nancy tells the children what a great job they did and overlooks all the imperfections.
moral_consequence: The children feel great about themselves and learn how to do a better job as they grow older.
immoral_action: Nancy points out all the things the children could have done better.
immoral_consequence: The children feel like they're not good at cleaning and don't try again.

norm: It's wrong to lie to your parents.
situation: Lucas got a disciplinary note from his teacher to give to his parents.
intention: Lucas wants to go to his friend's slumber party that night.
moral_action: Lucas gives his parents the note and explains to them how he has learned from the situation.
moral_consequence: Lucas's parents can see that Lucas is making an attempt to be better and allow him to go to the party.
immoral_action: Lucas tells his parents he had a good day at school and goes to the party.
immoral_consequence: Lucas's teacher calls his parents the following week about the note and Lucas gets grounded for having lied to them.

norm: It's bad for a teacher to be a predator.
situation: Merle is a high school English teacher, and finds himself attracted to one of his teenage students.
intention: Merle wants to do something about his attraction.
moral_action: Merle tamps down on his attraction and acts professionally toward the student like any other.
moral_consequence: The student graduates and goes away, and Merle keeps his job.
immoral_action: Merle grooms the student and eventually tries to get her alone with him.
immoral_consequence: The student's parents find out and call the police, and Merle is arrested.

norm: It's rude to ban your child's friend from seeing them.
situation: Jill has very strict controls on what type of movies her son is allowed to watch, and his friends' parents are more lenient.
intention: Jill wants to make sure her son only watches G-rated movies.
moral_action: Jill insists that her son's friends always come over to her house to play.
moral_consequence: Jill's son has several close friends, despite their complaining about Jill's strictness.
immoral_action: Jill disrupts every friendship her son starts to form because she doesn't trust the other parents to enforce her rules.
immoral_consequence: Jill's son never develops any social skills and becomes a miserable recluse.

norm: You should try to be sympathetic after someone's pet dies.
situation: Jean's friend Marcy had a pet cat who just died, and Marcy is crying while talking to Jean about it.
intention: Jean wants Marcy to feel better.
moral_action: Jean tells Marcy that she gave the cat a very enjoyable life and had a lot of good times with it.
moral_consequence: Marcy is grateful to be reminded of all of the good times that she had with the cat.
immoral_action: Jean tells Marcy that there are a million cats in the world and that she can just get another one to feel better.
immoral_consequence: Marcy gets upset and feels like Jean doesn't care about animals, nor about her special bond with her now-deceased cat.

norm: It's wrong to push a baby.
situation: Suzie has a baby sister, Kate, who is playing with one of Suzie's toys.
intention: Suzie wants to get her toy back from Kate.
moral_action: Suzie waits until Kate is done playing, then retrieves the toy.
moral_consequence: Suzie plays with the toy for as long as she wants.
immoral_action: Suzie pushes Kate over so that she drops the toy, then takes it.
immoral_consequence: Suzie's mother berates her and sends her to her room.

norm: It's rude to expect someone to buy you cigarettes.
situation: Tom who is sixteen is hanging out in front of the gas station, and he asks John who is older to buy him cigarettes which John refuses.
intention: Tom wants to express his disappointment to John.
moral_action: Tom tells John he understands, and he'll wait for someone else to ask them.
moral_consequence: John says OK as long as it's not him breaking the law for Tom he doesn't really care what happens after.
immoral_action: Tom tells John he's a jerk and that he's asking for a reasonable favor and that John is just a bad person.
immoral_consequence: John is annoyed because Tom thinks it's OK to ask other people to break the law for you and tells Tom he's an idiot.

norm: You should be very polite when visiting other people's home.
situation: Mary is visiting her in-laws' house for dinner one night when she notices a tasty looking pie cooling in the window.
intention: Mary wants to try the pie.
moral_action: Mary inquires about the pie and says that it looks very tasty.
moral_consequence: Mary and her in-laws each have a slice of pie after dinner and enjoy its delicious flavor.
immoral_action: Without asking Mary removes the pie from the window and scarfs down most of it using her hands.
immoral_consequence: Mary's in-laws' are offended by her rudeness and lack of manners and form a negative impression of her.

norm: It's good to sharpen your craft
situation: John is a programmer and recently comes across a course for a programming language he is unfamiliar with.
intention: John wants to consider signing up for the course.
moral_action: John signs up for the programming course and sets aside time for the course.
moral_consequence: John improves his programming skills and maintains relevancy in the programming world.
immoral_action: John decides the programming course is not worth his time and does not sign up for it.
immoral_consequence: John's programming skills stagnate as programming itself continues to change and improve.

norm: It's nice to play with others.
situation: Tara gets a popular new video game the she wanted for her birthday.
intention: Tara wants to play the game.
moral_action: Tara invites her friend who also has the game to play with her.
moral_consequence: Tara has a great time completing the mission with her friend.
immoral_action: Tara plays the game by herself going on a solo mission.
immoral_consequence: Tara wishes that she enjoyed the fun mission with her friend.

norm: It is wrong to force your roommate to switch dorms.
situation: Finn has been assigned to live with Reed who he does not get along with.
intention: Finn wants to separate from Reed.
moral_action: Finn and Reed go to the residence hall administrator and request to be put in different rooms.
moral_consequence: Finn and Reed are able to get new roommates who they tolerate better.
immoral_action: Finn stops cleaning his side of the room and behaves strangely towards Reed in order to drive Reed out of the room.

norm: You shouldn't spread gossip at work.
situation: Bill is told by Jane a rumor that Gary is going to be fired.

moral_consequence: The rumor fades into obscurity and some new rumor takes it's place.

norm: It's wrong not to respect the dead.
situation: Peter's grandfather had died in the past month, and he was missing him.
intention: Peter wanted to go to the cemetery.
moral_action: Peter goes to the cemetery after work and brings flowers to his grandfather's grave.

norm: You shouldn't have inappropriate conversations with people in public.

norm: It's good to break up with someone face to face.
