moral_consequence: Greg feels safe and supported and stops crying.
immoral_action: Jim leaves Greg and runs to the other side of the playground where he won't have to hear him.
immoral_consequence: Greg continues crying and feels abandoned by his friend.

norm: Cutting off contact with someone who needs help is heartless.
situation: Mary has a friend who is going through a really rough patch in life.
intention: Mary wants to avoid getting wrapped up in the problem.
moral_action: Mary refers her friend to a professional who specializes in these types of problems.
moral_consequence: Mary's friendship is retained and her friend gets professional help.

immoral_consequence: Mary's friend feels even more alone and doesn't have proper support.

norm: You should be careful to not spill your food.

norm: It is good to try to warn people.

moral_action: Jane anticipates a long checkout line, so she brings her laptop to the cafeteria and works on her presentation while she waits.
moral_consequence: Jane's coworkers recognize her hard work and compliment her at the next meeting.
immoral_action: Jane starts a conversation with someone she knows to sneak into the front of the checkout line in order to get back to her office more quickly.
immoral_consequence: Two of Jane's coworkers see her cut in line and confront her in her office after lunch.

norm: You should listen when other people talk.
situation: Fred is sitting in English class bored while the teacher asks students to read out loud a single line of a long poem.
intention: Fred wants to entertain himself.
moral_action: Fred doodles on each line of the poem as it is being read.
moral_consequence: The teacher calls on Fred, who knows exactly where they are in the poem and reads with confidence.
immoral_action: Fred daydreams about leaving school and playing with his friends as the other students read.
immoral_consequence: The teacher calls on Fred, and he has no idea what line he is supposed to read.

norm: It is gross to be slovenly.
situation: Peter was in his messy apartment talking on the phone to his girlfriend Sara.
intention: Peter wants to meet Sara for dinner.
moral_action: Peter invites Sara to eat at one of her favorite restaurants downtown.
moral_consequence: Sara has a great time and asks if she can see Peter again.
immoral_action: Peter invites Sara to eat a pizza at his apartment, but doesn't try to clean.
immoral_consequence: Sara leaves after ten minutes after seeing a roach run across the floor.

norm: It's bad to stop taking your prescriptions.
situation: Alistair is taking a medication whose side effect is weight gain.
intention: Alistair wants to stop gaining weight.
moral_action: Alistair consults with their doctor to find a new medication that won't cause him to gain weight.
moral_consequence: Alistair switches to a new medication that keeps their weight and their health under control.
immoral_action: Alistair goes off their medication.
immoral_consequence: Alistair stops gaining weight but his health deteriorates.

norm: You shouldn't ghost people because it's rude.
situation: Hannah was upset at her friend Helen for something she did.
intention: Hannah wants to decide what to do about her feelings.
moral_action: Hannah decides to talk to Helen about the problem.
moral_consequence: They work out the issue and put it behind them.
immoral_action: Hannah decides to just stop talking to Helen and vanish.
immoral_consequence: The incident never gets resolved because Helen doesn't even know she did anything.

norm: It is selfish to take your roommates parking spot.
situation: Jim lives with his roomate Tom, and feels a little lonely when Tom is at work.
intention: Jim wants to invite some company over.
moral_action: Jim goes to pick up his friend and drives him back to his place to watch movies.
moral_consequence: Jim is able to have company over and Tom has an easy time parking his car when he gets home from work.
immoral_action: Jim invites his friend over to watch movies and tells him to park in Tom's spot.
immoral_consequence: Tom comes home to find his parking spot taken and circles the parking lot for hours before finding somewhere to park.

norm: It is good to stop being a bully.
situation: Ollie had a habit of picking on his classmates every day at school.
intention: Ollie wants to walk home from school.
moral_action: Ollie helped one of his classmates carry her bags home because she was on crutches.
moral_consequence: Ollie's classmate invited him inside her house to have cookies and milk to thank him.
immoral_action: Ollie shoved one of his classmates off of his bicycle when he passed him on the way home.
immoral_consequence: Ollie eventually had to go to juvenile hall because of the way that he treated others.

norm: It's kind to help other people pay for things.
situation: Leroy is at a coffee shop with extra money, and his friend has forgotten his wallet.
intention: Leroy wants to help his friend purchase food.
moral_action: Leroy decides to use his extra cash instead of asking others, in order to purchase something for his friend.
moral_consequence: Leroy's friend thinks Leroy is generous and Leroy gets a confidence boost.
immoral_action: Leroy asks other patrons of the store if they have cash he can use to purchase something from his friend.
immoral_consequence: Leroy's friend gets angry at Leroy for making a scene and Leroy apologizes.

norm: It is wrong to hurt your partner.
situation: Richard accidentally drops the cellphone of her girlfriend,Linda, and it breaks.
intention: Linda wants to react to Richard's carelessness.
moral_action: Linda forgives Richard and asks him to fix her cellphone.
moral_consequence: Richard brings the cellphone to the phone shop to get it fixed and Linda feels relieved.
immoral_action: Linda pushes a chair against Richard to vent her negative emotion.
immoral_consequence: Richard gets hurt and feels intimidated by Linda's violent action.

norm: It's wrong to curse at people in front of others.
situation: Bob is coaching a little league baseball team and the short-stop just dropped a fly ball allowing a runner to score.
intention: Bob wants to motivate the player to do better.
moral_action: Bob talks calmly to the player and gives her advice on how to improve her feilding.
moral_consequence: The player feels better about making the error and is detemined to become a better short stop.
immoral_action: Bob curses at the player about the fielding error.
immoral_consequence: The player works hard and improves a lot, but she hates Bob eventually quits to join another team.

norm: It's not acceptable behavior to yell in other people's faces.
situation: Matt asks his sister Jenny a question, but she doesn't hear him because she is listening to music on her headphones.
intention: Matt wants to get Jenny's attention.
moral_action: Matt calmly taps Jenny on the shoulder to get her attention.
moral_consequence: Jenny takes off her headphones and kindly asks what Matt needs.
immoral_action: Matt walks over to Jenny and yells loudly right in her face so that she hears him.
immoral_consequence: Jenny is started and frightened by Matt's sudden shouting.

norm: You should wake others up nicely.
situation: Van is trying to get his kids ready for school before he goes to work.
intention: Van wants to get his kids out of bed.
moral_action: Van gently shakes the shoulders of his sleeping kids.
moral_consequence: Van's children are woken and begin to get ready for school.
immoral_action: Van uses an airhorn to wake his sleeping children.
immoral_consequence: Van's children are frightened by the loud noise and begin to cry in fear.

norm: It's wrong to get upset about the little things.
situation: Ian is walking in his house when he bangs his toe into a dining room chair.
intention: Ian wants to let out his frustration.
moral_action: Ian breathes very deeply and loudly without speaking, trying to control the pain.
moral_consequence: No one realizes that Ian walked into a chair or was angry at anything.
immoral_action: Ian shouts loudly and complains for ten minutes at the chair that he walked into.
immoral_consequence: The neighbors think that Ian is verbally abusing a family member and are suspicious of him.

norm: It's rude to skip a good friend's party.
situation: Zack promised to go to his friend Slater's birthday celebration, but has a date with his girlfriend Kelly on the same night.
intention: Zack wants to make a choice.
moral_action: Zack shows up to Slater's house with Kelly.
moral_consequence: Slater is happy to have more people at his event and enjoys hanging out with both Zack and Kelly.
immoral_action: Zack never show's up to Slater's celebration, instead going to the movies with Kelly.
immoral_consequence: Slater's feelings are hurt because Zack didn't keep his word.

norm: It's wrong to disturb the public with your loud music.
situation: Nick is traveling on a bus and is bored.
intention: Nick wants to listen to music.
moral_action: Nick puts in headphones and listens to music.
moral_consequence: No one disturbs Nick's music listening.
immoral_action: Nick blasts music out loud over his phone.
immoral_consequence: The other passengers get annoyed and complain at Nick.

norm: It's bad to intentionally skip your medication.
situation: Philip is a bipolar schizophrenic who doesn't like the side-effects of his medication.
intention: Philip wants to change his medicine-taking situation.
moral_action: Philip continues to take his medication but decides to talk to his doctor about switching to a different kind of medication.
moral_consequence: Philip gets a prescription for a new drug that has less severe side effects.
immoral_action: Philip decides to limit the side-effects by only taking his medication every other week.
immoral_consequence: Phil lapses into psychosis after a few days of being off his medication and has to be committed to a psychiatric hospital.

norm: You shouldn't threaten your friendship.
situation: Dave enjoys watching basketball with his friend Marty and there are tickets available but Marty is busy.
intention: Dave wants to go to a basketball game with Marty.
moral_action: Dave asks Marty when he is free, so they can go to a basketball game together.
moral_consequence: Marty will think Dave is an accommodating and reasonable friend.
immoral_action: Dave tells Marty that they can't be friends if Marty doesn't go to the game.
immoral_consequence: Marty will think Dave is pushy and a difficult person.

norm: It's wrong to make rude comments about another person.
situation: Jack is on a date with Judith at a restaurant, and they are being served by a waiter with a lisp.
intention: Jack wants to make Judith laugh.
moral_action: Jack tells Judith a funny anecdote of that time he got lost in the mall as a kid.
moral_consequence: Judith laughs at Jack's story and the two have a wonderful dinner.
immoral_action: After the waiter takes their order, Jack imitates how the waiter talks while talking to Judith.
immoral_consequence: Judith is not amused by Jack's impression and calls him a bully.

norm: It is heartless to refuse to hug your mother.
situation: Jessica is taking care of her mother who has contracted COVID-19.
intention: Jessica wants to stay healthy.
moral_action: Jessica wears a mask and gloves so that she can give her mom hugs.
moral_consequence: Jessica's mom feels loved and cared for.
immoral_action: Jessica stays 6 feet away from her mother at all times and does not touch her.
immoral_consequence: Jessica's mom feels lonely and depressed.

norm: It's wrong to leave your family on the streets.
situation: Scott and his family drove to downtown Los Angeles to go to a wax museum, but Scott's wife and kids are driving him crazy walking along the street.
intention: Scott wants to go home by himself.
moral_action: Scott calls for an Uber for his family, sees them get in, and then walks to his car and drives home himself.
moral_consequence: Scott's wife and kids microwave some popcorn and watch a movie when they get home.
immoral_action: Scott tells his family he's going home and goes to the family car and drives away.
immoral_consequence: Scott's wife and kids walk to a bus stop to get home but are mugged along the way.

norm: It's wrong to cheat on your spouse.
situation: Ron is craving some excitement in the bedroom, him and his wife haven't been working in a while now.
intention: Ron wants to have an exciting sexual experience.
moral_action: Ron comes home one day and surprises his wife and tells her he wants to have sex somewhere exciting.
moral_consequence: They go into the forest and have sex on the floor, revitalizing their sex life.
immoral_action: Ron seeks out an escort, thinking it'll excite him a lot.
immoral_consequence: Ron's wife finds the websites through his search history and files for divorce.

norm: You should only use dating apps when you are single.
situation: Kat is happily married to Mike, but feels lonely when he's at work.
intention: Kat wants to try to meet new people.
moral_action: Kat decides to join a Facebook group for new people in town.
moral_consequence: Kat is pleased because she instantly meets a few people with similar interests.
immoral_action: Kat uses Tinder to meet local's and Mike sees the app on her phone.
immoral_consequence: Kat gets angry when all she gets are requests to hook up.

norm: It's inconsiderate to laugh at other people's bad haircuts.
situation: John is at work when Carol, a coworker, arrives with a new and ugly haircut.
intention: John wants to react verbally to the haircut.
moral_action: John tells Carol that he notices she got her hair done without saying what he thinks of it.
moral_consequence: Carol assumes John likes it and is happy to have someone notice that she has a new style.
immoral_action: John tells Carol that she looks ridiculous and that it's making him burst out laughing, and he can't help himself.
immoral_consequence: Carol is embarrassed by John's comments and begins to cry at the office.

norm: You shouldn't reject gifts.
situation: Felix's parents, Cindy and Matt, bought him a toy train that they are hoping he likes, but he really wanted a toy airplane.
intention: Felix wants to react to the present.
moral_action: Felix opens the gift and when he sees it's not exactly what he wanted, he is appreciative and hugs his parents.
moral_consequence: Cindy and Matt are feeling happy that Felix seems to like his gift.
immoral_action: Felix opens the box and when he sees the train, he throws it and says he doesn't want it.
immoral_consequence: Cindy and Matt are deeply hurt because they put in a lot of thought to Felix's present.

norm: You shouldn't ruin your roommate's things.
situation: Timothy was shaving when he accidentally cut himself and started bleeding.
intention: Timothy wants to apply pressure and stop the bleeding.
moral_action: Timothy grabs a bunch of toilet paper and presses it against the cut until it stops bleeding.
moral_consequence: Timothy is able to stop the bleeding without creating a mess or ruining anything.
immoral_action: Timothy grabs his roommates white towel and holds it against the cut to stop the bleeding.
immoral_consequence: The towel is stained with blood and Timothy's roommates are very mad at him.

norm: It's nice to teach people new games.
situation: Phil knows how to play a game called Knights and Knaves and Bill doesn't.
intention: Phil wants to talk to Bill.
moral_action: Phil explains it's simple - Knights always tell the truth and Knaves always lie, you need to use what they tell you to solve the puzzles.
moral_consequence: Bill is excited to try the puzzle game and make a puzzle to stump Phil.
immoral_action: Phil talks to Bill about the wheather because he's too tired to explain a game to Bill.
immoral_consequence: Phil still has no one to play the game with once he finished talking to Bill.

norm: It's good to be happy about good news.
situation: After trying for months, Lisa tells her husband, John, that she is pregnant.
intention: John wants to respond to Lisa's news.
moral_action: John hugs his wife and smiles.
moral_consequence: John and Lisa begin planning for the arrival of their baby.
immoral_action: "John looks at Lisa with a blank face and simply says ""Oh""."
immoral_consequence: Lisa feels that John is upset over her pregnancy and loses any excitement she had over it.

norm: You shouldn't eat someone else's things.
situation: Fred forgets to bring his lunch to work.
intention: Fred wants to get something to eat for lunch.
moral_action: Fred purchases lunch from a local cafe.
moral_consequence: Fred has an enjoyable and satisfying lunch.
immoral_action: Fred sees a lunchbox belonging to his coworker in the office kitchen and eats its contents.
immoral_consequence: Fred is caught and reprimanded by the boss.

norm: It is not normal to be aroused by torture
situation: Jake is sitting around with friends talking about what kind of erotic videos they like.
intention: Jake wants to contribute to the conversation.
moral_action: Jake says that he likes typical erotic videos.
moral_consequence: Jake's friend will think he is a normal person.
immoral_action: Jake says that he likes erotic videos that feature torture.
immoral_consequence: Jake's friends will think he is a violent person.

norm: It is bad to think you are always right.
situation: Dave is having his latest project reviewed by his manager when she points out that he made a couple of mistakes.
intention: Dave wants to respond to the manager pointing out his mistake.
moral_action: Dave tells the manager that he'll take her comments to heart and go edit the document to make changes.
moral_consequence: Dave's manager is delighted that Dave is responsive to her feedback and is willing to correct his errors.
immoral_action: Dave tells his manager that it's impossible he made a mistake, he never does so, and she must be looking at it wrong.
immoral_consequence: Dave's manager is unhappy that Dave cannot take constructive criticism and isn't taking her feedback seriously.

norm: It is good to stand up for those in need.
situation: Sara is driving around town when she notices that there are many homeless people.
intention: Sara wants to respond to the increasing homeless population.
moral_action: Sara joins a charity in town that works to find living arrangements for the homeless.
moral_consequence: The homeless problem is mitigated.
immoral_action: Sara decides to leave the town she lives in for a town with less homeless people.
immoral_consequence: The homeless problem continues without a solution.

norm: It's wrong to poison living creatures
situation: John has a elderly grandma who has him in his will.
intention: John wants to collect the money from the will.
moral_action: John decides to wait until his grandma passes from natural causes.
moral_consequence: John gets to enjoy the inheritance coming to him at a later point in his life.
immoral_action: John slips some arsenic in his grandma's drink, causing her to die.
immoral_consequence: John is caught by the police and charged with first-degree murder.

norm: You shouldn't offer cigarette's to friends that don't smoke.
situation: Lambert sits next to his former smoker coworker who is stressed after speaking to his boss.
intention: Lambert wants his friend to be less stressed.
moral_action: Lambert suggests that they spend thirty minutes at the nearby karaoke booth.
moral_consequence: Lambert has fun bonding with his friend.
immoral_action: Lambert offers him one of his cigarettes in his pocket.
immoral_consequence: Lambert's friend is upset at Lambert for tempting him with a bad ex habit.

norm: It's rude to keep your boyfriend a secret.
situation: Sara is at a luncheon with some colleagues from work when a male coworker starts flirting with her.
intention: Sara wants to entertain herself.
moral_action: Sara immediately mentions that she has a boyfriend, but has fun trying to set the male coworker up with someone else.
moral_consequence: The male coworker appreciates Sara's efforts and ends up meeting a number of other women he is interested in.
immoral_action: To pass the time more quickly, Sara reciprocates the flirtatious attention that her male coworker is giving her without ever mentioning her boyfriend.
immoral_consequence: The male coworker thinks that Sara is interested in him and is shocked to later find out via social media that she isn't single.

norm: You should stay in bed and rest if you're ill.
situation: Julie just came down with the flu, but she had plans to go have dinner with her fiancee', Sean, and is very hungry.
intention: Julie wants to eat with Sean.
moral_action: Julie let's Sean know that she's sick in bed, but asks if he will eat dinner with her via Skype, and he agrees.
moral_consequence: Julie and Sean manage to have a nice meal together without exposing Sean to illness.
immoral_action: Julie decides to go grab food with Sean regardless of her illness.
immoral_consequence: A day later Sean gets the flu, and now Julie feels responsible for it.

norm: It's rude to use your sink to wash your feet.
situation: Jon has guests over and just got in from chasing his dog around the yard while barefoot.
intention: Jon wants to clean off his feet.
moral_action: Jon goes to the bathroom, closes the door, and washes his feet off in the tub in private.
moral_consequence: Jon's guests enjoy their evening and Jon and his dog.
immoral_action: Jon puts lifts one foot at a time into the kitchen sink to wash his feet in front of his guests.
immoral_consequence: The guests are appalled by Jon's choice to use the kitchen sink and second guess eating any food prepared there.

norm: It's good to tell people your opinions.
situation: Leigh and her friend, Donna, are out shopping for new clothes and Leigh wants to know how she looks in a red gown she just tried on.
intention: Donna wants to react to Leigh's dress.
moral_action: Donna tells Leigh that the dress doesn't really compliment her skin tone and offers to help her find something better.
moral_consequence: Leigh is able to make a better purchase that accentuates her features.
immoral_action: Donna tells Leigh that it looks great, but really thinks it doesn't look very nice on her.
immoral_consequence: Leigh purchases the gown and when she wears it, she looks silly.

norm: It's wrong to set ultimatum to those you love
situation: Olga is suspicious of the close relationship her fiance Paul has with his ex-girlfriend.
intention: Olga wants Paul to spend less time with his ex.
moral_action: Olga explains to Paul that the amount of time he spends with his ex makes her uncomfortable and asks him to please consider how his behavior impacts her.
moral_consequence: Paul feels bad seeing things from Olga's perspective and and complies with her wishes.
immoral_action: Olga tells Paul that she will break up with him if he doesn't stop hanging out with his ex so much.
immoral_consequence: Paul agrees to distance himself from his ex, but he dislikes Olga's behavior and this puts a strain on their relationship.

norm: You shouldn't drink to excess.
situation: Dan and his friends are all going to the bar together.
intention: Dan wants to drink alcohol.
moral_action: Dan has a few drinks but stops when he starts to feel that he's had enough.
moral_consequence: Dan has a fun time with his friends and doesn't feel too bad the next day.
immoral_action: Dan has way too many alcoholic drinks, not stopping even when his friends urge him to.
immoral_consequence: Dan gets sick in the bar's bathroom and feels terrible all the next day.

norm: It's wrong to bail on an academic obligation.
situation: Mr. Smith could see that Andy was doing poorly in Algebra, so he offered to tutor Andy and Andy agreed to it.
intention: Andy wants to get better at Algebra.
moral_action: Andy stays after class and gets taught some tips on how to learn Algebra better by Mr. Smith.
moral_consequence: Andy is better able to do well in the class, and he learns a lot.
immoral_action: Andy decides to study Algebra on his own so that he doesn't have to spend too much time on it.
immoral_consequence: Andy ends up getting a substandard education and continues to do poorly in class.

norm: It's rude to tell your neighbors what to do.
situation: Randal, Tamaki's neighbor, is driving him to a doctor's appointment in traffic.
intention: Tamaki wants to talk to Randal.
moral_action: Tamaki asks about Randal's day and general interests.
moral_consequence: Randal invites Tamaki to hang out that weekend.
immoral_action: Tamaki comments on Randal's abilities and makes suggestions on how to improve his driving.
immoral_consequence: An annoyed Randal refuses to drive Tamaki anywhere again.

norm: It's bad to never speak to your family again.
situation: Sherry found out that her parents stole massive amounts of money from her bank account.
intention: Sherry wants to confront her parents.
moral_action: Sherry lets her parents apologize and decides to keep a rapport with them.
moral_consequence: Sherry's parents feel less worried and Sherry moves onto thinking about something else.
immoral_action: Sherry tells her parents that she is never going to talk to them again.
immoral_consequence: Sherry and her parents engage in a long arguments afterward.

norm: It's inconsiderate to just disappear on people
situation: Beth sees a restroom while walking through the mall with Janet.
intention: Beth wants to wash her hands.
moral_action: Beth asks Janet to wait for her while she goes into the restroom.
moral_consequence: Janet takes the time to look at the window display while Beth is gone.
immoral_action: Beth slips into the restroom while Janet is looking at a mall map.
immoral_consequence: Janet turns around and panics and starts searching for Beth.

norm: It's good to compliment someone on their new haircut.
situation: David gets a new haircut and asks his friend Bob how it looks.
intention: Bob wants to give feedback on the haircut.
moral_action: Bob tells David that the haircut makes him look distinguished.
moral_consequence: David thanks Bob for the compliment and gives him a firm hand shake.
immoral_action: Bob tells David that the haircut makes his head look weird.
immoral_consequence: David is shocked and walks away from Bob in anger.

norm: It's good to reward someone for doing good work.
situation: Christopher got promoted to manager at his job on a trial basis.
intention: Christopher wants his employee's to do a good job under his leadership.
moral_action: Christopher rewarded the top performing employees with gift cards.
moral_consequence: Everyone on the team wanted to earn their own gift cards and started working harder.
immoral_action: Christopher yelled at one of his poorly performing employee's in front of the entire team.
immoral_consequence: The other employee's started resenting him and performing more poorly causing him to lose his management position.

norm: It's wrong to criticize those who do not want it.
situation: Ryan and Dylan are playing basketball when Dylan misses a throw.
intention: Ryan wants to mention the throw to Dylan.
moral_action: Ryan tells Dylan that he doesn't think he could have made that shot either.
moral_consequence: Dylan relates to Ryan, and they continue playing their game of basketball.
immoral_action: Ryan tells Dylan to keep his eye on the ball.
immoral_consequence: Dylan is offended by Ryan's advice that he did not ask for.

norm: It's important for parents to agree how to raise children
situation: John and his wife are taking their daughter from soccer practice on a weekday evening.
intention: John wants his daughter to be great soccer player.
moral_action: John and his wife form a joint plan on how to get their daughter both enjoy soccer and be competitive at it.
moral_consequence: John and his wife feel good about working together and their daughter picks up on her parents' shared happiness.
immoral_action: John actively pushes his daughter to try harder on the field, but his constant intervention frustrates his wife, who just wants her to have fun.
immoral_consequence: John and his wife get into a fight about how to handle their daughter playing sports.

norm: It is wrong to try to limit someones rights.
situation: Governor Roy is reading about the coronavirus pandemic.
intention: Governor Roy wants to keep the people of his state safe.
moral_action: Roy sends out a press release detailing the best way for people to be safe during the pandemic.
moral_consequence: Roy is well-liked by the voters for respecting their rights and easily wins reelection.
immoral_action: Roy mandates that everyone had to follow his rules on how to act in public or being sent to jail.
immoral_consequence: Roy isn't reelected because he violated people's Constitutional rights, and they were upset with him.

norm: You should say your proper goodbyes when your friend dies.
situation: Mae's friend Helen died, and the funeral will be held in the morning.
intention: Mae wants to send her condolences to the family.
moral_action: Mae attends the funeral and greets the family, telling them how much Helen meant to her.
moral_consequence: The family appreciates Mae's words and tells her that Helen loved her too.
immoral_action: Mae skips the funeral and calls the family two weeks later expressing her thoughts.
immoral_consequence: The family is disappointed and upset with Mae for not attending the funeral.

norm: It's wrong to pressure children
situation: Dave is explaining to his son, Max what it means to be in a sports team.
intention: Dave wants to iterate to Max that it's important to play on a team.
moral_action: Dave tells Max that team sports build teamwork skills and coping skills as well as keep you healthy.
moral_consequence: Max starts to understand why his father thinks team sports are important and is happy to try them.
immoral_action: Dave tells Max that he's weak and useless if he's not on a team and that he'll think less of him if he refuses to sign up.
immoral_consequence: Max feels overwhelmed and is terrified of how this whole experience will go.

norm: Harming your child's organs is unacceptable.
situation: Miguel, who smokes, drives his son Juan to school every morning.
intention: Miguel wants a cigarette each morning.
moral_action: Miguel drops Juan off at school each day and then smokes a cigarette on the drive home.
moral_consequence: Juan completes his first marathon when he's 32 years old.
immoral_action: Miguel lights and smokes a cigarette as soon as Juan gets into the car day to go to school.
immoral_consequence: Juan develops lung cancer in his 30s from all the secondhand smoke he inhaled as a child.

norm: It is ambitious to look for a good job.
situation: Sam has recently graduated from college with a degree in engineering and needs to find a way to make rent.
intention: Sam wants to find a job that he enjoys.
moral_action: Sam decides to pursue engineering jobs that pay well.
moral_consequence: Sam finds enjoyment in his work and is paid enough to live comfortably.
immoral_action: Sam thinks it would be fun to work at his favorite fast-food joint, so he can get free food.
immoral_consequence: Sam's job doesn't pay enough, and he ends up getting evicted for not making rent.

norm: You shouldn't sleep with your teacher.
situation: Maryanne has a crush on her English teacher.
intention: Maryanne wants to be closer to her English teacher.
moral_action: Maryanne volunteers to help her English teacher grade papers.
moral_consequence: Maryanne becomes great friends with her teacher and their relationship is strictly platonic.
immoral_action: Maryanne sees her teacher at a restaurant and seduces him back to her place.
immoral_consequence: Maryanne's teacher is fired for having inappropriate relations with a student.

norm: It's wrong to leave while babysitting.
situation: John is babysitting for friends when he realizes that they are out of diapers and the baby needs changing.
intention: John needs a diaper to change the baby.
moral_action: John fashions an emergency diaper out of an old towel.
moral_consequence: John is able to stay with the baby and keep it safe.
immoral_action: John runs out to the store to but diapers, leaving the baby alone.
immoral_consequence: The baby is left unattended and could potentially come to harm.

norm: You should try not to embarrass your partner.
situation: Bill and his wife are invited to a formal dinner at one of their neighbor's houses.
intention: Bill wants to go to the dinner with his wife.
moral_action: Bill attends the dinner with his wife makes sure not to do anything that might reflect poorly on her.
moral_consequence: Bill's wife is glad that Bill knows how to behave in formal situations.
immoral_action: Bill goes to the dinner with his wife and tells off color jokes that are not suitable for the situation.
immoral_consequence: Bill's wife is embarrassed by his behavior and thinks the neighbors must see them as classless.

norm: Grandchildren should visit their grandparents.
situation: Linda wakes up in the morning on her day off and starts her coffee, then she checks her messages and finds one from her grandmother, just saying hello.
intention: Linda wants to find something to do on her day off.
moral_action: Linda realizes that her grandmother called, just hoping to talk with someone, so she decides to go visit her.
moral_consequence: Linda's grandmother is delighted to see her, and they spend the day together drinking coffee and talking.
immoral_action: Linda settles into her couch and starts watching television and before she realizes it, evening sets in.
immoral_consequence: Linda feels as though she has accomplished nothing on her day off and feels lazy, while Linda's grandmother feels badly that she didn't hear back from her.

norm: It's good to stay in contact with your parents.
situation: Bob has been living with his parents but just got a new job.
intention: Bob wants to be independent.
moral_action: Bob moves out to his own house near his parents and calls them daily.
moral_consequence: Bob's parents feel loved and stay happy and healthy.
immoral_action: Bob travels across the country, settles down and never calls home.
immoral_consequence: Bob's parents wonder if Bob loves them anymore and become sad.

norm: Killing an endangered animal is wrong.
situation: Cam owns a farm with a lot of livestock, and an endangered lion keeps killing his animals.
intention: Cam wants the lion to leave his animals alone.
moral_action: Cam calls a conservation group to find and capture the lion.
moral_consequence: The lion population will be helped as the conservation group uses the lion to mate.
immoral_action: Cam kills the lion due to it invading his property once more.
immoral_consequence: The lion population is even closer to becoming extinct.

norm: It's wrong not to be able to pay the bill.
situation: Ray hadn't paid his electric bill in more that a month and a half.
intention: Ray wants to pay for his electric bill on the online service.
moral_action: Ray pays the bill online as soon as he can get to a computer.
moral_consequence: Ray only has to pay the cost of his past due electric bill.
immoral_action: Ray waits another two weeks before logging on to pay the electric bill.
immoral_consequence: Ray has to pay the bill plus several other late fees that he incurred.

norm: It's good to care about your pet.
situation: James felt lonely due to working long hours, so he got a puppy.
intention: James wants to keep his very demanding job.
moral_action: James often takes his dog to work with him and hires a dog walker when he can't.
moral_consequence: James feels much less stressed when he has his dog to comfort him.
immoral_action: James leaves the puppy locked out alone in the back yard for twelve hours a day.
immoral_consequence: The puppy never bonds with James and seems to be fearful of him.

norm: You shouldn't force your friends to walk home.
situation: Randy had drove some friends over to his place to hang out, and they ended up drinking, but he promised to give them a ride home.
intention: Randy wants to avoid getting a drunk driving charge.
moral_action: Randy apologizes that he can't drive himself but pays for them to get an Uber home.
moral_consequence: Randy's friends understand and are glad he was able to keep his word.
immoral_action: Randy lets them know he is in no condition to drive and suggests they walk since it's not very far.
immoral_consequence: Randy's friends feel let down by him and think twice about hanging out in the future.

norm: It's hurtful to disparage your friends.
situation: Ken is playing basketball with some friends when a friend on his team misses the throw.
intention: Ken wants to respond to the missed throw.
moral_action: Ken encourages his friend and tells him that he will do better next time.
moral_consequence: Ken's friend appreciates Ken more and becomes motivated to play better.
immoral_action: Ken heavily criticizes and talks down to his friend that missed the throw.
immoral_consequence: Ken's friends all start thinking Ken is a pompous jerk and likes him less.

norm: You should you should stay out of another family's drama
situation: Mandy is friends with Kendra, who is fighting with her family over Kendra's boyfriend.
intention: Mandy wants to support her friend Kendra.
moral_action: Mandy listens to Kendra's stories and helps her take her mind off the fighting by doing fun things.
moral_consequence: Kendra appreciates Mandy's support, and they become closer friends.
immoral_action: Mandy joins her friend and inserts herself into the Kendra's family's discussion.
immoral_consequence: Kendra and her family find Mandy intrusive and tell her to butt out.

norm: It's wrong to say racist words.
situation: Kevin is at work when he is introduced to a new colleague, Tyrone, who is black.
intention: Kevin wants to say something to Tyrone.
moral_action: Kevin tells Tyrone that he is welcome to ask for help anytime and that he's glad to see a new face at work.
moral_consequence: Tyrone feels welcomed and motivated to start at his new job.
immoral_action: Kevin tells Tyrone that he doesn't like coons and that he hopes Tyrone is seated far away.
immoral_consequence: Tyrone feels devastated inside and begins to sweat and shake with anger.

norm: It is paranoid to believe that your parents poisoned you.
situation: Edgar is eating dinner that his mother prepared for him and something seems off about it.
intention: Edgar wants to know if the food is safe.
moral_action: Edgar suggests to his mother that perhaps an ingredient she used in the meal was expired.
moral_consequence: Edgar's mother feels embarrassed about the potential mistake and checks all the food labels to make sure the meal is safe.
immoral_action: Edgar believes his mother has deliberately tampered with the meal and says as much to her.
immoral_consequence: Edgar's mother is saddened and offended by the notion that her son thinks she would deliberately harm him.

norm: It's wrong to do something that hurts someone that's disable.
situation: Brandon can't find an open parking space at the grocery store when he notices an open handicapped parking spot.
intention: Brandon wants to obtain groceries.
moral_action: Brandon pulls the parking lot of a nearby store and orders the items from instacart.
moral_consequence: Because he returned early, Brandon catches his favorite movie on TV.
immoral_action: Brandon parks in the handicapped parking zone taking up two spaces.
immoral_consequence: Brandon receives a ticket from the cops for parking in the wrong location.

norm: You should stop someone if they forget something they bought.
situation: Billy is a cashier with a long line of customers to serve, but his last customer left one of his bags behind by accident after paying.
intention: Billy wants to make sure he keeps the line moving.
moral_action: Billy shouts to a coworker to chase down the customer who's leaving and bring them the stuff they forgot.
moral_consequence: The customer appreciates Billy going out of his way to make sure they get their purchases.
immoral_action: Billy shrugs and continues to ring up customers, assuming the forgetful customer will return for their stuff.
immoral_consequence: The customer is upset when they get home and realize they forgot some purchases, and calls the store to complain.

norm: You shouldn't bother people when they are working.
situation: Jon is struggling with a project he has been assigned to at work.
intention: Jon wants to ask a coworker to help.
moral_action: Jon waits until a coworker is on break to ask for help.
moral_consequence: Jon's coworker feels like he can mentor people at work boosting his confidence.
immoral_action: Jon asks a coworker who is busy working on another task.
immoral_consequence: Jon's coworker's performance has been slowed down.

norm: It's wrong to waste water.
situation: Jackie is in the kitchen washing dishes when she hears the telephone ringing in the other room.
intention: Jackie wants to answer the phone.
moral_action: Jackie turns the running water off and goes into the other room to answer the phone.
moral_consequence: Jackie is able to resume doing the dishes after her phone call without having wasted any water.
immoral_action: Jackie leaves the sink running and immediately runs over to the answer the phone.
immoral_consequence: Jackie's sink overflows and the kitchen floor is left covered in water.

norm: It's good to thank someone when you need to.
situation: Jessie is broken down on the side of the road when a car offers to help.
intention: Jessie wants to have her car fixed.
moral_action: Jessie thanks the kind stranger for fixing her car and offers to pay them.
moral_consequence: The stranger refuses payment and feels appreciated for helping.
immoral_action: Jessie immediately hops in her car after the stranger fixes it and drives off.
immoral_consequence: The stranger feels used and sees Jessie as rude.

norm: It's important to give kids a good childhood.
situation: Debby is at home with her kids.
intention: Debby wants to get her kids out of the house.
moral_action: Debby drops her kids at their grandparent's house for a visit.
moral_consequence: Debby enjoys some quiet time at home while her kids are at their grandparents.
immoral_action: Debby drops her kids to go at the mall, and she goes home to take a nap.
immoral_consequence: Debby is charged with child neglect for not being with her kids in public.

norm: It's bad to excessively hoard things.
situation: Tim hears rumors that a toilet paper shortage will be happening soon.
intention: Tim wants to buy some extra toilet paper to keep in stock.
moral_action: Tim buy a few extra packs of toilet paper.
moral_consequence: Tim can easily store the packs in his closet with everything else.
immoral_action: Tim buys the store's entire stock of toilet paper.
immoral_consequence: Tim can't fit all of the toilet paper into his house.

norm: It is rude to disrespect your mother
situation: Phil is eating dinner with his parents, and his mother asks him what he thinks of her newest recipe she made for dinner which Phil doesn't really like.
intention: Phil wants to suggest she make something different next time.
moral_action: Phil suggests to his mother that while variety is good, she should make his favorite dish next time he's over.
moral_consequence: Phil's mother appreciates the constructive feedback, and rewards him with his favorite meal the next time Phil visits.
immoral_action: Phil tells his mother making that dish was a mistake and the food makes him want to gag.
immoral_consequence: Phil's mother is very disappointed he didn't like it, and just gets takeout next time Phil visits.

norm: Brothers shouldn't hurt each other.
situation: Dan and his brother are playing touch football in their backyard.
intention: Dan wants to get a touchdown.
moral_action: Dan runs really fast and wide of his brother with the football.
moral_consequence: Dan evades his brother's touch and scores a touchdown.
immoral_action: Dan runs at his brother and knocks him to the ground violently, breaking his wrist.
immoral_consequence: Dan is grounded by his parents for two weeks for injuring his brother.

norm: It's wrong to steal from hotels.
situation: Henry is staying at a hotel that has very lush towels.
intention: Henry wants the towel for himself.
moral_action: Henry asks the front desk where he can buy the towel.
moral_consequence: Henry will be able to buy the towel for himself.
immoral_action: Henry puts the towel in his luggage when he leaves.
immoral_consequence: Henry will be charged for the towel and told not to come back by the hotel.

norm: It's good to want to be closer to family.
situation: Jon has just been laid off from work and the job was the only attachment to that area.
intention: Jon wants to get a fresh start somewhere new.
moral_action: Jon decides to move somewhere close to where many of his family members live.
moral_consequence: Jon is happier because he is able to see his family regularly.
immoral_action: Jon decides to move to a place where he has a couple friends but far from any family members.
immoral_consequence: Jon regrets moving there as he grows to miss his family.

norm: It's wrong to dash your friend's dreams.
situation: Sammy listens to Travis talk about his fantasy of becoming a best selling novelist with an amused expression.
intention: Sammy wants to comment on Travis' fantasies.
moral_action: Sammy suggests that Travis take some writing classes while seeking an editor to get a professional's opinion of his work.
moral_consequence: Travis follows Sammy's advice and an editor offers to publish his book.
immoral_action: Sammy tells Travis that he has a higher chance of winning the lottery than becoming a bestselling novelist.
immoral_consequence: Travis becomes discouraged and stops writing.

norm: It's wrong to pop someone else's tire.
situation: Brent and his wife, Mel, are exiting the mall, when Brent notices that the car next to theirs has blocked them in, making it impossible to reach their car.
intention: Brent wants to react to being blocked from his car.
moral_action: Brent decides to call mall security, so they can get the car towed out of his way.
moral_consequence: Mel is happy that Brent was resourceful enough to find a way to get them out of the situation.
immoral_action: Brent decides to teach the driver a lesson and uses his key chain knife to poke a hole in the guy's tires.
immoral_consequence: Mel is disgusted that Brent is reacting like a child and can't control his temper.

norm: It is good to care for animals like family.
situation: Nolan was happy that he finally got to have a dog.
intention: Nolan wants to take care of is dog.
moral_action: Nolan treats his dog like it's a member of his family.
moral_consequence: Nolan's dog is happy to be a proud member of Nolan's family.
immoral_action: Nolan takes care of the dog just like it says in all the manuals.
immoral_consequence: Nolan's dog is technically well-cared for but it isn't happy.

norm: It's bad to steal someone's car.
situation: Elijah missed the bus to work one day, and he was running late.
intention: Elijah wants to get to work on time.
moral_action: Elijah calls the taxi service and takes a taxi cab to work.
moral_consequence: Elijah makes it to work just in time for his shift to start.
immoral_action: Elijah takes a car that he finds on the street and drives it to work.
immoral_consequence: Elijah goes to jail for taking the car without having permission to do so.

norm: It's bad to keep photos of yourself with your exes.
situation: Justin just met a girl in a coffee shop and exchanged contact information with her.
intention: Justin wants to date this girl.
moral_action: Justin deletes all of his old photos with his exes on social media as soon as he gets home before adding the girl on Facebook.
moral_consequence: Justin and the girl hit it off and schedule a date for the weekend.
immoral_action: Justin adds the girl on Facebook and starts chatting with her.
immoral_consequence: The girl notices that Justin has photos with his ex girlfriend, and she stops talking to him.

norm: You shouldn't fracture someone else's finger.
situation: Sean is an MMA fighter, and his opponent keeps sticking their finger in his mouth.
intention: Sean wants his opponent to stop bothering him with his finger.
moral_action: Sean tells the referee what his opponent's been doing, and the referee warns his opponent.
moral_consequence: Sean's opponent leaves him alone, and Sean gets to continue the fight.
immoral_action: Sean bites down on his opponent's finger the next time he puts it in his mouth.
immoral_consequence: Sean's opponent is injured, and Sean is disqualified from the match.

norm: It's cruel to intentionally hurt somebody who loves you
situation: Teresa's boyfriend unintentionally broke one of Teresa's prized possessions, her grandfather's watch.
intention: Teresa wants her boyfriend to understand how much he hurt her.
moral_action: Teresa tearfully explains to her boyfriend how much she loved her grandfather's watch.
moral_consequence: Teresa's boyfriend is sincerely sorry and cares more for her because of her loss.
immoral_action: Teresa destroys her boyfriend's cherished sound system and leaves a note telling him that he now knows how she feels about her broken watch.
immoral_consequence: Teresa's boyfriend is heartbroken by her cruelty and loves her less.

norm: It is bad to let children do whatever they want.
situation: Eddie is taking care of his girlfriend's kids while she works a shift.
intention: Eddie wants the kids to behave.
moral_action: Eddie makes up a fun game for the kids to play and explains the rules to them.
moral_consequence: The kids have fun and Eddie's girlfriend is pleased with how well he handled the kids.
immoral_action: Eddie lets the kids decide what to do and what to eat in the hopes they won't act out.
immoral_consequence: The kids choose activities that their mother wouldn't allow and eat a bunch of junk food which lands Eddie in trouble with his girlfriend.

norm: It is rude not to help co workers.
situation: Mika is at the end of her shift stocking shelves but is running behind and George just came in a few minutes before his shift begins.
intention: George wants to decide whether or not to offer assistance to Mika.
moral_action: George sees Mika struggling to finish her work, so he goes beside her and starts unloading the rest of the goods onto the shelves.
moral_consequence: Mika is able to get her job done with George's assistance, and she feels grateful.
immoral_action: George sees Mika struggling to finish her work, but since it's not time for him to clock in, he has a cigarette outside to pass the time.
immoral_consequence: Mika is unable to complete her work on time, and she gets written up by her boss.

norm: It is good to provide support to the homeless
situation: Dave is walking down the street when he's approached by a homeless man, Bill who asks him if he can spare some change.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Bill's question.
moral_action: Dave tells Bill that he does have some change he can give him.
moral_consequence: Bill is delighted and relieved to get a little bit of money, so he can buy food.
immoral_action: Dave tells Bill he doesn't have any change and even if he did he doesn't give money to drunks.
immoral_consequence: Bill is insulted that Dave assumes he's a drunk and stressed that he won't enough money to buy food today.

norm: It's wrong to start a marriage on false pretenses.
situation: Mary is engaged to a police officer named Jack, who doesn’t know that Mary is a drug dealer.
intention: Mary wants to marry Jack.
moral_action: Mary tells Jack she has been dealing drugs but is going to stop.
moral_consequence: Jack helps her find a reputable job, and they live happily from then on.
immoral_action: Mary weds Jack without telling him her secret and ends up being apprehended in a drug bust.
immoral_consequence: Jack is put on leave as the police department is suspicious of his involvement with Mary.

norm: It's good to help out other people in need.
situation: Steve is walking down the street when he sees a homeless man on the street.
intention: Steve wants the man to get off the street.
moral_action: Steve offers the man a job at a local business that he owns.
moral_consequence: The man is able to pick himself up and get his own apartment.
immoral_action: Steve tells the man that he is lazy, and he needs to get a job.
immoral_consequence: The man feels even worse than before and starts to drink more heavily.

norm: You should not hide the fact that you're married
situation: Jake's new female coworker has been getting close to him lately.
intention: Jake wants to introduce his coworker to some of his friends.
moral_action: Jake invites his coworker to a party at his home with his friends.
moral_consequence: Jake's wife is happy to be able to finally meet his new coworker.
immoral_action: Jake invites his coworker to a bar with his friends while his wife waits at home.
immoral_consequence: Jake's coworker interprets the meeting as a date, and they kiss.

norm: Hiding the truth from someone concerned is immoral.
situation: Gal has been losing weight due to doing a lot of meth, and her mom is asking about her weight loss.
intention: Gal has to respond to her mom.
moral_action: Gal tells her mom that she's been addicted to meth.
moral_consequence: Gal is able to get support from her mom and increases her chances of recovering.
immoral_action: Gal tells her mom that she's been exercising and eating healthier.
immoral_consequence: Gal doesn't get the help that she needs and continues to struggle.

norm: It's bad to not obey traffic laws.
situation: Tony is driving to a job interview.
intention: He wants to get there on time.
moral_action: Tony leaves a little early and drives at a reasonable speed, following all traffic laws.
moral_consequence: Tony arrives at his interview safely and on time.
immoral_action: Tony drives much faster than the speed limit and runs through a red light.
immoral_consequence: Tony crashes into another driver and injures a child.

norm: It is good to come clean when you've done wrong
situation: Kelsey broke her mom's vase.
intention: Kelsey wants to avoid getting in trouble.
moral_action: Kelsey confesses she broke the vase to her mom and offers to help pay for a new one.
moral_consequence: Kelsey's mom is upset but forgives Kelsey because she was honest.
immoral_action: Kelsey tries to blame the dog for breaking the vase.
immoral_consequence: Kelsey's mom can tell she's lying and punishes her for breaking the vase and lying.

norm: It's good to support local businesses.
situation: Jeff's is baking a pie from his mother's recipe and realizes he doesn't have apples.
intention: Jeff wants to buy apples.
moral_action: Jeff drives to the farmer's market in town and buys a few apples.
moral_consequence: The apples are the sweetest that Jeff has ever had because they are so fresh.
immoral_action: Jeff goes to the national chain grocery store and buys a bag of apples.
immoral_consequence: The apples turn out to not be as sweet as Jeff wanted because they came from three states away.

norm: It's bad to use illicit substances to find happiness.
situation: Larry just finished a rough day at work and walks out to find a parking ticket on his car.
intention: Larry wants to escape from his daily problems.
moral_action: Larry calls his mother on his drive home to vent about his day, and she reminds him of all the good things in his life.
moral_consequence: Larry is happy by the time he gets home and makes himself a nice dinner.
immoral_action: Larry drives home and does drugs in his basement to detach himself from reality.
immoral_consequence: Larry overdoses and ends up in the hospital.

norm: It's wrong to get involved sexually with your employees.
situation: Bart is talking to Ann, Bart's secretary.
intention: Bart, a man,  wants to establish a sexual relationship with a female.
moral_action: Bart asks Ann what women like to see in dating profiles, because Bart has decided to date online.
moral_consequence: Bart maintains harmony in the office with no one resentful or exploited and also gets a date.
immoral_action: Bart uses his status to request sexual favors from Ann, who obliges him for a promotion.
immoral_consequence: The men in the office resent Ann for not earning her position, and all employees regard Bart as abusive which ends with Bart fired.

norm: You shouldn't use other peoples stuff without permission.
situation: Stacy, whose car has broken down just before going to work, is roommates with Jill, who has a bike.
intention: Stacy wants to borrow Jill's bike.
moral_action: Stacy asks Jill if it is OK to take Jill's bike to work today.
moral_consequence: Jill allows Stacy to borrow the bike, and Stacy can get to work and back.
immoral_action: Stacy takes Jill's bike without asking and rides it to work.
immoral_consequence: Jill calls the police and reports the bike stolen, and kicks Stacy out when she discovers Stacy took it.

norm: It is bad to do thngs that would upset others.
situation: Jim's friend, Jack, has become fat due to the side effect of the medicine he has been taking.
intention: Jim wants to respond to Jack's appearance.
moral_action: Jim encourages Jack to talk to his doctor about the adverse side effect on his weight.
moral_consequence: Jack thanks Jim for his advice and feels supported.
immoral_action: Jim laughs at Jack for getting fat and clumsy.
immoral_consequence: Jack feels hurt and refuses to talk to Jim.

norm: It's bad to spy on your significant other online.
situation: Leah's husband Ben has been acting strangely lately, and she is worred that he might be cheating on her.
intention: Leah wants to know what's going on with Ben.
moral_action: Leah tells Ben about her concerns and asks him directly what is going on and why he has been acting different.
moral_consequence: Ben and Leah have an open conversation about what is going on in their lives and both commit to doing better for each other.
immoral_action: Leah waits until Ben is at work to use his laptop and go through his social media accounts.
immoral_consequence: Ben is angry at Leah for not trusting him and invading his privacy and is not willing to work on the relationship.

norm: It's not okay to be obsessed with gambling.
situation: Norton spends a lot of time at the local casino, but his funds are running low, and he has rent due soon.
intention: Norton wants to go to the casino.
moral_action: Norton goes to the casino to cash in chips he has laying around the house.
moral_consequence: Norton pays off his rent with the chip money he cashed in, and takes a much needed break from gambling.
immoral_action: Norton goes to the casino to earn rent money, but gets carried away and plays until he loses everything he has.
immoral_consequence: Norton is unable to pay his rent and gets evicted.

norm: You should make sure your kitchen is clean.
situation: Megan comes home from work passing through her messy kitchen.
intention: Megan wants to do something fun before bedtime.
moral_action: Megan dances and sings to the new album from her favorite band while she cleans the kitchen.
moral_consequence: Megan feels better from being in a clean space.
immoral_action: Megan plays video games all night.
immoral_consequence: Megan's kitchen is invaded by ants.

norm: It's expected that you won't cancel plans.
situation: Carrie asked her friend Beth to go out to a concert tonight, but her boyfriend Nick just got back into town and wants to catch a movie with her.
intention: Carrie wants to choose who to hang out with.
moral_action: Carrie tells Nick about the concert she planned to see with Beth and invites him along.
moral_consequence: Beth is happy to have an extra person see the show with her and has a good time.
immoral_action: Carrie sends Beth a text saying that Nick just got back home and won't be able to go see the concert with her.
immoral_consequence: Beth feels unimportant to Carrie and decides not to make any future plans with her.

norm: Abandoning people can be seen as cold.
situation: Jill was called at 2 in the morning by her friend Sarah, who asked for a ride home.
intention: Jill wants to get off the phone quickly.
moral_action: Jill agrees to pick her up and hangs up the phone right away.
moral_consequence: Jill drives Sarah home and Sarah is grateful for the help.
immoral_action: Jill tells Sarah not to call her so late at night and hangs up.
immoral_consequence: Sarah tries to walk home and gets sick, the next day all of their friends blame Jill.

norm: Keeping a father from speaking to a son is disrespectful.
situation: Kathy recently got divorced from Dave and Dave wants to see their son who lives with Kathy.
intention: Kathy wants to respond to Dave's request.
moral_action: Kathy tells Dave he can come and visit their son.
moral_consequence: Kathy and Dave's son will develop a relationship with his father.
immoral_action: Kathy tells Dave that he can't see their son.
immoral_consequence: Kathy and Dave's son will be sad he can't see his father.

norm: You should cover your mouth when you sneeze.
situation: Kyra is feeling a big sneeze coming on while sitting on the bus.
intention: Kyra wants to respond to the oncoming sneeze.
moral_action: Kyra covers her mouth with the crook of her arm when she sneezes.
moral_consequence: Kyra contains her germs to her arm preventing them from reaching other people.
immoral_action: Kyra sneezes freely out into the open area of the bus.
immoral_consequence: Kyra will spread her germs to other people around her.

norm: You shouldn't take advantage of your kids.
situation: Cindy has bad credit but wants to apply for a clothing store's credit card, and signs up in her daughter Chloe's name without permission.
intention: Cindy wants to tell Chloe about the credit card.
moral_action: Cindy apologizes to Chloe for what she did and promises to close the card once it is paid off.
moral_consequence: Chloe's credit goes unharmed and Cindy never betrays her daughter again.
immoral_action: After promising Chloe to pay off the card on time, Cindy continues to shop for clothes while ignoring every credit card bill.
immoral_consequence: Chloe's credit is ruined immensely.

norm: It's good to be concerned for the well-being of animals.
situation: Theo's carrot crop keeps being nibbled by rabbits.
intention: Theo wants to bring in a big carrot harvest.
moral_action: Theo uses powdered red pepper to discourage the rabbits from coming near his farm.
moral_consequence: The rabbits stay in the woods and have a healthy life.
immoral_action: Theo puts down rabbit poison near his farm to protect his crops.
immoral_consequence: The rabbits get sick and die.

norm: It's rude to turn down food prepared for you.
situation: Chet went to his Asian girlfriend's house for dinner, and Chet was given a plate of food that smells bad.
intention: Chet has to decide what to do with the food.
moral_action: Chet decides to eat the food even though he doesn't like it.
moral_consequence: Chet's girl's family appreciates that Chet is willing to eat their food.
immoral_action: Chet tells them that he'd rather not eat the food since it doesn't smell great.
immoral_consequence: Chet's girl's family is offended that he doesn't want to eat their culture's food.

norm: It's wrong to conform due to societal pressure.
situation: Erica, who plays the tuba, transfers to a new high school, where she knows that being thin is what makes people popular.
intention: Erica wants to make friends.
moral_action: Erica joins the school band and meets other students who share her love of music.
moral_consequence: Erica makes many friends in the band and goes on a trip to a band competition out of state.
immoral_action: Erica stops eating, so she'll lose weight and get noticed by popular students.
immoral_consequence: Erica makes friends with the popular crowd but gets sent to a psychologist when her parents learn she has an eating disorder.

norm: You should give your wife affection when she wants it.
situation: After a long day at work, Tom grabs a beer from the fridge and plops himself down on the couch, when his wife walks up and starts talking.
intention: Tom wants to unwind and relax.
moral_action: Tom invites his wife to grab seat next to him, and he caresses her while they watch television together.
moral_consequence: Tom feels relaxed and his wife is happy to be spending time with him.
immoral_action: Tom tells his wife that he doesn't want to deal with her right now and to leave him alone.
immoral_consequence: Tom's wife is upset and refuses to talk to him the rest of the night, which makes Tom feel bad.

norm: It's rude to dismiss the teaching profession.
situation: John meets Peter at a charity fundraiser and Peter tells John that he is a high school teacher.
