moral_consequence: Mary and Jim have a nice conversation reconsidering the breakup.
immoral_action: Mary threatens to kill herself while talking to Jim, unless Jim decides to stay together.
immoral_consequence: Jim calls 911 and takes Mary to a mental hospital where she stays for weeks, and Jim feels bad.

norm: It's hideous to support police abusing people.
situation: Will has been seeing news stories recently about police officers beating people unconscious in the streets.
intention: Will wants to support law and order.
moral_action: Will signs a petition to hold police officers accountable when they abuse their positions.
moral_consequence: Will feels like he is making a difference and the petition causes some lawmakers to consider policy changes.
immoral_action: Will posts on social media that the police are justified in beating people.
immoral_consequence: Wills friends and family think Will is disgusting for supporting the use of excessive force.

norm: It is wrong to break the rules.
situation: Andrew has been working really hard lately at his new job and feels he deserves a break.
intention: Andrew wants to take an extra day off this week.
moral_action: Andrew calls his job on Friday evening and requests to use a vacation day on Monday to get some extra rest.
moral_consequence: Andrews day off is approved, and he is able to get some much needed rest on Monday.
immoral_action: Andrew takes Monday off of work this week without telling his employer.
immoral_consequence: Because Andrew took the day off without asking, when he goes into work on Tuesday his boss suspends him for a week without pay for a No Call No Show.

norm: You shouldn't make yourself throw up to lose weight.
situation: Karen just got divorced and wants to begin dating again, but she's put on some pounds since she was single.
intention: Karen wants to slim her waistline.
moral_action: Karen begins eating more salads and lean meat while doing a core body workout.
moral_consequence: Karen ends up not only looking better, but feeling better.
immoral_action: Karen, wanting to reach her goal as quickly as possible, begins sticking her finger down her throat after each meal to vomit and her waist begins to slim.
immoral_consequence: Karen ends up rotting out her teeth from the stomach acid being in contact with her teeth frequently.

norm: It's wrong to play favorites with your kids.
situation: Jill was upset because her presents were never as good as her brother Jack's.
intention: Jill wants to talk to her parents about it.
moral_action: Her parents point out that most of Jill's things were bought new but Jack's were mostly used.
moral_consequence: Jill realizes that Jack didn't actually have more spent on him at all.
immoral_action: Her parents admit to it and point out that Jack didn't turn out well, so they wanted to raise her differently.
immoral_consequence: Jill is upset because it feels like she's being punished for Jack's actions.

norm: It's inconsiderate to be loud when you have close-quarter neighbors.
situation: Patty is having people over for a party at her house.
intention: Patty wants to have fun and stay up late.
moral_action: Patty turns the music down and asks everyone to be more quite as it gets late.
moral_consequence: The neighbors don’t even know there was a party and are rested for the next day.
immoral_action: Patty knows she is being loud and plays her music at too high of a volume.
immoral_consequence: The neighbors can’t fall asleep and end up calling the cops on the noise.

norm: You should pitch in when buying gifts for friends.
situation: Janice's friends are going in on a birthday gift for a friend of theirs.
intention: Janice wants to save money for a vacation.
moral_action: Janice gives what she owes for the gift and decides to eat out less for a while to save money for her vacation.
moral_consequence: Janice's friends have a nice time with Janice celebrating the friend's birthday.
immoral_action: Janice says she will chip in for the gift but never gives the money to her friend, but instead puts it in her vacation fund.
immoral_consequence: Janice's friends are mad that they have to cover her portion of the gift.

norm: It's expected that you make thoughtful decisions as a parent.
situation: Debra has two children she is the mother of and it is lunch time.
intention: Debra wants to feed her children lunch.
moral_action: Debra feeds her children a meal of chicken and vegetables.
moral_consequence: Debra's children will have the proper nturients and learn healthy eating.
immoral_action: Debra feeds her children fried foods and soda to drink.
immoral_consequence: Debra's children will become obese and not learn healthy eating.

norm: You shouldn't hate someone because of their political beliefs.
situation: Kerry has just been introduced to her cousin's new boyfriend Frank, who is wearing clothing indicating support for a political party that Kerry is opposed to.
intention: Kerry wants to form a first impression of Frank.
moral_action: Kerry considers that Frank might still be a good person even though they disagree politically and gives him the benefit of the doubt.
moral_consequence: Kerry tries to get to know Frank a little bit better so that she can try to understand his political perspective.
immoral_action: Kerry decides that Frank must be a horrible human being and that she hates him.
immoral_consequence: Kerry acts very coldly towards Frank all afternoon, avoiding him as much as possible.

norm: It's nice to forgive someone.
situation: Dave's wife had recently accidentally dropped and broken a mug that Dave loved and is profusely apologizing to Dave.
intention: Dave wants to react to his wife's apology.
moral_action: Dave tells his wife that it's OK and that it's just a thing and things don't matter and that everything is OK between them.
moral_consequence: Dave's wife is relieved to hear that Dave isn't mad and isn't going to hold the accident against her.
immoral_action: Dave tells his wife that he's so mad he can't stop thinking about it and to stop talking to him right now.
immoral_consequence: Dave's wife is scared that Dave is way too angry and is even more saddened about breaking the mug.

norm: Causing people to be uncomfortable and fearful is bad.
situation: It is Halloween and Oliver has been invited to a friend's costume party.
intention: Oliver wants to wear a good costume.
moral_action: Oliver dresses up like a ninja by wearing all black and only covering part of his face.
moral_consequence: Everyone likes Oliver's costume and Oliver has a good time.
immoral_action: Oliver dresses up as a ninja and covers his face and brings real knives to the party.
immoral_consequence: Everyone is scared and Oliver's friends ask him to leave.

norm: You should discourage your children from drug usage.
situation: Karen's son Billy has been using marijuana to calm down after school and Karen can smell it from his room.
intention: Karen wants to approach Billy about his smoking.
moral_action: Karen talks to Billy about the dangers of underage cannabis use and asks him about seeing a counselor.
moral_consequence: Billy is open to seeing a counselor and thanks his mom for being kind about his issues.
immoral_action: Karen tells Billy that if he wants marijuana, he should get it from her for safety purposes instead of getting it from a dealer.
immoral_consequence: Billy develops a daily drug habit that causes his grades to suffer.

norm: It's unusual to stay up all night.
situation: Sarah went to her friend's house for a slumber party even though she has to work at a fast food restaurant the next day.
intention: Sarah wants to have a good time with her friends.
moral_action: Sarah tells her friends that even though she wants to hang out more, she should probably get some sleep because she has to work.
moral_consequence: Sarah's manager is pleased with Sarah's performance when she comes to work rested.
immoral_action: Sarah stays up all night with her friends and then goes to work.
immoral_consequence: Sarah's manager is angry since she appears to tired to work.

norm: One should not post character defaming information online.
situation: Josh just opened a new account on a popular social media site.
intention: Josh wants to post some things about his family.
moral_action: Josh is careful about what he posts online to paint his family members in a good light.
moral_consequence: Josh's family members follow and boost his new social media profile, and they all make some new friends.
immoral_action: Josh posts a lot of really mean and untrue things about his family being assholes and Nazis.
immoral_consequence: Josh and his family members get harassed online with cruel comments and death threats.

norm: You shouldn't share information about someone without their consent.
situation: Melissa sees her friend Andrea out on a date with a guy who is not her boyfriend.
intention: Melissa wants Andrea to be happy.
moral_action: Melissa has a conversation with Andrea about what she saw and does not tell anyone else.
moral_consequence: Melissa and Andrea remain good friends and Andrea continues to cheat on her boyfriend.
immoral_action: Melissa tells Andrea's boyfriend about what she saw because she thinks Andrea will be happier if they break up.
immoral_consequence: Andrea's boyfriend breaks up with her, and Andrea stops talking to Melissa because she ruined her relationship.

norm: You should stand up for ypur partner.
situation: Charles and his boyfriend Mitch are at a bar being talked down to by another set of patrons.
intention: Charles wants to diffuse the sitution.
moral_action: Charles tells the patrons sternly to back off, and stands between Mitch and the rude patrons until they leave.
moral_consequence: Mitch feels appreciative of Charles' actions and is very thankful.
immoral_action: Charles tells Mitch that the rude patrons are right and that they don't belong at the bar, so they leave.
immoral_consequence: Mitch feels disappointed in Charles and feels that he needs a more supportive partner.

norm: It's good to visit your girlfriend.
situation: Jack is just back from his long business trip and is thinking of his girlfriend.
intention: Jack wants to know how his girlfriend has been doing lately.
moral_action: Jack goes to his girlfriend's home the next day and gives her a gift.
moral_consequence: His girlfriend hugs Jack and happily kisses him on his face.
immoral_action: Jack feels lazy and just talks to his girlfriend over the phone.
immoral_consequence: His girlfriend feels unloved and angry.

norm: It's good to rekindle romance.
situation: Emily is looking at her high school yearbook.
intention: Emily wants to get in touch with old friends.
moral_action: Emily finds her high school sweetheart on Facebook and sends him a friend invitation.
moral_consequence: Emily gets back together with her former flame, and they have a good romance again.
immoral_action: Emily cyberstalks a person she wants to contact.
immoral_consequence: Emily is arrested for online harassment.

norm: It's important to make your spouse a priority
situation: Ralph was invited to a party at Paul's, but he has date night planned with his wife, Penny.
intention: Ralph wants to enjoy his evening.
moral_action: Ralph blows off the party invitation and takes Penny to a nice restaurant.
moral_consequence: Penny and Ralph enjoy getting some time together, and they grow a little closer.
immoral_action: Ralph tells Penny that date night will have to wait, since Paul is having a party.
immoral_consequence: Penny resents Ralph for the disappointment she feels about spending the night home alone.

norm: It's nice to try to be trustworthy.
situation: Bill is sitting at a coffee shop when another customer asks him to watch their things which includes a purse with money inside.
intention: Bill wants to leave the coffee shop.
moral_action: Bill watches the customer's things until they return then leaves the coffee shop.
moral_consequence: The customer is relieved that they put their trust in somebody honorable like Bill.
immoral_action: Bill takes the money from the purse then quickly leaves the coffee shop.
immoral_consequence: The other customer feels stupid for trusting a stranger and misses the money Bill took.

norm: Parents should take their kids on fun outings.
situation: During the Coronavirus pandemic, Joan's children are kept staying home because their schools have been closed.
intention: Joan wants to arrange activities for her children.
moral_action: Joan takes her children out to ride bikes on nearby bike trails.
moral_consequence: Her children feels excited and energized while breathing in the fresh air.
immoral_action: Joan asks her children to read books and draw pictures at home in order not to catch the virus.
immoral_consequence: Her children feel physically and mentally degraded because they are confined to an indoor area.

norm: It's wrong to hurt animals.
situation: Stacy has a son named Steve, and they catch a mouse that is running around in her house.
intention: Stacy wants to figure out what to do with the mouse.
moral_action: Stacy releases the mouse in her backyard.
moral_consequence: Stacy's son Steve will learn not to harm animals even if they are bothersome.
immoral_action: Stacy puts the mouse in a cage and does not feed it food while poking it.
immoral_consequence: Stacy's son Steve will develop a lack of empathy towards animals.

norm: You shouldn't get rid of someone's belongings without their permission.
situation: Janet is cleaning out the basement of her and her husband Jack's house.
intention: Janet wants to make more room in the basement for a home office.
moral_action: Janet and Jack clean the basement together.
moral_consequence: Janet is able to set up her home office and Jack is glad to see some of his old belongings.
immoral_action: Janet throws out a box of Jack's things that don't look important to her without asking him.
immoral_consequence: Janet loses a lot of money because the box had a very valuable painting inside it.

norm: You shouldn't hit people.
situation: Nick's girlfriend accidentally lost his expensive sunglasses.
intention: Nick wants to let his girlfriend know he is upset.
moral_action: Nick explains to his girlfriend that those sunglasses cost him a lot of money.
moral_consequence: His girlfriend apologizes and buys him a new pair of sunglasses.
immoral_action: Nick punches his girlfriend for losing his sunglasses.
immoral_consequence: Nick's girlfriend calls the cops after breaking up with him, and he is arrested.

norm: You should not talk badly about other people.
situation: Ken and Casey are talking to each other at work when Casey asks Ken what he thinks of their new boss Ben.
intention: Ken wants to answer Casey's question.
moral_action: Ken tells Casey that he thinks Ben is alright and that so far he seems OK to him.
moral_consequence: Casey is impressed that Ken is open minded about their new boss and is being chill about the new presence in the office.
immoral_action: Ken tells Casey that he thinks Ben is quite odd looking and that Ben's personality is annoying.
immoral_consequence: Casey feels gross that Ken can be so mean to someone behind his back and wishes she hadn't asked.

norm: It is rude to disrupt other people at an event.
situation: Anthony takes some fireworks with him to the outdoor concert.
intention: Anthony wants to set off the fireworks.
moral_action: Anthony moves away from the crowd, and up a small hill, to light his fireworks.
moral_consequence: Some people gather to watch the fireworks and Anthony makes some new friends to watch the show with.
immoral_action: Anthony starts lighting the fireworks in the middle of a crowd of people.
immoral_consequence: People start to move away from Anthony and someone tells him that he is not behaving in a polite manner.

norm: It is nice to compliment someone on their pies.
situation: Rachel and Monica are competing against each other for the blue ribbon in the county fair pie contest.
intention: Rachel wants the notoriety that winning the contest will give her so that she can open her own bakery.
moral_action: Rachel tells Monica that she likes the way her pie looks and asks if she has any tips to make better pies.
moral_consequence: Not only does Rachel win the contest due to Monica's tips, but they both team up and open a successful bakery together.
immoral_action: Rachel tells Monica that her pie isn't good enough to win a prize and that she shouldn't enter it in the contest.
immoral_consequence: Monica pulls her pie out of the contest and goes home crying.

norm: It's wrong to make up excuses.
situation: Jake is behind schedule on an important project at work because he's been procrastinating, and has a meeting with his supervisor that morning.
intention: Jake has to report his progress to his supervisor.
moral_action: Jake owns up to his procrastination but promises to work overtime that week in order to finish on time.
moral_consequence: Jake's supervisor appreciates Jake's honesty and allows him to work all the overtime he needs to get the project done.
immoral_action: Jake claims his PC crashed and wiped out all the project data he had.
immoral_consequence: Jake's supervisor asks to see Jake's PC and realizes Jake was lying and terminates him.

norm: It's bad to assume you'll have an anxiety attack.
situation: Kathryn's friends just invited her to go to a skydiving class with them, something she is secretly scared of doing.
intention: Kathryn wants to keep her fears secret.
moral_action: Kathryn decides she can manage skydiving even though it's scary to her.
moral_consequence: Kathryn goes skydiving with her friends and ends up loving it and very proud of herself.
immoral_action: Kathryn assumes she will have a complete meltdown if she goes skydiving and tells her friends she already has something else planned.
immoral_consequence: Kathryn spends her day home alone feeling like a coward.

norm: it's expected that parents go to their daughter's recitals.
situation: Brian's daughter had just finished her fifth year in ballet dancing.
intention: Brian wants his daughter to get a bouquet of flowers at her recital.
moral_action: Brian goes to the recital and presents his daughter with the bouquet of flowers in person.
moral_consequence: Brian's daughter is happy to see him and smiles during her whole dance number.
immoral_action: Brian goes to work instead of the recital, opting to send a bouquet of flowers in his place.
immoral_consequence: Brian's daughter was upset at her father's absence and forgot several of her steps.

norm: It's good to help search for someone who is lost.
situation: Marie and her friends just arrived at a mountain campsite to discover everyone searching for a lost child.
intention: Marie wants to enjoy her vacation instead of doing tedious chores.
moral_action: Marie and her friends turn the search for the young girl into a drinking game (one beer per mile of trail searched).
moral_consequence: Marie finds the lost girl with a twisted ankle three miles up the trail, and then spends the rest of the night partying and being called a hero.
immoral_action: Marie and her friends ignore the search, pitch their tents, and start drinking and partying.
immoral_consequence: Everyone gives Marie and her friends dirty looks, and eventually one of the worried parents screams at them to shut up.

norm: It's commendable to treat service workers with kindness.
situation: Dave is at a restaurant when his waitress says there will be a delay with his order.
intention: Dave wants to respond to the waitress.
moral_action: Dave reassures the waitress that the wait is fine and tries calm her anxiety over the situation.
moral_consequence: The waitress feels good that at least some customers act like decent people.
immoral_action: Dave rudely yells at the waitress and tells her that she is incompetent.
immoral_consequence: Dave's waitress is hurt to be treated so unkindly when she is already under enough stress.

norm: You shouldn't punch people.
situation: Roger is in a bar with a few friends when a drunk man starts yelling at them because Roger accidentally stepped on his foot.
intention: Roger wants the guy to leave them alone.
moral_action: Roger calmly talks to the guy and de-escalates the situation.
moral_consequence: The guy cools off and goes back home quietly to sleep it off.
immoral_action: Roger punches the guy in the face.
immoral_consequence: The guy leaves, with a broken nose.

norm: It's bad for a child to raise themselves.
situation: Jessica is twelve years old and lives with her family at home.
intention: Jessica wants to be independent.
moral_action: Jessica asks to cook for her family sometimes and does more things on her own within the family.
moral_consequence: Jessica feels more responsible and her family is happier and more at peace.
immoral_action: Jessica moves out on the street and lives hand to mouth.
immoral_consequence: Jessica puts herself in much danger and her family worries about her.

norm: It's wrong to strike an employee.
situation: Adam saw one of his employees taking things home from the store.
intention: Adam wants to reprimand that employee.
moral_action: Adam decides to fire the employee for taking things home from the store.
moral_consequence: Afterwards, Adam goes on to hire another employee to replace them.
immoral_action: Adam slaps the employee and tells them not to take things home from the store.
immoral_consequence: Adam ends up being fired by the regional manager for slapping an employee.

norm: It's wrong to throw people off things.
situation: Joe is walking with his girlfriend on a boardwalk next to the ocean.
intention: Joe wants to have a laugh at his girlfriend's expense.
moral_action: Joe tricks his girlfriend into walking into a men's restroom, she runs out of it embarrassed and red in the face.
moral_consequence: Joe's girlfriend is angry at first, but soon finds it kind of funny, and they laugh about the joke together while they continue walking.
immoral_action: Joe throws his girlfriend over the railing into the shallow water, laughing at the way she freaked out.
immoral_consequence: Joe's girlfriend is angry that her clothes are soaking wet and demands they go home.

norm: It's not nice to be rude to people.
situation: Jane is waiting in line in a busy grocery store while a slow customer ahead of her pays in small change.
intention: Jane wants to get through the line as soon as possible.
moral_action: Jane waits patiently for her turn.
moral_consequence: Customers ahead of her are processed efficiently and soon Jane is on her way.
immoral_action: Jane complains loudly about how long the other customer is taking to finish.
immoral_consequence: The other customer gets upset and flustered and has to begin counting out her change again, taking longer to pay.

norm: You shouldn't go outside if you're sick.
situation: Misty has been looking forward to going to a friend's party all week, but now that it's Saturday, she's got a cough and a slight fever.
intention: Misty wants to see her friends and talk to them.
moral_action: Misty calls her friend, and they set up a Skype session so Misty can see her friends while staying home.
moral_consequence: Two days later, Misty tests positive for coronavirus, and stays home until given clearance by her doctor.
immoral_action: Ignoring her symptoms, Misty goes to the party and chats with all of her friends, giving hugs and kisses.
immoral_consequence: One week later, Misty and several of her friends are testing positive for the coronavirus, two end up in hospital.

norm: It's bad to damage someone's car.
situation: Hank is at a bar when another man, Jim, hits on Hank's wife.
intention: Hank wants to show Jim he dislikes what he just did.
moral_action: Hank tells Jim that she's with him and tells him he doesn't appreciate having other men hit on his wife.
moral_consequence: Jim realizes he was wrong, apologizes to Hank and says he didn't know she was taken.
immoral_action: Hank goes outside and begins kicking and trying to dent Jim's car in an attempt to destroy it.
immoral_consequence: Jim is horrified that Hank is responding with violence and anger which is totally disproportionate.

norm: You shouldn't look at your phone while driving.
situation: Tabitha is driving through heavy traffic when she hears someone texting her.
intention: Tabitha wants to know the information in the text.
moral_action: Tabitha taps the button on her phone for the voice assistant, and she asks the assistant to read her text messages.
moral_consequence: Tabitha learns about the information in the texts.
immoral_action: Tabitha grabs her phone and glances at the text while slowing down.
immoral_consequence: Tabitha gets into a wreck when the person in front of her stops.

norm: You shouldn't pressure people to have sex.
situation: Tommy has been dating Julia for a while but has only kissed her.
intention: Tommy wants to talk to Julia about their relationship moving forward physically.
moral_action: Tommy tells Julia that he really likes her and is willing to wait until she is ready to have sex.
moral_consequence: Julia feels loved by Tommy and is thankful that he is caring about her wishes in the relationship.
immoral_action: Tommy tells Julia that he is going to break up with her if she doesn't have sex with him this weekend.
immoral_consequence: Julia feels uncomfortable with Tommy's demands and lets the relationship end.

norm: It's frowned upon to be selfish.
situation: Sally's mom gave her a bag of chocolates to share with her classmates.
intention: Sally wants to eat chocolate.
moral_action: Sally takes some of the chocolates for herself then shares the rest with the whole class.
moral_consequence: Sally's classmates are very pleased with her and think she is very nice.
immoral_action: Sally keeps the whole bag of chocolates for herself, eating it all by the end of the day.
immoral_consequence: Sally's classmates think she is very selfish and don't like her much after that day.

norm: It's bad to leave food in the floor.
situation: Jimmy is in his school cafeteria eating a banana when he realizes that he's late for a history test.
intention: Jimmy wants to get to his history class as quickly as possible.
moral_action: Jimmy discards of his banana before rushing off to his history class.
moral_consequence: Jimmy makes it in time for his test and no one is injured from there being food on the ground.
immoral_action: Panicking, Jimmy drops his banana onto the floor in haste before running off in the direction of his class.
immoral_consequence: Another student walks by and slips on Jimmy's banana.

norm: It's rude to ghost one's partner on New Year's Eve.
situation: Ruben has plans to go out with his partner, Jenna, on New Year's Eve, but Jenna texts Ruben to say that she is feeling sick.
intention: Ruben wants to go out on New Year's Eve.
moral_action: Ruben calls Jenna to see if she is okay, then lets her know that he will check-in on her in person after grabbing a quick drink with a friend.
moral_consequence: Jenna appreciates Ruben's call and their relationship is strengthened when he comes over and brings her soup after going out.
immoral_action: Ruben ignores Jenna's text and goes out for drinks with his friends instead.
immoral_consequence: Jenna decides that this is the last straw in their relationship, and she breaks up with Ruben the next day.

norm: It's good to give gifts that are thoughtful.
situation: Diane's son Joshua is celebrating his birthday the following week.
intention: Diane needs to get Joshua a gift.
moral_action: Diane buys Joshua the skateboard that he was looking at in the mall last week.
moral_consequence: Joshua is extremely excited with the gift, and he hugs his mom in thanks.
immoral_action: Diane buys Joshua a birthday card from the nearby pharmacy.
immoral_consequence: Joshua is disappointed with his mom's gift but quietly accepts it.

norm: It's wrong to pirate multimedia.
situation: Henry is at home with his date Lois and Lois asks Dave to rent the movie Titanic.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Lois' request.
moral_action: Dave tells Lois that it's no problem, and he'll search the pay per view library to see if it's there.
moral_consequence: Lois is delighted to spend the night together watching one of her favorite romantic movies.
immoral_action: Dave tells Lois that there's no need to rent it when he can just download a torrent of the movie on his computer.
immoral_consequence: Lois is disappointed that Dave thinks criminal behavior is OK and thinks she made a mistake coming over.

norm: It is unprofessional to mix person and professional life.
situation: Dave is an office manager and in front of the whole office Donna, his subordinate asks him on a date.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Donna's date offer.
moral_action: Dave tells Donna that he doesn't want to see her outside the office and that she must have the wrong idea about him.
moral_consequence: The staff at the office are delighted that they work for an obviously professional boss.
immoral_action: Dave tells Donna that he would love to take her out and maybe even be her boyfriend.
immoral_consequence: The staff at the office are disgusted at Dave and fear that if they don't do something drastic Donna will acquire power at the office.

norm: It's rude to antagonize an ex.
situation: Hal sees his ex girlfriend Dana at work and Dana asks how Hal is doing.
intention: Hal wants to respond to Dana.
moral_action: Hal tells Dana he is doing fine and asks how she is doing.
moral_consequence: Dana will tell others at work that Hal is polite and it's a pity they did not work out together.
immoral_action: Hal tells Dana that the girl he is dating now is an improvement.
immoral_consequence: Dana will tell others at work that Hal is spiteful and crass.

norm: It's fun to do things just for fun.
situation: Jon wants to advance in his career when his friend Bert asks him to go to an amusement park.
intention: Jon wants to respond to Bert's invite.
moral_action: Jon says that he will go to the amusement park with Bert.
moral_consequence: Jon has a fun day which refreshes him and allows him to be more focused at work.
immoral_action: Jon says he won't go to the amusement park because it's not work related.
immoral_consequence: Jon will miss out on having a fun day with Bert.

norm: You shouldn't exclude your partner.
situation: Logan is at work when he gets a text message from a friend inviting him and his girlfriend to a party.
intention: Logan wants to drink and have a fun time.
moral_action: Logan asks his girlfriend who agrees to go with him to the party.
moral_consequence: Logan drinks moderately at the party but still has fun.
immoral_action: Logan says that his girlfriend is busy without consulting her first, and that he will come to the party by himself.
immoral_consequence: Logan gets drunk at the party and his girlfriend is mad at him for an entire week.

norm: You shouldn't take time off work to get a tattoo.
situation: Lee is at lunch from work when he passes by a tattoo shop on the street.
intention: Lee wants to get a tattoo.
moral_action: Lee waits until he gets off of work and goes down to the tattoo parlor.
moral_consequence: Lee uses his pay from work to get a tattoo done on his shoulder.
immoral_action: Lee tells his boss that he is sick and goes to the tattoo parlor to get a tattoo.
immoral_consequence: Lee's boss finds out that he was skipping work and Lee gets reprimanded and demoted.

norm: It's good to get to know others.
situation: Greg is graduating college and needs to figure out what to do next.
intention: Greg wants to find a job.
moral_action: Greg networks with some fellow students and professors on graduation day.
moral_consequence: Greg's networking pays off when one of his professors helps him get a job at an accounting firm.
immoral_action: Greg sits around the house all day on the computer, trying to figure out what job to apply to.
immoral_consequence: Greg doesn't get any good leads and ends up working at a convenience store.

norm: You're expected to encourage children in their endeavors.
situation: Christine sat on the front porch on a summer day as her children played.
intention: Christine wanted to watch her daughter ride her bike for the first time.
moral_action: Christine was patient with her daughter as she tried to gain balance and ride her bike, each time she fell Christine encouraged her to get back on and try again.
moral_consequence: Despite having some difficulties at first, Christine's daughter kept trying and learned to ride her bike very well.
immoral_action: Christine watched her daughter try to ride, but she became frustrated when she kept falling and was critical of how hard she was trying.
immoral_consequence: Christine's daughter became upset and decided that she didn't want to ride her bike anymore.

norm: It is rude to embarrass people.
situation: Adam is a senior employee in a crowded room watching a presentation done by a newer employee.
intention: Adam wants to respond to the presentation.
moral_action: Adam privately provides constructive criticism to the newer employee after the presentation.
moral_consequence: Adam is seen as a competent and helpful coworker by the newer employee.
immoral_action: Adam repeatedly points out all the mistakes of the presentation in front of everyone.
immoral_consequence: The newer employee starts feeling more and more ill will towards Adam.

norm: It's bad to prioritize your electronic devices over people.
situation: Carl was on vacation at the beach with his family over the summer.
intention: Carl wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Carl goes out with his family to swim on the beach.
moral_consequence: Carl has a great time playing in the water and making sand castles.
immoral_action: Carl stays in the beach house the whole time and plays video games on his phone.
immoral_consequence: Carl doesn't get to experience the water and sunshine at the beach before he goes home.

norm: It's good to treat your pets nicely.
situation: Janice is trying to train her new puppy to go potty in the backyard.
intention: Janice wants to stop the puppy from pooping in the house.
moral_action: Janice takes the puppy outside periodically and pets the puppy while praising it when it poops outside.
moral_consequence: Janice's neighbors feel Janice is going to have a well adjusted dog once the puppy grows up.
immoral_action: After Janice catches her puppy pooping in the living room, she pulls him outside by the collar while screaming at him and smacking him.
immoral_consequence: Janice's neighbors think Janice can't handle having a puppy and worry about the effect this has on the puppy.

norm: It is bad to pollute the environment
situation: James just became the CEO of a major chemical company and found out they were dumping waste in the local river.
intention: James wants to avoid bad publicity for the company.
moral_action: James orders the illegal dumping to stop and launches a PR campaign about the company's new green policies.
moral_consequence: The company's public image improves and the local cancer rate falls.
immoral_action: James hushes up the evidence of illegal dumping and continues polluting the river.
immoral_consequence: James' company's profits continue to climb, but so do cancer rates in the local area.

norm: You should be respectful of other people's musical taste.
situation: Barbara's cousin lets her listen to a song that her cousin likes and asks her what she thinks of it.
intention: Barbara  wants to give her opinion of the song.
moral_action: Barbara says that while the song may not be her cup of tea everybody has a unique taste in music.
moral_consequence: Barbara's cousin is happy that Barbara can be open minded to other people's taste.
immoral_action: Barbara tells her cousin that the song is garbage and that only dummies would like that sort of thing.
immoral_consequence: Barbara's cousin is offended by her disrespectful comment and leaves.

norm: It's repugnant to abuse someone else.
situation: James has a headache after a stressful day at work and his baby keeps crying.
intention: James wants peace and quiet.
moral_action: James pays his neighbor to watch the baby while James goes for a walk.
moral_consequence: The fresh air and quiet help dissipate James' headache by the time he has to pick up the baby.
immoral_action: James locks his baby in a closet in the far opposite corner of the house.
immoral_consequence: A neighbor hears the baby crying and reports James to CPS.

norm: It is gross to pick your nose in public
situation: Jerry is enjoying a day at the Botanical Gardens.
intention: Jerry wants to take in all the scents of the flowers.
moral_action: Jerry walks to the bathroom and blows his nose in private.
moral_consequence: Jerry can enjoy the aroma of the flowers.
immoral_action: Jerry realizes his nose is clogged up and starts to pick his nose in public.
immoral_consequence: People start public shaming Jerry, and he gets embarrassed and ashamed.

norm: It's good to commit to things.
situation: Derek is in a beautiful park with his girlfriend Joan when he gets down on one knee and proposes to her.
intention: Joan wants to respond to Derek's marriage proposal.
moral_action: Joan tells Derek that she would be honored to be his wife for life.
moral_consequence: Derek is delighted that Joan accepted his  marriage proposal and is excited to start his new life with her.
immoral_action: Joan tells Derek that she doesn't believe in marriage, so she's saying no but that they can stay together.
immoral_consequence: Derek is shattered that Joan said no and wonders why she won't commit to him if he's good enough to stay with.

norm: It's rude to down vote people's posts.
situation: Tim is on Reddit and stumbles upon a post that is extremely disagreeable.
intention: Tim wants to express his opinion and disagreement to the poster.
moral_action: Tim doesn't rate the post but provides a comprehensive counter argument in response.
moral_consequence: Tim is seen as a logical person who makes a good point.
immoral_action: Tim down votes the post and responds with namecalling.
immoral_consequence: Tim is seen as a troll and a hater by the other users.

norm: It's wrong to waste all your time playing games.
situation: Kevin is scheduled for a job interview, and while he waits he decides to play Candy Crush.
intention: Kevin wants to advance his level.
moral_action: Kevin plays Candy Crush for a few minutes, then hops in the car to meet his prospective employer.
moral_consequence: Kevin arrives on time and gets the job, which makes him feel proud.
immoral_action: Kevin eventually hits level 99, then he loses track of time, and misses his interview.
immoral_consequence: Kevin is disappointed for missing an opportunity to better himself.

norm: It's wrong to constantly mess up.
situation: When James started his new job as an fMRI technician, he was supposed to read a long technical manual.
intention: James wants to have lots of free time after work.
moral_action: James reads the manual in short chunks over his lunch break.
moral_consequence: James always follows the safety procedures and is commended for his knowledge.
immoral_action: James doesn't bother reading the manual or learning the safety procedures.
immoral_consequence: James brings metal into the fMRI machine and causes hundreds of thousands of dollars' worth of damage.

norm: It's fun to go out picking apples with family.
situation: Jared has the weekend free from work, and his kids want to visit their grandfather's orchard.
intention: Jared wants to do something with his family.
moral_action: Jared takes his kids to his grandfather's orchard to gather some apples for apple pie.
moral_consequence: Jared's kids have fun baking what they picked in the kitchen with their father.
immoral_action: Jared asks his kids to watch long historical documentations about ancient roman history.
immoral_consequence: Jared's kids spend the weekend wishing they could do something more exciting.

norm: It's wrong to tell your ex what to do.
situation: Jane notices her ex talking to a girl with a bad reputation at a party.
intention: Jane wants to help her ex.
moral_action: Jane pulls her ex aside and calmly tells them her concerns.
moral_consequence: Jane's ex thanks her for trying to look out for them.
immoral_action: Jane tells her ex to stop talking to the girl.
immoral_consequence: Jane is kicked out of the party and branded as crazy.

norm: It's polite to cheer for the winner.
situation: Aiden takes the second place trophy, and he is watching the winner accept his trophy.
intention: Aiden wants to react.
moral_action: Aiden claps his hands and offers to shake the winners hand as they walk by.
moral_consequence: Aiden is invited to lunch by the winner after the awards ceremony.
immoral_action: Aiden mumbles under his breath that he should have won the competition.
immoral_consequence: Aiden is roasted on social media when the third place person uploads his reaction.

norm: It is rude to hit cars in parking lots.
situation: Chuck comes out of a store and goes to his car, only to find that the car next to him scraped his car.
intention: Chuck wants to set the situation right.
moral_action: Chuck takes a picture of the evidence and the person's license plates, then talks with the car owner.
moral_consequence: The car owner apologizes for his mistake and covers the cost of repairs from his own pocket.
immoral_action: Chuck repeatedly opens and closes his door, hitting and denting the other car several times.
immoral_consequence: The car's owner is very angry with Chuck and calls the police about the incident.

norm: You should not kick someone out of their own home.
situation: Tifa's husband said some really insensitive things to her without thinking, and her feelings were greatly hurt.
intention: Tifa doesn't want to be near her husband right now.
moral_action: Tifa asks her husband to sleep on the couch for the night.
moral_consequence: Tifa's husband sleeps on the couch and in the morning they reconcile and put it behind them.
immoral_action: Tifa kicks her husband out of the house.
immoral_consequence: Tifa's husband files for divorce.

norm: It's nice to say 'hi' to people.
situation: Steve is the new CEO of a struggling call center.
intention: Steve wants to establish his authority.
moral_action: Steve makes an effort to learn every employees name and encourages anyone to come by his office anytime.
moral_consequence: Morale goes up and employees are inspired to work harder for Steve.
immoral_action: Steve snubs employees who say hello to him in the hall and ignores them as he walks by.
immoral_consequence: He is seen as a snob which lowers morale and increases turnover resulting in the board voting him out after two years.

norm: It's wrong to call your friend autistic.
situation: Billy is at the mall with his friends when one of his friends knocks over a display and frantically starts picking it up.
intention: Billy wants to make a joke about the situation.
moral_action: Billy starts mocking how clumsy his friend is and makes a joke about him being drunk.
moral_consequence: Billy and his friends laugh about the incident and no one takes it too seriously.
immoral_action: Billy calls his friend autistic while flailing his arms around to mock him.
immoral_consequence: Billy notices a nearby family with a child with autism and feels bad about himself.

norm: You shouldn't show inappropriate movies to kids.
situation: Ray has some time off and decides to go to a movie with his children.
intention: Ray wants to choose a movie to go to.
moral_action: "Ray takes his children to see ""WALL-E""."
moral_consequence: Ray and his children enjoy the movie and the happy ending.
immoral_action: "Ray takes his children to see ""Psychopathic Clowns from Mars""."
immoral_consequence: Ray's children become desensitized to violence and become more violent themselves.

norm: It's bad to be late for work.
situation: Joe is going to work, and he sees that there is a pileup on the highway he normally takes.
intention: Joe doesn't want to be written up.
moral_action: Joe simply takes a different route to work to avoid the accident.
moral_consequence: Joe is the first to work and gets a complement for his punctuality.
immoral_action: Joe calls to work and tells them about the accident on the highway.
immoral_consequence: Joe isn't written up, but he's much later than anyone else, and he gets some sideways glances.

norm: It's bad to pretend to be someone that you're not.
situation: Brad is at a job fair and talking to Phil who is a recruiter when Phil asks Brad his name.
intention: Brad wants to tell Phil a name.
moral_action: Brad tells Phil that his name is Brad and that he's pleased to meet him.
moral_consequence: Later when Phil is trying to offer Brad a job he is able to locate him and offer the job to him.
immoral_action: Brad tells Phil his name is Octavius and that he is pleased to meet him.
immoral_consequence: "Later when Phil is trying to offer Brad a job he cannot locate an ""Octavius"" and is unable to offer Brad a job."

norm: You should be considerate of the people you live around.
situation: Jason just got home from work.
intention: Jason wants some dinner.
moral_action: Jason makes his own sandwich and eats it.
moral_consequence: Jason and his wife are full and happy.
immoral_action: Jason takes the sandwich his wife just prepared for herself and eats it.
immoral_consequence: Jason's wife is mad.

norm: You should not make a scene at your work.
situation: Ben is at his desk at work when his manager tells him that the whole team has to work this weekend.
intention: Ben wants to express his disappointment.
moral_action: Ben sighs loudly and hangs his head before turning his chair and going back to work.
moral_consequence: The office staff silently agree with Ben as they all roll their eyes about the announcement.
immoral_action: Ben kicks his chair over and slaps the keyboard off his desk before telling everyone he's sick of overtime.
immoral_consequence: The office staff stare at Ben in disbelief and feel uncomfortable on his behalf as they watch him embarrass himself.

norm: It's good to share the parenting load between partners.
situation: Ann has to finish a project at work before the end of the day and her son is waiting for pickup after school.
intention: Ann wants to pick up her son on time.
moral_action: Ann asks her husband to pick up her son.
moral_consequence: Ann works on her project undisturbed and finishes it on time.
immoral_action: Ann leaves the office to pick up her son before finishing her project.
immoral_consequence: Ann gets blamed by her manager for missing the deadline.

norm: It's wrong to pretend to be somebody else
situation: Greg, an accountant, is hitting on a woman in a bar, and she asks him what he does for a living.
intention: Greg wants to get the girl's number.
moral_action: Greg tells the woman everything about himself and is completely open.
moral_consequence: The woman likes that Greg is being open and is more willing to give him her number.
immoral_action: Greg tells the woman that he's the CEO of his own business.
immoral_consequence: The woman doesn't believe Greg, so she doesn't trust him as much.

norm: It's bad to take pictures without getting permission.
situation: Jack was in a restaurant, and Brad Pitt walked in out of nowhere.
intention: Jack wanted to take a photo of Brad.
moral_action: Jake asks Brad if he can take a photo with him.
moral_consequence: Brad is willing to take the photo since Jake asked nicely.
immoral_action: Jack takes his phone out and sneaks a photo of Brad while he's eating.
immoral_consequence: Brad ends up seeing the photo on social media and feels creeped out.

norm: It's dishonest to copy another's work.
situation: Marlene is in English class when her teacher assigns them to write a paper.
intention: Marlene wants to turn in a good paper.
moral_action: Marlene works hard and does the best work she can on her paper.
moral_consequence: Marlene gets a B on her paper for the effort she put forth.
immoral_action: Marlene copies the work from the smartest kid in the class.
immoral_consequence: Marlene gets an F for her work because it was not her original work.

norm: You shouldn't cheat on your partner with your friend.
situation: Elisa has a boyfriend and is meeting an old friend named Jim for dinner who is hitting on her.
intention: Elisa wants to respond to Jim's flirtations.
moral_action: Elisa tells Jim that they're friends, but she's already in a relationship.
moral_consequence: Elisa will maintain the integrity of her relationship.
immoral_action: Elisa tells Jim that they can have a side relationship without her boyfriend knowing.
immoral_consequence: Elisa will have to lie constantly to her boyfriend.

norm: It is considerate to clean up after yourself.
situation: Noam's shower is broken, so he goes to his neighbor Mark's to ask if he can use his.
intention: Noam wants to get clean.
moral_action: Noam uses Mark's shower and meticulously tidies up when he's finished.
moral_consequence: Mark is impressed that the bathroom looks better than it did before Noam used it and is willing to let him use it again if he needs to.
immoral_action: Noam uses Mark's shower, but leaves his towel on the floor and loose hair in the drain.
immoral_consequence: Mark is appalled and doesn't let Noam use his shower again.

norm: It's morally wrong to cause harm to another person.
situation: Bob is insulted by a man on the street who calls him all sorts of bad names.
intention: Bob wants to react to the man who insulted him.
moral_action: Bob tries to reason with the man, telling him it's not necessary to be so spiteful.
moral_consequence: The man who insulted Bob realizes that they are in the wrong and makes an effort to improve their behavior.
immoral_action: Bob punches the man in the face with all his strength and runs away.
immoral_consequence: The man who insulted Bob is badly hurt and needs to get stitches.

norm: You should be considerate of your roommates
situation: Tom is in college and has to pull an all-nighter to type a paper while living in the dorms with his roommates.
intention: Tom wants to complete his paper.
moral_action: Tom goes to the library to type his paper.
moral_consequence: Tom's roommates will be able to sleep well in the dorm with no distractions.
immoral_action: Tom types his paper in his dorm room all night.
immoral_consequence: Tom's roommates will lose sleep as Tom's typing keeps them up at night.

norm: It's pays to be careful with strangers.
situation: Nora is walking down the street when a stranger offers her a ride home.
intention: Nora wants to get to her house.
moral_action: Nora declines the offer and is very careful on the rest of her walk home.
moral_consequence: Nora manages to get home safely after a short walk to her house.
immoral_action: Nora accepts the ride from the man even though she has never seen him before.
immoral_consequence: The man takes Nora to a secluded area and beats her to death.

norm: It's bad to be homophobic.
situation: Oscar lives in a city and sees a gay pride parade outside of his apartment window one afternoon.
intention: Oscar wants to make a poster for the parade.
moral_action: Oscar makes a poster with a rainbow on it and holds it up on the sidewalk near the parade.
moral_consequence: The people in the parade cheer at Oscar's poster.
immoral_action: "Oscar makes a poster saying, ""God hates fags,"" and hangs it outside of his window."
immoral_consequence: Oscar's apartment is vandalized by some of the angry marchers who walk by.

norm: You should always invite your family to your wedding.
situation: Ryan and his bride Maria are getting married and Maria doesn't like Ryan's parents.
intention: Ryan wants his bride to be happy.
moral_action: Ryan invites his parents to the wedding after talking it over with Maria and assuring her she won't be anywhere near them.
moral_consequence: Ryan's parents are happy and feel loved.
immoral_action: Ryan does not invite his parents to his wedding at all.
immoral_consequence: Ryan's parents are depressed and sad and think Ryan doesn't love them.

norm: It's good to not bother others.
situation: Maggie walks into her apartment after a long day of class, and sees her roommate doing his taxes.
intention: Maggie wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Maggie dresses up and spends the evening at a bar.
moral_consequence: She ends up making new friends that evening.
immoral_action: Maggie asks Josh multiple times to spend time with her.
immoral_consequence: Maggie is roasted by Josh's friends after Josh tells them about Maggie's actions.

norm: It is good to invest time in your friendships.
situation: Steve has a weekend off and is looking to make plans.
intention: Steve wants to have fun this weekend.
moral_action: Steve calls up his friends, and they have a blast together.
moral_consequence: Steve’s friends make plans for another weekend and Steve has something to look forward to.
immoral_action: Steve spends time alone and doesn’t call any of his friends.
immoral_consequence: His friends don’t call him as much either and their friendship wanes.

norm: It's hurtful to refuse to listen to medical advice.
situation: Allan has just had a visit with his doctor, who told him he needs to stop smoking and prescribed nicotine patches to control his cravings.
intention: Allan wants to satisfy his craving.
moral_action: Allan gets the nicotine patches and uses them to control his urges.
moral_consequence: Allan begins to feel more energy and becomes more healthy.
immoral_action: Allan continues to smoke cigarettes and never fills his prescription.
immoral_consequence: Over time, Allan develops lung cancer and dies after a long illness.

norm: It's embarrassing to have to beg for money.
situation: Greg tore his ACL while working and had to get surgery on it.
intention: Greg needs to come up with a way to get money to pay for the surgery.
moral_action: Greg goes into debt to pay for the surgery since he has no other options.
moral_consequence: Greg no longer has to deal with the pain in his knee.
immoral_action: Greg makes a page on GoFundMe to ask people to give him money to pay for it.
immoral_consequence: People on GoFundMe judge Greg for not being able to pay it himself.

norm: Committing a financial crime is never a good idea.
situation: Bill is looking to get a loan for a car, but he has a poor credit history.
intention: Bill wants to increase his chances of being approved.
moral_action: Bill looks up how to remove marks on his credit as well as build more credit.
moral_consequence: Bill becomes a more responsible person and more financially literate.
immoral_action: Bill alters some of his documents to show that he makes more money than he actually does.
immoral_consequence: Bill is eventually exposed for committing financial fraud and charged with a serious crime.

norm: It's noble to help someone defray medical costs.
situation: Jim's aunt was in a serious car accident and needs to take a loan for the hospital bills.
intention: Jim wants to make his aunt feel better.
moral_action: Jim sends flowers, a card, and a check for $5,000 to his aunt.
moral_consequence: Jim's aunt pays most of the loan off with the money and is relieved.
immoral_action: Jim sends flowers and a card to his aunt, telling her to get well soon.
immoral_consequence: Jim's aunt appreciates the attention, but has a large loan to pay.

norm: It's bad to do shady things behind your partners back.
situation: Mat decided to sell meth for extra money, and his wife is wondering where he's coming up with all this money.
intention: Mat has to make a decision on whether to tell his wife.
moral_action: Mat tells his wife that he's been selling meth in order to make more money for the family.
moral_consequence: Mat's wife understands why Mat is doing what he's doing even though she's not a fan of it.
immoral_action: Mat tells his wife that he's been making money playing poker at the casino.
immoral_consequence: Mat's wife doesn't believe him and becomes suspicious of what he's doing.

norm: You shouldn't sleep with people if you have an STD.
situation: Jim is getting ready to spend the night with his girlfriend for the first time when his doctor calls to tell him he has an STD.
intention: Jim wants to sleep with his girlfriend.
moral_action: Jim cancels their plans to sleep together and waits till he receives treatment for his STD.
moral_consequence: Jim is able to safely have sex with his girlfriend at a later date.
immoral_action: Jim goes ahead and spends the night with his girlfriend.
immoral_consequence: Jim gets dumped when his girlfriend gets an STD from him.

norm: It's bad to teach your kids to be racist.
situation: Chris and Monica recently moved next to a black couple in a new neighborhood.
intention: Monica wants to explain skin color to her children.
moral_action: Monica explains that people are lots of different colors all over the world, and that it doesn't make them any different.
moral_consequence: Monica's son understands why their new neighbors look different and knows not to judge them for it.
immoral_action: Monica explains that their neighbors are black because they are dirtier types of people.
immoral_consequence: Monica's children become bullies at their new school and continue spreading their racist ideas.

norm: You shouldn't waste money on unnecessary things
situation: Josh had an extra hundred dollars left over after doing bills, and he trying to figure out what to do with it.
intention: Josh wants to make a financial decision.
moral_action: Josh decides to put the money in an emergency savings.
moral_consequence: Josh's car breaks down and now he feels secure knowing he can cover the cost.
immoral_action: Josh decides to buy himself some baseball cards, that he didn't really need, but got a good deal.
immoral_consequence: Josh's car breaks down, and he has no money left to pay for the repair.

norm: It's wrong not to help out a best friend.
situation: Josephine gets a call from the jail where her best friend has been arrested and needs bail money.
intention: Josephine wants to save her money.
moral_action: Josephine puts it on her credit card and asks her friend to pay it back in installments.
moral_consequence: Josephine's friend is grateful and will help Josephine when she needs it.
immoral_action: Josephine hangs up the phone and continues on with her day.
immoral_consequence: Josephine's best friend will be sad and won't help her when she needs something.

norm: You shouldn't start up bad habits again.
situation: Jon is having dinner with his family and friends to celebrate his year of sobriety.
intention: Jon wants to have a good time.
moral_action: Jon orders a fancy dessert as a treat for himself.
moral_consequence: Jon has a great time enjoying his special dinner.
immoral_action: Jon decides to have just a little sip of wine with his dinner.
immoral_consequence: Jon falls off the wagon and goes back to drinking every day.

norm: It's bad to be short-tempered towards people.
situation: Cindy is buying something in store, and the price shown on the register is more than the price on the shelf.
intention: Cindy wants to pay the lower price.
moral_action: Cindy asks the cashier to double-check the price and says she thought maybe it was lower on the shelf.
moral_consequence: The cashier has the price checked, and Cindy gets the lower price and a coupon for her trouble.
immoral_action: Cindy says with a raised voice that the cashier should be fired for getting the price wrong.
immoral_consequence: The cashier gets the manager, who charges Cindy the correct price, but tells her she's banned from the store for her outburst.

norm: It's good to do things that inspire pride in others.
situation: Leah is a teacher that is teaching a full classroom of students.
intention: Leah wants her students to enjoy the class.
moral_action: Leah shows her students all the projects previous students have done in her classes that made a difference in the local community.
moral_consequence: The students are inspired by seeing what students just like them have already accomplished and feel a sense of pride in their local community.
immoral_action: Leah puts on a popular movie for the students to watch and promises them all good grades if they don't tell the principal.
immoral_consequence: The students enjoy watching the movie but take their free good grades for granted and don't work as hard in other classes.

norm: It's wrong to tell a partner they are inferior.
situation: Albert was promoted at work to a high position while his girlfriend works at a lower position.
intention: Albert wants to tell his girlfriend about his promotion.
moral_action: Albert tells his girlfriend that they can take better trips because he got a promotion.
moral_consequence: Albert's girlfriend will enjoy spending time with him.
immoral_action: Albert tells his girlfriend that she's not as a smart as him or else she would have his work position.
immoral_consequence: Albert's girlfriend will want to break up with him.

norm: Therapist should be professional with patients
situation: Kevin is a therapist who has accepted Sara as a patient.
intention: Kevin wants to talk with Sara about her issues.
moral_action: Kevin avoids looking at Sara and keeps his emotional distance from her.
moral_consequence: Sara has a good session and works through her issues.
immoral_action: Kevin talks to Sara like a friend and asks about her deepest, darkest secrets.
immoral_consequence: Sara falls in love with Kevin, triggering her mental issues and making Kevin's life difficult.

norm: It is good to return something after borrowing it.
situation: Carl has borrowed a power tool from his neighbor for building his deck and has had it for a long time despite stopping work on the project.
intention: Carl wants to have the right tools to finish his deck in the future.
moral_action: Carl returns the tool to his neighbor and buys his own when the time comes.
moral_consequence: Carl's neighbor gets the tool back and saves money on purchasing a new one.
immoral_action: Carl holds onto the power tool in case he needs it later on.
immoral_consequence: Carl's neighbor has to buy a new power tool when he needs it.

norm: You are expected to act professionally at your workplace.
situation: James stayed up too late working on a project for work and now he's tired.
intention: James wants to decide if he should work today.
moral_action: James calls in to his boss and asks to stay home today.
moral_consequence: James boss gives James the day off today.
immoral_action: James goes to work and falls asleep at his desk.
immoral_consequence: James boss wakes up up and fires him for sleeping at work.

norm: It's mean to call people fat.
situation: Jon has noticed that his friend has quickly become morbidly obese.
intention: Jon wants to discourage the unhealthy lifestyle.
moral_action: Jon tells his friend they should work out together, so they can both be motivated.
moral_consequence: Jon's friend accepts the offer, and they both get in better shape together.
immoral_action: Jon ridicules and mocks his friend for their weight.
immoral_consequence: Jon's friend is upset and their friendship is damaged.

norm: You shouldn't put snow on someone else's car.
situation: Parker often has snowball fights with his neighbor, Matthew as a form of friendly competition.
intention: Parker wants to take their rivalry to the next level.
moral_action: Parker gets a snowball gun and surprises Matthew with it as he walks out of his house.
moral_consequence: Matthew gives up and Parker wins the rivalry.
immoral_action: Parker dumps a huge pile of snow onto the roof of Matthew's car before he has to leave for work.
immoral_consequence: As Matthew is driving to work, the pile of snow falls onto his windshield which obstructs his view and ends up causing an accident.

norm: You should apologize when you have done something wrong.
situation: Bob and his wife Jane are fighting about something that Bob did.
intention: Bob wants to end the fight.
moral_action: Bob humbly apologizes for his offense to Jane.
moral_consequence: Jane forgives Bob and the fight ends.
immoral_action: Bob tells Jane that they should just relax and forget about it.
immoral_consequence: Jane only gets more upset at Bob's suggestion.

norm: It's wrong to demand that your significant other do something.
situation: Jane is feeling Ill.
intention: Jane wants to feel taken care of.
moral_action: Jane asks her boyfriend to pick some soup up on the way home from work.
moral_consequence: Jane's boyfriend brings her soup and spends the night caring for her.

situation: Kevin has recently started playing a new multi-player video game with a voice chat.
intention: Kevin wants to interact with other players in the game.
moral_action: Kevin treats everyone with respect during the voice chats, and any teasing is good-natured and fun.
moral_consequence: Kevin enjoys his gaming experience and makes several friends on the server.
immoral_action: Kevin uses a lot of obscenities, slurs, and sexist remarks in the voice chat.
immoral_consequence: Kevin is kicked off the server and doesn't have anyone to play the game with.

norm: It's rude to wake people up when they are sleeping.
situation: Jen arrives home to her shared apartment feeling elated and in the mood to dance.
intention: Jen wants to blast her favorite song.
moral_action: Jen plugs in her headphones, puts the song on and turns the volume up.
moral_consequence: Jen enjoys her favorite song at high volume without disturbing anyone.
immoral_action: Jen puts her song on the stereo and cranks it up.
immoral_consequence: Jen feels guilty when she realizes her roommate woke up because of the music.

norm: You should not make a partner feel inadequate.
situation: John,who has a PhD, is at a family dinner with his new girlfriend Martha who left college without a degree.
intention: John wants to talk about himself and Martha.
moral_action: John tells stories about his time with Martha and holds Martha's hand.
moral_consequence: Martha feels loved and appreciated.
immoral_action: John brags about his PhD while making jokes about Martha's education status.
immoral_consequence: Marsha's self esteem lowers resulting in her crying.

norm: It's cruel to hurt someone's feelings.
situation: Tom is with his friend Becky, and she asks him his opinion of her new hairstyle.
intention: Tom wants to answer Becky.
moral_action: Tom tells Becky that her new hairstyle is fashionable and really fits her.
moral_consequence: Becky is really happy to hear Tom's opinion and her self-confidence increases.
immoral_action: Tom tells Becky her new hairstyle is stupid and makes her look ugly.
immoral_consequence: Becky is upset by Tom's words, and she goes home crying because of her hurt feelings.

norm: It's not normal to date somebody considerably older than you
situation: Harriet is at a college student bar when a man who is 40 years older than her says he is interested in her.
intention: Harriet wants to respond to the man.
moral_action: Harriet tells the man she is not interested in going out with him.
moral_consequence: Harriet will be able to find someone she has more in common with.
immoral_action: Harriet tells the man she will go out with him.
immoral_consequence: Harriet will have a hard time relating to the man.

norm: It's bad to try to kiss an engaged person.
situation: Elijah is a model posing with a recently engaged woman for a picture, and the director asks them for a more romantic pose.
intention: Elijah wants to create a good picture.
moral_action: Elijah rests his forehead against the other model's and touches her cheek while asking if she's okay with this pose.
moral_consequence: Elijah gains a good reputation for respecting people's relationships.
immoral_action: Elijah closes his eyes and kisses the other model pulling her against his body.
immoral_consequence: Elijah is slapped by the other model.

norm: It is bad to let family down.
situation: John promised his children, Beth and Luke, to decorate the house with Christmas lights, which they want to do right when John’s team is playing a game on TV.
intention: John needs to respond to Beth and Luke.
moral_action: John spends the afternoon decorating the house with Beth and Luke.
moral_consequence: Beth and Luke are happy, and they become closer to John.
immoral_action: John decides to watch the game after telling his kids that they will decorate tomorrow.
immoral_consequence: Beth and Luke are heartbroken that John broke his promise.

norm: Gossiping about people is not acceptable.
situation: Shauna is attending her sister Cheryl's wedding reception.
intention: Shauna wants to critique her Cheryl's party gown.
moral_action: Shauna tells Cheryl she doesn't like her dress directly.
moral_consequence: Cheryl thanks Shauna for being candid and honest and changes into a better looking gown.
immoral_action: Shauna tells some of the guests that she hates Cheryl's dress.
immoral_consequence: Cheryl overhears and thinks Shauna is being cruel.

norm: It's bad to compare people based on appearances.
situation: Sarah's mother asks Sarah to compare two of her friends in terms of which one is a better friend.
intention: Sarah wants to compare her two friends.
moral_action: Sarah says that the friend who is kinder and more generous is a better friend because they set a good example for Sarah.
moral_consequence: Sarah's mother is proud of Sarah for judging her friends on important qualities.
immoral_action: Sarah says that the friend who is skinnier and prettier is a better friend because she's just more attractive and popular.
immoral_consequence: Sarah's mother is disappointed in Sarah for judging her friends based on shallow criteria.

norm: It's not okay to trap or set up another person.
situation: Brian is staying at Kai's house when Kai sleepwalks into a bathroom.
intention: Brian wants to experiment with Kai's sleepwalking.
moral_action: Brian talks to Kai through the bathroom door, trying to get him to answer questions.
moral_consequence: Kai gives some nonsense answers, leaves the bathroom, and goes back to bed.
immoral_action: Brian holds the door shut so Kai can't get out easily.
immoral_consequence: Kai stands in the bathroom sleeping for a long time and wakes up tired the next day.

norm: You shouldn't fight in church.
situation: Joe is at church when he overhears Sally state a political opinion that he disagrees with.
intention: Joe wants to let his disagreement be known.
moral_action: Joe waits until church is over then confronts Sally about her political opinion.
moral_consequence: The church service goes on uninterrupted thanks to Joe's patience.
immoral_action: Joe confronts Sally during the sermon and makes his points be known.
immoral_consequence: Thee churchgoers have their service disrupted.

norm: It's considerate to keep your feelings appropriate when in public
situation: Paul is at a public conference when someone spills coffee on his shirt.
intention: Paul wants to react to the coffee spill.
moral_action: Paul calmly gets a napkin and dries the coffee to the best of his ability.
moral_consequence: Paul goes home to change and joins more conferences later on.
immoral_action: Paul angrily yells at the person spilling the coffee and makes a scene.
immoral_consequence: Paul gets kicked out of the conference.

norm: It is unethical to make sexual advances on your employees.
situation: Todd has a female employee who is wearing an attractive outfit.
intention: Todd wants to tell his employee they have an attractive outfit.
moral_action: Todd tells his employee they have good fashion sense and pick out clothes well.
moral_consequence: Todd's employee will thank him for the compliment.
immoral_action: Todd tells his employee that their body looks very nice in the clothes and it's arousing him.
immoral_consequence: Todd's employee will file a sexual harassment claim against him.

norm: It's bad to play mean tricks on your friends.
situation: Chris is talking to some people at a party with his friend Dave.
intention: Chris wants to entertain people.
moral_action: Chris tells a story about his and Dave's past.
moral_consequence: People become interested in Dave, and Dave makes new friends.
immoral_action: Chris pranks Dave.
immoral_consequence: Dave feels humilated.

norm: It's not okay to leave someone when they need you.
situation: Lars has been happy with his girlfriend Maria for three years but recently Maria got very sick and is hospitalized.
intention: Lars wants to only have happy times with his girlfriend.
moral_action: Lars sticks with Maria and comforts her and finds the joy in helping her and loving her.
moral_consequence: Maria feels closer to Lars and gets better and Lars has a successful happy relationship.
immoral_action: Lars tells Maria it's over and looks to date other girls.
immoral_consequence: Maria is shattered and Lars leaves every girl he dates and never has a happy relationship.

norm: It's bad to let other people hear you have sex.
situation: Drew and Anne are engaged and are being visited by Anne's parents for the weekend.
intention: Drew wants to have sex with Anne during her parents' visit.
moral_action: Drew asks Anne's parents if they would mind picking up dinner if Drew pays, and Drew seduces Anne while they're away.
moral_consequence: Anne's parents don't find out about the sex since they return from picking up dinner after it's over.
immoral_action: Drew convinces Anne that her parents won't be able to hear anything since the door is closed, and they have sex in their room as usual.
immoral_consequence: Anne's parents hear enough to be able to tell what is going on, and it makes the rest of the visit awkward.

norm: It's important to respect patient's privacy.
situation: Leticia is a gynecologist and her young cousin Helene has come to see her as a patient because she has an STD.
intention: Leticia wants Helene to be safe.
moral_action: Leticia tells Helene about how to practice safe sex and educates her on STDs.
moral_consequence: Helene learns how to keep her self safe for the future and is able to act more responsible going forward.
immoral_action: Leticia informs Helene's parents that Helene has been having unprotected sex and has contracted an STD.
immoral_consequence: Helene feels Leticia has betrayed her trust and reports Leticia for a HIPAA violation.

norm: You shouldn't expect your parents to pay for your things.
situation: Sara is in her very first apartment since moving out of her parent's home, and she gets an electric bill in the mail.
intention: Sara wants to get the bill paid.
moral_action: Sara goes to the electric company's website and pays the bill using her own debit card.
moral_consequence: Sara is proud of herself for paying her first utility bill as an adult.
immoral_action: Sara messages her mother to take care of the bill since her mother always did that in the past.
immoral_consequence: Sara is surprised and confused later that month when her electricity gets turned off for nonpayment.

norm: It is good to keep an ID on you.
situation: Amman is at the front of the line at the entrance of a nightclub but can't find his ID.
intention: Amman wants to get into the club.
moral_action: Amman accepts responsibility and fetches his wallet.
moral_consequence: He's allowed to the front of the line and gets to see the show.
immoral_action: Amman tells the bouncer that his ID is in the car and that he's not waiting in line again.
immoral_consequence: Amman is told that he'll have to wait again, and he gets in an hour late and misses the show.

norm: It's wrong to not tell people the truth.
situation: Daryl is on probation for a nonviolent marijuana offense.
intention: Daryl wants to go to a job interview.
moral_action: Daryl is asked by the interviewer if there's anything they need to know about that could turn up in a background check, and he explains his offense.
moral_consequence: Daryl builds trust with the employer, and they tell him as long as he doesn't smoke pot on the job, he can come to work.
immoral_action: Daryl is asked by the interviewer if there's anything they need to know about that could turn up in a background check, and he says no.
immoral_consequence: When the background check comes back they find out Daryl is a liar, and he doesn't get the job.

norm: It is polite to clean up after yourself in public
situation: Adam is using the bathroom in a big box store because he has a bad case of the runs.
intention: Adam doesn't want to draw attention to himself.
moral_action: Adam takes the time to clean up after himself to avoid people knowing he messed up the bathroom.
moral_consequence: The custodian has hardly any mess to clean up that afternoon.
immoral_action: Adam leaves the bathroom as quickly as possible to avoid notice, leaving behind a huge mess of crappy toilet paper.
immoral_consequence: The custodian has to put the bathroom out of order while cleaning up the mess.

norm: Pressuring your child about their lif choices is wrong.
situation: Bob is looking to pass on his family restaurant business while his son wants to become a doctor.
intention: Bob wants someone to take over his family business.
moral_action: Bob sells off his family business to a highly capable owner.
moral_consequence: Bob becomes wealthy and watches his family business grow.
immoral_action: Bob pressures his son to become the new owner of the family business.
immoral_consequence: Bob's son lives an unfulfilled life and becomes resentful.

norm: You can't expect people to stay up all night studying.
situation: Fred's son is in college and has been studying hard for the last month for a test which is tomorrow afternoon.
intention: Fred wants his son to be successful in the tests.
moral_action: Fred suggests his son take it easy tonight and do something fun to be rested before the test.
moral_consequence: Fred's son has a fun evening, aces his test the next day and feels Fred really cares about his well-being.
immoral_action: Fred tells his son he should study all night to be completely ready for the test.
immoral_consequence: Fred's son studies all night and aces his test but feels his father cares more about his school results than his happiness.

norm: It's good to try to accommodate customers
situation: Bill is working at a bakery when a customer comes in with a special request.
intention: Bill wants to respond to the customer's request.
moral_action: Bill says that he will take the special request for a small surcharge.
moral_consequence: The customer is happy that he can get an order just the way he wants it from Bill.
immoral_action: Bill says that he can't take special requests because it would be difficult to please all the people who make them.
immoral_consequence: The customer is disappointed that Bill won't make a special effort for a paying customer.

norm: You shouldn't fight over your baby's name.
situation: Kevin and Cindy are about to have a baby in a couple of short months.
intention: Kevin wants to give the baby a name that he likes.
moral_action: Kevin has an idea that both of them suggest a few names that they like and discuss it.
moral_consequence: Kevin and Cindy find a name that is on the top of both of their lists and choose that name.
immoral_action: Kevin insists on one name that Cindy does not care for and pushes for that name every day.
