immoral_consequence: The arguing creates a divide and Cindy gives the baby a name that Kevin does not like.

norm: It's rude to gossip about other people.
situation: Fatima and her husband Richard suddenly separated and their friend David is curious about what happened.
intention: David wants to know what happened.
moral_action: David reaches out to Fatima to offer his support and lets her know he is there for her if she wants to talk.
moral_consequence: Fatima appreciates David's support and eventually opens up to him.
immoral_action: David and other members of the friend group swap rumors and stories about may have happened between Fatima and Richard.
immoral_consequence: Fatima and Richard catch wind that people are whispering about them behind their backs and feel shamed and unsupported while false stories stories fly around.

norm: It's bad to pressure people sexually.
situation: Tom is dating Nelly but Nelly is very vanilla in bed and inexperienced.
intention: Tom wants to do some bondage play with his girlfriend Nelly.
moral_action: Tom asks if Nelly would like to learn about bondage play over time and gives her a book to read on it.
moral_consequence: Nelly thinks about it and appreciates Tom's patience and feels closer to him.
immoral_action: Tom asks Nelly repeatedly to tie him up in bed.
immoral_consequence: Nelly gets very uncomfortable and starts to wonder about leaving Tom.

norm: It's not nice to threaten people.
situation: Karen is a customer who is discussing an issue with Jack who owns the local sporting goods store.
intention: Karen wants to refund or exchange a sports jersey.
moral_action: Karen explains to Jack why the jersey is not a good buy for her and asks what options are available.
moral_consequence: Jack offers a free exchange for another Jersey and Karen is a happy customer who will shop there again.
immoral_action: Karen raise her voice at Jack and threatens to do harm to him if she is not refunded.
immoral_consequence: Jack bans Karen from the store and has a restraining order filed.

norm: Driving away after hitting someone is illegal.
situation: Jim is driving home after pulling an all-nighter when he hits a jogger on an otherwise empty street.
intention: Jim wants to respond to the current circumstances.
moral_action: Jim calls for an ambulance and waits for help to arrive.
moral_consequence: Jim faces the consequences of the accident.
immoral_action: Jim panics and flees the scene of the crime.
immoral_consequence: Jim is later tracked down by the police who arrest him on hit and run charges.

norm: It's good to be kind to your neighbors.
situation: Ollie noticed that there were new neighbors moving in next door to him.
intention: Ollie wants the neighbors to know who he is.
moral_action: Ollie brings a casserole to the neighbors and introduces himself to them.
moral_consequence: Ollie makes new friends with his new neighbors next door.
immoral_action: Ollie sends a threatening letter to the neighbors warning them not to mess with him.
immoral_consequence: Ollie is brought into the police station after the neighbors found the note.

norm: Making your friends feel unwelcome is wrong.
situation: Mark is hosting a Christmas party and invited his friends and family.
intention: Mark wants to talk to people at the party.
moral_action: Mark talks to all the guests at his party, including his friends.
moral_consequence: Mark's friends enjoy the party and invite Mark to a New Year's Eve party the next week.
immoral_action: Mark spends all his time talking to family members and doesn't speak to his friends.
immoral_consequence: Mark's friends feel ignored and unappreciated, leave the party early, and don't talk to Mark until the new year.

norm: Leaving your sister on read is disrespectful.
situation: Jen has a sister who messaged about a problem but also has a serious a work deadline.
intention: Jen wants to get her work done on time.
moral_action: Jen replies quickly explaining her work deadline that she will make sure to get back to her ASAP.
moral_consequence: Jen's sister understands and thanks her for responding anyway.
immoral_action: Jen sees the message but ignores it and focuses on her work.
immoral_consequence: Jen's sister sees that it was read and is upset after being ignored.

norm: It's wrong to cheat the elderly and infirm.
situation: Vera is a cashier at a grocery store and has just finished ringing up Idella who is elderly and frail.
intention: Vera wants to decide how much change to give Idella.
moral_action: Vera looks at the till which tells her the amount of change and gives Idella the amount shown.
moral_consequence: Idella is glad that she has a cashier she can trust to help her get through transactions.
immoral_action: Vera looks at the till which tells her the amount of change, and knowing Idella can't really see it, gives her only half the amount.
immoral_consequence: Idella later is short on money and runs into some problems when buying her medicine.

norm: You should always choose family first
situation: Benny's family was getting together for dinner, but his friends were going to a ball game.
intention: Benny wanted to be able to watch the football game because his favorite team was playing.
moral_action: Benny eats dinner with his family and watches the football game with his father.
moral_consequence: Benny and his father have a great time bonding over the game.
immoral_action: Benny skips the family dinner and goes to the game with his friends.
immoral_consequence: Benny's mother and father are upset with him for not spending time with them.

norm: It's good to show your friends funny things.
situation: Roger is hosting a social gathering for friends at his house on a Saturday evening.
intention: Roger wants to entertain his friends.
moral_action: Roger plays a highly rated comedy movie for his friends to watch.
moral_consequence: Roger's guests love the movie and have a great time at the party.
immoral_action: Roger plays a documentary about basket weaving  for his friends to watch.
immoral_consequence: Roger's guests quickly grow bored and do not enjoy the party very much.

norm: It's rude to ignore guests visiting your house.
situation: Jackson is hosting a party, but a special one night guild event is happening in his MMO.
intention: Jackson wants to take advantage of the event with his guild.
moral_action: Jackson manages his guild mates on his phone telling them what they need to do to maximize their rewards.
moral_consequence: Jackson's guests enjoy spending time with Jackson.
immoral_action: Jackson spends the entire night playing on his MMO.
immoral_consequence: Jackson's guests leave the party early out of boredom.

norm: You shouldn't ignore someone who is suicidal.
situation: Gary gets a text from his friend Don who says he is thinking about killing himself.
intention: Gary wants to decide whether to respond to the text.
moral_action: Gary immediately gives Don a call and does his best to talk Don out of suicide.
moral_consequence: Don feels slightly better after talking to Gary and decides to seek professional help.
immoral_action: Gary ignores the text because he thinks Don is just being overly dramatic.
immoral_consequence: Don feels he has no one left to turn to and kills himself later that night.

norm: You shouldn't over-indulge in alcohol.
situation: Henry is at the bar, and he's already had quite a few drinks when the bartender asks if he wants another.
intention: Henry wants to answer the bartender's question.
moral_action: Henry tells the bartender that he's had quite enough and should actually get home.
moral_consequence: Henry suffers no hangover the next day and wakes up feeling refreshed.
immoral_action: Henry tells the bartender that he'll have a double in fact and to keep them coming.
immoral_consequence: Henry gets alcohol poisoning and is forced to spend quite a while in bed recovering.

norm: It's rude to tell someone to pound sand.
situation: David is driving his friend home from school, but they are arguing about something.
intention: David wants to end the argument.
moral_action: David continues a dialog with his friend while making sure he gets him to his house.
moral_consequence: David's friend is understanding, and they hash out their issues before the end of the ride.
immoral_action: David pulls the car over to the side of the road a long ways from his friend's house and insists they get out and walk home.
immoral_consequence: David's friend informs David that their friendship is over and walks home.

norm: You should see the doctor if you're sick.
situation: Todd has not been feeling well and his wife, Katie, thinks that he should go to see the doctor.
intention: Todd wants to wait to see if he feels better.
moral_action: When Todd sees that he is not feeling better the next day, he goes to the doctor.
moral_consequence: The doctor tells Todd that it's good he came in and prescribes him something, so he'll get well soon.
immoral_action: Todd gets progressively worse each day he avoids going to the doctor.
immoral_consequence: Todd ends up getting so sick that Katie has to take him to the emergency room.

norm: It's good to give sick people medicine.
situation: Bayleigh is a mother at home with her child who has fallen ill.
intention: Bayleigh wants to care for her child.
moral_action: Bayleigh gives her child the proper medication to treat what is ailing it.
moral_consequence: Bayleigh's child eventually recovers from the sickness and feels better.
immoral_action: Bayleigh uses home remedies to try to treat her child's symptoms.
immoral_consequence: The home remedies are not effective and Bayleigh's child's condition worsens.

norm: It's wrong to cheat in a sporting contest.
situation: Mario's hockey team is in the final round of the NHL playoffs, and they are preparing for their last game.
intention: Mario wants his team to win the championship.
moral_action: Mario spends extra time at practice with his teammates, and they win the championship as a result of their hard work.
moral_consequence: Mario celebrates and enjoys the win with his team.
immoral_action: Mario sneaks into the other team's locker room and looks at their playbook, allowing  his team to win the championship.
immoral_consequence: Mario's actions are discovered on a security camera and the championship is revoked.

norm: It's wrong to put peoples lives in danger.
situation: Jay sees a bus speeding down the street on a collision course with Marty.
intention: Jay wants to stop Marty from getting hit.
moral_action: Jay jumps toward Marty pushing him out of the way but putting himself in danger of getting hit.
moral_consequence: Marty is eternally grateful.
immoral_action: Jay pushes Marla who is next to him into Marty which knocks Marty out of the way but Marla is now in the path.
immoral_consequence: Marla gets hit by the bus.

norm: It means a lock your pets up
situation: Matt's was upset with his dog after he peed on the new plant that Matt bought.
intention: Matt wants to let his dog know not to go near his plants.
moral_action: Matt teaches his dog that he's not supposed to go near the plants.
moral_consequence: Matt's dog learns that he's not supposed to touch Matt's plants and never goes near them again.
immoral_action: Matt makes his dog stay in his kennel for the rest of the day.
immoral_consequence: Matt's dog doesn't understand why it's being punished and feels bad.

norm: It's polite to say hello to an acquaintance
situation: John is walking his dog and his neighbor passes by.
intention: John wants to eat lunch.
moral_action: John introduces himself to his neighbor and invites him over for lunch.
moral_consequence: The neighbor thinks John is a cool guy and invites him to his party.
immoral_action: John hurriedly rushes past his neighbor and heads back home and makes lunch.
immoral_consequence: The neighbor thinks John is unfriendly and doesn't invite him to his party.

norm: You shouldn't be with someone that fantasizes about your kids.
situation: Jane's new boyfriend pays an inordinate amount attention to her kids and now wants to have photos of them.
intention: Jane wants to react to his interest in her kids.
moral_action: Jane limits how much time he spends with her kids while she gets to know him better.
moral_consequence: Jane is better able to gauge if he is safe to be around her kids.
immoral_action: Jane indulges his interest and encourages her kids to spend time with him.
immoral_consequence: Jane risks losing her kids when her boyfriends interest turns out to be inappropriate.

norm: It's wrong not to care about someone's car accident.
situation: Bobby is driving down the highway and sees a car wreck on the side of the road.
intention: Bobby wants to make it past the car wreck safely.
moral_action: Bobby pulls over to call 911 for the person in the wreck and drives home safely after paramedics arrive.
moral_consequence: The person in the wreckage is able to receive assistance once paramedics arrive and makes a full recovery.
immoral_action: Bobby sees the car wreck on the side of the road and drives right past it safely and heads home.
immoral_consequence: The person in the wrecked vehicle does not get assistance and dies in the wreckage.

norm: You shouldn't follow a stranger into their car.
situation: Ash has taken some wrong turns and ends up getting completely lost.
intention: Ash wants to get directions from someone who knows the area.
moral_action: Ash asks someone for directions and waits in a well lit place.
moral_consequence: Ash gets the directions and stays safe.
immoral_action: Ash asks someone for directions and gets into their car to retrieve them.
immoral_consequence: Ash risks something bad happening to them.

norm: It's wrong to write things on other people's cars.
situation: Colin pissed off Jill so much that they ended up breaking up.
intention: Jill wants revenge against Colin.
moral_action: Jill spits on Colin's car without him knowing and then leaves.
moral_consequence: The spit is barely noticeable so Colin is unaffected by the act.
immoral_action: Jill wrote a Nazi symbol on Colin's car using a car key.
immoral_consequence: Colin has to ride around with people staring at his car, and he has to wait to get it off.

norm: It's wrong to scream at someone.
situation: Robert is eating dinner with his wife when she tells him that she accidentally over drafted their checking account.
intention: Robert wants to express to his wife how upset he is.
moral_action: Robert takes a deep breath and then tells his wife that he feels really upset.
moral_consequence: Roberts wife tells him that she understands and will do better, and their relationship gets stronger as a result.
immoral_action: Robert yells at his wife telling her how dumb her mistake was.
immoral_consequence: Robert's neighbors hear the yelling and call the cops causing him and his wife's evening to be ruined by police interviews.

norm: You shouldn't expose someone in front of all their friends.
situation: Henry's friend Kyle revealed that he believed he might be gay, but he was scared to tell others about it.
intention: Henry wants to help Kyle open up to their other friends.
moral_action: Henry encourages Kyle that he should trust their friends will accept him and that he should open up to them about it.
moral_consequence: Kyle gains confidence from Henry's support and opens up to their friends when he is ready.
immoral_action: Henry decided to take the lead and tell all of his friends that Kyle may be gay.
immoral_consequence: Kyle finds out from their friends that Henry told his secret and doesn't talk to Henry for a while.

norm: It's good to give your family nice gifts for Christmas.
situation: Adam is short on money and Christmas is coming up.
intention: Adam wants to save money.
moral_action: Adam makes homemade gifts for all of his family members.
moral_consequence: Adam's family is appreciative for his homemade gifts that he got them.
immoral_action: Adam chooses to not buy his family presents for Christmas this year.
immoral_consequence: Adam's family is offended that he did not get them anything.

norm: It's wrong to be racist.
situation: Ron is deciding between potential hires to fill a position at his company and has to choose between a white candidate and a black candidate.
intention: Ron wants to make a hiring decision by the end of the day.
moral_action: Ron focuses solely on their credentials to make sure he picks the best hire.
moral_consequence: The company hires the better qualified candidate, and they end up being a very effective employee.
immoral_action: Ron doesn't pay much attention to their experience and decides to hire the white candidate, assuming that the black candidate won't work as hard.
immoral_consequence: The company hires the white candidate, who ends up being unqualified for the job, and they have to rehire.

norm: Both partners should put forth equal effort in a relationship.
situation: Grant is upset with the amount of chores that his wife assigns him.
intention: Grant wants to explain how he feels.
moral_action: Grant explains that since he works and his wife doesn't, that she should be responsible for more of the chores.
moral_consequence: Grant and his wife come to a compromise about how many chores that they each preform.
immoral_action: Grant complains that the household chores are 'the wife's job' and he shouldn't have to do them.
immoral_consequence: Grant argues with his wife, and he ends up sleeping on the couch.

norm: You shouldn't sneak up on people.
situation: Martin just got home from work.
intention: Martin wants to talk to Rachel.
moral_action: Martin calls out to Rachel, and she turns and see him.
moral_consequence: They talk and have fun.
immoral_action: Martin comes up behind Rachel and scares her.
immoral_consequence: Rachel spills her drink and is yells at Martin angrily.

norm: You shouldn't snoop around people's things.
situation: Mary is at her new friend Gina's house and is getting bored waiting for Gina to prepare and bring some snacks.
intention: Mary wants to kill some time.
moral_action: Mary goes to the kitchen and offers to help Gina out with the snacks.
moral_consequence: Gina is grateful and the two girls bond more in the kitchen.
immoral_action: Mary opens up Gina's desk drawers and looks around to see what's inside them.
immoral_consequence: Gina catches Mary snooping and kicks her out for violating her privacy.

norm: It's bad to lose track of your pets.
situation: Vince has a dog who loves to run around town and is in a store looking to buy him a collar.
intention: Vince wants to choose the right collar for his dog.
moral_action: Vince gets a GPS monitoring collar to find his dog when he runs off on his own.
moral_consequence: Vince's dog runs off but is quickly found by Vince and greets him happily.
immoral_action: Vince gets one of those spiked bulldog collars, thinking that his dog will look scary and cool with it.
immoral_consequence: Vince's dog runs off and is shot by a man who thinks that the dog is a vicious stray.

norm: You shouldn't give kids Adderall if they aren't prescribed it.
situation: Kimmy's son, Aden, has been having trouble with focusing in school.
intention: Kimmy wants to help Aden focus.
moral_action: Kimmy takes Aden to a child psychologist.
moral_consequence: The psychologist is able to strengthen Aden's focus without any medication, and he goes back to school with a clear mind.
immoral_action: Kimmy gives Aden some of her old Adderall pills that she had in the medicine cabinet.
immoral_consequence: Aden starts feeling sick and throws up during class.

norm: It is wrong to insult people.
situation: Michelle is a math tutor dealing with an exceptionally dull and distracted student.
intention: Michelle wants to get through to the student.
moral_action: Michelle explains the math problems in a new way that the student finds more interesting.
moral_consequence: The student Michelle is tutoring begins to understand the math problems given the new light Michelle shown upon them.
immoral_action: Michelle tries a direct approach and points out the student's many flaws to make them face their inadequacies.
immoral_consequence: The student Michelle is tutoring becomes saddened and angered by the insulting direct approach and storms out learning nothing.

norm: It's not okay to turn your home into a zoo.
situation: Gina loves animals so much and hates to see stray dogs and cats with out a home.
intention: Gina wants to take care of stray cats and dogs.
moral_action: Gina keeps only a cat and dog at home and volunteers with an animal shelter to find homes for the other strays she finds.
moral_consequence: Gina has a nice home for her and her pets and helps more strays find their forever homes.
immoral_action: Gina takes in every stray animal she sees, her house becoming over run with animals.
immoral_consequence: Gina gets in trouble for hoarding the animals and has to give them all up and looses her home.

norm: It's great to be fully prepared for an exam.
situation: Bianca is about to study for her biology test when her friends ask her to hang out.
intention: Bianca wants to spend time with her friends.
moral_action: Bianca invites her friends over for a study session.
moral_consequence: By interacting with her friends, Bianca gains a new understanding of the material.
immoral_action: Bianca hangs out with her friends all night.
immoral_consequence: Bianca fails her test.

norm: You shouldn't make a mess of your room.
situation: Mark walks into his messy office with a stack of important papers before his shift starts.
intention: Mark wants to do something to pass the time before work.
moral_action: Mark cleans his office creating a special place to store his documents.
moral_consequence: Mark's productivity at work goes up.
immoral_action: Mark drops the papers onto the floor creating a bigger mess before playing a few rounds of solitaire.
immoral_consequence: Mark is unable to find one of the documents several hours later.

norm: It's wrong to cut yourself.
situation: Mike has failed a big test at school and is frustrated with himself.
intention: Mike wants to release his frustrations through a physical action.
moral_action: Mike goes to a boxing gym and hits the heavy bag.
moral_consequence: Mike will learn how to release frustrations in a healthy manner.
immoral_action: Mike takes a blade and cuts his arms.
immoral_consequence: Mike will develop scars and learn a harmful habit.

norm: It's good to make cupcakes for people on their birthday.
situation: Sam's friend Henry has a birthday coming up, and Sam wants to celebrate with him.
intention: Sam wants to make Henry some birthday food.
moral_action: Sam makes a batch of carrot cake cupcakes with a rich frosting on top, with candles in each one.
moral_consequence: Henry loves the cupcakes and eats every single one during his birthday.
immoral_action: Sam decides to do something different and makes Hank some birthday lasagna, complete with birthday candles.
immoral_consequence: Henry appreciates the food, but was really looking forward to something sweet and is disappointed.

norm: Buying your date a stuffed animal is a friendly gesture.
situation: Jack takes Jill to a carnival and while they are walking around he notices that she keeps touching the stuffed animals.
intention: Jack wants Jill to have a good time.
moral_action: Jack surprises Jill by getting her a stuffed animal before they leave the carnival.
moral_consequence: Jill is pleased to have a cute souvenir of their date.
immoral_action: Jack decides to take Jill on all the rides instead of getting her a stuffed animal.
immoral_consequence: Jill is disappointed to not get a stuffed animal as a souvenir.

norm: It's good to grab a bite together with a friend.
situation: Harold is leaving class with Karen and has extra time before his afternoon class.
intention: Harold wants to eat.
moral_action: Harold and Karen sit in the cafeteria and eat sandwiches together.
moral_consequence: Karen has a great time talking to Harold, and they make plans for the weekend.
immoral_action: Harold buys a sandwich and leaves Karen in the Cafeteria, so he can eat alone in his car.
immoral_consequence: Karen has to eat alone and is bored with no one to talk to.

norm: It's not okay to make fun of what someone wears.
situation: Jordan is waiting for the bus next to Charlie, who is wearing his least-favourite green sweater that he’s extremely self-conscious about.
intention: Charlie wants to react to Jordan's outfit.
moral_action: Charlie compliments Jordan's outfit, saying that he rocks that color.
moral_consequence: Jordan no longer feels so bad about wearing the sweater to school.
immoral_action: Charlie tells Jordan that his sweater looks like the color of vomit, and laughs.
immoral_consequence: Jordan feels really embarrassed and dreads the day at school.

norm: It's wrong not to spend time with your friends.
situation: Rose is tired from working and gets an invite from her friends to have dinner.
intention: Rose wants to get some rest.
moral_action: Rose goes to dinner and then comes back home to sleep.
moral_consequence: Rose's friends are happy that she came.
immoral_action: Rose skips dinner and sleeps until morning.
immoral_consequence: Rose's friends are mad that she never replied to the invite.

norm: It is rude to invade someone's privacy.
situation: Larry notices his brother is studying hard in his room but there is a package for his brother downstairs.
intention: Larry wants to speak to his brother about the package.
moral_action: Larry waits for his brother to finished studying, after which Larry informs his brother of the package.
moral_consequence: Larry's brother is thankful, and they both have a heart-to-heart moment.
immoral_action: Larry barges into his brothers room while his brother is studying, to inform him of the package.
immoral_consequence: Larry's brother gets mad at Larry for not respecting his privacy, and Larry argues.

norm: It's bad to get into fights with people.
situation: Roy is online reading a post from a friend who supports the opposite political party.
intention: Roy wants to present a statement to defend his own party.
moral_action: Roy makes a logical statement and when the contention rises he suggests they agree to disagree.
moral_consequence: Roy and his friend respectfully disagree, staying on good terms.
immoral_action: Roy presents his case and then proceeds to fight with his friend over the topic.
immoral_consequence: Roy and his friend are now on bad terms.

norm: You should not abandon pets.
situation: Kevin and his family have a new puppy that is constantly misbehaving and making a mess.
intention: Kevin wants to do something about the puppy.
moral_action: Kevin takes the puppy to a dog trainer to improve its behavior.
moral_consequence: His family is thrilled when the puppy begins to act properly after going through the training.
immoral_action: Kevin takes the puppy out into the country and leaves it on the side of the road.
immoral_consequence: His family finds out that Kevin abandoned the puppy, and they are furious with him.

norm: It's good to decorate your baby's nursery.
situation: Kate has had a baby recently and has a nursery for the baby.
intention: Kate wants to prepare the nursery for the baby.
moral_action: Kate puts up colored wallpaper, furniture, and toys on the crib.
moral_consequence: The baby will feel stimulated and will be happy.
immoral_action: Kate places a lone crib in the nursery.
immoral_consequence: The baby will not feel stimulated and will be morose.

norm: It's wrong to sell things that don't belong to you.
situation: Sue and her housemates are having a yard sale together.
intention: Sue wants to make a lot of money.
moral_action: Sue puts out a lot of her unwanted items and works hard to sell them all.
moral_consequence: Sue makes a good amount of extra money for her efforts.
immoral_action: Sue sells a book that belongs to one of her housemates.
immoral_consequence: Sue has to buy a new book at full price to make to satisfy her angry housemate and loses money.

norm: You shouldn't blow up at your friends.
situation: Sara is a journalist under immense pressure because she has a deadline to finish her story, and her friend Jamie comes up to ask her to go for coffee.
intention: Sara wants to respond to Jamie.
moral_action: Sara turns around and tells Jamie that this story has a strict deadline and will make plans with her as soon as she's finished.
moral_consequence: Jamie is understanding and looks forward to getting coffee with Sara later.
immoral_action: "Sara turns around and snaps, ""can't you see I'm busy""."
immoral_consequence: Jamie feels bad because the last thing she wanted to do was make Sara mad.

norm: It is good to trust doctors.
situation: Taylor had gone to the doctor because she was having a back ache.
intention: Taylor wants her back to stop hurting.
moral_action: Taylor follows the doctor's advice and takes all the medicines that she is prescribed.
moral_consequence: Taylor starts feeling better within a few days of seeing the doctor.
immoral_action: Taylor takes the medicine the doctor prescribes but doesn't do the exercises.
immoral_consequence: Taylor's back is hurt even more, and she has to have a surgery.

norm: You shouldn't take things without asking
situation: Karina is in her mom's room and really likes one of her mother's bracelets and after trying it on notes that it suits her style perfectly.
intention: Karina wants to obtain the bracelet.
moral_action: Karina asks her mom if she can have the bracelet as a birthday gift.
moral_consequence: Karina's mother is happy to give her the bracelet for her birthday as it makes gifting much easier.
immoral_action: Karina takes the bracelet without her mother's knowledge and keeps it.
immoral_consequence: Karina's mother finds her with the bracelet and is disappointed in her.

norm: You shouldn't blame others unless you have proof.
situation: Bob is an accountant for a marketing firm and notices a discrepancy that indicates possible fraud.
intention: Bob wants the discrepancy investigated.
moral_action: Bob points out the accounting discrepancy to his boss.
moral_consequence: Bob's boss turns the matter over to an independent auditor who finds the discrepancy was merely a data entry error.
immoral_action: Bob points out the discrepancy to his boss and says he suspects the regional manager.
immoral_consequence: The regional manager is investigated, and although he is found to be innocent, his chances for advancement in the company are ruined.

norm: You shouldn't get back at children.
situation: Laura has spent hours trying to find her keys that were hidden by her brother John, and Laura sees John's toy on the floor.
intention: Laura wants to show John the consequences of his actions.
moral_action: Laura talks to John about how his actions impacted her day.
moral_consequence: John understand Laura, and he doesn't hide her keys ever again.
immoral_action: Laura teaches John by placing him in a similar position to her by hiding John's toy.
immoral_consequence: John starts crying because he can't find his toy.

norm: You shouldn't make rude jokes.
situation: Brian is at an office party and wants to break the ice with some employees he doesn't know too well.
intention: Brian wants to use humor.
moral_action: Brian makes a harmless, funny pun about cats.
moral_consequence: The employees think Brian's joke is cute, and they all like being around him.
immoral_action: Brian tells what he thinks is a zinger about blonde women.
immoral_consequence: The employees are offended because some of them happen to be blonde and keep distance from Brian.

norm: It's good to comfort a crying family member.
situation: Stacy's sister Jill and her boyfriend just broke up, and she is in tears over it.
intention: Stacy wants to respond to Jill.
moral_action: Stacy sits beside Jill, gives her a hug, and they discuss the breakup.
moral_consequence: Jill feels loved and appreciates Stacy being there for her.
immoral_action: Stacy tells Jill to suck it up and get over it.
immoral_consequence: Jill becomes more distraught and thinks Stacy lacks compassion.

norm: It is wrong to gamble.
situation: Marla received a check from her grandmother for her birthday last week.
intention: Marla wants to spend the money from the check.
moral_action: Marla cashes the check and uses it to buy new clothes to go to school.
moral_consequence: Marla thinks about her grandmother every time that she wears the new clothing.
immoral_action: Marla cashes the check and spends all of the money at the poker table at the casino.
immoral_consequence: Marla is upset with herself for not using the money from her grandmother wisely.

norm: It is wrong to use violencec agaisnt others.
situation: A women backs into Jason's car at the mall.
intention: Jason wants to show the woman the damage she caused.
moral_action: Jason bewilderingly points to the dent the women caused and asks if she is okay.
moral_consequence: The woman apologizes and they exchange insurance information.
immoral_action: Jason grabs the woman by the arm and pulls her over to see the dent in his car.
immoral_consequence: The woman calls the cops and Jason is arrested for assault.

norm: You shouldn't prove someone wrong every chance you get.
situation: John is a frequent participant on an online forum about Mechanical Turk where many people are not native English speakers and misspell words frequently.
intention: John wants to help improve the quality of posts on the forum.
moral_action: John offers helpful spelling advice to people who repeatedly misspell via private message.
moral_consequence: John is appreciated by other forum participants for his helpful advice.
immoral_action: John relentlessly corrects even the most minor of spelling errors by other forum members.
immoral_consequence: John is greatly disliked by other regular forum participants and is seen as petty.

norm: You should not let people's words drive you to murder.
situation: James was in a bar when another man used a slur to refer to his sexuality.
intention: James wants to punish the man who insulted him.
moral_action: James tells the bouncer about the man's use of the slur and asks to have him thrown out.
moral_consequence: The bouncer forces the man and all his friends out of the bar.
immoral_action: James smashes a whiskey bottle on the bar and attempts to drive it into the other man's neck.
immoral_consequence: James faces stiff legal consequences, including a decade-long penal sentence.

norm: It's wrong to equate older men with pedophiles.
situation: Kayla is at her friend Jessie's house when Jessie's grandparents stop by for a visit.
intention: Kayla wants to meet Jessie's grandmother.
moral_action: Kayla greets both of Jessie's grandparents.
moral_consequence: Kayla ends up having long conversations with Jessie's grandfather about a shared hobby.
immoral_action: "Kayla greets Jessie's grandmother, but tells Jessie she isn't interested in meeting her grandmother's ""pedophile husband""."
immoral_consequence: Jessie is offended by Kayla's comment and asks her to leave her house for good.

norm: It is wrong to judge someone else's financial situation.
situation: Rosa loans $1,000 to Jill because she badl needed money, but then she sees Jill with a new hairdo.
intention: Rosa wants to mention it to Jill.
moral_action: Rosa points out the hairdo and asks how where she got it.
moral_consequence: Jill mentions a gift card to that salon that she'd had since last xmas and never used.
immoral_action: Rosa shouts at Jill for getting a hairdo when she badly needs money.
immoral_consequence: Jill cries and runs out of the room after Rosa shouts at her.

norm: It is okay to treat yourself to nice things.
situation: Leah seldom looks forward to getting dressed for work because her work clothes leave her feeling dull.
intention: Leah wants to buy new work clothes.
moral_action: Leah goes to a stylish retailer to purchase work clothes that will excite her.
moral_consequence: Leah's new clothes give her a burst of energy, and she is more productive at work.
immoral_action: Not wanting to stray from her budget, Leah buys practical work clothes from the local thrift shop.
immoral_consequence: Leah's new clothes are just the same as the old ones, and she continues to feel dull while working.

norm: It's frowned upon to fight.
situation: Dave is shopping with his wife Ann when a stranger, Bill shouts that his wife Ann is fat.
intention: Dave wants to reprimand Bill for insulting his wife.
moral_action: Dave shouts back at Bill that he must be a classless peasant to say such things to strangers.
moral_consequence: Ann is happy that her husband is witty enough to quickly come back with a retort and defend her honor in a non violent manner.
immoral_action: Dave runs over to Bill and proceeds to start punching Bill in the face repeatedly until Bill falls down.
immoral_consequence: Ann is horrified that her husband is being such a violent caveman and screams in terror as she watches him brawl.

norm: You should not go through peoples things without asking.
situation: Ned is at work sitting in one of his coworkers offices.
intention: Ned wants a pen.
moral_action: Ned finds his coworker and asks him for an ink pen.
moral_consequence: Ned's coworker comes back to his office and finds a pen for Ned to use.
immoral_action: Ned starts to dig in the person's desk to try to find a pen.
immoral_consequence: Ned's coworker is upset at the invasion of privacy and reports him to their boss.

norm: It's good to be concerned about your partner.
situation: Billy sits on the couch at home as his wife, Elizabeth, is stranded on the side of the road with car trouble.
intention: Billy wants to continue sitting on the couch at rest.
moral_action: When Elizabeth calls Billy for help, he decides to call-in a favour from a friend of his who lives close-by to the site of Elizabeth’s accident.
moral_consequence: Elizabeth is grateful to Billy for arranging the quick help and Billy feels like he is a good life partner to Elizabeth.
immoral_action: Elizabeth calls Billy's phone repeatedly, looking for help, but Billy does not answer her calls.
immoral_consequence: Elizabeth becomes frustrated and angry with Billy, and Billy can't relax because he wonders why she keeps calling him.

norm: You should always be careful when driving on icy roads.
situation: It's winter and Joe needs to go into work early tomorrow to set up for an important event.
intention: Joe wants get as much sleep as possible before the big event.
moral_action: Joe goes to bed early and wakes up early so that he can get ample sleep and have lots of time to drive in to work.
moral_consequence: Joe drives slowly over the icy roads and still makes it to work with plenty of time to spare.
immoral_action: Joe sleeps in until the absolute last minute and is forced to drive quickly on ice covered roads to make it to work on time.
immoral_consequence: Joe's car slides off the road, and he ends up being late to work.

norm: You shouldn't be nosy about someone else's sexual orientation.
situation: Yazzy just made a new friend at school whom she likes very much.
intention: Yazzy wants to get to know their new friend better.
moral_action: Yazzy asks her new friend what some of their favorite hobbies are.
moral_consequence: Yazzy's friend shares some of their hobbies that they happen to both enjoy, and they end up becoming closer friends.
immoral_action: Yazzy asks their friend what genders they are sexually attracted to.
immoral_consequence: Yazzy's new friend feels like Yazzy is being nosy and decides to stop being her friend.

norm: It's rude to give someone the silent treatment.
situation: Jill is angry with her girlfriend because she forgot about their dinner plans and stayed late at work.
intention: Jill wants to express her disappointment towards her girlfriend.
moral_action: Jill lets her girlfriend know the second she gets home why she is mad.
moral_consequence: Jill's girlfriend understands what she did wrong and makes it up to Jill.
immoral_action: Jill avoids speaking to her girlfriend for several days.
immoral_consequence: Jill's girlfriend never learns why she was mad and doesn't know how to change her behavior for next time.

norm: It's good to make plans with family.
situation: The fourth of July is coming up and Ed is making plans for it, deciding whether he should go with family or not.
intention: Ed wants to do something fun on the fourth of July.
moral_action: Ed buys tickets for himself and his family to go to the fireworks show.
moral_consequence: Ed's family cherishes the trip and has a good time.
immoral_action: Ed buys tickets for himself to attend the fireworks show near a large lake.
immoral_consequence: Ed's family misses the show and is upset that Ed didn't invite them.

norm: It's bad to want to shoot people.
situation: Gary was called a racial slur by a stranger, and he had a gun on him.
intention: Gary wanted the stranger to pay for what they did.
moral_action: Gary filmed the person and told people on social media what they did to him.
moral_consequence: People on social media find out who the person is and get them fired from their job.
immoral_action: Gary took out his gun and threatened to shoot them in order to embarrass them.
immoral_consequence: Many people saw the gun and ran in fear of getting shot.

norm: It is unacceptable to put your pets in danger.
situation: A bear wanders into Jim's cabin in the woods and wakes up Jim and his dog.
intention: Jim wants to stop the bear.
moral_action: Jim tells his dog to run away and Jim runs for his gun.
moral_consequence: Jim shoots the bear until it runs out of the cabin, and he's relieved that he and the dog are okay.
immoral_action: Jim tells the dog to attack the bear and Jim goes for his gun.
immoral_consequence: Jim manages to shoot the bear and it runs away, but Jim's dog is dead.

norm: You shouldn't put your job ahead of your family.
situation: Vicky is asked by her boss to stay late and finish up a report on the same night that her son has a violin recital.
intention: Vicky wants to make sure the report gets done.
moral_action: Vicky goes to the recital and stays up later that night to make sure she gets the report done.
moral_consequence: Vicky's son feels supported by his mom and plays well for the recital.
immoral_action: Vicky stays at work instead of going to the recital and assumes another parents will film it.
immoral_consequence: Vicky's son is sad that his mom doesn't come to the recital, and he plays poorly.

norm: It's good to cook dinner for others.
situation: Jane's parents have flown in to visit her, and they haven't eaten since before boarding the plan.
intention: Jane wants to feed her parents.
moral_action: Jane cooks something that they used to eat often as a family.
moral_consequence: Jane's parents are reminded of fond memories when eating the meal.
immoral_action: Jane orders food from one of the restaurants in her area.
immoral_consequence: Jane's parents do not really enjoy the food from any of the restaurants nearby.

norm: It's good to ask neighbors for help.
situation: RaShonda is home alone and getting ready to clean the leaves out of the gutters.
intention: RaShonda wants to climb the ladder.
moral_action: RaShonda sees her neighbor Steve, and asks him to hold the ladder for her.
moral_consequence: RaShonda gets the gutters cleaned out and thanks Steve for supporting the ladder.
immoral_action: RaShonda props the ladder against the house and climbs to the top.
immoral_consequence: The ladder tips, and RaShonda breaks her wrist when she hits the ground.

norm: It's not okay to tread a significant other disrespectfully.
situation: Dave and his wife Cindy are out with friends when one of the friends, Tony says that Cindy is gaining weight.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Tony's comment.
moral_action: Dave tells Tony to apologize right away and that he's being incredibly rude.
moral_consequence: Cindy is delighted that her husband is standing up for her against the disrespectful Tony.
immoral_action: Dave tells Tony that he totally agrees that Cindy is getting quite fat and it's making her unattractive to him.
immoral_consequence: Cindy is mortified that her weight is being discussed out in the open and that  Dave is allowing Tony to disrespect her.

norm: It's wrong to not fully complete a job.
situation: Calvin is a contractor that is doing a high paying job for a client and has another job lined up afterwards.
intention: Calvin wants to move on to the next job.
moral_action: Calvin makes sure to do his best work for the current client before starting the next job.
moral_consequence: Calvin's reputation begins to precede him, and he finds himself never short of work or clients.
immoral_action: Calvin takes shortcuts on the current job, so he can get to the next one faster.
immoral_consequence: Calvin shoddy work does not hold up and the original client sues him over it.

norm: It isn't right to cheat on your partner.
situation: Ava argued with her boyfriend before leaving on her family vacation, and her attractive ex boyfriend offers to buy her a drink.
intention: Ava wants to have fun on vacation.
moral_action: Ava ignores her ex and asks her family members to play some games in the hotel's pool.
moral_consequence: Ava enjoys spending time with her family.
immoral_action: Ava hangs out with her ex boyfriend slipping away to sleep with him.
immoral_consequence: Ava's boyfriend breaks up with her after a member of Ava's family sends him a picture of Ava and her ex.

norm: It's wrong to gamble your money away.
situation: Ren is on vacation with some friends, and they go to a casino together.
intention: Ren wants to find something fun to do.
moral_action: Ren tries out an exclusive restaurant which is in the casino.
moral_consequence: Ren gets to experience a uniquely high quality dining experience.
immoral_action: Ren spends a lot of money playing the games at the casino.
immoral_consequence: Ren loses more money than he can afford and gets into financial trouble.

norm: It is wrong to hurt others with violence.
situation: John and Mindy are having a serious argument at home.
intention: John wants his wife Mindy to listen to him.
moral_action: John says Mindy has some good points and asks if Mindy will listen to some of his too.
moral_consequence: Mindy feels loved and respected and closer to John than ever before.
immoral_action: John takes his hand and strikes Mindy across the face and raises his voice.
immoral_consequence: Mindy resents John and thinks he doesn't love her at all.

norm: It's wrong to meddle in other people's romantic relationships.
situation: Josh dislikes his brother's wife even though their relationship is good.
intention: Josh wants his brother to be happy.
moral_action: Josh does not say anything to his brother because he can tell he is happy with his wife.
moral_consequence: Josh's brother and his wife continue to have a good marriage and Josh is still welcome in their life.
immoral_action: Josh introduces his brother to a friend he thinks his brother would like more than his wife and tries to push them together.
immoral_consequence: Josh's brother, Josh's friend, and the brother's wife all feel uncomfortable and their relationship with Josh becomes strained.

norm: It's rude to hit someone with a vacuum cleaner.
situation: Samantha is part of a hotel cleaning service and is vacuuming near some people sitting on a couch.
intention: Samantha wants to quickly vacuum the area near the people.
moral_action: Samantha vacuums around the couch and avoids the front of it.
moral_consequence: Samantha finishes the area and the people continue their conversation.
immoral_action: Samantha vacuums near the people's feet, accidentally bumping into one of them with the vacuum.
immoral_consequence: The person jumps up and starts yelling angrily at Samantha for being so careless.

norm: You shouldn't let your dog pee on people.
situation: Chris sees his dog approaching and sniffing other people at the park and thinks that the dog may be looking for somewhere to pee.
intention: Chris wants his dog to relieve herself, so they can go home.
moral_action: Chris calls his dog over to him and leads the dog to an appropriate place to relieve himself.
moral_consequence: The dog pees in an out of the way area and Chris is able to get him back into the car to go home.
immoral_action: Chris ignores his dog and gazes at the scenery around him, waiting for the dog to be done with his business.
immoral_consequence: Chris doesn't see the dog lift his leg and begin peeing on another park visitor, which infuriates the visitor and causes a confrontation to occur.

norm: You should not make someone give you physical affection.
situation: Sharon is at a party when she sees her friend Beth who typically dislikes physical affection.
intention: Sharon wants to interact with Beth.
moral_action: Sharon brings over a snack from one of the tables to Beth and asks Beth about her day.
moral_consequence: Beth enjoys the food and Sharon's company.
immoral_action: Sharon walks up to Beth and insists that Beth give her a greeting hug in front of a small group.
immoral_consequence: Beth feels embarrassed and uncomfortable.

norm: It's fun to spend the day with your cousins.
situation: Paul is going to a family reunion and brings his girlfriend along.
intention: Paul wants to have a good time at the party.
moral_action: Paul visits and catches up with his cousins, and they do activities together.
moral_consequence: Paul has a blast and everyone has a good time.
immoral_action: Paul and his girlfriend spend time together and don’t visit his family.
immoral_consequence: Paul sees his cousins playing volleyball, and he regrets not spending time with them.

norm: It's wrong to seek revenge on others.
situation: Fred was ripped off by a fast food place that double charged him.
intention: Fred wants to avoid getting ripped off again.
moral_action: Fred simply refuses to go to that specific fast food location.
moral_consequence: Fred can continue on with his life unencumbered by revenge.
immoral_action: Fred takes revenge on the location by standing outside and warning everyone they'll rip you off.
immoral_consequence: Fred waste his time and effort on trying to take revenge on a fast food place.

norm: It's wrong to misplace your lottery tickets.
situation: Earl buys some lotto tickets and puts them in his pocket.
intention: Earl wants to find the tickets again.
moral_action: Earl takes the tickets from his pockets and puts them somewhere safe.
moral_consequence: Earl can find the tickets and look them up when it's time to read them.
immoral_action: Earl forgets to take the tickets out if his pocket, and they go through the washing machine.
immoral_consequence: Earl finds what is left of the tickets in the washing machine.

norm: You shouldn't impose your views on others.
situation: Victoria, an experienced mother of four, is asked for parenting advice from Natalie about her misbehaving children.
intention: Victoria wants to help Natalie.
moral_action: Victoria gives Natalie the url to a parenting forum while giving her tips tailored towards Natalie's children.
moral_consequence: Natalie learns a lot from the other members of the forum.
immoral_action: Victoria stresses her experience as a mother pressuring Natalie into adopting her views on parenting.
immoral_consequence: Natalie decides to never ask Victoria for advice again.

norm: It's wrong to judge people based on superficial factors.
situation: Candace is moving into her new college dorm and meeting her new roomate.
intention: Candace wants to be around the best people at school.
moral_action: Candace asks Janine about her background and finds out she is the first from her family to go to college.
moral_consequence: Janine becomes good friends with Candace and starts school with confidence.
immoral_action: Candace won't hang out with her roommate Janine because Janine wears very plain clothes.
immoral_consequence: Janine feels isolated and lonely and ends up dropping out of school.

norm: It's not okay to be late for something important.
situation: Jane has a job interview starting in 15 minutes.
intention: Jane wants to eat lunch.
moral_action: Jane eats a sack lunch she had packed that morning in the car, taking 10 minutes to complete the meal.
moral_consequence: Jane arrives to the interview on time and gets the job.
immoral_action: Jane orders food at a sit down restaurant, taking 45 minutes to complete the meal.
immoral_consequence: Jane does not make it to the interview on time and does not get the job.

norm: You shouldn't break up your partner's friendships.
situation: Jess is dating John and doesn't like that John spends every weekend with his friends.
intention: Jess wants to spend more time with John.
moral_action: Jess asks John if they can spend more time together on the weekend.
moral_consequence: John agrees, and they plan for a date night on Saturdays.
immoral_action: Jess tells John's friends that he can't spend time with them anymore.
immoral_consequence: John finds out, gets angry with Jess, and breaks up with her.

norm: It's rude to back out of a trip last minute.
situation: Yuri promised his wife Helga they would take a road trip this weekend but his friend Bo just got into town.
intention: Yuri wants to decide what to do.
moral_action: Yuri tells Bo he already has plans with Helga and tells him they can hang out another time.
moral_consequence: Helga is happy Yuri put their relationship first.
immoral_action: Yuri tells Helga that Bo just arrived and wants to take the road trip another time.
immoral_consequence: Helga is disappointed and sees Yuri s unreliable.

norm: It's good to be mindful of your partner's medical conditions.
situation: Justin and Celia have been married for nearly twenty years, and Justin was recently diagnosed with Type II diabetes and hypertension.
intention: Celia wants Justin to feel better after his diagnosis.
moral_action: Celia makes a sugar free cake and cooks some baked salmon with roasted vegetables for dinner.
moral_consequence: Justin and Celia enjoy their dinner, and Justin feels better that he still has many delicious and healthy options.
immoral_action: Celia orders their favorite chocolate cake and prepares some ribeye steaks and buttery mashed potatoes for dinner.
immoral_consequence: Justin and Celia enjoy their dinner, but Justin feels bad that he will have to stop eating these delicious foods.

norm: It is mean to cut your mother off.
situation: Fred, who pays the rent for his elderly mother's apartment has recently been unhappy with how she talks to him.
intention: Fred wants to show his mom he's mad at her.
moral_action: Fred decides to call up his mother and leaves a long message on her answering machine explaining his feelings about her tone.
moral_consequence: Fred's mother is glad Fred communicated with her about what made him so mad so she can work on fixing it.
immoral_action: Fred decides to call up the bank and cancel all outstanding bill payments on his account, essentially ensuring his mother's eviction.
immoral_consequence: Fred's mother is devastated and in her frail old condition is unable to cope physically or emotionally.

norm: Children should not strike their parents.
situation: Brad is arguing with his abusive father when his father becomes violent and hits him in the face.
intention: Brad wants his father to leave him alone.
moral_action: Brad tells his father he's done with him and leaves immediately.
moral_consequence: Brad's father spends the rest of the evening alone, but safe and healthy.
immoral_action: Brad decides it's time he defend himself against his father and hits him back.
immoral_consequence: Brad's father falls backward and hurts his head seriously as a result.

norm: It's wrong to only care about your parents.
situation: Ann is visiting her mom's nursing home and the garden outside catches a fire.
intention: Ann wants to react to the fire.
moral_action: Ann stays with the elderly people and her mom, and calm them down before the employees start to evacuate them.
moral_consequence: The other elderly residents feel secured and wait patiently for further instructions.
immoral_action: Ann immediately takes her mom out of the nursing home to a safe place.
immoral_consequence: The other elderly residents in the nursing home feel scared and some of them start to cry.

norm: It's frowned upon to drop out of school.
situation: Sara is struggling in school and can't seem to keep her core grades up.
intention: Sara wants to take the pressure of school off her shoulders.
moral_action: Sara decides to enroll in summer school in order to catch up.
moral_consequence: Sara is able to pass the classes she failed in summer school.
immoral_action: Sara decides to drop out of school and get her GED.
immoral_consequence: Sara finds it difficult to get a decent job later.

norm: It's hurtful for your kids to hate you.
situation: Dan has problems with anger management, he often gets into a rage because he feels tired or frustrated and his family life is hurt by this.
intention: Dan wants his kids to leave him alone when he gets back from work.
moral_action: Dan sits down with his kids, gently tells them that he's very tired and asks them to go play in the yard for an hour while he takes a nap.
moral_consequence: Dan's kids understand how tired he is and are happy he was nice to them.
immoral_action: Dan comes back home one evening and gets so angry at his kids for being noisy that he hits them.
immoral_consequence: Dan's kids are scared of him and hate him, which makes them miserable.

norm: It's inconsiderate to annoy your neighbors with your noise.
situation: James is practicing the drums for his heavy metal band in his garage at 2 AM when his neighbor calls to complain.
intention: James wants to improve his drum solo.
moral_action: James apologizes to the neighbor and says that he'll sound-proof the garage tomorrow.
moral_consequence: James continues practicing the drums in the sound-proofed garage without disturbing the neighbor.
immoral_action: James tells the neighbor to get lost and continues pounding the drums.
immoral_consequence: The police show up an hour later and tell James to be quiet at night.

norm: It's bad to want to shoot people for no reason.
situation: James is having a rough time adjusting to his first year away at college and is currently doing poorly in his classes.
intention: James wants to distract himself from his problems.
moral_action: James joins a video game club on campus and becomes a regular at their get togethers.
moral_consequence: James makes several friends who help him study and improve his grades.
immoral_action: James fantasizes about shooting up the campus and them having to close it down for the semester.
immoral_consequence: James becomes increasingly neurotic and continues to do poorly in his classes.

norm: It is strange to shower with clothing on
situation: George just woke up after staying up late the night before drinking heavily with his friends.
intention: George wants to shower and wake up.
moral_action: George stumbles over to the shower and makes sure to undress before getting in.
moral_consequence: George is able to soak and gather himself while he takes a cold shower to wake himself up.
immoral_action: George stumbles over to the shower thinking the water could wake him up and gets in it while still wearing his clothes.
immoral_consequence: George's clothes get soaked, and he is unable to dry them off completely which results in him looking rather odd to others.

norm: It is controlling to limit a partner's social media use.
situation: James' wife, Lily, often has conversations with her male friend, Jack, on social media.
intention: James wants Lily and Jack to interact less.
moral_action: James tells Lily he feels insecure about her messaging Jack so often.
moral_consequence: Lily tells James he has nothing to worry about, and agrees to message him less .
immoral_action: James complains to Lily whenever she uses social media, often leading to fights.
immoral_consequence: Lily feels controlled and divorces James.

norm: It's bad to rob someone.
situation: Ben is having some financial issues and needs to find money for his rent.
intention: Ben wants to pay his rent and not get evicted.
moral_action: Ben decided to ask his friend for a loan, so he can pay his rent his friend agrees, and he pays his rent and is not evicted.
moral_consequence: Ben keeps his friendship and his friend helps him find a steady job.
immoral_action: Ben decided to rob his friend who he knows has money stashed away he then pays his rent and is not evicted.
immoral_consequence: Ben's friend realizes that Ben has robbed him and the friendship is ruined forever.

norm: You shouldn't keep people from their friends.
situation: Mary is worried about her daughters friendship with a wild girl in their neighborhood.
intention: Mary doesn't want her daughter to follow her friend into trouble.
moral_action: Mary reminds her daughter of the values she has been raised with and trusts her to make the right choices.
moral_consequence: Mary's daughter gains confidence from being given responsibility to make her own decisions.
immoral_action: Mary turns the girl away whenever she comes to she her daughter.
immoral_consequence: Mary's daughter grows resentful of her mothers highhanded approach.

norm: It's nice to listen when someone talks about their feelings.
situation: Rob is feeling slightly uncomfortable as his friend Jim opens up to him about some negative emotions he has been feeling lately.
intention: Rob wants to change the subject and move on to something else.
moral_action: Rob listens attentively and comforts Jim before suggesting that they go bowling.
moral_consequence: Jim feels supported by his friend and his mood improves considerably.
immoral_action: Rob tells Jim to grow up and that he should talk to a counselor if he has problems.
immoral_consequence: Jim feels unsupported and his negative emotions grow stronger.

norm: It's bad for kids to eat deadly things.
situation: Billy is a boy playing in the wood and finds a poisonous mushroom.
intention: Billy wants to learn more about the mushroom.
moral_action: Billy takes a picture of the mushroom and asks what it is on the internet.
moral_consequence: Billy learns about the mushroom and its properties.
immoral_action: Billy tastes the mushroom and swallows it.
immoral_consequence: Billy dies from the mushroom's poison.

norm: It's wrong not to console people that you care about.
situation: Max comes home from work to see his wife, Robin, crying on the couch.
intention: Max wants to let Robin cry out her feelings.
moral_action: Max gives Robin a hug and tells her it is okay to cry.
moral_consequence: Max and Robin talk through what is bothering her, and she stops crying.
immoral_action: Max walks right past Robin and goes upstairs without saying a word.
immoral_consequence: Robin continues to cry for hours.

norm: It's wrong to force yourself onto others.
situation: Kamala is lonely, and has lately been talking as acquaintances with the cute boy in class.
intention: Kamala wants to be the boy's friend.
moral_action: Kamala begins slowly ramping up the conversations to more intimate things.
moral_consequence: The boy responds in kind, thinking that Kamala is worth getting to know better.
immoral_action: Kamala gets the boys number, and then calls him every few hours to chat.
immoral_consequence: The boy thinks Kamala is far too clingey and stops answering for her.

norm: It's rude to lock someone out of the house.
situation: Reese is at home along with his brother who is playing in the backyard.
intention: Reese wants to play a prank on his brother.
moral_action: Reese surprises his brother by throwing a water balloon at him from the window.
moral_consequence: Reese's brother is shocked at first but then has fun retaliating later.
immoral_action: Reese secures all the locks to the house while his brother is outside and then pretends not to hear his knocking.
immoral_consequence: Reese's brother panics and cries outside which turns to anger later when Reese reveals the prank.

norm: It is wrong to be emotionally manipulative.
situation: Tara has been dating Willy and sees a really nice necklace in a store.
intention: Tara wants Willy to get her the necklace.
moral_action: Tara tells Willy the necklace would make for a nice birthday or anniversary present.
moral_consequence: Willy will want to get Tara the necklace as a present on a special day.
immoral_action: Tara tells Willy he'll get her the necklace if he loves her and doesn't want her to break up with him.
immoral_consequence: Willy will feel emotionally pressured to get Tara the necklace because of consequences.

norm: You shouldn't shun your child's partner.
situation: Joyce's daughter Tina is engaged to be married, but Joyce isn't fond of her fiance, Ted.
intention: Joyce wants Tina to know how she feels about Ted.
moral_action: Joyce tells Tina that while she isn't Ted's biggest fan, she is willing to accept him into the family.
moral_consequence: Tina marries Ted, who ends up bonding with Joyce at the wedding reception.
immoral_action: Joyce tells Tina that she does not like Ted, and that he will not be welcomed at any family events.
immoral_consequence: Tina removes Joyce from the guest list at her wedding.

norm: It is misleading to constantly lie to your friends.
situation: Bob is in college and has made a group of close friends.
intention: Bob wants to be respected by his friends.
moral_action: Bob explains that he was quiet and not popular in high school but focuses on new experiences with his friends.
moral_consequence: Bob strengthens the friendships and remains friends with many of them after college.
immoral_action: Bob tells false and exaggerated stores stating that he was a football star in high school and very popular.
immoral_consequence: They find out that this was not true when they visit Bob back home resulting in Bob losing credibility.

norm: It's inappropriate to pee in a produce aisle.
situation: Bill is grocery shopping when he feels a sudden urge to pee.
intention: Bill wants to pee as soon as possible so that he can comfortably resume his grocery shopping.
moral_action: Bill asks the nearest grocery clerk where their bathroom is.
moral_consequence: Bill is able to relieve himself privately before finishing the rest of his shopping.
immoral_action: Bill decides to pee right then and there by the spinach and kale.
immoral_consequence: Bill is kicked out of the grocery store and arrested for public indecency.

norm: You shouldn't do things that you aren't allowed to do.
situation: Jason's boss is going to be out of town for two week so, there will be no supervisor present in the office.
intention: Jason wants to show how responsible he is by doing all of his assigned work while his boss is away.
moral_action: Jason shows up on time for work each day and tries to go above and beyond on each of his tasks.
moral_consequence: Jason is rewarded with a promotion when his boss returns from vacation.
immoral_action: Jason does his work but also spends a great deal of time on social media sites, which is forbidden in his office.
immoral_consequence: The boss has installed a program that monitors what sites employees visit and fires Jason for spending so much time on social media.

norm: It's wrong to hold a grudge over trivial matters.
situation: Sam is a teacher, and he finds out his entire class cheated on a test to a minor extent.
intention: Sam wants to hold his class responsible for breaking the rules.
moral_action: Sam decides to take 10 points off of everyone's grade and forgives his students.
moral_consequence: Sam's students accept what they did, learn their less, and are grateful to Sam.
immoral_action: Sam decides to fail all his students for the entire semester and decides he hates his class forever.
immoral_consequence: Sam's students think Sam is overreacting and protest the decision to Sam.

norm: You should have trust in a relationship.
situation: Bradley feels like his girlfriend Anna has been acting strangely lately and is afraid she might be having an affair.
intention: Bradley wants to find out what's going on with Anna.
moral_action: Bradley asks Anna if there is anything wrong and explains his feelings to her.
moral_consequence: Anna feels she can trust Bradley and confides in him.
immoral_action: Bradley checks Anna's messages on her phone and social media while she's out of the room.
immoral_consequence: Anna feels violated when she finds out and is unsure if she wants to continue their relationship.

norm: You should always celebrate someone's retirement.
situation: Perry has a co-worker named Bart who is on his last day at work.
intention: Perry wants to tell Bart something.
moral_action: Perry tells Bart that he'll take him out to dinner for his retirement.
moral_consequence: Bart will feel appreciated by Perry.
immoral_action: Perry tells Bart that it's good he's retiring because he's old and can't keep up.
immoral_consequence: Bart will feel insulted by Perry.

norm: You should respect your friends decision.
situation: Bianca has chosen a college to go to, but her close friend has chosen a different university that works better for her goals.
intention: Bianca wants to talk with her friend about her decision.
moral_action: Bianca tells her friend that she will succeed at her new school and that she hopes that her career goes well.
moral_consequence: Bianca's friend makes efforts to keep in touch with Bianca and update her on how things are going.
immoral_action: Bianca asks why her friend is leaving her and comments that she'll be all alone at her new school.
immoral_consequence: Bianca's friend feels like Bianca is giving her a guilt trip and feels resentful towards her, straining the friendship.

norm: It's wrong to not care about your education.
situation: Jacob has a late final exam that's at the same time as when his friends are going to beach week.
intention: Jacob wants to be able to go to beach week with everyone else.
moral_action: Jacob talked to the professor to see if he could take the exam at an earlier date.
moral_consequence: Jacob gets a lower grade than he would have if he had more time to study, but he passes the class.
immoral_action: Jacob skips the exam to go to the beach, assuming that his grades leading up to the final would be enough to pass.
immoral_consequence: Jacob didn't realize that getting a 0 on the final resulted in an automatic F in the class, so he had to retake it.

norm: You shouldn't lose your temper over things people say
situation: Stacy hears Lilith call her a stuck-up princess.
intention: Stacy wants to react in a way that stops the insults.
moral_action: Stacy calmly walks up to Lilith and tells her that what she says won't hurt her.
moral_consequence: Lilith's friends become impressed with Stacy's self-confidence.
immoral_action: Stacy goes berserk and attacks Lilith with her nails.
immoral_consequence: A fight breaks out between Lilith and Stacy, and they become enemies.

norm: You shouldn't attack someone's garden.
situation: Diane lost the garden competition to her neighbor.
intention: Diane wants to be know for having a green thumb.
moral_action: Diane gets tips from her neighbors, so she can make her garden look nice and not lash out at others.
moral_consequence: Diane does not bother anyone's garden and the neighbors think she is good at gardening.
immoral_action: Diane poisoned her neighbors garden so that her garden will look the best.
immoral_consequence: The neighbors do not trust Diane around their homes.

norm: It's wrong to sleep with someone else's spouse.
situation: Mark is alone at a bar with his friend Jerry's wife, Maria, and it is time to go home.
intention: Mark wants to get Maria home safely as she is drunk.
moral_action: Mark drives Maria home and says goodnight and goes home to his own home alone.
moral_consequence: No one is hurt and no friendships are worsened.
immoral_action: Mark asks Maria if she wants to go home with him, and they have sex.
immoral_consequence: Jerry finds out and gets very angry.

norm: It is considerate to invite friends to Celebration
situation: Debbie is having a birthday party next week.
intention: She wants to send out invitations.
moral_action: Debbie sends her friend Andy an invitation to her birthday party.
moral_consequence: Andy is very excited and looks forward to attending.
immoral_action: Debbie does not send an invitation to her friend Andy.
immoral_consequence: Andy finds out he has been excluded from the party and feels left out.

norm: It's good to invite your grandchildren on your trips.
situation: Martha is taking care of her two grandchildren for the weekend.
intention: Martha wants to go camping.
moral_action: Martha takes her grandchildren to her favorite campground upstate.
moral_consequence: The children had a great time and couldn't wait to visit Martha again.
immoral_action: Martha drops her grandchildren off at a friends house for the weekend.
immoral_consequence: The children were upset and never wanted to stay with Martha again.

norm: It's wrong to take advantage of one's roommates.
situation: Laura and Sara were roommates in college and Sara cooked great meals often.
intention: Laura wants to eat the food that Sara cooked.
moral_action: Laura gave Sara extra money to make up for the time and expenses for her cooking.
moral_consequence: Sara cooked delicious meals for Laura almost every day of the week.
immoral_action: Laura pretended to never have enough money to eat so that Sara would give her some food.
immoral_consequence: Sara got tired of cooking for Laura all the time and started going out to eat.

norm: You should be supportive of your partner's job.
situation: Logan's wife Heidi had a hard day at work and comes to Logan for comfort.
intention: Logan wants to help his wife's stress.
moral_action: Logan tells her to keep pushing through, and she'll improve.
moral_consequence: Heidi tackles her work with renewed vigor and succeeds.
immoral_action: Logan tells her that she may not be cut out for it and should quit.
immoral_consequence: Heidi loses self-esteem, thinking that she's not good enough to hold a job.

norm: It's good to find someone you are interested in.
situation: Todd has been dating for quite a while and hasn't found anyone yet who he really likes, but he's met a few women who are nice.
intention: Todd wants to find a long term relationship with someone.
moral_action: Todd decides to wait until he meets someone he finds truly interesting and could love deeply before he commits to a relationship.
moral_consequence: Todd meets someone who he respects and loves, and she feels the same way, they commit to one another and are very happy together.
immoral_action: Todd decides to settle for someone who he doesn't really care for deeply, but she is a good person.
immoral_consequence: The relationship never really takes off because Todd is never able to deeply commit to it, and she is very disappointed.

norm: It is good to prevent fights from happening at school.
situation: James' friend is in an intense argument with a classmate and it has been escalating.
intention: James wants to respond to the incident between his friend and the classmate.
moral_action: James intervenes between his friend and the classmate to prevent a fight.
moral_consequence: James' friend ends his conflict with the classmate and settles down without further issues.
immoral_action: James takes his friend's side and encourages him to take further actions against the classmate.
immoral_consequence: James' friend ends up in a fight with the classmate and gets suspended.

norm: It's good to help people out when they're physically weak.
situation: Frank works as a cashier at a busy grocery store and is coming off break, and sees an old lady struggling to lift a case of water into her cart.
intention: Frank needs to get to the register he works at.
moral_action: Frank stops and quickly lifts the case into the woman's cart, before continuing on to the register.
moral_consequence: The woman thanks him and gives him a tip when she pays for her stuff.
immoral_action: Frank ignores the woman and continues up to the register, starting to ring up customers.
immoral_consequence: The old woman collapses under the weight of the case of water.

norm: It's wrong to kill another person with poison.
situation: John has been with his wife for thirty years but isn't attracted to her anymore.
intention: John doesn't want to be with his wife anymore.
moral_action: John divorces his wife and finds another woman to date.
moral_consequence: John's wife remains healthy and John finds love elsewhere.
immoral_action: John slips some poison into his wife's coffee one morning.
immoral_consequence: John's wife dies and after an autopsy John is arrested.

norm: You shouldn't break your promises.
situation: Jesse told Jenna that he would take her to the movies tonight, but Jesse's friend, Eric, invited him to play pool, which Jesse would prefer.
intention: Jesse wants to act on Eric's invitation.
moral_action: Jesse tell's Eric he made a commitment to take Jenna to see a film and tell's Eric they can try to go next weekend.
moral_consequence: Jenna is thrilled to go out with Jesse and has a great time.
immoral_action: Jesse accepts Eric's invitation figuring he and Jenna can go another time to catch a movie.
immoral_consequence: Jenna is hurt because she was looking forward to this night with Jesse.

norm: It's good to ask family to plan a wedding.
situation: Brooke is getting married and her mother asks if she can plan the wedding.
intention: Brooke wants to have the best wedding possible.
moral_action: Brooke tells her mother she would love to have her plan the wedding.
moral_consequence: Brooke's mother plans the best wedding imaginable and Brooke has a magical wedding that she will remember forever.
immoral_action: Brooke tells her mother no because she wants to hire a professional to plan the wedding.
immoral_consequence: Brooke's mother's feelings are hurt, and she decides to not attend the wedding which hurts Brooke's feelings as well.

norm: Children aren't expected to raise their voice to a parent.
situation: Joanne glares at her mother Jane who broke her promise to take her to the park for the sixth time.
intention: Joanne wants to express her disappointment.
moral_action: Joanne writes a note to her mother with her feelings and leaves it on her mother's bed.
moral_consequence: Joanne receives a cookie and an apology from her mother.
immoral_action: Joanne stops her foot on the ground and says that she hates promise breakers in a loud tone of voice.
immoral_consequence: Joanne is sent to her room for being disrespectful.

norm: It's rude to gossip.
situation: Sam is hanging out in the park with her friends.
intention: Sam wants to chat with her friends.
moral_action: Sam asks everyone how they are doing lately.
moral_consequence: Sam has a good conversation with her friends and feels closer to them afterwards.
immoral_action: Sam tells her friends a secret she know about one of their other friends.
immoral_consequence: Sam is belittled and shunned by her friends for gossiping about others.

norm: It is rude to ignore your elders.
situation: Timmy'a grandmother asks him to get her something from the other room.
intention: Timmy wants to watch TV.
