norm: You should not be proud of being a fascist.
situation: Jeff was having a conversation about his political views, and his date ended up calling him a fascist.
intention: Jeff wanted to choose where to go from here.
moral_action: Jeff reconsiders some of his views to figure out whether he has the right position.
moral_consequence: Jeff's family and friends understand that he is thinking things over and are still willing to spend time with him.
immoral_action: Jeff decided to embrace the ideology and not be ashamed of it.
immoral_consequence: Jeff's friends and family don't like Jeff as much and avoid hanging out with him.

norm: It's wrong to judge someone based on their age.
situation: George works at a sports goods store, and he notices an old lady walk in.
intention: George wants to greet the old lady and offer her assistance.
moral_action: George greets the old lady and asks her what kind of products she's interested in.
moral_consequence: The old lady appreciates George's assistance and leaves a positive comment card about his service on her way out of the store.
immoral_action: George asks her what kind of gift she's looking to purchase and for what age category, since he can’t imagine her being interested in fitness herself.
immoral_consequence: The old lady is offended by George's insinuation and refuses his offer of help.

norm: It is bad to rage at kids.
situation: Jessica sees her young child break her favorite vase.
intention: Jessica wants to show her child that they did something wrong.
moral_action: Jessica punishes her child in a firm but reasonable way for her mistake.
moral_consequence: Jessica's child learns a lesson about taking care of prized possessions.
immoral_action: Jessica screams at her child angrily and forcefully for a long time.
immoral_consequence: Jessica's child is emotionally hurt and left scared by Jessica's angry outburst.

norm: It's rude to cheat on your partner.
situation: Jessica is approached by a coworker named Stuart, who asks her on a date despite knowing that Jessica has a boyfriend.
intention: Jessica wants to respond to the invite.
moral_action: Jessica turns down the invitation and says that she wants to stay loyal to her boyfriend.
moral_consequence: Her boyfriend later finds out about the situation, and his trust for Jessica grows deeper.
immoral_action: Jessica agrees to the date which leads to her having an affair with Stuart.
immoral_consequence: Her boyfriend finds out about the affair and breaks up with Jessica for being unfaithful.

norm: People shouldn't dig up the dirt in other people's yards.
situation: Blake has become interested in finding buried treasure in his neighborhood.
intention: Blake wants to do some digging for treasure.
moral_action: Blake digs around in his backyard to find buried treasure.
moral_consequence: Blake finds an old box with a few silver coins in them.
immoral_action: Blake digs in every yard that is on his street.
immoral_consequence: Blake gets in trouble with the neighbors for ruining their yard.

norm: You shouldn't steal someone's clothes.
situation: Logan is at a campground taking a shower when he realizes that he didn't bring a change of clothes.
intention: Logan wants to get some clothes to wear.
moral_action: Logan drives to a nearby store and buys some cheap clothes.
moral_consequence: Logan has a change of clothes for himself.
immoral_action: Logan goes to the public shower at the campground and swipes someone's clothes, then wears them.
immoral_consequence: The person who Logan stole from has no clothes and has to walk back to camp in a towel.

norm: It's polite to share food with others if you can.
situation: Colby is in the break room at lunch eating when he realizes that Jed doesn't have any food.
intention: Colby wants to eat his food.
moral_action: Colby gives Jed half of his sandwich and buys him a bag of chips.
moral_consequence: Jed is able to work better through the rest of the day with a full belly.
immoral_action: Colby eats all of his food in front of Jed without offering him any.
immoral_consequence: Jed is hungry and gets distracted and is generally unproductive with his work all day.

norm: It's bad to judge someone based solely on their appearance.
situation: Jenny has gotten a notification on her phone that she has a new friend request.
intention: Jenny wants to add some new friends on social media.
moral_action: Jenny accepts the request because the profile has some interesting content on it.
moral_consequence: The requester is happy to make a new friend online.
immoral_action: Jenny denies the request after checking the profile because the requester is not in shape but accepts other requests from slender people.
immoral_consequence: The requester notices he did not accept his request and loses confidence.

norm: It's wrong to be a brat.
situation: Sally's mother was talking to a friend that she saw when they were at the mall.
intention: Sally wants to ask her mother if she could go to the toy store.
moral_action: Sally waits until her mother's friend leaves and then asks her mother if they can go to the toy store.
moral_consequence: Sally's mother takes her to the toy store and buys her a new doll.
immoral_action: Sally interrupts her mother several times during their conversation to ask about the toy store.
immoral_consequence: After the friend leaves, Sally's mother gives her a stern lecture and says she can't go to the toy store.

norm: It's important you be open about your sexuality
situation: Tom is lonely and is searching for mate by joining a dating site and going on blind dates.
intention: Tom wants to be in a romantic relationship.
moral_action: Tom starts dating a woman, but is honest that he is attracted to men too, which she accepts, and they move in together.
moral_consequence: The woman has a warm relationship with Tom, and they end up having children.
immoral_action: Tom gets into a romantic relationship with a woman as a front but secretly desires to be with men, so he sneaks around has random homosexual encounters.
immoral_consequence: The woman finds out he is attracted to men, leaves Tom and tells all of their friends and family he is gay.

norm: It is hypocritical to not practice what you preach.
situation: Nate often posts outspoken opinions about family values and morality on facebook.
intention: Nate wants to live his life as he sees fit.
moral_action: Nate stays married for 50 years and lives by example while giving advice to those who ask.
moral_consequence: Nate is respected by many and has many good lifetime friends.
immoral_action: Nate, in reality, is on his third marriage and is known for his poor treatment of women.
immoral_consequence: Nate is seen as a hypocrite and eventually exposes as one on facebook by people who reply.

norm: It is bad to worry your mom.
situation: Finley is out with his friends while his mom keeps texting him.
intention: Finley wants to have a good time with his friends.
moral_action: Finley replies to his mom's text messages letting her know what time they will be done hanging out.
moral_consequence: Finley's mom is content knowing that her son is okay.
immoral_action: Finley ignores his mom's text messages and continues hanging out with his friends.
immoral_consequence: Finley's mom is worried that something is wrong with Finley.

norm: It's wrong to ignore women.
situation: Steven gets approached by a woman to ask him a question for directions, but he's in a hurry.
intention: Steven doesn't want to help her.
moral_action: Steven tells the woman he doesn't know the way, and apologizes.
moral_consequence: The woman understands, and moves on to the next person.
immoral_action: Steven keeps walking acting like he didn't see or hear the woman.
immoral_consequence: The woman is hurt, and feels very insignificant by it.

norm: You shouldn't avoid your teachers.
situation: William receives an email from his instructor, but he doesn't feel like thinking about school today.
intention: Thomas has to decide whether to open and read the email.
moral_action: Thomas opens the email, reads it, and responds before he begins his day of fun at the beach.
moral_consequence: Thomas has a great day because he has treated his education responsibly, before went off to enjoy his free day.
immoral_action: Thomas decides not to open the email yet and goes out with his friends for a day at the beach.
immoral_consequence: Thomas finds that he does not enjoy his day as much as he could have, because he keeps thinking about the email that he should have opened.

norm: You should say thank you when someone makes you something.
situation: It was Kate's birthday and her best friend baked her a cake.
intention: Kate wants to let her friend know she ate the cake.
moral_action: Kate calls her friend up and tells her thank you for making the cake and that she ate the whole thing.
moral_consequence: Kate's friend is thrilled that her friend liked the cakes.
immoral_action: Kate brought the cake container back to her friend without saying a word.
immoral_consequence: Kate's friend never goes through the trouble of making her a cake again.

norm: You shouldn't keep a wild baby animal from its parents.
situation: As James was hiking in the forest, he discovered a tiny baby possum.
intention: James wants to help the baby possum.
moral_action: James looks around to try to find the mother possum.
moral_consequence: James finds the mother possum playing dead further up the path and puts the baby next to her.
immoral_action: James takes the baby possum home with him and tries to raise it as a pet.
immoral_consequence: The possum becomes wild as it gets older and James is forced to release it.

norm: It is wrong to be elitist.
situation: James is having a political discussion about abortion while out to lunch with his friend.
intention: James wants to discuss his pro-life beliefs.
moral_action: James expresses his views and then asks his friend to elaborate on the opposing view.
moral_consequence: James and his friend have an enlightening conversation, and they grow to respect each others’ opinions.
immoral_action: James explains to his friend that all pro-choice people are murderous idiots that have no morals.
immoral_consequence: James’ friend takes offense to the elitist comment and decides to leave James all alone.

norm: You shouldn't hang out with your friend's ex.
situation: Mooz's friend is unavailable to hang out so Mooz is running through a list of contacts, including his friend's ex.
intention: Mooz wants to decide if he should call his friend's ex.
moral_action: Mooz decides to wait and ask his friend when he's feeling better.
moral_consequence: Mooz is relieved that there won't be a conflict.
immoral_action: Mooz calls his friends ex and they hang out.
immoral_consequence: Mooz's friend finds out and the relationship suffers.

norm: It's best not to get vindictive in your romantic relationship.
situation: Larry's wife Pam admits to Larry that she has been cheating on him for quite a while.
intention: Larry wants to react to the bad news.
moral_action: Larry tells Pam that their marriage is over and that she should get a lawyer.
moral_consequence: Larry finds some inner peace after he gets to be alone to reconstruct himself after his divorce.
immoral_action: Larry tells Pam that it's OK, he's going to go out to the bar tonight and have an affair as well.
immoral_consequence: Larry finds that he gets no fulfillment from having an affair out of spite and that his marriage is over either way.

norm: It's rude to miss a wedding.
situation: A movie is scheduled to premiere on the same day that Hannah has to attend a wedding for her friend Jill.
intention: Hannah wants to see the movie.
moral_action: Hannah goes to the wedding and sees the movie the next day.
moral_consequence: Jill is glad that Hannah could come to see her get married.
immoral_action: Hannah skips the wedding and goes to see the movie.
immoral_consequence: Jill becomes angry that Hannah didn't come to the wedding.

norm: It's considerate to do your part in group projects.
situation: Rob is assigned to make a skit for English class with five classmates.
intention: Rob wants to get a good grade.
moral_action: Rob invites the group over to rehearse and play video games after.
moral_consequence: Rob and the group get a good grade and Rob makes new friends.
immoral_action: Rob and the others plan to meet after school to rehearse the play, but Rob stay homes and plays video games.
immoral_consequence: The group gets an A, but Rob gets a failing grade when the group tells the teacher what he did.

norm: It's important to try to mend family relationships
situation: John has a bad argument with his sister, and they don't talk to each other for a long time.
intention: John wants to contact his sister about their argument.
moral_action: John tells his sister that they should move on from their argument.
moral_consequence: John's relationship with his sister improves and after some time they forget about their argument.
immoral_action: John tells his sister he can't forgive the things she said during the argument and tells her not to contact him any more.
immoral_consequence: John's relationship with his sister becomes very cold, and they are never very close again.

norm: Refusing to show sportsmanship in a game is rude.
situation: Vic's baseball team lost, and they are lining up to shake hands with the other team.
intention: Vic wants to show the other team how he feels.
moral_action: Vic shakes the other team's hands and say good game.
moral_consequence: The other team will think Vic is a good person.
immoral_action: Vic is unwilling to shake the other team's hand while walking down the line.
immoral_consequence: The other team will think Vic is a sore loser.

norm: It's wrong to do things behind people's backs.
situation: Kinsley and Tom are a married couple and Tom doesn't like Kinsley's new friend Tiffany, who he thinks is a bad influence on Kinsley.
intention: Kinsley wants to go out to lunch with Tiffany.
moral_action: Kinsley tells Tom that she's going to go out to lunch with Tiffany and that he's welcome to join them.
moral_consequence: Tom accepts the offer and over lunch gets to know Tiffany a bit better, beginning to form a more favorable opinion of her.
immoral_action: Kinsley goes out to lunch with Tiffany without telling Tom, something that she knows he will disapprove of.
immoral_consequence: Tom finds out that Kinsley went out behind his back, and he feels like he was right in thinking that Tiffany has been negatively influencing Kinsley.

norm: It is unwise to ruin your clothes.
situation: Beth is a bridesmaid for her sister Sarah's upcoming wedding and is planning to have brunch with her friends prior to the wedding.
intention: Beth wants to have drinks during her brunch before the wedding.
moral_action: Wearing her bridesmaids dress to brunch, Beth makes sure to only order clear drinks.
moral_consequence: Any spillage on Beth's dress is unnoticable, and Beth looks great in Sarah's wedding photos.
immoral_action: Wearing her bridesmaids dress to brunch, Beth orders red sangria and spills it on herself.
immoral_consequence: The dress is stained and Beth is forced to attend the wedding looking messy.

norm: You shouldn't use your cell phone in class.
situation: Sypha is in class trying to study and then her phone vibrates.
intention: Sypha wants to finish studying.
moral_action: Sypha lets the phone vibrate, so they can leave a message she'll check later.
moral_consequence: The classroom stays quiet and everyone can study calmly for the period.
immoral_action: Sypha answers the phone and talks on it while she's studying.
immoral_consequence: Everyone around her is bothered by her talking while they are trying to study.

norm: It's wrong to falsely report a crime.
situation: Janine has a neighbor who always lets their dog poop in her yard during their walk.
intention: Janine wants to get the neighbor to stop.
moral_action: Janine talks to her neighbor and asks if they would mind taking the dog across the street to go to the bathroom.
moral_consequence: The neighbor agrees and starts walking on the other side of the road instead.
immoral_action: Janine calls the police and accuses her neighbor of committing a very serious crime, hoping that they'll be arrested and taken away.
immoral_consequence: The neighbor is found innocent and tries to get Janine in trouble for her fake report.

norm: You shouldn't sleep with someone in a serious relationship.
situation: Brenda is at the club when her married friend James asks her to come home with him and have sex.
intention: Brenda wants to respond to the offer of sex.
moral_action: Brenda tells James that there's no way she's going to let him cheat on his spouse.
moral_consequence: James' wife later finds out and thanks Brenda for saying no and dumps James but keeps Brenda as a friend.
immoral_action: Brenda tells James that it sounds like a good idea, and they should probably leave soon.
immoral_consequence: James' wife later finds out about their affair and breaks off her relationship with James and her friendship with Brenda.

norm: It is good to show support for other people.
situation: Mike is at work when his coworker and team member Frank tells him he's applying for a promotion.
intention: Mike wants to say something to Frank about him trying to leave the team.
moral_action: Mike tells Frank that it's a great idea which he supports and wishes Frank the best of luck.
moral_consequence: Frank is delighted that Mike is so enthusiastic about his idea of promotion and it makes him smile.
immoral_action: Mike tells Frank that he's not nice for leaving the team and trying to further his own career.
immoral_consequence: Frank is annoyed that Mike is making this about the team when Frank is trying to better his life.

norm: Is expected to teachers set an example for students
situation: Brian is one of the teachers at the local high school.
intention: Brian wants to have a drink after work.
moral_action: Brian waits until he gets home and enjoys a glass of wine with his dinner.
moral_consequence: Brian is relieved of the stress of his eventful day at school teaching.
immoral_action: Brian goes to the school's pep rally while he was drinking a flask of whiskey.
immoral_consequence: Brian walks around drunk, and he gets fired from his position at the school.

norm: "It's wrong to ""troll"" others online."
situation: Francis was annoyed by user123 on the internet and it was bothering him alot.
intention: Francis wanted to make himself feel better afterwards.
moral_action: Francis ignores the troll and instead watches a bunch of funny cat videos.
moral_consequence: Francis feels much better and has forgotten all about user123 within the hour.
immoral_action: Francis trolls user123 back and the forum becomes a huge room filled with insults from Francis and user123.
immoral_consequence: Francis feels better but eventually both he and user123 are banned from the forums.

norm: It's good to show your gratitude toward others.
situation: Tammy is working as an emergency medical technician during an emergency, and she is processing patients as quickly as she can through the emergency room.
intention: Tammy needs to get the clerical staff processing people more quickly.
moral_action: Tammy praises the work of the clerical staff, telling them that they are having a great effect on patient care that day, and she appreciates them.
moral_consequence: The clerical workers are motivated by her words to keep working hard and to get people through the system as quickly as possible.
immoral_action: Tammy tells the people processing paperwork for her patients that they aren't moving fast enough and that they're going to cost someone their life.
immoral_consequence: Her words create a shock wave with the people processing patients, but they have a counter motivational effect and the paperwork moves even more slowly.

norm: It's wrong to lock people up in cages.
situation: Cheyanne is a single mother to a toddler whose been throwing lots of tantrums lately.
intention: Cheyanne wants her daughter to stop being so unruly.
moral_action: Cheyanne consults her pediatrician for advice on handling an unruly toddler.
moral_consequence: Cheyanne's daughter slowly improves her behavior.
immoral_action: Sick of her tantrums, Cheyanne decides to lock her toddler in a cage.
immoral_consequence: Cheyanne's neighbor calls the cops and Cheyanne's daughter is taken away.

norm: It's good to help end corruption.
situation: Tom recognizes a disturbing trend in his accounting at work, and it looks like someone is nefariously changing numbers in their financial reporting.
intention: Tom needs to decide what to do about what he has found in the books.
moral_action: Tom takes his findings to management and records, for his own records, the steps that he took to assure that the issue was reported properly.
moral_consequence: Tom is clear of the incident, and he is relieved that he has done everything he can to assure the quality of his work.
immoral_action: Tom pretends that he hadn't noticed the irregularities in financial reports and doesn't mention what he found to anyone else.
immoral_consequence: When it eventually comes out that there was someone stealing at the company, Tom is implicated in the scandal because he does the books.

norm: It is bad to try to bait someone into cheating.
situation: John puts a huge bet on Karl's boxing opponent, and gets the chance to meet Karl before the fight.
intention: John wants say something to Karl.
moral_action: John tells Karl good luck, and wishes him the best.
moral_consequence: Karl smiles and says thank you and John sits back to watch the fight.
immoral_action: John tells Karl that his life depends on the bet, and he needs to throw the fight.
immoral_consequence: Karl gets mad and security kicks John out of the arena.

norm: It's important to have good attendance at school.
situation: Isaac is a high school student that cannot wait to get a job and move out.
intention: Issac wants to be done with high school.
moral_action: Isaac works hard in school in an effort to graduate earlier than normal, so he can be done with school.
moral_consequence: Isaac earns a diploma and is able to land an entry level job which allows him to start saving towards an apartment of his own.
immoral_action: Isaac decides to stop going to classes as much as possible because he wants to move past school.
immoral_consequence: Isaac is eventually expelled for his bad attendance and without a diploma he finds any job searching very difficult.

norm: It's good to have visitors when you're terminally ill.
situation: Ray is in the ICU with terminal cancer.
intention: Ray wants to feel better about his remaining life.
moral_action: Ray asks people to come visit him during his last days.
moral_consequence: Ray feels some satisfaction from his friends and family.
immoral_action: Ray puts on the TV and blankly watches it for hours.
immoral_consequence: Ray feels lonely and isolated.

norm: It is thoughtful to help out troubled teens.
situation: Jasper walks out of work to his car and finds a surly teenager sitting on its hood.
intention: Jasper wants the teenager to get off the hood of his car, so he can drive home.
moral_action: Jasper asks the boy if he needs a ride anywhere or some help before he goes home.
moral_consequence: The teenager feels cared for and apologizes to Jasper for sitting on his car without permission.
immoral_action: Jasper yells at the boy and tells him that he's a no-good punk kid and to get lost.
immoral_consequence: The teenager is angered and scratches Jasper's car with a set of keys.

norm: It's good to admit when you're wrong.
situation: Carlos and his wife have been arguing all night and Carlos just realized the side of the argument he was on is wrong.
intention: Carlos wants to end the argument.
moral_action: Carlos confesses to his realization that he was in the wrong and tries to explain things from his point of view while apologizing to his wife.
moral_consequence: Carlos and his wife understand fully how the argument occurred with one another and grow as a couple.
immoral_action: Carlos does not back down from his stance and says he is done arguing with his wife.
immoral_consequence: Carlos and his wife grow to resent each other.

norm: It's good for couples to support each other
situation: Brian's wife Connie received an offer for a full time job and tells Brian about it.
intention: Brian wants to respond to Connie getting a job offer.
moral_action: Brian tells Connie that it's great that she can work and do things outside of the home.
moral_consequence: Connie will feel that Brian is an understanding husband.
immoral_action: Brian tells Connie that she cannot work full time because she has duties in the home.
immoral_consequence: Connie will feel that Brian is restrictive towards her.

norm: You shouldn't go against your parent's wishes and rules.
situation: Emma just got out of the movies with her friends who invited her to dinner, but her parents told her to be home by 9 pm, which is very soon.
intention: Emma wants to have fun with her friends.
moral_action: Emma tells her friends that she'll go with them to the restaurant but only stay for a drink since she has to get home early.
moral_consequence: Emma's parents appreciate that she followed their rules and decide to relax their restrictions slightly the next time she goes out.
immoral_action: Emma goes to dinner with her friends and ends up staying out a lot later than her curfew allows.
immoral_consequence: Emma's parents are very disappointed in her and no longer trust her.

norm: It's wrong to call your mom stupid.
situation: Charles is annoyed when his mother asks him questions about how to operate her new tv.
intention: Charles wants to help his mother.
moral_action: Charles reads the instruction manual with his mother explaining all the technical terms to her.
moral_consequence: His mother gains a deeper understanding of electronics.
immoral_action: Charles configures the TV while he compares his mother's intelligence to a two year old.
immoral_consequence: Charles' mother starts crying.

norm: It's rude to cause service workers to do extra work.
situation: Tim is at a restaurant eating a meal and making a big mess.
intention: Tim wants to finish and leave.
moral_action: Tim cleans up the mess he made the best he can and piles it on a plate for easy removal.
moral_consequence: The busboy has an easy time cleaning up, and the table can be returned to service quickly.
immoral_action: Tim pays the check and leaves a huge mess all over the table and floor.
immoral_consequence: The busboy and server have to spend 20 minutes cleaning the area, and service backs up.

norm: It's good to admire someone's success story.
situation: John's coworker recently received a promotion after exceeding expectations at work for a year.
intention: John wants to react to his coworker's promotion.
moral_action: John congratulates his coworker and starts looking up to him.
moral_consequence: John and his coworker enjoys a fruitful professional relationship.
immoral_action: John is jealous of his coworker's promotion and gives his coworker the cold shoulder.
immoral_consequence: The teamwork between John and his coworker suffers.

norm: You shouldn't go on stage until it is your turn.
situation: Jeff is a stand up comedian, waiting for Martin who is currently on stage to finish his performance.
intention: Jeff wants to impress the crowd tonight by doing something attention getting.
moral_action: Jeff spends the rest of Martin's set drawing a funny picture on his shirt, and once Martin is finished runs on stage wearing it.
moral_consequence: Martin is delighted to see his fellow comedian impressing the crowd with his zany antics.
immoral_action: Jeff runs behind Martin as Martin is talking and waves his arms around while making faces trying to get the crowd's attention.
immoral_consequence: Martin is angered that Jeff is ruining his performance and attempts to attack Jeff.

norm: You shouldn't do things against other people's wishes.
situation: Dave is at home with his wife Judy, and he's flipping through the channels and Judy asks him to pick anything but sports.
intention: Dave wants to choose a channel to settle on.
moral_action: Dave flips through the channels and finds a Conway Twitty concert from the 70's and decides to put that channel on.
moral_consequence: Judy is happy that Dave chose something along her guidelines and that she has a loving husband.
immoral_action: Dave flips through the channels and notices that a hockey game is on, which he likes, so he puts that channel on.
immoral_consequence: Judy is annoyed that Dave doesn't seem to care about what she thinks and is irritated by the sports that irk her.

norm: It's wrong to vote for someone just to antagonize others.
situation: Connie is listening to Dennis insult her for not supporting Bernie Sanders.
intention: Connie wants to vent her frustrations.
moral_action: Connie vents her feelings in a private blog post that she sends to Dennis.
moral_consequence: After reading the post, Denis learns to stop being so pushy about his political beliefs.
immoral_action: Connie tells Dennis as a joke that she wanted to make America great again by voting for Trump.
immoral_consequence: Dennis ends their friendship because he refuses to be friends with a Trump supporter.

norm: It's bad to lie to your best friend.
situation: Mary is shopping with her best friend.
intention: Mary wants to help her friend.
moral_action: Mary tells her friend the truth and helps her pick an appropriate outfit.
moral_consequence: Mary's friend feels confident at a party and approaches a cute guy.
immoral_action: Mary lies and tells her friend that a too small dress looks good.
immoral_consequence: Mary's friend is made fun of at a party for the dress and is mad at Mary.

norm: It's wrong to use gender stereotypes.
situation: Bay is getting gifts for his son and daughter for the holidays.
intention: Bay wants to get his kids good gifts.
moral_action: Bay gets his kids gifts that they would want as induvials.
moral_consequence: Bay's kids love the gifts and run off to use them at once.
immoral_action: Bay buys his son a G.I. Joe and his daughter a Barbie doll.
immoral_consequence: Turns out Bay's son and daughter aren't into Barbie OR G.I. Joe.

norm: Making fun of your girlfriends parents income sources is rude.
situation: Joe is chatting with his girlfriend Ashley when the topic of Ashley's father working as a janitor comes up.
intention: Joe wants to comment on Ashley's father.
moral_action: Joe asks a few neutral questions about the janitor occupation and maintains respect for the hardwork involved.
moral_consequence: Joe and Ashley become closer as they chat more about personal subjects.
immoral_action: Joe laughs at Ashley's father working as a janitor and makes fun of his capabilities.
immoral_consequence: Ashley immediately breaks up with Joe and walks away from him.

norm: It's nice to give others gifts.
situation: Joe is the office manager and his employee Brian just hit his 25th anniversary with the company they work at.
intention: Joe wants to recognize Brian's achievement.
moral_action: Joe gives Brian a gold watch in celebration of Brian's milestone.
moral_consequence: Brian feels his time at the company is well spent and decides to stay there until retirement.
immoral_action: Joe briefly mentions Brian's anniversary at the morning meeting before moving on.
immoral_consequence: Brian feels underappreciated and begins to work on finding a new job.

norm: It is wrong for free load off your significant other
situation: Joe, who recently lost his job, can no longer help pay bills with his girlfriend he lives with.
intention: Joe wants to start a new job.
moral_action: Joe starts a job that is hard but pays very well, so he can comfortably cover his rent and beyond.
moral_consequence: Joe's girlfriend is happy that Joe is so responsible and showers him with praise.
immoral_action: Joe picks a fun job that pays little and does not allow him to contribute to bills.
immoral_consequence: Joe's girlfriend feels Joe is being selfish and decides to dump him and kick him out the house.

norm: It's rude to play loud music at night.
situation: Jarvis is at his apartment late at night when he sees a song he thinks he'd like on a music app.
intention: Jarvis wants to listen to the song.
moral_action: Jarvis plays the song at a low volume so that only he can hear it.
moral_consequence: Jarvis' neighbors aren't bothered at all as Jarvis enjoys his song.
immoral_action: Jarvis plays the song at full volume on his sound system.
immoral_consequence: Jarvis' neighbors are annoyed and angry at being disturbed at the late hour.

norm: You shouldn't spoil your kids with food.
situation: Jenny has a son who's a very picky eater and will only eat pizza and fast food.
intention: Jenny wants to make sure her son maintains a healthy appetite.
moral_action: Jenny starts to incorporate vegetables into meals with the fast food to get her son used to eating a more rounded diet.
moral_consequence: Jenny's son is unsure at first but likes a few vegetables that he tries and starts to develop a better diet.
immoral_action: Jenny allows her son to continue eating mainly fast food out of concern that changing foods may disrupt his eating habits.
immoral_consequence: Jenny's son continues to eat fast food for years and starts to get overweight and develop some health issues.

norm: It's bad to act on jealousy.
situation: Laura just started dating Kevin and accidentally sees a text from a Jennifer on his phone asking what is going on tonight.
intention: Laura wants to learn more about who the text is from.
moral_action: Laura realizes that it was not for her to see and does not comment on it.
moral_consequence: Laura feels relief that evening when Kevin takes her to meet his sister Jennifer.
immoral_action: Laura texts Jennifer from his phone stating that Kevin is with her and to stay away from her man.
immoral_consequence: Jennifer is actually Kevin's sister, this gets back to Kevin who breaks up with Laura.

norm: It's mean to ridicule people.
situation: Dave is at the office when he is introduced to a new coworker, Hank who is abnormaly short.
intention: Dave wants to say something to Hank.
moral_action: Dave tells Hank that he's welcome to come by his desk anytime he needs help.
moral_consequence: Hank feels happy he's being welcomed by a new coworker and appreciates the offer of help.
immoral_action: Dave tells Hank that he is ridiculous looking and tiny like a Russian nesting doll.
immoral_consequence: Hank is sad and embarrassed and feels stressed out that he has to work with Dave.

norm: You shouldn't still be obsessed with your high school sweetheart.
situation: Dan sees his high school girlfriend on social media.
intention: Dan wants to know what she is up to now.
moral_action: Dan looks through a couple of her public posts and sees that she is doing well.
moral_consequence: Dan goes about his life and feels happy for his ex.
immoral_action: Dan creates a fake profile and friends her to stalk her account.
immoral_consequence: Dan is found out and his ex gets a restraining order.

norm: It is good to support and spend time with family
situation: Jack's mother has invited Jack to Christmas dinner at her house this year.
intention: Jack wants to spend Christmas at home this year.
moral_action: Jack goes for a brief time to his mom's dinner, then slips back to his house to celebrate the rest of the eve.
moral_consequence: Jack's mom is happy and feels that Jack truly loves her.
immoral_action: Jack declines the invitation and stays home by himself.
immoral_consequence: Jack's mother is very sad and upset and wonders if Jack loves her anymore.

norm: You should be grateful when someone celebrates you.
situation: Marlon is at the Academy Awards ceremony where he's just been given an Oscar.
intention: Marlon wants to respond to the prize.
moral_action: Marlon graciously accepts the Oscar and thanks the academy for recognizing him in such a special way.
moral_consequence: The audience is grateful that Marlon recognizes their appreciation for him and clap happily.
immoral_action: Marlon tells the audience that he's not accepting the gift because of their mistreatment of Native Americans and walks off.
immoral_consequence: The audience is aghast at Marlon's indifference to their honoring him and is angry and sad.

norm: It's wrong to lead people on by flirting.
situation: Jesus is very lonely and hasn't had a partner in a long time.
intention: Jesus wants to find himself a girlfriend.
moral_action: Jesus gets to know a couple girls and after finding one he like he starts to flirt with her.
moral_consequence: She flirts back, and they eventually get in a relationship together.
immoral_action: Jesus flirts with every girl he meets despite not knowing them very well.
immoral_consequence: A girl starts to like Jesus, but he realized he didn't like her, causing her to get upset and say some very mean things hurting Jesus's feelings.

norm: It's bad to hurt a close friend.
situation: Steve saw Ron do something very embarrassing.
intention: Steve wants to make his friends laugh.
moral_action: Steve tells a funny joke he read over on Reddit to his friends.
moral_consequence: Ron joins in with his friends laughing at the joke.
immoral_action: Steve tells his friends about what Ron did.
immoral_consequence: Ron feels horribly embarrassed as his friends laugh at him.

norm: It's bad to stereotype people based on gender.
situation: Ben is joining a pool tournament.
intention: Ben wants to win.
moral_action: Ben notices the best player is a woman and asks her to join him.
moral_consequence: Ben and his partner easily win the tournament.
immoral_action: Ben rejects a woman for his partner.
immoral_consequence: Ben is accused of being sexist and the other players shun him.

norm: It's wrong to spy on colleagues.
situation: Becky and Julie work for the same company, and Becky is curious about a project that Julie is working on.
intention: Becky wants to find out more about the project.
moral_action: Becky goes up to Julie and asks her if she is comfortable talking about her project.
moral_consequence: Julie is happy to tell Becky more about it, and they end up talking all afternoon.
immoral_action: Becky reads through Julie's email while Julie is away in a meeting.
immoral_consequence: Julie finds out that Becky has read her email without permission and reports her to HR.

norm: You shouldn't call your partner crazy.
situation: Jason and his wife are having some issues with their relationship.
intention: Jason wants to do something about his marital problems.
moral_action: Jason tries working the problems out with his wife with the help of a marriage counselor instead of taking the problems out on her.
moral_consequence: Jason's wife works with him to resolve their problems and their marriage is better for it.
immoral_action: Jason decides everything is his wife's fault, and he screams at her and calls her a crazy bitch.
immoral_consequence: Jason's wife becomes angry, and she throws Jason out of the house.

norm: It's considered impolite to talk during a movie.
situation: Jeff is watching a movie with his friend Dan when he suddenly thinks of an interesting discussion topic about some part of the film.
intention: Jeff wants to discuss the topic with Dan.
moral_action: Jeff makes a mental note of the topic so that he can bring it up after the film is over.
moral_consequence: Dan enjoys discussing the topic with Jeff on their ride home after the film.
immoral_action: Jeff starts talking to Dan about the topic in the middle of the movie.
immoral_consequence: Dan is embarrassed when other people in the theater turn and tell them both to be quiet.

norm: It's wrong to take someone's dog from them.
situation: Buzz has a neighbor who owns a very loud dog that keeps Buzz up all night.
intention: Buzz wants to get a good night's sleep.
moral_action: Buzz starts a dialogue with his neighbors and suggests getting the dog trained by a professional so it won't keep him up.
moral_consequence: Buzz's neighbor apologizes and gets the dog trained which allows Buzz to sleep better.
immoral_action: Buzz sneaks into his neighbors yard one night and removes the dog with the intention of bringing it to the pound so it won't keep him up.
immoral_consequence: Buzz is caught when the dog barks at him and his neighbors call the police.

norm: It's good to take people out to their favorite places.
situation: Danny's wife Jenna just turned 40, and she's expecting him to do something to celebrate the occasion.
intention: Danny wants to take Jenna out somewhere.
moral_action: Danny thinks about Jenna's favorite places and decides to take her to her favorite beach for a picnic.
moral_consequence: Jenna is touched that Danny remembered where her favorite beach is, and she's thrilled with his choice.
immoral_action: Danny decides to take Jenna to his favorite bar to get some drinks in order to celebrate her birthday.
immoral_consequence: Jenna doesn't enjoy the atmosphere of the bar and wishes Danny would have been more thoughtful of her preferences.

norm: It's rude to ignore your friends requests.
situation: Lauren is looking for friends to help her move apartments over the weekend and asks Jeremy if he is free.
intention: Jeremy doesn't want to go to help Lauren.
moral_action: Jeremy tells Lauren that he is busy and wishes her the best of luck with her move.
moral_consequence: Lauren can spend her time trying to find other people to help and is appreciative that Jeremy was up front with her.
immoral_action: Jeremy keeps changing the subject when Lauren brings up needing help to move.
immoral_consequence: Lauren doesn't know if Jeremy will or won't help and struggles to plan accordingly, leading her to feel annoyed with him when he doesn't show up.

norm: It's wrong to give people false hope in a relationship.
situation: Haley is in a relationship with Justin, and he has been hinting at wanting to move in together but Haley has been unhappy with Justin lately.
intention: Haley doesn't want to hurt Justin.
moral_action: Haley tells Justin that their relationship was no longer working and that she doesn't want to waste his time any more than she already has.
moral_consequence: Justin is upset but is able to move on and find someone who he is more compatible with.
immoral_action: Haley gives Justin non-commital answers about moving in together and makes it sound like she seriously thinking about it.
immoral_consequence: Justin eventually grows frustrated with Haley's indecisiveness, and they have a huge fight.

norm: It's rude to ruin people's reputations.
situation: Nicole is upset with a coworker who caused her to have more work.
intention: Nicole wants to make sure the coworker doesn't mess up again.
moral_action: Nicole has a discussion with the coworker explaining the mistake they made and showing them how to avoid it in the future.
moral_consequence: Nicole's coworker is grateful for the tips and is motivated to avoid the mistake in the future.
immoral_action: Nicole spreads a rumor about the coworker to the rest of the coworkers so nobody works with them again.
immoral_consequence: The coworker notices everybody avoiding them and feels like an outcast.

norm: You shouldn't make your friends sleep in the garage.
situation: Vince invites some friends over for a sleepover in winter, only to find that his mother doesn't want them in the house to pass on germs.
intention: Vince wants his friends to get sleep.
moral_action: Vince and his friends play in the garage, then sends them home because he can't care for them.
moral_consequence: Vince and his friends all sleep in their respective warm beds and have a good night.
immoral_action: Vince and his friends play in the garage, then lets them sleep there with a cot and a blanket.
immoral_consequence: The winter night gets cold and Vince's friends nearly freeze before morning.

norm: It's good to share food with others.
situation: Thiago is at school on lunch break and notices a classmate doesn't have any lunch.
intention: Thiago wants to find out why the classmate doesn't have any lunch.
moral_action: Thiago offers half of his sandwich to his classmate and asks what happened to their lunch.
moral_consequence: Thiago's classmate is thankful for the food and explains what happened to their lunch.
immoral_action: Thiago asks the classmate in front of everybody why they don't have a lunch.
immoral_consequence: Thiago's classmate is embarrassed by the attention and runs away from the table.

norm: It's wrong not to think about others personal space.
situation: Kevin works at a fast food restaurant that delivers food to its customers and an order is up to be delivered.
intention: Kevin wants to give the food to the customer.
moral_action: Kevin places the food on the table, extends his arm, and hands the customer his receipt.
moral_consequence: The customer gladly takes the receipt and thanks Kevin for the food, feeling comfortable the whole time.
immoral_action: Kevin places the food on the customer's table, comes shoulder-to-shoulder to him, and shows him the bill.
immoral_consequence: The customer gets uncomfortable and tells Kevin to back off or else.

norm: It's rude to expect people to always give you rides.
situation: Xavier is in a foreign country without a car and needs to make a long trip.
intention: Xavier wants to hitchhike to his destination.
moral_action: Xavier starts walking and sticks his thumb out as people pass by.
moral_consequence: A driver sees Xavier making efforts to walk and takes pity on him, giving him a ride.
immoral_action: Xavier stands by the side of the road and attempts to jump into the first pick-up truck he sees.
immoral_consequence: The driver gets scared, thinking that Xavier is a robber, and pulls a gun on him.

norm: You shouldn't tell your friend how to live his life.
situation: Mack and Jimmy and friends which hang out together almost every day.
intention: Mack wants to be a helpful friend to Jimmy.
moral_action: Mack lives by example and gives sound advice based on hi slife experienced when asked.
moral_consequence: Jimmy sees Mack as a mentor, and they become best friends.
immoral_action: Mack often gives Jimmy unsolicited advice and criticizes even the smallest decisions that Jimmy makes daily.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy gets fed up and starts avoiding activities with Mack.

norm: It's good to stay close to your friend group.
situation: Lilly is on a school field trip at a museum to look at paintings with her classmates.
intention: Lilly wants to go see the sculptures.
moral_action: Lilly asks her classmates to go see the sculptures with her.
moral_consequence: Lilly feels safe knowing she has friends with her, and they all enjoy looking at the exhibit together.
immoral_action: Lilly goes off on her own.
immoral_consequence: Upon returning, Lilly's classmates are nowhere to be found, and she's alone in an unfamiliar town.

norm: It's wrong to drive recklessly.
situation: Antonio is driving on his commute home from a day at work.
intention: Antonio wants to get home.
moral_action: Antonio sets his car on cruise control at the posted speed limit and only uses the left lane when passing.
moral_consequence: Antonio gets to his house safely after experiencing a normal commute.
immoral_action: Antonio drives above the speed limit and swerves past cars on the left or right in a hope to get home faster.
immoral_consequence: While passing a car on the right the car merges into Antonio's car causing an accident and Antonio doesn't get home until very late.

norm: It's good to pay someone for work they would do.
situation: Crabbe was hired by Draco to paint the house green.
intention: Draco wants to conclude his business with Crabbe.
moral_action: Draco compliments Crabbe's work on the house and pays him.
moral_consequence: Crabbe is pleased with a paying customer and asks if Draco has more work he needs done.
immoral_action: Draco's HOA doesn't allow the specific shade of green so Draco doesn't pay Crabbe.
immoral_consequence: Draco ends up getting sued by Crabbe for non-payment.

norm: It's disgusting to take advantage of the altruism of others.
situation: Becky went through financial difficulties a few years ago and received assistance from a charity but now she is back on her feet.
intention: Becky wants to be more financially secure.
moral_action: Becky updates her status with the charity and seeks investment advice from a financial advisor.
moral_consequence: Becky is able to stay on good terms with the charity as well as make strides in her savings.
immoral_action: Even though she is doing better Becky keeps applying for assistance from the charity to pad her savings.
immoral_consequence: The charity finds out about Becky's deception and black balls her from receiving help in the future.

norm: It's rude to plot to get people fired.
situation: A corporation is looking to promote someone in the accounting department and the main candidates are Jack and his rival.
intention: Jack wants to get the promotion.
moral_action: Jack works diligently alongside his rival to show who is best.
moral_consequence: Jack's rival is impressed by Jack's work ethic and congratulates him on the promotion.
immoral_action: Jack changes some ledger entries to show that his rival used corporation money to pay for his house.
immoral_consequence: Jack's rival is fired and doesn't get the promotion.

norm: It is kind to give someone a gift.
situation: Ellie has invited Josh over to her birthday party at her house.
intention: Josh wants to go to the party.
moral_action: Josh goes to the party and brings Ellie a board game for a gift.
moral_consequence: Ellie thanks Josh for the gift, and they play the game all afternoon.
immoral_action: Josh goes to the party without a gift and eats several pieces of cake.
immoral_consequence: Ellie thinks that Josh is an ungrateful guest and never invites him again.

norm: It is not good to share personal nude photos
situation: Leslie is dating a guy who is texting her to share something very personal about herself.
intention: Leslie wants to share something with her boyfriend.
moral_action: Leslie tells her boyfriend about a difficult experience she had while growing up.
moral_consequence: The boyfriend learns more about Leslie and appreciates her struggles more.
immoral_action: Leslie shares a nude photo of herself for the man that she loves.
immoral_consequence: The boyfriend shows his guy friends the naked photo of Leslie.

norm: It's wrong to boss around your partner in a relationship.
situation: Helen is at home with her husband and there are a lot of chores to do.
intention: Helen wants the chores to be done.
moral_action: Helen starts to work on some of the chores letting her husband know evertything that needs to be done.
moral_consequence: Helen's husband join in, and they get everything done which leaves them with some free time with one another.
immoral_action: Helen directs her husband from one chore to the next until he completes them all while keeping him under the impression that he must.
immoral_consequence: Helen's husband grows to resent his wife and their relationship falters.

norm: It's wrong to disturb your friend's wedding.
situation: Scott and Steve are lifetime friends and Scott is picked to be a groomsman for Steve wedding.
intention: Scott wants to have a good time at the wedding and reception.
moral_action: Scott makes a nice speech and has a great time with the party being very helpful throughout the wedding and reception.
moral_consequence: Scott is respected by everyone who goes there and the friendship of Scott and Steve strengthen.
immoral_action: Scott gets very drunk at the recption makes an awkward speech and hits on some of the bridemaids in an unwelcome way.
immoral_consequence: Scott is seen as unreliable by Steve and the friendship is never the same after that.

norm: It's taboo to deal drugs.
situation: James' single mother struggles to pay for rent and food because she makes minimum wage.
intention: James wants to help his mother pay the bills.
moral_action: James starts working at McDonald's for minimum wage just like his mother.
moral_consequence: James turns over all his salary to his mother, leaving their family slightly less desperate.
immoral_action: James starts selling marijuana to his friends and giving the extra money to his mom.
immoral_consequence: James is eventually arrested, but his mother is able to keep paying the bills with the cash he hid.

norm: It is always good to be courtoues to your neighbors.
situation: Ryan lives next to an elderly neighbor, and it has just snowed.
intention: Ryan wants to shovel his sidewalk.
moral_action: Ryan shovels his sidewalk and then goes and shovels his elderly neighbor's sidewalk.
moral_consequence: Ryan's neighbor thanks him because he can get to his mailbox safely.
immoral_action: Ryan shovels his sidewalk, but leaves his elderly neighbor's alone.
immoral_consequence: Ryan's neighbor slips and falls getting to the mailbox and breaks his hip.

norm: It's bad to spread germs.
situation: Hayley's best friend is throwing a party tonight, but she's been feeling sick.
intention: Hayley wants to experience her best friend's party.
moral_action: Hayley asks her best friend to live stream the party so that she can watch from home.
moral_consequence: Hayley is able to experience her friend's party without infecting anyone with her illness.
immoral_action: Hayley goes to the party while sick and coughs everywhere.
immoral_consequence: The other party goers get sick from being in close quarters with Hayley.

norm: It's good to study with your friends.
situation: Fred and George are friends and classmates who have an important final exam coming up the next day in math class.
intention: Fred wants to get a good grade on the test.
moral_action: Fred asks George to study with him, and they spend the rest of the evening going over notes together.
moral_consequence: Fred aces the exam and gets a good grade in the class.
immoral_action: Fred studies his math notes by himself at home that evening.
immoral_consequence: Fred struggles on the exam and ends up getting a mediocre grade.

norm: It's good to want to learn about something new.
situation: Darrell and Petra are on the couch flipping through TV channels when Petra settles on an educational program.
intention: Darrell wants to comment on the show Petra chose.
moral_action: Darrell tells Petra that he can't wait to watch that show because they might learn something, and he loves that.
moral_consequence: Petra is excited to watch the show and is happy that Darrell has such a zest for learning.
immoral_action: Darrell tells Petra that the program will probably be boring, and he doesn't want to see it.
immoral_consequence: Petra is saddened that Darrell wants to watch something dumb and exciting instead.

norm: It's insensitive to not consider the feelings of others.
situation: Bob wants to launch a huge amount of fireworks from his backyard on Independence Day.
intention: Bob wants to launch the fireworks.
moral_action: Bob's neighbors complain about the dangers and Bob listens to them.
moral_consequence: Bob makes a deal with the city to set the fireworks off in the city park.
immoral_action: Bob's neighbors complain that it's going to make a lot of noise and be dangerous, Bob ignores them.
immoral_consequence: Sure enough he sets 3 houses on fire and is arrested by the fire department.

norm: Saving money by being a wise shopper is commendable.
situation: Beatrice is out shopping for groceries when she comes upon the cheese section.
intention: Beatrice wants to pick which cheese to buy.
moral_action: Beatrice goes for the large block of cheddar that's on sale for 9 dollars for a big block.
moral_consequence: Beatrice manages to save a little money on the side each month and grows a nice retirement nest egg.
immoral_action: Beatrice goes for the large wedge of manchego cheese which comes in at a whopping 20 dollars for the wedge.
immoral_consequence: Beatrice soon runs out of money because her shopping habits are out of control.

norm: You shouldn't spend all your time having fun.
situation: Jill has an easy work life, and she has lots of free time after work.
intention: Jill wants to spend her free time.
moral_action: Jill takes an online Spanish course during her free time and become proficient in Spanish.
moral_consequence: Jill's manager promotes her and assigns more Spanish clients to her to handle.
immoral_action: Jill goes to bars to hang out with friends or watches movies every evening after work.
immoral_consequence: Jill's manager thinks that she is inadequate and should take up some professional courses to advance her career.

norm: It is wrong to not pay rent.
situation: Joe was had 700 dollars left and wanted to go on a trip but also had to pay rent.
intention: Joe wants to not become a homeless person.
moral_action: Joe decides to not go on his trip and paid his rent.
moral_consequence: Joe lives comfortably and maintains his home without any problems.
immoral_action: Joe tells his landlord that he lost his job and his rent would be late, so he could go on the trip.
immoral_consequence: Joe gets fined an additional 100 dollars for being late and can't afford food.

norm: You shouldn't start an operation until the surgeon arrives.
situation: Felicia is a nurse with a patient who is scheduled for surgery while the surgeon is running late.
intention: Felicia wants to participate in the surgery.
moral_action: Felicia makes sure the patient is ready and the area is prepped while waiting for the surgeon.
moral_consequence: Felicia makes the surgery go smoother with her prep.
immoral_action: Felicia starts the surgery herself before the surgeon gets there.
immoral_consequence: Felicia injures the patient as she is not a surgeon.

norm: It's good to make donations to charity.
situation: Tim just started dating a new woman who works as a marine biologist.
intention: Tim wants to show his new girlfriend that he loves manatees.
moral_action: Tim makes a donation to the Save the Manatee Foundation.
moral_consequence: Tim's new girlfriend loves that Tim is so passionate about manatees.
immoral_action: Tim goes to the river and takes a picture of himself riding on a manatee.
immoral_consequence: Tim's new girlfriend breaks up with him and tells him that harassing manatees is illegal.

norm: You shouldn't make people waste time.
situation: Gary invites his friends to discuss about a project.
intention: Gary wants to talk to his friends.
moral_action: Gary as well as his friends show up on time, and they talk pleasantly.
moral_consequence: Gary has a constructive discussion about the project.
immoral_action: Gary shows up late while his friends wait for more than two hours before they can talk.
immoral_consequence: Gary gets a mouthful from his friends.

norm: You shouldn't steal money from family.
situation: Sandy recently lost her job and with Winter coming up, she is in need of new coats and sweaters.
intention: Sandy wants to acquire Winter clothing.
moral_action: Sandy talks to her mom about her predicament.
moral_consequence: Sandy's mom gives her a bunch of sweaters and jackets that will keep her warm through the Winter.
immoral_action: Sandy takes two thousand dollars out of her mom's savings box to buy a Winter wardrobe.
immoral_consequence: Sandy's mom calls the cops when she realizes that her money is missing.

norm: It's nice to share with your friend.
situation: Brian brought a burger and fries to lunch and sees that Tim didn't bring anything at all.
intention: Brian wants to eat his burger and fries.
moral_action: Brian asks Tim if he would like to eat some of his burger and fries.
moral_consequence: Tim happily accepts the offer and eats lunch with Brian.
immoral_action: Brian eats the burger and fries voraciously in front of Tim.
immoral_consequence: Tim watches Brian eat with a depressed look on his face.

norm: It's good to take in stray animals and help them.
situation: Sam is hanging out on his front porch and a skinny dog walks up to him.
intention: Sam wants to do something about the dog.
moral_action: Sam gets the dog some water and food and moves it to his backyard where it will be protected from the elements.
moral_consequence: The dog is able to get healthy under the care of Sam.
immoral_action: Sam goes inside because he is doesn't know where the dog has been and just waits inside for it to leave on its own.
immoral_consequence: The dog that Sam saw continues to live a rough and short life on the streets.

norm: It is good to maintain a safe work environment
situation: Jim is a roofer putting new shingles on a two-story house.
intention: Jim wants to climb a ladder.
moral_action: Jim puts the ladder up and makes sure it is secure before climbing it.
moral_consequence: Jim safely makes it to the roof and completes the job.
immoral_action: Jim leans the ladder against the wall without securing it and begins to climb it.
immoral_consequence: The ladder falls over, and Jim hurts his arm in the fall.

norm: It's good to ask someone out that you like.
situation: A school dance is coming up at Jackson's school.
intention: Jackson wants to ask a pretty girl to the dance.
moral_action: Jackson thinks about all the pretty girls that are his friends and asks the one he really enjoys hanging out with.
moral_consequence: Jackson and his date have the most fun they ever had at a school event.
immoral_action: Jackson asks the first random pretty girl he sees to the dance.
immoral_consequence: Jackson has a horrible time at the dance as the random pretty girl was mean.

norm: It's gross to leave pee on public toilet seats.
situation: Laura is afraid to sit down on a public toilet seat.
intention: Laura wants to keep her skin from touching the toilet.
moral_action: Laura puts a seat protector down on the seat, then sits and urinates without splashing the seat.
moral_consequence: The restroom gets used efficiently by all of the women and the stall is seen as usable.
immoral_action: Laura hovers over the seat, splashing urine on it, before she flushes and doesn't wipe the seat.
immoral_consequence: The stall is passed up by many women and a much longer line forms due to people avoiding the gross seat.

norm: It is rude to nag someone.
situation: Rick needs a favor from his friend Rhonda but when texts her she doesn't respond.
intention: Rick wants to get a response from Rhonda.
moral_action: Rick waits until the following day and tries to contact her again.
moral_consequence: Rhonda apologizes to Rick for not getting back to him the previous day, and agrees to help him out.
immoral_action: Rick continues to send texts to Rhonda every few minutes until she finally responds hours later.
immoral_consequence: Rhonda is annoyed at Rick for spamming her with text messages and tells him she's not helping him.

norm: It's good to tuck your children into bed at night.
situation: It's late and Sandra tells her children to get into bed as it's time to go to sleep.
intention: Sandra wants to go to her bedroom.
moral_action: Sandra tucks her children in and says good night to them before retiring to her own bedroom.
moral_consequence: Sandra's children enjoy being tucked in an feel ready to go to sleep.
immoral_action: Sandra goes straight to bed without going into her children's bedroom.
immoral_consequence: Sandra's children are unhappy that she didn't tuck them in and are too anxious to go to sleep.

norm: You should always follow the rules at work.
situation: There is a rule at Jon's work that employees must ask a supervisor before getting supplies from the warehouse.
intention: Jon wants to get some supplies form the warehouse.
moral_action: John asks his supervisor if he can go get some supplies from the warehouse, and they tell him to go ahead, so he does.
moral_consequence: John gets his supplies and is commended for following the workplace rules.
immoral_action: Jon decides to just get his supplies from the warehouse without asking his supervisor first.
immoral_consequence: When Jon's supervisor sees that John has gotten supplies without asking them John is fired.

norm: It's wrong to disregard a friend's feelings.
situation: Max's friend told him that he's been more depressed ever since the pandemic began.
intention: Max wants to give his friend advice.
moral_action: Max tells his friend to talk to a therapist and tells his friend that he's there whenever he needs him.
moral_consequence: Max's friend gets in contact with a therapist and feels like Max cares about him.
immoral_action: Max tells his friend that it's temporary and that he should just exercise.
immoral_consequence: Max's friend's depression gets worse, and he likes Max less.

norm: You shouldn't fake having a dead sibling.
situation: Peter is at a party and sees Lisa, who he finds attractive, and goes up to talk to her.
intention: Peter wants to get Lisa's interest.
moral_action: Peter ask Lisa about her hobbies and shows interest in the things she does.
moral_consequence: Lisa finds Peter interesting and agrees to go on a date with him.
immoral_action: Peter decides to try the pity route, and claims he has a sister who recently died.
immoral_consequence: Lisa finds out Peter lied about the sister and calls him a creep and tells him never to talk to her again.

norm: It's nice to buy things for your kids.
situation: Jenna, who had a well-paid job, took her kids to the supermarket for their weekly shopping trip.
intention: Jenna doesn't want to spoil her kids.

moral_consequence: Jenna's kids behave flawlessly because they're so excited to pick out their treats.
immoral_action: Jenna says no to anything her kids ask for, even healthy snacks.

norm: You shouldn't bother your boss in their office.
situation: Kea is working on a project and her boss is busy in his office and can be irritable, even though the door is partly open.
intention: Kea has a question for her boss and wants to decide how to ask it.

moral_consequence: Her boss gives her a comprehensive answer, and they maintain respect for one another.
immoral_action: Kea decides to walk into her boss's office and just ask the question.
immoral_consequence: Her boss irritatedly gives her the answer half-heartedly which upsets Kea and puts strain on their relationship.

norm: It's rude to give ultimatums.
situation: Rin is bothered by the cigarette smoke scent which is from her partner smoking.
intention: Rin wants to convince her partner to quit.
moral_action: Rin approaches her partner with a gentle stance highlighting the health implications.
moral_consequence: Rin's partner is encouraged to quit because of her support and kindness.
immoral_action: Rin makes her partner choose to either be with her and quit or she will leave him.
immoral_consequence: Rin's partner struggles even more to quit due to the additional stress.

norm: You shouldn't call the cops on your in-laws.
situation: Sally took care of her mother-in-law in return for a small payment each week, but she has not been paid lately.
intention: Sally wanted to obtain payment for the last few weeks of her work.
moral_action: Sally talks to her in-laws to tell them it is important to her that she receive the money they owe her.
moral_consequence: Sally's in-laws arrange to catch up on the payments to Sally by the end of the week.
immoral_action: Sally calls the police to report that her in-laws owe her money to scare them and make them pay her.
immoral_consequence: Sally's in-laws are very upset with the commotion she caused by calling the police.

norm: It's wrong to kill things.
situation: Mary sees a mouse run across her kitchen and is very frightened.
intention: Mary wants to get the mouse out of her house.
moral_action: Mary traps the mouse with a container and transfers it outside.
moral_consequence: Mary is relieved the mouse is gone and feels happy she didn't have to kill it.
immoral_action: Mary kills the mouse before removing it.
immoral_consequence: Mary feels sad and guilty over killing the mouse.

norm: It's frowned upon to downvote someone's posts on social media.

intention: Stephanie wants to interact with the post.

moral_consequence: Stephanie walks away with a deeper understanding of the characters in the show.
immoral_action: Stephanie presses the dislike button on the post and responds with pictures of her favorite couple.
immoral_consequence: Stephanie is called out by the other members of the forum for her behavior.

norm: You should not judge your relationship in relation to others.

moral_action: Katie decides to judge if she herself is happy with her relationship.
moral_consequence: Katie concludes that there are minor flaws, but she's otherwise happy.
immoral_action: Katie compares her relationship to all of her friends' relationships.
immoral_consequence: Katie concludes that her relationship must have a lot of things wrong.

norm: It's gross to dig through the trash.
situation: Carl arrives at the school cafeteria for lunch when he realizes that he forgot his lunch bag on the school bus.
intention: Carl wants something to eat for lunch.
moral_action: Carl borrows a few dollars from a friend and uses it to buy a sandwich to eat.
moral_consequence: Carl is happy to get some food and enjoys eating the sandwich.
immoral_action: Carl digs through a trash can and finds a couple half eaten pizza slices which he proceeds to eat for lunch.

norm: Bailing on someone who needs your support is wrong.
situation: Robert is helping his friend Nathan through some difficult emotional times and is starting to feel burnt out.
intention: Robert wants to have time to recharge.
moral_action: Robert tells Nathan he needs some time to himself, so he can continue to be a supportive friends.
moral_consequence: Nathan understands and gives Robert the time he needs so their relationship can continue.

immoral_consequence: Nathan gets extremely upset and ends their friendship.

norm: It's rude to flash your genitalia in public.
situation: Jack is walking around town, and he is feeling kind of turned on when he sees some women.
intention: Jack wants to relieve his arousal.

norm: You should be paying your fair share of expenses.
situation: Rob's roommate Tim asks him for his share of the monthly rent, but Rob is short by a few hundred dollars.
intention: Rob wants the rent to be paid.
moral_action: Rob puts in extra hours at work and cuts back on spending, so he can pay his share of rent.
moral_consequence: The rent is paid and Rob continues to live happily in the apartment.
immoral_action: Rob refuses and tells Tim to pay for the entire month's rent himself.
immoral_consequence: Rob is kicked out of the apartment for not paying rent.

norm: It is bad to call 911 and hang up.
situation: John is a young child that was just taught about emergency services at school.
intention: John wants to call 911.
moral_action: John remembers the lesson and only calls 911 later when he witnesses an actual emergency.
moral_consequence: The people in an emergency that John witnessed are saved by emergency workers that John called.
immoral_action: John sneaks away a cell phone and practice calling 911 and hang up when the phone begins to ring.
immoral_consequence: John keeps the emergency lines busy and somebody in a real emergency is unable to get through to 911.

norm: It's wonderful to play games with others.
situation: Casey is at his friends house visiting with his friend in their bedroom.
intention: Casey wants to play a video game.
moral_action: Casey asks his friend if it would be okay if they could play video games together.
moral_consequence: Casey and his friend spend the whole afternoon playing video games together.
immoral_action: Casey turns on his friend's video console and plays a game, but doesn't let his friend take a turn.
immoral_consequence: Casey's friend tells him he doesn't want him to visit anymore and makes him leave the house.

norm: It's kind of friends to do things for each other.
situation: Jessica notices her friend accidentally left the stove on and the water is boiling over.
intention: Jessica wants to consider addressing the situation.
moral_action: Jessica immediately takes action to turn off the stove before the water completely boils over.
moral_consequence: The friend returns and is grateful towards Jessica for turning off the stove.
immoral_action: Jessica ignores the stove and simply lets the water boil over.

norm: It's good to give a stray animal a home.
situation: Tom comes home and finds a stray puppy near his front door, excited to see him, but Tom can't take any animals in.
intention: Tom wants the puppy to have shelter.
moral_action: Tom puts the puppy in a shed and posts adoption flyers over town for the puppy.
moral_consequence: The puppy's owner sees the flyers and picks up the puppy.
immoral_action: Tom takes the puppy and drops it off under the awning of a car wash to keep it dry.
immoral_consequence: The puppy runs off, gets lost in the woods, and dies of starvation.

norm: You shouldn't laugh when someone gets hurt.
situation: Susan is riding bikes with her boyfriend Tom, when she falls into a cactus.
intention: Tom wants to react to Susan's fall.
moral_action: Tom feels bad that Susan got hurt and rushes to help her up and pull out the thorns.
moral_consequence: Susan thinks Tom is very sweet for rushing to her aid.
immoral_action: Tom feels bad that Susan got hurt but finds the situation amusing, so he bursts into laughter.
immoral_consequence: Susan see's Tom as uncaring and mean.

norm: It's good to give your children gifts.
situation: John's son Matthew made an B+ on his report card.
intention: John wants to respond to Matthew's grade.
moral_action: John buys Matthew a new toy to celebrate his accomplishment and offers to help with his homework for a better grade in the future.
moral_consequence: Matthew feels happy, and he continues to do well in school.
immoral_action: John tells Matthew that he would do better next time.
immoral_consequence: Matthew feels like a failure for not meeting John's expectations.

norm: It's not okay to harm yourself.
situation: Rachel's father abused her physically, and she now lives in fear and emotional torment daily.
intention: Rachel wants to escape the pain.
moral_action: Rachel talks with a counselor about her issues and begins a long-term therapy plan with her.
moral_consequence: Rachel makes meaningful progress on overcoming her fears and mental distress, returning to a normal life.
immoral_action: Rachel begins to cut her arms in an attempt to distract herself from the mental pain.
immoral_consequence: Rachel doesn't feel any better and feels ashamed that she can't seem to overcome her feelings.

norm: It's good to get your children involved in sports.
situation: Lyle's son Travis has been invited to try out for an after school soccer team, but he doesn't feel like joining.
intention: Lyle wants Travis to do some sort of extracurricular activity.
