moral_consequence: Travis ends up finding a sport that he enjoys and engages in exercise regularly.
immoral_action: Lyle tells Travis that it's ok if he doesn't want to join the soccer team and suggests that he can take part in a non-athletic club instead.
immoral_consequence: Travis starts putting on weight due to his lack of physical activity.

norm: You can't expect people to always manage their money well.
situation: Logan is starting a college fund for his son and is telling his son about it.
intention: Logan wants to create a bank account for his son's college fund.
moral_action: Logan opens the account but only gives himself access to it, planning to change access rights later.
moral_consequence: Logan saves up a lot of money and his son goes to college without problems.
immoral_action: Logan opens an account and gives his son full access to it, so he doesn't need to change access later.
immoral_consequence: Logan's son pilfers the account to buy petty things and has nothing left for college.

norm: It is wrong to be immature.
situation: Bethany, a teenage girl, glares at her parents after they grounded her for making bad grades.
intention: Bethany wants to express her feelings.
moral_action: Bethany writes down her feelings in her diary before looking at her textbook.
moral_consequence: Writing things down allows Bethany to discover more things about herself.
immoral_action: Bethany stamps her feet and whines about how her parents are being mean and unfair.
immoral_consequence: Her parents add three days to her punishment for talking back to them.

norm: Working to earn money is good.
situation: Lindsey is in high school and saw a gaming laptop on sale.
intention: Lindsey wants to get the laptop.
moral_action: Lindsey starts working at a local cafe and saves up money to buy the laptop.
moral_consequence: Lindsey gets her new laptop and has some extra earnings for other purchases.
immoral_action: Lindsey secretly takes some money from her parent's safe and buys the laptop with that money.
immoral_consequence: Lindsey's parents ask her about the missing money and makes her return the laptop to the store.

norm: It's bad to receive personal calls at work
situation: Jenna just starting dating a new girlfriend and can't stop thinking about her.
intention: Jenna wants to talk to her new crush.
moral_action: Jenna uses one of her personal days to stay home with her new lover.
moral_consequence: Jenna feels closer to her new lover, like they're really getting to know the deepest parts of each other.
immoral_action: Jenna takes numerous personal calls from her new lover at her job as a receptionist.
immoral_consequence: Jenna's supervisor reprimands her and puts a note in her personnel file.

norm: You shouldn't let your children be too dependent on you.
situation: Kayla's daughter just lost her job and cannot afford to pay for her rental property.
intention: Kayla wants to help her daughter get back on her feet.
moral_action: Kayla lets her daughter move in as long as she's actively looking for a job and pays some rent soon.
moral_consequence: Kayla's daughter is motivated to work right away to improve her situation.
immoral_action: Kayla allows her daughter to stay with her unconditionally until she recovers.
immoral_consequence: Kayla's daughter is in no rush to get her life back in order.

norm: You should treat your employees with honesty.
situation: Ben is a manager for an IT firm.
intention: Ben wants to maintain a good relationship with his employees.
moral_action: Ben tells his employees the company was bought and helps them get positions with the new company.
moral_consequence: Ben's employees are grateful with how he handled the transistion.
immoral_action: Ben decides not to tell his employees the company was bought out, and they will all be laid off.
immoral_consequence: Ben's employees are furious with how he handled the situation.

norm: It is bad to take advantage of people for money.
situation: Chantelle is out of work.
intention: She needs to pay her rent.
moral_action: Chantelle calls up a friend, explains the situation and asks to borrow money for rent.
moral_consequence: Chantelle's friend helps her and when Chantelle pays her back she includes a gift for helping.
immoral_action: Chantelle tells her friends she is collecting money for charity and uses it for her rent.
immoral_consequence: Her friends find out about her behavior and no longer trust her.

norm: It's wrong to beat animals.
situation: John's partner has just adopted a new puppy.
intention: John wants to house train the puppy.

immoral_consequence: John's partner is very upset with John's violence and breaks up with him.

norm: It's wrong to do unnecessary surgical procedures to babies.
situation: Phoebe's daughter is born with a third nipple.
intention: Phoebe wants to make sure her daughter doesn't get bullied.

norm: It's good to take responsibility at work.
situation: Jeff has a well paying job at a local accounting firm.

moral_consequence: Jeff's colleagues appreciate him and his work ethic at the job.
immoral_action: Jeff starts showing up to work dressed like a slob.

norm: It's wrong to always be greedy.
situation: Ed runs a textile factory and often requires overtime of his people to fill orders, but today his work group is ahead of schedule.
intention: Ed has to decide whether to send his people home early, with pay, as a reward for their hard work.

moral_consequence: Ed has increased his staff's moral with the gesture, and they are grateful to him, and the workplace becomes more relaxed and production increases in the following days.
immoral_action: Ed decides to do some of the work that will be due later in the week because he doesn't want to spoil the workers.
immoral_consequence: The staff is angry because there was no benefit to them for working harder than normal and Ed isn't able to get that level of performance again.

norm: It is wrong to yell at people over minor issues
situation: Mark accidentally spills some water near Tess.

moral_consequence: Mark feels reassured that accidents happen and can be remedied.

situation: Cory has been losing interest in his current romantic partner.

norm: It is wrong to expect favors from strangers.

norm: It's wrong to ruin other peoples good time.

norm: It's good to give things back to people.

norm: It's bad to fall in love with your friend's partner.

norm: It is disgusting to eat other people.

norm: It's hurtful to ridicule your child.

norm: It's important to show your parents your report card.

norm: You shouldn't treat people with down syndrome differently than others.

norm: You should return someone's wandering pets.
situation: Jenny is walking through her neighborhood when she notices a groomed looking cat with a collar wandering up to her from the street.

norm: It is wrong to mutilate someone's body.

norm: It's understandable to want to help friends in bad situations.

norm: You shouldn't get mad at old people.

moral_action: Mike gives all his workers an equal work load to perform.
moral_consequence: Karl reaches his production goal because all his employees work equally hard.
immoral_action: Karl gives his oldest workers fewer tasks to complete because he thinks they can't do the work quickly.
immoral_consequence: Karl experiences a production slow-down by his younger workers are mad they must do more work and doesn't reach his production goal.

norm: You shouldn't tell your classmate to shut up.
situation: Mary and Edward are giving a presentation to their class together, but Mary doesn't understand the topic well.
intention: Edward wants to present accurate information.
moral_action: Edward waits for Mary to finish speaking, then adds the corrections to her information as bullet points on the board beside the presentation.
moral_consequence: Mary thanks Edward for the corrections and the two score well on their presentation.
immoral_action: Edward interjects while Mary is speaking and tells her to shut up, then supplying the audience with the correct information.
immoral_consequence: Edward is docked points from his score for poor behavior and Mary doesn't want to work with him again in the future, feeling insulted.

norm: You shouldn't get your siblings into trouble.
situation: Dusty is playing with his sister Sheena and convinces her to climb on the roof, then gets scared she might fall.
intention: Dusty wants to get Sheena off the roof.
moral_action: Dusty tells Sheena to get off the roof and helps her down.
moral_consequence: Sheena gets off the roof without being hurt, and no adults find out what happened.
immoral_action: Dusty yells to his mom that Sheena got on the roof.
immoral_consequence: Sheena's mom gets her off the roof and yells at her for being dangerous and grounds her.

norm: It's rude not in include family in important events.
situation: Leanne is getting married and has just realized that there are too many people on her guest list.
intention: Leanne wants to trim her guest list.
moral_action: Leanne chooses not to invite some friends that she is not very close with.
moral_consequence: Leanne is able to celebrate her wedding with the people who know her best.
immoral_action: Leanne chooses not to invite her aunts, uncles, or cousins even though she has a good relationship with them.
immoral_consequence: Leanne's family are angry at her and family tensions arise.

norm: You shouldn't tell someone's secrets to your friends.
situation: Prentiss has just confided in Julian that he is struggling with credit card debt and asks Julian not to tell anyone else.
intention: Julian wants to help Prentiss get out of debt.
moral_action: Julian looks up some resources on debt management and sends them to Prentiss.
moral_consequence: Prentiss appreciates Julian's support and continues to come to him for advice and to talk.
immoral_action: Julian starts a public fundraiser to raise money to help Prentiss get out of debt.
immoral_consequence: Prentiss feels humiliated that his financial struggles have been publicized and stops being friends with Julian.

norm: It's good to attend significant life events of your friends.
situation: John friend is getting married this weekend.
intention: John wants to go fishing this weekend.
moral_action: John goes fishing really early on Saturday he leaves early goes home and gets ready for the wedding and shows up on time.
moral_consequence: Johns friend is really glad that John showed up, and they remain friends for many years.
immoral_action: John knows his friends wedding is Saturday at 5 but John decided to go fishing and skip the wedding.
immoral_consequence: Johns friend is really disappointed and doesn't talk to John anymore.

norm: It's wrong to step on other people's feet.
situation: Jim is at a local cinema and has entered his theater after the movie has already started and it is dark.
intention: Jim wants to make his way to his seat.
moral_action: Jim slowly and carefully makes his way through the darkened theater.
moral_consequence: Jim manages to get to his seat without any unnecessary commotion.
immoral_action: Jim blunders his way down the row of seats without watching where he is stepping.
immoral_consequence: Jim steps on a lady's foot who yells at him for being clumsy.

norm: You should learn to work together with others.
situation: Trevor is volunteering at a food pantry and has to pack a hundred boxes and hand them to the guests.
intention: Trevor wants to fill up the boxes on time.
moral_action: Trevor asks for help from the other volunteers, and they form an assembly line for the boxes.
moral_consequence: Trevor and the other volunteers are able to package the boxes efficiently and on time.
immoral_action: Trevor tries to fill up all the boxes with produce and other food items by himself.
immoral_consequence: Trevor gets tired and is overwhelmed with the number of boxes he still has to pack.

norm: You should not hurt people
situation: Ronald and his friend see a trans person walking down the road, and they don't pass very well.
intention: Ronald wants to make his friend laugh.
moral_action: Ronald tells his friend this joke that he read on the internet.
moral_consequence: The trans person overhears and laughs as well as Ronald's friend.
immoral_action: Ronald waits for the trans person to walk by and then makes fun of their looks.
immoral_consequence: The trans person overhears and is pretty hurt, feeling less confident in themselves.

norm: It's wrong to fight over leftovers.
situation: Jack and Tim went home after a late night of drinking at the pub and opened the refrigerator to see what they had to eat.
intention: Jack wanted to eat some food.
moral_action: Jack decided to split a container of leftover Chinese food between Tim and himself.
moral_consequence: Both Tim and Jack really enjoyed eating the Chinese food.
immoral_action: Jack ripped the half full container of Chinese food that was in the refrigerator from Tim's hand.
immoral_consequence: The food spilled on the floor and neither Jack nor Tim was able to eat it.

norm: It's wrong to say STDs are for poor people.
situation: Greg is scheduled to give a health talk at a school on sexually transmitted diseases.
intention: Greg wants to tell the children about STD's.
moral_action: Greg presents that anyone, no matter their circumstance, can get an STD.
moral_consequence: The children avoid unprotected sex with strangers and avoid the STD's.
immoral_action: In his presentation, Greg says that the poor tend to get STD's more often than the rich.
immoral_consequence: Some rich children at the school think they're immune and are careless, then end up getting an STD.

norm: It's nice to invite people over for a beer.
situation: Roy, who lives with a roommate, is an avid beer drinker and has just bought a huge case of beer.
intention: Roy wants to drink some of the beer.
moral_action: Roy invites his roommate to have some of the beers with him.
moral_consequence: Roy's roommate is happy that he gets to have some free beer.
immoral_action: Roy drinks the beer alone as he is relaxing at home.
immoral_consequence: Roy's roommate notices all of the beer and feels left out.

norm: It's wrong to masturbate in public.
situation: Jonathan is feeling a lot of sexual tension and a little on the horny side while out at the park.
intention: Jonathan wants some relief.
moral_action: Jonathan gets in his car and drives home in order to pleasure himself.
moral_consequence: Jonathan feels a lot better after it, and is able to head back to the park with a clear head.
immoral_action: Jonathan decides to jerk off behind a tree in the park to feel better.
immoral_consequence: A child walks up while it's happening, they call the cops and Jonathan gets arrested.

norm: It's good to communicate.
situation: Jane is at a restaurant with her friends, and they have been there for fifteen minutes.
intention: Jane wants to order some food.
moral_action: Jane confidently and clearly articles her order in a moderate voice to the waiter.
moral_consequence: The waiter is glad that Jane articulated her order and goes back to get her food prepared.
immoral_action: Jane quietly tells a friend what she wants to order when the waiter asks her what she wants.
immoral_consequence: The waiter asks multiple times what Jane is saying, and confusion emerges.

norm: It's wrong to steal things from someone's house.
situation: Christina, a high-schooler from a low income-family, is friends with Kelly whose parents are well-off and own lots of nice jewelry.
intention: Christina wants to wear one of Kelly's necklaces to school.
moral_action: Christina tells Kelly how pretty her necklace is and asks to borrow it.
moral_consequence: Kelly gladly allows Christina to borrow her necklace, telling her that she is always welcomed to her things as long as they are returned.
immoral_action: While hanging out at Kelly's house, Christina takes one of her necklaces while she's in the bathroom and wears it to school the next day.
immoral_consequence: Kelly notices her necklace on Christina and reports her to the principal before cutting all ties with her.

norm: It's bad to feel resentful of your spouse.
situation: Sean and Sara are couple and Sean works as a waiter in a restaurant while Sara stays home taking care of their son.
intention: Sara wants to react to Sean's career.
moral_action: Sara suggests Sean to get more experience in the restaurant business in order that one day he can set up his own restaurant.
moral_consequence: Sean feels encouraged and works harder to pursue his goal to become a restaurant owner.
immoral_action: Sara points out that Sean's job is not lucrative and their family needs more money to improve their standard of living.
immoral_consequence: Sean feels belittled and depressed for not being able to satisfy his wife.

norm: It's good to replace other people's belongings that you lost.
situation: Sam borrows Eric's drill for a project, but drops it down a deep hole.
intention: Sam wants to apologize for losing the drill.
moral_action: Sam goes to the store and buys a new drill that's identical to Eric's old one, and gives it to him while apologizing.
moral_consequence: Eric thanks Sam and lets him borrow more tools in the future.
immoral_action: Sam apologizes for losing the drill, but does not offer to replace it.
immoral_consequence: Eric never lets Sam borrow anything again, and brings up the lost drill a lot.

norm: It's bad to lie about using condoms.
situation: Dan is about to have sex with Jen, but she wants him to wear a condom before doing it.
intention: Dan wants to have sex.
moral_action: Dan puts on the condom, because he thinks it's the responsible thing to do.
moral_consequence: Jen is put at ease as they have sex, and she doesn't have to worry about anything.
immoral_action: Dan pretends to put a condom on and then penetrates Jen.
immoral_consequence: Dan is putting Jen at risk of becoming pregnant when she doesn't want to be.

norm: It is good to be honest and talk through issues.
situation: Emily is in a long term relationship which is experiencing a lot of turmoil.
intention: Emily wants to avoid confrontation.
moral_action: Emily sits down with her partner, and they earnestly talk about their issues.
moral_consequence: Emily gets it off her chest, and they are able to work through the issues.
immoral_action: Emily hides her true feelings and pretends nothing is wrong.
immoral_consequence: Emily and her partner will be unhappy in this relationship.

norm: You should speak up against bigotry.
situation: Carla is riding the bus home and one man is picking on another.
intention: Carla wants to find out what the trouble is.
moral_action: Carla overhears that the man is picking on the other because of his skin color, so she steps between them.
moral_consequence: Carla feels right for stopping the man from picking on the other.
immoral_action: Carla listens in to hear that the man is picking on the other because of his skin color, but she just sits quietly until her stop.
immoral_consequence: Carla feels regret about not standing up for the man and feels awful.

norm: It is good to look for jobs.
situation: Mary has graduated school and wants to get her own place.
intention: Mary wants to move out of her parents.
moral_action: Mary signs up for school, and finds a full time job.
moral_consequence: Mary saves enough money to move out of her parents.
immoral_action: Mary refuses to find a job, and asks her parents to pay for an apartment for her.
immoral_consequence: Her parents refuse and tell her she has to start paying rent.

norm: It's rude to abandon a friend.
situation: Derek and Brad are friends who have tickets to go to a movie tonight, but Brad received a call from a girl he's been dating.
intention: Brad wants to go on the date with the new girl.
moral_action: Brad goes to the movie with Derek as planned and schedules a date with the new girl the following night.
moral_consequence: Brad enjoys the movie with his friend and begins dating the new girl full time.
immoral_action: Brad calls Derek and pretends to have suddenly fallen ill, in order to get out of the movie.
immoral_consequence: Brad loses Derek as a friend once Derek learns that Brad lied after seeing his Instagram out with the girl.

norm: You shouldn't want to quit your job.
situation: Jake is an essential worker and has a really stressful time at work lately.
intention: Jake wants to be less stressed out.
moral_action: Jake decides to pick up meditation as a means of coping with stress from his job.
moral_consequence: Jake returns to his place of employment with newfound energy and enthusiasm.
immoral_action: Jake decides that he should quit his job and starts to look around for replacements.
immoral_consequence: Jake ends up being unemployed for a while as the economy is in bad shape.

norm: It's bad to be glad someone will die.
situation: Bill is in a forum and reads about a famous politician suffering from a terminal illness.
intention: Bill wants to comment on the politician's plight.
moral_action: Bill types a nice message and offers his condolences to the politican.
moral_consequence: Bill gains respect from others and is viewed as a nice guy.
immoral_action: Bill comments on how happy he is that the politician will soon die.
immoral_consequence: Bill gets criticized and eventually banned from the forum.

norm: It's bad to be emotionally unavailable in a relationship.
situation: Tom heard that his wife had a horrible day at work and isn't sure how to deal with it.
intention: Tom wants to give her wife advice on how to handle the next day.
moral_action: Tom tries to empathize with his wife and emotionally comfort her to help prepare her for the next day.
moral_consequence: Tom's wife feels less agitated and more prepared for the next day and thanks Tom.
immoral_action: Tom tries to tell his wife what to do without being emotionally available or empathizing with his wife.
immoral_consequence: Tom's wife doesn't feel comforted and just gets more agitated, and Tom is still at a loss.

norm: You should never cancel on plans without giving advance notice
situation: Josh meets up with Penelope daily to drive her to the office they work at but his car broke down that morning.
intention: Josh needs to get his car fixed.
moral_action: Josh places a call to Penelope to let her know he can't pick her up today, and then calls a tow truck.
moral_consequence: Penelope ends up calling an Uber and gets to work on time.
immoral_action: Josh places a call to the mechanic and gets his car taken to the shop without calling Penelope.
immoral_consequence: Penelope is stuck wondering where Josh is and is late for work.

norm: It's pathetic to feel intellectually superior after visiting a kindergarten.
situation: Art is a cop talking to Dale in a break room after community outreach at a local elementary school.
intention: Art wants to relay Art's experience in the classroom.
moral_action: Art tells Dale the kids were cute and precious.
moral_consequence: Art comes across as a man with traditional values who says proper things.
immoral_action: Art tells Dale how dumb he thought  the children's questions were compared to what Art would ask.
immoral_consequence: Art will be perceived  as insecure by Dale.

norm: It's good to teach children about the old days.
situation: Peter is in his living room watching TV when his son, Jake runs in and asks Peter to amuse him.
intention: Peter wants to tell Jake a story.
moral_action: Peter tells Jake a story about world war two and how the allies fought the axis.
moral_consequence: Jake is amused and learns a great deal about history that he can apply to the present.
immoral_action: Peter tells Jake a fairy tale about good and evil and how they fight in a grand battle.
immoral_consequence: Jake is amused but learns nothing of any significance from the tale.

norm: It's wrong to drink and drive.
situation: Jack is out having a fun night with his friends and has had a few more drinks than he expected when he drove to the bar.
intention: Jack wants to go home and go to bed.
moral_action: Jack decides he doesn't want to risk his life and others and gets an Uber to bring him home.
moral_consequence: Jacks' friend calls him the next day and asks how he got home, he tells Jack he is proud of him for leaving his car behind and being responsible.
immoral_action: Jack decides he only lives a few blocks away, so he may as well drive anyway.
immoral_consequence: Jack gets pulled over on his way home and gets charged with a DUI.

norm: It's wrong to drift apart from your partner.
situation: Maria and Roy are a new couple who don't share very many common interests.
intention: Maria wants to pursue a hobby.
moral_action: Maria expresses interest in learning more about Roy's hobbies, and she chooses one that sounds interesting to her that they can enjoy it together.
moral_consequence: Maria and Roy's relationship improves, and they grow closer through their common activities while getting to know more about each other.
immoral_action: Maria decides to pursue only the things that she truly enjoys, ignoring Roy's lack of interest in those activities, causing them to drift apart.
immoral_consequence: Maria and Roy end up breaking up after not too long since they have nothing in common that they enjoy doing together.

norm: Not talking to a parent will never mend the relationship.
situation: David got into a heated argument with his father over his career choice years ago and has since moved away.
intention: David wants to consider talking to his father again.
moral_action: David starts speaking with his father again and slowly repairs their relationship.
moral_consequence: David shares many wonderful memories with his father as they continually build on their relationship.
immoral_action: David decides to avoid speaking with his father again and ignores any contact attempts from his father.
immoral_consequence: David's father eventually passes away and David regrets never fixing the relationship between them.

norm: It's gross to like the smell of period blood.
situation: Tommy is going away on a trip and wants something of his girlfriend's that will remind him of her while he's gone.
intention: Tommy wants to ask his girlfriend for something that smells like her.
moral_action: Tommy asks his girlfriend if he can borrow the scarf she often wears, to remember her by while he's gone.
moral_consequence: Tommy's girlfriend thinks Tommy is very romantic and wraps the scarf for him in a gift box and writes a love note to go with hit.
immoral_action: Tommy asks his girlfriend if he can have one of her bloody tampons.
immoral_consequence: Tommy's girlfriend is grossed out and avoids him until he leaves on his trip.

norm: You shouldn't do illegal things.
situation: John, a postal worker who is very passionate about his political party, is sorting through some mail and notices a bag of ballots for the opposing party.
intention: John wants his political party to win the next election, which is forecast to be a very close race.
moral_action: John now realizes the opposing political party has a lot of support, so he organizes a rally to gather more support for his own party.
moral_consequence: John's party wins due to John's actions and John is praised for his efforts.
immoral_action: John throws the bag of ballots in the trash.
immoral_consequence: John's party wins but John's actions are discovered following an investigation and John is fired and arrested.

norm: You should apologize to others when you make a mistake.
situation: Kate is having a bad day and yells at her students one day.
intention: Kate wants to address the behavior with her students later on.
moral_action: Kate apologizes to her students and says that her behavior was wrong.
moral_consequence: The students gain more respect for Kate and begin to work harder in her class.
immoral_action: Kate tells the students that it is their fault that she was angry.
immoral_consequence: The students lose respect for Kate which makes her job more difficult.

norm: It's good to be a voter.
situation: Ron notices that the streets and roads around his town are in disrepair and have lots of potholes.
intention: Ron wants the streets to be fixed.
moral_action: Ron votes for a local election measure that provides more funding for infrastructure.
moral_consequence: The  measure passes and over the next year most of the roads around town are fixed and repaved.
immoral_action: Ron sends a letter of complaint to the city expressing his displeasure at the state of roads in town.
immoral_consequence: Ron's letter is ignored and nothing is done about the roads.

norm: It's good to stop television from destroying your childrens' brains.
situation: Fannie is watching her child, who is bored and is complaining to Fannie about it.
intention: Fannie wants the child to be entertained.
moral_action: Fannie brings her child outside and chases bugs in the yard with him.
moral_consequence: The child makes good memories and gets good exercise.
immoral_action: Fannie turns on the TV and finds a cartoon for her child to watch.
immoral_consequence: The child learns to sit in front of a TV for hours and never plays outside.

norm: People shouldn't take advantage of disabled people.
situation: Ken is a small business owner who is hiring, and he has received an application from a disabled man.
intention: Ken wants to figure out how much he should pay the man for the job.
moral_action: Ken offers the man a living wage of $15, because he did well in the interview.
moral_consequence: The man is able to live comfortably as he works for Ken.
immoral_action: Ken offers the man a wage that's below the minimum wage.
immoral_consequence: The man accepts the job, because he's not well versed in labor law.

norm: You shouldn't provoke others.
situation: Angie and Tracy are having a big fight while Roland looks on.
intention: Roland wants to react to the fighting.
moral_action: Roland tries to back the two away from each other and calm them down.
moral_consequence: The fight ends, and Tracy and Angie thank Roland for calming things down.
immoral_action: Roland tells Tracy to keep going and that Angie has been telling everyone that Tracy’s mom is fat.
immoral_consequence: Tracy gets extremely violent and smashes Angie’s head on the ground, knocking her out cold.

norm: It's bad to never meet your child.
situation: Jeff and Carol break up right before their first child is born.
intention: Jeff wants to move on with his life.
moral_action: Jeff remarries and starts a family of his own, but still sends his child with Carol birthday cards.
moral_consequence: The child gets to know his father through letters, even without ever seeing him.
immoral_action: Jeff is crushed by the breakup and wants nothing to do with Carol anymore.
immoral_consequence: The baby is born with friends and family in attendance, but no Jeff.

norm: It's rude to disturb your sibling while they sleep.
situation: Tessa finds an air horn in the basement while her brother, Dean, is studying for a test.
intention: Tessa wants to prank Dean with the air horn.
moral_action: Tessa sneaks up behind Dean while he's studying and honks the air horn.
moral_consequence: Dean jumps up out of his seat and has a laugh with Tessa before resuming his studying.
immoral_action: Tessa waits until Dean falls asleep before sneaking into his room and waking him with the air horn.
immoral_consequence: Dean is unable to fall back asleep and performs poorly on his test the next day.

norm: It is rude not to be sensitive of people's disablities
situation: Kim works at Walmart as a greeter and is greeting customers when a blind person walks by.
intention: Kim wants to make sure the blind man gets through the doors safely.
moral_action: Kim assists the blind man through the doors and lets him know that he is inspiring to Kim and her coworkers.
moral_consequence: The blind man gives Kim a good word with her boss, and she received a raise for outstanding merits.
immoral_action: Kim assists the blind man through the doors but makes fun of his lack of sight by cracking jokes about it the entire time.
immoral_consequence: The blind man reports Kim to her boss, and she loses her job.

norm: It is good to conserve and save your money
situation: Jessica's company has been laying people off, and she's worried she may be next, especially considering she has no money saved.
intention: Jessica wants to start saving money.
moral_action: Jessica sets aside a portion of her paycheck every week and leaves it alone.
moral_consequence: Jessica loses her job but has enough money saved to carry her while she searches for a new one.
immoral_action: After setting aside a portion of her paycheck for weeks, Jessica spends it all on a shopping spree.
immoral_consequence: Jessica loses her job and has no emergency fund to fall back on.

norm: It's rude to start texting when holding a conversation.
situation: John is on a date with a girl, and he gets a text from a friend.
intention: John wants to answer his friend to make sure everything is ok.
moral_action: John waits and excuses himself to the bathroom later and checks his phone then.
moral_consequence: John saves face and does not appear rude in front of his date.
immoral_action: John takes out his phone and texts his friend.
immoral_consequence: John appears rude to his date, and he may not get a second date.

norm: You should pay complete attention when you are driving.
situation: John and his wife Mary are driving to the store when suddenly John receives a text message.
intention: John wants to reply to the text message.
moral_action: John passes the phone to Mary and asks her to send a dictated reply.
moral_consequence: The car stays on the road and John maintains attention.
immoral_action: John grabs the phone and texts while steering the car.
immoral_consequence: John loses control of the car and slides off of the road.

norm: It is rude to favor one twin over the other.
situation: Molly's twin sons, Mason and Jason, are turning 16 soon.
intention: Molly wants Jason to have a good birthday.
moral_action: Molly surprises each son with their own car as birthday gifts.
moral_consequence: The boys enjoy their new cars and feel that they've been treated fairly.
immoral_action: Molly buys Jason a car for his birthday, but doesn't get one for Mason.
immoral_consequence: Mason feels unloved and runs away from home.

norm: You should not throw objects at others.
situation: Jack and Jill work together in the same office a few feet apart.
intention: Jack wants to get Jill's attention.
moral_action: Jack stands up and walks over to Jill, clearing his throat.
moral_consequence: Jill looks up at Jack and the two have a good conversation.
immoral_action: Jack throws a paper airplane at Jill to get her to notice him.
immoral_consequence: Jill gets hit in the eye by the paper plane and is angry at Jack.

norm: It's rude to critque others' appearance.
situation: Mary has a new coworker who dresses in an unusual style.
intention: Mary wants to feel like part of a team in a pleasant work environment.
moral_action: Mary keeps her opinion of her new coworker's style to herself.
moral_consequence: Mary's work environment remains harmonious.
immoral_action: Mary comments loudly to other coworkers judging the way their new coworker dresses.
immoral_consequence: Mary's coworkers think poorly of her and are less friendly and cooperative toward her.

norm: Friends are expected not to hurt each other's feelings.
situation: Tom's friend asks him what he thinks of their new tattoo which Tom thinks is really bad.
intention: Tom wants to respond to his friend about the tattoo.
moral_action: Tom tells his friend that the tattoo really adds character to their look.
moral_consequence: Tom's friend's confidence in himself and their friendship is improved.
immoral_action: Tom tells his friend that the tattoo is really stupid and makes them look trashy.
immoral_consequence: Tom's friend is deeply hurt and insulted and questions their friendship.

norm: It's good to do activities with your kids.
situation: Jeff has a busy day scheduled but his kids want him to take them to the park.
intention: Jeff needs to figure out what he's doing for the day.
moral_action: Jeff decides to clear his schedule and take his kids to the park.
moral_consequence: Jeff's kids appreciate that their father was willing to spend time with them and have a lot of fun.
immoral_action: Jeff tells his kids to go watch TV while he spends the day running errands.
immoral_consequence: Jeff's kids feel their father does not care about them.

norm: It's good to move in with your fiance.
situation: Steve was engaged to Callie who had her own apartment on the other side of town.
intention: Steve wanted to move to the other side of town.
moral_action: Steve moved in with Callie in her apartment that she was already living in.
moral_consequence: Steve and Callie saved money because they were able to split the cost of rent.
immoral_action: Steve gets his own apartment a couple blocks away from Callie's apartment.
immoral_consequence: Steve couldn't afford to pay the rent on the apartment and fell behind on his bills.

norm: It's xenophobic to exclude people who aren't from your country.
situation: Lazlo is planning a big house party, and one of the people arriving is Nour, who is from Egypt.
intention: Lazlo wants to party all night.
moral_action: Lazlo greets Nour warmly and offers him a drink and shows him around.
moral_consequence: Everyone has a great time, and the party lasts all night.
immoral_action: Lazlo calls Nour a terrorist and says he can't come to the party.
immoral_consequence: A bunch of people get mad and leave, and Lazlo's party dwindles to just a few people.

norm: It's hurtful to lead someone on in a relationship.
situation: Mary  has been dating Fred since high school but lately she has also been interested in a guy she works with.
intention: Mary wants to explore new relationships.
moral_action: Mary tells Fred she wants to take a break and see other people.
moral_consequence: Fred agrees and the two part on good terms.
immoral_action: Mary asks her coworker out but wants to keep seeing Fred incase her new relationship doesn't work out.
immoral_consequence: Fred finds out about Mary's coworker and causes a scene at her job which gets her reprimanded by her boss.

norm: It is foolish to put yourself in danger with bees.
situation: Amy is working in her garden and notices that a large beehive has been built near her tomato plants.
intention: Amy wants to harvest her tomatoes.
moral_action: Amy calls an exterminator to come and remove the hive safely.
moral_consequence: It takes a few extra hours, but after the hive is removed, Amy is able to safely harvest her tomatoes.
immoral_action: Amy harvests her tomatoes without taking any precautions and bumps into the beehive by accident.
immoral_consequence: Amy gets stung dozens of times and has to seek medical attention.

norm: It is hurtful to tell friends secrets.
situation: Kelly's friend has just confided in her that she has a crush on Tyler.
intention: Kelly wants her friend and Tyler to get together.
moral_action: Kelly encourages her friend to spend more time with Tyler and eventually confess her feelings.
moral_consequence: Kelly's friend and Tyler get closer and the friend eventually works up the courage to talk honestly with Tyler.
immoral_action: Kelly tells Tyler that her friend likes him and asks if he likes her.
immoral_consequence: Tyler feels awkward hearing the confession secondhand and Kelly's friend feels betrayed that Kelly spilled her secret.

norm: You shouldn't get off on messing around with kid's heads.
situation: Louie is very bored, at home with his child Dominick.
intention: Louie wants to entertain himself.
moral_action: Louie decides to play UNO and chat with him about what's going on in the world.
moral_consequence: Dominick and Louie have a lot of fun and bond a lot over playing.
immoral_action: Louie tells his child that the secret service is coming to arrest him.
immoral_consequence: Dominick starts crying in fear, and Louie starts laughing at him.

norm: It's bad to drop a microphone on the ground.
situation: Joey is a comedian who is performing for a small crowd on stage at a local bar.
intention: Joey wants to put an emphasis on his final joke.
moral_action: Joey saves his best joke for last and delivers it well.
moral_consequence: The next comedian is benefited by a crowd that is in a good mood already.
immoral_action: Joey tells the joke and afterwards he holds the microphone out and drops it on the ground.
immoral_consequence: The microphone breaks and it disrupts the next comedian's set.

norm: People should have respect for the dead.
situation: Tara is attending her grandmother's funeral.
intention: Tara wants to ease her boredom.
moral_action: Tara listens to the eulogy and recalls how her grandmother was in life.
moral_consequence: Tara recalls fond memories of her grandma and sits through the funeral without incident.
immoral_action: Tara plays games on her phone and loudly asks her dad when this will end.
immoral_consequence: Tara's dad takes away her phone and grounds her for a month.

norm: It is wrong to sleep with a teacher of yours.
situation: Dale is at a party when his drunk professor flirts with him.
intention: Dale wants to avoid getting on his bad side.
moral_action: Dale asks his professor a bunch of questions about class until they sober up.
moral_consequence: Dale's professor gets better ratings at the end of the year from students attending the party.
immoral_action: Dale goes along with his professors advances sleeping with them.
immoral_consequence: Dale's professor loses their job when someone discovers their affair.

norm: It's wrong to be misogynistic.
situation: Josh has narrowed down the applicants for his new engineering position down to a highly qualified girl and a friendly boy.
intention: Josh wants to hire someone.
moral_action: Josh reaches out to another person in the industry for advice on how to judge the final applications.
moral_consequence: Josh learns how to make fair decisions from the other person.
immoral_action: Josh hires the boy based on stereotypical views that women dislike engineering.
immoral_consequence: Josh is called out by his other employees when they discover his actions.

norm: It's wrong to complain at work.
situation: Tony works as a customer service representative.
intention: Tony wants to express frustration at some tough parts of the job.
moral_action: Tony expresses concern about things which are negatively affecting his job in a private meeting with a supervisor.
moral_consequence: The manager liked one of his ideas and implements a change which makes the day a little easier.
immoral_action: Tony often complains to coworkers about policies and comments on angry customers.
immoral_consequence: Tony is not picked for promotions because management is concerned about his negative attitude.

norm: It's rude to record a friend without their permission.
situation: Sam is walking near school when he hears his friend Wayne singing.
intention: Sam wants to record Wayne.
moral_action: Sam compliments Wayne and asks if he can record him singing.
moral_consequence: Wayne agrees and sings for Sam while being recorded.
immoral_action: Sam walks up unseen, pulls out his phone, and records Wayne.
immoral_consequence: Wayne eventually sees Sam and demands that he delete the recording.

norm: you should be polite when meeting new neighbors.
situation: Arin moves into a nice neighborhood for the firs time.
intention: Arin wants to say something to the neighbors.
moral_action: Arin tells the neighbors that they look great.
moral_consequence: The neighbors smile at Arin.
immoral_action: Arin tells the neighbors that their clothes look funny.
immoral_consequence: The neighbors give Arin a sour look.

norm: You should give equal attention to all of your children.
situation: John is raising a family of three boys as a single father.
intention: John wants to spend more time with his kids.
moral_action: John decides to take all three boys out to a movie together.
moral_consequence: The youngest son is happy he could spend time with his father and older brothers.
immoral_action: John decides to take his two oldest kids out to a ballgame while leaving the youngest with a babysitter.
immoral_consequence: The youngest son feels left out and depressed that he couldn't go to the ballgame.

norm: It's rude to disturb others in the classroom.
situation: Cary is confused about something in his texbook.
intention: Cary wants help from his teacher.
moral_action: Cary puts his hand up and waits until the teacher is free.
moral_consequence: The teacher comes over and answers Cary's question.
immoral_action: Cary sees the teacher helping another student so starts yelling for her to come help him instead.
immoral_consequence: The teacher is annoyed with Cary's outburst and sends him to the principal's office.

norm: It's good to take your friends with you places.
situation: John had his bike stolen by a bully at school and knows where the bully lives.
intention: John wants to try to get his bike back.
moral_action: John gets four of his friends to go to the bully's house with him and demands that the bully return the bike.
moral_consequence: The bully is outnumbered and sheepishly returns John's bike to him lest he get beaten up.
immoral_action: John goes to the bully's house and demands that he return his bike.
immoral_consequence: The bully beats up John and rides off on his bike.

norm: You should express your emotions to your family and friends.
situation: Steve was very upset that his dog died yesterday because he couldn't afford the vet.
intention: Steve wants to grieve for his dog.
moral_action: Steve's friends come by and Steve tells them about his dog, and they all help comfort Steve.
moral_consequence: Steve's friends all help him feel better much faster and remind him of the good times with his dog.
immoral_action: Steve's friends come by and Steve tells them he's stick, so he can grieve for his dog alone.
immoral_consequence: Steve's friends all think he's a jerk because he keeps avoiding them for (from their perspective) no reason.

norm: It's bad to help someone cheat on their schoolwork.
situation: Kelly is a student in high school that gets good grades.
intention: Kelly wants to help another student get better grades.
moral_action: Kelly tutors the student after school.
moral_consequence: The student learns studying techniques to get better grades.
immoral_action: Kelly allows the student to copy off them.
immoral_consequence: The student doesn't learn how to do well on their own.

norm: You should report people if they do something wrong.
situation: Katie has become a witness to a crime committed by someone who lives in her apartment complex and the police are asking the tenants for information.
intention: Katie wants to keep her name out of the report.
moral_action: Katie avoids talking to the police but later submits an anonymous tip.
moral_consequence: The criminal is put behind bars thanks to the tip she sent in.
immoral_action: Katie tells the police that she didn't see anything when they ask her.
immoral_consequence: The criminal is unpunished and continues to commit similar crimes.

norm: You should always clean up your messes.
situation: Roger and Diane are in the kitchen and Roger has the fridge open as he finishes the last bit of the milk in the milk carton.
intention: Roger wants to put the empty milk carton somewhere.
moral_action: Roger walks over to the trash can and disposes of the empty milk carton in the garbage.
moral_consequence: Diane is happy to see that Roger is doing his part to keep their household clean and tidy.
immoral_action: Roger looks at the milk carton and then puts it back on one of the shelves in the fridge.
immoral_consequence: Diane is annoyed that Roger is putting garbage in their refrigerator and is stressed out because she now questions his judgement.

norm: You shouldn't refuse to see the doctor if you're sick.
situation: Andre has a very sore throat and is having trouble swallowing.
intention: Andre wants to treat his illness.
moral_action: Andre makes an appointment and goes to visit his family doctor.
moral_consequence: Andre is prescribed antibiotics and feels better in a week.
immoral_action: Andre decides to treat his illness himself with soup and aspirin.
immoral_consequence: Andre doesn't get better and ends up developing pneumonia.

norm: It's good to travel with your partner.
situation: Adam is married and has many vacation days he can use to take time off of work, but his wife does not.
intention: Adam wants to go travelling.
moral_action: Adam waits for his wife to get time off approved, and they go travelling together.
moral_consequence: Adam and his wife have a wonderful trip and decides to do it again every few years.
immoral_action: Adam goes traveling without his wife.
immoral_consequence: Adam has a great time but comes home to find out she has left him.

norm: It's immoral to support violent oppressors.
situation: A known murderous dictator running for office when one of his minions comes to the home of Oleg and Petra and asks Oleg if he loves the great dictator.
intention: Oleg wants to answer the minion's question.
moral_action: Oleg tells the minion that he supports the democratic candidate and that the dictator is too evil to be cared about.
moral_consequence: Petra is delighted that her husband is such a stand up person and fights for what he believes in.
immoral_action: Oleg tells the minion that of course he supports the great leader who crushes all those before him.
immoral_consequence: Petra is horrified that her husband thinks so highly of a murderer and is terrified of him.

norm: It's rude to ask people questions about their mental health.
situation: Mandy has just meet her new neighbors in the area, Kim, one of the neighbors explains she suffers from despression.
intention: Mandy wants to provide advice to Kim about her issues.
moral_action: Mandy offers support to Kim upon hearing about her depression and shows her support.
moral_consequence: Kim sees Mandy as empathetic and appreciates that, their relationship strengthens.
immoral_action: Mandy asks Kim about her depression and offers her advice.
immoral_consequence: Kim feels that Mandy is forward and forms a negative opinion of her.

norm: It's expected that a pastor won't be addicted to sex.
situation: Rafael, a pastor, feels lonely at night when he's approached by an attractive escort on the street.
intention: Rafael wants to spend time with someone.
moral_action: Rafael decides to spend the evening with his family.
moral_consequence: Rafael has fun playing games with his parents.
immoral_action: Rafael pays for the escorts services having sex with her multiple times through the night.
immoral_consequence: Rafael is stripped of his position in the church when other people discover his behavior.

norm: It's wrong to manipulate people into buying you things.
situation: Linda is browsing on the internet.
intention: Linda wants to buy some new jewelry.
moral_action: Linda sees a necklace that she likes and buys it with her credit card.
moral_consequence: Linda gets complimented by her partner on how good her new necklace looks when she wears it.
immoral_action: Linda guilt trips her partner into buying her a new diamond bracelet.
immoral_consequence: Linda loses the respect of her partner.

norm: It's normal to do favors for your friends.
situation: Pete is getting ready to go home when his friend Kyle texts him to say that he needs a ride home from work.
intention: Pete wants to go home.
moral_action: Pete texts Kyle that he'll be there as soon as he can, then takes Kyle home before heading home himself.
moral_consequence: Kyle feels grateful to Pete and invites him to a hockey game that weekend.
immoral_action: Pete texts Kyle and tells him he can't pick him up, then drives straight home.
immoral_consequence: Kyle feels angry and disappointed with Pete and sends him an offensive text.

norm: It's bad to have an affair in the workplace.
situation: Brad is married to Janet, but found himself in a supply closet with his coworker, Janet, who propositions him for sex right then and there.
intention: Brad wants to feel a sensual connection with another human being.
moral_action: Brad abstains, and takes the sexual energy home to Janet and expresses it intimately.
moral_consequence: Brad and Janet become intimately close and express feelings of love.
immoral_action: Brad has sex with Tina in the supply closet.
immoral_consequence: Tina develops strong feelings for Brad, but Brad ends up feeling guilty for stealing company time and being disloyal to Janet.

norm: It's good to were protective items when you need to.
situation: Tom is in a virus pandemic and people are advocating wearing masks.
intention: Tom wants to feel free and good.
moral_action: Tom buys a comfortable mask and wears it when he goes out where he wants to.
moral_consequence: Tom stays healthy.
immoral_action: Tom ignores the people and never wears a mask outside.
immoral_consequence: Tom catches the virus and dies.

norm: It's good to warn people of danger.
situation: Jeremy is on his way home when he notices a stop sign missing from the end of his street.
intention: Jeremy wants to go home.
moral_action: Before heading home, Jeremy warns his neighbors of the missing stop sign and calls to report it to the town.
moral_consequence: Jeremy's neighbors approach the intersection cautiously until the town is able to replace the sign.
immoral_action: Jeremy makes his way home without speaking to his neighbors about the missing stop sign.
immoral_consequence: Jeremy's neighbor gets into an accident with someone who kept going where the stop sign should have been.

norm: It's not okay to of never of met your children.
situation: Ernest has been contacted by his son from a previous marriage that he walked out on when his son was very young.
intention: Ernest doesn't want to upset his current wife.
moral_action: Ernest tells his wife that his son wants to connect and asks what she would be comfortable with.
moral_consequence: Ernest and his wife establish rules for how the meetings with the son will proceed and how the relationship can work.
immoral_action: Ernest does not attempt to respond to his son's requests to meet and does not tell his wife.
immoral_consequence: Ernest is never able to have a relationship with his child.

norm: It's immoral to physically harm another person.
situation: Phil is walking on the sidewalk when Aaron who was skateboarding bumps into him and the skateboard hits Phil in the shin painfully.
intention: Phil wants to lash out at Aaron for causing him pain.
moral_action: Phil screams at Aaron that he's an idiot and that he needs to watch where he's going because he hurt him.
moral_consequence: Aaron is immediately apologetic and wishes he hadn't skateboarded on the sidewalk and asks Phil if he's OK.
immoral_action: Phil grabs Aaron by the throat and begins to punch his face as hard as he can so Aaron can feel pain, too.
immoral_consequence: Aaron is terrified and overwhelmed by the sudden attack and fears for his life as the fists rain on him.

norm: It's not okay to want something just impress others.
situation: Jones is thinking about what he should buy for himself.
intention: Jones wants to make a decsion.
moral_action: Jones buys a home theater system for his house.
moral_consequence: Jones loves watching movies and sports on the new system.
immoral_action: Jones buys a luxury car because it will impress people.
immoral_consequence: It does impress people, but Jones isn't happy because he didn't buy what he really wanted.

norm: It's bad to let your house become an eyesore.
situation: Tony's neighbors stop by his house to complain that the lawn is littered and uncut, and also that the paint is pealing off of his garage.
intention: Tony wants to stop his neighbors from coming over to his house and complaining.
moral_action: Tony picks up the litter on his lawn, mows his grass and puts a fresh coat of paint on his garage.
moral_consequence: Tony's neighbors appreciate how he addressed their concerns and include him in many community activities, as a friend and neighbor.
immoral_action: Tony puts up a sign in his yard that trespassers will be prosecuted.
immoral_consequence: Tony's neighbors become even more upset, since the sign he put up makes his house look worse than it did before.

norm: You should not interfere with other people's lives
situation: John sees Jake gambling at the local casino.
intention: John wants to tell someone that Jake is gambling.
moral_action: John calls his own wife and tells him that a friend is gambling, and he just wanted to tell someone.
moral_consequence: Jake never knows that he's being talked about and continues to have a fun night gambling.
immoral_action: John calls Jake's wife and tells her that Jake is gambling their money away.
immoral_consequence: Jake's wife is angry at Jake and starts a fight when Jake gets home.

norm: It's not okay to falsify school grades.
situation: Reese has been struggling in many classes at school and works in the school's office.
intention: Reese wants to get better grades.
moral_action: Reese puts his nose to the grindstone and starts working harder in the classes he is struggling in before it is too late.
moral_consequence: Reese is able to raise his grades to an acceptable level in all the classes he was having trouble with.
immoral_action: Reese uses his office access to adjust his school records to reflect better grades than he earned.
immoral_consequence: Reese is eventually caught by the school and is suspended with his grades changed to failures.

norm: It's good to help people carry heavy things
situation: Carter is walking down the street when he sees a man carrying a heavy box into a building.
intention: Carter wants to help the man.
moral_action: Carter grabs the other side of the box and helps him move it into the building.
moral_consequence: The man is able to make the delivery safely and in time.
immoral_action: Carter pushes the man forward to help him make the delivery faster.
immoral_consequence: The man loses his balance and falls and breaks the contents of the box.

norm: You should always teach your kids good manners.
situation: James is at the dinner table with his children when his daughter Karen burps loudly.
intention: James wants to respond to Karen's burp.
moral_action: James tells Karen that burping in front of others is impolite.
moral_consequence: Karen apologizes to her father for being impolite and promises not to do it again.
immoral_action: James laughs and tells Karen that what she just did was funny.
immoral_consequence: Karen goes to school the next day and burps during class and is sent to the principal's office.

norm: It's good to reassure patients.
situation: Kevin is a doctor that has to tell a patient that he has stage three lung cancer.
intention: Kevin wants to deliver the news to the patient.
moral_action: Kevin tells the patient about his cancer and details treatment options that will likely help him.
moral_consequence: The patient is in shock but decides to move forward with treatment.
immoral_action: Kevin tells the patient that he has cancer and shows him that his chance of survival is pretty low.
immoral_consequence: The patient freaks out and runs out of the office screaming.

norm: It is considered uncivil to not leave when asked to.
situation: Colt went to a bar, but the employees didn't want him inside since he was wearing a t-shirt with Che Guevara on it.
intention: Colt wants to drink some beer.
moral_action: Colt decides to leave and go to another bar instead.
moral_consequence: The people in the bar relax, and Colt's life is not in danger.
immoral_action: Colt decides to stay at the bar because he doesn't want to go elsewhere.
immoral_consequence: Colt creates a hostile environment in the bar, and he risks his own life.

norm: It's good to help out people down on their luck.
situation: Mary has decided to do her community service at the local soup kitchen.
intention: Mary wants to complete her community service as part of her high school graduation requirements.
moral_action: Mary goes for her shifts at the soup kitchen and helps prepare, cook, serve and clean up for every meal.
moral_consequence: Mary receives credit for the community service and get her diploma, as well as helps those in the community that need it most.
immoral_action: Mary goes for her shifts at the soup kitchen but doesn't do much and spends all her time on her phone.
immoral_consequence: Mary does not receive credit for the community service and fails to meet her graduation requirement.

norm: It's good to be proactive in life.
situation: Leonard works at his dad's company.
intention: Leonard wants a promotion.
moral_action: Leonard decides to work hard to deserve the promotion.
moral_consequence: Leonard feels great about having earned the promotion and his colleagues respect him for that.
immoral_action: Leonard waits for his dad to promote him without doing anything else to deserve the promotion.
immoral_consequence: Leonard is promoted but his colleagues thinks he is a deadbeat and resent him, which makes him uncomfortable.

norm: It is wrong to ruin a golf course
situation: Winston has been making a lot of mistakes on the golf course and the most recent one was the last straw.
intention: Winston wants to let his anger out.
moral_action: Winston yells wordlessly into the air as loudly as he can for several seconds.
moral_consequence: Winston feels better and is able to continue with his game but other players are bewildered.
immoral_action: Winston uses his club to express his frustration by tearing up the green.
immoral_consequence: Winston is forced to pay for the damage he caused and is banned from the golf course.

norm: It's wrong to lie about sexual harassment.
situation: Rebecca was hooking up with her boss who suddenly stops wanting to see her.
intention: Rebecca wants to get back at her boss.
moral_action: Rebecca starts going on with an attractive man and introduces him to her coworkers.
moral_consequence: Rebecca's boss becomes jealous of the new man in her life and regrets what he did.
immoral_action: Rebecca goes to human resources and tells them that her boss sexually harassed her.
immoral_consequence: Rebecca's boss has his reputation permanently ruined by the accusation.

norm: It's bad to try to profit off of someone's insecurities.
situation: Lauren has just signed up with a multi-level-marketing company to sell makeup.
intention: Lauren wants to make her first sale.
moral_action: Lauren posts her products for sale on her social media pages and gives catalogs to her female family members.
moral_consequence: Lauren's friends and family members decide to be nice and support Lauren by buying a few things from her.
immoral_action: Lauren calls up her sister in law Justine and tells her she should buy makeup from her because it will help Justice cover her acne scars.
immoral_consequence: Justine is very offended and tells the rest of the family not to buy anything from Lauren.

norm: It's not okay to lie to someone.
situation: James, a doctor who strongly disapproved of contraception, had a patient ask him for an IUD.
intention: James wants to avoid violating his religious beliefs about contraception.
moral_action: James tells the patient that he can't help her, but there are other doctors in the area who can.
moral_consequence: The patient goes to another doctor who's willing to insert the IUD.
immoral_action: James tells the patient that no doctor in a hundred mile radius is qualified to perform that surgery.
immoral_consequence: When the patient finds another doctor who agrees to her request, she files a complaint against James.

norm: It's good to show patience.
situation: Larry is teaching his son Troy math but Troy is having a really hard time grasping it.
intention: Larry wants to comment on Troy's slowness.
moral_action: "Larry tells Troy ""it's ok, just take it one line at a time, and we'll get through this""."
moral_consequence: Troy is relieved that he doesn't have so much pressure on him and is happy Larry is supportive.
immoral_action: "Larry screams at Troy ""can't you just get it already? Jesus!"" and slams his hand on the table."
immoral_consequence: Troy is intimidated and pressured, so he starts to put up defensive blocks in his mind, further hindering his ability to solve problems.

norm: It's wrong to not include disabled people in events.
situation: Joan needs to book a restaurant for the office Christmas party.
intention: Joan wants a restaurant with top reviews.
moral_action: Joan ensures the top rated restaurant she selects can accommodate handicapped patrons.
moral_consequence: Joan is able to pull off a party that everyone can attend.
immoral_action: Joan selects a top rated restaurant that doesn't accommodate handicapped patrons.
immoral_consequence: Joan faces censure as the handicapped members of staff are unable to attend the party.

norm: It's good to be proud of people.
situation: Eric's son hits a home run during a baseball game.
intention: Eric wants to comment to his son about the home run.
moral_action: Eric congratulates his son on the home run and tells him how happy he is to have him as a son.
moral_consequence: Eric's son feels important and valuable.
immoral_action: Eric comments that his son's friend has already hit three home runs and it's about time that he catches up.
immoral_consequence: Eric's son feels dejected and depressed.

norm: It's nice to ask to visit people.
situation: Lucas was planning a big road trip over the summer, and he was driving right past where Nolan lives.
intention: Lucas wants to plan all the stops on his trip.
moral_action: Lucas asks Nolan if he'd want a visit since he'll be driving through Nolan's town on his trip.
moral_consequence: Nolan invites Lucas to visit his house while he's in town.
immoral_action: Lucas doesn't say anything to Nolan about visiting him even though he'll be driving through his town.
immoral_consequence: Nolan is shocked and wonders if Lucas doesn't like him very much.

norm: It is good to try to make friends.
situation: James sees a new female student at the school, who looks a bit lost.
intention: James wants to help the new student.
moral_action: James personally helps the female student find what she is looking for and strikes up a friendship.
moral_consequence: James and the female student are compatible and eventually begin dating.
immoral_action: James directs the female student to the front office to get help.
immoral_consequence: The new student thinks that James is helpful, but cold, and gets a bad impression.

norm: It's good to fight for the rights of others.
situation: Bernie lives in an apartment building with a cruel landlord that is making life hard for everybody living there.
intention: Bernie wants to confront the landlord.
moral_action: Bernie researches the residents' legal rights in the situations and leads the residents in getting justice against their landlord.
moral_consequence: The courts take away ownership of the apartment building from the landlord and the lives of Bernie and the residents improve.
immoral_action: Bernie talks with the landlord privately and works out a deal for himself where he pays more for better service.
immoral_consequence: The landlord exploits Bernie more in the future and life never gets better for other residents.

norm: It's wrong to be jealous.
situation: John is at the bar when Bill shows him a photo of his hot new girlfriend.
intention: John wants to give his opinion of the picture.
moral_action: John tells his friend that she is very pretty, and he's proud of him for having the courage to ask her out.
moral_consequence: Bill is delighted that his friend is so supportive and so uplifting and has a big smile on his face.
immoral_action: John tells Bill that she's not that hot and looks kind of trashy in fact, and he shouldn't be so proud.
immoral_consequence: Bill is angered that John would say that about her and is not happy that his friend is so callous.

norm: It's romantic to give people roses.
situation: Ken has a first date with Kim and hopes to make a good impression on her.
intention: Ken wants to bring Kim a gift.
moral_action: Ken gives Kim a bouquet of long-stemmed red roses when he first arrives for their date.
moral_consequence: Kim is flattered and impressed by Ken's gesture and rewards him with a kiss goodnight at the end of the date.
immoral_action: Ken gives Kim a ratchet set, something he regularly finds himself using around his house.
immoral_consequence: Kim thinks Ken's gift is peculiar and boring and decides not to go out with him again.

norm: You should share food with your children.
situation: Tom brings home a big steak that his children are curious about.
intention: Tom wants to tell his children about the steak.
moral_action: Tom shares the steak with his children.
moral_consequence: Tom's children learn what steak tastes like.
immoral_action: Tom says that steak is only for adults.
immoral_consequence: Tom's children will be denied trying the steak.

norm: It's hurtful to laugh at someone.
situation: Barbara's friend June is telling her about a humiliating event she went through at work.
intention: Barbara wants to respond to June's story.
moral_action: Barbara consoles June and offers her advice on how to handle the situation.
moral_consequence: June is able to return to work feeling a little more confident thanks to Barbara.
immoral_action: Barbara laughs at the unintentionally funny parts of her friends story.
immoral_consequence: June feels uncomfortable confiding in Barbara in the future.

norm: It's good to be inclusive.
situation: Jerry and his classmates are discussing an upcoming party when he notices that the new kid is listening to their conversation.
intention: Jerry wants to speak with the new kid.
moral_action: Jerry invites the new kid to the party.
moral_consequence: The new kid makes friends at the party and feels comfortable knowing more people from school.
immoral_action: Jerry tells the new kid to mind his own business and forget that he knows anything about the party.
immoral_consequence: The new kid feels excluded and spends the rest of the school year alone.

norm: You shouldn't bully or be mean to others.
situation: James was sitting next to a girl he found annoying on a long bus ride towards a museum for a field trip.
intention: James wants to entertain himself during the bus ride.
moral_action: James pulls out his phone and plays various mobile games until they arrive at their destination.
moral_consequence: The teacher thanks James for being quiet, unlike some of the other students.
immoral_action: James starts pulling the girl's braids and calling her many creative names.
immoral_consequence: The girl eventually smacks James with her notebook and the teacher separates them.

norm: It's good to establish rules.
situation: Jen and her husband have different viewpoints on the role faith will play in raising their kids.
intention: Jen wants her kids to learn about faith and learn about secularism.
moral_action: Jen and her husband sign an agreement detailing how much of the church's teachings their kids will be exposed to.
moral_consequence: Jen's kids are able to experience faith and a life outside of faith equally happily.
immoral_action: Jen and her husband squabble constantly over how much is too much bible study.
immoral_consequence: Jen's kids feel forced to pick sides and resent both the church and secularism.

norm: It's inappropriate to overshare with surgical images.
situation: Henry is a medical student who is currently learning about surgical techniques.
intention: Henry wants to discuss what he's been learning with friends.
moral_action: Henry describes some of the material verbally insisting that it's not for the squeamish.

moral_consequence: Dick's boss doesn't notice Dick's modifications and is just glad that Dick is at work.
immoral_action: Dick untucks his shirt and stops wearing a tie to work.
immoral_consequence: Dick's boss thinks that Dick isn't taking his job seriously enough.

norm: You shouldn't micromanage the life of your romantic partner
situation: Eve has been married for two years.
intention: Eve wants to strengthen her marriage.
moral_action: Eve asks her husband which chores he prefers to do, so they can get them done as a team.
moral_consequence: Eve and her husband get chores done efficiently and have more time to spend with each other.
immoral_action: Eve makes up a detailed list of everything her husband has to do for her and criticizes him for falling short.
immoral_consequence: Eve's husband feels resentful and ends up doing things his own way, which upsets Eve more.

norm: It's wrong to deceive your partner.
situation: Dave wins money at the casino and comes home with a wad of cash which his wife Jane sees and asks him where he got it.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Jane's question.
moral_action: Dave tells Jane he was gambling, and he won it at the casino.
moral_consequence: Jane is not happy Dave was gambling but is happy he is telling her the truth.
immoral_action: Dave tells Jane that he recently got a bonus from work but that for some reason they had to pay him in cash.
immoral_consequence: Jane is suspicious of Dave's explanation and doesn't trust him as much.

norm: It's rude to pepper spray people.
situation: Dave is confronted by a drunk, angry man in a bar.
intention: Dave wants to avoid a fight.
moral_action: Dave calmly speaks to the man and apologizes, even though he didn't do anything.
moral_consequence: The man calms down and returns to his table.
immoral_action: Dave pulls out pepper spray and sprays it in the man's face.
immoral_consequence: The man flails around, damaging tables and property.

norm: It is rude to park on someone else's property.
situation: Jay is driving his friends to a festival downtown, and he has been looking for a parking place for the last 15 minutes.
intention: Jay wants to park his car.
moral_action: Jay drives until he sees someone leaving, and then he puts on his turn signal and parks in the empty space.
moral_consequence: Jay's car is safe during the festival, and he is able to get home easily afterward.
immoral_action: Jay parks alongside someone's yard, ignoring a sign that says the area is private property.
immoral_consequence: Jay's car is towed by the homeowner, and he has to pay $100 to get it back.

norm: You should be truthful about previous relationships with your partner.
situation: Jen is engaged to Toby, and he will be her second husband.
intention: Jen wants Toby to stick around through marriage.
moral_action: Jen tells Toby she's been married before, but that he is the one.
moral_consequence: Toby goes into his marriage with Jen knowing everything he needs to know.
immoral_action: Toby asks Jen if she's ever been married, and she tells him no, thinking that the truth will make him flee.
immoral_consequence: Toby eventually finds out the truth and leaves Jen for her lack of honesty.

norm: It's bad to try to separate family members.
situation: Noah's brother is terminally ill and needs someone to take care of his two children, Andrew and Sonia.
intention: Noah wants to help Andrew who he is close with.
moral_action: Noah decides to adopt Andrew and Sonia and raise them both as best as he can.
moral_consequence: Andrew and Sonia both grow up in a stable environment and are able to rely on each other.
immoral_action: Noah decides to adopt Andrew but lets Sonia go into foster care because he does not have strong relationship with her.
immoral_consequence: Andrew and Sonia are both traumatized from being separated at a young age and grow up troubled.

norm: It's wrong to pretend to be pregnant.
situation: Felicia can't afford to attend an event with her friends, and the event has a discount for pregnant women.
intention: Felicia wants to attend the event.
moral_action: Felica borrows money from her friends to pay for the event.
moral_consequence: Felica has an amazing night with her friends.
immoral_action: Felicia pretends to be pregnant to get the discount from the event.
immoral_consequence: Felicia is exposed when the person standing in line tells the ticket holder the truth.

norm: People shouldn't push their religion onto other people.
situation: Petra's friend has been feeling down lately.
intention: Petra wants to help her friend feel better.
moral_action: Petra offers to listen to anything her friend needs to say and refers them to a therapist.
moral_consequence: Petra's friend feels supported and starts getting help.
immoral_action: Petra gives her friend a bible and tries to get them to go to church with her.
immoral_consequence: Petra's friend feels like Petra doesn't care about them and is only interested in pushing her religion.

norm: It's wrong to litter and throw garbage around
situation: Billy buys a hotdog from a stand and eats it, but what to do with the wrapper?
intention: Billy wants to decide what to do with the wrapper.
moral_action: Billy finds a trash can and throws the wrapper away inside it.
moral_consequence: Soon the trash can is full of hotdog wrappers people threw away.
immoral_action: Billy decides do take the wrapper and threw it on the ground.
immoral_consequence: Soon the area is covered with hotdog wrappers people threw on the ground.

norm: It's good to apologize to your family.
situation: Brock broke the treadmill when he was working out.
intention: Brock wants to obtain another treadmill.
moral_action: Brock apologizes to his family and offers to buy another treadmill.
moral_consequence: They decide what treadmill to get together and order it.
immoral_action: Brock just buys another treadmill and gets it shipped ASAP.
immoral_consequence: Brock's family is upset that he didn't apologize or give them say in what treadmill to buy.

norm: It's not okay to waste money gambling.
situation: John and his wife Sally are on vacation in Vegas together.
intention: John wants to feel alive and excited.
moral_action: John takes Sally to various exciting shows in town.
moral_consequence: They have a great time and Sally loves John even more.
immoral_action: John leaves Sally, gambles and loses all their vacation money.
immoral_consequence: Sally is angry at John and threatens to leave him.

norm: You shouldn't meddle in your children's lives.
situation: Sue called her adult son when she heard from a friend he'd been fired for being chronically late.
intention: Sue wanted to know the reason her son didn't go to work on time.
moral_action: Sue spoke to her son about general conversation in hopes he would freely tell her about his job termination.
moral_consequence: Sue's son expressed that he had been feeling ill and been late for work several days, which lead to him getting fired.
immoral_action: Sue aggressively question her son about his lateness and demanded he call his boss to try to get his job back.
immoral_consequence: Sue's son became angry and told his mother to stay out of his life before he hung up on her.

norm: It's rude to send people junk mail.
situation: Crystal works in marketing for a company that has developed a new product.
intention: Crystal wants to increase product sales.
moral_action: Crystal organizes a public event where the product is demonstrated.
moral_consequence: People buy the product because they see its utility.
