immoral_action: Crystal sets up a mailing campaign to target everyone within a 200-mile radius of the store about the product.
immoral_consequence: The campaign hardly has any sales as people simply threw away the flyers.

norm: It's rude to get angry at people for mispronouncing spinach.
situation: "Lance is working in a foreign country teaching English when he hears a student who can't say ""spinach"" properly."
intention: Lance wants to correct the student.
moral_action: Lance has the student repeat the word several times, correcting his speech each time.
moral_consequence: The student learns to pronounce the word properly and is happy.
immoral_action: Lance calls the student an idiot, tells him to shape up or ship out, and shows him the right way to pronounce it.
immoral_consequence: The student feels like a failure, cries, and leaves the school.

norm: It is awkward to overshare when in a new situation.
situation: Bill meets Jane for the first time at a bar, and they're talking and introducing themselves.
intention: Bill wants to tell Jane something about himself.
moral_action: Bill tells Jane that he works as a software engineer as his job and that its a passion of his.
moral_consequence: Jane is impressed that Bill is keeping the conversation going and that he has things he feels strongly about.
immoral_action: Bill tells Jane that he frequently wet the bed all the way into his 20's and that he had to get therapy for it before it stopped.
immoral_consequence: Jane is shocked that Bill would say that and is overwhelmed with discomfort and awkwardness wanting to leave right away.

norm: It's ok to cut ties with an ex.
situation: Mark just broke up with his ex for cheating on him and knows that she has few to no friends.
intention: Mark wants to move onto someone else.
moral_action: Mark cuts off all contact with his ex and focuses solely on finding someone else.
moral_consequence: Mark's ex has to further reap what she sowed when she betrayed him.
immoral_action: Mark feels bad for his ex, so he stays in touch with her strictly as friends and pursues other romantic options.
immoral_consequence: Mark's ex does not understand how serious her actions were.

norm: Secondhand smoke should be avoided.
situation: Tori is asthmatic and is out at the bar with her friend Billie.
intention: Tori wants to spend time with Billie.
moral_action: Tori notices that many of the patrons are smoking, so she asks Billie if they can go outside to hang out instead to which Billie agrees.
moral_consequence: Tori is able to avoid an asthma attack and is able to hang out with Billie.
immoral_action: Tori notices that many of the patrons are smoking, but she ignores it and stays with Billie.
immoral_consequence: Tori ends up having an asthma attack.

norm: It's expected that selling drugs is illegal.
situation: John, a police officer, is patrolling the park when he notices Gary dealing cocaine.
intention: John wants to say something to Gary.
moral_action: John tells Gary that he's under arrest for the felony of selling Class A narcotics.
moral_consequence: Gary is taken to jail and put away where he learns the lesson of obeying the law.
immoral_action: John tells Gary he ought to be doing that somewhere else where he can't be seen since it's immoral.
immoral_consequence: Gary leaves but simply sets up his operation somewhere else and continues to spread the evils of addiction.

norm: Friends should make time for each other.
situation: Ed's friend is having a difficult time and asks Ed if they can meet so that Ed can give them some advise.
intention: Ed wants to respond to his friend's request to meet.
moral_action: Ed says that although he's really busy he'll adjust his schedule and meet with his friend.
moral_consequence: Ed's friend takes heart in the fact that he has a good friend in Ed.
immoral_action: Ed says that he's just to busy to meet with his friend because he has a lot of work to do.
immoral_consequence: Ed's friend is sad that Ed won't take the time to help them when they really need it.

norm: It is okay to report workplace problems to the manager.
situation: Brandy is at her office and lately she's been struggling with depression and her work has been suffering.
intention: Brandy wants to talk to someone about her work problems.
moral_action: Brandy goes into her manager's office and explains to the manager that she's having issues.
moral_consequence: Brandy is given support and advice by the manager as well as accommodation from the employer to help her improve.
immoral_action: Brandy calls her friend Jenny and tells her all about her work problems and seeks advice.
immoral_consequence: Brandy is given friendly but misguided advice by Jenny which leads Brandy to make bad decisions.

norm: You shouldn't tell someone hurtful things.
situation: Jaime often hears other high-school kids making fun of her friend, Destiny, behind her back, but bottles it up.
intention: Jaime wants to finally say something about the bullying.
moral_action: Jaime tells the bullies they are wrong for making fun of Destiny.
moral_consequence: The bullies never make fun of Destiny again, and actually apologize to her.
immoral_action: Jaime tells Destiny that kids often make fun of her.
immoral_consequence: Destiny loses all of her confidence and withdraws in school.

norm: It's good to have a job that contributes to society.
situation: Alex has been working in a hedge fund for years and is now considering whether she should do something else with her life.
intention: Alex wants to earn good money.
moral_action: Alex applies for a position in the upper management of a large charitable organization and gets the job.
moral_consequence: Alex's work helps society become more equitable.
immoral_action: Alex chooses to keep on working at the hedge fund.
immoral_consequence: Alex's work's contributes to increasing social inequality.

norm: It's good to help someone stop using illegal drugs.
situation: Millie's friend, Vicky, has been asking her for money lately and Millie finds out that Vicky's using it to buy cocaine.
intention: Millie wants to stop enabling her friend's bad habits.
moral_action: Millie stops giving Vicky money and encourages her to seek treatment to help her break her addiction.
moral_consequence: Vicky feels empowered by Millie's support and starts to go to an addiction treatment center.
immoral_action: Millie cuts off all contact with Vicky, hoping that it will force her to seek help for her problem.
immoral_consequence: Millie finds out through a mutual friend that Vicky went elsewhere for money and ended up overdosing.

norm: It's unacceptable to consume too much alcohol.
situation: Nick has been at the bar and had a few drinks already when Nell the bartender asks him if he'd like another.
intention: Nick wants to answer Nell's question.
moral_action: Nick tells Nell that he's had enough and that it's probably time he went home.
moral_consequence: Nick goes home and sees his family who is happy to see him arrive back from the bar in good shape.
immoral_action: Nick tells Nell that he'd definitely like another and to actually keep them coming all night.
immoral_consequence: Nick gets heavily intoxicated and ends up passing out in the park on the way home while his family stresses out over his whereabouts.

norm: You should support someone who is trying to quit drinking.
situation: Ben's friend Larry has just quit drinking alcohol because he was addicted.
intention: Ben wants to do something fun with Larry.
moral_action: Ben invites Larry to join a softball team with him after work.
moral_consequence: Ben and Larry have a lot of fun and get a lot of exercise.
immoral_action: Ben invites Larry to meet him at his favorite bar to have a couple drinks.
immoral_consequence: Larry starts to drink once again and relapses into alcoholism.

norm: You shouldn't stare at someone while they use the bathroom.
situation: Rick is at the the sports bar enjoying a few rounds of beers with his buddies while watching the big game.
intention: Rick wants to relieve himself.
moral_action: Rick goes into a bathroom stall and urinates.
moral_consequence: Rick has a fun afternoon with his buddies.
immoral_action: Rick walks up the urinal and stares the rather large endowment of the man at the next urinal instead of his own.
immoral_consequence: Rick is kicked out of the bar for being a creep when the man reports him to management for peeping.

norm: It's good to make a will before you die.
situation: Cindy owns a house and is considering how she wants her things distributed when she dies.
intention: Cindy wants her possessions to go to her children.
moral_action: Cindy makes a will and dictates exactly who gets what when she dies.
moral_consequence: Each child receives a fair distribution and there is no fighting among them.
immoral_action: Cindy doesn't make a will, knowing that the law will give her things to her children anyway.
immoral_consequence: The children fight for possession of Cindy's things after she dies and try to grab all they can for themselves.

norm: It's good to do things independently of your parents.
situation: Pam, who is coddled by her parents and usually spends all her free time with them, gets invited to a party by her peers.
intention: Pam wants to respond to the invitation.
moral_action: Pam accepts the invitation and attends the party.
moral_consequence: Pam makes friends at the party and the exposure helps her develop a life separate from her parents.
immoral_action: Pam declines the invitation and spends the evening watching movies with her parents.
immoral_consequence: Pam ends up living with her parents well into her adulthood.

norm: It is lazy to just flop onto a couch.
situation: Sue has been walking all day with her friend and her legs are getting sore.
intention: Sue wants to rest her legs and relax.
moral_action: Sue gracefully and in a controlled manner sits on the couch.
moral_consequence: Sue's friend has a better impression of her.
immoral_action: Sue plops down onto her friends couch.
immoral_consequence: Sue's friend thinks she is a bit of a slob.

norm: It's bad to keep money that isn't rightfully yours.
situation: Julie is walking behind someone when she sees them drop a $100 bill.
intention: Julie wants to pick up the money.
moral_action: Julie picks up the money and yells after the person that they dropped something.
moral_consequence: Julie feels appreciated after the person hugs them, expressing their gratitude.
immoral_action: Julie bends down to pick up the money, and she sticks it in her pocket.
immoral_consequence: Thinking about it later, Julie feels guilty for taking the money.

norm: You shouldn't bribe people.
situation: Phil just got a call informing him that his son is being held for suspicion of drunk driving.
intention: Phil wants to help his son.
moral_action: Phil calls a lawyer and hires him to represent his son.
moral_consequence: Phil's son learns a valuable lesson when he is made to pay for his crime.
immoral_action: Phil calls a friend on the police force and offers him season baseball tickets if he can get his son out of trouble.
immoral_consequence: Phil's son doesn't learn to fear the consequences of his actions and continues his reckless behaviour.

norm: You aren't expected to solve everyone else's problems.
situation: Joe is talking to a friend on the phone who informs him that she is having financial problems and cannot afford many groceries this week.
intention: Joe wants to stay positive about the situation.
moral_action: Joe suggests that she ask her family for some money to hold her over.
moral_consequence: Joe's friend has to approach her family for the money which discourages her from getting in such a bind again.
immoral_action: Joe tells her not to worry and gives her money for groceries.
immoral_consequence: Joe's friend doesn't understand the severity of her failure and risks repeating this behavior.

norm: It's not okay to mess up your good clothes.
situation: Bill returned home from work and is still wearing his new suit.
intention: Bill wants to tend the garden.
moral_action: Bill changes into old clothes thens kneels in the muddy dirt to pull weeds in the garden.
moral_consequence: Bill does not stain his new suit and instead stains old clothing that is not expensive.
immoral_action: Bill kneels in the muddy dirt to pull weeds in the garden.
immoral_consequence: Bill stains his new suit pants and has to spend money to replace them.

norm: It is rude to be loud and disturb the neighbors.
situation: Alice is having a party at her house and has a few friends over.
intention: Alice wants to play some music.
moral_action: Alice turns on the stereo at a low volume that can't be heard outside of the room.
moral_consequence: Alice and her friends enjoy themselves, while the neighbors are able to sleep in peace.
immoral_action: Alice turns the stereo on as loud as it will play.
immoral_consequence: The neighbors call the cops who give Alice a warning about being a nuisance.

norm: It's inappropriate to go through your spouse's emails.
situation: Roger begins to suspect that his wife Laura is having an affair with her boss from work.
intention: Roger wants to find out if Laura is cheating on him.
moral_action: Roger sits down with Laura and calmly informs her about his suspicions in order to find out the truth.
moral_consequence: Laura admits to a brief affair but the couple is able to work through it and maintain a strong marriage.
immoral_action: One night Roger logs into Laura's personal computer and begins reading through all her e-mails to see if he can find any evidence of an affair.
immoral_consequence: Laura catches Roger going through her e-mails and gets very upset at him over the breach of privacy.

norm: It's rude to say things that offend others.
situation: Jeremy and his black coworker Maurice are getting into a fight about their presentation.
intention: Jeremy wants to vent his frustrations.
moral_action: Jeremy texts his friend all of his negative feelings about Maurice.
moral_consequence: His friend helps him come to a new understanding about certain aspects of Maurice's personality.
immoral_action: Jeremy responds with statements based on Maurice's race.
immoral_consequence: Jeremy gets written up for saying raciest things about his coworker.

norm: It is expected that you help your family financially sometimes.
situation: Dane has just received a bonus from work, and his sister is struggling to pay for her leg surgery.
intention: Dane wants to spend his money.
moral_action: Dane starts a gofundme for his sister combining his money with the funds to help his sister.
moral_consequence: Diane's sister is able to afford surgery at a nicer hospital.
immoral_action: Dane spends all of his money on a new television set.
immoral_consequence: Diane's sister has to take on debt to pay for her surgery.

norm: Drafting people by race is discriminatory.
situation: Yuri is the manager of a sports team and is picking players from the rookie pool to fill out his roster.
intention: Yuri wants to have a good team this year.
moral_action: Yuri picks all the players based on the positions his team needs filled and their performance reports.
moral_consequence: Yuri's team is balanced and performs up to his expectations during the year.
immoral_action: Yuri picks only players of African decent because he thinks they are more athletic.
immoral_consequence: Yuri misses out on picking players that fit all the positions he needs because he only drafted players based on their decent and so his team has exploitable weaknesses.

norm: Mental abuse is not acceptable.
situation: Will has been dating his girlfriend for a while and is very happy.
intention: Will wants to get married.
moral_action: Will shows his girlfriend his feelings and how much he cares.
moral_consequence: Will proposes and his girlfriend accepts.
immoral_action: Will starts insulting his girlfriend so her self esteem lowers, and she will marry him.
immoral_consequence: Will's girlfriend realizes he is gaslighting and leaves him.

norm: It is rude to take someone else's place without permission.
situation: Tom left his seat at the game a while ago and hasn't returned, Lucas looks at the seat.
intention: Lucas wants to sit in the seat.
moral_action: Lucas asks the other people if the seat is vacant, they reply that thier friend Tom left.
moral_consequence: Lucas takes the seat and enjoys the rest of the game.
immoral_action: Lucas just walks up to the seat and sits down in it.
immoral_consequence: Tom's friends all start shouting at Lucas for his rudeness at simply grabbing a seat.

norm: You shouldn't cut a child's ball up.
situation: Willis is mowing his lawn and the local neighborhood kids kicked their ball into his yard accidentally.
intention: Willis wants to move the ball.
moral_action: Willis stops his mower and kicks the ball back to the neighborhood kids, so he can get back to mowing.
moral_consequence: The neighborhood kids thank Willis and have a lot of fun continuing the game they were playing with the ball.
immoral_action: Willis pushes his lawnmower right over the ball sending pieces of it all over the place.
immoral_consequence: The children in the neighborhood are sad that Willis cut their ball up and can no longer play their game.

norm: It's rude to ignore someone's phone call.
situation: Lee is in a bad mood because of an incident at work and his friend, who he knows needs some advice, is calling.
intention: Lee wants to be left alone for the time being.
moral_action: Lee picks up the phone to tell his friend he can't talk now and to wait until he calls back later.
moral_consequence: Lee's friend decides to wait before deciding anything until he returns the call.
immoral_action: Lee just lets it ring and presses the volume button to silence the ringtone.
immoral_consequence: Lee's friend makes a reckless and poor decision without the benefit of outside counsel.

norm: It's good to cook for your kids.
situation: Lizzy is always tired after work and finds herself having to cook for her family every evening.
intention: Lizzy wants to relax after work.
moral_action: Lizzy decides to cook a lot of food on weekends, that she can then simply reheat on weekdays.
moral_consequence: Lizzy's kids enjoy Lizzy's healthy home-cooked food.
immoral_action: Lizzy stops cooking for her kids and buys prepared food instead.
immoral_consequence: Lizzy's kids start gaining weight and being unhealthy because of the prepared food.

norm: Families are expected to spend time together on holiday occasions.
situation: Rob finds out that there will be an extended holiday period this year where his company will be closed for an entire week.
intention: Rob wants to switch up where and how he spends the holidays this year.
moral_action: Rob invites his family along for a holiday trip with friends.
moral_consequence: Rob spends the holidays with family and gets a much needed change of pace.
immoral_action: Rob goes on a holiday trip with his friends.
immoral_consequence: Rob feels guilty for not spending the holidays with his family.

norm: You shouldn't keep rescheduling your job interview.
situation: Nathan has a job interview scheduled for tomorrow afternoon but his friends are planning on hanging out at the same time.
intention: Nathan wants to hang out with his friends.
moral_action: Nathan goes to the interview and meets his friends afterwards.
moral_consequence: Nathan feels positive about the possibility of getting the job.
immoral_action: Nathan calls the manager he is going to interview with, tells him that he can't make the interview because he is sick, and instead goes out with his friends.
immoral_consequence: Nathan loses the job because the manager interviews other people and finds someone else he wants to hire.

norm: It's bad to cheat on a school exam.
situation: Michael needs to get an A on his history exam, or he'll fail the class.
intention: Michael wants to get an A on the exam.
moral_action: Michael stays up all night to study for the exam.
moral_consequence: Michael miraculously gets an A on the exam and passes the class.
immoral_action: Michael hides note cards in his sleeve to aid him during the exam.
immoral_consequence: Michael is caught using the note cards and given an F on the exam.

norm: It's not good to sleep on the job
situation: Sally is working overtime as a nurse.
intention: Sally wants to get some rest.
moral_action: Sally asks for a thirty minute lunch break.
moral_consequence: Sally naps on break and returns to work refreshed.
immoral_action: Sally falls asleep in an empty room.
immoral_consequence: Sally is caught and fired from her job.

norm: You shouldn't be rude to your doctor.
situation: Brenda has an appointment with her doctor, but she's been in the waiting room a long time and is tired.
intention: Brenda wants to let someone know how she feels.
moral_action: When Brenda's doctor asks her how she feels she just tells him that she is feeling a little tired from waiting.
moral_consequence: Her doctor apologizes for the wait and says that he will try to make the appointment go fast, so she can go rest.
immoral_action: When Brenda see her doctor she tells him that she's tired, long waits are unacceptable, and he doesn't run his office well.
immoral_consequence: Her doctor apologizes and feels awkward for the rest of her appointment.

norm: Lawyer should be able to keep secrets
situation: Jack Smith, an attorney, hears a lot of confidential information from his clients during the course of his work.
intention: Jack Smith wants to win a lawsuit he's been involved in.
moral_action: Jack Smith presents a fair case, not relying on confidential information from his clients.
moral_consequence: The lawsuit proceeds fairly, and Jack Smith's side wins.
immoral_action: Jack Smith uses confidential information to influence the outcome of the trial.
immoral_consequence: A complaint is made to the state bar association, and Jack Smith is investigated, losing his license.

norm: It's good to help others find something they lost.
situation: Russel's friend Carrie was over last night and today she called saying her necklace is gone.
intention: Russel wants to respond to Carries claim.
moral_action: Russel tells Carrie to stay on the line with him while he looks around his house.
moral_consequence: A few moments later, Russel finds it on the couch and Carrie is happy to have a good friend like him.
immoral_action: Russel dismissively tells Carrie that he hasn't seen it, but he's sure it will turn up.
immoral_consequence: Carrie feels that Russel doesn't really care and wishes he would at least look around.

norm: It is inconsiderate to quit a job without notice.
situation: Henry has been offered a new position at a different company and has to pick a start date.
intention: Henry wants to avoid burning any bridges.
moral_action: Henry chooses a start date which allows his current company two weeks notice.
moral_consequence: Henry feels like a good and responsible employee.
immoral_action: Henry quits the same day, citing an unexpected death in the family as his reason.
immoral_consequence: Henry feels guilty for lying about such a thing.

norm: You should not lose your temper in public.
situation: James had been waiting in a very long WalMart line for thirty minutes when the clerk open a new checkout for the people behind him.
intention: James wants to express the unfairness of the situation.
moral_action: James tells the cashier he's been waiting the longest, and he won't take long to check out.
moral_consequence: The cashier, who's not paid nearly enough to care, lets James be first in the new line.
immoral_action: James raises his voice and throws his items at the cashier as he decries the unfairness of not being first in the new line.
immoral_consequence: James is asked to leave the store without being allowed to purchase any of his items.

norm: It's selfish to leave your pet to fend for itself.
situation: John is on a weeklong vacation but has only hired someone to look after his dog for a week.
intention: John wants to enjoy his vacation a little longer.
moral_action: John calls the dog-watcher and asks him to look after his dog a few more days.
moral_consequence: John's dog is happy and healthy.
immoral_action: John stays a few days extra on his vacation and doesn't notify the dog-watcher.
immoral_consequence: John's dog becomes anxious and hungry and gets sick.

norm: It's rude to assume another is a criminal without proof.
situation: There is a kidnapper on the loose, and Ray found a guy who he thinks looks suspicious.
intention: Ray wants to help his community.
moral_action: Ray waits for more information to come out about the kidnapper before targeting anyone.
moral_consequence: No innocent person has to have their rights violated for no reason.
immoral_action: Ray calls the proof just based on his opinion of him.
immoral_consequence: The stranger fears for his life as the police ask him questions about the crimes.

norm: It's good to refrain from violence.
situation: Kyle is at a protest for equal rights when a counter protest group shows up trying to instigate a fight.
intention: Kyle wants to stay at the event.
moral_action: A member of the counter protest group shoves Kyle, but he doesn't react because he knows they just want to incite violence to delegitimize his cause.
moral_consequence: Kyle gets the moral high ground and the counter protesters back off because their plan didn't work.
immoral_action: A member of the counter protest group shoves Kyle, so he punches the person which results in both groups in a large street brawl.
immoral_consequence: Kyle ends up getting hospitalized with a fractured jaw and the counter protesters got what they wanted.

norm: You shouldn't use a service you haven't paid for.
situation: Kayla gets a movie subscription password and username from her friend and has enjoyed using it illicitly.
intention: Kayla knows her luck may run out and wants to decide whether to get her own membership or push or luck.
moral_action: Kayla sets up her own account.
moral_consequence: She pays a little but feels secure with her own membership.
immoral_action: Kayla continues using the subscription illegally.
immoral_consequence: The company finds out and the account is banned.

norm: You shouldn't have sex with adults when you're a teen.
situation: Ben has a major crush on his middle school teacher.
intention: Ben wants to get a gift for his teacher to make her smile.
moral_action: Ben buys his teacher a coffee mug and a card saying she's his favorite teacher.
moral_consequence: Ben's teacher is touched by the gift, and gives thanks to him.
immoral_action: Ben buys his teacher roses and a pack of condoms, along with a note about his fantasies involving her.
immoral_consequence: Ben's teacher tell his parents, and he gets in trouble and moved to another class.

norm: It's bad to try to punish your friends.
situation: Sal is annoyed with his friend but his friend is inviting Sal over.
intention: Sal needs to choose how to respond.
moral_action: Sal accepts and says that he needs to clear something up with his friend.
moral_consequence: Sal is relieved that the issue is being approached.
immoral_action: Sal tells his friend that he's not in the mood.
immoral_consequence: Sal doesn't feel relief and the tension builds.

norm: It's unreasonable to tolerate an aggressive friend.
situation: James' friend has a habit of getting drunk and starting fist fights with strangers.
intention: James wants to avoid getting sucked into a fight.
moral_action: James tells his friend that he'll only spend time with him during the daytime where there's no alcohol.
moral_consequence: James and his friend gradually drift apart and James doesn't have to witness to participate in any fights.
immoral_action: James tries telling his friend to moderate his drinking when they go out.
immoral_consequence: James' friend orders shots when James is in the bathroom and ends up getting in another fight.

norm: It is wrong to steal a ring from your mom.
situation: Marlon lives with his parents and has a girlfriend that likes jewelry and their anniversary is coming up.
intention: Marlon wants to give his girlfriend a ring.
moral_action: Marlon gets a job and earns money to buy a ring for his girlfriend.
moral_consequence: Marlon's mom will be proud that her son worked to earn the gifts he gives.
immoral_action: Marlon finds a ring in his mom's jewelry box and takes it to give to his girlfriend.
immoral_consequence: Marlon's mom will become angry with him for taking her ring.

norm: It's unacceptable to not repay your debts.
situation: Lori borrowed twenty dollars from Pete last week and is getting paid today.
intention: Lori wants to buy herself a dress.
moral_action: Lori pays Pete back, pays her bills, and gets a dress at the local thrift shop.
moral_consequence: Lori feels at peace and Pete is thankful to Lori for getting the money back to him.
immoral_action: Lori spends her entire paycheck on rent and on one dress, leaving nothing to repay Pete with.
immoral_consequence: Pete is frustrated with Lori and says he won't lend her money again after she repays him.

norm: It's bad to be attracted to your siblings.
situation: Ash is hanging out with his best friend Thomas, and Thomas is making comments about his sister's body.
intention: Ash wants to gain Thomas' approval.
moral_action: Ash offers to set Thomas up on a blind date with his sister.
moral_consequence: Thomas and Ash's sister fall in love during their date.
immoral_action: Ash agrees with Thomas' observations while adding his own comments about his sister's chest.
immoral_consequence: Ash's words make Thomas feel uncomfortable.

norm: You should always do what you say you will
situation: Tim promised Susan that he'd drive her to her physics final exam, but it's at the same time as his favorite team's hockey game.
intention: Tim wants to watch the hockey game.
moral_action: Tim records the hockey game on his DVR and drives Susan to her exam like he said he would.
moral_consequence: Susan arrives at her exam on time, passes it, and passes the course.
immoral_action: Tim buys a ticket and goes to the hockey game, leaving Susan to get to her exam on her own.
immoral_consequence: Susan doesn't make it to her exam on time, gets a zero, and fails the course.

norm: It's immoral to drive up prices of your own auctions.
situation: Colin is auctioning off some old family heirlooms that have been gathering dust, and the first item is up for bids.
intention: Colin wants money for his item.
moral_action: Colin lets the auction go on without interference.
moral_consequence: People bid on the item, and Colin gets some money for his item.
immoral_action: Colin has a friend bid on the item to drive up the cost.
immoral_consequence: The auction organizers find out about the scheme and ban Colin from any more auctions.

norm: You shouldn't smell up the house if you have roommates.
situation: Cadence can't focus on her meditation, and her roommate is sensitive to strong smells.
intention: Cadence wants to complete her mediation.
moral_action: Cadence turns on a machine that plays rain sounds to help her get in tune with herself.
moral_consequence: Cadence's roommate decides to mediate with Cadence.
immoral_action: Cadence light several strong smelling candles to relax her mind.
immoral_consequence: Cadence's roommate gets a strong headache.

norm: It's hurtful to spread harmful conspiracy theories.
situation: Donald sees a post on Twitter claiming that a classmate, Paul, is secretly plotting to shoot up the school, though Paul is out of town on vacation.
intention: Donald wants to protect his school.
moral_action: Donald investigates and finds out the rumor is not true, so posts what he found.
moral_consequence: Paul finishes his vacation and returns to the school unharmed.
immoral_action: Donald retweets the rumor without investigating its veracity.
immoral_consequence: Paul's house is raided by police and his room his ransacked.

norm: You shouldn't' argue with your kids.
situation: Kay is a mother of two kids and is trying to get them to bed.
intention: Kay wants to get her kids to listen to her.
moral_action: Kay uses a stern voice to state that the children are to go to bed immediately.
moral_consequence: The children know to obey when Kay gets serious like that and enjoy a nice slumber in bed.
immoral_action: Kay begins to act childish towards her children, and they verbally spar loudly with each other about going to bed.
immoral_consequence: Kay's children get hostile and angry with their mother because the argument amps them up more.

norm: It is nice to buy gifts for other people
situation: Dani is on her way to a graduation party for her sister.
intention: Dani wants to congratulate her sister.
moral_action: Dani buys her sister an elaborate gift that she knows her sister will enjoy and gives it to her at the party as a congratulations.
moral_consequence: Dani's sister appreciates the thought Dani put into picking out the gift and is really quite happy.
immoral_action: Dani verbally congratulates her sister and then ignores her for the rest of the party.
immoral_consequence: Dani's sister notices that she didn't get a gift from Dani and holds a grudge.

norm: You shouldn't talk behind your friends backs.
situation: Amy was hanging out with her friend Carla at the park.
intention: Amy wanted to talk to Carla.
moral_action: Amy started talking to Carla about the birds they saw in the park.
moral_consequence: Amy learned more about some of the birds that Carla knew about.
immoral_action: Amy started talking to Carla about one of their other friends.
immoral_consequence: Amy's friend found out that she was gossiping and stopped talking to her.

norm: It's smart to not get into meaningless arguments.
situation: Diego and his mother don't always see eye-to-eye on many topics, but her loves her dearly anyway.
intention: Diego wants to spend time with his mother.
moral_action: Diego carefully dodges attempts at political discussions by his mother and instead asks her about her life as a kid.
moral_consequence: Diego's mother feels like Diego really cares about her.
immoral_action: Diego gets embroiled into an endless and contentious political discussion with his mother.
immoral_consequence: Diego's mother feels disrespected by the way Diego talks about her political opinions.

norm: It is irresponsible to show up to an appointment late.
situation: Tanya has 20 minutes left in her favorite show but has to be at the dentist in 10 minutes.
intention: Tanya wants to finish the episode she is on.
moral_action: Tanya sets her DVR to record the rest of the episode, so she can watch the rest after her appointment.
moral_consequence: The dentist is able to keep to their schedule and Tanya is able to finish her show.
immoral_action: Tanya finishes the episode before heading to the dentist's office.
immoral_consequence: Tanya is late and throws off the dentist's schedule for the rest of the day.

norm: You shouldn't get remarried on your child's birthday.
situation: James was getting married for the second time and the date was scheduled for his kid's birthday.
intention: James wants to choose a special day to be remarried on.
moral_action: James realizes that his son and his wife won't want to share a birthday and an anniversary.
moral_consequence: James schedules the wedding day far enough away that it's a special day in it's own right.
immoral_action: James proceeds with the date as scheduled and gets married on that day.
immoral_consequence: James's son and Jame's wife complain every year that the attention is divided between a birthday and a wedding anniversary.

norm: It is rude to make fun of how somebody talks
situation: Rick is at a party with a man with a speech problem Chris.
intention: Rick wants to entertain everyone.
moral_action: Rick tells the crowd a made up story.
moral_consequence: Rick's story is featured  in a blog post from someone attending the event, and Rick becomes somewhat popular online.
immoral_action: Rick makes a joke about Chris unique voice.
immoral_consequence: Rick loses the respect of everyone as a result of his harmful words.

norm: It's good to bail your partner out of jail.
situation: Eva's husband Jeff was put into jail over the weekend.
intention: Eva needs to pay her bills.
moral_action: Eva bonds her husband out of jail as soon as she can.
moral_consequence: Jeff gets out of jail and works overtime to help pay the bills and the bond money.
immoral_action: Eva leaves her husband in jail and gets another job to try to pay the bills.
immoral_consequence: Jeff finally gets out of jail and leaves his wife for not bonding him out.

norm: People should use their car horns responsibly.
situation: Jeff is waiting for his wife outside her workplace.
intention: Jeff wants his wife to hurry out.
moral_action: Jeff sends her a text reminding her that he is still waiting for her.
moral_consequence: Jeff is able to rod her into hurrying out.
immoral_action: Jeff lays on the horn in an attempt to get her attention.
immoral_consequence: Jeff embarrasses his wife by making a racket outside her job.

norm: It's bad to focus too much on video games.
situation: Joe got his latest report card and it's filled with C's and D's.
intention: Joe wants to play less video games in order to focus on schoolwork.
moral_action: Joe works really hard all night long and actually learns things.
moral_consequence: Joe ends up getting A's and B's on his next report card.
immoral_action: Joe decides to take a break from studying and play video games for 15 minutes that turns into and hour and a half.
immoral_consequence: Joe takes time away from studying and doesn't pull up his grades.

norm: You shouldn't pig out on cookies because it's unhealthy.
situation: Brian walks into the kitchen to see that his mother has made a fresh batch of chocolate chip cookies.
intention: Brian wants to taste the cookies.
moral_action: Brian eats one of the cookies that his mother made.
moral_consequence: Brian feels good and enjoys the delicious cookie.
immoral_action: Brian eats ten of the cookies that his mother made.
immoral_consequence: Brian feels a little bit sick and gains weight from all the cookies he ate.

norm: You should be grateful when someone makes you feel better.
situation: James stayed home sick from work and his girlfriend made him chicken noodle soup.
intention: James wants to go to sleep now.
moral_action: James thanked his girlfriend for the delicious soup and said he felt soothed enough to sleep now.
moral_consequence: James' girlfriend kissed him and went to sleep on the couch, so she wouldn't disturb him.
immoral_action: James snapped at his girlfriend because the soup didn't have enough salt.
immoral_consequence: James' girlfriend got fed up and left him alone in his apartment.

norm: You should tell your friend if they're making a mistake
situation: Jim is drunk at Jack's house party and wants to go home, so he decides to drive himself.
intention: Jack wants to react to Jim's decision.
moral_action: Jack tells Jim that would be a mistake and convinces him to sleep in his guest room.
moral_consequence: Jim wakes up sober and is able to drive himself home with no issue.
immoral_action: Jack tells Jim to drive safe and wishes him farewell.
immoral_consequence: Jim is pulled over by a cop and arrested for driving under the influence.

norm: It is wrong to marry someone just for their money.
situation: Laura has been dating Bob, a wealthy CEO, and he has just proposed, but she is not in love with him.
intention: Laura wants to answer his proposal.
moral_action: Laura tells Bob that she can't marry him because she's not in love with him.
moral_consequence: Bob is unhappy with Laura's answer but thanks her for being honest with him.
immoral_action: Laura decides that she can live in a marriage without love as long as she has lots of money, and accepts Bob's proposal.
immoral_consequence: Bob can tell that Laura really didn't want to marry him, she's only marrying him because he's rich.

norm: It's wrong to think violent thoughts about others.
situation: Wayne can't stand living in the same house as Garth any longer.
intention: Wayne wants to stop living with Garth.
moral_action: Wayne tells Garth that he's going to move out and find his own house.
moral_consequence: Garth accepts Wayne's decision and lets him move out of the house.
immoral_action: Wayne tells Garth he's going to kill him if he doesn't get out of the house.
immoral_consequence: Garth files a restraining order against Wayne and moves away.

norm: You should tell your friends to stop bullying people.
situation: Samantha is a high school student with some popular friends, recently she's noticed that they have been bullying some other kids.
intention: Samantha wants to be as popular as her friends.
moral_action: Samantha stands up to her friends and tell them bullying is wrong.
moral_consequence: The rest of the school finds out she stood up to them, and she ends up being more popular and having more friends.
immoral_action: Samantha joins in with her friends in the bullying.
immoral_consequence: Once the school catches wind Samantha and her friends are punished in front of the whole school humiliating them.

norm: It's wrong to lie about your past.
situation: Jon is talking to a new love interest who wants to know more about him.
intention: Jon wants to talk about his past experiences.
moral_action: Jon shares an interesting story about his past which he is comfortable being honest about.
moral_consequence: The girl is compelled by the story and is more interested.
immoral_action: Jon exaggerates his past in order to appear in a better light.
immoral_consequence: The girl finds out the truth and is upset she was lied to.

norm: It's understandable to love one's pet.
situation: Tommy and his friends are playing with one of his gerbils when one of his friends flings the gerbil on the road and laughs.
intention: Tommy wants to appear cool to his friends.
moral_action: Tommy tells his friends to stop, picks up his gerbil and cares for him medically.
moral_consequence: The gerbil lives and ultimately Tommy's friends learn something and respect him more.
immoral_action: Tommy joins in the laughter too.
immoral_consequence: The gerbil dies and Tommy's friends ultimately respect him less later on.

norm: It is rude to harass others.
situation: Jim found out his pencil was stolen in class by a friend and is upset.
intention: Jim wants to confront his friend about stealing his pencil.
moral_action: Jim tells his friend that he is upset and asks him not to steal again.
moral_consequence: Jim's friend apologizes, and they both have a nice conversation.
immoral_action: Jim punches his friend and calls him names for stealing his pencil.
immoral_consequence: Jim's friend calls the principle on James and James is mortified.

norm: You should try to pay bills you owe.
situation: Dave got a much higher than usual electricity bill this month and can't afford to pay it.
intention: Dave wants to avoid getting in trouble with the electricity company.
moral_action: Dave borrows money from his family and makes a plan to get his finances under control.
moral_consequence: Dave maintains his electricity and puts himself in a better position to be able to pay the bills.
immoral_action: Dave moves out of his apartment and moves in with a friend, hoping the electricity company won't track him down for such a small bill.
immoral_consequence: Dave gets tracked down and is given a much higher penalty with potential legal consequences.

norm: It's not okay to let your home fall apart.
situation: Polly is at home on vacation and notices a few problems like a major leak inside and mold on the dry wall.
intention: Polly wants to use her vacation time in a fulfilling way.
moral_action: Polly rolls her sleeves up and gets to work on her ailing home because she knows the problems need attention.
moral_consequence: Polly successfully rehabilitates her home and appreciates the way she spent her vacation knowing that there is a safe roof over her head.
immoral_action: Polly takes an expensive cruise she had always wanted to and leaves her home unattended to.
immoral_consequence: Polly's home gets worse while she is away and it becomes inhabitable, and she lacks the funds to fix it.

norm: It's unseemly to interrogate others about private matters.
situation: Jim and Pam are coworkers in an office, and are talking about their lives.
intention: Jim wants to ask Pam about her interests.
moral_action: Jim asks innocuous questions like what movies she likes.
moral_consequence: Pam finds Jim friendly and they ultimately become good friends.
immoral_action: Jim asks very private questions about Pam's former boyfriends and private health.
immoral_consequence: Pam is creeped out by Jim and avoids him from then on.

norm: It's best to not keep things from your parents.
situation: John is being bullied at school.
intention: John wants the bullying to stop.
moral_action: John tells his parents about the bullying.
moral_consequence: John's parents intervene and the bullying stops.
immoral_action: John asks the bully to stop.
immoral_consequence: John continues to be bullied.

norm: It's bad to gossip about others.
situation: Anita is having drinks with her sister - they are discussing one of Anita's friends' behavior.
intention: Anita wants to look like she cares about her friend's issues.
moral_action: Anita talks about her friend's many qualities and tells her sister that she wishes the best for her friend.
moral_consequence: Anita's sister understands that Anita is is a respectful and loving friend.
immoral_action: Anita tells her sister about Anita's friend's secrets as a possible explanation for the friend's behavior.
immoral_consequence: Anita's sister realizes that Anita is not a very loyal friend.

norm: It's expected that family should help each other out.
situation: It's a hot day, and Kelli's daughter, Erica, called to tell her that her car broke down, and she is stranded until a tow truck arrives in a few hours.
intention: Kelli wants to react to her daughter's dilemma.
moral_action: Kelli tell's Erica to sit tight, and she will be right there to pick her up and to leave a note for the tow truck driver.
moral_consequence: Erica doesn't have to suffer in the heat waiting.
immoral_action: Kelli tells Erica to just wait patiently until the truck arrives.
immoral_consequence: Erica is stuck out in the heat and faints from heat exhaustion.

norm: It's wrong to be disrespectful to her friends
situation: Ally just found out her friend has been stealing jewelry from the mall.
intention: Ally wants her friend to stop stealing.
moral_action: Ally explains to her friend why she thinks stealing is wrong.
moral_consequence: Ally's friend takes her words to heart and decides to stop stealing.
immoral_action: Ally calls her friend names including a thief and a thug.
immoral_consequence: Ally's friend gets made and ends their friendship.

norm: It's discouraged from causing hardship to others.
situation: Alex can get a better job at his company if he tells his boss that his colleague made a mistake and lost a major client.
intention: Alex has to decide whether to ruin his colleague's chances for promotion.
moral_action: Alex doubles his efforts at work, improving his own performance, but he doesn't say anything about the shortcomings of his colleague.
moral_consequence: His boss recognizes his strengths and his effort, and also understands his colleague's weaknesses, so Alex gets a promotion without sacrificing his social standing at work.
immoral_action: Alex meets with his boss and tells him that it was his colleague's mistake that cost the company a large client.
immoral_consequence: His colleague is fired and none of his other colleagues trust him anymore, leaving Alex isolated at work.

norm: It is wrong to cause interference in a game.
situation: Roberts loves his favorite basketball team and attends every home game.
intention: Robert wants to be a loyal fan.
moral_action: Robert has a front row seats and always says supporting things ot the team.
moral_consequence: Robert gets to know some of the players and gets soem autographs and memorabilia.
immoral_action: Roberts sneaks out to courtside and tries to trip an opposing player.
immoral_consequence: Robert is quickly tackled by other players and secuity, arrested and given a lifetime ban.

norm: You should give gifts to others.
situation: Matt's girlfriend Mona's birthday is today.
intention: Matt wants to show his appreciation to Mona.
moral_action: Matt buys Mona a new laptop for her birthday.
moral_consequence: Mona appreciates the gift and uses it to do gig work on Mechanical Turk.
immoral_action: Matt gives Mona a birthday card with nothing in it.
immoral_consequence: Mona is upset at the lack of effort Matt put into celebrating her birthday.

norm: It is wrong to act unprofessionally with a patient.
situation: Julie is meeting with a patient who likes to joke around and not be serious.
intention: Julie wants to provide good care to her patient.
moral_action: Julie remains professional and does not make any jokes.
moral_consequence: The patient receives good care and is at no risk of being offended or worried.
immoral_action: Julie makes jokes with her patient about her diagnosis and treatment.
immoral_consequence: Julie offends her patient and makes them worry over nothing.

norm: You are expected to not disturb others during an event.
situation: Megan is in the middle of a board meeting and starts feeling a bit sick.
intention: Megan wants to go home to recover.
moral_action: Megan slips out of the room and sends an apology email to her colleagues after she leaves.
moral_consequence: Megan's colleagues understand her situation and are sympathetic.
immoral_action: Megan stands up and announces she is unwell to everyone else in the room and then leaves.
immoral_consequence: Megan develops a reputation for being rude and unprofessional at work.

norm: Treating a client in an unfriendly manner is unacceptable.
situation: Web designer, David has been working a lot of overtime hours and just received a late evening call from his client Steve.
intention: David wants to make the conversation short with Steve.
moral_action: David tells Steve he would be happy to answer his questions when he is fresh and alert in the morning and schedules a call.
moral_consequence: Steve feels that David cares about his needs and recommends him to lots of friends.
immoral_action: David yells at Steve for calling so late and quickly slams the phone down to hang up.
immoral_consequence: Steve gets annoyed at David, cancels his contract and leaves a negative review online.

norm: It's bad to take advantage of someone when they're intoxicated.
situation: Harry was in New Orleans for Marti Gras.
intention: Harry wanted to party on Bourbon Street.
moral_action: Harry finds a guy passed out on the curb and goes to check on him and make sure he is okay.
moral_consequence: His friends come out of the bar to find the man and thank Harry for helping him.
immoral_action: Harry finds a guy passed out on the curb and takes money from his wallet and his watch.
immoral_consequence: Harry gets caught in a police sting and is arrested for theft.

norm: It is rude to be violent.
situation: The girl who sat behind James in school kept flicking spitballs at the back of his head.
intention: James wants his classmate to stop bothering him.
moral_action: James raises his hand and complains to the teacher about his classmate's behavior.
moral_consequence: The teacher gives the girl detention and moves her to a desk on the opposite side of the room.
immoral_action: James turns around and hits the girl in the face with his math textbook.
immoral_consequence: James is suspended for a week and has to talk to the school counselor.

norm: It's not okay to condemn women for their sexuality.
situation: John is a conservative father to an adult daughter who works as a model.
intention: John wants to be a good parent.
moral_action: John has a hard time understanding his daughter's profession but makes it clear that as long as she is safe and happy he will always be there for her.
moral_consequence: John's daughter appreciates the sentiment and remains close and open with her father.
immoral_action: John bluntly tells his daughter that he does not believe it is moral or good for her to work in an industry that objectifies her body.
immoral_consequence: John's daughter is disappointed that her father cannot see things from her perspective and their relationship is strained.

norm: It's wrong to cheat as a student.
situation: Bill has an important test in a difficult class coming up at school.
intention: Bill wants to do well on his test.
moral_action: Bill studies hard for his test spending a lot of time and effort to learn the subjects that will be covered on it.
moral_consequence: Bill passes the test and is proud of himself for learning the material well.
immoral_action: Bill buys the answers to his upcoming test so that he will be able to finish it easily.
immoral_consequence: Bill is caught using the answers he got during the test and is suspended from school.

norm: It's always nice to surprise someone for their birthday.
situation: Sergio is waiting at his home for a friend who he invited over because it was their birthday.
intention: Sergio wants to celebrate his friend's birthday.
moral_action: Sergio reveals to his friend an elaborate set of events and activities the pair will be doing to celebrate the birthday.
moral_consequence: Sergio's friend enjoys the unexpected fun and has a happy birthday.
immoral_action: Sergio entertains is friend exactly as if it were any other day and while they have fun, it is nothing out of the ordinary.
immoral_consequence: Sergio's friend enjoys the visit but is a little let down they didn't do anything special for his birthday.

norm: It is wrong to be self depreciating.
situation: Kyle is upset that he has been gaining weight and looks in the mirror to make an assessment of how he looks.
intention: Kyle wants to form an opinion of his personal appearance.
moral_action: Kyle gives himself a pep talk in the mirror, where he verbally expresses that he needs to do a little gym work but that he is worth the effort.
moral_consequence: Kyle starts a new gym membership and a whole new program of self-care, and he feels better than he ever has before, both physically and emotionally.
immoral_action: Kyle does not feel anything good about his appearance and forms the opinion that nobody could ever be attracted to him.
immoral_consequence: Kyle loses a lot of his self-confidence in social situations and starts to avoid other people due to his lowered self-esteem.

norm: You should offer support to struggling co-workers.
situation: Merlin works in IT and sees John, a new IT hire, having trouble getting a computer to work properly.
intention: Merlin wants to give John some words of encouragement.
moral_action: Merlin stops to help John and recounts how many mistakes he made when he was new on the job.
moral_consequence: John feels like Merlin cares and connects with Merlin's experiences, becoming a friend of Merlin.
immoral_action: Merlin tells John that the struggles will make him stronger, then walks off.
immoral_consequence: John feels somewhat resentful that Merlin just walked by without offering any help and acts coldly towards Merlin.

norm: It is nice to reward people for good behavior
situation: Jim is the manager of a company overseeing many salespeople.
intention: Jim wants to give out bonuses to those with high sales volumes.
moral_action: Jim rewards only the salespeople who performed well while maintaining ethical standards.
moral_consequence: The salespersons are encouraged to both work hard while maintaining a moral standard.
immoral_action: Jim rewards high performing salespeople who clearly used underhanded methods to reach those numbers.
immoral_consequence: The salespersons are encouraged to do the wrong thing in order to get paid more.

norm: fat shaming is mean
situation: Edna is attending one of Dina's cooking courses as a student.
intention: Dina wants to let Edna know she's used too much butter in her dish.
moral_action: Dina asks Edna if she used the recipe amount of butter when preparing her dish.
moral_consequence: Edna explains that she forgot if she added butter and may have added it twice, and they both laugh at the accident.
immoral_action: Dina approaches Edna and says that she can tell by Edna's waistline that she goes overboard on butter often.
immoral_consequence: Edna is terribly offended and requests a refund for the course after leaving early in tears.

norm: It's good to tell jokes.
situation: Ted is at a party and is talking with some people he's never met.
intention: Ted wants to carry a conversation.
moral_action: Ted tells the people some jokes he heard from his favorite comedian.
moral_consequence: Ted and the new people start a conversation about the comedian.
immoral_action: Ted talks about his job pushing papers at a corporation.
immoral_consequence: The people get bored and walk away from Ted.

norm: It's encouraged to help those in need.
situation: Brock has a lot of free time in the summer between semesters.
intention: Brock wants to find something to keep him busy.
moral_action: Brock volunteers at the local homeless shelter every day and helps people who are less fortunate than him.
moral_consequence: Brock is lauded in the local news for his tireless work helping out his city's indigent population.
immoral_action: Brock buys a new video game system and stays home all the time playing on it.
immoral_consequence: Brock wastes a lot of time and accomplishes nothing with his summer break.

norm: You should always pay back people for what you owe.
situation: Rob sometimes forgets to bring his wallet along on the guys' nights out, and one of his friends will always cover his tab.
intention: Rob enjoys those nights out with his friends and wants to keep them going.
moral_action: Rob is always very careful to pay his friends back within a few days.
moral_consequence: Robs friends laugh when he forgets his wallet, and continue to cover his tab.
immoral_action: Rob has forgotten to pay his friends back many times.
immoral_consequence: Rob's friends  are tired of his behavior and won't allow him to order anything unless he shows he can pay for it.

norm: It's expected that parents be diligent in watching their children.
situation: Amy is very busy with her career so it's been hard for her spend time with her kids.
intention: Amy wants her kids to be taken care of.
moral_action: Amy spends less time at work so that she can see her kids more.
moral_consequence: Amy's kids feel safer knowing that Amy is looking after them.
immoral_action: Amy hires a nanny to look after her kids, because she's too busy.
immoral_consequence: The nanny is too busy to look after her kids so the kids are not fully taken care of.

norm: It's good to take pride in your nationality.
situation: Pedro is with his friends at a Cinco de Mayo parade in the town he lives in.
intention: Pedro wants get the attention of a girl who's watching the parade.
moral_action: Pedro approaches the girl and asks if she knows about the battle of the Puebla, explaining that his great grandfather was in the Mexican army at the time.
moral_consequence: Pedro is able to start a conversation with the girl about the history of Cinco de Mayo.
immoral_action: Pedro approaches the girl and makes a joke mocking his Mexican heritage.
immoral_consequence: The girl awkwardly smiles before saying that she needs to go.

norm: It's wrong to commit suicide.
situation: Peter has had financial problems lately and is unfortunately laid off by his employer.
intention: Peter wants to react to his unfortunate life events.
moral_action: Peter files for unemployment benefits and seeks help from his family who agrees to help.
moral_consequence: Peter feels loved and works hard on finding a new job.
immoral_action: Peter feels hopeless and kills himself.
immoral_consequence: Peter is dead and his family feels very sad and heart-broken.

norm: It's good to celebrate someone's cake day.
situation: Josh is scrolling through his facebook and gets a notification that it's his friends birthday.
intention: Josh wants to wish his friend a happy birthday.
moral_action: Josh plans a small gather of friends to do something for his friend's birthday.
moral_consequence: Josh's friend has a much better birthday because he had nothing planned for himself.
immoral_action: Josh posts a happy birthday message onto his friends facebook timeline.
immoral_consequence: Josh's friend doesn't have any plans and spends his birthday alone.

norm: It is good to be honest about your feelings.
situation: Jane is asked by her boyfriend if his drinking bothers her.
intention: Jane wants to have a strong relationship.
moral_action: Jane tells her boyfriend that his drinking bothers her, and they need to talk about it.
moral_consequence: Jane's boyfriend sees how his drinking is affecting Jane and cuts back which makes Jane happy and their relationship stronger.
immoral_action: Jane doesn't want to upset him so tell him no, his drinking doesn't bother her.
immoral_consequence: Jane becomes resentful of her boyfriend's increasing drinking and breaks up with him.

norm: It is bad to lie about things.
situation: Jeff is in a math contest and wrote the wrong answer to a question, then realizes that he was wrong before he answers.
intention: Jeff wants to give an answer.
moral_action: Jeff gives his actual answer and is eventually removed from the math contest.
moral_consequence: The best person wins the contest and gets the recognition that they deserve.
immoral_action: Jeff gives the answer that everyone else gave, ignoring his actual answer on his paper and eventually winning the contest.
immoral_consequence: The best person, who should have won, doesn't get any prize or recognition even though they were honest.

norm: It's rude to fight with other people.
situation: Joey is waiting in a long line at a grocery store, and is stuck behind a man who is taking a long time to pay.
intention: Joey wants the man to finish quickly so Joey can get checked out.
moral_action: Joey offers to help the man finish up checking out.
moral_consequence: The man appreciates Joey offering to help and wishes him a good day.
immoral_action: Joey yells at the man to hurry up, and shoves him out of the way when he continues to dawdle.
immoral_consequence: The man is very embarrassed and tells Joey he's going to contact the police.

norm: It's rude to insult the people you love.
situation: Jake's wife has gotten a new haircut which he thinks looks terrible.
intention: Jake wants to tell his wife that her new haircut isn't right for her.
moral_action: Jake shows his wife a different haircut from a magazine and says that it would really suit her.
moral_consequence: Jake's wife appreciates his interest in her and considers his haircut suggestion.
immoral_action: Jake tells his wife that she looks ugly with her new haircut.
immoral_consequence: Jake's wife's feelings are hurt, and she resents his cruelty.

norm: You shouldn't blame family members.
situation: Liam is drawing a picture in the kitchen while his wife is trying to cook dinner when she accidentally bumps into him, and he ruins the picture.
intention: Liam wants to react to being bumped.
moral_action: Liam tells his wife it's his own fault that he got bumped, he shouldn't have been in the kitchen.
moral_consequence: Liam's wife is happy that he's realized he needs to get out of the way, so she can cook.
immoral_action: Liam tells his wife that she's so clumsy and that she completely ruined his almost perfect picture.
immoral_consequence: Liam's wife is annoyed that Liam is blaming her when she's busy trying to make food for him.

norm: You should say sorry to your partner.
situation: Jack found himself cheating on his partner a week ago and is now with his girlfriend his cheated on.
intention: Jack wants to confront his girlfriend about the fact that he cheated.
moral_action: Jack tells his girlfriend that he cheated and is extremely sorry.
moral_consequence: Jack's girlfriend is accepting of Jack, not too angry, and Jack feels he has control.
immoral_action: Jack comes clean about his mistake to his girlfriend but doesn't apologize and says that it was worth it.
immoral_consequence: Jack's girlfriend flips out, begins screaming, and they both engage in argument.

norm: It is not acceptable to hurt another persons feelings.
situation: Tony's made a new friend whom he has been hanging out with a lot, and just called to see if he wants to hang out today.
intention: Tony wants to spend a few days alone.
moral_action: Tony tells his friend he needs a few days to recharge, and that they should hang out next week.
moral_consequence: Tony's friend understands and gives him the space he needs.
immoral_action: Tony responds to his friend by calling names and being very rude.
immoral_consequence: Tony's friends feelings are hurt, and he stops being his friend.

norm: You shouldn't do everything your partner tells you to do.
situation: Ben's girlfriend Janice wakes him up in the middle of the night to go get her ice cream.
intention: Ben wants to respond to Janice's request.
moral_action: Ben tells Janice he needs to sleep, and he can get ice cream in the morning.
moral_consequence: Janice will learn when to make requests to Ben.
immoral_action: Ben goes to get Janice ice cream in the middle of the night.
immoral_consequence: Janice will continue to make requests of Ben that intrude on his sleep.

norm: It's not okay to over indulge in life's pleasures.
situation: Jay just got home from work to find a new season off his favorite show was released on netflix.
intention: Jay wants to be entertained.
moral_action: Jay watches a couple episodes each day throughout the rest of the week.
moral_consequence: Jay manages to have a great time a few hours every day, while still getting enough rest.
immoral_action: Jay binge watches the whole season all throughout that evening and night.
immoral_consequence: Jay barely sleeps and is exhausted the following day when he goes to work.

norm: It's wrong to stare at people.
situation: John is a single man who likes to people-watch when he is out in public.
intention: John wants to do some shopping.
moral_action: John does his shopping and minds his own business.
moral_consequence: Everyone in the store is able to shop without issue.
immoral_action: John sees a woman shopping alone and stares at her for a while.
immoral_consequence: The woman notices John staring and calls security.

norm: People shouldn't get married when inebriated.
situation: Terry and his friend Karen are fairly drunk one night in Las Vegas, and Karen suggests they get married.
intention: Terry wants to respond to Karen's suggestion.
moral_action: Terry laughs at the suggestion and tells Karen he doesn't think it would be a great idea.
moral_consequence: They both agree that it would be silly to marry while drunk, and they go and find a diner with coffee instead.
immoral_action: Terry agrees to the marriage while in his drunken state, and they find a quick chapel to get married in.
immoral_consequence: They both regret their decision the next morning, and they have to pay a lot to get the marriage annulled.

norm: It's discouraged to overdue it with toxic chemicals.
situation: Vera, a highly anxious person, is cleaning the kitchen after her roommate invited her maskless friends over.
intention: Vera wants her kitchen to be germ free.
moral_action: Vera asks her roommate to judge the condition of the kitchen after she's finished cleaning the kitchen.
moral_consequence: Vera creates a cleaning system with her roomate.
immoral_action: Vera goes over her kitchen multiple times with very strong bleach.
immoral_consequence: Vera has a headache from inhaling the strong fumes.

norm: It's good to use environmentally sustainable sources of energy.
situation: James needs to buy a new car for his daily commute.
intention: James wants a car that will impress people.
moral_action: James buys a Tesla and installs solar panels on his house to generate the energy.
moral_consequence: James impresses the majority of people who believe that global warming is real.
immoral_action: James buys an SUV with the lowest gas mileage on the market.
immoral_consequence: James impresses people who believe that global warming is a Chinese hoax.

norm: You should help out kids who have abusive parents.
situation: Ned is a principal of a school, and he's meeting with a student, Max who tells him his parents beat on him.
intention: Ned wants to say something to Max.
moral_action: Ned tells Max that it's horrible and that he'll contact child services on his behalf and get him help.
moral_consequence: Max is relieved because he was afraid to do anything and now he will get the help he needs.
immoral_action: Ned tells Max that it's unfortunate and that he should probably tell the police what's going on.
immoral_consequence: Max is terrified to speak to authorities and is now embarrassed that he told Ned and Ned didn't really react.

norm: You should be grateful for friends that help you out.
situation: Justin is moving homes and needs help moving his furniture.
intention: Justin wants his friends to help him move.
moral_action: Justin constantly thanks his friends for their help and buys them pizza at the end of the day.
moral_consequence: Justin's friends feel glad to help, and they get the move done seamlessly.
immoral_action: Justin is rude and demanding to his friends as they help him move.
immoral_consequence: Justin's friends grow sick of his abuse and leave him to move his things alone.

norm: It's not okay to inconvenience others with your problems.
situation: Colin is at work where all the workers are busy, and he is having trouble figuring out how to do his current work assignment.
intention: Colin wants to finish his work assignment.
moral_action: Colin does the research required to navigate himself through his issues because everybody else is busy with their own work.
moral_consequence: Colin and his coworkers are all able to complete their individual assignments.
immoral_action: Despite others being busy Colin decides to supersede their work with requests for help on his work.
immoral_consequence: Colin's coworkers are annoyed by his interruptions and give him low quality help that reflects poorly in his work.

norm: You should not try to humiliate other people.
situation: Ron has a really embarrassing story about Billy.
intention: Ron wants to make his friends laugh.
moral_action: Ron decides not to tell his friends the story, and instead makes a joke.
moral_consequence: Ron's friends laugh.
immoral_action: Ron tells all of his friends about what Billy did.
immoral_consequence: Billy's emotionally hurt, and his friends think less of him.

norm: You shouldn't bury animals alive.
situation: Steve wants to find a way to earn some quick money, and he looks over at his cat.
intention: Steve wants to make a plan to earn money.
moral_action: Steve teaches his cat some cool tricks and posts the videos online.
moral_consequence: Steve makes the money from the cat videos, and he's pleased.
immoral_action: Steve buries his cat in the backyard to collect the insurance money.
immoral_consequence: Steve gets the money but his family misses the cat and will hate Steve if they find out.

norm: It is rude to sit in another persons seat.
situation: Brenda is on a plane.
intention: Brenda wants to have a window seat.
moral_action: Brenda asks someone if in a window seat if they would be willing to trade.
moral_consequence: The person agrees and the flight takes off as scheduled.
immoral_action: Brenda sits down in a window seat even though it is not her assigned seat.
immoral_consequence: The flight is held up as Brenda and the person who was assigned the seat get into an argument.

norm: It is good to appreciate family.
situation: Logan watches television when a commercial reminds him of the time his father helped him in the yard.
intention: Logan wants to interact with his family.
moral_action: Logan calls his father wanting to take him to his favorite buffet for his yard work.
moral_consequence: Logan's father enjoys eating good food at the buffet.
immoral_action: Logan texts his father demanding that he continue doing his yard.
immoral_consequence: Logan's father feels hurt and used by his son.

norm: It’s bad to only clean your arms.
situation: Phil has been working overtime and is often exhausted when he wakes up in the morning.
intention: Phil wants to save time in the morning, so he can sleep in a little.
moral_action: Phil skips the sit down breakfast and instead starts taking his breakfast to go.
moral_consequence: Phil gains some extra sleep time and feels better rested.
immoral_action: Phil decides to skip showering and instead just wipes down his arms and pits.
immoral_consequence: Phil soon starts giving off an offensive body odor.

norm: It's good to overcome the disease of alcoholism.
situation: Tim's is a frequent drinker who is under a lot of stress and finds himself drinking more every year.
intention: Tim wants to relieve his stress and choose how much to drink.
moral_action: Tim recognizes that his drinking is out of control and gets help to fix it.
moral_consequence: Tim learns other ways to cope with stress and now only drinks one or two beers on special occasions.
immoral_action: Tim does not cut back on drinking and now drinks large amounts every day.
immoral_consequence: Tim loses his job and family and has major health issues by his early 40's.

norm: Is wrong to betray your friends
situation: Hillary's friend just confided to her that they are addicted to cocaine.
intention: Hillary wants to help her friend with their addiction.
moral_action: Hillary sits and talks with her friend and offers to do anything to help her quit.
moral_consequence: Hillary's friend uses them as support system and eventually is able to quit cocaine.
immoral_action: Hillary tells his friends parents that they are addicted to cocaine.
immoral_consequence: Hillary's friend feels betrayed, stops being her friend and continues to use drugs.

norm: It's good to get to know y our spouse's feelings.
situation: Fred is confused by his wife Meg's sudden changes in mood.
intention: Fred wants to avoid disagreements with Meg.
moral_action: Fred makes sure he and Meg spend time talking and asking each other about everything and anything.
moral_consequence: Fred gains insight into what drives Meg.
immoral_action: Fred starts buying Meg expensive gifts to cheer her up.
immoral_consequence: Fred fails to get to the root of Meg's dissatisfaction.

norm: You should cook for your partner.
situation: Todd lives with his girlfriend Jane who does all the cooking for them.
intention: Todd wants to grab a sandwich for lunch but Jane doesn't want to eat out and doesn't want to cook.
moral_action: Todd goes to the store and grabs a sandwich for himself then makes a quick meal which Jane wants.
moral_consequence: Jane is grateful for the meal Todd made and is happy all day.
immoral_action: Todd goes to the restaurant anyway, picking up sandwiches to eat.
immoral_consequence: Jane didn't want the sandwich and skips lunch instead, ignoring Todd all day.

norm: Children should not swear.
situation: Josh is in the third grade and is frustrated with the way his teacher is explaining a subject.
intention: Josh wants to let his teacher know he is frustrated.
moral_action: Josh explains to his teacher that he is having a hard time and asks the teacher to explain things again.
moral_consequence: Josh's teacher is happy to help and some of the other students benefit from the subject being explained again too.
immoral_action: Josh uses unacceptable language towards his teacher in front of the rest of the class.
immoral_consequence: Josh's teacher is offended by his swearing and some of the other students are badly influenced by it.

norm: It's not okay to put kids in an awkward situation.
situation: Maria sees her daughter Dana, who fears clowns, watching the movie IT on television with her friends.
intention: Maria wants to show concern for Dana.
moral_action: Maria gently squeezes Dana's shoulder to show support before switching the television to another channel.
moral_consequence: Dana feels like Maria understands her.
immoral_action: Maria asks Dana if she's scared because of her fear of clowns.
immoral_consequence: Dana is humiliated in front of her friends.

norm: It is wrong to lie to people you consider friends.
situation: Mike and Jack are classmates talking about their fathers' occupations and Mike's dad is a janitor at the school.
intention: Mike wants to respond to the conversation.
moral_action: Mike tells Jack that his father is a janitor at the school.
moral_consequence: Jack admires and appreciates the good work of Mike's father done to their school.
immoral_action: Mike tells Jack that his father is an accountant.
immoral_consequence: Jack sees in an occasion that Mike and his father talk in the hallway and knows that Mike has told a lie.

norm: It's good to move into your first apartment.
situation: Miranda,who hates spending money, has just landed a nice full time job after college, and her parents want to move into a smaller one bedroom house.
intention: Miranda wants to live somewhere she can afford.
moral_action: Miranda searches around town for a good deal until she finds an apartment she can afford.
moral_consequence: Miranda enjoys living on her own.
immoral_action: Miranda moves with her parents into their new home choosing to sleep on the couch because she wants to save money.
immoral_consequence: Miranda has no privacy and no space for her things.

norm: It's wrong to forge signatures.
situation: There is a class trip coming up and Ted is worried that his mother won't sign his permission slip because of his poor grades.
intention: Ted wants to go on the trip.
moral_action: Ted works hard in class to bring his grades up and then asks his mother to sign his permission slip for the trip.
moral_consequence: Ted is happy that he is doing better in the class and looking forward to the trip.
immoral_action: Ted signs his mother's name on the permission slip for the trip to make sure that he can go.
immoral_consequence: His mother finds out that he signed her name, Ted is grounded and can't go on the trip.

norm: You should always keep your bets.
situation: Todd lost a bet to Peter, and Peter is having trouble getting the money out of him.
intention: Peter wants Todd to answer for his lost bet.
moral_action: Peter asks Todd concisely why he hasn't paid him yet.
moral_consequence: Todd gives Peter a satisfying answer that makes Peter happy to wait a bit.
immoral_action: Peter attacks Todd, and physically holds him down while he takes his wallet and takes the money.
immoral_consequence: Peter gets arrested after Todd files charges against him.

norm: It's wrong to abandon your loved ones.
situation: John and Jane are in a jungle fleeing from lions, John trips over while fleeing.
intention: Jane wants to leave the jungle alive.
moral_action: Jane turns around and tries to help John up to help him escape.
moral_consequence: The lions roar at them but stop chasing them, seems they just wanted to chase John and Jane away from the cubs.
