immoral_action: Jane leaves John behind and saves herself by continuing to run.
immoral_consequence: Jane escapes the jungle but John is lion food, Jane has to live with that for the rest of her life.

norm: It's wrong to call someone out in public.
situation: Portia just found out that her boyfriend has been in touch with his ex.
intention: Portia wants to confront her boyfriend.
moral_action: Portia waits until her boyfriend gets home before bringing up her problems with his actions.
moral_consequence: Portia's boyfriend is able to understand her point of view and adjusts his behavior.
immoral_action: Portia goes to her boyfriends workplace and asks him about the situation in front of his coworkers.
immoral_consequence: Portia's boyfriend responds poorly to being put on the spot at work.

norm: It is bad to do harm to others.
situation: Chad is approaching the entrance to a convenience store but its blocked by noisy teenagers who are laughing and joking around.
intention: Chad wants to enter the store.
moral_action: Chad asks the teenagers to move out of the way so that he can enter the store.
moral_consequence: The teenagers move and Chad is able to enter the store and shop without incident.
immoral_action: Chad plows through the teens, shoving them to the ground and enters the store.
immoral_consequence: Chad is kicked out of the store by the manager who witnessed his violent actions.

norm: It's good to make a career out of one's passion.
situation: Lana is in university and finds she has different interest levels for different clases.
intention: Lana wants to choose a major that will lead to a career.
moral_action: Lana chooses a major that will lead to a career she his very interested in.
moral_consequence: Lana will become excited by her career and have many achievements.
immoral_action: Lana chooses a major that will lead to a career she is mildly interested in.
immoral_consequence: Lana will become bored of her career and perform poorly.

norm: If your job is preparing food you should wear gloves.
situation: Sally works in the kitchen at a diner and is chopping chicken and vegetables for a platter.
intention: Sally wants to create a meal.
moral_action: Sally cuts the chicken wearing gloves and after she's done she changes them, so she can cut the vegetables.
moral_consequence: Sally is able to make a healthy meal that the customers love.
immoral_action: Sally holds the chicken with her bare hand and cuts with the knife in the other, and then cuts the vegetables.
immoral_consequence: Sally cross contaminates the vegetables with chicken blood that was on her hand and the customers get sick.

norm: It's good to wash your hands frequently
situation: Jared is working in the sewer as part of his job and gets very dirty.
intention: Jared wants to clean himself throughout the day.
moral_action: Jared washes his hands and face well throughout the day.
moral_consequence: Jared feels clean throughout the day and has an enjoyable day.
immoral_action: Jared only washes his face but not his hands throughout the day.
immoral_consequence: Jared comes down with a horrible sickness a week later and regrets his actions.

norm: It's wrong to deliberately incite other people on the internet.
situation: Collin notices that his friend's social media post expresses political opinions that differ from his own.
intention: Collin wants to respond to his friend's post.
moral_action: Collin comments his friend's post with a genuine question about their beliefs.
moral_consequence: Collin's friend responds to the question thoughtfully and diplomatically.
immoral_action: Collin attacks the post and everyone who agrees with his friend.
immoral_consequence: Collin's friend is aggravated and blocks him from his profile.

norm: It's bad to spend all day on the computer.
situation: Jon has the day off of work, so he is at home with his girlfriend.
intention: Jon wants to do something to occupy his free time.
moral_action: Jon puts some hard work into a side hustle of his to make use of his time.
moral_consequence: Jon's girlfriend is impressed that he's working on something on his day off.
immoral_action: Jon surfs the internet and uses social media all day on his laptop.
immoral_consequence: Jon's girlfriend starts to see him as an unmotivated person.

norm: It's wrong to drug your children without their knowledge.
situation: Tammy put her son to bed an hour ago, but he is still awake making noises.
intention: Tammy wants her son to fall asleep.
moral_action: Tammy goes in to her sons room and reads him a couple of bedtime stories.
moral_consequence: Tammy's son falls asleep in the middle of the second story.
immoral_action: Tammy serves her son a glass of juice with sleeping medication in it.
immoral_consequence: Tammy's son get's very sick, and she has to take him to the hospital.

norm: You should pay rent for the places you stay at.
situation: Ted is balancing his checkbook.
intention: Ted wants to save money.
moral_action: Ted cancels some subscription services and decides to stop eating out so much.
moral_consequence: Ted saves money and the landlord can cunt on a regular payment to afford contractors for other properties.
immoral_action: Ted decides to save money by not paying Ted's rent anymore.
immoral_consequence: Ted's landlord is unable to hire a contractor to fix a mold problem because Ted didn't pay him.

norm: It is not okay to ruin someone's wedding
situation: Ryan and Cassie are at their friend Amber's wedding as a couple.
intention: Ryan wants to propose to Cassie.
moral_action: As Ryan and Cassie leave the wedding, Ryan proposes to Cassie in their car.
moral_consequence: Cassie is overjoyed and decides to let everybody know the next day to let Amber be the star of the day.
immoral_action: During Amber's wedding vows, Ryan stands up and proposes to Cassie.
immoral_consequence: Amber is furious and asks both Ryan and Cassie to leave the event.

norm: It is wrong to be rude to people.
situation: Alan is dining at a busy restaurant.
intention: He wants to get the check.
moral_action: Alan waits patiently until he sees his server and tells the server he is in a rush.
moral_consequence: Alan gets the check in a timely fashion and gives the server a generous tip.
immoral_action: Alan is mad at how long he has been waiting and finds a manager to scream at.
immoral_consequence: The manager is so worked up because of Alan that he takes his frustration out on the waitstaff and one of them end up quitting.

norm: It's wrong not to have sympathy for your partner.
situation: Albert's girlfriend Jessica told him that she was let go from her job.
intention: Albert wants to respond to Jessica.
moral_action: Albert tells Jessica she'll find a better job.
moral_consequence: Jessica will feel enthusiastic about looking for a new job.
immoral_action: Albert tells Jessica she was let go because she was a poor performer.
immoral_consequence: Jessica will not have confidence in finding a new job.

norm: It's rude not to respect the wishes of a partner.
situation: Bob asks his wife Cindy not to go to a specific business because they ripped him off 20 years ago.
intention: Cindy wants to find a good deal on a product.
moral_action: Cindy avoids the store since the wish may be irrational, but she'd want him to listen to her if she'd done the same.
moral_consequence: Cindy settles for the second-best deal in town when buying this specific product.
immoral_action: Cindy finds that deal in the very store Bob banned her from, deciding since the request is irrational that she need not obey.
immoral_consequence: Bob finds out, and he's furious, and they get into a big argument.

norm: It is rude to ditch your previous friends.
situation: Trudy has plans to go to the movies with her friends, but a cute boy asked her to go to the movies with him the same night.
intention: Trudy wants to go to the movies.
moral_action: Trudy tells the boy she already has plans but would love to go next weekend.
moral_consequence: The boy tells Trudy that's okay with him, and they have a wonderful date and end up being boyfriend and girlfriend.
immoral_action: Trudy ditches her friends and goes to the movies with the cute boy.
immoral_consequence: The boy finds out Trudy ditched her friends and decides to not date her any more.

norm: It's hurtful not to accompany your father on an outing.
situation: James' father invited him on a fishing trip up in the mountains.
intention: James wants to spend the weekend playing video games.
moral_action: James brings with portable gaming console with him on the fishing trip.
moral_consequence: James plays games while waiting for the fish to bite his bait.
immoral_action: James tells his father that fishing is boring, and he's staying home.
immoral_consequence: James' father calls James unappreciative and says he's cutting off James' allowance.

norm: It's wrong to have an affair.
situation: Keri is on a business trip out of state from her husband and has a free evening.
intention: Keri wants have a drink and enjoy herself.
moral_action: Keri takes a few drinks out of the mini bar in her hotel room and gives her husband a call to see how he is.
moral_consequence: Keri's husband is happy to talk with her and feels good about himself that she thought of him.
immoral_action: Keri heads to a local bar for some drinks and meets a local man who she brings back to her hotel room.
immoral_consequence: Keri's infidelity is eventually discovered and it makes her husband feel humiliated and betrayed.

norm: It's wrong to stalk a person you're attracted to.
situation: Warren likes a woman who goes to the same coffee shop as him.
intention: Warren wants to find out more about the woman.
moral_action: Warren introduces himself to the woman and asks her for her name.
moral_consequence: The woman tells Warren her name, and they have a conversation.
immoral_action: Warren follows the woman in his car when she leaves the coffee shop.
immoral_consequence: The woman becomes scared and drives to a police station.

norm: It's good to protect others.
situation: James saw a tornado warning on TV, then noticed there was a kid biking by his house.
intention: James wants to stay safe from the tornado.
moral_action: "James yells out his window, ""Get inside, there's a tornado warning!""."
moral_consequence: James and the kid shelter in his basement until the tornado warning is over.
immoral_action: James immediately runs down to his cellar and tries to forget about the kid.
immoral_consequence: James frequently wonders what happened to the kid who stayed outside during the warning.

norm: It's mean to point out someone's flaws.
situation: Curt is hanging out with his friend, Art, who has a noticeable stutter.
intention: Curt wants to talk to Art.
moral_action: Curt tells Art that he'll stick up for him no matter what.
moral_consequence: Art feels supported and doesn't have to think about his stutter as much.
immoral_action: Curt tells Art that his stutter makes him sound like Porky Pig.
immoral_consequence: Art's feelings are hurt, and he comes self-conscious about his stutter.

norm: It's good to respect people for the jobs helping others.
situation: Frank has been sick for weeks with a virus and enters a hospital clinic.
intention: Frank wants to get over his virus.
moral_action: Frank asks a doctor for help and says he admires all they do for others.
moral_consequence: The doctor feels appreciated and helps Frank a lot and Frank gets better.
immoral_action: Frank tells the doctor in a raised voice he wants help right away, and he better get well fast.
immoral_consequence: The doctor resents Frank's tone and helps him less than he would otherwise and Frank stays sick.

norm: It's good to help people fix things.
situation: Candice has the weekend off, and his mother asks him to look over her slow computer.
intention: Candice wants to have fun.
moral_action: Candice invites her friends over to join her  while Candice repairs his mother's computer.
moral_consequence: Candice's mother has fun bonding with Candice and her friends.
immoral_action: Candice spends the weekend at the beach.
immoral_consequence: Candice's mother breaks her computer trying to fix it on her own.

norm: It's good to care about the loss of a parent.
situation: Sally is hanging out with her friend Jessica who started crying over  the death of mother.
intention: Sally wants to make Jessica calm down.
moral_action: Sally hugs Jessica and tells Jessica that it's natural to be sad in this situation.
moral_consequence: Jessica feels loved and trusts Sally.
immoral_action: Sally tells Jessica to calm down because her tears are making Sally uncomfortable.
immoral_consequence: Jessica is shocked at Sally's apathy and decides to not hang out with her for the rest of the week.

norm: It shows maturity to not be shallow about appearances.
situation: Matt has joined a dating site and is looking through his potential matches.
intention: Matt wants to contact the matches to get to know them better.
moral_action: Matt contacts people based on their similar interests.
moral_consequence: Matt finds a nice girl who is passionate about the same hobby as him, and they really hit it off.
immoral_action: Matt contacts only the hottest girls he's been matched up with.
immoral_consequence: Matt misses out on really nice girls because of his shallow focus.

norm: It is hurtful to joke around too much with people.
situation: Penelope likes to joke around with her friends, but sees her friend Rita is having a bad day.
intention: Penelope wants to make a joke.
moral_action: Penelope decides to joke around with someone else in the group who is in a better mood.
moral_consequence: Everyone, including Rita, laugh at Penelope's joke, and Rita feels better.
immoral_action: Penelope makes a joke about Rita's hair that would normally not be taken seriously by Rita.
immoral_consequence: Rita gets very angry and tells Penelope that she doesn't want to talk to her again.

norm: It is good to come to a consensus.
situation: John is leading a group project at work that has an important assignment.
intention: John wants to finish the project.
moral_action: John holds a group meeting and uses his leadership to get useful input from every member.
moral_consequence: The project is a wild success and the group is rewarded for their efforts.
immoral_action: John speeds up the project by making executive decisions without input from the rest of the group.
immoral_consequence: The rest of the group resents John when the project does not meet expectations.

norm: It's wrong to embarrass a friend in public.
situation: Rose is at brunch with her friends.
intention: Rose wants to let Betsy know that she has a period stain on her skirt.
moral_action: Rose pulls Betsy aside in the bathroom and offers to give her a sweater to tie around her waist.
moral_consequence: Betsy is not embarassed and is thankful to Rose.
immoral_action: Rose loudly tells Betsy that she has a blood stain on her skirt while they are sitting with their friends.
immoral_consequence: Betsy is embarassed and gets angry at Rose.

norm: It's good to try to get along with siblings.
situation: Violet has never gotten along with her big brother, but her sister Rose wants them both to be attendants at her wedding, IF they can behave.
intention: Rose wants to have a beautiful wedding, without family drama.
moral_action: Violet agrees to try to get along with her brother for one day, and things are fairly smooth.
moral_consequence: The wedding is peaceful, and Rose has both of her siblings to share the day with her.
immoral_action: Violet says she won't be in the same place as her brother for anything, and declines to participate in the wedding.
immoral_consequence: The wedding is peaceful, but Rose misses having Violet there.

norm: It's rude to sleep with someone's ex.
situation: Alex runs into Kelly, his best friend's ex-wife, and she asks him if he'd like to stop by and see her new apartment.
intention: Alex has to decide if it's a good idea to visit Kelly at home.
moral_action: Alex thanks Kelly for the invitation but tells her that he would be uncomfortable being alone with her, given his relationship with her ex-husband.
moral_consequence: Alex is relieved, after some though about the situation, that he didn't visit Kelly in her new apartment, as he is sure it would have caused problems.
immoral_action: Alex goes to Kelly's house for dinner, and they end up in a romantic encounter that night.
immoral_consequence: Alex feels very badly and doesn't know how to tell his best friend that he just spent the night with his ex-wife.

norm: You should help others when they're in danger.
situation: Brian notices his neighbor's house is on fire.
intention: Brian wants to keep the fire from spreading to his house.
moral_action: Brian drags his hose next door and starts putting out the fire at his neighbor's house.
moral_consequence: Brian's neighbors are thankful for his help in saving their home.
immoral_action: Brian carefully protects his property by spraying  any flames on his property with his hose.
immoral_consequence: Brian's neighbor's house burns down and the neighbors perish.

norm: You should be nice to your pet.
situation: Tom has gone to bed quite late and his dog is barking loudly.
intention: Tom wants to get uninterrupted sleep.
moral_action: Tom gives the dog a toy and a treat to distract him.
moral_consequence: Tom's dog is happy with the attention and treat.
immoral_action: Tom yells at his dog and tells him to shut up.
immoral_consequence: Tom's dog is scared because he seems angry.

norm: It is good to support your friends even they're sad
situation: Paul is at a party hosted by James when James begins to cry after reading a sad email.
intention: Paul wants to react to James crying.
moral_action: Paul puts his arm around James and asks him if everything is OK and what happened.
moral_consequence: James is temporarily happy that his friend cares to ask and explains what's going on.
immoral_action: Paul thinks that the party is over since the host is in tears and grabs his jacket to leave.
immoral_consequence: James is sad to see that his friend thinks the party is ruined because of him which makes him even more sad.

norm: It's bad to mislead your employer during an interview.
situation: Jack is attending a job interview with an employer.
intention: Jack wants to get the job.
moral_action: Jack honestly describes his working experiences to the employer.
moral_consequence: Jack gets hired because the employer feels that he is honest and has a high potential of being trained to be a good manager.
immoral_action: Jack tells the employer that he has substantial managerial experiences even though he was only a supervisor in his previous company.
immoral_consequence: Jack fails the management test given by the employer and is not hired.

norm: You should help out your spouse when possible.
situation: Frank is at home on the computer when Jenny arrives from the store, her arms loaded with groceries.
intention: Frank wants the groceries to be put away.
moral_action: Frank gets off of the computer and grabs some grocery bags from Jenny.
moral_consequence: The groceries get put away quickly and Jenny is relieved of a burden.
immoral_action: Frank tells Jenny to put the groceries away, as he's on the computer and is busy.
immoral_consequence: Jenny gets upset and complains that she does all of the work, staring a fight.

norm: It's cruel to kill an animal
situation: Patricia has been dealing with a groundhog that comes around her garden and eats her plants.
intention: Patricia wants to save her plants from the groundhog.
moral_action: Patricia plants some lavender around her garden to deter the groundhog.
moral_consequence: The groundhog stops coming around the garden, rendering Patricia's plants safe.
immoral_action: Patricia grabs her slingshot and shoots rocks at the groundhog.
immoral_consequence: The groundhog is killed by Patricia's shots.

norm: You should always get your chores done on time.
situation: Eddie's father told him that he needed to clean his room before leaving the house.
intention: Eddie wants to go to his friend's house.
moral_action: Eddie cleans his room and then rides his bike over to his friend's house.
moral_consequence: Eddie has a great time playing video games with his friend.
immoral_action: Eddie goes into his room and climbs out the window to sneak out to his friend's house.
immoral_consequence: Eddie is grounded when his father finds out that his room is still a mess.

norm: Refusing a proposal after dating for a while is hurtful.
situation: Mitch shows his girlfriend Amy an engagement ring and asks her to marry him after 10 years of dating.
intention: Amy wants to continue being with Mitch.
moral_action: Amy tells Mitch that she would love to marry him.
moral_consequence: Mitch jumps for joy and places the ring on Amy's finger.
immoral_action: Amy tells Mitch that she only wants them to be a couple instead of a married couple.
immoral_consequence: Mitch becomes disappointed and finally ends the relationship with Amy.

norm: You should have empathy for others who have weight issues.
situation: Abbott listens to his overweight friend Abigail discuss her problems fitting into her jeans.
intention: Abbott wants to continue the conversation.
moral_action: Abbott makes a comment about his own clothes becoming tighter and suggests that they start working out together.
moral_consequence: Abbott and Abigail walk everyday losing ten pounds four months later.
immoral_action: Abbott tells Abigail that she will never be attractive if she keeps overeating and routinely stops exercising.
immoral_consequence: Abigail becomes stressed and binge eats.

norm: It's bad to be selfish at Christmas.
situation: Clarice is a working class single mother of two children and it is Christmas day.
intention: Clarice wants to spend her money wisely.
moral_action: Clarice goes out of her way to make sure she can provide her children with the Christmas gifts the asked for.
moral_consequence: Clarice's children appreciate the gifts and have a truly memorable Christmas.
immoral_action: Clarice decides to buy herself a Christmas gift at the expense of being able to buy her kids anything.
immoral_consequence: Clarice's children have an awful holiday where they receive no presents.

norm: It is bad to lie on things.
situation: Jake is at a sleepover trying to sleep and misplaced his phone, but it is dark, and he can't seem to find the phone.
intention: Jake wants to get rest tonight.
moral_action: Jake crawls on his hands and knees searching the floor in the dark until he finally locates his phone, then goes back to sleep.
moral_consequence: Jake gets his phone and keeps it safe, avoiding the loss of several hundred dollars and his pictures that are stored there.
immoral_action: Jake searches for a minute or two, then gives up, rolls over, and goes to sleep.
immoral_consequence: Jake rolls onto his phone, eventually breaking it from the pressure of his body during the night.

norm: You shouldn't sleep in if you have a baby.
situation: Margaret is a new mom who is learning how to balance her social life with her family life.
intention: Margaret wants to go out clubbing.
moral_action: Margaret goes clubbing but comes home at a reasonable hour.
moral_consequence: Margaret is able to wake up before her baby to make a bottle and take care of her.
immoral_action: Margaret spends all night at the club before coming home late and sleeping until noon.
immoral_consequence: Margaret's baby spends hours hungry and in a soiled diaper.

norm: It's wrong to make threats.
situation: Sam lives with his father Bill, who notices that his son's room is a mess.
intention: Bill wants Sam's room to be cleaned.
moral_action: Bill kindly asks Sam if he'll clean his room and tempts him with a treat as a reward.
moral_consequence: Sam cleans his room immediately and it looks spotless.
immoral_action: Bill threatens to spank Sam if he doesn't clean his room immediately.
immoral_consequence: Sam is defiant and runs away to his friend's house in response to the threat.

norm: It's wrong to date your therapist.
situation: Bill is a married man who starts to develop romantic feelings for his therapist.
intention: Bill wants to decide what to do about his feelings.
moral_action: Bill thanks his therapist for her service and begins using a different one going forward.
moral_consequence: Bill gets over his past feelings and maintains a strong and loving relationship with his wife.
immoral_action: Bill confesses his feelings to his therapist, and they begin a secret romantic relationship.
immoral_consequence: Bill's wife eventually finds out about his affair with the therapist and divorces him.

norm: It's rude to meddle in the adult affairs of others.
situation: Sam worried about his parents since he knows a lot of scams happen to elderly folks.
intention: Sam wanted to make sure his parents' money was safe.
moral_action: Sam spoke to his parents when they had gathered for a family meal and asked if they needed any advice or assistance to guide their financial matters.
moral_consequence: Sam's parents let them know they were on top of things and there was no need to worry.
immoral_action: Sam went through his parents bank statements when he was visiting at their home.
immoral_consequence: Sam's parents were very upset with Sam for violating their privacy and looking through their statements.

norm: It's good to help out people that are elderly.
situation: Richard's new neighbors George and Martha were really old but had a kid's bike that Richard really liked.
intention: Richard wanted to ride that bike.
moral_action: Richard offered to help George and Martha with their yard work or errands.
moral_consequence: George and Martha accept Richard's offer and pay him by giving him the bike.
immoral_action: Richard broke into the shed the bike was in and rode away on it.
immoral_consequence: The police got involved and now Richard has a criminal record.

norm: You shouldn't be rude at restaurants.
situation: Lance is eating at a restaurant when his phone rings.
intention: Lance wants to answer the call.
moral_action: Lance excuses himself and takes the call outside the restaurant.
moral_consequence: The other diners are able to eat quietly.
immoral_action: Lance answers the phone and loudly begins speaking and swearing.
immoral_consequence: The other diners complain and the manager asks Lance to leave.

norm: It's good to tell your partner the truth.
situation: Kelly's been with her husband Rob for 5 years, but she had a brief affair with Rob's friend Sam and Rob finally asks her about it.
intention: Kelly wants to say something to Rob.
moral_action: Kelly tells Rob that she had an affair and apologizes and would like to seek marriage counseling.
moral_consequence: Rob is angry, but wants to save his marriage, so he agrees to counselling.
immoral_action: Kelly tells Rob the accusation is ridiculous and changes the subject.
immoral_consequence: Rob is even more suspicious and decides to break up with Kelly.

norm: It's polite to send thank you notes
situation: Zachary just had his birthday and received a generous check from his grandparents.
intention: Zachary wants to express his gratitude to his grandparents for his birthday present.
moral_action: Zachary takes some time in the evening to write his grandparents a note thanking them for their present.
moral_consequence: Zachary's grandparents are touched by his polite gesture and are proud of how well mannered he's become.
immoral_action: Zachary waits until the next time he sees his grandparents and thanks them for their gift.
immoral_consequence: Zachary's grandparents tell his parents that they should probably be teaching him to be more polite and timely with his gratitude.

norm: You shouldn't call your parents racist.
situation: Sally is watching TV news with her parents and the news mentions BLM and Sally's dad says they're misguided people.
intention: Sally wants to respond to her dad's statement about BLM.
moral_action: Sally tells her dad that they're not misguided and that he can't understand them if he's not black.
moral_consequence: Sally's father backs off from his statement and tells her that she's right and that he has a lot to learn still.
immoral_action: Sally stands up and shouts at her dad that he's a racist idiot and that she can't be around him anymore and leaves.
immoral_consequence: Sally's dad is stunned that she's accusing him of such evil just because he said one thing.

norm: It's wrong to ignore your partners request for intimacy.
situation: Colin's girlfriend Jessica is frustrated and asks Colin to have sex with her because they haven't done it in a long time as he's been working so much.
intention: Colin wants to respond to his girlfriend's request for sex.
moral_action: Colin agrees to have sex with his girlfriend before going to sleep.
moral_consequence: Colin's girlfriend is happy that her boyfriend cares about her needs and makes him breakfast the next morning.
immoral_action: Colin tells his girlfriend that he's too tired and suggests she take a cold shower instead.
immoral_consequence: Colin's girlfriend is tired of not being satisfied and calls an old boyfriend for a hookup.

norm: It's wrong to mess with people's caffeine intake.
situation: Deo is about to make coffee for his lethargic roommate and craves excitement.
intention: Deo wants to help his roommate wake up.
moral_action: Deo asks his roommate how strong he can tolerate the coffee.
moral_consequence: Deo feels like a teammember and has a decent time with the roommate.
immoral_action: Deo makes super strong coffee and doesn't tell his roommate.
immoral_consequence: His roommate wakes up but gets sick and Deo feels guilty and can't go out.

norm: It's expected to RSVP to important events.
situation: Julie receives an invitation to Sue and Joe's wedding and places the invitation and RSVP card on her desk for later.
intention: Julie wants to her friends get married.
moral_action: Julie remembers about the RSVP  but won't have time to mail it back, so she calls the bride and lets her know she will be coming.
moral_consequence: Julie goes to the wedding and has a great time and has lots of pictures to remember her friends wedding.
immoral_action: Julie forgets to send the RSVP card back but shows up to the wedding anyway.
immoral_consequence: Julie forgot to send the RSVP card back so there is no spot for her at a table, and she has to leave.

norm: Leaving events early is not good.
situation: Jake isn't really having a good time at the party his friends invited him to.
intention: Jake wants to enjoy himself more.
moral_action: Jake decides to have a few drinks to loosen up and starts chatting up other party goers.
moral_consequence: Jake's friends notice he's making a good impression on others and are happy for him.
immoral_action: Jake decides to leave the party and go home and read a book.
immoral_consequence: Jake's friends notice he left early and think that's antisocial of him.

norm: You should not be irresponsible with family finances.
situation: Joseph and his wife, Kate, are saving up for a vacation, but Joseph finds out about a classic car that's for sale.
intention: Joseph wants to buy a classic car.
moral_action: Joseph does some work on the side to save up for the classic car.
moral_consequence: Joseph and Kate get to go on their vacation, and Joseph also has the car he always wanted.
immoral_action: Joseph uses the family's vacation money to buy the car.
immoral_consequence: Joseph and Kate can't go on vacation, and Kate is very angry with him.

norm: It's good to play sports with your buddies.
situation: Tyson is home on a Saturday and gets a text from his friends inviting him to play hockey with them.
intention: Tyson wants to spend his Saturday doing something fun.
moral_action: Tyson accepts his friends' offer and goes to the hockey rink to play with his friends.
moral_consequence: Tyson's friends have a good time playing hockey with Tyson, and they invite him to a movie that night.
immoral_action: Tyson declines his friends' offer to play hockey and instead stays home and plays video games.
immoral_consequence: Tyson's friends are disappointed that Tyson didn't come to play hockey, and they stop inviting him to activities.

norm: It's rude to discuss someone else's health with strangers.
situation: Jules is a hospice nurse with many stressful patients and is out at the grocery store after work.
intention: Jules wants to buy some groceries.
moral_action: Jules picks out everything she needs and uses the self checkout lane because there is no line.
moral_consequence: Jules gets out of the store and home with her groceries a little quicker.
immoral_action: When prompted by the cashier as to how her day is going Jules vents about some of her patients and their conditions.
immoral_consequence: Jules reveals privileged and confidential patient information to the cashier which the cashier probably didn't want to hear to begin with.

norm: Family should help each other.
situation: Steve and Bob are brothers, Steve is stranded at the other end of the city, and he calls Bob.
intention: Bob wants to conclude the call with Steve.
moral_action: Bob rushes over across the city to help out Steve.
moral_consequence: Steve thanks Bob for helping him and making sure he's okay.
immoral_action: Bob brushes him off and hangs up the phone, he isn't dealing with Steve.
immoral_consequence: Steve gets mugged trying to walk all the way home across the city.

norm: You shouldn't steal things from the grocery store.
situation: Oliver is shopping at the local grocery store to pick up food for the upcoming week.
intention: Oliver wants to stay under the fifty dollar budget he set for himself.
moral_action: Oliver estimates how much his cart costs in his head and decides he'll need to forgo buying any indulgent items this week in order to make his budget.
moral_consequence: Oliver checks out and ends up under budget by two dollars, causing him to feel happy.
immoral_action: To stay under budget, Oliver hides some premium chocolate bars in his pockets while checking out.
immoral_consequence: Oliver gets caught by the checkout clerk and banned from the store, forcing him to shop at a more expensive store that is further away.

norm: It's good to offer food to your friends.
situation: John and his friends are having a movie night at John's house.
intention: John wants to get something to eat.
moral_action: John prepares a spread of snacks and shares it with his friends.
moral_consequence: Johns friend's have a great time at his house and agree to bring snacks with them to share as well for the next movie night.
immoral_action: John grabs himself some leftovers from lunch and sits down to watch the movie while eating.
immoral_consequence: John's friends all plan to go out to dinner without him after the movie but don't invite him along since he already ate.

norm: You should pay for your own mistakes.
situation: Jason accidentally breaks a vase while out shopping with his girlfriend.
intention: Jason wants to make sure the vase is paid for.
moral_action: Jason offers to pay for the vase because he's the one broke it.
moral_consequence: Jason's girlfriend respects Jason's honesty.
immoral_action: Jason guilts his girlfriend into paying for the vase by saying it was her fault he dropped it.
immoral_consequence: Jason's relationship with his girlfriend suffers.

norm: It's bad to take someone else's dog.
situation: Michelle is walking past the dog park when she noticed a dog alone tied to a tree.
intention: Michelle is lonely and wants a dog to keep her company.
moral_action: Michelle walks over to the dog and gives him some pets.
moral_consequence: The dogs owner come back and introduce themselves to Tina, they tell her where they adopted the dog, and she eventually adopts her own dog from the same place.
immoral_action: Michelle walks over to the tree, and unties the dog and tries to leave with it.
immoral_consequence: The dogs owner see's Michelle, and calls the police getting her arrested.

norm: It's wrong to not support someone who is pregnant.
situation: Emily is in carefree in her twenties and just found out her best friend is pregnant.
intention: Emily doesn't want to stop being and acting young.
moral_action: Emily stays by her best friend's side while still seeing other friends and going out.
moral_consequence: Emily is able to maintain her friendship while still living her own life.
immoral_action: Emily starts to not pick up calls or respond to texts from her best friend because her nightly plans rarely gel with a pregnant person.
immoral_consequence: Emily continues to live fast and young but loses her friendship she had.

norm: It's wrong to treat people like terrorists without reason.
situation: Dan is suspicious of his new neighbor Ahmed from Iran.
intention: Dan wants to make sure Ahmed is a normal person.
moral_action: Dan walks over to Ahmed's home and has a conversation with him.
moral_consequence: Ahmed is glad that Dan came over and becomes friends with him.
immoral_action: Dan calls the FBI to do a search on Ahmed's home.
immoral_consequence: Ahmed is mad at Dan because the FBI raids his house.

norm: It is good to sleep inside.
situation: Ty has been working all day, and he is starting to get tired.
intention: Ty wants to take a nap.
moral_action: Ty goes home and takes a nap in his own bed.
moral_consequence: Ty sleeps well and gets a good rest in his comfortable bed.
immoral_action: Ty takes a nap in the middle  of a dark ally in the middle of town.
immoral_consequence: A criminal approaches Ty and mugs him at gunpoint.

norm: It's rude to have the volume up too loud.
situation: Harry is studying in his dorm room listening to music.
intention: Harry wants to use the music to study more effectively.
moral_action: Harry decides to put headphones on to block out all sound other than the music.
moral_consequence: Harry concentrates on his work and his dorm mates continue to find him pleasant to live with.
immoral_action: Harry turns the music up loudly on his speakers to block out any other distractions.
immoral_consequence: Harry concentrates on his work effectively, but is given a warning the next day for his music volume.

norm: It is good to always put forth your best effort
situation: Andrew is starting a workout routine and has a hard time lifting even light weights.
intention: Andrew wants to finish his workout routine.
moral_action: Andrew pushes himself hard and just barely finishes the routine before collapsing.
moral_consequence: Andrew's muscles grow and the weights become easier to handle, eventually accomplishing his goals.
immoral_action: Andrew lowers the weights a bit, so he can finish his routine easily and with energy to spare.
immoral_consequence: Andrew never gets stronger because the weights are too light and don't push his body to its limits.

norm: It's good to get help with your mental issues.
situation: Brody has been feeling depressed and run down the last few days.
intention: Brody wants to take some pills.
moral_action: Brody goes to the doctor's office and gets a prescription for antidepressants.
moral_consequence: Brody starts to feel better a few days after starting to take his medicine.
immoral_action: Brody takes a handful of pills from the medicine cabinet at his mother's house.
immoral_consequence: Brody overdoses on the pills that he takes and has to go to the hospital.

norm: You shouldn't make people miss class.
situation: Johanna is friends with Katelyn who is taking a very full courseload and doesn't get much time to see Katelyn.
intention: Johanna wants to see a movie with Katelyn.
moral_action: Johanna asks Katelyn when she's free to see a movie and picks a time that suits both of them.
moral_consequence: Johanna and Katelyn both have a good time seeing the movie together.
immoral_action: Johanna invites Katelyn to a movie at a time Katelyn has class but convinces Katelyn it's not a big deal to skip class once.
immoral_consequence: Katelyn falls behind a bit in class and gets a slightly worse grade than she would have otherwise.

norm: You should not bail on planned activities.
situation: Chris and Zoe had planned to go see a movie and while talking on the phone Zoe asks Chris if they're still on for tonight.
intention: Chris wants to respond to Zoe's question.
moral_action: Chris tells Zoe that, of course, he'll come, and he's been looking forward to seeing the movie with her.
moral_consequence: Zoe is delighted that everything is still going according to plan, and she expects to have a fun night.
immoral_action: Chris tells Zoe that, actually, good thing she asked because he really doesn't want to go anymore.
immoral_consequence: Zoe is angry that Chris is cancelling plans at the last minute with no explanation and now her evening is ruined.

norm: You shouldn't cut through someone's film set.
situation: Nancy is walking through a busy Hollywood studio lot, where a director is filming in the center, looking for her actor husband Tom.
intention: Nancy wants to pick a path to take to get to the other side of the lot.
moral_action: Nancy decides to exit the studio lot and go all the way around to the other gate on the other side.
moral_consequence: The director of the movie continues to film the movie and completes his scene.
immoral_action: Nancy decides to go through the middle, the fastest way, and cut through some film sets.
immoral_consequence: The director of the movie is furious that Nancy has ruined his shot, and he has to waste money on another take.

norm: You shouldn't feel up your best friend's partner.
situation: Earnest and his best friend's girlfriend Kelsey are hanging out.
intention: Earnest wants to be affectionate.
moral_action: Earnest offers to get Kelsey water and compliments her appearance and personality.
moral_consequence: Kelsey wants to become better friends with Earnest.
immoral_action: Earnest grabs and playfully smacks Kelsey's butt.
immoral_consequence: Kelsey feels violated.

norm: It is rude to intentionally dirty up someone's food.
situation: Steve is a cook at a restaurant, and a customer just complained at him.
intention: Steve wants to get the customer back.
moral_action: Steve asks the customer to leave the restaurant because he's being hostile.
moral_consequence: The customer leaves the restaurant, upset but doesn't want to be embarrassed so keeps it to himself.
immoral_action: Steve purposely drops the customer's food on the floor in the kitchen.
immoral_consequence: The customer ends up finding the dirt in the food and leaves a bad review on Yelp.

norm: It's wrong to disrespect the people who raised you.
situation: Bill is mad that his parents have grounded him for a month for sneaking out the house.
intention: Bill wants to say something to his parents about his punishment.
moral_action: Bill apologizes and asks for a shorter punishment.
moral_consequence: Bill gets two days knocked off his punishment.
immoral_action: Bill tells his parents that they're the worst parents ever.
immoral_consequence: Bill is grounded for an extra month.

norm: You should pass on your wisdom to the younger generations.
situation: Bob's son Bill is graduating college with honors and is deciding between various job offers.
intention: Bob wants his son to find productive employment.
moral_action: Bob tells his son that he would have been happier if he had chosen a career that he loved over one with better financial benefits.
moral_consequence: Bill listens to his father's advice and pursues a less lucrative career in a field that he loves.
immoral_action: Bob never mentions his own career experience and tells his son to objectively evaluate his job offers.
immoral_consequence: Bill makes the same mistake his father did in chasing money and finds himself in a job that he hates.

norm: It's good to keep track of your possessions.
situation: John has a new set of keys for a car he bought.
intention: He wants to set them down somewhere.
moral_action: John put his keys in a copper bowl he uses specifically for his possessions.
moral_consequence: John is able to find his keys easily the next day and drives to his job interview on time.
immoral_action: John throws his keys haphazardly onto the floor of his living room.
immoral_consequence: John cannot find his keys the next day and misses an important job interview.

norm: It's kind to return someone's lost pet to them.
situation: Mark is walking down the street, when he notices a cat with a tag around its neck which shows an address and phone number.
intention: Mark wants to take the cat somewhere so it's off the street.
moral_action: Mark takes the cat to the address listed on the cat's collar and gives the cat back to the people that live there.
moral_consequence: The cat's owners are relived and delighted that their loved pet has been returned safely to them.
immoral_action: Mark decides to take the cat to his house where he feeds the cat and keeps it for himself.
immoral_consequence: The cat's owners are devastated and sad as they remain ignorant about the fate of their cat, thinking it likely died.

norm: It's rude to pretend you have a disability.
situation: Robyn is able-bodied and just arrived at the big department store to buy a few things.
intention: Robyn wants to take her time shopping.
moral_action: Robyn enjoys her time walking slowly through the store, seeing what is on sale, and smiling at other customers.
moral_consequence: Other customers enjoy seeing somebody smile and return smiles to Robyn.
immoral_action: Robyn uses one of the motorized scooters the store provides, so she can drive casually through the store.
immoral_consequence: Other customers are annoyed by Robyn who clearly does not need the assistance of the motorized scooter.

norm: You should try to be nice to family members.
situation: David's least favorite uncle is in town visiting for the weekend and asks to spend time with him.
intention: David wants to spend the weekend with his friends.
moral_action: David explains to his uncle that he really wants to go to his friends for the weekend.
moral_consequence: David's uncle offers to take him and his friends to an amusement park, and they all have a great time.
immoral_action: David tells his uncle that he doesn't like him and goes to his friends for the weekend.
immoral_consequence: Once David comes back home his parents ground him for a month for being rude.

norm: It's bad to not train your pets properly.
situation: Willie juts got a new puppy that doesn't know how to behave properly and is frequently out of control.
intention: Willie wants to train his puppy.
moral_action: Willie takes his puppy to a dog training school and gets him enrolled in a comprehensive course that lasts for a few months.
moral_consequence: Willie's puppy is trained perfectly by the experienced trainer at the school and it greatly improves its behavior around others.
immoral_action: Willie decides to train the puppy himself even though he has no prior experience with training animals or knowledge of canine behavior.
immoral_consequence: Willie's puppy is trained to a certain degree but it only obeys Willie  and often fails to respond to other people's commands.

norm: It's bad to expose your kids to drug use.
situation: Barb and her sister Janet are watching her children over the weekend together.
intention: Barb wants to smoke a joint with her sister.
moral_action: Barb goes on the back porch with Janet and the two smoke together.
moral_consequence: Barb and Janet are mellow throughout the evening and enjoy crafting with the children, creating good memories.
immoral_action: Barb lights up the joint in the living room that her children are playing in.
immoral_consequence: Barb's children experience respiratory issues from the smoke and tell their teacher that their mom smokes 'funny cigarettes'.

norm: It is wrong to keep your partner a secret.
situation: Kyle and Abby had been dating for several months, but he hadn't met her parents.
intention: Abby wants Kyle to meet her parents.
moral_action: Abby introduces Kyle to her parents and tells them that they are together.
moral_consequence: Kyle is thrilled to have finally gotten to meet Abby's family.
immoral_action: Abby introduces Kyle to her parents, but says that they are just friends.
immoral_consequence: Kyle is annoyed and tells Abby that he wants out of the relationship.

norm: You should accept someone's offer of help.
situation: August is struggling with addiction and her family is offering to take her to rehab.
intention: August wants to remain in control.
moral_action: August decides to take the offer and promises to work hard at rehab.
moral_consequence: August overcomes her addiction and is able to get her life under control.
immoral_action: August turns down the offer and heads back out to the streets on her own.
immoral_consequence: August does not overcome her addiction and it just gets worse.

norm: You shouldn't let your kids disrespect you.
situation: Dave and his wife Cindy are in the process of admonishing their son Max for his bad grades when Max curses at them.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Max cursing at him and his mother.
moral_action: Dave tells Max to apologize immediately and to respect the rules or live elsewhere.
moral_consequence: Max realizes he's been disrespectful and vows to to better and learns how to control himself.
immoral_action: Dave tells Max to relax and that he understands he's frustrated and that they'll take it easy on him.
immoral_consequence: Max starts to believe that he can get away with basically anything and becomes a deadbeat adult.

norm: It's wrong to make light of people's death.
situation: Casey has just found out that his best friend's brother has died in a car accident.
intention: Casey wants to drive his friend home.
moral_action: Casey drives carefully on the way to his friend's house and makes sure he obeys all the traffic laws.
moral_consequence: Casey's friend thanks him for the ride and asks him to visit for a while.
immoral_action: Casey drives fast down the highway and laughs when his friend starts to cry.
immoral_consequence: Casey's friend slams the door as he gets out and doesn't talk to him for a month.

norm: It is wrong to be noisy in an apartment.
situation: Roger just bought the latest album from his favorite hard rock band.
intention: Roger wants to listen to his album.
moral_action: Roger listens to his album using headphones so as not to wake the others in his building.
moral_consequence: Roger's neighbors do not hear Roger's music and sleep soundly.
immoral_action: Roger plays the album at full volume despite the fact that it is past midnight.
immoral_consequence: Roger's neighbors are disturbed by the noise and call the police.

norm: It's good to give presents to your children.
situation: Joseph tells his mother Maple that he made a B on his math test.
intention: Maple wants to reply to Joseph.
moral_action: Maple buys Joseph a new video game to encourage his good grades.
moral_consequence: Joseph is inspired to see a tutor to help him make an A.
immoral_action: Maple tells Joseph that he will do better next time.
immoral_consequence: Joseph feel bad about himself.

norm: It's not okay to betray your vows in life.
situation: Jimmy is at the bar with some friends while his wife is at home when an attractive woman asks Jimmy to come home with her.
intention: Jimmy wants to answer the woman's proposal.
moral_action: Jimmy tells the woman that he is a married man who is faithful, so he'll have to decline.
moral_consequence: Jimmy's friends are proud of him and happy to see that he's a stand up guy who loves his wife.
immoral_action: Jimmy tells the woman that he will definitely go home with her, and they can leave right now.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy's friends are disgusted how easily Jimmy betrayed his marriage and his wife and don't like him anymore.

norm: It is bad to slack.
situation: Zack is hanging out at home.
intention: Zack wants to find something to do.
moral_action: Zack organizes and pays all of his bills.
moral_consequence: Zack has power to run his AC on a hot summer day.
immoral_action: Zack spends the day watching reruns of tv shows he has already seen.
immoral_consequence: Zack forgets to pay the light bill and it's turned off by the power company.

norm: You shouldn't judge people for their looks.
situation: Amy is looking for dates on Tinder, so she asked James if she should go out with a man who is talking to her on there.
intention: James wants to give Amy his thoughts on him.
moral_action: James tells Amy that it might be a good idea to go out with him since they have a lot of shared interests.
moral_consequence: Amy feels that she has the confirmation she needed to go out with the guy.
immoral_action: James tells Amy that he wouldn't trust him since he looks ugly.
immoral_consequence: Amy is less likely to meet with the guy even though she got along with him.

norm: It's wrong to avoid someone who is looking for you.
situation: Rod has made promises to a friend who is trying to call him at the moment.
intention: Rod wants to avoid fulfilling the promises for now.
moral_action: Rod picks up the phone and explains to his friend that he is busy right not but can help him out the next day.
moral_consequence: Rod's friend is okay with the delay and thanks Rod for wanting to help out.
immoral_action: Rod doesn't answer his phone when he sees who the call is from hoping that ignoring it will just make it go away.
immoral_consequence: Rod's friend loses faith in Rod because of his avoidance tactics.

norm: It's good to learn new thing when you're a child.
situation: Barry is at the playground.
intention: Barry wants to do a project.
moral_action: Barry buys a kit that he's never tried before.
moral_consequence: Barry is challenged by the kit and feels proud when he finishes.
immoral_action: Barry buys a model kit similar to one he had before.
immoral_consequence: Barry is bored and doesn't have much fun.

norm: It's bad to flirt with everyone.
situation: Tim is recently single and signs up on a dating site.
intention: Tim wants to meet a nice girl.
moral_action: Tim waits until he meets a nice girl and flirts with her only.
moral_consequence: The nice girl thinks Tim is a wholesome man and wants to date him.
immoral_action: Tim flirts with all the girls he talks to on the dating site.
immoral_consequence: A nice girl finds out about the flirting and loses interest in Tim.

norm: It's good to go to class even when you're nervous.
situation: Falcon has an upset stomach because he fears giving a presentation for his English class.
intention: Falcon wants to feel better.
moral_action: Falcon takes medicine and gives his presentation.
moral_consequence: The entire class stands up clapping at him for his hard work.
immoral_action: Falcon stays home for the afternoon.
immoral_consequence: Falcon misses the unplanned pop quiz at the end of class.

norm: Taking something that is not yours is wrong.
situation: Sue just got invited to the movies with her friends, but she has no money.
intention: Sue wants to acquire cash.
moral_action: Sue asks her brother Brent to borrow the money and offers to pay him back with interest.
moral_consequence: Brent happily agrees because Sue and him both get a good deal.
immoral_action: Sue walks into her brother Brent's room and takes money from his piggy bank without asking him first.
immoral_consequence: Sue feels bad when Brent goes to buy the toy that he wanted he realizes the money isn't there and cries.

norm: It is nice to involve other people in activities.
situation: Larry is a father and bought decorations to set up before Christmas eve, and his family is around.
intention: Larry wants the house decorated by Christmas eve.
moral_action: Larry decides to recruit the rest of his family to help him setup decorations that day.
moral_consequence: Larry's family develops a bond over that day and Larry feels connected with his family.
immoral_action: Larry doesn't recruit the help of others and decorates for Christmas eve all on his own.
immoral_consequence: Larry's family feel left out and betrayed and confront Larry about it.

norm: You should respect someone's food choices.
situation: Olivia is a vegan who is friends with Megan, a omnivore.
intention: Olivia wants to have lunch with Megan.
moral_action: Olivia has lunch with Megan and respects her food choices the same way Megan respects hers.
moral_consequence: Olivia and Megan continue to lunch together despite their difference in food preferences.
immoral_action: Olivia gives Megan a lecture on why you shouldn't eat meat after she orders a steak salad.
immoral_consequence: Not wanting to be lectured for her food choices, Megan never has lunch with Olivia again.

norm: It's good to ask your children about their school work.
situation: Ren notices his daughter has been going out a lot lately and senses she's been neglecting schoolwork.
intention: Ren doesn't want to argue about school with his daughter.
moral_action: Ren gives his daughter money to hang out with friends but helps her set goals for school as a contingent.
moral_consequence: They have a meaningful talk and his daughter does better in school.
immoral_action: Ren ignores it and lets his daughter free.
immoral_consequence: His daughter gets poor marks in school.

norm: It's not okay to lie.
situation: Angela was applying for a job at a new company and one of the questions asked her if she had been fired from a job before, which she had.
intention: Angela wants to answer the question.
moral_action: Angela admitted that she had been fired once before and explained the situation.
moral_consequence: The company felt she was a suitable and honest candidate, and they offered her the job.
immoral_action: Angela wrote that she had never been fired from a previous job, even though this was not true.
immoral_consequence: The company discovered that she had been fired when they did a background check, and they did not offer her a job.

norm: It's bad to be too arrogant.
situation: Susan has been assigned an important and difficult project at work.
intention: Susan needs to complete a difficult project for her work.
moral_action: Susan asks for help from her coworkers.
moral_consequence: The project is completed on time and successfully.
immoral_action: Susan does not ask for help from her coworkers because she is convinced she does not need help.
immoral_consequence: Susan fails to complete the project successfully.

norm: It's nice to make food for your significant others.
situation: Jordan is very hungry at home with his family, and has some food ready to prepare for dinner.
intention: Jordan wants to make a meal around dinner time.
moral_action: Jordan decides to make six servings of food for dinner, which was enough for the whole family.
moral_consequence: Jordan has a great meal with his family, and they all thank him for the meal.
immoral_action: Jordan only makes one serving of food, just for himself, for dinner.
immoral_consequence: Jordan's family feels disappointed at Jordan and chastise him for not making extra.

norm: A tip is a nice way to show appreciation.
situation: Dan experienced good service at the diner he ate at.
intention: Dan wanted to thank the waitress.
moral_action: Dan gives more than 20% for the tip.
moral_consequence: The waitress will remember them and treat them well again.
immoral_action: Dan offers his loose change as a tip to the waitress.
immoral_consequence: The waitress will feel upset and disrespected.

norm: It's rude to not attend family events.
situation: Rocky's parent's told him they are having a big Christmas meal with the entire family.
intention: Rocky wants to respond to the invite.
moral_action: Rocky accepts the invite and shows up on time.
moral_consequence: Rocky's parents are happy to see him, and he has a great time seeing everyone.
immoral_action: Rocky says yes but decides last minute he would rather stay home.
immoral_consequence: Rocky disappoints his parents and feels guilty afterwards.

norm: It's bad to obtain things by fraudulent means.
situation: Corey is shopping at the store with his wife Emily and sees a jacket he really likes, but he's short on money.
intention: Corey wants to acquire something new.
moral_action: Corey asks Emily if he can borrow the money he needs to cover the cost of the jacket.
moral_consequence: Emily agrees, so Corey gets what he wants and pays Emily back when he gets home.
immoral_action: Corey brings the jacket to the checkout,  writes a bad check, and brings it home.
immoral_consequence: Corey's check bounces and now he is left paying additional fees.

norm: It's wrong to throw drinks on people.
situation: Lance is drinking soda near a soccer game when he sees some fans of the opposing team walking by.
intention: Lance wants to annoy the other fans.
moral_action: Lance calls out to the other fans and makes some light jokes about their team.
moral_consequence: The fans return the jokes, and both sides have a good laugh.
immoral_action: Lance chucks his drink at the opposing fans, hitting one on the side of the head.
immoral_consequence: The fan runs over and assaults Lance, starting a large fight.

norm: It is rude to miss a special celebration.
situation: It is Luke's fathers birthday and his family is holding a large celebration at Luke's house for his father.
intention: Luke wants to stay home that day instead of going out.
moral_action: Luke joins the celebration in the main celebration areas.
moral_consequence: Luke's family welcomes him and has a good time with him, appreciating his presence.
immoral_action: Luke avoids the rooms in the house that contain celebration.
immoral_consequence: Luke is seen as the black sheep in the family for not attending his Dad's birthday.

norm: You shouldn't lie on forms.
situation: Rob is applying to an engineering job, but he's concerned that his resume doesn't quite stack up with the other candidates.
intention: Rob wants to be hired for the job.
moral_action: Rob works hard to make his resume as impressive and professional as possible while still being honest and accurate.
moral_consequence: Rob is hired for the job he applied for and is ecstatic.
immoral_action: Rob inflates his credentials to make himself look better throughout his resume.
immoral_consequence: The company discovers Rob's deception and rejects his job application.

norm: It is gross to keep your feet above the table.
situation: Kyle is watching TV with his family when he feels the need to change leg position.
intention: Kyle wants to stretch his legs.
moral_action: Kyle gets up from his seat and stretches his feet by standing up.
moral_consequence: Kyle's family continue watching TV and enjoying themselves.
immoral_action: Kyle throws his legs up on the dinner table and stretches out fully.
immoral_consequence: Kyle's family are disgusted by seeing his feet where they eat and yell at him to put them down.

norm: You shouldn't live a lie.
situation: Chuck is having a conversation with his parents.
intention: Chuck wants to gain their approval.
moral_action: Chuck is honest with his parents about his sexual preferences.
moral_consequence: Chuck gains the respect of his parents for being true to himself.
immoral_action: Chuck lies and tells his parents he is straight.
immoral_consequence: Chuck is stressed out over concealing his true sexuality and commits suicide.

norm: You shouldn't pay for someone's soul.
situation: Logan is going for a walk with his girlfriend when she mentions that she'd do anything for a cupcake right now.
intention: Logan wants to make his girlfriend laugh.
moral_action: Logan tells his girlfriend that he'll buy her a cupcake if she promises to never sell her soul.
moral_consequence: Logan spends five dollars on a cupcake at a local shop and his girlfriend is happy.
immoral_action: Logan tells his girlfriend that he will buy her soul for the price of a cupcake.
immoral_consequence: Logan's girlfriend jokingly agrees and sells her soul to Logan for five dollars, which she uses to buy a cupcake at a nearby shop.

norm: It is good to be polite to service people.
situation: Anthony is on a date at a fancy restaurant.
intention: Anthony wants to receive prompt service.
moral_action: Anthony reminds the waitress that they have been waiting a while for their food and asks if any issues have arisen.
moral_consequence: Anthony's date is impressed with his composure when addressing the waiting staff’s oversight.
immoral_action: Anthony calls the waitress over and loudly berates her for the slow meal service.
immoral_consequence: Anthony's date is scared by his mistreatment of the worker and leaves the date early.

norm: It is good to not ignore pain.
situation: Marco is working on an important project at work when he notices that his tooth is starting to bother him and his gums are swelling up.
intention: Marco wants to make sure he has enough time to finish his project before the workday is over.
moral_action: Marco takes a short break to call his dentist and schedules an appointment for the same evening after work.
moral_consequence: Marco is able to prevent a dental infection just in time and is treated promptly at the dentist's office.
immoral_action: Marco decides that the pain will likely subside, and he ignores it while focusing on his work.
immoral_consequence: Marco gets a tooth infection and develops a fever, requiring emergency treatment.

norm: You shouldn't disturb other's peace and quiet.
situation: Tom was playing loud music in his apartment at night and kept Frank awake, Frank tells Tom to be quiet.
intention: Tom wants decide what to do about Frank.
moral_action: Tom starts wearing headphones so as to not bother Frank anymore.
moral_consequence: It works and now Frank can sleep peacefully in his apartment.
immoral_action: Tom continues playing the loud music  all the time.
immoral_consequence: Eventually Frank has to complain to management to get Tom thrown out.

norm: You shouldn't pour vinegar into someone's drink.
situation: Nick's friend Matt ordered a drink and then Matt went to the bathroom while they are at a restaurant together.
intention: Nick wants to play a prank on Matt.
moral_action: Nick takes Matt's drink and hides it.
moral_consequence: Matt will be able to get his drink back and not have to order another one.
immoral_action: Nick pours vinegar that is on the table into Matt's drink.
immoral_consequence: Matt will have to order a new drink and spend more money.

norm: It's good to allow children the freedom to adventure.
situation: James is sitting on the beach with his son, Adam, when Adam asks to go swimming in the ocean.
intention: James wants to protect his son.
moral_action: James tells Adam he may go swimming as long as he wears a life vest.
moral_consequence: Adamexperiences the joys of swimming while James has peace of mind over his son's safety.
immoral_action: James forbids Adam from swimming, telling him that it is too dangerous as he may drown.
immoral_consequence: Adam grows up to be very sheltered and afraid of normal life activities.

norm: It's good that people get married to people they love.
situation: Rachel, who just turned 35 years old is feeling pressure from her biological clock and considering being with her platonic friend.
intention: Rachel wants to get married soon.
moral_action: Rachel gives it some time and puts more effort into finding someone more her type.
moral_consequence: Rachel and her friend both go on to find more suitable partners to marry.
immoral_action: Rachel ends up getting married to a close friend who she doesn't have romantic feelings towards.
immoral_consequence: Rachel and her partner don't have the passion in their relationship that a marriage should have.

norm: It's wrong to make up a story.
situation: Dave comes back from vacation and sees his friend Mark who asks him what he did while on vacation.
intention: Dave wants to answer Mark's question.
moral_action: Dave tells Mark that he did a lot of swimming and tanning and that it was a low key vacation with nothing particularly exciting happening.
moral_consequence: Mark is happy to hear his friend had a relaxing time and got to spend time in the sun.
immoral_action: Dave tells Mark that he fought a great white shark while swimming and that he managed to subdue it while underwater.
immoral_consequence: Mark finds that story hard to believe and feels weird about being near Dave and wants to leave.

norm: Is good to take your time in a new relationship
situation: Jonathan has started seeing a new girlfriend that he is really attracted to.
intention: Jonathan wants to start having sex with his girl friend.
moral_action: Jonathan has a conversation with his girlfriend about sex, and they agree that they should wait until they're both comfortable.
moral_consequence: His girlfriend is appreciative of his patience and agrees to have a sexual relationship not too long afterwards.
immoral_action: Jonathan tries to pressure his girlfriend to have sex even though they haven't been together for very long.
immoral_consequence: His girlfriend feels very uncomfortable and decides to stop seeing him now before things get worse.

norm: It is good to keep track of treasured possessions.
situation: Josh is packing up to get ready to move, and comes across his dead grandfather's rare coin collection.
intention: Josh needs to finish preparing to move.
moral_action: Josh places the coin collection in it's own box, carefully labeling its contents.
moral_consequence: After moving, Josh unpacks the coin collection and places it proudly on a shelf in his bedroom.
immoral_action: Josh hurls the coin collection into a random box and finishes packing quickly.
immoral_consequence: After moving, Josh can't seem to figure out where the coin collection is and is upset at losing a memento of his grandfather.

norm: It's wrong to un-invite someone.
situation: Larry was having a party and invited Steve to his house.
intention: Larry wants to invite Marco to the party as well.
moral_action: Larry invites both Steve and Marco to go to his party.
moral_consequence: Steve has a great time hanging out with Larry and Marco at the party.
immoral_action: Larry tells Steve not to come to the party because he wants Marco to go instead.
immoral_consequence: Steve gets mad at Larry and doesn't talk to him for a month.

norm: It's good to clean up your room.
situation: Roy has had a long day at school and comes home to a messy room.
intention: Roy wants to take a nap.
moral_action: Roy decides to pick up around the room a bit then take a nap.
moral_consequence: Roy's parents see that he's cleaned up a bit and are pleased with him.
immoral_action: Roy steps over the mess and climbs into his bed.
immoral_consequence: Roy's parents notice how messy his room is and are unhappy.

norm: It's wrong to overcharge people.
situation: Kerry is working on the register at the local grocery store.
intention: Kerry wants to make enough money to save up for a new car.
moral_action: Kerry asks her manager if she can have extra hours every week.
moral_consequence: Kerry's manager lets her work more, and she is able to save the money in no time.
immoral_action: Kerry rings up some of her customers' items several times and pockets the difference in cost.
immoral_consequence: Kerry's store manager catches her, and she loses her job working at the store.

norm: It's deceitful to fake an illness
situation: Steven has a big math test coming up the next day, and he is feeling nervous and unprepared for it.
intention: Steven wants to pass his math class.
moral_action: Steven stays up late studying hard on all the math topics to prepare for the test.
moral_consequence: Steven gets an A on the test and is proud of himself.
immoral_action: Steven feigns illness the morning of the test in order that he can skip it.
immoral_consequence: Steven's mother sees through his deception and makes him go to school, where he gets a poor grade on the test.

norm: You shouldn't sleep in class.
situation: Bob is very tired during math class.
intention: Bob wants to have energy for his next class.
moral_action: Bob drinks some water and does exercises in his chair.
moral_consequence: Bob gets the blood flowing and wakes up.
immoral_action: Bob lays down his head and tries to get a nap during class.
immoral_consequence: The teacher throws chalk at Bob's head, waking him up.

norm: It's rude to read other people's messages.
situation: James' sister left her laptop logged in to Facebook while she went to the bathroom.
intention: James wants to know who his sister is dating.
moral_action: When James' sister gets back, he keeps nagging her until she eventually tells him who she's dating just to get rid of him.
moral_consequence: "James dances around the house singing the ""sitting in a tree"" song."
immoral_action: James scrolls through his sister's Facebook messages and comes across graphic sexual descriptions.
immoral_consequence: James has to vomit in the sink because his sister is using the bathroom.

norm: It is appropriate to dress modestly.
situation: Jenna is getting ready to go out with her friends tonight.
intention: Jenna wants to look good for her night out.
moral_action: Jenna chooses to wear an elegant dress which is not too revealing.
moral_consequence: Jenna and her friends enjoy their night out without being singled out by drunks.
immoral_action: Jenna chooses to wear a pretty, but very lowcut dress.
immoral_consequence: Jenna and her friends are hit on all night long by drunk, vulgar guys.

norm: You should avoid seeing people who've hurt you.
situation: Gary wants to go to the grocery store but his ex shops there too.
intention: Gary wants to obtain food from the grocery store.
moral_action: Gary decides to order his food from the store online over the internet.
moral_consequence: The store delivers the food to Gary and there's no chance he'll see his ex.
immoral_action: Gary simply goes to the store and figures that they can't possibly run into each other.
immoral_consequence: Gary runs into his ex at the grocery store, and he's shocked.

norm: You should try to help your friends.
situation: Dan's friend says they really need Dan's help to study for their English exam.
intention: Dan wants to respond to his friend.
moral_action: Dan says he'll try to help his friend study for the test as best as he can.
moral_consequence: Dan's friend does fairly well on their exam and manages to pass the class.
immoral_action: Dan says he won't help his friend with their exam because they're probably not going to pass the class regardless.
immoral_consequence: Dan's friend does poorly on the exam and fails their English class.

norm: It's bad to harass your former spouse.
situation: Jesse and Zack are recently divorced and Jesse still has Zack's photo's.
intention: Zack wants to try and get his pictures from Jesse.
moral_action: Zack sends a text message to ask for his photos, but Jesse doesn't respond, so Zack decides to wait for a response.
moral_consequence: Jesse appreciates Zack being patient, so she calls him after work and tells him she will drop off his pictures that afternoon.
immoral_action: Zack sends a text message to ask for his photos and when Jesse doesn't respond, he calls her at work.
immoral_consequence: Jesse gets in trouble with her boss which makes her angry, and she doesn't give Zack his pictures.

norm: It's expected that people will be excited about big announcements.
situation: Josh is surprised when his daughter tells him she is getting married and asks for his blessing.
intention: Josh wants to respond to his daughters request.
moral_action: Josh congratulates his daughter and offers to contribute to the wedding.
moral_consequence: Josh is able to make his daughter even happier.
immoral_action: Josh expresses his disapproval of the planned marriage.
immoral_consequence: Josh's response causes his daughter great pain.

norm: It's good to apologize when you've done something wrong.
situation: Jacob accidentally throws a ball onto his neighbor's window and breaks it.
intention: Jacob wants to react to the accident.
moral_action: Jacob tells his neighbor that he broke his window accidentally and agrees to pay for the damage.
moral_consequence: His neighbor appreciates Jacob's honesty and says that he himself will take care of the repairing cost.
immoral_action: Jacob flees the scene immediately.
immoral_consequence: His neighbor records the accident in his security camera and claims Jacob for the damage.

norm: You should warn people if someone is dangerous.
situation: Lana had been drinking at a party, and was sexually assaulted by Clark, one of the men at that party.
intention: Lana doesn't want to be around Clark ever again.
moral_action: Lana tells her friends what happened to her, they spread the word that Clark is a creep, and he's not invited to any more parties.
moral_consequence: Eventually, Clark leaves town because none of his friends will talk to him any more.
immoral_action: Lana doesn't tell anyone about the assault because she is ashamed, she stays home where she feels safe instead of going to parties.
immoral_consequence: Clark has gotten away with assault, and goes on to assault more women until someone finally turns him in.

norm: It's not neighborly to call the police on your neighbors.
situation: Tom hears loud banging and yelling from his neighbor's house.
intention: Tom wants to quiet his neighbors down and have a peaceful day.
moral_action: Tom walks to his neighbors house, knocks on the door, and asks if everything is alright inside.
moral_consequence: The neighbors appreciate the visit and the concern, and Tom improves his standing as a member of the community.
immoral_action: Tom calls the police to report that his neighbors are making too much noise.
immoral_consequence: The neighbors feel a sense of betrayal after the police come and Tom develops a strained relationship with them.

norm: You shouldn't think your son is a loser.
situation: Austin played sports growing up but his son just informed him he doesn't want to participate in sports.
intention: Austin wants explain to his son why sports might be fun if he tried.
moral_action: Austin explains the concepts of teamwork and practice to his son as good benefits of playing team sports.
moral_consequence: Austin's son appreciates the talk but explains he can learn the same skills in other group activities that he actually likes.
immoral_action: Austin explains to his son that he does not think very much of people who don't play sports and that alone is a good reason to enjoy playing in them.
immoral_consequence: Austin's son is insulted by his father's wording and explains that he isn't going to play sports no matter what he thinks.

norm: It is wrong to call yourself a loser.
situation: Janice is doing poorly in a diving competition and is preparing for her next dive.
intention: Janice wants to say something to herself before her next dive.
moral_action: Janice tells herself that she's capable of making a great dive and has done it successfuly hundreds of times before.
moral_consequence: Janice is calm and focused and has her best dive of the competition.
immoral_action: Janice tells herself that she's a loser for doing so poorly and that she's going to blow her next dive.
immoral_consequence: Janice feels very dejected, expects to do poorly, and has her worst dive of the competition.

norm: You shouldn't expect people to always like certain foods.
