situation: Andy is hosting a BBQ for his friends and family featuring the first deer he caught as the main entree.
intention: Andy wants his friends to enjoy their dinner.
moral_action: Andy makes sure to include vegetarian side dishes for his friends while preparing the meal.
moral_consequence: Andy's friends all eat at the BBQ and thank Andy for a great night.
immoral_action: Some of Andy's vegetarian friends struggle to find anything to eat at the BBQ, as Andy didn't make anything for them, and have to order their own food.
immoral_consequence: Andy's friends feel frustrated that he didn't take them into consideration when preparing the meals for the party.

norm: Playing loud games at night is rude to other people.
situation: Jack is playing Call of Duty at 3 AM while his family is sleeping.
intention: Jack wants to hear the sound effects in the game.
moral_action: Jack puts on his headphones, so he can hear everything the way he likes it.
moral_consequence: The family's sleeping is not disturbed by Jack's game.
immoral_action: Jack turns up the volume, so he can hear all the sounds loudly.
immoral_consequence: Jack wakes up the entire household and everyone is angry with him.

norm: It is responsible to look after your grandchildren.
situation: Christina is watching over her grandchildren when her dog is begging at the front door.
intention: Wanted to go take the dog for a walk.
moral_action: Christina tells her grandchildren to come with her to walk the dog.
moral_consequence: They have a lot of fun walking the dog and stop for ice cream.
immoral_action: Christina tells her grandchildren to watch cartoons while she walks the dog.
immoral_consequence: Christina's grandchildren get into her alcohol closet while she's gone and get alcohol poisoning.

norm: It is kind to include everyone when giving out gifts.
situation: It's Christmas and all the family is arriving at Grandmother's house including Mark.
intention: Mark needs to give out the gifts he's brought.
moral_action: Mark gives gifts to all his nieces and nephews.
moral_consequence: They all feel loved.
immoral_action: Mark gives his gift to Leslie, his niece but does not have gifts for the nephews.
immoral_consequence: The nephews feel bad.

norm: It's wrong to catfish people.
situation: Ali is looking at a dating website.
intention: Ali wants to meet a very hot man.
moral_action: Ali sends a message to a man complementing him on his good looks.
moral_consequence: Ali gets a date with the attractive gentleman.
immoral_action: Ali sends a picture of a famous model to a guy he finds handsome.
immoral_consequence: Ali is turned down by the man because of the fake picture that he recieved.

norm: You should always take care of your pet's health.
situation: Pascal's dog is sick and it will cost him $50 to cure it but that's his whole month's allowance.
intention: Pascal wants to make a decison.
moral_action: Pascal decides to treat the dog right away and buys the medicine.
moral_consequence: The dog makes a full recovery and Pascal is happy.
immoral_action: Pascal decides his dog will probably get better on it's own and spends the $50 on himself.
immoral_consequence: A month later the vet tells Pascal the disease progressed and it will now cost $700 to cure; the dog dies before Pascal can raise the money.

norm: You shouldn't force your partner to do you sexual favors.
situation: Ian hasn't had sex in a week, as his wife has been sick.
intention: Ian wants to stop thinking about sex.
moral_action: Ian distracts himself with work and changes his thoughts to something besides sex.
moral_consequence: Ian's wife recovers, and they restore their sexual relationship.
immoral_action: Ian forces his wife to perform sexual acts on him to get rid of the urges, even though she's sick.
immoral_consequence: Ian's wife loses respect for him, and her health suffers.

norm: It is in poor taste to be jealous.
situation: Pat notices that his girlfriend laughs at all of the jokes told by his friend, but rarely laughs at any of his jokes.
intention: Pat wants to say something to his girlfriend about his observation.
moral_action: Pat tells his girlfriend that he is glad she liked his friend, but that he wished she laughed as much at his jokes as she did at his friend’s.
moral_consequence: His girlfriend is understanding and tells him that she loves his jokes, but sometimes she just laughs more than she does at others, helping Pat to feel better.
immoral_action: Pat accuses his girlfriend of liking his friend more than she likes Pat, and furthermore he insists that she never see his friend again.
immoral_consequence: She is unable to contain her amusement and lets Pat know that he is behaving in a ridiculous way, at which point Pat feels embarrassed about his outburst.

norm: It's wrong to stiff your friend's on a bill.
situation: Sal was eating lunch with his friend Jake at a diner.
intention: Sal wants to go home.
moral_action: Sal waits until after he pays the bill to get up and leaves.
moral_consequence: Jake shakes Sal's hand and tells him that he will see him later.
immoral_action: Sal leaves the diner before the waiter brings him his bill.
immoral_consequence: Jake is upset at Sal because he has to pay for his friend's bill.

norm: It's wrong to be rude to your family.
situation: John is teaching his brother Harley how to type, but Harley keeps typing too fast and making typos.
intention: John wants to tell Harley to slow down.
moral_action: John encourages Harley while telling him that accuracy is more important than speed.
moral_consequence: Harley slows down his typing and focuses on pressing the right keys.
immoral_action: John berates Harley while telling him not to move so fast.
immoral_consequence: Harley gets mad and decides that he wants someone else to teach him typing.

norm: You should lower the price for your family members.
situation: Casey is in his art store that sells expensive sculptures when his aunt comes in.
intention: Casey wants to try to sell a sculpture to his Aunt.
moral_action: Casey offers to sell his aunt a sculpture for half price because they're related.
moral_consequence: Casey's aunt is excited about getting such a good deal and buys the sculpture.
immoral_action: Casey offers to sell his aunt a sculpture and quotes her the listed price.
immoral_consequence: Casey's aunt thinks the sculpture's price is too high and decides not to buy it.

norm: It's nice to walk someone home to ensure their safety.
situation: John is walking towards his house when he sees a small boy on the street.
intention: John wants to know about the boy.
moral_action: John learns that the boy lives near his house, so he walks the boy to his house.
moral_consequence: the boy is happy to be with his parents who are frantically searching for him.
immoral_action: John learns that the boy is lost and can't get home by himself but John walks away after scolding the boy for being careless.
immoral_consequence: the boy cries because of John's scolding.

norm: It's wrong to hate certain animals
situation: Lonnie's friend is showing her pictures of her new snake.
intention: Lonnie wants to express her opinion.
moral_action: Lonnie expresses that snakes are not for her, but is glad that her friend is happy.
moral_consequence: Lonnie's friend thanks her for being civil and feels closer to Lonnie.
immoral_action: Lonnie declares she hates snakes and berates her friend for owning one.
immoral_consequence: Lonnie's friend storms off crying and ends the friendship.

norm: It's bad to hit on a friend's wife.
situation: Thomas is out to dinner with his friend Phil and Phil's wife Susan.
intention: Thomas wants to spend more time with Susan.
moral_action: Thomas tells Phil and Susan he enjoys hanging out with them as friends, and they should more often.
moral_consequence: Susan thinks Thomas is polite and hangs out with him more.
immoral_action: Thomas waits for Phil to go to the bathroom and then tells Susan they should go on a date.
immoral_consequence: Susan tells Phil what happened when Phil gets back and Phil ends his friendship with Thomas.

norm: Children shouldn't show disrespect to their parents.
situation: Having earlier received a call from her son Johnny's school notifying her that he was caught cheating, Mary asks if anything happened at school.
intention: Johnny wants to answer his mom's question.
moral_action: Johnny takes a sigh and tells his mother that he got caught cheating.
moral_consequence: Johnny's mom shows her appreciation for his honesty and Johnny is given a much less severe punishment.
immoral_action: Johnny responds to his mother by telling her nothing special happened an that it was normal day.
immoral_consequence: Johnny is caught by his mother and is grounded by his mother for 2 weeks for lying and cheating.

norm: It's wrong to be attracted to your future sister-in-law.
situation: Jay is about to get married, but he thinks his fiance's sister is really attractive.
intention: Jay wants to figure out how to handle this situation.
moral_action: Jay decides to leave his fiance's sister alone since he's in love with his fiance.
moral_consequence: Jay gets his priorities in order and focuses on what's important.
immoral_action: Jay decides to secretly have an affair with his fiance's sister.
immoral_consequence: Jay could ruin his relationship with his fiance if she ever finds out.

norm: It's good to tell customers to enjoy their food.
situation: Jordan is working at a cafe and waiting on several tables during his shift.
intention: Jordan wants to get food to all his tables.
moral_action: Jordon places the diner's order in front of them and looks them in eye and tells he hopes they like their dishes.
moral_consequence: Jordan gets a big tip from the customers when they finish their meal.
immoral_action: Jordon drops an order off at a table without saying a word and rushes back to the kitchen.
immoral_consequence: Jordan doesn't get tip because he didn't interact with his customers.

norm: It's not right to restrict a person's vote.
situation: Donald, a president of a once great country, is dealing with daily protests against his presidency from visible minorities.
intention: Donald wants to punish the visible minorities for exercising their constitutional rights.
moral_action: Donald decides to send out the riot police to spray the protesters with hefty doses of military grade tear gas.
moral_consequence: Donald temporarily eases the protests and is able to walk to a nearby church to hold a bible up to a camera.
immoral_action: Donald decides to ban mail-in balloting and institutes onerous ID checks making it harder for minorities to vote.
immoral_consequence: Donald ends up galvanizing most of the country against him and loses the presidency in the next election.

norm: It's rude to fart with other people in the room.
situation: Colin ate a heavy meal for lunch and his stomach is bothering him.
intention: Colin wants to relieve the pressure in his belly.
moral_action: Colin raises his hand and excuses himself to go to the bathroom.
moral_consequence: Colin finally is able to relieve himself and feels better.
immoral_action: Colin farts really hard in the classroom to let out all the gas.
immoral_consequence: All of Colin's classmates start to call him names and mock him.

norm: You shouldn't leave your dog at home.
situation: Rover was planning to walk around his neighborhood on Sunday while his dog Max lie in the corner.
intention: Rover wants to go on the planned walk.
moral_action: Rover takes Max on the walk with him around the nieghborhood.
moral_consequence: Max and Rover both enjoy the walk together and relax.
immoral_action: Rover takes the walk by himself and leaves Max at home.
immoral_consequence: When Rover gets home, Max has torn up the couch.

norm: You shouldn't push someone to eat something they're allergic to.
situation: Gerald is planning a birthday party for his son.
intention: Gerald wants his son to have a delicious cake.
moral_action: Gerald bakes a lemon cake which is not as good as his chocolate walnut cake.
moral_consequence: Gerald's son and the rest of the partygoers are all able to enjoy the cake.
immoral_action: Gerald bakes his famous chocolate walnut cake even though his son is allergic to walnuts.
immoral_consequence: Gerald's son has an allergic reaction and has to go to the hospital.

norm: It's wrong to rig a competition.
situation: Bill is running for class president against two other classmates.
intention: Bill wants to become class president.
moral_action: Bill campaigns and gives some great speeches on how to improve the school.
moral_consequence: Bill is elected fair and square, and becomes class president.
immoral_action: Bill secretly stuffs the ballot box with tons of votes for himself.
immoral_consequence: The scheme is detected, and Bill is forbidden from ever running again.

norm: It's good to care about your parent's mental health.
situation: Sam's mother is very stressed and is planning dinner for her children, after which she'll go to an important business dinner herself.
intention: Sam wants to eat something other than what her mother is planning.
moral_action: Sam tells her mother that she'll prepare dinner for everyone, including her own preferred meal, so that she can focus on the business dinner.
moral_consequence: Sam's mother relaxes, gets to the business dinner on time, and represents herself and the company well.
immoral_action: Sam asks that her mother make a special dinner for her in addition to what she's planning for the other children.
immoral_consequence: Sam's mother is overwhelmed by the demands placed on her, breaks down, and misses the important business dinner.

norm: It's polite to offer to cook someone dinner
situation: Bob's mom works late and just got home, completely exhausted, but Bob hasn't eaten yet.
intention: Bob wants to eat food.
moral_action: Bob tells his mom that he'll make something simple for dinner, so she doesn't have to, then gets to work.
moral_consequence: Bob's mom gets extra time to rest and enjoys the dinner that Bob makes for her.
immoral_action: Bob comes up to his mom and asks her when they will have dinner, pointing to his stomach.
immoral_consequence: Bob's mom doesn't get rest and wears herself out further cooking dinner for Bob.

norm: Violence is wrong.
situation: Wayne is walking home from school when he is accosted by a bully in a park outside of school property.
intention: Wayne wants to escape a beating from the bully.
moral_action: Wayne turns and runs as fast as he can away from the bully.
moral_consequence: Wayne outruns the bully and watches out for him in the future.
immoral_action: Wayne grabs a stick and assaults the bully before he can do Wayne harm.
immoral_consequence: The bully reports Wayne to the police, who arrest him.

norm: It's rude to flaunt your money.
situation: Danika is a very successful businesswoman but her brother has had a hard time holding a minimum wage job.
intention: Danika wants to have dinner with her brother.
moral_action: Danika meets her brother at a diner in town and talks about fun stories from their childhood.
moral_consequence: Danika's brother is happy that he had a nice meal with his sister.
immoral_action: Danika meets her brother at the most expensive restaurant in town and talks about how she has so much money she could eat there daily.
immoral_consequence: Danika's brother feels sad that he can't afford to go to the restaurant at all.

norm: It is wrong to text and drive.
situation: Sally is on her way to a job interview, and she gets stuck in traffic.
intention: Sally wants to notify the interviewer that she will be late.
moral_action: Sally uses her voice assistant to dial the interviewer hands free while driving in the traffic.
moral_consequence: Sally drives safely and does not endanger the other drivers.
immoral_action: Sally texts the interviewer while she is driving in the traffic.
immoral_consequence: Sally almost causes another accident because she is not looking at the road.

norm: It's good to move on after a breakup.
situation: Josh's girlfriend Shannon just broke up with him, and he is devastated.
intention: Josh needs something to occupy his attention.
moral_action: Josh spends time signing up and creating profiles on dating sites.
moral_consequence: Shannon appreciates that Josh was able to handle the breakup so maturely.
immoral_action: Josh spends his time following Shannon around, seeing if she's dating someone else now.
immoral_consequence: Shannon is creeped out that Josh is stalking her and gets a restraining order.

norm: You shouldn't brag to others.
situation: Tanner is a player on a team sport and just made a big play.
intention: Tanner wants to celebrate the play with his teammates.
moral_action: Tanner thanks all his teammates for their parts in the play that he was able to make and tries to get them to do high fives.
moral_consequence: Tanner's teammates are excited about the play and appreciate Tanner being humble.
immoral_action: Tanner describes to his teammates how it was him and him alone that pulled off the big play and tries to get them to do high fives.
immoral_consequence: Tanner's teammates are annoyed by his boasting and wish he was a better teammate.

norm: It's unacceptable to judge others.
situation: Dan is attending a festive dinner with his Indian friend’s family.
intention: Dan wants to contribute to the dinner conversation.
moral_action: Dan participates in the family’s customs and savors the food.
moral_consequence: The family members are delighted to share their customs with Dan and invite him to future events.
immoral_action: Dan criticizes the family’s habits during the dinner and makes fun of their personal hygiene.
immoral_consequence: The family members take offense and ask Dan to leave their home.

norm: It's not necessary to always invite all your friends
situation: Jim has moved into a small apartment.
intention: Jim wants to have a house warming party.
moral_action: Jim invites a handful of his closest friends.
moral_consequence: The guests enjoy their time at the party.
immoral_action: Jim invites every person he considers a friend from work, hobbies, and childhood.
immoral_consequence: Too many people attend the party and the guests can't move around.

norm: You shouldn't fire someone after they get surgery.
situation: Kevin is a manager at work, and his employee Zach just had his pancreas removed, so Zach's work is not getting done.
intention: Kevin wants Zach's work to get done.
moral_action: Kevin hires temporary help to handle Zach's workload until he recovers.
moral_consequence: Zach returns to work and does an excellent job, as before.
immoral_action: Kevin fires Zach and hires a new employee to take his place.
immoral_consequence: The new employee lacks Zach's experience and doesn't fit the position.

norm: You can't tell your partner what to do.
situation: Addy is not comfortable with her partner hanging out with a female friend of his.
intention: Addy wants to make sure nothing is going on with her partner and the girl.
moral_action: Addy sits down and talks with her partner about how she feels.
moral_consequence: Addy's partner is more receptive and tries to conform to make her comfortable.
immoral_action: Addy gives her partner an ultimatum not to spend time with the friend.
immoral_consequence: Addy's partner grows apart from her due to how she is behaving.

norm: It's expected that you apologize when you hurt others.
situation: Kari is fighting with her partner and ending up saying some hurtful things to him.
intention: Kari wants to move past the argument.
moral_action: Kari approaches her partner and takes back the things she said about him.
moral_consequence: Kari's partner accepts her apology, and they are able to move on together.
immoral_action: Kari lets some time go by and figures that they can just forget about it.
immoral_consequence: Kari's partner remains hurt and secretly hangs onto the words that she said.

norm: It's bad to break a toy belonging to a child.
situation: Chad calls his son to dinner, but Chad's son is playing with an action figure.
intention: Chad wants to stop his son from playing with the action figure.
moral_action: Chad takes the action figure and puts it in a drawer for storage.
moral_consequence: Chad's son will be able to play with the action figure again after dinner.
immoral_action: Chad snaps the action figure into pieces so it cannot be played with anymore.
immoral_consequence: Chad's son will be unhappy and angry about the action figure being permanently destroyed.

norm: It’s is rude to interrupt anyone private time
situation: Charlene's niece starts crying while she is babysitting.
intention: Charlene wants to find a way to calm her niece down.
moral_action: Charlene soothes her niece as she looks up ways to calm her down.
moral_consequence: Charlene's niece calms down eventually and her parents have a restful night.
immoral_action: Charlene calls her brother to ask what to do and interrupts his date night with his wife.
immoral_consequence: Charlene's brother is irritated because his night is cut short.

norm: Offending a co-worker is rude.
situation: Robert's coworker provided Robert with erroneous data so Robert goes to see him to make sure it doesn't happen again.
intention: Robert wants to speak with his coworker.
moral_action: Robert notifies his coworker about the erroneous data and offers legitimate advice to prevent the issue from happening again.
moral_consequence: Robert's coworker thanks Robert for informing him about the problem and strives to resolve the issue.
immoral_action: Robert aggressively talks down to his coworker and characterizes his work as sloppy.
immoral_consequence: Robert's coworker feels an intense dislike of Robert and avoids him whenever possible.

norm: It's wrong to take advantage of people's kindness and money.
situation: Jack's friend, Dave, is very generous and always helps people with money need.
intention: Jack wants to borrow money from Dave.
moral_action: Jack's mother has an accident and needs money for treatment, so he asks Dave for help.
moral_consequence: Dave immediately lends some money to Jack to deal with the emergency.
immoral_action: Jack asks Dave to lend him money for buying things that he cannot afford.
immoral_consequence: Dave feels offended by Jack's spending habit and refuses to lend him any money again.

norm: It is good to spend time with your friends.
situation: John has a good group of friends but is also suffering from anxiety and panic attacks.
intention: John wants to avoid situations where his anxiety is triggered.
moral_action: John explains his situation to his friends and still tries to do less crowded more low key activites with them.
moral_consequence: John keeps the friendships going and is able to overcome the anxiety more easily.
immoral_action: John isolates himself refusing activities with friends and staying home all of the time.
immoral_consequence: His friends notice that he never wants to come and stop inviting him to things.

norm: You should be tolerant of other's mistakes.
situation: Andy is mentoring Susan as a scientist, and Susan has messed up an equation.
intention: Andy wants to correct Susan's mistake.
moral_action: Andy points out Susan's mistake and tells her it's no big deal and shows her how to fix it.
moral_consequence: Susan learns from her mistake and becomes a better student.
immoral_action: Andy tells Susan he's never seen such a basic mistake done before, and that it's embarrassing.
immoral_consequence: Susan loses confidence in her abilities and ends up quitting the program.

norm: You shouldn't laugh at your coworkers.
situation: Joey is working construction with his coworker who keeps making mistakes.
intention: Joey wants to enjoy his time with his coworker.
moral_action: Joey shows his coworker how to correct their mistakes so that the both of them can work more smoothly and have more break time to enjoy.
moral_consequence: Joey's coworker appreciates the tips and feels more confident about their own work going forward.
immoral_action: At the expensive of his coworker's mistakes Joey is entertained by the coworker chuckling at every misstep.
immoral_consequence: Joey's coworker get fuming anger at consistently being laughed at.

norm: You shouldn't take away peoples home.
situation: One of Bartholomew's renters Sarah has not paid rent in two months.
intention: Bartholomew wants to get paid.
moral_action: Bartholomew asks Sarah to do some maintenance work in exchange for reduced rent.
moral_consequence: Sarah is able to add the maintenance work onto her resume which leads to her finding a better job.
immoral_action: Bartholomew seizes half of Sarah's paycheck and kicks them out of the apartment complex.
immoral_consequence: Sarah is homeless for the next couple of months.

norm: You shouldn't just throw out a good relationship.
situation: Ted's brother Tad has a gambling addiction and owes the mafia $2,000 he can't repay.
intention: Ted wants to give away some money.
moral_action: Ted gives Tad $2,000 to pay off his gambling debt.
moral_consequence: Tad repays his gambling debt and joins Gamblers Anonymous to get with his gambling addiction.
immoral_action: Ted gives $2,000 to a local charity that provides meals for the elderly.
immoral_consequence: Tad has his legs broken by the mafia when he doesn't repay his gambling debt.

norm: You shouldn't kiss people that don't want to be kissed.
situation: Donny is a politician holding a rally where a young girl has just finished giving a speech.
intention: Donny wants to congratulate the young girl.
moral_action: Donny shakes the young girl's hand and tells her it was a great speech.
moral_consequence: Donny receives tons of applause and good feedback from the media for his professional behavior.
immoral_action: Donny tries to kiss the young girl, who is clearly uncomfortable by the gesture.
immoral_consequence: Donny feels humiliated when a video of the awkward event goes viral on the Internet.

norm: It's good to auto-withdraw into your savings to save time.
situation: Finn is having some mechanical problems with his car which is very old.
intention: Finn wants to save up to buy a new car.
moral_action: Finn sets up his account to withdraw savings at an interval.
moral_consequence: Finn has a bit more time to do other things.
immoral_action: Finn deposits money into his savings account every week by atm.
immoral_consequence: Finn spends extra time visiting the bank more often.

norm: It's good to be kind to animals.
situation: Sue's dog has been barking for hours, to the point where it has become a public nuisance.
intention: Sue wants to get her dog to stop barking.
moral_action: Sue decides to take her dog outside for a walk, while the dog calms down and stops barking.
moral_consequence: Sue's dog is happy to go for a walk and is no longer agitated at all.
immoral_action: Sue screams at the dog to get it to stop barking, wildly flailing her arms until it stops barking.
immoral_consequence: Sue's dog becomes extremely frightened and hides in a corner.

norm: It's good to vote in elections.
situation: Charlie feels like he has ideas that could really change the world.
intention: Charlie wants to influence politics.
moral_action: Charlie joins a campaign he believes in and helps shuttle people to vote with him on election day.
moral_consequence: The increased voter turnout helps Charlie's favorite candidate win the election.
immoral_action: Charlie thinks that its a waste of time to vote, so he spends election day spreading information about a radical candidate.
immoral_consequence: More people are drawn to the radical candidate causing a worse candidate for Charlie's cause to be elected.

norm: It's bad to date someone that causes you pain.
situation: Julie's boyfriend is verbally abusive and her sister urges her to leave him.
intention: Julie wants to respond to her sisters suggestion.
moral_action: Julie listens to her sister and ends her relationship.
moral_consequence: Julie is free to pursue a healthier relationship.
immoral_action: Julie decides to ignore her sister and give her boyfriend another chance.
immoral_consequence: Julie's self-esteem continues to degrade as his abuse continues.

norm: It's good to take responsibly when you're young.
situation: Sam accidentally breaks a vase and his mother asks him what happened.
intention: Sam wants to respond to his mother's question.
moral_action: Sam tells his mother that he broke the vase and apologizes.
moral_consequence: Sams mother forgives him and Sam learns his lesson to be more careful in the future.
immoral_action: Sam tells his mother that the cat knocked the vase over.
immoral_consequence: Sam's mother later finds out the truth and grounds him for lying to her.

norm: It's not nice to hope that someone dies.
situation: Kendra is on the phone with Mike, and they're talking about the money Mike recently stole from her.
intention: Kendra wants to tell Mike how she feels.
moral_action: Kendra tells Mike that she's really angry with him and that she will never talk to him again.
moral_consequence: Mike understands why he hurt Kendra and vows to do better from here on out.
immoral_action: Kendra tells Mike that she's angry with him and that she truly wishes he gets killed soon.
immoral_consequence: Mike is sad to hear that Kendra is wishing death upon him and feels low about his worth.

norm: It's wrong to disobey your parents.
situation: Bailey's parents ask her to watch her little brother, but her friends want her to explore a haunted house with them.
intention: Bailey wants to see the haunted house.
moral_action: Bailey asks her friends to live stream their adventures in the haunted house.
moral_consequence: Bailey and her little brother bond over watching her friends.
immoral_action: Bailey leaves her brother at home to hang out with her friends.
immoral_consequence: Bailey gets in trouble when her little brother hurts himself while playing with sharp objects.

norm: It's wrong to want your family to move out.
situation: Gary's mom moved in with him and his wife and has stayed for longer than planned, and her habits are grating on him.
intention: Gary wants to stop being annoyed with his mother.
moral_action: Gary tries to compromise with his mom and get her to change her habits if she wants to continue to live with them.
moral_consequence: Gary's mom is unhappy that she is upsetting them, but understands, and they are able to work things out.
immoral_action: Gary gets into a big fight with him mom and demands that she move out immediately.
immoral_consequence: Gary's mom is insulted and leaves, and it fractures their relationship for a while.

norm: It's rude to use things that aren't yours without asking.
situation: Liz has been washing her hands a lot at work to avoid getting sick and now her hands are really dry.
intention: Liz wants to moisturize her dry hands.
moral_action: Liz sees that her coworker has lotion, so she asks her coworker if she can use some to moisturize her hands.
moral_consequence: Her coworker tells her that she can and hands her the lotion.
immoral_action: Liz notices that her coworker has lotion, and she uses some to moisturize her dry hands.
immoral_consequence: Her coworker sees her use the lotion and tells her that she could have at least asked her.

norm: It's rude to date two people at the same time.
situation: Brittney has been asked out next week by Todd and then her new neighbor Henry asks her out too.
intention: Brittney wants to go on a date.
moral_action: Brittney turns down Henry and only goes out with Todd since her asked her first.
moral_consequence: Brittney has a nice date with Todd, and he asks her out again.
immoral_action: Brittney makes a date with Todd for Friday night and a date with Henry for Saturday night.
immoral_consequence: Todd happens to see Brittney on her date with Henry, and he awkwardly asks her what's going on.

norm: It's important to practice reading when you struggle with it.
situation: Mina is in school and reads at a slower pace compared to other students.
intention: Mina wants to address her reading speed.
moral_action: Mina spends her free time trying to increase her reading speed.
moral_consequence: Mina becomes faster at reading.
immoral_action: Mina thinks she is just a slow reader and should concentrate on other subjects.
immoral_consequence: Mina will not become faster at reading.

norm: You should remember your obligations to your friends.
situation: Rob was working on an important project and his boss wanted him to work late but his friend had asked him to feed his cat at 7 pm.
intention: Rob wanted to impress his new boss and take on the extra work.
moral_action: Rob tells his boss that he can finish the work that night, but asks if he can do it from home as he has to tend to his friend's cat.
moral_consequence: Rob's friend is very happy his cat was taken care of.
immoral_action: Rob settles in at his desk and works many hours past 5 pm with his boss and never feeds his friend's cat.
immoral_consequence: Rob's friend is very disappointed when he comes home to a hungry cat.

norm: You shouldn't damage the environment.
situation: Jim is out sailing his yacht on the ocean and is drinking a six pack of soda he just opened.
intention: Jim wants to dispose of the plastic that holds the six-pack together.
moral_action: Jim disposes of the plastic trash in the proper trash receptacle.
moral_consequence: Jim watches the ocean waves contentedly as he sips his soda.
immoral_action: Jim hurls the plastic trash overboard and into the ocean.
immoral_consequence: Jim watches horrified as a seagull lands on the ocean surface and becomes ensnared in the plastic and drowns.

norm: It's wrong to ignore someone who is hungry.
situation: Jim is eating a big sandwich for lunch when he sees a beggar who looks like he hasn't eaten in a while stare at his food.
intention: Jim wants to finish his lunch.
moral_action: Alex buys the beggar a sandwich then finishes up his own sandwich.
moral_consequence: The beggar feels much better after eating the sandwich and his day is improved.
immoral_action: Jim pretends he doesn't see the beggar and eats his lunch.
immoral_consequence: The beggar goes hungry that day and is very unhappy.

norm: It's polite to split the cost of things.
situation: John and his friend take a taxi together and his friend asks John to pay half the fare.
intention: John wants to reply to his friend about the taxi fare.
moral_action: John says he'll pay half the cost of the taxi ride and his friend pays the rest.
moral_consequence: John's friend thinks that each person paying half the cost is fair and thinks John is being reasonable.
immoral_action: John says his friend should pay the whole fare because it was their idea to take a taxi, so they reluctantly do so.
immoral_consequence: John's friend thinks John isn't fair for not paying half the cost of the taxi that he used.

norm: It is expected to help out your parents.
situation: John's father asks John to mow the lawn as he's experiencing back pain.
intention: John wants to respond to his father's request.
moral_action: John tells his father that he'll do it right away.
moral_consequence: John's father is relieved that his lawn will be taken care of while he rests.
immoral_action: John tells his father that he cannot mow the lawn as he himself is also nursing a recent injury.
immoral_consequence: John's father is stressed out because of the uncertainty of who will help him mow the lawn.

norm: It's good to be a responsible pet owner.
situation: Marsha is watching over her sick dog fuzzy when her friend invites her to a movie.
intention: Marsha wants to hang out with her friend.
moral_action: Marsha invites her friend over to her house.
moral_consequence: The presence of another person distracts Fuzzy from their sickness for a little while.
immoral_action: Marsha locks her dog inside their kennel before meeting up with her friend.
immoral_consequence: Fuzzy's condition worsens.

norm: It's bad to serve unhealthy food.
situation: Carol's husband has heart disease and wants to only eat low fat meals to improve his health.
intention: Carol wants to make dinner.
moral_action: Carol makes grilled salmon and vegetables.
moral_consequence: Carol's husband appreciates that Carol is trying to help him get healthier.
immoral_action: Carol makes burgers stuffed with cheese and wrapped in bacon.
immoral_consequence: Carol's husband feels that Carol doesn't care about his health.

norm: People should never intentionally expose another person to a disease.
situation: Mary works in a grocery store.
intention: Mary wants to interact with customers.
moral_action: Mary wears a mask while at her register and makes small talk with her customers.
moral_consequence: Mary protects her customers while she has an asymptomatic infection.
immoral_action: Mary doesn't wear a mask or gloves while talking to customers at her register.
immoral_consequence: A customer catches the coronavirus from her and infects their family.

norm: It is important to not ignore responsibilities for games.
situation: Marc is playing video games one night when he realizes a group of friends is supposed to come over to his house in thirty minutes.
intention: Marc wants finish the video game he's been playing.
moral_action: Marc pauses his game and cleans his house to prepare for his guests, he then resumes and plays while his guests watch.
moral_consequence: Marc's guests are slightly bored, but they like his place and enjoy the opportunity to hang out together.
immoral_action: Marc continues playing his video game up until the moment his guests arrive, letting them see his messy house and kitchen full of dirt dishes.
immoral_consequence: Marc's guests are grossed out and decide to leave early.

norm: It's good to pay for your own things.
situation: John is out at a restaurant having dinner and drinks with his friend Ron when the waiter brings the bill.
intention: John wants the bill to be paid.
moral_action: John opens his wallet and pays for his half of the food bill.
moral_consequence: John and Ron enjoy their evening out and maintain a strong relationship.
immoral_action: John says he forgot his wallet and insists that Ron pay for the entire bill.
immoral_consequence: Ron feels irritated and upset with John's selfish behavior and it damages their relationship.

norm: You shouldn't let people get away with DUIs.
situation: George, a police officer, just caught his neighbor driving under the influence; he feels bad because he knows his neighbor needs his car for his job.
intention: George wants to help his neighbor.
moral_action: George decides to impound his neighbor's car, but tells him he will give him a ride to work every morning.
moral_consequence: George's neighbor goes home safely, without hurting anyone.
immoral_action: George decides to ignore his neighbor's DUI violation and give him a chance.
immoral_consequence: George's neighbor keeps driving home and ends up hitting a pedestrian.

norm: It is good to reject alcohol if you are 17.
situation: Brian has just turned seventeen and his friend is offering him a bottle of beer.
intention: Brian wants a drink.
moral_action: Brian asks his friend if he can have a soda to drink instead.
moral_consequence: Brian enjoys his glass of water and is fine to drive home that night.
immoral_action: Brian takes the beer and chugs it in front of his friend.
immoral_consequence: Brian gets drunk and is grounded when his parents find out.

norm: You shouldn't spoil a surprise.
situation: Kyle's mother is planning a surprise party for his brother.
intention: Kyle wants to go to the party.
moral_action: Kyle invites his best friend to go to the surprise party with him.
moral_consequence: Kyle and his best friend have a great time together.
immoral_action: Kyle invites his brother to go to the surprise party with him.
immoral_consequence: Kyle's brother tells his mother he knows about the party and Kyle gets grounded.

norm: You shouldn't expect people to always enjoy things you like.
situation: Allison is spending the evening with her boyfriend, and they want to watch a TV show.
intention: Allison wants to watch a sci fi show she heard good things about.
moral_action: Allison is not sure her boyfriend would like that specific show and asks him to choose a sci fi show to watch.
moral_consequence: Her boyfriend enjoys the show he chose and Allison is glad she let him choose.
immoral_action: Allison insists on watching the sci fi show and swears to her boyfriend that he will like it.
immoral_consequence: Her boyfriend doesn't like the show, and Allison is very disappointed to hear that.

norm: It's bad to cancel plans last minute.
situation: Jim is supposed to pick up Matt on his way to a concert that they're both going to.
intention: Jim needs to grab some food on the way to the show.
moral_action: Jim decides to get snacks at the venue, and him and Matt go to the concert together.
moral_consequence: Matt appreciates Jim being a good friend and offers to pay for the snacks.
immoral_action: Jim decides to hit up a convenience store on the way to the show and skips picking up Matt to save time.
immoral_consequence: Matt is left wondering when Jim is going to arrive, and ends up missing the show.

norm: You shouldn't put up with a friend that teases you.
situation: Gabriella is hanging out with her friend Marsha, and Marsha several hurtful jokes about Gabriella's appearance.
intention: Gabriella wants to be accepted.
moral_action: Gabriella plays truth or dare with Marsha, and she tells Marsha about her hurt feelings after selecting truth.
moral_consequence: Marsha understands her flaws, and she begins the long process of becoming a better person.
immoral_action: Gabriella pretends to laugh at the jokes while complimenting Marsha.
immoral_consequence: Marsha continues teasing Gavbriella.

norm: It's wrong to deceive your spouse.
situation: Joe's coworkers are all going out for a drink after work.
intention: Joe wants to go to the bar with his coworkers.
moral_action: Joe texts his wife to let her know he'll be joining his coworkers for a drink after work.
moral_consequence: Joe's wife is not worried and Joe has a great time with his colleagues.
immoral_action: Joe goes out to the bar without telling his wife.
immoral_consequence: Joe and his wife get into a fight when he comes home late smelling of alcohol.

norm: It's good to do something different every now and then
situation: Joe and his wife's wedding anniversary is in a week, and he knows that she would love to experience something new.
intention: Joe wants to plan something for the wedding anniversary.
moral_action: Joe organizes a day trip to a romantic location for the wedding anniversary.
moral_consequence: Joe's wife is pleasantly surprised and feels special and excited to enjoy their anniversary.
immoral_action: Joe makes a dinner reservation at the restaurant that he and his wife dine in all the time.
immoral_consequence: Joe's wife is disappointed and feels like Joe didn't make any effort to surprise her.

norm: It's wrong to peep in windows.
situation: John makes an unplanned stop at his friends house.
intention: John wants to know if anyone is home.
moral_action: John rings the doorbell to alert any occupants to his presence.
moral_consequence: John is able to pay a visit with being intrusive.
immoral_action: John looks through the window to see if anyone is home.
immoral_consequence: John is embarrassed to see his friend in an intimate position.

norm: It's not okay to make your parents upset.
situation: Paulo is hanging out with his friends late on a schoolnight while his parents wait for him to come home.
intention: Paulo wants to head home.
moral_action: Paulo calls his family to let them know where he is and that he's coming home.
moral_consequence: Paulo comes home, and after being told he needs to come home earlier, they all go to bed.
immoral_action: Paulo arrives home after curfew without having let his parents know where he was.
immoral_consequence: Paulo's parents yell at him about how worried they were and ground him.

norm: You should get dressed again before leaving a fitting room.
situation: Shelly is in a department store shopping for a new dress and finds one she likes.
intention: Shelly needs to try on the dress.
moral_action: Shelly changes back into her other clothing before she purchases the dress.
moral_consequence: Shelly now has her original clothing and a new dress she likes.
immoral_action: Shelly keeps wearing the dress after trying it on, leaving her other clothing in the changing room.
immoral_consequence: Shelly loses the clothing that she wore to the store.

norm: It's nice to give gifts for the holidays.
situation: Raymond knows his lonely friend doesn't get many gifts for Christmas and is thinking about buying him a gift.
intention: Raymond wants to consider buying his lonely friend a gift.
moral_action: Raymond thinks about what gift his lonely friend would want and buys it for him.
moral_consequence: Raymond's lonely friend is ecstatic on Christmas and feels very grateful towards Raymond.
immoral_action: Raymond decides to skip on a gift for his lonely friend.
immoral_consequence: Raymond's lonely friend feels depressed on Christmas since he didn't get any gifts again.

norm: It's good to recycle and reuse products as hand-me-downs.
situation: Eric lives at home with 2 older brothers, needs clothes and is poor.
intention: Eric wants some more clothes for himself.
moral_action: Eric asks his older brother for some of his nice shirts that he no longer wears.
moral_consequence: Eric has no financial stress and feels thrifty.
immoral_action: Eric buys expensive clothes at a store on his credit card.
immoral_consequence: Eric is more financially stressed out and can't pay his bills.

norm: It's good to make extra money.
situation: Roald is at work and the boss is letting the employees know that overtime is available this weekend and pays double.
intention: Roald wants to make use of his weekend.
moral_action: Roald signs up for the overtime to stay busy over the weekend because it never hurts to have some extra cash.
moral_consequence: Roald is able to save more money for a rainy day than he would have been able to with his normal hours.
immoral_action: Roald doesn't think the overtime is worth the extra money, so he spends the weekend drinking with his buddies.
immoral_consequence: Roald spends more than he planned and regrets not working the overtime for the extra money he could use now.

norm: It's wrong to lie to your family about your pregnancy.
situation: Joan grew up in an abusive household and is pregnant with her first child with her husband.
intention: Joan wants to protect her future child from her abusive parents.
moral_action: Joan tells her parents she is pregnant and lays out rules they must follow to have a relationship with their grandchild.
moral_consequence: Joan's parents improve their behavior to be able to see their grandchild.
immoral_action: Joan decides to hide her pregnancy from her parents for as long as she can.
immoral_consequence: Joan's parents are extremely angry when they eventually find out and treat her even worse.

norm: It's wrong to get tired of being nice.
situation: James is the most friendly person at his job and often helps his coworkers.
intention: James feels he is b show more appreciation for helping them eing taken for granted and wants people to.
moral_action: When a coworker asks James for help,  James agrees without hesitating.
moral_consequence: James's boss notices his unselfish behavior and offers him a promotion.
immoral_action: When a coworker asks James for help, he berates them and refuses.
immoral_consequence: James boss notices this behavior and reprimands him for being rude.

norm: It's good to move somewhere affordable.
situation: Imogene and her girlfriend are searching for apartments, and her girlfriend wants to move into an expensive place about their price range.
intention: Imogene wants to make her girlfriend happy.
moral_action: Imogene takes her girlfriend out to eat, and she brings up the advantages of living in a cheaper place while they eat.
moral_consequence: Imogene and her girlfriend learn more about each other during the conversation.
immoral_action: Imogene goes along with her girlfriend's request by moving into the pricey apartment.
immoral_consequence: Imogene and her girlfriend are evicted when they can't afford to pay rent.

norm: It is unlawful to commit several crimes.
situation: Steve is at a convenient mart when he notices the only employee on duty is in the restroom.
intention: Steve wants something cheap to eat.
moral_action: Steve waits for the store's attendant to return from the restroom then lawfully purchases a sandwich and chips.
moral_consequence: The attendant thanks Steve for waiting and gives him a discount on the purchase.
immoral_action: Steve takes a sandwich and drink from the store without paying and then decides to take a ride in a car that is idling nearby.
immoral_consequence: Steve is caught by the police and is sentenced to a serve a year in prison.

norm: It's expected that you take good care of your pets.
situation: Pat and her partner Lori are going on vacation and are leaving their two cats at home for the week.
intention: Pat wants the cats to have food while they are gone.
moral_action: Pat and Lori ask their friend to come feed and spend time with the cats until they return.
moral_consequence: The cats are relaxed and are well fed during Pat's vacation.
immoral_action: Pat puts all of the food for the cats in a large dish and hopes they will make it last the week.
immoral_consequence: Pat's cats experience high anxiety and over eat during the first days of the trip, then have no food until Pat and Lori return.

norm: You shouldn't lie about your whereabouts.
situation: Samantha is a teenager and is invited to a party.
intention: Samantha wants to go out to a party with her girlfriends.
moral_action: Samantha tells her parents she is going to a party and gives them the address.
moral_consequence: Samantha’s parents call to check on her later that evening and permit her to continue going to parties in the future.
immoral_action: Samantha tells her parents that she is going to stay the night at the neighbor’s house, and spends the night partying.
immoral_consequence: Samantha's parents call the neighbors to wish her a good night, find out she's not there, and proceed to ground her for a month.

norm: It's not okay to be unprofessional.
situation: Ben is meeting a new client in the office this morning.
intention: Ben wants to talk to the man about the work that he wants done.
moral_action: Ben meets the customer wearing a business suit and a tie.
moral_consequence: The man is impressed with how Ben presents himself and is sure that his company is the one for him.
immoral_action: Ben greets the man wearing a tank top and boxing shorts.
immoral_consequence: The man decides that Ben's company wouldn't do well to service his business.

norm: It's considerate to show gratitude when others help you.
situation: Omar was riding his bike in the park when he hit a pothole and flipped off the bike, and now Ken is helping him get up.
intention: Omar wants to say something to Ken.
moral_action: Omar tells Ken that he is very thankful someone was there to help him after his accident.
moral_consequence: Ken is happy to hear that Omar is grateful and is warmed to help someone out who deserves it.
immoral_action: Omar tells Ken that he didn't need to help him up, that Omar is a man, and he can handle his own problems.
immoral_consequence: Ken thinks Omar is bizarre in his hyper masculinity and is annoyed that Omar is brushing his help off.

norm: Raping someone is not a good thing to do.
situation: John notices a new coworker at his workplace that he finds attractive.
intention: John wants to have intimate romantic relations with the woman.
moral_action: John asks his coworker out on a date after work.
moral_consequence: John and his coworker begin dating and fall in love.
immoral_action: John follows his coworker home and sexually assaults her.
immoral_consequence: John is arrested and sentenced to several years in prison.

norm: It's good to use toilet paper.
situation: Ben is using the bathroom while camping in the woods when he realizes that he forgot to bring toilet paper.
intention: Ben wants to wipe himself.
moral_action: Ben calls a friend and asks him to bring some toilet paper from his tent.
moral_consequence: Ben has to wait but is able to clean himself up properly and without risk.
immoral_action: Ben grabs some nearby leaves and uses them as makeshift toilet paper.
immoral_consequence: The leaves were poison ivy and give Ben a terrible and painful rash.

norm: One should show respect to family members.
situation: Sal is at a family reunion.
intention: Sal wants to talk with someone.
moral_action: Sal see his cousin and asks him how everything is going for her.
moral_consequence: Sal has a good time talking with his family.
immoral_action: Sal chats with the people who are doing the catering for the party.
immoral_consequence: Sal is shunned by his family for not talking to them.

norm: It's wrong to question how someone else live's their lives.
situation: Erin feels a strong sense of disapproval as she watches her brother sign up for classes in school that won't help him earn a big salary.
intention: Erin wants to talk to her brother about his educational decisions.
moral_action: Erin explains to her brother that she is taking a different set of classes and talks about what she hopes to achieve in life, with her education.
moral_consequence: Her brother listens to her and considers what she has said, and they continue to have an open dialogue together.
immoral_action: Erin tells her brother that the classes he selects are worthless and a complete waste of money.
immoral_consequence: Her brother will be highly offended by her remarks and their relationship will become strained.

norm: It's frowned upon to consult your manager excessively.
situation: Sally is doing a complex project at work.
intention: Sally wants to do the project well.
moral_action: Sally emails her boss once concisely and then carefully rereads the instructions for the project.
moral_consequence: Sally is praised for the project and given a promotion.
immoral_action: Sally sends multiple emails to her boss each day asking excessive questions.
immoral_consequence: Sally is demoted after the completion of the project for needing too much direction.

norm: Supporting a depressed friend through a hard time is expected.
situation: Dave is hanging out with his friend Jose when Jose tells Dave he's feeling depressed.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Jose's statement.
moral_action: Dave tells Jose that it must be tough and offers to help him in any way he needs even if it's just talking.
moral_consequence: Jose feels supported and is feeling a tiny bit better that he has someone to help him get through the depression.
immoral_action: "Dave tells Jose that he is not a ""feelings kind of guy"" and that if he wants to talk about that to call someone."
immoral_consequence: Jose feels let down that his friend is ignoring his problem and dismissing talking about it.

norm: You should always make sure your friends are doing OK.
situation: Sharon is at a large party in a mansion with a few girlfriends, and one of them seems pretty drunk.
intention: Sharon wants to enjoy the party till the end.
moral_action: Sharon calls a cab for her drunk friend, sends her home and goes back to partying.
moral_consequence: Sharon's drunk friend spends a safe and peaceful night in her own bed.
immoral_action: Sharon figures her friend is an adult and will take care of herself.
immoral_consequence: Sharon's drunk friend is taken advantage of by a group of guys in a remote corner of the mansion.

norm: It's improper to share your bathroom habits with other people.
situation: Billy and Beatrice eating at a restaurant out on their first date.
intention: Billy wants to tell Beatrice more about himself.
moral_action: Billy talks about how he's a gig worker helping to train artificial intelligence.
moral_consequence: Beatrice is impressed by Billy's line of work and the two have a lively conversation.
immoral_action: Billy talks about how he has to shave his armpits in the shower every day because he's so hairy.
immoral_consequence: Beatrice is grossed out and loses her appetite and leaves shortly thereafter.

norm: It's wrong to go to brothels if you're underage.
situation: David is walking home from school with one of his friends.
intention: David wants to do something fun and exciting.
moral_action: David and his friend walk across a train bridge to cross over a creek instead of sticking to their usual route home.
moral_consequence: David's friend is a little scared by how high the bridge feels, but after crossing it he feels exhilarated.
immoral_action: David and his friend sneak in to an adult only club through an open door they notice in a nearby alley.
immoral_consequence: David's friend sees several naked women under bright, flashing lights and is scarred by the experience.

norm: You shouldn't steal from your family.
situation: John notices all the kids in school have the newest phones, and he does not.
intention: John wants to buy a new device too.
moral_action: John gets a part time job to save money.
moral_consequence: John is able to save up for a new phone like his friends have.
immoral_action: John takes money from his mothers purse when she isn't looking.
immoral_consequence: John's mother notices and grounds him.

norm: You shouldn't go into someone's room without their permission.
situation: Jane is playing a game with Liz where they need to hide coins from each other, they aren't allowed in their parents' room.
intention: Jane wants to find a spot Liz won't look in.
moral_action: Jane throws the coin into her parents' open door, so she doesn't actually go inside.
moral_consequence: "Liz lets Jane win this round but then amends the rules to require the coin to be ""placed"", not ""thrown""."
immoral_action: Jane hides the coin in their parent's room by entering it and putting it behind the dresser.
immoral_consequence: Liz gives up looking for the coin and tells on Jane when she reveals where it is.

norm: It's not nice to cheat on your spouse.
situation: Barry has been married to Lisa for several years now.
intention: Barry wants a dinner date to his work function.
moral_action: Barry brings his wife with him when he goes to the work function.
moral_consequence: Barry's coworkers are pleased to meet his wife and ask him occasionally how she is doing.
immoral_action: Barry takes his secretary as his dinner date to the work function.
immoral_consequence: Barry's coworkers think less highly of him and talk to him less in the office.

norm: It's wrong to be abusive towards children
situation: Ted sees that his son has started to make bad grades on his report card.
intention: Ted wants his son to make better grades.
moral_action: Ted encourages his son by taking him to a movie every time he does well on a test.
moral_consequence: The teacher calls Ted and tells him that his son is doing so much better in school.
immoral_action: Ted beats his son every time that he makes a bad grade on a test.
immoral_consequence: The teacher reports Ted to the authorities, and he goes to jail for child abuse.

norm: It is taboo to be attracted to your relatives.
situation: Dan is sitting beside his cousin Lisa on a living room couch.
intention: Dan wants to express that Dan thinks Lisa is good looking.
moral_action: Dan tells Lisa that Lisa has a strong fashion sense and chooses flattering outfits.
moral_consequence: Lisa appreciates the compliment and feels validated that her unique style is noticed.
immoral_action: Dan admits to Lisa that Lisa is exactly the type of woman Dan would like to have sex with.
immoral_consequence: Lisa feels violated because Dan is suggesting an act that will pollute potential offspring's gene pool.

norm: It is rude to burden others with your problems.
situation: After an argument with her mother, Maggie walks out of the room where Josh is studying.
intention: Maggie wants to find an outlit for her problems.
moral_action: Maggie vents her feelings in her journal.
moral_consequence: Maggie figures out the source of the fights she has with her mother.
immoral_action: Maggie sits down and talks to Josh about her issues.
immoral_consequence: Maggie hurts her relationship with Josh because he can't focus.

norm: You should not make assumptions about peoples' sexual preferences.
situation: Uri is hanging out with his new friend, Gozo and sees a pretty girl nearby eyeing up Gozo.
intention: Uri wants to see if Gozo is interested.
moral_action: Uri asks Gozo if he's interested.
moral_consequence: Uri learns about Gozo and feels relieved that he didn't push.
immoral_action: Uri  brings Gozo over and introduces him to the girl.
immoral_consequence: Uri stops getting calls from Gozo to hang out and is confused.

norm: You shouldn't drink martinis in the morning.
situation: Don has had a rough morning so far dealing with stressful problems at work.
intention: Don wants to take the edge off.
moral_action: Don waits for his lunch break and orders a martini with his lunch.
moral_consequence: Don's coworker enjoys a beer while he has the martini, and they have a relaxing lunch break.
immoral_action: Don prepares a martini and drinks it during his morning break.
immoral_consequence: Don's coworker notices him drinking early and thinks he is irresponsible.

norm: It's nice to do things with your family
situation: James and his kids unexpectedly got a day off due to heavy snowfall.
intention: James wants to have a fun, relaxing day.
moral_action: James takes his kids to a local park with a big hill where they can go sledding.
moral_consequence: James takes lots of photos and savors the memory of their sled trip together.
immoral_action: James lets his kids spend the day on their phones while he plays video games.
immoral_consequence: James and his kids spend the whole day alone with various entertainment.

norm: You shouldn't use social media vindictively
situation: Heather is on Facebook posting and interacting with her friends.
intention: Heather wants to tell her friends about her life.
moral_action: Heather post that she's feeling low after a recent break-up.
moral_consequence: Heather gets a lot of support and love from her friends and starts to feel better.
immoral_action: Heather posts about the boyfriend who just dumped her and claims that he embezzles from his work.
immoral_consequence: Heather is sued for libel by her ex-boyfriend over her baseless accusation.

norm: It's not okay to not sympathize with peoples feelings.
situation: Kyle lives in a neighborhood where a crime boss just died and meets a procession of people who are mourning him.
intention: Kyle wants to decide if he should join the procession.
moral_action: Kyle avoids the procession and goes another way to avoid getting tangled up with them.
moral_consequence: Kyle stays clear of the bad reputation of the crime boss and his followers.
immoral_action: Kyle joins the procession and is given a sign to hold that laments the crime boss' death.
immoral_consequence: Other people see Kyle in the procession and assume that Kyle is involved in organized crime.

norm: It's poor taste to make a joke about beheadings.
situation: Keith is watching some Youtube videos and comes across one about the guillotine.
intention: Keith wants to leave a comment on the video.
moral_action: Keith makes a tasteful comment about how horrible the guillotine is as a method of execution.
moral_consequence: Keith gets a lot of comments from other users agreeing with him.
immoral_action: Keith leaves a comment making a really off-color joke about the deaths discussed in the video.
immoral_consequence: Keith gets a lot of angry responses to his comment from other users.

norm: You shouldn't enjoy when people cry.
situation: John has been yelling at his wife Mindy, and she is starting to cry.
intention: John wants to feel better about himself.
moral_action: John breathes deeply, holds his wife and apologizes to her as he strokes her hair.
moral_consequence: Mindy feels closer to John and loves him even more and stops crying.
immoral_action: John says to Mindy she deserves to cry and laughs loudly as he puts on the tv.
immoral_consequence: Mindy resents John even more and considers divorcing him.

norm: It's good to donate to good causes.
situation: One of James' coworkers went around to everyone's desk collecting for UNICEF.
intention: James wants to stick to his monthly budget.
moral_action: James donates ten dollars and skips his morning coffee for a week.
moral_consequence: James feels happy about helping children across the world, and his coworker thanks him.
immoral_action: James tells his coworker that most charities waste their money on exorbitant salaries.
immoral_consequence: James' coworker becomes uncooperative every time James has to ask him for something.

norm: It's not okay to use the word retarded anymore.
situation: Rich came to his friend Ron's house and noticed that his friend has a brother with cerebral palsy.
intention: Rich wanted to make a comment on Ron's brother.
moral_action: Rich tells his brother that he should've told him that he had a brother.
moral_consequence: Ron feels good that Rich didn't mention his brother's disability.
immoral_action: Rich tells Ron that he didn't know that he had a retarded brother.
immoral_consequence: Ron feels offended and tells him never to say that word again.

norm: It's mean to make someone feel worthless.
situation: John just lost his job and sees his wife Mindy at home cooking dinner.
intention: John wants to feel powerful.
moral_action: John takes a breath, tells Mindy he lost his job and goes to work out.
moral_consequence: Mindy comforts John and feels closer to him.
immoral_action: John raises his voice and tells Mindy she can't cook, so she shouldn't even try.
immoral_consequence: Mindy resents John and wonders whether he even loves her.

norm: It's wrong to drive erratically.
situation: Henry is driving on the way to his work when he gets a text message.
intention: Henry wants to check the text message.
moral_action: Henry checks the text message as soon as he gets to work.
moral_consequence: Henry and his car both make it to his place of work safely.
immoral_action: Henry swerves all through the lanes while looking down at his phone.
immoral_consequence: Henry runs his car into the ditch on the side of the road.

norm: It's inconsiderate to take an employee's focus from their job.
situation: Jill sees her coworker concentrating on a task she is doing in the office.
intention: Jill wants to tell her coworker about some gossip she heard.
moral_action: Jill waits until the lunch break then tells her coworker the exciting gossip.
moral_consequence: Jill's coworker enjoys being in the know about the gossip and returns to work.
immoral_action: Jill goes over to her coworker while they are working and tells them about the gossip she heard.
immoral_consequence: Jill's coworker gets into trouble with the boss for gossiping when they were meant to be working.

norm: Partners should not make each other feel upset.
situation: Lee has been feeling depressed lately.
intention: Lee wants her husband to know about how depressed she feels.
moral_action: Lee tells her husband that she is feeling really low and asks for his help.
moral_consequence: Lee's husband is happy she opened up and actively thinks of ways he can support her.
immoral_action: Lee tells her husband about her depressive thoughts and tells him she thinks he has not been helpful.
immoral_consequence: Lee's husband feels very guilty and incapable of helping her meaningfully.

norm: It's rude to show pubic hair in public.
situation: Joseph is an adult and is at the public swimming pool where children are present.
intention: Joseph wants to get out of the water.
moral_action: Joseph keeps his swimming trunks tied tight, and they stay on his waist as he gets out of the pool.
moral_consequence: All the people at the pool, including Joseph, enjoy their day.
immoral_action: Joseph lets the weight of the water pull his trunks down to his pubic region and does not pull them back up.
immoral_consequence: Parents at the pool are outraged and call the police on Joseph.

norm: It is expected to hand out candy on halloween.
situation: Sue is a dentist home from work on Halloween evening.
intention: Sue wants to give something to the kids that are trick-or-treating.
moral_action: Sue gives each child a candy bar when they come to the door.
moral_consequence: The children are excited to receive a treat.
immoral_action: Sue gives each child a toothbrush when they come to the door.
immoral_consequence: The children are disappointed they didn't get something sweet.

norm: It's inappropriate to fart in public
situation: Fiona, who is at the mall with her friend, has eaten a bean burrito for lunch and it has made her very gassy.
intention: Fiona wants to let out some gas.
moral_action: Fiona uses the restroom and lets her gas out in the stall that she is in.
moral_consequence: Fiona's friend has fun shopping with her and makes plans to see her again soon.
immoral_action: Fiona passes gas while she is walking through the mall with her friend.
immoral_consequence: Fiona's friend is offended by the odor and thinks she is disgusting.

norm: It's good to be helpful and kind.
situation: It snowed heavily and Randy sees his elderly neighbor Joe trying to shovel his driveway.
intention: Randy wants to tell something to Joe.
moral_action: Randy tells Joe he will shovel his driveway for him.
moral_consequence: Joe will think Randy is a good neighbor and nice.
immoral_action: Randy tells Joe he's old and will break his back if he shovels too hard.
immoral_consequence: Joe will think Randy is annoying and not helpful.

norm: It is bad to stalk or creep on people online
situation: Mark has a crush on his classmate, and he finds her on Facebook.
intention: Mark wants to see what she is up to.
moral_action: Mark sends her a message and asks if she wants to catch up.
moral_consequence: If his classmate says yes, Mark may have a date, but he won’t be seen as creepy if she doesn’t.
immoral_action: Mark follows her every move online and obsesses over every post.
immoral_consequence: Mark is seen as creepy as he becomes obsessed, scaring people away.

norm: You shouldn't damage other people's cars.
situation: John made a mean joke at his co-worker Jim's expense leaving Jim feeling upset.
intention: Jim wants to react to the joke.
moral_action: Jim pulls John aside and privately expresses his negative feelings about the joke.
moral_consequence: John apologizes for making the joke and Jim is left feeling much better.
immoral_action: Jim reacts to the joke with extreme retaliation and decides to key John's car.
immoral_consequence: John calls the police and Jim is arrested for vandalism after being caught by the security camera.

norm: It's wrong to make cancer jokes.
situation: Maddie is sitting with a group of sad people with cancer at a party.
intention: Maddie wants to make everyone smile.
moral_action: Maddie tells everyone a funny story about her pet along with showing them pictures of her dog.
moral_consequence: Someone asks Maddie if she'd like to walk her dog with them.
immoral_action: Maddie performs a small skit with punchlines about cancer.
immoral_consequence: Maddie is removed from the party after someone complains about her behavior to the host.

norm: It's good to pet sit for others.
situation: Alice is sitting in her kitchen, talking with her sister Janet on the phone when she is asked to look after her dog while she is away.
intention: Alice wants to be happy and without stress in her life.
moral_action: Alice feeds and waters, and takes the dog for walks every day.
moral_consequence: The dog is happy, and Alice is happy that Karen can depend on her, and everyone continues to get along.
immoral_action: Alice refuses to look after the dog.
immoral_consequence: The dog dies and Karen is angry and creates a lot of familial problems for Alice.

norm: It's wrong to blame significant others for accidents that happen.
situation: Mark was driving in a car with his wife Kate when he crashed into another car.
intention: Mark wants to say something to Kate.
moral_action: Mark tells Kate that it was his fault and that he feels very bad about it.
moral_consequence: Kate feels sorry for Mark and isn't mad at him for crashing.
immoral_action: Mark tells Kate that they wouldn't be in this situation if she didn't talk so much.
immoral_consequence: Kate starts feeling guilty and gets mad at Mark for making her feel this way.

norm: It's wrong to try and dictate what your partner wears.
situation: Anthony's girlfriend, Martha, gets a hat promoting a political campaign that grinds against his core values, as a human being.
intention: Anthony doesn't want Martha to wear the hat when they're together.
moral_action: Anthony buys Martha a new hat, that is more politically neutral, that he knows she will love because she considered buying it herself.
moral_consequence: Martha finds the gift to be thoughtful and wears it all the time, and Anthony feels good that he gave her a gift, rather than complain about her political leanings.
immoral_action: Anthony gives Martha an ultimatum, telling her that he will not be seen in public with here, while she wears that hat.
immoral_consequence: Martha is offended and tells Anthony that she has every right to wear that hat, and Anthony regrets giving an ultimatum to someone he loves.

norm: It's nice to set mice free from glue traps.
situation: Pete's girlfriend Mary asks him to come by and help her get rid of a mouse.
intention: Pete wants to please Mary.
moral_action: Pete catches the mouse in a glue trap then releases it in the park.
moral_consequence: Mary is grateful for Pete's assistance.
immoral_action: Pete catches the mouse in a glue trap and tosses the trao and the live mouse into the trash.
immoral_consequence: Mary is disgusted with Pete's casual cruelty.

norm: It's not right to lie to people.
situation: Ray didn't do any of the homework, and his teacher is asking him what he did.
intention: Ray needs to tell his teacher what he's done.
moral_action: Ray tells his teacher that he hasn't started doing any of the homework.
moral_consequence: Ray is able to get help from his teacher, and he doesn't have to remember any lies.
immoral_action: Ray tells his teacher that he's almost done with all of the homework.
immoral_consequence: Ray has to quickly do all of his homework so that his teacher doesn't find out.

norm: It's kind to show patience towards those with disabilities.
situation: Dave is waiting behind Phil, who is mentally disabled for his turn at the street parking pay station and Phil is taking a long time.
intention: Dave wants to say something to Phil about how slow Phil is.
moral_action: Dave tells Phil that he can help him figure out the screen if he's having a hard time.
moral_consequence: Phil is happy Dave will help and relieved his little struggle with the machine is over with.
immoral_action: Dave tells Phil to hurry up because he doesn't have all day and if Phil can't figure it out to move aside.
immoral_consequence: Phil is stressed from the pressure and nervous about Dave standing behind him angry.

norm: It's bad not to wear a swimsuit to the pool
situation: It's ninety degrees outside, and an overheated Beth is picking up her sister at the pool.
intention: Beth wants to cool off.
moral_action: Beth buys a cold bottle of water and some ice cream from the food court.
moral_consequence: Beth befriends attractive person making her ice cream.
immoral_action: Beth jumps into the pool in her normal attire.
immoral_consequence: Beth's clothes turn weird colors from the pool water.

norm: It is hurtful to call your spouse negative things.
situation: John's wife is cooking dinner when she drops the main dish on the floor, ruining it.
intention: John wants to get his wife to be more careful.
moral_action: John laughs and tells his wife that there is no need to be in such a rush.
moral_consequence: John's wife laughs as well and no one's feelings are hurt.
immoral_action: John yells at his wife and tells her that she's clumsy.
immoral_consequence: His wife feelings are hurt and she begins to cry.

norm: It's rude to yell at someone.
situation: Sarah is driving to work but is stuck on a street corner by an old lady who is crossing the street very slowly.
intention: Sarah wants to get to work as soon as possible.
moral_action: Sarah asks the old lady if she can help her and ends up helping her to cross the street.
moral_consequence: The old lady crosses the street much quicker with Sarah's help and feels uplifted and happy that someone was so nice to her.
immoral_action: Sarah yells at the old lady and tells her to hurry up.
immoral_consequence: The old lady hurries up but feels sad and a little scared.

norm: Putting restrictions on what a roommate can cook is dramatic.
situation: Blackwell hates the smell of cooked pepers, and he notices Amanda about to cook them.
intention: Blackwell wants to escape the smell.
moral_action: Blackwell spends the afternoon outside in the park.
moral_consequence: Blackwell feels closer to nature after a long walk.
immoral_action: Blackwell demands that Amanda cook something else as he tosses the peppers in the trash.
immoral_consequence: Blackwell has a headache when Amanda cooks more peppers to spite him.

norm: You shouldn't go off on your ex.
situation: Mary broke up with her boyfriend and needs to get some things from his apartment.
intention: Mary wants to get her books back from him.
moral_action: "Mary retrieves the books without saying more than ""hi"" to her ex."
moral_consequence: Mary's ex remembers her fondly as a calm person.
immoral_action: Mary immediately raises her voice and starts demanding that her ex give her her books back.
immoral_consequence: Mary's ex speaks badly of her to their mutual friends.

norm: It's impolite to expect to receive gifts.
situation: It's Christmas Day and Billy is with his parents, waiting to open his gifts.
intention: Billy really wants a new bike.
moral_action: Billy excitedly tells his parents he hopes for a bike but that he will be happy with any other gift.
moral_consequence: Billy gets a bike and his parents are delighted with how happy and grateful he is.
immoral_action: Billy tells his parents he is sure he will get a bike and will be very angry if he doesn't get one.
immoral_consequence: Billy indeed gets a bike but his parents are hurt by how entitled and selfish Billy is.

norm: It is rude to grunt.
situation: James is in front of a large TV that needs to be put on a TV stand and it is too heavy to a person to lift it silently.
intention: James wants to setup the TV today.
moral_action: James asks for help and lifts the TV without making a loud noise.
moral_consequence: His friends are happy they were able to setup the TV and are pleased with James.
immoral_action: James lifts the TV by himself and makes a loud noise.
immoral_consequence: The friends around James are appalled by his noise making.

norm: You shouldn't commit arson.
situation: Another person was shot by the cops so James decided to go violently protest.
