intention: Jamie wants to cause chaos in the city.
moral_action: Jamie spray paints on the windows of a CVS the name of the person killed by police.
moral_consequence: An employee has to clean up the spray paint, but no employees have to lose their job.
immoral_action: Jamie set off fireworks inside a CVS in order to help light a fire inside it.
immoral_consequence: The employees lose their jobs, and it takes a while before the building is built back.

norm: It's rude to tell your spouse they are fat.
situation: Helga is putting on a new pair of very tight pants and asks her husband Joe if she looks good in them.
intention: Joe wants to tell Helga his feelings about the fit of the pants.
moral_action: Joe tells Helga that her pants are extremely tight which is a big turn on because it accentuates all her feminine curves.
moral_consequence: Helga is delighted that Joe is turned on by her and that he finds her attractive and is full of self confidence.
immoral_action: Joe tells Helga that she is hugely fat and the pants look like they're going to explode from all the pressure.
immoral_consequence: Helga is embarrassed about being fat and depressed that Joe doesn't find her very attractive.

norm: It is wrong to wish for destruction.
situation: Steve was about to be thrown out by rising rents but the pandemic pushed rents back down to where he could afford it.
intention: Steve wants his life to improve.
moral_action: Steve hope that things get better for everyone over time.
moral_consequence: After the disaster ends, Steve's rent once again climbs too high, and he's forced to move.
immoral_action: Steve hopes the pandemic keeps ruining the economy so that his rent will stay low.
immoral_consequence: Half of Steve's neighbors get evicted but Steve himself remains safe.

norm: It's wrong to steal someone's boyfriend.
situation: Tanya has just picked up her tickets for the senior prom in the school office.
intention: Tanya wants a date to attend the prom with her.
moral_action: Tanya asks a boy that sits behind her in English to go with her to the prom.
moral_consequence: Tanya has a great time at the prom with the boy in her class.
immoral_action: Tanya asks her friend's boyfriend to go to the prom with her.
immoral_consequence: Tanya's friend doesn't talk to her for the next few weeks.

norm: You should not try to make a friend uncomfortable.
situation: Kalyn's invited their friend Rachel over but now it's getting late and Rachel shows no sign of leaving.
intention: Kalyn wants Rachel to leave soon.
moral_action: Kalyn tells Rachel that she is tired and would love to catch up with Rachel again some other time.
moral_consequence: Rachel and Kalyn make plans to hang out again and Rachel leaves.
immoral_action: Kalyn begins asking Rachel about her recent infertility issues to try and make Rachel uncomfortable, so she will leave.
immoral_consequence: Rachel thinks Kalyn is insensitive and begins to distance herself from Kalyn.

norm: It's bad to physically assault people.
situation: Owen is hitting on Jake's girlfriend and making her uncomfortable.
intention: Jake wants Owen to leave his girlfriend alone.
moral_action: Jake tells Owen to back off and takes his girlfriend away from him.
moral_consequence: The situation is de-escalated and Jake and his girlfriend are both safe.
immoral_action: Jake punches Owen in the face.
immoral_consequence: Jake and Owen end up getting into a fist fight and both get injured.

norm: It's rude to expect gifts from others.
situation: John's mother just returned from a business trip abroad.
intention: John wants to greet his mother.
moral_action: John runs up to his mother, hugs her and asks her how her trip was.
moral_consequence: John's mother is very touched that he was so glad to see her and that he was curious about her trip.
immoral_action: John runs up to his mother, hugs her and asks her what she brought him from abroad.
immoral_consequence: John's mother tells him that she didn't have time to go shopping and now she feels very guilty.

norm: It's wrong to take advantage of the deceased.
situation: Hank's wife dies and Hank can't afford a nice headstone for her.
intention: Hank wants to get a headstone for his now-deceased wife.
moral_action: Hank finds a modestly-priced headstone and gets it for his wife.
moral_consequence: Hank honors his wife's memory and leaves a memento for others to see.
immoral_action: Hank goes to a graveyard at night, removes a headstone from a grave, and re-engraves it for his wife.
immoral_consequence: The family of the person Hank robbed are horrified that someone would steal a dead person's headstone.

norm: It's wrong to say things to make others feel hopeless.
situation: Billy is talking with a friend who keeps on complaining about his life.
intention: Billy is irritated by his friend and wants him to stop bothering him with his whining.
moral_action: Billy convinces his friend to try a new way of coping, which involves thinking only about the positive things.
moral_consequence: Billy's friend starts seeing that things in his life are actually not that bad and feels better.
immoral_action: Billy tells his friend there is no point in them talking about this anymore because his friend's situation is never going to improve.
immoral_consequence: Billy's friend feels terrible and goes back home thoroughly depressed.

norm: It's good to establish relationships with family.
situation: Gary has a day off work and cousins he has never met are in town.
intention: Gary wants to do something on his day off.
moral_action: Gary calls his cousins to spend the day off together.
moral_consequence: Gary meets his cousins and gets to know them.
immoral_action: Gary spends his day off playing video games by himself.
immoral_consequence: Gary does not meet his cousins to form a relationship.

norm: It is good to talk about kids before getting married.
situation: Danny and Layla are newly engaged.
intention: Danny wants to have children with Layla.
moral_action: Danny tells Layla he'd like to raise children with her.
moral_consequence: Layla and Danny decide to adopt a child, and they all live happily ever after.
immoral_action: Danny surprises Layla a bunch of pregnancy tests, so they can try for a baby.
immoral_consequence: Layla tells Danny she is infertile, and they break off their engagement.

norm: You can't expect people to exercise all the time.
situation: On a heavily rainy day Benard is waiting in his dance studio for his students.
intention: Benard wants to communicate with his students.
moral_action: Benard decides to cancel the class for the evening.
moral_consequence: Benard has a relaxing night reading in the studio.
immoral_action: Benard sends his students a text noting that they will never lose weight if they avoid exercising.
immoral_consequence: Benard is scolded by the owner of the studio for placing his students in unsafe conditions.

norm: Babies should never be treated poorly regardless of their behavior.
situation: Nancy is awakened by her screaming baby.
intention: Nancy wants to sleep.
moral_action: Nancy changes and feeds the baby getting it back to sleep.
moral_consequence: Nancy returns to bed and sleeps well knowing that her baby is cared for.
immoral_action: Nancy grabs the baby and hits it to make it stop crying.
immoral_consequence: Nancy is arrested for child abuse and her baby is taken away.

norm: It's bad to drive into a gate.
situation: Noah was visiting his friend who lived in a gated community, but the gate was locked when he got there.
intention: Noah wants to get past the gate.
moral_action: Noah calls his friend who calls the guard at the gate and tells him to let Noah in.
moral_consequence: The guard at the gate waves at Noah as he drives into the community.
immoral_action: Noah drives his car right through the gate and busts it to pieces.
immoral_consequence: The guard at the gate takes down Noah's phone number and calls the police.

norm: It's good to take your pet out for recreation.
situation: Patty craves companionship so she gets a puppy.
intention: Patty wants to maintain her busy work schedule.
moral_action: Patty makes sure to spend time playing in the park with her puppy everyday.
moral_consequence: Patty's pup is happy and healthy thanks to the activity.
immoral_action: Patty rarely has time to do more than take her puppy out to poop when she gets home.
immoral_consequence: Patty's pup grows listless from the lack of activity.

norm: It's unprofessional to make comments about your employees' wardrobe.
situation: Brandy thinks that her employee Janet's shirt is rather ugly despite being workplace appropriate.
intention: Brandy wants to talk about Janet's shirt.
moral_action: Brandy asks Janet where she got her top, but doesn't mention any opinion on the look of the top.
moral_consequence: Janet lets Brandy know where the top was bought and doesn't think twice about Brandy's question.
immoral_action: Brandy tells Janet that her top isn't very flattering and looks gaudy.
immoral_consequence: Janet feels uncomfortable working with Brandy and asks for a transfer, feeling insulted.

norm: It's considerate to drive a relative somewhere.
situation: Dave is just relaxing and doing nothing at home when his sister Suzy asks him to drive her to a doctor's appointment.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Suzy's request.
moral_action: Dave tells Suzy that he'd be glad to drop her off since he's got nothing to do anyway.
moral_consequence: Suzy is happy she won't have to ride the bus and is glad she has such a good brother.
immoral_action: Dave tells Suzy he's relaxing right now and doesn't feel like getting up, so she should take the bus.
immoral_consequence: Suzy is annoyed by Dave's laziness and is stressed that now she might not make it on time.

norm: Smelling bad is socially unacceptable.
situation: Mary is preparing to go out to a party.
intention: Mary wants to get ready quickly.
moral_action: Mary quickly sprays on some perfume, puts on clothes, and leaves for the party.
moral_consequence: Mary's friends don't notice any bad smells and are friendly with her.
immoral_action: Mary quickly puts on some clothes and leaves, without using deodorant or perfume.
immoral_consequence: Mary's friends gossip about her behind her back that she smells.

norm: It is wrong to sabotage your child's friendships.
situation: Pam has a son with a friend she thinks might be a bad influence who has called the house wanting to come over.
intention: Pam wants her son to focus on his homework.
moral_action: Pam tells her son's friend that he cannot have any guests because his homework is incomplete.
moral_consequence: Pam's son is able to complete the homework that he has been assigned.
immoral_action: Pam claims that her son no longer wants to hang out with the boy.
immoral_consequence: Pam's son finds out and is upset with his mom for lying to his friend.

norm: It's nice to fix things for other people.

intention: Nate wants to decide on a training program for his boy.
moral_action: Nate gets the boy involved in physical exercise and survivalist courses to teach him how to live off of the land.
moral_consequence: Nate's child becomes tough and independent and teaches survival courses for the military.
immoral_action: Nate leaves his boy out in the wilderness for days and teaches him to only serve himself, taking from others if needed.
immoral_consequence: Nate's child grows up and treats his father disrespectfully, just as his father taught him to treat people.

norm: It's good to open up presents for your children.
situation: Sarah has given her son Gus a new gift that is in a big box.
intention: Sarah wants her son Gus to have fun with the new gift.
moral_action: Sarah helps Gus open the box, so he can get to the gift.
moral_consequence: Gus has fun playing with the gift that Sarah has given to him.
immoral_action: Sarah lets her son try to open the box on his own.
immoral_consequence: Gus tries hard to get the box open, but he can't figure it out.

norm: It's good to do things together with your girlfriend.
situation: Keith's partner Jamie has been asking him to take her to the beach, but he has plans to hang out with his friend Thomas.
intention: Keith wants to respond to Jamie.
moral_action: Keith tells Thomas that he needs to spend time with Jamie instead and will make plans with him later.
moral_consequence: Jamie feels loved because Keith showed her she was important to him.
immoral_action: Keith tells Jamie that he already told Thomas he would see him and asks Jamie for a raincheck.
immoral_consequence: Jamie is sad because Keith put his friend over her.

norm: It's rude to keep tabs on someone's eating habits.
situation: Rebecca is with her friend at a restaurant and her friend ordered something unhealthy.
intention: Rebecca wants to have a conversation with her friend as they eat.
moral_action: Rebecca talks about the weather with her friend and other such day to day things.
moral_consequence: Rebecca's friend enjoys the conversation and meal with Rebecca.
immoral_action: Rebecca passively notes aloud that every time they go out to eat her friend picks the most unhealthy foods.
immoral_consequence: Rebecca's friend is insulted by Rebecca's observation and becomes self concious about her choices around Rebecca.

norm: It's deplorable to manipulate people into buying you free food.
situation: Mark waits for women to ask him out, agrees, and then vanishes after she buys him a meal.
intention: Mark wants to continue to get free food.
moral_action: Mark decides to get a job in the restaurant and work hard there.
moral_consequence: Mark's job comes with free meals for Mark.
immoral_action: Mark sits around in his best suit until sure enough a lady asks him out, and he gets his free meal.
immoral_consequence: Mark continues to take advantage of women for free food.

norm: It's rude to pretend you're something you aren't.
situation: Christen is at a hospital to visit a friend and is wearing a new white jacket that she got for Christmas.
intention: Christen wants to see her friend.
moral_action: Christen is almost mistaken for a doctor due to her coat but goes through security and explains that she is a visitor.
moral_consequence: Christen spends the day with her friend, and they are able to reconnect and relax together.
immoral_action: Christen is allowed to skip security when someone mistakes her for a doctor due to her coat.
immoral_consequence: Christen is later stopped in the hospital for not having a pass and can't spend very much time with her friend.

norm: You shouldn't steal someone's medication.
situation: Dana is an Oxycontin addict, and forgot to bring her Oxycontin when going on a family beach trip.
intention: Dana wants to take some Oxycontin to avoid withdrawal.
moral_action: Dana goes to a local doctor explaining the situation, who prescribes her limited Oxycontin supply.
moral_consequence: Dana is happy the rest of her trip and doesn't get into any altercations with family.
immoral_action: Dana decides to sneak into a pharmacy and take a few pills that were meant for other patients.
immoral_consequence: Dana's brother reports her to the police and Dana feels humiliated as she spends time in jail.

norm: It's good to spend time with your spouse.
situation: Derek and Julie are married and work long hours apart, but both have taken a week of vacation at the same time.
intention: Derek wants to go on a trip.
moral_action: Derek takes Julie on a cruise to the Caribbean, where she's never been before.
moral_consequence: Julie has fun in the Caribbean and thanks Derek with passionate sex while on the cruise.
immoral_action: Derek goes to Las Vegas with his male friends and enjoys gambling and drinking.
immoral_consequence: Julie wonders what she has in common with Derek and contacts a divorce lawyer.

norm: It's wrong to hate kids.
situation: Some of the neighborhood kids keep stepping on Nicholas's grass, and he is worried about keeping his lawn nice.
intention: Nicholas wants to stop the kids from stepping on his lawn.
moral_action: Nicholas talks to the kids, and he lets them know that he is trying to keep his grass nice, asking them to please keep to the walkway.
moral_consequence: The kids are mostly respectful of his wishes, and they stay on the walkway, while Nicholas enjoys a stress free relationship with most of his neighbors and their families.
immoral_action: Nicholas tells the kids that they aren't allowed near his house and threatens to prosecute them for trespassing.
immoral_consequence: The tension between Nicholas and the kids causes everyone to feel uncomfortable and, in some cases, the kids are antagonistic toward Nicholas because of his attitude toward them.

norm: It's bad to cheat to get through school.
situation: Janice is trying to study for a very hard exam later in the week.
intention: Janice wants to pass the exam.
moral_action: Janice studies very hard for the exam and gets a tutor to help her.
moral_consequence: Janice passes the exam and ends up doing well in the class.
immoral_action: Janice decides to write down the answers on a sheet that she surreptitiously checks during the exam.
immoral_consequence: Janice passes the test, but falls further behind because she can't keep up, and ends up failing the class.

norm: It's wrong to serve people food you know is bad.
situation: Sally is throwing a dinner party to celebrate her friend's birthday.
intention: Sally wants to feed her friends without spending a lot of money.
moral_action: Sally searches for a nice recipe that will be affordable and decides to serve pasta.
moral_consequence: Sally's friends enjoy the pasta dinner and hope there will be another dinner soon.
immoral_action: Sally finds some discarded food in a dumpster behind the grocery store and serves it to her guests.
immoral_consequence: Sally's guests fall ill the day after the party, and they all have to miss work.

norm: It's good to introduce people to new things.
situation: Jan's mom still uses a flip phone and doesn't use the internet.
intention: Jan wants to decide whether to tell her mom about smart phones.
moral_action: Jan buys her mom a new phone and tells her how to use all of the different features.
moral_consequence: Jan's mom is amazed by the phone, and her life will become more convenient.
immoral_action: Jan doesn't want her mom to think too hard, so she lets her continue using her flip phone.
immoral_consequence: Jan's mom is missing out on a better experience and others will judge her.

norm: Planting trees is good.
situation: Mandy lives in a house with its backyard facing the west, so it is very hot in the summer.
intention: Mandy wants to improve the hot condition in her backyard.
moral_action: Mandy grows her favorite Lilac tree and Sugar Maple Tree in her backyard which provide plenty of shade.
moral_consequence: Mandy feels refreshed and cooled down when she visits the backyard.
immoral_action: Mandy installs a gazebo in her backyard which costs her several thousand dollars.
immoral_consequence: Mandy runs out of money at the end of the month, and she feels frustrated.

norm: It's bad to disobey your parents.
situation: Natalie and Robert are outside with their son, Ian, who wants to go to the old dock by the lake, but his parents told him that it’s too dangerous.
intention: Ian wants to get a closer look at the water.
moral_action: Ian asks Natalie and Robert if he can stand near the water next to the dock, and they allow him.
moral_consequence: Ian is satisfied because he is still able to get a good view of the water.
immoral_action: When Natalie and Robert aren't paying attention, Ian goes on the dock anyway.
immoral_consequence: The dock breaks under Ian's feet, and he falls in the water.

norm: It's wrong to intentionally drug someone
situation: Bill meets Susan at a bar and is instantly smitten with her.
intention: Bill wants to sleep with Susan.
moral_action: Bill presents his best self to Susan and asks her if she'd like to leave the bar with him.
moral_consequence: Susan may say yes and start a wonderful relationship with Bill.
immoral_action: Bill slips a rufie in Susan's drink when she goes to the bathroom, then carries her to his car.
immoral_consequence: Susan will be scarred and Bill may go to jail.

norm: You shouldn't assault your partner.
situation: Sam is a fiery woman who has just been infuriated by her partner's rude comments.
intention: Sam wants to set her partner straight.
moral_action: Sam refuses to talk to her partner for a long time unless he apologizes.
moral_consequence: Sam's partner realizes how serious she is being and approaches her to make peace.
immoral_action: Sam puts her hands on her partner getting physical with him to get her point across.
immoral_consequence: Sam's partner feels like he is stuck in an abusive relationship.

norm: It is good to call people out for cheating.
situation: John is playing a game with his brother, and he sees that his brother is cheating, then his brother wins the game.
intention: John wants to react to his brother winning the game.
moral_action: John tells his brother that their winning is meaningless because they cheated and that they should be ashamed.
moral_consequence: John's brother is ashamed to have been caught cheating and it serves as a deterrent for them from cheating again.
immoral_action: John accepts that his brother won the game and doesn't tell him that he knows they were cheating.
immoral_consequence: John's brother sees that cheating is a good way to succeed and cheating becomes a habit for them.

norm: Crude jokes are impolite in public.
situation: Bob is at a social function where he doesn't know many people.
intention: Bob wants to break the ice and make friends.
moral_action: Bob joins a group of people talking and tells a funny joke about dogs.
moral_consequence: The other people laugh and Bob makes new friends.
immoral_action: Bob joins a group of people talking and tells a joke based on a racial stereotype.
immoral_consequence: The other people in the group are offended and avoid Bob the rest of the night.

norm: You should admire someone for their skills.
situation: Jamie has joined the art team for a games company and notices another artist named Lyle is very talented.
intention: Jamie wants to react to Lyle's ability.
moral_action: Jamie views Lyle as an inspiration.
moral_consequence: Jamie will be open to learning from Lyle.
immoral_action: Jamie becomes jealous of Lyle's ability.
immoral_consequence: Jamie will become resistant towards learning from Lyle.

norm: You shouldn't hate someone for getting sick a lot.
situation: Rachel is a manager and is annoyed with an employee who has called out too many times in one month.
intention: Rachel wants someone to cover the shift.
moral_action: Rachel considers that some people have weaker immune systems and finds another to cover the shift.
moral_consequence: The employee returns and works hard to make up for lost time.
immoral_action: Rachel detests the employee thinking they are lazy and switches her schedule.
immoral_consequence: The employee has trouble getting along with Rachel in the future.

norm: It's wrong to rob a store.
situation: Ben is at the local grocery store a few hours after losing his job.
intention: Ben wants a way to get extra money.
moral_action: Ben asks the manager of the store if they are hiring.
moral_consequence: Ben fills out an application and starts working at the store the next day.
immoral_action: Ben holds up the cashier at the store and tells them to empty the register.
immoral_consequence: Ben is arrested by the police the next day for robbing the store.

norm: Road rage is not acceptable.
situation: Brandon is on the highway when another car starts honking at him.
intention: Brandon wants to respond to the honker.
moral_action: Brandon slows down and moves to a lane further from the honking car.
moral_consequence: Brandon defuses the situation and is able to keep the highway safe.
immoral_action: Brandon honks back at the honking car and swerves at them.
immoral_consequence: Brandon might cause an accident on the highway.

norm: It is fun to do something with your friend.
situation: Len is at home relaxing when his friend Randy calls to ask him to come play baseball.
intention: Len wants to tell Randy how he feels about baseball.
moral_action: Len tells Randy he loves baseball and that he'll meet him at the diamond in the park.
moral_consequence: Randy is delighted and excited both to see his friend and to play some baseball.
immoral_action: Len tells Randy he hates baseball, and he doesn't want to come out, he'll stay home instead.
immoral_consequence: Randy is annoyed that Len doesn't want to hang out with him and play a fun sport and thinks Len is weird.

norm: It is rude to be loud and disturbing others.
situation: Bob is at a restaurant and gets into a disagreement with a friend.
intention: Bob wants to argue with his friend.
moral_action: Bob and his friend go outside and argue in the parking lot.
moral_consequence: The guests don't hear the argument and enjoy their meal.
immoral_action: Bob stand up and argues with his friend in the restaurant.
immoral_consequence: The other guests get annoyed and the employees ask them to leave.

norm: It's rude to make people angry.
situation: John was at work busy on some work assignment for his boss when Tim comes in.
intention: Tim wants to talk to John.
moral_action: Tim talks to John, and he points out that someone left the copy machine on.
moral_consequence: John runs to the copy machine and shuts it off to save the company the electricity.
immoral_action: Tim starts pestering John over and over again until he starts paying attention to Tim.
immoral_consequence: John is now annoyed with Tim and his antics at getting attention.

norm: You shouldn't hit kids.
situation: Dave and his wife Wendy are in the living room when they witness their son Max stealing money from Wendy's purse.
intention: Dave wants to reprimand Max.
moral_action: Dave tells Max to put the money back immediately and to apologize to his mother and that he's grounded.
moral_consequence: Max understands his father's reaction and apologizes and learns to never do it again.
immoral_action: Dave runs up to Max and slaps him in the face, demanding that Max puts the money back right away.
immoral_consequence: Max is shocked at the slap and terrified of further violence and starts to cry.

norm: It's good to clean your hands after petting someone's animal.
situation: After rubbing his hands on Greg's cat for an hour, Nick is feeling hungry.
intention: Nick wants to get something to eat.
moral_action: Nick washes his hands and makes a sandwich.
moral_consequence: Nick becomes full from the meal.
immoral_action: Nick grabs an apple and eats it.
immoral_consequence: Nick gets sick.

norm: It's wrong to abuse someone.
situation: Carlos has just realized that his girlfriend scratched his car when she borrowed it.
intention: Carlos wants to make sure his girlfriend doesn't scratch his car again.
moral_action: Carlos talks to his girlfriend about the importance of paying attention while driving.
moral_consequence: Carlos's girlfriend offers to pay the cost of fixing the paint on the car.
immoral_action: Carlos beats his girlfriend after he notices the scratches on his car.
immoral_consequence: The police are called and Carlos has to go to jail for domestic abuse.

norm: It is mean to stop talking to your mother
situation: Phil was grounded by his mother for his report card, which Phil claims was wrong.
intention: Phil wants to get revenge on his mother for the unfair punishment.
moral_action: Phil continues to insist that the report card was wrong and refuses any punishement.
moral_consequence: Sure enough, the school calls to inform his mother that his report card was for another student named Phil.
immoral_action: "Phil refused to talk to his mother at all, only giving silence and listening to instructions other than ""talk""."
immoral_consequence: Phil succeeded in hurting his mother's feelings but that only keeps him grounded longer.

norm: You shouldn't walk out on your job.
situation: Tony has been working a new job for a few months and is growing to hate it.
intention: Tony wants to quit his job.
moral_action: Tony puts in his two week notice.
moral_consequence: Tony's employer offers him a severance package and encourages him to use them as a reference for his next job.
immoral_action: Tony gets fed up and walks out of his job.
immoral_consequence: Tony gets blacklisted in his industry for leaving his job in an unprofessional manner.

norm: You shouldn't hate fat people.
situation: Scott is a high school student and sits down with a group of friends who are talking about other classmates.
intention: Scott wants to make a comment about a classmates.
moral_action: Scott brings up a female classmate he thinks is cute and funny.
moral_consequence: Scott's friends tease him in a friendly manner and Scott enjoys it.
immoral_action: Scott starts to lay into an overweight classmate and tells his friends that is the sole reason he doesn't care for that classmate.
immoral_consequence: Scott's friends find it rude that Scott would dismiss somebody just because of their weight and Scott feels awful.

norm: It's wrong to think you know everything.
situation: Amber is at the doctor's office with what has been diagnosed as a broken leg.
intention: Amber wants to take an active part in her wellness.
moral_action: Amber follows the doctor's advice despite questioning it, does more research, and combines alternative and conventional medicine to heal.
moral_consequence: Amber feels  empowered by using her home cures in combination with conventional treatment.
immoral_action: Amber tells the doctor that she thinks it might not be broken and that she would like to try and use essential oils on it first.
immoral_consequence: Ambre is confident about her oils but the bone sets improperly as Amber waited too long to get medical attention, and she is left with pain for life.

norm: You have to be understanding of people's different mental abilities.
situation: Stan is a teacher and has a poorly-performing student, who has some mental issues and tries very hard, in one of his classes.
intention: Stan wants the student to improve.
moral_action: Stan talks with the student and makes arrangements for the student to get tutoring.
moral_consequence: The student slowly improves his grades over time.
immoral_action: Stan has a talk with the student and tells him to shape up and try harder.
immoral_consequence: The student gets exasperated and cries out of frustration, as he's already trying very hard.

norm: It's good to pray when you're religious.
situation: Mike wakes up early and has an hour before the day starts.
intention: Mike wants to do some religious activites.
moral_action: Mike prays and asks God for help with his day.
moral_consequence: Mike develops a personal relationship with God.
immoral_action: Mike reads a spiritual book written by a guru.
immoral_consequence: Mike enjoys the book, but fails to connect with God.

norm: Parents should get their kids the gifts that they want.
situation: Dave's daughter Kim had previously asked Dave for a bike for her birthday and now Dave is in the store shopping.
intention: Dave wants to decide what to buy.
moral_action: Dave finds the exact bike that Kim wanted and takes it to the cash register to buy it.
moral_consequence: Kim is delighted that she got the exact bike she wanted and happily runs outside to ride it right away.
immoral_action: Dave sees some books that he thinks would be useful for Kim's development and decides to buy them for her.
immoral_consequence: Kim begins to cry when she sees she was given a bizarre present for her birthday and thinks her dad doesn't love her.

norm: You shouldn't take money from someone else.
situation: Sal is on the bus when he spots a twenty dollar bill sticking out of a sleeping mans pocket.
intention: Sal wants to go see a movie.
moral_action: Sal resists the urge to steal and buys a movie ticket with his own money.
moral_consequence: Sal feels good about himself for not taking something that doesn't belong to him and being self sufficient.
immoral_action: Sal grabs the twenty dollar bill and uses it to see a movie at the local theater.
immoral_consequence: Sal feels like a scumbag for taking money instead of just buying the ticket with his own money.

norm: It's wrong to mistreat your pets.
situation: Frank is at home with his pet dog who just chewed up his slipper.
intention: Frank wants to teach his dog not to chew slippers.
moral_action: Frank buys his dog a chew toy and researches how to train his dog to leave his slipper alone.
moral_consequence: Frank's dog is happy and jovial with his new chew toy which is the only thing it chews on now.
immoral_action: Frank roles up a newspaper and uses it on his dog until it runs.
immoral_consequence: Frank's dog lives a miserable and frightened life in constant fear of what Frank will do to it.

norm: You can't expect everyone to like dogs.
situation: Jeff has a pet great dane named Bowser that he brings along with him to a house party.
intention: Jeff wants Bowser to meet the people at the party.
moral_action: Jeff takes Bowser along with him on a leash as he hangs out at the party.
moral_consequence: Bowser loves the attention he gets from the dog enthusiasts at the party, and many guests enjoy having him there.
immoral_action: Jeff lets Bowser off the leash when he gets to the party.
immoral_consequence: Bowser runs around wildly at the house party, scaring some of the guests.

norm: You shouldn't squeal on people.
situation: Tom notices his wife underpaid her restaurant bill yesterday, but the waitress didn't notice.
intention: Tom wants to let someone know about the underpaid bill.
moral_action: Tom forgives his wife and only tells his wife about the underpaid bill instead of the restaurant.
moral_consequence: Tom's wife thanks Tom for letting her know and is relieved he didn't make a big deal out of it.
immoral_action: Tom calls the restaurant on the phone letting them know that his wife underpaid.
immoral_consequence: Tom's wife becomes furious at Tom for squealing on her, and feels she doesn't have to explain herself.

norm: No one respects a disloyal friend.
situation: Greg was hanging out with his friends at the mall when a popular jock asked him to come with his friends instead.
intention: Greg has to pick who he wants to hang out with.
moral_action: Greg tells the jocks that he's hanging out with his friends, so he's not leaving.
moral_consequence: Greg's friends feel better about Greg and trust him more.
immoral_action: Greg decides to hang out with the jocks and leaves his friends.
immoral_consequence: Greg's friends feel betrayed and don't like him as much as they used to.

norm: It's good to support someone's business.
situation: Becky looks in the mirror and thinks her hair looks bad.
intention: Becky wants a haircut.
moral_action: Becky goes to her usual stylist at the salon.
moral_consequence: Becky feels good because her hair turned out well, and she helped a small business stay afloat.
immoral_action: Becky decides to skip going to her usual salon and save some money by cutting her own hair.
immoral_consequence: Becky feels bad because her hair looks bad, and she didn't help her stylist make money.

norm: You shouldn't hook up with an ex's best friend.
situation: Austin has plans to hang out with Jackie, whose best friend is Tiffany, Austin's ex-girlfriend.
intention: Austin wants to spend time with Jackie.
moral_action: Austin and Jackie play some old video games in Jackie's living room.
moral_consequence: Jackie feels nostalgic about the games she played as a kid.
immoral_action: While hanging out, Austin and Jackie have sex in her room.
immoral_consequence: Jackie feels as if she's betrayed Tiffany by having sex with Austin.

norm: Using refillable containers for drinking is good.
situation: Sam just arrived with his water bottle at a drinking stand with plastic cups from a long hike and is very thirsty.
intention: Sam wants to drink water.
moral_action: Sam fills his water bottle and drinks from it.
moral_consequence: Other people can use the cups that Sam left.
immoral_action: Sam fills and drinks several plastic cups worth of water.
immoral_consequence: The garbage is more full and the cups are wasted.

norm: It's wrong to be happy that a celebrity died.
situation: James, who always hated Michael Jackson's music and was very disturbed by the allegations against the singer, just found out he died.
intention: James wants to avoid Michael Jackson-related content on social media.
moral_action: James turns off social media and goes for a walk in the park to distract himself.
moral_consequence: The natural beauty around him rapidly distracts James from his negative thoughts about Michael Jackson.
immoral_action: "James posts, ""Don't send me any Michael Jackson articles - I'm glad he's dead""."
immoral_consequence: James' friends bombard him with outraged emails, and he has to disconnect from social media.

norm: It is rude to block the grocery isle.
situation: Alexa is starting a new diet and is shopping for groceries to help her stay on track.
intention: Hailey wants to make sure everything she buys is low in carbs.
moral_action: Hailey puts a can in her cart and walks to the end of the isle to check the ingredient label.
moral_consequence: Others are able to navigate the isle effectively without being blocked by Hailey.
immoral_action: Hailey picks up a can of soup and studies the label intently while standing in the middle of the isle with her cart.
immoral_consequence: A family with kids is stuck behind her and the children end up knocking over several cans from a shelf.

norm: You shouldn't write in other people's diaries.
situation: Ali is at Kamryn's house when she sees Kamryn's diary sitting next to her bed.
intention: Ali wants to play a prank on Kamryn.
moral_action: When Kamryn goes to the bathroom, Ali uses lipstick to make kissy lips on Kamryn's mirror.
moral_consequence: Kamryn laughs when she sees the lip print on the mirror.
immoral_action: "When Kamryn goes to the bathroom, Ali opens up Kamryn's diary, reads a few pages, and then writes ""Ali was here"" on the next empty page."
immoral_consequence: Kamryn is mortified that night when she realizes that Ali had looked in her diary.

norm: It is good to apologize to others.
situation: Ree and her best friend Hayley are drunk at a party when they get into an argument.
intention: Ree wants to leave the party.
moral_action: Ree leaves the party and sends Hayley an apology text the following morning once she's sobered up.
moral_consequence: Hayley apologizes to Ree as well, and they get on speaking terms again.
immoral_action: Ree leaves the party and never apologizes to Hayley going forward.
immoral_consequence: Ree and Hayley never speak again.

norm: It's good to have your friends over sometimes.
situation: Linda would love to have a cookout over the coming weekend, but isn't sure.
intention: Linda has to decide whether to have a cookout or rest over the weekend.
moral_action: Linda spends her energy inviting people over for a cookout and asks everyone to bring something.
moral_consequence: Linda has an amazing and relaxing time at the cookout, and she feels rejuvenated when she goes back to work on Monday.
immoral_action: Linda settles in with movies and popcorn for the whole weekend and doesn't have any friends over.
immoral_consequence: Linda feels lazy and lonely at the end of the weekend, wishing she had taken some time to socialize before returning to work for the week.

norm: It's bad to have anger issues.
situation: Mitch is the boss of a company, and lately his employees have been slacking off.
intention: Mitch wants his employees to work harder.
moral_action: Mitch explains that he needs them to work harder and asks for advice on how to get them to be more efficient.
moral_consequence: Mitch's employees become better workers, and Mitch's company makes more money.
immoral_action: Mitch gets very animated with his employees and loudly tells them that they will be fired if they don't shape up.
immoral_consequence: Mitch's employees quit because of the stress, and Mitch has problems finding people to work for him due to his reputation.

norm: It's expected that you place your family first.
situation: Max is with his parents in a theme park and loves the rides.
intention: Max wants to go on the roller coaster.
moral_action: Max brings his parents to a roller coaster, and they ride together.
moral_consequence: Max's parents thank Max for the time together and Max feels accomplished.
immoral_action: Max jumps into the line of a roller coaster without consulting his parents first.
immoral_consequence: Max feels overwhelmed at being alone and his parents fear for him.

norm: You should always be concerned about your child's health.
situation: Sue's daughter Julie has been losing weight at a dramatic rate and failing her classes due to drug use.
intention: Sue wants to ask Julie what's been going on with her.
moral_action: Sue asks Julie if something has been going on in her life that she would like to talk about and ends up finding out about Julie’s drug habit.
moral_consequence: Julie checks into rehab with the help of Sue, and they are Sue is relived that she got her daughter much needed help.
immoral_action: Sue asks if Julie is losing weight to look pretty for a boy, without trying to dig deeper.
immoral_consequence: Julie ends up in the hospital from an obvious drug overdose and now Sue wishes she got her daughter the help she needed.

norm: It's wrong to buy an underage person cigarettes.
situation: Matthew asks his older brother Larry for a cigarette after the death of their mother.
intention: Larry wants to make Matthew feel better.
moral_action: Larry takes his younger brother to the arcade to distract him.
moral_consequence: Matthew beats his high score in his favorite arcade game.
immoral_action: Larry gives his younger brother a cigarette.
immoral_consequence: Matthew starts smoking as a habit, and he eventually develops lung cancer.

norm: You should not leave dirty laundry laying around.
situation: After exercising, an energetic  Usama walks into his room littered with his dirty clothes and trash.
intention: Usama wants to do something productive.
moral_action: Usama cleans his room placing all of his dirty clothes into a basket and tosses the trash into the trashcan.
moral_consequence: Usama's mental state improves from being in a clean room.
immoral_action: Usama organizes the massive number of files on his computer.
immoral_consequence: Usama is unable to find his favorite shirt due to all of the mess in his room.

norm: It's wrong to manipulate your friends for your own benefit.
situation: Dana is out at a restaurant with her friends for the night.
intention: Dana doesn't want to spend too much money.
moral_action: Dana only orders lower priced items to save money.
moral_consequence: Dana's friends will feel Dana is responsible with her money.
immoral_action: When it is time to pay the bill Dana says she forgot her wallet so her friends cover her.

situation: Greg is at home with his wife Claire when they get the news that Greg's dad has passed away.
intention: Greg wants to express his grief to Claire.
moral_action: Greg tells Claire that he's devastated, that his dad meant a lot to him and that it'll take him time to get over this.
moral_consequence: Claire understands Greg is hurt deeply by his father's passing and hugs him to give him some comfort.
immoral_action: Greg tells Claire that he's devastated, that his dad was everything and that he wants to kill himself.
immoral_consequence: Claire is freaked out by Greg's suicidal thoughts and starts to panic as to how to deal with it.

norm: It's wrong to root for the enemies of America.
situation: Tim is talking with his friends about a recent terrorist attack on America.
intention: Tim wants to give his opinion.
moral_action: Tim says that the terrorists were wrong to use violence on people.
moral_consequence: Tim's friends will think Tim has a well adjusted moral compass.
immoral_action: Tim says the terrorists had a point and were justified.
immoral_consequence: Tim's friends will think Tim is a traitor to America.

norm: It's kind to buy a gift for someone you love.
situation: John's wife Mindy wants a diamond ring for her birthday.
intention: John wants to grow his savings account.
moral_action: John puts some of his paycheck in savings and uses some to buy Mindy a cheaper diamond ring.
moral_consequence: Mindy is very happy and loves John a lot.
immoral_action: John puts all his paycheck in his savings account and doesn't buy Mindy a gift.
immoral_consequence: Mindy feels sad and unloved.

norm: It's good to discipline children.
situation: Carol and Tom have two children together but Tom always lets the children get away with they do wrong.
intention: Carol wants the children to be better behaved.
moral_action: Carol talks to Tom about the importance of making sure the children act good, and they act as a team when addressing the children's behavior issues.
moral_consequence: The children learn they will have to face punishment when they intentionally do wrong and become productive adult members of society.
immoral_action: Carol follows along with Tom's preferences in not disciplining the children, leaving it to teachers and family to make them act better.
immoral_consequence: The children grow up getting into a large amount of trouble and don't respect Carol and Tom.

norm: It's dishonest to cheat on your significant other
situation: Dave who is married to Ann is at a club with some friends when he's approached by a gorgeous woman who asks him to come home with her.
intention: Dave wants to answer the woman's proposal.
moral_action: Dave tells the woman  that while she's beautiful he cannot go home with her since he's promised to someone else.
moral_consequence: Ann finds out from the friends that Dave said no, and she is ecstatic that she has such a loyal and loving partner.
immoral_action: Dave tells the woman that she is amazingly beautiful and that he would love to come home with her.
immoral_consequence: Ann finds out from the friends that Dave violated their relationship and is really angry with him and feels used.

norm: You shouldn't pack things you don't need.
situation: Sally is going on vacation with her partner, and they are currently packing their bags.
intention: Sally wants to make sure she takes everything she needs.
moral_action: Sally makes an organized list of everything that they will need.
moral_consequence: Sally's partner finds the list very helpful as it reminds him to pack some things.
immoral_action: Sally packs as many things as she can into her bags.
immoral_consequence: Sally's partner thinks she is taking too long and becomes annoyed with her.

norm: It's always good to be on time.
situation: Steve was getting ready to go to work for his first day on his new job.
intention: Steve wants to go to work.
moral_action: Steve leaves the house early and makes sure that he goes straight to work to get there on time.
moral_consequence: Steve gets to work a few minutes early and the boss is impressed with his punctuality.
immoral_action: Steve takes his time getting ready and stops at the coffee shop for an hour before work.
immoral_consequence: Steve arrives to work late and the boss is not impressed with him.

norm: It's good to get along with your neighbors.
situation: Mary is on her way out when she notices her neighbor approaching.
intention: Mary wants to leave.
moral_action: Mary stops and helps her neighbor look for their lost dog.
moral_consequence: Mary's neighbor mows her lawn for her later that week in appreciation.
immoral_action: Mary jumps in her car and ignores her neighbor.
immoral_consequence: Mary's neighbor tells the other neighbors how rude she is.

norm: It's rude to tell people they are crazy.
situation: During a debate about politics, George's friend Tom says something that he finds incorrect and outlandish.
intention: George wants Tom to know he is wrong.
moral_action: George uses logic and reasoning to explain to Tom why the views that he expressed are flawed.
moral_consequence: Tom realizes that he was wrong and thanks George for correcting him.
immoral_action: George raises his voice and tells Tom that he is crazy and his views are ridiculous.
immoral_consequence: Tom gets defensive and doubles down on his views regardless of their validity.

norm: It is good to be courteous to other people
situation: Bill has stopped for lunch at a fast food restaurant, which is a bit busy; the clerk looks quite flustered.
intention: Bill wants to get his lunch quickly and get back to work.
moral_action: "Bill smiles at the clerk and says, ""I understand you're very busy, I can relate to how you're feeling""."
moral_consequence: The clerk calms down a bit and remembers to put everything in the bag.
immoral_action: Bill thinks the clerk is too slow and makes snide comments out loud.
immoral_consequence: The clerk is even more flustered, and forgets to include napkins and ketchup in the bag they give Bill.

norm: You should support your friends in their pursuits.
situation: Jamie's friend Faye has taken up painting and shows her a painting she has worked on that looks pretty bad.
intention: Jamie wants to give feedback on the painting.
moral_action: Jamie says that she likes Faye's effort and feels she can improve the painting with practice.
moral_consequence: Faye appreciates Jamie's encouragement and becomes a great painter after a few years.
immoral_action: Jamie says based on what she sees, Faye should give up painting.
immoral_consequence: Faye feels bad and starts to cry.

norm: You should participate in extracurricular activities if you're a child.
situation: Joe is a 12 year old kid with not many friends, and he's just starting the school year.
intention: Joe wants to do something to have fun.
moral_action: Joe joins a drama team since he always liked watching movies.
moral_consequence: Joe makes new friends and finds a new interest in life.
immoral_action: Joe plays video games every time he comes home from work.
immoral_consequence: Joe isn't able to make any close friends while playing video games.

norm: It's good to be there with family.
situation: Dave is planning a fishing trip on Sunday when he's told by his mother that she's throwing together a family gathering the same day.
intention: Dave wants to decide whether to cancel the fishing trip.
moral_action: Dave tells his mom that he'll cancel the fishing trip since family is more important to him, and he'll be there.
moral_consequence: Dave's mom is delighted to hear that her son will be attending and that her plans are coming together.
immoral_action: Dave tells his mom that since the fishing trip was planned first, it has priority, and he won't be able to attend.
immoral_consequence: Dave's mom is sad that her son won't prioritize her family and is stressed her gathering won't go as planned.

norm: It's bad to cancel on someone with little advance notice.
situation: Steve has a date scheduled with Mandy, but finds out he has to work on their date night.
intention: Steve wants to cancel the date.
moral_action: Steve cancels the date as soon as he finds out he has to work.
moral_consequence: Mandy agrees to reschedule the date, and they have a nice time together.
immoral_action: Steve waits until a few minutes before the date to tell Mandy he can't make it.
immoral_consequence: Mandy is annoyed and decided she doesn't want to see Steve anymore.

norm: It's good to inform your landlord of problems.
situation: Tom has his hours cut at the restaurant that he works at because of the pandemic.
intention: Tom wants to be able to maintain a place to live.
moral_action: Tom explains his work situation to his landlord, who agrees to allow Tom extra time to pay his rent over the coming months.
moral_consequence: Tom is able to slowly pay back his landlord when his restaurant reopens for business again.
immoral_action: Tom starts selling weed to get money to pay his rent.
immoral_consequence: Tom gets busted selling dope and gets arrested.

norm: It's wrong to be antisemitic.
situation: Jerome was answering questions by the media after his pro basketball game.
intention: Jerome wanted to show his displeasure with the media.
moral_action: Jerome informs the reports he won't be answering questions and leaves the room abruptly.
moral_consequence: Jerome shows his anger at the media without suffering any backlash.
immoral_action: Jerome goes on a rant about how Jews and Zionist pigs control the publishing industry.
immoral_consequence: Jerome is fined by the basketball team and suspended for 10 games without pay.

norm: It's wrong to not invite family to your wedding.
situation: Sam and his girlfriend are getting married, but she doesn't like his family.
intention: Sam wants to have the best wedding possible.
moral_action: Sam invites his family to the wedding and makes sure that his girlfriend invites her family as well.
moral_consequence: Everyone has a great time, and they have a wonderful wedding.
immoral_action: Sam decides to have a small wedding and only invite close friends.
immoral_consequence: Sam's family is very upset and disowns him.

norm: You shouldn't judge someone's body weight.
situation: Sally is starting a new school today.
intention: Sally wants to meet new people.
moral_action: Sally sees an overweight boy being made fun of by some girls and tells them to leave him alone.
moral_consequence: The boy appreciates Sally standing up for him and the two become good friends.
immoral_action: Sally sees some girls making fun of an overweight boy and joins in and laughs with the others.
immoral_consequence: The boy has his feelings hurt and Sally feels guilty afterwards.

norm: You should support someone who is struggleing in school.
situation: Carl is a teacher, and Bill, one of his students whose home life has been deteriorating, has started getting bad grades.
intention: Carl wants to let Bill know about his grades slipping.
moral_action: Carl asks Bill about his academic decline and helps him out when he finds out about Bill's home life.
moral_consequence: Bill's grades rise back up, and Bill graduates with a high GPA.
immoral_action: Carl warns Bill about his grades, but does not inquire about Bill's academic decline.
immoral_consequence: Bill continues to struggle and ends up flunking out of school.

norm: It's not okay to go chopping down trees.
situation: Edward becomes upset that his neighbor's tree has become so overgrown that it obstructs his view of the lake.
intention: Edward wants the overgrown tree out of the way of his lake view.
moral_action: Edward goes to his neighbor and explains that the tree is blocking his view of the lake and would like it trimmed.
moral_consequence: Edward's neighbor listens to his complaint, and they have a rational conversation about how to solve the problem.
immoral_action: Edward gets his chainsaw out of his shed and proceeds to cut down the neighbor's tree, low on the trunk.
immoral_consequence: Edward's neighbor becomes very upset, and he calls the police to file a report about the destruction of his property.

norm: You shouldn't act oddly around others.
situation: Seth was in the grocery store looking at some products on the shelf.
intention: Seth wants to pick up a can of corn.
moral_action: Seth picks up a can of corn and puts it into the cart.
moral_consequence: The manager of the store offers to ring up Seth himself.
immoral_action: Seth picks up cans of corn from the shelves and starts to make a tower with them.
immoral_consequence: The manager of the store sees Seth and asks him to leave the store.

norm: You shouldn't be toxic toward your kids.
situation: Mary is bitter about her husbands repeated infidelity when her son asks her why she is so angry with his dad.
intention: Mary wants to answer her son's question.
moral_action: Mary assures her son that her disagreement with his father doesn't impact their love for him.
moral_consequence: Mary is able to separate her son from her problems with his father.
immoral_action: Mary tells her son about his father’s history with women in great detail.
immoral_consequence: Mary alienates her son from his father.

norm: It's good to end a toxic relationship
situation: Tim and Amy don't get along that well, but Tim stays with her because of their kids.
intention: Tim wants to decide what to do with his marriage.
moral_action: Tim decides to split with Amy and agrees to split time watching the kids.
moral_consequence: Tim is much happier, and he still gets to spend time with his kids.
immoral_action: Tim decided it would be better to stay in the relationship.
immoral_consequence: Tim continues to be unhappy, and the kids know their parents aren't getting along.

norm: It's wrong to look at someone else's test.
situation: Lindsay is taking a math test when she encounters a problem that is stumping her.
intention: Lindsay wants to figure out how to do the problem.
moral_action: Lindsay tries to remember her lessons on how to solve the problem.
moral_consequence: Lindsay will be able to recall how to solve the problem.
immoral_action: Lindsay looks over at another student to see how they did the problem.
immoral_consequence: Lindsay will be caught by her teacher and punished for cheating.

norm: It's good to eat fruit.
situation: Max has never eaten fruit before so his friend offered him some watermelon.
intention: Max wants to try the watermeloon.
moral_action: Max eats the watermelon and finds out that he actually likes it quite a bit.
moral_consequence: Max starts eating more fruits and is happier with a healthier body.
immoral_action: Max takes a bite of the watermelon and then proceeds to spit it out.
immoral_consequence: Max continues to eat unhealthy and never tries a fruit again.

norm: Bringing people gifts is a good gesture.
situation: Ted is invited to dinner at the house of a married couple he knows.
intention: Ted wants to go to the married couple's house for dinner.
moral_action: Ted shows up for dinner at the couple's house with a nice bottle of red wine for them.
moral_consequence: The couple are charmed by Ted's nice gift of wine and share it at dinner.
immoral_action: Ted goes to the couple's house for dinner without bringing anything as a gift for them.
immoral_consequence: The couple thinks Ted isn't very polite since he didn't bring even a small gift to show his appreciation for being invited.

norm: It's wrong to mooch off other people all the time.
situation: Jackie watches her traditional boyfriend Jared fumble around his wallet for cash to pay for their meal.
intention: Jackie wants to avoid an embarrassing situation with the waitress.
moral_action: Jackie hands her card to the waitress before Jared can respond.
moral_consequence: Jared starts relying on Jackie more often.
immoral_action: Jackie tells Jared to  put the meal on his credit card.
immoral_consequence: Jared has to pay overdraft fees.

norm: It's good to work to make your marriage work.
situation: John and his wife Mary have been having an increasing amount of conflict and tension in their relationship.
intention: John wants to resolve the issues he is having with his wife.
moral_action: John seeks marriage counseling and the couple works through their issues in a positive and constructive way.
moral_consequence: John and Mary achieve a stronger and happier marriage that endures their whole lives.
immoral_action: John decides to file for a divorce and moves out of the house.
immoral_consequence: John and Mary are both sad and regretful that they did not make their marriage work.

norm: It is wrong to withhold information from a partner.
situation: Jeff is in a relationship with Tiarah, and they're at the mall shopping.
intention: Jeff needs to give Tiarah feedback on a dress she's considering, which she looks ridiculous in.
moral_action: Jeff suggests she try a different dress as this look might not be for her.
moral_consequence: Tiarah picks a different dress and receives compliments about it the following day.
immoral_action: Jeff tells Tiarah she looks lovely in it.
immoral_consequence: Tiarah wears it to work the following day and her coworkers make fun of her.

norm: Parents are expected to treat their children well.
situation: Helen's two kids hadn't been eating much and had started to lose weight.
intention: Helen wants her kids to gain weight.
moral_action: Helen keeps her kids hydrated and schedules them to see the doctor.
moral_consequence: Helen's kids are given a kid friendly diet rich with nutrients, and they start to gain weight.
immoral_action: Helen gives her kids chocolate every morning for breakfast and chips for lunch.
immoral_consequence: Helen's kids continue to lose weight, and they are visited by child protection services.

norm: It's disgusting to try to control your partner.
situation: Florence and Bobby haven't had much time together since Bobby accepted more hours at work and Florence is frustrated.
intention: Florence wants Bobby to be home more often.
moral_action: Florence asks Bobby if he could schedule more time for just the two of them.
moral_consequence: Bobby makes schedule alterations to spend more time with Florence without hurting his income.
immoral_action: Florence writes in to Bobby's job about his poor customer service resulting in Bobby losing his hours.
immoral_consequence: A few weeks after losing his hours, Bobby discovers a draft of Florence's writing and breaks up with her for sabotaging him.

norm: It's bad to enter property that you aren't allowed in.
situation: Jake is walking home when he sees what looks like a shortcut that goes through an area that is marked as private property.
intention: Jake wants to continue on his way.
moral_action: Jake decides not to enter private property and continues along the public road.
moral_consequence: Jake gets home eventually without any misadventures on the way.
immoral_action: Jake continues through the private property although he doesn't know who the property belongs to.
immoral_consequence: The owner of the property calls the police and Jake is charged with trespassing.

norm: It's wrong to lie to others about things you like.
situation: Carl is getting to know a girl he just met, and they are sharing interests.
intention: Carl wants to make a good impression on the girl.
moral_action: Carl expresses some interest in listening to her favorite band.
moral_consequence: The girl is excited because he seems open to listening to her music.
immoral_action: Carl says that he likes her favorite band when he's never listened to them before.
immoral_consequence: The girl finds out that he lied, and she loses interest in him.

norm: You shouldn't bug people to do things.
situation: Nancy noticed that her roommate Amber didn't clean up the kitchen after she cooked, and Amber is working on a work project.
intention: Nancy wants the kitchen cleaned.
moral_action: Nancy offers to clean the kitchen for her roommate in exchange for another chore.
moral_consequence: Amber feels glad that Nancy respects her.
immoral_action: Nancy drops by Amber's roommate's room asking her to clean the kitchen every thirty minutes.
immoral_consequence: Amber leaves the apartment to get away from Nancy.

norm: It's bad to cheat to get ahead.
situation: Jenna's boss promised her a bonus if she could complete ten house inspections in one week.
intention: Jenna wants to earn the bonus.
moral_action: Jenna works lots of overtime to thoroughly inspect all ten of the houses.
moral_consequence: Jenna's boss gives her the bonus and tells her he'll remember her hard work at bonus time.
immoral_action: Jenna only glances at the last two houses but fills out the paperwork like she did a thorough inspection.
immoral_consequence: Jenna gets her bonus, and by the time overlooked damage is discovered in one of the houses, she's moved to a new job in a new state.

norm: It's good to be unique.
situation: Bekah is creating a resume of her experience so that she can apply for jobs.
intention: She wants to decide how to design her resume.
moral_action: Bekah spices up her resume a bit and tries to make it reflect her personality.
moral_consequence: Bekah gets a lot of calls from interested companies who felt her resume stood apart from the pack.
immoral_action: Bekah designs her resume in a very traditional way, closely following templates she finds online.
immoral_consequence: Bekah has trouble getting noticed because her resume doesn't stand out from the pack.

norm: It's rude to have bad bedside manners.
situation: Dr. Carlos works in a hospital and realizes that a patient needs to have her appendix removed.
intention: Dr. Carlos wants to inform the patient.
moral_action: Dr. Carlos tells the patient that her appendix needs to be removed and stays for 20 minutes to answer her questions.
moral_consequence: The patient's fears are relieved, and she is ready to go into surgery.
immoral_action: Dr. Carlos tells the patient that her appendix needs to come out, tells her the scheduled surgery time, and leaves.
immoral_consequence: The patient is very afraid and has a lot of unanswered questions and concerns.

norm: It is wrong to steal someone's identity
situation: Tony finds a wallet on the ground when he is walking through the park.
intention: Tony wants to see who the wallet belongs to.
moral_action: Tony looks up the address listed on the driver's license he finds in the wallet.
moral_consequence: Tony is given a hundred dollar reward for the return of the wallet.
immoral_action: Tony takes the driver's license from the wallet and uses the information on it to create a new identity.
immoral_consequence: Tony is later arrested by the police when he is trying to buy things online using the false information.

norm: It's good to take your kids to the zoo.
situation: Mae is at home with her kids on a Saturday afternoon but her kids are bored.
intention: Mae wants to find something for her kids to do.
moral_action: Mae takes her kids to the local zoo to see the elephants.
moral_consequence: Mae's children get their pictures taken while they feed the elephants peanuts.
immoral_action: Mae sits her kids in front of the television and tells them to watch something.
immoral_consequence: Mae's children get into a fight because they each want to watch a different TV program.

norm: It is wrong to ruin someone else's party.
situation: Hank is working on a major project at work and needs help, while Steve is celebrating his birthday.
intention: Hank wants to get a subordinate to help him.
moral_action: Hank finds someone who is bored and orders him to come in.
moral_consequence: Steve enjoys his birthday party.
immoral_action: Hank contacts Steve and orders him to come in or else be fired.
immoral_consequence: Steve is angry with Hank for ruining his birthday.

norm: It's wrong to leave your date alone with the check.
situation: Cedric is at a restaurant with his date Irene and gets an urgent call from his mother asking for help.
intention: Cedric wants to leave so he can help his mother.
moral_action: Cedric leaves $200 on the table in the restaurant before leaving.
moral_consequence: Irene uses the money to pay the bill and tip.
immoral_action: Cedric rushes out of the restaurant without taking care of the bill.
immoral_consequence: Irene has to pay the entire bill and provide a tip on her own.

norm: Using profanity on people is rude.
situation: John is taking a walk in the neighborhood and notices young people playing soccer on the street.
intention: John wants youngsters not to play on the street.
moral_action: John approaches the youngsters calmly and advise them to play in the nearby park.
moral_consequence: John gets thanks and the players leave the street peacefully.
immoral_action: John screams and swears at the young people ordering them off the street.
immoral_consequence: The young people get offended and attack John causing serious harm before running away.

norm: You shouldn't blame new employees for everything.
situation: Gadah is at a convention with the two newest employees in the company and their presentation is sub par.
intention: Gadah wants to rise up the corporate ladder.
moral_action: Gadah assumes accountability for the poor performance and the group greatly improves the next time around.
moral_consequence: Gadah is praised for her leadership and given a promotion.
immoral_action: Gadah blames their poor presentation on the newbies and boasts about her own accomplishments.
immoral_consequence: Gadah's team does not want to work with her in the future.

norm: It's wrong to scam money from people.
situation: Craig is out of a job and has a computer with a good internet connection at home.
intention: Craig wants to earn money from home.
moral_action: Craig signs up for some online survey sites and does surveys.
moral_consequence: The survey creators get usable data from Craig's work.
immoral_action: Craig runs a Nigerian email scam and gathers people's account numbers, then takes their money for himself.
immoral_consequence: The people that give their account numbers lose their savings and have a hard time surviving.

norm: It's wrong to talk to people who have committed murder.
situation: Pam is lonely and is looking for a new boyfriend when she hears about lonely prisoners and decides to meet one.
intention: Pam wants to choose a prisoner to possibly date.
moral_action: Pam connects with a man convicted of a petty crime.
moral_consequence: The man gets out and he and Pam marry.
immoral_action: Pam connects with a convicted murderer, who's in prison for life, and starts seeing him.
immoral_consequence: Pam and the murderer can never have a normal life as he is always in prison.

norm: It's wrong to be bigoted against a group of people.
situation: Jane was raised around only people like her but just moved to a diverse area.
intention: Jane wants to make new friends.
moral_action: Jane focuses on what people are like on the inside rather than the outside when it comes to meeting new friends.
moral_consequence: Jane is exposed to new cultures and all the amazing things they have to offer and has a more fulfilling life experience than she otherwise would have.
immoral_action: Jane only looks to people who are the same background as her and look the same for prospective new friends.
immoral_consequence: Jane misses out on all the interesting things that various cultures and backgrounds of the world have to offer.

norm: You shouldn't refuse to meet your friend's partner.
situation: John and his lifelong best friend are having a conversation on the phone about his best friend's new girlfriend.
intention: John wants to be clear with his friend.
moral_action: John explains to his best friend that even though he feels uncomfortable meeting his new girlfriend, that he will do it for him.
moral_consequence: John's friend thanks John for understanding and appreciates that John will step out of his comfort zone for a friend.
immoral_action: John explains to his best friend his true feeling in that he has no desire to meet his new girlfriend.
immoral_consequence: John's friend his hurt that John doesn't want to meet somebody important to him.

norm: It's good to be well behaved.
situation: Sam is a 5 year old who just finished eating a piece of cake his mother made for dessert.
intention: Sam wants another piece of cake.
moral_action: Sam smiles asks his mother nicely for another piece of cake.
moral_consequence: Sam's mother gives him a small piece of cake which he enjoys eating.
immoral_action: Sam throws a tantrum, yelling, screaming and stomping his feet until his mom gives him more cake.
immoral_consequence: Sam is put in timeout by his mother for misbehaving and doesn't get any cake.

norm: It's good to get your own laundry machines.
situation: Annabelle has a big loan to pay off because she just bought her first home.
intention: Annabelle wants to watch her budget.
moral_action: Annabelle purchases laundry machines for her new home, so she doesn't have to spend time and money going to the laundromat.
moral_consequence: Annabelle saves good money on laundromat and travel costs and is able to devote her free time to other cost savings activities.
immoral_action: Annabelle frequents the laundromat because she thinks buying laundry machines is outside of her budget at the moment.
immoral_consequence: Annabelle spends more in the long run at the laundromat and on travel expenses to it than she would've on her own machines.

norm: It's not okay to miss someone's important events.
situation: Billy's grandmother is having a birthday party at the same time as a football game.
intention: Billy wants to see the football game.
moral_action: Billy goes to the party and records the game to watch later.
moral_consequence: Billy's grandmother is glad that he came to celebrate her birthday.
immoral_action: Billy stays home to watch the football game.
immoral_consequence: Billy's grandmother is sad that he didn't come to the birthday party.

norm: It's rude to laugh when someone dies.
situation: John is at home when his dad calls to tell him that his mother has died suddenly.
intention: John wants to react to the bad news.
moral_action: John tells his father that it's terrible and tells him to hang on since he's on the way over.
moral_consequence: John's father feels a bit of comfort from knowing his son will come be with him.
immoral_action: John instinctively bursts out laughing thinking that it must be a hoax, and he's being tricked.
immoral_consequence: John's father is suddenly taken aback and saddened that John is not taking the horrible news seriously.

norm: It's bad to rely too heavily on technology.
situation: Max is studying for his math exam on Monday.
intention: Max wants to do well on his exam.
moral_action: Max spends hours carefully reading the text book and copying his notes.
moral_consequence: Max does well on his test.
immoral_action: Max enters all of the math formulas into his calculator.
immoral_consequence: Max is unable to answer the short answer questions on the exam because he doesn't know the meaning behind the formulas.

norm: You shouldn't go to college parties if you're underage.
situation: Max is an 18-year-old college freshman and was invited by his roommates to hang out on Friday night.
intention: Max wants to have a fun time.
moral_action: Max and his roommates hang out in their dorm room and play video games.
moral_consequence: Max becomes close with his roommates and they become friends.
immoral_action: Max and his roommates go to a nearby frat party and start partying and drinking.
immoral_consequence: Max is not used to alcohol and gets alcohol poisoning.

norm: It's good to feed your pets to keep them healthy
situation: Riley has a pet greyhound that runs races.
intention: Riley wants to keep his pet slim.
moral_action: Riley feeds his pet a balanced diet to maintain its shape.
moral_consequence: Riley's pet is able to run quickly during races.
immoral_action: Riley starves his pet to maintain its body shape.
immoral_consequence: Riley's pet has health problems from malnutrition.

norm: You should protect others from being harassed.
situation: Oscar sees someone bullying his co-worker at work.
intention: Oscar wants to get back to work in peace.
moral_action: Oscar intervenes in the bullying, telling the bully to leave his co-worker alone.
moral_consequence: The fight stops peacefully and Oscar returns to work.
immoral_action: Oscar goes to another part of the building, so he can't hear the harassment.
immoral_consequence: Oscar's co-worker is assaulted by the other person.

norm: It is impolite to talk about someone behind their back.
situation: Mike is having lunch in his work’s cafeteria with some coworkers when he is asked what he thinks about their boss.
intention: Mike wants to find common ground with his coworkers through conversation.
moral_action: Mike changes the subject stating that he doesn't want to gossip.
moral_consequence: Mike's coworker praises Mike for being honest, and respectful, and their working relationship grows.
immoral_action: Mike shares with his coworkers that he thinks their boss is bad at their job.
immoral_consequence: Mike's coworker tells his boss, and he gets written up for gossiping.

norm: You shouldn't string people along in relationships.
situation: Melinda has been with her boyfriend for years but is tired of their relationship.
intention: Melinda wants to avoid being single.
moral_action: Melinda decides to have a serious discussion with her boyfriend about how they could improve their relationship.
moral_consequence: After having discussed their relationship, Melinda's relationship with her boyfriend gets much better, and they're both happier.
immoral_action: Melinda stays with her boyfriend, even though she doesn't love him anymore, while trying to meet someone else.
immoral_consequence: Melinda's boyfriend can feel she doesn't love him anymore and it makes him very sad.

norm: It's generous to treat someone to a meal.
situation: Sue is making 4 servings of food for dinner, and the fridge is almost full.
intention: Sue wants to not put any of the food in the fridge.
moral_action: Sue shares the food with her family, giving the other 3 portions away.
moral_consequence: Sue's family has a nice dinner and compliment Sue on her cooking.
immoral_action: Sue throws the rest of the leftovers out after making the food and doesn't share the food.
immoral_consequence: Sue's family expresses annoyance at Sue for not sharing, and get angry at her.

norm: It's good to celebrate someone's life.
situation: Alice's grandmother is celebrating her 80th birthday, and the family is having a big party, but Alice's friends are also having a party.
intention: Alice wants to party with her friends.
moral_action: Alice goes to her grandmother's birthday party and attends her friends' party afterward.
moral_consequence: Alice's grandmother is delighted to see her at the party.
immoral_action: Alice skips her grandmother's party and goes to her friends' party.
immoral_consequence: Alice's grandmother is sad that she didn't show, and Alice's parents are angry with her.

norm: People who idolize the Nazis are considered vile by society.
situation: John is a young man that is searching the internet for entertainment.
intention: John wants to find a new community to be a part of.
moral_action: John notices that many people are online are following a Nazi personality and decides to try to motivate them to stop.
moral_consequence: John becomes the founder of a group that helps tutor and mentor young men about the dangers of Nazi ideology.
immoral_action: John finds and begins to frequent a website where fans of a Nazi personality socialize and watch his videos.
immoral_consequence: John is indoctrinated into a dangerous belief system that leaves him a danger to the public.

norm: It's irresponsible to do things without thinking about the consequences
situation: Harper is on vacation in Las Vegas on a tight budget.
intention: Harper wants to gamble.
moral_action: Harper sets a gambling budget so that she doesn't overspend.
moral_consequence: Harper loses a game of poker but is still able to enjoy the rest of her vacation due to her budgeting.
immoral_action: Harper plays a game of poker and bets everything in her pocket.
