immoral_consequence: Harper loses everything she has and can't afford to do anything else for the remainder of her vacation.

norm: It's wrong to yell at a grandparent.
situation: Sandra's grandmother usually sends a card with money for Sandra's birthday, but this year she has been feeling sick and forgot.
intention: Sandra wants to call her grandmother.
moral_action: Sandra calls her grandmother to see if she is doing well since it is out of character for her to forget a birthday.
moral_consequence: Sandra learns that her grandmother is feeling sick, so she comes over to take her to the hospital.
immoral_action: Sandra calls her grandmother and yells at her for forgetting her birthday, saying that she was counting on receiving the money.
immoral_consequence: Sandra's grandmother does not feel comfortable telling Sandra about her health, and she continues to get sicker.

norm: It's wrong to use someone else's things without their permission.
situation: Matt is getting ready to go to work but his is running behind because his roommates had the shower tied up for a long time.
intention: Matt wants to get to work quickly.
moral_action: Matt calls an Uber to get to work faster than taking the subway.
moral_consequence: Matt arrives on time to his job.
immoral_action: Matt grabs one of his roommates car keys and takes their car to work instead of riding the bus.
immoral_consequence: Matt has the police show up at his work when his roommate calls them saying his car was taken without permission.

norm: It's wrong to get involved with coworkers.
situation: Fran is hired at a new company.
intention: Fran wants to get ahead at work.
moral_action: Fran spends a lot of time working nights and weekends at her job.
moral_consequence: The president of the company is impressed by Fran's hard work and gives her a promotion.
immoral_action: Fran has an affair with her boss, so he will give her a promotion.
immoral_consequence: The president of the company finds out about the affair and fires Fran.

norm: It is wrong to end yourself.
situation: Ted has been depressed for a long time and his mother is worried about him.
intention: Ted wants to stop experiencing the sadness he's feeling.
moral_action: Ted goes to see a psychiatrist and gets a prescription for antidepressants.
moral_consequence: Ted's mother is hopeful for her son's recovery and vows to help him any way she can.
immoral_action: Ted gets a gun, puts it in his mouth, and shoots himself.
immoral_consequence: Ted's mother is overcome with sadness at her son's death and goes into her own depression.

norm: It is wrong to insist on having your way.
situation: John is in a company meeting for product designs.
intention: John wants to support his favorite design.
moral_action: John makes a case for his favorite design and comes to an amicable decision with his coworkers.
moral_consequence: The coworkers of John starts viewing John as a friendly, professional and competent colleague.
immoral_action: John adamantly argues for a design he likes and will not back down.
immoral_consequence: John's coworkers dismisses John and starts to dislike him.

norm: It's good to share your feelings and emotions with others
situation: Sharon is having a very difficult time in life and her friends are worried.
intention: Sharon wants to feel better.
moral_action: Sharon opens up to her friends about her struggles and asks for their support.
moral_consequence: Sharon's friends give her helpful advice and a listening ear, making the friendships stronger.
immoral_action: Sharon pushes her friends away and spends time at home drinking alone instead.
immoral_consequence: Sharon's friends get frustrated and stop calling her health suffers from binge drinking.

norm: It's wrong to not take cancer seriously.
situation: John finds out his toxic ex girlfriend has cancer.
intention: John wants to tell his friends.
moral_action: John soberly tells his friends what he heard about his ex.
moral_consequence: John's friend tells them he has cancer, and they all give him support.
immoral_action: John goes to a bar and laughingly tells his friends his ex has cancer, and he's glad because of what happened between them.
immoral_consequence: John's best friend starts bawling because he just found out he has cancer and John has made fun of it.

norm: It is bad to betray those you love
situation: Alana is good friends with Josh, her sister's boyfriend, who has invited her to a party.
intention: Alana wants to attend the party with Josh.
moral_action: Alana asks her sister if it'd be alright to attend the party with Josh.
moral_consequence: Alana's sister is fine with the idea and wishes them a good night.
immoral_action: Alana and Josh go to the party without telling her sister.
immoral_consequence: Alana's sister loses trust in her, straining their relationship for a while.

norm: It's polite to cancel an appointment that you can't make.
situation: Frank is due to see his doctor this afternoon, but he feels better now.
intention: Frank wants to decide what to do.
moral_action: Frank calls up to inform the doctors office he won't be coming in.
moral_consequence: The doctor is able to fit someone in Franks place, so they can get medical attention.
immoral_action: Frank decides not to see his doctor but doesn't call to inform the office.
immoral_consequence: The doctor wastes time that could have been spent helping someone who needed help.

norm: People respect abuse victims that break free of the cycle.
situation: Jack abused John [his son], and John used that as an excuse to abuse Joe [John's son].
intention: Joe wants to raise his kids.
moral_action: Joe decides not to abuse his kids because he didn't like it when his dad abused him.
moral_consequence: Joe breaks the cycle of abuse and in turn his kids never know abuse.
immoral_action: Joe abuses his kids too because that's how he himself was raised.
immoral_consequence: Joe's kids in turn go on to abuse their own kids.

norm: You shouldn't fantasize about giving up on your life.
situation: Daisuki sits down on his lunch break feeling depressed and underappreciated at work.
intention: Daisuki wants to do something on break.
moral_action: Daisuki talks about the problems he's having at work with one of his coworkers.
moral_consequence: Daisuki learns how to approach people at work.
immoral_action: Daisuki daydreams about his coworkers having trouble functioning and missing him after he passes away.
immoral_consequence: Daisuki breaks down once he gets home from his depression.

norm: It's wrong to laugh at hurtful jokes.
situation: Daimen is at a party with his disabled sister Hannah when Travis makes fun of Hannah's disability.
intention: Daimen wants to get on his Travis good side.
moral_action: Daimen explains how Hannah's good qualities could assist Travis.
moral_consequence: A week after the party, Travis offers Hannah a drive.
immoral_action: Daimen giggles and builds on Travis' joke.
immoral_consequence: Hannah breaks down crying.

norm: It is not well seen to be dating multiple people.
situation: Zoe is a college student.
intention: Zoe wants to go on dates and stop being single.
moral_action: Zoe has fun with her date, and he asks her out again.
moral_consequence: Zoe develops a long term relationship and has fun going out again and again.
immoral_action: Zoe gets caught out on a date by another man she's dating.
immoral_consequence: The other man dumps Zoe on the spot, and so does the man she's on the date with.

norm: You shouldn't say racist things to kids in school.
situation: Sally is at school one day with her friends and sees a new Muslim boy arriving for his first day.
intention: Sally wants to impress her friends.
moral_action: Sally sees the new boy while eating with her friends at lunch and asks if he wants to join them.
moral_consequence: Sally learns new things about his culture, and they become great friends.
immoral_action: Sally sees the new boy and decides to show off for her friends and tells him to go back to his country where he belongs.
immoral_consequence: Sally's friends are disgusted by her behavior and refuse to be friends with her anymore.

norm: It is rude to disobey your family.
situation: Susan is trying to plan out her college career.
intention: Susan wants to pick a major.
moral_action: Susan knows her mother would like her to be a pre-med major and follows that path.
moral_consequence: Susan pleases her mother and may have a better relationship with her.
immoral_action: Susan knows her mother would like her to be a pre-med major and chooses to major in art instead.
immoral_consequence: Susan's relationship with her mother will be strained.

norm: Workplace romances are frowned up.
situation: Liz has been single for a long time and has been feeling lonely on her own.
intention: Liz wants to find someone to date.
moral_action: Liz decides to date a friend she's always liked.
moral_consequence: The friend feels validated by the reciprocated feelings.
immoral_action: Liz starts dating a coworker who she's attracted to.
immoral_consequence: The coworker's work performance is hindered by Liz.

norm: It's expected to bring a gift to a birthday party.
situation: John's classmate is having a birthday party and the whole class is invited.
intention: John wants to go to the birthday party.
moral_action: John neglects to get a present for his classmate and goes to the birthday party with nothing at all.
moral_consequence: John's classmate thinks John is weird and stingy for coming to his birthday and not bringing a present.
immoral_action: John buys a nice birthday present for his classmate and brings it to the birthday party.
immoral_consequence: John's classmate loves John's present and thinks John is very generous.

norm: It's nice to take pictures with others.
situation: A crowd gathered outside the concert to get autographs from the rockstar.
intention: The rockstar wants to get on the bus to the next town as fast as he can.
moral_action: The rockstar takes a few quick selfies with his fans before getting on the bus.
moral_consequence: The rockstar is adored by his fans when they see his generous nature even though he's in a rush.
immoral_action: The rockstar rushes by the gathered fans and their outstretched cameras to take a selfie with him.
immoral_consequence: The rockstar loses some fans because of his rude behavior.

norm: It's wrong to send texts to the wrong people.
situation: Daniel is reading a saucy sexual text from his girlfriend when he gets another incoming text from his mom.
intention: Daniel wants to reply to an outstanding text.
moral_action: Daniel replies to his mom's text without exiting the conversation with her.
moral_consequence: Daniel's mom is happy to hear back from her son so quickly.
immoral_action: Daniel replies to the saucy text but does not exit the conversation with his mom and sends it to her.
immoral_consequence: Daniel's mom is grossed out and recoils at the revealing information she didn't want to be privy to.

norm: It's rude to not thank someone for serving you.
situation: Bill was at a restaurant and Jane served him his food, Bill thought Jane did a poor job.
intention: Bill wants to react to Jane's service.
moral_action: Despite the poor service Bill still said thank you to Jane.
moral_consequence: Jane thanked Bill for the politeness but felt she should apologize for being late to Bill's table.
immoral_action: "Bill gave no response beliving in ""if you can't say something nice...""."
immoral_consequence: Jane thought Bill's silence was rude for not saying thank you.

norm: It's not okay to steal food without paying for it.
situation: Jen is very hungry but has a very low bank balance at the moment.
intention: Jen wants to eat without spending much money.
moral_action: Jen orders inexpensive items off the dollar menu.
moral_consequence: Jen saves money and enjoys a full meal.
immoral_action: Jen takes someone's lunch from the employee fridge at her workplace.
immoral_consequence: Jen feels guilty for stealing.

norm: It's inconsiderate to pull a girl's hair.
situation: Billy is in grade school and has a crush on a girl in his class.
intention: Billy wants to get the girl's attention.
moral_action: Billy offers the girl a dessert treat during lunch and asks if he can sit next to her.
moral_consequence: The girl is touched by the gift from Billy and feels happy.
immoral_action: Billy sneak up behind the girl to surprise her by giving her hair a tug because he doesn't know how to talk to girls.
immoral_consequence: The girl who gets her hair pulled by Billy feels pain from it and is upset.

norm: You shouldn't commit fraud.
situation: Amy just started a new business and wanted to attract more investors.
intention: Amy wanted more money to help run her business.
moral_action: Amy persuades new investors to invest in her new business by being truthful.
moral_consequence: Amy gets a few new investors that are willing to support her through the thick and thin.
immoral_action: Amy misrepresents her company's financials to persuade investors to give her their money.
immoral_consequence: She loses the business after the new investors sue her.

norm: You shouldn't ride a skateboard down the staircase.
situation: Ryan is carrying his skateboard home when he notices his crush hanging out by the stairs.
intention: Ryan wants to impress his crush.
moral_action: Ryan demonstrates his extensive trivia knowledge to his crush and her friends.
moral_consequence: Ryan's crush asks to him to hang out with him next weekend.
immoral_action: Ryan slides down the rail on the stairs while calling out his crush's name.
immoral_consequence: Ryan falls off his skateboard spraining his ankle.

norm: It's wrong to be lazy
situation: Patty has a big test tomorrow, but is feeling kind of tired.
intention: Patty wants to take a nap.
moral_action: Patty sets her alarm and takes a short nap before studying.
moral_consequence: Patty has time to study thoroughly and gets a good grade on the test.
immoral_action: Patty takes a long nap and wakes up late at night.
immoral_consequence: Patty does not have time to study properly and fails the exam.

norm: It's not good to be racist towards anyone.
situation: Martin works in a grocery store and notices a black customer opening different bottles of ketchup and pouring them on the floor.
intention: Martin wants to tell the black customer to stop opening ketchup bottles.
moral_action: Martin tells the customer that opening food products is not permitted in the store unless the customer pays for them.
moral_consequence: The black customer then leaves the store because they don't want to actually buy the ketchup.
immoral_action: Martin tells the customer that only uncivilized blacks would open and pour out ketchup bottles in a grocery store.
immoral_consequence: The black customer complains to the store manager about what Martin said, and he is fired.

norm: You shouldn't steal from your siblings.
situation: Joe is out of energy drinks and sees his brother Sam's drinks in the fridge.
intention: Joe wants an energy drink.
moral_action: Joe goes out to the store and buys more energy drinks.
moral_consequence: Sam drinks his energy drink the next day and is happy.
immoral_action: Joe takes one of his Sam's energy drinks out of the fridge and drinks it.
immoral_consequence: Sam is sad that he has a missing energy drink.

norm: It's rude to show up late for an engagement.
situation: John has an important work meeting at 10:00 am.
intention: John wants to attend the meeting.
moral_action: John shows up a few minutes early for the work meeting.
moral_consequence: John is praised for his preparedness and contributions in the meeting.
immoral_action: John arrives 20 minutes late for the meeting.
immoral_consequence: John is reprimanded for being tardy.

norm: It's wrong to emotionally cheat on your partner.
situation: Rich has been in a long term relationship and is feeling the spark disappearing.
intention: Rich wants to emotionally connect with someone.
moral_action: Rich thinks of a creative way to rekindle the spark with his partner.
moral_consequence: Rich's partner feels closer to him and is happy.
immoral_action: Rich starts getting closer and feeling emotional with an attractive friend.
immoral_consequence: Rich's partner is upset when she finds out what is happening.

norm: It's rude to ask too much of your friends.
situation: Sophie has a friend in Honduras, and some of her friends are going there.
intention: Sophie wants to send her friend a gift.
moral_action: Sophie buys a small phone for her friend and asks her other friends to take it.
moral_consequence: Sophie's friends easily fit the phone and are happy with the arrangement.
immoral_action: Sophie buys a large blender and asks her friends to take it in their luggage to Honduras.
immoral_consequence: Her friends can't fit their own clothes in the luggage and become annoyed with Sophie.

norm: It is kind to provide financial advice to someone.
situation: Mr. Buckson is approached by his student Robbie who wants to know how to build up his credit score.
intention: Mr. Buckson wants to respond to Robbie.
moral_action: Mr. Buckson tells Robbie everything he knows about the subject and guides him towards some further research.
moral_consequence: Robbie learns a lot about improving your credit score, and he feels grateful to his teacher.
immoral_action: Mr. Buckson feels this isn't part of his job and tells Robbie to ask someone else.
immoral_consequence: Robbie feels that he was being a burden and is now reluctant to ask anyone else.

norm: You shouldn't call your sibling selfish
situation: Richard and his brother Phil are playing and Phil asks Richard to share his toy, which Richard refuses.
intention: Phil wants to respond to Richard's refusal to share his toy.
moral_action: Phil tells his brother that's OK he won't give him his toys either next time he asks.
moral_consequence: Richard realizes that it doesn't feel so good to be on the other side and changes his mind about sharing.
immoral_action: Phil tells Richard that he is a horrible and selfish brother who never shares.
immoral_consequence: Richard is insulted that he is being called selfish and begins to act defensively worsening the situation.

norm: You shouldn't ignore someone's texts.
situation: Sam is on vacation when he receives text messages from his boss about an urgent work matter.
intention: Sam wants to decide whether to respond to the text messages.
moral_action: Sam responds to the texts and takes care of the work matter his boss needed help with.
moral_consequence: Sam receives credit and commendation at work and looks good to the boss.
immoral_action: Sam ignores the texts because he is on vacation and wants to relax.
immoral_consequence: Sam's boss is upset with him for failing to respond to the urgent matter and reprimands him in front of his colleagues.

norm: It is wrong to tell people how to feel.
situation: Georgia is talking to her friend when her friend tells her that she was sexually assaulted.
intention: Georgia wants to help her friend get over the bad experience.
moral_action: George tells her friend she understands how she feels and is there for her.
moral_consequence: Georgia's friend thanks her, talks to her about it on a regular basis and begins feeling better over time.
immoral_action: Georgia tells her friend that she should be grateful for the attention.
immoral_consequence: Georgia's friend is so hurt that she storms out and ends the friendship.

norm: It's bad to abuse women.
situation: Ryan is mad at his girlfriend Lily for cheating on him.
intention: Ryan wants to vent his frustrations.
moral_action: Ryan writes a letter expressing his desire to break up with Lily.
moral_consequence: Lily feels sad but understands why Ryan wants to break up.
immoral_action: Ryan grabs Lily by the wrist and strikes her across the face.
immoral_consequence: Lily starts to sob uncontrollably and calls the police on Ryan.

norm: You shouldn't expect your coworkers to pick up your slack.
situation: Lisa works at an accounting firm.
intention: Lisa wants to work on a consulting business on the side.
moral_action: Lisa schedules firm work during the week days and consulting work on the week ends.
moral_consequence: Lisa is able to complete all her work at the firm and for consulting at a high level of quality which pleases all her clients.
immoral_action: Lisa neglects her firm work leaving it to junior associates to complete while she focuses on consulting work.
immoral_consequence: Lisa's firm work suffers from lack of oversight and displeases the firm's clients.

norm: You should pay back money you owe.
situation: Jorge has gambling debts to the casino but just got some money and is on his way to the casino.
intention: Jorge wants to continue to be able to gamble.
moral_action: Jorge walks up to the casino's banker and settles his debt before heading to the floor to gamble.
moral_consequence: Jorge is extended a line of credit from the casino and is welcome to lose his money there as he pleases.
immoral_action: Jorge walks in and begins to bet the money he brought with him on the tables.
immoral_consequence: The owner of the casino cuts Jorge off since he hasn't settled his debt and kicks him outside where he is met by burly debt collectors.

norm: You shouldn't drink more alcohol than you can handle.
situation: John is at a frat party with many other students.
intention: John wants to drink some beer at the party.
moral_action: John actively controls his drinking throughout the party.
moral_consequence: John avoids getting too drunk and has a good time at the party.
immoral_action: John drinks more beer than he could tolerate.
immoral_consequence: John vomits and embarasses himself in front of the other students.

norm: It's not okay to grab unsuspecting animals.
situation: Shelly is at her friends house and sees her new rescue dog.
intention: Shelly wants to pet the dog.
moral_action: After asking if she can pet the dog, the owner allows Shelly to pet the dog.
moral_consequence: Shelly feels good as she runs her fingers through the dogs hair.
immoral_action: Shelly pets the dog from behind.
immoral_consequence: Shelly startles the dog and is bitten.

norm: It's good to leave a wet umbrella outside.
situation: Fern walked home in the rain, snug and dry under her umbrella; she steps into the porch, folds the umbrella, and opens her front door.
intention: Fern wants to get indoors out of the rain.
moral_action: Fern stands the umbrella in the porch near the door, and comes inside.
moral_consequence: The water from the umbrella makes a puddle on the porch, where it does no damage.
immoral_action: Fern comes inside and lays the wet umbrella down on the hall table next to the newspaper and mail.
immoral_consequence: The water from the umbrella makes a puddle on the table, getting the mail and the purse very wet.

norm: You shouldn't get involved with your therapist romantically.
situation: Debbie is being treated by Dr. Edwards in an effort to help her feel more attracted to the opposite sex.
intention: Debbie wants to feel more confident in being heterosexual.
moral_action: Karen flirts with Dr. Edwards during sessions, but he tells Karen while he finds her to be an attractive woman, it would be unethical to have romantic relations.
moral_consequence: Dr. Edwards honesty and professionalism leads to Karen's trust, and she is able to continue having productive sessions with him.
immoral_action: Karen seduces Dr. Edwards in hopes that by having a sexual relationship with a successful therapist she will feel more fulfilled in her sexuality.
immoral_consequence: Dr. Edwards relationship is discovered by his secretary, and she reports him to the medical board, which causes him to lose his license.

norm: You shouldn't give someone clothes with stains.
situation: Dave has his friend Frank over in his backyard for a bbq when Frank slips and falls in the pool getting soaked.
intention: Dave wants to find Frank some dry clothes.
moral_action: Dave goes upstairs and finds some clothes from his closet that he brings down to Frank.
moral_consequence: Frank is delighted that his friend is helping him out and relieved to be back in dry clothes.
immoral_action: Dave goes upstairs and finds some dirty clothes from his hamper that he brings down to Frank.
immoral_consequence: Frank is disgusted that his friend is giving him his unwashed, used, dirty clothes to wear.

norm: It's nice to volunteer to help others.
situation: A worker at a local homeless shelter asks Jim to volunteer to serve food to the homeless people.
intention: Jim wants to give the homeless shelter worker an answer.
moral_action: Jim responds to the homeless shelter worker that he'd be glad to help out.
moral_consequence: The homeless people at the shelter are served food that day which they are happy about.
immoral_action: Jim says he's too busy to help out at the homeless shelter.
immoral_consequence: There aren't enough volunteers to serve food at the shelter and the homeless people go hungry that day.

norm: It's rude to call people you cared about names.
situation: Jen has just been dumped by her partner after a huge argument.
intention: Jen wants to get back at her partner for leaving her.
moral_action: Jen takes time to focus on her goals and finds success.
moral_consequence: Jen's ex regrets leaving her when he sees that she is becoming successful.
immoral_action: Jen insults her ex and picks on his insecurities.
immoral_consequence: Jen's former partner brushes her as like a crazy ex.

norm: It is rude to be impatient with a disabled person.
situation: Bob is riding the bus to work when the driver stops to pick up a person in a wheelchair.
intention: Bob is in a hurry to get to work and wants to speed things up.
moral_action: Bob helps the driver secure the wheelchair in its proper position.
moral_consequence: The bus departs in a moment and the disables rider is appreciative of Bob's help.
immoral_action: Bob loudly complains about the delay.
immoral_consequence: The driver has to rush through securing the wheelchair, which leaves the disabled rider embarrassed as well as uncomfortable.

norm: It's bad to hound your kids too much.
situation: Rae has been studying hard for Chemistry, but her mother Susan is still disappointed in her grade performance.
intention: Susan wants Rae to get better grades.
moral_action: Susan asks Rae if she thinks a tutor could be helpful.
moral_consequence: Rae agrees to go to a tutor, and they work together to get her grades up.
immoral_action: Susan takes Rae's cell phone away and tells her she can have it back when she gets better grades.
immoral_consequence: Rae works tirelessly until she can get her cell phone back, but then decides to run away from home with it.

norm: You shouldn't complain when someone is being helpful.
situation: Richard got home from the hospital after having surgery.
intention: Richard wants to move from his bed to the couch to watch tv.
moral_action: Richard asks his friend if he'll help him get to the couch safely to watch tv.
moral_consequence: His friend does his best, and they both enjoy watching tv together.
immoral_action: Richard yells at his friend for almost dropping him while carrying him to the couch.
immoral_consequence: Richard's friend stops coming by to help him out and Richard is stuck in bed all day.

norm: You shouldn't procrastinate homework assignments.
situation: Nikki has been assigned a four-page paper for her English course, and it is due in two weeks.
intention: Nikki wants to write a good paper.
moral_action: Nikki starts on her paper the day after it's assigned, and works on it over the next week.
moral_consequence: Nikki finishes her paper early, and doesn't need to stress about getting it done.
immoral_action: Nikki doesn't start her paper until the day before it's due, then she must stay up very late to get it done on time.
immoral_consequence: Nikki is very tired the next day, and falls asleep in class after turning in her paper.

norm: You should always be prepared before you travel.
situation: Felix is setting out on a long road trip soon and is packing his luggage.
intention: Felix wants to enjoy the trip.
moral_action: Felix makes a comprehensive list of everything he needs for his road trip and checks each item off as he packs it.
moral_consequence: Felix packs only what he needs and his road trip goes smoothly.
immoral_action: Felix just grabs things he notices around his room that he thinks he may need on his road trip.
immoral_consequence: Felix over packs things he doesn't need and forgets things he does need so his road trip ends up worse than it could have been.

norm: It is mean to scream at your grandma.
situation: Philip's grandma accidentally broke Philip's laptop.
intention: Philip wants to express his frustration.
moral_action: Philip tells his grandma that he is disappointed and vents his feelings in his journal.
moral_consequence: Philip's grandma feels remorseful but not attacked.
immoral_action: Philip screams at his grandma and calls her stupid.
immoral_consequence: Philip's grandma cries and feels like Philip is mean-spirited.

norm: It is good for parents to play with their children.
situation: Jared finds out his children are not learning as fast as they need to in school.
intention: Jared wants to teach his children how to count.
moral_action: Jared tries to teach his children counting, through play and video games.
moral_consequence: Jared's children learn very fast and overcome their school issues, and Jared feels proud.
immoral_action: Jared tries to teach his children counting in a very rigid, textbook way.
immoral_consequence: Jared's kids have trouble paying attention, and Jared feels like a faillure.

norm: It's wrong not to get recognized for something you created.
situation: Tim wrote a new software program at work that is going to generate a lot of revenue for his company.
intention: Tim wants his company to be successful.
moral_action: Tim and his boss present Tim's idea to the management team at his company.
moral_consequence: Tim gets a huge bonus for creating the successful program.
immoral_action: Tim lets his boss take credit for the program thinking that the program will be more likely to be approved that way.
immoral_consequence: Tim doesn't get promoted even though his program is very successful.

norm: It's rude to point out someone's lazy eye.
situation: Janet meets a person for the first time and notices that they have a lazy eye.
intention: Janet wants to talk to the person she met.
moral_action: Janet just ignores the person's lazy eye and makes normal conversation.
moral_consequence: The person Janet met starts to feel comfortable around Janet and enjoys the conversation.
immoral_action: Janet tells the person she met that their lazy eye is weird because she can't tell where they are looking.
immoral_consequence: The person Janet met feels really embarrassed by Janet's comments about their lazy eye.

norm: It is good to have one partner.
situation: Talia has been married to her husband George for a long time and feels like the passion has dried up.
intention: Talia wants to feel the excitement of romantic relationship again.
moral_action: Talia tells George that she feels unfulfilled and that she wants to puts the spark back in their relationship.
moral_consequence: George agrees to work with Talia on reigniting their marriage.
immoral_action: Talia begins seeing one of her coworkers that she is attracted to without telling George.
immoral_consequence: George is devastated when he finds out and initiates a divorce.

norm: It is bad to lose your patience with your mother.
situation: Kirby's toy broke due to being worn down from use, but Kirby's mother thinks Kirby broke it by being irresponsible.
intention: Kirby wants to explain to his mother that he needs a new toy.
moral_action: Kirby calmly explains that the toy wore out from being played with so much.
moral_consequence: Kirby's mother replaces the worn out toy at the store.
immoral_action: Kirby reacts poorly under pressure and screams that it wasn't his fault.
immoral_consequence: Kirby gets the new toy, but he's grounded for a week and thus can't actually play with it.

norm: You shouldn't punch things when you're anger.
situation: Abby and Cory are dating and just had an argument over bills which made Cory angry.
intention: Cory wants to make himself feel better.
moral_action: Cory decides to take deep breaths before reacting.
moral_consequence: Cory is now calm and able to deal with the argument with Abby better.
immoral_action: Cory punches a hole in the wall in an expression of anger to make him feel better.
immoral_consequence: Cory now has to pay to get the hole in the wall fixed.

norm: It's rude not to give notice when quitting a job.
situation: Hannah has been working under a really tough boss for a while and has had enough of it.
intention: Hannah wants to quit her job.
moral_action: Hannah opens her email software and sends a resignation letter to her manager with two weeks notice.
moral_consequence: Hannah's manager is sad to see her go but understands and gives Hannah a glowing reference.
immoral_action: Hannah walks into her manager's office and throws her ID badge on the desk and tells the manager she's out and quits.
immoral_consequence: The manager is stressed out and scrambles to find a replacement on short notice.

norm: It is wrong to expose people's private information.
situation: Sherry sees a disagreeable political post online and realizes that her neighbor had posted it.
intention: Sherry wants express her disagreement with her neighbor.
moral_action: Sherry decides to put a sign for the political party that she supports in her front yard in clear view of her neighbor's house.
moral_consequence: The neighbor sees the sign and realizes that he should be considerate of Sherry's views when he speaks with her.
immoral_action: Sherry comments on the post by sharing her neighbor's address publically.
immoral_consequence: Many people show up at her neighbors house shouting their objections to the post.

norm: It's bad to stab people.
situation: James is drunk in a bar and the man sitting next to him just insulted his masculinity.
intention: James wants to get rid of the other man.
moral_action: James insults the other man back, and dodges when he attempts to punch James.
moral_consequence: The bouncers throw the other man out and James is able to continue drinking in peace.
immoral_action: James pulls out a switchblade and plunges it into the man's neck.
immoral_consequence: James is subdued by the bouncers and turned over to the local police.

norm: You shouldn't kick your friends out of important events.
situation: Joe enters the ballroom with his wife after their wedding ceremony, and he spots his drunk friend Alex acting like a fool.
intention: Joe wants to maintain an orderly enviornment.
moral_action: Joe seats Alex in a corner with some water urging him to stay put until he feels better.
moral_consequence: Alex is able to have fun with everyone in the party after he sobers up.
immoral_action: Joe escorts Alex out of the building telling him that he needs to go home.
immoral_consequence: Alex gets into a traffic accident for drunk driving.

norm: It is bad to cheat on someone who trust you.
situation: Jonah has been dating Martha, who he has promised to be faithful to.
intention: Jonah wants to date other people.
moral_action: Jonah tells Martha he wants to date other people.
moral_consequence: Martha accepts Jonah's honesty and moves on with her life while he dates other girls.
immoral_action: Jonah dates other girls behind Martha's back.
immoral_consequence: Martha finds out about Jonah's cheating and is never able to trust anyone again.

norm: You should appreciate your parents when they support your happiness.
situation: Jan lives with his parents while he's going through a rough time.
intention: Jan wants to tell his parents about how they've acted towards him.
moral_action: Jan thanks his parents for the opportunity of living rent-free for a while.
moral_consequence: Jan's parents feel loved and appreciated.
immoral_action: Jan berates his parents for lots of petty problems that the house has.
immoral_consequence: Jan's parents feel offended and unappreciated for their kindness.

norm: It's not okay to betray someone that trusts you.
situation: Tracy is dating Felix when Felix gives her one of his credit cards and its PIN in case she ever needs emergency cash.
intention: Tracy wants to buy some new clothes.
moral_action: Tracy uses her own credit card to buy herself some new outfits.
moral_consequence: Felix uses his own credit card to buy Tracy a necklace for their six-month anniversary.
immoral_action: Tracy uses Felix's credit card to buy herself a thousand dollars worth of new outfits.
immoral_consequence: Felix dumps Tracy when he discovers she's used his credit card for clothes and makes her pay him back with interest.

norm: It's wrong to take a bribe.
situation: Michael is a senator in Congress who has fallen on hard times.
intention: Michael wants some extra cash.
moral_action: Michael looks for a second job to earn more money.
moral_consequence: Michael maintains respect for himself and leads well.
immoral_action: Michael meets with a special interest who pays him for his vote.
immoral_consequence: Michael loses respect for himself eventually and is an ineffective leader.

norm: It's fun to laugh and joke around with family.
situation: Frank feels upset after getting a bad grade in his Math test and is back home.
intention: Frank wants to manage his bad mood.
moral_action: Frank stays in the living room with his family and talks about silly things.
moral_consequence: Frank bursts into laughter and gets more relaxed.
immoral_action: Frank locks himself in the bedroom and lies on the bed, hoping to fall asleep and get more optimistic afterwards.
immoral_consequence: Frank has a bad dream about his future while sleeping.

norm: It's wrong not to help family who is in distress.
situation: Nikki is talking with her son.
intention: Nikki wants to see what's going on in her son's life.
moral_action: Nikki learns her son is low on funds during the conversation, and she pays his rent for him.
moral_consequence: Nikki's son has place to live because of her help.
immoral_action: Nikki's son tells her he's struggling financially, and she encourages him to work harder.
immoral_consequence: Nikki's son gets evicted from his apartment.

norm: You shouldn't get married if you want to live alone.
situation: Matt just proposed to his girlfriend Jennifer, a very private person who values her alone time.
intention: Jennifer wants to respond to Matt's proposal.
moral_action: Jennifer declines Matt's proposal, telling him that she while she loves him very much she doesn't think she's capable of living with another person.
moral_consequence: Matt is taken aback but understands her hesitation and prefers to keep their relationship strong by living separately.
immoral_action: Jennifer agrees to marry Matt, knowing that she's going to have a difficult time living together with him.
immoral_consequence: Matt is miserable in the marriage from the beginning due to issues arising from Jennifer's need for personal space and her desire to live alone.

norm: It's rude to invite yourself to someone's house for dinner.
situation: Mark starts working closely with his new co-worker Amy.
intention: Mark wants to become friends with Amy.
moral_action: Mark asks Amy if she wants to join him at his house for dinner tomorrow.
moral_consequence: Mark and Amy have dinner at his house and have a good time.
immoral_action: Mark asks Amy if she will cook him dinner at her house tomorrow.
immoral_consequence: Mark makes Amy feel uncomfortable, and she spends less time with him.

norm: It's wrong to tell someone their partner is crazy.
situation: Andy is annoyed by some things that his wife has done recently.
intention: Andy needs to vent his frustration.
moral_action: Andy talks to a good friend about his frustrations and his friend makes suggestions.
moral_consequence: Andy feels better after getting it out and getting some advice.
immoral_action: Andy talks to a woman he knows is attracted to him about how awful his wife is.
immoral_consequence: Andy has an affair and gets caught.

norm: It's rude to interrupt people.
situation: Jamie wants to join in the conversation with her peers.
intention: Jamie wants to be noticed.
moral_action: Jamie waits for her turn to join in the conversation.
moral_consequence: Jamie Is liked and respected by her friends for being nice.
immoral_action: Jamie talks over the current speaker making her voice heard.
immoral_consequence: Jamie's friends are annoyed she acted rude.

norm: You shouldn't tell your boss what to do.
situation: Jim's boss tells Jim that the boss will be giving a presentation to some clients.
intention: Jim wants to react to his boss.
moral_action: Jim asks his boss let him know if there's anything Jim can so to help them.
moral_consequence: Jim's boss thanks Jim and sees Jim as a helpful employee.
immoral_action: Jim tells his boss not to give the presentation because it may not go well.
immoral_consequence: Jim's boss rebukes Jim for trying to give them orders and sees Jim more negatively after that.

norm: It is mean to discriminate against people with bipolar disorder.
situation: John is playing soccer with some friends, when Frank who is bipolar asks if he can join in and play.
intention: John wants to respond to Frank's question.
moral_action: John tells Frank that he would be happy to have another player join and tells him to come into the game.
moral_consequence: Frank is delighted that he's a part of the game and happily runs around with the others.
immoral_action: "John tells Frank that no, he cannot play as he's known to be ""mental"" and he doesn't like crazy people."
immoral_consequence: Frank is extremely saddened by his exclusion and begins to break down and cry.

norm: It's rude to yell at the top of your lungs
situation: Annie is having dinner at a restaurant.
intention: Annie wants to get a different dish than the one she has.
moral_action: Annie talks to the waiter politely, and he brings her a new dish.
moral_consequence: The waiter enjoys his job so much he ends up picking up another shift and makes extra money.
immoral_action: Annie yells at the waiter at the top of her lungs, and he brings her a new dish.
immoral_consequence: The waiter is so upset by Annie's actions that he ends up quitting his job.

norm: It's wrong to resort to violence when someone upsets you.
situation: Colin is hanging out at the park when Phil accidentally throws a baseball that hits him in the foot.
intention: Colin wants Phil to get the ball back.
moral_action: Colin brings the ball back to Phil and asks him to be more careful.
moral_consequence: Phil moves to the other side of the park to play and Colin is able to relax in peace.
immoral_action: Colin throws the ball as hard as he can at Phil's head.
immoral_consequence: Phil is taken to the hospital for a head injury and Colin is charged for assault.

norm: You shouldn't always do what your partner wants.
situation: Laura's partner Joanne is demanding that Laura change her hairstyle, as it draws too much attention for Joanne's preference.
intention: Laura wants Joanne to be happy.
moral_action: Laura recommends that she and Joanne go to therapy to talk about the request.
moral_consequence: Laura and Joanne work through the issue in therapy and both leave happy without Laura having to change her look.
immoral_action: Laura gets a haircut to satisfy Joanne's demands.
immoral_consequence: Joanne likes the haircut but Laura begins to feel resentful towards Joanne for her forcefulness.

norm: You shouldn't think about suicide.
situation: Jeff has had a run of bad luck both at work and in his personal life, and so he has sunk into depression.
intention: Jeff wants to put an end to his pain.
moral_action: Jeff decides to see a psychologist for his depression.
moral_consequence: Jeff's therapy helps him overcome his depression.
immoral_action: Jeff contemplates taking his own life.
immoral_consequence: Jeff feels remorse when he considers what killing himself would do to his loved ones.

norm: It's not okay to make someone feel insignificant.
situation: Hector is giving one of his underperforming employees a performance review.
intention: Hector wants to let his employee know that they need to do a better job.
moral_action: Hector gently points out where the employee is failing and gives them advice on how to improve.
moral_consequence: Hector's employee feels supported and encouraged to do better.
immoral_action: Hector insults his employee during the review and belittles their role.
immoral_consequence: Hector's employee feels demotivated and performs even worse.

norm: Is inconsiderate to disturb other churchgoers
situation: Sally is at church, but she is expecting an important business call.
intention: Sally wants to make sure she doesn't miss the call.
moral_action: Sally puts her phone on vibrate only and keeps it on her lap, so she can feel it.
moral_consequence: Sally's phone vibrates, and she steps away from mass to take the call.
immoral_action: Sally keeps her ringtone on, so she can hear the call.
immoral_consequence: Sally's phone goes off during service and bothers everyone at church.

norm: You should not expect to get things for free.
situation: Karen goes to the clothing store but the line to checkout is too long.
intention: Karen wants a shirt.
moral_action: Karen waits patiently in line until she is waited on at the register.
moral_consequence: Karen brings the shirt home to wear at the party later.
immoral_action: Karen demands to get the shirt for free because the line was too long.
immoral_consequence: The manager of the store bans Karen for a year for causing a scene.

norm: It's encouraging to have friends who support your new hobbies.
situation: Patrick's friend Eugene has recently gotten into painting and plans to participate in an amateur gallery showing.
intention: Patrick wants to attend Eugene's gallery showcase.
moral_action: Patrick attends Eugene's art gallery and praises him on his work.
moral_consequence: Motivated by his feedback, Eugene continues on to become an experienced painter.
immoral_action: Patrick attends Eugene's art gallery but never says anything to him about his work.
immoral_consequence: Eugene quits painting due to the lack of feedback during the gallery showing.

norm: It's not okay to judge hings others enjoy.
situation: "Paul and Tom is walking by a yoga room where they're practicing ""goat yoga""."
intention: Paul wants to comment on the goat yoga.
moral_action: Paul asks Tom why goat yoga is popular.
moral_consequence: Tom tells Paul about goat yoga's benefits.
immoral_action: Paul jokes to Tom that the yoga participants should just do yoga in a pasture.
immoral_consequence: Tom objects and says that Paul is rude.

norm: It is wrong to expect an ex to support you.
situation: Bill is in need of money as he's just lost his job and is becoming desperate.
intention: Bill wants to ask someone he knows for money.
moral_action: Bill calls his mom and asks him to give him some money to tie him over.
moral_consequence: Bill is delighted when his mother agrees to give him some money right away.
immoral_action: Bill calls his ex wife Susan and asks him to give him some money to tie him over.
immoral_consequence: Bill is depressed when Susan denies him because she wants nothing to do with him.

norm: You shouldn't keep things from your significant other
situation: Joey is spending time with a female coworker after hours for work purposes and knows that this would concern his insecure partner.
intention: Joey wants to keep his partner from worrying.
moral_action: Joey tells his partner upfront that they have to do a work project together.
moral_consequence: Joey's partner feel more comfortable with the situation because she was given a heads up.
immoral_action: Joey avoids telling his partner who is he with after work.
immoral_consequence: Joey's partner finds out the truth from social media and loses trust in him.

norm: one should never be demanding.
situation: Jake walks downstairs after a long day of studying, and he sees his sister Anna working.
intention: Jake wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Jake goes to a club to unwind with a nice drink.
moral_consequence: Jake becomes friends with the bartender.
immoral_action: Jake insists that Anna should spend some time with him poking her arm several times.
immoral_consequence: Jake later receives a text from his mother scolding him for his bad behavior.

norm: It's irresponsible for bartenders to serve people too much alcohol.
situation: Vic is a bartender and one of his regular customers has already had 10 shots of vodka, yet wants more.

moral_action: Vic tells the customer that he's had enough and that he can talk to security if he has a problem with that.
moral_consequence: The customer is angry, but goes to sit down and passes out shortly afterwards, avoiding a fight.
immoral_action: Vic tells the customer that he can have more if he gets a designated driver, then gives him all he wants.
immoral_consequence: The customer has a blood alcohol level of .45 and has to be taken to the hospital.

norm: It's not okay to wish death on someone.
situation: Mary and her mother were having an argument and Mary was upset.
intention: Mary wanted her mother to know her anger.
moral_action: Mary talks about her feelings with her mother.
moral_consequence: They reach and agreement and both understand each other's feelings.
immoral_action: Mary tells her mother she wished she was dead.
immoral_consequence: Mary's mother is horribly upset and gets depressed.

norm: You shouldn't break up over text messages.
situation: John has been dating Lisa for about a year but isn't happy anymore and wants to break up with her.
intention: John wants to end the relationship.
moral_action: John sits down with Lisa and has a hard, but necessary conversation explaining his feelings, and they break up.
moral_consequence: Despite being hurt, Lisa later respects John for talking with her and being honest about his feelings about their relationship.
immoral_action: John shoots Lisa a text saying he is breaking up with her because he's not happy.
immoral_consequence: Lisa is very hurt and feels like, after a year together, the least John could do is break up with her in person.

norm: It's bad to be obsessed with attention.
situation: Casey is a youtuber, and her new video is getting less views than others.

moral_action: Casey goes on a walk and posts pictures of herself having fun in nature with a promise of new content soon.
moral_consequence: Her nature posts go viral which gets her more followers.
immoral_action: Casey gets onto twitter posting an emotional message begging people to watch her video with a bunch of popular hashtags.
immoral_consequence: The commentary and drama community roasts Casey.

norm: You should never attempt suicide.
situation: Ed, who has had suicidal thoughts for a long time, is pacing back and forth on a tall bridge debating if he should jump.
intention: Ed wants to decide whether to jump or not.

immoral_action: Ed decides to jump, climbs the railing, and jumps off of the bridge into the water far below.
immoral_consequence: Ed regrets his decision to jump almost immediately and dies on impact, breaking his family and friend's hearts.

norm: It's not good to brag.
situation: Jim and his friends were playing basketball, and Jim beat all of them in 1v1 games.

immoral_consequence: Jim's friends get tired of his bragging and stop hanging out with him.

norm: It's rude to show up unexpectedly to visit a friend.
situation: Reggie was bored one day and decided to visit his friend Darryl at his house, who happened to have his girlfriend over at that time.

moral_consequence: Reggie visited Darryl later that day, after Darryl was done visiting with his girlfriend.
immoral_action: Reggie showed up unexpectedly at Darryl's door, interrupting Darryl's makeout session.
immoral_consequence: Darryl yelled at Reggie and Darryl's girlfriend was no longer in the mood.

norm: You're discouraged from being violent towards others.
situation: Joey gets upset at something rude Tristian said to him.

moral_consequence: Tristian gets in trouble for being rude to Joey in the first place.

immoral_consequence: Joey complains that he got in trouble when Tristian was bad first.

norm: It's bad to show up late to your appointments
situation: Jack made an appointment to go to a baseball game with his son Lee this afternoon.

moral_consequence: Lee has a great time with his dad at the baseball game.
immoral_action: Jack fails to manage his time properly and arrives to pick up his son two hours late.
immoral_consequence: Lee is very upset with his dad and no longer wants to go to the game.

norm: It's wrong to benefit from someone else's unemployment.
situation: Jeff's employee is trying to unionize Jeff's employees, and Jeff is upset.

moral_action: Jeff lets his employees unionize if they want to and steps out of the way.

immoral_action: Jeff lets go of the employee so that his employees don't become unionized.
immoral_consequence: Jeff ends up making money by firing his employee and feels bad.

norm: It's unsafe to ride a bicycle while intoxicated.
situation: Brad was having a few drinks with his friends at the local bar.

moral_action: Brad calls the taxi company and gets a taxi ride home.

immoral_consequence: Brad is drunk, and he falls off his bike and breaks his nose.

norm: It's normal for people to drive.
situation: Cleo and her friend Lou are jumping on the trampoline together when Lou falls and hurts his arm.

moral_consequence: Lou feels appreciative and thanks Cleo for her quick response.
immoral_action: Cleo doesn't want to use gas in her car, so she walks Lou to the nearest care center.
immoral_consequence: Lou's injury becomes swollen and painful, he feels resentful towards Cleo for making him walk.

norm: You should walk the dog sometimes.
situation: John's wife asks him to walk the dog.
intention: John wants to respond to his wife's request.
moral_action: John agrees and walks the dog.
moral_consequence: John's wife is pleased with him helping out.
immoral_action: John tells her he doesn't feel like walking the dog.
immoral_consequence: John's wife gets upset with him for not taking care of the dog.

norm: It is rude to purposefully upset another person
situation: Samantha is about to face off against someone in a public debate, and her opponent recently had a miscarriage.
intention: Samantha wants to win the debate.
moral_action: Samantha reads some tips on how to be an effective public speaker before entering the stage.
moral_consequence: Her opponent is happy that she's debating a challenging opponent.
immoral_action: Samantha tells her opponent that her actions led to the miscarriage.
immoral_consequence: Her opponent starts crying.

norm: It's wrong to fat-shame your daughter.

immoral_action: Billy starts making fun of his daughter loudly every single time she walks by.
immoral_consequence: Billy's daughter is devastated and thinks her father hates her, and starts crying.

norm: It's not expected that a person bites an animal.
situation: Jessica is watching fireworks at home with her barking scared dog Misu, and a character in a movie talks about biting dogs ears to get them to calm down.
intention: Jessica wants to calm down Misu.

moral_consequence: Misu stops barking and settles down.
immoral_action: Jessica follows the advise given by the character in the movie and bites Misu's ear.

norm: It's mean to discourage children from their creative outlets.
situation: Dave is at a kitchen table with Bill his son, who is coloring.

immoral_consequence: Bill will feel reluctant to express himself and only know the pursuit of material gain while never developing emotionally.

norm: You should ground children that break the rules.
situation: Felicia notices her son Davis pushing his brother Derrick down onto the ground.
intention: Felicia wants to decide how to handle the situation.
moral_action: Felicia pulls Davis aside and puts him in time out for the rest of the day for pushing his brother.
moral_consequence: Davis apologizes to Dennis after getting out of time out.
immoral_action: Thinking that Davis is just playing around, Felicia does nothing.
immoral_consequence: Davis continues to physically abuse Derrick.

norm: It's wrong to say bad things about your coworkers online.

intention: Peter wants to vent his frustrations.
moral_action: Peter writes an email to his boss explaining his frustration and detailing his coworkers' behavior.
moral_consequence: Peter's boss invites Peter and his coworkers to his office and has a talk with all of them focused on resolving their issue.
immoral_action: Peter makes a Facebook post about the argument he has with his coworkers and talks about them disparagingly.
immoral_consequence: Peter's boss sees the Facebook post and fires Peter since he believes it makes the company look bad.

norm: Cheating on others is wrong.
situation: Daphne is out at a party without her boyfriend, Dan, and her friend Jake gets really flirty with her.
intention: Daphne wants to party with Jake.
moral_action: Daphne tells Jake he can hang out with her as long as he stops being flirty.
moral_consequence: Jake respects Daphne's wishes, and they play beer pong like platonic friends.
