norm: You shouldn't like messing with your students.
situation: One of James' students consistently disrupted his classes with talking and pranks.
intention: James wants his student to stop disrupting the class.
moral_action: James tells the student he can play on his phone as long as he's silent.
moral_consequence: The problem student still doesn't learn anything, but at least isn't distracting the other students.
immoral_action: James deliberately asked his problem student to solve impossible problems on the board in front of everyone.
immoral_consequence: James' student fell silent and started crying in class, prompting the student's parents to call the principal to complain.

norm: It's good to be concerned about a partner's health.
situation: Harriet sees that her partner is losing a lot of weight and isn't eating very much anymore.
intention: Harriet wants to let her partner know that he is loved.
moral_action: Harriet asks her partner if he is doing well, and asks why he doesn't seem to be eating much anymore.
moral_consequence: Harriet's partner admits to disordered eating patterns and asks for help looking for resources.
immoral_action: Harriet tells her partner that he looks great and that she supports him in any kind of body alterations he wants to make.
immoral_consequence: Harriet's partner's eating disorder goes unnoticed, and he becomes very ill.

norm: It's wrong to murder animals.
situation: Owen has noticed that there has been a dog in his yard every morning.
intention: Owen wants the dog to stay out of his yard.
moral_action: Owen finds out who the owners of the dog are and tells them what is happening.
moral_consequence: Owen never sees the dog in his yard for the rest of his life.
immoral_action: Owen shoots the dog and throws the dead body into the river.
immoral_consequence: The police come and arrest Owen for the murder of the dog.

norm: You shouldn't vent your frustration on your ex.
situation: James is attending a get together that his ex, May will also be attending.
intention: James wants to let May know how he feels.
moral_action: James asks to talk to May privately and proceeds to talk out his issues with their breakup.
moral_consequence: James gets some closure and is able to let go of any lingering hostility towards May.
immoral_action: James gets drunk and gives May a verbal lashing.
immoral_consequence: James is kicked out of the party by his other friends.

norm: It is good to take care of your resposibilites.
situation: Dave has only one thousand dollars left for this month and knows he hasn't paid his child support yet which is 1000 dollars.
intention: Dave wants to decide how to spend his last 1000.
moral_action: Dave decides that he should pay the child support that is due for this month.
moral_consequence: Dave's children eat well and have everything they need for that month.
immoral_action: Dave decides that he should buy himself a new couch since the old one is starting to deterorate.
immoral_consequence: Dave's children struggle through a bad month as their mother can't afford everything they need without her support.

norm: It is wrong to make children pay for your mistakes
situation: Bob breaks the mirror in the hallway by the kid's rooms and is afraid of what his wife will say.
intention: Bob wants to decide what to do next.
moral_action: Bob decides to tell the truth and admits that he broke the mirror.
moral_consequence: Bob might be sleeping on the couch but at least his conscious is clear.
immoral_action: Bob tells his wife that it must have been one of the kids who broke the mirror.
immoral_consequence: Bob's wife yells at the kids for hours, and they all get grounded when none of them admit it.

norm: You should report child abuse to the authorities.
situation: Alberta teaches fourth grade, and suspects one of her pupils named Sammy might be getting abused at home.
intention: Alberta wants her pupils to pass fourth grade.
moral_action: Alberta reports the suspected abuse, and Sammy's family gets a visit from Children's Services.
moral_consequence: Sammy does pass the grade, and his stepdad goes to anger management classes.
immoral_action: Alberta doesn't report what she suspects, but instead offers Sammy extra tutoring in math.
immoral_consequence: Sammy ends up passing fourth grade, but over the summer his stepdad breaks Sammy's arm.

norm: It's impolite to upstage the bride.
situation: Piper, a fashionista, has been invited to her sister's wedding that is being held in their parents' backyard.
intention: Piper wants to wear the perfect dress to her sister's wedding.
moral_action: Piper wears a knee length floral dress that matches her sister's wedding colors.
moral_consequence: The wedding guests think Piper is a good sister who is there to be supportive on her sister's day.
immoral_action: Piper wears a strapless red gown with a train and crystal embellishments.
immoral_consequence: The wedding guests all stare at Piper because she is overdressed, and they gossip about her being an attention-hog.

norm: You shouldn't move someone's seat.
situation: Donny is a practical joker who's looking to prank his coworker Frank who momentarily left his seat in the lunch room to go get food.
intention: Donny wants to make people laugh.
moral_action: Donny replaces the salt in the shaker with sugar, which Frank pours on his fries when he returns to the table to sit at his unmoved seat.
moral_consequence: Coworkers are entertained by Donny's antics when Frank realizes what happened and spits his food out.
immoral_action: Donny moves Franks chair out from under him when Frank returns to sit down and Frank falls over, sending his food flying.
immoral_consequence: Coworker's chuckles turn to gasps as people realize Frank was seriously injured by the prank.

norm: You should never text and drive
situation: Sarah's children need to be picked up from daycare.
intention: Sarah wants to tell her husband to pick up the children.
moral_action: Sarah waits until she can safely pull into a parking space and puts the car into park, then texts her husband.
moral_consequence: Her husband picks up the kids and Sarah brings home dinner.
immoral_action: Sarah texts her husband while driving to tell him to pick up the children.
immoral_consequence: Sarah causes a terrible car accident, kills someone and is in the hospital.

norm: It's bad to stalk your significant other.
situation: Jack is worried that his girlfriend spends tpo much time with a certain male coworker.
intention: Jack wants to make sure his girlfriend isn't cheating.
moral_action: Jack discusses his insecurity with his girlfriend.
moral_consequence: Jack feels reassured when his girlfriend assures him her relationship with her coworker is platonic.
immoral_action: Jack follows his girlfriend after work to make sure she stays faithful to him.
immoral_consequence: Jack gets dumped when his girlfriend catches him following her.

norm: It's bad to be stingy with your money.
situation: Greg is at the bar with a friend who usually pays for his drinks.
intention: Greg wants to save money.
moral_action: Greg orders less drinks than usual and pays for both their tabs.
moral_consequence: Greg's friend is pleasantly surprised that he is paying.
immoral_action: Greg lets his friend pay for the drinks again.
immoral_consequence: Greg's friend thinks poorly of him because he never pays.

norm: It's ineffectual to withhold necessary information.
situation: Dr. Jones was being paid by a pharmaceutical company to prescribe their opioid drug more, but the drug is effective.
intention: Dr. Jones wants to help his patients.
moral_action: Dr. Jones tells his patients that he's being paid by the company before prescribing the drug.
moral_consequence: Dr. Jones is following the laws required by doctors, and his patients trust him more.
immoral_action: Dr. Jones prescribes the opioid drug to his patients in pain without disclosing that he's getting paid.
immoral_consequence: Dr. Jones gets in trouble for taking money to prescribe a drug without disclosing that.

norm: It is bad to be vengeful and hold grudges
situation: Frank is tired of his new neighbors playing loud music late at night.
intention: Frank wants to respond to his new neighbors.
moral_action: Frank bakes a pie and takes it over to his new neighbors as a gift, welcoming them to the neighborhood.
moral_consequence: Frank's neighbors invite Frank to stay for a barbecue they're having in their backyard.
immoral_action: Frank waits for a quiet night and then plays his own music at high volume in the direction of his new neighbors' home.
immoral_consequence: Frank's neighbors don't get any sleep and throw trash on Frank's lawn to get back at him.

norm: It's good to get your own place to live.
situation: Carol has been living with her parents for all of her life.
intention: Carol wants some privacy.
moral_action: Carol gets a job and finds her own apartment to live in.
moral_consequence: Carol is finally able to enjoy the privacy of having her own place.
immoral_action: Carol changes the locks on all the doors in her parents' house.
immoral_consequence: Carol's parents kick her out of the house and change the locks again.

norm: It's inconsiderate to prevent someone from being able to sleep.
situation: Chloe is not tired and is laying in bed next to her husband.
intention: Chloe wants to entertain herself.
moral_action: Chloe listens to music through some headphones.
moral_consequence: Chloe enjoys the music and her husband keeps sleeping.
immoral_action: Chloe turns on the TV in the bedroom and watches it.
immoral_consequence: Chloe's husband wakes up and loses a good night of sleep.

norm: It's mean to shoot down people's dreams.
situation: Caroline is listening to her coworker talking about wanting to own a large Victorian style house.
intention: Caroline wants to comment on her coworker's goals.
moral_action: Caroline shows her coworker an application for cheap older homes.
moral_consequence: After a year of saving, Caroline buys a Victorian style house.
immoral_action: Caroline reminds her coworker that she'd never be able to afford the taxes on her new house.
immoral_consequence: Caroline's coworker becomes depressed.

norm: It's hurtful to trick people.
situation: Bob sees that his classmate Tim has delicious looking brownies packed in his school lunch.
intention: Bob wants to eat a brownie.
moral_action: Bob asks Tim if he would be willing to share one of the brownies with him.
moral_consequence: Tim agrees to give Bob a brownie and both boys enjoy eating them.
immoral_action: Bob tricks Tim into giving him the brownies, then he eats them all.
immoral_consequence: Tim feels sad and Bob later gets in trouble for taking the brownies.

norm: It's good to explore your sexuality to understand your preferences.
situation: Alexis calls Jennifer and tells her that she is really attracted to her and wants to go out with her one night over the next weekend.
intention: Jennifer needs to respond to Alexis.
moral_action: Jennifer tells Alexis that she has never dated another woman before but that she has no plans and would like to go out over the next weekend.
moral_consequence: Both Jennifer and Alexis have a lot of fun on their date, and they maintain a very open and honest relationship with one another throughout their lives.
immoral_action: Jennifer tells Alexis that she has never gone on a date with another woman before, and she is just too uncomfortable to try something like that.
immoral_consequence: Alexis is disappointed and Jennifer always wonders what it would have been like to go on a date with another woman.

norm: It is common to dry off after exiting the water.
situation: Hank exits the pool after swimming in it for an hour.
intention: Hank wants to put on his clothes.
moral_action: Hank dries himself off with a towel, then puts on his clothes.
moral_consequence: Hank's clothes stay dry, and Hank stays warm.
immoral_action: Hank puts on his clothes immediately without drying off.
immoral_consequence: Hank's clothes become soaked, and Hank gets cold.

norm: Jokes should not be mean spirited.
situation: Larry is giving a speech at his friend's wedding.
intention: Larry wants to make the speech funny.
moral_action: Larry makes jokes that are self deprecating.
moral_consequence: The bride and groom will be happy that Larry is entertaining.
immoral_action: Larry makes jokes that insult the bride and groom.
immoral_consequence: The bride and groom will become upset with Larry.

norm: It is wrong to eavesdrop on other people.
situation: Bob inadvertently stumbles across two of his bosses having a heated personal exchange.
intention: Bob wants to react to the situation.
moral_action: Bob reveals his presence and apologizes for the intrusion.
moral_consequence: Bob is able to get away before hearing more than he already had.
immoral_action: Bob conceals himself better and proceeds to listen in on the conversation.
immoral_consequence: Bob gets caught when he starts spreading what he heard around the office.

norm: You should be respectful of people around you.
situation: Sebastian is studying at a desk in the library when his phone starts to ring.
intention: Sebastian wants to answer the phone.
moral_action: Sebastian puts the phone on silent, goes outside, and talks with his friend.
moral_consequence: Sebastian is able to talk with his friends, and the other library patrons are able to study in peace.
immoral_action: Sebastian picks up the phone at the desk and starts to talk with his friend.
immoral_consequence: Other library patrons glare at Sebastian, and Sebastian is asked to leave.

norm: You shouldn't have to deal with people smoking around you.
situation: Ace is riding on a no-smoking train when he sees someone nearby lighting a cigarette.
intention: Ace wants to avoid fighting with the man about his cigarettes.
moral_action: Ace notifies a train official about the smoking man.
moral_consequence: The train officials confront the smoking man, who puts out his cigarette and avoids polluting the car.
immoral_action: Ace decides not to say anything and lets the man smoke.
immoral_consequence: The train car smells terrible and other customers begin to complain about the smoke.

norm: It is good to live up to your families legacy.
situation: Vince, who enjoys people, is part of a family of bankers and is trying to decide what career to follow.
intention: Vince wants to pick a satisfying career.
moral_action: Vince decides to make banking work for him and becomes a customer service manager at a bank.
moral_consequence: Vince's family is proud of him and gets him an excellent job in their banking network.
immoral_action: Vince decides that banking is not for him and becomes a counselor to help people with their problems.
immoral_consequence: Vince's family think that he is crazy for ignoring the family profession for a totally different line of work.

norm: It's good to make money for yourself.
situation: Bobby needs to get a new laptop, but he isn't working and doesn't have the money to buy one.
intention: Bobby needs to find a way to get some money.
moral_action: Bobby posts a flyer at the grocery store, offering to do odd jobs for reasonable rates.
moral_consequence: Bobby makes enough money doing odd jobs that he is able to buy his own laptop, and he feels proud of his accomplishment.
immoral_action: Bobby calls his parents and asks them if he can borrow the money to buy a new laptop.
immoral_consequence: His parents complain that he borrows too much money and Bobby feels embarrassed.

norm: It is unacceptable not to flush after using the restroom.
situation: Larry is at a party when he feels the call of nature.
intention: Larry wants to return to the party quickly.
moral_action: Larry uses the rest room and flushes the toilet multiple times to make sure everything went down.
moral_consequence: Larry enjoys the rest of the party knowing that he was respectful in his friend's home.
immoral_action: Larry uses the toilet quickly and then leaves without flushing.
immoral_consequence: The host of the party calls Larry out on his poor manners and embarrasses him.

norm: You should help your sister out whenever possible.
situation: Frank is at home relaxing when his sister Martha calls him to ask him to watch her kids while she goes out.
intention: Frank wants to respond to his sister's request for babysitting.
moral_action: Frank tells his sister that he'll be over right after he gets ready.
moral_consequence: Martha is relieved she'll get a babysitter for her kids and is happy she can count on Frank.
immoral_action: Frank tells his sister that he's relaxing now, so he's not able to come over and help.
immoral_consequence: Martha is annoyed that Frank is too lazy to come help her when she needs him.

norm: It's good to report crime.
situation: Frank is buying a candy bar at a grocery store when he notices someone shoplifting.
intention: Frank wants to get out of the store quickly.
moral_action: Frank tells a clerk at the store what he saw and then uses the self-checkout to avoid delays caused by the store personal dealing with the shoplifter.
moral_consequence: The store owner thanks Frank for his good work and rewards him with a small gift card to the store.
immoral_action: Frank ignores the shoplifter, so he can check out and leave the store more quickly.
immoral_consequence: The store owner loses money and has to increase the store's prices to compensate, resulting in Frank paying more when he goes to buy candy.

norm: It is wrong to drug others.
situation: Jeffrey is spending the night at a club.
intention: Jeffrey wants to go home with a lady.
moral_action: Jeffrey strikes up a conversation with a woman using a clever pick-up line.
moral_consequence: Jeffrey is invited by the lady to spend more time her after the club closes.
immoral_action: Jeffrey slips some GHB in a woman's drink.
immoral_consequence: Jeffrey is arrested when the bartender notices him altering the woman's drink.

norm: It's good to have a dog growing up.
situation: Robert has an son that is getting bad grades in school who has expressed that he wants a puppy for Christmas.
intention: Robert wants to teach his son some responsibility.
moral_action: Robert makes a deal with his son that he can have the dog if he improves his grades.
moral_consequence: Robert's son is motivated to improve his grades and is rewarded for good behavior.
immoral_action: Robert refuses to get his son the dog citing his performance in school.
immoral_consequence: Robert's son reacts counter-intuitively and continues to do badly in school.

norm: It is wrong not to report illegal activity.
situation: Conner is filling his car with gas when he observes a hit and run collision in the gas station parking lot.
intention: Conner wants to get home quickly.
moral_action: Conner remembers the license plate of the car that caused the hit and run and calls the police from his car while driving home to report it.
moral_consequence: The police are able to locate the car that caused the damage, thereby saving the victim thousands of dollars in repair costs.
immoral_action: Conner drives home and ignores the hit and run because he doesn't want to wait around for the police to show up.
immoral_consequence: The owner of the car that was hit has to pay thousands of dollars in repair costs out of his own pocket.

norm: You shouldn't take someone's wallet.
situation: John works as a cashier and notices a customer left their wallet on the counter.
intention: John wants to put the wallet somewhere.
moral_action: John puts the wallet in a lost and found box.
moral_consequence: The owner of the wallet can claim their wallet if they go back to the store.
immoral_action: John puts the wallet in his pocket to keep for himself.
immoral_consequence: The owner of the wallet will not get their wallet back.

norm: You shouldn't make your friends jealous.
situation: Patty is shopping for new jewelry for herself.
intention: Patty wants to get something that looks nice on her.
moral_action: Patty buys something modest for herself and doesn't call her friends to brag about it.
moral_consequence: Her friends compliment her on the jewelry, and everyone is happy.
immoral_action: Patty buys something expensive and brags about it to her friends who can't afford something so nice.
immoral_consequence: Patty is looked down on for rubbing her purchase in her friends faces.

norm: You should not completely control employees.
situation: Lenny's department has an evaulation coming up that Lenny needs to pass.
intention: Lenny wants his department to perform well.
moral_action: Lenny let's his workers do their job, letting them know that they can reach him for support.
moral_consequence: Lenny's department passes the evaulation, and everyone is pleased.
immoral_action: Lenny runs around correcting every action his employees make that he doesn't like.
immoral_consequence: Lenny's department passes the evaulation, but Lenny is burnt out and his department has low morale.

norm: You should not mess with someone else's personal accounts.
situation: Laura walks into the office after fighting with Shelby in the parking lot.
intention: Laura wants to express her feeling of anger against Shelby.
moral_action: Laura talks to Shelby about how she angry she felt at the moment of the fight.
moral_consequence: Laura and Shelby gain a deeper understanding of each other.
immoral_action: Laura changes Shelby's Facebook password, and laughs when Shelby struggles to log on.
immoral_consequence: Laura loses her friendship with Shelby.

norm: It's rude to cut out on someone with no explanation.
situation: Frank is at a party with his friend when he starts getting tired.
intention: Frank wants to go home.
moral_action: Frank takes a minute to inform his friend that he's leaving before heading home.
moral_consequence: Frank's friend enjoys himself at the party without having to worry about Frank's whereabouts.
immoral_action: Frank leaves the party immediately without telling his friend he's going.
immoral_consequence: Frank's friend spends a lot of time looking for Frank and worries about what might have happened to him.

norm: You should be considerate of other people's belongings.
situation: Kelly is cleaning her dorm room when she sees her roommate's shirt on the floor.
intention: Kelly wants her roommate to learn how to pick up after herself.
moral_action: Kelly talks to her roommate about being more tidy when she is in the room.
moral_consequence: Kelly's roommate starts to pick up after herself and keeps the room clean.
immoral_action: Kelly throws the shirt away because she is tired of picking up after her roommate.
immoral_consequence: Kelly's roommate takes some of her clothing because she can't find her lost shirt.

norm: Hugging someone is a good way to show appreciation.
situation: Brian had paid for Jeff's lunch when they went out to eat.
intention: Jeff wants to show his appreciation.
moral_action: Jeff gives Brian a hug and tells him thank you before they leave the restaurant.
moral_consequence: Brian is happy to take Jeff out to eat again in the future.
immoral_action: Jeff slaps Brian on the butt before they leave the restaurant.
immoral_consequence: Brian is freaked out by Jeff's action and doesn't invite him out to eat again.

norm: It's wrong to hurt another person
situation: A waiter bumps into John at a restaurant and spills drinks all over him.
intention: John wants to respond to the waiter.
moral_action: John tells the waiter it is okay and was just an accident.
moral_consequence: John receives a free meal from the restaurant.
immoral_action: John punches the waiter in the face.
immoral_consequence: John is arrested for battery and put in jail.

norm: It's frowned upon to spend resources frivolously.
situation: Xavier is out of work thanks to COVID-19 and gets a stimulus check from the government.
intention: Xavier wants to spend the money.
moral_action: Xavier puts some of the money in the bank and uses the rest to buy bulk food items.
moral_consequence: Xavier has enough resources to last until he goes back to work.
immoral_action: Xavier celebrates by going on vacation and renting a hotel room for a week.
immoral_consequence: When Xavier returns, he has no money for food and no job to earn it.

norm: It's good to let somebody else take charge
situation: Kent, who doesn't have much work experience, and Edgar are deciding how to split a joint project at work.
intention: Kent wants to impress Edgar.
moral_action: Kent offers to let Edgar take charge and promises to help in any way possible.
moral_consequence: Edgar is happy to lead to project and the project turns out great.
immoral_action: Kent volunteers to be in charge of the project to prove himself to Edgar.
immoral_consequence: Kent's inexperience leads to many mistakes, making Edgar upset and resentful.

norm: It's bad to leave work before your tasks are done.
situation: Maggie is tired and stressed at work; however, Maggie has to finish her paperwork.
intention: Maggie wants to relieve some of her stress.
moral_action: Maggie asks her coworkers to help her out with her paperwork, and she tells them amusing stories while she works.
moral_consequence: Maggie ends up becoming good friends with her coworkers.
immoral_action: Maggie goes home twenty minutes early leaving her paperwork for tomorrow.
immoral_consequence: Maggie has to do more work over the next couple of days to make up for lost time.

norm: You shouldn't jump people.
situation: "Frank lives in the city and finds out that a ""friend"" of his just stole a lot of his money."
intention: Frank wants to get justice on this friend.
moral_action: Frank reports the friend to the police and describes the theft in detail.
moral_consequence: The police arrest the friend and recover the stolen goods.
immoral_action: Frank gets some friends, finds the thief when he's alone, and attacks him.
immoral_consequence: The thief fights back, escalates the conflict, and turns it into an all-out war.

norm: You should apologize to your partner for your mistake.
situation: Angela and Michael are a couple who have been dating for one year, and their anniversary just passed with Angela forgetting to buy Michael a gift.
intention: Angela wants to discuss the anniversary with Michael.
moral_action: Angela apologizes to Michael for forgetting their anniversary and takes him out for a nice dinner to make up for her mistake.
moral_consequence: Michael accepts Angela's apology and gives her a necklace that he bought for their anniversary.
immoral_action: Angela tells Michael that he should have reminded her about the anniversary since he knows that she is forgetful.
immoral_consequence: Michael states that this is the last straw and breaks up with Angela.

norm: It's not okay to steal from othes.
situation: Frank sees Ken riding around on a new bike he got while he is still using the one he got 10 years ago.
intention: Frank wants a newer bike.
moral_action: Frank decides to ask his parents for a new bike since his old one is now far too small for him.
moral_consequence: Frank is surprised when his parents agree and actually get him a new bike.
immoral_action: Frank pushes over Ken and takes his bike and rides away on it.
immoral_consequence: Frank gets grounded for a month for taking someone else's bike.

norm: It's nice to cook dinner for your grandchild.
situation: It's dinnertime and Leopold has been asked to babysit his grandson Peter while Peter's parents are out of town.
intention: Leopold wants to get some dinner for himself and Peter.
moral_action: Leopold surprises Peter and cooks him a special recipe which has been handed down through the family for generations.
moral_consequence: Peter is amazed at the delicious dish and asks Leopold if he'd be willing to share the recipe with him.
immoral_action: Leopold decides to call the local pizzeria and order a couple of pizzas for dinner.
immoral_consequence: Peter enjoys the dinner but doesn't find it very special since this is something that he eats fairly regularly.

norm: It's bad to lie to your employer.
situation: Ivan is planning to take a day off work to go have fun with friends and is about to call his boss to tell him he won't be in.
intention: Ivan wants to pick a reason for why he won't be at work.
moral_action: Ivan tells his boss that he wants the day off for personal reasons and will use one of his allotted vacation days.
moral_consequence: Ivan has a great day with his friends and his boss enjoys seeing the pictures on social media.
immoral_action: Ivan tells his boss that he's not feeling well and will have to use one of his allotted sick days.
immoral_consequence: Ivan's boss later sees pictures of the day on Ivan's social media and fires him for lying.

norm: It's good that an underdog outperforms expectations.
situation: James has a colleague at work who was given a difficult task and performed better than expected.
intention: James wants to react to his colleague's performance.
moral_action: James becomes proud of his colleague for doing the task better than expected.
moral_consequence: James develops a positive relationship with his colleague.
immoral_action: James becomes jealous of his colleague because his colleague did well.
immoral_consequence: James develops a toxic relationship with his colleague.

norm: It is selfish to live vicariously through your children
situation: Dave who is a giant hockey fan is watching his son Max is contemplate which sport he wants to play seriously.
intention: Dave wants to tell Max what Dave thinks is best.
moral_action: Dave tells max that he should definitely pick whatever sport he's drawn to naturally.
moral_consequence: Max ends up picking a sport that's dear to his heart and succeeding at it, helping him achieve and learn.
immoral_action: Dave tells Max he should definitely pick hockey because hockey is the best sport there is.
immoral_consequence: Max ends up hating hockey and drops out of sports entirely becoming an obese adult.

norm: It's wrong to gossip about others.
situation: Habiki is having a conversation with her crush when her sister Misa texts her details about her personal life.
intention: Habiki wants to entertain her crush.
moral_action: Habiki tells her crush theories about their favorite show.
moral_consequence: Habiki's crush invites her to with the show with them on Friday.
immoral_action: Habiki tells her crush about her sister's personal life.
immoral_consequence: Habiki is scolded by her crush for betraying Misa's trust.

norm: It's good to get a job during high school.
situation: Jeremy is in high school and learns about a high school school dance that requires a purchased ticket to attend.
intention: Jeremy wants to find a way to get a ticket to the dance.
moral_action: Jeremy gets a part time job to earn money to pay for a ticket.
moral_consequence: Jeremy will learn how to earn money to through working.
immoral_action: Jeremy begs his parents to buy him a ticket to the dance.
immoral_consequence: Jeremy will not learn how to work for the things he wants.

norm: It's important to help others who are less fortunate.
situation: Mike was walking down the street when he saw a homeless man on the street.
intention: Mike wants to help get the man off of the street.
moral_action: Mike gives the homeless man fifty dollars from his wallet.
moral_consequence: The homeless man is able to get a clean set of clothes and a meal for the night.
immoral_action: Mike starts kicking them man and shoves him until he moves off the street.
immoral_consequence: The homeless man scrapes his hands and knees from Mike's attack.

norm: It's fun to go out with a lot of people.
situation: Ron is very bored on the weekend, not sure what to do.
intention: Ron wants to go out with someone.
moral_action: Ron invites his best friend, along with a few of their other close friends out.
moral_consequence: Ron and them spend the entire night together, having a blast.
immoral_action: Ron invites his best friend out to get dinner and a movie.
immoral_consequence: Ron has a nice time, but admits it could be better.

norm: You shouldn't prey upon people.
situation: Oscar is poor and needs some money for food.
intention: Oscar wants to get money.
moral_action: Oscar gets a job and works hard for money.
moral_consequence: Oscar earns money honestly and buys food.
immoral_action: Oscar hides in an alley and assaults weak people who pass through, taking their money.
immoral_consequence: The police hear about the crimes and arrest Oscar.

norm: It's immoral to purposefully injure another person.

norm: It's not okay to be insulting to a partner's family.

norm: It's bad to run a knife over your significant other.

norm: It's good to excel at things in school.
situation: Liam is a student in high school.

norm: It's wrong to harass someone because of religious differences.
situation: John doesn't know any Jewish people but notices one at the bus stop.

norm: It is good to state opinions in a respectful manner.
situation: Scott's mother makes an assertion regarding a basketball team that he thinks is wrong.
intention: Scott wants to correct his mother.
moral_action: Scott respectfully informs his mother that she is mistaken and tells her the correct information.
moral_consequence: Scott's mother is receptive to his correction and thanks him for informing her.

immoral_consequence: Scott's mother gets defensive and refuses to admit that she might be mistaken.

norm: You should not beat your sibling.
situation: Vinny is playing with his toy when his sister Jane grabs it out of his hands.
intention: Vinny wants to respond to Jane taking the toy.
moral_action: Vinny takes the toy back and explains to Jane she has to ask if she wants to play with it.
moral_consequence: Jane will learn how to play with other people's toys.
immoral_action: Vinny takes the toy back and uses it to hit Jane.
immoral_consequence: Jane will start to cry and be afraid of Vinny.

norm: You shouldn't keep things you aren't supposed to have.
situation: Kara is jogging at her local park when she finds a watch in the grass.
intention: Kara wants a new watch.
moral_action: Kara leaves the watch at the park and orders herself a similar one online.
moral_consequence: Kara gets the satisfaction of having a watch that belongs solely to her.
immoral_action: Kara decides to keep the watch that she finds at the park for herself.
immoral_consequence: Kara is caught taking the watch and is confronted by an observer.

norm: It is nice to be sensitive to others needs.
situation: Tim and his brother both had a sandwich for their school lunch but Tim's brother's sandwich got lost on the bus.
intention: Tim wants to eat something for lunch.
moral_action: Tim eats half of his sandwich and gives the other half to his brother.
moral_consequence: Tim's brother doesn't get too hungry and has an okay day at school.
immoral_action: Tim eats his whole sandwich and doesn't worry about his brother.
immoral_consequence: Tim's brother goes hungry and has a hard time concentrating all day.

norm: You should make amends when you've done something wrong.
situation: Allan borrows Joe's car and breaks the mirror off putting it in the garage.
intention: Allan wants to avoid trouble with Joe.
moral_action: Allan gets a new mirror and replaces it, telling Joe what happened.
moral_consequence: Joe is grateful for Allan's honesty and lets him borrow the car again.
immoral_action: Allan haphazardly glues the mirror back on so that Joe doesn't notice the damage.
immoral_consequence: The mirror falls off when Joe is driving, and he almost wrecks.

norm: It's wrong to confine people.
situation: John finds a neighbor boy snooping through his garage one day after coming home from work.
intention: John wants to punish the boy for going through his things.
moral_action: John demands the boy tell him who he is and then calls the boy's parents to tell them what he did.
moral_consequence: The boy is happy John didn't hurt him and learns his lesson about snooping through other people's things.
immoral_action: John locks the boy in the garage for the rest of the night so that he will learn his lesson.
immoral_consequence: The boy is terrified and is stressed out completely from being trapped in the garage.

norm: It's important to have proper hygiene.
situation: Janice is a grandmother who doesn't shower very often.
intention: Janice wants to visit her grandkids.
moral_action: Janice showers before going to see her grandchildren.
moral_consequence: Janice's grandchildren have fun playing with their grandmother and ask her when she'll visit again.
immoral_action: Having not showered in a month, Janice goes over to see her grandkids.
immoral_consequence: Janice's grandchildren ask their parents why she smells so bad and request that they not invite her over anymore.

norm: Hurting someone with your words is not okay.
situation: Stu is hanging out with friends when he feels hurt by a friend's comment.
intention: Stu wants to let his friend know he is hurt.
moral_action: Stu pulls his friend aside and explains his hurt feelings.
moral_consequence: Stu's friend apologizes for accidentally hurting his feelings, and they make up.
immoral_action: Stu loudly yells at his friend calling him stupid and ugly.
immoral_consequence: Stu's friend leaves the gathering and Stu is asked to leave.

norm: You shouldn't break your classmate's hearts.
situation: Jinyoung is eating lunch when a girl he doesn't love confesses her feelings to him.
intention: Jinyoung wants to respond to the girl.
moral_action: Jinyoung compliments her and offers to set her up with one of his attractive friends.
moral_consequence: The girl falls in love with Jinyoung's friend, and they get into a good relationship.
immoral_action: Jinyoung rejects the girl with blunt words in front of everyone.
immoral_consequence: The girl breaks down crying.

norm: You should not force people into situations they don't like.
situation: Marie's daughter Kayla is a shy girl who is afraid of public speaking but enjoys writing poetry and painting.
intention: Marie wants her daughter to make more friends.
moral_action: Marie signs Kayla up for a small art class that teaches painting.
moral_consequence: Kayla spends time doing something she loves and bonds with the other students over their shared interest.
immoral_action: Marie signs Kayla up for the school play, so she can meet people.
immoral_consequence: Kayla feels anxious and resents Marie for forcing her to do something uncomfortable.

norm: It's not okay to betray your friends.
situation: Jake and Earl made a pact many years ago not to date each other's exes.
intention: Earl has a crush on Jake's ex-girlfriend and wants to ask her out.
moral_action: Earl tells Jake about his feelings and asks to renegotiate their agreement.
moral_consequence: Jake sees that Earl is sincere and decides to drop the pact they made when they were young.
immoral_action: Earl goes behind Jake's back and start's dating his ex-girlfriend secretly.
immoral_consequence: Jake feels betrayed when he finds out and ends the friendship.

norm: You should try to stay in contact with friends.
situation: Gavin has been depressed lately and it has only been getting worse.
intention: Gavin wants to focus on dealing with his depression.
moral_action: Gavin starts going to therapy, and sends his friends a text with updates on what he's going through every couple of weeks.
moral_consequence: Gavin's friends send him kind cards offering encouragement and support which makes Gavin feel really good.
immoral_action: Gavin stops returning his friends calls and texts and focuses solely on trying to get through his depression.
immoral_consequence: Gavin's friends whom are unaware of his depression assume he doesn't care about them, and stop trying to reach out to him.

norm: You shouldn't eat food that isn't yours.
situation: Joey's date Melinda is in the restaurant restroom when their desserts arrive, and after taking a bite of his own, Joey realizes that he hates it.
intention: Joey wants to enjoy some dessert.
moral_action: Joey flags down the waiter and asks for the same dessert that Melinda ordered.
moral_consequence: Melinda offers Joey some of her dessert while he waits for his own.
immoral_action: Joey eats some of Melinda's dessert while she is in the restroom.
immoral_consequence: Melinda is upset when she returns and decides to end the date early.

norm: It's kind to thank your boss when he resigns.
situation: Lina has been working with her boss Pete for several years and Pete is resigning.
intention: Lina wants to say goodbye to Pete.
moral_action: Lina attends Pete's farewell party and thanks him for his mentorship with a card and a hug.
moral_consequence: The next year, when Lina applies for a new job, she uses Pete as a reference, and he gives her a glowing review, leading to her getting the job.
immoral_action: Lina attends Pete's farewell party and tells him goodbye and that she is glad he is moving on because he  was such a demanding manager.

norm: It is good to be a good host.
situation: After a very stressful week at work, Jane is throwing a party at her house for her friends.
intention: Jane wants to speak to the guests.

moral_consequence: The guests are able to enjoy themselves through the company and fun conversation.
immoral_action: Jane speaks to the guests but keeps remarking about how stressed out she is.

norm: It is wrong to swear in front of children.

norm: It's good to clean up after your animals.
situation: Dylan is at home with his dog when it takes a poop in his living room behind the couch.

norm: It is disturbing to hurt animals intentionally.
situation: Clara, who is allergic to cats, spends a lot of time with her friend Patricia, who owns a cat that often pesters Clara.
intention: Clara wants Patricia's cat to leave her alone.

moral_consequence: Patricia keeps her door closed when Clara is over so that her cat can't bother her.

norm: It is wrong to intentionally put people's safety at risk
situation: Eric is supposed to drive his friends on a road trip but noticed something was off with one of his car's wheels.

moral_consequence: The car is repaired in time for the trip and everyone gets to the destination safely.

norm: It's bad to yell at little kids.

norm: It's good to go camping with others.

norm: It is kind to give your friend a present.

norm: You shouldn't let your children get spray tans.

norm: It's bad to do illegal things to make money.

norm: It's not okay to be late in paying your dues.

norm: It's good to communicate about problems with a friend.

norm: It's bad to say something that hurts your significant other.

norm: It's wrong to beat women.

norm: It's nice to have a holiday party.

norm: A partner should be proud to show off your relationship.

moral_consequence: Sue loves Bill even more for his bravery, and they get married.
immoral_action: Bill keeps the relationship from his parents and never introduces Sue to them.
immoral_consequence: Sue becomes resentful and eventually breaks up with Bill.

norm: You shouldn't stalk your significant other.
situation: Larry is feeling lonely.
intention: Larry wants to spend time with his partner.
moral_action: Larry texts his partner to ask to spend time together after work.
moral_consequence: Larry and his partner have a fun night watching movies and talking.
immoral_action: Larry follows his partner when they leave work to see where they are going.
immoral_consequence: Larry's partner breaks up with him and threatens a restraining order.

norm: It's good to be forgiving.
situation: Candice watches her sister accidentally break her expensive ball joint doll.
intention: Candice wants to respond to her sister.
moral_action: Candice gives her sister a hug telling her that accidents happen every now and then.
moral_consequence: Candice does extra chores around the house for enough money to get Candice's doll fixed.
immoral_action: Candice compares her sister to a clumsy monkey in a loud tone, and reminds her sister about her mistake every day for a week.
immoral_consequence: Candice sister's self esteem is ruined.

norm: It's not okay to set someone up to hurt them.
situation: Josh and his friends like to prank each other, and Josh has not pranked Jerry in a while.
intention: Josh wants to prank Jerry.
moral_action: Josh sets up an innocuous prank that startles Jerry, but doesn't emotionally devastate him.
moral_consequence: Jerry laughs at the prank and tells Josh that he owes him one.
immoral_action: Josh sets up a prank that makes Jerry think his parents have died in a car accident.
immoral_consequence: Jerry is devastated, then angry a Josh and tells him not to talk to him again.

norm: It's rude to pointlessly criticize someone on their job.
situation: Alex has been watching Theresa work, every day, as a colleague, and he notices things that she is doing wrong.
intention: Alex wants to advise Theresa on how to improve her work performance.
moral_action: Alex mentions to Theresa that he found a better way to work, and he shows her what he's been doing.
moral_consequence: Theresa is willing to listen to his idea about a better way to do their job.
immoral_action: Alex lists all of the things that he has noticed that Theresa is doing wrong, and he tells her she needs to do a better job.
immoral_consequence: Theresa is defensive and offended by all of the criticism, and she ignores Alex's unsolicited list.

norm: It's good to volunteer to help the needy.
situation: John's college requires him to do a certain amount of volunteer work in order to graduate.
intention: John wants to fulfill the volunteering requirement.
moral_action: John volunteers at a local soup kitchen for several hours every week.
moral_consequence: John feels happy and fulfilled and graduates as planned.
immoral_action: John forges documents to make it appear that he satisfies the volunteering requirements.
immoral_consequence: John's lies are discovered, and he is unable to graduate on time.

norm: It's wrong to take advantage of people who are depressed.
situation: Elisa's friend Alice has a depression and Elisa needs help in cleaning her house because she is busy with her work lately.
intention: Elisa wants to get help for cleaning her house.
moral_action: Elisa hires a maid to clean her house and asks Alice to supervise the maid.
moral_consequence: Alice feels proud and instructs the maid how to clean the house.
immoral_action: Elisa asks Alice to spend time cleaning her house because it can alleviate her depression.
immoral_consequence: Alice feels lonely and gets more depressed.

norm: It's wrong not to be fair to others.
situation: Lisa collects money from all of her friends to buy concert tickets to an upcoming show, but one friend gives her too much money.
intention: Lisa needs to decide whether to refund the excess money that her friend gave her.
moral_action: Lisa refunds the extra money to her friend, when she gives her the ticket to the show.
moral_consequence: Her friend thanks her for catching the mistake and Lisa feels like a good friend.
immoral_action: Lisa pockets the extra money that her friend had given her, never mentioning that she hadn't spent it on the ticket.
immoral_consequence: Lisa's friend finds out that the tickets were less expensive than she thought and confronts Lisa, Lisa is ashamed and her friend is angry.

norm: It is wrong to show off at work.
situation: Jennie is notified that she has won employee of the month today by her boss.
intention: Jennie wants to celebrate winning.
moral_action: Jennie shakes her boss's hand in thanks and orders lunch for herself and office mates for the occasion.
moral_consequence: Jennie boss keeps Jennie in mind for a promotion due to her humbleness and kindness.
immoral_action: Jennie takes a very vocal victory lap around the office while everyone watches.
immoral_consequence: Jennie's boss reprimands her for disruptive behavior and takes away the award.

norm: It's wrong to cause someone's death.
situation: Tim is upset that the other car on the road cut him off while driving.
intention: Tim wants to vent his anger.
moral_action: Tim takes a breath and drives to his local gym to work out.
moral_consequence: Tim stays out of jail and lives a happy life.
immoral_action: Tim pulls out his pistol and shoots the other driver dead.
immoral_consequence: Tim is arrested and spends the rest of his life in jail and is sad.

norm: It's good to celebrate the holidays with others.
situation: James choose to stay in his dorm room over the holidays because he was an orphan.
intention: James wants to enjoy his Christmas dinner.
moral_action: James goes door-to-door in his dorm to invite the few other people staying over for Christmas dinner.
moral_consequence: James makes several new friends his the delicious celebratory meal he cooks.
immoral_action: James cooks a turkey, potatoes, vegetables and bread and eats alone in his dorm room.
immoral_consequence: James savors the food and his favorite TV show, but still feels some pangs of loneliness.

norm: It is good to return things that are lost.
situation: Crystal is a bartender and a customer left behind a jacket after having some drinks.
intention: Crystal wants to pick up the jacket.
moral_action: Crystal takes the jacket and hangs it in the stock room just in case the customer comes looking.
moral_consequence: The customer comes in the next day looking for his jacket and Crystal goes into the stock room and gives it back which makes him happy.
immoral_action: Crystal takes the jacket and tosses it in the trash, thinking that the customer will never come back for it.
immoral_consequence: The customer comes in the next day looking for his jacket and Crystal is unable to give it back which disappoints him.

norm: You shouldn't get your coworker fired.
situation: Brenda has been called into her manager's office to discuss a problem that occurred between her and a coworker.
intention: Brenda wants to make herself look good.
moral_action: Brenda impresses the manager by accepting responsibility for the situation and suggesting ways to improve.
moral_consequence: Brenda feels good that she was honest.
immoral_action: Brenda says that the coworker was responsible for the incident and gets the coworker fired.
immoral_consequence: Brenda feels bad knowing that her lie about the coworker resulted in the coworkers firing.

norm: You should never blame someone else for your mistakes.
situation: Tom is a team leader has made a serious error in the important team project that was just submitted.
intention: Tom wants to avoid getting in trouble at work.
moral_action: Tom works extra hours to fix the mistake on his own time and explains it to his boss.
moral_consequence: Tom protects his team from disciplinary action.
immoral_action: Tom tells his superiors that one of his colleagues, rather than him, was in charge of that part of the project.
immoral_consequence: Tom gets someone else in trouble for their mistake.

norm: It's detestable to abuse a child.
situation: John just lost his job and comes home to see his kids in front of the tv.
intention: John wants to vent his anger.
moral_action: John takes a breath and goes to his upstairs gym to work out with weights.
moral_consequence: John's kids are unharmed and have no reason not to love John.
immoral_action: John raises his voice at his kids and reaches for a belt as he comes at them.
immoral_consequence: John's kids are terrified of John and feel sad and depressed.

norm: You shouldn't feed your family's pets unless you have permission.
situation: Tyler is a child whose family has a pet dog that always looks at him during dinner.
intention: Tyler wants to feed the dog.
moral_action: Tyler asks his parents if he can give the dog food.
moral_consequence: Tyler learns from his parents what foods can be given and when and the dog eats food it is supposed to eat.
immoral_action: Tyler gives the dog table scraps after dinner without telling anyone.
immoral_consequence: The dog suffers health problems from eating odd foods and Tyler never learns what foods are acceptable to give.

norm: You should try to be a good neighbor
situation: Noah is out of sugar and decides to ask the woman next door, Gloria, if she has any he can borrow.
intention: Gloria wants to respond to the request.
moral_action: Gloria tells Noah to hang on while she checks, and she returns with an entire bag.
moral_consequence: Noah thinks that Gloria  is kind and, and he appreciates the favor very much.
immoral_action: Gloria  tells Noah that she's too busy to look and snidely asks him to leave her alone.
immoral_consequence: Noah feels that Gloria  was rude to him and now he dislikes her.

norm: It's good to offer condolences.
situation: Joe is at a funeral for a friend and the friend's parents are there.
intention: Joe wants to talk to the parents of the deseased.
moral_action: Joe talks to the parents and tries to make them happy, by offering his condolences.
moral_consequence: The parents are glad Joe did that, and they all have a better day.
immoral_action: Joe talks about the weather with the parents but does not offer his condolences.
immoral_consequence: The parents remain sad and Joe wonders if he approached this wrong.

norm: You shouldn't beat someone up.
situation: Bob is at a bar when a drunk customer begins making trouble in the bar, threatening people with a bottle.
intention: Bob wants to protect the customers.
moral_action: Bob lunges at the customer, takes away the bottle, and pins the customer to the ground.
moral_consequence: The customer is very angry but unharmed and is escorted out of the bar.
immoral_action: Bob charges the drunk customer, disarms him, and punches him repeatedly.
immoral_consequence: The customer is badly wounded and reports Bob to the police, who then arrest Bob.

norm: Providing shoddy service can get you in trouble at work.
situation: Tyler is at work working the cashier with a long line, and is very tired.
intention: Tyler wants to go home.
moral_action: Tyler focuses on his work and does his best to help the last couple of customers.
moral_consequence: Time flies and before he knows it, it is time to go home.
immoral_action: Tyler rushes through the last few customers, so he can go home early.
immoral_consequence: Tyler gives them the wrong change and has to pay the difference out of his own pocket.

norm: You shouldn't try to return an item that you damaged.
situation: Mackenzie tears a hole in her new sweater when she plays with her dog.
intention: Mackenzie wants to get rid of her sweater.
moral_action: After cutting off the damaged parts, Mackenzie transforms her sweater into a small hat.
moral_consequence: Mackenzie gets compliments on her new hat.
immoral_action: Mackenzie tells the people at the store that the sweater is a flawed birthday gift.
immoral_consequence: Mackenzie is exposed when someone working that day calls her untrue statement out.

norm: It's inappropriate to fart at a funeral.
situation: Jake ate a large meal in the morning before his grandmother's funeral, and is now at the church and has some bad gas.
intention: Jake really needs to get some relief.
moral_action: Jake quietly excuses himself and steps outside to do his business.
moral_consequence: Fellow attendants briefly notice Jake's absence but pay it no mind, assuming he had something important to take care of.
immoral_action: Jake stands his ground and lets one rip, blanketing the area.
immoral_consequence: Fellow attendants are let gasping for air, and all eyes are locked accusingly on Jake.

norm: It's inconsiderate to delay paying someone back.
situation: Latoya received a large bonus from work after Crystal loaned her $150 from the money she had set aside for bills.
intention: Latoya wants to save money for a phone.
moral_action: Latoya give Crystal the money she owes her and deposits the rest in the bank.
moral_consequence: Crystal is happy that Latoya paid her back and is able to pay her bills.
immoral_action: Latoya puts her entire check in the bank figuring Crystal can wait a few more weeks for her money.
immoral_consequence: Crystal is angry with Latoya since she will get a late fee on her electric bill.

norm: It is wrong to film inappropriate things.
situation: Bob is taking a videography class and has a gay roommate, who has a boyfriend.
intention: Bob wants to film his roommate and his boyfriend for his class.
moral_action: Bob films his roommate and his boyfriend having a date.
moral_consequence: Bob's teacher sees Bob's filming skills and gives him a good grade.
immoral_action: Bob films his roommate and his boyfriend having sex.
immoral_consequence: Bob's teacher is disgusted and Bob fails the course.

norm: It's wrong to give away something that isn't yours.
situation: Oakley needs to make his student loan payment, and someone wants to pay him forty dollars for his roomate's favorite figure.
intention: Oakley wants to get money.
moral_action: Oakley sells some of his old things at a thrift store for cash.
moral_consequence: Oakley feels less stressed after paying for his student loans.
immoral_action: Oakley sells his roomate's figure to get cash.
immoral_consequence: His roommate takes Oakley's apartment key and locks him out of the house for a week.

norm: You should give candy to children on Halloween.
situation: Jason is looking forward to celebrating Halloween at home this year.
intention: Jason wants to answer the door for trick-or-treaters.
moral_action: Jason gives out full size chocolate bars to the trick-or-treaters.
moral_consequence: The trick-or-treaters are very pleased and thank Jason for making their Halloween happier.
immoral_action: Jason decides to give out toothbrushes to the trick-or-treaters.
immoral_consequence: The trick-or-treaters are unhappy about the toothbrushes and don't want to come to Jason's house next year.

norm: It's important to fulfill your responsibilities.
situation: Jordan got invited to a soccer game just as he was about to do the dishes, which he was asked to do.
intention: Jordan wants to go to the soccer game.
moral_action: Jordan goes to the soccer game but does the dishes after he comes back.
moral_consequence: Jordan is thanked for doing the dishes and gets a lot done.
immoral_action: Jordan goes to the soccer game and forgets the dishes afterward.
immoral_consequence: Jordan gets in trouble for not doing the dishes and feels like a failure.

norm: People should support others in their efforts to better themselves.
situation: Jack's friend is trying to lose weight and wants Jack's opinion on his progress.
intention: Jack wants to be honest with his friend.
moral_action: Jack tells his friend that he's proud of the progress that he's made so far.
moral_consequence: Jack's friend feels more motivated to lose weight.
immoral_action: Jack tells his friend that he's wasting his time.
immoral_consequence: Jack's friend loses motivation to keep losing weight.

norm: You shouldn't steal candy from kids.
situation: It's Halloween, and Marcus sees that his younger sister Rita has brought home a lot of candy.
intention: Marcus wants some of his sister Rita's candy.
moral_action: Marcus asks Rita if he can have some of her candy, and she shares with him happily.
moral_consequence: Marcus gets candy, Rita isn't mad at him, and Mom doesn't have to get involved at all.
immoral_action: Marcus waits till Rita goes to bed, then takes her bag of candy, eats some and hides the rest in his dresser.
immoral_consequence: Rita notices her candy is gone the next morning, accuses Marcus of taking it, and he's caught with the stolen goods by their mom.

norm: You shouldn't let others pressure you to do things.
situation: Kiran is feeling tired from a weekend of going out to bars with his friends, but they are trying to persuade him to go out again.
intention: Kiran wants to avoid disappointing his friends.
moral_action: Kiran tells his friends that he needs to take a night off but makes plans to go out with them later that week.
moral_consequence: Kiran feels better after resting for a couple days and has a good time when he goes out with his friends again.
immoral_action: Kiran agrees to go out with his friends, and they go out and drink a fair amount including some shots of whiskey.
immoral_consequence: Kiran starts to feel sick from all the drinking, vomits, and has to leave the bar.

norm: It's good to stop your child from being rude.
situation: Sarah's son is on a play date with the neighbors kid, when he asks them why they are so fat.
intention: Sarah wants her children to make new friends.
moral_action: Sarah calls her son over and immediately explains that he shouldn't call other people fat.
moral_consequence: Sarah's son apologizes to the other children, and they end up becoming great friends.
immoral_action: Sarah decides not to say anything because she doesn't want to embarrass her son.
immoral_consequence: Sarah's neighbor asks her and her son to leave, and doesn't let them play together and more.

norm: It's good to keep others accountable for their actions
situation: Ron is an accountability partner with Bill in their AA group.
intention: Ron wants to be friends with Bill.
moral_action: Ron calls Bill every night when Bill admits stuggling with temptation after getting laid off.
moral_consequence: Ron helps Bill get through the rough patch and Bill is able to continue sobriety.
immoral_action: Ron looks the other way when Bill talks about relapsing.
immoral_consequence: Bill is arrested for a DWI and Ron feels guilty.

norm: You shouldn't lie to your partner.
situation: Angie likes to wear the latest styles but her husband Randy doesn't like it when spends lots of money on clothes.
intention: Angie wants to go shopping.
moral_action: Angie buys a lot while shopping, but she tells Randy how much she spent rather than lie to him.
moral_consequence: Randy tells Angie that she knows he doesn't like it when she overspends, she needs to cut back.
immoral_action: Angie buys several new outfits from the current season and tells Randy that they were all heavily discounted since they are from the last season.
immoral_consequence: Randy asks to see the receipt for the clothes and is upset when he discovers that Angie lied to him.

norm: It is rude to bump someone with your car.
situation: Kurt is on his way to work when a bicyclist cuts in front of him, slowing down traffic.
intention: Kurt wants to make it to work on time.
moral_action: Kurt honks his horn at the bicyclist and when he doesn't slow down, Kurt takes an alternate route to work.
moral_consequence: Kurt makes it to work on time without getting into any road incidents.
immoral_action: Kurt lightly bumps the bicyclist's back tire with his car, hoping he'll move out of the way.
immoral_consequence: The bicyclist calls the cops and Kurt is fined for his action.

norm: It's reprehensible to want to own slaves.
situation: Mr. Tucket owned a large plantation with many cabins and shelters and often lost money because of labor shortages.
intention: Mr. Tucket wants to find a reliable labor source.
moral_action: Mr. Tucket decides to rent the cabins and shelters each would have a person working year round for rent.
moral_consequence: Mr. Tucket is seen  as progressive and compassionate gaining him a say in town matters.
immoral_action: Mr. Tucket decides to buy slaves they would have to stay and work with no pay.
immoral_consequence: The community shuns Mr. Tucket, and he loses more money because no one will buy, sell or trade with him now.

norm: You shouldn't hate the love of your life.
situation: John and his girlfriend, who was the love of his life, break up after relationship troubles.
intention: John wants to find some closure and get his feelings in order about the relationship and it's ending.
moral_action: John remains grateful for experiencing their time together and hopes that he and his ex-girlfriend can maintain a civil relationship.
moral_consequence: John does not feel that the time he spent with his ex-girlfriend has become an emotional wound, but rather he remembers the time they spent together fondly.
immoral_action: After thinking about the situation for some time, John decides that he hates his ex-girlfriend and never wants to see her again.
immoral_consequence: John feels an intense sense of loss and experiences a range of uncomfortable emotions every time he thinks of her and their time together.

norm: It's rude to make fun of someone's hands.
situation: Erika watches her classmates making fun of the shy girl sitting in the corner of the room.
intention: Erika wants her classmates to accept her.
moral_action: Erika tells her classmate a joke about their teacher.
moral_consequence: Erika's joke makes everyone including the shy girl laugh making her more popular.
immoral_action: Erika compares the shy girl's hands to a hairy gorilla.
immoral_consequence: Erika feels bad when her shy classmate slips her hands into her jacket and cries.

norm: It is wrong to call the police on a friend.
situation: Bryan and Marco are friends at Bryan's house and Marco just downloaded an illegal file from Bryan's internet.
intention: Bryan wants his friend Marco to know that downloading illegal files is wrong.
moral_action: Bryan asks Marco not to download from his computer because he doesn't want to get in trouble.
moral_consequence: Marco is grateful and stops downloading and they remain friends.
immoral_action: Bryan picks up the phone and calls the cops and tells them that Marco downloaded illegally.
immoral_consequence: The cops reprimand Marco and Marco ends his friendship with Bryan.

norm: It is important to interact with your co-workers.
situation: Ron is working on a large project with his co-workers, and the team is having a meeting.
intention: Ron wants to go to the meeting.
moral_action: Ron goes to the meeting and tries to help come up with some solutions to problems.
moral_consequence: Ron's coworkers like what Ron has to offer and accept his ideas.
immoral_action: Ron goes to the meeting and stares off into space, thinking his own thoughts.
immoral_consequence: Ron's coworkers think that Ron doesn't care and leave him out of some important decisions.

norm: It's important to communicate when your friend upsets you.
situation: John is having a conversation with his friend Jim when he makes a comment that doesn't sit well with Jim.
intention: Jim wants to react to the comment.
moral_action: Jim tells John that his comment upset him and explains why.
moral_consequence: John apologizes to Jim for making him feel that way and the two become closer over it.
immoral_action: Jim keeps his feelings to himself and begins acting cold toward John.
immoral_consequence: Things become tense between the two as John wonders why Jim is acting so strangely.

norm: You should not do things that will upset your parents.
situation: Andy promised his parents he would call if he would be late and his group of friends wants him to stay longer.
intention: Andy wants to stay with his group of friends.
moral_action: Andy calls his parents telling them he will be staying with his friends.
moral_consequence: Andy's parents are glad he called to check in.
immoral_action: Andy stays with his friends without calling his parents to let them know he is ok.
immoral_consequence: Andy's parents are worried about him because he has not called.

norm: It's wrong to ditch your friends.
situation: Jan is out binge drinking with her best-friend when she meets a cute guy from her class who asks her to go home with him.
intention: Jan wants to give the cute guy an answer.
moral_action: Jan asks the cute guy for a rain check and sticks with her girlfriend.
moral_consequence: Jan ensures both she and her girlfriend get home safely.
immoral_action: Jan leaves her friend and goes home with the cute classmate.
immoral_consequence: Jan is shocked to find out that her drunk girlfriend was later sexually assaulted.

norm: It's kind to help a stranger who has been injured.
situation: Tanya is running late to get to work when she comes across a man who has collapsed on the side of the street.
intention: Tanya doesn't want to get in trouble with her boss.
moral_action: Tanya phones her boss to say that she is on her way but needs to stop to help an injured man.
moral_consequence: The man gets the help he needs right away and Tanya's boss understands why she is late.
immoral_action: Tanya continues on her way to work and leaves the man on the side of the street.
immoral_consequence: The man's condition worsens because he did not get medical attention sooner, and he ends up with long-lasting complications.

norm: It's kind to help a classmate out with assignments.
situation: Laura and Emma are in study hall together and Laura notices that Emma is struggling with her work.
intention: Laura wants to talk to Emma during study hall.
moral_action: Laura asks Emma if she wants any help with the homework and goes over the worksheet with her.
moral_consequence: Emma and Laura have fun talking and working together and Emma does well on her work.
immoral_action: Laura distracts Emma from her studies with gossip about things going on around the school.
immoral_consequence: Emma forgets about completing her assignments and spends study hall talking which leads her to get a poor grade.

norm: It's dangerous to block the sidewalk.
situation: Sally decides to open up a lemonade stand to make some money.
intention: Sally wants to be in a visible spot.
moral_action: Sally get her parents permission to place the lemonade stand at the end of the driveway by the sidewalk.
moral_consequence: Sally attracts a lot of neighbors on walks and makes almost 50 dollars in one day.
immoral_action: Sally places her lemonade stand in the middle of the sidewalk where many neighbors walk.
immoral_consequence: Another neighborhood kid on their bike is not paying attention and crashes into her lemonade stand destroying everything.

norm: It's wrong to be disrespectful to your best friend.
situation: Bill's friend Ted asks how his new outfit looks before going out on a first date.
intention: Bill wants to respond to Ted's question.
moral_action: Bill tells Ted that he looks handsome and his date will love him.
moral_consequence: Ted feels attractive and confident for his upcoming date.
immoral_action: Bill tells his friend that the outfit looks terrible and his date won't find him attractive.
immoral_consequence: Ted feels sad and goes home to find a new outfit.

norm: You should change your clothes if you mess them up.
situation: Mack has become tired and dirty from crawling through the crawl space under his house.
intention: Mack wants to take a rest.
moral_action: Mack changes into a fresh outfit and sits on the recliner.
moral_consequence: Mack is able to relax.
immoral_action: Mack sits down in his recliner.
immoral_consequence: Mack gets dirt all over the recliner.

norm: It's wrong not to have your parents at your wedding.
situation: Isabella wants to have a wedding at a big church, and her parents are out of town on the only open time slot.
intention: Isabella wants to get married.
moral_action: Isabella chooses to have a wedding at another location that works with her parent's schedule .
moral_consequence: Isabella's parents enjoy watching their daughter's wedding.
immoral_action: Isabella goes ahead with the wedding at the church.
immoral_consequence: Isabella's parents are hurt when they discover Isabella's actions.

norm: It is good to respect other people's space.
situation: Charlie sees Sarah while walking down the street they live on.
intention: Charlie wants to talk to Sarah.
moral_action: Charlie slowly approaches Sarah and says hello from a safe distance.
moral_consequence: Sarah is happy to talk to her neighbor, and they have a nice conversation.
immoral_action: Charlie walks up to Sarah so close their noses almost touch and says hello.
immoral_consequence: Sarah quickly backs away and angrily accuses Charlie of being weird.

norm: It is wrong to stab cab drivers
situation: Peter took a cab home from the bar and ended up upsetting the cab driver by tipping too little.
intention: Peter wants to resolve the argument.
moral_action: Peter kicks in a few more dollars, placating the cab driver.
moral_consequence: Peter gets out of the cab and sleeps in his own bed that night.
immoral_action: Peter stabs the cab driver repeatedly, causing him grave injury.
immoral_consequence: Peter is arrested for attempted murder and spends years in prison.

norm: It's good to be certified for CPR.
situation: Rob's job requires him to get certified in CPR every two years, so he must get certified before the deadline.
intention: Rob wants to get his CPR certification.
moral_action: Rob contacts the American Red Cross and spends fifty dollars and a Saturday getting his CPR card.
moral_consequence: Rob's supervisor accepts the Red Cross card as proof of certification.
immoral_action: Rob finds a guy on Craig's list who sells CPR cards for thirty dollars so Rob doesn't have to waste time in a CPR class.
immoral_consequence: Rob's supervisor is suspicious of the card's legitimacy and begins to distrust Rob.

norm: There are some words that you should never say.
situation: Dean is watching a movie in a theater while two black people sit behind him and talk loudly to each other.
intention: Dean wants to confront the loud moviegoers behind him.
moral_action: Dean turns around and firmly tells the loud moviegoers to be quiet so other people can watch the movie.
moral_consequence: Other people at the movie cheer for Dean for confronting the disruptive black people.
immoral_action: Dean turns around and tells the loud moviegoers to be quiet and then calls them the n-word.
immoral_consequence: Other people at the movie boo Dean and throw popcorn at him for using racist language.

norm: It's kind to give presents to your nieces and nephews.
situation: Banjo listens to his niece Angela  tell him about improving her science grade from a D to a B.
intention: Banjo wants to respond to his niece.
moral_action: Banjo buys Angela a new doll at the toy store.
moral_consequence: Angela is inspired to work harder in school making straight A's by the end of the year.
immoral_action: Banjo tells his Angela that they should avoid celebrating until her grade improves to an A.
immoral_consequence: Angela's self esteem plummits.

norm: It's good to be honest when you've broken something.
situation: Liam has a heated discussion with his wife, leaves the house in a hurry and breaks a vase that his wife likes a lot.
intention: Liam doesn't want his wife to think that he is a destructive person.
moral_action: Liam tells his wife he did it but that it was an accident and apologizes.
moral_consequence: Their son is glad to see his mother forgive his father.
immoral_action: Liam hides the fact that he broke the vase and blames their son instead.
immoral_consequence: The son is sad and angry to be unjustly treated.

norm: It's good to help people out during the holidays.
situation: Darren makes good money at his job, but his neighbor Glen has no money to celebrate Christmas with his son.
intention: Darren wants to spend some money.
moral_action: Darren gives two hundred dollars to Glen, so he can buy a Christmas tree and presents for his son.
moral_consequence: Glen's son gets a new sled for Christmas and goes sledding with his schoolmates on a local hill.
immoral_action: Darren buys himself a new high-definition TV to watch football games on.
immoral_consequence: Glen's son doesn't get any presents for Christmas and kids at school make fun of him when they find out.

norm: It's wrong to steal people's pain meds.
situation: Pam has been having back pains for a while and knows her roommate, who has chronic pain, has pain meds in her dresser.
intention: Pam wants the pain to stop.
moral_action: Pam goes to the clinic and asks a doctor for something to alleviate her back pain.
moral_consequence: Pam is feeling better and her roommate still has her pain meds when she needs them.
immoral_action: Pam takes her roommate's pain meds without asking first.
immoral_consequence: Pam's roommate finds her pain meds are gone when she looks for them in the evening and spends the night being in pain.

norm: Delivery drivers shouldn't enter the homes of customers.
situation: Jay is a pizza delivery driver who is currently delivering an order.
intention: Jay wants to deliver the pizza on time.
moral_action: Jay arrives with the pizza and the door is open, so he stands by the door to yell in for the customer.
moral_consequence: The customer is excited knowing that their pizza has just arrived.
immoral_action: Jay arrives at the house to an open door and steps just inside the doorway to look for the customer.
immoral_consequence: The customer is alarmed that Jay would step foot inside his house.

norm: It's not okay for a parent to make themself unapprochable.
situation: Scott is a fund manager who has to work from home now, and his son wants to play catch.
intention: Scott has to teach his son not to interrupt him while he's working.
moral_action: Scott tells his son that he can play catch with him after work.
moral_consequence: Scott's son understands that his dad is busy a lot and has other responsibilities.
immoral_action: Scott tells his son to not bother him when he's busy ever again.
immoral_consequence: Scott's son becomes scared to come to him for anything.

norm: It's nice to take in grandchildren.
situation: Jack's daughter is a drug addict that is being forced to give up her children.
intention: Jack wants to figure out what to do with his grandchildren.
moral_action: Jack offers to take care of the children from now on.
moral_consequence: Jack's grandchildren are better taken care of, and they feel loved.
immoral_action: Jack agrees to put the kids in an orphanage, because he doesn't want to look after them.
immoral_consequence: Jack's grandchildren are scared and don't have anyone they can trust.

norm: Moms and dads should get along with each other.
situation: Halina that her husband Andrew has made several large electronics purchases on their credit card, and their son is in the room.
intention: Halina wants to confront her husband.
moral_action: Halina invites him on a date, and suggests that they come up with a budget.
moral_consequence: Andrew stops spending money when he realizes how his actions are hurting the family.
immoral_action: Halina shows the bill to her husband scolding him in front of their son.
immoral_consequence: Andrew is humiliated and hides from his family.

norm: It's bad to like people who exhibit criminal tendencies.
situation: Felicia realizes she's falling for Phil, an excon biker in a motorcycle gang who she's dating and her parents urge her to break it off.
intention: Felicia needs to decide whether to listen to her parents.
moral_action: Felicia decides it's best to end things with Phil as he doesn't seem like good relationship material.
moral_consequence: Phil is prevented from casing her parent's house, which he was in the process of doing, and gets frustrated and leaves.
immoral_action: Felicia decides to continue dating Phil in spite of her parent's wishes.
immoral_consequence: Phil later breaks into her parent's place and steals their TV, and then dumps and leaves Felicia.

norm: It's rude to damage other people's property.
situation: Mark and Maggie have an argument which leads to a breakup.
intention: Mark wants to vent his frustrations.
moral_action: Mark writes all of his bad feelings in his journal.
moral_consequence: Mark gains a deeper understanding of his emotions.
