immoral_action: Mark kicks the side of Maggie's car leaving a dent in the side.
immoral_consequence: Maggie sues Mark.

norm: You shouldn't tell your partner who to see.
situation: Brian and Danielle are dating but both busy people.
intention: Brian wants to spend more time with Danielle.
moral_action: Brian and Danille talk about htier schedule, they decide that friday is date night and saturday is a night for friends.
moral_consequence: The relationship is more balanced and beings to progress.
immoral_action: Brian forbids Danielle to see her friends and that she should be spending her free time with him only.
immoral_consequence: Danielle finds him to be too controlling and break up with him.

norm: You shouldn't take money that you didn't earn.
situation: Scott is finishing his breakfast at a diner when he receives the bill and realizes that he doesn't have enough cash in his wallet to cover it.
intention: Scott wants to pay for his meal.
moral_action: Scott uses his credit card instead of cash to pay his bill.
moral_consequence: Scott's payment is accepted, and he leaves the diner.
immoral_action: Scott takes a tip left by another diner for the waitress off of their table and uses it to pay for his meal.
immoral_consequence: Scott is caught taking the tip and banned from returning to the diner.

norm: You shouldn't access an online account that isn't yours.
situation: Tom's roommate Jim has an Amazon Prime account but Tom does not.
intention: Tom wants to watch a movie that's on Amazon Prime Video.
moral_action: Tom starts a trial Amazon Prime membership so that he can watch the movie.
moral_consequence: Tom really enjoys watching the film.
immoral_action: Without asking Tom goes into Jim's room, finds his password, and logs into his Prime account to watch the movie.
immoral_consequence: Jim comes home and gets angry at Tom for violating his trust and using his account without permission.

norm: It's bad to buy things you can't afford.
situation: Kate is in the jewelry shop in the mall and is excited to see different types of jewelries.
intention: Kate wants to look good in an upcoming wedding party.
moral_action: Kate looks around and picks up an affordable but beautiful necklace.
moral_consequence: Kate is happy to pay for the necklace without incurring any debts.
immoral_action: Kate buys a very expensive necklace with no regards to its price.
immoral_consequence: Kate needs to use multiple credit cards incurring high interest debts.

norm: You shouldn't prevent grandparents from seeing their grandchild.
situation: Toby's parents live in an old, decrepit house full of stairs - but they love Toby's young daughter and want to see her.
intention: Toby wants his daughter to be safe.
moral_action: Toby suggests meeting his parents in a park for a picnic with his daughter for the afternoon.
moral_consequence: Toby's parents are delighted to see their granddaughter.
immoral_action: Toby refuses to bring his daughter to his parents' place because he is afraid she will get hurt in the unsafe house.
immoral_consequence: Toby's parents are brokenhearted and pine for their granddaughter.

norm: Bullying is mean.
situation: Tom finds out a classmate of his stole a pencil from him without asking.
intention: Tom wants to teach his classmate a lesson for stealing.
moral_action: Tom tells his classmate to stop stealing, using examples, without being mean.
moral_consequence: Tom's classmate thanks Tom for the lesson, and they get along the rest of the year.
immoral_action: Tom comes up with mean nicknames for his classmate and taunts him the rest of the schoolyear.
immoral_consequence: Tom gets sent to the principle multiple times, and Tom's classmate feels humiliated.

norm: It's inconsiderate and rude to yell
situation: Christian has just checked in a hotel after a long and exhausting day of travel, and he is very dissatisfied with his hotel room.
intention: Christian wants to switch rooms and get a better hotel room.
moral_action: Christian goes to the front desk and explains the issues he has with his room, respectfully demanding to switch rooms.
moral_consequence: The receptionist is happy to assist Christian and appreciates the way he has conducted himself.
immoral_action: Christian goes to the front desk and yells at the receptionist, venting his frustration on her and demanding to be moved to a better room.
immoral_consequence: Christian's behavior makes the receptionist feel anxious, stressed and overall horrible.

norm: You should give plenty of notice before cancelling plans.
situation: Yuri has planned a vacation with a friend which is about 3 months away and has just found out she has to attend a work function during that time.
intention: Yuri wants to let her friend know she can't come.
moral_action: Yuri lets her friend know that she cannot go with her as soon as possible.
moral_consequence: Yuri's friend has plenty of time to make changes to her plans.
immoral_action: Yuri waits until a month before the vacation to break the news to her friend.
immoral_consequence: Yuri's friend has already made arrangements and has to go alone or lose money.

norm: It's bad to air your dirty laundry on social media.
situation: Nicole is unhappy with her partner and feels quite frustrated by lack of attention.
intention: Nicole wants to vent about how her partner is acting.
moral_action: Nicole talks to a close friend in private about what is going on.
moral_consequence: Nicole's friend is sympathetic and offers her support.
immoral_action: Nicole posts negative and lengthy status updates on Facebook about her partner.
immoral_consequence: Nicole's friends think less of her because of the drama.

norm: It's good to want to take people's mental conditions seriously.
situation: John and Mary just had a baby but Mary has been depressed since the birth.
intention: John wants Mary to get back to her normal self.
moral_action: John persuades Mary to seek professional help and takes on more responsibility caring for their child.
moral_consequence: John is relieved when Mary's counselling helps her deal with her depression.
immoral_action: "John ignores Mary's growing depression and assumes she'll ""snap out of it"" eventually."
immoral_consequence: John is dismayed when Mary leaves him and the child in order to get help for herself.

norm: You shouldn't let your pets terrorize other people
situation: Gia who owns a large dog is having guests over to her house.
intention: Gia wants her dog to feel comfortable with guests.
moral_action: Gia uses training techniques to sway her dog every time it starts to make a guest feel uncomfortable.
moral_consequence: Gia's guests feel comfortable around the dog as it is showing obedience.
immoral_action: Gia's dog gets very loud and attentive towards one of the particular guests but Gia insists it is nothing to worry about.
immoral_consequence: Gia's guest that the dog is threatening feels very frightened and uncomfortable due to the size of the dog.

norm: It's okay to take your partner to family events.
situation: Ellen is sitting at home with her spouse and just received a phone call from her family inviting her to a cookout tonight.
intention: Ellen wants to go to the cookout.
moral_action: Ellen informs her spouse about the cookout and suggests they go to it.
moral_consequence: Ellen's spouse enjoys the company of the in-laws at the cookout and has a good time.
immoral_action: Ellen informs her spouse that she is going to the cookout and suggests the spouse find something to do on their own tonight.
immoral_consequence: Ellen's spouse is hurt that they aren't invited to the cookout and has a bad evening.

norm: It is unacceptable to touch other people's belongings.
situation: Faye sees a fluffy sweater on Frances' desk.
intention: Faye wants to hold the sweater.
moral_action: Faye asks Frances if she can hold the sweater.
moral_consequence: Frances gives the sweater to Faye.
immoral_action: Faye grabs the sweater while no one is looking.
immoral_consequence: Frances catches Faye and gets mad.

norm: It's bad to hide things from your parents.
situation: Kyle takes the family car out without his parents' permission and gets a scratch on the door.
intention: Kyle wants to get the scratch fixed.
moral_action: Kyle comes clean about the scratch and offers to pay for the fix.
moral_consequence: Kyle's parents make him pay for the fix, but only ground him for a week because he was honest with them.
immoral_action: Kyle tries to hide what he did by fixing the scratch himself.
immoral_consequence: Kyle's repair is very obvious, and Kyle is grounded for a month for taking the car without permission.

norm: It's good to make your own choices.
situation: Keara got into another big fight with her partner and doesn't know what course of action to take.
intention: Keara wants to figure out whether or not to leave her partner.
moral_action: Keara deliberates while weighing the pros and cons of the relationship on her own.
moral_consequence: Keara decides it's better to stay with her current partner, and they work through the issues.
immoral_action: Keara asks her friend what she should do and follows their advice.
immoral_consequence: Keara gives up on a potentially good partner too easily and ends up regretting it.

norm: It is important to listen to your friend's opinions.
situation: Janet's friends have told her that her clothing reveals too much skin.
intention: Janet wants to wear her risque clothing.
moral_action: Janet only wears her risque clothing to certain places and covers it up some.
moral_consequence: Janet gets good attention and feels happier.
immoral_action: Janet ignores her friends and wears her risque clothing out on the town.
immoral_consequence: Janet receives much unwanted attention and feels very uncomfortable.

norm: It's wrong not to take showers.
situation: Corey is the new kid at school and doesn't often shower.
intention: Corey wants to make new friends.
moral_action: Corey showers every day before school and introduces himself to other kids from his classes.
moral_consequence: Corey appears clean to the other kids, and he is able to make new friends.
immoral_action: Corey forgoes a shower before going to school, then tries to introduce himself to people.
immoral_consequence: The other kids smell Corey as he approaches and walk away.

norm: It's rude to call someone names.
situation: Peter is acting loudly and obnoxious in public.
intention: Steve wants Peter to stop.
moral_action: Steve asks Peter quietly to calm down.
moral_consequence: Peter listens and stops.
immoral_action: Steve loudly calls Peter insulting names, making people look over at them.
immoral_consequence: Peter has his feelings hurt and thinks less of Steve.

norm: It's rude to yell out at someone you don't know.
situation: Fred and a friend are walking down the sidewalk when they see a random person driving by slowly in a pink car.
intention: Fred wants to make his friend laugh.
moral_action: Fred points out the paint job to his friend and says that he'd prefer to die than have a car like that.
moral_consequence: Fred's friend laughs and starts talking about his own pet peeves with cars.
immoral_action: Fred tells his friend to watch, then shouts at the person driving by as if he knows him very well.
immoral_consequence: The person gets very confused and is distracted from driving, almost hitting another person.

norm: It's kind to do things for a stranger.
situation: Brian is walking through a section of town where the homeless congregate.
intention: Brian wants to help someone.
moral_action: Brian sees a man sitting on bench looking skinny, so he goes into a nearby fast food place and buys him a big sack of sub sandwiches.
moral_consequence: The man has a good meal and is able to help some of his other homeless friends have a good meal.
immoral_action: Brian tells a man begging on the sidewalk to cheer up, things will get better one day.
immoral_consequence: The man goes hungry that night because Brian didn't give him any money.

norm: It's good to support things you love.
situation: Carla loves to listen to the free band concerts in the park on Friday nights.
intention: Carla wants to enjoy the Friday concerts.
moral_action: Carla always drops a couple of dollars in the donation boxes.
moral_consequence: The band plays the full concert without having to ask for donations.
immoral_action: Carla consistently walks past the donation boxes without contributing anything.
immoral_consequence: The band starts a policy of pausing after the first half hour and asking for contributions from the audience.

norm: You shouldn't rob a house.
situation: Jack is a rich teenager who lives in a rich neighborhood and is bored during the daytime.
intention: Jack wants to do something exciting.
moral_action: Jack decides to learn a new skill and starts taking pilot lessons for small planes.
moral_consequence: Jack learns to fly planes and eventually becomes a pilot for a major airline.
immoral_action: Jack uses his knowledge of the neighborhood to break into someone's house just for fun.
immoral_consequence: The victim becomes paranoid and spends thousands of dollars on a new security system.

norm: It's polite to say thank you.
situation: Jenny is checking out at her local grocery store and receives excellent service from the cashier.
intention: Jenny wants to decide how to respond to the cashier.
moral_action: Jenny thanks the cashier for doing such a good job.
moral_consequence: The cashier is happy that their hard work was recognized.
immoral_action: Jenny decides to pay and leave without saying a word to the cashier.
immoral_consequence: The cashier feels their quality service went unappreciated and is discouraged.

norm: You shouldn't assume the worst about your children
situation: Paul is at home when his son Jim comes home and tells him he got into a fight at school.
intention: Paul wants to discourage Jim from violence.
moral_action: Paul tells Jim that no matter what occurred that violence isn't the answer and if Jim tells him the details they can talk about what to do next time.
moral_consequence: Jim is eager to tell his dad the details and learn from the experience but already begins to understand that fighting is wrong.
immoral_action: Paul tells Jim that it's not good that he's attacking smaller children and beating them up, and he needs to stop.
immoral_consequence: Jim is sad that his dad thinks he was the attacker before even hearing the rest of the story and is confused how to proceed.

norm: It's rude to ignore someone after kissing them.
situation: Carl went out with Krista and kissed her good night at the end.
intention: Carl wants to break things off with Krista because he didn't enjoy their time together.
moral_action: Carl lets Krista down gently and tells her that he doesn't see them working out together.
moral_consequence: Krista is upset but understands.
immoral_action: Carl blocks Krista's number and ignores her.
immoral_consequence: Krista worries about Carl and feels hurt that he is dumping her without explanation since she thought the night went well.

norm: It's good to pay for school with your own funds.
situation: Hank is going to college and is filling out financial paperwork, including if he will take any loans out.
intention: Hank wants to decide on whether he should take a loan or not.
moral_action: Hank declines the student loan and decides to work for the money instead.
moral_consequence: Hank takes longer to finish his degree but pays only what the college charges him.
immoral_action: Hank takes a student loan that will pay for his entire education.
immoral_consequence: Hank graduates and spends the next 15 years repaying the student loan thanks to interest payments.

norm: It's good to not like gambling.
situation: Adam is at the store buying some snacks with his friend Ivan when Ivan asks him to play the lottery.
intention: Adam wants to respond to Ivan's suggestion that he play the lottery.
moral_action: Adam tells Ivan that the lottery is like a tax on stupidity and that only an idiot would waste money on it.
moral_consequence: Adam finds out the next morning that no one won and the draw carried over and that makes him smile.
immoral_action: Adam tells Ivan that it's a great idea since there's a chance he could win a lot of money.
immoral_consequence: Adam finds out the next morning that he didn't win anything and regrets throwing money down the drain.

norm: You shouldn't treat someone poorly.
situation: Cameron is very busy working on his laptop and his wife Lana asks him to help with dinner.
intention: Cameron wants to respond to Lana's request.
moral_action: Cameron explains to Lana he is very busy finishing some work and asks if she can wait until he's done.
moral_consequence: Lana says it's okay for him to help later and Cameron is able to finish his work.
immoral_action: Cameron turns around and snaps at Lana for interrupting him.
immoral_consequence: Lana gets angry and her and Cameron get into a big argument and his work doesn't get finished.

norm: You shouldn't pull someone's hair.
situation: Jack is hanging out with some friends, and they are all telling jokes and goofing off.
intention: Jack wants to get his friends to laugh.
moral_action: Jack tells a funny anecdote about pulling hair instead of actually pulling hair.
moral_consequence: Everyone has a laugh and enjoys Jack's story and everyone has a good time.
immoral_action: Jack pulls his friends hair hard to try to get a laugh from the others.
immoral_consequence: The friend is hurt and everyone is wondering why Jack did that because it is not funny.

norm: It is irresponsible to start a riot.
situation: John is in downtown Portland taking part in a protest against recent police brutality.
intention: John wants to energize the crowd.
moral_action: John grabs the megaphone and tells the crowd that they should sing amazing grace as they march through the streets.
moral_consequence: The crowd is happy to sing a song of solidarity together that symbolizes their struggle.
immoral_action: John grabs the megaphone and tells the crowd to attack the police and destroy all the symbols of capitalism around them.
immoral_consequence: The other protesters dismiss John as a lunatic and begin to fear that he is diluting their message and distracting from their mission.

norm: It's good to share with other people.
situation: Colby is sitting at the table for lunch when he realizes there is a boy near him with no food.
intention: Colby wants to eat his lunch.
moral_action: Colby shares half of his food with the little boy near him.
moral_consequence: The little boy starts to smile and thanks Colby for the food.
immoral_action: Colby eats all of his food in front of the boy, who sadly looked on.
immoral_consequence: The boy begins to cry because Colby is making him hungry.

norm: You shouldn't hate your pets.
situation: Jane has adopted a dog from a shelter as her companion but the dog doesn't appear to be active.
intention: Jane wants to react to the dog's behavior.
moral_action: Jane asks the shelter for advice on how to train the dog to be more active.
moral_consequence: The shelter staff is happy to help Jane with the training and the dog later becomes more lovely and active.
immoral_action: Jane feels dissatisfied with the dog and decides to return it to the shelter.
immoral_consequence: The shelter staff feels bad about Jane's decision.

norm: it's wrong to judge a person by their past mistakes.
situation: Connor is the boss at a tech company.
intention: Connor needs to hire a new tech support person.
moral_action: Gerald gives the candidate a chance since he did his time and is fully qualified.
moral_consequence: Gerald's company gets better reviews due to the new hire's good work.
immoral_action: Connor interviews a man who went to jail for possessing weed and refuses to hire him despite being a perfect candidate.
immoral_consequence: Gerald hires an inferior candidate who doesn't maintain the computers well.

norm: You shouldn't rob fast food restaurants.
situation: Brad is short on his rent and is at a restaurant with his friend Lilly.
intention: Brad wants to find a way to pay his rent.
moral_action: Brad asks Lilly if there is any way she can offer him a short term loan to make his rent.
moral_consequence: Lilly offers Brad the money for the rent and says he doesn't need to pay her back.
immoral_action: Brad approaches the register, threatens the cashier, and demands all of the money in the register.
immoral_consequence: Brad pays his rent and is apprehended within the week, being arrested for theft.

norm: It's unwise to stoop to the level of others.
situation: Bill is constantly elbowing Michael as they play basketball.
intention: Michael wants to avoid getting physically roughed up.
moral_action: Michael plays his best and does not retaliate.
moral_consequence: Bill follows out early in the second half and michael scores 30 in the second half leading the team to a win.
immoral_action: Michael elbows Bill back and they begin a brawl.
immoral_consequence: They are both ejected from the game in the first quarter and suspended for some games after.

norm: It's hurtful to assume things without evidence.
situation: Mindy enters a room to see a broken mirror that was fine 5 minutes ago, only her kids and husband are in the house.
intention: Mindy wants to know who broke the mirror.
moral_action: Mindy calmly asks her kids about it and none of them claim to have broke it or have seen the others break it.
moral_consequence: A few minute into the discussion Mindy's husband walks in and states that he broke the mirror.
immoral_action: Mindy immediately assumes that the kid she's on poor terms with is the culprit.
immoral_consequence: "Only after grounding the ""offending"" kid for a month does she learn her husband broke the mirror."

norm: You should let your kids get involved in extracurricular activities.
situation: Bob has two adolescent daughters now attending public school.
intention: Bob wants his daughters' free time supervised to keep them out of trouble.
moral_action: Bob encourages his daughters to participate in extracurricular activites at their school.
moral_consequence: Bob's daughters make friends and learn social skills, with one of them earning an athletic scholarship to college.
immoral_action: Bob insists that his daughters come directly home from school and only participate in family activites.
immoral_consequence: Bob's daughters stay out of trouble but fail to develop their innate abilities and social skills.

norm: You should compliment someone when you like their dress.
situation: Kyle is at home when his wife Claire comes home in a new fancy dress she just got which Kyle loves at first sight.
intention: Kyle wants to make a comment about the dress.
moral_action: Kyle tells Claire that the dress is amazing and that she looks breathtakingly beautiful in it.
moral_consequence: Claire is so happy to hear that Kyle loves the dress and that she thinks he's beautiful and is all smiles.
immoral_action: Kyle tells Claire that she shouldn't have spen their money on such fancy new clothes.
immoral_consequence: Claire is annoyed that Kyle is focusing on money and not her and her self confidence takes a dip.

norm: It's not okay being so absorbed in having a career.
situation: Trent is working at a prestigious consulting firm when his friends ask him to go out.
intention: Trent wants to respond to his friends' invitation.
moral_action: Trent says he can go out even though his work is important.
moral_consequence: Trent's friends will feel valued by him.
immoral_action: Trent says work is the most important thing, and he can't go out.
immoral_consequence: Trent's friends will think he doesn't care about them and will not ask him out again.

norm: It's wrong to throw your partner around against their will.
situation: John's mother just died and John is at home with his wife Mindy.
intention: John wants to vent his sadness.
moral_action: John tells MIndy the sad news and John goes and takes a bath.
moral_consequence: Mindy comforts John and feels closer to him and John doesn't get arrested.
immoral_action: John raises his voice at Mindy and throws her across the room.
immoral_consequence: Mindy cries and resents John and the cops arrest him.

norm: It's sexist to treat one gender differently than another.
situation: John and his friends Steve and Mary are hiking up a mountain and come to a large boulder they need to climb over.
intention: John wants to get home in time for dinner.
moral_action: After John and Steve get over the boulder, they leave Mary behind because she is having difficulties, and they continue on their hike without her.
moral_consequence: Mary misses out on a great hike and feels badly about herself.
immoral_action: After John and Steve get over the boulder, John and Steve assist Mary who is having difficulties, and they continue on their hike.
immoral_consequence: Mary is able to continue the hike and have a great day on the mountain.

norm: It is rude to ignore a dog.
situation: Jake has a pet dog named fluffy who is barking because he's hungry.
intention: Jake wants to stop hearing Fluffy bark.
moral_action: Jake grabs a bag of dog food out of the pantry and pours some in Fluffy's bowl.
moral_consequence: Jake's neighbors appreciate that his dog is so well behaved and quiet.
immoral_action: Jake lets fluffy outside and closes the door before putting on some earphones.
immoral_consequence: Jake's neighbors are annoyed that Fluffy is outside barking non-stop.

norm: It's not okay to question what people buy for themselves.
situation: Lacy is hanging out with her friend Joan when Joan shows Lacy her new expensive watch.
intention: Lacy wants to comment on the watch.
moral_action: Lacy tells Joan that it's good Joan buys things that make her happy.
moral_consequence: Joan will think that Lacy is an agreeable person.
immoral_action: Lacy tells Joan that the watch is a waste of money.
immoral_consequence: Joan will not want to hang out with Lacy anymore.

norm: You should not judge others by their appearance.
situation: Jane is going through her social media account looking at her messages and requests.
intention: Jane wants to accept some friend requests.
moral_action: Jane accepts people based on their overall profile and messages to her.
moral_consequence: Jane reconnects with an old friend who was among the requests.
immoral_action: Jane accepts only the people who she finds attractive based on their profile picture.
immoral_consequence: Jane denies a request from an old friend by mistake which makes saddens her friend.

norm: It's best not to keep secrets in a relationship
situation: Alex has been dating Penny for over a year and is ready to propose but is worried about telling her about a child he had previously.
intention: Alex wants his proposal to go smoothly.
moral_action: Alex comes clean about his son and introduces him to Penny.
moral_consequence: Alex is able to propose without any lies between them.
immoral_action: Alex keeps his child a secret and gets engaged to Penny.
immoral_consequence: Alex gets left at the altar when Penny finds out about his deceit.

norm: Excluding people from events they'd enjoy is rude.
situation: Tomas and Andy are friends and both are avid hikers, but Tomas recently moved to another city.
intention: Andy wants to go hiking.
moral_action: Andy plans a hiking trip to a national park and asks Andy if he is available to go with them.
moral_consequence: Tomas makes time in his schedule to go hiking with Andy, and the two remain close friends.
immoral_action: Andy plans a hiking trip to a national park and invites all his friends, except for Tomas.
immoral_consequence: Tomas feels left out and his friendship with Andy becomes strained.

norm: It's frowned upon to use illicit drugs.
situation: Brian is at a party when some people there offer him a hit of cocaine.
intention: Brian doesn't want to upset the people.
moral_action: Brian excuses himself, saying that he's had some friends who didn't do well while on cocaine.
moral_consequence: The people respect Brian and leave him alone.
immoral_action: Brian takes the hit of cocaine.
immoral_consequence: Brian gets addicted to cocaine, and his life goes downhill.

norm: You should not meddle in your siblings' love life.
situation: Homer was mad his brother broke his favorite toy.
intention: Homer wants revenge on his brother.
moral_action: Homer turns off the lights while his brother is in the shower.
moral_consequence: His brother's shower is ruined and aggravated by Homer's antics.
immoral_action: Homer tells his brother's girlfriend things about his brother, so she won't like him anymore.
immoral_consequence: Sure enough his brother's girlfriend dumps him and his brother is upset.

norm: You shouldn't ruin your marriage over money.
situation: Dean and Kristi have been married for a little over a year and Dean just lost his job, so the two of them have been fighting over finances.
intention: Dean wants to find a way to generate income.
moral_action: Dean finds a job overseas and explains to Kristi they will be better off if they make the journey together.
moral_consequence: Dean and Kristi are proud of themselves for sticking through rough times together and both feel their marriage is stronger.
immoral_action: Dean finds a job working overseas and because of his anger at Kristi as of late, decides to go alone.
immoral_consequence: The long distance relationship doesn't work out and Dean and Kristi divorce.

norm: It is wrong to put people's toothbrush in the toilet
situation: Karen is brushing her teeth and sees that her son Mark has left his toothbrush on the counter again.
intention: Karen wants Mark to put his toothbrush back.
moral_action: Karen calls Mark in and tells him she will dock his allowance if he keeps leaving his toothbrush out.
moral_consequence: Mark puts his toothbrush away and remembers to do so from now on.
immoral_action: Karen throws Mark's toothbrush in the toilet and tells him to retrieve it and put it back.
immoral_consequence: Mark is traumatized and grossed out, and no longer respects Karen.

norm: It's wrong to get into fights at the bar.
situation: Chad ran into a guy that he didn't like when he was at the bar drinking.
intention: Chad wanted to drink the rest of his beer.
moral_action: Chad took his beer and drank it on the other side of the bar.
moral_consequence: Chad enjoyed his beer and didn't see the man for the rest of the night.
immoral_action: Chad drank the rest of his beer and cracked the bottle over the other man's head.
immoral_consequence: The police were called and Chad was arrested for assault and battery on the man.

norm: It's pathetic to disregard taking care of familial elders.
situation: Manny's elderly dad, who took care of him when he was younger, needs help getting around the house after a car accident.
intention: Manny wants to help out his dad.
moral_action: Manny makes taking care of his father his number one priority.
moral_consequence: Manny's dad feels like he's in good hands and doesn't have to worry as much.
immoral_action: Manny helps his dad whenever he's not playing video games.
immoral_consequence: Manny's dad barely receives any help and feels neglected.

norm: You should always provide people with your correct address.
situation: Asher is checking out at the cash register when the cashier offers him a discount if he signs the form to join their mailing list.
intention: Asher wants to get the discount.
moral_action: Asher fills out the form while making sure that all the fields, including the address, are filled out correctly.
moral_consequence: Asher receives a lot of promotions and catalogs from the company in the mail.
immoral_action: Feeling like the information being asked is violating his privacy, Asher enters an old address on the form that is no longer valid.
immoral_consequence: Asher doesn't receive any of the coupons that are sent to him and misses out on some significant discounts.

norm: It's bad to burn bridges.
situation: Neil has already given his two week notice two weeks ago and it's his last day on the job.
intention: Neil wants to say goodbye to his manager.
moral_action: Neil tells his manager bye that he wishes him well in his future and that he hopes they run into each other someday.
moral_consequence: The manager is happy to hear Neil hope they see each other again and is ready to give Neil a reference for a new job.
immoral_action: Neil tells his manager bye, that he's an awful person and that he's so glad to never work with him again.
immoral_consequence: The manager is shocked and insulted that Neil thinks of him like that and vows to never give Neil a reference for a new job.

norm: It's unacceptable to forbid your significant other to do something.
situation: Anne has plans to go hang gliding alone, but her husband Frank is against the idea.
intention: Frank wants to keep his wife from hang gliding alone.
moral_action: Frank tells Anne that he wants to go hang gliding with her.
moral_consequence: Anne thinks it's a good idea, and she goes hang gliding with Frank.
immoral_action: Frank tells his wife that he won't allow her to go hang glidng alone.
immoral_consequence: Anne tells Frank that she can do whatever she wants and goes anyway.

norm: You shouldn't molest someone who is passed out.
situation: Karen drank too much at a party and is passed out on her roommate Chuck's bed.
intention: Chuck wants to get Karen onto her own bed.
moral_action: Chuck carries Karen to her bed and puts her in a safe position in case she gets sick.
moral_consequence: Karen sleeps off her drunkenness and wakes up thankful to Chuck in the morning.
immoral_action: Chuck carries Karen to her bed and removes her clothes, fondling her body as he does so.
immoral_consequence: Karen wakes up from the cold and discovers Chuck molesting  her, then reports him to the police.

norm: It's rude to deprive your colleagues of caffeine.
situation: Matt is a health reformer and doesn't like seeing people drink coffee at work, knowing that it's not good for their health.
intention: Matt wants to get people off of their caffeine addiction.
moral_action: Matt gives health talks at the office on ways to improve energy without using caffeine.
moral_consequence: Some people try Matt's methods and break free of their need of caffeine.
immoral_action: Matt comes in and removes all caffeinated coffee from the office, then throws it all in the trash.
immoral_consequence: The office workers go into caffeine withdrawals, bringing their productivity down to zero.

norm: Looking at another student's test is bad.
situation: Mary did not study her Math test hard enough, and she takes the test today.
intention: Mary wants to finish the test.
moral_action: Mary works over the test carefully and diligently.
moral_consequence: Mary gets a grade B on the test, and she feels relieved.
immoral_action: Mary peeks at the answers of the girl sitting next to her.
immoral_consequence: Mary gets caught and is disqualified from taking the test.

norm: You shouldn't associate with someone who is addicted to drugs.
situation: Mike was hanging out with Travis, a known drug dealer, an hour before he had to go to work.
intention: Mike needs a ride to work.
moral_action: Mike calls a taxi cab to bring him to work as soon as possible.
moral_consequence: Mike gets to work on time after getting a ride from the taxi company.
immoral_action: Mike asks Travis if he could give him a ride to his job site.
immoral_consequence: The cops pull Travis over for drugs and Mike ends up in jail with him.

norm: It's good to go out with someone that likes you.
situation: Don is looking thru the personal ads in the paper.
intention: Don wants to find a date.
moral_action: Don reads all the ads and the invites some he has a lot in common with on a date.
moral_consequence: Don has a wonderful date talking with his date about their shared interests.
immoral_action: Don sends invites the first person he reads about on a date.
immoral_consequence: Don has a bad date because the other person doesn't like Don.

norm: You should always be respectful of pregnant people.
situation: Paul uses public transportation and takes the bus to work every day.
intention: Paul needs to find a seat on the bus.
moral_action: Paul saves the seat at the front of the bus for a pregnant woman at the bus stop, and sits in the back instead.
moral_consequence: The pregnant woman is not crowded and has a comfortable ride.
immoral_action: Paul sits right in front of the bus, ignoring a pregnant woman who could have used the seat.
immoral_consequence: The pregnant woman has to sit in the crowded back of the bus and is very uncomfortable.

norm: It's good to be dedicated.
situation: Phil sees his friend Jane building an awesome treehouse in her yard.
intention: Phil wants to build an awesome treehouse in his yard.
moral_action: Phil gets to work on the treehouse right away and just keeps building with all of his spare time.
moral_consequence: 2 months later the treehouse is done and it looks awesome.
immoral_action: Phil gathers the materials and starts building, but then keeps putting it off.
immoral_consequence: 10 years later Phil finally finishes the treehouse, which is now too small for the tree.

norm: You shouldn't get your friends drunk
situation: A group of college students are at a bar on a Tuesday to console one of them who got dumped.
intention: Kevin wants to make his depressed friend feel better.
moral_action: Kevin tells his friend all the good things he has going for him.
moral_consequence: Kevin's friend cheers up and begins to look at the silver lining.
immoral_action: Kevin keeps buying his friend shots all throughout the night.
immoral_consequence: Kevin's friend is really sick the next morning and misses class.

norm: It's good to go for a walk with your dog.
situation: Julia is trying to lose weight after having a baby.
intention: Julia wants to get some exercise.
moral_action: Julia straps a leash on her dog and takes him for a walk.
moral_consequence: Julia feels refreshed and happy that she got to spend time with her dog.
immoral_action: Julia goes for a walk by herself around her neighborhood.
immoral_consequence: Julia feels refreshed but lonely, wishing she had brought a companion.

norm: It's disrespectful to not honor people's dietary restrictions.
situation: Gene hosts a party and invites his friend Vince, who is allergic to peanuts and will not eat them.
intention: Gene wants to give his party guests smoothies.
moral_action: Gene makes fruit and peanut butter smoothie for everyone else and gives Vince some frozen yogurt.
moral_consequence: All of Gene's guests enjoy the treat and the party.
immoral_action: Gene makes a fruit and peanut butter smoothie and serves it to all of his guests.
immoral_consequence: Vince, not knowing that it has peanuts, drinks the smoothie and gets very sick.

norm: You should smile back when someone smiles at you.
situation: Rob is working in his office when the new girl, Cleo walks in grinning and says hello.
intention: Rob wants to acknowledge Cleo.
moral_action: Rob stops working and stands up to shake Cleo's hand while giving her a friendly smile.
moral_consequence: Cleo feels welcomed and think she will enjoy working in this office.
immoral_action: Rob looks up from his computer and makes eye contact with Cleo, but just gives a quick wave.
immoral_consequence: Cleo sees Rob as dismissive and unapproachable which makes her uncomfortable on her first day.

norm: Its not okay to take something from someone that's  theirs.
situation: Fred's favorite team is in the playoffs but his tv is broken.
intention: Fred wants to watch the game.
moral_action: Fred asks his neighbor if he can go over and watch the game with him.
moral_consequence: Fred's neighbor tells him sure, and they watch the game together.
immoral_action: Fred goes into his neighbor's apartment and takes his tv.
immoral_consequence: Fred's neighbor calls the police and Fred gets arrested.

norm: You should not make money the bases of a relationship
situation: Anthony is single and looking for a relationship through dating websites.
intention: Anthony wants to get a girlfriend.
moral_action: Anthony tries to find women that he genuinely finds interesting on the dating websites to contact.
moral_consequence: After some date Anthony meets a girl, and they begin going out steadily much to his delight.
immoral_action: Anthony only picks women to contact on the dating websites who clearly have a lot of money.
immoral_consequence: All Anthony's dates see through his shallowness, and he never finds a girlfriend.

norm: It's good to be sorry about something you have done.
situation: Molly had accidentally broken a vase at her mother's house.
intention: Molly wants to talk to her mother about the vase.
moral_action: Molly tells her mother that she is very sorry that she broke the vase.
moral_consequence: Molly's mother accepts her apology and offers a hug to her.
immoral_action: Molly tells her mother that it was an ugly vase, and she needs to get over it.
immoral_consequence: Molly's mother is upset at Molly's insensitivity and gives her the cold shoulder for the rest of the day.

norm: It's good to invite your family over.
situation: The Fourth of July is coming up, and it's Evan's turn to have family over for a holiday.
intention: Evan wants to celebrate the Fourth of July.
moral_action: Evan invites his family over for a barbecue on the Fourth.
moral_consequence: Evan and his family have a good time, and they compliment him on his new home.
immoral_action: Evan celebrates the Fourth by himself by watching fireworks on TV.
immoral_consequence: Evan doesn't have all that much fun and feels a little lonely.

norm: You shouldn't cause car accidents.
situation: Cindy is coming up on an intersection behind another car and her phone falls of the car seat, followed shortly after by the car in front stopping suddenly.
intention: Cindy wants to retrieve her phone.
moral_action: Cindy waits to retrieve the phone and reacts to the car stopping suddenly.
moral_consequence: Cindy is able to stop her car before hitting the car in front of her and is then able to safely retrieve her phone.
immoral_action: Cindy immediately reaches down to get the phone, taking her eyes off the road.
immoral_consequence: Cindy rear ends the car in front of her and causes expensive damage to both cars.

norm: Lying about achievements is detestable behavior.
situation: Hector, who is part of Ryan's friend group, has an annoying habit of one-upping people during conversations.
intention: Ryan wants to tell his friends about his most recent fishing trip.
moral_action: Ryan shows his friends pictures of the trip and ignores Hector's attempts to one-up him.
moral_consequence: Hector feels foolish and reflects on his action while Ryan is quietly admired for shutting Hector down.
immoral_action: Ryan tells his friends about the trip and exaggerates the size and number of fish he caught to show up Hector.
immoral_consequence: Ryan and Hector get into a one-upping match that alienates the rest of the group and makes them look ridiculous.

norm: It's good to care about someone's feelings.
situation: Dan believes in tough love and thinks the best way to be a parent is to prepare children for the hardships of life.
intention: Dan wants his children to be autonomous.
moral_action: Dan takes his children on adventures and teaches them resourcefulness in an attentive and respectful way.
moral_consequence: Dan's children feel he really cares about them and love going on adventures with him.
immoral_action: Dan puts his children in difficult life situations and lets them figure a way out - he doesn't care how it makes them feel.
immoral_consequence: Dan's children feel he doesn't love them.

norm: It's rude to destroy your neighbor's things.
situation: Ezra is getting angry when the lawnmower he borrowed from his neighbor stops working in the middle of the lawn.
intention: Ezra wants to express his anger.
moral_action: Ezra knocks on his neighbors door and discusses his annoyed feelings with his neighbor.
moral_consequence: His neighbor shows him how to fix the lawnmower which allows Ezra to finish mowing the lawn.
immoral_action: Ezra kicks the lawnmower over and over again until it breaks.
immoral_consequence: Ezra has to buy his neighbor a new lawn mower.

norm: It's good to defend your sibling.
situation: Bobby and Chris are playing basketball on the court and some people start picking on them.
intention: Bobby wants to make it home safely.
moral_action: Bobby defends himself and Chris from the bullies, and they run home together safely.
moral_consequence: Bobby and Chris grow stronger through the experience and Bobby's mom signs them up for self defense classes.
immoral_action: Bobby does not defend Chris from the bullies and instead runs home by himself.
immoral_consequence: Chris is beaten up and Bobby gets into a lot of trouble from his parents for leaving his younger brother alone.

norm: It's rude to ignore your partner's texts.
situation: Nick is trying to plan what days to ask off from work to go on vacation.
intention: Nick wants to get his wife's opinion on their vacation dates.
moral_action: Nick texts back and forth with his wife until they settle on the perfect date for both of them.
moral_consequence: Nick enjoys a relaxing vacation with his lovely wife.
immoral_action: Nick sees his wife's reply to his text message, but he doesn't open and read it.
immoral_consequence: Nick chooses a date what won't work for his wife, and they don't vacation together.

norm: It's wrong to get angry over petty things.
situation: Kel is at a birthday party where they are handing out slices of cake to everybody, and he notices his piece of cake is smaller than the rest.
intention: Kel wants to enjoy his cake.
moral_action: Kel savors each bite of the piece of the cake he got, and he complements the person who made it.
moral_consequence: Kel is able to appreciate what he has and ends up satisfied because of it.
immoral_action: Kel decides his enjoyment of the cake is dependent on him receiving a piece as big as the others and makes a big scene about the size of his piece.
immoral_consequence: People are taken aback by the amount of anger Kel is showing over something so trivial and his standing among his peers drops.

norm: It immoral to have an affair while you are married.
situation: Jasmine is married but meets a new man who she has strong feelings for.
intention: Jasmine wants to be intimate with the new man.
moral_action: Jasmine divorces her husband then sleeps with the other man.
moral_consequence: Jasmine's husband respects that at least she didn't cheat on him.
immoral_action: Jasmine sleeps with the new man while still married to her husband.
immoral_consequence: Jasmine's husband feels betrayed when he finds out she has been sleeping with another man.

norm: It's rude to tell someone you don't like them.
situation: Larry has a co-worker that is working slowly on a project.
intention: Larry wants to address his co-worker's slow work.
moral_action: Larry tells his co-worker strategies to be a faster worker.
moral_consequence: Larry's co-worker will employ the strategies and become quicker.
immoral_action: Larry tells his co-worker that their slow work makes them unlikable.
immoral_consequence: Larry's co-worker will be sad and have doubts about themself.

norm: It's inappropriate to relieve yourself in dressing rooms.
situation: Tommy is trying on jeans at the mall when suddenly he gets the urge to pee.
intention: Tommy wants to relieve himself of the urge to pee.
moral_action: Tommy leaves his clothes in the dressing room and asks the salesman if he can use their bathroom.
moral_consequence: Tommy is relieved and can resume trying on jeans.
immoral_action: Tommy decides to pee onto the dressing room floor since no one can see him.
immoral_consequence: The salesman hears Tommy peeing, and calls mall security.

norm: It's wrong to make promises that you can't keep
situation: Tyler just met a new girl and has a big crush on her.
intention: Tyler wants to impress the girl and go out with her.
moral_action: After talking to the girl, Tyler promises to give her a call the next day if she will give him her number.
moral_consequence: Tyler calls the girl the next night, and they have a wonderful conversation and set up a date night.
immoral_action: Tyler tells the girl that he has a boat, which he doesn’t, and promises to take her fishing on it.
immoral_consequence: Tyler is unable to rent a boat anywhere and has to cancel the date, and the girl never talks to him again.

norm: It is not acceptable to stare at others.
situation: Frank is at a local bar when he sees an attractive woman at a table across the room.
intention: Frank wants to attract the woman's attention.
moral_action: Frank approaches the woman and asks if he can buy her a drink.
moral_consequence: The woman accepts Frank's offer, and they enjoy chatting while having a drink together.
immoral_action: Frank stares directly at the attractive woman until she notices him.
immoral_consequence: The woman sees Frank staring and finds it creepy, so she leaves the bar without speaking to him.

norm: It is expected to celebrate special events with family.
situation: John's sister is graduating from college and their parents are throwing her a graduation party.
intention: John hates parties and wants to avoid going to his sister's graduation party.
moral_action: John calls his sister and explains that he hates parties and offers to take her to dinner to celebrate her graduation.
moral_consequence: His sister is happy and they maintain a close relationship.
immoral_action: John does not go to the party.
immoral_consequence: His sister is hurt and upset with him.

norm: It's inhumane to kill other living beings.
situation: Jeff has a dog that he loves and has to move, but cannot take the dog with him.
intention: Jeff wants to relieve himself of responsibility for the dog.
moral_action: Jeff puts up flyers advertising the dog for a good home.
moral_consequence: Someone decides to adopt Jeff's dog and enjoys the dog very much.
immoral_action: Jeff decides to kill the dog so the dog won't starve or become a stray.
immoral_consequence: Jeff has trouble forgiving himself for killing his beloved pet.

norm: It's rude to threaten a former partner.
situation: Bob just broke up with his long-time girlfriend and moved out of her apartment when he realizes he left his favorite hat there.
intention: Bob wants to retrieve his beloved hat.
moral_action: Bob calls his ex-girlfriend and poilitely asks if he can come by later to get the hat.
moral_consequence: Bob's ex-girlfriend agrees, and he is happy to get back his favorite hat.
immoral_action: Bob threatens his ex-girlfriend with physical harm if she doesn't return the hat to him.
immoral_consequence: Bob's ex-girlfriend calls the cops on him over his threats, and he is arrested.

norm: It's mean to taunt your classmates at school.
situation: There is a new student named Sally that sits near Stella in math class.
intention: Stella wants to talk to Sally.
moral_action: Stella asks Sally if she wants to hang out after school.
moral_consequence: Sally hangs out with Stella and they become good friends.
immoral_action: Stella teases Sally constantly about the clothes she wears to class.
immoral_consequence: Sally cries every time Stella teases her about her clothes.

norm: It's wrong to make a new wife feel unwelcome
situation: Rick is at home when his son and his new bride arrive back from their honeymoon.
intention: Rick wants to talk about the couple's future.
moral_action: Rick tells his son and his wife that their marriage will have ups and downs but as long as their love is strong their future will be great.
moral_consequence: Rick's son and his wife are both delighted to hear supportive and wise words from their dad.
immoral_action: Rick tells his son and his wife that they can't stay with him long, and they both need jobs, so they can get out of there soon.
immoral_consequence: Rick's son and his wife both feel pressured to leave and wonder if Rick doesn't like them or doesn't want them to be together.

norm: You should care when someone gets in a crash.
situation: Ben's coworker recently came out of a car crash with minor injuries and is talking to Ben about the incident.
intention: Ben wants to respond to his coworker.
moral_action: Ben asks his coworker about how he is doing and if he needs any assistance.
moral_consequence: Ben's coworker thanks Ben and becomes more friendly towards Ben.
immoral_action: Ben ignores his coworker and proceeds to talk about his work.
immoral_consequence: Ben's coworker starts viewing Ben as an uncaring person and distances himself from Ben.

norm: Trivializing people's depression is rude.
situation: Mary is sitting with John on the couch when she tells John that she is feeling very depressed lately.
intention: John wants to respond to Mary.
moral_action: John tells Mary that depression is a serious health issue that requires expert assistance and offers to help Mary find a therapist.
moral_consequence: Mary is depressed, so she can't be too happy but is momentarily relieved that John is going to try to help her get better.
immoral_action: "John tells Mary that depression is easily cured by ""Simply cheering up"" and tells her not to look so glum."
immoral_consequence: Mary is devastated that John doesn't understand how deep and strong depression is and feels alone in her struggle.

norm: It is unsanitary to put hair in food.
situation: Marcel is cooking for a critic who gave the restaurant a bad review last time she was here, but he was not.
intention: Marcel wants to show the critic who is in charge of the kitchen.
moral_action: Marcel takes his time and perfects the dish he is serving to the critic.
moral_consequence: The critic writes a positive review, admitting she was too hasty in the first review.
immoral_action: Marcel adds a single strand of hair to the pasta.
immoral_consequence: The critic writes another scathing review about the quality and handling of the food.

norm: It's good to offer to buy pizza for your friends.
situation: Xavier's friends just spent all day helping him move into a new apartment, and they ordered pizza since they're starving.
intention: Xavier wants to thank his friends.
moral_action: Xavier pays all the pizzas in order to show his appreciation for his friends' help.
moral_consequence: Xavier's friends spend the evening hanging out in his new apartment, enjoying each other's company.
immoral_action: Xavier gives his friends money for his share of the pizza.
immoral_consequence: Xavier's friends feel unappreciated and decide to think twice before helping him again.

norm: It's good to share your kids with your partner.
situation: Mary has two kids with her partner.
intention: Mary wants her kids to want to spend time with her.
moral_action: Mary asks her kids what they want to do for fun with her and asks their dad along.
moral_consequence: They have fun together as a whole family.
immoral_action: Mary tells her kids their father is a terrible person and resents them, so they'll only want to be around her.
immoral_consequence: Their father feels lonely and confused and the children grow up thinking the worst of him.

norm: It's good to help out your partner financially.
situation: Phil's girlfriend recently had her work hours reduced, and she is struggling to make her monthly car payments.
intention: Phil wants his girlfriend to be able to make her car payments.
moral_action: Phil helps out his girlfriend by paying part of her car payments for a few months.
moral_consequence: Phil's girlfriend is able to make her payments in full and avoid going into debt.
immoral_action: Phil tells his girlfriend to borrow some money from her parents or get a second job.
immoral_consequence: Phil's girlfriend is unable to produce the cash needed to make her payments, and she falls into debt.

norm: It's wrong to enable your friend to be a bully.
situation: Jim sees his friend pick on and abuse a smaller boy.
intention: Jim wants to react to his friend's behavior.
moral_action: Jim tells his friend that he is a coward for picking on the smaller child.
moral_consequence: The smaller child feels good that somebody stuck up for them.
immoral_action: Jim laughs at the smaller child and tells his friend to keep picking on them.
immoral_consequence: The smaller child is left with painful memories of being bullied.

norm: It's wrong to shoot police
situation: Tyrone's brother was shot and killed by the police wrongfully.
intention: Tyrone wants justice on the police.
moral_action: Tyrone sues the police officers that were behind his brother getting killed.
moral_consequence: The judge rules in Tyrone's favor and the cops who abused their power get arrested.
immoral_action: Tyrone goes out with his glock and opens fire on a few random police officers.
immoral_consequence: Tyrone gets shot and killed in retaliation by the police.

norm: It's good to give people tips for their service.
situation: Sara is treating her friends to a nice meal and notices that the restaurant is somewhat pricey.
intention: Sara wants to save as much money as possible.
moral_action: Sara orders a lower priced meal and a water to save money.
moral_consequence: The server is happy to get a reasonable tip and everyone is happy Sara bought them dinner.
immoral_action: Sara decides to stiff the server on the tip in order to save money there.
immoral_consequence: The server is upset and Sara's friends think she is a cheapskate.

norm: It's considered taboo to date a cousin.
situation: Jeff is at a family get-together and finds his cousin Beverly very atractive.
intention: Jeff wants to be with his cousin Beverly.
moral_action: Jeff tells Beverly she is really beautiful, and they should hang out as friends more.
moral_consequence: Beverly feels flattered and likes her family more and feels good.
immoral_action: Jeff asks his cousin Beverly on a date and expresses his love for her.
immoral_consequence: They get married, have kids and the kids are deformed and sick.

norm: It's rude to pressure your children to diet.
situation: Michelle is preparing dinner for her family.
intention: Michelle wants her son to be healthy.
moral_action: Michelle serves her son carefully measured portions of lean protein and vegetables.
moral_consequence: Michelle's son maintains an appropriate body weight.
immoral_action: Michelle tells her son not to eat so much, so he won't get fat.
immoral_consequence: Michelle's son develops an eating disorder and has to have therapy.

norm: You are expected to defend your siblings in all situations
situation: Ted's witnesses his younger brother Bill at school being physically threatened by a bully who is demanding his lunch money.
intention: Ted wants the bully to leave his brother alone.
moral_action: Ted steps in front of the bully and tells him to pick on someone his own size.
moral_consequence: The bully backs down and Bill is relieved and grateful that his brother stood up for him.
immoral_action: Ted tells his brother Bill to give up his lunch money to the bully.
immoral_consequence: Bill is released by the bully after giving up his money but is sad now as he can't buy himself lunch.

norm: It's kind to give people compliments about themselves.
situation: Aaron is attending a formal work event with his partner who is dressed up nicely for the occasion.
intention: Aaron wants to make a good impression on the people attending.
moral_action: Aaron tells his partner how good she looks in front of the other attendees.
moral_consequence: Aaron's partner feels appreciated by him, and she feels attractive.
immoral_action: Aaron focuses on mingling with other work related attendees at the event.
immoral_consequence: Aaron's partner is complimented by other men at the event and feels unnoticed by him.

norm: It is wrong to just like someone for their looks.
situation: Bert has hired a matchmaker.
intention: Bert wants to go on a date.
moral_action: Bert chooses a girl to date who has multiple things in common with him.
moral_consequence: Bert has a fun date and develops a connection with another person.
immoral_action: Bert chooses a pretty girl to date who does not have anything in common with him.
immoral_consequence: Bert is bored out of his mind during the date.

norm: You shouldn't discriminate against women.
situation: Nick is interviewing some male and female applicants for an open computer programmer position.
intention: Nick wants to decide on a good applicant for the job.
moral_action: Nick considers each applicant, both men and woman, and finally settles on a highly qualified woman.
moral_consequence: The company does well because the woman Nick chose is an excellent programmer.
immoral_action: Nick shortens his list down to the men, as men are typically programmers, then picks one.
immoral_consequence: The company suffers because none of the men on the list were very good programmers.

norm: It's good to use the Internet to find new things.
situation: Kenny is looking at all the old clothing in his closet.
intention: Kenny wants to update his style of dress.
moral_action: Kenny gets on the GQ website and reads all about the latest trends inmenswear.
moral_consequence: Kenny gets some sharp new outfits and plenty of complements on his trendy look.
immoral_action: Kenny goes to a thrift shop and buys some used suits.
immoral_consequence: Kenny doesn't update his wardrobe and people still see him as a poorly dressed man.

norm: It's wrong to dislike handicapped kids.
situation: Layne is chaperoning her daughter's aquarium field trip where one of the kids in her group is handicapped.
intention: Layne wants to treat the kids she's chaperoning to an item from the aquarium's gift shop.
moral_action: Layne allows each and every child in her chaperone group to choose something they'd like from the gift shop.
moral_consequence: Layne's daughter learns the value of inclusion and all the kids leave happy.
immoral_action: Layne buys every kid in her chaperone group an item of their choosing from the gift shop, but excludes the handicapped kid.
immoral_consequence: The handicapped kid feels left out and cries when he gets home.

norm: It's wrong to get back at small children.
situation: Evelin is babysitting her friend's six year old daughter, Alissa, and Alissa throws a tantrum when Evelin refuses to buy her ice cream.
intention: Evelin wants to respond to Alissa's actions.
moral_action: Evelin explains to Alissa that her mom has a tasty dinner planned for her in an hour, and she can have ice cream afterwards.
moral_consequence: Alissa stops crying and agrees to play a game with Evelin instead of stopping for ice cream.
immoral_action: Evelin stops at the ice cream stand and buys an ice cream cone for herself and buys nothing for Alissa.
immoral_consequence: Alissa throws an even bigger tantrum and people on the street stop to stare and shake their heads.

norm: It's good to be intimate with people you love.
situation: John and his wife are in bed before they fall asleep when John's wife Jane asks him to get frisky.
intention: John wants to respond to Jane's request.
moral_action: John tells Jane that she doesn't have to ask twice and leaps on top of her to start kissing her passionatelly.
moral_consequence: Jane feels loved, aroused and happy as the love of her life ferociously attacks her body with kisses.
immoral_action: John tells Jane no because he is tired, and they both have to get up early in the morning for work.
immoral_consequence: Jane feels rejected and lonely and wonders if John actually still finds her attractive which makes her insecure.

norm: It's good to get gifts for your parents.
situation: It's the holidays and Andy is short on money.
intention: Andy wants to save money.
moral_action: Andy makes a homemade gift to give his parents for the holidays.
moral_consequence: Andy's parents are happy that their son got them a thoughtful gift.
immoral_action: Andy decides to not get his parents a gift for the holidays.
immoral_consequence: Andy's parents are disappointed that he did not get them anything.

norm: A host offering substandard refreshments is frowned upon.
situation: Joel is throwing a summer bash and invites all of his friends.
intention: Joel wants to provide all of the beverages for his party.
moral_action: Joel goes shopping to provide a DIY bar that will include a variety of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages for his guests.
moral_consequence: Joel's guests have a blast with the DIY bar and his party is a hit.
immoral_action: After telling everyone not to bring drinks, Joel sets out expired beer and flat soda for his guests.
immoral_consequence: Joel's guests are grossed out by the drinks and leave the party.

norm: It's good to give kids candy for Halloween.
situation: Brit stocks up on candy every year for Halloween, as it is her favorite time of the year.
intention: Brit wants make sure the kids in her neighborhood have an unforgettable halloween.
moral_action: Brit puts together cute little candy bags to hand out to the children.
moral_consequence: The children love the candy bags and vow to come back every year.
immoral_action: Brit makes sure to get the black licorice since it is on sale to hand out to the kids.
immoral_consequence: The kids despise their candy and avoid going to her house in the future.

norm: It's polite to want others follow their dreams
situation: Ted's son just told him that he wants to be a garbageman when he grows up.
intention: Ted wants to give his son some advice.
moral_action: Ted tells his son that he'll support whatever career decision that he decides to make.
moral_consequence: Ted's son feels supported by his dad, and he feels stronger in his decision.
immoral_action: Ted tells his son that he's going to be seen as a loser if he becomes a garbageman.
immoral_consequence: Ted's son's feelings are hurt, and he can't believe that his own dad would say such a thing to him.

norm: It's wrong to be bitter.
situation: Xander is at a party where he runs into Kevin, who used to steal his lunch money when they were in grade school.
intention: Xander wants to respond to Kevin.
moral_action: Xander says hello to Kevin and the two of them have a nice conversation where Kevin ends up apologizing for past behavior.
moral_consequence: Xander and Kevin strike up a new found friendship.
immoral_action: Xander angrily confronts Kevin about how he was picked on as a kid and the two of them get into a fist fight.
immoral_consequence: Xander and Kevin both get hurt and the party is ruined for everyone.

norm: It's rude to use rock pools as a toilet.
situation: James was exploring a rocky beach full of tide pools when he felt the overwhelming urge to poop.
intention: James wants to avoid pooping in his pants.
moral_action: James sprints back towards his car and poops in an empty KFC bucket.
moral_consequence: No one is aware of James' gastrointestinal problems, and he resumes exploring the tide pools.
immoral_action: James pulls down his pants and poops in one of the tide pools.
immoral_consequence: A passerby films James pooping and puts the video on YouTube.

norm: Family are expected to help each other with their problems.
situation: William's sister needs a ride to her soccer practice and asks William for a ride.
intention: William wants to respond to his sister.
moral_action: William obliges his sister's request and drives her to her soccer practice.
moral_consequence: William's sister thanks William and their relationship improves a bit.
immoral_action: William quickly says no to his sister and goes back to what he was doing.
immoral_consequence: William's sister becomes annoyed with William and does not help him the next time he needs help.

norm: It's rude to flip people off on the road.
situation: Terry is driving back home when someone cuts her off on the road suddenly.
intention: Terry wants to express her anger to the other driver.
moral_action: Terry leans in on her horn and gives the other driver a long honk.
moral_consequence: Other drivers are hear the horn and are more alert to dangers on the road.
immoral_action: Terry rolls her window down and gives the other driver the finger.
immoral_consequence: Other drivers see her flipping someone off and think she has road rage.

norm: It's good to care about the health of others.
situation: Ashley notices a Sarah crying about a headache at her party.
intention: Ashley wants to create a positive atmosphere.
moral_action: Ashley brings Sarah some water and headache medication sitting with her until she feels better.
moral_consequence: Ashley and Sarah become friends.
immoral_action: Ashley removes Sarah from the house asking her to go home.
immoral_consequence: Ashley appears heartless to her other guests.

norm: It's kind to do favors for people who are sick.
situation: Marcus is at home when he gets a call from his brother who has a bad flu and needs some food.
intention: Marcus wants to watch the ballgame.
moral_action: Marcus calls a delivery service and orders food to be delivered to his brother while watching the game.
moral_consequence: Marcus' brother is very thankful and starts to feel better and thinks Marcus loves him.
immoral_action: Marcus tells his brother he's very busy and hangs up and watches the game.
immoral_consequence: Marcus' brother wonders if Marcus loves him anymore and is sad and sick and hungry.

norm: You should knock before you enter someone else's room.
situation: It is early morning and Jane staying in a guest room at a friend's house she is visiting.
intention: Jane wants to see what her friend.
moral_action: Jane walks down the hall to her friend's room and knocks on the door, calling out her friend's name.
moral_consequence: Her friend avoids an awkward situation by letting Jane know that she is currently getting dressed and that she will meet her in the kitchen in a few moments.
immoral_action: Jane walks down the hall to her friend's room and opens the door to see what they are doing.
immoral_consequence: Jane walks in on the friend getting dressed and the friend is embarrassed to be seen in the compromising situation.

norm: It's bad to talk someone into eating something they shouldn't.
situation: William and his classmates are on lunch break at school.
intention: William wants to entertain his classmates.
moral_action: William gathers the attention of many of his classmates and then blows bubbles in his milk and sings a song.
moral_consequence: William's classmates laugh at his performance and William feels good.
immoral_action: William gathers the attention of many of his classmates and then dares a particular classmate to eat his paper napkin.
immoral_consequence: William's classmate eats the paper due to peer pressure, gets sick, and then tattles on William.

norm: Hurting other people's feelings is wrong.
situation: Caleb is helping his younger brother do his homework one afternoon.
intention: Caleb wants to give his brother feedback on his progress.
moral_action: Caleb encourages his brother and tells him that he can get the answers himself.
moral_consequence: Caleb's brother starts to understand the material that they are working on.
immoral_action: Caleb tells his brother that he is stupid, and he should know all the answers by now.
immoral_consequence: Caleb's brother begins to cry and stops trying to work on the material.

norm: You should always care about your education.
situation: Simon is normally a good student, but has recently gotten a job that takes up a lot of time.
intention: Simon wants to work at a job.
moral_action: Simon takes a less time-consuming job so that he can focus on his studies.
moral_consequence: Simon gets good grades and is able to attend his preferred college when he graduates.
immoral_action: Simon continues working at the time-consuming job and spends less time on his schoolwork.
immoral_consequence: Simon's grades drop, and he can't get into his preferred college.

norm: It's nice to wear panties.
situation: Martha goes to a summer picnic on a hot day.
intention: Martha wants to dress comfortably.
moral_action: Martha wears a bra and panties under her dress during the party.
moral_consequence: Martha is still comfortable and enjoys the party without incident.
immoral_action: Martha decides to wear just a dress with nothing under it.
immoral_consequence: An accidental wind gust occurs causes an unwelcome sight and awkward moment for those around her.

norm: It is irresponsible to leave a gate open.
situation: Carla is playing outside with her cat when she realizes it's time for her to leave for work.
intention: Carla wants to get to work on time.
moral_action: Carla quickly brings her cat inside and closes her gate before jumping into the car.
moral_consequence: Carla makes it to work on time and comes home to her cat safe and sound.
immoral_action: Carla rushes off to work, leaving her cat outside and her gate unlocked.
immoral_consequence: Carla's cat escapes the yard and is lost forever.

norm: You should show your parents grace.
situation: John's father Theobold is dying and asks John to come visit him.
intention: John wants his father to know how much he hurt him when he was younger.
moral_action: John comforts his father, tells him briefly that he forgives his father for any wrongs that occurred and says he loves him.
moral_consequence: Theobold feels loved and forgiven and stays healthy for a longer time.
immoral_action: John visits his dad and tells him how angry he is at him and how he'll never forget all the wrongs he did to him.
immoral_consequence: Theobold is upset and gets sicker and dies thinking John doesn't love him.

norm: It's hurtful to cheat on your spouse.
situation: John, who is married, is talking to Wendy at a bar when Wendy suddenly tells him she's attracted to him and asks him to sleep with her.
intention: John wants to respond to Wendy's question.
moral_action: John declines Wendy's request and reminds her that he is married and faithful.
moral_consequence: John's wife is told that John declined a woman's advances and feels happy and safe in their relationship.
immoral_action: John agrees to sleep with Wendy, and they leave the bar together.
immoral_consequence: John's wife finds out about the affair and is deeply hurt and ashamed and ends their relationship.

norm: It is wrong to force someone to have an abortion.
situation: Martin and his girlfriend are going to have a baby.
intention: Martin doesn't want to be a father.
moral_action: Martin gets to his girlfriend to agree to give the baby up for adoption.
moral_consequence: Martin and his girlfriend continue to have a strong relationship.
immoral_action: Martin forces his girlfriend to get an abortion.
immoral_consequence: Martin loses his girlfriend because she is mad that Martin forced her to get an abortion.

norm: You should not give people unsolicited advice
situation: Jenny is riding the train when she overhears two women discussing a problem they are having.
intention: Jenny wants to keep herself occupied during the train ride.
moral_action: Jenny minds her own business and pulls out her phone to read an e-book.
moral_consequence: Jenny has an uneventful train ride.
immoral_action: Jenny inserts herself in the pairs conversation and offers possible solutions.
immoral_consequence: Jenny is ignored by both women.

norm: It's rude to not help with dishes after a meal.
situation: Sean has just finished up dinner with his wife Linda and his plate sits empty on the table.
intention: Sean wants to do something about the plate.
moral_action: Sean takes the plate and washes it in the sink before putting it on the dish rack to dry.
moral_consequence: Linda is delighted to see Sean doing his part to keep the house clean, so she doesn't have to do everything.
immoral_action: Sean takes the plate and puts it in the sink and then walks away to go watch TV.
immoral_consequence: Linda is annoyed that Sean left the plate in the sink for her to wash while he relaxes.

norm: It's bad to become involved in unhealthy relationships.
situation: Julie is an aspiring students who is dating demanding high school dropout Joe.
intention: Julie wants to be in a committed relationship.
moral_action: Julie breaks up with Joe when he doesnt support her choice.
moral_consequence: Julie get a college degree and meets a more caring boyfriend in college.
immoral_action: Julie is admitted to a prestigous college, but does not go when Joe says that she is being selfish by going to college.
immoral_consequence: Julie is dumped by Joe a few years a later leaving Julie almost 30 with no education and job.

norm: It is good to not complain too much.
situation: Heather deals with chronic pain and has friends who are free-spirited and light.
intention: Heather wants to hang out with her friends.
moral_action: Heather accepts and deals with her condition without making it the only topic of discussion with her friends.
moral_consequence: Heather's friends continue to come around every week.
immoral_action: Heather sees her friends every week, but talks about about her pain nonstop when they are together.
immoral_consequence: Heather's friends find that she brings the mood down and decide not to hang out with her as often.

norm: You shouldn't murder people.
situation: John is walking his dog when a careless man on a bicycle runs into his dog at full speed hurting the dog badly.
intention: James wants to seek revenge on the careless man.
moral_action: John tells the man to stay there while he calls the police and a vet for his dog.
moral_consequence: John eventually is satisfied when the careless man is tried for criminal negligence.
immoral_action: John gets into such a rage that he pounds the man into the ground, beating him until the man dies.
immoral_consequence: John is arrested for murder and is vilified in the press ruining his life forever.

norm: You shouldn't ask people what their kinks are.
situation: Jadyen is out on a date, and he's running out of things to talk about.
intention: Jayden wants to continue the conversation.
moral_action: Jayden tells his date a random piece of trivia in an attempt to keep things going.
moral_consequence: Jayden's date learns more by asking  Jayden about his trivia knowledge.
immoral_action: Jayden asks his date what they like doing in the bedroom.
immoral_consequence: Jayden's date assumes that Jayden wants a one night stand, and she leaves in the middle of the date.

norm: It's wrong to breach a very close friends trust.
situation: Samantha tells Christina that she has a huge crush on the quarterback.
intention: Christina wants to fit in with the popular girls.
moral_action: Christina keeps Samantha's secret even though it would make her more popular.
moral_consequence: Samantha's reputation is spared.
immoral_action: Christina tells all the popular girls that Samantha likes the quarterback.
immoral_consequence: The popular girls spread the secret and humiliate Samantha.

norm: It is good to vent your frustrations.
situation: Micky has been having a lot of stresses in his life lately and is at home with his wife.
intention: Micky wants to spend quality time with his wife.
moral_action: Micky opens up to his wife about his situation and is able to get some weight off of his shoulders.
moral_consequence: Micky becomes closer with his wife and is able to effectively work towards solving his stressing issues.
