immoral_action: Micky puts on a front for his wife as to not make her share in his situation, and they watch a movie together.
immoral_consequence: Micky's is able to enjoy the evening but eventually the bottled up stress begins to affect his health in serious ways.

norm: Married people are expected to settle down.
situation: Anthony is sitting in the living room of his home with his wife, watching television.
intention: Anthony wants to find something exciting to do with his night.
moral_action: Anthony invites his wife to go out to the local pub for dinner and some drinks, offering to treat her to a fun night on the town.
moral_consequence: Anthony feels good that his wife will be having some fun with him, and his wife is happy that he doesn't want to go out at night without her.
immoral_action: Anthony decides to get dressed and go out to a local club for the evening, by himself.
immoral_consequence: Anthony feels guilty for leaving his wife home alone and his wife feels resentful and hurt that he went out without her.

norm: It's wrong to go after somebody else's significant other
situation: Lyla just recently broke up with her boyfriend, and she's having a hard time coping with being alone.
intention: Lyla wants to search for a new boyfriend.
moral_action: Lyla makes a profile on a dating website and browses for single men.
moral_consequence: Lyla finds a man that she thinks is perfect for her, and she plans a date with him.
immoral_action: Lyla begins flirting with a friend's boyfriend who she finds very attractive.
immoral_consequence: Lyla gets called out by her friend when she finds out about her behavior.

norm: Its wrong to grope people without their permission
situation: Troy and Kail are getting close at a house party, and Troy is curios about how Kail is feeling.
intention: Troy wants to know if Kail is into him or not.
moral_action: Troy asks Kail if she wants to go somewhere more private and waits for her answer.
moral_consequence: Kail agrees and head somewhere secluded with Troy.
immoral_action: Troy grabs Kail by the waist and tries to lead her to somewhere more secluded.
immoral_consequence: Kail is freaked out and backs away from Troy.

norm: It's wrong to complain all the time.
situation: Connie is out with friends on lunch break, and they are talking together.
intention: Connie wants to make conversation.
moral_action: Connie says how grateful she is for her job and her friends.
moral_consequence: Connie and her friends cheer each other up with the good things in their lives.
immoral_action: Connie complains about her job, her boss, and the company during the whole lunch break.
immoral_consequence: Connie's friends try to avoid talking with her from then on.

norm: It's good to listen to your grandma.
situation: Phil is having dinner at his grandmother's house, and she is talking about her newest knitting project.
intention: Phil wants to change the subject of conversation.
moral_action: Phil lets his grandmother finish the story, before talking about a game he's currently playing.
moral_consequence: Phil's grandmother appreciates him listening, and repays that consideration by listening to him talk about gaming.
immoral_action: Phil interrupts the conversation and starts talking about video games.
immoral_consequence: Phil's grandmother isn't impressed with the new topic, and is annoyed that Phil prevented her from finishing her story.

norm: It's good to donate your unused possessions to charity.
situation: Victoria has a lot of clothes that she doesn't wear anymore.
intention: Victoria wants to make room in her closet.
moral_action: Victoria drops off her clothes at a local women's shelter.
moral_consequence: The staff at the shelter thank Victoria for her clothes and Victoria feels good about herself.
immoral_action: Victoria throws out all the clothes that she doesn't wear anymore.
immoral_consequence: Victoria gets a lot of space in her closet, but feels wasteful for just throwing out her clothes.

norm: It's wrong to idealize violent groups
situation: Bob talks about how awesome pirates to his buddy Pete.
intention: Pete wants to give a disagreeing opinion.
moral_action: Pete points out that pirates plundered towns and killed people.
moral_consequence: Bob concedes that's valid, but he still thinks pirates' stance on democracy and equal pay made them progressive for the era.
immoral_action: Pete points out that the British Empire's many conquests in that same era were much cooler.
immoral_consequence: Bob counters by pointing out the British Empire's ships had grossly unequal pay and people forced to sail by threat of violence.

norm: It's wrong to hate people with disabilities.
situation: Dave is a police officer who is introduced to his new desk sergeant, Bill who is in a wheelchair.
intention: Dave wants to react to the news that he has a new boss.
moral_action: Dave tells Bill that he's glad to meet him and will try his hardest to show Bill he's a good officer.
moral_consequence: Bill is impressed by Dave's politeness and is happy that he has at least one good employee already.
immoral_action: Dave tells Bill that he cannot take a man in a wheelchair seriously as a police officer since he can't even make an arrest in his condition.
immoral_consequence: Bill is angry that Dave is so discriminatory towards him and saddened that he thinks he's incapable.

norm: It's good to want to keep one's home looking attractive.
situation: Leon has been feeling very bored and lonely lately.
intention: Leon wants to host a house party.
moral_action: Leon spends a few hours cleaning up his house and doing his dishes and then invites his friends over to drink.
moral_consequence: Leon and his friends have a great night, and he is complimented multiple times on how good his house looks.
immoral_action: Leon doesn't clean up and invites a bunch of friends over to drink.
immoral_consequence: After seeing what a huge mess his place is they all come up with excuses to leave, and he ends up drinking alone and crying.

norm: It's bad to act immature when approaching college age.
situation: Hagar is eating dinner with his potential  frat brothers at a restaurant.
intention: Hagar wants to entertain his friends.
moral_action: Hagar tells his friends stories from his personal life.
moral_consequence: Hagar and his friends become closer.
immoral_action: Hagar makes fart jokes and noises.
immoral_consequence: Hagar is roasted on tic tok when someone uploads a video of his actions.

norm: It's good to assure people when they are worried.
situation: Greg's friend Jim told them they were really worried for his next algebra exam.
intention: Greg wants to say something to Jim.
moral_action: Greg tells Jim that he's worried because he hasn't studied enough.
moral_consequence: Jim agrees with Greg and gets out his notes and textbook.
immoral_action: Greg tells Jim that he needs to suck it up and stop thinking about it.
immoral_consequence: Jim keeps worrying about the exam, and he think Greg is rude.

norm: It's important to be a careful driver.
situation: Roxy is a taxi driver who receives many time-sensitive emails throughout the day.
intention: Roxy wants to respond to her emails on time.
moral_action: Roxy sets aside a time every hour to pull over and check her emails.
moral_consequence: Roxy's emails are received in time, and she is able to drive safely.
immoral_action: Roxy receives an email while driving to pick up a passenger and opens it up right away.
immoral_consequence: Distracted by her email, Roxy crashes into another car and never arrives to pick up her next passenger.

norm: It's bad to oversleep and miss your obligations.
situation: Carlton is going to sleep after a wild party and sets his alarm, so he can get up for work.
intention: Carlton wants to respond to his alarm.
moral_action: Despite the urge to shut off his alarm, Carlton realizes this is risky and gets up from bed.
moral_consequence: Avoiding trouble with his boss, Carlton makes it to work and gets some extra sleep when he gets home.
immoral_action: Carlton hears the loud beeping on his clock and shuts it off because he wants to rest his eyes a few more minutes.
immoral_consequence: Carlton falls back asleep and never makes it into work and is thus written up.

norm: It is wrong make someone feel unimportant.
situation: Malcolm is a child who his at his brother's recital, but he is mad at his brother.
intention: Malcolm wants to get back at his brother.
moral_action: Malcolm waits until after the recital to get back at his brother because he knows he practiced hard for it.
moral_consequence: Malcolm's brother accepts what Malcolm dishes out and apologizes for making him mad in the first place.
immoral_action: Malcolm walks out of the recital when his brother takes the stage.
immoral_consequence: Malcolm's brother knows that he was mad at him but can't understand why he would ignore the recital.

norm: Making a big scene while confronting someone is dramatic.
situation: Roy had a problem with Matt, so he confronted him when he saw him at the store.
intention: Roy wanted Matt to know that he disagreed with him.
moral_action: Roy talked to Matt about the issue that he was having with him.
moral_consequence: Roy was able to resolve his problem with Matt after talking to him.
immoral_action: Roy started to scream at Matt in front of the patrons at the store.
immoral_consequence: Roy was kicked out of the store by the store manager and told not to return.

norm: It's wrong to steal from anyone.
situation: Daniel's bike was stolen and Daniel found out his sketchy neighbor stole it.
intention: Daniel wants to punish his neighbor.
moral_action: Daniel calls the police and tells them his neighbor stole his bike.
moral_consequence: The police find Daniel's bike at the neighbor's place, the neighbor is arrested and Daniel gets his bike back.
immoral_action: Daniel goes in his neighbor's yard at night and drives away in his neighbor's four-wheeler.
immoral_consequence: Daniel gets caught in the act and ends up being arrested.

norm: It's mean to lock your kids in their rooms.
situation: Dave's children Tom and Sandy have made a huge mess by leaving their things everywhere.
intention: Dave wants to punish his children.
moral_action: Dave decides to tell his children they won't be allowed to watch television that night as a punishment.
moral_consequence: Tom and Sandy grow up to realize what their chores and duties are and why it's important to do them.
immoral_action: Dave decides to put both Tom and Sandy in their respective rooms and to lock them in there for the rest of the day.
immoral_consequence: Tom and Sandy are both traumatized as they feel caged in and lonely since they can't call for help.

norm: You should respect the property of your family.
situation: Daphne is the barn on her families farm with her friends.
intention: Daphne wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Daphne invites her friend on a long hike in the park nextdoor.
moral_consequence: Daphne and her friend buy cookies from a vendor in the park for Daphne's family.
immoral_action: Daphne climbs into one of the tractors and attempts to race her friend around the field.
immoral_consequence: Daphne destroys all of her families crops which costs her family thousands of dollars.

norm: It's unacceptable to curse at people.
situation: Steve was having an argument with the manager in his local supermarket.
intention: Steve wants to express his distaste with the manager.
moral_action: Steve tells the manager he thinks he's not paying attention to the needs of the consumers.
moral_consequence: The manager listens, and tells Steve he'll consider what he's said.
immoral_action: Steve calls the manager all types of vulgar names, cursing at him.
immoral_consequence: The manager decides to not deal with Steve at all, just walking away from him.

norm: It is good to lay with your significant other.
situation: Jim is watching the football game when his wife Amy asks him to get a little frisky in the bedroom.
intention: Jim wants to respond to Amy's request.
moral_action: Jim tells Amy that he'll be upstairs before she can even blink a lash of her pretty eye.

norm: It's good to be a concerned citizen.
situation: Nancy called her friend Kay, who had been sick, one afternoon, and they talked for a bit before Nancy had to head off to work.
intention: Nancy wanted to catch up with her friend Kay.
moral_action: Nancy asked Kay if she had been feeling better lately since she had been sick.
moral_consequence: Kay was grateful Nancy asked about how she felt and checked on her with a call.
immoral_action: Nancy did not ask Kay how she had been feeling even though Kay had recently been sick.
immoral_consequence: Kay was disappointed when Nancy got off the phone and thought Nancy did not care about her.

norm: You shouldn't hate people just because of their age.
situation: John a recent grad is having trouble finding jobs, and the ones he applies for tells him he has too little experience.
intention: John wants to work and move out of his parents house.
moral_action: John realizes that while he is frustrated at his own circumstances, hating a particular group wont change things.
moral_consequence: John stops blaming old people for his unemployment and works on his resume to make it better.
immoral_action: John hates old people because they wont retire so young people can get the jobs and experience they need to start their careers.
immoral_consequence: John starts making fun of all the old people he meets, yelling at them to retire and get out of the way.

norm: You shouldn't harass citizens if you're a police officer.
situation: Victor is a new police officer fresh out of the academy whom was just assigned to patrol a new community.
intention: Victor wants his community to respect him.
moral_action: Victor goes out of his way to help members of his community and spends time talking and getting to know them.
moral_consequence: Victor's community grows to trust and respect him and will go out of their way to let him know when they learn of a crime occurring.
immoral_action: Victor constantly pulls people over whom are doing nothing wrong and is very mean to them.
immoral_consequence: Victors community grows to hate him and doesn't cooperate whenever major criminal activity occurs.

norm: It's important to maintain professional relationships at work
situation: William is upset about missing out on a promotion.
intention: He wants to share his feelings with a superior.
moral_action: William collects himself and arranges a meeting to discuss the issue with his boss.
moral_consequence: William is given a good explanation why he wasn't selected and his tact improves the way his superior views him.
immoral_action: William goes to his bosses office in a rage and starts yelling angrily about not being promoted.
immoral_consequence: He greatly offends his boss and is given a suspension.

norm: It is rude to tell everyone about private messages.
situation: Sally gets a private text message from her husband while she is visiting her friend.
intention: Sally wants to make conversation with her friend.
moral_action: Sally talks to her friend about topics of mutual interest but doesn't bring up the text.
moral_consequence: Sally's husband asks her if she told her friend about his text and is happy when she says she didn't.
immoral_action: Sally tells her friend what her husband wrote to her in the private text message.
immoral_consequence: Sally's husband is upset when he finds out that she told her friend about what was meant to be a private matter.

norm: It's bad to steal someone's wifi.
situation: Jason is out on the street and needs to access his email with his phone, so he goes into settings to connect to the internet.
intention: Jason wants to choose which method to connect to the internet with.
moral_action: Jason goes into data and turns it on and uses the mobile phone network to connect to the internet.
moral_consequence: Jason is able to access his email without problem and get what he needs from it.
immoral_action: Jason goes into wi-fi and finds an unsecured connection which he uses to connect to the internet.
immoral_consequence: Jason is caught by the owner of the network and booted out before he can access his email.

norm: It's wrong to be a drug dealer.
situation: Peter works full time, but is falling behind on his bills.
intention: Peter wants to make some extra cash.
moral_action: Peter mows lawns on the weekends to makes some extra cash.
moral_consequence: Peter makes enough to pay off his bills and go debt free.
immoral_action: Peter decides to sell drugs to make extra cash on the side.
immoral_consequence: Peter gets caught by the police and is sent to prison.

norm: You shouldn't honk your horn at people if you're angry.
situation: Jason is stuck behind a slow driver.
intention: Jason wants the driver to be out of his way.
moral_action: Jason passes the slow driver at the dotted yellow line.
moral_consequence: Jason is free of the slow driver.
immoral_action: Jason honks his horn at the driver.
immoral_consequence: The driver becomes angry and yells at Jason.

norm: It is bad taste to road rage.
situation: Jeff is cut off by another driver on his way home from work.
intention: Jeff wants to respond to the other drivers actions.
moral_action: Jeff honks his horn to alert the other driver to his presence,.
moral_consequence: Jeff avoids escalating the incident.
immoral_action: Jeff forces the other car to pull over then gets into a fight with the other driver.
immoral_consequence: Jeff gets arrested for his actions.

norm: People are expected to keep their children safe.
situation: Ralph took his 3 year old daughter to the lake for a family cookout.
intention: Ralph wants let his daughter play in the water.
moral_action: Ralph puts water wings on his daughter and goes into the lake with her.
moral_consequence: His daughter has a great time splashing in the water while staying afloat.
immoral_action: Ralph sits by his cousins on a lawn chair and tells his daughter to go swimming with the other kids.
immoral_consequence: His daughter runs into the lake unaware of the dangers of water and drowns.

norm: You should always help out your coworkers.
situation: Megan coworker's is struggling on a project which she has expertise with and has asked for her help during work hours.
intention: Megan wants to finish her own work on time.
moral_action: Megan makes some time to help her coworker in exchange for some help in return with part of her work.
moral_consequence: Megan's coworker learns how to complete her task and the project goes on without issue.
immoral_action: Megan refuses to help citing that she has her own deadline to meet.
immoral_consequence: Megan's coworker is written up because she struggles with the project.

norm: It's kind to let someone wait indoors instead of outside.
situation: Jake's pizza delivery has just arrived and after greeting the delivery driver he realizes he left his wallet upstairs.
intention: Jake wants to pay for his pizza.
moral_action: Jake invites the driver to step inside while he runs upstairs to grab his wallet.
moral_consequence: The delivery driver is touched by Jake's kindness and vows to be extra quick on his next delivery to Jake's address.
immoral_action: Jake tells the delivery driver to hold on for a second, shuts the door and runs upstairs to grab his wallet.
immoral_consequence: The delivery driver is left waiting outside and gets frustrated.

norm: It is rude to stare.
situation: Sue is eating lunch with a friend in a coffee shop and is sitting across from her.
intention: Sue wants to know what brand jacket her friend is wearing.
moral_action: Sue asks her friend what brand her jacket is, without staring at it for too long.
moral_consequence: Sue's friend is happy to have a conversation, and they talk about their favorite clothing.
immoral_action: Sue stares at her jacket for half an hour to gauge what exact brand it is.
immoral_consequence: Sue's friend gets weirded out at sue for staring and tells her to stop.

norm: You should be tolerant of other people's interests.
situation: Gord is at work and some coworkers have gathered around Nancy who is showing them a sweater she knitted for her cat.
intention: Gord wants to make a comment about the sweater.
moral_action: Gord tells Nancy that it looks just like a human sweater but miniature and that it's cute.
moral_consequence: Nancy smiles because she's delighted that Gord liked it and made a comment about it.
immoral_action: Gord tells Nancy that knitting clothing for cats is ridiculously stupid and a huge waste of time.
immoral_consequence: Nancy is appalled that Gord thinks her endeavor was a waste of time and is insulted that he hated on her.

norm: It's rude to spread negative stories about people.
situation: Wallace got a text that a friend of his might have stolen some clothing at a clothing store.
intention: Wallace wants to find out if his friend actually did steal the clothing.
moral_action: Wallace only texts back the person who told him and doesn't text anyone else about the incident.
moral_consequence: The person who texted Wallace clarifies whether it was true or not.
immoral_action: Wallace immediately tells everyone he knows who is in his contacts the story in order to get clarification.
immoral_consequence: The rumor spreads among Wallace's friends and ultimately his friends think Wallace is a gossiper.

norm: You should always get vaccinated.
situation: Peter works next door to a clinic that gives flu shots and is about to go on his lunch break.
intention: Peter wants to leave work during his lunch break.
moral_action: Peter goes to the clinic, waits in line, and gets a flu shot.
moral_consequence: Peter stays healthy all winter and gets a promotion from his employer because he's so dependable.
immoral_action: Peter walks past the clinic and goes to a sandwich shop to have lunch.
immoral_consequence: Peter catches the flu over winter and misses two weeks of work.

norm: It's bad to have sex with your friends' significant others.
situation: Tom is hanging out with his friend Bill and his wife Susie and realizes he enjoys her company.
intention: Tom wants to be around Jill more.
moral_action: Tom tells Bill and Susie he enjoys their company as good friends.
moral_consequence: Bill and Susie are flattered and hang out with Tom more often.
immoral_action: Tom asks Susie to sleep with him later that night when Bill isn't around.
immoral_consequence: Bill finds out and is angry at Susie and ends his friendship with Tom.

norm: It's not okay to cheat on others.
situation: Frank is in a monotonous relationship with a longtime partner and has fallen out of love with her.
intention: Frank wants to feel passion again.
moral_action: Frank talks with his partner and decides to end the relationship with her.
moral_consequence: Frank's partner appreciates his honesty, and they are able to stay friends afterwards.
immoral_action: Frank ends up seeing another woman outside of his relationship.
immoral_consequence: Frank's partner finds out which destroys their relationship and turns them into enemies.

norm: It's bad to not care if you're parent is crying.
situation: Wesley hears his mother crying through the wall in his bedroom.
intention: Wesley wants the noise to stop.
moral_action: Wesley goes in the next room to check up on his mother and sits with her a bit.
moral_consequence: Wesley's mom genuinely calms down after she feels Wesley's love.
immoral_action: Wesley puts headphones in his ears and blasts some music to drown out the noise.
immoral_consequence: Wesley's mom continues crying, and nobody comes in to check on her.

norm: It's bad to get into fights unless you're defending yourself.
situation: Adam is having bad day when Tom accidentally runs into him.
intention: Adam wants to release his anger.
moral_action: Adam goes home and punches his pillow repeatedly.
moral_consequence: Tom apologizes to Adam and continues his day.
immoral_action: Adam shoves Tom and verbally berates him while threatening to shove him again.
immoral_consequence: Tom get angry and wants to fight Adam back.

norm: It's wrong to ditch people.
situation: Ian and two friends are working on a geocache location project for school, but Ian's two friends are very slow and taking forever.
intention: Ian wants to finish the project.
moral_action: Ian waits for his friends and does his best to encourage them to hurry up, eventually finishing the project.
moral_consequence: Ian's two friends have some motivation to continue and end up getting a good grade thanks to Ian.
immoral_action: Ian goes on ahead without his friends and locates each of the geocaches, finishing the project on his own.
immoral_consequence: Ian's two friends feel left out and abandoned, and Ian's teacher fails him because it was supposed to be a group effort.

norm: It's good to attend a meeting.
situation: Joey has a meeting in the office after his normal work hours.
intention: Joey wants to have a drink with his friends after work.
moral_action: Joey meets his friends at the bar after the meeting in the office.
moral_consequence: Joey relaxes and has a drink, knowing all the new office policies.
immoral_action: Joey skips the office meeting and meets his friends in the bar instead.
immoral_consequence: Joey doesn't know what is going on when he goes to work the next day.

norm: It is wrong to use others.
situation: Kelly's boyfriend needs to borrow some money from her for rent.
intention: Sally wants to help her boyfriend.
moral_action: Sally does work for her neighbor in exchange for money.
moral_consequence: Sally gets paid and is able to help her boyfriend.
immoral_action: Sally is nice to her neighbor that she doesn't like to get money from them.
immoral_consequence: The neighbor gets mad at Sally when she asks for money.

norm: You shouldn't go into your parent's bedroom without their permission.
situation: James was invited to go to his friends house for dinner tonight.
intention: James wants to ask permission from his mom and dad.
moral_action: James knocks on his parents door, and they tell him to wait until they come out, and when they do James asks if he can leave to his friends.
moral_consequence: James gets to see his friend and his mom and dad are glad that he had the sense to knock first.
immoral_action: James walks into his parents room and asks if he can go, but catches them having sex.
immoral_consequence: James and his parents are all embarrassed, and he gets grounded for coming in without knocking.

norm: It's good to help a widow find a therapist.
situation: Kyler is talking to her friend who just lost her husband and is seeking help.
intention: Kyler wants to help her friend feel better.
moral_action: Kyler gets out her computer and helps her friend look up grief counselors in the region.
moral_consequence: Kyler's friend sees a therapist that really helps her in her time of need.
immoral_action: Kyler tells her friend she doesn't need professional assistance and suggests they get some drinks together to help.
immoral_consequence: Kyler's friend doesn't cope well over drinks and really misses out on the help a therapist could have provided.

norm: You shouldn't work so much that you injure yourself.
situation: One of Dustin's cars recently broke down.
intention: Dustin wants to repair his car.
moral_action: Dustin spends a few hours every day working to fix his car.
moral_consequence: Dustin finishes fixing the car by the end of the week and it runs better than it did before it broke down.
immoral_action: Dustin spends all day, and all night working to try to fix the car.
immoral_consequence: That night due to being tired Dustin accidentally kicks the jack causing the car to fall and crush his toes.

norm: It's kind to offer your friends a ride home.
situation: Clay and his friend Jack are at a party where Jack drinks too much and gets drunk, but Clay remains sober.
intention: Clay wants to leave the party.
moral_action: Clay asks Jack if he needs a ride home as he's obviously too drunk to drive.
moral_consequence: Jack accepts the ride and picks up his car the next day when he's sober.
immoral_action: Clay tells Jack and the others at the party he will be leaving and to have a great night.
immoral_consequence: Jack ends up with no one to take him home so drives his own car drunk and gets into an accident.

norm: You shouldn't tell your kids you regret having them.
situation: Gary, a mechanic who was studying engineering until his wife got pregnant, is asked by one of his children why he's a mechanic.
intention: Gary wants to give a response to his child.
moral_action: Gary tells his child that he likes cars and that it's a valuable skill.
moral_consequence: Gary's child sees the value of Gary's work and also learns to fix cars.
immoral_action: Gary tells him the story about studying engineering and says that he regrets having children so quickly.
immoral_consequence: Gary's child thinks that he helped make Gary's life worse and becomes depressed.

norm: It's inappropriate to crush on your wife's friend.
situation: Will and his wife headed to the beach with a married couple that they are friends with.
intention: Will wants to dip his feet in the ocean water.
moral_action: Will takes the group to a boardwalk where they can sit with their feet in the water.
moral_consequence: Will and his wife have a great time conversing with their friends while looking at the ocean in front of them.
immoral_action: Will brings everyone down to the waterfront and his friend's wife strips to a bikini, a sight that Will cannot take his eyes off of.
immoral_consequence: Will stares awkwardly at his friend's wife, causing his wife to get mad at him.

norm: It's bad to destroy people's things.
situation: Dallas watches her bully Sanders leave the room after making fun of her clothes.
intention: Dallas wants to vent her anger.
moral_action: Dallas talks to her teacher about her negative feelings and Sanders.
moral_consequence: Sanders is confronted by the teacher who convinces him to stop being a bully.
immoral_action: Dallas crumples up Sanders homework and tosses it inside the trash.
immoral_consequence: Sanders gets a zero for his homework assignment.

norm: It's good to surprise your wife.
situation: Ben is about to celebrate his wedding anniversary with his wife.
intention: Ben wants to have a good anniversary.
moral_action: Ben plans out a thoughtful evening and surprises his wife with the plan.
moral_consequence: Ben's wife feels loved and is impressed with how thoughtful he is.
immoral_action: Ben tells his wife to plan out the evening, and he will show up.
immoral_consequence: Ben's wife is underwhelmed and questions if he cares about her.

norm: You shouldn't stick your nose into your friend's business.
situation: Travis overhears his friend mumble something bad under her breath, and he sees her walking to the bathroom leaving her laptop open.
intention: Travis wants to know what's going on with his friend.
moral_action: Travis gives her a hug and says he will always be there for her before asking what's wrong.
moral_consequence: Travis' friend feels safe enough to open up to him about her problems.
immoral_action: Travis sits down on her computer and looks through her chat logs for any information.
immoral_consequence: Travis friend snaps at him for invading her privacy when she returns from the bathroom.

norm: It is good to be healthy
situation: James is in a hurry to get to choir practice after work and only has time to pick up fast food.
intention: James wants a tasty dinner.
moral_action: James walks into a Subway and orders a small veggie sandwich and a water.
moral_consequence: James feels light and energetic during choir practice and can tighten his belt a notch.
immoral_action: James pulls throw a McDonald's drive threw and orders a super-sized Big Mac meal.
immoral_consequence: James feels bloated during his choir practice and has to buy a bigger belt.

norm: It's hurtful to laugh at your significant other.
situation: Bevin his attending a party with his girlfriend who stutters in public.
intention: Bevin wants to entertain others.
moral_action: Bevin tells a story from his girlfriend's new book.
moral_consequence: Bevin's girlfriend is approached by a publisher who wants to publish her book.
immoral_action: Bevin laughs at his girlfriend and makes a joke about her speech problems.
immoral_consequence: Bevin's girlfriend starts crying.

norm: One shouldn't operate heavy machinery when drowsy.
situation: Ralph tried his new allergy medication while he was at work and is beginning to feel tired and unusual from it.
intention: Ralph wants to get a full day of work.
moral_action: Ralph tells his supervisor he isn't feeling well, and he is given desk jobs that he can complete without any risk.
moral_consequence: Ralph works despite his fatigue and goes home after working all day.
immoral_action: Ralph doesn’t mention his condition to his supervisor and begins to work using the forklift.
immoral_consequence: Ralph finds himself getting very sleepy towards the end of his shift and nods off while driving, running the forklift into a nearby wall.

norm: It's bad to run with injured legs.
situation: Keith fell down the stairs and hurt his legs over the weekend.
intention: Keith wants to work out.
moral_action: Keith does sit ups and arm curls while his legs are healing.
moral_consequence: Keith feels and looks great after he works out his arms and core.
immoral_action: Keith runs a few laps on the treadmill at the gym.
immoral_consequence: Keith has to go to the doctor because he pulled a muscle.

norm: It's rude to try to deceive other people.
situation: Shawn is applying for jobs that are listed in the wanted ads.
intention: Shawn wants to get a good job.
moral_action: Shawn applies to the jobs he is qualified for and gets enough offers that he can choose the best opportunity.
moral_consequence: Shawn's new boss is happy to have such an eager worker on board and Shawn is happy to have a job.
immoral_action: Shawn doesn't meet the qualifications for a particular opening but says he does on his resume.
immoral_consequence: Shawn gets a job, but the boss is angered when they find out Shawn can't do the basic functions required of the job, which embarrasses Shawn.

norm: It is rude to be loud and disruptive.
situation: An esteemed professor is giving a guest lecture at the University.
intention: Phil wants to ask a question of the Professor.
moral_action: Phil approaches the professor after the lecture.
moral_consequence: Phil learns quite a bit from the woman and finds his academic path in life.
immoral_action: Phil continuously interrupts the lecture, demanding the professor answer in a satisfactory way.
immoral_consequence: Phil never learns what was supposed to be in the lecture and fails that section of the final.

norm: You should keep an eye on your children.
situation: Tori is outside playing catch with her children when she hears the phone ringing from inside the house.
intention: Tori wants to answer the phone.
moral_action: Tori asks her kids to pause the game while she runs inside and watches them from the window as she takes her call.
moral_consequence: Tori's kids remain safe in the yard, and she rejoins them immediately after her phone call.
immoral_action: Leaving her kids to play, Tori runs inside to answer the phone.
immoral_consequence: Tori's son runs out into the street to catch the ball and is nearly hit by a car.

norm: You shouldn't have a fight with your siblings.
situation: Sarah sees her brother is playing a video game at home.
intention: Sarah wants to have fun.
moral_action: Sarah suggests to her brother that they play a two-player game together.
moral_consequence: Sarah's brother has a great time playing with Sarah.
immoral_action: Sarah takes the game away from her brother and starts fighting over who's turn it is.
immoral_consequence: Sarah's mother has to stop working to break up the fight.

norm: It's bad to not regulate the temperature of your apartment.
situation: Gabriel is struggling to pay for her electric bill, and it's one hundred degrees outside.
intention: Gabriel wants to save money.
moral_action: Gabriel eliminates unnecessary expenses.
moral_consequence: Gabriel is less stressed about her ability to afford things.
immoral_action: Gabriel turns off the air conditioner.
immoral_consequence: Gabriel almost passes out from the high heat.

norm: It's bad to drive too fast.
situation: Rob just purchased a brand new Tesla and is anxious to see how well it handles.
intention: Rob wants to see how fast the car can go.
moral_action: Rob contacts the owner of a local race track and makes arrangements to try the car out under safe and legal conditions.
moral_consequence: Rob has a great time, pushing the car to its limits on the smooth racetrack.
immoral_action: Rob drives to a winding road in a residential area and begins to drive very fast.
immoral_consequence: Rob is pulled over for driving 100 mps in a 15 mph school zone and the officer cites him and suspends Rob's license.

norm: It's good to care about your children's safety.
situation: David is at working at home with his three-year-old son and five-year-old daughter.
intention: David wants to get work done.
moral_action: David calls a babysitter to watch the children while he gets work done.
moral_consequence: The children play happily under the watchful eye of the babysitter and David finishes his work.
immoral_action: David lets the children play in the kitchen by themselves while he gets work done.
immoral_consequence: The children nearly burn themselves and make a mess in the kitchen.

norm: It's mean to hit someone.
situation: Jenna is a teenager babysitting Ronnie who is acting out and misbehaving.
intention: Jenna wants Ronnie to stop misbehaving.
moral_action: Jenna puts Ronnie in time out for a few minutes and temporarily takes his favorite toy away until he is ready to behave.
moral_consequence: Ronnie realizes that he has been bad and tries to stop.
immoral_action: Jenna slaps Ronnie the next time he does something he's not supposed to.
immoral_consequence: Ronnie cries and Jenna gets in trouble when Ronnie tells his parents what happened.

norm: You should not bring your bad habits to the workplace.
situation: After a tough work day Joe likes to watch pornographic movies when he gets home.
intention: Joe is having a rough morning at work and wants to relax.
moral_action: Joe goes out for a massage during his lunch break.
moral_consequence: Joe is able to return to work refreshed and ready to tackle the afternoon.
immoral_action: Joe locks himself in his office during lunch and watches a porno online to unwind.
immoral_consequence: Joe gets censured by HR when his computer is flagged for inappropriate content.

norm: You shouldn't kill yourself.
situation: Mary is saddened by her breakup with her boyfriend recently.
intention: Mary wants to overcome her sad feeling.
moral_action: Mary signs up for a yoga class to improve both her physical and mental health.
moral_consequence: Mary feels much better and meets another man in the class who starts to date her.
immoral_action: Mary commits suicide to end her problem.
immoral_consequence: Mary is dead and her family is heartbroken.

norm: It's wrong to copy the answers from someone else's paper.
situation: Jen has been struggling with her math class and there is a big test coming up.
intention: Jen wants to do well on the test to improve her grade.
moral_action: Jen spends as much time as possible studying for the test.
moral_consequence: Jen's parents are proud of her when she aces the math test.
immoral_action: Jen relies on the person sitting next to her who is good at math and looks at his answers during the test.
immoral_consequence: Jen gets caught cheating on the test and her parents are notified.

norm: It's not okay to threaten people in life.
situation: Charles is a poor, muscular man who needs to buy food for himself.
intention: Charles wants money to buy food.
moral_action: Charles takes up a job at a shipping dock that requires lots of muscle.
moral_consequence: Charles earns decent wages and has money to survive.
immoral_action: Charles hides in an alley and robs people at knife point as they pass by.
immoral_consequence: The people lose their money and report Charles to the police, who then put a warrant out for his arrest.

norm: You should always make your partner's birthday special.
situation: Ben's wife Melanie has her birthday on Saturday.
intention: Ben wants to spend a lazy Saturday in bed.
moral_action: Ben prepares ahead of time a surprise night birthday party for Melanie and sleeps in most of the day.
moral_consequence: Melanie thinks Ben loves her a lot and feels really close to him.
immoral_action: Ben sleeps in all day long and doesn't talk to his wife.
immoral_consequence: Ben's wife Melanie thinks Ben doesn't care about her anymore and loves him less.

norm: You should not judge others just for how they look.
situation: Josh is riding the subway when a man wearing clothes with holes in them comes up to him and asks him for directions.
intention: Josh wants to respond to the man.
moral_action: Josh gives the man directions, and it turns out the man needs to go to the laundromat because he was doing his laundry.
moral_consequence: The man gets to the laundromat.
immoral_action: Josh ignores the man because he assumes he's crazy and homeless.
immoral_consequence: The man feels bad about himself and doesn't get the directions he needs.

norm: It's bad to steal someone else's idea.
situation: Danelle is searching online for inspiration to help her complete her short story before class tomorrow.
intention: Danelle wants to turn in her assignment on time.
moral_action: Danelle does some writing exercises she sees online to overcome her writers block.
moral_consequence: Danelle applies this exercise successfully for her other assignments throughout the semester.
immoral_action: Danelle turns in a short story from someone's blog.
immoral_consequence: Danelle fails the class when the professors discovers the truth about her assignment.

norm: It's good to get exercise with your friends.
situation: Jenna's friends suggest going for a morning walk together to improve their health.
intention: Jenna wants to spend her free time in the morning on her phone.
moral_action: Jenna brings her phone on the walks to play inspiring music while she scrolls through her social media accounts.
moral_consequence: Jenna's friends gently mock her phone addiction as they walk together.
immoral_action: "Jenna convinces her friends to watch ""just one more"" cat video until they've used up all the time they meant to spend walking."
immoral_consequence: Jenna's friends eventually start going on walks without her, and she feels excluded.

norm: You shouldn't ask for a refund that you don't deserve.
situation: Erin is eating out at an expensive restaurant and is surprised by the menu prices.
intention: Erin wants to save money.
moral_action: Erin orders inexpensive items and sticks to water for the drink.
moral_consequence: The service staff is happy to get a tip and the restaurant gains a new customer.
immoral_action: Erin complains about the meal and gets it comped.
immoral_consequence: The servers and restaurant lose money on the order.

norm: You should stand up for your smaller sibling.
situation: Mia's friends all made fun of her sister Maya today.
intention: Mia wants to tell her friends something.
moral_action: Mia tells her friends to knock it off and to stop laughing at Maya.
moral_consequence: They quickly quit laughing after Mia stands up for her.
immoral_action: Mia tells them funnier stories about Maya, so they laugh even more.
immoral_consequence: Mia's friends continue to laugh at her sister.

norm: It's rude to expect your siblings to do your chores.
situation: Taylor and Joe are doing their weekly chores and Taylor begins to feel tired and bored.
intention: Taylor wants to find a way to get out of her chores.
moral_action: Taylor makes a deal with Joe to do his chores the following week if he does her chores today.
moral_consequence: Taylor is able to get out of doing her chores for the day.
immoral_action: Taylor tells Joe that the rest of the list is for him and walks out of the room.
immoral_consequence: Joe is left to pick up the slack of Taylor.

norm: It's wrong to use offensive terms.
situation: Dave is at a work training session on sensitivity and is shown a video fo some people who struggle with mental disabilities.
intention: Dave wants to react to the video.
moral_action: Dave tells the group that the people in the video must have a hard time in life.
moral_consequence: The group agrees with Dave and are happy that he recognizes that people with mental disabilities face a bigger struggle.
immoral_action: "Dave tells the group that the ""retards"" in the video must have a hard time in life."
immoral_consequence: The group is disgusted that Dave would use that derogatory term and are made uncomfortable.

norm: You shouldn't steal someone's wallet.
situation: Vince has excellent dexterity and puts on public performances where he removes things from people without them knowing.
intention: Vince wants to perform on a rich man.
moral_action: Vince performs on the man, steals anything he can, then returns it all.
moral_consequence: The man gets a good laugh and still has all of his possessions.
immoral_action: During the performance, Vince removes the man's wallet and puts a similar one in its place.
immoral_consequence: The man can't find his money and is unable to pay for his dinner.

norm: It is rude to hog equipment at the gym.
situation: James has a wrestling match coming up, and he always trains at the same small gym.
intention: James wants to put on lots of muscle match before his next match.
moral_action: James asks the gym manager if he can keep his own set of custom free weights in his locker.
moral_consequence: "The other gym patrons are impressed by James' custom equipment and start calling him ""Mr. Prepared""."
immoral_action: James starts hogging the gym's weight stations for four hours a day.
immoral_consequence: " All the gym regulars start addressing James as ""you equipment-hogging jackass""."

norm: It is wrong to interfere in someone else's friendship.
situation: Jane is chatting with her brother Bob, who's complaining about problems he's been having with his best friend Tim.
intention: Jane wants to offer Bob some solutions.
moral_action: Jane tells Bob about what she did when she was facing a similar problem, while also pointing out the differences in their respective situations.
moral_consequence: Bob applies parts of Jane's resolution to her problem to his own situation and manages to salvage his relationship with Tim.
immoral_action: Jane tells Bob that he should immediately sever the friendship, and she states her very negative opinion of Tim.
immoral_consequence: Bob considers Jane's solution and breaks off his friendship with Tim.

norm: You shouldn't date someone with a partner.
situation: Harry has been single for many years and is starting to feel very lonely.
intention: Harry wants to be affection with a partner.
moral_action: Harry joins a dating app and looks for someone who is a single.
moral_consequence: Harry finds a nice girl who is also very honest.
immoral_action: Harry starts dating his friends partner behind their back.
immoral_consequence: Harry feels guilty for betraying his friend.

norm: It's not okay to live a delinquent lifestyle.
situation: James just graduated from high school and is trying to decide what to do for the next five years.
intention: James wants a low-stress, enjoyable lifestyle.
moral_action: James decides to work part-time in fast food while attending classes at the local university.
moral_consequence: James graduates with a biology degree and finds a lucrative job as a pharmaceutical salesperson.
immoral_action: James decides to move into an abandoned building with his friends and support himself by taking things from unattended houses.
immoral_consequence: James is occasionally arrested but usually has a great time partying with his friends.

norm: It's good to have courage to do things.
situation: Sam is at school when the bully comes in to the room he's in and tells everyone to give him their lunch money.
intention: Sam wants to keep his lunch money.
moral_action: Sam stands up to the bully and tells him he's not letting him take anyone's lunch money.
moral_consequence: The bully looks at Sam and decides it's not worth it and leaves the room, the other kids thank Sam and offer to buy him a milkshake after school.
immoral_action: Sam runs out of the room away from the bully.
immoral_consequence: The bully tracks down Sam after school and beats him up.

norm: It's wrong to take advantage of peoples hospitality
situation: Gil is taken in by his friends Bob and Barb after falling on hard times.
intention: Gil wants to have a place to stay.
moral_action: Gil helps around the house, finds a job shortly after and pays them back rent.
moral_consequence: Gil is back on his feet and on good terms with Bob and Barb.
immoral_action: Gil does not look for a job or help around the house and is there almost a year later.
immoral_consequence: Gil is kicked out and loses the friendship with Bob and Barb.

norm: It's wrong to argue with your mother.
situation: Sarah bought a new outfit to wear to school but her mother tells her to wear something else because it's inappropriate.
intention: Sarah wants to respond to her mother.
moral_action: Sarah realizes her mother is right about the outfit and tells her that she will go change.
moral_consequence: Sarah's mother is glad she isn't going to be dressing inappropriately for school.
immoral_action: Sarah asks her mother why it's inappropriate and says that she's being too critical, this is what all her friends are wearing.
immoral_consequence: Sarah's mother tells her not to argue with her anymore, or she'll be grounded.

norm: It's bad to steal other people's things.
situation: Carl is at Monty's house and sees that Monty has gotten the same model bike that Carl has been eyeing.
intention: Carl wants the same bike Monty has.
moral_action: Carl saves up and gets the same bike Monty has.
moral_consequence: Carl and Monty ride their bikes together and have a good time.
immoral_action: Carl breaks into Monty's house when he isn't home and takes the bike for himself.
immoral_consequence: Monty calls the police, and Carl is arrested when he's caught.

norm: It is rude to get angry with retail workers.
situation: Mitch is trying to return a defective shirt he recently purchased, and the clerk tells him she is unable to refund the item.
intention: Mitch wants to get his money back.
moral_action: Mitch remains calm and tells the clerk he is going to speak to a manager about the issue.
moral_consequence: The clerk is relieved that Mitch is going to talk to someone else instead of her.
immoral_action: Mitch gets angry with the clerk and raises his voice while demanding a refund.
immoral_consequence: The clerk feels upset and frustrated dealing with a rude customer.

norm: It's nice to ask for permission to do things.
situation: Curt was staying at his father's house for the weekend.
intention: Curt wants pizza for dinner.
moral_action: Curt asks his father if they can have pizza for dinner that night.
moral_consequence: Curt's father calls the pizza restaurant and has a couple of pizzas delivered.
immoral_action: Curt calls and orders a pizza using his father's credit card.
immoral_consequence: Curt's father grounds him for using his card without his permission.

norm: It's wrong to postpone keeping yourself or others safe.
situation: Bob keeps putting off buying the new security system because it will take work to install it.
intention: Bob wants to prioritize tasks at work.
moral_action: Bob finally puts the new system in this month and people are happy it's finally there.
moral_consequence: After being installed for only days the new system both prevents a robbery and helps the police identify the robber.
immoral_action: Bob puts the system off this month as well, surprising no one.
immoral_consequence: Bob's office gets robbed and the old security system fails to prevent it.

norm: It's wrong to have two pets that don't get along.
situation: James knew his dog didn't like other dogs, but then his friend offered him an adorable Labradoodle puppy.
intention: James wants to spend time with the Labradoodle puppy.
moral_action: James says that he can't take another dog, but offers to walk the puppy for his friend.
moral_consequence: James regularly takes the puppy for long walks then goes home to his old dog.
immoral_action: James adopts the Labradoodle puppy and brings it home to meet his old dog.
immoral_consequence: The old dog keeps trying to bite the puppy and James has to lock her outside.

norm: You shouldn't steal money from others.
situation: Basil is in desperate need of a loan and is at the bank asking for one when he is turned down.
intention: Basil wants to find a way to acquire the money he needs.
moral_action: Basil goes to a pay day lender who will give him the loan but at higher rates.
moral_consequence: Basil gets the loan he needs giving him temporary financial relief that will get him through the month.
immoral_action: Basil reaches over into the teller's till and pulls out a wad of cash before running away.
immoral_consequence: The bank calls the police who quickly apprehend Basil and arrest him for theft.

norm: You are expected to be understanding of other people's problems.
situation: Paula and her friend Jenny are hanging out and Jenny is telling Paula about problems in her current relationship.
intention: Paula wants to give Jenny some advice.
moral_action: Paula listens to Jenny and tries to take her perspective when telling her what she would do if she found herself in such a situation.
moral_consequence: Jenny appreciates Paula's advice and takes it into consideration when trying to resolve her problems.
immoral_action: Paula criticizes Jenny for getting herself in such a situation and tells her what she need to do to get out of it.
immoral_consequence: Jenny is slightly put off by Paula's harsh attitude and decides to stop confiding in her in the future.

norm: It is wrong to waste company time.
situation: Carl works for as a shipping clerk, making sure products are shipped out in a timely manner.
intention: Carl wants to work at his own pace.
moral_action: Carl spends the morning packing the orders, then reorganizes the files after the carrier has picked up the orders.
moral_consequence: All orders are ready when the carrier drops by, and customers receive their shipments on time.
immoral_action: Carl spends half the morning reorganizing the files, then starts packing orders after lunch.
immoral_consequence: The orders are not ready for shipment when the carrier stops by at 3, so they are delayed by a day causing some customers to miss deadlines.

norm: You should say thank you when someone gives you money.
situation: Ginger receives a cash gift from her grandmother.
intention: Ginger wants to respond to the gift.
moral_action: Ginger thanks her grandmother for the gift.
moral_consequence: Ginger's grandmother hugs her.
immoral_action: Ginger tells her grandmother that she should have given more cash.
immoral_consequence: Ginger's grandmother takes the gift back.

norm: It's good to move somewhere to live with your partner.
situation: David has been dating his girlfriend Hanna for a while.
intention: David wants to move out from his mother's home.
moral_action: David gets an apartment with his girlfriend Hanna who is also moving from home.
moral_consequence: David and Hanna save more money than if they had rented an apartment themselves.
immoral_action: David moves out and lives in his car in the alley.
immoral_consequence: David is arrested for violating vagrancy laws in his town.

norm: It's rude to judge someone else's job.
situation: Paul is at a party where people are introducing themselves when Joe tells everyone he's a janitor.
intention: Paul wants to make a comment about janitors to Joe.
moral_action: Paul tells Joe that janitors do a hard and thankless job and that he should be proud to be one.
moral_consequence: Joe is happy to hear that Paul thinks so highly of janitors and his self esteem grows.
immoral_action: Paul tells Joe that janitors are low class people doing a disgusting and dirty job, and he should be ashamed of his class status.
immoral_consequence: Joe is insulted that Paul thinks that janitors are below him and angry that Paul thinks janitors should be ashamed of who they are.

norm: It's wrong to publish someone's secret emails.
situation: Crystal receives an email from a male friend, expressing deep feelings of attraction and love.
intention: Crystal wants get advice from her friends about the possibility of forming a new romantic relationship.
moral_action: Crystal calls a close friend and discusses the email she received, in private, asking for advice on how to proceed in the potential relationship.
moral_consequence: The friend who wrote the email feels that his privacy has been respected and Crystal's other friends have no reason to question her trustworthiness.
immoral_action: Crystal posts the full text of her friend's email to her Facebook account as a status, asking her friends for comments.
immoral_consequence: The friend who wrote the email feels betrayed and hurt, and all of Crystal's friends question her trustworthiness and judgement.

norm: It's bad to scam someone.
situation: James was faced with $20,000 of medical debt after surviving a car crash.
intention: James wants to get rid of all his debt.
moral_action: James declares bankruptcy and asks the court for mercy given his bad luck.
moral_consequence: James' medical debt is discharged in bankruptcy, allowing him to start over.
immoral_action: James starts calling people and telling them they can pay him a $200 processing fee to receive their next stimulus check early.
immoral_consequence: James earns the money and isn't caught because he uses proxies to hide where he's calling from.

norm: It's grossly immoral to maim another person's body.
situation: Richard is a medical researcher up for tenure if only his research on methods for replacing fingers had enough subjects.
intention: Richard needs to find one more subject for his research.
moral_action: Richard expands his search to include groups historically underrepresented in research.
moral_consequence: Richard gets a few more subjects and proves his theory.
immoral_action: Richard chops the finger off of his research assistant without his consent.
immoral_consequence: Richard is blacklisted from universities as he serves time in jail for assault.

norm: It's rude to spy on your neighbors.
situation: Jack suspects that his neighbor is stealing his mail every day.
intention: Jack wants to get to the bottom of this.
moral_action: Jack approaches his neighbor civilly and asks him if he knows what is going on with the mail lately.
moral_consequence: The neighbor reveals that the mail carrier sometimes mixes up addresses in this neighborhood, and just be patient.
immoral_action: Jack spies on his neighbor and sets up cameras to try to catch him in the act.
immoral_consequence: Jack gets caught spying on his neighbor and then their interactions going forward are very awkward.

norm: You shouldn't borrow things from others without asking.
situation: John's yard is covered in fallen leaves due to the season, and he noticed his neighbors rake up against a tree.
intention: John wants to rake his yard.
moral_action: John knocks on his neighbors door and asks to borrow the rake.
moral_consequence: The neighbor lets him borrow the rake and is pleased that he can help.
immoral_action: John takes the rake without permission and uses it to rake his yard.
immoral_consequence: John's neighbor spots him going over to take the rake and finds him to be rude.

norm: People should not overstay their welcome as a guest.
situation: Rachel is visiting a friend's house for dinner and her friend has work in the morning.
intention: Rachel wants to enjoy herself.
moral_action: Rachel makes sure to catch up with her friend over the meal and leaves soon after they finish eating, so that her friend can get enough sleep.
moral_consequence: Rachel's friend enjoys Rachel's visit and gets a good night's rest which leaves her ready for the work day.
immoral_action: Rachel lingers at her friend's house well after the meal is complete and into the night because she is enjoying the conversations.
immoral_consequence: Rachel's friend is too polite to ask her to leave and ends up losing sleep which makes her work performance suffer the next day.

norm: It's bad to frame someone for something.
situation: John has made a costly mistake at work that will have strong repercussions.
intention: John wants to resolve the issue.
moral_action: John owns up to his bosses about the mistake and presents possible solutions.
moral_consequence: John's bosses give him an opportunity to right the wrong, and he is luckily able to do so.
immoral_action: John knows that a co-worker has a reputation for making mistakes, so he makes it seem as though that co-worker was responsible.
immoral_consequence: The co-worker is fired and John's health deteriorates as he is racked with guilt.

norm: It is important to get along with your coworkers.
situation: Paul is part of a tight-knit team at work that has just added a new member, Brenda, whose personality and interests are very different from the rest of the team.
intention: Paul wants to maintain a good working environment.
moral_action: Paul gets to know Brenda better and finds ways to include her with the rest of the group.
moral_consequence: Paul makes a new friend in Brenda and the team continues to work together well.
immoral_action: Paul begins excluding Brenda from social settings because she doesn't fit in with the group and makes things awkward.
immoral_consequence: Brenda makes a complaint against Paul for bullying and Paul is reprimanded.

norm: It's bad to mooch off of your friends.
situation: Jane is invited on weekend trip by her well-to-do friend from school.
intention: Jane wants to go on the trip with her friend.
moral_action: Jane goes on the trip with her friend and insists of paying for most of her own expenses.
moral_consequence: Jan's friend has respect for Jane for paying her own way during the trip.
immoral_action: Jane goes on the trip with her rich friend then asks them to pay for all her expenses during the trip, which her friend does.
immoral_consequence: Jane's friend thinks Jane showed a lack of character by asking them to pay for everything on the trip.

norm: It's wrong to destroy a relationship.
situation: Jeff knows John has been unfaithful to his girlfriend.
intention: Jeff wants John to admit the truth.
moral_action: Jeff suggests to John he should own up to his actions and ask for forgiveness.
moral_consequence: John explains and apologizes for his behavior to his girlfriend, and she forgives him.
immoral_action: Jeff tells John's girlfriend about the infidelity and tells her she should confront John about it.
immoral_consequence: John is devastated when his girlfriend breaks up with him.

norm: It's okay you don't make every event for every friend.
situation: Chuck has RSVP'd to his friend Juan's dinner party, and a week later is invited to another one by his friend Dave for the same night.
intention: Chuck wants to please his friends.
moral_action: Chuck thanks Dave for his invite, but tells him that he already has commitments for that night.
moral_consequence: Dave tells Chuck that it isn't a problem, and they catch up at a later time.
immoral_action: Chuck leaves Juan's dinner party early to go to Dave's.
immoral_consequence: Juan feels like Chuck has chosen Dave over him.

norm: It's dishonest to scam people
situation: Amanda has a car that doesn't work very well, and she doesn't want to have to deal with it anymore.
intention: Amanda wants to sell her car.
moral_action: Amanda is honest about the car's quality and sells the car for parts.
moral_consequence: Amanda doesn't make a lot of money, but she also doesn't have to deal with the car anymore, and other people can use the pieces of the car for themselves.
immoral_action: Amanda tells people the car is fully operational and sells the car.
immoral_consequence: The person who buys the car realizes the car doesn't work and sues Amanda.

norm: It's wrong to burgle people's houses.
situation: Dave is being harassed by a loan shark to repay a loan by tomorrow or the loan shark will hurt him.
intention: Dave needs to acquire money quickly.
moral_action: Dave decides to call his  parents and beg them for a loan to get him out of trouble.
moral_consequence: Dave does not break any laws and manages to figure out a solution to the problem.
immoral_action: Dave decides to sneak into a house in a wealthy neighborhood and take some jewels he can pawn for cash.
immoral_consequence: Dave is later identified on a security camera and arrested and sent to jail.

norm: It's wrong to step on a persons biggest dreams.
situation: Martha is at home listening to her son Jack tell her he dreams of being a dancer.
intention: Martha wants to help her son be successful.
moral_action: Martha tells Jack he can do anything he wants to, and she supports him always.
moral_consequence: Jack feels closer to his mom and becomes more confident in himself.
immoral_action: Martha tells Jack there's no future in dancing, and he should become a doctor.
immoral_consequence: Jack resents his mom and gives up his dreams and loses confidence in himself.

norm: It's bad to have sex with prostitutes.
situation: Mark is in the mood for physical intimacy, but his girlfriend is in another state.
intention: Mark wants to have sex.
moral_action: Mark sends a sexy picture to his girlfriend with a request for fun times on a webcam.
moral_consequence: Mark's girlfriend gains confidence performing for Mark on camera.
immoral_action: Mark hires prostitutes to satisfy his cravings.
immoral_consequence: Mark's girlfriend breaks up with him when she discovers his affair.

norm: It's selfish to not share with others your living with.
situation: Coy has just gone to the grocery store and is putting his groceries away in the cabinet.
intention: Coy wants to eat some of the chips that he bought.
moral_action: Coy eats some of his chips and offers to share some with his father.
moral_consequence: Coy's father takes a few of his chips and offers Coy some of the snacks that he has.
immoral_action: Coy eats some of his chips and refuses to share any with his father.
immoral_consequence: At dinner time, Coy's father tells him to fend for himself and find his own food.

norm: It's bad to dictate what your significant other can do.
situation: Linda has a partner who is getting awfully close to their friend who seems flirty.
intention: Linda wants to stop the friend from getting too close.
moral_action: Linda calmly explains how she feels to her partner in a heartfelt way.
moral_consequence: Linda's partner understands and gives her the reassurance that she needs.
immoral_action: Linda scolds her partner and forbids him from interacting with the friend.
immoral_consequence: Linda's partner feels angry with her because he is mistrusted and controlled.

norm: It's ok to hunt for your own meat.
situation: James, who lives near a large forest, was recently laid off and his family is having trouble affording groceries,.
intention: James wants to make sure his family gets enough protein.
moral_action: James hunts deer and wild birds so his family can eat the meat.
moral_consequence: James' family has a hearty diet until he's eventually able to find work again.
immoral_action: James begins escorting wealthy businessmen into the forest to hunt for pleasure.
immoral_consequence: James uses his salary to buy his family meat until protests from animal rights groups put his tours out of business.

norm: You should not deceive your coworkers.
situation: Clark is scheduled to work on the same night he made a date with Lois.
intention: Clark wants Jimmy to cover his shift.
moral_action: Clark tells his boss the truth and asks if he can switch with Jimmy.
moral_consequence: Clark ends up working that night.
immoral_action: Clark asks Jimmy to switch shifts with him because his grandmother is in the hospital.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy ends up working that night while Clark has a great date night.

norm: It's good to be supportive of your depressed partner.
situation: Tracy's husband James is going through a bout of depression which is tough on the couple.
intention: Tracy wants to respond to James' depression.
moral_action: Tracy tells James that she will be there for him while he is going through depression.
moral_consequence: James will feel supported by Tracy and want to work to get better.
immoral_action: Tracy tells James that she's going to move out while he is going through depression.
immoral_consequence: James will feel that Tracy does not love him and go into deeper depression.

norm: It's wrong to question your friend's religion.
situation: Jessica's friend Amy is getting married and has decided to convert to Judaism for her future husband.
intention: Jessica wants to speak to Amy about her decision.
moral_action: Jessica offers Amy her support and understanding.
moral_consequence: Jessica gains insight into her friends spiritual side.
immoral_action: Jessica questions Amy incessantly about whether she is making the right decision.
immoral_consequence: Jessica creates a distance between herself and Amy with her doubts.

norm: It's hurtful to put your mother in a home.
situation: Kevin's mother has Alzheimer's and is losing touch with reality.
intention: Kevin wants his mother to be cared for.
moral_action: Kevin works part time so he can care for his mother in his home.
moral_consequence: Kevin's mother gets the care and support that she needs.
immoral_action: Kevin puts his mother into an assisted living home.
immoral_consequence: The employees at the home are not patient with Kevin's mother and abuse her.

norm: Siblings are expected to do nice things for each.
situation: Mila and her sister like each other but are not very close.
intention: Mila wants to feel loved by her sister.
moral_action: Mila makes a point of regularly helping her sister as much as her sister helps her.
moral_consequence: Mila's sister feels loved and respected by Mila.
immoral_action: Mila regularly asks her sister for favors but rarely reciprocates.
immoral_consequence: Mila's sister is always generous to Mila but feels taken advantage of.

norm: It's good to help someone who is choking on food.
situation: Robert sees a stranger choking on food at a restaurant and is considering using the heimlich maneuver on him.
intention: Robert wants to decide if he wants to help the stranger out or not.
moral_action: Robert quickly moves to the stranger and uses the heimlich maneuver to save the stranger.
moral_consequence: The food gets dislodged from the stranger's throat and his life is saved.
immoral_action: Robert sits back and waits for someone else to use the heimlich maneuver on the stranger.
immoral_consequence: No one steps up to use the heimlich maneuver on the stranger, so he dies from the lack of oxygen.

norm: You shouldn't marry somebody you can't trust
situation: Claudia is dating a salesman, who lies to his customers to make sales, and her boyfriend has just proposed to her.
intention: Claudia wants to give him a thoughtful response.
moral_action: Claudia decides that people are consistent and that he can't be trusted with anyone, so she breaks up with him.
moral_consequence: Claudia's ex-boyfriend sees that his way of living has cost him a good relationship and begins to change.
immoral_action: Claudia thinks about it and decides that her boyfriend will be honest with her, so she accepts his offer.
immoral_consequence: When they marry, Claudia's husband lies to her just like he lies to everyone else.

norm: It's wrong to start fights over trivial matters.
situation: Gabe is talking to his friend who made a point which he feels certain is incorrect.
intention: Gabe wants to feel validated that he is correct.
moral_action: Gabe emphasizes that it doesn't really matter but sends his friend a link proving him right.
moral_consequence: Gabe's friend is able to shrug it off and agree with him.
immoral_action: Gabe gets into a fight with his friend and proves his point to her.
immoral_consequence: Gabe's friend is put off because it wasn't that important to them to begin with.

norm: You should pay for the food you eat.
situation: Eric has just finished eating a pricey meal at a restaurant.
intention: Eric wants to save money on his food.
moral_action: Eric finds a coupon for the restaurant online which he redeems.
moral_consequence: The servers and restaurants are paid accordingly.
immoral_action: Eric performs a dine and dash leaving without paying the bill.
immoral_consequence: The service staff and business lose money.

norm: It's nice to take people  along on your traveling plans.
situation: John is looking through a travel book with his girlfriend when he decides he wants to travel.
intention: John wants to take a trip to Paris.
moral_action: John asks his girlfriend to join him on an exciting trip to Paris, which she does.
moral_consequence: John's girlfriend has a great time traveling with him and feels closer to him as a result of the trip.
immoral_action: John travels to Paris by himself telling his girlfriend he wants to have a personal adventure.
immoral_consequence: John's girlfriend feels insulted that John doesn't want her to join him and considers ending the relationship.

norm: It's rude to beg people for things.
situation: Dan is hungry and goes into the kitchen where his mom is cleaning the countertop.
intention: Dan wants some food.
moral_action: Dan opens the fridge and gets some yogurt to eat.
moral_consequence: Dan enjoys the food and satisfies his hunger.
immoral_action: Dan gets on his knees and begs for food, telling his mom that he's starving and won't survive.
immoral_consequence: Dan's mom gets annoyed with him and sends him to his room without food.

norm: It's good to try and include others.
situation: Tina was going to a movie and had extra tickets to the movie, and her sisters wanted to go.
intention: Tina wanted to talk with others at the movie theater.
moral_action: Tina brings her sisters with her to the movies and talks with them.
moral_consequence: Tina's sisters thank her for the opportunity and hug her after talking.
immoral_action: Tina told her sisters she didn't want to bring them with her and talks to the cash register instead.
immoral_consequence: Tina's sister feel left out and get mad at Tina.

norm: It is good to be honest with your siblings.
situation: Kate is going to meet a man she met on Tinder, but she hasn't told her sister yet.
intention: Kate doesn't want her sister to worry about her.
moral_action: Kate tells her sister about the date and gives the man's phone number and license plate to her.
moral_consequence: Kate should be safe in case anything bad happens and is happy that she doesn't have to lie to her sister.
immoral_action: Kate tells his sister that she's going with her friend to get ice cream.
immoral_consequence: Kate doesn't have anyone to help her in case the date with the man goes wrong.

norm: It's wrong not to go to school.
situation: Hamilton's family is paying his way through college, but he is getting bored with his courses.
intention: Hamilton wants to lose the boredom brought on by his courses.
moral_action: Hamilton sees a guidance counselor about changing his classes.
moral_consequence: Hamilton is able to change his classes to ones that motivate him to continue with college.
immoral_action: Hamilton drops out of college.
immoral_consequence: Hamilton's family is unable get a refund, and ultimately lose a lot of money by sending him off to school.

norm: It is rude to make unfounded complaints.
situation: Jeri was going to dinner at her local restaurant.
intention: Jeri wanted to get a free dessert at her local restaurant.
moral_action: Jeri praised the food to the restaurant manager and then presented a coupon to her waiter that entitled her to a free dessert.
moral_consequence: Because Jeri praised the food, the restaurant manager gave the cook a raise.
immoral_action: Even though she liker her food, Jeri complained about her meal to the restaurant manager so that he would offer her a free dessert.
immoral_consequence: Because Jeri complained about the food, the restaurant manager fired the cook.

norm: It's uncaring to avoid your friends.
situation: Kyle is playing video games when his phone starts ringing, and he can see it's from his friend John.
intention: Kyle wants the phone to stop ringing.
moral_action: Kyle answers the phone and says hello to his friend John.
moral_consequence: John is delighted to hear Kyle's voice and tells him what he was calling about.
immoral_action: Kyle quickly puts the phone on mute, stopping the phone from ringing.
immoral_consequence: John is annoyed that Kyle isn't answering his phone and wonders where he could be.

norm: It's wrong to stop your car randomly in the street.
situation: Bane got new anti-lock brakes put into his car, and he liked them.
intention: Bane wants to make sure his car is in good shape.
moral_action: Bane drives safely and makes sure to test his brakes in a parking lot.
moral_consequence: Bane knows his brakes work and now he can continue his drive.
immoral_action: Bane keeps randomly stopping in the street to test his new brakes out.
immoral_consequence: Bane has another car crash into him when he stops unexpectedly.

norm: You should dress up for special occasions.
situation: Mandy is going to a special and formal dinner with family that she doesn't see often.
intention: Mandy wants to get ready in a short time to deal with traffic on the way.
moral_action: Mandy goes with her reliable black dress with shoes that match.
moral_consequence: The family gives Mandy a lot of compliments on her dress.
immoral_action: Mandy dresses in her casual clothing, so she can leave in a hurry.
immoral_consequence: The family thinks badly of Mandy because of what she choose to wear.

norm: It's good to spend time with your grand-kids.
situation: Jan, who has arthritis in her hips, agrees to babysit her grandkids while her daughter is on a business trip.
intention: Jan wants to avoid too much walking.
moral_action: Jan sits in her chair as she tells the kids stories and teaches them recipes they carry out step by step.
moral_consequence: Jan's grandkids beg their mother to let them stay with their grandmother more often.
immoral_action: Jan shuts the kids in their own room with two iPads for their entire stay.
immoral_consequence: The kids are quiet, but say that they would have rather spent time with their grandmother.

norm: You should always look nice before you go on TV.
situation: Jon is about to go on TV for an interview about his job.
intention: Jon wants to look slick.
moral_action: Jon goes to a professional hair stylist before, getting all fancied up.
moral_consequence: Jon has a great showing on TV and people take him seriously.
immoral_action: Jon tries out a new hairstyle, spiking it in some places.
