immoral_consequence: Jon looks ridiculous and folks make memes about him on twitter.

norm: You shouldn't waste water
situation: Skip got lost on a hike on a hot day and is trying to find his way back to civilization carrying nothing but a canteen.
intention: Skip wants to cool off.
moral_action: Skip finds a large tree that provides shade from the sun and sits under it for a while.
moral_consequence: Skip cools off and regains enough energy to catch a lizard to eat for protein.
immoral_action: Skip pours the water in his canteen all over his face and body and feels refreshed.
immoral_consequence: Skip becomes dehydrated when he can't find a source of water to fill his canteen and drink from.

norm: People should take good care of their pets.
situation: Alex realizes that she is out of food for her two cats but doesn't feel like going to the store.
intention: Alex has to decide whether to go buy cat food.
moral_action: Alex gets dressed and goes out to the store to buy some cat food.
moral_consequence: The cats eat and feel much better, and Alex feels like a good person.
immoral_action: Alex decides that the cats will be alright until the next day, since it had only been one day since they last ate.
immoral_consequence: The cats cry through the night from hunger, Alex feels guilty and the cats suffer.

norm: You shouldn't get involved romantically with your friend's partner.
situation: Jackson is hanging out with his best friend's girlfriend Lindsey when Lindsey starts flirting with him.
intention: Jackson doesn't want to hurt Lindsey.
moral_action: Jackson brings up  memories with his best friend and Lindsey while resting his hand on Lindsey's shoulder.
moral_consequence: Jackson is thanked by Lindsey who realizes that she lover her boyfriend.
immoral_action: Jackson flirts with Lindsey getting into a relationship with her.
immoral_consequence: Jackson loses his friendship when he best friend catches him with Lindsey.

norm: It's wrong to put things off until the last minute.
situation: Tim had a big exam next week that will determine if he will pass the class.
intention: Tim wants to study for the exam.
moral_action: Tim does plenty of studying the week before the exam in order to be ready.
moral_consequence: Tim aces the exam, and his teach congratulates him for doing so well.
immoral_action: Tim only studies for the exam an hour before the class starts.
immoral_consequence: Tim does poorly on the exam and ends up failing the class.

norm: It's brave to ask someone out.
situation: Keith was going to be going to the school dance the next week.
intention: Keith wanted a date to the dance.
moral_action: Keith gathers his courage and asks out a girl in his class to the dance.
moral_consequence: The girl says yes, and she and Keith go to the dance together.
immoral_action: Keith got his friend to ask a girl out to the dance for him.
immoral_consequence: The girl turned Keith down because he didn't ask her himself.

norm: It's wrong to lie to your girlfriend.
situation: Jim has remained friends with his all his exes even though his girlfriend Jessica doesn't like it.
intention: Jim wants to call an ex-girlfriend to see how she's doing.
moral_action: Jim calls his ex-girlfriend and when Jessica asks who he was talking to he tells her it was his ex-girlfriend.
moral_consequence: Jessica tells Jim that she appreciates his honesty, but he knows she doesn't like him being friends with his exes.
immoral_action: Jim calls his ex-girlfriend but when Jessica asks him who he was talking to, he says it was his mother.
immoral_consequence: Jessica doesn't believe him, and she asks to see his phone which causes an argument.

norm: You should help out customers if you work there.
situation: Tommy was working at a bookstore when a customer asks him where a certain book was.
intention: Tommy wants to answer the customer.
moral_action: Tommy tells the customer that he doesn't know, but he asks another worker, and they find out where the book is.
moral_consequence: The customer is grateful for Tommy's assistance and leaves him a small tip.
immoral_action: Tommy truthfully tells the customer that he doesn't know but doesn't try to find out where it is.
immoral_consequence: The customer is upset and reports Tommy's lack of assistance to his boss.

norm: It is not acceptable to forge your mother's writing.
situation: Oscar needs to pay some important bills, but doesn't have money.
intention: Oscar wants to get money to pay the bills.
moral_action: Oscar asks his mom for a short-term loan to pay the bills.
moral_consequence: Oscar's mom gives Oscar some money, to be paid back later.
immoral_action: Oscar gets his mom's check book and forges her signature to take money out of the bank.
immoral_consequence: Oscar's mom finds out and gets very angry at him.

norm: You should be generous towards your family.
situation: Al just cashed in a scratch ticket on which he won a significant amount of money.
intention: Al wants to spend his newfound money.
moral_action: Al uses the winnings to surprise his wife and kids by taking them on a long vacation.
moral_consequence: Al's wife is thrilled and touched by his thoughtfulness and generosity.
immoral_action: Al uses the money to buy himself a brand new motorcycle.
immoral_consequence: Al's wife is offended that he didn't share the winnings with her and their relationship deteriorates.

norm: It's wrong to harm your mother.
situation: Jessie lives with her mom, Mary, who often opens Jessie's packages without permission.
intention: Jessie wants to confront her mom about opening her packages.
moral_action: Jessie kindly asks Mary to stop opening her packages and threatens to move out if she continues.
moral_consequence: Afraid to lose her daughter, Mary leaves Jessie's packages alone.
immoral_action: Jessie catches Mary with one of her packages and pushes her.
immoral_consequence: Mary falls to the floor and injures her back.

norm: It's nice to put in hard work.
situation: Ted has moved into a new house which has a large backyard.
intention: Ted wants to do something with his backyard.
moral_action: Ted digs out the yard and puts in many plants and grass.
moral_consequence: Ted will have an impressive yard.
immoral_action: Ted does a simple scattering of small stones over his yard.
immoral_consequence: Ted will have an unimpressive backyard.

norm: You shouldn't touch someone's hair without their permission.
situation: Kate's coworker Jill just got dreadlocks and Kate has never seen them in person before.
intention: Kate wants to see what the dreadlocks feel like.
moral_action: Kate asks Jill if it's ok if she touches her hair since she's never felt dreadlocks before.
moral_consequence: Jill is flattered by Kate's interest in her new hairstyle and gives her permission to touch them.
immoral_action: Kate reaches out and touches Jill's dreadlocks, exclaiming how beautiful they are.
immoral_consequence: Jill steps back and while thanking Kate for her compliment, asks her to respect her personal space.

norm: It's frowned upon to have mixed gender sleepovers.
situation: Olivia is about to turn 12 years old and her mom is asking her what kind of party she wants.
intention: Olivia wants to have a slumber party.
moral_action: Olivia invites all of the girls in her class to her slumber party.
moral_consequence: The other parents are happy that their children have fun at the party.
immoral_action: Olivia invites all of the boys and girls in her class to her slumber party.
immoral_consequence: The other parents are shocked when they realize that boys and girls will be sleeping together.

norm: It’s good to play games with family.
situation: Caius comes home on a Friday night, and his kids are sitting in the living room playing with toys.
intention: Caius wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Caius plays an educational game with his kids and their toys.
moral_consequence: His kids' grades improve.
immoral_action: Caius decides to watch movies on Netflix with his friends.
immoral_consequence: Caius kids miss spending time with their father.

norm: It's unusual to like single ply toilet paper.
situation: Karen and Larry are shopping at the store for toiletries when they come to the toilet paper section.
intention: Karen wants to pick a toilet paper to buy.
moral_action: Karen grabs the two ply toilet paper even though it's the more expensive choice.
moral_consequence: Larry is happy that Karen has such high standards and that he can comfortably go to the bathroom.
immoral_action: Karen grabs the single ply toilet paper because it's by far the cheaper option.
immoral_consequence: Larry is disgusted that Karen has no standards and that she would be willing to risk paper tearing to save pennies.

norm: It's bad to try and get sick
situation: John has a big math test at school the next day for which he is unprepared.
intention: John wants to get out of going to school, so he can skip the test.
moral_action: John pretends to be sick.
moral_consequence: John stays home from school and doesn't have to take the test.
immoral_action: John licks all the surfaces in the boy's bathroom in order to get sick.
immoral_consequence: John gets sick and feels ill for several days.

norm: It's good to catch up with old friends.
situation: Tom is on his way to the post office when he bumps into an old friend.
intention: Tom wants to send a package off in time.
moral_action: Tom offers for his friend to accompany him as he runs the errand.
moral_consequence: Tom's friend is glad to be able to spend some time with him.
immoral_action: Tom greets his friend quickly and hurries off the the post office.
immoral_consequence: Tom's friend wishes that they would have stopped to catch up.

norm: It's wrong to shoot things at others.
situation: Jacob plays with his new BB gun.
intention: Jacob wants to find interesting targets to shoot at.
moral_action: Jacob finds an empty ravine nearby and fires there once he verifies that no one is around.
moral_consequence: Jacob becomes good at shooting the BB gun while everyone keeps safe.
immoral_action: Jacob points the gun at the street where people are walking and fires.
immoral_consequence: A neighbor is hit, injured and sues Jacob's family as a result.

norm: It's wrong to take your child's medication.
situation: Kaito is having problems concentrating on work when he notices his son's adderall sitting on the table.
intention: Kaito wants to finish his work.
moral_action: Kaito drinks two cups of his favorite coffee before he continues working.
moral_consequence: Kaito finishes all of his work by the end of the night.
immoral_action: Kaito takes a pill of his son's adderall without asking his son.
immoral_consequence: Kaito gets a headache from the medication.

norm: It is wrong to bully online.
situation: Stephen's iMac was damaged by his friend who dropped it by accident.
intention: Stephen wants his friend to answer for the damage.
moral_action: Stephen asks his friend to cover the costs of the necessary repairs.
moral_consequence: His friend agrees to pay for the damage in order to fix the iMac.
immoral_action: Stephen insults and threatens his friend in a chat group for his damage.
immoral_consequence: His friend feels intimidated and complains to the moderator who decides to delete Stephen's account.

norm: It's bad to waste food that is just slightly burnt.
situation: Nancy is preparing for a banquet when she realizes that some bread she put in the oven has burnt edges.
intention: Nancy wants to serve good-looking food.
moral_action: Nancy cuts off the burnt parts of the bread and serves it.
moral_consequence: The bread is delicious and the guests hardly notice the cut-off sections.
immoral_action: Nancy throws the batch of bread away and starts a new batch.
immoral_consequence: The food is ready 20 minutes late and the guests grumble because they must wait.

norm: You shouldn't be pushy with people with medical conditions.
situation: Gayle is a supervisor and wants to reward her sales reps for exceeding their monthly quotas.
intention: Gayle wants to give her employees a free lunch buffet.
moral_action: Gayle provides a free lunch and extra time so that her disabled sales rep has ample time to get their food and eat.
moral_consequence: The sales rep feel appreciated and continue to work extra hard, leading to exceeding the next month's quota.
immoral_action: Gayle orders a large lunch buffet for her sales rep during their 30 minute lunch, but rudely rushes a handicapped sales rep through the line.
immoral_consequence: The sales rep become angry towards Gayle for her treatment of their medically disabled coworker and become less efficient in sales.

norm: It's rude to skip a friend's birthday celebration.
situation: Layne gets asked out on a date by her longtime crush Evan, on the same night of her friend Tori's birthday bash.
intention: Layne wants to hang out with Evan.
moral_action: Layne invites Evan to Tori's birthday party.
moral_consequence: Tori is happy for Layne, and they all have a great time.
immoral_action: Layne goes on the date with Evan, skipping Tori's party.
immoral_consequence: Tori is hurt that Layne chose a guy over her on her birthday.

norm: It's bad to disobey the rules of the road.
situation: Kate is driving to the store and notices there is heavy traffic on the freeway.
intention: Kate wants to get to the store quickly.
moral_action: Kate looks for alternate faster routes on her GPS.
moral_consequence: Kate finds a faster route on the GPS.
immoral_action: Kate pulls onto the shoulder of the freeway to try to bypass the traffic.
immoral_consequence: Kate gets pulled over and given a ticket by the police.

norm: You're expected to let your parents come visit with you.
situation: Roger is watching TV at home one afternoon when his parents call saying that they're in town and would like to stop by to visit.
intention: Roger wants to answer his parent's request.
moral_action: Roger invites his parents to come over to his home for a visit.
moral_consequence: Roger's parents are thrilled and enjoy the opportunity to visit their son.
immoral_action: Roger tells his parents that he is busy, and they will have to stop by another time.
immoral_consequence: Roger's parents are sad and disappointed that they won't get to visit with their son.

norm: It's good to help a disabled person.
situation: George is on his way to work and sees a disabled man struggling to move his wheelchair over the curb to cross the street.
intention: George wants to decide whether to stop and help the man or continue on his way.
moral_action: George goes over and helps the disabled man into the crosswalk.
moral_consequence: The disabled man is very thankful and is able to cross the street and get where he's going.
immoral_action: George acts like he doesn't notice the disabled man and keeps on walking to work.
immoral_consequence: The disabled man turns back because he is unable to get over the curb to cross the street.

norm: It's not good to leave your friends behind.
situation: Hannah is hiking to a waterfalls with her friend Stephanie, who is out of shape.
intention: Hannah wants to reach the waterfalls.
moral_action: Hannah and Stephanie walk the trail together, taking many breaks and many pictures together.
moral_consequence: Stephanie and Hannah have a fun time together on their hike and plan other trips together.
immoral_action: Hannah tells Stephanie she will be going ahead because Stephanie walks too slow.
immoral_consequence: Stephanie is hurt by what Hannah said, and Stephanie refuses to go with Hannah on other hikes.

norm: You shouldn't pry your nose into your child's love life.
situation: Sola's son has been hanging around a friend a lot, and she wonders if their are feelings involved.
intention: Sola wants to ask her son about his feelings towards a friend.
moral_action: Sola gently asks her son about this friend, and when he doesn't appear comfortable she reassures him that she'll let it go.
moral_consequence: Sola's son begins to trust her and Sola is happier.
immoral_action: Sola brings it up at breakfast and keeps asking little questions about it, even though her son is not responding directly.
immoral_consequence: Sola's son gets angry at her for being nosy abd their relationship becomes strained.

norm: It is rude to lie to somebody.
situation: David is an art teacher and his student Andy draws a picture that is lacking in technique.
intention: David wants to critique Andy's drawing.
moral_action: David points out the technique flaws in Andy's drawing and how to fix them.
moral_consequence: And will develop as an artist that has better technique.
immoral_action: David says that Andy's drawing is good and Andy doesn't need any tips.
immoral_consequence: Andy will not develop as an artist.

norm: It's good to help out helpless animals.
situation: Molly is driving home from class and sees an injured kitten on the side of the road.
intention: Molly wants to do something about the injured kitten.
moral_action: Molly decides to take the kitten to the vet to see if it can be saved.
moral_consequence: The vet saves the kitten's life and Molly adopts it as a new pet.
immoral_action: Molly decides to hit the kitten with her car and kill it.
immoral_consequence: The kitten is killed instantly and Molly ends up feeling guilty for a long time.

norm: Informing relative on the truth is always a good thing.
situation: Jay is out at a store, and sees his brother Todd's girlfriend making out with another man.
intention: Jay wants to respond to seeing his brother's girlfriend cheating.
moral_action: Jay takes a picture and shows Todd what he saw.
moral_consequence: Todd gets very angry and breaks up with his girlfriend right away, and soon finds a better person to date.
immoral_action: Jay keeps the information about Todd's girlfriend to himself.
immoral_consequence: Todd wastes his time dating his cheating girlfriend for a long time before being unexpectedly dumped.

norm: It's frustrating when someone cancels dinner at the last minute.
situation: Samantha is planning a huge dinner celebration for her recent retirement, and she invited Rudy to it.
intention: Rudy needs to cancel showing up because of a work engagement that same day.
moral_action: Rudy tells Sam the moment he receives the invitation that he has a work obligation and HAS to go.
moral_consequence: Samantha understands, she's hurt but doesn't think less of Rudy for it.
immoral_action: Rudy calls Samantha the day of and fake coughs into the phone saying he's ill and can't make it, because he's afraid to tell her the truth.
immoral_consequence: Samantha doesn't believe Rudy and is hurt that her friend would lie to her.

norm: It is rude to pressure a woman into buying something.
situation: Roger is a vacuum salesman who has been invited into the home of a woman named Martha.
intention: Roger wants to sell Martha a vacuum.
moral_action: Roger tells Martha about all the features and advantages of the vacuum as well as its limited time sale price.
moral_consequence: Martha is enticed by Roger's sales pitch and agrees to purchase a vacuum.
immoral_action: Roger uses forceful sales tactics and guilt to pressure Martha to buy a vacuum.
immoral_consequence: Martha is irritated by Roger's aggressive behavior and asks him to leave her home.

norm: It is kind to care for animals.
situation: Sue sees a stray gray cat outside.
intention: Sue wants to do something about the cat getting in the gardens.
moral_action: Sue leaves a food dish out and eventually takes the cat in as the pet.
moral_consequence: Sue now has a pet cat which she loves for years.
immoral_action: Sue barricades the garden and chases the stray away when it visits.
immoral_consequence: THe stray becomes feral and has kittens resulting in many stray cats in the area.

norm: It's not okay to do things that are unhygienic.
situation: Gloria just finished planting some flowers in her garden with her bare hands when her husband lets her know that he made her a sandwich for lunch.
intention: Gloria wants to eat the sandwich for lunch.
moral_action: Gloria goes to the bathroom and washes up before sitting down to eat her sandwich.
moral_consequence: Gloria enjoys the sandwich and feels full and satisfied for the rest of the afternoon.
immoral_action: Gloria goes into the kitchen and immediately starts eating the sandwich with her hands without washing up first.
immoral_consequence: Gloria gets a stomach ache a few hours later because she ingested some bacteria that were in the dirt.

norm: It's wrong to steal things from people.
situation: Tony got fired from his job and is behind on rent.
intention: Tony wants to be able to pay his rent, so he doesn't end up homeless.
moral_action: Tony asks his neighbor for help with his rent.
moral_consequence: Tony's neighbor helps pay his rent giving him time to get a new job, they also become closer and become good friends.
immoral_action: Tony breaks into his neighbors house because he knows they have cash hidden under their bed.
immoral_consequence: Tony's neighbor catches him breaking in and shoots him killing him.

norm: It's wrong to hog the bed.
situation: Steve is a large man who sleeps in the same bed as his wife Jill every night.
intention: Steve wants to be comfortable in bed.
moral_action: Steve finds a comfortable sleeping position that allows enough room for him and his wife.
moral_consequence: Steve and Jill sleep through the night without any issues.
immoral_action: Steve sprawls his entire body across the bed.
immoral_consequence: Jill is left with such little room that she falls off the bed in the middle of the night.

norm: It is irresponsible to neglect paying your fees.
situation: Steve had been parking his car illegally and found a ticket on his car.
intention: Steve wants to keep his car from getting towed.
moral_action: Steve went to the city hall and paid off the fine for the ticket that he got.
moral_consequence: Steve got the ticket and fine off of his driving record.
immoral_action: Steve left the parking ticket on the window so the meter maids would think he had already been ticketed that day.
immoral_consequence: Eventually, Steve was cited for not paying the original ticket on the car.

norm: You should be understanding when your parents are grieving.
situation: Joe's grandparents passed away which has made his family sad.
intention: Joe wants to talk with his parents about his grandparents.
moral_action: Joe mentions how he enjoyed his grandparent's cooking.
moral_consequence: Joe's parents will think he is kind and had a strong bond with his grandparents.
immoral_action: Joe mentions how he thought his grandparents smelled odd.
immoral_consequence: Joe's parents will think he is rude and crass.

norm: You should look your best for important events.
situation: Susan is invited to her friend's wedding.
intention: Susan wants to support her friend on a special day.
moral_action: Susan picks out a beautiful outfit to wear to the wedding.
moral_consequence: Susan takes many group pictures with her friend and makes good memories of a special day.
immoral_action: Susan shows up to the wedding hung over in clothes from the night before.
immoral_consequence: Susan's friend is hurt and says she ruined her special day.

norm: You shouldn't tell on others.
situation: Jack sees his coworker take supplies from the workplace which is not allowed.
intention: Jack wants his coworker to return the supplies to the workplace.
moral_action: Jack talks to the coworker privately and tells them that they should return the items.
moral_consequence: Jack's coworker returns the items but does not get in trouble for taking them.
immoral_action: Jack tells the supervisor that the coworker has taken things from the workplace.
immoral_consequence: Jack's coworker is forced to return the items and is then fired.

norm: It is important to own up to your mistakes.
situation: Jacob accidentally scratched his Mom's car while parking at the neighborhood store around the corner from their house.
intention: Jacob wants to tell his Mom her car is damaged.
moral_action: Jacob tells his mom what happened  to the car and promises to work to pay for the damages.
moral_consequence: Jacob's Mom is proud that Jacob took responsibility for what happened and tells him her insurance will cover the damages.
immoral_action: Jacob tells his Mom that the car was scratched when he was in the store, but he did not know by who.
immoral_consequence: A neighbor casually mentions he saw Jacob scratch the car making Jacob's Mom disappointed in him for lying.

norm: Avoiding someone just because they're sad makes you appear shallow.
situation: Philip's best friend just lost his job and feels miserable, so he asked Philip if he wanted to hang out on Saturday evening.
intention: Philip wants to have a pleasant Saturday evening.
moral_action: Philip spends the evening with his best friend - they play video games, drink beer and have a great time.
moral_consequence: Philip's best friend feels comforted that Philip is there for him.
immoral_action: Philip decides to hang out with other friends instead in order to avoid his best friend's depressing mood.
immoral_consequence: Philip's best friend feels like Philip is superficial and is letting him down.

norm: It's rude not to share with a sibling.
situation: Jane, who lives with her family, has just brought home a large order of chili fries which her sister wants to eat with her.
intention: Jane wants to eat enough to feel satiated.
moral_action: Jane gives her sister a small portion making sure to leave most of it for herself.
moral_consequence: Jane's sister enjoys eating the fries and is happy with the amount she's given.
immoral_action: Jane refuses to give her sister any of the fries because she is hungry.
immoral_consequence: Jane's sister thinks she is being greedy over her surplus of food.

norm: You shouldn't lie in front of your friends.
situation: Fred is with his friends at a party and the group are talking about cars.
intention: Fred wants to his friends to think he is handy.
moral_action: Fred tells his friends that he is planning to do a few DIY maintenance tasks on his car soon.
moral_consequence: One of Fred's friends asks to do one of these tasks together and two look up information online and spend all weekend working on their cars together.
immoral_action: Fred tells his friends that he re-did the brakes on his car last week when he actually knows nothing about car brake systems.
immoral_consequence: One of Fred's friends asks him to help re-do his brakes soon and Fred has to make up an excuse on the fly.

norm: You shouldn't hurt others by judging them too harshly.
situation: Daniel's son has come home from school and got a B on a paper.
intention: Daniel wants to talk to his son about the grade.
moral_action: Daniel tells his son that a B is good, and he can aim for an A on the next paper.
moral_consequence: Daniel's son will want to achieve an A.
immoral_action: Daniel tells his son that a B is a bad grade and people that get Bs are bottom tier.
immoral_consequence: Daniel's son will feel that he isn't worth much.

norm: It's unreasonable to routinely sacrifice yourself for others.
situation: Aaron is tired after spending a week helping his coworkers after work, and he coworkers want him to stay longer tonight.
intention: Aaron doesn't want to let anyone down.
moral_action: Aaron asks one of his friends if they could help out his coworkers for the night.
moral_consequence: Aaron is able to spend a relaxing at home.
immoral_action: Aaron stays after work to help his coworkers.
immoral_consequence: Aaron passes out while working from exhaustion.

norm: It's good to be grateful for people's kindness.
situation: Judy was walking inside a mall, and a man held open a door for her.
intention: Judy wanted to say something to the man.
moral_action: Judy grins at the man and thanks him for holding the door.
moral_consequence: The man feels good for doing something that made Judy smile.
immoral_action: Judy told the man that she can open her own door.
immoral_consequence: The man feels bad and feels guilty for thinking he would make Judy happy.

norm: It's considered rude and unkind to exclude family members.
situation: Jake invites his sister Maggie to hang out with his friends for the night.
intention: Jake wants to entertain his friends.
moral_action: Jake shows his friends Maggie's favorite movie.
moral_consequence: Maggie bonds with Jake's friends.
immoral_action: Jake starts a game of Smash Brothers handing a controller to everyone but Maggie.
immoral_consequence: Maggie sits around awkwardly before leaving the room.

norm: You shouldn't vomit on someone's clothes.
situation: Dante is out with a friend and is feeling a stomach ache from a bad oyster.
intention: Dante wants to regurgitate his bad food.
moral_action: Dante regurgitates his food in the bathroom of the restaurant.
moral_consequence: Dante will be relieved that his friend did not see him regurgitate.
immoral_action: Dante regurgitates his food on his friend's jacket.
immoral_consequence: Dante will be embarrassed and owe his friend a new jacket.

norm: It's encouraged to look out for your family members.
situation: James was at the public pool with his little brother and his friends.
intention: James wanted to swim.
moral_action: James played in the pool with his friends on the shallow side of the pool where his brother was.
moral_consequence: James, his little brother, and James' friends all had a great time playing at the pool.
immoral_action: James swam in the pool with his friends, ignoring his brother altogether.
immoral_consequence: James' little brother went under the water and almost drowned in the pool.

norm: It is good to use email instead of wasting paper.
situation: Frank needed to send messages to his coworkers.
intention: Frank needs to get the messages to the coworkers.
moral_action: Frank would send his coworkers the messages by email to save on the paper.
moral_consequence: Frank also got messages to them so much faster via the email.
immoral_action: Frank would write down the messages on pieces of paper and hand them to the coworker in person.
immoral_consequence: Frank consistently took longer than everyone else to send messages.

norm: It's bad to think your dad went nuts.
situation: Jimmy has noticed that his dad is exhibiting strange behavior lately.
intention: Jimmy wants to keep an eye out for his dad.
moral_action: Jimmy watches his dad to make sure the behavior continues and when it does he approaches him.
moral_consequence: Jimmy's dad is able to get something that is weighing on him off his chest.
immoral_action: Jimmy keeps observing his dad's behavior and just thinks he is slowly losing his mind.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy's dad has to cope with whatever is going on alone.

norm: You shouldn't interuppt others.
situation: Ellie's mother was on the phone when her friend asked her if she could sleep over.
intention: Ellie wants to ask her mother if she could sleep over at her friend's house.
moral_action: Ellie waits until her friend gets off the phone to ask her if she can go.
moral_consequence: Ellie's mother decides that she has behaved enough to go to her friend's house.
immoral_action: Ellie tugs at her mother's shirt and calls her name until she gets her attention.
immoral_consequence: Ellie's mother is annoyed and doesn't let her go sleep over at her friend's house.

norm: It's good to stick up for your friend.
situation: Brandon is sitting and having lunch with the new friend he met in class today when his friends approach them and start making jokes about the new kid.
intention: Brandon wants to respond to his friends.
moral_action: Brandon tells his friends to take it easy with the ribbing and introduces them to the new student.
moral_consequence: The new student is happy to meet them and feels good about his first day of school.
immoral_action: Brandon meets his friend's jokes with more jokes of his own about the new kid.
immoral_consequence: The new student begins to feel bullied and leaves the group feeling upset.

norm: You shouldn't sell your body to people.
situation: Jane just got fired from her job and doesn't know how she will make ends meet.
intention: Jane wants to earn some money quickly.
moral_action: Jane takes on some temporary gig work in order to make ends meet.
moral_consequence: Jane feels empowered because she has overcome a tough situation.
immoral_action: Jane decides to sell pictures of herself on the internet for money.
immoral_consequence: Jane feels a lack of self worth because of what she did.

norm: It's wrong to talk about sex with minors.
situation: Mike spends every saturday with his nephews and nieces for dinner.
intention: Mike wants to appear fun and entertaining to the kids.
moral_action: Mike tells funny age appropriate jokes and plays board games with the kids.
moral_consequence: Mike is loved by the kids and is still friends with them to this day.
immoral_action: Mike cracks graphic jokes and makes sexual comments to the kids.
immoral_consequence: The kids feels uncomfortable and tell the parents who stop inviting Mike over.

norm: You shouldn't hit dead animals.
situation: Troy is walking on the trail when he sees a dead possum on the path.
intention: Troy wants to pass by the dead body of the possum.
moral_action: Troy walks around the dead animal making sure to stay away from it.
moral_consequence: Troy has a great walk after he gets past the dead possum.
immoral_action: Troy walks over the dead animal, stepping on it when he crosses it.
immoral_consequence: The bloated animal explodes and spews bodily fluid all over Troy.

norm: It is wrong to recruit minors into a gang.
situation: Bruce started a gang with guys in his neighborhood and a lot of teenagers want to join it.
intention: Bruce wants to take care of the teenagers.
moral_action: Bruce disallows the teenagers from joining the gang so that they focus on their education.
moral_consequence: The teenagers get educated and lose their interest in joining the gang.
immoral_action: Bruce allows the teenagers into the gang so that they can be protected.
immoral_consequence: The teenagers never get their education and spend time in and out of jail.

norm: Kids should not smoke cigarettes.
situation: Bob has two pre-teenage children, a boy and a girl.
intention: Bob wants his children to learn to assume responsibility for their actions and make their own decisions.
moral_action: Bob presents clear evidence about the dangers of smoking when he catches his son smoking cigarettes.
moral_consequence: Bob's son examines the evidence and agrees that smoking is not smart and decides to quit.
immoral_action: Bob says nothing when he catches his son smoking cigarettes.
immoral_consequence: Bob's son continues to smoke and admits it's his own fault when he suffers lung damage.

norm: Yelling at your employees is a poor management style.
situation: Andy is a manager and one of his subordinates just made a huge mistake at work.
intention: Andy wants to make sure this kind of mistake never happens again.
moral_action: Andy gives the employee a warning making it clear there will be only one.
moral_consequence: Andy's subordinate learns to be more careful in his work.
immoral_action: Andy raises his voice to a shouting level at his subordinate when discussing the problem.
immoral_consequence: The employee feels distressed and that he is in a hostile workplace.

norm: It's healthy to express yourself and your sense of style.
situation: Cara's mother always told her that an elegant woman wears discreet, reasonable clothes.
intention: Cara wants people to admire her style.
moral_action: Cara decides to wear clothes she really likes, which are beautiful and original.
moral_consequence: Cara feels vibrant and happy.
immoral_action: Cara wears the clothes her mother taught her to choose, which are elegant but which she does not really like.
immoral_consequence: Cara feels drab and uninteresting.

norm: It's not okay to abuse drugs for what ever reason.
situation: Jane's doctor prescribes Jane some Valium to use sparingly in times of stress.
intention: Jane wants to take some Valium to relax around her child.
moral_action: Jane decides to take the recommended dose of Valium and does not abuse the drug around her children.
moral_consequence: Jane's children are glad that she is not stressed, and they play with her.
immoral_action: Jane decides to take triple the dose of Valium recommended to her to deal with her children.
immoral_consequence: Jane feels woozy and passes out while her children run wild.

norm: It is uncouth to defecate in public.
situation: Barry is walking down the street when he gets an urgent need to defecate.
intention: Barry needs to find somewhere to go to the bathroom.
moral_action: Barry decides to clench his cheeks and waddle into the nearest store and use their toilet.
moral_consequence: The people on the street aren't subjected to any of Barry's waste or odors.
immoral_action: Barry decides that he can't risk finding a real bathroom and goes right there on the street.
immoral_consequence: The people on the street are utterly disgusted as they all scatter and run away.

norm: You shouldn't make people angry.
situation: Tom, a racist man, is driving with some friends when he sees a car with some ethnic minorities in it.
intention: Tom wants the ethnic minorities to stay away from him.
moral_action: Tom intentionally slows down to let the other car speed ahead of him.
moral_consequence: Tom avoids all trouble with the car full of people that he dislikes.
immoral_action: Tom rolls down his window and tells the people not to come near his car or else he'll get out and fight them.
immoral_consequence: The people get angry, take Tom up on his offer, get out of their car, and surround Tom's car menacingly.

norm: You shouldn't be so pessimistic about your life.
situation: Jay lost his job and is at home alone, thinking about what to do next.
intention: Jay wants to decide what to do over the weekend.
moral_action: Jay takes a night off then applies for work on Sunday.
moral_consequence: He recovers and keeps focus on the future.
immoral_action: Jay chooses to stay home and drink.
immoral_consequence: He beats up on himself and damages his ego.

norm: You shouldn't put up with children that lie to you.
situation: Kayla has a child who has not completed his homework but claims that he did.
intention: Kayla wants to have a peaceful day at home.
moral_action: Kayla is firm with her kid and puts him on time out until the homework is done.
moral_consequence: Kayla's kid understands that there will be consequences for his actions.
immoral_action: Kayla decides to let it go and not deal with it, so she can take it easy.
immoral_consequence: Kayla's kid is now encouraged not to tell the truth when it's advantageous.

norm: You shouldn't make fun of someone's face.
situation: James is having lunch in the break room at work when he notices a new employee with a cleft lip walking in.
intention: James wants to introduce himself to the new employee.
moral_action: James walks over to greet the new employee and starts up a conversation without acknowledging his facial features.
moral_consequence: James and the new employee hit it off and look forward to working together.
immoral_action: James walks over to greet the new employee, then begins mocking his cleft lip.
immoral_consequence: Fearing that James' action would be indicative of the work environment, the new employee ends up quitting on his first day.

norm: It's good to make food for other people.
situation: Jason's friend is at Jason's house when Jason starts feeling a little hungry.
intention: Jason wants to make a sandwich.
moral_action: Jason makes a sandwich for himself and one for his friend who's visiting as well.
moral_consequence: Jason's friend is grateful that Jason was thoughtful enough to make them a sandwich.
immoral_action: Jason makes a sandwich for himself but not for his friend.
immoral_consequence: Jason's friend feels that Jason is very thoughtless for not offering to make them a sandwich too.

norm: You should invite your partner to your family's events.
situation: Julie's mother is planning a dinner and asks Julie if she will come and if she'll bring her husband, Ralph.
intention: Julie wants to answer her mother's question.
moral_action: Julie tells her mother that of course, both her and her husband will be there.
moral_consequence: Julie's mother is delighted that Julie will be attending and is also glad to see her husband soon.
immoral_action: Julie tells her mother that she will come, but she will not invite Ralph because she just doesn't want to.
immoral_consequence: Julie's mother is shocked that Julie does things without her husband and wouldn't invite him to see family.

norm: Taking things that don't belong to you is wrong.
situation: Gabe is walking through his neighborhood and notices a house with many items laying in the yard.
intention: Gabe wants to possess one of the items.
moral_action: Gabe rings the doorbell of the home the item is in front of and makes an offer to buy it from the homeowner.
moral_consequence: The homeowner agrees to sell it to Gabe and Gabe goes home happy with the item.
immoral_action: Gabe casually picks up the item he likes and walks home with it hoping that nobody saw him.
immoral_consequence: Gabe is eventually caught by the police for his theft and arrested.

norm: You shouldn't marry someone you never met.
situation: Glenda is walking down the street when she is approached by a stranger, Clark, who proposes marriage to her.
intention: Glenda wants to answer the marriage proposal.
moral_action: Glenda tells Clark that he needs to ask her out on a date first, and then they'll see.
moral_consequence: Glenda learns that Clark is really not her type and decides to not go any further.
immoral_action: Glenda tells Clark that he is ruggedly handsome so of course she accepts the marriage proposal.
immoral_consequence: Glenda and Clark get married first and find out they're totally incompatible second and thus have an awful life.

norm: It's inappropriate to make a mess of a friend's house.
situation: Bob is throwing a party at a house which belongs to a friend.
intention: Bob wants everyone to have a good time.
moral_action: Bob throws a nice party and leaves the house spotless when it's over.
moral_consequence: Bob's friend is happy because the house is even cleaner than it was before.
immoral_action: Bob parties heavily and leaves a huge mess afterward.
immoral_consequence: Bob's friend is upset because the house was trashed.

norm: It's good to train your pets.
situation: Claire adopted a new dog who gets stressed around people, and she has some friends who want to come meet the new dog.
intention: Claire wants to let her friends play with her new dog.
moral_action: Claire tells her friends to come visit next weekend after she has time to take the dog to a class and socialize it a bit.
moral_consequence: The dog improves throughout the week and behaves well when her friends come over to visit.
immoral_action: Claire invites her friends over that afternoon and lets them crowd around and pet the dog.
immoral_consequence: The dog starts to panic and bites one of her friends, and the friend is nervous around the dog from then on.

norm: You should answer the phone when your parents call.
situation: Sally is really busy at home doing a bunch of housework and her phone rings with the caller ID showing it is her parents.
intention: Sally wants to finish her housework.
moral_action: Sally knows that her parents could be calling about something important, so she picks up the phone while continuing her house work with her free hand.
moral_consequence: Sally's parents inform her about something that is extremely important and Sally is glad she answered.
immoral_action: Sally decides to ignore the call from her parents as to not interrupt the housework she is doing.
immoral_consequence: Sally misses important, time sensitive, family news that her parents were trying to contact her about.

norm: It’s rude to not return a call.
situation: John is in a movie theater when Lucy leaves him a voicemail and tells him that the call is really urgent.
intention: John wants to finish watching the movie.
moral_action: John returns Lucy's call, meets her to help her, and returns to see the movie another day.
moral_consequence: Lucy is really appreciative of John's assistance with her problem and pays for his movie tickets.
immoral_action: John ignores the voicemail on his phone after listening to it, sits back down, and enjoys his film.
immoral_consequence: Lucy feels let down, angry, and has significant difficulty without John returning her call.

norm: You should attend events you are invited to.
situation: Greg has been playing a great video game all day when he realizes his friend Bill's birthday party is coming up that evening.
intention: Greg wants to enjoy his night.
moral_action: Greg stops playing video games and goes to attend Bill's birthday party.
moral_consequence: Bill is happy to see Greg, and they both have a great time.
immoral_action: Greg decides to continue playing video games and skip the birthday party.
immoral_consequence: Bill is hurt that Greg didn't come and their relationship is damaged.

norm: You should be fair when tipping a server
situation: Carl is on a first date where their server is just out of training and messes up their dinner order.
intention: Carl wants to show his date the kind of person he is when paying the bill.
moral_action: Carl is sympathetic to the server's jitters and leaves a generous tip.
moral_consequence: His date excitedly makes plans for another date.
immoral_action: Carl leaves a small tip to show he doesn't tolerate poor performance.
immoral_consequence: His date does not return his calls later in the week.

norm: It is wrong to falsify experimentation evidence.
situation: Victor is a scientist who has been doing experimentation on some viruses.
intention: Victor needs to publish a paper about his findings.
moral_action: Victor is honest about his findings and warns people about the dangers of the virus.
moral_consequence: Many people avoid getting sick because they take precautions not to catch the virus.
immoral_action: Victor underplays the danger of the virus in order to make his findings sound less alarmist.
immoral_consequence: Many people are infected with the virus and become ill.

norm: It’s wrong to cheat.
situation: Greg has an important math test the next day in school that he isn't well prepared for.
intention: Greg wants to get a good grade on the test.
moral_action: Greg studies hard late into the evening and goes into the test well prepared.
moral_consequence: Greg gets an A+ on the test and is very proud.
immoral_action: Greg writes unauthorized crib notes on a small sheet of paper which he uses during the test.
immoral_consequence: Greg is caught cheating by the teacher and given a failing grade.

norm: Never complain about getting things for free.
situation: Carolina notices that she's received a plain free outfit in her dress up mobile game.
intention: Carolina wants to express herself.
moral_action: Carolina uses her creativity to make several outfits in the game uploading them to the game's server.
moral_consequence: Carolina gains new follwers in the game for her creative efforts.
immoral_action: On a forum Carolina makes a post saying that she's disappointed that her free gift isn't like the expensive paid outfits.
immoral_consequence: Carolina is called out by the other people in the forum for being ungrateful.

norm: It's wrong to be involved in organized crime.
situation: John is in his usual Brooklyn hangout when some known Mafioso come in and ask John if he's willing to help them out with a task.
intention: John wants to respond to the mafioso.
moral_action: John tells the mafioso that he respects him, but he cannot involve himself in such activities.
moral_consequence: John is allowed to continue his day and continues his crime free life  living happily.
immoral_action: John tells the mafioso that he'd be glad to do a task as he's sure the mafia will repay him bigtime later.
immoral_consequence: john slowly becomes a criminal over crime doing worse and worse crimes until he goes to prison.

norm: You shouldn't bust your parent's things.
situation: James wanted to go to a heavy metal concert, but his parents said he was grounded for poor grades.
intention: James wants to attend the concert.
moral_action: James agreed to his parents' faces, then snuck out his bedroom window at night.
moral_consequence: James got to go to the concert and made it back home before his parents realized he was gone.
immoral_action: James got a baseball bat, smashed the living room TV, and threatened to destroy the house if he wasn't allowed to go to concert.
immoral_consequence: James' parents let him leave, but when he came home later that night they locked him out of the house.

norm: It's bad to steal from others.
situation: Dan is at the park and sees a really cool skateboard.
intention: Dan wants the skateboard.
moral_action: Dan approaches the owner of the skateboard and asks them where they got it.
moral_consequence: Dan goes home and orders the same skateboard which he waits for eagerly.
immoral_action: Dan pushes the owner off the skateboard and grabs it, running away.
immoral_consequence: Dan is arrested for stealing.

norm: Cheating is frowned upon.
situation: Jon is taking an exam in his math class this is worth 50% of his final grade.
intention: Jon really wants to pass.
moral_action: Jon studies hard and tries his best on the exam.
moral_consequence: Jon does not ace the test, but does well enough to pass.
immoral_action: Jon copies the answers of the smart kid that sits right in front of him.
immoral_consequence: Jon gets caught and he automatically fails the exam.

norm: It is wrong to sell something that is stolen.
situation: Mike is in possession of a watch that he knows is stolen.
intention: Mike wants to get rid of the watch.
moral_action: Mike brings the watch to the police station to turn it in.
moral_consequence: Mike is given a reward for the return of the missing property.
immoral_action: Mike brings the watch to the pawn shop and tries to sell it.
immoral_consequence: Mike is arrested when the watch is tracked down to its legal owner.

norm: It's rude to litter other people's yards.
situation: Before heading to work Jill takes her dog for a walk around the neighborhood.
intention: Jill wants to make sure her dog poops before she leaves.
moral_action: Jill makes sure she picks up the poop her dog leaves on her neighbors yard.
moral_consequence: Jill avoids antagonizing her neighbors.
immoral_action: Jill lets her dog poop on a neighbors yard and fails to scoop it up.
immoral_consequence: Jill gets in trouble with the neighborhood's association.

norm: It's wrong to lie about things you've done.
situation: Larry saw on a jobs posting that a regional manager position was opening up in his department in another state.
intention: Larry wants to get the new regional manager job.
moral_action: Larry admits that he doesn't have an MBA, but points out his years of experience at the company.
moral_consequence: Larry doesn't get the job but the company offers him a scholarship to an MBA program, so he can eventually be qualified for it.
immoral_action: Larry falsely states in the application that he has the MBA required for the position.
immoral_consequence: Larry is found out for having lied about his education, and he is denied the job and gets demoted.

norm: It's wrong for parents to abuse their children.
situation: Mary's child steals a hairbrush from Mary and Mary gets upset.
intention: Mary wants to discipline her child for stealing.
moral_action: Mary decides to tell her daughter to go to her room, without abusing her.
moral_consequence: Mary's daughter accepts her punishment and goes to her room, while Mary feels proud.
immoral_action: Mary decides to beat her child hard with the stolen hairbrush.
immoral_consequence: Mary's daughter suffers emotional wounds, and she hits back at her mother.

norm: It's rude to steal something that another person is using.
situation: George's teacher just gave the entire class a writing assignment when he realizes he left his pencils at home.
intention: George wants a writing utensil.
moral_action: George asks his neighbor if he can borrow a pencil for the day.
moral_consequence: The student next to George gives him a pencil, and they start talking end up becoming friends.
immoral_action: George snags a pencil off of his neighbors desk when they aren't looking.
immoral_consequence: Somebody else see's George steal the pencil, and tells the teacher causing George to get sent to the principals office.

norm: You can't take something back after you give it away.
situation: Jack had given his old bike to his younger brother Zack for his birthday, and was recently asked by his friends to go bike riding with them.
intention: Jack wants to go on the bike ride with his friends.
moral_action: Jack asks Zack if he can borrow the bike for a while.
moral_consequence: Zack allows his brother to borrow the bike and Jack spends the evening with his friends.
immoral_action: Without asking Zack, Jack takes the bike back and joins his friends on their ride.
immoral_consequence: Zack notices his bike missing and frantically searches for it around the neighborhood.

norm: It's good to make sure you pay attention to animals.
situation: Jimmy lives in a condo with his two dogs.
intention: Jimmy wants to go on a weekend camping trip.
moral_action: Jimmy asks a kid who lives next door to watch the dogs while he is away.
moral_consequence: Jimmy's neighbors in the condo are undisturbed by the dogs while he is away.
immoral_action: Jimmy leaves his dogs at home with a bowl of food and goes away for the weekend.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy's neighbors in the condo are annoyed because the dogs bark continuously, and they call animal services.

norm: You shouldn't exclude your parents from your life.
situation: Mary is going to get married, but she's worried that her parents will embarrass her at the wedding.
intention: Mary wants to host a trouble free wedding.
moral_action: Mary tells her parents that they can attend the wedding if they promise to behave.
moral_consequence: Mary's parents promise Mary that they will be on their best behavior.
immoral_action: Mary tells her parents that they can't come to the wedding.
immoral_consequence: Mary's parents are sad that they can't participate in the wedding festivities.

norm: Calling another person fat is rude and disrespectful.
situation: Dave is at work in his cubicle when he is introduced to a new coworker, Ralph who is quite obese.
intention: Dave wants to say something helpful to Ralph.
moral_action: Dave tells Ralph that their computers store a technical help guide that will explain how to do most of the job tasks.
moral_consequence: Ralph is happy to hear Dave's helpful little tidbit of information and is glad he already has one helpful colleague.
immoral_action: Dave tells Ralph that since he's quite fat he might have to request a special chair from management and that he can help him do so.
immoral_consequence: Ralph is insulted that Dave called him fat and insinuated that regular chairs cannot handle his mass.

norm: Don't make messes when you visit your friends' homes.
situation: Lee is spending the weekend with their friend Alex, and they decide to make waffles for breakfast.
intention: Lee wants to eat tasty waffles.
moral_action: Lee is careful to clean up any spills as they cook, and puts the dirty dishes into the dishwasher after eating.
moral_consequence: Alex is happy with the way Lee left the kitchen, and the two of them enjoy the rest of their weekend.
immoral_action: Lee leaves dirty dishes in the sink and spills all over the counter as they make and eat the waffles.
immoral_consequence: Alex has to clean the kitchen and is grumpy with Lee for the rest of the day.

norm: It is not okay to have bad hygiene.
situation: John was invited to have a nice dinner with a group of his friends while he was at the gym.
intention: John wants to meet up with his friends for dinner.
moral_action: John gets a shower and changes clothes before meeting his friends.
moral_consequence: John and his friends have dinner together as planned, without any hiccups.
immoral_action: John didn't feel like getting a shower after the gym, so he just went strait to meet with his friends.
immoral_consequence: John's friends were uncomfortable all evening because they could smell his body odor.

norm: You shouldn't read your child's letters.
situation: Max is suspicious about letters his daughter has been getting and is home with an unopened letter.
intention: Max wants to decide if he should open and read the letter to his daughter.
moral_action: Max waits until his daughter is home and tells her his fears.
moral_consequence: Max earns his daughters trust.
immoral_action: Max opens and reads the letter.
immoral_consequence: It turns out innocent and his daughter loses respect for him.

norm: You shouldn't blame others for your problems.
situation: John gets fired at work and comes home and tells his wife Janet who asks him why he thinks he got let go.
intention: John wants to respond to Janet's question.
moral_action: John tells Janet that he thinks it's because he could do a lot more to improve his performance and vows to do so at his next job.
moral_consequence: Janet is proud that her husband is taking personal responsibility and vows to help him get through it.
immoral_action: John tells Janet that it's because she's not a supportive wife, and if he was married to someone else he'd still have a job.
immoral_consequence: Janet is devastated and begins to cry as she is overwhelmed by the sudden weight John is throwing on her conscience.

norm: It's wrong to not be supportive of coworkers.
situation: Katie's coworker Brad is very nervous about giving a presentation to the CEO today.
intention: Katie wants to go to lunch.
moral_action: Katie asks Brad if he wants to go to lunch with her, and she can help him prepare for his presentation.
moral_consequence: Brad is thankful for Katie's help and is able to go into the presentation more relaxed and prepared.
immoral_action: Katie tells Brad she doesn't really have time to talk about it because she is on her way to lunch.
immoral_consequence: Brad feels more nervous and let down that Katie wouldn't listen to him.

norm: It's bad to commit suicide.
situation: Brendan's found out his girlfriend died of a freak accident and Brendan and his friends are devastated.
intention: Brendan wants to end his emotional pain.
moral_action: Brendan decides to find a new girlfriend through his friend network.
moral_consequence: Brendan's friends help him out and pair him with a girl, and Brendan is satisfied.
immoral_action: Brendan decides to hill himself to end the pain.
immoral_consequence: Brendan is dead and his friends all mourn his death.

norm: You shouldn't shun others because of their romantic relationships.
situation: Brad is creating the invites for his birthday party, and he's unsure if he wants to invite Charlie because he hates Charlie's husband.
intention: Brad needs to make a decision about Charlie.
moral_action: Brad decides to spend more time with Charlie and his husband before inviting them both to the party.
moral_consequence: Charlie becomes closer friends with Brad.
immoral_action: Brad doesn't invite Charlie to the party.
immoral_consequence: Charlie feels sad when he finds out that he wasn't invited to the party.

norm: It's abhorrent to keep other people as slaves.
situation: Robert has trouble dealing with the rising costs needed to run his farm.
intention: Robert wants to pay less for farm workers.
moral_action: Robert hires some cheap laborers to work on his farm.
moral_consequence: Robert is able to run the farm while spending less.
immoral_action: Robert gets slaves to work on his farm for free.
immoral_consequence: Robert is caught and arrested.

norm: You should apologize if you behave badly
situation: Tina was hanging out with her friends at a bar, when she got really drunk and had a fight.
intention: Tina wanted to address the situation when she was drunk.
moral_action: Tina gave an embarrassed apology and promised not to drink so much next time.
moral_consequence: Tina and her friends made up, and they hung out more often.
immoral_action: Tina continued the fight the next day, arguing she had done nothing wrong.
immoral_consequence: Tina's friends shunned her and stopped hanging out with her.

norm: You shouldn't be overly distrustful of your romantic partner
situation: Dan and Jenny are going on vacation with some of their other friends to a resort in Mexico.
intention: Dan wants to go to dinner with everyone.
moral_action: Dan appreciates that Jenny gets along well with all his friends when they are hanging out during the day.
moral_consequence: Dan's friends love Jenny, and they enjoy their trip.
immoral_action: Dan sees Jenny laughing and drinking at the bar with one of their male friends and accuses them of sleeping together.
immoral_consequence: Dan and Jenny get in a big fight that ruins dinner and makes everyone uncomfortable.

norm: It's important to be loyal to your romantic partner.
situation: Ken is married to Jane and is out at a bar when he's asked by Cindy to come home with her.
intention: Ken wants to respond to Cindy's proposal.
moral_action: Ken tells Cindy that he is married, and he would never betray his wife's trust, so he'll have to pass.
moral_consequence: Jane is delighted to learn that Ken was faithful and that he can be trusted when out alone.
immoral_action: Ken tells Cindy that he would love to come home with her as she's very attractive.
immoral_consequence: Jane is devastated that Ken has broken her trust and cheated on her and cannot forgive him.

norm: It's nice to welcome family to your home.
situation: Peter is surprised to get a call from his buildings security telling him hus parents are there to see him.
intention: Peter wants to enjoy a rare day off alone.
moral_action: Peter welcomes his parents but explains that he was looking forward to some down time.
moral_consequence: Peter's parents are understanding and leave after a brief visit.
immoral_action: Peter tells the guard to tell his parents that he is not home.
immoral_consequence: Peter's parents are hurt when they see his car in the parking lot.

norm: People should take care of the environment.
situation: Stephanie has finished drinking a large bottle of water on a crowded beach, and she notices a young girl collecting sea shells in front of her.
intention: Stephanie wants to get rid of the empty bottle.
moral_action: Stephanie offers the bottle to a little girl picking up sea shells explaining that the girl can use the bottle to hold her shells.
moral_consequence: Stephanie is thanked by the girl who begins sliding the shells into an empty bottle.
immoral_action: Stephanie walks towards the ocean and tosses the bottle into the waves.
immoral_consequence: Stephanie is fined by a cop walking along the beach for littering.

norm: Is it wrong to date married people
situation: Murphy has been going out and getting flirty with her coworker, Ed, who is married.
intention: Murphy wants to talk to Ed about his marriage.
moral_action: Murphy tells Ed if he doesn't leave his wife, she can no longer continue to see him.
moral_consequence: Murphy and Ed end their fling, and she starts seeing someone who is unattached.
immoral_action: Murphy talks to Ed about his relationship status and when he says he will stay with his wife, she continues to see him.
immoral_consequence: Murphy feels like a second choice to Ed.

norm: It's wrong to keep a college textbook you borrowed.
situation: Adam needed to borrow a textbook from his college professor.
intention: Adam wanted to be able to use it for the class.
moral_action: Although the professor forgot that Adam had borrowed the book, Adam made sure to return it.
moral_consequence: The professor receives his property.
immoral_action: After the class ended, the professor didn't ask for it, so Adam kept the textbook.
immoral_consequence: The professor must pay to replace the book.

norm: You shouldn't lose your cool in class.
situation: Robbie gets a test back from his teacher during class, and his score is much lower than he was expecting.
intention: Robbie wants to react to his score.
moral_action: Robbie takes a deep breath to calm down and decides to discuss the score with the teacher after class.
moral_consequence: The teacher listens to Robbie's concerns and offers him a way to get some bonus points to help his grade.
immoral_action: Robbie begins using profanities and loudly accuses the teacher of treating him unfairly.
immoral_consequence: The teacher tells Robbie that his outburst is unacceptable and sends him to the principal's office.

norm: It is okay to buy gifts for your partner.
situation: Matt remembers that his partner's birthday is tomorrow.
intention: Matt wants to celebrate his partner's birthday.
moral_action: Matt buys a nice bicycle for his partner as a birthday gift and take them to a nice restaurant for dinner.
moral_consequence: Matt's partner feels overjoyed and thanks Matt for his thoughtfulness.
immoral_action: Matt invites other friends to his home and asks them not to bring any gifts.
immoral_consequence: Matt's partner gets unhappy for not getting any presents.

norm: It's bad to neglect personal hygiene.
situation: Aaron is getting dressed after getting home from the gym.
intention: Aaron wants to cuddle with his girlfriend.
moral_action: Aaron makes sure to reapply deodorant and clean the sweat off of his body.
moral_consequence: Aaron's girlfriend is excited to sit and cuddle with him.
immoral_action: Aaron decides to skip showering and putting on deodorant to save time.
immoral_consequence: Aaron's girlfriend doesn't want to cuddle with him because he doesn't smell good.

norm: You should be happy for people getting married.
situation: John and Chelsea are getting married and invite Hank, who is under a lot of stress, to the wedding.
intention: Hank wants to come to the wedding and eat at the reception.
moral_action: Hank puts on a smile and forces himself to congratulate John and Chelsea at the wedding.
moral_consequence: John and Chelsea remember that moment and send him a thank you card.
immoral_action: Hank comes to the wedding loaded with stress and is in a sour mood the whole time.
immoral_consequence: John and Chelsea think that Hank doesn't care about their wedding and are more reluctant to invite him in the future.

norm: It's wrong to let drugs and alcohol ruin your life.
situation: Jake just got out of rehab for an addiction to crack.
intention: Jake wants to celebrate his freedom.
moral_action: Jake decides to celebrate by going on a vacation to the beach.
moral_consequence: Jake has a great time, and those who care about him are happy.
immoral_action: Jake decides to celebrate by smoking some crack rock.
immoral_consequence: Jake overdoses and dies, greatly upsetting those who care about him.

norm: It's frowned upon to be in a bad mood.
situation: John is having a hard time at work and is in a bad mood because of it.
intention: John wants to stop by his parents house for dinner.
moral_action: John tries to suck it and be a little bit cheerful at dinner.
moral_consequence: John has a good time and his mood is impoved.
immoral_action: John stays in a sullen mood at dinner and brings down the whole room.
immoral_consequence: His parents think something is wrong or everyone has a bad time.

norm: It's not okay to be disrespectful to your parents.
situation: Caleb sees a toy he's been wanting at the store and asks his mother for it, but she says no.
intention: Caleb wants to respond to his mother's refusal to buy a toy for him.
moral_action: Caleb asks if he can get an allowance, so he can save up to buy the toy.
moral_consequence: Caleb's mother agrees to an allowance if he does his chores.
immoral_action: Caleb sits down in the middle of the aisle and says he's not moving until she buys him the toy.
immoral_consequence: Caleb's mother picks him up, carries him out of the store, and grounds him to his room when they get home.

norm: It's bad to hide drugs in your home.
situation: Dustin notices that his stoner best friend left weed on the table, and he hears cops knocking on his door.
intention: Dustin wants to avoid getting into trouble.
moral_action: Dustin quickly asks his roommate to take toss the drugs into the community trash can.
moral_consequence: Dustin gains the cop's trust, and they listen to the information Dustin gives them about his friend.
immoral_action: Dustin tosses the weed into the oven.
immoral_consequence: The cops find the drugs arresting Dustin on drug charges.

norm: People should be punctual.
situation: Evan had been called in for an interview for a new job.
intention: Evan wants to attend the interview.
moral_action: Evan gets to the interview ten minutes before it was scheduled.
moral_consequence: The person doing the interview is impressed with Evan, and he gets the job.
immoral_action: Evan gets to the interview fifteen minutes later than it was scheduled.
immoral_consequence: The person interviewing was not impressed and Evan doesn't get the job.

norm: It's unethical to not pay for overtime.
situation: James is a Walmart manager who's under a lot of pressure to cut costs.
intention: James wants to cut labor costs.
moral_action: James replaces some of the cashiers with automated self checkouts.
moral_consequence: James is congratulated and given a bonus for successfully cutting labor costs.
immoral_action: James insists that workers apply for two different jobs, so they can work two thirty-hour work weeks.
immoral_consequence: James is caught by the local labor board and faces numerous legal charges.

norm: It's rude to yell at your friends.
situation: Luke and his friend are arguing over a political issue which they both feel strongly about.
intention: Luke wants to get his point across.
moral_action: Luke calmly states his point and sticks to using logical statements.
moral_consequence: The debate becomes less heated, and they eventually agree to disagree.
immoral_action: Luke raises his voice loudly to talk over his friend.
immoral_consequence: The argument becomes even more heated and their friendship is worsened.

norm: Partners should be considerate of each others wants and needs.
situation: Mack and Jen are in a relationship.
intention: Mack wants to spend time with Jen.
moral_action: Mack and Jen develop a system where the take turn picking the activities.
moral_consequence: They find things which both of them enjoy and the relationship remians strong.
immoral_action: Mack always insists on playing cards and picking the movies despite knowing that they are not Jen's favorite activites.
immoral_consequence: Jen feels neglected and unfulfilled, so she ends the relationship.

norm: It's wrong to lie about your pet.
situation: Lisa is talking to a new guy whom she likes, whom happens to be very passionate about animals.
intention: Lisa wants to impress the guy.
moral_action: Lisa tells the guy that she is considering adopting a dog and asks for advice.
moral_consequence: The guy gives her advice, and they go on a date to the animal shelter and have an amazing time.
immoral_action: Lisa tells the guy that she has a dog when in fact she doesn't.
immoral_consequence: The guy comes over one night and finds out she was lying and leaves, ending their friendship.

norm: It's bad to be cruel to animals.
situation: Henry is walking home from school when he sees a stray dog.
intention: Henry wants to interact with the stray dog.
moral_action: Henry pets the stray dog and gives it some food.
moral_consequence: The stray dog will become friendly towards Henry.
immoral_action: Henry throws a can at the stray dog.
immoral_consequence: The stray dog will attack Henry.

norm: It's not okay to let your opinions cloud your judgement.
situation: Daisy has a huge crush on Italian men.
intention: Daisy wants to have an Italian boyfriend.
moral_action: Daisy goes on a few dates with Italian guys.
moral_consequence: Daisy finds a loving Italian boyfriend.
immoral_action: Daisy gets into a relationship with the first Italian guy she meets.
immoral_consequence: Daisy gets her heart broken.

norm: It is unacceptable to wear only underwear in public.
situation: Jim needs to get an important letter in the mail and has just rolled out of bed to see the mailman approaching his mailbox.
intention: Jim needs to hand the letter to the mailman.
moral_action: Jim shouts out his fron tdoor for the mailman to wait, before throwing on a bathrobe and going to meet him with the letter.
moral_consequence: The mailman accepts Jim's letter with a smile and continues on his route.
immoral_action: Jim immediately rushes to the front door and runs out in his underwear to give the mailman the letter.
immoral_consequence: The mailman is justifiably uncomfortable with the whole encounter and quickly walks away after receiving the letter.

norm: It's rude to put your nose in a neighbor's business.
situation: James heard his neighbor yelling at his teenage daughter before she stormed out of their house.
intention: James wants to find out what happened at his neighbors' house.
moral_action: James bakes cookies and takes some over to his neighbor to cheer him up.
moral_consequence: James' neighbor makes small talk and eventually vents about his daughter's stubbornness.
immoral_action: James knocks on the neighbor's door to ask numerous questions about why he was yelling.
immoral_consequence: James' neighbor tells him to get off his property before he calls the cops.

norm: It's wrong to kiss your relative.
situation: Mark is drunk at a party with his friends and his sister.
intention: Mark wants to kiss someone.
moral_action: Mark leans over and kisses his girlfriend who is sitting on the couch with him.
moral_consequence: Mark's girlfriend kisses him back and asks him if he wants to dance with her.
immoral_action: Mark leans over and tries to kiss his sister who is on the couch with him.
immoral_consequence: Mark's sister slaps him across the face and his friends all start to laugh at him.

norm: It is impolite to ask friends for money.
situation: Brian is invited to go to the diner after school with his friends, but he doesn't have any money.
intention: Brian wants to get something to eat.
moral_action: Brian goes to his house to eat and meets his friends later.
moral_consequence: Brian hangs out with his friends later that same night.
immoral_action: Brian orders a burger and fries and then asks his friends to pay for the meal.
immoral_consequence: Brian's friends never ask him to go eat out with them again.

norm: You shouldn't prevent someone from taking a vacation.
situation: Ron's employee has asked him whether he can take a paid vacation during a busy week.
intention: Ron has to decide whether to reward his employee with a paid vacation.
moral_action: Rob gives his employee paid time off for the entire week.
moral_consequence: Rob's employee feels grateful and wants to work even harder when they come back.
immoral_action: Ron tells the employee that it would not be a good time for them to take a vacation.
immoral_consequence: Ron's employee continues to feel overwhelmed and thinks about finding a new job.

norm: It is shallow to judge people based on height.
situation: Sandra is talking to her friend about their new boyfriend when she learns that he is under five feet tall.
intention: Sandra wants to react to learning about her friend's boyfriend's height.
moral_action: Sandra says that height doesn't indicate the positive qualities and worth of a person.
moral_consequence: Sandra's friend is glad that Sandra doesn't ascribe a person's value based on superficial things.
immoral_action: Sandra says that her friend's boyfriend can't be much of a man if he's that short.
immoral_consequence: Sandra's friend is really disappointed that Sandra would make such a disparaging comment based on a person's height.

norm: It's rude to spread your negativity to others.
situation: Jill is at her son's soccer game and is sitting with group of parents.
intention: Jill wants to talk to the other moms in the group.
moral_action: Jill talks about the potential of the team to improve and suggests trying some new team building strategies.
moral_consequence: Jill is seen as a leader and the other parents look for her at every game.
immoral_action: Jill complains to the group about the team's poor coaching and lack of organization.
immoral_consequence: The other parents try to avoid sitting next to Jill at future games.

norm: It's good to celebrate with someone when they are proud.
situation: Claire thinks gaming is a waste of time, but younger brother proudly announces that he has just won a gaming tournament.
intention: Claire wants her brother to be successful.
moral_action: Claire congratulates her brother and takes him out to dinner to celebrate and learn more about competitive gaming.
moral_consequence: Claire's brother feels happy to celebrate and tell his sister about gaming.
immoral_action: Claire tells her brother that he should stop wasting his time gaming and work on getting a real job.
immoral_consequence: Claire's brother feels bad that Claire doesn't support his passion.

norm: it's wrong to do something that could intentionally hurt someone.
situation: Joseph lives in an apartment building and recently bought a new gun.
intention: Joseph wants to test out his gun.
moral_action: Joseph tests his gun by shooting at a gun range.
moral_consequence: Joseph gets to safely see how his gun works.
immoral_action: Joseph tests his gun by shooting at his neighbor.
immoral_consequence: Joseph gets arrested for shooting his neighbor.

norm: You shouldn't eat things that are bad for you.
situation: Bobby hash extremely high blood pressure and the doctor has warned him to eliminate fats and cholesterol from his diet.
intention: Bobby wants to have a breakfast that tastes good.
moral_action: Bobby decides to change his diet and has a breakfast of toast and some of his favorite fruit.
moral_consequence: Bobby is able to lower his blood pressure and his doctor is extremely happy for him and his improved health.
immoral_action: Bobby does not listen to his doctor and makes a breakfast consisting of four eggs, four pieces of bacon and two pieces of toast to eat.
immoral_consequence: Bobby keeps eating unhealthy foods and has to get a heart transplant ASAP.

norm: It's rude to balk at someone else fashion.
situation: Rosa saw her friend's new clothes for the first time and was surprised.
intention: Rosa wants to decide how to react.
moral_action: Rosa complements her friends new clothes sincerely.
moral_consequence: Her friend smiles and thanks her for the complement.
immoral_action: Rosa is shocked at her friend's choice in clothing and says so.
immoral_consequence: Her friend's feelings are hurt, and she's upset for the rest of the day.

norm: It's not okay to be hypocritical about things in life.
situation: Frank, who is an anti-smoking advocate is talking with Paul when Paul tells him their anti-smoking charity missed their funding goal.
intention: Frank wants to ease his stress from the bad news.
