norm: It's nice to throw a farewell party for someone.
situation: Jessica is really close to her coworker Susan, who has recently accepted a job offer at a big firm.
intention: Jessica wants to say bye to Susan.
moral_action: Jessica plans a surprise farewell party for Susan.
moral_consequence: Susan is shocked to discover a party when she walks in to the office on her last day, and realizes how much she meant to everyone there.
immoral_action: Jessica and the rest of her coworkers go about their last day with Susan as usual, before simply saying goodbye to her at the end of her last shift.
immoral_consequence: Susan feels underwhelmed by the uneventful goodbye, and moves on thinking she didn't mean much to her old coworkers.

norm: It's bad to steal food.
situation: James lives near a college campus that runs buffet-style cafeterias for its students.
intention: James wants a free meal.
moral_action: James volunteers to handle some of the more unpleasant kitchen duties in exchange for free food.
moral_consequence: The university hires James as a part-time worker with a free shift meal as one of his benefits.
immoral_action: James sneaks into the cafeteria through the back door and eats his fill of free food.
immoral_consequence: James is eventually asked for his student ID and banned from campus on being unable to produce it.

norm: It's good to overcome your past when you're in love.
situation: Jon is in a relationship with Christi but is concerned about his embarrassing past.
intention: Jon wants to avoid being rejected for what he has done.
moral_action: Jon has a deep talk revealing his embarassing past to Christi wanting to be honest.
moral_consequence: Christi is understand and does not let it effect the relationship they are soon going to be married.
immoral_action: Jon panics when the relationship gets closer and finds an excuse to break up with Christi rather than reveal his past.
immoral_consequence: Jon never finds someone that he is as close to and ends up living life single.

norm: People shouldn't be loudly proud of minor achievements.
situation: James managed to bring his grade in history up from a D to a C.
intention: James wants to feel better about himself.
moral_action: James continues to work hard and manages to bring his grade up to an A.
moral_consequence: James' parents and teachers give him lots of praise and recognition.
immoral_action: James tells everyone he knows about how he's now getting a C in history.
immoral_consequence: When James is out of earshot, his friends say he really needs to reassess his life.

norm: You should not freeload from other people.
situation: Troy has been living at Donald's house for a few months after he lost his job and now Donald is asking if Troy is going to look for work.
intention: Troy wants to answer Donald's question.
moral_action: Troy tells Donald that he's going to look for work right away since he wants to free Donald of the burden of housing him.
moral_consequence: Donald is delighted that his friend is planning to move on with his life, and he won't be there too much longer.
immoral_action: Troy tells Donald that he'd much rather just continue to live there for free for a while, and he'll look for work sometime down the road.
immoral_consequence: Donald is furious that Troy is taking advantage of his good will and contemplates whether to throw Troy out.

norm: You should never throw someone else's property away
situation: James' sister just went away to college, and he wants to move into her room.
intention: James wants to have lots of space in his sister's room.
moral_action: James moves all of his sister's stuff into their garage.
moral_consequence: When Jame's sister comes home, she thanks James, sells some of her stuff and takes some to college.
immoral_action: James throws all of his sister's stuff into the trash, so he can move his own stuff in.
immoral_consequence: When James' sister comes home from college, she screams at him.

norm: Friends should be understanding.
situation: Todd is talking with his friend Ben right after Ben experiences a crushing defeat in a tournament that he tried very hard to win.
intention: Todd wants to talk about the tournament.
moral_action: Todd consoles Ben about the tournament loss and tells Ben that he did a great job in a tough tournament.
moral_consequence: Ben appreciates Todd's kind words, and they become closer friends over the event.
immoral_action: Todd laughs at Ben's major tournament loss and makes fun of him.
immoral_consequence: Ben starts viewing Todd as an insensitive person and becomes much less friendly towards Todd.

norm: It is wrong to lie about someone dying.
situation: Keira's final paper for her class is due tomorrow, and she doesn't think she can finish it in time.
intention: Keira wants to get more time to finish her paper.
moral_action: Keira goes to her professor, explains her situation, and requests an extension.
moral_consequence: Keira's professor appreciates her maturity and gives her an extension with a small grade penalty.
immoral_action: Keira tells her professor that her grandmother just died and that she needs an extension.
immoral_consequence: Keira gets in trouble when the professor finds out she lied.

norm: It is immature to take back a gift.
situation: Mike's birthday present to his brother is a trip to a football game together.
intention: Mike wants to have fun at the football game.
moral_action: Mike buys his brother's favorite food and drinks for the tailgate party before the game.
moral_consequence: Mike's brother has a great time at the game and can't wait to hang out with Mike again.
immoral_action: Mike meets a girl at the bar that night and decides to give her the ticket to the football game instead of his brother.
immoral_consequence: Mike's brother is heartbroken and has the worst birthday ever.

norm: It's wrong to attack someone.
situation: Sonny is hosting a dinner party and has invited his daughter, Piper, and her boyfriend, Peter to join.
intention: Sonny wants Piper and Peter to appreciate the meal he cooks.
moral_action: Sonny notices that Peter isn't eating much and asks how he can accomodate him.
moral_consequence: Peter tells Sonny that he often takes breaks in between bites and compliments him on his cooking.
immoral_action: Sonny notices that Peter isn't eating much and throws a plate at him.
immoral_consequence: Piper and Peter immediately leave Sonny's dinner party and refuse to speak with him ever again.

norm: It is rude to take up too much room.
situation: Claudia is on the train to visit her parents and starts to feel very tired from the long journey.
intention: Claudia wants to sleep during her train trip.
moral_action: Claudia sits in a window seat, rests her head against the window with her coat as a pillow and falls asleep.
moral_consequence: All passengers in the train car have a place to sit.
immoral_action: Claudia lies down, taking up three seats.
immoral_consequence: Other passengers have to stand for hours.

norm: You shouldn't clog toilets.
situation: John is at a friend's house visiting.
intention: John wants to finish using the restroom.
moral_action: John performs a courtesy flush before using an appropriate amount of toilet paper.
moral_consequence: John is able to rejoin his friend in the main room after washing up.
immoral_action: John uses half a roll of toilet paper before flushing.
immoral_consequence: John is embarrassed when he floods his friend's bathroom with toilet water.

norm: It's rude not to speak to one's siblings.
situation: Katie is going to Thanksgiving dinner at her parents house and her sister will be there who she is angry with.
intention: Katie wants to avoid fighting during the holiday.
moral_action: Katie approaches her sister ahead of time and talks the issue out with her.
moral_consequence: The family is able to have a nice holiday dinner together.
immoral_action: Katie does not speak to her sister the whole time she's at Thanksgiving dinner.
immoral_consequence: Katie's family can sense the tension between them and it makes dinner awkward.

norm: It is loving to agree to keep bonded cats together.
situation: Mark goes to the animal shelter.
intention: Marks wants to adopt a pet.
moral_action: Mark adopts two cats that have grown up together.
moral_consequence: Mark has two happy companions that make him feel needed.
immoral_action: Marks sees two bonded cats but only takes one.
immoral_consequence: The cat Mark takes destroys Mark's house and dies of heartbreak.

norm: It's not nice to always be a show-off.
situation: James' history teacher was lecturing the class about the Renaissance, which James knew a lot about.
intention: James wants to impress his teacher.
moral_action: James answers several questions and shares many interesting facts he's learned.
moral_consequence: James' teacher says that it's clear that he's an avid reader on this subject.
immoral_action: James answers every question until the other students start to lose interest in the lecture.
immoral_consequence: James' teacher eventually has to ask him to stop answering so the other students will have a chance.

norm: It's kind to babysit for your neighbors.
situation: Lisa's neighbors asked if she could babysit their two kids for the night.
intention: Lisa wants to watch a new show on television.
moral_action: Lisa goes to the couple's house to babysit and watches the television show there.
moral_consequence: The couple is grateful to have a night to enjoy each other's company without the children.
immoral_action: Lisa tells the couple no and watches the show from her house.
immoral_consequence: The couple is not able to have a night for themselves and have to stay home.

norm: You shouldn't dis-invite people to events.
situation: Thelma has planned a dinner for her friends, including her unpolished cousin, but just found out that a very refined man whom Thelma likes will also be attending.
intention: Thelma wants to impress her crush.
moral_action: Thelma decides that everything will be alright anyway and looks forward to seeing her cousin at the party.
moral_consequence: Thelma's cousin has a great time, and so does Thelma's crush who is impressed by how gracious a hostess she is.
immoral_action: Thelma calls her cousin and tells her the party is cancelled to avoid having her cousin embarrass her.
immoral_consequence: Thelma's cousin finds out the party is still on and is quite sad at having been rejected.

norm: You shouldn't cheat on tests.
situation: Vanessa is good at math but her friend Sally is bad at math and if she fails the next math test she will have to repeat the grade.
intention: Vanessa wants Sally to pass the test.
moral_action: Vanessa offers to help Sally study for the test and teach her what she doesn't know.
moral_consequence: Sally understands math better and ends up improving her math grades in general.
immoral_action: Vanessa offers to let Sally copy off her during the math test.
immoral_consequence: Sally and Vanessa both get caught and are suspended from school for cheating.

norm: You shouldn't use someone as an excuse.
situation: Rob, who was going to be a programmer but dropped out of school, is asked by his child Eric why he never finished school.
intention: Rob wants to justify his dropping out of school.
moral_action: Rob says that he dropped out because he didn't like programming that much.
moral_consequence: Eric is content with Rob's answer and continues the conversation.
immoral_action: Rob says that he dropped out because Eric was born, and he no longer had time.
immoral_consequence: Eric feels guity for ruining Rob's dreams of becoming a programmer.

norm: It's rude to miss a family funeral.
situation: Nia's grandfather has passed away and her grandmother Susan expectsher to come to the funeral.
intention: Nia wants to grieve her grandfather.
moral_action: Nia comes to the funeral and sits next to Susan.
moral_consequence: Susan is grateful that Nia came to the funeral to grieve.
immoral_action: Nia skips the funeral and cries in her room by herself.
immoral_consequence: Susan is hurt that Nia didn't come to the funeral.

norm: It's wrong to take more than your share.
situation: Jan's family are forced to stay inside, and toilet paper is running out in stores.
intention: Jan wants to buy some toilet paper at the grocery store.
moral_action: Jan only buys one pack of toilet paper.
moral_consequence: Other families will be able to have enough toilet paper.
immoral_action: Jan buys up all of the toilet paper at the toilet store.
immoral_consequence: Others will not be able to buy some toilet paper for themselves.

norm: People shouldn't lead other people on with a false kiss.
situation: Josh is listening to Christina, who has a crush on him, cry about the death of her mother.
intention: Josh wants to make Christina feel better.
moral_action: Josh tells Christina a funny joke.
moral_consequence: Christina laughs and trusts Josh more.
immoral_action: Josh leans forward and kisses Christina.
immoral_consequence: Christina is heartbroken when she discovers Josh's actions weren't genuine.

norm: It is expected that you dress appropriately for church
situation: Bobby is at home on a Sunday morning as his mother urges him to get ready because they're running late for church.
intention: Bobby wants to get dressed for church.
moral_action: Bobby throws on his formal church clothes and tells his mother that he's ready.
moral_consequence: Bobby and his family arrive just in time for church service.
immoral_action: Bobby puts on a swimsuit and basketball jersey and tells his mother he's ready.
immoral_consequence: Bobby's mother scolds him for dressing inappropriately and makes him go back and change into church clothes, causing them to be late.

norm: You should not use violence to solve problems
situation: Steve sees a man outside of a bar threatening a woman.
intention: Steve wants to stop the man from attacking the woman.
moral_action: Steve calls the police and confronts the man.
moral_consequence: The man gets scared and leaves without fighting.
immoral_action: Steve grabs a pipe and beats the man with it.
immoral_consequence: The police arrest Steve for using excessive force.

norm: You shouldn't do things without your doctor's permission.
situation: Jim recently had an operation and was ordered by his doctor to avoid anything vigorous for a few weeks.
intention: Jim wants to do something fun today.
moral_action: Jim follow his doctor's orders and spends the day reading a new book on the sofa.
moral_consequence: Jim thoroughly enjoys the novel, and his body has a chance to heal.
immoral_action: Jim decides to go on an intense run through the park despite his doctor's orders.
immoral_consequence: Jim has a heart attack from the strain and dies on the spot.

norm: It is wrong to cyberstalk people.
situation: Steven hasn't heard from Shawn in a while, and has been curious what he's been up to.
intention: Steven wants to learn about what Shawn has been doing.
moral_action: Steven calls Shawn up and asks him what he's been up to, and where he's been.
moral_consequence: Shawn explains he's just been super busy, but will start reaching out soon.
immoral_action: Steven starts looking into Shawn's facebook, looking into all of his recent follows and adding them.
immoral_consequence: Shawn finds out that Steven is digging into his business and cuts him off forever.

norm: It's rude to throw away someone else's belongings.
situation: Stacy and her family are in the process of moving, and she is going through things in the basement while her mom is at work.
intention: Stacy wants to get rid of some items.
moral_action: Stacy carefully goes through the boxes and only throws out the items that are hers.
moral_consequence: Stacy makes progress on cleaning things out, and nothing of value is tossed.
immoral_action: Stacy tosses boxes of items at a time, not bothering to check what is inside of them.
immoral_consequence: Stacy throws out her mom's wedding jewelery.

norm: It is important to treat everyone as equal.
situation: Roger is in charge of hiring a supervisor for his department, and he is choosing between candidates, Doris and Joe, who perform equally well in every aspect.
intention: Roger wants to fill the position.
moral_action: Roger asks Doris and Joe to solve a real-life problem, and he is impressed by Doris's answer and decides to recruit Doris.
moral_consequence: Doris feels proud and thanks Roger for this employment.
immoral_action: Roger thinking that female is less competent than male decides to recruit Joe.
immoral_consequence: Doris feels unfair and prejudiced.

norm: It's wrong to just ditch your friends for other people.
situation: Jan is at a party with her friend when she meets a new person she finds interesting.
intention: Jan wants to go over to the new person's house.
moral_action: Jan invites her friend to come along to the new person's house with her.
moral_consequence: Jan's friend feels included by Jan and has a good time at the person's house.
immoral_action: Jan goes to the new person's house leaving her friend at the party.
immoral_consequence: Jan's friend feels abandoned by Jan and that Jan values the new person over them.

norm: You shouldn't drive while distracted.
situation: Sally is driving to her friends house.
intention: Sally wants to enjoy the ride.
moral_action: Sally puts on an audio book she'd been meaning to listen to.
moral_consequence: Sally is entertained and stays safe.
immoral_action: Sally texts with her friend to pass the long ride.
immoral_consequence: Sally gets into an accident while distracted.

norm: It's wrong to use something that isn't yours without permission.
situation: Hank wanted to use his grill, but he was out of propane, and he saw his neighbor Dale had plenty.
intention: Hank wants to grill something quickly.
moral_action: Hank quickly rushes to the store where he restocks on propane as quickly as possible.
moral_consequence: Hank is pleased that he has refilled his propane supply.
immoral_action: Hank decides to take some of Dale's propane to start grilling.
immoral_consequence: Dale decides to keep mocking Hank for running out of propane.

norm: It's good to recycle what's being discarded as trash.
situation: Cathy is having a party and has many empty beer bottles.
intention: Cathy wants to throw them away.
moral_action: Cathy throws the glass bottles in the recycling.
moral_consequence: The party-goers respect Cathy for trying to do her part to help the environment.
immoral_action: Cathy throws the glass bottles in the regular trash.
immoral_consequence: The party-goers think that Cathy is hurting the environment.

norm: It is okay to set boundaries within a relationship.
situation: Jenna's boyfriend wanted her to come with him to heavy metal shows, but they made her very uncomfortable.
intention: Jenna doesn't want to feel uncomfortable.
moral_action: Jenna tells her boyfriend that she supports his love of heavy metal but doesn't want to go herself.
moral_consequence: Jenna's boyfriend tells her he understands, and she spends a pleasant night at home reading.
immoral_action: Jenna doesn't want to say no to her boyfriend, so she gets drunk before the shows to feel less anxious.
immoral_consequence: Jenna ends up vomiting everywhere at one of the shows, embarrassing herself and her boyfriend.

norm: It's expected that families should spend time together.
situation: Mario's family is about to hold a family reunion soon.
intention: Mario wants to decide if he should attend.
moral_action: Mario decides to go to the reunion and see his family.
moral_consequence: Mario's family is happy to see him there, and they have a lot of fun.
immoral_action: Mario decides not to go just like he didn't go to the last two.
immoral_consequence: Mario's family wonders why Mario never spends any time with them.

norm: You shouldn't tell someone they smell even if they do.
situation: Marcie is at the beach with her boyfriend, who is sweating, and his underarms have a bad aroma.
intention: Marcie doesn't want to have to smell her boyfriend's unpleasant scent.
moral_action: Marcie suggests to her boyfriend they take a swim, so they jump into the ocean and play in the water.
moral_consequence: Her boyfriend is rinsed off from the saltwater and no longer has a sweat smell.
immoral_action: Marcie tells her boyfriend he stinks and to get away from her, so he leaves the beach.
immoral_consequence: Her boyfriend decides he doesn't want to date a girl that treats him in that manner, and he dumps Marcie.

norm: It's wrong to dirty your friend's car.
situation: Sypha is driving Sonja's car down the street, she had to borrow it because her own is in the shop.
intention: Sypha wants to get her errands done.
moral_action: Sypha waits until she gets home and uses an app to order the food.
moral_consequence: Sypha eats the food in her living room and enjoys the meal.
immoral_action: On the way home Sypha orders drive through and spills the drink on the floor.
immoral_consequence: Sonja is mad at Sypha because now she has to have the car cleaned again.

norm: It's wrong to be a chronic masturbator.
situation: Hector is sitting in his car and starts fantasizing about a woman he sees.
intention: Hector wants to masturbate.
moral_action: Hector waits until he gets home and masturbates while thinking of the woman.
moral_consequence: Hector cleans up and goes on with his day without incident.
immoral_action: Hector starts masturbating in the car as he stares at the woman.
immoral_consequence: Hector is arrested and is put on a sex offender list.

norm: It's good show kindness to strangers.
situation: John is driving and sees a homeless man on the street corner holding a sign.
intention: John wants to go to the game.
moral_action: John stops and hands the man some money, wishes him well, then goes to the game.
moral_consequence: The homeless man feels loved and is not hungry tonight.
immoral_action: John pretends he doesn't see the homeless man and speeds off to the game.
immoral_consequence: The homeless man feels rejected and sad and goes hungry.

norm: It is bad to be mean to people
situation: A new kid showed up in Jack's class and is sitting all by themselves.
intention: Jack wants to say something to the new kid.
moral_action: Jack invites the new kid to hang out with him and his friends.
moral_consequence: The new kid feels like he belongs and doesn't feel sad anymore.
immoral_action: Jack makes fun of the new kid and tells him that he looks ugly.
immoral_consequence: The new kid hates coming to school and never makes any friends.

norm: It is wrong to withhold rent from a roommate.
situation: Rebekah shares an apartment with her roommate and knows the monthly rent payment is due.
intention: Rebekah wants to buy tickets to a concert.
moral_action: Rebekah gives the roommate her share of the rent money and works overtime to make money to pay for the concert tickets.
moral_consequence: Rebekah's roommate is happy that they have the money and can pay their bill.
immoral_action: Rebekah tells her roommate that she is going through a rough time and can't help pay the rent this month, but uses the money to buy tickets to the concert.
immoral_consequence: Rebekah's roommate is angry when she finds out that Rebekah spent the money on the concert.

norm: It is insensitive to name someone after a serial killer.
situation: Brenda was giving birth to a baby boy in the hospital.
intention: Brenda wants to name her son.
moral_action: Brenda decides to name her newborn son after Abraham Lincoln.
moral_consequence: Brenda's son grows up having high aspirations and becomes the president of the United States.
immoral_action: Brenda decides to name her newborn son after Jeffrey Dahmer.
immoral_consequence: Brenda's son grows up getting teased and has to change his name when he gets older.

norm: It is shallow to break up with someone over apperance.
situation: Paola's boyfriend is in the military and returns from duty with several serious scars on his face.
intention: Paola wants to react to her boyfriend's new look.
moral_action: Paola focuses on her boyfriend's personality and decides to stay with him.
moral_consequence: Paola and her boyfriend remain happy together.
immoral_action: Paola decides to break up with her boyfriend to avoid embarrassment.
immoral_consequence: Paola's boyfriend is heartbroken and loses much self-esteem.

norm: It's rude to heckle others during games.
situation: Stephen is watching a basketball game and his least favorite team misses a shot.
intention: Stephen wants to insult the team for missing a shot.
moral_action: "Stephen screams, ""boo"", along with a few hundred other people."
moral_consequence: Stephen feels he made the right choice and feels part of the crowd.
immoral_action: Stephen calls the fumbling team various expletives while shouting very loudly.
immoral_consequence: Stephen is told by security to tone it down and feels humiliated.

norm: You shouldn't get mad at your family.
situation: John's son comes home from school and tells him that he's gotten a bad grade on a test.
intention: John wants to react to the bad news.
moral_action: John tells his son that these things happen and that he'll help him study those topics, so he can grasp them better.
moral_consequence: John's son feels supported and is really glad someone will help him unravel the mystery of what he's trying to learn.
immoral_action: John tells his son that is unnacpetable, and he did not raise a moron and that he's grounded for two weeks.
immoral_consequence: John's son is devastated that his dad is angry with him and feels scared about being grounded.

norm: You should not sleep the day away.
situation: Roy has tickets to see a new movie in the evening.
intention: Roy wants to get some rest before going to the movie.
moral_action: Roy takes a short nap.
moral_consequence: Roy is well rested and gets to the movie on time.
immoral_action: Roy sleeps for most of the day.
immoral_consequence: Roy wakes up too late and misses half of the movie.

norm: It's wrong to grab people.
situation: Auston is at a party when he notices a guest, Bill, who is engrossed in a conversation, has a large wasp crawling on his shoulder.
intention: Auston wants to get Bill's attention, so he can warn him of the wasp.
moral_action: "Auston leans in and loudly says ""excuse me sir"" in the direction of Bill."
moral_consequence: Bill looks back at Auston and sees him gesturing about the wasp and is glad Auston warned him of danger.
immoral_action: Auston reaches towards Bill and grab's Bill's upper arm and yanks it to get him to stop talking.
immoral_consequence: Bill is upset that Auston caused him pain and grabbed him so hard and is so angry that he doesn't notice the wasp which stings him.

norm: You shouldn't feed pets human food.
situation: Sam is eating his dinner and his cat is standing by him looking hungry.
intention: Sam wants to feed his cat some meat.
moral_action: Sam opens up a can of meaty wet food for his cat.
moral_consequence: The cat is excited to get the wet food and is satiated.
immoral_action: Sam gives his cat a piece of his fried chicken.
immoral_consequence: The cat gets sick because of all the grease in the chicken.

norm: You shouldn't put off important things.
situation: Adam has been afraid of going to the dentist since he was a little kid.
intention: Adam wants to avoid going to the dentist as much as possible.
moral_action: Adam goes to the dentist twice a year for cleanings and a check up.
moral_consequence: Adam does not need to go to the dentist outside his yearly appointments because his teeth are well-kept.
immoral_action: Adam doesn't go to the dentist even when he starts feeling tooth pain.
immoral_consequence: Adam ends up needing extensive dental work because of how long he has neglected his teeth.

norm: It's good to keep your word.
situation: Mark agreed to help his friend with a construction project.
intention: Mark wants to go to bed earlier than usual.
moral_action: Mark reschedules with his friend and promises he will dedicate the time to help him.
moral_consequence: Mark's friend is happy that he's still willing to help.
immoral_action: Mark pretends that he forgot and stays at home.
immoral_consequence: Mark's friend is disappointed and finds him to be unreliable.

norm: It is expected to spend valentine's day with your partner.
situation: There is a movie coming out on Valentine's day that Steve is really interested in that his girlfriend isn't.
intention: Steve wants to go see the movie.
moral_action: Steve tells his girlfriend if she'll go see this movie, he'll see one of her favorites.
moral_consequence: Steve's girlfriend agrees, and they have a lovely time out seeing both movies.
immoral_action: Steve asks his girlfriend to go see the movie, she refuses, so he asks his buddies instead.
immoral_consequence: Steve's girlfriend feels very slighted and ends up dumping him.

norm: It's rude to threaten people with a gun.
situation: Hank, who is armed with a pistol, is walking down the street when he sees a stranger, Tom yelling at his girlfriend Janice.
intention: Hank wants to stop Tom from yelling at Janice.
moral_action: Hank tells Tom that he's making a public scene and that it's rude to yell when you talk.
moral_consequence: Tom snaps back into reality and realizes he's been getting out of hand and apologizes to Janice.
immoral_action: Hank pulls out his pistol and points it at Tom telling him to back off, or he'll shoot him.
immoral_consequence: Tom is terrified and fears for his life and is simultaneously angry at Hank for threatening him.

norm: It's good to forgive people.
situation: Pat and Kelly are friends and Pat unintentionally hurts Kelly during a group chatting in social media, and Pat wants to apologize to Kelly.
intention: Kelly wants to react to the apology.
moral_action: Kelly accepts the apology and Pat agrees to be respectful during group chatting in the future.
moral_consequence: Kelly feels belonged to the group and gets support from the group whenever she needs it.
immoral_action: Kelly is angry and decides to leave the group and ghost Pat.
immoral_consequence: Kelly becomes unforgiving and distances herself from others.

norm: It's wrong to be manipulative.
situation: Bob is assigned a new client by his company, in hopes that he will improve their sales relationship.
intention: Bob wants to make a big sale to the company.
moral_action: Bob gives a strong presentation about what he has to offer and asks directly for more of the company's business.
moral_consequence: The company he is working with appreciates his professionalism and rewards him with a large purchase.
immoral_action: Bob tells his new client that he can save them some money if they buy in quantity, but only for one day, which is not true.
immoral_consequence: The company finds out that Bob lied to them, when they talk to other people in the industry, and Bob loses all of their business.

norm: You shouldn't buy your ex expensive things.
situation: Ron was a terrible husband and that's why his wife divorced him - now he feels bad about how he was with her.
intention: Ron wants to apologize to his ex wife.
moral_action: Ron calls his ex wife and convincingly apologizes to her for all the bad things he did to her.
moral_consequence: Ron's ex wife believes he is sincere and feels vindicated.
immoral_action: Ron buys an expensive necklace to his ex wife and sends it to her with a heartfelt apology note.
immoral_consequence: Ron's ex wife feels he's trying to buy her forgiveness and feels used, once again.

norm: Friends should include each other.
situation: John and his friend Ted find out about a new action movie coming out that they both think looks exciting.
intention: John wants to go see the movie.
moral_action: John invites Ted to go see the movie together the following Saturday.
moral_consequence: Ted is excited and has a great time at the movie.
immoral_action: John goes to see the movie by himself the following Saturday.
immoral_consequence: Ted later finds out and is sad that John went without inviting him.

norm: It's wrong to lie to someone about their heritage.
situation: Jane has an adopted son named Jonas who doesn't know he's adopted who asks if she's his real mother.
intention: Jane needs to decide how to respond.
moral_action: Jane tells Jonas that he was adopted at a young age.
moral_consequence: Jonas appreciates the honesty and continues to love Jane dearly.
immoral_action: Jane tells Jonas that of course she's his real mother.
immoral_consequence: Jonas later finds out the truth and never forgives Jane for lying.

norm: It's good to have hopes and aspirations.
situation: Jules is applying for college and has to write about what she thinks of her future.
intention: Jules wants to write a thorough essay.
moral_action: Jules considers the ways attending college could improve her life and writes about what she imagines.
moral_consequence: Jules' letter is very convincing and it helps her a lot in the application proess.
immoral_action: Jules writes that she doesn't want any kind of future anymore because her depression is so deep.
immoral_consequence: Jules' letter concerns the college board, but does not help her get into the school.

norm: It's shabby to be a poor friend to your peers.
situation: John and his friends hear about a concert across the state and John is the only one of them with a car.
intention: John wants to go to the concert.
moral_action: John takes his friends along with him to the concert in his car.
moral_consequence: John's friends get to the concert quickly and for free.
immoral_action: John doesn't wait for his friends and drives to the concert by himself.
immoral_consequence: John's friends have to buy expensive bus tickets in order to get to the concert.

norm: It's wrong to give disease.
situation: Paul just found out from his doctor that he has a highly infectious disease.
intention: Paul wants to pick up his medicine from the store.
moral_action: Paul stays home and pays someone to deliver his medicine to the door.
moral_consequence: Paul eventually gets better and no one else gets the disease from him.
immoral_action: Paul goes to the store to pick up his medicine even though he knows he could spread the disease.
immoral_consequence: Several of the people at the store are infected by Paul's visit.

norm: You shouldn't laugh at someone's singing.
situation: James and his friends are out at a karaoke bar, and James' friend Linda is singing terribly off-key.
intention: James wants to spend more time listening to the good singers in his group.
moral_action: James keeps suggesting songs to the best singers in the group.
moral_consequence: James gets to hear relatively talented people singing instead of Linda.
immoral_action: James makes a joke about Linda's singing and gets his whole group of friends laughing at her.
immoral_consequence: Linda storms out of the room and refusing to ever come to karaoke again.

norm: Family members expect to be included in family events.
situation: Mary is invited to a family reunion but it required to bring one other person.
intention: Mary wants to go to the family reunion with someone.
moral_action: Mary invites her siblings to the reunion instead of a friend, and they go together.
moral_consequence: Mary and her siblings have a great time at the family reunion.
immoral_action: Mary decides to ask a friend instead of a family member to come with her, and they go together.
immoral_consequence: Mary's family feels Mary is ignoring them and their relationship weakens.

norm: It is good to apologize for your actions.
situation: Alvin and his wife Lucy had a big fight last night in which Alvin said some mean things.
intention: Alvin wants to address the situation with his wife.
moral_action: Alvin apologizes for the mean things he said and asks Lucy how he can make it up to her.
moral_consequence: Lucy is grateful to hear this from Alvin and apologizes for her own part in the argument.
immoral_action: Alvin tells Lucy that the fight was her fault and refuses to apologize for his words.
immoral_consequence: Lucy decides she cannot be with a person like Alvin and files for divorce.

norm: It is distasteful to think about incestuous relationships.
situation: Rebecca is talking to some people in the Supernatural fandom when one of the fans brings up her favorite paring of the twins dating each other.
intention: Rebecca wants to interact with the fandom.
moral_action: Rebecca gives the other fan evidence of other relationships in the show that she supports.
moral_consequence: Rebecca is thanked by later by the other fans for introducing them to unique parings.
immoral_action: Rebecca goes along with this fan reading some fanfiction before voicing her approval of the ship.
immoral_consequence: Rebecca finds herself blocked by her other friends for supporting an incest couple.

norm: It's encouraged you find a plumber when your pipes burst
situation: Taylor just finishes taking a shower when he heads down stairs and notices a huge water spot on the ceiling of his kitchen.
intention: Taylor wants to save money.
moral_action: Taylor calls a plumber and negotiates the price down to the point where he can afford it.
moral_consequence: Taylor still is able to save some money from his paycheck, and he gets to use his shower without damaging his house.
immoral_action: To avoid paying to fix the plumbing problem, Taylor stops using his upstairs bathroom and instead showers at work.
immoral_consequence: Taylor is inconvenienced by showering at work, but he ends up saving a lot of money.

norm: You shouldn't make your pet drink your urine.
situation: Tyson is on a hike with his dog on a very hot day and is carrying bottled water and cups in his backpack.
intention: Tyson wants to give his dog something to drink.
moral_action: Tyson pours some bottled water into a cup and gives it to his dog to drink.
moral_consequence: Tyson's dog is rehydrated by the water and finishes the hike with Tyson.
immoral_action: Tyson urinates into a cup and gives it to his dog drink.
immoral_consequence: Tyson's dog is not rehydrated from the urine and ends up collapsing on the hike.

norm: You shouldn't do something just because someone asks you.
situation: James is a Marine, and his Sergeant wanted him to shoot a prisoner they had.
intention: James has to respond to his Sergeant.
moral_action: James tells his Sergeant that he won't do it since it'd be against the law.
moral_consequence: James doesn't have to kill anyone even though the Sergeant becomes mad.
immoral_action: James takes out his gun and aims it right at the prisoner's head.
immoral_consequence: James commits a war crime, and his Sergeant feels that he can get James to do anything.

norm: It's expected that you'll be mindful of a friend's schedule.
situation: Frank often gives his friend Fiona a ride to work every day, and today has a bunch of errands to do in addition to taking her to work.
intention: Frank wants to finish his errands.
moral_action: Frank decides to wait to run his errands until after he's dropped Fiona off.
moral_consequence: Fiona appreciates Frank's consideration and thanks him for the ride.
immoral_action: Frank decides it'd be most efficient if he did some of his errands on the way to taking Fiona to work.
immoral_consequence: Fiona ends up being very late to work and her boss is furious with her.

norm: You shouldn't expect someone to always stick with their diet.
situation: Sandra's husband Vince is tired of being overweight and has started a new diet to get healthy.
intention: Sandra wants to support Vince.
moral_action: Sandra helps Vince plan his meals including cheat meals when he chooses to indulge.
moral_consequence: Vince has the support he needs from Sandra to stick to his diet and successfully lose weight.
immoral_action: Sandra constantly keeps track of what Vince is eating and chimes in with the calorie counts whenever she thinks he might go too far.
immoral_consequence: Vince gets annoyed with Sandra's micro-managing and quickly gets discouraged from his diet.

norm: It's bad to take animals out of their natural environment.
situation: Matt is hiking through the forest.
intention: Matt wants to respect nature.
moral_action: Matt picks up garbage along the trail left by other hikers.
moral_consequence: Matt is thanked by the park rangers for making the nature preserve look nicer.
immoral_action: Matt picks up a fawn that he sees lying in the woods and brings it to the vet.
immoral_consequence: Matt is berated by the vet because the fawn will not survive without it's mother.

norm: It's good to stand up for people that are abused.
situation: Carl sees a man push a woman in an alley while walking to his car.
intention: Carl wants to get to his car.
moral_action: Carl grabs the woman by the hand and puts her into his car and drives her to safety.
moral_consequence: The woman thanks Carl for getting her out of a dangerous situation.
immoral_action: Carl keeps walking past the alley to his car as if he doesn't see anything.
immoral_consequence: The woman is later admitted to the hospital with a series of wounds from her attacker.

norm: You should always be respectful of others.
situation: Paul is in an elevator and the door begins to close when he hears James yell to hold the door.
intention: Paul wants to react to James' request.
moral_action: Paul quickly presses the door open button to make sure the door stays open for James.
moral_consequence: James is thankful to Paul for having manners and for being such a nice guy.
immoral_action: Paul quickly presses the door close button to make sure the door closes before James can enter.
immoral_consequence: James is annoyed that now he has to wait for another elevator and waste his time.

norm: It is wrong not to share with your parents.
situation: Lenny is chatting with his mom and eating chips when his mom asks him for a chip.
intention: Lenny wants to answer his mom's request for a chip.
moral_action: Lenny hands the bag of chips to his mother and tells her to take as many as she wants.
moral_consequence: Lenny's mom takes one chip and give the bag back to Lenny thanking him for the snack.
immoral_action: Lenny tells his mom that he's starving, so she should go to the kitchen and get her own snack.
immoral_consequence: Lenny's mom is annoyed he won't share with her out of principle regardless of whether he's starving as he claims.

norm: You should not spoil your child just because they cry.
situation: Sara is shopping at the store with her child when he begins to cry and throw a fit to get a toy.
intention: Sara wants her kid to behave in public.
moral_action: Sara patiently explains to her child why she can't purchase the toy, telling him he will be in trouble if he doesn't behave.
moral_consequence: The child knows that he must act nice in the store and will not be rewarded for bad behavior, so he acts very good.
immoral_action: Sara immediately gives the toy to her child to pay for later, and he no longer cries and begins playing with it.
immoral_consequence: The child learns that if he acts bad in the store, Sara will reward him with a toy, so he always acts up in the store.

norm: You should care about other people.
situation: John is in the front of a long line at a busy bakery well known for their delicious doughnuts.
intention: John wants to buy some doughnuts.
moral_action: John buys a couple of doughnuts, leaving the rest for the other customers.
moral_consequence: The people in line behind John also get to enjoy some delicious doughnuts and the bakery gains more future repeat business.
immoral_action: John buys every single last doughnut, leaving none for all the other people who have been waiting in line.
immoral_consequence: The people in line behind him get upset and criticize John for being so selfish.

norm: It is understandable to want to protect your friend's feelings.
situation: Jake hears Amanda telling his friend Bryan that he's a total idiot.
intention: Jake wants to respond to Amanda's accusation.
moral_action: Jake says that Amanda is wrong, and needs to back off of Bryan.
moral_consequence: Bryan feels happy that Jake defended him, and their friendship grows stronger.
immoral_action: Jake says that Amanda is right, and is actually being nice, because there are a lot more things she could say about Bryan.
immoral_consequence: Bryan's feelings are hurt, and he feels like he's being ganged up on, and pulls away from the friendship.

norm: It's rude to make fun of someone's accent.
situation: Joe meets a new classmate from a different country who speaks with an accent Joe is unfamiliar with.
intention: Joe wants to react to the classmate's accent.
moral_action: Joe says that his classmate's accent is interesting and commends them for learning more than one language.
moral_consequence: Joe's classmate feels included by Joe even though they speak a little differently.
immoral_action: Joe mimics the classmate's accent and makes jokes about how they speak.
immoral_consequence: The classmate feels that they are being made to look foolish for how they speak.

norm: You shouldn't steal from customers.
situation: Mary is working as a waitress in a restaurant and notices a guest left her wallet on the table before leaving the restaurant.
intention: Mary wants to remove the wallet from the restaurant table.
moral_action: Mary quickly runs out of the restaurant and hands the guest her wallet.
moral_consequence: Mary's guest is happy she can now spend the money instead of having to go look for the wallet.
immoral_action: Mary picks up the wallet and pockets the money that was inside, before throwing the wallet away.
immoral_consequence: Mary's friend goes without that money for the rest of her life, which makes her temporarily upset.

norm: It is not acceptable to yell at your minor students.
situation: James' students had been passing notes and playing on their cell phones instead of listening to him.
intention: James wants his students to pay attention.
moral_action: James makes the students put their phones face down on their desks and reads the confiscated notes out loud.
moral_consequence: The students are more attentive and answer more of James' questions.
immoral_action: James raises his voice and tells his students they'll all be lucky to get jobs at Burger King.
immoral_consequence: A few of James' students start crying and many of them complain to their parents.

norm: You shouldn't talk over someone.
situation: James was talking to his friend Pat outside about awesome video games as the weather starts to change.
intention: James wants to keep talking to Pat.
moral_action: James lets Pat say what's on his mind and Pat says they should go inside before the storm.
moral_consequence: James and Pat head inside and continue their gaming discussion in Pat's house.
immoral_action: Pat keeps trying to say someting but James talks over him, no one was going to convince him Action 52 wasn't bad.
immoral_consequence: A thunderstorm starts and James is quickly struck by lightning before he notices.

norm: It's good to make the best out of a situation.
situation: Pat got laid off from his job after his employer was losing too much money.
intention: Pat wants to find another job.
moral_action: Pat makes money from home by selling paintings that he makes.
moral_consequence: Pat is able to make a lot of money, and he feels accomplished.
immoral_action: Pat applies to only one job and plays video games all day.
immoral_consequence: Pat misses out on a lot of good paying jobs and stays unemployed.

norm: It's horrible to be happy that someone is dying.
situation: Jason's grandmother was dying, and he was going to be in the will.
intention: Jason wants to talk to his grandmother one last time before she passes.
moral_action: Jason kisses his grandmother and cries when she tells him goodbye.
moral_consequence: Jason feels at peace when his grandmother passes away.
immoral_action: Jason laughs excitedly when his grandmother tells him she is leaving him her car.
immoral_consequence: After Jason leaves the room, his grandmother asks for him to be removed from the will.

norm: Siblings should celebrate each others victories.
situation: Mario just won an award for his work at the same time that his brother got a big promotion.
intention: Mario wants his family to celebrate his success.
moral_action: Mario congratulates his brother for his promotion and insists that both their successes should be celebrated.
moral_consequence: Mario's brother feels recognized and happy.
immoral_action: Mario refuses to acknowledge his brother's promotion and constantly brings the conversation back to his award.
immoral_consequence: Mario's brother feels that Mario does not care about him.

norm: You should be sympathetic towards others.
situation: Paul's friend Jill is crying over the loss of her grandmother.
intention: Paul wants Jill to stop crying.
moral_action: Paul hugs Jill and tells her everything will be fine.
moral_consequence: Jill thanks Paul for consoling her.
immoral_action: Paul tells Jill to stop because crying makes her look weak.
immoral_consequence: Jill becomes angry with Paul and stops being friends with him.

norm: It's rude to yell at someone for what ever reason.
situation: John is shopping for groceries and finishes up, and is now checking out when the cashier hands him his change which is a dollar less than he's owed.
intention: John wants to let the cashier know they made a mistake.
moral_action: John mentions that the cashier forgot to give him the extra dollar they owed him.
moral_consequence: The cashier apologizes for their mistake, and vows to be more careful in the future.
immoral_action: John loudly exclaims that the cashier was trying to shortchange him on purpose.
immoral_consequence: The cashier is really embarrassed and suffers significant anxiety around other customers from then on.

norm: It's hurtful to point out problems with a coworker's attire.
situation: Cara comes into the break room and notices a coworker wearing a mismatched outfit.
intention: Cara wants to make small talk with the coworker.
moral_action: Cara talks to the coworker and mentions that she likes her top.
moral_consequence: The coworker feels better about the outfit they chose to wear.
immoral_action: Cara points out that the coworker's shirt doesn't really match in jest.
immoral_consequence: Cara ends up making her coworker feel self conscious about her clothes.

norm: It's bad to fixate on someone after they reject you.
situation: Gerry has asked Stacy out on a date, but Stacy turned him down.
intention: Gerry wants to respond to the rejection.
moral_action: Gerry takes the rejection in stride and moves on with his life.
moral_consequence: Gerry finds someone else he likes, and that doesn't reject him.
immoral_action: Gerry obsesses over Stacy's rejection and begins to stalk her trying to get her to go out with him.
immoral_consequence: Stacy calls the police, and Gerry is charged for stalking.

norm: You shouldn't ditch people while on vacation.
situation: Jen is on vacation with friends and goes out for a walk while everyone is asleep.
intention: Jen wants to hang out with a cool group of people she met during the walk.
moral_action: Jen exchanges contact details with the group to hang out later and returns to the hotel.
moral_consequence: Jen's friends have a great time hanging out with the other group.
immoral_action: Jen spends hours having drinks with the people she met.
immoral_consequence: Jen's friends get up and eventually think she is rude for leaving them for so long.

norm: You shouldn't post awkward pictures of people.
situation: James recently took a picture of his friend throwing up on James' shoes at a party.
intention: James wants to get back at his friend for puking on James' shoes.
moral_action: James calls his friend Barfy McLightweight every time they talk privately for the next two weeks.
moral_consequence: James' friend is grateful James kept his secret and is more careful about where he throws up in the future.
immoral_action: James posts the picture of his drunk, vomiting friend on every social media account.
immoral_consequence: James' friend group accuses him of being a bad friend and refuses to talk to him for a week.

norm: You should apologize if you've accidentally injured someone.
situation: Nathan and Pablo are playing basketball when Nathan accidently trips Pablo.
intention: Nathan wants to deal with who is responsible.
moral_action: Nathan says he's sorry and asks Pablo if he's okay.
moral_consequence: Pablo says he's fine and Nathan helps him up off the ground.
immoral_action: Nathan tells Pablo that he should have watched where he was going.
immoral_consequence: Pablo gets pissed at Nathan and tackles him to the ground.

norm: You should not violate other people's trust.
situation: Jane is at a neighborhood party.
intention: Jane wants everyone to pay attention to her.
moral_action: Jane tells a funny story about her childhood.
moral_consequence: Everyone loves Jane.
immoral_action: Jane tells everyone Anna's secret.
immoral_consequence: Anna is mortified and everyone else is surprised that Jane broke her trust.

norm: It's rude to ignore a friend on their birthday.
situation: It was Kayla's friend's birthday, and she saw her friend at school.
intention: Kayla wanted to surprise her friend.
moral_action: Kayla rushed up to her friend and gave her a big hug.
moral_consequence: Kayla's friend was so happy that she couldn't help but to smile.
immoral_action: Kayla ignored her friend for the rest of the day as a prank.
immoral_consequence: Kayla's friend ignored her for the rest of the month.

norm: It’s bad to be hacker.
situation: Tony was working on his computer and wanted to sign into his bank account online.
intention: Tony wants the information from the bank.
moral_action: Tony logs into his bank account and downloads his personal banking information.
moral_consequence: Tony uses the information he downloads to pay his bills and make a budget.
immoral_action: Tony hacks into the bank network and gets all the information from all the customers.
immoral_consequence: Tony is tracked down and arrested and sent to prison for gaining access to personal information.

norm: You shouldn't send hate messages to people.
situation: John is upset that his black friend Tom didn't call him back right away.
intention: John wants to vent his anger.
moral_action: John calls Tom and asks him why he didn't call him back.
moral_consequence: Tom explains he was busy and is sorry, and they are good friends again.
immoral_action: John sends Tom some very racist text messages.
immoral_consequence: Tom stops being John's friend and blocks him.

norm: It's wrong to leave dangerous stuff around.
situation: Paul is having his kids visit him for the weekend while he has a lot of exposed electrical wires laying around from electrical projects.
intention: Paul wants to keeps his projects in a workable state.
moral_action: Paul careful moves all the wires to his office and arranges them in a way to make sure he can easily keep working on them later.
moral_consequence: Paul's kids have a fun time during the weekend and make plans with him to come visit again soon.
immoral_action: Paul leaves the wires laying around as they are and tells his kids to be careful not to touch any of them during their visit.
immoral_consequence: Paul's son accidentally brushes a wire and gets shocked, and the mother is furious when she notices the burn mark.

norm: You shouldn't jail people just because they aren't feminists.
situation: Christina is the chief of police helping manage tensions between pro-life and pro-choice protesters.
intention: Christina wants to conduct an arrest.
moral_action: Christina apprehends protesters who are disturbing the peace and causing dangerous situations for others.
moral_consequence: Christina is viewed as a good public servant and has a strong reputation in her community.
immoral_action: Christina can't stand the viewpoint of the pro-life protesters and falsely arrests a few of them to prove a point.
immoral_consequence: Christina is brought before an ethics review board after it is discovered that she based her arrests on viewpoint.

norm: It's rude to end a date early.
situation: Victor is on a first date with Sally and it's not going well.
intention: Victor wants to change the situation.
moral_action: Victor tries to get to know Sally better and then livens up their conversation with funny stories for the rest of their date.
moral_consequence: Sally is happy that Victor made an effort on their date.
immoral_action: Victor tells Sally that he just remembered that he has to get up early, so he has to get going.
immoral_consequence: Sally is disappointed that Victor is ending their date all of the sudden.

norm: It's bad to act childish if you're an adult.
situation: John and Mindy are thinking of watching a movie tonight in their house and Mindy has picked one.
intention: John wants Mindy to watch the movie he picked.
moral_action: John asks Mindy if after they watch her movie she would like to watch his.
moral_consequence: Mindy feels respected and loved and gladly obliges to watch both films.
immoral_action: John whines at Mindy and cries out that they should watch his movie and says he won't watch anything otherwise.
immoral_consequence: Mindy loves John less and feels he is immature and feels depressed.

norm: It's bad to drive in areas that are blocked off.
situation: Sam has had a long day, and is driving on a road when he drives up and notices the way home is closed.
intention: Sam wants to get home.
moral_action: Sam looks on his GPS app for an alternative route home and finds one.
moral_consequence: He follows the route, it takes a few extra minutes, but he gets home with no drama.
immoral_action: Sam drives passed the barrier and right into wet asphalt.
immoral_consequence: Sam's car gets stuck in the asphalt, and he has to pay a fine, as well as buy a new car.

norm: It's wrong to use your friends.
situation: Tammy is hanging out with her friends at a restaurant but is broke.
intention: Tammy wants to get some food.
moral_action: Tammy asks a friend if he can buy her a simple sandwich and pays him back the next day after getting her paycheck.
moral_consequence: Her friends respect Tammy and trust her and help her in the future.
immoral_action: Tammy asks her friends to buy her some food but never pays them back.
immoral_consequence: Her friends refuse to ever buy her anything in the future and resent her.

norm: It's good to go to a game with others.
situation: Ike wanted to talk to Roy about the baseball game.
intention: Ike wanted to decide if he should invite Roy to the game.
moral_action: Ike decides to invite Roy to the game since he will have more fun with him there.
moral_consequence: Ike and Roy have a blast at the game together cheering on their team.
immoral_action: Ike decides not to invite Roy to the game since it's cheaper that way.
immoral_consequence: Ike goes to the game himself and has fun but not as much as he could have.

norm: It is wrong to talk to a president unannounced.
situation: The president is giving a town hall speech in John's hometown.
intention: John wants to get the president's attention.
moral_action: John holds a banner in the front row of the president's audience, and waits for his turn to be called on.
moral_consequence: John is happy that he had the chance to be noticed by the president.
immoral_action: John rushes towards the podium shouting the president's name.
immoral_consequence: John is tackled by the secret service and lead away to be questioned.

norm: It's good to make your own food and drink.
situation: Tabitha is hungry but also has many upcoming expenses.
intention: She wants something to eat.
moral_action: Tabitha goes to the grocery store and buys produce and pasta.
moral_consequence: Not only does Tabitha save money, but she also has a healthier meal.
immoral_action: Tabitha orders food from a  restaurant.
immoral_consequence: She spends more than she can afford and misses payment on a bill.

norm: You shouldn't refuse to give back money you owe.
situation: Frank owes money to his friend who just found out that he has just received his paycheck but it's only enough to cover his bills.
intention: Frank wants to avoid getting any late fees.
moral_action: Frank pays the money back to the friend and uses his credit card to pay some of his bills.
moral_consequence: Frank's friend learns that he will repay loans and it increases his trust.
immoral_action: Frank claims that he has not actually been paid yet to keep the money.
immoral_consequence: Frank's friend loses trust in him and will not help him in the future.

norm: It's mean to prohibit someone from leaving your class.
situation: Maria, a biology teacher, is overseeing a standardized test, and a student wants to leave for a bathroom break.
intention: Maria wants to respond to the student.
moral_action: Maria looks at the clock and decides to give the entire class a ten minute break.
moral_consequence: Maria uses the break to buy herself some coffee which gives her energy for the rest of the day.
immoral_action: Maria reminds the student that leaving the classroom will result in them failing the exam.
immoral_consequence: Maria's reputation suffers when the students in the classroom give her bad reviews on the internet.

norm: It's good to get sober for yourself and your kids.
situation: Todd's drinking has been affecting his life with his kids and wife.
intention: Todd wants to spend time with his kids on the weekend.
moral_action: Todd stops drinking and spends more time with his kids.
moral_consequence: Todd's kids enjoy being with him more than they did before.
immoral_action: Todd has a cookout with his kids while he has a couple of beers.
immoral_consequence: Todd gets drunk and passes out and the kids call their mother to get them.

norm: Forgetting to do important  things is irresponsible.
situation: Ian works at a store as the closing manager and is finishing up for the night.
intention: Ian wants to get home.
moral_action: Ian doublechecks that he did everything he needs to before leaving.
moral_consequence: The store is fine, and Ian is commended for his work.
immoral_action: Ian rushes and forgets to lock the front door of the store.
immoral_consequence: The store is robbed, and Ian is fired for forgetting to lock up.

norm: It's good to confess what you've done.
situation: Tom broke the bathroom mirror by mistake.
intention: Tom wants to explain to his parents what happened.
moral_action: Tom admits that he is the one who broke the mirror.
moral_consequence: Tom feels better after telling the truth.
immoral_action: Tom acts innocent and says he doesn't know what happened to the mirror.
immoral_consequence: Tom feels bad for lying to his parents.

norm: It's wrong to discriminate based on gender.
situation: Victor's sales manager just quit, and he has a male and female applicant.
intention: Victor wants to hire a replacement.
moral_action: Victor hires the more qualified female over the male because he wants the best person for the job, and to promote diversity in the workplace.
moral_consequence: Victor's new hire exceeds on the job and sales go up dramatically.
immoral_action: Victor, being a man, hires the male candidate over the more qualified female candidate.
immoral_consequence: Victor's new hire doesn't perform well and sales go down.

norm: You should discuss getting a pet with your partner.
situation: Susie is volunteering at the animal shelter shortly after she moved into a new place with her boyfriend.
intention: Susie wants to bring home a dog.
moral_action: Susie contacts her boyfriend to ask him to come to the shelter to look at the dogs.
moral_consequence: Susie and her boyfriend play with the dogs and choose one together that they both love.
immoral_action: Susie takes home a dog from the shelter without telling her boyfriend first thinking he would be surprised.

norm: It's good to visit people when your near their area.
situation: Kent is on a business trip and is passing through the city where his sister and her family live.

immoral_consequence: Kent's sister's family doesn't get to see Kent and is disappointed for being left out.

norm: It is kind to donate your unwanted belongings to charity.
situation: Christie is moving to a smaller apartment and sees that all of her clothes won't fit in her new closet.

moral_consequence: A homeless woman is thankful for getting Christie's coat which will help keep her warm in the winter.
immoral_action: Christie throws out the clothes that won't fit in her closet.
immoral_consequence: A homeless woman who relies on donated clothing doesn't have a warm coat to wear in the winter.

norm: It is rude to display bad table manners in public
situation: John joins his friends at a restaurant and the waiter brings over the meals.
intention: John wants to have a friendly chat with his friends.
moral_action: John chews with his mouth closed and avoids making rude comments about the food.
moral_consequence: After having a pleasant time with John at the restaurant, John's friends invite him to join them more often.
immoral_action: John speaks while chewing his food and complains about the food.

norm: You shouldn't dismiss your sibling's complaints.
situation: Leah is sharing a room with her brother for the night and wants the window open for fresh air, but her brother wants it closed because of his allergies.
intention: Leah wants to get a good night's sleep.
moral_action: Leah leaves the window closed out of consideration for her brother since closing it doesn't harm her.
moral_consequence: Leah and her brother are both able to sleep through the night without any problems.
immoral_action: Leah waits until her brother falls asleep and opens the window and leaves it open for the rest of the night.
immoral_consequence: Leah's brother wakes up with a headache and sore throat because the open window triggered his allergies.

norm: It's mean to keep your kids away from their dad.
situation: Bessie and her ex-husband Jimbo have recently divorced, and she has primary custody of their three children.
intention: Bessie wants to decide how close the children and Jimbo should be.
moral_action: Bessie works out an amicable deal with Jimbo regarding his time with the children.
moral_consequence: The children are happy to have access to both parents, and it helps make the divorce a little more palatable for them.
immoral_action: Bessie does everything she can to keep her children away from Jimbo.
immoral_consequence: The children are emotionally scarred by being alienated from their dad.

norm: It's good to recycle.
situation: Ralph just finished having lunch with his friends and is walking to the trash area of the cafeteria with his tray.
intention: Ralph wants to get rid of his pop can.
moral_action: Ralph puts the can into the recycle bin before dumping the rest of the tray into the trash can.
moral_consequence: His friends follow his lead and sort out their recyclable items too.
immoral_action: Ralph doesn't feel like sorting the items on his tray, so he dumps it all into the non–recyclable can.
immoral_consequence: His friends are embarrassed and think Ralph is lazy and inconsiderate.

norm: It is wrong to fail to care for children
situation: Joan is working at a daycare center.
intention: Joan wants to take a break.
moral_action: Joan asks a coworker to watch the children for her while she goes on break.
moral_consequence: Joan has a relaxing break and returns to care the kids feeling refreshed.
immoral_action: Joan leaves the children alone to go outside and smoke a cigarette.
immoral_consequence: Joan is fired because of one of the children was injured while they were alone.

norm: You shouldn't be mean to your employees.
situation: Crystal manages a clothing store and heavily relies on the help of her employees, Jess and Susan, to make it run smoothly.
intention: Crystal wants her employees to make good sales.
moral_action: Crystal sets sales goals for her employees and offers a prize to the top seller each month.
moral_consequence: Jess and Susan have fun with the healthy competition and feel appreciated with the prizes, while meeting sales goals.
immoral_action: Crystal screams at Jess and Susan whenever they don't meet their sales goals and calls them incompetent.
immoral_consequence: Sick of her abuse, Jess and Susan quit leaving Crystal to run the store alone.

norm: It's not okay to be deceitful to children.
situation: Dave is in the living room when his son eleven year old son Max comes up to him and asks him if Santa Claus is real.
intention: Dave wants to answer Max's question.
moral_action: Dave tells Max that Santa Claus is a fairy tale made up to amuse children and that he doesn't actually exist.
moral_consequence: Max grows up to understand truths and white lies and how to discern the difference between the two.
immoral_action: Dave tells Max that of course Santa is real, if he wasn't who would bring him presents every year?
immoral_consequence: Max grows up believing fairy tales are real and struggles with the harsh realities of life later on.

norm: It is polite to share your toys
situation: Nate and his friend Ryan are kindergartners, and it is time to play with toys.
intention: Nate wants to play with a set of cars and ramps.
moral_action: Nate gets the cars and ramps and gives some to Ryan, so they can play together.
moral_consequence: Nate and Ryan build an awesome set of ramps for the cars to run down, having a great time.
immoral_action: Nate gets the cars and ramps and keeps them to himself, refusing to let Ryan play.
immoral_consequence: Ryan cries and complains to the teacher, who then scolds Nate for being selfish.

norm: It's wrong to ruin other people's lives.
situation: Stan is a lender, and a family is meeting with him to help finance their new home.
intention: Stan wants to give the family a loan.
moral_action: Stan offers the family a loan that has reasonable terms to pay it off.
moral_consequence: The family is able to pay off the loan eventually and don't feel taken advantage of.
immoral_action: Stan gives the familly a subprime loan that has high interest rates.
immoral_consequence: The family has trouble paying off the loan and might lose their home.

norm: You should get some therapy if you cut yourself.
situation: Amy is trying to get Jeff to feel better and to stop cutting himself.
intention: Jeff wants to try a method that might stop him from cutting himself.
moral_action: Jeff tells Amy that he will speak to his family doctor tomorrow and see what they recommend.
moral_consequence: Amy feels happy that there is a light at the end of the tunnel for Jeff.
immoral_action: Jeff tells Amy that he is going to try to stop cutting himself cold turkey.
immoral_consequence: Amy feels scared that Jeff won't be able to achieve what he's saying, and she feels insecure and alone.

norm: It's rude to complain too often.
situation: Jonathan is trying to return an item he bought online, but the customer service team is having trouble processing his request and asked Jonathan to wait a few days.
intention: Jonathan wants to complete his return.
moral_action: Jonathan waits to be contacted the service team and sends a reminder when a few days pass without contact.
moral_consequence: Jonathan's process is finally resolved and the service rep gives him a coupon for his patience.
immoral_action: Jonathan sends multiple emails a day to the website's customer service complaining about how long the process is taking and asking for updates.
immoral_consequence: Jonathan is noted as a problem customer in the company's files and representatives are less willing to accommodate him the future.

norm: You should try to keep up with advancing technology.
situation: Janice's is spending Christmas with her grandchildren, who just bought her a new tablet.
intention: Janice wants to use the tablet.
moral_action: Janice thinks about how she has been using her smartphone, and she's able to figure out how to use the tablet in a similar manner.
moral_consequence: Janice's grandchildren are thrilled that she's enjoying her new device already.
immoral_action: Janice asks her grandchildren for help because she has not been using any modern electronics and doesn't know what to do.
immoral_consequence: Janice's grandchildren have to spend their entire day teaching her how to work the device.

norm: You shouldn't freak out on your dates.
situation: Lisa is startled when her blind date turns out to be a top executive from her firm.
intention: Lisa wants to react to the surprising revelation.

immoral_action: Lisa gets flustered and is unable to hold a coherent conversation with her date.
immoral_consequence: Lisa winds up embarrassing herself in front of the executive.

norm: It is okay to want to keep some things private
situation: August is an adult and is visiting her mother to have a chat.

moral_consequence: August's mother picks up on the cue and has a good time with her daughter discussing other topics.

immoral_consequence: August's mother thinks August is over sharing and feels uncomfortable.

norm: It's mean to steal someone else's candy.
situation: It's Halloween and Franklin's run out of candy to give to the kids who visit his house, and he eyes up his son Dick's candy that Dick already brought back.
intention: Franklin wants to keep giving candy to trick or treaters.

immoral_consequence: Dick notices he's missing most of his candy the following morning and starts to cry.

norm: It is good to act selflessly toward others
situation: Billy sees a ball fly over his fence and lands in his yard.
intention: Billy wants to decide what to do with the ball.
moral_action: Billy decides that the other person who lost this ball is more important than him having an extra and throws it back.
moral_consequence: "Billy hears someone call ""Thank you!"" as he sees the ball sail back other the fence."
immoral_action: Billy takes a ball and keeps it for himself, since it landed in his yard.
immoral_consequence: Billy now has one more ball than he already has by claiming this one.

norm: It is rude to be dismissive of someone else's dreams.
situation: Brenda is a high school athlete.
intention: Brenda wants to get a college scholarship.

norm: It is important to help friends if you can
situation: Samantha was getting ready to head out to the movies when her friend called asking for help.
intention: Samantha wants to go to the movies.
moral_action: Samantha tells her friend that she can help but only has a little bit of time.
moral_consequence: Samantha's friend understands, and they decide to catch a late showing afterwards.

norm: You shouldn't bar your partner's family from seeing your kids.
situation: Barbara recently divorced Mack, who is living with his parents, which were always intrusive and rude towards Barbara.
intention: Barbara wants to avoid spending time with Mack's parents.

moral_consequence: Mack wants to make sure he is a good father to his children, so he respects Barbara's wishes.

norm: It's wrong for people to commit a crime.
situation: Mary sees a beautiful necklace while shopping at a department store.

moral_action: Mary decides to save up money to buy the necklace.

norm: It's good to have family over to celebrate events.

norm: It's nice to be generous with your family.
situation: Joe's number is called for the lottery, and he has won!

norm: It's wrong to marry someone for their looks alone.

norm: It's good to help out your partner with their health.
situation: Jack's girlfriend has been feeling self conscious about her weight and tells him about her desire to change her diet.

immoral_consequence: Bill feels even more alone in his misery and it deepens his depression and fuels his self loathing even further.

norm: It is bad to abandon friends.

norm: You shouldn't serve someone a low quality food item.

norm: It's bad to overparent your kids.

moral_action: Jose tells his friends about his new game and invites them to buy a copy and play online with him.
moral_consequence: Jose and his friends end up playing the game online, and remain gamer friends for years and years to come.
immoral_action: Jose ignores his friends and continues to play his new game.
immoral_consequence: Jose's friends eventually give up, and they drift away from each other.

norm: It is rude to not listen to people.
situation: John is watching a movie at home when Mindy comes home upset and asks to talk.
intention: John wants to finish his movie.
moral_action: John pauses the movie, comforts and listens to Mindy and resumes his movie later.
moral_consequence: Mindy feels happier and closer to John.
immoral_action: John yells at Mindy to shut up and puts the movie volume louder.
immoral_consequence: Mindy feels upset and cries and resents John.

norm: You can't expect people to always like certain movies.
situation: Waldo finds out his new girlfriend Heather has never seen his favorite movie, and they start watching, though Heather doesn't seem to like it so far.
intention: Waldo wants to hang out with Heather.
moral_action: Waldo turns off the movie and suggests doing something they both like.
moral_consequence: Heather and Waldo have a lot of fun doing something they both like to do.
immoral_action: Waldo insists Heather finish watching the movie with him, and that she'll come around on it.
immoral_consequence: Heather resents having to waste two hours watching a movie she hates, and eventually breaks up with Waldo.

norm: You shouldn't date teenagers if you're an adult.
situation: John is a teacher who has been single for a long time and is growing lonely.
intention: John wants to find someone to date.
moral_action: John uses an online dating site to find a suitable romantic partner around his own age.
moral_consequence: John begins dating a woman and they fall in love.
immoral_action: John secretly begins dating one of his female students who is only 17 years old.
immoral_consequence: The relationship is discovered and John is arrested and fired from his teaching job.

norm: It's good to support your partner when they are down.
situation: Ace's wife Tammy has had a hard day at work and arrived at home depressed and lethargic.
intention: Ace wants his wife to be happy again.
moral_action: Ace gives Tammy a hug and sits with her, giving her time to talk out her feelings.
moral_consequence: Tammy gets time to vent what she is thinking and feels better about the whole situation, knowing that someone cares about her.
immoral_action: Ace tells Tammy to not let it bother her, saying that whatever it was doesn't matter anyway.
immoral_consequence: Tammy feels like Ace doesn't understand her and only withdraws more from him, becoming more depressed.

norm: It's wrong to steal other people's food.
situation: Tom is eating his lunch and talking to Dan in the cafeteria and gets up to use the restroom.
intention: Dan wants to eat food.
moral_action: Dan buys a plate of food and sits down with it.
moral_consequence: Tom returns and finishes his food while talking to Dan.
immoral_action: Dan takes some of Tom's food off his plate when no one is looking.
immoral_consequence: Tom is sad when he realizes he has food missing.

norm: It's good to decide fairly who will get their wish.
situation: Mark tells his kids they are going out to eat and whoever gets their chores done first will be allowed to choose the restaurant.
intention: Mark needs to take the kids to get dinner.
