moral_action: Mark lets his younger daughter choose because she finished first, and they head to Olive Garden.
moral_consequence: Everyone is happy that they did their work and go to go out to eat.
immoral_action: Mark let's his older daughter pick the restaurant even though she didn't finish her chores, because she is smarter.
immoral_consequence: His younger daughter is furious that her dad treated her unfairly.

norm: It's wrong to tell secrets to your friend's partner.
situation: Jenna sees her friend Alanna smoking, even though she reluctantly promised her boyfriend she'd quit smoking.
intention: Jenna wants to help her friend.
moral_action: Jenna tells Alanna she knows she's been really stressed lately, and she (Jenna) won't tell Alanna's boyfriend.
moral_consequence: Alanna hugs Jenna and thanks her for being so understanding about this.
immoral_action: Jenna tells Alanna's boyfriend in the name of improving her health.
immoral_consequence: Alanna trusts Jenna less and stops telling her anything really personal.

norm: It's bad to beat someone up for being different.
situation: There is a new foreign exchange student at Kevin's school, and he doesn't speak much English.
intention: Kevin needs to show the student where classes are.
moral_action: Kevin shows the student around and tries to help him understand English better.
moral_consequence: The new student and Kevin become good friends.
immoral_action: Kevin is showing the new student around and, frustrated by his lack of English skills, smacks him in the mouth.
immoral_consequence: The student is hurt and Kevin is suspended from school.

norm: It's wrong to give up on school.
situation: Maya is in 11th grade and just found out she is pregnant with her first child.
intention: Maya wants to decide whether or not to drop out.
moral_action: Maya, wanting to be a good parent, signs up for homeschooling, so she can further her education and focus on being a new mom at the same time.
moral_consequence: After the baby is born, Maya has a good job and can afford all the necessities needed to care for her child.
immoral_action: Maya, wanting to focus on preparing to be a new mom, quits attending classes.
immoral_consequence: After the baby is born, Maya is unable to find decent employment and struggles to take care of her child.

norm: It's wrong to be rude to disabled people.
situation: Roy is standing in line and a man in a wheelchair cuts in line in front of him.
intention: Roy wants him to go to the back of the line.
moral_action: "Roy tells him ""hey, that isn't the back of the line"" and points to the back instead."
moral_consequence: The man apologizes and heads to the actual back of the line.
immoral_action: Roy tells him to get out of line because this line is only for STANDING in.
immoral_consequence: The man in the chair rolls to the back but Roy gets nasty looks from the line.

norm: It's good to spend time somewhere with your family.
situation: Carl has a family but is at work which he takes very seriously.
intention: Carl wants to be successful in life.
moral_action: Carl puts in for some well earned time off to spend with his family because he views them as his greatest accomplishment.
moral_consequence: Carl's family enjoys the time he gets off to spend with them and Carl feels content.
immoral_action: Carl stays at work after hours to put in the extra effort that he hopes will advance his career.
immoral_consequence: Carl's family misses him at home, and he becomes more distant by prioritizing work over them.

norm: It's good to go after your dreams.
situation: Sonia always wanted to be a musician, but she's making a lot of money as a financial analyst.
intention: Sonia wants to reassess her employment situation.
moral_action: Sonia decides to resign as an analyst and starts releasing songs on SoundCloud.
moral_consequence: Sonia becomes happier and starts feeling more fulfilled in life.
immoral_action: Sonia decides to stay in her job as a financial analyst.
immoral_consequence: Sonia continues to hate her work and realizes that money doesn't make her happy.

norm: It's frowned upon to get an F on an assignment.
situation: Ginny has a big test at school tomorrow that she hasn't studied for yet, but she wants to go out to play.
intention: Ginny wants show up for the exam.
moral_action: Ginny decides to have a cram study session instead of playing, then takes the test.
moral_consequence: Ginny gets a passing grade and learns next time to study earlier.
immoral_action: Ginny decides to not go over her notes and plays outside instead, and then takes the test.
immoral_consequence: Ginny ends up failing the exam and regrets not studying.

norm: It's nasty to watch someone else go to the bathroom.
situation: Margaret was on a date with Jesse at his house when he left to go to the restroom.
intention: Margaret wants to ask Jesse a question.
moral_action: Margaret sits at the table and waits for Jesse to return to continue their conversation.
moral_consequence: Jesse answers all of Margaret's questions when he gets back from using the restroom.
immoral_action: Margaret follows Jesse into the bathroom to continue talking to him.
immoral_consequence: Jesse asks Margaret to leave and ends the date early because he is creeped out.

norm: Is it wrong to cheat on your significant other
situation: Jaime has been married to Alyssa for three years, but Alyssa has been so busy with business trips that Jaime has started to feel lonely.
intention: Jaime wants to feel loved.
moral_action: Jaime talks to Alyssa about how he's feeling after she returned from a business trip.
moral_consequence: The two talk about their concerns and plan a long vacation together in a tropical island.
immoral_action: Jaime starts sleeping with a coworker while Alyssa is away in her business trips.
immoral_consequence: Alyssa finds out about Jaime's relationship with his coworker and the two get divorced.

norm: It's rude to ask a stranger for money.
situation: Derrick is at the mall shopping for video games but the one he wants is out of his price range.
intention: Derrick wants to be able to get the game.
moral_action: Derrick knows that he has to save longer and work more to be able to afford the game and does just that.
moral_consequence: Derrick helps others through hired labor and is able to eventually return and purchase the game.
immoral_action: Derrick begins asking other mall shoppers for any spare money they may have in hopes he gather the difference he needs.
immoral_consequence: Mall shoppers are annoyed by Derricks expectations of free handouts and mall security eventually asks him to leave.

norm: It's good to hold fundraisers.
situation: James' company recently went through an accounting scandal that was very damaging to their brand.
intention: James wants to rehabilitate his company's band.
moral_action: James has his company sponsor a fundraiser collecting money for cancer research.
moral_consequence: A new survey of potential customers reveals more of them have heard of the fundraiser than the accounting issues.
immoral_action: James runs ads exposing the inefficiency of his competitors' charitable efforts to make his company look better by comparison.
immoral_consequence: James' competitors respond by running ads criticizing his company's behavior.

norm: It's wrong to walk out on your job.
situation: James came to work at WalMart with a terrible headache and was shouted at by three customers before lunch.
intention: James wants a break from the screaming customers.
moral_action: James tells his manager that he's going to lose his mind unless he gets some peace and quiet.
moral_consequence: The manager transfers James to stocking inventory in the deserted back room for a few hours.
immoral_action: James rips off his name tag, throws it at the bellowing customer, and storms out the door.
immoral_consequence: James is blacklisted at that store and by several other employers who know the owner.

norm: It's irresponsible to abandon another person.
situation: Matt and Cindy are driving when their car breaks down in a shady part of town.
intention: Matt wants to get help.
moral_action: Matt and Cindy leave the car to find help nearby.
moral_consequence: Matt and Cindy get to a phone and are both safe.
immoral_action: Matt leaves Cindy with the car and goes to find a store to use a phone.
immoral_consequence: Cindy gets attacked and robbed while Matt is away.

norm: You shouldn't discriminate against people based on their height.
situation: Maria is looking at profiles of men on a dating site.
intention: Maria wants to pick a date.
moral_action: Maria considers numerous factors that focus on compatability.
moral_consequence: Maria may find a date that she will have lots of fun with.
immoral_action: Maria only considers tall people as potential dates.
immoral_consequence: Maria may miss out on someone that has other qualities she would like.

norm: You shouldn't get in someone's way.
situation: Sam is on the interstate and there is a lot of traffic.
intention: Sam needs to turn off to the next exit.
moral_action: Sam looks carefully, letting a car drive passed before going into the exit lane.
moral_consequence: Sam makes the exit with plenty of time to spare.
immoral_action: Sam sees the exit coming up and swiftly cuts across into the exit lane.
immoral_consequence: Sam doesn't see the car behind him, and it slams into him.

norm: It's frowned upon to spread conspiracy theories.
situation: Kyle hears a friend at school strongly defending their opinion that the Earth is flat.
intention: Kyle wants to gain his friend's approval.
moral_action: Kyle looks up information online and has a civil conversation with his friend about what he read.
moral_consequence: Kyle is able to convince his friend that his information makes sense and his friend sees him as smart.
immoral_action: Kyle decides to tell others that the Earth is flat when his friend is around and uses his friend's arguments when doing so.
immoral_consequence: Kyle starts to gain a reputation at school for spreading untrustworthy information.

norm: It is good to go to job interviews.
situation: James felt very depressed after he lost his job during a recession.
intention: James wants to improve his financial situation.
moral_action: James went to several job interviews even when he doubted he'd get the job.
moral_consequence: After several failures, James finally found a new position with a similar salary.
immoral_action: James rejected a friend's invitation to a job interview in favor of begging on street corners.
immoral_consequence: James made just enough money to pay for food and his half of the rent.

norm: It is wrong to create suspicion in a relationship.
situation: Joe works late on his job a few times a week causing his wife Beck to be concerned.
intention: Joe wants to avoid having Becky accuse him of an affair.
moral_action: Joe proactively explains why his work required more how and calls Becky whenever he works late.
moral_consequence: Becky understands and Joe eventually get better working hours again.
immoral_action: Joe says it's none of her business and never returns her calls when he is working late.
immoral_consequence: Becky suspects an affair and threaten to leave if he does not stop working late.

norm: You shouldn't disturb your roommate.
situation: Kelly's college roommate Nadia has a big test, but Kelly has free time.
intention: Kelly wants to listen to music.
moral_action: Kelly listens to music on her headphones.
moral_consequence: Nadia will not hear the music and will be able to study.
immoral_action: Kelly listens to music on her speakers.
immoral_consequence: Nadia will be distracted and won't be able to study.

norm: It's good to visit your partner for a holiday.
situation: Fred and his partner are both off for holiday break, and they are in a long distance relationship.
intention: Fred wants to surprise his partner for the holidays.
moral_action: Fred shows up at his partner's place to celebrate the holidays.
moral_consequence: Fred's partner is pleasantly surprised and has good company during the break.
immoral_action: Fred sends his partner an unexpected gift.
immoral_consequence: Fred's partner likes the gift but is forced to spend the holidays alone.

norm: It's wrong to belittle a victim of abuse.
situation: John is at home when Mindy brings her sister Annette over to the house who has just come from a battered women's shelter.
intention: John wants to feel good about himself.
moral_action: John asks how Annette is doing and comforts her and offers her some food.
moral_consequence: Annette is grateful and happy and grows fond of John.
immoral_action: John tells Annette that she probably deserved the battering she got.
immoral_consequence: Annette breaks down crying and resents John a lot.

norm: It is wrong to perform pranks on unsuspecting people.
situation: Jon has thought of a creative prank inspired by a youtube video he watched.
intention: Jon wants to use the prank on someone.
moral_action: Jon invites Jenny to pull the prank on their friend Tim who is always engaging in this kind of behavior.
moral_consequence: Tim is surprised by the prank but somewhat expected it because of their behavior and appreciates the effort.
immoral_action: Jon pranks his friend Jenny, who would never expect such a thing.
immoral_consequence: Jenny is terrified by the prank and is very upset with Jon.

norm: You shouldn't take someone's credit card.
situation: Will is at the store, but isn't sure he has enough money for the things he wants to buy, when he spots a lost credit card on the floor.
intention: Will wants to buy what he can from the store.
moral_action: Will turns the credit card into the lost and found and buys what he can with the money he has.
moral_consequence: Will gets what he can from the store, and the credit card owner gets their card back.
immoral_action: Will uses the credit card to buy the things he wants.
immoral_consequence: The credit card is reported stolen, and it is traced back to Will, who is arrested.

norm: It's dishonest to keep something you found
situation: Ann notices a man dropping his wallet in front of her in a street.
intention: Ann wants to return the wallet to the man.
moral_action: Ann runs to the man and return the wallet to him.
moral_consequence: The man thanks Ann for returning the wallet and feels very appreciated.
immoral_action: Ann pockets the cash inside the wallet and takes the wallet to the police.
immoral_consequence: The man loses the money which he needs for paying rent.

norm: It's wise for children to listen to their parent's advice.
situation: Norma is going to a party and her parents tell her not to drive back home if she's had too much to drink.
intention: Norma wants to have a good time at the party.
moral_action: Norma drinks more than she should and decides to take a cab back home.
moral_consequence: Norma safely makes it back home.
immoral_action: Norma gets drunk and decides to drive back home.
immoral_consequence: Norma crashes her car in a tree.

norm: It's bad to buy a car you can't afford
situation: Christian drives an old car and is sick of his coworkers making fun of him for it.
intention: Christian wants to buy a new car.
moral_action: Christian purchases a mid-range car with monthly payments that are within his budget.
moral_consequence: Christian's coworkers stop teasing him about his car.
immoral_action: Christian purchases a top-of-the-line car that is out of his price range.
immoral_consequence: Unable to keep up with the high payments, Christian's new car is reposessed.

norm: You should always tell your boss important things.
situation: Scott found a bug in the code for a project at work shortly before a deadline.
intention: Scott doesn't want to stress out his boss.
moral_action: Scott explains to his boss immediately what the bug is and requests help to make sure it is fixed in time.
moral_consequence: The boss is able to help Scott get the necessary help to get the bug fixed by the deadline.
immoral_action: Scott hides the fact that there is a bug from his boss and tries to fix it before anyone finds out.
immoral_consequence: The bug doesn't get fixed on time and the boss and client get very upset.

norm: You should always ask before you pick up someone's baby.
situation: Cindy saw a cute baby with it's parents in a grocery store.
intention: Cindy wants to pick up the baby.
moral_action: Cindy walks over to the parents and asks to pick up the baby.
moral_consequence: The parents let her, and she hugs the baby for a minute or so.
immoral_action: Cindy just walks over to the baby and picks it up.
immoral_consequence: Cindy finds herself explaining to annoyed police officers that she wasn't kidnapping the baby.

norm: It's atrocious to cut off someone's hair without their permission.
situation: Amy and Sue are sitting beside each other in class listening to a story being read.
intention: Amy wants to convince Sue to have short hair.
moral_action: Amy writes a note to Sue drawing the hairstyle she thinks she should get and sneaks it to her.
moral_consequence: Sue thinks the picture is cute and says she will ask her mom if she can get it.
immoral_action: Amy sneaks a pair of scissors from her bag and cuts one of Sue's pigtails off.
immoral_consequence: Sue screams and cries, interrupting the story, and never wants to talk to Amy again.

norm: It is wrong to steal from your brother.
situation: Dave is in his brother's bedroom where his brother John keeps cash openly and Dave wants to raise money for his favorite charity.
intention: Dave wants to decide in which way he will raise money.
moral_action: Dave decides that he will call his brother and some other friends and ask them if they're willing to donate.
moral_consequence: John and the others are delighted that Dave is including them in his charity drive.
immoral_action: Dave decides that he will take the cash that is sitting in john's bedroom and give it to the charity.
immoral_consequence: John finds his cash missing and is stressed out wondering who took it and feeling insecure and violated.

norm: You shouldn't put down others.
situation: Greg and Zach are high school students who are both interested in the same girl, Tammy.
intention: Greg wants to win Tammy's affection.
moral_action: Greg dresses nicely at school acts kindly towards Tammy whenever he has a chance.
moral_consequence: Tammy is impressed by Greg and agrees to go out on a date with him.
immoral_action: Whenever Greg talks to Tammy, he makes sure to mention Zach’s flaws and make himself look better by comparison.
immoral_consequence: Tammy doesn't like the way Greg behaves and decides to date Zach.

norm: You should not call women pet names.
situation: Joseph recently hired Anne to be his secretary and has some work for her to get done.
intention: Joseph wants to get Anne's attention to hand her the work.
moral_action: Joseph texts Anne a basic message asking her to come grab some work to do.
moral_consequence: Anne gets up and grabs the assignments she has from Joseph's desk.
immoral_action: "Joseph calls from across the office to Anne, saying ""Can you come pick this work up babe?""."
immoral_consequence: Anne is creeped out by Joseph and reports him to the HR department of the company.

norm: You shouldn't joke about having an affair.
situation: Saul made some new friends and is out at the bar with them.
intention: Saul wants his new friends to think he is funny.
moral_action: Saul makes a bunch of cheesy dad jokes.
moral_consequence: Everyone finds Saul hilarious and invites him out to a barbecue the next weekend.
immoral_action: Saul jokes about sleeping with another women besides his wife.
immoral_consequence: Saul's new friends find it in poor taste and tells his wife whom threatens to leave him.

norm: It's good to have people that listen to you.
situation: Noah's girlfriend often tries to talk to him about her issues, but he tends to ignore her.
intention: Noah wants to initiate conversations with his girlfriend more often.
moral_action: Noah apologizes to his girlfriend for being so aloof, and sits down to talk to her about her feelings.
moral_consequence: Noah's girlfriend feels heard and loved, and has a happier demeanor from then on.
immoral_action: Noah asks his girlfriend how her day was, but starts playing video games when she begins to talk.
immoral_consequence: Noah's girlfriend feels ignored and begins to resent him.

norm: It is hurtful to cheat.
situation: Tiffany, who has a crush on Peter, asks him to come over her house while his girlfriend Sarah is out of town.
intention: Peter wants to spend time with Tiffany.
moral_action: Peter and Tiffany watch a move while they're at her house.
moral_consequence: Peter enjoys the move and has a fun, platonic time with Tiffany.
immoral_action: Peter starts making out with Tiffany while he's at her house.
immoral_consequence: Peter tells Sarah out of guilt and she is devastated.

norm: Bigotry is unacceptable.
situation: Barney has two new neighbors which he learns are a gay couple.
intention: Barney wants to say something to the new neighbors.
moral_action: Barney welcomes his new neighbors and says he hopes they can hang out sometime.
moral_consequence: The neighbors are glad to meet Barney and bring him a pack of homebrew beer later that evening.
immoral_action: Barney tells his new neighbors that he thinks their lifestyle is disgusting, and they should get out of his neighborhood.
immoral_consequence: The neighbors film the incident, and Barney loses his job when the video goes viral.

norm: It's nice to invite your relative to a gathering.
situation: Lauren is hosting a family reunion, but she has an aunt with whom she doesn't always get along.
intention: Lauren wants to invite some relatives to the reunion.
moral_action: Lauren calls her aunt to make peace and invite her to the reunion.
moral_consequence: Lauren's aunt is impressed with the gesture and attends the reunion with a batch of homemade cookies.
immoral_action: Lauren invites all of her extended family to the reunion except her aunt.
immoral_consequence: Lauren's aunt sees photos of the reunion on Facebook and feels sad, and spreads rumors about Lauren to the rest of the family.

norm: You shouldn't take advantage of people with memory problems
situation: Warren's friend Jack paid him back after borrowing money, but forgot and tried to pay him back again a week later.
intention: Warren wants to respond to Jack's offer of money.
moral_action: Warren lets Jack know that he'd already paid him back last week.
moral_consequence: Jack laughs at his forgetfulness and pockets his money.
immoral_action: Warren takes Jack's money and keeps quiet about how he'd already been paid back.
immoral_consequence: Jack overpays Warren and has to crunch his budget to pay his rent.

norm: You shouldn't make others wait.
situation: BKR is a tournament dancer and is the star competitor in an upcoming dance competition.
intention: BKR wants to make a grand entrance to the competition.
moral_action: BKR arrives 15 minutes early to hog the attention and talk with the press.
moral_consequence: BKR gets the attention, performs great, and wins a prize in the tournament.
immoral_action: BKR decides to be fashionably late and delays his arrival by an hour to attract attention.
immoral_consequence: The tournament starts without BKR and he gets nothing.

norm: You should be patient with children.
situation: Remy is teaching a course on self defense for children in a kindergarten class.
intention: Remy wants the children to pay attention to him.
moral_action: Remy creates a reward system for students in the course who are especially quiet and attentive.
moral_consequence: Most of the students participate actively in trying to earn rewards, ensuring class attention.
immoral_action: Remy whistles loudly and tells the children he will cancel the class entirely if they don't listen to him.
immoral_consequence: The children's parents are displeased with Remy's discipline method and withdraw their children from his course.

norm: It's wrong to call your siblings bad names.
situation: John is with his friends and younger brother Chris at a house party.
intention: John wants his friends to like him more than his brother.
moral_action: John is more social than his brother is with his friends, and he even compliments his brother.
moral_consequence: John's friends like John more and gravitate to him more as well.
immoral_action: John raises his voice and tells his friends that Chris is a bunch of bad names.
immoral_consequence: John's friends respect John less and feel sorry for Chris more.

norm: It's wrong to hug someone without their consent.
situation: Steve is a new employee at Target, and he is being introduced his supervisor Jill for the first time.
intention: Steve wants to greet  Jill.
moral_action: Steve says hello to Jill, introduces himself and gives her a firm handshake.
moral_consequence: Jill sees Steve as professional and competent and forms a positive impression of him.
immoral_action: Steve goes right up to Jill and gives her a big hug.
immoral_consequence: Jill doesn't feel the hug was appropriate and forms a negative impression of Steve.

norm: It's bad to throw tantrums.
situation: Prince has a birthday party and doesn't get the present that he really wanted.
intention: Prince wants to get the desired gift.
moral_action: Prince offers to trade some of his presents for the gift that he wanted.
moral_consequence: A friend who owns the desired gift trades some gifts with Prince, and both of them are happy.
immoral_action: Prince throws himself on the floor and shouts that he wants the desired gift.
immoral_consequence: Prince's friends get disgusted and leave the party.

norm: You shouldn't take financial advantage of your children.
situation: Jill is looking at clothes at the mall but has no money in her bank account.
intention: Jill wants to buy a new coat.
moral_action: Jill opens a credit card in her name to purchase the coat.
moral_consequence: Jill is happy she has a new coat.
immoral_action: Jill opens a credit card in her daughters name to purchase the coat.
immoral_consequence: Jill finds out and no longer trusts her mother.

norm: You just can't expect someone to like everything you like.
situation: Zara is on a lake trip with her best friend Layla, and they plan on renting a boat.
intention: Zara wants to play some music while they hang out on the boat.
moral_action: Zara plays her music over the speakers but switches to let Layla play her music every other song.
moral_consequence: Both Layla and Zara sing their hearts out while enjoying a fun day on the lake.
immoral_action: Zara takes over the stereo system on the boat and never asks Layla what she wants to listen to.
immoral_consequence: Layla is so disinterested in the music that Zara plays, she falls asleep on the boat and has an overall boring time on the lake.

norm: Teenagers should not have sexual relationships with grown men.
situation: 16-year-old Jessica is at a party when an older guy named Corey starts flirting with her.
intention: Jessica wants to get to know Corey.
moral_action: Jessica shuts down all flirting but allows platonic conversation with Corey.
moral_consequence: Corey walks away eventually and Jessica leaves the party unharmed.
immoral_action: Jessica flirts back and they end up sleeping together.
immoral_consequence: The cops show up to bust the party and catch Corey with Jessica, resulting in Corey's arrest.

norm: It's good to do things every day for your health.
situation: Garret is an overweight man who wants to look and feel better.
intention: Garret wants to lose weight.
moral_action: Garret replaces all the unhealthy food with fruits and vegetables, while working out daily.
moral_consequence: Garret begins to lose some weight and is inspired to keep up with his goal.
immoral_action: Garret eats less, but he still enjoys sugary snacks on a daily basis.
immoral_consequence: Garret doesn't see any progress and reverts to eating as much as he wants.

norm: It is good to reconnect with people.
situation: Gabby has lost touch with an old friend and has been feeling lonely.
intention: Gabby wants to have meaningful relationships.
moral_action: Gabby's friend reaches out, and Gabby makes time to have a video chat to catch up.
moral_consequence: Gabby's friend feels valued and is glad to rekindle the friendship.
immoral_action: Gabby's friend tries to reaches out several times, but Gabby always prioritizes hanging out with other friends.
immoral_consequence: Gabby's friend feels rejected and hurt, and stops reaching out.

norm: It is rude to not tip a bartender.
situation: Joe orders drinks and drinks them very quickly by himself.
intention: Joe wants to finish his drinks.
moral_action: Joe drinks quickly and tips the bartender a lot for quick service.
moral_consequence: Joe runs out of the bar, but he comes back later on knowing he'll get good service again.
immoral_action: The bartender asks why Joe drank so fast, Joe empties his wallet and runs out of the bar.
immoral_consequence: The bartender counts exactly enough for the drinks.

norm: It's immoral to betray your partner's trust.
situation: Jack's friends invite him to go on a guys' night out and his girlfriend admonishes him not to do something that would damage their relationship.
intention: Jack wants to go out with his friends.
moral_action: Jack goes out with his friends but doesn't pursue any women while they're out.
moral_consequence: Jack's girlfriend is happy that she can trust Jack to be true to her.
immoral_action: Jack goes to a bar with his friends and ends up making out with a girl he met there.
immoral_consequence: Jack's girlfriend is devastated when she learns that he kissed another girl.

norm: You shouldn't vomit in someone's car.
situation: Lance has partied for most of the night and now feels pretty drunk and ready to go home.
intention: Lance wants his friend to drive him back home.
moral_action: Lance starts feeling really sick in the car and asks his friend to stop the car, so he can vomit by the side of the road.
moral_consequence: Lance's friend's car is spared and Lance's friend spends the next day relaxing.
immoral_action: Lance feels sick while he's in the car but does not tell his friend until it's too late - he profusely throws up in the car.
immoral_consequence: Lance's friend has to spend hours the next day cleaning his car.

norm: You shouldn't talk about people behind their backs.
situation: Patty is out with friends one night.
intention: Patty wants to know what is going on with Dave.
moral_action: Patty asks the rest of the group where is Dave and calls him to invite him.
moral_consequence: Patty makes Dave happy because she remembered him.
immoral_action: Patty rudely tells the rest of the group she is glad Dave is not there because she hates him.
immoral_consequence: Patty upsets the rest of the group because they like Dave.

norm: You shouldn't hook up with your sibling's friends.
situation: Jack is home from college for the summer vacation.
intention: Jack wants to have a fun summer.
moral_action: Jack takes his sister and her friends on fun outings throughout the summer.
moral_consequence: Jack gets to grow closer to his sister and make friends with her friends.
immoral_action: Jack starts going out with his sisters best friend then breaks up with her when he heads back to college.
immoral_consequence: Jack and his sister have a fight over his treatment of her friend and their relationship suffers.

norm: It's good to not treat others like they are liars.
situation: Nagisa listens to his coworker's explain that they didn't eat Nagisa's lunch.
intention: Nagisa wants to respond to his coworker.
moral_action: Nagisa asks his coworker to aid his search at finding the lunch eating culprit.
moral_consequence: Nagisa's coworker is praised for his detective skills when he figures out the identity of the thief.
immoral_action: Nagisa says that he doesn't believe his coworker and demands repayment for lunch.
immoral_consequence: Nagisa's coworker breaks down crying in the break room.

norm: You shouldn't tease people with disabilities.
situation: Kaiden is in the line with his mother at the grocery store.
intention: Kaiden wants to do an impression.
moral_action: Kaden acts like his favorite YouTube influencer and is spot on.
moral_consequence: Kaden is overjoyed when the people around him laugh loudly.
immoral_action: Kaden mocks the one armed worker by putting his arm inside his shirt and laughing loudly.
immoral_consequence: Kaden gets scolded by his mother and the worker frowns.

norm: It is expected that you help and support coworkers
situation: One of the clients at James' work suddenly asked for a huge rush job, and James' boss asked everyone to come in on Saturday to help the associated account manager.
intention: James doesn't want to give up his Saturday.
moral_action: James argues with his boss and says they should bill the clients for some temps to come help out.
moral_consequence: The boss agrees, since the client shouldn't have given them so little advance notice.
immoral_action: James calls in sick on Saturday because he doesn't want to deal with the workload.
immoral_consequence: James' coworkers are irritated with him when he comes into the office on Monday.

norm: You shouldn't leave electronics on when you aren't using them.
situation: John's phone rings while he is watching TV.
intention: John wants to answer the phone.
moral_action: John turns off the TV before answering the phone.
moral_consequence: John saves energy and has a lower electric bill.
immoral_action: John answers the phone and has a long conversation in another room while the TV remains on.
immoral_consequence: John wastes energy and his electric bill is more expensive.

norm: You should not use children to get to their parents.
situation: Philip, the principal at a prestigious private school, is hoping to get donations for the school.
intention: Philip wants his students parents to donate more.
moral_action: Philip sets up fundraising events invoving the entire student body to encourage donations.
moral_consequence: Philip is lauded for adding to the schools coffers.
immoral_action: Philip starts giving special privileges and boosted grades to kids with the richest parents.
immoral_consequence: Philip loses his position when other parents complain about the preferential treatment.

norm: It's wrong to take a game without paying for it.
situation: Lucas is in a game store and sees a bunch of games that he wants.
intention: Lucas wants to get some of the games.
moral_action: Lucas buys the games with money form his wallet.
moral_consequence: Lucas takes the games home and begins to play them all.
immoral_action: Lucas decides to take the games for himself without paying.
immoral_consequence: Lucas gets caught trying to walk out of the store with those games.

norm: It is mean not to consider the feelings of others
situation: Lizzy is cooking for her party, and she knows her vegetarian friend Sandy will be showing up.
intention: Lizzy wants to serve barbecue food.
moral_action: Lizzy invites Sandy over to her house to make some vegetarian friendly items for the menu.
moral_consequence: Sandy gains a deeper understanding of barbecue.
immoral_action: Lizzy makes an assortment of ribs and chicken wings for the party.
immoral_consequence: Sandy feels left out because she can't eat anything.

norm: It is rude to not pay back a friend.
situation: Rose owes her friend money, and they are going to see a movie together soon.
intention: Rose wants to maintain a good relationship with her friend.
moral_action: Rose offers to pay for her friend's movie ticket to pay her back.
moral_consequence: Rose's friend is grateful and feels like Rose is a trustworthy friend.
immoral_action: Rose hopes that her friend forgets about her owing money and makes her friend pay for her own ticket.
immoral_consequence: Rose's friend is annoyed that Rose didn't take the chance to pay her back and starts hanging out with her less.

norm: It's wrong to criticize someone's natural speech.
situation: Tom hears there is going to be a new student in their class this year.
intention: Tom wants to meet the new student.
moral_action: Tom meets the new student and thinks his accent is cool and wants to learn where he is from.
moral_consequence: Tom befriends the new student and helps him get used to the new school.
immoral_action: Tom meets the new student and teases at him for the way he talks, mimicking him in front of the whole class .
immoral_consequence: Tom makes the new student cry and is sent to the principals office.

norm: It's rude to judge someone for liking a celebrity.
situation: Pete is on a date with Stephanie who is known for being artsy and deep.
intention: Pete wants to impress Stephanie.
moral_action: Pete talks about the things he is passionate about and shares his enthusiasm with Stephanie.
moral_consequence: Stephanie thinks Pete is an interesting and self-assured guy and the date goes well.
immoral_action: Pete talks about stan culture and how shallow and silly he finds it because he thinks it will make him look like he's above popular culture.
immoral_consequence: Stephanie finds Pete negative and pretentious and the date goes badly.

norm: It's inconsiderate to deprive homeless people of money.
situation: John is driving on a street when he sees a homeless man with a sign on the corner waving at him.
intention: John wants to go to the mall.
moral_action: John stops briefly, hands the homeless guy ten dollars and drives to the mall.
moral_consequence: The homeless guy is happy and can eat tonight.
immoral_action: John pretends he does not see the homeless guy and drives quickly to the mall.
immoral_consequence: The homeless guy feels sad and rejected and spends another night hungry.

norm: It's greedy to eat too much
situation: Matt is starving after a long day at school and is sitting down for dinner with his family.
intention: Matt wants to eat food to satisfy his hunger.
moral_action: Matt eats a reasonable portion of the various foods his mother has prepared for dinner.
moral_consequence: Matt's family have a pleasant and enjoyable dinner together.
immoral_action: Matt eats all the dinner rolls before any of his family members can have a single one.
immoral_consequence: Matt's family is disappointed and upset that he was selfish and ate all the rolls.

norm: You shouldn't get your baby's ears pierced.
situation: Mary wants to bring her baby to get photographed.
intention: Mary wants her baby to look cute in the picture.
moral_action: Mary decides the baby should just dress nice and doesn’t go overboard.
moral_consequence: The picture turns out great and the baby doesn’t cry once.
immoral_action: Mary decides her baby would look better with earrings.
immoral_consequence: The baby screams and cries and has trouble sleeping for days.

norm: It's bad to move away from your partner.
situation: Ryan was offered a better position within his company, but it requires him to relocate away from his girlfriend Samantha to a big city.
intention: Ryan wants to accept the job.
moral_action: Ryan tells Samantha what a good opportunity the job is, and asks her to move with him.
moral_consequence: Samantha gladly accepts and their relationship flourishes in the new city.
immoral_action: Ryan tells his boss he will take the position and tells Samantha that he will fly in every weekend to see her.
immoral_consequence: The long distance puts a strain on their relationship, so Ryan and Samantha break up.

norm: It is not okay to brag
situation: Jan's friend is talking to her about the new purse she bought, but Jan's purse is much more expensive.
intention: Jan wants to compare her friend's purse to hers.
moral_action: Jan tells her friend that she likes her purse more than her own.
moral_consequence: Jan's friend gains confidence in her purchasing decisions and feels that Jan is modest.
immoral_action: Jan tells her friend that her purse is so much nicer than Jan's.
immoral_consequence: Jan's friend feels insecure and feels that Jan thinks she's better than her.

norm: You shouldn't swear at others.
situation: Sam's coworker Tom makes a big error on a group work project.
intention: Sam wants to inform his coworker Tom about the mistake.
moral_action: Sam informs Tom of the error he made and offers to help him fix it.
moral_consequence: Tom fixes the error and the project is a great success.
immoral_action: Sam angrily berates and swears at Tom about the error he made.
immoral_consequence: Tom gets upset and withdraws from the work project which becomes a failure.

norm: You should absolutely never steal money from your children
situation: Cindy is low on cash and knows that her daughter, Danielle, has been working through her senior year of high school in order to save for college.
intention: Cindy wants some of Danielle's money.
moral_action: Cindy asks Danielle if she can borrow some money and promises to pay her back with interest.
moral_consequence: Danielle agrees to Cindy's deal and ends up with enough money for books from the interest she made from her mother.
immoral_action: While Danielle is at school, Cindy goes into her room and takes a good chunk from her stash of money.
immoral_consequence: When it comes time to apply for colleges, Danielle realizes most of her money is missing, and she can't afford to go.

norm: It is irresponsible to leave without paying your dinner bill.
situation: Karen just finished dinner at a local restaurant.
intention: Karen wants to go home.
moral_action: Karen flags down her server and says she'd like to pay her check, so she can leave.
moral_consequence: Karen goes home, satisfied by the meal, and relaxes for the rest of the evening.
immoral_action: Karen grows impatient waiting for the server to bring her bill, so she decides to simply leave without paying.
immoral_consequence: The restaurant manager calls the police and Karen is arrested for theft of service.

norm: You shouldn't interfere in a country's election.
situation: Bob wants his favorite candidate to win the presidential election.
intention: Bob wants his candidate to get more votes.
moral_action: Bob goes door-to-door trying to convince people to vote for his candidate.
moral_consequence: Bob's candidate gets some more votes from Bob's neighbors.
immoral_action: Bob hacks a voting machine and adds 1,000 more votes for his candidate.
immoral_consequence: The hack is discovered and Bob is prosecuted.

norm: It's good to listen to people's stories.
situation: Paul and his family are having a big family reunion at his grandparent's ranch.
intention: Paul wants to play games with his cousins.
moral_action: Paul listens to his grandfather tell a story about the ranch, then he goes to play games with his cousins.
moral_consequence: His grandfather is happy that someone wanted to hear a story that he likes to tell.
immoral_action: Paul's grandfather starts to tell him a story about the ranch but Paul cuts him off to go play games with his cousins.
immoral_consequence: His grandfather gets hurt feelings because Paul doesn't want to hear his story.

norm: It's mean to ruin someone's reputation.
situation: Pat is a senior in high school and is about to graduate.
intention: Pat wants to make a speech at the graduation.
moral_action: Pat makes a speech at her graduation and it is a good speech.
moral_consequence: Everyone loves Pat's speech and give her a round of applause.
immoral_action: Pat makes a speech at her graduation in her speech she ruins the reputation of a girl she has never liked in her school.
immoral_consequence: Pat is removed from the stage by the principal and everyone laughs at her.

norm: You should ask for what you want politely when ordering.
situation: Jonny is at a restaurant and is in a hurry to get home.
intention: Jonny wants quick food service.
moral_action: Jonny asks the waiter if the food can be made quickly as he's running late.
moral_consequence: The waiter tries hard to get him the food fast and respects Jonny.
immoral_action: Jonny tells the waiter to bring his food fast in a raised voice.
immoral_consequence: The waiter likely resents Jonny and will take his time getting the food.

norm: It's important to give authorities accurate information.
situation: Bob flies a reconnaissance plane in the navy and is looking for enemy aircraft carriers when he sees some ships in the distance, but can't identify them.
intention: Bob wants to report the ships to the authorities.
moral_action: Bob flies in for a closer look and sees that they are carriers, then radios back what he sees.
moral_consequence: Bob's comrades send out aircraft to harass and defeat the carriers before they can attack.
immoral_action: Bob reports that he sees some ships and that he thinks that they are not carriers.
immoral_consequence: The ships are actually carriers and mount a surprise aerial attack on Bob's comrades.

norm: It's good to be upfront about your feelings for someone.
situation: Tim has grown apart from his girlfriend and can't stop thinking about another girl that he recently met.
intention: Tim wants to end the relationship with his girlfriend.
moral_action: Tim tells his girlfriend that he doesn't think there relationship has a future because they've grown apart.
moral_consequence: Tim's girlfriend agrees with Tim, and they remain friends after the breakup.
immoral_action: Tim ghosts his girlfriend and doesn't return any of her messages.
immoral_consequence: Tim's girlfriend is crushed and falls into a deep depression after being ghosted by Tim.

norm: It's not right to bully another person.
situation: Paul is bigger than all the kids at his school.
intention: Paul wants to get noticed this year at school.
moral_action: Paul decides to use his size to help smaller kids without being intimidating.
moral_consequence: Paul becomes well like as a nice person and gains many genuine friends.
immoral_action: Paul uses his size to intimate kids, and they all become aware of him and fear him.
immoral_consequence: No one likes Paul and Paul feels sad daily about this.

norm: You should be there for others when they need you.
situation: Ken is very tired and gets a late call from a friend who is in distress.
intention: Ken wants to get to bed soon.
moral_action: Ken offers to call them back tomorrow in order to be of more help at a better time.
moral_consequence: Ken's friend is able to get the help that they need.
immoral_action: Ken hurries off the phone after a few minutes and leaves his friend to deal with their own problems.
immoral_consequence: Ken's friend feels brushed off and it affects their friendship.

norm: It's wrong to threaten people with physical violence.
situation: Josh does not approve of his daughter's new boyfriend.
intention: Josh wants to intimidate his daughter's boyfriend.
moral_action: Josh lists a number of conditions his daughter's boyfriend must meet to stay on good terms.
moral_consequence: Josh's daughter's boyfriend behaves himself while in Josh's household.
immoral_action: Josh grabs his daughter's boyfriend by the collar and threatens to beat him.
immoral_consequence: Josh has the police called on him and spends the night in jail.

norm: People shouldn't misuse devices for purposes they weren't intended.
situation: Faye finds an old iron that has been sitting in the closet for a while.
intention: Faye wants to test out the iron.
moral_action: Faye uses the iron to press wrinkles out of some of her shirts.
moral_consequence: Faye hangs up the shirts and stores the iron away for future use.
immoral_action: Faye uses the iron to make a grilled cheese sandwich.
immoral_consequence: Faye clogs the iron with cheese and it stops working.

norm: It's wrong to steal from a parent.
situation: James hears about a new arcade game and sees his dad's coin jar in his bedroom.
intention: James wants to play the arcade game.
moral_action: James goes to his dad and asks for money to play a game.
moral_consequence: James' dad give him $5 to play the game.
immoral_action: James takes quarters from the coin jar and goes to play the game.
immoral_consequence: James gets away with it, but has a guilty conscience for years afterwards.

norm: Its not okay to demand more than your fair share.
situation: Bill wants to open a lemonade stand and tells Jack about it, the next day Jack has opened a stand himself.
intention: Bill wants to be paid for his idea.
moral_action: Bill goes up to Jack and asks for some money for his idea.
moral_consequence: Bill and Jack agree to work at the stand together and split the money.
immoral_action: Bill storms up to Jacks stand and demands all of the money from the stand.
immoral_consequence: Bill and Jack fight and don't make any money because they fight rather than make sales.

norm: It's good to communicate your concerns with your family.
situation: Ray has been having suicidal thoughts, and he hasn't talked to anyone about it.
intention: Ray wants to decide whether to talk to his family.
moral_action: Ray tells his family about his struggles with mental illness.
moral_consequence: Ray gets something off of his chest and is in a better position to receive help.
immoral_action: Ray doesn't want his family to get in his way if he does decide to kill himself, so he doesn't tell them.
immoral_consequence: Ray still needs serious help, and nobody is able to give it to him.

norm: It is hurtful to misspell your loved ones' names.
situation: After arguing with his mother, Matthew sits down to write a message in his mother's birthday card.
intention: Matthew wants to express his frustrations.
moral_action: Matthew vents his feelings to his friend to help clear his head.
moral_consequence: Matthew's mother bonds with her son after he shares his discussion with his friends.
immoral_action: Matthew scrambles every single word in his thank you message including his mother's name.
immoral_consequence: His mother is unable to read the message.

norm: It is bad to bully people online
situation: Anna is reading about the election on an internet forum.
intention: Anna wants to discuss her views.
moral_action: Anna has an informative discussion about who she thinks will win the election with another forum user.
moral_consequence: Anna gains a new online friend and has a pleasant time online.
immoral_action: Anna berates a person who doesn't agree with her views and calls them racist names.
immoral_consequence: Anna is banned from using the forum in the future.

norm: You shouldn't do drugs to cope with something.
situation: Marie's husband has recently passed away, and she is struggling to cope with her grief.
intention: Mary wants to feel better emotionally.
moral_action: Marie's sister convinces her to start seeing a therapist to talk through her problems.
moral_consequence: Marie's sister is glad to see that Marie is working through her grief.
immoral_action: Marie begins to take her sister's depression medication to try to improve her mood.
immoral_consequence: Marie's sister runs out of her medication unexpectedly and has to go without.

norm: It's good to be responsible for your payments.
situation: Carl has bought a car and the first payment for the car is coming up.
intention: Carl wants to keep the car.
moral_action: Carl makes sure that he pays the car before the due date.
moral_consequence: Carl's credit score gets higher and higher, and he eventually pays the car off.
immoral_action: Carl doesn't pay the car note and hides the car at his friend's house so it won't get repossessed.
immoral_consequence: Carl's credit score takes a hit and the lenders take legal action against Carl.

norm: It's wrong to disappoint your customers with gross negligence.
situation: Tom is managing a restaurant and is short-staffed during the busy lunch hour.
intention: Tom wants to keep up with the customers' orders.
moral_action: Tom puts on an apron and goes into the kitchen to help prepare food during the rush.
moral_consequence: The customers get their food in a timely fashion and all other bases are still covered.
immoral_action: Tom directs one of the bus boys to go into the kitchen and help cook and serve food.
immoral_consequence: The tables don't get cleaned and the customers become disgusted at all of the dirty dishes around.

norm: It's hurtful to others to be an alcoholic.
situation: Pete is an alcoholic at a work party and feels his mouth is dry.
intention: Pete wants something to drink.
moral_action: Pete orders a water.
moral_consequence: Pete feels hydrated and converses about life with his co-workers.
immoral_action: Pete orders a glass of wine.
immoral_consequence: Pete becomes intoxicated and insults his co-workers.

norm: It's selfish to only think about yourself.
situation: Kyle is married to Heidi and just won a $200 gift certificate for a fancy restaurant.
intention: Kyle wants to use his prize.
moral_action: Kyle takes Heidi to the restaurant, and they both enjoy a nice meal together.
moral_consequence: Heidi thinks it was nice of Kyle to take her, and he feels generous.
immoral_action: Kyle, having never been to an upscale restaurant goes alone and orders himself the most expensive items on the menu.
immoral_consequence: Heidi sees Kyle as selfish, and he feels like a glutton afterwards.

norm: You should respect your elders wishes.
situation: Dan's dad asked Dan to pull the plug if he ever forget who Dan is, and it actually happened.
intention: Dan wants to make a decision on his dad's life.
moral_action: Dan tells the doctors to pull the plug on his dad.
moral_consequence: Dan's dad doesn't have to suffer anymore, and this makes Dan relieved.
immoral_action: Dan doesn't tell the doctors what his dad wanted wants his dad to stay alive.
immoral_consequence: Dan's dad continues to suffer, and Dan doesn't like seeing his dad like this.

norm: It's wrong to hate Jews.
situation: Adolf was rejected from a primarily Jewish art school and is upset.
intention: Adolf wants to feel better about himself.
moral_action: Adolf works harder at his art skills and re-applies later on.
moral_consequence: Many Jews and others are unharmed and Adolf becomes a beloved artist.
immoral_action: Adolf vows revenge on the Jews and calls for their downfall.
immoral_consequence: Many Jews and others are hurt and Adolf dies a lonely death.

norm: It's bad to live a life of debauchery.
situation: Peter moves to Thailand to work and live.
intention: Peter wants to enjoy Thailand.
moral_action: Peter takes a different tour of Thailand every weekend to learn the culture.
moral_consequence: Peter becomes very knowledgeable about Thailand and Thai culture.
immoral_action: Peter goes to bars drinking and picking up prostitutes every night.
immoral_consequence: Peter catches AIDS from a hooker and gets very sick.

norm: You should ask before you drink someone else's beer.
situation: Brent is at his acquaintance's house and sees that there is a beer in the fridge.
intention: Brent wants to drink the beer in the fridge.
moral_action: Brent asks his acquaintance if he can drink the beer in their fridge, and they say yes, so he does.
moral_consequence: Brent's acquaintance is happy Brent asked them if he could have the beer instead of just helping himself.
immoral_action: Brent grabs the beer from the fridge without asking and drinks it all.
immoral_consequence: Brent's acquaintance thinks Brent has no manners if he will just take things from their fridge without asking.

norm: It's bad to blame all your problems on other people.
situation: Ash is having a terrible string of luck lately and everything seems to be going wrong.
intention: Ash wants to let off some steam and vent.
moral_action: Ash has a nice get together with friends and family.
moral_consequence: Ash and her close ones have a great time together which recharges everyone.
immoral_action: Ash blames their friends and family for never helping them.
immoral_consequence: Ash damages relationships with her support circle.

norm: It's wrong to take up other peoples space
situation: Mark has gotten onto a city bus, and sits down in the only open seat, next to an older woman.
intention: Mark wants to ride the bus home.
moral_action: Mark relaxes a bit, but is careful to stay within the limits of his seat and not annoy the woman next to him.
moral_consequence: Mark has a quiet ride home, and the woman next to him gives him a smile as he gets off the bus.
immoral_action: Mark relaxes, stretches his legs out, and spreads into the space of the woman seated next to him, ignoring her request for him to move over.
immoral_consequence: "The woman says very loudly ""Stop touching my butt, you creep!"" which embarrasses Mark so much that he moves to the back of the bus."

norm: You shouldn't give ultimatums to people.
situation: Mike notices that his son Tom still hasn't cleaned the dishes as he promised to do many hours earlier.
intention: Mike wants the dishes to be cleaned.
moral_action: Mike reminds Tom that he had promised to do the dishes, and they are still dirty.
moral_consequence: Tom apologizes and quickly makes his way to the kitchen to wash the dishes.
immoral_action: Mike tells Tom to wash the dishes immediately, or he will be grounded for a month.
immoral_consequence: Tom is defiant in response to the ultimatum and refuses to comply with the request.

norm: You shouldn't get drunk around people.
situation: Larry is at a party with his friends.
intention: Larry wants to have some beers and relax.
moral_action: Larry has two beers and sticks with water and soda after that.
moral_consequence: Larry goes home having enjoyed the evening and bonded with his friends.
immoral_action: Larry gets drunk, dances around naked and is has no memory of the night.
immoral_consequence: A friend videotapes and shares larry's dancing on social media and Larry is humiliated.

norm: It's bad to buy a pet from a puppy mill.
situation: Layla's daughter has been asking for a pet dog.
intention: Layla wants to get her daughter a pet.
moral_action: Layla takes her daughter to an animal shelter to adopt a dog.
moral_consequence: A dog is saved and Layla's daughter learns the values of love and compassion.
immoral_action: Layla purchases a dog from a puppy mill to surprise her daughter with.
immoral_consequence: The puppy has many health issues from being crammed into a tiny cage and dies not long after being purchased.

norm: It's good to look past people's ages.
situation: When Jenna met her blind date at the restaurant, she realized he was fifteen years older than her.
intention: Jenna wants to date someone with a similar outlook on life.
moral_action: Jenna decides to talk to her blind date to see how similar they are.
moral_consequence: Jenna discovers that actually share a lot of the same values and tastes and schedules a followup date.
immoral_action: Jenna assumes that her blind date won't understand her because he's too old.
immoral_consequence: Jenna leaves and feels lonely and unsatisfied, as does her blind date.

norm: It is bad to do things to hurt others.
situation: Ron is upset because he doesn't think his family is paying enough attention to him.
intention: Ron wants his family to know how he feels.
moral_action: Ron explains to his parents that he feels left out, and asks if they can do something together.
moral_consequence: Ron's family realizes he wants attention, and they do activities together.
immoral_action: Ron hits his sister to get his parents' attention, then throws a tantrum and calls them all stupid.
immoral_consequence: Ron's sister cries in pain, and his family is put through unnecessary drama, and Ron is grounded.

norm: It's wrong to use cellphones too often.
situation: Angelica is on a dinner date with Mark, a guy she's had a crush on for a long time.
intention: Angelica wants to feel interested and entertained during her date.
moral_action: Angelica leaves her phone in her purse and spends the night asking Mark about himself and telling him about herself.
moral_consequence: Mark enjoys conversing with Angelica, finds they have a lot in common, and asks her out on another date.
immoral_action: Angelica pulls out her phone and checks her social media accounts throughout the date.
immoral_consequence: Mark is offended and tells Angelica that he has no interest in going out with her again.

norm: It is wrong to steal from your work.
situation: Martin had to stay late at work and didn't have time to shop for poster making supplies.
intention: Martin wants to make some posters.
moral_action: Martin buys the supplies he needs the following day and still has time to make the posters.
moral_consequence: Martin is glad that he did not jeopardize his job by taking supplies from his work place.
immoral_action: Martin decides to take all the supplies that he needs from work, even though he knows it is prohibited.
immoral_consequence: Martin is fired after his boss found out what he did.

norm: You shouldn't lie about military service
situation: Donald can't afford to pay for his meal, and the restaurant offers a military discount.
intention: Donald wants to pay for his food.
moral_action: Donald moves money in his savings account to his checking account to cover the bill.
moral_consequence: Donald is able to enjoy his meal without worrying about finances.
immoral_action: Donald tells the waitress that he's in the Navy.
immoral_consequence: Donald is exposed in front of a large group of people when the waitress asks for his id.

norm: You shouldn't shoot people.
situation: Paul has a gun and finds a man trying to break into his car.
intention: Paul wants to stop the robber.
moral_action: Paul points the gun at the robber and tells him to get on the ground.
moral_consequence: The robber can be apprehended and Paul does not hurt anyone.
immoral_action: Paul shoots the robber with the gun.
immoral_consequence: The robber dies and Paul is charged with a crime.

norm: You shouldn't make people do things.
situation: Dudley bossed around all his friends because his parents employed all of their parents.
intention: Dudley wants to have fun with his friends.
moral_action: Dudley decides to make it as fun as possible to be one of his friends.
moral_consequence: Dudley's friends have lots of fun and want to hang out at Dudley's house more.
immoral_action: Dudley continued making all of his friends do all his chores and lose every game to him.
immoral_consequence: "The moment their parents get new jobs, Dudley's ""friends"" would vanish."

norm: It's bad to cheat on one's partner in a relationship.
situation: Terry has been dating the same woman fora year and their relationship hasn't worked for quite some time.
intention: Terry wants to pursue other women.
moral_action: Terry communicates to his partner that things aren't working out, leaving her before exploring his other options.
moral_consequence: Terry and his partner are able to end things amicably.
immoral_action: Terry goes after other women while he's still in the same relationship.
immoral_consequence: Terry's partner finds out what he's been doing, and they have a very dramatic break up.

norm: It's bad to smoke cigarettes.
situation: Quinn has been overworked and is feeling stressed from the job demands.
intention: Quinn wants to take the edge off.
moral_action: Quinn picks up a vape pen from a vape store to use to relax.
moral_consequence: Quinn supports a local business by purchasing the item there.
immoral_action: Quinn buys a pack of cigarettes to smoke.
immoral_consequence: Quinn's neighbors are bothered by the smoke.

norm: It's wrong to not take your studies seriously.
situation: Bob was contemplating going out with his friends on a Friday night.
intention: Bob wants to pass his history exam that is scheduled for Saturday morning.
moral_action: Bob tells his friends he needs to study and stays in, getting a full night of sleep.
moral_consequence: Bob takes the test and gets an A on it.
immoral_action: Bob decides to go out to the bar and drinks until two am.
immoral_consequence: Bob goes to the exam extremely hungover and ends up getting a D which puts him on academic probation.

norm: It is bad to try to sabotage people's jobs
situation: Rania and Julian are both competing for a manager position at work but only one can get it.
intention: Rania wants to get the job.
moral_action: Rania begins working harder at her job and is nicer to everyone around her to make a good impression.
moral_consequence: The promotion committee notice's Rania' efforts and give her the promotion.
immoral_action: Rania logs into Julian's computer and messes with his files, so he will look bad.
immoral_consequence: Rania gets caught and is fired while Julian gets the promotion.

norm: It's frowned upon in society to eat domesticated pets
situation: Todd is feeling hungry.
intention: Todds wants something unusual to eat.
moral_action: Todd orders delivery from an ethnic restaurant he has never dined at before.
moral_consequence: Todd has a tasty meal and broadens his culinary horizons.
immoral_action: Todd kills the family dog and cooks it for dinner.
immoral_consequence: Todd is arrested for animal cruelty.

norm: It is rude to take advantage of your host
situation: Bill was arriving at his girlfriend, Barb's, parent's house to meet them for the first time.
intention: Bill wants to make an impress on them.
moral_action: Bill connects with Barb's father and mother and helps clean up after dinner.
moral_consequence: Barb's parents like Bill after meeting him.
immoral_action: Bill has a long, engaging talk with Barb's father about fishing and then ask if he can borrow Barb's father's beloved bass boat sometime.
immoral_consequence: Barb's parents become remote and go to their room after dinner.

norm: You shouldn't try to injure animals.
situation: Francis just lost his job and is walking home when he sees a little puppy.
intention: Francis wants to vent his anger.
moral_action: Francis takes a breath, pets the puppy and jogs home for exercise.
moral_consequence: The puppy is happy to be petted and doesn't get hurt.
immoral_action: Francis picks up a stone and throws it strongly at the puppy.
immoral_consequence: The puppy gets injured and cries and is sad and lonely.

norm: You shouldn't set fireworks off around your pets.
situation: John's dog Lucy is out on the porch while John is setting up his firework launch area.
intention: John wants to have a huge firework display.
moral_action: John brings his dog inside and puts her in a safe room before setting off his fireworks.
moral_consequence: John's display is beautiful and the entire family can admire it.
immoral_action: John forgets to bring his dog inside before setting off the fireworks.
immoral_consequence: John's dog digs under the fence to escape in fear, and John's display is ignored by family trying to chase the dog down.

norm: It's wrong to steal at work.
situation: Ryan is still at the office working when he realizes that he is out of printer paper at home.
intention: Ryan wants to print out some documents at home.
moral_action: Ryan stops at a local store on the way home to buy some paper.
moral_consequence: Ryan is able to print his documents and has plenty of paper for future use.
immoral_action: Ryan takes a ream of printer paper from his job back home with him.
immoral_consequence: Ryan's gets caught taking the supplies from work and loses his job.

norm: It's rude to fart loudly in class.
situation: Jim has eaten a lot of beans for lunch and is feeling extremely gassy in his next class.
intention: Jim wants to release the extra gas build up.
moral_action: Jim asks to be excused to go to the bathroom.
moral_consequence: Jim gets to fart in the bathroom without anyone else noticing it.
immoral_action: Jim lets it rip while sitting in the middle of his class.
immoral_consequence: Jim is embarrassed when everyone reacts to his bodily functions.

norm: It is rude to leave family out of ceremonies.
situation: John and Mary are getting married and are deciding on who to invite.
intention: John wants all his friends to attend.
moral_action: John asks his mum to help with the guest list so as not to offend family members.
moral_consequence: John is pleased with the good mix of friends and family that attend the wedding.
immoral_action: John decides to exclude some of his cousins, so he can have more friends attend.
immoral_consequence: John gets chewed out by his mum for not inviting family.

norm: It's helpful to tell a coworker when they look unprofessional.
situation: Jade notices her coworker coming into work in a white sundress.
intention: Jade doesn't want to hurt her coworker.
moral_action: Jade compliments her coworkers outfit while giving her tips on proper workplace attire.
moral_consequence: Jade's coworker takes her advice coming into work the next day in work appropriate clothing.
immoral_action: Jade greets her coworker normally ignoring her coworker's attire.
immoral_consequence: Her coworker is scolded by HR for dressing unprofessionally.

norm: It is embarrassing to live your life in the nude.
situation: Doug is a hippie that lives in a mountain cave and panhandles in town to get money for food.
intention: Doug doesn't want to spend a lot of money.
moral_action: Doug wears some jeans and shirts that he picked up from a thrift store.
moral_consequence: Hikers who see Doug note his not-so-great clothes but otherwise treat him normally.
immoral_action: Doug doesn't buy clothes because no one is around him in the mountains.
immoral_consequence: Hikers occasionally see or meet up with Doug and are freaked out that he travels nude.

norm: You should always give people the chance to apologize.
situation: Sarah and Victoria are friends and Victoria carelessly says something that hurts Sarah.
intention: Sarah wants to respond to Victoria's behavior.
moral_action: Sarah receives a letter from Victoria who explains her carelessness in the previous conversation and Sarah accepts her explanation.
moral_consequence: Victoria thanks Sarah for her understanding, and they are still good friends.
immoral_action: Sarah ghosts and ignores Victoria despite Victoria's frequent attempts to reach her.
immoral_consequence: Victoria feels sad and frustrated.

norm: It's impolite to keep plans from your spouse.
situation: Mark gets invited on a weekend trip with friends.
intention: Mark wants to go this trip without his wife.
moral_action: Mark asks his wife if it would be alright if he goes on a trip next month with friends.
moral_consequence: Mark's wife will be able to prepare for him not being there that weekend.
immoral_action: Mark goes on a weekend trip without telling his wife.
immoral_consequence: Mark's wife will be upset because she had no idea he was going away.

norm: It's wrong to say things to make someone feel inferior.
situation: Clyde is a teacher who is working with a student that has trouble with a particular subject.
intention: Clyde wants the student to not worry about his performance.
moral_action: Clyde tells the student that he will understand it with time and practice.
moral_consequence: The student continues pushing until he masters the content, feeling good about himself.
immoral_action: "Clyde tells the student that not everyone can do it and not to feel bad if he doesn't have the ""knack"" for it."
immoral_consequence: The student thinks that he will never be able to do it and gives up.

norm: It is good to be smart with your moeny.
situation: Brent, who has a car loan, got a stimulus check from the government.
intention: Brent wants to spend the money.
moral_action: Brent puts the money towards the car loan.
moral_consequence: Brent pays off the car loan in time and keeps the car.
immoral_action: Brent spends the money on a wild party with his friends.
immoral_consequence: Brent doesn't have money to pay off his debts, and his car is repossessed.

norm: It's nice to help your spouse with the housework.
situation: Jim is reading a book on Saturday afternoon while his wife, Cindy, cleans the house.
intention: Jim wants to finish his book.
moral_action: Jim tells Cindy that he's just going to finish his book, and then he will do some of the housework, so she can relax.
moral_consequence: Cindy appreciates Jim's offer, without having had to ask him to help out.
immoral_action: When Cindy asks Jim for help he tells her that he just wants to finish his book.
immoral_consequence: Cindy gets frustrated that she is cleaning the house while Jim sits and reads.

norm: It's rude to refuse to help classmates.
situation: Nicole and James are competing to become valedictorian but Nicole had to miss some classes due to a surgery and has asked James for his notes.
intention: James wants to beat Nicole to be valedictorian.
moral_action: James shares his notes with Nicole and vows to study enough to beat her fair and square.
moral_consequence: Nicole is grateful to James and the two have a friendly rivalry that both enjoy.
immoral_action: James declines to give Nicole his notes because he wants any advantage he can get.
immoral_consequence: Nicole tells others about what James did, and he gets a reputation as a jerk.

norm: You should tell someone when they say something offensive.
situation: Brandon hears his brother say something in front on a classmate of theirs that Brandon knows would offend them.
intention: Brandon wants to talk to his brother.
moral_action: Brandon takes his brother aside and explains that what he said would cause offense.
moral_consequence: Brandon's brother understands that he was speaking hurtfully and starts being more careful with his words.
immoral_action: Brandon tells his brother that they should leave but doesn't explain to him that he was being offensive.
immoral_consequence: Brandon's brother doesn't understand that he said something wrong and continues making that mistake.

norm: It's not okay to disrespect people with an illness.
situation: Jimmy is walking through a park with friends when the see a man with a disfugured face and all laugh at him.
intention: Jimmy wants to react to the laughter from his friends.
moral_action: JImmy tells his friends to stop and approaches the man to apologize.
moral_consequence: Jimmy is thanked by man and and learns his story that he is a veteran who was injured in combat.
immoral_action: Jimmy joins in the laughter and shouts out comments to the person.
immoral_consequence: A coworker sees what Jimmy is doing and tells other coworkers the next day resulting in a lot of people being angry at Jimmy.

norm: You shouldn't take money from your in laws.
situation: Lisa has been accepted to design school, and she needs to find a way to have money for tuition.
intention: Lisa wants to pay for design school.
moral_action: Lisa finds a job where she can work part-time while going to school, so she can pay her tuition.
moral_consequence: Lisa's in law's are proud of Lisa and her ability to pay for her own tuition.
immoral_action: Lisa takes money from the safe in her in law's office when she goes over one day to help with cleaning.
immoral_consequence: Lisa's in law's are upset when they see their money is gone, and they cannot pay their bills.

norm: Gambling more than you can afford is unwise.
situation: Jim is going to the casino to have some fun with his friends.
intention: Jim wants to stick some money in the slot machines and see how lucky he can get.
moral_action: Jim puts in a small amount and after it is gone he quits.
moral_consequence: Jim is able to still afford all the rest of his monthly bills.
immoral_action: Jim spends way too much money and loses it all.
immoral_consequence: Jim has trouble paying his rent the next month because he is short cash.

norm: It's polite to accommodate your guests' comfort levels.
situation: Todd has moved into his house and has a large living room.
intention: Todd wants to host a party.
moral_action: Todd sets the air conditioning to maintain room temperature during the party.
moral_consequence: Todd's guests will feel relaxed and enjoy the party.
immoral_action: During the party Todd turns the air conditioning to very cold.
immoral_consequence: Todd's guests will feel too cold and uncomfortable.

norm: It is not okay to bully anyone.
situation: Jenna has just found out that her younger brother is being bullied by another kid at their school.
intention: Jenna wants the bully to get what they deserve.
moral_action: Jenna tells her parents what has been happening, so they can intervene.
moral_consequence: Jenna's parents resolve the situation with the school and the bully's parents.
immoral_action: Jenna re-enacts what her brother's bully has been doing to her brother to the bully.
immoral_consequence: Jenna earns a reputation as a bully herself so people continue to target her brother.

norm: It's rude to not give people change.
situation: Jim is selling his TV at a yard sale for $50 and Patrick has just handed him a $100 bill.
intention: Jim wants to make more money.
moral_action: Jim offers to throw a blu-ray player in with the TV for $15 more.
moral_consequence: Patrick takes Jim up on the offer, so Jim gives Patrick $35 back.
immoral_action: Jim brings the money inside and talks to Patrick long enough for him to forget about getting his change.
immoral_consequence: Patrick later realizes he's been fooled and goes to Jim's house to demand payment through threat of violence.

norm: People in the restaurant industry should maintain food handling standards
situation: Bob owns a restaurant that is getting very popular and has good reviews.
intention: Bob wants to make lots of money.
moral_action: Bob keeps up with the food storage and handling standards and makes sure his employees are working safely.
moral_consequence: Bob's restaurant becomes even more famous, and he makes enough money to open another one.
immoral_action: To save some money, Bob starts ignoring food handling standards.
immoral_consequence: Bob's restaurant has a major outbreak of foodborne illness, and his restaurant is temporarily shut down.

norm: It's good to donate leftover Christmas toys to charity.
situation: Eric is doing spring cleaning and notices a lot of unused items laying around all over the house.
intention: Eric wants to clear out some space in the house.
moral_action: Eric brings all the unused toys to goodwill to donate them.
moral_consequence: Needy kids get the toys they wouldn't have gotten, and they are happy.
immoral_action: Eric stuffs the Christmas toys into a box and puts it in the garage where it will likely be forgotten.
immoral_consequence: Kids who are in need wont get any Christmas toys.

norm: You should be polite to a parents partner.
situation: Andrew is visiting his girlfriend Linda's parents for dinner, but Linda's family cooked his least favorite food.
intention: Andrew wants to make conversation over dinner.
moral_action: Andrew makes conversation about the weather and his job while trying a small portion of the food.
moral_consequence: Linda's parents immediately like Andrew, and they invite him to another upcoming family event.
immoral_action: Andrew complains that he has never liked this type of food and announces that he will be stopping at McDonald's on the way home.
immoral_consequence: Linda's parents dislike Andrew and discourage Linda from continuing to date him.

norm: It's mean to give someone a gift that isn't real.
situation: James is a poor college student and needs to think of a Christmas present for a cousin he doesn't really like.
intention: James doesn't want to spend too much money.
