moral_action: James makes his cousin a home-made pan of his favorite fudge.
moral_consequence: James' cousin thanks James for the treat and offers him a piece.
immoral_action: James gives his cousin a gift card which he's already completely used up.
immoral_consequence: James' cousin notices the gift card isn't working but doesn't bother to bring it up.

norm: You should do what your teacher tells you to
situation: Victor's teacher asked the class to write a tasteful little poem, which they will then read aloud in class.
intention: Victor wants to make the students laugh.
moral_action: Victor composes a cute and funny poem.
moral_consequence: The teacher is amused by the poem, like everyone else, and gives Victor an A.
immoral_action: Victor writes a funny poem full of expletives.
immoral_consequence: Victor's teacher gives him an E for the poem.

norm: You shouldn't let your roommate abuse your pets.
situation: Willow has a dog and lives with Parker who she knows dislikes dogs.
intention: Willow wants to find someone to watch her dog while she's on a trip.
moral_action: Willow takes her dog to a boarding kennel for a few days.
moral_consequence: Willow's dog is taken care of and is able to play with other dogs.
immoral_action: Willow asks Parker to watch her dog for a few days and Parker ends up not feeding the dog for several days and keeping it in a crate.
immoral_consequence: Willow's dog is traumatized and needs to go to the vet when Willow returns.

norm: It is considered gross to skip showering for several days.
situation: Mike is having trouble adjusting to the winters in his new town.
intention: Mike wants to stay warm.
moral_action: Mike starts wearing long johns under his clothing to stay warm.
moral_consequence: Mike's body starts to grow accustomed to the new weather.
immoral_action: Mike starts skipping a shower because he gets cold when he undresses.
immoral_consequence: Mike's body odor begins to repulse the people around him.

norm: It's wrong to persist in sex after someone says no.
situation: Mio and Mia are fooling around in bed, but they've never gone all the way before.
intention: Mio wants to know how far he can go.
moral_action: Mio whispers to Mia to find out how things are progressing.
moral_consequence: Mio feels closer to Mia and learns to be slow.
immoral_action: Mio ups the intensity on his own initiative.
immoral_consequence: Mia becomes uncomfortable and Mio loses confidence.

norm: It's good to try to find a cure for Alzheimer's
situation: People think that Dr. White is the only person smart enough to make an Alzheimer's drug, but he's not sure if it's worth it.
intention: Dr. White wants to decide whether he should try and make an Alzheimer's cure.
moral_action: Dr. White decides to try and see what kind of drug he can make to assist Alzheimer's patients.
moral_consequence: Alzheimer's patients and their families feel hope that help might be on its way.
immoral_action: Dr. White decides money would be better used on other things than on a possible Alzheimer's drug.
immoral_consequence: Alzheimer's continues to harm people and their families with no end in sight.

norm: It is unacceptable to enter someone's home without permission.
situation: Jean is about to bake cookies in her kitchen but is missing an ingredient.
intention: Jean wants baking soda to help leven the dough.
moral_action: When Jean discovers her neighbor is not home, she drives to the store to buy the ingredient.
moral_consequence: Jean makes delicious cookies and shares them with her neighbor.
immoral_action: Jean knows her neighbor has baking soda, and sneaks in when noone is home to grab it.
immoral_consequence: Jean is caught on her neighbor's surveillance camera and confronted the next day, and is very ashamed.

norm: You shouldn't fake things to others.
situation: Henry and Jake are walking to the park together.
intention: Jake wants Henry to be impressed by him.
moral_action: Jake tells Henry that he'll always be there for him, and they'll be good friends.
moral_consequence: Henry thinks Jake is an awesome friend and vows to return the favor.
immoral_action: Jake tells Henry that he can rust faster than most olympic runners.
immoral_consequence: Henry thinks Jake is a liar and feels weird being friends with someone like that.

norm: It's wrong to brag about how much money you make.
situation: Debbie received a promotion at work with a higher salary, and she is spending time with friends.
intention: Debbie wants to talk about her promotion.
moral_action: Debbie talks about how her promotion gives her some interesting work opportunities.
moral_consequence: Debbie's friends will be curious about what kind of work she will be doing because of the promotion.
immoral_action: Debbie talks about how her promotion is paying her more than all of her friends make.
immoral_consequence: Debbie's friends will think she is arrogant and want to avoid talking to her.

norm: You shouldn't trust a liar.
situation: Andy's friend is known to lie, but he's trying to get Andy to invest in his new fund.
intention: Andy has to decide whether to invest in his friend's fund.
moral_action: Andy thinks that his friend's offer is too attractive to be true, so he denies the offer.
moral_consequence: Andy is able to save his money, and he doesn't have to worry about his friend having his money.
immoral_action: Andy decides to put money in the fund, and it ends up being a pyramid scheme.
immoral_consequence: Andy feels like an idiot, and he ends up losing a lot of money.

norm: People should be supportive of their friends.
situation: Jamie is having brunch with her best friend who is upset.
intention: Jamie wants to go to the beach later with a group of friends.
moral_action: Jamie takes her friend to the beach with her.
moral_consequence: Jamie's friend has great time and is feeling much better.
immoral_action: Jamie sees her friend needs some cheering up but head to the beach without her.
immoral_consequence: Jamie's friend goes home alone and is lonely and sad.

norm: It's bad to keep secrets from someone close to you.
situation: Dave who is young, but has had a couple of sexual partners is at his mom's house when she asks him if he's a virgin.
intention: Dave wants to respond to his mom's question.
moral_action: Dave tells his mom that he is not, but she need not worry because he used protection.
moral_consequence: Dave is happy to tell the truth to his mother even if it was a touchy topic.
immoral_action: Dave tells his mom that he is a virgin and that she has nothing to worry about.
immoral_consequence: Dave's conscience slowly eats at him for misleading his mother, and he gets depressed.

norm: It's good to super your local businesses.
situation: Victor just learned a new recipe and is driving out to go to the store.
intention: Victor wants to get all the ingredients he needs for the recipe.
moral_action: Victor decides to shop at local shops for his ingredients even if it means an extra stop or two.
moral_consequence: The quality of Victor's ingredients are excellent and the local community is served by his patronage to local businesses.
immoral_action: Victor drives past the locally own shops and goes to the supermarket, so he can get everything in one stop.
immoral_consequence: Local businesses suffer and money leaves the community because of shopping habits like Victor's which hurts Victor himself in the long run.

norm: It's rude to cancel an appointment without sufficient notice.
situation: James has an appointment with his realtor this tomorrow afternoon.
intention: James wants to cancel the meeting and reschedule for later this week.
moral_action: James calls his realtor firt thing in the morning the day before the appointment.
moral_consequence: The realtor thanks James for letting him know in advance and sets a new appointment for Sunday.
immoral_action: James waits until the last minute to try to cancel and reschedule the appointment.
immoral_consequence: His realtor gets upset, explaining that he could have lined up another client if he had time, and then refuses to reschedule.

norm: You shouldn't prank your principal.
situation: Billy found out that he had a new principal at the school he was going to.
intention: Billy wants to welcome the principal to the school.
moral_action: Billy brings the principal a fresh batch of brownies to his office.
moral_consequence: The principal thanks Billy and introduces himself in the office.
immoral_action: Billy drives by the principal's home and eggs the man's house.
immoral_consequence: The principal calls the police and Billy is brought in to the station.

norm: It is disrespectful to misbehave at a funeral wake.
situation: Camden, a four year old, is listening to someone give a long speech at his great uncle's funeral with a bored expression.
intention: Camden wants to get rid of his bordom.
moral_action: Camden daydreams about being a hero saving the world from a big monster.
moral_consequence: Camden submits a story based on a daydream to a writing contest later on in the school year.
immoral_action: Camden moves among the crowd poking people on the back before crawling away.
immoral_consequence: Camden's mother grounds him after she discovers him poking the man on the other side of the room.

norm: It's wrong to betray someone in a relationship.
situation: Corrie is in a relationship with a girl that he no longer feels the same for and his heart is wandering.
intention: Corrie wants to pursue another relationship.
moral_action: Corrie ends things with his current partner before dating the other woman.
moral_consequence: The other woman is happy that Corrie has come into her life.
immoral_action: Corrie gets involved with another woman while he is still in a relationship.
immoral_consequence: The other woman finds out that Corrie isn't single and distances herself from him.

norm: It's wrong to cut everyone out of your life.
situation: Doug is having a really difficult time lately with his mental health.
intention: Doug wants to feel better.
moral_action: Doug decided to call up his friend to see if he wanted to hang out and do something.
moral_consequence: Doug was able to take his mind off of his problems, and he realized no problem is too large to tackle.
immoral_action: Doug decided to turn his phone off, hang out alone in his bedroom, and drink his sorrows away.
immoral_consequence: Doug woke up feeling hungover, sad, and more alone than ever.

norm: It's important to bring your pets to the vet regularly.
situation: Tracy has a cat that is due to see the vet, but she is struggling financially.
intention: Tracy wants to save some money.
moral_action: Tracy goes to the vet and uses a payment plan to pay for the bill.
moral_consequence: The vet finds out the cat needs medicine and the cat's condition is improved.
immoral_action: Tracy decides to put off the vet visit because her cat seems fine.
immoral_consequence: The cat suffers from an underlying condition that the vet would have found.

norm: You should always have savings for a rainy day.
situation: Robert receives his stimulus money in the mail.
intention: Robert wants to do something with his money.
moral_action: Robert deposits the money into his bank and invests some of it in stable stocks.
moral_consequence: Robert is to cover his rent payment in half a year after his boss cuts his hours.
immoral_action: Robert spends all of the money on luxury items.
immoral_consequence: Robert is unable to afford to pay for an unexpected expensive trip to the doctor later in the month.

norm: You shouldn't be rude to your family.
situation: Derrick is on an important business call while working from home and his family is in the background making a lot of noise.
intention: Derrick wants to be able to hear the person he's talking to clearly.
moral_action: Derrick covers the receiver of his phone and quietly asks his family to tone down the noise for a bit.
moral_consequence: Derrick's family respects his wishes and allows him to have his conversation in peace.
immoral_action: Derrick covers the receiver of his phone for a moment and shouts at his family to shut up.
immoral_consequence: Derrick's family is upset that he spoke to them in such a fashion and stares at him resentfully as he continues his phone call.

norm: People shouldn't go to college just to party.
situation: Bob is a freshman in college begining his first semester.
intention: Bob would like to meet people and make friends.
moral_action: Bob socializes with other students from his intended major.
moral_consequence: Bob makes friends and gains insight into his proposed field of study.
immoral_action: Bob joins a frat and parties hard with his new fraternity brothers almost every night.
immoral_consequence: Bob neglects his studies and is placed on academic suspension, which earns him the sympathy of his new friends.

norm: It's wrong to leave a baby in a dirty diaper.
situation: Jenny is loading her baby into the car when she thinks she smells something coming from her baby's diaper area.
intention: Jenny wants to go shopping.
moral_action: Jenny takes the baby back inside to change the diaper and then goes to the store.
moral_consequence: The baby feels comfortable with a fresh, clean diaper.
immoral_action: Jenny decides to go to the store and wait to change the baby's diaper when they get home.
immoral_consequence: The baby gets diaper rash and is very uncomfortable.

norm: It's wrong not to talk to your roommate.
situation: Chris lives in an apartment with his roommate and is getting home from an exhausting day at work.
intention: Chris wants to be left alone and get to bed early.
moral_action: Chris greets his roommate and quickly notes that he's turning in early because of a rough day.
moral_consequence: Chris' roommate feels empathy for him and hopes that he feels better soon.
immoral_action: Chris walks by his roommate without saying anything and goes straight to his room.
immoral_consequence: Chris' roommate feels ignored by him and thinks he is rude.

norm: It's bad to neglect the needs of others.
situation: Carl is driving a car with his son Tony, and Carl feels hungry.
intention: Carl wants to stop and get food at a restaurant.
moral_action: Carl takes Tony inside the restaurant to eat.
moral_consequence: All parties get nutrition and the taste of food.
immoral_action: Carl parks the car in the hot sun, leaving Tony inside with the windows up while Carl goes and eats inside.
immoral_consequence: Tony succumbs to heat stroke and dies.

norm: You should take into account others disabilities before acting.
situation: Bob was planning a party for all of his friends to enjoy.
intention: Bob wants to finish planning.
moral_action: Bob puts the party on the 1st floor of the building.
moral_consequence: Everyone is able to arrive and have a good time.
immoral_action: Bob puts the party on the 3rd floor of the building.
immoral_consequence: There are no ramps or elevators for the disabled to be able to get to it.

norm: Judging people and kink shaming is wrong.
situation: Alice is meeting a friend who has a new boyfriend and is experimenting with different arousal techniques.
intention: Alice wants to talk about her friend's dating life.
moral_action: Alice asks questions about how effective the arousal techniques are.
moral_consequence: Alice's friend will feel comfortable discussing intimate matters with Alice.
immoral_action: Alice says what her friend is doing is against nature and forbidden by a higher power.
immoral_consequence: Alice's friend will cut the meeting short and avoid Alice in the future.

norm: It's hurtful to be distrustful of your significant other.
situation: Dania spots her girlfriend Christina walking into a club with her ex.
intention: Dania wants to confront Christina.
moral_action: Dania shares her insecurities and her trust in a text to Christina before leaving the area.
moral_consequence: Christina leaves to club early to spend time with Dania.
immoral_action: Dania walks into the club and accuses Christina of getting back together with her ex behind his back.
immoral_consequence: Christina breaks up with Dania.

norm: It's wrong to want to take part in violence.
situation: Joe sees his friends fighting with a gang of people in the park.
intention: Joe wants to react to the fighting.
moral_action: Joe asks his friends to run and stop fighting.
moral_consequence: Joe and his friends run to a safe place and are free from danger.
immoral_action: Joe joins the fighting hoping that it will help his friends.
immoral_consequence: Joe and his friends all get caught by the police.

norm: It's not okay to throw someone's things outside.
situation: Ben keeps putting his dirty clothes into Louis' hamper and Louis is tired of it.
intention: Louis wants to keep Ben's clothes separate from his.
moral_action: Louis buys Ben his own hamper and tells Ben to use that instead.
moral_consequence: Ben pays back Louis for the hamper and starts putting his dirty clothes in his own hamper.
immoral_action: Louis decides to throw out Ben's clothes that were in his hamper into the lawn.
immoral_consequence: Ben gets mad at Louis for throwing his clothes outside, and Louis shouts back that Ben should wash his own clothes.

norm: It's bad to lie to people with a fake review.
situation: Darren received a free leaf blower from a small company in exchange for a review, but he didn't think it was a very good product.
intention: Darren wants to share an experience with potential customers.
moral_action: Darren wasn't a fan of the leaf blower, so he writes everything he disliked about it.
moral_consequence: When potential buyers read Darren's review they decide to avoid the product and saving money.
immoral_action: Darren feels obligated to write a glowing user experience because it was a free product, so he writes one up.
immoral_consequence: When customers purchase the leaf blower they are all disappointed.

norm: It's wrong for people to misrepresent themselves to others.
situation: John is at the baseball game when the person beside him introduces himself as Dave and asks John where he works.
intention: John wants to respond to Dave's question.
moral_action: John tells Dave the truth, that he is a male flight attendant.
moral_consequence: Dave respects John for telling the truth, and asks John if he has any flight discounts he can hook up.
immoral_action: John tells Dave that he is a supreme court judge, but that his nomination hasn't been made public yet due to technicalities.
immoral_consequence: Dave obviously knows John is lying as there are no secret supreme court judges, and immediately becomes uncomfortable sitting next to John.

norm: It's good to confess to your crush.
situation: George has been developing strong feelings for a girl named Beth in his high school English class.
intention: George wants to talk to someone about his feelings.
moral_action: George pulls Beth aside one day after school and confesses his feelings for her.
moral_consequence: Beth tells George she feels the same way, and she agrees to go out on a date with him.
immoral_action: George tells his best friend that he has a crush on Beth.
immoral_consequence: George never works up the courage to talk to Beth and his love remains unrequited.

norm: It's wrong to slap your best friend in the face.
situation: Hugh is arguing with his best friend about who has the best baseball team.
intention: Hugh wants to win the argument.
moral_action: Hugh pulls up the statistics about all the baseball teams to prove his point.
moral_consequence: Hugh wins the argument because his friend can't deny the overwhelming data about Hugh's team.
immoral_action: Hugh smacks his friend in the face for saying Hugh's team is lousy.
immoral_consequence: Hugh get charged with assault by his best friend who never speaks to him again.

norm: It's obnoxious to constantly prattle on about yourself.
situation: Jennifer is going out on a first date.
intention: Jennifer wants to connect romantically.
moral_action: Jennifer asks her date questions about himself while talking a moderate amount about herself.
moral_consequence: Jennifer's date feels interested to get to know Jennifer more.
immoral_action: Jennifer talks non-stop about herself throughout the date.
immoral_consequence: Jennifer's date feels like he's being ignored and goes home early.

norm: Parents and children should discuss their issues calmly without anger.
situation: Pablo is tired of his children not feeding and walking the dog like they promised when they got him.
intention: Pablo wants to remind his children what their responsibilities are with the dog.
moral_action: Pablo gathers his children and explains to them what their responsibilities are with the dog.
moral_consequence: Pablo's children agree to make a schedule showing when each child is responsible for walking and feeding the dog.
immoral_action: Pablo gathers his children together and yells at them at the top of his lungs about their duty to feed and walk the dog.
immoral_consequence: Pablo's children are scared of their dad and in the future don't share problems they experience for fear he'll get mad at them.

norm: Employees shouldn't falsify time cards at work
situation: John works at an accounting firm.
intention: John wants to make some overtime this month.
moral_action: John works and bills 60 hours one week because he worked more than the usual 40 hours.
moral_consequence: John's bosses notice the extra time and work he did, so they promote him.
immoral_action: John decides to bill a 60 hour week when he only worked 40 hours this week.
immoral_consequence: John gets fired when he is caught stealing hours from the company.

norm: It is bad to be mean to your significant other
situation: Lilly isn't feeling well, so she lays down in bed to rest, when her husband Chris comes in the room to check on her.
intention: Lilly wants to respond to Chris.
moral_action: Lilly tells Chris that she has a migraine and thanks him for being concerned, so he goes out to the store for some asprin.
moral_consequence: Chris is glad to have helped and Lilly, and she feels better because he brought her medicine.
immoral_action: Lilly instantly tells Chris to get out because he's disturbing her.
immoral_consequence: Chris feels down because he was concerned for Lilly's well being and she feels guilty afterwards.

norm: It's good to get people gifts for Christmas.
situation: It is getting late in December and Jim is getting excited about the upcoming holiday.
intention: Jim wants to attend Christmas at a family member's house.
moral_action: Jim shows up with various gifts for the people in attendance.
moral_consequence: People open their gifts and all recipients of gifts from Jim thanked him for his thoughtfulness.
immoral_action: Jim shows up to his family member's house with out any presents.
immoral_consequence: People begin to act cold toward Jim when they realize none of the presents were from him.

norm: You shouldn't take Xanax if it wasn't prescribed to you.
situation: Due to the pandemic, Anders moved back home and has been feeling depressed and anxious.
intention: Anders wants to relieve his anxiety.
moral_action: Anders talks to his primary care doctor about his anxiety, who gives Anders a short term prescription for Xanax and the contact number of a therapist.
moral_consequence: The prescription helps Anders deal with anxiety for a time, while learning long-term coping skills from his therapist.
immoral_action: Anders takes some Xanax from his parent's medicine cabinet.
immoral_consequence: Anders becomes dependent on Xanax and develops an addiction.

norm: Smoking cigarettes is considered an unhealthy habit.
situation: Mindy is a busy college student that also works full time.
intention: Mindy wants to find a way to relive stress.
moral_action: Mindy begins taking Yoga classes.
moral_consequence: Mindy improves her strength, balance, and health.
immoral_action: Mindy begins smoking cigarettes.
immoral_consequence: Mindy developes lung cancer and dies.

norm: "It's rude to call short guys ""boys"" and not ""men."""
situation: Darla is on a date with a shorter man.
intention: Darla wants to break the ice.
moral_action: Darla tells some funny stories about her week and things that she has seen.
moral_consequence: Darla's date feels relaxed and is impressed with her confidence and sense of humor.
immoral_action: Darla makes a joke about the man's height and asks if he shops in the little boy's section.
immoral_consequence: Darla's date becomes offended and storms out of the restaurant.

norm: It is phony to act differently online and in person.
situation: Emily is answering an online dating ad from Sam, a paralegal, whom she finds interesting.
intention: Sam wants to meet Emily in person.
moral_action: Sam acts the same way online that he does in real life, and is honest about his work.
moral_consequence: Emily finds Sam likeable and charming when they meet in real life, and she agrees to go out with him again.
immoral_action: Sam pretends he is a lawyer online, and looks things up on the internet to make it seem like he is more knowledgeable than he really is.
immoral_consequence: Emily finds out Sam is only a paralegal, not the suave lawyer he seems, and rejects him after one date.

norm: It's rude to not do something you promised to do.
situation: Jeff's friend Josh is having his twenty-first birthday party and Jeff volunteers to be the designated driver.
intention: Jeff wants to have a good time.
moral_action: Jeff spends the night in lively conversation with Josh, and drives Josh home after closing time.
moral_consequence: Jeff and Josh's friendship grows stronger in light of Jeff being a reliable friend.
immoral_action: Jeff decides to have a few drinks during the birthday celebrations and ends up getting too drunk to drive.
immoral_consequence: Jeff and Josh are forced to walk several miles home from the bar at the end of the night.

norm: It is wrong to bully people.
situation: Jasmine just transferred to a new school and hasn't made any friends yet.
intention: Jasmine wants to be popular at her new school.
moral_action: Jasmine participated at the talent show telling a lot of jokes.
moral_consequence: Everyone in the school thought she was really funny and she made a lot of friends.
immoral_action: Jasmine said mean things to a girl at lunch trying to get the other kids to laugh with her.
immoral_consequence: A bunch of girls came over and told Jasmine that wasn't cool, and she never made any friends at that school.

norm: You shouldn't have a flashing porch light because it's annoying.
situation: Tim is decorating for Halloween, and he notices that his decorations look nice but are similar to what he sees on other houses.
intention: Tim wants to make his house stand out when people pass by.
moral_action: Bill buys a few more strands of lights and creates a spider web effect with them in a creative way.
moral_consequence: Some of Bill's neighbors compliment his use of light and Bill is happy that he has created something unique.
immoral_action: Bill installs a powerful strobe light in place of his normal porch light, streaming a powerful, pulsing ray of light out into the night.
immoral_consequence: Everyone with a direct view of the light is highly irritated by it and it becomes a distraction for passing motorists, creating a safety hazard.

norm: It's rude to use a relative's computer without their knowledge.
situation: Kevin is at his aunt's house, which has his aunt's computer that has unsaved info on it, and has to send an important email.
intention: Kevin wants to send the important email.
moral_action: Kevin asks his aunt if he can use the computer to send an email.
moral_consequence: Kevin's aunt warns him about the open programs, so Kevin sends the email without closing them.
immoral_action: Kevin logs on to his aunt's computer without asking, closes the open programs, and sends the email.
immoral_consequence: Kevin's aunt loses several hours worth of work from Kevin closing the programs.

norm: You shouldn't judge someone based on their past.
situation: Dave met a girl whom he loves but had a past criminal record.
intention: Dave wants to date the girl.
moral_action: Dave invites the girl out and ask her to be his girlfriend.
moral_consequence: The girl thanks Dave for his love and agrees to be his girlfriend.
immoral_action: Dave invites the girl out for one-night stand and leaves her thereafter.
immoral_consequence: The girl feels sad and hurt.

norm: You shouldn't marry your family members.
situation: James fell in love with his cousin as soon as he saw her at a family reunion.
intention: James wants to marry someone with whom he's in love.
moral_action: James avoids his cousin, so he won't feel tempted, and instead starts wooing an old friend from high school.
moral_consequence: James gradually forgets his cousin, falls in love with his friend, marries her and has a healthy child.
immoral_action: James proposes to his cousin and marries her despite the objections of their family.
immoral_consequence: The cousin gets pregnant with a baby with serious genetic defects, and James has to pay for a therapeutic abortion.

norm: It's frowned upon to be loud.
situation: Marcus stand in the hallway next to the testing area checking the results of his test, and he receives a perfect score.
intention: Marcus wants to express his excitement.
moral_action: Marcus shares the results of his test on Facebook and Twitter.
moral_consequence: Marcus' father texts him saying that he saw the post, and offers to take him out for dinner.
immoral_action: Marcus exclaims that he made a perfect score on the exam in a loud tone jumping up and down.
immoral_consequence: Marcus is escorted out of the building for being loud in the testing area.

norm: It's rude to make derogatory comments about someone else's food.
situation: Dan is sitting next to James in the school cafeteria.
intention: Dan wants to socialize during his lunch break.
moral_action: Dan tells James that his sandwich looks interesting and asks what's in it.
moral_consequence: James tells Dan how he made his sandwich, and they talk about different foods they like.
immoral_action: Dan tells James that the sandwich he is eating looks disgusting.
immoral_consequence: James is annoyed by Dan's insult and gets up to move to another table.

norm: It's bad to not share with others when you can.
situation: Jen is getting off after a long day at work soon and is far too tired to prepare dinner.
intention: Jen wants to find an easy dinner solution.
moral_action: Jen picks up enough pizza for her and the family.
moral_consequence: Jen feels good for surprising her family with pizza.
immoral_action: Jen picks up a smaller pizza and enjoys it entirely on her own.
immoral_consequence: Jen wishes she shared the delicious pizza with her family.

norm: You shouldn't criticize a teammate's work.
situation: John's coworker asks for questions or feedback after giving a work presentation.
intention: John wants to respond to the coworker.
moral_action: John provides his coworker with praise and constructive comments.
moral_consequence: The coworker feels proud and effective.
immoral_action: John tells his coworker that the presentation was terrible and a waste of time.
immoral_consequence: John's coworker feels bad for the rest of the day.

norm: You shouldn't let criminal behavior become an obsession.
situation: Mark used to illegally download movies, but now he has a job.
intention: Mark wants to watch more movies.
moral_action: Mark buys multiple streaming services so that he can watch as many movies as he can.
moral_consequence: Mark is able to support content creators and gets to support content creators.
immoral_action: Mark continues to download movies, because he loves how easy they are to obtain.
immoral_consequence: Mark is taking money away from content creators and is breaking the law.

norm: You shouldn't retaliate against people.
situation: Lydia has been bullied for a long time at school by a group of mean girls.
intention: Lydia wants the mean girls to be punished for what they did to her.
moral_action: Lydia forcefully denounces the mean girls' bullying behaviors to the authorities.
moral_consequence: The mean girls are punished and Lydia is commended for her bravery in denouncing them.
immoral_action: Lydia decides to retaliate and plays an elaborate prank on the mean girls, who suffer greatly from it.
immoral_consequence: Lydia is exposed as the author of the prank and ends up being punished for it.

norm: You should return found belongings to their rightful owner.
situation: Sue is a cashier at a convenience store and a customer, Bart, left his hat behind when paying.
intention: Sue wants to decide what to do.
moral_action: Sue runs out after Bart and hands him his hat that he left behind.
moral_consequence: Bart is thankful to Sue for giving him back his hat, and he leaves a happy customer.
immoral_action: Sue, having a few more customers decides to take care of them and assumes Bart will come back for his hat.
immoral_consequence: Bart drives away and when he realizes it's gone, can't remember where he left it, so now he has to buy a new one.

norm: You shouldn't kick your neighbor's dog.
situation: Daniel notices his neighbor's dog destroying his flower bed.
intention: Daniel wants to get the dog to leave his garden alone.
moral_action: Daniel chases the dog away and has a talk with his neighbors about controlling their dog.
moral_consequence: The dog is sppoked but safe and his owners assure Daniel they will do better.
immoral_action: Daniel runs up to the dog and kicks it as hard as he can.
immoral_consequence: The dog is injured and Daniel's neighbor files a report against him.

norm: It is bad to kill animals.
situation: Joe trains, raises and cares for horses involved in professional horse-racing and one of his horses becomes injured in a race.
intention: Joe needs to figure out what to do with the injured horse.
moral_action: Joe decides to retire the horse and put it through physical therapy.
moral_consequence: Joe is happy that he seems to be making a positive impact on the horse's health.
immoral_action: Joe decides to put shoot the horse and ship it to the glue factory.
immoral_consequence: Joe is haunted by the horse's final moments and is depressed.

norm: You should be grateful for help.
situation: Sun is struggling to lift a heavy box from the floor when Bruce comes by and helps him.
intention: Sun wants to move the heavy box onto a shelf.
moral_action: Sun smiles at Bruce and offer to repay Bruce for helping him.
moral_consequence: Sun buys Bruce a coffee and they chat about themselves.
immoral_action: Sun grumbles to Bruce that he could have lifted the box onto the shelf by himself.
immoral_consequence: Bruce tells Sun to go screw himself and walks away.

norm: It's good to have insurance for your car.
situation: Ace buys a used car from a friend, but hasn't gotten insurance just yet.
intention: Ace wants to go for a drive.
moral_action: Ace goes on his phone and buys car insurance before driving off.
moral_consequence: A police officer pulls him over, sees that he has insurance, and leaves.
immoral_action: Ace goes for a drive right away, promising to buy insurance later.
immoral_consequence: A police officer pulls him over and fines him for not having insurance.

norm: It's wrong to steal someone else's packages.
situation: Mark notices the mailman placing his neighbor's playstation 4 package on their doorstep.
intention: Mark wants a playstation 4.
moral_action: Mark does extra chores and odd jobs around the neighborhood earning enough cash to buy his own playstation 4.
moral_consequence: Mark feels a sense of pride when he unboxes his playstation 4.
immoral_action: Mark takes his neighbor's package into his home to claim the playstation 4.
immoral_consequence: His neighbor shames Mark on the internet pressuring him into giving him money along with the playstation four.

norm: It's unexpected for hair to change drastically.
situation: Ray has a wedding coming up, and he hasn't gotten a haircut in forever.
intention: Ray wants to get a haircut.
moral_action: Ray asks for a clean haircut that has a part on the side.
moral_consequence: People at Ray's wedding like Ray's haircut and want to take pictures with him.
immoral_action: Ray tells his barber to give him a mohawk cut.
immoral_consequence: People at Ray's wedding think he's weird and laugh at him.

norm: It's wrong to use things that aren't yours.
situation: Sam is very tired and hungry upon arriving home after a long day of work.
intention: Sam wants to avoid using too much energy making dinner.
moral_action: Sam orders a pizza as an easy fix.
moral_consequence: Sam's roommate enjoys the rest of his leftovers.
immoral_action: Sam uses his roommate's leftovers with a couple other ingredients to make a quick and easy meal.
immoral_consequence: Sam's roommate is disappointed because he was looking forward to eating the leftovers.

norm: It's bad to treat people rudely online.
situation: Marry is  annoyed with a new user Sarah for asking a common question in the subreddit.
intention: Marry wants to respond to Sarah.
moral_action: Marry directs Sarah to the subreddit's resource post with answers to frequently asked questions.
moral_consequence: Mary gains the respect of the moderating team, and she becomes a candidate for moderator.
immoral_action: Marry tells Sarah that she should pay attention because her question has been asked several times on the subreddit.
immoral_consequence: Marry's behavior deters people from asking questions.

norm: It's not okay to be a bully.
situation: Sam is at school, has had chronic low-self esteem this week, and it's the middle of the day.
intention: Sam wants to feel powerful during the day.
moral_action: Sam goes to the school gym and lifts weights, and feels confident.
moral_consequence: Sam gets his exercise for the day and talks to others in the gym.
immoral_action: Sam picks on a student and push him around, and feels strong.
immoral_consequence: Sam gets sent to the principle and feels sorry.

norm: It is naive to trust someone you don't know well.
situation: Ash is walking around a used car lot looking all the cars and truck they have for sale.
intention: Ash wants to get a different vehicle.
moral_action: Ash gets the VIN number off a car he likes and runs it through a car history website.
moral_consequence: Ash finds a good one-owner used car that has been well maintained over it's lifetime.
immoral_action: Ash gives in to the hard push of a salesperson and buys a car that is supposed to be a real jewel according to the sales pitch.
immoral_consequence: After taking the used car home, Ash has a lot of trouble with it because it turns out to be a flood car.

norm: It's not good to be a snitch.
situation: Robert witnesses a kid stealing candy from Walmart while he is waiting in line to pay.
intention: Robert wants to teach the boy that it's wrong to steal.
moral_action: Robert walks up to the boy and tells him that it is wrong to steal, making him promise not to steal in the future.
moral_consequence: The boy listens to Robert and does not steal anymore in the future.
immoral_action: Robert walks up to the boy, asks where his parent is and then tells his mom what the boy did.
immoral_consequence: The mother starts to violently yell and smack the boy on the butt, causing him a lot of pain.

norm: It's rude to come over without permission.
situation: Rudy is feeling lonely and misses his friends.
intention: Rudy wants to hang out with his friend Fred.
moral_action: Rudy calls Fred to ask if he wants to hang out later.
moral_consequence: Rudy and Fred go out for dinner and drinks and have a great time.
immoral_action: Rudy stops by Fred's house to socialize with him.
immoral_consequence: Fred is surprised and irritated that his friend came over unannounced.

norm: It's rude to continuously lie to someone
situation: Newly divorced Olivia is having lunch with her mom, when her mom asks her how her husband is doing.
intention: Olivia wants to respond to her mom's question.
moral_action: Olivia tells her mom that she's been hiding the fact that she got divorced a few weeks ago, but she has to come clean about it at this point.
moral_consequence: Olivia's mom offers to help her with anything that she needs and offers her emotional support.
immoral_action: Olivia continues to hide the fact that she's been divorced for a few weeks now and pretends that her marriage and husband are fine.
immoral_consequence: Olivia's mom is thrilled to hear this and thinks that everything is fine in Olivia's life.

norm: It is wrong to give your dog up.
situation: Jill and her boyfriend Tim recently moved in together and Tim realizes he is allergic to Jill's elderly dog.
intention: Jill wants her boyfriend to not experience allergies.
moral_action: Jill gives her boyfriend allergy medication.
moral_consequence: Jill's dog gets to live out its life in the same home and Tim no longer experiences allergy symptoms.
immoral_action: Jill gives her dog to the animal shelter.
immoral_consequence: The dog is unable to be adopted and is put to sleep.

norm: It's good to give tips on games to people.
situation: Steve sees his friend Will playing a game, but Will is terrible at playing it.
intention: Steve wants to watch Will play.
moral_action: Steve watches Will and gives him some pointers on how to do better.
moral_consequence: Will slowly improves and eventually conquers the game.
immoral_action: Steve sits down to watch and records Will's poor performance, then uploads it to the internet.
immoral_consequence: Steve's video goes viral and Will is completely embarrassed.

norm: It's good to learn new things from your parents.
situation: Kent's parents are warning Kent that taking a large home loan with no down payment is a bad idea.
intention: Kent wants to decide on the home loan.
moral_action: Kent decides to wait a few years until he's saved a large down payment.
moral_consequence: Kent saves tens of thousands of dollars on the interest payments.
immoral_action: Kent decides to take the home loan and buys the house.
immoral_consequence: Kent pays almost the cost of the house in interest payments alone.

norm: You shouldn't curse at others.
situation: Jeff is trying to merge onto the highway when another car cuts him off.
intention: Jake wants to convey his displeasure at the other driver.
moral_action: Jake bites his tongue and instead honks his horn at the driver who cut him off.
moral_consequence: Jake feels better after the display of passive-aggressiveness and continues driving.
immoral_action: Jake hurls profanities at the other driver, who stops when he hears them and squeezes his 7ft frame out of the car.
immoral_consequence: Jake gets a quick trip to the emergency room after the altercation.

norm: It is bad to be selfish and self centered
situation: Adam and his four friends are sitting at the table where there is a tray of 30 cookies.
intention: Adam wants to eat twenty cookies.
moral_action: Adam takes a few cookies and then orders more for himself from the waiter.
moral_consequence: Adam's friends each get their fair share of cookies and are happy.
immoral_action: Adam takes 20 cookies quickly off the tray and stashes them in his jacket.
immoral_consequence: Adam's friends get very upset and demand he give them back and be fair.

norm: It's frowned upon to work as a prostitute.
situation: Cindy is a college student who owes a lot of money on tuition and books.
intention: Cindy wants to be able to make money to pay her debts.
moral_action: Cindy gets a job working at the local movie theater on weekends.
moral_consequence: Cindy gets to see movies for free whenever she wants to.
immoral_action: Cindy gets a job with a pimp, working as a prostitute at night.
immoral_consequence: Cindy's professor sees her on the street and calls her out in class in front of everyone.

norm: It's bad to commit crimes and wind up in prison.
situation: Jeremy is dissatisfied with how the government operates in his town.
intention: Jeremy wants to express his frustration with government.
moral_action: Jeremy protests against the government by holding a sign at a rally.
moral_consequence: Jeremy meets other people that have similar views.
immoral_action: Jeremy throws a Molotov cocktail at city hall.
immoral_consequence: Jeremy gets arrested, prosecuted, then sent to prison.

norm: It's bad to give people the silent treatment.
situation: Liz is trying to read her book on a bus but another passenger keeps trying to talk to her.
intention: Liz wants the passenger to leave her alone.
moral_action: Liz tells the passenger that she's just not in the mood to talk and wants to read her book.
moral_consequence: The passenger sees that Liz isn't feeling very social and leaves her alone.
immoral_action: Liz simply doesn't respond to anything the passenger says and stays quiet.
immoral_consequence: The passenger feels that she is being treated very rudely by Liz and stops talking to her.

norm: It's wrong to ditch a date.
situation: Emily and Alex decide to meet for a drink after chatting on a dating app, but Emily realizes right away that there is no romantic chemistry between them.
intention: Emily wants to end the dating relationship.
moral_action: Emily ends the date after one drink and tells Alex that she does not want to continue to see him romantically.
moral_consequence: Alex agrees that there is no romantic chemistry and does not contact Emily again.
immoral_action: Emily tells Alex that she is going to the bathroom, but then she leaves through the back door instead.
immoral_consequence: Alex's feelings are hurt, and he gives up on using dating apps.

norm: It's important to stand up for what you believe in.
situation: Marry is browsing Twitter when she spots an anti mask tweet from Todd.
intention: Marry wants to reply to the tweet.
moral_action: Marry drops links to articles by scientists talking about the benefits of wearing masks.
moral_consequence: Tod accepts Mary's point of view and decides to order a mask.
immoral_action: Marry insults the poster's intelligence.
immoral_consequence: Marry's followers see the tweet and mimic her response hurting Todd's feelings.

norm: It's not okay to get overly worked up about things.
situation: Tom is running late for work but stops for coffee anyway, which is taking a lot longer than he expected.
intention: Tom wants to speed the process of getting his coffee along.
moral_action: Tom asks the Barista if there is anything he can do to get the coffee more quickly, and explains that he needs to get to work right away.
moral_consequence: The Barista offers to give Tom a ready made drink instead, saving him some time and relieving pressure on everyone.
immoral_action: Tom tells the Barista that if he gets into trouble at work over the wait, he will be back to get the young man fired from the coffee shop.
immoral_consequence: The Barista apologizes and explains that brewing the coffee takes a certain amount of time, which he has no control over, and Tom feels guilty.

norm: It's mean to criticize your host.
situation: While at a cocktail party hosted by her friend a waiter spills red wine on Patty's dress.
intention: Patty wants to inform her friend of what happened.
moral_action: Patty informs her friend of what transpired and asks for help removing the stain.
moral_consequence: Patty's friend is mortified and offers a change of clothes as well as to pay for her dry cleaning.
immoral_action: Patty angrily condemns her friend for hiring incompetent staff for her party.
immoral_consequence: Patty's friend excludes her from all future events that she is hosting.

norm: Racism is not acceptable.
situation: Jim has just moved to a new neighborhood with few minorities.
intention: Jim wants his neighbors to like him.
moral_action: Jim makes some purposefully bad puns.
moral_consequence: Jims' neighbors think he is goofy but a nice guy.
immoral_action: Jim makes a racist joke at a housewarming party.
immoral_consequence: Jim's neighbors are appalled and avoid Jim from then on.

norm: You should do favors for others.
situation: Sandra's sister asks her to go to the store to buy her something as she is too tired.
intention: Sandra wants to respond to her sister.
moral_action: Sandra says she will go to the store for her sister and asks her sister to help her too the next time she asks.
moral_consequence: Sandra's sister is grateful for her help and is happy to return the gesture in the future.
immoral_action: Sandra says she won't go to the store just because her sister is too lazy to go herself.
immoral_consequence: Sandra's sister is annoyed that she won't help her and decides not to help Sandra next time she asks for help.

norm: You shouldn't get involved romantically with your teachers or trainers.
situation: Sam is very transfixed by his teacher, he's never been this smitten.
intention: Sam wants to address his teacher with these feelings.
moral_action: Sam tells the teacher how he feels, but tells the teacher he knows it's wrong.
moral_consequence: The teacher sits with Sam a long time, and explains this is common, and he'll get over his feelings soon.
immoral_action: Sam tells the teacher exactly how he feels, stating he wants a relationship.
immoral_consequence: The teacher gives in, and gives him a relationship, they get caught and the teacher gets fired.

norm: It's nice to do things to help your friends.
situation: Kevin has the afternoon free from work, and his friend Danial asked people to help him move furniture on Facebook.
intention: Kevin wants to have fun.
moral_action: Kevin decides to help Danial while his favorite songs play on the stereo.
moral_consequence: Danial feels better in his newly organized room.
immoral_action: Kevin decides to spend the afternoon playing Call of Duty.
immoral_consequence: Danial injures himself trying to lift a heavy bookshelf alone.

norm: It's bad to cuss out your family.
situation: Belinda was already stressed after taking a test when her mother asked her to start cooking dinner.
intention: Belinda wants to rest instead of cooking.
moral_action: Belinda tells her mother that she's tired and stressed from her test.
moral_consequence: Belinda's mother agrees to cook tonight if Belinda cooks dinner tomorrow.
immoral_action: Belinda swears at her mother and says that she never does any work around the house.
immoral_consequence: Belinda's mother swears back at her and says she's not cooking, so Belinda can either cook or go hungry.

norm: If someone tells a joke it's polite to laugh.
situation: Anne's boss, who has to fill a manager position, is talking to her at her lunch break, and he makes a dumb joke.
intention: Anne wants to get back to work.
moral_action: Anne laughs at the joke, then says that she needs to get back to work.
moral_consequence: Her boss finds her friendly, and she later gets a promotion to manager.
immoral_action: Anne ignores the joke and tells her boss she needs to get back to work.
immoral_consequence: Anne's boss sees her as not people-friendly and passes her over for promotion to manager.

norm: You shouldn't download files at work that aren't allowed.
situation: Karen is very bored while working without music, she feels it makes her work better too.
intention: Karen wants to get more music on her computer.
moral_action: Karen buys herself a Spotify membership, so she can have some more music while she works.
moral_consequence: Karen learns about some new artists she never knew, and works better too.
immoral_action: Karen looks up how to download music illegally, and decides to go ahead and do it.
immoral_consequence: Karen's boss finds out she used the internet to download something illegal and fires her.

norm: It's kind to honor your mother.
situation: James' friend invited him to go out camping on Mother's Day.
intention: James wants to go camping with his friend.
moral_action: James makes his mother breakfast in bed and gives her a Mother's Day present before leaving around 11 AM.
moral_consequence: James and his friend still arrive at the campsite with plenty of time to set up their tent before dark.
immoral_action: James leaves at five in the morning without even saying goodbye to his mother.
immoral_consequence: James' mother's eyes look red-rimmed when he gets home a few days later.

norm: It's important to raise your children in a happy home.
situation: Linda's step husband is a jerk to her son, and his son hates him.
intention: Linda wants the best for her son.
moral_action: Linda decides to split with her husband for her son.
moral_consequence: Linda's son becomes happier as no one in the house would be mean to him anymore.
immoral_action: Linda decides to stay with her step husband so that her son has a dad in her life.
immoral_consequence: Linda's son is miserable and continues to be mentally abused by his stepdad.

norm: It's not okay to push people off on your friends.
situation: John's distant cousin Fred comes to spend a week with John, but John can't stand being around him.
intention: John wants to find a way to minimize his exposure to Fred.
moral_action: John rents Fred a bunch of movies and takes overtime at work.
moral_consequence: Fred has a way to stay entertained, and doesn't feel put out, because John is dealing with work responsibilities.
immoral_action: John drives Fred to a bar where his friends are, and then sneaks out to spend the evening alone.
immoral_consequence: Fred is uncomfortable around a bunch of strangers, and John's friends have their evening ruined by an obnoxious person.

norm: It's polite to wait your turn.
situation: John was waiting in line at the post office yesterday morning.
intention: John wanted to get a book of stamps.
moral_action: John stood in line and waited until it was his turn to buy his book of stamps.
moral_consequence: The man in line behind him paid for John's book of stamps.
immoral_action: John walked to the front of the line and demanded to be served.
immoral_consequence: The crowd yelled for John to get in the back of the line.

norm: It's bad to want to commit suicide.
situation: Omar hasn't been feeling good inside lately and is talking with his friend Chris who asks him what's wrong.
intention: Omar wants to tell Chris his inner feelings.
moral_action: Omar tells Chris that he's torn up inside and that he's thinking about getting some help.
moral_consequence: Chris is happy to hear that Omar is open to seeking help and tells him he'll drive him to the doctor if he wants.
immoral_action: Omar tells Chris he's torn up inside and that he's probably going to kill himself soon.
immoral_consequence: Chris is stressed beyond belief as his mind scrambles for a way to get Omar to stop thinking that way.

norm: You shouldn't just give up on life.
situation: Devin hasn't been feeling great ever since he got laid off from his job.
intention: Devin wants to feel less pain.
moral_action: Devin sees a therapist in order to get over what's been bothering him.
moral_consequence: Devin is able to find another job eventually, and his family is better taken care of.
immoral_action: Devin kills himself in order to stop feeling so much pain.
immoral_consequence: Devin never gets to experience anything anymore, and his family misses him greatly.

norm: It's rude to not want your partner to call you.
situation: John is leaving on a short one-day trip to attend a business meeting, and his wife, Jan, tells him that she'll call him after he lands.
intention: John wants to respond to Jan's statement.
moral_action: John tells Jan that it's a great idea and that he can't wait to hear her voice, but that the call has to be quick since he has meetings.
moral_consequence: Jan is delighted that her husband is eager to talk to her as soon as possible, and she feels loved.
immoral_action: John tells Jan that he's going to have the meetings pretty much right away and not to bother calling since he'll be back the next day.
immoral_consequence: Jan is suspicious of what John might really be up to and is feeling insecure she also thinks her husband doesn't like talking to her.

norm: It's hurtful to abandon someone.
situation: Joe has a young son named Josh.
intention: Joe needs to feel less stressed.
moral_action: Joe decides to take Josh to the movies, so they can both relax.
moral_consequence: Josh enjoys the quality time spent with his father.
immoral_action: Joe says he's going to the corner store, leaves and never comes back.
immoral_consequence: Josh grows up without a father, with emotionally devastating consequences.

norm: It's good to lend your things to people in need.
situation: Travis's neighbor was pulling out of his driveway when his car broke down on the road.
intention: Travis wants the car out of the roadway.
moral_action: Travis offers his tools for the neighbor to get his car running again.
moral_consequence: The neighbor fixes the car and pulls it back into the driveway.
immoral_action: Travis calls a tow truck to complain about the car blocking the roadway.
immoral_consequence: The tow truck takes the neighbor's car, and he has to pay to get it back.

norm: You shouldn't refuse to leave someplace if they are closing.
situation: Bob is eating at a restaurant that is about to close for the night.
intention: Bob wants to finish his meal.
moral_action: Bob has his meal boxed up to finish at home so the staff can close on time.
moral_consequence: The wait staff is friendly to him when he returns in the future.
immoral_action: Bob takes his time and forces the wait staff to stay half an hour after closing.
immoral_consequence: The wait staff get angry with Bob and the service he receives suffers.

norm: It's not okay to judge someone by their name.
situation: John is at work when he is introduced to a new co-worker named Osama.
intention: John wants to say something to Osasma.
moral_action: John tells Osama hello and offers to help him acclimate himself to the company.
moral_consequence: Osama feels welcomed to the company and feels optimistic about the future.
immoral_action: "John, upon being introduced, tells Osama that he ""doesn't work with terrorists"" and asks Osama why ""he hates America?""."
immoral_consequence: Osama is ashamed for being called a terrorist and is extremely angered by John's racism.

norm: It is bad to drive recklessly
situation: Ray is on a crowded highway and needs to get to work quickly.
intention: Ray wants to deal with the traffic problem.
moral_action: Ray finds a detour, gets off of the highway, and takes the detour.
moral_consequence: The detour has less traffic and Ray arrives at work faster.
immoral_action: Ray quickly weaves between cars and makes efforts to improve his time.
immoral_consequence: Other drivers get angry with Ray and attempt to block his progress.

norm: It is polite to share your tissues with people
situation: Bonnie has a runny nose due to allergies, and asks if she can borrow her co-worker Betty's box of tissues.
intention: Betty doesn't want to listen to Bonnie sniffling all afternoon.
moral_action: Betty gives Bonnie the box of tissues, and they both get their work done.
moral_consequence: Bonnie comes into work the next day with a new box of tissues and a Thank You card for Betty.
immoral_action: Betty refuses to share, and tells Bonnie to go home if she's sick.
immoral_consequence: Bonnie goes home, loses an afternoon's pay, and is peeved at Betty.

norm: You shouldn't ignore someone based on their job.
situation: James is on a blind date and just found out his current partner works as a waiter.
intention: James wants to avoid wasting time with partners he thinks are inadequate.
moral_action: James asks what his partner plans to be doing ten years from now.
moral_consequence: James finds out his partner is a passionate psychology grad student, and they have an interesting conversation about their experiences in therapy.
immoral_action: James immediately loses interest in the conversation and starts playing on his phone.
immoral_consequence: James' partner leaves in less than a minute, but not before explaining that his dad owns the restaurant chain where he works while he's in business school.

norm: You shouldn't believe that religions don't deserve respect.
situation: Gavin hasn't been apart of a religion for a long time, unlike his family.
intention: Gavin wants to join a new religion.
moral_action: Gavin chooses a popular, traditionally moral religion in his country to follow.
moral_consequence: Gavin's family is proud of him for maintaining a good image and Gavin is pleased at them.
immoral_action: Gavin joins the 'Church of Satan' and reads all their literature.
immoral_consequence: Gavin's family chastises Gavin for picking such a selfish religion and Gavin feels insulted.

norm: It's bad to be an alcoholic.
situation: Nancy's mother died recently, and she has been drinking a lot lately to forget her grief.
intention: Nancy wants to get over her grief.
moral_action: Nancy stops drinking and calls up a therapist to help her through her grief.
moral_consequence: Nancy is able to work past her grief and get on with her life.
immoral_action: Nancy drinks more and more, and is always late to work because of the hangovers.
immoral_consequence: Nancy loses her job, which causes her to drink even more.

norm: It's good to want to entertain others.
situation: Clara is having her friend David over to spend the weekend.
intention: Clara wants to watch her favorite show after dinner.
moral_action: Clara asks David if he would like to watch the show with her.
moral_consequence: David feels thankful to be included and watches the show with her.
immoral_action: Clara goes into her bedroom, closes the door, and leaves her friend by himself while she watches the show.
immoral_consequence: Her friend feels left out and confused about why Clara would just disappear.

norm: You should try to instill some confidence in your children.
situation: Brad's son Tim comes home sad one day after school because he did poorly on a big math test.
intention: Brad wants Tim to improve his test scores.
moral_action: Brad tells Tim that he is smart and capable, to keep trying his best and the results will follow.
moral_consequence: Tim feels confident and inspired and does very well on his next math test.
immoral_action: Brad scolds Tim for his poor grade and threatens to ground him if his scores don't improve.
immoral_consequence: Tim feels even worse about his performance and continues to struggle in math class.

norm: It's good to shop around for the best price.
situation: Lily is shopping online, and she just found some shoes she likes, but they seem a bit expensive.
intention: Lily wants to buy a pair of the shoes that she found.
moral_action: Lily decides to search online at other retailers for that specific model of shoe to see if she can find a better deal.
moral_consequence: Lily is able to obtain the shoes at a bargain price and saves a lot of money in the process.
immoral_action: Ignoring the price, Lily puts the shoes in her shopping cart immediately and checks out.
immoral_consequence: Lily pays a pretty hefty price for the pair of shoes which were being upcharged by the seller.

norm: It is rude to joke about a friends mom.
situation: Joe and his friends are joking around and one of his friends gets a good crack in against Joe.
intention: Joe wants to get his friend back.
moral_action: Joe cracks a joke about his friend that is similar to what the two have joked about before.
moral_consequence: Everyone laughs at the joke.
immoral_action: Joe responds by making a crude joke about his friend's mom.
immoral_consequence: Joe's friend is offended and gets upset with Joe.

norm: It's inappropriate to email your colleagues about personal matters.
situation: Jen just broke up with her girlfriend.
intention: Jen needs someone to talk to about it.
moral_action: Jen e-mails her best friend concerning her relationship issues while Jen is on break.
moral_consequence: Jen's coworkers approve of her staying professional.
immoral_action: Jen e-mails her coworkers about her emotional issues following her breakup.
immoral_consequence: Jen's coworkers go to HR about her using company time to complain about personal matters.

norm: You shouldn't date someone that is underage.
situation: John is a senior in college and is currently single.
intention: John wants to go on a date.
moral_action: John takes his 22 year old neighbor to dinner and the movies then has sex with her.
moral_consequence: John and his neighbor develop a relationship and later get married.
immoral_action: John takes his 16 year old neighbor to dinner and the movies then has sex with her.
immoral_consequence: John is arrested for statutory rape.

norm: It is good to pursue your dreams and passions
situation: Lena has to choose between two well-paying jobs - one that is boring but easy, and one that is challenging but more aligned with what she has always wanted to do.
intention: Lena wants to earn good money.
moral_action: Lena chooses the challenging, more exciting job.
moral_consequence: Lena is thrilled by her job and finds herself living her career dream.
immoral_action: Lena chooses the job that is less interesting to her, because it seems easier.
immoral_consequence: Lena is bored at work and feels she is wasting her life.

norm: It's good to try to earn enough money for rent.
situation: Ruth has one pay period left before rent is due.
intention: Ruth wants to take time to herself.
moral_action: Ruth works extra hours during the week but makes sure to give herself two hours of self-care every day.
moral_consequence: Ruth feels tired but finds that her relaxation time makes her feel a lot better every day.
immoral_action: Ruth takes the week off of work to stay home for a spa day and other self care rituals.
immoral_consequence: Ruth's paycheck isn't big enough to cover her rent, and she is charged a late fee.

norm: Kids should respect the wishes of their parent.
situation: Frank wants to go out and catch a movie with his friends, but he's been grounded by his parents.
intention: Frank wants to have a good time.
moral_action: Frank decides to read his favorite book while staying home for the night.
moral_consequence: Frank's parents appreciate his good behavior and allow him to go out with his friends the following night.
immoral_action: Frank sneaks out of the house while his parents are distracted and catches the movie.
immoral_consequence: Frank's parents find out he's gone and catch him when he returns, grounding him for even longer.

norm: It's wrong to park your car illegally.
situation: Tim can't find a parking spot nearby the mall on a rainy day.
intention: Tim wants to park close to the mall to avoid the rain.
moral_action: Tim waits for a while until a closer spots opens up that he parks in.
moral_consequence: Tim gets to park close enough to avoid most of the rain.
immoral_action: Tim decides to pull up on the curb and park right by the front door.
immoral_consequence: Tim's car get's towed away and Tim has to take the bus home and pay to get his car back.

norm: It's weird to tell your mother about your sex life.
situation: Mary has just started to date David, and she is in love with him.
intention: Mary wants to tell someone about her sex life with David.
moral_action: Mary calls her best friend to tell her all about her sex life with David.
moral_consequence: Mary and her friend laugh and talk about their sex life for hours.
immoral_action: Mary starts gushing to her mother about her and David's sex life while on a lunch date.
immoral_consequence: Mary's mother excuses herself and leaves from the restaurant earlier than planned.

norm: Stealing from a business is illegal and morally wrong.
situation: Jeff is at the store looking for a new pen.
intention: Jeff wants to return home with a pen.
moral_action: Jeff brings a pen to the cashier and purchases a pen with cash before returning home.
moral_consequence: Jeff is delighted with his new pen and uses it to write a postcard to his mom.
immoral_action: Jeff takes a pen, puts it in his pocket and leaves the store.
immoral_consequence: Jeff is visited by police that night and taken to be questioned.

norm: You shouldn't be friends with someone who is a dirtbag.
situation: Conan is a freshman in college and is meeting other students, some of them nice, others much less so.
intention: Conan wants to have friends.
moral_action: Conan decides to befriend a very creative and interesting guy.
moral_consequence: Conan learns a lot of new and fun things with his new friend and becomes a better person.
immoral_action: Conan chooses to become friends with a party guy who has the reputation of being disrespectful with women.
immoral_consequence: Conan's new friend is a bad influence on him.

norm: It's good to take your friends' input into consideration.
situation: Wes asks his friends what he should get his girlfriend for her birthday.
intention: Wes wants to get something good for his girlfriend.
moral_action: Wes considers his friends' advice and gets his girlfriend a perfect gift.
moral_consequence: Wes's friends are happy for him when she likes the gift they suggested.
immoral_action: Wes dismisses his friends' advice and gets tickets to a sports game.
immoral_consequence: Wes's friends are annoyed and don't offer advice in the future.

norm: It is good to encourage your boyfriend to stay sober.
situation: Samantha's boyfriend has been binge drinking large amounts of alcohol every night for the past few months.
intention: Samantha wants to help her boyfriend to be happy.
moral_action: Samantha tells her boyfriend that she is worried about how much he is drinking, and gently tells him she would support him even if he stopped drinking.
moral_consequence: Samantha's boyfriend slows down his drinking, and eventually gets to the point where he only drinks on special occassions.
immoral_action: Samantha knowing her boyfriend enjoys drinking, never says anything and starts drinking with him.
immoral_consequence: Samantha and her boyfriend start getting into drunken arguments and end up splitting up.

norm: It's kind to give your friends Christmas presents.
situation: Lance has been invited to spend Christmas with his friend.
intention: Lance wants to go to see his friend on Christmas.
moral_action: Lance buys a nice present for his friend and gives it to them when he visits.
moral_consequence: Lance's friend is happy that Lance took the time to buy them something for the holiday.
immoral_action: Lance goes to visit his friend empty handed and has nothing to give his friend after his friend gives him a gift.
immoral_consequence: Lance's friend thinks it's really inconsiderate that Lance didn't bother to give them any gift at all.

norm: It's rude to shush people.
situation: Nate was watching a movie in a theater, and the couple behind him kept talking.
intention: Nate has to decide whether to say anything to the couple.
moral_action: Nate lets the couple talk and just decides to ignores them.
moral_consequence: The couple gets to enjoy the movie without anyone bothering them.
immoral_action: Nate turns around and shushes the couple without saying anything.
immoral_consequence: The couple feels disrespected and think that Nate must be a jerk.

norm: It's wrong to ruin someone's event.
situation: Hannah has just found out she is pregnant with her first child and is very excited.
intention: Hannah wants to share her good news with everyone she knows.
moral_action: Hannah makes an announcement post on her social media accounts.
moral_consequence: Hannah's friends and family congratulate Hannah and share in her excitement.
immoral_action: Hannah announces her pregnancy at her sister's wedding reception.
immoral_consequence: Hannah's family are upset with Hannah for making her sister's wedding about her.

norm: It is good to care for and protect animals
situation: Gary has a pet rabbit that he no longer has the time or money to care for.
intention: Gary wants to get rid of the rabbit as quickly as possible.
moral_action: Gary talks to a local shelter to get help finding a good home for the rabbit.
moral_consequence: The shelter is able to quickly find a good home for the rabbit with their resources, and the rabbit enjoys a good life.
immoral_action: Gary takes the rabbit a mile away from his house and drops it off in the woods.
immoral_consequence: The rabbit gets caught by a predator and eaten.

norm: It's rude to stare at people you find unattractive.
situation: Ron sees a relatively ugly person eating at the table across from him.
intention: Ron wants to get a better look at them.
moral_action: Ron takes quick glances to get a look at this curious looking person, looking away quick too.
moral_consequence: The stranger never realizes, and Ron gets to complete his looking.
immoral_action: Ron just can't stop looking at the table across, looking directly at them.
immoral_consequence: Ron makes the stranger feel very uncomfortable and the stranger eventually leaves.

norm: You shouldn't pee on people's couches.
situation: Marlon was visiting his friend's house and had drank several sodas.
intention: Marlon wants to pee.
moral_action: Marlon excuses himself and goes to the bathroom to pee.
moral_consequence: Marlon and his friend are able to enjoy the rest of their evening together.
immoral_action: Marlon stays sitting on the sofa and pees right where he is.
immoral_consequence: Marlon's friend gets mad at him and tells him to get out of his house.

norm: It's wrong to take things from people that aren't yours.
situation: Giselle's mom only buys regular wooden pencils for her to bring to school, and she sees her schoolmates with fancy mechanical pencils.
intention: Giselle wants a mechanical pencil.
moral_action: Giselle brings her allowance with her to the store and buys a mechanical pencil.
moral_consequence: Giselle's mom is proud of her for the responsibility that she has shown.
immoral_action: Giselle picks a mechanical pencil out of someone else's art box when they are not looking.
immoral_consequence: Giselle's mom sees the pencil in her backpack and punishes her for stealing.

norm: It's important to do your chores.
situation: Jay hadn't washed any of his clothes for well over a week and has a date.
intention: Jay wants to change his clothes.
moral_action: Jay puts some clothes in the wash and gets them clean in time for his date.
moral_consequence: Jay's date tells him that he looks very handsome and asks him for a second date.
immoral_action: Jay can't find any clothes to wear, so he puts on the same clothes as he wore the day before.
immoral_consequence: Jay's date says that he stinks, and she leaves halfway through the date.

norm: Holdiays are expected to involve other people.
situation: John's not a big fan of travel but has been invited by his parents to drive to their home several hours away for holiday dinner.
intention: John needs to decide whether he should accept the invitation.
moral_action: John decides to make the drive and spend Thanksgiving with his parents.
moral_consequence: John's parents enjoy having him around and make a tasty dinner for him.
immoral_action: John decides he'd rather just avoid the long drive and stays at home watching Netflix and eating a TV dinner for Thanksgiving.
immoral_consequence: John's parents are upset that he declined their Thanksgiving invitation.

norm: It's dishonest to lie on a resume.
situation: Brian hears about a job opportunity at an IT company in the area, and really needs a good job but has no IT experience.
intention: Brian wants to submit an eye-catching resume to the company.
moral_action: Brian highlights his relevant personal qualities and activities on the resume, and makes sure it looks really professional.
moral_consequence: Brian lands an interview with the company, and impresses them enough with his personality that they give him a chance.
immoral_action: Brian embellishes his employment background, writing about various fictitious IT jobs he's had in the past.
immoral_consequence: Brian is interviewed by the company, who immediately realizes he has no idea how to do IT work and rejects him.

norm: You shouldn't get involved in forbidden relationships.
situation: Corey just discovered the fact that one of the girls he has been texting is underage.
intention: Corey wants to feel less lonely.
moral_action: Corey pursues one of the women he knows who is an adult.
moral_consequence: Corey goes on a date with the woman and the two become close.
immoral_action: Corey pursues the underage girl, despite knowing that it is illegal.
immoral_consequence: Corey gets to go on an in-person date with the girl and the two get close, but he is apprehended for child endangerment.

norm: You should be considerate of others.
situation: Daria is hosting a dinner party for friends, some of whom are vegan.
intention: Daria wants to cook all of the meals for her dinner party.
moral_action: Daria cooks a variety of dishes that will satisfy all of her friends, no matter their diet.
moral_consequence: Everyone feels included and thanks Daria for hosting such a lovely party with delicious dishes.
immoral_action: After telling her guests not to bring anything, Daria prepares nothing but dishes that include meat or animal products.
immoral_consequence: Daria's vegan friends are forced to sit and watch on hungrily as their friends eat the meat-rich dinner.

norm: It's not okay to be rough with your pets.
situation: John's young dog Teddy accidentally pees on the rug right in front of John.
intention: John wants to react to the accident.
moral_action: John shows Teddy the pee stain and calls Teddy a bad dog while pointing at the pee.
moral_consequence: Teddy starts to understand that peeing indoors is bad, and he shouldn't do that and wags his tail in agreement.
immoral_action: John shoves Teddy roughly out of the room while yelling at him about peeing everywhere.
immoral_consequence: Teddy is confused and scared and doesn't understand why he's suddenly being physically attacked.

norm: You shouldn't treat someone differently because of their race.
situation: Jack, a white storeowner, has a few white and black customers browsing his products.
intention: Jack wants to protect his store from thieves.
moral_action: Jack watches every customer equally from his counter.
moral_consequence: The black customers don't feel singled out or threatened and enjoy shopping.
immoral_action: Jack follows only the black customers closely around the store.
immoral_consequence: The black customers become upset and file a complaint with the police.

norm: It's rude to deposit snow onto a roommate's car.
situation: Emily is getting ready to leave the house and head to school.
intention: Emily wants to get to her destination quickly.
moral_action: Emily digs the snow out from her own car and piles it in the yard where it is not in anyone's way.
moral_consequence: Emily gets her car out quickly and leaves no mess behind.
immoral_action: Emily digs snow from around her car and dumps it on her roommate's car to save time.
immoral_consequence: Emily's roommate is angry at Emily because she has to take extra time to dig her car out.

norm: It is important that children see parents getting along
situation: Ken and his wife, Marion, have two kids together but have been arguing a lot lately.
intention: Ken wants to sit down with Marion to talk about their problems.
moral_action: Ken and Marion start seeing a counselor and apply their conflict avoidance skills in the home.
