moral_consequence: Ken and Marion are happier in their marriage and act as good role models for their children.
immoral_action: Ken and Marion start talking, which eventually leads to them arguing in front of their children.
immoral_consequence: Ken's children become anxious and fearful due to all of the arguments they've witnessed.

norm: It's good to offer to pay for someone's ride.
situation: John and Jim shared a taxi from work to the subway station when the taxi driver turns to ask for the 20 dollar fare.
intention: John wants to respond to the taxi driver's body gesture.
moral_action: John pulls out a twenty and tells the taxi driver that he's got the whole fare covered.
moral_consequence: Jim is delighted at the surprise gift from his coworker and vows to repay the gesture in the future.
immoral_action: John pulls out a ten and gives it to the taxi driver to pay for his half of the fare.
immoral_consequence: Jim thinks it is fine that he has to pay his half but is not impressed by John or happy about anything.

norm: People appreciate it when you keep them in the loop.
situation: John is meeting up with Jack in 10 minutes to work on a group project.
intention: John wants to get some food before working.
moral_action: John tells Jack then he needs to push the meeting back, so he can get some food first.
moral_consequence: The two agree to meet at a later hour as Jack thanks John for letting him know.
immoral_action: John decides to stop and eat some food before meeting without telling Jack and arrives an hour late.
immoral_consequence: Jack scolds John for making him wait an hour with no advanced notice.

norm: It's wrong to eat other people's food.
situation: Jack and Diane are at a restaurant and both have a plate of French fries in front of them.
intention: Jack wants to eat a french fry.
moral_action: Jack grabs a fry off his own plate and eats it.
moral_consequence: Diane watches Jack eat happily and continues to eat her own food.
immoral_action: Jack reaches over to Diane's plate and grabs a french fry off her plate before eating it.
immoral_consequence: Diane is angry that Jack is stealing her food and spreading his germs all over her plate.

norm: It's undesirable to involve children in marital drama.
situation: Recently separated, but not yet divorced, Toni and her son live together and are having a coffee-euphoria chat.
intention: Toni wants to hear her son's take on his father.
moral_action: Toni directly asks her son what he'd like to see happen.
moral_consequence: They talk about it and Toni opens her mind.
immoral_action: Toni expresses her desire to take her son to another state, away from the father, and waits for a response.
immoral_consequence: Her son's reaction complicates matters and the father finds out, exacerbating Toni's stress.

norm: It's good to help your in-laws.
situation: Jerry is told by his wife Lia that her parents are behind on their mortgage.
intention: Jerry wants to respond to Lia.
moral_action: Jerry tells Lia that they can help her parents pay for their mortgage.
moral_consequence: Lia will think that Jerry is a caring husband who values family.
immoral_action: Jerry tells Lia that her parents' house will be foreclosed on.
immoral_consequence: Lia will think that Jerry is cold and uncaring.

norm: It's not okay to leave people with out saying goodbye.
situation: Jane was at her best friend's birthday party, but her sister needed a ride home from school.
intention: Jane wanted to go help her sister.
moral_action: Jane tells her best friend why she has to leave early before leaving.
moral_consequence: Jane's friend understands Jane's situation and is okay with her leaving.
immoral_action: Jane leaves the party without telling her best friend what she's doing.
immoral_consequence: Jane's best friend feels disrespected and feels like Jane doesn't like her that much.

norm: You shouldn't flirt with coworkers.
situation: Sypha goes to work and notices that Jack the new IT guy is cute.
intention: Sypha wants to decide if she should flirt with Jack.
moral_action: Sypha decides that would be too dangerous, so she just continues working.
moral_consequence: Sypha's boss stops by and tells her she's doing a good job and to keep it up.
immoral_action: Sypha starts flirting with Jack while they are both at work.
immoral_consequence: Before Jack can respond, their boss reprimands her for flirting at work.

norm: It's wrong to do sexual things to underage persons.
situation: Jared is chatting online in a forum for people who are looking for romance.
intention: Jared wants to have sex.
moral_action: Jared invites a 22yr old woman to his home for sex.
moral_consequence: Jared has a rewarding sexual experience with the woman.
immoral_action: Jared meets a 15yr old girl from the chatroom at a local hotel and has sex with her.
immoral_consequence: Jared is arrested for statutory rape when the girl tells her parents about the encounter.

norm: You shouldn't be picky when it comes to food.
situation: Johnny is young and enjoys playing games.
intention: Johnny wants to play video games.
moral_action: Johnny goes down to dinner to find vegetables on his plate and quickly eats his dinner regardless returning to his video games.
moral_consequence: Johnny's mom is pleased with him leaving him to play his video games.
immoral_action: Johnny goes down to dinner to find vegetables on his plate and refuses to eat it returning to his video games.
immoral_consequence: Johnny makes his mother upset and she scolds him.

norm: It's wrong to lie about going to commit suicide.
situation: Kim has been punished by her parents, but she thinks that she didn't do wrong.
intention: Kim wants her parents to know it feels to hurt.
moral_action: Kim sits down and talks to her parents and explains how she feels.
moral_consequence: Kim and her parents feel much more open after they have their discussion.
immoral_action: Kim tells her parents that she wants to kill herself because she is so sad.
immoral_consequence: Kim's parents call a specialist and have her committed to a hospital.

norm: It's wrong to never give to charity.
situation: Tom is walking with his groceries out of the store when he bumps into a charity worker at a table asking for donations.
intention: Tom wants to save his money.
moral_action: Tom stops and gives what he can afford to the charity worker while saving the rest.
moral_consequence: The charity worker is very happy and grateful and thinks well of Tom.
immoral_action: Tom pretends not to see the charity worker and walks briskly to his car.
immoral_consequence: The charity worker is saddened and feels Tom doesn't care about others.

norm: You should be sensitive to your partner's needs.
situation: Ned is getting ready for bed when his wife Janet implies that she wants to have sex tonight by saying that it's been a while.
intention: Ned wants to mention how long it's been since they made love.
moral_action: Ned says it's been a while, too long in fact and jumps on Janet to begin having sex.
moral_consequence: Janet is delighted that Ned figured out what she was trying to hint at and enjoys the love making.
immoral_action: Ned says that it has been a while but who is counting and that they shouldn't keep a journal of frequency of sex.
immoral_consequence: Janet is annoyed because she's not commenting on the frequency she just wants to have sex now and Ned is clueless.

norm: It's bad to steal from Disneyland.
situation: Alicia is at a Disneyland gift shop with her daughter, Charlotte, when Charlotte asks for an expensive figurine.
intention: Alicia wants Charlotte to go home with the figurine.
moral_action: Alicia signs up for the gift shop's email list before checking out.
moral_consequence: Alicia receives a coupon in her email, and is able to buy the figurine for Charlotte on a discount.
immoral_action: Alicia tosses the figurine into her purse before walking out of the shop without paying.
immoral_consequence: Security personnel spot Alicia on camera and apprehend her outside of the store.

norm: It's not okay to harass someone with phone calls.
situation: Brenda's boyfriend Sam broke up with her, and she's been feeling lonely.
intention: Brenda wants to talk to Sam.
moral_action: Brenda only makes one phone call to Sam to see if he wants to talk.
moral_consequence: Sam talks to Brenda for a little while and the call ends well.
immoral_action: Brenda calls Sam multiple times during the day and even late at night.
immoral_consequence: Sam gets very annoyed with Brenda and tells her that she needs to leave him alone.

norm: It is inconsiderate to your teacher to distract the class.
situation: Tara understands the class materials and is feeling bored in class.
intention: Tara wants to do something to pass the time in class.
moral_action: Tara draws cartoon characters in her notebook.
moral_consequence: Tara will be able to pass the time without bothering anyone else.
immoral_action: Tara makes paper airplanes and throw them at other students.
immoral_consequence: Tara will be given detention by the teacher for bothering the other students.

norm: Being a ball hog during a game is selfish.
situation: Teddy has the ball at his team's basketball game and his other teammates are open.
intention: Teddy wants his team to score a point.
moral_action: Teddy passes the ball to one of his teammates under the goal.
moral_consequence: Teddy's coach tells him that he is proud of his teamwork.
immoral_action: Teddy dribbles the ball to the basket and shoots it in himself.
immoral_consequence: Teddy's coach makes him sit the bench for lack of cooperation with his teammates.

norm: You shouldn't expect others to do all of the cleaning.
situation: Will's wife, who typically does the house cleaning, is working on a Masters degree and is pressed for time.
intention: Will wants the house to get cleaned.
moral_action: Will offers to do the house cleaning while his wife is busy finishing her Masters degree.
moral_consequence: Will's wife is grateful to Will and finishes the degree with straight A's.
immoral_action: Will tells his wife that she needs to keep up on her duties and clean the house.
immoral_consequence: Will's wife loses time on her projects and jeopardizes her grades in her classes.

norm: It's good to call a truce with people.
situation: Travis and his friend have been pulling pranks on one another and the pranks are getting more and more dangerous.
intention: Travis wants to have fun with his friend.
moral_action: Travis decides they have gone too far and negotiates with his friend for both of them to stop doing the pranks.
moral_consequence: Travis and his friend stop doing the pranks and are able to look back at them as good times.
immoral_action: Travis comes up with another elaborate prank and pulls it off on his friend.
immoral_consequence: The escalation between Travis and his friend's pranks reaches a tipping point where they both are hurt physically and emotionally by each other.

norm: It's kind to give advice to a friend.
situation: Zachary's friend is having relationship troubles and is asking him for advice.
intention: Zachary wants whats best for his friend.
moral_action: Zachary tells his friend that communication is the most important thing and encourages him to communicate with his partner.
moral_consequence: Zachary's friend follows his advice and is able to save the relationship.
immoral_action: Zachary is afraid to give his bad advice so tells his friend he doesn't know what he should do.
immoral_consequence: Zachary's friend feels like he doesn't care and stops hanging out with him.

norm: You shouldn't cheat on your partner with their parent.
situation: Gary is dating Monica, and her mother Tina is flirting with Gary while Monica is away.
intention: Gary wants to respond to the flirting.
moral_action: Gary tells Tina that the flirting is inappropriate and that he'll tell Monica if it continues.
moral_consequence: Tina backs off, and Gary and Monica continue dating for a while.
immoral_action: Gary flirts back at Tina, and the two end up having sex.
immoral_consequence: Monica finds out and breaks up with Gary and cuts her mother out of her life.

norm: You shouldn't let money destroy your family.
situation: David inheretied a million dollars from his parents and it's his job to figure out what to do with it.
intention: David wants to divy out the inheritance to his family.
moral_action: David gives the inheritance to all his siblings.
moral_consequence: David's siblings are glad David didn't destroy the family and David is proud.
immoral_action: David only gives the inheritance to half of his siblings.
immoral_consequence: The other half of David's siblings never talk to David again, and David feels guilty.

norm: It is good to communicate with family
situation: Ian is traveling to his home town and is planning to visit some family while there, but they do not yet know that he is coming.
intention: Ian wants to take his family out to dinner.
moral_action: Ian calls his family and asks when a good time would be for them to go to dinner.
moral_consequence: Ian and the family find a good time to eat together and go out.
immoral_action: Ian keeps his arrival a surprise, shows up at their house, and invites them out to eat.
immoral_consequence: The family has already scheduled a get-together that evening and cannot go out with Ian.

norm: Leaving a family heirloom with your child is meaningful
situation: Audrey's daughter Candace is getting married and moving to Germany with her and her soon to be husbands new child.
intention: Audrey wants to give a gift to Candace.
moral_action: Audrey gives Candace her great grandmothers pearl necklace that's been passed down from generation to generation.
moral_consequence: Candace treasures the necklace and plans to give it to her child one day to keep the tradition.
immoral_action: Audrey buys a bouquet of flowers and gives it to Candace.
immoral_consequence: Candace takes the flowers with her to Germany, but they die within a week.

norm: It's rude to quit a job with no notice.
situation: Becca is a shy and socially awkward girl who is unhappy with her current job.
intention: Becca wants to avoid direct confrontation with her supervisor.
moral_action: Becca gives her two weeks notice by email and finishes the off her remaining time there.
moral_consequence: Becca's supervisor has time to find a replacement for her position.
immoral_action: Becca sends her supervisor a text message saying that she quits and does not return.
immoral_consequence: Becca's supervisor is upset for the lack of notice and will not give her a good referral.

norm: It is kind to give an animal a good life.
situation: Jeff's dog goes potty inside the house by accident.
intention: Jeff wants to scold his dog.
moral_action: Jeff tells the dog he's a bad dog but then pets him and tells him it's OK.
moral_consequence: The dog reluctantly wags his tail and runs off happily.
immoral_action: Jeff kicks his dog and loudly swears and curses at it as the dog runs away.
immoral_consequence: The dog feels terrified and doesn't understand why it's under attack.

norm: It's nice to offer support.
situation: Bobby is listening to his friend Jack talk about his recent financial troubles and thoughts of suicide.
intention: Bobby wants to offer his perspective and give advice relative to the situation.
moral_action: Bobby helps Jack to better his perspective and to help Jack understand that the problems are temporary and that he will be OK.
moral_consequence: Jack is able to get counselling for his troubles and feel better about life which helps him to turn his life around.
immoral_action: Bobby tells Jack that the way he sees it, the problems are his fault, and he needs to work to make his life better.
immoral_consequence: Jack takes the advice bad and commits suicide.

norm: You should throw food out when it's old and gross.
situation: James is roaming through the fridge at the house he shares with his wife Amy when he notices the tomatoes on the shelf are all rotten.
intention: James wants to relocate the bag of rotten tomatoes from the shelf.
moral_action: James takes the bag of rotten tomatoes and throws them away in the garbage can.
moral_consequence: Amy is delighted that James knows how to clean up after himself and is a house house mate.
immoral_action: James takes the tomatoes and throws them in the crisper drawer out of sight and out of mind.
immoral_consequence: Amy later finds the gross tomatoes and is disgusted that they've reeked up the whole fridge.

norm: It's unacceptable to break a promise on prom night.
situation: Leah calls Rick to see if he's ready to pick her up to take her to prom as he promised.
intention: Rick wants to respond to Leah.
moral_action: Rick tells Leah that of course he'll be over in just a few minutes.
moral_consequence: Leah is delighted that Rick is coming to pick her up and excited about going to prom.
immoral_action: Rick tells Leah that he really doesn't want to go to prom anymore there's too many people there.
immoral_consequence: Leah is devastated as she had been dreaming of the prom for a long time.

norm: It's rude to not share food with your friends.
situation: Lucas brought a giant sandwich to work for lunch while Greg forgot to bring his lunch.
intention: Lucas wants to eat his sandwich.
moral_action: Lucas eats half of the sandwich and gives Greg the other half.
moral_consequence: Greg happily eats the sandwich.
immoral_action: Lucas eats the entire sandwich.
immoral_consequence: Greg watches sadly with a rumbling stomach.

norm: It's wrong to be impatient.
situation: Steve was in a hurry waiting for Jill to finish.
intention: Steve wanted to finish quickly.
moral_action: Steve waits just a bit longer for Jill to finish before leaving.
moral_consequence: Jill finishes, and she's pleased with Steve, so she helps him hurry the rest of the way.
immoral_action: Steve leaves Jill behind and hurries off by himself.
immoral_consequence: Jill is upset with Steve for leaving her behind like that.

norm: Being obsessed with something shows a lack of control.
situation: Roger just got a new video game and invites his girlfriend, Sandy over.
intention: Roger wants to enjoy his new game.
moral_action: Roger plays his game and takes breaks to visit with Sandy.
moral_consequence: Sandy enjoys Roger enjoying his game and feels Roger cares about her.
immoral_action: Roger gets so involved with the game that he ignores Sandy.
immoral_consequence: Sandy ends up breaking up with Roger because she feels he cares more about video games than about her.

norm: You shouldn't hit your children.
situation: John just lost his job and came home where he sees his two kids.
intention: John wants to vent his anger.
moral_action: John takes a deep breath and asks his kids if they want to go jogging with him.
moral_consequence: John's kids feel closer to John and are happy to run with him.
immoral_action: John grabs a belt and swats his kids on the buttocks while raising his voice.
immoral_consequence: John's kids resent John and love him less and stay away from him.

norm: It's rude to laugh at other peoples misfortune
situation: Tom is walking down the street at night, and he sees someone fall down and drop all of their groceries.
intention: Tom wants to react to the situation.
moral_action: Tom rushes to the man's aid and asks if he's okay.
moral_consequence: The man is grateful for Tom's help and is happy for it.
immoral_action: Tom laughs at the man falling down and does not help him.
immoral_consequence: The man feels bad and is left alone to gather his things.

norm: It's bad to eat too many calories in one sitting.
situation: Jane is at Bob's birthday party, and he's just blown out the candles on the cake.
intention: Jane wants to eat some cake.
moral_action: Jane takes one small slice of cake for herself.
moral_consequence: Jane savors the delicious flavors and is proud of herself for showing restraint.
immoral_action: Jane takes three huge slices of cake and eats them all one after the other.
immoral_consequence: Jane gets sick to her stomach and ends up throwing up in the bathroom.

norm: It's rude to mess with other people's personal property.
situation: Lacy is in the living room with her roommates laptop on the couch.
intention: Lacy wants to lay down.
moral_action: Lacy asks her roommate if she can move the laptop.
moral_consequence: Lacy's roommate moves the laptop and Lacy has a guilt free nap.
immoral_action: Lacy throws the laptop on the floor and it's stepped on.
immoral_consequence: Lacy's roommate is angry and demands she replace the laptop.

norm: It's good to treat your customers well.
situation: Marco is working at his successful car cleaning business and discovers $100 hidden beneath the seats.
intention: Marco wants to do something about the money.
moral_action: Marco informs the customer about the money he found and returns it.
moral_consequence: Marco gets a lot of positive feedback when the customer posts about the good treatment online.
immoral_action: Marco puts the money in his pocket rather than giving it to the customer.
immoral_consequence: Marco loses a lot of business when the customer finds out and leaves a terrible review online.

norm: People shouldn't put others on the spot with their problems.
situation: Kelly is having relationship problems with Ryan.
intention: Kelly wants to vent her frustrations and get help.
moral_action: Kelly gets counseling about the relationship and Ryan agrees to go too.
moral_consequence: The relationship improves and Kelly is happier now.
immoral_action: Kelly complains daily to her coworkers about Ryan and often asks them to get involved.
immoral_consequence: Kelly has a poor reputation at work and coworkers begin to avoid and exclude her.

norm: It's bad to mock religious figures.
situation: Nicky is in Rome at the Vatican when he sees a procession of cardinals walk past in their red hats and robes.
intention: Nicky wants to react to the cardinal's outfits.
moral_action: Nicky laughs and says that the cardinals look amazing and that he's awed by the bright red outfits.
moral_consequence: The bystanders all agree that the cardinals pose a striking figure as they walk by.
immoral_action: Nicky points at the cardinals and laughs yelling about how they look ridiculous with their ancient outfits.
immoral_consequence: The bystanders are all shocked that Nicky is so disrespectful to these revered people and hate him for it.

norm: It is rude to issue an ultimatum in a relationship.
situation: Harold is married to Denise, and has been been having to look at an ugly figurine on their dresser that belonged do Denise's grandmother.
intention: Harold wants to stop seeing the ugly figurine.
moral_action: Harold asks if there is somewhere Denise could put the figurine that he can't see it as often, and she agrees to put it in her study room.
moral_consequence: Denise still has her figurine to remind her of her grandmother, and Harold doesn't have to see it as much.
immoral_action: Harold says that either the ugly figurine goes, or he goes, and Denise gets rid of the figurine.
immoral_consequence: Denise resents Harold for trying to boss her around, and the two split up.

norm: It's rude to hit your friend with something.
situation: John and Liam are wrestling around in a playful manner in John's basement when Liam lightly shoves John.
intention: John wants to return the favor and hit Liam.
moral_action: John uses his palm to playfully shove Liam in the shoulder making sure it's not too rough.
moral_consequence: Liam smiles and laughs and continues rolling around on the ground enjoying himself.
immoral_action: John picks up a shoe and whacks Liam over the head with the loose shoe.
immoral_consequence: Liam is in pain and is shocked that his friend would hit him with a blunt object like that.

norm: It's petty to wish for someone to go to prison.
situation: James, who deeply disliked country music, lived next to a neighbor who played it at top volume every night.
intention: James wants his neighbor to turn down the late-night music.
moral_action: James starts blasting heavy metal music at his neighbor's house until his neighbor comes over to complain.
moral_consequence: James and his neighbor come to a detente and stop playing music at night.
immoral_action: James calls the cops and tells them that he thinks his neighbor is selling prohibited pharmaceuticals.
immoral_consequence: The police ransack James' neighbor's house and arrest him, but are forced to let him go due to lack of evidence.

norm: It's rude to not eat food your parent has prepared.
situation: Jeff goes downstairs to see that his parents have made soggy, spongy meatloaf for dinner.
intention: Jeff wants his mother to think that he enjoys her cooking.
moral_action: Jeff scarfs down the meatloaf quickly, ignoring the nasty texture.
moral_consequence: Jeff's mother sees him eating and beams with pride.
immoral_action: Jeff feeds the dinner to the dog when his parents aren't looking.
immoral_consequence: He fools his mother into thinking that he likes meatloaf.

norm: Declining invitations can hurt a person's feelings.
situation: Simon plans to invite all of his friends to the party with him.
intention: Simon wants to have fun at the party.
moral_action: Simon doesn't want to force his friends to show up, so he only invites those he's sure want to come.
moral_consequence: Simon's friends are glad the don't have to decline an invitation and risk hurting Simon's feelings.
immoral_action: Simon invites all of his friends with on to the party.
immoral_consequence: Some of Simon's friends don't want to come but don't want to decline, so they come anyway.

norm: It is rude to judge someone from their apperance.
situation: Jordan manages a college talent show with thirty contestants.
intention: Jordan wants to pick a contestant.
moral_action: Jordan picks the contestants based on their skill.
moral_consequence: Jordan's contestants feel it is fair and Jordan starts the next round.
immoral_action: Jordan picks contestants based on their physical beauty.
immoral_consequence: Jordan gets fired for gross discrimination and feels bad about it.

norm: It's generally not acceptable to be racist.
situation: Alice is introduced to her son's girlfriend for the first time.
intention: Alice wants to make an impression.
moral_action: Alice embraces her son's girlfriend with a smile.
moral_consequence: Alice's son tells her he is thankful that she was nice to his girlfriend.
immoral_action: Alice tells her son's girlfriend that she is not welcome in their home because she is black.
immoral_consequence: Alice's son berates her and tells her he is not coming home anymore.

norm: It is wrong to make someone afraid.
situation: Karl is in bed with Julia, a woman Karl just met and slept with.
intention: Karl wants to inject humor into the silence between them.
moral_action: Karl  relates an amusing anecdote from Karl's office where the color copier ran out of ink  and Karl tried to fix it.
moral_consequence: Julie laughs and feels at ease and that Karl is a man whom Julie feels current;y comfortable.
immoral_action: Karl casually mentions he has AIDs and that Julia should probably take a test soon.
immoral_consequence: Julia feels psychological terror and fears for Julia's life.

norm: You shouldn't sleep around with random people.
situation: Brian is married and is feeling adventurous tonight.
intention: Brian wants some excitement in his sex life.
moral_action: Brian asks his wife how they can make their sex life more exciting.
moral_consequence: Brian and his wife try some new things and are happier.
immoral_action: Brian uses an app to hook up with a one-night stand.
immoral_consequence: Brian gets an STD from the experience.

norm: It's bad to destroy property for no reason.
situation: John asks to borrow his brother's luxury car that he received as a graduation gift from their parents because John doesn't have one since he didn't graduate.
intention: John needs transportation, so he can take him and his friends on a trip to Vegas.
moral_action: John drives the car to transport himself and his friends to Vegas and returns it to his brother in perfect condition.
moral_consequence: John's brother is satisfied with the car's care and tells John he can borrow it anytime he needs it.
immoral_action: John uses his brother's car for the trip but intentionally breaks the windshield out of jealousy.
immoral_consequence: John's brother is very upset  because it's expensive to repair, and he never lets John use the car again.

norm: It's wrong not to hang out with your best friend.
situation: Pete's friend Patty is having a birthday party.
intention: Pete wants to spend the night at home.
moral_action: Pete decides to show up at the party for a couple hours and then say he needs to leave early.
moral_consequence: Patty understands Pete doesn't really want to be there but appreciates that Pete put in the effort.
immoral_action: Pete decides to ignore Patty's invitation to the birthday party.
immoral_consequence: Patty is upset with Pete for not celebrating her birthday.

norm: It's nice to ask someone out to a school dance.
situation: Bob knows that his classmate doesn't have a date for the school dance, and he doesn't either.
intention: Bob wants to decide whether not to ask his classmate to go to the school dance with him.
moral_action: Bob decides to ask his classmate to the school dance, and they go together.
moral_consequence: Bob's classmate in overjoyed that they got a date for the school dance and has a great time there.
immoral_action: Bob decides not too invite his classmate to the school dance and just goes by himself.
immoral_consequence: Bob's classmate doesn't attend the school dance and is ashamed that nobody asked her to go.

norm: It's wrong to be too controlling of your significant other.
situation: Ron and his wife were really looking forward to the big dance.
intention: Ron wanted to show his wife a good time.
moral_action: Ron and his wife went to the dance, and they talked to many different people.
moral_consequence: Ron and his wife had a fantastic time at the dance.
immoral_action: Ron would not let his wife talk to any of the other male attendees, especially the good-looking ones.
immoral_consequence: Ron’s wife resenting his controlling ways, and they had a big fight after the dance.

norm: It is bad to gamble irresponsibly
situation: Martha was going to the casino with some of her friends one day.
intention: Martha wanted to play poker.
moral_action: Martha brought along fifty dollars to gamble with at the casino.
moral_consequence: Martha lost her money, but still had plenty of cash left in her account.
immoral_action: Martha gambled away her whole paycheck at the poker table.
immoral_consequence: Martha wasn't able to pay her house note or her electric bill that month.

norm: You shouldn't sabotage your relationships.
situation: Mitch is not getting along well with his girlfriend and wants the relationship to end.
intention: Mitch needs to decide how to proceed in bringing his relationship to a close.
moral_action: Mitch talks with his girlfriend and explains his position to her, after which the couple parts ways.
moral_consequence: The relationship ends as amicably as possible and both parties maintain a civil relationship.
immoral_action: Mitch starts behaving in a way that is sure to start arguments and cause his girlfriend to leave.
immoral_consequence: His girlfriend becomes angry with his behavior and leaves him in a very uncomfortable and nasty exchange.

norm: It is wrong to troll others.
situation: John enjoys participating in the comments section of youtube videos and sees an opinion of a video posted that he does not agree with.
intention: John wants to respond to the opinion.
moral_action: John replies to the comment, laying out a well-reasoned case for why John has a different opinion.
moral_consequence: The other person counters with reasons of their own, and a long and engaging conversation ensues.
immoral_action: John replies to the comment, calling the other poster a big dumb idiot and telling them their opinion sucks.
immoral_consequence: The other person feels stressed because they're being picked on over the internet.

norm: It's bad to obsesses over someone.
situation: Ivan coudn't stop thinking about how he was going to defeat Miles in the science fair.
intention: Ivan wants to enter the science fair.
moral_action: Ivan focuses on his actual project for the fair rather than his rival.
moral_consequence: Ivan's project wins the science fair by a landslide.
immoral_action: Ivan obsesses over how he's going to win that he doesn't spend time on his project.
immoral_consequence: Ivan comes in second place behind Miles in the fair.

norm: People shouldn't harm creatures intentionally.
situation: Ash has spotted a spider scurrying across the living room while walking by.
intention: Ash wants to get rid of the spider.
moral_action: Ash traps the spider with a cup and transports it outside.
moral_consequence: The spider is free and alive to take care of pests like roaches.
immoral_action: Ash grabs a slipper and smashes the spider with it.
immoral_consequence: A beneficial creature has been killed needlessly.

norm: It is wrong to replace a dead partner quickly.
situation: Tammy just divorced her husband after ten years and is upset.
intention: Tammy wants to stop feeling lonely at home.
moral_action: Tammy decides to get a cat instead of seducing someone online, and is no longer lonely.
moral_consequence: Tammy helps the cat grow, and is satisfied in her decision.
immoral_action: Tammy seduces someone online in order to replace her husband quickly, and stops feeling lonely.
immoral_consequence: Tammy gets into an abusive relationship and doesn't feel secure in herself.

norm: You shouldn't take back gifts that you give to people.
situation: Jack gave his friend a game but now wishes he could have it back.
intention: Jack wants to visit his friend's house.
moral_action: Jack goes to his friend's house and plays the game with them there then goes back home.
moral_consequence: Jack's friend thinks Jack is very generous for giving them such a thoughtful gift.
immoral_action: When Jack goes over to his friend's house he takes back the game he gave them before returning home.
immoral_consequence: Jack's friend thinks that he is very rude for taking back something he already gave them as a gift.

norm: It's wrong to scam people with junk mail.
situation: Rob has been fired from his job and is facing eviction if he doesn't pay his back rent soon.
intention: Rob needs to scrape together some money fast.
moral_action: Rob sells as many of his possessions as he can and starts working gig jobs.
moral_consequence: Rob is able to keep himself afloat long enough to find another stable job.
immoral_action: Rob decides to try running a phishing scheme he learned about from an old friend to get people to wire money to him.
immoral_consequence: Rob rips off several people and pays his rent but is eventually caught and arrested.

norm: It's wrong to abandon someone due to mental health issues.
situation: Don has a roommate Randy who is also a close friend going through a depression and acting more moody than normal.
intention: Don wants to create a more comfortable situation for himself.
moral_action: Don explains his concerns and talks things out with Randy asking what he can do to help.
moral_consequence: Randy and Don agree on some things to make things easier for both and remain good friends.
immoral_action: Don moves out in the middle of the lease leaving Randy alone and paying more rent.
immoral_consequence: Don loses the friendship and Randy moves on with life and new friends after he beats his depression.

norm: It's rude to leave a business during their busy season.
situation: Jordan is working during the busy season at a retailer and is becoming increasingly exhausted from the overtime work.
intention: Jordan wants to works less.
moral_action: Jordan is assertive with his boss about working too much, and they reduce his hours.
moral_consequence: Jordan maintains a good rep at work and gets time to recover.
immoral_action: Jordan quits his job abruptly.
immoral_consequence: Jordan gets underhanded recommendations from this employer and has trouble finding new work.

norm: It's bad to be toxic.
situation: Ray and Cindy are divorced and share custody with the children, and Ray wants to have the children for an extra day during one weekend.
intention: Cindy wants to get equal time with the children.
moral_action: Cindy works with Ray to find a compromise where she gets an extra day.
moral_consequence: Both Cindy and Ray are happy and get equal time with the kids.
immoral_action: Cindy refuses Ray's request and completely refuses to negotiate with him about it.
immoral_consequence: Ray becomes jaded with Cindy's lack of cooperation.

norm: You shouldn't disappear without explanation.
situation: Bob is at a large party at his friends' house.
intention: Bob wants to go home.
moral_action: Bob thanks his friends for inviting him and says he had fun.
moral_consequence: His friends hug him goodbye and tell him they were glad to see him.
immoral_action: Bob goes home without saying goodbye to anyone.
immoral_consequence: His friends think he is rude and don't invite him to anymore parties.

norm: It is wrong to expose others to second hand smoke.
situation: Terry is in his house with his son who had asthma.
intention: Terry wants to smoke a cigarette.
moral_action: Terry steps outside of the house to light up his cigarette and smoke.
moral_consequence: Terry's son is able to breathe comfortably as he is away from the smoke.
immoral_action: Terry lights up a cigarette while sitting in the same room as his son.
immoral_consequence: Terry's son breathes in the smoke and has a bad asthma attack.

norm: You should think about other people's feelings.
situation: John is at home watching a movie with his wife Mindy who is upset about her job loss.
intention: John wants to feel good and continue watching his movie.
moral_action: John pauses the film and comforts Mindy and listens to her lament.
moral_consequence: Mindy feels happier and closer to John.
immoral_action: John tells Mindy not to bother him now as he's in the middle of a film.
immoral_consequence: Mindy feels even worse about herself and more distant from John.

norm: It's not expected that you'll be abusive toward your parent.
situation: Cal's dad keeps bothering him about not being able to get a job.
intention: Cal wants his dad to stop bothering him.
moral_action: Cal decides to find a job and save up money to find his own place.
moral_consequence: Cal is no longer bothered by his dad, and he gets more freedom.
immoral_action: Cal decides to fight his dad and ends up putting him in a hospital.
immoral_consequence: Cal's dad sues Cal, and Cal is kicked out of the house.

norm: It's polite to tip service people who help you.
situation: Stacy is staying at a hotel where the bellhop takes her bags up to her room.
intention: Stacy wants to respond to the bellhop.
moral_action: Stacy gives the bellhop a few dollars for bringing up her bags.
moral_consequence: The bellhop will want to help Stacy with her bags when she leaves.
immoral_action: Stacy tells the bellhop that she hopes nothing is broken in her bags.
immoral_consequence: The bellhop will not want to help Stacy with her bags when she leaves.

norm: It is rude to smoke in someone's home.
situation: Jeremy is over at his friend Nick's house when he feels a craving for nicotine.
intention: Jeremy wants to smoke a cigarette.
moral_action: Jeremy tells Nick he has to go outside to have a cigarette.
moral_consequence: Nick will think Jeremy is considerate of his house and space.
immoral_action: Jeremy lights up a cigarette in his friend Nick's house.
immoral_consequence: Nick will kick Jeremy out of his house and tell him he smells.

norm: It's okay to split the cost of a date.
situation: Bob is out on an expensive date with someone he just met from a dating site.
intention: Bob wants to save money.
moral_action: Bob pays for only his portion of the bill.
moral_consequence: Bob's date thinks they are not entitled to being treated by someone they met recently.
immoral_action: Bob order cheaper items and water to drink.
immoral_consequence: Bob's date thinks he will always cover the whole cost leading to future problems.

norm: It's bad to ignore a person without explanation.
situation: Renee has a big test coming up.
intention: Renee wants to focus on studying with no distractions.
moral_action: Renee lets her friends know that she needs to focus for a few days and won't be as responsive.
moral_consequence: Renee's friends understand and give her time to study.
immoral_action: Renee stops answering texts and other messages from friends, so she won't get distracted.
immoral_consequence: Renee's friends worry about her and feel hurt that she is ignoring them.

norm: You shouldn't do anything that will make an argument worse.
situation: Mark was having an argument with his wife over finances.
intention: Mark doesn't want to keep arguing.
moral_action: Mark walks away so that they can agree to disagree.
moral_consequence: Mark's wife is still a little mad, but she'll get over it.
immoral_action: Mark tells his wife that she shouldn't tell him what to do with his own money.
immoral_consequence: Mark's wife feels disrespected that Mark would think that she doesn't contribute.

norm: You're expected to support your husband.
situation: Bane is watching his husband's baseball game when his stomach growls.
intention: Bane wants to get food.
moral_action: Bane buys a hot dog from the nearby food cart as he chants his husband's name.
moral_consequence: Hearing Bane's voice inspires Bane's husband to make several home runs.
immoral_action: Bane leaves the stadium to get fast food which results in him missing the rest of his husband's game.
immoral_consequence: Bane's husband becomes hurt when he finds out about Bane's actions.

norm: It's good to reward someone when they do well.
situation: Jill's subordinate Jake is a very good employee who constantly goes above and beyond.
intention: Jill wants to indicate her awareness of Jake's capability.
moral_action: Jill decides to give Jake an employee of the month award.
moral_consequence: Jake is really happy with the award and places it in the middle of his desk.
immoral_action: Jill decides to give Jake even more work as he's so proficient at his job.
immoral_consequence: Jake is really stressed out by the increased workload and feels taken advantage of.

norm: It's wrong to copy your friend's answers on final exams.
situation: Carl is having trouble on his final exam and notices that his friend Rey is nearly done.
intention: Carl wants to answer all of the final exam questions.
moral_action: Carl does his best to finish the exam using everything he already knows.
moral_consequence: Carl manages to get a passing grade on the final exam.
immoral_action: Carl looks at Rey's exam paper and copies the answers.
immoral_consequence: Carl is caught by his teacher and given a failing grade on the exam.

norm: It's wrong to tell lies about other people.
situation: Neo has been getting picked on by a bully at school.
intention: Neo wants to get the other kid in trouble.
moral_action: Neo tells the teacher that the other kid has been bullying him.
moral_consequence: The school investigates and ends up expelling the bully from the school.
immoral_action: Neo tells the teacher that the kid has been selling drugs, without having any evidence.
immoral_consequence: The school finds out Neo lied and expels him.

norm: It is expected that you take care of your children
situation: Sara is at a playground with her children along with one of her friends and the friend's children.
intention: Sara wants to discuss something that's been troubling her with her friend in private.
moral_action: Sara and her friend text back and forth about Sara's troubles while they watch their children play.
moral_consequence: Sara feels better and is able to supervise her children while they play.
immoral_action: Sara pulls her friend aside and lets her children play unsupervised while she explains her problem.
immoral_consequence: Sara feels better, but her son falls off the playground and injures himself with no one around to help.

norm: It's bad to make your girlfriend stranded.
situation: Jace was supposed to pick up his girlfriend Diane after she got off of work.
intention: Jace wants to take a nap.
moral_action: Jace takes a nap but makes sure to wake up in time to pick up Diane from work.
moral_consequence: Diane is happy to see Jace waiting for her when she walks out of her job.
immoral_action: Jace takes a nap and doesn't get up in time to pick up Diane from work.
immoral_consequence: Diane is annoyed that she has to get a ride home with a coworker.

norm: It's wrong to force sexual attention on a nonconsenting individual.
situation: Brandon meets a woman at a night club, and they have a lot of fun dancing and laughing.
intention: Brandon wants to keep the night going after the club closes.
moral_action: Brandon tells the girl he met that he really likes her and invites her to an all-night diner to sober up together and drink some coffee.
moral_consequence: The two have a nice conversation, which changes as they drink their coffee, but they enjoy the rest of their night and get to know one another.
immoral_action: Brandon asks the woman he met to a party at his house, but there is no party so once she gets there he tries to hold her there through coercion.
immoral_consequence: Brandon sobers up and realizes that his behavior is criminal and the woman he met, and really liked, never wants to see him again.

norm: It's wrong to joke about mass shootings.
situation: Jimmy is a little known stand-up comedian and has a big show at the local comedy club, which could jump start his career.
intention: Jimmy wants to test some new edgy material.
moral_action: Jimmy tells a joke filled with sexual innuendos to the audience.
moral_consequence: Jimmy's joke goes over well with the audience, and he gets loud applause at the end of the set.
immoral_action: Jimmy tells a joke about a recent mass shooting tragedy.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy bombs and gets booed offstage by a stunned and indignant audience.

norm: It's good to set boundaries with people.
situation: Gordon and Bill are friends, and they rent an apartment together in order to share the financial burden, and Bill recently smokes cigarette.
intention: Gordon wants to react to Bill's smoking behavior.
moral_action: Gordon requests Bill to stick to smoking in the balcony area.
moral_consequence: Gordon feels undisturbed while Bill is smoking.
immoral_action: Gordon locks himself up in his room when Bill starts smoking in order to avoid inhaling second hand smoke.
immoral_consequence: Gordon feeling bad and frustrated wants to end the roommate relationship with Bill.

norm: It's wrong for adults to fantasize about children
situation: Jack and his friend Hoffner are discussing sexual preferences while at lunch with coworkers.
intention: Jack wants to ask Hoffner his sexual preferences.
moral_action: Jack asks Hoffner the type of women that Hoffner prefers and Hoffner tells Jack that he prefers the older look, what some would call MILFs.
moral_consequence: Jack introduces Hoffner to his older sister and Hoffner, and she start dating.
immoral_action: Jack asks Hoffner the type of women that Hoffner prefers and Hoffner tells Jack that he prefers the prepubescent look but would never act on it.
immoral_consequence: Jack mentions to a work friend what Hoffner said and rumors start going around that Hoffner is a pedofile, and he is fired.

norm: It is rude to intentionally block an entrance.
situation: James is demonstrating his passionate opposition to abortion by protesting outside a women's health clinic.
intention: James wants to stop women from getting abortions.
moral_action: James stands beside the doorway and calls the woman walking past him babykillers.
moral_consequence: One or two of the women turn around rather than dealing with James.
immoral_action: James physically blocks the entrance to the clinic and pushes the patients away if they come too close.
immoral_consequence: James is promptly arrested for trespassing and assault and denied bail.

norm: You shouldn't be selfish.
situation: Gordon is out at an all you can eat buffet eating lunch one day.
intention: Gordon wants to each chicken.
moral_action: Gordon takes a piece of chicken, some noodles and a side salad.
moral_consequence: Gordon eats the food on his plate and his hunger is satisfied.
immoral_action: Gordon takes all the chicken on the platter and puts it onto his plate.
immoral_consequence: Gordon eats all the food on his plate and immediately gets a severe stomach ache.

norm: It's not okay to not finish what you start.
situation: Jim is exhausted from working on a labor intensive project all day.
intention: Jim wants to go to bed to rest his body.
moral_action: Jim chooses to get some rest and start again fresh in the morning.
moral_consequence: Jim is well rested and has more energy to complete the project.
immoral_action: Jim decides to quit on the project due to how much labor it requires and turns in for the night.
immoral_consequence: Jim feels regret for spending so much time on the project in vain.

norm: It is fun to spend time with friends fishing.
situation: Charlene has a group of good friends who are going to the lake and invited her, but she has never been.
intention: Charlene wants to hang out with her friends.
moral_action: Charlene decides to go with her friends when they go to the lake, and they end up fishing while there.
moral_consequence: Even if the fishing wasn't quite her thing, Charlene enjoys the companionship of her friends while they all do it.
immoral_action: Charlene decides that the lake and things to do there isn't something she wants to try but tells her friends to stop by after they are done.
immoral_consequence: Charlene's friends only talk about the fishing they did at the lake when they are at Charlene's house later and Charlene feels out of the loop.

norm: It's wrong to intentionally cause harm to someone's relationship.
situation: Ken and Bob are talking about Bob's girlfriend one day at lunch, and Ken does not like Bob's girlfriend.
intention: Ken wants to give Bob some advice.
moral_action: Ken keeps his mouth shut and gives Bob good advice while keeping his personal opinion aside.
moral_consequence: Bob and Ken's friendship is preserved.
immoral_action: Ken tells Bob he hates his girlfriend and tries to sabotage the relationship.
immoral_consequence: Bob gets mad at Ken, and they get into a fight.

norm: It's good to support charities by buying clothes from Goodwill.
situation: An airline has lost a suitcase with most of Jason's clothes in it.
intention: Jason wants to obtain new clothes.
moral_action: Jason decides to contribute to a good cause and buys his clothes from Goodwill.
moral_consequence: Jason's money goes to some good causes that help a lot of people.
immoral_action: Jason buys all his new clothes from a high-end retail establishment.
immoral_consequence: Less money goes to a good cause than could have with Jason's help.

norm: It's good to take a stray animal in.
situation: Thomas has noticed a small scruffy dog that regularly walks around his property.
intention: Thomas wants to do something about the dog.
moral_action: Thomas takes the dog into his house and adopts it once he fails to find an owner.
moral_consequence: The dog has a new owner and is healthy and happy as a result.
immoral_action: Thomas takes out his hunting rifle and shoots it at the dog.
immoral_consequence: The dog suffers and dies horribly as a result of the gunshot wound.

norm: It's good to care about the opinions of others.
situation: Alejandro has begun finding his old wardrobe boring and doesn't like any of his clothes anymore.
intention: Alejandro wants to develop a new personal style.
moral_action: Alejandro asks his friends and parents for their opinions on what would suit him best, and takes their advice into consideration when choosing what to wear.
moral_consequence: Alejandro develops a style that's the envy of all the kids at his school, and he becomes very popular.
immoral_action: Alejandro decides to just wear whatever he feels like, regardless of fashion trends or what others say about his choices.
immoral_consequence: Alejandro gets made fun of at school for his unusual wardrobe, and he begins feeling like an outcast.

norm: You shouldn't expect women to do all the chores.
situation: Harry and Sally live together in a messy apartment and are having company over.
intention: Harry wants the place to be clean before the company arrives.
moral_action: Harry and Sally divide up the house cleaning chores between them.
moral_consequence: Sally appreciates that Harry is willing to do his fair share of cleaning around the apartment.
immoral_action: Harry has Sally clean the place while Harry spends all day looking at Cat memes.
immoral_consequence: Sally is upset that Harry didn't do his fair share of the chores.

norm: It's rude to insult people.
situation: Tessa sees Jane on the street and notices that she has food on her face.
intention: Tessa wants Jane to know about the food on her face.
moral_action: Tessa whispers to Jane that she has a bit of food on her face.
moral_consequence: Jane wipes the food off and tells Tessa thank you for letting her know.
immoral_action: Tessa begins to laugh and ridicule Jane, calling her a sloppy pig.
immoral_consequence: Jane gets mad at Tessa and slaps her across the face.

norm: It's rude to ignore your parter for your friends.
situation: Jerry is dating Mindy and also has a close group of friends.
intention: Jerry wants to spend time with his friends.
moral_action: Jerry and Mindy agree to make friday a friends night and Saturdays a date night.
moral_consequence: Jerry and Mindy have a strong relationship and Jerry is happy with the time spent with friends.
immoral_action: Jerry hangs out with his friends almost every night and rarely spends time with mindy.
immoral_consequence: Mindy breaks up with Jerry because she feels ignored and neglected.

norm: It's not okay to pester people when it isn't needed.
situation: Laura has just learned a new dance in her ballet class.
intention: Laura wants to show her mother the dance.
moral_action: Laura waited until her mother wasn't busy before showing her the dance.
moral_consequence: Laura's mother was thrilled with the dance that Laura learned.
immoral_action: Laura starts dancing in front of her mother while her mother was cooking dinner.
immoral_consequence: Laura's mother spilled grease on her hand and was burned.

norm: It's good to open presents.
situation: Cindy arrives at her birthday party and spots a huge pile of gifts.
intention: Cindy wants to participate in the party.
moral_action: Cindy opens her presents after singing and having cake.
moral_consequence: Cindy's friends tell her she deserves everything she got to open.
immoral_action: Cindy walks past the gifts and spends the evening singing and having cake.
immoral_consequence: Cindy's friends are a bit disappointed that she didn’t seem excited about the gifts.

norm: It is important to be kind to the less fortunate.
situation: Stacy has a bunch of left-over food from a party she had.
intention: Stacy wants to get rid of the left-over food.
moral_action: Stacy gives the left-over food to a local soup kitchen.
moral_consequence: People in the area who would not have had anything to eat enjoy the left-over food.
immoral_action: Stacy throws the left-over food into a garbage dumpster where it rots.
immoral_consequence: People in the area who have no food go hungry.

norm: You should decorate for holidays if you have children.
situation: Andy is in his living room in early December when his son Wendel comes running in asking if they'll put up the tree this year.
intention: Andy wants to respond to Wendel's question.
moral_action: Andy tells Wendel that they definitely will put up a tree, and he'll let Wendel decorate it.
moral_consequence: Wendel gets excited and is happy about the tree and can't wait to put up decorations.
immoral_action: Andy tells Wendel that trees are annoying to clean up after, so he won't put one up this year.
immoral_consequence: Wendel is sad that he can't enjoy the joys of Christmas like all the normal kids.

norm: It's important to be a team player when playing soccer.
situation: Josh plays in a youth soccer league and his team is tied 1-1.
intention: Josh wants his team to win.
moral_action: Josh sees a teammate open downfield and quickly kicks the ball to them, who then scores.
moral_consequence: Josh is thrilled that his teammates appreciate his contribution to the victory.
immoral_action: Josh tries to take the ball all the way down the field by himself but is slide-tackled before scoring, with the ball then rolling into the goal by accident.
immoral_consequence: Josh suffers an ankle injury and his teammates dislike him.

norm: It's wrong to make a problem worse.
situation: Joe's friend Timmy is failing his classes and might not be able to graduate.
intention: Joe wants Timmy to get a high grade on his upcoming math test.
moral_action: Joe asks his friend Timmy to study with him for the big test.
moral_consequence: Timmy gets the highest grade in the class because of all the extra study time.
immoral_action: Joe convinces his friend Timmy to write secret notes on his arm for the test.
immoral_consequence: Timmy is caught cheating on the test and is kicked out of school.

norm: It's good to accept your family member's choices.
situation: Lucy and her husband John are hosting Thanksgiving for their asexual son Paul and their gay daughter Catherine.
intention: Lucy wants to know if her children are single.
moral_action: Lucy asks her son if he has any kind of romantic relationships despite his asexuality.
moral_consequence: Paul says he's in a queer-platonic relationship with someone at school and thanks his mom for not making assumptions about him.
immoral_action: Lucy asks Catherine when she is getting a boyfriend over the Thanksgiving table.
immoral_consequence: Catherine feels disrespected, as her family is aware of her sexuality and says she's dating a woman now.

norm: Teacher are expected to maintain order in their classrooms.
situation: Mr. Anderson is teaching a Geometry class when some students in the back began having a side conversation.
intention: Mr. Anderson wants to respond to the misbehavior.
moral_action: Mr. Anderson walks to the back of the room near the students and firmly asks them to stop talking.
moral_consequence: The students apologize and start paying attention to the lesson instead of each other.
immoral_action: Mr. Anderson quietly asks the whole class to please listen to the lesson and then goes back to writing on the board.
immoral_consequence: The students ignore Mr. Anderson and the misbehavior begins to spread around the classroom.

norm: It is bad to be in a gang.
situation: Pete has nothing to do after school when his parents aren't home from work.
intention: Pete wants friends to hang out with.
moral_action: Pete joins the robotics club at school and meets other boys his age.
moral_consequence: Pete learns more math and science and his grades go up.
immoral_action: Pete joins a gang of young hoodlums that hang around his house.
immoral_consequence: Pete has to go to jail when the gang gets in a fight with a rival gang.

norm: You shouldn't exclude people with mental disabilities.
situation: Bertha is getting married soon and her little brother suffers from depression.
intention: Wants to have the best wedding possible.
moral_action: Bertha asks her little brother to be the ring bearer for her wedding.
moral_consequence: Bertha's little brother says yes and has one of the happiest days of his life at the wedding.
immoral_action: Bertha decides to not invite her little brother because she doesn't want him to keep everyone down in the dumps.
immoral_consequence: Bertha's family are very upset at her actions and none of them show up to the wedding.

norm: It's not okay to put your kids into uncomfortable situations.
situation: Brad was just divorced and has his kids for the weekend, when his new girlfriend Sharon calls to invite him over.
intention: Brad wants to spend time with his children.
moral_action: Brad explains to Sharon that his kids need time to adjust and that for now, it's best that they just spend weekend with him.
moral_consequence: The kids are really glad to be able to be with their dad this weekend and have a nice time.
immoral_action: Brad accepts Sharon's invitation and brings his kids over to her house.
immoral_consequence: The kids aren't used to his parents being apart yet and the situation makes them feel sad and awkward.

norm: You shouldn't touch people who don't want to be touched.

norm: It's noble to fight for the rights of other people.

norm: It's good to help out pregnant people.

norm: It is wrong to escalate conflicts with your parents

norm: You shouldn't ruin someone's holiday.

norm: You shouldn't hold grudges against your family.

norm: It is wrong to shun or ignore family members

norm: It's wrong to lie about your education.

norm: It's wrong to betray your children's trust.
situation: Jim promised to buy his son a new game if he kept his grades up and the report card shows good grades.

norm: You shouldn't drive too slowly because it annoys people.

norm: You should be supportive when your partner is insecure.

norm: It's bad to be a lazy person.

norm: You shouldn't judge others on their appearance.

norm: You should learn to clean up your own messes.

norm: It's wrong to blame someone for something without having proof.

norm: You should listen to your kids about their problems.

norm: You shouldn't do shady things for your neighbors.

norm: It's not okay to let yourself be taken advantage of.

norm: You should eat your dinner before having dessert.

norm: It's wrong to try to kill people.
situation: Zach has always longed for a certain dream car that he has never been able to afford and notices that his neighbor Bill just bought one.

norm: You do not have any obligations to an ex partner.

norm: It's bad to steal office supplies.

norm: It's good not to overeat.

norm: It's wrong to not take the considerations of others seriously.

norm: It's rude to brag to others.

norm: It's wrong to harm your body with excessive drug use.

norm: It's wrong to hurt an innocent child.

norm: You should always respect your older family members.

norm: It's wrong to start confrontations with people you live near.

norm: It's good to have a job when you're young.

moral_action: Jared sets his alarm and gets to the theater a half-hour before the movie starts.

immoral_action: Jared wastes time talking on the phone and gets to theater after the movie has started.
immoral_consequence: Jared's friends are mad at him for making them miss the start of the movie.

norm: It's wrong to make fun of other people's suffering
situation: Josh works downtown.
intention: Josh wants to grab lunch with a friend.
moral_action: Josh brings a homeless man a sandwich after having lunch.
moral_consequence: Josh's friend sees him as a warm hearted and helpful.
immoral_action: Josh tells a homeless man to get a job and stop begging.
immoral_consequence: Josh's friends now sees him as cold hearted.

norm: You should never cheat on your spouse
situation: Maxine has been married to Phil for 10 years but has recently been flirting with a coworker.
intention: Maxine wants to have a more exciting relationship.
moral_action: Maxine quits flirting with her coworker and makes an effort to spice up her marriage.
moral_consequence: Maxine's marriage is reinvigorated.
immoral_action: Maxine decides to take flirting to the next level and sleeps with her coworker.
immoral_consequence: Maxine's marriage is jeopardized when her husband finds out about the affair.

norm: It's bad to be too critical of young children.
situation: Marcus has a son who is still learning how to do basic chores around the house.
intention: Marcus wants to give his son advice.
moral_action: Marcus points out some good things and then shows his son some things to improve.
moral_consequence: Marcus' son is grateful for the praise and works on the weak areas.
immoral_action: Marcus makes a list of everything that his son does wrong every day, so he can see his mistakes.
immoral_consequence: Marcus' son becomes discouraged and angry at Marcus and refuses to do his chores any longer.

norm: Showing respect to your work superiors is good.
situation: Steve was getting a dressing down by his boss for poor performance.
intention: Steve wants his boss to stop criticizing him.
moral_action: Steve tells his boss he completely understands, and will work hard to work better.
moral_consequence: Steve's boss is satisfied with that response, and backs off criticizing him so much.
immoral_action: Steve tells his boss that he thinks he's incompetent too.
immoral_consequence: Steve's boss fires Steve for talking back to him so rudely.

norm: It is wrong to cause harm to a significant other
situation: Linda works as a waitress and came home from work late to her husband James.
intention: James wants to know where Linda was so late at night.
moral_action: James calmly asks Linda where she was and makes dinner.
moral_consequence: Linda tells James all about her night over dinner.
immoral_action: James confronts Linda assuming she was out with some other man and ends up pushing her into a table, twisting her ankle.
immoral_consequence: James loses Linda's trust, and she can't work for several days.

norm: It's wrong to steal money from your school.
situation: Austin is part of a school drama club that needs to find a way to fund a team trip.
intention: Austin wants to have a benefit car wash where all of the group helps out.
moral_action: Austin helps with car wash, making sure to safely keep all of the proceedings locked up in a cash box.
moral_consequence: The drama team exceeds in obtaining necessary amount to pay for the group trip and puts the rest back for future activities.
immoral_action: Austin is in charge of handling the money received from car wash customers, which he sneaks half of the money for his own pocket.
immoral_consequence: The drama team was unable to get enough money to pay for a school sponsored excursion.

norm: You shouldn't drive a wedge between families.
situation: Owen's parents are having a serious argument and are asking him for his opinion on which one of them is correct.
intention: Owen wants to help his parents resolve the issue.
moral_action: Owen looks at both sides of the story and explains the pros and cons of each argument while proposing a solution with a viable compromise.
moral_consequence: Owen's parents thank him for his thoughtful contribution and take his solution into consideration.
immoral_action: Owen decides to take his father's side and tells his mother that she's wrong.
immoral_consequence: This ends up causing even further division between his parents, and they eventually end up filing for divorce.

norm: If you make a mistake you should fix it
situation: Chuck borrowed Tim's lawnmower and broke the blade.
intention: Chuck wants to mow his lawn.
moral_action: Chuck gets a new blade for the mower and returns it after he finishes mowing.
moral_consequence: Tim is grateful and lets him borrow other items from time to time.
immoral_action: Chuck give the mower back, with the broken blade, and borrows someone else's mower to finish the lawn.
immoral_consequence: Tim never lets Chuck borrow anything again, and the relationship is strained.

norm: It's wrong to cheat your employer.
situation: Steve has a car but its not running well anymore, and he wants to buy a new one but doesn't have enough money.
intention: Steve wants a new car.
moral_action: Steve asks if he can work more overtime to help him afford a new car.
moral_consequence: Steve is given extra projects at work, and he saves to buy a new car.
immoral_action: Steve uses an expense account at work to buy himself a new car.
immoral_consequence: Steve gets caught having misused his expense account and has to pay it back after being fired.

norm: It's good to appreciate your friend's religion.
situation: Wanda and Yasmin are talking about the cultural practices of their families.
intention: Wanda wants to learn more about Yasmin's religion.
moral_action: Wanda asks Yasmin to talk about some of her favorite aspects of her religion.
moral_consequence: Yasmin feels appreciated.
immoral_action: Wanda tells Yasmin her religion sounds really strange.
immoral_consequence: Yasmin gets offended.

norm: You should avoid your phone in some occasions.
situation: Theodore is sleeping over at his friend's house.
intention: Theodore wants to play a video game.
moral_action: Theodore asks his friend if they can play something on playstation together.
moral_consequence: Theodore's friend has fun playing against Theodore and invites him over often.
immoral_action: Theodore plays games on his phone all night.
immoral_consequence: Theodore's friend feels ignored and doesn't invite him over again.

norm: Vandalism is wrong.
situation: "Mark notices a ""for sale"" sign on his neighbor's home and thinks it'd be the perfect place to try out his new paint."
intention: Mark wants to paint his neighbor's home.
moral_action: Mark asks his neighbor if he needs help freshening up his exterior paint.
moral_consequence: Mark is able to try out his new paint and his neighbor pays him for a job well done.
immoral_action: Mark paints profanities on his neighbors home in the night.
immoral_consequence: Mark's neighbor loses his potential buyers after they see profanities painted onto the home.

norm: You shouldn't let a drunk friend walk home alone.
situation: Joe and Bill have been catching up over drinks but Bill has overindulged and is quite drunk by the end of the night.
intention: Joe wants to get some sleep before work the next day.
moral_action: Joe escorts Bill home and then heads home himself.
moral_consequence: Joe is able to look back at an enjoyable evening spent with his friend.
immoral_action: Joe parts ways with Bill outside the bar and heads home.
immoral_consequence: Joe is dismayed when he finds out that Bill was found passed out and mugged in an alley.

norm: It is good to pay it forward.
situation: Jim is in the drive-through at a local coffee place on his morning commute to work, when he’s told that the person in front of him bought him a coffee.
intention: Jim wants start his day on a positive note.
moral_action: Jim uses the money he saved to pay for a coffee and a donut for the car behind him in line.
moral_consequence: Jim feels good that he did something to help another person without them asking for it.
immoral_action: Jim decides to buy a second coffee and two donuts for himself.
immoral_consequence: Jim ends up feeling sick at work after consuming too much sugar and caffeine.

norm: It is almost never okay to kill somebody's pet.
situation: Bob is having problems with the neighbor's dog coming into his yard and trampling his garden.
intention: Bob wants to stop the dog's behavior.
moral_action: Bob goes and talks to his neighbor about controlling the dog better.
moral_consequence: Bob doesn't have any more problems with the dog after his neighbor agrees to put up a fence.
immoral_action: Bob puts some poisoned meat in his garden for the next time the dog comes over.
immoral_consequence: Bob is later arrested and charged with animal cruelty when the dog dies from eating the poison.

norm: You should not take back something that is given.
situation: John bought himself a new car and gave his old one to his daughter, but he recently totaled the new car in an accident.
intention: John wants to be able to drive to work.
moral_action: John buys himself a cheap beater car to drive to work until he saves up money for a nicer one.
moral_consequence: John's daughter is happy that she gets to keep the car that her dad gave her.
immoral_action: John takes his old car back from his daughter and uses it to commute to work.
immoral_consequence: John's daughter is upset and doesn't understand why her dad can't be more responsible.

norm: It's good to relieve oneself when the opportunity presents itself.
situation: Brandon's mom suggests Brandon use the restroom before they leave the drive would be along mostly deserted highways.
intention: Brandon wants to play another video game before the trip.
moral_action: Brandon decides to use the bathroom and then plays a video game until his mom calls him to leave.
moral_consequence: Brandon has a comfortable trip and enjoys the time with his mom.
immoral_action: Brandon gets involved with the video game and forgets to use the restroom.
immoral_consequence: Brandon has to pee by the side of the road and listen to his mom rant.

norm: You shouldn't use swear words against others.
situation: Gabe is talking to his mother when they get into a heated discussion.
intention: Gabe wants to get his point across.
moral_action: Gabe starts talking in depth about the points that he is trying to make.
moral_consequence: Gabe does a good job speaking and eventually his mother begins to see his point.
immoral_action: Gabe starts to accentuate his point with a variety of curse words.
immoral_consequence: Gabe's mother doesn't like his language and punishes him for a week.

norm: You shouldn't rely on someone else to do your laundry.
situation: Emma's mom has always done her laundry, but now Emma lives on her own.
intention: Emma has to get her laundry done.
moral_action: Emma watches YouTube videos on how to use a washing machine and goes to the laundromat.
moral_consequence: Emma learns how to do her own laundry and doesn't have to rely on anyone else.
immoral_action: Emma drives to his mom's house so that she can do Emma's laundry for her.
immoral_consequence: Emma relies on her mom and never learns how to do her own laundry.

norm: It's good to recognize when you did something wrong
situation: Dave is driving with Jane as his passenger when he absentmindedly blows through a red light and Jane screams in terror.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Jane's scream.
moral_action: Dave tells Jane he's sorry, and she doesn't have to worry, he knows he wasn't looking and will concentrate harder on driving.
moral_consequence: Jane feels relieved that Dave sees the error of his ways and that he's willing to correct it.
immoral_action: Dave tells Jane it was nothing and no one got hurt, so she should quiet down and relax.
immoral_consequence: Jane is annoyed that Dave doesn't seem to realize how dangerous what he just did was and doesn't feel safe anymore.

norm: It is rude to treat mentally disabled people differently.
situation: John is playing baseball as a pitcher when the next batter, Jim comes up and Jim has visible down syndrome.
intention: John wants to decide what pitch to throw.
moral_action: John decides to throw his usual first pitch, a sinking curveball on the outside corner.
moral_consequence: Jim is impressed by the sink on John's curveball and is happy to try his hardest to best John.
immoral_action: John decides to throw a slow, easy underhand lob to Jim so that Jim can easily hit it.
immoral_consequence: Jim is annoyed that John doesn't take his athletic prowess seriously and is throwing him patronizing pitches.

norm: It is unprofessional to make coworker's uncomfortable in the workplace.
situation: Bob's coworkers hinted to him yesterday that he has strong body odor.
intention: Bob wants to go to work.
moral_action: Bob makes sure to shower thoroughly and wear strong deodorant before going to work.
moral_consequence: Bob's coworker are much more comfortable at work since Bob took steps to control his body odor.
immoral_action: Bob goes to work without doing anything about his smell that his coworkers mentioned.
immoral_consequence: Bob's coworkers are really bothered by his body odor and can barely stand to be at the workplace because of it.

norm: You shouldn't spy into hotel windows because that's rude.
situation: James, a janitor at a large hotel chain, is cleaning the pool when he sees a couple getting undressed with the curtains open.
intention: James wants to see people having sex.
moral_action: James leaves the couple alone and goes to the bathroom to watch porn on his phone.
moral_consequence: James' morale improves and the couple is able to be intimate in private.
immoral_action: James watches the couple having sex in their hotel room without their knowledge.
immoral_consequence: James' manager comes looking for him, seeing him spying on the couple, and fires them.

norm: It is expected to selflessly support family in troubling times.
situation: Charles, who only has meager savings gets a phone call from his mother telling him she desperately needs to borrow money.
intention: Charles wants to respond to his mother's request.
moral_action: Charles tells his mother that she can have whatever meager savings he has, it's all hers.
moral_consequence: Charles' mother is thankful for any amount and is glad her son would go to greats lengths to help her.
immoral_action: Charles tells his mother that he cannot spare any money at the moment since he only has so little himself.
immoral_consequence: Charles' mother continues to be majorly stressed out and is sad that her son can't be there for her when she needs him.

norm: It is rude to criticize someone's gift to you
situation: Judy is having a birthday party for herself and opening up gifts from guests.
intention: Judy wants to see everything she received.
moral_action: Judy opens each gift and thanks each person individually as she enjoys getting gifts.
moral_consequence: Judy is seen as grateful and caring by her birthday guests.
immoral_action: Judy opens a gift she isn't particularly fond of a makes a crack about it before tossing it to the side to renew focus on the next gift.
immoral_consequence: Judy is seen as selfish and ungrateful for her commentary on the gift.

norm: It's not okay to be racist.
situation: Karen is working at the bakery she owns when a line starts to form.
intention: Karen wants to shorten the line.
moral_action: Karen puts out samples for all of her patrons, regardless of race, to enjoy in line, before hopping on the register so the line moves quicker.
moral_consequence: Karen's patrons appreciate the snack and write positive reviews about her bakery online.
immoral_action: Karen tells her patrons that all people of color must wait outside.
immoral_consequence: Karen's patrons are appalled by her request and a boycott of her bakery ensues.

norm: It's good to patronize your local stores.
situation: Mario was doing some home repairs and realized he didn't have all the tools he needed.
intention: He wants to purchase some tools.
moral_action: Mario goes to a local hardware store in his neighborhood to buy his tools.
moral_consequence: Mario is happy with the quality of the tools and is able to use them for years with no problem.
immoral_action: Mario goes to buy his tools at a large retail store where he can get them for a low price.
immoral_consequence: Mario ends up throwing most of the tools away after a few uses because they are cheaply made.

norm: It's bad to make obscene gestures to people.
