situation: James was driving to work when another driver cut him off on the freeway.
intention: James wants the other driver to feel bad about their behavior.
moral_action: James follows the other driver to their destination and lectures them about their behavior.
moral_consequence: The other driver is clearly uncomfortable and tries to get James to leave.
immoral_action: James puts alongside the other driver and raises his middle finger at him.
immoral_consequence: The other driver swears at James and says he's the worst driver he's ever seen.

norm: It's good to get over your ex.
situation: Bob is feeling lonely one evening at home.
intention: Bob wants some female companionship.
moral_action: Bob goes out to meet new people, possibly a new girlfriend.
moral_consequence: Bob finds new friends and a new girlfriend.
immoral_action: Bob calls up his ex girlfriend and wants to make up.
immoral_consequence: They get back together, but the relationship is just as bad as the first time.

norm: It's hurtful to avoid your sibling.
situation: Jan and Marsha had a falling out over a boy and now Jan is reluctant to see Marsha at their parents big anniversary party.
intention: Jan wants to decide on whether to go to the party or not.
moral_action: Jan puts aside her differences with Marsha and goes to her parents celebration.
moral_consequence: Jan's parents are thrilled to enjoy time with all of their children.
immoral_action: Jan makes an excuse and misses the celebration.
immoral_consequence: Jan's parents are disappointed that their daughter isn't there to celebrate with them.

norm: It's bad to steal money.
situation: Trevor is a gas station clerk who drives an old, beat-up car.
intention: Trevor wants to have more money, so he can buy a new car.
moral_action: Trevor picks up extra shifts at the gas station.
moral_consequence: With all of the extra shifts he's worked, Trevor is able to save up enough money to buy a new car.
immoral_action: One day at work when no one is around, Trevor takes money out of a medical charity's donation cup.
immoral_consequence: Trevor is seen on camera taking the money and is promptly fired from his job.

norm: Is good to reconnect with relatives
situation: Lonny wants to get closer to his family.
intention: Lonny wants to reconnect with his cousin.
moral_action: Lonny calls his cousin and apologizes for what broke them apart.
moral_consequence: Lonny gets his cousin back.
immoral_action: Lonny calls up his cousin and pretends to have an emergency to get his attention.
immoral_consequence: Lonny feels horrible about lying to his family.

norm: It's wrong to try to get revenge
situation: Morgan is told by a witness that it was Jim who attacked his wife last week.
intention: Morgan wants to act on the new information about Jim.
moral_action: Morgan looks up Jim's address and calls the police to report where he lives.
moral_consequence: The police arrest Jim and Morgan gets the closure he needs from the incident.
immoral_action: Morgan looks up Jim's address and finds him and then proceeds to beat him up as payback.
immoral_consequence: Morgan is found by the police and arrested himself for assaulting Jim.

norm: It's polite to offer food to a relative's significant other.
situation: Kathy brought a new recipe she made for the family's Thanksgiving potluck, where her brother Tom showed up with his new girlfriend.
intention: Kathy wants to share her dish with the family.
moral_action: Kathy offers her dish to Tom's girlfriend and makes small talk with her while they try everyone's dishes.
moral_consequence: Tom's girlfriend opens up to Kathy, and they start to become friends during the meal.
immoral_action: Kathy offers her dish to everyone but Tom's girlfriend and doesn't interact with her beyond introductions.
immoral_consequence: Tom's girlfriend does not feel welcome at the Thanksgiving dinner and rethinks her relationship with Tom.

norm: Health professionals are expected to maintain a level of professionalism.
situation: Danny is a nurse who has been working late and has been dealing with unruly patients.
intention: Danny wants to vent his frustrations.
moral_action: Danny talks about his problems with the other patients and asks advice from the other nurses.
moral_consequence: The other nurses give Danny their support and help him in dealing with the patients.
immoral_action: Danny gossips about his patients with the other nurses and nursing assistants during his break.
immoral_consequence: The charge nurse chastises Danny for gossiping about the patients during his break.

norm: You shouldn't wish ill on your kids.
situation: Randy is in his kitchen at home when his son Boyd tells him that he got in a fight in school.
intention: Randy wants to respond to his son's news.
moral_action: Randy tells his son to explain what happened and asks him if he's hurt or bruised.
moral_consequence: Boyd is happy his father wants to hear his side of things and that he's concerned for his health.
immoral_action: Randy tells his son that he shouldn't fight, and he hopes he gets beat up next time, so he can learn his lesson.
immoral_consequence: Boyd is confused why his father is hoping he gets beat up and scared that he actually will get beat up.

norm: It's wrong to insult other people.
situation: Jan is driving his new car to the store when another driver cuts him off.
intention: Jan wants to respond to the situation.
moral_action: Jan decides to just let it go and continues on his way to go shopping.
moral_consequence: Jan is able to avoid a conflict and get his groceries safely.
immoral_action: Jan yells obscenities and flips off the other driver.
immoral_consequence: The other driver notices and throws a drink out of his window which hits Jan's car and scratches the paint.

norm: You should not publicize cumming into a plant.
situation: Johnny is running for class president and has to do an interview for the school paper.
intention: Johnny wants to tell the school paper about himself.
moral_action: Johnny tells the school paper about his past leadership positions in student government.
moral_consequence: Johhny's classmates think Johnny would be good at getting things done in student government and elect him class president.
immoral_action: Johnny tells the school paper that his most memorable experience at school was cumming into a plant in the foyer after hours.
immoral_consequence: Johnny's classmates think Johnny is very strange and elect another candidate for class president.

norm: You shouldn't always assume people are faking their depression.
situation: Howard is talking with Eric who seems downhearted.
intention: Howard wants to spend time with his friend Eric.
moral_action: Howard notices that Eric is acting like his usual self and tells him he should talk to his doctor.
moral_consequence: Eric feels relieved someone cares, takes his advice and begins to feel better.
immoral_action: Howard ignores Eric's mood and thinks that he just wants attention.
immoral_consequence: Eric feels like no one understands what he's going through and overdoses on drugs.

norm: It's bigoted to target people because of their nationality.
situation: Someone has been stealing things from the office that Elise manages and corporate is upset.
intention: Elise wants to find the thief.
moral_action: Elise calls  in every employee for questioning.
moral_consequence: Elise eventually finds the thief and is rewarded by corporate.
immoral_action: Elise calls in the Mexican employees for questioning because she thinks they're more likely to break the law.
immoral_consequence: The employees file a report against Elise for racism, and she is fired.

norm: It's wrong to get upset with people who are disabled.
situation: A disabled man using a cane stumbles and bumps into Gary outside of a grocery store after which he apologizes.
intention: Gary wants to respond to the man's apology.
moral_action: Gary immediately accepts the man's apology and tells him not to worry about it.
moral_consequence: Gary and the man both feel better and quickly forget about the incident.
immoral_action: Gary refuses the man's apology and loudly tells him to watch where he's going.
immoral_consequence: Both Gary and the disabled man feel upset for a long time after the incident.

norm: It's wrong to steal a car.
situation: Ben and his pregnant wife are shopping downtown when his wife goes into labor.
intention: Ben wants to get his wife to the hospital right away.
moral_action: Ben calls 911 from his cell phone and sits with his wife calmly until the ambulance arrives.
moral_consequence: Ben and his wife arrive at the hospital in time to have their baby.
immoral_action: Ben notices a parked car that is running, so he puts his wife in the car and drives it away.
immoral_consequence: Ben is pulled over by the police, and he is arrested and put in jail.

norm: You shouldn't put your education above your children.
situation: Riley applied and got into a Master's program at a university but has small children that need to be cared for.
intention: Riley wants to decide on the Master's program.
moral_action: Riley chooses to delay attending the Master's program and take care of the children.
moral_consequence: Riley's children will grow up with a lot of care and support.
immoral_action: Riley chooses to attend the Master's program instead of caring for the children.
immoral_consequence: Riley's children will be neglected when they are young.

norm: It's nice to throw a birthday party.
situation: Linda was deciding what to do for her friend Luke's birthday.
intention: Linda wants to impress Luke.
moral_action: Linda throws Luke a birthday party and invites all of his friends.
moral_consequence: Luke has a grand time with all of his friends at the party, and he thanks Linda.
immoral_action: Linda gets Luke a nice present for his birthday and wraps it up.
immoral_consequence: Luke enjoys the gift and thanks Linda for the gift.

norm: You should pay people back if you owe them money.
situation: Heidi owes Drew two hundred dollars, and she doesn’t have the money.
intention: Heidi wants to continue to have a good relationship with Drew.
moral_action: Heidi decides to work a few extra shifts at her job, so she can pay Drew back.
moral_consequence: Heidi pays Drew the money and the two continue to have a good relationship.
immoral_action: Heidi tells Drew she won’t pay him back because he is rich and it is only two hundred dollars.
immoral_consequence: Drew decides to cut all ties with Heidi because she is not responsible and this makes Heidi very sad.

norm: It's nice to help your friends fix their vehicles.
situation: Randy is at home when his friend Lawrence calls him and tells him his car has broken down.
intention: Randy wants to respond to Lawrence's news.
moral_action: Randy tells Lawrence to tell him where he is, so he can come pick him up and get his car fixed.
moral_consequence: Lawrence is delighted Randy will come right away, and they can start fixing the car.
immoral_action: Randy tells Lawrence that it sounds pretty bad, and he hopes Lawrence will get help.
immoral_consequence: Lawrence is annoyed because he called Randy for help, not for Randy to tell him it was a bad situation.

norm: It's wrong to be unfaithful to your partner.
situation: James is a married man, and having a night out drinking with friends.
intention: James wants to have a good time.
moral_action: James ignores the attractive lady and plays a game of pool with his friends.
moral_consequence: James enjoys spending time with his friends.
immoral_action: James sees a pretty woman and starts flirting.
immoral_consequence: James ends up going home with the woman and violates his wedding vows.

norm: It's wrong to rip up something that someone else made
situation: John and his coworker Pete are both tasked with submitting a marketing plan to their boss but only one will be chosen.
intention: John wants his marketing plan to be chosen.
moral_action: John stays up late working hard on his marketing proposal to ensure it is high quality.
moral_consequence: John's marketing proposal is chosen, and he receives a promotion soon after.
immoral_action: John finds Pete's submission and tears it into tiny pieces so that his boss will not get it.
immoral_consequence: John's act of sabotage is discovered, and he is fired from his job.

norm: It is greedy to not let anyone use your stuff.
situation: Dora's roommate Kim has an interview in the morning and her iron broke, she knows Dora has an iron.
intention: Dora wants Kim to leave for the interview.
moral_action: Dora grabs her iron and lends it to Kim, wishing her well on her interview.
moral_consequence: Kim irons her outfit and her interviewer finds her appearance to be very professional.
immoral_action: Dora tells Kim that her iron is broken as well and that her outfit looks fine as is.
immoral_consequence: Kim's interviewer is unimpressed by the state of her clothes and holds it against her in the interview.

norm: It's wrong not to care about others.
situation: Dennis is planning to propose to his longtime girlfriend Tricia.
intention: Dennis wants the proposal to be special.
moral_action: Dennis proposes to Tricia privately during a moonlight picnic he planned.
moral_consequence: Tricia accpets the proposal and is happy that Dennis planned something so romantic.
immoral_action: Dennis proposes to Tricia at his sister's wedding reception.
immoral_consequence: Tricia is very embarassed and Dennis's family is angry at him.

norm: It is wrong to take someone's gas.
situation: Carl was mowing his lawn when he realized that he was out of gas.
intention: Carl wants to finish mowing the yard.
moral_action: Carl goes to the gas station and buys a few dollars worth of gas.
moral_consequence: Carl fills up his lawn mower and is able to finish his yard.
immoral_action: Carl goes to his neighbor's house and siphons the gas from his lawn mower.
immoral_consequence: The police arrest Carl for trespassing and theft of the neighbor's property.

norm: Families are expected to attend the weddings of it's members.
situation: James's father's brother's nephew's cousion is getting married.
intention: James wants to make a decision.
moral_action: James decides to go to the wedding and see what happens.
moral_consequence: James has a fun time with his family at the wedding of distant relatives.
immoral_action: James decides not to go because he can't go to every wedding of every far flung relative.
immoral_consequence: James gets angry calls from various distant relative wo are upset.

norm: You shouldn't pull other people's hair.
situation: Debbie is in a discussion with Nancy.
intention: Debbie wants to Nancy to see her side.
moral_action: Debbie gives Nancy her opinions with calm, rational points.
moral_consequence: Nancy listens and tells Debbie she can see where Debbie's coming from.
immoral_action: Debbie grabs Nancy by the hair when Nancy doesn't listen to her.
immoral_consequence: Nancy slaps Debbie in the face to get free from her and never wants to talk to her again.

norm: You shouldn't take inappropriate photos of people.
situation: Bill is at a crowded beach with his family taking photos.
intention: Bill wants to enjoy his day off with his faimly.
moral_action: Bill takes photos of his wife and children while they play in the water.
moral_consequence: Bill's wife feels touched that he wanted to preserve cherished memories and everyone has a lovely day.
immoral_action: Bill notices a woman undressing and takes photos of her.
immoral_consequence: The woman calls Bill out for his photo taking and gets him sent away from the beach.

norm: You shouldn't return gifts to people.
situation: Gladys is turning 50 years old next month.
intention: She wants to celebrate this milestone with her best friend by flying to Ireland.
moral_action: When they get to Ireland, Gladys is surprised to find out that her friend Gloria paid for her upgraded hotel accommodations.
moral_consequence: Gloria feels validated by her friends constant, lavish praise of her hotel room.
immoral_action: Gladys best friend Gloria buys her airline ticket to Ireland but Gladys refuses to accept it as being too costly.
immoral_consequence: Gloria feels badly the whole week because she had alternate gift to give her friend.

norm: You must not drink alcohol if you're pregnant.
situation: Becky is attending her baby shower.
intention: Becky wants to have fun.
moral_action: Becky sings karaoke with all her friends at the baby shower.
moral_consequence: Becky has a wonderful time with all her friends.
immoral_action: Becky has a few mimosas while opening her baby shower gifts.
immoral_consequence: Becky has a developmentally challenged baby.

norm: It's not good to put others lives at risk.
situation: Tyler is going to the grocery store where there is a mask requirement policy, but he has lost his mask.
intention: Tyler wants to buy something for dinner.
moral_action: Tyler fashions a t-shirt into a makeshift mask and wears it while he shops.
moral_consequence: The customers feel more secure seeing that his face is covered.
immoral_action: Tyler goes to the store without a mask on and picks up ingredients for dinner.
immoral_consequence: The customers feel unsafe around Tyler because he isn't wearing a mask.

norm: It's not okay to be overly into video games.
situation: Chris is in his first year in college and has a lot of work to do, and he is also in a competitive Halo league.
intention: Chris wants to maintain a high level of play in his Halo league.
moral_action: Chris makes sure to do most of his homework assignments and spend a fair amount of time reading before playing Halo.
moral_consequence: Chris' ranking drops slightly in the Halo league, but his grades are decent, and he is able to maintain his lifestyle.
immoral_action: Chris devotes himself fully towards Halo and regularly skips classes to play games online.
immoral_consequence: Chris is one of the top players in the league, but his grades are poor, and he is put on probation.

norm: It's expected that you always treat your parents with respect
situation: Pam wants to hang out with her friends, but her parents refuse to let her leave the house in bad weather.
intention: Pam wants to vent her frusterations.
moral_action: Pam rants about the situation to a friend on the phone.
moral_consequence: Pam is able to understand her parent's decisions after talking to her friend.
immoral_action: Pam walks around the house making goofy impressions of her parents.
immoral_consequence: Pam is sent to time out for the rest of the night.

norm: It's bad to take things from stores without paying.
situation: Jimmy is at a jewelry store looking for an anniversary gift for his girlfriend.
intention: Jimmy wants a necklace that he thinks his girlfriend wil like.
moral_action: Jimmy pays for the necklace and gives it to his girlfriend.
moral_consequence: Jimmy gets a big hug from his girlfriend when she sees what he got her for their anniversary.
immoral_action: Jimmy takes the necklace, puts it in his pocket, and walks out of the store.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy is arrested when the store's security alarm goes off as he tries to leave he store.

norm: It is wrong to make false accusations.
situation: Julie's house was recently broken into, and she has no idea who did it.
intention: Julie wants the cops to arrest someone for breaking into her home.
moral_action: Julie asks her neighbors if they saw or heard anything related to her home break-in.
moral_consequence: Julie's neighbor provides the police with video surveillance and the true suspect is caught and arrested.
immoral_action: Julie makes up a story about her ex-husband threatening to break into her home and reports it to the police.
immoral_consequence: Julie's ex-husband is falsely jailed for the break-in.

norm: You should shower more so you don't smell.
situation: Nancy is a church member who does not prioritize hygiene.
intention: Nancy wants to save time getting ready for church.
moral_action: Nancy prepares her clothes in advance and finds a low maintenance makeup style so that she can shower before church.
moral_consequence: Nancy smells good going to church and is complimented on her new style.
immoral_action: Nancy only showers a couple times a week and never does so before going to church.
immoral_consequence: Parishoners avoid Nancy and complain about her resulting in the pastor talking to her about hygiene.

norm: You shouldn't block the door.
situation: James is at the movie theater when he sees his friend Tim on his way in.
intention: James wants to chat with Tim before the movie starts.
moral_action: James asks Tim to step aside to chat for a bit.
moral_consequence: Everyone is able to enter the theater on time to find seats before the movie begins.
immoral_action: James stands between  the theater's entrance doors to talk to Tim.
immoral_consequence: James jams up the traffic of entering movie-goers, and they all end up missing the beginning of the movie.

norm: It is good to help people beat their addictions
situation: John is with his friend Andrew, a recovering alcoholic, at a party.
intention: John wants to party and drink a lot.
moral_action: John parties a bit, takes Andrew home, then returns to drink with others.
moral_consequence: Andrew has a good time and remains sober and happy.
immoral_action: John whoops it up and brings himself and Andrew a bunch of beers and whiskey.
immoral_consequence: Andrew relapses into alcoholism and loses his job.

norm: It's good to want to help your spouse.
situation: Patty just had a baby and still has to do household chores, but Bob has been busy with work.
intention: Bob wants Patty to be happy.
moral_action: Bob takes time off from work in order to help look after the baby.
moral_consequence: Patty is glad to finally have help around the house.
immoral_action: Bob buys Patty a new purse that's more expensive than the one she has.
immoral_consequence: Patty doesn't receive any help and feels just as overhelmed.

norm: You shouldn't irritate or harass people in online games.
situation: Brendon is playing an MMO when he stumbles across his classmate Natalie.
intention: Brendon wants to interact with Natalie.
moral_action: Brendon asks Natalie to trade with him.
moral_consequence: Brendon ends up befriending Natalie during their trade.
immoral_action: Brendon follows Natalie taking her kills, loot, and sending  her spam messages.
immoral_consequence: Brendon is reported for breaking the rules of the game.

norm: It's dishonest to steal funds from your employer.
situation: Gabbie notices an accounting error at work that leaves a thousand dollars unaccounted for.
intention: Gabbie wants to do something about the unaccounted money.
moral_action: Gabbie writes an email alerting her employer about the unaccounted money.
moral_consequence: Her employer admires Gabbie's honesty and eventually gives her a promotion.
immoral_action: Gabbie diverts the money into her personal bank account thinking no one will notice.
immoral_consequence: Her employer discovers the diversion of funds and files criminal charges against Gabbie.

norm: It's nice to keep your children happy.
situation: Craig was driving his son home from guitar lessons.
intention: Craig wanted to take his son somewhere.
moral_action: Craig takes his son to the theater to watch a movie he wanted to watch.
moral_consequence: Craig's son is happier and appreciates his dad more for what he does for him.
immoral_action: Craig takes his son to the gym so that he can lose some weight.
immoral_consequence: Craig's son starts to mistrust his dad and feels negatively about working out.

norm: It is rude to make inappropriate jokes.
situation: During an important meeting some of the members of Phil's team get into an argument.
intention: Phil wants to diffuse the situation.
moral_action: Phil turns the conversation to aspects of the meeting everyone can agree on.
moral_consequence: Phil manages to get the meeting back on track.
immoral_action: Phil decides to tell a racially insensitive joke to help lighten the mood.
immoral_consequence: Phil gets censured for making racist jokes.

norm: You should not judge others financial situation.
situation: Toni has a niece she loves.
intention: Toni wants her niece to go to a good school.
moral_action: Toni offers to help her sister with her niece's tuition.
moral_consequence: Toni's sister and grateful and Toni's niece is able to go to a good school.
immoral_action: Toni tells her sister that she needs to stop being lazy and get a better job, so she can actually provide for Toni's niece.
immoral_consequence: Toni's sister gets angry at her and cuts off her relationship with her niece.

norm: It's nice to surprise your partner.
situation: Jerry and his wife have been married for a long time and have a routine where they eat microwave dinners.
intention: Jerry wants to figure out dinner.
moral_action: Jerry takes his wife to a fancy restaurant as a surprise.
moral_consequence: Jerry and his wife have a fun time at the fancy restaurant.
immoral_action: Jerry makes microwave dinners that they have in the fridge.
immoral_consequence: Jerry and his wife will have a typical evening.

norm: It is wrong to drive irresponsibly.
situation: Hector is stuck in a traffic jam, as the highway is closed down to a single lane due to emergency vehicles.
intention: Hector wants to get home.
moral_action: Hector slowly creeps forward through traffic.
moral_consequence: Hector makes it home safely.
immoral_action: Hector swerves out of his lane and drives in the empty, closed lanes.
immoral_consequence: A police officer sees Hector and pulls him over.

norm: It's rude to bully others.
situation: Ken was at the playground waiting playing with some of the other kids from the neighborhood.
intention: Ken wants to go down the slide.
moral_action: Ken waits patiently in line to use the slide on the playground.
moral_consequence: Ken and the other kids have a great time playing at the park.
immoral_action: Ken cuts in front of some of the other kids that are in line to use the slide and threatens them if they don't let him go first.
immoral_consequence: After cutting in line, none of the other kids want to play with Ken.

norm: You shouldn't pee in your pet's water bowl.
situation: Jim has woken up in the middle of the night to use the bathroom, but his mom is currently using it.
intention: Jim wants to pee.
moral_action: Jim holds it and waits for his mother to finish.
moral_consequence: Jim is finally able to go to the bathroom and feels a sense of great relief.
immoral_action: Jim decides to use his dog's bowl as a toilet.
immoral_consequence: Jim's mom catches him after leaving the bathroom and grounds him.

norm: It's wrong to take things without paying for them.
situation: Quinn's baby daughter is out of diapers and the checkout line at the store is very long.
intention: Quinn wants to get home with the diapers as soon as possible.
moral_action: Quinn walks past the register with the diapers and gives some cash to the cashier on the way out.
moral_consequence: Quinn is able to leave the store and get the diapers to his daughter.
immoral_action: Quinn walks past the register with the diapers and tries to go home.
immoral_consequence: Quinn is stopped by loss prevention and detained in the store for a while.

norm: It's good to feel remorse after killing.
situation: Ron is serving in a war and shoot an enemy soldier killing him.
intention: Ron wants to react to killing someone.
moral_action: Ron thanks that killing someone is regrettable even if necessary.
moral_consequence: Ron will maintain his humanity while at war.
immoral_action: Ron thinks that killing someone else was a pleasurable experience.
immoral_consequence: Ron will become blood thirsty and crave violence.

norm: It's rude to assume what all women enjoy.
situation: Jim and Sammy are about to have sex for the first time ever.
intention: Jim wants to see what Sammy likes.
moral_action: Jim asks Sammy if she likes anal sex and proceeds to do it after she says yes.
moral_consequence: Sammy feels sexually fulfilled and is glad that Jim asked before doing it.
immoral_action: Jim chokes Sammy while penetrating her without asking if she liked it.
immoral_consequence: Sammy begins to cry and isn't interested in having sex anymore.

norm: It's good be well prepared for a long hike.
situation: Bud has taken a trip to the mountains and sees a rugged but scenic 20 mile hiking trail.
intention: Bud wants to go on the trail and hike it.
moral_action: Bud plans the route, buys the right equipment and meets up with an experienced hiker to go with him on it.
moral_consequence: Bud is challenged but finishes the trail and feels accomplished.
immoral_action: Bud starts the hike on a whim and starts with the just the tshirt and shorts that he is wearing and a bottle of water.
immoral_consequence: 24 hours later a sunburned, bug bitten and hungry Bud is found and rescued by a park ranger.

norm: It's immoral to trivialize another person's health.
situation: Ron is talking with James when he finds out that James has stomach problems.
intention: Ron wants to help James cope with his stomach problem.
moral_action: Ron asks if there's anything he can do to help James.
moral_consequence: James tells Ron about foods that are safe for him so Ron can avoid hurting him.
immoral_action: Ron says that James' stomach issues are likely in his head and that he shouldn't worry about them.
immoral_consequence: James gets upset and accuses Ron of not understanding what he's going through.

norm: It's very bad to kill someone.
situation: Terry is being held up by a young criminal with a knife who is demanding all his belongings.
intention: Terry wants to defend himself.
moral_action: Terry disarms the young man and calls the police for back up.
moral_consequence: The young man learns from the incident and changes his ways.
immoral_action: Terry defends himself and overpowers the young man which results in his death.
immoral_consequence: The young man's family has to mourn the loss of a family member.

norm: It's good to be happy to be alive.
situation: "Sandra is walking to her desk at the office after getting into work when her coworker greets her with a ""Good morning""."
intention: Sandra wants to respond to the coworker's good morning greeting.
moral_action: Sandra tells her coworker thank you and wishes her a good day as well.
moral_consequence: Sandra's coworker is happy that Sandra greeted her back and wished her a good day also.
immoral_action: Sandra tells her coworker it's not a good morning at all, and she wishes she were dead.
immoral_consequence: Sandra's coworker is irritated and having her greeting brushed off and feels weird being next to depressing Sandra.

norm: It's unacceptable to leave a dog with an animal abuser.
situation: John is about to go on vacation.
intention: John wants to have someone watch his dog.
moral_action: John books a stay at a well known boarding kennel for his dog.
moral_consequence: John and his dog both have fun on their vacations.
immoral_action: John leaves his dog with his friend that hates animals because it is free.
immoral_consequence: John comes back to find that his dog has been starved to death.

norm: Arrogance is frowned upon.
situation: Jake just landed a big client for the financial management company he is working at.
intention: Jake wants to be admired by his peers.
moral_action: Jake discusses the new client with his coworkers and is proud, yet modest about the whole thing.
moral_consequence: Jake's coworkers admire his success and love how humble he is.
immoral_action: Jake boasts about securing the client and how he used this clever technique to woo them.
immoral_consequence: Jake's colleagues admire him for being clever but can't stand his bragging.

norm: It's bad to be controlling with your partner's freedoms.
situation: Jeff's girlfriend Jenny has a lot of guy friends that she enjoys hanging out with, making Jeff jealous.
intention: Jeff wants to not be bothered by Jenny's behavior.
moral_action: Jeff decides to speak to a psychologist about his jealousy issues.
moral_consequence: Jenny appreciates Jeff's changes in behavior after he started receiving counseling.
immoral_action: Jeff tells Jenny that if she doesn't stop seeing these other guys he's going to leave her.
immoral_consequence: Jenny is bitter that Jeff doesn't want her to have a good time, and the relationship soon sours.

norm: It's rude to call your best friend an idiot.
situation: Sally has been going to college to become a school counselor.
intention: Sally wants to be on a short list of potential counseling interns at her school and tells her friends about it on social media.
moral_action: When Amelie asks questions about it, Sally makes sure her friend understands everything before continuing.
moral_consequence: When the intern counselors see Sally’s ability to talk to others and help them understand the situation, they put Sally’s name on the list with a commendation.
immoral_action: When Sally’s her best friend, Amelie, doesn’t understand some of the conversation; Sally publicly mocks her for being slow and stupid.
immoral_consequence: Sally hurts her friend deeply and when the intern counselors see Sally’s treatment of other online, they put her name on the list as a questionable candidate for counseling.

norm: It's irresponsible to have a baby as a teenager.
situation: Rosa wanted to have kids with her boyfriend Nate now so that they'd be grown before they were middle aged.
intention: Rosa wants to have kids with Nate.
moral_action: Rosa and Nate decide to wait until they're married and out out college first.
moral_consequence: Their families help put them through college first.
immoral_action: Rosa and Nate have their kids right away like they want.
immoral_consequence: Turns out their families don't agree with them and stop supporting them financially.

norm: You shouldn't approach a stranger's campsite unannounced.
situation: John is using the facilities in the middle of the night at a National Park camp site.
intention: John wants to find his campsite.
moral_action: John remembers what number campsite his tent is at and makes his way quietly back to it while avoiding other's campsites.
moral_consequence: All the campers at the campsite are able to sleep as they go undisturbed by John.
immoral_action: John approaches the first tent he sees and attempts to open it thinking it may be his.
immoral_consequence: The occupants of the tent scream in fright and freak out that a stranger is trying to come into their tent.

norm: It's gracious to tip a server well.
situation: Charles, a devout Christian, is dining out at a restaurant with his large family.
intention: Charles wants to show his appreciation to his server.
moral_action: Charles leaves the server a 25% tip on the bill.
moral_consequence: The server receives money they need and remembers to provide good service to Charles in the future.
immoral_action: "Instead of leaving a tip, Charles writes ""You are blessed"" on the receipt."
immoral_consequence: The server makes less money than they should and warns the other servers about Charles and his family.

norm: You shouldn't stay in a loveless relationship.
situation: Ray is becoming tired of his relationship and has fallen out of love.
intention: Ray wants to avoid confronting his partner directly.
moral_action: Ray explains his feelings over text and breaks up from a distance.
moral_consequence: Ray's partner knows the truth and is able to move on quickly.
immoral_action: Ray buries his feelings and keeps going through the motions pretending nothing is wrong.
immoral_consequence: Ray's partner thinks there is nothing wrong and is led on.

norm: It's good to be honest when dealing with others.
situation: Dan has an older car with some mechanical problems and has been looking at new cars.
intention: Dan wants to sell the car quickly to get money for a down payment.
moral_action: Dan posts the car for sale online at a lower price because of the issues it has.
moral_consequence: The buyer is happy to pay a reduced price and wants to fix it himself.
immoral_action: Dan posts an ad saying that the car is in perfect mechanical condition.
immoral_consequence: Dan sells the car and the buyer is livid when he finds out the car's true condition.

norm: You shouldn't send perverted messages to people.
situation: Cory has taken an interest in a girl and finds her to be quite attractive.
intention: Cory wants to flirt with the girl.
moral_action: Cory waits until they get to know each other more and acts suggestively with her in person.
moral_consequence: The girl feels comfortable enough to flirt back at him.
immoral_action: Cory starts to send her intimate messages about what he wants to do with her.
immoral_consequence: The girl is not into it and quickly loses interest in him.

norm: It's wrong to steal things from stores.
situation: Robert is at the mall when he realizes that it is father's day but he is low on funds.
intention: Robert wants to save money on a father's day gift.
moral_action: Robert uses a credit card to buy the gift for his dad.
moral_consequence: Robert doesn't have to pay for the gift until his billing cycle is up.
immoral_action: Robert finds something for his dad and slips it into his pocket without paying.
immoral_consequence: Robert gets caught shoplifting at the mall and faces criminal charges.

norm: It's rude to push expectations onto a new love interest.
situation: Ben and Dana have been dating only a short while and Ben had told Dana he wants to get married eventually and Dana is hesitant.
intention: Ben wants to comment on Dana's hesitancy to marry him.
moral_action: Ben tells Dana that he's only talking about an eventual dream and that she need not feel pressured.
moral_consequence: Dana is relieved that Ben didn't mean he wants to marry her right away and is open to exploring the future with him.
immoral_action: Ben tells Dana that he insists they get married very soon or their relationship is pointless.
immoral_consequence: Dana is quite turned off to be so pressured and ends up just breaking up with Ben right there.

norm: People shouldn't gross out their friends with surgical pictures.
situation: Paul is studying human anatomy with his friends.
intention: Paul wants to share what he's learning.
moral_action: Paul explains the material in his notes to his friends.
moral_consequence: Paul's knowledge impresses his friends who ask him questions whenever they need medical advice.
immoral_action: Paul points out the parts of the arm by showing them pictures of the arm he dissected during lab.
immoral_consequence: Paul's friends quietly excuse themselves leaving Paul alone for the rest of the evening.

norm: It's discouraged to act out for attention in public.
situation: Jacob and Marcy are at the mall together looking for a new pair of shoes for Marcy.
intention: Jacob wants Mary to be more interested in him.
moral_action: Jacob helps Marcy find the perfect shoes and asks if he can buy her lunch.
moral_consequence: Marcy and Jacob have a great dinner together and get to know each other more.
immoral_action: Jacob gets up onto a display and begins singing to Marcy to catch her attention.
immoral_consequence: Marcy stares at Jacob, feels embarrassed and leaves the mall, asking Jacob not to call her anymore.

norm: You shouldn't throw things at people that have special needs.
situation: Amanda is on the school bus and is trying to make her friends laugh about things on the school bus.
intention: Amanda wants her friends to think she's funny.
moral_action: Amanda makes a joke about how ugly the school bus seats are.
moral_consequence: Amanda's friends laugh and everyone has a good trip to school.
immoral_action: Amanda throws a piece of chewed gum at the hair of a child with multiple disabilities.
immoral_consequence: Amanda and her friends laugh, but the disabled child is very upset and panics all the way to school and reports Amanda for bullying.

norm: It's immoral to poke holes in condoms.
situation: Jake is about to have intercourse with Mary who asks him to wear a condom and  hands him one.
intention: Jake wants to put on the condom.
moral_action: Jake takes the condom and without much ado slips it on before contiuing.
moral_consequence: Mary does not get pregnant nor does she get any diseases transmitted to her.
immoral_action: Jake takes the condom and lets his nail scratch a hole into it before slipping it on.
immoral_consequence: A few weeks later Mary realizes that she is now pregnant with an unplanned child.

norm: It's not okay to hate others for who they are.
situation: James was raised in a very conservative, religious family and never met an LGBT person until he went to college.
intention: James wants to be a kind person.
moral_action: James talks to the LGBT people he meets and reads some of the books they recommend.
moral_consequence: James comes to realize that LGBT people aren't very different from anyone else.
immoral_action: James tries to convince the LGBT people he meets that they're going to hell and need to become straight.
immoral_consequence: James is shunned at most parties and generally unpopular on campus.

norm: You should not drive irresponsibly.
situation: Homer is driving home from work on a busy highway when he encounters heavy traffic.
intention: Homer wants to get home quickly.
moral_action: Homer decides their most be a better route and exits the highway to take back roads to home.
moral_consequence: A few other cars follow Homer, thereby reducing traffic on the highway and making it safer for everyone.
immoral_action: Homer sees an opening and quickly swerves through three lanes of traffic to get into a faster lane.
immoral_consequence: Homer cuts off another driver who slams on the brakes and barely avoids being rear-ended.

norm: It's rude to ask people to pay for your party.
situation: Greg is hosting a party for his co-workers when he realizes that he spent way more than he's able to pay.
intention: Greg wants to pay for the party.
moral_action: Greg contacts a family member and asks for a short-term loan to cover the party costs temporarily.
moral_consequence: The family member gives the loan and the co-workers enjoy the party.
immoral_action: Greg gets everyone's attention and announces that everyone needs to pay $20 to cover the costs of the party.
immoral_consequence: Greg's co-workers get upset, as Greg never told them that they had to pay.

norm: It's bad to cheat on someone you're dating.
situation: Sam's ex-girlfriend comes to town and asks him to join her for drinks, but Sam is currently dating someone else.
intention: Sam wants to respond to her request.
moral_action: Sam turns down the offer, mentioning that his girlfriend would disapprove if he did.
moral_consequence: Sam and his girlfriend maintain a strong relationship and get married.
immoral_action: Sam gets drinks with his ex-girlfriend and then has sex with her.
immoral_consequence: Sam's girlfriend finds out and dumps him.

norm: You shouldn't keep repeatedly contacting someone since it's obnoxious.
situation: Chris is on a date with his girlfriend, and Luke has run into an issue while working on their project.
intention: Luke wants to solve the problem.
moral_action: Luke watches several youtube tutorials on issues related to his project.
moral_consequence: Luke gains a deeper understanding of the various parts of his project.
immoral_action: Luke calls Chris multiple times hoping that speaking to someone will give him inspiration.
immoral_consequence: Luke is unable to contact Chris for the next couple of days after Chris blocks him.

norm: You should help old people out when they are sick.
situation: On the way to the store, Kevin noticed that the old woman that lived next to him wasn't feeling well.
intention: Kevin wants to get his groceries.
moral_action: Kevin goes to the grocery store and gets his things alone with soup and medicine for his neighbor.
moral_consequence: Kevin's neighbor starts to feel better after eating the soup and taking the medicine.
immoral_action: Kevin goes straight to the grocery store and returns to his house without checking on his neighbor.
immoral_consequence: Kevin's neighbor ends up getting sicker and has to go to the hospital.

norm: It's good to help someone with their homework.
situation: Kennedy is at the library during a study hour with other students and friends in her class.
intention: Kennedy wants to study to be prepared for class.
moral_action: Kennedy partners up with a friend, so they can quiz each other back and forth on the subject.
moral_consequence: Kennedy benefits from the mutual back and forth help and does well in the class.
immoral_action: Kennedy finds a quiet corner and keeps to herself while reading material from the class.
immoral_consequence: Kennedy inadvertently studies the wrong chapter and doesn't realize it until it is too late.

norm: It's good to invite family to your special events.
situation: Judy and Jarvis have been dating for a long time and want to get married.
intention: Judy wants to decide what kind of wedding they should have.
moral_action: Judy decides they should hold an extravagant wedding at the local church with a huge family guest list.
moral_consequence: Judy and Jarvis's families are overjoyed at the marraige announcement and offer to help pay for the ceremony.
immoral_action: Judy pushes for them to elope and get married privately.
immoral_consequence: Judy and Jarvis's families are upset at being excluded from such an important occasion.

norm: It's bad to highly value drinking.
situation: Elysse is having a busy season at work.
intention: Elysse wants to find a way to relax every night.
moral_action: Elysse takes a warm bath every night after work.
moral_consequence: Elysse allows herself to release her stress.
immoral_action: Elysse drinks a bottle of wine every night after work.
immoral_consequence: Elysse becomes addicted to alcohol.

norm: It is kind to get others Christmas gifts.
situation: It's December and this is the first year that Josh has had a real job.
intention: Josh wants to visit his family over his winter vacation.
moral_action: Josh uses money he earned at his new job to by wonderful gifts for his family that he delivers to them personally on Christmas Eve.
moral_consequence: Josh's family thanks him for the gifts and Josh feels warm and fuzzy inside.
immoral_action: Josh spends Christmas at his parents house but doesn't give anyone gifts.
immoral_consequence: Everyone in Josh's family scorns Josh causing him to feel dejected and embarrassed.

norm: It is good to thank someone who drives you home.
situation: Tom is very drunk, and Olivia is the designated driver for their group.
intention: Tom wants to go home.
moral_action: Tom says thanks when they get to his house and offers to return the favor.
moral_consequence: Olivia thinks Tom is a good guy and helps him with other things in the future.
immoral_action: When Olivia drops Tom off, he just leaves the car without saying anything.
immoral_consequence: Olivia feels slighted and doesn't offer to help Tom anymore.

norm: You shouldn't pretend to be someone you aren't online.
situation: Shannon is on a dating app and has grown very close to a man named Ted who also uses the app.
intention: Shannon wants to meet Ted in person.
moral_action: Shannon uses honest photos of herself on her profile and sets up a dinner date to meet Ted.
moral_consequence: Ted tells Shannon she looks just like her photos, and they start a new relationship in real life.
immoral_action: After using pictures of a supermodel on her dating profile, Shannon finally meets Ted in person.
immoral_consequence: Ted does not recognize Shannon and leaves after finding out what she had done.

norm: It's bad to profit off of a tragedy.
situation: Don has information about deadly viruses and drug companies before a pandemic.
intention: Don wants to make money.
moral_action: Don funds his own research into a vaccine for a deadly virus and sells it so people can get it.
moral_consequence: Many people are prepared for the pandemic and don't get sick and love Don a lot.
immoral_action: Don works to plant a deadly pandemic while investing in certain drug company's stocks related to the virus.
immoral_consequence: Many people die and get sick and people resent Don profusely.

norm: It is bad to exclude a partner from a vacation.
situation: Bill wins two tickets to an all-expenses paid vacation from a sweepstakes he enters, and both his girlfriend and his best friend want to go with him.
intention: Bill wants to give the second ticket to someone.
moral_action: Bill gives the ticket to his girlfriend, and they go on vacation together.
moral_consequence: Bill's girlfriend has a great time going on vacation with him.
immoral_action: Bill gives the ticket to his best friend, and they go on vacation together.
immoral_consequence: Bill's girlfriend dumps him when she finds out he's not going to bring her on vacation.

norm: Blaming others for your short-comings and rationalizing it is inappropriate.
situation: Lance, who has some duties to do at home, performs poorly in a class and fails the final exam because he didn't put in enough effort.
intention: Lance wants to feel better about his failure.
moral_action: Lance tells himself that he failed this time, but that he'll improve next time.
moral_consequence: Lance makes a concentrated effort to improve and succeeds next time.
immoral_action: Lance tells his parents that he failed the exam because they make him do too many chores.
immoral_consequence: Lance never overcomes his laziness and continues to perform poorly in school.

norm: It's good to get a new kitty as a pet.
situation: Rachel loves animals and is looking online at possible pets to have.
intention: Rachel wants to pick out a pet to get.
moral_action: Rachel sees some cute kittens, remembers that someone nearby has a litter, and picks one for herself.
moral_consequence: The kitten turns into a beautiful and affectionate cat that loves to hunt disgusting rodents.
immoral_action: Rachel sees how cute baby raccoons are and goes to the country to get one.
immoral_consequence: The raccoons are nice until they hit 18 months, then turn violent and hurt Rachel.

norm: It's good for brothers to do things together.
situation: Jonny has 3 brothers and tickets to a sports game.
intention: Jonny wants to find people to bring to the game.
moral_action: Jonny asks his 3 brothers to go to the game with him.
moral_consequence: Jonny and his brothers will develop their bond.
immoral_action: Jonny asks friends from school to go to the game instead of his brothers.
immoral_consequence: Jonny and his brothers will not share fun moments together.

norm: It's rude to ignore your spouse.
situation: Ted didn't sleep well last night and is really tired, but his wife keeps on telling him about something she read.
intention: Ted wants to take a nap right now.
moral_action: Ted tells his wife that he genuinely wants to hear about her story but that he's so tired he can't focus and needs a nap.
moral_consequence: Ted's wife is glad that he told her how he feels and plans on telling him the story after his nap.
immoral_action: Ted pretends he doesn't hear his wife as she keeps on talking, and he goes to bed.
immoral_consequence: Ted's wife doesn't understand why he's ignoring her and is hurt.

norm: It's bad to prevent someone from seeing their friends.
situation: Lee is in a new relationship that he is excited about.
intention: Lee wants to spend the most time possible with his partner.
moral_action: Lee asks if he can meet his partner's friends and go out with them sometimes.
moral_consequence: Lee meets his partner's friends and makes new friends as well.
immoral_action: Lee tells his partner that he can no longer go out once a week with his friends.
immoral_consequence: Lee's partner breaks up with him for being controlling.

norm: One should respect their family.
situation: Christina, a five year old, bites her lip as she stares at her father who refuses to take her to the park.
intention: Christina wants to express her anger.
moral_action: Christina calls her friend and vents to her about her parents.
moral_consequence: Christina feels better after getting all of the negative energy out of her.
immoral_action: Christina calls her father a strange monkey face and sticks her tongue out at him.
immoral_consequence: Christina is sent to time out for the remainder of the afternoon.

norm: You shouldn't call mentally challenged people losers.
situation: A mentally challenged man stopped Jeff on the sidewalk and wanted to have a conversation.
intention: Jeff wants to get away from the man.
moral_action: Jeff tells the man that he's late for an appointment.
moral_consequence: The man doesn't want to bother Jeff, so he leaves him alone.
immoral_action: Jeff tells the man to get away from him and calls him a loser.
immoral_consequence: The man's feelings are hurt, and he doesn't understand what he did wrong.

norm: You shouldn't call your friends bad words.
situation: Tim is playing his game together with his friend when his friend damages the game by mistake.
intention: Tim wants to show his friend that he's unhappy that they broke the game.
moral_action: Tim tells his friend that he's really upset they damaged the game and that they can't play it any more.
moral_consequence: Tim's friend thinks Tim's reaction is fair, and they apologize for damaging the game.
immoral_action: Tim yells at his friend calling him some by some very bad words.
immoral_consequence: Tim's friend is insulted and thinks Tim could have reacted in a nicer way to their mistake.

norm: Peeing on yourself is gross.
situation: Pete and his friends are on a long car ride to the mountains when he gets the urge to pee.
intention: Pete wants to relieve himself.
moral_action: Pete asks his friends to stop at the nearest rest area.
moral_consequence: Pete is able to relieve himself quickly and the trip resumes as scheduled.
immoral_action: Not wanting to slow down the trip, Pete soils himself in the car.
immoral_consequence: Pete's friends are grossed out, and have to stop anyway to clean out the car.

norm: It's bad to be a sore loser.
situation: Emma was upset that she lost the board game to Trucy.
intention: Emma wants to show her anger.
moral_action: Emma challenges Trucy to a rematch insisting Trucy was simply lucky.
moral_consequence: They begin to play the game once more for the fun.
immoral_action: Emma flips over the table on Trucy and the board and pieces and table all spill onto her.
immoral_consequence: Trucy doesn't want to play games with Emma anymore.

norm: It's bad to treat people poorly for expressing themselves.
situation: Jill decides to join a Buddhist temple and shaves her head as a indication of her faith.
intention: Jill wants to show evidence of Buddhist faith by denying the vanity.
moral_action: Betty inquires on Jill's new faith and hair while listening intently.
moral_consequence: Jill hugs Betty and happily feels her faith increase.
immoral_action: Jill's friend Betty mocks her hair and her faith.
immoral_consequence: Jill spends the entire day crying.

norm: You shouldn't stay with someone for their money.
situation: Charlotte is dating Logan who has inherited much wealth from his parents, but she is unsure if she feels strong feelings for him.
intention: Charlotte wants to have much wealth.
moral_action: Charlotte decides to focus on her own career and break up with Logan.
moral_consequence: Charlotte finds happiness by creating her own wealth and finding someone she is truly happy with.
immoral_action: Charlotte decides to move into Logan's mansion with him.
immoral_consequence: Charlotte realizes that money can't by love as she is incredibly unhappy in her relationship with Logan.

norm: It's expected that you will support your friends' businesses.
situation: Frank's friend Louis has worked very hard and recently opened a pizzeria that he is very proud of.
intention: Frank wants to order pizza for a party.
moral_action: Frank orders pizzas from Louis's new restaurant for his party.
moral_consequence: Louis's pizza gets good worth of mouth reviews from partygoers and more people start coming to his restaurants.
immoral_action: Frank orders pizzas from a large national chain for his party.
immoral_consequence: Louis is hurt that Frank did not give his restaurant a chance and becomes distant from Frank.

norm: It's wrong to expected people to buy you things
situation: Kyle, who receives money for doing chores around the house, is a teenager who learns about a sequel to his favorite video game series coming out.
intention: Kyle wants to obtain the game.
moral_action: Kyle saves up his allowance money in order to buy the game for himself.
moral_consequence: Kyle's parents notice him saving money and are view him as responsible.
immoral_action: Kyle goes up to his parents and asks them to buy the game for him.
immoral_consequence: Kyle's parents start to think that he is becoming spoiled.

norm: It is nice to apologize if you break something.
situation: Carrie is admiring her friend Debbie's china doll collection when she accidentally breaks the arm off one.
intention: Carrie wants to react to what happened.
moral_action: Carrie apologizes to Debbie and asks if she can somehow replace the china doll.
moral_consequence: Carrie tells Debbie not to worry, she will see if she can have the doll repaired.
immoral_action: Carrie says that she didn't expect the doll to be so fragile, and sets it back down.
immoral_consequence: Debbie is annoyed that Carrie doesn't seem to care that she broke she broke a part of her collection.

norm: It's rude to catfish people on a dating app.
situation: Toby joins an internet dating site for people around his age.
intention: Toby wants to meet someone with the same interests as him.
moral_action: Toby tells the other person immediately that he is not the person in the picture.
moral_consequence: The other person respects that Toby told the truth and still wants to get to know him.
immoral_action: Toby puts a picture of someone else that does not look like him and attracts someone.
immoral_consequence: Toby never meets the other person because then they would know he was lying the entire time.

norm: You shouldn't break into houses.
situation: James' TV broke, and he knew it would take months to save enough money to buy a new one.
intention: James wants a new TV immediately.
moral_action: James opens a new store card at Walmart and uses it to buy a new TV.
moral_consequence: James enjoys watching his new TV as he slowly pays off his credit card.
immoral_action: James knocks out a window in his neighbor's house and takes their TV.
immoral_consequence: James' neighbor calls the police, but they don't take much action on the case.

norm: You shouldn't hit someone because they're gay.
situation: Al's son Joe is having a discussion with Al when he mentions that he is gay.
intention: Al wants to respond to Joe coming out as gay.
moral_action: Al hugs Joe and tells him he will still love him.
moral_consequence: Joe will embrace Al back and tell him he loves him too.
immoral_action: Al balls up his fist and hits Joe in the face.
immoral_consequence: Joe will hit Al back and they will fight.

norm: It is rude to interrupt someone's dinner.
situation: Bob has a question to ask his friend, but he knows that they are sitting down to dinner at this time.
intention: Bob wants to ask their friend the question.
moral_action: Bob waits an hour then calls his friend and asks him a question.
moral_consequence: Bob's friend doesn't mind giving Bob an answer since they aren't doing anything else.
immoral_action: Bob calls his friend and asks them the question he has even though he knows that they're probably eating dinner.
immoral_consequence: Bob's friend is annoyed to be called up and queried by Bob while they are eating dinner.

norm: It's wrong to hate your country.
situation: James is attending a Fourth of July barbecue with his family and about a hundred neighbors.
intention: James wants to express his political views.
moral_action: "James leads all his neighbors in singing ""The Star Spangled Banner""."
moral_consequence: James and his neighbors feel closer after singing together to celebrate the holiday.
immoral_action: James sets a paper American flag on fire to protest the Trump administration.
immoral_consequence: James is asked to leave because his actions are contrary to the spirit of the holiday.

norm: You shouldn't take belongings that don't belong to you.
situation: At the end of gym class, while Mike is in the bathroom, Jim notices there is a PSP in Mike's locker.
intention: Jim wants to play the PSP.
moral_action: When Mike returns, Jim asks Mike if he can play the PSP sometime.
moral_consequence: Mike says he can play the PSP tomorrow and this makes Jim happy.
immoral_action: Jim takes the PSP before Mike comes back.
immoral_consequence: Someone saw Jim, reported Jim to the teacher and Jim got in trouble.

norm: You should share the household chores with your partner.
situation: Roy hates doing housework but his girlfriend, Shelly, can't stand it either, but neither of them want to live in a dirty house.
intention: Tom wants to decide on a proposal to put forth, about the household chores.
moral_action: Tom suggests that the two of them sit down and negotiate a housework schedule, to keep things in order.
moral_consequence: Shelly agrees with this approach, and they hash out a schedule that they can both live with, and the house stays relatively clean.
immoral_action: Tom takes a hard line approach and refuses to do any of the household chores, because he doesn't have time for that.
immoral_consequence: Shelly tells Tom that she will not be the only one cleaning the house, leaving the two at an impasse.

norm: It's wrong to yell at people at memorials.
situation: John is out for a walk when he sees his friend attending a memorial service.
intention: John wants to greet his friend.
moral_action: John decides to call his friend later to offer his condolences.
moral_consequence: John's friend appreciates John's sensitivity.
immoral_action: John shouts to his friend to get his attention.
immoral_consequence: John's friend is upset at John's rude behavior.

norm: It is foolish to take dangerous motorcycle rides by yourself.
situation: Biff just bought an expensive new motorcycle to show off and ride on.
intention: Biff wants to ride his motorcycle.
moral_action: Biff plans safe riding routes with his friends and then shows off how fast it can go.
moral_consequence: Biff and his friends have a lot of fun riding their motorcycles.
immoral_action: Biff rides the motorcycle and first time out he crashes into a tree.
immoral_consequence: Biff is fine but is motorcycle is totaled beyond repair, all he could do is buy another one.

norm: It is good to keep some space.
situation: Hank buys a used big screen television and has to put it in his cramped car to get it home.
intention: Hank wants to put the television in the car.
moral_action: Hank gets rid of some of the unnecessary items in his car to make room for the television.
moral_consequence: Hank is able to get the television home without any problems.
immoral_action: Hank squishes the television in the car on top of other stuff.
immoral_consequence: The television gets a crack in the screen and Hank has to buy another one.

norm: It's nice to respect the wishes of others.
situation: Niro has a crush on Mylah, his best friend Noah's ex-girlfriend,  but Noah has asked him not to date her.
intention: Niro wants to hang out with Mylah.
moral_action: Niro invites Mylah to his house party as friends.
moral_consequence: Niro and Mylah become platonic friends, and Noah is okay with the situation.
immoral_action: Niro asks Mylah out on a date.
immoral_consequence: Noah sees Niro and Mylah on their date together, and the guys lose their friendship over it.

norm: You shouldn't yell in someone's house.
situation: Henry and John are at John's house and are at a long dinner table.
intention: Henry wants John to pass him the salt.
moral_action: Henry sens John a text and asks him to slide the salt down the table.
moral_consequence: John thinks a text is a funny way to communicate and walks the salt over to John while laughing.
immoral_action: Henry  screams from across the table for John to slide the salt down to him.
immoral_consequence: John feels Henry is rude and is shocked at how loud and unpleasant Henry's voice is.

norm: People shouldn't be wasteful by using redundant products.
situation: Joanne is at the store examining various hair products.
intention: Joanne wants to have nice hair.
moral_action: Joanne looks up reviews on the internet before deciding to make her own hair mask.
moral_consequence: Joanne's hair feels soft and smooth for the rest of the week.
immoral_action: Joanne buys half of the different types of hair products.
immoral_consequence: Joanne is stuck with a bunch of products that do the same thing.

norm: You shouldn't force your family to do things.
situation: Margaret is looking into schools to send her son to.
intention: Margaret wants her son to go to a school that will help him be successful in the future.
moral_action: Margaret asks her son what kind of school he would like to attend.
moral_consequence: Her son tells her he would like to go to a law school and subsequently gets into one and does extremely well.
immoral_action: Margaret applies to the school for her son and forces him to go there when she finds out hes been accepted.
immoral_consequence: Her son hates the school, he doesn't want to do this type of work and eventually drops out.

norm: It's wrong to do something that will hurt a sibling
situation: Jane sees her brother Mark eat the last cookie.
intention: Jane wants to teach Mark a lesson.
moral_action: Jane explains to Mark why this was rude.
moral_consequence: Mark feels sorry for not asking if anyone else wanted the cookie.
immoral_action: Jane punches Mark.
immoral_consequence: Mark's arm is hurt, and he is mad at his sister.

norm: It's good to wait for your friend.
situation: Alex had planned to meet his friend Alyssa at the bar at 8 pm and it  is now 8:!10 and Alyssa still hasn't arrived.
intention: Alex wants to decide what to do next.
moral_action: Alex decides to wait for Alyssa for another while before leaving to see if she might show.
moral_consequence: Alyssa arrives and is relieved to see Alex still there and apologizes for being late.
immoral_action: Alex decides to leave and go back home as Alyssa has missed their scheduled meetup time.
immoral_consequence: Alyssa is annoyed when she finally does arrive that Alex had already left and ruined the night.

norm: It's rude to tell someone to shut up.
situation: Bobby is watching a movie at a movie theater and a man behind him begins talking a bit loudly.
intention: Bobby wants to get the man to stop talking.
moral_action: Bobby turns around and asks the man if he could please stop talking while the movie is on.
moral_consequence: The man feels embarrassed for disturbing Bobby and immediately goes quiet for the rest of the film.
immoral_action: Bobby turns around and rudely tells the man that he need to shut up so everyone can hear.
immoral_consequence: The man behind Bobby gets angry and escalates the scene by trying to start a fight.

norm: It's not okay to show off and be vain.
situation: Tammy is the head coach of a soccer team who just won their first regional tournament, and she's been called up to the podium to receive the trophy.
intention: Tammy wants to give an acceptance speech.
moral_action: Tammy invites the whole team up to the podium and thanks all the team members for their hard work and perseverance that earned them the trophy.
moral_consequence: Tammy's team is thrilled to have her as their coach, and they vow to try their hardest next season as well.
immoral_action: Tammy spends the entirety of her time at the podium talking about her skills and how well she coached the team.
immoral_consequence: Tammy's team finds her attitude off-putting, and they're offended that she is taking all the credit for the win.

norm: You should never resort to physical violence with anyone
situation: Robert can't concentrate in class because Dave is tapping on his shoulder.
intention: Robert wants Dave to stop.
moral_action: Robert asks Dave to stop tapping him.
moral_consequence: Dave stops and Robert can finally concentrate.
immoral_action: Robert punches Dave in the face.
immoral_consequence: Dave is injured and Robert gets in trouble.

norm: You shouldn't push away your friends.
situation: Betty is tired of hanging around with all of her friends.
intention: Betty wants her friend to leave her alone.
moral_action: Betty takes a vacation, so she can just get away from everyone.
moral_consequence: Betty returns refreshed and is happy to see all her friends again.
immoral_action: Betty gets into physical fights and arguments with all of her friends.
immoral_consequence: No one wants to be around Betty anymore because she is rude and nasty.

norm: You should return borrowed items.
situation: Sam forgot his calculator at home.
intention: Sam wants to find a calculator he can use on his math test.
moral_action: Sam borrows a calculator from his friends and gives it back once the class is over.
moral_consequence: Sam and his friend are both able to use the calculator on their tests.
immoral_action: Sam borrows a calculator from his friend but doesn't return it after the test.
immoral_consequence: Sam's friend does not have their calculator when it's their turn to take the math test.

norm: It's impolite to interrupt someone when they're speaking.
situation: Janet is in a work meeting.
intention: Janet wants to share a good idea she has.
moral_action: Janet waits until it is her turn to speak to share her idea.
moral_consequence: Janet's coworkers listen to her attentively.
immoral_action: Janet cuts off a co-worker to blurt her idea out.
immoral_consequence: Janet is reprimanded for being rude and her idea is put aside.

norm: You shouldn't say hurtful things to others.
situation: Rebecca just got a new haircut, and she's asking her friend Ellen what she thinks of it.
intention: Ellen wants to give Rebecca her opinion.
moral_action: Ellen tells Rebecca that while she doesn't like it as much as her old haircut, she still pulls it off well.
moral_consequence: Rebecca takes Ellen's input into consideration and decides to go back to the hairdresser to improve the hairstyle.
immoral_action: Ellen tells Rebecca that the haircut looks really bad and that she should get it fixed.
immoral_consequence: Rebecca's feelings are hurt, and she feels really ugly.

norm: Please consider to do your share of the work
situation: Nelson was in a group to do a project for school.
intention: Nelson wants to get a good grade.
moral_action: Nelson does all he can do to work with his classmates on the project.
moral_consequence: Nelson and his classmates make an A on the project that they turn in.
immoral_action: Nelson doesn't work on the project at all, letting his classmates do all of the work instead.
immoral_consequence: Nelson's classmates tell the teacher that he didn't work on the project at all.

norm: You shouldn't use loud headphones because it annoys other people.
situation: Fred is waiting at his doctor's office for a physical check up, and he sees a good music video while surfing the internet.
intention: Fred wants to watch the music video.
moral_action: Fred saves the video, and he decides to watch it later at home.
moral_consequence: The other patients are not disturbed while waiting in the room.
immoral_action: Fred uses his powerful headset and turns it up to the highest volume to watch the video.
immoral_consequence: The other patients get disturbed and annoyed by the sounds emitted from the headset.

norm: It's wrong to lie to your friends and family
situation: Mike didn't get offered the job he applied for and doesn't know what to tell his parents.
intention: Mike doesn't want his parents to be disappointed with him.
moral_action: Mike tells his parents that he didn't get the job but that he is going to volunteer at a homeless shelter until he does find a job.
moral_consequence: Mike's parents are proud of their son for helping people who are less fortunate.
immoral_action: Mike tells his parents that he got the job and his first day of work is Monday.
immoral_consequence: Mike's parents spend all of the money they saved for a special family trip on work clothes for Mike to wear to the new job.

norm: It's bad to be addicted.
situation: Meg has kids, but she has been going through a lot of stress lately due to her parents passing away.
intention: Meg wants to get rid of her pain.
moral_action: Meg starts working out and eating vegetables to get her body right.
moral_consequence: Meg is in a better mood to take care of and have fun with her kids.
immoral_action: Meg starts using crystal meth because she likes the feeling that it gives her.
immoral_consequence: Meg's kids don't get the support that they need to thrive, and Meg suffers.

norm: It's great to share your interests with those you love.
situation: James is a big fan of his video games and the type of entertainment they can bring.
intention: James wants to keep playing his video games.
moral_action: James shows the games to his family and tries to get them interested as well.
moral_consequence: Some of James's family start to like video games too.
immoral_action: James hides his games from his family and keeps them away.
immoral_consequence: James' family in turn avoids the games since James keeps them away.

norm: It's good to overcome the things you struggle with.
situation: Ben has been addicted to heroin ever since his friends gave him some at a party.
intention: Ben has to decide whether he wants to keep doing heroin.
moral_action: Ben meets with a counselor in order to see what he can do about his heroin use.
moral_consequence: Ben is able to get help, and he doesn't get too addicted to heroin.
immoral_action: Ben decides that heroin makes him feel good, so he's going to keep using it.
immoral_consequence: Ben becomes dependent on heroin and has trouble getting over the addiction.

norm: Being organized is good because it saves time.
situation: Charles lives in a messy house where he's always losing things, and is constantly wasting time trying to find stuff.
intention: Charles wants to become more efficient.
moral_action: Charles decides to clean up his bedroom, so he's no longer wasting time looking for things.
moral_consequence: Charles manages to find his personal items quickly every day from then on.
immoral_action: Charles decides to start speed walking around the house, avoiding piles of clutter in order to save time.
immoral_consequence: Charles trips on a pile of junk in his bedroom one day and twists an ankle.

norm: It's rude to judge others only by their physical appearance.
situation: Adam is at the gym when an obese woman comes and gets on the treadmill beside him.
intention: Adam wants to talk to the woman beside him.
moral_action: Adam strikes up a conversation with the woman and offers to help her with the treadmill controls.
moral_consequence: The woman is glad to accept Adam's help and converse with him to pass the time.
immoral_action: Adam tells the woman it's not easy to stop being lazy and try to lose weight.
immoral_consequence: The woman is embarrassed and discouraged from returning to the gym.

norm: You shouldn't hate your coworkers.
situation: Jim works in an office as as manager to employees, and Bob is his boss.
intention: Jim wants to give a report about his employees to Bob.
moral_action: Jim tells Bob his employees are doing well, but could be more hard working, and he doesn't hate them.
moral_consequence: Bob puts in measures to make Jim's employees more in line, and Jim appreciates it.
immoral_action: Jim tells Bob he hates his employees and doesn't want to be around them.
immoral_consequence: Bob fires Jim for not being a team player and Jim is now without a job.

norm: It's not okay to boss people around.
situation: Sara's partner wants to hang out with a female colleague after work.
intention: Sara wants to express how she feels uncomfortable by the idea.
moral_action: Sara calm explains her feelings and wonders if she can tag along.
moral_consequence: Sara's partner is understanding about the issue, and they find a compromise.
immoral_action: Sara yells at her partner and forbids him to go.
immoral_consequence: Sara's partner feels like she doesn't trust him.

norm: It's wrong to sleep while on the job
situation: Doe is tired at work and has four hours left on a slow day, with her boss out of sight.
intention: Doe wants to do something about her tiredness.
moral_action: Doe makes and drinks some coffee.
moral_consequence: She fights through her shift easier.
immoral_action: Doe takes a short nap at her desk.
immoral_consequence: Her boss walks in on her and yells at her.

norm: You shouldn't let your friends hold you back in life.
situation: John is hanging out with his friends when Jenny asks him to take her out on a date, but John’s friends tell him that Jenny is bad news.
intention: John wants to respond to Jenny's request for a date.
moral_action: John looks at his friends, then at Jenny and tells her he will take her out because he doesn't care what his friends think, he thinks she's swell.
moral_consequence: Jenny is delighted to see that John said yes and is extremely impressed that he's independent and can think for himself.
immoral_action: John looks at his friends, then at Jenny and tells her that if his friends think she's bad news, then she probably is and says no.
immoral_consequence: Jenny feels hurt by John's denial and the fact that he's legitimizing his friends' mockery of her.

norm: It is gross to spread germs when you are sick.
situation: Larry is sick with an infectious disease and his friend just gave him some soup in bed.
intention: Larry wants to hug his friend for giving him soup.
moral_action: Larry hugs his friend while keeping his infection away from his friend.
moral_consequence: Larry recovers and both have a good month, hanging out together.
immoral_action: Larry decides to hug, while rubbing his infection on his friend.
immoral_consequence: Larry's friend becomes infected a week later, and they both get angry at each other.

norm: Making someone feel bad when they just lost is rude.
situation: Jerome just beat his best friend Jeffrey at a close game of chess.
intention: Jerome wants to celebrate his victory.
moral_action: Jerome congratulates Jeffrey on playing a close game, and offers a couple bits of chess advice over dinner later.
moral_consequence: Jeffrey appreciates Jerome’s humility and takes his advice to heart during their next matches.
immoral_action: Jerome laughs at Jeffrey, calling him a big idiot for not seeing the checkmate coming.
immoral_consequence: Jeffrey thinks Jerome is being mean, and refuses to play him in the future.

norm: It's good to workout with your friends.
situation: Jack is stretching his legs in his local park when his friend, John, comes up to him and asks if he would like to run together.
intention: Jack wants to go on a run.
moral_action: Jack says sure and runs the trial with John.
moral_consequence: Jack and John have a nice chat and get some breakfast together.
