immoral_action: Jack tells John that he appreciates the offer, but he was intent on running alone today.
immoral_consequence: Jack runs off alone with his headphone on while John feels slighted.

norm: It is wrong to control other people's behavior.
situation: Sal's girlfriend spent a lot of time on the phone with her friends.
intention: Sal wanted his girlfriend to spend more time with him.
moral_action: Sal decided to plan dates for him and his girlfriend in advance to see if he could pry her from the phone.
moral_consequence: Sal and his girlfriend ended up spending much more time together becoming closer in their relationship.
immoral_action: Sal trying told his girlfriend she had to stop talking to her friends.
immoral_consequence: Sals girlfriend feeling pressured decided to break up with sal because he was being to controling.

norm: You shouldn't plagiarize your assignments.
situation: Ken is writing a paper for his class.
intention: He wants to gets good grade.
moral_action: Ken stays up late, does his research, and hands in a good original paper.
moral_consequence: Ken gets a good grade and learned along the way.
immoral_action: Ken copies a paper he found online and hands it in.
immoral_consequence: Ken’s teacher figures out it is a copy and gives Ken an F.

norm: It is good to encourage healthy habits in your children
situation: Mark is at home with his kids and needs to get some work done.
intention: Mark wants to find something to occupy his kid's attention for an hour.
moral_action: Mark hands his kids a ball and glove, telling them to go play catch in the yard.
moral_consequence: Mark's children get some exercise and learn to enjoy playing outside.
immoral_action: Mark blindly turns on the television to a cartoon.
immoral_consequence: Mark's children learn to be sedentary.

norm: It's good to listen to your parents.
situation: Colin is at home with his mother for the day instead of at school.
intention: Colin wants to find something entertaining.
moral_action: Colin says that she is bored and asks his mom for an idea of what to do.
moral_consequence: Colin's mom allows to hours of game time if he teaches her the game, he agrees, and they have a fun day.
immoral_action: Colin ignores his moms requests and plays video games throughout the day instead of the one hour of allowed game time.
immoral_consequence: Colin is sent to bed early and has game time taken away for one week.

norm: It's nice not to disturb someone.
situation: Joey sees that his Mother Mary is on a phone call, but wants to ask if he can go out to play.
intention: Joey wants to ask his question.
moral_action: Joey decides to wait until Mary finishes her call to ask if he can go out to play.
moral_consequence: Mary is proud of Joey for being patient and tells him he can go.
immoral_action: Joey decides to talk over Mary's conversation and ask if he can go outside.
immoral_consequence: Mary gets angry and tells Joey no because he interrupted her phone call.

norm: You should help others in times of need.
situation: Peter asks Kevin to borrow money as Peter recently lost his job.
intention: Kevin wants to respond to Peter's request.
moral_action: Kevin tells Peter that he would be glad to loan him money as long as Peter pays it back.
moral_consequence: Peter is delighted and relieved that his stress is eased and promises to pay it back quickly.
immoral_action: Kevin tells Peter that he actually doesn't have any money at all, even though he has a healthy bank account, and that he can't help.
immoral_consequence: Peter is scared and feels like the darkness around him is getting closer.

norm: It's wrong to sleep with underage girls.
situation: Robert is a handsome 25 year old high school teacher who is popular with his students.
intention: Robert wants to get a girlfriend.
moral_action: Robert asks his friends to introduce him to some women who might be interested.
moral_consequence: Robert meets a woman his own age that he connects with and can have a relationship with.
immoral_action: Robert starts dating and sleeping with one of his students who he gets along with.
immoral_consequence: Robert gets in legal trouble when the girl's parents find out.

norm: You shouldn't steal other people's content.
situation: Mika needs to submit her essay before the due date in six hours, and she has writer's block.
intention: Mika doesn't want her work to be late.
moral_action: Mika does some writing exercises she finds online to get rid of her writers block.
moral_consequence: Mika gains a skill that she uses throughout her time in college.
immoral_action: Mika copies someone's essay from a blog.
immoral_consequence: Mika fails the class when her professor discovers the truth.

norm: It is bad to be late with things.
situation: Jenny is working on her math homework for tomorrow and doesn't think that she will finish in time.
intention: Jenny wants to get a good grade.
moral_action: Jenny finishes as much as she can, leaves a few problems blank, and turns in the homework.
moral_consequence: The teacher deducts some points for the missing problems but still gives Jenny a good grade.
immoral_action: Jenny keeps the homework, finishes it, and turns it in a day late.
immoral_consequence: The teacher deducts 20% of the points for the homework assignment because it's late.

norm: It's wrong to say the n-word.
situation: Nancy, a white person, and her black best friend Claira are listening to music when Nancy's favorite rap song comes on.
intention: Nancy wants to sing the song.
moral_action: Nancy asks Claira about words she can use in place of the slurs before singing.
moral_consequence: Claira's respect for Nancy increases.
immoral_action: Nancy sings along to the song repeating the slurs and offensive language.
immoral_consequence: Claira is offended by Nancy's actions.

norm: It's wrong for kids to lie to their parents.
situation: Lara is invited to a party with older kids.
intention: Lara wants to go to the party.
moral_action: Lara asks to go to the party and promises to be responsible.
moral_consequence: Lara is allowed to go and her parents extend her curfew.
immoral_action: Lara tells her parents she is studying but goes to the party instead.
immoral_consequence: The police bring Lara home and she is grounded.

norm: Taking someone else's belongings is not okay.
situation: Joe usually rides the bus to work while his roommate Frank drives to his own job at the same time.
intention: Joe wants to get to work.
moral_action: Joe walks to the bus stop and takes his regular bus to work.
moral_consequence: Frank drives his car to work on time and earns his pay for the day.
immoral_action: Joe takes Frank's car without asking and drives to work.
immoral_consequence: Frank doesn't have a way to get to work, misses his shift, and doesn't get paid for the day.

norm: It is bad to beat a kid.
situation: Richard is at home alone with his teenage son Greg, and they are arguing about his grades.
intention: Richard wants Greg to understand how important it is to have good grades.
moral_action: Richard sits Greg down and shows him the kind of grades and schooling he will need in order to become a lawyer like he wants.
moral_consequence: Richard will be proud when Greg gets accepted into law school because of his great academic performance,.
immoral_action: Richard punches Greg after he yells that school is stupid.
immoral_consequence: Richard will lose further control of Greg and his grades because he makes friends with kids who are bad influences just to spite his father.

norm: It's hurtful to take peoples pets away from them.
situation: Bill is a city bylaw officer who has been called to a disturbance in a suburb regarding Nate's dog being too loud and disturbing the neighbors.
intention: Bill has wants to resolve the neighborly dispute.
moral_action: Bill decides to tell the owner to keep the dog indoors or to get a muzzle for the dog otherhwise.
moral_consequence: The dog's owner is relieved that he won't be fined or arrested and agrees to take better care of the noise.
immoral_action: Bill decides to confiscate the dog from the owner and remove it from the household and give it to the pound.
immoral_consequence: The dog's owner is devastated and feels like a part of their family is being kidnapped from them.

norm: You shouldn't be upset at your friends.
situation: Mark is playing basketball with his friends, and they are down several points.
intention: Mark wants to coach his friends.
moral_action: Mark develops a plan that utilizes his friends' skills.
moral_consequence: Mark and his friends learn to cooperate towards common goals.
immoral_action: Mark tells his friends that they're doing everything wrong, and they are unskilled players.
immoral_consequence: Mark's friends will not want to play with him and Mark becomes lonely.

norm: It's rude to criticize someone for wearing leather.
situation: Bill is at work when Jim comes in wearing a bright yellow leather jumpsuit.
intention: Bill wants to react in shock to Jim's outfit.

moral_consequence: Jim laughs at Bill's reaction and tells him that's the reaction he was looking for.
immoral_action: Bill tells Jim that wearing an all leather outfit to work is absurd, and he should get out of there and go change.
immoral_consequence: Jim is annoyed that Bill thinks he's the outfit police and is angry that he's calling him absurd.

norm: It's wrong to do things that are illegal.
situation: Wesley is very bored one night, and is trying to figure out something to do.
intention: Wesley wants to go out and have fun.
moral_action: Wesley goes for a late night bike ride through the town.
moral_consequence: Wesley gets some exercise, and really enjoys the breeze.
immoral_action: Wesley goes to the abandoned warehouse and throws some rocks at it.
immoral_consequence: A vagrant comes out and screams at Wesley to go away.

norm: You should not purchase attention.
situation: Alyssa is a new Instagram model who is looking to build her brand and her online presence.
intention: Alyssa wants to get more followers.
moral_action: Alyssa studies other models and influencers to find an unfilled niche and develops new content to fill that niche.
moral_consequence: Alyssa begins organically gaining followers who are genuinely interested in her, and they bring in more followers.
immoral_action: Alyssa buys a couple thousand followers from a website to boost her profile.
immoral_consequence: Alyssa gets called out by observers for being fake when her follower count jumps dramatically overnight but interaction with her posts doesn't.

norm: You shouldn't associate with someone that lies.
situation: Tim has a classmate that regularly lies and steals from other classmates.
intention: Tim wants to confront the classmate about her lying habit.
moral_action: Tim tells the classmate to stop lying and ceases contact with them.
moral_consequence: Tim is glad the situation is handled and the classmate feels sad.
immoral_action: Tim tells the lying classmate that he wants to be friends with them, and he forgives them.
immoral_consequence: Tim enters an abusive relationship with the classmate, and regrets doing so.

norm: It's bad to wear dirty shoes inside.
situation: Hal has been working in the muddy yard.
intention: Hal wants to get a bucket from the kitchen.
moral_action: Hal takes off his shoes outside before going to the kitchen.
moral_consequence: Hal will have a clean kitchen.
immoral_action: Hal walks into the kitchen without taking off his shoes.
immoral_consequence: Hal will have to clean the mud on the kitchen floor.

norm: It's wrong to love cheating.
situation: Dave is playing poker with friends when he gets caught dealing an ace to himself from the bottom of the deck, and they demand an explanation.
intention: Dave wants to give his reasons for cheating.
moral_action: Dave tells the group that he's in desperate need of money and that he's sorry he crossed the line.
moral_consequence: Dave's friends are concerned for Dave's financial situation and forgive him for his bad deed.
immoral_action: Dave tells the group that he just loves the thrill of getting away with such things, and they should try it sometime.
immoral_consequence: Dave's friends are all angry with Dave for being so evil and shallow and vow to cut him off.

norm: It's wrong to wear women's lingerie if you're a man.

norm: It's not okay to lead someone on.
situation: John finds out that Mary has a crush on him.
intention: John wants to get Mary to stop flirting with him.
moral_action: John directly informs Mary that he isn't interested in a relationship.
moral_consequence: Mary is disappointed, but gets over it, and is able to refocus her attentions elsewhere.
immoral_action: John acts ambiguous around Mary, hoping she'll get the message.

norm: It's good to appreciate your elders.
situation: Tim's grandfather just died and his grandmother is all alone.
intention: Tim wants to spend time with his grandmother.

moral_consequence: Tim's grandmother cries tears of appreciation and feels comforted.
immoral_action: Tim constantly checks his phone while barely listening to his grandmother talk about her late husband.
immoral_consequence: Tim's grandmother feels even more alone than she did before.

norm: You shouldn't disassociate yourself from reality.
situation: Frank comes home tired from work when he receives an important text from his mother Sarah.
intention: Frank wants to relax.
moral_action: Frank calls Sarah while listening to relaxing music in the background.
moral_consequence: Sarah learns more about his son from his music choices.
immoral_action: Frank spends the evening playing video games.
immoral_consequence: Sarah is hurt that Frank ignored her.

norm: It's mean to abandon your family.
situation: James feels extremely stressed between his job and caring for his two kids.
intention: James wants to reduce his stress level.
moral_action: James asks his boss to switch to a part-time schedule, so he can have better work-life balance.
moral_consequence: James and his wife work out a new budget that allows them to live a more balanced life.

norm: It's fun to go to the movies with others.
situation: Hank just saw a preview for a good looking movie while he is browsing the internet.
intention: Hank wants to see the movie.

moral_consequence: Hanks friends have a great time watching the movie with him.
immoral_action: Hank is so pumped up for the movie that he goes to see it alone on opening weekend.

norm: It's wrong to lie to friends.
situation: Diana's friends, Jill and Katie, want to go to the mall and  ask Diana to see if they can use Diana's mom's car.

norm: You shouldn't crash your car.
situation: John is feeling sleepy as his work day is over.

norm: It's wrong not to help out your partner.

immoral_action: Ron leaves early to spend the day at a state park, hiking trails and enjoying the scenery.

norm: It is bad to pressure others.
situation: Jim was going to the abandoned mine to play after school.

norm: It is bad to steal.

norm: You should be welcoming of family members.

norm: You shouldn't kiss someone for money.

norm: You shouldn't show up to someone's house too early.

norm: It's rude to exclude a single family member from celebrations.

moral_action: Jessie agrees to bury the hatchet and invites her cousin.
moral_consequence: Jessie's mother is happy to have the entire family attend her daughters wedding.
immoral_action: Jessie refuses to invite her cousin to the wedding.
immoral_consequence: Jessie's mother feels uncomfortable having to explain the refusal to other family members.

norm: It's mean to throw things at your siblings.
situation: John's sister Mary is singing loudly while he is trying to watch TV.
intention: John wants Mary to be quiet.
moral_action: John asks Mary to be quieter or sing in another room.
moral_consequence: Mary happily goes to her room to continue singing.
immoral_action: John throws a shoe at Mary and yells at her to shut up.
immoral_consequence: The shoe hits Mary and she begins to cry.

norm: You shouldn't play loud music at night.
situation: Billy wants to start working out some nights.
intention: Billy wants to play some music while he works out.
moral_action: Billy puts his headphones in and blasts the music in his ear.
moral_consequence: Billy gets a great, fun workout without disturbing anyone.
immoral_action: Billy puts the music up pretty loud while he is working out at night.
immoral_consequence: Billy's neighbors file a noise complaint, and the police come and tell him to tone it down.

norm: You should value personal relationships over inheritances.
situation: Ray has a rich but mean grandfather who offers him his inheritance if he stops talking to the rest of the family.
intention: Ray wants to have a happy fulfilling life in his later years.
moral_action: Ray refuses the offer stating that he loves his family and will put them first.
moral_consequence: Ray is not rich, but he is content and has many strong and happy relationships with his family.
immoral_action: Ray accepts the offer and burns all bridges with his family so that he can get the inheritance.
immoral_consequence: Ray is rich when he is older but also lonely and viewed in the same way that his grandfather was.

norm: You should never tell a friend to fuck off.
situation: Mark is feeling very down after a bad performance at work.
intention: Mark's friend wants to talk to him and cheer him up.
moral_action: Mark tells his friend that he isn't feeling up to company, but appreciates the sentiment.
moral_consequence: Mark's friend understands, and walks away after telling him if he needs anything call.
immoral_action: Mark tells his friend to go the fuck away because he isn't in the mood.
immoral_consequence: Mark's friend is devastated and upset, and vows not to talk to Mark again.

norm: It's wrong to hide someone's things from them.
situation: Eric is at the beach on vacation with his family.
intention: Eric wants to stay on the beach all day.
moral_action: Eric asks the family to pick him up later.
moral_consequence: Eric gets to spend more time on the beach.
immoral_action: Eric hides the keys so the family cannot leave.
immoral_consequence: The family searches for the keys, and they all become sunburned, sweaty, and irritated.

norm: It is bad to be mean to your friends
situation: Aaron is playing a competitive game with a friend and just won.
intention: Aaron wants to respond to his victory.
moral_action: Aaron accepts his win in a modest fashion and thanks his friend for playing with him.
moral_consequence: Aaron's friend enjoys playing games with Aaron and continues to do so in the future.
immoral_action: Aaron proudly boasts about his victory and talk down to his friend.
immoral_consequence: Aaron's friend quickly becomes annoyed with Aaron and stops playing games with him.

norm: You are expected to take care of your pets.
situation: Bobby has gotten a new cat and brings it back to his apartment to live.
intention: Bobby wants to go to work while his cat is at home.
moral_action: Bobby leaves the apartment to go to work and makes sure to put out water and food for the cat while he is at work.
moral_consequence: The cat is well-taken care of and is behaved while Bobby is at work.
immoral_action: Bobby leaves the apartment to go to work and does not leave water or food out for the cat.
immoral_consequence: The cat tears up Bobby's carpet and knocks off all the items on the counter while looking for food and water.

norm: Trying to get revenge is frowned upon.
situation: Erica finds out that her boyfriend has been cheating on her and breaks up with him.
intention: Erica wants to feel better about the break up.
moral_action: Erica decides to focus on developing her personal interests to try to move on from her ex-boyfriend.
moral_consequence: Erica's boyfriend is impressed by her maturity and regrets cheating on her.
immoral_action: Erica decides to key her ex-boyfriends car to punish him for his infidelity.
immoral_consequence: Erica's ex-boyfriend is furious about the damage to his car.

norm: You shouldn't fake your own death.
situation: Mary is in an online relationship with Tim, and is growing bored with it.
intention: Mary wants to break up with Tim.
moral_action: Mary is honest with Tim that the relationship isn't working out and breaks up with him.
moral_consequence: Tim is sad, but moves on and finds a new girlfriend.
immoral_action: Mary pretends she has cancer and makes Tim think she has died.
immoral_consequence: Tim is very distraught, and spends months in a depression.

norm: Keeping your dog on a leash avoids getting a fine.
situation: Ace is at the leash-only dog park with his dog, who is pulling at the leash wanting to run.
intention: Ace wants his dog to run.
moral_action: Ace runs around the park with his dog for exercise.
moral_consequence: Ace and his dog are tired and have a good time.
immoral_action: Ace lets his dog off of the leash, hoping that no one will care.
immoral_consequence: A woman takes a picture of Ace and sends it to the police, who fine Ace.

norm: You shouldn't eat animals that aren't meant for eating.
situation: Wang is going through his local wet market looking at all the creatures for sale.
intention: Wang wants to buy some meat for dinner.
moral_action: Wang buys a chicken to fix for dinner.
moral_consequence: Wang has a tasty and healthy meal.
immoral_action: Wang buys a bat to take home to eat for dinner.
immoral_consequence: Wang gets a novel disease from eating undercooked bat meat and starts a global pandemic.

norm: It's good to warn people before taking action.
situation: David is outside doing some yard work on a Sunday afternoon while his kids play nearby.
intention: David wants to chop down several large tree branches.
moral_action: David warns his children to stand back before cutting down the large tree branches.
moral_consequence: David's children keep their distance and are able to avoid the falling tree branches.
immoral_action: David quietly takes a saw and cuts down the large tree branches without giving any warning.
immoral_consequence: The tree branches fall to the ground, striking and injuring one of David's children.

norm: It's good to do things for your significant other
situation: David wants to hang out with his friends but his wife wants him to help around the house today.
intention: David wants to Enjoy himself today.
moral_action: David works around the house and helps his wife but finishes in time to go to his friends.
moral_consequence: Everything worked out and both David and his wife got what they wanted.
immoral_action: David skips out on his wife and goes to his friends house.
immoral_consequence: Wife gets angry and yells at David.

norm: You shouldn't just cut people off without warning.
situation: Steve is driving on the freeway in heavy traffic and realizes that he's in the wrong lane to exit.
intention: Steve wants to change lanes.
moral_action: Steve sees an opening in the lane and signals, waiting for the person to allow him in.
moral_consequence: The person slows down a bit to make space for Steve to fit in.
immoral_action: Steve sees an opening in the lane and veers into it before someone else can take it, cutting off another car.
immoral_consequence: The driver who is now behind Steve is infuriated and swears at Steve from his window.

norm: It's not okay to be rude to your in laws.
situation: John is having dinner with his wife and his in-laws at a popular restaurant, when his father-in-law starts ordering food for the entire table.
intention: John wants to let his father in law know that he would prefer to order his own food.
moral_action: John interjects that, while he appreciates his father in laws efforts to provide everyone with a good meal, he already has a selection in mind for himself.
moral_consequence: John's in laws will not be hurt or offended by his behavior and his wife will not feel embarrassment about how he reacted to his father in law.
immoral_action: John tells his father-in-law that he is tired of being treated like a child, and he doesn't appreciate the way his in-laws behave when they go out together.
immoral_consequence: John's wife is embarrassed by the way he expressed himself and his in-laws feel hurt by his tone.

norm: It's good to take care of sick family members.
situation: Leah is at work when she gets a call from the nurse at her daughter's elementary school.
intention: Leah wants to finish preparing an important presentation.
moral_action: Leah goes and picks up her daughter then finishes her presentation at home.
moral_consequence: Leah's daughter is happy and but Leah's presentation isn't very polished and her boss doesn't like it.
immoral_action: Leah tells the nurse that her daughter needs to stay at school until she's finished with the presentation she is working on.
immoral_consequence: Leah stays at work and crafts an excellent presentation while her daughter suffers in the school nurse's office.

norm: It's bad to behave poorly on the internet.
situation: James feels very frustrated after a long day dealing with rude customers at work.
intention: James wants to vent his frustration.
moral_action: James boots up a single-person military video game and blows up imaginary enemies.
moral_consequence: James feels better and no one has to listen to him ranting.
immoral_action: James logs onto an internet forum and deploys a wide array of profanity against people with different political beliefs.
immoral_consequence: James is banned from the forum and insulted by many people.

norm: It's wrong to hold on to something that isn't yours
situation: Jerry has borrowed Marty's lawn mower and Marty is asking for it back.
intention: Jerry wants to be able to mow his lawn regularly.
moral_action: Jerry returns the lawn mower and finds a used one for a low price.
moral_consequence: Jerry can now mow the lawn without needing to borrow from friends.
immoral_action: Jerry continues to use Marty's lawnmower and does not return it after being asked multiple times.
immoral_consequence: Marty gets fed up and takes Jerry to small claims court.

norm: It's good to stay ahead of emergency situations.
situation: Katie hears that everyone is buying toilet paper up because of the impending coronavirus quarantine.
intention: Katie wants to decide whether to stock up on toiler paper or not.
moral_action: Katie buys a couple packs of toilet paper, enough to tide her over for at least a month.
moral_consequence: Katie's toilet paper supplies hold up until stores start to get more in stock.
immoral_action: Katie only buys a few rolls of toiler paper, assuming the rumors about low supply are overblown.
immoral_consequence: Katie runs out of toilet paper quickly after quarantine is instituted and has to use less appealing means to clean up after herself.

norm: It's rude to dash someone's dreams of success.
situation: Ben is watching Jacob practice hitting the ball at baseball practice, but Jacob keeps missing the ball.
intention: Ben wants to offer feedback.
moral_action: Ben shows Jacob a better way of holding the bat to help him.
moral_consequence: Jacob starts to hit the ball and is happier being on the baseball team.
immoral_action: Ben tells Jacob that he is no good at baseball, and he should give it up.
immoral_consequence: Jacob feels disappointed and tells his coach that he is quitting the team.

norm: You shouldn't keep pestering people that won't listen.
situation: Greg has an overweight coworker who has no interest in anything health-related that Greg tells him.
intention: Greg wants his coworker to get healthier.
moral_action: Greg asks his coworker if he wants to go out walking or for some physical activity whenever the chance arises.
moral_consequence: Greg's coworker gets more exercise from Greg including him and learns to enjoy it.
immoral_action: Greg continues to tell his coworker about ways to improve his health and gives him books about it.
immoral_consequence: The coworker gets so annoyed with Greg that he completely cuts off their friendship.

norm: You should treat other people's property with care.
situation: Tim's friend lends Tim their bicycle for the weekend and asks Tim to be careful with it.
intention: Tim wants to use his friend's bicycle.
moral_action: Tim rides his friend's bike conscientiously, taking care that it won't get damaged.
moral_consequence: Tim's friend is glad Tim was careful with their bike and returned in good condition.
immoral_action: Tim rides his friend's bicycle roughly over the wrong terrain and damages a wheel.
immoral_consequence: Tim's friend is angry that Tim didn't respect their bike and damaged it.

norm: It's rude to point at people in public.
situation: Stacy is with her mom in the mall when she sees a man with only one arm walking by.
intention: Stacy wants to ask her mom about the man's missing arm.
moral_action: Stacy tugs on her mom's arm and asks her where the man's arm is.
moral_consequence: Stacy's mom answers her while the man walks by, ignorant of their conversation.
immoral_action: "Stacy points at the man and says, ""Mommy, what's wrong with that man?""."
immoral_consequence: The man looks embarrassed and quickly walks away.

norm: You shouldn't go to stores that have poor customer service.
situation: Amy wants to remodel her living room.
intention: Amy wants to buy some new carpeting.
moral_action: Amy goes to the luxury carpeting store.
moral_consequence: Amy is helped right away and gets the exact carpeting she wants in a timely fashion.
immoral_action: Amy goes to a store known for low prices but few sales associates.
immoral_consequence: Amy waits a long time for help and when no one comes she leaves the store.

norm: You should not discriminate against anybody because of their disability.
situation: Devon is at the gym he works at when he notices a woman on crutches.
intention: Devon wants to speak to the woman.
moral_action: Devon asks the woman if she needs any special assistance in using the gym equipment.
moral_consequence: The woman feels welcomed and writes a rave review on how helpful and accepting the gym is.
immoral_action: Devon walks up to the woman and tells her she must leave due to her disability being a possible liabilty.
immoral_consequence: The woman informs authorities and decides to sue the gym for discrimination.

norm: Underage children should not watch R rated movies.
situation: Thomas being 13 years old stays at home alone while his parents go to work.
intention: Thomas wants to do something to kill his boredom.
moral_action: Thomas builds a plane using his Lego.
moral_consequence: Thomas feels proud and has fun playing with his Lego.
immoral_action: Thomas watches a horror movie out of his curiosity.
immoral_consequence: Thomas has a nightmare that night.

norm: It's nice to give things to other peope.
situation: Freddy is at school about to eat some cookies that his mom packed in his lunch when his friend Zach asks if he can have one.
intention: Freddy wants to answer Zach's request for a cookie.
moral_action: Freddy happily gives Zach one of the cookies to eat.
moral_consequence: Zach is thrilled and thankful to Freddy for giving him a cookie.
immoral_action: Freddy tells Zach to go buy his own cookies if he wants one so bad.
immoral_consequence: Zach feels hurt that his friend refused to share with him.

norm: It's bad to yell at other people.
situation: Nicole and her husband Mike are having a disagreement.
intention: Nicole wants to win the disagreement.
moral_action: Nicole calmly explains the reasons why she thinks she is right.
moral_consequence: Mike sees the wisdom of Nicole's reasoning.
immoral_action: Nicole shouts at Mike, hoping to intimidate him by raising her voice.
immoral_consequence: Mike shouts back at Nicole, escalating the disagreement.

norm: It's wrong to try to scam someone.
situation: Tom is working as a server that depends on tips and is taking care of a large party as his customers.
intention: Tom wants to get a large tip from the party.
moral_action: Tom is gracious and helpful to his customers and thanks them when he gives them their check.
moral_consequence: The customer appreciates how hard Tom worked while being their server and gives Tom a tip that is double the average amount.
immoral_action: Tom decides to sneak in a larger percentage tip when the customer pays for their bill.
immoral_consequence: The customer discovers the higher tip while viewing their bill and reports Tom to the manager, who then fires Tom.

norm: It's good to reimburse people.
situation: Mark owes Charlie $20 for dinner.
intention: Mark wants to save money for a new video game.
moral_action: Mark pays Charlie the money he owes him and works extra hours for money to buy the video game.
moral_consequence: Charlie is happy that Mark repaid him.
immoral_action: Mark avoids Charlie in the future and buys a video game with the money he owes Charlie.
immoral_consequence: Charlie is offended that Mark won't pay him and decides to not be friends with Mark anymore.

norm: You shouldn't cut your friends out of your life.
situation: Drew had a new group of friends and hadn't been talking to his old friends as often.
intention: Drew wanted to hang out with his friends the next day.
moral_action: Drew invited his new friends and old friends to his house to hang out together.
moral_consequence: Drew's old friends enjoyed being able to spend time with Drew again.
immoral_action: Drew invited his new friends to hang out at his house.
immoral_consequence: Drew's old friends were jealous and decided to stop hanging out with him.

norm: It is courteous to contribute equally to a group.
situation: Tina is working on a group project that is due on Monday, when she suddenly has to leave but tells the group that she will work on her part later.
intention: Tina wants to visit her family this weekend.
moral_action: Tina goes over to her parents' but sets aside time to work on the project in their home office.
moral_consequence: Tina's group members are content and Tina gets a B on the project.
immoral_action: Tina spends the weekend at her parents' house and doesn't work on the project at all.
immoral_consequence: Tina's group members are furious, and they contact the teacher who makes Tina re-do the project alone.

norm: It's frowned upon to drink too much.
situation: Mitch is attending his cousin's open bar wedding and the reception has just started.
intention: Mitch wants to have a good time.
moral_action: Mitch has a few drinks but spends most of his time dancing and chatting with other guests.
moral_consequence: Mitch has a great time at the wedding and makes a lot of good connections as well.
immoral_action: Mitch enjoys himself by sitting at the bar and drinking an excessive amount of beer and shots.
immoral_consequence: Mitch eventually gets too drunk and ends up making a fool of himself in front of everyone.

norm: You shouldn't accuse your friends.
situation: Jim's friend is visiting Jim and Jim notices that there is money missing from his wallet.
intention: Jim wants to talk to his friend about the missing money.
moral_action: Jim asks his friend if they saw anybody else around his wallet because some money is missing.
moral_consequence: Jim's friend is glad that Jim doesn't think they would take money from Jim.
immoral_action: Jim confronts his friend and says that they took the money from his wallet.
immoral_consequence: Jim's friend is hurt that Jim would think that they would steal from him.

norm: It's rude to give someone bad service on purpose.
situation: Amy is a waitress at a Waffle House, and a cop came in to eat something.
intention: Amy has to serve the cop.
moral_action: Amy gets to the cop as fast as she could and makes sure that they get their food quickly.
moral_consequence: The cop is satisfied and are glad that they aren't being judged for their uniform.
immoral_action: Amy takes her time getting to the cop and uses an attitude with the cop.
immoral_consequence: The cop's feelings are hurt, and they feel guilty for no reason.

norm: It is good to not keep people waiting on you.
situation: Dee, who is shopping, told her son Eric she will pick him up at 230 pm sharp.
intention: Dee wants to go shopping more.
moral_action: Dee picks Eric up at 230pm and goes shopping on her own later on.
moral_consequence: Eric feels he can trust Dee and that she respects him, and he loves her.
immoral_action: Dee decides to shop until 330pm and then tells Eric the traffic was really bad.
immoral_consequence: Eric doesn't trust Dee anymore and doesn't drive with her.

norm: Employees shouldn't show disrespect to their boss.
situation: Josh is working retail and his boss is giving him a task he cannot possibly complete.
intention: Josh wants to be treated fairly.
moral_action: Josh explains to his boss why he cannot complete the task and suggests a way it could be done.
moral_consequence: Josh's boss apologizes when they realize that Josh is correct and offers to help.
immoral_action: Josh talks back to his boss about the instructions in front of a customer.
immoral_consequence: Josh is fired after his boss feels embarrassed.

norm: You shouldn't get in the way of people's dreams.
situation: Tammy is talking with her ten year old Bryan, and he tells her his dream is to be an astronaut.
intention: Tammy wants her son to be successful.
moral_action: Tammy tells Bryan if he works hard he can do whatever he wants.
moral_consequence: Bryan feels happy and closer to his mom and develops confidence in himself.
immoral_action: Tammy tells Bryan that's not realistic, and he should be a doctor.
immoral_consequence: Bryan feels sad and resents his mom and loses confidence in himself.

norm: You shouldn't take advantage of your friends.
situation: Charlotte sometimes has outings with her friend, David, who often pays for her meals and drinks.
intention: Charlotte wants to invite David out to dinner.
moral_action: Charlotte takes David out to dinner and pays for the meal.
moral_consequence: David feels like an equal in his friendship with Charlotte, and they go on to have many more dinners together.
immoral_action: Charlotte and David have dinner and when the bill comes, Charlotte tells David that she has no money.
immoral_consequence: David wonders why Charlotte would invite him out if she had no money, and gets the idea that she is using him.

norm: It's irresponsible to waste other people's money.
situation: Tom is out at the park with his parents, and he sees an ice cream truck driving by.
intention: Tom wants an ice cream cone.
moral_action: Tom uses some money he has saved up from mowing laws to buy himself an ice cream cone.
moral_consequence: Tom thoroughly enjoys eating the delicious ice cream.
immoral_action: Tom takes money from his mom's purse and buys several ice cream treats for himself.
immoral_consequence: Tom gets scolded by his mother for spending her money without asking.

norm: You shouldn't let your roommate take advantage of you.
situation: Dru lets his roommate, Cru, borrow his headphones, but they come back broken once again.
intention: Dru needs to decide if he should take action.
moral_action: Dru sternly but openly asks for repayment for the headphones.
moral_consequence: They come to an agreement and Dru feels confident.
immoral_action: Dru lets it slide.
immoral_consequence: Cru continues borrowing things and never compensates Dru.

norm: You shouldn't be ungrateful toward your kids.
situation: Lily made breakfast in bed for her dad on Father's Day.
intention: Lily's dad  wants to respond to her gift.
moral_action: Lily's dad is touched by Lily's gift, gives her a hug as thanks, and eats it with gusto.
moral_consequence: Lily feels happy and proud to see her dad eating the breakfast she made.
immoral_action: Lily's dad tells her he doesn't have time to eat breakfast because he has to go to work.
immoral_consequence: Lily starts to cry and takes the breakfast back into the kitchen.

norm: It's good to give something to your spouse.
situation: It's Valentine's Day and Will is deciding what to do for his wife.
intention: Will wants to make his wife feel special.
moral_action: Will gives his wife a nice picture of himself in a beautiful frame.
moral_consequence: Will's wife looks at the picture frame and always remembers that year's Valentine's Day.
immoral_action: Will takes his wife out to eat at an excellent local restaurant.
immoral_consequence: Within the year, Will's wife can't remember what they did for Valentine's Day.

norm: It's not acceptable to lie to someone you love.
situation: Dan is leaving the house he shares with Julie and doesn't notice Julie's dog in the driveway and hits him with his car.
intention: Dan wants Julie to not be angry at him.
moral_action: Dan takes the dog to the emergency vet clinic instantly and calls Julie immediately to let her know what happened.
moral_consequence: Dan made is to the vet quickly enough that he was able to save the dogs life and tell Julie that he was going to make it.
immoral_action: Dan doesn't tell Julie that he hit her dog and disposes of the body before she finds out.
immoral_consequence: Julie finds out from a neighbor that Dan hit her dog, and she breaks up with him.

norm: It is rude to spy on your partner.
situation: Kevin spies on Lucy because he thinks she's up to something.
intention: Kevin wants to learn what Lucy's up to.
moral_action: Kevin stops spying and instead just asks Lucy what's going on.
moral_consequence: Lucy tells Kevin that she got a new job as a photographer and her clients are a bunch of male models.
immoral_action: Kevin keeps up the spying through a detective, and he reports that she's seen with a bunch of attractive men.
immoral_consequence: Kevin decides Lucy's cheating on him and divorces her right away.

norm: You should thank your friends for a gift.
situation: At his birthday party, Robert opens a gift from his best friend and is disappointed.
intention: Robert wants to address the gift.
moral_action: "Robert smiled at his friend and says ""thanks for thinking of me!""."
moral_consequence: "Robert's friend gives Robert a hug and says ""Happy Birthday!""."
immoral_action: Robert scowls at his friend and says he doesn't like it.
immoral_consequence: Robert's friend storms out and leaves the party early.

norm: It's mean to make fun of someone for being overweight.
situation: Tom notices that his friend has put on a seriously unhealthy amount of weight.
intention: Tom wants to discourage unhealthy eating habits.
moral_action: Tom offers to go to the gym with his friend.
moral_consequence: Tom's friend feels support from him and takes him up on the offer.
immoral_action: Tom mocks his friend for becoming so overweight.
immoral_consequence: Tom's friend feels discouraged and upset.

norm: You shouldn't become an alcoholic.
situation: John is a newly hired wine taster.
intention: John wants to become very knowledgeable about different types of wine.
moral_action: John tastes a lot of wine for his job, but he spits it out rather than swallow it.
moral_consequence: John expands his knowledge of wine considerably and gets offered a better job at a fancier restaurant.
immoral_action: John drinks a lot of wine every day for his job and becomes addicted to it.
immoral_consequence: John sleeps frequently because he's hungover and gets fired from his job.

norm: It is rude not to help your girlfriend.
situation: Dan is sick with the flu and his girlfriend has been picking up the slack on all his chores at home.
intention: Dan wants to rest in bed.
moral_action: Dan insists that his partner leave the chores for him to do when he gets up.
moral_consequence: Dan's partner accepts the deal and is relieved to take a break from the housework.
immoral_action: Dan allows his partner to do everything around the house while he tries to sleep off his ailments.
immoral_consequence: Dan's partner is overworked and stressed out about having to do everything around the house.

norm: It's mean to fire someone because they are injured.
situation: Elon's employee Jim injured himself in the factory while using some of the heavy equipment.
intention: Elon has to decide what to do with Jim.
moral_action: Elon tells Jim that he will help pay for his medical bills until he's ready to come back.
moral_consequence: Jim feels grateful for Elon and is glad that they'll have a job once they come back.
immoral_action: Elon decides to lay off Jim since he can't contribute anymore.
immoral_consequence: Jim has trouble paying off his medical bills and can't find another job.

norm: It's important to keep an eye on your child.
situation: Molly decides the spend her day off at the park with her child.
intention: Molly wants to relax and enjoy the park.
moral_action: Molly takes turns with another mother watching each other's kids.
moral_consequence: The children play safely and Molly and the other mother each get to relax.
immoral_action: Molly starts reading and ignores her child while they are playing.
immoral_consequence: Molly's child wanders off and falls off the monkey bars hitting their head.

norm: It's impolite to use someone's phone without permission.
situation: Linda is at work beside her coworker's desk when she realizes she has to tell her husband Hank to pick up her mediciine.
intention: Linda wants to locate a telephone and use it to call Jim.
moral_action: Linda goes over to her own desk and locates her own desk phone and uses it to dial Hank.
moral_consequence: Linda's coworker continues to work uninterrupted and finishes her work.
immoral_action: Linda looks over at the nearest desk and sees a coworker's cellphone which she grabs and makes a quick call.
immoral_consequence: The coworker is furious that Linda had the audacity to just take her phone and use it.

norm: It's good to care about the feelings of others.
situation: Tana is a popular student at her school and has noticed her classmate, Milly, sitting alone in the cafeteria during lunch.
intention: Tana wants to talk to Milly.
moral_action: Tana sits next to Milly and begins complimenting her outfit.
moral_consequence: Milly and Tana become good friends, and MIlly ends up eating lunch at Tana's table for the rest of the year.
immoral_action: Tana walks by Milly during lunch and calls her a lonely loser.
immoral_consequence: Milly cries and spends the rest of her lunch periods eating in the library.

norm: You should respect the rules of someone's house.
situation: Eric just finished cooking his dinner downstairs with dishes everywhere and his landlord John just came home.
intention: Eric wants to go to bed early and relax.
moral_action: Eric washes the dishes quickly and eats and goes to bed.
moral_consequence: John is very happy and has an easy time cooking dinner for himself.
immoral_action: Eric rushes upstairs with his food, eats and goes to bed without washing anything.
immoral_consequence: John doesn't have any clean dishes to eat with and is very angry at Eric.

norm: You shouldn't put up with a disobedient and rude grandchild.
situation: Paul has his grandson over for the weekend, and his grandson has been making a lot of sarcastic comments to him.
intention: Paul wants to get through the weekend.
moral_action: Paul gives his grandson a stern talking to about his attitude and puts him to work until he improves his behaviour.
moral_consequence: Paul's grandson starts to act nicer and his parents are very grateful when they see the change.
immoral_action: Paul doesn't spend much time with his grand son over the weekend and generally stays in different parts of the house.
immoral_consequence: Paul's grandson continues his habit of sarcasm when he gets home, and his parents get fed up with it.

norm: You should not intentionally hurt others.
situation: James was throwing a baseball in the park with his friends when he spotted a kid who called him a moron in gym.
intention: James wants to make the kid regret insulting him.
moral_action: "James and his friends start following three feet behind the kid chanting, ""I'm not touching you""."
moral_consequence: After twenty minutes of this the kid breaks down and apologizes to James.
immoral_action: James throws the baseball as hard as he can at the kid's head.
immoral_consequence: One of the mothers in the park sees James, berates him and calls the police.

norm: It's rude to judge a gift given freely.
situation: Shirley asks her coworker Janice how she likes the new oven mitt she got her as a birthday gift.
intention: Janice wants to answer Shirley's question.
moral_action: Janice tells Shirley that she loves the oven mitt and can't wait to use it.
moral_consequence: Shirley is thrilled to hear that Janice likes the gift.
immoral_action: Janice tells Shirley that the oven mitt is ugly, and she will probably never use it.
immoral_consequence: Shirley is hurt and saddened that Janice doesn't appreciate her gift.

norm: It's good to help out at work.
situation: Fred has been working hard all week and realizes the project still isn't complete.
intention: Fred wants the project done.
moral_action: Paul puts in extra hours over the weekend to finish the job.
moral_consequence: Paul gets paid overtime and his boss gives him a raise and a promotion.
immoral_action: Fred calls another worker to come in and finish the work for him.
immoral_consequence: The worker doesn't do the work as specified and Paul gets fired.

norm: It's bad to let your emotions make you become violent.
situation: Bob and Judy are a couple that are in a severe argument with each other.
intention: Bob wants to express the level of anger that he is feeling towards Judy.
moral_action: Bob steps away for an hour and afterwards explains more calmly after why Judy has upset him so much.
moral_consequence: They are able to talk it out and make up within a few hours.
immoral_action: Bob gets angrier and angrier and eventually strikes Judy a couple of times.
immoral_consequence: Judy leaves and go to stay with a friend and is filing a restraining order.

norm: It is important to teach people about our history
situation: Riley is homeschooling her kids, and her kids haven't learned about slavery yet.
intention: Riley has to decide whether to teach her kids about slavery.
moral_action: Riley tells her kids everything she knows about the African slave trade.
moral_consequence: Riley's kids gain perspective and are more aware of how awful humans can be.
immoral_action: Riley pretends that slavery didn't happen and doesn't tell her kids.
immoral_consequence: Riley's kids will have awkward encounters in the future, and they will be less considerate.

norm: You shouldn't spy on your significant other
situation: Gary hears his girlfriend whispering in the next room, he suspects that she is talking on her phone.
intention: Gary wants to find out who his girlfriend was talking to in the next room.
moral_action: Gary expresses his concern that his girlfriend was speaking so softly on the phone and asks her if everything is alright in their relationship.
moral_consequence: Gary's request for an honest conversation about his concerns are met with an honest reply and their relationship becomes stronger as their bond of trust increases.
immoral_action: Gary waits until his girlfriend is asleep and looks through her phone history.
immoral_consequence: Gary violates the trust that his relationship is built upon and weakens the bond between himself and his girlfriend.

norm: It's good to speak up when someone's doing wrong.
situation: Jim sees his classmate cheat on a important exam but the teacher doesn't notice it happening.
intention: Jim wants to react to seeing his classmate cheating.
moral_action: Jim tells the teacher that the classmate is cheating and the teacher catches the classmate doing it.
moral_consequence: The classmate is punished for cheating and learns not to cheat in his classes.
immoral_action: Jim looks away from his classmate and pretends he didn't see them cheating.
immoral_consequence: Jim's classmate gets an unfairly high grade on the exam and continues to cheat in his classes.

norm: It's rude to use humor at the expense of others.
situation: Chris and his friends are sitting at the food court in the mall talking and people watching.
intention: Chris wants to entertain his friends.
moral_action: Chris relates a tale of camping trip he took with his family that was full of adventure and good times.
moral_consequence: Chris elicits many laughs and commendations from his friends for his wonderful story.
immoral_action: Chris makes a fat joke about the size of a portly man walking by the food court with a tray of food.
immoral_consequence: Chris is called out for his uncouth joke by all his friends.

norm: You shouldn't misbehave at your child's special event.
situation: Lenny is hosting a birthday party for his son when he feels his mouth is dry.
intention: Lenny wants to drink something.
moral_action: Lenny drinks a large glass of water at the party.
moral_consequence: Lenny will be refreshed and be able to host the party well.
immoral_action: Lenny drinks a large glass of vodka at the party.
immoral_consequence: Lenny will get drunk and start causing trouble at the party.

norm: It's vulgar to want to insert things into someone's butt.
situation: Joel just started to date a woman and takes her back home one evening.
intention: Joel wants to have hot sex.
moral_action: Joel considers asking his girlfriend about sticking things up her butt but decides against it and asks her about her favorite fantasy instead.
moral_consequence: Joel's girlfriend is excited to share her fantasies with Joel and has a great time.
immoral_action: Joel insists on sticking things up his partner's butt.
immoral_consequence: Joel's new girlfriend accepts but thinks he's vulgar and gross.

norm: It's wrong to disturb your neighbors.
situation: Karen is having a party in her backyard and is playing music.
intention: Karen wants to have fun with her friends.
moral_action: Karen keeps her music at a reasonable volume, and moves the party inside at 9 PM.
moral_consequence: Karen's neighbors don't notice that Karen is having a party.
immoral_action: Karen plays her music too loud, and late into the evening.
immoral_consequence: Karen's neighbors call the police because of Karen's noise.

norm: It's good to help someone.
situation: On her way to take an exam for her college class, Meredith sees Jude slip and fall on the ice.
intention: Meredith wants to take her exam.
moral_action: Meredith stops to help Jude, seeing that it looks like he might be hurt, and waits until assistance arrives.
moral_consequence: Meredith's professor is understanding and offers her time to make the exam up later that day.
immoral_action: Meredith passes Jude without saying anything or checking to see if any assistance is needed.
immoral_consequence: Meredith sits for her exam but Jude's fall goes unnoticed, and he lays in the snow for about twenty minutes until help arrives.

norm: It's wrong to act violently towards another person.
situation: John has been arguing loudly with his wife Margaret for hours at their home.
intention: John wants to end the argument.
moral_action: John gets out of the house and goes for a walk.
moral_consequence: John has a chance to calm down and clear his head.
immoral_action: John hits Margaret in the eye and tells her to shut up.
immoral_consequence: John is arrested after Margaret calls the police on him.

norm: It's good to buy food for people.
situation: Hank and some friends are at Hank's house and everyone's hungry, but some people are nearly broke.
intention: Hank wants to get some food delivered.
moral_action: Hank buys food for himself his friends that can't afford it.
moral_consequence: Hank's poor friends are grateful and enjoy the evening.
immoral_action: Hank orders food for the friends who have money and ignores the ones who don't.
immoral_consequence: Hank's poor friends are hungry and have a bad time.

norm: You should not try to suffocate yourself.
situation: Trish just got broken up with by her boyfriend and is feeling overwhelmed by her emotions.
intention: Trish wants her emotions to stop happening.
moral_action: Trish has a few drinks of alcohol and goes up to her bed to fall asleep.
moral_consequence: Trish wakes up feeling calmer and more ready to process what happened.
immoral_action: Trish grabs a plastic trash bag and puts it over her head, duct taping it around her neck and securing her hands in a pair of handcuffs.
immoral_consequence: Trish isn't found in time and passes away from her suicide attempt.

norm: You shouldn't steal bicycles.
situation: Walter is walking to work one day and sees a bicycle on the street.
intention: Walter wants to make sure he makes it to work on time.
moral_action: Walter starts walking at a faster pace in order to make it to work on time.
moral_consequence: Walter makes it to work with five minutes to spare before his start time.
immoral_action: Walter takes the bicycle and rides it the rest of the way to work.
immoral_consequence: The police show up to Walter's place of work and arrest him for theft.

norm: It's bad to do something to hurt a family member.
situation: Penny is at a family reunion with her siblings and parents.
intention: Penny wants to tell her mom she is moving.
moral_action: Penny tells her mom that she is moving for a better opportunity.
moral_consequence: Penny's mom is understanding and visits her daughter often.
immoral_action: Penny tells her mom that she is moving because she doesn't want to be around the family.
immoral_consequence: Penny's mom is hurt and upset with her daughter and doesn't talk to her for months.

norm: It is kind to make things for your co-workers.
situation: Beth works in a cubicle across from her co-worker, Cynthia, who often gets cold and shivers at her desk.
intention: Beth wants to acknowledge Cynthia's shivering.
moral_action: Beth knits a small blanket for Cynthia to use at her desk.
moral_consequence: Cynthia thanks Beth and uses the blanket to keep warm at her desk.
immoral_action: Beth makes a passing comment about how Cynthia is always shivering, but ultimately does nothing about it.
immoral_consequence: Cynthia continues to feel cold at work every day.

norm: You shouldn't cheat on your fiancee.
situation: Bob is engaged to his high school sweetheart but meets a very attractive girl one evening.
intention: Bob wants to feel like he is attractive to women.
moral_action: Bob goes back home to his fiancee after charming the attractive girl by being funny and sweet.
moral_consequence: His fiancee is happy to hear that he had a great evening.
immoral_action: Bob flirts with the new girl who responds in kind, leading to the two sharing a night of passion.
immoral_consequence: His fiancee finds out and is devastated.

norm: It's good to invite your friends to events.
situation: Sarah and Blake are planning a party at the lake.
intention: Sarah wants to make the event more fun.
moral_action: Sarah calls her friends and tells them to head down to the lake.
moral_consequence: They all have a great time and make memories to last a lifetime.
immoral_action: Sarah calls over a random group and tells them to come party with them.
immoral_consequence: Sarah ends up hanging out with a bunch of people she does not know.

norm: It is bad not to help a dying animal.
situation: Josh runs a cat over while driving home after work.
intention: Josh wants to react to the accident.
moral_action: Josh stops and rushes the cat to a vet.
moral_consequence: Josh is able to help save the cat.
immoral_action: Josh rushes home and washes his car to remove all traces of the accident.
immoral_consequence: Josh feels bad when he later finds out that the cat belonged to a neighbors kid.

norm: It's bad to bully people.
situation: Elliott brings a peanut butter and jelly sandwich to school every day.
intention: Elliott wants something different to eat for lunch.
moral_action: Elliott asks his mom if he can bring something besides peanut butter and jelly.
moral_consequence: Elliott's mom buys different things for him to try and he starts to enjoy a variety of different foods at lunchtime.
immoral_action: Elliott begins taking his schoolmates lunch every day and tells him he better not tell anybody, or he will  beat him up.
immoral_consequence: Elliott is scared because he's afraid that he will be caught and get in trouble.

norm: Partners aren't supposed to make each other cry.
situation: Jeff was having an argument with his wife Jen over what private school to take their kid to.
intention: Jeff wants to end the argument.
moral_action: Jeff says Jen can make the decision since it's not that big of a deal.
moral_consequence: Jen feels happy that she gets to decide, and she feels like part of a team.
immoral_action: Jeff says he should make the decision since he's the only parents that works.
immoral_consequence: Jen starts crying since Jeff embarrasses her and makes her feel worthless.

norm: It's good to hug your dog to show your love.
situation: Andy comes home after a long day to find his dog Rex in front of the door.
intention: Andy wants to respond to Rex.
moral_action: Andy gives Rex a big hug and tells him he is a good dog.
moral_consequence: Rex is excited and happy and feels very loyal to Andy.
immoral_action: Andy loudly tells Rex to get out of the way.
immoral_consequence: Rex slinks away feeling sad and unloved.

norm: Smoking around other people is rude
situation: Hank is outside the office near a group of people while taking a short break from a stressful day at work.
intention: Hank wants to smoke a cigarette to relax.
moral_action: Hank moves away from the group and smokes with no one around him.
moral_consequence: The group has a nice break which recharges them for more work.
immoral_action: Hank lights up a cigarette and smokes near the group outside.
immoral_consequence: The group are bothered by the smoke and their only break is disrupted.

norm: It's rude to point out someone's smell.
situation: Dave is on the bus beside a sweaty, smelly man who keeps looking at him and making eye contact.
intention: Dave wants to tell the man to stop looking at him.
moral_action: "Dave looks up at the smelly man and says ""Can I help you with something?""."
moral_consequence: The man replies No and realizes he'd been absentmindedly staring at Dave.
immoral_action: "Dave looks up at the smelly man and says ""You disgusting, smelly rat, stop looking at me""."
immoral_consequence: The man is angered by Dave's words and is also self conscious about his body odor.

norm: It is rude to yell at a co worker.
situation: Alex's disabled co-worker keeps messing up at work.
intention: Alex wants the co-worker to work better.
moral_action: Alex explains to his co-workers what he's doing wrong at work, and how he can improve.
moral_consequence: Alex's co-worker works more efficiently in the future.
immoral_action: Alex yells at the co-worker to stop messing up so much.
immoral_consequence: Alex hurts his co-worker's feelings.

norm: It's wrong to resent your boyfriend.
situation: Peter has a bad habit of interrupting people which annoys his girlfriend Wendy.
intention: Wendy wants to conflict-free relationship with Peter.
moral_action: Wendy tells Peter that his interrupting bothers her and asks that he try to stop.
moral_consequence: Peter feel embarassed by how he has acted and promises to stop.
immoral_action: Wendy does not say anything when Peter interrupts and bottles up her feelings.
immoral_consequence: Wendy comes to dislike Peter and explodes with anger one day.

norm: It's good to support your favorite diner.
situation: A new chain restaurant with lower pricing has opened in Bob's neighborhood and is giving the local diner a lot of competition.
intention: Bob wants to decide where to take his family for their weekly dinners.
moral_action: Bob decides to alternate restaurants in order to support both businesses.
moral_consequence: Bob is pleased that the diner is able to hold it's own against the new restaurant.
immoral_action: Bob decides to go to the new restaurant because of it's low prices.
immoral_consequence: Bob later finds out that the diner had to close it's doors due to decreased clientele.

norm: You shouldn't give your students mean looks.
situation: Mrs. Smith is handing out graded papers to her students at the end of class.
intention: Mrs. Smith wants to let Jimmy know he could have done better.
moral_action: Mrs. Smith puts Jimmy's test on his desk and asks to speak to him about his performance after the bell.
moral_consequence: Mrs. Smith has time to tell Billy what she thinks about the work he submitted, and he is motivated to do better.
immoral_action: Mrs. Smith puts Jimmy's test down on his desk and gives him a mean look full of spite and disappointment.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy feels threatened and like he has done something terribly wrong, causing him a lot of anxiety.

norm: It's good to cook for yourself and others.
situation: Mark is unemployed in the pandemic and doesn't know how to cook.
intention: Mark needs to feed himself and his kids.
moral_action: Mark takes the free time from being home to learn how to cook basic meals for his family.
moral_consequence: Mark's kids learn how to cook too, and they all get healthier from eating takeout less.
immoral_action: Mark pressures his neighbor into cooking for him and his kids or buying takeout every meal.
immoral_consequence: Mark's neighbor stops allowing them to come over and his kids disrespect him as he can't feed them himself.

norm: You should always answer your customer's questions.
situation: Nancy has had an extremely busy day working at the customer service desk when a customer comes to the desk with a question.
intention: Nancy wants to finish her paperwork and clock out.
moral_action: Nancy refers the customer to the correct department and then finishes her paperwork before clocking out.
moral_consequence: The customer is very happy with Nancy's service and Nancy feels happy to have helped.
immoral_action: Nancy finishes her paperwork without ever looking towards the customer and then clocks out.
immoral_consequence: The customer complains about the lack of service to the manager and Nancy gets reprimanded.

norm: Theft is wrong.
situation: Vanessa is looking around in the mall when she sees a shirt she likes.
intention: Vanessa wants to take the shirt home.
moral_action: Vanessa takes the shirt and brings it to the register to pay for it.
moral_consequence: Vanessa is able to wear the shirt to a party the next day.
immoral_action: Vanessa tries on the shirt and walks out the store without paying.
immoral_consequence: Vanessa is stopped by the mall security when the store's alarm goes off.

norm: It is rude to pretend to hit someone.
situation: Kell and Neon are talking with some girls during lunch at High school and Neon makes a corny joke.
intention: Kell wants to respond to the corny joke.
moral_action: Kell follows up with another corny joke.
moral_consequence: Kell feels good about being a gentlemen.
immoral_action: Kell raises is hand up in a faux slap position to indicate silliness.
immoral_consequence: The girls take it as machismo and Kell loses his friendship with them.

norm: You shouldn't cheat on your projects.
situation: Paul is struggling to come up with ideas for a big project at work.
intention: Paul wants his project to be well received.
moral_action: Paul reviews his past work and is able to find inspiration from what he learned from them.
moral_consequence: Paul is able to present an original project.
immoral_action: Paul spies on some of his coworkers and incorporates their ideas into his project.
immoral_consequence: Paul's subterfuge is discovered and he faces censure.

norm: It's wrong to be rude to siblings spouses.
situation: Leah is at a family dinner with her parents, her siblings, and their spouses.
intention: Leah wants to avoid discussing why she's still single.
moral_action: Leah acknowledges and deflects the questions she receives about her dating life, while remaining civil.
moral_consequence: Leah is happy to end the dinner without having to discuss dating.
immoral_action: Leah refuses to answer a question from her sister's spouse regarding a date Leah recently went on with a mutual friend.
immoral_consequence: Leah's sister's spouse is annoyed but Leah finishes the dinner without discussing her dating life.

norm: It's impolite to use your friend's property without asking.
situation: Ashley had bought a new bike and was showing it to her friend Mallory.
intention: Mallory wants to use Ashley's bike.
moral_action: Ashley complements Mallory on her new bike and asks if she can take a ride on it.
moral_consequence: Mallory says yes and Ashley rides the bike down the road and back.
immoral_action: After Ashley goes back into her house, Mallory goes into the garage and takes the bike for a ride.
immoral_consequence: Ashley is stopped by the police after Mallory calls them to report the missing bike.

norm: It's wrong to put someone in an uncomfortable situation.
situation: John is at a public even with a panel of celebrities including Tiger Woods and it's John's turn to have the audience microphone.
intention: John wants to ask Tiger Woods a question.
moral_action: John asks Tiger Woods what he thinks is the best way for John to become good at golf.
moral_consequence: Tiger Woods is happy with the question because it emphasizes something he is really good at.
immoral_action: John asks Tiger Woods how it feels to be vilified for being unfaithful to his spouse and having all the sordid information about him released.
immoral_consequence: Tiger Woods is embarrassed about the topic and is angry at John for bringing it up before so many people.

norm: It's not okay to put yourself into a bad situation.
situation: It's the end of the month and John does not have quite enough money to pay his rent.
intention: John wants to get the money he needs for rent.
moral_action: John works a few extra hours at work in order to make the money he needs.
moral_consequence: John remains debt free and is able to pay his next month's rent on time.
immoral_action: John takes out a risky high-interest payday loan in order to get the money he needs.
immoral_consequence: John goes deep into debt and his credit rating is negatively affected.

norm: You should always be mindful of others.
situation: Jules is taking a crowded bus to work and feels a bit bored.
intention: Jules wants to entertain himself until he gets to work.
moral_action: Jules listens to a podcast with his headphones on.
moral_consequence: Jules is entertained and the other passengers have a peaceful ride.
immoral_action: Jules takes out a handheld video game and starts playing it with the sound on.
immoral_consequence: Jules's elbows get in other people's space and the noise disturbs other bus riders.

norm: It's good to stop bad habits.
situation: Naga, a former smoker, is stressed about life when his friend offers him a cigar.
intention: Naga wants to lower his stress.
moral_action: Naga excuses himself to his car, and he practices mindfulness exercises.
moral_consequence: Naga becomes more attuned to his emotions.
immoral_action: Naga thanks his friend and smokes the cigar.
immoral_consequence: Naga falls back into his habit of smoking.

norm: You shouldn't let animals suffer.
situation: Jacklyn drops by the store to pick up some groceries with her dog in her car.
intention: Jacklyn needs to pick up some items from the store.
moral_action: Jacklyn orders the items from Instacart when she gets home.
moral_consequence: Jacklyn is able to cuddle with her dog a bit before her order arrives.
immoral_action: Jacklyn leaves her dog in the car while she spends the next hour shopping.
immoral_consequence: Jacklyn has to take her dog to the vet after they pass out from being trapped in the hot car.

norm: You shouldn't run away from your parents.
situation: Noah is visiting a themed park with his parents.
intention: Noah wants to go on the roller coaster.
moral_action: Noah asks his parents to take him to the roller coaster.
moral_consequence: Noah feels secure and go on to the roller coaster happily together with his parents.
immoral_action: Noah is too excited and runs to the roller coaster quickly himself.
immoral_consequence: Noah gets lost on his way to the roller coaster and feels panic because he does not know where his parents are.

norm: It's wrong to be sadistic and brutal.
situation: John just lost his job and is very upset when he gets home to his wife Mindy.
intention: John wants to vent his anger.
moral_action: John takes a deep breath, tells his wife he lost his job and asks if she wants to talk.
moral_consequence: Mindy feels supportive of John and loves him even more as they get closer.
immoral_action: John raises his voice, tells Mindy to take her clothes off and hits her hard.
immoral_consequence: Mindy cries, resents John and thinks of leaving him and ending the marriage.

norm: It's good to make a goal for your team.
situation: Alexis has been placed as the team lead for a big project at her job.
intention: Alexis wants her team to be independent thinkers.
moral_action: Alexis encourages her team to express their ideas and opinions but maintains control of the pace they work at.
moral_consequence: Alexis is praised for completing the task on time and with the full participation of her team.
immoral_action: Alexis lets her team work at their own pace with no clear directives.
immoral_consequence: Alexis loses credibility with her superiors when her project fails to meet deadlines.

norm: It's good to be honest and truthful
situation: Jim’s best friend is throwing a house party tonight that Jim’s parents don’t want him to attend.
intention: Jim wants to join his friend’s party.
moral_action: Jim makes a convincing case for why he should be allowed to go and promises to not stay too long.
moral_consequence: Jim's parents trust him and let him go, and he comes home by curfew.
immoral_action: Jim tells his parents that he wants to spend the night stargazing, but spends the night at his friend’s party.
immoral_consequence: Jim's parents eventually hear about Jim’s antics at the party and ground him for being dishonest.

norm: It's good to admit your own racist tendencies.
situation: Chris believes in justice and fairness and understands the issues faced by her Black friends.
intention: Chris wants to be a good ally to her Black friends.
moral_action: Chris takes a hard look at some of her intuitive reactions and acknowledges she does have some racist reactions sometimes.
moral_consequence: Chris feels that facing the truth about herself makes her more honest and more likely to improve.
immoral_action: Even though she is very involved in racial justice movements, Chris does not acknowledge her own racist feelings.
immoral_consequence: Chris feels like she is not completely honest with herself and others.

norm: It's wrong to worry your parents.
situation: Kim is going out with some friends for the night, but agreed to be home by 10 .
intention: Kim wants to have a good time with her friends.
moral_action: Kim's sets an alarm on her phone to make sure she is home in time while out with friends.
moral_consequence: Kim has a lot of fun, but still manages to be home by curfew much to the delight of her parents.
immoral_action: Kim is having so much fun she forgets all about her curfew and stays out way past 10.
immoral_consequence: Kim's parents ground her after they stay up and see her get home late.

norm: It is polite to smile at people.
situation: Naomi is walking down the street when an older man smiles at her.
intention: Naomi wants to say something to the man.
moral_action: Naomi grins at the man and asks him how his day is going.
moral_consequence: The man's day is made, and he's happy that Naomi smiled back.
immoral_action: Naomi tells the man to stop staring at her and walks faster.
immoral_consequence: The man's feelings are hurt, and he starts to feel like a creep.

norm: It's wrong to destroy things.
situation: While playing tennis with a borrowed racquet, Boj has become angry and frustrated after losing a big point.
intention: Boj needs to vent his emotions.
moral_action: Boj sets down the racquet then practices deep breathing.
moral_consequence: He overcomes his rage and preserves the racquet to continue play.
immoral_action: Boj smashes the racquet on the ground to vent.
immoral_consequence: He has to buy a new racquet, which is expensive.

norm: You shouldn't ridicule others.
situation: Brad is at his desk at work when Ralph comes in wearing really bright yellow pants.
intention: Brad wants to state his surprise at the brightness of Ralph's pants.
moral_action: Brad tells Ralph that he wasn't expecting to see pants that bright but that they make the office pop with good energy.
moral_consequence: Ralph is pleased that Brad thinks his pants add to the office atmosphere and is happy he chose to wear them.
immoral_action: Brad tells Ralph that the pants are shockingly bright and blinding and that he looks like a moronic clown wearing those to work.
immoral_consequence: Ralph is annoyed that Brad is insulting his wardrobe and now feels self conscious and embarrassed about his choice of clothing.

norm: It's expected that co-workers should look out for one another.
situation: Jace overslept, so he's going to be late for work, but Colin can do his work for him in the meantime.
intention: Colin doesn't want his boss to be mad at him.
moral_action: Colin does his work along with Jace's in order to keep the both of them from being criticized by their boss.
moral_consequence: Their boss doesn't notice anything wrong at work, and Jace gets away with oversleeping.
immoral_action: Colin only does his work so that his boss isn't suspicious of anything that he's doing.
immoral_consequence: Their boss notices that Jace is not at work after seeing that his work is left undone.

norm: It's bad to use others for your own pleasure.
situation: Heather knows everybody's gossip in school and is bored during lunch break.
intention: Heather wants to no longer be bored.
moral_action: Heather takes her mind off her classmates and opens a book to read for the rest of the lunch break.
moral_consequence: Heather enjoys the book and finds a potential new hobby in reading.
immoral_action: Heather uses her knowledge to create some interesting drama among classmates, so she can watch what happens.
immoral_consequence: Classmates eventually realize Heather was the source of the rumors and turn on her.

norm: It's bad to do drugs without a perscription
situation: Al is in pain and goes into the bathroom to see what's in the medicine cabinet and finds Advil, Tylenol and his mom's prescribed Oxycontin.
intention: Al wants to choose a pain killer to use.
moral_action: Al decides to take the Advil as he believes the pain is only moderate.
moral_consequence: Al's pain eventually goes away and Al resumes his activities for the day.
