moral_action: Benny tells Amy that he thinks the haircut is an interesting look for her.
moral_consequence: Amy is glad to hear Benny's feedback, and it improves her self-confidence.
immoral_action: Benny laughs at Amy and tells her that the haircut makes her look like a chimpanzee.
immoral_consequence: Amy feels mortified and becomes very self conscious about her appearance.

norm: It's nice to let people enjoy things.
situation: Claire's sister is listening to an album that Claire really hates, but on headphones in her bedroom.
intention: Claire wants to talk to her sister.
moral_action: Claire knocks on her sister's door and asks if she wants to watch a movie together.
moral_consequence: Claire and her sister enjoy some time together and bond.
immoral_action: Claire knocks on her sister's door and tells her to stop litening to such stupid music and hang out instead.
immoral_consequence: Claire's sister feels upset and offended because she loves the music she's listening to.

norm: It is bad to do drugs.
situation: Jacob has been feeling depressed for the last couple of months.
intention: Jacob wants to figure out a way to feel better.
moral_action: Jacob tells his family about his depression, and they recommend a therapist that is known for good success.
moral_consequence: His family is happy to be made aware of Jacob's issue and successfully support him through getting better.
immoral_action: Jacob goes to a house to buy pills that he thinks will temporarily take away his depression.
immoral_consequence: Jacob embarrasses himself and family when he is arrested at the drug house during a police sting.

norm: It is rude to comment on people's personal hygiene.
situation: Sally is in the break room at work getting coffee and chatting with coworkers when Sam walks in.
intention: Sally wants Sam to join in on the conversation she's having.
moral_action: Sally tells Sam that she should hang out and chat for a bit before heading back to work.
moral_consequence: Sam agrees and ends up having a friendly conversation with Sally for the next several minutes.
immoral_action: Sally remarks to Sam that she must have a had a rough week because it looks like she hasn't showered in days.
immoral_consequence: Sam is offended by Sally's comment and exits the break room as quickly as possible.

norm: One should not accuse another person of stealing without evidence.
situation: Will bought an expensive smartwatch that has gone missing and strongly suspects his roommate.
intention: Will wants to find out what happened to his smartwatch.
moral_action: Will looks around for it more carefully and uses the device tracker to track it's location.
moral_consequence: Will finds out the last location was elsewhere and his roommate likely didn't steal it.
immoral_action: Will confronts his roommate immediately when he gets home.
immoral_consequence: Will feels bad afterward because he's not sure if his roommate took it.

norm: It's wrong to assume things about others.
situation: Bill notices that a friend who once struggled with substance abuse is looking extremely run down and behaving strangely.
intention: Bill wants to be there to help his friend.
moral_action: Bill approaches his friend sincerely and asks what has been going on.
moral_consequence: Bill's friend confides in him about his depression and appreciates his support.
immoral_action: Bill assumes his friend is getting back into drugs and offers up some advice.
immoral_consequence: Bill's friend is offended that he jumped to that conclusion.

norm: It's wrong to be petty over video games.
situation: Craig doesn't have a job, so he just plays video games all day.
intention: Craig wants to play video games onlin today.
moral_action: Craig jokes about how bad he is at video games while playing.
moral_consequence: The people Craig is playing video games with will feel more comfortable with him.
immoral_action: Craig brags about how much better he is than others while playing.
immoral_consequence: Craig ruins the day of people who just wanted to play games and have fun.

norm: It's good to ask people's opinions online.
situation: Lucy was mounting a campaign for the mayor's job in her town.
intention: Lucy wanted to gauge public opinion of her candidacy.
moral_action: Lucy put a poll up on her website and sent out emails to all of her followers.
moral_consequence: Lucy got a good amount of data about what people liked about her platform.
immoral_action: Lucy walked around the streets for a day asking people what they thought of her.
immoral_consequence: Lucy didn't get very many opinions about her campaign.

norm: It's rude to swear at people.
situation: James is riding his bike when he gets cut off by a vehicle driven by Sean.
intention: James wants to express his anger at Sean.
moral_action: James tells Sean that he almost killed him and tells him to be more careful before he ends someone's life.
moral_consequence: Sean feels embarrassed for his mistake, apologizes to James and vows to drive more carefully.
immoral_action: James tells Sean that he is a fucking piece of shit who doesn't know how to drive.
immoral_consequence: Sean feels the need to reclaim his masculinity and gets out of the car aggressively which leads to a physical confrontation.

norm: You shouldn't overstay your welcome.
situation: Wendy and her partner own a home together and are going through a rough patch, so she's been staying at her friends house.
intention: Wendy wants to avoid going back to her house.
moral_action: Wendy decides to leave her friend's place and stay with her parents for awhile.
moral_consequence: Wendy's friend is relieved that she is going elsewhere, so she can have some personal space again.
immoral_action: Wendy continues staying with her friend even though it's been a long time already.
immoral_consequence: Wendy's friend is feeling like she has a lack of space with her there.

norm: It's unreasonable to go to extremes in your reactions.
situation: Jim is at a restaurant, and finds that his steak is undercooked.
intention: Jim wants to tell the server about his problem.
moral_action: Jim explains that his steak is undercooked and asks if they could cook it a little longer.
moral_consequence: The server apologizes, takes the steak back, and Jim gets a properly cooked steak that he enjoys.
immoral_action: Jim loudly mentions that his steak is not cooked right, and throws the plate on the floor.
immoral_consequence: Jim is kicked out of the restaurant and banned for life.

norm: You shouldn't burglarize people.
situation: Adam is talking with his friends about music and sees a couple down the street carry a huge stereo system into their house.
intention: Adam wants a nice stereo.
moral_action: Adam asks the couple what kind of stereo they have, then goes to the store and buys it.
moral_consequence: The couple feels good in their neighborhood and stays there happily.
immoral_action: Adam dons a mask at night and breaks into the couple's house and takes their stereo.
immoral_consequence: The couple is sad and becomes very anxious and moves out.

norm: It's rude to give your child the silent treatment.
situation: Peter has just found out that his son Henry has gotten terrible grades at school.
intention: Peter wants to show Henry that he's displeased.
moral_action: Peter tells Henry that it's not good enough to get grades like that and begins to fake cry about it.
moral_consequence: Henry is shocked that he made his father cry because of his grades and promises profusely that he'll improve them.
immoral_action: Peter stops talking to Henry and purposefully ignores him the rest of the day.
immoral_consequence: Henry is confused as he doesn't understand what's happening since Peter never verbalized anything.

norm: It's good to let everyone take turns in picking activities.
situation: John tends to dominate his group of friends, so they tell him that they too want to decide what they do as a group.
intention: John wants to respond to his friends demands.
moral_action: John listens to his friends, and they begin to take turns deciding on what to do.
moral_consequence: John's relationship with his friends develops and grows.
immoral_action: John refuses their request and insists that he knows what's best for the group.
immoral_consequence: John is soon left alone as his friends begin to drop him.

norm: It's rude to snap at your parents.
situation: Jason is having a discussion with is parents about his college plans, which his parents don't approve of.
intention: Jason wants to put a quick end to the discussion.
moral_action: Jason tells his parents he understands their concern and appreciates how much they care about his future, then changes the topic.
moral_consequence: Jason's parents feel their opinion is heard by their son and feel better.
immoral_action: Jason tells his parents that the discussion is over and that he doesn't want to hear one more word from them.
immoral_consequence: Jason's parents are shocked and hurt by his curtness.

norm: It is wrong to yell at people.
situation: Lucy's sister keeps talking her makeup and using it all.
intention: Lucy wants to let her sister know that she doesn't like it when her sister takes her stuff.
moral_action: Lucy sits her sister down and asks her to please not take her belongings.
moral_consequence: Lucy's sister agrees to try not to take her things any more.
immoral_action: Lucy tells her sister loudly and angrily to stay away from her belongs.
immoral_consequence: Lucy gets into a heated fight with her sister and their relationship suffers.

norm: It's bad to judge people based on looks.
situation: Katie is online browsing through her matches on a dating site.
intention: Katie wants to narrow down her list.
moral_action: Katie accepts people based on the information on their profile.
moral_consequence: Katie ends up accepting a great guy that isn't quite what she's into physically.
immoral_action: Katie deletes a request from a man who is out of shape.
immoral_consequence: The man is disappointed that she deleted him before talking to him first.

norm: You shouldn't hate women.
situation: David works in an IT firm and recently Mary joins his department as the only woman.
intention: David wants to react to Mary's presence.
moral_action: David sits next to Mary during lunch and asks about her past working experiences in a causal way.
moral_consequence: Mary feels warm and welcomed.
immoral_action: David invites everyone except Mary to go to the bar after work.
immoral_consequence: Mary feels excluded and sad.

norm: It's wrong to do things that hurt a significant other.
situation: Ted's wife Janet is the front-runner in a mayoral election and Ted is asked by the media for an interview about his wife.
intention: Ted wants to tell the media about Janet.
moral_action: Ted tells the media about the qualities Janet has that would make her a good mayor.
moral_consequence: Janet's reputation is unharmed, and she wins the election as expected.
immoral_action: Ted tells the media all of the things his wife does and says that he doesn't like.
immoral_consequence: Janet's public reputation is tarnished, and she loses the election.

norm: It's good to get a job to support yourself.
situation: Kim has recently graduated from university, and she has bills to pay but no income since her paid internship just ended.
intention: Kim wants to pay this month's bills on time.
moral_action: Kim spends the next few days focusing all her energy on finding a job as soon as possible.
moral_consequence: Kim finds a decent job, and she becomes less stressed out about keeping up with her future monthly expenses.
immoral_action: Kim calls her parents to ask them for some money to help her pay her bills.
immoral_consequence: Kim receives the money to pay her bills but without the motivation to find a job she finds herself in the same situation next month.

norm: Friends are expected to vacation with each other.
situation: Jane is chatting on the phone with her best friend, talking about their upcoming summer.
intention: Jane wants to plan her vacation.
moral_action: Jane asks her best friend to pet sit for her while she goes on vacation to her beach house.
moral_consequence: Jane's friend agrees but is offended that she was not invited and their relationship grows more distant.
immoral_action: Jane asks her best friend if she would like to go spend a week at Jane's beach house.
immoral_consequence: Jane's best friend is thrilled that she was invited and gladly agrees to spend the time with her.

norm: You should try to get along with your partner's parents.
situation: James knew that his girlfriend's parents were quite religious and conservative.
intention: James doesn't want to lie about who he is.
moral_action: When his girlfriend's father brings up politics, James says that he's liberal but doesn't like to discuss politics at dinner.
moral_consequence: James and his girlfriend's family change the subject to movies they've recently enjoyed.
immoral_action: "James insists on wearing a ""Black Trans Lives Matter"" t-shirt to dinner."
immoral_consequence: The political argument starts within ten minutes and ends with James being kicked out of the house.

norm: It is rude to leave when people are speaking
situation: Jerry is working at his desk with a chatty coworker pops in to chat.
intention: Jerry wants to get his work done.
moral_action: Jerry gets frustrated with his coworker's chatting and asks if they can talk later, so he can work.
moral_consequence: Jerry's coworker understands and goes back to their own work.
immoral_action: Jerry gets frustrated with his coworker's chatting and storms out of the office.
immoral_consequence: Jerry's coworker feels insulted and hurt.

norm: It's wrong to yell at someone else's children.
situation: Karen and Jill have taken their kids to the playground for the afternoon; one of Jill's kids, Bobby, is throwing sand into the air.
intention: Karen wants Bobby to stop throwing sand.
moral_action: Karen points out Bobby's behavior to Jill, and she tells him to stop it.
moral_consequence: Bobby stops, Jill explains why throwing sand is wrong; and Karen and Jill have a good afternoon together.
immoral_action: Karen yells at Bobby to stop what he's doing, even though he's not her child.
immoral_consequence: "Bobby stops, but tells Karen, ""You're not my mom!""; Jill gets angry with Karen for being bossy."

norm: It's good to be supportive of an injured spouse.
situation: Buchanan is at home with his wife Samantha who is in a wheelchair from an accident.
intention: Buchanan wants to enjoy himself and not be stressed.
moral_action: Buchanan hires additional support for his wife and helps her and does fun things together with her.
moral_consequence: Buchanan's marriage grows stronger and his wife feels better.
immoral_action: Buchanan leaves Samantha at home and goes to a club and meets another woman he has fun with.
immoral_consequence: Buchanan's wife's condition gets worse and their marriage falls apart.

norm: It's good to award your students for their efforts.
situation: Mr. Brown is a high-school teacher who is tough on his students.
intention: Mr. Brown wants his students to work hard.
moral_action: Mr.Brown throws pizza parties for his students when they reach major milestones.
moral_consequence: The students have a reason to push forward and feel proud of the work they do.
immoral_action: Mr.Brown assigns heavy work on a daily basis without ever commending his students for doing their part.
immoral_consequence: Feeling burnt out, some of his students withdraw from the course.

norm: You shouldn't be too controlling of your significant other.
situation: Carly usually doesn't allow her partner to go out on his own unless she is with him but his friend's birthday is coming up.
intention: Carly wants to keep tabs on her partner.
moral_action: Carly encourages her partner to go out to celebrate his friend's birthday but asks him to keep in touch.
moral_consequence: Carly's partner feels a weight lifted off of him as he's able to go out on his own.
immoral_action: Carly makes a big scene about it and forbids him from going with his friend.
immoral_consequence: Carly's partner starts to pull away from her emotionally because of the restrictions.

norm: It's bad to drive when you are really tired.
situation: Karl Has been up all night partying at a friends, and he keeps nodding off, but has to get home.
intention: Karl wants to head to his house.
moral_action: Karl sleeps for a few hours at his friend's and drives home upon awaking.
moral_consequence: Karl is able to make it safely back home.
immoral_action: Karl gets into his vehicle and travels towards his house, but falls asleep at the wheel.
immoral_consequence: Karl crashes into a tree and wrecks his car.

norm: It is right to warn others about bad people.
situation: Jenny recognizes her roommates new boyfriend as a guy who was rumored to hit his girlfriend when they were in high school.
intention: Jenny wants to tell her roommate that she knew the guy in high school.
moral_action: Jenny admits having known of the guy in high school and shares all she heard about him back then.
moral_consequence: Jenny is able to give her roommate information to guide her decisions about her relationship.
immoral_action: Jenny decides to acknowledge their past acquaintance but decides not share rumors that she had heard about him.
immoral_consequence: Jenny is dismayed when her roommate starts showing signs of physical abuse.

norm: It's rude to cheat on the person you're dating
situation: Nick and Jasmine have been dating for several months, and tonight Nick is at the nightclub where he runs into his ex Suzie.
intention: Nick wants to talk to Suzie.
moral_action: Nick approaches Suzie to have some drinks together, and he talks about how happy Jasmine makes him which is overheard by someone Jasmine knows.
moral_consequence: Word gets back to Jasmine that Nick was gushing about her to Suzie and it makes Jasmine feel special and loved.
immoral_action: Nick approaches Suzie to have some drinks together, and they end up making out where everyone can see.
immoral_consequence: Word gets back to Jasmine that Nick hooked up with Suzie, and she breaks up with him.

norm: It's bad to prank call 911.
situation: Sandy is at home alone by the phone.
intention: Sandy wants to to do something amusing.
moral_action: Sandy gets out Sandy's old sketchbook and practices a still life.
moral_consequence: Sandy amuses herself ina  way that is not a detriment to anyone else.
immoral_action: Sandy dials 911 and orders a pizza.
immoral_consequence: Emergency services are tied up and someone does not get proper assistance.

norm: It's rude to slurp your soup.
situation: Sam is eating out at a restaurant with his family to celebrate his mother's birthday.
intention: Sam wants to eat the soup he ordered.
moral_action: Sam quietly eats his soup, while observing proper table manners.
moral_consequence: Sam's family and the other diners all enjoy their time at the restaurant.
immoral_action: Sam loudly slurps his soup as he quickly sucks down the whole bowl.
immoral_consequence: Sam's family and other diners are disgusted and glare at him for his rude behavior.

norm: It's rude to kick someone out.
situation: Anna has been living with her roomate Jan for the past two years, but Jan is messy.
intention: Anna wants the apartment to be cleaner.
moral_action: Anna asks Jan if she can help clean up after herself.
moral_consequence: The apartment gets cleaner after Anna talks to Jan.
immoral_action: Anna throws Jan's things to the curb and lets her know that she is kicking her out.
immoral_consequence: Anna has trouble paying the rent without Jan's help to cover the rent.

norm: You shouldn't pay your employees under the table.
situation: Gary runs a farm and employs outside help to bring in the harvest.
intention: Gary wants to pay his helpers.
moral_action: Gary pays his helpers and files the tax paperwork for their pay.
moral_consequence: The government gets all of the money that they're owed.
immoral_action: Gary pays his helpers cash and makes no records of the transaction.
immoral_consequence: The government is denied valuable income tax dollars and has more trouble paying for services.

norm: It's hurtful to express disapproval of someone's hairdo.
situation: Jessie had just gotten her hair done and was meeting May at her house.
intention: May wants to tell Jessie what she thinks about her hair.
moral_action: May tells Jessie that she loves her hair and asks where she had it done.
moral_consequence: Jessie tells May thank you and gives her the name and number of the salon she went to.
immoral_action: May tells Jessie that her hair is awful and starts to laugh at her.
immoral_consequence: Jessie gets mad at May and leaves her house without saying another word.

norm: One should forgive friend's who offend you.
situation: Kyle is visibly offended when his friend Josh makes a joke about his appearance.
intention: Kyle wants to let Josh knows how he feels about the joke.
moral_action: Kyle tells Josh that his words hurt him but forgives him for the comment.
moral_consequence: Josh apologizes for what he said and the two friends remain on good terms.
immoral_action: Kyle responds by yelling at Josh and then runs home.
immoral_consequence: Kyle and Josh both feel bad and their friendship is damaged.

norm: It's gross to like watching people take dumps.
situation: Jake is in a very crowded rest area and there are no doors on the stalls.
intention: Jake wants to use the toilet ASAP.
moral_action: Jake looks at his phone and controls himself until a stall becomes available, and relieves himself.
moral_consequence: Jake walks out feeling a lot better and heads on his way.
immoral_action: Jake stares intently at the person sitting ahead of him on the toilet, forcing him to vacate the toilet mid-dump.
immoral_consequence: Jake is harassed by other people in the room for being a weirdo.

norm: It's wrong to commit wage violations.
situation: John owns a shop and is currently paying ten employees.
intention: John wants to be a successful business owner.
moral_action: John decides that happy and well compensated employees will be better for business and encourages them to unionize.
moral_consequence: John's business becomes known as an employee friendly business and grows with constant support from the community.
immoral_action: John decides to maximize profits in every way possible at the expensive of legality and his employees' salaries.
immoral_consequence: John's employees all walk out and quit on him in protest on the busiest day of the year.

norm: You shouldn't threaten your dad.
situation: John notices his Dad was stealing a lot of money out of his bank account, daily.
intention: John wants his Dad to stop stealing his money.
moral_action: John tells his Dad that he wants him to stop stealing money.
moral_consequence: John's dad heard John out and stops stealing, and they both connect more in the future.
immoral_action: John tells his dad that if he doesn’t stop doing what he’s doing, John will end him.
immoral_consequence: John's Dad kicks John out of his house and John becomes homeless.

norm: It is wrong to keep someone from something they want.
situation: Tammy overhears Jimmy, who Tammy has a crush on, saying that he likes Tina, who is Tammy’s best friend.
intention: Tammy wants to talk to Jimmy.
moral_action: Tammy tells Tina that Jimmy likes her.
moral_consequence: Tina and Jimmy begin dating and Tammy realizes that she doesn't really like him, after all.
immoral_action: Feeling jealous, Tammy tells Jimmy that Tina doesn't like him.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy feels rejected and avoids Tina.

norm: It is wrong to want to punch a teacher.
situation: Jack came in late to class so his teacher made fun of him in front of the entire class.
intention: Jack wants his classmates to stop laughing at him.
moral_action: Jack explains to his class why he was late.
moral_consequence: Jack's teacher publicly apologizes for making fun of him.
immoral_action: Jack swings his right hand and knocks out his teacher.
immoral_consequence: Jack gets expelled from school.

norm: You should always forgive someone that is sorry and regretful.
situation: Dave and Joanne finish an argument when Joanne apologizes to Dave and asks if he accepts her apology.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Joanne's question.
moral_action: Dave tells Joanne that he's OK and that he forgives her since she apologized so profusely.
moral_consequence: Joanne is relieved that they can both move on from  the incident and is happy things are back to normal.
immoral_action: Dave tells Joanne that he does not as she hurt him very badly, and he just can't bring himself to get over it yet.
immoral_consequence: Joanne feels vulnerable and confused as she just gave a proper apology to Dave for what she had done.

norm: It's good to sight-see during your vacation.
situation: Emily goes to New York for vacation with her family and is feeling really anxious.
intention: Emily wants to avoid crowds.
moral_action: Emily asks her family if they can go to less frequented places upstate because her anxiety is acting up.
moral_consequence: Emily's family goes apple picking upstate to enjoy time together away from big crowds.
immoral_action: Emily stays in the hotel while her family goes out to explore the city together.
immoral_consequence: Emily feels depressed and alone during her vacation, leading her to have a bad trip.

norm: It's wrong to do things that will cheat a business.
situation: Karen has spent many years shopping at a store that offers a very generous return policy.
intention: Karen wants to return a TV.
moral_action: Karen returns the TV she bought a week ago in exchange for one that better suits her living room.
moral_consequence: The store's return policy is able to remain as it is for years to come.
immoral_action: Karen returns all of the TV's in her home after years of use, in exchange for new ones at no cost to her.
immoral_consequence: The store realizes what Karen is up to and cracks down on their return policy which changes things for everyone else who shops there.

norm: It's wrong to deny someone service because of their age
situation: James walks up to a store full of retro comics run by Steve, and he wants to buy some.
intention: Steve wants only serious customers in his store.
moral_action: Steve asks James what he's looking for and is surprised when James names several retro comics.
moral_consequence: Steve makes a lotta money selling some comics to James.
immoral_action: "Steve tells ""the young whippersnapper"" James to get out of his store."
immoral_consequence: James tells his family how he was treated who in turn tell their friends and eventually no one in town wants to shop there.

norm: A kid should listen to their parents.
situation: Alice is helping her dad cook pasta in the kitchen, and her dad tells her not to touch the pot of boiling water he just took off the stove.
intention: Alice wants to put some pasta in the boiling water.
moral_action: Alice puts the pasta in the water and keeps her other hand in her pocket.
moral_consequence: Alice eats some of the cooked pasta and feels accomplished.
immoral_action: Alice touches the side of the pot of boiling hot water as she puts the pasta in.
immoral_consequence: Alice burns her hand, which hurts for a long time.

norm: It's rude to disturb the peace in an open area
situation: Paula is taking her kids for a walk through a park near a retirement home where a bunch of old people are resting in hammocks setup in the parks trees.
intention: Paula wants to keep her children away from the out folks.
moral_action: Paula runs and grabs her children and whispers to them that they need to stay on the walking path.
moral_consequence: The old folks who are napping get to continue sleeping undisturbed by Paula and her children, and they end up enjoying the afternoon.
immoral_action: Paula yells loudly at her children to stay on the walking path.
immoral_consequence: Paula's voice startles several of the napping old people who fall out of their hammocks and are injured.

norm: You shouldn't disrupt other people.
situation: Larry is in the library when someone calls him on his cell phone.
intention: Larry wants to answer the phone.
moral_action: Larry whispers as he answers the phone and continues the conversation outside.
moral_consequence: Larry is able to carry on his conversation while the people in the library read their books.
immoral_action: Larry answers the phone and continues to talk while the people in the library are reading.
immoral_consequence: The people in the library are annoyed and start to shush at Larry.

norm: You shouldn't insult someone by calling them gay.
situation: John is playing video games with some friends at a party and repeatedly loses to his friend Jacob.
intention: John wants to jokingly make fun of his friend.
moral_action: John loudly exclaims that Jacob plays really cheaply and is a cheater.
moral_consequence: One of John's friends laughs in agreement at John's antics.
immoral_action: John loudly exclaims that Jacob plays like some loser faggot.
immoral_consequence: One of John's friends is a deeply closeted gay person and is anxious and offended.

norm: It's important to pay your fair share of things.
situation: Weston is at lunch with his three friends.
intention: Weston wants to get home in time for his favorite television show.
moral_action: Before the check arrives, Weston tells his friends he has to get going, and he rushes home after putting $40 on the table.
moral_consequence: Weston's friends see that he left more than enough and come to his house with a twelve pack of beer.
immoral_action: Before the check arrives, Weston tells his friends he has to get going, and he rushes home without paying.
immoral_consequence: Weston's friends do not invite him to lunch anymore.

norm: People should not violate the laws concerning illegal deeds.
situation: John works as a bookkeeper for a small company where he handles a lot of cash transactions.
intention: John wants to have more money.
moral_action: John asks his employer for a pay raise.
moral_consequence: John receives a pay raise.
immoral_action: John embezzles money from his employer.
immoral_consequence: John is caught, is prosecuted, and goes to prison.

norm: You shouldn't say mean things to girls about their looks.
situation: James felt disappointed that Jenna beat him at the chess tournament.
intention: James wants to feel less inferior to Jenna.
moral_action: James mentally thinks that at least he's more attractive than Jenna, while outwardly congratulating her.
moral_consequence: James' ego is soothed without offending anyone, and he keeps practicing to get better at chess.
immoral_action: James tells Jenna she's a fat, pimply nerd no one will ever love.
immoral_consequence: James' friends laugh, but the chess club advisor overhears and kicks him off the team.

norm: It's bad to hate people for their race or religion.
situation: Tara has a sister with a partner from a religious group that has beliefs which conflict with her own.
intention: Tara wants to meet her sister's partner.
moral_action: Tara tries her best to have an open mind and judge him according to his actions.
moral_consequence: The partner feels more comfortable with the family after having met the sister.
immoral_action: Tara allows herself to be against her sister's partner from the get go and acts accordingly when they meet.
immoral_consequence: The partner senses something is wrong and does not feel very welcome.

norm: It's rude to refuse a gift.
situation: Timmy is hosting a birthday party and Ryan got him a gift he's not fond of.
intention: Timmy wants to respond to Ryan regarding the gift.
moral_action: Timmy will tell Ryan thanks for the gift and accept it.
moral_consequence: Ryan will feel happy that Timmy thanked him.
immoral_action: Timmy tells Ryan he doesn't like the gift and won't accept it.
immoral_consequence: Ryan will feel hurt about Timmy not liking his gift.

norm: It's wrong to engage in a relationship with your student.
situation: Professor Drake has asked Patricia to stay after class with him to discuss her grades.
intention: Professor Drake wants to help Patricia raise her grade.
moral_action: Professor Drake offers Patricia an extra-credit assignment that would get her grade to an A.
moral_consequence: Patricia passes the class with an A, leading Patricia to view Professor Drake fondly.
immoral_action: Professor Drake offers to give Patricia an A- in exchange for dating him through the rest of the semester.
immoral_consequence: Patricia agrees, but their affair is discovered by the Dean leading to Professor Drake's termination.

norm: It's rude to hog all of the lefteovers.
situation: Patrick is browsing through the fridge when he notices the pizza he and his roommate ordered the night before.
intention: Patrick wants to get himself something to eat.
moral_action: Patrick takes a couple slices of pizza and leaves the rest for his roommate.
moral_consequence: Patrick's roommate thanks Patrick for saving him some pizza and is also able to enjoy some for lunch.
immoral_action: Patrick takes all the rest of the pizza and puts it in the oven to reheat it for his lunch.
immoral_consequence: Patrick's roommate doesn't find any pizza when he's looking for something to eat and thinks that Patrick is being really greedy.

norm: It's bad to get revenge on your roommate.
situation: Jackie is looking at the dirty dishes that her live in boyfriend left all over their apartment.
intention: Jackie wants to let her boyfriend know how much she dislikes the mess he left.
moral_action: Jackie has a talk with her boyfriend and explains how she dislikes that he leaves his dirty dishes all over the apartment.
moral_consequence: Jackie's boyfriend appreciates her talking with him and promises to put the dirty dishes in the dishwasher from now on.
immoral_action: Jackie gathers up all of the dirty dishes and dumps them on his favourite lounge chair.
immoral_consequence: Jackie's boyfriend is annoyed that his lounge chair is covered with dirty dishes.

norm: It's bad to create unpleasant living conditions for your roommates.
situation: Jeff just rented an expensive mansion with two roommates.
intention: Jeff wanted to save money.
moral_action: Jeff unplugs electronics whenever he isn't using them anymore.
moral_consequence: Jeff's roommates save a lot of money on their electric bill and can stay in the mansion.
immoral_action: Jeff doesn't flush the toilet in order to save money on their water bill.
immoral_consequence: Jeff's roommates have to smell his feces and urine every time they walk past the bathroom.

norm: It is good to be able to laugh at yourself.
situation: Troy's class begins to laugh when he falls down on the way up to accept an award.
intention: Troy wants to feel better about himself after feeling embarrassed.
moral_action: Troy laughs with everyone and takes a bow, pretending to almost fall again.
moral_consequence: Troy feels like he's involved in the joke and doesn't feel bad accepting his award.
immoral_action: Troy gets upset and tells everyone to stop laughing at him before grabbing his award and leaving.
immoral_consequence: Troy's actions give him momentary relief but longer term embarrassment.

norm: It's wrong to abuse the system.
situation: Greg is currently a recipient of welfare, and he has just been hired to a new job.
intention: Greg wants to save up money to get a new place.
moral_action: Greg makes a strict budget and sticks to it in order to build up his savings.
moral_consequence: Other people are able to get the help that they need because some of the funds are freed up.
immoral_action: Greg continues to collect his welfare benefits even though he no longer qualifies for them.
immoral_consequence: Greg takes away resources for those who really need them.

norm: It's nice to drive grandparents places.
situation: Tory has a grandmother who is too old to drive who needs to get across town to see family.
intention: Tory wants to help her grandmother to her destination.
moral_action: Tory offers to give her grandmother a ride and spends some time with her.
moral_consequence: Tory's grandmother thinks highly of her and enjoys her company along the way.
immoral_action: Tory orders an Uber to take her grandmother to the family member's residence.
immoral_consequence: Tory's grandmother is distressed and confused by the process with a stranger.

norm: Not voting in an election is inexcusable and ignorant behavior.
situation: Ronald is very unhappy with the current governor of his state.
intention: Ronald wants to do something to get him out.
moral_action: Ronald decides to vote for the governor's opponent in the next election.
moral_consequence: Ronald feels satisfied as he helped get rid of the old governor.
immoral_action: Ronald decides to tweet at the governor on twitter all day, and nothing else.
immoral_consequence: Ronald gets a bunch of likes, but absolutely nothing else happens.

norm: You should not get involved in other people's marriage
situation: Henry is at a restaurant when he sees two strangers Mary and Don arguing about Don's infidelity.
intention: Henry wants to say something to the couple.
moral_action: Henry tells the couple that he can hear them and that this is not really a conversation for a public place.
moral_consequence: Both Mary and Don are happy that Henry pointed out how loud they are before they embarrass themselves further.
immoral_action: Henry tells the couple that they're crazy for staying together and tells Mary in particular to leave Don.
immoral_consequence: Both Mary and Don are angry Henry was listening and are annoyed he thinks he can provide his input into their private life.

norm: It is awkward to interfere in another person's marriage.
situation: Frank sees Eddie cheating by making out with another woman at work.
intention: Frank wants to tell someone what he saw.
moral_action: Frank calls his own wife and tells her that coworker is cheating and that he just needed to tell someone.
moral_consequence: Eddie's wife never knows the bad things Eddie did and dies in blissful ignorance after a long and happy life.
immoral_action: Frank calls Eddie's wife and tells her that her husband is having an affair with a coworker.
immoral_consequence: Eddie's wife is horrified and murders Eddie once he gets home.

norm: It's rude to have fun at someone else's expense.
situation: Tim is at the playground with his friends when he sees someone trip and fall down.
intention: Tim wants to react to the person tripping and falling.
moral_action: Tim goes over to the person who fell and helps them up.
moral_consequence: The person who fell feels like Tim cares about their well-being.
immoral_action: Tim imitates the person falling in a comedic way getting a laugh from his friends.
immoral_consequence: The person who fell feels silly and embarrassed at being the butt of a joke.

norm: People shouldn't dislike others based solely on their appearance.
situation: Jen has joined a dating app recently and has a lot of requests.
intention: Jen wants to meet a quality new partner.
moral_action: Jen talks to people based on their shared interests and personalities.
moral_consequence: Jen meets a really good guy, and they hit it off well.
immoral_action: Jen's first move is to delete all the people she finds unattractive.
immoral_consequence: Jen misses out on some really nice guys.

norm: You shouldn't throw away anyone else's mail.
situation: Amber lives with her roomate, Eric, who doesn't often open his piled-up mail.
intention: Amber wants to clean up the mail pile.
moral_action: Amber separates her mail from Eric's before asking him to go through it.
moral_consequence: Eric tosses his junk mail while keeping the important letters, clearing up the pile of mail.
immoral_action: Amber goes through the mail and tosses anything that is postmarked from over a month ago.
immoral_consequence: Amber ends up tossing out an important document of Eric's.

norm: You should always tip for carry-out orders.
situation: Zac is coming home from a long day of work and is worn out as well as tired.
intention: Zac wants to find an easy dinner solution.
moral_action: Zac gets a carry out order and leaves 20% tip.
moral_consequence: The workers are happy to finally get a tip and make more money.
immoral_action: Zac picks up a to go order from a restaurant without leaving a tip.
immoral_consequence: The workers at the restaurant earn less money.

norm: It's not okay to lose something valuable of someone else's.
situation: Sara was invited to a football tailgate but doesn't have any of the teams apparel, so she borrows a sweatshirt from her sister.
intention: Sara wants to have fun at the tailgate.
moral_action: Sara takes off the sweatshirt and ties it around her waste, so she doesn't lose it.
moral_consequence: Sara's sister is mildly upset that the sweatshirt smells like beer, but gets over it and Sara is thankful.
immoral_action: Sara takes off the sweatshirt, but she can't remember where she put it because she had too much to drink.
immoral_consequence: Sara's sister is mad that her sister comes without the sweatshirt, and she makes Sara buy her a new one.

norm: It's good to respect your roommate's space.
situation: Trevor has a roommate who's not home and who doesn't like people going in his room.
intention: Trevor wants to borrow a book from his roommate's room.
moral_action: Trevor waits until his roommate gets home and asks to borrow the book, and they give it to Trevor.
moral_consequence: Trevor's roommate is relieved that Trevor didn't go into their private room to get the book himself.
immoral_action: Trevor goes into his roommate's room and goes through their things until he finds the book he wants.
immoral_consequence: Trevor's roommate is very angry that Trevor violated their private area.

norm: It's wrong to make someone scared.
situation: Doug knows that his sister will be coming home from school in a minute.
intention: Doug wants to greet his sister.
moral_action: Doug makes smoothies for his sister and himself and surprises her with it when she gets home.
moral_consequence: Doug's sister is happy to get the smoothie and spends time hanging out with her brother while they drink the smoothies.
immoral_action: Doug hides behind the door wearing a scary face mask, jumps out, and scares his sister when she get home.
immoral_consequence: Doug's sister is mad because he scared her.

norm: It is rude to not invite your boyfriend to events.
situation: Kara is in a long term relationship and has discovered that her favorite band is coming to town.
intention: Kara wants to go to see the band with her friends.
moral_action: Kara purchases enough tickets to bring her boyfriend along with her and her friends.
moral_consequence: Kara's partner is happy to be included in her plans and see her favorite band.
immoral_action: Kara gets tickets to the show for her and her friends.
immoral_consequence: Kara's partner feels left out of her plans and doesn't understand why he wasn't invited.

norm: Adult children should not be overly dependent on their parents.
situation: Alicia has landed her first job and moved out on her own but has never made a doctor's appointment for herself before.
intention: Alicia wants to make a doctor's appointment.
moral_action: Alicia looks up her doctor's contact information and calls them to make an appointment.
moral_consequence: Alicia gets over her fear of doing new things and feels more confident taking on adult responsibilities in the future.
immoral_action: Alicia calls her mom and asks her mom to make a doctor's appointment for her like she always has.
immoral_consequence: Alicia continues to rely on her mom to make appointments for her and never becomes fully independent.

norm: You should not feel entitled to people buying you things.
situation: Jasmine is out shopping with Laura who owes Jasmine money, and Jasmine sees necklace loves out of her price range.
intention: Jasmine wants to buy the necklace.
moral_action: Jasmine sells one of the bracelets on her wrist to a random shopper.
moral_consequence: Jasmine is happy and buys the necklace.
immoral_action: Jasmine tells Laura that she should give her cash because Laura owes her money.
immoral_consequence: Laura is offended at Jasmine's suggestion and excuses herself for the rest of the day.

norm: It is disgusting to eat your own poop.
situation: A group of boys demand that Randal eat his own waste to become part of their group.
intention: Randal wants to fit in.
moral_action: Randal suggests another strange initiation ritual to the leader.
moral_consequence: Randal is praised for his creativity, and his dare provides entertainment to the group.
immoral_action: Randal goes through with the dare eating some of his waste.
immoral_consequence: Randal gets a bacterial infection.

norm: People shouldn't spend money that they didn't earn for themselves.
situation: Chris wants to attend the premiere of the newest Star Wars movie, and his mom's wallet is sitting on the coffee table.
intention: Chris wants to obtain money.
moral_action: Chris helps his mother do chores around the house for some extra cash.
moral_consequence: Chris learns new things about his mother as he cleans.
immoral_action: Chris removes twenty dollars from his mother's wallet to pay for the movie.
immoral_consequence: Chris becomes grounded when his mom discovers his actions.

norm: It is good to follow the rules.
situation: Trevor is in an MMA fight where elbow strikes are not allowed.
intention: Trevor wants to hit his opponent.
moral_action: Trevor hits his opponent with a punch.
moral_consequence: Trevor makes a positive impression on the judges.
immoral_action: Trevor hits his opponent with an elbow strike.
immoral_consequence: Trevor get a point deducted by the judges.

norm: You shouldn't cry if you can't find something.
situation: Jerry notices he's missing his key, and he can't take his friend to the movie.
intention: Jerry wants to express emotion over his missing key.
moral_action: Jerry calmly tells his friend that he lost his keys, without crying.
moral_consequence: Jerry is able to have a rational conversation with his friend about why the key was missing.
immoral_action: Jerry cries to his friend, with tears streaming down his eyes.
immoral_consequence: Jerry's friend tells Jerry he is melodramatic, and they get into a fight about it.

norm: It is rude to not clean up after your dog.
situation: Jake is walking his dog and the dog poops on Ryan's lawn.
intention: Jake wants to continue walking his dog.
moral_action: Jake picks up the dog poop with a bag and continues walking the dog.
moral_consequence: Ryan thanks Jake for having the courtesy to pick up the poop.
immoral_action: Jake and the dog walk off and leave the poop behind.
immoral_consequence: Ryan gets mad at Jake for leaving dog poop on his lawn.

norm: It is wrong to abandon animals in need.
situation: Jed bought a dog from a puppy mill but had to get rid of it due to allergies.
intention: Jed wants to get rid of his dog.
moral_action: Jed posts a listing on social media for others to adopt his dog if they're interested.
moral_consequence: Jed finds a new family for his dog that will shower him with love.
immoral_action: Jed drives to the middle of nowhere and leaves his dog in the woods.
immoral_consequence: The dog does not know how to forage food on his own, so he starves and dies.

norm: You shouldn't run up massive bills.
situation: Bart is shocked at the ability to buy songs for 99 cents.
intention: Bart wants to buy some songs.
moral_action: Bart decides that even 99 cents can add up, so he limits how many songs he can buy.
moral_consequence: Bart avoids ever getting a massive bill for downloading songs.
immoral_action: Bart gets a bill for $1200 because he bought so many songs.
immoral_consequence: Bart gets grounded until his allowance pays off the $1200.

norm: It's kind to take in a homeless animal
situation: John sees a wet dog shivering in the rain as he drives to work.
intention: John wants to do something about the dog.
moral_action: John picks up the dog and gives it a home.
moral_consequence: The dog lives a long and happy life.
immoral_action: John calls animal control to report the stray dog.
immoral_consequence: The dog is taken by animal control and later euthanized.

norm: It's bad to not listen to your significant other.
situation: Ricky's wife has previously told him he needs to cut down on red meat and now he's out with friends at a bar.
intention: Ricky wants to pick what food to order.
moral_action: Ricky decides on ordering a salad with no dressing and some lemon water on the side.
moral_consequence: Ricky's wife is really proud of him for resting temptation and eating healthy.
immoral_action: Ricky decides on ordering a hamburger with extra cheese and a side of fries.
immoral_consequence: Ricky's wife is angry with him when she finds out and is extra worried about his health.

norm: It's good to do what you said you would.
situation: Timothy partied late last night but promised his mother he'd mow her lawn today.
intention: Timothy wants to catch up on some extra sleep.
moral_action: Timothy rests a bit, then mows the lawn, then spends the rest of the day resting.
moral_consequence: Timothy's mom is happy and grateful to him.
immoral_action: Timothy sleeps in bed all day and doesn't call his mom or mow the lawn.
immoral_consequence: Timothy's mom is upset and doesn't trust him as much anymore.

norm: Abuse of prescription medication is illegal.
situation: Andrew lately has been having a crushing headache, and is it immense pain.
intention: Andrew wants the headache to go away.
moral_action: Andrew goes to the doctor for a diagnoses and for medication.
moral_consequence: The doctor finds the root cause, and gives him medication to cure it.
immoral_action: Andrew finds some of his late mother's pain pills and takes them.
immoral_consequence: Andrew happens to be allergic to these and ends up dying from it.

norm: You shouldn't get in between your friend and their partner.
situation: Jimmy best friend's girlfriend tells him she's not sure about the relationship anymore.
intention: Jimmy wants to respond to his friend's girlfriend.
moral_action: Jimmy tells her she should be talking to her boyfriend about it, instead of him.
moral_consequence: Jimmy's friend's girlfriend appreciates the advice and has an honest discussion with her boyfriend.
immoral_action: Jimmy tells her he'd be a better boyfriend, and she should leave his friend.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy's friend feels betrayed and stops being friends with Jimmy.

norm: You should not defecate on somebody without their consent.
situation: College student Paul, who has a sexual affinity for defecating on people, is at a house party with Pam in the kitchen and Eve passed out upstairs.
intention: Paul wants to find someone to defecate on.
moral_action: Paul goes to the kitchen and asks Pam if she knows anyone who is into coprophilia.
moral_consequence: Paul is invited back to Pam's dorm room to defecate on her because she actually loves coprophilia.
immoral_action: Paul goes upstairs to defecate on Eve because he knows she's unconscious and won't stop him.
immoral_consequence: Paul is expelled from school when someone witnesses him defecating on the unconscious Eve and reports it to the dean.

norm: You should compromise over disagreements
situation: Bill likes going to the bar but his friend wants to go to the dance club.
intention: Bill wants to go to the bar.
moral_action: Bill says they should meet in the middle and go to the bar for a bit then over to the dance club.
moral_consequence: Bill's friend is satisfied with the agreement that takes both their wants into consideration.
immoral_action: Bill says to his friend that if they won't agree to come to the bar with bill they can just go dancing on their own.
immoral_consequence: Bill's friend feels like bill is really selfish for not considering what they want.

norm: It's not okay to abuse drugs.
situation: Matt had a very difficult childhood and is haunted by it.
intention: Matt wants to feel less pain from his traumatic childhood.
moral_action: Matt starts seeing a psychotherapist weekly.
moral_consequence: Matt starts feeling much better after a few sessions with his therapist.
immoral_action: Matt starts to use heroin as a way to alleviate his moral pain.
immoral_consequence: Matt's life spirals downward rapidly.

norm: It's wrong to act stuck-up and better than somebody else
situation: Stuart is a senior employee interacting with other employees at a corporate event.
intention: Stuart wants to maintain an image.
moral_action: Stuart chats and networks with all other employees.
moral_consequence: Stuart develops a robust professional network.
immoral_action: Stuart brags about himself and avoids speaking to employees he views as inferior.
immoral_consequence: Some of the employees Stuart views as inferior eventually surpass him.

norm: It's mean to purposely hurt people's self esteem.
situation: Mindy is asking John, her husband, to show her how to use the new laptop.
intention: John wants to feel good about himself and smart.
moral_action: John writes some instructions down on paper and gives it to Mindy, saying she'll pick it up in no time.
moral_consequence: Mindy feels John loves her and feels happy and confident in using the laptop.
immoral_action: John says to Mindy he can't understand how she doesn't know how to use it, and she must be dumb.
immoral_consequence: Mindy resents John and feels sad and isn't confident using the laptop.

norm: It's rude to treat someone badly because they are overweight.
situation: Tony's sitting with his daughter whom is overweight, she asks him if she can have some chips.
intention: Tony wants his daughter to achieve a healthy weight.
moral_action: Tony gently tells his daughter he is worried about her weight, but respects her freedom and offers her some chips.
moral_consequence: Tony's daughter eats a couple of chips but thinking about what he said decides to stop and hands them back to him.
immoral_action: Tony tells his daughter that she is too fat and will get even uglier if she keeps eating, so she can't have any chips.
immoral_consequence: Tony's daughter runs to her room and cries and sneaks into the kitchen later and snacks in order to feel better.

norm: You shouldn't criticize your partner's home.
situation: Joel is visiting his boyfriend's small apartment for the first time even though they have been serious for a while.
intention: Joel wants to assess what living together would be like based on the state of his boyfriend's apartment.
moral_action: Joel comments on the fresh flowers and lived-in feel of the place.
moral_consequence: Joel's boyfriend appreciates that Joel noticed the effort he put in.
immoral_action: Joel casually questions why his boyfriend didn't clean up before he came over.
immoral_consequence: Joel's boyfriend is hurt and asks him to leave.

norm: It's honorable to help people involved in a car accident.
situation: Jake is driving down the highway when he sees a car starting on fire and someone waving for help.
intention: Jake wants to help the people.
moral_action: Jake stops and helps the people put out the car fire.
moral_consequence: The fire is put out before it grows huge and the car is saved.
immoral_action: Jake calls the fire department and reports the accident and its location.
immoral_consequence: The fire department arrives too late and the car can't be saved.

norm: It's inappropriate to get involved with your ex's friends.
situation: Andy's friend Scott breaks up with Andrea after they dated for two years.
intention: Andrea wants to have a new boyfriend.
moral_action: Andrea severs ties with Andy despite always seeing him as nice.
moral_consequence: Andrea meets someone new shortly after and is still on good terms with Scott.
immoral_action: Andrea decides that she is interested in Andy and starts to date him shortly after.
immoral_consequence: Scott accuses Andy of being the reason for the break up Andrea and stops being friends with both of them.

norm: You shouldn't distract the guard when entering the office building.
situation: Mario often chats with the guard at his office building, and they will sometimes exchange jokes in the morning.
intention: Mario wants to tell the guard a new joke.
moral_action: Mario tells the guard a short joke before entering the building.
moral_consequence: Mario and the guard have a short laugh before going back to their respective jobs.
immoral_action: Mario tells the guard a really long joke which takes his attention off of his job,.
immoral_consequence: While the guard is listening to Mario's joke, an unauthorized man enters the office building.

norm: You shouldn't kick your girlfriend out of your vehicle.
situation: Ray is driving to the store with his girlfriend when suddenly they get into a heated exchange, and she insults him.
intention: Ray wants to show that he wont tolerate insults.
moral_action: Ray informs his girlfriend that he will not be treated in this manner and refuses to talk with her.
moral_consequence: Ray's girlfriend realizes the error of her ways as they drive along in silence.
immoral_action: Ray stops the car and makes his girlfriend get out and walk.
immoral_consequence: Ray's girlfriend becomes even more angry and the argument intensifies.

norm: It is wrong to shoot at animals just for fun.
situation: Deacon received a rifle for his birthday from his father.
intention: Deacon wants to try out his new rifle.
moral_action: Deacon goes with his father to a gun range and shoots targets.
moral_consequence: Deacon's father is proud of Deacon's shooting ability and takes him out for ice cream afterwards.
immoral_action: Deacon sees his neighbor's cat and shoots and kills it.
immoral_consequence: Deacon's father takes away Deacon's gun and grounds him for a month.

norm: It's good to offer help to a new mother.
situation: George is walking down to the subway when he sees a mother having trouble with her stroller on the steps.
intention: George wants to react to the mother.
moral_action: George offers to carry the stroller down for the mother.
moral_consequence: The mother will be able to get where she is going faster.
immoral_action: George pushes past the mother and walks down into the subway.
immoral_consequence: The mother will become frustrated and have a stressful day.

norm: It's rude to insult the things a person cares about.
situation: Jim's friend loves a TV show that Jim hates, and they ask Jim what he thinks of the show.
intention: Jim wants to answer his friend.
moral_action: Jim says that he's not a fan of the show but that everybody has different tastes in entertainment.
moral_consequence: Jim's friend is glad that even though he doesn't like the show he doesn't judge them for liking it.
immoral_action: Jim tells his friend that the show is pretty dumb and that even children would find it laughable.
immoral_consequence: Jim's friend is offended at what Jim thinks of something they like and their taste in general.

norm: It's rude to discourage others from the job they want.
situation: Basil is talking to Austin and Austin tells him he wants to switch careers and quit his accounting job to pursue becoming an astronaut.
intention: Basil wants to offer advice to Austin regarding the career change.
moral_action: Basil tells Austin that he can do anything he sets his mind to, but he should research everything first before quitting his current job.
moral_consequence: Austin is filled with confidence and inspiration as he feels supported by his friend.
immoral_action: Basil tells Austin that it's too late to try that endeavor and that it's way too far fetched of an idea that will lead to financial ruin.
immoral_consequence: Austin is discouraged and feels silly for bringing it up as his confidence withers away.

norm: It's rude to yell at your sister.
situation: Maggie's sister is playing with Maggie's doll.
intention: Maggie wants to play with her doll.
moral_action: Maggie asks her sister if she can have her doll back when she's done playing with it.
moral_consequence: Maggie's sister tells her she's done with the doll and gives it back to Maggie.
immoral_action: Maggie screams in her sister's face that it is Maggie's doll not hers.
immoral_consequence: Maggie's sister tells their mother Maggie screamed at her and Maggie gets sent to her room.

norm: It's not okay to be overly concerned with your looks.
situation: Cassie has to go to her friend's wedding and is getting dressed.
intention: Cassie wants to look good for the wedding.
moral_action: Cassie puts on her favorite dress and matching shoes that knows look good on her, and gets her hair and makeup done with the bridal party.
moral_consequence: Cassie gets to spend time with her friend and listen to her talk about pre-wedding jitters.
immoral_action: Cassie takes a long time deciding which dress to wear, how to wear her hair, and which angles make her look the best in pictures.
immoral_consequence: Cassie arrives late at the wedding and her friend gets mad at her.

norm: It's bad to drink too much alcohol during a meal.
situation: Mike and his wife Debbie are having dinner at his in-laws, who he doesn't like all that much.
intention: Mike wants to have some wine.
moral_action: Mike enjoys sipping on a glass of Chardonnay and has a good conversation with his in-laws and Debbie.
moral_consequence: Debbie is proud of Mike for being on his best behavior at her parents house and thanks him.
immoral_action: Mike drinks one too many glasses of Chardonnay  and starts slurring his speech and making crude jokes.
immoral_consequence: Debbie is mortified and when they leave she let's Mike know hoe embarrassed and disappointed she is in him.

norm: It's good to pay for your financial obligations.
situation: Randall received his stimulus check from the government, and he owes his cousin twenty dollars.
intention: Randall wants to spend his money.
moral_action: Randall gives his friend his money, and takes his friend out to dinner.
moral_consequence: Randall and his friend grow closer.
immoral_action: Randall spends his stimulus money upgrading his kitchen and bathroom.
immoral_consequence: Randall's friend adds twenty dollars in interest to Randall's loan.

norm: It's good to try your best to help your team.
situation: The bases were loaded, there were two outs, and Nick's team was losing by one point when he was up to bat.
intention: Nick wants the game to be over.
moral_action: Nick swings the bat hard and hits an over the fence home run.
moral_consequence: Nick's hit wins the game and his coach moves him up in the lineup.
immoral_action: Nick watches three good pitches pass by and strikes out on purpose.
immoral_consequence: The coach makes Nick sit on the bench for the next game.

norm: It's bad to worry to much about other peoples' opinions.
situation: Emily has a very overbearing mother, who is always on her about her weight, even though she is fairly skinny.
intention: Emily wants to stay thin.
moral_action: Emily stands up to her mother, realizes her weight is fine, and learns to like the body she has.
moral_consequence: Emily retains her self-esteem and lives a long, healthy life.
immoral_action: Emily hides her eating, starts purging when she eats, and she eventually becomes bulimic.
immoral_consequence: Emily's teeth rot away from the vomiting, and she eventually dies from the stress on her body.

norm: It's bad to be wasteful.
situation: James went to a buffet with hundreds of different foods from dozens of cuisines.
intention: James wants to try dozens of new foods.
moral_action: James takes a small spoonful of everything he wants to try and only gets full portions of what he likes.
moral_consequence: James has so much fun trying different foods that he recommends the buffet to all his friends.
immoral_action: James takes ample servings of many different foods and leaves each plate three-quarters full.
immoral_consequence: The waitstaff eventually ask James to leave the restaurant to control their food costs.

norm: It's not okay to not want to help others.
situation: Bobby is playing a video game when Jennifer calls and asks for help because her car broke down.
intention: Bobby wants to play his video game.
moral_action: Bobby drives out to help Jennifer and then goes back to his video game afterward.
moral_consequence: Jennifer is grateful and helps Bobby out when he needs it.

moral_consequence: The Asian associate carefully checks the stock and gives very good suggestions to Sandy.
immoral_action: Sandy does not talk to the Asian associate thinking that she does not speak English well, and asks another white associate instead.
immoral_consequence: The Asian associate feels embarrassed and bad for being ignored.

norm: It is unhealthy to drink too much alcohol at once.
situation: Ben is out partying in a club with a group of friends.
intention: Ben wants to have a good time.
moral_action: Ben dances while having a few drinks spaced out.
moral_consequence: Ben ends up going home happy.
immoral_action: Ben drinks a 16 shots of vodka during a drinking contest.
immoral_consequence: Ben ends up spending the rest of the night and the next day vomiting.

norm: It is bad to violate workplace and company policies
situation: Jim has a major deadline coming up in the morning, and he needs several more hours to finish it.
intention: Jim wants to complete the assignment before 9:00 PM that evening.
moral_action: Jim stays at the company late and works until he finishes the job.
moral_consequence: Jim goes home tired but happy that he was able to complete the work without having to take his laptop home.
immoral_action: Jim takes his laptop home to work on the assignment, even though it is against company policy to take your laptop home.
immoral_consequence: Jim accidentally damages his laptop at home and is dismissed from his job for breaking company rules.

norm: It's expected to resist any dark thoughts you might have.
situation: Joe spilled coffee on his new suit after being bumped into by a stranger, making him wish suffering upon the stranger.
intention: Joe wants to make the stranger pay for his mistake.
moral_action: Joe explains to the stranger that the suit was brand-new and asks them to cover the dry-cleaning it now requires.
moral_consequence: The stranger apologizes to Joe and agrees to pay for the suit's cleaning.
immoral_action: Joe throws the rest of his coffee into the stranger’s face.
immoral_consequence: Joe gets arrested by the police after burning the stranger’s face with the hot coffee.

norm: It's good to make things for others to enjoy.
situation: Megan places the new fabric she bought at the store next to her sowing machine, and her grandkids need new doll clothes.
intention: Megan wants to create something.
moral_action: Megan uses the fabric to create a wide variety of doll clothes for her grandkids.
moral_consequence: Her grandkids become more popular after showing off their newly dressed dollls.
immoral_action: Megan uses all of the fabric to create a nice sweater for herself.
immoral_consequence: Megan's grandkids are sad that their grandmother didn't make doll clothes for them.

norm: It's fun to have a good time with your buddies.
situation: Lilly is babysitting her little brother when her friends invite her out to eat.
intention: Lilly wants to take care of  her brother.
moral_action: Lilly cooks a big meal in the kitchen and invites her friends over for dinner.
moral_consequence: Lilly cooking skills improve when her friends give her cooking tips as they eat.
immoral_action: Lilly tells her friends that she meet them today as she needs to watch her brother.
immoral_consequence: Lilly misses her friends.

norm: It is good to post things that are not nasty.
situation: Tammy posts often on Facebook.
intention: Tammy wants to make posts that are noticed by many.
moral_action: Tammy  shares uplifiting posts and interesting highlights of her day.
moral_consequence: Tammy has many facebook friends who often like and comment on her posts.
immoral_action: Tammy often makes controversial political statements and verbally attacks people with her posts.
immoral_consequence: Tammy loses a job opportunity with a company when they see her facebook account and have concerns about her character.

norm: It's important to take your pet to the vet.
situation: Mark's dog swallowed a large stone and is coughing up blood all over the house.
intention: Mark wants to stop having to clean up blood in his house.
moral_action: Mark takes his dog to the veterinarian to have the stone removed from the dog's stomach.
moral_consequence: Mark's dog undergoes surgery to have the stone removed and makes a full recovery.
immoral_action: Mark puts his dog on a chain in the yard.
immoral_consequence: Mark's dog continues coughing up blood and then dies overnight.

norm: You are expected to obey all parking rules.
situation: John is downtown and parking is only allowed on the right side of the street on weekdays such as today.
intention: John needs to park his car.
moral_action: John parks on the right side of the street.
moral_consequence: John does not get a ticket.
immoral_action: John parks on the left side of the street.
immoral_consequence: John gets a parking ticket.

norm: You shouldn't injure yourself at work on purpose.
situation: Cody was working on a dangerous part of a construction site.
intention: Cody wanted to go home.
moral_action: Cody asked his boss if he could have the rest of the day off.
moral_consequence: Cody is given the rest of the day off because he volunteers to come in early the next day.
immoral_action: Cody ran into a steel beam on purpose in order to get out of work.
immoral_consequence: Cody was fired immediately for blatantly ignoring the safety regulations on the site.

norm: It’s rude to make noise in a movie theater.
situation: Sandra is watching a movie with her boyfriend in a movie theater filled with other people, but she doesn't understand the plot.
intention: Sandra wants to ask her boyfriend about the plot of the movie.
moral_action: Sandra asks her boyfriend about the plot of the movie in a quiet whisper.
moral_consequence: The other people watching the movie are undisturbed and enjoy watching the movie.
immoral_action: Sandra constantly asks her boyfriend what's going on in the movie in a loud voice.
immoral_consequence: The other people watching the movie are bothered by Sandra being so loud and are distracted from the movie.

norm: You shouldn't cheat at games.
situation: Chad is playing a competitive game of golf with two of his friends.
intention: Chad wants to win the match.
moral_action: Chad focuses as hard as he can on playing well during the round.
moral_consequence: Chad beats his friends by a single stroke and feels very proud of himself.
immoral_action: Chad alters his scorecard to make his final score appear better than he actually performed.
immoral_consequence: Chad's friends discover his deception by double checking his scorecard and call out his cheating.

norm: It is wrong to misrepresent your relationship status to others.
situation: Kim has a partner but ends up meeting someone who is really cool but clearly interested in a relationship.
intention: Kim wants to stay in touch with the new person.
moral_action: Kim lets the guy know that she's taken but wants to be friends.
moral_consequence: Kim feels like a more loyal partner.
immoral_action: Kim leads the guy on and hides the fact that she's not single.
immoral_consequence: Kim feels guilty about lying.

norm: It's important to prioritize work over leisure.
situation: Donald and his friends have tickets to a Wednesday night Zedd concert, and he has a work deadline the next day.
intention: Donald wants to make sure that he gets to go to the concert.
moral_action: Donald stays later at work during the week leading up to the concert.
moral_consequence: Donald gets his work ahead of time and is able to go to the concert worry free.
immoral_action: Donald gets behind on his work and chooses to go to the concert anyway.
immoral_consequence: Donald doesn't get his work done by the deadline and misses out on a bonus as a result.

norm: You should respect others' privacy.
situation: Sue has two kids Mike and Bob which she is taking care of.
intention: Sue wants to raise her kids so that they turn out well.
moral_action: Sue teaches them right from wrong but respects their privacy and gives them a chance to learn things on their own.
moral_consequence: Sue's kids are well adjusted adults who have a good relationship with her.
immoral_action: Sue is a helicopter parent and always gets involved with their life while never letting them make their own decisions.
immoral_consequence: Sue's kids see her as overbearing and hardly ever visit her after they become adults.

norm: You shouldn't threaten to break up with your partner.
situation: John's wife Nancy comes home and tells John that she accidentally broke John's favorite watch.
intention: John wants to respond to the bad news he just heard.
moral_action: John tells Nancy not to worry that things are replaceable and that  he will find a way to get it fixed or get a new one.
moral_consequence: Nancy is relieved that John isn't angry about what she did with the watch and hugs him.
immoral_action: John angrily berates Nancy and tells her that he is so upset he is contemplating filing a divorce.
immoral_consequence: Nancy begins to cry as she feels remorseful and now also insecure about their relationship.

norm: It's important to ask for things you need
situation: Harry's electric bill is due in a week, but he doesn't have enough money to cover it.
intention: Harry wants to seek assistance with paying his bill on time.
moral_action: Harry rings up his parents and asks if he can borrow money to pay his electric bill.
moral_consequence: Harry is able to pay his bill on time, and can eventually pay off his parents, keeping their relationship stable.
immoral_action: Harry takes money from his parents’ bank accounts without consulting them about it to pay his electric bill.
immoral_consequence: Harry's parents lose trust in him and threaten to call the cops if it happens again.

norm: It's wrong to not make time for your family.
situation: Jim started a new business, so he hasn't had enough time to spend with his family.
intention: Jim wants to have a successful business to help support his family.
moral_action: Jim has a healthy work-life balance and spends lots of time with his family.
moral_consequence: Jim's business does well, and his family is happy.
immoral_action: Jim spends all of his time at work and never hangs out with his family.
immoral_consequence: Jim's wife divorces him and takes their kids with her.

norm: It's wrong not to attend parties you were invited to.
situation: John has been invited to a baby shower but also has a report to finish for work.
intention: John wants to decide how to allocate his time that evening.
moral_action: John attends the baby shower and finishes his report when he gets home.
moral_consequence: The party host is happy to see John and enjoys the baby shower.
immoral_action: John stays home and finishes his work without telling the host he can't make it to the baby shower.
immoral_consequence: The party host is sad that John never showed up to the party.

norm: It's wrong to hate trans people.
situation: Zach is out at a nightclub dancing and drinking with a bunch of his friends.
intention: Zach wants to pick up a lady to spend time with later that night.
moral_action: Zach asks his friend to introduce him to a pretty girl that he knows at the club.
moral_consequence: Zach and the girl have a nice conversation and go for waffles after the club closes.
immoral_action: Zach starts talking with an attractive woman who eventually tells him she has a penis.
immoral_consequence: Zach punches the transvestite in the face and is arrested for a hate crime.

norm: It's kind to mourn the loss of human life.
situation: Mike is attending the funeral of his grandfather on a cold morning.
intention: Mike wants to express his feeling.
moral_action: Mike feels grieved and sorrow  because he misses his grandfather so much.
moral_consequence: His relatives come close to Mike and hug him warmly.
immoral_action: Mike thinks that a man should be tough, so he appears to be cool, calm, and collected in front of his relatives.
immoral_consequence: His relatives feel that Mike is apathetic and insensitive.

norm: It's wrong to throw out other people's stuff.
situation: Lisa lives in an apartment with her roommate Beverly.
intention: Lisa wants to clean the apartment.
moral_action: Lisa gathers the personal papers Beverly has left in the living room and puts them in Beverly's room.
moral_consequence: Lisa has a clean apartment and Beverly appreciates Lisa tidying up.
immoral_action: Lisa gathers the personal papers Beverly has left in the living room and puts them in the dumpster.
immoral_consequence: Beverly is upset at Lisa and moves out, leaving Lisa with no roommate.

norm: It's bad to cheat on someone.
situation: Trevor is in a relationship when he meets a new girl he thinks he really likes.
intention: Trevor wants to sleep with the new girl he met.
moral_action: Trevor takes the time to end his current relationship before sleeping with the new girl he met.
moral_consequence: Trevor ends up in a long term relationship with the new girl and is very happy with her.
immoral_action: Trevor sleeps with the new girl he met behind his current partner's back.
immoral_consequence: His partner finds out about his cheating and it ends up ruining his relationships with both his partner and the new girl he met.

norm: It is good to write something you feel confident in.
situation: Jennita has a major paper due at the end of the week for English class.
intention: Jennita wants to write her paper.
moral_action: Jennita writes about her favorite book that she read last year.
moral_consequence: Jennita doesn't need to do much research and finishes the paper easily.
immoral_action: Jennita writes about a completely new subject, phonology, and does a ton of research.
immoral_consequence: Jennita has a very hard time finishing and stresses out about the paper.

norm: You shouldn't make fun of someone for their hair.
situation: Charlie is sitting next to his black friend with dreadlocks Maurice at a party with a group of people.
intention: Charlie wants to entertain the crowd.
moral_action: Charlie tells everyone some ghost stories.
moral_consequence: One of the guests asks if they can include Charlie's story in their upcoming  book.
immoral_action: Charlie makes a joke about Maurice's hair.
immoral_consequence: Charlie's reputation suffers because people assume he's racist.

norm: It's responsible to reuse or recycle old goods.
situation: Bob's garage is filling up with odds and ends to the point where there is almost no room for his car.
intention: Bob wants to get rid of some of his posessions to free up space in the garage.
moral_action: To free up space, Bob sorts through the boxes and contributes useable clothing and toys to a local charity.
moral_consequence: The lives of the underprivileged are made a bit better, and Bob gets good karma.
immoral_action: Bob indescriminately tosses boxes of unused items into a dumpster to free up room in the garage.
