immoral_consequence: The unwanted items end up in a landfill, possibly polluting the environment, and Bob gets bad karma.

norm: It is important to give your children privacy.
situation: Marlene has a teen daughter named Jessie who doesn't talk to her much.
intention: Marlene wants to know what is going on in her daughter's life.
moral_action: Marlene starts a conversation with Jessie over dinner.
moral_consequence: Jessie tells Marlene that she just wants some space.
immoral_action: Marlene sneaks into Jessie's room and reads her diary.
immoral_consequence: Jessie catches Marlene with her diary and doesn't speak to her for months.

norm: It's wrong to read someone's private diary.
situation: Martha has noticed that her daughter Crystal has been acting different lately.
intention: Martha wants to find out what her daughter is up to.
moral_action: Martha thinks about looking in Crystal's diary to see what she's up to but decides to ask her face to face.
moral_consequence: Crystal and her mother have a good talk about what is going on in Crystal's life.
immoral_action: Martha sees Crystal's diary on her desk and reads it to see if she can find out what she's up to.
immoral_consequence: Crystal sees her mother reading her diary and gets upset that she is invading her privacy.

norm: It's wrong to cause someone to get a bad grade.
situation: Sam's friend has an important test the next day that they haven't studied for yet.
intention: Sam wants to go out drinking.
moral_action: Sam leaves his friend to study for his test and finds some other people to go drinking with.
moral_consequence: Sam's friend passes his test the following day and ends up passing the class.
immoral_action: Sam insists that his friend go out drinking with him instead of studying for the test.
immoral_consequence: Sam's friend fails his test and his grades drop as a result.

norm: You shouldn't message a friend of your boyfriend.
situation: Francesca is worried that her boyfriend is starting to love her less than when they started dating.
intention: Francesca wants her boyfriend to pay more attention to her.
moral_action: Francesca decides to be more active and dynamic in her relationship with her boyfriend.
moral_consequence: Francesca's boyfriend loves the way she changed and it gives a new boost to their relationship.
immoral_action: Francesca starts sending flirty texts to her boyfriend's best friend.
immoral_consequence: Francesca's boyfriend learns about the texts and feels like she will leave him, which makes him very sad.

norm: You shouldn't go into someone's closet without their permission.
situation: Jane is getting dressed and doesn't have any more shirts to wear.
intention: Jane wants to find a shirt to wear.
moral_action: Jane asks her sister if she can borrow a shirt from her closet.
moral_consequence: Jane's sister compromises with Jane and lets her have a shirt.
immoral_action: Jane goes into her sister's closet and grabs a shirt.
immoral_consequence: Jane's sister can't find the shirt and gets upset.

norm: It's rude to befriend someone in order to use them.
situation: Jenny notices there is a new student named Anna in her class.
intention: Jenny wants to become her friend.
moral_action: Jenny makes friends with Anna so that they can have good conversations and help each other out.
moral_consequence: Anna enjoys being friends with Jenny and feels welcome in her new town.
immoral_action: Jenny makes friends with Anna just so that she can ride in Anna's nice car.
immoral_consequence: Anna finds out Jenny is only using her for her car, and this makes her sad.

norm: It is not okay to overreact to a breakup.
situation: Jeremy's girlfriend Eva tells him that she wants to start seeing other people, and doesn't want to be with him anymore.
intention: Jeremy wants to express his feelings about the breakup.
moral_action: Jeremy says he's hurt, but he understands, and hopes she finds happiness.
moral_consequence: Jeremy and Eva remain friends, and make a smooth transition into new relationships, and their circle of friends remains in tact.
immoral_action: Jeremy pounds his fist on the table and calls Eva a slut, and then posts a bunch of nasty messages on Facebook calling her a dirty whore.
immoral_consequence: Eva gets scared and stays away from Jeremy, and their friends split into factions to defend their favorite.

norm: It is never acceptable to hit a woman.
situation: Kevin and Missy are having a heated argument and Missy smacks Kevin.
intention: Kevin wants to react to Missy.
moral_action: Kevin is angry he was slapped, so he leaves the house.
moral_consequence: Missy and Kevin are both able to calm down and when Kevin returns they discuss things in a civil manner.
immoral_action: Kevin is angry he was slapped, so he slaps Missy back.
immoral_consequence: Missy falls to the ground from Kevin's force, and she calls the police who arrest him.

norm: It's wrong to talk about personal body functions with others.
situation: Anthony and Rebecca are at the gym together and there's an offensive odor in the air around them.
intention: Anthony wants to lighten the mood about the smell.
moral_action: Anthony laughs and mentions a funny story about a sewer line that broke near his house.
moral_consequence: Rebecca laughs at the story, and she continues her workout beside Anthony.
immoral_action: "Anthony sniffs the air and says ""I'm sure it can't be mine, they're a little frutier"" to try and make Rebecca laugh."
immoral_consequence: Rebecca is repulsed by the comment and steps away from Anthony, ignoring him for the rest of her workout.

norm: It's wrong to marry more than 2 women.
situation: Brigham is a married man twice over and is courting yet another woman.
intention: Brigham wants to be with the third woman.
moral_action: Brigham does some self reflection and ends his first two marriages so that he can be monogamous with the third woman.
moral_consequence: Brigham lives a normal life going forward having just one wife.
immoral_action: Brigham marries the third woman bringing his total number of wives to three.
immoral_consequence: Brigham's local community decides they cannot continue to put up with him marrying so many woman and exiles him.

norm: You shouldn't use the word retarded as an insult.
situation: Barry watches his friend clown around with his other friends, and he laughs hysterically.
intention: Barry wants to say something in the spirit of the moment.
moral_action: Barry tells his friend that he loves it when they all get together and laugh like that, it's his favorite part of life.
moral_consequence: His friends agree with him that the moments where they all get together and laugh are the best of times, and everyone feels great.
immoral_action: Barry jokingly calls his friend retarded for acting in such a silly manner.
immoral_consequence: One of Barry's friends is insulted by the comment, because he has a family member who is retarded and does not see it as a joke.

norm: It's important to let people rest when they're sick
situation: Mandy owns a business and one of her employees has contracted COVID.
intention: Mandy wants the business to continue.
moral_action: Mandy sends the person with COVID home to rest for a couple weeks.
moral_consequence: The rest of the office employees are fine, and business is largely unaffected.
immoral_action: Mandy makes the person come in while sick with COVID.
immoral_consequence: Most of the office comes down with COVID, and one of them dies.

norm: You shouldn't misbehave at someone's wedding.
situation: Samuel is at his brother's wedding where there is an open bar.
intention: Samuel wants to have a few drinks.
moral_action: Samuel limits himself to three drinks.
moral_consequence: Samuel has a good time at his brother's wedding.
immoral_action: Samuel drinks to the point that he feels sick.
immoral_consequence: Samuel vomits in the middle of the reception hall.

norm: You shouldn't give people nosebleeds.
situation: Nelson was annoyed by the other kids in school mocking them.
intention: Nelson wanted to make the other kids stop mocking him.
moral_action: Nelson simply decides to ignore the mocking kids completely and pay no attention at all.
moral_consequence: Eventually they stop mocking Nelson when they find something new to mock.
immoral_action: Nelson punches the mockers in the nose and gives then nosebleeds.
immoral_consequence: Sure enough they stop mocking him out of fear of another punch.

norm: It's good to stand up for your rights.
situation: Mark is getting ready to grocery shop when a manager tells him that blacks cannot shop here.
intention: Mark needs to buy groceries.
moral_action: Mark calls the police, and they arrest the manager and Mark is able to shop.
moral_consequence: Mark stops the racist manager.
immoral_action: Mark leaves and finds another grocery store.
immoral_consequence: The manager continues being racist.

norm: It's good to ask your parents for help.
situation: Zach is struggling with some homework and has been taking a long time to do it.
intention: Zach wants to ask someone to help him.
moral_action: Zach goes into his parents room and asks them for help with the homework.
moral_consequence: Zach's parents do a great job of explaining everything, and he gets a great grade on his work.
immoral_action: Zach goes online and posts on Reddit, requesting help with his homework.
immoral_consequence: Zach is given terrible advice by many random people and ends up getting a terrible grade.

norm: It's good to get into a relationship.
situation: Chris is in love with his coworker Maggie, but his job states that two people working in the same department can not be in a relationship.
intention: Chris wants to make a decision about his relationship with Maggie.
moral_action: Chris decides to transfer to another department, so he can get into a relationship with Maggie.
moral_consequence: Chris and Maggie spent three years together before becoming married.
immoral_action: Chris decides not to act on his feelings to focus on his job.
immoral_consequence: Maggie and Chris become distant from each other.

norm: It's good to take your partner to a nice restaurant.
situation: Samantha met a new girl named Alex and asked her out on a date.
intention: Samantha wants to take Alex out to dinner.
moral_action: Samantha takes Alex to an exquisite five star restaurant.
moral_consequence: Alex is quite impressed with Samantha's taste in cuisine and asks for a second date.
immoral_action: Samantha takes Alex to McDonald's for dinner.
immoral_consequence: Alex isn't very impressed and excused herself from the date shortly after finishing her meal.

norm: You shouldn't ruin people.
situation: Jerry is a powerful owner of a football team and one of his players Dion has been acting egotistical and crazy lately.
intention: Jerry wants to sever ties with Dion.
moral_action: Jerry tells Dion that he's being released and that he's free to sign with someone else.
moral_consequence: Dion is happy to get a fresh start and is excited to start looking for a new team to play for.
immoral_action: Jerry tells Dion that he's being released and that he's called the other teams and made sure he'll never play football again.
immoral_consequence: Dion is devastated especially because Jerry has made sure he has no prospects in football any more.

norm: It's not okay to be rude to your parents.
situation: Karen is visiting her parents for the weekend.
intention: Karen wants to introduce her parents to her new boyfriend.
moral_action: Karen and her boyfriend share some laughter with her parents, and she is loving and friendly.
moral_consequence: Everyone is glad they met and all think positively of each other.
immoral_action: Karen is rude to her parents for telling bad jokes and tells them she is embarrassed of them.
immoral_consequence: Karen’s parents are hurt and feel like their daughter is treating them poorly.

norm: It's wrong to not wear your wedding ring.
situation: Abe is going out to a wine bar for drinks with his coworkers after work.
intention: Abe wants to meet someone.
moral_action: Abe starts a conversation with a man at the next table.
moral_consequence: Abe makes a new friend when he finds out the man has similar interests.
immoral_action: Abe removes his wedding ring when he enters the wine bar.
immoral_consequence: Abe is called out by one of his coworkers for trying to appear single.

norm: It's not okay to deny yourself the things you need.
situation: Louie has a son that he is raising but does not have a lot of money.
intention: Louie wants to choose how to use his money.
moral_action: Louie buys food for both he and his son.
moral_consequence: Louie will be able to continue functioning to take care of his son.
immoral_action: Louie only buys food for his son.
immoral_consequence: Louie will become hungry and not be able to take care of his son.

norm: It is wrong to do anything that hurts your wife.
situation: Danny and his wife Diane invited their friends over for the night.
intention: Danny wants to entertain his friends.
moral_action: Danny suggests that they play a fun card game.
moral_consequence: Diane and Danny snuggle in bed after the party, and start planning their next party.
immoral_action: Danny pranks Diane in front of their friends.
immoral_consequence: Diane is humiliated and snaps at Dan which makes their friend's uncomfortable.

norm: It's inconsiderate to leave your waste in a public toilet.
situation: Mark is shopping at the grocery store, and he stops to use the toilet, but afterward he finds that the toilet will not flush.
intention: Mark wants to leave the restroom and continue shopping.
moral_action: Mark holds the toilet handle down for a few minutes until the toilet flushes.
moral_consequence: The janitor who cleans the restroom will not have a difficult time cleaning up at the end of the day.
immoral_action: Mark leaves his waste in the toilet and leaves the bathroom to continue his shopping.
immoral_consequence: The janitor who cleans the restroom will have to deal with waste that has been sitting in the toilet.

norm: It's mean to not take depression seriously.
situation: James college roommate confessed that he'd been too depressed to get out of bed or go to class for the last two weeks.
intention: James wants to help his friend.
moral_action: James tells his roommate that must be really hard, and asks if he's tried talking to a psychiatrist.
moral_consequence: James' roommate agrees to let James call a psychiatrist near campus and schedule him an appointment.
immoral_action: James tries to make a joke about how having depression is at least better than having herpes.
immoral_consequence: James' rooommate is not amused and doesn't confide in him again.

norm: It's good for children to show their parents respect.
situation: Niles has lots of schoolwork to get through today and his dad comes in.
intention: Niles wants to get back to his schoolwork.
moral_action: Niles tells his dad that he's busy with schoolwork today.
moral_consequence: Niles dad takes one look at the schoolwork and decides to leave him alone.
immoral_action: Niles tells his dad to leave the room, so he can finish the schoolwork.
immoral_consequence: Niles gets grounded for the rudeness to his father.

norm: It's nice to stay connected to your friends.
situation: Cindy recently had a death in the family and needs time to be alone but receives a voice message from her friend Karen.
intention: Cindy wants to spend time with herself to heal for a month.
moral_action: Cindy calls Karen and tells her she need a month of alone time.
moral_consequence: Karen waits for Cindy to contact her in the future and wants to be there for her when she needs it.
immoral_action: Cindy ignores Karen's call for a month.
immoral_consequence: Karen feels Cindy no longer wants to be friends and decides not to be a friend anymore.

norm: It's rude to borrow things without asking
situation: Anne notices a top that she really likes in her sister's closet.
intention: Anne wants to wear the top out on a date.
moral_action: Anne asks her sister ahead of time if she can borrow the top for a night.
moral_consequence: Anne's sister is pleased because she can borrow something in return.
immoral_action: Anne takes the top without asking and wears it while going out with the intention of returning it.
immoral_consequence: Anne's sister cannot find the top when she goes to wear it herself.

norm: It's bad to bother other people.
situation: Hayden's sister is studying for her exam in bedroom next to his.
intention: Hayden wants to listen to music.
moral_action: Hayden adjusts his speaker to a quiet level.
moral_consequence: Hayden's sister is unaffected by the music.
immoral_action: Hayden turns his speaker up to full volume.
immoral_consequence: Hayden's sister can't study because the music is too loud.

norm: It's good to celebrate with your friends.
situation: Blane's friend Giovanni won a million dollars on a game show, and he's throwing a party.
intention: Blane wants to decide to go to the party or not.
moral_action: Blane goes to the party to celebrate with his friend.
moral_consequence: Blane has a blast at the party with his friend.
immoral_action: Blane is envious of Giovanni for winning the money, so he stays home.
immoral_consequence: Blane misses out on the party and is bored and angry at home.

norm: It's good to cut yourself out of drama at work.
situation: Tom recently was hired at a new job.
intention: Tom wants to network and make work friends.
moral_action: Tom is asked how he feels about another coworker and says he'd prefer to stay out of the conversation.
moral_consequence: Tom gains the respect of his coworkers and is looked at favorably.
immoral_action: Tom overhears some gossip and spreads it to others, thinking it will make him look favorable.
immoral_consequence: Tom's coworkers decide he isn't trustworthy and keep him out of conversations.

norm: It is rude to complain about waiting.
situation: A bored Rachael has been waiting for her food at a restaurant for twenty minutes.
intention: Rachael wants to get rid of her boredom.
moral_action: Rachael plays games on her cellphone until her food arrives.
moral_consequence: Rachael receives a free desert for her  long wait time.
immoral_action: Rachael passes time by making comments about the wait time to the person sitting near her.
immoral_consequence: Rachael feels bad when she notices a waitress crying after walking by her table.

norm: It's bad to create unpleasant living conditions for your partner.
situation: Thomas has just moved in with his girlfriend Gina but Thomas hates doing housework.
intention: Thomas wants to avoid doing housework.
moral_action: Thomas hires a housekeeper to take care of most of the chores, so he and Gina can focus on other things.
moral_consequence: Thomas and Gina do minimal housework and can spend more time together.
immoral_action: Thomas does not do any of the housework and lets Gina take care of everything since she has higher standards of cleanliness.
immoral_consequence: Gina grows tired of having to do all the chores and breaks up with Thomas because they are not equal partners.

norm: It is good to let people know of game glitches.
situation: Jim is a game tester at a major game developer and toward the end of his work day found a glitch in the game he is testing.
intention: Jim wants to go home.
moral_action: Jim reports the glitch to the system before he leaves for home.
moral_consequence: The game ships with the glitch fixed and is a great success.
immoral_action: Jim doesn't spend the time reporting the glitch before going home.
immoral_consequence: The game ships with the glitch and costs the company lots of money to send out a patch.

norm: It is friendly to show a smile to someone.
situation: Nick is meeting Kara for the first time at the library.
intention: Nick wants to make a memorable first impression on Kara.
moral_action: Nick greets Kara with a warm smile and a hand shake.
moral_consequence: Kara likes how friendly Nick is and has a conversation with him.
immoral_action: Nick starts scowling after he introduces himself to Kara.
immoral_consequence: Kara becomes confused by Nick's weird behavior and leaves the library.

norm: You shouldn't be too busy for your family.
situation: Nakima's boss asks him to stay at his current location for another week, and his family waits for him at home.
intention: Nakima wants to avoid offending his boss.
moral_action: Nakima demonstrates his skills to his boss explaining that he can work from home.
moral_consequence: Nakima's explanations impress his boss, and he receives a promotion.
immoral_action: Nakima stays the extra week without contacting his family.
immoral_consequence: Nakima returns home to an empty house as his family went on vacation without him.

norm: It is rude to ignore other people.
situation: Paul is watching TV when his son Max walks in and starts asking a million annoying questions.
intention: Paul wants to get Max to stop talking.
moral_action: Paul tells Max that he needs to go upstairs and read an encyclopedia which will have all the answers.
moral_consequence: Max gets intrigued by the encyclopedia and runs upstairs to try to see what that is.
immoral_action: Paul decides to pretend not to hear Max and continues watching the game as if Max isn't there.
immoral_consequence: Max is annoyed he's not getting attention from Paul causing him to get even louder and more obnoxious.

norm: It's expected that people will finish what they start.
situation: Sam just bought a new house that needs work.
intention: Sam wants to fix the porch steps.
moral_action: Sam finishes the steps and paints them to compliment his home.
moral_consequence: His neighbors stop by to congratulate Sam on fixing up the place.
immoral_action: Sam gets bored and decides to leave the steps with loose boards.
immoral_consequence: The mailman falls on the steps and sues Sam.

norm: It's kind to cook for your partner.
situation: Tom lives with his girlfriend and doesn't have the money for take-out, but does have raw food material.
intention: Mark wants to prepare dinner.
moral_action: Mark cooks food for himself and his girlfriend, and they eat it.
moral_consequence: Mark's girlfriend hugs Mark, and they both have a wonderful dinner.
immoral_action: Mark cooks food only for himself, and eats it.
immoral_consequence: Mark's girlfriend calls Mark selfish and Mark feels humiliated.

norm: It's vicious to bully someone.
situation: Bill's parents are very tough on him and criticize him all the time, which makes him feel powerless.
intention: Bill wants to feel strong and dominant.
moral_action: Bill notices the shy kid and decides to take him under his wing.
moral_consequence: The shy kid feels protected and school becomes more fun for him.
immoral_action: Bill bullies a shy kid at school.
immoral_consequence: The shy kid feels terrible and starts hating school.

norm: You should be honest with your family.
situation: Jon has been struggling in school because he has been drinking with friends and his family is worried.
intention: Jon wants to avoid getting in trouble.
moral_action: Jon tells his family that he can do much better and vows to do so avoiding mentioning the reason why.
moral_consequence: Jon stays honest and doesn't let himself off the hook.
immoral_action: Jon tells his family that his school troubles are due to unfair teachers, and that he is doing his best.
immoral_consequence: Jon is encouraged to keep up his irresponsible behavior.

norm: You should report a neighbor that is breaking the law.
situation: Steve notices that his neighbor Chet seems to be selling drugs out of his house to all sorts of strange people.
intention: Steve wants Chet to stop selling drugs.
moral_action: Steve calls the police and reports Chet's illegal drug activity.
moral_consequence: Chet is arrested and sentenced to jail for selling drugs and the neighborhood returns to normal.
immoral_action: Steve knocks on Chet's door and asks him to stop selling drugs.
immoral_consequence: Chet threatens Steve, tells him to get lost and continues to sell drugs.

norm: It's good to be interested in your family's interests.
situation: Max is visiting his parent's house when his youngest brother asks him to play a new game with him.
intention: Max wants to respond to his brother's question.
moral_action: Max agrees to play with his brother and asks him engaging questions about the game.
moral_consequence: The younger brother is happy to explain the game further to Max.
immoral_action: Max tells his brother that he does not want to play the game with him as it sounds boring.
immoral_consequence: The younger brother quietly says okay and leaves the room upset.

norm: It's dangerous to mislead people on the internet.
situation: Jake has been talking to a girl online and has developed a crush on her.
intention: Jake wants to impress the girl.
moral_action: Jake listens to the girl and finds ways to show that he understands and respects her.
moral_consequence: Jake's relationship with the girl is able to develop.
immoral_action: Jake uses someone else's pictures and tells the girl that he has a high-paying job even though he doesn't.
immoral_consequence: Jake is unable to ever come clean to the girl and their relationship cannot go anywhere because Jake needs to cover his tracks.

norm: You shouldn't attend someone's party if you aren't welcome there.
situation: Gabe heard that Shelly was having a party, but he wasn't invited.
intention: Gabe wants to go out and have fun.
moral_action: Gabe meets up with some of his friends to go to the bar.
moral_consequence: Gabe has a great time having a few drinks with his friends.
immoral_action: Gabe gets dressed and drives over the Shelly's party at her house.
immoral_consequence: Shelly tells her friends to throw Gabe out of the party.

norm: It is bad when something makes a kid cry.
situation: Dagon wants to do something for Halloween, but his little clownphobic little brother is in the room.
intention: Dagon wants to have fun.
moral_action: Dagon reads some ghost stories stories about historical landmarks.
moral_consequence: The historical information his brother learns helps him pass his upcoming history test.
immoral_action: Dagon watches the movie It.
immoral_consequence: His brother has a major meltdown.

norm: It's rude to sing loudly over other people's objections.
situation: Mary has helped organize a protest at her college about the prevalent rape culture on campus.
intention: Mary wants the college president to acknowledge their efforts.
moral_action: When the president opens dialogue with the protesters Mary agrees to sit and talk to him.
moral_consequence: Mary is able to get the president to agree to meaningful changes.
immoral_action: When the president attempts to address the protesters Mary encourages the students to sing loudly to disrupt him.
immoral_consequence: Mary fails to influence the president to their cause.

norm: It's bad behavior to lock kids in their bedroom.
situation: Tina's son has refused to finish an important homework assignment in order to play a video game.
intention: Tina wants to discipline her child.
moral_action: Tina takes away her sons gaming console.
moral_consequence: Tina's son finishes the homework in order to keep playing.
immoral_action: Tina locks her son in his bedroom away from the video game.
immoral_consequence: Tina's son thinks his mom is going overboard.

norm: It's mean to ruin your friend's vacation plans.
situation: Chelsea was planning on going on vacation when Kelly called her.
intention: Kelly wants Chelsea to come to her party.
moral_action: Kelly reschedules her party so that Chelsea would be able to attend.
moral_consequence: Chelsea has a great time at both the party and on vacation.
immoral_action: Kelly calls the traveling agency to cancel Chelsea's vacation plans.
immoral_consequence: Chelsea isn't able to board the plane even though she paid for the trip.

norm: It's good to have a friendly competition.
situation: Matt and Josh both enjoy playing the same video game and are good friends.
intention: Matt wants to get better at the game.
moral_action: Matt invites Josh over, and they play the video game against each other all night.
moral_consequence: Matt has a great time hanging out with his friend Josh.
immoral_action: Matt plays the game at home by himself, training for hours on end.
immoral_consequence: Matt's social life suffers because he spends so much time by himself.

norm: You shouldn't call someone fat.
situation: Jerry is at the ballpark with his friends.
intention: He wants to sit and enjoy the game with the crowd.
moral_action: John notices the fan next to him is obese but minds his own business.
moral_consequence: Everyone has a good time and enjoys the game together.
immoral_action: Jerry calls a fan sitting next to him fat when they order a plate of food.
immoral_consequence: The fan and John gets into a argument and John hurts his feelings.

norm: It's mean to make fun of someone wearing a wig.
situation: Billy is at the mall with a friend and notices a stranger with a wig that looks really obvious.
intention: Billy wants his friend to see the wig.
moral_action: Billy quietly points out the wig to his friend commenting that it takes some bravery to choose to wear a wig like that.
moral_consequence: Billy and his friend shrug it off and continue about their day.
immoral_action: Billy makes a commotion while getting his friend's attention about the wig while laughing which draws the attention of the wig wearer.
immoral_consequence: The stranger in the wig yells at Billy for being so insensitive and explains that they have cancer.

norm: It's not okay to not make yourself look presentable.
situation: Ginny, a real estate agent, is out for a jog when she gets a call from a client.
intention: Ginny wants to take the client to see a house they are interested in.
moral_action: Ginny ends her jog early and goes home to take a shower before meeting with her clients.
moral_consequence: The clients are happy with Ginny and Ginny eventually gets the sale.
immoral_action: Ginny goes straight from her jog to meet the new clients even though she looks sweaty and disheveled.
immoral_consequence: The clients are disgusted with Ginny's appearance and decide to find a new realtor.

norm: It's frowned upon to lie to family.
situation: Abe is invited to a family gathering, but is very tired.
intention: Abe wants to get out of going to the gathering.
moral_action: Abe tells his family that he's exhausted and will come next time.
moral_consequence: His family understands and saves him some food to eat.
immoral_action: Abe makes up a story about how he broke his leg and can't come.
immoral_consequence: A family member sees Abe walking the next day and calls him out on his lie.

norm: You shouldn't abandon your child's pet.
situation: Deb has a son that she bought a dog for, and he can't take care of the dog because he's a toddler.
intention: Deb wants to figure out what to do with the dog.
moral_action: Deb decides to take care of the dog and teach her toddler what to do, so he can care for it when he grows up.
moral_consequence: The dog will be cared for and have a home to live in.
immoral_action: Deb decides to leave the dog out on the street by itself.
immoral_consequence: The dog will not be able to take care of itself on the streets.

norm: It's fun to go out dancing.
situation: Tiffany and her friends have the weekend off.
intention: Tiffany wants to find an activity to do.
moral_action: Tiffany and her friends decide to go to a club and dance.
moral_consequence: Tiffany and her friends experience positive emotions.
immoral_action: Tiffany and her friends decide to stay in and watch re-runs on TV.
immoral_consequence: Tiffany and her friends experience mundane emotions.

norm: It is bad to yell at your mother
situation: James was upset with his mother because she embarrassed him.
intention: James wants his mother to understand that he's upset.
moral_action: James explains that his mother embarrassed him with people important to him.
moral_consequence: His mother apologizes and they hug afterwards.
immoral_action: James speaks an angry stream of profanity at his mother.
immoral_consequence: His mother just starts the same thing back at him.

norm: It's wrong to sleep with your friend's parent.
situation: Diego and his friend Thom are both drinking whiskey with his mom, Monica, who begins to flirt with Thom, and Diego feels uneasy.
intention: Thom wants to react to Monica's advances.
moral_action: Thom decides to ignore Monica's flirting and asks Diego to go outside to hang out instead.
moral_consequence: Diego is happy that his friend didn't betray their friendship, but remains angry with Monica.
immoral_action: Thom flirts back with Monica who then invites him into her bedroom where they have sex.
immoral_consequence: Diego is angry at both Thom and Monica because he feels weird about the whole thing.

norm: You shouldn't be around people that are perverts.
situation: Jack and his friend Hoffner are standing in the park watching the female joggers run by.
intention: Jack wants to make his friend Hoffner laugh.
moral_action: Jack makes jokes at the jogging ladies and mentions flashing one of the women but Hoffner laughs at Jack and tells him it's time to go.
moral_consequence: Jack and Hoffner leave the park and go back to Jack's house to watch a movie.
immoral_action: Jack starts making jokes at the female joggers and ends up flashing his penis at one causing Hoffner to laugh with Jack.
immoral_consequence: A lady calls the cops on Jack and Hoffner is taken to the police station as well for being present.

norm: Giving a friend some good advice is very polite.
situation: Yang asked Iris for some advice regarding a tricky puzzle.
intention: Iris wants to decide to help Yang or not.
moral_action: Iris decides to give Yang a hint on the puzzle to help him out.
moral_consequence: With her advice Yang figures out the next piece of the puzzle.
immoral_action: Iris decides not to help him because it would make the puzzle less fun.
immoral_consequence: Yang remains stuck on the same tricky puzzle for a while.

norm: It's bad to open other people's mail.
situation: Greg lives with his partner, Kelly, who has received a letter which is in a strange looking envelope.
intention: Greg wants to know what is in the envelope.
moral_action: Greg waits for his partner to get home and for her to open it then asks her what was inside.
moral_consequence: Greg's partner is excited to share with him the good news she got in the mail.
immoral_action: Greg gives into his curiosity and proceeds to open the envelope.
immoral_consequence: Greg's partner later finds out and considers this an invasion of privacy.

norm: It's wrong to throw away someone's clothes without their permission.
situation: Karen doesn't like it when her husband Alex saves old clothes that don't fit him anymore.
intention: Karen wants to clean out their bedroom closet.
moral_action: Karen asks Alex if she can throw out any of his clothes that don't fit because she wants to clean out their closet.
moral_consequence: Alex tells Karen he will help her clean out the closet and go through all his old clothes.
immoral_action: Karen cleans out their closet and throws away Alex's clothes that she knows won't fit him.
immoral_consequence: Alex sees Karen tossing his clothes in the trash and tells her that she had no right to do that.

norm: You shouldn't feed babies to your partner.
situation: Amber's partner Jacob is coming over to meet her for dinner, she hasn't told him that she had a son.
intention: Amber wants to conceal her son from Jacob.
moral_action: Amber leaves her son at a daycare and doesn't pick him up in the evening.
moral_consequence: Jacob comes over for dinner and is charmed by Amber's kindness, promising to visit again.
immoral_action: Amber cooks and prepares her son as a meal for dinner, giving her Jacob a full plate.
immoral_consequence: Jacob notices blood spatter in the kitchen and that the meal tastes off, then reports Amber to the police for unusual behavior.

norm: It's impolite not to respect people's privacy.
situation: Marie is supposed to work on a project with the new employee Sandra, and Sandra leaves the window of her Facebook open on her computer.
intention: Marie wants to know more about Sandra.
moral_action: Marie asks Sandra questions about herself while they work and invites her to hang out at a more relaxed location.
moral_consequence: Marie forms a relationship with Sandra.
immoral_action: Marie searches on Sandra's Facebook reading her messages along with other things on her page.
immoral_consequence: Sandra discovers Marie, and she asks for Marie to not work on the project.

norm: You shouldn't take advantage of homeless people.
situation: James lived in an area of San Francisco known for its homelessness problem and sky-high rents.
intention: James wants to make some extra money to help pay his rent.
moral_action: James starts working a second part-time job at a charity that helps the homeless.
moral_consequence: James appreciates both the extra income and how much worse his life could be.
immoral_action: James starts organizing bum fights, videotaping them and selling access on the Internet.
immoral_consequence: James is widely deplored on social media, but successfully conceals his real identity.

norm: It is bad to pick on children
situation: John just lost his job and is at home with his kids who are watching tv.
intention: John wants to feel powerful.
moral_action: John takes a breath and goes to lift weights in his home gym.
moral_consequence: John's kids still like their dad and don't feel depressed at all.
immoral_action: John tells his kids to turn off the tv in a raised voice, and they are grounded for a week.
immoral_consequence: John's kids resent him and feel depressed and very sad.

norm: It is good to wash your hands occasionally
situation: Michael has grown increasingly nervous about the spread of coronavirus in his city.
intention: Michael wants to avoid contracting coronavirus.
moral_action: Michael always wears a mask and washes his hands regularly.
moral_consequence: Michael avoids contracting the coronavirus.
immoral_action: Even though always follows masking protocols, Michael often forgets to wash his hands after going shopping.
immoral_consequence: A few days after shopping, Michael starts to feel ill and tests positive for coronavirus.

norm: It's good to help coworkers do their job correctly.
situation: Tilly is a manager at a corporation.
intention: Tilly wants to give information to the new employees.
moral_action: Tilly sets up a comprehensive training program for the new employees.
moral_consequence: The new employees become efficient at their jobs.
immoral_action: Tilly gives vague suggestions to the new employees.
immoral_consequence: The new employees struggle doing the job and feel lost.

norm: You shouldn't buy someone fake jewelry.
situation: Peter is shopping for an engagement ring for his girlfriend, Sue.
intention: Peter wants to give Sue an engagement ring.
moral_action: Peter gets a ring with a real diamond, even though he has to save up longer for it.
moral_consequence: Sue loves the ring, and she agrees to marry him.
immoral_action: To save money, Peter gets a ring with a fake diamond instead of a real one.
immoral_consequence: Sue finds out the diamond is fake and breaks up with him because of the deception.

norm: It's not okay to deceive others.
situation: Phil is out shopping when a customer stops him and asks if a $100 bill they found on the floor belongs to Phil, which it doesn't.
intention: Phil needs to decide how to respond.
moral_action: Phil says the bill is not his and offers to help find the person it belongs to.
moral_consequence: The person the bill belongs to thanks Phil for helping him find his lost money.
immoral_action: Phil thanks the customer for finding his lost money and pockets it.
immoral_consequence: The person who actually owned the 100$ is standing right behind Phil and yells at him.

norm: It's good to follow advice.
situation: Lana is bored and has free time.
intention: Lana wants to learn to ski.
moral_action: Lana signs up for ski lessons.
moral_consequence: Lana has a great time and becomes a proficient skier.
immoral_action: Lana refuses to take lessons and goes down a slope for advanced skiers.
immoral_consequence: Lana falls and breaks her leg badly.

norm: You shouldn't chat about non-business-related things during a business meeting.
situation: Tom sees his friend and colleague, William, at a weekly sales meeting and decides to sit next to him.
intention: Tom wants to find out what William will be doing during the upcoming weekend.
moral_action: Tom takes care of business at the meeting and waits until after it is adjourned to talk with his friend about social issues.
moral_consequence: The meeting is productive and Tom is able to plan a nice weekend event with his friend, without sacrificing his work ethic.
immoral_action: Tom ignores the meeting agenda, and the other participants, and starts talking with his friend about possibly having a bar-b-que over the weekend.
immoral_consequence: The other meeting participants become visibly annoyed with the chatter and Tom is embarrassed.

norm: You shouldn't cut your arm.
situation: Doug just learned that his best friend died in a plane crash and is devastated.
intention: Doug wants to feel something, anything but numb.
moral_action: Doug calls a therapist hotline to talk about his sadness/numbness.
moral_consequence: Doug learns how to feel better slowly and is happier.
immoral_action: Doug takes a knife and cuts his arms up.
immoral_consequence: Doug bleeds profusely and has to be rushed to the hospital.

norm: It's bad to judge other people based on their sins.
situation: Mark and Bill are talking when Mark admits that he has killed someone in the past.
intention: Bill wants to respond to Mark's admission.
moral_action: Bill tells Mark that we all make mistakes and that he's sure there was a reason why Mark acted the way he did but that it's all over now.
moral_consequence: Mark feel supported by his friend and thanks Bill for being kind.
immoral_action: Bill tells Mark that he is a horrible human being for taking someone's life and hopes he never sees Mark again.
immoral_consequence: Mark is embarrassed by being called out and begins to cry and relive all the awful feelings from the murder incident.

norm: You shouldn't get your friends fired.
situation: John is having dinner at a restaurant where his friend Mary is a waitress.
intention: John wants to have some dessert.
moral_action: John orders a dessert.
moral_consequence: Mary receives a larger tip on the order since the dessert increased the price of the meal.
immoral_action: John pesters Mary to bring him a free dessert, which she reluctantly does.
immoral_consequence: Mary's boss notices what she did and fires her.

norm: It's good to compromise when you're in a relationship.
situation: Bob is discussing with his wife about how to spend their Saturday afternoon, going to the park, or to the museum?
intention: Bob wants to go to the museum.
moral_action: Bob comes to an agreement with his wife that they will do both the park and the museum.
moral_consequence: Bob's wife is happy to go to the museum and even enjoys the park.
immoral_action: Bob talks over his wife, and badgers her until she agrees to do what he wants.
immoral_consequence: Bob's wife is frustrated for the whole afternoon.

norm: You shouldn't call an older cat a kitten.
situation: Nick's cousin Sam has a very fat cat named Macho and is playing with it.
intention: Nick wants to get the cat's attention.
moral_action: "Nick tells Macho, ""Come here Macho, you big beastly cat""."
moral_consequence: Sam laughs and starts playing with the fat Macho.
immoral_action: "Nick tells Macho, ""Here little kitten, here little kitten...""."
immoral_consequence: "Sam gets confused and calls Nick an idiot for calling such a fat cat a ""kitten""."

norm: It's wrong for a student to harass a teacher.
situation: Marie is not doing well in class and may end up failing.
intention: Marie would like to get better grades.
moral_action: Marie tells her teacher that she is having a hard time understanding the material.
moral_consequence: Marie's teacher offers her extra help after class, and Marie's grades improve.
immoral_action: Marie threatens her teacher with violence if she is not given a good grade.
immoral_consequence: Marie is reported to the principal and expelled from school.

norm: It's good to make plans for someone's birthday.
situation: Rodrigo's father's birthday is coming up.
intention: Rodrigo wants to celebrate his fathers birthday with him.
moral_action: Rodrigo decides to make reservations for dinner and take his father out to eat.
moral_consequence: Rodrigo and his father have a great time at dinner.
immoral_action: Rodrigo puts off making plans until the day of, and tries to find a place to eat at the last minute.
immoral_consequence: Rodrigo is unable to find a restaurant with room for them and his father is very sad because they don't get to go out.

norm: It is rude to let down your friends
situation: Tony promised his friends he'd finish his part of the presentation they have tomorrow this evening but sees a movie on tv he likes.
intention: Tony wants to watch the movie tonight instead of working.
moral_action: Tony puts the movie on record, finishes his presentation work, then finishes watching it.
moral_consequence: The presentation is a success and Tony's friends are happy.
immoral_action: Tony turns on the film and watches all night long and goes to sleep.
immoral_consequence: The next day the presentation goes badly as Tony didn't prepare and his friends are upset with him.

norm: You should respect your leaders.
situation: Jim is the head of a project group that Ken is working in and has made a new change to the rules.
intention: Ken wants to ask about the rules.
moral_action: Ken approaches Jim about the rules he has questions about and works to seek compromise.
moral_consequence: Jim tells Ken that he will take his suggestions into consideration and thanks him for his honesty and good attitude.
immoral_action: Ken tells Jim that he thinks the rules are way out of line and don't make much sense.
immoral_consequence: Jim finds the tone and statements expressed by Ken to be harsh and unprofessional and no longer considers him for an upcoming promotion.

norm: It is positive to attempt to quit smoking
situation: Amy's doctor told her that she needs to quit smoking, or she'll develop serious health issues.
intention: Amy wants live long enough to play with her grandchildren.
moral_action: Amy decides to take an unproven supplement that claims to counteract the negative effects of smoking.
moral_consequence: The supplement doesn't work and Amy dies from emphysema before her first grandchild is born leaving them without a grandmother.
immoral_action: Amy enters a smoking cessation program and is able to stop smoking cigarettes.
immoral_consequence: Amy lives to be 100 years old and her grandchildren love her immensely.

norm: You shouldn't have an aggressive animal.
situation: Sally is looking at dogs at an animal shelter.
intention: Sally wants to adopt a pet.
moral_action: Sally adopts a beagle.
moral_consequence: The beagle brings Sally years of enjoyment and companionship while in turn receiving proper care and health.
immoral_action: Sally adopts a pit bull which, due to its naturally violent tendencies towards other dogs, kills a pug at a dog park.
immoral_consequence: The pug dies, Sally feels blame and responsibility, the owner feels grief over the owners loss.

norm: It's rude to expect your child to fail.
situation: Chris has a child that is struggling in school.
intention: Chris wants to review his child's report card.
moral_action: Chris says the low grades can be improved and wants to help his child study.
moral_consequence: The child will improve in school and gain confidence.
immoral_action: Chris says that the low grades on the card are what the child can achieve at best.
immoral_consequence: The child will have low expectations and not exceed them.

norm: It's good to save money for emergencies.
situation: Crystal studies the money in her bank account after getting a large inheritance from her uncle.
intention: Crystal wants to do something with her money.
moral_action: Crystal puts all of the money into a low interest saving account.
moral_consequence: Crystal is able to afford her car repairs after she gets into a wreck.
immoral_action: Crystal spends all of her money on speculative stocks.
immoral_consequence: Crystal loses money after the stocks perform poorly.

norm: You shouldn't drive when you are intoxicated.
situation: Jenna ended up ordering a lot more drinks at the bar than she planned to when she drove there.
intention: Jenna wants to get home without spending a lot of money.
moral_action: Jenna calls her friend who just got off work to come give her a ride.
moral_consequence: Jenna's friend takes her home and Jenna doesn't experience any financial or legal consequences.
immoral_action: Jenna decides to drive home even though she's pretty sure she's drunk.
immoral_consequence: Jenna runs into a tree in her front yard and has to pay for the repairs out of pocket.

norm: It is kind to help someone understand something.
situation: Dave is working away at his desk at his job when his coworker Frank asks him to come to his desk to help him make sense of a file.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Frank's request.
moral_action: Dave tells Frank that he'll be over in a few minutes, and he can take a look at the file for him.
moral_consequence: Frank is delighted that Dave will help him out and relieved that he'll get the file figured out.
immoral_action: Dave tells Frank that he's quite busy right now and that Frank should already know how to do the job anyway.
immoral_consequence: Frank is insulted that Dave is suggesting he doesn't know how to do his job and annoyed he can't get assistance.

norm: It's wrong to be passive aggressive with your friends.
situation: Paul wasn't invited on a road trip that his friend Neal organized because there wasn't enough room in the car and now his feelings are hurt.
intention: Paul wants to react to being left out by Neal.
moral_action: Paul tells Neal that he really wanted to go on the road trip and his feelings are hurt because he didn't get to.
moral_consequence: Neal makes sure to invite Paul to a concert that he only has a limited number of tickets for since Paul missed out on the road trip.
immoral_action: Paul doesn't read any of Paul's texts, answer any of his calls, or talk to him for a month after the road trip.
immoral_consequence: Neal can't get in touch with Paul, so he doesn't invite him to a party he's planning.

norm: It is rude to do things that make people mad
situation: Bobby and his sister Tammy are watching TV but Tammy has the remote and is watching reality TV which Bobby doesn't enjoy.
intention: Bobby wants to watch something else on TV.
moral_action: Bobby patiently waits until Tammy's show is over and then asks if he can watch something else.
moral_consequence: Bobby enjoys watching a TV program he enjoys.
immoral_action: Bobby pokes and pesters his sister to change the channel until she complies.
immoral_consequence: Tammy gets increasingly irritated and refuses to comply with Bobbyt.

norm: You aren't obligated to help others with their problems.
situation: Lee has a friend who is dealing with depression, and she has approached him again for help.
intention: Lee wants to make sure his friend gets help.
moral_action: Lee suggests that his friend talk to a mental health professional.
moral_consequence: Lee's friend takes his advice and gets appropriate help from a qualified doctor.
immoral_action: Lee takes time and energy for his friend to try to talk things out with her.
immoral_consequence: Lee's friend becomes too dependent on coming to him for help.

norm: It's rude to be mean to people on the internet.
situation: Someone posts an opposing viewpoint on one of Alex's political opinion, social media posts.
intention: Alex has to decide how to respond to the person.
moral_action: Alex provides a thoughtful response and explains why he believes that the person has been given some inaccurate information.
moral_consequence: The person still believes that Alex is wrong, but he feels respected and is willing to at least double check the information he believes to be correct.
immoral_action: Alex responds by telling the person why their viewpoint is wrong, and goes on to insult the person's intelligence.
immoral_consequence: The person who expressed a differing opinion feels hurt and disrespected by Alex's response.

norm: It's rude to not respond to messages.
situation: Justin lives alone, so his mom texts him every day to make sure that he's safe.
intention: Justin wants his mom to leave him alone.
moral_action: Justin tells his mom he is fine and asks her not to message him so often.
moral_consequence: Justin's mom changes her daily texts to weekly texts, and they both feel relief in the agreement.
immoral_action: Justin ignores his mother's messages for a three days.
immoral_consequence: Thinking the worst, Justin's mom files a missing persons report when in fact he is not missing.

norm: It's bad for one to hate their partner's child.
situation: Barbara is talking to her husband Jim and his daughter Cara.
intention: Barbara wants Jim to pay more attention to her.
moral_action: Barbara tells Jim that the three of them should do more activities as family.
moral_consequence: Jim is happy that Barbara cares about his daughter and Cara trusts her more.
immoral_action: Barbara tells Jim that she doesn't want Cara living with them.
immoral_consequence: Jim tells Barbara he won't choose her over his child and divorces her.

norm: It's gross to eat food that has gone rotten.
situation: Dan doesn't feel like cooking after work on Thursday and only has old leftovers in his fridge that smell weird.
intention: Dan wants to find something to eat for dinner.
moral_action: Dan gets rid of his old leftovers and orders some Chinese food for delivery.
moral_consequence: Dan has a delicious meal and has some leftover that he puts in the fridge for later.
immoral_action: Dan decides to heat up some old leftover pasta from a couple weeks ago and assumes the microwave will kill any germs.
immoral_consequence: Dan gets sick after eating the pasta because there was too much bacteria for the microwave to kill.

norm: It's immoral to be abusive toward your spouse.
situation: Mitch has a bad day at work and comes home feeling angry.
intention: He wants to work out his anger somehow.
moral_action: Mitch releases his anger though a vigorous workout in his home gym.
moral_consequence: Mitch feels better after his workout and has an enjoyable evening with his wife.
immoral_action: Mitch takes his anger out on his wife and beats her up badly.
immoral_consequence: Mitch is arrested by the police and his wife leaves him.

norm: It's good to strive to be inclusive when throwing celebrations.
situation: As Tony develops plans for a surprise birthday party for his wife, he evaluates the guest list.
intention: Tony must decide if he wants to invite people he would like to have at the party, or people his wife would like to have there.
moral_action: Tony only considers who he believes his wife would want to see, as he populates the guest list for her party.
moral_consequence: Tony's wife has a great time at her surprise party, sharing the experience with the people who mean the most to her.
immoral_action: Tony decides to omit a few of his wife's cousins, who he finds annoying, from the guest list.
immoral_consequence: His wife notices that her cousins are not there, and she regrets their absence.

norm: It's good to volunteer for things.
situation: Pat is in a meeting with his manager Beth, and she asks him if he is interested in running a new company project.
intention: Pat wants to answer Beth.
moral_action: Pat tells Beth that he would like to volunteer to run the project.
moral_consequence: Beth gives Pat the project which ultimately leads to a promotion and a pay raise for Pat.
immoral_action: Pat tells Beth that he doesn't think he would have time for the project.
immoral_consequence: Beth finds another employee to run the project, and that employee eventually gets noticed by the CEO.

norm: It is unacceptable to yell at people.
situation: While walking through the supermarket, someone almost runs into Kathy's daughter.
intention: Kathy wants to scold the person who almost hit her daughter.
moral_action: Kathy pulls the person aside and points out what the person almost did.
moral_consequence: The person is a bit ashamed and apologizes, and promises to be more attentive.
immoral_action: Kathy instantly raises her voice and screams at the person to watch where she's going.
immoral_consequence: The other person looks at her like she's a lunatic and simply walks off.

norm: It's immoral to masturbate onto or into other people's things.
situation: James is very unhappy in his low-paid, dead-end job at Subway with a vindictive manager.
intention: James wants to get revenge on his manager.
moral_action: James waits until the store has a massive catering order and walks off the job.
moral_consequence: James' manager has to struggle to make 200 sandwiches by himself.
immoral_action: James masturbates into the tub of mayonnaise he puts on the customers' sandwiches.
immoral_consequence: James is caught on the store's security cameras and immediately fired, as is his manager.

norm: You shouldn't be too clingy in a relationship.
situation: Ben is in a relationship with Sandy, and they have been dating for a few months.
intention: Ben wants to spend time with Sandy.
moral_action: Ben sets up dates a few nights a week for him and Sandy to spend time together.
moral_consequence: Sandy feels the relationship is moving at an even pace and enjoys Ben's company.
immoral_action: Ben visits Sandy at work and wants to have lunch and dinner with her every day.
immoral_consequence: Sandy becomes annoyed with how often Ben is visiting her and re-considers the relationship.

norm: It's respectable to pursue higher education.
situation: Emily wanted a to get a job, but she didn't want to work that hard for one.
intention: Emily wanted a high paying job.
moral_action: Emily decides to go to college to get a degree despite not wanting to.
moral_consequence: Emily is able to get a high paying job eventually with her degree.
immoral_action: Emily applies to high paying jobs without having a degree or being in college.
immoral_consequence: Emily never gets a high paying job and is forced to go on unemployment.

norm: It's not okay to disrespect your elders.
situation: Mike is at a family reunion all his family is there.
intention: Mike wants to discuss politics with his grandparents.
moral_action: Mike and his grandparents discuss politics and Mike respects their views.
moral_consequence: Mike is happy and his grandparents are glad he came.
immoral_action: While Mike and his grandparents are discussing politics he calls them stupid.
immoral_consequence: Mike feels bad and his grandparents are upset.

norm: You should not depend on others to pay for you.
situation: Bob is out at a restaurant with friends, but only has enough money for a small meal.
intention: Bob is hungry and wants to eat a big meal.
moral_action: Bob orders himself a small meal, and asks his friends if they would pay for an appetizer to split with him because he doesn't have a lot of money.
moral_consequence: His friends order him an appetizer, and even buy him a desert as well to try to make him feel better about being broke.
immoral_action: Bob orders a large meal and, once the bill arrives, tells his friends that he just discovered that he forgot his wallet, expecting them to pay for his meal.
immoral_consequence: His friends refuse to pay for his meal, and Bob is forced to clean dishes in order to work off his debt.

norm: It is unacceptable to sexually harrass someone.
situation: John notices a new girl at school named Jane.
intention: John wants to talk to Jane.
moral_action: John asks Jane what she did on the weekend.
moral_consequence: John and Jane become friends.
immoral_action: John goes up to Jane and compliments her on her butt.
immoral_consequence: Jane files a sexual harassment complaint against him.

norm: It's good to address strangers politely.
situation: Deacon is at the mall looking for the shoe store, when he sees another customer holding a bag from the shoe store.
intention: Deacon wants to ask the other shopper where the shoe store is located.
moral_action: Deacon introduces himself to the other customer and asks if he might be able to direct him to the shoe store.
moral_consequence: The other customer smiles at Deacon and describes how to find the shoe store.
immoral_action: Deacon grabs the other customer and demands that he tell him where the shoe store is.
immoral_consequence: The other customer is scared of Deacon and goes to find mall security.

norm: It's detestable to ogle young girls on the internet.
situation: Owen is at his job in his cubical taking a break from his work.
intention: Owen wants to relax.
moral_action: Owen gets on his cell phone and plays a word trivia game.
moral_consequence: Owen has fun and is ready to get back to work after a few minutes.
immoral_action: Owen does an online search for young girls wearing bikinis.
immoral_consequence: A coworker sees Owen and reports him for his behavior.

norm: It's good to tell someone the truth.
situation: Greg got fired from his job today and his girlfriend notices he seems different.
intention: Greg wants to avoid talking about what really happened.
moral_action: Greg tells his girlfriend that he's had a really bad day and doesn't want to talk about it.
moral_consequence: Greg's girlfriend is concerned but mostly sympathetic and gives him space.
immoral_action: Greg pretends that there is nothing wrong when his girlfriend asks him about it.
immoral_consequence: Greg's girlfriend begins to think he is keeping secrets from her.

norm: It's good to be excited about finally being parents.
situation: Taylor and Marie just got news back from their doctor's office that they are pregnant with twins!
intention: Taylor wants to express her feelings.
moral_action: Taylor cries and hugs Marie, saying over and over again how fantastic the news is.
moral_consequence: Taylor and Marie share in their excitement and begin to ready themselves to welcome a life into the world.
immoral_action: Taylor jokingly yells for someone to toss her down the stairs immediately.
immoral_consequence: Taylor's friends judge her harshly for talking about her child that way and worry about her fitness to be a mother.

norm: It's wrong to ignore your family.
situation: Kyle has a work project with a deadline coming up soon and his mom has been calling and texting him.
intention: Kyle wants to focus on his work.
moral_action: Kyle sends his mom a quick text back promising to get back to her when he's done.
moral_consequence: Kyle's mom appreciates the heads up and waits for him to finish.
immoral_action: Kyle turns off his phone and continues to work on his project.
immoral_consequence: Kyle's mom feels like she is not a priority to her own son.

norm: It's good to want to rescue others.
situation: Gary was walking by the lake in the park when he saw someone fall in.
intention: Gary wants to watch the person in the water.
moral_action: Gary watches the person until they go under water, then he jumps in to save them.
moral_consequence: The person in the lake is very grateful that Gary has saved their life.
immoral_action: Gary watches the person as they go under water and then walks away.
immoral_consequence: The person in the lake doesn't know how to swim, and they drown.

norm: You should always accept your kids no matter what.
situation: Yuri's daughter has just come out of the closet and it goes against her devout religious beleifs.
intention: Yuri wants to discuss her daughter's sexuality with her.
moral_action: Yuri allows her daughter to convince her that this is the way she is and accepts it at that.
moral_consequence: Yuri feels better after talking about it with her mom further.
immoral_action: Yuri tries to convince her daughter to come to the temple in order to fix her.
immoral_consequence: Yuri's daughter feels ostracized by her own family and grows to resent her mother.

norm: It is wrong to threaten to leave someone.
situation: Sara has a partner with a drinking problem and it is taking a toll on the relationship.
intention: Sara wants to discourage the drinking.
moral_action: Sara expresses her concerns over the health issues related to alcoholism.
moral_consequence: Sara's partner finds the concerns to be valid and tries to cut back.
immoral_action: Sara gives her partner an ultimatum and says she will leave him if he doesn't quit.
immoral_consequence: Sara's partner feels bad about the situation and copes with more drinking.

norm: It's wrong to mislead others.
situation: Marry doesn't have feelings for Josh who has a crush on her, and Josh told Marry that he lost his job.
intention: Marry wants to cheer up Josh.
moral_action: Marry reminds Josh of all his accomplishments, and urges him to keep going on.
moral_consequence: Josh is inspired by Mary's words, and he applies to several jobs.
immoral_action: Mary flirts with Josh.
immoral_consequence: While Josh feels better for a little bit, Josh becomes heartbroken when he discovers Marry doesn't love him.

norm: You shouldn't reveal your best friend's secrets.
situation: Jim's best friend has confided in him and revealed that he has had an affair.
intention: Jim wants his best friend's wife to know the truth.
moral_action: Jim discusses with his friend reasons why he must tell his wife what happened.
moral_consequence: Jim's best friend caves in and tells his wife the secret he's been keeping.
immoral_action: Jim contacts the wife and explains what he has learned from his best friend.
immoral_consequence: Jim's best friend feels betrayed by him and no longer trusts him.

norm: It's good to be happy for someone else in life.
situation: David doesn't get into a college he likes but his friend Alex does.
intention: David wants to respond to Alex getting into the college.
moral_action: David tells Alex that they did well getting into the college.
moral_consequence: Alex will think David is a supportive friend.
immoral_action: David tells Alex that it's a mistake that they got into the college.
immoral_consequence: Alex will think David is petty and jealous.

norm: It is bad to damage others' property
situation: Jane is walking in the neighborhood and sees a parked cute Porsche car.
intention: Jane wants to click a picture of the car.
moral_action: Jane takes a selfie with the car in the background and continue to walk.
moral_consequence: Jane is glad with the picture and posts it on her social media.
immoral_action: Jane takes a picture of Porsche and then scratch it with her keys.
immoral_consequence: Jane gets arrested for causing the damage on the car.

norm: You should not leave food unattended
situation: Sam is birdwatching while eating lunch in the park when he receives a phone call.
intention: Sam wants to answer the phone call.
moral_action: Sam answers the phone call while remaining seated on a bench.
moral_consequence: Sam is able to finish enjoying his lunch.
immoral_action: Sam leaves his food on the bench to get up and walk around while talking on the phone.
immoral_consequence: A bird swoops down and steals Sam's lunch, so he has nothing left to eat.

norm: It's wrong to make people worry about where you are.
situation: Joey is out partying with some friends while her parents wait up at home.
intention: Joey wants to continue partying a little longer.
moral_action: Joey calls her parents and asks if she can stay out longer.
moral_consequence: Joey's parents let her stay out another hour.
immoral_action: Joey parties until dawn without letting her parents know where she is.
immoral_consequence: Joey's parents yell at her when she comes home and grounds her for a month.

norm: It's wrong to refuse to do your job.
situation: Henry is at the dump where he works when his boss Bill tells him to move some particularly foul garbage to another location.
intention: Henry wants to respond to Bill's request.
moral_action: Henry tells Bill that he'll get right on it and asks him where he wants the pile moved.
moral_consequence: Bill is happy that Henry didn't make a fuss about the dirty job and is impressed with his work ethic.
immoral_action: Henry tells Bill that the job is disgusting, and he's not doing it and Bill should ask a more junior employee.
immoral_consequence: Bill is angry that Henry is insubordinate and that he's refusing a direct order and vows to speak to senior management.

norm: It's wrong to spite someone.
situation: James is a school counselor, and his least favorite student just gave him a scholarship application to submit.
intention: James wants to teach the student some humilty.
moral_action: James submits the scholarship application and subjects the student to an hour-long lecture about humility.
moral_consequence: The student can't leave without James' permission and is forced to silently listen to the lecture.
immoral_action: James deliberately sends in the application late so the student doesn't get the scholarship.
immoral_consequence: The principal finds out and threatens to fire James if he's similarly incompetent in the future.

norm: You shouldn't discriminate against immigrants.
situation: James needed a new accountant right away and most of the applicants he could find were on green cards.
intention: James wants to hire someone who'll fit in well with the team.
moral_action: James hires the candidate with the best resume regardless of nationality.
moral_consequence: James is quickly able to find a highly qualified candidate for the accounting position.
immoral_action: James refuses to hire anyone but a native-born American for the job opening.
immoral_consequence: James has to look for three months, creating an enormous backlog of work.

norm: You shouldn't be late for things.
situation: Tanya, a makeup lover, has plans to meet with friends and go to a show.
intention: Tanya wants to do her makeup before heading out.
moral_action: Tanya does a simple look that only takes 10 minutes and meets up with her friends before the show starts.
moral_consequence: Tanya and her friends enjoy the show together.
immoral_action: Tanya does an elaborate makeup look that ends up taking an hour and makes her and her friends late for the show.
immoral_consequence: Tanya and her friends aren't allowed into the venue because the show already started and now Tanya's friends are mad at her.

norm: It is bad to put items in your nose.
situation: Faith's nose is blocked and blowing her nose isn't helping.
intention: Faith wants to clear her nasal passage.
moral_action: Faith buys a nasal spray and uses it on her nose.
moral_consequence: Faith clears her nasal passage and finds it easier to breath.
immoral_action: Faith sticks a Q-tip up her nose to try to unblock it.
immoral_consequence: Faith gives herself a nose bleed by sticking the Q-tip too far.

norm: It's bad to spill a drink inside a car.
situation: Roy is getting a ride from his friend, and they stop at Mcdonald's to get a bite to eat.
intention: Roy wants to take his drink with him.
moral_action: Roy gets a top for the cup before he takes it with him into the car.
moral_consequence: Roy's friend enjoys spending time with him during the ride.
immoral_action: Roy brings his drink along him without a cap.
immoral_consequence: The drink spills in Roy's friend's car which makes him upset.

norm: It is rude to misbehave at a family funciton.
situation: Dewey is a child and his family is at a wedding for his aunt.
intention: Dewey wants to have fun.
moral_action: Dewey uses his imagination to pretend he is somewhere else during the ceremony and is on a grand adventure.
moral_consequence: Dewey enjoys himself and before he knows it the ceremony is over, and he is eating cake at the reception.
immoral_action: Dewey gets up and starts to dance and sing right in the middle of the ceremony part of the wedding.
immoral_consequence: Dewey gets in trouble and is punished for weeks on end.

norm: You shouldn't be nude in public.
situation: Laura is in the shower when she sees her son leaving the house with her wallet.
intention: Laura wants to stop her son.
moral_action: Laura calls her neighbor and asks them to stop her son.
moral_consequence: Laura and her neighbor become closer friends after they talk later on in the day.
immoral_action: Laura chases after her son grabbing the wallet.
immoral_consequence: Laura is approached by a cop who fines her for exposing herself in public.

norm: It's good to maintain your privacy.
situation: Lindsey is a very outgoing person who loves to post on social media, and is about to go on a two-week vacation in another country.
intention: Lindsey wants to post about her vacation on social media.
moral_action: Lindsey does not mention her vacation until after she gets back.
moral_consequence: Lindsey has a good time on her vacation and her house remains safe.
immoral_action: Lindsey posts all about her upcoming vacation and when she will be gone.
immoral_consequence: One of the people on her friends list sees this and robs her house while she is away.

norm: It is conceited to feel superior because of your intelligence.
situation: Carl went to Harvard, his friend Corey who has no degree is visiting him for the weekend.
intention: Carl wants to talk about his job.
moral_action: Carl mentions his place of work and asks Corey about his own workplace.
moral_consequence: Carl and Corey have a good discussion and enjoy their weekend together.
immoral_action: Carl mentions his place of work, then says Corey probably has no idea about anything they do because of his intellect.
immoral_consequence: Corey feels insulted and decides to spend the rest of the weekend in a hotel, no longer wanting to be friends with Carl.

norm: It's wrong to enter a country illegally.
situation: Wayne is taking a road trip thru his native Canada on his week-long vacation from his job on the farm.
intention: Wayne wants to visit the United States.
moral_action: Wayne drives to a border checkpoint and crosses over into the US.
moral_consequence: Wayne has a good time on his trip to the United States.
immoral_action: Wayne takes a back road into the US because he has no passport.
immoral_consequence: Wayne is arrested for coming into the US illegally.

norm: You shouldn't exaggerate things.
situation: John is applying for a job at a new company.
intention: He wants his job interview to go well.
moral_action: John is honest and upfront about his past job history.
moral_consequence: John gets the job and is happy about his new employment.
immoral_action: John over-exaggerates his roles in his past company and is not entirely honest about his past duties.
immoral_consequence: The company finds out when they call his references, and he loses the job.

norm: It's good to honest with people you care about.
situation: Cliff has been drinking heavily and has developed an alcohol problem, but when his wife, Cathy, asks him why he's been at the bar so much lately, he hesitates.
intention: Cliff wants to talk to Cathy.
moral_action: Cliff tells Cathy the truth about drinking so much and explains he's been stressed lately.
moral_consequence: Cathy tells Cliff she is there to help him get through this difficult time and is happy Cliff trusts her.
immoral_action: Cliff, being ashamed of his alcohol problem tells Cathy he's been watching the band play at the bar.
immoral_consequence: Cliff doesn't get any support and Cathy knows he's lying because she can see he's hungover every morning and now feels like Cliff doesn't trust her.

norm: It's bad to give away someone else's pet.
situation: Mike was upset with his son Dave because he wasn't doing his homework.
intention: Mike wants to teach Dave a lesson.
moral_action: Mike grounds Dave until he starts getting all of his homework done on time.
moral_consequence: Dave is upset but he starts studying harder in school.
immoral_action: Mike gives away Dave's dog while he's at school.
immoral_consequence: Dave is furious with Mike because that wasn't Mike's dog to give away.

norm: It's good to be a team player when playing soccer.
situation: Dave joined a soccer team and was excited to play and score goals.
intention: Dave wanted to impress the team.
moral_action: Dave scores some goals but also some assists as well with his new teamamtes.
moral_consequence: Dave is popular with his new teammates after his first game.
immoral_action: Dave hogs the ball and scores 6 goals by himself to prove he's worthy of the team.
immoral_consequence: The boss and the fans like Dave but his teammates don't like the ball hogging.

norm: It's not nice to expect others to wait for you
situation: Jenna was supposed to meet her friends at 8 AM to drive to an amusement park, and woke up hungover at 7:30.
intention: Jenna wants to get more sleep.
moral_action: Jenna goes directly to meet her friends and asks them if she can sleep in the backseat of their car.
moral_consequence: Jenna wakes up at the amusement park ready to go on all the rides.
immoral_action: Jenna falls back asleep in her bed and arrives to the meeting point an hour late.
immoral_consequence: All of Jenna's friends spend the first half hour of the trip complaining about her.

norm: It's expected that you go to your friend's birthday parties.
situation: Today is Ton'y best friends birthday, and he has been invited to their birthday party.
intention: Tony is tired and wants to catch up on rest.
moral_action: Tony let's his friend know how exhausted he is, and shows up to the party to drop a gift off and wish him a happy birthday before going back home.
moral_consequence: Tony's friend invites him out for drinks the next weekend, so they can make up for time lost at the birthday party.
immoral_action: Tony ignores his best friends calls and doesn't go to the party.
immoral_consequence: Tony's friend stops hanging out with him as often, and fails to show up to Tony's birthday later that year.

norm: You shouldn't delight in other people's misfortune
situation: James recently heard through the grapevine that his ex-wife was diagnosed with breast cancer.
intention: James wants to feel better about his divorce.
moral_action: James practices meditation to make it easier to let go of unpleasant thoughts.
moral_consequence: James gradually become less upset about things that happened in the past.
immoral_action: James thinks about his wife getting sick from chemo whenever he feels down.
immoral_consequence: James has to keep his thoughts secret because he knows people would disapprove.

norm: You shouldn't talk trash about people's things.
situation: Samantha has noticed that her neighbor, Jolene, has a brand new car in her driveway.
intention: Samantha wants to have a conversation with Jolene about her car.
moral_action: Samantha asks Jolene how she feels about her new car.
