moral_consequence: Samantha and Jolene have a long conversation and grow closer as neighbors.
immoral_action: Samantha tells Jolene that her car is low class.
immoral_consequence: Jolene stops acknowledging Samantha's presence when they see each other.

norm: It's rude to blow up at other students.
situation: Elijah is getting annoyed at his clumsy lab partner who keeps spilling chemicals onto the table in lab.
intention: Elijah wants to express his emotions.
moral_action: Elijah talks to his teacher about his current frustrations.
moral_consequence: Elijah's teacher hands him materials that are less likely to cause spills.
immoral_action: Elijah slams his fists onto the table and compares the boy's intelligence to an insect.
immoral_consequence: Elijah is written up for disrupting the class.

norm: You shouldn't make your partner cry.
situation: Jack is having trouble teaching his wife Sofia how to play the piano.
intention: Jack wants to tell his wife what she's doing wrong.
moral_action: Jack tells Sofia that she needs to pay closer attention to the keys she hits.
moral_consequence: Sofia carefully presses the piano keys and starts to make progress.
immoral_action: Jack raises his voice at Sofia and tells her that she's not smart enough to hit the right keys.
immoral_consequence: Sofia starts crying and no longer wants to play the piano.

norm: It wrong to strangle people you don't like.
situation: Ron did not like Reggie, Ron's neighbor, he would come and bang at Ron's door at all hours asking to borrow things.
intention: Ron wants to stop Reggie from coming to his door.
moral_action: Ron fences his property and keeps the gate locked.
moral_consequence: Ron enjoys peaceful uninterrupted nights.
immoral_action: Reggie comes to Ron's door and Ron loses it, Ron grabs Reggie around his neck and squeezes the life out of Reggie.
immoral_consequence: Ron goes to jail for 20 years.

norm: You shouldn't push your partner off the bed.
situation: Joe needs some sleep and has a partner that snores quite loudly.
intention: Joe wants to stop the snoring which is keeping him up.
moral_action: Joe gently shakes his partner and then cuddles her romantically.
moral_consequence: Joe's partner awakens but is comforted by his actions.
immoral_action: Joe pushes his partner off the bed which makes them fall but does stop the snoring.
immoral_consequence: Joe's partner awakens and is upset.

norm: It is bad to cheat on your partner.
situation: Tina has a boyfriend and is out with her friends at the bar when an attractive man tries to kiss her.
intention: Tina wants to respond to the man's kiss attempt.
moral_action: Tina stop the man and tells him she is in a relationship.
moral_consequence: Tina will feel proud that she stayed faithful to her boyfriend.
immoral_action: Tina leans towards the man and accepts his kiss.
immoral_consequence: Tina will feel guilty for kissing a man that isn't her boyfriend.

norm: It is bad to fake a death.
situation: Karen has a long and important essay due for school the next day, but she hasn't even started it yet.
intention: Karen wants to avoid having to turn in the essay the next day.
moral_action: Karen tells her teacher the truth and requests and extension on the essay.
moral_consequence: Karen's teacher grants her an extension, and she is able to finish the essay a couple days later.
immoral_action: Karen elaborately stages a rock climbing accident in order to fake her own death.
immoral_consequence: Karen's deception is discovered, and she fails the class and gets grounded by her parents.

norm: It's good to have a relationship that lasts multiple years.
situation: Jorge has been with the same girl for about a year and things are getting dull.
intention: Jorge wants more excitement in his life.
moral_action: Jorge thinks of a way to introduce new excitement into their relationship.
moral_consequence: Jorge's partner feels encouraged by this because their passion has been renewed.
immoral_action: Jorge decides to change it up and start dating someone else.
immoral_consequence: Jorge's partner is devastated that he left and could move on so easily.

norm: It is good to tip waitresses.
situation: Cam is eating at a restaurant and is getting bad service from the waitress.
intention: Cam wants the waitress to know that she was unhappy with the service.
moral_action: Cam leaves a tip, but tells the waitress that her service was subpar.
moral_consequence: The waitress was more attentive the next time that Cam went to the restaurant.
immoral_action: Cam leaves a nasty note on the table for the waitress.
immoral_consequence: The waitress recognizes Cam the next time she is in the restaurant and spills water on her.

norm: It's to help others when they need some assistance.
situation: Jack sees Phil's car broken down by the side of the road.
intention: Jack wants to decide to stop or not.
moral_action: Jack stops his car and tries to help Phil out by the side of the road.
moral_consequence: Jack is able to fix Phil's car and Phil thanks Jack for his efforts.
immoral_action: Jack speeds on by Phil's car and continues driving along.
immoral_consequence: Phil stands out in the rain for hours before a tow truck arrives.

norm: It's rude to answer a phone while helping a customer.
situation: There is a long line at the counter where Pedro works at the bakery.
intention: Pedro wants to sell a cake.
moral_action: Pedro puts his phone on silent and is attentive to his many customers, and checks it on his break.
moral_consequence: The line full of customers is helped quickly and Pedro's business thrives.
immoral_action: Pedro answers his cell phone in the middle of a transaction for an expensive wedding cake without greeting the customer.
immoral_consequence: Pedro gets a glare from the customer, and they never return, and spread negative reviews on social media.

norm: It's illegal to break into things.
situation: Calvin left important documents for work in his friends house, and his friend is out of town.
intention: Calvin needs to get his documents.
moral_action: Calvin requests another copy of the documents from his coworkers.
moral_consequence: Calvin gets complimented by his boss who is impressed by his honesty.
immoral_action: Calvin enters his friend's house by picking the lock and grabs his documents.
immoral_consequence: Calvin is arrested by the police after his friend's security system catches him breaking in.

norm: You shouldn't hate things.
situation: Dave is at a party when he's offered some cocktail shrimp by Sandy.
intention: Dave wants to decline the cocktail shrimp.
moral_action: Dave tells Sandy that he already had too much to eat and isn't feeling too great any longer, so he'll decline.
moral_consequence: Sandy is understanding as to why Dave would not want any Shrimp and moves to the next guest.
immoral_action: Dave tells Sandy that he absolutely despises shrimp in all forms, and he doesn't want any.
immoral_consequence: Sandy is shocked that Dave has such intensely negative feelings towards Shrimp and finds him odd.

norm: It is okay to be protective over your friends.
situation: Jill heard Bill was going to go through the rough part of town by himself.
intention: Jill wants to decide what to do.
moral_action: Jill makes sure that Bill has someone with him before he goes.
moral_consequence: Bill gets through safely without any issues because his guide knew where to go.
immoral_action: Jill ignores what she hears about Bill, thinking it not true.
immoral_consequence: Bill gets lost and it takes until 3:30am for him to get home.

norm: You shouldn't fall in love with your professor.
situation: Sam was taking an English in the local college which was instructed by handsome instructor.
intention: Sam wants to talk to the instructor.
moral_action: Sam waits until after class and asks the professor if he could recommend someone for tutoring.
moral_consequence: The instructor gives Sam a slip of paper with the name and number of an English tutor on campus.
immoral_action: Sam waits until after class and asks the instructor if he wants to join her on a date.
immoral_consequence: The instructor sees her proposal as indecent and makes her drop the class.

norm: It's good to be concerned for the health of others.
situation: Carol lives in a building where there are many activities organized for the residents, many of whom are elderly like Carol.
intention: Carol wants to have fun by joining an in-person activity.
moral_action: Carol calls each participant ahead of the activity and asks how they feel.
moral_consequence: Carol discovers that one of the potential participants doesn't feel well and encourages her to stay home - and no one in the activity is infected.
immoral_action: Carol doesn't care much about other people's health and doesn't ask anyone involved in the activity how they feel.
immoral_consequence: One of the participants is actually a bit sick, and soon after discovers she has Covid - Carol and others are infected.

norm: You should call the cops on people who steal.
situation: Frank catches his neighbor's son taking his amazon package from his porch.
intention: Frank wants to take action against the son.
moral_action: Frank calls the police and reports the boy for taking the package.
moral_consequence: The cops charge the boy and the experience teaches him a valuable lesson.
immoral_action: Frank tells his neighbors who are the kid's parents about the incident.
immoral_consequence: The neighbors go easy on their son and his behavior does not change.

norm: It's wrong to cause your child to die.
situation: It's a hot summer day and Frank just drove home from the grocery store with his toddler strapped in the car seat.
intention: Frank wants to unload the groceries.
moral_action: Considering the possibility of heatstroke, Frank takes his toddler out of the car seat first and then unloads the groceries.
moral_consequence: Frank finishes his shopping trip uneventfully with his toddler arriving home safe and sound.
immoral_action: Frank takes the groceries inside first and then gets distracted, leaving his child to die of heatstroke in the car.
immoral_consequence: Frank gets arrested and charged with murder.

norm: You shouldn't let your kids smoke cigarettes.
situation: Jim is a pack a day smoker with a child named Roger, who has expressed interest in trying smoking.
intention: Jim wants to teach Roger a lesson about smoking.
moral_action: Jim tells Roger about the various adverse health consequences of smoking.
moral_consequence: Roger is scared off by all the side effects Jim tells him about and decides he doesn't want to try smoking any more.
immoral_action: Jim lets Roger try a cigarette, figuring he'll be disgusted by it and stop being interested.
immoral_consequence: Roger ends up enjoying the cigarette and later starts smoking daily.

norm: Being a burden on one's parents is wrong.
situation: Donald is an adult and recently got a new job near where his retired parents live.
intention: Donald wants to find somewhere to live.
moral_action: Donald tells his parents he will live on the same street as them, so he can visit them often.
moral_consequence: Donald's parents will be happy that he will be able to visit them often.
immoral_action: Donald tells his parents he will live with them, so he doesn't have to pay rent.
immoral_consequence: Donald's parents will be stressed as they have to pay for his housing expenses on retirement money.

norm: It's helpful to figure things out on your own.
situation: Kelri is trying to put together a model kit, which has confusing instructions.
intention: Kelri wants to complete the kit and give the model to a friend.
moral_action: Kelri watches a tutorial, figures out how to build the kit, and finishes it on her own.
moral_consequence: Kelri gives the model to her friend, and is able to build another one for herself.
immoral_action: Kelri gets frustrated, and asks her dad to finish the kit for her.
immoral_consequence: Kelri gives the model to her friend, but has no idea how to build that kind of kit when she is given another one.

norm: It's good to keep in touch with your significant other.
situation: Sam is going on a long trip and wont see his partner for awhile.
intention: Sam wants to contact his partner everyday while he's gone.
moral_action: Sam texts and calls his partner everyday, while engaging in meaningful conversations.
moral_consequence: Sam's partner feels appreciated and loved.
immoral_action: Sam texts his partner daily but only sends short messages and neglects to call.
immoral_consequence: Sam's partner feels neglected.

norm: It's wrong to put someone down for their weight.
situation: Felton is at a party with his overweight friend Tracy.
intention: Felton wants to entertain people.
moral_action: Felton asks Tracy to help him act out a scene from their favorite movie.
moral_consequence: A guest at the party  asks Tracy to audition for the lead in their upcoming play.
immoral_action: Felton makes a joke comparing Tracy to a whale.
immoral_consequence: Tracy starts crying.

norm: You should not go to work without a shirt on.
situation: Keith is getting in his bedroom getting ready for work that morning.
intention: Keith wants to decide what to wear.
moral_action: Keith decides to wear his gray suit and red tie and goes to work happily.
moral_consequence: Keith's coworkers think he looks quite handsome today and are happy to have a stylish figure in the office.
immoral_action: Keith decides to wear only half a suit and go topless, but he still puts on a tie just in case.
immoral_consequence: Keith's coworkers are shocked when they see him and are uncomfortable working next to a half naked man.

norm: It's good to care about your work.
situation: Todd realizes after a few hours of working on a project that he has approached it incorrectly, and all of his work to this point has been substandard.
intention: Todd has to decide whether to go back and redo his work from earlier, or just proceed differently from this point.
moral_action: Todd informs his work group that he made errors early in the day that he will have to fix, and that his production will be lowered for the day.
moral_consequence: Todd's colleagues understand the problem, and they try to help him by compensating by increasing their production for the day.
immoral_action: Todd decides that it is too time consuming to go back over his work from earlier, so he just leaves it in its unacceptable state.
immoral_consequence: Todd gets into trouble for leaving extra work for other people, who have to fix his errors, after he obviously realized that he had made mistakes.

norm: You should respect your partner's wishes.
situation: John is all set to go bowling with his buddies when his wife Nancy says she isn't feeling so great and wants him to stay home toight.
intention: John wants to respond to Nancy's request.
moral_action: John tells Nancy that he'll call the guys right away and tell them that something came up, and he'll stay with her.
moral_consequence: Nancy feels relieved that she'll have her love near her in her time of need.
immoral_action: John tells Nancy that he's already planned this and the guys will mock him if he skips out on it, besides he'll be back in a few hours.
immoral_consequence: Nancy feels like her husband doesn't care about her well being and is sad that she can't count on comfort from him.

norm: Contacting a parent on their birthday is expected.
situation: Josephine's mom's birthday is here.
intention: Josephine wants to maintain her independence from her family.
moral_action: Josephine calls her mom to wish her a happy birthday while maintaining her own independence four states away.
moral_consequence: Josephine's mom feels loved.
immoral_action: Josephine ignores her mom's birthday and never calls her.
immoral_consequence: Josephine's mom is hurt and wonders if Josephine loves her.

norm: It's wrong not to help out around the house.
situation: Jim's wife is cleaning the house on her only day off of work.
intention: Jim wants the house to be clean.
moral_action: Jim helps his wife with the laundry and the dishes.
moral_consequence: Jim's wife is able to finish the chores early and relax for a few hours.
immoral_action: Jim sits on the couch and watches television while his wife does all the cleaning.
immoral_consequence: Jim's wife is too tired to talk to him and goes to bed early.

norm: You should not abandon your job.
situation: Mark is in a job he is unhappy with, and he is thinking about leaving it to collect unemployment.
intention: Mark has to decide whether to leave his job.
moral_action: Mark doesn't want to disappoint his coworkers, so he stays.
moral_consequence: Mark's coworkers know he is unhappy, so they are grateful for him staying.
immoral_action: Mark doesn't want to get up early to go to work anymore, so he doesn't come the next day.
immoral_consequence: Mark angers his coworkers, and they have to do his work for him.

norm: It is good to do things for others.
situation: Bill earns a bonus at the end of the week that he didn't expect to get.
intention: Bill wants to spend his extra money on something.
moral_action: Bill takes his bonus and buys canned goods to take to a food pantry, and he spends his weekend packaging and delivering food to people who need it.
moral_consequence: Bill spends his weekend with people who he thoroughly enjoys, and they do great work for the community, leaving bill with a sense of accomplishment.
immoral_action: Bill goes out over the weekend and spends his bonus on fun.
immoral_consequence: Bill feels empty about his life because even when he has something extra, it doesn't do much to enrich his life.

norm: It's wrong to take things that don't belong to you.
situation: Marie is a 10 year old who loves collecting rings.
intention: Marie wants a new ring to add to her collection.
moral_action: Marie saves up her allowance and buys a pretty silver ring at a store in the mall.
moral_consequence: Marie is proud that she was able to save money to buy something she wanted.
immoral_action: Marie shoplifts a pretty ring from a store in the mall.
immoral_consequence: Marie is ashamed and embarrassed as he explains what she did to her mother, after being caught by the store’s security guard.

norm: You shouldn't get drunk and pass out.
situation: Tami just found out her long time friends are in town visiting.
intention: Tami wants to have some drinks with her friends.
moral_action: Tami has only enough drinks to start feeling a slight buzz.
moral_consequence: Tami's friends enjoy spending the night with her and plan to visit again soon.
immoral_action: Tami drinks so much that she loses consciousness in front of her friends.
immoral_consequence: Tami's friends are worried that she may have a drinking problem.

norm: It's good to reward your customers for their trouble.
situation: Bill runs an electronics store and has to address a customer complaint about a product he bought.
intention: Bill wants to respond to the customer.
moral_action: Bill gives his customer a full refund along with a coupon for his next purchase.
moral_consequence: Bill gains a new loyal customer who eventually returns to purchase more items from Bill's store.
immoral_action: Bill apologizes to the customer but does nothing more than that.
immoral_consequence: The customer leaves angry and never returns to the store again.

norm: It's not okay to talk excessively about your problems.
situation: Linda and several colleagues are having lunch at work and chatting, and Linda just went through a breakup.
intention: Linda wants to participate in the conversation.
moral_action: Linda briefly brings up her situation and asks for advice from her colleagues.
moral_consequence: Linda's colleagues are engaged in the conversation and give her some helpful relationship advice.
immoral_action: Linda monopolizes the conversation, rehashing her recent breakup in intimate, excrutiating detail.
immoral_consequence: Linda's colleagues feign interest but are secretly bored and annoyed.

norm: It's wrong for an adult to abuse a child.
situation: Chloe, Nina’s 12-year-old daughter, wants to go to a friend's house even though she has homework to do.
intention: Nina wants Chloe to do her homework.
moral_action: Nina tells Chloe that she can leave as long as she gets her homework done first.
moral_consequence: Chloe completes her homework, so Nina happily takes her to her friends house.
immoral_action: Nina gives Chloe a slap and tells her she'll hit her again if she doesn't get her homework done.
immoral_consequence: Chloe begins to cry and resents her mom.

norm: It's wrong to kidnap someone.
situation: Jake's friend Sam has a birthday coming up and loves surprises.
intention: Jake wants to play a joke on Sam.
moral_action: Jake hides a new phone inside of Sam's car in a very hard-to-reach place and calls it repeatedly.
moral_consequence: Sam spends an hour trying to get the new phone and has a good laugh about it.
immoral_action: Jake plans and executes a fake kidnapping by renting a van and having some friends grab Sam while walking.
immoral_consequence: Sam is terrified and overreacts, then gets really angry with Jake.

norm: You shouldn't steal someone's car.
situation: John's bike has a flat and won't hold air.
intention: John wants to get to work on time.
moral_action: John asks his neighbor to drive him to work.
moral_consequence: John and his neighbor strike up a conversation and become good friends.
immoral_action: John takes his neighbor's unlocked car with the keys in it.
immoral_consequence: John is arrested at work after his neighbor reports the car stolen.

norm: You are expected to help family in times of need.
situation: Kevin, a successful stockbroker, is on the phone with his mom who tells him that she and his dad are in financial trouble and need to borrow some money.
intention: Kevin wants to respond to his mom's request for money.
moral_action: Kevin tells his mom that it's no problem, and she can take as much as they need.
moral_consequence: Kevin's mom is relieved that her and his dad will get some help and get through the tough times.
immoral_action: Kevin tells his mom that he cannot spare any money right now as most of his money is tied up in stocks.
immoral_consequence: Kevin's mom knows he can just sell the stock and lend her money and is both furious and heartbroken that her son is so unsupportive.

norm: It's wrong to kick down your estranged wife's door.
situation: Fred just found out his ex wife is trying to gain full custody of his child.
intention: Fred wants to confront his wife on the issue.
moral_action: Fred contacts his attorney and prepares to meet his wife on the issue through legal means.
moral_consequence: Fred is able to prove there has been no change in their situation and the court allows him to retain some custody of his child.
immoral_action: Fred lets his mood get the better of him and goes to his wife's front door and makes his way through it when she does not answer.
immoral_consequence: Fred is arrested by the police and his ex wife easily wins full custody of their child.

norm: You shouldn't ignore friends.
situation: Dawson is walking down the street when he gets an unexpected phone call from his friend Keith.
intention: Dawson wants to respond to his ringing phone.
moral_action: Dawson answers the phone and Keith invites him to a baseball game that afternoon.
moral_consequence: Dawson has a great time at the baseball game with Keith.
immoral_action: Dawson turns off the ringer and does not answer the call because he doesn't feel like talking.
immoral_consequence: Dawson later learns that he missed out on a chance to go see his favorite baseball team because he didn't answer his phone.

norm: It's bad to procrastinate on assignments until the last minute.
situation: Julia has a paper due the same week as a major upcoming party she's planning.
intention: Julia wants to enjoy the party without worrying about the paper.
moral_action: Julia works hard on her paper early on, so she can spend the rest of her week planning her fun party.
moral_consequence: Julia is able to turn her paper in early and enjoys her party without any worries.
immoral_action: Julia decides not to do her paper, so she can prepare for her party.
immoral_consequence: Julia fails her class and has to go to Summer school.

norm: It's good to teach children about abuse.
situation: The school Jim's daughter attends recently had a sexual misconduct issue.
intention: Jim wants to talk to his daughter about the issue.
moral_action: Jim talks to his daughter about ways to identify predators and about how to protect herself.
moral_consequence: Jim's daughter is able to keep herself safe and helps apprehend the predator in the school.
immoral_action: Jim tells his daughter not to worry about what happened and not to ask her friends about it.
immoral_consequence: Jim's daughter isn't aware of any way to protect herself and falls victim to the same sexual predator.

norm: It's wrong to play loud music in an apartment.
situation: Larry just moved out of his parent's house and into his own apartment.
intention: Larry wants to throw a party.
moral_action: Larry throws a quiet party, keeping the music low, so he doesn't disturb his anyone.
moral_consequence: Larry's neighbors are unaware there's a party going on in the apartment complex.
immoral_action: Larry invites all his friends, they blast music and are having a really noisy party.
immoral_consequence: Larry's neighbor comes knocking on his door and complains about the loud noise.

norm: It's wrong to hurt yourself.
situation: Jack walks out of the room after getting into a fight with Marry.
intention: Jack wants to vent his anger.
moral_action: Jack talks to another one of his friends on the phone about his problems.
moral_consequence: Jack forms a deeper relationship with his friend.
immoral_action: Jack smashes his fist against a hard surface on purpose breaking his finger.
immoral_consequence: Jack has to pay high medical bills to fix his finger.

norm: Its not ok to handcuff kids.
situation: James' brother asked him to babysit even though he didn't like kids, and the kids kept running around the house and yelling.
intention: James wants the kids to sit quietly until his brother gets back.
moral_action: James gives each of his brother's kids an iPad or laptop to use.
moral_consequence: James' brother's kids sit quietly while surfing the Internet until his brother comes to collect them.
immoral_action: James handcuffs his brother's kids to chairs at the dining room table.
immoral_consequence: James' brother hits the roof when he comes home and James is banned from his house.

norm: It's wrong to gamble too much.
situation: Sue wants to join her friends for some fun at the casino.
intention: Sue decides she wants to put some money in a slot machine.
moral_action: Sue spends a moderate amount and stops when she lost what she could afford.
moral_consequence: Sue had fun and still has money for her bills.
immoral_action: Sue puts way too much money in the machine an loses it all.
immoral_consequence: Sue has a hard time paying her bills for the month and is broke.

norm: It's wrong to skip out on your family member's memorial.
situation: James grandfather has passed away from a heart attack.
intention: James wants to go on a trip with his friends.
moral_action: James attends his grandfather memorial and meets his friends the next day.
moral_consequence: James and his family are happy they attended the memorial together.
immoral_action: James skips his grandfathers memorial and goes on his trip with his friends.
immoral_consequence: James family is very disappointed and stop speaking to him.

norm: You shouldn't refuse to help out your roommate.
situation: Before leaving for work, Hank's car stops working right before his roommate Bill is about to leave for work.
intention: Bill wants to get to work.
moral_action: Bill gives Hank a ride on the way to work.
moral_consequence: Hank arrives at his job.
immoral_action: Bill drives to work as planned.
immoral_consequence: Hank is left at home with no way to get to work.

norm: It is good to leave a wild snake alone.
situation: Robert is hiking through the woods and sees a snake sitting in the middle of the path.
intention: Robert wants to walk on the path past the snake to his destination.
moral_action: Robert walks past the snake giving a wide berth and not messing with it.
moral_consequence: Robert continues on his path and makes it to his destination.
immoral_action: Robert walks past the snake and pokes it with his walking stick.
immoral_consequence: The snake gets irritated and bites Robert on the leg.

norm: You should not be racist in the presence of minorities.
situation: Fred was taking a walk through the hispanic part of his town.
intention: Fred wants to greet a man he sees on the street.
moral_action: Fred tells the man that he meets up with on the street hello.
moral_consequence: The man talks to Fred for a few minutes before going on his way.
immoral_action: Fred uses a racial slur to greet the man on the street.
immoral_consequence: The man is offended and calls over his sons to beat Fred up.

norm: You shouldn't get your coworkers in trouble.
situation: John is at work and sees his coworker Tom taking a few sheets of office paper and putting them in his bag to take home for personal use.
intention: John wants to do correct Tom's behavior.
moral_action: John informs Tom that taking office paper for personal use is against company policy, and he could get in trouble.
moral_consequence: Tom thanks John for letting him know and Tom maintains a good working relationship with Tom.
immoral_action: John tattles on Tom to their boss to get him in trouble for taking the paper.
immoral_consequence: John's relationship with Tom is tense in the future and his other coworkers trust him less.

norm: It's wrong to be jealous of an animal.
situation: Glenn's wife pays a lot of attention to her dog and Glenn is feeling annoyed and isolated.
intention: Glenn wants to express frustration.
moral_action: Glenn is frank with his wife and asks for attention.
moral_consequence: He is given attention and feels loved.
immoral_action: Glenn walks out of the room and mumbles to himself.
immoral_consequence: Glenn feels worse and his relationship is deteriorating.

norm: It's wrong to misuse your discounts.
situation: Milo works at a retail store and his friends want them to use his employee discount for them.
intention: Milo wants to respond to his friends' requests.
moral_action: Milo tells his friends that he can't use the discount for their purchases.
moral_consequence: Milo will be able to work at the store without incident.
immoral_action: Milo lets his friends use his discount on all the thinks they buy.
immoral_consequence: Milo will get in trouble with management for using his employee discount too much.

norm: It's good to realize the truth.
situation: Brandon has been noticing his girlfriend go out for ladies night more and more, and is getting suspicious when she starts turning down his requests for sex afterwards.
intention: Brandon wants to have a happy and fulfilling relationship.
moral_action: Brandon confronts his girlfriend and asks what is going on.
moral_consequence: Brandon's girlfriend confesses to cheating on him, they seek couples counseling and eventually make it past this hurdle and live a long and happy life together.
immoral_action: Brandon ignores the signs and never brings it up, hoping that it will pass.
immoral_consequence: Brandon's girlfriend get's pregnant, and he ends up supporting her for years before discovering the child is not his.

norm: It's wrong to dictate your significant other's friendships.
situation: Harry and Lisa are dating, and Harry does not like one of Lisa's friends, Tina.
intention: Harry wants to avoid Tina.
moral_action: Harry is honest with Lisa, and asks that he not be around when she hangs out with Tina.
moral_consequence: Lisa is not happy, but obliges and Lisa and Harry keep dating.
immoral_action: Harry tells Lisa she has to stop hanging out with Tina.
immoral_consequence: Lisa gets angry with Harry and breaks off the relationship.

norm: It's wrong to miss having a medical disorder.
situation: Benjamin is a child and just had his cast removed from a recovered broken leg.
intention: Benjamin wants attention from his parents.
moral_action: Benjamin runs and jumps around in front of his parents as best as he can on his recovered leg.
moral_consequence: His parents smile and congratulate Benjamin on his healed leg.
immoral_action: Benjamin tries to call for his parents help getting things like he had to when he had a cast because he liked having things done for him.
immoral_consequence: Benjamin's parents tell him he has to start moving around and behaving like normal again.

norm: It's good to help people out who are poor.
situation: Mary has some furniture she doesn't want anymore, and she knows her neighbor who doesn't have much money could use it.
intention: Mary wants to get the furniture out of her house.
moral_action: Mary gives the furniture to her neighbor and helps them move it into their home.
moral_consequence: Mary's neighbor has all the furniture they need after her kind gift.
immoral_action: Mary pays to have the furniture taken to the dump as that seems like the most convenient solution.
immoral_consequence: Mary's neighbor has to make due with an insufficient amount of furniture.

norm: It's considered polite to chew quietly with your mouth closed.
situation: Donald has a dinner reservation with his new work clients, and is feeling a bit nervous about meeting them.
intention: "Donald wants to avoid a ""stiff"" dinner meeting."
moral_action: Donald orders a bottle of wine for the table, and uses his best manners when eating.
moral_consequence: Donald and his clients are able to relax and bond over wine while developing a work plan.
immoral_action: Donald orders spaghetti and sits back while he slurps loudly and chews with his mouth agape.
immoral_consequence: Donald's clients are put off by his behavior and decide not to go through with their deal.

norm: It's wrong to try to sabotage others.
situation: Jackson is up for promotion at work against his coworker Mary who has completed a nice project.
intention: Jackson wants to get promoted.
moral_action: Jackson makes a speech highlighting all of the hard work he's done over the years for Mary and Jackson's boss.
moral_consequence: While Jackson gets promoted, Mary feels like she has been beat in respectful competition, and her relationship with Jackson deepens.
immoral_action: Jackson removes key elements of Mary's project making her presentation fail in front of Jackson and Marry's boss.
immoral_consequence: Mary is humiliated.

norm: It's not normal to not eat
situation: Jan is not happy with her weight, and she wants clothes to look better on her.
intention: Jan wants to lose weight.
moral_action: Jan starts working out more and eats a lot more fruits and vegetables.
moral_consequence: Jan is able to lose weight and become healthier at the same time.
immoral_action: Jan only eats one meal a day in order to lose weight.
immoral_consequence: Jan becomes bulimic and feels too weak to do her ordinary activities.

norm: You shouldn't kick out your partner.
situation: Lisa is enraged when her husband once again comes home drunk after being out all night with his buddies.
intention: Lisa wants to confront her husband about his behaviour.
moral_action: Lisa waits until her husband is rested and sober then lets him know how she is feeling.
moral_consequence: Lisa is able to convince her husband to adjust his behavior.
immoral_action: After a heated exchange Lisa tells her husband to leave their home.
immoral_consequence: Lisa has a hard time making up with her husband once he is out of the house.

norm: It is bad to look through someone else's things.
situation: Tom's mother Susan suspects that he has been dating a girl without telling her about it.
intention: Susan wants to find out if Tom has a girlfriend.
moral_action: Susan sits down with Tom and asks him if he is seeing anyone.
moral_consequence: Tom tells his mother that he has been dating someone, and he feels relieved.
immoral_action: Susan goes into Tom's room and reads his journal to see if he has written about a girlfriend.
immoral_consequence: Tom discovers that Susan went through his journal and feels upset and violated.

norm: It's rude to exclude someone with social anxiety.
situation: Sally is planning a party and deciding if she should invite Megan or not because Megan gets nervous in crowds.
intention: Sally wants to throw a fun party.
moral_action: Sally decides to invite Megan and stay by her side until Megan feels comfortable.
moral_consequence: Megan feels comfortable enough to come out of her shell and tell jokes and makes everyone laugh.
immoral_action: Sally decides that Megan would ruin her party and doesn't invite her.
immoral_consequence: Megan finds out she isn't invited to Sally's party and tells their friends who decide not to attend the party either.

norm: You shouldn't waste food.
situation: Craig is tired of always eating at the same restaurants.
intention: Craig wants to try the new buffet restaurant in town.
moral_action: Craig is mindful of how much he can eat at the buffet and takes only the amount he knows he can finish.
moral_consequence: Craig is happy that her tried the new buffet restaurant.
immoral_action: Craig repeatedly loads his plate with food at the buffet, but then he's too full to finish it all, so he throws the rest out.
immoral_consequence: Craig feels bad for taking more than he was able to eat and wasting food.

norm: It's good to keep one's vehicle in good running order.
situation: Brad is in the middle or a long road trip when he notices some warning lights coming on in his dashboard.
intention: Brad wants to decide what to do in response to the warning lights.
moral_action: Brad takes the car into the nearest auto maintenance shop where the issue is quickly fixed.
moral_consequence: Brad's car is running as good as new, and he is soon back on the road enjoying his trip.
immoral_action: Brad decides to ignore the warnings for the time being and keeps on driving.
immoral_consequence: Brad's engine overheats and the car breaks down leaving him stranded on the side of the road.

norm: It is okay to want to separate business and family.
situation: Dave's son Max is interested in a summer job and asks Dave if he can find him something at his work.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Max's request.
moral_action: Dave tells Max that he's not comfortable pulling strings for family, and he needs to apply elsewhere.
moral_consequence: Max finds a different job eventually and there are no conflicts of interest created for Dave.
immoral_action: Dave tells Max that he'll talk to his boss and make sure Max gets a position.
immoral_consequence: Max performs badly and Dave is put under huge pressure at work for having recommended him.

norm: It is good not to contribute to others' self-destructive behaviors
situation: Henry is planning a party to celebrate his friend David's sobriety.
intention: Henry wants to have a fun party.
moral_action: Henry throws the party at a park and only serves soft drinks.
moral_consequence: David has a great time and the outpouring of support gives him strength for his journey ahead.
immoral_action: Henry throws the party at a bar with a lot of alcohol.
immoral_consequence: David has some drinks and relapses.

norm: You shouldn't be selfish when you have a baby.
situation: Dayton is a new mother, and her friends invite her to the party.
intention: Dayton wants to do something run.
moral_action: Dayton asks her friends to play games with her at home while she watches her son.
moral_consequence: Dayton learns how to be a better parent from her more experienced friends.
immoral_action: Dayton leaves her child in the crib while she parties with her friends.
immoral_consequence: Dayton has to take her son to the hospital after he escapes from the crib and hurts himself.

norm: You shouldn't expect others to clean up behind you.
situation: Dan always cooks a big breakfast for the family before leaving for work.
intention: Dan wants to go to work.
moral_action: Dan does the dishes and heads for work.
moral_consequence: Dan's wife is thankful that she doesn't have to wash dishes.
immoral_action: Dan leaves the breakfast dishes for his wife to wash.
immoral_consequence: Dan's wife is annoyed that Dan didn't wash the dishes himself.

norm: It's rude to ignore someone after hooking up with them.
situation: Kyle just had a fun date with Marissa, and they ended up sleeping together, so the next day Marissa sends him a text.
intention: Kyle wants to read the text.
moral_action: Kyle sees that Marissa was asking what he's up to later, so he texts back that he's free after he finishes cleaning.
moral_consequence: Marissa is thrilled that Kyle has some free time, so she can see him.
immoral_action: Kyle sees that Marissa was asking what he's up to later, but decides to not respond because he was busy cleaning his house.
immoral_consequence: Marissa feels like Kyle got what he wanted from her and will probably not talk to her again which makes her sad.

norm: It's wrong to take long breaks at work.
situation: A stressed out Baston is surrounded by mountains of paperwork at the office.
intention: Baston wants to relieve his stress.
moral_action: Baston asks his coworkers to help him while listening to their favorite music in the background.
moral_consequence: Baston bonds with his friends.
immoral_action: Baston extends his lunch break to relax by watching youtube videos.
immoral_consequence: Baston is unable to finish his paperwork.

norm: It's not okay to lie or mislead other people.
situation: Jeff wants to sell his car and has found a buyer named Martin.
intention: Jeff wants to convince Martin to buy the car.
moral_action: Jeff explains what issues the car might have and drops the price to make the deal more attractive.
moral_consequence: Martin buys the car for the reduced price and gets the issues serviced.
immoral_action: Jeff hides a lot of problems with the car from Martin and tells him it runs perfectly.
immoral_consequence: Martin buys the car and is furious when it breaks down the next day.

norm: It's wrong to kill a living being.
situation: Jeff's dog keeps pooping on Roy's lawn and Roy is tired of it.
intention: Roy wants to stop the dog from ruining his lawn.
moral_action: Roy tells Jeff that his dog is pooping on his lawn.
moral_consequence: Jeff makes sure that his dog doesn't go near Roy's lawn in the future.
immoral_action: Roy kills the dog while it's in the middle of pooping on his lawn.
immoral_consequence: Jeff sees Roy kill the dog and attacks him out of anger.

norm: You should not interfere with your spouse's friendships.
situation: Max is relaxing on the couch after work when his wife comes up and asks if it'd be okay for her to go to the mall with her friend.
intention: Max wants his family to stick to their budget.
moral_action: Max tells his wife to go but not to spend any money because they've already spent the entire budget for this month.
moral_consequence: Max's wife grumbles about not being able to buy anything, but ends up having fun just spending time with her friend.
immoral_action: Max tells his wife that she has to stay in because they are already at the limit of their budget.
immoral_consequence: Max's wife is upset that he won't let her spend time with her friend, and she refuses to speak to him the rest of the night.

norm: It is nice to invite your friend to a movie.
situation: Dave who is going to see a movie Friday, is talking with Jim when Jim asks him what he's doing Friday night.
intention: Dave wants to answer Jim's question.
moral_action: Dave tells Jim that he was going to see a movie and asks Jim if he wants to come along.
moral_consequence: Jim is delighted that Dave invited him out and is excited to come with him.
immoral_action: Dave tells Jim that he's doing nothing and plans to sit at home and do his taxes.
immoral_consequence: Jim later finds out from friends that Dave went to see a movie and is insulted that he was lied to.

norm: You shouldn't hide important medical issues from your loved ones.
situation: Ray was diagnosed with terminal stage 4 lung cancer and is considering when to break the news to his young adult son who's in college.
intention: Ray wants to tell his son about his cancer at the right time.
moral_action: Ray tells his son as soon as possible about his illness.
moral_consequence: Ray's son takes time off of school to take care of Ray and spend precious time with him.
immoral_action: Ray delays telling his son as long as possible, so he continues his schooling.
immoral_consequence: Ray's son finds out at the very end of Ray's life, denying him the opportunity of spending quality time with Ray.

norm: It's not right to be lazy at work.
situation: Steve is sitting at his desk working at his computer at work.
intention: Steve wants to take a nap.
moral_action: Steve waits until lunch time and goes to his car to take a nap.
moral_consequence: Steve comes back from his lunch break and is more productive than ever.
immoral_action: Steve gets down under his desk and takes a nap during work hours.
immoral_consequence: Steve is fired from his job when his boss sees that he isn't being productive.

norm: You shouldn't expect rides from people.
situation: Chris is headed to a basketball game.
intention: Chris wants to get there on time but doesn't have a car.
moral_action: Chris asks a friend if they'll give him a ride since they're headed to the game too.
moral_consequence: Chris and his friend enjoy the game.
immoral_action: Chris pressures his dad into driving him out of his way to the game, making his dad late to work.
immoral_consequence: Chris's dad gets disciplined for being late to work.

norm: It's wrong to disavow saving forever.
situation: Sebastian is at home and just received news that his savings investment has lost all its value.
intention: Sebastian wants to decide what to do with his finances going forward.
moral_action: Sebastian decides he will stick to more stable ways to save his money.
moral_consequence: Sebastian is able to save money and is ready for a proverbial rainy day when it arrives.
immoral_action: Sebastian swears off saving and decides he will spend the money he has day to day.
immoral_consequence: Sebastian runs into trouble when he has an unexpected financial emergency and no way to pay for it.

norm: It’s bad to trust everyone you know.
situation: Jose gets an email from a Nigerian prince asking for a small payment to which he will repay with interest once he accesses his bank account.
intention: Jose wants to find out what to do.
moral_action: Jose googles to see if the email and request is legitimate.
moral_consequence: Jose finds out it's a scam and deletes the email.
immoral_action: Jose listens to the Nigerian prince and sends the small payment to him.
immoral_consequence: Jose is scammed out of his money.

norm: Fabricating a pregnancy scare is lying.
situation: Katie has been fighting with her partner frequently and is worried about their relationship.
intention: Katie wants her partner to stay with her.
moral_action: Katie takes note of the issues in the relationship and works hard to control her end of them.
moral_consequence: Katie's partner notices her efforts and is motivated to stay with her.
immoral_action: Katie tells her partner that she is pregnant even though she is not in order to get him to stay.
immoral_consequence: Katie's partner finds out and this is the final straw for him.

norm: It's bad to damage someone's personal property.
situation: Jason is at a house party and is being rowdy with friends.
intention: Jason wants to show off to the partygoers.
moral_action: Jason gathers a crowd outside and performs some acrobatic stunts like cartwheels.
moral_consequence: The crowd is impressed and cheers on Jason which makes him feel good.
immoral_action: Jason hurls himself into the air and lands on the dining table of the homeowner's and splitting in down the middle.
immoral_consequence: The crowd is shocked by Jason's actions and escort him out of the party for damaging the homeowner's property.

norm: Parents should protect their children.
situation: James' toddler throws an enormous fit every time James tries to put him in his car seat.
intention: James wants his toddler to be quiet during the car ride.
moral_action: James bribes his toddler with two cookies if he sits in the car seat.
moral_consequence: James' toddler sits quietly chewing on his cookies until they reach their destination.
immoral_action: James lets his toddler sit in the back with no car seat or seat belt.
immoral_consequence: When James is cut off in traffic and breaks suddenly, his toddler flies forward and gets a concussion from hitting his head on the seat.

norm: It's bad to show disrespect toward other people's beliefs.
situation: Sarah is looking through her social media feed and notices that an acquaintance of hers believes in a popular conspiracy theory.
intention: She wants to respond to the person who is expressing this belief.
moral_action: Sarah responds respectfully, that she does not believe this theory, and she posts links that disprove the conspiracy.
moral_consequence: The person is still not convinced, but they feel respected and are much more inclined to keep an open mind about their beliefs.
immoral_action: Sarah responds to the post by indicating that the conspiracy theory is completely crazy, and so must be anyone who believes it to be true.
immoral_consequence: The person is hurt and outraged by Sarah's response and their belief in the conspiracy is galvanized by the personal attack.

norm: It's good to be honest with your parents.
situation: Liza is off at college, and she has decided to start a page on the internet with dirty pictures as a job.
intention: Liza wants to earn money for her college years.
moral_action: Liza tells her parents about her unconventional job when they ask if she has found work.
moral_consequence: Liza's parents are glad she has told them about this, and they have a chance to talk to her about it.
immoral_action: Liza tells her parents she is working at a pizza restaurant and does not mention her webpage.
immoral_consequence: Liza's parents find out about her webpage from a friend of the family, and they are very upset with Liza.

norm: It's bad to give people predatory advice.
situation: Daiki's best friend Hoshi asks him how to approach his crush online.
intention: Daiki wants to be helpful.
moral_action: Daiki arranges a meeting between Hoshi and his crush in an online chat room.
moral_consequence: Hoshi makes friends with everyone in the chat room.
immoral_action: Daiki tells Hoshi that he should send messages about her personal posts multiple times to start a conversation.
immoral_consequence: Hoshi is blocked by his crush.

norm: You should not interfere with someone else's money.
situation: Paul is at his friends house having dinner when the topic turns to finances and investments.
intention: Paul wants to sound smart and impress his friends.
moral_action: Paul mentions that he keeps part of his savings in bitcoin and it has given him good returns.
moral_consequence: Paul's friend researches bitcoin later that night and decides it isn't worth the risk, but he still enjoys discussing money with Paul.
immoral_action: Paul pressures his friend to move a large amount of his savings into bitcoin.
immoral_consequence: Paul's friend loses thousands of dollars in the next year as bitcoin prices decline, causing him to be angry with Paul.

norm: You shouldn't abuse medication.
situation: Xavier gets his wisdom teeth removed and is prescribed a sedative to help him with the pain.
intention: Xavier wants to block out the pain.
moral_action: Xavier takes the sedatives to dull the pain and deals with the pain when it's not so bad.
moral_consequence: Xavier learns to deal with the pain and continues to function as normal.
immoral_action: Xavier takes more than the recommended dose of sedatives, so he feels less pain.
immoral_consequence: Xavier becomes dependent on the sedatives and finds ways to get more, becoming an addict.

norm: It is important to give your children good names.
situation: Elon and his girlfriend are expecting a baby boy in the spring.
intention: Elon wants to pick out a name for his son.
moral_action: Elon gives his son a strong name after a member of the family.
moral_consequence: Elon's son feels acceptance for his name.
immoral_action: Elon names his son after a random string of special characters, numbers, and letters.
immoral_consequence: Elon's son grows up with the stigma of having a strange name.

norm: It is good to prevent crime.
situation: Josh is about to enter a convenience store when he sees an armed robber through the window.
intention: Josh wants to avoid getting hurt.
moral_action: Josh gets to safety and calls the police.
moral_consequence: Josh is relieved that the thief is apprehended with no one getting hurt.
immoral_action: Josh is too scared to get involved, so he runs away.
immoral_consequence: Josh feels like a coward later.

norm: You should not back out on your commitments.
situation: Charles pledged money for a community construction project and needs to pay it, but has fallen on hard times.
intention: Charles wants to have enough money to survive.
moral_action: Charles pays his pledge and gets a loan from a family member to keep afloat.
moral_consequence: The community project is able to continue right away and is quickly finished.
immoral_action: Charles tells the community project leaders that he won't be able to fulfill his pledge.
immoral_consequence: The community project doesn't have the money that it needs and is delayed by six months.

norm: It's nice to decorate your house.
situation: Angelica saved up money to buy a new house and is moving to her new house.
intention: Angelica wants to throw a party at her new place.
moral_action: Angelica invites her friends for the party after all the furniture in the house had been delivered and decorates the house.
moral_consequence: Her friends admire Angelica's new home, and they all feel at home.
immoral_action: Angelica invites her friends to her new house while it is still unfurnished.
immoral_consequence: Her friends admire the open space but feel uncomfortable and unwelcome.

norm: It is dark to hope for your own death.
situation: Angel is a poet who has published a few books and many pieces in periodicals, over her career, but hasn’t sold any of her work for the past year.
intention: Angel wants to publish some new work.
moral_action: Angel's new poem talks about her depression but turns toward a hopeful tone as she also talks about the work she loves, writing poetry.
moral_consequence: Her readers find the work to be inspirational and it sparks more success, and she is proud of her work when she talks about it to her family and friends.
immoral_action: Angel publishes a poem in which she details her depression and states that she hopes she doesn't live much longer.
immoral_consequence: Her readers find the poem disturbing and it is not well reviewed, and her family and friends become deeply concerned about her welfare.

norm: You should have empathy for those less fortunate than yourself.
situation: While walking back to home Jasmine sees a homeless man with a sign asking for help.
intention: Jasmine wants to talk to the man.
moral_action: Jasmine listens to the man patiently and offers a small monetary help.
moral_consequence: Jasmine feels warm seeing a smile on the homelessman.
immoral_action: Jasmine asks the homeless man about his story and tells the man to get over it and start working.
immoral_consequence: Jasmine feels guilty about her action as she remembers the similar story of her grandfather.

norm: It's wrong to lead on other people if you're married.
situation: Jenna, who was married to John, gained ten pounds and felt very unhappy about how her body was changing.
intention: Jenna wants reassurance that she's still attractive.
moral_action: Jenna poses for naked photos and turns them into a calendar for John.
moral_consequence: John tells Jenna in detail about how beautiful she is in each of the photos.
immoral_action: Jenna starts going to bars and flirting with various people to see if they're attracted to her.
immoral_consequence: John says that Jenna's flirting makes him worry about whether he's still attractive to her.

norm: Arguing is impolite.
situation: Amber and Chris are having dinner at her parents non-smoking house, and Chris just lit up a cigarette at the table.
intention: Amber wants to confront Chris.
moral_action: Amber calmly tells Chris that her parents don't smoke, and asks him to please put out his cigarette.
moral_consequence: Amber's parent's appreciate her and Chris handling the issue like adults, and they all enjoy dinner.
immoral_action: Amber begins to yell at Chris, accusing him of knowingly breaking the non-smoking rule, so he yells back.
immoral_consequence: Amber's parent's ask them to both leave for their childish behavior.

norm: You shouldn't let your small kids wear makeup.
situation: Jenna's seven year old daughter saw her putting on makeup and said she wanted to wear it too.
intention: Jenna wants to make her daughter happy.
moral_action: Jenna distracts her daughter by suggesting that they bake cookies together.
moral_consequence: Jenna and her daughter have a pleasant afternoon baking cookies and the daughter forgets about the makeup.
immoral_action: Jenna gives her daughter a full makeover and lets her go to school that way.
immoral_consequence: Jenna's daughter's teacher sends home a note asking Jenna not to allow makeup again.

norm: It's not okay to physically harm an infant.
situation: Carrie is at her neighbor's house babysitting when their infant begins to cry.
intention: Carrie wants to quiet the baby.
moral_action: Carrie rocks the baby in her arms as she sings to it.
moral_consequence: Carrie is relieved after the baby stops and begins to smile at her.
immoral_action: Carrie picks the baby up out of its crib and begins to quickly shake it.
immoral_consequence: Carrie must face the consequences after she realizes the baby is no longer conscious.

norm: It's bad when someone's behavior is too bratty.
situation: Darlene is in a toy store with her mom when she sees a toy she wants.
intention: Darlene wants to ask for the toy.
moral_action: Darlene tells her mom she will do chores for the toy.
moral_consequence: Darlene's mom will agree with Darlene and get her the toy for chores.
immoral_action: Darlene lays on the ground and refuses to move unless she gets the toy.
immoral_consequence: Darlene's mom will think Darlene is misbehaving and pick her up and take her home without the toy.

norm: It's kind to include others in your activities.
situation: Dan is going to the beach with his friends and his little sister asks if she can come along.
intention: Dan wants to tell his sister if she can come with him to the beach.
moral_action: Dan say's his sister can come to the beach with him and his friends as long as she behaves herself.
moral_consequence: Dan's sister feels like she can be part of the fun because Dan is bringing her to the beach.
immoral_action: Dan tells his sister that she's too young to come the beach with him and his friends.
immoral_consequence: Dan's sister feels left out because Dan won't take her to the beach with him.

norm: Using a disability as an excuse is shameful.
situation: Joey has been diagnosed with ADHD at an early age and is struggling with a college course because he skips the homework.
intention: Joey wants to explain to his professor why his test scores are so low.
moral_action: Joey admits that he could do better if he focused on completing the work.
moral_consequence: Joey's professor is surprised by his honesty and offers him some extra credit assignments.
immoral_action: Joey blames his performance on the fact that he has ADHD.
immoral_consequence: Joey's professor feels like he is not doing enough to accommodate his disabled students.

norm: It's not okay to gamble funds beyond your means
situation: Cassidy and Danny are playing slots at a casino, and Danny wants Cassidy to put more rounds on her credit card.
intention: Cassidy wants to have fun.
moral_action: Cassidy suggests that they spend the afternoon at the casino's pool.
moral_consequence: Cassidy and Danial have fun swimming with others in the pool.
immoral_action: Cassidy pays for ten credits on the slot machine.
immoral_consequence: Cassidy's card is hit with overdraft fees.

norm: You shouldn't interrupt people when they are talking.
situation: Uriel, a six year old, wants his mother to drive him to his friend's house, but his mother is talking on the phone.
intention: Uriel wants to spend time with his friend.
moral_action: Uriel sends a text to his best friend inviting him over to his house.
moral_consequence: Uriel's mother orders pizza for Uriel and his friend after getting off the phone.
immoral_action: Uriel asks his mother to take him to his friends house in a loud tone as she talks.
immoral_consequence: Uriel is put into time out by his mother.

norm: It's wrong to not help others when they need it.
situation: Matt is the manager of a grocery store, and one of his cashiers is asking for a raise because they're struggling.
intention: Matt has to decide whether the cashier should get a raise.
moral_action: Matt decides that the cashier should get a raise and offers them a living wage.
moral_consequence: The cashier feels grateful for Matt and feels more loyal to the grocery store.
immoral_action: Matt chooses not to give his cashier a raise because he doesn't think they work hard enough.
immoral_consequence: The cashier continues to struggle and has to look for a 2nd job to get by.

norm: It's not okay to insult people when having a confrontation.
situation: Bob and Lee were having a disagreement about a project they were working on at work.
intention: Bob wants to get his way.
moral_action: Bob takes his time explaining to Lee why he wants to do it a certain way.
moral_consequence: Lee agrees with Bob, and they work on the project under Bob's direction.
immoral_action: Bob punches Lee out and knocks him unconscious, leaving Bob to work on the project alone.
immoral_consequence: Bob's boss finds out and terminates Bob from his position immediately.

norm: You shouldn't have an affair.
situation: Cage has been married for five years, and his boss is flirting with him after work.
intention: Cage doesn't want to offend his boss.
moral_action: Cage shows his boss pictures of his good looking single friend and sets him up on a blind date.
moral_consequence: Cage's boss meets his future husband during the date.
immoral_action: Cage goes along with his boss' advances kissing him.
immoral_consequence: Cage's boss is written up by HR for abusing his authority.

norm: You shouldn't get mad at people and throw a fit.
situation: Bill is playing softball and disagrees with the umpire's call that he was out.
intention: Bill wants to question why the call happened.
moral_action: Bill expresses his dispute to his coach, and they both talk to the umpire who explains the call to their satisfaction.
moral_consequence: Bill continues to play and helps lead the team to a comeback victory.
immoral_action: Bill gets in the umpire's face and shouts at him asking if he is blind.
immoral_consequence: Bill is kicked out of the game and asked by his teammates not to come back.

norm: It's wrong to scam your friends.
situation: Francine works for a pyramid scheme and has several friends who are looking for money making opportunities.
intention: Francine wants to add people to her network and increase her profits.
moral_action: Francine tells her friends that the pyramid scheme isn't a great money maker and instead advertises the scheme to random people online.
moral_consequence: Francine's friends appreciate her honesty and help her find people to add to her network.
immoral_action: Francine tells her friends that joining her pyramid scheme will guarantee them a lot more money than it does.
immoral_consequence: Francine's friends join, find out that it's a scam, and stop being friends with her.

norm: You shouldn't give a fake credit card to people.
situation: Larry's lawnmower has broke, and he went to a store to buy a new one.
intention: Larry wants to pay using a credit card.
moral_action: Larry pays for his new lawnmower with his new credit card.
moral_consequence: Larry has a new, working lawnmower.
immoral_action: Larry pays for his new lawnmower with a fake credit card linked to a stolent identity.
immoral_consequence: Larry's fake credit card is discovered, and he is arrested for fraud.

norm: It's rude to cancel plans you have made with someone.
situation: On his way to a concert with John, Dave steps into a pothole and injures his ankle, prompting John to ask if Dave can still attend the concert as planned.
intention: Dave wants to respond to John's question.
moral_action: Dave tells John that he just needs to get to his seat, and he'll be fine, he just needs some pain killers, so he'll go.
moral_consequence: John is delighted that their plans are still intact and vows to help his friend move around if needed.
immoral_action: Dave tells John that his ankle is really painful and that there's no way he can go now, he'll have to cancel.
immoral_consequence: John is sad as they've planned the concert for months and now isn't so sure he wants to go either.

norm: It's rude to steal your colleagues' lunches.
situation: Bob is at work when he realizes that he forgot to bring his lunch with him.
intention: Bob wants to have something to eat.
moral_action: Bob goes downstairs and orders food from the work cafeteria.
moral_consequence: Bob is full after eating his meal and remembers to bring his food to work the next day.
immoral_action: Bob takes some of the food from a coworkers lunch box in the office fridge.
immoral_consequence: Bob is called into his boss's office and loses a day's worth of pay.

norm: It's wrong to be distracted when you're out in public.
situation: Frank is using a paper map to guide his family around an amusement park.
intention: Frank wants to not get lost.
moral_action: Frank divides his attention between the map and keeping track of his family.
moral_consequence: Frank successfully guides his family around the park.
immoral_action: Frank focuses his full attention on reading the map.
immoral_consequence: Frank gets separated from is family because of his inattention.

norm: It is rude to desecrate a grave.
situation: James' high school bully Andy was hit by a bus and buried in a local cemetary.
intention: James wants closure on his resentment towards Andy.
moral_action: James writes a letter to Andy about all of his resentment, then burns it.
moral_consequence: James feels like writing the letter helped him let go of high school.
immoral_action: James knocks over Andy's tombstone and pees on his grave.
immoral_consequence: James is caught by the caretaker and hauled off to jail.

norm: It's good to enjoy your new pets.
situation: Sandy just got a new dog who is a handful to deal with because he is young.
intention: Sandy wants to spend time with the dog.
moral_action: Sandy loves her pet even though he is young and not house trained.
moral_consequence: Sandy allows herself to develop more of a bond with the dog.
immoral_action: Sandy doesn't have a good time because the dog uses the bathroom in the house.
immoral_consequence: Sandy is tired of cleaning up after her pet and shows it less affection.

norm: People shouldn't gross out others by being stinky and dirty.
situation: Brandon is working out at the gym in the morning and gets really sweaty.
intention: Brandon wants to hang out with friends after exercising.
moral_action: Brandon takes a shower before going to see his friends.
moral_consequence: Brandon and his friends have a great time.
immoral_action: Brandon leaves straight from the gym to see his friends, without taking a shower.
immoral_consequence: Brandon's friends all avoid being near him.

norm: You shouldn't go back on your word.
situation: Mark has agreed to help George paint his house on the weekend.
intention: Mark wants to have a fun weekend.
moral_action: Mark asks other friends to join him and George for a house painting party.
moral_consequence: Mark is able to help George and have a good time with his friends.
immoral_action: Mark cancels his plans with George and goes to the shore for the weekend.
immoral_consequence: Mark feels bad for bailing on George so isn't able to fully enjoy himself.

norm: It's rude to forget somebody gave you a gift
situation: "Steve is at John's house and notices that John is still using the small rug Steve bought him years ago and says 'oh wow you still like that rug huh?""."
intention: John wants to respond to Steve's statement about the rug.
moral_action: John tells Steve that yeah he does love that rug and is so glad Steve gifted it to him years ago.
moral_consequence: Steve is delighted that his friend is getting such long use out of his gift and that he remembers he gave it to him.
immoral_action: John tells Steve that yeah he does as he likes the style, but he cannot remember where he bought it.
immoral_consequence: Steve is annoyed that John doesn't even remember that Steve bought it for him and thinks he bought it himself.

norm: It's wrong to disrespect a person's mother.
situation: Clayton is trying to comfort his best friend Maurice who was punished by his parents for low grades.
intention: Clayton wants Maurice to make Maurice smile.
moral_action: Clayton recites an inspirational quote and offers to help Maurice study.
moral_consequence: With Clayton's help Maurice's grades start improving.
immoral_action: Clayton makes a silly impersonation of Maurice's parents.
immoral_consequence: Maurice's parents forbids Maurice from hanging out  with Clayton after discovering his actions.

norm: It's bad to abandon someone without a ride.
situation: Stanley is sitting in his car when a colleague pleads with him for a ride home.
intention: Stanley wants to respond to his colleague's request.
moral_action: Stanley accepts his colleague's request and asks where he wants to go.
moral_consequence: Stanley's colleague becomes more helpful and friendly towards Stanley.
immoral_action: Stanley decides to say no to his colleague and drives away.
immoral_consequence: Stanley's colleague starts giving Stanley the cold shoulder afterwards.

norm: It's wrong to disobey an officer.
situation: Tom is pulled over by a police officer for speeding.
intention: Tom wants to get out of having to pay for a speeding ticket.
moral_action: Tom tells the police officer that his wife is in labor, and he is rushing to the hospital.
moral_consequence: Tom is allowed to go on his way without being fined.
immoral_action: Tom refuses to provide identification or cooperate with the officer in any way.
immoral_consequence: Tom is arrested for failure to comply with the officer's requests.

norm: It's good to encourage your kids.
situation: Mike, a doctor, is listening to his kid Joey talk about his dreams of becoming a fireman.
intention: Mike wants his kid to admire him.
moral_action: Mike tells Joey he can be anything he wants to be, and he supports him.
moral_consequence: Joey pursues his dream, is happy and has high self-esteem.
immoral_action: Mike tells Joey that a doctor is a more respectable job.
immoral_consequence: Joey gives up his fireman dream and loses self-esteem.

norm: It's wrong to steal food.
situation: Peter is with his mother at the market when he notices a stand full of delicious desserts.
intention: Peter wants to get some chocolate.
moral_action: Peter asks his mother if she would be willing to buy him a bar of chocolate.
moral_consequence: Peter's mother agrees to purchase the chocolate bar for Peter and puts it in her shopping cart.
immoral_action: Peter walks over to the counter and takes a chocolate bar and puts it in his pocket without paying.
immoral_consequence: Peter's mother later on notices that he's eating chocolate she didn't pay for and gets very angry.

norm: You shouldn't marry someone that cheats on you.
situation: Jane's boyfriend, who has cheated on her several times with other women, asks her to marry him.
intention: Jane wants to tell her boyfriend if she'll marry him.
moral_action: Jane refuses to marry her boyfriend, and they end up breaking up.
moral_consequence: Jane is spared an unhealthy marriage and soon finds a partner she can trust.
immoral_action: Jane accepts her boyfriend's marriage proposal, and they get married.
immoral_consequence: Jane's boyfriend keeps cheating on her when he is her husband, and she is unhappy in the marriage.

norm: It's wrong to cause stress at a family function.
situation: Henry is celebrating Christmas at a large family gathering and his bother has made a disrespectful comment towards him.
intention: Henry wants to give his brother a piece of his mind.
moral_action: Henry decides to wait until after Christmas to bring up the issue to his brother.
moral_consequence: Henry's family end up having a nice Christmas celebration overall.
immoral_action: Henry starts getting into it with his brother immediately at the gathering.
immoral_consequence: Henry's family is disturbed by the fight that they are having.

norm: You shouldn't base a relationship on looks
situation: Jamie has a crush on Angel who is beautiful but mean, and he knows that Michelle being an average but nice girl loves him.
intention: Jamie wants to get a girlfriend.
moral_action: Jamie admiring Michelle's niceness asks her to be his girlfriend and forgets about Angel.
moral_consequence: Michelle agrees to be his girlfriend, and she takes care of Jamie very well.
immoral_action: Jamie being fascinated by Angel's charm asks her to be his girlfriend and Angel agrees.
immoral_consequence: Michelle feels sad and depressed because she loves Jamie so much.

norm: You shouldn't stalk people on social media.
situation: Finn has an acquaintance who he has recently taken more of an interest in.
intention: Finn wants to get to know his acquaintance better.
moral_action: Finn engages in conversation to get to know the acquaintance more.
moral_consequence: The girl gets to know Finn better at the same time, and they hit it off.
immoral_action: Finn goes through his acquaintance's social media to find out more about her.
immoral_consequence: The girl finds out that he's been looking through her profile and pulls away.

norm: You shouldn't lie to your classmates.
situation: Rodney is in university and his friends are talking about their upcoming internships.
intention: Rodney wants to join the conversation.
moral_action: Rodney asks his friends what are good internships to apply to.
moral_consequence: Rodney will be able to find a great internship.
immoral_action: Rodney says he has a great internship which is not true.
immoral_consequence: Rodney will have to keep up with his lie and become stressed.

norm: It's not okay for police to abuse their authority.
situation: Andy being a policeman has had an argument with his wife recently, and he feels sad and stressed.
intention: Andy wants to take care of his stress.
moral_action: Andy takes a day off, stays home and calms himself down.
moral_consequence: Andy's colleague messages him asking why he hasn't been to work and tells him to take care of himself.
immoral_action: Andy swears at a suspect at the scene of a crime to release his stress.
immoral_consequence: Andy's colleague feels bad and thinks that he is acting inappropriately.

norm: It is wrong to be sexist.
situation: Don is hosting a beauty pageant on live tv.
intention: Don wants to be with many women and appear confident.
moral_action: Don makes respectful complimentary remarks about the contestants on the show.
moral_consequence: Many women find Don charming and attractive and like him.
immoral_action: Don makes sexist jokes about the contestants and says he can get any woman he wants.
immoral_consequence: Many women are turned off by him and file lawsuits against him in court.

norm: You shouldn't drive fast in a residential neighborhood.
situation: Alex is trying to get home in time to watch the game.
intention: Alex wants to get home quickly.
moral_action: Alex takes a short cut to arrive home more quickly.
moral_consequence: Alex gets home safely just in time to watch the game.
immoral_action: Alex exceeds the speed limit and doesn't slow down at stop signs on his way home.
immoral_consequence: Alex gets pulled over, is issued a ticket and misses the beginning of the game.

norm: It is wrong to discriminate against people for being different
situation: Ron is annoyed by his new friend, Bruce, who eats strange foods and behaves differently from Ron's other friends.
intention: Ron has to decide whether or not to end his friendship with Bruce.
moral_action: Ron talks to Bruce about what is bothering him, and Bruce explains some of his behaviors in more detail.
moral_consequence: Ron understands Bruce more than before and actually respects some of the behaviors that he previously found strange, and Bruce feels more confident and comfortable in their friendship.
immoral_action: Ron decides that his new friend is just too different from what he is used to, and stops responding to his calls and text messages.
immoral_consequence: Bruce is hurt and confused by Ron's refusal to communicate with him, and Ron feels like he has failed to be a real friend for inconsequential reasons.

norm: You should consider how your actions will effect other people.
situation: Jack is driving on the interstate as his family heads to see relatives that reside in another state.
intention: Jack wants to reach his destination quickly.
moral_action: Jack sets his cruise control above the speed limit and uses the left lane to pass when he catches a slower vehicle.
moral_consequence: Jack fits in smoothly with the other cars on the highway and his family feels secure.
immoral_action: Jack weaves in and out of traffic to pass slow moving cars on the highway.
immoral_consequence: Jack almost causes a number of accidents and makes the family members travelling with him feel nervous.

norm: It's wrong to cheat on someone you're with.
situation: While on a date with Olivia at a restaurant, Mick sees his ex-girlfriend Patty.
intention: Mick wants to talk to Patty.
moral_action: Mick greets Patty in a friendly manner and introduces her to Olivia.
moral_consequence: Olivia and Patty talk and trade funny stories about Mick.
immoral_action: Mick says hi to Patty and gives her a long kiss on the lips in front of Olivia.
immoral_consequence: Olivia becomes furious with Mick and breaks up with him in the restaurant.

norm: It's important to get along with other people
situation: When James met his three roommates at summer camp, it seemed like they had nothing in common.
intention: James wants to spend the summer focused on his own interests.
moral_action: James goes off on his own during the day, but chats with his roommates about their activities at night.
moral_consequence: Some of James' best memories from camp turn out to be the late night conversations.
