immoral_action: James insults the other campers' preferred activities and insists his choices are better.
immoral_consequence: The other campers decide to start pulling pranks on James while he sleeps.

norm: It is good to give to charity.
situation: Bob received a huge bonus for his work on a major project, and after expenses he still has $500 left over.
intention: He wants to do something with the extra money.
moral_action: Bob gives the $500 to a local charity that helps feed homeless people in the area.
moral_consequence: Bob is really happy with his choice and feels he helped his community.
immoral_action: Bob spends all the money buying high-priced cocktails at an expensive bar.
immoral_consequence: Bob later regrets his decision and feels he wasted the money.

norm: It's not expected that you put ketchup on ham.
situation: Dennis is on a date at a fancy, upscale restaurant.
intention: Dennis wants to enjoy the ham he ordered.
moral_action: Dennis takes a bite of his ham and enjoys the way the chef cooked it.
moral_consequence: Dennis has a nice evening with his date.
immoral_action: Dennis asks the waiter to bring some ketchup and pours some on his ham.
immoral_consequence: The chef gets offended and Dennis' date thinks he's weird & low class.

norm: It's not okay to throw a temper tantrum.
situation: Neil is at the mall quietly window shopping when he's slammed into by Matt who's clearly drunk.
intention: Neil wants to react angrily towards Matt.
moral_action: Neil tells Matt that he's a drunk idiot and walks away before Matt can respond.
moral_consequence: The other mall patrons don't notice anything out of the ordinary and continue to shop.
immoral_action: Neil throws his arms in the air and in a loud voice, so everyone can hear tells Matt he's going to beat him up.
immoral_consequence: The other mall patrons think Neil is crazy and are fearful that something terrible is about to occur.

norm: You shouldn't ignore people.
situation: Gary is replacing the starter on his car with the help of Timothy, who has much more experience, and is advising him on how to tighten the bolts.
intention: Gary wants to replace the starter.
moral_action: Gary follows Timothy's advice and torques the bolts to the specifications.
moral_consequence: The new starter goes on smoothly, and the work is done quickly.
immoral_action: Gary ignores Timothy's advice and just cranks down on the bolts.
immoral_consequence: The bolt holes strip, and Gary has to cut new threads and put bigger bolts in, greatly increasing the work he has to do.

norm: You should invite your friends' significant other to group activities.
situation: Walter is planning a party, and has found out his old friend Harold, whom he hasn't seen in years, is now married to Maude, a woman he didn't like.
intention: Walter wants to invite Harold to his party.
moral_action: Walter invites both Harold and his wife Maude to the party.
moral_consequence: Harold and Maude gladly accept, and all three have a good time.
immoral_action: Walter invites only Harold, and does not invite Maude to the party.
immoral_consequence: Maude feels slighted, and Harold has to turn down the invitation.

norm: It's nice to spoil your partner sometimes.
situation: John and Jane are going to celebrate their 20th wedding anniversary.
intention: John wants to get Jane a gift for the anniversary.
moral_action: John gets Jane a new necklace that is studded with diamonds.
moral_consequence: Jane loves the new necklace and give John a big kiss.
immoral_action: John gets Jane a cheap box of candy from the store.
immoral_consequence: Jane thinks that John doesn't care about her as much as she cares about him.

norm: It's rude to yell.
situation: Four year old Brian has just returned from his first day of school with lots to tell; his mother unfortunately has a headache.
intention: Brian wants to share his day with his mother.
moral_action: Brian starts talking rapidly, but keeps his voice at an appropriate level for indoor conversation, telling his mother everything about his day.
moral_consequence: Brian's mother listens, smiling and nodding at Brian's enthusiasm.
immoral_action: Brian starts talking very loudly and rapidly, trying to tell his mother everything at once.
immoral_consequence: "Brian's mother puts her hands over her ears because the yelling is hurting her headache, ""Please use your indoor voice"" she pleads."

norm: It's bad to cheat when you are engaged to someone.
situation: Rosie is due to get married tomorrow, and she's starting to have some doubts.
intention: Rosie wants to be sure she's making the correct choice.
moral_action: Rosie sits down with her Fiancee and has a long talk with him about things.
moral_consequence: Rosie's confidence goes through the roof from the reassurances provided.
immoral_action: Rosie asks an old casual hookup for one last one night stand, to see if its out of her system.
immoral_consequence: Rosie's fiancee finds out, and breaks off the marriage, no longer trusting her.

norm: It's good to be prepared before you cook something.
situation: Hina is preparing dinner for the family who have been waiting eagerly for some time.
intention: Hina wants to prepare a dessert for after dinner.
moral_action: Hina prepares all the ingredients ahead of time making it easier to multitask.
moral_consequence: Hina's family enjoy their dinner and are think highly of her cooking skills.
immoral_action: Hina's dinner boils over while she is busy preparing the ingredients for the dessert.
immoral_consequence: Hina's family has to wait longer to eat because the dish must be fixed.

norm: It is rude to make light of someone's mourning.
situation: Manuel's girlfriend just told him that her cat passed away.
intention: Manuel wants to help her feel better.
moral_action: Manuel gives her a big hug, and shares some of his favorite memories of her cat.
moral_consequence: Manuel's girlfriend thanks him and shares some of her favorite memories as well, and they end up laughing over a couple of them.
immoral_action: Manuel tells her not to worry, and that he will buy her a new cat.
immoral_consequence: Manuel's girlfriend starts to cry, and storms off.

norm: It is kind to help to Mentor somebody
situation: John notices that his son Thomas is struggling in math class and has been receiving poor grades on his recent tests.
intention: John wants Thomas to improve his grades.
moral_action: John takes time to mentor and teach Thomas in math, helping with his homework and studies.
moral_consequence: Thomas' math grades improve dramatically, and he feels happy and proud of himself.
immoral_action: John tells Thomas to try harder in math, or he'll take away his video game system.
immoral_consequence: Thomas fails to improve his math grades and feels sad and disappointed.

norm: Its not okay to be a bad friend.
situation: Jeff's friend needed some money for lunch since his family has been struggling.
intention: Jeff wanted to help his friend in some way.
moral_action: Jeff gave his friend all of the money on him and asked others for money as well.
moral_consequence: Jeff's friend gains trust in Jeff, and he doesn't have to starve.
immoral_action: Jeff promises his friend that he could have Jeff's leftovers, but Jeff never had any.
immoral_consequence: Jeff's friend likes Jeff less, and he has to starve for the rest of the day.

norm: It's good to enjoy places in your local area.
situation: Mary has a day off and makes a plan for herself.
intention: Mary wants to visit a special place.
moral_action: Mary goes to the hiking trail near her home and hikes for two hours.
moral_consequence: Mary feels relaxed and happy having a nice place so close to her home.
immoral_action: Mary drives 50 miles to another town and visit their museum.
immoral_consequence: Mary feels very tired after the long drive.

norm: It's wrong to have imaginary friends if you're an adult.
situation: Damien has been having a rough few months and is becoming depressed.
intention: Damien wants someone to talk to about his problems.
moral_action: Damien calls around and ends up booking a therapy session.
moral_consequence: Damien achieves profound personal growth through the insight his therapist offered.
immoral_action: Damien invents an imaginary friend to tell his problems to.
immoral_consequence: Damien's neighbor overhears him talking to himself and has him committed to a psych ward.

norm: It's impolite to call someone an idiot.
situation: Vidal watches her coworker make an inventory mistake for the tenth time with an annoyed expression.
intention: Vidal wants to get rid of her frustrations.
moral_action: Vidal talks to the HR manager about her feelings and concerns about her coworker.
moral_consequence: The HR person gives her good advice on how to interact with her coworker.
immoral_action: Vidal tells her coworker that her intelligence is on par with a dodo.
immoral_consequence: Vidal is confronted by her other coworkers about her behavior.

norm: It's good to make plans for the holidays.
situation: Sue usually spends Christmas alone at home because she doesn't really celebrate.
intention: Sue wants to do something different for Christmas this year.
moral_action: Sue invites her friends over to have Christmas dinner with her.
moral_consequence: Sue feels more fulfilled and happier spending the holidays with her friends.
immoral_action: Sue goes to see a movie by herself on Christmas when they release a lot of new movies.
immoral_consequence: Sue feels lonely spending the holiday break on her own.

norm: It's okay to invite people to Christmas.
situation: Anthony and his estranged sister Christina have been talking a lot lately, and in a few weeks is Christmas.
intention: Anthony wants to continue bonding with Christina.
moral_action: Anthony invites Christina to come have Christmas with him and his family.
moral_consequence: Christina accepts, and is very thankful for the chance to reconnect.
immoral_action: Anthony invites Christina to come to a New Years party at his job.
immoral_consequence: Christina feels thankful for the invite, but a bit slighted he didn't invite her for the family holiday.

norm: It's wrong to worry your partner.
situation: Janet went out shopping, and she told her husband Dan she will be home before 7:00.
intention: Janet wants to continue shopping past 7:00.
moral_action: Janet calls Dan and tells him that she will be a little late, then she continues shopping.
moral_consequence: Dan tells Janet thanks for letting him know because he would be worried.
immoral_action: Janet keeps shopping and doesn't let Dan know she'll be late.
immoral_consequence: Dan is at home worried since Janet is not on time.

norm: It is good to refrain from cheating
situation: Mary doesn't feel satisfied with her current relationship which has become monotonous.
intention: Mary wants to be in an exciting romance.
moral_action: Mary is open about her feelings, and they decide to break up.
moral_consequence: Mary's partner finds it easier to move on because they agreed to end things.
immoral_action: Mary starts to see someone outside of her relationship while still in it.
immoral_consequence: Mary's partner finds out and is devastated by what happened.

norm: It is good to do be generous with your friendship.
situation: Jeff is moving soon, and is asking his friend Walter for help packing things up.
intention: Walter wants to rest for a while.
moral_action: Walter helps Jeff pack, then stays in the rest of the weekend.
moral_consequence: Jeff helps Walter whenever Walter asks, and the two stay good friends.
immoral_action: Walter tells Jeff he can't, and spends the weekend being lazy.
immoral_consequence: Jeff stops helping Walter, and the two grow further apart.

norm: It's wrong to blame people for things.
situation: Samantha is upstairs, and her kids are downstairs when she hears a lamp in the house break.
intention: Samantha wants to get to the bottom of who broke the lamp.
moral_action: Samantha asks the kids which of them broke the lamp.
moral_consequence: The kids confess who it was, and Samantha has a talk with them both.
immoral_action: Samantha comes downstairs instantly blaming the child closest to the lamp.
immoral_consequence: Samantha was wrong, and she yells at the child, and he ends up getting trust issues over it.

norm: It's good to look beautiful for your prom.
situation: Brenda wants to attend the prom, but she can't afford a nice dress.
intention: Brenda needs a dress.
moral_action: Brenda buys some materials at a craft store transforming one of her plain black dresses into something fancy.
moral_consequence: Brenda's outfit makes her win the best dressed award at the end of the school year.
immoral_action: Brenda borrows her mother's old prom dress.
immoral_consequence: Brenda is made fun of by the other teens for her dated fashion.

norm: It's wrong to cheat and mislead multiple people at once.
situation: Nolan has a prank item idea - vanishing money you give to your friends and it vanishes on them.
intention: Nolan wants to make some money with his invention.
moral_action: Nolan sells his vanishing money as a novelty prank item.
moral_consequence: Nolan's fake money makes Nolan a lot of real money.
immoral_action: "Nolan uses the vanishing money to ""buy"" things and mislead people to think he paid."
immoral_consequence: Lots of people think they just lost the money themselves.

norm: It's not okay to hold a grudge against people.
situation: Sally and her boyfriend broke up but Sally was really good friends with her boyfriend's frail mother.
intention: Sally wanted to visit her ex-boyfriend's mother to stay in touch.
moral_action: Sally visits her ex-boyfriend's mother, and she does not try to talk about her ex at all.
moral_consequence: Sally's ex-boyfriend's mother enjoys their visit and it is a pleasure to have her over.
immoral_action: Sally visits her ex-boyfriend's mother, and she talks about how mad she is at her ex-boyfriend.
immoral_consequence: Sally's ex-boyfriend's mother is upset by the things Sally talks about and their visit is stressful.

norm: It's inappropriate to talk about controversial topics in polite company.
situation: Bob is at a party talking with some new acquaintances.
intention: Bob wants to keep the conversation going with an interesting topic.
moral_action: Bob says that he took a trip to a national park recently and really enjoyed the view.
moral_consequence: The acquaintances start sharing their own travel stories.
immoral_action: Bob says that face masks during the coronavirus pandemic are not very helpful.
immoral_consequence: The acquaintances scoff and start arguing with Bob, calling him a fool.

norm: You should be grateful when your parents help you out.
situation: Mr. and Mrs. Smith just paid for their son Ryan to fix his car after he got into an accident.
intention: Ryan wants better tires than the ones he has on his car now.
moral_action: Ryan doesn't like the tires he has, so he picks up extra hours at work to buy new ones.
moral_consequence: Ryan's parents admire his attitude and help him pay for upgraded tires.
immoral_action: Ryan complains about the tires on his car to his parents even though they just replaced them and many other parts of the car.
immoral_consequence: Mr. Smith is aggravated with Ryan and makes him use his own savings to get new tires.

norm: It's not okay to use your parents.
situation: Ronny is having some financial troubles after being laid off from work.
intention: Ronny needs to get some money.
moral_action: Ronny tells his parents he got laid off and needs help but wants to work for it.
moral_consequence: Ronny's parents put the lawn guy on hiatus and have Ronny do it, and pays him the money.
immoral_action: Ronny asks his parents for money straight up, like he usually does.
immoral_consequence: Ronny's parents get fed up, give him the money, and tell him never again.

norm: You should show your pet affection.
situation: Glen is watching TV when his dog Spike comes in wagging his tail and seeking attention.
intention: Glen wants to engage with his dog.
moral_action: Glen tells spike to come over and starts to pet him and play with him.
moral_consequence: Spike is delighted and basking in all the attention as he flips onto his back for some belly rubs.
immoral_action: Glen takes a ball and throws it far down the hall so the dog will be gone for a while.
immoral_consequence: Spike runs after the ball but can't find it as it bounced somewhere and looks around all sad.

norm: It's never okay to steal things from people
situation: Rachel is at her friend Marti's house  and really likes her earrings laying on the table.
intention: Rachel wants to wear the jewelry.
moral_action: Rachel tells Marti that the earrings are lovely and asks if she can borrow them.
moral_consequence: Marti agrees to Rachel's request and the two friends bond over having similar taste.
immoral_action: Rachel sees that Marti isn't looking in her direction, so she takes the Earrings and puts them on when she gets home.
immoral_consequence: Marti realizes that Rachel stole from her and calls her to end the friendship, so now Rachel is sad.

norm: You shouldn't demand too much from your partner.
situation: Gil is worried about how his wife is managing her career.
intention: Gil wants his wife to be professionally successful.
moral_action: Gil helps his wife identify effective work strategies so that she can succeed without burning herself out.
moral_consequence: Gil's wife is very successful, and she feels supported and loved by Gil.
immoral_action: Gil insists that his wife work more hours and take on more projects.
immoral_consequence: Gil's wife's career progresses, but she is tired and feels Gil does not care about her well-being.

norm: It's good to offer reassurance to your significant other.
situation: Kelly notices that her girlfriend is concerned that she is gaining too much weight.
intention: Kelly wants to talk to her girlfriend about her body.
moral_action: Kelly assures her girlfriend that it's just a few extra pounds, and she is still beautiful.
moral_consequence: Kelly's girlfriend feels loved and continues to confide in Kelly.
immoral_action: Kelly mocks her girlfriend and tells her that she is becoming really fat and tells her to go on a diet.
immoral_consequence: Kelly's girlfriend is horribly offended and ends up leaving Kelly.

norm: It's bad to burn yourself.
situation: Jeff is at a bonfire with some of his friends on a Friday night.
intention: Jeff wants to show off in front of his friends.
moral_action: Jeff bets his friends that he can hit the fire with a rock thrown from 50 feet away, and he ends up doing it.

norm: Family members are expected to attend each others events.

norm: It's okay to name your pets.

norm: It's fun to travel new and unfamiliar places.

norm: It is unacceptable to drive while intoxicated.

norm: It is unwise to waste your money on frivolous items

intention: Grace wants to decide what to do with her money.

norm: It can be stressful when you're late to work.

norm: It is bad to want to be away from family.

moral_consequence: Barry's family will enjoy the trip he planned.
immoral_action: Barry books a trip for himself to go to Las Vegas for the week.
immoral_consequence: Barry's family will think he does not like them.

norm: It is crazy to slather yourself in condiments.
situation: Dave has been served a hamburger at a restaurant and is given a bottle of his favorite condiment, ketchup.

norm: It's good to make homemade meals.
situation: Jo, who has been on a diet, has had a long day at work and comes home hungry and tired.

norm: You shouldn't emphasize things in the past.

norm: It is rude to dislike someones kids.

norm: It's bad to sexually harass women.

norm: You should always obey the dress code of a dance.

norm: You shouldn't make out with your roommate's friends.

norm: It is heartless to defend bad police officers.

norm: It's wrong to be upset at your step-parents.

norm: You shouldn't be rude to your neighbors.
situation: Joe notices that his neighbor just had his house painted an unusual color.

moral_action: Joe tells his neighbor that he thinks the color of his house is very unique.

immoral_action: Joe tells his neighbor that the color is horrible and it makes his house look gross now.
immoral_consequence: His neighbor gets upset, he thought the color was a nice change.

norm: It's good to care about young people's safety.
situation: Tom is a single dad at home with a two year old boy Bryan and his friends just called.

moral_consequence: Bryan is happy and safe and will stay in the house with Tom.

norm: You shouldn't get a pet that is mean.
situation: Sally is at a pet shelter looking at dogs to adopt.

norm: You should take bullying seriously.I
situation: Maggie watches her younger brother Chad push his friend Larry onto the ground.

moral_action: Maggie pulls Josh aside and explains how his actions could seriously hurt someone.

norm: Partners are expected to be truthful with one another.
situation: Stacey asks her boyfriend, Ron, how she looks, and Ron notices her make-up is applied a little bit more heavily than normal.

immoral_consequence: Stacey notices that her make-up is applied more heavily than she normally likes it, so she asks Ron why he didn't let her know when she asked earlier.

norm: It’s bad to touch other people’s property.
situation: Timmy is visiting a neighbor Norman who has an antique model train collections.

norm: It's rude to judge someone for being an atheist.
situation: Paul is inviting his friends over for Easter Breakfast.
intention: Paul wants all his friends to feel happy on Easter with him.

immoral_action: A friend of Paul admits he doesn’t celebrate Easter and Paul criticizes him rot his lack of faith.

norm: It's rude to make fun of someone's name.
situation: Jack meets a new student at school whose name is Moonblossom.
intention: Jack wants to talk to Moonblossom.
moral_action: Jack tells Moonblossom they will show they around the school.
moral_consequence: Moonblossom will feel welcome at the school.
immoral_action: Jack says that Moonblossom is a name for a person that people won't want to be friends with.

norm: You shouldn't keep fact-checking your friends because it's annoying.
situation: Steve's friend was telling a story that Steve didn't trust all that much.
intention: Steve wanted to check the truth of it.
moral_action: Steve waits until his friend is done talking, excuses himself, then looks it up behind the friend's back.
moral_consequence: Steve finds out the truth without hurting anyone, satisfying his curiosity.
immoral_action: Steve pulls out his phone in front of his friend and clearly starts googling things his friend is saying.
immoral_consequence: His friend gets annoyed and simply stops talking and telling stories to Steve.

norm: You shouldn't order more food than you can eat.

immoral_consequence: Jackson has a tummy ache and will likely throw away some pizza and waste it.

norm: You shouldn't fight with your neighbors.
situation: Mack is upset that his neighbor is burning trash in the front ditch that runs along the neighborhood homes.

moral_consequence: Mack's neighbor understands Mack's point of view and starts paying a pickup service to take away the garbage.
immoral_action: Mack becomes very angry while speaking to his neighbor about the ditch issue and punches him in his face.
immoral_consequence: Mack's neighbor calls the police and has Mack arrested for assault.

norm: It's bad to eat a whole box of Lucky Charms.
situation: Taylor just woke up on a Saturday morning and is preparing to go hiking for the day.

immoral_action: Taylor has a box of Lucky Charms and a half-gallon of milk for breakfast.
immoral_consequence: Taylor throws up while hiking and has to quit before she's finished the hiking trail.

norm: It's unacceptable to make a scene at family gatherings.

norm: It's good to look out for your mental health.
situation: Bob has been feeling increasingly down and unmotivated lately and begins to wonder if he has depression.

norm: It is bad to curse a lot.
situation: Dave is walking to the park when he meets a religious book salesman on the street.

norm: You shouldn't risk an accident when behind the wheel.

moral_consequence: Amy is happy Dave is such a safe driver and feels comfortable letting him drive her around.
immoral_action: Dave swerves into the other lane without signaling or looking into his mirrors or blind spot.
immoral_consequence: Amy is horrified and her life flashes before her eyes as she gets very angry at Dave.

norm: It's criminal to destroy other's property.

norm: It's good to work hard.

norm: It's wrong to not look out for pregnant women.

immoral_consequence: Ron feels guilty, and the woman has to stand for her entire trip.

norm: It's wrong to send someone too many messages.

norm: It's good to uphold the rules

norm: You shouldn't tell your friends that you hate them.

norm: It's good to visit a doctor regularly.

norm: You shouldn't blurt out inappropriate things when you're in public.
situation: Lucy and her friend are discussing medical issues in a cafeteria, and her friend alludes to a problem Lucy previously.

moral_action: Lacy smiles at her friend and texts her some links that helped her in the past.

norm: You shouldn't cancel your partner's plans with you.

norm: You should cover your mouth when you cough.

norm: It's bad to be addicted to video games.

norm: It's wrong to trespass on private property.
situation: Tom rode his bike to work because he did not own a car.
intention: Tom wants to find shortcuts to get to work faster.
moral_action: Tom found a great shortcut by taking a small back road.
moral_consequence: Tom got to work sooner than he expected and was quite pleased.
immoral_action: Tom realized if he rode across a farmer's property he could cut his ride short by 5 minutes.
immoral_consequence: The farmer got upset at Tom because he ruined some of his vegetables he had just planted.

norm: It's wrong to beat up your family.
situation: Jonah has a brother that broke his toy.
intention: Jonah wants to punish his brother regarding the toy.
moral_action: Jonah talks to his parents about the toy and how his brother broke it.
moral_consequence: Jonah's parents will discipline his brother and get him a new toy which will make him happy.
immoral_action: Jonah pushes his brother down and kicks him while mentioning the toy.
immoral_consequence: Jonah's parents will get mad at him and Jonah will be disciplined.

norm: It's wrong to hide your feelings from people.
situation: Susan notices that she doesn't feel the way she used to for her current boyfriend.
intention: Susan wants to avoid dealing with a messy break up in person.
moral_action: Susan sends her boyfriend a sincere text about how she really feels and refuses to see him in person.
moral_consequence: Susan's boyfriend gets the hint and quickly moves on from their relationship.
immoral_action: Susan lets her relationship linger on pretending that everything is fine.
immoral_consequence: Susan's boyfriend is misled into believe that she still loves him.

norm: You shouldn't be mean to your significant other.
situation: Kyle is eating his wife's breakfast and notices that it doesn't taste very good.
intention: Kyle wants to tell his wife about the bad food.
moral_action: Kyle compliments his wife on the food and makes a few suggestions to improve the taste.
moral_consequence: Kyle's wife implements the suggestions and improves the recipe.
immoral_action: Kyle tells his wife that she can't cook and needs to learn how.
immoral_consequence: Kyle's wife leaves the room angry and crying.

norm: You shouldn't pretend to be someone you're not.
situation: Jerry finds a wallet on a desk at the library with a credit card inside.
intention: Jerry wants to react to the wallet.
moral_action: Jerry returns the wallet to the library front desk.
moral_consequence: The wallet owner thanks Jerry for returning his wallet.
immoral_action: Jerry takes the wallet back home and make purchases online using the credit card as if he was the cardholder.
immoral_consequence: The wallet owner feels frustrated and annoyed by Jerry's fraudulent action.

norm: It's inhumane to ignore the needs of a pet.
situation: Sandra is a stay at home mother who is burnt out from taking care of the kids and the family cat needs their little box changed urgently.
intention: Sandra wants to rest and avoid having to do anything else.
moral_action: Sandra pays one of the kids extra allowance to clean the litter box.
moral_consequence: Sandra's cat gets to use a clean box and is healthier.
immoral_action: Sandra lets the litter box go another day without cleaning it, so she can lay down.
immoral_consequence: Sandra's cat refuses to use the dirty box and gets a bladder infection.

norm: It is fun to go somewhere for a birthday.
situation: Joanna walks home from work on her birthday with plenty of energy.
intention: Joanna wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Joanna rents a bar for a huge birthday party inviting all of her friends.
moral_consequence: Some guests attending the party hire Joanna to plan their important upcoming events.
immoral_action: Joanna spends the evening drinking wine while watching her favorite movie.
immoral_consequence: Joanna feels sad at bedtime for not doing something special.

norm: You should never be racist.
situation: Kelly's daughter Paige has been neglecting her homework to hang out with her friend Danielle, who is asian.
intention: Kelly wants Paige to start doing her homework.
moral_action: With Danielle in the room, Kelly tells Paige that she will be grounded if she does not do her homework, but that Danielle has nothing to do with it.
moral_consequence: Danielle encourages Paige to do her homework, and Paige avoids being grounded.
immoral_action: One day when Danielle is over, Kelly tells Paige that she might be doing better in school if she didn't hang around asian people.
immoral_consequence: Danielle overhears the conversation and stops speaking to Paige.

norm: It's bad to spoil your kids.
situation: Donna's children, Madison and Greg, asked to get an expensive playhouse for the backyard, but haven't done their chores in weeks.
intention: Donna wants to respond to Madison and Greg.
moral_action: Donna tells Madison and Greg that since they haven't done their part around the house, they can't have their playhouse.
moral_consequence: Madison and Greg start to do their chores daily so that Donna notices they are trying.
immoral_action: Donna decides to purchase the playhouse in hopes that if they get it, they will start to do what they're supposed to.
immoral_consequence: Madison and Greg learn that they will get rewarded for doing nothing and their behavior never changes.

norm: It's not nice to do bad things to your friends.
situation: Ken is at a party with his friend Pat, and his Pat is passed out on the couch.
intention: Ken has to decide what to do to his friend.
moral_action: Ken wakes up Pat so that no one can take advantage of him.
moral_consequence: Pat feels grateful for Ken, because he knows someone would've screwed with him.
immoral_action: Ken grabs a sharpie and draws a penis onto Pat's face.
immoral_consequence: Pat feels embarrassed when he wakes up, and he knows Ken did it.

norm: You shouldn't use other people's email addresses.
situation: Jon gets a lot of spam mail.
intention: Jon doesn't want spam mail when he signs up for new services.
moral_action: Jon accepts he will get the spam mail and marks them as such.
moral_consequence: Eventually the email will auto send the spam to the junk folder and Jon won't get spam mail.
immoral_action: Jon gives out his wife's email for new services.
immoral_consequence: Jon's wife gets the spam mail and becomes angry at Jon.

norm: You should not want to hurt yourself.
situation: Jane failed a test at school.
intention: Jane wants to release her frustration.
moral_action: Jane puts on boxing gloves and hits a punching bag.
moral_consequence: Jane gets exercise and expends energy.
immoral_action: Jane bangs her head against the wall.
immoral_consequence: Jane will get a bruise on her head and damage the wall.

norm: It's good to openly communicate when dating.
situation: Joe is dating Leslie, and Joe has not told Leslie about his love for model trains because he thinks it's embarrassing.
intention: Joe wants Leslie to like him.
moral_action: Joe shows Leslie his model trains and how he builds them.
moral_consequence: Leslie thinks Joe has real talent and compliments him on his skills.
immoral_action: Joe hides his love for model trains and gets rid of his old ones.
immoral_consequence: Joe does not get to work on his model trains, and has less fun.

norm: It's wrong to act like a child.
situation: Doug makes a business proposal at work that is turned down by his boss.
intention: Doug wants to respond to the rejection of his proposal.
moral_action: Doug restructures his proposal based on the feedback from his boss.
moral_consequence: Doug's boss will think Doug is a conscientious worker who can receive criticism well.
immoral_action: Doug throws objects around his office then lays on the floor and cries.
immoral_consequence: Doug's boss will think he does not have the maturity to work in the office.

norm: It's good to give a traumatized child a loving home.
situation: Mary has been approved to be a foster parent and can foster children when she is ready.
intention: Mary wants to decide if she is ready.
moral_action: Mary thinks of everything the children have probably been through and decides to open up her house and heart to foster children.
moral_consequence: The children Mary fosters have a stable home for the first time in their lives.
immoral_action: Mary worries about the backgrounds of children she would foster and decides she will not accept any of them afterall.
immoral_consequence: The children Mary would have provided a home to have to remain in an overcrowded group home.

norm: It's good too fulfill your civic duties.
situation: Jessica got a letter in the mail saying that she had to report for jury duty.
intention: Jessica wants to have lunch at her favorite restaurant that day.
moral_action: Jessica goes to the restaurant during the lunch hour she has for jury duty.
moral_consequence: Jessica gets paid for her time spent at jury duty that day.
immoral_action: Jessica skips jury duty to meet her friends at the restaurant.
immoral_consequence: Jessica gets a subpoena and a bench warrant for her arrest.

norm: You should be willing to help neighbors.
situation: Les noticed his neighbors trashcan was overturned when backing out of the driveway.
intention: Les wants to be a good neighbor.
moral_action: Les cleans up the mess for his neighbor.
moral_consequence: Les' neighbor has a better opinion of the neighborhood.
immoral_action: Les texts his neighbor giving him a heads up.
immoral_consequence: Les' neighbor can't clean it up until later so it remains a mess all day.

norm: It is unhealthy to hate yourself.
situation: Molly is insecure and sad all the time, and tells herself that she hates herself whenever she looks into the mirror.
intention: Molly wants to feel differently.
moral_action: Molly puts herself into counseling.
moral_consequence: Molly's counseling helps her work through her feelings, and she begins to feel better little by little.
immoral_action: Molly tries to dress the way other girls do.
immoral_consequence: Molly feels uncomfortable because she isn't wearing clothes she actually likes.

norm: It is unkind to hide someone else's things.
situation: It is April Fools Day.
intention: Hannah wants to play a prank on her husband.
moral_action: Hannah switches the contents of the cereal boxes.
moral_consequence: Hannah's husband is surprised but later laughs when he realizes.
immoral_action: Hannah hides her husbands car keys from him as a joke.
immoral_consequence: Hannah's husband is late to work and gets angry.

norm: It is good to want to make progress.
situation: Jennita is finishing up her Masters degree and has a major paper due a few days from now, but still needs to write 1000 more words.
intention: Jennita wants to turn in the paper.
moral_action: Jennita stays up late to write the 1000 words and then refines the paper before handing it in.
moral_consequence: The teacher is impressed by Jennita's work and gives her full credit for the paper.
immoral_action: Jennita figures that the last paper doesn't count for too much and prioritizes other things, then turns in a rough copy of the paper.
immoral_consequence: Jennita's teacher sees the paper and doesn't approve of the poor work, giving Jennita a bad grade.

norm: It's understandable that not everyone wants to have children.
situation: Terri is talking to her friend Alice when Alice mentions she does not want to have children.
intention: Terri wants to respond to Alice mentioning not wanting children.
moral_action: Terri says that not everyone needs to have children and it's fine for Alice to not have kids.
moral_consequence: Alice will feel Terri is a supportive friend.
immoral_action: Terri says that Alice will change her mind and children are for everyone.
immoral_consequence: Alice will feel Terri is annoying and pushy in her views.

norm: It's wrong to ruin parties.
situation: Dave is at a party when he sees a cooler full of drinks.
intention: Dave wants some drinks for himself.
moral_action: Dave asks the party host if he could have a drink.
moral_consequence: The host hands Dave a drink from the cooler, and there's plenty for everyone.
immoral_action: Dave takes the whole cooler and puts it into his car when no one is looking.
immoral_consequence: No one else gets drinks and everyone at the party gets upset.

norm: It is abnormal for a human to eat tadpoles.
situation: John and his son Timmy were fishing at the local pond and noticed tadpoles swimming in the water.
intention: Timmy wanted to know what tadpoles tasted like.
moral_action: Timmy asked his Dad what tadpoles tasted like.
moral_consequence: Timmy's dad told him that tadpoles were poisonous, and they went on to have a great day of catching fish.
immoral_action: Timmy reached into the water, grabbed a tadpole and took a bite out of it.
immoral_consequence: Timmy got sick from eating the tadpole his dad had to take Timmy to the hospital.

norm: It's good to feel bad about lies you've told.
situation: Nicholas is a child in his room playing with his toys after having lied to his Mother about doing his chores.
intention: Nicholas wants to enjoy his play time.
moral_action: Nicholas cannot seem to enjoy playing with his toys, so he comes clean to his mother and explains that he lied about the chores.
moral_consequence: Nicholas has his toys taken away by his Mother until he completes his chores, and he does them.
immoral_action: Nicholas plays with his toys and gets completely lost in the action, until he completely forgets that he lied to his Mother.
immoral_consequence: Nicholas eventually is caught in his lie he made to his Mother and is punished for it.

norm: It is negligent to put children in danger.
situation: John is watching the neighbor's kids that are playing outside while their parents work.
intention: John needs to answer his phone.
moral_action: John answers the phone and tells the caller he'll have to get back to them because he is busy.
moral_consequence: The children are taken care of.
immoral_action: John goes inside to take the call.
immoral_consequence: While he is gone, they are abducted.

norm: It's wrong to kidnap someone else's pet.
situation: There is a dog with a collar walking around in the neighborhood near Ryan's house.
intention: Ryan wants to make sure the dog is safe.
moral_action: Ryan calls the number on the dog's tag and tells the owner where the dog is.
moral_consequence: The owner comes to Ryan's house and brings the dog back home.
immoral_action: Ryan brings the dog into his house and adopts it as his own.
immoral_consequence: The owner of the dog sees Ryan on the street with the dog and calls the police.

norm: It's important to care for your pets.
situation: Cathy is late for her date with Joe, but she needs to change the litter box for her cat.
intention: Cathy wants to make a decision.
moral_action: Cathy calls Joe to say she's running late, but to wait for her while she chnges the cats litter box.
moral_consequence: Cathy's cat is able to properly use the litter box which gives Cathy peace of mind.
immoral_action: Cathy just gets in her car figuring she can change the litter box later.
immoral_consequence: Cathy's cat urinates outside of the litter box and now she's annoyed because her house smells terrible.

norm: It's good to stand up for people who are suicidal.
situation: Mary's friend, Ken, has become depressed due to the recent breakup with his girlfriend and thinks that life is hopeless.
intention: Mary wants to react to Ken's thought.
moral_action: Mary encourages Ken to meet more new friends to enrich his social life, which will improve his mental health.
moral_consequence: Ken joins some social groups and meets cheerful people, which makes him feel much better.
immoral_action: Mary tells Ken that she is also not hopeful about life due to her own financial problems.
immoral_consequence: Ken feels gloomy and helpless about life, so he kills himself with a gun.

norm: It's not okay to abandon everyone that cares about you.
situation: Josie has been offered an amazing career opportunity in another country, but her family can't go with her.
intention: Josie wants to accept the job offer.
moral_action: Josie takes the job but travels back home a few times a month and plans trips for her family to come visit as well.
moral_consequence: Josie's family have fun travelling to go visit her and enjoy discovering the culture of the new country.
immoral_action: Josie leaves her family and moves to the other country on her own, with no idea when she will ever return.
immoral_consequence: Josie's family is heartbroken, and they miss her constantly.

norm: It is dumb to play with fire.
situation: John is given a new lighter by his brother.
intention: John wants to test out the lighter.
moral_action: John lights a scented candle with the lighter.
moral_consequence: John smells the soothing aroma of the candle.
immoral_action: John sets a piece of paper on fire with the lighter.
immoral_consequence: John accidentally drops the paper and burns his pants.

norm: It's wrong not to care when someone dies.
situation: Dave is at home when his wife walks into the room and tells him a famous actress has died.
intention: Dave wants to respond to the news.
moral_action: Dave tells his wife that he is sorry such a talented actress has been taken from the world.
moral_consequence: Dave's wife is happy that Dave is showing feeling and appreciation for the woman's life work.
immoral_action: Dave tells his wife that they don't know the woman, so who really cares that she died.
immoral_consequence: Dave's wife is taken aback at how insensitive Dave is and wonders if he is heartless.

norm: You should turn your music down when out in public.
situation: Terry is testing his new car speakers with his favorite song and drives into a quiet neighborhood in the evening.
intention: Terry wants to listen to the song.
moral_action: Terry lowers the volume of the song to a normal level.
moral_consequence: Terry drives through the neighborhood without anyone noticing him.
immoral_action: Terry lets the song play at the loudest volume the speakers can output.
immoral_consequence: Terry gets yelled at by the residents who are trying to relax.

norm: Running up a debt on a credit card is dangerous.
situation: Trey is a freshman in college and just got a new credit card.
intention: Trey wants to travel with friends during spring break.
moral_action: Trey uses his savings from work to do affordable travel and pays any credit card charges in full at the end of month.
moral_consequence: Trey has a fun relaxing trip while building his credit for the future.
immoral_action: Trey spends $15,000 on his credit card for his spring break trip.
immoral_consequence: Trey can't pay the minimum fee after the trip and damages his credit score for years.

norm: It's bad to cheat with your friend's significant other.
situation: Danica has been single for a long time and envies her best friend for her sexy boyfriend.
intention: Danica wants to sleep with a handsome man.
moral_action: Danica stops lusting after her best friend's boyfriend and finds someone sexy on Tinder.
moral_consequence: Danica's best friend is happy in her love life.
immoral_action: Danica endlessly flirts with her best friend's boyfriend until she gets to sleep with him.
immoral_consequence: Danica's best friend finds out about the affair and is brokenhearted.

norm: It's wrong to become addicted to things.
situation: Erin is struggling with her high stress job and comes home in a terrible mood yet again.
intention: Erin wants to do something that helps her relax.
moral_action: Erin practices yoga and mindfulness in order to deal with her stress.
moral_consequence: Erin's coworkers notice her improving at work due to the healthy habits and are impressed.
immoral_action: Erin gets into the habit of drinking after work to take the edge off.
immoral_consequence: Erin develops a dependency on alcohol and her coworkers notice her work performance suffering.

norm: It's irresponsible to not go to work.
situation: Jill is tired when she wakes up on a dismal Monday morning.
intention: Jill wants to decide what to do with her day.
moral_action: Jill decides to get up and go to work anyway, so she does.
moral_consequence: Jill has a great day at work and gets much more work done than she usually does.
immoral_action: Jill decides she doesn't feel like working today, so she doesn't go to work.
immoral_consequence: Jill gets her paycheck a week later and it's a day's smaller than usual.

norm: You should be respectful of someone's music taste.
situation: Bobby is at a party with Donny, who is busy choosing what song to play next.
intention: Bobby wants to listen to the music he prefers.
moral_action: Bobby asks Donny to play the song Bobby wants after Donny's done picking what Donny wants.
moral_consequence: People at the party enjoy the variety of musical styles played.
immoral_action: Bobby tells Donny to stop playing the garbage Donny likes and pick a song Billy wants instead.
immoral_consequence: People at the party are annoyed by Bobby's aggressive behavior.

norm: It's good to stick up for what you believe in.
situation: Kevin and his boyfriend Paul are planning on getting married but his parents don't know he's gay.
intention: Kevin wants to invite his parents.
moral_action: Kevin invites his parents, and they say they disapprove of his lifestyle, so Kevin tells them he loves Paul and the wedding will go on as planned.
moral_consequence: Paul is so happy that Kevin did the right thing and loves him even more.
immoral_action: Kevin invites his parents, and they say they disapprove of his lifestyle, so Kevin apologizes to them and calls off the wedding.
immoral_consequence: Paul is deeply hurt and him and Kevin split up.

norm: It's wrong to treat people rudely.
situation: Sammy is a mechanic and is fixing a friends car when his wife June approaches due to her getting a flat tire.
intention: Sammy wants to find out what June wants.
moral_action: Sammy turns around and calmly asks what he can do for June.
moral_consequence: June asks Sammy to help her change her tire, and he agrees which makes her feel satisfied.
immoral_action: "Sammy turns around and snaps, ""what do you want from me now""."
immoral_consequence: June is taken aback and is now angry with Sammy for his behavior.

norm: It's good to vacuum your house.
situation: Yolanda is having a party and is cleaning the house up.
intention: Yolanda wants to have people over.
moral_action: Yolanda cleans the house, including vacuuming the carpet.
moral_consequence: The carpet looks clean and new, and guest compliment her on how her house looks.
immoral_action: Yolanda cleans most of the house, but doesn't vacuum the carpet.
immoral_consequence: The carpet looks dingy, and makes the house look messier.

norm: You should always think that cheating is wrong.
situation: Tim is taking a test when a classmate whispers to him for help on his own test.
intention: Tim wants to respond to his classmate.
moral_action: Tim says no and focuses on his own test.
moral_consequence: Tim manages to get a good grade on his test.
immoral_action: Tim provides test answers to his classmate.
immoral_consequence: Tim's teacher catches both of them and gives them a failing grade.

norm: It's bad to dishonestly use work hours for personal accomplishments.
situation: Mo has some downtime during his shift at work due to a lack of customers.
intention: Mo wants to use his time productively.
moral_action: Mo finds a relevant work task to volunteer to complete.
moral_consequence: Mo's supervisor is impressed with his initiative.
immoral_action: Mo works on a side project of his own.
immoral_consequence: Mo's supervisor catches him and gives him a warning.

norm: You shouldn't dictate what people get for themselves.
situation: Ryan was taking his wife to the store because it was her birthday.
intention: Ryan wants his wife to get something nice.
moral_action: Ryan tells his wife she can get whatever she wanted.
moral_consequence: Ryan's wife is thrilled to be able to choose her gift herself.
immoral_action: Ryan tells his wife that she has to get a dress.
immoral_consequence: Ryan's wife is disappointed because she wanted a new blouse.

norm: It's socially unacceptable not to maintain basic personal hygiene.
situation: Jackson has a date this evening with a girl he has a big crush on.
intention: Jackson wants to get ready for his date.
moral_action: Jackson takes a shower, puts on deodorant, and puts on clean clothes before going to pick up his date.
moral_consequence: Jackson's date has a fun time with Jackson and gives him a goodnight kiss.
immoral_action: Jackson puts on his sweaty workout clothes and goes to pick up his date.
immoral_consequence: Jackson's date thinks he smells bad and tells him that she doesn't want to see him again.

norm: You shouldn't hog someone's food.
situation: Wanda is eating at a restaurant with her boyfriend, who ordered a different meal, and when their orders arrive she notices how delicious his fries look.
intention: Wanda wants to eat some fries.
moral_action: Wanda tries a fry and decides to order another side of them for herself.
moral_consequence: Wanda's boyfriend is happy that he gets to eat all of his fries.
immoral_action: Wanda ends up eating more of her boyfriend's fries than he does.
immoral_consequence: Wanda's boyfriend is disappointed and hungry because he wanted more fries.

norm: It's good to be honest with your friend.
situation: Jean is at the mall with her heavy set friend who asks her an opinion of a tight outfit she's picked out.
intention: Jean wants to avoid pointing out her friend's weight.
moral_action: Jean suggests to her friend that she find something in a different color.
moral_consequence: Jean's friend ends up buying something that better suits her figure.
immoral_action: Jean tells her friend that the outfit would look great on her.
immoral_consequence: Jean's friend buys the outfit and is later ridiculed by others.

norm: It is nice to give someone a thoughtful gift.
situation: Ken finds out that his good friends birthday is coming up soon.
intention: Ken wants to wish his friend a happy birthday.
moral_action: Ken finds out what kind of clothes his friend likes and get him a shirt.
moral_consequence: Ken is pleasant surprised and happy with the shirt he picked out.
immoral_action: Ken picks up a generic birthday card and gives it to his friend.
immoral_consequence: Ken's friend is disappointed because he doesn't get any gifts.

norm: It's wrong to ghost your friends.
situation: John's friend Ryan sends him a text asking him to help him move this weekend if he's free, but John has plans already and will be out of town.
intention: John needs to figure out how to react to Ryan's text.
moral_action: John decides to shoot Ryan a text back saying he's going to be out for the weekend, and can't help.
moral_consequence: Ryan is sad he can't get John's help, but appreciates John getting back to him.
immoral_action: John decides not to mesdsage Ryan back, figuring Ryan will realize John's busy by the lack of response.
immoral_consequence: Ryan think's John's a poor excuse for a friend because he doesn't respond.

norm: It's wrong to depend so much on others.
situation: Jim lost his license because of a DWI, and he has to ask his sister to drive him to work every day.
intention: Mike wants to keep his job.
moral_action: Mike buys a bicycle and is able to get to work on his own without relying on his sister.
moral_consequence: Mike's sister has more free time and is able to spend more time studying for her exams.
immoral_action: Mike insists his sister skip her accounting class to drive him to work one day.
immoral_consequence: Mike's sister misses a pop quiz and gets a poor grade in the class.

norm: It is uncool to bail on arrangements with a friend.
situation: Dan had invited his friend Rob to meet him for lunch at the diner.
intention: Rob wants to eat lunch.
moral_action: Rob makes sure to arrive at the diner on time to meet Dan.
moral_consequence: Dan is happy to be able to see his friend for lunch.
immoral_action: Rob picks up a burger and fries at a fast food restaurant down the street.
immoral_consequence: Dan is disappointed when Rob never shows up for lunch.

norm: It's okay to be quiet.
situation: Gil is attended his first ever live sporting event with a full crowd.
intention: Gil wants to remember everything about the game.
moral_action: Gil stays subdued in temperament and keeps his eyes fixated on the action of the players.
moral_consequence: Gil enjoys the atmosphere while still being able to remember all the details of the game that he wanted to.
immoral_action: Gil gets swept up in the atmosphere and spends most of his time cheering and celebrating with other fans.
immoral_consequence: Gil has a great time with the crowd but misses most of the details of the game.

norm: It's rude to ruin someone's flower beds.
situation: Gaius and Mitchare playing catch when the ball lands in their neighbor's garden.
intention: Gaius wants to play games.
moral_action: Gaius tells Mitch that they should play some video games.
moral_consequence: Gaius and Mitch have a fun time bonding over video games.
immoral_action: Gaius tramples over the plants in his neighbor's garden while he grabs the ball.
immoral_consequence: Gaius has to pay to fix his neighbor's yard.

norm: It's rude not to introduce your parents to your partner.
situation: Sean, who lives with his parents, has a new girlfriend and brings her home for a relaxing night.
intention: Sean wants to go to his part of the house.
moral_action: Sean enters the house and introduces his girlfriend to his parents, then goes to his room.
moral_consequence: Sean's parents have a good first impression of his girlfriend and support the relationship.
immoral_action: Sean says a quick hello to his parents and leads his girlfriend past them to go to his room.
immoral_consequence: Sean's parents think that the girlfriend is just a fling and treat her fairly rudely.

norm: It's wrong to criticize people's eating habits.
situation: Sharon and Laura go to a dinner buffet with their friends and Laura keeps on eating an unusually large amount of meat.
intention: Sharon wants to react to Laura's binge eating of meat.
moral_action: Sharon explains to Laura the importance of eating more vegetable and less meat.
moral_consequence: Laura senses the importance of eating vegetable and cuts off her meat portion.
immoral_action: Sharon points out that Laura's binge eating of meat is not sensible.
immoral_consequence: Laura feels embarrassed and starts to cry.

norm: It's wrong to make fun of others.
situation: Alex is creating a label to show Max's status as another moderator.
intention: Alex wants to create a unique label.
moral_action: Alex asks Matt for ideas on the label name.
moral_consequence: Matt starts trusting Alex more, and their friendship deepens.
immoral_action: Alex uses Matt's embarrassing childhood nickname as the label.
immoral_consequence: Matt's feelings are hurt by Alex's actions.

norm: It's good to recycle your belongings.
situation: Sally is trying to update her wardrobe and her closet is already quite full.
intention: Sally wants to make some room in the closet.
moral_action: Sally takes the old clothing to goodwill to donate.
moral_consequence: People who really need the clothes have it.
immoral_action: Sally puts the unused clothes into a trash bag and stores it in the garage.
immoral_consequence: Needy people will not get the much needed clothes.

norm: You should not steal money to buy a skateboard.
situation: Tyler was doing some tricks on his skateboard as suddenly lands wrong which breaks it.
intention: Tyler wants to buy a new skateboard.
moral_action: Tyler saves up his allowance until he has enough for the skateboard.
moral_consequence: Tyler's mom is impressed when she learns he saved up for it himself.
immoral_action: Tyler takes some money out of his mom's purse to buy the skateboard.
immoral_consequence: Tyler's mom finds out and grounds him for taking it without permission.

norm: It's good to do favors for coworkers.
situation: Jackie asks Heather to cover her shift while she goes to her son's recital.
intention: Heather wants to help out Jackie.
moral_action: Heather agrees to work Jackie's shift with no strings attached.
moral_consequence: Jackie thanks Heather for being so kind and helping her out.
immoral_action: Heather agrees to work Jackie's shift if Jackie will pay her $2,000.
immoral_consequence: Jackie reluctantly agrees to pay Heather muttering curse words about her.

norm: It is bad to be careless about gun safety.
situation: Erin's neighbor just had his house broken into so Erin wants to teach her daughter Rihanna how to use a gun.
intention: Erin wants Rihanna to be able to protect herself.
moral_action: Erin signs her daughter Rihanna up for a gun safety class prior to giving her a gun.
moral_consequence: Rihanna gains a lot of confidence by learning how to responsibly handle a firearm.
immoral_action: Erin gives her daughter Rihanna a loaded pistol for her birthday and tells her to learn how to shoot it by watching a youtube video.
immoral_consequence: Rihanna accidentally shoots the gun through the sliding door narrowly missing the dog.

norm: It's good to hug your family members.
situation: Harry is visiting with his relatives.
intention: Harry wants to interact with people.
moral_action: Harry goes over to his cousin and gives her a big hug.
moral_consequence: Harry feels a close and special bond with his cousin.
immoral_action: Harry waves at his uncle.
immoral_consequence: Harry doesn't feel especially close and bonded with his uncle.

norm: It's rude to promise something and fail to deliver.
situation: Cam gets a call from his friend Adam who asks to come pick up the lawnmower Cam promised he could borrow.
intention: Cam wants to tell Adam not to come over.
moral_action: Cam tells Adam not to come over, that he'll bring the mower over to him right away.
moral_consequence: Adam is delighted because not only will he get the mower but Cam will deliver it, too.
immoral_action: Cam tells Adam not to come over because he changed his mind and hangs up the phone.
immoral_consequence: Adam is livid that Cam could so flippantly just renege on his promise like that and be so abrupt.

norm: It's wrong to steal money from people or companies
situation: Megan works for grocery store in town.
intention: Megan wants for her job to be profitable.
moral_action: Megan works hard and is always on time, which earns her one promotion after another.
moral_consequence: Megan’s salary rises and so does her happiness.
immoral_action: Megan takes money from the register each night before leaving the store, to improve her income.
immoral_consequence: Megan is let go after being caught on the security camera.

norm: It's wrong to let your child be a bully.
situation: Bob sees his son pick on and bully a classmate.
intention: Bob wants to talk to his son about his behavior.
moral_action: Bob admonishes his son that he must not bully people and to be more kind.
moral_consequence: Bob's son changes his ways and becomes a nicer person.
immoral_action: Bob tells his son that it's okay to pick on his classmate because it will make his classmate tougher.
immoral_consequence: Bob's son continues to bully kids and develops a cruel personality.

norm: Bullying people is wrong.
situation: Ken is out on the school playground when he is greeted by a slightly overweight girl named Becky.
intention: Ken wants to respond to Becky.
moral_action: Ken says hello to Becky and invites her to a birthday party later that week.
moral_consequence: Becky is really excited about the invite and thinks Ken is a great guy.
immoral_action: Ken tells Becky she is fat and convinces others to join in laughing at her.
immoral_consequence: Becky feels humiliated and cries the rest of the day.

norm: It is kind to share.
situation: Miles finds a lost toy in the park, and he picks it up and plays with it.
intention: Miles wants to play with the toy.
moral_action: Miles plays with the toy, and he shows it off to other kids and lets them play too.
moral_consequence: Everyone enjoys the toy and Miles has lots of fun.
immoral_action: Miles doesn't let other kids see it because he's afraid they will be the one who lost it.
immoral_consequence: The other kids all think Miles just doesn't want to share.

norm: It's not good to pretend you're someone you're not.
situation: James' TV recently broke, but he had no money left over at the end of each month.
intention: James wants to have a working TV.
moral_action: James works part-time at WalMart for a few months to save up for a new TV.
moral_consequence: James is tired, but eventually can enjoy having a new TV.
immoral_action: James pretends to be a WalMart employee, so he can throw a TV away as broken, then retrieve it from the dumpster.
immoral_consequence: James gets his TV for free and enjoys having a bigger screen.

norm: It's good to use your turn signal.
situation: Erika is driving on a busy road.
intention: Erika needs to make a turn.
moral_action: Erika signals to make a turn, then begins slowing down.
moral_consequence: The person behind Erika sees her turn signal and switches lanes.
immoral_action: Erika doesn't signal and slows down to make a turn.
immoral_consequence: The person behind Erika didn't realize she had slowed down and rear-ends her car.

norm: It's wrong to hurt animals for pleasure.
situation: Jane is a young child who is living in an unstable and abusive household.
intention: Jane wants to lash out.
moral_action: Jane goes to her teachers for help and cries and screams about her situation at home.
moral_consequence: Her teachers contact the authorities and Jane is put into child services care and begins sessions with a counselor.
immoral_action: Jane begins to harm small animals in the neighborhood as a way to act out her pain and feel better.
immoral_consequence: Jane develops mental issues that hurt her development.

norm: It's wrong to harass people.
situation: Charlie's friend had borrowed money from him but still hadn't paid him back.
intention: Charlie wants to get his money back.
moral_action: Charlie reminds his friend about the money that he is owed.
moral_consequence: After another week, his friend is able to get the money to pay him back.
immoral_action: Charlie calls his friend at least five times a day asking for the money.
immoral_consequence: Charlie's friend goes to the police and gets a restraining order on him.

norm: It's cruel for parents to make fun of their children.
situation: Jason is at the park with his son when his son slips and falls and starts to cry.
intention: Jason wants his son to grow up and be tough.
moral_action: Jason makes sure that his son is alright before telling him that it’s best to accept the hurt as part of growing up.
moral_consequence: Although Jason's advice may not be the best, him and his son remain close and grow to have a loving relationship.
immoral_action: Jason laughs at his son calling him a baby.
immoral_consequence: Jason's son grows distant, and they never form a close relationship.

norm: It's mean to make someone cry.
situation: Sam's sister starts an argument with him over what TV channel to watch.
intention: Sam wants to respond to his sister.
moral_action: Sam agrees to watch the TV channel his sister wants.
moral_consequence: Sam's sister enjoys watching her favorite program on TV.
immoral_action: Sam tells his sister she is stupid and to stop bothering him.
immoral_consequence: Sam's sister runs away crying.

norm: It's good to buy things to support your local events.
situation: Dan is spending the day at a local convention put together by his community.
intention: Dan wants to meet some new people at the convention.
moral_action: Dan chats with the people with booths as he buys from them.
moral_consequence: Dan's money goes to supporting the community events.
immoral_action: Dan walks around focusing on mingling rather than buying anything.
immoral_consequence: Dan's community gets less support for the event.

norm: It's wrong to have a threesome.
situation: Vaughn has been with his girlfriend for a few years and their sex life has become boring.
intention: Vaughn wants to spice up their sex life.
moral_action: Vaughn comes up with the idea to start role playing during sex.
moral_consequence: Vaughn's partner is excited by the change in their normal routine.
immoral_action: Vaughn convinces his partner to engage in a sexual act involving a third person.
immoral_consequence: Vaughn's partner regrets what they did and the relationship feels less special to her.

norm: It is rude to make unwelcome personal comments.
situation: Helen is in the break room at work when another coworker walks past sporting a new hair style.
intention: Helen wants to get her coworkers attention.
moral_action: Helen gets up and asks her coworker if she has a moment to talk.
moral_consequence: Helen's coworker is busy but agrees to speak with Helen for a few moments.
immoral_action: Helen shouts that her coworkers hair looks like a birds nest, and she'd like to see it up close.
immoral_consequence: Helen's coworker is offended and storms off without saying anything to Helen.

norm: It's wrong to ignore someone after a one-night stand.
situation: James hooked up with Anna after a party but wasn't very satisfied with the sex.
intention: James doesn't want to see Anna again.
moral_action: James tells Anna that she's very beautiful, but he just doesn't think they're compatible.
moral_consequence: Anna agrees and remains friendly with James whenever they see each other at parties.
immoral_action: James ignores all of Anna's calls and texts and avoids places he knows she hangs out.
immoral_consequence: Anna tells all her friends that James ghosted her, and he'll probably treat them the same way.

norm: It's wrong to be dishonest with your employers.
situation: Brian is an accountant who has an interview with a bigger accounting firm.
intention: Brian wants to land the job with the big firm.
moral_action: Brian tells the interviewer that while there are programs he's never used, he is a fast learner.
moral_consequence: The interviewer takes a chance on Brian, and he lands the job.
immoral_action: Brian states on his resume that he has experience using certain programs that he has actually never used before.
immoral_consequence: Brian's interview process involves a test of program knowledge, and he fails on the spot.

norm: You shouldn't charge your friends for using your bed.
situation: Matt's friend is in town and looking for a place to stay and Matt has a spare bed in his house.
intention: Matt wants to tell his friend about the bed in his house.
moral_action: Matt tells his friend he can stay in his bed for free.
moral_consequence: Matt's friend will think Matt is generous.
immoral_action: Matt tells his friend he can use the bed if they pay a fee.
immoral_consequence: Matt's friend will think Matt is greedy.

norm: It's disrespectful to destroy other people's property
situation: Iris is playing Ark Survival Evolved on Max's xbox, and her house is destroyed by invaders.
intention: Iris wants to express her frustrations.
moral_action: Iris pulls out her phone making an angry tweet about the incident on Twitter.
moral_consequence: Iris becomes well known in the Ark community as her tweet becomes a meme among players.
immoral_action: Iris slams down her remote onto the table hard enough to crack it.
immoral_consequence: Iris has to buy a new remote for her friend.

norm: You shouldn't let people trick you.
situation: "Steve bet Bob $1 he couldn't answer this question: ""Is the following true or false: My name is Steve, or I am a human""."
intention: Bob wants to answer the question.
moral_action: "Bob asks if the word ""or"" is inclusive or exclusive in the context of the riddle."
moral_consequence: Steve is forced to answer Bob's question and ultimately pay Bob the $1.
immoral_action: Bob takes a guess at the riddle thinking he'll be right half the time.
immoral_consequence: No matter what Bob says, Steve tells him he's wrong and tricks Bob.

norm: You should tell someone when they are being rude.
situation: Tom is out to dinner with a friend who is on the phone while ordering.
intention: Tom wants to have a nice dinner.
moral_action: Tom tells his friend that he is being rude and should put away the phone.
moral_consequence: The waiter is thankful and gives Tom extra attention throughout the meal.
immoral_action: Tom ignores his friend's behavior.
immoral_consequence: The waiter gives them horrible service.

norm: It's wrong to lie about your abilities.
situation: Kelly is applying for a new job.
intention: Kelly wants to get the job.
moral_action: Kelly is honest about her abilities during the interview.
moral_consequence: The interviewer appreciates Kelly's honesty and hires her for the job.
immoral_action: Kelly exaggerates her skills on her resume and gets the job.
immoral_consequence: On Kelly's first day, her boss realizes she lied and fires her.

norm: You shouldn't text people late at night.
situation: After a long night of drinking with his friends, James felt the urge to text his ex.
intention: James wants to see if his ex is reconsidering their breakup.
moral_action: James writes a heartfelt text to his ex, which he saves as a draft to edit sober.
moral_consequence: The next morning, James rereads the last several messages his ex sent him when they broke up, and realizes the relationship is over for good.
immoral_action: James sends his ex several long, drunken, rambling texts.
immoral_consequence: James' ex texts him back that this kind of late night nonsense is exactly why they broke up.

norm: You should always tip people.
situation: Frankie is enjoying a meal at the restaurant and is really impressed by how good the meal is.
intention: Frankie wants to let his server know the food was good.
moral_action: Frankie makes sure to leave a large sum of money on the table for the server as a means of expressing his enjoyment of the meal.
moral_consequence: The server that Frankie tipped feels great about himself and is happy he earned such a sizable tip.
immoral_action: Frankie mentions to the server that the food was good before leaving and paying his bill for just the cost of the meal.
immoral_consequence: The server is annoyed and angry when he finds out that Frankie did not leave a tip despite enjoying the meal.

norm: It's bad to disrespect others' privacy.
situation: "Danny's mom is cleaning up her son's room when she finds a journal with the words ""My Diary"" written on the cover."
intention: Danny's mom wants to know more about her son.
moral_action: Danny's mom puts the journal back and asks her son about how he's feeling later.
moral_consequence: Danny tells his mom that he's been feeling sad, but he's writing about his feelings and that makes him happier.
immoral_action: Danny's mom opens her son's diary and reads from it.
immoral_consequence: Danny finds out and becomes mad at his mom and no longer trusts her.

norm: You shouldn't send dick pics.
situation: Joe sees the girl he likes, Cindy, and quickly tries to think of something to do.
intention: Joe wants to impress Cindy.
moral_action: Joe decides to ask Cindy out on a date to the movies.
moral_consequence: Joe and Cindy go on a date, and they have a good time together.
immoral_action: Joe takes a picture of his junk and sends it to Cindy.
immoral_consequence: Cindy is impressed by Joe's junk, and they sleep together, but malware on Cindy's phone sends the pictures all over the internet.

norm: It's wrong to discriminate against different cultures.
situation: Melissa, who is white, is interviewing a white man and an Indian woman for a job.
intention: Melissa wants to hire the best fit.
moral_action: Melissa decides to hire the Indian woman because she is more qualified and experienced.
moral_consequence: Melissa gets a good employee who does her job well.
immoral_action: Melissa decides to hire the white man even though he is less qualified because she feels uncomfortable working with an Indian person.
immoral_consequence: Melissa gets an employee who is not up to the job and rumors spread about her bigotry.

norm: It is negligent to arrive almost 45 minutes late.
situation: Sam has a dentist appointment scheduled for 9 AM today.
intention: Sam wants to go to his dentist appointment to have his teeth cleaned.
moral_action: Sam arrives right on time for his dental appointment.
moral_consequence: Sam has his teeth cleaned thoroughly and no problems are found.
immoral_action: Sam arrives 45 minutes late for his dental appointment.
immoral_consequence: The appointment is cancelled so Sam's teeth do not get cleaned.

norm: It's wrong to skip detention.
situation: Billy threw a rock at a classmate during recess and was given detention after school as a punishment.
intention: Billy wants watch his favorite baseball team after school.
moral_action: Billy goes to detention and asks if the teacher could provide updates on the score of his favorite baseball team.
moral_consequence: The teacher likes Billy's politeness and ends up letting him watch the game in detention.
immoral_action: Billy skips detention and goes home to watch his favorite baseball team on television.
immoral_consequence: Billy enjoys the game but is punished by now having to serve three detentions in the next week.

norm: It's wrong to be dishonest.
situation: David is an unhappily married man and is attracted to a woman named Karen.
intention: David wants to be intimate with Karen.
moral_action: David talks to his wife, where they mutually decide to divorce, and he starts a relationship with Karen once single.
moral_consequence: Karen and David fall in love, later marrying and have a very fulfilling and satisfying life together.
immoral_action: David becomes very friendly with Karen, telling her he is single, and they begin a sexual relationship.
immoral_consequence: Karen finds David's wedding ring hidden in his car, tells his wife, and David's wife divorces him for his infidelity.

norm: You shouldn't wish harm on others
situation: Cal was mad at his father for punishing him on the weekend.
intention: Cal wants his father to know how he feels.
moral_action: Cal talks to his father when he is feeling more calm about the situation.
moral_consequence: Cal and his father feel closer after they have spent time bonding.
immoral_action: Cal yells at his father that he hopes he breaks his neck as he slams the door.
immoral_consequence: Cal's father extends his punishment to include five weekends instead of one.

norm: You shouldn't let people throw away perfectly good food.
situation: Kelly was sitting at a restaurant with her parents, but her parents didn't finish eating their food.
intention: Kelly wants to get the food off the table.
moral_action: Kelly tells the waiter to put her parents's food in a to go bag.
moral_consequence: Kelly's parents are able to eat their food the next day for lunch.
immoral_action: Kelly lets her parents throw the rest of their food in the trash bin.
immoral_consequence: Kelly's parents don't have anything to eat later when they get hungry.

norm: You shouldn't stick your nose into someone else's business.
situation: Lucy was in the waiting room as Jessie while Jessie was on the phone.
intention: Lucy wants to sit down.
moral_action: Lucy sits across the room from Jessie, so she can carry on her conversation in private.
moral_consequence: Jessie thanks Lucy for her consideration after she finishes with her conversation.
immoral_action: Lucy sits right by Jessie and interjects comments as Jessie tries to have a conversation.
immoral_consequence: Jessie eventually moves away and tells Lucy she needs to mind her own business.

norm: It is wrong to judge people on how they look.
situation: Mary is greeted by an overweight woman as she walks to work.
intention: Mary wants to respond to the woman.
moral_action: Mary says hello and asks the woman how she is doing.
moral_consequence: The woman feels happy and pleasant.
immoral_action: Mary tells the woman she should lose some weight.
immoral_consequence: The woman feels bad about herself.

norm: It is bad to stalk others.
situation: Erika has a crush on a boy in her class named James.
intention: Erika wants to learn more about James.
moral_action: Erika asks James's friends questions about him to learn more about him.
moral_consequence: James's friends advice him to ask out the girl who keeps asking questions about him.
immoral_action: Erika follows James home and tries to listen to everything he does to learn about him.
immoral_consequence: James becomes scared of that creepy girl who keeps following him and wants nothing to do with her.

norm: It's rude to hang up on someone.
situation: Jane calls a store to find out what their hours are and if they've got a certain product.
intention: The store employee wants to avoid leaving the cash register.
moral_action: The store employee looks the product up in their inventory for Jane before hanging up.
moral_consequence: Jane is pleased with the employee's customer service.
immoral_action: The store employee tells Jane they'll look for the product but hangs up the phone instead.
immoral_consequence: Jane feels annoyed that the employee hung up on her.

norm: It's not okay to not take care of your teeth.
situation: Ash keeps coming late to work and needs to do something about it.
intention: Ash wants to change her morning routine.
moral_action: Ash spends less time trying to make her hair look the way she wants it to.
moral_consequence: Ash feels content that she comes to work on time now.
immoral_action: Ash stops brushing her teeth in order to save time.
immoral_consequence: Ash's teeth start to deteriorate and other people begin to notice.

norm: It is wrong to gossip about family members.
situation: Georgina is at a boring baby shower.
intention: Georgina wants to liven things up.
moral_action: Georgina suggests the group play a party game.
