moral_consequence: Georgina and her family have a fun time at the baby shower.
immoral_action: Georgina starts talking about an affair she suspects her cousin is having.
immoral_consequence: Georgina's family think she is overstepping her bounds and are reluctant to share with her in the future.

norm: You shouldn't overreact in situations.
situation: Lawrence is cooking bacon on the stove top in his kitchen when the bacon catches fire.
intention: Lawrence wants to respond to the fire.
moral_action: Lawrence removes the pan from the stove top and contains it.
moral_consequence: The fire is put out and does not spread to the rest of Lawrence's house.
immoral_action: Lawrence runs out of the kitchen and says the house will burn down.
immoral_consequence: The fire is not contained and spreads to other rooms in Lawrence's house.

norm: It's good to celebrate things with people.
situation: Lily's grandmother, who hasn’t seen her sister Mary in years, has an upcoming birthday party.
intention: Lily wants to contact her grandmother's sister.
moral_action: Lily calls Mary to tell invite her to her grandmother's party.
moral_consequence: Mary surprises her sister at her party, and the two hit it off like best friends.
immoral_action: After the party is over, Lily calls her grandmother's sister, Mary.
immoral_consequence: Mary feels left out after discovering there was a party she wasn't invited to.

norm: It's wrong to lie to the people in your life.
situation: Mark and his girlfriend are invited to a friend's house for a party Friday night, but there will be drinking.
intention: Mark wants to be able to see his girlfriend.
moral_action: Mark invites his girlfriend over to watch a movie instead of going to the party.
moral_consequence: Mark gets to see his girlfriend and stays out of trouble.
immoral_action: Mark tells his mother he is going spend the night at a friend's house, but goes to the party.
immoral_consequence: Mark's mother finds out about the party and grounds him for a month.

norm: It's good to let your friends crash at your place.
situation: Pam has some friends coming into town for a visit.
intention: Pam wants her friends to have a place to stay.
moral_action: Pam invites her friends to stay with her.
moral_consequence: Pam and her friends have a good time all day, every day.
immoral_action: Pam arranges for her friends to stay at her mom's place.
immoral_consequence: Pam's mom gets upset with all of the people in her house.

norm: Children shouldn't secretly work against their parents.
situation: Joe's dad spanked him for violating curfew.
intention: Joe is angry at his dad and wants to express that.
moral_action: Joe tells both his parents he's upset at dad and feels mistreated.
moral_consequence: Joe and his parents calmly talk things over and come to an understanding.
immoral_action: Joe secretly plants a pair of women's panties in his dad's car where his mom will find it.
immoral_consequence: Joe's mother is mad at his dad but eventually talk it out and punish Joe.

norm: You shouldn't take your small children to work with you.
situation: Jane is upset with her kids for not mopping the kitchen.
intention: Jane wants to educate her kids.
moral_action: Jane makes her kids do extra homework for every chore they don't do.
moral_consequence: The kids eventually start getting the chores done to avoid the homework.
immoral_action: Jane brings her kids to work and has them preform work tasks all day.
immoral_consequence: Jane's kids are tired out and even less willing to do cores at home afterwards.

norm: It's wrong not to help out your parents.
situation: Joe is working on a rickety ladder while his son Tom is watching and holding his phone.
intention: Tom wants to text his friend.
moral_action: Tom holds the ladder for Joe until Joe is finished, then goes to texting his friend.
moral_consequence: Joe's work gets done, and Joe thanks Tom for the help.
immoral_action: Tom looks down at his phone while texting his friend.
immoral_consequence: The ladder falls, causing Joe to fall off and break his arm.

norm: It's good to take care of your looks.
situation: James has very long unkempt hair and has a job interview coming up.
intention: James wants to look good for his job interview.
moral_action: James goes and gets a hair cut and then goes to his interview.
moral_consequence: The interviewer is impressed with James's looks and offers him the job.
immoral_action: James puts his hair in a ponytail and goes to his interview.
immoral_consequence: The interviewer doesn't think James looks professional and doesn't offer him the job.

norm: It's good to be there for others who are upset.
situation: Lilian's friend is going through a bad breakup and asks Lilian to spend Saturday evening with her because she feels very lonely.
intention: Lilian wants to have a pleasant Saturday evening.
moral_action: Lilian spends the evening with her lonely friend, and they watch a great comedy together.
moral_consequence: Lilian's friend has a great time and forgets about her problems.
immoral_action: Lilian tells her friend she is not free on Saturday evening and goes out with other friends instead.
immoral_consequence: Lilian's friend spends her Saturday evening alone and is very sad.

norm: It's nice to send postcards.
situation: Jason is traveling and his mother asked him to get in touch sometimes to tell her how he's doing.
intention: Jason wants to go back to his hotel.
moral_action: Jason gets a postcard on his way to his hotel and writes his mother on it about what he's been doing then has the concierge send it.
moral_consequence: Jason's mother is happy to hear about his time traveling and is relieved that he's okay.
immoral_action: Jason forgets to contact his mother and goes back to hotel room.
immoral_consequence: Jason's mother worries that something may have happened to him as she hasn't heard from him at all.

norm: It's wrong to be a burden on your partner's family.
situation: Joe, who has a girlfriend, decides to move out of his parents' house and in with his girlfriend's family.
intention: Joe wants to live in a place for cheap.
moral_action: Joe arranges a utility payment agreement with his girlfriend's parents and moves in.
moral_consequence: Joe's parents are satisfied that Joe is helping to pay the bills.
immoral_action: Joe lives with his girlfriend's parents and doesn't help pay any of the house bills.
immoral_consequence: Joe's girlfriend's family gets frustrated with Joe and eventually kicks him out of the house.

norm: It's good not to borrow money from a coworker.
situation: John is experiencing financial hardship.
intention: John wants to buy a new TV.
moral_action: John saves money to pay for the new TV.
moral_consequence: John maintains a good relationship with his wocorkers.
immoral_action: John borrows money from a coworker to buy a TV.
immoral_consequence: John is unable to repay the coworker and their relationship is damaged.

norm: It's important to practice things you're not good at.
situation: Jose wants to join the high school football team, but isn't so great at catching the ball.
intention: Jose wants to go to the tryouts.
moral_action: Jose tosses the ball around on a daily basis and when he goes to the tryout, he does very well.
moral_consequence: Jose ends up making the team, and learns the value of practicing.
immoral_action: Jose decides to just wing it when he goes to the tryout without trying to improve his skills beforehand.
immoral_consequence: Jose doesn't end up making the team and feels disappointed in himself.

norm: It's disrespectful to snoop through someone else's communications.
situation: Jake suspects Jenny is cheating on him with another man.
intention: Jake wants to find out if his suspicions are true.
moral_action: Jake asks Jenny if she's been seeing someone else.
moral_consequence: Jenny mentions she's been talking to another guy, but he's just a childhood friend.
immoral_action: Jake hacks Jenny's social media accounts to try and investigate.
immoral_consequence: Jake finds no proof but Jenny finds out what Jake was doing and dumps him.

norm: It is rude to get someones password without asking them.
situation: Will is bored after a long day of work and doesn't know what to do.
intention: Will wants to watch a good movie or TV show.
moral_action: Will offers to pay for half the Netflix subscription, so they can share it.
moral_consequence: Will gets to enjoy streaming shows and movies on Netflix for half the price.
immoral_action: Will gets on his roommate's laptop to get the saved Netflix password.
immoral_consequence: Will feels guilty for invaded his roommate's privacy.

norm: It's wrong to love someone other than your partner.
situation: Sara is in a relationship but has been getting emotionally close to a friend.
intention: Sara wants to deepen her relationship with the friend.
moral_action: Sara decides to end the relationship with her partner before pursuing the friend.
moral_consequence: Sara's partner is able to move on and find someone who loves him.
immoral_action: Sara allows her relationship with the friend to deepen emotionally and falls in love with him while still in a relationship.
immoral_consequence: Sara's partner is led on and continues to think she only has feelings for him.

norm: It is wrong to break into another person's property.
situation: Jackson is strolling along the pathway when he notices an appealing porsche parked by the side.
intention: Jackson wants to have a peek on the car.
moral_action: Jackson checks the car out from the safe distance.
moral_consequence: Jackson develops a willpower to work hard in order to own a Porsche in the future.
immoral_action: As Jackson is looking at the car he breaks the window to check out the inside of the car.
immoral_consequence: Jackson gets arrested for breaking the window of the car.

norm: It's hurtful to decline a friend's wedding invitation.
situation: Milo just received a call from his friend Janelle, asking him to come see her get married this weekend, but he was supposed to go golfing.
intention: Milo wants to respond to the request.
moral_action: Milo says that he would love to go and cancels his golfing plans rigtht away.
moral_consequence: Janelle is pleased to have Milo there because she knows he cares.
immoral_action: Milo tells Janelle that he already had plans to play golf, but wished her good luck.
immoral_consequence: Janelle's feelings are hurt because she thinks Milo feels sports are more important than her happiness.

norm: You shouldn't pity-date people.
situation: Leila knows a nice guy, Bart, who has been single for years because he is very shy.
intention: Leila wants Bart to date someone.
moral_action: Leila realizes that one of her good friends would be a perfect match for Bart and introduces them to each other.
moral_consequence: Bart and Leila's friend fall in love and are both very happy.
immoral_action: Leila decides to start going on dates with Bart because she feels sorry for him, even though she is not in love with him.
immoral_consequence: Bart understands that Leila is dating him out of pity and it makes him feel even worse than being single.

norm: You shouldn't force others to come to your wedding.
situation: Emily is getting married soon, and has planned a big wedding in Hawaii, she wants both her sisters to attend even though they live in Europe.
intention: Emily wants to have a wonderful wedding.
moral_action: Emily invites her sisters, but understands when they can't afford the trip; they Skype in to the reception to say hello to everyone.
moral_consequence: Emily has a wonderful wedding, and her sisters enjoy attending digitally.
immoral_action: Emily nags at her sisters and her parents, until they reluctantly agree to come despite not being able to afford the trip.
immoral_consequence: Emily has her wonderful wedding, but her sisters are now in debt and so severely jet-lagged they really don't enjoy it at all.

norm: It's mean to convince someone to let you cheat.
situation: Ron has a very important test coming up in school, and he feels underprepared.
intention: Ron wants to do well on the test.
moral_action: Ron stays home the night before the test and studies for several hours.
moral_consequence: Ron does very well on the test,, passing with flying colors.
immoral_action: Ron begs his best friend to let him copy his solutions during the test.
immoral_consequence: Ron gets caught cheating off his friend, and gets himself expelled.

norm: It's good to let family members stay at your place.
situation: Candice's mom's home is being renovated.
intention: Candice's mom needs to find somewhere to live.
moral_action: Candice offers her spare bedroom to her mom.
moral_consequence: Candice's mom stays with Candice and saves money.
immoral_action: Candice's mom has to stay at a hotel.
immoral_consequence: Candice's mom spends a lot of money for her room.

norm: It's bad to take advantage of your significant other.
situation: Karla just finished shopping at the mall, and she knows her fiance Logan is nearby at home, busy studying for an exam.
intention: Karla wants to get home.
moral_action: Karla decides to walk home.
moral_consequence: Logan studies properly for his exam and is able to spend the evening relaxing with Karla.
immoral_action: Karla calls Logan to ask him for a ride home.
immoral_consequence: Logan gets distracted from his studying and fails his exam.

norm: It is good to play with your dog.
situation: Jennifer adopted two dogs to play with each other as she's very busy but one of the dogs won't play with the other.
intention: Jennifer wants her dog to play more with the other dog.
moral_action: Jennifer plays games with both her dogs to socialize them.
moral_consequence: Jennifer's more timid dog learns to play with the other dog and is happy.
immoral_action: Jennifer leaves the two dogs together all alone with each other all the time.
immoral_consequence: Jennifer's one dog grows more and more anxious and never learns to play.

norm: People should take responsibility for their legal duties.
situation: Devin divorced his wife and was ordered by the court to pay child support for his child.
intention: Devin wants to respond to the court order.
moral_action: Devin pays the child support the court orders him to pay.
moral_consequence: Devin's child grows up with an adequate amount of material support.
immoral_action: Devin ignores the court order and does not pay the child support.
immoral_consequence: Devin's child grows up lacking in material support.

norm: It's kind to let a friend borrow your possessions.
situation: Dave is at home when he gets a phone call from his friend Jim who wants to borrow his lawn mower.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Jim's request.
moral_action: Dave tells Jim that he'd be glad to lend it to him, and he can come pick it up.
moral_consequence: Jim is delighted that Dave has helped him solve his problem and is happy to have a friend like Dave.
immoral_action: Dave tells Jim that he's not comfortable having his lawn mower  leave his home as it's expensive.
immoral_consequence: Jim is annoyed that Dave won't share with him and stressed out about locating another mower.

norm: It's rude to look down on others.
situation: Gina is a teacher in a school that has mixed income students.
intention: Gina wants to give personal attention to the students.
moral_action: Gina gives personal attention all of the students.
moral_consequence: The lower income students will have a higher chance for success.
immoral_action: Gina gives personal attention to the wealthier students.
immoral_consequence: The lower income students will have a low chance for success.

norm: It's good to help out your buddies.
situation: Larry is listening to music when Russell calls him for help with a flat tire on his car.
intention: Larry wants to continue listening to music.
moral_action: Larry listens to music in the car while driving to Russell's location.
moral_consequence: Russell is able to tackle the flat tire problem with Larry's help.
immoral_action: Larry tells Russell that he can't come and goes back to his music.
immoral_consequence: Russell is stranded for hours until someone else helps him with the tire.

norm: It's good to perform CPR on someone who is dying.
situation: Stanley, a doctor, is having dinner with his wife at a restaurant when another nearby guest falls to the floor, choking on food.
intention: Stanley wants to see the choking guest live.
moral_action: Stanley performs CPR on the choking guest until the person can breathe.
moral_consequence: The choking person thanks Stanley for saving their life.
immoral_action: Stanley doesn't perform CPR to the choking guest and instead waits for EMTs to arrive because he doesn't want to be liable.
immoral_consequence: The choking guest dies before the EMTs arrive.

norm: It's wrong to clog toilets.
situation: Jerry is on a florida trip renting a home with some friends.
intention: Jerry is not feeling well and needs to use the bathroom.
moral_action: Jerry is careful about how much toilet paper is used and leaves the bathroom clean.
moral_consequence: Jerry feels better shortly after and enjoys the rest of his vacation.
immoral_action: Jerry uses too much toilet paper and badly clogs the toilet.
immoral_consequence: A plumber is needed to fix it and the group is charged extra by the rental home owner.

norm: You shouldn't let your partner nag you.
situation: Dana told her boyfriend Paul that she would wash the dishes at night, but he keeps telling her to do them during the day.
intention: Dana wants to respond to Paul.
moral_action: Dana tells Paul to stop bothering her as she said she will do the dishes at night.
moral_consequence: Paul will learn that he cannot bother Dana into doing things when he wants.
immoral_action: Dana tells Paul she will do the dishes during the day.
immoral_consequence: Paul will think he can get Dana to do what he wants if he keeps repeating what he wants.

norm: It's bad to undermine the self-esteem of a grandchild.
situation: Joan granddaughter confides that she wants to be an actor when she gets older.
intention: Joan, a failed actor, wants to respond to her granddaughters declaration.
moral_action: Joan is cautionary but encouraging to her granddaughter wish.
moral_consequence: Joan's support gives her granddaughter a boost of confidence.
immoral_action: Wanting to curtail what she feels is a fruitless dream Joan decides to crush her granddaughters dream before it grows too big.
immoral_consequence: Joan's harsh response leads her granddaughter to lose faith in her ability to succeed.

norm: It's wrong to hang out with a family member's ex.
situation: Paul's sister divorces her cheating husband Jeff, but then Paul gets a reminder about his monthly golf game with Jeff.
intention: Paul wants to respond to the reminder.
moral_action: Paul cancels their monthly game out of loyalty to his sister.
moral_consequence: Paul is able to show his sister the support she needs.
immoral_action: Paul decides to continue meeting his ex brother in law for golf.
immoral_consequence: Paul's relationship with his sister becomes strained when she realizes he is still in touch with her ex.

norm: You shouldn't make fun of someone that wears adult diapers.
situation: James' best friend just confided in him that he has to wear adult diapers due to incontinence.
intention: James wants his friend to stop oversharing.
moral_action: James tells his friend he should only talk about that issue with his doctor.
moral_consequence: James' friend is upset but quickly forgets about the incident.
immoral_action: "James starts calling his friend ""Diaper Man"" in front of everyone they know."
immoral_consequence: James' friend stops hanging out with him and complains about him to all their mutual friends.

norm: You should always pay back money you owe to others.
situation: Brock borrowed a good amount of money from his friend a long time ago and his financial situation has improved significantly.
intention: Brock wants to consider paying his friend back.
moral_action: Brock pays back his friend in full with a little extra for helping him out.
moral_consequence: Brock is seen as someone with integrity and his relationship with his friend strengthens.
immoral_action: Brock decides to never pay back his friend and simply moves on.
immoral_consequence: Brock's friend thinks Brock is a dishonest person and is no longer friends with Brock.

norm: Excluding your father from your academic achievements is hurtful
situation: Joan hasn't been close to her dad since her parents divorced nevertheless he asks to attend her graduation ceremony.
intention: Joan wants to make a decision about whether or not to invite her dad.
moral_action: Despite their distance Joan asks her dad to come to her graduation.
moral_consequence: Joan and her dad are able to begin rebuilding a relationship.
immoral_action: Since they aren't that close Joan asks her dad not to attend her graduation.
immoral_consequence: The gulf between Joan and her dad grows as a result.

norm: You should not feel attracted to underage girls.
situation: Jason is at his little sister's birthday party with a bunch of teenaged girls.
intention: Jason wants to go out on a date to the movies later on that night.
moral_action: After the party, Jason calls his girlfriend and asks her if she wants to go to the movies.
moral_consequence: Jason and his girlfriend enjoy a night together at the movies.
immoral_action: Jason asks one of the young girls at the party if she wants to go to the movies with him.
immoral_consequence: Jason is later arrested by the police for dating an underage girl.

norm: It's wrong to starve an animal
situation: Sam's cat is meowing at him because it is hungry.
intention: Sam doesn't want to hear the cat anymore.
moral_action: Sam feeds his cat.
moral_consequence: The  cat feels happy and well fed.
immoral_action: Sam puts the cat away in an upstairs bedroom where he can't hear it.
immoral_consequence: The cat goes hungry and experiences discomfort.

norm: It's wrong to cheat in school.
situation: James is in class and the teacher gives him a pop quiz.
intention: James wants to take the test.
moral_action: James isn't sure of all the answers, but he tries his best.
moral_consequence: James does better than he thought and gets a B+.
immoral_action: James idn't very well prepared, so he takes out his phone to look for the answers online.
immoral_consequence: James gets caught looking up the answers and fails the test.

norm: It's wrong to like war.
situation: A war between neighboring countries breaks out and both sides approach Tim's company for supplies.
intention: Tim wants his company to be successful.
moral_action: Tim ponders the meaning of success across realms other than the bottom line and refuses to sell to either side.
moral_consequence: A journalist covers Tim's moral stand garnering the company positive attention.
immoral_action: Tim sells to both sides, privately relishing the war's affect on his profits.
immoral_consequence: An expose shows how immoral Tim's is being and the company's stocks drop.

norm: It's not okay to break up siblings.
situation: Gilbert works at his country's border and is responsible for sending immigrant orphans to different orphanages.
intention: Gilbert wants to serve his country.
moral_action: Gilbert knows that humanity sometimes supersedes the written rules, and makes sure to keep two orphan immigrant brothers he encounters during his work together with one another.
moral_consequence: The two brothers that Gilbert kept together are very happy to have one another.
immoral_action: Gilbert follows the letter of the law of his country and finds himself in a situation where he sends two brother orphan immigrants to separate orphanages.
immoral_consequence: The brothers that Gilbert separates become frightened and grow up to resent the separation that was forced on them.

norm: You are allowed to voice your opinion to loved ones.
situation: James' father liked to go on long rants about godless liberals at the dinner table.
intention: James wants to express his feelings.
moral_action: James expresses his own liberal beliefs to his father at the dinner table.
moral_consequence: After a major fight, the family agree to ban talk about politics and religion at the dinner table.
immoral_action: James complains about his father to all his friends but doesn't confront him directly.
immoral_consequence: James' father keeps ranting so James increases the frequency of his complaints.

norm: You shouldn't ignore an abusive pet owner.
situation: Darren lives next door to Rob who owns a dog, and Darren hears Rob screaming and the dog yelping in pain.
intention: Darren wants to find out what's going on next door.
moral_action: Darren knocks on Robs door and is told everything is fine, and Darren doesn't believe him, so he calls animal control who take the dog from Rob.
moral_consequence: Darren saves the dogs life and finds out the dog has a new owner who treats him kindly.
immoral_action: Darren knocks on Robs door and is told everything is fine, and Darren doesn't believe him, but still chooses to do nothing.
immoral_consequence: Later that night, Darren hears the dog in pain again and finds out the next day the dog has passed away.

norm: You should talk in private about sensitive topics.
situation: Vance just separated from his wife because she cheated and is asked by Tony in the open concept office about how he is doing.
intention: Vance wants to tell Tony about his wife's infidelity.
moral_action: Vance motions for Tony to come outside with him and then tells him all about his wife's infidelity and how he left her.
moral_consequence: The other coworkers notice Tony and Vance leaving but don't think anything of it and continue working.
immoral_action: Vance tells Tony all about how he found out about his wife’s infidelity, and how they had a huge fight about it before he left.
immoral_consequence: The other coworkers overhear everything Vance is saying and are uncomfortable knowing his personal life details.

norm: It's not okay to bully people.
situation: Milton is at school and does not have money for lunch.
intention: Milton wants to get money for lunch.
moral_action: Milton asks the principal if he can borrow money for lunch.
moral_consequence: Milton gets money to be able to buy food.
immoral_action: Milton tells another student to give them money, or they will be hit.
immoral_consequence: Milton gets in trouble because he took money from another student.

norm: It's wrong for someone to make impossible demands.
situation: Jeff solicited the services of a professional tax firm and notices a small mistake by the tax firm.
intention: Jeff wants to demand reparations.
moral_action: Jeff contacts the tax firm about the mistake and waits for a response.
moral_consequence: The tax firm never makes the same mistake again and compensates Jeff an appropriate amount.
immoral_action: Jeff demands the tax firm pay him millions of dollars for the small mistake.
immoral_consequence: Jeff's demand goes nowhere and the tax firm stops doing business with him.

norm: You shouldn't block people on your partner's phone.
situation: Chris' girlfriend, Meg, often messages her male coworkers and it makes him jealous.
intention: Chris wants to stop feeling jealous about Meg talking to her coworkers.
moral_action: Chris explains to Meg how he's been feeling.
moral_consequence: Meg assures Chris that her communication with coworkers is strictly professional.
immoral_action: Chris blocks all of the male contacts in Meg's phone.
immoral_consequence: Meg misses an important work update that was sent to her by a male coworker, causing her to fall behind on her work.

norm: You should always be on time.
situation: Jim is on his way to see his girlfriend when he sees a dine-in restaurant, knowing that he will be late if he stops by.
intention: Jim wants to satisfy his hunger.
moral_action: Jim waits instead of stopping and eats dinner with his girlfriend at her house.
moral_consequence: Jim keeps his girlfriend and his girlfriend doesn't get angry.
immoral_action: Jim eats at a dine in restaurant which makes him late to see his girlfriend.
immoral_consequence: Jim's girlfriend gets angry and breaks up with him.

norm: It's rude to yell at people
situation: Tim is riding his bike down the road when Tom almost hits him with his car.
intention: Tim wants to reprimand Tom for the close call.
moral_action: Tim tells Tom that he could have killed him and that one day he probably will kill someone driving like that.
moral_consequence: Tom tells Tim that he is sorry and that he will be much more careful from now on.
immoral_action: Tim starts yelling at Tom and calling him names saying he almost killed him.
immoral_consequence: Tom thinks Tim is crazy and attempts to run away before Tim can get violent with him.

norm: You should not let your appearance control your life.
situation: Nick is obese, so he hates going outside, but he has to go see a doctor for an issue.
intention: Nick has to decide whether to go to the doctor.
moral_action: Nick decides that he cares more about his issue than his weight, so he goes to see his doctor.
moral_consequence: Nick becomes more okay with going outside and gets help with his issue.
immoral_action: Nick doesn't want people looking at him, so he decides to stay at home.
immoral_consequence: Nick is not able to get help for his issue and suffers.

norm: It is nice to invite your friend on a hike.
situation: Jacob is camping in a natural area with his close friend.
intention: Jacob wants to go on a nature hike.
moral_action: Jacob asks his friend to come along on a nature hike with him.
moral_consequence: Jacob's friend feels that Jacob enjoys their company because he wants to hike together.
immoral_action: Jacob goes on a hike by himself leaving his friend at the camp.
immoral_consequence: Jacob's friend feels like Jacob doesn't want to be around them.

norm: It's good to propose to a paramour.
situation: George has been dating his partner for a few years, and she keeps hinting at wanting to get married.
intention: George wants to make his partner happy.
moral_action: George decides to take the hints seriously and proposes to his partner.
moral_consequence: George's partner is thrilled and accepts the proposal.
immoral_action: George ignores the hints about marriage but asks his partner to move in with him instead.
immoral_consequence: George's partner feels that he is afraid of commitment and breaks off the relationship.

norm: One should never yell at their parents.
situation: Benjamin is tired of his elderly mother wasting household expenses by buying items on TV, and he sees his mother about to order something.
intention: Benjamin wants his mother to stop shopping.
moral_action: Benjamin gets out the bills and sits down beside his mother showing her how her shopping habits are harming the house budget.
moral_consequence: His mother stops buying things she doesn't need.
immoral_action: Benjamin asks her if she has the brains of a fly in a loud tone as he shuts off the computer.
immoral_consequence: His mother starts crying.

norm: It's not normal to put your life in danger
situation: Carey is driving on the highway at night, and gets stuck behind two trucks side by side in each lane.
intention: Carey wants to get past the trucks.
moral_action: Carey flashes her headlights to let them know she wants to pass, then waits for an opening.
moral_consequence: The trucks eventually stagger their positions, and Carey is able to drive past them.
immoral_action: Carey drives between the trucks, scraping along each side of her car.
immoral_consequence: The trucks swerve to the sides and Carey nearly crashes her car.

norm: It's honorable to not cheat on a test.
situation: Jeff notices his classmates cheating on a hard math test and is tempted to do the same.
intention: Jeff wants to do well on the test.
moral_action: Jeff decides to see if he can ace the test based on his own knowledge.
moral_consequence: Jeff is able to see how much he actually learned in class.
immoral_action: Jeff decides to look at his classmate's answer and copy them down on his test sheet.
immoral_consequence: Jeff doesn't learn anything and doesn't earn his good grade.

norm: It's wrong to leave the scene of an accident
situation: Azure hits another car while driving on the road.
intention: Azure wants to get help for the accident.
moral_action: Azure pulls out her phone and calls the non-emergency police number.
moral_consequence: The police come out and help Azure and the person in the other car.
immoral_action: Azure drives to a nearby gas station to ask the attendant for help.
immoral_consequence: The police charge Azure with leaving the scene of an accident, despite her good intentions.

norm: It's good to buy children gifts for their first birthday.
situation: James' son is about to turn one year old and is starting to outgrow the toys he got at his baby shower.
intention: James wants to be frugal.
moral_action: James buys a few toys for his son, but asks his friends to donate to his college fund instead.
moral_consequence: James' son has a lot of fun playing with his new toy dinosaurs.
immoral_action: James asks his friends to make contributions to his son's college fund instead of buying toys.
immoral_consequence: James' son barely seems to notice his first birthday party.

norm: It's good to surprise your kids.
situation: Doug is the father of two kids and is doing some shopping before Christmas.
intention: Doug wants to buy some presents for his kids.
moral_action: Doug decides to buy expensive toys that his kids always wanted.
moral_consequence: Doug's kids are surprised and ecstatic as they open their presents on Christmas.
immoral_action: Doug buys some generic sweaters as presents for his kids.
immoral_consequence: Doug's children are disappointed beyond belief when they open their presents.

norm: People should respect other people's physical boundaries.
situation: Tom runs into his old acquaintance Summer in the park for an early morning jog.
intention: Tom wants to greet Summer.
moral_action: Tom tries to give Summer a hug, but she informs him she wants to maintain social distance, so he complies and just asks how she's doing.
moral_consequence: Summer and Tom maintain proper social distance and chat together comfortably as they walk through the park.
immoral_action: While Tom reaches out for a hug, Summer informs Tom that she wants to maintain social distance, but Tom gives her a big hug anyway claiming that he's a hugger.
immoral_consequence: Summer feels uncomfortable, pushes Tom away, and quickly walks away.

norm: It's wrong to get revenge on your partner.
situation: Julie walked in on her boyfriend cheating with another woman.
intention: Julie wants to teach her boyfriend a lesson.
moral_action: Julie tells her boyfriend how much he hurt her and asks how he would feel if she cheated on him.
moral_consequence: Julie cries with her boyfriend as they discuss the next steps for their relationship.
immoral_action: Julie screams at her boyfriend, throwing a glass at his head.
immoral_consequence: Julie gets arrested for domestic violence and goes to jail.

norm: It is good to keep your living area neat.
situation: James has been working lots of overtime and coming home very late.
intention: James wants to go to bed as soon as he gets home.
moral_action: James uses some of his overtime pay to hire a cleaning crew.
moral_consequence: It's easy for James to relax and fall asleep in his clean house.
immoral_action: James doesn't bother to clean anything for six months, so he has more time to sleep.
immoral_consequence: James' house becomes infested with rodents and roaches because of all the unwashed plates.

norm: It's wrong to look down on others.
situation: Susan is going to go out to a fancy party with Emily, but Emily is wearing jeans and a tshirt.
intention: Susan wants to attract positive attention.
moral_action: Susan lends Emily a nice dress to wear.
moral_consequence: Emily wears the dress, and they go to the party and have fun.
immoral_action: Susan tells Emily she won't be seen in public with her dressed like that.
immoral_consequence: Emily feels ashamed and goes home instead of the party.

norm: It's bad to get distracted while driving.
situation: John is driving home from work when he hears his phone alert him to a text message.
intention: John wants to find out the content of the text message.
moral_action: John waits until he stops at the next traffic light and then looks at his phone.
moral_consequence: John drives home safely and without incident.
immoral_action: John looks at his phone immediately and reads the next message while driving.
immoral_consequence: John fails to notice the car in front of him stop unexpectedly, and he rear ends it.

norm: You should not kick others.
situation: Monty is standing in line at the store but the person in front of him isn't moving up.
intention: Monty wants the person in front of him to move up.
moral_action: Monty taps the person in front of him on the shoulder to let him know the line is moving.
moral_consequence: The person that was standing in front of Monty starts walking forward.
immoral_action: Monty kicks the person in front of him to make him start walking.
immoral_consequence: The man that was standing in front of Monty turns around and punches him the gut.

norm: You shouldn't let someone quit school.
situation: Jon's son Billy has been really unhappy in school lately.
intention: Jon wants Billy to be happy.
moral_action: Jon, Billy and the school guidance counselor sit down and have a long discussion.
moral_consequence: Billy starts feeling a little better about his schooling.
immoral_action: Jon signs Billy out of school after Billy begs him to do it.
immoral_consequence: Billy can't find a job because he doesn't have a high school diploma.

norm: Parents should acknowledge important milestones in a child's life.
situation: Fred's son recently graduated from college and invites Fred to attend his graduation.
intention: Fred wants to respond to the invitation.
moral_action: Fred accepts the invitation and clears out his schedule to attend his son's graduation.
moral_consequence: Fred's relationship with his son improves, and he gets to watch his son become successful.
immoral_action: Fred ignores the invitation and never shows up at his son's graduation.
immoral_consequence: Fred's son views Fred as uncaring and starts to distance himself from Fred.

norm: It's not okay to leave someone without a home.
situation: Dorian is a landlord to Jasmine and a father to Callie, who will soon be returning home from college.
intention: Dorian wants Jasmine out so that he can give her space to Callie.
moral_action: Dorian gives Jasmine 60 days to move out.
moral_consequence: Jasmine is able to find new living arrangements and Callie moves into her father's property.
immoral_action: Dorian evicts Jasmine without warning.
immoral_consequence: With no family, money, or anywhere to go, Jasmine is left homeless.

norm: It is best to keep friendship and romance separate.
situation: Bill and Nancy have been best friends since childhood when one day Nancy asks Bill on a romantic date.
intention: Bill wants to respond to Nancy's request.
moral_action: Bill tells Nancy that he doesn't want to go out with her as he fears it'll ruin their friendship.
moral_consequence: Nancy is happy that Bill is respectful of their friendship and cherishes it enough to protect it.
immoral_action: Bill tells Nancy that he would love to take her out on a date that very night.
immoral_consequence: Nancy learns new things about Bill which lead to break up and the end of their friendship.

norm: It's normal for parents to support your children's dreams
situation: Nancy is at home when her son Paul comes in and tells her he wants to be an astronaut when he grows up.
intention: Nancy wants to mention how hard that would be.
moral_action: Nancy tells Paul that it's a difficult tasks but that if others have done it so can he if he works hard.
moral_consequence: Paul is full of inspiration and drive and wants to prove to his mom he can be one of the few who make it.
immoral_action: Nancy tells Paul that it's an impossible dream since only a few people every few years get to be astronauts.
immoral_consequence: Paul feels terrible because he's being told his dream is not possible and is discouraged from trying.

norm: It's wrong for someone to lock up their child.
situation: Rover's son Barker dropped a laptop and broke it, so Rover couldn't finish his project for work until the weekend.
intention: Rover wants to teach Barker a lesson.
moral_action: Rover takes away Barker's laptop and gives it back to him on Friday afternoon.
moral_consequence: Barker has to do homework all weekend and realizes that that's what he made his dad do.
immoral_action: Rover locks Barker in his room with his dog Joe until Rover's work project is done.
immoral_consequence: Both Barker and Joe are starving by the time Rover lets them out and have learned nothing except not to tick off Rover.

norm: It's wrong to sell something that isn't yours.
situation: Deborah and Emily are cleaning out their closets and Emily finds a lot of valuable old records.
intention: Deborah wants to earn some money.
moral_action: Deborah asks Emily if she wants to sell her records to make money.
moral_consequence: Emily agrees, and the two women share their profits.
immoral_action: Deborah takes Emily's records and sells them online.
immoral_consequence: Emily gets mad at Deborah and yells at her, demanding that Deborah give her the money.

norm: Outbursts are frowned upon.
situation: Mary's kid broke a vase at home by accident.
intention: Mary wants her kid  to answer for the damage.
moral_action: Mary asks her kid to explain the accident and promise to be careful next time.
moral_consequence: Her kid feels relieved and hugs Mary for her kindness and understanding.
immoral_action: Mary gets very furious while questioning her kid about the accident.
immoral_consequence: Her kid feels scared and immediately starts to cry.

norm: You shouldn't pry into someone's relationship.
situation: Kelly and her husband Marc are having personal problems that she's been secretive about, and her friend Sue is curious as to why.
intention: Sue wants to ask Kelly about her and Marc's issues.
moral_action: When Sue asks Kelly what's wrong, she says she doesn't want to discuss it right now, so Sue leaves it at that until Kelly's ready to talk about it.
moral_consequence: Kelly appreciates Sue respecting her boundaries and see's her as a good friend.
immoral_action: When Sue asks Kelly what the problem is, she says it's personal, but Sue keeps pressing her about it.
immoral_consequence: Kelly doesn't appreciate Sue being so nosy, and she tells her to stay out of her life if she can't mind her own business.

norm: It's good to convince people of things.
situation: Bob has been looking forward to a scary movie, but his friend Ted isn't sure if he wants to join him.
intention: Bob wants to see the scary movie.
moral_action: Bob talks Ted into seeing the scary movie with him.
moral_consequence: Bob has a great time at the movie because Ted was with him.
immoral_action: Bob goes to see the scary movie all by himself.
immoral_consequence: Bob is sad that he wasn't able to enjoy the movie with Ted.

norm: You should not eat in the bathroom.
situation: Sally is working at home, and she has a to have a task competed by noon, but she is very hungry.
intention: Sally wants to eat something without taking additional break time.
moral_action: Sally gets a drinkable yogurt to have while she is working to hold her off until later.
moral_consequence: Sally feels nourished from her yogurt snack and has a nice lunch after noon.
immoral_action: Sally takes a sandwich into the bathroom with her and eats it while she is in the bathroom taking a break.
immoral_consequence: Sally gets sick later because it was not sanitary to eat in the bathroom.

norm: You shouldn't abuse return policies at stores.
situation: Ash is unhappy with an item from the store after wearing it a few times.
intention: Ash wants to get a different item to wear.
moral_action: Ash donates the item to charity and buys something else which is on sale.
moral_consequence: Ash feels good about herself and helps the needy.
immoral_action: Ash pretends the item hasn't been used and returns the item.
immoral_consequence: Ash feels guilty and another customer ends up buying a used item.

norm: It shows kindness to be forgiving of minor transgressions.
situation: Brad is walking down the hallway at school when he is bumped into by another student named Scott, who quickly apologizes.
intention: Brad wants to respond to Scott's apology.
moral_action: Brad accepts Scott's apology with a smile and tells him not to worry about it.
moral_consequence: Brad and Scott both feel happy about the resolution of the incident and go on with their day.
immoral_action: Brad gives Scott a push and angrily tells him to watch where he's going.
immoral_consequence: Brad and Scott both remain upset about the incident for some time.

norm: You shouldn't tell others information that seems impossible.
situation: Don is talking about religion with his friend, and his friend asked him why he believes in God.
intention: Don wants to explain why he believes in God.
moral_action: Don tells his friend that his family used to read him bible verses all the time.
moral_consequence: Don's friend understands his explanation and doesn't look down on him.
immoral_action: Don tells his friend that God spoke to him when he was younger.
immoral_consequence: Don's friend will think that Don is crazy and will think that he's a liar.

norm: It's good to be compassionate in life.
situation: Sarah is watching her children play at a local playground in an affluent area one afternoon when a low-income family arrives in a beat up car and worn out clothes.
intention: Sarah wants her children to make friends.
moral_action: Sarah welcomes the low-income family and introduces her children to theirs.
moral_consequence: Sarah's children play with their new friends and don't care at all about their social or economic standing.
immoral_action: Sarah refuses to acknowledge the arrive of the low-income family and takes her children to a nearby walking trail where another family is hiking.
immoral_consequence: Sarah's children are sad that they don't get to continue playing on the playground.

norm: It's bad to make fun of those with special needs.
situation: Larry is hanging out with his friends in a store when a person he knows with Down syndrome walks in.
intention: Larry wants to respond to the person with Down syndrome.
moral_action: Larry waves to the person with Down syndrome and invites him to the group.
moral_consequence: The person with Down syndrome waves back, and they have a good time hanging out.
immoral_action: Larry makes fun of the person with Down syndrome by imitating how he speaks.
immoral_consequence: Larry's friends are appalled and leave him alone in the store.

norm: Is wrong to lie about your experience
situation: Henry is being interviewed for a job by Tim when Tim asks Henry if he has any managerial experience.
intention: Henry wants to respond to Tim's question.
moral_action: Henry admits that he has no managerial experience but that he's a quick learner and would love the opportunity to show he's capable in the job.
moral_consequence: Tim decides to take a chance of Henry as he's appreciative of Henry's honesty and ambition.
immoral_action: Henry falsely tells Tim that he has plenty of managerial experience at his most recent job.
immoral_consequence: Tim follows up with Henry's references, finds out Henry was lying and declines to offer Henry a job.

norm: It's important to communicate honestly with your partner.
situation: Becky's husband snores loudly everynight.
intention: Becky wants to have a happy marriage.
moral_action: Becky approaches her husband about his snoring, and he agrees to see a doctor.
moral_consequence: Becky's husband gets help for his snoring and Becky gets good sleep every night.
immoral_action: Becky doesn't want to hurt her husband's feelings so doesn't tell that his snoring bothers her.
immoral_consequence: Becky never gets a decent night's sleep and resents her husband.

norm: It's rude to call someone at dinnertime.
situation: Gabrielle broke the toilet, and her roommate is having dinner with her mother.
intention: Gabrielle needs help fixing the toliet.
moral_action: Gabrielle watches tutorials on fixing toilets on youtube.
moral_consequence: Gabrielle stops relying on others because she can take care of her own problems.
immoral_action: Gabrielle calls her roommate several time through the night.
immoral_consequence: Gabrielle is scolded by her roommate later for butting in on her time with her mother.

norm: It's rude to expect others to pay your bill.
situation: Stefy is on a first date with a boy at a restaurant and the waiter has just brought the bill, but the boy hasn't said anything about who pays.
intention: Stefy wants her portion of the meal to get paid for.
moral_action: Stefy flags down the waiter and asks him to split the check, so she can pay for her part, then does so.
moral_consequence: The boy is impressed that Stefy is independent and willing to do her part in a relationship.
immoral_action: Stefy bats her eyelashes at the boy and thanks him for taking care of her bill and that she would appreciate it.
immoral_consequence: The boy thinks that Stefy is a money-loving manipulator and doesn't go out with her again.

norm: It's mean to dump someone for someone else.
situation: Melanie's boyfriend just introduced her to his roommate, who is really good looking but single.
intention: Melanie wants to help her boyfriend's roommate find a girlfriend.
moral_action: Melanie introduces her boyfriend's roommate to one of her good friends who she thinks will make a good match.
moral_consequence: Melanie's boyfriend is happy that Melanie helped his roommate and his feelings of love and loyalty for her increase.
immoral_action: Melanie breaks up with her boyfriend, so she can ask out her boyfriend's roommate.
immoral_consequence: Melanie's boyfriend is heartbroken and feels betrayed by Melanie and jealous of his roommate.

norm: It's best to be kind to animals.
situation: Steve is at a petting zoo feeding animals when a goat takes his hat.
intention: Steve wants to get his hat back from the goat.
moral_action: Steve waves some food in front of the goat to coax it.
moral_consequence: The goat drops the hat and goes after the food in Steve's hand.
immoral_action: Steve uses the back of his hand to smack the goat.
immoral_consequence: The goat gets mad at Steve and rams into him.

norm: You shouldn't try to sleep with someone else's significant other.
situation: Ted is talking to his brother's girlfriend because she's sad.
intention: Ted wants to cheer up his brother's girlfriend.
moral_action: Ted tells his brother's girlfriend he thinks of her as family.
moral_consequence: The girlfriend feels comforted that Ted cares about her.
immoral_action: Ted seduces his brother's girlfriend to distract her from her problems.
immoral_consequence: The girlfriend gets dumped by Ted's brother.

norm: It's wrong to do things out of retibution.
situation: Tina is about to head out when she notices her neighbor ride his bike right into her parked car which results in a dent.
intention: Tina wants to react to the accident that just occured.
moral_action: Tina runs up to the neighbor and asks him if he's OK and needs any assistance.
moral_consequence: The neighbor is happy to see Tina trying to help him and is relieved she's not mad about her car.
immoral_action: Tina runs up to the neighbor and picks up his bike only to throw it back down on the ground in an attempt to damage it.
immoral_consequence: The neighbor is terrified because he thinks Tina might attack him next.

norm: It's wrong to start fights at school.
situation: Ken gets picked on every day by a bully at schoool.
intention: Ken wants to make the bully stop bothering him.
moral_action: Ken goes to the school counselor and informs them about the situation with the bully.
moral_consequence: Ken isn't bothered by the bully any longer after the bully is disciplined.
immoral_action: Ken goes up to his bully and kicks him in the crotch then punches him in the face.
immoral_consequence: Ken is suspended from school for two weeks.

norm: People shouldn't give their word unless they mean it.
situation: Paul is flying home for Christmas tonight when his friend Josh asks him for a ride to the airport the next morning.
intention: Paul wants to respond to Josh's request for a ride to the airport.
moral_action: Paul tells Josh that he would help if he could, but he's leaving town tonight.
moral_consequence: Josh finds another friend to give him a ride and makes his flight.
immoral_action: Paul tells Josh not to worry and promises he'll give him a ride the next morning.
immoral_consequence: Josh misses his flight when Paul doesn't show up to take him to the airport, and he has to buy another plane ticket.

norm: It's rude to poop exclusively at work.
situation: Ron is at home, about to go to work when he realizes he has to use the bathroom, he has lately been trying to last until work.
intention: Ron wants to poop.
moral_action: Ron decides to poop in his own toilet for a change.
moral_consequence: Ron is more efficient at work, not wasting hours on the clock.
immoral_action: Ron decides to wait to get to work, so he can get paid for it.
immoral_consequence: Ron's boss notices that he's been doing this a lot lately, and yells at him for it.

norm: It's not okay to make people feel out of place.
situation: Chris is hanging out with his best friend Chad and Chad's new girlfriend Anna.
intention: Chris wants to entertain Chad and Anna.
moral_action: Chris suggests that Chad and Anna join Chris in a three person board game.
moral_consequence: Anna becomes closer friends with Chris.
immoral_action: Chris makes inside jokes that only Chris and Chad understand.
immoral_consequence: Anna feels left out of the group.

norm: It's rude to eat food that doesn't belong to you.
situation: Andy and Bobby are roommates that share a refrigerator and kitchen.
intention: Bobby wants to make himself something as a late night snack.
moral_action: Bobby makes himself a sandwich for his midnight snack, leaving Andy's ice cream alone.
moral_consequence: Bobby is full and has a nice night sleep after eating.
immoral_action: Bobby makes himself a late night snack which happens to be Andy's ice cream and eats it.
immoral_consequence: Bobby gets very sick from eating Andy's ice cream as Andy put laxatives in it.

norm: It's wrong to assume someone is lying without proof
situation: Jan is upset about her partner coming home late and giving a questionable excuse.
intention: Jan wants to confront her partner.
moral_action: Jan brings it up later and decides to trust her partner until given more reason not to.
moral_consequence: Jan's partner appreciates her understanding and being able to move past it.
immoral_action: Jan confronts her partner and doesn't believe a word he says.
immoral_consequence: Jan's partner is upset because of her lack of trust.

norm: It's wrong to hide that you're in a relationship.
situation: Jane is at a family reunion, chatting her old-fashioned aunt May who she hasn't seen in years.
intention: Jane wants to tell aunt May about what she's been up to recently.
moral_action: Jane tells her Aunt May all about her life, including about her live-in boyfriend.
moral_consequence: Aunt May is shocked but tells Jane she's glad that she found someone she loves.
immoral_action: Jane tells aunt May about her new job and apartment, avoids mentioning that she has a boyfriend who also lives with her.
immoral_consequence: Aunt May tries to set Jane up with a young man that she knows since she thinks Jane might be lonely.

norm: You shouldn't make comments about other people's weight.
situation: Jenny has just been introduced to a new coworker who happens to be overweight.
intention: Jenny wants to have a conversation with the new employee.
moral_action: Jenny offers to show the new employee around the building.
moral_consequence: Jenny makes a good first impression.
immoral_action: Jenny suggests the new employee join her at the company gym to help kick start her weight loss.
immoral_consequence: Jenny alienates the new employee with her suggestion.

norm: Forgetting to buckle your child's seat belt is irresponsible.
situation: Owen was putting his son in the car before they went to their house.
intention: Owen wants to drive home.
moral_action: Owen makes sure that his son is buckled in safely to his carseat.
moral_consequence: Owen and his son arrive safe and sound to the house without incident.
immoral_action: Owen tells his son that he doesn't have to wear his seatbelt.
immoral_consequence: A police officer pulls Owen over and gives him a ticket for putting his son in danger.

norm: It's good to take a sick puppy to the vet.
situation: James' puppy suddenly seemed tired all day and then started throwing up.
intention: James wants his puppy to feel better.
moral_action: James takes his puppy to the vet late in the afternoon.
moral_consequence: The vet says that the puppy has a bowel obstruction and needs surgery right away.
immoral_action: James cuddles the puppy and gives him lots of water, but doesn't take him to the vet.
immoral_consequence: The puppy starts having seizures in the middle of the night.

norm: It is wrong to think of other people as wretched.
situation: Dave and Karen are back home after attending a party when Karen asks Dave what he thought of Rick, who they met that night.
intention: Dave wants to give an opinion of Rick to Karen.
moral_action: Dave tells Karen that so far Rick seems like a normal guy and that he looks to be a potential friend.
moral_consequence: Karen is happy to hear Dave interacted nicely with Rick and that he might make a new friend out of him.
immoral_action: Dave tells Karen that Rick gave him a scumbag vibe and that he already has strong feelings of dislike for him because he thinks he's no good.
immoral_consequence: Karen is unpleasantly surprised that Dave could make such judgements so quickly and is turned off by Dave's hatred of Rick.

norm: You shouldn't be the cause of someone else's death.
situation: Nancy is driving to work when her cell phone starts ringing, while ahead is a stop sign intersection with a pedestrian crossing.
intention: Nancy wants to answer her phone.
moral_action: Nancy stops at the stop sign and answers the phone while stopped.
moral_consequence: The pedestrian crosses safely and Nancy finishes her phone call.
immoral_action: Nancy reaches out and answers her phone, taking her eyes off the road.
immoral_consequence: Nancy runs over a pedestrian crossing in the crosswalk and kills them.

norm: Attacking people without talking to them is wrong.
situation: Lisa's neighbor had been letting her dog poop in her yard for the past few weeks.
intention: Lisa wants her neighbor's dog to stay out of the yard.
moral_action: Lisa talks to her neighbor about her dog as soon as she got home from work.
moral_consequence: Lisa's neighbor makes sure that her dog doesn't go in Lisa's yard anymore.
immoral_action: Lisa starts swinging at her neighbor as soon as she got home from work.
immoral_consequence: Lisa's neighbor calls the police and has her arrested for assault.

norm: It's good to care for sick pets.
situation: Berkeley has taken his sick dog back to the vet when his girlfriend asks him on a date.
intention: Berkeley wants to spend time with his girlfriend.
moral_action: Berkeley explains the situation with his dog, and invites her over.
moral_consequence: Berkeley and his girlfriend discover the cause of his dog's sickness while they hang out.
immoral_action: Berkeley takes his girlfriend to the arcade leaving his dog alone.
immoral_consequence: Berkeley has to take his dog back to the vet when its conditions worsens due to neglect.

norm: Dog fighting is unacceptable.
situation: James just bought a pitbll puppy and is ready to start training it.
intention: James wants the pitbull to protect him.
moral_action: James takes his dog to a reputable trainer to be trained as a guard dog.
moral_consequence: James' dog is devoted to him but very intimidating to any strangers who come to the house.
immoral_action: James takes his pitbull to underground dog fighting rings to increase its aggressiveness.
immoral_consequence: James' pitbull is traumatized and begins attacking him every time he tries to take it to the car.

norm: It's not okay to obscure things from others.
situation: Pascal doesn't want anyone to know what his favorite food is.
intention: Pascal wants to made a decision if he should hide this information about himself.
moral_action: Pascal decides he shouldn't hide this about himself and orders his favorite food at restruants.
moral_consequence: Pascal is presently surprised how few people actually seem to care.
immoral_action: Pascal continues to hide his favorite food from others out of fear of being perceived as childish.
immoral_consequence: This means that Pascal almost never actually gets to eat his favorite food and has to make it for himself.

norm: It is gross to leave a house dirty.
situation: Anna is about to go on a two week trip out of town.
intention: She wants to clean up a little before she goes.
moral_action: Anna gives the house a thorough cleaning and washes all her dishes and clothes.
moral_consequence: Anna returns from her trip to a clean and spotless house which makes her happy to be home.
immoral_action: Anna does some minimal cleaning but leaves a bunch of dirty dishes and clothes lying around.
immoral_consequence: Anna returns to a house that smells like mildew and is full of bugs.

norm: It's wrong not to do the dishes when asked.
situation: Eric has cooked dinner for himself at home where he lives with his roommates.
intention: Eric wants to relax and take it easy at night after dinner.
moral_action: Eric washes his dishes and puts them away before going to bed.
moral_consequence: Eric's roommates wake up to clean dishes in the morning and are happier.
immoral_action: Eric leaves his dishes unwashed in the sink and goes to sleep.
immoral_consequence: Eric's roommates wake up angry in the morning and have no clean dishes for themselves.

norm: It is ok good to teach yourself things.
situation: Sophia opens an infected email which results in her computer becoming infected with viruses, and her tech savvy brother can't help her at the moment.
intention: Sophia wants her computer to be free of viruses.
moral_action: Sophia learns how to remove viruses from watching tutorials on youtube.
moral_consequence: Sophia is able to help her coworker with virus removal a week later.
immoral_action: Sophia waits for her brother to fix her computer.
immoral_consequence: By the time he arrives, the virus has permanently harmed ten of her files.

norm: You should apologize when you do a bad deed.
situation: Tom was playing baseball outside and accidentally throws the ball and breaks someone's house window.
intention: Tom wants to keep his pride.
moral_action: Tom apologizes to the house owner and tells him it was an accident, but he'll pay for it.
moral_consequence: Tom stays out of jail and the houseowner respects Tom.
immoral_action: Tom walks away as if nothing happened and avoids that house for a while.
immoral_consequence: The cops come to Tom's house later and arrest him for vandalism and the house owner dislikes Tom.

norm: It's polite not to disturb people who are asleep.
situation: Farrell comes home from work stressed after midnight.
intention: Farrell wants to have fun.
moral_action: Farrell plays his favorite MMO with his friends.
moral_consequence: Farrell gains rare items from beating a boss.
immoral_action: Farrell watches a movie at a high volume.
immoral_consequence: Farrell gets a visit from the police after a neighbor reports him for making too much noise.

norm: People would be offended if you reject their customs.
situation: John is visiting a foreign country with a culture that his vastly different than his.
intention: John wants to enjoy his vacation.
moral_action: John attempts to immerse himself in the local culture and learn about their customs.
moral_consequence: John has an enriching vacation where he is able to enjoy himself and learn new things.
immoral_action: John shows no interest in learning local customs and goes about his business as he pleases.
immoral_consequence: The locals are offended by John's behavior, so they give him food poisoning and pick his pockets.

norm: It's not politically correct to use ethnic slurs.
situation: James is standing in line at a fast food restaurant when a black man cuts in front of him.
intention: James wants to confront the black man who cut in front of him.
moral_action: James tells the black man who cut in front of him to go to the back of the line, since that would be fair to everyone.
moral_consequence: The other people in line at the restaurant are pleased when the black man goes to the back of the line.
immoral_action: James tells the black man who cut in front of him to go to the back of the line, then calls him a racist name.
immoral_consequence: The other people in line at the restaurant are upset and offended and regret going to the restaurant.

norm: It's unacceptable to go for a long time without showering.
situation: Beth is excited for this weekend's auditions for the college musical.
intention: Beth wants to go and audition for a leading role.
moral_action: Beth showers and gets properly ready for the audition.
moral_consequence: The director is impressed with her audition, and she gets the leading role in the musical.
immoral_action: Beth doesn't believe in showering regularly and smells so bad that the director cuts her audition short because the smell is so offensive.
immoral_consequence: Despite being talented, Beth doesn't get any parts because no one can be near her because she stinks.

norm: You should not go against your significant others wishes
situation: Dave and his wife are looking at cars at a dealership, and she wants him to buy a red car she sees there.
intention: Dave wants to come back to the dealership later and buy a car.
moral_action: Dave goes back to the dealership and buys the red car his wife liked.
moral_consequence: Dave's wife is happy that they have a new car that she wanted.
immoral_action: Dave returns to the dealership and buys a blue car that he prefers over the red one his wife liked.
immoral_consequence: Dave's wife is disappointed that he didn't buy the red car that she wanted.

norm: It's polite to acknowledge and greet people you know.
situation: Julie is shopping, but starts feeling sick in the store.
intention: Julie wants to hurry so she can go home.
moral_action: Julie waves at the friend, telling her in passing she feels bad, and is able to end her shopping trip early.
moral_consequence: The friend waves back, says she understands, and wishes Julie a speedy recovery.
immoral_action: Julie sees a friend in the store, but doesn't greet her, so she can not spend the time chatting and quickly leave.
immoral_consequence: The friend's feelings are hurt because she saw Julie ignore her, so she tells their mutual friends that Julie is rude and avoids her in the future.

norm: It's good to try to save someone from choking.
situation: John is eating at a nearly empty restaurant when he notices the person at the table near him starts to flail and make gasping noises.
intention: John needs to decide whether to ignore this strange behavior.
moral_action: John gets up and checks on the person, noticing they're choking at he gets closer, and starts doing the Heimlich.
moral_consequence: The other person eventually spits out the food that was lodged in their throat, and breathlessly thanks John.
immoral_action: John looks back down at his meal, figuring the situation will sort itself out.
immoral_consequence: The other person turns blue and slumps in their chair before a waiter notices.

norm: It is kind to adopt animals.
situation: Jenna felt lonely after she moved away after college and had always loved animals.
intention: Jenna wants to get a pet.
moral_action: Jenna goes to a shelter and adopts a four-year-old dog with sad eyes.
moral_consequence: Jenna quickly bonds with the dog and it becomes much more energetic.
immoral_action: Jenna pays a breeder thousands of dollars to get a designer puppy.
immoral_consequence: Jenna enjoys posting pictures of her designer dog on all her social media accounts.

norm: It's wrong to not take someone's misfortune seriously.
situation: John sees a homeless man on the side of the road as John is walking down the sidewalk.
intention: John wants to give the man some advice.
moral_action: John suggests the local man get cleaned up at the nearest shelter and tells him about job opportunities in the area.
moral_consequence: The homeless man follow's John's advice and lands a job as a clerk at a local business.
immoral_action: John tells the homeless man to stop being lazy and get a job.
immoral_consequence: The homeless man feels ashamed and upset about his current circumstances.

norm: You shouldn't tell someone who they can hang out with.
situation: Jake is at home watching TV when his wife Anne tells him she's off to see her friend Adam.
intention: Jake wants to respond to Anne.
moral_action: Jake tells Anne to have a great time and to say hi to Adam for him.
moral_consequence: Anne is delighted that Jake greeted her before she left and that he is thoughtful enough to think of Adam, too.
immoral_action: Jake tells Anne that he does not allow her to hang out with other men and that she cannot see Adam.
immoral_consequence: Anne is infuriated that Jake is trying to tell her who she can be friends with and thinks he's overly controlling.

norm: It is unacceptable to hurt animals.
situation: Jill sees that a raccoon has been eating from her trash bin, making a huge mess.
intention: Jill wants to get rid of the raccoon.
moral_action: Jill buys a humane trap that catches animals without hurting them.
moral_consequence: Jill catches the raccoon and takes it to a wooded area far from her house.
immoral_action: Jill puts some poisoned food in the trash bin for the raccoon to eat.
immoral_consequence: The raccoon suffers a slow and painful death from the poison.

norm: It's not okay to kill a helpless animal.
situation: Lina has just spotted a mouse run across her kitchen and is terrified of mice.
intention: Lina wants to get rid of the mouse.
moral_action: Lina traps the mouse with a container and releases it outside.
moral_consequence: Lina feels relieved that the mouse has been removed humanely.
immoral_action: Lina gets a broomstick and uses it to end the mouse's life.
immoral_consequence: Lina feels guilty after having killed such a small creature.

norm: It's wrong to steal from a person's place of business.
situation: John is at work and sees fancy desserts set up on the table for another department's business meeting.
intention: John wants to satisfy his craving for a sweet treat.
moral_action: John uses the vending machine to purchase a candy bar.
moral_consequence: John satisfies his craving for a sweet and continues working.
immoral_action: John sneaks some cheesecake and pie from the business meeting room.
immoral_consequence: John is caught red handed and is given disapproving looks by his superiors.

norm: It is rude to expect money from family.
situation: James has been living in a rented apartment for a long time and is tired of it but doesn't have a lot of money, even though his parents have some.
intention: James wants to buy a house.
moral_action: James realizes he should be autonomous and saves enough money by spending less.
moral_consequence: James' parents are proud of their son.
immoral_action: James thinks his parents should help him financially and tells them so.
immoral_consequence: James' parents are shocked at how callous and entitled he is.

norm: It's bad to condone bad behavior.
situation: Dave meets up with his friend Bill who offers him a chocolate bar and tells him he just stole it from the store.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Bill's offer of stolen chocolate.
moral_action: Dave tells Bill that since it's stolen he doesn't want it and Bill should really take it back to the store.
moral_consequence: Bill is annoyed at first but then realizes what he did was wrong and goes back to return the chocolate.
immoral_action: Dave accepts and takes the chocolate from Bill and thanks him before eating it.
immoral_consequence: Bill believes that he can gain status from thieving and continues to do so until he goes to prison.

norm: It's good to ask permission before doing things.
situation: Mark has started a new job in an office.
intention: Mark wants to eat lunch.
moral_action: Mark asks a coworker if he can have their chips in exchange for bringing them a snack tomorrow.
moral_consequence: Mark's coworker knows where their chips went and takes up the offer.
immoral_action: Mark eats a coworker's chips in the break room while they're working.
immoral_consequence: The coworker has no snack and doesn't know where it went.

norm: It's rude to insult people out of anger.
situation: James was talking to his friend on the playground when Bill accidentally hit him with a basketball.
intention: James wants Bill to be more careful with the ball.
moral_action: "James tosses the ball back to Bill and says, ""Hey, be more careful""."
moral_consequence: "Bill says, ""I'm sorry I hit you - I'll be more careful""."
immoral_action: James calls Bill a clumsy four-eyes and tells him he's a loser.
immoral_consequence: Bill chases the ball down and throws it at James deliberately.

norm: You shouldn't cheat on anyone.
situation: Carla is on a girls weekend out of town and meets George at a bar who buys her drinks and dances with her.
intention: Carla wants to have a carefree weekend.
moral_action: Carla thanks George for the drink and dances with him, but tells him she has a boyfriend.
moral_consequence: Carla calls her boyfriend to check in and tells him about George, he is proud of her honesty and suggest they talk about taking their relationship to the next level.
immoral_action: Carla decides since it is a girls weekend she can do what she wants and takes George back to her hotel room that night.
immoral_consequence: Carla's friends find out what she did and tell her boyfriend who breaks up with her.

norm: Using fake pictures on a dating site is misleading.
situation: Marco is setting up a listing on a dating site and is deciding what pictures to use.
intention: Marco wants to get someone to reply to his listing.
moral_action: Marco puts up current pictures that show what he looks like today.
moral_consequence: The person that replies to his ad likes him for what he looks like now, and they hit it off.
immoral_action: Marco puts up pictures of a male model that looks nothing like him.
immoral_consequence: When someone does reply to his ad, they find out he looks nothing like his pictures and stop seeing him.

norm: It is caring to help people who are in distress.
situation: Lyle is walking down the street when he sees Karen on the ground bleeding from a probable stab wound.
intention: Lyle wants to express his concern to Karen.
moral_action: Lyle tells Karen that her wound looks awful and that he's calling 911 right away.
moral_consequence: Karen is delighted that someone is calling for help and hopeful that she can get through the ordeal.
immoral_action: Lyle tells Karen that it's terrible that she's bleeding and that she should probably find a hospital or something.
immoral_consequence: Karen is annoyed that Lyle is just stating the obvious and not helping her in any way.

norm: It's rude to leave a chat room without saying goodbye.
situation: Ben has stayed up too late being online chatting and notices the time.
intention: Ben wants to quickly get to bed.
moral_action: Ben quickly tells the chat he lost track of time and has to leave in a hurry.
moral_consequence: Ben's friends tell him goodnight, and they leave on better terms.
immoral_action: Ben closes out of the chat without saying anything and hurries off to bed.
immoral_consequence: Ben's friends think poorly of him for leaving without saying anything.

norm: You shouldn't mess with other people's foods
situation: Alex had a huge fight with a customer at her sandwich shop.
intention: Alex wants to get back at him.
moral_action: Alex refuses to serve the customer for his rudeness.
moral_consequence: The customer leaves the shop irritated, but doesn't go further than that.
immoral_action: Alex decides to hide some hot sauce in the client's food.
immoral_consequence: The customer gets very ill, being allergic to hot sauce, and throws up.

norm: It is rude to touch someone uninvited.
situation: Clint is at the bar when he notices a girl he finds attractive.
intention: Clint wants to let the girl know he's interested in her.
moral_action: Clint talks to the girl and compliments her.
moral_consequence: The girl will be charmed by Clint.
immoral_action: Clint puts his arm around the girl's shoulders.
immoral_consequence: The girl will think Clint is a creep.

norm: You shouldn't try to harm yourself.
situation: Jessica's parents just died in a plane crash and Jessica feels totally numb.
intention: Jessica wants to stop feeling numb.
moral_action: Jessica calls a therapy hotline and talks about her pain with a caring therapist.
moral_consequence: Jessica heals herself slowly and starts to feel things again and be happy.
immoral_action: Jessica takes a razor and cuts herself all over, and she bleeds.
immoral_consequence: Jessica becomes very sick and is rushed to the hospital where she almost dies.

norm: It's wrong to let your pet rule your life.
situation: Heather's friends have been trying to invite her on a lake trip all summer, but she always says no because her pet chickens require lots of work.
intention: Heather wants to make sure her chickens are cared for.
moral_action: Heather hires a sitter to care for her chickens while she's away on the lake trip.
moral_consequence: Heather is able to live a well-balanced life while caring for her chickens.
immoral_action: Heather once again tells her friends that she can't make the trip because of her chickens.
immoral_consequence: Heather's friends give up on inviting her out ever again.

norm: It is unacceptable to destroy people's relationships.
situation: Jack is the only child of his parents who are arguing a lot.
intention: Jack wants his parents to stop fighting around him.
moral_action: Jack tells his parents that they need to keep their disagreements between them, he's just a kid.
moral_consequence: Jack's parents go to counseling and work on their disagreements.
immoral_action: Jack tells his mom that his dad is abusing him, so they'll get a divorce.
immoral_consequence: Jack's dad is investigated over the lies and his mom moves him and herself to another city.

norm: You should always try to work hard.
situation: Kent was just hired to mow grass for a large institution and isn't sure how to handle all of the work.
intention: Kent wants to earn a paycheck.
