moral_action: Kent works overtime to cut all of the grass everywhere.
moral_consequence: Kent gets paid extra for his overtime work.
immoral_action: Kent mows the more well-traveled areas and neglects the more out-of-the-way ones.
immoral_consequence: Kent's supervisor sees the unmowed areas and gives Kent a pay cut.

norm: You shouldn't brag about what you own.
situation: King Rick, who has a lavish treasure room, is receiving a group of royal ambassadors from another country.
intention: King Rick wants to impress the ambassadors.
moral_action: King Rick shows the ambassadors around a bit and talks about the honorable subjects under his rule.
moral_consequence: The ambassadors are impressed by the visit and the happiness of the people, giving a good report to their master.
immoral_action: King Rick gives the ambassadors a tour of his treasure room, detailing what everything is an how much it is worth.
immoral_consequence: The ambassadors let their country know that King Rick is rich, leading the country to send an army and plunder his kingdom.

norm: It's nice to read someone's thoughts when they write them.
situation: Ms. Henderson received a card from her student Miyona, where Miyona wrote how much Ms. Henderson has meant to her as a teacher.
intention: Ms. Henderson wants to respond to the card.
moral_action: Ms. Henderson reads the card and thanks Miyona for her encouraging words.
moral_consequence: Miyona feels happy to know that her words had an effect, and she is glad she gave Ms. Henderson the card.
immoral_action: Ms. Henderson puts the card in her desk without reading it.
immoral_consequence: Miyona feels hurt when she sees that Ms. Henderson was not interested in reading what she had to say.

norm: You shouldn't make fun of other races.
situation: Nick and Nancy are a married couple at an old west exhibit where they see a display of Apache Indians in traditional garb.
intention: Nick wants to comment on the display.
moral_action: Nick tells Nancy that the display is so beautiful and vivid, and he feels as he was with the Apache when he looks at it.
moral_consequence: Nancy is delighted that Nick seems to be enjoying the display and that he's so into it.
immoral_action: Nick tells Nancy that Indians are a ridiculous people for wearing feathers and painting their faces.
immoral_consequence: Nancy is disgusted that Nick is so narrow minded and judgmental of people instead of learning from them.

norm: It is rude to be critical of someone's appearance
situation: Rudy hadn't seen his friend in forever, and he now has long hair.
intention: Rudy wants to comment on his friend's hair.
moral_action: Rudy tells his friend that he pulls off having long hair well.
moral_consequence: Rudy's friend's confidence is greater, and he feels that he made the right choice.
immoral_action: Rudy tells his friend that he looks like a girl, and he should cut it all off.
immoral_consequence: Rudy's friend feels disrespected and doesn't want to hang out with Rudy as much.

norm: It's a bad idea to share too much on Facebook
situation: Courtney has been getting into arguments with her boyfriend, Justin, every night.
intention: Courtney wants to tell others about her problems with Justin.
moral_action: Courtney decides that she will talk to her parents about the problems she is having with Justin.
moral_consequence: Courtney's parents make her feel better, and she is glad she talked to them.
immoral_action: Courtney posts detailed information about her arguments with Justin on Facebook.
immoral_consequence: Justin sees Courtney's post and gets upset with her for posting about their personal business on social media.

norm: You should wave at someone who is waving at you.
situation: Tom is walking down the street when he sees a guy he knows waving at him from across the street.
intention: Tom wants to react to the guy waving at him.
moral_action: Tom waves back at the guy waving at him in a friendly way before going on his way.
moral_consequence: The guy is happy to have seen Tom and thinks Tom is friendly.
immoral_action: Tom just looks at the guy for a few seconds then looks away and keeps walking down the street.
immoral_consequence: The guy who was waving at Tom is hurt and confused by Tom's reaction and figures Tom might have forgotten who the guy is.

norm: It's wrong to copy things.
situation: Lewis is comes from a family of talented artists, and he is entering the school art competition.
intention: Lewis wants to win the competition.
moral_action: Lewis puts a lot of effort into his painting asks his older sister for advice on how to make his painting look better.
moral_consequence: Lewis improves his art skill and enters his best work into the competition.
immoral_action: Lewis finds one of his older sister's old paintings that he thinks is really good and copies it for his submission.
immoral_consequence: Lewis's family discover that he copied his sister's painting and alert the school to have him disqualified.

norm: You should not help corporations violate people's rights.
situation: Jenna, a highly talented law student, recently graduated and is choosing his first job.
intention: Jenna wants a prestigious job.
moral_action: Jenna goes to work for the local public defender's office and plans to run for office in a decade or so.
moral_consequence: Jenna keeps many indigent people out of jail and builds a solid basis for a political career.
immoral_action: Jenna goes to work for Monsanto and argues, against the balance of scientific evidence, that their pesticides are safe.
immoral_consequence: The pesticides remain in use, sickening many people, and Jenna is promoted.

norm: You shouldn't post online just to get attention.
situation: John was offered a large signing bonus with his new job.
intention: John wants to share his good fortune.
moral_action: John posts to his friend and family group that he got his dream job.
moral_consequence: John's friends and family congratulate him on his new job.
immoral_action: John posts a public message on his Facebook page with a picture of his offer letter.
immoral_consequence: His new company rescinds their offer because John violated their privacy rules.

norm: It's rude to take a soda from someone else.
situation: Jacob was at a diner with all of his friends, but he ran out of his drink.
intention: Jacob wants something to drink.
moral_action: Jacob calls the waitress over to order himself another drink.
moral_consequence: The waitress brings a fresh, cold soda over to Jacob's table.
immoral_action: Jacob takes a sip of soda that his best friend had ordered for himself.
immoral_consequence: Jacob's friend gets made and makes him pay for his food.

norm: It is hurtful to call someone overweight.
situation: Josh's coworker Steve is a fat guy who loves to eat more than his fair share of the office's donuts every day.
intention: Josh wants to tell Steve to stop eating so many donuts.
moral_action: Josh suggests to Steve that it would be fairer to his colleagues is Steve only had a couple donuts every day.
moral_consequence: Steve realizes he was being selfish and vows to be more considerate with his allotment of donuts in the future.
immoral_action: Josh tells Steve he needs to stop eating so many donuts because he's morbidly obese.
immoral_consequence: Steve is deeply embarrassed and develops an eating disorder, fasting for days at a time.

norm: You shouldn't kill wildlife.
situation: Jake was taking a walk in the woods when he saw a snake on the trail.
intention: Jake doesn't want the snake to bite him.
moral_action: Jake takes another path and walks in a direction away from the snake.
moral_consequence: Jake enjoys his walk in the park knowing that he was not near the snake.
immoral_action: Jake finds a sharp stick and uses it to kill the snake on the trail.
immoral_consequence: Jake is given a fine to pay for killing the snake in the park.

norm: It is rude to perform bodily functions in public.
situation: Tim is on a busy bus after eating a big meal and feels gas building in his stomach.
intention: Tim wants to release his gas.
moral_action: Tim gets off the bus and finds a private place to release his gas.
moral_consequence: Tim will be relieved that he released his gas without anyone else around.
immoral_action: Tim releases his gas while on the bus.
immoral_consequence: Tim will be embarrassed that he released his gas around other people.

norm: You shouldn't walk away from people.
situation: Tammy is walking to work.
intention: Tammy wants to get to work on time today.
moral_action: Tammy sees a woman needs help calls 911 then takes a taxi to work and is on time.
moral_consequence: The woman gets the help she needed.
immoral_action: Tammy sees a woman needing help but keeps walking and is on time for work.
immoral_consequence: The woman passes out on the street.

norm: You shouldn't date someone that steals from your parents.
situation: Geoffrey lives with his girlfriend, Cora, who recently stole his mom's necklace while she was visiting.
intention: Geoffrey wants to forgive Cora.
moral_action: Geoffrey tells Cora that he forgives her for what she did, but he can't keep seeing her.
moral_consequence: Geoffrey and Cora break up, and he finds a new girlfriend who is more honest.
immoral_action: Geoffrey decides to put the necklace incident behind and continue on in his life with Cora.
immoral_consequence: Cora steals money from his mom's purse the next time she comes over.

norm: It's wrong to lie to someone about having a partner.
situation: Hank, a married man, is in a bar when a woman begins to hit on him.
intention: Hank wants to talk to the woman.
moral_action: Hank tells the woman that he's married, but that they can talk if she wants.
moral_consequence: The woman chats a bit with Hank in a friendly way.
immoral_action: Hank says that he's not married and talks with the woman.
immoral_consequence: Hank commits adultery with the woman.

norm: It's wrong to harm a relative's pet.
situation: Harold is walking to the front door of his sister's house when her dog runs toward him barking.
intention: Harold wants to avoid getting bitten.
moral_action: Harold stops walking when he sees the dog and yells for his sister.
moral_consequence: Harold's sister comes out to get the dog, and they all go into the house to visit.
immoral_action: Harold kicks the dog and makes a run for the door.
immoral_consequence: Harold's sister is upset and doesn't speak to him for months.

norm: It is bad to keep money from others.
situation: Gloria being rich is the grandma of Alice who needs financial support to pay her college fees.
intention: Gloria wants to react to Alice's financial needs.
moral_action: Gloria has set up a college fund for Alice and regularly deposits money to make the fund grow.
moral_consequence: Alice feels hopeful about her college dream and thanks Gloria for her kindness and generosity.
immoral_action: Gloria opens an oversea bank account to save up her money and no one knows about it, and she doesn't intend to help Alice.
immoral_consequence: Alice feels stressed and helpless about her huge college fees.

norm: You should notbe forcd to attend religious services.
situation: Bobby's mother, Susan, wakes up early on Sunday morning.
intention: Susan wants to get her family ready to go to church.
moral_action: Susan wakes Bobby up by talking with him about their plans for the day and asks him if he would like to go see his friends at the church.
moral_consequence: Susan has a relaxed and open talk with her son, and Bobby feels as though he has some say in how he spends his day.
immoral_action: Susan yells at Bobby to get up and get ready, that he must go to church because that is what people do.
immoral_consequence: Susan feels upset after yelling at her son and Bobby feels resentful toward the Religious community.

norm: It's rude to be judgmental of the choices of others.
situation: Stacy's friend has gotten a body piercing and asks Stacy what she thinks of it.
intention: Stacy wants to give her friend an opinion on their body piercing.
moral_action: Stacy tells her friend that she doesn't mind their body piercing and only judges them on their character.
moral_consequence: Stacy's friend is happy that Stacy is open minded about the choices they make.
immoral_action: Stacy tells her friend that getting a body piercing was a mistake and that is reflects badly on them.
immoral_consequence: Stacy's friend is unhappy that Stacy would judge them for getting a body piercing.

norm: It's wrong not to own up to your mistakes.
situation: Don is a business owner who has had COVID run through his business because he refuses to let his employees distance or wear masks.
intention: Don wants his employees to continue work.
moral_action: Done says that he made a mistake and has his employees wear masks when possible and stay home if they feel sick.
moral_consequence: Don's business muddles through the pandemic and recession and recovers afterward.
immoral_action: Don doubles down and tells his employees they will be let go if they stay home from work sick.
immoral_consequence: Some of Don's employees die, many quit, and Don's business goes under.

norm: It's nice to let your parents live with you.
situation: Barry's parents had to file for bankruptcy, and they lost their house.
intention: Barry wants to find a place for his parents to live.
moral_action: Barry invites his parents to move into the spare bedroom in his house.
moral_consequence: Barry's parents are grateful and help out Barry in every way that they can.
immoral_action: Barry sends his parents to live in a homeless shelter.
immoral_consequence: Barry's parents are broken and cry every night knowing they lost everything.

norm: People shouldn't brag about manipulating people for money.
situation: Joe is working an sales job for an insurance company.
intention: Joe wants to impress a date when discussing his work.
moral_action: Joe explains how it is hard work and that he wants to give people the best plans.
moral_consequence: Joe's date is impressed with his character and the date goes well.
immoral_action: Joe brags about tricking customers into paying more for life insurance than necessary.
immoral_consequence: His date out of concern calls the company to report him, and he is fired from his job.

norm: Never enter the press area until the machine is fully locked out and tagged out.
situation: A coworker is caught in a conveyor and is unconscious; the emergency stop has failed.
intention: The trained colleague must decide whether to intervene immediately or wait for full lockout.
moral_action: The trained colleague decides to ignore the protocol temporarily, steps in, and frees the trapped worker.
moral_consequence: The trapped coworker is freed in time and survives.
immoral_action: The trained colleague adheres to the safety protocol and waits for the full lockout procedure.
immoral_consequence: The delay likely costs the trapped worker their life.

norm: It's fun to see movies with people.
situation: Angie and Jordan are each in their separate homes on a Friday night, looking for something to do.
intention: Angie wants to watch a movie.
moral_action: Angie invites Jordan to go to the movie theater with her and watch a new release.
moral_consequence: Angie thinks the movie is really bad but has a great time laughing about all the stupid scenes with Jordan on the way home.
immoral_action: Angie goes to the movie theater by herself and watches a new release.
immoral_consequence: Angie thinks the movie is really bad and wants to complain about it to someone, but she's by herself.

norm: You shouldn't tell off people.
situation: Dave is driving down the street when he is dangerously and abruptly cut off by Jane in another car.
intention: Dave wants to yell at Jane for scaring him.
moral_action: Dave yells at Jane that she needs to watch where she's driving and that she could have killed him.
moral_consequence: Jane apologizes to Dave and realizes she made a mistake and vows to do better next time.
immoral_action: Dave yells at Jane that she's insane and proceeds to call her a bunch of names and tell her he's going to beat her up.
immoral_consequence: Jane is terrified that Dave is aggressive and is scared that he might actually hit her physically.

norm: It is expected that people show appreciation to veterans
situation: Jake is meeting his friend's father, Mike,  who is a veteran but struggling mentally and physically.
intention: Jake wants to know about the veteran's story.
moral_action: Jake talks with Mike about his story and thanks him for serving the country.
moral_consequence: Jake receives a piece of souvenir from Mike that he brought from the country he was deployed to.
immoral_action: Jake talks with Mike and tells him he got what he deserved for murdering people.
immoral_consequence: Jake is immediately asked to leave Mike's place.

norm: It is disrespectful to make advances on someone else's spouse.
situation: Tyler is having some drinks out at a bar with his friend Tom and his spouse.
intention: Tyler wants to flirt with a pretty girl.
moral_action: Tyler, feeling loose after a few drinks, decides to flirt with the bartender.
moral_consequence: The bartender playfully flirts back with Tom who enjoys the attention.
immoral_action: Tyler, feeling less inhibitions because of the alcohol, makes some suggestive comments to his friend's spouse.
immoral_consequence: Tom and his spouse feel disrespected by the comments he made.

norm: It's annoying when people talk while the movie's playing.
situation: Kevin and Alex are at a movie when Alex taps Kevin's shoulder, wanting to tell him something.
intention: Kevin wants to respond to Alex.
moral_action: Kevin makes a motion as if he's zipping his lips, then points at the movie screen.
moral_consequence: Alex holds his peace until the movie is over.
immoral_action: Kevin asks Alex, who then starts loudly cracking jokes about one of the main characters.
immoral_consequence: The audience around Kevin and Alex tell them to be quiet or else.

norm: It's mean to push children.
situation: Connor is on the playground and sees a lineup of children waiting to use the slide.
intention: Connor wants to use the slide.
moral_action: Connor waits his turn in line and then goes down the slide.
moral_consequence: Connor and the other children talk to each other about how much fun they had going down the slide as the wait in line to go again.
immoral_action: Connor pushes the other children out of the way and goes down the slide.
immoral_consequence: Connor is removed from the playground by a teacher and doesn't get to ride the slide anymore.

norm: It's wrong to fire someone just because they got injured.
situation: John owns a small construction business, and one of his workers just fell off a roof.
intention: John wants to make sure his business's worker's comp rates don't go up.
moral_action: John offers to give the worker eight weeks of informal paid leave without the need to file a worker's comp claim.
moral_consequence: John's worker has time to recover from his injury and John doesn't have to pay more for worker's comp insurance.
immoral_action: John claims that the worker was drinking on the job and therefore can be fired for cause.
immoral_consequence: The worker files suit for wrongful termination and his coworkers testify on his behalf, and the resulting settlement bankrupts John.

norm: Good to sympathize with other peoples who make mistakes.
situation: Dan is a soccer player who saw his teammate kick and miss a goal.
intention: Dan wants to respond to the missed goal.
moral_action: Dan tells his teammate that it is okay and tries to cheer him up.
moral_consequence: Dan's teammate picks himself up and tries to do better.
immoral_action: Dan points and blames his teammate for missing the goal.
immoral_consequence: Dan's teammate becomes demotivated and puts out a lackluster performance.

norm: It's good to make someone feel better about themselves.
situation: Dina goes to watch her friend Gigi perform in the opening night of the school play where Gigi forgets one of her lines.
intention: Dina wants to talk to Gigi about missing the line.
moral_action: Dina tells Gigi that she missed a line and that was bad.
moral_consequence: Gigi will feel self conscious about her next performance.
immoral_action: Dina tells Gigi her acting was very believable, and she'll remember the line in her next performance.
immoral_consequence: Gigi will feel confident going into the next performance of the play.

norm: It's wrong to cheat on your wife with your secretary.
situation: Bill, a married man, is the CEO of a large multinational firm and has a very attractive secretary.
intention: Bill wants to consider starting an intimate relationship with his secretary.
moral_action: Bill resists starting an affair with his secretary and remains faithful to his wife.
moral_consequence: Bill enjoys a long lasting relationship with his wife and becomes a very successful CEO.
immoral_action: Bill decides to have sex with his very attractive secretary.
immoral_consequence: Bill's wife demands a divorce after finding out about the affair and Bill loses his position as CEO.

norm: Joining the Navy is patriotic.
situation: Stan is young, is a bit wild, and loves his country and all that it stands for.
intention: Stan wants to show his love for his country.
moral_action: Stan joins the Navy, so he can contribute to the security of his beloved country.
moral_consequence: Stan's actions in the navy help make the country safer and stronger.
immoral_action: Stan puts up a giant flag pole in his front yard and hangs a very large national flag from it to inspire national pride.
immoral_consequence: When the country is in a crisis, the flag pole does absolutely nothing to help it.

norm: Sometimes people need help doing something
situation: Ted is working on a team project at work.
intention: He wants to be noticed for doing a good job.
moral_action: Ted sees Melissa struggling with her tasks and guides her through how to complete them.
moral_consequence: Ted's managers see this as showing leadership ability and give him a promotion to management.
immoral_action: Ted sees Melissa struggling with her tasks and takes them over himself.
immoral_consequence: Ted's managers thank him for doing extra work but do not select him for a promotion as he lacks leadership skills.

norm: It's good to be diligent about cleaning.
situation: Rob returns home from a long day at work and sits down on the couch.
intention: Rob wants to invite his friend over for dinner.
moral_action: Rob invites his friend over and diligently cleans in the half hour before he arrives.
moral_consequence: Rob's friend is impressed by how clean his house is and suggests they hang out together more often, making Rob feel happy.
immoral_action: Rob invites his friend over for dinner and sits on the couch until he arrives.
immoral_consequence: Rob's friend is repulsed by his messy house and never comes over again, making Rob feel sad.

norm: It's important to do well in school
situation: Stan is in a math class that he doesn't like and has a new chapter to learn.
intention: Stan wants to get through the chapter.
moral_action: Stan forces himself to understand the material well and does the home.
moral_consequence: Stan has an easier time when the same subject appears later in the course.
immoral_action: Stan does the homework as fast as he's able.
immoral_consequence: Stan doesn't learn the material deeply, which makes future lessons more difficult.

norm: It's wrong to dirty up other people's things.
situation: Steven's car is at the mechanic's getting fixed, so his friend Rocco has lent him one of his cars to drive around for the week.
intention: Steven wants to go fishing.
moral_action: After a day of fishing, Steven changes into clean clothes and puts his fish in a secure cooler before getting into Rocco's car to drive home.
moral_consequence: Rocco's car is returned in perfect condition.
immoral_action: Steven spends a day fishing before returning to Rocco's car in muddy boots and spilling a bucket of fish all over the back seat.
immoral_consequence: Rocco is left to clean up the mess when Steven returns the car and loses his trust in him forever.

norm: It's unkind to abandon a pet.
situation: Corey has a pet but moved into an apartment building that does not allow pets.
intention: Corey wants to stay in the apartment building.
moral_action: Corey posts on a local classifieds website about his pet and puts it up for adoption.
moral_consequence: The pet eventually has a new home and lives a happy pet life.
immoral_action: Corey drives his pet to the woods on the edge of town and then leaves the pet there.
immoral_consequence: The pet is frightened and does not last long in the wild.

norm: It is wrong to disrupt the productivity of others.
situation: Max is at work in an office building in a cubicle surrounded by coworkers who are currently working on an important project.
intention: Max wants to entertain himself.
moral_action: Max finds an interesting podcast and listens to it at his desk using headphones.
moral_consequence: Max's coworkers don't even notice that Max is wearing headphones, and they continue working on their projects.
immoral_action: Max tries to start conversations with his coworkers about things that do not pertain to their work.
immoral_consequence: Max's coworkers are distracted by his attempts to talk to them, and they struggle to stay focused on their projects.

norm: It's good to get a strike when you go bowling.
situation: John is bowling competitively at the local bowling alley.
intention: John would like to win the competition.
moral_action: John rolls three strikes in a row for a turkey in the 10th frame of the game.
moral_consequence: The strikes are enough for his score to be the best among the competitors, and he wins the game.
immoral_action: John is in the tenth frame of the game and rolls two gutterballs in a row.
immoral_consequence: John misses out on getting a third roll in the frame and his score is too low to win.

norm: It is wrong to discount someone's grief.
situation: Jenny's friend is crying because their cat that they had for many years dies.
intention: Jenny wants to react to friend crying.
moral_action: Jenny says she knows how hard it can be to lose something you really care about and tells her friend that she's there for them.
moral_consequence: Jenny's friend feels that Jenny's support is very comforting to them in this difficult time.
immoral_action: Jenny says that her friend should just get over it because it was just a cat so it's not a big deal.
immoral_consequence: Jenny's friend thinks Jenny is heartless for not accepting how upset they are over their cat's death.

norm: It's rude to publicly offend someone on the radio.
situation: Larry listens to the Don and Mike radio show at work every afternoon.
intention: Larry wants to call and be on the radio show.
moral_action: Larry calls on a break and tells them he is a big fan.
moral_consequence: Larry gets to be on his all time favorite show and hear himself later.
immoral_action: Larry calls from work and badmouths his boss on national radio.
immoral_consequence: Others at work hear the show and Larry is fired for misconduct when it gets back to the boss.

norm: Bragging about winning a ribbon is cocky.
situation: Danial has just won first place in a race while he friends were in the bottom three.
intention: Danial wants to celebrate his victory.
moral_action: Danial invites everyone to a post victory party at a bar where he buys everyone drinks.
moral_consequence: Danial's friends have a fun evening spending time with each other.
immoral_action: Danial continues to talk about his win and his great skills all the way home.
immoral_consequence: Danial's friends feel like losers.

norm: It's kind to help out homeless people.
situation: Tiffany often sees articles about the presence of homeless people in her city when reading the newspaper.
intention: Tiffany wants to see how bad the situation is for herself.
moral_action: Tiffany prepares hot food and gift bags full of toiletries and warm clothing to give out to the homeless people in her city.
moral_consequence: The homeless people go to bed full and warm.
immoral_action: Tiffany drives downtown and sees many hungry, cold, homeless people before driving away.
immoral_consequence: The homeless situation in Tiffany's city remains as it is.

norm: It's wrong to do drugs.
situation: Jenny has a free weekend with her friend Bill, a shady drug dealer.
intention: Jenny wants to decide how to spend the weekend.
moral_action: Jenny decides to spend the weekend writing short stories about morals.
moral_consequence: Jenny is relaxed after spending some quality free time on creative pursuits.
immoral_action: Jenny decides to hang out at Bill's place and smoke his pot all weekend.
immoral_consequence: Jenny spends way too much on junk food and puts on some weight.

norm: You should not hide things from your spouse.
situation: Colin spends time playing Dungeons and Dragons with his friends but does not tell his wife, who asks him where he was.
intention: Colin wants to respond to his wife.
moral_action: Colin tells his wife he's playing a game with his friends.
moral_consequence: Colin's wife will be understanding and not be suspicious of him.
immoral_action: Colin tells his wife that what he does is none of her business.
immoral_consequence: Colin's wife will think he is cheating on her or doing illegal things.

norm: It's wrong to hide things from your significant other.
situation: Margo wants to meet-up with Barb, an old friend from college whom her husband dislikes.
intention: Margot wants to have a quiet lunch with Barb and catch up.
moral_action: Margot tells her husband she is having lunch with Barb, and he can just deal with it.
moral_consequence: Margot enjoys her lunch with Barb and reminiscing about college days.
immoral_action: Margot tells her husband she is having lunch with a different person.
immoral_consequence: Margot feels guilty throughout her lunch date about telling a lie to her husband.

norm: It's good to be optimistic about love.
situation: Lynn and Lester are newlyweds who are sitting in their backyard having a romantic moment when Lynn says they'll be together forever.
intention: Lester wants to respond to Lynn's statement.
moral_action: Lester tells Lynn that he too is convinced they'll be together forever and that he loves her very much.
moral_consequence: Lynn is delighted to hear that Lester feels the same as her and it validates her opinion that he's her soulmate.
immoral_action: Lester tells Lynn that over half of marriages end up in divorce and that it's more likely they won't be together forever.
immoral_consequence: Lynn is upset that Lester is annoyingly factual and unromantic and that he has no confidence in their love.

norm: It is good to help a friend if they needed
situation: Bryan is thinking about dinner when Randy calls and needs a ride to the store.
intention: Bryan wants to go out to eat.
moral_action: Bryan says he'll drop Randy off at the store on his way to dinner.
moral_consequence: Randy is happy and likes Bryan even more now.
immoral_action: Bryan tells Randy he is very busy and rushes out to the restaurant to eat.
immoral_consequence: Randy is depressed and won't help Bryan when he needs help.

norm: It's wrong to not allow your family on trips.
situation: Robert is planning a trip over the weekend and little sister asks if she can come too.
intention: Robert wants to go on his trip.
moral_action: Robert brings his sister along on his weekend trip, taking her to all the destinations.
moral_consequence: Robert's sister has a fun time on the weekend trip.
immoral_action: Robert forbids his sister from joining him on his weekend trip and goes alone.
immoral_consequence: Robert's sister feels sad that she can't take part in Robert's fun trip.

norm: You shouldn't exclude your parents from your wedding.
situation: Dawn is getting married and her parents aren't happy with her fiance.
intention: DAwn wants a peaceful wedding.
moral_action: Dawn invites her parents to her wedding, but tells them to behave.
moral_consequence: The parents accept Dawn's fiance as part of the family.
immoral_action: Dawn prohibits her parents from attentiding the wedding.
immoral_consequence: The parents are hurt and no longer talk to Dawn.

norm: It's fun to play sometimes even if you're an adult.
situation: Linda's toddler daughter is crying and wants Linda to play pretend with her.
intention: Linda wants her daughter to stop crying.
moral_action: Linda starts talking to her daughter in a fake accent and plays pretend with her.
moral_consequence: Linda's daughter laughs at her mom's fake accent and the mother and daughter enjoy their time together.
immoral_action: Linda tells her daughter she's too old to play with her and gives her daughter an iPad instead.
immoral_consequence: Linda's daughter is distracted by the iPad, and she never asks Linda to play with her again.

norm: It's bad to fall behind on bills.
situation: Ashley's rent and electric are due, but she wants to go to Disney with her friend Karen.
intention: Ashley wants to prioritize whats most important.
moral_action: Ashley decides her electric and rent must come first and postpones Disney with Karen until next payday.
moral_consequence: Ashley has peace of mind knowing she has running power and a roof over hear head and still gets to enjoy her trip with Karen.
immoral_action: Ashley decides going to Disney with Karen would be a blast and put her electric on hold.
immoral_consequence: Ashley gets her power shut off and has to pay an additional deposit to have it restored.

norm: It's good to want to work.
situation: Shaun is currently in a job, but he's thinking about quitting and just collecting unemployment money.
intention: Shaun has to decide whether to work or just receive unemployment money.
moral_action: Shaun decides to stay in his job and work towards getting a promotion.
moral_consequence: Shaun receives a lot more money than he'd be getting on unemployment.
immoral_action: Shaun gets fired on purpose so that he can apply for unemployment.
immoral_consequence: Shaun gets unemployment money even though he doesn't really need it.

norm: It's wrong to be materialistic in life.
situation: Tory makes a lot of money and is listening to Jane talk about how her kids are her pride.
intention: Tory wants to respond to Jane.
moral_action: Tory says that it's great that Jane values her family and that's inspirational.
moral_consequence: Jane will feel that having a family is worthwhile.
immoral_action: Tory says that kids are okay but buying new things is the height of life.
immoral_consequence: Jane will think that Tory is a snob.

norm: It’s bad to let your curiosity lead to danger.
situation: Ted is a boy that finds electric outlets interesting.
intention: Ted wants to find out how electrical outlets work.
moral_action: Ted looks up how electrical outlets work on the internet.
moral_consequence: Ted learns about electrical outlets by reading articles online.
immoral_action: Ted plays with the electrical outlet in his room.
immoral_consequence: Ted gets shocked by the electrical outlet.

norm: Refusing to help animals in need is seen as bad.
situation: Ben was driving down the road when he sees a wounded dog on the side of the road.
intention: Ben wants to get home.
moral_action: Ben stops and picks up the dog and takes it back to his house.
moral_consequence: Ben is able to nurse the dog back to health at his home.
immoral_action: Ben drives past the dog and goes straight to his house without worrying about the dog.
immoral_consequence: The dog ends up dying because of the wounds that it was suffering from.

norm: Kicking someone out of anger is immature.
situation: Donovan has just lost a game of monopoly against his little brother.
intention: Donovan wants to react to losing.
moral_action: Donovan tells his brother they should play again.
moral_consequence: Donovan's brother will get to play monopoly again.
immoral_action: Donovan goes over to his brother and kicks him.
immoral_consequence: Donovan's brother will cry because he was kicked.

norm: It is good to help animals.
situation: James notices a skinny looking stray cat outside of his house one night.
intention: James wants to make sure the cat is okay.
moral_action: James adopts the cat into his home.
moral_consequence: The cat lives a better life in James' home.
immoral_action: James calls animal control about the cat.
immoral_consequence: The cat is taken by animal control and euthanized.

norm: You shouldn't tell someone how to parent.
situation: Tony is walking down the street when he sees Al spanking his son for misbehaving.
intention: Tony wants to express his displeasure at the spanking.
moral_action: Tony sighs loudly so that Al can hear him and shakes his head as he walks past.
moral_consequence: Al sees that Tony is miffed about something but can't be sure why and goes back to talking to his son.
immoral_action: Tony tells Al that he doesn't know how to be a good dad and that spanking is wrong.
immoral_consequence: Al is annoyed as Tony doesn't even know the context and is inserting himself into his private situation.

norm: You shouldn't give customers the runaround regarding refunds.
situation: Lynette is a call center representative for a cell phone provider.
intention: Lynette wants to meet her job metrics.
moral_action: Lynette works with a customer who initally wants a refund and fixes their device instead, leaving the customer satisfied.
moral_consequence: The customer writes the company about how helpful Lynette was and Lynette is given an award.
immoral_action: Lynette tells her customer to call back and ask for tech support in order to get a 1000 dollar refund for their defective Iphone.
immoral_consequence: When the rep calls tech support and does not get the refund, the customer disconnects all of their lines and Lynette is wriiten up for misconduct.

norm: Drinking and driving is against the law.
situation: Jim is at a bar with his friends and is very drunk, to the point where it would be illegal for him to drive.
intention: Jim wants to get home from the bar.
moral_action: Jim decides to give his keys to a friend and the friend drives him home.
moral_consequence: Jim's friends are glad that Jim is safe, and they help him get to sleep.
immoral_action: Jim decides to drive home despite being drunk.
immoral_consequence: Jim's friends are horrified that Jim is driving while drunk and try to stop him.

norm: It's rude to frame someone.
situation: John's coworker Bob did something nasty to him.
intention: John wants Bob to be punished.
moral_action: John complains about Bob to his supervisor and asks for help to resolve it.
moral_consequence: Bob is punished by the supervisor.
immoral_action: John takes $10,000 from the company’s cash box and puts it in Bob’s locker to make it seem like he did it.
immoral_consequence: Bob is prosecuted, but John feels very guilty.

norm: It's nice to give people discounts.
situation: Laura was working at the register at a shop and saw a customer was having trouble.
intention: Laura wanted the customer to return to the store again even though they were having trouble.
moral_action: Laura gave the customer a discount on the item that she wanted to get.
moral_consequence: The boss praised Laura for the good job that she had done with the customer.
immoral_action: Laura gave the customer the item that they wanted for free.
immoral_consequence: Laura ended up losing her job because she basically stole the item.

norm: It's wrong to ignore your coworkers.
situation: Mike is working with his friend James in a factory.
intention: Mike wants to listen to his music on his phone.
moral_action: Mike sees his friend wants to talk and chats with him before he puts on his headphones.
moral_consequence: Mikes friend feels happy and accepted.
immoral_action: Mike sees his friend James wants to talk about something but puts on his headphones.
immoral_consequence: Mikes friend feels ignored and irritated.

norm: It is rude to refuse to help around the house.
situation: Bill is playing video games when his wife Samantha comes and asks him to please do the dishes.
intention: Bill wants to respond to Samantha.
moral_action: Bill tells Samantha that he will do it just as soon as he can find a save point in his game, so he doesn't lose progress.
moral_consequence: Samantha is happy that she will get help around the house and feels relieved that she has a partner who cares to help her.
immoral_action: Bill tells Samantha that clearly he's busy as he's playing video games and that he doesn't have the time right now.
immoral_consequence: Samantha is annoyed that Bill is being lazy and is generally infuriated that she has to do all the work.

norm: It's good to blast someone who abuses someone's animal.
situation: Ollie sometimes witnesses his neighbor, Ken, abusing his wife's cat.
intention: Ollie wants to avoid confrontation with Ken.
moral_action: Ollie puts out an anonymous post on social media about what Ken has been doing to his cat.
moral_consequence: People on social media alert the authorities and Ken is arrested.
immoral_action: Ollie watches the abuse go on without ever saying anything.
immoral_consequence: Ken continues to abuse the cat until it perishes.

norm: It is good to do work for others.
situation: Willow has the evening off, and her mother needs help with the yard work.
intention: Willow wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Willow asks her friend to help her out with her mother's yard.
moral_consequence: Willow and her friend bond over goofing off outdoors.
immoral_action: Willow spends the evening shopping for new clothes.
immoral_consequence: Willow has to take her mother to the hospital that night after her mother injures herself in the yard.

norm: It is generous to pay for everyone's items.
situation: Bob brought all of his friends to the bar after a hard day's work.
intention: Bob wants his friends to have fun.
moral_action: Bob brings everyone into the bar and buys everyone from work a drink from the bar.
moral_consequence: Everyone from work is very pleased with Bob's generosity.
immoral_action: Bob orders drinks for everyone but then expects them to pay for those drinks.
immoral_consequence: Some people got confused and thought Bob was buying them all a drink.

norm: You shouldn't punish good workers.
situation: Jack is the boss of a small company with all good workers.
intention: Jack wants to manage his employees.
moral_action: Jack provides incentives for workers to do well and manages them using reasonable strategies.
moral_consequence: Jack's employees perform better than ever as they enjoy working under Jack.
immoral_action: Jack decides to punish a good worker for not performing as well as another good worker.
immoral_consequence: The punished employee leaves the company as the work culture becomes toxic.

norm: It's inconsiderate to act out in your teacher's classroom.
situation: Tim has moved to a new school and is sitting in math class with the other students and their teacher.
intention: Tim wants to show his classmates that he is funny.
moral_action: Tim waits till lunch time then entertains his classmates with jokes and silly dances.
moral_consequence: Tim's classmates think he's funny and Tim gets quite popular.
immoral_action: Tim starts goofing around in class even getting up and doing a silly dance.
immoral_consequence: Tim's teacher sends him to the principal's office, and he gets detention.

norm: You should not abuse children.
situation: While playing catch outside, Max’s young son excitedly chucks the ball hard, breaking a window in the neighbor's house.
intention: Max wants to get his son to understand that impulsive behavior is not acceptable.
moral_action: Max talks with his son, and they plan a punishment to repay the damage done.
moral_consequence: Max learns how to talk and work with his son.
immoral_action: Max knocks his son upside the head and scolds him.
immoral_consequence: His son begins to hate Max.

norm: You shouldn't discriminate against overweight people.
situation: Mark who is overweight but has relevant experience and Joseph who is average weight but has no experience are both applying to be counselors at the camp Robert runs.
intention: Robert wants to hire the best candidate for the job.
moral_action: Robert decides to hire Mark because Mark is more qualified for the job.
moral_consequence: Robert's camp goes well that summer because Mark knows how to do the job well.
immoral_action: Robert decides to hire Joseph because he thinks Mark is too heavy to do the job.
immoral_consequence: Robert's camp does not go well that summer because his counselor Joseph does not know what he is doing.

norm: People might get annoyed if you practice singing too loud.
situation: John is listening to some tunes on the radio while eating dinner with his family.
intention: John wants to be a better singer on karaoke night.
moral_action: John hums along with a song he likes on the radio.
moral_consequence: John memorizes the melody of the song, so he can sing it better.
immoral_action: John starts singing along to a song on the radio as loudly as he can.
immoral_consequence: John is admonished for his rude behavior by his family.

norm: You shouldn't use the n-word because it offends black people.
situation: Ron is in a big fight on twitter with a black person.
intention: Ron wants to escalate the argument.
moral_action: Ron decides to tell the person that he has no respect for him.
moral_consequence: The person is offended and insults him right back, and they continue.
immoral_action: Ron decides to call the person he's arguing with the N-word.
immoral_consequence: Other folks see the argument on twitter and report Ron to his manager and get him fired.

norm: It's not okay to eat something that isn't yours.
situation: Jerry is at work and about to go on lunch break.
intention: Jerry wants to find something to fill him up at work.
moral_action: Jerry goes to the vending machine and buys a sandwich.
moral_consequence: Everyone at work has their own meal and is full.
immoral_action: Jerry notices a coworkers lunch and eats it without asking.
immoral_consequence: The coworker gets upset at Jerry and does t have food of their own.

norm: It is mean to make your grandmother feel badly.
situation: Jared finds out his grandmother broke his super expensive vase.
intention: Jared to wants to talk to his grandmother about the vase.
moral_action: Jared expresses disappointment to his grandmother but doesn't make her feel bad.
moral_consequence: Jared's grandmother apologizes and the two have a nice chat.
immoral_action: Jared hurls expletives and shaming language at her grandmother.
immoral_consequence: The grandmother sobs on a couch for hours and Jared feels bad.

norm: It's good to share knowledge.
situation: Colby is at work when he sees that Mike is struggling with some machinery.
intention: Colby wants the machine to work correctly.
moral_action: Colby shows Mike how to work with the machine correctly.
moral_consequence: Mike is able to use the equipment correctly and between the two they get the job done quickly.
immoral_action: Colby tells Mike to get lost, and he does the work on the machine himself.
immoral_consequence: Mike quits the job and Colby has to do the rest of the work himself.

norm: You shouldn't snoop around things that don't belong to you.
situation: Mary is a house cleaner.
intention: Mary needs to clean the bedroom of her employer.
moral_action: Mary discreetly but thoroughly cleans around the things in her employer's closet.
moral_consequence: Mary's employer is very happy with the job she's done and gives her a raise.
immoral_action: Mary looks through boxes in the closet when cleaning her employer's room and doesn't put things back.
immoral_consequence: Mary's employer thinks a burglar has been through their home and doesn't trust anyone coming in again.

norm: It's bad to track people's movements without their consent.
situation: Carrie is afraid that her boyfriend will cheat on her.
intention: Carrie wants peace of mind.
moral_action: Carrie decides that it's better to not just assume her boyfriend will cheat.
moral_consequence: Carrie calms down and is able to enjoy the relationship.
immoral_action: Carrie installs an app on her boyfriend's phone to track where he is 24/7.
immoral_consequence: Carrie follows her boyfriend on the maps excessively and has no time for anything else.

norm: It's bad to continue to hold a grudge.
situation: Bob is mistreated by his boss, and he is very angry at them for this.
intention: Bob wants decide whether to keep holding his boss's actions against them.
moral_action: Bob decides to forgive his boss for mistreating him in the past.
moral_consequence: Bob is a much happier once he's let go of his anger towards his boss.
immoral_action: Bob decides he will never forgive his boss for the way they treated him.
immoral_consequence: Bob never lets go of anger towards his boss and so is never happy at his workplace.

norm: You shouldn't make a mess.
situation: Jim's wife is out, and he's hungry and wants to have an elaborate dinner.
intention: Jim wants to cook dinner.
moral_action: Jim is careful to put everything away and clean as he is preparing dinner so that the kitchen stays clean.
moral_consequence: Jim's wife is pleasantly surprised that Jim managed to make dinner without causing a huge mess in the kitchen.
immoral_action: As Jim makes dinner he leaves all sorts of stuff out and doesn't bother to clean anything so that the kitchen is soon very dirty.
immoral_consequence: When Jim's wife gets home she's very disappointed to find the kitchen in a messy state.

norm: It is good to make your health a priority.
situation: John promised to see a movie with David, but caught a cold before the movie date.
intention: John wants to see the movie with David.
moral_action: John asks David to postpone their meeting until he is fully recovered.
moral_consequence: John recovers soon before their postponed meeting date, and they enjoy the movie happily.
immoral_action: John meets David at the cinema as promised despite his sickness.
immoral_consequence: John's illness worsened the following date after the movie.

norm: You should share your good fortune with others.
situation: Phil just won the lottery and all of his poor family members are asking for some monetary help from him.
intention: Phil wants to save his lottery winnings.
moral_action: Phil puts his winnings in good investments and donates his interest to his family.
moral_consequence: Phil's family is very grateful to Phil and loves him and Phil lives a rich life with his family.
immoral_action: Phil pretends he doesn't hear his family's requests and doesn't give a dime to them.
immoral_consequence: Phil's family resents Phil and avoids him and Phil dies a lonely rich man.

norm: It's mean to swear at people in public.
situation: John is walking down the street when a man bumps into him.
intention: John wants to let the man know he doesn't like being bumped by them.
moral_action: John firmly but politely tells the man that it's not okay to bump into people in the street.
moral_consequence: The man apologizes for bumping into john and learns to be more careful.
immoral_action: John uses strong language against the man calling him bad words for bumping into him.
immoral_consequence: The man who bumped into John is angered and doesn't feel sorry for bumping into John.

norm: It is rude to expect to monopolize a friend's time.
situation: It's Friday afternoon and it's time to plan the weekend.
intention: Joe wants to do something with his friend Bo.
moral_action: Joe asks Bo to hang out for an hour on Saturday.
moral_consequence: Joe and Bo have fun together.
immoral_action: Joe asks Bo to spend the entire weekend helping him clean his apartment.
immoral_consequence: Bo is annoyed that Joe isn't respectful of his time but helps anyway.

norm: You should make your partner feel special on their birthday.
situation: It's Jennifer's birthday and Brad and Jennifer wake up in bed together in the morning.
intention: Brad wants to say something to Jennifer.
moral_action: Brad tells Jennifer happy birthday before smothering her with kisses and telling her that her presents await her.
moral_consequence: Jennifer is beaming as she  loves the attention Brad is giving her and feels loved and safe with him.
immoral_action: Brad tells Jennifer that she better get to it and start making breakfast because he's starving.
immoral_consequence: Jennifer is annoyed that Brad doesn't remember it's her birthday and that he's being so demanding of her.

norm: It's not okay to overspend on something you don't need.
situation: Sam is looking around an electronics store when he stumbles upon a big, one day only, sale on televisions.
intention: Sam wants to buy a new television.
moral_action: Sam takes the opportunity to buy a nice, but reasonably priced, television with the special discount.
moral_consequence: Sam still maintains some of his savings and has an easier time paying his monthly bills.
immoral_action: Sam decides on an expensive, huge television that he can barely afford because he can only get a discount on it today.
immoral_consequence: Sam spent so much on the television that he struggles with his bills and has no savings left in the bank for unforeseen expenses.

norm: It is nice to say hello back to others.
situation: Paul is walking through a park when he's about to pass by another man, Ken who says hello to him.
intention: Paul wants to greet Ken.
moral_action: Paul looks Ken in the eye and tells him hello and says that it's a nice day.
moral_consequence: Ken smiles and agrees with Paul that it's a nice day and wishes him a good walk.
immoral_action: Paul sort of looks down at the ground as he gives Ken a quick wave without saying anything.
immoral_consequence: Ken thinks Paul is a little weird to be so shy and is miffed he wasn't enthusiastic in his greeting.

norm: It's wrong to be jealous of your friends.
situation: Gary went to see his friend Luke at his mansion.
intention: Gary wants to see Luke.
moral_action: Gary says hello to his buddy Luke and is excited about seeing him.
moral_consequence: They hang out and watch movies together in Luke's movie room.
immoral_action: Gary is envious of his friend's wealth and how much cool stuff he has.
immoral_consequence: Gary ruins his visit by thinking about his envy the whole time.

norm: You shouldn't lick someone without their permission.
situation: Pamela is in the mood, and she sits down on the bed beside her boyfriend.
intention: Pamela wants to have sex.
moral_action: Pamela makes a suggestive comment as she reaches out for his hand.
moral_consequence: Pamela and her boyfriend have an erotic experience.
immoral_action: Pamela kisses and drags her tongue alongside her boyfriend's neck.
immoral_consequence: Pamela is pushed away by her stressed out boyfriend.

norm: You shouldn't spread your germs in publicly used things.
situation: Jordan is at home sick this weekend.
intention: Jordan wants to go get some medicine.
moral_action: Jordan makes sure to wear a mask and gloves before he heads out to the pharmacy and only sneezes into his sleeve.
moral_consequence: Thanks to Jordans precautions the next customer to enter does not get sick.
immoral_action: Jordan heads to his local pharmacy without a mask or gloves on.
immoral_consequence: He opens the pharmacy door after sneezing into his hand, subsequently, the next customer opens the door bare handed and gets sick because of it.

norm: It's wrong to blow off someone's special event.
situation: Bobby realizes that his best friend Blake's bachelor party falls on the same date as a date with a woman he likes.
intention: Bobby wants to have a fun night.
moral_action: Bobby chooses to reschedule his date and attends Blake's bachelor party, having a fun night with the boys.
moral_consequence: Bobby and Blake continue to be friends for years.
immoral_action: Bobby ignores his friend's bachelor party and decides to go on the date with his woman friend to have a fun night with her.
immoral_consequence: Blake is offended by Bobby's absence and their friendship deteriorates over time.

norm: It's nice to help your partner's parents.
situation: George has a wife named Allison and her parents are moving to a new house.
intention: George wants to comment on the move.
moral_action: George says he can help Allison's parents pack up some of their belongings.
moral_consequence: Allison will think George is helpful and cares about her family.
immoral_action: George says that Allison's parents have too many pieces of furniture.
immoral_consequence: Allison will think George is unhelpful and makes unnecessary comments.

norm: It's bad form to use handicap stalls if you're non-handicapped.
situation: Bob enters a public bathroom right before a man on crutches, and notices that the only open stall is the handicapped stall.
intention: Bob wants to go to the bathroom.
moral_action: Bob waits until a stall opens up, and he uses that one.
moral_consequence: The handicap person can use the stall, and Bob is able to finish his business.
immoral_action: Bob decides he can't wait, and uses the handicap stall.
immoral_consequence: The handicap person has to wait even longer, and everyone glares at Bob and calls him names.

norm: It's polite to choose your words carefully around others.
situation: Nina just got a hideous new haircut and asks Ryan what he thinks about it.
intention: Ryan needs to decide how to respond.
moral_action: Ryan tells Nina that it looks nice, but suggests some small changes that she might be interested in trying to make it look even better.
moral_consequence: Nina thinks Ryan's advice over and decides to try it out, and is happy with the results.
immoral_action: Ryan asks Nina if she's looked in a mirror lately, ssaying the haircut is not very good.
immoral_consequence: Nina is upset and feels greatly self-conscious about the new haircut.

norm: You shouldn't talk during a test.
situation: Mya was in her desk in math class taking a test one day.
intention: Mya wants to make a good grade on the test.
moral_action: Mya thinks hard on every question before putting an answer on the paper.
moral_consequence: Mya finds out the next day that she made an A on the math test.
immoral_action: Mya whispers to her friend to get the right answer for one of the problems.
immoral_consequence: The teacher hears Mya and picks up her test before she was finished.

norm: It is bad to want harm on anyone even yourself.
situation: Adam is a high school student who has been feeling very depressed and lonely lately.
intention: Adam wants to feel better.
moral_action: Adam tells his parents how he has been feeling and asks to get medical help.
moral_consequence: Adam is able to see a therapist and work through his problems to become more mentally healthy.
immoral_action: Adam takes up cutting to relieve his stress after he hears it's used as a release by others in his position.
immoral_consequence: Adam gets hooked on self-harm and ends up with many scars all over his body that he feels ashamed of.

norm: It's nice to give birthday presents.
situation: It's Danny's sister's birthday today, and she calls Danny up and asks him to come see her at her place.
intention: Danny wants to go visit his sister.
moral_action: Danny goes shopping for a nice little present for his sister's birthday then goes over to her place with it.
moral_consequence: Danny's sister is happy that he remembered to get her a present for her birthday.
immoral_action: Danny goes over to his sister's house empty-handed even though he knows it's her birthday.
immoral_consequence: Danny's sister is a little disappointed that he didn't think to get her anything for her birthday.

norm: You shouldn't get back at your friends.
situation: Pascal beat Steve at Monopoly yesterday evening during board game night.
intention: Steve wants to get Pascal back.
moral_action: Steve vows to get Pascal back at the next board game they play.
moral_consequence: Next time they play Clue and Steve finds out it was Colonel Mustard with the knife in the lounge.
immoral_action: Steve clues Pascal's locker at school shut, so he can't open it.
immoral_consequence: Pascal can't hand in any of his homework because it's all in his locker.

norm: You shouldn't take someone's things.
situation: Gretchen is at her friend Kara's house discussing Kara's upcoming job interview when she notices a new blazer in her closet.
intention: Gretchen wants to try on Kara's new blazer.
moral_action: Gretchen asks Kara if she can try her blazer on.
moral_consequence: Kara tells Gretchen she can try the blazer on as soon as her interview is over.
immoral_action: While Kara is in the bathroom, Gretchen puts the blazer into her bag, so she can try it on at home.
immoral_consequence: On the day of her interview, Kara has no blazer to wear and is unable to dress professionally.

norm: It's wrong to send someone to kill your spouse.
situation: Jack and Abby have not been getting along well recently.
intention: Jack wants out of the marriage.
moral_action: Jack files for divorce.
moral_consequence: Abby gets to live and no one goes to jail.
immoral_action: Jack hires someone to kill Abby.
immoral_consequence: Abby dies and Jack might get caught and arrested.

norm: Getting your pet from a breeder is frowned upon.
situation: Conrad has been lonely, and his friends tell him that maybe getting a pet would help him feel less lonely.
intention: Conrad wants to get a dog.
moral_action: Conrad visits the animal shelter to find a dog to adopt.
moral_consequence: Conrad rescues a dog that might have otherwise been put down.
immoral_action: Conrad finds a breeder and inquires about buying a dog from them.
immoral_consequence: Conrad spends money on a dog that has been bred solely for profit.

norm: It's unfounded to hate groups of people for no reason.
situation: Cal is at a convince store, seeing the new owner, Steve, at the register is Iranian.
intention: Cal wants to express his insecurity that there will be no people of Cal's race at convenience stores anymore.
moral_action: Cal asks for a job to make sure people like Cal still have jobs at convenience stores.
moral_consequence: Steve is honored that a person like Cal would want to work for him, and they develop a lasting friendship.
immoral_action: Cal tells Steve to go back to his own country and stop taking away jobs from Americans.
immoral_consequence: Steve feels hurt and unwelcome in the country and distrusts people like Cal from then on.

norm: It's annoying when people are too thrifty.
situation: Willy has a lot of coupons which can be applied to the same item with the right strategy.
intention: Willy wants to save money.
moral_action: Willy decides to only use one coupon since there is a line forming.
moral_consequence: The people in the queue are happier to have a shorter wait time.
immoral_action: Willy holds up the line at the store by getting the clerk to apply every coupon he has.
immoral_consequence: The people in line are annoyed with Willy.

norm: It's wrong to think more about yourself than your child.
situation: Alice took her children with her shopping.
intention: Alice wanted to have a long shop.
moral_action: Alice takes the kids out of the car and has them involved in the shopping.
moral_consequence: The kids are happy to be involved in the shopping.
immoral_action: Alice left her children in the hot car.
immoral_consequence: Alice ends up getting arrested for child endangerment.

norm: It is unorganized to leave toys all over.
situation: Mia is very tired and spending the evening at home with her children who left their toys all over the living room floor.
intention: Mia wants to spend the evening on the couch, reading a book.
moral_action: Mia asks her children to pick up their toys and put them in the toy chest.
moral_consequence: Mia's husband has a safe and comfortable evening.
immoral_action: Mia decides to leave the toys all over the floor of the living room.
immoral_consequence: Mia's husband walks into the living room later and walks on a bunch of Legos, which hurts a lot.

norm: You should always return someone's call.
situation: Chris gets a call from a distraught friend while busy working on a project.
intention: Chris wants to finish working on the project in time.
moral_action: Chris apologizes and says he will call him back as soon as possible and calls back after finishing up.
moral_consequence: Chris' friend thanks him and appreciates his friendship more.
immoral_action: Chris quickly gets off the phone and says that he has to work on something.
immoral_consequence: Chris' friend feels sad and alone.

norm: It's discouraged to text women you've broken up with.
situation: John is home alone on a Saturday night and feels bored.
intention: John wants some company so he can have fun.
moral_action: John texts one of his friends to go to a bar.
moral_consequence: John's ex-girlfriend is undisturbed and enjoys her Saturday evening.
immoral_action: John texts his ex-girlfriend who he broke up with for another woman to go out again on a date.
immoral_consequence: John's ex-girlfriend is angry because John mistreated her before and feels he is using her.

norm: It's disgusting to spy on people.
situation: Kyle has a big crush on a girl in his neighborhood, but she doesn't know yet.
intention: Kyle wants to get closer to the girl.
moral_action: Kyle starts up a conversation with the girl the next time he sees her.
moral_consequence: The girl likes Kyle immediately and feels closer to him.
immoral_action: Kyle spies on the girl and tracks her every movement to learn more about her.
immoral_consequence: The girl senses that Kyle is stalking her and feels creeped out.

norm: It's good to recover from severe eating disorders.
situation: Becky suffers from binge eating disorder.
intention: Becky wants to go on a diet.
moral_action: Becky seeks counseling for her binge eating.
moral_consequence: Using the tools she's learned in counseling, Becky slowly undoes her binge eating habits.
immoral_action: Becky starts a diet but quits halfway through.
immoral_consequence: Becky begins to binge even more than she did before she began the diet.

norm: You shouldn't be cheap.
situation: Mark has decided that he would like to invite the new girl in town, Ashley, out for a date.
intention: Mark wants to take Ashley to his favorite restaurant for dinner.
moral_action: After dinner Mark pays the bill and asks Ashley how she likes his favorite restaurant.
moral_consequence: Ashley thanks Mark for the nice dinner and says she loves the restaurant.
immoral_action: After dinner when the bill comes Mark adds each meal up with a calculator and tells Ashley how much her share is.
immoral_consequence: Ashley is surprised and tells Mark that she thought he would pay since he invited her.

norm: It is nice to treat your friends.
situation: Dave Mike and Bill are at a restaurant when the waitress brings the bill which is 60 dollars total.
intention: Dave wants to decide how much to pay.
moral_action: Dave throws in 75 dollars and tells the other two not to worry about it as it's his treat.
moral_consequence: Mike and Bill are delighted that Dave is such a good friend and are happy for the gift of free food.
immoral_action: Dave throws in 20 dollars and another 3 dollars for the tip in the middle of the table.
immoral_consequence: Mike and Bill also pay the same amount each and nothing particularly interesting occurs.

norm: It's wrong to post someone's conversation online without their permission.
situation: Tom has a long and important business conversation with his friend during lunch.
intention: Tom wants to let her friend know what he thought about their conversation.
moral_action: Tom posts in a private message to his friend what he thought about the lunch conversation.
moral_consequence: Tom's friend thanks Tom for respecting his privacy, and they exchange further details.
immoral_action: Tom posts publicly on Facebook to his friend what he thought about their conversation.
immoral_consequence: Tom's friend gets mad at Tom for revealing private info in public and Tom feels sorry.

norm: Partners should be willing to do favors for each other.
situation: Maryanne is at home talking to her husband on the phone who needs their spare set of keys because he has locked his keys out of the car.
intention: Maryanne wants her husband to get home.
moral_action: Maryanne tells her husband that she has the other set of keys and will be there shortly to open up the car doors.
moral_consequence: Maryanne's husband thanks her profusely to show his appreciation.
immoral_action: Maryanne suggests to her husband that he call a towing agency rather than her bring him the spare set of keys.
immoral_consequence: Maryanne's husband cannot fathom why Maryanne thinks that is a good idea and resents her for not bringing him the spare keys.

norm: You shouldn't drive your car recklessly.
situation: A marketing firm is holding a meeting with a client that will make them a lot of money.
intention: John has to get to the meeting on time.
moral_action: John takes a scenic route to the meeting place.
moral_consequence: John is relaxed and centered when he arrives for the meeting.
immoral_action: John plows through a newly turned red light in his haste to get there.
immoral_consequence: John is pulled over for running a red light so misses the meeting entirely.

norm: It's wrong to shoot someone.
situation: Dan notices a burglar broke through his window and is stealing his food.
intention: Dan wants to get the burglar out of his house.
moral_action: Dan calls 911 and lets the police come and apprehend the burglar without lethal means.
moral_consequence: Dan is able to enjoy his day without worrying excessively about anything.
immoral_action: Dan takes out his gun and shoots the burglar 5 times until the burglar is dead.
immoral_consequence: Dan worries about his legal safety and what to do with a rotting corpse.

norm: People feel it's rude to leave a family gathering early.
situation: Garrett is attending a family reunion, where numerous family members have yet to arrive.
intention: Garrett wants to go home.
moral_action: Garrett decides to hold on and wait for the remaining members to show up before heading home.
moral_consequence: The family members who arrived late are sad Garrett must leave, but are very happy to have gotten to see him.
immoral_action: Garrett tells those in attendance that he must leave the gathering and goes home.
immoral_consequence: Later arriving family are upset to learn that they have just missed Garrett.

norm: You shouldn't steal things from your friends.
situation: It's the first of the month and Steffie needs to pay her part of the rent, but she's low on cash.
intention: Steffie wants to get some some quickly.
moral_action: Steffie takes her TV to the pawn shop and gets a loan on it.
moral_consequence: Steffie is able to pay her rent on time.
immoral_action: Steffie goes in her friend Brad's wallet and takes $200 without telling him.
immoral_consequence: Steffie loses Brad as a friend when he finds out she has stolen money from him.

norm: It's bad to arrive too early.
situation: Ricky has been invited to Tonya's birthday party for Friday night and it's now Friday morning.
intention: Ricky wants to decide what time to head over to Tonya's house.
moral_action: Ricky decides to leave shortly after seven, so he can arrive at seven thirty for the party.
moral_consequence: Tonya is happy to see Ricky when he arrives and welcomes him inside excitedly.
immoral_action: Ricky decides that he'll leave right after breakfast at around nine thirty AM and get there by ten.
immoral_consequence: Tonya is unpleasantly surprised to see Ricky arrive in the AM for an evening party and feels uncomfortable having him there all day.

norm: It is rude to intentionally hurt people emotionally
situation: Jim is a judge in a singing competition and the last singer performed poorly.
intention: Jim wants to motivate the singer to do better.
moral_action: Jim offers constructive criticism to the singer.
moral_consequence: The singer feels motivated to work harder to become a better singer.
immoral_action: Jim tells the singer that they wasted his time with their performance.
immoral_consequence: The singer becomes severely depressed and becomes addicted to drugs.

norm: It's good to be available when others need you.
situation: James works at a school and the school asks him to pick up a large order of groceries from a distant city.
intention: James wants to give them an answer.
moral_action: James agrees and clears out his schedule, so he can pick up the food.
moral_consequence: The school gets the food that they ordered, and they don't need to sacrifice someone else to do it.
immoral_action: James says that he is busy and declines to get the food for the school.
immoral_consequence: The school needs to find someone else to get the order and that person can't do what they need to.

norm: It's wrong to leave toddlers near pools.
situation: Jennifer is watching her 2 year old niece by the pool.
intention: Jennifer is thirsty and wants something to drink.
moral_action: Jennifer brings her niece inside, and they both get a glass of water.
moral_consequence: Jennifer and her niece continue playing by the pool.
immoral_action: Jennifer leaves her niece to get a glass of water.
immoral_consequence: Jennifer's niece falls into the pool and drowns.

norm: It's good to take your family on trips.
situation: Destiny is a mother and her children are on vacation from school.
intention: Destiny wants to keep her children busy during their vacation.
moral_action: Destiny brings her children on a family trip similar to one she had when she was young.
moral_consequence: Destiny's children have fun and go on to cherish their memories of the trip.
immoral_action: Destiny buys her children new tablets for them to distract themselves with all vacation.
immoral_consequence: Destiny's children spend too much time sedentary than is healthy and create no lasting memories.

norm: You shouldn't go shirtless if it makes other people uncomfortable.
situation: John is at a summertime cocktail party outdoors.
intention: John is really hot and wants to cool off.
moral_action: John goes to the bar and orders a frozen margarita to sip on.
moral_consequence: John finds the delicious drink very refreshing and cooling, and he spends the rest of his time mingling with the other guests.
immoral_action: John takes of his shirt.
immoral_consequence: John has a hard time socializing since the other guests are uncomfortable and avoid being around him.

norm: You shouldn't expect a significant other to change for you.
situation: Anna is bothered by her partner's smoking, and he was a smoker since before they started dating.
intention: Anna wants to convince her partner to stop smoking.
moral_action: Anna expresses her concern about the health consequences but lets her partner decide what to do.
moral_consequence: Anna's partner is receptive to the health risks and is encouraged to quit.
immoral_action: Anna starts to bring the subject of quitting regularly to her partner.
immoral_consequence: Anna's partner is disturbed by her nagging and it makes him smoke even more.

norm: It's not okay to do things that hurt a friendship.
situation: Jenny is in love with her best friend Sue's ex-boyfriend.
intention: She wants to be in a relationship with him.
moral_action: Jenny asks Sue to talk and tells her she would like to date Sue's ex.
moral_consequence: Sue gives her blessing and thinks they will be happy together.
immoral_action: Jenny sneaks behind Sue's back and starts secretly dating her ex.
immoral_consequence: When Sue finds out she is hurt and pushes Jenny out of her life.

norm: It's kind to offer help to those in need
situation: Alex was walking down the sidewalk when Paul, a homeless person, asked him for money.
intention: Alex wants to continue walking.
moral_action: Alex stops briefly and gives Paul a couple dollars, then goes on his way.
moral_consequence: Paul has enough money to buy some food and stave off hunger for a while.
immoral_action: Alex pretends he doesn't hear Paul and continues walking to his destination.
immoral_consequence: Paul does not have enough money for food and goes hungry.

norm: It's not okay to pry into other peoples lives.
situation: Joel is talking to his friend Jim when Jim accidentally mentions something about their spouse which may be embarrassing.
intention: Joel wants to respond to the potentially embarrassing information.
moral_action: Joel acknowledges what Jim said and moves the conversation to a different topic.
moral_consequence: Jim will feel relieved that Joel wants to talk about something else.
immoral_action: Joel asks numerous questions about their Jim's spouse looking to get information.
immoral_consequence: Jim may become annoyed with how curious Joel is about his spouse's situation.

norm: It is bad to murder innocent animals
situation: Brayden is a child that is not being supervised in his backyard as he plays with his BB gun.
intention: Brayden wants to shoot targets with his BB gun.
moral_action: Brayden sets up empty soda cans and takes aim at them picking them of one by one.
moral_consequence: Brayden has a fun and safe time with his BB gun despite being unsupervised.
immoral_action: Brayden takes aim at the birds in his backyard picking them off one by one.
immoral_consequence: Brayden develops feelings of enjoyment from killing for sport, which doesn't bode well for his future.

norm: It is rude to spoil the ending of a show.
situation: Jill is rewatching her favorite show with Jim, who hasn't seen it yet.
intention: Jill wants Jim to know how the episode ends.
moral_action: Jill waits and watches the show quietly with Jim till the end.
moral_consequence: Jim is amazed by the surprise ending of the episode becomes a huge fan of the show.
immoral_action: Jill reveals halfway through the show that the main character dies at the end of the episode.
immoral_consequence: The episode is ruined for Jim, who soon loses interest in the show.

norm: It's wrong to sleep with someone else's husband.
situation: Camille is feeling lonely when her handsome married coworker Steven compliments her and touches her thigh.
intention: Camille wants companionship.
moral_action: Camille quickly excuses herself, and has a girls night with her friends after work.
moral_consequence: Camille meets an attractive guy while she's hanging out with her friends.
immoral_action: Camille returns Steven's affections hooking up with him in a nearby hotel.
immoral_consequence: Camille is attacked by Steven's wife after she discovers the affair.

norm: It's bad to let your vehicle run out of gas.
situation: John is driving to Miami for a weekend getaway with his wife Helene, who points out that the gas tank is almost empty.
intention: John wants to respond to Helene.
moral_action: John heeds Helene's advice and pulls into the next gas station to fill up his car.
moral_consequence: John is able to make it to Miami worry free and Helene is satisfied he listened to her.
immoral_action: John tells Helene that he thinks they can make it, but ends up breaking down on a road with no gas stations for miles away.
