immoral_consequence: John has to walk and Helene is angry he didn't listen to her warning.

norm: You shouldn't lock people out of the house.
situation: Lori has a friend sleeping over at her house and is having a good time with her while a winter storm rages outside.
intention: Lori wants to play a joke on her friend.
moral_action: Lori goes outside, sneaks in some snow, and throws some snow balls at her unsuspecting friend.
moral_consequence: Lori's friend recovers, laughs, and grabs the snow, starting an in-house snowball fight.
immoral_action: Lori lures her friend outside, shuts the door, locks it, and laughs at her through the window.
immoral_consequence: Lori's friend starts to freeze and quickly gets frostbite, requiring medical attention to heal.

norm: It's bad to neglect your wife.
situation: Aaron goes out with his buddies every evening while his wife, Claire, stays home alone.
intention: Aaron wants to maintain his friendship with his buddies.
moral_action: Aaron invites Claire to party with his friends.
moral_consequence: Claire hits it off with Aaron's friends, and they begin hanging out as a group.
immoral_action: Aaron and his friends go out to a party without inviting Claire.
immoral_consequence: Sick of being alone all the time, Claire leaves Aaron.

norm: It is mean to throw things at people
situation: Ethan and his friends are riding on the bus going home from school.
intention: Ethan wants to get a friend's attention who is sitting far away from him.
moral_action: Ethan sends his friend a text message telling them to turn around, so they can talk.
moral_consequence: Ethan has a good time talking with his friend and makes plans to spend time when they get home.
immoral_action: Ethan throws a pencil at his friend and it ends up sticking in his friend's arm.
immoral_consequence: Ethan is suspended from school for a week for injuring another student.

norm: Studying in your spare time is very responsible.
situation: Fredric arrives home tired after work, and he has a math test the next day.
intention: Fredric wants to spend the evening doing something fun.
moral_action: Fredric studies for his test by creating a fun math game based on the material from his notes.
moral_consequence: Fredric learns new study skills that help him throughout his academic life.
immoral_action: Fredric watches a marathon of his favorite television show with some pizza.
immoral_consequence: Fredric fails his test.

norm: You shouldn't be late around your kids.
situation: Sandra's child and teacher are waiting for her to get to a school meeting.
intention: Sandra wants to get to the meeting.
moral_action: Sandra is careful to arrive at the meeting on time and fully prepared.
moral_consequence: Sandra's child is relieved that she's on time and Sandra's punctuality serves as a lesson to them.
immoral_action: Sandra loses track of time doing unrelated things and arrives to the school meeting very late.
immoral_consequence: Sandra's child is embarrassed by her lateness and her poor time management becomes a bad influence on them.

norm: It's rude to act conceited
situation: Tyler acts like he is better than everyone else at his school.
intention: Tyler wants to show off.
moral_action: Tyler decides to pratice his skills, so he's better able to show them off.
moral_consequence: The other kids are more impressed with skills than wealth displays.
immoral_action: Tyler shows how good he is at bike riding by showing off his expensive bike.
immoral_consequence: The other kids point out that Tyler can barely pedal it, but hey it's expensive!

norm: You shouldn't eat an entire pan of brownies by yourself.
situation: Anthony ran into the kitchen, with a big smile, to get some brownies, but his mother told him that they have to cool before being eaten.
intention: Anthony wants to eat brownies.
moral_action: Anthony waits patiently for his mother to cut the pan of brownies into portions, and he takes a couple for himself to eat.
moral_consequence: Anthony enjoys his brownies and even has some left over for later in  the day.
immoral_action: Anthony sneaks into the kitchen, when no one is looking, and eats the whole pan of brownies, all by himself.
immoral_consequence: Anthony feels guilty for eating brownies when he wasn't supposed to, and he gets physically ill from eating the whole pan at once.

norm: It's rude to pry into a person's private affairs.
situation: Nicole is working out at the gym, and she sees her friend, Becky, who recently got a divorce.
intention: Nicole wants to know how Betty is doing.
moral_action: Nicole stays away from any sensitive topics and just inquires about Betty's general well being.
moral_consequence: Betty is happy to have a friend to talk to and thanks Nicole for concern.
immoral_action: Nicole repeatedly asks Betty lots of personal questions about her divorce.
immoral_consequence: Betty feels uncomfortable and tries to change the subject each time.

norm: Shaming people for being fat is not acceptable.
situation: Rosa is at a party with her friends, and sees an old friend who has recently gained a lot of weight.
intention: Rosa wants people to think she's funny and fierce.
moral_action: Rosa tells a story about something funny and crazy her old friend and her did when they were much younger.
moral_consequence: Her old friend is happy to recall those fun memories.
immoral_action: Rosa starts making fun of the overweight girl and her friends laugh at her jokes.
immoral_consequence: Her overweight friend is hurt and feels miserable.

norm: It is wrong to judge a friend's personal life.
situation: Tom notices his friends Jerry is drinking more alcohol than he has in the past.
intention: Tom wants to address Jerry's alcohol use with him.
moral_action: Tom expresses his concern,  offers assistance and finds out that Jerry has a lot of recent work and family stress.
moral_consequence: Jerry feels better knowing that he has someone to talk to and begins to drink less again.
immoral_action: Tom tells Jerry that he is sinning with his choices and that he is not being a true friend when he drinks so much.
immoral_consequence: Jerry stops hanging around with Tom and over the months increases his drinking more.

norm: It is rude to disrespect your parents.
situation: Randal learns about a concert at midnight from a radio ad, but his parents don't want him out past 9pm by himself.
intention: Randal wants to go to the concert.
moral_action: Randal asks his parents to go with him to the concert.
moral_consequence: Randal's parents agree, and they have a good time.
immoral_action: Randal sneaks out of the house to go to the concert alone.
immoral_consequence: Randal's parents find out that he snuck out and punish him.

norm: Being reckless while driving puts other peoples' lives in danger.
situation: Ben is driving to work on the highway  when he gets a phone call.
intention: Ben wants to answer the phone.
moral_action: Ben waits until it is safe and pulls over on the side of the road to answer the phone.
moral_consequence: The other motorists are able to drive by safely while Ben is on the phone.
immoral_action: Ben looks down for a moment to answer the phone while he is driving.
immoral_consequence: Ben slams into the side of another car and kills the person inside of it.

norm: It's bad to not support your family member's goals.
situation: Steven's sister is telling him about her dream of becoming a dancer.
intention: Steven wants to go to sleep.
moral_action: Steven takes a few minutes to encourage his sister about her dream, telling her she can definitely succeed if she tries, before heading to bed.
moral_consequence: Steven's sister feels that he is a really supportive person that she can rely on.
immoral_action: Steven doesn't respond to his sister's conversation and goes straight to bed.
immoral_consequence: Steven's sister feels that he doesn't care about her life at all.

norm: It's bad to snoop on your neighbor's correspondence.
situation: Deloris and her husband Ned offered to help out their neighbor while she's away on vacation.
intention: Deloris needs to pick up their neighbor's mail every day.
moral_action: Deloris picks up all her neighbor's mail and puts it in a pile without looking at any letters.
moral_consequence: Ned tells Deloris that it's good she's picking up the neighbor's mail every day.
immoral_action: When Deloris picks up her neighbor's mail she looks her letters to see who writing to her.
immoral_consequence: Ned sees Deloris looking at the neighbor's letters and tells her she shouldn't be so nosy.

norm: It's good to want to teach others things you know.
situation: John is a guitar prodigy who learned how to play guitar at a young age and is now considering tutoring for money.
intention: John needs to make some money.
moral_action: John decides to start his own tutoring business for young students.
moral_consequence: John's tremendous skill is passed on in part to his willing students.
immoral_action: John decides to get a job as a mechanic instead, keeping his talents all to himself.
immoral_consequence: John's musical skills are not appreciated by society at large.

norm: You shouldn't lie about being molested.
situation: Tom is feeling really burnt out from school, and hears about how his friend who got molested got to stay home from school for a week.
intention: Tom wants to take a vacation from school.
moral_action: Tom tells his parents he is feeling burnt out from school and asks if he can take a break.
moral_consequence: Tom's parents call the school and arrange for some school work to be sent home, so he can take a weeks break from school.
immoral_action: Tom tells his parents he was molested and says he doesn't want to go to school.
immoral_consequence: The police are called and after finding out he lied he is grounded for months.

norm: One shouldn't feel hatred toward a family member.
situation: Joey is a teenager and his dad recently moved away because his parents got divorced.
intention: Joey wants to react to his father moving away.
moral_action: Joey tries to understand his parents' reasoning for divorce and does not blame his father for moving away.
moral_consequence: Joey continues a relationship with his father.
immoral_action: Joey blames his father for the divorce and moving away and doesn't want to talk to him.
immoral_consequence: Joey does not continue a relationship with his father.

norm: It's good to want to dress nicely.
situation: Dave and his wife Wendy are getting ready in their bedroom to go out to a very fancy restaurant tonight.
intention: Dave wants to choose what to wear.
moral_action: Dave decides that he's going to go full out and puts on a tuxedo with a black bowtie.
moral_consequence: Wendy is impressed by how dapper Dave looks and is proud to stand next to him in public.
immoral_action: Dave decides to put on some basketball shorts, a thick plaid shirt, black socks and running shoes.
immoral_consequence: Wendy is horrified that Dave looks ridiculous and is breaking every rule of fashion embarrassing her to be seen with him.

norm: You shouldn't skateboard somewhere dangerous.
situation: Tony has the day off and decides to ride his skateboard around the neighborhood instead of sitting at home.
intention: Tony wants to go out.
moral_action: Tony decides to play it safe and rides his board on the sidewalk.
moral_consequence: Tony enjoys the fresh air and enjoys seeing the sights around town.
immoral_action: Tony sees some concrete stairs and decides to try to ride down the railing on his board.
immoral_consequence: Tony wipes out and breaks his leg, so now he has to wear a cast.

norm: It is good to support family.
situation: Donnie finds out his daughter Madonna is pregnant with a child out of wedlock.
intention: Donnie wants to help his daughter through her trying time.
moral_action: Donnie pays for all his daughter's medical bills and opens his heart to her.
moral_consequence: Madonna gets to keep her baby.
immoral_action: Donnie ignores his daughter's calls and changes his phone number.
immoral_consequence: Madonna has to have an abortion because she can't afford care for her baby.

norm: It's fun to eat pizza with others.
situation: Ash is very hungry after a long day of work and has not eaten all day.
intention: Ash wants to have pizza for dinner.
moral_action: Ash invites friends over for some pizza together.
moral_consequence: Ash has a great time with her friends and the pizza is amazing.
immoral_action: Ash orders a pizza for herself and enjoys it at home.
immoral_consequence: Ash wishes she had shared the delicious pizza with friends.

norm: You shouldn't kiss your in-laws.
situation: Vince is hosting a party at his house and his in-laws are coming over.
intention: Vince wants to welcome his in-laws to his house.
moral_action: Vince shakes his in-laws' hands and tells them to come into his home.
moral_consequence: Vince's in-laws will think he is a polite and formal man.
immoral_action: Vince kisses his in-laws and tells them to come into his home.
immoral_consequence: Vince's in-laws will think he is too affectionate with them.

norm: It's strange to eat paper.
situation: Lawrence is at the school cafeteria with his friends during lunch time.
intention: Lawrence wants to eat lunch.
moral_action: Lawrence takes out a sandwich and consumes it.
moral_consequence: Lawrence's friends will think he is a normal guy.
immoral_action: Lawrence takes out sheets of paper and consumes them.
immoral_consequence: Lawrence's friends will think he is weird.

norm: It is good to achieve things independently.
situation: Nadia is working on an project for a school contest that's due tomorrow.
intention: Nadia wants to win the contest.
moral_action: Nadia spends all afternoon and evening working on the project, making sure she pays attention to every little detail.
moral_consequence: Nadia wins the contest and feels a sense of fulfillment and accomplishment since the work reflected her own efforts.
immoral_action: Nadia asks her parents for help to make the project extra special so that she can win.
immoral_consequence: Nadia wins the contest but doesn't learn very much since she didn't do a lot of the work herself.

norm: It is rude to criticize people due to their weight
situation: Sara has a friend who put on tons of extra weight which is clearly having a dangerous unhealthy effect.
intention: Sara wants to help her friend lose weight.
moral_action: Sara convinces her friend to go hiking with her.
moral_consequence: Sara's friend has a great time and loses weight as it becomes a regular activity.
immoral_action: Sara constantly comments on her friend's weight and nags her about it.
immoral_consequence: Sara's friend becomes very upset by her treatment.

norm: It's wrong to make jokes about places with crime.
situation: Ron is a comedian, and he has a scheduled performance tonight at a local comedy club.
intention: Ron wants to give a good comedy show.
moral_action: Ron performs a comedy act featuring lots of jokes about airports and traveling.
moral_consequence: The crowd loves Ron's jokes, and he exits the stage to a standing ovation.
immoral_action: Ron performs a comedy act that includes lots of jokes about crime in inner city Chicago.
immoral_consequence: The crowd finds Ron's jokes to be in poor taste, and he gets booed during his performance.

norm: It's rude to call the police on a friend.
situation: Andrea's friend Wanda has been smoking weed a lot to cope with her depression and Andrea is concerned.
intention: Andrea wants Wanda to stop smoking so much.
moral_action: Andrea talks to Wanda about her concerns and refers her to a therapist.
moral_consequence: Wanda is able to address her underlying mental health problems, so she can stop using drugs as a crutch.
immoral_action: Andrea calls the police and tells them Wanda is in possession of drugs.
immoral_consequence: Wanda is arrested and her emotional state worsens.

norm: It's rude to interrupt a performer.
situation: Abe and Allie are at a play, which has proven a bit dull for both.
intention: Abe wants to get out, since there's more than half left.
moral_action: Abe tells Allie they should leave next intermission, which they do.
moral_consequence: They don't wait long and get out politely.
immoral_action: Abe convinces Allie to leave right away, bumping through the aisle and making a sound when opening the door.
immoral_consequence: The custodian tells them not to come back because of the disturbance.

norm: It's hurtful to share photos of a friend's confession.
situation: Larry is friends with Jacob, who is an alcoholic and is telling his friends about something bad he did while drunk.
intention: Larry wants to talk about Jacob's alcoholism.
moral_action: Larry tells Jacob privately that he has a drinking problem and that he needs help.
moral_consequence: Jacob appreciates Larry's concern and agrees to see someone about his drinking.
immoral_action: Larry posts pictures from Jacob's confession on social media and tells everyone about Jacob's problems.
immoral_consequence: Jacob is very hurt and embarrassed and stays away from Larry in the future.

norm: You shouldn't let your kids damage store merchandise.
situation: Kayla is at the store with her young son who is hyperactive and destructive.
intention: Kayla wants to distract her son with something.
moral_action: Kayla gives her son a stress ball to play with at the store.
moral_consequence: Kayla's son interacts with the stress ball and people at the store think he's cute.
immoral_action: Kayla gives her son a store product to keep him busy.
immoral_consequence: Kayla's son ends up causing damage to the merchandise causing onlookers to think badly of him.

norm: It is foolish to put your life at risk
situation: Brian's cat gets swept away by a flash flood and is clinging onto a tree branch for dear life while surrounded by raging water.
intention: Brian wants his cat to be saved.
moral_action: Brian calls emergency services and asks them to rescue his poor cat.
moral_consequence: The emergency personnel use their training and equipment to rescue the cat.
immoral_action: Brian takes off his outer clothes and shoes, jumps into the water, and swims towards his cat.
immoral_consequence: Brian gets swept away by the fierce current and needs to be rescued himself.

norm: It's wrong to make plans and then break them.
situation: Jane agrees to meet her friend for lunch on Saturday afternoon, then has a date with her boyfriend on Sunday.
intention: Jane wants to get her hair done before her date on Sunday.
moral_action: Jane makes a salon appointment for Saturday morning, so she can make to to lunch with her friend as planned.
moral_consequence: Jane and her friend become closer by spending time together.
immoral_action: Jane cancels her plans with her friend and makes a salon appointment for Saturday afternoon.
immoral_consequence: Jane's friend is upset and resents Jane.

norm: It's rude to dismiss someone based on their issues.
situation: Henry is a supervisor at a grocery store and has a shelf stocker with Down syndrome who isn't doing very well.
intention: Henry wants to get the shelves stocked well.
moral_action: Henry assigns another employee to work with the troubled employee and train him thoroughly.
moral_consequence: With time, the mentally handicapped employee learns to do his job well and contributes to society.
immoral_action: Henry fires the employee with Down syndrome and hires someone else who can learn the job quickly.
immoral_consequence: The employee with Down syndrome never manages to find another job and feels terribly about life.

norm: You shouldn't let gambling cause you to get into trouble.
situation: Janice is in Las Vegas for vacation and is visiting a casino.
intention: Janice wants to play the roulette wheel.
moral_action: Janice sets aside a small amount of money for gambling and stops when she runs out of that money.
moral_consequence: Janice has enough money to do other fun things and has a great time.
immoral_action: Janice gambles away everything she has in a few hours.
immoral_consequence: Janice is stuck because she doesn't have money for a ride back to her hotel.

norm: Pulling someone's earbuds from their ears is unnecessarily aggressive.
situation: James is doing his math homework while his older sister listens to music wearing earbuds.
intention: James wants his sister to help him with a hard problem.
moral_action: James stands in front of his sister and waves his hands to get her attention.
moral_consequence: James' sister takes out her earphones, hears his request and agrees to help.
immoral_action: James pulls his sister's earbuds out of her ears to get her attention.
immoral_consequence: James' sister yells and him and refuses to help him because he was pushy.

norm: Roommates are expected to respect each other's privacy.
situation: Willis's girlfriend is sleeping over and his roommate Juan wants to borrow a book.
intention: Juan wants get reading material.
moral_action: Juan sends Willis a text asking if he can borrow his book.
moral_consequence: Willis shoves the book under the door and him and his girlfriend continue to make love.
immoral_action: Juan goes into Willis's room to ask for the book.
immoral_consequence: Willis and his girlfriend are interrupted while having sex.

norm: It's wrong to support bad behavior.
situation: Desiree is friends with Lana, who has been saying mean things to other kids at their school.
intention: Desiree wants Lana to know she's on her side.
moral_action: Desiree tells Lana that she's better than how she's been acting, and suggests being kinder.
moral_consequence: Lana takes Desiree's advice to heart and apologizes to all the kids she's ever been mean to.
immoral_action: Desiree witnesses Lana making fun of another girls outfit, and laughs along.
immoral_consequence: The other girl feels ganged up on and begins to cry.

norm: You can't expect people to like everything.
situation: Suzy and Lilly were playing in Suzy's backyard, but while Suzy wanted to play baseball, Lilly didn't.
intention: Suzy wants to play with Lilly.
moral_action: Suzy agrees to play something else that they both like.
moral_consequence: Suzy and Lilly play for hours and have a great time.
immoral_action: Suzy persuades Lilly to play baseball without considering what Lilly might want to play.
immoral_consequence: Lilly doesn't go to Suzy's house to play anymore, and they drift apart.

norm: Calling a child a name is mean.
situation: John and his friend Steve are in the ice cream parlor and there is an obese child buying ice cream there.
intention: John wants to make Steve laugh.
moral_action: John tells Steve a funny joke he heard on the Fallon show last night.
moral_consequence: Steve laughs at the joke and John feels good about himself.
immoral_action: John calls the obese child a fatty and tells him that he should be eating vegetables instead of ice cream.
immoral_consequence: The child begins to cry and the owner of the ice cream parlor throws John out.

norm: It's good to take care of babies.
situation: Jack's sister and her husband need to attend a funeral last minute and needs someone to watch their baby.
intention: Jack wants to be helpful to his sister.
moral_action: Jack offers to watch the baby so they can go.
moral_consequence: Jack's sister is very happy and Jack gets to bond with his nephew.
immoral_action: Jack tells his sister to go hire a sitter, he is busy.
immoral_consequence: Jack fails to help his sister and he disappoints her.

norm: It's cheap to not tip.
situation: Francis is going out to eat with friends, knowing that his rent is due the next day.
intention: Francis wants to save money on dinner.
moral_action: Francis orders a value-meal, leaving enough in his budget to tip.
moral_consequence: Francis' waiter is paid, and Francis makes rent the next day.
immoral_action: Francis orders a large steak and decides to save money by foregoing the waiter's tip.
immoral_consequence: The waiter works all day and goes home without the appropriate compensation.

norm: You shouldn't expose yourself to strangers.
situation: John was out in town and had been drinking soda all day.
intention: John wanted to use the restroom and relieve himself.
moral_action: John found a restroom in a shop where he was browsing.
moral_consequence: John felt much better after he was able to relieve himself.
immoral_action: John pulled his pants down and urinated in the middle of the park.
immoral_consequence: A police officer arrested John for indecent exposure.

norm: It's wrong to trick people into thinking you can sing.
situation: Jess would brag that she could do anything, so when one of her friend brought up singing she said she could do that too.
intention: Jess wants to end the discussion.
moral_action: Jess points out that technically anyone can sing, using auto-tune.
moral_consequence: Her friends all laugh and admit it's technically true and move on to the next thing.
immoral_action: Jess insists that she can sing better than any of them could.
immoral_consequence: Of course no one believes Jess, and when she brags the next time no one believes her then either.

norm: It's bad to belittle others who are not tech savvy.
situation: Kramer is in charge of training a new guy, Harry to use the PC at work.
intention: Kramer wants to explain how to log in.
moral_action: Kramer shows Harry how to get into the PC, Harry fails to understand, so Kramer explains it in simpler terms.
moral_consequence: Harry understands how to log into the PC now and is glad to have someone take the time to teach him properly.
immoral_action: Kramer shows Harry how to get into the PC, but when Harry fails to understand, he is mocked.
immoral_consequence: Harry feels incompetent and quits the job before he ever really had a chance to start.

norm: It is unprofessional to cry at work.
situation: Dave is a grocery store clerk who is restocking a shelf when he gets a text that his wife is dead, and he immediately has an urge to cry.
intention: Dave wants to find a place to cry.
moral_action: Dave sneaks outside by the loading dock at the back of the store and finds a place between two parked semi trucks to cry in private.
moral_consequence: The customers go on shopping without any clue that there is a man outside whose life has been torn to pieces.
immoral_action: Dave gets up from the floor where he was stocking and wanders into the cashier area where he begins to bawl his eyes out.
immoral_consequence: The customers all feel pity on Dave and are saddened by his public display of sorrow and start to cry too.

norm: It is good to encourage your kids to be creative.
situation: Ronald has a daughter who he loves very much.
intention: Ronald wants his daughter to have a happy future.
moral_action: Ronald encourages his daughter to follow her creative passions and pursue art.
moral_consequence: Ronald's daughter appreciates his support and develops useful creative skills.
immoral_action: Ronald refuses to let his daughter take art classes because he wants her to focus on science, so she can get a good job.
immoral_consequence: Ronald's daughter resents him for not allowing her to follow her interests.

norm: You shouldn't make fun of someone else.
situation: Lisa sees the same kid in the corner of the lunchroom not eating because they never have lunch money.
intention: Lisa wants to decide what to do.
moral_action: Lisa heads over and talks to the kid and asks some questions.
moral_consequence: Turns out the kid just doesn't like the food the school has.
immoral_action: Lisa makes fun of the kid for not having any money.
immoral_consequence: The kid beats up Lisa and takes her money and then laughs at her.

norm: It's wrong to let the american flag touch the ground
situation: Len is a janitor at a school and has been told by the school administration to take down the flag flying at the entrance.
intention: Len wants to take the flag off the pole and put the flag somewhere.
moral_action: Len takes the flag off the pole, folds it and takes it indoors for storage.
moral_consequence: The students at the school see Len treating the flag with extra respect and learn that it's important to respect the flag.
immoral_action: Len takes the flag off the pole and throws it on the grass nearby.
immoral_consequence: The students at the school see Len disrespecting the flag and assume that it's OK to do so.

norm: It is rude to say negative things about someone's appearance.
situation: James is at his party with his poorly dressed friend Randy.
intention: James wants to entertain people.
moral_action: James tells the crowd a story about his adventures with Randy including his friend in the conversation.
moral_consequence: James and Randy make a positive impression on the crowd who ask to hear more stories.
immoral_action: James makes a joke based on Randy's attire.
immoral_consequence: James damages his relationship with Randy.

norm: It's nice to make a meal for someone else.
situation: Dennis has an elderly neighbor who has trouble getting around.
intention: Dennis wants to cook a salmon he has in the freezer.
moral_action: Dennis bakes the salmon and takes it to his neighbor as a gift.
moral_consequence: Dennis' neighbor invites him in and the two eat dinner together and tell each other stories.
immoral_action: Dennis bakes the salmon for dinner and eats it by himself.
immoral_consequence: Dennis' elderly neighbor tries to drive to the store to get some groceries but slips and falls.

norm: It's good to stand up to racism.
situation: John overhears his coworker make a racist comment.
intention: John wants to respond.
moral_action: John tells his coworker his words are inappropriate and offensive.
moral_consequence: John's coworker refrains from insensitive remarks in the future.
immoral_action: John laughs and nods in agreement.
immoral_consequence: The coworker persists with occasional racist remarks.

norm: It's important to reinforce children's good behaviors with praise.
situation: Hank's son was normally a slob but today he cleaned his room properly.
intention: Hank wants to decide what to tell his son.
moral_action: Hank praises his son for cleaning his room this time.
moral_consequence: Hank's son starts to clean his room more often.
immoral_action: Hank does nothing since it's something he's supposed to do anyway.
immoral_consequence: Hank's son goes right back to being messy as before.

norm: It's important to fight harmful urges.
situation: Carrie has a job interview coming up.
intention: Carrie wants to get the job.
moral_action: Carrie spends the evening reviewing information about the company.
moral_consequence: Carrie aces the interview and gets a job offer.
immoral_action: Carrie is nervous about the interviews, so she copes by going out to a bar and drinking too much.
immoral_consequence: Carrie has an accident on the way home and never makes it to the job interview.

norm: People are expected to be considerate of their family members.
situation: Ray needs to practice his guitar, and his mother is sleeping in the other room.
intention: Ray wants to play guitar.
moral_action: Ray goes over to his friends house to practice.
moral_consequence: Ray has a fun night getting closer to his friend after practice.
immoral_action: Ray practices in his room for several hours.
immoral_consequence: Ray's mother grounds him for making too much noise during her nap.

norm: It's good to have a job.
situation: Jessica just graduated college.
intention: Jessica wants to be happy and take it easy.
moral_action: Jessica looks for a job and lands one and lives on her own.
moral_consequence: Jessica feels good about herself and her parents are happy too.
immoral_action: Jessica moves in with her parents and lives off of them.
immoral_consequence: Jessica's self-esteem goes down and her parents become upset.

norm: It's wrong to break all one's possessions.
situation: Livia feels that she is too attached to material possessions which makes her life devoid of meaning.
intention: Livia wants to feel free.
moral_action: Livia goes through her possessions and gets rid of a lot of things she has not used in a while.
moral_consequence: Livia feels free and in control of her life.
immoral_action: Livia decides to get rid of everything she owns by destroying all the possessions in her life.
immoral_consequence: Livia feels free but destabilized and a bit lost.

norm: It is wrong to push people into traffic
situation: John and Ted are waiting at a crosswalk to cross the street.
intention: John wants to play a practical joke on Ted.
moral_action: John points at Ted's chest and says he has something on his shirt, then hits Ted's chin as Ted looks down to see.
moral_consequence: Ted laughs at John for being so silly and juvenile.
immoral_action: John pushes Ted into the street before the light has turned green for them to walk.
immoral_consequence: Ted is hit by an oncoming car and has to be rushed to the hospital.

norm: It's inappropriate to use racial slurs.
situation: James, a white student, was frustrated that his friend, who was black, kept outscoring him on tests.
intention: James wants to feel less inferior to his friend.
moral_action: James tells his friend that he may be smart, but he (James) is much better at sports.
moral_consequence: The friend agrees and says that James was really impressive in PE the other day.
immoral_action: James tells his friend that he's just a stuck-up n-word.
immoral_consequence: James is suspended for two weeks and permanently loses the friendship.

norm: It's nice to share your belongings with siblings.
situation: Mason just got a new toy set and is playing with them in his room when his sister comes in and asks to play with him.
intention: Mason wants to play with his new toys.
moral_action: Mason invites his sister to come play with him.
moral_consequence: Mason and his sister invent a new game with the toys which they play every day for over a year.
immoral_action: Mason tells his sister to leave and plays with his toys alone.
immoral_consequence: Mason get's bored of the new toys and loses interest after a few hours.

norm: It's good to share your things with others.
situation: Sally has a roommate who is getting ready for a date but has misplaced some make up.
intention: Sally wants to recommend her favorite brand of make up.
moral_action: Sally recommends the brand she uses and lets her roommate try some of her's now.
moral_consequence: The roommate feels more confident on the date having all her make up on.
immoral_action: Sally tells her roommate what her favorite brand is and where to buy it.
immoral_consequence: The roommate has to go without the make up because of time constraints.

norm: It's wrong for someone to be cruel or racest.
situation: Elon was posting on Twitter when a black Twitter user made fun of him in his replies.
intention: Elon wants to get the user to leave him alone.
moral_action: Elon tells a joke about the user's profile and then blocks the user.
moral_consequence: The user cannot bother Elon anymore, and others are aware of the user's behavior.
immoral_action: Elon calls the user a racial slur in a public tweet.
immoral_consequence: The user's feelings are hurt, and others are hurt by it as well.

norm: You shouldn't steal from your partner's parents.
situation: Maya is having trouble paying her rent and doesn't want to ask anyone for the money.
intention: Maya wants to pay the rent without having to owe someone else.
moral_action: Maya tries working odd jobs in her spare time until she has the money.
moral_consequence: Maya manages to earn enough to pay the rent.
immoral_action: Maya goes to her boyfriend's house and takes money from his wealthy parents when no one is looking.
immoral_consequence: Her boyfriend's neighborhood goes into high security because of the theft making it difficult to see her boyfriend.

norm: It's good to strike up conversations with others.
situation: John takes the bus to work everyday, and sits on a crowded bus one day next to a total stranger who seems to want to socialize.
intention: John wants to have an enjoyable ride.
moral_action: John greets the stranger and asks him how his day is going.
moral_consequence: The stranger excitedly begins to tell John a fascinating story about what's going on in his life.
immoral_action: John spends the time relaxing, staring out the bus windows and daydreaming.
immoral_consequence: The stranger seems somewhat annoyed that John doesn't want to chat.

norm: It is customary to only use your own toothbrush.
situation: Jerry is late for work and cannot find his toothbrush, but he sees his partner's toothbrush is still in the bathroom.
intention: Jerry wants to brush his teeth.
moral_action: Jerry goes and buys a new toothbrush and brushes his teeth in the workplace restroom.
moral_consequence: Jerry makes it to work on time, and a coworker compliments him on his shiny teeth.
immoral_action: Jerry uses his partner's toothbrush to brush his teeth.
immoral_consequence: Jerry's partner finds out he used her toothbrush, and she ends the relationship and kicks him out.

norm: It's rude to cut in front of others in line.
situation: Claire is at the front of the prison commissary line and Amber is at the end of the line.
intention: Amber doesn't want to wait in the line for very long.
moral_action: Amber walks up to Claire and explains that her need is an emergency.
moral_consequence: Claire asks Amber what she needs and buys the items for her, saving her the wait time.
immoral_action: Amber walks towards the front of the line and stands in front of Claire.
immoral_consequence: Claire pushes Amber and both prisoners end up getting punished for their behavior.

norm: It's good to have a plan for a costume party.
situation: Halloween is approaching and Roger has a lot of friends who enjoy dressing up.
intention: Roger wants to have a costume party.
moral_action: Roger tells everyone to come to his house in a work-themed costume.
moral_consequence: Roger's friends rise to the challenge and create some excellent and tasteful costumes.
immoral_action: Roger tells everyone to come to his house in their favorite costume without imposing any limits.
immoral_consequence: Some friends come in racist and offensive costumes, offending some of his other friends.

norm: It's mean to kick your family out of your house.
situation: Denise's cousin Jerry fell on hard times and has been staying in her house for months as he is unemployed.
intention: Denise wants to talk to Jerry about his situation.
moral_action: Denise tells Jerry he can continue staying if he does chores.
moral_consequence: Jerry contributes to the upkeep of the house and has a place to live.
immoral_action: Denise tells Jerry he has to leave as he has no money to pay rent.
immoral_consequence: Jerry will be distraught and homeless.

norm: It's good to buy a new place to live.
situation: Chris is repairing a broken door in his house when his wife Linda says she's sick of the rickety house and constant repairs.
intention: Chris wants to calm Linda down.
moral_action: Chris tells Linda that she's right and that they really ought to get a new place already.
moral_consequence: Linda is delighted that Chris said that and is excited to start looking for a new place.
immoral_action: Chris tells Linda to calm down, it's their house, and she should have some respect for it.
immoral_consequence: Linda is annoyed that Chris seems to love the house more than her and thinks her point is valid about it being a disaster.

norm: You should not be condescending to another adult.
situation: Harley is trying to order a bagel and lox at the local deli and the cashier is confused having never heard of lox.
intention: Harley wants to eat breakfast.
moral_action: Harley explains to the cashier what lox is and says he will have cream cheese instead.
moral_consequence: The cashier is interested and suggests to the store manager that they add lox to the menu.
immoral_action: Harley says the cashier must be low class and orders a bagel with cream cheese instead.
immoral_consequence: The cashier is offended and gives Harley a stale bagel.

norm: It's good to clap to encourage performers.
situation: Jones is at a concert with his friends and the band finishes a song.
intention: Jones wants to decide to clap or not.
moral_action: Jones claps for the band even though it wasn't his favorite song.
moral_consequence: Jones friends clap for the song and the band as well.
immoral_action: Jones didn't like the song, so he thinks the band is lucky he's not booing.
immoral_consequence: Jones's friends think that Jones is being a jerk to not clap.

norm: It's wrong to expect someone to work for free.
situation: Olivia, who runs an accounting firm, has recently hired Kelly to be a receptionist.
intention: Olivia wants her firm to thrive financially.
moral_action: Olivia decides to pay Kelly a fair wage plus bonuses for good work.
moral_consequence: Kelly is motivated by her bonuses and does extra well on the job, resulting in good reviews and more clients for the firm.
immoral_action: "Olivia decides not to pay Kelly for her first two weeks of work, referring to it as ""unpaid training"", thinking this will save her money."
immoral_consequence: Kelly quits the firm and Olivia ends up losing money by not having a receptionist to schedule clients.

norm: It is rude to curse at your friends.
situation: Jenna's friend walked through a door in front of her and accidentally let it slam in Jenna's face.
intention: Jenna wants her friend to be more careful.
moral_action: "Jenna says, ""Hey, be more careful,"" and frowns at her friend."

situation: Luke has a dog that he brings to the dog park.
intention: Luke wants to play fetch with his dog.
moral_action: Luke notices the dog is hurt and decides to go back home so the dog can rest.
moral_consequence: The dog gets better faster and is up and active sooner.
immoral_action: Luke noticed his dog has a limp but continues to throw the ball which the dog can’t resist chasing.
immoral_consequence: The dogs leg gets worse, and he is more severely injured.

norm: It's wrong to wish someone's relationship fails.
situation: Sean's best friend just got into a new relationship and Sean is feeling lonely.
intention: Sean wants to make sure he remains close with his friend.
moral_action: Sean shows support for his friend's relationship and has a conversation with him about making sure they still find time to do things together.
moral_consequence: Sean's friend appreciates the concern and assures Sean they will still have good times together.
immoral_action: Sean never shows any enthusiasm for his friend's relationship hoping to will an end to it into existence, so he and his friend can spend more time together.
immoral_consequence: Sean's friend becomes bothered by Sean clearly not liking his partner and the strength of their friendship dwindles.

norm: It's not okay to be dangerous with tools.
situation: Dad brings his young son into the garage where he has set up a work space for them with wood and power tools, so they can build a bird house.
intention: Dad wants to introduce his son to woodworking and carpentry.
moral_action: Dad shows his son how to properly and safely use a jigsaw and watches him make practice cuts on scrap wood before cutting the pieces for the bird house.
moral_consequence: His son learns to be confident with power tools and learns to use them safely and properly, and they complete the bird house.
immoral_action: Dad hands him a jigsaw with the safety disabled and tells him to cut along the line.
immoral_consequence: The son pulls the trigger while holding it near his face and the noise scares him, and he cuts his fingers as he drops the saw.

norm: It's wrong to take things from someone without permission.
situation: Carson's mother is sleeping and her car is in the garage.
intention: Carson wants to go to his friend's house.
moral_action: Carson rides his bike down the road to his friend's house.
moral_consequence: Carson gets exercise when he rides his bike around town.
immoral_action: Carson takes his mother's keys and takes the car to his friend's house without asking.
immoral_consequence: Carson's mother wakes up and calls the cops when she sees the car is not there.

norm: You should not treat mental illness like it is cool.
situation: Sophie is listening to her friend Moira talk about depression that she experiences.
intention: Sophie wants to add to the conversation.
moral_action: Sophie tells Moira she has never experienced depression but wants to be able to help.
moral_consequence: Moira feels supported and is comfortable coming to Sophie with problems relating to her depression.
immoral_action: Sophie tells Moira that she is jealous because her depression makes her seem more mature and mysterious.
immoral_consequence: Moira is insulted by Sophie's misunderstanding of a disabling condition and no longer feels comfortable confiding in her.

norm: It's good to think about others when doing things.
situation: Clark stands with a group of friends after a meeting and someone suggests that they all go out together for the evening.
intention: Clark wants to do something fun with the group.
moral_action: Clark suggests that they go to see a movie and mentions the one that he wants to see, and then he asks what everyone else thinks.
moral_consequence: The group weighs their options, including Clark's suggestion, and they all decide together about what to do with their evening.
immoral_action: Clark tells the group that they should all go see the new superhero movie that just came out, and he calls the theater to find out the showtimes.
immoral_consequence: Most of the group is irritated that Clark just assumed that everyone will do what he wants to do, and Clark is embarrassed.

norm: It is rude to cancel on someone for a date.
situation: Ezra is about to go on a date with Shelly he met online when he notices Shelly's new profile picture makes her look drastically different.
intention: Ezra wants to go on a date.
moral_action: Ezra asks Shelly about her dramatic change in appearance before he agrees to go on their date.
moral_consequence: Shelly becomes more confident in herself as Ezra warms up to her.
immoral_action: Ezra ditches his original date for another young woman who works at the bar.
immoral_consequence: Shelly is heartbroken that Ezra canceled their date.

norm: It's good to wish someone a happy birthday.
situation: Laura sees her friend Jessica walking towards her.
intention: Laura wants to greet her friend.
moral_action: Laura tells Jessica happy birthday.
moral_consequence: Jessica smiles and thanks her.
immoral_action: Laura waves at Jessica and says hi.
immoral_consequence: Jessica is upset that Laura seemed to forget her birthday.

norm: It is important to pay your bills.
situation: Denise signed up for a cell phone plan and gets the first bill in the mail.
intention: Denise wants to respond to the bill.
moral_action: Denise pays the bill on time with a check.
moral_consequence: Denise will be able to use her cell phone.
immoral_action: Denise put the bill in a drawer and forgets about it.
immoral_consequence: Denise's cell phone plan will be turned off.

norm: You should be respectful of people at the gym.
situation: Jamie is running on the treadmill beside Bob, a stranger to him.
intention: Bob wants to let Jamie know he's interested in him.
moral_action: Bob tells Jamie that he thinks that he is cute and apologizes when he finds out that Jamie isn't interested in anyone at the moment.
moral_consequence: Jamie says that it's not a big deal and the two complete their workouts without any awkwardness.
immoral_action: "Bob makes an advance on Jamie, but when it is turned down, he starts trying to take pictures of Jamie saying that they are ""for later""."
immoral_consequence: Jamie reports Bob to the gym management and Bob is forced to forfeit his membership and leave.

norm: Drinking to excess is wrong.
situation: Sam drives from his house to meet a few friends at a local bar for some socializing and live music.
intention: Sam wants to have a really fun evening.
moral_action: Sam has two beers and spends most of the night on the dance floor enjoying the live music.
moral_consequence: Sam has a great experience and returns home safely later that evening.
immoral_action: Sam drinks nine beers at the bar and is extremely intoxicated.
immoral_consequence: Sam is pulled over on his way home and gets arrested for drunk driving.

norm: You shouldn't ask someone to give a present back.
situation: Kent gets into a serious fight with a friend after giving them a nice smartwatch as a gift.
intention: Kent wants to own the same smartwatch.
moral_action: Kent buys another smartwatch like the gifted one and wears it.
moral_consequence: Kent's friend sees him wearing it and is reminded of the gift he was given.
immoral_action: Kent asks for the smartwatch back from his friend.
immoral_consequence: Kent's friend starts to think even less of him.

norm: It’s bad to leave your spouse out of things.
situation: Randy and Ryan have been married for two years and are considering buying a home.
intention: Randy wants to surprise Ryan.
moral_action: Randy buys a special set of china to use with Ryan when they finally pick a home and gift wraps it for him.
moral_consequence: Ryan is touched by such an intimate and kind gesture and the two eagerly house shop together.
immoral_action: Randy signs a mortgage on a home without telling Ryan and surprises him with it after work one day.
immoral_consequence: Ryan is off-put by Randy's willingness to make such a big decision alone and needs time from the relationship.

norm: It is heartless to wish death on someone's loved one.
situation: Bill and Ted are best friends, but Bill is having a heated argument with Stacy, Ted's wife.
intention: Bill wants to end the argument.
moral_action: Bill offers to let bygones be bygones and stop arguing with Stacy.
moral_consequence: Bill and Stacy make up, and she and Ted continue to be friends with Bill.
immoral_action: Bill loudly tells Stacy that he wishes she were dead.
immoral_consequence: Stacy and Ted are appalled and never speak to Bill again.

norm: It's good to be exclusive with someone you're dating.
situation: Timmy has been dating Laura for a few months now.
intention: Timmy wants to see a movie.
moral_action: Timmy invites Laura on a date with him to the movies.
moral_consequence: Timmy and Laura have a great time and enjoy their time together.
immoral_action: Timmy invites a female coworker on a date with him to the movies.
immoral_consequence: Laura finds out and breaks up with Timmy right away.

norm: You should respond to communication in a timely manner.
situation: Evan's mother sent him a text to find out where he was.
intention: Evan wants to respond to his mother.
moral_action: Evan texts his mother back to tell her where he was.
moral_consequence: Evan's mother doesn't worry about him while he is gone.
immoral_action: Evan waits until he gets home hours later to tell his mother where he was.
immoral_consequence: When Evan gets home, he realizes that his mother has called the cops to report him missing.

norm: It's not expected that you'll be suspicious of your girlfriend.
situation: Doug follows his girlfriend Sonja because he's suspicious of cheating since all his previous girlfriends cheated on him.
intention: Doug wants to decide if he should continue this behavior.
moral_action: Doug realizes he's basically punishing Sonja for the actions of previous girlfriends.
moral_consequence: Doug stops and instead spends more time with her rather than following her.
immoral_action: Doug continues to stalk Sonja because he now thinks that women cannot be loyal by default.
immoral_consequence: Doug doesn't have time to spend with Sonja because he pretend to be busy, so he can follow her.

norm: You shouldn't dislike entire groups of people
situation: Harold plans on going to a concert and doesn't want to go alone.
intention: Harold wants to get a date.
moral_action: Harold is open to a variety of women and asks his group of friends to get him a date, and he goes with a blind date.
moral_consequence: Harold's friends know Harold is lonely and continue setting him up on dates, which he eventually ends up marrying one of them.
immoral_action: Harold declines his friend's suggestion of a different race woman and tells him he is going with another pal's sister, who is his own race.
immoral_consequence: Harold's friend is offended by his racist attitude and their friendship over his racist attitude.

norm: It's not okay to sabotage an election.
situation: Hannah is running for class president, and it's expected to be a tight race.
intention: Hannah wants to win the election.
moral_action: Hannah changes her plans for when she's class president, so they appeal more to the members of her class.
moral_consequence: Hannah gathers a lot of support and ends up winning the election legitimately.
immoral_action: Hannah decides to stuff the ballot box with her name until there are enough votes for her to win.
immoral_consequence: Hannah's teachers recognize her handwriting on the ballots, and she loses the election by default.

norm: You shouldn't intentionally break rules.
situation: Corey has moved to a new town and is looking at books in the library, despite not having a library card.
intention: Corey wants to bring a book about programming home with him.
moral_action: Corey fills out the paperwork for a library card and checks the book out.
moral_consequence: Corey is able to study programming and get more books when he needs them.
immoral_action: Corey walks to a back corner of the library and puts the book in his backpack.
immoral_consequence: A librarian notices missing books and reviews security tapes, resulting in Corey being banned from the library.

norm: You shouldn't intimidate children.
situation: Nick is babysitting his little nephew and his nephew just misbehaved.
intention: Nick wants to correct his nephew's behavior.
moral_action: Nick explains to his nephew what he did wrong and why he shouldn't behave like that.
moral_consequence: Nick's nephew learns his lesson and does not repeat the bad behavior.
immoral_action: Nick gets loud and hollowly threatens his nephew with physical harm if the nephew misbehaves again.
immoral_consequence: Nick's nephew does not realize the threat is hollow and becomes extremely fearful of Nick.

norm: You should be more responsible with your pets.
situation: Samantha's parents gifted her a pet gerbil recently.
intention: Samantha wants to show her friends her new gerbil.
moral_action: Samantha invites her friends over to take a look at her gerbil in it's cage.
moral_consequence: Samantha's friends think it's very cute and buy treats for it every once in a while.
immoral_action: Samantha carries the gerbil in her hands to her friends house to show them.
immoral_consequence: Samantha's friends get scared and scream when they see her gerbil, who then jumps out of Samantha's hands and gets hurt.

norm: It's good to travel and visit the people you love.
situation: Joe and his friends are going on vacation to Miami without Joe telling his grandmother, who lives in Miami, about his trip.
intention: Joe wants to have fun with his friends in Miami.
moral_action: Joe decides to surprise his grandmother with a visit from himself and his friends.
moral_consequence: Joe's grandmother is delighted to see him, and she allows him and his friends to party in her pool.
immoral_action: Joe posts about his adventures with his friends in Miami on social media, but never visits his grandmother.
immoral_consequence: Joe's grandmother sees Joe's social media posts and is hurt that he didn't visit her while he was in the area.

norm: Defacing school property is disrespectful.
situation: Martin is at the principal's office at school, where the principal tells him he will call Martin's parents and tell them he's been skipping school.
intention: Martin wants to emotionally react to the principal's statement.
moral_action: Martin starts to cry and tells the principal his pent up feelings about why he's been skipping and how he promises to do better.
moral_consequence: The principal is happy Martin is being open about his situation and is happy to see Martin share his feelings.
immoral_action: Martin runs out of the office angrily and slams the door so hard that it breaks the office window causing a thousand dollars of damage.
immoral_consequence: The principal is shaken by the violent crash of the door slamming and the glass breaking and is temporarily terrified.

norm: You shouldn't throw something at a family member.
situation: Timothy drops a cup of water over his sister Bella covering her with water, and Bella looks at the cup on the floor.
intention: Bella wants to vent her frustrations.
moral_action: Bella rants to her mother about the situation with her brother.
moral_consequence: Bella feels better after getting all of the anger out of her.
immoral_action: Bella picks up the cup and tosses it at her brother.
immoral_consequence: Bella is punished when her mother walks in on them.

norm: It's fun to go to the fair with people.
situation: Jamie hears that there is a fair in town a few miles from his home.
intention: Jamie wants to go to the fair.
moral_action: Jamie convinces several of his friends to go with him, and he drives them all to the fair that evening.
moral_consequence: Jamie has a wonderful evening at the fair with all his friends.
immoral_action: Jamie buys a ticket online and goes to the fair by himself that evening.
immoral_consequence: Jamie doesn't know anyone else there, and he doesn't really enjoy himself that much.

norm: You shouldn't get in arguments with your in-laws.
situation: John is having dinner with his in-laws, and they express a political view that he disagrees with.
intention: John wants to respond to his in-laws statement.
moral_action: John acknowledges his in-laws' point of view and then expresses his own in a respectful manner.
moral_consequence: Everyone continues to get along well, and they enjoy the rest of their evening.
immoral_action: John criticizes his in-laws' point of view and starts a heated political argument with them.
immoral_consequence: Everyone gets angry and the dinner is ruined because of the argument.

norm: You shouldn't turn against people.
situation: Selma used to be friends with one her coworkers but now sees that their boss doesn't like the coworker much at all.
intention: Selma wants her boss to think highly of her.
moral_action: Selma stays friend with her coworker and convinces her boss that the coworker is actually great.
moral_consequence: Selma's coworker doesn't have problems with their boss anymore and is grateful to Selma.
immoral_action: Selma stops hanging out with her coworker and starts being cold and distant with her.
immoral_consequence: Selma's coworker feels sad and betrayed.

norm: Is good for brothers to be nice to their sister
situation: Sam's sister Mary asks him for help mowing the lawn.
intention: Sam wants to respond to Mary.
moral_action: Sam agrees to help his sister mow the lawn.
moral_consequence: Mary is happy and feels supported.
immoral_action: Sam refuses to help his sister and watches TV instead.
immoral_consequence: Mary is sad that her brother won't help her.

norm: It's expected that friends will remain loyal to one another.
situation: Jack is going through a depression with makes him angry and talks to Ed about it.
intention: Ed wants to react to Jack's tough times.
moral_action: Ed realizes that Jack is struggling and is patient with him.
moral_consequence: Jack recovers from the depression and remains frineds with Ed for a long time.
immoral_action: Ed avoids Jack and talks about him to others.
immoral_consequence: Jack finds out and makes new friends which he sees as more trustworthy.

norm: It's foolish to press your luck.
situation: Sam is having a good time gambling at the local casino and is on quite a roll at the roulette table.
intention: Sam wants to bring home some winnings from the casino.
moral_action: Sam cashes in half of his chips and continues to play with the other half of them.
moral_consequence: Sam banks a decent amount of money from his night at the casino gambling.
immoral_action: Sam continues to place bet after bet with all the chips he has in front of him.
immoral_consequence: Sam eventually loses a round and all of his money is gone.

norm: You shouldn't miss your partner's birthday.
situation: Rover is putting in extra hours every week at work, but next Tuesday is his wife's birthday.
intention: Rover wants to put in 60 hours this week.
moral_action: Rover takes the day off Tuesday and decides to work on Saturday instead.
moral_consequence: Rover works all of his hours and still gets to spend time with his wife on her birthday.
immoral_action: Rover works a 12 hour shift on tuesday and misses his wife's birthday.
immoral_consequence: Rover's wife is furious at him for missing her birthday, you might say he's in the doghouse.

norm: It is good to accept people for who they are.
situation: Jan's brother is a hardcore sports fan, and Jan is not a sports fan.
intention: Jan has to decide whether to get his brother to read more books.
moral_action: Jan doesn't think that her brother would read the books, so he decides to leave him alone.
moral_consequence: Jan's brother is as happy as he's always been, and he still gets to enjoy his sports.
immoral_action: Jan buys his brother a bunch of books and makes him read them.
immoral_consequence: Jan's brother doesn't enjoy reading the books and doesn't feel like himself.

norm: It's not okay to forget the things that you need.
situation: Marley just arrived at the grocery store and realized that she left her shopping list on her husband's desk at home.
intention: Marley wants to finish her grocery shopping trip.
moral_action: Marley wants to make sure that she doesn't forget anything important, so she calls her husband and asks him to send her a picture of the list.
moral_consequence: Marley is able to find all the items that she needed without leaving anything behind.
immoral_action: Marley shops without consulting a list, picking up the things that she can remember off the top of her head.
immoral_consequence: Marley can't make the exact dinner she had planned since she's missing ingredients, so she's forced to improvise while cooking.

norm: It's unprofessional to discuss someone's race in the workplace.
situation: Bill is in the break room of his office talking to a few coworkers.
intention: Bill wants to chat casually with his coworkers.
moral_action: Bill asks how everyone's weekend was.
moral_consequence: Everyone engages in light chit chat that is non-offensive.
immoral_action: Bill loudly asks Karen about her skin tone and what ethnicity she might be.
immoral_consequence: Karen feels uncomfortable as if everyone is scrutinizing and categorizing her and applying stereotypes based on her background.

norm: It's good to take in interest in your child's life.
situation: Jordan's son just started to play on the local little league team.
intention: Jordan wants to see a ball game.
moral_action: Jordan makes sure that he is off of work for his son's first ball game.
moral_consequence: Jordan's son is excited and plays great at his first ball game.
immoral_action: Jordan goes to see a minor league ball game when his son is playing his first game.
immoral_consequence: Jordan's son is disheartened that his father isn't there and quits the team.

norm: It's not okay to let your lawn be in shambles.
situation: Jeff was at work all the time and never had time to take care of his lawn.
intention: Jeff wants to get his lawn mowed.
moral_action: Jeff hires a lawn care service to take care of his lawn every week.
moral_consequence: The homeowner association gives Jeff an award for the nicest lawn in the neighborhood.
immoral_action: Jeff makes sure to mow his lawn at least once every other month.
immoral_consequence: The homeowner association is disgusted with Jeff's lawn and fines him for it.

norm: You shouldn't say bad things about your parents.
situation: Flora is having a few friends over for the evening.
intention: Flora wants to tell a riveting story to her friends.
moral_action: Flora tells her friends about an incredible and funny adventure her parents had when they were young.
moral_consequence: Flora's friends now think Flora's parents are cool and exciting.
immoral_action: Flora decides to tell her friends about one of her parents' dark secrets.
immoral_consequence: Flora's friends see Flora's parents more negatively after hearing the story.

norm: It's frowned upon to not go to class.
situation: Tim, a student in high school, and his friends are talking about skipping class to go skateboarding.
intention: Tim wants to hang out with his friends.
moral_action: Tim convinces his friends to go skateboarding after school instead.
moral_consequence: Tim and his friends have a good time skateboarding and hang out regularly after class.
immoral_action: Tim skips class and goes out skateboarding with his friends.
immoral_consequence: Tim's parents find out, and he is grounded for weeks.

norm: It's wrong to cause other people to be stressed out.
situation: Stephen is helping Chris study for a big test they both have tomorrow.
intention: Stephen wants Chris to take the test seriously.
moral_action: Stephen mentions how important the test is to their overall grade and offers to study through the week together.
moral_consequence: Chris realizes how important the test is and agrees to daily study sessions.
immoral_action: Stephen begins questioning Chris's ability to do well on the test, telling him if he won't study enough he might as well quit.
immoral_consequence: Chris feels determined to do well and studies very seriously, but stress causes him to struggle to retain any of the information.

norm: It's okay not to support people who do bad things
situation: Jeffrey is a young and ideologically impressionable kid who enjoys reading history and is looking to get politically active.
intention: Jeffrey wants to express himself politically.
moral_action: Jeffrey identifies himself with FDR and his opposition to Nazism.
moral_consequence: Jeffrey's appreciation of history is noted approvingly by others.
immoral_action: Jeffrey identifies himself with Nationalist movements from the 1920's to 1940's and preaches National Socialist ideology.
immoral_consequence: Jeffrey's actions are viewed with concern by older, more mature people.

norm: It is rude to charge family for small things.
situation: Sally's sister was sick with the flu and could not cook or get to the store.
intention: Sally wants to get some dinner to her sister to be sure she gets well.
moral_action: Sally leaves the soup for sister and wishes tell her to get well.
moral_consequence: Sally's sister feels loved and enjoys her soup that night.
immoral_action: Sally asks her sister for $5.75 to cover the cost of the soup.
immoral_consequence: Sally's sister is irritated by Sally's request, and she doesn't even have any cash on hand to give Sally.

norm: You shouldn't serve people stale donuts.
situation: Sadie was working at a bakery when she realized the donuts in the display were stale.
intention: Sadie wants to get rid of the donuts.
moral_action: Sadie takes the donuts and throws them in the garbage.
moral_consequence: The customers at the shop are happy knowing that they will always get fresh donuts.
immoral_action: Sadie puts the donuts in the box of the next customer that orders a dozen.
immoral_consequence: The customer is upset and demands to get all their money back.

norm: It's wrong to blame your problems on other people.
situation: Joe recently developed a problem with alcohol that he's having trouble getting over.
intention: Joe wants to get over his alcholism.
moral_action: Joe decides to stop buying alcohol and has his wife keep his credit cards until the problem is fixed.
moral_consequence: Joe's wife is happy that Joe fixed the problem on his own using discipline.
immoral_action: Joe blames his wife for the problem and shames her into helping him.
immoral_consequence: Joe's wife begins to think that it was all her fault and feels intense guilt.

norm: It's wrong to insult another person's religious beliefs.
situation: Jack and Abhed are discussing their religious beliefs during a work lunch while having some beers.
intention: Jack wants to offer his perspective on religion.
moral_action: Jack explains that his perspective on religion stems around personal morality and that no religion is more right than another except to the individual.
moral_consequence: Jack and Abhed have a constructive conversation on religion and become closer friends.
immoral_action: Jack mentions that while people have the choice to practice whatever religion they want, only Christianity is the correct religion for humans one Earth.
immoral_consequence: Abhed takes extreme offence and tells Jack that they can no longer be friends and that he will tell HR about this comment.

norm: It's wrong to make people angry.
situation: Sam is having a tense debate with his friend Mike about abortion, and they have opposing views.
intention: Sam wants to end the argument.
moral_action: Sam tells Mike that he understands and appreciates his viewpoint even though they don't agree on this particular issue.
moral_consequence: Mike appreciates Sam's understanding attitude and feels good about their interaction.
immoral_action: Sam tells Mike that he's an idiot and his position is ridiculous.
immoral_consequence: Mike gets angry and yells back at Sam before storming away.

norm: You shouldn't give inappropriate gifts.
situation: It's Xmas time and Phil wants to give all of his friends gifts.
intention: Phil wants to give his friends great gifts.
moral_action: Phil goes through carefully and picks out a special gift for each friend.
moral_consequence: All of his friends love the gifts they received from Phil.
immoral_action: Phil buys all of his friends expensive gift cards to the same restruant.
immoral_consequence: Several of his friends don't eat the food they serve, some are allergic, and one is even suing that specific restruant.

norm: It's discouraged to play favorites with your grandchildren.
situation: Megan and Rafael have their three grandchildren at their house for their yearly Christmas party.
intention: Rafael wants to pass out gifts.
moral_action: Rafael makes sure to give each child one gift he picked out specifically for them.
moral_consequence: All of the children feel loved by Rafael and continue coming year after year.
immoral_action: Rafael gives two of the children two gifts each, but the other child ends up with six gifts to open.
immoral_consequence: Two of the children feel like they were only invited out of pity and over time stop attending the event.

norm: You shouldn't make people cry.
situation: Jill just lost a swim competition to a girl from another high school.
intention: Jill wants to feel better about losing.
moral_action: Jill privately tells her friends that she bets the winner takes steroids.
moral_consequence: Jill's friends say she's probably right so that she'll feel better.
immoral_action: Jill tells the winner that she looks fat and ugly in her swimsuit and the girl starts crying.
immoral_consequence: The referee yells at Jill for unsportsmanlike conduct and bans her from the next meet.

norm: You shouldn't make a commitment that you aren't sure about.
situation: Mary's birthday is coming and a birthday party will be held at her home.
intention: Jill, Mary's sister, wants to make the party more fun.
moral_action: Jill has practiced a song for a while and sings it in front of the guests at the party.
moral_consequence: Everyone is surprised by Jill's outstanding performance and enjoy the party very much.
immoral_action: Jill promises to make a birthday cake for Mary even though it is her first time making cake.
immoral_consequence: Everyone is disappointed at the taste of the cake.

norm: It is good to share your experiences.
situation: Joanna, who just got back from a long trip, is having dinner with her boyfriend Thomas, who's asking her about how her trip was.
intention: Joanna wants to answer Thomas' question.
moral_action: Joanna describes her trip in detail to Thomas, telling him all about what she did and where she went.
moral_consequence: Thomas is thrilled to hear about Joanna's travels and is glad she feet like she could be so open with him.
immoral_action: Joanna tells Thomas that the trip was fine and then quickly changes the conversation to another subject.
immoral_consequence: Thomas becomes suspicious, feeling like Joanna must have been up to something since she doesn't want to talk about her trip.

norm: It's wrong to spray someone with something without their consent.
situation: Ally is working at the perfume counter.
intention: Ally wants to sell perfume.
moral_action: Ally approaches a customer and asks if they would like to smell a sample on paper.
moral_consequence: The customer buys a large bottle and Ally gets a bonus.
immoral_action: Ally sees a potential customer approaching and sprays them with perfume.
immoral_consequence: The customer has an asthma attack and Ally is fired.

norm: You shouldn't rob people's houses.
situation: Andy has bills due soon and needs to come up with the money for them.
intention: Andy wants to pay off his bills.
moral_action: Andy works overtime to make enough money for his bills.
moral_consequence: Andy's bills are paid on time.
immoral_action: Andy sneaks into his neighbors’ house when they aren't home and takes their jewelry to sell off and pay his bills.
immoral_consequence: Andy is caught on security camera and sent to jail.

norm: You shoul not steal from people who trust you.
situation: Donald sees a computer game he really wants at his best friend John's house.
intention: Donald wants to take the game home to play it.
moral_action: Donald asks John if he can borrow the game for a few weeks.
moral_consequence: John lends Donald the game and feels happy to help a friend.
immoral_action: Donald puts the game in his backpack without telling John.
immoral_consequence: John later finds out the game is gone and loses trust in Donald.

norm: You shouldn't eat cream cheese by itself because it's fattening.
situation: Matt is feeling hungry and decides to browse the various foods he has available in his refrigerator.
intention: Matt wants to find something tasty to satisfy his hunger.
moral_action: Matt eats some veggies and hummus to satisfy his cravings for food.
moral_consequence: Matt feels happy, healthy, and satisfied and his weight remains unchanged.
immoral_action: Matt takes a tub of cream cheese from his fridge and eats the entire container with a spoon.
immoral_consequence: Matt feels guilty and a little sick, and he gains a small amount of weight due to his gluttony.

norm: It's good to report missing items to the proper people.
situation: While cleaning the school cafeteria, Gavin the janitor finds a wallet on the floor that belongs to a student named Dan.
intention: Gavin wants to move the wallet off the floor.
moral_action: Gavin takes the wallet to the school lost and found.
moral_consequence: Dan gets the wallet from the lost and found and thanks Gavin.
immoral_action: Gavin puts the wallet in his pocket and takes it home.
immoral_consequence: Dan never finds his wallet and has to get a new one.

norm: It's good to act mature.
situation: Tia was invited to her friend's birthday celebration dinner at a fancy restaurant.
intention: Tia wants to enjoy her night at the restaurant.
moral_action: Tia uses the correct forks during the dinner and makes sure she says please and thank you.
moral_consequence: Tia's friend's family is impressed with the manners that the young lady has and invites her over more often.
immoral_action: Tia orders a soda and slurps it very loudly during the meal.
immoral_consequence: Tia's family doesn't like her table manners, and she isn't invited to any more events.

norm: It is bad to spit on others.
situation: Carson was playing in the sand box at the park when another child joins him.
intention: Carson wants to play by himself.
moral_action: Carson leaves the sand box and goes to play on the swing set.
moral_consequence: Carson has a great time playing with himself at the park.
immoral_action: Carson spits at the other child who is sitting in the sand box with him.
immoral_consequence: Carson is removed from the sand box and told not to return to the park.

norm: You shouldn't be cold-hearted toward people.
situation: A bunch of coworkers go out drinking after learning some of them have been laid off.
intention: Jake wants to network to ensure his job security before the next downsizing.
moral_action: Jake listens empathetically to a coworker's frustrations about being fired.
moral_consequence: Jake learns a valuable lesson on how to handle the company VP one-on-one.
immoral_action: Jake turns his back to a former coworker and talks to everyone else.
immoral_consequence: The coworker doesn't contact Jake for the opportunity to join his well-funded start-up.

norm: Drinking too much is frowned upon.
situation: Dave goes to a party where there's a cooler full of alcohol for anyone who wants a drink.
intention: Dave wants to drink some alcohol.
moral_action: Dave grabs a cup and pours himself a glass of alcohol.
moral_consequence: There is plenty of drink left for the other people at the party.
immoral_action: Dave grabs several bottles and heroically drinks them all.
immoral_consequence: Other people at the party don't have anything to drink and get angry with Dave.

norm: It's rude to prevent someone from talking.
situation: Jocelyn and her friends are discussing politics, and she knows her friend Derek has strong views that oppose hers.
intention: Jocelyn wants her friends to be on her side rather than Derek's.
moral_action: Jocelyn lets Derek express his opinions and rebuts them with the best arguments she can think of.
moral_consequence: Jocelyn examines her own views and Derek's more closely and is able to develop stronger convictions and more nuanced opinions.
immoral_action: Jocelyn interrupts Derek every time he tries to say anything, so he doesn't get a chance to express his opinion.
immoral_consequence: Jocelyn's friends notice that Jocelyn is interrupting Derek and call her out for being rude and mean to Derek.

norm: You should coax your pets out of hiding with treats.
situation: Tracy has been trying for hours to find her cat, but it is nowhere to be seen.
intention: Tracy wants to get her cat to come out of hiding.
moral_action: Tracy puts some of the cat's favorite treats in a bowl and leaves them in the center of the room and just waits.
moral_consequence: The cat comes out of hiding and enjoys its treats and Tracy is relieved because she can see that her cat is safe.
immoral_action: Tracy starts banging on the floor and the walls near the cat's normal hiding places, hoping to flush it out.
immoral_consequence: The cat digs in deeper into its hiding place, feeling fear from all the loud banging, and Tracy is even more frustrated.

norm: It's wrong to abuse drugs to get by.
situation: Karen is having a stressful time in life.
intention: Karen wants to relax and cope.
moral_action: Karen makes an appointment with a therapist.
moral_consequence: Karen learns new healthy ways to cope and feels better.
immoral_action: Karen starts doing heroin to unwind.
