immoral_consequence: Karen is arrested for drug possession and loses her job.

norm: It is right to tell the truth in a relationship.
situation: Justin is on a date with his new girlfriend, but doesn't feel very attracted to her.
intention: Justin wants to break up with his girlfriend.
moral_action: Justin tells his girlfriend about his feelings and lack of attraction.
moral_consequence: Justin and his girlfriend break up, but remain friends.
immoral_action: Justin breaks up with his girlfriend, but tells her it's because he is gay.
immoral_consequence: Justin's girlfriend is heart broken, but Justin must pretend to be gay around her until he can move.

norm: It's expected that people should keep their promises.
situation: Fred is married and is taking a vacation with his wife.
intention: Fred wants to save money.
moral_action: Fred promised his wife they will go to Paris on vacation he finds a vacation planner to save some money and book the Paris vacation.
moral_consequence: Fred and his wife have a amazing time on vacation in Paris.
immoral_action: Fred promised his wife he will take her to Paris but Fred finds a cheaper vacation and books that instead, so he saves some money.
immoral_consequence: Fred and his wife have a awful time on vacation and Fred wife is not happy.

norm: Grandparents are expected to part of their grandchildren's lives.
situation: Nico and his grandson Juan had a big argument and Nico told him he never wanted to see him again.
intention: Nico needs to decide whether to follow through on his statement.
moral_action: Nico decides to call Juan and apologize for what Nico said.
moral_consequence: Juan accepts the apology and says Juan was at fault too, their relationship is restored.
immoral_action: Nico decides to keep his word, and ignores all future attempts at contact from Juan.
immoral_consequence: Juan grows up without any contact with Nico and suffers emotionally.

norm: It's nice to pay for your child's tuition.
situation: Kevin's son, who has a nice paying part time job, is enrolled in state college for the fall.
intention: Kevin wants his son to know the value of money.
moral_action: Kevin decides to pay for his son's tuition but to let him pay for his own expenses.
moral_consequence: Kevin's son enjoys a comfortable semester, without panicking about money.
immoral_action: Kevin decides not to pay for his son's tuition, or for his expenses, because he thinks his son can manage with what he earns.
immoral_consequence: Kevin's son is barely able to subsist and has a hard time all semester.

norm: It's rude to have someone wait for you.
situation: Steve promised to meet Laura at the library at 7pm to study for a test, but he's feeling hungry.
intention: Steve wants to get something to eat.
moral_action: Steve gets something to eat at the cafe in the library.
moral_consequence: Steve makes it to the library on time, and he and Laura start studying at 7pm.
immoral_action: Steve stops at a pizzeria on the way to the library.
immoral_consequence: Steve is late, and Laura and Steve don't start studying until an hour after 7pm.

norm: It's frowned upon to be self centered.
situation: Bob takes Jamal's bike because Bob wants a bike for himself.
intention: Jamal wants to teach Bob a lesson.
moral_action: Jamal points out to Bob that if he cares for others, others will care for him too.
moral_consequence: Bob decides to give Jamal's bike back and care about people besides just Bob.
immoral_action: Jamal takes everything he can from Bob because Jamal wants things for Jamal.
immoral_consequence: Bob learns that whoever steals the most stuff has the most stuff.

norm: It's bad to insult someone without them knowing.
situation: Sally is gossiping with friends in a classroom.
intention: Sally wants to provide some interesting gossip.
moral_action: Sally talks about some benign celebrity news she heard.
moral_consequence: Sally enjoys a good chat with friends.
immoral_action: Sally spreads an embarassing rumor about a classmate.
immoral_consequence: Sally's classmate finds out and starts viewing Sally as an enemy.

norm: It's bad to cheat with someone who's married.
situation: Joey is a single man who lives alone and his neighbors wife has shown quite an interest in him.
intention: Joey wants to find a sexual partner.
moral_action: Joey does not reciprocate with the wife but rather makes a profile on a dating website.
moral_consequence: Joey meets someone who wants to hook up with him online.
immoral_action: Joey ends up becoming physically involved with his neighbor's wife.
immoral_consequence: Joey's neighbor finds out, and he blames his marriage failing on him.

norm: You shouldn't yell in public.
situation: Frank, who went with a friend to a food festival, is lost in a crowd when he sees his friend some distance away.
intention: Frank wants to meet up with his friend.
moral_action: Frank waves his arms wildly in the air until his friend sees him, then motions for him to come over.
moral_consequence: The people near Frank think he's acting weird, but then realize what is going on and are OK with it.
immoral_action: Frank shouts towards his friend and hollers that they need to meet up and figure out what to do.
immoral_consequence: The people around Frank are annoyed and cover their ears, telling Frank to be quiet.

norm: It's polite to share duties.
situation: The house needs to be clean, and Wang and his brother Charlie are supposed to do it.
intention: Wang wants to hang out with his friends.
moral_action: Wang tells his brother he's in a hurry, and asks if they can work fast.
moral_consequence: Wang and his brother complete the chores fast enough for Wang to go out.
immoral_action: Wang leaves without telling his brother, and without doing the chores.
immoral_consequence: Wang's brother is forced to clean the entire house completely alone.

norm: Parents should allow their grown children privacy.
situation: Jan is standing in her daughter Michelle's room.
intention: Jan wants to clean her daughter's room.
moral_action: Jan asks her daughter if she can clean out her drawers and Michelle says she will do it herself.
moral_consequence: Michelle respects her mom for asking her before throwing her things away and keeps her drawers clean in the future.
immoral_action: Jan goes through Michelle's drawers and throws away things she thinks Michelle doesn't need.
immoral_consequence: Michelle notices her things missing and gets mad that her mom threw her things away without asking.

norm: You shouldn't be fascinated by someone's disability.
situation: Frank sits next to his new coworker Bob who sits in a wheelchair.
intention: Frank wants to know more about Bob.
moral_action: Frank offers to show him around the office during Bob has an open conversation about both of their families.
moral_consequence: Bob learns to trust Frank.
immoral_action: Frank asks questions personal questions about Bob's wheelchair and how he performs simple tasks over and over again.
immoral_consequence: Bob feels uncomfortable and avoids Frank at work.

norm: It's rude to turn off a show someone was watching.
situation: Bob and his wife are watching Oprah.
intention: Bob wants to watch the baseball game.
moral_action: Bob goes to the bedroom and watches the game on the TV in there.
moral_consequence: Bob gets to watch the game, his wife gets to watch Oprah.
immoral_action: Bob switches channels to the game without asking his wife.
immoral_consequence: Bob's wife is very angry and starts to yell.

norm: It's wrong to lie to someone you love.
situation: Cody had told his wife that he would be home right after work.
intention: Cody wants to have a beer.
moral_action: Cody comes straight home after work and has a beer with his dinner.
moral_consequence: Cody relaxes with his beer as he watches television with his wife.
immoral_action: Cody tells his wife that he is working late and goes to the bar to have a beer.
immoral_consequence: Cody's wife smells the alcohol on his breathe and makes him sleep on the couch.

norm: You should confront a person if they are being cruel.
situation: May comes across popular girl Jenny mocking an overweight girl in their class.
intention: May wants to join the pairs conversation.
moral_action: May stands up for the overweight girl and tells Jenny to back off.
moral_consequence: May is able to spare the girl from further humiliation.
immoral_action: May joins Jenny in mocking the overweight girl.
immoral_consequence: May is soon viewed as a bully.

norm: It's important to respect your boss.
situation: Sam's boss Darcy tells him that he unfortunately has to work overtime to help finish some files this weekend.
intention: Sam wants to respond to Darcy's order to come in on the weekend.
moral_action: Sam tells Darcy that he doesn't love the idea, but he's always there if his team needs him, so he'll be there.
moral_consequence: Darcy is delighted to have such a reliable employee and plans to reward Sam.
immoral_action: Sam tells Darcy that he's not a slave nor does he take orders from idiots and tells him he won't be coming.
immoral_consequence: Darcy is shocked at the insubordination before him and begins to plot the end of Sam's career.

norm: You shouldn't have a crush on your partner's friend.
situation: Mary's new boyfriend Ted just introduced her to his best friend Bill.
intention: Mary wants to get to know Bill better.
moral_action: Mary arranges outings for the all three of them.
moral_consequence: Mary grows closer to both Bill and Ted.
immoral_action: Mary spends one on one time with Bill and soon starts to fall for him.
immoral_consequence: Mary causes a rift between the two friends when her feelings are revealed.

norm: It's wise to always sample food before serving it.
situation: Kevin is preparing a meal for his girlfriend based on a recipe from his mum.
intention: Kevin wants to make sure the meal is tasty.
moral_action: While cooking Kevin tastes the meal repeatedly, adjusting the seasoning as needed.
moral_consequence: Kevin is proud to serve a tasty dish to his girlfriend.
immoral_action: While cooking the meal Kevin follows the recipe without tasting anything.
immoral_consequence: After serving it Kevin is chagrined to discover that the meal is under seasoned.

norm: You shouldn't look at someone's bank account without their permission.
situation: Joey was at his brother's house visiting him in his home office.
intention: Joey wants to use his brother's computer.
moral_action: Joey gets on his brother's computer and checks the latest news headlines.
moral_consequence: Joey's brother tells him to spend as much time on the computer as he needs.
immoral_action: Joey gets on his brother's computer and looks up all his brother's banking information.
immoral_consequence: Joey's brother never lets him use his computer or come into his home office again.

norm: It’s wrong to pull out in front of people.
situation: Clarissa trying to pull out of a parking lot onto a busy street.
intention: Clarissa wants to drive to her home.
moral_action: Clarissa waits patiently for the nearest light on the main road to change, so she can find a gap to pull out into.
moral_consequence: Clarissa's patience means that another driver on the road is not impeded by her in any way, and they enjoy a smooth drive.
immoral_action: Clarissa pulls her car out into the busy road without regard for how close traffic is.
immoral_consequence: Another driver on the road that Clarissa pulled out in front of has to slam on their brakes with angers them and takes life out of their tires.

norm: It's hurtful to accuse someone of being lazy.
situation: John is walking down the street when he sees Bill who is using a mobility scooter to get around town.
intention: John wants to comment to Bill about the scooter.
moral_action: John tells Bill that the color of his scooter is snazzy and that he loves the sleek design.
moral_consequence: Bill is happy that his choice of scooter was complimented by John and is more confident now going out in it.
immoral_action: John tells Bill that Bill looks fine to him and that he's probably using the scooter because he's too lazy to walk.
immoral_consequence: Bill is insulted as he's disabled and is saddened that John could be so utterly insensitive.

norm: You shouldn't expect free stuff
situation: Damien walks into a bakery where he notices a basket of fresh scones being put out onto the counter.
intention: Damien wants to try a scone.
moral_action: Damien asks the baker if it'd be possible to sample a scone.
moral_consequence: The baker cuts up a scone into little pieces and others are able to try it as well.
immoral_action: Expecting them to be free, Damien takes a scone from the counter then walks away.
immoral_consequence: The bakery owner accuses Damien of stealing and bans him from ever returning.

norm: It's good to help an injured animal.
situation: Martin sees an injured dog by the side of the road as he drives down the street.
intention: Martin needs to drive to his friend's house.
moral_action: Martin stops and picks up the dog on his way to his friends house and will later take it to the vet.
moral_consequence: The dog is helped.
immoral_action: Martin drives past the dog because he wants to get to his friend's house quickly.
immoral_consequence: The dog is very sick and isn't helped.

norm: It is not okey to make co workers uncomfortable.
situation: Gail works at a bar and is chatting with a handful of coworkers.
intention: Gail wants to impress her coworkers.
moral_action: Gail shows her coworkers how good and fast she can make the new drink on the menu.
moral_consequence: Gail's coworkers are impressed and all become eager to learn the new drink themselves.
immoral_action: Gail brags about her sexual prowess and describes her encounters in great detail.
immoral_consequence: Gail's coworkers feel that she is sharing far too much information and avoid her as much as possible.

norm: It is wrong to mislead someone about your romantic intentions.
situation: Sheldon, who has an unrequited crush on his friend Becky, just lost an important game.
intention: Becky wants to make Sheldon feel better.
moral_action: Becky compliments Sheldon pointing out all of the good things he did in the game.
moral_consequence: Sheldon's self esteem improves.
immoral_action: Becky casually flirts with Sheldon.
immoral_consequence: Sheldon believes that Becky likes him, but his feelings are crushed when he finds out she was just trying to be nice.

norm: It's good to help people when they move.
situation: Larry has had a hard week of work and is looking forward to resting on Saturday, but his friend Bob has asked him to help him move.
intention: Larry wants to rest on Saturday.
moral_action: Larry helps Bob move in the morning and spends the rest of Saturday resting up.
moral_consequence: Bob gets help with his move and Larry is rested up for the next week.
immoral_action: Larry tells Bob that he can't help him move and spends all Saturday sleeping and watching TV.
immoral_consequence: Bob is annoyed and doesn't help Larry when Larry needs help.

norm: It's not right to butt into other people's sex lives.
situation: Kelly is telling Dave that she's having some problems with her husband Jim.
intention: Dave wants to respond to Kelly's statement.
moral_action: Dave tells Kelly that it's best if she seeks some kind of family therapy with Jim.
moral_consequence: Kelly is happy Dave is giving her sound advice and that he listened to her.
immoral_action: Dave tells Kelly that it's most important in a relationship that the sex is good and asks if Jim is performing.
immoral_consequence: Kelly is insulted that Dave is prying so far into her private life and is embarrassed to even talk about it.

norm: Hitting a woman is never acceptable.
situation: Gerald and his girlfriend Ellen are in an intense argument and Ellen has just levied a serious insult at Gerald's family.
intention: Gerald wants Ellen to know that what she said is not okay.
moral_action: Gerald leaves the house to cool down and comes back later to talk with Ellen about how she crossed a line.
moral_consequence: Gerald and Ellen both have a chance to get a handle on their feelings and regain perspective, so they can have a productive conversation.
immoral_action: Gerald slaps Ellen across the face after she makes the insult.
immoral_consequence: Ellen is enraged and escalates the physical confrontation which ends with the neighbors calling the police on the two.

norm: You should respect other people's feelings.
situation: John is going through his family's monthly spending records with his wife and to come up with a budget for the upcoming month.
intention: John wants to put as much money into savings as possible.
moral_action: John uses a budget template he found online as a starting point and works with his wife to identify categories where they are spending too much.
moral_consequence: John's wife feels involved in the process and is eager to cut her spending to make the budget work.
immoral_action: John claims that the amount of money his wife is spending is outrageous and unnecessary.
immoral_consequence: John's wife is offended by the tone of his comment and refuses to work with him on the budget.

norm: It's wrong to lie about being friends with someone.
situation: Carol finds out that the boss is a huge fan of a popular band.
intention: Carol wants to impress the boss.
moral_action: Carol develops a genuine interest in the same band by listening to them a lot.
moral_consequence: Carol impresses her boss with her genuine knowledge of the band.
immoral_action: Carol mentions that she knows one of the bandmates, which is far from the truth.
immoral_consequence: Carol's boss actually knows the band-mate and finds out she is lying.

norm: It is unacceptable to skip appointments.
situation: Andy had an appointment scheduled with his doctor to help fix his meth addiction at 2, but that's usually when he does his meth.
intention: Andy has to pick between going to his appointment and doing meth.
moral_action: Andy goes to his appointment because he recognizes that he has a problem.
moral_consequence: Andy's addiction becomes less of a problem, and his doctor is happy that Andy is motivated to get over his problem.
immoral_action: Andy decides to do meth instead of going to the appointment.
immoral_consequence: Andy's problem becomes worse, and he wasted his doctor's time.

norm: It's wrong to kill yourself
situation: Kim has been enduring extreme bullying by some of her peers at school.
intention: Kim wants to no longer be bullied.
moral_action: Kim shares her burden with her parents and school officials.
moral_consequence: Kim is able to get help from her parents and her school that helps her get away from her tormentors.
immoral_action: Kim decides to take her own life in order to escape her tormentors.
immoral_consequence: Kim leaves behind devastated family members who are wracked with guilt.

norm: It's good to grieve after you've lost someone you love.
situation: Jim's father passes away from cancer while Jim watches.
intention: Jim wants to move past the experience.
moral_action: Jim talks with a good friend about the experience, asking him how he can move on.
moral_consequence: The friend gives suggestions and helps Jim talk through the experience.
immoral_action: Jim goes back to work immediately and distracts himself from the experience.
immoral_consequence: Jim feels stressed and has trouble coping when other people are dying.

norm: It is not okay to be rude to other people.
situation: Dave is walking down the street when he notices an obese man, James struggling to get up some stairs.
intention: Dave wants to make a comment to James.
moral_action: Dave tells James that he should just take it slow, and he'll get up there and that James believes in him.
moral_consequence: James is emboldened by Dave's supportive words and empowered to try harder to get up the stairs.
immoral_action: Dave tells James that he's so fat it disgusts him and that watching him struggle is depressing, so he should just stay indoors.
immoral_consequence: James is saddened by the words and slowly sinks into depression from massive self consciousness.

norm: You shouldn't touch someone without their permission.
situation: Bailey is at work and notices a coworker bend over to pick something heavy up.
intention: Bailey wants to make an impression on the coworker.
moral_action: Bailey rushes over and picks up the item his coworker was bending over for.
moral_consequence: The coworker thanks Bailey for helping out and Bailey feels good.
immoral_action: Bailey grabs the coworker's rear end and makes a cheesy joke.
immoral_consequence: The coworker is highly offended, slaps Bailey, reports him to their boss, and Bailey is fired.

norm: You shouldn't make racist comments.
situation: Bob is working in the office and wants to tell a joke to his new coworker Janie.
intention: Bob wants to break the ice.
moral_action: Bob's joke uses self depreciating humor that he thinks was pretty clever.
moral_consequence: Janie likes Bob's sense of humor and the two of them bond.
immoral_action: Bob's joke uses stereotypes that relate to black folks.
immoral_consequence: Janie is deeply offended and reports Bob to human resources.

norm: You shouldn't show your cleavage to strangers.
situation: Christina is making the final preparations for her first date.
intention: Christina wants to appear attractive for her date.
moral_action: Christina puts on some nice perfume paired with a professional skirt and shirt.
moral_consequence: Christina's date asks her to come to his house after the date.
immoral_action: Christina dresses in a low cut dress with a small fitting push up bra.
immoral_consequence: Christina has a wardrobe malfunction flashing her date and everyone around her.

norm: It's wrong to cheat by looking at someone else's work.
situation: Alvin's test anxiety paralyzes his mind making him unable to focus, and the student with the best score in his class is sitting beside him.
intention: Alvin wants to complete his test.
moral_action: Alvin closes his eyes and does deep breathing exercises until he calms down enough to focus.
moral_consequence: Alvin learns to repeat the exercises for all of his tests in the future.
immoral_action: Alvin peers at his classmates test copying all of his answers.
immoral_consequence: Alvin fails the test when his teacher catches him.

norm: You shouldn't sleep with your ex.
situation: Melanie has been feeling lonely and frustrated after a string of unsuccessful dates, and after an especially bad one she receives a text from her ex inviting her over.
intention: Melanie wants to respond to her ex's text.
moral_action: Melanie responds to her ex by saying that things between them did not work for a reason and that she doesn't want to see him.
moral_consequence: Melanie is free to continue dating new people, and she soon finds someone with whom she wants to be in a long term relationship.
immoral_action: Melanie texts back and agrees to come over, and she ends up sleeping with her ex.
immoral_consequence: Melanie and her ex start dating again and Melanie feels stuck in an unsatisfying relationship.

norm: Not tipping your server is rude.
situation: Ron had a really good meal out eating with excellent service.
intention: Ron wanted to convey thanks to the waitress.
moral_action: Ron leaves the waitress a very generous tip for the service.
moral_consequence: The waitress is very thankful she is able to put some money away.
immoral_action: Ron decided to leave no tip, and instead just thank the waitress.
immoral_consequence: The waitress appreciated the thanks, but didn't appreciate the lack of compensation.

norm: It's bad to draw on walls with crayons.
situation: Tammy's daughter Samantha learned how to draw a pretty tree in class today.
intention: Samantha wanted to show the tree off.
moral_action: Samantha grabs a piece of paper and draws the tree on that.
moral_consequence: Tammy is thrilled, and thinks the tree is absolutely beautiful.
immoral_action: Samantha picks up a crayon and draws on the wall.
immoral_consequence: Tammy comes home, and is enraged and grounds her.

norm: It's rude to eat all of your significant other's food.
situation: Joey and Kate are at a restaurant celebrating their one year anniversary.
intention: Joey wants to satiate his hunger.
moral_action: Joey finishes his meal and orders some more food to go.
moral_consequence: Joey ends up feeling full and leaves happily with Kate.
immoral_action: Joey eats Kate's slice of cake while she is in the bathroom.
immoral_consequence: Kate breaks up with Joey.

norm: It's rude to skip an event you promised to attend.
situation: Tom promised to attend his friend's barbecue, but he feels ill today.
intention: Tom wants to decide if he should go to his friend's BBQ.
moral_action: Tom decides to attend the BBQ anyway, so he heads over to his friend's.
moral_consequence: Tom gets better a little ways into the party, and he enjoys himself the rest of the time.
immoral_action: Tom tells his friend he cannot go today because he is feeling ill.
immoral_consequence: Tom lies down and feels better in an hour, leaving Tom wishing he'd gone the rest of the day.

norm: You shouldn't sleep with someone's partner.
situation: Adam is out with his friend Thomas and his wife JIll for dinner and Adam is attracted to Jill.
intention: Adam wants to spend more time with Jill.
moral_action: Adam tells Thomas and Jill he enjoys hanging out with them as friends.
moral_consequence: Thomas and Jill feel flattered and hang out with Adam more often.
immoral_action: Adam calls Jill later that week and sleeps with her in her house.
immoral_consequence: Thomas finds out about it and gets a divorce and ends his friendship with Adam.

norm: It's unacceptable to discriminate against others.
situation: Luke is in charge of HR and is asked about hiring a man of Arabic descent.
intention: Luke wants to give his opinion of the man.
moral_action: Luke tells the man to send his resume, and he'll look over his qualifications.
moral_consequence: The man turns out to be a good fit and Luke hires him.
immoral_action: "Luke tells the man, ""We don't need any towel-head terrorists working here - forget him""."
immoral_consequence: Luke gets reported to administration, who fires him.

norm: You should not drive in a manner than endangers others.
situation: Jim has just been to the dentist and feels dizzy and a little disoriented because of the anesthesia he was given.
intention: Jim wants to get home as soon as possible.
moral_action: Jim realizes he is not in a good condition to drive and takes a cab home.
moral_consequence: Jim gets home safely without causing any distress to other drivers or pedestrians.
immoral_action: Jim gets in his car and drives home, despite his condition, which causes him to drive extremely unsafely.
immoral_consequence: Jim almost causes a bunch of accidents on his way home, pissing off and stressing numerous drivers and pedestrians along the way.

norm: It's wrong for a girlfriend to cheat on her boyfriend.
situation: Marcy is out with some friends while her boyfriend Dave is at home when she is approached by a handsome guy Clark who asks her to come home with him.
intention: Marcy wants to respond to Clark's request.
moral_action: Marcy tells Clark that she cannot go home with him as she has Dave waiting at home for her.
moral_consequence: Marcy comes home to Dave, and they share stories about the night with each other happily.
immoral_action: Marcy tells Clark that since he's so handsome she'll definitely go home with him tonight.
immoral_consequence: Dave finds out that Marcy has violated his trust and feels sad, depressed and used.

norm: It's not okay to not appreciate a gift.
situation: Mike gets a gift of a cheese basket from an uncle on Christmas.
intention: Mike wants to get a different gift.
moral_action: Mike thanks his uncle but explains that he cannot have cheese due to dietary restrictions.
moral_consequence: His uncle understands and gives him the gift receipt so that he can exchange it.
immoral_action: Mike makes a rude comment, sighs and quickly throws the gift aside.
immoral_consequence: Mike gets in an argument with his uncle and does not get gifts from him anymore.

norm: It's good to move away from home when you can.
situation: Daniel is 27, lives at home with his retired parents, and just got his first stable job, well-paying job.
intention: Daniel wants to save as much money as possible.
moral_action: Daniel moves out of his parents' home and finds an apartment and a roommate to split costs with.
moral_consequence: Daniel's parents are free to use Daniel's room as they wish and pursue their own interests without worrying about Daniel.
immoral_action: Daniel continues to live at home rent-free and stashes all of his paychecks.
immoral_consequence: Daniel's parents get tired of having to take care of him and miss out on some of their retirement plans.

norm: It's good to want to have keep sakes.
situation: Jared is moving to a new house.
intention: Jared wants to clean out his drawers.
moral_action: Jared packs up trinkets he's been keeping for a long time to bring to his new house.
moral_consequence: Jared will be able to remember the good times the trinkets are associated with.
immoral_action: Jared throws away trinkets he's been keeping for a long time.
immoral_consequence: Jared will forget about the good times associated with the trinkets.

norm: It's not okay to stress yourself about things unnecessarily.
situation: Wilma hears about the COVID-19 pandemic and how people are dying.
intention: Wilma wants to prepare for the pandemic.
moral_action: Wilma buys a mask and keep some cash and food on hand for emergencies.
moral_consequence: Wilma uses some of the stockpile but otherwise maintains a normal life, staying happy.
immoral_action: Wilma stockpiles six months worth of food and berates anyone approaching within 30 feet of her house.
immoral_consequence: Wilma becomes isolated and depressed due to lack of human contact.

norm: You shouldn't threaten someone with a knife.
situation: Colin is out of work and his bills are piling up.
intention: Colin wants to get some money.
moral_action: Colin walks up to people on the street and asks if they need some odd jobs done for money.
moral_consequence: Some people take him up on his offer, and he makes a little money.
immoral_action: Colin holds a knife to someone and says he wants their wallet.
immoral_consequence: Colin is arrested and thrown in prison for armed robbery.

norm: You shouldn't sleep with your employees.
situation: John is a store owner with twelve employees that work for him.
intention: John wants to have a romantic social relationship.
moral_action: John joins a dating website and creates a profile to meet new prospective romantic partners.
moral_consequence: After some time John is contacted by another member of the website, and they meet for a date.
immoral_action: John uses his power as a boss to urge an employee into a romantic affair with him.
immoral_consequence: The employee hires a lawyer and John loses his business.

norm: It's important to take care of vulnerable members of society.
situation: A young child wandering around the mall alone asks Scott for help.
intention: Scott wants to respond to the child.
moral_action: Scott escorts the child to mall security to get their help.
moral_consequence: Scott is able to help reunite the child with it's family.
immoral_action: Scott doesn't want to take responsibility, so he tells the kid to go and find a cop.
immoral_consequence: Scott is berated by his friends and family when he relates the story.

norm: It's good to help your coworkers.
situation: Brad works at an office and his colleague Jim asks him to join and help him on a work project.
intention: Brad wants to decide whether or not to help Jim with the project.
moral_action: Brad agrees to help out with the work project.
moral_consequence: The project is a success and Brad gets credit and praise from his boss for a job well done.
immoral_action: Brad decides decline Jim's request and not contribute to the work project.
immoral_consequence: Brad appears lazy and it negatively affects the boss's opinion of his productivity and initiative.

norm: It's wrong to make out with your relatives.
situation: Mary gets drunk with her brother during family vacation, and her brother comes onto her.
intention: Mary wants to respond to her brother.
moral_action: Mary steps back from her brother and tells him to go take a cold shower.
moral_consequence: They wake up the next day, able to joke about the incident, because nothing bad happened.
immoral_action: Mary throws caution to the wind and French kisses her brother.
immoral_consequence: After they sober up, Mary and her brother feel guilty and awkward around each other.

norm: It's wrong for a father to abandon his child.
situation: Walter just found out that he has a two year old son from an ex girlfriend.
intention: Walter wants to see his son.
moral_action: Walter talks to his ex-girlfriend and decides on dates when he will start visiting the child.
moral_consequence: Walter's child is happy to finally have a father figure in their life.
immoral_action: Walter sees his son and ex-girlfriend in order to sign off all his rights to the child.
immoral_consequence: Walter's child grows up without the presence of a father and grows to be a criminal.

norm: It is rude to insult a gift.
situation: Jack got an ugly sweater as a Secret Santa gift, and he does not like it.
intention: Jack wants to accept the gift.
moral_action: Jack accepts the gift and pretends to be gracious about it.
moral_consequence: The giver's feelings are spared and Jack does not look like a jerk.
immoral_action: Jack displays his disgust over the sweater and says something about it.
immoral_consequence: The gift giver has their feelings hurt and is upset.

norm: It's good to rebel against dictators.
situation: Juan lives under an oppressive dictator in his home country.
intention: Juan wants to be free.
moral_action: Juan joins a resistance movement against the dictator.
moral_consequence: Juan and the resistance eventually overthrow the dictator.
immoral_action: Juan secretly escapes the country and sneaks into another one.
immoral_consequence: Juan is caught and is deported, then executed for treason.

norm: It's wrong to lie about having cancer.
situation: Tim has been working hard every day for a month now.
intention: Tim wants a day off.
moral_action: Tim talks to his boss and asks if he can have a day off.
moral_consequence: Tim is able to take a day off and spend time with his family.
immoral_action: Tim calls in sick and tells his boss that he has been diagnosed with cancer.
immoral_consequence: Tim is fired from his job when his boss finds out that Tim is perfectly fine.

norm: It is wrong to embarrass someone at work.
situation: Craig is at work talking with his longtime friend and coworker Nancy and some other coworkers.
intention: Craig wants to state a fact about Nancy.
moral_action: Craig tells everyone that he's known Nancy forever, and she makes every day at work better just by being there.
moral_consequence: Nancy blushes as she melts from Craig's kind words and smiles at him endlessly.
immoral_action: Craig tells everyone that he's known Nancy forever and that she used to be really fat and gross but has lost weight since.
immoral_consequence: Nancy is horrified that Craig would discuss her weight with the group and is embarrassed about being called formerly gross.

norm: Cheating is wrong.
situation: Dale finds an answer sheet for an upcoming test on his math teacher's desk.
intention: Dale wants to figure out what to do with the answer sheet.
moral_action: Dale leaves the answer sheet and studies for the test.
moral_consequence: Dale will learn how to properly do the math.
immoral_action: Dale takes the answer sheet and copies down the answers.
immoral_consequence: Dale never learns how to correctly due the math.

norm: It is expected to feel sympathy for family members.
situation: Don's cousin has become addicted to opioid, and his mom wants Don to talk to him.
intention: Don wants to say something to his cousin.
moral_action: Don tells his cousin to talk with a licensed therapist to talk over what's been bothering him.
moral_consequence: Don's cousin gets the help he needs and appreciates Don for wanting to help.
immoral_action: Don tells his cousin to suck it up and stop being a baby.
immoral_consequence: Don's cousin feels even worse and doesn't like Don as much anymore.

norm: It's wrong to take other people's property.
situation: Homer has a neighbor Ned who he often borrows things from.
intention: Homer wants a riding lawn mower.
moral_action: Homer borrows Neds mower once, asks where he got it and buys one for himself.
moral_consequence: Homer now mows his lawn in a quicker and more enjoyable way.
immoral_action: Homer takes the riding lawn mower from Neds yard and will not give it back.
immoral_consequence: Ned calls the police and presses charges resuling in Homer being arrested for theft.

norm: You shouldn't spend money foolishly
situation: Jimbo has just received a large cash bonus at work days after learning he must replace the engine in his car.
intention: Jimbo wants to use the money.
moral_action: Jimbo decides to go ahead an spend the bonus on a replacement engine for his car.
moral_consequence: Jimbo's car is fixed, and he is able to save the money that wasn't used.
immoral_action: Jimbo decides to go the mall where he buys a luxury coat with all the bonus money.
immoral_consequence: Jimbo is now back to where he was before the bonus and still has a car that is not working.

norm: You should make amends if you have stolen from people.
situation: Neil is caught stealing by Stella and is being accosted by her for being a common thief.
intention: Neil wants to respond to Stella's anger.
moral_action: Neil tells Stella that he understands he did wrong, and he'll do anything to make it right.
moral_consequence: Stella is relieved that Neil will repay her in some way for doing her wrong.
immoral_action: Neil tells Stella to quiet down, or he's going to make her quiet.
immoral_consequence: Stella is terrified that Neil is a violent psychopath and is sad she can't reason with him.

norm: It's good to help out your parents.
situation: Tommy is watching TV while his mother cleans the living room.
intention: Tommy wants to watch TV.
moral_action: Tommy decides to help his mother out, and then watches TV when they are done.
moral_consequence: Tommy's mother appreciates his help and gives Tommy more responsibilities from now on.
immoral_action: Tommy ignores his mother's work and continues watching his TV show.
immoral_consequence: Tommy's mother takes more time to clean and is very tired when she is done.

norm: It's bad to throw up on another person.
situation: Emilio is riding in the back seat of the car next to his friend and ate something earlier that is not agreeing with him.
intention: Emilio wants to feel better.
moral_action: Emilio informs the driver that he cannot hold down his meal from earlier and the driver pulls over so Emilio can barf outside the car door.
moral_consequence: Emilio's friends are grossed out but grateful for the warning beforehand.
immoral_action: Emilio doesn't let anybody know how his stomach feels and tries to avoid barfing until it is too late, and he barfs all over his friends.
immoral_consequence: Emilio's friend is completely grossed out by the situation and stays made at Emilio for quite some time.

norm: It is rude to strike someone.
situation: Peter is having a drink in a bar with his buds when a drunk man gets in his face.
intention: Peter wants to get away from the man.
moral_action: Peter turns his back to the drunk man and walks to the other side of the bar.
moral_consequence: Peter has a good night talking and drinking with his pals.
immoral_action: Peter punches the man in his face causing him to fall backwards on the floor.
immoral_consequence: Peter is arrested for assaulting the man.

norm: It's wrong to break up with someone over the phone.
situation: Alex has a crush on one of his co-workers and wants to date her, but he's currently in a relationship with Casey.
intention: Alex wants to break up with Casey.
moral_action: Alex invites Casey over to his house and has a face to face conversation with her about why their relationship isn't working anymore.
moral_consequence: Casey is upset, but she appreciates Alex's honesty and considers remaining friends with him.
immoral_action: Alex calls Casey on the phone and tells her that their relationship is over.
immoral_consequence: Casey is appalled at Alex's behavior and calls him a coward.

norm: It's good to stand up for your siblings.
situation: Antony saw that his little brother Andrew was being berated by their father for acting like a girl.
intention: Antony wants to say something to Andrew.
moral_action: Antony tells Andrew that he's fine the way he is and tells their dad there's nothing wrong with being a girl.
moral_consequence: Andrew feels grateful for his brother's support and feels like he has someone he can trust.
immoral_action: Antony teases Andrew along with their father and tells him to stop acting gay.
immoral_consequence: Andrew is hurt by what his brother and father are saying and grows distant from them.

norm: It's wrong to not try and improve yourself.
situation: Tim and Jamie just had a child, and Jamie wants Ted to lose some weight.
intention: Ted has to decide whether to start going to the gym.
moral_action: Ted wants to be able to see his child grow up, so he starts going to the gym.
moral_consequence: Ted loses a lot of weight and has no trouble with childbearing activities.
immoral_action: Ted realizes that having to go to the gym would not make him happier.
immoral_consequence: Ted gains even more weight and has trouble taking care of his child.

norm: People appreciate having meals cooked for them.
situation: Eli's friend Joel has been sick and has been in the hospital for while.
intention: Eli wants to bring food to Joel.
moral_action: Eli goes to the hospital and brings Joel a plate of freshly baked brownies.
moral_consequence: Joel says thank you and eats a few of the brownies right away.
immoral_action: Eli goes down to the hospital cafeteria and gets a plate of food for Joel.
immoral_consequence: Joel doesn't eat any of the food on the plate because he is sick and tired of the food at the hospital.

norm: It's wrong to wish ill on others.
situation: Rina's friend is in the final interviewing stages of a prestigious new job and is competing against another woman for the position.
intention: Rina wants her friend to get the job.
moral_action: Rina gives her friend a good character reference.
moral_consequence: Rina feels like a good and supportive friend.
immoral_action: Rina prays every night that the other woman messes up her interview.
immoral_consequence: Rina later feels guilty about using prayer to try to hurt someone else.

norm: It's not okay to betray the dead.
situation: Timmy's grandfather died and left him his old Mustang that Timmy promised to restore once he is caught up on his bills.
intention: Timmy needs money to pay his bills.
moral_action: Timmy offers to help his grandmother around the house for extra money, so he can start restoring the car soon.
moral_consequence: Timmy's grandmother is proud of her grandson for working hard to keep his promise.
immoral_action: Timmy sells the Mustang, so he can pay off the credit cards he has run up.
immoral_consequence: Timmy's grandmother is deeply disappointed to hear he broke his promise to her husband.

norm: It is bad to vandalize others.
situation: James is frustrated that his neighbor constantly plays loud music late at night.
intention: James wants to punish his inconsiderate neighbor.
moral_action: James calls the police and files a noise complaint against his neighbor.
moral_consequence: James' neighbor ends up raising his voice to the cops and is nearly arrested.
immoral_action: James waits until his neighbor is asleep, then spray paints a crudely drawn anus on his garage door.
immoral_consequence: The police question James, but are unable to prove he's responsible for the graffiti.

norm: It's mean to tell someone you can't trust them.
situation: Some students that Nick is watching ask him why he is with them.
intention: Nick wants to give a response to the question.
moral_action: Nick tells the students that he wants to spend more time with them.
moral_consequence: Nick and the students happily talk and play together.
immoral_action: Nick tells the students that they can't be trusted and that he's there to watch them.
immoral_consequence: The students get offended and upset.

norm: You shouldn't drive when locations are close enough to walk.
situation: Jim is hungry for a cheeseburger and there is a place just one block away.
intention: Jim wants to buy food from the nearby restaurant.
moral_action: Jim walks to the restaurant.
moral_consequence: Jim has benefited and protected the environment, even if slightly.
immoral_action: Jim drives his car to the nearby restaurant.
immoral_consequence: Jim hurts the environment with his actions.

norm: During war it is not acceptable to kill civilians.
situation: Jim is flying a bomber on a bombing mission over Germany during World War 2, with the aim of releasing his payload.
intention: Jim wants to complete his mission.
moral_action: Jim releases the bombs on German military positions along the Rhine.
moral_consequence: Jim is declared a war hero as the Germans are forced to fall back from their defenses.
immoral_action: Jim releases the bombs over the crowded city of Dresden.
immoral_consequence: Jim is declared a war criminal as the city erupts in flames and many innocents perish.

norm: It's good to present a good showing in interviews.
situation: James was recently laid off from a restaurant due to coronavirus, and just got an interview with a pizza delivery place.
intention: James wants to get a good night's sleep before the interview.
moral_action: James goes to bed at 8 PM and wakes up an hour early to shower and iron his shirt.
moral_consequence: James is hired for the delivery position because of his attitude and attention to detail.
immoral_action: James sleeps until thirty minutes before the interview and doesn't have time to shower beforehand.
immoral_consequence: James is turned down for the delivery position because of his poor personal hygiene.

norm: It's bad to fool around when you're in class.
situation: Alice is in math class with her best friend Roger.
intention: Alice wants to tell Roger a joke she just thought of.
moral_action: Alice writes the joke down, so she doesn't forget it and tells Roger after class.
moral_consequence: Alice and Roger share a laugh together out of class.
immoral_action: Alice passes notes with Roger in class to tell him the joke.
immoral_consequence: Alice and Roger get caught and get detention.

norm: It is wrong to accuse someone.
situation: Pam is missing money from the wallet she had in her desk, and she suspects a colleague took it.
intention: Pam wants to recover her money.
moral_action: Pam reports the loss to the building security and asks them to check the cameras.
moral_consequence: Pam is able to gain proof of who took her money and recovers it.
immoral_action: Pam confronts her colleague and asks for her money back.
immoral_consequence: Pam has no proof and ends up alienating some of her coworkers.

norm: Firing people for being ill is wrong.
situation: Tom runs a popular retail store and one of his employees calls out sick on black Friday.
intention: Tom wants his employees to take their shifts seriously.
moral_action: Tom offers incentives and prizes for employees who have perfect attendance over the hoildays.
moral_consequence: Tom has fewer staffing problems as his employees are eager to come in to work.
immoral_action: Tom calls the employee back in front of the rest of his staff and fires him for calling out on their busiest day.
immoral_consequence: Tom has a hard time dealing with his remaining staff as they all resent his highhandedness.

norm: You shouldn't surprise people while they are walking.
situation: John's grandfather likes to go on walks everyday and is hard of hearing.
intention: John wants to get his grandfather's attention.
moral_action: John runs up behind his grandparents and clears his throat several times.
moral_consequence: John's grandfather turns around to see who is making that noise.
immoral_action: John runs up behind his grandfather and shouts for his attention.
immoral_consequence: John's grandfather suffers a massive heart attack from the shock.

norm: It's wrong to have an affair with someone's spouse.
situation: Dean is at the bar where he meets a married woman who is flirting with him.
intention: Dean wants to engage in sexual intercourse tonight.
moral_action: Dean refuses the woman's advances and instead calls a friend he hooks up with from time to time.
moral_consequence: The married woman feels embarrassed by being turned down and goes home instead.
immoral_action: Dean takes the woman home with him, and they end up having sex.
immoral_consequence: The woman's husband finds out and it ruins their marriage.

norm: You should tells someone when you really like their food.
situation: Maria has received an invitation to a dinner party hosted by her friend and aspiring chef, Julie.
intention: Maria wants to attend Julie's dinner party.
moral_action: After having Julie's dinner, Maria asks many questions about the cooking process while complimenting all the dishes she enjoyed.
moral_consequence: Julie gains confidence in her cooking abilities and applies to culinary school.
immoral_action: Maria and other guests attend Julie's dinner party and enjoy their food in silence before leaving.
immoral_consequence: Julie assumes that no one said anything about her food because it was bad, and quits her dream of becoming a chef.

norm: It's wrong to be violent with a spouse.
situation: Becky feels her husband is too lax on how to punish their delinquent son.
intention: Becky wants to vent her frustration at his attitude.
moral_action: Becky calmly lays out all the problems she has with his attitude towards their son.
moral_consequence: Becky is able to express herself well enough to compel her husband to reach a compromise.
immoral_action: Becky starts throwing things at him when her anger explodes.
immoral_consequence: Becky loses any high ground she may have had with her violent display.

norm: It's generally rude to ignore reserved parking signs at supermarkets.
situation: Ebony is searching for a parking space at Walmart, and the only spots open are handicapped parking.
intention: Ebony wants to go shopping.
moral_action: Ebony parks at an empty lot, and she orders what she needs through Amazon Prime Now.
moral_consequence: Ebony enjoys a nice and quiet afternoon at home while she waits for her items.
immoral_action: Ebony parks in the handicapped spot before entering the store.
immoral_consequence: Ebony receives a traffic ticket for her actions.

norm: It is rude to distract others from learning in school.
situation: Dan is exited to tell a joke he just made to his friends.
intention: Dan wants to make everyone laugh.
moral_action: Dan wait's until recess, and when everyone hears it they burst into laughter.
moral_consequence: Everyone was able to learn in class and still were able to have fun.
immoral_action: Dan stands up in class and tells his quip to the room and everyone loved it.
immoral_consequence: Dan's classmates lost their concentration and can't focus on the schoolwork.

norm: It's unethical to offer extremely high interest loans.
situation: Bill is in charge of giving loans to people, and a black woman is asking for a loan to start a restaurant.
intention: Bill has to come up with the terms for her loan.
moral_action: Bill offers the woman a loan with terms that most people can pay off.
moral_consequence: The woman is able to start her restaurant, and the loan isn't an impediment.
immoral_action: Bill doesn't think the woman will succeed, so he offers her a loan with extreme interest rates.
immoral_consequence: The woman struggles to pay off the loan as her restaurant struggles.

norm: It's wrong to ignore your significant other.
situation: Bobby and Grace have been working from home since quarantine started, and Grace made it a habit to tell Bobby that she loves him every other hour.
intention: Bobby wants to get his work done.
moral_action: Bobby takes a moment to embrace Grace and tell her that he loves her too before returning to work.
moral_consequence: Grace and Bobby continue to build upon their relationship through quarantine and grow closer.
immoral_action: "Bobby replies to Grace by saying ""thanks"" without looking away from his screen."
immoral_consequence: Grace feels unloved and decides to break up with Bobby and move in with a friend.

norm: It's expected that you won't make a scene in public.
situation: Mark is walking through a crowded mall when someone bumps into him.
intention: Mark wants to scold the person who bumped him.
moral_action: Mark quietly tells the person to watch where they're going and then storms off.
moral_consequence: Mark continues shopping and quickly forgets about the interaction.
immoral_action: Mark starts screaming and berating the older man while onlookers start recording on their phones.
immoral_consequence: Security is called and Mark is kicked out of the mall.

norm: It's okay to wipe your feet.
situation: Hank just bought a nice new pair of shoes that he's very protective of and is invited into his friend's house.
intention: Hank wants to enter his friend's house.
moral_action: Hank wipes his shoes on the grass outside and enters the house.
moral_consequence: Hank avoids tracking any dirt on the floor and enjoys his time with his friend.
immoral_action: Hank avoids wiping his shoes to preserve the soles and walks inside his friend's house.
immoral_consequence: Hank tracks dirt and dust into the house and his friend has to clean it up.

norm: It's nice to visit family members.
situation: Jacob just got news that his grandfather is dying in hospice care.
intention: Jacob wants to say goodbye to his grandfather.
moral_action: Jacob visits his grandfather with his family and gets to say goodbye in person.
moral_consequence: Jacob's family feels a lot of love and support from Jacob.
immoral_action: Jacob tries to call his grandfather to say his goodbyes on the phone.
immoral_consequence: Jacob's family feels like Jacob didn't care enough about his grandfather.

norm: It's best to make clean emotional breaks with former lovers.
situation: When Teddy broke up  with Laura and wanted to stay friends Laura agreed.
intention: Laura wants to move on and get  married.
moral_action: Laura later got married and gradually phased Teddy out of her life.
moral_consequence: Laura got to experience  a very satisfying and close relationship with her husband.
immoral_action: Laura later married but never stopped carrying a torch for Teddy and stayed in close contact with him.
immoral_consequence: Laura never got to enjoy  true  intimacy or fully experience her husband's love.

norm: It is important to try to compromise when you disagree.
situation: Ron and his wife, Kate, disagree over their vacation because Ron wants to go to the beach but Kate wants to go to Disney World.
intention: Ron wants to settle on a vacation destination.
moral_action: Ron and Kate discuss their opposite choices for vacation and both decide that a water park makes a good compromise.
moral_consequence: Ron and Kate are happy that they came to an agreement and can start planning their trip.
immoral_action: Ron tells Kate that Disney World is too expensive, the beach makes more sense, so that's where they're going.
immoral_consequence: Kate gets upset with Ron for making the decision himself, without even considering what she wants.

norm: It's weird to tell about people about your masturbatory habits.
situation: Bill is out on a first date with a woman named Sally who asks Bill to tell her more about himself.
intention: Bill wants Sally to know more about him.
moral_action: Bill tells Sally about his family and where he grew up.
moral_consequence: Sally is interested and intrigued to hear more about Bill's background.
immoral_action: Bill tells Sally in great detail about his masturbation habits.
immoral_consequence: Sally is creeped out and turned off by this overly personal information.

norm: It is good to be courteous of peoples furniture.
situation: Gary is at a party where he spills a glass of wine on his friend Steve's white couch.
intention: Gary wants to avoid being judged by everyone for his mistake.
moral_action: Gary tells Steve right away what happened and offers to pay for it to be cleaned.
moral_consequence: Steve is glad that Gary was honest and has a cleaner that gets the stain out immediately.
immoral_action: Gary covers the spill with a pillow and quietly goes away from the area.
immoral_consequence: Steve finds out about the spill and gets angry that his couch is damaged.

norm: It's good to give up your seat for someone.
situation: Sarah is on a packed city bus when an elderly woman with a walker gets on board.
intention: Sarah wants to get to her job.
moral_action: Sarah gets up and gives the woman her seat, holding on to a nearby pole for support.
moral_consequence: Sarah's bus ride goes quickly, and she feels glad to have helped someone.
immoral_action: Sarah notices the woman and puts her earbuds in to avoid being asked to give up her seat.
immoral_consequence: The old woman is made to stand on the crowded bus and falls at the next stop, causing Sarah to feel regretful.

norm: You should always have auto insurance when you drive.
situation: Jeff owns a truck that he loves but doesn't like paying insurance on it.
intention: Jeff wants to save his money.
moral_action: Jeff shop's around for the best auto insurance prices.
moral_consequence: Jeff finds an affordable plan and is always insured when he drives.
immoral_action: Jeff ignores his auto insurance bill.
immoral_consequence: Jeff's license is revoked after being stopped by police without insurance.

norm: People shouldn't try to pigeonhole others into convenient holes.
situation: Bill has known Tom for many years but now Tom wants to start hanging out more with Bill, and Bill isn't sure they are very good friends.
intention: Bill wants to decide if Tom is a good enough friend to hang out with.
moral_action: Bill doesn't label Tom in any particular way and hangs out with him when he is not busy.
moral_consequence: Tom and Bill find that they both enjoy life more thoroughly as a result of the increased social interaction.
immoral_action: Bill decides that Tom is an acquaintance, not really a friend, and declines to hang out with him.
immoral_consequence: Bill is hurt by Tom's refusal to hang out with him and Tom misses an opportunity to go out more often and socialize.

norm: You shouldn't get high with your friends.
situation: Lee, whose parents are firmly against drugs, is hanging out with a group of friends who offer him a pipe filled with weed to smoke with them.
intention: Lee wants to avoid looking uncool.
moral_action: Lee refuses and cites that he would, but he has an upcoming drug test.
moral_consequence: Lee's parents hear about his decision and are proud of him for making a responsible choice.
immoral_action: Lee accepts the pipe and takes a hit, smoking for the first time.
immoral_consequence: Lee's parents become concerned when they notice him coming home high.

norm: It's wrong to allow your pet to harm others.
situation: Ben wanted to take his dog to the dog park, but he knows his dog is aggressive with other dogs.
intention: Ben has to decide whether to take his dog to the park.
moral_action: Ben decides that he can play with his dog at home.
moral_consequence: Ben's dog can't hurt anyone, and Ben feels more relaxed.
immoral_action: Ben takes his dog to the dog park and takes his leash off.
immoral_consequence: Ben's dog is able to attack other dogs, and Ben cannot stop him.

norm: You should be willing to help with family responsibilities.
situation: Joe's father asks him to mow the lawn this weekend.
intention: Joe wants to visit his friends this weekend.
moral_action: Joe mows the lawn for his dad before going to his friend's house.
moral_consequence: Joe's father is happy to let Joe enjoy the rest of his weekend after getting the help he asked for.
immoral_action: Joe goes to his friend's house instead of mowing the lawn.
immoral_consequence: Joe's father is disappointed that Joe didn't help with the housework before taking off.

norm: It's wrong to call people making complaints cry babies.
situation: Nathan looks out of the window annoyed as his classmate Charles makes negative comments about their field trip and conditions of the bus.
intention: Nathan wants Charles to stop talking about negative things.
moral_action: Nathan tells Charles that they should play a game on the ride home.
moral_consequence: In the future Charles plays the game whenever he's in a car with someone.
immoral_action: Nathan tells Charles that his criticism is akin to a two year old having a temper tantrum, and that he should stop before he continues to embarrasses himself.
immoral_consequence: Charles blushes and sinks down into his seat completely humiliated.

norm: It is good to plant a garden.
situation: Lisa lives a very healthy lifestyle, and she believes in using fresh herbs as opposed to dried ones.
intention: Lisa wants to have fresh mint to put in her tea.
moral_action: Lisa starts a small garden and grows her own mint as well as other herbs.
moral_consequence: Lisa has a positive effect on the environment by reducing greenhouse gases and growing plants.
immoral_action: Lisa continues to buy mint from the grocery store once a week.
immoral_consequence: Lisa has more of a carbon impact on the environment by buying imported herbs.

norm: It's good to care about your pet's safety.
situation: When James' new neighbor saw he let his cat outside, he told James there were a lot of cat-eating coyotes in the area.
intention: James wants his cat to get lots of exercise.
moral_action: James builds an enclosed outdoor catio with climbing stands and an exercise wheel.
moral_consequence: James' cat spends hours climbing and playing in the catio, separated from the coyotes by wire.
immoral_action: James continues to allow his cat to explore the coyote-infested neighborhood.
immoral_consequence: James' cat is eaten by a coyote and James grieves for him.

norm: It's good to say thanks.
situation: Laura has been waiting for 20 minutes for her drink at a busy restaurant and the server finally brings it.
intention: Laura wants to respond to the service.
moral_action: Laura thanks the server for bringing the drink.
moral_consequence: Laura's server feels appreciated and his day is improved.
immoral_action: "Laura rolls her eyes and says ""it's about time""."
immoral_consequence: Laura's server takes a break to cry in the back room.

norm: It's wrong to get rid of your child's toys.
situation: John is doing some spring cleaning around the house.
intention: John wants to get rid of unnecessary items.
moral_action: John removes some old clutter from the basement.
moral_consequence: John's son remains happy and content.
immoral_action: John throws away most of his child's toys.
immoral_consequence: John's son is upset and begins to cry.

norm: It's not okay to not do your fair share.
situation: Billy and Ryan were two roommates that lived in a dorm together.
intention: Billy wants the dorm to be clean.
moral_action: Billy helps Ryan when he sees him trying to clean the room.
moral_consequence: Billy and Ryan are able to enjoy relaxing in a clean dorm room.
immoral_action: Billy lets Ryan do all the cleaning in the dorm, but never offers to help.
immoral_consequence: Ryan gets annoyed with Billy and starts letting the room get messy.

norm: One must obey all game regulations when fishing.
situation: Jim plans on fishing on a lake not far from home.
intention: Jim wants to catch enough fish for supper.
moral_action: Jim catches what is acceptable and follows the rules.
moral_consequence: Jim brings his fish home and has a nice supper.
immoral_action: Jim catches more fish than the DNR allows.
immoral_consequence: Jim is caught at the shore and is given a fine for overfishing.

norm: You shouldn't half-ass things.
situation: John is assembling a wooden table that he ordered online.
intention: John is tired and wants to go to bed.
moral_action: John postpones building the table until tomorrow when he can do a more thorough job and goes to bed.
moral_consequence: John has to wake up early to finish the table and is tired at work.
immoral_action: John rushes through the building instructions and doesn't end up using all of the required screws so that he can go to bed sooner.
immoral_consequence: The table collapses the first time John uses it, and he ends up breaking his toe.

norm: It's wrong to fake liking someone.
situation: Vanessa notices that her boss, who she hates, is going to promote someone to the recently opened manager position.
intention: Vanessa wants the promotion.
moral_action: Vanessa works hard demonstrating her skills in a informative presentation.
moral_consequence: Vanessa receives a raise along with being promoted to manager.
immoral_action: Vanessa acts like her boss' best friend going out of her way to be nice to her boss.
immoral_consequence: Vanessa is given a secretary position where she has to spend most of her time with her boss.

norm: It's wrong to cause harm to animals.
situation: John's dog is barking in the backyard.
intention: John wants his dog to be quiet.
moral_action: John takes his dog for a walk.
moral_consequence: John enjoys the exercise and time spent with his pet.
immoral_action: John yells at his dog and kicks it.
immoral_consequence: John is reported for animal abuse and arrested.

norm: It's good to make schools safe for kids.
situation: John is a member of the school board and is at a meeting about schools reopening during an infectious disease outbreak.
intention: John wants to get students back in school.
moral_action: John convinces the school board to work with local public health officials to come of with safety measures to protect students returning to school.
moral_consequence: The plan works and all the students remain safe from the infectious disease throughout the school year.
immoral_action: John convinces the school board to reopen schools just as they normally would.
immoral_consequence: The infectious disease is spread through the student body when the schools reopen.

norm: It is bad to hurt the planet for personal gain.
situation: Dana is a CEO of a large industrial company at a board meeting and is told one of the plants is losing money.
intention: Dana needs to find a way to cut costs at the plant.
moral_action: Dana tells the board that they will have to temporarily lay off a percentage of the staff.
moral_consequence: The board is in agreement that superfluous staff will have to be cut for the time being and can be rehired later.
immoral_action: Dana tells the board that she's ordering the plant to cease the costly waste disposal method and to dump waste in the nearby river.
immoral_consequence: The board is disturbed that Dana is proposing purposefully damaging the environment in order to save money.

norm: It's bad to not be understanding of your partner's past.
situation: John asks Mary to marry him but before accepting she tells him she has a secret she has been keeping from him.
intention: John wants to respond to Mary's revelation.
moral_action: John decides to trust what he knows of Mary and encourages her to be open with him.
moral_consequence: Mary is able to be honest with John and thus strengthen their bond.
immoral_action: John gets angry that she has kept something from him and withdraws his proposal.
immoral_consequence: Mary is hurt by his reaction and withdraws from him.

norm: You should never exclude someone for their religion.
situation: Richard has recently opened a new retail business in his neighborhood.
intention: Richard wants to hire some employees.
moral_action: Richard puts out a help wanted ad in order to find qualified candidates and hires people from a variety of religious backgrounds.
moral_consequence: Richard's business is successful due to the quality and diversity of his staff.
immoral_action: Richard puts out a help wanted ad that makes it clear that Muslims are not invited to apply.
immoral_consequence: Richard is seen as anti-Islamic and loses a lot of business because of his discrimination.

norm: You should always obey your teachers.
situation: Jim is on his way to meet his classmates during a free period when a teacher asks him to move some equipment for him.
intention: Jim wants to respond to the teachers request.
moral_action: Jim acquiesces to the teachers request.
moral_consequence: Jim earns brownie points for being helpful.
immoral_action: Jim tells the teacher that he has an important project to work on, so that he can meet his friends instead of helping.
immoral_consequence: Jim gets scolded for lying to a teacher.

norm: It's wrong to start untrue rumors about others.
situation: Dave and Bill are making small talk and the conversation seems to be fading out.
intention: Dave wants to say something interesting to keep the conversation going.
moral_action: Dave tells Bill a story about some interesting sports highlights he watched last night.
moral_consequence: John is never smeared and lives his life happily as he would have normally.
immoral_action: "Dave says ""hey did you hear about John? I heard he is wearing a hairpiece. "" which is untrue, and he knows it."
immoral_consequence: John finds out about the false rumor and is saddened and angry that his reputation has been tarnished for no reason.

norm: It's invasive to take photos of someone without their knowledge.
situation: James has a crush on Sarah and likes to look at pictures of her.
intention: James wants to get new photos of Sarah.
moral_action: James friends Sarah on Facebook and downloads every picture she uploads.
moral_consequence: James can tell his friends about this behavior because it's so common.
immoral_action: James follows Sarah around and takes candid photos of her when she's not looking.
immoral_consequence: Sarah notices James and tells him she'll pepper spray him if he doesn't leave her alone.

norm: It's bad to lash out at someone.
situation: Gary is waiting at a coffee shop to meet a client that is vital to his company's survival.
intention: Gary wants to order a coffee while he meets with the client.
moral_action: Gary smiles at the frazzled waiter when he finally visits the table.
moral_consequence: The client is impressed by Gary's sympathy and signs the contract.
immoral_action: Gary calls out to the waiter to hurry up and take their order as they are in a rush.
immoral_consequence: The client is put off by Gary's rudeness and does not sign the contract.

norm: It's not okay to lie to make yourself look good.
situation: Steph is applying for a job that she really wants.
intention: Steph wants to make sure that she gets the job by providing the most impressive resume possible.
moral_action: Steph fills out her resume to the best of her abililty, making sure to highlight all of her skills.
moral_consequence: She might get the job due to how impressed they were with her skills.
immoral_action: Steph exaggerates the amount of relevant experience on her resume, charitably interpreting what may be deemed relevant.
immoral_consequence: Steph my get the job, but she will struggle as she is clearly not qualified.

norm: It's not okay to impose on others and their homes.
situation: Adam's parents are moving to another state, but he has no desire to move with them and resolves to stay where he is.
intention: Adam wants to find a place to live.
moral_action: Adam gets a job and finds an apartment to rent with a few other guys to keep the costs down.
moral_consequence: Adam's friends maintain a good relationship with him and Adam preserves his sense of self-worth.
immoral_action: Adam goes to a friend's house and starts living on his couch without paying anything for it.
immoral_consequence: Adam's friend gets disgusted with Adam's lack of responsibility and eventually kicks him out of the house.

norm: It's good to address your marital problems.
situation: John has been really annoyed by Harriet's singing in the early mornings.
intention: John wants Harriet to stop singing.
moral_action: John tells Harriet that he can't sleep in the morning when she is singing.
moral_consequence: John's morning sleep quality improves as Harriet only sings outside during the mornings, and she is thankful for him being honest.
immoral_action: John puts sleeping pills in Harriet's morning water glass to make her sleep through the mornings.
immoral_consequence: Harriet discovers that she is being drugged and leaves John, feeling furious at him.

norm: It's bad to be living in a country illegally.
situation: Pablo moved to the United States in order to work and provide a better life for his family.
intention: Pablo wants to stay in the United States.
moral_action: Pablo applies for a work visa in order to work in the United States.
moral_consequence: Pablo is able to work in the country legally and make money to support his family.
immoral_action: Pablo continues working hard and getting paid under the table as an illegal immigrant.
immoral_consequence: Pablo is arrested by the federal government and gets sent back to his home country.

norm: You shouldn't remain with a cheating partner.
situation: Dave is at home when his wife Cindy comes back from being out with friends and admits to him she just slept with someone else.
intention: Dave wants to react to Cindy's admission.
moral_action: Dave tells Cindy that she needs to pack her things and move out as soon as possible as their relationship is finished.
moral_consequence: Dave gains a bunch of self respect and feels stronger and more in control of his life.
immoral_action: Dave tells Cindy that it's OK, and she just made a mistake, and he's sure she won't do it again.
immoral_consequence: Cindy is emboldened to cheat even more and stays with Dave just to exploit him for money.

norm: It's OK to avoid seeing an ex-partner on social media.
situation: After breaking up with Jill, Joe joins a social media website to find new friends.
intention: Joe wants to add people to his social media account.
moral_action: Joe blocks Jill's account the moment he sees it on the website.
moral_consequence: Joe makes new friends on the website and forgets about Jill.
immoral_action: Joe comes across Jill's profile and tries to add her as a friend.
immoral_consequence: Joe gets depressed when Jill doesn't accept his friend request.

norm: It's rude to leave your friends behind
situation: Janet and her friends went to the dance together because they were all nervous to go by themselves.
intention: Janet wants to go home.
moral_action: Janet tells her friends that she wants to leave and asks if anyone wants to come with her.
moral_consequence: Janet's friends decide to leave with her, and they have fun together elsewhere.
immoral_action: Janet doesn't want to dance anymore, so she leaves and goes home without telling anyone.
immoral_consequence: Janet's friends are worried about her and are then annoyed when they find out she left without saying anything.

norm: You shouldn't let someone try to fatten you up.
situation: Roland's wife, who loves desserts, is at a lunch with Roland and offers him one piece of every dessert on the table.
intention: Roland wants to please his wife.
moral_action: Roland eats one of the desserts, wraps the plate in saran wrap, and takes the rest of the desserts home to eat later.
moral_consequence: Roland maintains control of his weight and keeps his blood sugar levels in check, sparing him from diabetes.
immoral_action: Roland takes the plate and eats every single piece of dessert that his wife picked out for him.
immoral_consequence: Roland gains weight and becomes susceptible to diabetes because of his high sugar intake and weight gain.

norm: It's wrong to say mean things about one's partner.
situation: Barry is talking with his friend on the phone.
intention: Barry wants to tell his friend about his relationship.
moral_action: Barry tells his friend that he loves his wife more now than the day they were married.
moral_consequence: Barry is treated to a nice romantic dinner by his wife after she overhears his loving comment about her.
immoral_action: Barry tells his friend that he no longer finds his wife attractive.
immoral_consequence: Barry is divorced by his wife when she overhears his conversation about how ugly she is.

norm: It's good to want what is best for animals.
situation: Jane recently got a promotion at work that has her working 12 hour days and doesn't leave much room for her dog.
intention: Jane wants to make sure her dog has a good life.
moral_action: Jane finds a friend who is looking for a dog and lets her friend adopt her dog.
moral_consequence: Jane's dog is thriving and happy at his new home without being left alone all day.
immoral_action: Jane decides to leave the dog outside all day while she works, so he can run around.
immoral_consequence: Jane's neighbor notices the dog outside all day and night and reports her causing her to lose her dog.

norm: It's wrong to confront a partner in an aggressive way.
situation: Tom and Britt are trying to save for a house, but Britt keeps buying unnecessary things.
intention: Tom wants to get Britt to stop spending money.
moral_action: Tom sits Britt down and explains that their spending is unsustainable.
moral_consequence: Britt promises to do better and works with Tom to curb their spending.
immoral_action: Tom shouts at Britt, threatening to cut up their credit cards.
immoral_consequence: Britt becomes upset and leaves Tom.

norm: You shouldn't bribe your kids.
situation: Andy is a father of two.
intention: Andy needs his kids to do their chores.
moral_action: Andy sets an example for his kids by cleaning up after himself and teaching them to set a schedule for themselves to make it easy to do.
moral_consequence: Andy's kids develop a work ethic and are responsible.
immoral_action: Andy tells his kids he'll take them shopping at the mall if they clean their rooms.
immoral_consequence: The kids will only clean up after themselves if they're rewarded heavily by their dad in exchange.

norm: You shouldn't hide your medical conditions from others.
situation: Jackie has joined a new club that does a variety of fun activities.
intention: Jackie wants to sign up for club activities.
moral_action: Jackie tells the club that she has asthma and needs to find suitable activities, so they go see a movie.
moral_consequence: Jackie enjoys seeing the movie with the club and feels included despite her asthma.
immoral_action: Jackie doesn't tell the club that she has asthma, and they take her on a hike with them.
immoral_consequence: Jackie has an asthma attack while on the hike and needs medical intervention.

norm: You shouldn't disturb people at work.
