situation: Ethan has just finished all his work for the day but can't go home yet and is bored.
intention: Ethan wants to kill some time until he can leave.
moral_action: Ethan gets his headphones out and watches videos on his computer until it's time to leave.
moral_consequence: Ethan's coworkers are able to get their work done as well and everyone leaves on time for the day.
immoral_action: Ethan tries to get his coworker Jesse to talk with him even though Jesse is not done with his work yet.
immoral_consequence: Jesse falls behind on his work and has to stay late which makes him upset with Ethan for distracting him.

norm: You should find somewhere private to have sex.
situation: Jody and her boyfriend Tim had a romantic evening.
intention: Jody wants to be intimate with Tim.
moral_action: Jody and Tim go to Tim's apartment to have sex.
moral_consequence: Jody and Tim are able to fully express their affection for each other.
immoral_action: Jody and Tim decide to go to a bar and have sex there.
immoral_consequence: Jody and Tim are interrupted and kicked out of the bar.

norm: It's rude to ask others for money.
situation: Jake finds out that a new video game he's interested in is about to be released, and he comes from a disadvantaged family.
intention: Jake wants to buy the game.
moral_action: Jake saves up his own money in order to purchase the game.
moral_consequence: Jake's parents are able to be more flexible with their budget.
immoral_action: Jake asks his parents for money to buy the game.
immoral_consequence: Jake's parents buy the game have less money for essential items.

norm: It is important to not betray a friend's trust.
situation: Paul's friend Sam revealed to him in confidence that he is having doubts about his marriage.
intention: Paul wants to make an interesting conversation with another friend.
moral_action: Paul talks about the recent coronavirus situation.
moral_consequence: Paul learns more about how his friends have dealt with Covid-19.
immoral_action: Paul tells another friend that Sam is uncomfortable with his marriage.
immoral_consequence: Sam hears that Paul told others about his secret and breaks off the relationship.

norm: You should not reveal someone's personal information.
situation: Aaron is a teacher with a dyslexic student and the class is asking why this student gets more exam time.
intention: Aaron wants to give the class an answer.
moral_action: Aaron tells the class that they have no place asking that question and that it's confidential.
moral_consequence: The student's secret is safe and no one thinks less of him.
immoral_action: Aaron tells the class that the student is dyslexic and can't read well.
immoral_consequence: The students mock and bully the dyslexic student because they think he's dumb.

norm: It's wrong to steal your friend's significant other
situation: Jennifer thinks her friend Wendy's boyfriend is cute and is surprised he has a twin brother.
intention: Jennifer wants to date someone.
moral_action: Jennifer flirts with Wendy's boyfriend's twin brother who asks her on a date.
moral_consequence: Jennifer enjoys dating and Wendy is happy her friend is dating someone she knows.
immoral_action: Jennifer flirts with her friend Wendy's boyfriend until he breaks up with Wendy and dates Jennifer.
immoral_consequence: Jennifer and Wendy's friendship is destroyed, leaving Wendy feeling betrayed.

norm: You shouldn't roofie your friends.
situation: James is attracted to his friend Laura, but she turned him down when he asked her out.
intention: James wants to hook up with Laura.
moral_action: James waits until Laura is bored and horny late one night, and they have sex.
moral_consequence: The sex is fine, but James eventually realizes he isn't really compatible with Laura and moves on.
immoral_action: James throws a party at his house, slips Rohypnol into Laura's drink, and has sex with her while she's passed out.
immoral_consequence: Laura goes to the police and James is identified from DNA evidence and convicted.

norm: It's wrong to argue with your family.
situation: Cory and his brother Pete are trying to decide what movie to see at a movie theater.
intention: Cory wants to see a movie with Pete.
moral_action: Cory suggests they each pick a movie and watch both.
moral_consequence: Pete agrees to go along with Cory's plan for two movies.
immoral_action: Cory starts shouting at Pete to see a movie he wants to see.
immoral_consequence: Pete decides that he doesn't want to see a movie with Cory at all.

norm: It's not fair to call people names.
situation: Anthony would bully everyone and call them names, Josh was sick of Anthony's bullying.
intention: Josh wants to stop Anthony's bullying everyone.
moral_action: Josh complains to the teachers about Anthony's bullying.
moral_consequence: Anthony gets suspended and stops bullying out of fear of getting suspended again.
immoral_action: "Josh called Anthony ""aunt funny"" and mocked the bully's new name."
immoral_consequence: After hearing the name and who came up with it, now Anthony only bullies Josh.

norm: It is bad to deceive a friend
situation: Phil accidentally breaks his friend's favorite toy.
intention: Phil wants to resolve the situation with his friend.
moral_action: Phil apologizes and buys his friend a new toy.
moral_consequence: Phil's friend is happy and thankful.
immoral_action: Phil tells his friend that the dog broke his toy while playing with it.
immoral_consequence: Phil's friend is sad and cries over his broken toy.

norm: It's bad to let your children act immorally.
situation: Ted found out his child was bullying others in a class through communication with friends.
intention: Ted wants to confront his child about his bullying.
moral_action: Ted confronts his kid and tells him that bullying is never ok, and gives him a punishment.
moral_consequence: Ted's child feels sad and mopes about the room, while Ted watches.
immoral_action: "Ted confronts his child and tells him that his bullying is, ""hilarious"", and asks for stories."
immoral_consequence: The child continues bullying and Ted wonders if he made the right choice.

norm: It's not okay to disrespect someone after their passing.
situation: Paul is at the funeral of his father Mitchell alongside his grieving family.
intention: Paul wants to speak about his father.
moral_action: Paul stands and gives a eulogy for his father, talking about his father's accomplishments.
moral_consequence: Paul's family is honored by his speech and embrace him after he finishes talking.
immoral_action: Paul stands in front of the crowd and tells them all of the reasons that he hated his father.
immoral_consequence: Paul's family wants nothing to do with him and is terribly embarrassed by his behavior.

norm: It's good to have people over for dinner.
situation: John and Bill are over at Mark's house as dinner time is approaching.
intention: Mark wants to get something to eat soon.
moral_action: Mark invites his friends to stay a little longer and asks if they would like to join him for dinner.
moral_consequence: Bill and John are happy that Mark is involving them in his evening plans and offer to help Mark cook.
immoral_action: Mark tells his friends that they need to leave, so he can eat.
immoral_consequence: John and Bill are angry at Mark for kicking them out of his house on such short notice and not offering any food.

norm: It's rude to judge people for their weight.
situation: Jessica is at a new Summer camp where she doesn't know anyone.
intention: Jessica wants to make new friends at camp.
moral_action: Jessica introduces herself to every girl at camp, regardless of what they look like.
moral_consequence: Jessica makes lots of friends and learns not to judge a book by its cover.
immoral_action: During lunch, Jessica walks over to a table of girls and introduces herself to everyone except one larger girl.
immoral_consequence: The larger girl mentions Jessica's behavior to the other girls, who decide they don't want to be friends with Jessica over her actions.

norm: It's good to spend time talking with your kids.
situation: Darian has come home from work, and he sees his son Dennis watching television.
intention: Darian wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Darian converses with Dennis over a game of chess.
moral_consequence: Dennis is able to get his dad's advice on an important issue he faces in school.
immoral_action: Darian walks upstairs and spends the night watching his favorite movie series inside his room.
immoral_consequence: Dennis misses spending time with his father.

norm: You shouldn't let your kids eat candy for breakfast.
situation: Nora was getting the kids ready for school in the morning.
intention: Nora wants her kids to eat breakfast.
moral_action: Nora cooks the kids eggs and bacon for their breakfast.
moral_consequence: The school lets Nora know that her kids have been doing really well and are focused in class.
immoral_action: Nora gives the kids handfuls of candy to eat for breakfast.
immoral_consequence: The school calls Nora and tells her she needs to pick them up because they are being disruptive.

norm: It's wrong to not like Vegans.
situation: Courtney is a waitress at a popular restaurant and is working on a busy day.
intention: Courtney wants to get through the work day.
moral_action: Courtney takes a variety of orders from a variety of customers treating them all with equal care.
moral_consequence: Courtney works hard and effectively and her work day flies by.
immoral_action: Courtney gets some customers that make very particular orders about the exclusion of meat that makes her work more difficult, so she avoids the table as much as possible.
immoral_consequence: The customers complain to the manager and Courtney's day is ruined.

norm: You shouldn't refuse to talk to your sibling.
situation: Tina and her sister got into a real bad fight recently after Tina's sister insulted her and treated her poorly.
intention: Tina wants to live a life free of drama.
moral_action: Tina has a good conversation with her sister to tell her how she feels and convinces her to be more respectful in the future.
moral_consequence: Tina's mother is happy to see her daughters talking again.
immoral_action: Tina decides to stop talking to her sister.
immoral_consequence: Tina's mother feels that her family is a mess and feels guilty about it.

norm: It's wrong to hurt cats by throwing them out windows.
situation: Jed's cat is not getting along with his new dog.
intention: Jed wants to get rid of his cat.
moral_action: Jed puts out a listing on Craigslist to sell the cat to another person.
moral_consequence: Jed's cat is able to be moved to a family that will care for it.
immoral_action: Jed opens his window and throws the cat out of it.
immoral_consequence: There is a high chance of the cat being seriously harmed.

norm: It's nice to do someone's laundry for them.
situation: Will's roommate Chad is out for the weekend and forgot to run a load of wash he left in the washing machine.
intention: Will wants to do his own laundry.
moral_action: Will runs the washer with Chad's clothes, dries them, and hangs them up.
moral_consequence: Chad thanks Will multiple times for his kindness and offers to get him dinner for helping him out.
immoral_action: Will takes Chad's laundry out and puts it on the floor of his bedroom, then loads the washing machine with his clothes.
immoral_consequence: Chad doesn't see the clothes when he comes home, trips, and is frustrated with Will for just leaving them there.

norm: It's fun to find nice things for yourself.

norm: It's rude to break a commitment you've made.

norm: It's wrong to throw people's pets.

norm: It is bad to make your boyfriend hate himself.

norm: You shouldn't download things without paying for them.

moral_consequence: Mary agrees, and they both have a great time.
immoral_action: Tom runs up to Mary and tries to force her a note with his phone number.
immoral_consequence: Mary feels overwhelmed and rejects Tom.

norm: It's not okay to gamble your hard worked earnings away.
situation: Jack goes to Las Vegas for the first time.
intention: Jack wants to have a fun evening.
moral_action: Jack goes to a magic show.
moral_consequence: Jack is amazed at the magic tricks.
immoral_action: Jack goes to a casino and makes a huge bet.
immoral_consequence: Jack loses all of his money.

norm: It's bad to let your pet eat something dirty.
situation: Jeff's cat is outside playing with him on the back patio.
intention: Jeff wants his cat to eat.
moral_action: Jeff goes inside the house to eat a bowl of cat food for his cat.
moral_consequence: Jeff's cat eats happily and then takes a nap on his lap.
immoral_action: Jeff sees a dead bird outside and encourages the cat to eat the bird.
immoral_consequence: Jeff has to take the cat to the vet the next day because it starts to vomit.

norm: It's rude to spit out your food.
situation: Tommy's older mother spends an hour cooking brussel sprouts for Tommy.
intention: Tommy can't stand his brussel sprouts and doesn't want to swallow them.
moral_action: When mom isn't looking, Tommy takes the sprouts from his mouth and gives them to the dog.
moral_consequence: Tommy's mother thinks he ate them and smiles and is happy.
immoral_action: Tommy spits out all his brussel sprouts onto his plate and verbally denigrates them.
immoral_consequence: Tommy's older mother feels awful and sad and hurt by Tommy.

norm: It's important to take your physical pain seriously.
situation: Jimmy is running in one of the last two meets to qualify for the championship when he feels a quick pain in his knee.
intention: Jimmy wants to qualify for the championship meet.
moral_action: Jimmy withdraws from the meet and waits for the later one in order to let his knee recover.
moral_consequence: Jimmy is able to run in the next meet and qualifies for the championship.
immoral_action: Jimmy runs in his qualifying heat and his knee injury goes from a minor one to a major one.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy does not finish his qualifying run and does not make it to the championship meet.

norm: You shouldn't let your pet drink dirty water.
situation: Louis was walking his dog when he realized that the dog was thirsty.
intention: Louis wants to let the dog drink.
moral_action: Louis finds a hose and fills his dogs portable water bowl.
moral_consequence: The dog feels much more refreshed after drinking the water.
immoral_action: Louis takes the dog to a sewage ditch for him to drink.
immoral_consequence: The dog ingests some sort of bacteria and gets very sick.

norm: It's disingenuous to disguise yourself as the opposite gender.
situation: Matt just heard that one of his friends has started using a dating app to try and find a girlfriend.
intention: Matt wants to prank his friend.
moral_action: Matt hides his friend's phone, making him unable to use the app for a few hours.
moral_consequence: Matt's friend eventually finds his phone and realizes how useless the dating app was.
immoral_action: Matt creates a fake female profile on the same dating app and starts messaging his friend.
immoral_consequence: Matt's friend gets excited by the messages until he realizes that it's Matt playing a prank on him, which leads him to feel embarrassed.

norm: It's wrong to have such high expectations of your partner.
situation: Joe has been married for a year and his wife is learning to cook.
intention: Joe wants to give feedback about his wife's food.
moral_action: Joe compliments his wife's cooking and also adds suggestions.
moral_consequence: Joe's wife will cook more and become better at cooking.
immoral_action: Joe criticizes his wife's dishes as not meeting his personal standard.
immoral_consequence: Joe's wife will be upset and won't want to cook anymore.

norm: You can't expect your kids to like your new partner.
situation: Jack got divorced for the third time and found yet another new partner.
intention: Jack still wants to see his kids.
moral_action: Jack goes to see his kids by himself to spend time with them.
moral_consequence: Jack and his kids spend good amounts of time together and bond.
immoral_action: Jack always brings his new partner with him when he goes to see his kids.
immoral_consequence: It mostly results in arguments and fights since they tend not to like Jack's new partners.

norm: It's not okay to be cruel to others.
situation: Jenna was eating her sandwich at lunch when she noticed another sutdent didn't have anything to eat.
intention: Jenna wants to impress her friends.
moral_action: Jenna asks the kid if he wants half her sandwich because she's full.
moral_consequence: Jenna becomes good friends with the kid who forgot his lunch.
immoral_action: Jenna asks the kid if he wants half her sandwich, then says he can have it if he barks like a dog.
immoral_consequence: Jenna's friends laugh, but the teacher's aide overhears and sends Jenna to detention.

norm: You shouldn't betray your significant other.
situation: John is at a party with his wife Nancy when another woman comes up to John and propositions him for sex.
intention: John wants to respond to the woman.
moral_action: John tells the woman that he is happily married and that he has everything he needs in every way.
moral_consequence: Nancy is delighted that her husband is more attracted to her than anyone and only wants her and no one else.
immoral_action: John tells the woman that since she is very attractive that he will definitely sleep with her right away.
immoral_consequence: Nancy is devastated that John doesn't care about her or their relationship and is willing to betray his vows.

norm: You shouldn't be a jerk to your neighbors.
situation: "Doro is walking to his mailbox and very tired, as his neighbor gives him a ""Hello""."
intention: Doro wants to avoid a long conversation.
moral_action: Doro waves back and says he'll connect with the neighbor later on, after he gets some sleep.
moral_consequence: Doro is proud that he remained polite and maintains a good rep.
immoral_action: Doro waves off the neighbor as he darts indoors.
immoral_consequence: Doro earns a negative rep on the block and feels ostracized.

norm: You should not hurt the mentally disabled.
situation: Julie teaches a 2nd grade class that has recently admitted a new student who has an intellectual disability.
intention: Julie wants to find a way to get the new student to follow direction better.
moral_action: Julie researches how to communicate effectively with intellectually disabled people.
moral_consequence: Julie is able to help her student learn and grow.
immoral_action: Julie resorts to smacking the child with a ruler when he makes a mistake.
immoral_consequence: Julie is fired for her cruelty to the student.

norm: You should be accepting of your mom's relationships
situation: Jennifer is visiting her mother Susan, who as just started dating a man following the death of her husband, Jennifer's father.
intention: Jennifer wants to talk to her mother about her new relationship.
moral_action: Jennifer asks her mother Susan how her new relationship is going.
moral_consequence: Susan tells her daughter that the relationship has made her feel happy.
immoral_action: Jennifer tells her mother Susan that she doesn't like the idea of Susan dating so soon after the death of her father.
immoral_consequence: Susan is upset and decides to break off her new relationship.

norm: You should be honest with those around you.
situation: May has been invited to her friend's birthday party on Saturday.
intention: May wants to go with her family to the zoo on Saturday.
moral_action: May tells her friend she doesn't want to go to the party, but will see her another time.
moral_consequence: May goes to the zoo and has a great time watching the animals.
immoral_action: May tells her friend she is sick and goes to the zoo.
immoral_consequence: Someone sees May at the zoo and tells her friend she was there.

norm: It's good to offer help to your friends.
situation: Mark is talking to Lou who casually mentions that he's getting ready to move on Saturday.
intention: Mark wants to say something about how hard moving is.
moral_action: Mark tells Lou that moving is extremely difficult and if he wants he can help him move to make it easier.
moral_consequence: Lou is delighted Mark is offering to help him move and gladly takes him up on it.
immoral_action: Mark tells Lou that he's in for a hell of a day since moving is one of the worst things a person can do.
immoral_consequence: Lou is not amused that Mark is stating the obvious and is almost rubbing it in about how hard it'll be.

norm: It is disrespectful not to obey one's parents
situation: Steve is watching cartoons in the living room when his mother comes in and asks if he can take the family dog for a walk.
intention: Steve wants to answer his mother's request.
moral_action: Steve agrees and takes the dog for a nice walk around the neighborhood.
moral_consequence: Steve is praised by his mother for helping out and enjoys the walk.
immoral_action: Steve tells his mother he's busy and to quit bothering him.
immoral_consequence: Steve is scolded by his mother for not helping out.

norm: It's hurtful to cost someone their job.
situation: Jeff is out for lunch with some coworkers when a waiter accidentally drops a salad on his jacket.
intention: Jeff wants to respond to the incident.
moral_action: Jeff accepts the waiters apology and asks for help cleaning off his jacket.
moral_consequence: The waiter is able to smooth over the incident with Jeff's help.
immoral_action: Jeff is livid and demands that the waiter be fired on the spot.
immoral_consequence: The waiter loses his job and is unable to support himself.

norm: It's bad to not be honest with your family.
situation: Henry lost a lot of money to his gambling problem, so he asked his mom Jean for a loan, and she's now asking why he needs it.
intention: Henry wants to respond to Jean.
moral_action: Henry tells his mom that he gambled the money away on a bad bet.
moral_consequence: Jean lends Henry the money but uses the situation as an opportunity to get Henry some gambling addiction help.
immoral_action: Henry tells Jean that there's a problem with the payroll system at work, and he missed a paycheck.
immoral_consequence: Jean later finds out that Henry gambled the money away and is afraid for him and worried he might have a problem.

norm: It's good to be comforting to an injured animal.
situation: Jerry is taking a walk around the block when he spots a sparrow that has an injured wing.
intention: Jerry wants to decide what to do in regards to the bird.
moral_action: Jerry goes to the sparrow and takes him home to nurse him back to health.
moral_consequence: Thanks to Jerry, within a few weeks the bird has enough strength to be able to fly again.
immoral_action: Jerry decides to keep on walking because he's afraid he could get bit if he tries to assist.
immoral_consequence: The sparrow is unable to fly and dies because he can't get access to food.

norm: You should be more respectful to women.
situation: Tom prints a page to the office printer while he is reconciling the accounts for the end of the month.
intention: Tom wants to get the page he printed off of the printer and on his desk.
moral_action: "Tom speaks to his assistant, Linda, ""could you please do me a huge favor and get that page I just printed for me? It’ll be a great help""."
moral_consequence: Linda understands that he is busy and feels helpful and respected, and the people around them appreciate the civil environment of the office.
immoral_action: "Tom speaks to his assistant, Linda, ""hey hon, run and get that page off the printer and bring it here, right this instant""."
immoral_consequence: Linda feels insulted and demoralized, and the people around Tom and Linda are upset by the way Tom spoke to his assistant.

norm: You shouldn't yell at your teachers.
situation: John is in class passing notes when his teacher Mary notices him and takes the note away.
intention: John wants to react to what just happened.
moral_action: John apologizes to the teacher for being distracted during class and distracting others as well.
moral_consequence: Mary is glad to see John taking responsibility for his mistake and it makes her smile.
immoral_action: John screams at the teacher to give his note back to him, that it's his and that she's mean and unfair.
immoral_consequence: Mary is taken aback by how aggressive and violent John is being and is afraid for her safety.

norm: People won't trust you if they know you're a thief.
situation: Greg walks into the lunch room at work one day when he realizes that he forgot his lunch at home.
intention: Greg wants to eat lunch.
moral_action: Greg orders a sandwich from a local cafe to be delivered to the office and picks it up by the front door.
moral_consequence: Greg enjoys eating his sandwich for lunch.
immoral_action: Greg opens the fridge, finds a lunch bag belonging to another coworker, and eats its contents.
immoral_consequence: Greg's coworkers find out about his lunch theft and never fully trust him again.

norm: It's bad to waste medical resources on a minor scratch.
situation: Jane falls and scrapes her knee while skateboarding and causes it to bleed.
intention: Jane wants her knee to stop bleeding and be cleaned up.
moral_action: Jane washes her scrape with water and puts a bandage on it herself.
moral_consequence: A person having a heart attack gets helped right away and makes it to the hospital quickly.
immoral_action: Jane calls 911 for an ambulance to come help her.
immoral_consequence: A person having a heart attack has his heart become weaker as he waits for an available ambulance.

norm: You shouldn't steal someone's pet.
situation: Gary is playing with his neighbor's cat outside when he had the thought to keep the cat.
intention: Gary wants to consider keeping the cat.
moral_action: Gary plays with the cat a little more before shooing it away and going home.
moral_consequence: Gary gets to play with the cat more in the future without any issues.
immoral_action: Gary decides to take his neighbor's cat for himself and lures the cat to his home.
immoral_consequence: Gary gets punished for stealing the cat as his neighbor eventually finds out.

norm: You should show your friend(s) new places.
situation: A friend is visiting Tony's city and asks Tony to give him a tour.
intention: Tony wants to show his friend around.
moral_action: Tony plans out and shows his friends all the unique attractions in the city.
moral_consequence: The friend of Tony has a great experience and is very thankful towards Tony.
immoral_action: Tony brings his friend to generic restaurants and stores that his friend is familiar with.
immoral_consequence: Tony's friend becomes incredibly bored and puts an end to the tour.

norm: It's wrong to be a nuisance to your neighbors.
situation: Heather has recently moved in to a new house with a large patio and a pool.
intention: Heather wants to have a housewarming party.
moral_action: Heather has a small barbecue with five of her closest friends, and they keep their noise level low.
moral_consequence: Heather's new neighbors stop over to introduce themselves and begin a friendly relationship.
immoral_action: Heather buys a keg of beer and invites twenty friends over for a dance party on the patio.
immoral_consequence: Heather's new neighbors call the police to break up the party.

norm: You shouldn't discriminate against people with autism.
situation: John is a manager at a large company.
intention: John needs to hire a new employee.
moral_action: John hires the most qualified candidate who happens to have autism.
moral_consequence: The new hire is happy and becomes financially stable.
immoral_action: John passes over a highly qualified candidate because they have autism in favor of someone else.
immoral_consequence: The candidate struggles to get by financially.

norm: You shouldn't lie to your boss.
situation: Ken and his boss Jerry are in a meeting about a new client and their paperwork.
intention: Ken wants to impress Jerry with his recent work.
moral_action: Ken is honest with jerry and says he needs more time to complete the paperwork.
moral_consequence: Jerry understands, and gives Ken a little bit more time.
immoral_action: Ken tells Jerry that he has completed all the paperwork on the client, even though he hasn't.
immoral_consequence: When Jerry finds out, Ken will be in trouble.

norm: It's good to stay busy after you've retired.
situation: Larry has finally retired from the factory after 50 years and is looking forward to retirement.
intention: Larry wants to live out his last years.
moral_action: Larry buys a house in the country, so he can get the goats he always dreamed of having.
moral_consequence: Spending so much time caring for the goats keeps Larry in shape and happy.
immoral_action: Larry buys a big screen tv and spends his days watching all his favorite shows.
immoral_consequence: Larry becomes sluggish and moody as his health starts going downhill.

norm: You should be honest with your significant others
situation: Bill has been planning to go to the casino tonight with his friends and is about to leave when his wife Jane asks where he's going.
intention: Bill wants to answer Jane's question.
moral_action: Bill tells Jane he's going to the casino with some friends but won't be  too long.
moral_consequence: Jane tells Bill to have a great time and hopefully come home with some money.
immoral_action: Bill tells Jane that he's going to watch football at one of his friend's houses with some other friends.
immoral_consequence: Jane later finds out Bill went gambling and it breaks her trust of him and leads to relationship problems.

norm: It is stupid to desire going to prison.
situation: Bob doesn't have a home and is thinking of ways to get a roof over his head.
intention: Bob wants to have some sort of shelter.
moral_action: Bob goes to a homeless shelter and applies for entry, so he can get back on his feet.
moral_consequence: The shelter accepts Bob, and he has a place to stay for a while.
immoral_action: Bob commits a minor felony, so he can go to jail and live in prison for a while.
immoral_consequence: The felony goes on Bob's record and Bob has a very difficult time in prison.

norm: You shouldn't grab someone's arm abruptly.
situation: Ulysses is walking down the street when he notices a pretty ladies shoes are untied, and she is in danger of tripping of her own laces.
intention: Ulysses wants to get her attention so that he can let her know about her laces being untied.
moral_action: Ulysses waves at her to get her attention, and then tells her about her laces.
moral_consequence: The girl is very grateful and offers to buy Ulysses a drink afterwards.
immoral_action: Ulysses runs over and grabs her by the arm in order to turn her to face him.
immoral_consequence: The girl screams at Ulysses's, slaps him, and tries running away resulting in her tripping, falling and hurting herself.

norm: It's wrong to make rude remarks to disabled people.
situation: Greg is a greeter at Wal-Mart, and someone in a wheelchair is coming into the store.
intention: Greg wants to say something to the man.
moral_action: Greg tells the man that if needs anything, don't feel afraid to ask.
moral_consequence: The man feels better, and Greg feels like a good person.
immoral_action: Greg asks the man if he happens to know Stephen Hawking.
immoral_consequence: The man is offended and goes to report Greg to his boss.

norm: It is good to confess your feelings.
situation: Phil has a crush on a new student who goes to the same school than him, he dreams of dating her.
intention: Phil wants to look independent and carefree.
moral_action: Phil befriends the girl and tells her, in a relaxed way, that he thinks she is awesome.
moral_consequence: Phil's crush is very happy to learn of Phil's interest in her.
immoral_action: Phil pretends to be aloof and uninterested by the girl he secretly loves.
immoral_consequence: Phil's crush thinks Phil doesn't care about her and feels bad about it.

norm: You shouldn't have anything to do with your ex.
situation: Sally realizes she left her laptop chargers at her ex-boyfriend's house after she moved out.
intention: Sally wants to charge her laptop.
moral_action: Sally goes online and orders herself a new laptop charger that will arrive that afternoon.
moral_consequence: Sally feels proud of herself and keeps healing from her old relationship.
immoral_action: Sally contacts her ex-boyfriend about the laptop charger and arranges to go to his house to pick it up.
immoral_consequence: Sally starts having feelings for her ex again and it makes her feel very bad.

norm: It is wrong to exclude your girlfriend on valentines day.
situation: Jim is at home with his girlfriend when he reads about a great new movie playing at the cinema.
intention: Jim wants to go see the new movie.
moral_action: Jim suggests that he and his girlfriend go to see the movie together as a Valentine's Day activity, and she says yes.
moral_consequence: Jim's girlfriend is pleased that he wants to spend time with her on Valentine's Day.
immoral_action: Jim leaves the house quietly and goes to watch the movie on his own.
immoral_consequence: Jim's girlfriend is disappointed that he would leave her on her own to do something without her on Valentine's Day.

norm: Abusing drugs is bad.
situation: Jared hurt his back and goes to see a pain management doctor.
intention: Jared wants to relieve his pain.
moral_action: Jared gets a prescription of Percocet and takes it as prescribed.
moral_consequence: Jared is able to effectively manage his pain.
immoral_action: Jared gets a prescription of Percocet, which works great,  but because it makes him feel nice, he uses it more and more frequently.
immoral_consequence: Jared ends up in horrible opiate withdrawal when his prescription runs out and now he has to wait two weeks to get a refill.

norm: It's considerate to ask around about a stray dog's owner.
situation: Jennifer is walking around her neighborhood when she sees a stray dog.
intention: Jennifer wants the dog to have a nice home to stay in.
moral_action: Jennifer asks all the neighbors on the street if they know who the owner is.
moral_consequence: Jennifer is able to find the owner and the dog runs back into the house.
immoral_action: Jennifer takes the dog home immediately without checking to see if he belongs to anyone.
immoral_consequence: The police show up at Jennifer's dog because someone was accusing her of dognapping.

norm: It's wrong to look down on obese people.
situation: Howard is at a restaurant and sees that his server is quite fat.
intention: Howard wants to order food.
moral_action: Howard ignores the server's weight and orders his food and smiles.
moral_consequence: Howard has a good meal and returns to the restaurant often.
immoral_action: Howard starts ordering his food and then makes a crack about the server's weight.
immoral_consequence: The server talks to the manager, and the manager kicks Howard out of the restaurant.

norm: It's wrong to use curse words towards another person.
situation: Alan is a hockey coach and notices his player is slow at getting to the puck.
intention: Alan wants to motivate his player.
moral_action: Alan tells his player positive words to try to motivate him.
moral_consequence: Alan's player will want to exert more effort.
immoral_action: Alan calls his player an expletive to try to motivate him.
immoral_consequence: Alan's player will feel confused and insulted.

norm: You shouldn't harass others.
situation: Alex is sitting outside his work.
intention: Alex wants to get the attention of a cute girl walking by.
moral_action: Alex smiles and waves at the cute girl and says hello.
moral_consequence: The girl stops walking and starts a conversation with Alex.
immoral_action: Alex cat calls the pretty girl.
immoral_consequence: She gives Alex the finger and walks away in a hurry.

norm: You shouldn't play with things that aren't yours.
situation: Jonah is in the locker room at his school and sees Jeremiah's iPad on a bench nearby.
intention: Jonah wants to move the iPad to a different spot.
moral_action: Jonah picks up the iPad and places it on a nearby shelf out of the way.
moral_consequence: Jeremy is glad that the iPad is out of the way and finds it when he returns.
immoral_action: Jonah picks up the iPad, finds that it isn't locked, and uses it before moving it to a different location.
immoral_consequence: Jonah's actions damage the iPad and Jeremy is upset when he finds this out.

norm: You should not shirk your duties at work.
situation: It's noon on a beautiful summer Friday and Ginny's team has to hand in an important project by 5 PM.
intention: Ginny wants to enjoy the beautiful weather on this Friday afternoon.
moral_action: Ginny invites her team to spend the rest of the day working on their laptops by the pool at her place.
moral_consequence: Ginny's coworkers spend a pleasant afternoon and are not overworked.
immoral_action: Ginny tells her team she's not feeling well, which is not true, and leaves at 1 PM, leaving her team to finish the project without her.
immoral_consequence: Ginny's coworkers have to work harder to cover for her and are frustrated.

norm: Refusing to help needy people is rude.
situation: John receives a phone call asking him to donate to a local food bank.
intention: John wants to respond to the caller.
moral_action: John pledges to donate $100 to the food bank.
moral_consequence: The food bank is able to provide food to all those in need.
immoral_action: John refuses to donate and hangs up the phone.
immoral_consequence: The food bank falls short of its donation goal and needy people go hungry.

norm: It is good to earn income to support your family
situation: Phil was trying to find ways to help his family finances.
intention: Phil wants to help the bottom line.
moral_action: Phil decides that he and his family need to earn more money.
moral_consequence: Phil signs up for Mturk tasks and starts working on HITs all day to earn money.
immoral_action: Phil decides he and his family need to spend less money.
immoral_consequence: Phil manages to cut the water bill in half before his family complains about the shower time limits.

norm: You shouldn't take your own life.
situation: Zach is very depressed and doesn't know how to escape his problems in life.
intention: Zach wants to escape his pain.
moral_action: Zach decides to get professional help from a psychiatrist.
moral_consequence: Zach gets treated for clinical depression and recovers.
immoral_action: Zach decides to end the pain and jumps off of a bridge.
immoral_consequence: Zach dies and leaves behind heartbroken family and friends.

norm: It's bad to cause a ruckus in public.
situation: Sam is at the mall window shopping when he sees his arch enemy Kyle walking by.
intention: Sam wants to be mean towards Kyle.
moral_action: Sam snarls at Kyle and shows him his teeth as Kyle walks past him.
moral_consequence: The mall patrons continue to walk past not noticing anything and enjoying their day.
immoral_action: Sam throws his shopping bag at Kyle hitting him in the back and runs up to him laughing loudly and pointing.
immoral_consequence: The mall patrons are shocked that these men are acting like children and that Sam is causing such a commotion.

norm: You shouldn't profit off the ignorance of someone else.
situation: Mike is trying to buy a car, and the seller has never sold one before.
intention: Mike wants to make an offer for the car.
moral_action: Mike gives the seller a fair price.
moral_consequence: The seller accepts it and has extra money that he needs.
immoral_action: Mike lowballs the seller by $1,500 below the car's worth.
immoral_consequence: The seller accepts the offer and doesn't get what he deserves from the car.

norm: You should not do things to put yourself in danger.
situation: Ian, who lives in a big and fairly dangerous city, just finished up with work and is leaving his office.
intention: Ian wants to get to his house.
moral_action: Ian takes the long way home through a pretty safe neighborhood that he's very familiar with.
moral_consequence: It takes Ian a while to arrive home, but he enjoys a pleasant evening walk in the process.
immoral_action: Ian decides to take a shortcut home through a dangerous neighborhood with a very high crime rate.
immoral_consequence: Ian gets held up at knifepoint and has his cell phone stolen from him, but he manages to get home in one piece.

norm: It's good for someone to stick up for their family.
situation: Bill's younger brother Bob is getting picked on at school and Bob asks him for help.
intention: Bill needs to decide how to help.
moral_action: Bill tells Bob that tomorrow he'll scare off the bully for him.
moral_consequence: Bob gets left alone by the bully after Bill tells the bully to knock it off or else.
immoral_action: Bill tells Bob that he needs to learn to stand up for himself and that Bill can't fight all Bob's battles.
immoral_consequence: Billy continues to get picked on at school because Bob refused to intercede.

norm: You shouldn't take things from your parents.
situation: Sally found a beautiful bracelet in her mom's drawer while looking for something else.
intention: Sally wants to obtain the bracelet.
moral_action: Sally asks about the bracelet and requests it for her upcoming birthday.
moral_consequence: Sally gets the bracelet as a gift.
immoral_action: Sally takes the bracelet without asking.
immoral_consequence: Sally gets in trouble for taking the bracelet.

norm: It's not okay to be obsessed with an ex.
situation: Taylor just got into a relationship with Jack and is mainly doing it long-distance.
intention: Taylor wants to text her boyfriend.
moral_action: Taylor decides to text Jack only a couple times a day, to build rapport.
moral_consequence: Jack is impressed with Taylor's texting skills, and they both hit it off and feel elated.
immoral_action: Taylor decides to text Jack every hour to build up a rapport with Jack.
immoral_consequence: Jack feels overwhelmed and tells Taylor to back off, while Taylor feels insulted.

norm: You shouldn't stalk your crush.
situation: Dave has a crush on Lila but is too nervous to talk to her, so he finds her on social media and sees that she works at a nearby bakery.
intention: Dave wants to find out more about Lila.
moral_action: Dave messages Lila on social media and strikes up a conversation about baking.
moral_consequence: Dave and Lila hit it off as they connect over baking and hobbies.
immoral_action: Dave goes to the bakery every day just to sit and stare at Lila.
immoral_consequence: Lila gets creeped out and asks the manager to ban Dave from their shop.

norm: It's good for a parent to treat their children well.
situation: Don's son David comes in second place at his track meet and is disappointed.
intention: Don wants to motivate David to do better.
moral_action: Don tells David that his performance was excellent and that there is no shame in taking second place.
moral_consequence: It lifts David's spirits to hear his father say that his performance was excellent, and he is motivated to keep training and trying to win.
immoral_action: Don tells David that he is ashamed of his lack of effort and that coming in second place is just as bad as coming in last.
immoral_consequence: David is angry and hurt that his father called his performance bad, and he does not feel motivated at all.

norm: It's wrong to ignore your boss's calls to you.
situation: Anna is tired and sick of her workplace.
intention: Anna wants to have a day off.
moral_action: Anna called and left a message that she was not going to be in that day.
moral_consequence: When he boss called, Anna answered, and they determined if she would use personal or sick time off.
immoral_action: Anna does not call anyone to tell them she is not going to work, she ignores the calls from her boss.
immoral_consequence: Anna is terminated the next day.

norm: You shouldn't organize race based on hierarchy because that's wrong.
situation: Savanna is planning a lesson that covers the relationship between colonists and natives to her students.
intention: Savanna wants to teach her kids.
moral_action: Savanna shows her students a documentary that presents both sides in a respectful way.
moral_consequence: Savanna gains a new appreciation of history through the video and her student's reactions.
immoral_action: Savanna creates a pyramid chart with the natives on the bottom and the colonists on the top.
immoral_consequence: Savanna is called out for being racist by her students.

norm: It's bad to give gifts people are allergic to.
situation: Sam's girlfriend, who is allergic to some foods, has a birthday today.
intention: Sam wants to buy her a gift.
moral_action: Sam checks with one of his girlfriend's friends for an appropriate food gift to give, then buys it.
moral_consequence: Sam's girlfriend loves the food.
immoral_action: Sam buys some food for his girlfriend without checking the ingredients to see if she has an allergy to it.
immoral_consequence: Sam's girlfriend has an allergic reaction and goes to the hospital.

norm: It's wrong to abandon your friends when they need you.
situation: John is at home when his friend Eric calls him asking him for a ride home as he's stuck at a store alone.
intention: John wants to go to a movie tonight.
moral_action: John quickly drives to pick Eric up, and they both go to the movie together.
moral_consequence: Eric is very grateful and thinks John is a great friend and likes him.
immoral_action: John says he can't because he's very busy and drives off to his movie.
immoral_consequence: Eric gets very depressed and feels that John isn't really his friend.

norm: It's fun to take a cruise with your friends.
situation: Annie's friends told her that they were going on a cruise in a few months.
intention: Annie wanted to do something with her friends over the summer.
moral_action: Annie booked a cabin on the same cruise that her friends were going on.
moral_consequence: Annie had a great time on the cruise with her friends during the summer.
immoral_action: Annie invited her friends to her house to help her clean.
immoral_consequence: Annie's friends started to stay away from her because they thought she was a bore.

norm: You should not ignore your spouse.
situation: Amanda is having a stressful day.
intention: Amanda wants to relax at home after work.
moral_action: Amanda cuddles up with her husband and watches a movie.
moral_consequence: Amanda and her husband have a good evening and decompress from the day together which strengthens their relationship.
immoral_action: Amanda plays games on her phone all evening and barely talks to her husband.
immoral_consequence: Her husband feels hurt and resents Amanda.

norm: You shouldn't lose belongings that don't belong to you.
situation: Karen is at May's house, and they decide to go dancing, but she didn't bring the right evening attire.
intention: Karen wants to borrow some jewelry from May.
moral_action: Karen asks May if she can wear a necklace and May lets her pick out the one Karen likes the most to use.
moral_consequence: May gets her necklace back in the same condition from Karen the next day, and she continues to loan her items.
immoral_action: Karen loses May's earrings she borrowed at a man's house that she met the night they went dancing, but he said they aren't there.
immoral_consequence: May is very upset with Karen because the earrings have sentimental value, and they have an argument.

norm: You shouldn't be with someone you don't have feelings for.
situation: Dan is looking for a romantic partner online.
intention: Dan wants to bring someone along to an event he is attending.
moral_action: Dan realizes he can't find a date so quickly, so he asks a friend to join him.
moral_consequence: Dan and his friend end up enjoying the event, they always have a great time together.
immoral_action: Dan asks Tina, who likes him and will agree to go to the event, even though he doesn't like her.
immoral_consequence: Dan leads Tina on by inviting her, and she is really upset when he reveals he isn't actually interested.

norm: It's wrong to abandon someone when they need you most.
situation: Alex's son from a previous marriage has messaged Alex saying his mom is abusing him and that he wants to come live with Alex.
intention: Alex wants to keep his current family happy.
moral_action: Alex tells his family about his son's situation and works out an agreement with his wife.
moral_consequence: Alex's son is able to get away from his father and have some stability in his life.
immoral_action: Alex ignores his son so his current wife and children won't have to deal with his son.
immoral_consequence: Alex's son continues to suffer from his mother's abuse and feels abandoned by Alex.

norm: It's wrong to make offensive jokes.
situation: Danny is hanging out with a group of friends which includes an Asian American.
intention: Danny wants to tell a joke.
moral_action: Danny tells a funny joke that isn't offensive towards anybody in the group.
moral_consequence: Danny's Asian American friend laughs at the joke along with the rest if the group.
immoral_action: Danny tells a racial joke which is offensive towards his Asian American friend.
immoral_consequence: Danny's Asian American friend is hurt and offended that Danny would tell such a disrespectful joke.

norm: You shouldn't reject your parents.
situation: Jeremy's parents Beth and Louis have recently converted to Christianity after being lifelong atheists.
intention: Jeremy wants to comment on Beth and Louis's new faith.
moral_action: Jeremy congratulates his parents on finding something that feels fulfilling for their lives.
moral_consequence: Jeremy and his parents bond and his parents are thankful that he was understanding of their conversion.
immoral_action: Jeremy tells his parents that they can no longer be a part of his life, as their faith is one he disagrees with.
immoral_consequence: Jeremy's parents grow isolated and sad, feeling rejected by their son.

norm: Shouting at others when you're upset isn't polite.
situation: James came home with a headache, and his roommates kept talking loudly.
intention: James wants peace and quiet that won't trigger his headaches.
moral_action: James asks his roommates to keep it down so his head doesn't throb.
moral_consequence: James' roommates agree to be quiet and one volunteers to make him a cup of tea.
immoral_action: James screams at his roommates that they're inconsiderate jerks for being so loud.
immoral_consequence: James' roommates say that he's the jerk, before abandoning him to go out to a bar together.

norm: It's not okay to vandalize someone's personal possessions.
situation: Sharon and Jared have a huge fight which results in them breaking up, and Sharon is still angry when she sees Jared's car.
intention: Sharon wants to release her frustrations on something.
moral_action: Sharon punches the boxing sandbag in her backyard.
moral_consequence: Sharon feels better.
immoral_action: Sharon damages the tires with a sharp knife.
immoral_consequence: Jared's neighbor sees her and reports her to the police which results in Sharon being arrested.

norm: You shouldn't try to fool someone with dementia.
situation: Samantha's grandmother has dementia and her favorite video game was just remastered, but she can't afford to purchase it.
intention: Samantha wants to obtain a copy of the new game.
moral_action: Samantha tells her grandmother she really wants to buy a new game but is broke.
moral_consequence: Samantha's grandmother offers to buy the game for her as a gift.
immoral_action: Samantha approached her grandmother, tells her that it's her birthday and asks for birthday money.
immoral_consequence: Her grandmother having a better day, checks the calendar, realizes she is lying, and kicks her out of the house.

norm: It's wrong to have sexual thoughts about one's family.
situation: At a family reunion, George is asked by his cousin Gloria how she looks in her new dress.
intention: George wants to give Gloria a compliment.
moral_action: George tells Gloria that she looks elegant in the dress.
moral_consequence: Gloria thanks George for the kinds words about her appearance.
immoral_action: George tells Gloria that she looks good enough to shag.
immoral_consequence: Gloria walks away from George with a disgusted look on her face.

norm: You should not fap at work.
situation: James works as a security guard in a high-tech office building at night.
intention: James wants to amuse himself during his long, boring shifts.
moral_action: James begins writing a fantasy/detective novel on his work computer during his long, isolated night shifts.
moral_consequence: James publishes the novel in installments on his blog and gets lots of positive feedback from his fans.
immoral_action: James begins watching porn on his work computer and masturbating.
immoral_consequence: An employee returns late one night to collect their laptop and catches James, getting him fired.

norm: It's good to help people out with their problems.
situation: Jennifer just started her new office job and noticed that one of her co-workers is having trouble figuring something out.
intention: Jennifer wants to make a positive impression on her supervisor.
moral_action: Jennifer walks up to her coworker and asks him if he would like some help with the problem.
moral_consequence: Jennifer's coworker is grateful that she helped him figure out the problem and invites her out to lunch.
immoral_action: Jennifer decides to work out the problem on her own and submits the solution to her supervisor before her coworker does.
immoral_consequence: Jennifer's coworker forms a negative impression of her and tells the rest of the office about how ruthless and competitive she is.

norm: It's good to quit self-harming behavior.
situation: Penny is an alcoholic who has been feeling depressed and stressed.
intention: Penny wants to make her pain go away.
moral_action: Penny decides to quit drinking and go to therapy.
moral_consequence: Penny feels physically and mentally healthier.
immoral_action: Penny continues to drink to dull the pain.
immoral_consequence: Penny spirals further into depression and finds it increasingly difficult to recover.

norm: It's good to sew a dress for your daughter.
situation: Burton is a single father and his daughter got the lead in a school play which requires a specific costume.
intention: Burton wants to help his daughter prepare for the roll.
moral_action: Burton uses the internet to learn to sew, so he can construct a costume for his daughter's roll.
moral_consequence: Burton's dress looks great and his daughter is overjoyed because she loves it.
immoral_action: Burton goes over the character's lines with his daughter but doesn't ever fulfill the costume needs.
immoral_consequence: Burton's daughter is upset that she doesn't have the right costume for the play and lets it ruin her fun.

norm: It's bad to insult people.
situation: Mitch is a politician who just won an election against another black politician named James.
intention: Mitch wants to call James.
moral_action: Mitch tells James that he has a bright future in politics and tells him not to give up.
moral_consequence: James feels inspired and is appreciative of Mitch for going out of his way to tell him that.
immoral_action: Mitch tells James that maybe he should become a rapper instead.
immoral_consequence: James feels disrespected by that and hangs up the phone immediately.

norm: It's important to show sympathy to disadvantaged members of society.
situation: Joel is walking down the street when he sees a homeless man asking for money on the sidewalk.
intention: Joel wants to respond to the homeless man.
moral_action: Joel gives the homeless man money for food.
moral_consequence: The homeless man will think Joel is generous.
immoral_action: Joel tells the homeless man that he's in his situation because he's lazy.
immoral_consequence: The homeless man will think Joel is cruel.

norm: It is rude to only think of yourself.
situation: Liz got a large inheritance from her deceased uncle and has a friend who needs money to pay rent.
intention: Liz wants to figure out what to do with the money.
moral_action: Liz offers to help her friend pay their rent and uses the leftover money to go on a small local trip.
moral_consequence: Liz's friend is extremely grateful for the help and is able to live in their apartment for a while longer.
immoral_action: Liz decides to use the money to go on a nice trip to Europe by herself.
immoral_consequence: Liz's friend is unable to pay their rent and has to move out of their apartment.

norm: You shouldn't refuse your bosses' orders.
situation: Jason is on site working an entry level construction job where the foreman has laid out specific rolls for each worker.
intention: Jason wants to get through the work day.
moral_action: Jason sticks to the script so to speak and does each task he was assigned in order.
moral_consequence: Due to staying on task and busy, Jason is finished with the work day before he has the opportunity to think about it.
immoral_action: Jason skirts around his assigned duties and performs tasks outside of his qualifications because he thinks it'll get the work done quicker.
immoral_consequence: Jason compromises the construction quality with shoddy work and is fired for his negligence.

norm: It's good to get divorced if you're unhappy.
situation: Freya and Nathan are in an unhappy marriage but have two children who they both love.
intention: Freya wants to do what is best for the kids.
moral_action: Freya decides to divorce Nathan and find a partner she can be happy with because she believes the kids should not have unhappy parents.
moral_consequence: Freya's children are upset at first but quickly adjust to having two loving and happy households instead of one unhappy one.
immoral_action: Freya decides to stay with Nathan to provide stability for the kids because she believes that will best for them.
immoral_consequence: Freya's children sense their parents are unhappy and learn unhealthy relationship behaviors from them.

norm: You should never abuse your significant other.
situation: Mike was a mixed martial arts fighter that had just gotten married.
intention: Mike wants to hit something to work out.
moral_action: Mike sets up a punching bag in the middle of the garage.
moral_consequence: Mike's wife sets him up an account with the local gym to work out there.
immoral_action: Mike gets his wife in a corner and starts to beat her.
immoral_consequence: Mike's wife leaves him immediately and files for divorce soon after.

norm: It's wrong to sacrifice customer's privacy.
situation: Janet had to deal with a rude customer while doing customer service.
intention: Janet wanted to post on social media about her bad experience.
moral_action: Janet posts about the experience without providing any identifying information.
moral_consequence: The customer doesn't have to worry about retribution from people on the internet.
immoral_action: Janet posts the customer's information in order to get them in trouble.
immoral_consequence: The customer's life is ruined after people on the internet contact their employer.

norm: You shouldn't discriminate against vegans.
situation: James is looking for a partner for an upcoming cupcake baking context, and an award-winning vegan pastry chef just asked him to partner up.
intention: James wants to pick the partner who will most increase his chances of winning the bakeoff.
moral_action: James accepts the partnership because he's interested in learning new baking techniques.
moral_consequence: James and his partner cruise to first place and have their cupcake featured on the cover of Bon Appetit.
immoral_action: James turns down the partnership request because he thinks vegan food is for pussies.
immoral_consequence: The vegan pastry chef finds a vegan partner and easily defeats James' team in the bakeoff.

norm: You should not be loud and disrupt others.
situation: Amy is celebrating her new promotion at a bar with coworkers.
intention: Amy wants to have fun at the bar.
moral_action: At the party, Amy makes sure to tell her coworkers how much she appreciates them and enjoys working with them.
moral_consequence: Amy's boss sees how well Amy interacts with her coworkers and assigns her to lead an important project.
immoral_action: Amy starts dancing on tables and singing obnoxiously at the bar.
immoral_consequence: Amy's boss is embarrassed by Amy's behavior and rescinds the promotion.

norm: You shouldn't be so unreliable at work.
situation: Paula has gotten a new job after being unemployed for several months.
intention: Paula wants to pass the time at her job.
moral_action: Paula creates a checklist for work everyday and spends the day trying to complete as much of it as possible.
moral_consequence: Paula becomes promoted and moves up in the company.
immoral_action: Paula spends her time at work on her phone and talking to other co-workers.
immoral_consequence: Paula ends up getting reprimanded before eventually getting fired.

norm: It's good to care about your family's health.
situation: Greg's kids love sweets, and it's really hard to get them to eat vegetables.
intention: Greg wants his kids to be happy.
moral_action: Greg wants his kids to eat fruits and vegetables, but he allows them to eat sweets in moderation.
moral_consequence: Greg's kids are happier since their bodies are healthier, and they aren't too upset.
immoral_action: Greg allows his kids to continue eating sweets if they want to.
immoral_consequence: Greg's kids' health continues to deteriorate, and they continue to gain weight.

norm: You should ask for forgiveness when you do something wrong
situation: Carl is poking fun at Beth and accidentally hurts her feelings.
intention: Carls wants to try to cheer Betty up.
moral_action: Carl sits down and apologizes to Beth for hurting her feelings.
moral_consequence: Beth is able to forgive Carl.
immoral_action: Carl starts making fun of himself.
immoral_consequence: Beth still feels down but laughs at his jokes.

norm: It's rude to embarrass people.
situation: John was bored from sitting in Miss Parker's English class.
intention: John wants to get out of class.
moral_action: John raises his hand and asks if he can go to the restroom.
moral_consequence: Miss Parker gives John the hall pass, and he is able to leave the classroom for a few minutes.
immoral_action: John starts calling the teacher names and mocking and laughing at her.
immoral_consequence: Miss Parker sends John to the office, and he is given detention after school.

norm: It is good to be committed to your relationship.
situation: Kent's girlfriend is going to serve in a foreign country for a year.
intention: Kent wants to say goodbye to his girlfriend.
moral_action: Kent says goodbye and promises to be faithful to her while she's gone.
moral_consequence: Kent's girlfriend is encouraged and feels supported.
immoral_action: Kent tells his girlfriend goodbye and that their relationship is over because she is leaving.
immoral_consequence: Kent's girlfriend cries and becomes depressed.

norm: It is wrong to murder people's pets
situation: Fred's neighbor has a dog that is constantly barking in the backyard, and he grows increasingly annoyed by it.
intention: Fred wants the dog to stop barking.
moral_action: Fred explains the situation to his neighbor and kindly asks if he can find a way to keep the dog quiet.
moral_consequence: The neighbor trains the dog not to bark so much and Fred is relieved by the increased peace and quiet.
immoral_action: One night Fred sneaks into his neighbors yard and kills the dog.
immoral_consequence: Fred's actions are caught on his neighbor's security camera, and he is arrested for the crime.

norm: It is kind to donate things to the less fortunate.
situation: Helga is cleaning out her house and has collected many possessions she no longer wants or needs.
intention: Helga wants to get rid of the possessions she no longer wants or needs.
moral_action: Helga finds a secondhand store that she can bring the items to as somebody else may have a use for them.
moral_consequence: Helga's donation of the items helps her society give those with economic disadvantages a way of procuring products at a less harmful price.
immoral_action: Helga throws everything she doesn't desire into her trash to be rid of it for good.
immoral_consequence: Helga's wastefulness adds to the larger trash problem of her society.

norm: It's good to respect the plans of others.
situation: Jessie is on a date with John, and Maggie, her coworker, needs help with an issue on her project with Jessie.
intention: Jessie wants to solve the issue.
moral_action: Maggie searches for the solution to the problem on a tech website.
moral_consequence: Maggie gains a deeper understand on the issues surrounding the problem.
immoral_action: Maggie continues pestering Jessie during her date insisting that solving the issue is more important.
immoral_consequence: Maggie spends the evening getting more and more frustrated with Jessie.

norm: You should be supportive of a friend that is upset.
situation: John sees that his friend Tony is crying because his dog died.
intention: John wants Tony to stop crying.
moral_action: John tells Tony his dog is in a better place and would want to see him smiling.
moral_consequence: Tony smiles for a bit and eventually he stops crying.
immoral_action: John tells Tony not to cry like a baby and get over the dog.
immoral_consequence: Tony gets angry with John and never speaks to him again.

norm: It is bad to betray your siblings' trust.
situation: Blake is hanging out at home when his sister's boyfriend Mitch flirts with him.
intention: Blake doesn't want to hurt Mitch's feelings.
moral_action: Blake turns on the television to Mitch's favorite tv show and asks him information about the characters.
moral_consequence: Blake uses the information he learns from Mitch to impress another cute guy.
immoral_action: Blake returns Mitch's advances allowing Mitch to kiss him.
immoral_consequence: Blake's relationship with his sister is destroyed when she walks in on them.

norm: It is kind to be welcoming to a new student
situation: It's lunchtime and Jacob is entering the cafeteria along with Martin who is a new student.
intention: Jacob wants to find a table in the cafeteria.
moral_action: Jacob invites Martin to join him and his friends at their lunch table.
moral_consequence: Martin feels included and welcome.
immoral_action: Jacob decides to sit with his friends and leave Martin alone.
immoral_consequence: Martin feels unwelcome at the school.

norm: Shunning people close to you is hurtful.
situation: Sally is a very religious person, and has found out that her friend Jack is gay.
intention: Sally wants to follow her religion.
moral_action: Sally disagrees with Jack's homosexuality, but agrees to still be his friend.
moral_consequence: Sally and Jack come to understand each other better and become better friends.
immoral_action: Sally says she can't abide by Jack's orientation and cuts him from her life.
immoral_consequence: Jack becomes depressed, and Sally's other mutual friends cut her off, as well.

norm: It is good to confide in your significant other
situation: Jonah just found out that she lost her grandfather and is staying over at her boyfriend's house.
intention: Jonah wants to get her feelings out.
moral_action: Jonah tells her partner what happened and cries while he listens to what happened.
moral_consequence: Jonah's grief is manageable, and she begins to feel better about what's going on.
immoral_action: Jonah withdraws and won't talk to anyone, hurting herself to express what she is feeling.
immoral_consequence: Jonah's mental health declines, and she begins to lose support from her partner.

norm: You shouldn't be around other people if you're ill.
situation: Matt a poor man sick with the flu, and he has work in an hour.
intention: Matt wants to make money.
moral_action: Matt calls work, and asks if he use one of his paid sick leave days.
moral_consequence: Matt is able to rest and recover from his illness.
immoral_action: Matt goes into work for his shift.
immoral_consequence: Matt faces backlash from his coworkers who worry about being exposed to his illness.

norm: It's rude to leave someone because their body changed.
situation: Tammy feels less attracted to her partner after they have put on a lot of weight.
intention: Tammy wants to be in a passionate relationship.
moral_action: Tammy makes going to the gym a couple's activity.
moral_consequence: Tammy's partner regains confidence and health.
immoral_action: Tammy leaves her partner for someone who is more attractive.
immoral_consequence: Tammy's partner is devastated that she has left.

norm: It is creepy to send long emotional texts to people.
situation: John receives a text from Sandy about a work lunch that's being planned for tomorrow afternoon.
intention: John wants to respond to the text.
moral_action: John replies with a quick message telling Sandy that he thinks the lunch would be productive, and he'll be there.
moral_consequence: Sandy is delighted that her lunch plans are coming together smoothly.
immoral_action: John replies with a ten paragraph text to Sandy explaining that he's loved her for years and thinks they're meant to be together.
immoral_consequence: Sandy feels extremely uncomfortable and becomes afraid to see John at work tomorrow.

norm: It is good to treat your dog for fleas.
situation: Wesley's Dog is scratching itself relentlessly.
intention: Wesley wants the dog to stop itching itself.
moral_action: Wesley takes hi dog to the vet and finds out about the fleas.
moral_consequence: Wesley's dog gets flea treatment, and stops itching itself.
immoral_action: Wesley hits the dog every time it scratches itself.
immoral_consequence: Wesley's dog becomes terrified of Wesley and won't come near him anymore.

norm: It's not okay to be demanding.
situation: Ichiro wants to go to the park, but his mother is busy working on her computer.
intention: Ichiro wants to have fun.
moral_action: Ichiro invites his friend over to play his favorite park games in his backyard.
moral_consequence: Ichiro enjoys spending time with his friends.
immoral_action: Ichiro asks in mother to take him to the park every five minutes.
immoral_consequence: Ichiro is sent to time out for the rest of the afternoon.

norm: You should take responsibility for the things you've done.
situation: Dave is cleaning up his home and accidentally knocks over his wife's favorite knick-knack.
intention: Dave wants to explain what happened to his wife.
moral_action: Dave explains to his wife that he bumped the knick-knack while dusting the shelf and it fell off and broke.
moral_consequence: Dave feels relief for telling his wife the truth after she forgives him for the accident.
immoral_action: Dave tells his wife that the dog ran through the room and knocked over her item.
immoral_consequence: Dave feels a deep sense of guilt and shame for lying to his partner.

norm: Is wrong to try to kill yourself
situation: Dave, who is married to Kelly is an extremely depressed man struggling with inner demons that burden him.
intention: Dave wants to be rid of his inner turmoil.
moral_action: Dave calls up a therapy clinic and asks them if he can come in to make an appointment for therapy.
moral_consequence: Kelly is delighted to see Dave taking a proactive and positive approach to fixing his depression.
immoral_action: Dave takes a knife and slits his wrists thinking that death will set him free from his darkness.
immoral_consequence: Kelly is devastated that her husband is suicidal and is sad and depressed about his survival.

norm: It's wrong to not obey your parents.
situation: James is not letting his son Dan play video games until he cleans up his room.
intention: Dan wants to play video games.
moral_action: Dan cleans his room and lets his dad know in order to be allowed to play video games.
moral_consequence: James is surprised that Dan actually cleaned his room and ends up being proud.
immoral_action: Dan plays video games when his dad isn't paying attention and hasn't cleaned his room.
immoral_consequence: James becomes upset when he sees that Dan hasn't cleaned his room yet.

norm: It's rude to ignore your friends for no reason.
situation: Ben is reading a book when his friend asks him a question.
intention: Ben wants to consider responding to his friend.
moral_action: Ben quickly answers his friend's question before returning to his book.
moral_consequence: Ben's friend appreciates and thanks Ben for the answer before leaving Ben to his book.
immoral_action: Ben decides to ignore his friend completely and simply continue reading his book.
immoral_consequence: Ben's friend start to think Ben is an unfriendly person and becomes less of a friend to him.

norm: You shouldn't throw your future away.
situation: Steve is trying to decide on what he wants to do with himself after school.
intention: Steve wants to take it easy for a while after high school.
moral_action: Steve takes two night classes a week to keep educated and involved.
moral_consequence: Steve takes a little longer than normal to get through school, but finds a great job after.
immoral_action: Steve decides to scrounge off his parents for a few years, doing absolutely nothing.
immoral_consequence: Life passes Steve by, and nobody wants to hire him for the gaps in his resume.

norm: It is bad to defecate in the shower or bathtub
situation: While taking a shower after working out at the gym Frank is suddenly overcome with the urge to poop.
intention: Frank wants to void his bowels as soon as possible.
moral_action: Frank exits the shower and goes to the nearest toilet to poop.
moral_consequence: Franks gym membership is not put at risk, so he continues to attend the gym.
immoral_action: Since he is alone in the shower area Frank decides to poop in the shower and hopes it goes down the drain.
immoral_consequence: A fellow gym member walks in on Frank and reports him to the staff which results in Franks gym membership being revoked.

norm: Losing your temper is frowned upon.
situation: Ray and his wife Ellen are out of town and are looking for a restaurant.
intention: Ray wants Ellen to help him with the directions, so he can keep his eye on the road.
moral_action: When Ellen gives Ray the wrong directions, and he realizes they went the wrong way he tells her to look at the directions again.
moral_consequence: Ellen tells Ray she's sorry and looks at the directions again.
immoral_action: When Ellen gives Ray the wrong directions by mistake he takes a wrong turn, so he gets mad and yells at her.
immoral_consequence: Ellen gets upset and tells him that she was just trying to help.

norm: You shouldn't try to get back at your ex.
situation: Sam has just proposed to his partner Jo.
intention: Jo wants to show off how happy she is.
moral_action: Jo privately sends a picture of her ring to her close friends.
moral_consequence: Jo's friends are happy and excited for her.
immoral_action: Jo posts an engagement announcement on social media bad mouthing her ex and tags her ex.
immoral_consequence: Jo's friends think she is petty and shallow.

norm: It's mean to make jokes about your friend's dancing.
situation: Jane is at a wedding reception and notices her friend Bob started dancing for the first time.
intention: Jane wants to talk to Bob about his dancing.
moral_action: Jane compliments Bob for his courage to get on the dance floor, and dances with him.
moral_consequence: Jane and Bob enjoy each other on the dance floor and Bob embraces Jane.
immoral_action: Jane tells Bob he dances like a, 'square', and continues to make jokes about his dancing.
immoral_consequence: Bob feels humiliated and stops dancing while him and Jane argue.

norm: You should be more respectful of people's property.
situation: Jack and his friends are playing in his backyard on a sunny day.
intention: Jack wants to have fun with his friends.
moral_action: Jack sets up an inflatable pool and swims in the pool with his friends.
moral_consequence: His neighbor feels secure about Jack's non-threatening activity.
immoral_action: Jack tosses a ball around with his friends, and he accidentally hit a window of his neighbor.
