norm: It is wrong to go into someone's room without permission.
situation: Mary's hair is wet, and she just remembered that her roommate Anna most recently borrowed her hair dryer.
intention: Mary wants to find her hair dryer.
moral_action: Mary texts Anna to ask if she knows where the hair dryer is and Anna tells her to go get it off of her desk in her room.
moral_consequence: Anna is grateful that Mary asked her before searching all over the place for it and messing up her room.
immoral_action: Mary goes into Anna's room and searches for the hairdryer, which she finds on Anna's desk.
immoral_consequence: Anna is upset that Mary went into her room without permission and this strains their relationship.

norm: It is inconsiderate to monopolize a restroom
situation: Tommy has to use the public restroom, but he doesn't like other people being in there at the same time as him.
intention: Tommy wants to use the restroom alone.
moral_action: Tommy waits until the restroom is empty and then goes inside.
moral_consequence: Tommy uses the restroom without worrying about anyone else being inside.
immoral_action: Tommy enters the restroom and blocks the door so no one else can enter.
immoral_consequence: Tommy gets yelled at by other people from outside who want to enter.

norm: It's bad to take your anger out with your fists.
situation: Justin is out clubbing with friends when he notices a guy screaming at his girlfriend.
intention: Justin wants to confront the guy.
moral_action: Justin goes over to the guy and tells him to knock it off, or he'll call security.
moral_consequence: The guy leaves the club and his girlfriend thanks Justin for sticking up for her.
immoral_action: Justin goes over to the guy and punches him in the face.
immoral_consequence: Justin and the guy get into a big fight and are kicked out of the club before they are arrested.

norm: It is good to respect family.
situation: Shaun is at his grandmother's birthday party.
intention: Shaun wants to make his grandmother happy.
moral_action: Shaun reads a poem he wrote about his grandmother out loud.
moral_consequence: Shaun's family are proud of Shaun for being so thoughtful.
immoral_action: Shaun makes insulting jokes about his uncle who his grandmother dislikes.
immoral_consequence: Shaun's family get angry at Shaun for being rude.

norm: It's okay to be protective of your child.
situation: Patty's daughter wants to go to the park with her friends, but Patty just heard something in the news about a possible kidnapper.
intention: Patty wants her daughter to be happy.
moral_action: Patty doesn't let her daughter go to the park, but she invites her friends over, so they can watch a movie together.
moral_consequence: Patty's daughter stays safe and still ends up having fun with her friends.
immoral_action: Patty lets her daughter go to the park with her friends by themselves with no supervision.
immoral_consequence: Pat's daughter is at risk of being preyed on by predators at the park.

norm: It's wrong to discriminate based on age.
situation: Bill is deciding between a 55 and a 28 year old applicant for a position in his tech company.
intention: Bill wants to hire the best candidate for the job.
moral_action: Bill hires the applicant that will better contribute to the companies growth.
moral_consequence: Bill gains the right employee for the position.
immoral_action: Bill decides to hire the younger candidate because he feels his youth will give him more vigor.
immoral_consequence: Bill substitutes vigor for experience.

norm: You shouldn't compare someone to an animal.
situation: James is frustrated that his kids don't pick up their toys because he just stepped on a lego.
intention: James wants to encourage his children to clean up after themselves.
moral_action: James takes his children's devices away until they pick up all their toys.
moral_consequence: James' children whine, but eventually capitulate, so they can get back online.
immoral_action: James tells his children that if they keep living like pigs, he's going to move them into a pigpen in the backyard.
immoral_consequence: James' children burst into tears and tell their mother, who then scolds James.

norm: It's rude to ask your classmates for their food.
situation: Bella is at school eating lunch with her friends, and she sees one of her friends with a twinkie.
intention: Bella wants to eat a twinkie.
moral_action: Bella stops at a store on the way home from school and buys a twinkie.
moral_consequence: Bella's friend still likes Bella and everyone is happy.
immoral_action: Bella asks her friend with the twinkie over and over if she can have it.
immoral_consequence: Bella's friend feels very uncomfortable and eats lunch away from Bella from then on.

norm: It is nasty to give your partner the cold shoulder.
situation: Pete and Mandy are fighting and are angry at each other.
intention: Pete wants to let Mandy know his displeasure.
moral_action: Pete sits down with Mandy and expresses why he feels hurt.
moral_consequence: A dialogue starts and Pete and Mandy work through the argument and the pain.
immoral_action: Pete refuses to talk with Mandy for a week.
immoral_consequence: Mandy refuses to talk with Pete as well, and the two eventually break up.

norm: It's okay to report theft.
situation: Tammy is leaving work when she realizes someone has smashed in her car mirrors.
intention: Tammy wants to find the person who vandalized her car.
moral_action: Tammy reports the incident to higher-ups at her company.
moral_consequence: The company seizes surveillance footage and finds the person responsible for vandalizing Tammy's car.
immoral_action: Too afraid to stir things up at work, Tammy goes home to think about who could have smashed her car mirrors.
immoral_consequence: Tammy never finds the person who vandalized her car.

norm: You shouldn't make others sick.
situation: Alice is in the kitchen making chicken and salad for dinner for her hungry kids.
intention: Alice wants to hurry up and feed her children.
moral_action: Alice throws a salad together and tells the kids to start with that while she finished the chicken.
moral_consequence: Alice's kids feel better because they have something in their stomachs.
immoral_action: Alice is rushing and doesn't cook the chicken all the way.
immoral_consequence: Alice's kids get food poisoning and miss school the next day.

norm: You shouldn't make jokes about priests.molesting kids.
situation: Tim is at a Sunday church service with his friend who invited him to come.
intention: Tim wants to enjoy the experience.
moral_action: Tim takes in the scenery and architecture of the church and compliments it to his friend.
moral_consequence: Tim's friend appreciates that Tim is taking in the whole experience.
immoral_action: When the priest comes out Tim leans over to his friend and cracks a joke about the priest being a pervert.
immoral_consequence: Tim's friend and others in the congregation that hear the joke are justifiably offended.

norm: Plagiarism is wrong.
situation: Terri received an advance from her publisher for a novel but feels uninspired.
intention: Terri wants her novel to be successful.
moral_action: Terri works hard on her novel and finds inspiration in her own life.
moral_consequence: Terri's book is a success and Terri feels it's well deserved.
immoral_action: Terri decides to borrow copious parts of an old, unknown novel.
immoral_consequence: Terri's novel is well received but Terri feels like a fraud.

norm: It's immoral to steal money from another person.
situation: Will, who is very dexterous, is out of a job and needs to pay bills and loan payments soon.
intention: Will wants to find another source of income.
moral_action: Will decides to go into business for himself and becomes a locksmith, using his dexterous hands to open locked doors.
moral_consequence: The people that Will helps are grateful to get back into their locked cars and houses without having to break in.
immoral_action: Will joins a gang of pickpockets and works the city streets, taking lots of money from rich people.
immoral_consequence: The people Will steals from are upset that their money goes missing and go to the police for justice.

norm: It's bad to not honor the promises you made.
situation: Ann promised Marie they would go out to lunch together, but Ann doesn't feel like going out.
intention: Ann wants to take Marie out for lunch.
moral_action: Ann decides to go anyway since she made a promise and Marie was looking forward to it.
moral_consequence: Ann ends up having a good time and doesn't regret going.
immoral_action: Ann tells Marie that she's sick to get out of her obligation, even though she isn’t, and reschedules for a different day.
immoral_consequence: Marie finds out Ann lied and gets angry with her.

norm: You should give an employee a warning before firing them.
situation: Jim has received notice that the department needs to be downsized starting with the lowest performers.
intention: Jim wants to raise his department's overall quality of work.
moral_action: Jim hands out warnings to those struggling with performance.
moral_consequence: The employees put in extra effort in order to keep their jobs.
immoral_action: Jim fires the employee with the worst performance to set an example.
immoral_consequence: The employees feel demoralized and work under stress which is a hindrance.

norm: You shouldn't pursue your teacher as a romantic interest.
situation: Bobby thinks his favorite teacher Brenda is smart and attractive, and stares at her during class.
intention: Bobby wants to express to his attraction.
moral_action: Bobby keeps his crush a secret and writes a journal about his feelings towards Brenda and keeps it to himself.
moral_consequence: Bobby eventually outgrows the crush, and Brenda is never put on the spot, and their student/teacher relationship stays strong.
immoral_action: Bobby stays after class and tells Brenda she's beautiful and would make a wonderful girlfriend.
immoral_consequence: Brenda tells Bobby it's not okay to date students and their relationship becomes awkward.

norm: It's not okay to brag to others.
situation: Don is a basketball player, and he's talking to a player on a team he just beat.
intention: Don wants to say something to the player.
moral_action: Don tells the player that it was really hard to beat them.
moral_consequence: The player feels proud, and they know that Don is just being nice.
immoral_action: Don tells the player that his team was so much better than his.
immoral_consequence: The player's feelings are hurt, and he feels that Don is a jerk.

norm: It's wrong to pretend things.
situation: Josh visited an African country, and the people there were asking him if he's an angel.
intention: Josh wants to respond to the people.
moral_action: Josh tells the people that he's a human being just like them.
moral_consequence: Josh feels closer to the people and likes that they trust him.
immoral_action: Josh tells the people that he was sent by God to serve them.
immoral_consequence: Josh feels guilty that the people believe him and wants to do something to help them.

norm: It's unacceptable fight over a cartoon.
situation: Delanie and Darcie were watching cartoons on TV last Saturday morning.
intention: Delanie wanted to watch another cartoon.
moral_action: Delanie waited until the cartoon was over and then asked Darcie if she would like to watch something else.
moral_consequence: Darcie was happy to change the channel and both girls continued to watch TV.
immoral_action: Delanie changed the channel, which made Darcie very mad and soon they were screaming at each other.
immoral_consequence: Delanie and Darcie were both grounded from TV for a week because of their behaviors.

norm: You shouldn't take someone else's things.
situation: Julie needs a dress for the prom, but can't afford the one she wants.
intention: Julie wants to look her best at the dance.
moral_action: Julie asks her mom to borrow the money and promises to pay it back with her summer job.
moral_consequence: Julie's mom makes the purchase and Julie looks stunning.
immoral_action: Julie takes her mom's credit card without asking and buys herself a beautiful gown.
immoral_consequence: Julie's mom finds out and tells her she can't go to the dance at all.

norm: You shouldn't eat all your friend's food.
situation: While hanging out at his friend Ryan's apartment, Tom is beginning to get hungry but didn't bring any food with him.
intention: Tom wants to get something to eat.
moral_action: Tom uses his cell phone to order Chinese delivery to the apartment.
moral_consequence: Ryan is happy to have dinner to eat and enjoys it.
immoral_action: Tom goes to Ryan's fridge and eats all the leftover food in it.
immoral_consequence: Ryan is sad and upset and has nothing to eat for dinner.

norm: It's wrong to fat shame people.
situation: Janie makes a New Years resolution to get in shape.
intention: Janie wants a workout partner to join her.
moral_action: Janie tells Alexis that she is such a hard worker that she would inspire her in her workouts.

immoral_action: Janie asks Alexis to come to the gym with her because Janie will look thinner next to Alexis.
immoral_consequence: Alexis won't go with Janie and breaks off their friendship because she is so hurt.

norm: It's good to let your employees have the weekend off.
situation: Brian has been promoted to president of this company.
intention: Brian wants to increase profits at the company.
moral_action: Brian hires an expert who helps to streamline operations to increase profit.
moral_consequence: The employees are happy that their jobs run more smoothly.
immoral_action: Brian decides to continue operations seven days a week causing some employees to add weekend hours to their schedules.
immoral_consequence: The employees are upset and look for new jobs elsewhere.

norm: It's bad to annoy people.
situation: Berry runs home after a long day of school, and he sees his mother working on her laptop.
intention: Berry wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Berry runs upstairs to play an online video game.
moral_consequence: Berry makes new friends while playing the game.
immoral_action: Berry asks his mother to play outside with him over and over again while poking her leg.
immoral_consequence: Berry's mother forces him to spend the rest of the afternoon locked in his room.

norm: It's bad to harm other people's pets.
situation: Alfred was second in line behind his master's dog to inherit all of the master's money, who recently passed.
intention: Alfred wants to obtain the money.
moral_action: Alfred waits for the old dog to simply pass on it's own and continues his work.
moral_consequence: Sure enough the dog passes away a few months later and Alfred gets the money.
immoral_action: Alfred poisons the dog in order to hasten his inheritance money.
immoral_consequence: Alfred is not caught, but people think it suspicious the dog died so soon after it's owner.

norm: It's good to warn others of any risks.
situation: Sam is at the beach with his friend Paul when he sees an ominous wave coming their way.
intention: Sam wants to evade the large wave.
moral_action: Sam quickly jumps into action and warns Paul of the wave as both boys run toward safety.
moral_consequence: Paul eludes the incoming wave and is thankful that Sam warned him.
immoral_action: Without saying a word Sam immediately runs up the beach away from the approaching wave.
immoral_consequence: Paul is struck by the wave, knocked over and nearly drowns before escaping the ocean's watery grasp.

norm: It's wrong not to listen to people.
situation: Jessica's friend is telling her about what they did over the weekend but Jessica isn't all that interested.
intention: Jessica wants to do something while her friend tells her about their weekend.

norm: It's nice to want to include your siblings in activities.

immoral_action: Billy tells his mother that she assumed he wants his brothers there, but he doesn't, and he doesn't care who else comes.

norm: It's rude to berate your significant other.
situation: Jennifer's boyfriend bought a different item at the store than the one she asked for.

moral_consequence: Jennifer's boyfriend is more careful to get the right stuff the next time he goes to the store.
immoral_action: Jennifer scolds her boyfriend in an angry way about getting the wrong item.

norm: It's bad to go to prison.

norm: Taking extra without permission is greedy.

norm: You should always help out a disabled person.

norm: You shouldn't say things to hurt your significant other

norm: It's not right to steal from those close to you.

norm: It is important to never drink and drive.

norm: It's not expected that you'll dump things on your head.

norm: You shouldn't lie to your children.

norm: Parents should encourage their children to get exercise.

norm: It is wrong to listen to other people's conversations.

norm: You should do what you can to protect the environment.

immoral_action: Figuring that everyone else is doing it, Maci takes her empty chip bag and soda can and tosses it into the ocean too.

norm: It's expected that spouses are kind to each other.

norm: It's important to fulfill your promises to others.

immoral_consequence: Waldo's best friend's significant other leaves him, and he decides to stop being Waldo's friend.

norm: It is irresponsible to skip work without calling your job.

norm: It's mean to make someone homeless.

norm: It's good to tell people thank you.

norm: You shouldn't dominate your kids-in-law.

immoral_consequence: Michael's wife disproves and ends up divorcing him.

norm: You shouldn't drink while you're driving.

norm: You should be there for others.

moral_consequence: Cam's brother feels appreciative and feels less scared about being stranded.
