moral_consequence: Ryan's crush thinks he is kind and tough for defending Todd in class.
immoral_action: Ryan thinks bullying will make him seem tough, so he mocks Todd for his Native heritage.
immoral_consequence: Ryan's crush notices immediately, thinks of him as a tough thug, and reports him to the Professor.

norm: It's wrong to lie.
situation: Red is standing before Al, his dad, and KEvin, the family pet, and a broken lamp lying on the floor.
intention: Red wants to explain why the lamp is broken.
moral_action: Red takes responsibility for breaking the lamp.
moral_consequence: Red, the true culprit is punished and justice prevails with none harmed undeservedly.
immoral_action: Red tells an untruth indicating Kevin broke the lamp.
immoral_consequence: Al inflicts corporal punishment upon Kevin who feels intense pain without knowing why and suffers.

norm: IS it not good to get your friends into trouble
situation: Dan was at a party that involved underage drinking, and police are asking him about it.
intention: Dan doesn't want to get in trouble.
moral_action: Dan tells the police that he's not aware of any underage drinking that was going on at the party.
moral_consequence: Dan's friends feel grateful for Dan, and they gain trust in him.
immoral_action: Dan snitches on his friends for drinking alcohol when they're under the legal age.
immoral_consequence: Dan's friends get into a lot of trouble, and their parents lose trust in them.

norm: It is good to laugh about things in your family.
situation: Victor is a teen who is out with his family on vacation, and his father is making corny dad jokes.
intention: Victor wants to respond to his father's bad jokes.
moral_action: Victor says the jokes are bad, but he laughs at them anyway.
moral_consequence: Victor and his dad bond over the experience and become closer.
immoral_action: Victor rolls his eyes and says that is dad is lame.
immoral_consequence: Victor's dad feels hurt and the relationship between the two of them grows cold.

norm: It's wrong to call your friends names.
situation: Richard and his best friend Josh are about to play a game online.
intention: Richard needs to make Josh's gamer id for the game.
moral_action: Richard asks Josh what he wants as his user id.
moral_consequence: Josh appreciates Richard considering his feelings which improves their friendship.
immoral_action: Richard creates an id based on one of Josh's most embarrassing moments.
immoral_consequence: Josh becomes mad at Richard which hurts their friendship.

norm: It's expected to do favors for a friend.
situation: Victoria is watching television on the couch when her roommate texts her asking her to walk their hyperactive dog.
intention: Victoria doesn't want to miss a moment of her favorite show.
moral_action: Victoria asks another one of her friends to record the show before she takes the dog on a walk.
moral_consequence: Getting out of the house improves Victoria's mental state.
immoral_action: Victoria does not reply to her friend and continues watching television.
immoral_consequence: Victoria has to clean up the apartment when the dog makes a mess in the living room.

norm: It's good to rescue stray animals.
situation: Nicholas has many pets at his home and recently noticed a cat that has been hanging out around his property.
intention: Nicholas wants to keep an eye on the cat.
moral_action: Nicholas starts putting food and water out for the cat before slowly introducing himself to it more and more until it becomes another one of his pets.
moral_consequence: The cat gets to live a long and comfortable life inside Nicholas' home.
immoral_action: Nicholas doesn't put out any food or water for the cat and just watches it from afar.
immoral_consequence: The cat sees no reason to be around Nicholas' house and soon moves on.

norm: You can't be expected to pay everyone's way.
situation: Cherry doesn't have a lot of money, and her friends are pressuring her into treating them to lunch.
intention: Cherry wants to make everyone happy.
moral_action: Cherry offers everyone to drop by her house for a nice home cooked meal.
moral_consequence: Cherry and her friends become closer over eating in a quiet environment.
immoral_action: Cherry takes her friends to an expensive buffet, and she pays for the entire party with her debit card.
immoral_consequence: Cherry is unable to pay for her bills.

norm: You shouldn't eat loudly around others.
situation: Frank is at a crowded diner eating his sandwich.
intention: Frank wants to finish his sandwich.
moral_action: Frank keeps his mouth closed while quietly chewing his sandwich.
moral_consequence: Frank is seen as polite and considerate of others around him.
immoral_action: Frank loudly chews his sandwich.
immoral_consequence: Customers next to Frank are grossed out and thinks Frank is a slob.

norm: Allowing homeless people into your home is dangerous.
situation: George has befriended a homeless guy who camps out on his street, even as a blizzard is coming their way.
intention: George wants to help the homeless guy.
moral_action: George takes the homeless guy to a homeless shelter.
moral_consequence: George is safe in his house.
immoral_action: George invites the homeless guy to stay with him in his house for a few days.
immoral_consequence: The homeless guy gets high, gets in a fight with George and hurts him badly.

norm: You should respect others' opinions.
situation: David is talking to some friends about basketball and one of them disagrees with him about which team is better.
intention: David wants to make a counterargument to his friend.
moral_action: David says he understands his friend's points and calmly expresses his thoughts about which team is better.
moral_consequence: David's friend understands, and they are able to have a civil conversation on the topic.
immoral_action: David yells at his friend and calls him a moron for thinking what he thinks.
immoral_consequence: David's friend gets upset and there is awkwardness in their group of friends for the rest of the day.

norm: It's good to take care of life's responsibilities.
situation: Anna, a lego collector, has been laid off from her job and is depending on her savings to pay her mortgage.
intention: Anna wants to add new limited edition lego set for her collection.
moral_action: Anna buys the set from a reseller at a mark up after she finds a new job and saves up for the set.
moral_consequence: Anna's finances remain in order thanks to her being responsible.
immoral_action: Anna uses some of her savings to buy the limited edition set when it comes out.
immoral_consequence: Anna doesn't have enough money to pay her mortgage and her credit score goes down.

norm: It's rude to not help your elders struggling with technology.
situation: Alana is at her grandparents home, and they keep asking her questions about emails they've been receiving in their spam folder.
intention: Alana wants to move to a different subject.
moral_action: Alana explains what the spam folder is and the dangers of scam emails before changing the subject.
moral_consequence: Alana's grandparents learn to avoid opening spam emails and avoid being defrauded.
immoral_action: Alana tells her grandparents not to worry about the emails and starts talking about something different.
immoral_consequence: Alana's grandparents get scammed because their curiosity draws them back to the emails.

norm: It's good to have a relationship with your parents.
situation: Ivan and Paula are proud of there son Ray being successful and wished they saw him more.
intention: Ray wants to go visit his parents more often.
moral_action: Ray takes a real vacation and immerses himself in his parents, Ivan and Paula, and making memories together.
moral_consequence: Ray and his parents become close knit and the family bonds becomes strong.
immoral_action: Ray schedules meetings and does business on his phone and laptop for most of his visit with his parents, Ivan and Paula.
immoral_consequence: Ray and his parents become distant and the family loses its support system.

norm: It's not okay to pity yourself to much.
situation: Ed experiences a setback in his life and is feeling very low about things.
intention: Ed wants to react emotionally to his situation.
moral_action: Ed decides stay positive and hopeful even in the face of the obstacles he's facing.
moral_consequence: Ed is able to work up the motivation to improve his situation and his life improves.
immoral_action: Ed lets himself fall into self-pity focusing on all the problems he is facing.
immoral_consequence: Ed loses his motivation to change his life and his mental condition becomes bleak.

norm: It's good to care about not disturbing others.
situation: Erin, who lives in an apartment with a roommate, is doing a late night gaming session and music helps her skills get into rhythm.
intention: Erin wants to do well in the game.
moral_action: Erin puts on headphones to listen to her music on and is able to play better.
moral_consequence: Erin's roommate is able to sleep soundly because the apartment is quiet.
immoral_action: Erin turns up some music through the speakers and her focus is improved.
immoral_consequence: Erin's roommate wakes up from the music playing and think's she is a bad roommate.

norm: It's wrong to cheat on people.
situation: Jack is married, but a girl he has always had a crush on want to come over to his place.
intention: Jack wants to invite the girl over.
moral_action: Jack invites the girl over to meet his wife and eat lunch together.
moral_consequence: Jack's wife doesn't have to worry about Jack cheating on her since Jack introduced the girl to her.
immoral_action: Jack invites the girl over when his wife isn't home, and they have sex.
immoral_consequence: Jack's wife could end up finding out and be completely heartbroken.

norm: You shouldn't hit your friend's pets.
situation: Billy is going on a business trip and asks Sam to watch his new dog, that has a tendency to jump on people.
intention: Sam wants the dog to stop jumping on him.
moral_action: "Sam trains the dog to stop jumping on people by saying ""No!"" loudly every time it jumps and giving it treats for listening."
moral_consequence: The dog stops jumping on people and Billy is grateful to Sam for training the dog.
immoral_action: Sam smacks the dog every time it tries to jump on him.
immoral_consequence: The dog becomes afraid of Sam and Billy stops asking Sam to watch the dog.

norm: It is wrong to be unfaithful
situation: Glenn is away from his wife on a business trip in another city, and he runs into his ex-girlfriend Cindy, who gives him her number.
intention: Glenn wants to decide what to do this evening.
moral_action: Glenn goes back to his hotel room and calls his wife to chat all evening.
moral_consequence: His wife enjoys talking with Glenn while he is away, and their marriage grows stronger.
immoral_action: Glenn calls Cindy up to meet for drinks, and he ends up spending the night with her.
immoral_consequence: His wife finds out about this later, and she files for divorce.

norm: It is rude to be nasty to elderly people.
situation: Doug's elderly mom needs help going to the doctor once a month.
intention: Doug wants to save his vacation time at work.
moral_action: Doug decides to hire a caretaker who can take his mom to her appointments and help with other things around the house.
moral_consequence: Doug's mom feels cared for and enjoys the companionship of the caretaker.
immoral_action: "Doug tells his mom he's tired of driving the ""old bat"" around and tells her to find someone else to take her."
immoral_consequence: Doug's mom is hurt and feels let down by her son.

norm: It's bad to make yourself feel sad.
situation: Chuck is bored and has time to watch a movie to relieve his boredom.
intention: Chuck wants to pick a movie and watch it.
moral_action: Chuck picks a happy movie with a happy ending and watches it.
moral_consequence: Chuck feels enthused and works harder the next day.
immoral_action: Chuck feels like watching a sad movie, picks one, and watches it.
immoral_consequence: Chuck feels depressed and can hardly get out of bed the next day.

norm: It's wrong judge someone based on a stereotype.
situation: Roger is a store manager, and a black person walks up to him holding a wallet he found on the floor.
intention: Roger wants to get the wallet to the rightful owner.
moral_action: Roger thanks the person for bringing the wallet and saves it for when the rightful owner returns.
moral_consequence: The rightful owner gets their wallet back and is grateful to Roger.
immoral_action: Roger accuses the black person of stealing the wallet and calls the police.
immoral_consequence: Roger's business suffers because he is assumed to be racist.

norm: You shouldn't do things that upset your neighbors.
situation: Corey has been working on his house and has a lot of heavy construction to get done.
intention: Corey wants to get his new driveway poured.
moral_action: Corey invites his friend to help him pour the driveway during a weekend afternoon so as not to disturb anyone's sleep.
moral_consequence: Corey's driveway looks great, and he gets plenty of compliments on it from his neighbors.
immoral_action: Corey has his friend help him pour the concrete for the driveway late at night, even though he knows his neighbors are early birds.
immoral_consequence: Corey's neighbors file a complaint with the HOA about his behavior and his noise problems.

norm: It's unacceptable to scream at children that you don't know.
situation: Wanda is at a grocery store when an unsupervised child rushes by her.
intention: Wanda wants the child to be with their parents.
moral_action: Wanda asks the child if they know where their parents are.
moral_consequence: Wanda is able to reunite the child with their parents.
immoral_action: Wanda yells at the child and tells them to go find their parents.
immoral_consequence: The child begins to cry because they don't know where their parents are.

norm: It's wrong to spit in another person's food.
situation: Robert is working in the drive thru of a fast food restaurant when a customer starts yelling at him through the window.
intention: Robert wants to teach the customer a lesson.
moral_action: Robert opens the window to tell the customer that they will not be served until they stop yelling.
moral_consequence: Robert gets an apology from the customer and then fixes the customer's issue.
immoral_action: Robert takes the sandwich into the back of the restaurant and spits into it.
immoral_consequence: Robert gets reprimanded by his manager when a coworker sees what he did.

norm: It's wrong to exclude family from weddings.
situation: Gary is having a wedding and is trying to decide who to invite when he realizes that the hall is too small for everyone.
intention: Gary wants to solve the invitation problem.
moral_action: Gary searches for a larger venue, finds one, and books it for his wedding, then invites everyone who is close.
moral_consequence: Gary's family all come to the wedding and have a great time, feeling included in Gary's life.
immoral_action: Gary invites his close friend and some family and doesn't invite some cousins, aunts, and uncles.
immoral_consequence: The uninvited family feel left out and shunned, eventually holding a grudge against Gary.

norm: It's good to care about the well-being of others.
situation: Mack works as a nurse for a nursing home and doesn't have anyone supervising him.
intention: Mack wants to get his day over with at the nursing home.
moral_action: Mack decides to watch over and take care of the elderly there until the end of his shift.
moral_consequence: Mack gets a congratulations from his higher-ups and feels accomplished.
immoral_action: Mack decides to ignore the customers and patients until the day is over.
immoral_consequence: Mack gets in trouble for gross negligence and apologizes.

norm: It's kind to help people who are having trouble.
situation: Troy is at home when he gets a call from his friend Andrew asking him to borrow some money short term.
intention: Troy wants to answer Andrew's request.
moral_action: Troy tells Andrew that he will take a quick trip to the bank right now and Andrew can come over in the meantime to grab it.
moral_consequence: Andrew is delighted that his friend is bailing him out and completely relieved that his stress is temporarily gone.
immoral_action: Troy tells Andrew that he can't spare any right now and Andrew should go to a pay day lender.
immoral_consequence: Andrew is sad that his friend can't help him and continues to be stressed out about money.

norm: You shouldn't give kids horrible ideas.
situation: Josh is watching the neighbor's kids for the day while they're out of town.
intention: Josh wants to entertain the kids.
moral_action: Josh shows the kids the joys of creative story writing.
moral_consequence: The kids both grow up to be well-paid short story writers.
immoral_action: Josh takes the kids and shows them how burning stuff can be fun!
immoral_consequence: The kids burn their house down a few days later.

norm: You shouldn't hide things from your coworkers.
situation: Maria is the only person at her office that has a stapler and many of her coworkers borrow the stapler.
intention: Maria wants to have easy access to her stapler.
moral_action: Maria puts a sign next to her stapler on her desk asking her coworkers to please not take her stapler.
moral_consequence: Maria enjoys having her coworkers come to her desk and chat while they use her stapler.
immoral_action: Maria hides her stapler in her drawer so that nobody else can use the stapler.
immoral_consequence: Maria feels like a bad person when her coworkers are looking for the stapler.

norm: It's dishonest to cheat on a test
situation: Scott has his final test in a week and feels he might flunk it.
intention: Scott wants to make his parents proud.
moral_action: Scott asks a friend to help him study for the test, he studies day and night for a week.
moral_consequence: Scott aces the test and is prouder than he's ever been.
immoral_action: Scott writes helpful notes on a tiny piece of paper that he hides in his sock and checks during the test.
immoral_consequence: Scott aces the test but feels like a fraud.

norm: It's wrong to peep into someone's window.
situation: Gordy was doing gardening outside of Jan's window when he notices her changing her clothing inside.
intention: Gordy wants to finish gardening.
moral_action: Gordy moves to another area of the property to avoid looking at Jan.
moral_consequence: At the end of the day, Jan pays Gordy for the work that he has done.
immoral_action: Gordy looks into the window and watches Jan take off her clothes as he trims the leaves.
immoral_consequence: Jan fires Gordy from his job when she sees what he is doing.

norm: You shouldn't leave work without your bosses' permission.
situation: Cage is at work when he gets an emergency call from his son, asking him to come home.
intention: Cage wants to go home.
moral_action: Cage quickly tells his boss that he has a home emergency and must leave.
moral_consequence: Cage's boss lets him go home without problems.
immoral_action: Cage leaves his desk, gets into his car, and goes home.
immoral_consequence: Cage's boss looks for him, can't find him, and thinks that he's abandoned his work.

norm: It is bad to be egotistical and narcissistic
situation: Ryan just hit the game winning shot for his basketball team, so he's now being interviewed.
intention: Ryan has to respond to the interviewer.
moral_action: Ryan says that he wouldn't be where he is without his teammates.
moral_consequence: Ryan's teammates feel appreciative of him and feel more motivated to win games.
immoral_action: Ryan credits himself for winning the game and doesn't mention his teammates.
immoral_consequence: Ryan's teammates feel that he is a jerk and want to pass the ball to him less.

norm: One should always report those that abuse power.
situation: Jim's boss threatens to fire workers who unionize.
intention: Jim doesn't want to lose his job.
moral_action: Jim unionizes with his coworkers and reports his boss.
moral_consequence: Jim's coworkers feel more secure with their jobs.
immoral_action: Jim doesn't unionize with his coworkers.
immoral_consequence: Many of Jim's coworkers lose their jobs.

norm: It's wrong to make fun of your partner.
situation: Kelly and Stan have been dating for a while, and are on a double date with friends.
intention: Kelly wants to make a joke.
moral_action: Kelly makes a self-deprecating joke and makes Steve the hero of her story.
moral_consequence: Steve defends Kelly, and the two become closer as a couple.
immoral_action: Kelly makes fun of Steve's appearance and mocks his accent.
immoral_consequence: Steve feels hurt, and decides he no longer wants to date Kelly.

norm: It's good to honor your commitments.
situation: John promised Jessie that he would take her to the bookstore after work.
intention: John wants to relax after work.
moral_action: John asks Jessie if he can take a quick nap before heading out to the bookstore.
moral_consequence: Jessie doesn't mind waiting while John naps and makes a list of books that she wants to pick out at the store.
immoral_action: John avoids seeing Jessie and heads straight to bed, afraid to have to let her down.
immoral_consequence: Jessie is sad and trusts John's word a lot less, feeling like he is unreliable.

norm: You should not let others put you down.
situation: Dave is in the library with his math tutor Jeremy, who just told Dave that he might as well quit trying to improve.
intention: Dave wants to stop studying for the day.
moral_action: Dave tells Jeremy that he isn't being supportive, nor is he filling his role as a helpful tutor, and says he will be finding a new tutor to learn from.
moral_consequence: Dave is able to find a tutor who is patient and supportive, while Jeremy loses a client because of his bad attitude.
immoral_action: Dave says that Jeremy is probably right and packs his things to go home, feeling terrible about himself.
immoral_consequence: Dave loses ambition to continue learning and begins to suffer a lot academically.

norm: It is dishonest to keep extra change.
situation: Will receives an extra twenty dollars from the cashier while buying something.
intention: Will wants money to buy a meal at a restaurant.
moral_action: Will gives the money back and borrows money from a friend to go eat.
moral_consequence: The cashier's drawer is balanced at the end of the day.
immoral_action: Will keeps the twenty dollars and goes to the restaurant.
immoral_consequence: The cashier is twenty dollars short that evening and has to pay it from his own wages.

norm: It's wrong to discriminate against fat people.
situation: Harry has to hire a new employee for his business, and he has been interviewing candidates all day.
intention: Harry wants to make a hiring decision.
moral_action: Harry hires the candidate with the best qualifications for the job and the most experience.
moral_consequence: The new employee works out well for Harry's business, so he knows he made the right decision.
immoral_action: Harry makes his decision without considering any candidates that are overweight, because he thinks they won't work as hard.
immoral_consequence: Harry does not end up hiring the best person for the job.

norm: It's good to buy people new clothes.
situation: Leanne is planning what she needs to buy for her daughter, Lacy, to go back to school in the fall.
intention: Leanne needs to buy Lacy clothes.
moral_action: Leanne goes to a department store and buys Lacy new clothes in the newest styles.
moral_consequence: Lacy goes to school in her new clothes and gets compliments from some of the other girls.
immoral_action: Leanne goes to a rummage sale and buys some very old clothes for Lacy.
immoral_consequence: Lacy goes to school in her clothes from the rummage sale and gets made fun of by the other children.

norm: It is good to stick up for people.
situation: Leslie hears a group of her friends making fun of a childhood friend that she doesn't talk to anymore, but still cares for.
intention: Leslie has to decide whether to join the conversation and what she wants to say.
moral_action: Leslie speaks up and tells the group that she has known the person they're talking about for a long time, and she feels offended by their conversation.
moral_consequence: Leslie feels good about how she reacted to the group and several members of her group apologize to her, and tell her they didn't mean to be hurtful.
immoral_action: Leslie doesn't want to sacrifice her place in the social order of her friends, so she ignores the conversation she hears.
immoral_consequence: Leslie feels guilty about not saying something to the group about making fun of her friend.

norm: You should be more grateful for your parents.
situation: Donna's parents are making her do online school because of the pandemic.
intention: Donna wants to see her friends in person more often.
moral_action: Donna decides to be thankful that her parents care about her and after explaining her feelings, they allow her to visit a friend while wearing a mask.
moral_consequence: Donna maintains a good relationship with her mom and dad while still staying safe.
immoral_action: Donna disparages her parents to her friends when she sneaks out to hang out with them.
immoral_consequence: Her parents find out and force her to stay in her room since they have lost trust in her.

norm: It's wrong to drug people.
situation: Will met a girl he likes at a bar, and he wants to take her home with him.
intention: Will wants to have sex with the girl.
moral_action: Will has a conversation with the girl and asks her to come to his place.
moral_consequence: The girl is more willing to go with him and have sex.
immoral_action: Will puts something in the girl's drink that slows down her thinking.
immoral_consequence: The girl finds out that Will drugged her and thinks about getting legal action.

norm: You should always greet people.
situation: Sarah is in an office building waiting for a job interview and Amanda enters the room.
intention: Sarah wants to finish waiting and get to the interview quickly.
moral_action: Sarah greets Amanda and wishes her good luck on her interview.
moral_consequence: Amanda replies thank you, but also that she's the interviewer, not a candidate.
immoral_action: Sarah ignores Amanda as she enters the room and says nothing.
immoral_consequence: Sarah is called into the interview 10 minutes later and Amanda is the person interviewing her.

norm: You shouldn't take advantage of someone's generosity.
situation: Ricky and Mark are about to order dinner at a restaurant, and Ricky offers to pay for the food.
intention: Ricky wants to eat food.
moral_action: Ricky thanks Mark, and offers to pay for drinks and deserts.
moral_consequence: Mark's friendship with Ricky deepens.
immoral_action: Ricky orders over half of the items on the menu.
immoral_consequence: Mark's account goes under, and he's forced to pay overdraft fees.

norm: It's good to surprise people for their birthdays
situation: Bill is going to the birthday party of his friend, Jack, but he is too busy recently to shop for birthday gift.
intention: Bill wants to celebrate Jack's birthday.
moral_action: Bill asks his mother to make him a dog-like  costume, and he wears it to Jack's birthday.
moral_consequence: Jack is impressed by Bill's costume and thanks Bill for his good idea.
immoral_action: Bill spends 15 minutes shopping and buys a regular T-shirt for Jack as a birthday gift.
immoral_consequence: Jack feels disappointed and does not react to the T-shirt  much.

norm: It's wrong to freeload off people.
situation: Tim moved back in with his parents after graduating from college and getting a job at Walmart.
intention: Tim wants to spend his money.
moral_action: Tim pays his parents rent and contributes to the grocery and utility bills.
moral_consequence: Tim's parents feel Tim is being very responsible, so they buy him a car to help him commute to work.
immoral_action: Tim spends all his money on going to bars with his friends whenever he's not working.
immoral_consequence: Tim's parents don't think Tim is trying to improve his life, so they kick him out of the house.

norm: It is rude to talk back to a parent.
situation: Billy is at home where his dad is admonishing him for not mowing the lawn like he was supposed to.
intention: Billy wants to express displeasure to his father.
moral_action: Billy walks outside to mow the lawn but gives his father the silent treatment the rest of the day.
moral_consequence: Billy's dad is understanding of why Billy is upset, so he allows him to brood and is also happy to see that Billy did his chores.
immoral_action: "Billy tells his father to ""shove it"" and to mow the lawn himself if he thinks it's so importanat."
immoral_consequence: Billy's father is shocked that his son is so rude and hurt that his son won't listen to him.

norm: It's disloyal to leave a job shortly after beginning it.
situation: John has just begun working at a coffee shop when an impressed customer, right in front of Carlos the owner, offers John a higher paying job at his sandwich shop.
intention: John wants to respond to the customer.
moral_action: John declines the customer's offer stating that he just began at this job, and he's not disloyal.
moral_consequence: Carlos is happy to see John be a stand up person and is happy his choice to hire him has been validated in a way.
immoral_action: John tells the customer that of course he will accept the job as it's higher paying.
immoral_consequence: Carlos is angry that the training he just gave John is wasted and that he has to look for another employee.

norm: It's bad to not invite close friends to important events.
situation: Sue is getting married and is sending out wedding invitations, keeping in mind that her two best friends Betty and Jane aren't getting along.
intention: Sue doesn't want to upset her friends and wants to have a great wedding without any drama.
moral_action: Sue doesn't take sides and invites both friends to the wedding.
moral_consequence: Betty is happy to go the wedding and feels close with Sue.
immoral_action: Sue is closer friends with Jane, so she doesn't invite her friend Betty to the wedding.
immoral_consequence: Betty is very offended by Sue's decision and her feelings are hurt.

norm: It's wrong to take something that belongs to someone else.
situation: Stacey always brings lunch to work, but today she forgot her lunch.
intention: Stacey wants to wants to get something to eat.
moral_action: Stacey decides to go to the cafeteria to see if she can get something for lunch.
moral_consequence: Stacey enjoys her lunch and thinks that she will eat in the cafeteria more often.
immoral_action: Stacey looks in the fridge in the break room and takes a coworker's sandwich to eat.
immoral_consequence: Another coworker sees Stacey take the sandwich and tells her she shouldn't take someone else's lunch.

norm: You should have important conversations in person.
situation: James is in a relationship that has been strenuous for a long time and his heart begins to waiver.
intention: James wants to break up with his partner.
moral_action: James sits down and has a heart to heart with his partner, explaining his feelings and desire to leave.
moral_consequence: The sincere conversation helps James' partner to move on more easily.
immoral_action: James breaks up with his partner while they are talking using text messages.
immoral_consequence: James' partner thinks that the relationship meant nothing since he broke up with her over text.

norm: It's rude to disturb others by yelling.
situation: Candy was studying with her friend in the library after school.
intention: Candy wants to discuss a topic with her friend.
moral_action: Candy works quietly with her friend asking questions and working on their assignment.
moral_consequence: The librarian offers to stay open an extra half hour because Candy and her friend were so well behaved.
immoral_action: Candy calls out to her friend across the library to understand the material.
immoral_consequence: The librarian gets annoyed and asks if Candy and her friend can leave.

norm: It's good to offer things to your friends.
situation: Ben invites Carol over to his house for dinner one night.
intention: Ben wants to eat.
moral_action: Ben puts his and Carol's plates on the table, so they can eat.
moral_consequence: Ben and Carol had a nice and peaceful dinner together.
immoral_action: Ben eats his dinner without offering anything for Carol to eat.
immoral_consequence: Carol leaves and doesn't go back to Ben's house for dinner again.

norm: It's bad to be too loud around other people.
situation: Keith and Chris are in the library working on a problem set, near the librarian and other students.
intention: Keith wants to check his answers with Chris.
moral_action: Keith motions to Chris to show him his answer each time they finish a problem.
moral_consequence: The librarian finishes putting away the stack of books that were returned the previous day.
immoral_action: Keith asks Chris at normal volume what answer he got each time they finish a problem.
immoral_consequence: The librarian eventually asks Keith to leave the library because he's disturbing other people.

norm: Is wrong to judge somebody's lifestyle
situation: Paul is at the mall when he's approached by an LGBTQ group led by Tony who asks him if he's pro LGBTQ.
intention: Paul wants to tell Tony that he is not pro LGBTQ.
moral_action: Paul tells Tony that he isn't because it's not an issue of concern to him one way or the other.
moral_consequence: Tony tells Paul that he understands and that he's happy at least he's not against LGBTQ either.
immoral_action: Paul tells Tony that he is not because God will smite those who commit buggery, and they're sinners.
immoral_consequence: Tony is angry that Paul is calling him a sinner and walks away from Paul.

norm: You shouldn't be ashamed of your physical disabilities.
situation: Lara, who is very physically attractive, was born with a problem in her legs that leaves her with a severe limp, which she doesn't like people to see.
intention: Lara wants to participate in a speed dating event at a local nightclub.
moral_action: Lara has fun at the dating event and finds herself walking from table to table without even thinking about it, and she meets a lot of interested, prospective dates.
moral_consequence: Lara feels proud that she didn't let her leg get in the way of taking part in a fun, exciting event.
immoral_action: Lara is very popular with prospective dates, but she is ashamed of her limp and avoids walking in front of them, so she doesn't get to meet as many people.
immoral_consequence: Lara is disappointed in herself that she was too ashamed to walk in front of the others at the event.

norm: It's wrong to shoplift.
situation: Bobby is at the mall when he sees a shirt he thinks he'd look good in.
intention: Bobby wants to take the shirt he saw back home with him.
moral_action: Bobby pays for the shirt with his credit card and takes it home in a bag.
moral_consequence: Bobby enjoys wearing the shirt and thinks it suits him well.
immoral_action: Bobby stuffs the shirt down his pants and walks out of the store casually and goes home.
immoral_consequence: Bobby is caught on camera taking the shirt and later gets in trouble for it.

norm: You shouldn't be friends with someone who gets you arrested.
situation: Jake's friend stole money from a store and blamed Jake for it to avoid prison time.
intention: Jake wants to decide whether to forgive his friend or not.
moral_action: Jake told his friend that his behavior was unacceptable and cut all ties with him.
moral_consequence: Jake's friend felt extremely guilty for his actions and decided to take responsibility for his actions from then on.
immoral_action: Jake told his friend it's understandable to frame others for your crime and ended up forgiving him after he got out of prison.
immoral_consequence: Jake's friend committed another crime and framed someone else, getting them in trouble.

norm: It's good that a person takes their academics seriously.
situation: Sam is being lectured by his mom about his bad grades when she asks him what he's going to do about it.
intention: Sam wants to propose a way to get better grades.
moral_action: Sam tells his mom he'll start studying and doing his homework on a regular basis.
moral_consequence: Sam's mom is proud that Sam is choosing to try harder to get over an obstacle.
immoral_action: Sam tells his mom that he'll either sleep with the teachers or pay them but it'll be fine either way.
immoral_consequence: Sam's mom is appalled that Sam thinks he can bribe or use his body for sex to get his way and is concerned about him.

norm: It's wrong to wish that your loved ones were dead.
situation: Katie feels very angry after an argument with her sister.
intention: Katie wants to vent her anger somehow.
moral_action: Katie goes for a run to work off some of her anger.
moral_consequence: Katie feels better after exercising and patches things up with her sister.
immoral_action: Katie tells her sister that she wishes she was dead.
immoral_consequence: Katie experiences incredible guilt when her sister dies in a car crash that evening.

norm: You shouldn't become addicted to alcohol.
situation: Bob is a frequent drinker who enjoy trying new beers and wines.
intention: Bob wants to drink to relax.
moral_action: Bob never drinks more than three drinks in a day and three and tries to not drink a few times a week.
moral_consequence: Bob becomes a beer and wine afficianado and enjoys qulaity over quantity.
immoral_action: Bob drinks more and more as time progresses until he get to over 30 drinks a day.
immoral_consequence: Bob is anxious and shaky every morning and the drinking is now to avoid withdrawal rather that feel pleasure.

norm: Don't be bossy with your SO.
situation: Rob and Tia are walking through the food court in a mall.
intention: Rob wants to get a pretzel.
moral_action: Rob asks Tia if she would like to get a pretzel with him.
moral_consequence: Tia agrees and even buys Rob an extra large pretzel.
immoral_action: Rob grabs Tia by the arm and drags her to the pretzel counter.
immoral_consequence: Tia pulls away from Rob and goes to another part of the food court on her own.

norm: You should not be possessive of a partner.
situation: Dan is in the living room when his wife Kelly comes in to tell him she'll be going out to the mall with her friend Diane.
intention: Dan wants to react to Kelly's statement.
moral_action: Dan tells Kelly to have fun and to drive safely and to text him if anything comes up.
moral_consequence: Kelly feels loved by her husband and is appreciative that he's offering to be by his phone if she needs anything.
immoral_action: Dan tells Kelly that he's allowing her to go on the condition that she comes back within an hour and spends no money.
immoral_consequence: Kelly feels imprisoned by her husband and secretly resents him and how much he tries to tell her what to do.

norm: It's good to ensure kids are getting proper nutrition.
situation: Michael is in the kitchen when his son, Scott, tells him that he is hungry.
intention: Michael wants to prepare a meal for Scott.
moral_action: Michael prepares a plate of fruit, vegetables, and a chicken breast sandwich on whole wheat bread for Scott.
moral_consequence: Scott feels energetic and alert throughout the rest of the day.
immoral_action: Michael takes a package of Lunchables out of the refrigerator and makes it for Scott.
immoral_consequence: Scott feels lethargic throughout the rest of the day.

norm: You should approach sensitive topics gently.
situation: Jeffrey meets up with a group of friends, including Kevin, to let them know he's transitioning into a woman.
intention: Kevin wants to learn more about Jeffrey's motivation.
moral_action: Kevin thanks Jeffrey for telling him, and asks if he's comfortable being asked some questions about it.
moral_consequence: Jeffrey feels heard and respected, and opens up with more information, and grows closer with Kevin.
immoral_action: Kevin curls his lip and asks if this means he's turning into some kind of faggot.
immoral_consequence: Jeffrey is hurt, and feels Kevin can not longer be trusted, and pulls away from him as a friend.

norm: It is romantic to give a love interest flowers.
situation: Jimmy and Sam have been in the same class all year and Jimmy has developed a crush on her.
intention: Jimmy wants to show Sam how he feels.
moral_action: Jimmy brings Sam a bouquet of hand picked sunflowers from outside his dorm.
moral_consequence: Sam is charmed by Jimmy's gesture and asks him on a date.
immoral_action: Jimmy brings Sam a new copy of the class textbook and draws a heart on the inside cover.
immoral_consequence: Sam is confused by Jimmy's gift, thanks him, and never bothers opening it.

norm: You shouldn't make jokes about Jews.
situation: Kevin goes to a bar mitzvah for his friend Daniel and is nervous about meeting Daniel's parents.
intention: Kevin wants to say something funny to break the ice.
moral_action: Kevin tell a funny story about birds.
moral_consequence: Kevin makes everyone laugh with his story.
immoral_action: Kevin makes a funny remark to Daniel's parents about their customs.
immoral_consequence: Kevin is thrown out of the bar mitzvah.

norm: It's good to share your wealth with your child.
situation: Roger has won the lottery, and his son is about to have an expensive leg surgery.
intention: Roger wants to spend his money.
moral_action: Roger saves some from himself, and he pays for his son's surgery along with giving some money to help him during his recovery period.
moral_consequence: Roger and his son become closer.
immoral_action: Roger spends all of his money on different cars.
immoral_consequence: Roger can not afford the car insurance and taxes on the cars.

norm: It is overwhelming to be a teen parent.
situation: June and her friends are high school students who greatly admire a character on a TV show they like.
intention: June wants to emulate her favorite character.
moral_action: June imitates the TV characters sense of style and fashion.
moral_consequence: June gains admiration from her peers.
immoral_action: When the TV character she admires gets pregnant June decides she wants a baby too.
immoral_consequence: June soon discovers the burden an unwed teenage mother carries.

norm: It's bad to stalk someone on their break.
situation: Jon knows that his female coworker with big breasts is on her lunch break right now.
intention: Jon has to decide whether to creep on his coworker.
moral_action: Jon doesn't want to creep out his coworker, so he decides to let her be.
moral_consequence: Jon's coworker is able to enjoy her lunch break without anyone bothering her.
immoral_action: Jon goes into the break room and gets to a spot where he has a good view of her breasts.
immoral_consequence: The coworker knows that Jon is staring at her and is thinking about reporting him.

norm: It is rude to end a serious relationship over text
situation: Robert and his girlfriend Sally are experiencing a lot of conflicts in their relationship lately.
intention: Robert wants to end the relationship with Sally.
moral_action: Robert breaks up with Sally face to face the next time they see each other.
moral_consequence: Sally is initially sad but appreciates Robert's honesty and moves on.
immoral_action: Robert breaks up with Sally by sending her a text saying the relationship is over.
immoral_consequence: Sally is sad and also very angry at Robert for not telling her in person.

norm: It is important to respect diversity.
situation: Nick works in HR for a software company and has qualified job candidates from many different ethnicities who want work.
intention: Nick wants to select someone to hire.
moral_action: Nick chooses someone from a minority background to hire.
moral_consequence: The new hire has a different perspective, allowing the company to better align their products for different ethnicities.
immoral_action: Nick prioritizes white people and picks a white person to hire.
immoral_consequence: The all-white staff can't understand the struggles of minority groups and become bigoted.

norm: It is rude to not tip for good service.
situation: Matt is out at a restaurant that appears to be slightly out of his budget as he looks through the menu.
intention: Matt wants to save money on his dinner.
moral_action: Matt orders an inexpensive item off the menu and leaves a modest tip.
moral_consequence: The server is satisfied to get a tip for serving the table.
immoral_action: Matt enjoys his food, and he does not leave a tip in order to spend less money.
immoral_consequence: The server is discouraged as he is dependent on tips to make a living wage.

norm: You shouldn't have sex with someone you barely know.
situation: Dirk goes on vacation to a tropical island, attends a party, and meets up with a beautiful foreign girl who wants to go home with him.
intention: Dirk wants to have a good time.
moral_action: Dirk refuses but continues to dance and party with the girl at the event.
moral_consequence: Dirk goes home, gets some good sleep, and leaves the tropical island without regrets.
immoral_action: Dirk brings the girl back to his hotel room and spends the night with her, then parts ways with her.
immoral_consequence: The girl gives Dirk an STD, cursing him for life, and the one-night stand was unsatisfying in the end.

norm: It's good to be up front and honest with others.
situation: Tom's mother notices he seems to be falling behind in his school work and asks if everything is okay.
intention: Tom wants to respond to his mother's question.
moral_action: Tom tells his mother he is struggling in class and needs help.
moral_consequence: Tom's mother hires a tutor for him, and he graduates with a high GPA.
immoral_action: Tom tells his mother that everything is going extremely well at school.
immoral_consequence: Tom does not get the help he needs and fails out of school.

norm: It's good to play sports with your siblings.
situation: Icarus just finished his homework, and his little brother stands in the hall holding a basketball.
intention: Icarus wants to get out of the house.
moral_action: Icarus plays basketball with his younger brother in the outdoor basketball court in his neighborhood.
moral_consequence: Icarus and his brother make new friends when others ask to join their game.
immoral_action: Icarus goes for a walk around the park.
immoral_consequence: Icarus is lonely when he observes the people around him clustered in small groups.

norm: It is wrong to get rid of a pet.
situation: Chris had a new pet puppy, but his mother said that he couldn't keep it in the house.
intention: Chris wants the puppy to stay outside of the house.
moral_action: Chris builds a fence and doghouse in the backyard for the puppy.
moral_consequence: Chris takes care of the puppy and gets to see it everyday.
immoral_action: Chris drives to the edge of town and throws the puppy out of the car.
immoral_consequence: Chris gets fined and ticketed for endangerment of an animal.

norm: It's wrong to judge others solely based on their appearance.
situation: John goes to school with a fat kid named Jim who he shares gym class with, and they are forming dodgeball teams.
intention: John wants to pick his team members.
moral_action: John decides to take a risk and pick Jim before anyone else.
moral_consequence: Jim ends up winning the game for John's team, as he can throw the ball really fast.
immoral_action: John leaves Jim to be picked last, grabbing everyone in better shape first.
immoral_consequence: Jim ends up on the other team, which proceeds to win because Jim can throw the ball really fast.

norm: You shouldn't spray paint your name on public property.
situation: A corporation declared bankruptcy firing the majority of its' employees but the CEO got a multi-million dollar bonus.
intention: Mike wants to express his disgust at the situation as a former employee.
moral_action: Mike hands out fliers on the sidewalk in front of the office building decrying what the CEO did.
moral_consequence: Mike raises awareness and a campaign against these corporate practices is begun.
immoral_action: "Mike spray paints ""Mike worked here and is broke now but the CEO isn't"" all over the sidewalk in front of the office building."
immoral_consequence: Mike is arrested for vandalism and is fined.

norm: You shouldn't do anything that will get you in jail.
situation: Larry has had too much to drink at the bar, and now it's time to go home.
intention: Larry wants to leave for home.
moral_action: Larry calls a cab to pick him up at the bar and drive him home.
moral_consequence: Larry gets home safely and retrieves his car the next day.
immoral_action: Larry gets in his car and starts heading for home.
immoral_consequence: Larry gets busted for DUI, has to spend the night in jail, and is late for work the next day.

norm: It's impolite not to open the door for someone.
situation: Barry was walking into the hotel and Sally was walking in after him.
intention: Barry wants to open the door.
moral_action: Barry opens the door for himself and holds it open for Sally to go through.
moral_consequence: Sally is grateful that she doesn't have to open the door herself.
immoral_action: Barry opens the door for himself and lets it close behind him.
immoral_consequence: The door swings shut and hits Sally in the face and breaks her nose.

norm: It is good to recognize the sacrifices Soldiers made
situation: Adam is the leader of a country that recently exited a long bloody war and has to make a speech about it.
intention: Adam wants to make a speech about the long and bloody war.
moral_action: Adam talks about all the sacrifices soldiers have made for the country and honors them with a monument.
moral_consequence: Adam maintains some popular support and gets new recruits for the country's military.
immoral_action: Adam never mentions the sacrifices made by his soldiers and simply focuses on his own agendas.
immoral_consequence: Adam's soldiers becomes demotivated and Adam loses popular support in his country.

norm: You don't have to react emotionally to everything.
situation: Matt Goes to school with Robin who is intellectually disabled and in the special ed class.
intention: Matt wants to impress other people and be popular.
moral_action: Matt sticks up for Robin when others make fun of her and treats her respectfully.
moral_consequence: Robin is a sister to one of the popular kids who gain respect for Matt and befriend him.
immoral_action: Matt mocks Robin and plays mean pranks on her in order to make others laugh.
immoral_consequence: Robin is the sister of a popular girl who had a crush on him but now dislikes him and tells her friends what Matt has done to Robin.

norm: You should be supportive when your child is depressed.
situation: Rick has a teenage son named Roger who's been struggling with depression lately.
intention: Rick wants to give Roger advice on handling depression.
moral_action: Rick tells Roger he's here for him if he wants to talk his issues out, or will help him find someone to talk to, if he prefers.
moral_consequence: Roger appreciates his father being there for him, and ends up speaking to a psychologist Rick pays for that helps him work out his problems.
immoral_action: Rick tells Roger it's all in his head and tells him to shake his depression off.
immoral_consequence: Roger feels even worse when he realizes he's unable to follow his father's advice.

norm: It is good to have a list to organize yourself.
situation: Susan is preparing for a big presentation at work.
intention: Susan wants to give a good presentation.
moral_action: Susan jots down everything she needs to do for the presentation and keeps checking back on her notes as she spends the evening preparing.
moral_consequence: Thanks to practice and being organized, Susan's presentation goes off without a hitch and is well received.
immoral_action: Susan doesn't want to overthink the presentation, so she decides to relax and watch television before going to bed.
immoral_consequence: Susan forgets a few key points during her presentation and it doesn't go well.

norm: It's rude not to help with housework
situation: John and his wife are spending the weekend at home, which needs some tidying both inside and outdoors.
intention: John wants to get some exercise.
moral_action: John gets out the manual lawnmower and mows the entire yard, getting some exercise in the process.
moral_consequence: John's wife thanks him for helping out, and they have a nice picnic outside on the freshly mowed lawn.
immoral_action: John goes to the gym to work out, leaving his wife to finish the chores.
immoral_consequence: John's wife gets very upset at him and this causes a big argument when he gets home.

norm: It's nice to tell your kids bedtime stories.
situation: It was almost bedtime and Vicki's children were still playing with their toys.
intention: Vicki wants her kids to go to sleep.
moral_action: Vicki gets a book and reads a bedtime story to the children.
moral_consequence: The children fall asleep quickly after Vicki starts to read.
immoral_action: Vicki takes the toys away from the children and throws them in the trash.
immoral_consequence: The children whine and cry all night themselves to sleep.

norm: it's rude to spend someone else's money without their consent
situation: Josephine is on a school field trip to NYC, and her mother gave her a credit card to use for emergencies only.
intention: Josephine wants to purchase souvenirs with her mother's credit card.
moral_action: Josephine calls her mom to ask if it is okay that she buys some souvenirs.
moral_consequence: Josephine's mom sets a strict budget, but allows her to use the card for souvenirs.
immoral_action: Josephine goes on a shopping spree with her mom's card.
immoral_consequence: Josephine's mom goes to use the card back home, and it is declined.

norm: You shouldn't ejaculate on someone's things.
situation: Pete is obsessed with his ex Brittany and is having a hard time letting her go.
intention: Pete wants Brittany to not forget about him.
moral_action: Pete sends Brittany flowers on the important anniversary's from their relationship.
moral_consequence: Pete is able to keep in limited contact with Brittany.
immoral_action: Pete breaks into Brittany's home and masturbates over her underwear.
immoral_consequence: Pete winds up in jail when the DNA he left behind identifies him as the intruder at Brittany's house.

norm: It's hurtful to not invite someone to dinner.
situation: Ryan has been planning to have dinner with friends at a fancy restaurant.
intention: Ryan wants to decide on who to invite.
moral_action: Ryan makes sure he invited every single one of his friends.
moral_consequence: Ryan's friends all appreciate Ryan more, and they enjoy a wonderful dinner together.
immoral_action: Ryan invites all his friends to the dinner except for one.
immoral_consequence: The one friend that did not get an invite feels left out and starts to like Ryan less.

norm: You can't expect everyone to attend your party.
situation: Randy is apologizing to David for not being able to attend his party last week because his daughter was ill.
intention: David wants to react to Randy's apology.
moral_action: David tells Randy that there's no need to apologize that family comes first, always.
moral_consequence: Randy is relieved that David isn't upset about his absence and happy that David is understanding.
immoral_action: David tells Randy that it's unacceptable, and he cannot forgive him for not attending the party.
immoral_consequence: Randy is stressed out that his relationship with David is falling apart for something so stupid.

norm: It's irresponsible to not shower.
situation: It had been well over a week since the last time the Chance had taken a shower.
intention: Chance wanted to talk to his boss.
moral_action: Chance went home and took a shower and changed his clothes before talking to his boss.
moral_consequence: Chance's boss was attentive to him and impressed with the way he looked.
immoral_action: Chance talked to his boss in his dirty clothes without even putting on deodorant.
immoral_consequence: Chances boss sent him to human resources who told him he was offensive to other workers.

norm: You shouldn't judge others by their amount of sexual experience.
situation: Maddie just started a relationship with a guy she's been dating.
intention: Maddie wants to know what her boyfriend's sexual history is.
moral_action: Maddie and her boyfriend have an open dialog about past relationships.
moral_consequence: Maddie and her boyfriend are open about their sexual history and make peace with the past.
immoral_action: Maddie asks her boyfriend how many people he's slept with in an accusatory manner.
immoral_consequence: Maddie's boyfriend realizes she doesn't trust him and breaks up with her.

norm: It is good to maintain positive relationships with others
situation: Joan realizes she hasn't talked to her best friend from high school since starting college.
intention: Joan wants to reach out to her best friend.
moral_action: Joan calls her best friend to catch up on the weekend.
moral_consequence: Joan's best friend is happy to hear from her and chats about what's been going on.
immoral_action: Joan texts her best friend, accusing her of forgetting about Joan.
immoral_consequence: Joan's best friend is angry that Joan hasn't talked to her, either.

norm: You shouldn't expect people to pay for your purchases.
situation: Jane is out having drinks with friends after work.
intention: Jane wants to enjoy the night.
moral_action: Jane follows her friends up to the bar as they order their drinks in turn and pay for them individually.
moral_consequence: The friends enjoy their drinks, the atmosphere and the evening together.
immoral_action: Jane tells a friend what she wants to drink when the friend goes up to order a drink for themself.
immoral_consequence: Jane's friend complains that Jane never pays for her own drinks and the mood is ruined for the evening.

norm: You shouldn't out your friends after their death.
situation: Luke's friend Han dies and everyone they know goes to his funeral.
intention: Luke wants to talk about Han at the funeral.
moral_action: Luke talks about all the good times he had with his friend Han and all the ties Han helped him.
moral_consequence: Han's family is pleased to hear all these wonderful stories from Luke.
immoral_action: Luke tells Han's family all about Han smuggling drugs and weapons and such in his life.
immoral_consequence: Han's family doesn't believe Luke's stories and calls him a liar.

norm: It's rude to act out when eating out with friends.
situation: Lucy is having dinner with her friends has has found a hair in her food.
intention: Lucy wants compensated for her meal.
moral_action: Lucy points out the hair in her food and asks for another one.
moral_consequence: The server replaces Lucy's meal and gives her her drink for free.
immoral_action: Lucy goes on and on about the hair in her food to the server and becomes very animated.
immoral_consequence: Lucy's friends are embarrassed, and they never go with Lucy to dinner again.

norm: You should be supportive of your partner and their choices.
situation: Tom notices his wife Sue recently got a tattoo, when he had previously told her not to get one.
intention: Tom wants to talk to Sue about her new tattoo.
moral_action: Tom compliments Sue on her tattoo and is respectful of her choice.
moral_consequence: Tom and Sue laugh together about previous disagreement and Sue thanks Tom.
immoral_action: Tom immediately tells Sue she must remove her tattoo and that he hates it.
immoral_consequence: Sue feels overwhelmed and lets Tom know that he is out of line.

norm: You should not mislead others about who you really are.
situation: George who is unemployed meets Elaine for the first time and Elaine asks George what he does for a living.
intention: George wants to respond to Elaine's question.
moral_action: George tells Elaine that he is currently between jobs and living at home with his parents Estelle and Frank.
moral_consequence: Elaine is impressed that George has the moral fortitude required to admit a hard thing like that and gains respect for him.
immoral_action: George tells Elaine that he is an Architect at the firm Vandelay industries who mostly deal with importing latex.
immoral_consequence: Elaine later finds out that George was lying and feels violated and questions whether George might have been taking advantage of her.

norm: You shouldn't let your child's animal suffer.
situation: Mary's daughter's cat is getting older and often suffers from untreated arthritis pain.
intention: Mary wants to care for her daughter's pet.
moral_action: Mary brings her daughter's cat into see a vet and learns how to care for the animal's arthritis.
moral_consequence: Mary's daughter's cat is healthier and feels happier.
immoral_action: Mary feeds the cat some human medication for arthritis rather than see a vet.
immoral_consequence: The cat overdoses on the unprescribed medication.

norm: It is rude to refer to people as homeless.
situation: Jon's friend Ken just told him that he has to live on his brother's couch.
intention: Jon wants to say something to his Ken.
moral_action: Jon tells Ken that he's lucky to have his brother in his life.
moral_consequence: Ken agrees with Jon and feels more appreciative of his brother.
immoral_action: Jon tells Ken that he should just say that he's homeless.
immoral_consequence: Ken feels insulted and thinks that Jon is a real jerk.

norm: It's bad to misrepresent yourself in a chatroom.
situation: Will is bored and logs onto a chatroom full of teenagers.
intention: Will wants to have fun chatting with people.
moral_action: Will starts talking about life, the universe, and everything with the other people.
moral_consequence: Will and the others have a deep conversation and feel satisfied.
immoral_action: Will pretends to be a girl and starts flirting with the guys in the chatroom.
immoral_consequence: Some of the guys start cyber-stalking Will and sending sexual photos to him.

norm: It's wrong to ask a friend to pay for something.
situation: Marie goes shopping at the mall with her friends.
intention: Marie wants to get some new clothing.
moral_action: Marie sees a coat she likes and pays for it with her debit card.
moral_consequence: Maria gets many compliments from her friends about her nice new coat.
immoral_action: Marie finds the perfect outfit and asks her friend Ivanka to pay for it since she's rich.
immoral_consequence: Marie loses Ivanka as a friend over her very rude request.

norm: You shouldn't be against people of certain religions.
situation: Catherine is a feminist atheist who thinks that Islam hurts women, and the father of an Islamic family asks her for directions.
intention: Catherine wants to respond to the man.
moral_action: Catherine explains the layout of the city, and she buys the family a map while talking to them.
moral_consequence: Catherine changes her opinion on Islam after reflecting on her time with the family.
immoral_action: Catherine tells the man that she refuses to help someone with bad values before walking away.
immoral_consequence: Catherine is called a bigot when someone uploads her actions on social media.

norm: You shouldn't catfish people.
situation: Sally has a crush on Henry, but is too shy to talk to him.
intention: Sally wants to get closer with Henry.
moral_action: Sally works out the courage to talk to Henry during class.
moral_consequence: Sally talks to Henry more during class, and they become good friends.
immoral_action: Sally makes a fake account with a totally different picture on social media and starts messaging Henry.
immoral_consequence: Sally and Henry become close but Sally feels apprehensive when Henry asks if they can meet in real life.

norm: You shouldn't leave your family.
situation: Tim, who is 16, experiences regular abuse from his family and has had enough.
intention: Tim wants to talk to his famly about their abuse.
moral_action: Tim tells his family that he will never fully leave them and that he loves them despite the abuse.
moral_consequence: Tim's family apologizes, and they work out a plan to solve their issues.
immoral_action: Tim tells his family that he is moving out of his parents house forever.
immoral_consequence: Tim's parents send police to retrieve Tim and Tim gets in trouble.

norm: It is shallow to judge someone for their weight.
situation: James was looking for a new receptionist and the most qualified applicant was significantly overweight.
intention: James wants to present a good image for his business.
moral_action: James hires the more qualified candidate to handle the receptionist duties regardless of her appearance.
moral_consequence: The new receptionist rapidly improves general office efficiency and is promoted to office manager.
immoral_action: James hires a less qualified but thinner woman as the receptionist.
immoral_consequence: The less qualified candidate frequently forgets to schedule meetings or give James messages.

norm: It's wrong to steal money from your parents.
situation: Zoe is at home putting her makeup on in order to get ready to go to the movies with her friends.
intention: Zoe wants to buy her friends snacks at the movie theater.
moral_action: Zoe asks her money if she can borrow some money to buy snacks at the movie theater.
moral_consequence: Zoe's mom agrees and gives Zoe twenty dollars in exchange for agreeing to do some household chores the next day.
immoral_action: Zoe sees her mom's purse on the counter and grabs a twenty dollar bill from inside of it without asking.
immoral_consequence: Zoe's mom doesn't notice the missing money and Zoe gets to buy snacks at the theater.

norm: It's wrong to lie to your partner about your sexuality.
situation: Rick has been dating Shelly for a few months, when she asks him about his sexual history and health status.
intention: Rick needs to decide what to share about himself.
moral_action: Rick has a direct conversation with her about his sexual preferences and shares the health information that Shelly needs.
moral_consequence: Shelly is grateful for his honesty and feels closer to him than she did before the conversation.
immoral_action: Rick give her a general overview of his health but omits the part of his sexual history which would illustrate that he is bisexual.
immoral_consequence: When Rick does share his sexual preferences, Shelly is hurt by his initial dishonesty.

norm: It's inappropriate to show children gore
situation: Carolyn is stuck watching her brother on Halloween.
intention: Carolyn wants to do something scary.
moral_action: Carolyn turns off the lights and reads her brother some scary stories from the internet.
moral_consequence: Her little brother becomes more popular in school after he tells the stories to his classmates.
immoral_action: Carolyn decides to watches all of the Halloween movies.
immoral_consequence: Her little brother starts crying as he watches the movies.

norm: It's wrong to doubt yourself.
situation: Jacob, who has low self esteem, listens to his boss offer him a promotion, but the promotion has demands above his skill level.
intention: Jacob wants to make money.
moral_action: Jacob takes classes to sharpen his skills, and asks his coworkers to help him out in his new job.
moral_consequence: Jacob has higher self esteem because he's excelling at something challenging.
immoral_action: Jacob refuses the job choosing to stay at his current position.
immoral_consequence: Jacob continues working at a dead end job.

norm: You shouldn't knock someone into the water.
situation: Bill and his toddler son are at a pool.
intention: Bill wants to bring his son into the pool.
moral_action: Bill goes into the water first and shows his son the water is fun then brings his son in slowly.
moral_consequence: Bill's son learns to enjoy playing in the pool.
immoral_action: Bill pushes his son into the water from the back.
immoral_consequence: Bill's son starts crying and becomes traumatized.

norm: It's bad to get an unfair advantage.
situation: Sara works at a company where her boyfriend holds an executive position.
intention: Sara wants to advance in her career.
moral_action: Sara puts in the work, earning a promotion with her results and persistence.
moral_consequence: Sara's peers admire her work ethic and think she is a driven person.
immoral_action: Sara gets her boyfriend to pull some strings and get her a promotion.
immoral_consequence: Sara's peers find out what happened and see her in a bad light.

norm: It is bad to use other people's property without asking.
situation: David has a tree with a branch that is growing too large and see his neighbor's chainsaw.
intention: David wants to obtain the chainsaw.
moral_action: David asks his neighbor if he can use the chainsaw.
moral_consequence: David's neighbor will allow David to use the chainsaw and be open to lending David other items in the future.
immoral_action: David takes his neighbor's chainsaw without asking first.
immoral_consequence: David's neighbor will be annoyed with him and not let him borrow anything in the future.

norm: It's fun to go traveling with others.
situation: Robert and his parents have been reading about Paris for a long time.
intention: Robert wants to visit Paris over the summer.
moral_action: Robert asks his parents to come with him on a trip to Paris.
moral_consequence: Robert and his parents have the time of their life in Paris.
immoral_action: Robert decides to travel to Paris by himself even though he knows his parents would like to come with him.
immoral_consequence: Robert loves Paris but feels a bit lonely during his trip, and Robert's parents are disappointed he didn't ask them to visit Paris with him.

norm: It's bad to fall back on bad habits.
situation: Calvin has been sober from alcohol for 2 years, but is going through a stressful divorce.
intention: Calvin wants to relive his anxiety.
moral_action: Calvin thinks about having a drink, but decides instead to meditate.
moral_consequence: Calvin is able to ease his mind and get himself into a better mental state.
immoral_action: Calvin decides to have some vodka and orange juice to relax him.
immoral_consequence: Calvin ends up drinking on a daily basis again and all his progress is ruined.

norm: It's good to be focused on women's health
situation: While selecting health plans for his company Phil is advised to pick a plan that also supports women's health.
intention: Phil wants to contemplate this suggestion.
moral_action: Phil selects a plan that covers women's health concerns as well as mens.
moral_consequence: Phil is praised for ensuring all employees are adequately covered.
immoral_action: Phil disregards women's health needs and picks a plan that he would get for himself.
immoral_consequence: Phil faces censure when the health plan he selected doesn't suit the company's female employees.

norm: You shouldn't drive fast.
situation: Terry has bought a new corvette.
intention: Terry wants to show off the new car.
moral_action: Terry takes the car to the beach and slowly cruises down the road.
moral_consequence: Terry impresses many with the car and enjoys the drive.
immoral_action: Terry tears down the road at 80mph but never sees the sudden curve until it's way too late.
immoral_consequence: Terry crashes the car beyond repair and is hospitalized for severe injuries.

norm: It's good to tell children the truth about their parentage.
situation: Logan's adopted son, who doesn't know he was adopted, is asking Logan why he looks different than Logan.
intention: Logan wants to give his son an answer.
moral_action: Logan says that he was adopted and gives him details about why the adoption happened.
moral_consequence: Logan's adopted son understands some of his difficulties and reconnects with his biological parents.
immoral_action: Logan says that sometimes children look very different from their parents.
immoral_consequence: Logan's son always feels different than his parents and unsatisfied, but can never figure out why.

norm: It's wrong to let other people take blame for you.
situation: Jack broke the microwave in the break room while he was reheating his rotisserie chicken.
intention: Jack doesn't want to get into trouble.
moral_action: Jack tells his boss that he broke the microwave right after he does it.
moral_consequence: Jack is seen as responsible by his boss, and his employees don't get mad at him.
immoral_action: Jack leaves the microwave broken without telling anyone that he broke it.
immoral_consequence: Jack's boss trusts his employees less and has to buy a new microwave.

norm: It is fun to sing to someone you love.
situation: "Bill is throwing a birthday party for his girlfriend Jade, and she asks Bill to sing ""Happy Birthday"" to her."
intention: Bill wants to respond to Jade's request.
moral_action: "Bill boisterously sings ""Happy Birthday"" to Jade and gets others to join in."
moral_consequence: Jade is so happy to hear Bill sing to her, and it really makes her day.
immoral_action: Bill tells Jade that he doesn't feel like singing and that he thinks the song is silly.
immoral_consequence: Jade is really disappointed, and it puts a cloud over the whole party.

norm: It's not okay to steal something from someone.
situation: Amy needs a graphing calculator for an upcoming test and knows that her brother Mark has one.
intention: Amy wants to use Mark's graphing calculator for her test.
moral_action: Amy asks Mark if she can borrow his graphing calculator.
moral_consequence: Mark happily lends Amy his calculator, and she passes her test.
immoral_action: While Mark is downstairs with friends, Amy goes into his room and takes his graphing calculator.
immoral_consequence: Mark notices that his calculator is missing and argues with his friends over who took it.

norm: It is considerate to break up with someone in person.
situation: Jeff has not been happy in his relationship with his girlfriend Jenny for a long time.
intention: Jeff wants to break up with Jenny.
moral_action: Jeff goes to Jenny's house and tells her that he wants to break up with her.
moral_consequence: Jenny tells Jeff that she's not happy to hear that but at least he came to tell her in person.
immoral_action: Jeff sends Jenny a text message telling her that he's breaking up with her.
immoral_consequence: Jenny feels hurt that Jeff would break up with her, and to make matters worse, it's by a text message.

norm: Studying is a productive way to spend time.
situation: It is midterm season and Jim has his first exam in two days.
intention: Jim wants to plan today and tomorrow.
moral_action: Jim allocates a few hours each day to review his notes and textbooks.
moral_consequence: Jim takes his exam with confidence and is able to pass.
immoral_action: Jim decides to start binging a new show on Netflix.
immoral_consequence: Jim does not pass his exam two days later due to insufficient preparation.

norm: It's wrong to call a fellow worker rude names.
situation: Carl is in the break room at work when a coworker asks him what he thinks of Kim the secretary.
intention: Carl wants to respond to the question.
moral_action: Carl says he thinks Kim is friendly, helpful and good for the company.
moral_consequence: Kim finds out and thinks very highly of Carl in the future.
immoral_action: Carl says he thinks Kim is stupid and looks like a dog.
immoral_consequence: Kim finds out and files a complaint against Carl, getting him fired.

norm: You should return items that have been lent to you.
situation: Peter is packing up to move to another state when he realizes he still has a drill that his neighbor John lent him.
intention: Peter wants to decide what to do with the drill.
moral_action: Peter takes the drill back over to John and thanks John for lending it to him.
moral_consequence: John is glad to get his drill back and tells Peter he will miss having him as a neighbor.
immoral_action: Peter packs the drill to take with him because he thinks it will be useful in the future.
immoral_consequence: John later realizes that Peter moved away with his drill, and he sends him an angry text.

norm: You shouldn't tell your friend's kids what to do.
situation: Harry's son plays with his neighbor's son all of the time.
intention: Harry wants to be a good mentor to both boys.
moral_action: Harry notices his neighbor's kid just copies his son's homework.
moral_consequence: Harry's neighbor thanks him for bringing it to his attention.
immoral_action: Harry tells his neighbor's kid he needs to go to church with them in order to be saved.
immoral_consequence: His neighbor forbids him from every speaking to his son again.

norm: It's wrong to sleep on someone else's dime.
situation: Glenn did not sleep well the night before and is feeling very tired during his shift.
intention: Glenn wants to stop feeling so tired at work.
moral_action: Glenn makes himself a few cups of strong coffee to get the caffeine kick.
moral_consequence: Glenn perks up a little thanks to the caffeine, and he is able to make it through the rest of his shift before going home to sleep.
immoral_action: Glenn goes to the supply closet when no one is looking to take a quick nap.
immoral_consequence: Glenn gets caught by his manager and is written up for sleeping at work.

norm: It's irresponsible to download illegal content from the internet.
situation: Maci just heard that her favorite artist has released a brand new album.
intention: Maci wants to get the new album.
moral_action: Maci goes to the store and buys the album as soon as she can.
moral_consequence: Maci finds out that there is exclusive content in the album she bought from the store.
immoral_action: Maci illegally downloads the album on her mother's computer that night.
immoral_consequence: Maci finds out that her mother's computer has a virus from the files she downloaded.

norm: It's bad to have road rage.
situation: Taylor is in traffic and is stuck behind a driver who does not notice the light turned green.
intention: Taylor wants to get the driver to press on their gas pedal.
moral_action: Taylor beeps her horn once to let the driver know about the light, and the driver goes forward.
moral_consequence: The other drives waves in a friendly way to Taylor, and they both get to their destinations stress free.
immoral_action: Taylor screams and yells at the car in front of her, hurling expletives, until the drives goes forward.
immoral_consequence: The other driver shouts back and Taylor feels guilty.

norm: It's good to be civil during a break up.
situation: Janet is breaking up with her boyfriend after a long relationship.
intention: Janet wants to let her boyfriend know the things that he did wrong while they were together.
moral_action: Janet gently points out mistakes that her boyfriend has made and makes some constructive suggestions of ways to improve.
moral_consequence: After the break-up Janet's boyfriend uses her input to improve his behavior.
immoral_action: Janet yells at her soon-to-be ex angrily, cruelly highlighting all his faults.
immoral_consequence: Janet's boyfriend is emotionally hurt and is bitter towards her.

norm: It is rude to have bad manners.
