situation: John is eating at a fancy restaurant with some colleagues when he feels indigestion rising up in his throat.
intention: John wants to relive the gastric pressure he's feeling.
moral_action: John excuses himself from the table with a hand gesture and turns away with a hand over his mouth, to quietly and slowly let some gas escape.
moral_consequence: John's colleagues hardly  notice him as they continue talking and having a great evening.
immoral_action: John lets out a gloriously loud and long burp that thunders over the table.
immoral_consequence: John's colleagues recoil in horror as they watch their colleague act like a common animal in public.

norm: It's dangerous to speed when you're driving on the highway.
situation: Shaun's girlfriend just arrived in town, and he decides to go over and surprise her.
intention: Shaun wants to drive.
moral_action: Being that Shaun is surprising his girlfriend, he takes his time driving.
moral_consequence: Shaun gets over to his girlfriends place at a reasonable time and is glad to see her.
immoral_action: Being exited that his girlfriend is in town, Shaun drives faster than normal and loses control of his ca.
immoral_consequence: Shaun gets into a car accident and gets injured.

norm: It's kind to avoid hurting other people's feelings.
situation: Julie's sister asks her if Julie thinks her sister is an attractive girl.
intention: Julie wants to answer her sister.
moral_action: Julie tells her sister that she's attractive enough and besides that has a nice personality.
moral_consequence: Julie's sister feels more confidence after hearing Julie's complimentary answer.
immoral_action: Julie tells her sister that she was born unlucky and that she just isn't attractive at all.
immoral_consequence: Julie's sister is emotionally devastated by Julie's comment and her self-esteem suffers.

norm: You shouldn't share photos without permission.
situation: Vanessa attended Willow's wedding and took lots of nice photos on her phone during the reception.
intention: Vanessa wants to post the photos on her social media.
moral_action: Vanessa asks Willow when she can post the photos she took of the wedding and waits until Willow says it's okay.
moral_consequence: Vanessa happily shares her photos with everyone and doesn't upstage Willow's official photos.
immoral_action: Vanessa posts the photos on social media as soon as she gets home from the wedding.
immoral_consequence: Willow is upset that Vanessa is sharing photos of her wedding without permission and stops being friends with Vanessa.

norm: You should always make time to spend with your kids.
situation: Paul is very busy at his job and his kids have asked him to play baseball with them.
intention: Paul wants to respond to his kids' request.
moral_action: Paul tells his kids that he can make time to play baseball with them.
moral_consequence: Paul's kids will build a stronger bond with their father.
immoral_action: Paul tells his kids he's too busy at work to play baseball with them.
immoral_consequence: Paul's kids will feel that he doesn't care about them.

norm: It's not okay to not care about your children.
situation: Jeffrey has to move away from his family for his work for a few years, and leaves his children with his wife.
intention: Jeffrey wants to earn a lot of money.
moral_action: Jeffrey calls his kids every day to talk to them and tries to go back home whenever possible.
moral_consequence: Jeffrey's children feel close to their father and know that he is working hard for them.
immoral_action: Jeffrey buries himself in work and doesn't take the time to contact his family.
immoral_consequence: Jeffrey's relationship with his children becomes cold and distant.

norm: It's wrong to not appreciate your friends.
situation: Mike doesn't have a car, so he gets a ride to school every day from his friend Joe.
intention: Mike wants to continue riding to school with Joe.
moral_action: Mike thanks Joe for giving him rides to school everyday by treating him to dinner.
moral_consequence: Joe feels appreciated and continues to have a strong friendship with Mike.
immoral_action: For a week straight, Mike has been asking Joe to drive him to many different places before school without even saying thanks.
immoral_consequence: Joe begins to feel used and tells Mike to find his own ride to school.

norm: You shouldn't keep pestering someone with calls and texts.
situation: Margaret's husband was at work, and she called him non-stop all day.
intention: Margaret wants to know when her husband will get off.
moral_action: Margaret calls her husband once and leaves a message on his voice mail.
moral_consequence: Margaret's husband calls her back when he can and lets her know when he is working until.
immoral_action: Margaret calls her husband every five minutes until he answers the phone.
immoral_consequence: Margaret's husband gets annoyed and yells at her when she does get in touch with him.

norm: It is wrong to support people that molest children.
situation: Mary is a citizen of her state.
intention: Mary wants to vote for a candidate for governor.
moral_action: Mary votes for a man who isn't her favorite but doesn't have a criminal record.
moral_consequence: Mary's friends who were worried the child molester would win feel supported.
immoral_action: Mary votes for a man convicted of molesting children.
immoral_consequence: Friends of Mary's who were molested confront her and break off their friendship.

norm: It's bad to partake in illegal activities.
situation: Jess really wants to watch a film, but she has to buy a streaming service to watch it.
intention: Jess wants to watch the movie.
moral_action: Jess buys the new streaming service in order to watch the movie.
moral_consequence: Jess is able to watch the movie she wanted and other movies as well.
immoral_action: Jess downloads the film off of a website from Mexico without paying.
immoral_consequence: Jess could get in a lot of trouble if the copyright holders find out.

norm: It's bad to discriminate against different lifestyle choices.
situation: Fabian and Lance are in a cake shop run by Donald, the baker where they ask Donald to bake them a wedding cake for their same-sex wedding.
intention: Don wants to respond to Fabian and Lance's request.
moral_action: Donald tells the two lovers that he's happy to make them a cake as he's done hundreds of times for other weddings.
moral_consequence: Lance and Fabian are delighted that their dream wedding plans are coming together smoothly.
immoral_action: Donald tells the two lovers that gays will burn in hell and that he does not take money from disgusting sinners.
immoral_consequence: Lance and Fabian are horrified by Donald's discrimination and are scared Donald might physically attack them.

norm: You shouldn't break people's things.
situation: Tina is playing with her friend Nancy's toy, but Tina and Nancy have started fighting.
intention: Tina wants to express her anger.
moral_action: Tina yells at Nancy some, but does not get violent.
moral_consequence: Tina and Nancy stop fighting and start playing together again.
immoral_action: Tina throws Nancy's toy on the ground, breaking it in two.
immoral_consequence: Nancy's mother sends Tina home, and Tina gets in trouble with her parents.

norm: It is rude to blow off a friend's birthday.
situation: Samantha was looking to buy tickets to a concert on Friday, but Samantha had already accepted Christine's invitation to her birthday party that same day.
intention: Samantha wants to go to the concert.
moral_action: Samantha looks for other concert dates and invites Christine to go the concert the following week as a birthday gift.
moral_consequence: Samantha has a great time at Christine's birthday party and the two get to bond in the concert too.
immoral_action: Samantha skips Christine's birthday party, and tells Christine she'd rather go to a concert than her party.
immoral_consequence: Christine gets mad at Samantha and the two friends stop talking to each other.

norm: It is disrespectful to throw away your flatmate's food.
situation: Kyle is going through the fridge when he notices a terrible smell coming from it.
intention: Kyle wants to get rid of whatever is causing the smell.
moral_action: Kyle points out the old food and asks his friend if the items have spoiled.
moral_consequence: Kyle's roommate throws away the food himself and avoids risking eating it.
immoral_action: Kyle discards all of the older looking food in the fridge including his roommates items.
immoral_consequence: Kyle's roommate feels that his roommate has wasted his food that was still edible.

norm: It's rude to risk someone's academic standing by copying them.
situation: Larry has a big exam coming up in school that is notoriously long.
intention: Larry wants to complete the exam on time.
moral_action: Larry does practice exams to make sure he is within the time limit.
moral_consequence: Larry completes the exam on time and the other students are not bothered.
immoral_action: Larry looks for a student that is ahead of him in the exam and writes what they write on the exam.
immoral_consequence: Larry and the other student get in trouble with the Professor.

norm: It's polite to abide by others' schedules.
situation: Jennifer is opening a new joint bank account with her husband, and they need to go to the branch during weekday business hours.
intention: Jennifer wants to schedule an appointment for their bank meeting.
moral_action: Jennifer asks her husband when his lunch break is and then schedules the meeting for that time.
moral_consequence: Jennifer's husband makes it to the bank and then back to work in time.
immoral_action: Jennifer schedules the appointment for the time that suits her best without consulting with her husband first.
immoral_consequence: Jennifer's husband ends up missing an important meeting at work in order to make the appointment at the bank.

norm: You shouldn't leave your partner for someone else.
situation: Mark and Anna are in a long distance relationship, and Mark is lonely on a Friday night while his ex asks him out.
intention: Mark wants to do something to make himself less lonely.
moral_action: Mark calls Anna and asks to watch a movie with her over Zoom.
moral_consequence: Mark has a fun night.
immoral_action: Mark accepts his ex's offer, and being with her Mark stops talking to Anna to be with his ex.
immoral_consequence: Mark is stuck in a rough relationship which ends in heartbreak.

norm: You shouldn't ignore someone's birthday message.
situation: Jerry is turning 30 and is hosting a party for himself with some close friends.
intention: Jerry wants to celebrate his birthday.
moral_action: During the party, one of Jerry's friends from out of town sends him a text message wishing him a happy birthday, which Jerry replies to immediately.
moral_consequence: Jerry's friend feels happy and connected with Jerry because of his quick response.
immoral_action: During the party, one of Jerry's friends from out of town sends him a text message wishing him a happy birthday, which Jerry ignores.
immoral_consequence: Jerry's friend feels hurt and frustrated about being ignored by Jerry.

norm: It's wrong to break up with people for their appearance.
situation: Steve is being flirted with by a girl at work who is prettier than his girlfriend.
intention: Steve wants to get to know the girl at work.
moral_action: Steve hangs out with the girl at work at lunchtime.
moral_consequence: Steve learns that the girl at work is boring, and he is glad that he is still with his girlfriend.
immoral_action: Steve breaks up with his girlfriend because she is not as pretty and begins dating the girl at work.
immoral_consequence: Steve soon learns that the girl at work is boring, and he misses his old girlfriend.

norm: It's good to be concerned about defenseless animals.
situation: Noah is driving down the road when he spots a dog running beside the highway.
intention: Noah wants to help the dog.
moral_action: Noah pulls over and goes over to the dog and picks it up, puts it in his car and takes it to a vet.
moral_consequence: The dog is reunited with it's owner when the vet finds their name on the dog's microchip.
immoral_action: Noah calls the police to alert animal control about a dog that's near the highway.
immoral_consequence: The dog is hit and killed because it takes animal control too long to get to it's location.

norm: It is good to spend money on yourself.
situation: Pete doesn't make that much money, so he can't buy too much stuff.
intention: Pete wants to save money for Christmas.
moral_action: Pete doesn't spend too much money on other people's gifts so that he can buy himself a new car.
moral_consequence: Pete's new car makes him happy, and it makes him feel accomplished.
immoral_action: Pete spends all of his money buying gifts for other people.
immoral_consequence: Pete makes other people happy, but he's not happy himself.

norm: It's irresponsible to let your children run amok.
situation: Molly's young son Jaden has a birthday coming up.
intention: Molly wants to take Jaden out to dinner for his birthday.
moral_action: Molly teaches Jaden dinner manners and enforces them.
moral_consequence: Jaden is so well-behaved at dinner that the waiters bring him a complimentary ice cream for his birthday.
immoral_action: Molly ignores Jaden while she goes over the dinner menu.
immoral_consequence: Jaden runs around the restaurant and bumps into a waiter, causing him to spill food everywhere.

norm: You shouldn't share certain things with other people.
situation: James' best friend is staying at his house for a sleepover and forget his toothbrush.
intention: James wants to help his friend brush his teeth.
moral_action: James tells his friend to order a new toothbrush from Amazon with 2-hour Prime delivery.
moral_consequence: James' friend orders a new toothbrush, and they continue enjoying the sleepover.
immoral_action: James tells his friend that he can use James' toothbrush for that night.
immoral_consequence: James' friend calls him gross and insists on being driven home to get his toothbrush.

norm: You should always do favors for others.
situation: Lenny is relaxing at home about to watch a movie when his friend Norbert asks him to come babysit for him in an emergency.
intention: Lenny wants to answer Norbert's call for help.
moral_action: Lenny tells Norbert he can watch the movie at his house with his kids and watch them that way, so he'll be right over.
moral_consequence: Norbert thinks that's a great idea and is glad his friend will help him.
immoral_action: Lenny tells Norbert that he was just about to watch a movie, so he's busy and Norbert should find someone else.
immoral_consequence: Norbert is annoyed that Lenny thinks watching a movie means he's busy and is angry his friend won't help him.

norm: It's good to be attracted to your significant other
situation: Henry can either watch porn on his computer or spend time with his wife.
intention: Henry wants sexual gratification.
moral_action: Henry spends time with his wife and has eyes only for her.
moral_consequence: Henry's wife feels beautiful and appreciated, building their relationship.
immoral_action: Henry watches porn and fantasizes about the woman he watches.
immoral_consequence: Henry's wife feels neglected and unappreciated, so she divorces him.

norm: You should not make fun of people for their interests
situation: Bruce is attending a freshman mixer just before the beginning of fall semester.
intention: Bruce wants to make friends and increase his social status a bit if he can.
moral_action: Ed stands up for Harold saying he admires anyone with a mind for mathematics.
moral_consequence: Ed becomes friends with Harold who tutors him to a good grade in freshman calculus.
immoral_action: Bruce joins in with a group of frat boys giving Harold the math nerd a hard time about his major.
immoral_consequence: Bruce embarrasses Harold, but is invited to rush the fraternity.

norm: Sometimes it's a mercy to put down an ailing creature.
situation: Kacy's dog is very old and can no longer control it's bladder.
intention: Kacy wants to have clean carpet.
moral_action: Kacy brings the dog to the vet who advises her to have the dog put down because of quality of life issues.
moral_consequence: Kacy's dog dies feeling loved in the arms of Kacy.
immoral_action: Kacy puts the dog in a cage in her basement and checks on it once a day.
immoral_consequence: Kacy's dog eventually dies by itself in the basement.

norm: It's rude to annoy and exasperate people.
situation: Sabrina has received a call from a telemarketer in the middle of dinner, and she is annoyed.
intention: Sabrina wants the telemarketers to leave her alone.
moral_action: Sabrina tells the the telemarketer she is not interested and to put her number on a do-not-call list.
moral_consequence: The telemarketer is able to end the call quickly and continue doing their job.
immoral_action: Sabrina decides to mess with the telemarketer by pretending to misunderstand and misinterpret everything they are saying until they give up and hang up.
immoral_consequence: The telemarketer is annoyed and upset because they are a minimum wage worker who was just trying to do their job.

norm: It's rude to break up with someone over text.
situation: Bill and his girlfriend Jane have arguing intensely for months.
intention: Bill wants to end the relationship with Jane.
moral_action: Bill meets with Jane and tells her that he wants to break up.
moral_consequence: Jane agrees to an amicable split from Bill.
immoral_action: Bill sends a text to Jane that he wants to break up.
immoral_consequence: Jane becomes mad at Bill for not breaking up with her in person.

norm: It's rude to dominate a conversation
situation: Casey and Tom are friends who have not seen each other in awhile.
intention: Casey wants to have a conversation with Tom in order to catch up on things.
moral_action: Casey asks Tom open ended questions about how he has been doing and actively listens at his responses.
moral_consequence: They talk for hours and have a very pleasant overall conversation.
immoral_action: Casey talks without a break and makes it challenging for Tom to get a word in.
immoral_consequence: Tom gets frustrated and excuses himself in order to talk to others at the party.

norm: It's rude to throw food at your significant other.
situation: James is having dinner with his wife at a fancy restaraunt.
intention: James wants to enjoy the meal.
moral_action: James spends the meal having lively and entertaining conversation with his wife and enjoying the food.
moral_consequence: James' wife has a great time as well and really enjoys the experience all around.
immoral_action: James rips off a small piece of his dinner roll and tosses it at his wife when she isn't paying attention.
immoral_consequence: James' wife does not find the action funny in the least and gets angry at him for doing such a thing at a fancy restaraunt.

norm: It's good to give a friend a place to stay
situation: Dave's apartment burns down, and he asks his friend Fred to help him find a new place to stay.
intention: Fred wants to help Dave find a place to live.
moral_action: Fred offers to let Dave stay in his home for a while.
moral_consequence: Dave accepts the offer and thanks Fred for being so helpful.
immoral_action: Fred tells Dave to go live at the homeless shelter.
immoral_consequence: Dave goes to the homeless shelter and has to sleep on a dirty cot.

norm: It is offensive to make fun of someones weight.
situation: Tanya notices her daughter has been gaining way too much weight lately.
intention: Tanya wants to tell her daughter to lose weight.
moral_action: Tanya tells her daughter she is too heavy very directly, and offers to help with a diet.
moral_consequence: Tanya's daughter is initially offended, but later accepts that it is a good plan, and Tanya feels proud.
immoral_action: Tanya makes fun of her daughter's weight in hopes of setting her straight.
immoral_consequence: Tanya's daughter cries and Tanya feels sad and hugs her.

norm: It's rude to demean someone for their opinion.
situation: Donny is in the middle of a debate with a friend.
intention: He wants to make his point heard.
moral_action: Danny lays out the reasons for his argument but listens intently to what his friend has to say.
moral_consequence: Danny and his friend understand each other better and find common ground.
immoral_action: Danny screams at his friend and calls him dumb.
immoral_consequence: Danny's friend now respects him less and doesn't trust that they can talk about sensitive issues anymore.

norm: It's wrong to dictate how people use their cell phones.
situation: Jen is having trouble studying because of her roommate talking on speakerphone with the volume up high.
intention: Jen wants to minimize external noise in order to focus.
moral_action: Jen puts on some noise cancelling headphones to drown out the sound.
moral_consequence: Jen is relieved because she can think clearly.
immoral_action: Jen tells her roommate to take it her phone off speakerphone.
immoral_consequence: Jen feels bad and thinks she was rude and bossy.

norm: It is bad to get into fights at school.
situation: Brian and Cole are having a disagreement at school.
intention: Brian wants to settle their disagreement.
moral_action: Brian listens to Cole's perspective, then offers his own.
moral_consequence: Brian learns about how Cole thinks and feels.
immoral_action: Brian insults Cole's intelligence, then punches him.
immoral_consequence: Brian gets suspended from school.

norm: It is good to say how you are feeling.
situation: Ines is at home feeling queasy when her friends call to invite her out for drinks.
intention: Ines wants to see her friends.
moral_action: Ines tells her friends that she doesn't feel good but would love to video chat.
moral_consequence: Ines and her friends are able to see each other while she tries to feel better.
immoral_action: Ines goes out with her friends without telling them how she's been feeling.
immoral_consequence: Ines' friends feed her drinks until she throws up.

norm: You should always return things to their rightful owner.
situation: Mike is an Uber driver, and his last passenger left their wallet in his car.
intention: Mike has to decide whether to give the wallet back.
moral_action: Mike drives all the way to the passenger's house to give the wallet back.
moral_consequence: The passenger feels grateful and no longer has to worry about it.
immoral_action: Mike decides to keep the wallet and tells the passenger he didn't find it.
immoral_consequence: The passenger has to wait to get another licence and loses any money in it.

norm: It is wrong to glorify injuries.
situation: Ray is called into the room by his dad when he is suspended from school for fighting a bully.
intention: Ray's dad wants to talk to him about fighting.
moral_action: Ray's dad explains to him that violence is never the answer, and he should report bullying to his teachers.
moral_consequence: Ray isn't suspended for fighting in school any more.
immoral_action: Ray's dad tell him that he did the right by busting the bully's nose.
immoral_consequence: Ray gets into another fight with the bully and is suspended again.

norm: It is wrong to waste your employer's money.
situation: Alex is granted a large amount of autonomy at his job and the company will cover fairly high food costs while traveling.
intention: Alex wants to eat a quality meal and have some drinks to recharge.
moral_action: Alex spends a reasonable amount on food and drinks at a casual restaurant.
moral_consequence: Alex is granted continued free reign on food expenses he reports.
immoral_action: Alex orders very expensive food and drink at an expensive restaurant.
immoral_consequence: Alex's boss notices the high charge and limits his priveleges.

norm: You should respect your grandparents.
situation: Joe is at his Grandmother's house for Thanksgiving dinner and is listening to her talk about old black and white movies.
intention: Joe wants to talk about something different.
moral_action: Joe waits until his Grandmother is done talking and then strikes up a conversation about sports.
moral_consequence: Joe's Grandmother appreciates having somebody that listens to her and gives him an extra slice of pumpkin pie for dessert.
immoral_action: Joe tells his Grandmother that her stories are boring and starts talking about sports instead.
immoral_consequence: Joe's Grandmother is upset at how she was treated and doesn't invite Joe to Thanksgiving next year.

norm: Stealing money is something that you shouldn't do.
situation: Bob has been laid off from work.
intention: Bob needs to pay his rent before the end of the month.
moral_action: Bob asks his brother if he can borrow money to pay his rent and his brother says yes.
moral_consequence: Bob is relieved that he can pay his rent on time and feels grateful that his brother helped him out.
immoral_action: Bob goes to the local convenience store that night and robs it.
immoral_consequence: The convenience store had a video camera and Bob is caught and arrested.

norm: You shouldn't drive without your glasses.
situation: Brian had left his glasses in the house when he was leaving to go to work.
intention: Brian wants to drive to work.
moral_action: Brian goes back into the house to get his glasses before he leaves.
moral_consequence: Brian is able to drive to his job and get there safely.
immoral_action: Brian drives his car to work without wearing his glasses.
immoral_consequence: Brian can't see a red light in front of him and gets into an accident.

norm: It's despicable to stab a hamster.
situation: Moe is in his friends room when his friend's hamster crawls on him.
intention: Moe wants the hamster off of him.
moral_action: Moe gently removes the hamster and hands it to his friend.
moral_consequence: Moe's friend puts the hamster in the cage, and they resume their visit.
immoral_action: Moe stabs the hamster with a pencil.
immoral_consequence: Moe's friend calls the police and Moe is arrested.

norm: It's wrong to get high before you go to work.
situation: Nan is on the way to work for another boring shift.
intention: Nan wants to decide if she should smoke a bit of pot to ease into her shift.
moral_action: Nan waits until after work to smoke.
moral_consequence: She gets through the shift and is pleased.
immoral_action: Nan smokes before work in the car.
immoral_consequence: She is loopy at work and performs poorly.

norm: It's wrong to irritate your partner.
situation: Jill was watching her favorite television show when Bobby got a phone call.
intention: Bobby wants to answer the phone.
moral_action: Bobby answers the phone and goes outside to carry on his conversation.
moral_consequence: Jill is able to peacefully watch her television show without any interruptions.
immoral_action: Bobby answers the phone and lowers the volume on the television.
immoral_consequence: Jill is upset because she misses half the dialogue on the television show.

norm: It's good to visit your mother.
situation: The holidays are approaching and John has vacation time to spare.
intention: John wants to create memorable moments during his vacation.
moral_action: John chooses to head back to his home town for the holiday vacation to see family.
moral_consequence: John's mother reconnects with him, and she enjoys the quality time together before her passing in the next year.
immoral_action: John chooses to spend his holiday vacation alone at a far away resort.
immoral_consequence: John's mother misses him over the holidays, and they grow more distant.

norm: It's hurtful to steal from your girlfriend.
situation: Donald is really hungry, and doesn't have much money, he's embarrassed to tell his girlfriend this though, and notices her purse.
intention: Donald wants money for food.
moral_action: Donald asks his girlfriend for some money for lunch, stating that he's a little broke at the moment.
moral_consequence: The girlfriend scolds him for not telling her sooner, and grabs him the money.
immoral_action: Donald puts his hand into his girlfriend's purse and takes the money.
immoral_consequence: Donald's girlfriend comes out, catching him, and instantly breaks up with him.

norm: It's disrespectful to make fun of your teacher's name.
situation: Billy just moved and switched schools, so he is the new kid in class.
intention: Billy wants to make the class laugh.
moral_action: Billy raises his hand and asks a ridiculous and funny question.
moral_consequence: The teacher is amused by the question Billy asked and has a good laugh.
immoral_action: Billy intentionally says his teacher's name wrong making it sound funny.
immoral_consequence: The teacher writers Billy up and sends him to detention.

norm: It is good to participate in activities at school.
situation: John has a free period during school.
intention: John wants to fill the time with something to do.
moral_action: John decides to join a school club that tutors other students.
moral_consequence: John will meet new people and help others.
immoral_action: John decides to hang out in the school parking lot and smoke cigarettes.
immoral_consequence: John will develop a smoking habit and not do anything productive.

norm: It is wrong to abadon you friends.
situation: Keith drove with Jim to the beach, where Keith met two girls who invited him to go to a movie.
intention: Keith wants to go to the movie with the girls he met.
moral_action: Keith finds Jim and drives him and the two girls to the movie theater.
moral_consequence: Jim partners up with one of the girls, and they end up making dinner plans for later in the week.
immoral_action: Keith takes his car and drives with the girls to the movie theater without informing Jim.
immoral_consequence: Jim wanders around the beach looking for Keith, gets sunburned, and has to walk home.

norm: You shouldn't pronounce things wrong just to bother others.
situation: "Casey was talking to his friends about baseball, and he referred to a ""Kay"" when talking about the pitcher."
intention: Casey wants to talk baseball.
moral_action: "Casey corrects himself when he learns that ""K"" on the scoresheet stands for ""strikeout""."
moral_consequence: "They get into aa discussion over why it's ""K"" and not ""S"" or ""STR"" or ""SO"" which would all make more sense."
immoral_action: "Casey keeps calling them ""kays"" even after his friends figure out he means ""strikeout""."
immoral_consequence: It annoys his friends and ticks them off and makes them have less fun.

norm: You shouldn't grab a chair that belongs to someone else.
situation: John is walking into his biology class.
intention: John wants to find a seat for the class.
moral_action: John finds an empty seat near the front of the class.
moral_consequence: John learns a lot about biology and enjoys the lecture.
immoral_action: John takes a seat away from a smaller, weaker student.
immoral_consequence: John is sent to the principal's office.

norm: It is good to talk about experiences.
situation: Caleb is in the break room at work making coffee when a new employee walks in and asks Caleb for advice.
intention: Caleb wants to get back to his office.
moral_action: Caleb tells the new employee to send him an email about it, and he'll respond soon.
moral_consequence: The new employee trusts Caleb and sends him a detailed email about an hour later.
immoral_action: Caleb tells the new employee that he can't talk right now because he has to get back to working.
immoral_consequence: The new employee thinks Caleb doesn't like him and never initiates another conversation with him.

norm: It's kind to care for family when they're ill.
situation: John's mother is sick and in bed, but John has to go to work.
intention: John wants to go to work.
moral_action: John asks a neighbor to take care of his mother while he's at work.
moral_consequence: John's mother gets taken care of and improves in health.
immoral_action: "John tells his mother ""Get well soon"", leaves her a glass of water, then goes to work."
immoral_consequence: John's mother gets worse because she can't get up to get food or medicine.

norm: You should never tell other people about you misdeeds.
situation: James suffers from kleptomania and frequently shoplifts from local stores.
intention: James wants to feel less guilty about shoplifting.
moral_action: James writes about his feelings in a paper journal, then burns the confessions.
moral_consequence: James is able to work through some of his emotional issues and take things less often.
immoral_action: One night James gets drunk and tells his best friend about his habit of taking things without paying for them.
immoral_consequence: James' best friend tells him to repay the store owners, or he'll go to the cops.

norm: It's good to tip well.
situation: Jim finishes at a restaurant and is ready to pay.
intention: Jim wants to pay and tip at the restruant.
moral_action: Jim tips a rather large amount of money for his meal.
moral_consequence: Jim comes back and receives much better service than he did before.
immoral_action: Jim tips $1 seeing as how he only ordered a $10 meal.
immoral_consequence: Jim comes back and receives pretty much the same service he did before.

norm: It's good to forgive others for their past.
situation: Nick meets his former fifth grade teacher, who made his life very difficult, on the street one day.
intention: Nick wants to say something to her.
moral_action: Nick tells his ex-teacher that it's good to see her again and that he learned to deal with difficulties that year.
moral_consequence: Nick's teacher apologizes for the difficulties and is glad to hear some encouragement.
immoral_action: Nick tells his ex-teacher that she made his fifth grade year very difficult.
immoral_consequence: Nick's teacher feels unappreciated and questions why she even bothers teaching.

norm: It's mean to make your spouse unhappy.
situation: Randy is home when his wife arrives back from work looking tired and stressed.
intention: Randy wants to tell his wife to start an activity.
moral_action: Randy tells his wife that she looks tired, and she should go for a swim in the pool while he makes dinner.
moral_consequence: Randy's wife is delighted that he sees that she's stressed and that he suggested for her to do something fun while he takes care of chores.
immoral_action: Randy tells his wife that she should go ahead and start dinner right away.
immoral_consequence: Randy's wife is angry that Randy clearly doesn't see she's tired and that the first thing he tells her is to do something for him.

norm: Refusing to speak to someone is rude.
situation: Stacy is on a long flight when her seat mate tries to start a conversation.
intention: Stacy wants to relax and read a book.
moral_action: Stacy tells her seatmate that she would like to quietly read.
moral_consequence: Stacy's seat mate thanks her for her honesty and leaves her alone for the rest of the flight.
immoral_action: Stacy opens a book and starts reading without acknowledging her seatmate.
immoral_consequence: Stacy's seat mate calls her rude and feels offended.

norm: You shouldn't let your parents track your phone.
situation: Stefy, a lady in high school whose parents monitor her through the phone, is thinking of ways that she can make her parents happy.
intention: Stefy wants to buy a surprise gift for her dad.
moral_action: Stefy leaves her phone at home and goes to a men's watch store to get her dad a watch.
moral_consequence: Stefy's dad is totally surprised by the watch and loves the gift very much.
immoral_action: Stefy goes to a men's watch store and looks up different types of watches with her phone, then buys one.
immoral_consequence: Stefy's parents see that she went to a men's watch store and the surprise is ruined.

norm: It's wrong to go to a concert without your partner.
situation: John's friend invites him to a concert and also says that his new girlfriend can come if she wants to.
intention: John wants to decide whether to invite his girlfriend to come to the concert.
moral_action: John decides to invite his new girlfriend to come to the concert with him.
moral_consequence: John's girlfriend has a great time at the concert and feels happy and included.
immoral_action: John decides they will have more fun on their own and declines to invite his girlfriend.
immoral_consequence: John's girlfriend finds out that she wasn't invited and feels sad and left out.

norm: It's expected that you write thank you notes
situation: Jack got married and his boss got him a very expensive gift.
intention: Jack wants to thank his boss.
moral_action: Jack write a handwritten letter to his boss thanking him for the gift.
moral_consequence: Jack's boss will think Jack appreciates the gift and is grateful.
immoral_action: Jack says thanks to his boss while passing him in the hallway at work.
immoral_consequence: Jack's boss will think Jack is too casual and not appreciative enough of the gift.

norm: It is wrong to draw on photographs.
situation: Thomas' grandmother was showing him her old wedding photograph's and talking about missing his departed grandfather.
intention: Thomas wants to make a gift for his grandmother.
moral_action: Thomas redraws his grandmother's wedding photograph and writes her a lovely letter.
moral_consequence: Thomas's grandmother is happy to receive the drawing and thanks him for his thoughtful gift.
immoral_action: Thomas gets the black and white photograph of his grandmother and colors it with his pencils.
immoral_consequence: Thomas's grandmother is shocked and saddened at what Thomas had done to her wedding photograph.

norm: It's wrong to mock people.
situation: Jim is sitting in the quad between classes chatting with some classmates.
intention: Jim wants to entertain his classmates.
moral_action: Jim tells a funny joke that he learned the other day.
moral_consequence: Jim makes his classmates laugh, and they compliment him on the clever joke.
immoral_action: Jim walks behind a disabled person imitating their limp.
immoral_consequence: Tim is shunned by his classmates for his inappropriate action.

norm: You should not be nosy about someone else's life.
situation: Lynn overhears her friend arguing with her boyfriend.
intention: Lynn wants to be there for her friend.
moral_action: Lynn gives her friend privacy but lets her know she is there to talk.
moral_consequence: Lynn's friend appreciates the gesture and feels closer to Lynn.
immoral_action: Lynn eavesdrops on the conversation and then gives her friend unsolicited advice.
immoral_consequence: Lynn's friend accuses her of being nosy and stops speaking to her.

norm: You should have your kids respect your financial situation.
situation: Bryan, a poor man, has children who are begging him to buy an expensive video game system.
intention: Bryan wants to stop the begging.
moral_action: Bryan explains that he doesn't have a lot of money and needs it for food and clothes.
moral_consequence: Bryan's kids learn to economize money and get what you really need.
immoral_action: Bryan buys the children the game system they want.
immoral_consequence: Bryan has very little money left and the children have to sacrifice food and clothing.

norm: It is worrying to leave your wallet behind unintentionally.
situation: Zach is eating at a diner and has to leave in a hurry because he is running late for a movie he has tickets to.
intention: Zach wants to get to the movie on time.
moral_action: Zach makes sure he has all of his personal belongings before leaving the diner for the movie theater.
moral_consequence: Zach makes it to the movie just in time and finds the movie ticket he needs in his wallet.
immoral_action: Zach is in such a hurry that he accidentally leaves his wallet behind on the table at the diner.
immoral_consequence: Zach later realizes he forgot his wallet, gets very worried and ends up missing the movie because the tickets were inside of it.

norm: You should share concerns with your significant other.
situation: Rob's company is laying off dozens of positions causing him great concern and his partner, who notices this, asks him what is wrong.
intention: Rob wants to keep his partner from worrying about their financial situation.
moral_action: Rob tells his partner what's happening but focuses on possible solutions in the event that they need them.
moral_consequence: Rob's partner feels prepared even if the worse case scenario is true.
immoral_action: Rob tells his partner that there is nothing wrong and acts like he doesn't know anything.
immoral_consequence: Rob's partner finds out the truth eventually and feels that he withholds important information from her.

norm: It's dangerous to lie about medical conditions
situation: Perry just got dumped by his long time girlfriend and is extremely depressed over it.
intention: Perry wants to get something to numb the pain.
moral_action: Perry parties with his friends, and they drink some alcohol together.
moral_consequence: Perry's friends enjoy being able to spend more time with him.
immoral_action: Perry tells his doctor that he has chronic back issues in order to get a prescription for pain medicine.
immoral_consequence: Perry's friends become concerned that he has developed a dependency on opiates.

norm: You shouldn't let your lawn become overrun.
situation: Mabel, a poor woman, can't work on her lawn because she's visiting her mother in another state for a month.
intention: Mabel wants to save money.
moral_action: Mabel asks her cousin to do the yard work in exchange for free home cooked meals for the rest of the month.
moral_consequence: Mabel learns new recipes through cooking food for her cousin,.
immoral_action: Mabel tells herself that she'll take care of her yard when she returns home.
immoral_consequence: Mabel receives a citation from the homeowners association for her messy lawn.

norm: It's rude to refer to people as pigs.
situation: Jerry made new friends at school, and they hang out during the day.
intention: Jerry wants to give nicknames to his friends.
moral_action: Jerry calls his friends nicknames based on what they're good at.
moral_consequence: Jerry's friends think Jerry is a positive person and like being around him.
immoral_action: Jerry calls his friends pigs because they eat lunch together.
immoral_consequence: Jerry's friends are offended and don't want to eat with Jerry.

norm: It's good to inform your employer of potential workplace problems.
situation: Glenn works in an office when he smells an unusual smell, which is a gas leak, coming through the air ducts.
intention: Glenn wants to stop smelling the smell.
moral_action: Glenn calls up the maintenance crew and reports that he smells something strange.
moral_consequence: The maintenance crew realizes what the problem is and evacuates the building, saving the workers.
immoral_action: Glenn moves his work location so that he doesn't smell the strange smell.
immoral_consequence: The gas leak continues and eventually poisons other people in the building.

norm: It is good to stand up for family.
situation: Nick is walking down the street with his mom Nancy when a strange man calls Nancy ugly.
intention: Nick wants to talk to the strange man about what he just said.
moral_action: Nick tells the strange man to back off and apologize before he makes him ugly, too.
moral_consequence: The strange man gets a little scared and apologizes to Nancy and learns to keep his rude comments to himself.
immoral_action: Nick tells the strange man that his mom is ugly because she's old so his point is too obvious.
immoral_consequence: Nancy is insulted that Nick is agreeing with the man that she's ugly and that he's not being very forceful with the man.

norm: It's bad to play pranks if they're harmful to people.
situation: Jim's sister Ann put a fake spider in Jim's bed to scare him.
intention: Jim wants to get back at Ann.
moral_action: Jim throws a rubber snake in Ann's room.
moral_consequence: Ann screams and runs out of the room.
immoral_action: Jim lights a firecracker and throws it in Ann's room.
immoral_consequence: The firecracker explodes injuring Ann.

norm: You shouldn't steal things from people.
situation: Gina is hanging out with her friends in a mall.
intention: Gina wants a stick of lipstick.
moral_action: Gina takes the lipstick to the cashier and pays for it.
moral_consequence: Gina adds the lipstick to her collection.
immoral_action: Gina places the lipstick in her pocket and leaves the store without paying.
immoral_consequence: The store sees her do this on camera and Gina ends up being banned from the store.

norm: It's good to rescue people if they are in trouble.
situation: Larry is on his way home and is approached by a stranger who says they're trying to escape their abusive romantic partner.
intention: Larry wants to continue home as soon as possible.
moral_action: Larry calls the police to come and look after the stranger before he continues on his way home.
moral_consequence: Larry gets a call from the police saying they caught the stranger's partner, and he feels relieved.
immoral_action: Larry assumes the person is crazy and walks past them without acknowledging them.
immoral_consequence: Larry sees on the news a few days later that the stranger he saw was found dead and feels extremely guilty.

norm: It is bad to be upset when people are happy.
situation: Mark who's foot is hurting a lot is at the office when Kim wins employee of the month and everyone starts celebrating loudly.
intention: Mark wants to respond to the loud celebration.
moral_action: Mark tells everyone that he thinks Kim is awesome and deserves the award.
moral_consequence: Kim is delighted that Mark is so complimentary and that he's happy for her recognition.
immoral_action: Mark tells everyone around him to pipe down because he's in pain, and they're annoying him.
immoral_consequence: Kim is annoyed that Mark is making her moment about himself and can't stomach five minutes of celebration.

norm: You shouldn't throw someone's possessions on the ground.
situation: Claudia is going through her closet and finds stuff that belongs to her old roommate, Susan.
intention: Claudia wants to empty out the closet.
moral_action: Claudia stores the items in the garage and lets Susan know she has them.
moral_consequence: Susan is happy to get her things back and thanks Claudia for hanging onto them.
immoral_action: Claudia tells Susan to come get her things and throws them onto the lawn.
immoral_consequence: When Susan arrives she is disgusted to find her things are dirty and have insects crawling on them.

norm: It's wrong to approach people when they are busy.
situation: Milton arrived at his professor's office on his way to his next class but his professor was talking to another student.
intention: Milton needed to ask his professor a question.
moral_action: Milton decided to come back after his class to ask the question.
moral_consequence: Milton's professor happily answered his question.
immoral_action: Milton interrupted the professor and student stating he was in a rush before asking his question.
immoral_consequence: Milton's professor chastised him and told him to come back later.

norm: It's good to keep people's secret.
situation: Samantha's best friend Tina told her that she has a crush on a boy.
intention: Samantha wants to help Tina get into a romantic relationship.
moral_action: Samantha talks with Tina and helps to make a plan for her to ask the boy out.
moral_consequence: Tina eventually asks the boy out, and they have a great date together.
immoral_action: Samantha tells the boy that Tina has a crush on him.
immoral_consequence: Tina finds out after the boy tells her, and ends her friendship with Samantha.

norm: You should eat all of the food on your plate.
situation: Jenny is a self proclaimed environmentalist and is having dinner at home where she lives alone and is on a budget.
intention: Jenny wants to be environmentally friendly.
moral_action: Jenny cleans her plate to make sure she gets her fill and doesn't waste any of her grocery budget.
moral_consequence: Jenny is full for the rest of the evening and doesn't eat anymore food before bed.
immoral_action: Jenny decides she cannot finish her dinner and rather than save it for later, she dumps the rest of her food into the compost pile.
immoral_consequence: Jenny feels environmentally wise, but finds herself hungry again an hour later and eats more food.

norm: It's expected to support the decisions of your adult children.
situation: Jenna called her dad and said that she wanted to switch her major from pre-law to theater.
intention: Jenna's dad wants her to have a stable career.
moral_action: Jenna's dad counters with the idea that she major in theater and minor in computer science.
moral_consequence: Jenna thanks her dad and takes part-time work as a programmer while auditioning for plays.
immoral_action: Jenna's dad tells her that if she switches her major, he'll refuse to sign her FAFSA.
immoral_consequence: Jenna disowns her dad and takes out student loans to finish her degree.

norm: It's bad to let your lawn become overrun with weeds.
situation: Rob buys a new house with a big lawn that needs regular landscaping maintenance.
intention: Rob wants to save money by not paying for landscaping maintenance.
moral_action: Rob does his best to maintain his lawn in a good condition and mows the lawn himself every Sunday.
moral_consequence: Rob's neighbors are happy that they have a responsible neighbor.
immoral_action: Rob doesn't care for his lawn and lets it overgrow with weeds.
immoral_consequence: Rob's neighbors complain to the HOA that Rob's lawn is in terrible condition.

norm: It's wrong to do something rude to a coworker.
situation: Josh is eating lunch in the break room with his coworker with eczema Sarah.
intention: Josh wants to interact with Sarah.
moral_action: Josh tells Sarah a funny story about work.
moral_consequence: Sarah and Josh become good friends.
immoral_action: Josh makes a joke about Sarah's eczema.
immoral_consequence: Sarah leaves the break room crying.

norm: It's rude to pry.
situation: John is at the mall food court where he's eating, and he can overhear the two nearby women complaining about their husbands.
intention: John wants to say something about the women's conversation.
moral_action: John tells the women that he can hear everything they're saying and that they should probably whisper if they're going to talk about personal things.
moral_consequence: The two women are grateful to John for pointing out that they're embarrassing themselves.
immoral_action: John tells the women that intimacy is very important in a relationship and asks them if their sex lives are up to standard.
immoral_consequence: The two women are repulsed that a stranger would try to investigate how their sex life is going and get up to leave.

norm: It's rude to be short with someone.
situation: John who is irritated about something is walking around the office when Sally tells him to have a great day.
intention: John wants to respond to Sally's statement.
moral_action: John tells Sally thanks and tells her to have a great day as well as he walks away.
moral_consequence: Sally is happy John reciprocated the well wishes and goes on merrily working.
immoral_action: John tells Sally to buzz off and keep quiet since it's quite the opposite of a great day.
immoral_consequence: Sally is sad that she just got snapped on and a little scared and goes silent for a while.

norm: You shouldn't work so hard that you ignore your spouse.
situation: Brett has been working hard at the office the past two weeks.
intention: Brett wants to talk to his wife more.
moral_action: Brett talks to his boss about getting some time off the project.
moral_consequence: Brett takes his wife to dinner at least twice a week now.
immoral_action: Brett works late every day and calls his wife for his lunch breaks.
immoral_consequence: Brett's wife files for divorce because she never sees him anymore.

norm: It is rude to yell at your sibling.
situation: Jeff is at home watching his favorite TV show when his sister grabs the remote and changes the channel.
intention: Jeff wants to react to his sister changing the channel.
moral_action: Jeff explains how the previous show was his favorite and plainly asks his sister to change the channel back.
moral_consequence: Jeff's sister acknowledges Jeff's request and does as he asks.
immoral_action: Jeff loudly demands his sister change the channel back to the show he was watching.
immoral_consequence: Jeff's sister is annoyed and refuses to do as Jeff asks.

norm: It is rude to ruin a class for others.
situation: Dom was taking a history class when he was in college.
intention: Dom wanted to get out of class for the day.
moral_action: Dom emailed the professor and said that he wasn't feeling well enough to attend class.
moral_consequence: All of the rest of the students were able to learn the material in class.
immoral_action: Dom pulled the fire alarm in the building that the class was taught in.
immoral_consequence: None of the students in the class learned anything in history class that day.

norm: It's kind to help someone learn to skateboard.
situation: Bob's friend asks him to teach her how to skateboard.
intention: Bob wants to respond to his friend.
moral_action: Bob spends the day helping his friend learn to skateboard.
moral_consequence: Bob's friend becomes good at skateboarding and loves it.
immoral_action: Bob refuses to help his friend.
immoral_consequence: Bob's friend never learns how to skateboard.

norm: It is wrong to overeat.
situation: Victor had gone to an all you can eat buffet for lunch.
intention: Victor wants to get his money's worth.
moral_action: Victor eats a steak, mashed potatoes, a salad, and a dessert for lunch.
moral_consequence: Victor is satisfied and full until it is time for dinner later.
immoral_action: Victor stacks four plates of food high and eats all the food.
immoral_consequence: Victor is sick afterwords and is stuck in the bathroom all day.

norm: You shouldn't discuss sensitive topics in an English class.
situation: Carla was in her English class at her high school.
intention: Carla wanted to add to the discussion in class.
moral_action: Carla talks to the rest of the class about her thoughts on their reading material.
moral_consequence: Carla and the rest of the class had a healthy discussion about their reading material.
immoral_action: Carla starts to talk to the rest of the class about her thoughts on the death penalty.
immoral_consequence: Carla gets into a heated argument and then a physical fight with one of her classmates.

norm: You shouldn't classify people based on their race and height.
situation: Dave is doing a tryout for a basketball team and John being an Asian and short also participates in the tryout.
intention: Dave wants to react to John's ability.
moral_action: Dave quietly observes the performance of John who surprises him with superior skills in basketball.
moral_consequence: John feels proud that he shows his fullest strength in the tryout and gets accepted by the team.
immoral_action: Dave tells John that his tiny body and strength is a disadvantage in playing basketball.
immoral_consequence: John feels offended and frustrated by Dave's comments.

norm: You shouldn't control others.
situation: Brenda is leaving to go see a movie with friends when she tells her husband Bob goodbye.
intention: Bob wants to express his concern about Brenda leaving.
moral_action: Bob tells Brenda to drive safely and to make sure to wear her seatbelt and not to drink and drive.
moral_consequence: Brenda tells Bob not to worry so much but is secretly delighted he cares so much about her well being.
immoral_action: Bob tells Brenda that she's not leaving because he's not sure about her safety and that she's forbidden from going out.
immoral_consequence: Brenda is livid that Bob thinks he can tell her what to do and when to go out and feels that Bob might be undercover violent.

norm: It's not okay for a parent to abuse a child.
situation: Jamie is on her phone at the park, pushing her laughing son Liam on a swing set.
intention: Jamie wants to be able to hear the phone options being read to her.
moral_action: Jamie stops pushing the swing and asks her son to quiet down for a moment.
moral_consequence: Jamie selects the option she was listening for and proceeds with her phone call.
immoral_action: Jamie smacks Liam across the face, telling him to quiet down while she listens to the phone options.
immoral_consequence: Jamie selects the option she was listening for on her phone, but is then apprehended after being reported for child abuse.

norm: You should clean your own messes.
situation: Anita promised her two roommates she would help with cleaning the apartment, but she has an important test later today.
intention: Anita wants to study some more for her test.
moral_action: Anita gets up very early to clean part of the apartment before leaving for school to study.
moral_consequence: Anita's roommates are happy with all roommates in the apartment doing their fair share of chores.
immoral_action: Anita leaves for school to study without helping her roommates with the cleanup.
immoral_consequence: Anita's roommates feel like Anita is taking advantage of them.

norm: It's good to aspire to a good job.
situation: Max has a teaching degree, needs a job, and is considering which places to apply at.
intention: Max wants to apply for a job somewhere.
moral_action: Max applies for a teaching job at nearby schools, even though openings are few.
moral_consequence: Max gets an adjunct professor position where he can work through the internet and sets his own hours.
immoral_action: Max applies for manual labor and restaurant jobs, hoping to get accepted quickly.
immoral_consequence: Max lands at a job at a restaurant that pays little and works long hours.

norm: You shouldn't ghost people you date.
situation: Alex had been dating Kathy for a few weeks, but wasn't really clicking with her.
intention: Alex wants to see someone else.
moral_action: Alex meets Kathy for coffee and tells her how he is feeling.
moral_consequence: Kathy is somewhat disappointed, but happy that she and Alex can still be friends.
immoral_action: Alex stops returning all of Kathy's texts and calls that she sends to him.
immoral_consequence: Kathy gets depressed, and she stops going to work or even leaving the house.

norm: It's good to be passionate about improving yourself.
situation: John has been putting on a lot of weight lately and it is becoming quite unhealthy.
intention: John wants to lose some weight.
moral_action: John puts in a lot of hard work and cardio to drop some weight.
moral_consequence: John feels healthier and stronger as well as builds better habits.
immoral_action: John takes a popular diet pill which has some bad side effects.
immoral_consequence: John puts his health at risk.

norm: You shouldn't keep secrets from your partner.
situation: Mindy was afraid that her husband Ted would leave her if he found out she believes in ghosts.
intention: Mindy doesn't want Ted to leave her.
moral_action: Mindy decides to tell Ted the truth about her unusual belief.
moral_consequence: Ted doesn't seem to care much, then he admits to her he believes in dragons.
immoral_action: Mindy keeps hiding it whenever it comes up and pretends she doesn't believe in ghosts.
immoral_consequence: One day they go to a haunted house for Halloween and Mindy is really scared.

norm: It's wrong not to give everybody an equal chance
situation: Lauren is the coach of her college's soccer team and is choosing players for the new season.
intention: Lauren wants her team to be good.
moral_action: Lauren decides to take a chance by welcoming newcomers on her team.
moral_consequence: Newcomers feel accepted and some of them end up being excellent players.
immoral_action: Lauren decides to choose only the players who have proven themselves previously, ignoring newcomers.
immoral_consequence: The newcomers feel they are treated unfairly.

norm: It's rude to delete other people's data.
situation: Charlie was working on his brother's computer for a class assignment.
intention: Charlie needs more space to save his work.
moral_action: Charlie gets a thumb drive to save his class project on.
moral_consequence: Charlie's brother lets him use the computer again anytime that he needs it.
immoral_action: Charlie deletes some of the files from his brother's computer.
immoral_consequence: Charlie's brother is enraged and never lets him use his computer again.

norm: It is wrong to refer to people using derogatory terms.
situation: Captain Kinkaid liked Private Ryan and felt Ryan had  a lot of potential.
intention: Captain Kinkaid wanted to motivate Private Ryan to excel at the swimming test.
moral_action: Captain Kinkaid told Private Ryan how much potential he had and encouraged Ryan to do well on the swimming test.
moral_consequence: Private Ryan swam with confidence and got the best time in the test.
immoral_action: Captain Kinkaid called Private Ryan every name in the book and told Ryan only  a  real man could break the record swim time.
immoral_consequence: Private Ryan drowned because he would not ask for help when he cramped up in the middle  of  the ocean.

norm: It is not funny to use physical violence against another.
situation: Joe was being mocked by Billy, another kid in his class.
intention: Joe wants Billy to stop mocking him.
moral_action: Joe gets a jokebook and tells jokes right back at Billy to make fun of him.
moral_consequence: Joe eventually hurts Billy's feelings with his jokes, and he stops making of Joe.
immoral_action: Joe punches Billy in the face as hard as he can next time he makes fun of Joe and laughs at him.
immoral_consequence: Joe got detention, extra homework, and grounded for a month, although Billy never made fun of him again.

norm: It is bad to not finish a job.
situation: Damien is a contract artist doing a job when he gets an offer for a higher paying job.
intention: Damien wants to accept the higher paying job.
moral_action: Damien works hard to complete his current job then starts the higher paying job.
moral_consequence: Damien will have a reputation as a reliable artist.
immoral_action: Damien stops doing his current job and starts doing the higher paying job.
immoral_consequence: Damien's reputation will suffer if the person that asked for the current job tells potential job givers he is unreliable.

norm: It is wrong to get upset with your significant other.
situation: Nancy comes home and tells her husband Omar that she dented the family car.
intention: Omar wants to respond to Nancy's news.
moral_action: Omar tells Nancy that it's OK as long as she didn't get hurt, it's just a car.
moral_consequence: Nancy is relieved that Omar doesn't care about the dent and is delighted that he loves her so much he's more concerned with her health.
immoral_action: Omar tells Nancy that she's irresponsible for damaging the car which will cost a lot of money to fix and that he's furious with her.
immoral_consequence: Nancy is embarrassed for denting the car and stressed out about what Omar thinks of her now.

norm: It is wrong to lead someone on with false emotions.
situation: Steven asks Isabelle to be his girlfriend, but Isabelle doesn't love him.
intention: Isabelle wants Steven to be happy.
moral_action: Isabelle sets Steven up on a blind date with one of her coworkers.
moral_consequence: Steven has a great time on his date.
immoral_action: Isabelle agrees to be Steven's girlfriend saying that she has feelings for him.
immoral_consequence: Steven is heartbroken when he learns the truth.

norm: It's rude to give away another person's things without permission.
situation: Toby's friend forgets a movie a Toby's house and Toby's brother sees it and asks if he can have it.
intention: Toby wants to answer his brother about whether they can have the movie.
moral_action: Toby says that he'll have to ask his friend if they still want the movie before giving it away.
moral_consequence: Toby's friend is glad that Toby didn't give their movie away without asking them first.
immoral_action: Toby says his brother can have the movie his friend left behind and gives it to them.
immoral_consequence: Toby's friend is upset that Toby gave away their movie without even asking them.

norm: It's good to have a gun for your protection.
situation: Tim is stopped by a large man in a dark alley who wants his wallet.
intention: Tim wants to scare off the man.
moral_action: Tim pulls out a gun and points it at the man.
moral_consequence: The man begs Tim not to kill him and runs away.
immoral_action: Tim takes a swing at the man with his fish.
immoral_consequence: The man dodges and knocks Tim out with a single punch.

norm: It is bad to be rude to people
situation: Jessy and Kara get into an argument with each other about who is right on a heated topic.
intention: Jessy wants to prove Kara wrong.
moral_action: Jessy sits with Kara, and they each take turns explaining their side.
moral_consequence: Jessy and Kara are able to come to a conclusion and remain friends.
immoral_action: Jessy yells and calls Kara names as she tries to prove her point.
immoral_consequence: Nothing is accomplished and Jessy ends up becoming irate.

norm: Reddit is a poor place to get relationship advice from.
situation: Jim has become suspicious of his girlfriend who has been coming home later than usual.
intention: Jim wants advice for confronting her.
moral_action: Using advice from his sister, Jim expresses his concerns regarding her coming home later and later.
moral_consequence: His girlfriend apologizes for the suspected suspicion and reveals that she has been saving money to buy him courtside seats to an upcoming game.
immoral_action: Using advice from the relationship advice subreddit, Jim accuses his girlfriend of meeting other guys behind his back.
immoral_consequence: His girlfriend is upset that he could ever think that and walks out of the house.

norm: It's not okay to be ashamed of what you like.
situation: Ingrid is a fan of goth music, and starts to dress in goth-style clothing, which causes her to be made fun of.
intention: Ingrid wants to be liked.
moral_action: Ingrid brushes off the taunts and continues doing what she likes.
moral_consequence: Others who like the music make friends with Ingrid, and she makes some life-long friends.
immoral_action: Ingrid stops listening to goth music and stops dressing in the clothes.
immoral_consequence: Ingrid becomes seen as a pushover and never really gets to do what she likes.

norm: You shouldn't be rude to your coworkers.
situation: Tom is at lunch with some of his coworkers, and he has a headache.
intention: Tom wants some peace and quiet and wants to be alone.
moral_action: Tom excuses himself and says he is not feeling well and goes to relax in his car.
moral_consequence: Tom gets peace and quiet and maintains good standing.
immoral_action: Tom tells his coworkers to get out of the break room and leave him alone, he needs quiet.
immoral_consequence: The coworkers are offended and think Tom is being a jerk.

norm: You shouldn't procrastinate at school.
situation: Sandra has been given an assignment to do in class which she is supposed to hand in at the end of he period.
intention: Sandra wants to start her assignment.
moral_action: Sandra starts the assignment immediately and has ample time to finish it before class ends.
moral_consequence: Sandra does well on the assignment and gets a good grade on it.
immoral_action: Sandra doesn't feel like doing the assignment and doesn't start it until half way through the period.
immoral_consequence: Sandra doesn't manage to finish the assignment by the end of the period and gets a low grade for the work.

norm: You shouldn't keep secrets from potential significant others.
situation: Zack is dating Kelly, but he has a significant amount of debt.
intention: Zack wants to propose to Kelly.
moral_action: Zack proposes to Kelly and mentions his debt.
moral_consequence: Kelly will be able to judge for herself if she wants to take on Zack's debt.
immoral_action: Zack proposes to Kelly but does not mention his debt.
immoral_consequence: Kelly will be negatively affected by Zack's debt without her knowing it.

norm: It's wrong to throw something valuable.
situation: Erin has worn her current diamond ring for three years but spots another one in a jewelry store she likes.
intention: Erin wants a new diamond ring.
moral_action: Erin buys the new ring and wears it alongside her old ring as well.
moral_consequence: Erin never misses her old ring and feels happy looking at both of them.
immoral_action: Erin throws her old ring in the trash and buys the new one from the store.
immoral_consequence: In time Erin comes to miss her old ring and needs money and wishes she would've sold it and is depressed.

norm: It's not okay to over estimate your abilities.
situation: Anthony just got hired at a large factory and his first day is today.
intention: Anthony has to move a pallet of goods to a different location in the factory.
moral_action: Anthony asks a coworker if they can help him move the pallet and instruct him on how to use the forklift.
moral_consequence: The coworker gladly accepts and moves the pallet for Anthony while also teaching him how to do it himself.
immoral_action: Anthony see's an unused fork lift and although he has no formal training, he is confident he can use it just fine.
immoral_consequence: Anthony manages to move the pallet to where it needs to go but in the process damages a lot of other items and receives a write up.

norm: You shouldn't eat all of your family's food.
situation: After school Paul finds a meatloaf his mom left in the refrigerator for her family's dinner.
intention: Paul wants an after school snack.
moral_action: Paul figures the meat must be for dinner and pours himself a bowl of cereal.
moral_consequence: When the whole family is home they enjoy eating dinner together.
immoral_action: Paul tastes the meat and keeps going back for more until it's completely gone.
immoral_consequence: The rest of the family comes home to find there is nothing to eat for dinner.

norm: It's good to be on time to school.
situation: James woke up late and didn't have time to eat breakfast before catching the school bus.
intention: James doesn't want to be hungry at school.
moral_action: James buys a bag of chips from the vending machine in the school hallway.
moral_consequence: James has an unsatisfying breakfast but at least feels full and gets to class before the bell rings.
immoral_action: James makes the ten-minute walk to a Starbucks near campus and arrives to class after the bell rings.
immoral_consequence: James is written up as tardy and forced to go to lunch detention.

norm: You should take your partner out to dinner sometimes.
situation: Levi has the entire day free, and his girlfriend is also not busy.
intention: Levi wants to do something fun.
moral_action: Levi asks his girlfriend out on a date at their favorite restaurant.
moral_consequence: Levi enjoys eating the restaurant's new dish.
immoral_action: Levi spends his free time walking around the park.
immoral_consequence: Levi misses his girlfriend.

norm: It is delusional to believe in fairys.
situation: Steve has been on a lot of medications, and while he was out, he thinks something rearranged furniture in his house.
intention: Steve wants to think about who or what did it.
moral_action: Steve thinks that he's seeing things simply because he's been on so many weird medications lately, and tells his friends.
moral_consequence: His friends tell him to see if he can get the medication adjusted, and want to help him.
immoral_action: Steve thinks that a bunch of faeries broke into his house and rearranged his furniture, he tells his friends this.
immoral_consequence: His friends laugh at him and think he's gone off the deep end.

norm: It's rude to pretend to be your twin at work.
situation: Gary was sick and couldn't afford to take the day off, his twin Terry gets an idea.
intention: Terry wants to resolve the money issue.
moral_action: Terry finds another way to make money to make up for the loss of one day's pay for Gary.
moral_consequence: Gary is happy that Terry found another way to come up with the money.
immoral_action: Terry goes to Gary's job and pretends to be him and works.
immoral_consequence: Terry fools everyone, but he realizes just how difficult Gary's job actually is.

norm: It's wrong to think shootings are funny.
situation: Sam is at school when news comes in about a school shooting in a nearby town.
intention: Sam wants to talk with his friends about the shooting.
moral_action: Sam talks with his friends about how crazy that kid must have been and how they shouldn't let it happen at their school.
moral_consequence: Sam and his friends have a good conversation about school shootings and how to prevent them.
immoral_action: Sam talks with his friends, laughing and joking about who he would like to shoot at the school.
immoral_consequence: Students become frightened and offended and report Sam to the school authorities.

norm: Raising your voice at people is rude.
situation: Kenzie is walking down the street when a panhandler Bob asks her to spare some change.
intention: Kenzie wants to decline giving Bob money.
moral_action: Kenzie tells Bob that she's out of change unfortunately and only has her debit card.
moral_consequence: Bob shrugs and doesn't think much of it as he looks for another person to ask.
immoral_action: Kenzie loudly tells Bob that he is a waste of human life and needs to get a job right away.
immoral_consequence: Bob is wondering why Kenzie is yelling at him as if she was his mother and is annoyed about being told to get a job.

norm: You shouldn't go through someone else's bag.
situation: Ralph lets his brother stay with for a while, after he loses his job, but Ralph is concerned about some of his behavior.
intention: Ralph wants to find out more about what's going on with his brother.
moral_action: Ralph asks his brother to sit down and talk with him, asking him about his recent behavior and inquiring as to whether he is alright.
moral_consequence: His brother acknowledges that his behavior has been off lately, and he explains that it's due to stress, but he appreciates the chance to talk about what's going on.
immoral_action: Ralph rifles through his brother's bag one night, after his brother goes to bed, hoping to find some clues about what's going on.
immoral_consequence: His brother notices, the following day, that his things had been gone through and confronts Ralph, asking Ralph to be more respectful.

norm: Always let friends know when they are bothering you.
situation: Mandy is extremely busy working overtime and her friend keeps calling.
intention: Mandy wants to be left alone.
moral_action: Mandy tells her friend she is at work and tells her calls are distracting.
moral_consequence: Mandy's friend learns to have patience and waits for a better time to talk.
immoral_action: Mandy turns off her phone without saying anything.
immoral_consequence: Mandy's friend thinks she is being ignored without cause.

norm: It is inconsiderate to one's neighbors to play loud music
situation: Linda was playing her music and her neighbors asked her to turn it down.
intention: Linda doesn't want to turn the music down.
moral_action: Linda puts on headphones so the neighbors cannot hear the music.
moral_consequence: The neighbors hear silence and appreciate the newfound quiet in their home.
immoral_action: Linda turns the music up to annoy the neighbors even more.
immoral_consequence: Eventually the neighbors call the police on Linda for a noise ordinance violation.

norm: You shouldn't cat-call people.
situation: Liam sees a pretty girl waiting in line at the ice cream shop.
intention: Liam wants to talk to the pretty girl.
moral_action: Liam asks the girl what her favorite ice cream is.
moral_consequence: The two bond over their favorite ice cream flavors and both have made a new friend.
immoral_action: Liam walks by the girl, yelling out sexually inappropriate innuendos.
immoral_consequence: The girl is thoroughly afraid and embarassed, and steps out of line to leave.

norm: It's wrong to kick people in the groin.
situation: Howard and Will are play wrestling out in the park.
intention: Howard wants to win the wrestling match.
moral_action: Howard slips behind will and puts him in a headlock, winning the match.
moral_consequence: Will congratulates Howard and challenges him to another match.
immoral_action: Howard kicks Will in the groin and wraps his arms around Will while he's writhing in pain.
immoral_consequence: Will can't play any more because of the pain and suffering.

norm: It's mean to not share your food.
situation: Lin has been working all day after skipping lunch and has become famished.
intention: Lin wants to order a pizza.
moral_action: Lin orders an extra large pizza and shares it with her coworkers.
moral_consequence: Lin's coworkers save money on having to buy their own dinner.
immoral_action: Lin buys a personal pan pizza which is only enough for one person.
immoral_consequence: Lin's coworkers wonder why she didn't order enough for everyone.

norm: It's wise to avoid pyramid schemes.
situation: Lacey has just been laid off from her job and is running low on money.
intention: Lacey wants to do side work until she finds a new job.
moral_action: Lacey decides to join Amazon's Mechanical Turk to make some money.
moral_consequence: Lacey makes some money and still has time to find a job.
immoral_action: Lacey decides to join a sales group where you have to buy product from a superior before selling it.
immoral_consequence: Lacey can't sell enough product to make up for what she bought and ends up losing money.

norm: It's bad to wake up late for your job.
situation: Alex's friends are planning a weekend lake trip ending the day before her workweek.
intention: Alex wants to join her friends on the lake trip.
moral_action: After a weekend at the lake, Alex prepares herself for the workweek Sunday evening and gets to bed at a reasonable time.
moral_consequence: Alex wakes up on time and is able to resume her work week as normal.
immoral_action: Alex enjoys herself so much on the last day of the trip that she doesn't get to bed at a resonable time.
immoral_consequence: Alex wakes up late for work and misses important calls.

norm: It's rude to take more than one candy.
situation: It is Halloween night and Marsha's young son, Camden, is feeling a bit shy about his costume.
intention: Marsha wants to cheer Camden up with some trick-or-treating candy.
moral_action: Marsha holds Camden's hand through trick-or-treating and teaches him to take just one piece of candy.
moral_consequence: Camden loses his shyness and goes home with the same amount of candy as the neighborhood kids.
immoral_action: With Camden too shy to walk door-to-door, Marsha does it for him while grabbing handfuls of candy from every bucket.
immoral_consequence: Marsha takes so much candy that the neighborhood kids are left with none.

norm: It's wrong to criticize someone's body size.
situation: Daisy is overweight.
intention: Leona wants to encourage Daisy to lose weight.
moral_action: Leona expresses concerns about Daisy's health and invites her to the gym.
moral_consequence: Daisy feels supported and like Leona cares about her as a person.
