situation: A very hungry Pedro is camping deep in the wilderness with Derek.
intention: Pedro wants to have a meal.
moral_action: Pedro and Derek make some soup with the vegetables they brought.
moral_consequence: Pedro and Derek have a nice meal before bed.
immoral_action: Pedro kills Derek and consumes Derek's roasted corpse for dinner.
immoral_consequence: Derek dies and Pedro finally answers his long timed desire to find out what people taste like.

norm: It's bad to try to snoop about families' secrets.
situation: Sam is invited to a family reunion and hasn't seen most of the guests in years.
intention: Sam wants to catch up and see how everyone is doing.
moral_action: Sam goes around speaking with everyone and asks what they've been up to.
moral_consequence: The guests enjoy their time with Sam and make sure to ask her to return next year.
immoral_action: Sam is overly nosey during the reunion and secretly listens in on other conversations.
immoral_consequence: Most of the guests catch on and avoid Sam the whole time.

norm: You shouldn't refuse to apologize to your partner.
situation: Chris has been in an argument all day with his wife and just realized he was actually in the wrong the whole time.
intention: Chris wants to stop the argument.
moral_action: Chris tells his wife about his realization and offers to make amends for his error in the argument.
moral_consequence: Chris's wife accepts his apology and the couple agree to talk things out better in the future.
immoral_action: Chris tells his wife that he is done arguing and wants to just drop it, but never mentions that he found out he was wrong.
immoral_consequence: Chris and his wife never settle the issue and it is bad for their relationship.

norm: It's nice to be friendly to customers.
situation: Mike is a cashier at a grocery store and Bill just finished paying for his groceries.
intention: Mike wants to end the transaction with Bill.
moral_action: Mike tells Bill thanks for shopping with us, and he hopes he sees him again soon and then hands him the receipt.
moral_consequence: Bill feels like a valued customer and that Mike really cares whether he shops there or not and is happy to be treated that way.
immoral_action: Mike tells Bill that the transaction is complete, gives him a receipt and tells him to move along quickly for the next customer.
immoral_consequence: Bill is annoyed that he's being rushed through and that Mike seems robotic in trying to pump through customers.

norm: It's good to do what your boss tells you.
situation: Ryan is working at his job.
intention: Ryan wants to get a raise from his employer.
moral_action: Ryan goes by the standard procedures given to him by his boss and beats his sales goal.
moral_consequence: Ryan is rewarded with a raise for doing a good job.
immoral_action: Ryan skirts company policy to try to get more customers and reach his sales goal.
immoral_consequence: Ryan is let go for not following the rules that his employer laid out.

norm: it's good to keep your dog on your own property.
situation: James bought a border collie puppy that has a massive amount of energy.
intention: James wants his dog to get enough exercise.
moral_action: James takes his dog on long walks every day and throws a ball for her to chase in his backyard.
moral_consequence: James' dog is always tired enough to sleep at night and behave in the house.
immoral_action: James lets his dog wander all over the neighborhood and doesn't even fence his yard.
immoral_consequence: James' dog is hit by a car one day and James spends hours crying about it.

norm: It's good to have your priorities in order.
situation: James woke up to find his house burning and only time enough to grab one thing.
intention: James wants to save his most valued possession.
moral_action: James grabs a folder with all his most critical documents (social security card, mortgage agreement, etc.).
moral_consequence: The firefighters tell James they're glad he was able to keep his documentation with him.
immoral_action: James snatches his stash of porn magazines from underneath his bed.
immoral_consequence: The firefighters are amused and dismayed by what James choose to save.

norm: It's wrong to tell someone else's secrets without their permission.
situation: Jack's friend has had a crush on the same coworker for several years but has a girlfriend.
intention: Jack wants to help his friend figure out who he belongs with.
moral_action: Jack sets up an appointment with a therapist so his friend has a space to work through his attraction.
moral_consequence: Jack's friend is grateful to talk over his girl troubles.
immoral_action: Jack tells the coworker about his friend's attraction to her.
immoral_consequence: Jack's friend is furious as his girlfriend has now dumped him.

norm: It's rude to wake people up.
situation: Emily lives with family and arrives home quite late but is very excited after receiving some good news.
intention: Emily wants to listen to her favorite song to keep the good vibe going.
moral_action: Emily listens to her music using a pair of headphones.
moral_consequence: Emily enjoys her music and her parents get a good night's rest.
immoral_action: Emily cranks up the stereo and puts on her favorite song.
immoral_consequence: Emily wakes up her parent's, and she feels bad about it.

norm: It is good to have principles.
situation: Heather and Tim are studying for a hard exam, and Tim suggests that they cheat.
intention: Heather wants to get the exam questions correct.
moral_action: Heather says she wants to pass on her own merits and studies harder.
moral_consequence: Heather gets a passing grade on her test and feels like she accomplished something.
immoral_action: Heather goes along with Tim’s suggestion, and they copy each other's work.
immoral_consequence: The teacher discovers Heather and Tim's cheating as she's grading and fails them both.

norm: It is good to ignore people who are ignorant.
situation: Ted is walking down the street when a group of boys start to call him names.
intention: Ted wants to stop hearing the taunting.
moral_action: Ted puts on his headphones and turns the music on loud.
moral_consequence: Ted walks the rest of the way to his house without hearing the boys.
immoral_action: Ted rushes up to the boys and starts to beat them all up.
immoral_consequence: The police are called to the brawl and Ted is taken to the police station.

norm: It's bad to be violent toward others.
situation: Ken was being bothered by his fiance, and she wouldn't stop talking no matter what.
intention: Ken wants to stop being bothered by his fiance.
moral_action: Ken walks outside of the home and decides to smoke a cigarette.
moral_consequence: Ken cannot be bothered by his fiance anymore and is more calm.
immoral_action: Ken grabs his fiance by her hair and throws her to the ground.
immoral_consequence: Ken's fiance starts becoming scared of Ken and thinks about leaving him.

norm: You shouldn't take food from others without asking.
situation: John works at an office and is really hungry, and sees a candy bar sitting on the empty desk of a nearby coworker.
intention: John wants to eat.
moral_action: John waits until the coworker comes back and offers to give him a dollar for it.
moral_consequence: The coworker gives it to John for free, just asking that John return the favor every once in a while.
immoral_action: John grabs the candy bar from the empty desk and eats it.
immoral_consequence: The coworker notices the empty candy wrapper in John's hand when he gets back and reports him to management.

norm: It's wrong to refuse to date someone of another race.
situation: Jade and her coworker David have been flirting and getting along well, but she is unsure of whether or not she wants to date someone outside of her race.
intention: Jade wants to find a boyfriend.
moral_action: Despite their racial differences, Jade decides to take a chance on David.
moral_consequence: Jade realizes that her hesitations were silly, and ends up learning a lot about David's culture.
immoral_action: Jade passes David over for someone of her race.
immoral_consequence: Jade realizes that she doesn't really like the other guy, and she can't stop thinking about David.

norm: It is bad to sell people defective goods
situation: Hannah buys a vacuum from the store and it breaks immediately.
intention: Hannah wants to get the money she spent on the vacuum back.
moral_action: Hannah goes to the store where she bought the vacuum and asks for a refund.
moral_consequence: Hannah gets a refund from the store after spending time and energy arguing with the manager.
immoral_action: Hannah sells the vacuum on Craigslist, saying it works perfectly.
immoral_consequence: Hannah gets her money back and feels guilty for cheating a stranger.

norm: Its wrong to report someone for something they didn't do.
situation: George witnesses a robbery but doesn't see the perpetrator's face and can't identify him.
intention: George wants to give a statement to the police about the crime.
moral_action: George tells the police the height and weight of the man he saw committing the robbery.
moral_consequence: The police use George's description plus other evidence to identify and arrest the robber.
immoral_action: George tells the police that a man who lives in his building committed the robbery.
immoral_consequence: The police arrest the man who lives in George's building even though he is innocent.

norm: It's wrong to make racist jokes.
situation: Chris, who dislikes black people, is with some friends in the parking lot when he sees a black person.
intention: Chris wants to amuse his friends.
moral_action: Chris tells a joke that he heard from a comedy show that he watched earlier that week.
moral_consequence: Chris' friends laugh and no one is offended.
immoral_action: "Chris decides to make fun of the black person and makes jokes about ""darkies in the melon patch"" to his friends."
immoral_consequence: The black man hears, walks over to Chris, and starts a fight with him.

norm: You shouldn't be jealous of your child's partner.
situation: Claire has a son that has a girlfriend.
intention: Claire wants to talk to her son and his girlfriend about their relationship.
moral_action: Claire tells the girlfriend that she supports her son well.
moral_consequence: The girlfriend is happy that Claire thinks well of her.
immoral_action: Claire tells the girlfriend that she's taking up all of her son's time that he could be spending with his mother.
immoral_consequence: The girlfriend will feel awkward and not want to date the son anymore.

norm: "It's rude to offer unsolicited opinions or ""grievances"" to others."
situation: Mike is driving Jessie to her doctor's appointment through heavy traffic.
intention: Jessie wants to help Mike.
moral_action: Jessie puts on Mike's favorite song.
moral_consequence: Mike's mood improves which allows Mike and Jessie to have a good time despite the traffic jam.
immoral_action: Jessie acts like a backseat driver bombarding Mike with advice.
immoral_consequence: Mike gets more stressed, and he almost runs into someone.

norm: It's wrong to make fun of black people.
situation: Mark is on a cruise with his wife, and they walked by a large black family dancing.
intention: Mark wants to say something about the family.
moral_action: Mark tells his wife that he wishes that they were as lively as the black family.
moral_consequence: Mark's wife is glad that Mark said something nice and agrees with Mark.
immoral_action: Mark tells his wife that he's happy that the black people are actually wearing shoes.
immoral_consequence: Mark's wife feels embarrassed that Mark would say something so racist.

norm: It's hurtful to exclude friends from big life events.
situation: Bree is getting married this fall and is currently making her guest list for the wedding.
intention: Bree wants the wedding to be afforable.
moral_action: Bree decides to save money by finding a cheaper wedding venue that will allow her to invite all of her friends.
moral_consequence: Bree's friends love the wedding and don't care that the venue was cheap because they got to share an important moment with Bree.
immoral_action: Bree decides to save money by inviting fewer people and chooses not to invite several of her friends to the wedding.
immoral_consequence: Bree's friends who aren't invited are sad and start not inviting Bree to events they host.

norm: It's good to give your stepchildren advice.
situation: Dave has a stepson, who needs to choose which college to go to.
intention: Dave wants to comment on the stepson's choice.
moral_action: Dave discusses with his stepson the different choices and asks him to also consider his interest of study.
moral_consequence: His stepson feels supported and thanks Dave for his excellent advice.
immoral_action: Dave tells his stepson to choose a college with the lowest college fee.
immoral_consequence: His stepson feels frustrated and helpless for not being able to choose his favorite college.

norm: It's rude to tell someone they aren't normal.
situation: James is at a party when he's introduced to Frank who has a septum piercing through his nose.
intention: James wants to react to the septum piercing on Frank.
moral_action: James tells Frank that his piercing is unique and interesting, and he likes it.
moral_consequence: Frank feels happy that a stranger likes his body art and is delighted that James called it unique.
immoral_action: James tells Frank that he's a weirdo and that having a septum piercing makes him look tribal and weird.
immoral_consequence: Frank is insulted and feels shy and insecure about his piercing now.

norm: You should not waste other people's time.
situation: Harmony is browsing the displays at a busy jewelry store without planning to buy anything, when a sales clerk approaches her and asks her if she needs help.
intention: Harmony wants to respond to the sales clerk.
moral_action: Harmony explains that she's currently just browsing and doesn't require assistance.
moral_consequence: The sales clerk appreciates how straightforward Harmony was and is able to spend his time efficiently by helping other customers who are trying to buy jewelry.
immoral_action: Harmony asks the sales clerk a bunch of questions about the jewelry and requests to try some of it on even though there's no chance of her purchasing it.
immoral_consequence: The sales clerk eventually figures out that she's just there to browse and decides to move on to help some other customers.

norm: You shouldn't call a pregnant woman fat.
situation: Christine meets her friend Debbie, who is currently pregnant, for coffee.
intention: Christine wants to comment on Debbie's appearance.
moral_action: Christine tells Debbie that she's glowing and looks very good.
moral_consequence: Debbie feels good about herself and her appearance and feels thankful to Christine for not mentioning her weight.
immoral_action: Christine tells Debbie that she should be careful about what she's eating, because she's gained quite a lot of weight.
immoral_consequence: Debbie feels horrible about her appearance and her self confidence is completely shattered.

norm: You shouldn't hurt your dog.
situation: Marv walks into his bedroom and realizes that his dog peed on his bed.
intention: Marv wants his dog to learn not to pee on the bed.
moral_action: Marv starts bringing the dog out for walks more often.
moral_consequence: Marv's dog starts to use the restroom outside rather than in the house.
immoral_action: Marv takes off his belt and beats his dog with it.
immoral_consequence: Marv's dog runs away and Marv never sees it again.

norm: It's rude to sneeze or cough on others.
situation: James was feeling sick, but was down to only rice and canned beans to eat.
intention: James wants a decent meal.
moral_action: James uses Uber Eats to order delivery from his favorite Thai restaurant.
moral_consequence: James savors his meal from the safe isolation of his own home.
immoral_action: James goes to his local grocery store without a mask and coughs and sneezes on everyone.
immoral_consequence: James is asked to leave the store by employees concerned about him infecting other people.

norm: It is wrong to drive under the influence.
situation: Chris is at a friend's house and has drank a lot, but now needs to drive home to sleep before work tomorrow.
intention: Chris wants to go home.
moral_action: Chris asks a sober friend who lives near him to drive his car home, so he doesn't have to get in trouble.
moral_consequence: The friend drives Chris home, keeping everyone else on the road safe and unharmed.
immoral_action: Chris gets into his car and starts driving home, weaving all over the road and nearly colliding with several people.
immoral_consequence: The people near Chris are frightened by his terrible drunken driving and call the police on him.

norm: It's wrong to abuse a martial partner.
situation: Sean was in an MMA fight, and he is a lot better than his opponent.
intention: Sean wants to win his match.
moral_action: Sean take it easy on his opponent and works to beat him by getting a choke in.
moral_consequence: Sean's opponent is not permanently damaged and gets to live their life pain free.
immoral_action: Sean wants to teach his opponent a lesson and doesn't hold back.
immoral_consequence: Sean's opponent could end up with brain damage and will feel pain for a long time.

norm: It is rude to make disparaging remarks about someone's plans.
situation: Chris is talking to his friend Pete who is going on a trip to help people in Haiti.
intention: Chris wants to respond to Pete's trip.
moral_action: Chris tells Pete that Pete will be able to do a lot of good.
moral_consequence: Pete will be more motivated to help people.
immoral_action: Chris tells Pete that it is a waste of time to go to Haiti.
immoral_consequence: Pete will think that Chris is lacking in compassion.

norm: You shouldn't let kids watch the Exorcism.
situation: Ed spends Friday evening with his kids at home, and they're planning on watching a movie.
intention: Ed wants to watch a movie he enjoyed when he was younger.
moral_action: "Ed watches ""Back To The Future"" with his kids."
moral_consequence: Ed's kids have a great time.
immoral_action: "Ed watches ""The Exorcist"" with his kids."
immoral_consequence: Ed's kids are terrified.

norm: It is nice to encourage others to keep trying.
situation: Sam is a guidance counselor who is meeting with a student about pursuing art as a career after losing a local art competition.
intention: Sam wants to make sure the student realistically understands their goal in life.
moral_action: Sam cautions the student towards the perils of pursuing art but tells them to not give up on their passion after one setback.
moral_consequence: The student is invigorated and works harder towards being an artist.
immoral_action: Sam tells the student that art is financially impractical, and they should switch focus after the loss.
immoral_consequence: The student feels unsupported and never returns to Sam for advice.

norm: You shouldn't rob people.
situation: John has been laid off from his job.
intention: John wants to find a new source of money.
moral_action: John goes into a local store and fills out a job application.
moral_consequence: The owner of the store hires John and is relieved to solve his staffing issue.
immoral_action: John goes into a local store and robs the clerk at gunpoint.
immoral_consequence: The clerk suffers emotional distress and spends the rest of the day talking to the police.

norm: It is wrong to hurt someone's feelings on purpose.
situation: Carl is eating dinner with his family at home and his son Jake has spilled his drink.
intention: Carl wants to say something about the drink spilling.
moral_action: Carl says that it's no big deal and gets a towel for Jake to clean up the spill.
moral_consequence: Jake learns what mistakes are important and what ones aren't and is able to take calculated risks to improve his life.
immoral_action: Carl tells Jake he is so clumsy and that he's always been a disappointment.
immoral_consequence: Jake becomes so afraid of making a mistake around Carl that he never tries anything new and leads a boring life.

norm: It's good to show respect for soldiers.
situation: Jane hears there's a military parade around her house, but the parade requires absolute silence from the audience.
intention: Jane wants to participate in the military parade up close.
moral_action: Jane goes to the parade and is silent during it.
moral_consequence: Jane is able to watch the full parade, walk at their speed, and enjoys every second of it.
immoral_action: Jane goes to the military parade and shouts in glee during it.
immoral_consequence: Jane is escorted by security away from the parade for making noise, and Jane feels humiliated.

norm: It's rude to tip someone an extremely low amount.
situation: Kenny just finished some drinks at the bar, and was served by a top-notch bartender.
intention: Kenny wants to leave a gratuity.
moral_action: Kenny pays for his tab and leaves the bartender a 20 dollar bill to keep.
moral_consequence: The bartender is grateful for the generous amount and looks forward to the next time Kenny comes in.
immoral_action: Kenny digs into his pocket and takes out 25 cents for the bartender to keep.
immoral_consequence: The bartender is offended by the tiny amount and promises himself next time not to provide as good of service.

norm: It's immoral to support racism.
situation: Eric is applying for colleges.
intention: Eric wants to win a competitive scholarship.
moral_action: Eric works hard on his scholarship application essay.
moral_consequence: Eric becomes a finalist for the scholarship.
immoral_action: Eric begins a campaign against affirmative action by the scholarship committee and disparages minorities and their abilities.
immoral_consequence: Eric is out of contention for the scholarship and is blacklisted by many colleges.

norm: It's fun to watch a sports game at the bar.
situation: Baxter has just clocked out of work for the evening.
intention: Baxter wants to have fun.
moral_action: Baxter visits a sports bar and eats wings while observing a football game.
moral_consequence: Baxter befriends other sports fans hanging out at the bar.
immoral_action: Baxter goes to home and plays sports video games online.
immoral_consequence: Baxter goes to bed wishing he would have done something more exciting.

norm: It is romantic to buy your significant other a ring.
situation: Dave is in his room thinking of ways to propose to his girlfriend Gwen.
intention: Dave wants  to pick out an item to offer Gwen as part of the proposal.
moral_action: Dave decides that he will offer Gwen a nice diamond ring when he asks her to marry him.
moral_consequence: Gwen feels delighted that Dave proposed in such a beautiful and old fashioned way.
immoral_action: Dave decides that he will offer Gwen a nice watch when he asks her to marry him.
immoral_consequence: Gwen feels awkward about the watch and thinks the entire proposal is bizarre.

norm: You shouldn't upset your family by taking your own life.
situation: Jeff is experiencing depression.
intention: Jeff wants to not be sad.
moral_action: Jeff talks to his family about his depression, and they take him to a psychiatrist.
moral_consequence: The psychiatrist prescribes some medicine and talks to Jeff which eases Jeff's depression and makes his family happy for him.
immoral_action: Jeff overdoses on pills because he can't take the pain anymore.
immoral_consequence: Jeff's family is devastated and never recover from the loss.

norm: It's disgusting when adults take advantage of children.
situation: Peter is a toy collector and has noticed that his neighbor's 8-year old son Ben has a rare toy.
intention: Peter wants to buy the toy from Ben.
moral_action: Peter offers to buy the toy from Ben for its full value.
moral_consequence: Peter acquires the toy he wants and doesn't compromise his integrity.
immoral_action: Peter offers to trade a common toy from his collection to Ben for Ben's rare toy.
immoral_consequence: Ben's parents find out about the trade and are very angry at Peter.

norm: It is bad to stay with someone who is cheating.
situation: After having forgiven his infidelity once before Paula has just discovered that her husband is cheating again.
intention: Paula wants to respond to her current situation.
moral_action: Paula gives her husband an ultimatum, either he stays faithful or their marriage ends.
moral_consequence: Paula is empowered and her sense of self worth grows.
immoral_action: Scared of losing her husband Paula decides to ignore the infidelity and stay with her husband.
immoral_consequence: Paula's sense of shame grows as her husband becomes more brazen.

norm: It's good to plan for a trip.
situation: Steve has a weekend off from work.
intention: Steve wants to go to Texas.
moral_action: Steve packs his bags the night before and goes through a checklist.
moral_consequence: Steve forgets nothing and enjoys his trip.
immoral_action: Steve jumps in his car and drives off without packing or planning.
immoral_consequence: Steve forgets a bunch of stuff and has a bad trip.

norm: It's expected that you'll spend time with your girlfriend.
situation: Stan and Pam have been together for a year and their anniversary is tonight, but Stan has a chance to meet with a high end client.
intention: Stan wants to meet with the client.
moral_action: Stan explains how important the meeting is to Pam, and they reschedule their dinner for the following night.
moral_consequence: Stan closes a big deal with the client and is still able to celebrate his anniversary.
immoral_action: Stan gets out of the anniversary dinner by pretending that he's got the flu, and is able to meet with the client.
immoral_consequence: Stan will disappoint Pam and she breaks up with him.

norm: You shouldn't steal money from your partner.
situation: David's wife Elena is shopping online when she comes across a pair of sunglasses she likes, but can't afford.
intention: Elena wants to make a purchase.
moral_action: Elena asks David if he would put the sunglasses on his credit card and sje will pay him back from her next paycheck.
moral_consequence: David agrees and tells Elena not to worry about paying him back because it makes him feel good doing something kind.
immoral_action: Elena realizing David isn't in the room, takes his credit card from his wallet and buys the sunglasses.
immoral_consequence: David isn't happy with Elena when he see's the charges on his statement.

norm: You can't expect your partner to do things for you.
situation: Mike's and Molly's son, Brandon, needs to be picked up from soccer practice while Mike watches TV.
intention: Mike wants to watch a football game that just started.
moral_action: Mike tapes the football game and goes to pick up Brandon from soccer.
moral_consequence: Brandon watches the taped football game with his dad when they get home.
immoral_action: Mike watches the entire football game while assuming that Molly will pick up Brandon from soccer.
immoral_consequence: Brandon has to walk home when no one comes to pick him up.

norm: Parents are expected to show support for their children's interests.
situation: Verlin is at his computer struggling to pay the bills when his son asks if he can take karate classes.
intention: Verlin wants to save money.
moral_action: Verlin decides to cancel several streaming services they don't need in order to pay for karate classes.
moral_consequence: His son rises through the ranks eventually becoming a black belt.
immoral_action: Verlin tells his son that martial arts is a complete waste of resources as he continues looking at his screen.
immoral_consequence: His son starts crying.

norm: It's good to pay for meals that you ate.
situation: Jeff is at a restuarant with his friends eating lunch and gets into an argument with one of them.
intention: Jeff wants to leave.
moral_action: Jeff puts money on the table to cover his share and walks out.
moral_consequence: One of Jeff's friends run out behind him to apologize and returns the money back to Jeff saying he will take care of it.
immoral_action: Jeff says he is going to the bathroom but instead leaves the restaurant without paying.
immoral_consequence: Jeffs friends are stuck with his part of the bill and are angry at Jeff.

norm: You shouldn't fall for someone you don't know.
situation: Mark is lonely and only has strangers as Facebook friends, and they are the only people he talks to.
intention: Mark wants to build a relationship with someone off Facebook.
moral_action: Mark decides to have a platonic, casual friendship with someone from his Facebook network.
moral_consequence: Mark and his friend have a lot of good chats together online.
immoral_action: Mark starts a romantic relationship with a stranger from his Facebook network.
immoral_consequence: The romance falls apart due to lack of knowledge about each other and Mark feels bad.

norm: It's good to stand up to discrimination.
situation: Jamin notices that the waiter at the restaurant continues being rude to his black friend Mark.
intention: Jamin wants to have a nice dinner.
moral_action: Jamin talks to the manager about the waiter's behavior.
moral_consequence: Marcus receives his meal for free.
immoral_action: Jamin decides not to comment on the issue as he enjoys his food.
immoral_consequence: Marcus feels depressed by the waiter's behavior.

norm: It's good to take trips to new places.
situation: Bob went on the same vacation from work every year for 20 years.
intention: Bob wants to enjoy his vacation.
moral_action: Bob goes somewhere new not knowing what it will be like.
moral_consequence: Bob has a lot of fun and a bunch of new experiences at the new destination.
immoral_action: Bob goes to the same place he always does, and he drinks to the 21st anniversary of the vacation location.
immoral_consequence: Bob does what he always does and it feels the same as always.

norm: It's not okay to stalk somebody else.
situation: Yoshi met a new girl at his high school and has developed a crush on her.
intention: Yoshi wants to let the girl know that he likes her.
moral_action: Yoshi buys some flowers and gives them to the girl telling her that he likes her.
moral_consequence: The girl is flattered and asks if he wants to date her.
immoral_action: Yoshi starts following the girl around town constantly trailing behind just at the edge of her vision.
immoral_consequence: The girl is creeped out by Yoshi and eventually tells him to stay away from her, or she will call the police.

norm: Leaving a young child alone in the bathroom is foolish.
situation: Marissa is bathing her toddler son, Bradley, when the phone rings.
intention: Marissa wants to answer the phone.
moral_action: Marissa answers the phone with one hand while continuing to bathe Bradley with the other.
moral_consequence: Marissa learns the importance of multitasking as a parent.
immoral_action: Marissa answers the phone and leaves the bathroom for a quieter area of the house.
immoral_consequence: Marissa returns to find Bradley choking on water.

norm: It is good to help others prepare for a presentation.
situation: Jonah's colleagues are in a hurry to wrap up fine-tuning their upcoming presentation and ask him for help, but he is busy on an important project of his own.
intention: Jonah wants to be recognized as an outstanding worker.
moral_action: Jonah decides to help his colleagues polish their presentation and stays late to work on his own project.
moral_consequence: Jonah's colleagues' presentation is a big success because it's so well rounded and elegant.
immoral_action: Jonah doesn't help his colleagues and intensely focuses on his project.
immoral_consequence: Jonah's colleagues' presentation is not well received because it's a bit rough around the edges.

norm: It's wrong to exclude someone because they can't afford something.
situation: Blake's friend Jimmy just lost his job and Blake invites Jimmy out with some other friends to go see a movie and when Jimmy shows Jimmy says he's broke.
intention: Blake wants to enjoy the movie.
moral_action: Blake offers to pay for Jimmy's tickets, so he can enjoy the movie as well.
moral_consequence: Jimmy enjoys the movie and later gets a new job and pays Blake back.
immoral_action: Blake tells Jimmy tough luck, and takes the rest of his friends in to buy tickets and watch the movie.
immoral_consequence: Jimmy is depressed that his friends are such awful people.

norm: You should be considerate of people.
situation: Pat is listening to the radio while he works his construction job on a busy street, when his favorite song starts playing.
intention: Pat wants to turn up his favorite song.
moral_action: Pat gets closer to the radio while his favorite song is playing and turns it up very slightly.
moral_consequence: The noise doesn't bother anyone and Pat enjoys listening to his song without consequences.
immoral_action: Pat turns the radio up as loud as it will go and holds it up to get the maximum amount of sound out of the box.
immoral_consequence: The sound reverberates into the local businesses surrounding Pat and someone calls the police to complain about the excessive noise.

norm: You should not feel entitled to touch other people's belongings.
situation: Cody is at his friends house, and he sees that he has an expensive collectible.
intention: Cody wants to get a closer look at the collectible.
moral_action: Cody asks his friend to show him the collectible and asks a lot of questions.
moral_consequence: Cody's friend is happy to show Cody his collectible that he is proud of.
immoral_action: Cody walks over and picks the collectible up getting his fingerprints all over it and risking dropping it.
immoral_consequence: Cody's friend freaks out and gets really angry that his friend thinks he can just grab expensive things like that.

norm: You shouldn't shoplift.
situation: Mary is at the corner store during her lunch break.
intention: Mary wants to eat a snack.
moral_action: Mary buys a candy bar from the store.
moral_consequence: The store owner makes a profit from the sale.
immoral_action: Mary hides a candy bar in her purse and exits the store.
immoral_consequence: The store owner loses money because Mary did not pay.

norm: It is responsible to plan for parenthood.
situation: Sam and Sally have sex every single night with protection on at all times because they are unable to afford a child, and don't believe in abortion.
intention: Sam wants to try something different.
moral_action: Sam asks Sally to have sex with him in the woods instead of at home.
moral_consequence: Sam and Sally have very exciting sex, both feeling thrilled.
immoral_action: Sam tells Sally he wants to try it with no condom, and promises her he will pull out in time.
immoral_consequence: Sam is unable to pull out in time, and Sally gets pregnant.

norm: It is important to do maintenance on vehicles
situation: Cecil borrows his mom's regularly car and is responsible for maintaining it.
intention: Cecil wants to save money on maintenance costs.
moral_action: Cecil finds a coupon code online for a discount on the maintenance.
moral_consequence: Cecil's mom hears that he took care of the maintenance and is proud of him.
immoral_action: Cecil delays the required maintenance of the car for a long time after it's due.
immoral_consequence: Cecil's mom finds out and is hesitant to let him continue using the car.

norm: Never ignore another humans cry for help.
situation: Bryce is on his phone on the bus when a woman in red sitting across from him holds up a small sign that says 'Help, I'm being trafficked'.
intention: Bryce wants to finish his phone call.
moral_action: Bryce tells his conversational partner he will call them back and hangs up the phone before attempting to help the woman in red.
moral_consequence: Bryce is able to separate the woman from the people trafficking her and helps her get to a police station.
immoral_action: Bryce puts his sunglasses on to avoid looking at the woman and continues talking until his conversation is finished.
immoral_consequence: The woman in red falls victim to international sex trafficking and is terribly abused.

norm: It's rude to view women based on their weight.
situation: Sam is a long time single person longing for an intimate connection who just made a profile on a dating app.
intention: Sam wants to find a romantic partner.
moral_action: Sam spends time getting to know people regardless of their appearance.
moral_consequence: Sam ends up meeting a wonderful woman who is a bit on the heavy side.
immoral_action: Sam brushes off the women who are overweight and focuses on those who are in shape.
immoral_consequence: Sam misses out on an honorable woman who happened to be heavier.

norm: It's good to attend college.
situation: George just graduated from High School and is debating what to do with his life.
intention: George wants to decide on what his next step should be.
moral_action: George decides to further his education and goes to the local community college.
moral_consequence: George transfers to a 4 year college later and gets a degree in Computer Science which makes him a ton of money.
immoral_action: George decides to work at the local convenience store for the foreseeable future.
immoral_consequence: George ends up working at the store for the rest of his life, barely making minimum wage.

norm: You shouldn't put all the responsibility on certain family members.
situation: Anne has decided to live with her parents while she is attending college.
intention: Anne wants to save money to pay tuition.
moral_action: Anne agrees on a small amount of rent to pay her parents each month.
moral_consequence: Anne's parents are able to cover her costs with the rent she pays.
immoral_action: Anne relies fully on her parents to pay for all her living expenses.
immoral_consequence: Anne's parents have a difficult time making ends meet and are struggling.

norm: It's good to make sure you don't upset your partner.
situation: Lisa loves dogs and cats, but her girlfriend Sandra is allergic to pet dander.
intention: Lisa wants to get a dog as a pet.
moral_action: Lisa tells Sandra she wants to get a dog, but she understands if Sandra does not want to get one.
moral_consequence: Lisa and Sandra look up hypoallergenic dog breeds and find a reputable dog breeder together.
immoral_action: Lisa secretly adopts a golden retriever from the local pound and surprises Sandra.
immoral_consequence: Sandra's allergies flare up and the two argue about the dog.

norm: It's rude to throw someone else's food away.
situation: Jack just brought home a lot of groceries and the fridge is already quite full.
intention: Jack wants to make some room in the fridge.
moral_action: Jack reorganizes the fridge and throws away some of his own old food which frees up space.
moral_consequence: Jack's roommate is happy the fridge is clearer.
immoral_action: Jack throws out some of his roommate's old leftovers to make room in the fridge.
immoral_consequence: Jack's roommate gets upset because he was still going to eat the food.

norm: It's rude to wear someone else's underwear without their knowledge.
situation: Adam is getting dressed and realizes he has no underwear clean when he see his brother's.
intention: Adam wants clean underwear.
moral_action: Adam does a load of laundry and makes sure the load contains underwear.
moral_consequence: Adam's brother wears his clean underwear the next day.
immoral_action: Adam takes his brother's clean underwear and wears them for the day.
immoral_consequence: Adam's brother is offended that Adam used his underwear without his permission.

norm: You should be honest about having children
situation: Casey is on the fence about having children, and his wife is asking him whether he wants kids.
intention: Casey has to tell his wife whether he wants kids.
moral_action: Casey tells his wife that he doesn't think he's ready to have kids.
moral_consequence: Casey feels good that he wasn't afraid to tell his wife the truth.
immoral_action: Casey tells his wife that he would love to have kids.
immoral_consequence: Casey regrets telling his wife this and is scared about having to take care of kids.

norm: It's rude to ridicule other people.
situation: Roger is at school walking to class when he sees a fellow student Josh trip and drop all of his books on the ground.
intention: Roger wants to acknowledge Josh's accident.
moral_action: Roger goes over to Josh to help pick up his books and asks if he's okay.
moral_consequence: Josh feels better and appreciates Roger's kindness and assistance.
immoral_action: Roger points at Josh on the ground and begins laughing at him.
immoral_consequence: Josh feels embarrassed and humiliated by Roger making fun of him.

norm: You should be respectful when you're on a date
situation: Dave and Alison are at a restaurant having dinner for their first date.
intention: Dave wants to make a comment about Alison.
moral_action: Dave tells Alison that he likes the way her dress brings out her eyes.
moral_consequence: Blushing, Alison smiles at Dave and thanks him for the compliment.
immoral_action: Dave tells Alison that he is not a fan of how she is wearing her hair.
immoral_consequence: Alison, visibly offended, takes all her belongings and walks out on the date.

norm: It's good to teach others about technology.
situation: Pat's dad just bought a new phone, but he doesn't know how to use it.
intention: Pat has to decide whether to help his dad learn how to use his phone.
moral_action: Pat decides to show his dad how to use his phone.
moral_consequence: Pat's dad feels relieved that he actually received help and doesn't have to beg.
immoral_action: Pat doesn't want to baby his dad, so he decides not to help him.
immoral_consequence: Pat's dad continues to struggle with his phone, and he would feel too embarrassed to ask for help.

norm: It is wrong to abuse your loved ones
situation: John sees his son Andrew take a cookie from the jar before dinner.
intention: John wants his kids to listen to him.
moral_action: John reminds Andrew if he eats cookies now he will be too full for dinner.
moral_consequence: Andrew thinks about what John says and realizes he loves him and is looking out for him and is happy.
immoral_action: John raises his voice and comes at Andrew with a belt swinging at him.
immoral_consequence: Andrew cries and resents John and becomes afraid of him as he grows up.

norm: You shouldn't cut off a conversation with your partner.
situation: Greg and his husband are discussing whether or not they should buy a new car.
intention: Greg wants to get out of the conversation.
moral_action: Greg tells his partner that he is free to do what he wants to about a new car and leaves the room.
moral_consequence: Greg gets his favorite dinner cooked for him by his partner for being so agreeable in the car discussion.
immoral_action: Greg turns and walks away from his partner who is in mid-sentence about his views on a new car.
immoral_consequence: Greg is left alone when his upset partner leaves and spends the night at a friend's house because he's upset at Greg's rude treatment.

norm: You shouldn't take someone else's cigarettes.
situation: Tom is a social smoker and is out at a bar with friends on a weekend night.
intention: Tom wants to smoke a cigarette.
moral_action: Tom buys a pack of cigarettes from a vending machine inside the bar.
moral_consequence: Tom enjoys having a relaxing smoke on the bar's back patio.
immoral_action: Without asking, Tom takes a cigarette from the pack of a stranger who left it on their table.
immoral_consequence: Tom is yelled at by the stranger for stealing a cigarette, and he feels bad about it.

norm: It's rude to force someone to go to therapy.
situation: Joseph and his wife Linda are talking and Linda is complaining to Joseph that she feels a little blah lately.
intention: Joseph wants to suggest a solution to Linda for her troubles.
moral_action: Joseph tells Linda that perhaps they could do some fun activities together to get her back into the swing of things.
moral_consequence: Linda is happy to hear Joseph cares about her well being and is trying to come up with ways to make her feel better.
immoral_action: Joseph tells Linda that the only solution is to go therapy and that she must go or their marriage will be in peril.
immoral_consequence: Linda feels extreme pressure now to get better because her marriage is on the line, causing her massive stress.

norm: It is wrong to blow off a friend.
situation: Tracy has plans to console her recently dumped best friend when Tracy gets asked out by a guy she likes.
intention: Tracy wants to respond to the request for a date,.
moral_action: Tracy gives the guy a rain check and goes out with her girl friend.
moral_consequence: Tracy is able to lend her friend her support.
immoral_action: Tracy decides to cancel on her best friend and goes on the date instead.
immoral_consequence: Tracy's friend feels let down in her time of need.

norm: It is good to help those who need it.
situation: On the way to the store, Anthony sees a homeless man begging for change.
intention: Anthony wants to get to the store.
moral_action: Anthony gives the homeless man $20 as he walks by him.
moral_consequence: The homeless man thanks Anthony for giving him the money.
immoral_action: Anthony pretends he doesn't see the homeless man and walks by him.
immoral_consequence: The homeless man starts to frown because Anthony ignored him.

norm: Excluding your classmates from gaming is hurtful.
situation: Chad was planning to play video games with some of his friends on the weekend.
intention: Chad wants to invite his classmates to his house.
moral_action: Chad makes sure to invite all the kids in his class to his house.
moral_consequence: The kids all have a great time together playing video games at Chad's house.
immoral_action: Chad invites everyone but one of the boys in his class to his house.
immoral_consequence: The boy that isn't invited feels left out and spends the weekend alone and depressed.

norm: It's ok to report a teacher's wrongdoings.
situation: Chester's teacher has been bullying a student in Chester's class and Chester is bothered by it.
intention: Chester doesn't want to become a target for his teacher.
moral_action: Chester makes an anonymous report to the school administration about the situation.
moral_consequence: The school intervenes to help Chester's classmate.
immoral_action: Chester stays silent and watches the teacher continue to mistreat his classmate.
immoral_consequence: Chester's classmate is emotionally broken down and Chester feels guilty.

norm: You shouldn't scream at elders.
situation: Andrew is visiting his grandfather and is mad about his grandfather's old-fashioned views.
intention: Andrew wants to tell his grandfather why he's wrong.
moral_action: Andrew listens to his grandfather's point of view, and explains his own.
moral_consequence: Andrew's grandfather realizes that he may be misinformed and thanks Andrew for teaching him something.
immoral_action: Andrew yells at his grandfather that he's ignorant.
immoral_consequence: Andrew's grandfather is upset and cuts Andrew out of his will.

norm: You should give gifts to your partner for their birthday.
situation: Lee is getting ready for her husband's birthday.
intention: Lee wants to celebrate her husband's birthday.
moral_action: Lee buys her husband an antique watch that her husband had been eyeing.
moral_consequence: Lee's husband is touched that she remembered what he wanted.
immoral_action: Lee tells her husband happy birthday and puts on a movie for them to watch.
immoral_consequence: Lee's husband is hurt that she didn't bother to pick out a thoughtful gift for him.

norm: It is unacceptable to call other people rude names.
situation: Craig is in line at the movie theater concession stand waiting to get some popcorn.
intention: Craig wants to hurry up and get into the theatre before the movie starts.
moral_action: Craig asks the person in front of him if he can switch places because his movie is about to start.
moral_consequence: Craig moves up in the line and gets his popcorn in time to catch his movie.
immoral_action: Craig steps up to make his order but a woman cuts in front of him, so he calls her a rude name.
immoral_consequence: Craig is asked to leave the theater for using profane language toward the woman.

norm: You shouldn't embarrass your family.
situation: Lilly's parents are hosting a wake after a funeral.
intention: Lilly wants to kiss her boyfriend.
moral_action: Lilly asks her boyfriend to go outside with her and kisses him.
moral_consequence: None of the attendees see Lilly kiss her boyfriend, and it is kept between the two of them.
immoral_action: Lilly grabs her boyfriend and kisses him passionately in the middle of the crowd.
immoral_consequence: Lilly's parents are ashamed by her behavior.

norm: Parents are allowed to decide what's best for their children.
situation: Angel and his friend Roy are arguing about what movies each of thier kids watch.
intention: "Angel wants to explain that Roy's kids are allowed to watch ""worse"" movies than his own."
moral_action: Angel decides that Roy can decide what's best for his own kids but not Angel's.
moral_consequence: Roy agrees, and they decide to work out what to do when their kids hang out together.
immoral_action: Angel and Roy both insist that the other's kids should have to follow their set of rules on what to watch.
immoral_consequence: Angel and Roy keep arguing and their kids have to deal with their dads arguing.

norm: You should ask before borrowing someone else's property.
situation: Omar is getting ready to do some yard work when he notices his neighbor left his shears on his lawn while his are in his garage.
intention: Omar wants to choose which shears to use.
moral_action: Omar decides to walk to his own garage and grab his own shears before cutting the shrub.
moral_consequence: Omar's neighbor sees Omar working on his lawn and comes out to say hello to him.
immoral_action: Omar decides to grab his neighbor's shears since they're right there and use them to cut some shrubs.
immoral_consequence: The neighbor notices Omar using his shears and is annoyed that Omar is touching his things.

norm: It is wrong to lose contact with a grandparent.
situation: Grace, who is very close to her grandma, just graduated from university and doesn't have any jobs lined up.
intention: Grace wants to spend a few years travelling the world.
moral_action: Grace makes sure to send her grandma postcards detailing her travels on a regular basis and calls to check up on her whenever she can.
moral_consequence: Grace's grandma is very happy for Grace and eagerly awaits her phone calls.
immoral_action: Grace goes on her traveling adventures and doesn't attempt to contact anyone while she's away.
immoral_consequence: Grace's grandma gets very worried about Grace and misses her dearly.

norm: It is not okay to point out people's awkwardness.
situation: Briana is sitting with Wayne, who is very shy, and trying to talk with him.
intention: Briana wants to pull Wayne out of his shell.
moral_action: Briana asks Wayne about his hobbies, then questions him about ones that he likes.
moral_consequence: Wayne opens up and starts telling her about his hobbies.
immoral_action: Briana tells Wayne that he's really bad at talking and that he needs to do better.
immoral_consequence: Wayne feels even more awkward and refuses to talk with Briana.

norm: You shouldn't judge yourself or others based on height.
situation: John, who is short, runs a powerful health institution and deals with a lot of taller clients and workers.
intention: John wants to have authority over other people.
moral_action: John uses his superior business skills and knowledge to direct people's projects wisely, helping them complete them successfully.
moral_consequence: John's associates come to respect John and seek his advice and counsel, listening to and obeying what he says.
immoral_action: John mounts a ruler on his office door and notes how tall each person is who enters his office, then tries to dominate the taller ones.
immoral_consequence: The taller people find John to be overbearing and controlling and decide not to work for him any more.

norm: It's wrong not to help injured animals.
situation: Bert was driving down the road when he sees a dog with a broken leg on the side of the road.
intention: Bert wants to get home.
moral_action: Bert stops and takes the dog to his house to care for it.
moral_consequence: The dog is up and back on his feet within just a few days.
immoral_action: Bert drives past the injured dog and pays no mind to it on the way to his house.
immoral_consequence: The dog suffers from his injuries and eventually dies a day later.

norm: It's good to show your appreciation.
situation: Lance got his first paycheck from a job his sister recommended him for.
intention: Lance wants to use his first paycheck.
moral_action: Lance uses the paycheck to take his sister out for dinner.
moral_consequence: Lance will be able to show how much his sister means to him.
immoral_action: Lance uses the paycheck to buy himself a lot of food.
immoral_consequence: Lance will not learn to treat other people to things.

norm: It's irresponsible to postpone responsibilities.
situation: John has a very important assignment due in two weeks.
intention: John wants to progress in the new video game that he has just purchased.
moral_action: John finishes his assignment early and spends his new free time playing his new game.
moral_consequence: John is able to make good progress in the game, while receiving the highest marks on his assignment.
immoral_action: John procrastinates on his assignment and instead spends more time playing his video game.
immoral_consequence: John begins his assignment 3 days before the deadline and realizes that the assignment is much more complex than he thought, and receives a failing grade for submitting unsatisfactory work.

norm: It is rude to tell your spouse to shut up.
situation: Bobby and Grace are discussing their lack of intimacy and ways to fix this in the future.
intention: Bobby wants to state his side of the situation and how it makes him feel.
moral_action: Bobby states his side of the situation and listens to Grace's reply as she offers validation for his points.
moral_consequence: Bobby and Grace are able to work through their intimacy problems and fix their relationship.
immoral_action: Bobby states his side of the problem and when Grace trys to offer input Bobby tells her to shut-up and that he is not finished yet.
immoral_consequence: The conversation between Bobby and Grace breaks down and their intimacy remains stagnant.

norm: It's not okay to be obsessed with doing childish things.
situation: Before going to the grocery store, Bill goes to the toy store to look for action figures to add to his toy collection.
intention: Bill wants to buy some new action figures.
moral_action: Bill only buys two action figures at the toy store.
moral_consequence: Bill has money left over to spend at the grocery store.
immoral_action: Bill spends his entire paycheck at the toy store.
immoral_consequence: Bill has no money left for food.

norm: You should respect the schedules and privacy of neighbors.
situation: It's midnight and Rachel's neighbors are sleeping, but she can't seem to herself, so she wants to exercise.
intention: Rachel wants to play music.
moral_action: Rachel turns on her workout playlist  and listens in her headphones.
moral_consequence: Rachel's neighbors are able to sleep, and she is able to tire herself out.
immoral_action: Rachel turns on her workout playlist  through the speakers on her home theater.
immoral_consequence: Rachel's neighbors wake up and pound on her door for her to knock off the racket.

norm: Not being accepting of different lifestyle choices is wrong.
situation: Tucker's daughter Anna is getting married to her partner Louise.
intention: Tucker wants to react to the news.
moral_action: Tucker tells Anna that he is happy that she found someone she loves.
moral_consequence: Anna and Louise invite Tucker to  the wedding where he walks his daughter down the aisle, and he feels proud.
immoral_action: Tucker tells Anna he will never approve of her marriage because he was raised to believe two people of the same gender should not be married.
immoral_consequence: Anna tells Tucker that he is not welcome in her and Louise's lives and now he feels remorseful for not being accepting.

norm: It is rude to impose your food choice on others.
situation: Tom is out at a local Italian restaurant to have dinner with his family.
intention: Tom wants to order food.
moral_action: John orders a meal for himself and allows his family to each choose their own.
moral_consequence: John's family has a wonderful experience at the restaurant, and they all enjoy their food.
immoral_action: Tom decides on a number of different dishes and orders them for everyone at the table.
immoral_consequence: Tom's family doesn't enjoy the meal very much because the food he ordered didn't match their preferences.

norm: It is important to keep children safe.
situation: Mary is preparing to cook dinner and realizes she is out of eggs.
intention: Mary wants to go to the grocery store with her child.
moral_action: Mary buckles her baby in the car seat in the back seat of her truck and drives to the market.
moral_consequence: If Mary is in an accident, the baby will be safe.
immoral_action: Mary lays her baby in the front seat of the truck and drives to the market.
immoral_consequence: If Mary is in an accident, the baby will be hurt.

norm: Is bad to blow off work for no reason.
situation: Art is laying bricks in the hot sun, constructing a wall.
intention: Art wants to give art's tired muscles a rest.
moral_action: Art sits under a tree for a few minutes with a bottle of water and recovers in the shade before returning to work.
moral_consequence: An obligation is fulfilled and Art's work history remains unblemished, the wall is completed for the customer.
immoral_action: Art leaves the wall behind and gets drunk with Art's friends.
immoral_consequence: Cement dries inside a mixer, ruining the mixer, Art does't get paid for the wall, and owes money for a new mixer, the wall is not built for the customer.

norm: It's wrong to defecate in other people's belongings.
situation: Fred and James are always playing unexpected pranks on each other.
intention: Fred wants to prank James in way that he's never done before.
moral_action: Fred gives James a spring snake disguised as a can of chips.
moral_consequence: James opens the can and laughs as the snake pops out.
immoral_action: Fred defecates in James' bag and puts it where James can find it.
immoral_consequence: James becomes furious with Fred for ruining his bag with feces.

norm: It's rude to call someone trailer trash.
situation: Ben is at the mall when he's bumped into by Zeke which causes Ben pain.
intention: Ben wants to react to the painful bump.
moral_action: "Ben yells ""ouch"" and tells Zeke to be more careful as it really hurt him when he got bumped."
moral_consequence: Zeke is remorseful immediately and offers Ben an apology as well as to call a medical person for him.
immoral_action: Ben tells Zeke that he's trailer trash who doesn't belong in the city and certainly not at the mall.
immoral_consequence: Zeke is insulted and feel self conscious because he wonders if the other mall patrons feel the same way.

norm: It's rude to catfish people.
situation: Chad hadn't talked to Charli yet, but he just found her on Facebook.
intention: Chad wants to talk to Charli.
moral_action: Chad requests a friend request on his main account and talks to her once she accepts.
moral_consequence: Chad is able to have a conversation with Charli, and he gets to be friends with her.
immoral_action: Chad makes a fake account on Facebook and messages Charli.
immoral_consequence: Chad is not able to form a real relationship with her and has to tell a lot of lies.

norm: It is good to talk through situations with partner.
situation: Jane has been married to her partner for three years.
intention: Jane wants to move on from a disagreement she is having with her partner.
moral_action: Jane and her partner sit down and discuss their disagreement and communicate openly.
moral_consequence: Jane and her partner get over the disagreement and grow closer to one another thanks to the communication.
immoral_action: Jane and her partner bury and ignore the issue as if it never happened.
immoral_consequence: Jane becomes more passive aggressive and resentful towards her partner eventually leading to their separation.

norm: You shouldn't be biased against mentally challenged people.
situation: James had to choose between two applicants for a cashier position, someone who got fired from their last few jobs or someone with Down Syndrome.
intention: James wants to hire a reliable long-term worker.
moral_action: James hires the worker with Down Syndrome and talks to them and their family about necessary accomodations.
moral_consequence: The worker with Down Syndrome comes in early and leaves late every day.
immoral_action: James insists on not hiring the worker with Down Syndrome out of concern over possible unusual behavior.
immoral_consequence: James soon becomes the latest employer to fire the other candidate for the job.

norm: It's wrong to end an relationship without explaining why.
situation: Greg has been dating Sarah for a few months but wants to break it off because they don't have much in common.
intention: Greg wants to break up the relationship.
moral_action: Greg goes to Sarah's house and explains that while she is sweet, they just don't like the same things and says they should explore new relationships.
moral_consequence: Sarah is still hurt, but can understand Greg's point, and they remain friends.
immoral_action: Greg writes a message to Sarah that says, It's over, and ignores Sarah's messages asking why.
immoral_consequence: Sarah is left to ponder what went wrong and is left feeling confused and hurt.

norm: It is appreciative to recognize how someone helps you.
situation: Heather is in need of a new car but doesn't have the money, though her mom often provides her with financial help.
intention: Heather wants to ask her mom if she will help her buy a new car.
moral_action: After receiving a check from her mom, Heather thanks her immensely and bakes her a cake to show her gratitude.
moral_consequence: Heather's mom feels appreciated and gives Heather a hug.
immoral_action: Heather cashes a check from her mom then proceeds to purchase a new car without ever thanking her.
immoral_consequence: Heather's mom feels used by her and cuts her off entirely.

norm: You shouldn't spit in someone's face.
situation: Maggie is fighting with Shauna, and Shauna tosses water at Maggie.
intention: Maggie wants to express her frustration.
moral_action: Maggie explains her feelings and the source of her anger to Shauna.
moral_consequence: Shauna and Maggie have a deep conversation, and they come up with ways to stop arguments.
immoral_action: Maggie steps forwards and spits on Shauna's cheek.
immoral_consequence: Shauna gives Maggie a black eye.

norm: It's wrong to take other people's cutlery.
situation: Pedro is at dinner with a dining companion and notices he is missing a fork.
intention: Pedro wants to get a fork.
moral_action: Pedro asks the server for a fork.
moral_consequence: Pedro's dining companion will think he is well mannered.
immoral_action: Pedro takes the fork of his dining companion.
immoral_consequence: Pedro's dining companion will think Pedro lacks manners.

norm: It's wrong to get someone fired.
situation: Joe is having dinner at a restaurant where their waiter's service is poor.
intention: Joe wants the waiter to know Joe is upset.
moral_action: Joe leaves a 5 percent tip for the waiter on his check.
moral_consequence: The waiter vows to do better in the future, so he can increase his earnings.
immoral_action: Joe complains to the waiter's manager who terminates the waiter.
immoral_consequence: The waiter is unable to provide for his family now.

norm: It's bad to stalk an ex on social media.
situation: Jerry noticed that he and his ex had similar friends on facebook.
intention: Jerry wants to talk to his friends on facebook.
moral_action: Jerry sends messages to his friends and ignores the fact that they know his ex.
moral_consequence: Jerry maintains a healthy relationship with his friends even though they know his ex.
immoral_action: Jerry asks his friends to spy on his ex's facebook page for him.
immoral_consequence: Jerry's ex finds out, and she files a restraining order against him.

norm: It's not okay to lie to your parents.
situation: Hannah skipped school today and the principles office called to tell her mom, Karen, who asks Hannah why she wasn't in school.
intention: Hannah wants to respond to Karen.
moral_action: Hannah admits to not being in class because she wanted to go to a protest.
moral_consequence: karen tells Hannah the importance of education, but understands her need to stand up for her beliefs, so Hannah gets grounded for 2 days.
immoral_action: Hannah tells her mom that she was at school and there must be some mix up, but Karen knows this in untrue.
immoral_consequence: Hannah gets grounded for 2 weeks by Karen.

norm: It's rude to use a service without paying for it
situation: Silas can't watch Stranger things because he lacks a Netflix subscription, but he sees the log in information for his friend's netflix account on the table.
intention: Silas wants to watch Stranger Things.
moral_action: Silas asks his friend if they could watch stranger thing while he's hanging out at his friend's house.
moral_consequence: Silas and his friend bond over watching the show.
immoral_action: Silas uses his friend's log in information to watch Netflix on his tv.
immoral_consequence: Silas friend yells at him when he discovers Silas using his account.

norm: It's rude to take up more than one seat.
situation: Ralph and his girlfriend Eliza get on a bus and look for a place to sit down.
intention: Ralph wants to sit on the bus.
moral_action: Ralph sits down in one empty seat and lets Eliza sit in the other.
moral_consequence: Ralph and Eliza ride comfortably on the bus to their destination.
immoral_action: Ralph sits down in the only two empty seats on the bus.
immoral_consequence: Ralph is relaxed while Eliza is annoyed that she has to stand.

norm: It is inappropriate to call family pieces of shit.
situation: Molly is at Thanksgiving dinner, listening to her relatives champion political ideology she firmly disagrees with.
intention: Molly wants to tell her family members that she disagrees with their politics.
moral_action: Molly tells her family that everyone is entitled to their political opinions but that she doesn't believe they're right.
moral_consequence: Molly's family decides not to talk politics anymore and instead starts serving the pumpkin pie.
immoral_action: Molly tells her family that because of what they believe politically she thinks they're pieces of shit.
immoral_consequence: Molly's family is very insulted and refuses to invite Molly for Thanksgiving dinner next year.

norm: It's not okay to base your appreciation on finances.
situation: Nicole is a young attractive woman that recently signed up on a singles site to only meet men with high incomes.
intention: Nicole wants to get a romantic partner that is rich.
moral_action: Nicole signs up on a dating site and goes on dates with a variety of different kind of men, until she meets one that is compatible for her.
moral_consequence: Nicole falls in love with the man, and they end up getting married.
immoral_action: Nicole starts dating a significantly wealthy older man that lavishes her with gifts, but she isn't attracted to him.
immoral_consequence: Nicole later meets a man that she genuinely likes, but he knows by her social media status her dating lifestyle and will not date her.

norm: It is bad to choke others.
situation: Tom is listening to Mary shout in pain after she stubbed her toe on a door.
intention: Tad wants to stop Mary from shouting.
moral_action: Tom asks Mary to please stop with the shouting.
moral_consequence: Mary thanks Tom for being polite and Tom puts a bandage on Mary's toe.
immoral_action: Tom chokes Mary, so she can't make any more noise.
immoral_consequence: Mary calls the police on Tom and Tom regrets his actions.

norm: You shouldn't discriminate against people with lisps.
situation: Mary is the judge of a singing contest right now, and some of the contestants have lisps.
intention: Mary wants to pick a singing contestant as a winner.
moral_action: Mary ignores the fact that some of her contestants have lisps and lets a few contestants with lisps win.
moral_consequence: Mary's contestants feel the competition was fair and didn't discriminate based on trivial mouth noises.
immoral_action: Mary explains that all participants with lisps are automatically disqualified from winning.
immoral_consequence: Mary's contestants are all bewildered at the requirement and gossip about Mary.

norm: You shouldn't do other people's homework.
situation: Calvin is sitting in the school library.
intention: Calvin wants to find something to do.
moral_action: Calvin goes to the non-fiction section picks out a book to read.
moral_consequence: Calvin learns a lot of new facts from reading the book.
immoral_action: Calvin does a friend's homework for them when they ask him for help.
immoral_consequence: Calvin is put on probation for violation of the school's honor code.

norm: You should back up so you can let people park.
situation: Jed is parked at a busy shopping mall when people are looking for spots and is tired.
intention: Jed wants to sleep in his car.
moral_action: Jed sees the other drivers and moves his car offroad somewhere and sleeps there.
moral_consequence: The other drivers are grateful to Jed and no one is upset.
immoral_action: Jed pretends there's no one looking for his spot and puts his seat back and dozes off.
immoral_consequence: Other drivers become very upset and tap on his window and wake him up.

norm: It's good to be there for your step-kids.
situation: Charlie marries Betty who moves into his house with her two kids from a previous marriage.
intention: Charlie wants to decide how to treat his new step-kids.
moral_action: Charlie tells his step-kids that even though they aren't his biological children, he will always help them out just like a father.
moral_consequence: His step-kids become very attached to Charlie and think of him as a real dad.
immoral_action: Charlie tells his step-kids that they aren't his, so they need to stay out of his way.
immoral_consequence: His step-kids resent Charlie and always look for ways to undermine his marriage with their mother.

norm: It's wrong for people to not let teens be teens.
situation: Brad has a teenage daughter who asks him to take her to the mall, so she can hang out with friends.
intention: Brad wants to respond to his daughter's request.
moral_action: Brad drives his daughter to the mall, so she can hang out with friends.
moral_consequence: Brad's daughter will appreciate him and learn social skills.
immoral_action: Brad tells his daughter she cannot hang out at the mall.
immoral_consequence: Brad's daughter will resent him and not learn how to be social.

norm: You should be more sensitive to people with mental issues.
situation: Colin's son has anxiety about going to public places.
intention: Colin wants to get his son to go to the park.
moral_action: Colin talks to his son about how it is good for him to go to the park.
moral_consequence: Colin's son will be more open to going to the park.
immoral_action: Colin physically carries his son to the park without talking about it.
immoral_consequence: Colin's son will have greater anxiety.

norm: It's good to respond to your spouse's text messages.
situation: Ben is doing overtime at work when he receives a text message from his wife.
intention: Ben wants to consider responding to the text message.
moral_action: Ben quickly shoots a reply to his wife's text message and tells her that he is working overtime.
moral_consequence: Ben's wife acknowledges Ben's response and increasingly views Ben as a hardworker.
immoral_action: Ben chooses to completely ignore the text message and just focus on his work.
immoral_consequence: Ben's wife becomes suspicious and less trusting of what Ben as a result of him not responding.

norm: You should help people that are having a hard time.
situation: Gary gets a call from his friend who lost his job and needs a loan.
intention: Gary wants to respond to his friend's loan request.
moral_action: Gary tells his friend he can loan him some money.
moral_consequence: Gary's friend will be able to get back on his feet.
immoral_action: Gary tells his friend that he can't loan him any money.
immoral_consequence: Gary's friend will have a hard time financially.

norm: It's wrong to swear at people for any reason.
situation: Jim is returning an item to a store that arrived broken.
intention: Jim wants his money back.
moral_action: Jim explains simply that the item is broken and asks for a refund.
moral_consequence: The cashier apologizes, gives him his money back, and tells him to have a nice day.
immoral_action: Jim uses lots of profanity when describing the item's condition and explaining what he wants.
immoral_consequence: The cashier gets the manager, who gives him his money back, then bans him from the store.

norm: It's not okay to be obsessed with competition.
situation: Adam is an avid Pokemon Go player.
intention: Adam wants to be the best Pokemon Go player in his town.
moral_action: Adam starts a town group chat and gets to know other players so that they can work cooperatively.
moral_consequence: Adam always has many people to play the game and do raids with resulting in him being known as the top player in town.
immoral_action: Adam insists on taking over all of the gyms in town at all costs and will stoop to any level to get them.
immoral_consequence: He is reported by others for cheating and harassing others and has his account suspended.

norm: It's good to take your father to a ball game.
situation: Dick calls in to a radio station and wins a contest for two tickets to the baseball game.
intention: Dick wants to pick who to take with him.
moral_action: Dick decides to take his father, Bill to the ball game as his guest.
moral_consequence: Dick spends a great day bonding with his dad and enjoying life like it used to be when he was young.
immoral_action: Dick decides to take his wife Sandy as his guest to the baseball game.
immoral_consequence: Dick spends most of the game arguing with his wife who's not really a sports fan.

norm: People shouldn't get angry with their relatives.
situation: Dave is at a family function with his extended family when his cousin accidentally drops the punch bowl and it shatters and spills.
intention: Dave wants to react to the breaking of the punch bowl.
moral_action: Dave asks his cousin if he's OK and tells him not to worry about the bowl, it's just a material object.
moral_consequence: Dave's cousin is relieved Dave isn't upset and is glad Dave asked him if he's OK.
immoral_action: Dave screams at his cousin that he's an idiot, and he needs to watch where he's walking.
immoral_consequence: Dave's cousin is embarrassed to be called out in front of everyone and is afraid that Dave is angry and might hurt him.

norm: You should make an effort to call your parents more.
situation: Toby is getting ready to go to a party when he remembers that his parents asked him to call them.
intention: Toby wants to go to the party.
moral_action: Toby gives his parents a quick call before going to the party telling him about his plans.
moral_consequence: Toby's parents are relieved to hear from him and are happy he remembered to call.
immoral_action: Toby heads to the party without calling his parents as they had requested.
immoral_consequence: Toby's parents worry about him since they haven't heard from him.

norm: It's good to discuss things over with your family.
situation: Mike lives with his parents but wants to live in another part of the country.
intention: Mike wants to tell his parents about his desire.
moral_action: Mike tells his parents he wants to move away from home and gets their opinion.
moral_consequence: Mike's parents will support him and try to be understanding.
immoral_action: Mike tells his parents he's leaving to move away from home.
immoral_consequence: Mike's parents will be surprised and think Mike doesn't care about their feelings.

norm: "It's inappropriate to ""troll"" people on the internet."
situation: John is reading Reddit forums when he notices a user ask what John thinks is a dumb question.
intention: John wants to respond to the user's question.
moral_action: John answers the question matter of factly giving the user the information they need without adding anything extra.
moral_consequence: the user is glad he has received help and is relieved they got the answer they were seeking.
immoral_action: John writes a sarcastic response with false information that only experienced users would understand and tries to belittle the user.
immoral_consequence: The user feels shamed for their lack of knowledge and is sad about the experience.

norm: It's good to speak out against predatory behavior.
situation: Maddock watches his manager sexually harassing his coworker from his office.
intention: Maddock wants to avoid getting dragged into workplace drama.
moral_action: Maddock records a video of the incident and shows it to HR asking them to keep his identity a secret.
moral_consequence: The manager is fired, and his coworker is promoted to the position of manager.
immoral_action: Maddock continues working ignoring his boss' behavior.
immoral_consequence: His coworker continues getting harassed by their manager.

norm: It's good to return someone else's property.
situation: Payton has borrowed a hair dryer from her friend that makes her hair look really nice.
intention: Payton wants to own a hair dryer just like her friend's.
moral_action: Payton asks her friend where she bought the hair dryer so that she can buy one for herself.
moral_consequence: Payton's friend is happy that Payton liked the hair dryer so much.
immoral_action: Payton keeps the hair dryer and tells her friend that the hair dryer was broken.
immoral_consequence: Payton's friend gets mad when she sees the blow dryer at Payton's house.

norm: You must try to be faithful to your significant other.
situation: Helen and her husband have been together for many years and the passion has faded a bit.
intention: Helen wants to bring the spark back into her romantic life.
moral_action: Helen has a conversation with her husband about how they can make more time for each other and help each other feel special.
moral_consequence: Helen and her husband are happier and their marriage is stronger.
immoral_action: Helen starts an affair with an attractive coworker.
immoral_consequence: Helen's husband is devastated and files for divorce when he finds out.

norm: It's bad to get enraged at people.
situation: Cole is driving on the freeway when another driver cuts him off.
intention: Cole wants to respond to the situation.
moral_action: Cole moves away from the vehicle that cut him off and ignores them.
moral_consequence: The other driver stays away from Cole.
immoral_action: Cole drives up to the side of the driver that cut him off and honks his horn while making gestures with his hands.
immoral_consequence: The other driver tries to ram into Cole's car.

norm: It's wrong to snap at your friends.
situation: Harry's tire on his car is flat, and he is working on it when his friend Steve offers to help.
intention: Harry wants to talk to Steve.
moral_action: Harry asks Steve what he should be doing to fix the tire.
moral_consequence: Steve gives Harry a hand, and they have the tire fixed in no time.
immoral_action: Harry starts to curse at Steve because he was so aggravated.
immoral_consequence: Steve walks away, leaving Harry to deal with his problem himself.

norm: It's bad when a father is often absent.
situation: Andrew wanted his father to come to the baseball game, but his father missed it like usual.
intention: Andrew wants to find out why his Father is never around.
moral_action: Andrew confronts his father, and tells him how hurt he is by him not being around.
moral_consequence: Andrew's father realizes he's been abdicating his child, and promises to do better.
immoral_action: Andrew snoops into his father's phone to find out who he's been messaging.
immoral_consequence: Andrew's father finds out, and is really hurt that his kid violated his trust.
